trackers.name: Justice Canada – Legal Aid Program
trackers.desc: Federal program supporting provincial/territorial legal aid, with funding and access data. · Find here: the federal legal-aid program in Canada. FOR A CIVIL LAND MATTER THE FEDERAL PROGRAMME IS NOT YOUR ROUTE — read this before you write to it. Justice Canada's Legal Aid Program funds criminal legal aid in all provinces through contribution agreements, plus immigration and refugee legal aid. Federal support for CIVIL legal aid in the provinces runs through the Canada Social Transfer — a block payment for health, education and social services administered by the Department of Finance Canada, under which civil legal aid is merely an eligible expenditure. THE EXCEPTION IS THE THREE TERRITORIES: in Yukon, NWT and Nunavut the federal government does support civil legal aid directly, through consolidated Access to Justice Services Agreements, because it holds responsibility for the administration of justice there — so a civil applicant in a territory is in a different position from one in a province. GO TO YOUR PROVINCIAL PLAN INSTEAD: there are 13 recognised legal aid plans, each province delivering on its own policies and procedures, and under the cost-sharing agreements the provinces retain the right to determine financial eligibility and coverage restrictions — plans differ in delivery mechanisms and levels of financial eligibility and coverage. SCALE: plans reported over $947 million in 2021–22, of which provinces and territories contributed more than $671 million (71 percent) against Justice Canada's $196 million. THE PRESSURE IS STRUCTURAL: the federal contribution was capped at about $86 million in 1990–91 and fell to $82 million in 2000–01, rising only slightly since.

trackers.name: BC First Nations Justice Council (BCFNJC)
trackers.desc: Indigenous-led council advancing First Nations self-determination over justice in British Columbia and implementing the BC First Nations Justice Strategy. Through a province-wide network of Indigenous Justice Centres (and a virtual centre), it provides free, culturally grounded legal advice and representation to Indigenous people in criminal-defence and child-protection matters — available regardless of legal-aid eligibility — along with Gladue reports, diversion and healing plans, and wraparound supports (housing, mental-health and addictions, employment) that address the causes of criminalisation. Its work responds to the drastic over-representation of Indigenous people in the justice system and to the Truth and Reconciliation and MMIWG Calls to Action.

trackers.name: Alliance of Canadian Land Trusts (ACLT)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the national body representing roughly 150 local and regional Canadian land trusts — charities that conserve private land through donation, acquisition and conservation agreements (easements and covenants) held in perpetuity. USE IT: to find the land trust covering your area, and to understand which instrument (sale, donation or easement) fits the parcel you are trying to save.

trackers.name: East Coast Environmental Law (ECELAW) — Atlantic Canada
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: provides public-interest environmental law services throughout Atlantic Canada, running an inquiry line, legal and policy research and workshops on environmental assessment, water, mining, energy, protected places and species at risk. WHO IT SUITS: anyone in Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, PEI or Newfoundland and Labrador — the regional first call, where Ecojustice and CELA have less reach.

trackers.name: Indigenous Leadership Initiative — Indigenous Protected and Conserved Areas
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: works at Nation, territorial, provincial and federal level to secure recognition and long-term funding for IPCAs — lands and waters where Indigenous governments hold the primary role in protecting ecosystems through their own laws, governance and knowledge systems. IPCAs are central to Canada's commitment to protect 30% of lands and waters by 2030. USE IT: for the funding and recognition side of standing up an IPCA, and for the national argument that Indigenous-led conservation delivers better ecological outcomes.

trackers.name: CPAWS BC — Indigenous Protected and Conserved Areas explainer
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a plain guide to what an IPCA is and, critically, what legal footing it stands on. THE KEY POINT: no federal or provincial statute currently recognises IPCAs. Indigenous Peoples have the right to self-determination and CAN establish an IPCA in their territories WITHOUT recognition from non-Indigenous governments — the Tsilhqot'in National Government declared Dasiqox Tribal Park in 2014 on that basis, following the Supreme Court of Canada's recognition of their Aboriginal title. USE IT: recognition from BC or Canada is not required to declare, but where it is given it helps ensure management plans are respected and prohibited activities such as mining, logging or bottom-trawling are actually limited. Know which of the two you are asking for.

trackers.name: Environmental Damages Fund (Canada) — fines redirected to the affected area
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a federal fund holding money from FINES, PENALTIES, COURT ORDERS AND VOLUNTARY PAYMENTS FOR ENVIRONMENTAL VIOLATIONS, which is then spent on projects benefiting the natural environment — USUALLY IN THE AREA WHERE THE VIOLATION OCCURRED. Over $255 million across 600+ projects since 1995. Four categories: restoration, environmental quality improvement, research and development, and education and awareness. WHO IT SUITS: communities living with the consequences of a prosecuted polluter — the geographic tie is the point. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is the polluter's own money paying for the remedy on the ground they damaged, so if there has been a conviction or settlement near you, ask where that money went. Generally one to two calls for applications a year; requirements vary by call, so read the current Applicant Guide rather than assuming.

trackers.name: Environment and Climate Change Canada — environmental funding programs
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the federal department's index of its grants and contributions programs, covering species-at-risk recovery, freshwater quality, habitat protection, ecologically sensitive land, and community action. Indigenous communities, landowners, environmental groups, schools, other levels of government and businesses are all eligible applicants across the suite. WHO IT SUITS: start here rather than at a single programme page — the right fit is often not the obvious one. HOW IT DIFFERS: it also links the EcoAction Community Funding Program, which has run since 1995 for community-based non-profits and typically requires that at least half your project value come from non-federal sources, so line up matching support first.

trackers.name: ATRIS — Aboriginal and Treaty Rights Information System
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a web-based geographic information system giving access to the documents and maps used to work out who must be consulted about activity on a given piece of land — data co-developed with Indigenous communities, in one interactive platform. USE IT: to establish, before anything else, which Indigenous groups hold or assert rights over the site in question, and therefore who the Crown was obliged to consult. If a project has been approved and a rights-holding group on ATRIS was never properly consulted, that is the gap a challenge is built on. Training is available and a government account can be requested.

trackers.name: Corporations Canada (company register)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); Corporations Canada (company register) — the official register of companies and legal entities in Canada — the primary public record of corporate existence, ownership, directors and filings. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A BENEFICIAL-OWNERSHIP REGISTER: this shows the registered entity, its directors and filings; where a separate beneficial-ownership register exists, use that to reach the real humans behind a shell company.

trackers.name: Participant Funding — it pays for data, expert review and travel to hearings
trackers.desc: IT PAYS FOR THE THREE THINGS THAT ACTUALLY DEFEAT COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION. The Agency states that people face challenges ‘like their ability to gather data, review scientific documents or travel to panel hearings’ and that the Participant Funding Program supports these related activities. Compare Ireland and England, where costs protection limits your downside but nobody pays for your expert. INDIVIDUALS ARE ELIGIBLE: Indigenous communities and organizations, non-profit groups, and individuals qualify if they can show their contribution will add value to an assessment with relevant knowledge or expertise — and for individuals it is also good to have a direct local interest. THE TEST IS VALUE ADDED, NOT STANDING: lead with what you know that the Agency does not — local observation, long residence, species records, water knowledge — rather than with how the project affects you. All money received is publicly disclosed. THE TIMING IS WHAT MOST APPLICANTS GET WRONG: funding is offered at key stages, not once. Published notices show planning-phase money specifically for reviewing and commenting on the draft Tailored Impact Statement Guidelines and the draft Public Participation Plan, with another opportunity to apply for later phases. Missing the first round does not end it — but the first round shapes the guidelines the whole assessment is then conducted against, so money to comment on the DRAFT guidelines is worth more than money to comment on the finished Impact Statement. Later rounds have funded review of Review Panel Terms of Reference, the Impact Statement, and participating in public hearings. Deadlines are project-specific and short — published examples ran three to four weeks from notice — and are found on the Canadian Impact Assessment Registry, which is also where written comments go. THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE MOMENT: the Minister may refer a project to an independent Review Panel no later than 45 days after the Notice of Commencement, and that decision must consider public concerns related to the adverse effects and impacts on the rights of Indigenous Peoples — that window is when public concern can change the forum from an Agency assessment to an independent panel with hearings. The proponent has up to three years to submit its Impact Statement, so rounds recur. AND WATCH FOR RULEMAKING NOTICES: funding has been opened to help groups comment on a fee proposal to modernize the Cost Recovery Regulations — money to participate in rulemaking about the process itself is rare. The Agency notes its guidance does not supersede the Act or regulations, which prevail.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Environmental Dispute Resolution Fund — pays for your lawyer and your expert (British Columbia)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: environmental legal aid, run by West Coast Environmental Law since 1989, and one of the very few programmes of its kind in Canada. It gives money to individuals, First Nations, community groups and non-profits to hire a private lawyer, an expert or a mediator. More than $5 million distributed to over 700 recipients from every region of British Columbia, and it says plainly that in many cases it has supported public-interest cases that would otherwise not have proceeded or would have gone unrepresented. THE NUMBERS TO PLAN AROUND: Stage 1 is a smaller one-time grant for initial legal advice and action, or for an opinion on whether a deeper challenge could succeed — up to $3,800 from May 2025. Stage 2 is for applicants already using legal tools inside a wider campaign, up to $19,700 at a time, with a ceiling of $50,000 across any one case. Lawyers and experts are paid at the median legal aid tariff, $135.46 an hour plus taxes for grants approved after 1 May 2025. TWO THINGS THAT DECIDE YOUR APPLICATION. It funds the expert as well as the lawyer — scientific, Indigenous or other — and mediation, consultation and joint rule-making as well as litigation. And it gives priority to groups running a broader community campaign that includes raising money towards their own legal fees, so arrive with a campaign rather than only a grievance. It also keeps a roster of lawyers willing to take these cases and will refer you. CONTACT THEM BEFORE YOU FILL ANYTHING IN: it asks applicants to speak to its access to justice team first, which then decides your stage and invites the application. Applying cold wastes the attempt.

trackers.name: The Ecological Gifts Programme — 242,000 hectares protected, and DEGRADED LAND can qualify
trackers.desc: WHAT IT OFFERS AN OWNER: landowners can donate their land, OR A PARTIAL INTEREST such as a conservation easement agreement, TO AN ELIGIBLE RECIPIENT ORGANISATION THAT WILL CARE FOR IT FOREVER — such as a LAND TRUST, conservation organisation, or government — and receive significant income tax benefits INCLUDING ELIMINATION OF ANY TAX ON THE CAPITAL GAIN. Canada's bucket held the national conservancy and the land-trust alliance; this is the federal machinery they run on. Donating only a partial interest lets an owner keep the farm and give away the right to develop it — the cheapest form of protection there is. THE RECORD: implemented in 1995 and administered by the federal environment department, from its inception to autumn 2023 the programme has led to THE PROTECTION OF MORE THAN 242,000 HECTARES ACROSS CANADA; an earlier count recorded MORE THAN 1,000 ECOLOGICAL GIFTS VALUED AT OVER $635 MILLION. AND THE HONEST NOTE FROM A FORMER LAND-TRUST DIRECTOR, which tells a community how to pitch it: although the financial incentive is TYPICALLY NOT THE PRIMARY REASON for a land donation, IT MAKES SUCH A DONATION FEASIBLE FOR A MUCH LARGER GROUP OF PEOPLE. The programme works with qualified recipient organisations who accept land donations and are responsible for the protection and stewardship of the properties IN PERPETUITY.

trackers.name: Give Green Canada's ecogift guide — who qualifies, and why DEVELOPERS do not
trackers.desc: WHAT COUNTS AS THE GIFT: an ecogift may be a donation of the FEE SIMPLE TITLE to a parcel of land, or a gift of CERTAIN RIGHTS to the land that, depending on the circumstance and province, are known as A COVENANT, EASEMENT OR SERVITUDE. Ecogifts have resulted in thousands of hectares of land across Canada protected for nature IN PERPETUITY. AND THE ELIGIBILITY LINE MOST OWNERS DO NOT KNOW: DEGRADED LANDS MAY ALSO QUALIFY IF THE DONATION IS ACCOMPANIED BY A FIRM COMMITMENT TO A RESTORATION PLAN. A wrecked field with a restoration plan attached can be given under the same programme as pristine habitat — which opens the route to exactly the ground a community is usually fighting over. AND WHO IT SUITS: generous individuals who care about the environment and wish to reduce taxes now, and community-minded COMPANIES OR THOSE WITH SIGNIFICANT TAX LIABILITIES. AND THE ONE IT DOES NOT SUIT, worth knowing before wasting an approach: these gifts may not be as appealing to LAND DEVELOPERS, because land held for development — business inventory — is not eligible for the same tax treatment on capital gains as non-inventory lands; any gain in land value would be TAXED AS REGULAR INCOME. Owners of inventory land may still donate and have the full value recognised as a charitable donation.

trackers.name: A land trust primer — why a PRIVATE body succeeds where a government agency cannot
trackers.desc: THE ARGUMENT FOR USING A LAND TRUST RATHER THAN A PUBLIC AGENCY, stated by one of them: PRIVATE STATUS IS AN IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE FROM OTHER LAND PROTECTION AGENCIES SUCH AS CONSERVATION AUTHORITIES, AND MUNICIPAL, PROVINCIAL AND FEDERAL PARKS. GOVERNMENT AGENCIES OFTEN HAVE ENFORCEMENT POWERS THAT SOME LANDOWNERS FIND THREATENING, AND GOVERNMENT BUDGET CUTS HAVE UNDERMINED SOME DONORS' CONFIDENCE IN THEIR LONG-TERM COMMITMENT. AS PRIVATE ENTITIES WITH NO GOVERNMENT AUTHORITY OR POWER, LAND TRUSTS ATTRACT A WIDE RANGE OF DONORS AND VOLUNTEERS. Canada had four acquisition entries against 54 total. Having no enforcement power is what makes a land trust approachable to a suspicious owner — the exact opposite of the assumption that more authority helps, and the answer to the Romanian distrust recorded in batch504. AND HOW THEY WORK: LAND TRUSTS WORK MAINLY THROUGH SECURING LAND BY PURCHASE OR DONATION OR BY ACQUIRING AN EASEMENT THROUGH THE SAME MEANS. AN EASEMENT IS AN INTEREST IN THE LAND THAT PROHIBITS CERTAIN ACTIVITIES SUCH AS NEW STRUCTURES, DEVELOPMENT, TREE CUTTING AND DRAINAGE PROJECTS. After securement they care for the land, FOR EXAMPLE INVASIVE SPECIES REMOVAL. AND THE TAX HISTORY THAT MADE IT CHEAP, which is worth knowing when arguing for such a regime elsewhere: an easement power extended TO ALL QUALIFIED LAND TRUSTS in 1994 GREATLY REDUCED COSTS AND GAVE THE LANDOWNER A TAX INCENTIVE TO AGREE TO PROTECTION, and later measures RELIEVED LAND TRUSTS OF MUNICIPAL TAXES FOR QUALIFYING PROPERTIES.

trackers.name: Keeping the land while giving it away — remainder interests and reserved life estates
trackers.desc: THE OPTION MOST OWNERS DO NOT KNOW EXISTS, and it removes the commonest objection to donating: AN OUTRIGHT DONATION IS NOT THE ONLY WAY TO GIVE LAND. YOU CAN CONTINUE TO LIVE ON THE LAND OR USE IT BY DONATING A REMAINDER INTEREST AND RETAINING A RESERVED LIFE ESTATE. An owner can give the land away and go on living on it for the rest of their life — which turns 'I can't afford to move' into a solvable problem rather than a refusal. AND THE TAX TERMS THAT MAKE THE GIFT WORTH MAKING: the federal programme CAN PROVIDE SIGNIFICANT CANADIAN TAX BENEFITS FOR DONATING ECOLOGICALLY-SENSITIVE LAND, and these include THE ELIMINATION OF ANY TAXABLE CAPITAL GAINS AND A CARRY-FORWARD PERIOD OF TEN YEARS TO CLAIM THE DONATION ON YOUR TAXES. Ten years to use the tax receipt means a modest-income owner can still absorb the benefit of a large gift — the detail that decides whether an ordinary landowner can afford to be generous. The programme HAS HELPED PROTECT THOUSANDS OF HECTARES OF LAND ACROSS CANADA. AND THE OTHER ROUTE OFFERED ALONGSIDE: the trust CAN ACCEPT THE DONATION OF CONSERVATION EASEMENT AGREEMENTS, EITHER DIRECTLY OR THROUGH THE ECOLOGICAL GIFTS PROGRAM, with detailed guidance published by the provincial land trust alliance and a named federal handbook.

trackers.name: Réseau de milieux naturels protégés (RMN) — Québec conservation network
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the Québec network of conservation organisations — national, regional and local groups, plus municipalities and MRCs — supporting voluntary conservation of natural areas on PRIVATE land across the province. Members protect somewhere between 66,000 and 80,000 hectares, and RMN maintains the Répertoire des sites de conservation volontaire du Québec, which has passed 1,500 registered protected sites covering roughly 75,000 hectares. USE IT: the site carries a search tool to find a conservation organisation near you, which is the fastest route in — you do not need to know which group covers your area. Worth knowing: more than 40 Québec municipalities and MRCs conserve natural areas voluntarily, so a municipal approach is a real option here in a way it is not in most provinces.

trackers.name: RMN — Accélérer la conservation dans le sud du Québec (ACSQ), $144 million
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a $144 million Québec programme aimed at southern Québec — the part of the province where biodiversity is both richest and most threatened. Four streams, and the shape of them matters: $100 MILLION for conserving natural areas INCLUDING THE ACQUISITION OF PRIVATE LAND, by real right or by conservation servitude; $8.65 million for knowledge-building and awareness work on sites of interest WITH A VIEW TO EVENTUAL ACQUISITION; and $870,000 to help owners get natural reserves recognised. WHO IT SUITS: Québec conservation organisations and their partners, with explicit intent to work more closely with the Indigenous conservation movement. HOW IT DIFFERS: the knowledge stream funds the survey and case-building BEFORE a purchase — so a site you cannot yet afford to buy can still be worked up now.

trackers.name: The Nature Trust of British Columbia
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a non-profit land conservation organisation that BUYS ecologically significant private land in BC and manages it — more than 500 parcels acquired since 1971, over 180,000 acres (73,000 ha) protected, with regional land managers stationed across the province. Carries no debt and no mortgages. USE IT: the strategic point is the inverse of what you might expect. Only about 6% of BC's land base is privately owned — but a DISPROPORTIONATE share of at-risk species and ecosystems sit in the low valley bottoms and coastal lowlands where that private land is concentrated. So a small privately-held parcel in a valley bottom can matter far more than its size suggests, and it is exactly the kind of site the Trust assembles into larger conservation complexes with partners and government.

trackers.name: Land Trust Alliance of British Columbia (LTABC)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the provincial alliance representing around 35 land trust members across British Columbia (roughly 100 including associate members — consultants, environmental groups and individuals). Founded 1997. BC land trusts have between them protected well over a million acres. USE IT: LTABC takes direct approaches — its own invitation is to TALK TO THEM ABOUT A PROPERTY YOU WOULD LIKE TO PROTECT THROUGH A LAND DONATION OR CONSERVATION COVENANT — so you do not need to identify the right member trust yourself; start here and be routed. Its published guidance is unusually practical, including Greening Your Title, a guide to conservation covenants, and Green Legacies on planned giving, which is the route when a landowner wants to leave land protected rather than sell it now. Its news coverage extends to Alberta as well as BC.

trackers.name: HCTF Habitat Acquisition Grants — money to buy private land (BC)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: grants of $100,000 and up to LAND TRUSTS, COMMUNITY ORGANISATIONS AND FIRST NATIONS to PURCHASE private property protecting fish and wildlife habitat in British Columbia. One intake a year, deadline in April. WHO IT SUITS: know where the money comes from, because it decides what gets funded — the grant is paid for by LICENCE SURCHARGE FEES FROM HUNTERS, ANGLERS, TRAPPERS AND GUIDE OUTFITTERS, and from 2026 the stated priorities are lands providing PUBLIC ACCESS for fishing, hunting and non-motorised recreation, wetland or grassland conservation, and large properties with values such as ungulate winter range. A no-access habitat purchase is a weak fit here; frame the access case honestly or look elsewhere. Proposals are scored on species richness, connectivity, planning priority and IMPENDING THREATS — that last criterion is where a live development proposal counts in your favour. Applications only through their Survey Apply system; email is refused.

trackers.name: HCTF — all grant programmes, amounts and deadlines (BC)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the Habitat Conservation Trust Foundation (est. 1981, trustee of the Habitat Conservation Trust under the BC Wildlife Act) runs a ladder of grants, and the smaller rungs are the ones a new group can actually reach. COMMUNITY GRANTS up to $10k for volunteer-driven hands-on work, deadline February. SEED GRANTS up to $10k for proposal development, scoping and technical work — that is money to BUILD a bigger application, deadline November. CAPACITY GRANTS for early-stage planning and skills. LAND STEWARDSHIP GRANTS $10k–$60k for managing NGO-held conservation properties, but note the cycle is EVERY THREE YEARS, so missing it costs you three. WHO IT SUITS: provincial and municipal governments, First Nations, academic institutions, NGOs, industry and community groups. HOW IT DIFFERS: the Seed Grant route means you do not need a finished proposal to start — get funded to write the real one.

trackers.name: Canadian Environmental Law Association (CELA) — Ontario legal aid clinic
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a specialty legal aid clinic funded by Legal Aid Ontario (est. 1970) that will ACT AT HEARINGS AND IN COURT on behalf of citizens or citizens' groups, with nearly 50 years of groundbreaking cases. WHO IT SUITS: Ontario residents and groups for whom cost is the barrier — representation is free for those who qualify on means.

trackers.name: Ontario Land Trust Alliance — find a land trust
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a registered charity representing the network of land trusts across Ontario, with a searchable directory of members — community-based non-profits that protect natural landscapes, agricultural land and cultural heritage features. More than 85,000 acres protected through Ontario land trusts to date. USE IT: start with the directory to find the trust covering your area rather than approaching a national body. Note the Associate category takes in CONSERVATION AUTHORITIES AND MUNICIPALITIES as well as charities, so the directory can also tell you which public bodies in your area already hold a conservation mandate — useful when you need a local institution to take on a site.

trackers.name: Conservation Ontario — the 36 watershed Conservation Authorities
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the network of Ontario's 36 CONSERVATION AUTHORITIES — local watershed management agencies formed jointly by the province and municipalities under the Conservation Authorities Act 1946, mandated to conserve, restore and manage water, land and natural habitat on a watershed basis. USE IT: unlike a land trust, an authority is a public body with a statutory footing that CONTRIBUTES TO MUNICIPAL PLANNING PROCESSES — so where a development affects floodplain, wetland or watercourse, the relevant authority is a formal participant in the decision, not an outside objector. Find the authority for your watershed and check its position before framing your own. TIMING CAUTION: a provincial proposal to consolidate authority boundaries regionally is live, so confirm which body currently covers your area rather than relying on an older map.

trackers.name: Greenlands Conservation Partnership — land acquisition grants (OLTA)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY (to buy the land): the Greenlands Conservation Partnership, run by the Ontario Land Trust Alliance with the Nature Conservancy of Canada, funds land acquisition — fee simple or conservation easement — plus the associated costs of acquisition, and restoration, stewardship and outreach on land already secured. Ontario invested CAD 38 million between 2020 and 2024 and renewed it with CAD 20 million over four more years. READ THE MATCH RULE FIRST: projects need CAD 2.00 of non-provincial investment for every CAD 1.00 of provincial funds, and must have some form of public access before 18 February 2028 — the access condition does not apply to conservation easement agreements with private landowners. OLTA says to contact it directly if your expected match would fall below 2:1.

trackers.name: CELA lawyer referral list — Ontario lawyers taking environmental cases
trackers.desc: WHO TO CONTACT: the Canadian Environmental Law Association maintains a list of Ontario lawyers practising environmental law who may take cases pro bono or at reduced fee, including firms whose stated practice is municipal and land use planning — which is the specialism a development fight actually needs. Ask for the current list on 416-960-2284 ext 7211 or info@cela.ca. CELA states the list is not a recommendation of any firm, so check each one yourself. CELA itself is funded by Legal Aid Ontario and gives free legal services in environmental justice, representing qualifying low-income and disadvantaged communities in litigation — use its intake form first, and the referral list if you do not qualify.

trackers.name: Toronto and Region Conservation Authority (TRCA) — Greater Toronto Area
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: TRCA owns about 16,000 hectares (40,000 acres) across the Greater Toronto Area and its jurisdiction covers 3,467 square kilometres on a watershed basis. THE POWER THAT MATTERS: when the Toronto-area authorities were merged in 1957 it was given full legal authority to purchase and expropriate land for conservation, alongside provincial legislation making building on floodplains illegal. Few local bodies anywhere hold expropriation power aimed at conservation. USE IT: if a threatened parcel sits in a GTA floodplain or valley system, TRCA is the body that can acquire it and the one whose floodplain mapping can stop a build outright.

trackers.name: Toronto Environmental Alliance — City of Toronto
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a non-profit formed in 1988 that acts as an environmental watchdog at Toronto City Hall — the level at which a development is approved or refused — campaigning on urban environmental problems and working with individuals, community groups and local residents on local issues. USE IT: for a fight over a specific Toronto site, City Hall is the decision point, and TEA is the standing presence there that a one-off residents' group is not.

trackers.name: Southern Alberta Land Trust Society (SALTS)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a rancher-led, landowner-driven land trust holding CONSERVATION EASEMENTS across Alberta's Eastern Slopes, prairie and foothills — roughly Red Deer south to the US border, the South Saskatchewan River Basin. It accepts donated easements and issues charitable tax receipts (cash, gift and split receipts), and in extraordinary circumstances may consider PURCHASING an easement. USE IT: its stated purpose is supporting landowners who want to keep remaining grassland in grazing rather than see it converted to uses that permanently undermine its benefits — so for Alberta grassland threatened with conversion, this is a direct fit. Be aware they apply an assessment guide and there are grounds on which they will decline an easement; strong landowner representation on the board means the rancher's position carries weight.

trackers.name: The Conservation Trust (Manitoba) — provincial endowment funding
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a Manitoba fund delivered by Manitoba Habitat Conservancy and supported by the Province, drawn from a $204 million provincial endowment that also created the GROW and Wetland GROW Trusts. Since 2019 it has invested close to $1.5 million into conservation projects with the Nature Conservancy of Canada alone. Funding categories cover Habitat and Wildlife, Innovation, Conservation Planning, and Connecting People with Nature. WHO IT SUITS: Manitoba habitat, wildlife, water and soil conservation work. HOW IT DIFFERS: endowment-backed, so it is not dependent on annual budget rounds the way most government programmes are. NOTE: described here via NCC's own site; Manitoba Habitat Conservancy's own domain not verified this session.

trackers.name: Nature Saskatchewan — stewardship, sanctuaries and easement support
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: Saskatchewan's provincial nature society (since 1949), holding nature sanctuaries and running the Stewards of Saskatchewan programmes — Operation Burrowing Owl, Shrubs for Shrikes, Plovers on Shore and Rare Plant Rescue — which work with landowners on species-at-risk habitat. READ THIS LIMIT FIRST: by its own statement NATURE SASKATCHEWAN DOES NOT ACTIVELY PURSUE THE HOLDING OF CONSERVATION EASEMENTS. It explains them and will give logistical support to a landowner who wants to establish one, but you will need a different holder — in Saskatchewan an easement can be held by a conservation organisation, a government agency OR A RURAL MUNICIPALITY, which is a route worth remembering where no trust is active. USE IT: the other reason to contact them is evidential — they collect biodiversity information that is used in assessing the environmental impact of land development, so if you need documented species records for a threatened site, this is where they are.

trackers.name: Nova Scotia Nature Trust
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the province's only conservation charity dedicated solely to Nova Scotian land, protecting it either by CONSERVATION AGREEMENT with a private landowner or by ACQUIRING THE LAND ITSELF, in perpetuity — more than 200 sites over 30 years. USE IT: the reason a land trust matters more here than almost anywhere else in Canada is ownership. By the Trust's own account 65% of Nova Scotia and 85% OF ITS COASTLINE ARE PRIVATELY OWNED, against roughly 90% public ownership across the rest of the country. Provincial protected-area designation simply cannot reach most Nova Scotian land, so if a coastal or old-forest site is threatened here, a private conservation agreement or purchase is often the ONLY route — not a fallback.

trackers.name: Nova Scotia Environment — private land conservation
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the province's own page on securing ecologically significant private land, noting that SEVERAL PROVINCIAL STATUTES enable private land protection and that the department works in partnership with the Nova Scotia Nature Trust on conservation projects. USE IT: to identify which provincial statutory instrument fits your parcel before approaching anyone — the route differs by mechanism, and a landowner who already wants to protect their land may qualify for a designation rather than needing a sale.

trackers.name: Nature Trust of New Brunswick
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a provincial land trust (formed 1987) that conserves and stewards PRIVATE land in New Brunswick, holding more than 100 nature preserves including entire islands in the Bay of Fundy. Runs a land stewardship programme with farmers and landowners where the owner commits to conservation measures WITHOUT handing over any control. USE IT: two routes rather than one — outright protection of a parcel, or a stewardship agreement for an owner who wants to keep managing their own land. The Trust also holds land in trust for, and has transferred land to, Indigenous land-conservation groups in the province, so it is a realistic partner where a site has both ecological and territorial significance.

trackers.name: Nature Trust of New Brunswick — land conservation options
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a charitable land trust (est. 1987) that conserves private land in New Brunswick by purchase, donation and conservation easement, now holding around 100 nature preserves — including entire islands in the Bay of Fundy. USE IT: this page is the intake route. They assess EACH PARCEL ON ITS OWN ECOLOGICAL MERITS, so the pitch matters: species at risk found in only a handful of places, wide-ranging species such as Canada lynx, Appalachian hardwood or old Acadian forest, wetlands, rare plant habitat, or areas important for migrating birds and waterfowl breeding. They also run a stewardship programme where a landowner commits to conservation measures WITHOUT handing over any control — the option to raise where an owner is sympathetic but will not sell.

trackers.name: CPAWS Newfoundland & Labrador
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the provincial chapter (founded 2003) of the Canadian Parks and Wilderness Society, working specifically to get NEW terrestrial and marine protected areas established in Newfoundland and Labrador and to hold government to managing existing ones properly. Track record includes advancing the South Coast Fjords National Marine Conservation Area and the Eagle River Watershed protected area. USE IT: this is a designation-focused ally rather than a land trust — Newfoundland has no provincial land trust, and protection here runs through the Wilderness and Ecological Reserves Act and the volunteer advisory council (WERAC) that recommends new reserves. CPAWS-NL tracks the 'A Home for Nature' protected areas plan and the public engagement WERAC is running on ten proposed protected areas, so if your site is near one of them there is an open process to push into rather than a cold start.

trackers.name: Nature Conservancy of Canada — Newfoundland and Labrador
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: NCC's provincial programme, conserving ecologically significant land in Newfoundland and Labrador since 1996 by working with private landowners — including large corporate donations of forest land. USE IT: also the route to an unusual provincial mechanism. NCC works with the STEWARDSHIP ASSOCIATION OF MUNICIPALITIES to get natural areas inside municipal boundaries formally recognised as protected areas, via assessment of local land-management practice and stewardship agreements with the provincial government — over 2,600 hectares of municipal public land recognised so far, and the programme is seeking new municipal partners. If the land you are defending is municipally owned, that is a route no land trust offers.

trackers.name: Island Nature Trust (Prince Edward Island)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: PEI's provincial land trust (est. 1979), acquiring ecologically sensitive land by DONATION, BEQUEST OR PURCHASE and managing it to restore ecological integrity — nearly 13,000 acres across more than a hundred Natural Areas. It also assists private landowners to protect their own properties without transferring them. USE IT: 87% OF PEI IS PRIVATELY OWNED, so almost nothing can be protected without a landowner agreeing, and the Trust is built around that. The teeth are statutory: land it takes on is protected from development IN PERPETUITY under the PEI Natural Areas Protection Act, not merely by contract. It also runs a Stewardship Fund so the long-term maintenance cost of a donated property is covered — worth raising with an owner who worries what happens after they hand it over.

trackers.name: CPAWS Northwest Territories
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the NWT chapter of the Canadian Parks and Wilderness Society, working from conservation science and in collaboration with communities across the territory on conservation planning and stewardship. USE IT: the NWT is where Indigenous-led protection has gone furthest in Canada — Edéhzíe, established with the Dehcho First Nations, was CANADA'S FIRST INDIGENOUS PROTECTED AND CONSERVED AREA, covering more than 14,000 square kilometres, over twice the size of Banff, managed through a management board and Dehcho Indigenous guardians. Live work includes the Slave River Delta IPCA and the Dehcho Land Use Plan. If you are defending land here, the realistic route runs through Indigenous governments and land use planning rather than acquisition.

trackers.name: CPAWS Yukon
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Whitehorse-based chapter of the Canadian Parks and Wilderness Society, working on wilderness protection across the Yukon alongside the territory's 14 First Nations and the Inuvialuit. USE IT: in the Yukon the decisive instrument is LAND USE PLANNING, not land purchase — almost all land is Crown or under settled land claims, so there is no trust to sell to. The precedent to know is the Peel Watershed: in 2017 the SUPREME COURT OF CANADA ruled the Yukon government had to complete meaningful final consultation on a plan protecting 80% of the watershed. CPAWS Yukon tracks the regional planning commissions and pushes for Indigenous Protected and Conserved Areas. The standing risk they flag: mineral development keeps advancing in regions where land use planning has not been completed, so the sequence matters more than the objection.

trackers.name: ANLA + VITAL — national environmental licences
trackers.desc: Colombia's National Environmental Licensing Authority, with VITAL, the single national window where licence files (expedientes) are public. You CAN get: any national-scale project's licence file by name, company or expediente number — the EIA, resolutions, sanctions and modification requests — plus regional authority (CAR) filings routed through the same system. You CAN'T get: full files for some purely municipal permits, and the search interface is exact-match and takes practice. For activists: expediente numbers unlock everything — find the project's LAV/LAM number once and you can track every move the company and the state make, and time interventions to open procedural windows.

trackers.name: Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) — Protección de Datos
trackers.desc: Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) — Protección de Datos — Colombia’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Procuraduría General de la Nación — Acceso a la Información
trackers.desc: National right-to-information guarantor; Colombia’s Procuraduría (Ministerio Público) acts as garante of the Ley de Transparencia 1712/2014 with disciplinary powers — there is no dedicated information commission, Colombia.

trackers.name: Queremos Datos — FOI requests (COL)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); Queremos Datos — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: Dejusticia
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Colombian centre for law, justice and society combining research with strategic litigation on rights, including environmental and territorial rights. WHO IT SUITS: Colombian communities where a project threatens collective or territorial rights.org. DOMAIN NOW VERIFIED — dejusticia.org is confirmed as its own site. Founded 2005 in Bogotá, it litigates and participates in strategic public interest litigation, consolidated a dedicated litigation area in 2016, and won the Tang Prize in Rule of Law (2020). AN UNUSUAL CAPABILITY WORTH KNOWING: it organises trainings for human rights practitioners, government officials AND JUDGES — where the obstacle is judicial unfamiliarity with environmental doctrine, that is an organisation which already runs those trainings.

trackers.name: AIDA — Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional organisation of Latin American environmental legal experts providing FREE legal and scientific support to communities and local groups, using international and inter-American human-rights law. Track record includes stopping a large dam in Mexico, halting clear-cutting of native forest in Chile, and the La Oroya smelter ruling in Peru. WHO IT SUITS: communities whose national system has already failed them and whose fight needs to go to an international body. AIDA works across Latin America, so it may be able to act in your country even if it has no office there — ask.

trackers.name: Resnatur — Reservas Naturales de la Sociedad Civil
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the association that wrote the Reserva Natural de la Sociedad Civil into articles 109 and 110 of Ley 99 de 1993 — still the only private protected-area category inside Colombia's SINAP — and helps owners set reserves up and register them. Registration with Parques Nacionales enters the reserve in the RUNAP, is recorded against the title at the property registry, and is constitutive of rights: under article 11 of Decreto 1996 de 1999 a registered holder gains the right of prior consent to public investments affecting the reserve. LIMIT: under article 332 of the Constitution and article 7 of Ley 685 de 2001 the subsoil and its minerals belong to the State, so registration does not stop a mining or hydrocarbon title being granted underneath. USE IT: to get a threatened parcel registered, and to gain a consent right over state projects on the surface.

trackers.name: Fundepúblico — Fundación para la Defensa del Interés Público
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Colombian public-interest foundation, one of the five environmental law groups that founded AIDA in 1998, working the acción popular and acción de tutela routes that let any citizen defend collective rights to a healthy environment without showing personal injury. WHO IT SUITS: communities and citizens bringing collective-rights actions. DISCLOSE: it also works with the private sector on compensation and habitat-banking instruments, so it is a mixed practice — it is not known to act for proponents against communities, but ask directly about conflicts before you brief it on a live dispute. Its website is also visibly unmaintained, with template markup rendering on the page, so confirm the team is active by phone first.

trackers.name: Fondo Acción — Fondo para la Acción Ambiental y la Niñez
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: administrator of the TFCA Colombia debt-for-nature agreement signed with the United States in 2004, and of the Fondo de Resiliencia para Niñas, Niños y Mujeres, running repeated open convocatorias with published, unusually explicit eligibility rules. WHO IT SUITS: non-profit organisations with legal representation — and the eligible list names Juntas de Acción Comunal, cabildos indígenas and consejos comunitarios alongside NGOs, so an ethnic-territorial authority can apply in its own name. Typical bar is one to two years of legal existence and six months of relevant experience; some windows are open to individuals. Calls are often restricted to named departments, so check the geography first. HOW IT DIFFERS: it publishes the full bases and the list of selected projects, so you can see who actually got funded before you spend a week writing.

trackers.name: COICA — Coordinadora de las Organizaciones Indígenas de la Cuenca Amazónica
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the basin-wide confederation of Amazonian Indigenous organisations, founded to act for 511 Indigenous peoples across the nine Amazon countries, around 66 of them in voluntary isolation or initial contact. It works through one national member organisation per country — in this country that is OPIAC, Organización Nacional de los Pueblos Indígenas de la Amazonía Colombiana — and its governing Council brings those presidents together. Its standing work areas are territorial rights and natural resources, human and sociocultural rights, and international law, and it has issued a formal declaration on the defence of Amazonian Indigenous defenders. USE IT: go to OPIAC first — COICA is the regional weight behind a national organisation, not a direct service. It is the route to carry a territorial case or a threat against leaders from your community into regional and international forums.

trackers.name: Consejo de Redacción
trackers.desc: Colombian investigative network promoting reporting on corruption and public resources.

trackers.name: Colombia Confecamaras (company register)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); Colombia Confecamaras (company register) — the official register of companies and legal entities in Colombia — the primary public record of corporate existence, ownership, directors and filings. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A BENEFICIAL-OWNERSHIP REGISTER: this shows the registered entity, its directors and filings; where a separate beneficial-ownership register exists, use that to reach the real humans behind a shell company.

trackers.name: Constitutional Court of Colombia
trackers.desc: Constitutional Court of Colombia — supreme court (Colombia).

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Justice of Colombia
trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Justice of Colombia — supreme court (Colombia).

trackers.name: SECOP (Colombia Compra Eficiente)
trackers.desc: Colombia's electronic public-procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Colombia, and for how much.

trackers.name: Corte Constitucional
trackers.desc: Official jurisprudence of Colombia's Constitutional Court. · Find here: the case-law (relatoría) of Colombia's Constitutional Court.

trackers.name: DANE
trackers.desc: Colombia's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Colombia.

trackers.name: Función Pública (DAFP)
trackers.desc: Colombia's public-administration department — the Manual del Estado directory of executive entities and the SIGEP asset-and-income declarations of senior officials. — Holds to account: executive entities and senior officials — find the Manual del Estado directory and the SIGEP asset-and-income declarations.

trackers.name: RUES
trackers.desc: Colombia's unified business registry across chambers of commerce. — Holds to account: companies in Colombia — find the unified registry across chambers of commerce of entities and registration data.

trackers.name: FONAM — Fondo Nacional Ambiental
trackers.desc: WHERE THE NATIONAL MONEY SITS: FONAM is a special account-management system of the environment ministry with its own juridical personality and independent patrimony, no administrative structure or staff of its own, and jurisdiction across the whole national territory — so it is a financing vehicle attached to the ministry rather than a grant-making organisation with a programme office, and approaches run through the ministry. Filing window (ventanilla única de radicación) and in-person citizen attention at Calle 37 Nº 8-40, Bogotá, Monday to Friday 8:00–16:00; switchboard +57 601 332 3821, national freephone 018000919301, info@minambiente.gov.co. Corruption reports go separately to soytransparente@minambiente.gov.co.

trackers.name: Colombia's municipal personerías - an autonomous public lawyer in every municipality whose duties include DEFENDING COLLECTIVE INTERESTS, ESPECIALLY THE ENVIRONMENT, filing popular and protection actions for anyone who asks, and promoting citizen oversight committees
trackers.desc: EVERY MUNICIPALITY HAS AN OFFICER WHOSE PUBLISHED DUTY IS TO DEFEND COLLECTIVE INTERESTS, ESPECIALLY THE ENVIRONMENT, BY BRINGING COURT CASES. The municipal officer's listed functions include TO DEFEND THE COLLECTIVE INTERESTS, ESPECIALLY THE ENVIRONMENT, BRINGING AND INTERVENING IN THE JUDICIAL, POPULAR, COMPLIANCE AND GOVERNMENTAL ACTIONS THAT ARE APPROPRIATE BEFORE THE AUTHORITIES; TO BRING, BY DELEGATION OF THE OMBUDSMAN, THE PROTECTION ACTIONS IN THE NAME OF ANY PERSON WHO REQUESTS IT OR WHO IS IN A SITUATION OF DEFENCELESSNESS; TO DEFEND THE RIGHTS AND INTERESTS OF SOCIETY, THROUGH THE POPULAR ACTIONS REQUIRED FOR THEIR PROTECTION; and TO INTERVENE IN THE PROCEEDINGS AND BEFORE THE JUDICIAL OR ADMINISTRATIVE AUTHORITIES WHEN IT CONSIDERS IT NECESSARY FOR THE DEFENCE OF THE JURIDICAL ORDER, THE PUBLIC PATRIMONY OR FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS. A public lawyer in your own town whose job description already includes suing on environmental grounds and filing a protection action for anyone who asks. Ask in writing, cite that function by number, and keep the reply. WHERE THE OFFICE SITS AND WHAT IT IS: municipal and district offices of this kind ARE THE ENTITIES CHARGED WITH EXERCISING ADMINISTRATIVE CONTROL IN THE MUNICIPALITY AND HAVE BUDGETARY AND ADMINISTRATIVE AUTONOMY, exercising the functions of the public ministry conferred by the constitution and statute and those delegated by the national prosecutor's office; the officer acts UNDER THE SUPREME DIRECTION of that national office, which maintains a delegated unit TO COORDINATE THE FUNCTIONS THAT THE OFFICERS MUST FULFIL. Budgetary autonomy matters: this office is not a department of the mayor's administration, and it can act against municipal decisions. If it refuses, the national delegated unit that coordinates these offices is the place to complain. THE OTHER FUNCTIONS WORTH NAMING IN A LETTER: to WATCH OVER COMPLIANCE WITH THE CONSTITUTION, THE LAWS, THE ORDINANCES, THE JUDICIAL DECISIONS AND THE ADMINISTRATIVE ACTS, PROMOTING THE ACTIONS TO WHICH THERE MAY BE PLACE; to ACT IN CIVIL, ADMINISTRATIVE, LABOUR, FAMILY, CRIMINAL, AGRARIAN, MINING AND POLICE PROCEEDINGS; to OVERSEE THE EFFICIENT AND DILIGENT EXERCISE OF THE MUNICIPAL ADMINISTRATIVE FUNCTIONS; to RECEIVE AND PROCESS COMPLAINTS AND CLAIMS ABOUT THE VIOLATION OF CIVIL RIGHTS, POLITICAL LIBERTIES AND SOCIAL GUARANTEES; and to PROMOTE THE CREATION AND FUNCTIONING OF THE CITIZEN AND COMMUNITY OVERSIGHT COMMITTEES. Agrarian and mining proceedings are named among the matters this officer may enter. And the duty to promote citizen oversight committees means a community can ask the office to help it constitute one, rather than doing it alone. THE SCALE OF THE ROLE, AND WHY IT IS UNDER-USED: a published statute of the office, produced with the national prosecutor's office, notes that its functions COULD COME TO BE AT LEAST 1,400. Fourteen hundred functions means nobody in the office knows them all. Bring the numbered function you are relying on, printed, to the first meeting. THE HONEST LIMIT ON ITS DISCIPLINARY POWER: THE DISCIPLINARY POWER OF THE OFFICER SHALL NOT BE EXERCISED WITH RESPECT TO THE MAYOR, THE COUNCILLORS AND THE COMPTROLLER; THAT COMPETENCE CORRESPONDS TO THE NATIONAL PROSECUTOR'S OFFICE, WHICH MAY DISCRETIONALLY DELEGATE IT. Complaints about the mayor go to the regional office of the national prosecutor, not to the municipal officer. Send them there from the start and copy the municipal office, so both records exist.

trackers.name: Colombia's basin councils and corporation boards - seats for COMMUNITY ACTION BOARDS, peasant, indigenous and Afro-Colombian organisations, water operators and small environmental NGOs, with a further NGO seat on the board that grants the licence
trackers.desc: NEIGHBOURHOOD COMMUNITY ACTION BOARDS HAVE A SEAT OF THEIR OWN ON THE BASIN COUNCIL THAT WRITES THE WATERSHED PLAN. Public convocations by regional corporations invite, among others, INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES TRADITIONALLY SETTLED IN THE BASIN, AFRO-COLOMBIAN COMMUNITIES, ORGANISATIONS THAT ASSOCIATE OR UNIONISE PEASANTS, ORGANISATIONS THAT ASSOCIATE OR UNIONISE PRODUCTIVE SECTORS, PERSONS PROVIDING AQUEDUCT AND SEWERAGE SERVICES, NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS WHOSE EXCLUSIVE OBJECT IS THE PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT AND THE RENEWABLE NATURAL RESOURCES, THE COMMUNITY ACTION BOARDS, INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER EDUCATION, MUNICIPAL ADMINISTRATIONS and departments to take part in forming the basin council; the council is THE CONSULTATIVE AND REPRESENTATIVE INSTANCE OF ALL THE ACTORS WHO LIVE AND DEVELOP ACTIVITIES WITHIN THE HYDROGRAPHIC BASIN. Community action boards, peasant organisations, water system operators and small environmental NGOs each hold their own category. Whatever your group already is, one of those categories fits it — and the seat is on the body that helps write the watershed ordering plan. WHAT THE PAPERWORK ACTUALLY ASKS FOR: the published requirements include a CERTIFICATE OF EXISTENCE AND LEGAL REPRESENTATION, a COPY OF THE DOCUMENT OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OR THE ORGAN ACTING IN ITS PLACE RECORDING THE DESIGNATION of the candidate, and a REPORT ON PROJECTS OR ACTIVITIES DEVELOPED IN THE BASIN; for black communities, certification of the community council's location and the inscription of its board and legal representative, and certification on the existence of collective territories legally titled or in process of adjudication in the jurisdiction. A report on what your organisation has already done in the basin is one of three documents. Start keeping that record now, because it is the only item that cannot be produced in a week. WHEN THESE SEATS OPEN: corporations publish convocations by name of basin and list the municipalities of the jurisdiction, sometimes jointly between two or three corporations under a joint commission, and they also publish extensions of the deadline and convocations FOR THE UPDATING OF THE COUNCIL of an already constituted basin. Updating convocations are the second chance. If your basin's council was formed years ago without you, watch for the update notice rather than assuming the door closed. THE SEAT ABOVE THAT ONE: a decree regulates the election of the representatives of the non-governmental environmental organisations BEFORE THE DIRECTIVE COUNCILS OF THE REGIONAL AUTONOMOUS CORPORATIONS AND THE SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT CORPORATIONS, who in turn elect their representative and substitute to the national environmental council; the minister convokes them through the secretary of the corporation's directive council, and the representative and substitute are elected at that meeting, of which minutes are drawn. Environmental organisations hold a seat on the board of the corporation itself, not only on the basin council. That board is the body that grants the licence — so this is the highest seat a small local organisation can realistically reach here. THE PRECEDENT ON STANDING: the constitutional court has recorded that a named person IS LEGITIMATED TO BRING THE PRESENT ACTION OF PROTECTION IN REPRESENTATION OF THE COMMUNITY COUNCIL of a black community AND AGAINST THE REGIONAL AUTONOMOUS CORPORATION. A community council has sued its own regional corporation and been held to have standing. Where the corporation is the problem rather than the remedy, that route exists and has been used.

trackers.name: Colombia's federation of municipalities - a TERRITORIAL ORDERING SERVICE of urbanistic, environmental and legal experts for less than one consultant's fee, three-day training open to actors the mayor designates, a weekly legal bulletin and a threatened-mayors protection programme
trackers.desc: THERE IS A PAID SERVICE OF TERRITORIAL ORDERING EXPERTS THAT WILL SIT WITH YOUR MUNICIPALITY ON ITS LAND USE PLAN, FOR LESS THAN ONE CONSULTANT'S FEE. The federation of municipalities describes it as A SERVICE OF DIRECT AND PERSONALISED ATTENTION WITH THEMATIC EXPERTS IN TERRITORIAL ORDERING WHO WILL PROVIDE ORIENTATION AND TECHNICAL AND JURIDICAL SUPPORT TO THE DIFFERENT PROCESSES OF TERRITORIAL ORDERING DEVELOPED IN THE MUNICIPALITIES, including TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE IN THE PROCESSES OF FORMULATION, REVISION OR MODIFICATION OF THE TERRITORIAL ORDERING PLAN, backed by professionals in URBANISTIC, ENVIRONMENTAL, FINANCIAL, JURIDICAL and other areas, and offered FOR LESS THAN THE VALUE OF THE FEES OF ONE PROFESSIONAL. The land use plan is the document that decides whether a project can be built at all. Experts in environmental and urbanistic questions will help your municipality revise it, and the cost is less than hiring one consultant. WHAT ELSE THAT SERVICE INCLUDES: THREE DAYS OF IN-PERSON TRAINING FOR THE OFFICIALS OR OTHER ACTORS THAT THE MAYOR DESIGNATES OR CONSIDERS, covering INSTRUMENTS OF TERRITORIAL MANAGEMENT, PLANNING AND FINANCING, ENVIRONMENTAL ORDERING, RISK MANAGEMENT, PUBLIC FINANCE, TERRITORIAL GOVERNANCE AND CITIZEN PARTICIPATION; technical support in building up to two budgets for reviewing or implementing plan programmes; and technical accompaniment IN THE FORMULATION OF INVESTMENT PROJECTS FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF RESOURCES, with the funds sought AT DEPARTMENTAL, NATIONAL OR INTERNATIONAL LEVEL. Other actors that the mayor designates can attend the training. Ask to be among them: three days on environmental ordering and citizen participation, at the municipality's expense, is the cheapest technical education available in this file. WHAT THE FEDERATION IS: A JURIDICAL PERSON WITHOUT PROFIT MOTIVE, OF ASSOCIATIVE NATURE AND GUILD CHARACTER, GOVERNED BY PRIVATE LAW, to which ALL THE MUNICIPALITIES, DISTRICTS AND ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES OF THE COUNTRY BELONG BY OWN RIGHT, its purpose being the defence of their interests and the consolidation of DECENTRALISATION AND LOCAL AUTONOMY; its associates by right are THE 1,096 MUNICIPALITIES, 5 DISTRICTS AND APPROXIMATELY 40 SUBNATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES, and annual dues are fixed in minimum wages by municipal category. Every municipality is a member by right, and there are some forty subnational associations of municipalities. That is a ready-made map of which neighbouring councils already meet together. THE TWO SERVICES A CAMPAIGN CAN USE DIRECTLY: the federation produces a weekly MUNICIPAL JURIDICAL BULLETIN WITH THE CONTENT OF THE NORMATIVITY AND JURISPRUDENCE RECENTLY ISSUED, and it runs a PROGRAMME OF PROTECTION OF THREATENED MAYORS, sitting on the national protection unit's special committee, through which protection measures have been assigned to some four hundred local officeholders. If a mayor who backs your community is being threatened, there is a named national programme and the federation sits on the committee that assigns the measures. THE DEPARTMENTAL EQUIVALENT: a national federation of departments INTEGRATES, STRENGTHENS AND REPRESENTS THE DEPARTMENTS BEFORE THE STATE, THE PRIVATE SECTOR AND INTERNATIONAL ORGANISMS, covering all thirty-two. Where the decision sits with the department rather than the municipality, that federation is the equivalent door, and it deals with international bodies on the departments' behalf.

trackers.name: FLACMA - the Latin American federation of cities and municipal associations, open to affiliation by ANY INDIVIDUAL MUNICIPALITY, whose assembly passes resolutions signed by mayors across eighteen countries
trackers.desc: ANY CITY OR MUNICIPALITY IN THE REGION MAY AFFILIATE DIRECTLY, NOT ONLY THROUGH ITS NATIONAL ASSOCIATION. Its membership rule is that MEMBERS ARE ALL THE CITIES, MUNICIPALITIES, NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND MUNICIPALIST INSTITUTIONS OF LATIN AMERICA THAT HAVE EXPRESSED THEIR WILL TO AFFILIATE; it is AN ORGANISATION OF FREE ADHESION THAT REPRESENTS THE 16,132 MUNICIPALITIES, INTENDANCIES AND PREFECTURES, THE CITIES AND THE ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, NETWORKS AND GUILDS OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, and it is the regional section of the world organisation of local governments. A single municipality may join in its own right. Where your national association is captured or inactive, that is a way for one sympathetic town hall to reach the regional table on its own. WHOSE PRESIDENTS SIT ON IT: its published leadership is drawn from the presidents of the national municipal bodies of the region — the federation of municipalities of one southern country, the association of municipalities of another, the Brazilian association of municipalities, the congress of intendants of another, the national federation of municipalities of one large federal country and the association of municipalities of an Andean one — each of them a serving mayor. The people who chair your own national municipal association sit here. A matter raised through that association can be carried into a regional assembly by the same person. WHAT IT SAYS IT IS FOR: TO BE THE VOICE OF LATIN AMERICAN MUNICIPALISM, TO CONSOLIDATE THE LATIN AMERICAN MUNICIPAL ASSOCIATIVE MOVEMENT, TO REPRESENT AND SERVE AS INTERLOCUTOR OF ALL THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND THEIR NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES, and TO PROMOTE IN LATIN AMERICA AUTONOMOUS, STRONG AND DEMOCRATIC LOCAL GOVERNMENTS; it ADHERES TO AND PROMOTES THE WORLD AND REGIONAL CONVENTIONS THAT THE NATIONAL STATES OF THE REGION SUBSCRIBE. Promoting the conventions the states have signed is written into its purpose. Where your country has signed an environmental or rights convention and a municipality is being told to ignore it, that is a body with a standing commitment to the opposite. THE PRECEDENT THAT SHOWS IT TAKES POSITIONS: its general assembly has approved unanimously a declaration on a territorial sovereignty dispute, signed by the president and BY MUNICIPAL AUTHORITIES AND HEADS OF ASSOCIATIONS AND FEDERATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES of eighteen named countries of the region, which also REAFFIRMED THE LEGITIMATE RIGHTS... OVER THE NATURAL RESOURCES OF THE AREA IN QUESTION. The assembly passes resolutions that name natural resources and get signed by mayors across eighteen countries. A community campaign that can be framed as a municipal cause has a forum that has done exactly that before. THE OTHER REGIONAL NETWORKS BESIDE IT: regional analysis names, among the principal associations and networks of local and regional governments with EXPERIENCES, IDEAS AND RESOURCES TO FOSTER INITIATIVES AND PROJECTS LINKED TO SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AT LOCAL LEVEL, a network of Mercosur cities alongside this federation, and global initiatives with regional presence for local sustainability and for city climate action; various cities have prepared VOLUNTARY LOCAL REPORTS on implementing the global development agenda in their territories. A voluntary local report is a document a municipality writes about itself. Getting your community's situation named in one is cheap, public and lasting. THE HONEST NOTE ON REPRESENTATION: the region's representation in the world body has been the subject of negotiations between this federation, the Mercosur cities network and the world organisation to form A LATIN AMERICAN REPRESENTATION THAT IS PLURAL, DIVERSE AND PARTICIPATORY. More than one body claims to speak for the region's municipalities. Approach both this federation and the Mercosur cities network rather than assuming one covers the other.

trackers.name: Mercociudades - a South American city network whose cooperation calls admit UNIVERSITIES AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS as partners alongside two or more municipalities, with an environment and sustainable development unit coordinated by a member city
trackers.desc: UNIVERSITIES AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS CAN BE PARTNERS IN THE COOPERATION PROJECTS THIS CITY NETWORK FUNDS. Its south-south cooperation call is open to MEMBER CITIES AND ASSOCIATED STATES, to universities of a regional university association, and to ORGANISATIONS OF CIVIL SOCIETY; THE PROJECT MUST INVOLVE AT LEAST TWO MEMBER LOCAL GOVERNMENTS OR ASSOCIATED STATES, and THE UNIVERSITIES AND SOCIAL ORGANISATIONS MAY PARTICIPATE AS PARTNER ENTITIES ALONGSIDE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, each city able to stand as coordinator of one proposal and partner in another. Two municipalities and your organisation is a fundable consortium. Where a threatened area straddles two towns, or two towns face the same developer, that is the shape the call is written for. THE THEMATIC UNIT THAT COVERS LAND AND WATER: among its seventeen thematic units and four working groups is one for ENVIRONMENT AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT, coordinated by a city with sub-coordinating cities, which has run exchanges on waste, sustainability and circular economy and marked world water day, and has opened AN OPPORTUNITY OF COOPERATION TOGETHER WITH THE UNITED NATIONS ENVIRONMENT PROGRAMME FOR THE STRENGTHENING OF LOCAL CAPACITIES; other units cover AUTONOMY, MANAGEMENT AND PARTICIPATION, HUMAN RIGHTS, URBAN DEVELOPMENT, PLANNING AND METROPOLITAN AREAS and BORDER INTEGRATION. A coordinating city runs each unit, and it is a city like yours rather than a secretariat. Write to the coordinator of the environment unit with your case: that is a mayor's office, not an agency. WHAT THE NETWORK COMMITS ITSELF TO DO: among its statutory objectives are TO CARRY OUT STUDIES AND COLLABORATE IN THE ELABORATION OF PLANS AND STRATEGIES IN THE URBAN-ENVIRONMENTAL AREA, WITH THE OBJECTIVE OF HARMONISING AND COORDINATING THE ACTIONS IN THIS AREA, TO COLLABORATE IN THE PLANNING OF THE POLICIES AND PLANS OF DEVELOPMENT OF THE CITIES, TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE NEED TO IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF LIFE, TO ADVOCATE AND RAISE AWARENESS ABOUT CITIZEN PARTICIPATION AND SOCIAL INCLUSION, and TO IDENTIFY THE CAUSES OF ACCENTUATION OF THE SOCIAL INEQUALITIES, IN ORDER TO PROPOSE AND SUPPORT SOLUTIONS POSSIBLE TO BE EXECUTED BY THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS. Collaborating in city development plans is a stated commitment. A municipality revising its plan can ask the network for that collaboration rather than paying a consultancy. WHO ELSE MAY TAKE PART: THE OTHER INSTANCES OF THE SUB-NATIONAL GOVERNMENTS OF THE COUNTRIES of the two regional blocs THAT EXPRESS THEIR WILL TO DO SO AND WHOSE GOVERNMENTS HAVE BEEN DEMOCRATICALLY ELECTED may participate as collaborators, and COOPERATION WITH CONSORTIA AND ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES WILL BE CARRIED OUT BY MEANS OF AGREEMENTS. Provinces, departments and municipal consortia can join as collaborators. Where the decision sits above the town hall, that tier can be brought to the same table. THE PLATFORM THAT MATCHES NEEDS TO SOLUTIONS: its cooperation programme runs an interactive platform DESIGNED SPECIALLY TO SHARE LOCAL SOLUTIONS... AND TO INTERWEAVE STRENGTHS AND TECHNICAL NEEDS OF CITIES OF ALL SOUTH AMERICA, with a directory of good practices through which member cities HAVE THE POSSIBILITY OF EXCHANGING WITH THE REFERENTS OF SOLUTIONS OF THE CITIES. Post the technical need rather than the complaint. A city that has already solved the same problem is what the platform is built to find.

trackers.name: ICLEI - a sustainability network open to individual councils AND to associations of local governments, giving fee-paying members year-round telephone and email support on designing environment and water projects, plus local biodiversity planning tools and an environmental award
trackers.desc: MEMBERSHIP OF THIS GLOBAL SUSTAINABILITY NETWORK IS OPEN TO ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AS WELL AS TO INDIVIDUAL COUNCILS, AND THE FEE SCALES WITH POPULATION AND NATIONAL INCOME. Its membership page states that AFFILIATION IS OPEN TO ALL LOCAL AND REGIONAL GOVERNMENTS, AS WELL AS TO THEIR WORLD, REGIONAL, NATIONAL AND SUBNATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS, that members MAY VOTE AND PARTICIPATE IN THE GOVERNING ORGANS OF THE WHOLE NETWORK, and that they CONTRIBUTE AN ANNUAL AFFILIATION FEE THAT VARIES REGIONALLY AND ACCORDING TO POPULATION AND GROSS NATIONAL INCOME PER CAPITA. A small municipality pays a small fee and votes in the same network as a capital city. Where a national association is the member, ask whether your council is covered by it already. WHAT A MEMBER ACTUALLY GETS, IN THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT'S OWN WORDS: it SUPPORTS ITS PARTNERS TO FIND SUSTAINABLE SOLUTIONS THROUGH PROJECTS, INITIATIVES AND PROGRAMMES, offers cities and states A PLATFORM TO INTERACT WITH OTHER LOCAL GOVERNMENTS and provides RESOURCES AND TOOLS TO PROMOTE POSITIVE ENVIRONMENTAL, ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL CHANGES; support runs DURING THE YEAR THAT THE FEE LASTS, PERMANENTLY, BY TELEPHONE OR BY EMAIL, and covers THE DESIGN OF PROGRAMMES AND PROJECTS OF SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN THEMES SUCH AS: ENVIRONMENT, WATER, PUBLIC SERVICES, ENERGY EFFICIENCY, SOLID WASTE. Joining requires A REQUEST TO THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT addressed to the named regional secretary, plus a membership form. Permanent telephone and email support on designing water and environment projects, for one annual fee. That is a standing technical helpline for a town hall that has none. THE BIODIVERSITY WORK THAT MATTERS FOR LAND: its recorded local biodiversity work is TO PROMOTE THE BIODIVERSITY STRATEGIES OF THE STATE AND MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENTS, AS WELL AS THEIR ACTION PLANS, AND ALSO TO REINFORCE THE CAPACITIES OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS TO INCORPORATE BIODIVERSITY INTO THE PLANNING PROCESSES, and it notes that MORE MONETARY RESOURCES ARE INVESTED GLOBALLY IN BIODIVERSITY AT LOCAL AND SUBNATIONAL LEVEL THAN AT NATIONAL LEVELS; a member municipality has launched an urban biodiversity index, and a global initiative on NATURE IN URBAN PLANNING is promoted through the network. Incorporating biodiversity into planning processes is the exact point at which a project is stopped or waved through. Ask the secretariat which of its tools your municipality can adopt in its next plan revision. THE RECOGNITION THAT GIVES A COUNCIL A REASON: the regional secretariat runs an award for local governments THAT HAVE CARRIED OUT ACTIONS IN FAVOUR OF THE PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT IN THEMES OF CLIMATE CHANGE, BIODIVERSITY, ENERGY EFFICIENCY, MOBILITY, AMONG OTHERS, open to municipalities, city boroughs and federal entities. An award with a biodiversity category. A council weighing whether to protect a site has a public reason to do so, and the application is a deadline you can work to. THE OFFICES THAT COVER THIS REGION: there is a secretariat for one large federal country together with Central America and the Caribbean, and a separate South American secretariat, each publishing member lists that include municipalities of several countries. Two regional offices cover the whole file. Write to the one for your subregion rather than to the global body.

trackers.name: Colombia's territorial associative schemes - 66 already registered, public-law bodies with patrimony INDEPENDENT of the member councils, able to receive delegated national attributions with resources and to exercise territorial ordering functions
trackers.desc: SIXTY-SIX TERRITORIAL ASSOCIATIONS ARE ALREADY REGISTERED NATIONALLY, EACH A PUBLIC-LAW BODY WITH ITS OWN PATRIMONY. The statute provides that THE ASSOCIATIONS OF TERRITORIAL ENTITIES WILL BE FORMED FREELY BY TWO OR MORE TERRITORIAL ENTITIES TO PROVIDE JOINTLY PUBLIC SERVICES, ADMINISTRATIVE FUNCTIONS PROPER OR ASSIGNED TO THE TERRITORIAL ENTITY BY THE NATIONAL LEVEL, EXECUTE WORKS OF COMMON INTEREST OR FULFIL FUNCTIONS OF PLANNING, AS WELL AS TO PROCURE THE INTEGRAL DEVELOPMENT OF THEIR TERRITORIES, and that associations of departments, provinces and associations of districts and municipalities ARE ADMINISTRATIVE ENTITIES OF PUBLIC LAW, WITH JURIDICAL PERSONALITY AND PATRIMONY OF THEIR OWN AND INDEPENDENT OF THE ENTITIES THAT COMPOSE THEM. As of one recent count A TOTAL OF 66 TERRITORIAL ASSOCIATIVE SCHEMES HAVE BEEN REGISTERED with the interior ministry. Sixty-six already exist, and the patrimony is independent of the member councils. Land or funds held by one of these does not sit at the mercy of a single mayor. WHO MAY CREATE ONE, AND WHO MAY NOT: the national guidance is explicit that these schemes MUST BE CONSTITUTED BY TERRITORIAL ENTITIES, SO THAT THE ONLY FACULTY FOR THE CREATION OF A TERRITORIAL ASSOCIATIVE SCHEME LIES WITH THE MAYORS OF THE MUNICIPALITIES OR THE GOVERNORS OF THE DEPARTMENTS. A community cannot create one. The whole task is persuading two mayors, or a mayor and a governor, to sign — so build the case for them, not for a ministry. THE SEVEN FORMS AVAILABLE: the schemes are THE ADMINISTRATIVE AND PLANNING REGIONS, THE PLANNING AND MANAGEMENT REGIONS, THE ASSOCIATIONS OF DEPARTMENTS, THE METROPOLITAN AREAS, THE ASSOCIATIONS OF SPECIAL DISTRICTS, THE ADMINISTRATIVE AND PLANNING PROVINCES, AND THE ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES; territorial entities may also continue associating THROUGH THE CELEBRATION OF INTER-ADMINISTRATIVE AGREEMENTS. Seven forms, from two neighbouring towns to a whole region. Pick the lightest one that covers the territory in question rather than the grandest. WHAT THE NATIONAL LEVEL CAN HAND THEM: THE NATION AND THE ORGANS OF THE CENTRAL LEVEL MAY DELEGATE IN THE TERRITORIAL ENTITIES OR IN THE DIFFERENT TERRITORIAL ASSOCIATIVE SCHEMES, BY MEANS OF AGREEMENTS, ATTRIBUTIONS PROPER TO THE ORGANISMS AND PUBLIC ENTITIES OF THE NATIONAL LEVEL, the delegated competences being written into the inter-administrative agreement with the corresponding assignment of resources; the schemes may PROVIDE JOINTLY PUBLIC SERVICES, FULFIL ADMINISTRATIVE FUNCTIONS... EXECUTE WORKS OF COMMON INTEREST OR FULFIL FUNCTIONS OF PLANNING, TERRITORIAL ORDERING AND MANAGEMENT. Territorial ordering is a named function these bodies may exercise, and national attributions can be delegated to them with money attached. That is the argument for creating one where planning decisions keep being taken elsewhere. THE PHRASE THAT MATTERS FOR A PROTECTED AREA: the same statute names among the matters of national interest THE PROTECTED AREAS AND THE SYSTEM OF NATURAL NATIONAL PARKS. Protected areas are listed as a matter of national interest in the same law that creates these bodies. That connection is worth citing when asking a scheme to take on a conservation function. THE REGISTRY AND THE CHECK IT PERFORMS: registered schemes must appear in a national register of associative schemes; during registration THE NATIONAL PLANNING DEPARTMENT CARRIES OUT A VERIFICATION OF THE MINIMUM CONTENTS required by the regulation, and it publishes a frequently asked questions service and an associativity kit. Read the minimum contents before the councils draft anything. Most refusals at registration are for missing clauses, not for the idea.

trackers.name: Fundo Casa Socioambiental - a small-grants fund for community groups across South America that funds groups WITHOUT LEGAL PERSONALITY through a partner organisation, with calls prioritising repeatedly rejected and newly formed groups
trackers.desc: A GROUP WITH NO LEGAL PERSONALITY AT ALL CAN RECEIVE A GRANT, BY BORROWING ANOTHER ORGANISATION'S.
