THE REGIONAL ORGANISATION BEHIND AFRO-CENTRAL AMERICAN CLAIMS: a Black Central American organisation WAS BORN IN DANGRIGA, BELIZE, ON AUGUST 25, 1995, WITH THE PURPOSE OF ESTABLISHING A CROSS-BORDER ORGANIZATION CAPABLE OF MAKING VISIBLE AND STRENGTHENING THE SOCIAL, POLITICAL, ECONOMIC, CULTURAL, ENVIRONMENTAL AND ORGANIZATIONAL LIFE OF THE AFRO-CENTRAL AMERICAN COMMUNITIES and those in the diaspora, and is described as THE ONLY ORGANIZATION OF ITS KIND, holding annual assemblies since its foundation; it STRENGTHENS THE POPULATION'S INSTITUTIONAL DEVELOPMENT THROUGH THE ESTABLISHMENT OF COORDINATION MECHANISMS AND INTER-INSTITUTIONAL SUPPORT. A cross-border body for Garifuna, Creole and Black communities from Belize to Panama. Where the same people are split by a national border, that is the organisation that can carry a claim on both sides. WHAT ITS MEMBER ORGANISATIONS ARE, BY COUNTRY: recorded members include national Garifuna and Creole councils and an educational foundation in one country, Black organisations and a Black women's organisation in another, a community and ethnic development organisation in a third, a Garifuna organisation and a coast development association in a fourth, a Caribbean project association and an Afro-Costa Rican women's centre in a fifth, and an Afro-Panamanian response body, an Afro-Panamanian women's network and an ethnic museum association in a sixth, plus diaspora organisations. Each is a real, named organisation in a named country. Find the one nearest you rather than writing to the regional body first. WHAT ITS ASSEMBLIES HAVE WORKED ON: recorded agendas include MAPPING AND INVENTORY OF RESOURCES IN THE AFRO-CENTRAL AMERICAN COMMUNITIES, land tenure, participation of Afro communities in the local economy, and guaranteeing AT THE HIGHEST LEVEL THE PARTICIPATION OF THE AFRO-CENTRAL AMERICAN COMMUNITIES AND POPULATIONS WITHIN THE MESOAMERICAN BIOLOGICAL CORRIDOR INITIATIVE; one assembly recorded a DECLARATION OF DENUNCIATION BEFORE THE INTER-AMERICAN COMMISSION ON HUMAN RIGHTS. It has taken a denunciation to the inter-American commission before. Ask the national member how that was done and what it produced. THE HONEST CURRENCY WARNING: much of the accessible documentation of this network's membership and assemblies dates from the 2000s, though it remains listed as a member of a contemporary regional alliance and holds recent assemblies. Verify who currently leads it and which organisations are still members before relying on the list. The national members are the durable part; the regional office is not always reachable.

trackers.name: International Land Coalition, Latin America and the Caribbean - a regional platform of 61 member organisations across 20+ countries supporting MORE THAN 30 NATIONAL LAND COALITIONS, with a defender-protection commitment signed by every member and an independent land governance index
trackers.desc: MORE THAN THIRTY NATIONAL LAND COALITIONS EXIST, AND THEY ARE BROAD PLATFORMS THAT A LOCAL ORGANISATION CAN JOIN. The coalition SUPPORTS MORE THAN 30 NATIONAL LAND COALITIONS, described as BROAD PLATFORMS OF MEMBERS AND ALLIES THAT WORK IN FAVOUR OF land rights; its regional platform BRINGS TOGETHER 61 MEMBER ORGANISATIONS OF LOCAL, NATIONAL AND REGIONAL CIVIL SOCIETY OF DIVERSE PROFILES: GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS (SMALL PRODUCERS, PEASANTS, INDIGENOUS), WOMEN'S ORGANISATIONS AND/OR THOSE FOCUSED ON THIS SECTOR, NGOs, RESEARCH OR ACADEMIC CENTRES, AND ORGANISATIONS SPECIALISED IN KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT, drawn from MORE THAN 20 COUNTRIES, within a global membership of nearly three hundred in eighty-one countries. A grassroots organisation sits in the same platform as the research centres and the NGOs. Ask whether your country has a national coalition: that is the room where land conflicts get compared and carried upward. THE TWO COMMITMENTS EVERY MEMBER SIGNS: ALL THE MEMBERS OF THE coalition SIGN TWO IMPORTANT COMMITMENTS THAT PROTECT AND EMPOWER BOTH WOMEN AND LAND DEFENDERS WITHIN OUR NETWORK. Defender protection is a membership condition, not an optional programme. If members of your community are threatened, that commitment is something you can invoke by name. THE DATA TOOL THAT MEASURES YOUR GOVERNMENT: the coalition runs a land governance index whose data officer records that it REVEALS WORRYING TRENDS IN LAND GOVERNANCE and shows THE GAPS IN THE MONITORING THAT GOVERNMENTS CARRY OUT ON LAND GOVERNANCE, AND HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM THE WAY IN WHICH WOMEN AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, AMONG OTHER ACTORS, EXPERIENCE THAT GOVERNANCE; recorded country findings include one Caribbean island where THE INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES HAVE LITTLE ROOM FOR MANOEUVRE TO DECIDE ON THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROJECTS THAT AFFECT THEIR TERRITORIES, SINCE PRIOR CONSULTATION IS APPLIED DEFICIENTLY, one Central American country where only 3.18% OF A BUDGET OF USD 184 MILLION reached family farming while THE CRISIS FACED BY LAND DEFENDERS... IS PERPETUATED BY THE STATE IN ALLIANCE WITH THE CORPORATIONS WITH INTEREST IN THEIR TERRITORIES, and another with AN ALARMING DISPOSSESSION OF LANDS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND AFRO-DESCENDANT COMMUNITIES, BECAUSE OF THE EXPANSION OF THE AGRICULTURAL FRONTIER. An independent index that contradicts the government's own monitoring, country by country. Quote your country's score back at the ministry that claims consultation works. THE LAND DEAL DATABASE AND ITS REGIONAL FOCAL POINT: a global land acquisitions observatory names a regional focal point organisation for Latin America and coordinates national pilot land observatories in several countries with the coalition. If a large land acquisition has been announced near you, check whether it is already recorded there — and if it is not, the focal point is who records it. WHAT ITS OWN ANALYSIS SAYS ABOUT THIS REGION: land IS AT THE CENTRE OF DIVERSE CONFLICTS IN THE REGION, WHERE THE HIGHEST NUMBER OF ATTACKS AGAINST THE PEOPLE WHO DEFEND IT IS RECORDED, LINKED IN GREAT MEASURE TO THE EXTRACTIVE INDUSTRIES; the coalition works THROUGH THE PROMOTION OF REGIONAL PLATFORMS AND NATIONAL COALITIONS... SO THAT THE WOMEN, MEN AND COMMUNITIES WHO LIVE ON AND FROM THE LAND HAVE DECISION-MAKING POWER OVER THEIR LANDS AND TERRITORIES. The region with the most attacks on land defenders is the one you are in. Read this entry with the protection funds and the pro bono routes already filed.

trackers.name: The Global Alliance of Territorial Communities and its Shandia platform - direct funding channelled to territorial organisations' own financial mechanisms, with FISCAL SPONSORSHIP and financial capacity support where an organisation cannot yet receive funds, plus named community-led funds already re-granting
trackers.desc: IF A COMMUNITY ORGANISATION HAS NO WAY TO RECEIVE INTERNATIONAL MONEY, THIS PLATFORM SAYS IT WILL FIND IT A FISCAL SPONSOR. Its published design states that regional and national component funding WILL BE CHANNELLED TO alliance member organisations, that those members WILL DETERMINE HOW REGIONAL/NATIONAL FUNDS WILL BE USED, CHANNELLED AND ADMINISTERED, USING THEIR OWN REGIONAL/NATIONAL FINANCIAL MECHANISMS, and that IF A REGIONAL/NATIONAL indigenous or local community ORGANISATION REQUIRES A FISCAL SPONSOR, THEY WILL BE SUPPORTED IN THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE FUNDS, AND PROVIDED CAPACITY BUILDING SUPPORT ON FINANCIAL management. The commonest reason a community group is refused international funding is that it cannot receive or account for the money. This platform treats that as the thing to fix rather than a reason to refuse. WHAT THE PLATFORM IS FOR: it is OUR COMMON PLATFORM TO PROMOTE AND FACILITATE DIRECT, PREDICTABLE, EFFECTIVE, AND SUSTAINABLE FUNDING FOR INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES THROUGH THE ESTABLISHMENT OF DIRECT REGIONAL AND NATIONAL FUNDING MECHANISMS, CAPACITY-BUILDING, EXCHANGE OF EXPERIENCES, AND ENHANCED DIALOGUE WITH DONORS; for the communities behind it, DIRECT FINANCING IS MORE THAN JUST MONETARY SUPPORT — IT IS A VITAL TOOL FOR SECURING OUR FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS... TO LIVE ON OUR LANDS, EXERCISE FREE, PRIOR, AND INFORMED CONSENT, PRESERVE AND ADAPT OUR TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE, AND LIVE FREE FROM VIOLENCE. Direct means the money does not pass through an intermediary NGO that takes the overhead and the decisions. Ask any donor offering to fund your community whether it can pay through one of these mechanisms. THE FUNDS THAT ALREADY EXIST UNDER IT: named community-led mechanisms include a Mesoamerican territorial fund, an Amazonian fund led by the Brazilian Amazon indigenous coordination, a fund launched by the national Brazilian indigenous articulation DEVELOPED THROUGH A COLLABORATIVE PROCESS LED BY a national forum of indigenous leaders and a fund working group, REFLECT[ING] A STRONG COMMITMENT TO DEMOCRATIC AND TRADITIONAL GOVERNANCE PRACTICES, a quilombola fund, a fund led by a movement of babassu coconut breaker women, and further funds in Asia that have BEGUN RE-GRANTING IN SIX COUNTRIES, FOCUSING ON INDIGENOUS WOMEN, YOUTH, AND PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES and working to REACH REMOTE COMMUNITIES, SIMPLIFY GRANT ACCESS, BUILD CAPACITY. Several of these funds re-grant to communities in their own region. Ask which one covers your country and whether it has an open window — they are separate from the alliance itself. WHO THE ALLIANCE IS: A COALITION OF INDIGENOUS AND LOCAL COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS FROM MESOAMERICA, AMAZONIA, AFRICA AND ASIA, PROTECTING MORE THAN 958 MILLION HECTARES OF TROPICAL FORESTS and representing 35 MILLION PEOPLE FROM FOREST TERRITORIES IN 24 COUNTRIES, made up of five named networks including the Amazon basin coordination, the Mesoamerican forest peoples alliance and the national Brazilian indigenous articulation; the Mesoamerican alliance's own members are listed by name, from national forestry alliances to named indigenous nations and general congresses. Your national organisation is probably already inside this structure through one of the five networks. Trace the chain upward before assuming you need a new relationship. THE EXCHANGES IT RUNS BETWEEN TERRITORIES: recorded exchanges include Brazilian community funds invited to Mesoamerica to bring their experience to the grassroots of the alliance there, and a delegation from eight African countries meeting Brazilian community fund experts for nine days in indigenous communities; one review recorded honestly that grassroots organisations in that African network STILL HAVE LIMITED, THOUGH GROWING, CAPACITY TO REQUEST AND MANAGE RESOURCES FROM INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION. That honesty is useful. If your organisation cannot yet manage an international grant, say so and ask for the capacity support first — it is a stated part of the offer, not a disqualification.

trackers.name: Business & Human Rights Resource Centre - invites companies to answer a community's allegation and PUBLISHES THE NON-RESPONSE on the company's own page, with regional researchers, investor escalation and published policy and benchmark data on 10,000+ companies
trackers.desc: A COMPANY'S REFUSAL TO ANSWER A COMMUNITY'S ALLEGATION IS ITSELF PUBLISHED, ON ITS OWN PAGE. The centre INVITE[S] COMPANIES TO RESPOND TO ALLEGATIONS OF MISCONDUCT AND PUBLISH[ES] THEIR COMMENTS, doing so WHEN WE FIND NO EVIDENCE THAT THEY HAVE OTHERWISE RESPONDED TO THE CONCERNS; the process ENCOURAGES COMPANIES TO PUBLICLY ADDRESS HUMAN RIGHTS CONCERNS, AND PROVIDES THE PUBLIC WITH BOTH THE ALLEGATIONS AND THE COMPANY'S COMMENTS. It states plainly: WE INDICATE RESPONSE RATES IN THE COMPANY SECTIONS OF THE SITE, and IF A COMPANY IS LISTED AS HAVING FAILED TO RESPOND TO A PARTICULAR ALLEGATION, BUT IT HAS IN FACT ISSUED A RESPONSE... PLEASE LET US KNOW. A permanent public record that the company was asked and said nothing. For a developer that presents itself as responsible to lenders and buyers, that line on its own page is a cost. THE SCALE AND WHO DOES THE ASKING: it collects evidence on MORE THAN 10,000 COMPANIES IN MORE THAN 180 COUNTRIES and takes up ALLEGED ABUSE QUICKLY AND DIRECTLY WITH COMPANIES, INVITING THEM TO RESPOND TO SPECIFIC ALLEGATIONS (OVER 1,500 PER YEAR); a network of regional researchers BUILD LONG TERM RELATIONSHIPS WITH HUMAN RIGHTS ADVOCATES ON THE GROUND, BRINGING UNDERSTANDING OF THE DYNAMICS IN THE COUNTRIES THEY COVER, and WHERE THERE IS AN ALLEGATION OF CORPORATE HUMAN RIGHTS ABUSE THAT HAS NO PUBLIC RESPONSE, THEY REACH OUT TO THE COMPANY. Its site runs in several languages including Spanish and Portuguese. There is a researcher for your region who already knows the local advocates. Send the documented allegation to them rather than to a general address. WHAT IT DOES BEYOND PUBLISHING: its recorded practice is that DIALOGUES CAN EXTEND FURTHER AND OCCASIONALLY WE TAKE AN ACTIVE ROLE IN SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES AND NGOs; in one recorded case concerning an imprisoned indigenous leader who HAD LED THE OPPOSITION TO A PROPOSED... MINE IN HIS COMMUNITY'S TERRITORY, it POSTED THE ALLEGATIONS ON OUR WEBSITE AND SOUGHT RESPONSES FROM TWO COMPANIES WHO DID NOT RESPOND, AND ASSISTED THE LOCAL VILLAGERS IN SUBMITTING THE CASE TO THE UN SPECIAL REPRESENTATIVE ON HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, then CONTACTED PUBLIC INVESTORS... AND INVITED THEM TO COMMENT, of whom two responded and ONE COMMITTED TO RAISING THE ISSUE WITH ITS CLIENTS WHO ARE INVESTED in the company. Going up the chain to the investors is the step that moves a company. Identify who holds the shares or the loan before you send the allegation, and ask that they be invited to comment too. THE HONEST NUMBERS: the centre records a response rate averaging 43% on one page and 60% on another, and its own field acknowledges criticism about WEAK AND TANGENTIAL COMPANY RESPONSES and about the LACK OF REMEDY AND THE INEQUITY IN ARMS FOR THOSE AFFECTED BY ABUSE; a published analysis notes that A COMPANY RESPONSE TO A CRITICAL CIVIL SOCIETY REPORT IS NOT NECESSARILY A POSITIVE SIGN. Roughly half of companies answer, and an answer is not a remedy. Treat this as a public record and a pressure point, not as a complaint procedure that decides anything. WHAT IT ALSO PUBLISHES ON EACH COMPANY: company pages carry news, allegations, KEY DATA POINTS BASED ON CORPORATE POLICIES, AND SCORES FROM PROMINENT CIVIL SOCIETY BENCHMARKS, and its stated goals include a SAFE AND ENABLING ENVIRONMENT IN WHICH COMMUNITIES AND WORKERS CAN ADVOCATE FOR THEIR RIGHTS AND INTERESTS, INCLUDING THROUGH FREE AND FAIR NEGOTIATIONS. Read the company's page before your first meeting with it. Its own published policies and benchmark scores are the standard you can hold it to at the table.

trackers.name: Fundación Avina - a Latin American foundation with staff in up to 19 countries, six programmes including WATER and BIOMES, a record of SEED GRANTS to organisations that became leading deforestation monitors, and convening offered alongside money
trackers.desc: A FOUNDATION WITH STAFF LIVING IN NINETEEN LATIN AMERICAN COUNTRIES THAT HAS MOVED MORE THAN A BILLION DOLLARS THROUGH LOCAL ALLIES. It is A REGIONAL NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION WITH A MANDATE TO SUPPORT SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN THE LATIN AMERICAN REGION, whose activities cover ACCESS TO WATER AND ENERGY, RESOURCE MANAGEMENT and which works THROUGH A BROAD NETWORK OF GRASS-ROOTS AND COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS, NATIONAL AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS, THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY AND THE PRIVATE SECTOR; one account records 75 FULL-TIME STAFF MEMBERS BASED IN 19 COUNTRIES IN LATIN AMERICA and another 95 STAFF MEMBERS ACROSS 15 COUNTRIES, with OVER $500 MILLION ACROSS 13,000 INITIATIVES mobilised on one count and OVER USD 1.21 BILLION since 1994 on another. Staff who live in the country rather than visit it, and grant-making measured in thousands of small initiatives. Ask who the country contact is before writing to any regional address. THE PROGRAMME LIST THAT TELLS YOU WHERE A LAND CASE FITS: it works through SIX KEY PROGRAMS — CLIMATE, CIRCULAR ECONOMY, LABOR INNOVATION, BIOMES, DEMOCRACY, AND WATER, and elsewhere describes KEY AREAS INCLUDING CLIMATE ACTION, DEMOCRATIC STRENGTHENING, INCLUSIVE CIRCULAR ECONOMIES, BIOMES CONSERVATION, WATER MANAGEMENT, AND LABOR INNOVATION, with SUPPORT FOR LOCAL INITIATIVES. Biomes and water are separate programmes with their own staff. A watershed case goes to the water programme and a forest or savannah case to biomes — sending it to the wrong one is how a request gets lost. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DID FOR MONITORING ORGANISATIONS: a foundation officer records that in one phase it USED GRANTMAKING... TO MOBILIZE FUNDS WITH PARTNERS TO ORGANIZATIONS IN PAN-AMAZON, NOT ONLY IN THE BRAZILIAN AMAZON, WHICH IS OFTEN THE FOCUS, BUT THE PAN-AMAZON AND THE CHACO REGION, TO STRENGTHEN THEIR ABILITIES TO MONITOR DEFORESTATION, and that MANY OF THE ORGANIZATIONS THAT NOWADAYS ARE LEADING ORGANIZATIONS IN THIS AREA HAVE BEEN SUPPORTED AS A SEED GRANT. Seed grants to organisations that later became the leading monitors. If your group is at the beginning, that is the stage this foundation has repeatedly funded — and the Chaco, usually ignored beside the Amazon, is named. HOW IT DESCRIBES ITS OWN ROLE, WHICH SHAPES WHAT TO ASK FOR: it works AS A BROKER, CO-INVESTOR AND FACILITATOR, its PRIMARY CONTRIBUTION TO ITS ALLIES IS THE PROMOTION OF COLLABORATIVE ACTION THROUGH SERVICES AND FINANCIAL SUPPORT, and it BRINGS ITS ABILITIES AND RESOURCES TO THE TABLE AS A PEER INSTITUTION, providing ITS ABILITY, SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE, CONTACTS, RESOURCES, STRATEGIES, AND TOOLS TO WORK TOWARDS A COMMON CAUSE. Contacts and convening are offered alongside money. Where a case needs a mayor, a ministry and a company in one room, that is the service to ask for rather than a grant. THE UNITED STATES ENTITY, AND WHAT IT FUNDS: a separate United States non-profit MOBILIZES RESOURCES AND PARTNERSHIPS FROM THE UNITED STATES TO SUPPORT AND EXPAND THE IMPACT OF THIS MISSION and SUPPORTS INITIATIVES ALIGNED WITH THE FOUNDATION'S PRIORITIES ACROSS THREE INTERCONNECTED PILLARS... DEMOCRATIC INNOVATION, CLIMATE ACTION, AND A JUST AND REGENERATIVE ECONOMY, having COME TO EMBRACE FEMINIST PRINCIPLES THAT CENTER THE IMPORTANCE OF BUILDING COLLECTIVE POWER. Two legal entities, two funding routes. Which one can pay you depends on where your organisation is registered, so ask that first. THE HONEST NOTE ON ORIGIN AND COMPANY: it was FOUNDED IN 1994 BY a Swiss industrialist, is headquartered in one Central American capital with a northern office, works BY ENCOURAGING ALLIANCES BETWEEN SOCIAL AND BUSINESS LEADERS, and its recent activities include projects with a named water technology company in one country's semi-arid region. Its model is explicitly to put business leaders at the table with social ones. Decide whether that suits your fight before joining a programme, and read who co-funds it.

trackers.name: Fundación ProAves - a Colombian foundation holding 27-28 purchased nature reserves over 60,000-65,000 hectares, which manages THREE COMMUNITY PROPERTIES THROUGH MUNICIPALITY AGREEMENTS and established the country's first conservation easement
trackers.desc: THIS FOUNDATION MANAGES THREE COMMUNITY PROPERTIES ADJOINING ITS RESERVES THROUGH MUNICIPALITY AGREEMENTS, AND ESTABLISHED THE COUNTRY'S FIRST CONSERVATION EASEMENT. Its recorded achievements include THE MANAGEMENT OF THREE COMMUNITY PROPERTIES THAT ADJOIN RESERVES THROUGH MUNICIPALITY AGREEMENTS and THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THE FIRST COLOMBIAN CONSERVATION EASEMENT, alongside a national bird banding programme, three annual awareness campaigns and A NETWORK OF 10 LOCAL ECOLOGICAL GROUPS. An agreement with the municipality to manage community land next to a reserve. That is a route that needs no purchase and no title transfer, and this organisation has done it three times. THE SCALE OF WHAT IT HOLDS: it has established 27 NATURE RESERVES AT STRATEGIC POINTS THE LENGTH AND BREADTH OF THE COUNTRY TO PROTECT IN PERPETUITY THE HABITAT OF DIFFERENT SPECIES WITH SOME DEGREE OF THREAT OF EXTINCTION — an earlier count records twenty-eight totalling MORE THAN 60,000 HECTARES, and its conservation page records having conserved MORE THAN 65,000 HECTARES, reforested and restored 1,200 HECTARES and placed 3,600 HECTARES under payment for environmental services. Its reserves sit in RELICTS OF HIGH ANDEAN FOREST, PÁRAMOS, SUBTROPICAL, HUMID TROPICAL AND DRY TROPICAL FORESTS, MANGROVES AND COASTAL ZONES. Payments for environmental services on top of ownership. Buying the land and then enrolling it is how the running costs get covered. WHAT ITS CONSERVATION DEPARTMENT IS ACTUALLY FOR: it works to maintain habitat THROUGH THE ESTABLISHMENT AND MANAGEMENT OF NATURE RESERVES OF CIVIL SOCIETY, AND TO DEVELOP OTHER FIGURES OF PROTECTION SUPPORTED ON A CONCEPT OF SELF-SUSTAINABILITY AND COMMUNITY INTEGRATION, INFLUENCING LOCAL, REGIONAL AND NATIONAL POLICIES OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION; its stated objectives are to ESTABLISH, ENLARGE AND MANAGE INTEGRALLY THE PROTECTED AREAS OF THE FOUNDATION, GUARANTEEING COMPLIANCE WITH THE FUNCTION IN PERPETUITY and to PROMOTE AND DEVELOP ACTIONS THAT GUARANTEE THE SELF-SUSTAINABILITY IN PERPETUITY OF THE RESERVES. Nature reserves of civil society is the registrable figure a private owner uses here, and this foundation both holds them and helps develop other protection figures. Ask it which figure fits your parcel before choosing one. WHAT ONE ACQUISITION DID FOR A MUNICIPALITY: one reserve of nearly 4,000 HECTARES protects the basin of the most important river of its region, WHICH SERVES AS A VITAL ECONOMIC RESOURCE FOR TENS OF THOUSANDS OF INHABITANTS WHO LIVE IN THE NEIGHBOURING RURAL COMMUNITIES; THE ACQUISITION OF THIS LAND HELPS TO CONSOLIDATE A SECURITY ZONE FOR THE PROTECTION OF BIODIVERSITY, AGAINST RAPID AND UNSUSTAINABLE COLONISATION, AND REINFORCES THE PROTECTION OF SEVERAL COMMUNITIES; the municipality itself SIGNED THE MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING to join a zero-extinction alliance. The purchase was framed as protecting the water supply of neighbouring communities, and the municipality signed on. That is how a land purchase gets local political backing rather than local suspicion. HOW IT PAYS FOR ITSELF, AND WHO ELSE HOLDS THE LAND: it created the country's first birdwatching tourism company to operate tours and administer the reserves' tourist infrastructure, publishing that ecotourism IS A VERY GOOD ALTERNATIVE TO GENERATE EMPLOYMENT IN THE COUNTRYSIDE; one reserve of 221 HA adjoining a national park is governed jointly with an international bird conservation organisation. Joint governance with an international partner is how a small reserve next to a national park gets funded. Employment for neighbours is what keeps it from being resented.

trackers.name: CRIC — Consejo Regional Indígena del Cauca
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the association of indigenous authorities to which roughly 90% of Cauca's cabildos belong — 115 cabildos and 11 cabildo associations of the Nasa, Misak, Totoró, Polindara, Guanaco, Kokonuko, Kisgó, Yanacona, Inga and Eperara peoples, across nine zones. Founded in Toribío in 1971, its Plataforma de Lucha has always led with recovering resguardo land and expanding resguardos, and it added defence of the natural and environmental resources of indigenous territories to that list. It runs the Guardia Indígena, the community's own unarmed territorial control body, trained in human rights, self-protection, first response, indigenous jurisdiction and evidence handling. USE IT: if you are a Cauca community, this is your own authority structure for recovering or expanding a resguardo and for physically holding territory. It acts through cabildos, not individuals, and its members are killed for this work.

trackers.name: Movimiento Ríos Vivos
trackers.desc: A movement of fifteen associations and families from the Occidente, Norte and Bajo Cauca sub-regions of Antioquia, formed by people displaced and harmed by the Hidroituango dam on the río Cauca — Colombia's largest, with a 79 km reservoir and a 225 m wall. It is not an NGO acting for affected people; it IS the affected people, organised. Working with partner lawyers it has won two rulings in Bogotá: precautionary measures for Hidroituango victims from the 75th criminal court, and an order for restoration of fundamental rights and reparation from the 45th civil circuit court. It also took a complaint to the Inter-American Development Bank's accountability mechanism. WHO IT SUITS: dam- and mining-affected communities on the Cauca. Note the affected municipalities extend beyond Antioquia into Sucre, Bolívar and Córdoba. Its members face sustained threats and killings.

trackers.name: Fundación Horizonte Verde (Orinoquía)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: based in Cumaral, Meta, a founding member of Resnatur which ran its Nodo Orinoquía for ten years and set up the region's first private reserves in Meta from 1994. It does the technical justification and registration paperwork that turns a working finca into a Reserva Natural de la Sociedad Civil, and publishes free manuals and management plans for reserve owners in the Orinoquía. USE IT: in Meta, Casanare, Arauca or Vichada, to get land registered as an RNSC — more than 200 private reserves covering over 200,000 hectares now exist in the region, in a territory where state protected areas are scarce.

trackers.name: Comisión Ambiental Local (CAL) — take a seat in your locality, Bogotá
trackers.desc: THIS IS A SEAT, NOT A SERVICE. Under Decreto Distrital 575 de 2011 (modified by art. 12 of Decreto Distrital 81 de 2014) every Bogotá locality has a Comisión Ambiental Local chaired by the Alcalde Local, and its membership includes 5 representatives of environmental organisations recognised by the Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente and active in that locality — alongside the SDA, an Edil of the Junta Administradora Local, the Consejo de Planeación Local, the water utility EAAB, the Jardín Botánico, UAESP, a university, a school student and ASOJUNTAS. The CAL supports and channels community environmental proposals to public and private bodies at local, district, national and international level, and must produce an annual action plan and an annual report of what it did — documents worth holding it to. The SDA lists among its concerns conflicts arising from environmental deterioration, identified principally by the affected community. ANYONE OF ANY AGE MAY ATTEND ITS SESSIONS: to find where yours meets, ask the locality's environmental referente at the alcaldía local or the SDA's local environmental managers. USE IT: a standing seat with a published plan beats a one-off objection.

trackers.name: Bogotá
trackers.desc: Sub-national government portal (Colombia) — entry point to this unit's budget, procurement and finance information.

trackers.name: Archipelago of San Andrés, Providencia and Santa Catalina
trackers.desc: Sub-national government portal (Colombia) — entry point to this unit's budget, procurement and finance information.

trackers.name: Agencia de Acceso a la Información Pública (AAIP)
trackers.desc: Argentina's national authority guaranteeing the right of access to public information and data protection. — Holds to account: Argentine public bodies — find the agency's resolutions guaranteeing the right of access to public information.

trackers.name: Ministerio de la Defensa Pública del Chubut
trackers.desc: Public-defense ministry within the judiciary of Chubut, representing people who cannot afford a lawyer and protecting vulnerable groups — indigenous peoples, people deprived of liberty, victims of police abuse, women and children.

trackers.name: ADC (Asociación por los Derechos Civiles)
trackers.desc: Argentine civil-society organisation (since 1995) and member of the Latin American Legislative Transparency Network. Monitors institutions, proposes political and institutional reforms, and advocates on access to public information and legislative transparency.

trackers.name: ACIJ (Asociación Civil por la Igualdad y la Justicia)
trackers.desc: Argentine civil-rights organisation working on access to public information and legislative transparency.

trackers.name: FARN — Fundación Ambiente y Recursos Naturales
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Argentina's leading environmental-legal organisation (founded 1985, two years after democracy was restored). Provides FREE legal advice to people of limited means affected by environmental problems, and litigates on behalf of individuals and communities — including Indigenous communities resisting lithium mining, on consulta previa and free, prior and informed consent, access rights and environmental impact assessment. WHO IT SUITS: they prioritise public-interest cases that can set or strengthen jurisprudence, so a case with wider precedent value has the best chance; low-income claimants are explicitly the target of the free advice service.

trackers.name: Fundación Vida Silvestre Argentina
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: one of the few Argentine organisations that actually buys land for conservation. For the Urugua-í reserve in Misiones it identified the property, secured donated funds from three organisations including The Nature Conservancy, and bought 3,243 hectares of Atlantic Forest; the reserve is now managed by the foundation and it holds others across the country. Its earlier work documenting the vulnerability of the Urugua-í basin is what pushed the province to create the 84,000-hectare provincial park in the first place. USE IT: to propose a threatened property for purchase, and for the technical case that moves a provincial government to declare a park around it.

trackers.name: Banco de Bosques
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a foundation that intervenes in the land market itself — it watches classified listings for native forest advertised as apto desarrollo, meaning it already carries a clearance permit, and raises the purchase price through georeferenced donations, where satellite imagery ties each donor to the specific square metres they saved. Bought land is then donated on to expand protected areas: 5,005 hectares of Andean-Patagonian forest annexed to Parque Nacional Los Glaciares, and three chacras of Selva Misionera annexed to Parque Provincial Urugua-í. Its statute commits the forests to protection in perpetuity. WHO IT SUITS: this works the other way round from a grant — if you know of a threatened native forest parcel on the market, especially on the agricultural frontier in Chaco, Jujuy, Formosa or northern Santa Fe, bringing it to them is the ask. HOW IT DIFFERS: it buys the land rather than funding the campaign against clearing it.

trackers.name: Auditoría General de la Nación
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Argentina, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: SAIJ
trackers.desc: Sistema Argentino de Información Jurídica: free case law and legislation. · Find here: Argentina's official legal-information system — legislation, case-law and doctrine (SAIJ).

trackers.name: COMPR.AR
trackers.desc: Argentina's national electronic procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Argentina, and for how much.

trackers.name: Justicia Abierta – Datos Abiertos
trackers.desc: Argentina's open judicial-data portal publishing datasets from the Ministry of Justice and 50+ justice institutions. · Find here: Argentina's open-justice data portal (Justicia Abierta).

trackers.name: Auditoría General de la Nación (AGN)
trackers.desc: Argentina's national external-audit body — control of the national public sector's finances and management. — Holds to account: the national public sector — find external audit reports on how federal funds, programmes and state companies were managed.

trackers.name: Registro de Audiencias de Gestión de Intereses
trackers.desc: National lobbying / interest-meeting register. — Holds to account: those seeking to influence officials — find the register of interest-management meetings with public officials.

trackers.name: Inspección General de Justicia (IGJ)
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: companies in the City of Buenos Aires — find the Inspección General de Justicia register of entities and directors.

trackers.name: CSJN – Fallos
trackers.desc: Official rulings of Argentina's Supreme Court of Justice. · Find here: the rulings (Fallos) of Argentina's Supreme Court of Justice.

trackers.name: INDEC
trackers.desc: Argentina's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Argentina.

trackers.name: Argentina's eleven provinces that formally recognise private reserves - with annotation on the title binding future owners, municipal ordinance and university-agreement alternatives, and provincial directorates writing procedures with the owners' network
trackers.desc: ELEVEN PROVINCES FORMALLY RECOGNISE THE PRIVATE RESERVE, AND ONE OF THEM HAS SEVENTY OF THEM. The reserves network records that one northern province IS ONE OF THE 11 ARGENTINE PROVINCES THAT FORMALLY RECOGNISES THE FIGURE OF PRIVATE RESERVE IN ITS PROTECTED AREAS LAW, and that with 70 PRIVATE NATURE RESERVES IN FORCE it is THE PROVINCE OF THE COUNTRY THAT REGISTERS THE MOST INITIATIVES, because THERE EXISTS A PROVINCIAL NORM THAT GRANTS THE PRIVATE PARTY THE POSSIBILITY OF OBTAINING JURIDICAL RECOGNITION FOR ITS RESERVE and THERE EXIST NUMEROUS ASSOCIATIONS AND FOUNDATIONS THAT WORK ACTIVELY IN THE PROVINCE. By 2022 that province recorded MORE THAN 45 PRIVATE RESERVES INCORPORATED INTO THE PROVINCIAL SYSTEM OF PROTECTED NATURAL AREAS. Recognition is provincial, not national, and the provinces differ sharply. Establish first whether yours is among the eleven — where it is, a reserve can be given legal status without buying anything. THE FIVE KINDS OF RESERVE, WHICH TELL YOU WHAT IS POSSIBLE WITHOUT A LAW: reserves are classified as those RECOGNISED FORMALLY BY PROVINCIAL LEGISLATION OR MUNICIPAL ORDINANCES; those IN AGREEMENT WITH CIVIL ENVIRONMENTALIST ORGANISATIONS OR WITH UNIVERSITIES; those holding both recognitions; those ESTABLISHED BY SERVITUDES, LOAN FOR USE OR OTHER MECHANISMS ADAPTED FROM THE ARGENTINE CIVIL CODE; and those WITHOUT LEGAL OR INSTITUTIONAL RECOGNITION, BUT SELF-DENOMINATED AS SUCH BY THEIR OWNERS. Municipal ordinances are named alongside provincial statutes. Where the province offers nothing, a municipal ordinance or a university agreement can still give a reserve standing — and a university partner brings researchers with it. THE PROTECTION THAT SURVIVES A SALE: in one large province recognition of private and mixed reserves MUST NECESSARILY BE ESTABLISHED BY LAW and REQUIRES THE PRIOR CONSENT OF THE HOLDER OF THE DOMAIN, who must be formally notified and MAY OPPOSE THE DECLARATION WITHIN THIRTY WORKING DAYS; once final, the authority SHALL ORDER THE ANNOTATION OF THE AFFECTATION OF THE PROPERTY TO THE NATURE RESERVE REGIME, and THOSE WHO BECOME NEW OWNERS, BY VIRTUE OF A TRANSFER OF DOMAIN CARRIED OUT AFTER THAT REGISTRATION, SHALL EQUALLY BE SUBJECT TO THE REGIME OF THE RESERVE. The protection is annotated on the title and binds whoever buys next. For an owner who fears their heirs will sell, that annotation is the whole point. THE PROVINCIAL OFFICE THAT DOES THE WORK: in one province a DIRECTORATE OF FLORA, WILD FAUNA AND SOILS drafted the procedure for constituting private reserves WITH THE CONTRIBUTIONS OF a named university reserve AND THE ARGENTINE NETWORK OF PRIVATE NATURE RESERVES, presenting it at the network's fourth national meeting; in another, an ORGANISM FOR SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT is the authority of application, with powers to issue research permits and appoint trained reserve and park wardens. Provincial procedures are being written with the owners' network in the room. If your province lacks one, that network is the body to ask to propose it — it has done so before. THE HONEST EXPLANATION FOR THE UNEVENNESS: the distribution of reserves IS MARKED BY THE DISPARITY OF RECOGNITION AND GOVERNMENTAL INCENTIVES TO PRIVATE CONSERVATION, THE GEOGRAPHIC INCIDENCE OF THE CIVIL ENVIRONMENTALIST ORGANISATIONS THAT PROMOTE THEM and the character of the ecoregion. Where reserves are few, it is usually because no organisation works there rather than because owners refuse. Inviting one of the national foundations to open a programme in your province is a realistic ask.

trackers.name: Argentina's municipal and urban nature reserves - the national parks administration drafts the creating ordinance and helps form a warden corps, and a century-old bird organisation accompanies municipalities, both free and by open invitation
trackers.desc: THE NATIONAL PARKS ADMINISTRATION WILL HELP A TOWN HALL WRITE THE ORDINANCE THAT CREATES A MUNICIPAL RESERVE, AND WILL HELP IT BUILD A WARDEN CORPS. Its programme of interinstitutional collaboration for the promotion of municipal reserves PUTS AT THE DISPOSITION OF THE MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENTS OF THE WHOLE COUNTRY THE EXPERIENCE, THE TECHNICAL CAPACITY AND THE RESOURCES AVAILABLE TO NATIONAL PARKS TO STRENGTHEN THE URBAN AND PERIURBAN PROTECTED NATURAL AREAS, aiming TO PROMOTE THE CREATION, CONSOLIDATION AND ENLARGEMENT OF THE MUNICIPAL PROTECTED AREAS; among the services listed are TO LEND COLLABORATION IN THE DRAFTING OF THE NORM OF CREATION OF THE PROTECTED AREA, IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF INTERNAL REGULATIONS AND IN THE FORMATION OF A CORPS OF CONSERVATION AGENTS, and TO COLLABORATE IN THE CONSTRUCTION OF MANAGEMENT PLANS OF THE MUNICIPAL RESERVES, PLANS OF PUBLIC USE OR OF FIRE MANAGEMENT. The national parks service will draft your municipality's ordinance for it, free. A mayor who says the town lacks the technical capacity has just been answered. THE ORGANISATION THAT RUNS THE PARALLEL PROGRAMME, AND ITS EMAIL: a national bird conservation organisation, in existence since 1916 and the official representative of the world birdlife federation, runs an urban reserves programme spreading the goal IN EVERY MUNICIPALITY, AN URBAN NATURAL RESERVE; it also runs a fiscal reserves line for MUNICIPALITIES OR OTHER STATE ORGANISMS THAT HAVE UNDER THEIR DOMAIN NATURAL AREAS THAT MAY BE DESTINED TO THE CONSERVATION OF NATURE, seeking TO ENCOURAGE THE CREATION OF PROTECTED NATURAL AREAS BY MUNICIPALITIES OR OTHER STATE ORGANISMS AND TO ACCOMPANY THEM IN THEIR MANAGEMENT, HANDLING AND VISITATION, and it says plainly: IF IN YOUR MUNICIPALITY THERE IS AN AREA WITH POTENTIAL TO BECOME A NATURAL RESERVE, CONTACT US BY WRITING TO a published address. Reported support includes TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, TRAINING, AND SUPPORT IN THE DESIGN OF TRAILS, SIGNAGE, MANAGEMENT PLANS AND AWARENESS CAMPAIGNS. One email address, a standing invitation, and a century-old organisation behind it. Send the site with photographs and a map before approaching the council, so the proposal arrives with a partner already attached. WHY SIZE IS NOT AN OBSTACLE: the programme notes that IT USUALLY DOES NOT MATTER WHAT ITS SURFACE IS, SINCE HOWEVER SMALL IT MAY BE IT IS ALWAYS IMPORTANT TO CONSERVE IT, and that MANY VACANT PLOTS THAT ARE TOTALLY MODIFIED CAN BE CONVERTED INTO SMALL NATURAL RESERVES THROUGH THE RECONSTRUCTION OF THE ORIGINAL LANDSCAPE. A degraded vacant plot qualifies. That removes the usual objection that the land is not pristine enough to be worth protecting. WHAT AN ORDINANCE HAS ACTUALLY CITED: one provincial municipal gazette records a council reciting that two of the non-governmental organisations of longest standing CONSIDER THE SITE OF GREAT IMPORTANCE, INCLUDING IT AS PART OF THE PROGRAMME OF URBAN RESERVES OF THE METROPOLITAN AREA and in an inventory of valuable grassland areas, that the site appears in published nature area guides, and that an international union's classification PUTS IN RELIEF THE IMPORTANCE OF CONSERVING ITS SINGULARITIES. Inclusion in a programme or an inventory is quotable in the ordinance itself. Get the site listed first; councils prefer to ratify an existing recognition rather than invent one. THE EXAMPLES THAT SHOW THE RANGE: reserves recorded include a thirty-hectare sea inlet in the centre of a southern city, an eco-area of a metropolitan municipality conserving riverine forest and grassland, a 150-hectare marginal forest, a lagoon refuge in a small town, and an 1,100-hectare area four kilometres from a mountain town centre. From thirty hectares in a city centre to eleven hundred at the edge of a town. Find the closest comparable case and take its ordinance to your own council.

trackers.name: Argentina's municipal climate network - free consultancies that produced DRAFT ORDINANCES for councils, technical accompaniment for local plans, pooled network financing for small communes, and a green jobs mapping programme
trackers.desc: A MUNICIPAL NETWORK HERE PAID FOR CONSULTANCIES THAT PRODUCED DRAFT ORDINANCES FOR COUNCILS TO PASS. Its record shows that two named municipalities FINISHED THEIR CONSULTANCIES ON SUSTAINABLE PUBLIC PURCHASING, and that those municipalities WERE BENEFITED WITH A CONSULTANCY... WHICH GAVE AS A RESULT A DRAFT ORDINANCE TO BE PRESENTED IN THE RESPECTIVE DELIBERATIVE COUNCILS. Municipalities joining SIGN THE ADHESION AGREEMENT, and their local climate action plans ARE DESIGNED AND IMPLEMENTED WITH THE ADVICE AND ACCOMPANIMENT OF THE TECHNICAL TEAM OF THE EXECUTIVE SECRETARIAT OF THE NETWORK. An outside body wrote a draft ordinance and handed it to the council. That is the shape of help to ask for: not a report, but text a councillor can table. WHAT MEMBER MUNICIPALITIES GET: the environmental teams of adhering municipalities CONTINUOUSLY RECEIVE PROPOSALS OF TRAINING AND USEFUL DATA FOR THE REALISATION OF PROJECTS OF ADAPTATION AND MITIGATION, and MAY BE INCORPORATED INTO PROGRAMMES OF NETWORK FINANCING AND INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION; members TRAIN THEMSELVES AND COLLABORATE IN THE ELABORATION OF PROJECTS, PROGRAMMES AND MUNICIPAL ORDINANCES. Network financing pooled across municipalities is the part small councils cannot reach alone. A town of a few thousand people can enter an international programme through the network that it would never qualify for by itself. WHAT THE NETWORK IS AND WHAT IT SAYS IT DOES: it is A COALITION OF MUNICIPALITIES AND COMMUNES THAT COORDINATES AND DRIVES STRATEGIC PLANS in this country AND OTHER COUNTRIES OF LATIN AMERICA; it is AN INSTRUMENT OF COORDINATION AND IMPULSE OF LOCAL PUBLIC POLICIES, through which LOCAL ACTIONS ARE COORDINATED, EXPERIENCES ARE SOCIALISED AND THE RESULTS OF THE PROGRAMMES DEVELOPED BY THE MEMBER MUNICIPALITIES ARE EVALUATED, seeking to be AN INSTRUMENT OF TECHNICAL SUPPORT FOR THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS; its objective is TO EXECUTE MUNICIPAL, REGIONAL OR NATIONAL PROJECTS OR PROGRAMMES... FROM THE MOBILISATION OF LOCAL, NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL RESOURCES. Its organs include an executive secretariat and a council of mayors, and it publishes a climate planning guide, a list of adhering municipalities and a local action plan template. Communes as well as municipalities are members, and it works beyond this country. If your local authority is tiny, it is not too small to join. WHAT IT HAS PHYSICALLY BUILT AND WHO PAID: works of energy rehabilitation were inaugurated in two named small municipalities under a European programme, implemented by a development agency, executed by a national university with the network and a climate centre. Physical works in villages, financed by an external programme and executed through a university partnership. Ask which of these lines is currently open, and whether your municipality can be added to an existing project rather than starting one. THE OTHER PROGRAMME WORTH NAMING: the network runs a project of MAPPING, TRAINING AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE OF GREEN JOBS IN THE PARTICIPATING MUNICIPALITIES, defined as jobs that PRESERVE THE ENVIRONMENT THROUGH MODELS OF SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION, AT THE SAME TIME STRENGTHENING THE LOCAL AND REGIONAL ECONOMIES. Where a project is defended on jobs, this is the counter-argument with a programme behind it rather than a slogan.

trackers.name: FLACMA - the Latin American federation of cities and municipal associations, open to affiliation by ANY INDIVIDUAL MUNICIPALITY, whose assembly passes resolutions signed by mayors across eighteen countries
trackers.desc: ANY CITY OR MUNICIPALITY IN THE REGION MAY AFFILIATE DIRECTLY, NOT ONLY THROUGH ITS NATIONAL ASSOCIATION. Its membership rule is that MEMBERS ARE ALL THE CITIES, MUNICIPALITIES, NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND MUNICIPALIST INSTITUTIONS OF LATIN AMERICA THAT HAVE EXPRESSED THEIR WILL TO AFFILIATE; it is AN ORGANISATION OF FREE ADHESION THAT REPRESENTS THE 16,132 MUNICIPALITIES, INTENDANCIES AND PREFECTURES, THE CITIES AND THE ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, NETWORKS AND GUILDS OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, and it is the regional section of the world organisation of local governments. A single municipality may join in its own right. Where your national association is captured or inactive, that is a way for one sympathetic town hall to reach the regional table on its own. WHOSE PRESIDENTS SIT ON IT: its published leadership is drawn from the presidents of the national municipal bodies of the region — the federation of municipalities of one southern country, the association of municipalities of another, the Brazilian association of municipalities, the congress of intendants of another, the national federation of municipalities of one large federal country and the association of municipalities of an Andean one — each of them a serving mayor. The people who chair your own national municipal association sit here. A matter raised through that association can be carried into a regional assembly by the same person. WHAT IT SAYS IT IS FOR: TO BE THE VOICE OF LATIN AMERICAN MUNICIPALISM, TO CONSOLIDATE THE LATIN AMERICAN MUNICIPAL ASSOCIATIVE MOVEMENT, TO REPRESENT AND SERVE AS INTERLOCUTOR OF ALL THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND THEIR NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES, and TO PROMOTE IN LATIN AMERICA AUTONOMOUS, STRONG AND DEMOCRATIC LOCAL GOVERNMENTS; it ADHERES TO AND PROMOTES THE WORLD AND REGIONAL CONVENTIONS THAT THE NATIONAL STATES OF THE REGION SUBSCRIBE. Promoting the conventions the states have signed is written into its purpose. Where your country has signed an environmental or rights convention and a municipality is being told to ignore it, that is a body with a standing commitment to the opposite. THE PRECEDENT THAT SHOWS IT TAKES POSITIONS: its general assembly has approved unanimously a declaration on a territorial sovereignty dispute, signed by the president and BY MUNICIPAL AUTHORITIES AND HEADS OF ASSOCIATIONS AND FEDERATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES of eighteen named countries of the region, which also REAFFIRMED THE LEGITIMATE RIGHTS... OVER THE NATURAL RESOURCES OF THE AREA IN QUESTION. The assembly passes resolutions that name natural resources and get signed by mayors across eighteen countries. A community campaign that can be framed as a municipal cause has a forum that has done exactly that before. THE OTHER REGIONAL NETWORKS BESIDE IT: regional analysis names, among the principal associations and networks of local and regional governments with EXPERIENCES, IDEAS AND RESOURCES TO FOSTER INITIATIVES AND PROJECTS LINKED TO SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AT LOCAL LEVEL, a network of Mercosur cities alongside this federation, and global initiatives with regional presence for local sustainability and for city climate action; various cities have prepared VOLUNTARY LOCAL REPORTS on implementing the global development agenda in their territories. A voluntary local report is a document a municipality writes about itself. Getting your community's situation named in one is cheap, public and lasting. THE HONEST NOTE ON REPRESENTATION: the region's representation in the world body has been the subject of negotiations between this federation, the Mercosur cities network and the world organisation to form A LATIN AMERICAN REPRESENTATION THAT IS PLURAL, DIVERSE AND PARTICIPATORY. More than one body claims to speak for the region's municipalities. Approach both this federation and the Mercosur cities network rather than assuming one covers the other.

trackers.name: Mercociudades - a South American city network whose cooperation calls admit UNIVERSITIES AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS as partners alongside two or more municipalities, with an environment and sustainable development unit coordinated by a member city
trackers.desc: UNIVERSITIES AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS CAN BE PARTNERS IN THE COOPERATION PROJECTS THIS CITY NETWORK FUNDS. Its south-south cooperation call is open to MEMBER CITIES AND ASSOCIATED STATES, to universities of a regional university association, and to ORGANISATIONS OF CIVIL SOCIETY; THE PROJECT MUST INVOLVE AT LEAST TWO MEMBER LOCAL GOVERNMENTS OR ASSOCIATED STATES, and THE UNIVERSITIES AND SOCIAL ORGANISATIONS MAY PARTICIPATE AS PARTNER ENTITIES ALONGSIDE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, each city able to stand as coordinator of one proposal and partner in another. Two municipalities and your organisation is a fundable consortium. Where a threatened area straddles two towns, or two towns face the same developer, that is the shape the call is written for. THE THEMATIC UNIT THAT COVERS LAND AND WATER: among its seventeen thematic units and four working groups is one for ENVIRONMENT AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT, coordinated by a city with sub-coordinating cities, which has run exchanges on waste, sustainability and circular economy and marked world water day, and has opened AN OPPORTUNITY OF COOPERATION TOGETHER WITH THE UNITED NATIONS ENVIRONMENT PROGRAMME FOR THE STRENGTHENING OF LOCAL CAPACITIES; other units cover AUTONOMY, MANAGEMENT AND PARTICIPATION, HUMAN RIGHTS, URBAN DEVELOPMENT, PLANNING AND METROPOLITAN AREAS and BORDER INTEGRATION. A coordinating city runs each unit, and it is a city like yours rather than a secretariat. Write to the coordinator of the environment unit with your case: that is a mayor's office, not an agency. WHAT THE NETWORK COMMITS ITSELF TO DO: among its statutory objectives are TO CARRY OUT STUDIES AND COLLABORATE IN THE ELABORATION OF PLANS AND STRATEGIES IN THE URBAN-ENVIRONMENTAL AREA, WITH THE OBJECTIVE OF HARMONISING AND COORDINATING THE ACTIONS IN THIS AREA, TO COLLABORATE IN THE PLANNING OF THE POLICIES AND PLANS OF DEVELOPMENT OF THE CITIES, TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE NEED TO IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF LIFE, TO ADVOCATE AND RAISE AWARENESS ABOUT CITIZEN PARTICIPATION AND SOCIAL INCLUSION, and TO IDENTIFY THE CAUSES OF ACCENTUATION OF THE SOCIAL INEQUALITIES, IN ORDER TO PROPOSE AND SUPPORT SOLUTIONS POSSIBLE TO BE EXECUTED BY THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS. Collaborating in city development plans is a stated commitment. A municipality revising its plan can ask the network for that collaboration rather than paying a consultancy. WHO ELSE MAY TAKE PART: THE OTHER INSTANCES OF THE SUB-NATIONAL GOVERNMENTS OF THE COUNTRIES of the two regional blocs THAT EXPRESS THEIR WILL TO DO SO AND WHOSE GOVERNMENTS HAVE BEEN DEMOCRATICALLY ELECTED may participate as collaborators, and COOPERATION WITH CONSORTIA AND ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES WILL BE CARRIED OUT BY MEANS OF AGREEMENTS. Provinces, departments and municipal consortia can join as collaborators. Where the decision sits above the town hall, that tier can be brought to the same table. THE PLATFORM THAT MATCHES NEEDS TO SOLUTIONS: its cooperation programme runs an interactive platform DESIGNED SPECIALLY TO SHARE LOCAL SOLUTIONS... AND TO INTERWEAVE STRENGTHS AND TECHNICAL NEEDS OF CITIES OF ALL SOUTH AMERICA, with a directory of good practices through which member cities HAVE THE POSSIBILITY OF EXCHANGING WITH THE REFERENTS OF SOLUTIONS OF THE CITIES. Post the technical need rather than the complaint. A city that has already solved the same problem is what the platform is built to find.

trackers.name: ICLEI - a sustainability network open to individual councils AND to associations of local governments, giving fee-paying members year-round telephone and email support on designing environment and water projects, plus local biodiversity planning tools and an environmental award
trackers.desc: MEMBERSHIP OF THIS GLOBAL SUSTAINABILITY NETWORK IS OPEN TO ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AS WELL AS TO INDIVIDUAL COUNCILS, AND THE FEE SCALES WITH POPULATION AND NATIONAL INCOME. Its membership page states that AFFILIATION IS OPEN TO ALL LOCAL AND REGIONAL GOVERNMENTS, AS WELL AS TO THEIR WORLD, REGIONAL, NATIONAL AND SUBNATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS, that members MAY VOTE AND PARTICIPATE IN THE GOVERNING ORGANS OF THE WHOLE NETWORK, and that they CONTRIBUTE AN ANNUAL AFFILIATION FEE THAT VARIES REGIONALLY AND ACCORDING TO POPULATION AND GROSS NATIONAL INCOME PER CAPITA. A small municipality pays a small fee and votes in the same network as a capital city. Where a national association is the member, ask whether your council is covered by it already. WHAT A MEMBER ACTUALLY GETS, IN THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT'S OWN WORDS: it SUPPORTS ITS PARTNERS TO FIND SUSTAINABLE SOLUTIONS THROUGH PROJECTS, INITIATIVES AND PROGRAMMES, offers cities and states A PLATFORM TO INTERACT WITH OTHER LOCAL GOVERNMENTS and provides RESOURCES AND TOOLS TO PROMOTE POSITIVE ENVIRONMENTAL, ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL CHANGES; support runs DURING THE YEAR THAT THE FEE LASTS, PERMANENTLY, BY TELEPHONE OR BY EMAIL, and covers THE DESIGN OF PROGRAMMES AND PROJECTS OF SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN THEMES SUCH AS: ENVIRONMENT, WATER, PUBLIC SERVICES, ENERGY EFFICIENCY, SOLID WASTE. Joining requires A REQUEST TO THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT addressed to the named regional secretary, plus a membership form. Permanent telephone and email support on designing water and environment projects, for one annual fee. That is a standing technical helpline for a town hall that has none. THE BIODIVERSITY WORK THAT MATTERS FOR LAND: its recorded local biodiversity work is TO PROMOTE THE BIODIVERSITY STRATEGIES OF THE STATE AND MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENTS, AS WELL AS THEIR ACTION PLANS, AND ALSO TO REINFORCE THE CAPACITIES OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS TO INCORPORATE BIODIVERSITY INTO THE PLANNING PROCESSES, and it notes that MORE MONETARY RESOURCES ARE INVESTED GLOBALLY IN BIODIVERSITY AT LOCAL AND SUBNATIONAL LEVEL THAN AT NATIONAL LEVELS; a member municipality has launched an urban biodiversity index, and a global initiative on NATURE IN URBAN PLANNING is promoted through the network. Incorporating biodiversity into planning processes is the exact point at which a project is stopped or waved through. Ask the secretariat which of its tools your municipality can adopt in its next plan revision. THE RECOGNITION THAT GIVES A COUNCIL A REASON: the regional secretariat runs an award for local governments THAT HAVE CARRIED OUT ACTIONS IN FAVOUR OF THE PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT IN THEMES OF CLIMATE CHANGE, BIODIVERSITY, ENERGY EFFICIENCY, MOBILITY, AMONG OTHERS, open to municipalities, city boroughs and federal entities. An award with a biodiversity category. A council weighing whether to protect a site has a public reason to do so, and the application is a deadline you can work to. THE OFFICES THAT COVER THIS REGION: there is a secretariat for one large federal country together with Central America and the Caribbean, and a separate South American secretariat, each publishing member lists that include municipalities of several countries. Two regional offices cover the whole file. Write to the one for your subregion rather than to the global body.

trackers.name: Argentina's inter-municipal entities and micro-regions - 76 counted across 770 local governments and 22 provinces, some interprovincial, with one provincial statute allowing consortia to take credit, lend and form majority-public companies
trackers.desc: SEVENTY-SIX INTER-MUNICIPAL BODIES WERE COUNTED ACROSS 770 LOCAL GOVERNMENTS IN 22 PROVINCES, AND SOME CROSS PROVINCIAL LINES. A national survey recorded 76 INTER-MUNICIPAL ENTITIES, OF WHICH 4 ARE INACTIVE, including 770 LOCAL GOVERNMENTS OF 22 ARGENTINE PROVINCES, with only one province where none was detected; ELEVEN WERE INTERPROVINCIAL. Two basic forms are distinguished: the commonwealth, A FORMAL OR INFORMAL INTER-MUNICIPAL ARRANGEMENT TO WHICH THE ASSOCIATES DETACH CERTAIN ATTRIBUTIONS OF THEIR OWN WITH THE OBJECTIVE OF PROVIDING A JOINT SERVICE, for works and services OF A TEMPORARY OR INDEFINITE CHARACTER; and the micro-region — ALSO CALLED CONSORTIUM, ENTITY, COMARCA OR CORRIDOR — which implies A GREATER LEVEL OF INTERJURISDICTIONAL COORDINATION, SINCE IT SUPPOSES CREATING AN INTER-MUNICIPAL AGENDA IN ALL THE ORDERS OF THE ADMINISTRATION. Bodies that cross provincial boundaries already exist. Where a river or a forest spans two provinces, that is not an obstacle without precedent here. WHERE THE POWER TO FORM ONE COMES FROM: provincial constitutions authorise it in different terms — one permits municipalities to constitute consortia for building power stations, another authorises association FOR LOCAL DEVELOPMENT, others authorise CONSTRUCTING INTER-MUNICIPAL ORGANISMS FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF WORKS AND PROVISION OF COMMON SERVICES; one province's constitution gives municipalities the attribution to CELEBRATE AGREEMENTS AMONG THEMSELVES AND CONSTITUTE INTER-MUNICIPAL ORGANISMS WITH SPECIFIC FACULTIES AND ENDS FOR THE PROVISION OF PUBLIC SERVICES, REALISATION OF PUBLIC WORKS, TECHNICAL AND FINANCIAL COOPERATION or other activities; specific legislation exists in only three provinces. Check your provincial constitution before assuming a consortium needs a new law. In several provinces the power is already there, and one province grants it in terms broad enough to cover technical cooperation on almost anything. THE STRONGEST PROVINCIAL STATUTE FOUND: one province's law creating management and development consortia is recorded as advancing THE POSSIBILITY OF HAVING A PROVINCIAL ORGAN OF FISCALISATION, THE CAPACITY TO TAKE CREDITS, THE ASSOCIATION WITH PRIVATE SECTORS, THE POSSIBILITY OF GRANTING LOANS, MAKING JOINT PURCHASES AND THE APTITUDE TO CONSTITUTE PUBLIC LIMITED COMPANIES WITH MAJORITY STATE PARTICIPATION. Taking credit, lending and forming a company with majority public ownership. That is a vehicle capable of buying and holding land, and one province has already legislated it. WHO MAY BE INVOLVED BESIDES THE COUNCILS: inter-municipal and supra-municipal relations MAY INVOLVE PUBLIC, PRIVATE AND THIRD SECTOR SUBJECTS AND INTERNATIONAL ORGANISMS; management follows either AUTONOMOUS MANAGEMENT or COORDINATION DELEGATED IN A MUNICIPAL OFFICIAL OF ONE MEMBER LOCAL GOVERNMENT. Third sector organisations are named as possible parties. A foundation or association can be inside the arrangement rather than lobbying it from outside. THE HONEST RECORD OF WHY THEY FAIL: the first inter-municipal entity of one large province was progressively deactivated after a change of political control and dissolved; the same literature notes that FORMALISED CONSORTIA ENTER INTO INACTIVITY OR OTHER ENTITIES ARE LIQUIDATED even as new ones appear, and that in a sample of sixty-two cases business chambers participated permanently in only a quarter. These bodies die when the mayors change party. Write continuity into the statute — permanent technical staff, a fixed seat, an asset that cannot be returned — because political goodwill will not survive one election.

trackers.name: Fundo Casa Socioambiental - a small-grants fund for community groups across South America that funds groups WITHOUT LEGAL PERSONALITY through a partner organisation, with calls prioritising repeatedly rejected and newly formed groups
trackers.desc: A GROUP WITH NO LEGAL PERSONALITY AT ALL CAN RECEIVE A GRANT, BY BORROWING ANOTHER ORGANISATION'S. The fund's calls state that ORGANISATIONS THAT DO NOT POSSESS a registered company number ARE ALSO ELIGIBLE AND MAY SEND PROJECTS IN THIS CALL; the partner organisation field MUST ONLY BE FILLED IN IN THE CASES IN WHICH THE PROPOSING ORGANISATION DOES NOT POSSESS one, that partner being THE NON-PROFIT INSTITUTION THAT CEDES ITS LEGAL STRUCTURE TO THE GROUPS and THE LEGAL RESPONSIBLE FOR THE PROJECT, receiving the resource in an institutional bank account; one organisation may be PROPOSER OF ONE PROJECT OF ITS OWN AND PARTNER FOR UP TO ONE OTHER GROUP WITHOUT JURIDICAL PERSONALITY. An unincorporated village committee can be funded tomorrow if one registered neighbour signs as partner. That single rule removes the obstacle that blocks most community groups in this file. WHO THE FUND IS AND HOW SMALL THE GRANTS ARE: it is A NON-GOVERNMENTAL, NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION THAT FINANCES SMALL PROJECTS, AND CAPACITY STRENGTHENING, FOR SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL INITIATIVES OF NGOs AND COMMUNITY GROUPS IN SOUTH AMERICA, whose strategy is THE SUPPORT OF MANY PROJECTS WITH SMALL AMOUNTS INSTEAD OF SUPPORTING FEW PROJECTS WITH LARGE AMOUNTS; founded in 2005, its mission is TO PROMOTE CONSERVATION AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY, DEMOCRACY AND SOCIAL JUSTICE THROUGH THE SUPPORT AND STRENGTHENING OF CAPACITIES AND INITIATIVES OF CIVIL SOCIETY IN SOUTH AMERICA, with experience supporting POPULAR ORGANISATIONS, SOCIAL MOVEMENTS, NETWORKS AND ARTICULATIONS; recorded totals run from more than three thousand projects in ten countries to almost five thousand. Many small grants rather than a few large ones. A group asking for a few thousand is inside this fund's model rather than beneath its notice. WHAT A CALL ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE: one recorded call supported UP TO 24 PROJECTS OF UP TO R$ 35,000.00 in named river regions and one state, open to LOCAL ASSOCIATIONS AND COMMUNITY GROUPS WITH AN ANNUAL BUDGET OF UP TO R$ 150 THOUSAND, its priority publics being TRADITIONAL COMMUNITIES SUCH AS INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, QUILOMBOLA, RIVERSIDE AND EXTRACTIVIST COMMUNITIES; a later edition raised the ceiling to fifty thousand per project and expanded from thirty-four approved projects to fifty-seven after two hundred and thirty-three applications arrived. Another call prioritises ORGANISATIONS RECENTLY CREATED, IN AN INITIAL STAGE OF ACTIVITIES OR RESUMING THEIR ACTIVITIES AFTER A PERIOD OF PARALYSIS, and INITIATIVES OF ORGANISATIONS THAT HAVE NOT YET ACCESSED RESOURCES from the fund or that have applied three or more times without success. Applying and failing repeatedly is itself a stated priority criterion. If your group has been rejected three times, say so in the next application. THE THREE-COUNTRY ALLIANCE BEHIND THE AMAZON CALLS: one initiative unites this fund with a Colombian and a Peruvian socio-environmental fund, aiming TO PROMOTE GREATER CONTRIBUTION OF DIRECT RESOURCES TO INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, QUILOMBOLA COMMUNITIES AND OTHER TRADITIONAL PEOPLES IN THE AMAZON OF BRAZIL, PERU AND COLOMBIA, ESPECIALLY IN THE BORDER REGION, supporting twenty-four, fourteen and nineteen projects respectively in one year; all members of a southern socio-environmental funds alliance WILL LAUNCH CALLS IN THEIR COUNTRIES, each publishing its own. Border regions are named as a priority rather than a complication. Look up the member fund for your own country and read its call, not only this one. THE RULES THAT CATCH PEOPLE OUT: resources may not be spent before the contract is signed; funds from other budget lines may not be moved to pay consultancies; groups with PENDING ACCOUNTS from a previous grant are not accepted; and where a group hires advice it MUST SEEK PEOPLE OF TRUST, with the project ELABORATED TOGETHER WITH THE COMMUNITY and its final version OF WIDE KNOWLEDGE OF THE COMMUNITY. Do not spend a peso before signature, and do not let a consultant write the proposal alone. Both are stated grounds for losing the grant.

trackers.name: Alianza Socioambiental Fondos del Sur - the alliance listing each country's own grassroots socio-environmental fund, several of which pay for MOBILISATIONS IN DEFENCE OF RIGHTS and run joint cross-border calls
trackers.desc: EVERY MAJOR COUNTRY IN THIS REGION NOW HAS ITS OWN SMALL-GRANTS FUND RUN BY LOCAL ENVIRONMENTALISTS, AND THEY ARE LISTED IN ONE PLACE. The alliance names among its members funds in BRAZIL — a socio-environmental fund founded in 2005, an institute of society, population and nature with its own ecos fund, and a Brazilian fund for environmental education — plus MEXICO, CENTRAL AMERICA, BOLIVIA, PERU, COLOMBIA, ECUADOR and, in ARGENTINA, a rural communities network and a socio-environmental fund; each fund is A NATIONAL OR REGIONAL ENTITY DEDICATED TO PROVIDING GRANTS AND OTHER FORMS OF SUPPORT TO LOCAL GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS THAT PROPOSE JUST AND SUSTAINABLE ALTERNATIVES TO PROTECT THE RIGHTS AND ECOSYSTEMS OF COMMUNITIES, and all were FOUNDED BY LOCAL SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTALISTS. One page lists the fund for your country. Start there rather than with an international donor, because these funds exist precisely because grassroots groups cannot reach the large external financiers. WHY THESE FUNDS EXIST, IN THEIR OWN WORDS: they attend to how THE MOST VULNERABLE POPULATIONS FACING ENVIRONMENTAL CHALLENGES ARE ALSO THE MOST EXCLUDED FROM PHILANTHROPIC SUPPORT, whose RIGHTS ARE CONSTANTLY VIOLATED AND WHO IN GENERAL CANNOT ACCESS A LARGE EXTERNAL FINANCIER. Being too small for the big funders is the qualifying condition here, not a disqualification. WHAT THE COLOMBIAN FUND SAYS IT DOES, AS A TEMPLATE: it is AN ALLY OF THE GRASSROOTS COMMUNITIES, WHICH WORKS TO STRENGTHEN AND AMPLIFY THEIR AUTONOMY, KNOWLEDGE AND CAPACITIES IN THE DEFENCE OF LIFE, TERRITORIES AND COMMON GOODS, functioning as A MECHANISM OF FINANCIAL, POLITICAL AND ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT TO COMMUNITY AGENDAS THAT PROTECT ECOSYSTEMS, HUMAN RIGHTS AND SOCIAL JUSTICE AT LOCAL LEVEL, responding IN AN AGILE MANNER TO COMMUNITY PROJECTS AND ACTIONS, INCLUDING EMERGENT NEEDS SUCH AS MOBILISATIONS IN DEFENCE OF RIGHTS; since 2020 it has SUPPORTED 280 GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS... AND MOBILISED MORE THAN US$1,000,000 IN SMALL DONATIONS. Mobilisations in defence of rights are named as fundable. Very few funders in this file will pay for that, and this one says so on its own page. THE CENTRAL AMERICAN FUND, WHICH COVERS SEVERAL COUNTRIES AT ONCE: it gives STRATEGIC ACCOMPANIMENT AND AGILE AND TIMELY DONATIONS TO INDIGENOUS, PEASANT AND AFRO-DESCENDANT ORGANISATIONS, IN THEIR PROCESSES OF IMPROVING THEIR SOCIAL, ECONOMIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESILIENCE IN CENTRAL AMERICA. For the Central American countries there is one regional door rather than seven national ones. Address it as a regional fund and say which country and territory you are in. WHAT THE ALLIANCE ADDS ON TOP OF THE INDIVIDUAL FUNDS: members run joint calls across borders, publishing separate deadlines per country for the same initiative, and have documented the experience in a case study on how one project PROMOTED COLLABORATION AMONG LOCAL FUNDS OF BRAZIL, COLOMBIA AND PERU IN THE AMAZON BORDER REGION; the alliance also includes a youth-led global thematic fund. The same call closes on different dates in each country. Check your own fund's deadline rather than the one you saw quoted elsewhere.

trackers.name: The GEF Small Grants Programme - grants of up to $50,000 DIRECT to community organisations, with a national coordinator in each country who helps write the concept paper, planning grants, and a companion window of up to $300,000
trackers.desc: THERE IS A NAMED NATIONAL COORDINATOR IN YOUR COUNTRY WHOSE JOB INCLUDES HELPING YOU WRITE THE APPLICATION. The programme's own procedure is that THE PROJECT PROPONENT — A NATIONAL CBO OR NGO — CONTACTS THE SGP NATIONAL COORDINATOR TO RECEIVE PROJECT APPLICATION GUIDELINES AND FORMS, and that WITH ASSISTANCE FROM THE NATIONAL COORDINATOR, THE PROPONENT PREPARES A BRIEF PROJECT CONCEPT PAPER; the coordinator pre-screens it, and if eligible the proponent prepares a full proposal — IN SOME CASES, THIS STEP MAY BE SUPPORTED BY A PLANNING GRANT — which goes to a national steering committee that accepts, rejects or returns it for further work. A planning grant to write the proposal, and an official whose job is to help you write it. Contact the coordinator before drafting anything, because the concept paper is short and they will tell you whether it fits. WHAT IT PAYS AND TO WHOM: the programme PROVIDES GRANTS OF UP TO $50,000 DIRECTLY TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES INCLUDING INDIGENOUS PEOPLE, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS AND OTHER NON-GOVERNMENTAL GROUPS, for projects in BIODIVERSITY, CLIMATE CHANGE MITIGATION AND ADAPTATION, LAND DEGRADATION AND SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT, INTERNATIONAL WATERS AND CHEMICALS, with SPECIAL CONSIDERATION FOR INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, WOMEN, AND YOUTH; it COMPLEMENTS THE LARGE AND MEDIUM-SIZED facility funding BY PROVIDING A WINDOW FOR THE DIRECT PARTICIPATION OF NGOs, LOCAL COMMUNITIES, AND OTHER GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS. Since 1992 it has supported CLOSE TO 30,000 GRANTS, ADMINISTERING $1.54 BILLION... ACROSS 136 COUNTRIES. Fifty thousand dollars, paid direct to a community organisation, on biodiversity or land degradation. That is the largest routine sum in this file available without an intermediary. HOW IT IS RUN LOCALLY: it operates IN A DECENTRALIZED AND COUNTRY-DRIVEN MANNER THROUGH COUNTRY PROGRAM TEAMS COMPOSED OF A NATIONAL COORDINATOR, OFTEN A PROGRAM ASSISTANT, AND A NATIONAL STEERING COMMITTEE IN EACH PARTICIPATING COUNTRY, each country publishing a country programme strategy that proposals must align with. In one small island state an operational phase was advertised with A GRANTS PORTFOLIO OF APPROXIMATELY US$750,000... FOR COMMUNITY-BASED ENVIRONMENTAL PROJECTS. Download your country's programme strategy before writing. Proposals are judged against that document, and it names the priorities and often the specific landscapes. THE THREE AGENCIES THAT NOW RUN IT: the core programme is implemented by a development programme, an agriculture organisation and a conservation organisation, the second bringing expertise in AGRICULTURE, FISHERIES, FORESTRY, BIOENERGY, CLIMATE-RESILIENT PRACTICES, LIVESTOCK, AND LAND & WATER to thirteen countries; national coordinator posts in some small states are contracted through the conservation organisation, working alongside a Caribbean islands biodiversity hotspot fund. Which agency runs your country's programme changes who you write to. Check the country page rather than assuming it is the development programme. THE LARGER WINDOW BESIDE IT: a civil society challenge programme led by a conservation union SUPPORTS COMPETITIVE OPPORTUNITIES FOR LOCAL CSOs TO ACCESS FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL RESOURCES TO SCALE UP INNOVATIVE ENVIRONMENTAL SOLUTIONS, OFFERING GRANTS OF UP TO $300,000. Three hundred thousand for an organisation that has already proved something small works. Treat the fifty-thousand grant as the step that qualifies you for it.

trackers.name: World Land Trust and its 52 local partners - raises the money for LAND PURCHASE but leaves the title with the local organisation, funds reserve rangers and watershed buy-outs, and has signed shared-management agreements with an environment ministry
trackers.desc: THIS IS A FUNDER THAT PAYS FOR LAND PURCHASE AND THEN PUTS THE TITLE IN A LOCAL ORGANISATION'S NAME, NOT ITS OWN. It DOESN'T OWN ANY OF THE LAND ITSELF, which IS ALL OWNED BY ITS LOCAL NGO PARTNERS, so that THE LAND IS IN THE CONTROL OF LOCAL CONSERVATION PARTNERS; it HELPS RAISE THE FUNDS TO PURCHASE THE LAND AND THEN PROVIDES ASSISTANCE TO THE LOCAL ORGANIZATION IN MANAGING AND PROTECTING it, with ownership ENTRUSTED TO CONSERVATION ORGANISATIONS RUN BY LOCAL PEOPLE WHO TAKE ON THE RESPONSIBILITY OF PROTECTING THE LAND, MONITORING THE WILDLIFE AND BIODIVERSITY ON THE RESERVE, AND EMPLOYING PARK WARDENS. Money for the purchase, and the deed stays local. For a community group with a willing seller and no capital, this is the closest thing in this file to a buyer. WHERE IT WORKS IN THIS REGION: partners and projects are recorded in ARGENTINA... BELIZE, BOLIVIA, BRAZIL, COLOMBIA, ECUADOR, GUATEMALA, HONDURAS... MEXICO, PARAGUAY, PERU... VENEZUELA among other countries, with 52 active conservation partners after five new ones joined in one year. Twelve countries in this file already have a partner. Find the partner nearest you and approach it, because the funder works through partners rather than taking applications from communities directly. WHAT THE PURCHASE PROGRAMME ACTUALLY DOES: its land purchase appeal RAISES FUNDS SO THAT partner organisations CAN PURCHASE LOCAL LAND AND CREATE RESERVES TO PROTECT THE LOCAL HABITAT AND WILDLIFE IN PERPETUITY; recorded cases include funding a partner to expand an existing reserve by hundreds of hectares, and a purchase that was THE CULMINATION OF 16 YEARS OF NEGOTIATIONS. Cumulatively the trust and its partners have been INSTRUMENTAL IN THE PURCHASE AND PROTECTION OF MORE THAN 3,312,183 ACRES of threatened habitat. Sixteen years of negotiation ended in a purchase. If the owner is not ready to sell yet, that is not a reason to stop asking — it is the normal timescale. WHAT ELSE IT FUNDS BESIDES THE PURCHASE: partnerships encompass LAND PURCHASE, LAND PROTECTION through a carbon scheme and FUNDING FOR RESERVE RANGERS, and recorded projects include WATERSHED PROTECTION BY PURCHASING KEY AREAS TO SAFEGUARD WATER SUPPLIES and work WITH LOCAL COMMUNITIES TO PRESERVE CULTURAL TRADITIONS; one Amazon corridor project proceeded THROUGH LAND PURCHASE, WORKING WITH LOCAL indigenous COMMUNITIES, RESTORATION, MONITORING AND MANAGEMENT. Ranger salaries are funded, not only the acquisition. A reserve nobody can afford to guard is the usual failure, and this is one of the few sources that pays for the guarding. THE AGREEMENT MODEL WORTH COPYING: in one country the trust signed A SHARED-MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT WITH its partner organisation AND THE MINISTRY OF THE ENVIRONMENT, aiming TO ENSURE THE PROTECTION OF RESERVES TOTALLING OVER 2.5 MILLION ACRES. A three-way agreement between funder, local organisation and the environment ministry. Where the state owns land it cannot manage, that is the arrangement to propose. THE PARTNERS THEMSELVES ARE THE ROUTE: named partners include foundations protecting foothill and cloud forests and páramo whose RESERVES PROTECT LOCAL CENTRES OF ENDEMISM THAT ARE NOT PROTECTED BY the country's NATIONAL PARKS OR PROTECTED AREAS, a habitat and development foundation in one southern country, a body creating protected areas while PROMOTING THE PARTICIPATION OF LOCAL STAKEHOLDERS, and a multi-country organisation supporting PUBLIC, COMMUNAL AND PRIVATE PROTECTED AREAS with a team of local conservationists, legal professionals and mapping experts. One partner explicitly supports communal protected areas and employs its own lawyers and mappers. Where a community holds land collectively and needs title work or a boundary map, ask that partner first.

trackers.name: Rainforest Trust - FEASIBILITY AWARDS of about $10,000 to fund the legal pathway study and species survey, then uncapped creation awards for land purchase, community land titling or converting extractive concessions into protected areas
trackers.desc: THERE IS A GRANT OF AROUND TEN THOUSAND DOLLARS JUST TO FIND OUT WHETHER PROTECTING A SITE IS POSSIBLE. The funder provides FEASIBILITY AWARDS TO ASSESS THE POTENTIAL FOR CREATING OR EXPANDING PROTECTED OR CONSERVED AREAS, INTENDED TO ADDRESS SPECIFIC INFORMATION GAPS... AS PRECURSORS TO APPLYING FOR a full award; these can SUPPORT DEVELOPING A LEGAL PATHWAY TO PROTECT A PROPOSED SITE, OR FIELD SURVEYS TO DETERMINE THE PRESENCE AND ABUNDANCE OF CRITICALLY ENDANGERED OR ENDANGERED SPECIES, at typical funding of about US $10,000 and up to about US $20,000 in exceptional cases, ACCEPTED ON A ROLLING BASIS. Ten thousand dollars to pay for the legal pathway study and the species survey — the two documents every protection file needs and no community can afford. Apply for this before applying for anything else. WHAT THE MAIN AWARD BUYS: primary awards SUPPORT THE CREATION AND EXPANSION OF PROTECTED OR CONSERVED AREAS, ON LAND OR SEA, BE IT THROUGH DESIGNATION, LAND TITLING, PURCHASE OR ANY OTHER RECOGNIZED METHODOLOGY; tools named include LAND PURCHASE; DESIGNATION AS NATIONAL PARKS; NATURE RESERVES; COMMUNITY RESERVES; AND CONVERSION OF LOGGING, MINING, OR OTHER TYPES OF EXTRACTIVE CONCESSIONS TO FORMALLY PROTECTED AREAS. Applications above a quarter of a million dollars have fixed deadlines; smaller ones MAY BE SUBMITTED ON A ROLLING BASIS THROUGHOUT THE YEAR, and THERE IS NO FIXED UPPER LIMIT. Converting an existing logging or mining concession into a protected area is a named, fundable route. Where a concession has already been granted over the land you are defending, that is the door rather than a dead end. THE COMMUNITY LAND TENURE TRACK: for projects where indigenous or community land tenure is the primary strategy, the funder looks for cases where LAND OWNERSHIP, I.E. LAND TITLE, IS GRANTED TO A COMMUNITY RATHER THAN TO AN INDIVIDUAL OR AN NGO, or SUBSTANTIAL MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY OF THE AREA WILL BE LED BY THE INDIGENOUS PEOPLES OR LOCAL COMMUNITY, or THE GRANT IS DIRECTLY MANAGED BY AN INDIGENOUS OR LOCAL COMMUNITY-LED ORGANIZATION, including designation as A MULTIPLE-USE TERRITORY WITH MANAGEMENT (OR CO-MANAGEMENT) BY THE INDIGENOUS OR LOCAL COMMUNITY; such organisations are STRONGLY ENCOURAGED TO APPLY. Title to the community rather than to an NGO is a funding criterion here, not a complication. If your aim is communal title, this funder prefers it. WHEN PURCHASE IS THE STRATEGY, THE TEST IS URGENCY: for land purchase projects the funder asks that LAND IS LIKELY TO BE CONVERTED IN THE NEAR FUTURE IF PURCHASE IS NOT COMPLETED, that AN ALTERNATIVE PROTECTION STRATEGY IS NOT POSSIBLE, MORE EXPENSIVE, OR SIGNIFICANTLY LESS EFFECTIVE, and that CONSERVATION VALUE IS GREATER THAN EXPECTED BASED ON THE COST. Imminent conversion is the argument that wins a purchase grant. Document the threat — the permit application, the clearing, the road survey — as carefully as the biodiversity. WHO MAY APPLY, AND THE WARNING ABOUT MIDDLEMEN: ALL APPLICANTS MUST BE LEGALLY REGISTERED, NON-GOVERNMENT ORGANIZATIONS THAT ARE AUTHORIZED TO CONDUCT WORK IN THE COUNTRY, and partners SHOULD BE NGOs BASED IN THE COUNTRY OF THE PROPOSED PROTECTED AREA; the funder states plainly: YOU NEVER NEED TO PAY A CONSULTANT OR INTERMEDIARY TO APPLY FOR its funding, it ONLY REVIEW[S] APPLICATIONS SUBMITTED DIRECTLY BY ELIGIBLE ORGANIZATIONS, and WE WILL WORK WITH YOU TO REFINE YOUR PROPOSAL. Beyond acquisition it HELPS BUILD THE CAPACITY OF ITS PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS, including TRAINING FOR EMPLOYMENT AS FOREST GUARDS, WILDLIFE MONITORS AND ECO-GUIDES. Anyone offering to broker this application for a fee is to be refused. The funder says so itself, and it will help refine the proposal free.

trackers.name: Pro Bono Network of the Americas and its national clearinghouses - non-profits in 16 countries that place SOCIAL ORGANISATIONS with volunteer law firms free, plus free representation for cases at the merits stage before the inter-American commission
