trackers.desc: THERE IS A CLEARINGHOUSE IN MOST OF THESE COUNTRIES WHOSE JOB IS TO FIND A LAW FIRM WILLING TO ACT FOR YOUR ORGANISATION FREE. Its members are NON-PROFIT ENTITIES THAT FACILITATE THE PROVISION OF FREE LEGAL SERVICES TO PEOPLE OF SCARCE RESOURCES, SECTORS OR GROUPS IN A CONDITION OF VULNERABILITY, ENTREPRENEURS AND SOCIAL ORGANISATIONS, WITH A VIEW TO IMPROVING ACCESS TO JUSTICE AND THE DEFENCE OF THE PUBLIC INTEREST; the network born in 2011 HAS NOW BECOME THE MAIN INSTITUTIONAL HOME OF THE PRIMARY PRO BONO CLEARINGHOUSES IN THE REGION and INCLUDES MORE THAN 20 ORGANIZATIONS, REPRESENTING 16 COUNTRIES, coordinated jointly by a New York bar association centre and a national pro bono foundation. Social organisations are named alongside individuals as eligible. A community association fighting a project is exactly the kind of client these clearinghouses were built to place. HOW A CASE ACTUALLY REACHES A LAWYER: one national foundation RECEIVES REQUESTS FOR PRO BONO CASES THROUGH ITS WEB PLATFORM OR OTHER ENTITIES, and ARTICULATES AND CHANNELS FREE LEGAL ADVICE, CARRIES OUT WORKSHOPS AND INFORMATIVE TALKS AND SEEKS TO GENERATE PUBLIC INFLUENCE; another states that cases ARRIVE AT THE FOUNDATION THROUGH the regional centre, the regional network, or national NGOs in contact with member firms and university professors, and that WHOEVER HAS A CASE OR A PROJECT FOR WHICH THEY NEED PRO BONO ADVICE MAY PRESENT IT BY SENDING AN EMAIL to a published address. One email with the case attached. That is the whole entry procedure in at least one country, and the others run a web form. THE HONEST LIMIT, STATED BY THE CLEARINGHOUSE ITSELF: one alliance RESERVES THE RIGHT TO EVALUATE AND DECIDE WHETHER A REQUEST MAY BE CONSIDERED A PRO BONO CASE; THE PRESENTATION OF A REQUEST DOES NOT GUARANTEE ITS ACCEPTANCE, NOR THE ASSIGNMENT OF A LAWYER OR FIRM; it ACTS ONLY AS AN INTERMEDIARY BETWEEN THE PERSON OR ORGANISATION REQUESTING AND THE VOLUNTEER LAWYERS, and taking a case DEPENDS EXCLUSIVELY ON THE VOLUNTARY DECISION OF THOSE LAWYERS OR FIRMS, WITHOUT ANY OBLIGATION OF SPONSORSHIP EXISTING. No guarantee, and no obligation on any firm. Apply to more than one clearinghouse, and make the request specific enough that a commercial firm can see the discrete piece of work being asked for. WHAT THE NETWORK COORDINATES BEYOND SINGLE CASES: volunteer lawyers and firms work on PARTICIPATION BEFORE THE INTER-AMERICAN SYSTEM OF HUMAN RIGHTS, COOPERATION TO SOCIAL ORGANISATIONS THAT REQUIRE LEGAL SUPPORT, THE ELABORATION OF THEMATIC REPORTS AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT TO INITIATIVES; under a collaboration agreement with the inter-American human rights commission the network PROVIDES PRO BONO LEGAL REPRESENTATION TO PEOPLE WITH CASES AT THE MERITS STAGE, the commission notifying petitioners of that opportunity. Free representation for a case already before the inter-American commission, arranged through this network. If a matter has reached that stage, ask the commission and the network at the same time. THE REGIONAL PROGRAMME AIMED AT SMALL ORGANISATIONS: under a civic space strengthening project the network HAS DECIDED TO JOIN FORCES TO SUPPORT THE NON-PROFIT INITIATIVES OF CENTRAL AMERICAN COUNTRIES BY MEANS OF ITS NETWORK OF LAWYERS TO PROVIDE FREE ADVICE TO APPLICANTS, with an application form; it also runs law student competitions and internship placements across member organisations. For the Central American countries there is a dedicated window rather than only the national clearinghouse. Use it, and note that the same network places law students who can do the document work.

trackers.name: The Alliance of Environmental Legal Clinics of Latin America and the Caribbean - more than 30 university clinics in 10 countries taking REAL, COLLECTIVE public-interest environmental cases free, with dam-affected and mining-affected communities among their clients
trackers.desc: MORE THAN THIRTY UNIVERSITY LEGAL CLINICS IN TEN COUNTRIES TAKE REAL ENVIRONMENTAL CASES FOR COMMUNITIES, FREE. The alliance ARTICULATES MORE THAN 30 CLINICS IN 10 COUNTRIES and has, since 2019, brought together universities WITH THE OBJECTIVE OF PROMOTING CLINICAL EDUCATION IN ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS AND STRENGTHENING THE FORMATION OF STUDENTS IN THE DEFENCE OF THE ENVIRONMENT AND HUMAN RIGHTS; one member clinic states that its course USES THE CLINICAL METHOD OF TEACHING LAW, BASED ON THE PRACTICE OF THE STUDENTS ON REAL AND NOT SIMULATED CASES, and that THESE CASES MUST ALWAYS BE OF PUBLIC INTEREST. Real cases, not exercises, and public interest is the entry condition. A community with a dispute and no money is what these clinics need in order to teach. WHAT THEY ARE, IN A CLINIC DIRECTOR'S WORDS: they are INSTANCES OF FORMAL TEACHING AND LEARNING AND AT THE SAME TIME OF SERVICE TO THE COMMUNITY AT A MOMENT WHEN THERE EXISTS A GREAT BARRIER OF ACCESS TO JUSTICE IN GENERAL; the initiative FOCUSES ON COLLECTIVE CASES AND EXERCISES THE DEFENCE OF ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS IN CASES OF PUBLIC INTEREST, seeking TO BALANCE THAT ASYMMETRY IN THE DEFENCE OF THE RIGHTS RELATED TO THE ENVIRONMENT. Collective cases are the speciality. Where the harm is shared by a whole village, that is the shape these clinics prefer, not a weakness in the claim. WHAT THEY HAVE ACTUALLY CARRIED: one university clinic CARRIES 22 CASES TO RESOLVE SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL AND PUBLIC HEALTH CONFLICTS in its country, including SUPPORT TO THE COMMUNITIES AFFECTED BY a named large dam, and a claim over mercury contamination from mining harming indigenous peoples; another works on mercury in the Amazon; students of two universities prepared AN AMICUS CURIAE in an unprecedented case on climate change and indigenous childhood; and in 2023 the network filed a report before the inter-American human rights court in an advisory opinion request on climate emergency, EXPRESSLY CITED IN THE FINAL DECISION. Twenty-two live cases in one clinic, and dam-affected communities among the clients. Ask the nearest clinic for its current case list before describing your own. THE OLDER NETWORK BESIDE IT, AND WHAT IT USES: a Latin American network of legal clinics aims TO STRENGTHEN CLINICAL TEACHING AND THROUGH THIS INSTRUMENT TO INTERVENE IN THE DEFENCE OF THE PUBLIC INTEREST AND HUMAN RIGHTS BY MEANS OF STRATEGIC LITIGATION AS A TOOL, its membership including named university clinics paired with human rights and environment centres in several cities. Some clinics are paired with an established rights centre. That combination gives a case both student capacity and an experienced litigating partner. HOW THEY WORK WITH COMMUNITIES: the method promotes ACTIVE LEARNING FROM THE APPROACH TO STATE ACTORS, CIVIL SOCIETY, LOCAL COMMUNITIES, EXPERTS... TO STRENGTHEN THE STRATEGIES OF APPROACHING THE CASES FROM EXPERIENCE; since 2022 the alliance also collaborates with a global network promoting STRUCTURED COLLABORATION BETWEEN UNIVERSITIES AND COMMUNITIES, sharing EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING, PARTICIPATORY PLANNING and social transformation. Structured collaboration between a university and a community is a defined programme, not a favour. Ask the clinic's coordinator which faculty course could adopt your case this term — the academic calendar, not the litigation calendar, decides when they can start.

trackers.name: Fondo de Acción Urgente para América Latina y el Caribe - rapid response grants of up to $5,000 decided in NO MORE THAN 10 WORKING DAYS for defenders under threat, plus a strategic window for organisations defending territories and common goods
trackers.desc: A REQUEST IS STUDIED IN NO MORE THAN TEN WORKING DAYS AND THE MONEY MOVES THREE DAYS AFTER APPROVAL. The fund's rapid response grants are A UNIQUE, FLEXIBLE, AND SHORT-TERM FINANCING MODEL... TO PROVIDE TIMELY AND STRATEGIC SUPPORT FOR ACTIONS THAT RESPOND TO SITUATIONS OF RISK OR THREATS THAT IMPACT THE SECURITY OF WOMEN ACTIVISTS AND DEFENDERS, THEIR COLLECTIVES, OR ORGANIZATIONS, or that TAKE ADVANTAGE OF OPPORTUNITIES TO ADVANCE OR DETER SETBACKS TO THE RIGHTS; ONCE A REQUEST IS RECEIVED, IT IS STUDIED DURING NO MORE THAN 10 WORKING DAYS. IF IT IS APPROVED, IT TAKES AT LEAST THREE WORKING DAYS TO TRANSFER THE RESOURCES, depending on each country's banking requirements. Applicants REGISTER their COLLECTIVE OR ORGANIZATION IN OUR ONLINE SYSTEM and make the request through it. Two weeks from request to money. When a defender has to leave home tonight or a hearing is next month, that is the only timescale in this file that matches the emergency. WHAT IT PAYS AND FOR HOW LONG: the support comprises FLEXIBLE RESOURCES (UP TO AN ALLOCATION OF 5,000 DOLLARS), GRANTED TO SUPPORT THE ACTIVISTS AND THEIR ORGANISATIONS IN A STRATEGIC AND TIMELY MANNER IN THE FACE OF UNFORESEEN AND UNPLANNED SITUATIONS THAT REQUIRE AN IMMEDIATE INTERVENTION, for a maximum of three months; THESE ACTIONS CANNOT BE ACTIVITIES OF PROGRAMMES AND/OR PROJECTS, and applicants MUST DEMONSTRATE THE URGENT CHARACTER OF THE UNFORESEEN AND UNPLANNED SITUATION. It will not pay for anything already in your workplan. Frame the request around what changed this month — the threat, the eviction date, the hearing — and nothing else. THE SECOND WINDOW, WHICH IS ABOUT TERRITORY: alongside the rapid grants the fund gives STRATEGIC SUPPORTS: TO STRENGTHEN THE PROCESSES OF RESISTANCE AND THE STRATEGIES OF THE ORGANISATIONS LED BY WOMEN, TRANS, NON-BINARY OR GENDER-DISSIDENT PEOPLE, THAT PROMOTE IN AN INTEGRATED MANNER THE PROTECTION OF THE TERRITORIES, THE COMMON GOODS AND THE RIGHTS; one recorded call was directed at LOCAL, DEPARTMENTAL OR NATIONAL ORGANISATIONS AND COLLECTIVES OF WOMEN AND/OR FEMINISTS THAT HAVE PERMANENT WORK AROUND THE DEFENCE OF THE TERRITORIES AND NATURE, and at MIXED COMMUNITY, INDIGENOUS, AFRO-DESCENDANT, RAIZAL AND PEASANT ORGANISATIONS THAT HAVE A SPECIFIC LINE OF WORK ON WOMEN'S RIGHTS LINKED TO ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE, AND IN WHICH WOMEN HAVE SIGNIFICANT LEADERSHIP. Mixed community, indigenous and peasant organisations qualify for the territorial window, not only women's organisations, provided women lead a strand of the work. That is a wider door than the fund's name suggests. WHO IT IS AND WHERE IT REACHES: it is THE REGIONAL FEMINIST FUND FOR SPANISH-SPEAKING LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, created in 2009 in one national capital as part of a global urgent action fund founded in 1997 that regionalised IN ORDER TO UNDERSTAND LOCAL CONTEXTS BETTER AND TO BE CLOSER TO THE WORK SITES OF GRASSROOTS ACTIVISTS, now AN INTERNATIONAL ALLIANCE OF THREE AUTONOMOUS SISTER FUNDS. Spanish-speaking countries only for this fund. If you are in Brazil, Guyana, Suriname, Haiti or the English-speaking Caribbean, ask which sister fund covers you before applying. WHAT IT FUNDS THE MONEY FOR: recorded lines are PROTECTION AND SECURITY, RESPONDING TO SITUATIONS OF RISK OR THREAT AGAINST THE SECURITY OF ACTIVISTS AND DEFENDERS, THEIR COLLECTIVES OR ORGANISATIONS, and opportunity grants that let a movement act before a window closes. Security costs — relocation, a lawyer's retainer, travel to a hearing — are exactly what this covers, and they are the costs that no project grant in this file will pay.

trackers.name: Protection grants for defenders at risk - up to €7,500 for LEGAL FEES OF THOSE BEING JUDICIALLY HARASSED, physical and digital security, medical and family costs, with a 24-hour hotline, plus emergency, relocation, trial-monitoring and respite programmes
trackers.desc: THESE GRANTS PAY THE LEGAL FEES OF SOMEONE BEING SUED OR PROSECUTED FOR DEFENDING LAND. The protection grants programme, launched in 2001 TO PROVIDE RAPID AND PRACTICAL FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS AT RISK, pays for IMPROVING PHYSICAL SECURITY OF AN ORGANISATION OR INDIVIDUAL, DIGITAL SECURITY AND COMMUNICATION SECURITY; SUPPORTING LEGAL FEES FOR HRDs WHO ARE BEING JUDICIALLY HARASSED; PAYING FOR MEDICAL FEES FOR HRDs WHO HAVE BEEN ATTACKED OR WHO HAVE SUFFERED A MEDICAL CONDITION AS A RESULT OF THEIR PEACEFUL HUMAN RIGHTS ACTIVITIES; PROVIDING FAMILY ASSISTANCE FOR IMPRISONED HRDs OR FAMILY MEMBERS WHO ARE AT RISK BECAUSE OF A HRD'S ACTIVITIES, up to a maximum of €7,500. Applications CAN BE SUBMITTED ANYTIME VIA THEIR ONLINE SYSTEM, and there is a 24-HOUR EMERGENCY HOTLINE. A criminal complaint or a defamation suit filed by a developer is judicial harassment, and the legal fees are payable. That is the single most common attack on land defenders in this file, and this is the grant written for it. WHAT IT WILL NOT FUND, WHICH DECIDES HOW YOU WRITE IT: the programme excludes RETROSPECTIVE FUNDING, INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS, ORGANISATIONS THAT HAVE APPLIED OR ARE ALREADY RECEIVING FUNDING FOR THE SAME PURPOSE ELSEWHERE, PROJECTS WHICH FOCUS ON BROADER HUMAN RIGHTS ISSUES RATHER THAN THE SPECIFIC SITUATION OF HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, COSTS FOR HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS WHO ARE ALREADY IN EXILE and ongoing office running costs; grants ARE GENERALLY NOT AWARDED FOR 100% OF THE PROPOSED BUDGET, and applicants must commit to return the grant if the work does not go ahead or is funded elsewhere. Write about the named people at risk, not about the campaign. A proposal that describes the environmental issue rather than the threat to specific defenders is refused on its own terms. THE OTHER EMERGENCY FUNDS THAT COVER THE SAME GROUND: a European defenders mechanism provides EMERGENCY GRANTS UP TO 10,000€ and runs a TEMPORARY RELOCATION PROGRAMME that funds a host organisation to relocate a defender, responding to AN INCREASED RISK, AN ANTICIPATED INCREASED RISK OR FOR A HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDER WHO HAS BEEN WORKING IN A DIFFICULT ENVIRONMENT FOR A PROLONGED PERIOD OF TIME AND WHO NEEDS A BREAK, covering REST AND RESPITE, PROFESSIONAL CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT... EMOTIONAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL WELL-BEING, FAMILY SUPPORT; a civil society lifeline fund covers LEGAL REPRESENTATION, PRISON VISITS, TRIAL MONITORING, TEMPORARY RELOCATION, EQUIPMENT REPLACEMENT, applying by email after describing a secure contact method, in several languages including Spanish; and a federation offers SECURE TRANSPORTATION, LEGAL SUPPORT, MEDICAL SUPPORT... HUMANITARIAN ASSISTANCE... URGENT RELOCATION, URGENT MONITORING. Trial monitoring is fundable, and so is a paid observer at the hearing. Where a case is being heard in a small town, an outside monitor changes how it is conducted. THE RESPITE OPTIONS WHEN SOMEONE MUST LEAVE: recorded schemes include a protective fellowship allowing UP TO TEN DEFENDERS PER YEAR to join a university centre FOR THE PURPOSES OF TRAINING, NETWORKING, AND REST, a foundation offering A YEAR LONG RESPITE PROGRAMME, a refuge for journalists forced to flee providing ADMINISTRATIVE, LEGAL AND SOCIAL ASSISTANCE, and a cities of refuge network offering PHYSICAL SAFETY AND ECONOMIC SECURITY FOR A TWO-YEARS FIXED PERIOD. Leaving for a year is not the end of a campaign if someone else can hold the file. Identify who that is before the threat arrives, because these programmes take applications from the person at risk and their host, not from a court. THE SECURITY WARNING BUILT INTO THE APPLICATION: applicants are asked to ENSURE THAT THE METHOD OF CONTACT YOU ARE PROVIDING IS SECURE AND THAT IT IS OK TO BE CONTACTED IN THAT WAY, and one fund asks applicants to describe HOW it CAN CONTACT YOU SECURELY BEFORE SENDING SENSITIVE INFORMATION. Do not send the details from a shared community email account. The application itself can expose the person it is meant to protect.

trackers.name: Inter-American Foundation grants - CURRENTLY PAUSED - direct grants of $25,000-$400,000 to grassroots organisations with no sector calls, no deadline, five application languages, and LAND AND LABOUR accepted as counterpart
trackers.desc: THIS FUNDER IS CURRENTLY PAUSED — CHECK BEFORE SPENDING TIME ON IT. Its own application page states: WE ARE CURRENTLY PAUSING GRANT FUNDING IN ALIGNMENT WITH EXECUTIVE ORDER REEVALUATING AND REALIGNING UNITED STATES FOREIGN AID. CHECK THIS PAGE FOR FURTHER UPDATES. It is AN INDEPENDENT AGENCY of that government. Everything below describes how it worked when open, and is recorded because the terms are unusual enough to be worth watching for. Read the page before writing anything. A funder under a foreign aid review can reopen with different rules, and the counterpart and eligibility terms are the first things such reviews change. WHY IT MATTERED: IT FUNDED GRASSROOTS GROUPS DIRECTLY, WITH NO INTERMEDIARY: it ONLY SUPPORT[S] COMMUNITY-LED PROJECTS SUBMITTED BY LOCAL AND GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS THAT ARE BASED IN INDEPENDENT COUNTRIES OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, requiring proof that YOUR ORGANIZATION HAS A HISTORY OF WORKING TOGETHER AS A GROUP AND IS CAPABLE OF EFFECTIVELY USING GRANTS FUNDS; it DOES NOT IDENTIFY PROBLEMS OR SUGGEST PROJECTS; INSTEAD IT RESPONDS TO INITIATIVES PRESENTED, and PROJECTS ARE SELECTED FOR FUNDING ON THEIR MERITS RATHER THAN BY SECTOR. Grants ran FROM US$25,000 TO $400,000 OVER ONE TO FOUR YEARS, with proposals accepted 365 DAYS A YEAR in SPANISH, PORTUGUESE, ENGLISH, FRENCH, OR HAITIAN CREOLE. No sector calls, no themes, no deadline. A community proposing its own solution in its own language is the entire model, and it is worth having a proposal ready if the pause lifts. THE COUNTERPART RULE, WHICH IS THE PART TO UNDERSTAND: all funded organisations must COMMIT RESOURCES TO ADVANCE THEIR DEVELOPMENT INITIATIVES, called counterpart; COUNTERPART FUNDING MUST BE A COMPONENT OF THE BUDGET... BUT NO MINIMUM AMOUNT IS REQUIRED. HIGHER COUNTERPART FUNDING MAKES A PROPOSAL MORE ATTRACTIVE, and it MAY BE IN CASH DONATIONS OR IN KIND, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, LAND, SUPPLIES, INFRASTRUCTURE, LABOR, AND OFFICE, STORAGE AND MEETING SPACE. Salaries are A LEGITIMATE EXPENSE. Land and volunteer labour count as counterpart. A community that owns the site and works it has already met the requirement without spending anything. WHAT IT LOOKED FOR IN A PROPOSAL: CREATIVE USE OF THE COMMUNITY'S RESOURCES; A DIVERSE ARRAY OF COMMUNITY VOICES IN PROJECT DEVELOPMENT AND EXECUTION; SUBSTANTIAL BENEFICIARY ENGAGEMENT in identifying the problem, choosing the approach, designing the project and managing it; PARTNERSHIPS WITH LOCAL GOVERNMENT, THE BUSINESS COMMUNITY AND OTHER CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS; feasibility, sustainability, measurable results and EVIDENCE OF BENEFICIARIES' ENHANCED CAPACITY FOR SELF-GOVERNANCE; its recorded interests included COMMUNITY CONSERVATION; AND LOCAL MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES (FORESTS, FISHERIES, ETC.). Partnership with the local government is a scoring criterion. That is the argument for bringing your municipality into the proposal rather than fighting it. THE EXCLUSIONS AND THE FIELD OFFICE RULE: support was limited to independent countries of the region, with recorded exclusions of two countries and a period when FUNDING IN THE CARIBBEAN was RESTRICTED TO three named states; public universities could not apply directly BUT MAY PARTNER WITH AN ORGANIZATION THAT IS ELIGIBLE; and an organisation headquartered abroad could apply only if its field office CAN DEMONSTRATE LOCAL LEADERSHIP. Local leadership had to be demonstrated, not asserted. Where an outside NGO offers to apply on your behalf, insist that your own organisation is the applicant.

trackers.name: RedLAC - the network of 32 national and regional ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS in 20 countries, permanent conservation trust institutions financing protected areas and local communities, with a published member list by country and zone
trackers.desc: THIRTY-TWO NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS IN TWENTY COUNTRIES, AND THE NETWORK PUBLISHES WHICH ONE COVERS YOURS. It GROUPS 32 ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS FROM 20 COUNTRIES OF THE REGION, UNITING EFFORTS TO PROTECT THE RICH BIODIVERSITY OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, with its member list filterable by zone — Caribbean, Mesoamerica and South America — alongside regional funds; more than twenty-five years old, it counts MORE THAN 100 ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS WORLDWIDE. Find the fund for your country on that member page. These are permanent national institutions with endowments, not project offices that close when a grant ends. WHAT THESE FUNDS DO, IN THE NETWORK'S WORDS: they HAVE DEMONSTRATED TO BE A KEY MECHANISM IN THE SUSTAINABLE FINANCING OF BIODIVERSITY AND IN THE STRENGTHENING OF PROTECTED AREAS AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, with a role in THE PROTECTION OF NATURAL AREAS AND THE SUPPORT TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES, described as MULTIDIMENSIONAL FUNDS, WITH APPROACHES THAT INTEGRATE PROTECTION OF BIODIVERSITY, CLIMATIC RESILIENCE AND COMMUNITY EMPOWERMENT. Support to local communities is named alongside protected areas. A community managing land next to a park is inside the mandate, not adjacent to it. SOME OF THE MEMBERS BY NAME AND KIND: recorded members include a Caribbean biodiversity fund, a national forever-protection association in one Central American country, an action fund and a Pacific foundation in one Andean country, a nature fund in one southern country, an island life fund and a regional marine fund — the last two showing that funds exist for a single archipelago and for a shared sea as well as for whole countries. There are funds scoped to one archipelago and to one reef system. If your site sits in either, that narrower fund is a better fit than the national one. WHAT THE NETWORK ITSELF OFFERS ITS MEMBERS: joining gives funds THE OPPORTUNITY TO CONNECT AND COLLABORATE WITH OTHER MEMBERS OF THE NETWORK THROUGHOUT THE REGION, to SHARE KNOWLEDGE, RESOURCES AND EXPERIENCES TO IMPROVE THEIR CAPACITIES, and ACCESS TO A WIDE VARIETY OF RESOURCES AND TOOLS, with TRAINING AND ADVICE ON DIVERSE THEMES, FROM PROJECT MANAGEMENT TO COMMUNICATION AND ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION. Where your country has no environmental fund, this network is where one would be built, and it trains new members. That is a long project, but it is the route. WHY THEY MATTER FOR PERMANENT PROTECTION: these funds are conservation trust funds — institutions holding capital whose returns finance protected areas and community work year after year, and the network works alongside a global environment facility, an African funds consortium and a large conservation finance initiative on that model. An endowment pays for wardens and monitoring long after a campaign ends. Where a protected area has just been declared, the next question is which of these funds can endow its running costs.

trackers.name: The ICCA Consortium and the international register of territories of life - a community-reviewed register open to any well-defined community with its own governance, plus national catalytic organisations, documentation workshops and life plan support
trackers.desc: A COMMUNITY CAN PUT ITS OWN TERRITORY ON AN INTERNATIONAL REGISTER, REVIEWED BY OTHER COMMUNITIES RATHER THAN BY OFFICIALS. The international register IS A TOOL DEVELOPED TO SERVE AS SUPPORT AND RECOGNITION TO THOSE COMMUNITIES WITH OUTSTANDING VALUES IN GOVERNANCE AND CONSERVATION OF NATURE, run by a United Nations environment body with the consortium and a commons organisation; its PEER REVIEW PROTOCOL is A CONSENSUS DOCUMENT IN WHICH THE DIFFERENT STEPS THAT EACH COMMUNITY MUST TAKE IN ORDER TO FORM PART OF THE REGISTER ARE DESCRIBED, including SUBMITTING TO A PROCESS OF REVIEW OF THE CANDIDATURE BY ANONYMOUS MEMBERS (REVIEWERS) OF OTHER SIMILAR COMMUNITIES THAT ALREADY FORM PART OF THE REGISTER. Other communities judge the application, and the protocol is published so you can read the test before applying. Registration is a public record of who governs the land, made without asking the state's permission. WHAT QUALIFIES AS ONE OF THESE TERRITORIES: they exist IN ANY TYPE OF CULTURE AND ECOSYSTEM WHERE THERE IS A COMMUNITY LINKED TO A TERRITORY, WITH ITS OWN SYSTEM OF GOVERNANCE, AND THAT GIVES POSITIVE RESULTS IN TERMS OF CONSERVATION OF NATURE AND LIVELIHOODS FOR THE COMMUNITY; the first defining characteristic is that THE AREA OR TERRITORY MUST HAVE A WELL DEFINED COMMUNITY, WITH A CLEAR LINK TO A TERRITORY ALSO WELL DEFINED. A well defined community and a well defined territory. Neither a formal title nor a state designation is in that test. WHO THE CONSORTIUM IS AND WHAT ITS MEMBERS DO: it is AN INTERNATIONAL NON-PROFIT ASSOCIATION DEDICATED TO SUPPORTING INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES THAT GOVERN AND CONSERVE THEIR LANDS, WATERS AND TERRITORIES, its members from more than eighty countries acting on themes including THE DOCUMENTATION, SUSTAINING AND DEFENCE OF THE TERRITORIES OF LIFE, and comprising ALMOST 180 MEMBERS (ORGANISATIONS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND COMMUNITY ORGANISATIONS, TOGETHER WITH THE CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS THAT SUPPORT THEM) AND MORE THAN 420 HONORARY MEMBERS. Community organisations are members in their own right, alongside the NGOs that support them. Ask the national focal point how your organisation joins. WHAT THE REGIONAL NETWORK ACTUALLY DELIVERS: the Latin American network runs workshops WITH THE AIM OF SHARING KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERIENCES COMING FROM THE TERRITORIES, including a practical workshop on the register itself, a case study workshop drawing on one country's experience, and one on a GUIDE OF SELF-STRENGTHENING: A GUIDE FROM COMMUNITIES FOR COMMUNITIES; communities are recorded pursuing PROCESSES OF DOCUMENTATION, THE CONSTRUCTION OF LIFE PLANS, THE register AND THE STRENGTHENING OF THEIR OWN GOVERNANCE. A life plan is the document that states what a community will and will not permit on its land. Building one is the work these workshops exist to support. WHAT IT HAS SUPPORTED ON THE GROUND: in one country an observatory and a named indigenous community organised A WORKSHOP OF EXCHANGE OF KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERIENCES, ATTENDED BY TWENTY-FIVE REPRESENTATIVES OF TEN INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, TO EXCHANGE ABOUT LEGAL AND NON-LEGAL STRATEGIES OF TERRITORIAL DEFENCE AND PROTECTION; in another, five indigenous peoples, an Afro-descendant community and a coastal community met with a foundation and the small grants programme TO DEBATE AND DECIDE ON THE WORLD REGISTER; national members have planned A STUDY OF THE EXISTING LEGAL FRAMEWORK ON CONSERVATION AND RIGHTS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, ACTIONS FOR COMMUNITY STRENGTHENING AND A NATIONAL ADVOCACY STRATEGY; a global support initiative works through NATIONAL CATALYTIC ORGANISATIONS in more than twenty-six priority countries. Ask which organisation is the national catalytic body for your country. It is the one already funded to accompany communities through documentation and registration.

trackers.name: Mapeo and its successor - a free, offline, open-source mapping and evidence toolset built with Amazonian indigenous partners, where ALL DATA IS OWNED BY THE COMMUNITY, exporting shapefiles and reports for lawsuits and land claims
trackers.desc: A FREE OFFLINE APP THAT TURNS A PHONE INTO AN EVIDENCE RECORDER, AND THE COMMUNITY KEEPS THE DATA. It is A FREE DIGITAL TOOLSET FOR DOCUMENTING, MONITORING, AND MAPPING MANY TYPES OF DATA, OFFLINE-FIRST OPEN-SOURCE TECHNOLOGY needing NO INTERNET OR SPECIAL HARDWARE... TO COLLECT, VIEW, OR SHARE DATA; WITH THE PUSH OF A BUTTON, CONTRIBUTORS CAN GATHER MAP DATA BY LINKING GPS POINTS, PHOTOS, AND NOTES, and ALL DATA IS COMPLETELY OWNED BY THE COMMUNITIES THEMSELVES, exchanged between phones by a peer-to-peer sync that works OVER A LOCAL WIFI NETWORK WITHOUT NEEDING A CONNECTION. No signal, no server, no subscription, and nobody else holds the file. For a community watching a road survey or a clearing crew, that is the difference between a rumour and an exhibit. WHAT IT WAS BUILT TO BE USED FOR: it was CO-DESIGNED AND DEVELOPED WITH INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES WHO FACE THREATS TO THEIR LAND SUCH AS ILLEGAL GOLD MINING, OIL CONTAMINATION AND POACHING, and built TO SUPPORT THEM TO DOCUMENT THESE ACTIVITIES IN ORDER TO TAKE COMMUNITY ACTION AGAINST THEM, TO REPORT THEM TO AUTHORITIES, FILE LAWSUITS, LAUNCH MEDIA CAMPAIGNS, OR CREATE MAPS FOR LAND CLAIMS; it allows USERS TO COLLECT EVIDENCE IN THE FIELD, SUCH AS PHOTOGRAPHS AND GPS POINTS, AND ORGANIZE THIS DATA FOR ACTIONS SUCH AS WHISTLEBLOWING AND CLAIMING LAND RIGHTS. Filing a lawsuit and making a map for a land claim are the stated purposes. Set up the categories to match what a court or a ministry will ask for, before the incursion happens. THE CASE THAT SHOWS WHAT IT IS WORTH: in one country OVER TWENTY indigenous COMMUNITIES DEFENDED THEIR TERRITORY... AGAINST THE IMPOSITION OF DEVASTATING OIL EXPLORATION PROPOSED BY THE GOVERNMENT, having USED the tool FOR OVER FOUR YEARS TO RECORD TERRITORIAL DATA ...AND MAPS, WHICH THEY USED AS EVIDENCE AGAINST THE government; the account records: THEY WON! Four years of routine recording before the case existed. The evidence that wins these cases is gathered long before anyone knows there will be a case. WHAT COMES OUT OF IT, AND IN WHICH LANGUAGES: export options include PDF OR PRINT REPORT, GEOJSON, CSV OR SHAPEFILE from the desktop version and direct sharing from the phone; the interface IS AVAILABLE IN LOCAL LANGUAGES, AND ALSO HAS AN IN-BUILT TRANSLATION FEATURE, supporting THE UNDERSERVED DIALECTS OF INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES; one community leader records that IT IS SO EASY TO USE THAT EVEN OUR ELDERS — WHO DO NOT SPEAK SPANISH — USE IT. A newer version adds audio, tracks and routes. A shapefile is what a planning office and a court will accept. Elders who do not speak the national language can gather it themselves, which also answers the objection that the data was collected by outsiders. THE SUPPORT AROUND THE TOOL: the developers publish TRAINING AND TECHNICAL RESOURCES, a COMPLETE REFERENCE GUIDE... ON PLANNING AND IMPLEMENTING PROJECTS and customisation of the tools, and a defenders toolkit site; a dedicated version was built with a United Nations monitoring centre and a forest peoples organisation so that custodian communities can MAP, MONITOR AND SUPPORT THEIR TERRITORIES OF LIFE ON THEIR TERMS and may, SHOULD THEY WISH TO, CONTRIBUTE TO GLOBAL CONSERVATION DATABASES. Contributing to the global database is optional and separate. Decide as a community what stays local before the first survey, because that choice is hard to reverse once data is shared.

trackers.name: Global Forest Watch - free near-real-time deforestation alerts by email for any drawn area, an offline field app that walks patrols to the clearing, and a small grants fund whose examples include GETTING CONCESSIONS REVOKED and compiling evidence for formal complaints
trackers.desc: YOU CAN SUBSCRIBE TO EMAIL ALERTS FOR A SINGLE PLOT OF FOREST AND BE TOLD WITHIN DAYS WHEN TREES ARE CUT. The platform is FREE AND SIMPLE TO USE, ENABLING ANYONE TO CREATE CUSTOM MAPS, ANALYZE FOREST TRENDS, SUBSCRIBE TO ALERTS, OR DOWNLOAD DATA FOR THEIR LOCAL AREA OR THE ENTIRE WORLD, providing NEAR-REAL-TIME ALERTS SHOWING SUSPECTED LOCATIONS OF RECENT TREE COVER LOSS; it moved BEYOND ANNUAL DATA ON FORESTS to MONTHLY AND WEEKLY DEFORESTATION ALERTS, with EMAIL SUBSCRIPTIONS bringing them DIRECTLY INTO THE HANDS OF USERS. Users CAN SIGN UP FOR ALERTS AND DOWNLOAD DATASETS WITHOUT ANY SUBSCRIPTION OR LICENSING FEE. Draw the boundary of the land you are defending and subscribe. From then on the clearing tells you rather than the other way round, and the date stamp is independent of anything the developer says. THE FIELD APP THAT WORKS WITHOUT SIGNAL: a companion mobile application ALLOWS RANGERS TO ACCESS the data and alerts OFFLINE, WHICH IS CRITICAL IN AREAS WITH LIMITED TO NO CELL SIGNAL; USING CACHED DATA, THE APP DIRECTS USERS TO NEARBY FOREST CLEARING AND ENABLES THEM TO CAPTURE PHOTOS AND FILL OUT FORMS ABOUT DEFORESTATION, WHICH ARE UPLOADED NEXT TIME THEIR DEVICE CONNECTS, so that patrols KNOW EXACTLY WHERE TO LOOK... AND STOP THE ILLEGAL ACTIVITY BEFORE IT GETS OUT OF CONTROL; it is FREE, OPEN SOURCE, AND AVAILABLE IN ENGLISH, SPANISH, PORTUGUESE, FRENCH, AND BAHASA INDONESIAN. The alert gives the coordinates and the app walks you to them. A ground photograph taken at a satellite-flagged point, on a known date, is the evidence a prosecutor can use. THE GRANT ATTACHED TO IT, AND WHAT IT HAS PAID FOR: a small grants fund SEEKS TO BUILD THE CAPACITY OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS TO EFFECTIVELY USE the tools TO REDUCE ILLEGAL OR UNPLANNED DEFORESTATION; funded project types include USING DATA AND IMAGERY... ALONGSIDE COMMUNITY TERRITORIAL MAPS TO ADVOCATE FOR LAND TITLES AND OTHER STRENGTHENED LAND RIGHTS; CROWDSOURCING, COMPILING AND PUBLISHING DATA ON CONCESSIONS THAT OVERLAP WITH ANCESTRAL COMMUNITY LANDS, AND SUPPORT COMMUNITIES IN APPLYING PUBLIC PRESSURE TO GET THESE CONCESSIONS REVOKED; DEVELOPING THE CAPACITY OF FOREST MONITORING BRIGADES TO CONDUCT FIELD VERIFICATIONS OF NEAR-REAL TIME ALERTS; and SUPPORTING INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES IN DEVELOPING RESPONSE PROTOCOLS, FORMULATING LEGAL STRATEGIES AND COMPILING EVIDENCE OF ILLEGAL DEFORESTATION INCLUDING SATELLITE IMAGERY, DATA AND ANALYSES, AND SUBMITTING IT TO LAW ENFORCEMENT THROUGH FORMAL COMPLAINTS OR OTHER LEGAL PROCESSES. Getting concessions revoked and compiling evidence for formal complaints are funded project types, written into the fund's own examples. That is the grant to cite when describing what you intend to do. THE DEADLINE DISCIPLINE: the fund runs an annual call, and the platform states of a recent round: THE CALL FOR APPLICATIONS HAS CLOSED AS OF THE DEADLINE... WE CANNOT GRANT ANY EXTENSIONS, advising applicants to PREPARE FOR THE NEXT CALL FOR APPLICATIONS BY REVIEWING the current materials, while noting that SOME ITEMS IN THE GUIDELINES FOR APPLICANTS MAY CHANGE YEAR TO YEAR. One deadline a year, strictly enforced. Download this year's guidelines now and write the proposal before the next call opens. WHO ELSE IS ALREADY USING IT: the platform serves GOVERNMENTS, THE PRIVATE SECTOR, NGOs, JOURNALISTS, UNIVERSITIES, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC, and is convened as a partnership of OVER 200 ORGANIZATIONS; a fellowship accompanies the grants. Your municipality and your national forest agency can subscribe to the same alerts you do. Sending them the alert with a covering letter turns your observation into their file.

trackers.name: Public Lab and the open science hardware community - free open-source, low-cost instruments and toolkits communities build themselves for water, air, soil and land use, plus BALLOON AND KITE AERIAL MAPPING with stitching software and an open question forum

RANGING FROM WATER QUALITY SENSORS TO INDOOR AIR QUALITY AND KITE MAPPING KITS; its tools and data are CREATED BY THE community, OPEN SOURCE, AND TYPICALLY INEXPENSIVE TO USE. Its earliest technique was LOW-ALTITUDE AERIAL MAPPING WITH BALLOONS AND KITES with software to stitch the photographs into a map. A kite, a camera and free stitching software produce a dated aerial photograph of a site at a resolution no public satellite gives you. That is how you show what a hillside looked like before the machines arrived. TO ADDRESS AN ENORMOUS GAP IN COMMUNITY KNOWLEDGE ABOUT THE IMPACTS OF THE SPILL, launching AS AN OPEN SOURCE PLATFORM, COLLECTING DATA AND MAPS OF THE COASTLINE OVER TIME TO SHOW THE COAST BEFORE, DURING, AND AFTER THE SPILL. Before, during and after is the sequence that wins arguments about damage. Start the baseline photographs now, while there is still a before. WHAT THE PLATFORM ACTUALLY GIVES YOU: it is A PLATFORM FOR COMMUNITY SCIENCE PRACTITIONERS WORKING ON ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES TO DOCUMENT THEIR WORK, SHARE TOOLS FOR ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING AND ADVOCACY, AND CONNECT WITH EACH OTHER; THE COMMUNITY IS OPEN AND FREE FOR ANYONE TO JOIN, members CAN ADD THEIR OWN PROJECT PAGE TO DOCUMENT THEIR METHODS AND SHARE EXPERTISE, and users CAN BROWSE LOW-COST ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING TOOLS FOR APPLICATION AREAS SUCH AS AIR QUALITY, LAND USE, STORMWATER, alongside ADVOCACY METHODS, AND ACTION TOOLKITS BY SCIENCE TOPICS covering WATER, SOIL, AIR, INDUSTRY, CLIMATE, ORGANIZING, AND MONITORING; COMMUNITY MEMBERS CAN ASK OR ANSWER QUESTIONS. Post the question with your site's details. Somebody has usually measured the same pollutant with the same cheap instrument and will say what went wrong the first time. THE KINDS OF INSTRUMENT PEOPLE HAVE BUILT: recorded tools include a spectrometer made from LEGO OR CARDBOARD, WEBCAMS OR RASPBERRY PI CAMERAS, RECYCLED DVDs so that SPECTROSCOPY IS A RESEARCH METHOD THAT ANYONE CAN EXPLORE; a SIMPLE AIR SENSOR whose REALTIME READOUT CHANGES COLOR WHEN THE SENSOR READS DIFFERENCES IN AIR QUALITY, usable WITHOUT HAVING TO LEARN HOW TO PROGRAM; a low-budget water kit with probes MEASURING TEMPERATURE, DISSOLVED OXYGEN AND CONDUCTIVITY, developed to measure sewage outfalls after storms; a DIY device to TEST FOR HEAVY METALS IN WATER; DIY infrared cameras; and a marine microplastics trawler. Dissolved oxygen, conductivity and heavy metals are the readings that show a river has been damaged. A community that takes them weekly for a year has a record no consultant's single sample can rebut. WHAT THE WIDER COMMUNITY ADDS: a water data collaborative HELPS GUIDE COMMUNITY GROUPS ON HOW TO ADOPT DIY, OPEN HARDWARE METHODS FOR COLLECTING THE QUALITY OF WATER DATA THEY NEED TO ACHIEVE THEIR OUTCOMES, alongside research centres publishing open hardware loggers, and an annual gathering for open science hardware makes tools ACCESSIBLE THROUGH OPEN-SOURCE LICENSING; recorded projects include WATER MONITORING IN THE AMAZON. Decide what outcome the data is for before choosing the instrument. A reading that will go to a court needs a different protocol from one that will go to a public meeting, and these groups will tell you which.

trackers.name: Asociación Interamericana para la Defensa del Ambiente (AIDA) - a regional team of Latin American lawyers AND scientists giving FREE legal and technical support to communities harmed by environmental damage, litigating through national and international human rights law

Scientists and lawyers in the same team, both free. International human rights law applied to a local environmental case. Where the national courts have closed, that is the route this organisation was built to open. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY DONE: recorded work includes a long campaign in one Andean town where it FOUGHT THE POISONING OF THE POPULATION BY HEAVY METALS AND OTHER CONTAMINANTS EMITTED BY A LOCAL SMELTER, and significant impact on the protection of a sea turtle in a Central American country THROUGH AN ASSOCIATION WITH a national environmental law organisation. Its method is to work through a national organisation rather than around it. Approach it together with the environmental lawyers already in your country, which makes acceptance more likely. WHO IT IS AND WHERE ITS PARTNERS ARE: founded in 1998 by five environmental law groups from four Latin American countries and one northern one TO BUILD AND EXTEND THE CAPACITIES OF NATIONAL DEFENDERS, it WORKS WITH PARTNERS IN COUNTRIES SUCH AS ARGENTINA, CANADA, CHILE, COLOMBIA, COSTA RICA, ECUADOR, MEXICO AND PERU, with recorded legal work also in Brazil; it is a member of an international land coalition. Ask which national organisation is its partner in your country. That is the door, and the partner list is published by the coalitions it belongs to. THE CAPACITY IT ADDS BEYOND ONE CASE: its stated aim is TO STRENGTHEN THE CAPACITY OF PEOPLE TO GUARANTEE THE INDIVIDUAL AND COLLECTIVE RIGHT TO A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT... THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT, IMPLEMENTATION AND EFFECTIVE ENFORCEMENT OF NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL LAW, and it seeks to ensure that INTERNATIONAL POLICIES, LAWS AND FINANCIAL FLOWS CONTRIBUTE TO THE PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT; it runs legal internships placing law students on country work. Financial flows are named among its targets. Where a project depends on an international bank or investor, that is a second front this organisation already works on.

trackers.name: Accountability Counsel - free support for communities complaining to the accountability offices of banks financing a harmful project, taking cases ONLY WHERE THE COMMUNITY ASKS, plus a searchable global complaints database and a resource guide

A complaint to a bank's own accountability office runs alongside any court case rather than replacing it. Ask for the training even if you never file: it maps every route available against a financed project. WHAT IT HAS ACHIEVED, INCLUDING IN THIS REGION: recorded results include supporting communities TO PREVENT ABUSES IN MEXICO and elsewhere, TO COMPEL REDESIGN OF A PROJECT in one country and TO REACH HISTORIC AGREEMENTS in others including one Caribbean state; its impact includes REDESIGNED PROJECTS THAT NOW REFLECT COMMUNITY NEEDS, HARM STOPPED AND PREVENTED TO DEFEND WATER RESOURCES, AND AGREEMENTS RESULTING IN COMPENSATION. Redesign, prevention and compensation are the realistic outcomes. A complaint of this kind rarely cancels a project outright, and knowing that before starting keeps a community's expectations intact. THE DATABASE AND GUIDE ANYONE CAN USE: it runs THE WORLD'S MOST COMPREHENSIVE COMMUNITY COMPLAINT DATABASE — SEARCH BY REGION, SECTOR, INSTITUTION, TYPE OF HARM, and a comparison of accountability policies ACROSS SIXTEEN INSTITUTIONS; its resource guide contains INFORMATION ABOUT TOOLS FOR REDRESSING HUMAN RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL VIOLATIONS BY INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS, EXPORT PROMOTION AGENCIES, AND PRIVATE CORPORATE ACTORS, intended TO ASSIST COMMUNITY LEADERS, LAWYERS, NGOs, AND INDIVIDUALS IN DETERMINING WHAT RIGHTS THEY HAVE AND HOW TO FILE A COMPLAINT, and it also covers INFORMATION DISCLOSURE RULES at those institutions. Search the database for your sector before writing anything. Someone has complained about a comparable project and the outcome tells you what to ask for. WHICH OFFICES EXIST, AND WHERE THE GAPS ARE: the offices it works with include those of the regional development bank for this continent, the world bank's public and private arms, a climate fund, a development programme's compliance unit and one national development bank's ombudsperson; it records that THERE ARE MANY COMMUNITIES THAT LACK AN AVAILABLE ACCOUNTABILITY OPTION BECAUSE NO SUCH ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICE EXISTS AT THE INSTITUTION(S) FINANCING A PROJECT, and works to open avenues where investment has none, INCLUDING IMPACT INVESTMENT, PRIVATE EQUITY, AND FINANCING FROM CHINESE INSTITUTIONS; its advocacy removed a requirement that complainants cite specific policy violations, since PREVIOUSLY A COMPLAINT COULD BE REJECTED IF IT DID NOT CONTAIN THIS TECHNICAL INFORMATION. Identify the financier before assuming there is a complaint office. Where the money is private equity or a Chinese lender there may be none, and that absence is itself worth publicising.

IS PERPETUATED BY THE STATE IN ALLIANCE WITH THE CORPORATIONS WITH INTEREST IN THEIR TERRITORIES, and another with AN ALARMING DISPOSSESSION OF LANDS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND AFRO-DESCENDANT COMMUNITIES, BECAUSE OF THE EXPANSION OF THE AGRICULTURAL FRONTIER. An independent index that contradicts the government's own monitoring, country by country. Quote your country's score back at the ministry that claims consultation works. THE LAND DEAL DATABASE AND ITS REGIONAL FOCAL POINT: a global land acquisitions observatory names a regional focal point organisation for Latin America and coordinates national pilot land observatories in several countries with the coalition. WHAT ITS OWN ANALYSIS SAYS ABOUT THIS REGION: land IS AT THE CENTRE OF DIVERSE CONFLICTS IN THE REGION, WHERE THE HIGHEST NUMBER OF ATTACKS AGAINST THE PEOPLE WHO DEFEND IT IS RECORDED, LINKED IN GREAT MEASURE TO THE EXTRACTIVE INDUSTRIES; the coalition works THROUGH THE PROMOTION OF REGIONAL PLATFORMS AND NATIONAL COALITIONS... PLEASE LET US KNOW. A permanent public record that the company was asked and said nothing. For a developer that presents itself as responsible to lenders and buyers, that line on its own page is a cost. THE SCALE AND WHO DOES THE ASKING: it collects evidence on MORE THAN 10,000 COMPANIES IN MORE THAN 180 COUNTRIES and takes up ALLEGED ABUSE QUICKLY AND DIRECTLY WITH COMPANIES, INVITING THEM TO RESPOND TO SPECIFIC ALLEGATIONS (OVER 1,500 PER YEAR); a network of regional researchers BUILD LONG TERM RELATIONSHIPS WITH HUMAN RIGHTS ADVOCATES ON THE GROUND, BRINGING UNDERSTANDING OF THE DYNAMICS IN THE COUNTRIES THEY COVER, and WHERE THERE IS AN ALLEGATION OF CORPORATE HUMAN RIGHTS ABUSE THAT HAS NO PUBLIC RESPONSE, THEY REACH OUT TO THE COMPANY. Its site runs in several languages including Spanish and Portuguese. There is a researcher for your region who already knows the local advocates. Send the documented allegation to them rather than to a general address. WHAT IT DOES BEYOND PUBLISHING: its recorded practice is that DIALOGUES CAN EXTEND FURTHER AND OCCASIONALLY WE TAKE AN ACTIVE ROLE IN SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES AND NGOs; in one recorded case concerning an imprisoned indigenous leader who HAD LED THE OPPOSITION TO A PROPOSED... MINE IN HIS COMMUNITY'S TERRITORY, it POSTED THE ALLEGATIONS ON OUR WEBSITE AND SOUGHT RESPONSES FROM TWO COMPANIES WHO DID NOT RESPOND, AND ASSISTED THE LOCAL VILLAGERS IN SUBMITTING THE CASE TO THE UN SPECIAL REPRESENTATIVE ON HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, then CONTACTED PUBLIC INVESTORS... AND INVITED THEM TO COMMENT, of whom two responded and ONE COMMITTED TO RAISING THE ISSUE WITH ITS CLIENTS WHO ARE INVESTED in the company. Going up the chain to the investors is the step that moves a company. Identify who holds the shares or the loan before you send the allegation, and ask that they be invited to comment too. THE HONEST NUMBERS: the centre records a response rate averaging 43% on one page and 60% on another, and its own field acknowledges criticism about WEAK AND TANGENTIAL COMPANY RESPONSES and about the LACK OF REMEDY AND THE INEQUITY IN ARMS FOR THOSE AFFECTED BY ABUSE; a published analysis notes that A COMPANY RESPONSE TO A CRITICAL CIVIL SOCIETY REPORT IS NOT NECESSARILY A POSITIVE SIGN. Roughly half of companies answer, and an answer is not a remedy. Treat this as a public record and a pressure point, not as a complaint procedure that decides anything. WHAT IT ALSO PUBLISHES ON EACH COMPANY: company pages carry news, allegations, KEY DATA POINTS BASED ON CORPORATE POLICIES, AND SCORES FROM PROMINENT CIVIL SOCIETY BENCHMARKS, and its stated goals include a SAFE AND ENABLING ENVIRONMENT IN WHICH COMMUNITIES AND WORKERS CAN ADVOCATE FOR THEIR RIGHTS AND INTERESTS, INCLUDING THROUGH FREE AND FAIR NEGOTIATIONS. Read the company's page before your first meeting with it. Its own published policies and benchmark scores are the standard you can hold it to at the table.

trackers.name: Fundación Avina - a Latin American foundation with staff in up to 19 countries, six programmes including WATER and BIOMES, a record of SEED GRANTS to organisations that became leading deforestation monitors, and convening offered alongside money
trackers.desc: A FOUNDATION WITH STAFF LIVING IN NINETEEN LATIN AMERICAN COUNTRIES THAT HAS MOVED MORE THAN A BILLION DOLLARS THROUGH LOCAL ALLIES. It is A REGIONAL NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION WITH A MANDATE TO SUPPORT SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN THE LATIN AMERICAN REGION, whose activities cover ACCESS TO WATER AND ENERGY, RESOURCE MANAGEMENT and which works THROUGH A BROAD NETWORK OF GRASS-ROOTS AND COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS, NATIONAL AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS, THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY AND THE PRIVATE SECTOR; one account records 75 FULL-TIME STAFF MEMBERS BASED IN 19 COUNTRIES IN LATIN AMERICA and another 95 STAFF MEMBERS ACROSS 15 COUNTRIES, with OVER $500 MILLION ACROSS 13,000 INITIATIVES mobilised on one count and OVER USD 1.21 BILLION since 1994 on another. Staff who live in the country rather than visit it, and grant-making measured in thousands of small initiatives. Ask who the country contact is before writing to any regional address. THE PROGRAMME LIST THAT TELLS YOU WHERE A LAND CASE FITS: it works through SIX KEY PROGRAMS — CLIMATE, CIRCULAR ECONOMY, LABOR INNOVATION, BIOMES, DEMOCRACY, AND WATER, and elsewhere describes KEY AREAS INCLUDING CLIMATE ACTION, DEMOCRATIC STRENGTHENING, INCLUSIVE CIRCULAR ECONOMIES, BIOMES CONSERVATION, WATER MANAGEMENT, AND LABOR INNOVATION, with SUPPORT FOR LOCAL INITIATIVES. Biomes and water are separate programmes with their own staff. A watershed case goes to the water programme and a forest or savannah case to biomes — sending it to the wrong one is how a request gets lost. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DID FOR MONITORING ORGANISATIONS: a foundation officer records that in one phase it USED GRANTMAKING... TO MOBILIZE FUNDS WITH PARTNERS TO ORGANIZATIONS IN PAN-AMAZON, NOT ONLY IN THE BRAZILIAN AMAZON, WHICH IS OFTEN THE FOCUS, BUT THE PAN-AMAZON AND THE CHACO REGION, TO STRENGTHEN THEIR ABILITIES TO MONITOR DEFORESTATION, and that MANY OF THE ORGANIZATIONS THAT NOWADAYS ARE LEADING ORGANIZATIONS IN THIS AREA HAVE BEEN SUPPORTED AS A SEED GRANT. Seed grants to organisations that later became the leading monitors. If your group is at the beginning, that is the stage this foundation has repeatedly funded — and the Chaco, usually ignored beside the Amazon, is named. HOW IT DESCRIBES ITS OWN ROLE, WHICH SHAPES WHAT TO ASK FOR: it works AS A BROKER, CO-INVESTOR AND FACILITATOR, its PRIMARY CONTRIBUTION TO ITS ALLIES IS THE PROMOTION OF COLLABORATIVE ACTION THROUGH SERVICES AND FINANCIAL SUPPORT, and it BRINGS ITS ABILITIES AND RESOURCES TO THE TABLE AS A PEER INSTITUTION, providing ITS ABILITY, SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE, CONTACTS, RESOURCES, STRATEGIES, AND TOOLS TO WORK TOWARDS A COMMON CAUSE. Contacts and convening are offered alongside money. Where a case needs a mayor, a ministry and a company in one room, that is the service to ask for rather than a grant. THE UNITED STATES ENTITY, AND WHAT IT FUNDS: a separate United States non-profit MOBILIZES RESOURCES AND PARTNERSHIPS FROM THE UNITED STATES TO SUPPORT AND EXPAND THE IMPACT OF THIS MISSION and SUPPORTS INITIATIVES ALIGNED WITH THE FOUNDATION'S PRIORITIES ACROSS THREE INTERCONNECTED PILLARS... DEMOCRATIC INNOVATION, CLIMATE ACTION, AND A JUST AND REGENERATIVE ECONOMY, having COME TO EMBRACE FEMINIST PRINCIPLES THAT CENTER THE IMPORTANCE OF BUILDING COLLECTIVE POWER. Two legal entities, two funding routes. Which one can pay you depends on where your organisation is registered, so ask that first. THE HONEST NOTE ON ORIGIN AND COMPANY: it was FOUNDED IN 1994 BY a Swiss industrialist, is headquartered in one Central American capital with a northern office, works BY ENCOURAGING ALLIANCES BETWEEN SOCIAL AND BUSINESS LEADERS, and its recent activities include projects with a named water technology company in one country's semi-arid region. Its model is explicitly to put business leaders at the table with social ones. Decide whether that suits your fight before joining a programme, and read who co-funds it.

trackers.name: OIKOS Red Ambiental
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Mendoza NGO that litigates provincial environmental cases and wins them. Its collective amparo of January 2003 over oil drilling inside the Laguna Llancanelo protected wetland was upheld by the Suprema Corte de Justicia de Mendoza, keeping the hydrocarbon prohibition in place — a rare precedent of a court halting a transnational's plans in a protected area. It also brought the unconstitutionality challenge to Decreto 248/2018 on environmental impact assessment for fracking, drawing amicus briefs from FARN, Earthjustice and AIDA, and in 2025 an amparo over the public hearing for the San Jorge mine at Uspallata. WHO IT SUITS: Mendoza residents and groups facing hydrocarbon, fracking or mining projects, and anyone refused environmental information — access to information is its standing theme. NOTE: the live domain is oikosredambiental.org, not the .org.ar that directories list.

trackers.name: OPSur — Observatorio Petrolero Sur
trackers.desc: Formed in 2008 and working from Neuquén and Río Negro alongside the communities living inside Vaca Muerta, the fracking formation spanning Neuquén, Río Negro, La Pampa and Mendoza. Its strength is documentary: it obtained and analysed 1,184 pages of state inspection records of Comarsa's fracking-waste plants covering 2013 to 2021, showing that provincial, national and municipal authorities knew what was happening and did not act. It took the Vaca Muerta case to the UN Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights with CIEL and the Global Initiative for ESCR, for the Mapuche community of Campo Maripe whose territory was conceded to YPF and Chevron without consultation. WHO IT SUITS: residents and Mapuche lof facing wells, waste plants or pipelines — it supplies evidence and analysis of impact studies, not legal representation.

trackers.name: Ley del Lobby / InfoLobby
trackers.desc: Chile's official lobbying platform recording lobbyist meetings, trips and gifts with public officials. Notably, its scope extends to lobbying of the judicial branch — one of the few regimes worldwide that does so. — Holds to account: anyone lobbying Chilean officials — find logged lobbyist meetings, trips and gifts — uniquely also covering the executive.

trackers.name: Consejo para la Transparencia (CPLT)
trackers.desc: Chile's independent Transparency Council, created by Ley 20.285, and the body you go to when a public agency will not hand over a file. You CAN get: a free amparo — no cost, no lawyer needed — if a request goes unanswered past 20 working days, is refused, comes back incomplete, or arrives late. The deadline is 15 working days from notification of the denial, and the Council can ORDER the agency to release the information; it has done so against ministries and Gendarmería. Its decisions are searchable at jurisprudencia.cplt.cl, so you can check whether a similar refusal has already been overturned. You CAN'T get: speed — an amparo can take up to 120 calendar days — and the agency may then take the decision to the Corte de Apelaciones by reclamo de ilegalidad, delaying release further. For activists: this is the route when an environmental impact file, an inspection record or monitoring data is withheld. The agency cannot refuse because of WHO you are; discrimination is barred by article 11(g). WHEN NOT TO USE IT: the amparo lies against a denial, so you must have filed the underlying request first.

trackers.name: SEA — e-SEIA project evaluation system
trackers.desc: Chile's Environmental Evaluation Service and its e-SEIA platform: every project entering environmental evaluation (DIA or EIA), its full file, and the citizen-participation (PAC) and indigenous-consultation (PCPI) processes. You CAN get: the complete study and evaluation file for any project by name or region, the RCA resolutions that approve or reject, and formal PAC windows where anyone can file observations (and demand PAC even on DIAs). You CAN'T get: projects that never entered the system. For activists: an unfavourable RCA legally blocks execution — the observation record you build in PAC is also the foundation for reclamation before the environmental tribunals.

trackers.name: AIDA — Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional organisation of Latin American environmental legal experts providing FREE legal and scientific support to communities and local groups, using international and inter-American human-rights law. Track record includes stopping a large dam in Mexico, halting clear-cutting of native forest in Chile, and the La Oroya smelter ruling in Peru. WHO IT SUITS: communities whose national system has already failed them and whose fight needs to go to an international body. AIDA works across Latin America, so it may be able to act in your country even if it has no office there — ask.

trackers.name: Fundación Tierra Austral — Derecho Real de Conservación
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: Chile's first land trust, founded 2012, and co-author of Ley 20.930 (2016) creating the Derecho Real de Conservación — a new real property right letting an owner bind their land to conservation in perpetuity while keeping title. The law requires the holding counterparty to be a non-profit without conflicting interests; Tierra Austral acts as that holder. USE IT: to lock a Chilean property against development permanently and against any future owner, without the state buying or declaring it.

trackers.name: Defensoría Ambiental
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Chilean association, interdisciplinary and mainly women-led, giving legal representation plus communications and technical support to communities in environmental conflicts — it sued the state and the companies operating in the Quintero-Puchuncaví sacrifice zone over accumulated environmental damage, and has taken community representatives to the UN Universal Periodic Review. WHO IT SUITS: organised communities and territorial and indigenous organisations, not individuals. Its founding premise is that the cost of environmental defence should be collective rather than borne by the affected community, so it fundraises to cover the lawyers and the expert reports that ordinary judicial assistance in Chile will not fund.

trackers.name: ONG FIMA — Fiscalía del Medio Ambiente
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Chile's first and largest public-interest environmental law office, a non-profit founded in 1998 and explicitly independent of any government body or party — which is what lets it take cases against the state. Its record includes the Mina Invierno blasting case on Isla Riesco, ended when the Supreme Court rejected the last cassation appeals. WHO IT SUITS: communities and citizens facing a project or environmental damage. Its Poder Ambiental platform gives FREE remote legal orientation — plain-language guides to citizen complaints and the environmental institutions, a forum, and a route to FIMA lawyers — built deliberately around the many steps that need no lawyer at all. FIMA also runs poderambiental.cl, a free online platform of legal orientation for defending the environment, with one section written for citizens and one for municipalities — start there before writing to the firm.

trackers.name: Fondo Naturaleza Chile
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: Chile's national environmental fund, created to mobilise and complement the finance needed for conservation and restoration in a country that is both exceptionally biodiverse and among the most exposed to climate impacts and biodiversity loss in the region. It is part of the RedLAC network of Latin American and Caribbean environmental funds. WHO IT SUITS: check its current instruments before assuming — as a national fund it works largely through programmes and partnerships rather than a standing open call, so the realistic route is often a co-financing conversation rather than a grant application. HOW IT DIFFERS: it is the country-level counterpart to the regional funds, and the only Chilean body of its kind.

trackers.name: Contraloría General de la República
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Chile, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: datos.gob.cl
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Chile.

trackers.name: Instituto Nacional de Estadísticas (INE)
trackers.desc: Chile's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Chile.

trackers.name: InfoProbidad
trackers.desc: National — public portal of officials’ declarations of interests and assets (Contraloría / CPLT).

trackers.name: Mercado Público (ChileCompra)
trackers.desc: Chile's public-procurement marketplace — every state tender and purchase order. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Chile, and for how much.

trackers.name: Poder Judicial de Chile
trackers.desc: Official judiciary portal: judgments, case search and court statistics. · Find here: the Chilean Judiciary's portal with case search and judgments.

trackers.name: Registro de Empresas y Sociedades
trackers.desc: Chile's online company and partnership register. — Holds to account: companies in Chile — find the online company-and-partnership register of entities and constitution data.

trackers.name: INECE — not where you report, but how you find who enforces
trackers.desc: READ THIS BEFORE YOU WRITE TO THEM: INECE IS NOT A COMPLAINT ROUTE. Its members are inspectors, prosecutors, regulators, parliamentarians and judges — a community cannot report a violation to INECE. It is worth an entry for three other reasons. FIRST, THE REGIONAL NETWORKS ARE A ROUTING DEVICE: INECE names AECEN (Asian Environmental Compliance and Enforcement Network), AELERT (Australasian Environmental Law Enforcement and Regulators network) and RedLaFiCA (Red Latinoamericana de Fiscalización y Cumplimiento Ambiental) as part of the network — if you do not know which body enforces in your country, the regional network is a shorter list to search than the world. SECOND, ITS CITIZEN-SCIENCE POSITION IS LEVERAGE: INECE runs an ongoing webinar series on ‘how can citizen and community science contribute to environmental compliance and enforcement?’ — that the global network of enforcers is itself asking that question is citable when an agency dismisses community-gathered evidence. THIRD, IT SHOWS WHAT KIND OF BODY TO LOOK FOR: its named members include a superintendency, a protection agency, a ministry and a supreme court — which is why searching for ‘EPA’ by name fails outside the US. The Secretariat is the Environmental Law Institute, not a government; it keeps an online library of compliance and enforcement resources and runs training — a recent series on environmental and social impact assessment drew 161 people from 31 countries. Founded 1989, covering administrative, civil, criminal and judicial enforcement, with support from UNEP, the World Bank, the European Commission and the OECD. BE AWARE OF THE MEMBERSHIP WALL: members have exclusive access to INECE materials and capacity-building programmes. IN THIS COUNTRY: Chile's Superintendencia del Medio Ambiente is named as a current member — that is the body to approach here.

trackers.name: Chile's municipal environmental certification system and its COMMUNITY ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITTEES - over 1,400 resident members nationwide, a communal environmental strategy addressing local conflicts, and ministry subsidies for municipalities that apply
trackers.desc: OVER 1,400 RESIDENTS ALREADY SIT ON COMMUNITY ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITTEES INSIDE THEIR OWN TOWN HALLS, AND THOSE COMMITTEES EXIST TO ADDRESS LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL CONFLICTS. The municipal environmental certification system CONSIDERS CITIZEN PARTICIPATION THROUGH THE CONSTITUTION OF THE COMMUNITY ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITTEES, WHICH CURRENTLY HAVE MORE THAN 1,400 MEMBERS IN ALL THE REGIONS OF THE COUNTRY; participating municipalities develop a COMMUNAL ENVIRONMENTAL STRATEGY, AN INSTRUMENT OF ACTION THAT SEEKS TO ADDRESS IN A SYSTEMATIC MANNER THE PRINCIPAL CONFLICTS OR ENVIRONMENTAL SITUATIONS PRESENT IN THE COMMUNAL TERRITORY. Principal conflicts, in the programme's own words, and a committee of residents convened to work on them. Ask your municipality whether it is in the system and how to join the committee — the seats are already there. WHAT THE MUNICIPALITY MUST DO TO REACH THE SECOND LEVEL: that level requires THE PERMANENT FUNCTIONING OF THE COMMUNITY ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITTEE AND THE MUNICIPAL ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITTEE; DESIGNS OF SYSTEMS OF CITIZEN ENVIRONMENTAL PARTICIPATION; ENVIRONMENTAL ORDINANCES; DESIGN OR REDESIGN OF THE LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT UNIT, alongside recycling, water and energy plans and sustainable purchasing, with MINIMUM COMPLIANCE OF 95% OF THE DEMANDABLE FACTORS and an eleven-month deadline. There are five certification levels. Environmental ordinances and a permanent residents' committee are certification requirements, not favours. A municipality chasing the next level has a direct institutional reason to pass the ordinance you want. WHAT THE SYSTEM IS AND HOW A MUNICIPALITY ENTERS: created in 2009, it is AN INTEGRAL SYSTEM OF VOLUNTARY CHARACTER, WHICH ALLOWS MUNICIPALITIES TO INSTALL THEMSELVES IN THE TERRITORY AS A MODEL OF ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT, WHERE THE ORGANIC STRUCTURE, THE INFRASTRUCTURE, THE PERSONNEL, THE INTERNAL PROCEDURES AND THE SERVICES THE MUNICIPALITY PROVIDES TO THE COMMUNITY INTEGRATE THE ENVIRONMENTAL FACTOR, referenced to international management standards; applications go BY OFFICIAL LETTER TO THE CORRESPONDING REGIONAL SECRETARIAT, in two modes — WITH REQUEST FOR FINANCING AND SELF-FINANCED — the first carrying A FINANCIAL SUBSIDY FROM THE ENVIRONMENT MINISTRY awarded on score and need, with an interview and the mayor's appointment decree required. Money is attached for municipalities that ask. Where a town hall pleads cost, the answer is that the ministry subsidises entry — and the application is a letter from the mayor. THE PUBLISHED LISTS AND MANUALS: the ministry publishes the certified municipalities, the certification levels, the entry manual and the governing resolution, all downloadable. Check whether your municipality is certified and at what level before the meeting. A council that advertises its certification is easier to hold to the commitments that certification required. WHERE THE UNIT SITS INSIDE THE TOWN HALL: municipalities house this work in an environment directorate — one publishes it under a directorate of environment, cleaning and ornament — and the programme's lines include THE DEVELOPMENT OF INSTRUMENTS THAT ENCOURAGE THE PARTICIPATION OF THE NEIGHBOURS IN COMMUNAL ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT. Ask for the environment directorate by name rather than the mayor's office. That unit owns the certification file and the committee's minutes.

trackers.name: Chile's municipalities' association - MODEL ORDINANCES and studies for all 346 councils, a standing environment commission of mayors and councillors, regional associations in every region, and state help to give a multi-municipality association legal personality
trackers.desc: THE MUNICIPALITIES' ASSOCIATION PUBLISHES MODEL ORDINANCES THAT ANY OF THE 346 COUNCILS CAN ADOPT. Its site offers STUDIES, MODEL ORDINANCES, BULLETINS AND PUBLICATIONS, alongside COURSES, SEMINARS AND CONGRESSES FOR MAYORS, COUNCILLORS AND OFFICIALS OF THE 346 MUNICIPALITIES, a projects bank and agreements offering ALLIANCES AND SERVICES FOR ASSOCIATED MUNICIPALITIES AND OFFICIALS THROUGHOUT CHILE. A model ordinance is the single most transferable thing in local government. Ask the association for the environmental ones and take the text to your council rather than asking it to draft from nothing. WHAT THE ASSOCIATION EXISTS TO DO, IN ITS REGISTERED STATUTES: THE DEFENCE OF THE COMMON INTERESTS OF THE MUNICIPALITIES OF CHILE; COLLABORATING IN THE DESIGN OF PUBLIC POLICIES RELATED TO THE MUNICIPALITIES; THE TECHNICAL STRENGTHENING OF MUNICIPAL MANAGEMENT AND ADMINISTRATION; THE PERFECTING, PROMOTION AND DEVELOPMENT OF THE SYSTEM OF MUNICIPAL AUTONOMY; THE TRAINING AND PERFECTING OF MAYORS, COUNCILLORS AND MUNICIPAL PERSONNEL; LINKAGE WITH PUBLIC AND PRIVATE ORGANS AND WITH REGIONAL, NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL INSTITUTIONS; and FACILITATING THE SOLUTION OF COMMON PROBLEMS THAT AFFECT THE MUNICIPALITIES. It has held its own legal personality since November 2012, and its technical commissions, COMPOSED OF MAYORS AND COUNCILLORS, cover FINANCE, HOUSING, HEALTH, EDUCATION, ENVIRONMENT, AMONG OTHERS. There is a standing environment commission of serving mayors and councillors. A community problem that several communes share is exactly what that commission exists to take up. THE REGIONAL ASSOCIATIONS BELOW IT: the association works TO STRENGTHEN THE REGIONAL ASSOCIATIONS, WHERE THE MUNICIPALITIES HAVE ORGANISED THEMSELVES AT REGIONAL LEVEL TO WORK SPECIFIC THEMES OF THEIR TERRITORIAL REALITY, so that THERE EXISTS IN EACH REGION OF THE COUNTRY AN ASSOCIATION, WITH ITS RESPECTIVE TECHNICAL COMMISSIONS, EMULATING THE NATIONAL ORGANIC STRUCTURE. Every region has its own association with its own technical commissions. That is a smaller room, closer to the site, and easier to get onto the agenda of. THE STATE UNIT THAT HELPS ASSOCIATIONS FORM: a national subsecretariat unit runs PROGRAMMES OF TRAINING AND/OR TECHNICAL ADVICE ON THE THEMES PROPER TO ASSOCIATIVE MANAGEMENT, manages and evaluates PROJECTS OF STRENGTHENING OF MUNICIPALITIES AND MUNICIPAL ASSOCIATIONS FOR TERRITORIAL DEVELOPMENT, and TECHNICALLY ASSISTS THE ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES IN OBTAINING LEGAL PERSONALITY AND MANAGING THE INSTRUMENT PRIVATE LAW CORPORATION, administering the SINGLE REGISTER OF ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES WITH LEGAL PERSONALITY. Several municipalities sharing one threatened watershed can form their own association with legal personality, and the state will help them do it. That association can then hold funds and contract for the basin as a whole. THE MANUAL ITS ENVIRONMENT COMMISSION WROTE: the commission produced a communal environmental manual which NOT ONLY SHOWS PROBLEMS AND SOLUTIONS TO SPECIFIC THEMES, IT ALSO DELIVERS THE LEGAL FRAMEWORK AND THE USEFUL MODELS SO THAT EACH MUNICIPALITY MAY IMPLEMENT A DIAGNOSIS, PLAN AND ENVIRONMENTAL UNIT, WHICH COORDINATES INTERNALLY THE WORK OF ALL THE MUNICIPAL AREAS, and it argues that municipalities BE PART OF THE TECHNICAL COMMISSIONS OF THAT ENVIRONMENTAL AUTHORITY, SO AS TO CONTRIBUTE THEIR VISION TO THE PROJECTS THAT AFFECT THEIR TERRITORY. Municipalities are meant to sit on the technical commissions that review projects affecting their own territory. If your council is not at that table for the project near you, the association's own manual is the argument for putting it there.

trackers.name: FLACMA - the Latin American federation of cities and municipal associations, open to affiliation by ANY INDIVIDUAL MUNICIPALITY, whose assembly passes resolutions signed by mayors across eighteen countries
trackers.desc: ANY CITY OR MUNICIPALITY IN THE REGION MAY AFFILIATE DIRECTLY, NOT ONLY THROUGH ITS NATIONAL ASSOCIATION. Its membership rule is that MEMBERS ARE ALL THE CITIES, MUNICIPALITIES, NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND MUNICIPALIST INSTITUTIONS OF LATIN AMERICA THAT HAVE EXPRESSED THEIR WILL TO AFFILIATE; it is AN ORGANISATION OF FREE ADHESION THAT REPRESENTS THE 16,132 MUNICIPALITIES, INTENDANCIES AND PREFECTURES, THE CITIES AND THE ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, NETWORKS AND GUILDS OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, and it is the regional section of the world organisation of local governments. A single municipality may join in its own right. Where your national association is captured or inactive, that is a way for one sympathetic town hall to reach the regional table on its own. WHOSE PRESIDENTS SIT ON IT: its published leadership is drawn from the presidents of the national municipal bodies of the region — the federation of municipalities of one southern country, the association of municipalities of another, the Brazilian association of municipalities, the congress of intendants of another, the national federation of municipalities of one large federal country and the association of municipalities of an Andean one — each of them a serving mayor. The people who chair your own national municipal association sit here. A matter raised through that association can be carried into a regional assembly by the same person. WHAT IT SAYS IT IS FOR: TO BE THE VOICE OF LATIN AMERICAN MUNICIPALISM, TO CONSOLIDATE THE LATIN AMERICAN MUNICIPAL ASSOCIATIVE MOVEMENT, TO REPRESENT AND SERVE AS INTERLOCUTOR OF ALL THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND THEIR NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES, and TO PROMOTE IN LATIN AMERICA AUTONOMOUS, STRONG AND DEMOCRATIC LOCAL GOVERNMENTS; it ADHERES TO AND PROMOTES THE WORLD AND REGIONAL CONVENTIONS THAT THE NATIONAL STATES OF THE REGION SUBSCRIBE. Promoting the conventions the states have signed is written into its purpose. Where your country has signed an environmental or rights convention and a municipality is being told to ignore it, that is a body with a standing commitment to the opposite. THE PRECEDENT THAT SHOWS IT TAKES POSITIONS: its general assembly has approved unanimously a declaration on a territorial sovereignty dispute, signed by the president and BY MUNICIPAL AUTHORITIES AND HEADS OF ASSOCIATIONS AND FEDERATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES of eighteen named countries of the region, which also REAFFIRMED THE LEGITIMATE RIGHTS... OVER THE NATURAL RESOURCES OF THE AREA IN QUESTION. The assembly passes resolutions that name natural resources and get signed by mayors across eighteen countries. A community campaign that can be framed as a municipal cause has a forum that has done exactly that before. THE OTHER REGIONAL NETWORKS BESIDE IT: regional analysis names, among the principal associations and networks of local and regional governments with EXPERIENCES, IDEAS AND RESOURCES TO FOSTER INITIATIVES AND PROJECTS LINKED TO SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AT LOCAL LEVEL, a network of Mercosur cities alongside this federation, and global initiatives with regional presence for local sustainability and for city climate action; various cities have prepared VOLUNTARY LOCAL REPORTS on implementing the global development agenda in their territories. A voluntary local report is a document a municipality writes about itself. Getting your community's situation named in one is cheap, public and lasting. THE HONEST NOTE ON REPRESENTATION: the region's representation in the world body has been the subject of negotiations between this federation, the Mercosur cities network and the world organisation to form A LATIN AMERICAN REPRESENTATION THAT IS PLURAL, DIVERSE AND PARTICIPATORY. More than one body claims to speak for the region's municipalities. Approach both this federation and the Mercosur cities network rather than assuming one covers the other.

trackers.name: Mercociudades - a South American city network whose cooperation calls admit UNIVERSITIES AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS as partners alongside two or more municipalities, with an environment and sustainable development unit coordinated by a member city
trackers.desc: UNIVERSITIES AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS CAN BE PARTNERS IN THE COOPERATION PROJECTS THIS CITY NETWORK FUNDS. Its south-south cooperation call is open to MEMBER CITIES AND ASSOCIATED STATES, to universities of a regional university association, and to ORGANISATIONS OF CIVIL SOCIETY; THE PROJECT MUST INVOLVE AT LEAST TWO MEMBER LOCAL GOVERNMENTS OR ASSOCIATED STATES, and THE UNIVERSITIES AND SOCIAL ORGANISATIONS MAY PARTICIPATE AS PARTNER ENTITIES ALONGSIDE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, each city able to stand as coordinator of one proposal and partner in another. Two municipalities and your organisation is a fundable consortium. Where a threatened area straddles two towns, or two towns face the same developer, that is the shape the call is written for. THE THEMATIC UNIT THAT COVERS LAND AND WATER: among its seventeen thematic units and four working groups is one for ENVIRONMENT AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT, coordinated by a city with sub-coordinating cities, which has run exchanges on waste, sustainability and circular economy and marked world water day, and has opened AN OPPORTUNITY OF COOPERATION TOGETHER WITH THE UNITED NATIONS ENVIRONMENT PROGRAMME FOR THE STRENGTHENING OF LOCAL CAPACITIES; other units cover AUTONOMY, MANAGEMENT AND PARTICIPATION, HUMAN RIGHTS, URBAN DEVELOPMENT, PLANNING AND METROPOLITAN AREAS and BORDER INTEGRATION. A coordinating city runs each unit, and it is a city like yours rather than a secretariat. Write to the coordinator of the environment unit with your case: that is a mayor's office, not an agency. WHAT THE NETWORK COMMITS ITSELF TO DO: among its statutory objectives are TO CARRY OUT STUDIES AND COLLABORATE IN THE ELABORATION OF PLANS AND STRATEGIES IN THE URBAN-ENVIRONMENTAL AREA, WITH THE OBJECTIVE OF HARMONISING AND COORDINATING THE ACTIONS IN THIS AREA, TO COLLABORATE IN THE PLANNING OF THE POLICIES AND PLANS OF DEVELOPMENT OF THE CITIES, TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE NEED TO IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF LIFE, TO ADVOCATE AND RAISE AWARENESS ABOUT CITIZEN PARTICIPATION AND SOCIAL INCLUSION, and TO IDENTIFY THE CAUSES OF ACCENTUATION OF THE SOCIAL INEQUALITIES, IN ORDER TO PROPOSE AND SUPPORT SOLUTIONS POSSIBLE TO BE EXECUTED BY THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS. Collaborating in city development plans is a stated commitment. A municipality revising its plan can ask the network for that collaboration rather than paying a consultancy. WHO ELSE MAY TAKE PART: THE OTHER INSTANCES OF THE SUB-NATIONAL GOVERNMENTS OF THE COUNTRIES of the two regional blocs THAT EXPRESS THEIR WILL TO DO SO AND WHOSE GOVERNMENTS HAVE BEEN DEMOCRATICALLY ELECTED may participate as collaborators, and COOPERATION WITH CONSORTIA AND ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES WILL BE CARRIED OUT BY MEANS OF AGREEMENTS. Provinces, departments and municipal consortia can join as collaborators. Where the decision sits above the town hall, that tier can be brought to the same table. THE PLATFORM THAT MATCHES NEEDS TO SOLUTIONS: its cooperation programme runs an interactive platform DESIGNED SPECIALLY TO SHARE LOCAL SOLUTIONS... AND TO INTERWEAVE STRENGTHS AND TECHNICAL NEEDS OF CITIES OF ALL SOUTH AMERICA, with a directory of good practices through which member cities HAVE THE POSSIBILITY OF EXCHANGING WITH THE REFERENTS OF SOLUTIONS OF THE CITIES. Post the technical need rather than the complaint. A city that has already solved the same problem is what the platform is built to find.

trackers.name: ICLEI - a sustainability network open to individual councils AND to associations of local governments, giving fee-paying members year-round telephone and email support on designing environment and water projects, plus local biodiversity planning tools and an environmental award
trackers.desc: MEMBERSHIP OF THIS GLOBAL SUSTAINABILITY NETWORK IS OPEN TO ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AS WELL AS TO INDIVIDUAL COUNCILS, AND THE FEE SCALES WITH POPULATION AND NATIONAL INCOME. Its membership page states that AFFILIATION IS OPEN TO ALL LOCAL AND REGIONAL GOVERNMENTS, AS WELL AS TO THEIR WORLD, REGIONAL, NATIONAL AND SUBNATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS, that members MAY VOTE AND PARTICIPATE IN THE GOVERNING ORGANS OF THE WHOLE NETWORK, and that they CONTRIBUTE AN ANNUAL AFFILIATION FEE THAT VARIES REGIONALLY AND ACCORDING TO POPULATION AND GROSS NATIONAL INCOME PER CAPITA. A small municipality pays a small fee and votes in the same network as a capital city. Where a national association is the member, ask whether your council is covered by it already.
