trackers.desc: THIRTY-TWO NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS IN TWENTY COUNTRIES, AND THE NETWORK PUBLISHES WHICH ONE COVERS YOURS. It GROUPS 32 ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS FROM 20 COUNTRIES OF THE REGION, UNITING EFFORTS TO PROTECT THE RICH BIODIVERSITY OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, with its member list filterable by zone — Caribbean, Mesoamerica and South America — alongside regional funds; more than twenty-five years old, it counts MORE THAN 100 ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS WORLDWIDE. Find the fund for your country on that member page. These are permanent national institutions with endowments, not project offices that close when a grant ends. WHAT THESE FUNDS DO, IN THE NETWORK'S WORDS: they HAVE DEMONSTRATED TO BE A KEY MECHANISM IN THE SUSTAINABLE FINANCING OF BIODIVERSITY AND IN THE STRENGTHENING OF PROTECTED AREAS AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, with a role in THE PROTECTION OF NATURAL AREAS AND THE SUPPORT TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES, described as MULTIDIMENSIONAL FUNDS, WITH APPROACHES THAT INTEGRATE PROTECTION OF BIODIVERSITY, CLIMATIC RESILIENCE AND COMMUNITY EMPOWERMENT. Support to local communities is named alongside protected areas. A community managing land next to a park is inside the mandate, not adjacent to it. SOME OF THE MEMBERS BY NAME AND KIND: recorded members include a Caribbean biodiversity fund, a national forever-protection association in one Central American country, an action fund and a Pacific foundation in one Andean country, a nature fund in one southern country, an island life fund and a regional marine fund — the last two showing that funds exist for a single archipelago and for a shared sea as well as for whole countries. There are funds scoped to one archipelago and to one reef system. If your site sits in either, that narrower fund is a better fit than the national one. WHAT THE NETWORK ITSELF OFFERS ITS MEMBERS: joining gives funds THE OPPORTUNITY TO CONNECT AND COLLABORATE WITH OTHER MEMBERS OF THE NETWORK THROUGHOUT THE REGION, to SHARE KNOWLEDGE, RESOURCES AND EXPERIENCES TO IMPROVE THEIR CAPACITIES, and ACCESS TO A WIDE VARIETY OF RESOURCES AND TOOLS, with TRAINING AND ADVICE ON DIVERSE THEMES, FROM PROJECT MANAGEMENT TO COMMUNICATION AND ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION. Where your country has no environmental fund, this network is where one would be built, and it trains new members. That is a long project, but it is the route. WHY THEY MATTER FOR PERMANENT PROTECTION: these funds are conservation trust funds — institutions holding capital whose returns finance protected areas and community work year after year, and the network works alongside a global environment facility, an African funds consortium and a large conservation finance initiative on that model. An endowment pays for wardens and monitoring long after a campaign ends. Where a protected area has just been declared, the next question is which of these funds can endow its running costs.

trackers.name: The ICCA Consortium and the international register of territories of life - a community-reviewed register open to any well-defined community with its own governance, plus national catalytic organisations, documentation workshops and life plan support
trackers.desc: A COMMUNITY CAN PUT ITS OWN TERRITORY ON AN INTERNATIONAL REGISTER, REVIEWED BY OTHER COMMUNITIES RATHER THAN BY OFFICIALS. The international register IS A TOOL DEVELOPED TO SERVE AS SUPPORT AND RECOGNITION TO THOSE COMMUNITIES WITH OUTSTANDING VALUES IN GOVERNANCE AND CONSERVATION OF NATURE, run by a United Nations environment body with the consortium and a commons organisation; its PEER REVIEW PROTOCOL is A CONSENSUS DOCUMENT IN WHICH THE DIFFERENT STEPS THAT EACH COMMUNITY MUST TAKE IN ORDER TO FORM PART OF THE REGISTER ARE DESCRIBED, including SUBMITTING TO A PROCESS OF REVIEW OF THE CANDIDATURE BY ANONYMOUS MEMBERS (REVIEWERS) OF OTHER SIMILAR COMMUNITIES THAT ALREADY FORM PART OF THE REGISTER. Other communities judge the application, and the protocol is published so you can read the test before applying. Registration is a public record of who governs the land, made without asking the state's permission. WHAT QUALIFIES AS ONE OF THESE TERRITORIES: they exist IN ANY TYPE OF CULTURE AND ECOSYSTEM WHERE THERE IS A COMMUNITY LINKED TO A TERRITORY, WITH ITS OWN SYSTEM OF GOVERNANCE, AND THAT GIVES POSITIVE RESULTS IN TERMS OF CONSERVATION OF NATURE AND LIVELIHOODS FOR THE COMMUNITY; the first defining characteristic is that THE AREA OR TERRITORY MUST HAVE A WELL DEFINED COMMUNITY, WITH A CLEAR LINK TO A TERRITORY ALSO WELL DEFINED. A well defined community and a well defined territory. Neither a formal title nor a state designation is in that test. WHO THE CONSORTIUM IS AND WHAT ITS MEMBERS DO: it is AN INTERNATIONAL NON-PROFIT ASSOCIATION DEDICATED TO SUPPORTING INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES THAT GOVERN AND CONSERVE THEIR LANDS, WATERS AND TERRITORIES, its members from more than eighty countries acting on themes including THE DOCUMENTATION, SUSTAINING AND DEFENCE OF THE TERRITORIES OF LIFE, and comprising ALMOST 180 MEMBERS (ORGANISATIONS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND COMMUNITY ORGANISATIONS, TOGETHER WITH THE CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS THAT SUPPORT THEM) AND MORE THAN 420 HONORARY MEMBERS. Community organisations are members in their own right, alongside the NGOs that support them. Ask the national focal point how your organisation joins. WHAT THE REGIONAL NETWORK ACTUALLY DELIVERS: the Latin American network runs workshops WITH THE AIM OF SHARING KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERIENCES COMING FROM THE TERRITORIES, including a practical workshop on the register itself, a case study workshop drawing on one country's experience, and one on a GUIDE OF SELF-STRENGTHENING: A GUIDE FROM COMMUNITIES FOR COMMUNITIES; communities are recorded pursuing PROCESSES OF DOCUMENTATION, THE CONSTRUCTION OF LIFE PLANS, THE register AND THE STRENGTHENING OF THEIR OWN GOVERNANCE. A life plan is the document that states what a community will and will not permit on its land. Building one is the work these workshops exist to support. WHAT IT HAS SUPPORTED ON THE GROUND: in one country an observatory and a named indigenous community organised A WORKSHOP OF EXCHANGE OF KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERIENCES, ATTENDED BY TWENTY-FIVE REPRESENTATIVES OF TEN INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, TO EXCHANGE ABOUT LEGAL AND NON-LEGAL STRATEGIES OF TERRITORIAL DEFENCE AND PROTECTION; in another, five indigenous peoples, an Afro-descendant community and a coastal community met with a foundation and the small grants programme TO DEBATE AND DECIDE ON THE WORLD REGISTER; national members have planned A STUDY OF THE EXISTING LEGAL FRAMEWORK ON CONSERVATION AND RIGHTS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, ACTIONS FOR COMMUNITY STRENGTHENING AND A NATIONAL ADVOCACY STRATEGY; a global support initiative works through NATIONAL CATALYTIC ORGANISATIONS in more than twenty-six priority countries. Ask which organisation is the national catalytic body for your country. It is the one already funded to accompany communities through documentation and registration.

trackers.name: Mapeo and its successor - a free, offline, open-source mapping and evidence toolset built with Amazonian indigenous partners, where ALL DATA IS OWNED BY THE COMMUNITY, exporting shapefiles and reports for lawsuits and land claims
trackers.desc: A FREE OFFLINE APP THAT TURNS A PHONE INTO AN EVIDENCE RECORDER, AND THE COMMUNITY KEEPS THE DATA. It is A FREE DIGITAL TOOLSET FOR DOCUMENTING, MONITORING, AND MAPPING MANY TYPES OF DATA, OFFLINE-FIRST OPEN-SOURCE TECHNOLOGY needing NO INTERNET OR SPECIAL HARDWARE... TO COLLECT, VIEW, OR SHARE DATA; WITH THE PUSH OF A BUTTON, CONTRIBUTORS CAN GATHER MAP DATA BY LINKING GPS POINTS, PHOTOS, AND NOTES, and ALL DATA IS COMPLETELY OWNED BY THE COMMUNITIES THEMSELVES, exchanged between phones by a peer-to-peer sync that works OVER A LOCAL WIFI NETWORK WITHOUT NEEDING A CONNECTION. No signal, no server, no subscription, and nobody else holds the file. For a community watching a road survey or a clearing crew, that is the difference between a rumour and an exhibit. WHAT IT WAS BUILT TO BE USED FOR: it was CO-DESIGNED AND DEVELOPED WITH INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES WHO FACE THREATS TO THEIR LAND SUCH AS ILLEGAL GOLD MINING, OIL CONTAMINATION AND POACHING, and built TO SUPPORT THEM TO DOCUMENT THESE ACTIVITIES IN ORDER TO TAKE COMMUNITY ACTION AGAINST THEM, TO REPORT THEM TO AUTHORITIES, FILE LAWSUITS, LAUNCH MEDIA CAMPAIGNS, OR CREATE MAPS FOR LAND CLAIMS; it allows USERS TO COLLECT EVIDENCE IN THE FIELD, SUCH AS PHOTOGRAPHS AND GPS POINTS, AND ORGANIZE THIS DATA FOR ACTIONS SUCH AS WHISTLEBLOWING AND CLAIMING LAND RIGHTS. Filing a lawsuit and making a map for a land claim are the stated purposes. Set up the categories to match what a court or a ministry will ask for, before the incursion happens. THE CASE THAT SHOWS WHAT IT IS WORTH: in one country OVER TWENTY indigenous COMMUNITIES DEFENDED THEIR TERRITORY... AGAINST THE IMPOSITION OF DEVASTATING OIL EXPLORATION PROPOSED BY THE GOVERNMENT, having USED the tool FOR OVER FOUR YEARS TO RECORD TERRITORIAL DATA ...AND MAPS, WHICH THEY USED AS EVIDENCE AGAINST THE government; the account records: THEY WON! Four years of routine recording before the case existed. The evidence that wins these cases is gathered long before anyone knows there will be a case. WHAT COMES OUT OF IT, AND IN WHICH LANGUAGES: export options include PDF OR PRINT REPORT, GEOJSON, CSV OR SHAPEFILE from the desktop version and direct sharing from the phone; the interface IS AVAILABLE IN LOCAL LANGUAGES, AND ALSO HAS AN IN-BUILT TRANSLATION FEATURE, supporting THE UNDERSERVED DIALECTS OF INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES; one community leader records that IT IS SO EASY TO USE THAT EVEN OUR ELDERS — WHO DO NOT SPEAK SPANISH — USE IT. A newer version adds audio, tracks and routes. A shapefile is what a planning office and a court will accept. Elders who do not speak the national language can gather it themselves, which also answers the objection that the data was collected by outsiders. THE SUPPORT AROUND THE TOOL: the developers publish TRAINING AND TECHNICAL RESOURCES, a COMPLETE REFERENCE GUIDE... ON PLANNING AND IMPLEMENTING PROJECTS and customisation of the tools, and a defenders toolkit site; a dedicated version was built with a United Nations monitoring centre and a forest peoples organisation so that custodian communities can MAP, MONITOR AND SUPPORT THEIR TERRITORIES OF LIFE ON THEIR TERMS and may, SHOULD THEY WISH TO, CONTRIBUTE TO GLOBAL CONSERVATION DATABASES. Contributing to the global database is optional and separate. Decide as a community what stays local before the first survey, because that choice is hard to reverse once data is shared.

trackers.name: Global Forest Watch - free near-real-time deforestation alerts by email for any drawn area, an offline field app that walks patrols to the clearing, and a small grants fund whose examples include GETTING CONCESSIONS REVOKED and compiling evidence for formal complaints
trackers.desc: YOU CAN SUBSCRIBE TO EMAIL ALERTS FOR A SINGLE PLOT OF FOREST AND BE TOLD WITHIN DAYS WHEN TREES ARE CUT. The platform is FREE AND SIMPLE TO USE, ENABLING ANYONE TO CREATE CUSTOM MAPS, ANALYZE FOREST TRENDS, SUBSCRIBE TO ALERTS, OR DOWNLOAD DATA FOR THEIR LOCAL AREA OR THE ENTIRE WORLD, providing NEAR-REAL-TIME ALERTS SHOWING SUSPECTED LOCATIONS OF RECENT TREE COVER LOSS; it moved BEYOND ANNUAL DATA ON FORESTS to MONTHLY AND WEEKLY DEFORESTATION ALERTS, with EMAIL SUBSCRIPTIONS bringing them DIRECTLY INTO THE HANDS OF USERS. Users CAN SIGN UP FOR ALERTS AND DOWNLOAD DATASETS WITHOUT ANY SUBSCRIPTION OR LICENSING FEE. Draw the boundary of the land you are defending and subscribe. From then on the clearing tells you rather than the other way round, and the date stamp is independent of anything the developer says. THE FIELD APP THAT WORKS WITHOUT SIGNAL: a companion mobile application ALLOWS RANGERS TO ACCESS the data and alerts OFFLINE, WHICH IS CRITICAL IN AREAS WITH LIMITED TO NO CELL SIGNAL; USING CACHED DATA, THE APP DIRECTS USERS TO NEARBY FOREST CLEARING AND ENABLES THEM TO CAPTURE PHOTOS AND FILL OUT FORMS ABOUT DEFORESTATION, WHICH ARE UPLOADED NEXT TIME THEIR DEVICE CONNECTS, so that patrols KNOW EXACTLY WHERE TO LOOK... AND STOP THE ILLEGAL ACTIVITY BEFORE IT GETS OUT OF CONTROL; it is FREE, OPEN SOURCE, AND AVAILABLE IN ENGLISH, SPANISH, PORTUGUESE, FRENCH, AND BAHASA INDONESIAN. The alert gives the coordinates and the app walks you to them. A ground photograph taken at a satellite-flagged point, on a known date, is the evidence a prosecutor can use. THE GRANT ATTACHED TO IT, AND WHAT IT HAS PAID FOR: a small grants fund SEEKS TO BUILD THE CAPACITY OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS TO EFFECTIVELY USE the tools TO REDUCE ILLEGAL OR UNPLANNED DEFORESTATION; funded project types include USING DATA AND IMAGERY... ALONGSIDE COMMUNITY TERRITORIAL MAPS TO ADVOCATE FOR LAND TITLES AND OTHER STRENGTHENED LAND RIGHTS; CROWDSOURCING, COMPILING AND PUBLISHING DATA ON CONCESSIONS THAT OVERLAP WITH ANCESTRAL COMMUNITY LANDS, AND SUPPORT COMMUNITIES IN APPLYING PUBLIC PRESSURE TO GET THESE CONCESSIONS REVOKED; DEVELOPING THE CAPACITY OF FOREST MONITORING BRIGADES TO CONDUCT FIELD VERIFICATIONS OF NEAR-REAL TIME ALERTS; and SUPPORTING INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES IN DEVELOPING RESPONSE PROTOCOLS, FORMULATING LEGAL STRATEGIES AND COMPILING EVIDENCE OF ILLEGAL DEFORESTATION INCLUDING SATELLITE IMAGERY, DATA AND ANALYSES, AND SUBMITTING IT TO LAW ENFORCEMENT THROUGH FORMAL COMPLAINTS OR OTHER LEGAL PROCESSES. Getting concessions revoked and compiling evidence for formal complaints are funded project types, written into the fund's own examples. That is the grant to cite when describing what you intend to do. THE DEADLINE DISCIPLINE: the fund runs an annual call, and the platform states of a recent round: THE CALL FOR APPLICATIONS HAS CLOSED AS OF THE DEADLINE... WE CANNOT GRANT ANY EXTENSIONS, advising applicants to PREPARE FOR THE NEXT CALL FOR APPLICATIONS BY REVIEWING the current materials, while noting that SOME ITEMS IN THE GUIDELINES FOR APPLICANTS MAY CHANGE YEAR TO YEAR. One deadline a year, strictly enforced. Download this year's guidelines now and write the proposal before the next call opens. WHO ELSE IS ALREADY USING IT: the platform serves GOVERNMENTS, THE PRIVATE SECTOR, NGOs, JOURNALISTS, UNIVERSITIES, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC, and is convened as a partnership of OVER 200 ORGANIZATIONS; a fellowship accompanies the grants. Your municipality and your national forest agency can subscribe to the same alerts you do. Sending them the alert with a covering letter turns your observation into their file.

trackers.name: Public Lab and the open science hardware community - free open-source, low-cost instruments and toolkits communities build themselves for water, air, soil and land use, plus BALLOON AND KITE AERIAL MAPPING with stitching software and an open question forum
trackers.desc: THE INSTRUMENTS ARE OPEN SOURCE AND CHEAP ENOUGH THAT A COMMUNITY CAN BUILD ITS OWN, INCLUDING AERIAL PHOTOGRAPHY FROM A KITE. The network is DEVOTED TO EMPOWERING COMMUNITIES AND CITIZEN SCIENTISTS TO MONITOR THEIR OWN ENVIRONMENTS THROUGH THE USE OF INEXPENSIVE DIY TECHNIQUES, hosting AN IMPRESSIVE CATALOG OF OPEN SOURCE TOOLKITS... RANGING FROM WATER QUALITY SENSORS TO INDOOR AIR QUALITY AND KITE MAPPING KITS; its tools and data are CREATED BY THE community, OPEN SOURCE, AND TYPICALLY INEXPENSIVE TO USE. Its earliest technique was LOW-ALTITUDE AERIAL MAPPING WITH BALLOONS AND KITES with software to stitch the photographs into a map. A kite, a camera and free stitching software produce a dated aerial photograph of a site at a resolution no public satellite gives you. That is how you show what a hillside looked like before the machines arrived. WHY IT EXISTS, AND WHAT THAT PRECEDENT MEANS: it was founded in 2010 FOLLOWING THE BP OIL DISASTER IN THE GULF OF MEXICO... TO ADDRESS AN ENORMOUS GAP IN COMMUNITY KNOWLEDGE ABOUT THE IMPACTS OF THE SPILL, launching AS AN OPEN SOURCE PLATFORM, COLLECTING DATA AND MAPS OF THE COASTLINE OVER TIME TO SHOW THE COAST BEFORE, DURING, AND AFTER THE SPILL. Before, during and after is the sequence that wins arguments about damage. Start the baseline photographs now, while there is still a before. WHAT THE PLATFORM ACTUALLY GIVES YOU: it is A PLATFORM FOR COMMUNITY SCIENCE PRACTITIONERS WORKING ON ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES TO DOCUMENT THEIR WORK, SHARE TOOLS FOR ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING AND ADVOCACY, AND CONNECT WITH EACH OTHER; THE COMMUNITY IS OPEN AND FREE FOR ANYONE TO JOIN, members CAN ADD THEIR OWN PROJECT PAGE TO DOCUMENT THEIR METHODS AND SHARE EXPERTISE, and users CAN BROWSE LOW-COST ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING TOOLS FOR APPLICATION AREAS SUCH AS AIR QUALITY, LAND USE, STORMWATER, alongside ADVOCACY METHODS, AND ACTION TOOLKITS BY SCIENCE TOPICS covering WATER, SOIL, AIR, INDUSTRY, CLIMATE, ORGANIZING, AND MONITORING; COMMUNITY MEMBERS CAN ASK OR ANSWER QUESTIONS. Post the question with your site's details. Somebody has usually measured the same pollutant with the same cheap instrument and will say what went wrong the first time. THE KINDS OF INSTRUMENT PEOPLE HAVE BUILT: recorded tools include a spectrometer made from LEGO OR CARDBOARD, WEBCAMS OR RASPBERRY PI CAMERAS, RECYCLED DVDs so that SPECTROSCOPY IS A RESEARCH METHOD THAT ANYONE CAN EXPLORE; a SIMPLE AIR SENSOR whose REALTIME READOUT CHANGES COLOR WHEN THE SENSOR READS DIFFERENCES IN AIR QUALITY, usable WITHOUT HAVING TO LEARN HOW TO PROGRAM; a low-budget water kit with probes MEASURING TEMPERATURE, DISSOLVED OXYGEN AND CONDUCTIVITY, developed to measure sewage outfalls after storms; a DIY device to TEST FOR HEAVY METALS IN WATER; DIY infrared cameras; and a marine microplastics trawler. Dissolved oxygen, conductivity and heavy metals are the readings that show a river has been damaged. A community that takes them weekly for a year has a record no consultant's single sample can rebut. WHAT THE WIDER COMMUNITY ADDS: a water data collaborative HELPS GUIDE COMMUNITY GROUPS ON HOW TO ADOPT DIY, OPEN HARDWARE METHODS FOR COLLECTING THE QUALITY OF WATER DATA THEY NEED TO ACHIEVE THEIR OUTCOMES, alongside research centres publishing open hardware loggers, and an annual gathering for open science hardware makes tools ACCESSIBLE THROUGH OPEN-SOURCE LICENSING; recorded projects include WATER MONITORING IN THE AMAZON. Decide what outcome the data is for before choosing the instrument. A reading that will go to a court needs a different protocol from one that will go to a public meeting, and these groups will tell you which.

trackers.name: Asociación Interamericana para la Defensa del Ambiente (AIDA) - a regional team of Latin American lawyers AND scientists giving FREE legal and technical support to communities harmed by environmental damage, litigating through national and international human rights law
trackers.desc: THIS IS A REGIONAL TEAM OF LAWYERS AND SCIENTISTS WHO WORK FOR COMMUNITIES FREE, AND ITS SCIENTISTS COME WITH THE LAWYERS. It is A REGIONAL NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION THAT USES LAW AND SCIENCE TO PROTECT THE ENVIRONMENT AND THE COMMUNITIES AFFECTED BY ENVIRONMENTAL HARM, PRINCIPALLY IN LATIN AMERICA, providing FREE LEGAL AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT and FREE ADVICE THAT SERVES AS A BRIDGE BETWEEN COMMUNITIES, LOCAL MOVEMENTS, NATIONAL ORGANISATIONS, GOVERNMENTS AND INTERNATIONAL ORGANISMS; its team of ADVOCATES, ATTORNEYS, AND SCIENTISTS... ARE BOTH FROM AND IN LATIN AMERICA and UNDERSTAND THE LEGAL AND POLITICAL CONTEXT OF THE REGION BECAUSE they WERE BORN AND LIVE IN LATIN AMERICA. It has MORE THAN 25 YEARS OF EXPERIENCE. Scientists and lawyers in the same team, both free. The usual gap in a community case is not the legal argument but the technical rebuttal of the developer's study, and this organisation supplies both. WHAT IT SAYS IT DOES WITH THAT COMBINATION: it works at THE NEXUS BETWEEN THE ENVIRONMENT AND HUMAN RIGHTS, BRINGING INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS LAW TO ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS, and through STRATEGIES OF LITIGATION AND ADVOCACY, USING NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL LEGAL TOOLS, SUPPORTED BY SCIENCE, it presses states TO COMPLY WITH THEIR OBLIGATION TO PROTECT THE HUMAN RIGHT TO A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT; it uses LEGAL STRATEGIES BASED ON SCIENCE AND PUBLIC PARTICIPATION and works WITH SCIENTISTS TO ENSURE THAT ITS WORK HAS SOLID BASES AND WITH COMMUNICATORS TO SPREAD THE MESSAGES. International human rights law applied to a local environmental case. Where the national courts have closed, that is the route this organisation was built to open. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY DONE: recorded work includes a long campaign in one Andean town where it FOUGHT THE POISONING OF THE POPULATION BY HEAVY METALS AND OTHER CONTAMINANTS EMITTED BY A LOCAL SMELTER, and significant impact on the protection of a sea turtle in a Central American country THROUGH AN ASSOCIATION WITH a national environmental law organisation. Its method is to work through a national organisation rather than around it. Approach it together with the environmental lawyers already in your country, which makes acceptance more likely. WHO IT IS AND WHERE ITS PARTNERS ARE: founded in 1998 by five environmental law groups from four Latin American countries and one northern one TO BUILD AND EXTEND THE CAPACITIES OF NATIONAL DEFENDERS, it WORKS WITH PARTNERS IN COUNTRIES SUCH AS ARGENTINA, CANADA, CHILE, COLOMBIA, COSTA RICA, ECUADOR, MEXICO AND PERU, with recorded legal work also in Brazil; it is a member of an international land coalition. Ask which national organisation is its partner in your country. That is the door, and the partner list is published by the coalitions it belongs to. THE CAPACITY IT ADDS BEYOND ONE CASE: its stated aim is TO STRENGTHEN THE CAPACITY OF PEOPLE TO GUARANTEE THE INDIVIDUAL AND COLLECTIVE RIGHT TO A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT... THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT, IMPLEMENTATION AND EFFECTIVE ENFORCEMENT OF NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL LAW, and it seeks to ensure that INTERNATIONAL POLICIES, LAWS AND FINANCIAL FLOWS CONTRIBUTE TO THE PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT; it runs legal internships placing law students on country work. Financial flows are named among its targets. Where a project depends on an international bank or investor, that is a second front this organisation already works on.

trackers.name: Accountability Counsel - free support for communities complaining to the accountability offices of banks financing a harmful project, taking cases ONLY WHERE THE COMMUNITY ASKS, plus a searchable global complaints database and a resource guide
trackers.desc: IT ONLY TAKES CASES WHERE THE COMMUNITY ASKS FIRST, AND IT SAYS WHY. It states: TO ENSURE THAT WE DO NOT REPLICATE THE POWER DYNAMIC WE SEEK TO UPEND AND ARE A TRUSTED, WANTED PARTNER IN COMMUNITIES, WE ONLY TAKE CASES IN WHICH COMMUNITIES REQUEST OUR SUPPORT; assistance BEGINS WITH A REQUEST FOR SUPPORT FROM THE COMMUNITY ITSELF OR A LOCAL CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATION, and NEARLY ALL CASES COME TO US THROUGH REFERRALS THROUGH CIVIL SOCIETY NETWORKS, OFTEN WITH ONLY ONE OR TWO DEGREES OF SEPARATION; it asks that a case INVOLVE A TRUSTWORTHY LOCAL PARTNER WITH WHOM WE CAN CLOSELY COLLABORATE, and weighs THE LIKELIHOOD OF A COMPLAINT LEADING TO A POSITIVE RESULT AT THE COMMUNITY LEVEL and of CREATING SYSTEMIC CHANGE AT THE INSTITUTIONAL LEVEL. Ask through an organisation that already knows you. One or two degrees of separation is the stated norm, so the introduction matters more than the application. WHAT IT DOES: it ASSIST[S] COMMUNITIES TO DEFEND THEIR RIGHTS THROUGH COMPLAINTS TO ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICES TIED TO PROJECTS THAT CAUSE HARM, specialising in NON-JUDICIAL COMPLAINT OFFICES ESTABLISHED TO RECEIVE COMMUNITY COMPLAINTS; its case work RANGES FROM INTENSIVE AND COMPREHENSIVE ASSISTANCE TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND THEIR PARTNERS THROUGHOUT A COMPLAINT PROCESS, TO PROVIDING MORE TARGETED SUPPORT WITH DAILY CASE WORK CONDUCTED PRIMARILY BY LOCAL PARTNERS, and it CONDUCT[S] TRAININGS IN LOCAL COMMUNITIES ABOUT ALL OPTIONS FOR ADDRESSING HUMAN RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL ABUSES ASSOCIATED WITH INTERNATIONALLY FINANCED PROJECTS. A complaint to a bank's own accountability office runs alongside any court case rather than replacing it. Ask for the training even if you never file: it maps every route available against a financed project. WHAT IT HAS ACHIEVED, INCLUDING IN THIS REGION: recorded results include supporting communities TO PREVENT ABUSES IN MEXICO and elsewhere, TO COMPEL REDESIGN OF A PROJECT in one country and TO REACH HISTORIC AGREEMENTS in others including one Caribbean state; its impact includes REDESIGNED PROJECTS THAT NOW REFLECT COMMUNITY NEEDS, HARM STOPPED AND PREVENTED TO DEFEND WATER RESOURCES, AND AGREEMENTS RESULTING IN COMPENSATION. Redesign, prevention and compensation are the realistic outcomes. A complaint of this kind rarely cancels a project outright, and knowing that before starting keeps a community's expectations intact. THE DATABASE AND GUIDE ANYONE CAN USE: it runs THE WORLD'S MOST COMPREHENSIVE COMMUNITY COMPLAINT DATABASE — SEARCH BY REGION, SECTOR, INSTITUTION, TYPE OF HARM, and a comparison of accountability policies ACROSS SIXTEEN INSTITUTIONS; its resource guide contains INFORMATION ABOUT TOOLS FOR REDRESSING HUMAN RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL VIOLATIONS BY INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS, EXPORT PROMOTION AGENCIES, AND PRIVATE CORPORATE ACTORS, intended TO ASSIST COMMUNITY LEADERS, LAWYERS, NGOs, AND INDIVIDUALS IN DETERMINING WHAT RIGHTS THEY HAVE AND HOW TO FILE A COMPLAINT, and it also covers INFORMATION DISCLOSURE RULES at those institutions. Search the database for your sector before writing anything. Someone has complained about a comparable project and the outcome tells you what to ask for. WHICH OFFICES EXIST, AND WHERE THE GAPS ARE: the offices it works with include those of the regional development bank for this continent, the world bank's public and private arms, a climate fund, a development programme's compliance unit and one national development bank's ombudsperson; it records that THERE ARE MANY COMMUNITIES THAT LACK AN AVAILABLE ACCOUNTABILITY OPTION BECAUSE NO SUCH ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICE EXISTS AT THE INSTITUTION(S) FINANCING A PROJECT, and works to open avenues where investment has none, INCLUDING IMPACT INVESTMENT, PRIVATE EQUITY, AND FINANCING FROM CHINESE INSTITUTIONS; its advocacy removed a requirement that complainants cite specific policy violations, since PREVIOUSLY A COMPLAINT COULD BE REJECTED IF IT DID NOT CONTAIN THIS TECHNICAL INFORMATION. Identify the financier before assuming there is a complaint office. Where the money is private equity or a Chinese lender there may be none, and that absence is itself worth publicising.

trackers.name: The Latin American Water Funds Partnership - 26 operating water funds in named cities across ten countries, paying for conservation in the catchments that supply them, some composed of INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, with technical accompaniment to create new ones
trackers.desc: TWENTY-SIX WATER FUNDS ARE ALREADY OPERATING IN NAMED CITIES, PAYING FOR CONSERVATION IN THE CATCHMENTS THAT SUPPLY THEM. The alliance behind them PROMOTED THE CREATION OF water funds described as ORGANISATIONS OF COLLECTIVE ACTION THAT DRIVE A SHARED AND LONG-TERM VISION OF WATER SECURITY; twenty-six now operate in cities including named capitals and provincial cities across ten countries, and in one recent year the programme recorded 44,116 HECTARES POSITIVELY IMPACTED WITH 16,271 FAMILIES. Cumulatively the funds have LEVERAGED MORE THAN US$249 MILLION and convened MORE THAN 340 PUBLIC, PRIVATE and other actors; an earlier count recorded THE CONSERVATION OF 252,000 HECTARES CRITICAL FOR THE WATER SECURITY OF THE REGION THROUGH PROJECTS DEVELOPED WITH 37,500 FAMILIES. Money that flows from a city's water users to the families who keep the upper catchment intact. Where the land you are defending sits above a city's intake, that is the argument with a funding mechanism already attached. WHO SITS INSIDE THEM: the funds WORK CLOSELY WITH THE LOCAL COMMUNITIES, SOME BEING EVEN COMPOSED OF INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, one such fund having won a United Nations equatorial prize; the model is described as PLATFORMS OF GOVERNANCE TO ADDRESS WATER CHALLENGES AND SHARE RESPONSIBILITIES AND ACCOUNTABILITY for society, as EFFECTIVE MECHANISMS TO IMPROVE WATER AVAILABILITY, BIODIVERSITY AND CLIMATE ADAPTATION for governments, and as a way for companies to address RISKS OF PHYSICAL ACCESS TO WATER IN QUALITY AND QUANTITY. A fund composed of indigenous communities is a precedent, not an exception. Ask to see that one's governing documents before agreeing to any structure a utility proposes. WHAT THE ALLIANCE PROVIDES TO A NEW FUND: it supports funds through SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE TO REACH AND MAINTAIN WATER SECURITY WITH NATURE-BASED SOLUTIONS; THE SYSTEMATISATION, MANAGEMENT AND DIFFUSION OF KNOWLEDGE; THE DEVELOPMENT OF CAPACITIES AND TECHNICAL ACCOMPANIMENT; THE PROMOTION OF DIALOGUE BETWEEN RELEVANT ACTORS OF THE REGION IN AN INCLUSIVE MANNER... ACTIVE PARTICIPATION IN THE DESIGN OF WATER GOVERNANCE AND THE MOBILISATION OF RESOURCES FROM PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SOURCES; at one point 15 ADDITIONAL WATER FUNDS were IN THE PROCESS OF CREATION. Technical accompaniment to design the fund and to mobilise the money. A municipality that wants one does not have to invent the model, and fifteen were being built at once. WHO IS BEHIND IT, WHICH DECIDES HOW YOU APPROACH IT: the alliance is AN AGREEMENT CREATED IN 2011 between a regional development bank, a global environment fund, a corporate foundation, an international climate initiative and a global conservation organisation, with A GROWING LIST OF LOCAL PARTNERS and more than two hundred organisations involved. A bottler's foundation and a development bank sit at the same table as the conservation organisation. Read the governance before joining, and be clear what the fund may and may not spend on. WHAT INDIVIDUAL FUNDS HAVE BUILT: recorded innovations include THE FIRST LABORATORY FOR CENTRAL AMERICA OF STABLE ISOTOPES and THE CREATION OF THE BANK CARD FOR WATER CONSERVATION by one national fund; two funds have concentrated on EFFICIENCY IN THE USE OF WATER in agriculture. A stable isotope laboratory can trace where water in a well actually comes from. Where a project is accused of drying a spring, that is the technical service to ask a water fund for.

trackers.name: Mongabay Latam and the regional environmental journalists' network - a newsroom of 90+ journalists across 14 countries with a published contact for story tips, satellite and data investigations that have INFORMED JUDICIAL AND POLICE ACTION, and an honest account of the risk to sources
trackers.desc: A REGIONAL NEWSROOM OF MORE THAN NINETY ENVIRONMENTAL JOURNALISTS, AND A PUBLISHED EMAIL FOR TAKING A STORY TO THEM. A network of environmental journalists across the region records MORE THAN 120 SERIES AND INVESTIGATIONS IN THE LAST EIGHT YEARS THAT HAVE INCLUDED JOURNALISTS AND MEDIA OF 14 COUNTRIES OF THE REGION; the regional newsroom behind it publishes a contact address for anyone who NEEDS HELP WITH A STORY and asks writers to CONSULT THE PAGE THAT EXPLAINS THE CONDITIONS FOR COLLABORATIONS first. Its reporting draws on INDIGENOUS LEADERS, LOCAL SCIENTISTS, PARK RANGERS, FISHERS, FARMERS AND ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDERS as SOURCES AND PRINCIPAL ACTORS. An editor's email address, and community sources treated as principal actors rather than colour. Read the collaboration conditions before writing, then send the documents, not the outrage. WHY COVERAGE CHANGES A LAND FIGHT: the newsroom has built 20-PLUS DATABASES CONTAINING CRITICAL INFORMATION ON MINING, DRUG TRAFFICKING, FINES IMPOSED ON FOSSIL FUEL AND PALM OIL COMPANIES, CASES OF ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDER KILLINGS THAT HAVE GONE UNPUNISHED OR THAT HAVE BEEN PROSECUTED, GEOLOCATED ENVIRONMENTAL LIABILITIES LIKE CONTAMINATED SITES LEFT BEHIND BY THE OIL INDUSTRY, and records that THE FINDINGS HAVE BEEN USED TO INFORM JUDICIAL AND POLICE ACTION; one series analysed MORE THAN 724,000 satellite DEFORESTATION ALERTS... TO DOCUMENT ILLEGAL DEFORESTATION OF INDIGENOUS LANDS in four countries, and a satellite analysis of two protected areas in one country counted alerts inside each before A TEAM OF JOURNALISTS TRAVELLED TO THESE AREAS. Their analysis has fed judicial and police action. A published investigation is not only pressure — it can be the document a prosecutor opens a file on. WHAT THE JOURNALISTS BRING THAT A COMMUNITY USUALLY CANNOT BUY: collaborators have acquired experience in INVESTIGATION, SATELLITE ANALYSIS, DATA JOURNALISM, MULTIMEDIA PRODUCTION AND CROSS-BORDER WORK, and for allied outlets these collaborations HAVE OPENED ACCESS TO SPECIALISED COVERAGE THAT, IN MANY CASES, WOULD BE COSTLY TO PRODUCE ON THEIR OWN; the strongest reporting came from JOURNALISTS WHO KNEW THE LOCAL STORY AND COULD RECOGNISE WHEN A SPECIFIC CONFLICT FORMED PART OF A BROADER PATTERN. Show the editor how your case fits a pattern across several places. A single village dispute is a local story; the same company or the same permit failing in five places is a regional investigation. THE HONEST RISK, IN THEIR OWN WORDS: the network records AN ESCALATION OF VIOLENCE THAT GROWS AT GREAT SPEED AND THAT INCREASINGLY PUTS AT RISK OUR SECURITY AND THAT OF OUR SOURCES, ESPECIALLY THOSE OF INDIGENOUS AND COMMUNITY LEADERS, alongside THE LEGAL ONSLAUGHT FROM POLITICAL AND ECONOMIC POWER TO THREATEN JOURNALISTS WHO REVEAL UNCOMFORTABLE TRUTHS. Sources are named in print unless you agree otherwise in advance. Decide who speaks and under what protection before the first interview, and read this alongside the protection funds filed for defenders. THE WIDER STRUCTURE BEHIND IT: the regional newsroom operates as part of a global environmental news organisation producing content IN FOUR LANGUAGES WITH 500 CORRESPONDENTS IN 50 COUNTRIES, largely as a non-profit, and it seeks A NETWORK OF COLLABORATORS; the regional journalists' network was formed because OUR COUNTRIES HAVE THE SAME ENVIRONMENTAL PROBLEMS WITH DIFFERENT NUANCES AND, LIVING IN A GLOBALISED WORLD, IMPUNITY CANNOT be treated as local. Ask which correspondent covers your country. A local journalist inside a regional network can place a story that a national outlet would drop under pressure.

trackers.name: CLOC-Vía Campesina - a continental coordination of 96 peasant, indigenous and Afro-descendant member organisations across 18-21 countries, organised around RECOVERY OF LAND, with women's and youth assemblies and a campaign against persecution of rural activists
trackers.desc: NINETY-SIX PEASANT, INDIGENOUS AND AFRO-DESCENDANT ORGANISATIONS ARE FORMALLY MEMBERS OF ONE CONTINENTAL BODY, AND THE LIST IS PUBLIC. It describes itself as AN INSTANCE OF CONTINENTAL ARTICULATION representing PEASANT, WORKER, INDIGENOUS AND AFRO-DESCENDANT MOVEMENTS OF ALL LATIN AMERICA, formally constituted at a congress in 1994; it recorded 84 ORGANISATIONS IN 18 COUNTRIES OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, and at a recent congress ten further organisations were INTEGRATING (OR RE-INTEGRATING IN SOME CASES) AS FORMAL MEMBERS... TAKING THE TOTAL NUMBER OF MEMBER ORGANISATIONS TO 96, with representatives of 21 COUNTRIES attending. A published membership list of ninety-six organisations. Find the member in your country and your province: it is the body that already has lawyers, buses and people for a land conflict, and it costs nothing to ask. WHAT ITS MEMBERS ORGANISE AROUND: members work for THE PRESERVATION, RECOVERY AND CONQUEST OF THE LAND, THE WATER, THE SEEDS AND OTHER NATURAL RESOURCES, FOOD SOVEREIGNTY BASED ON AGROECOLOGY, SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION AND AN EQUALITY BASED ON SMALL AND MEDIUM SCALE PRODUCTION, developing SOLIDARITY, COOPERATION, THE UNITY IN DIVERSITY BETWEEN THE MEMBER ORGANISATIONS; its recent congress had the aim of CONSOLIDATING A COMMON STRUGGLE IN DEFENCE OF THE RIGHTS OF PEASANT AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, AND GUARANTEEING ACCESS TO LAND AND AGROECOLOGICAL PRODUCTION, in a context of organisations UNITING WITH RENEWED FORCE... IN DEFENCE OF THEIR TERRITORIES. Recovery of land is stated as an aim, not implied. Where your dispute is about who holds the land rather than how it is used, this is the network whose members have done that work for thirty years. WHERE IT SITS IN THE WIDER STRUCTURE: it PROMOTED AND WAS THE ORGANISING PILLAR OF the international peasant movement, A SPACE OF INTERNATIONAL ARTICULATION OF RURAL ORGANISATIONS AND SOCIAL MOVEMENTS OF AMERICA, ASIA AND EUROPE, and it is that movement's DIRECT ALLY... ON OUR CONTINENT; a recorded congress drew delegates of 88 PEASANT AND INDIGENOUS ORGANISATIONS FROM 25 COUNTRIES OF THE CONTINENT. A local conflict raised through a member reaches an international movement with standing at the United Nations food agency. That is a route no single village association has on its own. WHAT IT HAS ACHIEVED IN POLICY: one of its first global disputes involved THE INCORPORATION OF THE CONCEPT OF FOOD SOVEREIGNTY AS A RESPONSE TO THE WORLD FOOD CRISIS, after which the United Nations food and agriculture organisation modified its initial position, and the movement has been central to the defence of PEASANT RIGHTS recognised internationally. The peasant rights declaration it drove is now an international instrument. Members can tell you how it has been used in national courts. THE INTERNAL ASSEMBLIES WORTH KNOWING ABOUT: it holds continental assemblies of rural women and of rural youth, its women's assembly declaring for A SOCIETY WHERE THE WOMEN OF THE COUNTRYSIDE LIVE FREE OF VIOLENCE, WITH LAND, AUTONOMY, RIGHTS, JUSTICE AND DIGNITY; and, FACED WITH THE GROWING CRIMINALITY AND THE PERSECUTIONS THAT PEASANT ORGANISATIONS AND ACTIVISTS SUFFER, it has run a campaign on the demilitarisation of the countryside. It has organised for years around persecution of rural activists. Where members of your community are being criminalised, its members know which lawyers and which alarm networks work in your country. THE HONEST NOTE ON WHAT IT IS: the body is explicitly political, describing itself as anti-capitalist and anti-imperialist and assuming THE CLASS STRUGGLE AS A MEANS TO ACHIEVE A DEMOCRATIC AND PLURAL SOCIETY. That framing is stated openly, so decide whether it fits your community before affiliating. Working with a member organisation on one land case does not require adopting its whole platform, but it will be read as alignment by opponents.

trackers.name: COICA - the Amazon basin indigenous coordination representing 511 peoples through named national organisations in nine countries, whose first statutory objective is to DEFEND TERRITORIAL CLAIMS, and which covers peoples in voluntary isolation
trackers.desc: ONE COORDINATION SPEAKS FOR 511 INDIGENOUS PEOPLES ACROSS NINE AMAZON COUNTRIES, THROUGH A NAMED NATIONAL ORGANISATION IN EACH. It describes itself as AN INDIGENOUS ORGANISATION OF INTERNATIONAL CONVERGENCE THAT ACTS IN REPRESENTATION OF 511 INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, OF WHICH APPROXIMATELY 66 ARE INDIGENOUS PEOPLES IN VOLUNTARY ISOLATION AND INITIAL CONTACT, ARTICULATED THROUGH POLITICAL-ORGANISATIONAL BASE ORGANISATIONS, PRESENT IN THE 9 AMAZON COUNTRIES; those members are named individually for Peru, Brazil, Venezuela, Bolivia, Ecuador, Guyana, Colombia, Suriname and French Guiana. Founded in 1984 at a first congress, it has been domiciled in one Andean capital since 1993. Nine national indigenous organisations, each named and reachable. Your national member is the body that already sits in ministries and courts on territorial matters, and it has affiliates at regional and community level below it. WHAT ITS STATUTES COMMIT IT TO: its objectives are TO PROMOTE, DEVELOP AND DRIVE THE MECHANISMS FOR THE INTERACTION OF THE PEOPLES AND INDIGENOUS ORGANISATIONS that are its members, and TO DEFEND THE TERRITORIAL CLAIMS, THE FREE DETERMINATION OF THE INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, THE HUMAN RIGHTS OF THEIR MEMBERS AND OTHER RIGHTS AND INTERESTS; its mission is THE PROMOTION, PROTECTION AND SECURITY OF THE INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND TERRITORIES THROUGH THE DEFENCE OF THEIR FORMS OF LIFE, PRINCIPLES AND SOCIAL, SPIRITUAL AND CULTURAL VALUES. Defending territorial claims is the first stated objective, not a programme it might add. A dispute over the boundary of a titled or untitled territory is the core of what this structure exists for. THE PEOPLES IT SPECIFICALLY COVERS THAT OTHERS DO NOT: some sixty-six of the peoples it represents are IN VOLUNTARY ISOLATION AND INITIAL CONTACT. Where a project's footprint may touch a people in isolation, that is a distinct legal and ethical regime and this coordination and its national members hold the evidence and the standing on it. HOW THE MEMBERSHIP HAS CHANGED, WHICH MATTERS WHEN YOU WRITE: the recorded history shows members added and substituted over time — a Brazilian organisation replacing an earlier body, a Colombian Amazon organisation replacing a national indigenous organisation in 1995, and a regional Venezuelan organisation replacing a national council in 2005 — and the figure of president was replaced by a general coordinator. Check which organisation currently holds the seat for your country before writing. Older directories still list bodies that were replaced twenty years ago. THE SCALE AND THE STANDING: it is described as THE LARGEST INDIGENOUS ORGANISATION IN THE WORLD, recorded a population of nearly 2.8 million people across its member organisations, holds membership of an international conservation union, and built its own communication system including a magazine and a portal PROGRAMMED FOR THE 4 LANGUAGES and a mail system to SUPPORT THE DEMANDS OF ALL THE MEMBER ORGANISATIONS. Membership of the international conservation union gives it a seat where protected areas are decided. Where a state proposes a park over a territory, that is a table your national member can reach. THE HONEST NOTE ON ROUTE: the coordination works through its national members and their affiliates rather than with individual communities directly. Go to your national member first, and to its regional affiliate before that. A request arriving at the continental office without the national organisation behind it will be sent back down the chain.

trackers.name: Afro-descendant territorial mapping viewer and the Central American Black Organization - a free regional cartographic tool built with Afro-descendant representatives showing lands and territories, alongside the cross-border network of national Garifuna, Creole and Black organisations
trackers.desc: THERE IS NOW A FREE CARTOGRAPHIC VIEWER SHOWING AFRO-DESCENDANT PRESENCE, LANDS AND TERRITORIES ACROSS LATIN AMERICA. A joint investigation TO IDENTIFY THE PRESENCE, THE LANDS AND TERRITORIES OF THE AFRO-DESCENDANT PEOPLE IN LATIN AMERICA produced, FOR THE FIRST TIME, A FREELY ACCESSIBLE CARTOGRAPHIC VIEWER that BRINGS TOGETHER DECISIVE DATA IN THE REGION ON THE TERRITORIAL PRESENCE AND THE SIGNIFICANT RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THESE TERRITORIES AND AREAS OF GREAT IMPORTANCE FOR CONSERVATION AND TERRESTRIAL AND OCEANIC CLIMATE STABILITY; it COMBINES MORE THAN 100 STATE, PRIVATE AND ORGANISATIONAL SOURCES and has been CONTRASTED AND ENRICHED WITH CARTOGRAPHIC INFORMATION BUILT WITH REPRESENTATIVES OF THE AFRO-DESCENDANT PEOPLE IN THE COUNTRIES OF THE STUDY, covering AFRO-DESCENDANT, BLACK, MAROON, GARIFUNA AND CREOLE PEOPLES. A map built with Afro-descendant representatives rather than about them, and free to open. Where a community's occupation of land is denied in an official file, that viewer is a published source it can cite. WHY IT MATTERS FOR A LAND CLAIM: it is THE FIRST TIME THERE IS A TOOL THAT MAKES VISIBLE POPULATION, TERRITORIAL AND ECOSYSTEM DATA AT REGIONAL SCALE, and it was built to show the overlap between those territories and areas critical for conservation and climate. Overlap with a conservation priority area is an argument a ministry understands. Print the map layer showing your territory inside such an area and attach it to the submission. THE REGIONAL ORGANISATION BEHIND AFRO-CENTRAL AMERICAN CLAIMS: a Black Central American organisation WAS BORN IN DANGRIGA, BELIZE, ON AUGUST 25, 1995, WITH THE PURPOSE OF ESTABLISHING A CROSS-BORDER ORGANIZATION CAPABLE OF MAKING VISIBLE AND STRENGTHENING THE SOCIAL, POLITICAL, ECONOMIC, CULTURAL, ENVIRONMENTAL AND ORGANIZATIONAL LIFE OF THE AFRO-CENTRAL AMERICAN COMMUNITIES and those in the diaspora, and is described as THE ONLY ORGANIZATION OF ITS KIND, holding annual assemblies since its foundation; it STRENGTHENS THE POPULATION'S INSTITUTIONAL DEVELOPMENT THROUGH THE ESTABLISHMENT OF COORDINATION MECHANISMS AND INTER-INSTITUTIONAL SUPPORT. A cross-border body for Garifuna, Creole and Black communities from Belize to Panama. Where the same people are split by a national border, that is the organisation that can carry a claim on both sides. WHAT ITS MEMBER ORGANISATIONS ARE, BY COUNTRY: recorded members include national Garifuna and Creole councils and an educational foundation in one country, Black organisations and a Black women's organisation in another, a community and ethnic development organisation in a third, a Garifuna organisation and a coast development association in a fourth, a Caribbean project association and an Afro-Costa Rican women's centre in a fifth, and an Afro-Panamanian response body, an Afro-Panamanian women's network and an ethnic museum association in a sixth, plus diaspora organisations. Each is a real, named organisation in a named country. Find the one nearest you rather than writing to the regional body first. WHAT ITS ASSEMBLIES HAVE WORKED ON: recorded agendas include MAPPING AND INVENTORY OF RESOURCES IN THE AFRO-CENTRAL AMERICAN COMMUNITIES, land tenure, participation of Afro communities in the local economy, and guaranteeing AT THE HIGHEST LEVEL THE PARTICIPATION OF THE AFRO-CENTRAL AMERICAN COMMUNITIES AND POPULATIONS WITHIN THE MESOAMERICAN BIOLOGICAL CORRIDOR INITIATIVE; one assembly recorded a DECLARATION OF DENUNCIATION BEFORE THE INTER-AMERICAN COMMISSION ON HUMAN RIGHTS. It has taken a denunciation to the inter-American commission before. Ask the national member how that was done and what it produced. THE HONEST CURRENCY WARNING: much of the accessible documentation of this network's membership and assemblies dates from the 2000s, though it remains listed as a member of a contemporary regional alliance and holds recent assemblies. Verify who currently leads it and which organisations are still members before relying on the list. The national members are the durable part; the regional office is not always reachable.

trackers.name: International Land Coalition, Latin America and the Caribbean - a regional platform of 61 member organisations across 20+ countries supporting MORE THAN 30 NATIONAL LAND COALITIONS, with a defender-protection commitment signed by every member and an independent land governance index
trackers.desc: MORE THAN THIRTY NATIONAL LAND COALITIONS EXIST, AND THEY ARE BROAD PLATFORMS THAT A LOCAL ORGANISATION CAN JOIN. The coalition SUPPORTS MORE THAN 30 NATIONAL LAND COALITIONS, described as BROAD PLATFORMS OF MEMBERS AND ALLIES THAT WORK IN FAVOUR OF land rights; its regional platform BRINGS TOGETHER 61 MEMBER ORGANISATIONS OF LOCAL, NATIONAL AND REGIONAL CIVIL SOCIETY OF DIVERSE PROFILES: GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS (SMALL PRODUCERS, PEASANTS, INDIGENOUS), WOMEN'S ORGANISATIONS AND/OR THOSE FOCUSED ON THIS SECTOR, NGOs, RESEARCH OR ACADEMIC CENTRES, AND ORGANISATIONS SPECIALISED IN KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT, drawn from MORE THAN 20 COUNTRIES, within a global membership of nearly three hundred in eighty-one countries. A grassroots organisation sits in the same platform as the research centres and the NGOs. Ask whether your country has a national coalition: that is the room where land conflicts get compared and carried upward. THE TWO COMMITMENTS EVERY MEMBER SIGNS: ALL THE MEMBERS OF THE coalition SIGN TWO IMPORTANT COMMITMENTS THAT PROTECT AND EMPOWER BOTH WOMEN AND LAND DEFENDERS WITHIN OUR NETWORK. Defender protection is a membership condition, not an optional programme. If members of your community are threatened, that commitment is something you can invoke by name. THE DATA TOOL THAT MEASURES YOUR GOVERNMENT: the coalition runs a land governance index whose data officer records that it REVEALS WORRYING TRENDS IN LAND GOVERNANCE and shows THE GAPS IN THE MONITORING THAT GOVERNMENTS CARRY OUT ON LAND GOVERNANCE, AND HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM THE WAY IN WHICH WOMEN AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, AMONG OTHER ACTORS, EXPERIENCE THAT GOVERNANCE; recorded country findings include one Caribbean island where THE INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES HAVE LITTLE ROOM FOR MANOEUVRE TO DECIDE ON THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROJECTS THAT AFFECT THEIR TERRITORIES, SINCE PRIOR CONSULTATION IS APPLIED DEFICIENTLY, one Central American country where only 3.18% OF A BUDGET OF USD 184 MILLION reached family farming while THE CRISIS FACED BY LAND DEFENDERS... IS PERPETUATED BY THE STATE IN ALLIANCE WITH THE CORPORATIONS WITH INTEREST IN THEIR TERRITORIES, and another with AN ALARMING DISPOSSESSION OF LANDS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND AFRO-DESCENDANT COMMUNITIES, BECAUSE OF THE EXPANSION OF THE AGRICULTURAL FRONTIER. An independent index that contradicts the government's own monitoring, country by country. Quote your country's score back at the ministry that claims consultation works. THE LAND DEAL DATABASE AND ITS REGIONAL FOCAL POINT: a global land acquisitions observatory names a regional focal point organisation for Latin America and coordinates national pilot land observatories in several countries with the coalition. If a large land acquisition has been announced near you, check whether it is already recorded there — and if it is not, the focal point is who records it. WHAT ITS OWN ANALYSIS SAYS ABOUT THIS REGION: land IS AT THE CENTRE OF DIVERSE CONFLICTS IN THE REGION, WHERE THE HIGHEST NUMBER OF ATTACKS AGAINST THE PEOPLE WHO DEFEND IT IS RECORDED, LINKED IN GREAT MEASURE TO THE EXTRACTIVE INDUSTRIES; the coalition works THROUGH THE PROMOTION OF REGIONAL PLATFORMS AND NATIONAL COALITIONS... SO THAT THE WOMEN, MEN AND COMMUNITIES WHO LIVE ON AND FROM THE LAND HAVE DECISION-MAKING POWER OVER THEIR LANDS AND TERRITORIES. The region with the most attacks on land defenders is the one you are in. Read this entry with the protection funds and the pro bono routes already filed.

trackers.name: Rainforest Foundation US - land titling accelerated with regional government agrarian offices (75,000 acres for 20 communities in months), 400+ trained and financed community patrollers monitoring 19.6M acres, and support to strengthen organisations' capacity to manage funds
trackers.desc: WHAT HISTORICALLY TOOK YEARS WAS DONE IN MONTHS: TWENTY COMMUNITIES TITLED 75,000 ACRES IN ONE INITIATIVE. The foundation records that, working IN CLOSE PARTNERSHIP with a national indigenous federation and a regional government agrarian directorate, it WAS ABLE TO SIGNIFICANTLY ACCELERATE THE TITLING PROCESS, MEANING WHAT HISTORICALLY TOOK YEARS WAS ACCOMPLISHED IN JUST MONTHS; through that initiative 20 COMMUNITIES... SECURED LEGAL TITLES IN RECORD TIME FOR 75,000 ACRES OF THEIR ANCESTRAL LANDS, and in another year SIXTEEN INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES it supported RECEIVED LEGAL TITLE TO THEIR ANCESTRAL LANDS; separately it supported titling initiatives AIMING TO SECURE LAND TENURE FOR MORE THAN 11M ACRES ACROSS three countries and advanced tenure security for NEARLY 300,000 ACRES with two peoples in another. Titling accelerated by working with the regional government office that issues the titles, not around it. That is the partnership shape to copy. THE MODEL, STEP BY STEP: its PROVEN LAND-TITLING MODEL is that COMMUNITIES MAP THEIR ANCESTRAL BOUNDARIES, STRENGTHEN THEIR GOVERNANCE, AND USE REAL-TIME MONITORING TOOLS... TO DETECT THREATS; INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS, FEDERATIONS, REGIONAL GOVERNMENTS and the foundation HAVE JOINED FORCES TO MAP AND TITLE INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' LANDS. Mapping, governance and monitoring are done together rather than in sequence. A community that starts mapping while its governance documents are weak will stall at the titling office. THE MONITORING PROGRAMME AND ITS SCALE: it has TRAINED AND FINANCED OVER 400 COMMUNITY-BASED PATROLLERS TO MONITOR AND PROTECT 19.6 MILLION ACRES OF THEIR LANDS ACROSS four countries, using a programme in which INDIGENOUS FOREST MONITORS USE SMARTPHONES, SATELLITE IMAGERY, AND DRONES TO DETECT THREATS AND PREVENT DEFORESTATION against ILLEGAL LOGGING, MINING, AND CRIMINAL ACTIVITY; an earlier year recorded 307 COMMUNITY-BASED FOREST PATROLLERS ACROSS 129 COMMUNITIES. In one country it supports AROUND 114 INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, FIVE INDIGENOUS FEDERATIONS, AND ONE REGIONAL INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' ORGANISATION to run it. Patrollers are trained and paid. Community monitoring fails when it depends on volunteers, and this programme treats it as work. THE MONEY IT MOVES TO COMMUNITIES: it UNLOCKED OVER $10.5 MILLION IN FUNDING FROM AROUND THE WORLD TO FUEL INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES' FOREST PROTECTION WORK in one year, and supports partners to STRENGTHEN ORGANIZATIONAL GOVERNANCE AND THEIR CAPACITY TO MANAGE FUNDS AND PROJECTS FOR THE COMMUNITY'S BENEFIT; its forward plan is to STRENGTHEN 67 INDIGENOUS AND LOCAL ORGANIZATIONS AND INCREASE THEIR ACCESS TO FUNDING. Capacity to manage funds is what unlocks direct financing. Ask for that support before asking for a grant, because the audit trail is what most community organisations lack. WHO IT WORKS THROUGH, AND THE DEFENDER RISK: its named partners include a Central American regional forest peoples alliance, a national umbrella organisation of one large country's indigenous peoples, a district council representing one people, and two national congresses representing peoples inside and outside a comarca; it records that THE AMAZON IS THE MOST DANGEROUS REGION IN THE WORLD FOR ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDERS and collaborates with a national federation TO IMPLEMENT PREVENTIVE MEASURES, ENABLING COMMUNITIES TO BE BETTER PREPARED AGAINST THESE THREATS. It works through representative organisations, not with communities directly. Approach through your federation or council — and note that it also plans titling for communities next to territories reserved for peoples in voluntary isolation, to build a protection corridor.

trackers.name: The Global Alliance of Territorial Communities and its Shandia platform - direct funding channelled to territorial organisations' own financial mechanisms, with FISCAL SPONSORSHIP and financial capacity support where an organisation cannot yet receive funds, plus named community-led funds already re-granting
trackers.desc: IF A COMMUNITY ORGANISATION HAS NO WAY TO RECEIVE INTERNATIONAL MONEY, THIS PLATFORM SAYS IT WILL FIND IT A FISCAL SPONSOR. Its published design states that regional and national component funding WILL BE CHANNELLED TO alliance member organisations, that those members WILL DETERMINE HOW REGIONAL/NATIONAL FUNDS WILL BE USED, CHANNELLED AND ADMINISTERED, USING THEIR OWN REGIONAL/NATIONAL FINANCIAL MECHANISMS, and that IF A REGIONAL/NATIONAL indigenous or local community ORGANISATION REQUIRES A FISCAL SPONSOR, THEY WILL BE SUPPORTED IN THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE FUNDS, AND PROVIDED CAPACITY BUILDING SUPPORT ON FINANCIAL management. The commonest reason a community group is refused international funding is that it cannot receive or account for the money. This platform treats that as the thing to fix rather than a reason to refuse. WHAT THE PLATFORM IS FOR: it is OUR COMMON PLATFORM TO PROMOTE AND FACILITATE DIRECT, PREDICTABLE, EFFECTIVE, AND SUSTAINABLE FUNDING FOR INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES THROUGH THE ESTABLISHMENT OF DIRECT REGIONAL AND NATIONAL FUNDING MECHANISMS, CAPACITY-BUILDING, EXCHANGE OF EXPERIENCES, AND ENHANCED DIALOGUE WITH DONORS; for the communities behind it, DIRECT FINANCING IS MORE THAN JUST MONETARY SUPPORT — IT IS A VITAL TOOL FOR SECURING OUR FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS... TO LIVE ON OUR LANDS, EXERCISE FREE, PRIOR, AND INFORMED CONSENT, PRESERVE AND ADAPT OUR TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE, AND LIVE FREE FROM VIOLENCE. Direct means the money does not pass through an intermediary NGO that takes the overhead and the decisions. Ask any donor offering to fund your community whether it can pay through one of these mechanisms. THE FUNDS THAT ALREADY EXIST UNDER IT: named community-led mechanisms include a Mesoamerican territorial fund, an Amazonian fund led by the Brazilian Amazon indigenous coordination, a fund launched by the national Brazilian indigenous articulation DEVELOPED THROUGH A COLLABORATIVE PROCESS LED BY a national forum of indigenous leaders and a fund working group, REFLECT[ING] A STRONG COMMITMENT TO DEMOCRATIC AND TRADITIONAL GOVERNANCE PRACTICES, a quilombola fund, a fund led by a movement of babassu coconut breaker women, and further funds in Asia that have BEGUN RE-GRANTING IN SIX COUNTRIES, FOCUSING ON INDIGENOUS WOMEN, YOUTH, AND PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES and working to REACH REMOTE COMMUNITIES, SIMPLIFY GRANT ACCESS, BUILD CAPACITY. Several of these funds re-grant to communities in their own region. Ask which one covers your country and whether it has an open window — they are separate from the alliance itself. WHO THE ALLIANCE IS: A COALITION OF INDIGENOUS AND LOCAL COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS FROM MESOAMERICA, AMAZONIA, AFRICA AND ASIA, PROTECTING MORE THAN 958 MILLION HECTARES OF TROPICAL FORESTS and representing 35 MILLION PEOPLE FROM FOREST TERRITORIES IN 24 COUNTRIES, made up of five named networks including the Amazon basin coordination, the Mesoamerican forest peoples alliance and the national Brazilian indigenous articulation; the Mesoamerican alliance's own members are listed by name, from national forestry alliances to named indigenous nations and general congresses. Your national organisation is probably already inside this structure through one of the five networks. Trace the chain upward before assuming you need a new relationship. THE EXCHANGES IT RUNS BETWEEN TERRITORIES: recorded exchanges include Brazilian community funds invited to Mesoamerica to bring their experience to the grassroots of the alliance there, and a delegation from eight African countries meeting Brazilian community fund experts for nine days in indigenous communities; one review recorded honestly that grassroots organisations in that African network STILL HAVE LIMITED, THOUGH GROWING, CAPACITY TO REQUEST AND MANAGE RESOURCES FROM INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION. That honesty is useful. If your organisation cannot yet manage an international grant, say so and ask for the capacity support first — it is a stated part of the offer, not a disqualification.

trackers.name: Business & Human Rights Resource Centre - invites companies to answer a community's allegation and PUBLISHES THE NON-RESPONSE on the company's own page, with regional researchers, investor escalation and published policy and benchmark data on 10,000+ companies
trackers.desc: A COMPANY'S REFUSAL TO ANSWER A COMMUNITY'S ALLEGATION IS ITSELF PUBLISHED, ON ITS OWN PAGE. The centre INVITE[S] COMPANIES TO RESPOND TO ALLEGATIONS OF MISCONDUCT AND PUBLISH[ES] THEIR COMMENTS, doing so WHEN WE FIND NO EVIDENCE THAT THEY HAVE OTHERWISE RESPONDED TO THE CONCERNS; the process ENCOURAGES COMPANIES TO PUBLICLY ADDRESS HUMAN RIGHTS CONCERNS, AND PROVIDES THE PUBLIC WITH BOTH THE ALLEGATIONS AND THE COMPANY'S COMMENTS. It states plainly: WE INDICATE RESPONSE RATES IN THE COMPANY SECTIONS OF THE SITE, and IF A COMPANY IS LISTED AS HAVING FAILED TO RESPOND TO A PARTICULAR ALLEGATION, BUT IT HAS IN FACT ISSUED A RESPONSE... PLEASE LET US KNOW. A permanent public record that the company was asked and said nothing. For a developer that presents itself as responsible to lenders and buyers, that line on its own page is a cost. THE SCALE AND WHO DOES THE ASKING: it collects evidence on MORE THAN 10,000 COMPANIES IN MORE THAN 180 COUNTRIES and takes up ALLEGED ABUSE QUICKLY AND DIRECTLY WITH COMPANIES, INVITING THEM TO RESPOND TO SPECIFIC ALLEGATIONS (OVER 1,500 PER YEAR); a network of regional researchers BUILD LONG TERM RELATIONSHIPS WITH HUMAN RIGHTS ADVOCATES ON THE GROUND, BRINGING UNDERSTANDING OF THE DYNAMICS IN THE COUNTRIES THEY COVER, and WHERE THERE IS AN ALLEGATION OF CORPORATE HUMAN RIGHTS ABUSE THAT HAS NO PUBLIC RESPONSE, THEY REACH OUT TO THE COMPANY. Its site runs in several languages including Spanish and Portuguese. There is a researcher for your region who already knows the local advocates. Send the documented allegation to them rather than to a general address. WHAT IT DOES BEYOND PUBLISHING: its recorded practice is that DIALOGUES CAN EXTEND FURTHER AND OCCASIONALLY WE TAKE AN ACTIVE ROLE IN SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES AND NGOs; in one recorded case concerning an imprisoned indigenous leader who HAD LED THE OPPOSITION TO A PROPOSED... MINE IN HIS COMMUNITY'S TERRITORY, it POSTED THE ALLEGATIONS ON OUR WEBSITE AND SOUGHT RESPONSES FROM TWO COMPANIES WHO DID NOT RESPOND, AND ASSISTED THE LOCAL VILLAGERS IN SUBMITTING THE CASE TO THE UN SPECIAL REPRESENTATIVE ON HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, then CONTACTED PUBLIC INVESTORS... AND INVITED THEM TO COMMENT, of whom two responded and ONE COMMITTED TO RAISING THE ISSUE WITH ITS CLIENTS WHO ARE INVESTED in the company. Going up the chain to the investors is the step that moves a company. Identify who holds the shares or the loan before you send the allegation, and ask that they be invited to comment too. THE HONEST NUMBERS: the centre records a response rate averaging 43% on one page and 60% on another, and its own field acknowledges criticism about WEAK AND TANGENTIAL COMPANY RESPONSES and about the LACK OF REMEDY AND THE INEQUITY IN ARMS FOR THOSE AFFECTED BY ABUSE; a published analysis notes that A COMPANY RESPONSE TO A CRITICAL CIVIL SOCIETY REPORT IS NOT NECESSARILY A POSITIVE SIGN. Roughly half of companies answer, and an answer is not a remedy. Treat this as a public record and a pressure point, not as a complaint procedure that decides anything. WHAT IT ALSO PUBLISHES ON EACH COMPANY: company pages carry news, allegations, KEY DATA POINTS BASED ON CORPORATE POLICIES, AND SCORES FROM PROMINENT CIVIL SOCIETY BENCHMARKS, and its stated goals include a SAFE AND ENABLING ENVIRONMENT IN WHICH COMMUNITIES AND WORKERS CAN ADVOCATE FOR THEIR RIGHTS AND INTERESTS, INCLUDING THROUGH FREE AND FAIR NEGOTIATIONS. Read the company's page before your first meeting with it. Its own published policies and benchmark scores are the standard you can hold it to at the table.

trackers.name: Fundación Avina - a Latin American foundation with staff in up to 19 countries, six programmes including WATER and BIOMES, a record of SEED GRANTS to organisations that became leading deforestation monitors, and convening offered alongside money
trackers.desc: A FOUNDATION WITH STAFF LIVING IN NINETEEN LATIN AMERICAN COUNTRIES THAT HAS MOVED MORE THAN A BILLION DOLLARS THROUGH LOCAL ALLIES. It is A REGIONAL NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION WITH A MANDATE TO SUPPORT SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN THE LATIN AMERICAN REGION, whose activities cover ACCESS TO WATER AND ENERGY, RESOURCE MANAGEMENT and which works THROUGH A BROAD NETWORK OF GRASS-ROOTS AND COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS, NATIONAL AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS, THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY AND THE PRIVATE SECTOR; one account records 75 FULL-TIME STAFF MEMBERS BASED IN 19 COUNTRIES IN LATIN AMERICA and another 95 STAFF MEMBERS ACROSS 15 COUNTRIES, with OVER $500 MILLION ACROSS 13,000 INITIATIVES mobilised on one count and OVER USD 1.21 BILLION since 1994 on another. Staff who live in the country rather than visit it, and grant-making measured in thousands of small initiatives. Ask who the country contact is before writing to any regional address. THE PROGRAMME LIST THAT TELLS YOU WHERE A LAND CASE FITS: it works through SIX KEY PROGRAMS — CLIMATE, CIRCULAR ECONOMY, LABOR INNOVATION, BIOMES, DEMOCRACY, AND WATER, and elsewhere describes KEY AREAS INCLUDING CLIMATE ACTION, DEMOCRATIC STRENGTHENING, INCLUSIVE CIRCULAR ECONOMIES, BIOMES CONSERVATION, WATER MANAGEMENT, AND LABOR INNOVATION, with SUPPORT FOR LOCAL INITIATIVES. Biomes and water are separate programmes with their own staff. A watershed case goes to the water programme and a forest or savannah case to biomes — sending it to the wrong one is how a request gets lost. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DID FOR MONITORING ORGANISATIONS: a foundation officer records that in one phase it USED GRANTMAKING... TO MOBILIZE FUNDS WITH PARTNERS TO ORGANIZATIONS IN PAN-AMAZON, NOT ONLY IN THE BRAZILIAN AMAZON, WHICH IS OFTEN THE FOCUS, BUT THE PAN-AMAZON AND THE CHACO REGION, TO STRENGTHEN THEIR ABILITIES TO MONITOR DEFORESTATION, and that MANY OF THE ORGANIZATIONS THAT NOWADAYS ARE LEADING ORGANIZATIONS IN THIS AREA HAVE BEEN SUPPORTED AS A SEED GRANT. Seed grants to organisations that later became the leading monitors. If your group is at the beginning, that is the stage this foundation has repeatedly funded — and the Chaco, usually ignored beside the Amazon, is named. HOW IT DESCRIBES ITS OWN ROLE, WHICH SHAPES WHAT TO ASK FOR: it works AS A BROKER, CO-INVESTOR AND FACILITATOR, its PRIMARY CONTRIBUTION TO ITS ALLIES IS THE PROMOTION OF COLLABORATIVE ACTION THROUGH SERVICES AND FINANCIAL SUPPORT, and it BRINGS ITS ABILITIES AND RESOURCES TO THE TABLE AS A PEER INSTITUTION, providing ITS ABILITY, SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE, CONTACTS, RESOURCES, STRATEGIES, AND TOOLS TO WORK TOWARDS A COMMON CAUSE. Contacts and convening are offered alongside money. Where a case needs a mayor, a ministry and a company in one room, that is the service to ask for rather than a grant. THE UNITED STATES ENTITY, AND WHAT IT FUNDS: a separate United States non-profit MOBILIZES RESOURCES AND PARTNERSHIPS FROM THE UNITED STATES TO SUPPORT AND EXPAND THE IMPACT OF THIS MISSION and SUPPORTS INITIATIVES ALIGNED WITH THE FOUNDATION'S PRIORITIES ACROSS THREE INTERCONNECTED PILLARS... DEMOCRATIC INNOVATION, CLIMATE ACTION, AND A JUST AND REGENERATIVE ECONOMY, having COME TO EMBRACE FEMINIST PRINCIPLES THAT CENTER THE IMPORTANCE OF BUILDING COLLECTIVE POWER. Two legal entities, two funding routes. Which one can pay you depends on where your organisation is registered, so ask that first. THE HONEST NOTE ON ORIGIN AND COMPANY: it was FOUNDED IN 1994 BY a Swiss industrialist, is headquartered in one Central American capital with a northern office, works BY ENCOURAGING ALLIANCES BETWEEN SOCIAL AND BUSINESS LEADERS, and its recent activities include projects with a named water technology company in one country's semi-arid region. Its model is explicitly to put business leaders at the table with social ones. Decide whether that suits your fight before joining a programme, and read who co-funds it.

trackers.name: Fundação Grupo Boticário - a Brazilian conservation funder whose thematic lines include the CREATION AND ENLARGEMENT of protected areas and private reserves, with no minimum grant value, peer review by 123 volunteer specialists, and two reserves of its own
trackers.desc: ONE OF ITS FOUR FUNDING LINES PAYS FOR THE CREATION OR ENLARGEMENT OF PROTECTED AREAS, INCLUDING PRIVATE RESERVES. Its conservation support programme lists as a thematic line UNITS OF CONSERVATION OF INTEGRAL PROTECTION (CONTINENTAL AND MARINE) AND PRIVATE NATURAL HERITAGE RESERVES: CREATION, ENLARGEMENT AND EXECUTION OF PRIORITY ACTIVITIES OF THEIR MANAGEMENT PLANS, seeking PROPOSALS THAT CONTEMPLATE THE CREATION OR THE ENLARGEMENT OF CONSERVATION UNITS IN CONTINENTAL OR MARINE AREAS, with priority to PROJECTS THAT BECOME A REFERENCE IN MANAGEMENT, PUBLIC USE, RESEARCH AND THAT BRING BENEFITS FOR THE COMMUNITIES OF THE SURROUNDINGS. The other lines cover threatened species, marine environments and INNOVATIONS AND NEW TECHNOLOGIES FOR THE CONSERVATION OF NATURE. Benefit to surrounding communities is a stated priority, not a box to tick. A proposal to enlarge a protected area that names what the neighbouring villages gain scores better than one that does not. WHO MAY APPLY, WHICH IS THE FIRST FILTER: TO COMPETE FOR THE SUPPORT IT IS NECESSARY THAT THE INITIATIVE BE CARRIED OUT BY PRIVATE NON-PROFIT INSTITUTIONS, SUCH AS FOUNDATIONS LINKED TO UNIVERSITIES AND NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS; ONLY NON-PROFIT INSTITUTIONS MAY PARTICIPATE. A community group needs a registered non-profit or a university foundation to carry the application. Line that partner up before the call opens, because the deadlines are fixed. WHAT IT PAYS AND WHEN: recorded rounds ran UNTIL 31 MARCH and UNTIL 31 AUGUST in some years and were concentrated into a single first-semester call in another; projects may run BETWEEN 12 AND 24 MONTHS; THERE ARE NO MINIMUM OR MAXIMUM VALUES DEFINED IN THE CALL, with one period's total varying between roughly six hundred and fifty and seven hundred and fifty thousand reais, another round distributing R$750 THOUSAND, DIVIDED BY, ON AVERAGE, 20 SELECTED INITIATIVES, and later rounds totalling UP TO R$ 2 MILLION. No minimum means a small, precise request is admissible. Twenty grants from one round is a realistic chance, not a lottery. HOW PROPOSALS ARE JUDGED: selection IS MADE BY OPINIONS ISSUED BY 123 SPECIALISTS FROM ALL OVER THE COUNTRY, WHO ACT AS VOLUNTARY CONSULTANTS, with FINAL APPROVAL... MADE BY THE MEMBERS OF THE foundation's BOARD OF TRUSTEES, WHICH INCLUDES RENOWNED PROFESSIONALS FROM THE AREAS OF CONSERVATION OF NATURE, ENVIRONMENTAL LAW, COMMUNICATION AND MANAGEMENT. Peer review by working scientists, then a board that includes environmental lawyers. Write the proposal so a specialist in your ecosystem can verify every claim. ITS OWN LAND, AND ITS RECORD: the foundation PROTECTS 11 THOUSAND HECTARES OF ATLANTIC FOREST AND CERRADO, THROUGH THE CREATION AND MAINTENANCE OF TWO NATURAL RESERVES, and has supported MORE THAN 1,500 INITIATIVES FINANCIALLY, an earlier count recording 1,377 INITIATIVES CHOSEN OVER 58 CALLS in twenty-three years and a summary recording support to 456 conservation units and 238 threatened species. It owns and runs reserves itself, so it understands what a management plan costs. Ask for the running costs as well as the creation costs. THE HONEST CURRENCY NOTE: the call details recorded here come from several past editions between the mid 2010s and 2019, and the format has changed between one and two rounds a year. Check the current edition's rules before writing. The thematic lines have been stable for years, but the deadlines and totals have not.

trackers.name: FEMA — Fundo Especial de Meio Ambiente (Município de São Paulo)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY, CITY LEVEL: São Paulo's municipal environment fund, created by Lei nº 13.155 of 29/06/2001, redisciplined by Lei nº 14.887 of 15/01/2009 and regulated by Decretos 52.153 and 52.388 of 2011. READ THE PURPOSE CLAUSE: it funds projects for the sustainable use of natural resources, maintenance and recovery of environmental quality, research, and activities of control, inspection and defesa do meio ambiente — defence of the environment. A city fund that will pay for environmental defence work is unusual; most cover planting and education only. WHO CAN APPLY: Brazilian non-profit OSCIPs and NGOs, legally constituted, and public bodies — one edital required a minimum of 3 years' existence. You apply through editais de chamamento and must register in CENTS; the Comissão Técnica de Avaliação issues an opinion, and CONFEMA decides. Scale: Edital 11 put R$ 1.710 million behind 10 proposals. READ THIS FIRST: priorities are set annually by CADES, the municipal environment council, so write to this year's directives. SVMA, CADES and FEMA together form the local organ of SISNAMA inside the municipality, which is why a São Paulo fight is fought here and not only federally. Contact svmafema@prefeitura.sp.gov.br, Rua do Paraíso 387, 1º andar, tel (11) 5187-0301; awards are published in the Diário Oficial da Cidade.

trackers.name: Instituto Guaicuy — Assessoria Técnica Independente
trackers.desc: The lever to know in Minas Gerais: since early 2021 an Assessoria Técnica Independente is a RIGHT of dam-affected people under the state Política Estadual de Pessoas Atingidas por Barragens, and the adviser is chosen democratically by the affected communities themselves, not by the company. Guaicuy serves in that role for communities hit by the 2019 Vale dam collapse across Pompéu, Curvelo, Felixlândia, Três Marias, São Gonçalo do Abaeté, Martinho Campos, Morada Nova de Minas, Biquinhas, Paineiras and Abaeté, and for the Doutor dam decommissioning at Antônio Pereira, Ouro Preto. WHO IT SUITS: communities facing a mining company across a table with far better technical and legal resources — the ATI exists precisely to close that asymmetry, covering damage assessment, compensation matrices and monitoring of the reparation agreement.

trackers.name: NACAB — Núcleo de Assessoria às Comunidades Atingidas por Barragens
trackers.desc: A second Independent Technical Assistance body operating in Minas Gerais, working with communities affected by the Brumadinho collapse and, under licensing Condicionante 39, with thirteen communities across Alvorada de Minas, Dom Joaquim and Conceição do Mato Dentro. That condicionante is the point worth knowing: a mining licence can itself require the company to fund an independent adviser that the affected communities choose. WHO IT SUITS: dam- and mine-affected communities entering a reparation process — NACAB does the loss-and-damage survey, the valuation of what should be indemnified, and monitors delivery of what was agreed. Choose between the accredited ATIs rather than approaching one at random; the selection is run by the public prosecutors and defensoría.

trackers.name: FMDA — Fundo Municipal de Defesa Ambiental (Belo Horizonte)
trackers.desc: A CITY FUND AN INDIVIDUAL CAN APPLY TO. Created by Lei 4.253/85, the FMDA funds projects improving environmental quality in the municipality, proposed by organised civil society and/or by duly qualified individuals. Eligible: non-profit legal persons and natural persons domiciled in Belo Horizonte, NGOs, and direct and indirect administration bodies — a resident can apply in their own name, which is rarer than anything in the wealthy-country funds where the barrier is membership numbers or a half-million-euro project floor. Recorded round: R$ 240,000 through an edital published in the Diário Oficial do Município, with proposals delivered in person to the Secretaria Municipal de Meio Ambiente by the stated hour on the closing day. It funds recovery, maintenance or improvement of environmental quality. Questions to smma@pbh.gov.br.

trackers.name: Fundo de Conservação Ambiental (FCA) — Município do Rio de Janeiro
trackers.desc: CITY MONEY FOR CONSERVATION: the FCA is provided for in the sole paragraph of Art. 129 of Rio's Lei Orgânica, created by Lei Municipal nº 2.138 of 11 May 1994 and now regulated by Decreto nº 41.248 of 19 February 2016, which replaced the original 1994 decree. Attached to the city environment secretariat (SMAC), it finances environmental recovery and restoration, prevention of environmental damage, and environmental education. READ THIS BEFORE APPLYING — IT IS NOT AN OPEN GRANT: under Art. 4 of the regulating decree the resources go to projects developed by SMAC or agreed with it (conveniados), to payment for services executing specific projects, to management and planning instruments, and to running conservation units. A community group therefore needs a convênio with the secretariat rather than simply submitting a proposal — a materially different route from São Paulo's FEMA, which runs open editais. Approach SMAC about a convênio first.

trackers.name: SPVS (Paraná) — RPPNs e reservas próprias
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Curitiba conservation organisation founded in 1984, an OSCIP since 2001, which owns and manages 19,000 hectares of its own reserves on the northern Paraná coast — Águas and Guaricica in Antonina, Papagaio-de-Cara-Roxa in Guaraqueçaba — and works with private owners to turn land into RPPNs, the only private protected-area category in the national SNUC system. USE IT: to get Atlantic Forest land in Paraná protected as an RPPN or acquired outright. The argument that lands with owners and mayors: Paraná's ICMS Ecológico redistributes a share of state tax to municipalities holding conservation units, so an RPPN pays the municipality real money every year — Antonina and Guaraqueçaba have drawn millions of reais on the back of SPVS reserves alone.

trackers.name: RPPNM Curitiba — Secretaria Municipal do Meio Ambiente
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: Curitiba's municipal environment secretariat runs the Reserva Particular do Patrimônio Natural Municipal, the city-level private reserve Brazil's first municipality created for URBAN green land. You apply to the SMMA through the PROCEC electronic portal with a management and conservation plan; if approved the reserve is created by municipal decree, in perpetuity and irrevocably, recorded against your title at the property register. Live and current — reserves were still being created by decree in 2026. USE IT: the incentives are the point, and they are financial. Full exemption from IPTU urban property tax on the wooded land, and transfer of 100% of the building rights you give up to unrestricted parts of the city — which you may sell on the construction market. Land stays yours; the reserve may be used for visitation, ecotourism, education and research. For an owner of a wooded urban lot under development pressure, this converts the threat into an asset.

trackers.name: Conselho Municipal do Meio Ambiente — the seat that controls the fund
trackers.desc: GET ONTO THE COUNCIL — IT DECIDES WHAT THE CITY FUND PAYS FOR. Under Curitiba's Lei nº 15.852 of 01/07/2021, the Conselho Municipal do Meio Ambiente is consultative, normative and deliberative: it analyses and approves the plan for applying the resources of the Fundo Municipal do Meio Ambiente and deliberates on its programmes, projects and money. It also decides at second administrative instance, on appeal, on fines and on gaps in environmental legislation — an appeal route inside the city, before any court. AND YOU CAN SIT ON IT: the council and its Technical Chambers are composed of representatives of the public authority, organised civil society and academia in equal numbers (de forma paritária). THE PATTERN IS NATIONAL: the model municipal environment fund statute has the fund administered by the environment secretariat in articulation with the municipal environment council, which defines the criteria and priorities for applying the money. In a Brazilian city, the council seat is worth more than any single grant application.

trackers.name: Idesam — Instituto de Conservação e Desenvolvimento Sustentável da Amazônia
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Manaus-based institute working across the interior of Amazonas state, whose concrete offer to a community is technical assistance to get a Plano de Manejo Florestal written, certified and selling. Through the Cidades Florestais project, backed by the Fundo Amazônia and BNDES, it works with residents, settlers and extractivists in fourteen Amazonas municipalities; the Uatumã reserve association it supported won FSC certification and saw its oil price rise from R$1 to R$8 a kilo, with average income for 370 extractivists reaching close to R$3,000. USE IT: where community forest management is the realistic alternative to illegal logging on your territory, and you need the plan, the equipment and the buyer, not a lawyer.
