Do not send the details from a shared community email account. The application itself can expose the person it is meant to protect.

trackers.name: Inter-American Foundation grants - CURRENTLY PAUSED - direct grants of $25,000-$400,000 to grassroots organisations with no sector calls, no deadline, five application languages, and LAND AND LABOUR accepted as counterpart
trackers.desc: THIS FUNDER IS CURRENTLY PAUSED — CHECK BEFORE SPENDING TIME ON IT. Its own application page states: WE ARE CURRENTLY PAUSING GRANT FUNDING IN ALIGNMENT WITH EXECUTIVE ORDER REEVALUATING AND REALIGNING UNITED STATES FOREIGN AID. CHECK THIS PAGE FOR FURTHER UPDATES. It is AN INDEPENDENT AGENCY of that government. Everything below describes how it worked when open, and is recorded because the terms are unusual enough to be worth watching for. Read the page before writing anything. A funder under a foreign aid review can reopen with different rules, and the counterpart and eligibility terms are the first things such reviews change. WHY IT MATTERED: IT FUNDED GRASSROOTS GROUPS DIRECTLY, WITH NO INTERMEDIARY: it ONLY SUPPORT[S] COMMUNITY-LED PROJECTS SUBMITTED BY LOCAL AND GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS THAT ARE BASED IN INDEPENDENT COUNTRIES OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, requiring proof that YOUR ORGANIZATION HAS A HISTORY OF WORKING TOGETHER AS A GROUP AND IS CAPABLE OF EFFECTIVELY USING GRANTS FUNDS; it DOES NOT IDENTIFY PROBLEMS OR SUGGEST PROJECTS; INSTEAD IT RESPONDS TO INITIATIVES PRESENTED, and PROJECTS ARE SELECTED FOR FUNDING ON THEIR MERITS RATHER THAN BY SECTOR. Grants ran FROM US$25,000 TO $400,000 OVER ONE TO FOUR YEARS, with proposals accepted 365 DAYS A YEAR in SPANISH, PORTUGUESE, ENGLISH, FRENCH, OR HAITIAN CREOLE. No sector calls, no themes, no deadline. A community proposing its own solution in its own language is the entire model, and it is worth having a proposal ready if the pause lifts. THE COUNTERPART RULE, WHICH IS THE PART TO UNDERSTAND: all funded organisations must COMMIT RESOURCES TO ADVANCE THEIR DEVELOPMENT INITIATIVES, called counterpart; COUNTERPART FUNDING MUST BE A COMPONENT OF THE BUDGET... BUT NO MINIMUM AMOUNT IS REQUIRED. HIGHER COUNTERPART FUNDING MAKES A PROPOSAL MORE ATTRACTIVE, and it MAY BE IN CASH DONATIONS OR IN KIND, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, LAND, SUPPLIES, INFRASTRUCTURE, LABOR, AND OFFICE, STORAGE AND MEETING SPACE. Salaries are A LEGITIMATE EXPENSE. Land and volunteer labour count as counterpart. A community that owns the site and works it has already met the requirement without spending anything. WHAT IT LOOKED FOR IN A PROPOSAL: CREATIVE USE OF THE COMMUNITY'S RESOURCES; A DIVERSE ARRAY OF COMMUNITY VOICES IN PROJECT DEVELOPMENT AND EXECUTION; SUBSTANTIAL BENEFICIARY ENGAGEMENT in identifying the problem, choosing the approach, designing the project and managing it; PARTNERSHIPS WITH LOCAL GOVERNMENT, THE BUSINESS COMMUNITY AND OTHER CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS; feasibility, sustainability, measurable results and EVIDENCE OF BENEFICIARIES' ENHANCED CAPACITY FOR SELF-GOVERNANCE; its recorded interests included COMMUNITY CONSERVATION; AND LOCAL MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES (FORESTS, FISHERIES, ETC.). Partnership with the local government is a scoring criterion. That is the argument for bringing your municipality into the proposal rather than fighting it. THE EXCLUSIONS AND THE FIELD OFFICE RULE: support was limited to independent countries of the region, with recorded exclusions of two countries and a period when FUNDING IN THE CARIBBEAN was RESTRICTED TO three named states; public universities could not apply directly BUT MAY PARTNER WITH AN ORGANIZATION THAT IS ELIGIBLE; and an organisation headquartered abroad could apply only if its field office CAN DEMONSTRATE LOCAL LEADERSHIP. Local leadership had to be demonstrated, not asserted. Where an outside NGO offers to apply on your behalf, insist that your own organisation is the applicant.

trackers.name: RedLAC - the network of 32 national and regional ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS in 20 countries, permanent conservation trust institutions financing protected areas and local communities, with a published member list by country and zone
trackers.desc: THIRTY-TWO NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS IN TWENTY COUNTRIES, AND THE NETWORK PUBLISHES WHICH ONE COVERS YOURS. It GROUPS 32 ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS FROM 20 COUNTRIES OF THE REGION, UNITING EFFORTS TO PROTECT THE RICH BIODIVERSITY OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, with its member list filterable by zone — Caribbean, Mesoamerica and South America — alongside regional funds; more than twenty-five years old, it counts MORE THAN 100 ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS WORLDWIDE. Find the fund for your country on that member page. These are permanent national institutions with endowments, not project offices that close when a grant ends. WHAT THESE FUNDS DO, IN THE NETWORK'S WORDS: they HAVE DEMONSTRATED TO BE A KEY MECHANISM IN THE SUSTAINABLE FINANCING OF BIODIVERSITY AND IN THE STRENGTHENING OF PROTECTED AREAS AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, with a role in THE PROTECTION OF NATURAL AREAS AND THE SUPPORT TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES, described as MULTIDIMENSIONAL FUNDS, WITH APPROACHES THAT INTEGRATE PROTECTION OF BIODIVERSITY, CLIMATIC RESILIENCE AND COMMUNITY EMPOWERMENT. Support to local communities is named alongside protected areas. A community managing land next to a park is inside the mandate, not adjacent to it. SOME OF THE MEMBERS BY NAME AND KIND: recorded members include a Caribbean biodiversity fund, a national forever-protection association in one Central American country, an action fund and a Pacific foundation in one Andean country, a nature fund in one southern country, an island life fund and a regional marine fund — the last two showing that funds exist for a single archipelago and for a shared sea as well as for whole countries. There are funds scoped to one archipelago and to one reef system. If your site sits in either, that narrower fund is a better fit than the national one. WHAT THE NETWORK ITSELF OFFERS ITS MEMBERS: joining gives funds THE OPPORTUNITY TO CONNECT AND COLLABORATE WITH OTHER MEMBERS OF THE NETWORK THROUGHOUT THE REGION, to SHARE KNOWLEDGE, RESOURCES AND EXPERIENCES TO IMPROVE THEIR CAPACITIES, and ACCESS TO A WIDE VARIETY OF RESOURCES AND TOOLS, with TRAINING AND ADVICE ON DIVERSE THEMES, FROM PROJECT MANAGEMENT TO COMMUNICATION AND ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION. Where your country has no environmental fund, this network is where one would be built, and it trains new members. That is a long project, but it is the route. WHY THEY MATTER FOR PERMANENT PROTECTION: these funds are conservation trust funds — institutions holding capital whose returns finance protected areas and community work year after year, and the network works alongside a global environment facility, an African funds consortium and a large conservation finance initiative on that model. An endowment pays for wardens and monitoring long after a campaign ends. Where a protected area has just been declared, the next question is which of these funds can endow its running costs.

trackers.name: The ICCA Consortium and the international register of territories of life - a community-reviewed register open to any well-defined community with its own governance, plus national catalytic organisations, documentation workshops and life plan support
trackers.desc: A COMMUNITY CAN PUT ITS OWN TERRITORY ON AN INTERNATIONAL REGISTER, REVIEWED BY OTHER COMMUNITIES RATHER THAN BY OFFICIALS. The international register IS A TOOL DEVELOPED TO SERVE AS SUPPORT AND RECOGNITION TO THOSE COMMUNITIES WITH OUTSTANDING VALUES IN GOVERNANCE AND CONSERVATION OF NATURE, run by a United Nations environment body with the consortium and a commons organisation; its PEER REVIEW PROTOCOL is A CONSENSUS DOCUMENT IN WHICH THE DIFFERENT STEPS THAT EACH COMMUNITY MUST TAKE IN ORDER TO FORM PART OF THE REGISTER ARE DESCRIBED, including SUBMITTING TO A PROCESS OF REVIEW OF THE CANDIDATURE BY ANONYMOUS MEMBERS (REVIEWERS) OF OTHER SIMILAR COMMUNITIES THAT ALREADY FORM PART OF THE REGISTER. Other communities judge the application, and the protocol is published so you can read the test before applying. Registration is a public record of who governs the land, made without asking the state's permission. WHAT QUALIFIES AS ONE OF THESE TERRITORIES: they exist IN ANY TYPE OF CULTURE AND ECOSYSTEM WHERE THERE IS A COMMUNITY LINKED TO A TERRITORY, WITH ITS OWN SYSTEM OF GOVERNANCE, AND THAT GIVES POSITIVE RESULTS IN TERMS OF CONSERVATION OF NATURE AND LIVELIHOODS FOR THE COMMUNITY; the first defining characteristic is that THE AREA OR TERRITORY MUST HAVE A WELL DEFINED COMMUNITY, WITH A CLEAR LINK TO A TERRITORY ALSO WELL DEFINED. A well defined community and a well defined territory. Neither a formal title nor a state designation is in that test. WHO THE CONSORTIUM IS AND WHAT ITS MEMBERS DO: it is AN INTERNATIONAL NON-PROFIT ASSOCIATION DEDICATED TO SUPPORTING INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES THAT GOVERN AND CONSERVE THEIR LANDS, WATERS AND TERRITORIES, its members from more than eighty countries acting on themes including THE DOCUMENTATION, SUSTAINING AND DEFENCE OF THE TERRITORIES OF LIFE, and comprising ALMOST 180 MEMBERS (ORGANISATIONS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND COMMUNITY ORGANISATIONS, TOGETHER WITH THE CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS THAT SUPPORT THEM) AND MORE THAN 420 HONORARY MEMBERS. Community organisations are members in their own right, alongside the NGOs that support them. Ask the national focal point how your organisation joins. WHAT THE REGIONAL NETWORK ACTUALLY DELIVERS: the Latin American network runs workshops WITH THE AIM OF SHARING KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERIENCES COMING FROM THE TERRITORIES, including a practical workshop on the register itself, a case study workshop drawing on one country's experience, and one on a GUIDE OF SELF-STRENGTHENING: A GUIDE FROM COMMUNITIES FOR COMMUNITIES; communities are recorded pursuing PROCESSES OF DOCUMENTATION, THE CONSTRUCTION OF LIFE PLANS, THE register AND THE STRENGTHENING OF THEIR OWN GOVERNANCE. A life plan is the document that states what a community will and will not permit on its land. Building one is the work these workshops exist to support. WHAT IT HAS SUPPORTED ON THE GROUND: in one country an observatory and a named indigenous community organised A WORKSHOP OF EXCHANGE OF KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERIENCES, ATTENDED BY TWENTY-FIVE REPRESENTATIVES OF TEN INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, TO EXCHANGE ABOUT LEGAL AND NON-LEGAL STRATEGIES OF TERRITORIAL DEFENCE AND PROTECTION; in another, five indigenous peoples, an Afro-descendant community and a coastal community met with a foundation and the small grants programme TO DEBATE AND DECIDE ON THE WORLD REGISTER; national members have planned A STUDY OF THE EXISTING LEGAL FRAMEWORK ON CONSERVATION AND RIGHTS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, ACTIONS FOR COMMUNITY STRENGTHENING AND A NATIONAL ADVOCACY STRATEGY; a global support initiative works through NATIONAL CATALYTIC ORGANISATIONS in more than twenty-six priority countries. Ask which organisation is the national catalytic body for your country. It is the one already funded to accompany communities through documentation and registration.

trackers.name: Mapeo and its successor - a free, offline, open-source mapping and evidence toolset built with Amazonian indigenous partners, where ALL DATA IS OWNED BY THE COMMUNITY, exporting shapefiles and reports for lawsuits and land claims
trackers.desc: A FREE OFFLINE APP THAT TURNS A PHONE INTO AN EVIDENCE RECORDER, AND THE COMMUNITY KEEPS THE DATA. It is A FREE DIGITAL TOOLSET FOR DOCUMENTING, MONITORING, AND MAPPING MANY TYPES OF DATA, OFFLINE-FIRST OPEN-SOURCE TECHNOLOGY needing NO INTERNET OR SPECIAL HARDWARE... TO COLLECT, VIEW, OR SHARE DATA; WITH THE PUSH OF A BUTTON, CONTRIBUTORS CAN GATHER MAP DATA BY LINKING GPS POINTS, PHOTOS, AND NOTES, and ALL DATA IS COMPLETELY OWNED BY THE COMMUNITIES THEMSELVES, exchanged between phones by a peer-to-peer sync that works OVER A LOCAL WIFI NETWORK WITHOUT NEEDING A CONNECTION. No signal, no server, no subscription, and nobody else holds the file. For a community watching a road survey or a clearing crew, that is the difference between a rumour and an exhibit. WHAT IT WAS BUILT TO BE USED FOR: it was CO-DESIGNED AND DEVELOPED WITH INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES WHO FACE THREATS TO THEIR LAND SUCH AS ILLEGAL GOLD MINING, OIL CONTAMINATION AND POACHING, and built TO SUPPORT THEM TO DOCUMENT THESE ACTIVITIES IN ORDER TO TAKE COMMUNITY ACTION AGAINST THEM, TO REPORT THEM TO AUTHORITIES, FILE LAWSUITS, LAUNCH MEDIA CAMPAIGNS, OR CREATE MAPS FOR LAND CLAIMS; it allows USERS TO COLLECT EVIDENCE IN THE FIELD, SUCH AS PHOTOGRAPHS AND GPS POINTS, AND ORGANIZE THIS DATA FOR ACTIONS SUCH AS WHISTLEBLOWING AND CLAIMING LAND RIGHTS. Filing a lawsuit and making a map for a land claim are the stated purposes. Set up the categories to match what a court or a ministry will ask for, before the incursion happens. THE CASE THAT SHOWS WHAT IT IS WORTH: in one country OVER TWENTY indigenous COMMUNITIES DEFENDED THEIR TERRITORY... AGAINST THE IMPOSITION OF DEVASTATING OIL EXPLORATION PROPOSED BY THE GOVERNMENT, having USED the tool FOR OVER FOUR YEARS TO RECORD TERRITORIAL DATA ...AND MAPS, WHICH THEY USED AS EVIDENCE AGAINST THE government; the account records: THEY WON! Four years of routine recording before the case existed. The evidence that wins these cases is gathered long before anyone knows there will be a case. WHAT COMES OUT OF IT, AND IN WHICH LANGUAGES: export options include PDF OR PRINT REPORT, GEOJSON, CSV OR SHAPEFILE from the desktop version and direct sharing from the phone; the interface IS AVAILABLE IN LOCAL LANGUAGES, AND ALSO HAS AN IN-BUILT TRANSLATION FEATURE, supporting THE UNDERSERVED DIALECTS OF INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES; one community leader records that IT IS SO EASY TO USE THAT EVEN OUR ELDERS — WHO DO NOT SPEAK SPANISH — USE IT. A newer version adds audio, tracks and routes. A shapefile is what a planning office and a court will accept. Elders who do not speak the national language can gather it themselves, which also answers the objection that the data was collected by outsiders. THE SUPPORT AROUND THE TOOL: the developers publish TRAINING AND TECHNICAL RESOURCES, a COMPLETE REFERENCE GUIDE... ON PLANNING AND IMPLEMENTING PROJECTS and customisation of the tools, and a defenders toolkit site; a dedicated version was built with a United Nations monitoring centre and a forest peoples organisation so that custodian communities can MAP, MONITOR AND SUPPORT THEIR TERRITORIES OF LIFE ON THEIR TERMS and may, SHOULD THEY WISH TO, CONTRIBUTE TO GLOBAL CONSERVATION DATABASES. Contributing to the global database is optional and separate. Decide as a community what stays local before the first survey, because that choice is hard to reverse once data is shared.

trackers.name: Global Forest Watch - free near-real-time deforestation alerts by email for any drawn area, an offline field app that walks patrols to the clearing, and a small grants fund whose examples include GETTING CONCESSIONS REVOKED and compiling evidence for formal complaints
trackers.desc: YOU CAN SUBSCRIBE TO EMAIL ALERTS FOR A SINGLE PLOT OF FOREST AND BE TOLD WITHIN DAYS WHEN TREES ARE CUT. The platform is FREE AND SIMPLE TO USE, ENABLING ANYONE TO CREATE CUSTOM MAPS, ANALYZE FOREST TRENDS, SUBSCRIBE TO ALERTS, OR DOWNLOAD DATA FOR THEIR LOCAL AREA OR THE ENTIRE WORLD, providing NEAR-REAL-TIME ALERTS SHOWING SUSPECTED LOCATIONS OF RECENT TREE COVER LOSS; it moved BEYOND ANNUAL DATA ON FORESTS to MONTHLY AND WEEKLY DEFORESTATION ALERTS, with EMAIL SUBSCRIPTIONS bringing them DIRECTLY INTO THE HANDS OF USERS. Users CAN SIGN UP FOR ALERTS AND DOWNLOAD DATASETS WITHOUT ANY SUBSCRIPTION OR LICENSING FEE. Draw the boundary of the land you are defending and subscribe. From then on the clearing tells you rather than the other way round, and the date stamp is independent of anything the developer says. THE FIELD APP THAT WORKS WITHOUT SIGNAL: a companion mobile application ALLOWS RANGERS TO ACCESS the data and alerts OFFLINE, WHICH IS CRITICAL IN AREAS WITH LIMITED TO NO CELL SIGNAL; USING CACHED DATA, THE APP DIRECTS USERS TO NEARBY FOREST CLEARING AND ENABLES THEM TO CAPTURE PHOTOS AND FILL OUT FORMS ABOUT DEFORESTATION, WHICH ARE UPLOADED NEXT TIME THEIR DEVICE CONNECTS, so that patrols KNOW EXACTLY WHERE TO LOOK... AND STOP THE ILLEGAL ACTIVITY BEFORE IT GETS OUT OF CONTROL; it is FREE, OPEN SOURCE, AND AVAILABLE IN ENGLISH, SPANISH, PORTUGUESE, FRENCH, AND BAHASA INDONESIAN. The alert gives the coordinates and the app walks you to them. A ground photograph taken at a satellite-flagged point, on a known date, is the evidence a prosecutor can use. THE GRANT ATTACHED TO IT, AND WHAT IT HAS PAID FOR: a small grants fund SEEKS TO BUILD THE CAPACITY OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS TO EFFECTIVELY USE the tools TO REDUCE ILLEGAL OR UNPLANNED DEFORESTATION; funded project types include USING DATA AND IMAGERY... ALONGSIDE COMMUNITY TERRITORIAL MAPS TO ADVOCATE FOR LAND TITLES AND OTHER STRENGTHENED LAND RIGHTS; CROWDSOURCING, COMPILING AND PUBLISHING DATA ON CONCESSIONS THAT OVERLAP WITH ANCESTRAL COMMUNITY LANDS, AND SUPPORT COMMUNITIES IN APPLYING PUBLIC PRESSURE TO GET THESE CONCESSIONS REVOKED; DEVELOPING THE CAPACITY OF FOREST MONITORING BRIGADES TO CONDUCT FIELD VERIFICATIONS OF NEAR-REAL TIME ALERTS; and SUPPORTING INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES IN DEVELOPING RESPONSE PROTOCOLS, FORMULATING LEGAL STRATEGIES AND COMPILING EVIDENCE OF ILLEGAL DEFORESTATION INCLUDING SATELLITE IMAGERY, DATA AND ANALYSES, AND SUBMITTING IT TO LAW ENFORCEMENT THROUGH FORMAL COMPLAINTS OR OTHER LEGAL PROCESSES. Getting concessions revoked and compiling evidence for formal complaints are funded project types, written into the fund's own examples. That is the grant to cite when describing what you intend to do. THE DEADLINE DISCIPLINE: the fund runs an annual call, and the platform states of a recent round: THE CALL FOR APPLICATIONS HAS CLOSED AS OF THE DEADLINE... WE CANNOT GRANT ANY EXTENSIONS, advising applicants to PREPARE FOR THE NEXT CALL FOR APPLICATIONS BY REVIEWING the current materials, while noting that SOME ITEMS IN THE GUIDELINES FOR APPLICANTS MAY CHANGE YEAR TO YEAR. One deadline a year, strictly enforced. Download this year's guidelines now and write the proposal before the next call opens. WHO ELSE IS ALREADY USING IT: the platform serves GOVERNMENTS, THE PRIVATE SECTOR, NGOs, JOURNALISTS, UNIVERSITIES, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC, and is convened as a partnership of OVER 200 ORGANIZATIONS; a fellowship accompanies the grants. Your municipality and your national forest agency can subscribe to the same alerts you do. Sending them the alert with a covering letter turns your observation into their file.

trackers.name: Public Lab and the open science hardware community - free open-source, low-cost instruments and toolkits communities build themselves for water, air, soil and land use, plus BALLOON AND KITE AERIAL MAPPING with stitching software and an open question forum
trackers.desc: THE INSTRUMENTS ARE OPEN SOURCE AND CHEAP ENOUGH THAT A COMMUNITY CAN BUILD ITS OWN, INCLUDING AERIAL PHOTOGRAPHY FROM A KITE. The network is DEVOTED TO EMPOWERING COMMUNITIES AND CITIZEN SCIENTISTS TO MONITOR THEIR OWN ENVIRONMENTS THROUGH THE USE OF INEXPENSIVE DIY TECHNIQUES, hosting AN IMPRESSIVE CATALOG OF OPEN SOURCE TOOLKITS... RANGING FROM WATER QUALITY SENSORS TO INDOOR AIR QUALITY AND KITE MAPPING KITS; its tools and data are CREATED BY THE community, OPEN SOURCE, AND TYPICALLY INEXPENSIVE TO USE. Its earliest technique was LOW-ALTITUDE AERIAL MAPPING WITH BALLOONS AND KITES with software to stitch the photographs into a map. A kite, a camera and free stitching software produce a dated aerial photograph of a site at a resolution no public satellite gives you. That is how you show what a hillside looked like before the machines arrived. WHY IT EXISTS, AND WHAT THAT PRECEDENT MEANS: it was founded in 2010 FOLLOWING THE BP OIL DISASTER IN THE GULF OF MEXICO... TO ADDRESS AN ENORMOUS GAP IN COMMUNITY KNOWLEDGE ABOUT THE IMPACTS OF THE SPILL, launching AS AN OPEN SOURCE PLATFORM, COLLECTING DATA AND MAPS OF THE COASTLINE OVER TIME TO SHOW THE COAST BEFORE, DURING, AND AFTER THE SPILL. Before, during and after is the sequence that wins arguments about damage. Start the baseline photographs now, while there is still a before. WHAT THE PLATFORM ACTUALLY GIVES YOU: it is A PLATFORM FOR COMMUNITY SCIENCE PRACTITIONERS WORKING ON ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES TO DOCUMENT THEIR WORK, SHARE TOOLS FOR ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING AND ADVOCACY, AND CONNECT WITH EACH OTHER; THE COMMUNITY IS OPEN AND FREE FOR ANYONE TO JOIN, members CAN ADD THEIR OWN PROJECT PAGE TO DOCUMENT THEIR METHODS AND SHARE EXPERTISE, and users CAN BROWSE LOW-COST ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING TOOLS FOR APPLICATION AREAS SUCH AS AIR QUALITY, LAND USE, STORMWATER, alongside ADVOCACY METHODS, AND ACTION TOOLKITS BY SCIENCE TOPICS covering WATER, SOIL, AIR, INDUSTRY, CLIMATE, ORGANIZING, AND MONITORING; COMMUNITY MEMBERS CAN ASK OR ANSWER QUESTIONS. Post the question with your site's details. Somebody has usually measured the same pollutant with the same cheap instrument and will say what went wrong the first time. THE KINDS OF INSTRUMENT PEOPLE HAVE BUILT: recorded tools include a spectrometer made from LEGO OR CARDBOARD, WEBCAMS OR RASPBERRY PI CAMERAS, RECYCLED DVDs so that SPECTROSCOPY IS A RESEARCH METHOD THAT ANYONE CAN EXPLORE; a SIMPLE AIR SENSOR whose REALTIME READOUT CHANGES COLOR WHEN THE SENSOR READS DIFFERENCES IN AIR QUALITY, usable WITHOUT HAVING TO LEARN HOW TO PROGRAM; a low-budget water kit with probes MEASURING TEMPERATURE, DISSOLVED OXYGEN AND CONDUCTIVITY, developed to measure sewage outfalls after storms; a DIY device to TEST FOR HEAVY METALS IN WATER; DIY infrared cameras; and a marine microplastics trawler. Dissolved oxygen, conductivity and heavy metals are the readings that show a river has been damaged. A community that takes them weekly for a year has a record no consultant's single sample can rebut. WHAT THE WIDER COMMUNITY ADDS: a water data collaborative HELPS GUIDE COMMUNITY GROUPS ON HOW TO ADOPT DIY, OPEN HARDWARE METHODS FOR COLLECTING THE QUALITY OF WATER DATA THEY NEED TO ACHIEVE THEIR OUTCOMES, alongside research centres publishing open hardware loggers, and an annual gathering for open science hardware makes tools ACCESSIBLE THROUGH OPEN-SOURCE LICENSING; recorded projects include WATER MONITORING IN THE AMAZON. Decide what outcome the data is for before choosing the instrument. A reading that will go to a court needs a different protocol from one that will go to a public meeting, and these groups will tell you which.

trackers.name: Asociación Interamericana para la Defensa del Ambiente (AIDA) - a regional team of Latin American lawyers AND scientists giving FREE legal and technical support to communities harmed by environmental damage, litigating through national and international human rights law
trackers.desc: THIS IS A REGIONAL TEAM OF LAWYERS AND SCIENTISTS WHO WORK FOR COMMUNITIES FREE, AND ITS SCIENTISTS COME WITH THE LAWYERS. It is A REGIONAL NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION THAT USES LAW AND SCIENCE TO PROTECT THE ENVIRONMENT AND THE COMMUNITIES AFFECTED BY ENVIRONMENTAL HARM, PRINCIPALLY IN LATIN AMERICA, providing FREE LEGAL AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT and FREE ADVICE THAT SERVES AS A BRIDGE BETWEEN COMMUNITIES, LOCAL MOVEMENTS, NATIONAL ORGANISATIONS, GOVERNMENTS AND INTERNATIONAL ORGANISMS; its team of ADVOCATES, ATTORNEYS, AND SCIENTISTS... ARE BOTH FROM AND IN LATIN AMERICA and UNDERSTAND THE LEGAL AND POLITICAL CONTEXT OF THE REGION BECAUSE they WERE BORN AND LIVE IN LATIN AMERICA. It has MORE THAN 25 YEARS OF EXPERIENCE. Scientists and lawyers in the same team, both free. The usual gap in a community case is not the legal argument but the technical rebuttal of the developer's study, and this organisation supplies both. WHAT IT SAYS IT DOES WITH THAT COMBINATION: it works at THE NEXUS BETWEEN THE ENVIRONMENT AND HUMAN RIGHTS, BRINGING INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS LAW TO ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS, and through STRATEGIES OF LITIGATION AND ADVOCACY, USING NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL LEGAL TOOLS, SUPPORTED BY SCIENCE, it presses states TO COMPLY WITH THEIR OBLIGATION TO PROTECT THE HUMAN RIGHT TO A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT; it uses LEGAL STRATEGIES BASED ON SCIENCE AND PUBLIC PARTICIPATION and works WITH SCIENTISTS TO ENSURE THAT ITS WORK HAS SOLID BASES AND WITH COMMUNICATORS TO SPREAD THE MESSAGES. International human rights law applied to a local environmental case. Where the national courts have closed, that is the route this organisation was built to open. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY DONE: recorded work includes a long campaign in one Andean town where it FOUGHT THE POISONING OF THE POPULATION BY HEAVY METALS AND OTHER CONTAMINANTS EMITTED BY A LOCAL SMELTER, and significant impact on the protection of a sea turtle in a Central American country THROUGH AN ASSOCIATION WITH a national environmental law organisation. Its method is to work through a national organisation rather than around it. Approach it together with the environmental lawyers already in your country, which makes acceptance more likely. WHO IT IS AND WHERE ITS PARTNERS ARE: founded in 1998 by five environmental law groups from four Latin American countries and one northern one TO BUILD AND EXTEND THE CAPACITIES OF NATIONAL DEFENDERS, it WORKS WITH PARTNERS IN COUNTRIES SUCH AS ARGENTINA, CANADA, CHILE, COLOMBIA, COSTA RICA, ECUADOR, MEXICO AND PERU, with recorded legal work also in Brazil; it is a member of an international land coalition. Ask which national organisation is its partner in your country. That is the door, and the partner list is published by the coalitions it belongs to. THE CAPACITY IT ADDS BEYOND ONE CASE: its stated aim is TO STRENGTHEN THE CAPACITY OF PEOPLE TO GUARANTEE THE INDIVIDUAL AND COLLECTIVE RIGHT TO A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT... THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT, IMPLEMENTATION AND EFFECTIVE ENFORCEMENT OF NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL LAW, and it seeks to ensure that INTERNATIONAL POLICIES, LAWS AND FINANCIAL FLOWS CONTRIBUTE TO THE PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT; it runs legal internships placing law students on country work. Financial flows are named among its targets. Where a project depends on an international bank or investor, that is a second front this organisation already works on.

trackers.name: Accountability Counsel - free support for communities complaining to the accountability offices of banks financing a harmful project, taking cases ONLY WHERE THE COMMUNITY ASKS, plus a searchable global complaints database and a resource guide
trackers.desc: IT ONLY TAKES CASES WHERE THE COMMUNITY ASKS FIRST, AND IT SAYS WHY. It states: TO ENSURE THAT WE DO NOT REPLICATE THE POWER DYNAMIC WE SEEK TO UPEND AND ARE A TRUSTED, WANTED PARTNER IN COMMUNITIES, WE ONLY TAKE CASES IN WHICH COMMUNITIES REQUEST OUR SUPPORT; assistance BEGINS WITH A REQUEST FOR SUPPORT FROM THE COMMUNITY ITSELF OR A LOCAL CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATION, and NEARLY ALL CASES COME TO US THROUGH REFERRALS THROUGH CIVIL SOCIETY NETWORKS, OFTEN WITH ONLY ONE OR TWO DEGREES OF SEPARATION; it asks that a case INVOLVE A TRUSTWORTHY LOCAL PARTNER WITH WHOM WE CAN CLOSELY COLLABORATE, and weighs THE LIKELIHOOD OF A COMPLAINT LEADING TO A POSITIVE RESULT AT THE COMMUNITY LEVEL and of CREATING SYSTEMIC CHANGE AT THE INSTITUTIONAL LEVEL. Ask through an organisation that already knows you. One or two degrees of separation is the stated norm, so the introduction matters more than the application. WHAT IT DOES: it ASSIST[S] COMMUNITIES TO DEFEND THEIR RIGHTS THROUGH COMPLAINTS TO ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICES TIED TO PROJECTS THAT CAUSE HARM, specialising in NON-JUDICIAL COMPLAINT OFFICES ESTABLISHED TO RECEIVE COMMUNITY COMPLAINTS; its case work RANGES FROM INTENSIVE AND COMPREHENSIVE ASSISTANCE TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND THEIR PARTNERS THROUGHOUT A COMPLAINT PROCESS, TO PROVIDING MORE TARGETED SUPPORT WITH DAILY CASE WORK CONDUCTED PRIMARILY BY LOCAL PARTNERS, and it CONDUCT[S] TRAININGS IN LOCAL COMMUNITIES ABOUT ALL OPTIONS FOR ADDRESSING HUMAN RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL ABUSES ASSOCIATED WITH INTERNATIONALLY FINANCED PROJECTS. A complaint to a bank's own accountability office runs alongside any court case rather than replacing it. Ask for the training even if you never file: it maps every route available against a financed project. WHAT IT HAS ACHIEVED, INCLUDING IN THIS REGION: recorded results include supporting communities TO PREVENT ABUSES IN MEXICO and elsewhere, TO COMPEL REDESIGN OF A PROJECT in one country and TO REACH HISTORIC AGREEMENTS in others including one Caribbean state; its impact includes REDESIGNED PROJECTS THAT NOW REFLECT COMMUNITY NEEDS, HARM STOPPED AND PREVENTED TO DEFEND WATER RESOURCES, AND AGREEMENTS RESULTING IN COMPENSATION. Redesign, prevention and compensation are the realistic outcomes. A complaint of this kind rarely cancels a project outright, and knowing that before starting keeps a community's expectations intact. THE DATABASE AND GUIDE ANYONE CAN USE: it runs THE WORLD'S MOST COMPREHENSIVE COMMUNITY COMPLAINT DATABASE — SEARCH BY REGION, SECTOR, INSTITUTION, TYPE OF HARM, and a comparison of accountability policies ACROSS SIXTEEN INSTITUTIONS; its resource guide contains INFORMATION ABOUT TOOLS FOR REDRESSING HUMAN RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL VIOLATIONS BY INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS, EXPORT PROMOTION AGENCIES, AND PRIVATE CORPORATE ACTORS, intended TO ASSIST COMMUNITY LEADERS, LAWYERS, NGOs, AND INDIVIDUALS IN DETERMINING WHAT RIGHTS THEY HAVE AND HOW TO FILE A COMPLAINT, and it also covers INFORMATION DISCLOSURE RULES at those institutions. Search the database for your sector before writing anything. Someone has complained about a comparable project and the outcome tells you what to ask for. WHICH OFFICES EXIST, AND WHERE THE GAPS ARE: the offices it works with include those of the regional development bank for this continent, the world bank's public and private arms, a climate fund, a development programme's compliance unit and one national development bank's ombudsperson; it records that THERE ARE MANY COMMUNITIES THAT LACK AN AVAILABLE ACCOUNTABILITY OPTION BECAUSE NO SUCH ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICE EXISTS AT THE INSTITUTION(S) FINANCING A PROJECT, and works to open avenues where investment has none, INCLUDING IMPACT INVESTMENT, PRIVATE EQUITY, AND FINANCING FROM CHINESE INSTITUTIONS; its advocacy removed a requirement that complainants cite specific policy violations, since PREVIOUSLY A COMPLAINT COULD BE REJECTED IF IT DID NOT CONTAIN THIS TECHNICAL INFORMATION. Identify the financier before assuming there is a complaint office. Where the money is private equity or a Chinese lender there may be none, and that absence is itself worth publicising.

trackers.name: The Latin American Water Funds Partnership - 26 operating water funds in named cities across ten countries, paying for conservation in the catchments that supply them, some composed of INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, with technical accompaniment to create new ones
trackers.desc: TWENTY-SIX WATER FUNDS ARE ALREADY OPERATING IN NAMED CITIES, PAYING FOR CONSERVATION IN THE CATCHMENTS THAT SUPPLY THEM. The alliance behind them PROMOTED THE CREATION OF water funds described as ORGANISATIONS OF COLLECTIVE ACTION THAT DRIVE A SHARED AND LONG-TERM VISION OF WATER SECURITY; twenty-six now operate in cities including named capitals and provincial cities across ten countries, and in one recent year the programme recorded 44,116 HECTARES POSITIVELY IMPACTED WITH 16,271 FAMILIES. Cumulatively the funds have LEVERAGED MORE THAN US$249 MILLION and convened MORE THAN 340 PUBLIC, PRIVATE and other actors; an earlier count recorded THE CONSERVATION OF 252,000 HECTARES CRITICAL FOR THE WATER SECURITY OF THE REGION THROUGH PROJECTS DEVELOPED WITH 37,500 FAMILIES. Money that flows from a city's water users to the families who keep the upper catchment intact. Where the land you are defending sits above a city's intake, that is the argument with a funding mechanism already attached. WHO SITS INSIDE THEM: the funds WORK CLOSELY WITH THE LOCAL COMMUNITIES, SOME BEING EVEN COMPOSED OF INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, one such fund having won a United Nations equatorial prize; the model is described as PLATFORMS OF GOVERNANCE TO ADDRESS WATER CHALLENGES AND SHARE RESPONSIBILITIES AND ACCOUNTABILITY for society, as EFFECTIVE MECHANISMS TO IMPROVE WATER AVAILABILITY, BIODIVERSITY AND CLIMATE ADAPTATION for governments, and as a way for companies to address RISKS OF PHYSICAL ACCESS TO WATER IN QUALITY AND QUANTITY. A fund composed of indigenous communities is a precedent, not an exception. Ask to see that one's governing documents before agreeing to any structure a utility proposes. WHAT THE ALLIANCE PROVIDES TO A NEW FUND: it supports funds through SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE TO REACH AND MAINTAIN WATER SECURITY WITH NATURE-BASED SOLUTIONS; THE SYSTEMATISATION, MANAGEMENT AND DIFFUSION OF KNOWLEDGE; THE DEVELOPMENT OF CAPACITIES AND TECHNICAL ACCOMPANIMENT; THE PROMOTION OF DIALOGUE BETWEEN RELEVANT ACTORS OF THE REGION IN AN INCLUSIVE MANNER... ACTIVE PARTICIPATION IN THE DESIGN OF WATER GOVERNANCE AND THE MOBILISATION OF RESOURCES FROM PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SOURCES; at one point 15 ADDITIONAL WATER FUNDS were IN THE PROCESS OF CREATION. Technical accompaniment to design the fund and to mobilise the money. A municipality that wants one does not have to invent the model, and fifteen were being built at once. WHO IS BEHIND IT, WHICH DECIDES HOW YOU APPROACH IT: the alliance is AN AGREEMENT CREATED IN 2011 between a regional development bank, a global environment fund, a corporate foundation, an international climate initiative and a global conservation organisation, with A GROWING LIST OF LOCAL PARTNERS and more than two hundred organisations involved. A bottler's foundation and a development bank sit at the same table as the conservation organisation. Read the governance before joining, and be clear what the fund may and may not spend on. WHAT INDIVIDUAL FUNDS HAVE BUILT: recorded innovations include THE FIRST LABORATORY FOR CENTRAL AMERICA OF STABLE ISOTOPES and THE CREATION OF THE BANK CARD FOR WATER CONSERVATION by one national fund; two funds have concentrated on EFFICIENCY IN THE USE OF WATER in agriculture. A stable isotope laboratory can trace where water in a well actually comes from. Where a project is accused of drying a spring, that is the technical service to ask a water fund for.

trackers.name: Mongabay Latam and the regional environmental journalists' network - a newsroom of 90+ journalists across 14 countries with a published contact for story tips, satellite and data investigations that have INFORMED JUDICIAL AND POLICE ACTION, and an honest account of the risk to sources
trackers.desc: A REGIONAL NEWSROOM OF MORE THAN NINETY ENVIRONMENTAL JOURNALISTS, AND A PUBLISHED EMAIL FOR TAKING A STORY TO THEM. A network of environmental journalists across the region records MORE THAN 120 SERIES AND INVESTIGATIONS IN THE LAST EIGHT YEARS THAT HAVE INCLUDED JOURNALISTS AND MEDIA OF 14 COUNTRIES OF THE REGION; the regional newsroom behind it publishes a contact address for anyone who NEEDS HELP WITH A STORY and asks writers to CONSULT THE PAGE THAT EXPLAINS THE CONDITIONS FOR COLLABORATIONS first. Its reporting draws on INDIGENOUS LEADERS, LOCAL SCIENTISTS, PARK RANGERS, FISHERS, FARMERS AND ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDERS as SOURCES AND PRINCIPAL ACTORS. An editor's email address, and community sources treated as principal actors rather than colour. Read the collaboration conditions before writing, then send the documents, not the outrage. WHY COVERAGE CHANGES A LAND FIGHT: the newsroom has built 20-PLUS DATABASES CONTAINING CRITICAL INFORMATION ON MINING, DRUG TRAFFICKING, FINES IMPOSED ON FOSSIL FUEL AND PALM OIL COMPANIES, CASES OF ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDER KILLINGS THAT HAVE GONE UNPUNISHED OR THAT HAVE BEEN PROSECUTED, GEOLOCATED ENVIRONMENTAL LIABILITIES LIKE CONTAMINATED SITES LEFT BEHIND BY THE OIL INDUSTRY, and records that THE FINDINGS HAVE BEEN USED TO INFORM JUDICIAL AND POLICE ACTION; one series analysed MORE THAN 724,000 satellite DEFORESTATION ALERTS... TO DOCUMENT ILLEGAL DEFORESTATION OF INDIGENOUS LANDS in four countries, and a satellite analysis of two protected areas in one country counted alerts inside each before A TEAM OF JOURNALISTS TRAVELLED TO THESE AREAS. Their analysis has fed judicial and police action. A published investigation is not only pressure — it can be the document a prosecutor opens a file on. WHAT THE JOURNALISTS BRING THAT A COMMUNITY USUALLY CANNOT BUY: collaborators have acquired experience in INVESTIGATION, SATELLITE ANALYSIS, DATA JOURNALISM, MULTIMEDIA PRODUCTION AND CROSS-BORDER WORK, and for allied outlets these collaborations HAVE OPENED ACCESS TO SPECIALISED COVERAGE THAT, IN MANY CASES, WOULD BE COSTLY TO PRODUCE ON THEIR OWN; the strongest reporting came from JOURNALISTS WHO KNEW THE LOCAL STORY AND COULD RECOGNISE WHEN A SPECIFIC CONFLICT FORMED PART OF A BROADER PATTERN. Show the editor how your case fits a pattern across several places. A single village dispute is a local story; the same company or the same permit failing in five places is a regional investigation. THE HONEST RISK, IN THEIR OWN WORDS: the network records AN ESCALATION OF VIOLENCE THAT GROWS AT GREAT SPEED AND THAT INCREASINGLY PUTS AT RISK OUR SECURITY AND THAT OF OUR SOURCES, ESPECIALLY THOSE OF INDIGENOUS AND COMMUNITY LEADERS, alongside THE LEGAL ONSLAUGHT FROM POLITICAL AND ECONOMIC POWER TO THREATEN JOURNALISTS WHO REVEAL UNCOMFORTABLE TRUTHS. Sources are named in print unless you agree otherwise in advance. Decide who speaks and under what protection before the first interview, and read this alongside the protection funds filed for defenders. THE WIDER STRUCTURE BEHIND IT: the regional newsroom operates as part of a global environmental news organisation producing content IN FOUR LANGUAGES WITH 500 CORRESPONDENTS IN 50 COUNTRIES, largely as a non-profit, and it seeks A NETWORK OF COLLABORATORS; the regional journalists' network was formed because OUR COUNTRIES HAVE THE SAME ENVIRONMENTAL PROBLEMS WITH DIFFERENT NUANCES AND, LIVING IN A GLOBALISED WORLD, IMPUNITY CANNOT be treated as local. Ask which correspondent covers your country. A local journalist inside a regional network can place a story that a national outlet would drop under pressure.

trackers.name: CLOC-Vía Campesina - a continental coordination of 96 peasant, indigenous and Afro-descendant member organisations across 18-21 countries, organised around RECOVERY OF LAND, with women's and youth assemblies and a campaign against persecution of rural activists
trackers.desc: NINETY-SIX PEASANT, INDIGENOUS AND AFRO-DESCENDANT ORGANISATIONS ARE FORMALLY MEMBERS OF ONE CONTINENTAL BODY, AND THE LIST IS PUBLIC. TAKING THE TOTAL NUMBER OF MEMBER ORGANISATIONS TO 96, with representatives of 21 COUNTRIES attending. A published membership list of ninety-six organisations. Find the member in your country and your province: it is the body that already has lawyers, buses and people for a land conflict, and it costs nothing to ask. IN DEFENCE OF THEIR TERRITORIES. Recovery of land is stated as an aim, not implied. Where your dispute is about who holds the land rather than how it is used, this is the network whose members have done that work for thirty years. WHERE IT SITS IN THE WIDER STRUCTURE: it PROMOTED AND WAS THE ORGANISING PILLAR OF the international peasant movement, A SPACE OF INTERNATIONAL ARTICULATION OF RURAL ORGANISATIONS AND SOCIAL MOVEMENTS OF AMERICA, ASIA AND EUROPE, and it is that movement's DIRECT ALLY... ON OUR CONTINENT; a recorded congress drew delegates of 88 PEASANT AND INDIGENOUS ORGANISATIONS FROM 25 COUNTRIES OF THE CONTINENT. A local conflict raised through a member reaches an international movement with standing at the United Nations food agency. That is a route no single village association has on its own. WHAT IT HAS ACHIEVED IN POLICY: one of its first global disputes involved THE INCORPORATION OF THE CONCEPT OF FOOD SOVEREIGNTY AS A RESPONSE TO THE WORLD FOOD CRISIS, after which the United Nations food and agriculture organisation modified its initial position, and the movement has been central to the defence of PEASANT RIGHTS recognised internationally. The peasant rights declaration it drove is now an international instrument. Members can tell you how it has been used in national courts. THE INTERNAL ASSEMBLIES WORTH KNOWING ABOUT: it holds continental assemblies of rural women and of rural youth, its women's assembly declaring for A SOCIETY WHERE THE WOMEN OF THE COUNTRYSIDE LIVE FREE OF VIOLENCE, WITH LAND, AUTONOMY, RIGHTS, JUSTICE AND DIGNITY; and, FACED WITH THE GROWING CRIMINALITY AND THE PERSECUTIONS THAT PEASANT ORGANISATIONS AND ACTIVISTS SUFFER, it has run a campaign on the demilitarisation of the countryside. It has organised for years around persecution of rural activists. Where members of your community are being criminalised, its members know which lawyers and which alarm networks work in your country. THE HONEST NOTE ON WHAT IT IS: the body is explicitly political, describing itself as anti-capitalist and anti-imperialist and assuming THE CLASS STRUGGLE AS A MEANS TO ACHIEVE A DEMOCRATIC AND PLURAL SOCIETY. That framing is stated openly, so decide whether it fits your community before affiliating. Working with a member organisation on one land case does not require adopting its whole platform, but it will be read as alignment by opponents.

trackers.name: COICA - the Amazon basin indigenous coordination representing 511 peoples through named national organisations in nine countries, whose first statutory objective is to DEFEND TERRITORIAL CLAIMS, and which covers peoples in voluntary isolation

Defending territorial claims is the first stated objective, not a programme it might add. A dispute over the boundary of a titled or untitled territory is the core of what this structure exists for. THE PEOPLES IT SPECIFICALLY COVERS THAT OTHERS DO NOT: some sixty-six of the peoples it represents are IN VOLUNTARY ISOLATION AND INITIAL CONTACT. Where a project's footprint may touch a people in isolation, that is a distinct legal and ethical regime and this coordination and its national members hold the evidence and the standing on it. HOW THE MEMBERSHIP HAS CHANGED, WHICH MATTERS WHEN YOU WRITE: the recorded history shows members added and substituted over time — a Brazilian organisation replacing an earlier body, a Colombian Amazon organisation replacing a national indigenous organisation in 1995, and a regional Venezuelan organisation replacing a national council in 2005 — and the figure of president was replaced by a general coordinator. Check which organisation currently holds the seat for your country before writing. Older directories still list bodies that were replaced twenty years ago. THE SCALE AND THE STANDING: it is described as THE LARGEST INDIGENOUS ORGANISATION IN THE WORLD, recorded a population of nearly 2.8 million people across its member organisations, holds membership of an international conservation union, and built its own communication system including a magazine and a portal PROGRAMMED FOR THE 4 LANGUAGES and a mail system to SUPPORT THE DEMANDS OF ALL THE MEMBER ORGANISATIONS. Membership of the international conservation union gives it a seat where protected areas are decided. Where a state proposes a park over a territory, that is a table your national member can reach. THE HONEST NOTE ON ROUTE: the coordination works through its national members and their affiliates rather than with individual communities directly. Go to your national member first, and to its regional affiliate before that. A request arriving at the continental office without the national organisation behind it will be sent back down the chain.

trackers.name: Afro-descendant territorial mapping viewer and the Central American Black Organization - a free regional cartographic tool built with Afro-descendant representatives showing lands and territories, alongside the cross-border network of national Garifuna, Creole and Black organisations

A cross-border body for Garifuna, Creole and Black communities from Belize to Panama. Where the same people are split by a national border, that is the organisation that can carry a claim on both sides. WHAT ITS MEMBER ORGANISATIONS ARE, BY COUNTRY: recorded members include national Garifuna and Creole councils and an educational foundation in one country, Black organisations and a Black women's organisation in another, a community and ethnic development organisation in a third, a Garifuna organisation and a coast development association in a fourth, a Caribbean project association and an Afro-Costa Rican women's centre in a fifth, and an Afro-Panamanian response body, an Afro-Panamanian women's network and an ethnic museum association in a sixth, plus diaspora organisations. It has taken a denunciation to the inter-American commission before. Ask the national member how that was done and what it produced. THE HONEST CURRENCY WARNING: much of the accessible documentation of this network's membership and assemblies dates from the 2000s, though it remains listed as a member of a contemporary regional alliance and holds recent assemblies. Verify who currently leads it and which organisations are still members before relying on the list. The national members are the durable part; the regional office is not always reachable.

trackers.name: International Land Coalition, Latin America and the Caribbean - a regional platform of 61 member organisations across 20+ countries supporting MORE THAN 30 NATIONAL LAND COALITIONS, with a defender-protection commitment signed by every member and an independent land governance index

IS PERPETUATED BY THE STATE IN ALLIANCE WITH THE CORPORATIONS WITH INTEREST IN THEIR TERRITORIES, and another with AN ALARMING DISPOSSESSION OF LANDS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND AFRO-DESCENDANT COMMUNITIES, BECAUSE OF THE EXPANSION OF THE AGRICULTURAL FRONTIER. An independent index that contradicts the government's own monitoring, country by country. Quote your country's score back at the ministry that claims consultation works. THE LAND DEAL DATABASE AND ITS REGIONAL FOCAL POINT: a global land acquisitions observatory names a regional focal point organisation for Latin America and coordinates national pilot land observatories in several countries with the coalition. If a large land acquisition has been announced near you, check whether it is already recorded there — and if it is not, the focal point is who records it. WHAT ITS OWN ANALYSIS SAYS ABOUT THIS REGION: land IS AT THE CENTRE OF DIVERSE CONFLICTS IN THE REGION, WHERE THE HIGHEST NUMBER OF ATTACKS AGAINST THE PEOPLE WHO DEFEND IT IS RECORDED, LINKED IN GREAT MEASURE TO THE EXTRACTIVE INDUSTRIES; the coalition works THROUGH THE PROMOTION OF REGIONAL PLATFORMS AND NATIONAL COALITIONS... SO THAT THE WOMEN, MEN AND COMMUNITIES WHO LIVE ON AND FROM THE LAND HAVE DECISION-MAKING POWER OVER THEIR LANDS AND TERRITORIES. The region with the most attacks on land defenders is the one you are in. Read this entry with the protection funds and the pro bono routes already filed.

trackers.name: Rainforest Foundation US - land titling accelerated with regional government agrarian offices (75,000 acres for 20 communities in months), 400+ trained and financed community patrollers monitoring 19.6M acres, and support to strengthen organisations' capacity to manage funds
trackers.desc: WHAT HISTORICALLY TOOK YEARS WAS DONE IN MONTHS: TWENTY COMMUNITIES TITLED 75,000 ACRES IN ONE INITIATIVE. SECURED LEGAL TITLES IN RECORD TIME FOR 75,000 ACRES OF THEIR ANCESTRAL LANDS, and in another year SIXTEEN INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES it supported RECEIVED LEGAL TITLE TO THEIR ANCESTRAL LANDS; separately it supported titling initiatives AIMING TO SECURE LAND TENURE FOR MORE THAN 11M ACRES ACROSS three countries and advanced tenure security for NEARLY 300,000 ACRES with two peoples in another. Titling accelerated by working with the regional government office that issues the titles, not around it. That is the partnership shape to copy. THE MODEL, STEP BY STEP: its PROVEN LAND-TITLING MODEL is that COMMUNITIES MAP THEIR ANCESTRAL BOUNDARIES, STRENGTHEN THEIR GOVERNANCE, AND USE REAL-TIME MONITORING TOOLS... TO DETECT THREATS; INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS, FEDERATIONS, REGIONAL GOVERNMENTS and the foundation HAVE JOINED FORCES TO MAP AND TITLE INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' LANDS. THE MONITORING PROGRAMME AND ITS SCALE: it has TRAINED AND FINANCED OVER 400 COMMUNITY-BASED PATROLLERS TO MONITOR AND PROTECT 19.6 MILLION ACRES OF THEIR LANDS ACROSS four countries, using a programme in which INDIGENOUS FOREST MONITORS USE SMARTPHONES, SATELLITE IMAGERY, AND DRONES TO DETECT THREATS AND PREVENT DEFORESTATION against ILLEGAL LOGGING, MINING, AND CRIMINAL ACTIVITY; an earlier year recorded 307 COMMUNITY-BASED FOREST PATROLLERS ACROSS 129 COMMUNITIES. In one country it supports AROUND 114 INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, FIVE INDIGENOUS FEDERATIONS, AND ONE REGIONAL INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' ORGANISATION to run it. Patrollers are trained and paid. Community monitoring fails when it depends on volunteers, and this programme treats it as work. THE MONEY IT MOVES TO COMMUNITIES: it UNLOCKED OVER $10.5 MILLION IN FUNDING FROM AROUND THE WORLD TO FUEL INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES' FOREST PROTECTION WORK in one year, and supports partners to STRENGTHEN ORGANIZATIONAL GOVERNANCE AND THEIR CAPACITY TO MANAGE FUNDS AND PROJECTS FOR THE COMMUNITY'S BENEFIT; its forward plan is to STRENGTHEN 67 INDIGENOUS AND LOCAL ORGANIZATIONS AND INCREASE THEIR ACCESS TO FUNDING. Capacity to manage funds is what unlocks direct financing. Ask for that support before asking for a grant, because the audit trail is what most community organisations lack. WHO IT WORKS THROUGH, AND THE DEFENDER RISK: its named partners include a Central American regional forest peoples alliance, a national umbrella organisation of one large country's indigenous peoples, a district council representing one people, and two national congresses representing peoples inside and outside a comarca; it records that THE AMAZON IS THE MOST DANGEROUS REGION IN THE WORLD FOR ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDERS and collaborates with a national federation TO IMPLEMENT PREVENTIVE MEASURES, ENABLING COMMUNITIES TO BE BETTER PREPARED AGAINST THESE THREATS. It works through representative organisations, not with communities directly. Approach through your federation or council — and note that it also plans titling for communities next to territories reserved for peoples in voluntary isolation, to build a protection corridor.

trackers.name: The Global Alliance of Territorial Communities and its Shandia platform - direct funding channelled to territorial organisations' own financial mechanisms, with FISCAL SPONSORSHIP and financial capacity support where an organisation cannot yet receive funds, plus named community-led funds already re-granting

TO LIVE ON OUR LANDS, EXERCISE FREE, PRIOR, AND INFORMED CONSENT, PRESERVE AND ADAPT OUR TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE, AND LIVE FREE FROM VIOLENCE. THE FUNDS THAT ALREADY EXIST UNDER IT: named community-led mechanisms include a Mesoamerican territorial fund, an Amazonian fund led by the Brazilian Amazon indigenous coordination, a fund launched by the national Brazilian indigenous articulation DEVELOPED THROUGH A COLLABORATIVE PROCESS LED BY a national forum of indigenous leaders and a fund working group, REFLECT[ING] A STRONG COMMITMENT TO DEMOCRATIC AND TRADITIONAL GOVERNANCE PRACTICES, a quilombola fund, a fund led by a movement of babassu coconut breaker women, and further funds in Asia that have BEGUN RE-GRANTING IN SIX COUNTRIES, FOCUSING ON INDIGENOUS WOMEN, YOUTH, AND PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES and working to REACH REMOTE COMMUNITIES, SIMPLIFY GRANT ACCESS, BUILD CAPACITY. Several of these funds re-grant to communities in their own region. Ask which one covers your country and whether it has an open window — they are separate from the alliance itself. WHO THE ALLIANCE IS: A COALITION OF INDIGENOUS AND LOCAL COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS FROM MESOAMERICA, AMAZONIA, AFRICA AND ASIA, PROTECTING MORE THAN 958 MILLION HECTARES OF TROPICAL FORESTS and representing 35 MILLION PEOPLE FROM FOREST TERRITORIES IN 24 COUNTRIES, made up of five named networks including the Amazon basin coordination, the Mesoamerican forest peoples alliance and the national Brazilian indigenous articulation; the Mesoamerican alliance's own members are listed by name, from national forestry alliances to named indigenous nations and general congresses. Your national organisation is probably already inside this structure through one of the five networks. Trace the chain upward before assuming you need a new relationship. THE EXCHANGES IT RUNS BETWEEN TERRITORIES: recorded exchanges include Brazilian community funds invited to Mesoamerica to bring their experience to the grassroots of the alliance there, and a delegation from eight African countries meeting Brazilian community fund experts for nine days in indigenous communities; one review recorded honestly that grassroots organisations in that African network STILL HAVE LIMITED, THOUGH GROWING, CAPACITY TO REQUEST AND MANAGE RESOURCES FROM INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION. trackers.name: Business & Human Rights Resource Centre - invites companies to answer a community's allegation and PUBLISHES THE NON-RESPONSE on the company's own page, with regional researchers, investor escalation and published policy and benchmark data on 10,000+ companies
trackers.desc: A COMPANY'S REFUSAL TO ANSWER A COMMUNITY'S ALLEGATION IS ITSELF PUBLISHED, ON ITS OWN PAGE. The centre INVITE[S] COMPANIES TO RESPOND TO ALLEGATIONS OF MISCONDUCT AND PUBLISH[ES] THEIR COMMENTS, doing so WHEN WE FIND NO EVIDENCE THAT THEY HAVE OTHERWISE RESPONDED TO THE CONCERNS; the process ENCOURAGES COMPANIES TO PUBLICLY ADDRESS HUMAN RIGHTS CONCERNS, AND PROVIDES THE PUBLIC WITH BOTH THE ALLEGATIONS AND THE COMPANY'S COMMENTS. PLEASE LET US KNOW. A permanent public record that the company was asked and said nothing. For a developer that presents itself as responsible to lenders and buyers, that line on its own page is a cost. THE SCALE AND WHO DOES THE ASKING: it collects evidence on MORE THAN 10,000 COMPANIES IN MORE THAN 180 COUNTRIES and takes up ALLEGED ABUSE QUICKLY AND DIRECTLY WITH COMPANIES, INVITING THEM TO RESPOND TO SPECIFIC ALLEGATIONS (OVER 1,500 PER YEAR); a network of regional researchers BUILD LONG TERM RELATIONSHIPS WITH HUMAN RIGHTS ADVOCATES ON THE GROUND, BRINGING UNDERSTANDING OF THE DYNAMICS IN THE COUNTRIES THEY COVER, and WHERE THERE IS AN ALLEGATION OF CORPORATE HUMAN RIGHTS ABUSE THAT HAS NO PUBLIC RESPONSE, THEY REACH OUT TO THE COMPANY. Its site runs in several languages including Spanish and Portuguese. There is a researcher for your region who already knows the local advocates. Send the documented allegation to them rather than to a general address. WHAT IT DOES BEYOND PUBLISHING: its recorded practice is that DIALOGUES CAN EXTEND FURTHER AND OCCASIONALLY WE TAKE AN ACTIVE ROLE IN SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES AND NGOs; in one recorded case concerning an imprisoned indigenous leader who HAD LED THE OPPOSITION TO A PROPOSED... MINE IN HIS COMMUNITY'S TERRITORY, it POSTED THE ALLEGATIONS ON OUR WEBSITE AND SOUGHT RESPONSES FROM TWO COMPANIES WHO DID NOT RESPOND, AND ASSISTED THE LOCAL VILLAGERS IN SUBMITTING THE CASE TO THE UN SPECIAL REPRESENTATIVE ON HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, then CONTACTED PUBLIC INVESTORS... AND INVITED THEM TO COMMENT, of whom two responded and ONE COMMITTED TO RAISING THE ISSUE WITH ITS CLIENTS WHO ARE INVESTED in the company. THE HONEST NUMBERS: the centre records a response rate averaging 43% on one page and 60% on another, and its own field acknowledges criticism about WEAK AND TANGENTIAL COMPANY RESPONSES and about the LACK OF REMEDY AND THE INEQUITY IN ARMS FOR THOSE AFFECTED BY ABUSE; a published analysis notes that A COMPANY RESPONSE TO A CRITICAL CIVIL SOCIETY REPORT IS NOT NECESSARILY A POSITIVE SIGN. Roughly half of companies answer, and an answer is not a remedy. Treat this as a public record and a pressure point, not as a complaint procedure that decides anything. WHAT IT ALSO PUBLISHES ON EACH COMPANY: company pages carry news, allegations, KEY DATA POINTS BASED ON CORPORATE POLICIES, AND SCORES FROM PROMINENT CIVIL SOCIETY BENCHMARKS, and its stated goals include a SAFE AND ENABLING ENVIRONMENT IN WHICH COMMUNITIES AND WORKERS CAN ADVOCATE FOR THEIR RIGHTS AND INTERESTS, INCLUDING THROUGH FREE AND FAIR NEGOTIATIONS. It is A REGIONAL NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION WITH A MANDATE TO SUPPORT SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN THE LATIN AMERICAN REGION, whose activities cover ACCESS TO WATER AND ENERGY, RESOURCE MANAGEMENT and which works THROUGH A BROAD NETWORK OF GRASS-ROOTS AND COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS, NATIONAL AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS, THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY AND THE PRIVATE SECTOR; one account records 75 FULL-TIME STAFF MEMBERS BASED IN 19 COUNTRIES IN LATIN AMERICA and another 95 STAFF MEMBERS ACROSS 15 COUNTRIES, with OVER $500 MILLION ACROSS 13,000 INITIATIVES mobilised on one count and OVER USD 1.21 BILLION since 1994 on another. Staff who live in the country rather than visit it, and grant-making measured in thousands of small initiatives. Ask who the country contact is before writing to any regional address. THE PROGRAMME LIST THAT TELLS YOU WHERE A LAND CASE FITS: it works through SIX KEY PROGRAMS — CLIMATE, CIRCULAR ECONOMY, LABOR INNOVATION, BIOMES, DEMOCRACY, AND WATER, and elsewhere describes KEY AREAS INCLUDING CLIMATE ACTION, DEMOCRATIC STRENGTHENING, INCLUSIVE CIRCULAR ECONOMIES, BIOMES CONSERVATION, WATER MANAGEMENT, AND LABOR INNOVATION, with SUPPORT FOR LOCAL INITIATIVES. Biomes and water are separate programmes with their own staff. A watershed case goes to the water programme and a forest or savannah case to biomes — sending it to the wrong one is how a request gets lost. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DID FOR MONITORING ORGANISATIONS: a foundation officer records that in one phase it USED GRANTMAKING... TO MOBILIZE FUNDS WITH PARTNERS TO ORGANIZATIONS IN PAN-AMAZON, NOT ONLY IN THE BRAZILIAN AMAZON, WHICH IS OFTEN THE FOCUS, BUT THE PAN-AMAZON AND THE CHACO REGION, TO STRENGTHEN THEIR ABILITIES TO MONITOR DEFORESTATION, and that MANY OF THE ORGANIZATIONS THAT NOWADAYS ARE LEADING ORGANIZATIONS IN THIS AREA HAVE BEEN SUPPORTED AS A SEED GRANT. Seed grants to organisations that later became the leading monitors. If your group is at the beginning, that is the stage this foundation has repeatedly funded — and the Chaco, usually ignored beside the Amazon, is named. HOW IT DESCRIBES ITS OWN ROLE, WHICH SHAPES WHAT TO ASK FOR: it works AS A BROKER, CO-INVESTOR AND FACILITATOR, its PRIMARY CONTRIBUTION TO ITS ALLIES IS THE PROMOTION OF COLLABORATIVE ACTION THROUGH SERVICES AND FINANCIAL SUPPORT, and it BRINGS ITS ABILITIES AND RESOURCES TO THE TABLE AS A PEER INSTITUTION, providing ITS ABILITY, SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE, CONTACTS, RESOURCES, STRATEGIES, AND TOOLS TO WORK TOWARDS A COMMON CAUSE. Contacts and convening are offered alongside money. Where a case needs a mayor, a ministry and a company in one room, that is the service to ask for rather than a grant. THE UNITED STATES ENTITY, AND WHAT IT FUNDS: a separate United States non-profit MOBILIZES RESOURCES AND PARTNERSHIPS FROM THE UNITED STATES TO SUPPORT AND EXPAND THE IMPACT OF THIS MISSION and SUPPORTS INITIATIVES ALIGNED WITH THE FOUNDATION'S PRIORITIES ACROSS THREE INTERCONNECTED PILLARS... DEMOCRATIC INNOVATION, CLIMATE ACTION, AND A JUST AND REGENERATIVE ECONOMY, having COME TO EMBRACE FEMINIST PRINCIPLES THAT CENTER THE IMPORTANCE OF BUILDING COLLECTIVE POWER. Two legal entities, two funding routes. Which one can pay you depends on where your organisation is registered, so ask that first. THE HONEST NOTE ON ORIGIN AND COMPANY: it was FOUNDED IN 1994 BY a Swiss industrialist, is headquartered in one Central American capital with a northern office, works BY ENCOURAGING ALLIANCES BETWEEN SOCIAL AND BUSINESS LEADERS, and its recent activities include projects with a named water technology company in one country's semi-arid region. Its model is explicitly to put business leaders at the table with social ones. Decide whether that suits your fight before joining a programme, and read who co-funds it.

trackers.name: Fundación de Conservación Jocotoco - an Ecuadorian foundation whose method is BUYING LAND, holding sixteen reserves over 24,500 hectares, targeting sites outside the national protected area system, with a single announced purchase of 23,000 further hectares
trackers.desc: ITS ENTIRE METHOD IS BUYING THE LAND: SIXTEEN RESERVES AND MORE THAN 24,500 HECTARES BOUGHT AND HELD. The foundation states that WE REACH OUR CONSERVATION GOALS BY ACQUIRING LANDS AND MANAGING THEM AS BIOLOGICAL RESERVES, having ESTABLISHED A NETWORK OF SIXTEEN RESERVES THAT TOGETHER ADD UP TO AROUND 23,500 HECTARES, another account putting the network at MORE THAN 24,500 HECTARES across the country's four regions; it was ESTABLISHED TO PURCHASE AND PROTECT LAND IMPORTANT TO THE CONSERVATION OF ENDANGERED species, and works specifically on AREAS OF CRITICAL IMPORTANCE... THAT ARE NOT UNDER THE PROTECTION OF THE NATIONAL SYSTEM OF PROTECTED AREAS. It exists precisely for the sites the state protected area system misses. If your site is ecologically important and legally unprotected, that gap is the criterion this foundation was built around. THE SCALE OF WHAT ONE PURCHASE CAN BE: in one year, despite travel restrictions, it EXPANDED OUR RESERVE NETWORK BY 1,263 HECTARES, including THE CREATION OF OUR RESERVE NUMBER 16 for a recently discovered and highly threatened hummingbird; and it announced THE PURCHASE OF ANOTHER 23,000 HECTARES, saying that WHEN THIS TRANSACTION IS COMPLETED, WE WILL DOUBLE THE AREA WE CURRENTLY CONSERVE. Its first reserve, created in 1998, NOW PROTECTS MORE THAN 2870 HECTARES. Doubling a national reserve network in one transaction. Where a large threatened property comes on the market, an organisation of this kind can move at that scale — but only if it hears about the sale. WHY IT BUYS IN THAT PARTICULAR PLACE: its conservation director records that the country has LOST MORE THAN 98% OF ITS NATIVE COASTAL FORESTS IN THE BIOGEOGRAPHIC CHOCÓ REGION since 1938, MOSTLY CONVERTED INTO PALM PLANTATIONS, and that the region WOULD RAPIDLY APPROACH AN ABYSS OF EXTINCTION IF ANOTHER 100,000 HECTARES OF THESE COASTAL FORESTS ARE DEFORESTED; the aim is to connect a national park WITH PRIVATE RESERVES, FORMING AN ECOLOGICAL CORRIDOR, since otherwise MANY SPECIES COULD DISAPPEAR FROM THIS BIODIVERSITY HOTSPOT. Private reserves bought to connect an existing national park. That corridor argument is what turns a single parcel into a fundable priority. WHO PAYS FOR THE PURCHASES: as a non-profit its main sources are DONATIONS AND INTERNATIONAL TRUST FUNDS DEDICATED TO ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION, with named international conservation organisations having DONATED AND SUPPORTED its activities; one such trust records that it HAS BEEN FUNDING LAND PURCHASE AND PROTECTION WITH the foundation SINCE 2003. Because those funds are used MAINLY FOR THE PURCHASE OF LANDS and offer little for new projects, it founded a travel agency in 2006 to SUPPORT ITS CONSERVATION ACTIVITIES, using local and expert guides. The money for buying land and the money for running it come from different places. A community proposing a purchase should identify both before approaching anyone. WHAT IT DOES WITH NEIGHBOURS AND ON THE GROUND: it WORKS WITH COMMUNITIES NEAR ITS RESERVES TO DEVELOP FOREST-FRIENDLY LIVELIHOOD STRATEGIES THAT PROTECT LOCAL BIODIVERSITY, runs species monitoring and environmental education, facilitates research with local and foreign institutions, and has AN EXPERIENCED REFORESTATION TEAM THAT HAS SUCCESSFULLY PLANTED 1.6 MILLION TREES IN THE PAST 13 YEARS, INCLUDING ~130 NATIVE SPECIES; it also ACHIEVED THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A 60,000 KM² MARINE RESERVE. A reforestation team of that size is a service, not just a statistic. Where degraded land is bought cheaply, ask whether they will replant it.

trackers.name: Nature and Culture International - a team that removes the financial, technical and legal barriers stopping municipalities creating protected areas, with a 16,029 ha MUNICIPAL protected area inside a national system and 12 stacked conservation areas in one corridor
trackers.desc: A DEDICATED TEAM EXISTS TO REMOVE THE FINANCIAL, TECHNICAL AND LEGAL BARRIERS THAT STOP A MUNICIPALITY CREATING A PROTECTED AREA. The organisation states that GOVERNMENTS AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES... ARE MOTIVATED TO PROTECT THEIR ENVIRONMENTS BUT OFTEN FACE FINANCIAL, TECHNICAL, AND LEGAL BARRIERS, and that it has A DEDICATED TEAM OF EXPERTS WHO WORK TO OVERCOME THESE BARRIERS BY COLLABORATING DIRECTLY WITH LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND GOVERNMENTS TO CREATE PROTECTED AREAS WITH LONG-TERM SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT PLANS. In one recorded case, with funding from an Amazon fund, THE TEAM WORKED CLOSELY WITH MUNICIPAL LEADERS AND LOCAL STAKEHOLDERS TO LEAD A PARTICIPATORY PROCESS THAT RESULTED IN LEGAL protection. Financial, technical and legal, in that order. A council that wants to protect a watershed usually fails on all three, and this is an organisation whose whole job is supplying them. THE MUNICIPAL PROTECTION FIGURE AND WHO USES IT: in one country, areas of conservation and sustainable use are ALSO CALLED MUNICIPAL CONSERVATION AND SUSTAINABLE USE AREAS BY SOME MUNICIPAL decentralised governments, and a monitoring guide SYSTEMATISES MONITORING PROTOCOLS for them, an interactive tool DESIGNED TO STRENGTHEN THE TECHNICAL CAPACITIES OF THE PROVINCIAL AND MUNICIPAL TEAMS CHARGED WITH THE MANAGEMENT OF THE NATURAL PATRIMONY; a ministry incorporated one area as THE FIRST MUNICIPAL PROTECTED AREA in the national system, WITH AN EXTENT OF 16,029.03 HECTARES, and with that declaration THE ROLE OF decentralised governments TO CONSERVE PROTECTED AREAS WAS DEFINED AS FUNDAMENTAL. A municipal protected area of sixteen thousand hectares inside the national system. Where a mayor asks what the precedent is, that is the file to put in front of them. THE PROBLEM IT NAMES, WHICH IS PROBABLY YOUR PROBLEM: decentralised governments HAVE CONSERVED AREAS IN THEIR TERRITORIES, BUT NOT ALL ARE DELIMITED OR THEY DO NOT HAVE THE PRIMARY OBJECTIVE OF CONSERVATION; in other cases THEY ARE RECOGNISED AS PROTECTED AREAS BY LEGAL INSTRUMENTS OR BY THE LOCAL POPULATION, BUT NOT IN THE NATIONAL SYSTEMS, and this PROBLEM OCCURS AT REGIONAL LEVEL. Land everyone locally treats as protected but no register records. Delimiting it and getting it into the national system is the work — and it is cheaper than buying anything. WHAT LOCAL AUTHORITIES CAN DO, PER THE EXPERT QUOTED: they CAN ELABORATE NORMS AND STRATEGIES OF TERRITORIAL ORDERING SEEKING TO ENSURE THE SUSTAINABLE USE OF THE NATURAL RESOURCES, BE THE FIRST INSTANCE OF NEGOTIATION AND RESOLUTION OF CONFLICTS, FOSTER ENVIRONMENTAL GOVERNANCE PROMOTING THE ANALYSIS OF LANDSCAPE AND CONNECTIVITY OF AREAS. First instance of negotiation and conflict resolution. Your municipality is a party to the dispute whether or not it wants to be. THE SCALE ALREADY ACHIEVED IN ONE CORRIDOR: in one zone MORE THAN 150 THOUSAND HECTARES OF PÁRAMOS AND MONTANE FORESTS have been conserved THANKS TO THE COMMITMENT OF THE PEASANT COMMUNITIES, LOCAL AND REGIONAL GOVERNMENTS AND the national protected areas service, WHICH GIVE LIFE TO 12 AREAS OF CONSERVATION; AMONG NATIONAL, REGIONAL, PRIVATE AND MUNICIPAL; in the other country the organisation partnered with indigenous communities, authorities and organisations for conservation in MORE THAN 7.3 MILLION ACRES of rain forest, and is protecting a biological corridor of ALMOST 5 MILLION ACRES that will also protect SEVERAL BINATIONAL WATER SOURCES. Twelve areas of four different legal kinds in one landscape. You do not have to choose a single figure — stack whichever ones each parcel qualifies for. WHAT A MAYOR SAID ABOUT ONE OF THEM: a water protection area IS VITAL FOR WATER SECURITY NOT ONLY IN its own canton BUT THROUGHOUT THE WATERSHED, and the mayor is quoted saying it NOT ONLY PROTECTS WATER, BUT UNITES A REGION. The mayor made the argument himself, after ten years of community work. That sequence — community first, mayor second — is the one that holds when administrations change.

trackers.name: Senace — EVA environmental certification registry
trackers.desc: Peru's national reviewer of the biggest projects' environmental studies (EIA-d) in mining, energy, hydrocarbons, transport, agriculture and waste, with the EVA single-window where every study is filed. You CAN get: the full EIA, its resolutions, the company and consultant behind a project, its current stage, and a formal channel to submit citizen observations during participación ciudadana. You CAN'T get: projects below the detailed-EIA threshold (those sit with sector ministries or regions). For activists: when a mine or pipeline is announced near your community, pull its EIA here before it's approved — the comment window is your legal opening, and the study's own baseline data becomes your evidence.

trackers.name: OEFA — environmental enforcement + SINADA complaints
trackers.desc: Peru's environmental enforcement agency for mining, energy, fisheries and industry, with public enforcement reporting (PIFA portal) and SINADA, where any citizen can file an environmental complaint. You CAN get: supervision and sanction records against named companies, administrative measures, and a formal complaint channel that obliges a response. You CAN'T get: criminal prosecution (that's the Fiscalía Ambiental) or enforcement in sectors held by regional EFAs. For activists: a contaminated river or illegal discharge becomes actionable the moment it's a SINADA case number — and a company's OEFA sanction history is ammunition in any campaign against its next project.

trackers.name: Autoridad Nacional de Transparencia y Acceso a la Información Pública (ANTAIP)
trackers.desc: Autoridad Nacional de Transparencia y Acceso a la Información Pública (ANTAIP) — Peru’s national authority for transparency and access to public information (within the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights). — Holds to account: Peru’s public bodies on disclosure — find access-to-information guidance, supervision and reports.

trackers.name: Manolo (manolo.rocks)
trackers.desc: Civic tool scraping Peru's official visitor/interest-management logs to expose who meets public officials. — Holds to account: those who meet Peruvian officials — find a civic tool scraping official visitor logs to expose who met whom.

trackers.name: Tribunal de Transparencia y Acceso a la Informacion Publica (Peru)
trackers.desc: Peru's Transparency and Access to Information Tribunal, the last administrative instance when a public body refuses a request. You CAN get: a free appeal, filed online through the gob.pe mesa de partes, which the Tribunal must resolve within 10 working days; the Ministry of Justice publishes a model appeal form you can adapt. The deadline is 15 working days from an EXPRESS refusal — but where the body simply stayed silent, a tacit denial, there is NO time limit, so an old unanswered request is still live. The Tribunal applies the exceptions in articles 15 to 17 restrictively: an agency stamping a document reservado without justifying it has no effect. You CAN'T get: enforcement beyond the administrative route. For activists: use it for withheld permit files, inspection reports or concession records. WHEN NOT TO USE IT — the useful part: you do NOT have to exhaust this route. A habeas data action goes straight to a civil judge within 60 working days of the refusal, so if the matter is urgent, go to court instead of appealing here.

trackers.name: Comision de Derechos Humanos (COMISEDH)
trackers.desc: Peru Comision de Derechos Humanos is a non-profit association that is dedicated to the protection and promotion of human rights in Peru. It mainly works on combatting torture and sexual violence against women and girls. It also supports transitional justice and Indigenous people’s rights.

trackers.name: AIDA — Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional organisation of Latin American environmental legal experts providing FREE legal and scientific support to communities and local groups, using international and inter-American human-rights law. Track record includes stopping a large dam in Mexico, halting clear-cutting of native forest in Chile, and the La Oroya smelter ruling in Peru. WHO IT SUITS: communities whose national system has already failed them and whose fight needs to go to an international body. AIDA works across Latin America, so it may be able to act in your country even if it has no office there — ask.

trackers.name: Profonanpe — fondo ambiental del Perú
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: Peru's national environmental fund, running Bosques Tropicales — built from the Peru–US debt swap, awarding non-repayable grants — and Conserva Aves calls aimed squarely at creating new subnational protected areas: regional, municipal, communal, indigenous, public or private. WHO IT SUITS: indigenous organisations, native communities and local or regional groups with a recognised record of work with indigenous and local people, plus holders of the various conservation titles; universities qualify only with community participation. HOW IT DIFFERS: it also sub-grants climate finance directly to indigenous organisations, so a federation can hold the money itself.

trackers.name: DAR — Derecho, Ambiente y Recursos Naturales
trackers.desc: A Peruvian non-profit working since 2004 on Amazon governance — hydrocarbons, roads, the Hidrovía Amazónica, energy projects and the finance behind them. WHO TO ENLIST for technical and policy backup on consulta previa, environmental impact assessment, the Escazú Agreement and defender protection; it has backed successful court actions brought by indigenous federations, though partner lawyers usually run the litigation. You CAN: use its free guides and consulta-previa protocols, including autonomous protocols written by federations themselves. For activists: strongest while a project is still at the permitting or financing stage, where the leverage is procedure.

trackers.name: COICA — Coordinadora de las Organizaciones Indígenas de la Cuenca Amazónica
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the basin-wide confederation of Amazonian Indigenous organisations, founded to act for 511 Indigenous peoples across the nine Amazon countries, around 66 of them in voluntary isolation or initial contact. It works through one national member organisation per country — in this country that is AIDESEP, Asociación Interétnica de Desarrollo de la Selva Peruana — and its governing Council brings those presidents together. Its standing work areas are territorial rights and natural resources, human and sociocultural rights, and international law, and it has issued a formal declaration on the defence of Amazonian Indigenous defenders. USE IT: go to AIDESEP first — COICA is the regional weight behind a national organisation, not a direct service. It is the route to carry a territorial case or a threat against leaders from your community into regional and international forums.

trackers.name: Declaraciones Juradas (Contraloría)
trackers.desc: National — Contraloría asset & interest declarations system.

trackers.name: CONVOCA
trackers.desc: Peruvian investigative outlet reporting on corruption, extractive industries and abuse of public resources.

trackers.name: EITI Perú
trackers.desc: National Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative body — discloses mining, oil and gas revenues at national and regional level in Peru.

trackers.name: IDL-Reporteros
trackers.desc: Peruvian investigative newsroom known for major corruption and judicial-graft expos  s.

trackers.name: OjoPúblico
trackers.desc: Peruvian investigative outlet reporting on corruption, illicit finance and corporate power.

trackers.name: Corte Superior de Justicia de La Libertad
trackers.desc: Corte Superior de Justicia de La Libertad — appellate court (Peru).

trackers.name: Corte Superior de Justicia de Ica
trackers.desc: Corte Superior de Justicia de Ica — appellate court (Peru).

trackers.name: SPDA — Sociedad Peruana de Derecho Ambiental
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Peru's leading environmental-law organisation (est. 1986). Runs LITIGIO ESTRATÉGICO in emblematic public-interest cases and operates FREE legal clinics (Consultorios Jurídicos Gratuitos) that have taken on hundreds of cases. WHO IT SUITS: Peruvian communities facing EIA, consulta previa or territorial-defence issues — and environmental or land defenders under threat, who have a dedicated protection programme.

trackers.name: Datos Abiertos Perú
trackers.desc: National — Peruvian government open data portal. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Peru.

trackers.name: Contraloría General de la República del Perú
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Peru — audits government accounts and the use of public money.

trackers.name: SUNARP
trackers.desc: Peru's national public registries superintendency (incl. company registry). Here you can trace companies, their directors and filings registered in Peru.

trackers.name: INEI
trackers.desc: Peru's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Peru.

trackers.name: Poder Judicial del Perú
trackers.desc: Official judiciary portal with jurisprudence and case search. · Find here: the Peruvian Judiciary's portal with case search and resolutions.

trackers.name: SUNARP
trackers.desc: Peru's National Superintendency of Public Registries (company registry). — Holds to account: companies in Peru — find the public registry of legal entities, directors and powers.

trackers.name: Corte Superior de Justicia del Cusco
trackers.desc: Corte Superior de Justicia del Cusco — appellate court in Peru (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: SEACE
trackers.desc: Peru's electronic state-contracting system run by the procurement supervisor OECE/OSCE. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Peru, and for how much.

trackers.name: Defensa Pública — 34 district directorates and the ALEGRA centres
trackers.desc: A FREE LAWYER THROUGH 34 DISTRICT DIRECTORATES nationwide, grounded in Article 139, numeral 16 of the Constitution guaranteeing effective access to justice, particularly for people in situations of vulnerability. HOW IT WORKS: go to a Centro de Asistencia Legal Gratuita (ALEGRA) with your DNI and any evidence; a public defender opens a carpeta de defensoría setting out what to do, and the case is tracked through it. The lawyer will accompany you to the relevant institution. You sign a declaración jurada of your economic situation.
