THE CAPACITY IT ADDS BEYOND ONE CASE: its stated aim is TO STRENGTHEN THE CAPACITY OF PEOPLE TO GUARANTEE THE INDIVIDUAL AND COLLECTIVE RIGHT TO A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT... THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT, IMPLEMENTATION AND EFFECTIVE ENFORCEMENT OF NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL LAW, and it seeks to ensure that INTERNATIONAL POLICIES, LAWS AND FINANCIAL FLOWS CONTRIBUTE TO THE PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT; it runs legal internships placing law students on country work. Financial flows are named among its targets. Where a project depends on an international bank or investor, that is a second front this organisation already works on.

trackers.name: Accountability Counsel - free support for communities complaining to the accountability offices of banks financing a harmful project, taking cases ONLY WHERE THE COMMUNITY ASKS, plus a searchable global complaints database and a resource guide
trackers.desc: IT ONLY TAKES CASES WHERE THE COMMUNITY ASKS FIRST, AND IT SAYS WHY. It states: TO ENSURE THAT WE DO NOT REPLICATE THE POWER DYNAMIC WE SEEK TO UPEND AND ARE A TRUSTED, WANTED PARTNER IN COMMUNITIES, WE ONLY TAKE CASES IN WHICH COMMUNITIES REQUEST OUR SUPPORT; assistance BEGINS WITH A REQUEST FOR SUPPORT FROM THE COMMUNITY ITSELF OR A LOCAL CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATION, and NEARLY ALL CASES COME TO US THROUGH REFERRALS THROUGH CIVIL SOCIETY NETWORKS, OFTEN WITH ONLY ONE OR TWO DEGREES OF SEPARATION; it asks that a case INVOLVE A TRUSTWORTHY LOCAL PARTNER WITH WHOM WE CAN CLOSELY COLLABORATE, and weighs THE LIKELIHOOD OF A COMPLAINT LEADING TO A POSITIVE RESULT AT THE COMMUNITY LEVEL and of CREATING SYSTEMIC CHANGE AT THE INSTITUTIONAL LEVEL. Ask through an organisation that already knows you. One or two degrees of separation is the stated norm, so the introduction matters more than the application. WHAT IT DOES: it ASSIST[S] COMMUNITIES TO DEFEND THEIR RIGHTS THROUGH COMPLAINTS TO ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICES TIED TO PROJECTS THAT CAUSE HARM, specialising in NON-JUDICIAL COMPLAINT OFFICES ESTABLISHED TO RECEIVE COMMUNITY COMPLAINTS; its case work RANGES FROM INTENSIVE AND COMPREHENSIVE ASSISTANCE TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND THEIR PARTNERS THROUGHOUT A COMPLAINT PROCESS, TO PROVIDING MORE TARGETED SUPPORT WITH DAILY CASE WORK CONDUCTED PRIMARILY BY LOCAL PARTNERS, and it CONDUCT[S] TRAININGS IN LOCAL COMMUNITIES ABOUT ALL OPTIONS FOR ADDRESSING HUMAN RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL ABUSES ASSOCIATED WITH INTERNATIONALLY FINANCED PROJECTS. A complaint to a bank's own accountability office runs alongside any court case rather than replacing it. Ask for the training even if you never file: it maps every route available against a financed project. WHAT IT HAS ACHIEVED, INCLUDING IN THIS REGION: recorded results include supporting communities TO PREVENT ABUSES IN MEXICO and elsewhere, TO COMPEL REDESIGN OF A PROJECT in one country and TO REACH HISTORIC AGREEMENTS in others including one Caribbean state; its impact includes REDESIGNED PROJECTS THAT NOW REFLECT COMMUNITY NEEDS, HARM STOPPED AND PREVENTED TO DEFEND WATER RESOURCES, AND AGREEMENTS RESULTING IN COMPENSATION. Redesign, prevention and compensation are the realistic outcomes. A complaint of this kind rarely cancels a project outright, and knowing that before starting keeps a community's expectations intact. THE DATABASE AND GUIDE ANYONE CAN USE: it runs THE WORLD'S MOST COMPREHENSIVE COMMUNITY COMPLAINT DATABASE — SEARCH BY REGION, SECTOR, INSTITUTION, TYPE OF HARM, and a comparison of accountability policies ACROSS SIXTEEN INSTITUTIONS; its resource guide contains INFORMATION ABOUT TOOLS FOR REDRESSING HUMAN RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL VIOLATIONS BY INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS, EXPORT PROMOTION AGENCIES, AND PRIVATE CORPORATE ACTORS, intended TO ASSIST COMMUNITY LEADERS, LAWYERS, NGOs, AND INDIVIDUALS IN DETERMINING WHAT RIGHTS THEY HAVE AND HOW TO FILE A COMPLAINT, and it also covers INFORMATION DISCLOSURE RULES at those institutions. Search the database for your sector before writing anything. Someone has complained about a comparable project and the outcome tells you what to ask for. WHICH OFFICES EXIST, AND WHERE THE GAPS ARE: the offices it works with include those of the regional development bank for this continent, the world bank's public and private arms, a climate fund, a development programme's compliance unit and one national development bank's ombudsperson; it records that THERE ARE MANY COMMUNITIES THAT LACK AN AVAILABLE ACCOUNTABILITY OPTION BECAUSE NO SUCH ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICE EXISTS AT THE INSTITUTION(S) FINANCING A PROJECT, and works to open avenues where investment has none, INCLUDING IMPACT INVESTMENT, PRIVATE EQUITY, AND FINANCING FROM CHINESE INSTITUTIONS; its advocacy removed a requirement that complainants cite specific policy violations, since PREVIOUSLY A COMPLAINT COULD BE REJECTED IF IT DID NOT CONTAIN THIS TECHNICAL INFORMATION. Identify the financier before assuming there is a complaint office. Where the money is private equity or a Chinese lender there may be none, and that absence is itself worth publicising.

trackers.name: Mongabay Latam and the regional environmental journalists' network - a newsroom of 90+ journalists across 14 countries with a published contact for story tips, satellite and data investigations that have INFORMED JUDICIAL AND POLICE ACTION, and an honest account of the risk to sources
trackers.desc: A REGIONAL NEWSROOM OF MORE THAN NINETY ENVIRONMENTAL JOURNALISTS, AND A PUBLISHED EMAIL FOR TAKING A STORY TO THEM. A network of environmental journalists across the region records MORE THAN 120 SERIES AND INVESTIGATIONS IN THE LAST EIGHT YEARS THAT HAVE INCLUDED JOURNALISTS AND MEDIA OF 14 COUNTRIES OF THE REGION; the regional newsroom behind it publishes a contact address for anyone who NEEDS HELP WITH A STORY and asks writers to CONSULT THE PAGE THAT EXPLAINS THE CONDITIONS FOR COLLABORATIONS first. Its reporting draws on INDIGENOUS LEADERS, LOCAL SCIENTISTS, PARK RANGERS, FISHERS, FARMERS AND ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDERS as SOURCES AND PRINCIPAL ACTORS. An editor's email address, and community sources treated as principal actors rather than colour. Read the collaboration conditions before writing, then send the documents, not the outrage. WHY COVERAGE CHANGES A LAND FIGHT: the newsroom has built 20-PLUS DATABASES CONTAINING CRITICAL INFORMATION ON MINING, DRUG TRAFFICKING, FINES IMPOSED ON FOSSIL FUEL AND PALM OIL COMPANIES, CASES OF ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDER KILLINGS THAT HAVE GONE UNPUNISHED OR THAT HAVE BEEN PROSECUTED, GEOLOCATED ENVIRONMENTAL LIABILITIES LIKE CONTAMINATED SITES LEFT BEHIND BY THE OIL INDUSTRY, and records that THE FINDINGS HAVE BEEN USED TO INFORM JUDICIAL AND POLICE ACTION; one series analysed MORE THAN 724,000 satellite DEFORESTATION ALERTS... TO DOCUMENT ILLEGAL DEFORESTATION OF INDIGENOUS LANDS in four countries, and a satellite analysis of two protected areas in one country counted alerts inside each before A TEAM OF JOURNALISTS TRAVELLED TO THESE AREAS. Their analysis has fed judicial and police action. A published investigation is not only pressure — it can be the document a prosecutor opens a file on. WHAT THE JOURNALISTS BRING THAT A COMMUNITY USUALLY CANNOT BUY: collaborators have acquired experience in INVESTIGATION, SATELLITE ANALYSIS, DATA JOURNALISM, MULTIMEDIA PRODUCTION AND CROSS-BORDER WORK, and for allied outlets these collaborations HAVE OPENED ACCESS TO SPECIALISED COVERAGE THAT, IN MANY CASES, WOULD BE COSTLY TO PRODUCE ON THEIR OWN; the strongest reporting came from JOURNALISTS WHO KNEW THE LOCAL STORY AND COULD RECOGNISE WHEN A SPECIFIC CONFLICT FORMED PART OF A BROADER PATTERN. Show the editor how your case fits a pattern across several places. A single village dispute is a local story; the same company or the same permit failing in five places is a regional investigation. THE HONEST RISK, IN THEIR OWN WORDS: the network records AN ESCALATION OF VIOLENCE THAT GROWS AT GREAT SPEED AND THAT INCREASINGLY PUTS AT RISK OUR SECURITY AND THAT OF OUR SOURCES, ESPECIALLY THOSE OF INDIGENOUS AND COMMUNITY LEADERS, alongside THE LEGAL ONSLAUGHT FROM POLITICAL AND ECONOMIC POWER TO THREATEN JOURNALISTS WHO REVEAL UNCOMFORTABLE TRUTHS. Sources are named in print unless you agree otherwise in advance. Decide who speaks and under what protection before the first interview, and read this alongside the protection funds filed for defenders. THE WIDER STRUCTURE BEHIND IT: the regional newsroom operates as part of a global environmental news organisation producing content IN FOUR LANGUAGES WITH 500 CORRESPONDENTS IN 50 COUNTRIES, largely as a non-profit, and it seeks A NETWORK OF COLLABORATORS; the regional journalists' network was formed because OUR COUNTRIES HAVE THE SAME ENVIRONMENTAL PROBLEMS WITH DIFFERENT NUANCES AND, LIVING IN A GLOBALISED WORLD, IMPUNITY CANNOT be treated as local. Ask which correspondent covers your country. A local journalist inside a regional network can place a story that a national outlet would drop under pressure.

trackers.name: CLOC-Vía Campesina - a continental coordination of 96 peasant, indigenous and Afro-descendant member organisations across 18-21 countries, organised around RECOVERY OF LAND, with women's and youth assemblies and a campaign against persecution of rural activists
trackers.desc: NINETY-SIX PEASANT, INDIGENOUS AND AFRO-DESCENDANT ORGANISATIONS ARE FORMALLY MEMBERS OF ONE CONTINENTAL BODY, AND THE LIST IS PUBLIC. It describes itself as AN INSTANCE OF CONTINENTAL ARTICULATION representing PEASANT, WORKER, INDIGENOUS AND AFRO-DESCENDANT MOVEMENTS OF ALL LATIN AMERICA, formally constituted at a congress in 1994; it recorded 84 ORGANISATIONS IN 18 COUNTRIES OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, and at a recent congress ten further organisations were INTEGRATING (OR RE-INTEGRATING IN SOME CASES) AS FORMAL MEMBERS... TAKING THE TOTAL NUMBER OF MEMBER ORGANISATIONS TO 96, with representatives of 21 COUNTRIES attending. A published membership list of ninety-six organisations. Find the member in your country and your province: it is the body that already has lawyers, buses and people for a land conflict, and it costs nothing to ask. WHAT ITS MEMBERS ORGANISE AROUND: members work for THE PRESERVATION, RECOVERY AND CONQUEST OF THE LAND, THE WATER, THE SEEDS AND OTHER NATURAL RESOURCES, FOOD SOVEREIGNTY BASED ON AGROECOLOGY, SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION AND AN EQUALITY BASED ON SMALL AND MEDIUM SCALE PRODUCTION, developing SOLIDARITY, COOPERATION, THE UNITY IN DIVERSITY BETWEEN THE MEMBER ORGANISATIONS; its recent congress had the aim of CONSOLIDATING A COMMON STRUGGLE IN DEFENCE OF THE RIGHTS OF PEASANT AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, AND GUARANTEEING ACCESS TO LAND AND AGROECOLOGICAL PRODUCTION, in a context of organisations UNITING WITH RENEWED FORCE... Seed grants to organisations that later became the leading monitors. If your group is at the beginning, that is the stage this foundation has repeatedly funded — and the Chaco, usually ignored beside the Amazon, is named. HOW IT DESCRIBES ITS OWN ROLE, WHICH SHAPES WHAT TO ASK FOR: it works AS A BROKER, CO-INVESTOR AND FACILITATOR, its PRIMARY CONTRIBUTION TO ITS ALLIES IS THE PROMOTION OF COLLABORATIVE ACTION THROUGH SERVICES AND FINANCIAL SUPPORT, and it BRINGS ITS ABILITIES AND RESOURCES TO THE TABLE AS A PEER INSTITUTION, providing ITS ABILITY, SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE, CONTACTS, RESOURCES, STRATEGIES, AND TOOLS TO WORK TOWARDS A COMMON CAUSE. Contacts and convening are offered alongside money. Where a case needs a mayor, a ministry and a company in one room, that is the service to ask for rather than a grant. THE UNITED STATES ENTITY, AND WHAT IT FUNDS: a separate United States non-profit MOBILIZES RESOURCES AND PARTNERSHIPS FROM THE UNITED STATES TO SUPPORT AND EXPAND THE IMPACT OF THIS MISSION and SUPPORTS INITIATIVES ALIGNED WITH THE FOUNDATION'S PRIORITIES ACROSS THREE INTERCONNECTED PILLARS... DEMOCRATIC INNOVATION, CLIMATE ACTION, AND A JUST AND REGENERATIVE ECONOMY, having COME TO EMBRACE FEMINIST PRINCIPLES THAT CENTER THE IMPORTANCE OF BUILDING COLLECTIVE POWER. Two legal entities, two funding routes. Which one can pay you depends on where your organisation is registered, so ask that first. THE HONEST NOTE ON ORIGIN AND COMPANY: it was FOUNDED IN 1994 BY a Swiss industrialist, is headquartered in one Central American capital with a northern office, works BY ENCOURAGING ALLIANCES BETWEEN SOCIAL AND BUSINESS LEADERS, and its recent activities include projects with a named water technology company in one country's semi-arid region. Its model is explicitly to put business leaders at the table with social ones. Decide whether that suits your fight before joining a programme, and read who co-funds it.

trackers.name: ANCON - a Panamanian association owning the country's first and Central America's largest private reserve (30,000 ha), which bought a farm to create a BUFFER ZONE at a national park's gate, funds all maintenance itself and names local income as the biggest threat
trackers.desc: IT BOUGHT A FARM SPECIFICALLY TO CREATE A BUFFER ZONE AROUND A NATIONAL PARK — AND THE PARK'S OWN OFFICE IS NOW REACHED BY CROSSING IT. The association records that THE FARM OF PERRESÉNICO WAS ACQUIRED BY it TO CREATE BUFFER ZONES TO THE DARIÉN NATIONAL PARK. IN FACT TO ENTER THE ADMINISTRATIVE HEADQUARTERS OF THE PARK ONE MUST CROSS THE FARM it owns; on that farm it has a harpy eagle nest MONITORED THANKS TO CONTRIBUTIONS FROM DONORS AND THE COMMUNITY OF PIJIBASAL WITH WHICH it HAS CELEBRATED AN AGREEMENT. A parcel bought at the gate of a national park, protecting the approach and the administration itself. Small strategic purchases at the entrance can matter more than large ones in the interior. THE RESERVE IT OWNS AND WHAT THAT COSTS: it PROTECT[S] 30,000 HECTARES OF FOREST IN THE PRIVATE NATURAL RESERVE, described as THE FIRST PRIVATE NATURAL RESERVE IN THE REPUBLIC and THE LARGEST OF CENTRAL AMERICA, a reserve of 263 KM² OF JUNGLE AND WETLANDS on an international wetlands list; crucially, THE RESOURCES FOR ITS MAINTENANCE AND PROTECTION ARE RAISED IN THEIR TOTALITY BY the association itself. Every peso of the running cost is raised by the owner. Before a community accepts a donated reserve, that is the question to settle: who pays for it in year five. THE THREATS IT NAMES, WITH THE LAST ONE FIRST IN IMPORTANCE: protecting it REQUIRES AN IMPORTANT EFFORT SINCE WE MUST WORK DAY BY DAY TO MITIGATE THE THREATS IT FACES SUCH AS ILLEGAL LOGGING, THE EXPANSION OF THE AGRICULTURAL FRONTIER, FOREST FIRES, HUNTING AND THE MOST IMPORTANT CHALLENGE, THE LACK OF OPPORTUNITIES FOR INCOME FOR THE local POPULATIONS. The owner of the largest private reserve in the region names local income as the biggest threat, above logging and fire. A protection plan without an income plan is a plan to fail. WHAT IT BUILT INSTEAD OF FENCES: from sustainable use of natural resources it develops PROJECTS THAT GENERATE ALTERNATIVE SOURCES OF INCOME TO THE INDIGENOUS EMBERÁ-WOÜNAAN, AFRO AND SETTLER COMMUNITIES THAT LIVE AROUND THE... RESERVE, and it runs A COCONUT OIL PRODUCTION PLANT... OPERATIONAL, INSIDE THE RESERVE, DIRECTLY BENEFITING THE COMMUNITIES THAT LIVE THERE, with published work on the JUST AND EQUITABLE DISTRIBUTION OF BENEFITS IN THE COCONUT OIL VALUE CHAIN. A processing plant inside the reserve, with a published benefit-sharing study. Settler communities are named alongside indigenous and Afro ones, which is what stops a reserve becoming a boundary dispute. THE OTHER PROPERTIES AND PARKS IT HAS SECURED: it has OBTAINED THE PROPERTY OF ENVIRONMENTALLY DELICATE AREAS including named farms, agroforestry systems in four named places, and a hill that is both a natural reserve and a historic monument in the capital's core; its collaborators have driven THE CREATION OF THE NATIONAL PARKS OF five named protected areas, including an international park shared with a neighbouring country. The same organisation buys private farms and drives national park declarations. Ask which route it recommends for your site rather than assuming it only does one. WHO IT IS AND WHO ELSE PAYS: founded in 1985, it is a national organisation with 40 YEARS OF HISTORY, staffed by biologists, zoologists, botanists, forestry engineers and data managers, and COUNTS ON THE BACKING OF ALLIED COMPANIES; recorded outputs include a cement company's biodiversity action plan and experiments TO RECOVER FOREST COVER IN THE QUARRIES FROM WHICH THE RAW MATERIAL FOR CEMENT MANUFACTURE IS EXTRACTED. It works with a cement company on quarry restoration. Read the corporate list before approaching, because the same company may be behind the development you are fighting.

trackers.name: Consorcio Ambiental Dominicano (CAD)
trackers.desc: A membership organisation founded in 1999, made up of around nine state and civil-society institutions and working with more than 40 allied national and international organisations. WHO TO ENLIST as a route into the Dominican environmental sector rather than as a single actor: it convenes specialists across biodiversity, protected areas, sustainable agriculture and coastal-marine ecosystems, and concentrates its work inside protected areas and their buffer zones and along the border zone with Haiti. WHO IT SUITS: communities in or beside a protected area who need technical backing and an introduction to whichever member organisation actually handles their issue. It is a consortium and a technical service network, not a litigator or a grantmaker.

trackers.name: Ministerio de Medio Ambiente y Recursos Naturales (República Dominicana)
trackers.desc: The Dominican environment ministry and the authority for the Sistema Nacional de Áreas Protegidas. You CAN get: the register of protected areas — 131 conservation units in six categories under Ley Sectorial 202-04 as at August 2023, covering 25.32% of the land area and 10.8% of marine waters under Ley 66-07 — downloadable protected-area maps, and the ministry's own lookup services for environmental authorisations, so you can check whether a project near you actually holds one. You CAN'T get: the underlying impact studies as a matter of course, or any guarantee the register is current. For activists: establishing that a project sits inside or beside a declared área protegida, or is operating without an authorisation, is the strongest opening move available here.

trackers.name: Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a regional environmental endowment established in 2012, managing an endowment plus a sinking fund for Ecosystem-based Adaptation, which it disburses mainly through partner National Conservation Trust Funds rather than directly — it helped establish several of them, including the Dominica, Grenada, Jamaica, St Kitts & Nevis, St Lucia and St Vincent funds. Its EbA window runs open calls for proposals. WHO IT SUITS: organisations doing on-the-ground ecosystem work that reduces climate vulnerability. Check whether your country has a national trust fund first — that is usually the door, and the CBF itself is the wholesaler behind it. HOW IT DIFFERS: endowment income committed for the long term, so it funds sustained protected-area management rather than a campaign. APPLY TO YOUR NATIONAL FUND, NOT TO CBF — for most of the money. CBF is a regional umbrella: at national level the partner National Conservation Trust Funds (NCTFs) lead the grantmaking process, with endowment proceeds held in country-based subaccounts and channelled through them. So for the Conservation Finance stream, the regional body is the wrong door — find your NCTF. THE EXCEPTION IS THE EbA FACILITY, which awards through competitive calls for proposals and is a direct route. THE NUMBERS: EbA medium grants USD 250,000–1 million, large grants up to USD 2 million — large by the standards of most funds here, and not aimed at a small unincorporated group acting alone. Eligible recipients expressly include NCTFs, NGOs, community-based organisations, government agencies, universities and the private sector. SCOPE CHECK: the EbA Facility covers the marine and coastal zone of the insular Caribbean, so an inland project must show its connection to marine and coastal ecosystems. IF YOU ARE TOO SMALL FOR EbA: CBF partners with GEF SGP across 12 shared countries — that is the sibling route for community-scale grants, and it is recorded separately in this map. Endowment disbursements go to NCTFs that have signed agreements with CBF, the first in 2016 with Fondo MARENA in the Dominican Republic.

trackers.name: Special Mining Contracts (Dominican Republic, MEM)
trackers.desc: Dominican Republic Ministry of Energy & Mines portal publishing the full text of special mining contracts and licences. Here you can trace who holds public concessions over land, resources or infrastructure in the Dominican Republic.

trackers.name: Cámara de Cuentas
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of the Dominican Republic. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Dominican Republic.

trackers.name: Compras Dominicana
trackers.desc: Dominican Republic's public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in the Dominican Republic, and for how much.

trackers.name: DGCP — Datos Abiertos (Rep. Dominicana)
trackers.desc: Dominican Republic's public-procurement directorate open-data portal (OCDS-format contracting data). Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in the Dominican Republic, and for how much.

trackers.name: Dominican Republic — ONAPI (Registro Mercantil / Propiedad Industrial)
trackers.desc: National corporate & industrial-property registry; ONAPI registers company names & trade names and is the main source of registered-business information in the Dominican Republic (alongside the Registro Mercantil of the Chambers of Commerce), Dominican Republic. — Holds to account: companies in the Dominican Republic — find ONAPI's registry of company and trade names.

trackers.name: Oficina Nacional de Estadística (ONE)
trackers.desc: Dominican Republic's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Dominican Republic.

trackers.name: Poder Judicial (Rep. Dominicana)
trackers.desc: Official judiciary portal with jurisprudence of the Supreme Court of Justice. · Find here: the Dominican Republic Judiciary's portal and case information.

trackers.name: Interés difuso — a legal interest that does not come from owning land
trackers.desc: THE DOORWAY FOR RESIDENTS WHO OWN NO PART OF THE SITE. Ley 64-00 defines interés difuso in the statute itself as an interest disseminated in a collectivity, corresponding to each of its members, and which does not emanate from titles of property, rights or concrete actions. That last clause is the point — in a field where most routes turn on tenure, this is a legally recognised interest that exists without property title. AND THERE IS A DEDICATED PROSECUTOR: the magistrado procurador fiscal for defence of the environment and natural resources of the corresponding jurisdiction, acting as judge of the querella, is obliged — if he considers the case has indications of gravity — to give it course. File with that office and frame the gravity explicitly, because gravity is the trigger the provision names. NOTE ALSO the definition of licencia ambiental: a document stating the impact study has been delivered and the activity may proceed conditioned on applying the programa de adecuación y manejo ambiental — so a licence is conditional by definition, and failure to apply that programme goes to the licence's own terms. CONSTITUTIONAL HOOK: Article 194 requires ensuring efficient and sustainable use of the Nation's natural resources.

trackers.name: Article 172 — directors are liable where the board authorised the act
trackers.desc: TWO THINGS THAT CHANGE WHO PAYS AND WHAT PROVES IT. ARTICLE 172: where two or more persons participated in the act they are jointly and severally liable (solidariamente) for the totality of the economic damages — and for legal persons that liability is established when the organs of direction or administration authorised the actions that caused the damage. So the board's authorisation is the fact to evidence: minutes, approvals, resolutions. That is what converts corporate conduct into liability here. WHAT THE TRIBUNAL IS DIRECTED TO WEIGH: in determining the magnitude of damages it shall take into account the actas drawn up by technicians and inspectors and formal reports issued by the environment ministry and other state environmental bodies — without prejudice to expert opinions the judge requires on his own initiative or at the request of a party. OBTAIN THE INSPECTION ACTAS AND MINISTRY REPORTS EARLY: they are the court's named evidence base, they are already being generated, and a party can ask the judge to appoint an expert rather than funding one alone. REPARATION means restoring the prior situation where possible, plus compensation for damage to the environment, to communities or to private parties — communities being a named claimant category in their own right.

trackers.name: Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund (CEPF)
trackers.desc: A FUND WHOSE SMALL-GRANT APPLICATION IS A SINGLE LETTER. CEPF (founded 2000; a joint initiative of the French Development Agency, Conservation International, the EU, the GEF, the Government of Japan, the MacArthur Foundation and the World Bank) has funded more than 2,500 grantees. FOR SMALL GRANTS THE LETTER OF INQUIRY IS THE ENTIRE APPLICATION — no longer project proposal is required — reviewed by the hotspot's Regional Implementation Team, with an offline template provided in the call's languages. Large grants go through the ConservationGrants portal and only then invite a full proposal. Reported averages: small grants around US$15,000, large around US$150,000; the small/large threshold varies by call (US$20,000 and US$50,000 both recorded), so read it. TIMING: calls run 6–8 weeks and notification comes several months after closing — but CEPF stops accepting letters once the designated funds are committed, so an open call can close early. WHO IS DISQUALIFIED: individuals cannot apply — you need a legally registered organisation with its own bank account — and government cannot apply. Community groups, farmers' cooperatives, Indigenous Peoples' organisations and women's groups all can, and CEPF welcomes first-time applicants. TWO RULES THAT SINK GOOD APPLICATIONS: your letter must aim at one single strategic direction; and site-based directions are geographically bound — community management work must be in a listed priority KBA, corridor work in a named corridor, while civil-society strengthening can be anywhere in the hotspot. THE STEP MOST PEOPLE SKIP: CEPF encourages you to contact RIT staff to discuss the idea before submitting — free, and the cheapest way to learn whether it fits.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: The Dominican Republic's participatory municipal budget - 40% of the national transfer decided in community assemblies with money pre-assigned by section, municipal technicians providing pre-feasibility studies, and national agencies required to align with the approved plan
trackers.desc: FORTY PER CENT OF EVERY MUNICIPALITY'S NATIONAL TRANSFER IS DECIDED BY COMMUNITY ASSEMBLIES, AND THE MONEY IS PRE-ALLOCATED TO YOUR OWN SECTION. The statute establishes the participatory municipal budget to set THE MECHANISMS OF CITIZEN PARTICIPATION IN THE DISCUSSION, ELABORATION AND FOLLOW-UP OF THE BUDGET OF THE MUNICIPALITY, ESPECIALLY IN WHAT CONCERNS THE 40% OF THE TRANSFER THAT THE MUNICIPALITIES RECEIVE FROM THE NATIONAL BUDGET... WHICH THEY MUST DESTINE TO CAPITAL AND INVESTMENT EXPENDITURE; the money IS PRE-ASSIGNED AMONG THE SECTIONS OR BLOCKS OF THE MUNICIPALITY ACCORDING TO THE QUANTITY OF INHABITANTS, and where a section's share is very low THE COUNCIL OF ALDERMEN MAY TRANSFER MORE MONEY TO IT FOR REASONS OF SOLIDARITY. Your section already has a number attached to it. The question at the assembly is not whether there is money but what it buys — and a small rural section can be topped up on solidarity grounds if it asks. HOW THE DECISION IS ACTUALLY TAKEN: in the second stage THE POPULATION IDENTIFIES ITS MOST PRIORITY NEEDS AND DECIDES THE PROJECTS AND WORKS THAT THE MUNICIPALITY MUST EXECUTE NEXT YEAR through a sequence of assemblies — COMMUNITY ASSEMBLIES IN EACH HAMLET OR COMMUNITY, then sectional, neighbourhood or block assemblies, then an OPEN COUNCIL OR MUNICIPAL ASSEMBLY; a third stage covers transparency and follow-up of the municipal investment plan. The first assembly is in your own hamlet. Bring the proposal there with a costing, because what survives to the open council is what a community assembly has already adopted. WHAT THE MUNICIPALITY MUST PROVIDE: it SHALL SPECIALISE THE TECHNICIANS AND OFFICIALS IT CONSIDERS CONVENIENT TO SUPPORT AND FACILITATE THE PARTICIPATORY MUNICIPAL BUDGET, WITH SPECIAL EMPHASIS ON THE PRE-FEASIBILITY PROCESS OF THE PROJECTS DECIDED BY THE CORRESPONDING ASSEMBLIES, AND SHALL PROVIDE THE NECESSARY MEANS FOR THE ORGANISATION, CONVOCATION AND HOLDING of the assemblies. Pre-feasibility studies for community-chosen projects are the municipality's job, at its cost. A protective work — a retaining wall, a spring catchment, a boundary fence — can be studied that way without the community paying an engineer. THE STANDING BODIES THAT WATCH THE MONEY: the citizenry and communities have THE RIGHT... TO CONSTITUTE THEMSELVES IN FOLLOW-UP COMMITTEES TO WATCH OVER THE GOOD FUNCTIONING OF A PUBLIC SERVICE, and a consultative body of council members and civil society representatives exists TO PROPITIATE CITIZEN AND COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION IN THE PROCESSES OF DESIGN OF PUBLIC POLICIES, OF PLANNING, AND IN DECISION-MAKING. Each council was required to issue its own application regulation including the procedure for the assemblies and committees. Ask for your municipality's own regulation: it names the assembly dates and the committee rules, and it is the document that tells you when the window opens. THE OTHER RULES THAT GOVERN NEIGHBOURHOOD ORGANISATIONS: one capital council approved a REGULATION OF THE NEIGHBOURHOOD ASSOCIATIONS... WHICH GOVERNS THE RELATIONS OF THE MUNICIPALITY WITH THE COMMUNITY ORGANISATIONS, INCLUDING WHAT RELATES TO THE PARTICIPATORY BUDGET. Registering the neighbourhood association under that regulation is what gets it convoked to the assemblies. Do it before the budget cycle, not during it. AND THE OBLIGATION ON NATIONAL AGENCIES: central government sectoral bodies MUST PARTICIPATE IN THE ACTIVITIES OF THE PARTICIPATORY MUNICIPAL BUDGET... AND COORDINATE THEIR INVESTMENT PLANS IN THE MUNICIPALITY WITH THE MUNICIPAL INVESTMENT PLANS APPROVED through it. A national agency planning works in your municipality is required to align with the plan the assemblies approved. That is the clause to quote when a ministry project contradicts what the community decided.

trackers.name: FLACMA - the Latin American federation of cities and municipal associations, open to affiliation by ANY INDIVIDUAL MUNICIPALITY, whose assembly passes resolutions signed by mayors across eighteen countries
trackers.desc: ANY CITY OR MUNICIPALITY IN THE REGION MAY AFFILIATE DIRECTLY, NOT ONLY THROUGH ITS NATIONAL ASSOCIATION. Its membership rule is that MEMBERS ARE ALL THE CITIES, MUNICIPALITIES, NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND MUNICIPALIST INSTITUTIONS OF LATIN AMERICA THAT HAVE EXPRESSED THEIR WILL TO AFFILIATE; it is AN ORGANISATION OF FREE ADHESION THAT REPRESENTS THE 16,132 MUNICIPALITIES, INTENDANCIES AND PREFECTURES, THE CITIES AND THE ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, NETWORKS AND GUILDS OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, and it is the regional section of the world organisation of local governments. A single municipality may join in its own right. Where your national association is captured or inactive, that is a way for one sympathetic town hall to reach the regional table on its own. WHOSE PRESIDENTS SIT ON IT: its published leadership is drawn from the presidents of the national municipal bodies of the region — the federation of municipalities of one southern country, the association of municipalities of another, the Brazilian association of municipalities, the congress of intendants of another, the national federation of municipalities of one large federal country and the association of municipalities of an Andean one — each of them a serving mayor. The people who chair your own national municipal association sit here. A matter raised through that association can be carried into a regional assembly by the same person. WHAT IT SAYS IT IS FOR: TO BE THE VOICE OF LATIN AMERICAN MUNICIPALISM, TO CONSOLIDATE THE LATIN AMERICAN MUNICIPAL ASSOCIATIVE MOVEMENT, TO REPRESENT AND SERVE AS INTERLOCUTOR OF ALL THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND THEIR NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES, and TO PROMOTE IN LATIN AMERICA AUTONOMOUS, STRONG AND DEMOCRATIC LOCAL GOVERNMENTS; it ADHERES TO AND PROMOTES THE WORLD AND REGIONAL CONVENTIONS THAT THE NATIONAL STATES OF THE REGION SUBSCRIBE. Promoting the conventions the states have signed is written into its purpose. Where your country has signed an environmental or rights convention and a municipality is being told to ignore it, that is a body with a standing commitment to the opposite. THE PRECEDENT THAT SHOWS IT TAKES POSITIONS: its general assembly has approved unanimously a declaration on a territorial sovereignty dispute, signed by the president and BY MUNICIPAL AUTHORITIES AND HEADS OF ASSOCIATIONS AND FEDERATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES of eighteen named countries of the region, which also REAFFIRMED THE LEGITIMATE RIGHTS... OVER THE NATURAL RESOURCES OF THE AREA IN QUESTION. The assembly passes resolutions that name natural resources and get signed by mayors across eighteen countries. A community campaign that can be framed as a municipal cause has a forum that has done exactly that before. THE OTHER REGIONAL NETWORKS BESIDE IT: regional analysis names, among the principal associations and networks of local and regional governments with EXPERIENCES, IDEAS AND RESOURCES TO FOSTER INITIATIVES AND PROJECTS LINKED TO SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AT LOCAL LEVEL, a network of Mercosur cities alongside this federation, and global initiatives with regional presence for local sustainability and for city climate action; various cities have prepared VOLUNTARY LOCAL REPORTS on implementing the global development agenda in their territories. A voluntary local report is a document a municipality writes about itself. Getting your community's situation named in one is cheap, public and lasting. THE HONEST NOTE ON REPRESENTATION: the region's representation in the world body has been the subject of negotiations between this federation, the Mercosur cities network and the world organisation to form A LATIN AMERICAN REPRESENTATION THAT IS PLURAL, DIVERSE AND PARTICIPATORY. More than one body claims to speak for the region's municipalities. Approach both this federation and the Mercosur cities network rather than assuming one covers the other.

trackers.name: ICLEI - a sustainability network open to individual councils AND to associations of local governments, giving fee-paying members year-round telephone and email support on designing environment and water projects, plus local biodiversity planning tools and an environmental award
trackers.desc: MEMBERSHIP OF THIS GLOBAL SUSTAINABILITY NETWORK IS OPEN TO ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AS WELL AS TO INDIVIDUAL COUNCILS, AND THE FEE SCALES WITH POPULATION AND NATIONAL INCOME. Its membership page states that AFFILIATION IS OPEN TO ALL LOCAL AND REGIONAL GOVERNMENTS, AS WELL AS TO THEIR WORLD, REGIONAL, NATIONAL AND SUBNATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS, that members MAY VOTE AND PARTICIPATE IN THE GOVERNING ORGANS OF THE WHOLE NETWORK, and that they CONTRIBUTE AN ANNUAL AFFILIATION FEE THAT VARIES REGIONALLY AND ACCORDING TO POPULATION AND GROSS NATIONAL INCOME PER CAPITA. A small municipality pays a small fee and votes in the same network as a capital city. Where a national association is the member, ask whether your council is covered by it already. WHAT A MEMBER ACTUALLY GETS, IN THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT'S OWN WORDS: it SUPPORTS ITS PARTNERS TO FIND SUSTAINABLE SOLUTIONS THROUGH PROJECTS, INITIATIVES AND PROGRAMMES, offers cities and states A PLATFORM TO INTERACT WITH OTHER LOCAL GOVERNMENTS and provides RESOURCES AND TOOLS TO PROMOTE POSITIVE ENVIRONMENTAL, ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL CHANGES; support runs DURING THE YEAR THAT THE FEE LASTS, PERMANENTLY, BY TELEPHONE OR BY EMAIL, and covers THE DESIGN OF PROGRAMMES AND PROJECTS OF SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN THEMES SUCH AS: ENVIRONMENT, WATER, PUBLIC SERVICES, ENERGY EFFICIENCY, SOLID WASTE. Joining requires A REQUEST TO THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT addressed to the named regional secretary, plus a membership form. Permanent telephone and email support on designing water and environment projects, for one annual fee. That is a standing technical helpline for a town hall that has none. THE BIODIVERSITY WORK THAT MATTERS FOR LAND: its recorded local biodiversity work is TO PROMOTE THE BIODIVERSITY STRATEGIES OF THE STATE AND MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENTS, AS WELL AS THEIR ACTION PLANS, AND ALSO TO REINFORCE THE CAPACITIES OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS TO INCORPORATE BIODIVERSITY INTO THE PLANNING PROCESSES, and it notes that MORE MONETARY RESOURCES ARE INVESTED GLOBALLY IN BIODIVERSITY AT LOCAL AND SUBNATIONAL LEVEL THAN AT NATIONAL LEVELS; a member municipality has launched an urban biodiversity index, and a global initiative on NATURE IN URBAN PLANNING is promoted through the network. Incorporating biodiversity into planning processes is the exact point at which a project is stopped or waved through. Ask the secretariat which of its tools your municipality can adopt in its next plan revision. THE RECOGNITION THAT GIVES A COUNCIL A REASON: the regional secretariat runs an award for local governments THAT HAVE CARRIED OUT ACTIONS IN FAVOUR OF THE PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT IN THEMES OF CLIMATE CHANGE, BIODIVERSITY, ENERGY EFFICIENCY, MOBILITY, AMONG OTHERS, open to municipalities, city boroughs and federal entities. An award with a biodiversity category. A council weighing whether to protect a site has a public reason to do so, and the application is a deadline you can work to. THE OFFICES THAT COVER THIS REGION: there is a secretariat for one large federal country together with Central America and the Caribbean, and a separate South American secretariat, each publishing member lists that include municipalities of several countries. Two regional offices cover the whole file. Write to the one for your subregion rather than to the global body.

trackers.name: Fundación DEMUCA - a foundation for strengthening local governments across Central America and the Caribbean, working through the national municipal associations, with a work line covering ENVIRONMENTAL AND RISK MANAGEMENT and cohorts of twenty municipalities
trackers.desc: A FOUNDATION EXISTS WHOSE WHOLE PURPOSE IS STRENGTHENING LOCAL GOVERNMENTS IN CENTRAL AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, AND IT WORKS THROUGH THE NATIONAL MUNICIPAL ASSOCIATIONS. It is described as AN INSTRUMENT OF TECHNICAL AND FINANCIAL COOPERATION of a national development agency THAT PROMOTES THE STRENGTHENING OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS IN CENTRAL AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, its work focused on THE DESIGN OF STRATEGIES AND THE EXECUTION OF NATIONAL AND REGIONAL PROJECTS AIMED AT IMPROVING THE MANAGEMENT CAPABILITIES OF MUNICIPALITIES AND THEIR VARIOUS FORMS OF ASSOCIATION; it SUPPORTS THE NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES IN THE GENERATION OF STRATEGIC POLICY PROPOSALS and COLLABORATES IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPROVEMENT OF THE MEANS AND INSTRUMENTS OF ADMINISTRATION OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS. It is a foundation constituted under the law of one member country in 1995, with a delegation registered in the cooperating country. Where a national municipal association is weak, this is the body that funds and staffs its policy work. Ask your association what it currently receives, and whether your municipality is in the next cohort. THE THREE WORK LINES, ONE OF WHICH COVERS ENVIRONMENT: the cooperation is channelled through this foundation in three lines — TAX REFORM AT LOCAL LEVEL, TO STRENGTHEN THE FINANCIAL CAPACITY OF THE MUNICIPALITIES WITH THEIR OWN RESOURCES TO IMPLEMENT THEIR POLICIES; implementation of the municipal administrative career statute FOR THE STABILITY OF THE HUMAN RESOURCE AND OF THE MUNICIPAL PLANS; and STRENGTHENING OF CAPACITIES OF THE MUNICIPALITIES AND ASSOCIATIONS, TO PROMOTE MUNICIPAL ASSOCIATIVISM, LOCAL ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, POLICIES AND PLANS OF EQUALITY, ENVIRONMENTAL AND RISK MANAGEMENT, STRENGTHENING OF THE SOCIAL FABRIC AND THE PREVENTION OF VIOLENCE. Environmental and risk management sits inside the third line, alongside strengthening the social fabric. A request framed as municipal capacity on environmental management fits the existing programme rather than asking for something new. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DELIVERS, FROM RECORDED EXAMPLES: with a national municipalities corporation and a state municipal development institute it launched a second phase of implementation FOR 20 NEW MUNICIPALITIES AT NATIONAL LEVEL; TO WHICH TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE WILL BE GIVEN TO STRENGTHEN THEIR CAPACITIES through LABOUR TECHNIFICATION, PERMANENT TRAINING AND THE CREATION, DESIGN AND APPLICATION OF TOOLS AND INSTRUMENTS; it co-published a guide for the internal functioning of plural municipal councils; and it produced a model to improve municipal tax management, described by its own technician as A SIMPLE GUIDE DIRECTED TO STRENGTHENING MUNICIPAL AUTONOMY, WHICH CAN BE IMPLEMENTED WITHOUT HAVING EXTERNAL TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, piloted in ten named municipalities with external financing of twenty-seven thousand dollars. Twenty municipalities in one cohort, and a tax guide a town hall can apply on its own. Both are the kind of thing a small municipality can be nominated for without a budget of its own. THE REGIONAL BODY IT SITS BESIDE: the federation of municipalities of the Central American isthmus is one of the organisations from which the Latin American municipal federation was formed, and has appeared as a regional counterpart in municipal research and in Mesoamerican biological corridor work. Verify whether that federation is currently active before relying on it; the foundation above is the better documented door at present.

trackers.name: The GEF Small Grants Programme - grants of up to $50,000 DIRECT to community organisations, with a national coordinator in each country who helps write the concept paper, planning grants, and a companion window of up to $300,000
trackers.desc: THERE IS A NAMED NATIONAL COORDINATOR IN YOUR COUNTRY WHOSE JOB INCLUDES HELPING YOU WRITE THE APPLICATION. The programme's own procedure is that THE PROJECT PROPONENT — A NATIONAL CBO OR NGO — CONTACTS THE SGP NATIONAL COORDINATOR TO RECEIVE PROJECT APPLICATION GUIDELINES AND FORMS, and that WITH ASSISTANCE FROM THE NATIONAL COORDINATOR, THE PROPONENT PREPARES A BRIEF PROJECT CONCEPT PAPER; the coordinator pre-screens it, and if eligible the proponent prepares a full proposal — IN SOME CASES, THIS STEP MAY BE SUPPORTED BY A PLANNING GRANT — which goes to a national steering committee that accepts, rejects or returns it for further work. A planning grant to write the proposal, and an official whose job is to help you write it. Contact the coordinator before drafting anything, because the concept paper is short and they will tell you whether it fits. WHAT IT PAYS AND TO WHOM: the programme PROVIDES GRANTS OF UP TO $50,000 DIRECTLY TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES INCLUDING INDIGENOUS PEOPLE, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS AND OTHER NON-GOVERNMENTAL GROUPS, for projects in BIODIVERSITY, CLIMATE CHANGE MITIGATION AND ADAPTATION, LAND DEGRADATION AND SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT, INTERNATIONAL WATERS AND CHEMICALS, with SPECIAL CONSIDERATION FOR INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, WOMEN, AND YOUTH; it COMPLEMENTS THE LARGE AND MEDIUM-SIZED facility funding BY PROVIDING A WINDOW FOR THE DIRECT PARTICIPATION OF NGOs, LOCAL COMMUNITIES, AND OTHER GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS. Since 1992 it has supported CLOSE TO 30,000 GRANTS, ADMINISTERING $1.54 BILLION... ACROSS 136 COUNTRIES. Fifty thousand dollars, paid direct to a community organisation, on biodiversity or land degradation. That is the largest routine sum in this file available without an intermediary. HOW IT IS RUN LOCALLY: it operates IN A DECENTRALIZED AND COUNTRY-DRIVEN MANNER THROUGH COUNTRY PROGRAM TEAMS COMPOSED OF A NATIONAL COORDINATOR, OFTEN A PROGRAM ASSISTANT, AND A NATIONAL STEERING COMMITTEE IN EACH PARTICIPATING COUNTRY, each country publishing a country programme strategy that proposals must align with. In one small island state an operational phase was advertised with A GRANTS PORTFOLIO OF APPROXIMATELY US$750,000... FOR COMMUNITY-BASED ENVIRONMENTAL PROJECTS. Download your country's programme strategy before writing. Proposals are judged against that document, and it names the priorities and often the specific landscapes. THE THREE AGENCIES THAT NOW RUN IT: the core programme is implemented by a development programme, an agriculture organisation and a conservation organisation, the second bringing expertise in AGRICULTURE, FISHERIES, FORESTRY, BIOENERGY, CLIMATE-RESILIENT PRACTICES, LIVESTOCK, AND LAND & WATER to thirteen countries; national coordinator posts in some small states are contracted through the conservation organisation, working alongside a Caribbean islands biodiversity hotspot fund. Which agency runs your country's programme changes who you write to. Check the country page rather than assuming it is the development programme. THE LARGER WINDOW BESIDE IT: a civil society challenge programme led by a conservation union SUPPORTS COMPETITIVE OPPORTUNITIES FOR LOCAL CSOs TO ACCESS FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL RESOURCES TO SCALE UP INNOVATIVE ENVIRONMENTAL SOLUTIONS, OFFERING GRANTS OF UP TO $300,000. Three hundred thousand for an organisation that has already proved something small works. Treat the fifty-thousand grant as the step that qualifies you for it.

trackers.name: Rainforest Trust - FEASIBILITY AWARDS of about $10,000 to fund the legal pathway study and species survey, then uncapped creation awards for land purchase, community land titling or converting extractive concessions into protected areas
trackers.desc: THERE IS A GRANT OF AROUND TEN THOUSAND DOLLARS JUST TO FIND OUT WHETHER PROTECTING A SITE IS POSSIBLE. The funder provides FEASIBILITY AWARDS TO ASSESS THE POTENTIAL FOR CREATING OR EXPANDING PROTECTED OR CONSERVED AREAS, INTENDED TO ADDRESS SPECIFIC INFORMATION GAPS... AS PRECURSORS TO APPLYING FOR a full award; these can SUPPORT DEVELOPING A LEGAL PATHWAY TO PROTECT A PROPOSED SITE, OR FIELD SURVEYS TO DETERMINE THE PRESENCE AND ABUNDANCE OF CRITICALLY ENDANGERED OR ENDANGERED SPECIES, at typical funding of about US $10,000 and up to about US $20,000 in exceptional cases, ACCEPTED ON A ROLLING BASIS. Ten thousand dollars to pay for the legal pathway study and the species survey — the two documents every protection file needs and no community can afford. Apply for this before applying for anything else. WHAT THE MAIN AWARD BUYS: primary awards SUPPORT THE CREATION AND EXPANSION OF PROTECTED OR CONSERVED AREAS, ON LAND OR SEA, BE IT THROUGH DESIGNATION, LAND TITLING, PURCHASE OR ANY OTHER RECOGNIZED METHODOLOGY; tools named include LAND PURCHASE; DESIGNATION AS NATIONAL PARKS; NATURE RESERVES; COMMUNITY RESERVES; AND CONVERSION OF LOGGING, MINING, OR OTHER TYPES OF EXTRACTIVE CONCESSIONS TO FORMALLY PROTECTED AREAS. Applications above a quarter of a million dollars have fixed deadlines; smaller ones MAY BE SUBMITTED ON A ROLLING BASIS THROUGHOUT THE YEAR, and THERE IS NO FIXED UPPER LIMIT. Converting an existing logging or mining concession into a protected area is a named, fundable route. Where a concession has already been granted over the land you are defending, that is the door rather than a dead end. THE COMMUNITY LAND TENURE TRACK: for projects where indigenous or community land tenure is the primary strategy, the funder looks for cases where LAND OWNERSHIP, I.E. LAND TITLE, IS GRANTED TO A COMMUNITY RATHER THAN TO AN INDIVIDUAL OR AN NGO, or SUBSTANTIAL MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY OF THE AREA WILL BE LED BY THE INDIGENOUS PEOPLES OR LOCAL COMMUNITY, or THE GRANT IS DIRECTLY MANAGED BY AN INDIGENOUS OR LOCAL COMMUNITY-LED ORGANIZATION, including designation as A MULTIPLE-USE TERRITORY WITH MANAGEMENT (OR CO-MANAGEMENT) BY THE INDIGENOUS OR LOCAL COMMUNITY; such organisations are STRONGLY ENCOURAGED TO APPLY. Title to the community rather than to an NGO is a funding criterion here, not a complication. If your aim is communal title, this funder prefers it. WHEN PURCHASE IS THE STRATEGY, THE TEST IS URGENCY: for land purchase projects the funder asks that LAND IS LIKELY TO BE CONVERTED IN THE NEAR FUTURE IF PURCHASE IS NOT COMPLETED, that AN ALTERNATIVE PROTECTION STRATEGY IS NOT POSSIBLE, MORE EXPENSIVE, OR SIGNIFICANTLY LESS EFFECTIVE, and that CONSERVATION VALUE IS GREATER THAN EXPECTED BASED ON THE COST. Imminent conversion is the argument that wins a purchase grant. Document the threat — the permit application, the clearing, the road survey — as carefully as the biodiversity. WHO MAY APPLY, AND THE WARNING ABOUT MIDDLEMEN: ALL APPLICANTS MUST BE LEGALLY REGISTERED, NON-GOVERNMENT ORGANIZATIONS THAT ARE AUTHORIZED TO CONDUCT WORK IN THE COUNTRY, and partners SHOULD BE NGOs BASED IN THE COUNTRY OF THE PROPOSED PROTECTED AREA; the funder states plainly: YOU NEVER NEED TO PAY A CONSULTANT OR INTERMEDIARY TO APPLY FOR its funding, it ONLY REVIEW[S] APPLICATIONS SUBMITTED DIRECTLY BY ELIGIBLE ORGANIZATIONS, and WE WILL WORK WITH YOU TO REFINE YOUR PROPOSAL. Beyond acquisition it HELPS BUILD THE CAPACITY OF ITS PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS, including TRAINING FOR EMPLOYMENT AS FOREST GUARDS, WILDLIFE MONITORS AND ECO-GUIDES. Anyone offering to broker this application for a fee is to be refused. The funder says so itself, and it will help refine the proposal free.

trackers.name: Pro Bono Network of the Americas and its national clearinghouses - non-profits in 16 countries that place SOCIAL ORGANISATIONS with volunteer law firms free, plus free representation for cases at the merits stage before the inter-American commission
trackers.desc: THERE IS A CLEARINGHOUSE IN MOST OF THESE COUNTRIES WHOSE JOB IS TO FIND A LAW FIRM WILLING TO ACT FOR YOUR ORGANISATION FREE. Its members are NON-PROFIT ENTITIES THAT FACILITATE THE PROVISION OF FREE LEGAL SERVICES TO PEOPLE OF SCARCE RESOURCES, SECTORS OR GROUPS IN A CONDITION OF VULNERABILITY, ENTREPRENEURS AND SOCIAL ORGANISATIONS, WITH A VIEW TO IMPROVING ACCESS TO JUSTICE AND THE DEFENCE OF THE PUBLIC INTEREST; the network born in 2011 HAS NOW BECOME THE MAIN INSTITUTIONAL HOME OF THE PRIMARY PRO BONO CLEARINGHOUSES IN THE REGION and INCLUDES MORE THAN 20 ORGANIZATIONS, REPRESENTING 16 COUNTRIES, coordinated jointly by a New York bar association centre and a national pro bono foundation. Social organisations are named alongside individuals as eligible. A community association fighting a project is exactly the kind of client these clearinghouses were built to place. HOW A CASE ACTUALLY REACHES A LAWYER: one national foundation RECEIVES REQUESTS FOR PRO BONO CASES THROUGH ITS WEB PLATFORM OR OTHER ENTITIES, and ARTICULATES AND CHANNELS FREE LEGAL ADVICE, CARRIES OUT WORKSHOPS AND INFORMATIVE TALKS AND SEEKS TO GENERATE PUBLIC INFLUENCE; another states that cases ARRIVE AT THE FOUNDATION THROUGH the regional centre, the regional network, or national NGOs in contact with member firms and university professors, and that WHOEVER HAS A CASE OR A PROJECT FOR WHICH THEY NEED PRO BONO ADVICE MAY PRESENT IT BY SENDING AN EMAIL to a published address. One email with the case attached. That is the whole entry procedure in at least one country, and the others run a web form. THE HONEST LIMIT, STATED BY THE CLEARINGHOUSE ITSELF: one alliance RESERVES THE RIGHT TO EVALUATE AND DECIDE WHETHER A REQUEST MAY BE CONSIDERED A PRO BONO CASE; THE PRESENTATION OF A REQUEST DOES NOT GUARANTEE ITS ACCEPTANCE, NOR THE ASSIGNMENT OF A LAWYER OR FIRM; it ACTS ONLY AS AN INTERMEDIARY BETWEEN THE PERSON OR ORGANISATION REQUESTING AND THE VOLUNTEER LAWYERS, and taking a case DEPENDS EXCLUSIVELY ON THE VOLUNTARY DECISION OF THOSE LAWYERS OR FIRMS, WITHOUT ANY OBLIGATION OF SPONSORSHIP EXISTING. No guarantee, and no obligation on any firm. Apply to more than one clearinghouse, and make the request specific enough that a commercial firm can see the discrete piece of work being asked for. WHAT THE NETWORK COORDINATES BEYOND SINGLE CASES: volunteer lawyers and firms work on PARTICIPATION BEFORE THE INTER-AMERICAN SYSTEM OF HUMAN RIGHTS, COOPERATION TO SOCIAL ORGANISATIONS THAT REQUIRE LEGAL SUPPORT, THE ELABORATION OF THEMATIC REPORTS AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT TO INITIATIVES; under a collaboration agreement with the inter-American human rights commission the network PROVIDES PRO BONO LEGAL REPRESENTATION TO PEOPLE WITH CASES AT THE MERITS STAGE, the commission notifying petitioners of that opportunity. Free representation for a case already before the inter-American commission, arranged through this network. If a matter has reached that stage, ask the commission and the network at the same time. THE REGIONAL PROGRAMME AIMED AT SMALL ORGANISATIONS: under a civic space strengthening project the network HAS DECIDED TO JOIN FORCES TO SUPPORT THE NON-PROFIT INITIATIVES OF CENTRAL AMERICAN COUNTRIES BY MEANS OF ITS NETWORK OF LAWYERS TO PROVIDE FREE ADVICE TO APPLICANTS, with an application form; it also runs law student competitions and internship placements across member organisations. For the Central American countries there is a dedicated window rather than only the national clearinghouse. Use it, and note that the same network places law students who can do the document work.

trackers.name: The Alliance of Environmental Legal Clinics of Latin America and the Caribbean - more than 30 university clinics in 10 countries taking REAL, COLLECTIVE public-interest environmental cases free, with dam-affected and mining-affected communities among their clients
trackers.desc: MORE THAN THIRTY UNIVERSITY LEGAL CLINICS IN TEN COUNTRIES TAKE REAL ENVIRONMENTAL CASES FOR COMMUNITIES, FREE. The alliance ARTICULATES MORE THAN 30 CLINICS IN 10 COUNTRIES and has, since 2019, brought together universities WITH THE OBJECTIVE OF PROMOTING CLINICAL EDUCATION IN ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS AND STRENGTHENING THE FORMATION OF STUDENTS IN THE DEFENCE OF THE ENVIRONMENT AND HUMAN RIGHTS; one member clinic states that its course USES THE CLINICAL METHOD OF TEACHING LAW, BASED ON THE PRACTICE OF THE STUDENTS ON REAL AND NOT SIMULATED CASES, and that THESE CASES MUST ALWAYS BE OF PUBLIC INTEREST. Real cases, not exercises, and public interest is the entry condition. A community with a dispute and no money is what these clinics need in order to teach. WHAT THEY ARE, IN A CLINIC DIRECTOR'S WORDS: they are INSTANCES OF FORMAL TEACHING AND LEARNING AND AT THE SAME TIME OF SERVICE TO THE COMMUNITY AT A MOMENT WHEN THERE EXISTS A GREAT BARRIER OF ACCESS TO JUSTICE IN GENERAL; the initiative FOCUSES ON COLLECTIVE CASES AND EXERCISES THE DEFENCE OF ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS IN CASES OF PUBLIC INTEREST, seeking TO BALANCE THAT ASYMMETRY IN THE DEFENCE OF THE RIGHTS RELATED TO THE ENVIRONMENT. Collective cases are the speciality. Where the harm is shared by a whole village, that is the shape these clinics prefer, not a weakness in the claim. WHAT THEY HAVE ACTUALLY CARRIED: one university clinic CARRIES 22 CASES TO RESOLVE SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL AND PUBLIC HEALTH CONFLICTS in its country, including SUPPORT TO THE COMMUNITIES AFFECTED BY a named large dam, and a claim over mercury contamination from mining harming indigenous peoples; another works on mercury in the Amazon; students of two universities prepared AN AMICUS CURIAE in an unprecedented case on climate change and indigenous childhood; and in 2023 the network filed a report before the inter-American human rights court in an advisory opinion request on climate emergency, EXPRESSLY CITED IN THE FINAL DECISION. Twenty-two live cases in one clinic, and dam-affected communities among the clients. Ask the nearest clinic for its current case list before describing your own. THE OLDER NETWORK BESIDE IT, AND WHAT IT USES: a Latin American network of legal clinics aims TO STRENGTHEN CLINICAL TEACHING AND THROUGH THIS INSTRUMENT TO INTERVENE IN THE DEFENCE OF THE PUBLIC INTEREST AND HUMAN RIGHTS BY MEANS OF STRATEGIC LITIGATION AS A TOOL, its membership including named university clinics paired with human rights and environment centres in several cities. Some clinics are paired with an established rights centre. That combination gives a case both student capacity and an experienced litigating partner. HOW THEY WORK WITH COMMUNITIES: the method promotes ACTIVE LEARNING FROM THE APPROACH TO STATE ACTORS, CIVIL SOCIETY, LOCAL COMMUNITIES, EXPERTS... TO STRENGTHEN THE STRATEGIES OF APPROACHING THE CASES FROM EXPERIENCE; since 2022 the alliance also collaborates with a global network promoting STRUCTURED COLLABORATION BETWEEN UNIVERSITIES AND COMMUNITIES, sharing EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING, PARTICIPATORY PLANNING and social transformation. Structured collaboration between a university and a community is a defined programme, not a favour. Ask the clinic's coordinator which faculty course could adopt your case this term — the academic calendar, not the litigation calendar, decides when they can start.

trackers.name: Fondo de Acción Urgente para América Latina y el Caribe - rapid response grants of up to $5,000 decided in NO MORE THAN 10 WORKING DAYS for defenders under threat, plus a strategic window for organisations defending territories and common goods
trackers.desc: A REQUEST IS STUDIED IN NO MORE THAN TEN WORKING DAYS AND THE MONEY MOVES THREE DAYS AFTER APPROVAL. The fund's rapid response grants are A UNIQUE, FLEXIBLE, AND SHORT-TERM FINANCING MODEL... TO PROVIDE TIMELY AND STRATEGIC SUPPORT FOR ACTIONS THAT RESPOND TO SITUATIONS OF RISK OR THREATS THAT IMPACT THE SECURITY OF WOMEN ACTIVISTS AND DEFENDERS, THEIR COLLECTIVES, OR ORGANIZATIONS, or that TAKE ADVANTAGE OF OPPORTUNITIES TO ADVANCE OR DETER SETBACKS TO THE RIGHTS; ONCE A REQUEST IS RECEIVED, IT IS STUDIED DURING NO MORE THAN 10 WORKING DAYS. IF IT IS APPROVED, IT TAKES AT LEAST THREE WORKING DAYS TO TRANSFER THE RESOURCES, depending on each country's banking requirements. Applicants REGISTER their COLLECTIVE OR ORGANIZATION IN OUR ONLINE SYSTEM and make the request through it. Two weeks from request to money. When a defender has to leave home tonight or a hearing is next month, that is the only timescale in this file that matches the emergency. WHAT IT PAYS AND FOR HOW LONG: the support comprises FLEXIBLE RESOURCES (UP TO AN ALLOCATION OF 5,000 DOLLARS), GRANTED TO SUPPORT THE ACTIVISTS AND THEIR ORGANISATIONS IN A STRATEGIC AND TIMELY MANNER IN THE FACE OF UNFORESEEN AND UNPLANNED SITUATIONS THAT REQUIRE AN IMMEDIATE INTERVENTION, for a maximum of three months; THESE ACTIONS CANNOT BE ACTIVITIES OF PROGRAMMES AND/OR PROJECTS, and applicants MUST DEMONSTRATE THE URGENT CHARACTER OF THE UNFORESEEN AND UNPLANNED SITUATION. It will not pay for anything already in your workplan. Frame the request around what changed this month — the threat, the eviction date, the hearing — and nothing else. THE SECOND WINDOW, WHICH IS ABOUT TERRITORY: alongside the rapid grants the fund gives STRATEGIC SUPPORTS: TO STRENGTHEN THE PROCESSES OF RESISTANCE AND THE STRATEGIES OF THE ORGANISATIONS LED BY WOMEN, TRANS, NON-BINARY OR GENDER-DISSIDENT PEOPLE, THAT PROMOTE IN AN INTEGRATED MANNER THE PROTECTION OF THE TERRITORIES, THE COMMON GOODS AND THE RIGHTS; one recorded call was directed at LOCAL, DEPARTMENTAL OR NATIONAL ORGANISATIONS AND COLLECTIVES OF WOMEN AND/OR FEMINISTS THAT HAVE PERMANENT WORK AROUND THE DEFENCE OF THE TERRITORIES AND NATURE, and at MIXED COMMUNITY, INDIGENOUS, AFRO-DESCENDANT, RAIZAL AND PEASANT ORGANISATIONS THAT HAVE A SPECIFIC LINE OF WORK ON WOMEN'S RIGHTS LINKED TO ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE, AND IN WHICH WOMEN HAVE SIGNIFICANT LEADERSHIP. Mixed community, indigenous and peasant organisations qualify for the territorial window, not only women's organisations, provided women lead a strand of the work. That is a wider door than the fund's name suggests. WHO IT IS AND WHERE IT REACHES: it is THE REGIONAL FEMINIST FUND FOR SPANISH-SPEAKING LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, created in 2009 in one national capital as part of a global urgent action fund founded in 1997 that regionalised IN ORDER TO UNDERSTAND LOCAL CONTEXTS BETTER AND TO BE CLOSER TO THE WORK SITES OF GRASSROOTS ACTIVISTS, now AN INTERNATIONAL ALLIANCE OF THREE AUTONOMOUS SISTER FUNDS. Spanish-speaking countries only for this fund. If you are in Brazil, Guyana, Suriname, Haiti or the English-speaking Caribbean, ask which sister fund covers you before applying. WHAT IT FUNDS THE MONEY FOR: recorded lines are PROTECTION AND SECURITY, RESPONDING TO SITUATIONS OF RISK OR THREAT AGAINST THE SECURITY OF ACTIVISTS AND DEFENDERS, THEIR COLLECTIVES OR ORGANISATIONS, and opportunity grants that let a movement act before a window closes. Security costs — relocation, a lawyer's retainer, travel to a hearing — are exactly what this covers, and they are the costs that no project grant in this file will pay.

trackers.name: Protection grants for defenders at risk - up to €7,500 for LEGAL FEES OF THOSE BEING JUDICIALLY HARASSED, physical and digital security, medical and family costs, with a 24-hour hotline, plus emergency, relocation, trial-monitoring and respite programmes
trackers.desc: THESE GRANTS PAY THE LEGAL FEES OF SOMEONE BEING SUED OR PROSECUTED FOR DEFENDING LAND. The protection grants programme, launched in 2001 TO PROVIDE RAPID AND PRACTICAL FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS AT RISK, pays for IMPROVING PHYSICAL SECURITY OF AN ORGANISATION OR INDIVIDUAL, DIGITAL SECURITY AND COMMUNICATION SECURITY; SUPPORTING LEGAL FEES FOR HRDs WHO ARE BEING JUDICIALLY HARASSED; PAYING FOR MEDICAL FEES FOR HRDs WHO HAVE BEEN ATTACKED OR WHO HAVE SUFFERED A MEDICAL CONDITION AS A RESULT OF THEIR PEACEFUL HUMAN RIGHTS ACTIVITIES; PROVIDING FAMILY ASSISTANCE FOR IMPRISONED HRDs OR FAMILY MEMBERS WHO ARE AT RISK BECAUSE OF A HRD'S ACTIVITIES, up to a maximum of €7,500. Applications CAN BE SUBMITTED ANYTIME VIA THEIR ONLINE SYSTEM, and there is a 24-HOUR EMERGENCY HOTLINE. A criminal complaint or a defamation suit filed by a developer is judicial harassment, and the legal fees are payable. That is the single most common attack on land defenders in this file, and this is the grant written for it. WHAT IT WILL NOT FUND, WHICH DECIDES HOW YOU WRITE IT: the programme excludes RETROSPECTIVE FUNDING, INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS, ORGANISATIONS THAT HAVE APPLIED OR ARE ALREADY RECEIVING FUNDING FOR THE SAME PURPOSE ELSEWHERE, PROJECTS WHICH FOCUS ON BROADER HUMAN RIGHTS ISSUES RATHER THAN THE SPECIFIC SITUATION OF HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, COSTS FOR HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS WHO ARE ALREADY IN EXILE and ongoing office running costs; grants ARE GENERALLY NOT AWARDED FOR 100% OF THE PROPOSED BUDGET, and applicants must commit to return the grant if the work does not go ahead or is funded elsewhere. Write about the named people at risk, not about the campaign. A proposal that describes the environmental issue rather than the threat to specific defenders is refused on its own terms. THE OTHER EMERGENCY FUNDS THAT COVER THE SAME GROUND: a European defenders mechanism provides EMERGENCY GRANTS UP TO 10,000€ and runs a TEMPORARY RELOCATION PROGRAMME that funds a host organisation to relocate a defender, responding to AN INCREASED RISK, AN ANTICIPATED INCREASED RISK OR FOR A HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDER WHO HAS BEEN WORKING IN A DIFFICULT ENVIRONMENT FOR A PROLONGED PERIOD OF TIME AND WHO NEEDS A BREAK, covering REST AND RESPITE, PROFESSIONAL CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT... EMOTIONAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL WELL-BEING, FAMILY SUPPORT; a civil society lifeline fund covers LEGAL REPRESENTATION, PRISON VISITS, TRIAL MONITORING, TEMPORARY RELOCATION, EQUIPMENT REPLACEMENT, applying by email after describing a secure contact method, in several languages including Spanish; and a federation offers SECURE TRANSPORTATION, LEGAL SUPPORT, MEDICAL SUPPORT... HUMANITARIAN ASSISTANCE... URGENT RELOCATION, URGENT MONITORING. Trial monitoring is fundable, and so is a paid observer at the hearing. Where a case is being heard in a small town, an outside monitor changes how it is conducted. THE RESPITE OPTIONS WHEN SOMEONE MUST LEAVE: recorded schemes include a protective fellowship allowing UP TO TEN DEFENDERS PER YEAR to join a university centre FOR THE PURPOSES OF TRAINING, NETWORKING, AND REST, a foundation offering A YEAR LONG RESPITE PROGRAMME, a refuge for journalists forced to flee providing ADMINISTRATIVE, LEGAL AND SOCIAL ASSISTANCE, and a cities of refuge network offering PHYSICAL SAFETY AND ECONOMIC SECURITY FOR A TWO-YEARS FIXED PERIOD. Leaving for a year is not the end of a campaign if someone else can hold the file. Identify who that is before the threat arrives, because these programmes take applications from the person at risk and their host, not from a court. THE SECURITY WARNING BUILT INTO THE APPLICATION: applicants are asked to ENSURE THAT THE METHOD OF CONTACT YOU ARE PROVIDING IS SECURE AND THAT IT IS OK TO BE CONTACTED IN THAT WAY, and one fund asks applicants to describe HOW it CAN CONTACT YOU SECURELY BEFORE SENDING SENSITIVE INFORMATION. Do not send the details from a shared community email account. The application itself can expose the person it is meant to protect.

trackers.name: Inter-American Foundation grants - CURRENTLY PAUSED - direct grants of $25,000-$400,000 to grassroots organisations with no sector calls, no deadline, five application languages, and LAND AND LABOUR accepted as counterpart
trackers.desc: THIS FUNDER IS CURRENTLY PAUSED — CHECK BEFORE SPENDING TIME ON IT. Its own application page states: WE ARE CURRENTLY PAUSING GRANT FUNDING IN ALIGNMENT WITH EXECUTIVE ORDER REEVALUATING AND REALIGNING UNITED STATES FOREIGN AID. CHECK THIS PAGE FOR FURTHER UPDATES. It is AN INDEPENDENT AGENCY of that government. Everything below describes how it worked when open, and is recorded because the terms are unusual enough to be worth watching for. Read the page before writing anything. A funder under a foreign aid review can reopen with different rules, and the counterpart and eligibility terms are the first things such reviews change. WHY IT MATTERED: IT FUNDED GRASSROOTS GROUPS DIRECTLY, WITH NO INTERMEDIARY: it ONLY SUPPORT[S] COMMUNITY-LED PROJECTS SUBMITTED BY LOCAL AND GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS THAT ARE BASED IN INDEPENDENT COUNTRIES OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, requiring proof that YOUR ORGANIZATION HAS A HISTORY OF WORKING TOGETHER AS A GROUP AND IS CAPABLE OF EFFECTIVELY USING GRANTS FUNDS; it DOES NOT IDENTIFY PROBLEMS OR SUGGEST PROJECTS; INSTEAD IT RESPONDS TO INITIATIVES PRESENTED, and PROJECTS ARE SELECTED FOR FUNDING ON THEIR MERITS RATHER THAN BY SECTOR. Grants ran FROM US$25,000 TO $400,000 OVER ONE TO FOUR YEARS, with proposals accepted 365 DAYS A YEAR in SPANISH, PORTUGUESE, ENGLISH, FRENCH, OR HAITIAN CREOLE. No sector calls, no themes, no deadline. A community proposing its own solution in its own language is the entire model, and it is worth having a proposal ready if the pause lifts. THE COUNTERPART RULE, WHICH IS THE PART TO UNDERSTAND: all funded organisations must COMMIT RESOURCES TO ADVANCE THEIR DEVELOPMENT INITIATIVES, called counterpart; COUNTERPART FUNDING MUST BE A COMPONENT OF THE BUDGET... BUT NO MINIMUM AMOUNT IS REQUIRED. HIGHER COUNTERPART FUNDING MAKES A PROPOSAL MORE ATTRACTIVE, and it MAY BE IN CASH DONATIONS OR IN KIND, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, LAND, SUPPLIES, INFRASTRUCTURE, LABOR, AND OFFICE, STORAGE AND MEETING SPACE. Salaries are A LEGITIMATE EXPENSE. Land and volunteer labour count as counterpart. A community that owns the site and works it has already met the requirement without spending anything. WHAT IT LOOKED FOR IN A PROPOSAL: CREATIVE USE OF THE COMMUNITY'S RESOURCES; A DIVERSE ARRAY OF COMMUNITY VOICES IN PROJECT DEVELOPMENT AND EXECUTION; SUBSTANTIAL BENEFICIARY ENGAGEMENT in identifying the problem, choosing the approach, designing the project and managing it; PARTNERSHIPS WITH LOCAL GOVERNMENT, THE BUSINESS COMMUNITY AND OTHER CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS; feasibility, sustainability, measurable results and EVIDENCE OF BENEFICIARIES' ENHANCED CAPACITY FOR SELF-GOVERNANCE; its recorded interests included COMMUNITY CONSERVATION; AND LOCAL MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES (FORESTS, FISHERIES, ETC.). Partnership with the local government is a scoring criterion. That is the argument for bringing your municipality into the proposal rather than fighting it. THE EXCLUSIONS AND THE FIELD OFFICE RULE: support was limited to independent countries of the region, with recorded exclusions of two countries and a period when FUNDING IN THE CARIBBEAN was RESTRICTED TO three named states; public universities could not apply directly BUT MAY PARTNER WITH AN ORGANIZATION THAT IS ELIGIBLE; and an organisation headquartered abroad could apply only if its field office CAN DEMONSTRATE LOCAL LEADERSHIP. Local leadership had to be demonstrated, not asserted. Where an outside NGO offers to apply on your behalf, insist that your own organisation is the applicant.

trackers.name: RedLAC - the network of 32 national and regional ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS in 20 countries, permanent conservation trust institutions financing protected areas and local communities, with a published member list by country and zone
trackers.desc: THIRTY-TWO NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS IN TWENTY COUNTRIES, AND THE NETWORK PUBLISHES WHICH ONE COVERS YOURS. It GROUPS 32 ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS FROM 20 COUNTRIES OF THE REGION, UNITING EFFORTS TO PROTECT THE RICH BIODIVERSITY OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, with its member list filterable by zone — Caribbean, Mesoamerica and South America — alongside regional funds; more than twenty-five years old, it counts MORE THAN 100 ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS WORLDWIDE. Find the fund for your country on that member page. These are permanent national institutions with endowments, not project offices that close when a grant ends. WHAT THESE FUNDS DO, IN THE NETWORK'S WORDS: they HAVE DEMONSTRATED TO BE A KEY MECHANISM IN THE SUSTAINABLE FINANCING OF BIODIVERSITY AND IN THE STRENGTHENING OF PROTECTED AREAS AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, with a role in THE PROTECTION OF NATURAL AREAS AND THE SUPPORT TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES, described as MULTIDIMENSIONAL FUNDS, WITH APPROACHES THAT INTEGRATE PROTECTION OF BIODIVERSITY, CLIMATIC RESILIENCE AND COMMUNITY EMPOWERMENT. Support to local communities is named alongside protected areas. A community managing land next to a park is inside the mandate, not adjacent to it. SOME OF THE MEMBERS BY NAME AND KIND: recorded members include a Caribbean biodiversity fund, a national forever-protection association in one Central American country, an action fund and a Pacific foundation in one Andean country, a nature fund in one southern country, an island life fund and a regional marine fund — the last two showing that funds exist for a single archipelago and for a shared sea as well as for whole countries. There are funds scoped to one archipelago and to one reef system. If your site sits in either, that narrower fund is a better fit than the national one. WHAT THE NETWORK ITSELF OFFERS ITS MEMBERS: joining gives funds THE OPPORTUNITY TO CONNECT AND COLLABORATE WITH OTHER MEMBERS OF THE NETWORK THROUGHOUT THE REGION, to SHARE KNOWLEDGE, RESOURCES AND EXPERIENCES TO IMPROVE THEIR CAPACITIES, and ACCESS TO A WIDE VARIETY OF RESOURCES AND TOOLS, with TRAINING AND ADVICE ON DIVERSE THEMES, FROM PROJECT MANAGEMENT TO COMMUNICATION AND ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION. Where your country has no environmental fund, this network is where one would be built, and it trains new members. That is a long project, but it is the route. WHY THEY MATTER FOR PERMANENT PROTECTION: these funds are conservation trust funds — institutions holding capital whose returns finance protected areas and community work year after year, and the network works alongside a global environment facility, an African funds consortium and a large conservation finance initiative on that model. An endowment pays for wardens and monitoring long after a campaign ends. Where a protected area has just been declared, the next question is which of these funds can endow its running costs.

trackers.name: Global Forest Watch - free near-real-time deforestation alerts by email for any drawn area, an offline field app that walks patrols to the clearing, and a small grants fund whose examples include GETTING CONCESSIONS REVOKED and compiling evidence for formal complaints
trackers.desc: YOU CAN SUBSCRIBE TO EMAIL ALERTS FOR A SINGLE PLOT OF FOREST AND BE TOLD WITHIN DAYS WHEN TREES ARE CUT. The platform is FREE AND SIMPLE TO USE, ENABLING ANYONE TO CREATE CUSTOM MAPS, ANALYZE FOREST TRENDS, SUBSCRIBE TO ALERTS, OR DOWNLOAD DATA FOR THEIR LOCAL AREA OR THE ENTIRE WORLD, providing NEAR-REAL-TIME ALERTS SHOWING SUSPECTED LOCATIONS OF RECENT TREE COVER LOSS; it moved BEYOND ANNUAL DATA ON FORESTS to MONTHLY AND WEEKLY DEFORESTATION ALERTS, with EMAIL SUBSCRIPTIONS bringing them DIRECTLY INTO THE HANDS OF USERS. Users CAN SIGN UP FOR ALERTS AND DOWNLOAD DATASETS WITHOUT ANY SUBSCRIPTION OR LICENSING FEE. Draw the boundary of the land you are defending and subscribe. From then on the clearing tells you rather than the other way round, and the date stamp is independent of anything the developer says. THE FIELD APP THAT WORKS WITHOUT SIGNAL: a companion mobile application ALLOWS RANGERS TO ACCESS the data and alerts OFFLINE, WHICH IS CRITICAL IN AREAS WITH LIMITED TO NO CELL SIGNAL; USING CACHED DATA, THE APP DIRECTS USERS TO NEARBY FOREST CLEARING AND ENABLES THEM TO CAPTURE PHOTOS AND FILL OUT FORMS ABOUT DEFORESTATION, WHICH ARE UPLOADED NEXT TIME THEIR DEVICE CONNECTS, so that patrols KNOW EXACTLY WHERE TO LOOK... AND STOP THE ILLEGAL ACTIVITY BEFORE IT GETS OUT OF CONTROL; it is FREE, OPEN SOURCE, AND AVAILABLE IN ENGLISH, SPANISH, PORTUGUESE, FRENCH, AND BAHASA INDONESIAN. The alert gives the coordinates and the app walks you to them. A ground photograph taken at a satellite-flagged point, on a known date, is the evidence a prosecutor can use. THE GRANT ATTACHED TO IT, AND WHAT IT HAS PAID FOR: a small grants fund SEEKS TO BUILD THE CAPACITY OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS TO EFFECTIVELY USE the tools TO REDUCE ILLEGAL OR UNPLANNED DEFORESTATION; funded project types include USING DATA AND IMAGERY... ALONGSIDE COMMUNITY TERRITORIAL MAPS TO ADVOCATE FOR LAND TITLES AND OTHER STRENGTHENED LAND RIGHTS; CROWDSOURCING, COMPILING AND PUBLISHING DATA ON CONCESSIONS THAT OVERLAP WITH ANCESTRAL COMMUNITY LANDS, AND SUPPORT COMMUNITIES IN APPLYING PUBLIC PRESSURE TO GET THESE CONCESSIONS REVOKED; DEVELOPING THE CAPACITY OF FOREST MONITORING BRIGADES TO CONDUCT FIELD VERIFICATIONS OF NEAR-REAL TIME ALERTS; and SUPPORTING INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES IN DEVELOPING RESPONSE PROTOCOLS, FORMULATING LEGAL STRATEGIES AND COMPILING EVIDENCE OF ILLEGAL DEFORESTATION INCLUDING SATELLITE IMAGERY, DATA AND ANALYSES, AND SUBMITTING IT TO LAW ENFORCEMENT THROUGH FORMAL COMPLAINTS OR OTHER LEGAL PROCESSES. Getting concessions revoked and compiling evidence for formal complaints are funded project types, written into the fund's own examples. That is the grant to cite when describing what you intend to do. THE DEADLINE DISCIPLINE: the fund runs an annual call, and the platform states of a recent round: THE CALL FOR APPLICATIONS HAS CLOSED AS OF THE DEADLINE... WE CANNOT GRANT ANY EXTENSIONS, advising applicants to PREPARE FOR THE NEXT CALL FOR APPLICATIONS BY REVIEWING the current materials, while noting that SOME ITEMS IN THE GUIDELINES FOR APPLICANTS MAY CHANGE YEAR TO YEAR. One deadline a year, strictly enforced. Download this year's guidelines now and write the proposal before the next call opens. WHO ELSE IS ALREADY USING IT: the platform serves GOVERNMENTS, THE PRIVATE SECTOR, NGOs, JOURNALISTS, UNIVERSITIES, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC, and is convened as a partnership of OVER 200 ORGANIZATIONS; a fellowship accompanies the grants. Your municipality and your national forest agency can subscribe to the same alerts you do. Sending them the alert with a covering letter turns your observation into their file.

trackers.name: Public Lab and the open science hardware community - free open-source, low-cost instruments and toolkits communities build themselves for water, air, soil and land use, plus BALLOON AND KITE AERIAL MAPPING with stitching software and an open question forum
