trackers.desc: THE INSTRUMENTS ARE OPEN SOURCE AND CHEAP ENOUGH THAT A COMMUNITY CAN BUILD ITS OWN, INCLUDING AERIAL PHOTOGRAPHY FROM A KITE. The network is DEVOTED TO EMPOWERING COMMUNITIES AND CITIZEN SCIENTISTS TO MONITOR THEIR OWN ENVIRONMENTS THROUGH THE USE OF INEXPENSIVE DIY TECHNIQUES, hosting AN IMPRESSIVE CATALOG OF OPEN SOURCE TOOLKITS... RANGING FROM WATER QUALITY SENSORS TO INDOOR AIR QUALITY AND KITE MAPPING KITS; its tools and data are CREATED BY THE community, OPEN SOURCE, AND TYPICALLY INEXPENSIVE TO USE. Its earliest technique was LOW-ALTITUDE AERIAL MAPPING WITH BALLOONS AND KITES with software to stitch the photographs into a map. A kite, a camera and free stitching software produce a dated aerial photograph of a site at a resolution no public satellite gives you. That is how you show what a hillside looked like before the machines arrived. WHY IT EXISTS, AND WHAT THAT PRECEDENT MEANS: it was founded in 2010 FOLLOWING THE BP OIL DISASTER IN THE GULF OF MEXICO... TO ADDRESS AN ENORMOUS GAP IN COMMUNITY KNOWLEDGE ABOUT THE IMPACTS OF THE SPILL, launching AS AN OPEN SOURCE PLATFORM, COLLECTING DATA AND MAPS OF THE COASTLINE OVER TIME TO SHOW THE COAST BEFORE, DURING, AND AFTER THE SPILL. Before, during and after is the sequence that wins arguments about damage. Start the baseline photographs now, while there is still a before. WHAT THE PLATFORM ACTUALLY GIVES YOU: it is A PLATFORM FOR COMMUNITY SCIENCE PRACTITIONERS WORKING ON ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES TO DOCUMENT THEIR WORK, SHARE TOOLS FOR ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING AND ADVOCACY, AND CONNECT WITH EACH OTHER; THE COMMUNITY IS OPEN AND FREE FOR ANYONE TO JOIN, members CAN ADD THEIR OWN PROJECT PAGE TO DOCUMENT THEIR METHODS AND SHARE EXPERTISE, and users CAN BROWSE LOW-COST ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING TOOLS FOR APPLICATION AREAS SUCH AS AIR QUALITY, LAND USE, STORMWATER, alongside ADVOCACY METHODS, AND ACTION TOOLKITS BY SCIENCE TOPICS covering WATER, SOIL, AIR, INDUSTRY, CLIMATE, ORGANIZING, AND MONITORING; COMMUNITY MEMBERS CAN ASK OR ANSWER QUESTIONS. Post the question with your site's details. Somebody has usually measured the same pollutant with the same cheap instrument and will say what went wrong the first time. THE KINDS OF INSTRUMENT PEOPLE HAVE BUILT: recorded tools include a spectrometer made from LEGO OR CARDBOARD, WEBCAMS OR RASPBERRY PI CAMERAS, RECYCLED DVDs so that SPECTROSCOPY IS A RESEARCH METHOD THAT ANYONE CAN EXPLORE; a SIMPLE AIR SENSOR whose REALTIME READOUT CHANGES COLOR WHEN THE SENSOR READS DIFFERENCES IN AIR QUALITY, usable WITHOUT HAVING TO LEARN HOW TO PROGRAM; a low-budget water kit with probes MEASURING TEMPERATURE, DISSOLVED OXYGEN AND CONDUCTIVITY, developed to measure sewage outfalls after storms; a DIY device to TEST FOR HEAVY METALS IN WATER; DIY infrared cameras; and a marine microplastics trawler. Dissolved oxygen, conductivity and heavy metals are the readings that show a river has been damaged. A community that takes them weekly for a year has a record no consultant's single sample can rebut. WHAT THE WIDER COMMUNITY ADDS: a water data collaborative HELPS GUIDE COMMUNITY GROUPS ON HOW TO ADOPT DIY, OPEN HARDWARE METHODS FOR COLLECTING THE QUALITY OF WATER DATA THEY NEED TO ACHIEVE THEIR OUTCOMES, alongside research centres publishing open hardware loggers, and an annual gathering for open science hardware makes tools ACCESSIBLE THROUGH OPEN-SOURCE LICENSING; recorded projects include WATER MONITORING IN THE AMAZON. Decide what outcome the data is for before choosing the instrument. A reading that will go to a court needs a different protocol from one that will go to a public meeting, and these groups will tell you which.

trackers.name: Asociación Interamericana para la Defensa del Ambiente (AIDA) - a regional team of Latin American lawyers AND scientists giving FREE legal and technical support to communities harmed by environmental damage, litigating through national and international human rights law
trackers.desc: THIS IS A REGIONAL TEAM OF LAWYERS AND SCIENTISTS WHO WORK FOR COMMUNITIES FREE, AND ITS SCIENTISTS COME WITH THE LAWYERS. It is A REGIONAL NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION THAT USES LAW AND SCIENCE TO PROTECT THE ENVIRONMENT AND THE COMMUNITIES AFFECTED BY ENVIRONMENTAL HARM, PRINCIPALLY IN LATIN AMERICA, providing FREE LEGAL AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT and FREE ADVICE THAT SERVES AS A BRIDGE BETWEEN COMMUNITIES, LOCAL MOVEMENTS, NATIONAL ORGANISATIONS, GOVERNMENTS AND INTERNATIONAL ORGANISMS; its team of ADVOCATES, ATTORNEYS, AND SCIENTISTS... ARE BOTH FROM AND IN LATIN AMERICA and UNDERSTAND THE LEGAL AND POLITICAL CONTEXT OF THE REGION BECAUSE they WERE BORN AND LIVE IN LATIN AMERICA. It has MORE THAN 25 YEARS OF EXPERIENCE. Scientists and lawyers in the same team, both free. The usual gap in a community case is not the legal argument but the technical rebuttal of the developer's study, and this organisation supplies both. WHAT IT SAYS IT DOES WITH THAT COMBINATION: it works at THE NEXUS BETWEEN THE ENVIRONMENT AND HUMAN RIGHTS, BRINGING INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS LAW TO ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS, and through STRATEGIES OF LITIGATION AND ADVOCACY, USING NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL LEGAL TOOLS, SUPPORTED BY SCIENCE, it presses states TO COMPLY WITH THEIR OBLIGATION TO PROTECT THE HUMAN RIGHT TO A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT; it uses LEGAL STRATEGIES BASED ON SCIENCE AND PUBLIC PARTICIPATION and works WITH SCIENTISTS TO ENSURE THAT ITS WORK HAS SOLID BASES AND WITH COMMUNICATORS TO SPREAD THE MESSAGES. International human rights law applied to a local environmental case. Where the national courts have closed, that is the route this organisation was built to open. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY DONE: recorded work includes a long campaign in one Andean town where it FOUGHT THE POISONING OF THE POPULATION BY HEAVY METALS AND OTHER CONTAMINANTS EMITTED BY A LOCAL SMELTER, and significant impact on the protection of a sea turtle in a Central American country THROUGH AN ASSOCIATION WITH a national environmental law organisation. Its method is to work through a national organisation rather than around it. Approach it together with the environmental lawyers already in your country, which makes acceptance more likely. WHO IT IS AND WHERE ITS PARTNERS ARE: founded in 1998 by five environmental law groups from four Latin American countries and one northern one TO BUILD AND EXTEND THE CAPACITIES OF NATIONAL DEFENDERS, it WORKS WITH PARTNERS IN COUNTRIES SUCH AS ARGENTINA, CANADA, CHILE, COLOMBIA, COSTA RICA, ECUADOR, MEXICO AND PERU, with recorded legal work also in Brazil; it is a member of an international land coalition. Ask which national organisation is its partner in your country. That is the door, and the partner list is published by the coalitions it belongs to. THE CAPACITY IT ADDS BEYOND ONE CASE: its stated aim is TO STRENGTHEN THE CAPACITY OF PEOPLE TO GUARANTEE THE INDIVIDUAL AND COLLECTIVE RIGHT TO A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT... THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT, IMPLEMENTATION AND EFFECTIVE ENFORCEMENT OF NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL LAW, and it seeks to ensure that INTERNATIONAL POLICIES, LAWS AND FINANCIAL FLOWS CONTRIBUTE TO THE PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT; it runs legal internships placing law students on country work. Financial flows are named among its targets. Where a project depends on an international bank or investor, that is a second front this organisation already works on.

trackers.name: Accountability Counsel - free support for communities complaining to the accountability offices of banks financing a harmful project, taking cases ONLY WHERE THE COMMUNITY ASKS, plus a searchable global complaints database and a resource guide
trackers.desc: IT ONLY TAKES CASES WHERE THE COMMUNITY ASKS FIRST, AND IT SAYS WHY. It states: TO ENSURE THAT WE DO NOT REPLICATE THE POWER DYNAMIC WE SEEK TO UPEND AND ARE A TRUSTED, WANTED PARTNER IN COMMUNITIES, WE ONLY TAKE CASES IN WHICH COMMUNITIES REQUEST OUR SUPPORT; assistance BEGINS WITH A REQUEST FOR SUPPORT FROM THE COMMUNITY ITSELF OR A LOCAL CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATION, and NEARLY ALL CASES COME TO US THROUGH REFERRALS THROUGH CIVIL SOCIETY NETWORKS, OFTEN WITH ONLY ONE OR TWO DEGREES OF SEPARATION; it asks that a case INVOLVE A TRUSTWORTHY LOCAL PARTNER WITH WHOM WE CAN CLOSELY COLLABORATE, and weighs THE LIKELIHOOD OF A COMPLAINT LEADING TO A POSITIVE RESULT AT THE COMMUNITY LEVEL and of CREATING SYSTEMIC CHANGE AT THE INSTITUTIONAL LEVEL. Ask through an organisation that already knows you. One or two degrees of separation is the stated norm, so the introduction matters more than the application. WHAT IT DOES: it ASSIST[S] COMMUNITIES TO DEFEND THEIR RIGHTS THROUGH COMPLAINTS TO ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICES TIED TO PROJECTS THAT CAUSE HARM, specialising in NON-JUDICIAL COMPLAINT OFFICES ESTABLISHED TO RECEIVE COMMUNITY COMPLAINTS; its case work RANGES FROM INTENSIVE AND COMPREHENSIVE ASSISTANCE TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND THEIR PARTNERS THROUGHOUT A COMPLAINT PROCESS, TO PROVIDING MORE TARGETED SUPPORT WITH DAILY CASE WORK CONDUCTED PRIMARILY BY LOCAL PARTNERS, and it CONDUCT[S] TRAININGS IN LOCAL COMMUNITIES ABOUT ALL OPTIONS FOR ADDRESSING HUMAN RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL ABUSES ASSOCIATED WITH INTERNATIONALLY FINANCED PROJECTS. A complaint to a bank's own accountability office runs alongside any court case rather than replacing it. Ask for the training even if you never file: it maps every route available against a financed project. WHAT IT HAS ACHIEVED, INCLUDING IN THIS REGION: recorded results include supporting communities TO PREVENT ABUSES IN MEXICO and elsewhere, TO COMPEL REDESIGN OF A PROJECT in one country and TO REACH HISTORIC AGREEMENTS in others including one Caribbean state; its impact includes REDESIGNED PROJECTS THAT NOW REFLECT COMMUNITY NEEDS, HARM STOPPED AND PREVENTED TO DEFEND WATER RESOURCES, AND AGREEMENTS RESULTING IN COMPENSATION. Redesign, prevention and compensation are the realistic outcomes. A complaint of this kind rarely cancels a project outright, and knowing that before starting keeps a community's expectations intact. THE DATABASE AND GUIDE ANYONE CAN USE: it runs THE WORLD'S MOST COMPREHENSIVE COMMUNITY COMPLAINT DATABASE — SEARCH BY REGION, SECTOR, INSTITUTION, TYPE OF HARM, and a comparison of accountability policies ACROSS SIXTEEN INSTITUTIONS; its resource guide contains INFORMATION ABOUT TOOLS FOR REDRESSING HUMAN RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL VIOLATIONS BY INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS, EXPORT PROMOTION AGENCIES, AND PRIVATE CORPORATE ACTORS, intended TO ASSIST COMMUNITY LEADERS, LAWYERS, NGOs, AND INDIVIDUALS IN DETERMINING WHAT RIGHTS THEY HAVE AND HOW TO FILE A COMPLAINT, and it also covers INFORMATION DISCLOSURE RULES at those institutions. Search the database for your sector before writing anything. Someone has complained about a comparable project and the outcome tells you what to ask for. WHICH OFFICES EXIST, AND WHERE THE GAPS ARE: the offices it works with include those of the regional development bank for this continent, the world bank's public and private arms, a climate fund, a development programme's compliance unit and one national development bank's ombudsperson; it records that THERE ARE MANY COMMUNITIES THAT LACK AN AVAILABLE ACCOUNTABILITY OPTION BECAUSE NO SUCH ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICE EXISTS AT THE INSTITUTION(S) FINANCING A PROJECT, and works to open avenues where investment has none, INCLUDING IMPACT INVESTMENT, PRIVATE EQUITY, AND FINANCING FROM CHINESE INSTITUTIONS; its advocacy removed a requirement that complainants cite specific policy violations, since PREVIOUSLY A COMPLAINT COULD BE REJECTED IF IT DID NOT CONTAIN THIS TECHNICAL INFORMATION. Identify the financier before assuming there is a complaint office. Where the money is private equity or a Chinese lender there may be none, and that absence is itself worth publicising.

trackers.name: The Latin American Water Funds Partnership - 26 operating water funds in named cities across ten countries, paying for conservation in the catchments that supply them, some composed of INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, with technical accompaniment to create new ones

The alliance behind them PROMOTED THE CREATION OF water funds described as ORGANISATIONS OF COLLECTIVE ACTION THAT DRIVE A SHARED AND LONG-TERM VISION OF WATER SECURITY; twenty-six now operate in cities including named capitals and provincial cities across ten countries, and in one recent year the programme recorded 44,116 HECTARES POSITIVELY IMPACTED WITH 16,271 FAMILIES. Money that flows from a city's water users to the families who keep the upper catchment intact. Where the land you are defending sits above a city's intake, that is the argument with a funding mechanism already attached. WHO SITS INSIDE THEM: the funds WORK CLOSELY WITH THE LOCAL COMMUNITIES, SOME BEING EVEN COMPOSED OF INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, one such fund having won a United Nations equatorial prize; the model is described as PLATFORMS OF GOVERNANCE TO ADDRESS WATER CHALLENGES AND SHARE RESPONSIBILITIES AND ACCOUNTABILITY for society, as EFFECTIVE MECHANISMS TO IMPROVE WATER AVAILABILITY, BIODIVERSITY AND CLIMATE ADAPTATION for governments, and as a way for companies to address RISKS OF PHYSICAL ACCESS TO WATER IN QUALITY AND QUANTITY. A fund composed of indigenous communities is a precedent, not an exception. Ask to see that one's governing documents before agreeing to any structure a utility proposes. WHAT THE ALLIANCE PROVIDES TO A NEW FUND: it supports funds through SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE TO REACH AND MAINTAIN WATER SECURITY WITH NATURE-BASED SOLUTIONS; THE SYSTEMATISATION, MANAGEMENT AND DIFFUSION OF KNOWLEDGE; THE DEVELOPMENT OF CAPACITIES AND TECHNICAL ACCOMPANIMENT; THE PROMOTION OF DIALOGUE BETWEEN RELEVANT ACTORS OF THE REGION IN AN INCLUSIVE MANNER... ACTIVE PARTICIPATION IN THE DESIGN OF WATER GOVERNANCE AND THE MOBILISATION OF RESOURCES FROM PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SOURCES; at one point 15 ADDITIONAL WATER FUNDS were IN THE PROCESS OF CREATION. Technical accompaniment to design the fund and to mobilise the money. A municipality that wants one does not have to invent the model, and fifteen were being built at once. WHO IS BEHIND IT, WHICH DECIDES HOW YOU APPROACH IT: the alliance is AN AGREEMENT CREATED IN 2011 between a regional development bank, a global environment fund, a corporate foundation, an international climate initiative and a global conservation organisation, with A GROWING LIST OF LOCAL PARTNERS and more than two hundred organisations involved. A bottler's foundation and a development bank sit at the same table as the conservation organisation. Read the governance before joining, and be clear what the fund may and may not spend on. WHAT INDIVIDUAL FUNDS HAVE BUILT: recorded innovations include THE FIRST LABORATORY FOR CENTRAL AMERICA OF STABLE ISOTOPES and THE CREATION OF THE BANK CARD FOR WATER CONSERVATION by one national fund; two funds have concentrated on EFFICIENCY IN THE USE OF WATER in agriculture. A stable isotope laboratory can trace where water in a well actually comes from. Where a project is accused of drying a spring, that is the technical service to ask a water fund for.

trackers.name: Caribbean Natural Resources Institute (CANARI) - a regional technical institute with staff in four countries that COACHES community organisations to write proposals and then manages the grants, and sells participatory forest, site planning and protected area management services

Among its listed services is MANAGEMENT OF GRANT PROGRAMMES. Coaching on the proposal, not just a form to fill in. For a small island organisation with no grant writer, that coaching is worth more than the grant. WHAT IT IS AND WHERE ITS PEOPLE ARE: it is A REGIONAL, NON-PROFIT TECHNICAL INSTITUTE WITH MORE THAN 30 YEARS OF DEDICATED EXPERIENCE ACROSS THE COUNTRIES AND TERRITORIES OF THE CARIBBEAN REGION, headquartered in one island capital with staff based in three further countries; it CHAMPION[S] LOCALLY LED APPROACHES TO USING AND MANAGING NATURAL RESOURCES THAT PUT THE NEEDS OF COMMUNITIES FIRST, ESPECIALLY THOSE WHICH ARE OFTEN OVERLOOKED, and promotes CARIBBEAN SOLUTIONS FOR CARIBBEAN CHALLENGES, RECOGNISING THAT THE REGION'S UNIQUE ISSUES REQUIRE HOMEGROWN RESPONSES. Staff living in four countries, not a distant headquarters. For the small islands, where most entries in this file point to bodies far away, this is the regional organisation that is actually present. THE TECHNICAL SERVICES IT SELLS OR PROVIDES: named areas include DEVELOPMENT OF TOOLKITS AND TRAINING IN FACILITATING PARTICIPATORY APPROACHES, PARTICIPATORY FOREST POLICY DEVELOPMENT, SITE PLANNING AND COMMUNITY FORESTRY, PARTICIPATORY PROTECTED AREA POLICY DEVELOPMENT, PLANNING AND MANAGEMENT, CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONAL CAPACITY BUILDING, SUPPORTING DEVELOPMENT OF SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITY SMALL AND MICRO-ENTERPRISES and DEVELOPMENT OF COMMUNICATION STRATEGIES AND PRODUCTS such as case studies and policy briefs. Site planning and protected area management planning are services you can commission. Where a community has been told to produce a management plan it cannot write, this is who writes it with them. WHAT THE MICRO-GRANTS LOOK LIKE: one programme assisted SIX CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS WITH TECHNICAL SUPPORT AND MICRO-GRANTS TO SCALE UP ECOSYSTEM-BASED SOLUTIONS... IN SIX HIGH-RISK COMMUNITIES across three island states, covering HILLSIDE, RIVERBANK, MANGROVE, AND COASTAL VEGETATION RESTORATION; a recent advocacy facility awarded grants RANGING FROM $1,500 TO $8,000 to six organisations for work from recognising women in agriculture and fisheries to DOCUMENTING THE IMPACTS OF HURRICANES and advocating equitable resilience. Fifteen hundred dollars is a real grant here. Hillside and riverbank restoration is exactly the work a community does after a development has destabilised a slope. WHAT IT HAS BUILT WITH OTHERS: it convenes a regional climate justice alliance, implements a forest sector project IN PARTNERSHIP WITH two named national organisations in one island, and has run a project to STRENGTHEN THE TECHNICAL AND FINANCIAL CAPACITY OF SELECTED CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS and to improve understanding of THE INSTITUTIONAL REQUIREMENTS FOR EFFECTIVE CIVIL SOCIETY PARTICIPATION IN NATURAL RESOURCE GOVERNANCE; earlier work included SAFEGUARD[ING] WATERSHEDS THROUGH TARGETED PAYMENTS and participatory forest management across seven islands. trackers.name: Mongabay Latam and the regional environmental journalists' network - a newsroom of 90+ journalists across 14 countries with a published contact for story tips, satellite and data investigations that have INFORMED JUDICIAL AND POLICE ACTION, and an honest account of the risk to sources
trackers.desc: A REGIONAL NEWSROOM OF MORE THAN NINETY ENVIRONMENTAL JOURNALISTS, AND A PUBLISHED EMAIL FOR TAKING A STORY TO THEM. An editor's email address, and community sources treated as principal actors rather than colour. Read the collaboration conditions before writing, then send the documents, not the outrage. WHY COVERAGE CHANGES A LAND FIGHT: the newsroom has built 20-PLUS DATABASES CONTAINING CRITICAL INFORMATION ON MINING, DRUG TRAFFICKING, FINES IMPOSED ON FOSSIL FUEL AND PALM OIL COMPANIES, CASES OF ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDER KILLINGS THAT HAVE GONE UNPUNISHED OR THAT HAVE BEEN PROSECUTED, GEOLOCATED ENVIRONMENTAL LIABILITIES LIKE CONTAMINATED SITES LEFT BEHIND BY THE OIL INDUSTRY, and records that THE FINDINGS HAVE BEEN USED TO INFORM JUDICIAL AND POLICE ACTION; one series analysed MORE THAN 724,000 satellite DEFORESTATION ALERTS... TO DOCUMENT ILLEGAL DEFORESTATION OF INDIGENOUS LANDS in four countries, and a satellite analysis of two protected areas in one country counted alerts inside each before A TEAM OF JOURNALISTS TRAVELLED TO THESE AREAS. Their analysis has fed judicial and police action. A published investigation is not only pressure — it can be the document a prosecutor opens a file on. trackers.name: Legal Aid Agency
trackers.desc: Executive agency of the UK Ministry of Justice administering civil and criminal legal aid for England & Wales. · Find here: the body administering legal aid in England & Wales (Legal Aid Agency). IT FACES THREE SEPARATE TESTS — scope, means, and merits or interests of justice — and most people plan for means and are defeated by scope. THE SCOPE LOGIC REVERSED IN 2013: before April 2013, under the Access to Justice Act 1999, legal aid was available in any matter of English or Welsh law unless specifically excluded. Under LASPO 2012 a case must now come within the types of dispute listed in Part 1 of Schedule 1, with Part 2 listing express exclusions. So the question is not ‘is my case excluded’ but ‘is my case listed’ — which is why pre-2013 guidance misleads. WHAT IS IN: judicial review is a category for which means-tested legal aid can be available, alongside Human Rights Act claims — the route most environmental challenges take. IF YOU ARE OUT OF SCOPE: Exceptional Case Funding under section 10(3) or 10(4) of LASPO — but providers have no delegated power to grant it: under regulation 67(2)(a) of the Civil Legal Aid (Procedure) Regulations 2012 a written application goes to the Director of Legal Aid Casework for an exceptional case determination. TREAT IT AS A LONG SHOT, NOT A FALLBACK: Law Society evidence to Parliament states the discretion will be exercised sparingly and slowly and does not cover cases settled between refusal and renewal of a permission application. ASK ABOUT PROTECTIVE COSTS ORDERS in public law cases, and about the Aarhus costs regime for environmental challenges. The LAA has been an executive agency of the Ministry of Justice since 1 April 2013, replacing the Legal Services Commission.

trackers.name: John Muir Trust — wild land ownership and community buy-outs
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a conservation charity that protects wild land across the UK both by owning estates directly and by backing community buy-outs of land that comes up for sale. USE IT: for upland, wild and Scottish estate land — they buy, and they put money and weight behind communities trying to buy. IT HELPS OTHERS BUY, RATHER THAN BUYING AND HOLDING FOR YOU — grasp that before you approach it. Its record is a list of other bodies' purchases that it enabled: a major contributor to the Knoydart Foundation purchase (1999); helped Borders Forest Trust buy Carrifran woodland (2000); supported the North Harris Community buy-out of the 55,000-acre North Harris Estate (2002); a key role in the Assynt Foundation's purchase of Glencanisp and Drumrunie (2005); supported the Galson Estate Trust on North Lewis (2007); and supported the Langholm community buyout (2020). Six community buyouts across 21 years — and in every case the land ended up with the community body, not with the Trust. THE PLANNING HOOK IS THE MOST ACTIONABLE FACT HERE: in 2014 the Scottish Government adopted the Wild Land Areas map into planning policy — so a proposal inside a mapped area meets an existing policy objection rather than one you must construct. Establish first whether your site falls within a Wild Land Area. A REPLICABLE ARRANGEMENT: the Trust is recorded as the only external representative on the North Harris Trust, the community body managing that estate — a single external seat on a community landowner's board is a specific thing to propose. It works with crofters, landowners, other organisations and charities, manages estates of its own in the Highlands and Islands, and is a Scottish charitable company limited by guarantee based in Pitlochry, founded 1983. The John Muir Award (1997) exists to connect people with wild places that feel accessible to them — a route to people who do not already identify as conservationists. NOT TO BE CONFUSED with the John Muir Land Trust (jmlt.org), an unrelated California land trust.

trackers.name: Environmental Law Foundation (ELF)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a UK public-interest environmental law organisation that connects communities and individuals with legal help on environmental and planning matters. WHO IT SUITS: a community or individual affected by a development, a pollution source or the loss of green space, who needs to find out whether there is a legal route at all — and who could run it.

trackers.name: ClientEarth — environmental law charity
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an environmental law charity of roughly 250 lawyers and experts that goes to court to enforce environmental law against governments and companies, with around 168 active cases and offices in London, Brussels, Warsaw, Berlin, Madrid, Beijing and Tokyo. Won the case forcing the UK government to admit it was breaching legal air-pollution limits. WHO IT SUITS: systemic or precedent-setting challenges rather than a single local application — they pick cases that change the rules for everyone.

trackers.name: Rewilding Britain — Rewilding Innovation Fund and buyout support
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the Rewilding Innovation Fund has awarded more than half a million pounds to dozens of rewilding initiatives across Britain since 2021, and the charity has put money behind community land buyouts (it helped fund the Langholm crowdfunder). WHO IT SUITS: restoration and rewilding projects in Britain, and communities preparing a buyout. HOW IT DIFFERS: it also publishes the legislation, subsidy and tax guides you need BEFORE taking land out of intensive use — do that homework first.

trackers.name: The Rivers Trust — find your local Rivers Trust
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the umbrella body for 65+ INDEPENDENT member Rivers Trusts across Britain, Northern Ireland and Ireland, each covering its own river catchment. Members restore waterways, run citizen-science monitoring, and drive policy change; the umbrella holds catchment data and expertise. USE IT: the map finds the trust for your catchment. Two reasons to go here rather than to a county body — rivers cross county lines, so a catchment trust may be the only organisation whose remit matches the actual impact area of a development; and they hold long-run water-quality monitoring data, which is documentary evidence a planning objection can rest on. Scotland and Wales have sister bodies (Fisheries Management Scotland, Afonydd Cymru).

trackers.name: National Lottery Heritage Fund — heritage grants
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the UK's largest heritage funder, awarding £10,000 to £10 million across the whole country. NATURE IS EXPLICITLY IN SCOPE — eligible heritage covers natural habitats and landscapes alongside buildings and archives, and funding can pay for capital works, staff posts, professional fees, conservation and volunteer costs. WHO IT SUITS: not-for-profit organisations, partnerships led by one, and — for the £10k–£250k tier only — private owners of a heritage asset who can show significant public benefit. HOW IT DIFFERS: three things decide whether it is worth your time. Applications are ROLLING, not to a deadline. You must bring MATCH FUNDING — at least 5% for grants under £1m, 10% above. And for requests up to £250,000 you can submit a Project Enquiry and get feedback on the idea WITHIN TEN WORKING DAYS, which is the cheapest way to find out if your project fits before writing anything. Note the limit: community sub-grants you pass on to others cannot be used to acquire land.

You CAN'T get: Scotland (SEPA), Wales (NRW) or Northern Ireland registers — separate systems.
