Fundación Global Nature is one of the largest operators: it reports work with almost 200 owners under 179 agreements covering about 23,700 hectares across six autonomous communities. Nationally the inventory kept by Fundación Biodiversidad counts more than 225 custodia entities, some 3,100 agreements and close to 600,000 hectares. USE IT: two facts change what a Spanish community does. A municipality can itself be the custodia entity, not merely the owner — the national inventory records 23 municipalities signed up as entities across 151 agreements on more than 2,000 hectares, and 466 agreements struck on public patrimonial land. And the agreement may be verbal or written, which lowers the threshold for a first conversation with an owner considerably. THE TRAP, AND READ THE CAVEAT WITH IT: custodia agreements are also being used as the vehicle for the compensation packages attached to renewable-energy consents. The Castilla-La Mancha regional government has described a custodia contract with this same foundation covering 1,570 hectares of agri-environmental measures as compensation for steppe habitat taken by eighteen photovoltaic plants from six developers across four municipalities. Ask any custodia entity you approach whether it already holds a compensation contract tied to the project you are fighting. That account comes from regional government statements and I could not confirm it on the foundation's own site — verify before relying on it. Published totals for this foundation vary widely between sources and dates, from around 9,000 to 26,000 hectares and from 157 to 470 owners, and it holds only a few hundred hectares outright: its scale is in agreements, not in ownership.

trackers.name: Fundación Naturaleza y Hombre — Spain's buyer, in three tiers (Spain)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a foundation created in 1994 which, unlike most Spanish custodia entities, buys land outright as well as making agreements. Its Reserva Biológica Campanarios de Azaba in the Azaba valley, Salamanca, is more than 600 hectares the Foundation acquired, and its Iberian West programme is explicit that the method is land purchase plus active management agreements, working towards 6,000 hectares under conservation management across Salamanca, Zamora and Cáceres and into Portugal. THE THREE TIERS, WHICH ARE THE USEFUL PART: it works through reservas municipales, agreed with town councils and juntas vecinales; reservas voluntarias, agreed with private owners; and reservas en propiedad, where the Foundation itself is the owner. A community can therefore approach it about common land held by the council, about a neighbour's finca, or about a parcel for sale, and there is an existing route for each. Its Club de Fincas gathers owners across Salamanca, Cáceres and Portugal, so an owner who signs is joining something rather than signing something alone — which is usually the easier ask. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR SPAIN SPECIFICALLY: purchase is rare here. Spanish custodia entities buy only occasionally, and the largest of them holds a few hundred hectares outright against tens of thousands under agreement. If your case needs the land taken off the market rather than managed in place, the number of Spanish bodies that will do it is small and this is one of them. WHAT TO BRING: dehesa, Mediterranean woodland, cereal steppe and river canyon in the Iberian West are its ground. It has also built reserves in Cantabria in the Alto Pas and Miera valleys. Outside those areas it is a longer conversation.

trackers.name: Fundació Catalunya La Pedrera — owns a network of 27 natural spaces (Catalonia)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: it owns land. Its Xarxa d'Espais Natura is a network of natural spaces it describes as acquired in order to preserve and manage places of great ecological value, and which it calls a model unique in Catalonia and Spain — 27 spaces, of which it jointly manages 20 with other bodies. Its holdings include the Mont-rebei gorge, the Alinyà mountain, the Ivars i Vila-sana lake and the Tavertet cliffs. It descends from the Fundació Territori i Paisatge, which was set up on the British and American land-trust model and whose director's summary of the approach was simply: buy in order to conserve. READ THE TWO NUMBERS CAREFULLY, BECAUSE THEY ARE OFTEN CONFUSED: in its first decade of stewardship work it reached more than 70 advisory agreements covering over 160,000 hectares in Catalonia, about 5% of the country. Those were advisory. Its current stewardship agreements amount to 82 hectares. The 160,000 figure circulates widely and means something quite different from what a community will assume. What is solid is the owned network and 33 forest preserves under stewardship covering a further 200 hectares or so. WHAT IT IS DOING NOW THAT YOU CAN ASK FOR: between 2023 and 2026 it carried out forestry work across twelve of its own and custodied spaces — 341 hectares treated, 189 of them at strategic points for fire management, 30 kilometres of forest track improved, eight water points restored, 44 hectares of agroforestry mosaic recovered and twelve extensive livestock holdings supported. It also works in Collserola, where more than 60% of the massif is privately owned, on restoring farmhouses and putting agricultural, forestry and grazing uses back into the mosaic. If your case is a Catalan site that needs an owner or a working partner rather than a lawyer, this is the largest one there is.

trackers.name: Fundación Lurgaia — every euro raised goes to buying the land (Basque Country)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Basque foundation recovering Atlantic forest, chiefly in the Urdaibai Biosphere Reserve, which buys the ground it works on. It states that the money from its campaigns and from members' subscriptions normally goes entirely to buying land and the costs directly associated with the purchase, and that it negotiates and deals directly with the private owners, so beyond the obligatory notary costs there are no intermediaries. Almost nothing else in this file says where the donations actually go, and this is the clearest statement of it I have found. THE PATTERN TO COPY: its first custodia agreement, in 2008 at Undabaso in Muxika, came from a family who owned pine and eucalyptus plantations and decided they wanted to live surrounded by native woodland. From that one agreement it has kept acquiring adjoining ground — past 230 hectares in that one place, and more than 870 hectares in recovery across the Cantabrian coast. It runs open campaigns with a stated target and a stated price: 105 hectares managed, 153 wanted, €45,000 needed. A community can see exactly what its field would cost. IT DOES NOT ALWAYS NEED THE TITLE: it says that in some custodia agreements ownership stays with the owner and Lurgaia does the management and the recovery. So an owner who will not sell still has a route, and the conversation does not have to start with a price. WHERE IT WORKS: Urdaibai and the Cantabrian cornice, on ground currently under pine and eucalyptus. Native woodland recovery is the purpose; a site that does not fit that is a longer conversation.

trackers.name: GOB Menorca Custòdia Agrària — keeps farmers farming the protected land
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: an agreement programme between Menorcan farm managers and GOB Menorca, described by GOB as a pact of mutual help rather than a restriction — the farmers commit to managing the land with respect for nature, and GOB channels support of various kinds to them in return, on the reasoning that the only thing that keeps sustainable management in place is the economic viability of the farm. It runs alongside a renewed agreement with the island council. Forty-three custodia agreements now cover 2,740 hectares, about 3.9% of Menorca. THE PART THAT IS ACTUALLY UNUSUAL: it publishes a catalogue and a map of the participating farms with their products and direct contacts, so the public can buy from them at the farm, at markets, in shops or by delivery. The conservation is funded by people buying the food. For a community anywhere arguing that protection and farming are compatible, this is a working island-scale demonstration with numbers attached: GOB reports the beef from custodia farms carrying an ecological footprint up to 64% below the national average, partly because much of this land would not be considered optimal by conventional agriculture at all and works as a mosaic of crops and wild vegetation. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer. Menorca only. If the fight is over a farm whose owner would keep farming under an agreement, this is the route; if the land has to change hands, it is not.

trackers.name: Xarxa per a la Conservació de la Natura (XCN) — the Catalan custodia network
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a second-level non-profit declared of public utility, formed in February 2019 by the merger of the Xarxa de Custòdia del Territori, itself constituted in March 2003, with the Catalan environmental volunteering network. Its members are the custodia entities themselves — associations, foundations, public administrations, companies, universities and research centres — more than 170 of them at the merger. Its stated job is to represent and support the organisations working on natural, cultural and landscape heritage, and to provide information, training, advice, support and research in favour of custodia. WHY A CATALAN COMMUNITY SHOULD START HERE: Spain's conservation sector runs on custodia agreements rather than purchase, and the entity that will take on your site is a local one you have never heard of. This is the body that knows which of the 170 covers your comarca and your habitat. Its own project pages name working custodia organisations across the territory — Fundació Emys, Sambucus, Eixarcolant, the Grup d'Estudi i Protecció dels Ecosistemes Catalans, La Sínia, Grup Natura Freixe, the Associació per a la Conservació dels Ecosistemes Naturals, the Societat Catalana d'Herpetologia, and Fundació Catalunya La Pedrera, which is already in this file as a landowner. A SPECIFIC ROUTE WORTH KNOWING: it runs a river custodia programme, more than ten years old, aimed at getting new custòdia fluvial agreements signed and at improving the administrative and legal side of those agreements. If the threatened ground is a riverbank, Catalonia has a decade-old dedicated programme for exactly that. ALSO: it keeps the inventory of custodia agreements and entities across Catalonia, the Balearics and Andorra, and it runs public-facing events including a nature week and a charity race, which are ways for a local group to make itself visible cheaply. WHAT IT IS NOT: a network, not an ally. It does not buy land, fund campaigns or take cases. Its members do the first two.

trackers.name: ORGACCMM — the Galician commons communities: 700,000 hectares the neighbours own
trackers.desc: WHAT THE UNDERLYING THING IS, because it changes everything for a Galician community: a monte veciñal en man común is collective private property owned by the whole body of neighbours with an open house and habitual residence in the parish or settlement where the mount lies. Under the Galician law of 1989 these lands are inalienable, indivisible, unseizable and imprescriptible — they cannot be bought or sold, cannot be divided among the neighbours, cannot be seized, and cannot be acquired by long possession. Around a quarter of Galicia — some 650,000 to 700,000 hectares — is held this way by roughly 2,800 to 3,000 communities of montes, with Ourense holding the most and large areas in Lugo and Pontevedra. The same institution exists in western Asturias, western León and Zamora. WHY THIS IS THE MOST POWERFUL ENTRY IN THIS FILE FOR THE RIGHT COMMUNITY: if the threatened ground is a monte veciñal, the neighbours are the owners, decisions are taken by assembly with a Xunta Reitora as managing body, and anyone who moves to live in that parish joins the community and takes part in the decisions. There is no need to buy the land, form a trust or find standing. The land legally cannot be sold out from under them. ORGACCMM is the Galician organisation of these communities and it fights their corner in public — on councils wrongly charging property tax on montes veciñais despite the exemption and two superior court rulings, on debts the regional agriculture department generated under consortium arrangements and then billed to communities, on so-called temporary public management contracts that it argues hand community forests to private forestry firms, and on eucalyptus planting moratoria. That is a body already litigating the exact question of who controls community forest. IF THE COMMUNITY LAPSED, IT CAN BE RESTARTED: the procedure is documented — prove a neighbour community of full-right comuneiros exists, elect a provisional board, have that board undertake before a notary to assume the mount's accounts and management instrument, and apply for management to revert to the neighbours. Statutes and a governing board must follow within a year. THE PORTUGUESE EQUIVALENT is the baldío, recognised in the Constitution of the Portuguese Republic, with BALADI — Federação Nacional dos Baldíos — as the national federation. Its representatives have warned that regulatory change puts the baldíos under threat of disappearing.

trackers.name: SEO/BirdLife Grupos Locales — 44 local groups that file alegaciones, and you can start one
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: Spain's oldest conservation NGO, founded 1954, with 44 to 45 Grupos Locales across the country, a headquarters in Madrid and delegations in Aragón, Andalucía, the Canaries, Cantabria, Catalonia, Extremadura and Valencia plus offices at Doñana and the Ebro Delta. It mobilises more than 20,000 volunteers a year. Spain's bucket had four land buyers and a legal institute but nothing producing the species record. THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR A PLANNING FIGHT: in one recent year the Grupos Locales carried out more than 40 actions relating to alegaciones, reports and advice on conservation matters — alegaciones being the formal objections filed in Spanish administrative procedures. That is a standing, distributed capacity to object, staffed by volunteers, in 44 places. AND YOU CAN START ONE WHERE THERE ISN'T ONE: the map of active groups carries each one's contact details, area of operation and main activities. If a group of you want to work on the birds and nature of your area you can form a Grupo Local; the stated minimum is six people, and if you cannot reach six SEO will help you organise a meeting or field day — you draft the invitation, they forward it to members across your province and neighbouring ones, since data protection prevents them handing over member details. A community can convert itself into a recognised local branch of a national organisation. THE MONITORING BEHIND IT, which is what gives an objection weight: SACRE for common breeding birds since 1996, SACIN for winter, NOCTUA for nocturnal birds, wintering-bird atlases, a phenology network and ringing through the Centro de Migración de Aves, run by over a thousand volunteers under protocols analysed statistically under the same protocol in every participating country. It also maintains the Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas (IBA) inventory for Spain, and its Catalan delegation's work on the Lleida dry farmland ended in those areas being included as ZEPA within the Natura 2000 network.

trackers.name: Ley 27/2006 acción popular — two years old, and your association can sue on its own
trackers.desc: THE THREE REQUIREMENTS, AND THEY ARE SHORT: under article 23, any non-profit legal person may exercise the environmental acción popular of article 22 if (a) its statutes include among its accredited aims the protection of the environment in general or of one of its elements in particular, (b) it was legally constituted at least two years before exercising the action and has been actively carrying out the activities needed to achieve those statutory aims, and (c) it operates in the territorial area affected by the act or omission challenged. WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN FINDING AN ALLY: no membership threshold, no accreditation by a ministry, no public-utility status required. A residents' association with the right sentence in its statutes and two years of real activity has legal standing in its own name to make the administration comply with environmental law. The law's own explanation is that it enshrines standing to protect a diffuse interest in favour of organisations whose social object is precisely the protection of natural resources. Spain's bucket had four land buyers and a legal institute; this is what a group can do without any of them. AND THE COMPLEMENTARY ROUTE, because administrations sometimes get this wrong: environmental acción pública under Ley 27/2006 and standing to defend collective interests under article 31.2 of Ley 39/2015 and article 19.1 of the LJCA are not mutually exclusive but complementary. Being refused on one basis does not settle the other. THE LEGAL AID POSITION, RECORDED HONESTLY BECAUSE IT IS CONTESTED: article 23.2 gives these associations the right to free legal assistance in the terms of Ley 1/1996 — and the majority position of the Andalusian provincial commissions is that the right is not enjoyed ex lege, so an association must still demonstrate insufficient economic resources to litigate. The regional ombudsman has argued the opposite and pressed for a uniform criterion. Expect to argue for it rather than to receive it. SO THE PRACTICAL ADVICE IS ONE SENTENCE: put environmental protection in your statutes, and start the clock — the two years cannot be recovered later.

trackers.name: Fundación Biodiversidad — 60 per cent paid up front, and local groups qualify via networks
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the foundation of the Spanish environment ministry (MITECO), which periodically calls competitive ayudas for activities in biodiversity, climate change and sustainable development. Scale in one year: the board approved more than 73 million euro across four calls, including 39.6 million for bioeconomy projects of up to three years fostering sustainable land uses and the conservation of natural resources in rural settings, and 6 million for marine conservation research. WHO CAN APPLY, AND THE ROUTE IN FOR A SMALL GROUP: non-profit entities and organisations of state or Community scope, OR of regional or local scope provided they take part in networks or programmes of state or Community character — with a seat in Spain, legally constituted and entered in the corresponding register. A local association qualifies by belonging to a network. That is the same routing solution the Netherlands uses with its collectives, in a different form, and it is the answer for a group too small to apply alone. Public research bodies, public universities, and local administrations integrated in state or Community networks are also eligible. THE TERMS THAT MAKE IT USABLE: co-financing up to 95 per cent, with advances of 60 per cent at the start of the project and a further 20 per cent once partial justification shows at least 50 per cent of planned spending executed. Against Portugal's pure reimbursement and Austria's 20 per cent start instalment, this is the most generous cash flow recorded in this sweep. Projects have run to a maximum of four years. AND IT PUSHES YOU TO PARTNER: projects should preferably be developed through groupings of beneficiaries that contribute to solvency and cooperation between entities, and one marine call took groupings of up to four entities. Note the common restriction: only ONE application per entity in several calls. SPECIFIC LINES SEEN: marine green infrastructure and protected space management; strandings and marine species rescue networks at 50,000 to 400,000 euro; CITES rescue centres up to 200,000 euro; urban renaturalisation through green infrastructure and connectivity; and support for environmental and social non-profits at 100,000 to 500,000 euro in a disaster recovery call.

trackers.name: Keatia — a Spanish directory of urbanism lawyers by city, WITH the going rates published
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a directory for comparing profiles and quotes of urbanism lawyers city by city, which publishes the going rates so a group knows what it is walking into. Spain had 47 filed entries and no lawyer at all. THE RATES, AS PUBLISHED: initial consultation 60–150 euro; written legal opinion 300–900; administrative appeal 600–1,500; and a contencioso-administrativo before the Madrid courts usually 2,000–6,000, plus procurador and any experts. Many practices quote by phases and require a provision of funds, and it advises: always ask for the engagement letter and an itemised breakdown — VAT, procurador, fees where applicable. Third country in this file where the cost of fighting is on the record, after Italy and France. AND THE STRATEGY IT SETS OUT FOR CHALLENGING A PLAN, which tells you what your lawyer will need from you: it is key to check WHETHER YOU TOOK PART IN THE PUBLIC INFORMATION STAGE (alegaciones) and the date of publication, because the deadlines are strict — usually two months. The work then covers analysis of the memoria, the environmental assessment, the sectoral reports, the reasoning, and compatibility with state and regional legislation, and interim measures can be sought if there is immediate execution. Its advice in one line: act early and with a specialised lawyer.

trackers.name: Spanish urbanism practices — who takes the neighbour's side, and how long it really takes
trackers.desc: WHAT THESE PRACTICES DO FOR SOMEONE FIGHTING A SCHEME, from their own service lists: impugnación of plans and urban regulations — alegaciones and recursos to the urban plan itself; administrative and contencioso-administrativo appeals on discipline, coercive fines, DEMOLITION ORDERS OR THE HALTING OF WORKS; defence of the justiprecio, impugning the administration's valuation; REVERSION AND RETASACIÓN — recovery of the expropriated property or updating of its value; and patrimonial liability of the administration, claiming damages caused by illegal or defective urbanistic actions. Reversion — getting expropriated land back — is a named service in Spain, and so is claiming against the council for an unlawful scheme. THE TIMES, SO NOBODY PLANS ON HOPE: from lodging the claim to first-instance judgment in the Madrid contencioso-administrativo chamber usually takes 18 to 30 MONTHS; a later cassation appeal can add 18 to 24 more. The general deadline is two months from notification, and the definitive approval of a general urban plan, once published, can be challenged directly before the regional high court within two months. AND ONE WORKED CASE FROM THE OTHER SIDE, filed as a conflict warning: a Barcelona practice advertises that a neighbour impugned its client's licence as soon as construction began, alleging the maximum permitted height was breached — and the practice defeated it. Check whose side a firm usually takes before instructing.

trackers.name: Fundación Biodiversidad — and the flood-restoration call that pays for NATURE-BASED SOLUTIONS
trackers.desc: WHAT IT FUNDS AND AT WHAT SCALE: a disaster-recovery call with a global maximum of 5,000,000 EURO, split across two axes — Axis 1, RESILIENT ECOSYSTEMS, between 350,000 and 1,000,000 euro per project; Axis 2, SUPPORT TO NON-PROFIT ENTITIES OF AN ENVIRONMENTAL AND/OR SOCIAL CHARACTER, between 100,000 and 500,000. Spain had 49 filed entries and three funders. An axis that funds the ORGANISATION rather than only the project is what keeps a body alive to fight the next one — here expressly to reinforce their environmental work and contribute to maintaining and creating green employment. AND A SECOND CALL WORTH KNOWING ABOUT WHEREVER FLOODING IS THE ARGUMENT: the same foundation funds actions directed at THE RESTORATION OF FLUVIAL ECOSYSTEMS AND THE REDUCTION OF FLOOD RISK IN SPANISH URBAN ENVIRONMENTS THROUGH NATURE-BASED SOLUTIONS, requiring projects whose results must themselves be DURABLE IN TIME and generate a positive socio-economic impact. AND THE ELIGIBILITY SHAPE TO NOTE: non-profit entities can be beneficiaries provided they join GROUPINGS alongside at least one qualifying public body, which acts as representative — and where local authorities form part of a grouping, they must be NEIGHBOURING and share a common project. Some money is only reachable by applying jointly with your own council.

trackers.name: Comprar para conservar — the Spanish record of buying land outright, since the 1960s
trackers.desc: THE PRECEDENTS, and they are old enough to settle any argument about whether this works: in the 1960s a recently created WWF BOUGHT SEVERAL THOUSAND HECTARES in a named marshland to save them from the advance of agricultural industrialisation, WITH MONEY RAISED INTERNATIONALLY THROUGH PRIVATE DONATIONS. Those lands would later form THE HEART OF THE FUTURE NATIONAL PARK. Land bought by donation became the core of a national park — which is the answer to anyone who says buying a field cannot lead anywhere. OTHER ORGANISATIONS DID THE SAME: a Balearic group acquired a named estate in 1980 to devote it to a nature reserve; an Extremadura body began in the same year to create A NETWORK OF RESERVES THROUGH AGREEMENTS WITH THE OWNERS of the estates; and another was founded in 1988 with the intention of BUYING RIVERSIDE WOODLAND to restore and conserve it. AND THE HONEST LIMIT, from a foundation director: buying land is one part of the broader tool that is land stewardship, but for farmland we would have to buy thousands of hectares and become producers to protect significant areas by purchase, and we do not have those resources — so agreements with farmers and graziers are the main strategy, and owned land is used as PILOT FARMS demonstrating sustainable techniques and recovering traditional seeds and livestock breeds.

trackers.name: A RESIDENTS' ASSOCIATION can be the custodian — who may hold land in Spain
trackers.desc: THE LIST THAT MATTERS MOST TO A SPANISH COMMUNITY, because it puts them on it: custody bodies are NON-PROFIT ORGANISATIONS, PUBLIC OR PRIVATE, THAT PARTICIPATE ACTIVELY IN THE CONSERVATION OF THE TERRITORY UNDER CUSTODY, and ORGANISATIONS AS DIVERSE AS A RESIDENTS' ASSOCIATION, A CONSERVATIONIST ORGANISATION, A FOUNDATION, A TOWN COUNCIL, A CONSORTIUM AND OTHER KINDS OF PUBLIC BODIES CAN ACT AS A CUSTODY ENTITY. Spain had four acquisition entries against 51 total. A neighbourhood association can itself be the body that holds and protects the land — no foundation needs to be created and no national organisation persuaded first. AND WHAT AN OWNER GETS OUT OF IT: FOR PRIVATE PROPERTY, GETTING INVOLVED IN CUSTODY INITIATIVES OFFERS AN OPPORTUNITY TO LOOK AFTER THEIR TERRITORY WITH TECHNICAL AND FINANCIAL SUPPORT. Technical and financial support, not just a restriction, is what is being offered to the owner — which is the version of the ask that gets a hearing. In Spain THE OWNERSHIP OF LAND UNDER CUSTODY IS MAINLY PRIVATE, ALTHOUGH AGREEMENTS ARE ALSO FORMALISED ON PUBLIC OR COMMUNAL LAND. AND THE NAMED PARTNERSHIP BEHIND THE CURRENT PUSH, useful because each partner is a door: a national biodiversity foundation coordinates a European-funded custody project IN WHICH EUROSITE, THE FORUM OF NETWORKS AND ENTITIES OF LAND CUSTODY, a named GLOBAL NATURE FOUNDATION, a named UNIVERSITY FOUNDATION, a BIRDLIFE PARTNER AND A CATALAN NATURE CONSERVATION NETWORK TAKE PART AS PARTNERS.

trackers.name: The custody agreements ladder — from advice-for-management all the way to SELLING the parcel
trackers.desc: THE RANGE OF AGREEMENTS AVAILABLE, set out as a ladder a community can walk an owner up: they RANGE FROM A PACT BETWEEN THE OWNER AND THE CUSTODY ENTITY TO MANAGE A GIVEN ESTATE ON SUSTAINABLE CRITERIA IN EXCHANGE FOR ADVICE, THROUGH TO THE SALE OF THE PARCEL ITSELF SO THAT THE CUSTODY ENTITY DEVOTES IT EXCLUSIVELY TO THE CONSERVATION OF THE NATURAL HABITAT. IN OTHER CASES THEY ARE AGREEMENTS TO LIMIT EXPLOITATION. The lightest rung costs the owner nothing and gains them free advice; the heaviest is an outright sale — and an owner who refuses the last will often accept the first. AND THE PRECEDENTS IT NAMES, which show how long this has worked: a well-known naturalist, as president of a national conservation body, WAS A PIONEER IN SPAIN IN INTRODUCING THIS KIND OF EXPERIENCE BY CREATING IN 1974 A RAPTOR REFUGE, THANKS TO MANAGEMENT AGREEMENTS REACHED WITH THE LOCAL BODIES. Then A MALLORCAN GROUP ACQUIRED A NAMED ESTATE IN 1980 TO DEDICATE IT TO A NATURE RESERVE, and in the same year another association BEGAN THE CREATION OF A NETWORK OF RESERVES BY MEANS OF AGREEMENTS WITH THE OWNERS OF THE ESTATES. A network of reserves built from agreements rather than purchases is the cheapest route to scale, and one Madrid foundation holds agreements with large estate owners EXCEEDING 82,000 HECTARES.

trackers.name: Xarxa per a la Conservació de la Natura (XCN)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the Catalan network of environmental NGOs, foundations, public administrations, universities and companies that drives custòdia del territori — its member entities act as the custody organisation for participating fincas, holding the agreement that keeps land in conservation. Formed in 2019 by the merger of the environmental-volunteering network XVAC with the Xarxa de Custòdia del Territori, which was founded in 2003 and was the first network of its kind in Spain. Maintains the Catalan inventory of custody agreements and entities. USE IT: to find the custody entity that can take on a threatened finca in Catalonia, and to reach the owner-side of the deal — custòdia works by voluntary agreement with the landowner, so it needs a willing seller or holder, not a fight.

trackers.name: National Transparency Authority (NTA) — lobbying register
trackers.desc: National Transparency Authority (NTA) — lobbying register — Greece’s official register of those paid to lobby ministers and government agencies. — Holds to account: who influences Greece’s executive — find lobbyist registrations and activity.

trackers.name: Hellenic Data Protection Authority (HDPA)
trackers.desc: Hellenic Data Protection Authority (HDPA) — Greece’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Areios Pagos (Supreme Court)
trackers.desc: Official site of Greece's Supreme Civil and Criminal Court, with judgments browsable/searchable (English interface covers 2006 onwards). · Find here: decisions of Greece's Supreme Civil and Criminal Court (Areios Pagos).

trackers.name: arthro5A.gr — FOI requests (GRC)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); arthro5A.gr — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: Justice and Environment — European green-law network
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the European network of environmental-law NGOs, whose national member here is Greek Helsinki Monitor. Its fifteen members act as the environmental-law service point in their own countries, taking cases and intervening in legislative processes, while the network defends communities and nature in court and lodges infringement complaints against member-state governments. Its standing themes are access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, environmental assessment and pollution control. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who does not yet know which lawyer to call — knock on Greek Helsinki Monitor's door first, and use the network only if your problem crosses a border. The network itself does not take individual cases; its members do. YOUR NATIONAL MEMBER IS Greek Helsinki Monitor (greekhelsinki.wordpress.com) — go to them, not to the network. J&E members serve as environmental law ‘service points’ in their countries, handling cases, participating in legislative processes and sometimes providing legal analyses and consultations for national governments. The network has 11 full and 4 associate members, and can launch infringement proceedings against faulty governments — a route a national body alone does not have. CURRENT SCOPE: access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, climate, environmental assessments, and the Environmental Liability Directive. It previously worked on waste, transport, health and Natura 2000, so an older document may overstate what it covers today.

trackers.name: General Commercial Registry (G.E.MI.)
trackers.desc: registration authority

trackers.name: Court of Audit (Elegktiko Synedrio)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Greece, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: data.gov.gr
trackers.desc: National — Greek government open data portal. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Greece.

trackers.name: GEMI (Business Registry)
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: companies in Greece — find the General Commercial Registry (GEMI) of entities and filings.

trackers.name: Register of Beneficial Owners (Single Digital Portal)
trackers.desc: Register of Beneficial Owners (Single Digital Portal) — Greece’s beneficial-ownership register, disclosing the real individuals who ultimately own or control companies. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A PLAIN COMPANY REGISTRY: this names the real HUMAN owners behind a company; a company registry names only the legal entity, its directors and filings. Use the registry first to find the entity, then this to pierce the shell to the people who profit. — Holds to account: the hidden owners behind firms dealing with Greece’s government — find beneficial-owner filings.

trackers.name: Pothen Esches – Asset Declarations
trackers.desc: Legislator / public-official financial interest & asset declarations.

trackers.name: Promitheus (KIMDIS/ESIDIS)
trackers.desc: Greece's national electronic public-procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Greece, and for how much.

trackers.name: Reporters United
trackers.desc: Greek investigative newsroom exposing corruption, surveillance and the abuse of public power.

trackers.name: Hellenic Statistical Authority (ELSTAT)
trackers.desc: Greece's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Greece.

trackers.name: Πράσινο Ταμείο — your statutory purposes decide eligibility
trackers.desc: GREECE'S GREEN FUND, established under Law 3889/2010, finances exclusively through published financing programmes structured as priority axes → measures → actions. WHO QUALIFIES IS A TEST OF YOUR OWN CONSTITUTION: Article 6(1) allows financing of associations or other unions of legal and natural persons which, according to their statutory purposes, aim at the protection, upgrading and restoration of the environment. A recent programme spells it out further — NGOs operating as non-profit Σωματεία, ΑΜΚΕ, charitable foundations, ΚΟΙΝΣΕΠ or Σύλλογοι that include in their statutory purposes protection and management of the natural and built environment and/or protection of wild species. THAT IS NOW 4 COUNTRIES IN THIS MAP — with Finland, Italy and Poland — where the wording of your constitution is the gate. Write environmental protection into your statutory purposes before you need the money. The Fund's own vocabulary works with the idea of a green natural solution: an intervention based on nature, using natural processes and ecosystems to address environmental, social and economic issues — frame proposals in those terms.

trackers.name: Where the Greek money actually is — and it is mostly municipal
trackers.desc: KNOW WHICH POT YOU ARE AIMING AT. The Green Fund announced about EUR 123.3 million in credits across its programmes for 2026 — but the largest single instrument, «Δράσεις Περιβαλλοντικού Ισοζυγίου» 2025–2026, carries EUR 79,177,351 and is addressed to all 332 municipalities, not to NGOs, with its budget up EUR 25 million on the previous call. So the biggest money is municipal: if your council can be persuaded to apply, that is the larger route. THE NGO INSTRUMENT IS SMALLER BUT REAL: «Καινοτόμες Δράσεις με τους Πολίτες» offered EUR 1 million in total, up to EUR 50,000 per project across about 20 projects, open to ΜΚΟ, ΑΜΚΕ, ΚΟΙΝΣΕΠ and charitable foundations or their partnerships with local authorities and universities. TWO SCORING CRITERIA TO BUILD IN: that the project is supported by broader public sector bodies — local government, environmental education centres, research institutes — with a letter of support attached; and that the methodology embeds technical, organisational or social innovation and creates synergies with other local actions or wider programmes.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: WWF Greece — Citizens' Legal Support Team (Nomiki Omada)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: WWF Greece runs a volunteer Citizens' Legal Support Team — Nomiki Omada Ypostiρixis Politon — which answered more than 700 environmental-degradation cases in its first ten years and was decorated for it by the President of the Republic in 2009. At an earlier milestone it published its own tally as 500 cases in seven years. USE IT: but read the limit it states in writing before you build a plan on it. The team will help you document a complaint to the authorities; it will not bring the legal action instead of you. What it asks for is a written, signed report setting out the problem and every step you have already taken, with photographs, drawings, map extracts and whatever other evidence exists — because it does not make site visits and cannot go and look for itself. Two things nobody expects to find here. Where revealing the complainant's identity could carry serious consequences, the team will itself handle the correspondence with the public services on WWF Greece's behalf, which is the route for someone who cannot be seen to object. And priority goes to WWF Greece supporters because of the volume of requests, so joining is not a formality. SOURCE CAVEAT: the team's own intake page now sits on WWF Greece's content archive at contentarchive.wwf.gr/legal-team, which blocks automated retrieval; the requirements above are taken from it and should be reconfirmed against the live site. General contact for the organisation is Charilaou Trikoupi 119-121, 11473 Athens, tel. 210 3314893, support@wwf.gr.

trackers.name: Hellenic Ornithological Society — intervenes on breaches of environmental law (Greece)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Greek non-governmental organisation founded in 1982, the national BirdLife partner since 1994, working on the study and protection of wild birds and their habitats. Its own description of its work is the reason it is here: conservation and research actions, public awareness and education — and direct action on urgent issues of environmental law breach. It also advocates and intervenes in environmental policy and works on the conservation of Important Bird Areas across Greece. WHAT TO ASK IT FOR: whether your site is an Important Bird Area, and what it holds on it. Greece had almost nothing in this file before — the WWF Greece legal team documents complaints but will not litigate for you, and there is no Greek conservation land buyer that three searches could find. This is the organisation that can say what a site is worth ecologically and has said so publicly when the law was being broken. It employs professional staff and works with local collaborators, so ask who its collaborator is in your region. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer and not a law firm. It manages the Antikythira Bird Observatory but I found no evidence it acquires sites. For Greece the honest position is that the ally is expertise and public intervention, not purchase.

trackers.name: Bodossaki Foundation — Greece's grant-maker, and its environment pillar
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: established 1972 and one of Greece's best-known public benefit foundations, working on four strategic priorities — education, healthcare, protecting the environment and empowering civil society. It was among the first public benefit organisations in Greece to turn to environmental protection, funding research on environmental issues, helping implement large-scale environmental protection programmes and supporting environmental education. It has published action plans for the Environment and Climate and for Civil Society. Greece had no funder at all in this file. ITS TRACK RECORD AS A FUND OPERATOR, which is how most of its money reaches small organisations: from 2013 to 2017 it ran the EEA Grants Greek NGO programme 'We are all Citizens', €7.3 million funding 76 projects across Greece. It then ran the Active Citizens Fund for Greece in consortium with SolidarityNow — a €12 to 15 million programme funded by Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway, with successive open calls including one on increased citizen participation in public debate and decision-making, and one on institutional development. Greece and Portugal are the two western states inside the EEA Grants scheme, which is otherwise for newer member states — a fact a Greek group would not guess. THE ELIGIBILITY WARNING THAT MATTERS MOST: one of those calls — the organisational grants for institutional development — required applicants to be CSOs with legal status in Greece and an average annual turnover of at least €300,000 across three financial years, plus a multiannual strategic plan. That excludes essentially every community group in this file. Different calls under the same programme had far lower thresholds. Read each call, never the programme. USE IT WITH GREECE'S OTHER TWO: the WWF Greece legal team, which documents complaints but will not litigate for you, and the Hellenic Ornithological Society, which holds the bird record and intervenes on breaches of environmental law. This is the money and the capacity building.

trackers.name: EEPF — complaints to the European Commission and cases at the Council of State (Greece)
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: the Hellenic Society for the Protection of Nature, founded 1951 and the oldest national environmental NGO in Greece, continuously active since. A member of IUCN, and the national operator in Greece of the Foundation for Environmental Education's programmes including Blue Flag and Green Key. THE AXIS THAT MATTERS FOR A LAND FIGHT is the first of its five: environmental intervention — continually confronting serious threats to Greece's natural environment, taking part in actions that have ended in formal complaints to the European Commission or in legal proceedings before the Council of State, Greece's supreme administrative court. That is the escalation route for a Greek case, and this is a body that has used both ends of it. IT IS ALSO THE NURSERY OF THE GREEK SECTOR, which makes it a directory as much as an ally: the more specialised Greek environmental organisations grew out of it — the Hellenic Ornithological Society, ARCHELON for sea turtles, and MOm for the Mediterranean monk seal. Match your species to the body that studies it. WHAT IT CAN PUT BEHIND A CASE: projects and programmes run alone or with universities, research institutes and other NGOs, national and international — it coordinated a five-year LIFE project on priority habitats and flora in Natura 2000 sites, and has carried out biodiversity assessment studies of flora and fauna, including, notably, an assessment commissioned by a cement company across three of its extraction areas. Read that both ways: it has the survey capability, and it takes industry commissions. AND IT HAS RECORDED THE NATURA 2000 NETWORK: with the environment ministry it ran an awareness programme that included recording habitat types and important flora and fauna species in the Greek network sites. It publishes the quarterly magazine 'I FYSI' continuously since 1975, holds conferences and seminars, and awards the Byron Antipas prize. Its finances come from member and friend donations and from foundation and private-sector sponsorship, audited by chartered accountants.

trackers.name: ARCHELON — records violations on the beach, and its data became the Natura 2000 case
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: the Sea Turtle Protection Society of Greece, founded 1983, nationwide and non-profit. It monitors the main loggerhead nesting areas — Zakynthos, Kyparissia Bay, Lakonikos and Koroni in the Peloponnese, and Rethymno, Chania and Messara in Crete — and runs a Rescue Centre at Glyfada near Athens plus a rescue network along the coastline. THE LINE A COMMUNITY SHOULD ACT ON: its trained volunteers and researchers, covering 75 to 110 kilometres of Greek coastline from May to October, follow international protection protocols and among other things record violations, threatening incidents and dangers to sea turtles on the nesting beaches. There is a standing mechanism, staffed every summer, for logging what is being done to a Greek nesting beach. AND THE PRECEDENT THAT PROVES WHY THAT MATTERS: the standardised long-term monitoring produced nesting data over fifteen years and more, and that information was used to strengthen the case for protection measures and formed the backbone of proposed Natura 2000 sites. Earlier still, promotion of the cause produced a Presidential Decree in 1983 protecting the nesting beaches of Zakynthos, based on building restrictions because at the time no relevant nature protection laws existed. A volunteer count on a beach became a building restriction. THE THREATS IT NAMES ARE DEVELOPMENT THREATS: light pollution, noise pollution, and occupation of available space by beach furniture, alongside habitat loss. If your Greek coastal case involves any of those, the vocabulary and the evidence base already exist. SCALE AND RESULTS: over 500 volunteers a year from around the world; in a recent season more than 10,000 loggerhead nests recorded and protected across the Peloponnese, Zakynthos and Crete, with Kyparissia Bay now the largest breeding population in the Mediterranean — a result attributed to nest-protection measures run since 1992. It also supplies data and scientific information to the European Union, the Council of Europe and national and local authorities, and works with municipalities and with the national protected-areas agency.

trackers.name: NECCA and the MΔΠΠ — the protected-area management unit nearest you (Greece)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Organismos Fysikou Perivallontos kai Klimatikis Allagis (O.FY.PE.K.A. / NECCA), a public body established by the 2020 environmental law 4685/2020, supervised by the environment ministry, whose purpose is implementing the ministry's policy for the management of protected areas in Greece, conserving biodiversity, and promoting sustainable development actions. THE STRUCTURAL FACT A GREEK COMMUNITY MUST KNOW: NECCA is the overall successor of the 36 former Protected Area Management Bodies and of the National Centre for Environment and Sustainable Development, and it now operates through MΔΠΠ — Protected Area Management Units. If your site sits in or beside a protected area, the body you deal with is the management unit for that area, and it is part of a single national organisation rather than a standalone local body as before. Anyone working from pre-2020 contacts for a ΦΔΠΠ is writing to an organisation that no longer exists. WHAT THE LAW SAYS CAN BE PROTECTED, which is the test your site must meet: terrestrial, aquatic or mixed areas, individual elements or ensembles of nature and landscape can be objects of protection and conservation because of their ecological, geomorphological or other value, so that natural processes, the efficiency of natural resources, the balance and evolution of ecosystems, and the diversity, particularity or uniqueness of their components are secured. Uniqueness and particularity are named criteria — not only rarity of species. PRACTICAL POINTS: management plans are approved by acts that take account of national conservation objectives set by ministerial decision, their specifications and content are set by ministerial decision, and management plans are valid for five years — a recurring, dated moment when a community can seek changes. NECCA also concludes cooperation memoranda and works with areas recognised by UNESCO as Greek Global Geoparks and Biosphere Reserves.

trackers.name: Prásino Tameío — five kinds of Greek civil body are named eligible
trackers.desc: THE ELIGIBILITY LIST, WHICH IS UNUSUALLY WIDE: potential beneficiaries of the Green Fund's financing programmes include the environment ministry and bodies it supervises, other ministries, first- and second-tier local authorities, municipal enterprises, public- and private-law legal persons supervised by the Greek State, decentralised administrations, universities and research centres — and non-governmental organisations established and operating as non-profit somateia, astikes mi kerdoskopikes etaireies (AMKE), charitable foundations in Greece, KOINSEP social cooperative enterprises, or syllogoi. AND THE QUALIFYING CLAUSE IS THE FAMILIAR ONE: those bodies must include in their statutory purposes the protection and management of the natural and built environment and/or the protection of wild species. The founding law adds that the fund may finance programmes of somateia or unions of legal and natural persons in any other form which, according to their statutory purposes, aim at the protection, upgrading and restoration of the environment. Seventh country in this file where a sentence in the statutes is the gate. Greece's bucket held EEPF, ARCHELON and NECCA; this is the state money. THE SCALE: annual credit allocations of 144,715,000 EUR in one year with 112.16 million distributed to environmental programmes, and 123.3 million in another — against Hungary's 70 million forint for its whole sector. This is one of the largest environmental funds recorded in this sweep. TWO RULES OF THE ROAD, from its own management guide: a proposal may include interventions in more than one site with the same physical object; but if a beneficiary submits proposals under two different Measures, or more than two proposals under the same Measure, the applications will not be examined. Read that before submitting a scatter of bids. AND THE APPROVAL THRESHOLD, worth knowing when you ask for a programme to exist at all: a financing programme of 50,000 EUR or more excluding VAT is approved by ministerial decision on the proposal of the fund's board; below 50,000 EUR the fund's own board decides.

trackers.name: ELLET — fifty years old, and it runs a standing 'under threat' list of Greek places
trackers.desc: WHY THIS ONE: Greece had 21 filed entries and NOT ONE ORGANISATION THAT TAKES OR HOLDS GROUND — six countries in this file are in that position, and this closes Greece. The Elliniki Etairia — Society for the Environment and Cultural Heritage — works across both the natural environment and cultural heritage, marked fifty years of work, and is structured for public membership through a Friends scheme. WHAT MAKES IT USABLE BY A COMMUNITY WITH A THREATENED PLACE: it runs a standing campaign naming places UNDER THREAT — in one round five Aegean islands among seven listed — framed as a continuous struggle and argued on the ground that our islands matter to the whole of Europe. A national body that publishes a named list of endangered places is one a local group can ask to be added to, and the European framing is the argument that follows. AND IT MAKES ITS OWN AWARD: the Kostas Karras European Citizens' Prize, with open calls for entries. Recognition is a resource in itself when a place needs standing it does not have. ALSO IN GREECE, ALREADY FILED HERE, and worth pairing with this: EEPF, the oldest national environmental NGO in Greece, continuously active since 1951, which led the creation of National Forests and Protected Areas and works on habitat and species protection, including coordinating a five-year LIFE project on priority habitats and flora in Natura 2000 areas, and creating a seed bank for local flora and restoring a cedar forest under a private donation.

trackers.name: Kallisto — scientists who work the forest, the bear and the land-use conflict
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: the Environmental Organisation for Wildlife and Nature 'Kallisto', created in 2004 by scientists with long experience and specialisation in environmental questions, with the original group of specialist scientists later joined by concerned citizens, volunteers, local collaborators and supporters. Greece's bucket held WWF's legal support team, the ornithological society and the state protected-areas body — this is the field science organisation, based in Thessaloniki. An organisation founded by working scientists is the one that can produce the survey a designation needs, and this file has recorded that document as the bottleneck in eleven countries. AND THE COALITION IT SITS IN, which is the free membership list Greece offers: twelve environmental organisations filed a joint comment against a legislative provision opening building inside Natura 2000 areas, calling it multiply problematic and highlighting the pretextual character of the government's justifications. The twelve: ANIMA, Arcturos, ARCHELON, the Hellenic Society for Environment and Culture, the Hellenic Society for the Protection of Nature, the Hellenic Ornithological Society, the Society for the Protection of Prespa, Kallisto, iSea, MEDASSET, MEDINA and WWF Greece. Four are already filed here individually; the other eight are doors a community has not knocked on. THE THREAT THEY WERE ANSWERING, recorded plainly: a provision allowing up to 20 per cent of 'Sustainable Resource Management Zones' to be urbanised, placed in a bill open for public consultation. Building inside Natura 2000 is being legislated for, not merely permitted case by case.

trackers.name: Greek forestry cooperatives — the collective bodies that already hold and work forest land
trackers.desc: WHY THIS MATTERS TO THE ACQUIRER QUESTION: Greece has no conservation land trust that I could verify, but it has dasikoi synetairismoi — forestry cooperatives, and a published account of the Greek legal framework governing them and their institutional path through time. The framing is the useful part: they perform a serious task and contribute not only to the organisation of forestry work but also TO THE PROTECTION OF THE FOREST AS A COMMON GOOD. Where no land trust exists, the collective body that already works the ground is the candidate — this file has recorded the same shape in Italy's domini collettivi, Andorra's comuns, Liechtenstein's Bürgergenossenschaften and Sweden's allmänningsskogar. Greece is the fifth. HOW TO USE IT: a cooperative that holds or works forest near a threatened site is a legally constituted local body with standing interests in the land, and one a residents' group can approach as a partner rather than build from nothing. The published legal-framework article is the place to start on what they may and may not do.

trackers.name: Σημεία Στήριξης — eight foundations funding small organisations, each with its own named theme
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a recurring grant programme announced through the partnership of EIGHT PUBLIC BENEFIT FOUNDATIONS, supporting 27 actions in one cycle across social inclusion, environmental protection and local community cohesion. Greece had 24 filed entries and two funders. AND THE THEMES THAT MATTER HERE, each attached to a NAMED foundation, so a community knows exactly which door its site fits: PROTECTION OF FLORA AND FAUNA IN THE NATURAL AND HUMAN-MADE ENVIRONMENT; PROTECTION AND RESTORATION OF AQUATIC ECOSYSTEMS AND COASTAL AREAS; PROTECTION OF FOREST AND OTHER TERRESTRIAL ECOSYSTEMS; and STRENGTHENING OF ISLAND AND OTHER COASTAL LOCAL COMMUNITIES. Four separate environmental windows, each with its own funder, is a better map than any single grant call — match your site to the theme before writing. AND WHAT COMES WITH THE MONEY: alongside the funding, the programme includes FREE PARTICIPATION of the organisations in CAPACITY-BUILDING activities aimed at improving their operation and long-term sustainability, funded and delivered by an NGO hub run by one of the foundations. A published deadline is given for applications each cycle.

trackers.name: WWF Greece's fundraising guide for volunteer organisations — written for groups with no money
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a published guide to finding resources for VOLUNTEER ORGANISATIONS, produced by WWF Greece — the practical companion to the grant lists, and aimed at exactly the kind of unfunded local group this file exists for. THE DISTINCTION IT DRAWS THAT MOST GROUPS MISS: help can come in MONEY (covering fuel, operating costs) or IN KIND (personal protective equipment, forest-firefighting gear) — and SPONSORSHIPS IN KIND USUALLY ENSURE A GREATER DEGREE OF TRANSPARENCY AND ACCOUNTABILITY AND ARE PREFERRED BY VOLUNTEER ORGANISATIONS. Cash sponsorship requires additional formal conditions, such as a bank account in the organisation's name. An unincorporated group can accept equipment before it can accept money, which is the order most campaigns get backwards. AND THE THIRD CATEGORY IT NAMES: professionals donating their services — an accountant offering the corresponding services free, or an engineer maintaining volunteers' vehicles. It also records that in Greece there are many private public-benefit foundations of national or local reach which subsidise environmental actions, some having funded the fire service directly, and points to the national corporate social responsibility network for company approaches.

trackers.name: Αρκτούρος — it runs sanctuaries on the ground, and it breeds the guard dog that ends the conflict
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: an urban, non-governmental and non-profit environmental organisation founded in 1992 whose aim is the protection of wild fauna and the natural environment in Greece and abroad. It was founded in response to the then constantly growing problem of bears and wolves held in captivity, and grew from that into a full framework of actions. Greece had one land-holding body filed. WHAT IT ACTUALLY OPERATES: a sanctuary at a named mountain village — a physical site, open to visitors, that this file can point a Greek community to. AND THE ACTIVITY WORTH COPYING ANYWHERE THERE IS A PREDATOR CONFLICT: the centre continually enriches its activities, the most significant being THE CONTROLLED BREEDING AND PERPETUATION OF THE GREEK SHEPHERD DOG. Breeding and placing livestock guard dogs is the intervention that removes the reason farmers want a predator killed — and it is run by a conservation organisation, not a state agency. It works to sensitise the public on biodiversity and sustainability and to strengthen biodiversity in Greece, and it appears in the twelve-organisation Natura coalition already filed here.

trackers.name: The Greek Φορείς Διαχείρισης — who manages a protected area, and what you can ask them to do
trackers.desc: WHO RUNS A GREEK PROTECTED AREA, compiled by a conservation organisation rather than a ministry: management bodies established under a 1999 law, authorised with responsibilities that include DRAWING UP MANAGEMENT PLANS AND OPERATING REGULATIONS; MONITORING AND ASSESSING THE APPLICATION OF THOSE REGULATIONS; CONTROLLING INTERVENTIONS IN THE AREAS; GIVING OPINIONS ON THE PRE-APPROVAL OF SITING AND ON THE SETTING OF ENVIRONMENTAL TERMS; carrying out studies, implementing works and conducting research; and PUBLIC AWARENESS. Giving an opinion on the pre-approval of siting and on the environmental terms is the point at which a management body can stop or reshape a project — so a Greek community's first letter goes there, not to the ministry. And controlling interventions in the area is a standing duty someone can be asked to discharge. WHY IT IS FILED AS A RESOURCE RATHER THAN A RULE: the compilation is maintained by the field science organisation already in this file, as its own reference page on national and Community legislation for the natural environment — so a community that cannot read the statute can ask the people who indexed it.

trackers.name: The Greek specialist societies — one nursery organisation, four named bodies, all reachable
trackers.desc: WHY THIS IS FILED SEPARATELY: because it names, in one place, the specialised Greek environmental organisations that grew out of the country's oldest society — a bird society, a sea turtle protection society, and a Mediterranean monk seal society — each working on a specific species or habitat rather than the whole environment. A community defending a coastline should write to the turtle society, not the general environmental one: the specialist body has the survey data, the species records and the standing that a designation argument runs on. AND THE INTERNATIONAL PROGRAMMES THE PARENT BODY RUNS, which give a coastal or tourist-area community a lever: it represents in Greece the international Foundation for Environmental Education, on whose behalf it has managed FIVE INTERNATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION AND AWARENESS PROGRAMMES SINCE 1992, and coordinates two international FEE programmes for sustainable management in the tourism sector — the BLUE FLAG and Green Key. Where a beach or a hotel holds an international award, the body that awards it is a body that can be written to about what is happening there. It is also a member of international conservation unions and works closely with the other large Greek environmental organisations.

trackers.name: WWF Ελλáς klirodotis — a bequest can be SHARES OR PROPERTY, not only money
trackers.desc: WHAT THE ORGANISATION WILL ACCEPT, and it is the line a Greek owner needs: your future donation MAY TAKE THE FORM OF SHARES OR OF PROPERTY, may be a fixed sum, or — for greater impact — may concern the RESIDUE OR PART OF THE RESIDUE OF YOUR ASSETS. Greece had one land-acquisition entry filed; this is a national body that takes land by will. An owner with no heir who wants a field kept can leave the field itself, not its sale proceeds — and 'part of the residue' means it need not be the whole estate. AND WHAT THE ORGANISATION DOES WITH IT: the bequest will help us continue our vital work for the protection of GREEK NATURE, and it states that the contribution honours us and BINDS US to do the best we can on your behalf. AND WHERE IT WORKS, which tells a community whether it has a local team to approach: founded in 1990, it has carried out MORE THAN 70 ACTION PROGRAMMES, and while its seat is in the capital there are PERMANENT TEAMS AND FIELD ACTIONS in the ecologically important areas of five NAMED REGIONS. Its work includes ACTIVE PROTECTION AND MANAGEMENT of the natural environment, and documented interventions on critical questions of environmental policy such as SPATIAL PLANNING, THE CREATION OF A NETWORK OF PROTECTED AREAS, the country's development policy and water resources management.

trackers.name: WWF Ελλáς on its own funding — who pays for Greek environmental work
trackers.desc: WHERE THE MONEY COMES FROM, published under the organisation's own transparency section: THE LARGEST PART OF THE FUNDING of the organisation's work COMES FROM PUBLIC-BENEFIT FOUNDATIONS OF GREECE AND ABROAD. If the biggest single source of Greek environmental funding is charitable foundations, that is where a local group should be applying too — not to the state, and not only to the public. AND WHAT THOSE FUNDERS ADD BEYOND MONEY: their offer goes beyond the limits of financial support, since our partners often offer VALUABLE ADVICE AND KNOW-HOW, with an eye on our common vision for the protection of the environment and the climate. A foundation that gives advice as well as money is worth approaching even when the grant is small. AND THE STRUCTURE, which matters when a community is deciding whom it is really dealing with: the Greek office is the national office of the network in Greece, AN INDEPENDENT GREEK NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATION and at the same time an active part of the international network. Its core work is based on SALARIED STAFF able to meet complex environmental challenges, while its activity and effectiveness are supported to a great degree by voluntary labour.

trackers.name: The Greek KE.SY.PO.TH.A. appeal — a 200–1,000 EURO deposit, REFUNDED IF YOU WIN
trackers.desc: THE COST AND THE REFUND, which is what a Greek resident needs before deciding: the appeal must obligatorily be accompanied by A DEPOSIT IN FAVOUR OF THE GREEN FUND, WHICH STARTS AT 200 EURO AND CAN REACH 1,000 EURO, depending on the size of the infringement. IF THE APPELLANT IS ULTIMATELY VINDICATED, THE DEPOSIT IS RETURNED. Greece had three legal entries filed. Two hundred euro, refunded if you win, is the entry price of a Greek planning challenge — and the money goes to an environmental fund rather than to the state's general revenue. AND THE FORMALITIES THAT DECIDE ADMISSIBILITY: it is necessary that the appeal BE NOTIFIED TO THE GENERAL DIRECTORATE OF THE BODY OF INSPECTORS, and that it contain all the necessary details — TAX NUMBER, EMAIL and others. AND THE CLOCK ON THE OTHER SIDE, which is unusually short: the committee MUST DECIDE WITHIN ONE (1) MONTH, and the decision is sent electronically. A one-month statutory deadline on the decision-maker is a rare thing in this file — most of the appeal routes recorded here bind only the appellant. The same practice lists related work including compensation for deprivation of the use of a property and compensation for non-construction where a property has been tied up long-term.

trackers.name: Greek planning-law practices — and the ruling that a NEIGHBOUR has standing BY DEFINITION
trackers.desc: THE STANDING RULE, quoted from settled case law of the supreme administrative court, and it is the single most useful sentence for a Greek neighbour: THE ADJOINING OWNER OF A PROPERTY HAS BY DEFINITION A LEGAL INTEREST TO CHALLENGE ADMINISTRATIVE ACTS by which the building or other development of an adjoining property is attempted, INVOKING THE HARM CAUSED TO THE ENVIRONMENT OF THE AREA — and all the more so when it is the owner WHO HAD PREVIOUSLY COMPLAINED TO THE ADMINISTRATION about the allegedly environmentally harmful activity. Complaining to the authority first strengthens your standing later, which turns an ignored letter into a legal asset. AND A SECOND RULING THE SAME PRACTICE RECORDS, useful where building is proposed outside a plan: in a Plenary decision, for out-of-plan building the minimum area is NOT ENOUGH — since 1985 it also requires FRONTAGE ONTO A COMMON SPACE, that is A ROAD; on that basis an appeal was rejected and a building permit, as revised, was ANNULLED. A permit already granted can be annulled years later on a frontage point, so the technical detail of the site is worth checking before the campaign chooses its ground. The practice publishes its urban and spatial planning law casework openly.

trackers.name: The EEPF history — MONASTERIES AND A CORPORATE DONOR provided the land and the money
