So for a rare or protected species the record may sit with NPWS, which primarily collects records of species on the Checklist of protected and threatened species in Ireland — and some of that data is treated as sensitive, obtainable only by submitting a data request form. Two custodians, two routes. THE HELP OFFERED TO A BEGINNER, which is unusually explicit: it says if you are not sure or have no idea what species you are looking at, you can always ask for assistance with the identification; its Citizen Science Portal has dedicated recording forms for the major taxonomic groups plus an 'Other Species' form for anything else; and the Biodiversity Data Capture App or the web portal will give you the spatial reference from a map or your phone's GPS. It also sells identification swatches and guides. Its own instruction is to be certain of identification before entry, and to seek help rather than guess. IT RUNS SCHEMES YOU CAN JOIN: a Bumblebee Monitoring Scheme, Flower-Insect Timed Counts, Dragonfly Ireland — coordinated with the Centre for Environmental Data and Recording in Northern Ireland and funded by the EPA as a citizen science project on aquatic species as bio-indicators of climate change and water quality — and the annual BioBlitz.

trackers.name: Ireland's community biodiversity grants — an ecologist writes your plan, then funds it
trackers.desc: THE TWO-STEP THAT MAKES THIS UNUSUAL: a joint Biodiversity Fund of Community Foundation Ireland and the National Parks and Wildlife Service, matching private and public money since 2019. Successful grantees work with ecologists to create a Community Biodiversity Action Plan, and can then seek funding to implement it — and all the data they collect is shared with the National Biodiversity Data Centre, already filed here. So a residents' group gets a professional survey, a written plan, money to act on it, and its records land in the national dataset. 213 action plans have been developed across the country through a joint investment of 1.76 million euro since 2019. WHERE THE COUNCIL MONEY IS: the Local Biodiversity Action Fund, operated by NPWS to help local authorities carry out projects targeting the National Biodiversity Action Plan — 3 million euro allocated in one year, capped at 96,700 euro per local authority, with 262 projects approved across 31 local authorities in another year. Councils then pass some of it on: one county runs a Community Biodiversity Action Plan Small Grant Scheme at up to 90 per cent of project costs, generally to a maximum of 1,500 euro, one grant per organisation, and asks groups to discuss proposals with the Heritage and Biodiversity team before applying. TWO MORE NAMED SCHEMES: the Peatlands and Natura Community Engagement Scheme, competitive, with 800,000 euro supporting forty-five community groups in one year — eligible work includes development of conservation management plans, monitoring or surveying to inform restoration, and invasive species control in and around designated sites. And the Small Recording Grants scheme, 193,000 euro to 67 applicants, explicitly for volunteers, groups, societies and associations of recorders who have limited or no access to financial supports. AND THE ARGUMENT THE STATE ITSELF MAKES: officials note that 85 per cent of Ireland's EU-protected habitats are in unfavourable condition and that the Nature Restoration Regulation has been adopted. The Heritage Council separately runs an Organisation Support Fund for core costs and a Community Heritage Grant Scheme.

trackers.name: Green Sod Ireland — a land trust that takes land as a GIFT and holds it in trust
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: founded in 2007, an Irish land trust with charitable status that protects land and its biodiversity, and has been gifted more than 100 acres of land across Ireland by individuals and communities since foundation. Ireland had one land acquirer filed; this is a second, and it works by donation rather than purchase. HOW IT WORKS, and why that matters to someone with land: land gifted to the trust is managed with steadily decreasing intervention and allowed to rewild naturally, after an initial evaluation by ecologists creates a baseline for the site. The local community participates in the protection of the land. Its own framing: together we hold this land in trust. An owner who does not want to sell to a developer but cannot afford to keep the land can give it away and see it protected — and this file has recorded bequest routes in Denmark, Italy and Luxembourg, but a working gift-based land trust is rarer. IT SETS ASIDE NAMED SITES: it designates 'Wild Acres' for rewilding, runs ecological education programmes in a number of counties, and is a member of the European Rewilding Network.

trackers.name: Hometree and The Nature Trust — monthly subscriptions that buy land, and blended finance that plants it
trackers.desc: THE SUBSCRIPTION THAT BUYS GROUND: Hometree runs a restoration membership in which each monthly payment from supporters pays for THE ACQUISITION OF LAND to be restored and conserved, with a rich mosaic of interconnected forest habitat. A standing order that accumulates into land purchase is the cheapest entry point to conservation buying recorded in this file — and a model a local group could copy. WHAT IT HOLDS AND DOES: named restoration sites including its Ennistymon headquarters, Cnocán Bán, Gleneaskey, Illaun and Avoca; a Wild Atlantic Rainforest Project; work with farmers and an Iveragh Woodlands EIP; a tree nursery and monthly tree planting days open to volunteers; and tree pledges on behalf of organisations from schools to clothing brands. AND THE OTHER IRISH VEHICLE, for scale rather than smallness: The Nature Trust, a not-for-profit set up in 2021 that combines public and private finance to plant new native woodlands and revitalise wild habitats on a large scale across Ireland, managing those lands on a NON-COMMERCIAL basis for ecosystems, climate, local communities and wider society, working with forestry and ecology professionals. Between them: one takes gifts, one takes subscriptions, one takes blended finance.

trackers.name: The Irish objection guides — anyone can object, five weeks, and write it in metres
trackers.desc: WHO CAN OBJECT, and it corrects the commonest mistake: this is one of the most misunderstood aspects of the Irish planning system. Many people believe only neighbours can object — this is not the case. COMMUNITY GROUPS, RESIDENTS' ASSOCIATIONS, individuals living streets away, and even people with no direct connection to the area can all make valid submissions. You need neither to own property nor to live next door. THE CLOCK: five weeks — 35 days — from the date the application was RECEIVED by the local authority. Miss this deadline and your objection cannot be accepted, no exceptions. AND THE WRITING ADVICE, which is the most practical in the file: instead of 'this will affect my privacy', write 'the proposed first-floor rear window will have a direct line of sight into my garden at [address], which is located 8 METRES to the south'. SPECIFIC, MEASURABLE CONCERNS ARE HARDER TO DISMISS. State your grounds upfront; planning authorities rely on evidence, not emotion; and keep the tone factual, since the process is public and comments could be viewed as defamatory. THE GROUNDS THAT COUNT: privacy and overlooking; overshadowing and loss of daylight; traffic hazards and parking; residential amenity including noise and visual dominance; environmental concerns such as drainage, FLOOD RISK or disruption to local habitats; and CONFLICT WITH THE COUNTY OR LOCAL DEVELOPMENT PLAN on zoning, density or design. Practitioners add: it is best if everybody submits an INDIVIDUAL submission rather than one combined one, and an observation at this stage is what preserves the later appeal.

trackers.name: The Irish local-authority environment funds — every one of the 31 councils has money
trackers.desc: THE STANDING NATIONAL SCHEME: the Community Environment Action Fund, formerly Local Agenda 21, which HAS OPERATED SINCE 1997, promotes sustainable development by assisting SMALL SCALE, NON-PROFIT environmental projects at local level, administered by local authorities in conjunction with the department. Projects involve partnership arrangements between local authorities and various local groups including COMMUNITY GROUPS, SCHOOLS and environmental NGOs, and it notes that the value of the scheme is enhanced by the VOLUNTARY EFFORT that it facilitates. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY FUNDED: community gardens and allotments, compost schemes, RAINWATER HARVESTING and biodiversity projects, with priority to climate and biodiversity. AND THE SECOND, LARGER SCHEME RUNNING ALONGSIDE IT: a Local Environmental Action Fund delivered through a partnership between an insurer and ALL 31 LOCAL AUTHORITIES IN IRELAND, in which each local authority receives approximately 50,000 EURO, FULLY MATCHED through existing local authority environmental grants — with grants ranging from 1,000 to 25,000 euro for biodiversity enhancement, HABITAT CREATION, community gardens, litter reduction, environmental improvement and small-scale climate action. Every council in the country holds the same pot — and in at least one area eligibility runs through groups registered with the Public Participation Network.

trackers.name: A bog bought by a FOREIGN foundation — and then made a national nature reserve
trackers.desc: THE SEQUENCE WORTH KNOWING — private purchase first, state designation afterwards: a bog of APPROXIMATELY 112.5 ACRES in County Kerry WAS LEGALLY PROTECTED AS A NATIONAL NATURE RESERVE BY THE IRISH GOVERNMENT IN 1994, having been INITIALLY PURCHASED BY THE DUTCH FOUNDATION FOR THE CONSERVATION OF IRISH BOGS IN THE 1990s WITH THE IRISH PEATLAND CONSERVATION COUNCIL, ALONG WITH two other named bogs. Buying the ground first and having the state designate it afterwards is the reverse of the usual order, and it worked — the purchase created the fact that the designation then recognised. AND THE DETAIL MOST WORTH CARRYING ABROAD: the first buyer was A DUTCH FOUNDATION FOR THE CONSERVATION OF IRISH BOGS — a body in another country, founded for the sole purpose of buying land in this one. A foreign foundation set up specifically to buy your country's habitat is a category of funder most communities never think to look for, and it acted together with the domestic specialist body rather than instead of it. Three bogs were secured in the one effort, and the reserve is now under the state wildlife service.

trackers.name: Österreichische Datenschutzbehörde (DSB)
trackers.desc: Österreichische Datenschutzbehörde (DSB) — Austria’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Austria Lobbying & Interest Register
trackers.desc: Austria's official register of lobbyists and interest-representation organisations. Notably, its scope extends to lobbying of the judicial branch — one of the few regimes worldwide that does so. — Holds to account: lobbyists and interest organisations in Austria — find the official register, which uniquely also covers lobbying of the judiciary.

trackers.name: RIS (Rechtsinformationssystem)
trackers.desc: Free official Legal Information System of the Republic of Austria, including federal/state legislation and court decisions (incl. Constitutional Court). · Find here: Austria's legal information system — legislation and court decisions (RIS).

trackers.name: ÖKOBÜRO — Umweltrechtsservice (free environmental legal advice)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the alliance of 21 Austrian environmental, nature and animal-protection organisations, whose in-house environmental-law team has run a free first-consultation service since 2003 — email your case and they assess it, plus plain-language Informationstexte on the UVP (environmental impact assessment) procedure explaining how objectors get standing. Litigates and intervenes on recognised environmental organisations' participation rights in permit proceedings. WHO IT SUITS: an individual, a Bürgerinitiative or an environmental NGO facing a large project going through UVP or a Land planning process. Advice is by email only — no phone consultations — and a first opinion, not ongoing representation.

trackers.name: Justice and Environment — European green-law network
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the European network of environmental-law NGOs, whose national member here is ÖKOBÜRO. Its fifteen members act as the environmental-law service point in their own countries, taking cases and intervening in legislative processes, while the network defends communities and nature in court and lodges infringement complaints against member-state governments. Its standing themes are access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, environmental assessment and pollution control. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who does not yet know which lawyer to call — knock on ÖKOBÜRO's door first, and use the network only if your problem crosses a border. The network itself does not take individual cases; its members do. YOUR NATIONAL MEMBER IS ÖKOBÜRO (oekobuero.at) — go to them, not to the network. J&E members serve as environmental law ‘service points’ in their countries, handling cases, participating in legislative processes and sometimes providing legal analyses and consultations for national governments. The network has 11 full and 4 associate members, and can launch infringement proceedings against faulty governments — a route a national body alone does not have. CURRENT SCOPE: access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, climate, environmental assessments, and the Environmental Liability Directive. It previously worked on waste, transport, health and Natura 2000, so an older document may overstate what it covers today.

trackers.name: Rechnungshof (Court of Audit)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Austria, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Austria Firmenbuch (company register)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); Austria Firmenbuch (company register) — the official register of companies and legal entities in Austria — the primary public record of corporate existence, ownership, directors and filings. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A BENEFICIAL-OWNERSHIP REGISTER: this shows the registered entity, its directors and filings; where a separate beneficial-ownership register exists, use that to reach the real humans behind a shell company.

trackers.name: Firmenbuch (JustizOnline)
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: companies in Austria — find the Firmenbuch register of entities, directors and filings via JustizOnline.

trackers.name: Austria Register of Beneficial Owners
trackers.desc: Austria Register of Beneficial Owners — Austria’s beneficial-ownership register, disclosing the real individuals who ultimately own or control companies. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A PLAIN COMPANY REGISTRY: this names the real HUMAN owners behind a company; a company registry names only the legal entity, its directors and filings. Use the registry first to find the entity, then this to pierce the shell to the people who profit. — Holds to account: the hidden owners behind firms dealing with Austria’s government — find beneficial-owner filings.

trackers.name: Bundesbeschaffung (BBG)
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Austria, and for how much.

trackers.name: Federal Administrative Court
trackers.desc: Federal Administrative Court — administrative court (Austria).

trackers.name: Dossier
trackers.desc: Austria's pioneering nonprofit newsroom investigating corrupt ties between politics, money and media.

trackers.name: Commercial Court of Vienna
trackers.desc: Commercial Court of Vienna — tribunal in Austria.

trackers.name: Regional Court Feldkirch
trackers.desc: Regional Court Feldkirch — tribunal (Austria).

trackers.name: Offener Haushalt (Open Budget)
trackers.desc: National public-procurement / budget-transparency portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this shows the specific firms winning specific tenders and contracts — for aggregate budget totals use the open-data/statistics portal, and for findings of waste use the audit body. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Austria.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Justice
trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Justice — supreme court (Austria).

trackers.name: Parlament – Declarations
trackers.desc: Legislator / public-official financial interest & asset declarations.

trackers.name: Statistics Austria
trackers.desc: Austria's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Austria.

trackers.name: Supreme Administrative Court of Austria
trackers.desc: Supreme Administrative Court of Austria — supreme court (Austria).

trackers.name: Naturfreikauf — buying land specifically to block development
trackers.desc: AN ACQUISITION PROGRAMME THAT NAMES BLOCKING DEVELOPMENT AS A REASON TO BUY. The Naturschutzbund holds over 1,380 parcels covering more than 12 million m², secured permanently. Its stated grounds for purchase include protection from destruction where there is ‘Gefahr in Verzug’ (imminent danger), preserving wilderness, restoration, stepping-stone biotopes, rounding out existing holdings — and strategic purchases, ‘Sperrgrundstücke’ (blocking parcels). In the Salzburg and Styrian floodplains such purchases are made expressly to prevent the destruction of valuable areas by building development, or at least to delay it. WHO DECIDES, AND WHO TO APPROACH: the choice of what to buy is made decentrally by biologists in the local, district and state groups, who have both the expertise and experience in negotiating with landowners — so approach your local or district group, not a national office. It acts only where rescue of an ecologically significant area is acutely necessary. AND THE FALLBACK MOST GROUPS FORGET: where purchase is impossible, it seeks at minimum a Pachtvertrag (lease) to manage the site to conservation standards.

trackers.name: Where Naturfreikauf works, where it doesn't, and how to fund it
trackers.desc: REGIONAL REALITY, FROM THE ORGANISATION ITSELF. Focus varies by Land: Burgenland — purchase or lease of species-rich dry and semi-dry grassland; Carinthia — a long tradition of acquiring moors, around 200 moor areas, supported by the Land and by an annual sum from the Kärntner Jägerschaft, the hunters' association; Pinzgau — creation and care of dozens of small waters and ponds; Upper Austria — securing forest for site-appropriate natural woodland. THE BARRIER TO CHECK FIRST: in Vorarlberg and Tyrol buying is considerably harder, because the Grundverkehrskommission allows agricultural land to be acquired only if no farmer wishes to buy it — which, the organisation notes, is almost never the case. Check your Land's Grundverkehr rules before planning a purchase, because they can rule it out entirely. FUNDING: the work runs on membership fees, sponsors and donations, which are tax deductible; the Umweltdachverband also takes donations for nature and environment, noting that pressure on nature is great while conservation budgets are small.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Blühendes Österreich — pays farmers and community groups to keep the habitat (Austria)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a charitable private foundation set up in 2015 by the REWE International retail group with BirdLife Österreich as co-founder and partner, on the Austrian list of donation-privileged organisations. Austria had no funder in this file. WHO IT ACTUALLY PAYS, WHICH IS THE POINT: through its FLORA programme it has supported over 300 farmers, conservation organisations, municipalities, NGOs and civil society initiatives, with an annual premium to farms, associations and communes for protecting and maintaining ecologically valuable land. Its own running total is 1,500 to 1,600 hectares of valuable biotopes — bogs, dry grassland, traditional orchard meadows and others — preserved or improved, having started from a target of 1,000 hectares. It has also co-financed project delivery in 60 protected areas: biosphere parks, European protection sites, national parks, nature parks and UNESCO World Heritage sites. A CONSERVATION ASSOCIATION OR A COMMUNE CAN APPLY, not only a farm. That distinction matters in a country where this file's other Austrian entries are advisory and legal bodies. AND IT FUNDS THE PHYSICAL THINGS OTHER FUNDERS WILL NOT: its WIN #landwirtschaft call, with €1 million, explicitly states that its financing complements public support programmes and pays for basic measures — investment in water supply, stable buildings, fences, grazing infrastructure and other steps to restore extensively used farmland. Fences and water are exactly what a community with a grazing plan cannot otherwise pay for. IT RUNS THEMED CALLS WITH PUBLISHED AWARDS: its #wein.landschaft call put €250,000 into five viticulture and nature projects, one of them €39,900 to a wine-growers' association of eleven businesses and thirty members working across about 400 hectares on dry stone walls, stone piles, native seed greening, orchard trees, new amphibian spawning waters and an amphibian fence along a road. That is the level of detail an Austrian application is expected to reach. WHERE THE MONEY COMES FROM, so you can judge it: retail customer donations, including a cent per marked product and a deposit-return donation scheme, plus corporate partnerships.

trackers.name: naturbeobachtung.at — 940,000 records, and 60 experts who will verify yours
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Naturschutzbund's reporting platform and app, running since 2006, where anyone can report observations of animals, plants and fungi, discuss them in a forum and view others' records in galleries and distribution maps. 940,000 observations with 660,000 images are documented. WHY IT MATTERS FOR A CASE, and this is the part to act on: more than 60 specialists from every biological discipline help identify and check incoming records — mostly volunteers from universities, museums and technical offices, joined over time by amateur experts granted validation rights. They guarantee data of high quality, used for nature conservation work and for scientific publications. A verified record from your ground is not an anecdote; it is data the conservation sector already relies on. HOW TO MAKE A RECORD COUNT: you may report a species you cannot name as an unidentified species and the community will determine it afterwards; where a reporter can only assign a record to a group, experts can refine it to species level, and reporters are told the result of the check. Uploading a documentary photograph is expressly wanted, and is compulsory in the app. Optional fields allow weather data and a detailed site description with site photographs. AND THE ORGANISATION BEHIND IT IS A LAND BUYER AND A LOCAL ADVOCATE: the Naturschutzbund has around 80,000 members in nine Landesgruppen plus numerous district and local groups, and states that interest representation on the spot is one of its strengths — work ranging from stream clean-ups to preventing nature-destroying 'mega' projects. One of its strategies is to lease or buy parcels to save them from destruction: over 1,000 ecologically valuable areas have been bought, usually with targeted improvements made to those biotopes. Membership is handled by the Landesgruppe, not the federal office — so contact your provincial group.

trackers.name: Naturfreunde Österreich — 460 local groups, and it publishes joint position papers
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: founded 1895, around 160,000 members organised in 460 Ortsgruppen, nine Landesorganisationen and 9,500 officials and staff, with roughly 130 to 140 huts and houses, 100 climbing halls and a whitewater centre. The category this file has repeatedly found under-represented: a very large resource-user membership body whose members are physically on the ground every weekend. THE HISTORY THAT EXPLAINS THE POLITICS: the movement's achievements include Wegefreiheit — free access to alpine landscapes — alongside access to education, affordable excursions and hut building. Access rights are its founding cause, so a scheme that closes off ground touches its core purpose, not a side interest. WHAT IT DOES ON LIVE CASES, from its own environment portal: joint statements and campaigning on named threats — a wave of development threatening the Ötztal Alps, with associations demanding an extension of the quiet zone (Ruhegebiet); an environmental alliance in Upper Austria presenting an action plan on environmental offences; a position paper on photovoltaics and solar thermal specifically with regard to the alpine space; and a comparison of parties' environmental policy positions at European elections. If your Austrian case is alpine infrastructure, there is an existing position paper and an existing alliance. AND IT USES ITS OWN CONFERENCE TO SET POLICY: motions at its federal conference have covered the statutes of the federal, provincial and local organisations, an exemption from general path-keeper liability in the civil code for the protection of nature, and the preservation and extension of a named area as a sport and recreation zone. A local group can put a site into the national organisation's policy through a motion. PRACTICAL: its academy trains active Ortsgruppe members and motivated members who want to become active; its Respect Nature initiative addresses recreation pressure on intact natural space. Contact the Ortsgruppe or the Landesorganisation, which are listed by province.

trackers.name: Biodiversitätsfonds — up to 100 per cent for NGOs, and private persons can apply
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: an Austrian federal funding programme running since late 2022 for the preservation, improvement and restoration of biological diversity in Austria, with 80 million euro available to 2026, of which 50 million from the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility; one call alone put 18 million euro into area-related implementation projects. It is administered by Kommunalkredit Public Consulting, Türkenstraße 9, 1090 Vienna, +43 1 31631-807, biodiversitaetsfonds@publicconsulting.at. WHO IT IS FOR, WHICH IS BROADER THAN ANY OTHER FUND IN THIS SWEEP: NGOs, universities, businesses, municipalities and also private individuals who want to make a significant contribution to protecting biodiversity. A private person can apply — nowhere else in nineteen funds. THE RATE, AND THE ASYMMETRY: support can be up to 100 per cent of eligible costs; for competitors — undertakings under the general block exemption regulation — it is 40 to 60 per cent depending on company size. Only direct project costs are funded. THE CONDITION TO PREPARE BEFORE YOU APPLY: fundable projects are implementation projects which improve the situation for the species or habitats at the site, and at the time of submission it must be clear which protection-worthy species or habitats are present, and the nature-conservation and access permissions must already have been obtained. That is a survey and a landowner's consent, in hand, before the form. HOW THE MONEY ARRIVES, which decides whether a small group can carry it: a start instalment of up to 20 per cent of the approved sum once the contract takes effect, an interim instalment after a progress report at six months, further interim instalments depending on project duration, and a final instalment after the closing report is accepted. Unlike Portugal's pure reimbursement, money comes up front. CALL THEMES SO FAR: restoration of priority damaged ecosystems, especially bogs and dry grassland; protection of endangered species and habitats with a focus on habitat connectivity; and recording and assessing the state and trends of biodiversity in Austria. Applications are assessed by KPC, evaluated by a Biodiversity Commission and approved by the climate ministry.

trackers.name: Umweltanwaltschaft — a public environmental advocate that appeals on nature's behalf, and wins
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: each Austrian Land has a Landesumweltanwaltschaft — a publicly funded environmental ombuds office with PARTY STATUS in permitting procedures, which can lodge its own Beschwerde to the Landesverwaltungsgericht. Austria's bucket had two legal advice services and two funds; this is a body that litigates without being asked and without charging. ITS RECORD, COUNTED BY A PRACTITIONER: a Salzburg lawyer reviewed the office's Beschwerden in the federal legal information system and found that of 23 decisions, only three were unsuccessful; four were outright refusals of the permit, and in 16 cases partial changes were achieved. Twenty of twenty-three brought a refusal or a change — the strongest success rate recorded anywhere in this file, against Finland's 6–10 per cent for private appeals. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES, from its own newsletter: carries out its own noise measurements after residents' complaints — in one case several measurements over two months following complaints about night freight traffic; files Stellungnahmen on new Bebauungspläne; and appeals nature permits — in one case the Landesverwaltungsgericht, contrary to the administrative authority's own result, found on the office's Beschwerde that a forest road impaired the landscape. AN HONEST CAUTION: the offices are politically exposed — press reporting describes one Land government curtailing its Umweltanwaltschaft's powers after such disputes. Check what yours can still do. A free public body that takes measurements and files appeals is the first call in Austria, before any lawyer.

trackers.name: Austrian Naturschutzrecht practices — representation in the Naturverträglichkeitsprüfung
trackers.desc: WHAT THEY OFFER, from an Austrian firm's own nature-law service list: legal examination of a project under the Land Naturschutzgesetz and across other environmental permitting procedures; representation in nature-law notification and approval procedures; advice on the Fauna-Flora-Habitat Directive and the Birds Directive; advice on the ALTERNATIVES ASSESSMENT and the examination of compensatory measures; representation in the Naturverträglichkeitsprüfung — the Natura 2000 appropriate assessment; and representation in administrative and criminal penalty proceedings. The alternatives assessment is where most Natura 2000 approvals are actually beaten, and it is a named service here. AND THE BUILDING-LAW SIDE, from another practice: we check your Parteistellung and draft well-founded Einwendungen, and where appropriate lodge a Beschwerde to the Landesverwaltungsgericht — adding that neighbours can object only if you have Nachbarrechte, and that conditions attached to a permit are challengeable only if legally covered and objectively justified. Several offer a free first consultation. CAUTION: these firms advise investors and private builders as well as neighbours. Check for conflicts.

trackers.name: BIV — an association that exists to support Bürgerinitiativen and individuals
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS, plainly: BIV supports BÜRGERINITIATIVEN AND INDIVIDUALS in the fields of environmental protection and of fundamental and human rights. Austria's bucket held a public environmental advocate, nature-law firms, a land-buying action and a holding foundation — but nothing whose stated purpose is helping the citizens' initiative itself. An association set up to back initiatives and INDIVIDUALS is the first call for one person with a problem and no group yet, which is where most of the fights in this file begin. AND THE STATE-LEVEL NETWORKS ALONGSIDE IT: an Alliance of Carinthian Citizens' Initiatives — an open, non-party network of civil society initiatives formed in 2011 to give local citizens' initiatives a platform for statewide networking and to put isolated issues into a larger context — which holds a regular meeting roughly once a month with the provincial environment councillor in the state government, and expressly invites further initiatives with similar aims to join. A monthly standing meeting between a citizens' alliance and the responsible minister is the most direct access recorded in this file, and the alliance publishes its member list — including a local 'citizens' forum' working with the municipal council, and a mothers' initiative on heavy metals and HCB.

trackers.name: Guter Grund and the Bodenbündnis — they organise the doorstep conversations for you
trackers.desc: WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES FOR A LOCAL CAMPAIGN, and it is a method rather than a petition: using the proven method of BASISORGANISIERUNG — base organising — we work locally with citizens' initiatives. Together we hold ONE-TO-ONE CONVERSATIONS, find new supporters and ORGANISE THE LOCAL MAJORITY BEHIND THE CAUSE. It is active Austria-wide to NETWORK LOCAL CITIZENS' INITIATIVES AND MAKE THEM MORE VISIBLE, because coordinated joint actions show how many people nationwide are massively affected by soil sealing. An organisation that will come and do the doorstep work with you is rarer than one that will write a submission — and it also runs participation days on farms, where town and country meet not at a discussion table but while working together. AND THE MUNICIPAL SIDE: a national Bodenbündnis network of municipalities, organisations, schools and committed individuals, with an interactive map of who has joined, running talks on how municipalities can actively contribute to soil protection and what soil consumption does to the water balance, agriculture and climate. Soil protection begins in the municipality, in its own words — and a touring exhibition cube visits the whole country.

trackers.name: Naturschutzbund's national competition — open to Vereine, INITIATIVEN, schools and firms
trackers.desc: WHO MAY ENTER, and the breadth is the point: VEREINE, INITIATIVEN, institutions, businesses, SCHOOLS — all who can make a contribution to promoting biodiversity in Austria are invited to submit their projects to THE LARGEST NATIONAL SPECIES-PROTECTION COMPETITION. An unincorporated initiative can enter the country's biggest conservation competition on the same footing as an institution, and the aim is to stimulate AND DISTINGUISH projects throughout Austria that work for the protection, enhancement and preservation of THREATENED PLANT OR ANIMAL SPECIES OR HABITATS. Being publicly distinguished is worth as much as the prize money to a group facing a council — and the competition itself is funded through the national biodiversity fund of the climate and environment ministry, which is the fund filed alongside it. AND THE PROVINCIAL TIER, which is where the recurring money sits: one Land's environmental protection department runs its own guideline-based nature protection funding in three named lines — HABITAT funding: preserving, tending and CREATING habitats; SPECIES funding: protecting and promoting particular species; LANDSCAPE funding: preserving traditional rural small architecture — and states that nature protection projects funded from provincial means CAN BE SUBMITTED AT ANY TIME, with technical advice offered alongside.

trackers.name: How the buying decision is actually made — decentralised, and a LEASE when purchase fails
trackers.desc: WHO DECIDES WHETHER YOUR SITE GETS BOUGHT, which is what a community needs to know before it asks: THE DECISION AS TO WHICH AREAS ARE PURCHASED IS TAKEN DECENTRALLY, and it is THE PROVINCIAL-GROUP EXPERTS WHO DECIDE ON LAND PURCHASE. The decision sits with provincial experts, not a national office — so the approach should be made regionally, to people who already know the ground. AND THE THRESHOLD: THE ASSOCIATION BECOMES ACTIVE ONLY WHERE IT IS A MATTER OF THE ACUTELY NECESSARY RESCUE OF AN ECOLOGICALLY SIGNIFICANT AREA. Those experts have not only the necessary specialist knowledge for such a decision, but are also EXPERIENCED WHEN IT COMES TO CONVERSATIONS WITH THE LANDOWNERS. Experienced negotiators with owners are a resource in themselves, separate from the money. AND THE FALLBACK WHEN A PURCHASE CANNOT BE MADE, which is the sentence most worth carrying abroad: WHERE THE PURCHASE OF A VALUABLE HABITAT IS NOT POSSIBLE, THE ASSOCIATION TRIES AT LEAST, BY MEANS OF A LEASE CONTRACT, TO MANAGE THE AREA OPTIMALLY FROM A NATURE-CONSERVATION POINT OF VIEW. AND WHAT FOLLOWS ACQUISITION: THE ACQUISITION OF A PLOT ALWAYS BRINGS A GREAT RESPONSIBILITY WITH IT. MANY OF THE NATURE PARADISES MUST BE REGULARLY TENDED — countless volunteers help with DEBRUSHING MOORS, LAYING OUT AMPHIBIAN PONDS, OR MOWING LITTER MEADOWS.

trackers.name: The Umweltanwaltschaften — a free, independent environmental advocate in EVERY Austrian state
trackers.desc: A PUBLIC BODY WHOSE CLIENT IS NATURE, one in each of the nine states, and its powers are the point: THE UMWELTANWALTSCHAFTEN HAVE PARTY STATUS AS A FORMAL PARTY IN ENVIRONMENTALLY RELEVANT FEDERAL PERMITTING PROCEDURES SUCH AS THE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT AND THE WASTE-MANAGEMENT PROCEDURE. PARTICIPATION RIGHTS IN THE PROVINCIAL PROCEDURES ARE REGULATED DIFFERENTLY IN EACH STATE, BUT ALL THE UMWELTANWALTSCHAFTEN HAVE PARTY STATUS IN THE NATURE-PROTECTION PROCEDURES. Austria is joint-smallest bucket in this file. An official party to the case, on nature's side, exists before a community organises anything — and it is already in the room a residents' group is trying to enter. AND WHAT IT DOES FOR RESIDENTS DIRECTLY: CITIZEN ADVICE AND INFORMATION — CITIZENS ARE ADVISED PROFESSIONALLY IN ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEDURES. THEY RECEIVE INFORMATION ABOUT THE COURSE OF THE PROCEDURE AND THE ESSENTIAL PROCEDURAL STEPS. AND THE POWER THAT MATTERS WHEN EVIDENCE IS THE PROBLEM: THE UMWELTANWALTSCHAFTEN HAVE THE POSSIBILITY OF OBTAINING EXPERT OPINIONS OR CARRYING OUT FURTHER INVESTIGATIONS, and so of working on solutions. A public body that can commission the expert report is the answer to the cost that stops most objections. They are described as THE ONLY INSTITUTIONS THAT REPRESENT THE INTERESTS OF NATURE AND THE ENVIRONMENT NON-PARTISAN AND FREE OF INSTRUCTIONS, and stand as partners for CITIZENS, CITIZENS' INITIATIVES AND NGOs.

trackers.name: Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (Dutch DPA)
trackers.desc: Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (Dutch DPA) — the Netherlands’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Netherlands — Tweede Kamer lobbyist register
trackers.desc: National lobbying register; the House of Representatives (Tweede Kamer) maintains a public register of interest representatives/lobbyists holding a standing access pass to the parliament building (since 1 July 2012), Netherlands. — Holds to account: lobbyists with parliament access — find the register of interest representatives holding a standing pass to the Tweede Kamer.

trackers.name: Rechtspraak.nl
trackers.desc: Official Dutch judiciary portal: published judgments and court information. · Find here: published judgments of the Dutch courts (Rechtspraak.nl).

trackers.name: NJCM (Dutch Section, International Commission of Jurists)
trackers.desc: Dutch section of the International Commission of Jurists — a volunteer jurists' association that monitors human-rights and rule-of-law compliance, comments on legislation, files shadow reports and pursues strategic human-rights litigation through its Public Interest Litigation Project.

trackers.name: Advisory Board on Open Government and Information Management (ACOI, Netherlands)
trackers.desc: Advisory Board on Open Government and Information Management (ACOI, Netherlands) — independent body overseeing the right of access to public information.

trackers.name: de Woo-Knop — FOI requests (NLD)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); de Woo-Knop — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: Both ENDS — small grants funds for environmental defenders
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: co-founds and works with small-grants funds that pass money from large donors down to grassroots groups and environmental and human-rights defenders — often only a few thousand euros, with the recipient deciding what it is spent on. WHO IT SUITS: a local group that would never survive an international application cycle. HOW IT DIFFERS: decisions are made by the regional fund, not a distant donor, and can move fast enough to get a threatened defender to safety.

trackers.name: Natuurmonumenten — aankoop van natuurgebieden (land purchase)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the Netherlands' largest nature-conservation membership association (founded 1905, 968,000 members), which BUYS and manages land — over 112,000 hectares across some 355 reserves. Its stated strategy is to purchase ground both to create new nature and to CONNECT existing fragmented reserves. USE IT: Dutch land under threat that adjoins or bridges an existing reserve is exactly their acquisition priority — make that connectivity argument when you approach them.

trackers.name: Stichting DOEN — grants and loans for green initiatives
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the fund of the Dutch Postcode Loterij and VriendenLoterij, giving both grants and loans to front-runner initiatives — including citizens' collectives (burgercollectieven) working on landscape restoration and regenerative agriculture. Lends where banks will not, because applicants cannot offer security, and recycles repayments into new green and social initiatives. WHO IT SUITS: a legal person only — applications from individuals are not considered — with a costed SMART plan, past the research stage and into pilot or early rollout. Organisations already holding sufficient reserves are excluded. Apply any time, but at least four months before the project starts; the procedure takes about four months. HOW IT DIFFERS: purely political or awareness campaigns are excluded, so this funds the alternative you are building, not the fight against the development.

trackers.name: Nationaal Groenfonds — leningen voor groene projecten
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the Dutch green financing institution, lending into nature and landscape, water, sustainable agriculture, circular economy and climate adaptation — including, in some cases, subordinated debt or equity. WHO IT SUITS: read this before spending an afternoon on it, because the screen is hard. It lends to organisations and enterprises ONLY and states flatly on its own front page that it NEVER provides loans, subsidies or payments to private individuals, not even through intermediaries. The minimum loan is €200,000 apart from its sustainable-agriculture fund, security such as a mortgage charge may be required, and it funds only projects with a demonstrable return for the green environment. HOW IT DIFFERS: it gives no grants at all. This is debt. It is the right instrument for a land trust or a foundation buying ground it can service, and the wrong one for a residents' campaign.

trackers.name: Netherlands Court of Audit (Algemene Rekenkamer)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Netherlands, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: data.overheid.nl
trackers.desc: National — Netherlands government open data portal. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Netherlands.

trackers.name: Aruba — Chamber of Commerce registry (company register)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); Aruba — Chamber of Commerce registry (company register) — the official company register for Aruba (Dutch Caribbean) — a key offshore corporate-transparency source for directors, ownership and filings.

trackers.name: Statistics Netherlands (CBS)
trackers.desc: Netherlands's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Netherlands.

trackers.name: Curaçao — Chamber of Commerce registry (company register)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); Curaçao — Chamber of Commerce registry (company register) — the official company register for Curaçao (Dutch Caribbean) — a key offshore corporate-transparency source for directors, ownership and filings.

trackers.name: NCEA — per-country ESIA country profiles (worldwide)
trackers.desc: The Netherlands Commission for Environmental Assessment (NCEA) — a worldwide reference, not a Dutch-only resource. You CAN get: per-country ESIA profiles for ~150 countries — the environmental-assessment law, the review process and the consultant-accreditation rules of each. You CAN'T get: the project documents themselves (it maps each country's system, not its files). For activists: the fastest way to learn how EIA works in a country with no online registry of its own, and where its documents should live.

trackers.name: Follow the Money (investigative outlet)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (investigative newsroom); Follow the Money (investigative outlet) — Dutch-based pan-European investigative platform doing deep, long-form follow-the-money work on EU lobbying, subsidies, party funding & (lack of) oversight — a counterforce to concentrated power.

trackers.name: Dutch Business Register
trackers.desc: official company register in the Netherlands

trackers.name: KVK — Netherlands Business Register
trackers.desc: Official Dutch company register (Chamber of Commerce). Here you can trace companies, their directors and filings registered in the Netherlands.

trackers.name: UBO register
trackers.desc: UBO register — the Netherlands’ beneficial-ownership register, disclosing the real individuals who ultimately own or control companies. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A PLAIN COMPANY REGISTRY: this names the real HUMAN owners behind a company; a company registry names only the legal entity, its directors and filings. Use the registry first to find the entity, then this to pierce the shell to the people who profit. — Holds to account: the hidden owners behind firms dealing with the Netherlands’ government — find beneficial-owner filings.

trackers.name: TenderNed
trackers.desc: The Netherlands' official public-procurement platform. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in the Netherlands, and for how much.

trackers.name: Tweede Kamer
trackers.desc: Official Dutch House of Representatives with comprehensive legislative data, voting records, and open data API. — Holds to account: top officials & cabinet — find their assets, interests and integrity declarations.

trackers.name: UBO-register trusts
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Access restricted to authorities/obliged entities.

trackers.name: Bezwaar en beroep tegen een omgevingsvergunning — the sequence and the costs
trackers.desc: OBJECTING IS FREE; APPEALING IS NOT, AND THE FEE IS REFUNDABLE IF YOU WIN. Filing a bezwaar or zienswijze against a permit costs nothing. You do not need a lawyer — in Dutch administrative law you may run the procedure yourself, or be helped by a jurist from a legal expenses insurer or by someone you authorise (machtigen). If you go to beroep, the court must receive it within 6 weeks of the date on the decision letter, and you will be invoiced griffiekosten. PAY THEM ON TIME: under art. 8:41(6) Awb late payment makes you niet-ontvankelijk and the entire effort is lost — the most avoidable way to lose a Dutch case. WIN AND YOU GET THE FEE BACK, plus a possible proceskostenvergoeding for whoever gave you legal assistance or for an expert; lose and you recover neither. HOW TO PAY FOR HELP: on a low income, apply to your gemeente for bijzondere bijstand toward the griffiekosten — the municipality decides. If you cannot afford a lawyer or mediator you may qualify for a toevoeging from the Raad voor Rechtsbijstand, which assigns counsel for a specific procedure, with the amount depending on your income and assets. And if you hold a rechtsbijstandverzekering it will in principle pay for an omgevingsrecht lawyer — but cover depends on the policy terms and on when the dispute arose, so check before relying on it.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: INECE — not where you report, but how you find who enforces
trackers.desc: READ THIS BEFORE YOU WRITE TO THEM: INECE IS NOT A COMPLAINT ROUTE. Its members are inspectors, prosecutors, regulators, parliamentarians and judges — a community cannot report a violation to INECE. It is worth an entry for three other reasons. FIRST, THE REGIONAL NETWORKS ARE A ROUTING DEVICE: INECE names AECEN (Asian Environmental Compliance and Enforcement Network), AELERT (Australasian Environmental Law Enforcement and Regulators network) and RedLaFiCA (Red Latinoamericana de Fiscalización y Cumplimiento Ambiental) as part of the network — if you do not know which body enforces in your country, the regional network is a shorter list to search than the world. SECOND, ITS CITIZEN-SCIENCE POSITION IS LEVERAGE: INECE runs an ongoing webinar series on ‘how can citizen and community science contribute to environmental compliance and enforcement?’ — that the global network of enforcers is itself asking that question is citable when an agency dismisses community-gathered evidence. THIRD, IT SHOWS WHAT KIND OF BODY TO LOOK FOR: its named members include a superintendency, a protection agency, a ministry and a supreme court — which is why searching for ‘EPA’ by name fails outside the US. The Secretariat is the Environmental Law Institute, not a government; it keeps an online library of compliance and enforcement resources and runs training — a recent series on environmental and social impact assessment drew 161 people from 31 countries. Founded 1989, covering administrative, civil, criminal and judicial enforcement, with support from UNEP, the World Bank, the European Commission and the OECD. BE AWARE OF THE MEMBERSHIP WALL: members have exclusive access to INECE materials and capacity-building programmes. IN THIS COUNTRY: The Dutch environment ministry co-founded INECE in 1989 and co-chairs its Executive Planning Committee — enforcement policy here is set at ministry level.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Mobilisation for the Environment (MOB) — files against permits (Netherlands)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Dutch foundation built as a national network of jurists, founded by Johan Vollenbroek, whose principal activity is bringing legal proceedings against permit decisions. It files objections, appeals and requests to revoke existing permits, and it does this at scale: objections and appeal against a Vattenfall biomass plant the province let through without an environmental impact report, revocation requests against both Maasvlakte coal plants, sixteen poultry and duck farms in Gelderland, and ten industrial ammonia emitters including Tata Steel, SABIC, Saint-Gobain, Yara, Rockwool, FrieslandCampina and Cargill. It also works with other environmental organisations and supports citizens and municipalities, which is the door for a local group. Contact is by email. WHY IT GETS THROUGH THE DOOR: its standing has been tested and held. When the province of Friesland hired outside counsel specifically to have MOB declared inadmissible, the Raad van State's administrative division ruled against the province on 19 December 2014; MOB sets out on its own site that it meets all four criteria in article 11(1) of Regulation (EC) 1367/2006 for NGO access to justice. A local committee normally has to prove its standing; MOB does not. WHAT TO EXPECT: it says itself that running appeal procedures is neither its main activity nor an end in itself, but a means when other routes fail. It chooses its own cases at national scale and is not a legal-aid service, so approach it with a permit decision and a documented breach rather than a grievance. Be aware too that MOB is politically contested in the Netherlands and farming organisations have publicly attacked its standing; allying with it brings that with you. Its site moved in December 2023 and publications before that date sit on the older site.

trackers.name: Wösten juridisch advies — permit decisions and agricultural environmental law (Netherlands)
trackers.desc: WHO TO CALL: a Dutch administrative-law practice run by Valentijn Wösten, working in agrarisch omgevingsrecht. It describes its own work exactly as a community needs it framed: it acts for parties who want it established whether the public administration kept to the rules when it took a decision — and the decisions in question are usually permit decisions. It has acted as counsel to Mobilisation for the Environment in the proceedings pressing provinces to revoke livestock permits. WHO IT SUITS: a group that has a consent it believes was granted wrongly and needs someone to test that rather than campaign about it. Its published explanation of how Dutch administrative law works makes one distinction that is worth absorbing before the first meeting: the procedural rules and the toetsingskader — the standard the decision is measured against — are separate things, and confusing them is how groups arrive with the wrong argument. NOTE WHAT IT IS: a juridisch advies practice rather than an advocatenkantoor. For administrative proceedings that is usually sufficient in the Netherlands, but establish at the outset who will appear if the matter goes further.

trackers.name: NDFF — 250 million records, free to search, and it is what the ecologists consult
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Nationale Databank Flora en Fauna, described as the most complete nature database in the Netherlands, holding over 250 million observations with roughly 20 million added a year, contributed by volunteers and professionals from hundreds of organisations. Partner organisations bring observations together, check them, and make the data available. THE PART A COMMUNITY CAN USE TODAY: the Flora & Fauna Verkenner is the gateway, open to everyone, showing which observations are in the database, of which species, and the place and time of each — over 200 million records across the whole country. Before you argue that a site matters, look up what has already been recorded on it, by other people, over decades. WHAT FEEDS IT, which tells you who else to ask: Sovon for birds, FLORON, BLWG, NMV and ANEMOON on daily update, the Vlinderstichting for butterflies, EIS and RAVON, the national flora monitoring network, Waarneming.nl weekly, Telmee, the Verspreidingsatlas daily, plus provincial and municipal networks. Each of those is a national volunteer organisation with its own experts. AND THE GAP TO KNOW ABOUT, stated by the NDFF itself: data from quickscans and follow-up ecological surveys — the studies developers commission — go into the NDFF only to a limited extent, except from some municipalities, water boards, infrastructure bodies and consultancies that actively share.
