So the developer's own survey may not be there, and the absence of records is not evidence of absence. HOW TO CONTRIBUTE: the most used apps for individual records are the NDFF Invoer app, ObsIdentify and Waarneming.nl. Records of common species entered by website or app become visible after about a day to a week; rare species usually have to be checked first. Organisations needing bulk data go through Het Natuurloket.

trackers.name: Sovon — will do an effect study for you, and you can claim a survey plot on your own ground
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: the national data-managing organisation for ornithology in the Netherlands, based in Nijmegen, founded 1973 on the British Trust for Ornithology model. It has managed and developed high-quality national and provincial monitoring networks for almost 50 years, coordinating thousands of volunteers to fixed protocols. Its bird networks form part of the Netwerk Ecologische Monitoring, the government's system of nature monitoring networks. THE SERVICE A COMMUNITY CAN COMMISSION, in its own words: advice based on reliable bird data, or a targeted effect study (effectstudie) — ask without obligation for a quotation or a telephone conversation through its information request form, and it says it will help even if you have not yet formulated the question clearly. That is a national research institute offering to scope your problem for free before quoting. WHAT IT CAN PRODUCE: spatial models combining its own counts, other species organisations' data and the NDFF to map species distribution across the whole country — including quantile maps showing the smallest possible area containing, say, 10 or 50 per cent of a population. For a site whose importance is disputed, that is the analysis that answers 'is this ground significant'. It also does reproduction research, which shows whether extra protection measures are necessary, and passive acoustic monitoring. AND THE PART YOU CAN DO YOURSELF, WITHOUT MONEY: volunteers claim survey plots. Its portal shows vacant telgebieden — count areas nobody currently surveys — with those in under-surveyed habitats and in Natura 2000 areas flagged as extra important. You select the area on a map, it is assigned within days, and if a previous counter stopped, another can continue the series. Breeding-bird counting is explicitly a long game: the longer an area is surveyed, the more valuable the series. There is a helpdesk with named staff, courses run year-round, and observers receive reports on the counts they joined. Counting is free to join and membership is not required.

trackers.name: SNL natuurbeheer — provincial money for managing nature land, and how a small owner joins
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: managers with nature land inside the Natuur Netwerk Nederland can receive subsidy for nature and landscape management; the provinces set the possibilities and conditions, state in the provincial Natuurbeheerplan which beheertype is eligible where, and publish Openstellingsbesluiten saying which types are funded, at what contribution, and how much money is available in total. BIJ12 runs the shared administration for the provinces. THE TWO BARRIERS, AND THE WAY ROUND THEM — this is the useful part: managers must hold a certificate, applied for from the Stichting Certificering SNL before the application period, and since 2017 must have and manage a minimum number of hectares within the Natuur Netwerk in that province to apply directly. One province states the threshold plainly: private individuals may apply if they are certified and manage at least 150 hectares of nature — and if not, they can join one of the named natuurcollectieven and apply through that route. A smallholder is not excluded; they are routed through a collective. WHO ELSE QUALIFIES: terreinbeherende organisaties, private nature managers who own the land, hold it in erfpacht of more than 25 years, or have beklemrecht, and municipalities. Named TBOs in one province are Het Drents Landschap, Natuurmonumenten and Staatsbosbeheer, plus the Natuurcollectief and the Unie van Bosgroepen. Waterschappen, water companies, central government bodies and the provinces themselves are excluded — so in the Netherlands, unlike France, the water authority is not the funder here. THE TERMS: subsidy normally stays the same for a six-year run; a lump sum agreement is a performance arrangement between province and manager covering at least six years and able to include layout, recreation and species policy alongside management. Provinces may add their own money and, in special cases such as extra protection for Natura 2000 areas or particular species, add area-specific management packages. AND SEPARATELY, PROVINCES FUND THE CONVERSION ITSELF: one province states there is subsidy available for converting agricultural land into nature, laying out new nature areas, and restoring existing ones.

trackers.name: The provincial Natuurfonds — 7,700 donors, €1.1 million, nine land purchases
trackers.desc: THE MODEL, AND ITS ACTUAL NUMBERS: a provincial landscape foundation launched a Natuurfonds to buy land together with concerned residents in order to create new nature, and five years later 7,700 donors had raised 1.1 million euro and NINE LAND PURCHASES had been made. The stated aim is to expand local nature by 1 million m² in five years by buying ground and turning it into nature. HOW THE ARITHMETIC IS PUT TO A DONOR, which is the part to copy: they reckon with 7.50 euro per square metre, financing BOTH THE PURCHASE OF LAND AND ITS LAYOUT, using an average price per hectare — and they say plainly that land prices differ strongly by region. The donor makes it possible to buy a piece of nature but does not become its owner; the land is added to the 100 nature areas the foundation already protects, and is thereby immediately secured for the future. A WORKED PURCHASE: in one historic polder, three parcels of agricultural grassland totalling eight hectares, which together with an earlier purchase forms the basis for a large, coherent nature area. AND THE OPENING LINE OF THEIR OWN APPEAL, which is why this belongs here: you probably know the feeling — out of nowhere, yet another business park appears in the neighbourhood. Or another road, or a storage centre.

trackers.name: Which Dutch bodies buy what — and the honest warning about small parcels
trackers.desc: THE WARNING FIRST, because it saves a wasted approach: nature organisations such as Staatsbosbeheer, Natuurmonumenten or the provincial landscapes generally buy ONLY LARGE nature areas, often financed by government for both purchase and management. SMALL PARCELS OF WOODLAND ARE USUALLY NOT INTERESTING to them. THE TWO EXCEPTIONS THAT MAKE YOUR PARCEL INTERESTING: if the parcels are STRATEGICALLY SITUATED in relation to their existing holdings, or if the realisation of the ecological network is brought closer by them. Argue adjacency and network, not beauty — and the national body's own 2025 acquisitions bear that out: 5 hectares that adjoined its other parcels, creating a more robust meadow-bird area; 2.1 hectares of wet nature ALREADY SURROUNDED by its ownership, allowing efficient management and a new ditch; 5 hectares already enclosed on three sides; and 12 hectares assigned by the province, falling within the national ecological network. SCALE, FOR CONTEXT: the national body owns and manages more than 112,000 hectares with over 2,100 special buildings, built up over 115 years, and the twelve provincial landscapes hold a comparable area between them; one provincial landscape alone owns almost 5,700 hectares and states that ALL LAND IT BUYS IS LAID OUT AS NATURE. A CAUTION RECORDED PLAINLY: there have been plans by the state forestry body to SELL forest and nature grounds lying outside the ecological network — politically contested. Check whether the ground near you sits inside or outside the network.

trackers.name: Natuur en Milieufederatie Limburg — it tells you what land COSTS before you start raising it
trackers.desc: THE PRICES, WHICH NOBODY ELSE IN THIS FILE PUBLISHES: land is expensive, certainly in the Netherlands. A HECTARE OF WOODLAND SOON COSTS 10,000–15,000 EURO. FOR A HECTARE OF AGRICULTURAL LAND IT CAN BE 50,000 TO AS MUCH AS 100,000 EURO, depending on soil type, location and workability. A community deciding whether to buy or to fight needs that number first, and a provincial environmental federation is the body that will give it to you straight. AND THE THREE THINGS IT SAYS YOU MUST HAVE, which is the honest checklist for any purchase plan: there must be money for the acquisition; there must be A PARTY THAT TAKES THE LAND INTO OWNERSHIP; and there must also be money AND ORGANISATIONAL CAPACITY to manage the area 'for eternity'. WHY IT IS WORTH IT ANYWAY, in its own words: once the land is privately held for nature, the decision about what happens to the area is no longer (only) up to politics, or to how much money can be made from it — by turning it into a business park, building houses, growing lilies or maize, or developing a holiday park. The quality of the area — its meaning for biodiversity, its landscape beauty and its experiential value — becomes central, and is SECURED BY THE PRIVATE OWNERSHIP. AND WHO TO JOIN: it names the national association and the provincial landscape body, which has A SPECIAL PURCHASE FUND FOR NATURE.

trackers.name: The Noord-Hollands Natuurfonds — 7.50 euro a square metre, and it buys BEFORE the land is lost
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS FOR, stated exactly: the fund exists to finance land purchases and so secure nature BEFORE IT IS LOST TO NEW BUILDING SUCH AS DISTRIBUTION CENTRES, DATA STORAGE AND ROADS. By becoming the owner of the land, it is easier to protect the nature for eternity. Buying ahead of the threat rather than after it is the whole logic, and this file has recorded the same reasoning in Czechia (insurance policy) and Austria (blocking parcels). THE RESULTS, FIVE YEARS ON: 7,700 donors raised 1.1 million euro, leading to NINE LAND PURCHASES totalling more than 63 hectares — 630,000 square metres secured. Individual purchases named: just over 4 hectares near one village in 2021, nearly 5 hectares in a polder in 2022, and 4 hectares of agricultural land in a dune-edge nature area in a strategic spot, creating A CONTINUOUS NATURE AREA. HOW IT WORKS FOR AN ORDINARY DONOR: for 7.50 euro per square metre, residents can buy a piece of nature — for themselves, the family, or as a gift for someone else — and receive a PERSONAL CERTIFICATE stating the number of square metres secured for the future. The purchased land is added to the more than 100 nature areas the organisation already manages, and is thereby protected for ever, within the national ecological network. Donors were invited to come and see the area they had paid for, and the crowdfunding runs continuously.

trackers.name: Omnius — a free intake desk into omgevingsrecht advocates, and it tells you to move fast
trackers.desc: WHAT IT OFFERS: a route into affiliated omgevingsrecht advocates through an INTAKE DESK, with a FREE INTAKE CONVERSATION with a jurist — and it will support a zienswijze, a bezwaar, a beroep or hoger beroep, or an application for a VOORLOPIGE VOORZIENING, the interim measure that stops work while the case runs. The Netherlands had 32 filed entries and two legal resources. ITS WARNING, WHICH IS THE POINT: has someone else's permit been (provisionally) granted and do you have objections? ACT QUICKLY, because the ways to make your voice heard have STRICT TIME LIMITS. And it names the harms it deals with plainly — a festival or street party causing nuisance to residents and DAMAGING THE GREENERY at the location, or a neighbour whose building plans disadvantage you. AND THE FOUR MOMENTS IT IDENTIFIES: a ZIENSWIJZE while a plan is not yet final; a BEZWAAR against a decision taken; BEROEP at the court; and HOGER BEROEP at the Council of State. The zienswijze is the free one, and it comes before everything else. IT ALSO NAMES THE ENFORCEMENT ROUTE: where someone builds contrary to the bestemmingsplan or fails to keep to the conditions of a permit, the municipality must act — and a second Dutch practice calls this a HANDHAVINGSVERZOEK: you can ask your municipality to act against an infringement or to investigate a possible one, after which it must investigate and can impose a fine or end the infringement itself.

trackers.name: Dutch omgevingsrecht specialists — free first conversation, and the nature-law side named
trackers.desc: WHAT THEY OFFER A RESIDENT: one practice invites you to call for a FIRST FREE CONVERSATION with a published phone number, for help making a bezwaar or lodging a beroep; another describes itself as a firm specialised in omgevingsrecht and general administrative law whose listed fields include omgevingsplannen, omgevingsvergunningen, VERGUNNINGVRIJ BOUWEN, NADEELCOMPENSATIE AND PLANSCHADE, NATUURBESCHERMING, NITROGEN, NOISE, AIR QUALITY, EXTERNAL SAFETY, SOIL AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT. Nature protection, nitrogen and planschade sit in the same practice as the permit itself — so one instruction can cover the ecological objection and the compensation claim together. AND THE TWO TECHNICAL POINTS THESE FIRMS PUT IN PUBLIC, which decide many Dutch cases: the omgevingsvergunning is a GEBONDEN BESCHIKKING — the municipal executive has NO POLICY FREEDOM and MUST grant it if the conditions are met, chiefly that the activity is not contrary to the Bouwbesluit, not contrary to the municipal Bouwverordening, and PERMITTED UNDER THE BESTEMMINGSPLAN. So the fight is usually about the bestemmingsplan, not the permit. And the plan itself carries building rules — maximum height, the permitted building envelope — AND USE RULES, so an office in a building designated solely for housing is itself a breach. A welstandscommissie advises separately on appearance.

trackers.name: Natuurfonds Brabant — buy land by the SQUARE METRE, at a published price
trackers.desc: THE SMALLEST UNIT OF LAND PURCHASE RECORDED IN THIS FILE: AS A PROTECTOR YOU CAN, ALONGSIDE THE ANNUAL CONTRIBUTION, ALSO BUY ONE OR MORE SQUARE METRES OF LAND THROUGH THE NATURE FUND. EVERY SQUARE METRE COUNTS. Netherlands had five acquisition entries against 34 total. A resource priced per square metre lets a village of ordinary households buy a field between them — no single donor and no grant application required. AND THE PRICE, PUBLISHED WITH ITS REASONING: WE RECKON WITH AN AMOUNT OF 7.50 EURO PER SQUARE METRE. WITH THIS WE FINANCE BOTH THE PURCHASE OF LAND AND THE RESTORATION OF NATURE AND THE MANAGEMENT IN THE YEARS AFTERWARDS. The foundation is candid that LAND PRICES DIFFER STRONGLY BY REGION; IN PRACTICE SOME PARCELS WILL TURN OUT MORE EXPENSIVE, FOR EXAMPLE WHERE IT IS SOUGHT-AFTER AGRICULTURAL LAND. THEN THE PRICE QUICKLY RISES FROM EIGHT TO TWELVE EURO PER SQUARE METRE. A price that covers purchase, restoration and years of management is the honest number — most appeals quote only the purchase. AND WHICH PARCELS THEY WANT, which tells a community what to offer: PARCELS THAT BORDER OUR EXISTING NATURE AREAS ARE VERY INTERESTING, BECAUSE WITH THEM WE CAN MAKE NATURE BIGGER AND MORE ROBUST. Since a first purchase in 1963 the foundation protects SOME 19,000 HECTARES.

trackers.name: Four ways to buy land together — and the scale the Dutch private bodies reached
trackers.desc: THE SCALE THAT PRIVATE PURCHASE HAS REACHED IN ONE SMALL COUNTRY: DO NOT FORGET THE PRIVATE NATURE ORGANISATIONS THAT, WITH THE SUPPORT OF THEIR LARGE NUMBERS OF MEMBERS AND OF THE GOVERNMENT, BUY NATURE AREAS AND DEVELOP NEW ONES. FOR YEARS ON END — with one body having made 110,000 HECTARES OF PURCHASES IN 115 YEARS, and THE 12 PROVINCIAL LANDSCAPE ORGANISATIONS WITH A COMPARABLE SURFACE AREA. Netherlands had five acquisition entries against 34 total. Twelve provincial land-buying bodies means there is one for every region, not a single national office to queue at — and between them they match the national body's holdings. AND THE ROUTES IT SETS OUT FOR ACTING TOGETHER: THERE ARE ORGANISATIONS THAT BUY UP PIECES OF LAND AND THEN LET NATURE TAKE ITS FREE COURSE, ORGANISATIONS THAT PROTECT NATURE AREAS IN COOPERATION WITH NATURE-CONSERVATION ORGANISATIONS, OR INITIATIVES WHERE LAND IS BOUGHT FOR SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE. Buying land for farming that will not be developed is a route a community can take where conservation buyers are not interested, and the piece names working examples — a citizens' farm, a pick-your-own garden, a market gardener, a land foundation, a regional future park and a bee foundation. The stated principle of one initiative is COLLECTIVE BUYING, DECIDING TOGETHER AND COLLECTIVE PROTECTION.

trackers.name: Groene Bewonersinitiatieven — 3 neighbours, no legal entity needed
trackers.desc: THE OPPOSITE OF EVERY OTHER FUND IN THIS MAP. Applicants can be a group of at least 3 neighbours, each registered at a different address in the same neighbourhood — no association, foundation or legal personality required. Up to 100 percent of eligible costs, maximum EUR 4,000 per application. APPLY EARLY, NOT PERFECTLY: subsidy is allocated in order of arrival, not by competitive scoring. WHAT TO SUBMIT: a project plan with a management and maintenance plan for the coming year, and a signed written document describing the cooperation and naming a penvoerder (lead applicant), signed by every participant. REFUSAL GROUNDS — CHECK THESE BEFORE YOU START: the project is not accessible to the public; the activity began before you applied; subsidy already received for a comparable project; or costs exceed the maximum with no covering budget. No chemical pesticides, and the initiative must fit provincial, municipal and water board policy. Favoured: biodiversity-strengthening measures, and applicants who do the work themselves.

trackers.name: Finding your municipality's green money (NME Fonds, Amsterdam)
trackers.desc: A CITY FUND AND, MORE USEFULLY, HOW TO FIND YOURS. Amsterdam's NME Fonds is provided by the municipality for nature and sustainability education and is open to residents' groups as well as foundations and associations, with roughly EUR 20,000 available a year, executed by Natuurhub Amsterdam. THE TRANSFERABLE METHOD: municipalities support residents' initiatives from many different policy areas — health, liveability, play policy, climate adaptation, biodiversity — so the money is rarely filed under ‘nature’. In larger municipalities ask for the district wijkregisseur, wijkteam or wijkmakelaar, who is the first contact and will find which pot fits; in smaller ones ask for the policy officer for green, nature or landscape, or the local nature and environmental education centre. And search your own municipality's website for adoptiegroen, boomspiegel, boomtuintje, geveltuintje and regenton — the terms the schemes are actually filed under.

trackers.name: Datatilsynet (Danish DPA)
trackers.desc: Datatilsynet (Danish DPA) — Denmark’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.desc: Official portal of the Danish courts with selected judgments and court information. · Find here: the Danish courts' portal with information and selected judgments (Danmarks Domstole).

trackers.name: Danish Parliamentary Ombudsman
trackers.desc: Denmark’s Parliamentary Ombudsman, appointed by the Folketing to scrutinise public administration.

trackers.name: Danmarks Naturfredningsforening (Danish Society for Nature Conservation)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: Denmark's largest nature and environment organisation (founded 1911, ~130,000 members, 95 local branches) and — uniquely — THE ONLY PRIVATE ASSOCIATION IN DENMARK WITH THE STATUTORY RIGHT TO PROPOSE THAT AN AREA BE PROTECTED (rejse fredningssager), a power granted by the 1937 amendment to the Nature Conservation Act. Over 5% of Denmark's land area is now protected. USE IT: this is the sharpest protection lever in Denmark — if a Danish site is threatened, getting DN to raise a fredningssag is a route no other NGO has. They also work on planning consideration for nature, and have local branches across the country.

trackers.name: Danmarks Naturfredningsforening — local branches (afdelinger)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a list and map of DN's local branches across Denmark. USE IT: to reach the volunteers who already know the municipality, the planners and the site — the people to call first before escalating to a national protection case.

Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Denmark.

trackers.name: Fredning — how a protection case is raised and appealed
trackers.desc: A ROUTE THAT EXISTS ALMOST NOWHERE ELSE: Danmarks Naturfredningsforening holds statutory status in conservation matters — granted by a 1937 amendment to the Nature Conservation Act — and can raise a fredning case over land it does not own, typically together with the kommune. ASK FOR THE INTERIM BAN: while a fredning case is being prepared, the minister and the kommunalbestyrelse may impose a preliminary prohibition on using the property or establishing anything that conflicts with the intended fredning — that is the thing to request when machinery is arriving. The proposal goes to the fredningsnævn, which as a rule holds a public meeting and a site inspection, decides content and extent, and awards compensation and costs for expert assistance. Its decision can be appealed to the Miljø- og Fødevareklagenævnet by owners, users, authorities, DN and others who asked to be heard; the substance can then go to the ordinary courts within 6 months, while the size of compensation is appealed separately to the Taksationskommissionen. BE REALISTIC ABOUT TIME: in the Gisselfeld Kloster case, raised in October 2022 over 255 hectares, the nævn protected only 14.3 hectares in October 2024, and the appeal continues — with reports that the nævn takes about 2 years before it is ready to inspect.

trackers.name: Klagevejledning — who may complain, and does it stop the works?
trackers.desc: TWO QUESTIONS TO SETTLE BEFORE FILING. First, you must be klageberettiget, and the rules differ for each statute — named bodies hold specific rights, for instance Danmarks Naturfredningsforening, Danmarks Sportsfiskerforbund and Forbrugerrådet over water-abstraction permits under §§ 20, 21 and 32. Second, and more urgent: whether a complaint has opsættende virkning (suspensive effect) is set by each special act — so filing does not automatically stop the works. A complainant may expressly request that suspensive effect be granted, or that it be lifted. ASK FOR IT IN THE COMPLAINT rather than assuming it. Most complaints go through the klageportal; some categories must be sent via Digital Post. ENCOURAGING NUMBER: Danmarks Naturfredningsforening reported winning 85 percent of decisions on complaints it filed in 2018 — 175 complaints filed, 92 decided — on a small and selective caseload.

trackers.name: Den Danske Naturfond — grants, and a buyer of last resort
trackers.desc: TWO WAYS TO USE IT. AS A GRANT SOURCE: the Naturfond's local nature and biodiversity pool is open to associations, organisations and private landowners — individual owners are excluded from most conservation money, so this is a different door. One round allocated up to 15 million kroner. It funds locally rooted projects that secure and improve existing natural areas or create new ones and more habitats; projects must target specific areas or habitats and the money must go to actual nature restoration or management on that land — not campaigning, staff or study. AS A PURCHASER: the Naturfond buys land itself. It has bought in Vejle Ådal 3 times to assemble large connected nature, and expanded Grønnestrand by 135 hectares to more than 600 with 37.5 million kroner from Nordea-fonden. USE THAT: if a threatened site is too big for a local group to buy, the Naturfond is the body that can.

trackers.name: Udlodningsmidler til Friluftsliv — Friluftsrådet's grant pools
trackers.desc: REGULAR, DATED MONEY AT BOTH ENDS OF THE SCALE. Local projects: grants from 20,000 kroner. National projects: from 200,000 kroner. Scale from the 2025 annual report: 71.8 million kroner to 504 projects. DEADLINES RECUR, SO PLAN AROUND THEM: 15 June for national projects, 15 September for local and national together; the Lokalforeningspulje, for local associations under Friluftsrådet's member organisations, next closes 15 May 2027. Ring the pool administration before applying on 33 79 00 79 (option 2) or tilskud@friluftsraadet.dk — they offer sparring on whether an idea fits. MIND THE PURPOSE LIMIT: this is friluftsliv money — improving access to nature, getting more people outdoors, strengthening public knowledge of nature. A pure habitat or anti-development project fits badly; a public-access angle is what makes it eligible. SEPARATE AND USEFUL: Friluftsrådet says there are thousands of illegal barriers in Danish nature, and invites you to send in a sign, gate or other barrier you suspect is unlawful and get help assessing it.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Danmarks Naturfond — the fund that buys, separate from the society that campaigns
trackers.desc: DENMARK SEPARATES THE CAMPAIGNING BODY FROM THE LAND-BUYING BODY, AND YOU NEED THE RIGHT ONE. Danmarks Naturfond is a separate foundation, established by Danmarks Naturfredningsforening in 1967 expressly to add a capability the society did not have: ‘køb af dansk natur’ — the purchase of Danish nature. In its own words the fund buys and develops some of Denmark's wildest natural areas. So if the answer to a development is that somebody should buy the land, the FUND is the counterparty, not the society. Its board is seven unpaid members on three-year terms, and it publishes board meeting minutes, bank details and staff contact details — published minutes mean you can see what it is considering and when it meets. THE SOCIETY IS THE OTHER HALF, AND ITS POSITION IS UNUSUAL: founded 1911, Danmarks Naturfredningsforening was given a statutory status in conservation matters when the Nature Conservation Act was modified in 1937. A private membership organisation holding a statutory role in conservation cases is rare — in most countries an NGO must establish standing case by case. Here the legislature granted it. That is why DN is the body to bring into a Danish conservation case. AND IT IS EVERYWHERE: 95 local branches across the country and around 130,000 members (sources give 130,000 to 140,000, with a peak of 260,784 in 1987), with a secretariat of about fifty. Ninety-five branches means there is one near your site — and as in Belgium, the local branch is the practical entry point, not the national secretariat. Its stated concerns expressly include consideration for the natural environment in public planning and public access to natural resources.

trackers.name: Den Danske Naturfond — buys land by voluntary agreement (Denmark)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: an independent, private, non-profit foundation that buys land anywhere in Denmark, restores it, manages it and holds it permanently, with free public access. It was created in 2015 with start capital from three founders together — the Danish state, Aage V. Jensen Naturfond and VILLUM FONDEN. It states that every purchase is made by voluntary agreement with a private landowner, which means the fund is a buyer waiting for a willing seller, and persuading the owner is the community's job rather than the fund's. USE IT: the route nobody suggests is in one of its own purchases. At Grønnestrand on the Jammerbugt coast it bought 145 hectares from six local owners at once, taking the protected area to roughly 800 hectares — neighbours selling together made viable what no single parcel would have. It also buys and runs sites in partnership with the municipality and other local bodies as a matter of course, so a council is a party to the deal rather than an obstacle to it, and a 20-hectare purchase in Vejle Ådal sat inside a 450-hectare climate-and-nature project. Separately it funds local grassroots nature projects through its ildsjælepuljer, which is a smaller and much faster door. THE LIMIT IT PUBLISHES: it deliberately does not spend its capital at once, because wages, rent and property tax on everything it owns must be paid every year for the next fifty. Donations, by contrast, go entirely to buying land. Contact: Hillerødgade 30A, 2200 København N, kontakt@naturfonden.dk, 71 99 72 01.

trackers.name: DOF BirdLife — 13 local branches that handle your council's planning cases (Denmark)
trackers.desc: THE STRUCTURE THAT MATTERS: DOF BirdLife's local work is done by 13 local branches covering the whole country — from the North Jutland dunes and the Limfjord bird fjords to the Wadden Sea tidal flats, Funen's green archipelago, the Zealand woodlands and the rocky coasts of Bornholm. All the work in the branches is done on a voluntary, unpaid basis, and each holds an annual general meeting at which every member has a vote. WHY THIS IS THE ENTRY POINT FOR A DANISH PLANNING FIGHT: a branch's Naturpolitisk Udvalg — nature policy committee — works chiefly on nature management, conservation-order and planning cases coming from the municipalities, and aims to have a representative for every municipality in the branch's area. DOF is also represented on the Grønne Råd — green councils — in several municipalities and on the state forest district user council, and it says openly that anyone interested in sitting on those bodies should contact the board to discuss it. A resident can end up in the room where the council discusses green matters, by asking. WHAT IT CAN PUT BEHIND YOUR CASE: the branches are described as the backbone of the organisation's nature protection work — collecting bird population data through DOFbasen, running projects for threatened species, and advising municipalities, schools and nature managers on better habitats. Nationally the organisation works through political work, expert consultation responses and cooperation with the authorities, and it has established the network of volunteer caretaker groups watching over Denmark's 128 Important Bird Areas, and contributed to the designation of Special Protection Areas holding legal protection under EU law. SO THE TWO QUESTIONS TO ASK YOUR BRANCH: is our site inside an IBA or a Special Protection Area, and does the branch already have a representative for our municipality. Both are answerable in a phone call. WHAT IT IS NOT: a membership society, not a land buyer and not a law firm. Denmark's land buyers are the two nature foundations already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Danmarks Naturfond — land acquired by bequest, and local branches propose the purchases
trackers.desc: NOT TO BE CONFUSED with Den Danske Naturfond, already in this file. This is a different body: founded 1967 by Danmarks Naturfredningsforening, with the purpose of preserving landscape and cultural-historical values, protecting animal and plant life and securing recreational areas for the population by acquiring and operating real property, and of supporting conservation purposes. Its head office is at Skovsgaard Gods on Langeland. WHERE ITS MONEY COMES FROM, WHICH IS THE POINT: collections, gifts and inheritance — particularly testamentary gifts. Its acquisitions over the years are described as largely the result of generous contributions, legacies and gifts. A first legacy of one million kroner in 1969 paid for its first purchase. Skovsgaard Gods came in 1979 as a bequest from an owner who wanted the property and its nature not to be exploited or built on after her death but to stay in nature-conserving hands. An owner who wants their land protected after death has a Danish body built to receive it. AND LOCAL BRANCHES CAN PROPOSE WHAT IT BUYS: on the parent association's 75th anniversary in 1986, all its local committees around the country were invited to propose acquisitions for the money raised by an anniversary collection; the Randers committee put forward an oak wood at Langå, which the fund bought in 1992. A community that knows the ground worth saving can put it into that pipeline. WHAT IT HOLDS: it owned 16 properties with nature areas totalling more than 600 hectares as at 2016, and by a later account 13 nature areas, with public access at every one. Named holdings include Skovsgaard Gods on Langeland, Rubjerg Knude in Vendsyssel, Jordløse Bakker on Funen, Allindelille Fredskov on Zealand, and Helligdomsklipperne and Døndalen on Bornholm. WHAT IT DOES WITH THE LAND: at Skovsgaard it is converting farmland to wild nature — 234 to 245 hectares of fields, nature areas and forest inside one fence with cattle, wild horses and pigs living out all year, unfed and never stalled — a project to which Den Danske Naturfond contributed 1.25 million kroner. The two Danish foundations fund each other's work, which is worth knowing before choosing which to approach. ONE HONEST CAVEAT: converting productive farmland to untouched forest and wild grazing at Skovsgaard has drawn litigation against the parent association. Ambitious rewilding on donated agricultural land is contested in Denmark, and a community proposing it should expect that.

trackers.name: HOMANN Advokater — runs plan cases at the appeal board and the ordinary courts
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: a Copenhagen firm whose plan and environment practice states that this is specialist law requiring assistance from specialised lawyers, and that the office's lawyers have extensive experience conducting cases on planning-law questions before the appeal board and the ordinary courts. Denmark's bucket had DN, the two land funds and DOF but no lawyer; this is the first. WHAT THEY COVER, and it is the whole toolkit a community needs: the miljøbeskyttelseslov, planlov and naturbeskyttelseslov; nævnssager, kommissionssager and court cases about lokalplaner and kommuneplaner — the local and municipal plans that decide what may be built; and hævd, nabo­ret including the tålegrænse (tolerance limit) and servitutter — prescription, neighbour law and easements, which are the private-law routes when the public ones run out. It advises landowners, companies AND authorities, so check for conflicts before instructing.

trackers.name: Danish plan-law appeal practice — what the Planklagenævn will and will not overturn
trackers.desc: WHY THIS IS FILED ALONGSIDE A FIRM: a Danish plan-law practice publishes worked appeal outcomes that tell a community which objections succeed. Before a municipality grants a landzone permit, neighbours must be given the chance to comment — the nabo­høring — and the applicant is obliged to take account of the objections raised, which the authority must carefully consider. If you are refused or dissatisfied, the Planklagenævn is the highest appeal instance and its decisions cannot be appealed to a higher authority; you file through its klageportal. THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES CASES, from published outcomes: a dispensation from a lokalplan was set aside as invalid because a heating plant was a production facility contrary to the plan's PRINCIPLES — but where a municipality allowed breaches of bebyggelsesprocent, storey numbers and building height, the board agreed the detail provisions had been exceeded yet could not overturn the decision, because those detail provisions were not part of the plan's principles. Attack the plan's purpose and principles, not its numbers. Dispensations must also comply with administrative law on neighbour and party hearing and on detailed reasoning — a separate line of attack when the process was rushed.

trackers.name: Aage V. Jensen Naturfond — it asks volunteers to FIND small sites for it to buy
trackers.desc: THE INVITATION, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT: the fund has in recent years encouraged voluntary organisations — the botanical society, Danmarks Naturfredningsforening and the ornithological society — TO FIND SMALLER AREAS OF NATURE WHICH, AFTER ACQUISITION BY THE FUNDS, COULD BE CARED FOR BY THOSE ORGANISATIONS' LOCAL BRANCHES. The stated purposes were to secure small natural jewels by purchase, to give local people responsibility for the operation and care of smaller areas in their own neighbourhood, and to promote local nature. A fund that wants local groups to bring it land to buy is the rarest resource in this file. WHAT IT IS: an erhvervsdrivende fond established in 2007 when a charity transferred all 24 of its Danish nature properties, about 14,000 hectares, plus 300 million DKK for nature restoration and protection. It now owns 31 individual nature areas across 23 localities totalling 19,300 hectares. HOW TO APPLY, AND THE THRESHOLD RECORDED PLAINLY: through its application portal only — applications are not accepted by email or ordinary post. It supports conservation and development of nature and protection of wild animals in Denmark, via research, management or communication. It does not as a rule support projects under 300,000 DKK, unless they are aimed at the Fund's own nature areas. A separate sister fund supports wild nature in Denmark, Greenland and the Faroes.

trackers.name: KL's oversigt over fonde — a published list of the Danish funds that pay for nature projects
trackers.desc: WHY IT EXISTS: local government Denmark records that many municipalities find it difficult to get an overview of which funds are relevant for financing nature projects, and so published an overview of the funds that can contribute. It says plainly that although aimed primarily at municipalities, it is also relevant for private actors and organisations working on more and better nature. WHAT THE LIST GIVES YOU PER FUND: who may apply, what may be applied for, and the application rhythm — several entries note no fixed application rounds, but four annual board meetings, which tells you when to submit. Eligible categories recorded include nature restoration projects, preliminary studies and research, and communication, involvement and dialogue. AND THE LARGEST NUMBER IN IT, with its limit stated: one foundation has committed 10 billion DKK over ten years to projects supporting the green tripartite agreement, focused on concrete measures affecting nature, biodiversity and sustainable land use — but it does not itself buy areas; it supports projects run by actors with relevant competence and experience. Read what a fund will NOT do before applying. NAMED ELSEWHERE AS 'NATURE'S FUNDS': Aage V. Jensen Naturfond, Villum and Velux, Den Danske Naturfond, Nordea-fonden and 15. Juni Fonden — which have jointly run open pools for local associations, one distributing six million DKK in grants of 20,000 to 100,000 DKK to non-profit associations.

trackers.name: How a Danish fredning case is actually raised — and it usually starts in the local branch
trackers.desc: WHERE THE CASES COME FROM, which is the whole point for a community: many of the fredning cases raised by DN are raised ON THE INITIATIVE OF THE ASSOCIATION'S LOCAL BRANCHES. Since 1937 it has held a special statutory right to propose areas for protection, on a par with the state and the municipalities, and it can independently submit a proposal to the board. Its local branches are already filed here. HOW THE PROPOSAL IS BUILT: once the national board decides to raise a case, the secretariat prepares the proposal WITH INPUT FROM THE LOCAL BRANCH and often in consultation with the specialist committees; proposals differ because each is adapted to the area and the purpose; and the finished proposal plus a budget estimate of expected compensation goes to a four-week consultation with the authorities not co-raising it. THE TIMELINE, HONESTLY: a case can go twice round the fredningsnævn and twice round the appeals board — up to eight years — though that is rare and most are finally decided within four years. AND THE ARGUMENT ABOUT LOCAL OPPOSITION, worth carrying anywhere: it is common for a fredning proposal to get a mixed reception or provoke outright resistance at first. Experience shows, however, that once completed, fredninger are almost always popular. They become a source of local pride and often make the neighbourhood more attractive — house advertisements refer to protected areas nearby. Reasons still to raise them include that many worthy areas are periodically threatened by urban development and road schemes, and that old, outdated fredning provisions need revising to work as intended.

trackers.name: Ekholm Scheffmann — planret specialists, and they tell you the two clocks that decide everything
trackers.desc: WHAT THEY DO: a Danish practice offering honest and objective advice based on extensive practical experience and specialised legal expertise within PLANRET, with extensive experience working with LOKALPLANER. Denmark had 42 filed entries and only two legal resources. AND THE ADVICE THEY GIVE FREE ON THEIR OWN PAGE, which is the single most useful thing a Danish resident can know: when the municipality does not take your comments into account and does not adjust its plan in the consultation phase as you wished, you can appeal the decision on the lokalplan — once finally approved — to the Planklagenævn, WITH A DEADLINE OF FOUR WEEKS after the municipality adopts it. BUT ONLY LEGAL QUESTIONS CAN GO TO THAT BOARD; A DISCRETIONARY JUDGEMENT MADE BY THE MUNICIPALITY MUST BE TAKEN TO THE COURTS, WHERE THE DEADLINE IS SIX MONTHS. Two forums, two clocks, and choosing the wrong one loses the case on admissibility. AND THE NEIGHBOUR ROUTE THE SAME FIRM SETS OUT: you can complain if you believe the building conflicts with the building act, the building regulations, the lokalplan or the building permit — OR IF YOU WERE NOT GIVEN NABOORIENTERING OR PARTSHØRING despite having substantial neighbour interests. React quickly, especially while the building work is under way, and with the complaint you can request that it be given SUSPENSIVE EFFECT, so the board decides whether the building must be halted while it considers the case.

trackers.name: Danish naboret and forvaltningsret practices — free first call, and the cases they have won
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: nationwide specialists in NABORETSSAGER, construction law, PLANRET and family cases, offering a free and non-binding conversation and an unobligated assessment of your case. A second practice offers assistance in building cases, COMPLAINTS TO THE PLANKLAGENÆVN, and assessment of errors in building-case handling or planning, plus advice in naboret cases — fences, boundaries, NOISE AND OVERLOOKING NUISANCE — and representation in cases against municipalities and public authorities, where success turns on administrative principles such as PARTSHØRING, THE DUTY TO GIVE REASONS, AND PROPORTIONALITY. THE WINS THEY PUBLISH, which tell you what actually succeeds: a municipality permitted a heating plant in an area zoned for public purposes, and the board held it was a production facility not serving public purposes, so the dispensation was SET ASIDE as contrary to THE PLAN'S PRINCIPLES; and separately, lokalplaner must be formulated in clear and accessible language and must not be unclear. A CLIENT ACCOUNT RECORDED AS EVIDENCE THE ROUTE WORKS: one describes a case about exceeding the naboretlige tålegrænse because of high trees against a neighbour — WE WON THE CASE IN BOTH THE CITY COURT AND THE HIGH COURT. AND A TRAP THEY NAME: builders sometimes evade storey limits with large dormers and knee walls, making the upper floor habitable without it counting as a full storey — and an open balcony on a garage or roof can also be regarded as a separate storey.

trackers.name: The Danish nature funds together — six funders in one room, and a pool for LOCAL activities
trackers.desc: WHAT THIS RECORDS: the country's nature funders act together, and publish it. Six funds appear side by side at the national nature meeting, each with a NAMED CONTACT AND DIRECT PHONE NUMBER — a nature fund, a national nature fund, a June-dated foundation, a bank-linked foundation and two building-linked foundations — and all six are present for dialogue with interested parties for half an hour afterwards. Six named funders with published phone numbers, in one room, on one day, is the cheapest fundraising trip a Danish community will ever make. AND THE POOL THAT IS ACTUALLY REACHABLE: alongside a five-million-kroner contribution from one fund, a pool from the three funds and the outdoor-life lottery distribution has awarded a total of 6.4 MILLION KRONER TO LOCAL ACTIVITIES. AND WHAT EACH LOOKS FOR, in their own words: one prioritises supporting projects that direct Danish nature management towards IMPORTANT AND CONSERVATION-WORTHY BIODIVERSITY, so that management becomes increasingly KNOWLEDGE-BASED AND WITH LASTING EFFECT; the other, in acquiring land, states plainly we do not compete with the public sector, other funds or green organisations for the acquisition of nature areas, and works with green associations in LOCAL NATURE COUNCILS for our large properties to ensure LOCAL ANCHORING.

trackers.name: Den Danske Naturfond — 26 km² bought, and a fund FOR LOCAL ENTHUSIASTS' own projects
trackers.desc: WHAT IT HAS BOUGHT: since beginning work in 2016 the fund has bought up around 26 SQUARE KILOMETRES of land across 20 PROJECTS — and counting the private projects it has supported through its ILDSJÆLEPULJER (enthusiasts' funds), it has helped nature IN 75 AREAS totalling around 65 SQUARE KILOMETRES, with a combined investment budget of around 500 MILLION KRONER. A national land-buying fund that ALSO runs a pot for local enthusiasts' own projects is two resources in one, and the second is the one a small group can reach. HOW IT WORKS WITH PEOPLE ON THE GROUND: the projects on the purchased areas are ALWAYS carried out IN COOPERATION WITH MUNICIPALITIES AND OTHER LOCAL FORCES, and there is free access to the fund's areas. Restoration can mean REMOVING CONIFER PLANTATIONS to give more room to broadleaf woodland, or releasing grazing animals such as horses. AND THE DONATION FLOOR, which is unusually low: supporters can receive a FOREST CERTIFICATE OR A NATURE CERTIFICATE if they finance the purchase of A MINIMUM OF 120 SQUARE METRES. A hundred and twenty square metres is a floor a school class can clear, and the fund states that all donations go undiminished to the purchase of more wild nature. One recorded purchase was about 170 hectares of a named forest holding an island's last population of a named butterfly.

trackers.name: 145 hectares bought from SIX LOCAL LANDOWNERS at once — how a Danish purchase is assembled
trackers.desc: HOW A LARGE AREA IS ACTUALLY PUT TOGETHER, which is the practical answer to fragmented ownership: with the acquisition of A FURTHER 145 HECTARES OF LAND, the national nature fund takes a step toward CREATING DENMARK'S LARGEST CONTINUOUS WILDERNESS across two named districts, and THE NEW NATURE AREA HAS BEEN BOUGHT FROM SIX LOCAL LANDOWNERS. Denmark had four acquisition entries against 46 total. Six neighbours selling together is how a fragmented landscape becomes one protected block — and it means a community's task is to bring the neighbours to the table, not to find one large owner. AND WHO CARRIES IT AFTERWARDS: the land WILL IN FUTURE FORM PART OF A CLOSE COOPERATION ON NATURE MANAGEMENT AND RESTORATION BETWEEN the municipality AND THE NATURE AGENCY. The purchase is by a private fund, the aftercare by the council and the state agency — the division of labour that makes a purchase survivable, and the answer to the German endowment problem from the other direction. The effort is described as AN INTEGRATED PART OF A NATURE ALLIANCE'S WORK TO STRENGTHEN BIODIVERSITY.

trackers.name: Who founded the Danish nature fund — the STATE and two private foundations together
trackers.desc: THE OWNERSHIP MODEL WORTH COPYING, because it explains where the money came from: IN 2015 THE STATE, TOGETHER WITH two named private foundations, CREATED THE DANISH NATURE FUND, which BUYS UP AND CREATES WILD NATURE ALL OVER DENMARK, IN COOPERATION WITH MANY DONORS AND ACTORS, and by 2025 OWNS ALMOST 100 NATURE AREAS IN DENMARK, WITH A TOTAL AREA OF AROUND 8,700 HECTARES. Denmark had four acquisition entries against 46 total. A fund founded jointly by the state and private philanthropy buys with public legitimacy and private speed — neither a ministry nor a charity alone. AND THE ROUTES IT TAKES MONEY BY, each of which a supporter can use: it ACTIVELY ENCOURAGES PEOPLE TO SUPPORT IT THROUGH CAMPAIGNS, FOREST CERTIFICATES, DONATIONS, WILLS AND GIFTS. THE MONEY THEN GOES TO BUYING UP LAND THROUGH VOLUNTARY AGREEMENTS WITH LANDOWNERS, and to creating BIODIVERSITY, NATURE AND A SETTING FOR OUTDOOR LIFE ON THE AREAS. Voluntary agreement is stated as the only acquisition method — no compulsion, which is what keeps a national buyer welcome in a village. It publishes AN OVERVIEW OF THE FUND'S AREAS so anyone can see where it already holds ground.
