trackers.name: Rettslig klageinteresse — can your group appeal at all?
trackers.desc: SETTLE THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: the plan- og bygningsloven contains no provision on who may appeal decisions taken under it — it refers to the forvaltningsloven (pbl. § 1-9). Under forvaltningsloven § 28 a party to the case, and anyone else with rettslig klageinteresse (a legal interest in appealing), may appeal an individual decision. An environmental organisation that is not a party must establish that interest, and it is a legal standard requiring a concrete, discretionary assessment in every case, built from case law and theory rather than a checklist — so expect to argue it rather than assert it. WHAT THE GOVERNMENT CONFIRMS: the ordinary § 28 rules do not prevent environmental organisations from appealing an order to rectify (pålegg om retting) or a penalty decision (overtredelsesgebyr) — both are enkeltvedtak and both are appealable, and further clarity is expected to come through practice.

trackers.name: Miljøinformasjonsloven — what you can force out, and what you cannot
trackers.desc: USE IT, KNOWING THE EDGE: the environmental information law generally cannot be used to demand that new surveys or samples be carried out — but where information already exists in some form, the recipient has a duty to compile it so that it answers your questions. PRECEDENT WORTH CITING: Naturvernforbundet i Oslo og Akershus won a Supreme Court judgment on access to a forest owner's nature-value registrations, establishing that information must be delivered in a usable form — in practice written. Being invited to a single meeting where the material is shown once is not compliance, and that is the answer when an authority offers you a briefing instead of documents. You cannot use it to extract genuinely sensitive trade secrets of limited environmental relevance, such as mixing ratios or specific technical arrangements. RELATED RIGHT: under the forvaltningsloven public bodies must guide not only the parties but anyone else interested in the case, and ‘persons’ in Norwegian law includes legal persons — so a local association can simply ask the municipality for guidance on a plan affecting nature values.

trackers.name: Søknadssenter — Miljødirektoratet's grant schemes
trackers.desc: WHERE NORWEGIAN ENVIRONMENTAL MONEY IS APPLIED FOR: Miljødirektoratet's Søknadssenter carries the schemes in one place — support for voluntary climate and environment organisations, the pollution-area scheme, natural-science organisations, mapping and valuation of outdoor-recreation areas and route plans, and measures in state-secured outdoor recreation areas. CHECK THE THRESHOLD BEFORE YOU START: the headline scheme for voluntary climate and environment organisations requires more than 5,000 members (3,000 for children's and youth organisations), or a foundation of national significance — so a neighbourhood group does not qualify, and the realistic route is through a national organisation that does. Money there is paid as core operating support and allocated purely on objective criteria; grant size weighs activity level nationally and locally, the organisation's finances, its alternative funding options and its membership numbers. Some posts are earmarked to named recipients in the state budget (kap. 1420 post 77), which is worth knowing before investing effort. TIMING AND MECHANICS: forms generally open around 1 December and are closed outside the window — the pollution-area deadline was 15 January 2026. You need ID-porten to apply. Recipients are followed up on delivery and use of funds, documentation must be kept 5 years from 1 January of the application year, and organisations must report unprompted anything affecting their grant. Help: esshjelp@miljodir.no, 951 23 500.

trackers.name: Frivillig skogvern — the owner offers, the state pays, tax-free
trackers.desc: THE MECHANISM THAT INVERTS WHO STARTS: the forest owner offers an area for protection against compensation, instead of the state designating and the owner resisting. If it has the natural qualities and the authorities accept, it becomes a naturreservat under the Nature Diversity Act — bound for all time, with forestry no longer permitted. THE TERMS ARE BETTER THAN MOST CONSERVATION SALES ANYWHERE: compensation is a tax-free lump sum based on the value of forestry in the area, with the state paying interest from the day the owner signs until payment; the owner keeps freehold title and keeps hunting, fishing and grazing rights — only the right to conduct forestry is given up; and the owner may withdraw at any time until the compensation agreement is signed. Forest owner organisations give free advice and act as the owner's negotiating party against the state's valuation. PROCESS: biologists carry out a bioregistrering of the area's qualities (if the values are insufficient it ends there), then valuation, an offer, public consultation, and adoption by the King in Council — typically about 3 years. Where the area lies in reindeer grazing land the local reindeer grazing district must be consulted. SCALE: piloted in 2003 after the conflict-heavy processes of the 1980s and 90s, first 8 areas protected in 2005, and since then this has been the only route by which privately owned forest is protected — past 1,000 forest areas by June 2025, reaching 5.4 percent of all Norwegian forest and 4.2 percent of productive forest.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Frivillig vern — the forest-owners' co-operatives that run it for the owner (Norway)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: since 2005, protection of privately owned forest in Norway has happened one way only — the owner offers the ground, and their regional forest-owners' co-operative runs the whole process for them. Norges Skogeierforbund coordinates it with Miljødirektoratet; the co-operatives doing the work include AT Skog, Viken Skog, ALLSKOG and FramTre, several of them at it since 2002. They advise the owner free of charge, handle the delineation, commission the timber valuation, and negotiate the state's compensation offer on the owner's behalf. It began as a 2003 pilot and the first eight areas became nature reserves in 2005. USE IT: this is the offer to put in front of a landowner who has a buyer, and four facts decide it. The owner can withdraw at any point up to signature, so putting ground forward commits them to nothing. The compensation is exempt from capital-gains tax. The owner keeps ownership, hunting, fishing and grazing rights — and gets no compensation for them, because the payment covers forestry value only, which is also the answer to anyone claiming protection ends all use of the land. And the ecological survey that decides whether the ground qualifies, the bioregistrering, is commissioned by the conservation authorities rather than paid for by the owner. Be clear what these bodies are: forest-owners' co-operatives, part of the timber sector, acting for the owner and not for a community — which is exactly why an owner will take a meeting with them.

trackers.name: Fjellstyrene and Norges Fjellstyresamband — local boards holding rights over 26.6 million dekar
trackers.desc: WHAT THEY ARE: under the fjellov, every municipality containing a statsallmenning must have a fjellstyre, appointed by the municipal council but not a municipal body, which administers the use of rights and benefits in that common — summer farming, grazing, hunting and fishing. There are 93 to 94 of them. Norges Fjellstyresamband, at Stortingsgata 30, 0161 Oslo, nfs@fjellstyrene.no, is their joint organisation, funded by member subscriptions and a statutory contribution from the landowner fund. THE SCALE: the statsallmenninger of southern and central Norway total 26.6 million dekar. Norway had no acquirer in this file, and this is why the question was the wrong one — over much of the Norwegian mountains the relevant thing is not who owns the ground but who holds and administers the use rights on it, and that is a local board. THE THREE-WAY SPLIT A NORWEGIAN COMMUNITY NEEDS TO KNOW: Statskog SF holds the landowner right; the allmenningsstyre administers timber rights and, unlike the fjellstyre, is elected by and from among the rights-holders themselves; and the fjellstyre administers the other common rights including hunting and fishing. Where there is no allmenningsstyre, Statskog administers the timber right. Approach the right one of the three for your question. WHY THE RIGHTS MATTER BEYOND THE INDIVIDUALS HOLDING THEM: the Fjellstyresamband's own framing is that alongside their value as recreation areas for the whole country, the villages' collective rights in these areas are decisive for maintaining viable rural communities. Rights of use vary between commons and change over time; grazing, summer farming, hunting, trapping and fishing are the important ones today. WHAT THE FEDERATION WILL DO: act as the link between individual fjellstyrer and public authorities, guide them on particular questions, and give opinions to public authorities, private organisations and others on the basis of the fjellov's purpose. ONE THING IN MOTION: a government-appointed committee worked from 2016 to 2018 on a new fjellov, and NOU 2018:11 proposed one; as of May 2026 the proposal was reported to be with the department. The framework may change.

trackers.name: The six Norwegian associations that hold and defend appeal rights — and how to reach them
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST, and they act together: in a joint consultation response on the new Norwegian public administration act, six organisations welcomed the bill stating clearly that an association or foundation has a right of appeal where the decision lies within its purpose or natural field of activity. They are Den Norske Turistforening, Friluftsrådenes Landsforbund, Naturvernforbundet, Norges Jeger- og Fiskerforbund, Norsk Friluftsliv and Sabima. For a Norwegian community, that list is the set of national bodies with the standing to appeal on outdoor recreation, nature and species — and they are demonstrably willing to act jointly. Match your ground to the one whose purpose covers it. WHY STANDING IS THE WHOLE QUESTION IN NORWAY: the planning and building act contains no provision on who may appeal decisions made under it; it refers to the public administration act, under which parties and others with rettslig klageinteresse — legal interest in appealing — may appeal. For an environmental organisation that is not a party, the department's own interpretation is that whether it has that interest requires a concrete overall assessment in each individual case, on a legal standard developed through practice and theory. So it is arguable, not automatic. And if a body is found not to have it, that refusal is itself a decision which can be appealed. WHERE AN APPEAL GOES: municipalities do the area planning and grant building permissions; the Statsforvalteren is the appeal body for building cases and for cases concerning zoning plans, and takes a wholly fresh look at the case — it may consider new circumstances and may raise matters that do not concern the appellant at all. It also is not bound by the municipality's view that the conditions for hearing the appeal were met. Note the stopping rule: once the appeal body has decided, the administrative route is exhausted, and going further means a lawsuit or the Sivilombudet. AND A PRACTICAL POINT ON DEFECTIVE APPEALS: where an appeal has errors or gaps the municipality must guide the appellant under its general duty to advise, and the appeal should not be rejected outright — a short deadline for correction may be given instead.

trackers.name: Sabima — the biological societies, and money to survey the species on your ground
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: the umbrella organisation for Norway's biological societies, working to stop the loss of natural diversity, with 15 staff. Its member societies are the specialist bodies a community actually needs: Norsk Botanisk Forening, Norges sopp- og nyttevekstforbund, Norsk Zoologisk Forening and Norsk entomologisk forening — plants, fungi, animals and insects. It invites people with an interest in a biological field to join one. THE OFFER THAT MATTERS MOST, AND IT IS MONEY: each year Sabima distributes funds, on behalf of its member societies, to associations and members who carry out voluntary species mapping. There is an annual call. If your ground needs its species recorded and nobody will pay for a survey, this is a Norwegian route to funded fieldwork — and the file has repeatedly found that a survey is what turns a community's claim into evidence. AND VOLUNTEERS ALREADY DO MOST OF IT: more than half of all species mapping in Norway is carried out by voluntary mappers, who record findings in Artsobservasjoner, run by Artsdatabanken — and those records become immediately available to the administration, researchers and others working with species occurrences. A record made today is in the system the authorities consult. That is the cheapest evidence-creation route in this entire file. IT ALSO PUBLISHES ITS SURVEY NOTES: reports from mapping activity funded through those grants are published on its site, tagged by place and by subject — red-listed species, alien species, deciduous woodland, calcareous forest and so on. Check whether your area is already covered. WHY IT ENGAGES WITH MUNICIPALITIES, in its own framing: land-use change is the largest cause of species extinction, and many of the decisions to carry out interventions in nature are made in the municipalities, which need better competence on nature and on the consequences of losing biodiversity. It works on forest protection, mires and peat extraction, cultural landscape, alien species, sea and coast, and municipal nature management, and publishes its consultation responses.

trackers.name: Miljødirektoratet's søknadssenter — one portal, and 'alle kan søke' on the nature schemes
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Norwegian Environment Agency's single application centre, listing every tilskudd it runs with its own form, criteria and deadline. Norway's bucket held Sabima, the six appeal-standing associations and Naturvernforbundet; this is the state money behind them, and the page above is the index. THE TWO SCHEMES A COMMUNITY SHOULD READ FIRST, and note who may apply: Natursats — tilskudd til arbeid med å ivareta naturmangfold, for measures contributing to conservation of threatened species and nature types, selected nature types, wild pollinating insects and valuable cultural landscapes, and to prevent negative impact from alien species — where the agency states alle kan søke, anyone can apply. And midler til naturrestaurering, where municipalities, organisations and private developers can apply for measures that restore degraded nature, including nature-based solutions improving conditions for biodiversity, climate adaptation, carbon stores or other ecosystem services. AND ONE SCHEME AIMED SQUARELY AT COMMUNITIES LIVING WITH A BUILT PROJECT: a tilskuddsordning to safeguard and promote nature and outdoor life in municipalities affected by land-based wind power plants — open to municipalities, municipal and intermunicipal undertakings, intermunicipal friluftsråd and voluntary organisations, and covering municipalities where the wind farm sits AND neighbouring municipalities whose outdoor or nature interests are negatively affected. If a wind development has already gone in near you, there is a named national fund for the aftermath. THE CORE FUNDING FOR ORGANISATIONS, with its honest threshold: operating grants to voluntary climate and environment organisations require over 5,000 members (3,000 for youth organisations), or national significance as a foundation; size is set from activity level nationally and locally, finances, alternative funding and membership. A parallel scheme covers pollution-focused organisations and one covers naturfaglige organisations. Small groups will not qualify for core funding — use the project schemes above. PRACTICAL: several nature schemes share a 15 January deadline with forms opening in November or December; the agency runs an application webinar; questions to esshjelp@miljodir.no or 951 23 500.

trackers.name: Advokatene Borgersen, Steinsvåg & Sæther — plan law plus the naturmangfoldlov
trackers.desc: WHY THIS FIRM AND NOT ANOTHER: most Norwegian plan-law practices sell help with getting your own extension approved. This one states that plan and building law further encompasses various sector laws and names them: jordlova, NATURMANGFOLDLOVEN and forurensingsloven — the nature diversity act and the pollution act. It says it assists in all cases concerning the plan and building act with its associated sector legislation, whether in connection with a REGULATION PLAN PROCESS, a building measure, ULOVLIGHETSOPPFØLGING — unlawfulness follow-up — or other cases about real property where permission from public authorities is required. THE POINT IT MAKES THAT A COMMUNITY CAN USE: even where a measure is exempt from the application duty, it must still comply with the reguleringsplan. Exemption from applying is not exemption from the plan. Norway had six associations with statutory appeal rights and one legal network; this is a named practitioner who works the nature act alongside the planning act.

trackers.name: Norwegian building-case practice — your home insurance may pay the lawyer
trackers.desc: THE LINE THAT CHANGES WHAT A COMMUNITY CAN AFFORD: many Norwegian home insurance policies cover legal costs through the rettshjelpdekning in neighbour disputes. The cover normally applies once a dispute exists — that is, once a claim has been made and rejected. Check your policy terms or ring the insurer. Across forty-three countries this file has recorded crowdfunding, legal aid schemes and pro bono clinics; household legal-expenses cover is the first route found that most residents already own. WHEN A LAWYER IS WORTH IT, from the same practitioner guidance: as soon as disagreement arises with the municipality, neighbours or contractors — typically when a building application is refused and you are considering a klage, when the municipality has ordered demolition or rectification, or WHEN YOU DISCOVER THAT A NEIGHBOUR'S BUILDING HAS BEEN ERECTED CONTRARY TO THE RULES. And it is candid that simple small applications often need no lawyer at all. AND THE STEP BEFORE THE LAWYER: if the municipality does not act, you can engage an advocate to assess further legal steps — so the sequence is complain to the municipality first, then escalate. Norwegian appeals run to the Statsforvalteren, with the Sivilombudet as a further route named by practitioners.

trackers.name: Norwegian ekspropriasjon and naturfredning counsel — for the owner who is offered too little
trackers.desc: WHAT THEY DO: a Norwegian firm with long experience assisting GRUNNEIERE in cases about fredning or protection of areas under the naturmangfoldlov, offering a no-obligation telephone conversation first. Its wider practice covers ekspropriasjon from agricultural property, expropriation through the jordskifterett, commercial property, housing and holiday property, and PRIVATE DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS. THE LEGAL CHANGE IT RECORDS, which matters to anyone near a protected landscape: under the old nature protection act, compensation rules gave a right to compensation essentially only on protection as naturreservat or naturminne, and owners affected by LANDSKAPSVERNOMRÅDER had weak compensation protection. Under the naturmangfoldlov, landskapsvernområde is put on an equal footing with naturreservat. AND THE PRACTICAL WARNING: it is important to assess the State's offer carefully before asking for skjønn to be taken out — the valuation procedure. A community persuading an owner into voluntary protection should make sure the owner has independent advice on the figure, because the offer, not the principle, is what the owner will judge it by.

trackers.name: Frivilligvern.no — the owner offers the forest, keeps the title, and the payment is TAX-FREE
trackers.desc: WHAT THE SCHEME IS: voluntary forest protection is an arrangement where THE FOREST OWNER THEMSELVES OFFERS FOREST AREA FOR PROTECTION AGAINST COMPENSATION. If the area has natural and environmental qualities that make it relevant, and the protection authorities accept the offer, it can be protected as a NATURE RESERVE under the biodiversity act. Norway's bucket held the deletion of outdated permissions; this is the route for an owner who wants out. AND THE TERMS THAT MAKE IT WORTH DOING: the owner receives TAX-FREE COMPENSATION, paid as a lump sum after the reserve is adopted and exempt from capital gains tax, including for co-owned holdings; the owner still keeps the title, and the hunting, fishing and grazing rights; and the state pays interest on the compensation from the day the owner signs. An owner who can be paid, keep the deed, keep the hunting and pay no tax on the money has little left to lose by offering. AND THE PART THAT SUITS AN AWKWARD PARCEL: if you have large tied-up areas you can get compensation for forest you COULD NOT HAVE LOGGED ANYWAY, because low deductions are made for environmental considerations; and forest that for various reasons gives low economic yield may be relevant for protection. AND THE HONEST TIMESCALE: if the areas must be surveyed the process often takes 2 TO 3 YEARS; where the natural values are already known it can be done in under a year — and the owner can withdraw at any time until the compensation agreement is signed. Once protected, management moves from the Forestry Act to the Biodiversity Act.

trackers.name: The forest owners' organisations — FREE advice, mapping and negotiation on the owner's side
trackers.desc: WHO ACTS FOR THE OWNER, and it costs nothing: the forest owner receives FREE ADVICE AND HELP from the organisation through the investigation process for voluntary protection. We can help with everything from DELIMITING THE PROTECTED AREA, the conditions for protection, and THE COMPENSATION NEGOTIATIONS WITH THE STATE. A free negotiator on the landowner's side of the table, in a deal with the state, is the single most valuable thing in this entry — and more than one organisation offers it, with a state page naming two organisations that negotiate on the owner's behalf in one region and pointing to contact people at the forest owners' organisations. WHAT THE HELP COVERS, item by item: advice, MAPPING, site visits, VALUATION, contact with the authorities, compensation negotiations, and discussions about the content of the protection regulation. The process runs in four phases, beginning with an INFORMAL process between the owner and the organisation, in which a proposal for the boundary and the owner's own conditions are worked out before anything formal is offered. An informal first phase where the owner sets the conditions before offering is what stops a designation being done to someone. Usually biologists are commissioned to carry out a BIOREGISTRATION — a mapping of the environmental qualities of the area.

trackers.name: FramTre — free advice and NAMED staff to negotiate protection compensation with the state
trackers.desc: A SECOND ORGANISATION OFFERING THE SAME FREE SERVICE, which matters because it means a Norwegian owner has a choice of adviser: VOLUNTARY FOREST PROTECTION IS A SCHEME IN WHICH THE FOREST OWNER HIMSELF OFFERS FOREST AREA FOR PROTECTION AGAINST COMPENSATION. IF THE AREA HAS NATURE AND ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITIES THAT MAKE IT RELEVANT... THE AREA CAN BE PROTECTED AS A NATURE RESERVE UNDER THE NATURE DIVERSITY ACT. Norway has the thinnest acquisition coverage of the large buckets in this file. AND WHAT THE OWNER KEEPS, which is why this is an easier ask than a sale: THE FOREST OWNER STILL HAS THE OWNERSHIP RIGHT, AS WELL AS HUNTING, FISHING AND GRAZING RIGHTS, and receives TAX-FREE COMPENSATION based on THE VALUE OF RUNNING FORESTRY IN THE AREA. The owner sells the logging and keeps everything else, tax-free. AND THE SERVICE, free and staffed: THE FOREST OWNER GETS FREE ADVICE AND HELP DURING THE INVESTIGATION PROCESS. WE CAN HELP WITH EVERYTHING FROM DELIMITING THE PROTECTED AREA, THE CONDITIONS FOR PROTECTION, AND THE COMPENSATION NEGOTIATIONS WITH THE STATE. It lists FIVE EMPLOYEES WITH BROAD EXPERIENCE OF FOREST PROTECTION PROCESSES, each with name, role, email and mobile number, plus a switchboard number. AND THE ESCAPE HATCH THAT REMOVES THE RISK OF ASKING: IF THE FOREST OWNER IS NOT SATISFIED, HE OR SHE CAN WITHDRAW FROM THE PROCESS AT ANY TIME.

trackers.name: The forest billion — 800 MILLION KRONER a year, and a queue of offered land
trackers.desc: THE MONEY BEHIND THE SCHEME, and it is the reason an offer is likely to be accepted: after a budget agreement THE ALLOCATION TO VOLUNTARY FOREST PROTECTION IS UP TO 800.4 MILLION KRONER, with the current year's budget raised by A FURTHER 200 MILLION. THE NEW 'FOREST BILLION' GOES TO PAYING COMPENSATION TO FOREST OWNERS WHO OFFER TO PROTECT FOREST. A national budget line whose entire purpose is paying landowners to protect forest is a fund a community can point an owner at — and it survived an attempted cut, having been reduced to 351 million in the government's draft before being restored. AND THE BOTTLENECK, which is the opening for a community: THERE ARE TODAY LARGE AREAS OF NORWEGIAN FOREST WITH HIGH NATURAL VALUE STANDING IN A QUEUE FOR PROTECTION. THESE ARE AREAS OFFERED BY FOREST OWNERS THROUGH THE VOLUNTARY PROTECTION SCHEME. The shortage is money and processing, not willing owners — so an owner persuaded to offer joins a queue that is being funded, not a hope. AND THE ARGUMENT FOR WHICH FOREST MATTERS MOST, from a named conservation leader: FOREST THAT HAS NEVER BEEN SUBJECT TO CLEAR-FELLING HAS MORE THAN HALF OF THE THREATENED SPECIES. Never-clearfelled is the single most useful thing to establish about a threatened wood.

trackers.name: BirdLife Norge — the argument that PRIVATE ownership of important nature is conflict-driving
trackers.desc: A NATIONAL CONSERVATION BODY ARGUING THE OPPOSITE OF MOST ENTRIES IN THIS FILE, and worth having for exactly that reason: FOR MANY AREAS THE STATE, THROUGH THE ENVIRONMENTAL AUTHORITIES, MUST TAKE OVER THE OWNERSHIP RIGHT, SINCE PRIVATE OWNERSHIP OF IMPORTANT NATURE IS CONFLICT-DRIVING OVER TIME. Norway has the thinnest acquisition ratio of any large bucket in this file — five entries against 117. A community choosing between a private buyer and a public one now has both arguments on file: the Canadian trust in batch584 says private status is what makes a buyer approachable, and this body says private ownership stores up conflict. Both are right about different timescales, and a group should decide deliberately rather than by default. AND WHAT ELSE IT WANTS CHANGED, which is a live campaign a Norwegian community can join: THE PROTECTION PROVISIONS FOR A LONG LIST OF PROTECTED AREAS MUST BE CHANGED SO THAT HUNTING, FISHING AND THE USE OF GRAZING ANIMALS BECOME FORBIDDEN, noting that HUNTING IS PERMITTED IN MANY PROTECTED AREAS, INCLUDING IN OUR NATIONAL PARKS. Designation in Norway does not by itself stop hunting or grazing — a community should check what its own protected status actually prohibits. The body is candid that THERE IS NO POLITICAL MAJORITY FOR SUCH THINKING TODAY.

trackers.name: Norway's oldest conservation body — 43,000 members and a local branch in every county
trackers.desc: THE BODY A NORWEGIAN COMMUNITY IS MOST LIKELY TO HAVE NEARBY: founded in 1914 and based in the capital, it is ONE OF THE LARGEST NORWEGIAN ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATIONS WITH APPROXIMATELY 43,000 MEMBERS, and THE ORGANISATION IS BASED ON VOLUNTEER WORK AMONG THE MEMBERS, CONSTITUTING WORK BOTH AT LOCAL AND NATIONAL LEVELS. An organisation that runs on member volunteering at local level is one a village group joins rather than petitions — and its own pages record COUNTY BRANCHES IN ALL THE COUNTRY'S COUNTIES AND ABOUT 100 LOCAL BRANCHES ACROSS THE WHOLE COUNTRY. AND THE ROUTE BY WHICH IT CAN COME TO OWN LAND, which is why it belongs in an acquisition seam: it accepts testamentary gifts, and ONE CAN BEQUEATH MOVABLE PROPERTY, REAL PROPERTY AS WELL AS MONEY AND SECURITIES, with TESTAMENTARY GIFTS TO NON-PROFIT ORGANISATIONS EXEMPT FROM INHERITANCE DUTY. Leaving the land itself to a conservation body, tax-free, is a route that costs a living owner nothing — and it is the quietest way a threatened parcel can change hands before a developer reaches it. It is also the national member of a global federation, and employs staff as well as volunteers.

trackers.desc: IMY — Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection — Sweden’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Naturskyddsföreningen — talerätt och kretsar
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Sweden's largest environmental association, founded 1909, and the practical route to the statutory right of appeal. Under 16 kap. 13 § miljöbalken a non-profit association whose statutes give it the purpose of protecting nature or the environment may appeal decisions granting permits, approvals and dispensations under the Environmental Code — but the section sets minimum thresholds for membership and years of operation that exclude most local groups in practice. WHO IT SUITS: a neighbourhood group that does not itself qualify. The association's kretsar and länsförbund do, and there is case law where a länsförbund took over a local krets's action by power of attorney after the krets was found to fall short. Bring the case to them rather than filing alone and being dismissed on standing.

trackers.name: LONA — Lokala naturvårdssatsningen (local nature-conservation grant)
trackers.desc: THE STANDING LOCAL GRANT, under Förordning (2003:598). Money comes from Naturvårdsverket and the länsstyrelse decides which projects get it. Ordinary LONA covers up to 50 percent of costs for nature conservation, outdoor recreation and public health, and its stated purpose covers both kommuner and ideella föreningar. THE CATCH THAT DECIDES EVERYTHING: only a kommun can apply. Projects may be initiated and run by associations, landowners or private individuals, but the kommun is always legally and financially responsible for delivery and reporting — so your first move is to contact the LONA-ansvarig at your kommun, or failing that at the länsstyrelse, well before the deadline, and expect an agreement between your association and the kommun if it succeeds. TIMING: kommuner normally submit by 1 December for projects starting the next year (it varies, and extra rounds happen); decisions usually come in spring; annual reports by 1 March, final report within 3 months of project end. CHECK STATUS FIRST — IT IS BUDGET-DEPENDENT: Naturvårdsverket states no new ordinary LONA projects are being approved at present except for vandringsleder and ängs- och betesmarker, with only ongoing projects completed in 2026 because of the budget situation. Targeted rounds can be far more generous — an extra wetland round spread about 12 million kronor across 17 län at up to 90 percent of costs. AND IT IS MONEY, NOT PERMISSION: a LONA decision does not release anyone from other law on consultation, permits and dispensations.

trackers.name: Sök bidrag — other Swedish grants for a local group
trackers.desc: SMALLER MONEY YOU CAN APPLY FOR DIRECTLY, which matters because LONA must go through your kommun. Alvins fond: Naturvårdsverket decides grants for projects promoting Swedish nature protection, especially bird protection — apply by 30 November each year. Grannskapsinitiativet from Postkodsstiftelsen: an ideell förening or public-benefit foundation can apply for 20,000–60,000 kronor. The page also routes you to LONA through your kommun. USE IT: these are the routes open to an association in its own name, on its own timetable.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Naturarvet — buys old-growth forest ahead of the felling plan (Sweden)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Swedish insamlingsstiftelse whose sole purpose is raising money to buy gammelskog — old forest with high conservation value — and hold it permanently. Its founding observation is the one to quote at a Swedish council: only a very small share of Sweden's forest is old-growth, half of what remains has no secure protection, and it is being felled faster than it is being protected. USE IT: the Djupsjöån purchase is a template worth reading in full, because it shows a community how a buy can be committed before the money exists. A forest management plan of August 2023 proposed felling 50 hectares of the old forest within two years — that document is the clock, and it is the thing to go and find. The property came up for sale; Naturarvet signed the contract and paid the deposit in May 2024 on the strength of earlier large gifts and an autumn-and-spring appeal, borrowed 4 million kronor from private lenders to cover the rest, and the state paid out 4 million kronor that September to clear the loans, with further financing following from the county administrative board on a nature-reserve decision. The sequence is buy first, designate after, and bridge the gap with private lending against the expected state money. THE CHEAP ENTRY POINT: donors buy a named umbrella tree or a forest square identified by coordinates, so anyone can visit the exact patch they paid for — a campaign shape that builds a constituency rather than a donor list.

trackers.name: Allmännings- och besparingsskogar — commonly owned forests, and their federation (Sweden)
trackers.desc: WHAT THEY ARE: commonly owned forests in Norrbotten and Dalarna, formed in the second half of the 1800s — the Dalarna besparingsskogar through the storskifte land reform, the Norrbotten allmänningsskogar through the avvittring of crown land to local farmers — and governed by the Act on common forests in Norrland and Dalarna. They were created precisely because timber companies had begun buying up forests and whole farms and the state feared the farmers would sell their land. The commons were the protection against that, and they still are. THE SCALE AND WHERE TO LOOK: their federation, Sveriges Allmänningsskogars Förbund, publishes a list of every allmänning and besparingsskog with its area and ownership. Examples from it: Jokkmokk's allmänning at around 81,000 hectares; Arjeplog's at over 40,000; Arvidsjaur's, formed 1877, owned in common by the owners of assessed properties in the municipality — about 32,000 hectares with some 1,600 co-owners; other commons with around 3,000 co-owners across some 1,500 properties. Reported totals for the allmänning and association forests run to around 670,000 hectares. WHY A SWEDISH COMMUNITY SHOULD CHECK: ownership goes with the property, not with a subscription. If your farm or house is an assessed property in one of these municipalities you may already be a delägare, entitled to attend the jordägarstämma — the landowners' meeting, held twice a year in Älvdalen — and to vote on how the forest is run. That is standing you already have. TWO FEATURES THAT MATTER FOR PROTECTING LAND: the statutory objective is even and good yield in perpetuity, with felling calculations made roughly every ten years, and Älvdalen's besparingsskog states sustainable forestry and preserving biological diversity as further aims. And the money is locked to land: if the besparingsskog receives money from selling a property it must use it to buy new forest. Rather than a cash dividend, the return goes back to the delägare and the district as grants, many tied to agriculture and forestry. BE CLEAR ABOUT THE POLITICS: the federation describes part of its purpose as giving these forests a voice as a consultee to the state and as a counterweight to the environmental lobby. It is a forest-owning interest, not a conservation body.

trackers.name: Artportalen — open to everyone, and the EIA consultants take their extract from it
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: Sweden's largest reporting system for species observations, run by SLU Artdatabanken. Open to everyone to report and to search among millions of records, contributed by private individuals as well as professional conservation officers and researchers. The founding principle is that records are open and free for anyone to use, displayed publicly as soon as they are published. THE SENTENCE THAT MAKES THIS A CAMPAIGN TOOL, and it is SLU Artdatabanken's own example: when land is to be exploited for housing, roads or wind farms, an environmental impact assessment is always made — and an extract from Artportalen is often taken as its basis. The database a community can search for free is the same one the developer's consultant will draw on. Records you put in before the assessment is written are records the assessment has to reckon with. HOW TO REPORT: create an account, optionally upload a photograph, and state where and when you saw the species; there is also a mobile checklist for reporting from a ready-made species list, plus bulk import and project administration. THE PART TO UNDERSTAND BEFORE YOU RELY ON A SEARCH: species on SLU Artdatabanken's national skyddsklassade list are automatically protected — their locations are diffused on the map to a degree depending on protection class, and marked with a crossed-out eye. Diffused maps show only whether a species was reported inside a predefined square. Records from the last month are not in the diffused maps at all. Access to exact data is limited to designated officials at authorities such as the county administrative board, the forest agency and the municipalities, and to the most closely concerned people in the voluntary associations, and to consultants or researchers only after a confidentiality assessment. A blank map may mean a hidden species, not an empty site. A reporter can also choose to hide their own find. WHO SITS BEHIND IT: run with the Artportalsråd, whose members include the Swedish ornithological, botanical, mycological and entomological societies, the county administrative boards, the municipalities, the forest agency, the agriculture board, Naturskyddsföreningen, the marine and water authority and the environmental protection agency, which largely funds it. That list is Sweden's whole nature-recording sector in one place.

trackers.name: Bevaka strandskyddet — the krets handbook for watching and appealing shoreline cases
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a kretshandledning — a handbook written for local branches — giving an overview of the shoreline protection legislation and showing how to take part in decision processes and how to appeal cases concerning strandskydd. Sweden's bucket had a records portal, a land buyer and 270 local branches, and nothing showing a group how to monitor and object. This is that document, and it is free. WHAT IT TELLS YOU TO DO FIRST: get facts about the shoreline area in danger — the municipality and the county administrative board may have inventories, and there may be biologists in the association, in the municipality or at universities who would come out and survey the shores. Document with camera, map and preferably GPS. That is the evidence routine this file has been assembling from five countries, written as instructions for a volunteer branch. THE LEGAL FRAME IT SETS OUT: strandskydd reaches 100 metres from the shoreline, over land and into the water, extended in many places to 300 metres; a decision to extend a strandskydd area applies immediately even if it is appealed; and the prohibition covers buildings, changes of use, other installations, and excavation or preparatory works — where these hinder or deter the public from entering an area it could otherwise cross freely. Certain works are outside it, including permitted industry, roads and railways. THE TWO WARNINGS IT GIVES ITS OWN PEOPLE: the appeal must arrive in time or you lose the chance to have the decision legally tested; and when describing what is destroyed, the values need not be exceptional — strandskydd is meant to protect ordinary shoreline too. The second removes the commonest reason a group talks itself out of objecting. AND THE SCALE OF WHAT IS AT STAKE: of 4,273 red-listed species in Sweden, 1,628 are tied to shorelines. Pressure is highest in the big-city regions and along popular coasts.

trackers.name: Boverket's PBL kunskapsbank — the official answer to 'who is allowed to appeal'
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the national board's knowledge bank on the plan and building act, with pages answering exactly who may appeal a bygglov, a marklov, a förhandsbesked or a detaljplan and on what basis. Sweden had 80 entries and almost nothing that tells a resident whether they can act; this does, from the regulator itself. THE RÅGRANNE RULE: decisions on bygglov, marklov and förhandsbesked may be appealed by the applicant and by the owner of a property directly bordering the one the permit concerns, or separated from it only by a street or road. A rågranne has the right to appeal REGARDLESS OF THE DISTANCE between the place where the works are planned and their own property or dwelling. Samfälligheter directly bordering the affected property are also sakhägare with the right to appeal. AND THE ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATION ROUTE: environmental organisations have a special right to appeal decisions on bygglov and förhandsbesked for EIA projects OUTSIDE detailed plan areas — specifically where the building committee concluded that the measure cannot be assumed to cause significant environmental impact and granted the permit or a positive preliminary decision. ON DETAILED PLANS, a point worth knowing: the restriction on the right to appeal does not apply where the decision went against the sakhägare because the proposal was CHANGED AFTER THE REVIEW PERIOD — and standing can extend beyond the plan area, for instance where planned development presupposes through traffic past the property, even if that property lies outside the plan area.

trackers.name: Swedish miljorätt directories and firms — 7,380 law firms, filtered by speciality
trackers.desc: WHY A DIRECTORY: Sweden's legal market is large and this file had no Swedish lawyer at all. A national directory lets a community compare specialists in miljörätt among 7,380 law firms across the whole country, free, rather than pick a name from outside. It states the position plainly: neighbours can appeal environmental permits and bygglov if they consider the project contrary to the miljöbalk, and the mark- och miljödomstol decides the dispute. WHAT SWEDISH MARK- OCH MILJÖRÄTT PRACTICES OFFER, from their own pages: they assist companies, MUNICIPALITIES AND PRIVATE INDIVIDUALS and litigate in the länsstyrelse, the mark- och miljödomstol and the Mark- och miljööverdomstol. Their listed law includes the fastighetsbildningslag — which governs how properties may be newly formed or reformed and WHO HAS THE RIGHT TO APPEAL such decisions — plus the samfällighet management act, the ledningsrättslag and the expropriation act. A SPECIALIST NICHE WORTH KNOWING: one Swedish practitioner is described as having run over 900 cases on strandskydd and bygglov, and a related service sells legal document templates for appealing a refused strandskydd dispensation, bygglov or förhandsbesked, drafted by specialists, expressly so that people need not carry the high costs of engaging a lawyer. Templates drafted by a specialist are the cheapest legal help recorded in this file.

trackers.name: Framtidens Natur & Kulturarv — give the land, or keep it and sign a 20–50 year agreement
trackers.desc: THE TWO OFFERS TO A LANDOWNER, stated plainly on its own site: transfer ownership to the foundation, directly or by will — OR sign a long-term nature conservation agreement (often 20 to 50 years) under which THE FOUNDATION GETS THE MANAGEMENT RIGHT AND YOU KEEP THE OWNERSHIP. It answers the question directly: I have land I want to protect — can I donate it? Yes, absolutely. We welcome landowners who want to strengthen biodiversity and protect their land for future generations. AND THE THIRD ROUTE, for someone with money rather than land: you can donate cash to the foundation, which can then buy properties itself. WHAT THE PROTECTION ACTUALLY CONSISTS OF: a nature conservation plan drawn up TOGETHER WITH THE LANDOWNER, mapping natural values, the land's history and any cultural traces, and judging which parts should be allowed to develop freely, which need restoration, and which require recurring management to keep their values. The work proceeds stepwise, adapted to the site, the resources and local engagement. Its expertise rests on reserve management experience and nature conservation biology research. A PRACTICAL NOTE IT GIVES ON BUYING: there is a relatively extensive set of rules to handle; it is generally easier if the buyer is resident in Sweden, and it helps if the seller is a limited company or other legal person.

trackers.name: Naturarvet and the local naturarv foundations — buy a square of old forest and get its coordinates
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a Swedish insamlingsstiftelse whose purpose is to acquire forest land with protection-worthy OLD FOREST, in order to protect its threatened animal and plant species, registered in 2004, non-profit, and holding a 90-account — meaning it is audited by Svensk Insamlingskontroll and at least 75 per cent of funds must go to the purpose. Ask whether a fundraising body holds the national audit account before donating; in Sweden that number is the check. THE FUNDRAISING MECHANIC WORTH COPYING: on its site you can buy a gift certificate in the 'forest shop', or EARMARK YOUR OWN COORDINATE-TAGGED FOREST SQUARE and an 'umbrella tree' in the most recently acquired forests, receiving the GPS COORDINATES so you can visit it; monthly givers are called forest godparents. Tying a gift to a specific piece of ground creates a personal relationship between the giver and the forest — and it began with 840,000 kronor raised for its first purchase. Twelve forests acquired to date, the latest 182 hectares of birch-rich mire mosaic. AND THE MUNICIPAL VERSION, which is the model a single town can copy: a local naturarv foundation exists to protect valuable nature in ONE municipality, using collected funds as a COMPLEMENT to state and municipality, accepting gifts of property as well as money, listed with funeral directors for memorial giving, and taking company donations. Its purpose: through land purchase, land exchange or otherwise, to secure the protection of ecologically especially sensitive environments — with its board keeping a running dialogue with the county board and the municipality.

trackers.name: Donera skog — give your forest, or give a TRADE-IN forest to swap with
trackers.desc: THE OFFER, in one sentence: if you own a forest that you wish to be preserved for all time, YOU CAN DONATE IT to the foundation. Or why not donate A TRADE-IN FOREST — ordinary woodland given so it can be exchanged for the old-growth parcel someone else will not sell. A trade-in forest is a way for an owner of unremarkable woodland to save a remarkable one somewhere else, and this file has now recorded the same swap logic in Belgium and Finland. WHAT THE FOUNDATION IS FOR: a charitable foundation whose purpose is TO ACQUIRE FOREST PROPERTIES WITH OLD-GROWTH FOREST, in order to preserve biodiversity by protecting endangered animal and plant species, and otherwise to promote research, OUTDOOR LIFE AND TOURISM for present and future generations. AND THE FINANCIAL GUARANTEES, which answer the first question any donor asks: it was registered on 15 January 2004, is non-profit, and holds a 90-ACCOUNT, WHICH GUARANTEES THAT COLLECTED FUNDS ARE NOT BURDENED BY UNREASONABLE COSTS AND THAT AT LEAST 75 PER CENT IS USED for the purpose. Its own structure and statutes GUARANTEE THAT FOREST BOUGHT BY THE FOUNDATION IS PROTECTED FOR ALL FUTURE TIME.

trackers.name: A LOCAL collection foundation — a branch that started its own land-buying fund
trackers.desc: THE MOST COPYABLE THING IN THIS ROUND: a local branch FORMED, IN OCTOBER 2021, THE COLLECTION FOUNDATION BORLANGE'S NATURAL HERITAGE. JUST LIKE THE NATURE CONSERVANCY AND NATURARVET, WE WANT TO COLLECT MONEY FROM INDIVIDUALS, COMPANIES, ASSOCIATIONS AND POLITICAL PARTIES IN ORDER TO BUY FOREST AND LAND, TO GIVE IT PERMANENT PROTECTION, AS A COMPLEMENT TO THE MUNICIPALITY AND THE STATE. Sweden had five acquisition entries against 85 total. A local branch can found its own collection foundation and buy in its own municipality — the national bodies are a model to copy, not only a door to knock on. AND THE FIGURE THAT MADE THEIR CASE, which any community can compute for its own area: OF BORLANGE'S AREA, AT PRESENT ABOUT 3.9 PER CENT IS FORMALLY PROTECTED. WITH THE NATURE RESERVES THAT ARE UNDER FORMATION THE AREA WILL INCREASE TO ABOUT 4.5 PER CENT. A municipality's own protected percentage, set against the international target, is the argument that starts a local fund — they cite the position that WE NEED TO PROTECT AT LEAST 30 PER CENT OF ALL LAND AND WATER SURFACE... IN SWEDEN, IN THE COUNTY AND ALSO IN THE MUNICIPALITY, PERMANENTLY, IN ECOLOGICALLY REPRESENTATIVE AND INTERCONNECTED AREAS. AND THE HONEST QUALIFIER THEY ADD: THAT DOES NOT MEAN THE REMAINING 70% CAN BE CLEAR-FELLED; GENTLER METHODS ARE NEEDED THAT TAKE ACCOUNT OF THE FOREST AS A CARBON SINK.

trackers.name: A purchase agreed with TWO YEARS to raise the money — five million crowns for an old forest
trackers.desc: THE DEAL STRUCTURE THAT MAKES A COMMUNITY PURCHASE POSSIBLE: the foundation HAS AGREED WITH THE OWNERS OF a named OLD-GROWTH FOREST ON THE PURCHASE OF THE FOREST FOR PERPETUAL PRESERVATION, and HAS BEEN GIVEN TWO YEARS TO COLLECT THE JUST OVER FIVE MILLION CROWNS REQUIRED TO BUY THE FOREST. An agreed price with a two-year window to raise it is the arrangement that lets a public collection outrun a developer — the land is off the market while the money is found, and progress is public: WE HAVE TWO YEARS, AND ON THE WEBSITE YOU CAN FOLLOW HOW THE COLLECTION IS GOING. AND THE SCARCITY FIGURES THAT JUSTIFY IT, which transfer to any Swedish case: OF OLD NATURAL FORESTS IN SWEDEN ONLY AROUND FOUR PER CENT REMAIN, AND EVERY YEAR MORE OLD-GROWTH FOREST IS FELLED. OF THE FOREST BELOW THE MOUNTAIN RANGE, ABOUT 1.5 PER CENT HAS FORMAL PROTECTION IN NATIONAL PARKS AND NATURE RESERVES, WHILE SWEDEN HAS PROMISED IN INTERNATIONAL AGREEMENTS TO PROTECT AT LEAST 17 PER CENT OF ITS LAND AREA. trackers.name: Naturskyddsföreningen i Stockholm — länsförbund
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Naturskyddsföreningen länsförbund for Stockholm — the county tier of Sweden's largest environmental association, an association in its own right with its own board, whose stated job is to support the local kretsar and to watch and influence nature and environment questions in its own county. WHY IT MATTERS HERE: under 16 kap. 13 § miljöbalken the right to appeal permits, approvals and dispensations is limited by membership and years-of-operation thresholds that most neighbourhood groups fail. It also coordinates the kretsar in the county, so it can tell you which local group already covers your municipality.

trackers.name: UODO — Personal Data Protection Office
trackers.desc: UODO — Personal Data Protection Office — Poland’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Register of Professional Lobbyists
trackers.desc: Poland's official register of professional lobbyists. — Holds to account: professional lobbyists in Poland — find the official register of who conducts professional lobbying.

trackers.name: SAOS – Court Judgment Analysis System
trackers.desc: Open database aggregating judgments of Polish common, administrative and supreme courts. · Find here: a free system aggregating and analysing Polish court judgments (SAOS).

trackers.name: Pracownia na rzecz Wszystkich Istot (Workshop for All Beings)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Polish association that has spent since 1990 forcing its way into administrative proceedings and winning — a civil suit against Lasy Państwowe over the Białowieża Forest logging, brought under art. 323 of the environmental protection act, produced an interim order banning felling in the most valuable fragments; the Gliwice administrative court confirmed its right to be a party in the environmental proceeding for a Pilsko chairlift; the Kraków court fined a building inspectorate for a 54-month delay over an illegally expanded resort. Publishes 'Paragrafy dla przyrody', a watchers' handbook on joining a proceeding as a party and appealing the decision. WHO IT SUITS: a group facing a road, ski lift, resort or logging plan that needs standing first and arguments second.

trackers.name: Klub Przyrodników — wykup gruntów i tworzenie rezerwatów
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: buys ecologically valuable ground and then gets the state to protect it — land it purchased was, on the Klub's own application, given nature-reserve status, which is the whole sequence a community needs and the reason this is more than a land trust. It has been buying since close to its founding: xerothermic grassland at Owczary, land in the Obra valleys, then peatlands and grasslands scattered across the country from the Odra to the Rospuda, passing 150 hectares owned or co-owned, latterly with WWF Polska under a privately-protected-areas programme. USE IT: two doors. If a parcel is for sale, this is the buyer of last resort for peatland, fen and dry grassland in particular. And its current programme exists precisely to bring local organisations, activists and enthusiasts into the creation of NEW nature reserves, working from a database of sites that qualify for reserve protection — so if your site is good enough, the route is to get it onto that list rather than to fight the development on its own terms.

trackers.name: Provincial Administrative Court in Warsaw
trackers.desc: Provincial Administrative Court in Warsaw — administrative court (Poland).

trackers.name: Central Register of Beneficial Owners (CRBO)
trackers.desc: Central Register of Beneficial Owners (CRBO) — Poland’s beneficial-ownership register, disclosing the real individuals who ultimately own or control companies. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A PLAIN COMPANY REGISTRY: this names the real HUMAN owners behind a company; a company registry names only the legal entity, its directors and filings. Use the registry first to find the entity, then this to pierce the shell to the people who profit. — Holds to account: the hidden owners behind firms dealing with Poland’s government — find beneficial-owner filings.

trackers.name: KRS (National Court Register)

trackers.name: e-Zamówienia

trackers.name: Provincial Administrative Court in Łódź

trackers.name: Central Registration and Information on Business

trackers.name: Statistics Poland (GUS)
trackers.desc: Poland's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Poland.

trackers.name: Najwyższa Izba Kontroli (NIK)
trackers.desc: Poland's supreme audit office — independent audit of the government's economy, public spending and administration. — Holds to account: the Polish government — find audits of state spending and the annual analysis of budget execution.

trackers.name: Sejm Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej
trackers.desc: Official Polish Sejm (lower house) website with legislative documentation, voting records, and comprehensive parliamentary archives. — Holds to account: top officials & cabinet — find their assets, interests and integrity declarations.

trackers.name: WFOŚiGW — your statute wording is the eligibility gate
trackers.desc: APPLY REGIONALLY, NOT NATIONALLY. NFOŚiGW is central and has no regional branches; the 16 voivodeship funds (WFOŚiGW) are where a local association realistically applies.
