trackers.name: Personal Data Protection Service of Georgia
trackers.desc: Personal Data Protection Service of Georgia — Georgia’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Georgia
trackers.desc: Official site of Georgia's highest (cassation) court with judgments and case information. · Find here: information and judgments of the Supreme Court of Georgia.

trackers.name: Ask Gov — FOI requests (GEO)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); Ask Gov — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: GYLA (Georgian Young Lawyers' Association)
trackers.desc: Georgian legal-watchdog NGO (since 1994) that monitors government activities and elections (15+ years of election observation), advocates legislative and institutional reform, and runs accountability projects on budget spending and freedom of information.

trackers.name: Green Alternative (Association Green Alternative)
trackers.desc: Georgia's leading environmental and social-justice organisation, formed out of the campaigners of Friends of the Earth Georgia and a member of the CEE Bankwatch Network. It targets large projects with severe environmental or social impacts — hydropower above all, plus transport schemes and privatisation deals — and its published case files are unusually detailed, documenting for instance a hydropower plant approved inside Kazbegi National Park despite an explicit statutory prohibition. WHO TO ENLIST when a dam, road or concession lands on your valley. You CAN: use its alternative report on Aarhus Convention implementation in Georgia to argue access to information and public participation, and reach the wider Georgian Green Network and the independent forest monitoring network, both of which it founded. For activists: it explicitly pairs campaign work with capacity building of local groups and getting them directly into the campaign, so approach it as a partner rather than a service — with around ten staff, it cannot take everything. IF THE PROJECT HAS AN INTERNATIONAL LENDER, YOU HAVE A SECOND FORUM THAT IS NOT A GEORGIAN COURT. Green Alternative's distinctive capability is filing to the independent accountability mechanisms of the banks funding a scheme — the EBRD's Project Complaint Mechanism and its successor IPAM, the European Investment Bank's Complaints Mechanism, the IFC and the ADB — and it publishes the filed texts under a Complaints section on its own site, which is the closest thing to a template a Georgian community will find. COMMUNITIES CAN BE CO-COMPLAINANTS, NOT JUST SUBJECTS: the Nenskra hydropower complaints of 30 May and 1 June 2018 were submitted by CEE Bankwatch Network, Green Alternative and community representatives from the potentially affected areas, and on the Shuakhevi scheme it was one of the heavily affected villages that filed to the EBRD, IFC and ADB mechanisms itself. THE TIMELINES ARE THE PLANNING FIGURE AND THEY VARY ENORMOUSLY: on Paravani the EBRD's mechanism concluded that three sections of the bank's Environmental and Social Policy had been breached about six months after the complaint; on Nenskra it took roughly two years, with the EIB concluding in February 2020 and the EBRD compliance review reporting in July 2020, and both found the 280 MW project non-compliant on indigenous peoples' rights, cultural heritage, gender, assessment and management of environmental and social impacts, information disclosure and community engagement. THE LIMIT THAT MUST BE UNDERSTOOD BEFORE YOU FILE: a non-compliance finding is a ruling about the bank's own standards, not an injunction. It does not by itself stop construction; its value is leverage over the lender, evidence for a domestic case, and a public record. WHO TO ASK FOR: David Chipashvili coordinates the international financial institutions monitoring programme; Rusudan Panozishvili is media and community coordinator at panozishvili@greenalt.org. SECURITY CONTEXT, STATED BECAUSE IT CHANGES WHAT IS SAFE TO DO: on the Namakhvani cascade the state dispersed a local protest at Zhoneti with police on 14 November 2020, and on Khudoni the organisations criticising the project reported a campaign aimed at undermining their reputation. Green Alternative works alongside the Social Justice Center and GYLA, the latter already in this file, so a community facing that kind of pressure should be routed to legal representation early rather than late.

trackers.name: State Audit Office
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Georgia, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Anti-Corruption Bureau — Asset Declarations
trackers.desc: National asset-declaration registry; Georgia’s Anti-Corruption Bureau publishes ~60,000 searchable officials’ asset declarations online (monitoring moved here from the Civil Service Bureau; two-month review before publication), Georgia.

trackers.name: Georgia — public officials’ asset declarations
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official asset-declaration register); Georgia — public officials’ asset declarations — the Civil Service Bureau’s public database and monitoring system for Georgian officials’ asset declarations.

trackers.name: IDFI (Institute for Development of Freedom of Information)
trackers.desc: Georgian watchdog/think-tank (since 2009) promoting freedom of information, open governance and anti-corruption. Monitors public procurement, the state and municipal budgets, and proactive disclosure by public bodies; advances citizen participation in decision-making, budgeting and lawmaking at central and local levels; and publishes officials' asset-declaration data (including after access to the official portal was restricted).

trackers.name: NAPR
trackers.desc: Georgia's National Agency of Public Registry (company registry). — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Public Defender of Georgia — National Preventive Mechanism
trackers.desc: Public Defender of Georgia — National Preventive Mechanism — Georgia’s OPCAT National Preventive Mechanism — the Public Defender’s Special Preventive

trackers.name: State Procurement (Ge)
trackers.desc: Georgia's unified electronic state-procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Georgia, and for how much.

trackers.name: National Statistics Office of Georgia (GeoStat)
trackers.desc: Georgia's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Georgia.

trackers.name: დაცული ლანდშაფტი — the category for a place where people live
trackers.desc: GEORGIA'S PROTECTED AREA LAW, adopted 1996, provides 5 categories — state reserve, national park, natural monument, managed reserve and protected landscape. THE LAST IS THE ONE THAT FITS AN INHABITED PLACE: დაცული ლანდშაფტი is created expressly for the harmonious coexistence of nature and people, development of recreation and tourism, and support for the region's economic potential and the population's living conditions — and different zones may be arranged within it. That zoning flexibility is what makes it usable where people live and work, and it is the same category Skopje used for Vodno. It may sit inside a biosphere reserve or World Heritage site, or itself contain a natural monument. For sustainable resource use, zones with different permissible ratios of conservation and multiple use may be delineated. The first official reserve on Georgian territory dates to 1912.

trackers.name: Caucasus Nature Fund — it matches your government, so lobby your government
trackers.desc: A FUNDING MODEL WITH A LEVERAGE ARGUMENT BUILT IN. CNF is a conservation trust fund founded in 2007 by Conservation International, Germany's development ministry and WWF, with offices in Tbilisi and Yerevan, supporting 18 protected areas across Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia. Its mission is long-term funding for operating costs — the hardest money to raise anywhere in this map — plus improved management. THE MECHANISM: it works through partnerships with the three governments by matching, but not exceeding, the state budgets. So CNF money rises and falls with what your own government commits, which means lobbying your government to raise its protected-area budget also raises the matched international money. Use that argument directly. WHAT ASSEMBLES AT SCALE: a five-year initiative for 12 Georgian protected areas totalled USD 10 million — USD 1.8m GEF, USD 4.8m from the environment ministry, USD 3.1m CNF and USD 200,000 from the Bank of Georgia. AND KNOW WHO MANAGES YOUR SITE: protected areas total 600,597 ha, about 8 percent of the country, but only 387,800 ha — 64 percent of them — is managed by the Agency of Protected Areas. More than a third sits elsewhere, so identify the manager before directing a complaint.

trackers.name: Caucasus Nature Fund — matches the state park budget, so cutting the park costs the state euros
trackers.desc: THE LEVER HERE IS THE MATCHING RULE, NOT THE GRANT. CNF publishes an “up to 50 percent principle”: it matches, but never exceeds, what the state itself budgets for a protected area. Read that backwards and it is an argument you can put in writing to the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture or the Agency of Protected Areas — every lari stripped from a park's operating budget, and every hectare degazetted out of it, strips matching European money with it. Georgia is the bulk of CNF's programme: 16 of its 21 parks, among them Borjomi-Kharagauli, Vashlovani, Tusheti, Lagodekhi, Kolkheti, Kobuleti, Mtirala, Machakhela, Kintrishi, Kazbegi, Algeti, Javakheti, Batsara-Babaneuri, Pshav-Khevsureti and the newer Racha National Park, Aragvi and Truso Protected Landscapes. WHO TO CONTACT: the Tbilisi programme office, via the contact page and named executive director at caucasus-naturefund.org/about_us/contact/. WHAT YOU CANNOT GET: a grant. The money goes to protected-area administrations under agreement with the government, not to community groups, and there is no community application window. Two practical uses instead: CNF funds SMART patrolling and a ten-year biodiversity monitoring plan in Georgia, so ask the park administration what CNF-funded monitoring already covers your area before you pay for your own survey; and CNF states that the management plans it funds are made with a participatory approach involving local communities and farmers, which is a documented commitment you can hold a park administration to when a plan is written without you. EXCLUSION: CNF's mandate names Azerbaijan but its published park list contains no Azerbaijani site. A CLOSED GRANT PROGRAMME STILL LEAVES A DIRECTORY BEHIND, AND THIS IS HOW TO FIND THE LOCAL ORGANISATIONS THIS MAP COULD NOT. The international hotspot fund that helped establish this body ran a Caucasus investment programme covering Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan, awarding 42 large and 87 small grants — TWENTY-ONE LOCAL ORGANISATIONS RECEIVED ABOUT 3.08 MILLION DOLLARS BETWEEN THEM, and more than seventy-five local organisations and scientific institutions received grants across the wider regional programme. That investment programme has concluded, so it is not a place to apply for money now. BUT THAT FUND PUBLISHES A GRANTEE-PROJECTS DATABASE WITH A PAGE FOR EACH PROJECT, NAMING THE ORGANISATION THAT RECEIVED IT. Browse it for this country and you have a list of local conservation bodies that were funded, vetted and capable enough to manage a grant — which is precisely the layer this map has repeatedly failed to reach by searching. Many will still exist; some will have moved on; all are worth a name search. THE SAME LOGIC APPLIES TO ANY FUNDER: ASK, OR LOOK UP, WHO HOLDS OR HELD ITS GRANTS IN YOUR DISTRICT. A funder has already done the work of finding and checking the small organisations in a country, and that work is usually public. ONE MORE THING WORTH KNOWING IF YOUR OWN GROUP IS SMALL: in that programme, local organisations with less capacity to manage small grants WERE TRAINED IN PROPOSAL WRITING, REPORTING AND PROJECT MANAGEMENT by the coordinating office. Lack of grant-management experience is a common reason small groups do not apply; ask any funder whether that support comes with the grant, because it sometimes does.TWO THINGS THIS ENTRY DID NOT RECORD, AND THE SECOND IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS TO A COMMUNITY WITH NO PARK NEARBY. FIRST, WHAT THE MATCHING GRANTS ACTUALLY BUY: OPERATING COSTS INCLUDING SALARY SUPPLEMENTS, ESSENTIAL EQUIPMENT AND MAINTENANCE — ALONGSIDE MANAGEMENT PLANS, BIODIVERSITY MONITORING SYSTEMS AND ECOTOURISM PROGRAMMES THAT SUPPORT LOCAL LIVELIHOODS. SALARY SUPPLEMENTS ARE THE RAREST LINE IN THIS ENTIRE FILE. ALMOST EVERY FUNDER RECORDED HERE PAYS FOR PROJECTS; THIS ONE HELPS PAY THE WAGES OF THE PEOPLE WHO GUARD THE LAND — CURRENTLY SUPPORTING THE WORK AND LIVELIHOODS OF AROUND EIGHT HUNDRED AND FIFTY PARK EMPLOYEES ACROSS FIVE PROTECTED AREAS IN ONE COUNTRY AND SIXTEEN IN ANOTHER, WITH FUNDING ALSO REACHING MONITORING, CAPACITY BUILDING AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT IN AND AROUND THOSE AREAS. THE FUND HAS GROWN FROM SEVEN AND A HALF MILLION EUROS AT ITS START IN 2008 TO MORE THAN EIGHTY-FIVE MILLION IN ASSETS, RUNNING AN ANNUAL PROGRAMME OF JUST UNDER FOUR MILLION. AND ITS FIRST ACT IS WORTH KNOWING BECAUSE IT SHOWS WHAT IT WILL DO QUICKLY: SIXTY THOUSAND EUROS OF EMERGENCY FUNDING FOR FIREFIGHTING EQUIPMENT FOR A NATIONAL PARK AFTER FIRES, IN ITS FIRST YEAR. SECOND, AND MORE USEFUL WHERE THERE IS NO PROTECTED AREA YET: THE SAME EUROPEAN DEVELOPMENT MINISTRY THAT CAPITALISED THIS FUND ALSO FINANCES THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW PROTECTED AREAS AND MAJOR PROTECTED-AREA INFRASTRUCTURE THROUGH SEPARATE OPEN PROGRAMMES FOR ALL THREE COUNTRIES OF THE REGION, AND FINANCES TRANSBOUNDARY COOPERATION THROUGH A JOINT SECRETARIAT. SO THE MONEY TO CREATE A PROTECTED AREA IS HELD SEPARATELY FROM THE MONEY TO RUN ONE. A COMMUNITY WHOSE GROUND HAS NO STATUS SHOULD ASK ABOUT THE OPEN PROGRAMME, NOT THE TRUST FUND — the fund matches the budgets of areas that already exist, while the open programme pays for bringing new ones into being. ASKING THE WRONG ONE WASTES A YEAR.

trackers.name: Legal Aid Service — the free consultation has no means test; only representation does
trackers.desc: THE INVERSION: THE CONSULTATION IS OPEN TO EVERYONE, AND YOU NEED BRING NOTHING. The Service states that its free consultation may be used by any person and that no document is required to obtain one, though bringing the papers about your problem makes it a better one. The means test bites only at the next stage — a state-paid advocate to actually run your case requires registration as a low-income person or another reason you cannot pay. So the sequence for a community facing a permit or a land decision is: take the free consultation first, on the facts, before spending anything on establishing eligibility. WHERE: the Service works through a network of bureaux, consultation centres and a register of invited public advocates; ka.wikipedia lists 13 bureaux and 39 consultation centres, a figure this entry does not treat as established — use the office list on legalaid.ge. Contact info@legalaid.ge, +995 32 292 00 55. HONEST GAP, AND IT IS THE IMPORTANT ONE: this entry does not establish that administrative disputes over land, planning permissions or environmental decisions fall within the case categories eligible for a state-paid advocate. Ask that question on the first call and get the answer before building a plan around it. A second claim seen only on a third-party legal directory, not on legalaid.ge, is that the Service is subordinate to no state body and reports only to the Parliament of Georgia; if true it matters a great deal when your opponent is a ministry, so ask them to confirm it rather than relying on it. SEARCH TRAP: querying this body in English returns the United States state of Georgia almost exclusively, and adding “legalaid.ge” to the query does not fix it — search the Georgian name. IT NOW TRAVELS: ASK FOR THE MOBILE LEGAL CLINIC. With support from a foreign government and a United Nations agency, the service launched a mobile legal clinic to bring free legal assistance to PEOPLE LIVING IN THE HIGHLANDS, IN VILLAGES AFFECTED BY CONFLICT, AND IN HARD-TO-REACH REGIONS — with a team of lawyers and consultants travelling out, the first journey going to a village on the administrative boundary line. That matters for land defence specifically, because the communities least able to reach a lawyer are usually the ones whose land is furthest from scrutiny. If you are in a mountain village or a border district, ask when the mobile clinic is next in your municipality rather than assuming you must travel to a city office.FOUR OPERATIONAL FACTS WERE NOT RECORDED HERE, AND THE FIRST IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST TO ANYONE FIGHTING A PERMIT: THE SERVICE'S HELP EXTENDS TO PUBLIC ADVOCATE REPRESENTATION IN CERTAIN CIVIL AND ADMINISTRATIVE CASES — AND TO REPRESENTATION BEFORE AN ADMINISTRATIVE ORGAN, NOT ONLY IN COURT. REPRESENTATION AT THE AGENCY STAGE IS THE HELP COMMUNITIES ALMOST NEVER GET. MOST FREE-AID SCHEMES IN THIS REGION BEGIN ONLY WHEN A CASE REACHES COURT, BY WHICH TIME THE PERMIT IS ISSUED AND THE ARGUMENT IS ABOUT UNDOING IT — SO ASK EXPLICITLY FOR REPRESENTATION IN THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDING WHILE IT IS STILL RUNNING. SECOND, THE CONSULTATION ITSELF REQUIRES NO DOCUMENTS AT ALL, AND CAN BE TAKEN IN PERSON OR REMOTELY THROUGH THE SERVICE'S ONLINE HELP OR IN WRITING. THAT REMOVES THE USUAL FIRST OBSTACLE: A HOUSEHOLD THAT CANNOT PROVE ITS TITLE, OR HAS NOT YET SEEN THE PROJECT PAPERS, CAN STILL ASK WHAT ITS POSITION IS — AND A VILLAGE DOES NOT HAVE TO TRAVEL TO ASK. THIRD, TIMING DIFFERS BY CASE TYPE: IN CRIMINAL MATTERS AN ADVOCATE IS ENGAGED IMMEDIATELY, WHILE CIVIL AND ADMINISTRATIVE MATTERS FOLLOW A SLOWER PROCEDURE UNLESS THE CIRCUMSTANCES REQUIRE AN IMMEDIATE DECISION. SO IF A DEADLINE IS RUNNING — AN OBJECTION PERIOD, A NOTICE, A CONSULTATION CLOSING — SAY SO IN WRITING AT FIRST CONTACT AND ASK FOR THE MATTER TO BE TREATED AS REQUIRING AN IMMEDIATE DECISION. THE EXCEPTION EXISTS BUT HAS TO BE INVOKED. FOURTH, COVERAGE IS SOMEBODY'S DECISION: THE SERVICE'S COUNCIL DECIDES ON THE CREATION AND ABOLITION OF BUREAUX AND CONSULTATION CENTRES AND DEFINES THEIR OPERATING TERRITORIES, AND ALSO APPROVES THE PROCEDURE FOR ENGAGING A REGISTERED ADVOCATE IN A CASE AND THEIR REMUNERATION. IF NO OFFICE COVERS YOUR DISTRICT, THE BODY THAT DECIDES COVERAGE IS NAMED AND CAN BE WRITTEN TO — AND A JOINT REQUEST FROM SEVERAL VILLAGES FOR A CONSULTATION CENTRE IS A DIFFERENT AND MORE WINNABLE ASK THAN A REQUEST FOR A LAWYER IN ONE CASE.

trackers.name: Agency of Protected Areas — its mandate covers landslide, erosion and water-recharge ground, not only wildlife
trackers.desc: READ ITS OBJECTIVES BEFORE YOU DECIDE WHAT YOUR SITE IS, BECAUSE ONE OF THEM IS NOT ABOUT WILDLIFE AT ALL: the Agency lists among its aims the protection of territories actively affected by erosion, mudslides, floods, avalanches and landslides, and of areas of surface and underground water formation together with their flow and discharge areas, from anthropogenic impact. Most Georgian development fights are about slopes and water rather than species, and this is the clause that lets a community put such a site forward on its own terms instead of straining to find a rare animal. A second, separately useful aim is the conservation and restoration of historical-cultural landscapes and landscapes characteristic of architectural and archaeological complexes — the heritage-landscape route. THE DOOR: the Agency's stated objective includes planning, creating and developing NEW protected areas, so there is a body whose job is to take ground into protection, not merely to run what already exists. It is doing so — a national park of roughly 15,000 hectares in Guria has been announced by the minister. It administers strict nature reserves, national parks, natural monuments, managed reserves, protected landscapes, biosphere reserves, world heritage sites and wetlands of international importance, and has been a legal entity of public law since 1 February 2008. TWO ENTRY POINTS THAT ARE PUBLIC AND EASY TO MISS. Management plans get public discussion sessions held at the Agency — the Batsara-Babaneuri protected areas plan was aired that way — so the plan governing your area is amendable at a meeting you can attend rather than a document handed down. And the Agency runs grant projects: it launched one for Ajameti with financial support from BP Georgia. That funding source is worth knowing before you rely on it: an oil company underwriting a protected-area grant programme is a real tension, not a detail. WHO: chaired by David Iosebashvili with Tamar Khakhishvili as deputy chair; Tbilisi. THE LIMIT, AND THIS FILE HAS NOW SEEN IT TWICE: the body that holds the land can be the body developing it. The Agency also runs ecotourism and visitor-centre infrastructure inside protected areas, and it sits under the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture, so do not expect it to front a fight against a scheme the government backs. Where that is the situation, Green Alternative is already in this file with a record of taking such projects to international lenders' accountability mechanisms. Cross-reference the Caucasus Nature Fund entry too: CNF matches state budgets for many of the parks this Agency administers, which is why cutting or shrinking one of them costs the state matched money.

trackers.name: NACRES — it drafts the management plan, and the management plan is what decides what is allowed inside a protected area
trackers.desc: THE POINT OF INTERVENTION MOST PEOPLE MISS IS THE PLAN, NOT THE PERMIT. A Georgian government analysis of protected areas records the Tusheti National Park management plan being revised by NACRES, and management plans determine what activity is permitted inside a protected area — grazing, infrastructure, tourism development, extraction. Read alongside the Agency of Protected Areas entry in this file, which holds public discussion sessions on draft management plans, that gives two nameable points at which a community can act on the document that will govern its area for years: the organisation drafting it, and the meeting where it is aired. Both come long before anyone applies for anything. WHAT MAKES IT USABLE RATHER THAN MERELY EMINENT: NACRES runs a Community Ranger programme that trains community members to take part in biodiversity monitoring of Georgia's protected areas, and its grassland work is built around exactly the conflict a rural community faces — it notes that local people have used grasslands now inside protected areas as grazing land for hundreds of years, and its Kazbegi assessment produces a grassland habitat distribution map and a database of pasture biodiversity, fodder quantity and ecological status feeding into a pasture management plan. If your dispute is about grazing or access inside a protected area, that baseline already exists or can be commissioned. It also works on human-wildlife conflict around protected areas and with the single settlement inside Borjomi-Kharagauli National Park. TRACK RECORD AND STANDING: founded as a group in 1989 and registered in 1991 as Noah's Ark Centre for the Recovery of Endangered Species, later renamed while keeping the acronym; more than seventy conservation projects, more than twenty-five donors, and per the Aarhus Clearinghouse some 130 scientific articles and nine books by its staff. It implemented Georgia's Biodiversity Country Study for the government with UNEP, and a named staff member coordinated the finalisation of the national biodiversity strategy — so its work is inside national policy, not outside it. Current field analysis of key species distribution across Georgia's protected areas, funded by the Caucasus Nature Fund and WWF, identifies pressures on populations and produces recommendations to the protected areas. THE LIMIT, AND IT IS THE SAME ONE THIS FILE HAS NOW RECORDED FOR RSCN, THE AGENCY OF PROTECTED AREAS AND OTHERS: NACRES is commissioned by the Caucasus Nature Fund, WWF, GEF/UNDP and the government itself. It is embedded with the institutions that manage the land rather than opposed to them, and should not be expected to front a fight against a scheme the state backs — Green Alternative, already in this file, is the body with that record. Use NACRES for the plan, the baseline and the evidence. Note also that the Tusheti plan-revision record comes from a 2012 government document; that NACRES still holds a plan-writing role today was not established this round.TWO PROGRAMMES OF THIS ORGANISATION TURN VILLAGERS INTO PEOPLE WITH A ROLE, AND NEITHER WAS RECORDED HERE. THE FIRST IS A COMMUNITY RANGER PROGRAMME FOCUSED ON INCREASING COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION IN BIODIVERSITY MONITORING OF THE COUNTRY'S PROTECTED AREAS, TRAINING ITS PARTICIPANTS TO ASSIST WITH WILDLIFE MONITORING. A TRAINED COMMUNITY RANGER IS A PERSON WHOSE OBSERVATIONS COUNT — THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A VILLAGE SAYING THE ANIMALS HAVE GONE AND A VILLAGE PRODUCING MONITORING DATA THE PARK ADMINISTRATION ALREADY ACCEPTS. THE SECOND IS A COMMUNITY FIREFIGHTERS PROGRAMME WITH NAMED LOCAL VOLUNTEERS FROM A MOUNTAIN TOWN — CAPACITY THAT EXISTS BEFORE THE FIRE, IN A REGION WHERE THIS FILE HAS RECORDED BLAZES DESTROYING TENS OF THOUSANDS OF HECTARES. THE ORGANISATION'S OWN DESCRIPTION OF WHAT IT DOES FOR COMMUNITIES IS THE PART TO QUOTE WHEN APPROACHING: MOBILISING LOCAL COMMUNITY GROUPS AND LOCAL INITIATIVE GROUPS AND INVOLVING THEM IN CONSERVATION ACTIVITIES, STRENGTHENING THE CAPACITY OF LOCAL AND CENTRAL GOVERNMENT STRUCTURES AND OTHER ORGANISATIONS, AND RAISING AWARENESS AMONG LOCAL RESOURCE USERS. LOCAL INITIATIVE GROUP IS THEIR TERM FOR WHAT MOST COMMUNITIES IN THIS FILE ACTUALLY ARE: A FEW HOUSEHOLDS WITH A PROBLEM AND NO REGISTRATION. AN ORGANISATION THAT NAMES THEM AS ITS WORK IS ONE THAT WILL TAKE A CALL FROM ONE. IT IS ALSO REACHABLE IN TWO PLACES RATHER THAN ONE — A HEAD OFFICE IN THE CAPITAL WITH A STREET ADDRESS, TWO TELEPHONE NUMBERS AND AN EMAIL, AND A SECOND OFFICE IN A MOUNTAIN TOWN — AND IT PUBLISHES POLICY DOCUMENTS, MANAGEMENT PLANS, NEWS AND A SPECIES DATABASE, THE LAST BEING THE DOCUMENT THAT SHOWS WHETHER WHAT LIVES ON YOUR GROUND MATTERS NATIONALLY.

trackers.name: SABUKO — it wrote the stocking rates meant to become the terms of the state's own grazing lease
trackers.desc: THE LEVER IS THE LEASE, AND SABUKO IS WRITING ITS TECHNICAL BASIS. Its published pasture management recommendations for the Chachuna Managed Reserve set estimated stocking rates and a provisional rotational grazing scheme, and state their purpose directly: the plan should serve as the basis for a future leasing contract that meets the requirements of a protected area. Where land is grazed under state lease, the terms of that lease decide what actually happens on the ground, and this is the organisation putting numbers into them. If your dispute concerns grazing pressure inside or beside a protected area, the stocking rate is the argument. UNDERSTAND THE SUBLEASE CHAIN FIRST, BECAUSE IT EXPLAINS THE OVERGRAZING AND MOST OUTSIDERS MISS IT: a large part of pasture is leased by the state to individuals, who then sub-let it to farmers at a considerably higher price. Farmers economise by leasing less land than they need and grazing more animals on it than permitted. The person degrading the land is often not the person holding the lease, and an intervention aimed at shepherds rather than at the rent structure will fail. Georgian sheep numbers fell roughly forty per cent after the Soviet period while pasture pressure rose, because the flocks were concentrated into small areas. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY DONE: since January 2019 it has led a gallery forest and grassland restoration project in the Iori river valley under the Endangered Landscapes Programme with the Cambridge Conservation Initiative and BirdLife International, assessing land cover across 748.1 hectares of Chachuna's 5,032, and it works in partnership with the local shepherds rather than over them. A SECOND CASE WORTH KNOWING IF YOUR SITE SITS BELOW AN UNFINISHED SCHEME: the Dali reservoir, begun in the 1980s and never completed as intended, is now sealed and limited to fishing and irrigation — but it drove desertification downstream, replacing floodplain forest species with arid ones. SABUKO's position is that state policy on the reservoir should serve conservation and not irrigation alone, with staged water release to restore natural flooding. Infrastructure that was never finished can still be the thing destroying your valley, and its operating rules can be reopened. The reserve holds over twenty-five raptor species, ten of Georgia's seventeen imperial eagle pairs, and a count of ten thousand little bustard on the grasslands. Successor to the Georgian Centre for the Conservation of Wildlife; BirdLife's Georgian partner. ONE THING TO WEIGH: SABUKO also builds ecotourism infrastructure inside the reserve, and reporting on the opening acknowledged that many Georgian protected-area tourism projects have damaged biodiversity through noise, light and habitat pressure. Its own stated safeguard is a management plan per site with income returned to conservation. Pair with NACRES, already in this file, which drafts the management plans themselves. ASK FOR THE PASTURE PASSPORT FOR YOUR UNIT BEFORE ARGUING ABOUT ANYTHING ELSE. Georgian pasture units are documented in a four-page passport giving the unit's code and total area, maps of the land cover types with the area of each, A MAP OF AVAILABLE BIOMASS AND CARRYING CAPACITY, and THE NAMES OF THE FARMERS AND SHEPHERDS USING THAT UNIT WITH THEIR LIVESTOCK NUMBERS. The administering bodies use it to contract leases and to adjust unit boundaries, which means the document that decides your grazing already exists and already names you. It is the most specific land record this file has found anywhere in the region. KNOW WHO ACTUALLY ADMINISTERS THE GROUND, BECAUSE IN ONE MAJOR CASE IT IS NOT THE NATIONAL AGENCY: the Tusheti Protected Landscape, some 31,500 hectares, is unique among Georgia's protected areas in being MANAGED BY THE LOCAL SELF-GOVERNMENT — its administration sits inside Akhmeta municipality — and that administration, together with the protected areas agency, is what CONTRACTS THE LEASE AGREEMENTS WITH SHEPHERDS. This file recorded the same pattern in Lebanon, where reserve committees are composed of the surrounding municipalities: where a protected area is administered locally, your council is not petitioning the decision-maker, it IS the decision-maker. AND THERE IS A COMMUNITY BODY WITH REAL AUTHORITY: pasture user unions are community organisations with ELECTED EXECUTIVE BODIES THAT ARE LEGALLY AUTHORISED TO GOVERN PASTURES INDEPENDENTLY, working through community pasture management plans that carry maps delineating borders and specify how many animals can sustainably graze. If no union covers your pasture, forming one is the route to holding it — the same structure this file records for Kyrgyz pasture committees, which do have a national association behind them. Georgia's unions do not, so expect to work municipality by municipality. This organisation's own contribution sits directly on top of all of this: it has developed a pasture management scheme setting out how shepherds can use grazing sustainably and how the LEASING MECHANISMS CAN WORK MORE TRANSPARENTLY, built on a review of the legislation and years of consultation with pastoralists, and being written into a protected area management plan.

trackers.name: Social Justice Center — it argues mining benefit-sharing, not just whether the mine happens, and it works with environmental activists
trackers.desc: THE MOST USEFUL THING THIS ORGANISATION HAS DONE FOR A MINING COMMUNITY IS TO TREAT THE QUESTION AS THREE-SIDED RATHER THAN TWO. Its work on the Georgian mining sector examines the taxation and benefit-sharing arrangements around extraction, analyses the models in use, proposes a more equitable framework, and is deliberately published to local communities through articles, videos and infographics so that they can take it to government and to the companies themselves. Most communities are handed a binary — the project goes ahead or it does not — and lose it. What the community gets from a project that proceeds is a separate argument, and this is a body that has already built the case. IT ALSO ATTACKS LARGE DEVELOPMENTS ON THE GROUNDS A COMMUNITY CAN ACTUALLY USE: its published analysis of a major real-estate development project addresses the opacity of the underlying agreement, restricted access to environmental information, and disregard for public participation. Those three are procedural failures with remedies, unlike an argument about whether a scheme is desirable. WHAT IT PROVIDES DIRECTLY: legal assistance to individuals in human rights cases within its areas of expertise, and it names environmental activists among the groups it works with, alongside workers, minorities and others. On the manganese mining crisis at Chiatura it set out publicly that a reorganisation and mass dismissal affecting thousands of miners was being conducted unlawfully — identifying the exclusion of miners from the government's crisis working group, template consent forms circulated without informing workers of the new structures or terms, and the absence of the consultation with trade unions required before mass layoffs. That is the kind of specific procedural documentation that turns a grievance into a case. Founded in 2012 and based in Tbilisi; it describes its own politics openly, which a community should weigh in deciding whether it is the right partner for a particular fight. BEFORE YOU RELY ON IT, KNOW THIS: the organisation is under legal and financial pressure of its own. The European Court of Human Rights has begun examining the merits of its application concerning Georgia's foreign agents legislation and its law on grants, and a defenders network reports that the prosecutor's office has frozen the bank accounts of several Georgian human rights and civil society organisations. Its capacity may be constrained for reasons unrelated to your case. NAME CHECK: searching this name returns a large number of unrelated organisations in the American state of Georgia. Match on the .ge domain. FIND OUT WHICH FIRM WROTE THE IMPACT ASSESSMENT, AND WHAT ELSE IT HAS APPROVED. The assessment for a major Georgian hydropower scheme was prepared by a named private consultancy that green policy advocates had criticised for approving unsuccessful energy projects before. The document is not produced by the state — it is commissioned by the developer from a firm whose business depends on such commissions, and that firm's earlier approvals are on the record. A pattern of them is an argument about the reliability of the document itself, which is a different and stronger attack than disputing its conclusions. The same assessment confirmed that the scheme would submerge three villages, take land used by two more, isolate two others, and resettle 297 households — numbers taken from the developer's own document, which is where the strongest figures usually are. TWO THINGS FROM THE MANGANESE TOWN THIS ORGANISATION HAS WORKED ON ARE WORTH COPYING ANYWHERE. First, a local eco-club there convenes RESIDENTS, GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS AND COMPANIES TOGETHER for public discussion of local environmental problems and how to address them — a standing tripartite forum run by the community rather than by the company is a different footing from responding to consultations. Second, the miners coordinated their strike with that eco-club. Labour and environmental grievances in the same place, acting together rather than separately, is the combination this file has seen produce results in Turkiye as well, where village headmen joined associations as co-claimants. AND THE DIAGNOSIS OF WHY GEORGIAN CAMPAIGNS FAIL IS WORTH READING BEFORE YOU START: an independent analysis of these mobilisations found that the campaigns are often ISOLATED AND INWARD-LOOKING, which makes it hard to achieve unity with other social causes and therefore hard to draw strength from them. A campaign that stays local stays small. The federations and umbrella bodies recorded elsewhere in this file exist precisely to solve that, and reaching one early is cheaper than reaching one late. WHEN FINES FAIL, ASK FOR A SPECIAL MANAGER. The escalation against one Georgian mining operator is the clearest enforcement sequence this file has found anywhere, and it ends somewhere most campaigns never think to aim: the company operated until 2009 WITH NO ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT AND NO APPROPRIATE PERMIT AT ALL; its permit conditions were first inspected only in 2012, producing a fine of five thousand lari; in 2014, AFTER UNSUCCESSFUL ATTEMPTS TO FINE IT, the ministry imposed limits and restrictions; and in 2017 the city court APPOINTED A SPECIAL MANAGER OVER THE COMPANY to ensure compliance with its licence and permit conditions. THREE THINGS TO TAKE FROM THAT. A fine of a few thousand lari is not a deterrent and its real value is EVIDENTIARY — it establishes a documented breach you can point to later. The gap between the fine and the special manager was five years of the company continuing, so start the record early. And a court-appointed manager is a remedy worth naming explicitly in submissions, because it addresses the problem this file has recorded four times over — in Istanbul, on the Black Sea, in Ordu and here — that an order is not self-enforcing and a determined operator simply carries on. ALSO WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU START: the operator went thirteen years from privatisation to its first permit inspection, which means that in a mining region the absence of enforcement history is not evidence of compliance — it may be evidence that nobody has ever looked. Ask when the licence conditions were last inspected and what was found; if the answer is never, that is itself the finding. Residents of one village have protested since 2019 over destruction of their property and unpaid compensation, which is the situation this organisation's benefit-sharing work addresses.

trackers.name: Bankwatch — if the project is financed with international public money, the money has a complaints desk and this is who helps you use it
trackers.desc: FIND OUT WHO IS PAYING BEFORE YOU DECIDE HOW TO FIGHT. If a scheme is financed by a development bank rather than purely by private money, there is a second route entirely separate from your national courts: the lender's own accountability mechanism, which can investigate and can hold up disbursement. The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development established an independent project accountability mechanism in 2020; the European Investment Bank and the World Bank have their own. THIS NETWORK EXISTS TO HELP COMMUNITIES USE THAT ROUTE. In its own words it investigates the impacts of public finance, works with affected communities and local organisations, helps them protect their rights and livelihoods, and makes sure their stories are told in Europe's power centres — it meets the institutions it monitors and keeps staff in Brussels. Its stated purpose is working with local communities on campaigns to stop or change harmful investment projects funded by international public finance. IT HAS DONE THIS IN GEORGIA SPECIFICALLY, MAINTAINING PROJECT PAGES ON NAMED GEORGIAN HYDROPOWER SCHEMES, and it reports supporting civil society across the Caucasus and Central Asia since 2000 in influencing internationally financed projects. USE IT ALONGSIDE THE GEORGIAN ORGANISATION THAT IS ITS MEMBER HERE, NOT INSTEAD OF IT — the member knows the valley and the ministry; the network is in the room when the lender's board meets. Those are different jobs and a community needs both. It has seventeen member groups across fourteen countries in central and eastern Europe and the Caucasus, with a secretariat in Prague and staff spread across the region, and it publishes an anti-corruption reporting procedure with named contacts and protection for those who report. THE LIMIT DECIDES WHETHER IT IS YOUR ROUTE AND IT IS SHARP: it works on projects financed with international public money. If your quarry, road or dam is funded domestically or by a private company with no development bank behind it, this is not the door — check the financing first, because the answer determines which of the routes in this file applies. It is also a network rather than a local service: it works through its member organisations, and in Georgia that means approaching the member.

trackers.name: Inclusive Development International — it traces who is actually financing a project, on request from the community
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE BODY THAT ANSWERS THE QUESTION THE OTHER FINANCE ENTRIES IN THIS FILE TELL YOU TO ASK FIRST. Since 2016 it has taken requests from community advocates to research and map the investment and supply chains behind harmful projects, identifying the banks, investors, insurers, development finance institutions and major brands that make them possible. Its researchers work from financial databases, company reports, import data and shipping manifests — so ownership can be traced even where a developer discloses nothing locally and the national registry shows only a shell. WHAT COMES BACK IS NOT RAW DATA BUT A SUMMARY WITH AN ANALYSIS OF PRESSURE POINTS AND POSSIBLE ADVOCACY STRATEGIES. In cases it judges to have high potential it will, on request, help execute legal, advocacy and negotiation strategies — and where it cannot take a case itself it refers it to partners with the capacity to help, so an approach that fails may still produce a referral. IT ALSO PUBLISHES FREE TOOLS THAT AUTOMATE THIS WORK — a shareholder tracker and a development bank investment tracker — built expressly because the financial databases it relies on are unaffordable for the communities that need them. Start there before asking anyone for anything. It trains advocates around the actual projects they are fighting, having trained more than fifteen hundred people in selected methods, and continues supporting them afterwards. USE IT WITH THE TWO OTHER FINANCE ENTRIES RECORDED FOR GEORGIA: this body finds the financier, the network carries the case to the lender's board in Brussels, and the Georgian member organisation knows the valley and the ministry. THE HONEST LIMIT: its documented casework and requests are from Southeast Asia, Africa and the Americas, and no work in Georgia or anywhere in this region could be established. The service is described as open to requests from community advocates without a stated geographic restriction, so the route is untested here rather than closed — approach it knowing that.

trackers.name: Front Line Defenders — a 24-hour line answered in Russian, and grants that pay the legal fees when you are the one being sued
trackers.desc: THE GRANT COVERS THE SITUATION THIS FILE HAS RECORDED IN GEORGIA: protection grants of up to €7,500 can pay LEGAL FEES FOR DEFENDERS WHO ARE BEING JUDICIALLY HARASSED, improve the physical security of an individual or an organisation, cover digital and communications security, pay medical fees for defenders attacked or made ill by their work, and provide family assistance where a defender is imprisoned or their family is at risk. This payload already records a Georgian organisation operating while a prosecutor froze the bank accounts of several rights bodies and its own legal status was contested at the European Court — which is precisely the circumstance this grant exists for. AND THERE IS A 24-HOUR EMERGENCY LINE, WITH THE OPTION TO BE FORWARDED TO SOMEONE SPEAKING RUSSIAN, alongside a secure encrypted email channel for urgent assistance. The person who answers can mobilise rapid international support. Note the language list before a crisis rather than during one. IT ALSO OFFERS TEMPORARY RELOCATION, training on holistic and digital security, and a rest and respite programme for defenders under extreme stress — the last of which matters in a country where campaigns run for years. READ THE EXCLUSIONS CAREFULLY, BECAUSE THEY DEFINE WHAT THIS IS NOT: it will not fund projects addressing broader human rights issues rather than the specific situation of defenders, will not cover defenders already in exile, and will not pay ongoing office costs such as salaries and rent. This is protection money, not programme money. Based in Dublin. THE LIMIT: no case of its own in Georgia could be established from what was reached, and the organisation publishes no country eligibility list; its service is described as open to defenders at risk without a stated geographic restriction. Treat it as available and untested rather than confirmed.

trackers.name: Legal assistance centres — free lawyers on private property cases, in four cities, who will file in court
trackers.desc: THE TWO THINGS THAT MATTER ARE THE CASE TYPE AND THE FACT THAT THEY FILE. Its lawyers provide free legal consultations, help prepare legal documents, AND SUBMIT THEM TO COURT IF NECESSARY — and the case types it names first are those relating to PRIVATE PROPERTY. A free consultation that stops at advice leaves a community where it started; this is a service that will put a document in front of a judge. AND IT IS NOT ONLY IN THE CAPITAL: centres operate in Tbilisi, Kutaisi, Batumi and Zugdidi — which puts a free property lawyer within reach of western Georgia, the Black Sea coast and Samegrelo, in a country where this file has recorded that almost everything else it lists is Tbilisi-based. Published street addresses and telephone numbers exist for the regional offices. WHAT IT IS NOT: a specialist environmental or planning practice. The other case type it names is labour rights in public service, and nothing found shows it litigating a development scheme or an environmental permit. Approach it as a property lawyer — which, for a community whose land is being taken, expropriated, devalued or encroached on, is frequently the more precise framing anyway, and this file has recorded elsewhere in the region that the property route often succeeds where the environmental one does not. IT SITS INSIDE THE GEORGIAN CHAPTER OF AN INTERNATIONAL ANTI-CORRUPTION NETWORK, so a matter that involves a permit obtained irregularly, a discretionary exception, or an undisclosed beneficiary falls squarely within its parent organisation's core work — this file recorded in R131 that a Tbilisi park permit rested on a discretionary exception granted in haste, and in R119 that identifying who benefits is a distinct and harder exercise than identifying who breached. USE IT ALONGSIDE THE OTHER GEORGIAN ROUTES RECORDED HERE: the state legal aid service for representation where you qualify, the rights litigator for strategic cases and benefit-sharing arguments, and the international financial complaint routes where a lender is involved.

trackers.name: Georgian National Platform — a published member list, and an environment working group with named members
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE DIRECTORY OF GEORGIAN CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS THAT THIS FILE PREVIOUSLY RECORDED AS NOT EXISTING. It publishes a list of member organisations, each tagged with the working groups it belongs to — and WORKING GROUP 3 IS ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION, CLIMATE CHANGE AND ENERGY SECURITY, with its own group members page, its own subgroups and published minutes. A community that cannot find who works on its issue in Georgia should read that group's membership before searching anything else; this map has failed three separate times to reach the Georgian organisational layer by searching, and here it is listed. IT ALSO HAS REGIONAL REPRESENTATIVES, which matters in a country where nearly everything else in this file operates from Tbilisi. MEMBERSHIP BRINGS TWO THINGS A COMMUNITY ORGANISATION CAN USE DIRECTLY: access to a REGRANTING SCHEME, and participation in consultations organised by the Council of Europe, the World Bank and the EUROPEAN INVESTMENT BANK. That last one is the sharpest: where an international lender finances the scheme you are contesting, a seat in its consultations is a route this file has otherwise only reached through foreign accountability organisations. Members also get advocacy training and access to European networks. IT IS PROPERLY CONSTITUTED RATHER THAN INFORMAL: an elected coordination council of nine, chosen at a general meeting, with a charter, a code of ethics, a compliance committee, a secretariat operating since 2013, and a published route to join. It exists to represent Georgian civil society in the European Union's eastern partnership structures and to work with government on association agreement implementation. AND IT DEFENDS ITS MEMBERS PUBLICLY: it has issued statements on a draft transparency law of the kind this file has recorded shutting down civil society in Kyrgyzstan, and on a smear campaign against civil society experts in Georgia. A body that will put its name to a defence of organisations under attack is worth knowing before the attack comes. THE LIMITS: it is a general civil society and European integration platform, not an environmental organisation — it will not object to a scheme, assess one, or litigate. Its membership is organisational, so an unregistered village group is unlikely to qualify directly; use it as a directory and a route to members who can act. ASK ABOUT SEA, NOT ONLY EIA. The environment working group's formal recommendations demand that ALL ENERGY PROJECTS ATTRACTING EUROPEAN UNION SUPPORT FULLY RESPECT BOTH ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT AND STRATEGIC ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT REGULATIONS — naming hydropower in this country specifically. This file has recorded impact assessment twenty times and strategic environmental assessment never. The difference matters: an impact assessment examines a project, while a strategic assessment examines the PLAN OR PROGRAMME the project sits inside. THAT IS THE ANSWER TO A TRICK THIS FILE HAS DOCUMENTED TWICE — a scheme split into small pieces to keep each below an assessment threshold, in Kazakhstan and Turkiye. THE PIECES MAY EACH ESCAPE AN IMPACT ASSESSMENT; THE PLAN THAT CONTAINS THEM SHOULD NOT ESCAPE A STRATEGIC ONE. Ask which plan or programme your project implements, and whether that plan was strategically assessed. AND THIS PLATFORM'S WORKING GROUP IS A ROUTE INTO THE EUROPEAN COMMISSION ITSELF: it meets twice a year, presents recommendations directly to the Commission's energy, environment, climate and neighbourhood departments, and its members have stated they are ready to act as partners in MONITORING AND CONDUCTING ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENTS. Where a scheme carries European funding or sits under an association agreement, a member organisation can carry your case to the people who fund it. ITS OWN STANDING POSITION IS WORTH QUOTING BACK: that despite the adoption of impact assessment legislation, SMALL AND LARGE-SCALE HYDROPOWER CONTINUES TO POSE A SERIOUS ENVIRONMENTAL THREAT across the region. A community objecting to a hydropower scheme here is not making a novel argument; it is making one an EU-facing civil society body has already put to the Commission in writing. THE RE-GRANTING SCHEME FUNDS REAL WORK, NOT JUST MEETINGS: past rounds financed an energy regulator watchdog coalition and waste management capacity building in selected regions of this country, run across several countries at once. A cross-border application with partners in neighbouring countries fits this scheme better than a purely local one.

trackers.name: IUCN NL Land Acquisition Fund — it pays for long-term rights over land, not only for buying it
trackers.desc: IT FUNDS THE ACQUISITION OF LONG-TERM MANAGEMENT RIGHTS WITHOUT ANY TRANSFER OF OWNERSHIP — long-term leases and conservation agreements — as well as outright purchase, with grants of up to around a hundred thousand euros to locally registered non-profit organisations. Read that against what this file has recorded in this country: a wildlife corridor declared by municipal decree without anyone's land being taken, pasture user unions legally authorised to hold and manage grazing land, and passports documenting who uses which pasture. THE MECHANISM THIS FUND PAYS FOR IS THE MECHANISM ALREADY IN USE HERE. ITS STRONGEST PRIORITY FOR A COMMUNITY FACING A SCHEME IS CONNECTIVITY: land that links fragmented habitat as a corridor or stepping stone, alongside sites holding critically endangered, endangered or vulnerable red list species and areas of recognised biodiversity value such as important bird areas. A scheme that severs a corridor creates exactly the case this fund exists to fund. THE LOCAL ORGANISATION HOLDS THE LAND AND THE RESPONSIBILITY, not the funder — the model is explicitly that the reserve belongs to the local body, which is familiar with the context and works with the community. ELIGIBILITY: locally registered as a non-profit, non-governmental or civil society organisation; directly responsible for the project; and holding A BANK ACCOUNT IN THE ORGANISATION'S OWN NAME in the country of establishment or of the project. An unregistered residents' group cannot apply alone and should work through one of the registered conservation bodies recorded elsewhere in this file. Annual call with a published spring deadline. Running since 2001 across more than forty countries. THE LIMITS, STATED PLAINLY: no project in this country was found in its published record, its examples run heavily to tropical habitats, and it funds acquisition rather than objection or litigation. Confirm eligibility with the fund before building an application around it.

trackers.name: Guardians of the Rioni Valley — the residents' movement that forced a government retreat on a dam
trackers.desc: THIS IS WHAT A COMMUNITY THAT WON LOOKS LIKE IN THIS COUNTRY, AND IT IS THE ONLY RESIDENTS' MOVEMENT THIS FILE HAS BEEN ABLE TO REACH HERE AFTER FOUR FAILED ATTEMPTS. Local residents along a river valley north of the country's third city organised against an eight-hundred-million-dollar hydropower cascade, and after months of protest the prime minister announced a SUSPENSION OF DAM CONSTRUCTION FOR NINE TO TWELVE MONTHS, a re-examination of environmental impact by foreign AND local experts, and a five-million-lari fund for the valley's development. WHAT MOVED PUBLIC OPINION WAS NOT THE ECOLOGY — IT WAS THE CONTRACT. Two facts became public and changed everything: that the state had transferred LAND TO THE COMPANY AT A SYMBOLIC PRICE, and that the CONFIDENTIAL AGREEMENT signed for the project contained onerous terms. This file has recorded elsewhere that following the money reaches places an environmental objection cannot; here is the clearest case in the payload. Ask what the land was sold for and what the agreement says before you argue about fish. THEIR CAMP EXISTED BECAUSE ONE OF THEM OWNED THE GROUND: the permanent protest camp at the construction area was pitched ON LAND BELONGING TO ONE OF THE ACTIVISTS. That is the practical precondition for a camp that cannot simply be cleared as trespass — and note that police removed it anyway, on the stated ground that the nearby river might flood it. THEIR DEMANDS WERE SPECIFIC AND WENT BEYOND THEIR OWN VALLEY: halt construction, ANNUL THE CONTRACT, impose a MORATORIUM ON ALL SUCH PROJECTS nationally, and open criminal proceedings over the approval. A demand list that names the contract and the sector is harder to buy off than one that names only the site. EXPECT WHAT THEY GOT: villages placed under police checkpoints, camps dismantled, and a campaign portraying them as enemies of energy independence, as backward, and as foreign agents — with an electricity price rise publicly blamed on them, and slander directed at a named leader. AND EXPECT ISOLATION: reporting records that the movement had only moderate support, or silence, from the capital's civil society organisations — which is the failure this file identified in Georgian campaigns generally. Two things broke that: a mass rally in the regional city rather than the capital, and support from a small number of named rights and environmental organisations recorded elsewhere in this file. TWO PIECES OF EVIDENCE THAT WORKED: an institute's computer simulation showing that a dam failure in an earthquake would send a thirty-four-metre wave into a city of that size — though the institute itself cautioned the modelling used incomplete data — and the fact that the SAME COMPANY'S EARLIER HYDROPOWER PLANT IN THIS COUNTRY COLLAPSED WITHIN TWO MONTHS of a four-hundred-million-euro investment. Check what the developer has already built and what happened to it. THE LIMITS: this is a movement, not a registered organisation, reachable through its public page; the project's later status is not established here; and a movement is a source of experience and solidarity rather than a service that will act for you.THE OUTCOME AND THE ARGUMENT THAT PRODUCED IT WERE NOT RECORDED HERE, AND THEY ARE THE PART WORTH COPYING. IN SEPTEMBER 2021 THE CONSTRUCTION FIRM ANNOUNCED IT WAS TERMINATING ITS CONTRACT FOR THE EIGHT HUNDRED MILLION DOLLAR PROJECT, CITING LONG-STANDING BREACHES OF CONTRACT AND FORCE MAJEURE - AND AN ENVIRONMENTAL GROUP OPPOSED TO THE SCHEME SAID THE GRASSROOTS MOVEMENT HAD PLAYED A DECISIVE ROLE IN THE CANCELLATION. WHAT DID THE REAL DAMAGE WAS NOT ENVIRONMENTAL BUT CONTRACTUAL: A JUSTICE MINISTRY DOCUMENT OBTAINED BY A LOCAL NEWS WEBSITE FOUND THAT THE VAST MAJORITY OF LIABILITIES FELL ON THE GOVERNMENT AND STATE-OWNED COMPANIES, WHILE THE COMPANY WAS MAXIMALLY PROTECTED BY THE SAME AGREEMENT. A DEAL THAT LOADS RISK ONTO THE PUBLIC PURSE OFFENDS PEOPLE WHO DO NOT CARE ABOUT A RIVER. THIS PAYLOAD RECORDS PROCUREMENT PORTALS, OWNERSHIP REGISTERS AND CONTRACT DISCLOSURE ROUTES IN MOST OF ITS COUNTRIES — THIS IS THE CASE THAT SHOWS WHY THEY MATTER MORE THAN ANOTHER SPECIES LIST. THE SCALE AND THE NAMING ARE WORTH ADDING TOO: THE SCHEME WOULD HAVE TAKEN FIFTEEN HUNDRED HECTARES AND FLOODED FIVE HUNDRED AND TWENTY WITH A RESERVOIR, IN A VALLEY WHOSE MICROCLIMATE SUSTAINS VINEYARDS AROUND ONE VILLAGE — AND A GUARDIAN OBSERVED THAT THE PROJECT'S NAME WAS INVENTED SO AS NOT TO MENTION THAT VILLAGE. IF THE PAPERWORK CALLS IT A CASCADE OR A CLUSTER, SAY THE VILLAGE. AND NOTE THE HONEST POSTSCRIPT FROM THE MOVEMENT'S OWN LEADER: BECAUSE THE CONTRACT WAS SO UNFAIR, THE STATE SUFFERED EVEN FROM CANCELLATION, SINCE THE COMPANY WON IN EVERY CASE — BUT HAD IT STAYED, THE LOSSES WOULD HAVE BEEN FAR GREATER.

trackers.name: ELAW — free scientific and legal backing for whichever lawyer takes your case
trackers.desc: IT DOES NOT TAKE YOUR CASE — IT ARMS THE LAWYER WHO DOES. A global alliance of attorneys and scientists supplying legal, scientific, SECURITY and organisational expertise to public interest lawyers, with more than three hundred advocates across over eighty countries and upwards of four hundred projects calling on it each year. ITS SCIENCE TEAM DOES EXACTLY WHAT THIS FILE HAS FOUND DECIDES CASES IN THIS COUNTRY: it CRITIQUES ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENTS, SUBMITS EXPERT TESTIMONY TO COURTS, helps advocates explain technical matters to communities, builds systems to MONITOR environmental conditions, and RECOMMENDS CLEANER ALTERNATIVES to proposed projects. This payload recorded that Georgian campaigns turn on who wrote the assessment and on whether a project was wrongly held outside assessment scope, and that a court sent such a question back for an expert report; an independent critique of an assessment is the document that argument needs. AND IT DOES THE ONE THING THIS FILE IDENTIFIED AS MISSING HERE AND COULD NOT SUPPLY: IT FACILITATES ENGAGEMENT BETWEEN LOCAL SCIENTISTS AND LOCAL LAWYERS. A university with the data and an advocate with the case rarely find each other unaided; this exists to introduce them. ITS LAW TEAM HELPS PARTNERS BRING ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS, critique proposed statutes and REPLICATE MODEL LAWS FROM OTHER COUNTRIES — which matters where a community is told no law covers its situation, and where this file has recorded that a body elsewhere responded by drafting the legal framework it lacked. It also works explicitly on DEFENDING DEFENDERS, improving the safety of advocates under attack, and publishes guidebooks for challenging particular kinds of project. HOW TO USE IT: it works through PARTNERS — public interest lawyers in their own countries — rather than directly with communities. Find or instruct a local advocate first, then ask them to approach the alliance for scientific and legal support; the support is provided at no cost to the partner and the alliance describes its model as high impact at low cost. THE LIMITS: it will not represent you, fund your litigation or lobby your government. It is a support network for lawyers, and its reach in this region was not established here — ask whether it has partners in this country before relying on it. DO NOT CONFUSE IT WITH THE SIMILARLY NAMED ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDER LAW CENTER recorded elsewhere in this file, which is a different organisation that finds pro bono lawyers.

trackers.name: ELKANA — a farmers' union of more than two thousand members that helped write the national biodiversity plan
trackers.desc: IT IS A UNION OF FARMERS AND ITS MEMBERSHIP IS OPEN TO ANY CITIZEN INTERESTED IN ORGANIC FARMING AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION — which means a rural household defending its land can join the body that already speaks for two thousand others. Founded in 1994, working with more than two thousand farmers across different regions, with a head office in the capital and TWO DEMONSTRATION AND CONSERVATION FARMS IN NAMED VILLAGES, one running since 1995 and one since 2004. This file failed four separate times to reach Georgia's community layer; this is a membership organisation rooted in it. ITS POLICY STANDING IS THE PART TO USE AGAINST A SCHEME: its experts were involved in drawing up THE AGRICULTURAL BIODIVERSITY COMPONENT OF THE COUNTRY'S FIRST AND SECOND NATIONAL BIODIVERSITY STRATEGY AND ACTION PLANS. A body that helped write the national plan is a body that can say authoritatively whether a project conflicts with it — and this file has recorded across the region that an objection framed against the state's own commitments travels further than one framed against a company. IT ALSO GIVES A COMMUNITY SOMETHING SPECIFIC TO PROTECT: it reintroduces INDIGENOUS WHEAT VARIETIES that were wiped out under the Soviet planned economy in the 1960s, putting them back into fields for local and commercial use, networked with mills, shops and restaurants. Land carrying rare local varieties is not interchangeable with land elsewhere, and a seed programme that documents which varieties grow where turns that from sentiment into a record. Its work also covers organic farming extension, training and advisory services, agro-ecological practice, and diversifying rural economic activity. ITS INTERNATIONAL MEMBERSHIPS MATTER MORE THAN THEY LOOK: it belongs to the European coordination of the global peasant movement, alongside seed and breed conservation, agricultural biodiversity and food sovereignty networks. The peasant movement in particular exists to defend land and seed rights, which gives a Georgian farming community a route to international solidarity that no other entry in this country's listing provides. THE LIMITS: it is an organic farming and rural development association, not an objector or a law practice — nothing found shows it opposing a mine, a dam or a road, and its subject is farming rather than planning. Use it for membership, for the varieties argument, for the national plan, and for the networks; take the objection to the litigators and the free lawyers recorded elsewhere in this file.

trackers.name: CASE — referral to lawyers, campaign help and emergency funding when a lawsuit is used to silence you
trackers.desc: WHEN A COMPANY OR AN OFFICIAL SUES A CAMPAIGNER TO SHUT THEM UP, THIS IS THE BODY THAT FINDS THEM HELP. It is a coalition of more than a hundred and twenty organisations across Europe and beyond, and it CONNECTS TARGETS OF ABUSIVE LAWSUITS TO THOSE WHO CAN ASSIST, drawing on a network of lawyers, NGOs and advocacy organisations for LEGAL EXPERTISE, CAMPAIGN ASSISTANCE AND EMERGENCY FUNDING where circumstances permit, plus published guidance on protecting yourself in advance. This file recorded that a residents' movement here faced a campaign portraying it as an enemy of energy independence and as foreign agents, with slander directed at a named leader, and that a national civil society platform issued a statement on a smear campaign against civil society experts. PREPARE FOR THE FORM THE ATTACK TAKES: its analysis finds such suits are COMMONLY BROUGHT AGAINST INDIVIDUALS rather than organisations, usually rely on DEFAMATION PROVISIONS, and claim a median of around fifteen thousand euros — an amount designed to ruin a person rather than an institution. Decide before a campaign starts who is named on statements and what support that person has. ITS DATABASE IS ALSO EVIDENCE IN ITSELF: more than thirteen hundred documented cases across dozens of countries, with the silenced subjects identified as corruption, government action, business practices and ENVIRONMENTAL CONCERNS. A court or a journalist shown that a claim fits a documented international pattern hears it differently from one shown a single aggrieved defendant. AND IF THE OTHER SIDE'S LAWYERS ARE THE WEAPON, IT PUBLISHES A LEGAL ETHICS REPORT ON HOW THE PROFESSION AND THE COURTS SHOULD PREVENT LAWYERS ENABLING SUCH ABUSE — the document to hand a bar association with a complaint. THE LIMITS: a coalition and a referral network rather than a law firm; it will not represent anyone; its emergency funding is conditional; and although this country sits within the wider European human rights system, the European Union's anti-SLAPP directive does not apply here. Pair it with the free legal centres and the rights litigator recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Aarhus Centre Georgia — it monitors public participation in impact assessments, and counsels citizens on the law
trackers.desc: IT DOES THE TWO THINGS THIS COUNTRY'S DISPUTES KEEP TURNING ON. It MONITORS PUBLIC PARTICIPATION DURING THE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT PROCESS, and it PROVIDES LEGAL COUNSELLING TO CITIZENS ON ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS — alongside facilitating access to environmental information and training people on the convention that underpins all three. This file has recorded here a valley movement that forced a construction moratorium and a development fund, a scheme declared to fall OUTSIDE ASSESSMENT SCOPE until a court overturned that determination, and campaigns that turned on who wrote the assessment. EVERY ONE OF THOSE IS A QUESTION ABOUT WHETHER THE PUBLIC WAS PROPERLY LET INTO THE ASSESSMENT — AND THIS IS AN INSTITUTION WHOSE PUBLISHED JOB IS TO WATCH EXACTLY THAT. If a hearing was not advertised, if comments were taken after a decision, if a scoping stage was skipped, that is the body to tell. THE LEGAL COUNSELLING MATTERS BECAUSE IT IS FREE AND EARLY. This map records litigators and free legal centres for this country, but a community usually needs an answer before it needs a lawyer — what the procedure requires, when the window opens, what documents must be published. KNOW THE NAME CHANGE OR YOU WILL THINK IT HAS CLOSED: established in 2005, it has SINCE 2013 BEEN TRANSFORMED INTO AN ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION AND EDUCATION CENTRE, which provides access to environmental education and to comprehensive information on the environment. Search both names. THE NETWORK BEHIND IT IS LARGE AND ITS REACH INTO THE COURTS IS REAL: sixty such centres operate across fourteen countries, and judges and representatives of national judicial training centres from this country and its neighbours have been trained specifically on the ACCESS TO JUSTICE pillar of the convention, alongside the chair of that convention's own task force on the subject. A judge who has been trained on those procedural requirements is a different audience for an argument about participation than one who has not. THE LIMITS: it is supported by an intergovernmental organisation and has been folded into a government-facing information and education function — IT IS NOT AN INDEPENDENT ADVOCATE, and it will not represent you or oppose a project. Counselling is advice, not representation. Use it to establish what the process owes you and to have a failure of participation recorded by an institution; take the case itself to the litigators, the free legal centres and the rights organisations recorded separately here.

trackers.name: Public Defender — it can file an amicus brief in your case, in the ordinary courts
trackers.desc: IT IS AUTHORISED TO EXERCISE THE AMICUS CURIAE FUNCTION AT THE COMMON COURTS AS WELL AS THE CONSTITUTIONAL COURT. THE COMMON COURTS ARE WHERE A LAND DISPUTE ACTUALLY SITS — which makes this the most directly usable court power found anywhere in this file's survey of complaints institutions. A community already in litigation over a permit, a valuation or an assessment can ask the Public Defender to submit a legal opinion in that case. An opinion from the constitutional watchdog, filed in your proceedings, is a weight no community can generate for itself. IT ALSO ANALYSES THE STATE'S LAWS, POLICIES AND PRACTICES AGAINST INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS AND ISSUES RECOMMENDATIONS. This file has recorded here a scheme declared outside assessment scope until a court overturned that determination, and a payload-wide finding that strategic environmental assessment is missing; a permitting regime, not only a permit, can be put to this office. ITS INDEPENDENCE IS PROTECTED BY STATUTE RATHER THAN BY CUSTOM: it exercises its functions independently, bound only by the Constitution, international treaties and law — and ANY INFLUENCE OR INTERFERENCE WITH ITS ACTIVITIES IS PROHIBITED AND PUNISHED BY LAW. Its powers sit in an organic law of 1996, and it also serves as the national preventive mechanism under the torture convention's optional protocol and as the body for the disability convention. THE LIMITS: an amicus brief is an OPINION, NOT REPRESENTATION — it does not become your lawyer, and this file records litigating organisations and free legal centres for this country that do. It advises and recommends; it does not decide. And it is a state office, so what you send it is disclosed to a public institution. Use it to add weight to a case already running, to have a permitting practice measured against international standards, and alongside the impact-assessment participation monitoring recorded separately here.THREE FURTHER POWERS AND PUBLICATIONS OF THIS OFFICE WERE NOT RECORDED HERE, AND THE FIRST CHANGES WHO CAN SAFELY USE IT. IT CAN STUDY A DECISION ON ITS OWN INITIATIVE — IT HAS DONE SO WITH A DECISION OF THE NATIONAL PUBLIC REGISTRY AGENCY — WHICH MEANS A MATTER CAN BE EXAMINED WITHOUT AN INDIVIDUAL PUTTING THEIR NAME TO A COMPLAINT. THAT IS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A ROUTE A FRIGHTENED HOUSEHOLD CAN USE AND ONE IT CANNOT. WHERE NAMING PEOPLE WOULD EXPOSE THEM, ASK THE OFFICE TO OPEN THE MATTER ITSELF — THAT IS A DIFFERENT REQUEST FROM FILING A COMPLAINT, AND IT SHOULD BE MADE EXPLICITLY. SECOND, IT PUBLISHES EVERY RECOMMENDATION IT ISSUES IN A DATED, SEARCHABLE SERIES WITH THE CASE BEHIND EACH ONE DESCRIBED — INCLUDING RECOMMENDATIONS ADDRESSED TO A CITY MUNICIPALITY'S ADMINISTRATION. SO LOCAL GOVERNMENT IS INSIDE ITS REACH, WHICH MATTERS BECAUSE MUNICIPALITIES ZONE, LEASE AND PERMIT. THAT PUBLISHED SERIES IS TWO TOOLS AT ONCE: IT SHOWS WHICH SUBJECTS THE OFFICE ACTUALLY TAKES UP, SO A MATTER CAN BE FRAMED IN A CATEGORY THAT HAS SUCCEEDED BEFORE, AND IT SUPPLIES A PRECEDENT TO CITE — WHICH MOVES OFFICIALS MORE RELIABLY THAN ARGUMENT. THIRD, IT PUBLISHES ANNUAL ACTIVITY REPORTS COVERING INDIVIDUAL CASEWORK, MONITORING AND PUBLIC EDUCATION, AND ITS OWN INTERNAL RULE ON ISSUING AND PROACTIVELY PUBLISHING PUBLIC INFORMATION. AN INSTITUTION WITH A WRITTEN PUBLIC-INFORMATION PROCEDURE CAN BE ASKED FOR DOCUMENTS UNDER ITS OWN STATED RULES. ITS STAFF ALSO RUN INFORMATION EVENTS IN THE REGIONS RATHER THAN ONLY IN THE CAPITAL — THE PRACTICAL WAY A VILLAGE GROUP MEETS SOMEBODY FROM THE OFFICE WITHOUT TRAVELLING. ONE HONEST CAVEAT ON SCOPE: THE PAGES SEARCHED SHOWED LABOUR, DISCRIMINATION AND CHILDREN'S RIGHTS WORK RATHER THAN LAND OR ENVIRONMENT, AND NO DEDICATED ENVIRONMENTAL UNIT WAS IDENTIFIED. CHECK THE RECOMMENDATIONS SERIES FOR COMPARABLE CASES BEFORE RELYING ON THIS ROUTE.

trackers.name: The cadastral map — see every registered plot, and who is buying around you
trackers.desc: AN OFFICIAL INTERACTIVE CADASTRAL MAP, WITH AN ENGLISH INTERFACE. It shows the geographic data uploaded to the public registry and lets you VIEW LAND PLOTS BY CADASTRAL CODE. Every parcel in this country carries a unique cadastral code in a fixed four-part format; it appears on the title deed, and it can also be found by looking up an address on the registry portal. USE IT TO CHECK THE PARCELS AROUND YOURS, NOT ONLY YOUR OWN. Schemes are assembled quietly, plot by plot, and a single buyer accumulating neighbouring parcels is the earliest warning a community gets — this file has recorded here a site sold at a symbolic price and agreements kept confidential, both of which show first in who owns what. AND THE REGISTRY IS NOT ONLY IN THE CAPITAL: it delivers its services through PUBLIC SERVICE HALLS, COMMUNITY CENTRES AND TERRITORIAL OFFICES as well as authorised users — so there is a physical counter to walk into outside the city, which matters when a lookup needs to become a certified extract. THE LIMITS: the map shows what has been REGISTERED, so unregistered, customary or disputed holdings may not appear as their occupants would describe them; and viewing a plot on a map is not the same as obtaining an extract naming its owner, which is a separate service and may carry a fee. NOTE THE RELATIONSHIP: the agency that maintains this map is ALREADY IN THE LIVE MAP as a separate entry. This is its cadastral map service rather than the agency itself — a different address doing a different job, and both are worth holding.

trackers.name: Small Grants Programme — a country strategy written jointly with civil society
trackers.desc: THE FEATURE WORTH ACTING ON IS HOW ITS STRATEGY IS MADE: THE COUNTRY PROGRAMME STRATEGY IS DESIGNED JOINTLY BY DONORS, GOVERNMENT, CIVIL SOCIETY AND ACADEMIA. That means the document deciding which landscapes and which themes get funded in this country is not handed down — civil society sits in its drafting. A community organisation that wants its valley, forest or wetland to be a funding priority should be asking who represents civil society in that process and when the strategy is next revised. THIS PAYLOAD HAS RECORDED MANY FUNDERS AND HAS NEVER BEFORE FOUND ONE WHOSE PRIORITIES A COMMUNITY CAN HELP WRITE. THE PROGRAMME WAS LAUNCHED HERE IN 2012 and is tailored to the specific needs of the country. It covers biodiversity conservation, climate change, INTERNATIONAL WATERS, LAND DEGRADATION, and chemicals and wastes, and alongside environmental benefits it is directed at poverty reduction, livelihood improvement, GENDER EQUALITY AND WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT. AND THE MONEY GOES STRAIGHT TO THE COMMUNITY'S OWN ORGANISATION. Grants are made directly to community-based organisations and non-governmental organisations rather than through an intermediary, which distinguishes this from almost every other funder in this file. WHAT TO DO FIRST: obtain the country programme strategy, read which landscapes it names, and establish whether your ground lies inside one — strategies commonly commit most of the funding to a few priority areas. Then find the national coordinator, and ask when the strategy will next be reviewed. THE LIMITS: the applicant must be a constituted organisation; co-financing of roughly half is normally expected THOUGH IT MAY BE IN KIND, meaning volunteer labour, land use and materials can be counted; and proposals must be framed as environmental work rather than as opposition to a particular scheme. Decisions are made by a national steering committee. Use it with the land acquisition fund and the cadastral map recorded separately for this country: the strategy sets the priorities, the fund can buy or lease, and the map shows what is where.

trackers.name: Registering land you already occupy — the free window closed, and what replaced it
trackers.desc: IF YOUR FAMILY USES LAND IT HAS NEVER REGISTERED, THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING — AND THE EASY VERSION OF IT HAS JUST ENDED. Under the systemic registration reform, in areas fixed by ministerial order, THE AGENCY MEASURED PLOTS ON ITS OWN INITIATIVE, SEARCHED OUT THE DOCUMENTATION AND REGISTERED OWNERSHIP, across 59 MUNICIPALITIES — the whole country apart from the self-governing cities. THE PROGRAMME ENDED ON 1 JANUARY 2026. THE SUCCESSOR ROUTE IS NAMED AND MOST PEOPLE WILL NOT KNOW IT: THOSE WHO FOR OBJECTIVE REASONS COULD NOT USE THE REFORM BETWEEN 2022 AND 2025 MAY, FROM 1 JANUARY 2026, APPLY TO THE PUBLIC REGISTRY UNDER THE SPORADIC PROCEDURE. The door did not close; it changed shape and price. WHAT CHANGED, PRECISELY. REGISTERING A SELF-OCCUPIED PLOT IS NO LONGER FREE. The service and registration fee for the sporadic route — reported at six hundred lari — is to be reset by government decision, so CHECK THE CURRENT FIGURE BEFORE BUDGETING. AND THE MUNICIPAL LAND-RECOGNITION COMMISSIONS HAVE HAD THEIR POWERS SUSPENDED FOR A YEAR, which removes the local body that used to recognise possession. WHAT THE FREE PERIOD ACTUALLY COVERED IS WORTH KNOWING, BECAUSE IT SHOWS WHAT THESE STEPS NORMALLY COST: document search and systematisation, certification of the parties' signatures on a transaction, NOTARIAL MEDIATION, recognition of the ownership right, and constatation of facts were performed without charge, and registration itself carried no agency service fee. Under the paid route each of those is a cost line. TWO WARNINGS THAT DECIDE WHETHER AN APPLICATION SUCCEEDS. FIRST, AFTER YOU APPLY THE REGISTRY ALLOWS TEN DAYS FOR BOUNDARIES TO BE CLARIFIED — and where documents do not prove where the plot is and a municipal representative's testimony is not accepted, THE APPLICANT MUST GO TO THE NATIONAL BUREAU OF ENFORCEMENT TO HAVE THE FACTS ESTABLISHED.
