When our partners are targeted, we act quickly to help defend and protect them.’ That last one is a named function, not an aspiration, and ELAW co-founded the Alliance for Land, Indigenous and Environmental Defenders. HOW TO USE IT — THROUGH A LAWYER, NOT AS A CLIENT: ELAW works through more than 300 public interest advocates in its network, and its stated strategy is ‘locating strong lawyers who are committed to protecting the environment in their home countries’. You can approach ELAW directly, but the leverage is greatest when a local advocate is the conduit — that is how the network is built. It has hosted nearly 300 advocates from more than 65 countries as Fellows and provided support on thousands of cases; several partners have won the Goldman Environmental Prize. Focus areas include biodiversity, fossil fuels — expressly assisting advocates in contesting fossil fuel development projects — plastic pollution, and work with coastal communities. It publishes guidebooks, including one to give communities sufficient understanding to challenge oil and gas projects, and clause-level summaries of national EIA law — so its site is also a route to learning exactly what your own EIA law requires. ASK WHETHER ELAW HAS A PARTNER IN YOUR COUNTRY: the network is described as spanning 70 to 80 countries but the member list is not published country by country, so this entry does not assert a presence in yours.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: EcoContact and its Aarhus Centre — free environmental legal help (Moldova)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Moldovan association operating since 2001 and registered in 2010, successor in the country to Milieukontakt International. Since 2013 it has hosted the Aarhus Environmental Information and Consultancy Centre, set up with the support of the OSCE Mission in Moldova, which gives the local population information and legal expertise on environmental matters free of charge. Contact through ecocontact.md. WHY IT REACHES FURTHER THAN MOST: it moderates a standing platform of more than 230 environmental organisations and experts, exchanging information and expertise between them. For a village in a country this size, one call can reach the person who has already handled your problem elsewhere — ask it who else has fought this, not only what the law says. IT COMES TO THE VILLAGES: under its green-justice programme its platform secretariats visited 182 of the 187 localities in the target districts during 2024 to give free legal assistance on environmental protection and access to justice, and to help draft and monitor local environmental regulations. Its own account is that these visits also produced model local acts on matters such as grazing and mowing, recording infringements, and transparency in decision-making. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer, and its work sits close to government and donor programmes — it drafts national legislation and trains judges and prosecutors as well as advising residents. Useful reach; ask early whether your specific fight falls inside a current programme, because that is what determines whether anyone can travel to you.

trackers.name: Fundația Est-Europeană — Moldova's main grant-maker, and its rules (Moldova)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: registered 3 November 2009 as successor to the Eurasia Foundation in Moldova, which had worked in the country since 1994. Offices at Str. 31 August 1989 nr. 98, floor 3, Chișinău MD-2004, +373 22 235343, info@eef.md. Its mission is equipping Moldovan citizens with the capacity and means for sustainable development, through education, technical assistance and grant programmes. It has run the Cetățeni activi, comunități prospere programme — active citizens, prosperous communities — across successive phases with Swedish funding, and publishes a record of grants awarded since 2010. Moldova had no funder in this file. READ THESE TWO RULES BEFORE YOU PLAN ANYTHING AROUND IT. Only non-governmental organisations legally registered in the Republic of Moldova are eligible — unlike the Serbian, Montenegrin, Kosovar and Belgian funders elsewhere in this file, an informal village group cannot apply and must register first or find a registered partner. And most of its grants are made either by invitation or through competitions, with all proposals initiated by the Foundation itself — you cannot submit an unsolicited application and expect it to be read. Watch for the calls; do not write in cold. WHAT IT FUNDS: its programmes have covered social enterprise creation and development by local civil society organisations, employment for young people outside education and work, access to social, legal and medical services for disadvantaged groups in partnership with local authorities, and civic monitoring of business, government and donors. It is a democracy and development funder, not an environmental one — frame accordingly, as the community funders in Bosnia, Serbia and Montenegro also require. USE IT WITH THE OTHER TWO: Moldova's existing allies are the Aarhus centre that gives free environmental legal expertise and visits villages, and the Dniester river-keepers association. This is the money.

trackers.name: Institutul de Ecologie și Geografie — keeps the cadastre, and revalidated every protected area
trackers.desc: WHO HOLDS THE RECORD: by Government Decision no. 414 of 2 May 2000, the Institute of Ecology and Geography is designated to create and maintain the Data Bank of the Cadastre of objects and complexes of the state protected areas fund. Moldova had one conservation-side ally in twenty entries; this is the body that holds the official record of what is protected and where its boundaries run. WHAT IT HAS ALREADY DONE FOR EVERY SITE IN THE COUNTRY: with the Botanical Garden and the Institutes of Zoology, Ecology and Geography, and Geology and Seismology, researchers carried out the revalidation of Moldova's protected areas system in 2010–2014, work that established floristic and faunistic composition, valuable elements and details, clarified the boundaries of the protected areas, produced the necessary maps and accumulated a database. The published collection covers forest reserves, meadows and landscape architecture monuments. If your ground is in or beside a protected area, its boundary has been checked and mapped in the last fifteen years. AND THE REVALIDATION MADE CONCRETE PROPOSALS FOR EXPANSION: it proposed annexing the Suta de Movile landscape reserve to Pădurea Domnească, adding 67 hectares to Plaiul Fagului that had been taken during privatisation, and recorded 64 hectares annexed to Prutul de Jos by decision of Moldsilva. Consolidation and extension of existing reserves is an established, documented route — and easier to argue than a new designation. THE STATUTORY DUTY THAT A COMMUNITY CAN INVOKE: under Law 1538 of 25 February 1998, the Government requires holders of publicly owned land to submit, obligatorily, proposals for taking representative natural areas under state protection, and central and local authorities and land holders must supply data for ecological monitoring to the central environmental authority free of charge. Withdrawal of land from the protected areas fund is strictly prohibited except where it loses value through natural calamity and cannot be restored. THE NUMBER TO ARGUE WITH: the national environment strategy targeted expansion of protected areas to 8 per cent of the country; the Emerald Network already identifies 52 sites covering 269,871 hectares — 8.0 per cent — but establishing protected-area status for those sites requires legislative change. A community whose site is an Emerald site is inside a queue the state has already committed to.

trackers.name: BIOTICA — builds a volunteer nature-guardian network where the state structure is missing
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: Asociația Obștească Societatea Ecologică BIOTICA, which has implemented more than 60 projects with funding from the Austrian Development Agency, the GEF Small Grants Programme, the Czech foreign ministry's Transition programme, the National Ecological Fund, UNDP Moldova, the US Embassy, the Ramsar Convention small grants fund, the World Bank, the Michael Otto Stiftung and the Government of Norway. Its named target groups include the local population, central and local public authorities, educational institutions and public associations. Moldova had a river-keepers network, an Aarhus centre, a funder and a cadastre institute — and nothing doing fieldwork with communities. THE PROJECT THAT DEFINES IT: strengthening the right to a healthy environment for communities on both banks of the Dniester, it says it will create a network of citizen guardians of nature from volunteers in the rural communities around the Tipova and Iagorlic natural areas and in the Lower Dniester — creating an alternative to the missing state structure. It will run workshops and training, help the volunteers obtain state registration, and publish a manual for volunteers summarising all the competences in a clear structure. An organisation that helps village volunteers register as a legal body, then trains them and writes their handbook, is the most complete community-capacity offer in this file — and it names the reason plainly: the state structure is not there. IT ALSO WORKS WITH THE MAYORS: it will help three localities implement landscape improvement measures and then organise field trips so that mayors and activists can visit them, and plant green belts along rivers with volunteers. WHAT IT DOES ON THE GROUND: afforestation of over 23 hectares in the Lower Dniester region, installing feeders for deer and nest boxes in protected areas, land restoration by planting, and construction of infrastructure elements for the protection of biological resources.

trackers.name: Fondul Ecologic Național — state money that pays for protected-area project documents
trackers.desc: WHY THIS CLOSES A GAP THE DESIGNATION PATTERN OPENED: across eleven countries the binding constraint on protecting a site has been who pays for the expert study. Moldova's National Ecological Fund lists, among the purposes it finances, the elaboration of projects for protected areas of natural and built heritage of national and international importance, and scientific investigations in the field of environmental protection carried out at the order of the environment ministry, with co-financed participation in research and development work. WHAT ELSE IT PAYS FOR, from the same list: organising and managing the system of ecological information and publicity and propagating ecological knowledge; organising international cooperation in environmental protection, including by engaging foreign specialists to give consultative and expert assistance; paying for representatives of the country to take part in the international environmental conventions Moldova is party to, and paying the contributions; and awards to specialists regardless of departmental affiliation, up to 1 per cent of the fund's income. SO THREE THINGS A MOLDOVAN COMMUNITY MIGHT ACTUALLY NEED ARE INSIDE THE FUND'S OWN REMIT: the protected-area project document, a foreign expert's opinion, and the cost of getting a Moldovan voice to the convention meeting. AND IT IS ALREADY FUNDING THE SECTOR: the National Ecological Fund is named among the donors of BIOTICA — filed here last round — alongside the Austrian Development Agency, GEF Small Grants, UNDP Moldova and the Ramsar small grants fund. So an established Moldovan NGO has already been through this fund's process and can say how it works. PRACTICAL NOTE: the fund sits under the agriculture and food industry ministry's environment component; Moldova's environment ministry is at 162 Stephen the Great Boulevard, Chișinău, mediu.gov.md, and there is a separate public institution, the National Office for the Implementation of Projects in the Field of the Environment, with its own supervisory committee.

trackers.name: Moldova's fondul ariilor protejate register — every protected area, its hectares and its LANDHOLDER
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the state ecological inspectorate publishes the schedules of Law 1538/1998 on the fondul ariilor naturale protejate de stat — each protected area listed with its name, its area in hectares, its raion and village, AND ITS DEȚINĂTORI DE TERENURI, the holders of the land. The scientific reserves alone run to 19,378 hectares across five named sites. A public register that names who holds the land under each protected area is exactly what a community needs before asking anyone to act, and it is the answer to Moldova's missing landholder: for the state reserves the holder is the central environmental authority. THE OWNERSHIP RULE, WHICH DECIDES WHAT IS POSSIBLE: under the law, objects and complexes of the protected areas fund are PUBLIC PROPERTY, with an exception for specified land. Conservation in Moldova generally runs through public title, not private purchase — which is why no land trust was found, and why the register matters more than a buyer would. WHAT THE LAW EXPRESSLY GIVES CITIZENS AND NGOs: it sets out the attributions of central and local public authorities, OF NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS AND OF CITIZENS in creating and operating the fund, and among its stated purposes is holding natural and legal persons liable where they have caused damage to protected natural areas and observing the international conventions — biological diversity, Bern, Bonn. AND THE CATEGORIES YOU CAN ASK FOR: scientific reserve, national park, monument of nature, natural reserve, landscape reserve, resources reserve, multifunctional management area and biosphere reserve — of international, national or LOCAL importance.

trackers.name: Mișcarea Ecologistă din Moldova — ten regional organisations and 15 affiliates
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a national, non-governmental, non-profit organisation formed in November 1990 — the first non-governmental organisation of the new democratic type in Moldova — with ten regional organisations and 15 affiliated organisations, headquartered at 13 S. Lazo St., Chișinău, and a member of the International Union for Conservation of Nature. Moldova's bucket held Eco-TIRAS and BIOTICA; this is the third national body and the one with the widest regional spread. Ten regional organisations is a map of where a Moldovan community can find a local affiliate, and this file has found across eighteen countries that the branch list is the most useful free artefact. WHAT IT WORKS ON: restoration of natural balance, conservation and care of natural and cultural heritage, ecological education, information and training, ACCESS TO ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION AND PUBLIC PARTICIPATION. Its named current projects include 'Responsible community — conserved terrestrial landscape' and work with young people to promote a named reserve, and past projects include 'Monitoring for good environmental governance'. AND IT PUBLISHES: the ecology, tourism and culture magazine NATURA, whose founder has produced numerous albums dedicated to the natural monuments of Moldova — useful where a community needs its site documented and named. A related environmental journalists' association runs the news platform ecopresa.md.

trackers.name: Hai Moldova — 350,000 volunteers, and it plants where the forest cover is lowest in Europe
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: an environmental NGO formed as a civic initiative in 2011, which has run dozens of projects and four national awareness and ecological education campaigns, involving more than 350,000 volunteers. THE NUMBER THAT MAKES THE CASE IN MOLDOVA: Moldova has the lowest degree of forest cover of any European country — only 11 per cent of the territory is covered by forest, and the organisation's position is that afforestation is the surest solution for restoring ecological balance. WHAT IT RUNS THAT A COMMUNITY CAN JOIN: Million Trees Moldova, which sets out to involve the community broadly in the planting, growing AND PROTECTING of trees across the whole country. An organisation that mobilises volunteers at that scale is the one to call when a site needs hands rather than lawyers — and planting is one of the few conservation acts that establishes a visible, defensible use of ground. AND A NEIGHBOURING MODEL WORTH KNOWING: a Moldovan nursery project specialising in rare species with higher economic potential, able to grow over five thousand species from seed, created Pădurea Corporativă (Forest-as-a-Service), through which any organisation can grow its own forest, planting the saplings with its employees.

trackers.name: Moldova's Codul funciar 22/2024 — who may be given public land, and the council's power over derelict fields
trackers.desc: WHY THIS IS THE ACQUIRER ANSWER FOR MOLDOVA: the file recorded in batch 312 that protected-area objects are public property. The land code sets out who exercises that ownership and how ground can be given out: the State's right of ownership over land is exercised by the Government through the central public administration, and THAT OF THE ADMINISTRATIVE-TERRITORIAL UNIT BY THE DELIBERATIVE AUTHORITY OF THE LOCAL PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION — that is, the elected council. THE LIMIT THAT PROTECTS PUBLIC GROUND, worth knowing before anyone proposes a transfer: goods of the public domain may be used only according to their destination AND MAY NOT BE TRANSMITTED IN COMODAT TO NATURAL PERSONS OR TO LEGAL PERSONS WITH PRIVATE CAPITAL; and transmitting land of the water fund from the public domain of the State or of an administrative-territorial unit into the administration of private-law subjects IS FORBIDDEN. Water-fund land cannot be handed to a private body at all. AND THE POWER A COUNCIL HAS OVER NEGLECTED LAND, which cuts the other way: under article 36, where agricultural land is left derelict long-term and affects the surrounding land, local authorities may transmit it IN ARENDA — the ministry stressing that the owner is NOT dispossessed, remains the legal owner, and the lease is a temporary measure meant to prevent the degradation of the land and to protect the neighbours. A council can put a neglected field into productive hands without taking it, under a government regulation setting the procedure, with a commission negotiating the terms directly with the owner and minuting the result.

trackers.name: Law 1538/1998 — it gives NGOs and citizens named powers over Moldova's protected areas
trackers.desc: WHAT THE FOUNDING STATUTE ACTUALLY SAYS, and it is the sentence a Moldovan community should quote: the law establishes the legal bases for creating and running the state protected areas fund, its principles and the manner of its conservation, AS WELL AS THE ATTRIBUTIONS OF CENTRAL AND LOCAL PUBLIC AUTHORITIES, OF NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS AND OF CITIZENS IN THIS FIELD. Non-governmental organisations and citizens are named in the founding article alongside the authorities — not as consultees but as holders of attributions, and the batch 312 entry recorded that the same law's purposes include holding natural and legal persons liable where they have caused damage to protected natural areas. AND THE DEFINITIONS THAT DECIDE WHICH CATEGORY FITS YOUR GROUND: a protected natural area is a geographically delimited natural space WITH REPRESENTATIVE AND RARE NATURAL ELEMENTS, designated and regulated for the conservation and protection of ALL environmental factors within its limits; and an area with multifunctional management covers terrestrial and other space where use continues alongside conservation. Representative and rare are the two tests — a site does not have to be unique, only representative of something worth keeping.

trackers.name: Civic.md — the Moldovan civil society portal: organisations, grants, jobs and volunteers
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the principal portal of civil society in the Republic of Moldova, offering news, announcements, JOBS, GRANTS, VOLUNTEERING and resources for NGOs, with organisations browsable by field. Moldova's bucket held the state fund, the regional network and the volunteer planters — this is the single place a Moldovan group finds funders, staff and volunteers at once. Where a country has one civil society portal, it is the cheapest research a new group can do — this file has recorded the same shape in Slovenia's CNVOS and Croatia's Zeleni forum. AND THE STRUCTURAL FACT THAT DECIDES WHAT YOUR GROUP CAN BE, recorded from a Moldovan justice sector portal: the law on non-commercial organisations gathers THREE LEGAL FORMS under one umbrella — the ASOCIAȚIE OBȘTEASCĂ, the FUNDAȚIE and the INSTITUȚIE PRIVATĂ — and it simplified the registration procedure. AND THE ARGUMENT A MOLDOVAN GROUP CAN PUT TO ITS OWN MAYOR, from the same source: a public association can help the local public administration to write an infrastructure project, because the local administration does not have project-writing competences but the association does — AND THE ASSOCIATION IS ELIGIBLE FOR PROJECTS THE LOCAL ADMINISTRATION IS NOT, AND VICE VERSA. The plea is that councils should not see local organisations as a competitor but as an ally.

trackers.name: Lista ONG-uri de mediu — the Moldovan environmental NGO list, with street addresses and mobiles
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a published list of environmental NGOs in the Republic of Moldova, each with A STREET ADDRESS, A TELEPHONE OR MOBILE NUMBER AND AN EMAIL — not a portal, a contact sheet. Moldova had 29 filed entries and one land-holding body. A village committee with no lawyer and no funder can work down a list like this in an evening, and the entries are not all capital-city bodies: the second name on it is an association based IN A NAMED VILLAGE, reachable only by mobile phone. WHO IS ON IT: alongside the national organisations it lists a youth and environment association, a youth association for tourism and ecological education, a parents' and teachers' association from a named village, and an organisation called PARKS OF THE FUTURE — with addresses across the country rather than one city. The rural entries matter most, because this file has repeatedly found that a community facing a scheme needs someone within driving distance, not a head office. The list is published as an open PDF and needs no login.

trackers.name: GEF SGP Moldova — grants to 150,000 DOLLARS for local environmental projects, since 2012
trackers.desc: WHAT IT FUNDS AND HOW MUCH: grants of up to 150,000 DOLLARS for environmental and climate projects, offered by the Small Grants Programme of the Global Environment Facility TO CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS. Organisations may apply for STANDARD GRANTS OF UP TO 75,000 DOLLARS or STRATEGIC GRANTS OF UP TO 150,000 DOLLARS, with implementation up to 18 MONTHS and a total call value of 900,000 DOLLARS. Moldova had three funding entries filed, all national. AND THE TWO CONDITIONS THAT SHAPE AN APPLICATION: projects must be carried out IN PARTNERSHIP WITH ACTORS FROM THE AREA OF IMPLEMENTATION, and must ensure CO-FINANCING OF AT LEAST 50 PER CENT of the total cost. Half the money must come from somewhere else, and a local partner is compulsory — so this is a fund for a coalition, not for a single group, and co-financing can include the in-kind contribution a community is best placed to supply. AND WHAT THE PROGRAMME IS FOR: launched globally in 1992 and in Moldova IN 2012, it FINANCES LOCAL COMMUNITY INITIATIVES to address global environmental challenges, designed to generate innovative and impactful LOCAL ACTION by strengthening the capacities of civil society organisations AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, with priority areas including BIODIVERSITY, SUSTAINABLE LAND AND FOREST MANAGEMENT, chemicals and waste, AND SOCIAL INCLUSION. It supports projects ON BOTH BANKS OF THE DNIESTER.

trackers.name: The World Bank land governance review — only 12% of Moldova's state land is REGISTERED
trackers.desc: THE FINDING THAT CHANGES WHAT A MOLDOVAN COMMUNITY SHOULD CHECK FIRST: only 12% OF STATE PUBLIC LAND AND 15% OF PUBLIC LAND HELD BY LOCAL AUTHORITIES IS REGISTERED IN THE CADASTRE, and an even smaller percentage of it is DEMARCATED ON THE GROUND. Moldova had one land acquisition entry filed. If the state cannot show a registered, demarcated title, a project on that ground is standing on an unproven claim — and the review says this CAUSES CONFLICTS between the state and local authorities, AND WITH THE POPULATION WHO USE THESE LANDS or the areas adjacent to them. AND THE COMMUNITY PRACTICE IT RECORDS, which is a foothold rather than a grievance: the rural population uses public lands for GRAZING, AGRICULTURE OR FORESTRY, and COMMUNITIES WHICH USE THE FORESTS AND HAVE A CLOSE CONNECTION TO THEM MANAGE THEM INDEPENDENTLY, although most forests belong to the state forestry authority. Long-standing independent community management of a forest is a claim worth documenting before anyone else asserts one. AND THE WEAKNESS IN THE STATE SIDE: the institutional arrangement is WEAK IN PRACTICE — there is a LACK OF CLARITY IN REVENUE-SHARING AGREEMENTS and NO SEPARATION BETWEEN MANAGEMENT AND REGULATION, with practically NO DIALOGUE between investors and local authorities and communities regarding investments in forest management.

trackers.name: Agenția de Mediu's protected-areas page — the TEN categories, and the law that lists every site
trackers.desc: WHAT THE STATE PROTECTED-AREA FUND CONTAINS, and it is the menu a Moldovan community chooses from: categories following the IUCN classification — SCIENTIFIC RESERVE, NATIONAL PARK, NATURE MONUMENT, NATURE RESERVE, LANDSCAPE RESERVE, RESOURCE RESERVE, and AREA WITH MULTIFUNCTIONAL MANAGEMENT — plus categories outside that classification (DENDROLOGICAL GARDEN, MONUMENT OF LANDSCAPE ARCHITECTURE, ZOOLOGICAL GARDEN) and those set by international instruments (BIOSPHERE RESERVE under a UNESCO programme, and WETLAND OF INTERNATIONAL IMPORTANCE under the Ramsar Convention). Moldova had two land-acquisition entries filed. Ten categories mean a site that fails one test may still qualify under another — a landscape reserve and a nature monument ask for very different things. AND WHERE THE SITES ARE LISTED: the source for all of it is a NAMED AND NUMBERED 1998 LAW ON THE FUND OF STATE-PROTECTED NATURAL AREAS, and the agency publishes the share of each category in the total protected area and the EVOLUTION OVER TIME of the fund's surface FROM 1971 TO THE PRESENT. A single statute that lists every protected site by name is a document to check your own ground against before assuming it has no status.

trackers.name: The 2% designation list — every Moldovan association a taxpayer can send money to, by name and address
trackers.desc: WHAT THIS DOCUMENT IS: the ministry's published LIST OF BENEFICIARIES OF THE PERCENTAGE DESIGNATION — every civic association a Moldovan taxpayer may direct a share of their income tax to — given with, for each one, its STATE IDENTIFICATION NUMBER, ITS FULL REGISTERED NAME, AND ITS STREET ADDRESS down to the village or district. Moldova had two land-acquisition entries filed. A tax-designation route means a supporter funds a local group without giving any money of their own — the same mechanism recorded for Lithuania in batch501, and here the eligible list is published in full. AND WHAT IT GIVES A COMMUNITY BESIDES THE MONEY: the list runs to hundreds of entries including an ECOLOGIST MOVEMENT of Moldova, a REGIONAL CENTRE FOR COMMUNITY POLICIES, and named associations registered IN VILLAGES AND SMALL DISTRICTS, not only the capital. A state-verified directory of registered associations, with addresses, is how a village finds the nearest body already entitled to receive designated tax — and how it checks its own standing if it registers one.

trackers.name: A citizens' referral guide — including a chapter of ASSOCIATIONS THAT GIVE LEGAL AID
trackers.desc: A PUBLISHED GUIDE FOR REFERRING CITIZENS TO THE COMPETENT INSTITUTIONS, structured so a person with a problem can find the right door: its chapters are CENTRAL PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION, LOCAL PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION, and CIVIC ASSOCIATIONS WHICH PROVIDE LEGAL ASSISTANCE. Moldova is among the least-worked buckets in this file. A third chapter listing the associations that give legal help, printed beside the state bodies, is what a village needs when the state office cannot act — and it sits in the same volume, so a person who reaches the wrong institution is redirected rather than turned away. AND THE FORM OF THE ENTRIES, which is what makes it usable rather than merely descriptive: each body is given with CONTACT DETAILS — POSTAL CODE, STREET ADDRESS AND TELEPHONE NUMBERS, and in at least one case A CONFIDENTIAL TELEPHONE LINE separate from the main switchboard. Street addresses and direct numbers, not just organisation names, is the difference between a directory and a list. The guide was produced with a national council for state-guaranteed legal assistance and an international mission, which financed its publication.

trackers.name: Moldovan judges and prosecutors TRAINED in environmental law — what they now know
trackers.desc: THE BENCH ITSELF BEING PREPARED, which changes what a community can expect from a court: over THREE THEMATIC DAYS, THE PARTICIPANTS EXPLORED CRITICAL ASPECTS OF ENVIRONMENTAL LEGISLATION — namely THE ANALYSIS OF THE CONTROL OF ACTIVITIES WITH AN IMPACT ON THE ENVIRONMENT, ENVIRONMENTAL PERMITTING AND THE MANAGEMENT OF INDUSTRIAL EMISSIONS, THE LEGAL REGIME OF FORESTS, OF HUNTING ZONES AND OF STATE PROTECTED NATURAL AREAS, AND THE MANAGEMENT AND LEGAL PROTECTION OF WATER, SOIL AND SUBSOIL. Judges have been trained specifically on permitting and on protected areas, so those arguments will be understood rather than explained from scratch — the counterpart to the Greek guide written for judges in batch607, arriving as training rather than as a book. AND THE PROCEDURAL GUARANTEES COVERED, which a defendant community should know are on the curriculum: THE EUROPEAN PROCEDURAL GUARANTEES, INCLUDING THE RIGHT TO INFORMATION, ACCESS TO A LAWYER AND THE PRESUMPTION OF INNOCENCE IN ECOLOGICAL CASES. Access to a lawyer in ecological cases was taught to the bench as a guarantee, which matters where activists are themselves prosecuted. A central point was THE EXAMINATION OF INVESTIGATION MECHANISMS AND OF CRIMINAL LIABILITY THROUGH THE PRISM OF EU DIRECTIVES, and the training was explained by a named environmental organisation.

trackers.name: PravoDaZnam (Right to Know BiH)
trackers.desc: PravoDaZnam (Right to Know BiH) — Bosnia and Herzegovina’s civil-society Freedom of Information request portal (Transparency International BiH / Zašto ne) — helps citizens file access requests to all public institutions and publishes requests and responses online. — Holds to account: Bosnia and Herzegovina’s public authorities on disclosure — find public FOI requests, responses and non-responses.

trackers.name: Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina
trackers.desc: Official site of the state-level Court of BiH with verdicts and case information. · Find here: the judgments and case records of the Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina (including the war-crimes sections).

trackers.name: Centar za životnu sredinu (Center for Environment, Banja Luka)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Bosnia and Herzegovina's leading environmental association, which litigates permits and wins — it sued the Republika Srpska ministry over the environmental permit for the Ugljevik III thermal power plant and the court annulled it, and it has repeatedly forced disclosure of withheld information about geological exploration. Long-running campaigns against small hydropower on Balkan rivers and against new coal, plus support for local initiatives defending specific sites. WHO IT SUITS: a community facing a dam, mine or power plant in BiH, especially where the authorities are refusing documents — the record here is administrative-court challenges, so bring the decision you want overturned.

trackers.name: Justice and Environment — European green-law network
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the European network of environmental-law NGOs, whose national member here is Center for Environment (Centar za životnu sredinu). Its fifteen members act as the environmental-law service point in their own countries, taking cases and intervening in legislative processes, while the network defends communities and nature in court and lodges infringement complaints against member-state governments. Its standing themes are access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, environmental assessment and pollution control. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who does not yet know which lawyer to call — knock on Center for Environment (Centar za životnu sredinu)'s door first, and use the network only if your problem crosses a border. The network itself does not take individual cases; its members do. YOUR NATIONAL MEMBER IS Center for Environment (CZZS) (czzs.org) — go to them, not to the network. J&E members serve as environmental law ‘service points’ in their countries, handling cases, participating in legislative processes and sometimes providing legal analyses and consultations for national governments. The network has 11 full and 4 associate members, and can launch infringement proceedings against faulty governments — a route a national body alone does not have. CURRENT SCOPE: access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, climate, environmental assessments, and the Environmental Liability Directive. It previously worked on waste, transport, health and Natura 2000, so an older document may overstate what it covers today.

trackers.name: Constitutional Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina
trackers.desc: Constitutional Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina — supreme court (Bosnia and Herzegovina).

trackers.name: Constitutional Court of Republika Srpska
trackers.desc: Constitutional Court of Republika Srpska — supreme court (Bosnia and Herzegovina).

trackers.name: Agency for Statistics of BiH
trackers.desc: Bosnia and Herzegovina's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

trackers.name: Register of Business Entities
trackers.desc: National — unified register of business entities, Bosnia and Herzegovina. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Transparency International BiH (Bosnia and Herzegovina)
trackers.desc: Transparency International's Bosnia and Herzegovina chapter. Advocacy, a legal-advice centre (ALAC) and corruption monitoring — with work on political integrity (asset declarations, party finance), public procurement, whistleblower protection and parliamentary transparency.

trackers.name: Center for Investigative Reporting (CIN)
trackers.desc: Bosnian center exposing corruption and organized crime.

trackers.name: Public Procurement Portal (eJN)
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and for how much.

trackers.name: Privremena zaštita — full protection from the day the notice is published
trackers.desc: THE FASTEST PROTECTIVE EFFECT IN THIS ENTIRE MAP. Under the Zakon o zaštiti prirode FBiH (‘Službene novine FBiH’ 66/13), natural values that are the subject of a procedure to place them under protection are under temporary protection from the day the notice of public inspection is published in the daily press until the procedure concludes — and during that period the provisions of the Law apply as if the area had already been declared protected (Article 149). Everywhere else a designation campaign must survive years of process before anything binds; here publishing the public-inspection notice switches on full legal protection immediately. If your site is under imminent threat, getting the procedure formally started and the notice published IS the intervention — not the eventual declaration. WATCH THE GAZETTE BOTH WAYS: an act terminating protection is published in the Službene novine (Article 150). AND CHECK THE PERMIT TRIGGER: where nature protection measures are not contained in spatial planning documents, construction and other works in a protected area — and works needing an environmental impact assessment or an assessment of acceptability for nature — still require the separate nature-protection route.

trackers.name: Go cantonal — and quote the 4.5 percent against the 17 percent
trackers.desc: THERE IS NO SINGLE NATIONAL ROUTE, SO AIM AT THE CANTON. A protective zone outside a protected natural value can be established by special decision of the FBiH Government or of the cantonal assembly, with protection measures prescribed, on the proposal of the federal or cantonal ministry — so a buffer zone is obtainable at cantonal level, a far shorter path than federal legislation. Public institutions managing protected areas other than national parks are founded at cantonal level, and municipal nature protection work is done by municipal services under the Law on Principles of Local Self-Government. THE NUMBER THAT MAKES YOUR CASE: the Federation has 14 protected areas — only 1 national park — covering about 4.5 percent of territory, far below the 17 percent commitment accepted under the Convention on Biological Diversity. You are arguing that the entity is roughly a quarter of the way to a promise it already made; quote the gap. DATA AND CONTACT: the Fond za zaštitu okoliša FBiH maintains the protected-areas dataset from data supplied by the federal ministry and area managers, with boundaries digitised from the declaring act, and cantonal ministries must file an annual report to it — a checkable document. Sarajevo, +387 33 723 680. MIND THE ENTITY SPLIT: this Fond is not the Fond za zaštitu životne sredine i energetsku efikasnost Republike Srpske — both are Bosnian, neither is interchangeable.

trackers.name: Energy Community — private bodies may complain, and refusal is appealable
trackers.desc: A COMPLAINT MECHANISM WHERE REFUSAL BY THE GATEKEEPER CAN BE TAKEN OVER ITS HEAD — which is rare, and is the reason to know about this. Under Article 90 of the Energy Community Treaty, private bodies may approach the Secretariat with complaints about a Party's non-compliance, and under Article 12.2 of the Consolidated Rules the Secretariat initiates procedures in response to a complaint by a private body as well as on its own initiative. AND IF THE SECRETARIAT DECLINES: the revised Rules give the complainant the right to approach the Permanent High Level Group directly, which may hear the complaint directly or initiate a preliminary procedure — in most systems recorded in this map, a secretariat declining to act ends the matter. The PHLG can also take interim measures in matters of urgency under Article 47(c) — that is what matters when works are already under way, so ask for it expressly. THE ENVIRONMENTAL ACQUIS IS IN SCOPE, including the EIA Directive as amended by 2014/52, which was to be transposed by 1 January 2019. CHECK THE TRANSPOSITION DEADLINE FOR THE DIRECTIVE YOU RELY ON — failure to transpose by the stated date is itself the non-compliance, and is a far simpler case than arguing about how a rule was applied. THE REALISTIC WIN CONDITION: a case opens with an Opening Letter, escalates to a Reasoned Opinion giving two months to rectify, then to the Ministerial Council — but a case closes whenever the Party complies, and many are recorded as complied with before any decision was adopted. The opening of proceedings is the lever, not the final decision. YOU CAN ALSO JOIN AN EXISTING CASE: interested third parties may access the case file and submit written observations, provided they substantiate their legitimate interest. Case law from Opening Letters is published with dates and numbers, so precedent is visible. Write to the Energy Community Secretariat, Am Hof 4, 1010 Vienna. ONE MORE ROUTE: the amended Rules provide for cooperation with national authorities and courts, giving concrete assistance to national courts on the interpretation of Energy Community law — a domestic judge unsure how an EU-derived rule applies can be pointed at it.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: ELAW — free attorneys and scientists who will critique the developer's EIA
trackers.desc: IT WILL READ THE DEVELOPER'S EIA AND TELL YOU WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT — which is the thing a community cannot produce alone and usually cannot afford. ELAW is a global alliance of attorneys, scientists and other advocates, founded 1989 in Eugene, Oregon by public interest lawyers from ten countries, that provides legal and scientific support to grassroots advocates to challenge destructive projects. FOUR CONCRETE FORMS OF HELP: legal support to local public interest lawyers; scientific support, including critiquing environmental assessments; economic insights on projects; and security expertise — ‘ELAW helps environmental lawyers improve their security so they can work without fear. When our partners are targeted, we act quickly to help defend and protect them.’ That last one is a named function, not an aspiration, and ELAW co-founded the Alliance for Land, Indigenous and Environmental Defenders. HOW TO USE IT — THROUGH A LAWYER, NOT AS A CLIENT: ELAW works through more than 300 public interest advocates in its network, and its stated strategy is ‘locating strong lawyers who are committed to protecting the environment in their home countries’. You can approach ELAW directly, but the leverage is greatest when a local advocate is the conduit — that is how the network is built. It has hosted nearly 300 advocates from more than 65 countries as Fellows and provided support on thousands of cases; several partners have won the Goldman Environmental Prize. Focus areas include biodiversity, fossil fuels — expressly assisting advocates in contesting fossil fuel development projects — plastic pollution, and work with coastal communities. It publishes guidebooks, including one to give communities sufficient understanding to challenge oil and gas projects, and clause-level summaries of national EIA law — so its site is also a route to learning exactly what your own EIA law requires. ASK WHETHER ELAW HAS A PARTNER IN YOUR COUNTRY: the network is described as spanning 70 to 80 countries but the member list is not published country by country, so this entry does not assert a presence in yours.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Centar za životnu sredinu, Banja Luka — sues permits and wins (Bosnia and Herzegovina)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a non-profit, non-partisan environmental association at Miše Stupara 5, Banja Luka, which brings administrative lawsuits against environmental permits and has a record of winning them. It publishes the judgments on its own site. In July 2024 the District Court in Banja Luka upheld its claim and annulled the environmental permit for the Ugljevik III thermal plant, ordering the ministry to pay its costs and rejecting the developer's costs claim. On the Jovići small hydro scheme it had already overturned two environmental permits in court before a third was issued. On Sutjeska 2B it has run a series of actions since 2019, after establishing that the ministry exempted the investor from impact assessment in 2018 despite its own binding 2010 decision requiring one. It also turns out to the site when residents call it. Its own account of the Pliva at Otomalj is exactly that — local people called, and it went to the ground to get ahead of works it suspected were coming. That is a rarer offer than litigation. THE EXPECTATION IT SETS, AND IT IS THE HARDEST THING IN THIS FILE: winning does not end the project. At Jovići the permit was quashed twice and issued a third time. A Bosnian community should plan for a sequence of annulments rather than one, and should understand that the costs recovered are nominal — two hundred convertible marks in the Ugljevik case — so success in court funds nothing. What repeated annulment buys is time and a public record of the authority ignoring its own decisions, and in several of these cases that has been enough.

trackers.name: Fondacija Mozaik — 50 municipal funds, and grants a village group can actually get
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a development foundation founded in 2000 in Sarajevo, which has grown from supporting the local NGO sector into the main community-philanthropy body in Bosnia and Herzegovina. More than 3,000 projects supported with over 5 million convertible marks, across more than 100 communities. Bosnia had no funder at all in this file before this. THE STRUCTURE THAT MATTERS: its Omladinske banke — youth banks — have established 50 municipal funds, mobilised around 10,000 volunteers, and enable more than 550 projects a year. Decisions are made locally, in the municipality, by people from it. For a village group in BiH that is a nearer and far more reachable source of money than any national or international call in this file. THE GRANT SIZE, WHICH IS THE HONEST PART: its orange grants run to 3,000 convertible marks — roughly €1,500 — for a young person ready to start and run a socially useful project from beginning to end. That will not buy land or fund litigation. It will pay for a survey, a public meeting, printing, a valuation, a small piece of evidence, or the first organising work — and those are the costs that stop most community campaigns before they begin. WHO IT IS FOR, AND THE LIMIT TO ACCEPT: its focus is young people, entrepreneurship and community development, not environmental protection. Frame the ask as a young person leading a project that solves a concrete problem in their own community, because that is what it funds. If the group is not young, the youth bank route is not open, and the national programmes are the alternative. WHAT IT ALSO OFFERS: mentoring and advisory support to citizens across BiH since 2002, and membership of philanthropy networks including the regional SIGN network and European foundation associations, which is how a Bosnian group reaches funders outside the country.

trackers.name: Eko Bistro, Kruščica — the community that won, and what it says success required
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: an environmental citizens' association at Kruščica in the municipality of Vitez, central Bosnia, bistro.kruscica@gmail.com, formed by villagers — the women who had been blocking the bridge organised themselves into a citizens' association to formalise the fight. The river supplies drinking water to Kruščica's 2,500 residents and to some 145,000 people in two nearby towns. WHAT THEY DID AND WHAT IT COST: from August 2017 they held the access bridge to the construction site around the clock for over 500 days, through police violence, threats from the authorities and the investor, and winter. On 24 August a special police unit attacked women sitting on the bridge. Charges brought against them — assaulting a police officer — were dismissed by the court. AND THEY WON IN COURT: the cantonal court in Novi Travnik ruled that the environmental permit for the dam be annulled immediately, making further construction illegal, and on 14 December a court decision stopped all dam plans. But the concessions were not revoked — they remain in local planning documents, and the association has continued to challenge them. A community that wins a permit case has not necessarily removed the scheme from the plan. THE PART TO READ TWICE, because it is a checklist from people who did it: their own case study names what success requires as an attorney, a biologist, a spatial planner, and media communication, alongside strengthening the internal capacity of the local initiative — there the Eko Bistro association, the Kruščica Local Community and an informal women's group working together. It records 817 locals signing a petition to give power of attorney for the represented parties, and around 2,000 people taking part in the daytime vigil. IT ALSO NAMES WHO DECIDES: the Central Bosnia Canton government line ministry, and the Vitez Municipal Council through the municipal spatial plan. SUPPORT CAME FROM OUTSIDE TOO: the Czech organisation Arnika found the women in 2017 and began supporting them; the Centre for Environment in Bosnia and Herzegovina worked on the court case; and the campaign was carried internationally through the Balkan rivers network. Maida Bilal received the Goldman Environmental Prize.

trackers.name: Ornitološko društvo 'Naše ptice' — ten years of member records won IBA status for 13 areas
trackers.desc: WHAT THEY ACHIEVED, and it is the plainest demonstration in this file of what volunteer recording buys: on the basis of research carried out over the previous ten years by members of the society, BirdLife International awarded Important Bird Area status to a further 13 areas — Duvanjsko, Gatačko, Glamočko, Kupreško and Lušci polje, Mostarsko blato, Nevesinjsko, Podašničko and Popovo polje, and the Vukovsko-Ravanjsko, Dabarsko-Fatničko, Petrovačka and Grahovska complexes. It also prepared the nomination of 15 karst poljes to the IBA list. Members counting birds produced international designation for thirteen landscapes. AND THE WARNING THEY ATTACH TO IT: apart from Hutovo blato nature park, none of Bosnia's internationally important wetlands and none of the newly declared IBAs falls under any category of legal protection, and accordingly none has a management plan — with consequences including peat extraction. IBA status is recognition, not protection. A community should know which it is getting. THE LIVANJSKO POLJE CASE, worth reading before any Bosnian campaign: the society established regular bird monitoring there and the species count has climbed to 273 species, far ahead of Hutovo blato and anywhere else in the country. A protection study and a draft law were prepared long ago and, in the society's words, filed away in the drawers of the responsible municipal and cantonal institutions. The evidence can be overwhelming and still sit unused. HOW TO CONTRIBUTE, and it asks openly: install a recording app such as NaturaList or ObsMapp and follow the complete-list methodology — a complete list being every species an observer records at a given place in a given period. Records in your own yard, a park or a nearby wood are enough, and they feed EuroBirdPortal, the EBBA2 farmland work, and distribution modelling for national atlases. Its own framing: the European Bird Census Council's motto is that every bird counts, but in south-east Europe every bird counts double, because the region is under-recorded. ALSO: Sarajevo-based, active more than fifteen years, BiH coordinator for the European breeding bird atlas, running winter counts of wetland habitats with the Društvo za zaštitu i istraživanje biodiverziteta in Banja Luka, working against illegal killing of birds, and building birdwatching infrastructure — hides, rest areas and information points — on Livanjsko and Duvanjsko polje to strengthen local community capacity.

trackers.name: Aarhus centar Sarajevo — it finances the stručno obrazloženje your designation needs
trackers.desc: THE SENTENCE THAT CLOSES BOSNIA'S GAP: the Aarhus Centre in Sarajevo states that it contributed to the declaration of two new protected areas in Posavina Canton — Bara Starača and bara Tišina — and that it finances and co-finances the preparation of stručna obrazloženja, the expert justifications, for declaring new protected areas across the whole of the Federation of BiH, naming Prenj, the Pliva lakes, Okresanica on Majevica, Mokra Megara and Martinski Vis. WHY THAT IS THE ANSWER TO THE RIGHT QUESTION: three countries in this file now show that protection runs through designation rather than purchase, and that the binding constraint is the expert study. A valorisation of one Bosnian area records the obstacle directly — several initiatives to declare protected areas were launched at both city and cantonal level and have still not been realised, the main obstacle being the lack of expert groundwork to start the legally prescribed procedure. This is a body that pays for exactly that document. WHO DECLARES, SO YOU KNOW WHO TO CONVINCE: an area is declared protected by the Federal Ministry of Environment and Tourism for the Federation of BiH, or the Ministry of Spatial Planning, Construction and Ecology of Republika Srpska, under the inter-entity arrangement. The expert explanation is prescribed by FBiH law (article 145 of the Zakon o zaštiti prirode, Sl. novine FBiH 66/13), and must include the assessment and sources of funds needed to implement the declaration act. WHAT THE STUDIES COST, AND WHO ELSE PAYS: for the Pliva lakes the federal ministry secured 80,000 KM for the expert study and selected the consortium by public tender; for three further areas — Ravna Vala on Bjelašnica, Čemerska planina and the Misoča canyon, and the Čuda gorge near Olovo — 560,000 KM was provided, implemented by UNDP, which selects expert contractors through a public call. AND THE NUMBER TO USE IN AN ARGUMENT: around 4.5 per cent of the territory is protected, far below the 17 per cent commitment taken on under the Convention on Biological Diversity and far below the 30 per cent agreed at COP15. A Bosnian community proposing protection is helping the state meet a target it is publicly failing.

trackers.name: Ekofond RS — biodiversity and geodiversity are named uses, and the scoring rules are published
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Fond za zaštitu životne sredine i energetsku efikasnost Republike Srpske, Kralja Alfonsa XIII 21, 78000 Banja Luka; projects line 051/231-342. Bosnia's bucket held an Aarhus centre, two litigating groups and a municipal-fund foundation — this is the entity-level environmental fund, and it awards bespovratna — non-repayable — financial means. WHAT IT IS ALLOWED TO PAY FOR, from its own list: protection, preservation and improvement of the quality of air, water, soil and forests; landfill remediation and waste reduction; protection and preservation of biodiversity and geodiversity; encouraging sustainable use of protected natural assets; encouraging sustainable development of rural areas; energy efficiency and renewables; cleaner transport; and financing educational, research, innovation and development studies, programmes and projects in the field of environmental protection. Studies are a named purpose. WHERE ITS MONEY COMES FROM: environmental charges, plus means realised through international programmes and projects, and contributions, donations, gifts and aid. HOW THE COMPETITION WORKS, AND WHY THAT MATTERS: the javni konkurs is published on the fund's site, in the daily Glas Srpske and in the Official Gazette, with a 30-day deadline running from publication in the last of those — watch all three. Applications must be submitted in both electronic and printed form, in person or by post. And the fund publishes, alongside each call, the management board's decision with the plan for distributing the means, the commission's rules of procedure, and the rulebook for scoring programmes and projects, plus the application forms and the declarations required — on financial participation in the project, on not using budget means or other sources of financing, and on the security instrument. A published scoring rulebook tells you how your application will be marked before you write it, and the decisions selecting beneficiaries are published too. Note also that one call ran open until the available means were exhausted rather than to a fixed date.

trackers.name: Fond za zaštitu okoliša FBiH — the Federation's fund, and the protected-areas database it keeps
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the environmental protection fund of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Hamdije Čemerlića 39a, Sarajevo, +387 33 723 680 — the Federation counterpart to the Republika Srpska fund already filed here, which completes both entities. Its work programme runs on four-year cycles in line with the environmental protection strategy, and the fund's work is public, with reports submitted to the Federation Government. AND THE DATABASE IT MAINTAINS, which is the practical part: the Fund updates the data on protected areas in FBiH on the basis of information supplied by the ministry and BY THE MANAGERS OF THE PROTECTED AREAS, with boundaries digitised according to the description in the act — law, regulation or decision — proclaiming each area, INSPIRE-compliant. THE CATEGORIES YOU CAN ASK FOR, from the nature protection law: strict nature reserve, wilderness area, national park, nature park, monument of nature and natural features, habitat or species management area, protected landscapes, regional park, and protected areas with sustainable use of natural resources. AND THE ARGUMENT THAT COMES FREE WITH ALL OF IT: the Federation environment ministry states that only 4.5 per cent of the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina is formally protected, far below the European Union target of 30 per cent by 2030, and that the decisions taken by cities and municipalities, local companies and communities directly shape the country's future. Establishing a protected area proceeds on the basis of a stručni elaborat assessing the natural values.

trackers.name: eko.ba — Arnika's Bosnian platform, and the river surveys it has already paid for
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a platform devoted to publishing environmental information in Bosnia and Herzegovina, with an emphasis on ECOLOGICAL DEMOCRACY AND CIVIL SOCIETY CAMPAIGNS, run by the Czech NGO Arnika in cooperation with local partner organisations. Arnika has worked in Bosnia since 2014. Bosnia's bucket held two litigating groups and an Aarhus centre; this is the campaign platform and the foreign partner behind them. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY DELIVERED FOR NAMED RIVERS: biological research on the rivers Sana and Rzav carried out over two years through the project 'Dragulji prirode' — Jewels of Nature. A funded two-year biological survey of a named river is precisely the expert document this file has recorded as the bottleneck, and here a foreign NGO paid for it in partnership with local groups. THE NUMBERS IT PUBLISHES FOR ARGUMENT: Bosnia is among the five countries in Europe with the greatest biological diversity, with 252 ecosystem types and unique biotopes significant at European and global level — while protection is very weak, at only about three per cent of the territory, against an EU average of nearly 30 per cent. A community with a threatened river should ask which international NGO already works in its country and what surveys it has funded.

trackers.name: Udruženje Zeleni Neretva — it wrote the plain-language manual for protecting a site in BiH
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: an association that, as a contribution to the procedures for protecting natural areas, decided to create a publication covering the basic information on nature protection, both in international frameworks and in the existing situation in BiH. Bosnia's bucket held two litigating groups, an Aarhus centre, both entity funds and the Arnika platform — but nothing that tells a resident HOW A SITE GETS PROTECTED. WHAT IS IN IT, and why it is the right document for a village: it is written in simple language, expressly so it reaches readers from non-governmental organisations, employees of local self-government institutions, and all other interested groups and individuals, and is completely free of any political commentary. It sets out the international standards in nature protection AND THE PROCEDURES THAT MUST BE CARRIED OUT IN ORDER TO LEGALLY PROTECT PARTICULAR NATURAL VALUES IN BiH. AND THE PART NOBODY ELSE COMPILES: alongside the currently existing sites, it contains completed lists of the 'OLD' PROTECTED NATURAL OBJECTS — sites protected under earlier regimes whose status has since been left uncertain. A previously protected site is a far stronger case for re-protection than an unprotected one, and this is the list. The association is named for the Neretva, the river at the centre of Bosnia's hydropower conflicts.

trackers.name: The FBiH environment ministry — it is promoting protection OUTSIDE formally protected areas
trackers.desc: THE STATEMENT A COMMUNITY CAN BUILD ON: the Federation environment ministry says Bosnia is among the first countries in Europe developing NEW APPROACHES TO NATURE CONSERVATION WHICH RECOGNISE THE ROLE OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES, RESPONSIBLE LANDOWNERS AND PUBLIC INSTITUTIONS IN PROTECTING BIODIVERSITY EVEN OUTSIDE FORMALLY PROTECTED AREAS. These models support traditional practices and responsible stewardship of nature, while allowing the expansion of nature protection WITHOUT CREATING UNNECESSARY ADMINISTRATIVE BURDENS, strengthening cooperation with the private sector and helping BiH meet its international obligations. A ministry that has publicly committed to protection outside designated areas is one a community can hold to that commitment — and it is the closest thing Bosnia has to the stewardship route recorded in France, Germany, Ukraine and Portugal. AND WHOSE DECISIONS IT SAYS MATTER: biodiversity protection cannot remain the responsibility only of the institutions competent for the environment — it requires coordinated action by governments, cities and municipalities, companies, academia, civil society, local communities and international partners, and above all the understanding that LOCAL DECISIONS HAVE GLOBAL SIGNIFICANCE and that global nature protection goals can be achieved only through credible local action. IT ALSO RECORDS what has recently been launched: initiatives for financing biodiversity, climate adaptation, forest fire prevention and greater citizen participation in environmental management.

trackers.name: Kantonalna javna ustanova za zaštićena prirodna područja — the cantonal body that runs the sites
trackers.desc: WHO HOLDS AND RUNS PROTECTED LAND AT CANTONAL LEVEL, which is the tier a Bosnian community can actually reach: a KANTONALNA JAVNA USTANOVA — a cantonal public institution for protected natural areas, whose stated purposes are protection and preservation of original natural values and environmental diversity, and ensuring the smooth running of natural processes. Bosnia had no land-holding body filed. Where the federal ministry is remote, the cantonal institution is the one that manages the site next to you, and it is the body a resident writes to about damage, access or works. AND THE SCALE THAT MAKES THE CASE, published by an EU information centre: 49 areas are currently protected in Bosnia and Herzegovina, covering 185,335.26 hectares — a little over 3.6 PER CENT of the territory; 15 areas in the Federation over 112,296.83 hectares (about 4.3 per cent), and 34 areas in Republika Srpska over 73,038.43 hectares (about 2.96 per cent). Against that, in the EU 26 per cent of land is covered by protected areas, across more than 135,920 sites. AND THE CATEGORIES TO ASK FOR: strict nature reserve, wilderness area, national park, nature park, monument of nature, habitat/species management area, protected landscapes, regional park, and protected areas with sustainable use of natural resources.

trackers.name: The Bosnian warning about concessions inside protected areas — read before you campaign for one
trackers.desc: WHY THIS IS FILED, and it cuts against most of this file: a published critique argues that a Bosnian nature protection draft is presented as a defence of nature, but at the same time PERMITS CONCESSIONS IN PROTECTED PARTS OF NATURE — not just anywhere, but precisely where special value is claimed to exist. THE MECHANISM IT NAMES: the activity for which a concession may be issued is determined by THE PUBLIC INSTITUTION OR PUBLIC ENTERPRISE THAT MANAGES THE AREA, with the consent of the Ministry — which it calls a model in which the same circle of people manages the space, decides what is permitted, and opens the door to commercial use. A community that wins a designation should ask who will hold the concession power afterwards — this file has recorded Albania stripping protection from 5,000 hectares and Hungary moving protected land to forestry companies; this is the same risk at the moment of designation. AND WHO IT SAYS BEARS THE COST: if you own a piece of land, want to build a house, work the land, or live near a forest, river or mountain, this law concerns you — the draft bringing prohibitions, cost and legal uncertainty to the ordinary person while opening wide space for decision-making and earnings for authorities, management structures and future concessionaires. Its warning is that similar laws are increasingly appearing across Europe under the same argument.

trackers.name: The Biologer community camps — volunteers gather the survey data a protection study needs
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS AND WHY IT WORKS: a community bringing together several associations from Serbia, Croatia, Montenegro and Bosnia, alongside a named research centre, a Czech NGO, the Banja Luka environment centre and a Sarajevo Aarhus centre, running field camps on rivers under threat. AND THE STATED PURPOSE, which is the most directly copyable act in the Bosnian bucket: we saw the need to really make an effort, to use our contacts and invite colleagues we have in all the countries of the region, TO COLLECT AS MUCH DATA AS POSSIBLE WHICH WE WILL SUBMIT TO THE INSTITUTE FOR CULTURAL, HISTORICAL AND NATURAL HERITAGE, AND ON THE BASIS OF THAT DATA FOR A STUDY TO BE MADE FOR THE PROTECTION OF THIS AREA. Volunteers gathering the records, then handing them to the institute that writes the protection study, is the whole designation route done from below — and the reason it was needed: from this area there is almost no data at all; the only records findable in the literature were about flora from the 1970s. WHAT ONE CAMP PRODUCED: species entirely NEW TO BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA — a preliminary figure of over twenty spider species — new butterfly species, and many records that are the second or third ever for the country, including species endangered and rare, about whose distribution we know little or nothing. The river had been under great pressure from small hydropower construction; all those plans were halted.

trackers.name: Udruženje upravljača zaštićenih područja — six park managers in one association, with a named president
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: an ASSOCIATION OF PROTECTED AREA MANAGERS whose aims are support to managers in their work, improvement of activities connected with the protection and preservation of nature, EXCHANGE OF EXPERIENCE AND COOPERATION OF ALL MANAGERS for the purpose of protecting, preserving and promoting protected areas and their values. Bosnia had 24 filed entries and one land-holding body. AND WHO FOUNDED IT, which is a contact list in itself: three national parks, TWO NATURE PARKS AND THE ENTITY FOREST ENTERPRISE — with a named president published. Six bodies that between them hold most of the protected ground in an entity, sitting in one association with one named president, is a single door to all of them. AND WHAT REACHING THEM CAN YIELD, from the UNDP reporting alongside: modern firefighting equipment was delivered to several named parks, with TAILORED TRAINING FOR RANGERS AND STAFF; in one park staff were trained in GRANT PROPOSAL WRITING AND PROJECT PLANNING, enabling them to better access national and EU funding streams; and that park was selected as a pilot for the development and testing of INNOVATIVE FINANCING MECHANISMS supporting the wider community of protected area managers. The parks are described as moving from underfunded nature reserves into proactive, well-governed institutions, with one manager saying it helps them shift from reactive to proactive management.

trackers.name: JP Nacionalni park 'Una' — and the residents' and property-owners' entry status
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the public enterprise governing body of Bosnia and Herzegovina's LARGEST NATIONAL PARK, established in 2008 around a named river and its tributaries and covering 350 square kilometres, with a street address in a named town published on its own price list. AND THE PROVISION THAT MATTERS TO PEOPLE WHO LIVE THERE: the tariff recognises LOCAL INHABITANTS WHO LIVE IN THE PARK, that is in the named local communities, as a distinct category — and persons not previously known to the enterprise's employees AS RESIDENTS OR OWNERS OF PROPERTY IN THE PARK, or who visit these zones rarely, are obliged to PROVE THEIR STATUS at the entrance to an authorised person. Where a park charges for entry, the recognised categories of resident and property owner are worth knowing before you are stopped at a gate on your own land. AND THE LOYALTY SCHEME, which is how a park funds itself from its own public: the enterprise establishes a LOYALTY PROGRAMME as a voluntary programme for users; the right to a discount belongs to users with REGISTERED RESIDENCE IN BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA, proved by identification, and to those who register in it. Insurance of visitors is included in the ticket price, and group transport on a named route is charged separately.

trackers.name: Vaša prava BiH — a NETWORK of free legal aid offices AND MOBILE TEAMS across the country
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the leading non-governmental, non-profit organisation providing help to users ACROSS THE WHOLE TERRITORY of Bosnia and Herzegovina in ALL QUESTIONS OF CIVIL LAW AND HUMAN FREEDOMS, based in the capital. Bosnia had courts filed but no free legal service. AND HOW IT REACHES PEOPLE, which is the part that matters in a country of scattered villages: through A NETWORK OF FREE LEGAL AID OFFICES AND MOBILE TEAMS, it provides ALL FORMS OF LEGAL AID, in accordance with domestic laws, the EUROPEAN CONVENTION ON HUMAN RIGHTS and other international human rights instruments. Mobile legal teams are the answer for a community too small or too remote to have an office — the first such service recorded in this file. WHAT IT COVERS: labour law, PROPERTY RELATIONS, family law, social rights, status rights, pension and disability insurance, RECONSTRUCTION AND REBUILDING, and the rights of refugees, directed at categories from displaced people and returnees through to THE ENDANGERED LOCAL POPULATION. Property relations is a named practice area, and 'endangered local population' is a named client group, which is where a village facing a project fits. It was founded in 1996 as a network of information and legal aid centres, and alongside the legal work runs an INFORMATION COMPONENT supporting all legal activities through comprehensive campaigns.

trackers.name: Udruženje TUTOR — free legal aid under the NAMED statutes, entity by entity
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS AND THE LIMIT IT SETS ITSELF: an association established in the form of FREE LEGAL AID, based in the capital, which also provides GENERAL INFORMATION ON THE RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF CITIZENS of Bosnia and Herzegovina. AND THE HONESTY THAT MAKES IT USABLE: it states plainly that its pages will IN NO CASE be interpreted as a SUBSTITUTE FOR COMPETENT PROFESSIONAL ADVICE FROM A LICENSED ADVOCATE in your country, and that the association is NOT RESPONSIBLE for actions a reader may take on their own. A free service that tells you where its advice stops is one you can rely on for the part it does cover. AND THE LEGAL BASIS IT PUBLISHES, which is the useful part for anyone in Bosnia trying to find out what they are entitled to: legal counselling takes place ONLY AND STRICTLY under the conditions and standards prescribed by THE LAW ON THE PROVISION OF FREE LEGAL AID, and it lists the citation for the state-level law and separately for FOUR NAMED CANTONS and for THE LAW ON EXERCISING THE RIGHT TO FREE LEGAL AID IN REPUBLIKA SRPSKA, each with its official gazette number and year. Free legal aid in Bosnia is governed by a different statute in each canton and entity, so a community must check the one covering its own municipality.

trackers.name: Advokatska kancelarija Prnjavorac — the five expropriation rules, set out for owners
