ASK WHETHER ELAW HAS A PARTNER IN YOUR COUNTRY: the network is described as spanning 70 to 80 countries but the member list is not published country by country, so this entry does not assert a presence in yours.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Eko-svest, Skopje — has a community support coordinator (North Macedonia)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Centre for Environmental Research and Information Eko-svest, whose stated mission is to research, inform and act to improve public policy and practice. It employs a coordinator for community support — a named person whose job is backing local communities, which across thirty-one batches almost no organisation in this file has. It also keeps a local office at Vevčani rather than working only from Skopje, running the sustainable-management project for the Vevčani Springs protected area and the Jablanica–Karaorman biological bridge, both funded by the Prespa Ohrid Nature Trust. WHAT IT IS ALREADY FIGHTING: small hydropower inside protected areas. It points to the State Audit Office's 2021 findings on the damage those schemes cause and on irregularities in how their permits were issued, and notes that institutions carried on encouraging them regardless. Its public concern in early 2026 was that investors would start building in the window before a required study was completed — which tells a Macedonian community what to watch for: the gap between a deadline extension and the study that is supposed to fill it. It has also opposed amendments allowing permanent conversion of agricultural land into construction land for renewable projects. THE LEGAL ROUTE IT OPENS: Eko-svest is not a law firm, but it has produced regulatory analysis jointly with the Macedonian Young Lawyers Association. If your case needs counsel rather than research, that partnership is the introduction to ask for. WHAT TO BRING: it works on rivers, protected areas and energy consents. A case outside that is unlikely to be its priority, so say in the first message which protected area or watercourse is affected.

trackers.name: Macedonian Young Lawyers Association (MZMP) — free legal aid and strategic litigation
trackers.desc: WHO TO CALL: an independent non-profit professional organisation established in 2003, at Donbas St. 14-6, 1000 Skopje, +389 2 3220 870, contact@myla.org.mk. It describes its expertise as free legal aid, strategic litigation and public policy development, and it is one of the leading legal organisations in North Macedonia. Around nineteen staff. WHY IT IS IN THIS FILE: it is Eko-svest's partner on regulatory analysis of renewable energy law, and it has run a project on youth activism for greener municipalities funded by the EU delegation in Skopje, publicly recruiting trainers on the legal protection of the environment. North Macedonia previously had no named counsel in this file at all — only the cross-national Justice and Environment network and two campaigning organisations. This is the domestic legal body that the country's environmental organisation goes to. HOW TO APPROACH IT: it is a human rights and rule-of-law organisation whose core caseload is asylum, statelessness, discrimination and access to justice, not planning. So do not open with the landscape. Open with the right that is being denied — access to information, exclusion from a consultation, unequal treatment of a community — because strategic litigation is what it does, and a case that changes a practice is what it selects for. Ask specifically whether the environmental strand of its work is currently funded, since that strand has run on project money. USE IT WITH EKO-SVEST: batch 31 filed Eko-svest, which has a community support coordinator and a local office at Vevčani but is not a law firm. The two have already worked together. Bring them the same case.

trackers.name: Macedonian Ecological Society — holds the country's biodiversity data
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an environmental civil society organisation founded in 1972, based at Todor Skalovski 9A, Skopje, +389 2 240 2773, contact@mes.org.mk, an IUCN member and described by IUCN as the leading national expert on ecology and environment in Macedonian civil society. It is the largest environmental CSO in the country by staff, members, volunteers and university collaborators. THE REASON TO RING IT FIRST: it holds what is almost certainly the largest collection of biodiversity data in North Macedonia, with a dedicated GIS and databases programme, and it publishes scientific material publicly. A community that needs to establish what lives on a threatened site does not need to commission a survey before it knows whether one already exists. Ask what records it holds for your location, and ask for them in a form you can attach to an objection. WHAT ELSE IT HAS DONE THAT MATTERS: it carried out the development of a national representative network of protected areas under a UNDP and GEF project on the ecological, institutional and financial sustainability of the country's protected area system — so it has already assessed which parts of the country ought to be protected and were not. If your site appeared in that work, that is a national-level finding you did not have to pay for. It also runs species recovery work including the griffon vulture across the Balkans and long-running research in Prespa. USE IT AS THE THIRD LEG: this file already holds Eko-svest for community support and a local office at Vevčani, and the Macedonian Young Lawyers Association for free legal aid and strategic litigation. This is the science. Three organisations, three jobs, all in Skopje, all reachable. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer, not a funder, not a law firm. It works through projects and scientific gatherings, so ask whether a current project covers your area — that is what determines whether anyone has time.

trackers.name: HORUS — teaches a local group to raise its own money (North Macedonia)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a North Macedonian foundation, the country's member of the SIGN network of independent south-east European foundations, working on building the capacity of civil society organisations. Its main focus is strengthening the skills to mobilise resources from local sources and to build cross-sector cooperation for solving problems in the community, along with support in devising sustainability strategies and in identifying and developing project ideas for corporate and individual donors. WHY THAT IS THE RIGHT OFFER FOR A COMMUNITY RATHER THAN THE WRONG ONE: this file has recorded again and again that international rounds are slow, that national funds are oversubscribed, and that the money which actually arrives is local. An organisation whose speciality is teaching a local group to raise money from its own town, its own businesses and its own diaspora is addressing the constraint rather than the symptom. North Macedonia had no funder of any kind in this file. SOMETHING CONCRETE TO ASK FOR: it publishes a study of how 15 different civil society organisations in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro and Kosovo raised money in their own communities. Fifteen worked examples from neighbouring countries with comparable economies is a more usable document than any general fundraising guide. WHAT IT IS NOT: not an environmental organisation, not a land buyer, not a law firm, and its grants are not the point — capacity is. Pair it with the two Macedonian bodies already in this file, the community support organisation with a coordinator and local office and the free legal aid and strategic litigation association, and with the Prespa Ohrid Nature Trust, which funds environmental actors in this region including their operating costs.

trackers.name: MED's valorisation studies — 14 years to designate Osogovo, and the file that did it
trackers.desc: THE DESIGNATION ROUTE, WORKED THROUGH IN ONE COUNTRY: in 2017–2020, with local expertise from the Macedonian Ecological Society, a Study on the valorisation of the natural values of the Osogovo Mountains was produced, with a proposal to protect them in the category 'protected landscape' — and the process accelerated from there. An Annex to the Study followed once the proposal was harmonised; the institutions then agreed; the ministry submitted an Information on the acceptability of the proposal to the Government; and the Government adopted it on 5 May 2020, making Osogovo the country's first protected landscape — a category V protected area. HOW LONG IT TOOK, STATED PLAINLY BY THE ORGANISATION: the decision was the crown of 14 years of work, with partners and donors, domestic and foreign experts, the Nature Conservation Programme in North Macedonia and the environment ministry. Stakeholder engagement in the region ran from 2018 to 2020, and in August a public campaign for the declaration was carried out. A community starting this should plan in years, not seasons. WHAT MED ACTUALLY CONTRIBUTES, in its own words: expertise on biological diversity and defining the proposed boundaries of the area, plus capacity building, exchange between experts and institutions on defining and managing protected areas, and informing all affected parties — which it calls a key process for overcoming potential conflicts about future management. Drawing the boundary and squaring the neighbours are treated as one job. AND A CASE STILL OPEN, if your ground is there: MED is pressing for Mount Jablanica to become the country's fifth national park — ancient glacial lakes, endemic plants and animals — an initiative running for years and facing numerous obstacles. Its contact person on that is named publicly. MED also runs Prespa work going back nearly half a century and holds the country's biodiversity record, already noted in this file.

trackers.name: NCP Bregalnica — twelve years of Swiss money, and it funded local associations directly
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Programme for Conservation of Nature in North Macedonia, financed by the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation and implemented by Farmahem Skopje with HELVETAS Swiss Intercooperation, running twelve years across phases. Its aim was to help the country conserve its biological diversity and natural ecosystems by promoting their sustainable management and use, focused on the Bregalnica basin. WHY IT BELONGS IN A COMMUNITY'S FILE: it funded projects run by small local associations directly. Named grantees on its own site include the Association Regional Advocacy Center from Delchevo, setting up an educational trail; the association OHO, on conserving biodiversity through education and application; and a Municipal Sports Association from Kochani. A municipal sports association receiving nature-conservation money is the clearest signal in this file that the applicant does not have to be a conservation body. AND IT PUBLISHES THE EVIDENCE BASE: the site carries documents and publications issued under the Programme, plus documents from other institutions and organisations relating to nature conservation in the Bregalnica basin — a regional library a local group can cite from. WHAT THE MONEY ACHIEVED, for the argument: the Programme supported the designation of the Osogovo Mountains as the country's first protected landscape (IUCN category V) — the crown of fourteen years' work by the Macedonian Ecological Society, already filed here — and funded preparation of the management plan for it.

trackers.name: The public enterprises that hold North Macedonia's protected land — Jasen and the three national parks
trackers.desc: THE ANSWER TO 'WHO HOLDS THE LAND' IN NORTH MACEDONIA, after two rounds of looking for a land trust that does not exist: protected areas are held and run by javni pretprijatija — public enterprises. The ministry publishes the nature protection law with its subordinate acts, including the founding decision for the Javno pretprijatie za upravuvanje i zaštita na poveќenamenskoto podračje 'JASEN' — Skopje (JPUZPP JASEN), whose basic activity is stated as protection of nature, carrying out economic activities, and the improvement and use of the natural wealth in the multipurpose area. AND THE OTHERS NAMED IN THE SAME INSTRUMENT: the national parks Pelister, Galičica and Mavrovo, each an established managing body. These are the bodies a Macedonian community approaches about ground inside or adjoining a protected area — not an NGO, and not a buyer. WHY THIS CLOSES THE QUESTION HONESTLY: North Macedonia has no private conservation landholder, and I looked twice. Its bucket already holds MES (an association), the Swiss-funded programme, Eko-svest, HORUS, FRONT 21/42 and the young lawyers' free legal aid. What was missing was the public body with title and a management mandate, and this is it. PRACTICAL, FROM THE SAME DOCUMENT SET: the ministry portal carries the nature protection law together with its amendments and subordinate acts in one place — the founding decisions, the staffing transfers between park enterprises, and the official gazette references. If you need to know which enterprise is responsible for a given area and under what decision, it is there.

trackers.name: PONT — a standing nature fund for one named region, and it paid for a regional office
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Prespa Ohrid Nature Trust — a nature fund for the Prespa–Ohrid region — which, with a private foundation, financed a cross-border project under which the Macedonian ecological society began monitoring large mammals, plants and aquatic habitats at cross-border level. North Macedonia's bucket held one Swiss-funded programme and the state fund; this is a standing trust dedicated to a single named landscape. A region-specific nature trust is worth looking for wherever a lake, river basin or mountain range crosses a border — it funds the long monitoring that no annual grant round supports, and its executive director spoke at the opening of the office it helped make possible. AND WHAT THE MONEY BOUGHT, which is the model: the ecological society opened a REGIONAL BRANCH OFFICE in the Prespa town of Resen, described by the society as an important step forward. Funding a permanent local office is worth more to a community than funding a project, because the office is still there when the project ends. The work sits within a named partner network for the Prespa basin.

trackers.name: The revalorisation study — how a Macedonian protected area gets re-declared, and who writes it
trackers.desc: THE PROCEDURE, NAMED: a national park is to be RE-PROCLAIMED as a protected area under the current nature law, and the environment ministry, in cooperation with an international conservation organisation and the Macedonian ecological society, began the procedure for SUPPLEMENTING THE REVALORISATION STUDY and for drafting a MANAGEMENT PLAN — work to be carried out over the following ten years with support from a conservation fund. The revalorisation study is the document that re-declares a protected area in North Macedonia, and an NGO co-writes it with the ministry. This file has recorded the same shape in Montenegro, where the NGOs drafted the protection study and the agency adopted it — and in Croatia, where an association writes boundary-change studies. Ask who is writing the revalorisation study for the area near you, and whether they need local records. AND THE SPECIES THAT CARRIES THE ARGUMENT THERE: the Balkan lynx is the most endangered species in Macedonian fauna and the danger of its disappearance still exists. The same society has run a programme for the study and protection of vultures since 2003, and a cross-border project on the Osogovo Mountains aimed at forming a transboundary protected area with the support of the local authorities.

trackers.name: Opština Resen — the MUNICIPALITY is the managing body of a nature park
trackers.desc: THE FINDING, AND IT IS THE ONE A MACEDONIAN COMMUNITY CAN USE: the managing body of the protected area is THE MUNICIPALITY OF RESEN, which is obliged EVERY YEAR to assess the implementation of the management plan and, where appropriate, to introduce new elements into it. North Macedonia's holders were the state public enterprises filed in batch 313; this is a nature park run by a town hall. A municipality can be the manager of a protected area, and it must review the plan annually — which gives a resident a yearly, dated moment to bring evidence to a body they can walk into. AND WHO WROTE THE PLAN, which is the second usable fact: it was prepared by experts from the natural sciences faculty AND THE MACEDONIAN ECOLOGICAL SOCIETY, within a transboundary ecosystem management project run by the environment ministry across Albania, Macedonia and Greece. The society is already filed here. WHAT THE PLAN ITSELF CONTAINS, so a community knows what to ask for: the legal and administrative framework for managing the site; its INTERNATIONAL STATUS; RIGHTS OF POSSESSION AND OTHER RIGHTS; and OTHER AFFECTED PARTIES. A management plan that lists possession rights and affected parties tells you who else has standing before you start. The area sits beside two national parks and within a UNESCO transboundary biosphere reserve.

trackers.name: The Prespa protected-area cluster — Ramsar, Emerald and a UNESCO reserve on one lake
trackers.desc: WHAT THE DESIGNATIONS ARE, stacked on one place, and each is a separate lever: the lake is on the RAMSAR CONVENTION list (1995), an EMERALD area (2008), and identified as a future Natura site; it borders a nature park and two national parks; and it forms part of the UNESCO Ohrid-Prespa TRANSBOUNDARY BIOSPHERE RESERVE (2014) together with those parks, a second lake and a named natural monument. Where several designations overlap, a community has several bodies to notify and several conventions to cite — and this file has recorded the Bern Convention working as a lever in Montenegro and Cyprus. AND THE STATED PURPOSES OF THE PROTECTION, which are the words to quote back at the manager: integral protection of natural habitats and species of NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL IMPORTANCE; SUSTAINABLE USE OF THE NATURAL HERITAGE IN THE INTEREST OF PRESENT AND FUTURE DEVELOPMENT WITHOUT DAMAGING THE PARTS OF NATURE; MAINTAINING THE ECOLOGICAL BALANCE through permanent preservation of the lake's biotic characteristics; and creating conditions for tourism development IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE PRINCIPLE OF SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT. The report is the environment ministry's own analysis of the lake's condition, naming the institutions competent to manage it.

trackers.name: Eko-svest — a FREE GREEN TELEPHONE for reporting an environmental problem, and a local office
trackers.desc: THE SERVICE, AND IT IS THE SIMPLEST RESOURCE IN THE WHOLE MACEDONIAN BUCKET: citizens can communicate with us on our FREE SERVICE — THE GREEN TELEPHONE — and REPORT A PROBLEM in the field of the environment and nature. A published number, no cost, no membership. A free national reporting line run by an NGO rather than a ministry is the first call a villager can make, and North Macedonia had 25 filed entries. AND IT WORKS LOCALLY, NOT JUST FROM THE CAPITAL: the centre operates THROUGH A LOCAL OFFICE in a named village, and within a biological-bridge project financed by the Prespa Ohrid Nature Trust — the standing transboundary fund already filed here. WHAT ELSE IT PUTS IN PEOPLE'S HANDS: training for citizens and activists who want to acquire PRACTICAL KNOWLEDGE FOR DEALING WITH FOREST FIRES AND PROTECTING NATURE, especially in mountain areas, described as strengthening LOCAL CAPACITY TO ACT IN CRISIS SITUATIONS; and, through a small grants programme of the Global Environment Facility, it equipped local schools with computer stations, 3D printers and filament extruders so pupils turn collected plastic into teaching material. It has raised the status of a named mountain as a priority, in the context of initiatives to obtain NATIONAL PARK STATUS. Its street address is published.

trackers.name: Macedonian Ecological Society — founded 1972, the country's oldest, and it takes members
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: an ASSOCIATION OF CITIZENS active in the field of ecology and environmental protection, which is THE OLDEST ECOLOGICAL ORGANISATION IN MACEDONIA, FOUNDED IN 1972. It pursues its aims through carrying out and participating in projects and organising scientific and expert gatherings. An association of citizens, not a foundation, means a resident can join it and vote — and it builds capacity by training its own members and creating young scientific cadres, bringing in young ecologists, biologists, AGRONOMISTS, FORESTERS, technologists and other enthusiasts. WHAT IT ACTUALLY RUNS, which is why it can support a designation case: a project for the full recovery of the griffon vulture population on the Balkan Peninsula; and one named the Green and Blue Prespa Initiative: STRENGTHENING PROTECTION THROUGH RESEARCH AND EDUCATION. It says of that lake region: for almost half a century, Prespa has occupied a special place in our work, going back to early research by a named professor. Half a century of continuous research on one landscape is the evidence base a protection study is built from — and this file recorded this society co-writing exactly such a study. It publishes procurement notices and public calls, and hosts the national congress of ecologists.

trackers.name: J.U. Nacionalen Park Mavrovo — 73,088 hectares, a NAMED DIRECTOR and his mobile number
trackers.desc: WHO ANSWERS, published on the park's own management page: the DIRECTOR of the public institution, by name, with HIS PERSONAL EMAIL, HIS MOBILE TELEPHONE NUMBER, the park's own email and its landline. North Macedonia had one land-holding body filed; this is the largest, and its director's mobile is public. WHAT IT HOLDS: 73,088 HECTARES, the largest of the country's three national parks, declared by law of the national assembly on 19 April 1949, taking in named mountain ranges and the valley and catchment of a named river. AND THE FOUNDING PURPOSE, which is the wording to quote back at any proposal inside it: the park was formed BECAUSE OF THE PARTICULAR NATURAL BEAUTIES, AND THE HISTORICAL AND SCIENTIFIC SIGNIFICANCE OF THE FORESTS AND FOREST LANDSCAPES around the plain. A founding statute that names beauty, history and science as the reasons is broader ground to argue on than a species list. AND WHAT IT ACTUALLY ENFORCES: the institution has published a notice introducing A COMPLETE BAN ON UNREPORTED MOVEMENT IN THE FORESTS AND FOREST LAND. Its zoning is published too, including scientific-research departments for forestry and other fields and named tourist-recreational zones.

trackers.name: JP Jasen — a 24,000-hectare multipurpose reserve run by its own public enterprise
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Public Enterprise for Managing and Protection of the Multipurpose Area Jasen — a nature reserve only 15 km from the capital, made a protected reserve in 2010, with part of it declared a reserve as far back as 1958. A public enterprise created to manage one named area is a body a nearby community can address directly, rather than a ministry covering the whole country. WHAT IT COVERS: around 24,000 HECTARES of caves, mountains, UNDERGROUND RIVERS AND LAKES, with the lowest point a STILL UNCHARTED canyon lake and the highest a mountain of almost 2,500 metres. It is home to the endangered Eurasian lynx and the rare Balkan chamois — the same lynx this file recorded as having fewer than 10 individuals left in neighbouring Albania. AND THE ORIGINAL GROUNDS OF DECLARATION, useful because they are broader than a habitat designation: the 1958-60 declaration had as its goal the protection of the FAUNAL, FLORAL, BIOLOGICAL, GEOLOGICAL, NATURAL AND HYDROLOGICAL RARITIES. Where geology and hydrology are named in the founding act, a community can object on grounds of caves and water, not only wildlife.

trackers.name: Pravnapomos.mk — the national free legal aid portal, with THE REGISTER OF ADVOCATES
trackers.desc: WHAT IT CARRIES: the national portal for free legal aid, publishing ALL LAWS, SECONDARY LEGISLATION, FORMS AND OTHER MATERIALS in the field of Free Legal Aid IN ONE PLACE — and, most usefully, THE REGISTER OF ADVOCATES ENTERED FOR SECONDARY LEGAL AID. North Macedonia had three legal entries filed; this is the list every one of them draws from. A published register of the lawyers the state itself will pay is the shortest route from 'we need a lawyer' to a name — and it costs nothing to read. AND WHY THE DISTINCTION MATTERS, from the same system: PRIMARY legal aid is given by an authorised official of the Ministry, BY AN AUTHORISED ASSOCIATION, AND BY A LEGAL CLINIC, and covers information, advice, guidance and help in submitting the applications for free legal aid; SECONDARY free legal aid covers LEGAL AID IN PROCEEDINGS BEFORE A COURT; REPRESENTATION AND DEFENCE BEFORE THE COMPETENT COURT and other state bodies; and THE DRAFTING OF SUBMISSIONS — the claim, the response to the claim, THE APPEAL and others. The free-aid system splits into advice you can get from an association and representation that needs a registered advocate, so a community should ask for the second by name.

trackers.name: Koalicija Site za pravično sudenje — an AUTHORISED association on the state register, reachable by Viber
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: an AUTHORISED ASSOCIATION for providing free legal aid, ENTERED IN THE STATE REGISTER OF LEGAL AID PROVIDERS at the Ministry of Justice. Being on the ministry's register is what separates an association that can formally act from one that can only sympathise, and the register is public, so a community can check any body offering it help. AND HOW TO REACH IT, which is the part that lowers the barrier: if you need PRIMARY legal aid you can contact us BY MOBILE, EMAIL, VIBER OR THROUGH FACEBOOK MESSENGER; and if after that contact you need further help, you can arrange a meeting WITH OUR LEGAL ADVISER. A legal service reachable on the messaging app people already use is one a villager will actually contact — this file has recorded free phone lines and email addresses, but not this. AND THE WIDER SYSTEM IT SITS IN: another authorised association records that its free legal aid is provided in individual cases DIRECTLY CONNECTED WITH THE PROTECTION OF HUMAN RIGHTS, THE RULE OF LAW AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF CIVIL SOCIETY, and includes LEGAL ADVICE AND STRATEGIC REPRESENTATION in cases of violations of constitutionally guaranteed human rights.

trackers.name: Civica Mobilitas AD HOC grants — open to UNREGISTERED groups of citizens, for BURNING issues
trackers.desc: WHO CAN APPLY, and this is the rarest eligibility line filed in this whole file: the ad hoc grants are intended for associations and foundations AS WELL AS FOR INFORMAL, UNREGISTERED GROUPS OF CITIZENS, to support URGENT, NON-POSTPONABLE, so-called 'BURNING' QUESTIONS which arise and which demand urgent attention and action AT EVERY LEVEL OF INTERVENTION in Macedonia — LOCAL, MUNICIPAL, REGIONAL OR NATIONAL. North Macedonia had three funding entries filed. A neighbourhood group that formed last week, has no registration and no bank history, can apply here — every other fund recorded in this file requires one to three years of registration first. AND THE TERMS: the size of the requested grant should be AT MOST 400,000 DENARS; the total available for the call is 20,000,000 DENARS; and the duration of activities should be AT MOST SIX MONTHS. AND THE TWO-STAGE ROUTE, which lowers the work: applicants initially submit ONLY THE CONCEPT FORM. The application form is filled in ONLY IF the applicant has received A WRITTEN INVITATION to submit an application, after the preliminary selection of the concept. Concepts and applications go by electronic mail to a published address.

trackers.name: Civica Mobilitas INSTITUTIONAL grants — core funding built on the applicant's OWN self-assessment
trackers.desc: WHAT THIS MONEY IS FOR, and it is different from project money: the institutional grants support the process of INSTITUTIONAL DEVELOPMENT / ORGANISATIONAL STRENGTHENING of the selected grantees, BASED ON THE APPLICANTS' OWN SELF-ASSESSMENT and on 'ROADMAPS' PROPOSED BY THEM for their own organisational transformation. The second self-assessment-based funder recorded in this file after Ukraine's — money for whatever the group itself names as its weakest point, rather than for a project shaped to fit a call. In preparing the application, organisations must go through a self-assessment process, filling in A SELF-ASSESSMENT QUESTIONNAIRE. AND THE AMOUNTS AND LIMITS: grants will be BETWEEN 15,000 AND 40,000 SWISS FRANCS PER YEAR, with 500,000 SWISS FRANCS available for the first year. The call is open to organisations registered in Macedonia under the Law on Associations and Foundations (2010); each organisation may submit ONLY ONE application, and winners will NOT be able to receive another institutional or action grant in this phase. Assessment and selection are made by AN INDEPENDENT GRANT SELECTION COMMITTEE. Elsewhere the programme has funded environmental associations working IN PARTNERSHIP with a second named association.

trackers.name: MCMS — the Macedonian centre that ADMINISTERS the grants, and its own calls page
trackers.desc: WHO ACTUALLY HANDS OUT THE MONEY: the Macedonian Centre for International Cooperation is one of the bodies implementing the Swiss-funded civil society programme already recorded in this file, and it publishes ITS OWN NOTICES AND CALLS PAGE, separate from the programme's site, carrying CALLS FOR APPLICATIONS FOR SMALL ACTION GRANTS with their closing dates and the postal address applications must reach. Knowing which organisation administers a foreign donor's money tells a community whose door to knock on — the donor is abroad, the decision is made locally. AND THE STEP IN ITS APPLICATION PROCESS WORTH COPYING: for institutional grants, applications go in through a form, but IN THE PROCESS OF PREPARING THE APPLICATION, ORGANISATIONS WILL ALSO HAVE TO GO THROUGH A PROCESS OF SELF-ASSESSMENT, filling in A SELF-ASSESSMENT QUESTIONNAIRE. The same self-assessment-first method recorded in Ukraine appears here under a different donor, which suggests a group that has already worked out its own weakest point is prepared for more than one funder's form. AND THE TERMS ON THAT MONEY: institutional grants run FOR A PERIOD OF UP TO THREE YEARS (36 MONTHS), and support in the second and third year DEPENDS ON THE GRANTEES' ACHIEVEMENTS and is subject to approval by the grant selection committee.

trackers.name: Agency for Personal Data Protection & Free Access to Information
trackers.desc: Agency for Personal Data Protection & Free Access to Information — Montenegro’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Agency for Prevention of Corruption (ASK)
trackers.desc: Legislator / public-official financial interest & asset declarations. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers, top officials & cabinet — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held; their assets, interests and integrity declarations.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Montenegro
trackers.desc: Official site of the Vrhovni sud Crne Gore with a national case-law database. · Find here: information and judgments of the Supreme Court of Montenegro.

trackers.name: Agency for Personal Data Protection & Free Access to Information (AZLP)
trackers.desc: National right-to-information authority (dual-mandate); Montenegro’s AZLP is the supervisory authority for both personal-data protection and free access to information, Montenegro.

trackers.name: Green Home (NVO Green Home, Podgorica)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Podgorica environmental organisation that RERI's regional environmental-law conference names as its Montenegrin participant, alongside the Serbian and Bosnian bodies in that circle — which makes it the country's point of contact in the Western Balkans environmental-law network. WHO IT SUITS: anyone in Montenegro looking for a first door on an environmental or land question, but note that what it will take on is not stated in the source that names it, so ask before assuming it litigates or takes casework. Domain unverified this session — only aggregator listings resolved, so no URL is given rather than a guessed one. Reach it through the participant listing on RERI's conference site at envlawcon.reri.org.rs, or via RERI in Belgrade. Green Home convenes Coalition 27, the informal network of Montenegrin NGOs that acts as the civil-society platform on EU environmental standards, and publishes a shadow report on Chapter 15.

trackers.name: Eko-fond — Fond za zaštitu životne sredine Crne Gore
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: Montenegro's state environmental fund, set up by government decision under the Law on Environment as a single-member company wholly owned by the Government, to finance the preparation, implementation and development of programmes and projects in environmental conservation, protection and improvement, energy efficiency and renewables, at both state and local level. Its founding remit expressly covers nature, soil, forests, water and the sea, and the promotion of sustainable use of natural resources, and it awards money through public calls. WHO IT SUITS: read the current call before investing effort. The awards visible on its own site skew heavily towards waste infrastructure and energy efficiency, and towards companies and municipalities rather than residents' groups — a €200,000 contract for a tyre shredder is a fair sample. HOW IT DIFFERS: it is the state's own money rather than a foundation's, so a municipality willing to sponsor your site is a far stronger route in than an association applying alone.

trackers.name: Crime and Corruption Reporting Network — LUPA
trackers.desc: Montenegrin crime-and-corruption reporting network exposing organized crime and illicit finance.

trackers.name: Center for Investigative Journalism of Montenegro (CIN-CG)
trackers.desc: Montenegrin center investigating organized crime, corruption and abuse of public funds.

trackers.name: State Audit Institution
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Montenegro, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Electronic Public Procurement (CeJN)
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Montenegro, and for how much.

trackers.name: Statistical Office of Montenegro (MONSTAT)
trackers.desc: Montenegro's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Montenegro.

trackers.name: CRPS Business Registry
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Zakon o zaštiti prirode — your municipal assembly can protect land itself
trackers.desc: A ROUTE THAT DOES NOT START AT THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT. Under the Zakon o zaštiti prirode (‘Službeni list CG’ 54/16), declaration of protected natural assets — articles 55–61 — happens at the level matching the category: national assets by Government decision, but other protected natural assets by the assembly of the local self-government unit, and where an area crosses two or more municipalities the assemblies of each adopt the decision. AND THE STUDY IS PAID FOR FROM PUBLIC BUDGET, NOT BY YOU: the studija zaštite is prepared by a legal person and funds for it are provided in the budget of Montenegro or of the local self-government unit — as in Turkey, the decisive expense falls on the state. ONCE DECLARED, use must follow the studija zaštite or special purpose spatial plan and the management plan; prohibited is use causing damage to land and loss of its natural fertility or damage to geological, hydrogeological and geomorphological values. Actions not subject to impact assessment and not in the management plan need a permit from the administrative body — which is where small unassessed works get caught.

trackers.name: What the studija zaštite must contain — including the cost to owners
trackers.desc: EFFECTIVELY THE CHECKLIST FOR MAKING YOUR CASE. The study must set out: the natural, created and landscape features; the locality's characteristics and values; the existing state of resources with valorisation; an opinion on placing the asset under protection; proposed classification by significance; the proposed category and protection regime (zones); a cartographic display with boundaries drawn from cadastral real estate data; the concept of protection, improvement, sustainable development and management; and the consequences the declaration will produce, particularly for ownership rights and existing economic activities, plus possible sources of funds for implementation. THAT LAST ELEMENT IS WHERE A LOCAL CAMPAIGN IS WON OR LOST — and it is a required part of the document, so engage with it rather than leaving it to be raised against you. THREE INSTRUMENTS IN THE REGISTER WORTH KNOWING: the act on preventive protection, useful where a threat is imminent; the revision study; and the act on cessation of protection — watch for that one if protection is being removed. NGOs do feature: Montenegro's second marine protected area was credited to national institutions together with the NGO sector, naming Green Home and MEDCEM.

trackers.name: Energy Community — private bodies may complain, and refusal is appealable
trackers.desc: A COMPLAINT MECHANISM WHERE REFUSAL BY THE GATEKEEPER CAN BE TAKEN OVER ITS HEAD — which is rare, and is the reason to know about this. Under Article 90 of the Energy Community Treaty, private bodies may approach the Secretariat with complaints about a Party's non-compliance, and under Article 12.2 of the Consolidated Rules the Secretariat initiates procedures in response to a complaint by a private body as well as on its own initiative. AND IF THE SECRETARIAT DECLINES: the revised Rules give the complainant the right to approach the Permanent High Level Group directly, which may hear the complaint directly or initiate a preliminary procedure — in most systems recorded in this map, a secretariat declining to act ends the matter. The PHLG can also take interim measures in matters of urgency under Article 47(c) — that is what matters when works are already under way, so ask for it expressly. THE ENVIRONMENTAL ACQUIS IS IN SCOPE, including the EIA Directive as amended by 2014/52, which was to be transposed by 1 January 2019. CHECK THE TRANSPOSITION DEADLINE FOR THE DIRECTIVE YOU RELY ON — failure to transpose by the stated date is itself the non-compliance, and is a far simpler case than arguing about how a rule was applied. THE REALISTIC WIN CONDITION: a case opens with an Opening Letter, escalates to a Reasoned Opinion giving two months to rectify, then to the Ministerial Council — but a case closes whenever the Party complies, and many are recorded as complied with before any decision was adopted. The opening of proceedings is the lever, not the final decision. YOU CAN ALSO JOIN AN EXISTING CASE: interested third parties may access the case file and submit written observations, provided they substantiate their legitimate interest. Case law from Opening Letters is published with dates and numbers, so precedent is visible. Write to the Energy Community Secretariat, Am Hof 4, 1010 Vienna. ONE MORE ROUTE: the amended Rules provide for cooperation with national authorities and courts, giving concrete assistance to national courts on the interpretation of Energy Community law — a domestic judge unsure how an EU-derived rule applies can be pointed at it.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: ELAW — free attorneys and scientists who will critique the developer's EIA
trackers.desc: IT WILL READ THE DEVELOPER'S EIA AND TELL YOU WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT — which is the thing a community cannot produce alone and usually cannot afford. ELAW is a global alliance of attorneys, scientists and other advocates, founded 1989 in Eugene, Oregon by public interest lawyers from ten countries, that provides legal and scientific support to grassroots advocates to challenge destructive projects. FOUR CONCRETE FORMS OF HELP: legal support to local public interest lawyers; scientific support, including critiquing environmental assessments; economic insights on projects; and security expertise — ‘ELAW helps environmental lawyers improve their security so they can work without fear. When our partners are targeted, we act quickly to help defend and protect them.’ That last one is a named function, not an aspiration, and ELAW co-founded the Alliance for Land, Indigenous and Environmental Defenders. HOW TO USE IT — THROUGH A LAWYER, NOT AS A CLIENT: ELAW works through more than 300 public interest advocates in its network, and its stated strategy is ‘locating strong lawyers who are committed to protecting the environment in their home countries’. You can approach ELAW directly, but the leverage is greatest when a local advocate is the conduit — that is how the network is built. It has hosted nearly 300 advocates from more than 65 countries as Fellows and provided support on thousands of cases; several partners have won the Goldman Environmental Prize. Focus areas include biodiversity, fossil fuels — expressly assisting advocates in contesting fossil fuel development projects — plastic pollution, and work with coastal communities. It publishes guidebooks, including one to give communities sufficient understanding to challenge oil and gas projects, and clause-level summaries of national EIA law — so its site is also a route to learning exactly what your own EIA law requires. ASK WHETHER ELAW HAS A PARTNER IN YOUR COUNTRY: the network is described as spanning 70 to 80 countries but the member list is not published country by country, so this entry does not assert a presence in yours.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: MANS — investigates the permit and files the criminal complaint (Montenegro)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Montenegrin investigative organisation that takes building and planning cases apart on the documents and then puts them in front of the state prosecutor. It has filed a criminal complaint over unlawful construction against a sitting minister of ecology, spatial planning and urbanism and his son, having compared site conditions from 2018 with the present to show that work continued after the legalisation request had been formally refused. WHAT IT ACTUALLY PRODUCES, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART FOR A COMMUNITY: the Valdanos case in Ulcinj is the model. It established that a building permit had been issued for a structure inside an olive grove where the municipality's own spatial-urban plan forbids construction and the governing plan reserves the land for olive growing; that the Olive Growing Act separately bars residential building there; that the municipality later added a use permit; and that the same operation had drawn close to €140,000 of IPARD agricultural support intended for farm production. A community can supply the local knowledge; MANS assembles the paper trail that makes it actionable. WHAT TO EXPECT: this is an anti-corruption investigator, not a legal aid office. It selects its cases, it works from documents, and it is politically exposed in a small country — expect the association to be attacked rather than the findings. Bring it dates, parcel numbers, permit references and photographs from before and after, because that is the material its cases are built from. A complaint to a prosecutor is also a slower and less certain route than an administrative challenge, so it is best used alongside one rather than instead of it.

trackers.name: fAKT — funds informal local groups, and prioritises outside Podgorica (Montenegro)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Fund for Active Citizenship, a local non-governmental grantmaking foundation at Vaka Đurovića 20/1, Nova Varoš II, 81000 Podgorica, +382 20 665 600, fond@faktcg.org. It supports citizens' initiatives that tackle problems people face in their own communities, using local resources, and its stated aims include strengthening communities by backing initiatives that come from the local community rather than being brought to it. Montenegro's only other money in this file is a state fund. THE TWO ELIGIBILITY FACTS THAT MATTER MOST, AND THEY ARE UNUSUAL: its grant calls have been aimed explicitly at less developed organisations, local informal groups, activists and civic movements — and particularly those outside Podgorica. A village committee with no legal form, in a place a long way from the capital, is not an awkward fit here; it is the intended applicant. Across 138 candidates only the Belgian foundation in batch 47 has been as explicit about taking unincorporated groups. GRANT SIZES TO PLAN AROUND: recent small-grant schemes have run €3,000 to €6,000 per project. Its wider programme has combined three grant streams — community in action, active participation and public advocacy — with mentoring, capacity building and peer learning, aimed deliberately at newly formed organisations and informal groups in less developed parts of the country. The public advocacy stream is the one to ask about if the problem is a decision rather than a project. WHAT IT IS NOT: not an environmental funder, not a land buyer and not a law firm. Frame the application as citizens organising to solve a concrete local problem and to take part in a public decision, which is precisely what it exists to fund. It belongs to the regional SIGN network of independent foundations alongside its Bosnian, Serbian, Kosovar and Macedonian counterparts, which is the route to the equivalent body in a neighbouring country.

trackers.name: CRNVO's konkursi page — every open Montenegrin call in one place, including two on nature
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the running list of open calls (konkursi) for Montenegrin non-governmental organisations, published by CRNVO, the country's NGO resource centre. Montenegro already has fAKT and the Eko-fond in this file; what it lacked was the page that tells you what is open right now. THE TWO CALLS THAT MATTER MOST, both from the Ministry of Ecology, Sustainable Development and Development of the North: a javni konkurs distributing funds to non-governmental organisations for protected species of the Natura 2000 network, and a javni konkurs distributing funds to non-governmental organisations for the protection of Montenegro's breeding birds. The deadline for applications to these calls is 30 days from the day of publication, which is short — watch the page rather than waiting to hear. AND MUNICIPALITIES RUN THEIR OWN: the page also carries municipal calls, such as Danilovgrad's annual public competition for the distribution of funds to non-governmental organisations, again with a 30-day window. Your own municipality may fund you to oppose what another arm of it is permitting, and in a country of this size the municipal call may be the least contested money available. WHO MAY APPLY, from the national co-financing rules: non-governmental organisations registered and operating in Montenegro, with projects carried out wholly or partly in Montenegro, either as project holder or as partner in implementation. Registration in the Register of Non-Governmental Associations must be completed within 20 days of a proper and complete application — so an unincorporated group can become eligible quickly. IT ALSO CARRIES CIVIL-SOCIETY CALLS ISSUED BY NGOs THEMSELVES, including a public call issued jointly by MANS — already filed here as Montenegro's permit investigator — and another association.

trackers.name: Montenegro's studija zaštite — the municipality can pay for it and its assembly can declare
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE, AND IT IS UNUSUALLY OPEN TO A LOCAL COMMUNITY: under Montenegro's Zakon o zaštiti prirode the declaration procedure runs on a studija zaštite — a protection study — produced by a legal person, and the funds for producing it are secured in the budget of Montenegro OR in the budget of the unit of local self-government. Your own municipality can lawfully pay for the study that protects your ground. Across the four designation countries in this file, this is the clearest statement that the bottleneck document has a local funding route. WHAT THE STUDY MUST CONTAIN, so a community knows what it is commissioning: a description of the natural, created and landscape features; the characteristics and values of the locality; the existing state of resources with an assessment of their valorisation; an evaluation of the state of the area; an opinion on placing the natural good under protection; and a proposal for the category and the significance ranking. AND A WORKED LOCAL EXAMPLE: for the upper course of the Ćehotina, the study records that after the procedure under article 34(3), the Assembly of the Municipality of Pljevlja will, having first obtained the consent of the Ministry and the opinion of the state bodies responsible for agriculture, forestry, water management and culture, adopt the decision proclaiming the Nature Park. The municipal assembly declares; the ministry consents. That is two doors, both nameable. WHO ELSE IS IN THE PROCESS: the Agencija za zaštitu životne sredine prepares protection studies for declaring protected natural goods, issues acts of preventive protection, prepares the Red Book of threatened wild species, and monitors wild bird populations; for marine areas it works with the Institut za biologiju mora. THE MOMENT TO ACT IN: on 26 June the government adopted a draft plan for the national Natura 2000 network and submitted it to Brussels — 97 areas proposed by the Agency, covering 7,040 square kilometres of land and 179 of sea, close to half the country's land area, including the Ulcinj salina and the Bojana-Buna delta. If your site is inside a proposed Natura 2000 area, say so now.

trackers.name: Advokatska komora Crne Gore — the imenik advokata, and the fee tariff behind it
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Montenegrin Bar, Bratstva i jedinstva 7, Podgorica, open Monday to Friday 9–15, +382 20 602 805 / 602 807, advkomora@t-com.me. It keeps the imenik advokata — the roll of advocates — and is obliged to supply courts and other bodies with the list of advocates entered on it, so that in civil, non-contentious, enforcement, administrative and other proceedings they provide expert and effective legal help to parties. Montenegro's bucket had MANS, which investigates permits and files criminal complaints, and nothing that leads to a private lawyer; this does. TWO THINGS ON IT A COMMUNITY CAN USE: the Bar sets the advokatska tarifa — the fee scale — so what a lawyer may charge is published rather than guessed; and it operates disciplinary organs, with penalties running from a warning and fine to temporary or permanent deletion from the roll. A lawyer who takes your money and does nothing is answerable to a named body. AND A CROSS-BORDER POINT WORTH KNOWING IN THE BALKANS: under the treaty on legal assistance between Montenegro and Serbia, advocates entered on the roll in one contracting state may represent parties in proceedings before the courts and other competent bodies of the other; the Montenegrin Bar links directly to the bars of Serbia, Bosnia, Macedonia, Slovenia and Croatia. A community may be able to instruct a specialist from a neighbouring country.

trackers.name: Advokatska kancelarija Duraković — runs upravni spor over urbanistic consents and building permits
trackers.desc: WHY THIS ONE: most Montenegrin practices list administrative disputes generically. This office in Bar names the planning steps specifically. Its stated work includes, in upravni sporovi — administrative disputes — legal advice, filing and representing claims or answering them, and representation before the court; and initiating administrative proceedings for the purpose of obtaining URBANISTIC CONSENTS, the issue of BUILDING PERMITS, and the legalisation of unlawfully built structures. AND THE PART THAT MATTERS AFTER A LOSS: within those proceedings and disputes it files ordinary and EXTRAORDINARY legal remedies for clients. Extraordinary remedies are what remain when the ordinary appeal is exhausted, and few firms in this file name them. It also handles property transactions — sale and purchase, gift, lease, brokerage — which is the same practice a community needs if the answer turns out to be buying the ground.

trackers.name: CZIP — it wrote the draft protection study the state then adopted
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: the Centar za zaštitu i proučavanje ptica, a non-party, non-governmental and non-profit organisation founded on 5 January 2001 by professional ornithologists from the state institute for nature protection, the Natural History Museum and the national parks enterprise, together with biology students. Its mission is protection of birds and their habitats, biodiversity monitoring of Montenegro, citizen education and cooperation with organisations at home and abroad. WHAT IT DID THAT A COMMUNITY SHOULD COPY: CZIP and EuroNatur drew up a PROPOSED DRAFT OF THE PROTECTION STUDY for the Ulcinj salina, and after revision it was ADOPTED BY THE ENVIRONMENT PROTECTION AGENCY. The NGOs wrote the state's own designation document. This file has recorded the expert study as the bottleneck in eleven countries; here the campaigners produced it and the agency took it. AND THE REST OF THE MACHINERY THEY BUILT AROUND IT: CZIP, BirdLife International, EuroNatur and a named association helped gather over 100,000 signatures for the petition to declare the salina protected; CZIP ran an ecosystem services assessment from 2018 using BirdLife's TESSA methodology, funded by a foundation, to give an additional argument for why the area should be protected; and the EU Delegation approved 300,000 euro for a cost-benefit assessment of salt production to fill the economic analysis the study lacked. THE RESULT AND THE LEVER: the salina was declared a Park prirode. It was the only locality whose urgent protection was demanded in the European Commission's annual progress reports on Montenegro for 2015, 2016, 2017 and 2018, confirmed in European Parliament resolutions, and became a closing benchmark for Chapter 27 in Montenegro's EU negotiations. In an accession country, getting your site named in the Commission's progress report is the strongest lever available.

trackers.name: JPNPCG — the public enterprise that holds and runs Montenegro's national parks
trackers.desc: WHO HOLDS THE GROUND: the Public Enterprise for National Parks of Montenegro, Trg vojvode Bećir-bega Osmanagića 16, Podgorica — a member since 2013 of IUCN, the world's largest network of nature conservation organisations and experts. Montenegro had no land-holding body filed; as in Moldova, North Macedonia, Albania and Kosovo, the holder is a public body, and this is it. WHAT THE PARKS ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR, and therefore what you can ask of them: protection and management, the preparation and implementation of protection programmes, CONTROL OF THE USE OF NATURAL RESOURCES, establishing internal rules, and promotion. Each park is characterised by specific natural and cultural heritage and has not only national but international significance. Control of the use of natural resources is a named duty — so a report of unauthorised use inside a park has an addressee with a statutory obligation to act. AND WHO ELSE SITS AROUND THE TABLE, from a national biodiversity project's management commission: the spatial planning and environment ministry, UNDP, the agriculture and forestry ministry, the director of the national parks enterprise, the director of the Republic Institute for Nature Protection, and — as observers — representatives of three named NGOs. Observer seats for named NGOs on a state project commission are worth asking for.

trackers.name: Ekološki pokret OZON — it advertises for law firms willing to represent citizens FOR FREE
trackers.desc: THE PUBLIC CALL, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE OF ITS KIND IN THIS FILE: the movement invites LAW OFFICES FROM MONTENEGRO that are interested in REPRESENTING CITIZENS AND NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS FREE OF CHARGE, in the struggle to realise the rights guaranteed to them, to enter into partnership with it. An environmental organisation that recruits pro bono lawyers on an open call, and publishes that call, is a standing legal resource a Montenegrin community can approach — rather than hunting for a sympathetic firm alone. WHO THEY ARE: founded on 16 September 2006 — the international day for the protection of the ozone layer — and entered in the register of non-governmental associations, with the stated mission of contributing to increased PUBLIC PARTICIPATION IN DECISION-MAKING, through constant education about the importance of a preserved environment, and SUPPORT FOR ALL INITIATIVES whose aim is a substantial improvement in the overall state of the environment. AND ITS RECORD OF DOING EXACTLY THAT: it took on a public role in environmental impact assessment — its first case being the assessment for the construction of a named wind power plant — and describes mass participation in public procedures as the essential mechanism for protecting the public interest, and something that reduces the space for manipulation of the public, corruption or abuse of official position.

trackers.name: Ozelenimo Crnu Goru — it cleans the riverbank, then puts up the cameras and the signs
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DID, and it is a method a village can copy in a weekend: the organisation ran a riverbank clean-up action TOGETHER WITH PARTNERS FROM THE CIVIL SECTOR AND WITH THE HELP OF THE MUNICIPAL CLEANING COMPANY, covering the ground around the city dump and along the river. AND THE PART THAT MAKES IT STICK, which most clean-ups skip: we realised that the riverbank and several scrapyards nearby are a source of pollution, and that we must resolve this situation — so the action will continue, PARK FURNITURE IS PLANNED, and TO PREVENT ILLEGAL DUMPING HAPPENING AGAIN AT THIS LOCATION, CAMERAS AND WARNING SIGNS WILL BE INSTALLED. Clearing a site without occupying it invites the tipping back; furniture, cameras and signs are what convert a clean-up into possession. AND THE FRAMING IT USED PUBLICLY, which is worth borrowing in any accession country: the capital city should have clean rivers, especially when we are speaking of the capital of a FUTURE MEMBER OF THE EUROPEAN UNION. The action was reported through the EU delegation's own channel — a local clean-up documented by an international mission is harder for a council to ignore.

trackers.name: Agencija za upravljanje zaštićenim područjima Podgorice — the CITY's own agency, with a named director
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: an agency formed with the aim of preserving and effectively managing the protected areas ON THE TERRITORY OF THE CAPITAL CITY, which are distinguished by richness of biological diversity, endemic plant and animal species and characteristic ecosystems. Montenegro's bucket held the pro bono recruiter and the clean-up model; this is the body that actually holds municipal ground. AND THE AIM IT PUBLISHES, which a resident can hold it to: our goal is to protect, improve and preserve the protected areas on the territory of the Capital City, TO ESTABLISH GOOD COOPERATION WITH THE LOCAL COMMUNITY AND THE CIVIL SECTOR, and to work on education and strengthening the awareness of people and institutions. It will pay special attention to HARMONISING HUMAN ACTIVITY, ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL DEVELOPMENT PLANS, PROGRAMMES AND PROJECTS WITH THE DETERMINED DEGREE OF PROTECTION. An agency whose own stated job is checking development plans against the protection level is the first body to write to about a scheme inside a protected area. AND HOW IT WORKS WITH PEOPLE: when a city assembly proclaimed a new natural monument, the agency took over its management; it convened a workshop with partners from Albania and Kosovo and representatives of Montenegrin environmental NGOs; and it ran a large spring volunteer action clearing burnt plant waste, thanking named participating schools. Its acting executive director and street address are published.

trackers.name: EPA Montenegro — a department for NATURE PROTECTION with its own direct phone numbers
trackers.desc: WHY THIS IS A RESOURCE RATHER THAN A LISTING: the environmental protection agency publishes a named director, a street address in the capital, an email address, AND SEPARATE DIRECT TELEPHONE NUMBERS FOR EACH SECTOR — including the SECTOR FOR ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING (five numbers), the SECTOR FOR NATURE PROTECTION, the sector for project management and information support, and the department for implementing ECONOMIC INSTRUMENTS in environmental protection. A direct number for the nature protection sector saves a community weeks of being passed around a switchboard, and the monitoring sector is where the measurements behind any objection live. WHAT THE BODY IS: established in 2008 by decree, it cooperates with international bodies and organisations of other countries that deal with environmental protection, and is a member of the International Union for Conservation of Nature — which means a community's complaint to it sits inside an international framework rather than a purely national one. It also holds a department for radiological and nuclear safety and protection from ionising and non-ionising radiation, with its own mobile number, and a service for general and legal affairs.

trackers.name: CZIP — it got two wetlands protected, and it publishes two phone numbers for volunteers
trackers.desc: WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY WON, year by year, which is the record a Montenegrin community should read first: the proclamation of a named salt marsh as a SPECIAL FLORISTIC-FAUNISTIC NATURE RESERVE; participation with two other named organisations in a joint campaign against the construction of FOUR DAMS on a named river — and although the public forced the investor to withdraw, the Government is still looking for new ones; a joint campaign against the intention of government officials to recognise a protected salt-pan area IN THE SPATIAL PLANNING DOCUMENTATION AS BUILDING LAND; and the entry of the salt marsh on the RAMSAR LIST of wetlands of international importance. An organisation that has already stopped a rezoning from protected area to building land is the one to call when the same is proposed near you. Montenegro had two land-holding bodies filed. WHO THEY ARE AND HOW TO REACH THEM: a non-party, non-governmental and non-profit organisation founded in December 2000 BY PROFESSIONAL ORNITHOLOGISTS OF THE REPUBLIC INSTITUTE FOR NATURE PROTECTION, THE NATURAL HISTORY MUSEUM, THE PUBLIC ENTERPRISE NATIONAL PARKS, AND STUDENTS of the biology faculty — with a street address in Podgorica, TWO TELEPHONE NUMBERS AND TWO EMAIL ADDRESSES published. It is an IUCN member and won a national environmental award.

trackers.name: The Ulcinj salt pan — a company declared its own land the country's FIRST PRIVATE NATURE PARK
trackers.desc: THE PRECEDENT, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE OF ITS KIND IN THIS FILE: in 2004 THE MANAGEMENT OF THE SALTWORKS DECLARED THE SALT PAN THE FIRST PRIVATE NATURE PARK, and formed a working unit — the Nature Park — to run it. A landowner declaring its own ground a private nature park, and staffing it, is a route open to any owner who wants the land kept, and it is recorded here as done rather than proposed. HOW THE PROTECTION WAS BUILT UP BEFORE THAT, each step a separate lever: the first act of protection came in 1984, when a decision of the workers' council PROHIBITED ALL HUNTING; a few years later the site became the FIRST AREA OF INTERNATIONAL IMPORTANCE FOR BIRDS in Montenegro, and then an EMERALD site of the Bern Convention. AND THE FUNDING ROUTE NAMED ON THE SAME PAGE: a fund that provides means TO NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS AND PRIVATE ENTERPRISES for the protection of biodiversity in the biologically richest and most threatened areas. A fund that will pay a private company to protect its own land is the missing half of the private-park model — and the bird organisation has run regular bird monitoring on a neighbouring reserve since 2009, with that site counted in the International Waterbird Census, the oldest bird monitoring in the world.

trackers.name: The Kotor area law — a PUBLIC DATABASE the council must keep, and an annual report to government
trackers.desc: WHAT THIS LAW SETS UP, and it is a template a community elsewhere can point to: a dedicated statute regulating the protection, management and SPECIAL MEASURES OF CONSERVATION of a named natural and cultural-historical area, adopted by parliament in 2013. AND THE TWO OBLIGATIONS WORTH KNOWING. First, the database: legal and natural persons are OBLIGED to submit to the local administration body the data and documents needed for maintaining the database, and that database is used for the work of the Council AND IS AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC. A statutory database that developers must feed and the public may read is a permanent source of evidence about what is happening in a protected area. SECOND, THE ANNUAL REPORT: the Council is obliged, BY 1 MARCH each year, to submit to the Government an annual report on implementation of the Management Plan and the state of the Area, containing an analysis of the dynamics and effects of implementing the Management Plan; AN ASSESSMENT OF THE STATE OF THE AREA; the activities carried out on conservation, maintenance and MONITORING; an analysis and assessment of the conditions for achieving the aims of protection; and THE PROTECTION MEASURES CARRIED OUT and the ways they were implemented. A dated annual report on whether protection is actually working is a document to request, read, and quote back.

trackers.name: Društvo prirodnjaka Crne Gore — the naturalists' society, and how it describes itself
trackers.desc: A NAMED MONTENEGRIN NATURALISTS' BODY, filed for what it is: a NON-GOVERNMENTAL, NON-PROFIT AND NON-PARTY organisation of FREELY AND VOLUNTARILY ASSOCIATED MEMBERS, which rests on the PRINCIPLES OF EQUALITY AND MUTUALITY, and acts on the basis of the Constitution and the law. Montenegro is joint-smallest bucket in this file. A standing naturalists' society is where the species records and the local field knowledge sit — the material a community needs when it must show what a site holds and has no survey of its own. Montenegro's own Nature Protection Act names NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS among the SUBJECTS OF NATURE PROTECTION alongside state and local authorities, and provides that THE STATE ENCOURAGES THE PARTICIPATION OF NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS IN THE ADOPTION AND REALISATION OF DECISIONS AND MEASURES of significance for protection. An NGO is a named subject of nature protection in the statute, not a bystander to it. HONEST LIMIT ON THIS ENTRY: the society's own page gives its legal character and its principles but not its projects, staff or current campaigns. It is filed as a CONTACT POINT to approach, not as a documented track record — a community should ask it directly what it holds for their area.

trackers.name: Eko-tim — the Montenegrin NGO that assessed SMALL HYDRO and runs a river-protection initiative
trackers.desc: AN ORGANISATION WITH THE EXACT PROJECT-FIGHTING RECORD A MONTENEGRIN RIVER COMMUNITY NEEDS, from its own published project list: ASSESSMENT OF THE CUMULATIVE IMPACTS OF SMALL HYDROELECTRIC PLANTS ON THE ENVIRONMENT AND LOCAL ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT and SMALL HYDROELECTRIC PLANTS AS AN ECOLOGICAL, SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC PROBLEM, both supported by a foreign government. A cumulative-impact assessment is the single document a run-of-river scheme is least able to survive, because each plant is permitted as though it were alone — and this body has already produced one. AND THE LIVE CAMPAIGN, named with its start date: the INITIATIVE FOR THE PROTECTION OF THE RIVER MRTVICA AND THE UPPER COURSE OF THE RIVER MORACA, on which activities began in JUNE 2022, with the general aim of PROTECTING those rivers IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE RELEVANT LEGAL FRAMEWORK. AND THE BACKERS BEHIND IT, which tell a community what weight it carries: PERMANENT PROTECTION OF THE RIVERS OF SOUTH-EASTERN EUROPE, SUPPORTED BY WWF ADRIA AND THE NATURE CONSERVANCY; work supported by THE EUROPEAN CLIMATE FUND; and MONITORING OF PUBLIC PROCUREMENT IN THE FIELD OF THE ENVIRONMENT under a regional tender-watch project. An NGO that watches environmental procurement can see a project's contracts before the diggers arrive.

trackers.name: EXPEDITIO — a centre for SUSTAINABLE SPATIAL DEVELOPMENT, which is the planning fight itself
trackers.desc: AN ORGANISATION WHOSE WHOLE SUBJECT IS HOW LAND GETS BUILT ON: EXPEDITIO is a NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATION whose mission is ENCOURAGING SUSTAINABLE SPATIAL DEVELOPMENT IN MONTENEGRO AND THE REGION OF SOUTH-EASTERN EUROPE through action in the field of sustainable architecture and related areas. Spatial development is the formal name for the decision a community is usually fighting — and a body that works on it professionally can read a plan a residents' group cannot. AND THE PROJECT THAT MATTERS MOST HERE, run jointly with another named Montenegrin environmental NGO: EKOPlan — MONITORING OF THE APPLICATION OF THE PRINCIPLES OF SUSTAINABLE SPATIAL DEVELOPMENT AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION. A standing monitoring project on whether spatial-planning principles are actually applied is where a community's own case may already be documented. AND THE WIDER WORK IT PUBLISHES: a campaign BUILD ECOLOGICALLY — BUILD WITH NATURE, aimed at acquainting THE WIDER AND THE PROFESSIONAL PUBLIC with different forms of sustainable development in the field of ecological construction; and a STUDY TRIP for 15 REPRESENTATIVES OF THE ADMINISTRATION AND OF ECOLOGICAL NGOs FROM MONTENEGRO. An organisation that takes officials and campaigners on the same trip is one with access to both sides of a planning table.

trackers.name: What Montenegro's free legal aid actually covers — including REPRESENTATION IN COURT
trackers.desc: THE SCOPE OF THE FREE SERVICE, set out from the statute rather than from a brochure: parliament adopted THE LAW ON FREE LEGAL AID, BY WHICH CITIZENS OF WEAKER PROPERTY STANDING ARE SECURED THE RIGHT TO FREE LEGAL AID. THE LAW PROVIDES THAT FREE LEGAL AID COVERS LEGAL ADVICE, THE DRAFTING OF DOCUMENTS, REPRESENTATION IN PROCEEDINGS BEFORE A COURT, THE STATE PROSECUTOR'S OFFICE, THE CONSTITUTIONAL COURT, AS WELL AS IN PROCEEDINGS FOR THE OUT-OF-COURT SETTLEMENT OF DISPUTES. Montenegro is among the least-worked buckets in this file. Representation before the Constitutional Court is inside the free service here — which is a wider grant than the Albanian scheme in batch611, where in practice the offer stops at information and documents. The same words 'free legal aid' cover court representation in one country and only paperwork in its neighbour, so a community must read the statute rather than the label. AND HOW IT IS APPLIED FOR: THE REQUEST IS SUBMITTED TO THE COMPETENT BODY THROUGH THE SERVICE, ON A PRESCRIBED FORM, and legal advice itself COMPRISES THE PROVISION OF LEGAL INFORMATION AND LEGAL COUNSEL.

trackers.name: Who actually qualifies — the five eligible categories, and the portability rule
