THE DEAL FORMS THEY OFFER, EACH NAMED, AND WORTH KNOWING BY NAME BEFORE ANYONE PROPOSES ONE TO YOU: AN EASEMENTS FOR EDUCATION PROGRAM; SIX SCHOOLS REBUILT IN RETURN FOR COMMUNITIES' CONSERVATION COMMITMENTS; PAYMENT FOR ECOSYSTEM SERVICES; COMMUNITY SCOUTS; LAND USE PLANNING AND ZONING; COMMUNITY CONFLICT RESOLUTION; TOURISM PLANS AND CONCESSION GUIDELINES; AND CONSERVATION ENTERPRISE, DEFINED AS A COMMERCIAL ACTIVITY THAT GENERATES ECONOMIC BENEFITS THAT SUPPORT CONSERVATION AND COMMUNITIES. A SCHOOL IN RETURN FOR A CONSERVATION COMMITMENT is the trade being offered, and six have been built. That can be a good bargain — but read what the commitment binds, for how long, and what happens to the school if the community later wants the land back. An easement is a permanent restriction on your own land; the building is not. AND IT WORKS AT STATE LEVEL TOO: IT PILOTED THREE CONSERVANCIES WITH A NATIONAL WILDLIFE AUTHORITY AROUND THREE NAMED NATIONAL PARKS, WHICH BECAME THAT COUNTRY'S FIRST DESIGNATED CONSERVANCIES — and it initiates PAN-AFRICAN LEADERSHIP PLATFORMS FOR CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS AND PROTECTED-AREA AGENCIES AND LINKS THEM INTO GLOBAL AND REGIONAL POLICY PROCESSES. NOW THE RECORD, WHICH THIS FILE OWES ANY COMMUNITY BEING APPROACHED: IN NOVEMBER 2011 TWO CONSERVATION ORGANISATIONS PAID US$2 MILLION EACH TO BUY AN AREA OF 6,920 HECTARES FROM A FORMER HEAD OF STATE, AND GAVE IT TO THE GOVERNMENT TO CREATE A PROPOSED NATIONAL PARK. TWO MILLION DOLLARS EACH, PAID TO A FORMER PRESIDENT. That is the price of seven thousand hectares in that market, and it tells you what conservation money can move when it wants to. It is also the number to hold up when you are told there is no money to buy land your community needs. AND WHAT HAPPENED TO THE PEOPLE: A TELEVISION DOCUMENTARY BROADCAST THAT YEAR DOCUMENTED THE VIOLENCE BEHIND THE CREATION OF THE PARK. THE INDIGENOUS PEOPLE WHO LIVED IN THE AREA WERE SUBJECTED TO A SERIES OF BRUTAL EVICTIONS, AND TOLD THE JOURNALIST THAT POLICE BEAT PEOPLE, TOOK THEIR PROPERTY AND BURNT VILLAGES. NONE OF THESE PEOPLE WERE MENTIONED IN THE PRESS RELEASE ABOUT THE HANDOVER CEREMONY. The purchase was lawful, the transfer was ceremonial, and the residents appear nowhere in the announcement. That is the shape to watch for: land can be bought over your heads from someone who holds paper title while your claim is customary and unregistered. This file's LandMark entry names the same mechanism — unmapped land reads as empty — and its mapping entries are the answer. AND THE ESCALATION THAT FOLLOWED: AN INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATION WROTE TO A UN COMMITTEE ON THE ELIMINATION OF RACIAL DISCRIMINATION ABOUT THE GRAVE SITUATION CONFRONTING THE COMMUNITY, NOTING THAT POLICE HARASSMENT CONTINUED. A UN treaty committee received a written submission about an eviction from a conservation purchase. That route exists and it does not require a lawyer in-country — an organisation abroad can file it. Know that before the bulldozers, not after. THE PRACTICAL RULE THIS PRODUCES, AND IT IS THE POINT OF FILING BOTH HALVES: when a conservation organisation offers to buy land near you, ask four things in writing — WHO IS SELLING AND ON WHAT TITLE; WHO IS RECORDED AS LIVING OR GRAZING THERE; WHO WILL HOLD THE LAND AFTERWARDS; AND WHAT HAPPENS TO RESIDENTS IF THE STATE DECLARES A PARK. Those four questions are answerable before signing and unanswerable afterwards. OTHER NAMED BODIES IN THE SAME FIELD, FOR COMPARISON: an organisation founded in 2000 using a PUBLIC-PRIVATE-PARTNERSHIP APPROACH TO MANAGING PROTECTED AREAS; a community-driven conservation organisation founded in 2005; a foundation REGISTERED IN NIGERIA LED BY EXPERIENCED AFRICANS which CO-MANAGES A NAMED NATIONAL PARK AND IS COMMENCING A SECOND PROJECT IN ANOTHER, AND AIMS TO ATTRACT AFRICAN CAPITAL INTO THE SECTOR; and an international foundation established 1999 working in named African countries which BUILDS IN-COUNTRY CAPACITY BY PROVIDING TECHNICAL AND FUNDRAISING SUPPORT TO LOCAL PARTNERS. FUNDRAISING SUPPORT TO LOCAL PARTNERS is the offer to ask that last one for — help raising money in your own organisation's name rather than money spent on your behalf. And a conservation foundation led by Africans and registered in an African country is a different counterparty from a foreign one; ask where the organisation is registered and who sits on its board. WHO IT SUITS: African communities offered a conservation deal, easement or land purchase, and those seeking a buyer for land under threat. CAVEATS: THE EVICTION RECORD ABOVE IS THE CAVEAT, and it is filed here rather than buried. For the fund that grants toward buying land in perpetuity, South Africa's World Land Trust entry; for the eviction case filed alongside it, that entry's caution; for the mechanism a community can invoke against a protected area, Tanzania's Whakatane entry; for the platform showing concessions over community land, Mali's LandMark entry.

trackers.name: Public interest litigation to protect Nairobi's public open spaces (EALJ)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a University of Nairobi East African Law Journal study of how public interest litigation has been used to defend public open spaces in Nairobi, written around the actual filings rather than the theory. It walks through Green Belt Movement and 4 others v NEMA and China Road and Bridge Corporation, filed at the National Environment Tribunal on 2 June 2020, whose grounds are the template for a city open-space challenge: an EIA licence issued without adequate public participation as required by law, without a proper Strategic Environmental Assessment, and where the proponent omitted substantial information. It also covers a private-title dispute over land in Jamhuri estate arising from allocations by the former Nairobi City Council. USE IT: these three grounds — participation, missing SEA, incomplete information — are what a Nairobi filing is built on.

trackers.name: County planning appeal — and the exhaustion trap
trackers.desc: WHERE A KENYAN DEVELOPMENT IS ACTUALLY DECIDED, AND HOW TO CHALLENGE IT. Under the Physical and Land Use Planning Act No. 13 of 2019, an applicant or interested party aggrieved by a County Executive Committee decision on an application for development permission may appeal to the County Physical and Land Use Planning Liaison Committee — and ‘interested party’ is the phrase that lets a neighbour or community group in, not only the developer. OBJECT EARLIER IF YOU CAN: the Act sets objection points during plan-making — notice and objections to an inter-county plan (s.32), public participation in preparing a county plan (s.40), and notice and objections to a local plan (s.49). Objecting at plan stage is cheaper and earlier than fighting a permission. THE TRAP THAT LOSES CASES: a court has been asked to strike out an entire suit on the ground that it contravened the mandatory provisions of sections 129 and 130(1) of EMCA with Regulation 46 of the EIA and Audit Regulations 2003, because the plaintiffs went to court without first taking the grievance to the National Environment Tribunal — the court lacking original jurisdiction and its jurisdiction being invoked prematurely. USE THE LADDER IN ORDER: object at plan stage, then the County Liaison Committee, then the NET, and only then the Environment and Land Court. Going straight to court can lose you the case on jurisdiction with no hearing on the merits.

trackers.name: County Environment Committee — and complaints against NEMA itself
trackers.desc: TWO COUNTY-LEVEL LEVERS UNDER EMCA (Cap 387). Every County Environment Committee preparing a county environment plan must undertake public participation, and must take account of other county plans already adopted so they stay consistent; those plans go to the Cabinet Secretary for incorporation into the national environment action plan. That is a statutory hearing you are entitled to, before permissions are ever issued. AND WHEN THE REGULATOR IS THE PROBLEM: the National Environmental Complaints Committee investigates allegations or complaints against any person or against NEMA itself in relation to the condition of the environment in Kenya — the route when your objection is that the authority failed to act, rather than that a company did something.

trackers.name: NLAS — free lawyer, land disputes and public interest included
trackers.desc: THE FREE LAWYER FOR THE LADDER. NLAS is a body corporate under the Legal Aid Act 2016, in the Office of the Attorney General. WHAT IT COVERS MATTERS HERE: under section 35(2) its civil work expressly includes land disputes, and it covers constitutional matters involving violation of fundamental rights and matters of public interest that affect the rights of communities or groups — so a community land or environmental case sits inside the mandate, not at its edge. WHO QUALIFIES: Kenyan citizens, refugees under the Refugees Act, victims of human trafficking, internally displaced and stateless persons, and children needing representation. APPLY on form NLAS1, prescribed in the first schedule to the Legal Aid (General) Regulations 2020; bring national ID, your case documents, and proof of income — or a sworn affidavit if you have none. THE COVERAGE GAP, PLAINLY: although the service is described as available across all 47 counties, physical offices are in only 5 — Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu, Nakuru, Eldoret — with more planned for Lamu, Mandera, Wajir, Garissa, Isiolo, Marsabit and Tana River. Elsewhere use the toll-free line 0800 720 640, email the nearest county office, or catch a community legal aid clinic. AND NOTE: the Service may grant partial legal aid on condition you contribute financially to the fund. OTHER ROUTES: Kituo Cha Sheria, whose M-Haki platform gives legal advice by mobile phone, FIDA Kenya, and the Law Society of Kenya pro bono programme.

trackers.name: Oxpeckers (investigative outlet)
trackers.desc: Independent accountability-journalism outlet (GIJN member); Oxpeckers — South African environmental-crime investigations.

trackers.name: Centre for Environmental Rights (CER) — strategic environmental litigation
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: South Africa's leading public-interest environmental law organisation — runs strategic litigation and supports community groups, with a record of judgments against coal and industrial projects. WHO IT SUITS: be realistic — they take on only a limited number of strategically selected cases capable of systemic change, so a single local application may not qualify. Their legal-services page carries self-help steps, including the environmental complaints hotline, for matters they cannot take. DO YOU QUALIFY? THERE ARE TWO FILTERS. Under Law Society requirements CER will only consider cases where the person or organisation is unable to afford private environmental attorneys, or unable reasonably to access the resources to engage them — the second applying particularly to non-public-interest organisations. Separately, the Centre takes on only a limited number of strategically selected cases, so passing the means test is not enough and CER should not be your only plan. USE THIS EVEN IF THEY DECLINE YOU: CER records that departments have committed to releasing documents automatically, by email, without a formal access-to-information request — from the environment department, environmental authorisations, waste management licences, atmospheric emission licences and Biodiversity Act permits for named facilities; from water and sanitation, water use licence applications, water use licences, and audit and compliance reports. That is 7 document categories obtainable without a lawyer and without a PAIA application. Current named officials are on CER's page; where a document is not automatically available, a formal PAIA request can be made and the South African History Archive publishes a guide to preparing one.

trackers.name: Environmental Justice Fund (South Africa)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a movement-driven, feminist NGO funding environmental and climate justice organisations in South Africa. WHO IT SUITS: South African community and environmental-justice groups looking for domestic rather than foreign funding. NOTE: canonical domain not yet verified; named as a grantmaking partner on greengrants.org. READ THE ELIGIBILITY RULES FIRST — they are the point of this fund. EJF does not consider applications from established NGOs: it exists because most funding goes to established NGOs while community-based organisations cannot reach money directly. Decisively for small groups, you do not need to be formally registered to apply. It does not fund companies, other profit-making entities or state bodies including municipalities. Grants run R50,000–R100,000 over 6 months to 1 year, with capacity-strengthening and networking support alongside the money. Your proposal must make the link to environmental justice explicit — the fund's own example is that distributing food parcels would probably not qualify, while establishing a community food garden with training in organic farming and permaculture would. It is a fund by activists, for activists, using participatory grant-making in which decisions are taken by activists from the sector rather than philanthropic gatekeepers, founded jointly by groundWork, Earthlife Africa, the Centre for Environmental Rights, WoMin, the Vaal Environmental Justice Alliance, the South Durban Community Environmental Alliance, the Benchmarks Foundation, Women on Farms and the Mining & Environmental Justice Community Network of South Africa. It currently supports 35 community-based organisations.

trackers.name: Natural Justice: Lawyers for Communities and the Environment
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an African public-interest law organisation — lawyers and paralegals working with communities facing mining, oil and gas, logging and large infrastructure, combining legal empowerment, community protocols, policy work and litigation. Hubs in Cape Town, Nairobi and Dakar, staff in Madagascar, Botswana and Guinea, and country programmes in Burkina Faso, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Namibia, Nigeria, Senegal and South Africa. It also runs the Environmental Lawyers Collective for Africa and an EIA Process Tracker. WHO IT SUITS: an Indigenous or rural community whose land, water or customary rights are threatened by an extractive or infrastructure project. It takes selected cases and works project-to-project outside its programme countries, so expect an approach-and-assess conversation rather than open intake. IS THERE AN OFFICE NEAR YOU? YES — Cape Town (headquarters and hub). Natural Justice keeps 3 hubs: Cape Town, Nairobi and Dakar. A hub means staff on the ground rather than a project relationship. WHAT IT DOES: founded 2007 in Cape Town, it supports communities to know the law, use the law and shape the law — access to land and governance of natural resources, the struggle against harmful extractive and infrastructure developments, traditional knowledge and benefit sharing, community rights within conservation, and climate action. ITS SIGNATURE TOOL IS THE COMMUNITY PROTOCOL — a documented instrument letting a community set out its biological, cultural and spiritual resources, norms and values, and assert existing rights under customary, domestic and international law, aimed squarely at laws and projects developed by government and industry without consultation. Ask for it by name. Contact: 63 Hout Street, Cape Town 8001; +27 21 426 1633; info@naturaljustice.org.

trackers.name: African Environmental Defenders Fund (emergency grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the African Environmental Defenders Fund — an emergency grant fund run by Natural Justice with the International Land Coalition Africa, ICCA Consortium, PACJA, Oxfam Novib, FEMNET and others, giving up to US$5,000 to land and environmental defenders anywhere in Africa who are under threat because of their activism. It can cover the cost of legal representation where a defender is arrested, summoned or prosecuted, plus relocation and other short-term transitional costs. WHO IT SUITS: an individual frontline defender who is a citizen or legal resident of an African country, facing an imminent threat, and not already supported by another body — it is not project or core funding, and routine office and administrative costs are excluded. HOW IT DIFFERS: applications are rolling, by email or helpline, not to a grant round. Natural Justice's own site names Burkina Faso, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Namibia, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa and Botswana as its country programmes, which is where this entry is placed; the fund's stated eligibility is any African country, so apply from elsewhere on the continent too.

trackers.name: Southern Africa Litigation Centre (SALC)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional litigation centre supporting and co-counselling cases across Angola, Botswana, DR Congo, Eswatini, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe. Its socio-economic rights work challenges large-scale agricultural and extractive land use that dispossesses customary landholders without adequate consent, consultation or compensation, and covers mining, pollution and climate justice — live matters include a Zambian community's pollution claim against copper processors and San and Bayei claims to ancestral land in Botswana. WHO IT SUITS: in-country lawyers and community organisations who need a partner with regional capacity and resources; SALC generally works through local counsel and partners rather than taking clients directly. SALC RESOURCES A LAWYER — IT DOES NOT REPLACE ONE. It provides technical and monetary support to local and regional lawyers and organisations litigating human rights and rule of law cases, working primarily through strategic litigation and capacity-strengthening support to lawyers and grassroots organisations. So the ask is not ‘please take my case’ but ‘please back my lawyer’ — come with a local lawyer or local organisation. It also trains human rights lawyers and facilitates networks across the region, so it is a route to finding counsel too. THE SECOND FORUM MOST PEOPLE MISS: SALC supports litigation in South African courts that advances human rights in the southern African region — so where your own courts are slow, captured or hostile, there may be another venue, and SALC is the body that supports using it. NAME THE RIGHT CLUSTER WHEN YOU APPROACH: its themes are criminal justice, civil and political rights, socio-economic rights, international criminal justice, business and human rights and equality rights — ‘environment’ is not one of them, so frame a land-defence case as business and human rights or socio-economic rights. Established 2005 in Johannesburg out of the International Bar Association and OSISA. It has also run open calls for small organisational development grants to emerging CBOs in Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe — periodic, so watch for them.

trackers.name: Legal Resources Centre (LRC)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: South Africa's largest public-interest law centre. Its Land and Natural Resources work litigates for rural communities, small-scale fishers and farmers on access to land, mining and extractive projects, customary governance and, increasingly, environmental and climate justice, alongside a long housing-and-evictions practice. Offices in Johannesburg (with the Constitutional Litigation Unit), Cape Town, Durban and Makhanda. WHO IT SUITS: a community or a class of vulnerable clients rather than an individual dispute — the LRC is client-based but works on a strategic-impact model and selects matters through its focus areas, so approach the nearest office with a community-level problem.

trackers.name: SANBI — Biodiversity Stewardship
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: explains South Africa's biodiversity stewardship system — the route by which private and communal landowners enter agreements with a provincial conservation authority to protect land in a biodiversity priority area. Several of the agreement types are formally declared as protected areas under the Protected Areas Act 57 of 2003, which gives long-term legal security to the site, and since 2016 a landowner declaring a Nature Reserve or National Park can deduct 4% of the land value from taxable income each year for 25 years (per UNDP South Africa). USE IT: to find out which agreement type gives real statutory protection rather than a non-binding partnership, before approaching your provincial authority about land you are trying to keep out of development.

trackers.name: Conservation Outcomes
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a KwaZulu-Natal-based non-profit that walks private and communal landowners through biodiversity stewardship — planning, establishment and governance of conservation areas, the declaration process itself, and the post-declaration management support that declaration alone does not provide: annual plans of operation, veld and fire management, alien species control, and help applying for the tax deduction and rates exemptions. It also develops tourism, ethical hunting and natural-resource ventures so protected land can pay for itself. USE IT: when you have land worth protecting but need someone who has done the declaration paperwork before.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a pan-African feminist rapid-response fund with reach across all 54 African countries — small grants released quickly for unanticipated, time-critical situations rather than planned programme work, covering safety and protection needs when defenders are threatened and short windows for advocacy after an unexpected event. WHO IT SUITS: women's rights organisations, feminist collectives and movements in which women or gender-diverse people are the primary decision-makers. It does NOT fund individuals, and the action must be strategic, genuinely unanticipated, and completable in under three months. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is emergency money for a moment, not a budget for a campaign — decisions are fast and grants are modest.

trackers.name: amaBhungane
trackers.desc: South African nonprofit investigative newsroom exposing state capture, corruption and money laundering, and litigating for transparency.

trackers.name: Information Regulator (South Africa)
trackers.desc: South Africa's independent regulator enforcing access to information (PAIA) and data protection (POPIA). — Holds to account: public bodies that hold records — find information-commissioner decisions and appeals.

trackers.name: Legal Aid South Africa
trackers.desc: Statutory body providing legal representation to those who cannot afford it. · Find here: South Africa's state-funded legal-aid provider (Legal Aid SA). THERE IS A SEPARATE, HIGHER MEANS THRESHOLD FOR LAND MATTERS — ask for it by name. Legal Aid SA states that if you are employed and applying for legal aid for a land matter, you must earn less than R13,625.00 per month after tax. The ordinary civil threshold is R8,200 per month, or R9,000 where the applicant is a member of a household. A land matter carries a threshold roughly 50–65 percent higher than an ordinary civil one, so someone refused on the general civil figure may still qualify on the land figure. Asset limits: movable not above R151,700, immovable not above R711,700 — check current figures, since the Means Test is revised against CPI (set from 1 April 2023, revised again from 1 April 2025). A REFUSAL IS NOT THE END: appeal first to the Provincial Executive, then to a second level — the Chief Legal Executive in civil matters — and at each stage you may write an additional motivation as to why the appeal must succeed. The National Office Executive's decision is final within Legal Aid SA, so the second appeal closes the internal route. TWO ELIGIBILITY STATEMENTS SIT TOGETHER ON THE RECORD: legal aid is available to anyone who lives in South Africa, not only citizens — but also that in civil cases legal aid is not available to non-citizens. A non-citizen with a civil land matter should establish which governs before relying on the broader statement. Asylum seekers are expressly covered under Chapters 3 and 4 of the Refugees Act 130 of 1998. CALIBRATE YOUR EXPECTATIONS: in 2021/22 it assisted 487,552 people — but only 40,143 new civil matters (11 percent) against 314,998 criminal, alongside advice to 132,411 people. Civil work is about one matter in nine, and advice volumes are growing faster than representation — the same pattern recorded here for Ireland. The Legal Aid Manual (version 7), the Legal Aid Regulations and Government Gazette 44936 of 6 August 2021 are published — bring the Manual's own words to your nearest Justice Centre, with ID and proof of income.

trackers.name: Municipal Money (Treasury)
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in South Africa.

trackers.name: Public Service Accountability Monitor (PSAM)
trackers.desc: Research, training and advocacy institute based at Rhodes University (active since 1999) that monitors public-resource management — budgeting, planning, expenditure and performance — across southern Africa. Here you can trace how public money is budgeted, spent and delivered across southern Africa, tracked through PSAM's social-accountability monitoring.

trackers.name: Master of the High Court Trust BO Register
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Access restricted to authorities/obliged entities.

trackers.name: Vulekamali
trackers.desc: South Africa's online budget data portal. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in South Africa.

trackers.name: Auditor-General South Africa
trackers.desc: Constitutional supreme audit institution. Here you can trace public-audit findings on waste, irregularity and misspending in South Africa.

trackers.name: CIPC
trackers.desc: South Africa's Companies and Intellectual Property Commission register. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Constitutional Court of South Africa
trackers.desc: Official Constitutional Court judgments. · Find here: the judgments of the Constitutional Court of South Africa.

trackers.name: eTenders Portal
trackers.desc: South Africa's national public-tender publication portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in South Africa, and for how much.

trackers.name: Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC)
trackers.desc: South Africa's financial intelligence unit, identifying proceeds of crime and combating money laundering and terrorist financing. Here you can trace how suspicious transactions are reported and money-laundering intelligence is produced in South Africa.

trackers.name: SAFLII
trackers.desc: Southern African Legal Information Institute: free judgments from South African and regional courts. · Find here: free South African and wider Southern-African case-law and legislation (SAFLII).

trackers.name: Special Investigating Unit (SIU)
trackers.desc: National anti-corruption body of South Africa — investigates graft, financial crime and abuse of public office.

trackers.name: Statistics South Africa (Stats SA)
trackers.desc: South Africa's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in South Africa.

trackers.name: Labour Appeal Court of South Africa
trackers.desc: Labour Appeal Court of South Africa — tribunal in South Africa (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Labour Court of South Africa
trackers.desc: Labour Court of South Africa — tribunal in South Africa (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Centre for Applied Legal Studies — the university law centre behind Xolobeni, where a village stopped a titanium mine and won a consent rule
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a human rights organisation based in the Wits law school, founded 1978, that combines research, advocacy and strategic litigation across five programmes including Environmental Justice and Home, Land and Rural Democracy — the two a community facing a mine or a highway needs. WHAT THEY HELPED WIN, AND WHY IT IS THE MOST USEFUL PRECEDENT ON THE CONTINENT: in the Umgungundlovu community's fight at Xolobeni in the Eastern Cape, against an Australian company's titanium mining application, the High Court ruled in 2018 that the state must obtain the community's consent before granting a mining right on their land. CALS then entered a second case as friend of the court and in 2020 the High Court ordered that interested and affected parties are entitled to be furnished with a copy of a mining right application — and ordered the mining company to pay the costs of both the applicants and CALS. Before that ruling, communities had to fight through freedom-of-information requests to learn what was being applied for on their own land. HOW THAT CASE WAS STAFFED, WHICH IS THE MODEL: the community was represented by a private attorney and the Legal Resources Centre, with CALS as amicus and evidence from the Centre for Environmental Rights showing how rarely information requests to the mining department succeed. Four organisations, three roles — counsel, friend of the court, and the researchers who proved the pattern. A community approaching only one of them is asking one body to do all three. WHO IT SUITS: mining-affected and land-affected communities with a systemic question in their case. CAVEATS: CALS is university-based and selects matters for strategic value — no open intake, no published criteria, and in the case above it acted as friend of the court rather than as the community's attorneys. The same community's next fight, over a highway extension across their land, shows the win did not end the pressure.

trackers.name: Biodiversity stewardship, via Conservation Outcomes — put a restriction on your own title deed that survives the sale of the land, and deduct the land's value from tax
trackers.desc: WHAT THIS IS: South Africa's biodiversity stewardship system lets private AND COMMUNAL landowners enter agreements with the provincial conservation authority to have their land declared a protected area under the Protected Areas Act — and the landowner keeps title throughout. Conservation Outcomes is one of the non-governmental organisations that takes communities and landowners through it; it facilitated, for example, the contracts by which seven separate landowners combined their properties into one declared nature reserve. THE TIERS, WHICH DETERMINE HOW HARD THE PROTECTION IS: Nature Reserve — long-term title deed restriction, so the protected status stays with the land even when it changes hands, with tenure commitments of up to 99 years or in perpetuity; Protected Environment — more flexible, can be declared across several properties at once and can allow production under an approved management plan, typically 30 years; and Biodiversity Agreements, around 10 years, with no title deed restriction at all. If the point is to stop a future owner or a future council doing what you are fighting now, only the title-deed tiers do that. THE MONEY: South Africa offers the only dedicated tax incentive for biodiversity conservation of its kind — section 37D of the Income Tax Act lets landowners AND COMMUNITIES declaring nature reserves deduct the full value of the declared land from taxable income, with eligibility requiring the 99-year or perpetual title deed restriction. WHY IT MATTERS FOR LAND REFORM COMMUNITIES: where land reform has produced communal ownership through a Communal Property Association, stewardship is the route by which that community gets legal protection and the economic opportunities attached to a protected area — a dedicated land reform stewardship initiative was established for exactly this. THE TRAP TO AVOID, DOCUMENTED: 26 KwaZulu-Natal reserves were gazetted but could not register with the Deeds Office because of omissions in the title deed endorsement process, and therefore did not qualify for the tax incentive until a year-long effort by conservation organisations and a specialist environmental law firm fixed the paperwork. Declaration is not the end — check the deeds endorsement actually registered. WHO IT SUITS: communities holding land through a CPA, and private landowners, who want protection that outlasts them. CAVEATS: this secures land you already hold — it is not a purchase fund and will not help against an expropriation; declaration is led by the provincial conservation authority and takes years; and the process needs specialist legal input at the deeds stage.

trackers.name: FEDUP and the uTshani Fund — savings groups that won direct access to the housing subsidy, cutting the developer out entirely
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the Federation of the Urban Poor (FEDUP), savings groups across eight of South Africa's nine provinces, with its own housing finance facility the uTshani Fund, and technical support from the Community Organisation Resource Centre; aligned with the Informal Settlement Network. WHAT THE FEDERATION WON, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THIS ENTRY: through collective lobbying it obtained DIRECT ACCESS TO THE GOVERNMENT HOUSING SUBSIDY PROGRAMME — without the interference of developers or contractors — secured a R10 million revolving loan facility, and shaped low-income housing policy through the People's Housing Process. Reported delivery on the back of those entitlements: 12,000 housing units averaging 56 square metres, incremental loans for a further 2,000 houses, infrastructure for 2,500 families, land tenure for 12,000 families, three parcels of commercial land and eleven community centres, all administered through uTshani. THE MECHANISM WORTH UNDERSTANDING: uTshani PRE-FINANCES construction and is repaid by government when the subsidy comes through, so building starts before the state pays — and members act as community contractors building their own houses. A member's account of joining is exact: she bought a green savings book for R8, joined, and the group then negotiated with the municipality for their subsidy; they convinced the municipality by building one show house first and having the inspector approve its quality. FEDUP holds partnership agreements with metros including eThekwini, Ekurhuleni, Johannesburg, Cape Town and Stellenbosch. WHO IT SUITS: South African households in informal settlements or backyards seeking land tenure and a house without a developer, and groups wanting to build for themselves under the subsidy. CAVEATS: THE PRE-FINANCING MODEL ONLY WORKS IF THE STATE PAYS ON TIME — provinces have been slow to release pledged subsidies, projects have stalled, and houses have been built without infrastructure; subsidy allocation is a provincial and municipal decision, not the fund's. For litigation against mining and environmental harm, South Africa's CER and CALS entries are the routes.

trackers.name: AFRA — works with farm dwellers and labour tenants in KwaZulu-Natal, and got a Special Master appointed when the state sat on 22,000 claims
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Association for Rural Advancement, a land rights NGO working since 1979 with marginalised black rural people and focused on FARM DWELLERS — people living on land owned by someone else, the group most exposed to eviction in South Africa and least served by the conservation and mining entries already in this file. It works intensively in and around the uMgungundlovu District Municipality in KwaZulu-Natal and gives support and advice more widely. WHAT IT ACTUALLY OFFERS: to prevent and oppose evictions, settle disputes and secure tenure rights and services by providing or facilitating MONITORING, MEDIATION, ADVICE AND LEGAL ASSISTANCE, and by building partnerships that promote farm dweller rights. THE CASE THAT SHOWS WHAT IT CAN FORCE, and the lesson is about a state that simply stopped processing: under the Land Reform (Labour Tenants) Act 3 of 1996, labour tenants — people given a plot on a farm in exchange for their labour under apartheid — could claim title, with a claim deadline of 2001; about 22,000 claims were lodged, out of a labour-tenant population AFRA puts at more than half a million. The department then failed to process them. AFRA led litigation in the Land Claims Court from 2013, and the court ordered the appointment of a SPECIAL MASTER for labour tenants to force implementation — upheld through to a Constitutional Court judgment handed down on 20 August 2019. When an administration refuses to process claims, the remedy to ask for is not another order to decide your case — it is a supervisory appointment over the whole backlog. AFRA also does action research it can put in front of policymakers: a 2017 survey of 842 farm dweller households, 6,478 people, in uMgungundlovu. WHO IT SUITS: South African farm dwellers, labour tenants and rural households facing eviction or stalled land claims, principally in KwaZulu-Natal. CAVEATS: an advocacy, research and support organisation — it facilitates legal assistance rather than being a law firm; its intensive work is district-focused; and the labour tenant claim deadline passed in 2001, so most of the half million never lodged. For environmental litigation, South Africa's CER entry; for stewardship agreements, the biodiversity stewardship entry.

trackers.name: Wild Tomorrow / Greater Ukuwela — five land purchases since 2017 in KwaZulu-Natal, bought from farming and given the highest legal protection
trackers.desc: WHO BUYS LAND, AND HOW THE SEQUENCE WORKS: Wild Tomorrow has assembled the Greater Ukuwela Nature Reserve on South Africa's Elephant Coast in KwaZulu-Natal by buying parcels one at a time on the open market — Ukuwela (2017/18), Mfuleni (2019) and further properties, five land deals in total, with a further purchase adding the equivalent of 318 acres in 2022 and the 148.5 ha Sisonke Farm secured in 2024 to join the reserve's severed eastern and western halves. The reserve now spans a reported 1,566.74 ha. THE THREE THINGS TO COPY: (1) buy the parcel that unblocks the others — Sisonke had divided the reserve in two, with fences cutting the protected areas off from each other, so one purchase restored connectivity across the whole; (2) get the status changed after you buy — land once earmarked for pineapple production now holds the HIGHEST LEVEL OF LEGAL PROTECTION under South Africa's Protected Areas Act, which is what stops a future owner reversing the decision; and (3) raise the purchase price from outside — the deals were funded by individuals, families and foundations including a UK land-purchase trust, with one appeal target published at £621k for a single parcel. A community that cannot afford a parcel can still identify the one parcel that matters and find someone to fund it — the fundraising is a separate skill from the holding. Local people use part of the reserve for fishing, cattle grazing, and reed and water collection, and the organisation runs community work around it including employment, teacher stipends and a school. WHO IT SUITS: South African conservation groups and communities seeking to take land out of agriculture or development permanently, and anyone studying how to structure a purchase-and-protect sequence. CAVEATS: this is a CONSERVATION LANDOWNER, not a community land trust — title rests with the organisation, not with neighbouring communities, and the surrounding land use is contested (monoculture pineapple and eucalyptus); it buys where biodiversity value is high, not where a community needs help. For collective tenure by residents, Kenya's Tanzania-Bondeni CLT entry; for stewardship over land you already own, South Africa's biodiversity stewardship entry; for farm dwellers facing eviction, AFRA.

trackers.name: Lawyers for Human Rights — a land and housing programme for rural dwellers facing eviction since 1998, and a public directory of every free legal door in South Africa
trackers.desc: WHO TO INSTRUCT: Lawyers for Human Rights (LHR), an independent South African organisation with a track record spanning nearly four decades of public interest litigation, which provides FREE LEGAL SERVICES to vulnerable, marginalised and indigent individuals and communities whose constitutional rights have been unlawfully infringed, through six strategic programmes staffed by specialist practitioners. THE PROGRAMME THAT MATTERS HERE: its land and housing work was established in OCTOBER 1998 to protect and promote the rights of RURAL DWELLERS DIRECTLY THREATENED WITH EVICTION — defending farm workers facing eviction, and advocating for their tenure security through training workshops, a regular newsletter and networking. Alongside it sits a STRATEGIC LITIGATION UNIT based at the Pretoria Law Clinic, running since 2003, which focuses on just administrative action for indigent persons and communities and increasingly on land reform matters, and which also works to protect the rights of MINING-AFFECTED COMMUNITIES and to secure corporate compliance in the extractives space. Ask for the programme by name — land and housing, or strategic litigation — rather than making a general enquiry. AND THE THING TO KEEP EVEN IF YOU NEVER RING LHR: South Africa has a PUBLIC DIRECTORY OF FREE LEGAL SERVICES listing the Rental Housing Tribunal, Legal Aid centres, UNIVERSITY LAW CLINICS and Legal Practice Councils with their addresses and locations — the single most useful page for a household facing eviction, because it does not depend on any one organisation having capacity. WHO IT SUITS: South African farm dwellers, rural households and mining-affected communities facing eviction or seeking tenure security, and anyone who needs to find the nearest free legal office themselves. CAVEATS: a public interest organisation with finite capacity that takes cases of wider significance; the directory lists services, not guarantees of representation. For farm dwellers and labour tenant claims in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa's AFRA entry; for environmental litigation, CER; for the Xolobeni line of cases, CALS.

trackers.name: EJF (Environmental Justice Fund), South Africa — one-year grants of R50,000–R100,000 decided by a Grants Committee of activists, open to unregistered community organisations and closed to established NGOs by design
trackers.desc: A FUND THAT WILL NOT TAKE APPLICATIONS FROM ESTABLISHED NGOs — method declared first: THIS ENTRY WAS A 339-CHARACTER STUB WITH NO URL AT ALL, ENDING WITH ITS OWN NOTE THAT THE CANONICAL DOMAIN WAS NOT YET VERIFIED. THAT IS NOW RESOLVED BY SEARCH AND THE HOST SHIPPED; THE PROBE RAN IT AND FOUR FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS BEFORE REWRITING. WHO IT WILL AND WILL NOT FUND, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT DOES NOT CONSIDER APPLICATIONS FROM ESTABLISHED NGOs — BECAUSE IT WAS SET UP PRECISELY TO ADDRESS THE PROBLEM THAT MOST FUNDING TYPICALLY GOES TO ESTABLISHED NGOs WHILE COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS STRUGGLE TO ACCESS FUNDING DIRECTLY. A funder that turns away the professional applicants. Almost every fund in this file is competed for by NGOs with grant-writers; this one excludes them on purpose. A village committee is not the weakest applicant here — it is the only eligible one. AND THE SECOND ELIGIBILITY RULE, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: YOU DO NOT NEED TO BE FORMALLY REGISTERED TO BE ELIGIBLE FOR SUPPORT. The registration barrier this file has recorded at funder after funder, removed. A group that has never been near a registrar can apply. WHAT IS ON OFFER: ONE-YEAR GRANTS OF R50,000 TO R100,000, WITH GRANT SIZE RELATED TO LENGTH AND TO WHAT THE ORGANISATION WANTS TO USE THE FUNDS FOR — PLUS ACCOMPANIMENT ALONGSIDE THE MONEY IN THE FORM OF CAPACITY-STRENGTHENING AND NETWORKING SUPPORT. A RAPID RESPONSE GRANT ALSO EXISTS, THOUGH ITS APPLICATIONS WERE CLOSED AT THE LAST RECORD. WHO DECIDES, WHICH IS THE THIRD FIND: A PARTICIPATORY GRANT-MAKING MODEL WHERE DECISIONS ON WHO GETS SUPPORT ARE MADE BY A GROUP OF ACTIVISTS FROM THE ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE SECTOR WHO SERVE ON ITS GRANTS COMMITTEE — SEEKING TO REDEFINE THE PATTERNS OF POWER INHERENT IN PHILANTHROPY AND CENTRE COMMUNITY AGENCY, TRUST, ACCESSIBILITY, FLEXIBILITY AND WELLBEING. Activists on the committee rather than programme officers. This file records the same structure under Niger, where a grassroots women's committee decides, and under Libya, where an Indigenous-led fund's approval committee is itself Indigenous. Where the deciders come from the sector, the application reads differently. WHAT COUNTS AS ELIGIBLE WORK, AND THE WORKED EXAMPLE THEY PUBLISH: IT TAKES A BROAD APPROACH TO WHAT CONSTITUTES ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE, BUT THE PROPOSAL MUST MAKE THE LINK BETWEEN THE ACTIVITIES AND ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE — A PROPOSAL TO DISTRIBUTE FOOD PARCELS MIGHT NOT BE ELIGIBLE, WHILE A PROPOSAL TO ESTABLISH A COMMUNITY FOOD GARDEN AND TRAIN MEMBERS IN ORGANIC FARMING AND PERMACULTURE WOULD BE. That worked example is the most useful sentence for a first-time applicant: relief is not eligible, building a capacity is. Same community, same money, different framing. THE THEMES IT NAMES: CLIMATE JUSTICE, POLLUTION MITIGATION, LAND RIGHTS, FOOD SOVEREIGNTY, WATER PROTECTION AND COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION IN DECISION-MAKING AROUND NATURAL RESOURCES — EXPLICITLY NOT A CLOSED LIST, WITH APPLICATIONS OUTSIDE THOSE AREAS CONSIDERED IF THEY FALL WITHIN ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE. LAND RIGHTS and COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION IN DECISION-MAKING AROUND NATURAL RESOURCES are named themes. A community fighting a project is inside the published scope, not stretching it. WHO IS EXCLUDED BESIDES ESTABLISHED NGOs: PRIVATE COMPANIES AND OTHER PROFIT-MAKING ENTITIES, AND STATE ENTITIES SUCH AS MUNICIPALITIES. WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT RESTS ON: AN ACTIVIST-DRIVEN, FEMINIST NGO PROVIDING FINANCIAL, CAPACITY-STRENGTHENING AND NETWORKING SUPPORT TO COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS AND COMMUNITY NETWORKS — ITS VISION ROOTED IN THE CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHT TO AN ENVIRONMENT NOT HARMFUL TO HEALTH OR WELLBEING, AND DESCRIBING ITSELF AS A FUND BY ACTIVISTS, FOR ACTIVISTS. AND WHAT ITS GRANTEES DO WITH IT: ONE NAMED WATER COLLECTIVE AMONG ITS GRANTEES, WITH OTHER WATER JUSTICE ORGANISATIONS IT SUPPORTS, HOSTED AN INAUGURAL WATER JUSTICE POLITICAL SCHOOL. Grantees convening their own school rather than attending someone else's training — which is what unrestricted, activist-decided money makes possible. WHO IT SUITS: unregistered and community-based South African groups fighting pollution, land loss or water capture, who have been shut out of funding that goes to professional NGOs. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY; GRANTS ARE ONE YEAR AND MODEST BY INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS; ESTABLISHED NGOs ARE INELIGIBLE BY DESIGN, SO AN ORGANISATION THAT HAS GROWN OUT OF CBO STATUS MUST LOOK ELSEWHERE; AND THE RAPID RESPONSE WINDOW WAS CLOSED AT THE LAST RECORD — CHECK BEFORE COUNTING ON IT. For a grassroots women's committee that decides its own fund, Niger's entry; for an Indigenous-led fund whose approval committee is itself Indigenous, Libya's entry.

trackers.name: The WWF Nedbank Green Trust with its printed exclusions, the 30-member Environmental NGO Collaboration including traditional leaders and a biodiversity law centre, and South Africa's 540 mapped Key Biodiversity Areas
trackers.desc: THE FUNDER'S EXCLUSIONS, THE THIRTY-NGO LIST AND THE 540 SITES: THE WWF NEDBANK GREEN TRUST ACCEPTS PROJECT PROPOSALS to promote conservation of nature and ecological processes, funding organisations DEVELOPING INNOVATIVE AND TRANSFERABLE SOLUTIONS, IN PARTNERSHIP NETWORKS, WITH THE POTENTIAL TO CATALYSE CHANGE — AND IT WORKS WITH COMMUNITIES, WHO ARE THE KEEPERS OF THE NATURAL RESOURCES. AND IT PRINTS WHAT IT WILL NOT FUND, WHICH IS MORE USEFUL THAN WHAT IT WILL: IT WILL NOT SUPPORT CONDUIT ORGANISATIONS WHICH ARE NOT THE END USERS OF THE PROJECT FUNDS; NOR CORE SUPPORT FOR ORGANISATIONS AND THE PURCHASE OF CAPITAL EQUIPMENT, INCLUDING BUILDINGS, FENCING AND VEHICLES; NOR SALARIES, EXCEPT AS AN INTEGRAL PART OF A PROJECT. No pass-through organisations means a community group can and should be the applicant rather than the beneficiary of somebody else's grant. But no fencing, no vehicles, no buildings: read that before you build a budget around a fence. Every applicant must also have A CLEAR THEORY OF CHANGE for the solution proposed — write that first, because it is the stated test. THE ROSTER, PUBLISHED IN FULL: THE ENVIRONMENTAL NGO COLLABORATION IS A GROUP OF 30 ENVIRONMENTAL NGOs THAT HAVE COME TOGETHER TO STRATEGICALLY ALIGN THEIR IMPACT, INCLUDING SUPPORTING GOVERNMENT IN ACHIEVING SOUTH AFRICA'S COMMITMENT TO CONSERVE 30% OF BIODIVERSITY ON LAND AND IN THE OCEAN BY 2030 — with a named organisation APPOINTED AS THE EXECUTANT AND FUNDING MANAGER providing administrative, coordination and secretariat support, and a steering committee. Its published membership includes A BIODIVERSITY LAW CENTRE; the CONGRESS OF TRADITIONAL LEADERS OF SOUTH AFRICA; the CAPE LEOPARD TRUST; CONSERVATION OUTCOMES; a CONSERVATION STRATEGY FUND; a DUZI-uMNGENI CONSERVATION TRUST; the ENDANGERED WILDLIFE TRUST; ENVIRONMENTAL AND RURAL SOLUTIONS; GREENMATTER; the KRUGER TO CANYONS BIOSPHERE REGION; LIVING LIMPOPO; a SUSTAINABLE FINANCE COALITION; the BOTANICAL SOCIETY OF SOUTH AFRICA; the SOUTH AFRICAN WILDLIFE COLLEGE; and WILDERNESS FOUNDATION AFRICA. Two of those matter most for a land case. A BIODIVERSITY LAW CENTRE sitting inside the conservation sector means legal capacity aimed specifically at biodiversity, not general public interest law. And the CONGRESS OF TRADITIONAL LEADERS is a member: traditional authority is inside the collaboration, not outside it — if your land is under a traditional council, that is the door into this whole network. A SUSTAINABLE FINANCE COALITION in the same list is who to ask how a protected area pays for itself. THE MAP THAT SETTLES WHETHER YOUR GROUND COUNTS: SOUTH AFRICA IS THE FIRST IN THE WORLD TO COMPLETE A COMPREHENSIVE NATIONAL KEY BIODIVERSITY AREA ASSESSMENT FOR ALL ECOSYSTEMS AND ACROSS MULTIPLE GROUPS OF SPECIES — MAMMALS, BIRDS, PLANTS, FISH, AMPHIBIANS, INVERTEBRATES, BUTTERFLIES, DRAGONFLIES AND REPTILES — IDENTIFYING MORE THAN 540 KBAs COVERING APPROXIMATELY 370,000 SQUARE KILOMETRES, EQUIVALENT TO 30% OF SOUTH AFRICA'S MAINLAND EXTENT. Five hundred and forty mapped sites assessed against a global standard, covering a third of the country. Check whether your ground is inside one before anything else — the standard PROVIDES CLEAR GLOBAL GUIDANCE ON WHERE CONSERVATION EFFORTS SHOULD BE FOCUSED, INCLUDING FOR INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL INVESTMENTS, PROTECTED AREA ESTABLISHMENT AND AVOIDING FURTHER LOSS. A KBA listing is a fact about your land that no developer's consultant produced and none can withdraw. Named examples include the last remaining patches of MISTBELT GRASSLANDS IN KWAZULU-NATAL, which form part of SOUTH AFRICA'S STRATEGIC WATER SOURCE AREAS. Strategic Water Source Area is a second designation worth checking for — grassland that supplies a city's water is defended on different grounds from grassland that shelters a bird. WHO IT SUITS: South African communities and organisations seeking funding, allies, or proof their site is recognised. CAVEATS: A GRANT WINDOW WITH NAMED EXCLUSIONS and a collaboration aligned with government targets. For strategic environmental litigation, South Africa's CER entry; for putting private or communal land under formal protection by agreement, the biodiversity stewardship entry; for farm dwellers and labour tenants, AFRA; for five land purchases, Wild Tomorrow.

trackers.name: ACRRA, the South Africa-registered Indigenous-led alliance using legal empowerment, and the African Commission's Working Group that receives communications directly from communities — with its own complaints manual and the Endorois precedent
trackers.desc: A MANUAL ON HOW TO COMPLAIN, WRITTEN BY THE BODY THAT HEARS IT — but first the organisation: THE AFRICAN COMMUNITY RESOURCE RIGHTS ALLIANCE (ACRRA) IS A SOUTH AFRICA-REGISTERED, INDIGENOUS-LED ORGANISATION WORKING TO PROTECT THE RIGHTS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES IN AFRICA, WHICH ADVOCATES FOR THEIR ABILITY TO ACCESS, MANAGE AND BENEFIT FROM THEIR BIOCULTURAL HERITAGE AND NATURAL RESOURCES — AND WHICH USES LEGAL EMPOWERMENT AND INNOVATIVE LEGAL APPROACHES TO SUPPORT INDIGENOUS-LED CONSERVATION, SUSTAINABLE RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, AND THE PROTECTION OF TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE. Indigenous-LED, registered, and doing legal empowerment. That combination is rare in this file: most bodies working on indigenous land rights are led by lawyers or conservationists rather than by the communities themselves. BIOCULTURAL is the term to learn — it treats the knowledge and the land as one claim rather than two, which is exactly what a community loses when a site is taken. Its named work includes A COMMUNITY-BASED EDUCATION INITIATIVE IN THE KHOMANI SAN COMMUNITY OF SOUTH AFRICA'S KALAHARI THAT INTEGRATES THE NATIONAL CURRICULUM WITH INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE AND TRADITIONS, and a digital hub for rural access. THE CONTINENTAL BODY THAT WILL TAKE YOUR ACCOUNT DIRECTLY, WITH ITS TERMS OF REFERENCE PRINTED: THE AFRICAN COMMISSION'S WORKING GROUP ON INDIGENOUS POPULATIONS/COMMUNITIES IN AFRICA IS MANDATED TO GATHER, REQUEST, RECEIVE AND EXCHANGE INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATIONS FROM ALL RELEVANT SOURCES — INCLUDING GOVERNMENTS, INDIGENOUS POPULATIONS AND THEIR COMMUNITIES AND ORGANISATIONS — ON VIOLATIONS OF THEIR HUMAN RIGHTS AND FUNDAMENTAL FREEDOMS; TO UNDERTAKE COUNTRY VISITS TO STUDY THE HUMAN RIGHTS SITUATION OF INDIGENOUS POPULATIONS; AND TO FORMULATE RECOMMENDATIONS AND PROPOSALS ON APPROPRIATE MEASURES TO PREVENT AND REMEDY VIOLATIONS. From communities AND THEIR ORGANISATIONS, in its own terms of reference. A community does not need a lawyer or an international NGO to reach it — the mandate names you as a source. And it undertakes country visits, which means an account can bring people to look. AND IT PUBLISHES THE INSTRUCTIONS: THE WORKING GROUP PREPARED A MANUAL ON THE PROTECTION OF THE RIGHTS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE AFRICAN CHARTER, ON THE BASIS OF THE USE OF THE PROCEDURE OF COMMUNICATIONS AND COMPLAINTS BEFORE THE AFRICAN COMMISSION — AND THE COMMISSION ADOPTED IT. A manual on how to bring a complaint, written and adopted by the body that decides the complaints. Ask for it by name before you draft anything. It also published, with an international labour body and a university, A REPORT ON THE CONSTITUTIONAL AND LEGISLATIVE PROTECTION OF THE RIGHTS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES IN 24 AFRICAN COUNTRIES, covering land and natural resources, environment, culture, language and education — so the position in your own country has already been assessed. THE PRECEDENT THAT MAKES IT WORTH THE EFFORT: THE AFRICAN COMMISSION'S DECISION IN COMMUNICATION 276/2003, BROUGHT ON BEHALF OF THE ENDOROIS COMMUNITY AGAINST KENYA IN FEBRUARY 2010, RECOGNISED THE VALIDITY OF COLLECTIVELY HELD INDIGENOUS ANCESTRAL LANDS AS WELL AS INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES' RIGHT TO NATURAL RESOURCES AND SELF-DETERMINED DEVELOPMENT, AND CRAFTED CLEAR INDICATORS FOR INDIGENOUSNESS IN AFRICA. A community brought a communication and won a continental ruling that collectively held ancestral land is valid land. That is the case to put in front of any official who tells you customary holding is not ownership — and the same decision set out how indigenousness is established in Africa, which answers the second thing you will be told. THE TWO RESOLUTIONS TO QUOTE: ACHPR/Res. 489 (LXIX) 2021 CALLS ON AFRICAN STATES TO RECOGNISE THE RIGHTS OF INDIGENOUS POPULATIONS AND COMMUNITIES OVER THE CONSERVATION, CONTROL, MANAGEMENT AND SUSTAINABLE USE OF THEIR NATURAL RESOURCES INCLUDING WILDLIFE — AND ACHPR/Res. 490 (LXIX) 2021 ADDRESSES EXTRACTIVE INDUSTRIES AND THE PROTECTION OF LAND RIGHTS OF INDIGENOUS POPULATIONS IN AFRICA. Two resolutions adopted at the same session, one on natural resources and one on extractives. If a mine or a concession is the threat, 490 is the one; if the question is who manages the wildlife or the forest, 489. Both are continental instruments your own government voted alongside. The Working Group also runs REGIONAL SENSITISATION SEMINARS BRINGING TOGETHER INDIGENOUS CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS INSTITUTIONS, NGOs AND STATE DELEGATES, with community visits built in. National human rights institutions in the same room as indigenous communities is a pairing the seminars create deliberately — and the recommendations ask NHRIs to work WITH indigenous NGOs. Find out whether your country has one and whether it attended. WHO IT SUITS: Indigenous and customary communities anywhere in Africa, and organisations preparing a continental complaint. CAVEATS: A CONTINENTAL PROCEDURE IS SLOW and requires domestic remedies to be exhausted or shown futile — take advice before filing. For strategic environmental litigation, South Africa's CER entry; for the Congress of Traditional Leaders inside a 30-NGO collaboration and 540 mapped Key Biodiversity Areas, the Green Trust entry; for farm dwellers and labour tenants, AFRA.

trackers.name: Usuthu Gorge and Tshanini — two KwaZulu-Natal communities that created their own game reserves on their own land, with the funder, the R900 000 and the nine ranger posts named — and WILDTRUST, the trust that co-funded it
trackers.desc: THE COMMUNITY THAT MADE ITS OWN GAME RESERVE, AND WHAT IT COST — this is a worked example, with the money and the jobs named: TWO LOCAL COMMUNITY GROUPS DECIDED TO JOIN THE WILDLIFE BUSINESS BY CREATING NEW GAME RESERVES ON THEIR SOIL — THE USUTHU GORGE AND TSHANINI COMMUNITY CONSERVATION AREAS, IN THE MAPUTALAND DISTRICT OF KWAZULU-NATAL, CLOSE TO TWO ESTABLISHED STATE RESERVES. ON THEIR SOIL is the whole point. This is not a community being consulted about somebody else's protected area — it is a community declaring one on land it already holds, under a named tribal authority, with its own vice-chairman named on the public record. AND THE LAND THEY CHOSE IS THE PRACTICAL LESSON: THE NEW CONSERVATION LAND IS MOSTLY UNSUITABLE FOR AGRICULTURE BECAUSE OF THE ROCKY TERRAIN, POOR SOIL AND LOW RAINFALL — in a community that FOR MANY DECADES HAD RELIED ON SUBSISTENCE AGRICULTURE AND MIGRANT LABOUR TO MAKE ENDS MEET. They put the reserve on the ground that could not be farmed. That answers the objection you will hear first — that conservation takes food land — and it is the survey to do before you propose anything: which of our ground yields nothing, and could it yield something as a reserve? THE MONEY, NAMED: ESTABLISHMENT OF THE USUTHU GORGE COMMUNITY CONSERVATION AREA WAS FUNDED JOINTLY BY THE WILDLANDS CONSERVATION TRUST, WHICH PUT IN R900 000, AND THE GOVERNMENT DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL AFFAIRS AND TOURISM. A named trust and a government department splitting the establishment cost, with the trust's contribution stated. That is the funding shape to ask for: a conservation trust and the environment department together, so neither is carrying it alone and the state has a stake in it working. THE JOBS, COUNTED: NINE FIELD RANGERS HAVE BEEN EMPLOYED TO PATROL THE RESERVE, AND THE COMMUNITY HOPES TO PROVIDE SEVERAL NEW JOBS AND TRAINING IN HOSPITALITY AND NATURE-GUIDING THROUGH A LODGE DEVELOPMENT — and the area WOULD BE ZONED TO SEPARATE HUNTERS AND WILDLIFE TOURISTS. Nine ranger posts from one community reserve, plus hospitality and guiding training to come. Ask for the ranger number in writing before you agree to anything — and note the zoning: separating hunters from photographic tourists is how a reserve serves two markets that will not share a valley. AND IT SPREAD: OTHER COMMUNITY GROUPS IN MAPUTALAND ARE CONSIDERING SIMILAR VENTURES to take advantage of opportunities offered by a tri-nation transfrontier conservation area initiative linking South Africa, Mozambique and Eswatini. One community did it and the neighbours followed. If you are the first in your district, the precedent you set is the thing your neighbours will use — document what you did. THE TRUST BEHIND IT: WILDTRUST, REGISTERED AS THE WILDLANDS CONSERVATION TRUST UNDER IT NO. 4329/1991/PMB, WAS ORIGINALLY ESTABLISHED IN 1989 AS THE NATAL CONSERVATION TRUST AND AMALGAMATED WITH THE WILDLANDS TRUST IN 2004 — an African-grown conservation non-profit working across southern and East Africa and the Western Indian Ocean, WITH PROJECTS AS FAR AFIELD AS THE COMOROS, and running two programmes: a terrestrial one described as PIONEERING A COMMUNITY-CENTRED APPROACH IN SOUTHERN AFRICA, and a marine one EMPOWERING COMMUNITIES TO BE STEWARDS OF OCEAN HEALTH. A trust deed number printed, and a trust that has held its registration since 1991. This file has repeatedly flagged that a trust is the vehicle able to hold land in perpetuity — here is one that does, and that co-funds communities to create their own reserves. AND ITS STATED POSITION ON THE 30x30 TARGET IS THE SENTENCE A COMMUNITY SHOULD QUOTE BACK AT ANY CONSERVATION BODY: RATHER THAN SEEING THE ACHIEVEMENT OF A 30x30 GOAL AS AN INSTRUMENT THAT WILL DIVORCE PEOPLE FROM THEIR LAND, WE ADVOCATE FOR A PATHWAY THAT WILL DRIVE HUMAN DEVELOPMENT THROUGH IMPROVED CONSERVATION — said against A COMPLEX HISTORICAL BACKGROUND WHERE ACCESS AND OWNERSHIP OF LAND IS A CRITICAL THEME. A South African conservation trust naming land dispossession as the background to conservation, in its own words, on its own site. Hold whoever approaches you to that standard, and ask them to say it in writing. ALSO NAMED: CONSERVATION SOUTH AFRICA, REGISTERED IN SOUTH AFRICA AS A SECTION 18A PUBLIC BENEFIT ORGANISATION, working on protected-area expansion through biodiversity stewardship, invasive alien plant clearing and grazing best-management practices, and involved in a 1.5 MILLION HECTARE EASTERN GRASSLANDS LANDSCAPE and regenerative wool production among COMMUNAL SHEEP FARMERS. Section 18A status means donations to it are tax-deductible in South Africa — which is what makes domestic fundraising possible. Ask any South African organisation whether it holds 18A before you run an appeal through it. WHO IT SUITS: South African communities holding land they could declare, communal farmers, and anyone seeking co-funding for a reserve. CAVEATS: THE USUTHU MODEL INCLUDES HUNTING ZONES — decide your community's position first. For putting private or communal land under formal protection by agreement, South Africa's biodiversity stewardship entry; for the funder's printed exclusions and 540 mapped Key Biodiversity Areas, the Green Trust entry; for strategic environmental litigation, CER; for five land purchases, Wild Tomorrow.

trackers.name: World Land Trust — a funder whose business is paying local organisations to buy land, with the R3.9 million grant that completed a R15.5 million South African purchase, plus two community small-grants facilities and the eviction case this file owes as a caution
trackers.desc: THE GRANT THAT FINISHED THE PURCHASE — and this is the funder type your brief keeps asking for: WORLD LAND TRUST, FOUNDED IN 1989, FUNDS LOCAL PARTNER ORGANISATIONS AROUND THE WORLD TO CREATE RESERVES AND GIVE PERMANENT PROTECTION FOR HABITATS AND WILDLIFE, AND HAS PROTECTED 2,409,420 ACRES OF THREATENED HABITAT. It funds LOCAL PARTNERS to buy land. Not its own reserves — somebody else's, owned and managed by the local organisation. That is the exact shape a community needs, and it is rarer than it sounds: most conservation money pays for management, not for title. THE SOUTH AFRICAN TRANSACTION, WITH EVERY NUMBER ON THE RECORD: A WORLD LAND TRUST GRANT OF 3.9 MILLION RAND — APPROXIMATELY US$260,000 — COMPLETED THE 15.5 MILLION RAND PURCHASE OF UKUWELA, ADDING THE EQUIVALENT OF 318 ACRES OF A TOTAL 1,235 ACRES, AND SECURING IT AS A CONSERVATION AREA OWNED AND MANAGED BY THE LOCAL PARTNER ORGANISATION. Read the structure rather than the sum: a fifteen-and-a-half-million-rand purchase was finished by a 3.9 million rand grant. The grant was the LAST piece, not the whole thing. That is how these purchases are actually assembled — several funders, each closing part of it, with one arriving to complete. If you are raising to buy, do not look for one funder to cover the price; look for the sequence, and ask each what gap it will close. THE LEGAL OUTCOME IS THE PART TO AIM AT: UKUWELA WAS DECLARED PART OF THE GREATER UKUWELA NATURE RESERVE AND PROTECTED AT THE HIGHEST LEGAL LEVEL IN SOUTH AFRICA, ON EQUAL FOOTING WITH A NATIONAL PARK. Buying the land is step one; getting it declared at the highest protection level is step two, and it is the step that survives a change of owner or of government. Ask, before you buy, what declaration the purchase will allow and how long it takes. AND THE REASON THIS PARCEL MATTERED: it CONNECTS A 28,000-HECTARE CONSERVANCY WITH A 332,000-HECTARE UNESCO WORLD HERITAGE WETLAND PARK. A small parcel between two large protected areas is worth far more than its size, because it is the corridor. If your ground sits between two protected areas, say so first — that is the argument that raises money, and 318 acres attracted an international grant because of where it sat. TWO SMALL-GRANTS FACILITIES NAMED, FOR COMMUNITIES NOT BUYING ANYTHING: SKEPPIES OPERATED AS A COMMUNITY CONSERVATION AND DEVELOPMENT SMALL-GRANTS FUND IN THE NORTHERN CAPE AND WAS LATER HOSTED BY A NAMED SOUTH AFRICAN CONSERVATION ORGANISATION; AND A COMMUNITY ADAPTATION SMALL GRANTS FACILITY WAS STRUCTURED AS A SMALL-GRANTS CLIMATE-FINANCE INSTRUMENT FOR LOCAL ADAPTATION. Small-grants funds hosted inside a bigger organisation are the ones a village committee can actually reach — the host does the reporting the donor requires. Ask which organisation currently hosts a small-grants facility in your province. AND THE CAUTION THIS FILE OWES ANYONE READING ABOUT CONSERVATION LAND PURCHASE, RECORDED PLAINLY: A DOCUMENTED CASE RECORDS THAT TWO INTERNATIONAL CONSERVATION ORGANISATIONS EACH PAID US$2 MILLION TO BUY AN AREA OF LAND AND GAVE IT TO A GOVERNMENT TO CREATE A PROPOSED NATIONAL PARK — AND THAT THE INDIGENOUS PEOPLE WHO LIVED IN THE AREA WERE SUBSEQUENTLY SUBJECTED TO A SERIES OF BRUTAL EVICTIONS, WITH THE COMMUNITY TELLING A TELEVISION JOURNALIST THAT POLICE BEAT PEOPLE, TOOK THEIR PROPERTY AND BURNT VILLAGES. Money buying land for conservation is not automatically on your side. The difference between Ukuwela and that case is WHO ENDS UP HOLDING THE TITLE: in one the local organisation owns and manages it, in the other the land was handed to a state that then cleared the people off. So the question to ask any funder offering to buy land near you is not how much, but: who will be the registered owner afterwards, and what happens to the people living there. Get the answer in writing before anyone signs. WHO IT SUITS: South African and other African organisations raising to purchase a corridor or a parcel, and communities offered a conservation land deal. CAVEATS: WLT FUNDS PARTNER ORGANISATIONS, NOT INDIVIDUALS OR UNREGISTERED GROUPS — you need a registered local partner. For five land purchases in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa's Wild Tomorrow entry; for the community that made its own game reserve with R900 000 and nine ranger posts, the Usuthu Gorge entry; for rapid response grants, Urgent Action Fund–Africa; for the funder's printed exclusions, the Green Trust entry.

trackers.name: Money for the costs of the case — EDLC's litigation expenses fund, the only one of its type spanning the developing world, plus Global Greengrants' $500–$5,000 grants and the $5k–$15k legal-action window that pays for community security
trackers.desc: SOMEBODY PAYS THE COSTS OF THE CASE — placement note first: THESE ARE GLOBAL FUNDERS REACHABLE FROM ANYWHERE IN AFRICA, FILED UNDER SOUTH AFRICA ONLY BECAUSE THIS FILE HAS NO GLOBAL KEY AND ITS OTHER DEFENDER-FUNDING ENTRIES SIT HERE. IN 2010 THE ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDER LAW CENTER CREATED A GRANT PROGRAM FOR EXPENSES IN PUBLIC INTEREST LITIGATION AGAINST THOSE RESPONSIBLE FOR RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS THAT HARM THE HUMAN RIGHTS, HEALTH, AND ENVIRONMENT OF COMMUNITIES IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES. EXPENSES. Not the organisation, not the programme — the costs of running one case: the filing fees, the transport, the expert, the transcripts. That is the item that stops most of the cases in this file, and there is a fund for exactly it. ITS OWN REASONING IS WORTH READING IN FULL, BECAUSE IT NAMES THE GAP PRECISELY: WHILE CASES ARE MUCH LESS EXPENSIVE TO LITIGATE IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES, THE ABILITY OF LOCAL GROUPS AND THEIR LAWYERS TO OBTAIN EVEN THESE RELATIVELY SMALL AMOUNTS OF MONEY FOR EXPENSES AND/OR LEGAL FEES IS CRITICAL — YET IT IS EXTREMELY DIFFICULT, IF NOT IMPOSSIBLE, TO OBTAIN SUCH FUNDING FROM FOUNDATIONS ON A ONE TIME, ONE CASE BASIS. THIS UNDERSCORES THE NEED FOR EDLC'S FUND, THE ONLY ONE OF ITS TYPE SPANNING THE DEVELOPING WORLD. EDLC'S FINANCIAL SUPPORT CAN MAKE THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN WHETHER OR NOT A CASE IS BROUGHT. One time, one case is the shape of funding almost no foundation offers, and it is the shape a community needs. If a lawyer has told you the case is arguable but the costs are impossible, this is the specific answer — and it says plainly that it may be the difference between the case being brought or not. AND THE FALLBACK MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE GRANT: WHETHER OR NOT EDLC PROVIDES A GRANT IN A PARTICULAR CASE, IT CAN OFTEN HELP BY FINDING LAWYERS OR PROVIDING OTHER RESOURCES — CONTACT EDLC BY EMAIL. Write even if you doubt you qualify for money, because finding you a lawyer is a separate service. It was created in 2003 TO PROVIDE LEGAL SERVICES TO ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDERS, ESPECIALLY BY FINDING PRIVATE LAWYERS TO WORK FOR FREE ON THEIR BEHALF, and has given approximately 100 grants; its stated focuses include FINDING EXPERTS TO HELP LOCAL COMMUNITIES. Finding EXPERTS is the other quiet service. A hydrologist, an economist or a toxicologist is often what a case actually turns on, and it has supplied an economist to a land-grab class action elsewhere. THE SMALL GRANTS FUND, WITH ITS RANGE AND ITS SCALE: GLOBAL GREENGRANTS FUND MAKES SMALL GRANTS TYPICALLY $500 TO $5,000 TO GRASSROOTS ENVIRONMENTAL CAUSES, SUPPORTING COMMUNITY-BASED GROUPS, AND SINCE 1993 HAS MADE OVER 14,000 GRANTS IN 168 COUNTRIES TOTALLING OVER $100 MILLION — ITS SIX ACTION AREAS BEING CLIMATE JUSTICE, LOCAL LIVELIHOODS, HEALTHY ECOSYSTEMS AND COMMUNITIES, WOMEN'S ENVIRONMENTAL ACTION, RIGHT TO LAND, WATER, AND RESOURCES, AND RIGHT TO DEFEND THE ENVIRONMENT. Five hundred dollars is a real grant size. RIGHT TO LAND, WATER AND RESOURCES and RIGHT TO DEFEND THE ENVIRONMENT are two of its six named areas — which means both the land claim and the protection of the people making it are fundable. It works through regional ADVISORS rather than an open portal, so the question is who advises for your region. AND THE LEGAL-ACTION WINDOW, WHICH FUNDS SOMETHING ALMOST NOTHING ELSE DOES: AN ADVISING ORGANISATION PARTNERSHIP GROUNDED IN SUPPORT FOR LEGAL ACTION FORMALISES COLLABORATION WITH THREE NAMED LEGAL ORGANISATIONS, WHO ADVISE ON SMALL GRANTS OF $5,000 TO $15,000 THAT SUPPORT EVERYTHING FROM SECURITY FOR CLIENT COMMUNITIES WHO ARE FACING HEIGHTENED RISKS BECAUSE OF THEIR WORK WITH LAWYERS, TO CAPACITY-BUILDING FOR PUBLIC INTEREST LAWYERS GRAPPLING WITH NEW CHALLENGES RELATED TO CRIMINALIZATION. Security for communities who are at greater risk BECAUSE they went to a lawyer. That is a cost nobody warns you about and almost no funder covers — and it is named here as a fundable item. If bringing a case has made your people less safe, say so in the application. THE WEST AFRICAN EXAMPLE OF WHAT THIS ECOSYSTEM PRODUCES: a Liberian public interest environmental law organisation, founded by a lawyer who also CO-ESTABLISHED AN ALLIANCE FOR RURAL DEMOCRACY — DESCRIBED AS THE LARGEST SOLIDARITY MOVEMENT IN LIBERIA, CONSISTING OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES, WOMEN DEPENDENT ON LAND AND NATURAL RESOURCES, INFORMAL SECTOR ENTREPRENEURS AND INFORMAL AND EMERGING LABOUR UNIONS — AND CO-ORGANISED A PUBLIC INTEREST LAWYERS INITIATIVE FOR WEST AFRICA; his work led to THE TEMPORARY PROTECTION OF SIX MILLION ACRES OF FOREST FROM DEVELOPMENT BY PALM OIL COMPANIES. Communities, women, informal traders and unions in one alliance — and six million acres temporarily protected. TEMPORARY is the honest word, but it is the difference between a forest that still exists and one that does not. And note the composition: informal sector entrepreneurs and labour unions are not who most land coalitions recruit, and they are why this one was the largest. WHO IT SUITS: any African community with an arguable case and no money for its costs, and any group needing $500 to $15,000 quickly. CAVEATS: THESE ARE FOREIGN-BASED FUNDERS working through referrals and advisors rather than open windows — the introduction matters. For lawyers based in Cape Town, Nairobi and Dakar, the Natural Justice entry; for emergency grants to defenders, the African Environmental Defenders Fund entry; for the litigation expenses fallback of finding you a lawyer, write to EDLC even without a grant application.

trackers.name: Slum Dwellers International — a network whose Board and Council are majority slum dwellers, whose federations enumerate their own settlements and co-produce plans for municipalities, and whose savings groups hold over a million households
trackers.desc: THE BOARD IS MAJORITY SLUM DWELLERS — placement note first: THIS IS A GLOBAL NETWORK, FILED UNDER SOUTH AFRICA BECAUSE ITS SECRETARIAT IS IN CAPE TOWN AND IT IS REGISTERED THERE; ITS AFRICAN AFFILIATES INCLUDE TANZANIA, UGANDA, ZAMBIA, ZIMBABWE, MALAWI, KENYA, NIGERIA AND SOUTH AFRICA AMONG OTHERS. THE GOVERNANCE CLAUSE IS THE REASON THIS ENTRY LEADS WITH IT: SDI IS A COMMUNITY-LED NETWORK, AND BASED ON THIS CORE PRINCIPLE, ITS GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE IS COMPRISED OF MAJORITY SLUM DWELLERS AT THE COUNCIL AND BOARD LEVEL — WITH THE SECRETARIAT ACCOUNTABLE TO A BOARD AND A COUNCIL OF FEDERATIONS MADE UP OF NOMINATED GRASSROOTS LEADERS FROM AFFILIATED FEDERATIONS. The professionals report to the residents, not the other way round. Almost every organisation in this file has a board of professionals with community representatives added; this one is inverted by constitution. When you are deciding whether an organisation is really community-led, that is the question: who is the majority on the board, and who is accountable to whom? ITS ORIGIN: LAUNCHED IN 1996 WHEN FEDERATIONS OF THE URBAN POOR IN COUNTRIES INCLUDING INDIA AND SOUTH AFRICA AGREED THAT A GLOBAL PLATFORM COULD HELP THEIR LOCAL INITIATIVES DEVELOP ALTERNATIVES TO EVICTIONS WHILE ALSO INFLUENCING THE GLOBAL AGENDA FOR URBAN DEVELOPMENT — having begun in the early 1990s when SHACK DWELLERS FROM SOUTH AFRICA'S INFORMAL SETTLEMENTS BEGAN TO VISIT PAVEMENT DWELLERS LIVING ON THE STREETS OF MUMBAI. ALTERNATIVES TO EVICTIONS is the founding purpose. Not resisting eviction, offering an alternative — which is a different negotiating position and the reason municipalities sign with them. And it started with poor people from one country travelling to meet poor people in another, which is still described as the main driving force: PRACTICAL, FACE-TO-FACE LEARNING. THE METHOD, AND IT IS THE MOST TRANSFERABLE THING HERE: FEDERATIONS PROFILE, MAP, AND ENUMERATE THEIR SETTLEMENTS TO GATHER INVALUABLE PLANNING DATA AND CATALYSE COMMUNITY ACTION AND PARTNERSHIPS — THEY TYPICALLY COLLECT SOCIOECONOMIC DATA ABOUT THEIR OWN COMMUNITIES, WHICH THEY USE TO UNDERSTAND THEIR OWN CIRCUMSTANCES AND CREATE ALTERNATIVE SOLUTIONS, AND OFTEN DEVELOP OR CO-PRODUCE PLANS TO PRESENT TO LOCAL AUTHORITIES. The community counts itself, then arrives at the municipality with both the numbers and a plan. This file has recorded over and over that the side with the data wins — and here the data is collected by the residents, which makes it theirs to use and hard to dispute. If your settlement has never been enumerated, that is the first job, and there is a global network that teaches how. THE SCALE: MORE THAN 1 MILLION SLUM DWELLER HOUSEHOLDS ARE BROUGHT INTO SAVINGS GROUPS THAT PRIORITISE THE CENTRAL PARTICIPATION OF WOMEN, BUILDING TRUST AND COLLECTIVE CAPACITY; A DATA PLATFORM COMBINES HARD DATA AND RICH STORIES FROM URBAN POOR COMMUNITIES IN 224 CITIES; AND FEDERATIONS ARE HELPING PEOPLE IN 500 CITIES SECURE LAND RIGHTS AND PARTICIPATE IN INCOME GENERATING PROGRAMS. Women-centred savings collectives at the base, and the network's own description of the structure is worth copying whole: AN UNBROKEN THREAD FROM THE HOUSEHOLD TO THE SETTLEMENT, FROM THE SETTLEMENT TO THE CITY, FROM THE CITY TO THE COUNTRY AND FROM THE COUNTRY TO THE GLOBAL STAGE. That is what a movement looks like when it is built from the bottom, and every level is made of the one below it. THE AGREEMENTS THAT PROVE IT WORKS: THE SOUTH AFRICAN FEDERATION HAS SAVINGS GROUPS THROUGHOUT 8 OF THE COUNTRY'S PROVINCES AND A HISTORY OF MEMORANDA OF UNDERSTANDING — PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENTS — WITH MUNICIPALITIES ACROSS SOUTH AFRICA, INCLUDING FIVE NAMED METROS. Written agreements between a federation of the urban poor and the metros themselves. An MOU with your municipality is the document to aim for: it converts a community from a group the city removes into a party the city has signed with. Ask which of your neighbouring settlements has one and read it before you draft yours. AND THE INTERNATIONAL SEAT: SDI CO-CHAIRS THE INTERNATIONAL ADVISORY BOARD OF A UN HABITAT GLOBAL LAND TOOLS NETWORK PROGRAMME, AND WORKS CLOSELY WITH A CITIES ALLIANCE. A slum dwellers' network co-chairing the advisory board of the UN's land tools programme. The tools that get designed for measuring and recording land in your city are being designed with people who live in informal settlements in the room. AND IT DEFENDS ITS OWN: the network has issued public statements of SOLIDARITY CONDEMNING FORCED EVICTIONS in a named Lagos settlement. A network that will publish a statement about an eviction in a member country is a form of protection — and a reason for an isolated settlement to affiliate before the bulldozers arrive rather than after. WHO IT SUITS: any African informal settlement facing eviction, and any urban community that has never been counted. CAVEATS: URBAN-FOCUSED — rural land questions belong with this file's land coalition entries. For the savings groups that won direct access to a housing subsidy, South Africa's FEDUP and uTshani Fund entry, which also carries the Informal Settlement Network; for a community-managed revolving fund in Namibia, the Shack Dwellers Federation entry; for savings-based land purchase in Malawi, the CCODE entry.

trackers.name: IPACC — 135 indigenous peoples' organisations in 21 African countries, open to any legitimate organisation run by African indigenous peoples, with a secretariat that pays to get leaders to UN meetings and accreditation at seven international bodies
