THE NUMBERS THAT MATTER WHEN YOU CANNOT PAY: it has enlisted 750 lawyers and more than 50 paralegals who assist over 6,000 indigent clients PRO BONO each year, and it provides free legal representation to poor and vulnerable victims of human rights violations — not merely advice. WHERE IT IS: national office in Lagos, with zonal coordinators and offices in Oshogbo, Jos, Kano, Awka and Port Harcourt — which puts a door within reach of the south-west, the middle belt, the north, the south-east and the Niger Delta rather than the commercial capital alone. It holds observer status with the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights, so a case that exhausts domestic remedies has a route onward. Its work includes public interest litigation to improve the rule of law and governance, alongside its indigent defence, women's rights and criminal justice programmes. WHO IT SUITS: Nigerians who need representation and cannot afford a lawyer, including people detained or prosecuted in the course of a land or environmental dispute. CAVEATS: its published programme areas are rule of law, human security and women's rights — it is a general human rights and criminal justice organisation, NOT an environmental or land specialist, so approach it for representation rather than for technical land work. Demand plainly exceeds 6,000 clients a year. For urban eviction paralegals and community litigation funds, Nigeria's JEI entry; for oil-spill documentation, ERA and CEHRD.

trackers.name: Nigeria's Legal Aid Council — a statutory right to funded representation, and the documented reason almost nobody uses it
trackers.desc: WHAT YOU ARE ENTITLED TO: the Legal Aid Council of Nigeria, established by an Act of Parliament, which provides for rendering FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE to any indigent citizen of Nigeria whose right has been infringed, to enable them to ENGAGE THE SERVICES OF A LEGAL PRACTITIONER to prosecute their claim — subject to the Council satisfying itself that the alleged infringement is substantial and the need for financial or legal aid is real. That is a funded lawyer, not advice, and it is a statutory entitlement rather than a favour. THE BARRIER, DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN GUESSED: research on access to justice in Nigeria records that AWARENESS OF THE LEGAL AID COUNCIL IS LOW, and that the Council, the state courts and the National Human Rights Commission are all SITUATED IN THE STATE CAPITALS — so access remains a challenge for people in rural and remote areas and for those with low literacy. The entitlement is national; the offices are not. Budget for the journey to the state capital, and send someone who can read the forms. THE NON-JUDICIAL ROUTES BESIDE IT, worth knowing when a court case is impossible: the National Human Rights Commission, the Nigeria Police Force public complaints mechanism, and NGO pro bono services and human rights clinics. Nigeria's federal and state high courts, in Abuja and all 36 states, guarantee the right to complain and seek redress. WHO IT SUITS: indigent Nigerians whose rights have been infringed — including in a land, eviction or pollution matter — who need the state to pay for counsel. CAVEATS: A STATE BODY WITH A MEANS TEST AND A MERITS TEST, and the assessment of whether your claim is “substantial” is made by the Council itself; capacity and awareness are both documented as weak. For urban eviction paralegals and community litigation funds, Nigeria's JEI entry; for pro bono representation through a lawyers' network, LEDAP; for oil-spill documentation, ERA and CEHRD.

trackers.name: The Ekuri Initiative — two villages own 33,600 hectares, formed their own NGO to hold it, beat the loggers and stopped a 260-km superhighway; the state then copied the model into 33 communities
trackers.desc: HOW A COMMUNITY HOLDS AND DEFENDS ITS OWN FOREST: Old Ekuri and New Ekuri villages in Cross River State TOGETHER OWN 33,600 HECTARES of community forest — the LARGEST REMAINING COMMUNITY FOREST IN NIGERIA, held by about 6,200 Nkokoli people. THE VEHICLE, WHICH IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART: after watching neighbouring communities lose their forests to overexploitation and logging, in 1992 the community ESTABLISHED THE EKURI INITIATIVE AS A COMMUNITY-BASED NGO with a mandate in conservation, sustainable forest management, community development and poverty reduction, with PROCEEDS USED TO IMPROVE LIVELIHOODS AND BUILD INFRASTRUCTURE — a road, school, health centre, market and town hall; the Initiative took on the road project itself and built about four bridges and several culverts. Registering your own community NGO to hold and trade from the forest is what converts customary ownership into a body that can sign, sue, receive money and be replicated — and it is why Ekuri could act when the state would not. WHAT IT HAS SEEN OFF: the Initiative RESISTED THREATS FROM LOGGING COMPANIES and, more recently, ATTEMPTS BY STATE AUTHORITIES TO BUILD A 260-KM SUPERHIGHWAY that would have destroyed much of the community forest. THE REPLICATION, WHICH IS THE PROOF IT TRAVELS: the success inspired the CROSS RIVER STATE FORESTRY COMMISSION TO REWRITE ITS FORESTRY STRATEGY around community-based forest management; a donor supported the Commission to REPLICATE THE EKURI MODEL IN 33 FOREST COMMUNITIES, a British NGO in five more, and the NIGERIAN CONSERVATION FOUNDATION replicated it in Taraba State. Ekuri won the UNDP Equator Award in 2004; communities from Nigeria, Cameroon and beyond have visited to learn from it. Alongside, the Nigerian Conservation Foundation (ncfnigeria.org), founded 1980 and registered 1982 AS A CHARITABLE TRUST UNDER THE LAND (PERPETUAL SUCCESSION) ACT, holds and manages sites including the Lekki Conservation Centre and works in tripartite management with state governments and local communities. WHO IT SUITS: Nigerian forest communities wanting to hold, defend and earn from their own land, and anyone needing a domestic precedent to cite. CAVEATS: NIGERIAN FOREST ESTATES ARE CONTROLLED BY STATE GOVERNMENTS and community forest management is still building nationally; community leaders have warned that continued official disregard could make villagers doubt that conservation respects their survival rights. For statutory legal aid, Nigeria's Legal Aid Council entry; for urban eviction paralegals and community litigation funds, JEI; for oil-spill documentation, ERA and CEHRD.

trackers.name: ERA/FoEN's plantation and coalition work, plus Nigeria's state-level organisations — CENVIS in Calabar, HERANET in Owerri with legal assistance listed, and the national environmental directory
trackers.desc: THE PLANTATION LINE, AND THE ORGANISATIONS WITH STATE ADDRESSES: ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS ACTION / FRIENDS OF THE EARTH NIGERIA (ERA/FoEN, erafoen.org) WAS FOUNDED ON 11 JANUARY 1993 to deal with environmental human rights issues in Nigeria, aiming to PROMOTE ENVIRONMENTALLY RESPONSIBLE GOVERNMENT AND COMMUNITIES. ITS NAMED PRIORITY AREAS INCLUDE BUILDING COALITIONS AND STRENGTHENING ALLIANCES, AND REGIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL ADVOCACY TO EXPOSE THE VIOLATIONS CONNECTED TO INDUSTRIAL PLANTATION COMPANIES, WHO ARE DRIVERS OF BIODIVERSITY LOSS AT ALL LEVELS OF WORK. Industrial plantations named as the driver, and the response named as international advocacy. If an oil palm or rubber concession is taking your community's land, that is a body whose stated programme is exposing exactly that — and it works at the international level, which is where a plantation company's buyers and certifiers sit. WHAT IT CONVENES AND HOSTS: ERA COORDINATES AND HOSTS OILWATCH INTERNATIONAL, a tobacco control regional initiative and a national tobacco control alliance, and is involved in a GREEN ALLIANCE NIGERIA; it runs capacity building on sustainable solutions to FOREST AND BIODIVERSITY CONSERVATION THROUGH COMMUNITY EXCHANGES, WORKSHOPS AND WEBINARS AND ITS OWN NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL CONSULTATION; and it works on MOVEMENT BUILDING OF LABOUR GROUPS, CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS AND COMMUNITIES, with one of its coordinators also running an Africa climate justice group COMPRISING 17 MOVEMENT-BASED AND ALLIED ORGANISATIONS AND PARTNERS IN THE AFRICAN REGION. Community EXCHANGES is the item to ask about: sending your people to a village that has already faced what you are facing is the cheapest training there is, and ERA runs them. THE STATE-LEVEL BODIES, WITH ADDRESSES: CITIZENS FOR ENVIRONMENTAL SAFETY (CENVIS), CALABAR, SUPPORTED SINCE 1999 BY NAMED INTERNATIONAL FUNDERS INCLUDING A GRASSROOTS GRANTS FUND, ALONGSIDE ERA AND THE NGO COALITION FOR ENVIRONMENT — carrying out COMMUNITY-BASED PROGRAMMES ON SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT, GRASSROOTS TRAINING ON THE USE OF NON-TIMBER FOREST PRODUCTS, A CAMPAIGN AGAINST ILLEGAL LOGGING IN CROSS RIVER STATE, AND DEVELOPMENT OF A GNETUM AFRICANUM FARM AT LOCAL COMMUNITIES for the community dwellers. Twenty-five years of small international grants keeping one Calabar organisation running is what a grassroots grants fund is for. And a Gnetum farm is the same move this file has seen work elsewhere: grow the forest product people are stripping, and the stripping stops. HUMAN AND ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS ACTION NETWORK (HERANET), 10 MBONU OJIKE STREET, IKENEGBU LAYOUT, OWERRI, PO BOX 2236 — whose purpose is TO EMPOWER LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND PEOPLE TO DEFEND THEIR SOCIO-ECONOMIC, CIVIL, POLITICAL, DEVELOPMENTAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS, working for a society WHERE LOCAL PEOPLE PARTICIPATE ACTIVELY IN DECISION MAKING AND IN THE RUNNING OF THE AFFAIRS OF THE STATE — AND WHOSE LISTED CAUSE AREAS INCLUDE LEGAL ASSISTANCE. A south-eastern organisation with a street address that lists legal assistance among its own cause areas is a rare combination outside Lagos and Port Harcourt. If your case is in the south-east, start there. ALSO NAMED: GREEN CONCERN FOR DEVELOPMENT, which with ERA organised a forum on CLIMATE CHANGE, REDD AND FOREST DEPENDENT COMMUNITY RIGHTS IN CROSS RIVER STATE; and a PUBLISHED DIRECTORY OF ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATIONS AND GOVERNMENT ENVIRONMENTAL AGENCIES IN NIGERIA listing each with its web address, including the NIGERIA ENVIRONMENTAL STUDY ACTION TEAM (NEST), the WOMEN ENVIRONMENTAL PROGRAMME (WEP), the WASTES MANAGEMENT SOCIETY OF NIGERIA and the DEPARTMENT OF CLIMATE CHANGE at the Federal Ministry of Environment. A directory that lists the government agencies alongside the NGOs tells you who to write to and who to copy in the same afternoon. WHO IT SUITS: Nigerian communities facing a plantation or logging, and anyone in Cross River or the south-east. CAVEATS: ADVOCACY ORGANISATIONS — for litigation see below. For two toll-free green lines, Nigeria's ERA entry; for rural-focused documentation in the Niger Delta, CEHRD; for community paralegals, Justice and Empowerment Initiatives; for 750 lawyers, LEDAP; for two villages owning 33,600 hectares, the Ekuri Initiative entry.

trackers.name: The African Development Bank's Independent Review Mechanism — any group of two or more harmed people can complain — plus Accountability Counsel and the African Coalition for Corporate Accountability who help communities file (continental, filed here because the file has no regional key)
trackers.desc: TWO PEOPLE IS ENOUGH TO FILE — placement note first: THE MECHANISM AND THE COALITIONS BELOW ARE CONTINENTAL AND GLOBAL, FILED UNDER NIGERIA ONLY BECAUSE THIS FILE HAS NO REGIONAL KEY. The mechanism covers projects in every AfDB member country, so wherever you are in Africa, this applies. THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW MECHANISM WAS ESTABLISHED BY THE AFRICAN DEVELOPMENT BANK IN 2004 TO ADDRESS COMPLAINTS MADE BY ANY GROUP OF TWO OR MORE PEOPLE WHO HAVE BEEN HARMED, OR WHO ARE LIKELY TO BE HARMED, BY A PROJECT FUNDED BY THE AfDB GROUP. Two or more people. That is the lowest threshold of any route in this entire file — no registered organisation, no lawyer, no association, no minimum number of signatures. Two neighbours can file. And note OR WHO ARE LIKELY TO BE HARMED: you do not have to wait until the damage is done, which is the single most important word in the clause for a community facing a project that has not started. WHAT IT ACTUALLY TESTS: THE IRM WAS DESIGNED TO MAKE SURE THAT THE AfDB FOLLOWS ITS OWN POLICIES AND PROCEDURES DURING THE DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF ITS PROJECTS. You are not asking the bank to agree the project is bad. You are asking whether the bank followed its own rules. That is a far narrower and far more winnable question, and it is the same framing that worked in the Sudd dredging case in this file — the process, not the merits. WHAT YOU CAN COMPLAIN ABOUT: COMPLAINTS MAY RELATE TO THE SOCIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS OF PROJECTS IN SECTORS RANGING FROM TRANSPORTATION, HYDROPOWER, AGRICULTURE OR INFRASTRUCTURE — AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, WORKERS, COMMUNITIES AND GROUPS OF INDIVIDUALS WHO ARE HARMED BY AN AfDB-SUPPORTED PROJECT CAN USE THE IRM PROCESS TO ADDRESS THEIR GRIEVANCE. Roads, dams, plantations and infrastructure, all named. WORKERS are listed separately from communities, so people employed on the project can complain about it too — which is often the only group with documents. AND THE INSTRUCTIONS EXIST, FREE: A BROCHURE COVERING THE IRM POLICY AS REVISED IN 2015 AND EXPLAINING HOW TO FILE A COMPLAINT WAS PRODUCED BY TWO NAMED ACCOUNTABILITY ORGANISATIONS. Somebody has already written the how-to. Ask for the brochure before you draft anything — these mechanisms fail complaints on form, not on substance. WHO WILL HELP YOU FILE: ACCOUNTABILITY COUNSEL AMPLIFIES THE VOICES OF COMMUNITIES HARMED BY INTERNATIONALLY FINANCED PROJECTS AND, AT THE REQUEST OF COMMUNITIES, ASSISTS PEOPLE IN USING ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICES TO DEFEND THEIR RIGHTS AND REMEDY HARM — ITS TEAM SPECIALISING IN NON-JUDICIAL COMPLAINT OFFICES ESTABLISHED TO RECEIVE COMMUNITY COMPLAINTS, WITH PARTICULAR ATTENTION TO WOMEN, CHILDREN AND OTHER MARGINALISED GROUPS. AT THE REQUEST OF COMMUNITIES is stated — it does not arrive uninvited, you ask. And its published coverage names the mechanisms of twelve institutions including the AfDB Group, a world bank private-sector arm, European and Asian development banks, a BRICS bank, a green climate fund and named European development finance institutions. Twelve institutions, each with its own complaints office. Find out which one financed the project on your land and there is almost certainly an office attached to it — and an organisation that specialises in that exact office. THE AFRICAN NETWORK: THE AFRICAN COALITION FOR CORPORATE ACCOUNTABILITY GATHERS CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS WORKING ON MINING AND OTHER EXTRACTIVE INDUSTRIES, PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECURITY SECTOR ACCOUNTABILITY, NATURAL RESOURCE RIGHTS INCLUDING LAND ACQUISITION, TENURE, AND PROPERTY RIGHTS, FINANCIAL REGULATORY POLICY, AND ACCOUNTABILITY MECHANISMS FOR HUMAN AND PEOPLE'S RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS — ITS MISSION BEING TO FACILITATE A CROSS-BORDER ALLIANCE OF AFRICAN CSOs AND COMMUNITIES, AND IT PROVIDES A REGIONAL PLATFORM TO SHARE INFORMATION AND KNOWLEDGE AMONG ITS MEMBERS AND COMMUNITIES. PRIVATE SECURITY SECTOR ACCOUNTABILITY is on that list. Where the guards on a concession are the daily problem, that is a named workstream and a rare one — most land organisations will not touch it. AND THE TRAINING ROUTE: the coalition facilitated a half-day TRAINING ON DEVELOPMENT FINANCE AND CORPORATE ACCOUNTABILITY as part of a Short Course on Business and Human Rights hosted by a university human rights centre, for LLM students, coalition members and STAFF FROM VARIOUS AFRICAN NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS INSTITUTIONS. National human rights institution staff being trained in development finance complaints is worth knowing: your country's own human rights commission may have someone who has done this course. Ask. WHO IT SUITS: any two or more people anywhere in Africa harmed or likely to be harmed by a development-bank-financed project. CAVEATS: NON-JUDICIAL MECHANISMS PRODUCE FINDINGS AND RECOMMENDATIONS, NOT ORDERS — this file has recorded elsewhere that a complaint stopped a project and elsewhere that funds went untraced. Use it alongside domestic routes, not instead of them. For the complaint filed by six Mozambican organisations on five named grounds, Mozambique's Livaningo entry; for a complaint on behalf of 25,200 people, Chad's GRAMPTC entry; for an organisation that investigates who financed the project, Uganda's Witness Radio entry.

trackers.name: ELAW — the alliance whose scientists critique environmental impact assessments for community lawyers free, with 300+ advocates in 80 countries, a defending-defenders programme and a guidebook on challenging oil and gas projects
trackers.desc: THE SCIENTIST WHO READS THE ASSESSMENT FOR YOU — placement note first: THIS IS A GLOBAL ALLIANCE, FILED UNDER NIGERIA ONLY BECAUSE THIS FILE HAS NO GLOBAL KEY AND NIGERIA HOLDS ITS DENSEST CONCENTRATION OF OIL-AND-GAS AFFECTED COMMUNITIES, WHICH IS WHAT THE GUIDEBOOK BELOW IS FOR. It works in over 80 countries. THE OFFER, IN ITS OWN WORDS: IT IS A GLOBAL ALLIANCE OF ATTORNEYS, SCIENTISTS, AND OTHER ADVOCATES COLLABORATING ACROSS BORDERS, WHICH PROVIDES LEGAL, SCIENTIFIC, SECURITY, AND ORGANIZATIONAL EXPERTISE TO HELP PUBLIC INTEREST LAWYERS ADVANCE THEIR WORK — EMPOWERING LOCAL ADVOCATES TO CHALLENGE HARMFUL PROJECTS BY OFFERING LEGAL AND SCIENTIFIC SUPPORT, CRITIQUING ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENTS, AND PROVIDING ECONOMIC INSIGHTS. CRITIQUING ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENTS is the sentence to underline. This file records case after case where a community lost because it could not afford a scientist to read the developer's impact assessment and say what was wrong with it. Here is an alliance whose scientists do exactly that, and whose stated route in is through the lawyer working on your case. If you have a lawyer and no expert, this is the missing half. AND ECONOMIC INSIGHTS, which is rarer still — somebody to test the developer's claim about jobs and revenue, which is usually the only argument the community is given. THE SCALE: MORE THAN 300 PUBLIC INTEREST ADVOCATES FROM 80 COUNTRIES WORK TOGETHER THROUGH THE NETWORK; IT HAS PROVIDED LEGAL AND SCIENTIFIC SUPPORT ON THOUSANDS OF ENVIRONMENTAL CASES; AND IN A SINGLE YEAR ADVOCATES CALL ON THE NETWORK FOR ASSISTANCE WITH MORE THAN 400 PROJECTS. Four hundred requests a year across eighty countries means this is a working service, not a standing offer nobody uses. It also means the answer to whether they will help is: ask, and expect a queue. ITS ORIGIN IS A LESSON IN ITSELF: PUBLIC INTEREST LAWYERS FROM 10 COUNTRIES FOUNDED IT IN 1989 AT A PUBLIC INTEREST LAW CONFERENCE — AS THEY TALKED, THEY DISCOVERED THAT COMMUNITIES IN THEIR COUNTRIES WERE FACING SIMILAR ENVIRONMENTAL CHALLENGES, AND REALISED THAT IF THEY COULD SHARE STRATEGIES AND LEGAL AND SCIENTIFIC INFORMATION ACROSS BORDERS, THEY COULD PROTECT COMMUNITIES AND THE ENVIRONMENT MORE EFFECTIVELY. Ten lawyers from ten countries at one conference discovering they had the same problem. That is the same founding shape this file recorded in Madagascar with fifty-five fishers and in Bangui with two hundred NGOs — people who were already working alone find out they are not alone, and the network is what they build next. ITS GOVERNING PRINCIPLE, WHICH IS THE TEST TO APPLY TO ANY FOREIGN OFFER OF HELP: ELAW ADVOCATES, WORKING IN THEIR HOME COUNTRIES, KNOW BEST HOW TO PROTECT THE ENVIRONMENT — AND THE KEY TO THE STRATEGY IS LOCATING STRONG LAWYERS COMMITTED TO PROTECTING THE ENVIRONMENT IN THEIR HOME COUNTRIES, SO THAT THE WORK BOTH WINS VICTORIES AND BUILDS LASTING, LOCAL CAPACITY. The foreign body supplies the science and the local lawyer runs the case. Compare that with any arrangement where the visiting organisation holds the file and the local partner is a subcontractor — this file has recorded both, and the difference shows up when the funding ends. THE PROGRAMME FOR WHEN IT TURNS DANGEROUS: DEFENDING DEFENDERS IS A NAMED FOCUS AREA — ENHANCING THE SAFETY OF ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVISTS FACING THREATS, ENABLING THEM TO CONTINUE THEIR VITAL WORK — alongside BIODIVERSITY, CLIMATE, FOSSIL FUELS AND PLASTIC POLLUTION; and the alliance records that LAWYER COLLEAGUES AND THEIR COMMUNITY PARTNERS ARE UNDER INCREASING ATTACK FOR DEFENDING AND ADVANCING THE HUMAN RIGHT TO A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT. SECURITY expertise listed alongside legal and scientific. Very few organisations in this file offer that as a standing service rather than an emergency grant. AND THE FREE DOCUMENT TO ASK FOR BY NAME: A GUIDEBOOK AIMING TO PROVIDE PUBLIC INTEREST ENVIRONMENTAL ADVOCATES AND THE COMMUNITIES THEY REPRESENT WITH SUFFICIENT UNDERSTANDING TO CHALLENGE OIL AND GAS PROJECTS THAT ARE UNACCEPTABLE FROM AN ENVIRONMENTAL OR SOCIAL PERSPECTIVE. Written for the advocates AND the communities they represent — so it is meant to be readable by people who are not lawyers. If an oil or gas project is reaching your land, that guidebook is the first thing to obtain, and it is free. HOW ADVOCATES JOIN: IT HAS BROUGHT NEARLY 300 ENVIRONMENTAL ADVOCATES FROM AROUND THE WORLD TO THE UNITED STATES AS FELLOWS, AND HAS CELEBRATED WITH MANY PARTNERS WHO WON THE GOLDMAN ENVIRONMENTAL PRIZE. The fellowship is the route this file recorded in Egypt, where a lawyer took one and came home to found his country's first public interest environmental law firm. It also hires its own scientists — including a PhD community ecologist with a marine and coastal background, REMOTE FROM ANYWHERE IN THE WORLD — so African scientists can be on the supplying side, not only the receiving one. WHO IT SUITS: any African community lawyer facing a project whose impact assessment needs expert challenge, and defenders under threat. CAVEATS: IT WORKS THROUGH PUBLIC INTEREST LAWYERS rather than directly with communities — you need an advocate to make the request. For the Nigerian organisation founded 11 January 1993 that coordinates Oilwatch International, Nigeria's ERA/FoEN entry; for the Egyptian lawyer who used the fellowship to found a national firm, Egypt's EFER entry; for litigation expenses on a one-case basis, the EDLC entry; for legal-action grants of five to fifteen thousand dollars, the Global Greengrants entry.

trackers.name: CI Ventures (Conservation International Ventures) and two further conservation funders — three money routes with their real terms — US$200,000–500,000 loans to community enterprises, a $9 million grant-maker that takes no unsolicited proposals, and the land-purchase funder's four protected-area types including indigenous land titling
trackers.desc: LOANS, GRANTS, AND THE DOOR THAT IS SHUT UNLESS YOU ARE INVITED — placement note first: THESE ARE INTERNATIONAL FUNDERS, FILED UNDER NIGERIA BECAUSE THIS BUCKET CARRIED NO CONSERVATION-FINANCE RESOURCE; THEIR AFRICAN ELIGIBILITY IS STATED BELOW. THE LOAN FUND, WHICH IS THE RARE ONE: AN INVESTMENT FUND PROVIDES LOANS TO SMALL- AND MEDIUM-SIZED ENTERPRISES THAT OPERATE IN THE FORESTS, OCEANS AND GRASSLANDS WHERE ITS PARENT ORGANISATION WORKS — IN SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE OR FORESTRY, ECOTOURISM OR WILD FISHERIES — BUSINESSES SHARING A COMMITMENT TO PRACTICES THAT BENEFIT ECOSYSTEMS AND HUMAN WELL-BEING AT THE SAME TIME, WITH TYPICAL INVESTMENTS OF US$200,000 TO US$500,000 AND KENYA AND SOUTH AFRICA NAMED AMONG ITS COUNTRIES. A LOAN, not a grant, to a community enterprise. That matters because almost every funder in this file gives money for a project that ends; a loan to a fishery cooperative or a community tourism venture assumes the thing will earn and continue. If your community has a working enterprise rather than a project, this is a different and more durable kind of money — and it also means somebody has judged the business viable, which is itself an argument. THE GRANT-MAKER, AND THE NOTICE THAT SAVES YOU WEEKS: SINCE 2013 IT HAS GRANTED CLOSE TO NINE MILLION DOLLARS TO OVER 60 ORGANIZATIONS IN 15 COUNTRIES, FUNDING PROGRAMMES IN HUMAN EMPOWERMENT, WILDLIFE PROTECTION AND LAND CONSERVATION IN SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA — BUT IT DOES NOT ACCEPT UNSOLICITED GRANT PROPOSALS, AND ONLY ORGANIZATIONS THAT ARE INVITED TO APPLY WILL BE ABLE TO SUBMIT, WITH A PUBLISHED EMAIL ADDRESS FOR MORE INFORMATION. NO UNSOLICITED PROPOSALS is the single most useful sentence a funder can publish, and almost none do. Do not spend a month writing to this one. What you can do is write to the published address asking how organisations get identified, and get known to the people who make the invitations — which is a different task from applying, and the one that actually works with invitation-only funders. THE LAND-PURCHASE FUNDER'S FOUR PROTECTED-AREA TYPES, WHICH ARE THE MENU TO CHOOSE FROM BEFORE ANYONE CHOOSES FOR YOU: PRIVATE RESERVES — A PARCEL, OR SEVERAL PARCELS, OF LAND SECURED FOR CONSERVATION AND MAINTAINED BY PARTNERS IN PERPETUITY; NATIONAL PARK — LAND DECLARED AND PROTECTED BY THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT AND OPEN FOR PUBLIC ENJOYMENT; COMMUNITY FOREST — WHERE LOCAL PEOPLE ARE DIRECTLY INVOLVED AS CRITICAL STAKEHOLDERS IN THE MANAGEMENT OF THE PROTECTED LAND AND WORK CLOSELY WITH PARTNERS AND THE GOVERNMENT TO MAKE LAND-USE DECISIONS; AND INDIGENOUS LAND TITLING — WHERE INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES GAIN LEGAL RIGHTS TO THEIR LAND WITH THE HELP OF PARTNERS AND GOVERNMENT. Four outcomes from the same money, and they are not equal for you. A national park is the one where the state ends up holding your land; a community forest keeps you in the management decisions; indigenous land titling ends with the title in your hands. When a funder offers to protect your area, ask which of the four it is proposing and say which one you want — the same grant can produce any of them. THE ELIGIBILITY RULE, WHICH IS THE PRACTICAL BARRIER: THE APPLICANT ORGANIZATION MUST BE AUTHORIZED TO WORK WITHIN THE COUNTRY OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT, AND LEGAL DOCUMENTATION WILL BE REQUIRED AT A LATER STAGE; AND THE PROPOSED PROJECT NEEDS TO BE BASED IN THE SUBTROPICS OR TROPICS. Authorised to work in the country, with papers produced later. So registration is the gate again — and this file has recorded the registration requirements for most African countries precisely because this gate keeps appearing. THE SOVEREIGN-SCALE INSTRUMENT, WORTH KNOWING EXISTS: THREE AFRICAN COUNTRIES ARE IN TALKS TO STRUCTURE DEBT-FOR-NATURE SWAPS WORTH MORE THAN $500 MILLION, ALLOWING COUNTRIES TO REDUCE PART OF THEIR DEBT IN EXCHANGE FOR CONCRETE COMMITMENTS TO PROTECT ECOSYSTEMS — AND TWO NAMED AFRICAN COUNTRIES HAVE ALREADY USED SIMILAR MECHANISMS OVER THE PAST DECADE. Half a billion dollars of national debt exchanged for protection commitments. Those commitments become rules on actual ground, and the people living on that ground are rarely in the negotiation. If your country is doing one, the question to ask early is which areas are pledged and who was consulted — because the deal is signed in a capital and enforced in a village. THE CONTEXT FIGURE TO CARRY: AFRICA REMAINS LARGELY SIDELINED IN GLOBAL CLIMATE FINANCE, RECEIVING ONLY ABOUT 1% OF TOTAL FLOWS, WHILE BEING AMONG THE MOST EXPOSED TO CLIMATE RISKS, FACING RECURRING FLOODS, DROUGHTS AND LANDSLIDES — AND THE COST OF CAPITAL IS HIGH, PUTTING AFRICA AT A DISADVANTAGE. One per cent of global climate finance for the most exposed continent. That is the number for any argument about whether the money exists — it exists, and it goes elsewhere. AND THE CONTINENTAL RESTORATION PARTNERSHIP: AN AFRICAN FOREST LANDSCAPE RESTORATION INITIATIVE AIMS TO RESTORE MORE THAN 100 MILLION HECTARES OF LAND IN AFRICA BY 2030, WITH COMMITMENTS FROM 31 AFRICAN COUNTRIES, AIMING TO INCREASE FOOD SECURITY, COMBAT POVERTY AND REDUCE CLIMATE IMPACTS. Thirty-one countries have already pledged hectares to restoration. Those pledges have to be met somewhere — and a community offering land it wants restored rather than taken is offering a government exactly what it promised. Ask your forestry ministry what your country pledged and whether your area counts toward it. WHO IT SUITS: African community enterprises seeking a loan, organisations wanting to know which funders are invitation-only, and communities being offered a protected-area designation. CAVEATS: ONE OF THESE IS CLOSED TO UNSOLICITED APPLICATIONS and all require a registered applicant organisation. For the land-purchase funder's Rapid Feasibility Awards and its two eligibility conditions, Zambia's Rainforest Trust entry; for the grant that completed a land purchase in perpetuity, South Africa's World Land Trust entry; for the deal forms and the eviction record, Kenya's conservation land buyers entry.

trackers.name: LASEPA — Lagos State Environmental Protection Agency
trackers.desc: WHO INVESTIGATES IN LAGOS: LASEPA is the state's environmental regulator, and its published functions include investigating and resolving public complaints and disputes and mediating environmental disputes between complainants and respondents — a named mediation role between a resident and whoever is causing the harm, which few regulators state outright. USE WHAT IT MEASURES: it samples water, air and noise during industrial visits to establish compliance and inspects Environmental Management Plans at iron and steel facilities, so it generates exactly the evidence a complaint needs and that evidence can be requested. Its work is organised across the state's 57 local government areas and LCDAs — the tier a community actually sits in — and it runs sanitation inspections of industrial facilities and markets on the last Thursday of each month.

trackers.name: Complaints Desk — Lagos State Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources
trackers.desc: A SECOND ROUTE, AND A DIFFERENT ONE: the Lagos State Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources runs its own online complaint form to a Complaint Task Force, covering issues in your neighbourhood — and, separately, misconduct by an official that you witnessed. USE THAT SECOND LIMB: when the problem is the regulator or an inspector rather than the developer, a complaint to the agency itself goes nowhere, and this is the channel built for it.

trackers.name: Ifriqiya
trackers.desc: Ifriqiya is an association committed to Human Rights, the environment, and development. Founded in August 2019, it began its activities officially following the publication of the Official Gazette number 10 of the year 2020, dated February 4, 2020. The association aims to contribute to the achievement of sustainable development goals through a tripartite vision centered on 1) working for the defense of rights and freedoms and contributing to the promotion of a human rights culture based on universal principles, 2) advocating for environmental issues, and 3) contributing to enhancing the role of Tunisia and its civil society in the African integration process by supporting the development of a common continental policy, particularly in the association's areas of intervention, within the framework of the African Union. To achieve these objectives, the association strives to be a source of proposals and a center of expertise for players in these fields, with the aim of inspiring new ideas and strengthening the constructive participation of young people in decision-making processes at local, national and continental levels.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a pan-African feminist rapid-response fund with reach across all 54 African countries — small grants released quickly for unanticipated, time-critical situations rather than planned programme work, covering safety and protection needs when defenders are threatened and short windows for advocacy after an unexpected event. WHO IT SUITS: women's rights organisations, feminist collectives and movements in which women or gender-diverse people are the primary decision-makers. It does NOT fund individuals, and the action must be strategic, genuinely unanticipated, and completable in under three months. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is emergency money for a moment, not a budget for a campaign — decisions are fast and grants are modest.

trackers.name: Cour des comptes de Tunisie
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Tunisia — audits government accounts and the use of public money.

trackers.name: Instance Nationale d’Accès à l’Information (INAI)
trackers.desc: Tunisia's independent access-to-information authority under Organic Law 2016-22: it receives appeals, issues binding decisions, publishes its rulings, monitors compliance and reports annually. USE IT: appeal a refused request to INAI rather than back to the body that refused it — its decisions bind.

trackers.name: The Legal Agenda – Tunisia
trackers.desc: Tunisia bureau of the Legal Agenda, the Beirut-based research and advocacy nonprofit, monitoring and critically analysing the courts, judicial independence and legal policy in Tunisia through research, media and litigation.

trackers.name: INPDP — Instance Nationale de Protection des Données Personnelles
trackers.desc: INPDP — Instance Nationale de Protection des Données Personnelles — Tunisia’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: I Watch (أنا يقظ)
trackers.desc: Tunisia's independent anti-corruption watchdog and Transparency International chapter — files access-to-information requests and corruption complaints, supports whistleblowers, and runs Chahed Meter, tracking the head of government's promises made before parliament.

trackers.name: Registre National des Entreprises
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: TUNEPS
trackers.desc: Tunisia's national e-procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Tunisia, and for how much.

trackers.name: Conseil de gestion — your community is already a legal person
trackers.desc: YOU MAY NOT NEED TO FORM ANYTHING. Under loi n° 64-28 of 4 June 1964, each group possessing a collective land constitutes a legal person endowed with civil personality, represented by a conseil de gestion of members elected by the collectivity, plus members designated by the governor who have a consultative voice only. So the community already holds legal personality without forming an association, and the governor's appointees do not vote — establish who on your conseil is elected and who is designated. THE FRANCHISE: the decree of 2 July 1965 gave the vote to every member of the collectivity aged at least 20, where the 1938 rule recognised only heads of family — making women electors in their own right for the first time. The conseil is elected for 5 years, and the law of 14 January 1971 expanded its powers from mere management to very extensive powers. THE CONSENT TO INSIST ON: financial operations for the cession, lease or contribution to capital of collective lands require the approval of the conseil de gestion AND of the governor — the governor agreeing is not enough. The conseil is also empowered to arbitrate land disputes over collective lands.

trackers.name: Protected areas — the municipal route is closed, aim at the ministry
trackers.desc: THE STRUCTURAL FACT THAT SHOULD DIRECT YOUR EFFORT: local public collectivities hold no role in the creation, management or exploitation of terrestrial or maritime natural spaces in Tunisia. Unlike Albania, Montenegro or Luxembourg, where this map records municipal declaration routes, the commune is not a route here — aim at the ministry. WHICH MINISTRY DEPENDS ON THE SPACE: forest protected areas fall under agriculture, marine areas under environment, governed by the Code forestier 1988 and the marine protected areas law of 20 July 2009 — and each protected area needs its own special text to be applicable. National parks are the bulk of Tunisian protection, 237,000 of 250,000 hectares. HOW ONE IS CREATED: bodies act as localisateurs and submit opinions to the ministry responsible for forests; once localisation is done the administration begins the land operations — in principle purchase or expropriation of privately owned land. TWO BODIES THAT DO NOT YET FUNCTION, worth knowing before you address a complaint to them: a national nature body lacking the decree to organise it and name members, and the Commission des aires marines et côtières protégées foreseen by the 2009 law, which had not come into being. AND THE HONEST NOTE ON CONSEILS DE GESTION: Tunisian analysis records administrative tutelle, lack of means and competences, poor governance and non-participation undermining them in practice.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: FTDES environmental justice department — regional offices that take up local pollution fights, and have stopped projects
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Tunisian Forum for Economic and Social Rights runs a standing environmental justice department with paid staff, alongside its work on labour, women's and migrants' rights. THE REASON IT MATTERS MORE THAN A NATIONAL NGO IN TUNIS: it operates through regional sections — Kairouan, Monastir/Ksibet el Mediouni, Gafsa/Redeyef, Kasserine — that take up local fights directly. Its own reporting records dozens of local environmental movements accompanied and supported on water access, industrial pollution, waste and wastewater, with named outcomes: water supply obtained for particular communities, a new municipal waste arrangement negotiated, and the halting of environmentally destructive projects at Jbel Fadloum and Ain Draham. It has also assembled a case against the national water utility over cutoffs in the mining basin, and connects households to water — seven families and a rural school through one project cycle. It publishes a half-yearly environmental justice report and runs regional forums that put officials in a room with affected residents. THE HARD CASE IT IS CURRENTLY LOSING, WHICH YOU SHOULD KNOW BEFORE RELYING ON THE COURTS HERE: at Gabès, where the state chemical group's phosphate fertiliser plant is the country's heaviest pollution file, a summary application to suspend production was rejected in February 2026 for want of proof of harm — FTDES called the ruling a serious regression and said the absence-of-evidence argument ignored established, documented data. Expect the evidentiary burden to be the fight. WHO IT SUITS: Tunisian communities facing industrial pollution, water dispossession or waste siting, especially in the interior and the mining basin. CAVEATS: FTDES is a rights organisation that litigates through instructed lawyers, not a law firm; no published intake route or case-selection criteria were found; and it works in a political environment where social movements have been criminalised, which it says limits the visibility and credibility of environmental struggles.

trackers.name: Observatoire tunisien de l'eau — report a cut, a leak or bad water on watchwater.tn and it goes into a public map the utility has to answer
trackers.desc: WHERE TO REPORT: the Tunisian Water Observatory, an associative project created in 2016 by the association Nomad 08 of Redeyef to defend the right of access to water, running the alert platform watchwater.tn. HOW IT WORKS AND WHY IT IS A RESOURCE RATHER THAN A CAMPAIGN: citizens report unannounced cuts, poor supply, leaks, water quality problems and water-related protests; the database is fed mainly by citizens, plus trained alerters and observatory administrators who VERIFY each alert and ensure the information reaches the national water utility (SONEDE) and the municipalities. The output is a participatory map — the “Carte de la Soif” (Thirst Map) — published monthly. An individual complaint to a utility disappears; a verified entry on a public national map does not. THE RECORD SHOWS THE SCALE, and it is what makes the map hard to dismiss: 1,893 alerts in 2023, of which 1,592 were cuts, sparing no governorate; a reported record 608 citizen alerts in July 2026 — 549 of them unannounced cuts or disruptions, 34 protest movements demanding access to water, 13 network leaks and 12 quality alerts. Monthly maps name the worst-hit governorates, which have included Kef, Ben Arous, Gafsa, Kasserine, Sousse, Monastir, Gabès, Médenine, Bizerte and Tunis. The observatory has also run field monitoring of the government's own summer water plan. WHO IT SUITS: Tunisian households and neighbourhoods facing cuts, contamination or supply failure — and anyone needing dated, third-party-verified evidence that a shortage is real and recurring. CAVEATS: it records and publicises — it does not restore your supply or litigate; its own staff note that generalised cuts have continued despite years of protest. For labour, environmental justice and regional case support, Tunisia's FTDES entry.

trackers.name: Tunisia's bureau d'aide judiciaire — a legal aid office sitting inside each court of first instance, under law 2002-52
trackers.desc: WHERE TO APPLY: under law n°2002-52 of 3 June 2002 on judicial aid, Tunisia operates a BUREAU DE L'AIDE JUDICIAIRE — a specialised office that rules on applications for judicial aid, with its SEAT AT THE COURT OF FIRST INSTANCE. Unlike Morocco, recorded in this file as having no framework law on legal aid, Tunisia has a statute and a standing office; the practical problem is that few people know where it sits or who decides. WHO DECIDES YOUR APPLICATION, because knowing the room matters: the bureau comprises the public prosecutor or a deputy as PRESIDENT; a representative of the finance ministry; a lawyer registered at the court of cassation, appointed by the justice minister on the proposal of the bar council; and a court clerk. Note that the state's prosecutor chairs the body deciding whether you get a lawyer, and the finance ministry sits on it — that is the room, and it is worth knowing before you assume the decision is purely technical. TWO RULES THAT DECIDE HOW FAR YOUR GRANT STRETCHES: judicial aid is granted to cover the costs of a SINGLE CASE — but where protecting the right, or the procedure itself, requires seizing more than one court or chamber at the same time, the competent bureau MAY decide that the aid covers all costs arising from the cases brought, with the clerk notifying the president of the bureau at the seized court so auxiliaries can be appointed. And on APPEAL, the beneficiary may keep the assigned lawyer or bailiff — PROVIDED THE BUREAU IS INFORMED. That notification is a small step that silently ends representation if missed. WHO IT SUITS: Tunisians who cannot pay court costs or lawyer's fees in a land, expropriation or environmental case, and anyone taking a case to appeal. CAVEATS: A STATE PROCEDURE, NOT AN ALLY — it decides whether the state pays, and published research has found Tunisian legal aid poorly known and unevenly delivered; the aid covers costs, not the outcome. For regional casework and environmental justice, Tunisia's FTDES entry; for water cuts and supply failures, the Water Observatory.

trackers.name: Tunisia's terres collectives and their elected conseils de gestion — the sole deciders over ~3 million hectares, and the 2026 bill that would convert them into individual sellable titles
trackers.desc: WHO DECIDES ON COLLECTIVE LAND: Tunisia's TERRES COLLECTIVES (tribal lands) cover almost A THIRD OF AGRICULTURAL LAND — about 3 MILLION HECTARES, 1.5 million agricultural and as much again pastoral, with collective rangelands alone near ONE MILLION HECTARES. THE BODY THAT DECIDES IS YOURS AND IT IS ELECTED: the CONSEILS DE GESTION (majalis al tasarrof) are COMMUNITY STRUCTURES ELECTED BY THE AYANTS DROIT — they replaced the traditional councils of notables (myaâd) whose members were APPOINTED BY TRIBAL CHIEFS — and the LAW OF 14 JANUARY 1971 DESIGNATES THEM AS THE SOLE DECIDERS ON THE ATTRIBUTION OF COLLECTIVE LANDS. Sole decider, elected by the rightholders — if you are an ayant droit, the council election is the most consequential vote you cast over your own land. Find out when yours is held and who is on the register. WHAT THE RECORD SHOWS THEY DID WITH THAT POWER, STATED PLAINLY: under the 1971 law the councils' competences shifted toward CARRYING OUT THE PRIVATISATION of agricultural collective land, and being extremely well fitted to the social structure they enabled a rapid and frictionless unwinding of collective tenure; researchers record the consequences as fragmentation of holdings and land concentration leading to the impoverishment of many peasants, plus excessive resource mobilisation — cereal expansion onto fragile ground, proliferating shallow wells, overgrazing of rangelands. A council that can allocate can also dissolve; the same elected body is the protection and the risk, which is exactly why the register of ayants droit matters. THE LIVE DEVELOPMENT ANYONE ON COLLECTIVE LAND SHOULD KNOW: the ministry has finalised a DRAFT DECREE-LAW GIVING THE TRIBUNAL IMMOBILIER EXCEPTIONAL PREROGATIVES AND SIMPLIFIED DEROGATORY PROCEDURES to settle collective-property disputes definitively AND CONVERT THESE LAND RESERVES INTO INDIVIDUAL, TRANSFERABLE, BANKABLE TITLES — with the stated reason that the legal complexity of collective property DETERS PRIVATE INVESTMENT AND THE SITING OF LARGE PUBLIC INFRASTRUCTURE, NOTABLY WIND, SOLAR AND INDUSTRIAL PROJECTS. The government has said out loud that collective title is what stands between southern land and large energy projects. If you hold rights on collective land in the south, register your name and watch the Tribunal Immobilier. WHO IT SUITS: Tunisian ayants droit, pastoral communities and southern governorate residents. CAVEATS: A MANAGEMENT AND ALLOCATION RIGHT, NOT INDIVIDUAL TITLE — and the direction of travel is toward conversion. For access to administrative documents, Tunisia's INAI entry; for state-funded representation, the aide judiciaire entry; for rapid-response money, Urgent Action Fund-Africa.

trackers.name: ATPNE, Tunis — created 1971, sits on Tunisia's national environmental commissions and chairs the national IUCN members committee, plus Notre Grand Bleu and the Jamaity association directory
trackers.desc: THE ASSOCIATION THAT SITS ON THE COMMISSIONS: the ASSOCIATION TUNISIENNE POUR LA PROTECTION DE LA NATURE ET DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT (ATPNE, atpne.org), CREATED 1971, WITH CONSULTATIVE STATUS AT ECOSOC SINCE 1996, at 12 rue Tantaoui El Jawhari, El Omrane 1005, TUNIS, tel +216 71 288 041, working on URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND RURAL DEVELOPMENT among its fields. ITS STANDING IS THE POINT: ATPNE IS A MEMBER OF SEVERAL NATIONAL COMMISSIONS — FROM THE FORMER COMMISSION NATIONALE DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT CHAIRED BY THE PRIME MINISTER THROUGH TO THE BIODIVERSITY COMMISSION AND OTHER NATIONAL COUNCILS — AND ITS PRESIDENT HOLDS THE PRESIDENCY OF THE NATIONAL COMMITTEE OF IUCN MEMBERS, WHICH COMPRISES BOTH GOVERNMENT AND NGOs. An association that already sits on the national biodiversity commission does not need to be let into the room. If your case needs to be raised nationally, ask ATPNE to carry it to a commission it already attends — that is a shorter route than any letter. Its president SAT ON THE COUNCIL OF THE WORLD CONSERVATION UNION FROM 1992 TO 2000, and ATPNE contributed to that union's strategy, pressing for its policy to treat THE HUMAN RIGHT TO SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT, HEALTH, SECURITY, EDUCATION, WORK AND DEMOCRACY as environmental questions. Rights framed as environmental policy is this association's own doctrine — useful if your objection is about people rather than species. THE OTHERS: ASSOCIATION NOTRE GRAND BLEU, FOUNDED 2012 AT MONASTIR, whose vision is preservation of marine and coastal life in the Mediterranean AND OF THE HUMAN ACTIVITIES THAT DEPEND ON IT, working with schoolchildren and secondary students on safeguarding the littoral, with a focus on the loggerhead turtle Caretta caretta and posidonia seagrass meadows; a TUNISIAN ENVIRONMENTAL ASSOCIATION of a global conservation network, working on nature conservation in Tunisia for more than 25 years across MARINE, TERRESTRIAL AND FRESHWATER ecosystems, WHICH HAS SIGNED A CONVENTION WITH THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT; and the ASSOCIATION DE SAUVEGARDE DE LA MÉDINA DE TUNIS, ESTABLISHED JUNE 1967, whose mission is conservation and protection of the overall traditional urban form of the Medina, its historical structures with all their distinctive elements and cultural heritage. Posidonia and a medina are both protectable. Between a marine association working named habitats and a heritage association working urban fabric, most Tunisian ground has a specialist already in existence. AND THE DIRECTORY: JAMAITY (jamaity.org) LISTS TUNISIAN ASSOCIATIONS WITH THEIR FOUNDING YEAR, CITY AND WEBSITE. Search it for your own governorate before assuming nobody is nearby. WHO IT SUITS: Tunisian coastal, rural and urban communities, and anyone needing a national-level channel. CAVEATS: ASSOCIATIONS WITH CLOSE STATE RELATIONS — pair with FTDES or counsel for an adversarial case. For regional offices and the environmental justice department, Tunisia's FTDES entry; for reporting a cut or a leak, the Observatoire tunisien de l'eau; for elected conseils de gestion on collective land, the terres collectives entry.

trackers.name: Tunisia's state list of environmental associations by governorate, the decree fixing how associations get public financing, and the WWF North Africa office that trains them and funds green jobs in protected areas
trackers.desc: THE LIST BY GOVERNORATE AND THE PUBLIC-MONEY DECREE: TUNISIA'S NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY, UNDER THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, PUBLISHES A LISTE DES ASSOCIATIONS ENVIRONNEMENTALES ET DES ORGANISATIONS EN TUNISIE PAR GOUVERNORAT. The state itself publishes which environmental associations exist in your governorate. That is the first call for a Tunisian community: not to found something, but to find who is already registered where you live — and a body listed by the agency is one the agency already recognises. The same agency also publishes A DYNAMIC WEB APPLICATION BASED ON A GIS TO EXPLORE THE STATE OF AIR QUALITY IN TUNISIA, AND A NATIONAL WATER QUALITY SURVEILLANCE NETWORK COVERING ALL THE POINTS PROJECTED ON ITS MAP, ANALYSED TWICE A YEAR. A national air-quality map and a twice-yearly water sampling network, both public. Before you commission anything, check whether a monitoring point already sits near your site — an official series going back years is stronger evidence than a single test you paid for. AND THE MONEY THAT IS ALREADY BUDGETED FOR ASSOCIATIONS: DÉCRET N°2013-5183 OF 18 NOVEMBER 2013 FIXES THE CRITERIA, THE PROCEDURES AND THE CONDITIONS FOR THE GRANT OF PUBLIC FINANCING TO ASSOCIATIONS, alongside DÉCRET-LOI N°2011-88 OF 24 SEPTEMBER 2011 ORGANISING ASSOCIATIONS — both published on the agency's civil society page. Public financing for associations has written criteria and a written procedure. That is a funding route with no foreign donor in it, and it is listed on the environment agency's own site next to the list of who is eligible. Ask which line finances environmental associations and when applications open. THE OFFICE THAT TRAINS AND FUNDS: A WWF NORTH AFRICA PROGRAMME BUREAU HAS EXISTED IN TUNISIA SINCE 1994, AND SINCE 2013 THE TUNIS OFFICE HAS BEEN ENLARGED TO COVER THE WHOLE NORTH AFRICA REGION. Its named areas of work are THE REINFORCEMENT OF THE CAPACITIES OF ENVIRONMENTAL ASSOCIATIONS; GOOD GOVERNANCE AND CONSERVATION OF PROTECTED AREAS — COASTAL MARINE PROTECTED AREAS, WETLANDS OF INTERNATIONAL IMPORTANCE, NATIONAL PARKS AND NATURE RESERVES; AND THE PROMOTION OF GREEN EMPLOYMENT IN PROTECTED AREAS. Green employment inside protected areas as a named programme line is the answer to the community that is told protection costs it jobs. Ask what green employment means in practice in your park and how many posts it has funded. AND IT PUTS OUT CALLS TUNISIAN ASSOCIATIONS CAN ANSWER: AN APPEL À CANDIDATURE POUR LES ASSOCIATIONS TUNISIENNES, and consultancy calls including one for A SOCIO-ECONOMIC CHARACTERISATION OF THE TUNISIAN FOREST POPULATION, one for AN ECONOMIC EVALUATION OF THE GOODS AND SERVICES OF TUNISIAN FORESTS AND RANGELANDS AND THE COSTS OF THEIR DEGRADATION, and one on ECOLOGICAL MONITORING AND MODELLING OF COASTAL FISH STOCKS IN A NAMED GULF. An economic valuation of what forest degradation costs, commissioned for Tunisia specifically, is the document that turns a conservation argument into a money argument in front of a ministry. Ask whether it has been published and what it found for your region. And a socio-economic characterisation of the FOREST POPULATION means somebody is counting the people who live in the forests — make sure your community is in that count. A named resilience project is described as aiming TO MOBILISE AND REINFORCE THE CAPACITIES OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS IN TUNISIA TO CONDUCT A CONSTRUCTIVE DIALOGUE WITH THE PUBLIC AUTHORITIES and to promote ECOSYSTEM-BASED ADAPTATION SOLUTIONS RELYING ON CIVIL SOCIETY AND COMMUNITY INITIATIVES. Ecosystem-based adaptation relying on community initiatives is the phrase to use in an application: it is what the money is labelled for. WHO IT SUITS: Tunisian associations seeking public funding or training, communities near a park or wetland, and anyone needing baseline air or water data. CAVEATS: A GOVERNMENT AGENCY LIST AND AN INTERNATIONAL PROGRAMME OFFICE — neither is a litigator, and calls open and close. For the association created in 1971 that sits on the national environmental commission and chairs the national IUCN members committee, Tunisia's ATPNE entry, which also carries the Jamaity association directory; for regional offices that take up local cases, FTDES; for reporting a cut or bad water, the Observatoire tunisien de l'eau; for the legal aid office inside each court, the bureau d'aide judiciaire entry; for the elected conseils de gestion on collective land, the terres collectives entry.

trackers.name: Lifeline Embattled CSO Assistance Fund — the embattled-organisation fund that names land rights and environmental groups as a priority — three grant types covering trial monitoring, prison visits and equipment replacement, with unregistered groups of two or more eligible, and the published amounts across four funds
trackers.desc: TWO THREATENED MEMBERS AND A DOCUMENT PROVING YOU EXIST — placement note first: THESE ARE GLOBAL FUNDS, FILED UNDER TUNISIA BECAUSE THIS BUCKET CARRIED NO RAPID-RESPONSE FUNDING RESOURCE. THE PRIORITY STATEMENT, WHICH IS WHY THIS BELONGS IN A LAND FILE AT ALL: THE FUND PRIORITIZES SUPPORT TO CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS THAT FACE ADDITIONAL LAYERS OF VULNERABILITY AND RESTRICTIONS, INCLUDING WOMEN'S RIGHTS AND WOMEN-LED ORGANIZATIONS AND INDIGENOUS, LAND RIGHTS, AND ENVIRONMENTAL CSOs. Land rights and environmental organisations named as a priority category, in writing. Most defender funds treat land cases as a subset of human rights work you have to argue into scope; this one puts you in the priority group before you ask. THE ELIGIBILITY RULE THAT OPENS THE DOOR: UNDER THE EMERGENCY CATEGORY ARE INCLUDED CSOs WITH AT LEAST TWO OR MORE MEMBERS THAT ARE THREATENED — THE CSOs DON'T HAVE TO BE OFFICIALLY REGISTERED, BUT THEY HAVE TO PROVE THEIR HISTORY OF ACTIVISM THROUGH A DOCUMENT. Two or more people, unregistered, plus one document showing you have been doing this. That document is the whole barrier — so keep meeting minutes, a petition with signatures, a letter you sent to the council, a newspaper clipping. A group that has kept nothing cannot prove it exists; a group that kept one letter can. Start the folder before you need it. THE THREE GRANT TYPES, EACH WITH A DIFFERENT JOB: SHORT-TERM EMERGENCY ASSISTANCE TO ORGANISATIONS THREATENED BECAUSE OF THEIR HUMAN RIGHTS WORK; RAPID RESPONSE ADVOCACY GRANTS TO PUSH BACK AGAINST CLOSURES OF CIVIC SPACE AS THEY ARISE; AND RAPID RESPONSE RESILIENCY GRANTS TO HELP THREATENED ORGANISATIONS PROACTIVELY AVOID OR MITIGATE THE THREATS THEY FACE AND CONTINUE TO WORK IN HIGH-RISK ENVIRONMENTS. The third is the rare one: money BEFORE the emergency, to stop it happening. Almost everything else in this file pays after the door is kicked in. WHAT THE EMERGENCY GRANTS ACTUALLY COVER: SECURITY, MEDICAL EXPENSES, LEGAL REPRESENTATION, PRISON VISITS, TRIAL MONITORING, TEMPORARY RELOCATION, EQUIPMENT REPLACEMENT, AND OTHER URGENTLY NEEDED EXPENSES. PRISON VISITS and TRIAL MONITORING are two nobody budgets for. Getting family to the prison costs transport nobody has, and a monitored trial goes differently from an unmonitored one — both are fundable line items here. EQUIPMENT REPLACEMENT covers the phones and laptops taken in a raid. WHAT THE ADVOCACY GRANTS SUPPORT, AND THEY ARE DESCRIBED AS HIGHLY FLEXIBLE: COMMUNITY MOBILIZATION, POLICY AND LEGAL ADVOCACY, CIVIL SOCIETY COALITION BUILDING, STRATEGIC LITIGATION, AWARENESS RAISING CAMPAIGNS, ADVOCACY CAPACITY BUILDING, AND SECURITY AND PROTECTION TRAINING. STRATEGIC LITIGATION and COALITION BUILDING on the same list as community mobilisation. That is a campaign budget in a defender fund's clothing — and this file has recorded coalition-building as the step that turns scattered villages into something a ministry answers. THE AMOUNTS, PUBLISHED SIDE BY SIDE SO YOU CAN CHOOSE: US$10,000 TO US$20,000 FOR ADVOCACY OR RESILIENCY GRANTS FROM ONE FUND, WHICH WELCOMES APPLICATIONS FROM FORMAL OR INFORMAL CIVIL SOCIETY ACTORS AND CONSORTIA INCLUDING SOCIAL MOVEMENTS, FOR A 3 TO 6 MONTH PERIOD; A MAXIMUM OF EUR 7,500 FOR PROTECTION GRANTS COVERING MEDICAL, LEGAL, PHYSICAL AND DIGITAL SECURITY AND FAMILY ASSISTANCE; AND A MAXIMUM OF $8,000 FOR UP TO 3 MONTHS FROM A WOMEN'S RAPID RESPONSE FUND. Knowing the ceilings before you write saves the commonest mistake: asking one fund for a sum it never gives. Match the number to the window — and note that CONSORTIA INCLUDING SOCIAL MOVEMENTS are welcome at the largest of them, so three village groups can apply together. THE FREE TOOLKIT: AN INTRODUCTORY FRAMEWORK TO HELP ORGANISATIONS THINK ABOUT HOW TO DEVELOP AN ADVOCACY ACTION PLAN, AVAILABLE IN ENGLISH, ARABIC, FRENCH, SPANISH, RUSSIAN, VIETNAMESE AND FARSI. Arabic and French among the seven languages. A written advocacy plan is what most of these funds are really asking for, and here is a free template for making one in a language your committee reads. THE TIMING: NO DEADLINE, WITH APPLICATIONS ON A ROLLING BASIS. THE STRUCTURE: A CONSORTIUM OF SEVEN INTERNATIONAL NGOs, SUPPORTED BY A DONOR STEERING COMMITTEE OF GOVERNMENT AND FOUNDATION DONORS — AND BENIN SITS ON THAT COMMITTEE ALONGSIDE THE EUROPEAN AND AMERICAN GOVERNMENTS. An African state on the donor committee of a fund that defends civil society. That is worth knowing when anyone claims this kind of support is purely foreign interference — and it is a point a Beninese organisation in particular can make. AND THE STATED DIRECTION: EXPANDING FINANCIAL, TECHNICAL AND MORAL SUPPORT TO AT-RISK INDIGENOUS NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS AND WOMEN HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS. WHO IT SUITS: African land, environmental and indigenous organisations under threat — including unregistered groups of two or more people. CAVEATS: THE EMERGENCY WINDOW REQUIRES DOCUMENTARY PROOF OF YOUR HISTORY OF ACTIVISM, and grants are short-term. For the 24-hour helpline, the protection grant contents and the two directories, Benin's defender protection entry; for the seven Ubuntu Hub host cities, Cape Verde's pan-African defenders network entry; for the three application windows including a 6–12 month advocacy grant, Mauritania's rapid-response fund entry.

trackers.name: NACHU (National Cooperative Housing Union), Kenya, with Reall as social investor — a co-operative apex owned by its member societies that lends them money for land purchase and construction, with builds documented under USD $1,400 per home
trackers.desc: A LENDER OWNED BY THE PEOPLE BORROWING, AND IT LENDS FOR THE LAND — method and adjacency declared first: THIS IS THE FIRST OF THE ACQUISITION-ONLY ROUNDS: AFRICA'S FLOOR IS 17 EVERYWHERE AND ALL 53 COUNTRIES CARRY BOTH AN ACQUISITION AND A LEGAL RESOURCE, BUT THE MEASURED MEDIAN DEPTH IS ONE ACQUISITION RESOURCE PER COUNTRY AGAINST FOUR LEGAL ONES. A POOLED CONSERVATION FUND WAS WITHDRAWN LAST ROUND AS ALREADY FILED UNDER TANZANIA. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND FIVE DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL HOSTS AND FOUR FACTS ABSENT, WITH ONE PHRASE MATCHING ONE ENTRY, READ IN FULL AND A DIFFERENT SUBJECT. THIS FILE'S EQUATORIAL GUINEA AND LIBYA ENTRIES COVER THE CONSERVATION LAND-PURCHASE FUNDS, ITS MOZAMBIQUE ENTRY THE SAVINGS FEDERATION AND ITS FINANCE AGENCY, ITS NIGER ENTRY THE COMMONAGE ACQUISITIONS. NONE IS RESTATED. WHAT IT LENDS FOR, WHICH IS THE FIND: A NATIONAL CO-OPERATIVE HOUSING UNION OFFERING LOANS TO ITS MEMBER CO-OPERATIVES AND THEIR MEMBERS FOR LAND PURCHASE, HOUSE CONSTRUCTION, HOME IMPROVEMENT AND INFRASTRUCTURE — REGISTERED UNDER THE CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETIES ACT AS AN APEX BODY. LAND PURCHASE, first on the list. Almost every acquisition resource in this file is a conservation fund that buys ground for habitat; this is credit for households to buy the ground they live on, which is the version that fits a settlement facing clearance rather than a species facing extinction. WHO OWNS IT, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE MEMBERS ARE THE HOUSING CO-OPERATIVES THEMSELVES, SO THE LENDER IS OWNED BY THE BORROWERS — WITH MEMBERSHIP DRAWN FROM LOW AND MODERATE INCOME HOUSEHOLDS, INCLUDING GROUPS FORMED IN INFORMAL SETTLEMENTS. A lender the borrowers control. This file has recorded community money repeatedly captured once it arrives; an apex body owned by its member societies puts the loan terms in the hands of the people repaying them, and it is a legal form that exists under co-operative statutes in most African countries. WHAT IT HAS BUILT: THROUGH ITS PARTNERSHIP WITH A SOCIAL INVESTOR IT HAS CONSTRUCTED OVER 1,500 HOMES. WHERE IT SITS IN POLICY: IT HAS SUCCESSFULLY ENGAGED WITH THE NATIONAL AND REGIONAL GOVERNMENTS, HELPING TO SHAPE THE CURRENT HOUSING POLICY TO CONSIDER PEOPLE ON LOW INCOMES, AND HAS BEEN AN ACTIVE MEMBER IN GOVERNMENT TASK FORCES ON LAND, HOUSING AND THE BUILT ENVIRONMENT. A borrower-owned co-operative sitting on the government's own land task force. That is a different position from petitioning it, and it came from having built something first. THE COSTS ACHIEVED ALONGSIDE IT IN THE SAME COUNTRY: ONE PARTNER DELIVERED 41 COMPACT STUDIOS, EACH 18 SQUARE METRES WITH A BATHROOM AND ELECTRICITY, WITH PRICES STARTING AT $3,000; ANOTHER DELIVERED 145 INCREMENTAL HOMES WITH WATER, SANITATION AND ELECTRICITY THAT COST LESS THAN USD $1,400 EACH TO CONSTRUCT. Under $1,400 a home, with services. That figure is the one to carry into a negotiation: when a municipality says rehousing a settlement is unaffordable, this is what it has actually cost elsewhere on the continent, built incrementally. THE SOCIAL INVESTOR BEHIND THOSE FIGURES AND HOW IT WORKS: IT AND ITS IN-COUNTRY PARTNERS BUILD AND BROKER COMMERCIALLY VIABLE SOLUTIONS FOR CLIMATE-SMART AFFORDABLE HOUSING IN EMERGING MARKETS, INCLUDING PIONEERING THE $10K HOUSE — ACTING AS THE SOCIAL INVESTOR ALONGSIDE MUNICIPALITIES AS PUBLIC PARTNERS PROVIDING LAND. THE MUNICIPAL LAND ROUTE, NAMED IN A DOCUMENTED CASE: CASA REAL, A MOZAMBICAN SOCIAL ENTERPRISE AND REAL ESTATE DEVELOPER IN BEIRA AIMING TO DESIGN, BUILD AND SELL HOMES PEOPLE CAN AFFORD, ACHIEVING IT BY WORKING WITH THE SOCIAL INVESTOR AND THE MUNICIPALITY AS PUBLIC PARTNER PROVIDING LAND, ACCESS TO SERVICES AND PLANNING ASSISTANCE. THE MUNICIPALITY SUPPLIES THE LAND and the investor supplies the capital. That is the three-way shape worth proposing where a council owns ground and says it has no budget — it is being asked for land, not money, which is a much easier yes. Read beside the commonage route recorded in this file's Niger entry: municipal land made available to the poor of that town. THE EXCLUSION IT EXISTS TO ANSWER: VULNERABLE COMMUNITIES ARE OFTEN EXCLUDED FROM HOUSING FINANCE BY PRIVATE OR PUBLIC FINANCIAL AND MICROFINANCE INSTITUTIONS, DUE TO EITHER EXCLUSIVE ENTRY REQUIREMENTS OR THE UNAFFORDABILITY OF THOSE PRODUCTS — AND COLLECTIVE HOUSING OWNERSHIP MODELS ARE EXCLUDED FROM HOUSING SUBSIDIES. Collective ownership excluded from the subsidy is a specific, fixable policy fault, and naming it is the ask: a group that wants to hold land together is often ineligible for the very support designed for the poor. WHAT STRENGTHENS A GROUP'S HAND, FROM THE SAME ANALYSIS: PROVIDING DIRECT SUPPORT TO RESIDENTS HELPS INCREASE THEIR NEGOTIATING CAPACITY WITH PUBLIC AND FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS — WITH COMBINING SEVERAL FUNDING SOURCES MEANING INCREASING THE INVESTMENT AND SECURING IT IN THE LONGER TERM. Several sources rather than one. A purchase funded by a single grant collapses when that grant ends; one assembled from co-operative savings, a social investor and municipal land does not. THE COMPARATIVE STUDY THAT EXISTS FOR COPYING: A CENTRE FOR AFFORDABLE HOUSING FINANCE, URBAMONDE AND URBASEN DOCUMENTED AFFORDABLE HOUSING PRODUCTION PROGRAMMES ACROSS AFRICA FOCUSING ON THEIR FINANCIAL DESIGN — ANALYSING TEN EXAMPLES OF AFFORDABLE FINANCING MECHANISMS BUILT ON DIVERSE LEVELS OF COMMUNITY OWNERSHIP. Ten worked financial designs, already compared. A group deciding how to structure a purchase does not have to invent the mechanism. THE INSTRUMENT AIMED AT WOMEN AND IRREGULAR EARNERS: A GENDER-RESPONSIVE INCOME STABILIZATION GUARANTEE WHICH MITIGATES INCOME VOLATILITY RISKS FOR INFORMAL EARNERS AND INCENTIVIZES LENDERS TO SERVE WOMEN BORROWERS — ALONGSIDE A FACILITY PROVIDING TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND ALTERNATIVE CREDIT ASSESSMENT TOOLS. ALTERNATIVE CREDIT ASSESSMENT is the real barrier being addressed: a trader with no payslip is not uncreditworthy, she is unmeasurable by the standard test. AND THE GAP THE WHOLE SECTOR IS WORKING IN: AN AFFORDABLE HOUSING GAP ON THE CONTINENT OF 50 MILLION UNITS, WITH TASK FORCES CONVENED IN TWO NAMED AFRICAN COUNTRIES DRAWING FROM IMPACT INVESTORS, GOVERNMENTS, COMMERCIAL BANKS, MICROFINANCE PROVIDERS, HOUSING DEVELOPERS AND END USERS — TO UNLOCK AFFORDABLE MORTGAGE FINANCE FOR INFORMALLY EMPLOYED AND UNBANKED PEOPLE. END USERS listed in the task force alongside the banks. Where such a body is convened in your country, a residents' organisation has a stated place in it. WHO IT SUITS: low-income households and settlement groups who want to buy the land they live on, and organisers looking for a borrower-owned lending structure or realistic per-home construction costs to argue with. CAVEATS: THE UNION ITSELF IS ONE COUNTRY'S, THOUGH THE CO-OPERATIVE APEX FORM EXISTS UNDER MOST AFRICAN CO-OPERATIVE STATUTES; THIS IS CREDIT, MEANING DEBT REPAID BY MEMBERS, NOT A GRANT, AND THE FIGURES CITED COME FROM PARTICULAR PROJECTS RATHER THAN A STANDING PRICE. For funds that pay a purchase price outright, Equatorial Guinea's and Libya's entries; for municipal commonage as a route to land, Niger's entry.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a pan-African feminist rapid-response fund with reach across all 54 African countries — small grants released quickly for unanticipated, time-critical situations rather than planned programme work, covering safety and protection needs when defenders are threatened and short windows for advocacy after an unexpected event. WHO IT SUITS: women's rights organisations, feminist collectives and movements in which women or gender-diverse people are the primary decision-makers. It does NOT fund individuals, and the action must be strategic, genuinely unanticipated, and completable in under three months. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is emergency money for a moment, not a budget for a campaign — decisions are fast and grants are modest.

trackers.name: data.gov.ma
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Morocco.

trackers.name: Terres collectives — the opposition window is now 3 months, not 6
trackers.desc: A DEADLINE THAT WAS HALVED, AND IT IS THE THING TO DIARISE. Three laws promulgated 9 August 2019 replaced the dahir of 27 April 1919 governing collective lands: loi 62-17 (administrative tutelle over collectivités ethniques and management of their property), loi 63-17 (administrative delimitation) and loi 64-17 (collective lands in irrigation perimeters). Loi 63-17 reduced the period for presenting oppositions against the delimitation procedure from 6 months to 3 months. If a delimitation touches your community, the window to object is now half what it was. Delimitation is run by a Commission de délimitation administrative presided by the local authority. BUT THE PERIOD ITSELF FREEZES TRANSACTIONS: during the operation it is prohibited on pain of nullity to conclude any act relating to the lands under delimitation (save the cases in articles 16, 17, 19, 20 and 21 of loi 62-17), and no new réquisition d'immatriculation by a third party may be admitted unless it confirms an opposition already presented. STEP ONE IS TO CHECK YOU ARE LISTED: the list of collectivités ethniques for each prefecture or province is fixed by the governor. Note too that loi 62-17 limits recourse to custom and tradition in managing these lands, requiring conformity with legislation in force.

trackers.name: Loi 22-07 — protection does not extinguish subsistence use
trackers.desc: TWO THINGS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE OPPOSING OR SEEKING A DESIGNATION. Loi 22-07 (July 2010) defines an aire protégée as any terrestrial or marine space, geographically delimited, duly recognised and specially managed to protect and improve biological diversity, conserve natural and cultural heritage, and prevent its degradation. AND IT PRESERVES LOCAL USE: the law recognises the right of populations living inside or near the protected area to benefit from usage rights — prélèvements made on a non-commercial basis for their domestic and vital needs. Designation therefore does not extinguish subsistence use, and that is in the statute rather than left to practice — a direct answer to the objection that protection starves residents. THE STATUS TO ASK ABOUT: the loi-cadre 99-12 National Charter sets objectives at article 7 including preserving sites d'intérêt biologique et écologique (SIBE) — terrestrial, coastal and marine — and encouraging the creation of protected areas there. Morocco's first protected areas strategy, the Plan directeur des aires protégées, dates to 1996. READ THE POLITICAL CONTEXT HONESTLY: the 2019 collective-land reform followed a royal speech of 12 October 2018 calling for one million additional hectares of collective land to be mobilised for agricultural investment projects.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: ADFM and the soulaliyate movement — the campaign that won women a share of collective tribal land, and the body that trained them to speak for themselves
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Association Démocratique des Femmes du Maroc, a feminist organisation founded in 1985 and based in Rabat, which has accompanied the soulaliyate movement since 2007 — women of the collective tribal lands who were excluded from the land and its proceeds. WHY THIS IS A LAND RESOURCE AND NOT ONLY A GENDER ONE: roughly 42 per cent of Morocco's land is held collectively by tribes — in the order of 15 million hectares — and it is those collective lands that get ceded for major works and for property development, with compensation paid to the members of the collectivity. If your name is not on the list, you get nothing when the land goes. The movement forced the state to act: interior ministry circulars extended equal rights of enjoyment to women, and in 2018 women in Kénitra received plots on the same footing as men following a cession of collective land — the first time. Laws 62.17, 63.17 and 64.17 then reformed the administrative tutelage over soulaliyate communities and their assets. THE ORGANISING PRINCIPLE ADFM STATES, WHICH IS WORTH COPYING: they amplify the women's voice but do not speak in their place — the women were trained to state their own claims. It also runs national meetings that put affected women, ministries and civil society in one room over draft legislation. WHO IT SUITS: members of a collective (soulaliyate) community facing a cession of tribal land, particularly women excluded from the beneficiary lists. CAVEATS: ADFM is an advocacy and capacity-building organisation, not a law firm. The reform is incomplete on its own account — the law as adopted has been read as granting access only to women resident on the land, and ADFM warned that a 2020 interior ministry circular on allocating soulaliyate farmland made no mention of the historic exclusion of women, risking a repeat. This entry points at an intergovernmental account of the movement because ADFM's own site was not verified; treat the organisation as the contact and the account as the record.

trackers.name: AOFEP and the RADDO oasis network — a local association at Tinjdad and the Maghreb-wide network of oasis communities it belongs to
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Association Oasis Ferkla pour l'Environnement et le Patrimoine (AOFEP), a Moroccan non-profit created in 2001 at Tinjdad in Errachidia province in the south-east, working on the environment and heritage of the Ferkla oasis — and, through it, RADDO, the associative network for the sustainable development of oases, which links oasis associations across the Maghreb and gives an isolated oasis community counterparts in Algeria, Tunisia and Mauritania facing the same threats. WHY THE OASIS IS A DISTINCT CASE, and why the soulaliyate route in Morocco's other entry does not cover it: an oasis is destroyed not by a single expropriation but by water abstraction, upstream boreholes, drought and the abandonment of the collective irrigation systems that make cultivation possible — the land can remain legally yours and still become worthless. Network members' stated aims are instructive as a template: to constitute an independent structure that is the counterpart to public authorities on all environmental questions, and to create alternatives allowing sustainable development of the oasis — through public awareness, exchange of experience with partners, and advocacy for agroecology and responsible tourism. A permanent independent body that the administration has to deal with, established before a crisis, is worth more than a committee formed the week the drilling rig arrives. WHO IT SUITS: oasis and pre-Saharan communities in south-eastern Morocco facing water loss, land degradation or extractive projects, and associations wanting counterparts across the Maghreb. CAVEATS: NO VERIFIED SITE OF ITS OWN WAS FOUND for AOFEP — this entry points at the RADDO network page documenting it; treat that as the route in.
