It is a local environment-and-heritage association, not a law firm or a fund, and for collective tribal land and the soulaliyate movement Morocco's other entry is the one.

trackers.name: Morocco's university legal clinics and ADALA — free first advice in a country with no framework law on legal aid
trackers.desc: WHERE TO GET LEGAL HELP, AND THE STRUCTURAL FACT THAT EXPLAINS WHY IT IS HARD: there is as yet NO FRAMEWORK LAW in Moroccan law setting out the contours of legal aid; in practice judicial assistance services are not known to the general public, and legal aid provision is largely carried by CIVIL SOCIETY. So do not start by asking a court for assistance you have never heard described — start with the organisations that actually run the service. WHAT EXISTS: UNIVERSITY LEGAL CLINICS, developed by the Moroccan justice-focused association ADALA together with an international lawyers' organisation, explicitly to strengthen access to justice for women. The clinics provide reception, listening, FIRST LEGAL ADVICE AND ORIENTATION to people in situations of vulnerability, supervised and supported by law teachers and legal professionals — law students doing the intake under supervision, which is what makes the service free and repeatable. A university law faculty is the cheapest legal door in any country that has one; ask whether yours runs a clinique juridique and on which days. The same international organisation works across North Africa and has published on how colonial-era penal provisions on begging, vagrancy and informal trade still bring people before the police and courts in Morocco, Tunisia and Algeria — relevant to anyone whose land dispute becomes a public-order charge. WHO IT SUITS: Moroccan households, and especially women, who need first legal advice and orientation on a land, inheritance or expropriation problem and cannot pay a lawyer. CAVEATS: FIRST ADVICE AND ORIENTATION, NOT REPRESENTATION — a clinic will tell you where you stand and where to go, not argue your case; ADALA has no verified live site of its own, so this entry points at the international partner that documents the programme, and clinic availability depends on the university and the academic year. For collective tribal land and the soulaliyate movement, Morocco's ADFM entry; for oasis territories, the AOFEP/RADDO entry.

trackers.name: SPANA Maroc and ASMAPEC — a nature association recognised as d'utilité publique by decree with signed conventions with the forestry agency, and the first Moroccan environmental association, founded by university researchers
trackers.desc: THE STATUS THAT GETS YOU IN THE ROOM: the SOCIÉTÉ PROTECTRICE DES ANIMAUX ET DE LA NATURE (SPANA, spana.org.ma), FIRST DECLARED IN 1959 and RECOGNISED AS D'UTILITÉ PUBLIQUE IN 1976 BY DÉCRET N°2.76.228, at 41 Lotissement Zohra, 12000 HARHOURA-TÉMARA, tel +212 537 74 72 09, with a named president. RECONNUE D'UTILITÉ PUBLIQUE IS THE MOROCCAN STATUS TO ASK ABOUT: it is conferred by decree, it is durable, and it is what distinguishes an association a ministry must deal with from one it may ignore. Ask whether the organisation helping you holds it — and if you are building an association for the long term, ask what the route to it is. WHAT THAT STATUS BUYS, IN ITS OWN RECORD: SPANA is LINKED BY PARTNERSHIP CONVENTIONS WITH THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE, MARITIME FISHERIES, RURAL DEVELOPMENT AND WATER AND FORESTS (AGENCE NATIONALE DES EAUX ET FORÊTS), WITH THE MINISTRY OF NATIONAL EDUCATION AND ITS REGIONAL ACADEMIES FOR RABAT-SALÉ-KENITRA, CASABLANCA-SETTAT AND MARRAKECH-SAFI, AND WITH THE REGIONAL DIRECTORATES OF THE NATIONAL WATER AND FORESTS AGENCY. A signed convention with the regional water and forests directorate covering your region is a standing relationship with the very administration that classes and declasses forest land. That is worth more than a campaign. ITS NETWORKS: SPANA belongs to the world conservation union, a Mediterranean environment and sustainable development office, a Middle East animal welfare network, an Arab environment and development network, the ALLIANCE MAROCAINE POUR LE CLIMAT ET LE DÉVELOPPEMENT DURABLE (AMCDD), a Mediterranean wetlands alliance and the ALLIANCE MAROCAINE DES ZONES HUMIDES. If your ground is a wetland, there is a Moroccan wetlands alliance and a Mediterranean one above it — two doors most Moroccan communities never knock on. AND THE OLDEST: ASMAPEC IS THE FIRST MOROCCAN ASSOCIATION FOR ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION, CREATED IN 1986 ON THE INITIATIVE OF UNIVERSITY RESEARCHERS FROM THE HASSAN II AGRONOMIC AND VETERINARY INSTITUTE together with educators, which CARRIES OUT FIELD STUDIES AND PRODUCES SCIENTIFIC DOCUMENTS AND SUPPORTS — GUIDES, BOOKLETS, LEAFLETS AND POSTERS — and works to make known to citizens the efforts deployed at national, regional and international level for the conservation of natural resources. An association founded by agronomy and veterinary researchers can produce a field study that stands up against a developer's consultant. Ask ASMAPEC what it has published on your area before you commission anything. A national environment foundation has also convened work on THE COASTLINE, including an international conference on the littoral. WHO IT SUITS: Moroccan communities facing coastal, forest or wetland loss, and associations seeking durable legal standing. CAVEATS: CONSERVATION AND EDUCATION BODIES with close state relations — not adversarial litigators; for a contested case pair them with counsel. For the campaign that won soulaliyate women's land rights, Morocco's ADFM entry; for the oasis network, AOFEP and RADDO; for free first advice, the university legal clinics and ADALA entry.

trackers.name: Named Moroccan associations with addresses — CMED with antennas at Rissani and Ouazzane, Ribat Al Fath recognised d'utilité publique since 1988, IFKER in Meknes province, and AMDH with a Rabat street address
trackers.desc: TWO ANTENNAS, AND AN ASSOCIATION NAMED AFTER A TORTOISE: THE CLUB MAROCAIN POUR L'ENVIRONNEMENT ET LE DÉVELOPPEMENT (CMED) IS A NATIONAL NGO FOUNDED IN 1993 TO CONTRIBUTE TO THE CONSERVATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES, AND AN IUCN MEMBER — BORN OF AN INITIATIVE OF SEVERAL UNIVERSITY AND EDUCATIONAL COMPETENCES working on population, environment and sustainable development. IT HAS REGIONAL ANTENNAS AT RISSANI IN THE SOUTH OF MOROCCO AND AT OUAZZANE IN THE NORTH-CENTRE. Two named regional antennas is the difference between a Rabat organisation and one that can send somebody. If your ground is in the pre-Saharan south or the northern hills, ask the antenna, not the head office — and note that it was founded by academics, which means it can produce the study as well as the letter. IT STATES THAT ITS ACTIVITIES HAVE NO LUCRATIVE AND NO POLITICAL PURPOSE, AND IT IS A MEMBER OF ESPACE ASSOCIATIF — DESCRIBED AS A NETWORK GROUPING ENVIRONMENT AND DEVELOPMENT ASSOCIATIONS — AND OF A RESEARCH GROUP ON RENEWABLE ENERGIES. A declared non-political purpose is what lets an association keep working in a constrained space, and Espace Associatif is the national network to ask for the list of who else is in it. THE ONE WITH PUBLIC-UTILITY STATUS: ASSOCIATION RIBAT AL FATH POUR LE DÉVELOPPEMENT DURABLE, RABAT, CREATED IN 1986 AND RECOGNISED D'UTILITÉ PUBLIQUE SINCE 1988, at RUE MADANI BEN HOUSNI, HAY RIAD, with its own site — described as the reference association in Rabat, whose aims include MAKING THE HERITAGE AND IDENTITY OF THE CITY LIVE, PERMITTING EACH CITIZEN TO PLAY THEIR ROLE IN THE SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT PROCESS, AND OFFERING EACH PERSON THE OPPORTUNITY TO BE USEFUL TO THE COMMUNITY. Utilité publique since 1988 is the durable status this file keeps flagging in Francophone countries: it is what makes a ministry deal with an association rather than ignore it. Ribat Al Fath has held it for nearly forty years — which makes it a co-signatory worth having on a letter even when the subject is not Rabat. THE LOCAL ONE, AND IT IS THE SHAPE MOST COMMUNITIES ACTUALLY NEED: ASSOCIATION IFKER — IFKER BEING AN AMAZIGH WORD MEANING TURTLE — IS A MOROCCAN ASSOCIATION FOR ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT CREATED IN JUNE 2014, BASED AT MOULAY IDRISS ZERHOUN, PROVINCE OF MEKNES, AT N°52 DERB SELFATY, HAY EL HOUFRA, WITH A PUBLISHED MOBILE NUMBER. It says of itself that it IS INTENDED TO BE A LOCAL ORGANISATION FOR EDUCATION, DEVELOPMENT AND ADVOCACY, AND IS INCLUSIVE OF ALL CATEGORIES — CHILDREN, YOUTH, ADULTS, WOMEN AND MEN, RURALS — BECAUSE PROTECTING THE ENVIRONMENT AND STIMULATING SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IS A MATTER OF ALL; and its founding members SUPPORTED LOCAL SOCIO-ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS FOR MORE THAN SEVEN YEARS BEFORE AND ALONGSIDE, IN COLLABORATION WITH NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL PARTNERS. An Amazigh name, a house number in a small town, and ADVOCACY written into what it is for. That is a template worth copying exactly: a local association does not have to choose between education and advocacy, and naming itself in the local language is not decoration — it is what makes the village recognise it as theirs. AND THE RIGHTS BODY, FOR WHEN THE CASE TURNS: THE ASSOCIATION MAROCAINE DES DROITS HUMAINS (AMDH, amdh.org.ma), FOUNDED 24 JUNE 1979 IN RABAT, IS ONE OF THE BIGGEST MOROCCAN HUMAN RIGHTS NGOs, at AV. HASSAN II, RUE AGUENSOUS, IMM 6, APPT 1, RABAT, with a NAMED PRESIDENT AND A NAMED EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR — working through THE PUBLICATION OF A MONTHLY NEWSPAPER, SIT-INS AND THE HOLDING OF CONFERENCES, and considering it equally crucial TO BUILD PARTNERSHIPS WITH INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL ORGANISATIONS AND NETWORKS. A monthly newspaper is a publication route that does not depend on a journalist taking an interest. If your case needs to be on paper somewhere permanent, ask whether AMDH will carry it. WHO IT SUITS: Moroccan communities in the south or north-centre, small-town associations forming, and anyone needing a public-utility co-signatory or a rights body. CAVEATS: MEMBERSHIP AND EDUCATION ASSOCIATIONS — for litigation, see the entries below. For the campaign that won women a share of collective land, Morocco's ADFM and the soulaliyate movement entry; for a local association at Tinjdad and the oasis network, AOFEP and RADDO; for free first advice, the university legal clinics and ADALA entry; for a nature association recognised d'utilité publique with ministry conventions, SPANA Maroc and ASMAPEC.

trackers.name: The ICCA Consortium and the ICCA Registry — a membership body whose members are community organisations themselves, and a public database a community documents itself into on its own terms (global, filed here because the named African member and the agdals are Moroccan)
trackers.desc: THE COMMUNITY MAPS ITSELF ONTO THE WORLD MAP — placement note first: THE CONSORTIUM AND THE REGISTRY ARE GLOBAL, FILED UNDER MOROCCO ONLY BECAUSE THIS FILE HAS NO GLOBAL KEY AND THE NAMED AFRICAN MEMBER AND THE AGDAL SYSTEM BELOW ARE MOROCCAN. They are open to communities anywhere in Africa. THE REGISTRY'S FOUNDING PRINCIPLE IS THE SENTENCE TO READ TWICE: THE ONLY WAY TO TRULY KNOW ABOUT TERRITORIES CONSERVED BY INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES — INCLUDING THEIR LOCATION, EXTENT AND DIVERSE VALUES — IS TO SUPPORT INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES TO DOCUMENT AND MAP THEIR OWN TERRITORIES ON THEIR OWN TERMS. THE ICCA REGISTRY EXISTS TO FACILITATE THIS. ON THEIR OWN TERMS, and the data is VOLUNTARILY PROVIDED BY THE CUSTODIANS THEMSELVES OR THROUGH THEIR SUPPORTING ORGANISATIONS. That is the opposite of every mapping exercise this file has recorded being done TO a community. You decide what goes in, and you decide the boundary — which means the map that ends up in a global database is yours rather than a consultant's. AND IT REACHES THE MAP THAT MATTERS: A LISTED SITE CAN ALSO BE ENTERED IN THE WORLD DATABASE OF PROTECTED AREAS, and the registry is COLLABORATIVELY GOVERNED BY A UN CONSERVATION MONITORING CENTRE WITH REPRESENTATIVES OF A UN DEVELOPMENT AGENCY, THE CONSORTIUM, A GLOBAL CONSERVATION UNION, A FOREST PEOPLES ORGANISATION AND TWO COMMUNITY FOUNDATIONS. Getting your territory into the world protected areas database is what makes it visible to every planner, funder and researcher who looks at a map of your country — and it does not require your government to declare anything. This file has recorded again and again that a place nobody has recorded is the easiest place to take. This is the recording route that starts with you. THE MEMBERSHIP, AND ITS COMPOSITION IS THE POINT: THE CONSORTIUM BRINGS TOGETHER 161 MEMBERS THAT ARE EITHER INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' ORGANISATIONS AND FEDERATIONS, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS AND FEDERATIONS, OR CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS WORKING CLOSELY WITH INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES — PLUS 401 HONORARY MEMBERS FROM 80 COUNTRIES, NOMINATED INDIVIDUALS WITH REMARKABLE EXPERIENCE, CONCERNS AND CAPACITIES TO SUPPORT THESE TERRITORIES. Community-based organisations and their FEDERATIONS are a membership category in their own right. Your village association can be a member of a global body without an NGO speaking for it. And four hundred honorary members are individuals — a lawyer, an ecologist, an anthropologist who can be asked for help. Ask which honorary members are in your country. THE AFRICAN PROGRAMME, WITH ITS THREE STATED PRIORITIES: IT APPEARS CRUCIAL TO CLAIM LEGAL AND SOCIAL RECOGNITION FOR THE TERRITORIES THAT STILL EXIST OR CAN BE EFFECTIVELY RESTORED; TO OBTAIN ECONOMIC SECURITY FOR THE LOCAL LIVELIHOODS THEY CAN SUPPORT; AND TO COMMAND RESPECT FOR THE LOCAL CUSTOMARY INSTITUTIONS THAT CAN STILL GOVERN EFFECTIVELY THE COMMUNITIES' INTERACTION WITH THEIR NATURAL RESOURCES — AND THE CONSORTIUM AND ITS AFRICAN MEMBERS STRIVE TO STRENGTHEN THOSE GOVERNING INSTITUTIONS AND TO SUPPORT COMMUNITIES TO DOCUMENT AND ENFORCE THEIR OWN COMMUNITY PROTOCOLS FOR BIODIVERSITY. OR CAN BE EFFECTIVELY RESTORED. A system that has lapsed is still eligible — you do not have to have kept it unbroken. And a COMMUNITY PROTOCOL that the community writes and enforces itself is the document to ask about: it states your rules in your terms, and it is what outsiders are then held to. THE NAMES MATTER, AND THEY ARE LISTED: himas, agdals, oran, ili, baldíos, wilayah adat, tagal, qoroq and many more — alongside COMMONS AND GREENS, ANCESTRAL DOMAINS, COMMUNITY CONSERVED AREAS, SACRED NATURAL SITES, AND LOCALLY MANAGED MARINE AREAS AND FISHING GROUNDS. Your system already has a name in your own language, and that name is recognised. When an official says there is no legal category for what your community does, this is the list showing the category exists and is documented worldwide. THE MOROCCAN MEMBER: A MOROCCAN BIODIVERSITY AND LIVELIHOODS ASSOCIATION ORGANISED A BIOCULTURAL FESTIVAL FOCUSED ON SUSTAINING TERRITORIES OF LIFE AND PRESERVING FARMERS' SEEDS AND TRADITIONAL CULINARY KNOWLEDGE, EMPHASISING SEMI-NOMADIC PASTORALISTS AND THE AGDALS' CONTRIBUTIONS TO BIODIVERSITY CONSERVATION. A festival about seeds and cooking that is also a land-rights event. Where a direct claim is difficult, the cultural route is a real one — and it brings the people who hold the knowledge into the same room as the people who write the policy. THE SCALE FIGURE FOR ANY ARGUMENT: POTENTIAL TERRITORIES OF LIFE ARE ESTIMATED TO COVER AT LEAST ONE-FIFTH OF THE WORLD'S LAND, AN AREA APPROXIMATELY THE SIZE OF THE AFRICAN CONTINENT. WHO IT SUITS: any African community with a customary conserved area, sacred site, agdal, hima or community fishing ground. CAVEATS: REGISTRY LISTING IS DOCUMENTATION, NOT LEGAL PROTECTION — pair it with a domestic instrument. For an association named after a turtle in a small town, Morocco's IFKER entry; for the campaign that won women a share of collective land, ADFM and the soulaliyate movement; for an oasis network crossing the Algerian border, AOFEP and RADDO; for the emergency fund with a 48-hour decision, Liberia's African Defenders Emergency Fund entry.

trackers.name: Digital Defenders Partnership — a free 24/7 digital security helpline for activists and community groups, four funds that pay for digital protection — including restoring internet access during a shutdown — and a free first aid kit for digital emergencies
trackers.desc: THERE IS A NUMBER TO CALL WHEN THE PHONES ARE THE PROBLEM — placement note first: THESE ARE GLOBAL SERVICES, FILED UNDER MOROCCO BECAUSE THIS BUCKET CARRIED NO DIGITAL-PROTECTION RESOURCE. THEY ARE REACHABLE FROM ANYWHERE IN AFRICA. THE HELPLINE, AND IT COSTS NOTHING: A FREE-OF-CHARGE RESOURCE FOR CIVIL SOCIETY WORLDWIDE, OFFERING DIRECT TECHNICAL ADVICE AND RAPID-RESPONSE EMERGENCY ASSISTANCE TO DIVERSE AT-RISK GROUPS — INCLUDING INDIVIDUAL ACTIVISTS, RESEARCHERS, MEDIA ORGANIZATIONS, JOURNALISTS, BLOGGERS, AND HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, AS WELL AS CIVIL SOCIETY COLLECTIVES OR ORGANIZATIONS — AVAILABLE 24/7 AND ACCESSIBLE ACROSS BORDERS AND TIME ZONES. INDIVIDUAL ACTIVISTS and COLLECTIVES, not only registered organisations. If your committee's WhatsApp group has been compromised, your Facebook page taken down, or your phone behaving strangely after a meeting with officials, there is a technical team that will answer at any hour, free. Almost nothing else in this file offers a person that. AND THE HONEST NOTE ABOUT WHAT USING IT COSTS YOU IN PRIVACY, WHICH IS PUBLISHED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: TO PROVIDE THESE SERVICES THE HELPLINE MAY REQUEST PERSONALLY IDENTIFIABLE INFORMATION, SUCH AS DETAILS RELATED TO YOUR COMPUTING SYSTEM OR WEBSITE, OR ACCESS TO YOUR DEVICES AND THEIR CONTENTS, WHICH MAY ALSO INCLUDE THIRD PARTY INFORMATION — IT ONLY REQUESTS THE DATA NEEDED TO PROVIDE ASSISTANCE, AND ONLY SHARES IT WITH SELECTED TEAM MEMBERS, TRUSTED PARTNERS, OR TECH PLATFORMS AS AND WHEN NEEDED TO SOLVE THE PROBLEM. Your device contents may include information about other people in your community. Decide before you hand over a phone what is on it and whose it is — that is a conversation to have with your committee once, calmly, rather than during an emergency. THE FUND'S STATED CONSTITUENCY PUTS THIS FILE'S READERS FIRST: IT SUPPORTS ACTIVISTS AND HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS WORKING ON ISSUES SUCH AS ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS, LGBTIQ+ ADVOCACY, GENDER EQUALITY, AND ELECTION MONITORING. ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS named first among the examples. THE FOUR FUNDS, EACH FOR A DIFFERENT SITUATION: A RAPID RESPONSE MECHANISM FOR DEFENDERS, JOURNALISTS AND ACTIVISTS FACING DIGITAL THREATS OR ATTACKS; A REGIONAL PARTNERSHIP FUND FOR INITIATIVES OPERATING IN A SINGLE COUNTRY OR REGION; A FUND TO HELP ORGANISATIONS BUILD DIGITAL SECURITY CAPACITIES OVER A MORE EXTENDED PERIOD; AND A FUND FOR INITIATIVES FROM RAPID RESPONDERS AND DIGITAL SECURITY FACILITATORS. AND WHAT THE REGIONAL FUND WILL PAY FOR IS THE FIND: THE PROVISION OF INTERNET ACCESS IN CASES OF SHUTDOWNS, SLOWDOWNS, CENSORSHIP, OR INFRASTRUCTURAL DAMAGE; THE PROVISION OF TRAINING OR ACCOMPANIMENT ON DIGITAL SECURITY OR OTHER ASPECTS OF SECURITY TO DEFENDERS AT RISK; THE PROVISION OF EXPERT ADVICE, DIGITAL FORENSIC ANALYSIS, HOSTING, OR OTHER TECHNICAL SERVICES TO CIVIL SOCIETY; AND LOBBYING AND ADVOCACY WORK FOR DIGITAL RIGHTS AND INTERNET FREEDOM. Money to restore internet access during a shutdown. Governments in this file's record cut the network precisely when a community is being moved or a protest is happening, and that is the moment evidence stops leaving the area. A fund that pays to get a connection back is paying for the record to survive. DIGITAL FORENSIC ANALYSIS is the other one to note: if you suspect a phone was infected after a meeting, forensics is what turns a suspicion into a documented fact — and it is expensive and fundable. THE REGIONAL OWNERSHIP, WHICH AFFECTS WHO READS YOUR APPLICATION: WHILE IT OPERATES GLOBALLY AND PRESENTS AS A SINGLE ORGANISATION, REGIONAL TEAMS HAVE OWNERSHIP OVER THE GRANTS TO BEST ALLOCATE THEM ACCORDING TO THEIR NEEDS AND CONTEXTS — AND APPLICANTS SHOULD BE COMMITTED TO STRENGTHENING LOCAL OR REGIONAL RESOURCES AND CAPACITIES, TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE NEEDS OF MARGINALISED PEOPLES. THE LANGUAGES: APPLICATIONS CAN BE PROCESSED IN ENGLISH, SPANISH, FRENCH AND PORTUGUESE — AND IF YOU WOULD LIKE TO SUBMIT IN ANOTHER LANGUAGE, YOU CAN CONTACT THEM WITH YOUR LANGUAGE REQUEST AND THEY WILL EXPLORE A SECURE SOLUTION. Four languages processed, and others negotiable on request. Ask rather than assume — and note the word SECURE: they will find a translator who can be trusted with the content, which is not a small thing when the application describes your security situation. THE RECORD: 133 DEFENDERS AND THEIR ORGANIZATIONS SUPPORTED WITH INCIDENT EMERGENCY FUNDING, AND 42 ORGANIZATIONS RECEIVED SUSTAINABLE PROTECTION FUNDING TO BUILD THEIR CAPACITY. THE FREE KIT: A DIGITAL FIRST AID KIT — A FREE RESOURCE TO HELP RAPID RESPONDERS, DIGITAL SECURITY TRAINERS, AND TECH-SAVVY ACTIVISTS BETTER PROTECT THEMSELVES AND THE COMMUNITIES THEY SUPPORT AGAINST THE MOST COMMON TYPES OF DIGITAL EMERGENCIES. Download it before anything happens and give it to the one person in your group who is good with phones. Most digital emergencies in this file's record are the common ones — a stolen account, a seized device, a phishing message — and the kit is written for exactly those. AND THE ACCOUNTABILITY ROUTE, WHICH FEW ORGANISATIONS PUBLISH: DONORS, PARTNERS, GRANTEES, CONSULTANTS AND OTHER STAKEHOLDERS WHO EXPERIENCE UNDESIRABLE BEHAVIOUR FROM ITS EMPLOYEES OR REPRESENTATIVES ARE INVITED TO REPORT IT VIA AN EXTERNAL COMPLAINTS MECHANISM. An external complaints mechanism for grantees, published on the funder's own site. Ask every organisation in this file whether it has one — the answer tells you what happens if the relationship goes wrong. WHO IT SUITS: African community organisations, individual activists and journalists facing surveillance, account takedowns, seized devices or network shutdowns. CAVEATS: THE HELPLINE MAY NEED ACCESS TO YOUR DEVICES — read the data note above before handing anything over. For the 24-hour helpline and protection grants covering digital security, Benin's defender protection entry; for the seven relocation host cities, Cape Verde's pan-African defenders network entry; for the fund naming land and environmental groups a priority, Tunisia's embattled-organisation fund entry.

trackers.name: The World Bank Grievance Redress Service (GRS) and Inspection Panel — two standing complaint desks a community can write to for free about a project it is living with — a development bank's grievance service that accepts complaints while a project is still under preparation, and a carbon standard's desk that takes anonymous complaints and charges no fee
trackers.desc: TWO DESKS THAT TAKE A WRITTEN COMPLAINT, FREE, BEFORE THE PROJECT EVEN STARTS — method and adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S LESOTHO ENTRY NOTES THAT THE STANDARDS BODIES AUDIT BENEFIT-SHARING WITHOUT NAMING THE COMPLAINTS DESK OR SHIPPING ITS HOST; ITS COMOROS BUCKET CARRIES A CARBON-MARKET WATCHDOG HOST; ITS ETHIOPIA ENTRY THE DEVELOPMENT-BANK PROJECT DATABASE; ITS NIGERIA BUCKET AN INSPECTION PANEL MENTION. THE BANK'S NAME APPEARS IN FIVE DESCRIPTIONS IN PASSING; NEITHER IS THIS DESK. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THE SHIPPED HOST AND FOUR SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE BANK'S COMPLAINT DESK, WHICH IS THE FIND: AN AVENUE FOR INDIVIDUALS AND COMMUNITIES TO SUBMIT COMPLAINTS DIRECTLY TO THE BANK IF THEY BELIEVE A BANK-SUPPORTED PROJECT HAS OR IS LIKELY TO HAVE ADVERSE EFFECTS ON THEM, THEIR COMMUNITY, OR THEIR ENVIRONMENT. DIRECTLY. No lawyer, no NGO intermediary, no national court first. A community writes to the institution financing the road, dam or plantation on its land, and that institution has an office obliged to receive the letter. THE THREE ADMISSIBILITY CONDITIONS, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE COMPLAINT RELATES TO A BANK-SUPPORTED PROJECT UNDER PREPARATION, ACTIVE, OR CLOSED FOR LESS THAN 15 MONTHS; IT IS SUBMITTED BY AFFECTED INDIVIDUALS OR COMMUNITIES, OR BY THEIR AUTHORIZED REPRESENTATIVE; AND THE COMPLAINANTS ALLEGE THEY HAVE BEEN OR WILL BE AFFECTED. UNDER PREPARATION IS ADMISSIBLE, AND SO IS HARM THAT IS ONLY LIKELY. That is the sentence that matters most in this whole entry: almost every route recorded in this file requires damage to have already happened. Here a community can complain about a project that has not broken ground — which is the only point at which stopping it is cheap. And CLOSED FOR LESS THAN 15 MONTHS means a finished project is not automatically out of reach. THE THREE WAYS TO SEND IT: ONLINE THROUGH A FORM; BY EMAIL TO A PUBLISHED ADDRESS; OR BY LETTER OR HAND DELIVERY TO THE BANK'S HEADQUARTERS OR ANY BANK COUNTRY OFFICE, USING A PRINTABLE FORM. HAND DELIVERY TO ANY COUNTRY OFFICE. There is one in most capitals, so a delegation can carry the letter in and get it stamped — no internet, no postage, and a witness that it was received. WHAT THE COMPLAINT MUST CONTAIN: IT MUST BE IN WRITING AND ADDRESSED TO THE SERVICE, IDENTIFY THE PROJECT SUBJECT OF THE COMPLAINT, AND CLEARLY STATE THE PROJECT'S ADVERSE IMPACTS. Two requirements: name the project, state the harm. Identifying the project by its official number and title is where community complaints usually fail — and this file's Ethiopia entry records the database where those numbers are found. THE VOLUME IT HANDLES: AN AVERAGE OF 302 COMPLAINTS OVER THE LAST THREE FISCAL YEARS, COVERING A WIDE SPECTRUM OF PROJECT-RELATED ISSUES — WITH AN ANNUAL REPORT, A BROCHURE, A VIDEO AND PUBLISHED FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS. Three hundred a year worldwide, which is few enough that a well-made complaint is genuinely read rather than lost in a queue. THE CARBON STANDARD'S DESK AND ITS TERMS: ALL NEW COMPLAINTS SHOULD BE DIRECTED TO A PUBLISHED COMPLAINTS EMAIL ADDRESS; IF NECESSARY, COMPLAINTS MAY BE SUBMITTED ANONYMOUSLY; AND IT WILL NOT CHARGE FEES FOR PROCESSING COMPLAINTS. ANONYMOUS AND FREE. Where naming yourself is dangerous — the condition this file records again and again — that combination is rare enough to be worth the entry on its own. HOW THAT COMPLAINT IS HANDLED: ADDRESSED TO THE APPROPRIATE PROGRAM MANAGER LISTED ON THE WEBSITE AND EMAILED WITH THE WORD COMPLAINT IN THE SUBJECT LINE; RECEIPT IS ACKNOWLEDGED BY EMAIL; AN APPOINTED PERSON ORGANISES AN ANALYSIS INVOLVING EXTERNAL EXPERTS AS REQUIRED; AND A WRITTEN RESPONSE IS PREPARED AND APPROVED BY THE CHIEF EXECUTIVE. The word COMPLAINT in the subject line is a literal routing instruction. Get it wrong and the message goes to general correspondence. THE SEPARATE COMMENT WINDOW BEFORE A PROJECT IS APPROVED: A 60-DAY COMMENT PERIOD PUBLISHED ON THE WEBSITE DURING VALIDATION, SUBMITTED THROUGH A PUBLIC COMMENT BOX ON THE PROJECT PAGE, WITH A CONTACT NAME, COUNTRY OR AREA, ORGANISATION NAME AND EMAIL, TO A MAXIMUM OF 5,000 CHARACTERS, AND WITH ALL AVAILABLE PROJECT INFORMATION SHOWN BELOW THE BOX. Sixty days, on a public page, BEFORE the project is certified — and the project's own documents are displayed right there to be read and answered. Objecting during the window is far more effective than complaining after certification, and 5,000 characters is roughly two pages. THE REFORMS FORCED ON ONE DEVELOPER, WHICH SHOW WHAT A GRIEVANCE PROCEDURE MUST CONTAIN: DETERMINE WHY THE EXISTING PROCEDURE FAILED TO SUPPORT REPORTING AND DETECTION; ESTABLISH ONE PROVIDING FOR ANONYMOUS FILING AND PROTECTING COMPLAINANT CONFIDENTIALITY; PROVIDE ALL STAFF AND CONTRACTORS REGULAR AND ONGOING MANDATORY TRAINING; AND PUBLICIZE IT TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES IN A CULTURALLY-APPROPRIATE MANNER, INCLUDING LANGUAGE AND GENDER SENSITIVITY. That is a four-point checklist for judging any developer's own complaints procedure. If the company on your land cannot show anonymous filing, staff training and materials in your language, its procedure has already failed the standard its certifier applies. WHAT AN ASSESSMENT OF THESE MECHANISMS FOUND CHANGED: SUBMISSION FEES ELIMINATED, A DETAILED PROCESS DESCRIPTION PUBLISHED, ANONYMOUS COMPLAINTS ACCEPTED, AND IN CASE OF LEGAL DISPUTES THE COMPLAINT AND ITS OUTCOME NOTED ON THE RELEVANT REGISTRY PROJECT WEBSITE; A SECOND REGISTRY SPECIFIED TIMEFRAMES FOR EACH PHASE, BROADENED SUBMISSIONS TO ANY STAKEHOLDER, AND PROVIDES ADEQUATE ASSISTANCE FOR THOSE WHO MAY FACE BARRIERS TO ACCESSING THE MECHANISM. A complaint recorded permanently on the project's own public registry page is a lasting mark on an asset somebody is trying to sell credits from — which is leverage of a kind no letter to a ministry produces. And ASSISTANCE FOR THOSE WHO FACE BARRIERS is a thing to ask for by name. AND THE PRINCIPLE A WATCHDOG PUT IN WRITING WHEN IT FILED: WE CALL ON YOU TO CONDUCT THE NECESSARY INVESTIGATION FREE OF CHARGE TO THE COMPLAINANT — REQUIRING THE COMPLAINANT TO PAY THE ASSOCIATED COSTS WOULD BE TO RESTRICT ACCESS TO THE GRIEVANCE MECHANISM DESIGNED TO ADDRESS THE CONCERNS OF CIVIL SOCIETY, VULNERABLE GROUPS AND MARGINALISED COMMUNITIES. Worth copying verbatim if any body ever asks a community to fund the investigation of its own complaint. WHO IT SUITS: African communities affected by, or about to be affected by, a development-bank-financed project or a certified carbon project — including those who cannot safely put their names to a complaint. CAVEATS: THESE ARE THE FINANCIER'S AND THE CERTIFIER'S OWN DESKS, NOT INDEPENDENT COURTS — THEY REVIEW, THEY DO NOT ORDER COMPENSATION; THE BANK'S DESK ONLY COVERS PROJECTS THAT BANK SUPPORTS, AND A PROJECT CLOSED OVER 15 MONTHS IS OUT OF TIME. For the database that identifies which bank finances a project, Ethiopia's entry; for the community carbon project and its published criticism, Lesotho's entry.

trackers.name: Mikoko Pamoja, Gazi Bay, Kenya — the world's first community-led blue carbon project: a registered community organisation guarding 117 hectares of state-owned mangrove and holding the revenue, certified under Plan Vivo with ACES
trackers.desc: THE STATE OWNS THE FOREST; THE VILLAGE OWNS THE INCOME FROM GUARDING IT — method and adjacency declared first: FIFTH ACQUISITION-ONLY ROUND. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL HOSTS AND FOUR FACTS ABSENT. TWO MATCHED AND WERE READ IN FULL: A UGANDA ENTRY DESCRIBING A TERRESTRIAL SCHEME OF INDIVIDUAL LANDOWNER CONTRACTS ON ITS OWN HOST, AND A GENERIC ASSOCIATION NAME IN TWO BUCKETS. DIFFERENT SUBJECTS, NOT RESTATED. THIS FILE'S LESOTHO ENTRY COVERS THE CARBON ROUTE WHERE COMMUNITY LAND STAYS IN TITLE AND ITS CAPE VERDE ENTRY THE PAY-TO-KEEP-IT-OPEN LEASE. NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHAT THE COMMUNITY ACTUALLY GOT, WHICH IS THE FIND: THE COMMUNITY ORGANISATION NOW SERVES AS THE GUARDIAN OF 117 HECTARES OF STATE-OWNED MANGROVES, NEARLY 16% OF THE BAY'S MANGROVE ECOSYSTEM — COMMITTING OVER 20 YEARS TO PROTECTING 107 HECTARES OF NATURAL FOREST AND CONSERVING 10 HECTARES OF PLANTATION. The four acquisition rounds before this assumed the community could get title, or be paid as titleholders. This is the route for the far commoner situation in Africa: the land is the state's, and it always will be. What was acquired instead was the guardianship and the revenue — which is a weaker claim than ownership and a far more available one. WHO HOLDS THE MONEY, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: REVENUE FROM THE TRADING OF CARBON CREDITS FLOWS INTO A COMMUNITY BENEFIT FUND, MANAGED BY THE COMMUNITY-LED STEERING GROUP, SUPPORTING LOCAL DEVELOPMENT IN EDUCATION, WATER AND SANITATION, AND REFORESTATION — WITH AN INITIAL GOAL TO RETURN AT LEAST 70% OF THE PROFITS TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES. The fund is managed by the community's own steering group, not by the certifying body or the research partner. Compare the peer-reviewed criticism recorded in this file's Lesotho entry, where ranch owners held binding contracts and communities held the residue: here the percentage was set at the outset and the account is theirs. THE REGISTERED BODY THAT IS REQUIRED: COMMUNITY ASSOCIATIONS ARE A REQUIRED PART OF PROJECTS UNDER THIS STANDARD AND HELP ENSURE EQUITABLE BENEFIT SHARING — THE TWO SITES HAVING ESTABLISHED THE MIKOKO PAMOJA COMMUNITY ORGANIZATION (MPCO) AND THE VANGA JIMBO AND KIWEGU COMMUNITY FOREST ASSOCIATION (VAJIKI), WITH POLICIES THAT MUST BE FOLLOWED FOR THE GOVERNMENT TO AUTHORIZE THE SALE. The registered community body is not optional — the standard requires it. That is the first task for any village considering this, and it is the same registration barrier this file records at every funder, here with a clear payoff at the end of it. THE MONEY, WITH ITS HONEST RANGE: VALIDATED TO SELL AT LEAST 3,000 METRIC TONS OF CO2 EQUIVALENT PER YEAR FROM 2013 TO 2033 — WITH ONE ACCOUNT PUTTING EXPECTED ANNUAL REVENUE AT ABOUT $130,000, ANOTHER RECORDING OVER US$12,000 EARNED ANNUALLY, AND A THIRD RECORDING 9,880 CREDITS FROM 2014 TO 2018 WITH PAYMENTS TO THE COMMUNITY TOTALLING $58,591. The spread between $130,000 expected and roughly $14,600 a year actually received is the most useful number here. Carbon revenue projections are not revenue. A community negotiating one of these should ask what was PAID at comparable sites, not what was forecast. WHAT THE INCOME PAID FOR IN STAFF: A FULL-TIME PROJECT MANAGER AND TWO FULL-TIME GUARDS TO PREVENT ILLEGAL DEFORESTATION — WITH OVER 200 DIRECT AND INDIRECT EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES FOR LOCAL VILLAGERS. Three salaried posts out of that revenue, and the guards are the mechanism: the forest is protected because the village now employs people to protect it, rather than because a law says so. WHAT IT PAID FOR IN THE VILLAGES: PUMPS PROVIDING CLEAN DRINKING WATER FOR SEVERAL HUNDRED SCHOOLCHILDREN AND NEARLY 5,400 PEOPLE IN THE BROADER COMMUNITY, AND TEXTBOOKS, SPORTS UNIFORMS AND OTHER LEARNING MATERIALS FOR 700 CHILDREN, PLUS SCHOOL BUILDINGS. Modest sums, visible results. Worth knowing the realistic scale before a community commits twenty years of a forest to it. THE TRIGGER AND THE TIMELINE: IN 2010, AFTER LOSING ABOUT 20 PER CENT OF THEIR MANGROVE FORESTS TO TIMBER HARVESTING, RESIDENTS PARTNERED WITH A UK CHARITY AND A SCOTLAND-BASED COASTAL ECOSYSTEM SERVICES ASSOCIATION — FORMALLY ESTABLISHED IN 2012 FOLLOWING OVER TWO DECADES OF RESEARCH AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT LED BY TWO NAMED SCIENTISTS. Two decades of prior research is the uncomfortable precondition. This did not start from nothing; it started from a bay that was already among the best-studied in the world, which is why the baseline could be proved. A community without that history should expect the measurement stage to be the expensive part. THE PLANTING AND WHO DOES IT: OVER 10,000 MANGROVE TREES PLANTED BETWEEN 2012 AND 2017, SUPPLIED BY A NURSERY ESTABLISHED TO CULTIVATE WILD SEEDLINGS COLLECTED FROM OTHER AREAS OF THE BAY — WITH NEARLY 500 COMMUNITY MEMBERS PARTICIPATING IN REGULAR PLANTING. Seedlings collected locally rather than bought. The nursery is the cheap, copyable component. THE FOUR STEPS TO CERTIFICATION, PUBLISHED: EACH SITE FOLLOWED A NUMBER OF STEPS TO BE CERTIFIED — THE PROJECT DESIGN STAGE INCLUDING DEVELOPING A PROJECT CONCEPT, CHOOSING OR DEVELOPING A BASELINE AND MONITORING METHODOLOGY, AND STAKEHOLDER CONSULTATIONS. The route is documented rather than proprietary, and a second community used it. Ask for the published guidance before engaging a developer who offers to handle it for you. WHAT THE PARTNERS WERE FOR: PARTNERS INCLUDING AN ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE, A UNIVERSITY AND A NATIONAL MARINE AND FISHERIES RESEARCH INSTITUTE PLAYED A PIVOTAL ROLE IN LINKING COMMUNITY TO CARBON BUYERS — WITH THE STATE FOREST SERVICE AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES TOGETHER FORMING THE STEERING GROUP. LINKING COMMUNITY TO CARBON BUYERS is the function to procure. A community can guard a forest and measure it; finding a buyer is the part that requires an outside partner, and naming that gap honestly is better than assuming a broker will be fair. WHAT ITS OWN PARTICIPANTS SAY MADE IT WORK: BROAD SCALE ENGAGEMENT INCLUDING WOMEN AND YOUTH, AND INCLUSIVE IMPLEMENTATION ESPECIALLY REGARDING THE USE OF INCOMES FROM CARBON CREDIT SALES, ENSURING TRANSPARENT AND EQUITABLE BENEFIT DISTRIBUTION — WITH GENDER BALANCE IN THE LEADERSHIP, AN ECOTOURISM BOARDWALK MANAGED BY 27 WOMEN, AND A PARTICIPANT WITH A DISABILITY RECORDING THAT PEOPLE WITH DISABILITIES ARE OFTEN LEFT OUT BUT HERE ARE RECOGNIZED, RESPECTED AND GIVEN A PLATFORM. Transparency about the money named as the success factor, by the people receiving it. This file has recorded royalty accounts turning won claims into disputes; the answer given here is that the spending is decided and reported in public. AND WHAT FOLLOWED IT: IT INSPIRED OTHER COMMUNITY-LED PROJECTS INCLUDING VANGA BLUE FOREST ON THE BORDER WITH TANZANIA UNDER THE SAME STANDARD; IT WON A GLOBAL EQUATOR PRIZE IN 2017 AND A NATIONAL UN AWARD IN 2023 — WITH THE CAVEAT THAT FOR COMMUNITIES TO EARN FUNDS THROUGH CARBON PROJECTS, NECESSARY LEGISLATION HAS TO BE IN PLACE. That last clause is the checkable precondition: find out whether your country has authorised community sale of carbon from state land before spending anything on design. WHO IT SUITS: coastal and forest communities living beside state-owned land they cannot own but already protect, and any village weighing a carbon offer against what comparable projects were actually paid. CAVEATS: THE COMMUNITY DOES NOT ACQUIRE THE LAND — IT ACQUIRES GUARDIANSHIP AND REVENUE, UNDER A 20-YEAR COMMITMENT; REVENUE FIGURES VARY WIDELY BETWEEN SOURCES AND THE RECEIVED AMOUNTS ARE FAR BELOW THE PROJECTIONS; AND IT REQUIRES A REGISTERED ASSOCIATION, GOVERNMENT AUTHORISATION AND A MEASURED BASELINE. For the carbon route with its peer-reviewed criticism, Lesotho's entry; for payment to keep titled land open, Cape Verde's entry.

trackers.name: Ask Your Government Uganda
trackers.desc: Ask Your Government Uganda — Uganda’s civil-society FOI request portal (Africa Freedom of Information Centre) — citizens make requests under the 2005 Access to Information Act and responses are published publicly. — Holds to account: Uganda’s public authorities on disclosure — find public FOI requests, responses and non-responses.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a pan-African feminist rapid-response fund with reach across all 54 African countries — small grants released quickly for unanticipated, time-critical situations rather than planned programme work, covering safety and protection needs when defenders are threatened and short windows for advocacy after an unexpected event. WHO IT SUITS: women's rights organisations, feminist collectives and movements in which women or gender-diverse people are the primary decision-makers. It does NOT fund individuals, and the action must be strategic, genuinely unanticipated, and completable in under three months. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is emergency money for a moment, not a budget for a campaign — decisions are fast and grants are modest.

trackers.name: Government Procurement Portal (PPDA)
trackers.desc: Uganda's central government-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Uganda, and for how much.

trackers.name: ULII
trackers.desc: Uganda Legal Information Institute: free case law and legislation (AfricanLII network). · Find here: free Ugandan judgments and legislation (ULII / Laws.Africa).

trackers.name: Uganda Registration Services Bureau (URSB)
trackers.desc: Uganda’s official registry of companies and business entities — searchable incorporation records.

trackers.name: ACODE (Advocates Coalition for Development and Environment)
trackers.desc: Ugandan public-policy research and advocacy think tank. Runs the Local Government Councils Scorecard Initiative, assessing the performance of district councils, chairpersons, speakers and individual councillors across 35+ districts, and strengthens parliamentary and district oversight through budget tracking and Public Accounts Committee support.

trackers.name: Civil Society Budget Advocacy Group (CSBAG)
trackers.desc: Ugandan coalition (formed 2004) of CSOs influencing national and district budget processes — resource mobilisation, allocation and utilisation — and pushing for transparency and accountability in public spending. Here you can trace how Uganda's national and district budgets allocate resources, tracked by the CSBAG civil-society coalition.

trackers.name: Inspectorate of Government (IGG)
trackers.desc: National anti-corruption body of Uganda — investigates graft, financial crime and abuse of public office.

trackers.name: Office of the Auditor General (Uganda)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Uganda — audits government accounts and the use of public money.

trackers.name: CCO and Communal Land Association — the vehicle and the instrument
trackers.desc: UGANDA STARTS FROM AN UNUSUALLY STRONG POSITION: Article 237 of the Constitution and section 2 of the Land Act vest land in the citizens of Uganda — the opposite of Nigeria, where all land vests in the Governor. TWO ROUTES THAT COMBINE. Section 4(1) lets any person, family or community holding under customary tenure apply for a Certificate of Customary Ownership; a Land Committee processes it under section 5 and the District Land Board decides under section 8. THE EFFECT IS THE POINT: the certificate shall be taken as conclusive evidence of the customary rights specified in it — conclusive, not merely prima facie, unlike Nigeria's rebuttable Certificate of Occupancy. Section 15 then allows a Communal Land Association to be formed by any group of persons for any purpose connected with communal ownership and management of land, whether under customary law or otherwise — and communal land may be held under a CCO or freehold title by the managing committee on behalf of the association. So the CLA is the vehicle and the CCO the instrument. Formation is controlled by the Registrar of Titles, and disputes are resolved by the Registrar under section 20 — an administrative route, not only the courts. WATCH section 22, individual holding created out of communal land, if fragmentation is your threat.

trackers.name: Record your boundary markers and witnesses before a dispute
trackers.desc: THE HONEST PICTURE, FROM UGANDAN LAND ORGANISATIONS. Registration of customary land is described as complex, tedious and unaffordable to the majority of communities, with the process marred by gaps in service delivery in land administration institutions — and the National Land Policy 2013 and the Land Act contradict each other on the type of registry and documentation intended. THE SMALLEST PROPORTION OF LAND IN UGANDA IS REGISTERED, so rights recognition relies on informal mechanisms and non-documentary evidence: boundaries demarcated by ant hills, streams, hill tops, trees, shrubs or stones, with ownership witnessed by the clan, council of elders or family head. THOSE WITNESSED MARKERS ARE YOUR EVIDENCE — photograph them, map them and record who witnessed them now, not after a dispute starts. WHAT COUNTS AS COMMUNAL LAND is wider than productive ground: grazing grounds, hunting grounds, forest, rock outcrops, spiritual sites, and rivers and wetlands. HELP THAT EXISTS: a published step-by-step guide covers the CCO, the Communal Land Association and establishing a Land Trust in three chapters, written for chiefdoms, clans and cultural leaders. And two state remedies are under way — SLAAC systematic adjudication and certification, and Zonal Land Offices decentralising services.

trackers.name: ECOTRUST Trees for Global Benefits — it pays landowners to keep land under trees, in instalments, against a 25-year lock-in
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a Ugandan conservation trust that pays smallholders and community groups to put and keep their land under trees, selling the resulting carbon credits to buyers on the voluntary market under the Plan Vivo standard. Running since 2003, it works across districts in the Albertine Rift, the Queen Elizabeth and Murchison landscapes and the Mount Elgon ecosystem. Through 2024 it reports having paid out US$8.78 million to 51,874 participating households across 34,286 hectares in 26 districts, and states that US$6 of every US$10 raised reaches the farmer. For a household under pressure to sell or clear land, this is one of the few routes in the region where keeping land wooded produces cash rather than only costing money. HOW THE MONEY ARRIVES, WHICH IS THE PART TO UNDERSTAND BEFORE SIGNING: payments are performance-based and staged — reported as falling in years 1, 3, 5, 7 and 10, on verification that the trees are there — and they sit inside a 25-year carbon contract with a land use plan attached. WHO IT SUITS — AND THE TRAP: the payments stop around year 10 but the obligation to maintain the trees runs the full 25 years, so the last fifteen years are unpaid stewardship on land you can no longer convert. Independent analysts also find that minimum plot sizes and the opportunity cost of taking cropland out of production push participation toward households with larger holdings, disadvantaging the poorest, and that the trust answers in practice to credit buyers more than to the smallholders it contracts with. A newer northern Uganda programme is designed around free, prior and informed consent and grower-developed land use plans, which suggests the criticism has landed — ask which terms apply to your scheme. Treat this as a way to fund holding land against development, entered with the lock-in understood, rather than as a grant.

trackers.name: Greenwatch — 29 years of environmental public interest litigation in Uganda, and it is opening a legal aid clinic
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the organisation that built environmental public interest litigation in Uganda. It brought the cases the profession names — the chimpanzee case, the kaveera (plastic bags) case, the pangolin case — and in 2012 it went to court with four children suing through a next friend, on their own behalf and that of the born and unborn children of Uganda, against the Attorney General and the national environment authority over failure to act on climate change. It publishes handbooks on Ugandan environmental law and a casebook of the decisions, which is the cheapest preparation available to a community lawyer here. IT IS ALSO EXPANDING WHAT IT OFFERS: Greenwatch states it is opening a legal aid clinic to widen its environmental justice and litigation work, and is training young lawyers, journalists, and — the unusual one — science experts in how to write witness statements and present evidence for environmental court proceedings. If your fight will turn on technical evidence, that last programme is the one to ask about. THE LESSON ITS OWN CASEBOOK RECORDS, WHICH YOU SHOULD READ BEFORE CELEBRATING A WIN: in one successful action the applicants could not enforce the judgment because it was merely declaratory — the permit was revoked but the developer stayed on the forest land, which it had already cut and replanted. Ask what order you are actually seeking, and whether anyone can execute it. Greenwatch also publishes a community-based guide to monitoring the impacts of oil and gas activity. WHO IT SUITS: Ugandan communities facing forest loss, oil and gas displacement, or a permit granted without consultation. Plot 7/9 Second Street, Industrial Area, Kinyara House, Kampala; +256 41 4344613; environment@greenwatch.or.ug. CAVEATS: no published intake criteria or means test; the legal aid clinic was announced rather than described, so confirm it is running; and its own practitioners point to the difficulty of funding environmental litigation as the recurring constraint.

trackers.name: LEMU — helps northern Ugandan communities register their commons, and publishes the risks of the certificates it helps them get
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Land and Equity Movement in Uganda, working mainly in the north and east where land ownership is almost entirely customary, to secure family and community land rights. It is a legal aid service provider: its listed work includes legal representation, legal advice, mediation and community paralegal work, alongside research and advocacy. THE PROCESS IT RUNS WHEN A COMMUNITY ASKS IT TO PROTECT A COMMONS — grazing land or wetland — is a sequence worth copying: collectively envisioning past, present and future use of the land; publicly drafting, evaluating and agreeing rules for managing it; strengthening the local governance structure that will hold it; resolving disputes and documenting boundaries with boundary trees and maps; and then formally documenting it, by registering a Communal Land Association and/or applying for a Certificate of Customary Ownership or a freehold title. Note the order: the rules and the boundaries come before the paperwork. In northern Uganda the commons is not a luxury — grazing land is also where households get fuel, water, food, building materials and traditional medicines. THE REASON TO READ ITS PUBLICATIONS BEFORE APPLYING FOR ANYTHING: LEMU publishes a policy brief titled, in effect, that Certificates of Customary Ownership are not what they seem on the surface, setting out the risks of CCOs, and another with questions to ask the promoters of current titles and certificates. It has also documented the complexities and failures of Communal Land Associations in Karamoja and written on the tragedy of the owners of the commons. An organisation that hands you the case against its own instrument is the one to trust on which instrument you need. It has codified customary law in the Principles, Practices, Rights and Responsibilities papers for Lango, Acholi and Kumam/Teso, published in local languages, which courts and land managers can be pointed at. Plot 39A Namuwongo Bukasa Road, Kampala. WHO IT SUITS: customary landholding families and communities in northern and eastern Uganda, especially those defending communal grazing land or wetland, and women whose customary rights are being denied. CAVEATS: focused on the north and east, not nationwide; documenting land is not the same as winning a fight with a developer, and LEMU's own briefs warn that a certificate can create new exposure as well as protection.

trackers.name: ACTogether Uganda and the National Slum Dwellers Federation — communities that map their own settlements, and whose maps the city had to use
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the National Slum Dwellers Federation of Uganda (NSDFU), a movement of urban poor residents organised around savings groups — reported at 355 savings groups across cities including Kampala, Arua, Jinja, Kabale, Mbale and Mbarara, and operating in some 20 towns and cities — together with ACTogether Uganda, the support NGO founded in September 2006 that provides its technical assistance. WHAT THEY DO THAT NOBODY ELSE WILL DO FOR YOU: residents profile, enumerate and map their own settlements, gathering data on land tenure, services, housing and livelihoods, with questionnaires administered by slum dwellers themselves. In Kampala they identified and profiled 62 settlements and handed the mapped report to the city authority. THE MOMENT THAT PROVES WHY THIS IS WORTH DOING: the city's own most recent map showed 31 slums; the federation's showed 62. When international consultants were commissioned for a water and sanitation feasibility study, they found official population data twelve years old and seriously understating the scale of settlement — and asked the federation to share its map to overlay with the city's. The federation and ACTogether were invited onto the project steering committee as the only community representatives. Whoever holds the only current map of where people actually live has to be dealt with. Their own profiling found nearly 70 per cent of Kampala's settlements had faced eviction threat, and a federation organiser explains the database is updated precisely because the data government cites to justify evictions is out of date. WHO IT SUITS: Ugandan urban communities facing eviction, upgrading or resettlement, and any community that needs to prove who lives where before someone else counts them. CAVEATS: this is legal-empowerment-by-data and negotiation, not litigation — for court work Uganda's Greenwatch entry is the route, and for rural customary land, LEMU. ACTogether's own site did not resolve to a verified page; this entry points at the network affiliate record documenting the alliance.

trackers.name: Uganda Land Alliance — 60+ member consortium running Land Rights Information Centres you can walk into in district towns
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Uganda Land Alliance, a membership consortium of more than 60 national and international organisations and individuals working on land rights for poor and marginalised people, listed on Uganda's legal aid service providers' network. WHAT MAKES IT USABLE RATHER THAN JUST NATIONAL: it has established LAND RIGHTS INFORMATION CENTRES hosted WITH partner organisations in the regions — reported at Kibaale district (Kagadi) with a rural development and training programme for the west; Mbale with the Uganda Association of Women Lawyers (FIDA-Uganda); Kapchorwa and Luweero with a development organisation and a volunteer development body for the east; and a centre in Kampala with the Legal Aid Project of the Uganda Law Society. It also uses public meetings, radio and newspaper advertising to explain land law and policy to people who will never read a statute. A referral consortium is worth more than any single organisation when you do not yet know which kind of help you need — a household facing eviction, an inheritance dispute and a company survey all start at the same counter. WHERE IT HAS DONE THE FIELDWORK: studies on land tenure and livelihoods in the Albertine Graben oil districts of Hoima, Buliisa, Amuru and Nwoya, where international oil companies operate, and documentation across eight districts on women's progress in claiming land. Its stated standard is that no one should be deprived of the use and control of the land their well-being depends on — through eviction, expulsion or exclusion — and that compulsory changes to tenure happen only in line with international human rights standards, with explicit emphasis on women's ability to defend, inherit and bequeath land. Plot 54, Muwafu Road, Ntinda, Kampala. WHO IT SUITS: Ugandans anywhere in the country who need to find the right land-rights help locally, especially women, and communities in the oil districts. CAVEATS: a consortium and information network — the casework happens at member organisations, so expect a referral rather than direct representation; centre coverage is partial and partner-dependent. For customary certificates and their risks, Uganda's LEMU entry; for litigation, Greenwatch; for urban settlements, ACTogether.

trackers.name: Bwindi Mgahinga Conservation Trust — an endowment where the BULK of the income is legally earmarked for the communities, not the park
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: BMCT, a registered trust fund established in 1994 under the Uganda Trust Act to provide long-term funding for the biodiversity of Bwindi Impenetrable and Mgahinga Gorilla national parks in south-western Uganda. It is a registered NGO run by a Trust Management Board under a Trust Deed, and it does NOT manage the parks — the wildlife authority does — so it is not the body that excluded you from the forest; it is the body that disburses money to the people living beside it. HOW THE MONEY IS SPLIT, AND WHY THAT SPLIT IS THE POINT: its principal strategy is working with the communities close to the two parks through the PROVISION OF GRANTS, intended to reduce dependency on the protected areas; park management receives grants amounting to a reported 20 per cent of income, and the BULK of net annual income is LEGALLY EARMARKED for community development — from common-good projects such as primary school classrooms, health units and rural roads to individual income-generating activities. Ask of any conservation trust near you what share of its income the deed obliges it to spend on communities; an endowment whose deed says “bulk” is a different instrument from one that grants at the board's discretion. The operational arm, the Trust Administrative Unit, is based at Kabale, with a Kampala office at Plot 1 Katalima Crescent, Naguru. WHO IT SUITS: communities and households adjacent to Bwindi and Mgahinga — including those displaced or restricted by the parks — seeking grant funding for community projects or livelihoods. CAVEATS: STRICTLY GEOGRAPHIC — it funds only around those two parks, and it funds development and conservation, NOT litigation, land purchase or opposition to a project; it works in partnership with the wildlife authority, so it is not an independent champion against park policy. For payments to landowners for keeping land under trees, Uganda's ECOTRUST entry; for customary certificates, LEMU.

trackers.name: Justice Centres Uganda — a state one-stop legal aid service with a TOLL-FREE line, and the extractives lawyers to call alongside it
trackers.desc: WHERE TO GET A FREE LAWYER: Justice Centres Uganda, a one-stop legal aid model within the justice sector, offering legal advice, LEGAL REPRESENTATION, alternative dispute resolution, counselling, legal awareness, referrals and a TOLL-FREE PHONE LINE. ELIGIBILITY IS THE FIRST THING TO CHECK, because it is strict: to qualify you must be among the most indigent persons in Uganda. Districts served from the Lira centre are published — Amolatar, Pader, Apac, Kitgum, Oyam, Dokolo, Kaberamaido and Kotido — so northern Uganda is covered from a named base rather than only from Kampala. WHY IT MATTERS HERE: justice-needs research cited by the justice sector found 88 per cent of Ugandans had experienced difficulty accessing justice over four years, with LAND and family cases the top two most critical disputes; a later study found 45 per cent of legal problems unresolved — 29 per cent still ongoing and 16 per cent abandoned. Abandonment is the real outcome to guard against: most people do not lose their land case, they stop being able to pursue it. Alongside the state service, regional legal aid clinics run with the Uganda Law Society provide pro bono civil and criminal services including land disputes. AND FOR OIL, GAS AND MINERALS SPECIFICALLY: ANARDE (Advocates for Natural Resources and Development) is a Ugandan non-profit of researchers, organisers and LAWYERS working on environmental governance and corporate and government accountability, arguing that the environment and land rights of communities where oil, gas and minerals are located must be protected and that extractive revenues be disclosed — with explicit focus on women in the natural resource sector. WHO IT SUITS: indigent Ugandans with a land or family dispute, especially in the north; and communities in the oil and mineral districts needing lawyers who know the sector. CAVEATS: JUSTICE CENTRES HAS NO VERIFIED STANDALONE SITE — this entry points at the justice sector's published account, and the indigence test excludes many who still cannot afford a lawyer; coverage is by centre, so confirm which districts your nearest one serves. For land rights information centres, Uganda's ULA entry; for environmental litigation, Greenwatch; for customary certificates, LEMU.

trackers.name: NatureUganda and the sacred natural sites custodians — East Africa's oldest conservation society as a membership body, and the eco-cultural mapping that won Africa's first law recognising sacred sites
trackers.desc: THE THREE MAPS AND THE LAW THEY WON: NATUREUGANDA (NU, natureuganda.org) IS THE OPERATIONAL NAME OF THE EAST AFRICA NATURAL HISTORY SOCIETY IN UGANDA — EANHS WAS SET UP IN 1909 AND IS THE OLDEST CONSERVATION ORGANISATION IN EAST AFRICA; the Uganda branch was restarted in the early 1990s with bird walks, REGISTERED AS A NON-PROFIT INDEPENDENT NATIONAL ORGANISATION IN 1995, and is NOW THE LEADING MEMBERSHIP-BASED CONSERVATION ORGANISATION IN UGANDA, holding an ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING its members are invited to. Its stated mission includes ADVOCATING FOR POLICIES FAVOURABLE TO THE ENVIRONMENT AND TAKING ACTION TO CONSERVE PRIORITY SPECIES, SITES AND HABITATS FOR THE BENEFIT OF PEOPLE. A membership society with an AGM is one where joining buys a vote and a floor. If your site needs to become a national conservation priority, the members' meeting is where that argument is made — and a body founded in 1909 has the records to say what your area held before. WHAT THE UGANDAN NETWORK ACTUALLY ACHIEVED, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST PRECEDENT IN THIS FILE FOR A SPIRITUAL CLAIM OVER LAND: A LAW RECOGNISING SACRED NATURAL SITES — THE FIRST OF ITS KIND IN UGANDA AND IN AFRICA — WAS SPEARHEADED AT PARLIAMENTARY LEVEL BY A GROUP OF LAWYERS, WHILE A PARTNER ORGANISATION WORKED AT COMMUNITY LEVEL TO PROVIDE GROUND EVIDENCE OF THE SITES, INCLUDING THE DIFFERENT ECOSYSTEMS AND NATURAL ENTITIES INVOLVED AND THE HUMAN CUSTODIANS WHO COULD REPRESENT NATURE IN COURTS OF LAW. Lawyers in parliament and custodians on the ground, at the same time — neither half would have carried it. And the law that resulted lets a named human custodian stand for a place in court, which is the answer to the question of who has standing when the land itself is the injured party. THE METHOD THE CUSTODIANS USED, WHICH ANY COMMUNITY CAN COPY: IN 2017 THEY LAUNCHED ECO-CULTURAL MAPPING PROCESSES LED BY OLDER CUSTODIANS AND CLAN HEADS, DRAWING THREE MAPS — THE ANCESTRAL MAP OF THE PAST, A MAP OF THE CURRENT SHOWING WHAT WAS HAPPENING NOW, AND A MAP OF THEIR DESIRED FUTURE — WHILE THE WOMEN CUSTODIANS OF SEED DIVERSITY DEVELOPED AN ANCESTRAL CALENDAR OF PAST, PRESENT AND FUTURE. Three maps and a calendar, drawn by elders and clan heads rather than by consultants, is the cheapest and most defensible record a community can make of what it has lost and what it wants back. Start with the ancestral map: it is the one nobody else can produce. AND THE LAW HAD TEETH: IT ENABLED CUSTODIANS TO REGULATE ACCESS TO DIFFERENT AREAS — in one case fishing in a named lake, IN ORDER TO RESPECT THE LIFE CYCLE OF THE LAKE AND THE FISH — with the recorded result that when these rules are followed THERE IS ENOUGH FOR EVERYONE WHO DEPENDS ON THE LAKE. ALSO NAMED: UGANDA ENVIRONMENT EDUCATION FOUNDATION, AN INDIGENOUS NGO FOUNDED 1997 BY A GROUP OF PROFESSIONAL ENVIRONMENTALISTS AND REGISTERED BY THE NATIONAL NGO BOARD; CLIMATE ACTION NETWORK UGANDA, REGISTERED WITH THE NGO BOARD AS A NATIONAL NETWORK; and the EAST AFRICAN WILDLIFE SOCIETY, which has an office in KAMPALA and offers INDIVIDUAL MEMBERSHIP PRICED BY COUNTRY. WHO IT SUITS: Ugandan communities with a sacred site, a lake or a customary territory, and anyone wanting a vote inside a conservation body. CAVEATS: MEMBERSHIP AND ADVOCACY ORGANISATIONS, not funders. For 29 years of environmental public interest litigation, Uganda's Greenwatch entry; for registering customary land in the north, LEMU; for the 60+ member consortium, the Uganda Land Alliance entry; for payments to landowners who keep trees, ECOTRUST.

trackers.name: NAPE's Community Green Radio and Sustainability School — a station the listeners' clubs demanded and now broadcast on daily, plus the grassroots women's movement organised through it
trackers.desc: THE RADIO STATION THE LISTENERS DEMANDED: COMMUNITY GREEN RADIO (greenradio.ug) IS ONE OF THE MAJOR PROGRAMMES OF THE NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF PROFESSIONAL ENVIRONMENTALISTS (NAPE, nape.or.ug), AND IS AN OFFSHOOT OF ITS SUSTAINABILITY SCHOOL PROGRAMME, WHICH WORKS ON EMPOWERING COMMUNITIES TO IDENTIFY THEIR RIGHTS AND ENTITLEMENTS AND WORKS TOWARDS ATTAINING AND DEFENDING THEM — aimed at AMPLIFYING THE VOICES OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES IN THE ECO-SENSITIVE BUNYORO AND BUGANDA REGIONS TO EFFECTIVELY PARTICIPATE IN NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT PROCESSES. IT BEGAN THROUGH AFFILIATION WITH A DISTRICT FM COMPANY IN CENTRAL UGANDA — AND THE LISTENERS' CLUB MEMBERS, WHO HAD FOR LONG DEMANDED A FULLY-FLEDGED RADIO SO AS TO HAVE ENOUGH TIME TO ADVOCATE FOR ENVIRONMENTAL CONSERVATION AND HUMAN RIGHTS, GOT ONE: IT NOW BROADCASTS DAILY. A named listeners' club chairperson records what changed: WE ARE HAPPY THAT NOW THE MEMBERS CAN GO ON AIR ANY TIME THEY WISH, NOT LIKE THOSE DAYS WHEN THEY WOULD HAVE TO WAIT FOR TIME BETWEEN 1.00 AND 3.00 PM — and he thanks the organisation FOR ADHERING TO OUR DEMAND. Village listeners' clubs asked their own NGO for a whole radio station instead of a two-hour slot, and got it. Two things to take: a listeners' CLUB is the unit — an organised group with a chairperson, not an audience — and an NGO that changes its programme because members demanded it is one worth joining. Ask what airtime your community can have, and ask who decides. WHAT NAPE USES IT FOR, AND WHAT IT WORKS ON: PROTECTING THE RIGHTS OF COMMUNITIES AFFECTED BY BIG INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT, WITH PRINCIPAL EXAMPLES INCLUDING EXOTIC TREE PLANTATIONS FOR CARBON TRADING AT TWO NAMED SITES IN EASTERN AND WESTERN UGANDA, plus water governance, and an ECOSYSTEMS ALLIANCE PROGRAMME TO EMPOWER COMMUNITIES FOR SUSTAINABLE NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT IN THE ALBERTINE RIFT, IMPLEMENTED BY A CONSORTIUM OF THREE ORGANISATIONS — NAPE, THE UGANDA WILDLIFE SOCIETY AND AN AFRICA INSTITUTE FOR ENERGY GOVERNANCE. Carbon-trading tree plantations named as a threat to community rights, not as a solution. If a carbon forestry scheme is proposed on your land, there is a Ugandan organisation that has documented two of them. THE ORGANISING FORM: WOMEN ORGANISED UNDER NAPE'S GRASSROOTS WOMEN MOVEMENT IN TWO NAMED DISTRICTS APPEARED ON THE RADIO TO DEMAND COLLECTIVE ACTION AGAINST CLIMATE INJUSTICES, FOOD INSECURITY, LAND RIGHTS VIOLATIONS AND MALE DOMINATION IN LEADERSHIP AND DECISION-MAKING POSITIONS — naming LARGE LAND-BASED INVESTMENTS INCLUDING OIL AND GAS AND LARGE-SCALE AGRICULTURE as what is fuelling the violations. The station manager states the radio IS COMMITTED TO AMPLIFYING THE VOICES OF WOMEN AND SUPPORTING THEM IN HOLDING THE LEADERS ACCOUNTABLE. A women's movement with its own airtime holds its own leaders to account in public. That is a governance mechanism, not a communications one. THE FIGURE TO CARRY INTO ANY LAND MEETING: RESEARCH LAUNCHED BY NAPE AND PARTNERS FOUND THAT ABOUT 85% OF WOMEN IN UGANDA DEPEND ON USE OF LAND FOR LIVELIHOOD AND FOOD PRODUCTION FOR THEIR FAMILIES, AND 75% OF WOMEN ARE SMALLHOLDER FARMERS DEPENDENT ON RAIN-FED AGRICULTURE AND CLIMATE-SENSITIVE RESOURCES. Eighty-five per cent. When a project takes land, it takes the livelihood of nearly every woman in the area — that is the sentence to put in the objection, and a Ugandan study supports it. ALSO NAMED: NAPE supports COMMUNITY-LED RESTORATION OF DEGRADED WETLANDS AND PROTECTION OF REMAINING NATURAL FORESTS IN A NAMED VILLAGE AND SUB-COUNTY, and a named woman MP publicly credited it for establishing the community radio. WHO IT SUITS: Ugandan communities in Bunyoro and Buganda, women's groups, and anyone facing carbon forestry or oil infrastructure. CAVEATS: A CAMPAIGNING NGO — pair with counsel for litigation. For the custodians who can represent Nature in court and the three eco-cultural maps, Uganda's NatureUganda entry; for 29 years of environmental public interest litigation, Greenwatch; for registering customary land in the north, LEMU; for payments to landowners who keep trees, ECOTRUST.

trackers.name: Witness Radio — Ugandan lawyers, investigative journalists and social workers in one registered organisation that represents land-grab affected communities and investigates the financiers behind the projects
trackers.desc: LAWYERS, JOURNALISTS AND SOCIAL WORKERS IN ONE ORGANISATION — which is a combination this file has not found anywhere else: WITNESS RADIO ORGANIZATION, STARTED IN 2016, IS A NONPARTISAN AND NOT-FOR-PROFIT REGISTERED NETWORK OF HUMAN RIGHTS INVESTIGATIVE JOURNALISTS, LAWYERS, AND SOCIAL WORKERS, USING LEGAL AID SUPPORT AND MEDIA-LEANING APPROACHES — AND IT PROVIDES LEGAL REPRESENTATION AND SUPPORT TO POOR, VULNERABLE, AND LAND GRAB-AFFECTED COMMUNITIES. A lawyer to file it, a journalist to publish it and a social worker to hold the family together while it runs. Most communities in this file have to assemble those three from three different organisations, and usually cannot. If your case needs all three, this is one door. ITS ORGANISING METHOD IS STATED IN ITS OWN WORDS AND IS THE PART TO COPY: IT MOBILIZES, ORGANIZES, AND EMPOWERS NATIVE COMMUNITIES TO UNDERSTAND LAND LAWS AND TO TAKE A CENTRAL ROLE IN DEFENDING AND PROTECTING THEIR LANDS USING THE SAME LEGAL FRAMEWORK. The community takes the central role and uses the same legal framework as the company. Not a lawyer acting for you — you, taught the law, with a lawyer beside you. Ask any organisation offering help which of those two it is proposing. AND THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST FOR ANYONE FACING A FINANCED PROJECT: IT INVESTIGATES LAND INVESTMENT PROJECTS WITH NEGATIVE IMPACTS ON COMMUNITIES IN UGANDA, ESPECIALLY THOSE FINANCED BY GLOBAL ENTITIES LIKE A DEVELOPMENT BANK AND BY GOVERNMENT FINANCIAL AGENCIES INCLUDING NAMED EUROPEAN DEVELOPMENT FINANCE INSTITUTIONS, THAT ARE FUNDING COMPANIES DISPOSSESSING COMMUNITIES THROUGH VIOLENT AND EXCESSIVE FORCE. It goes after the money, not only the company. A development finance institution has a complaints office, a board and a home parliament — all of which the operator on your land does not. This file has recorded that route working in Mozambique and Chad; here is a Ugandan organisation whose standing programme is finding out who financed the project. Ask it who is behind yours. ITS NAMED CONSTITUENCIES ARE BROADER THAN LAND: CHILDREN, CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, PEOPLE WITH DISABILITIES, RURAL COMMUNITIES, URBAN COMMUNITIES, WOMEN AND GIRLS, AND WORKERS. Urban communities and workers on the same list as indigenous peoples. An eviction in a town and a plantation clearance are the same file to this organisation — useful if your case does not look like a classic rural land grab. WHAT IT CONVENES: IT RUNS A LEGAL AID CLINIC; IT BRINGS LAND-GRAB VICTIM COMMUNITIES TOGETHER WITH COUNTERPARTS TO COMMEMORATE AN INTERNATIONAL DAY OF STRUGGLE AGAINST INDUSTRIAL PLANTATIONS; AND IT CONVENES LAND AND ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS DEFENDERS, CSOs, SCHOLARS AND GOVERNMENT IN KAMPALA TO ASSESS UGANDA'S PERFORMANCE ON THE UN GUIDING PRINCIPLES ON BUSINESS AND HUMAN RIGHTS. Bringing affected communities from different districts into one room is how an isolated village learns it is not the only one. And a meeting that assesses the government's performance against the business and human rights principles, with the government present, is a forum your case can be raised in by name. THE CUSTODIAN ORGANISATIONS IN THE OIL REGION, NAMED: the Bagungu community's work on customary law and sacred sites is carried by ADVOCATES FOR NATURAL RESOURCES AND DEVELOPMENT (ANARDE), THE NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF PROFESSIONAL ENVIRONMENTALISTS (NAPE), AND THE AFRICAN INSTITUTE OF CULTURE AND ECOLOGY (AFRICE) — and a BUGUNGU HERITAGE AND INFORMATION CENTRE has a named founder. Three organisations and a heritage centre behind one community's customary claim. If your case rests on sacred sites, that is the shape of the support you need: a legal body, an environmental body, a culture-and-ecology body, and your own centre holding the record. AND THE FINDING THAT EVERY COMMUNITY EXPECTING COMPENSATION SHOULD READ: IN BULIISA, THE LAND RUSH DESTROYED THE CULTURAL COMMONS AS LANDOWNERS FENCED OFF THEIR PROPERTIES IN ANTICIPATION OF COMPENSATION — AND UNMARKED NATURAL SITES IN THE JUNGLE ARE ESPECIALLY VULNERABLE AMID A CASH BONANZA. The commons died before the project did, because neighbours fenced against each other hoping to be paid. That is the internal damage a compensation process does, and it happens fast. Mark and record your shared sites BEFORE the survey teams arrive — unmarked is unprotected, and once the fencing starts the commons is gone whether or not the project proceeds. A published human rights report on the same area found that HOUSEHOLDS AFFECTED BY LAND ACQUISITIONS ARE WORSE OFF THAN THEY HAD BEEN, WITH THE PROCESS MARRED BY DELAYS, POOR COMMUNICATION, AND INADEQUATE COMPENSATION. WHO IT SUITS: Ugandan communities facing plantations, oil infrastructure or urban eviction, and anyone needing to know who financed a project. CAVEATS: A CAMPAIGNING LEGAL AID ORGANISATION operating in a contested space. For 29 years of environmental public interest litigation, Uganda's Greenwatch entry; for a state one-stop legal aid service with a toll-free line, Justice Centres Uganda; for the custodians who can represent Nature in court, the NatureUganda entry; for a radio station the listeners' clubs demanded, NAPE's Community Green Radio; for registering customary land in the north, LEMU.

trackers.name: The Karamoja cluster youth declaration — 150+ young pastoralists from five countries demanding a cross-border movement protocol — and RECONCILE, the regional institute that writes technical support into a land commission and two parliamentary groups
trackers.desc: A HUNDRED AND FIFTY YOUNG HERDERS WROTE THEIR OWN DECLARATION — placement note first: THE GATHERING AND THE CLUSTER SPAN FIVE COUNTRIES, FILED UNDER UGANDA BECAUSE THE DECLARATION WAS ADOPTED IN THE UGANDAN PART OF THE CLUSTER AND A NAMED UGANDAN YOUTH ENVIRONMENT ORGANISATION CO-HOSTED IT. MORE THAN 150 YOUNG PASTORALISTS FROM UGANDA, KENYA, TANZANIA, ETHIOPIA AND SOUTH SUDAN ADOPTED A NAMED DECLARATION, ADVOCATING FOR THE FULL IMPLEMENTATION OF A REGIONAL TRANSHUMANCE PROTOCOL — A REGIONAL FRAMEWORK ENSURING THE FREE AND ORDERLY MOVEMENT OF PASTORALISTS ACROSS BORDERS. A named declaration adopted by young herders themselves, demanding a protocol that already exists be implemented. That is the strongest form an ask can take: not create a new right, enforce the one your governments already signed. Ask the coalitions below for the declaration text and the protocol by name — a herder crossing a border with a copy of both is in a different position from one with neither. THE CLUSTER IT COVERS: A 150,000 SQUARE KILOMETRE SEMI-ARID REGION SPANNING ETHIOPIA, KENYA, SOUTH SUDAN AND UGANDA, WHERE CROSS-BORDER AGREEMENTS ARE CRUCIAL FOR SUSTAINING THE LIVELIHOODS OF PASTORALIST AND AGRO-PASTORALIST COMMUNITIES. THE SPECIFIC ASK, FROM A NAMED WOMEN'S COUNCIL REPRESENTATIVE: THE PROTECTION OF COMMUNAL LAND TENURE AND STRONGER SAFEGUARDS AGAINST LAND GRABBING, UNSUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE, INDUSTRIAL PLANTATIONS, AND MINING IN RANGELANDS. Four named threats to rangeland, in order. Industrial plantations and mining are the ones rangeland communities are least prepared for, because grazing land is routinely classed as empty and available. THE METHOD OF THE GATHERING, WHICH IS CHEAP AND COPYABLE: FIELD VISITS TO KRAALS, COMMUNAL GRAZING AREAS AND RANGELAND RESTORATION SITES ALLOWED PARTICIPANTS TO OBSERVE TRADITIONAL LIVESTOCK MANAGEMENT AND COMMUNITY-LED INNOVATIONS FIRSTHAND — FOSTERING INTERGENERATIONAL DIALOGUE, CONNECTING THE WISDOM OF ELDERS WITH THE CREATIVITY OF YOUNG PASTORALISTS. Take people to the kraal rather than to a hotel conference room. Field visits between communities are the format this file has recorded working from Madagascar to Mumbai — people believe what they have walked over. THE REGIONAL INSTITUTE BEHIND MUCH OF IT: ESTABLISHED IN 1999 AND REGISTERED IN KENYA AS A REGIONAL NGO IN MAY 2001, IT IMPLEMENTS PROGRAMMES IN KENYA, UGANDA, TANZANIA, RWANDA AND BURUNDI — AND IS BASED IN A NAMED PROVINCIAL TOWN RATHER THAN THE CAPITAL, WHICH IT STATES GIVES IT ACCESS TO THE RURAL LIVELIHOODS IN LINE WITH ITS MANDATE. An organisation that says its provincial base is an advantage over the ones in the capital. Where an organisation sits changes who can walk into it — a herder can reach a town office in a day and a Nairobi office almost never. WHAT IT DOES: POLICY AND LEGAL RESEARCH ON ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURAL RESOURCE GOVERNANCE; PUBLIC INTEREST ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION; AND ADVOCACY FOR POLICIES, LAWS AND PRACTICES THAT EMPOWER RESOURCE-DEPENDENT COMMUNITIES TO INFLUENCE THE POLICY PROCESSES AND INSTITUTIONS THAT BEAR ON THEIR ACCESS, USE, OWNERSHIP AND MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES — FOCUSING ON BUILDING THE CAPACITY OF CITIZENS AND COMMUNITY GROUPS ON POLICY PROCESSES, ADVOCACY, AND COLLABORATIVE NATURAL RESOURCE GOVERNANCE. AND THE SEATS IT HOLDS, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH APPROACHING: IT PROVIDES TECHNICAL SUPPORT TO A NATIONAL LAND COMMISSION IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND PRODUCTION OF GUIDELINES ON COUNTY SPATIAL PLANNING, AND FACILITATES THE INPUT OF A PASTORAL PARLIAMENTARY GROUP AND A COAST PARLIAMENTARY GROUP IN THE FINALIZATION OF A COMMUNITY LAND BILL — AND CO-ORGANISED A COUNTRY'S FIRST RANGELANDS CONGRESS. COUNTY SPATIAL PLANNING guidelines decide what your county's land is zoned for, and a PASTORAL PARLIAMENTARY GROUP is a bloc of MPs who already represent herders. Both are reachable through one organisation. If a bill affecting communal land is before your parliament, ask which parliamentary group covers your constituency — they exist more often than communities assume. AND THE LOBBYING COALITION IN EUROPE: AN INFORMAL ADVOCACY GROUP OF EUROPEAN ORGANISATIONS PARTNERING WITH PASTORALIST ORGANISATIONS IN EASTERN AFRICA, WHOSE MEMBERS COMBINE FORCES TO LOBBY THEIR NATIONAL GOVERNMENTS AND EUROPEAN AND EASTERN AFRICAN BODIES TO EXPLICITLY RECOGNISE AND SUPPORT PASTORALISM AND PASTORALISTS IN THE DRYLANDS — MANAGED BY AN ELECTED EUROPEAN FOCAL POINT AND AN EASTERN AFRICAN FOCAL POINT, WITH A CORE GROUP INCLUDING NAMED PARTNERS IN UGANDA, ETHIOPIA AND THE SOMALI REGION, A NAMED CONTACT PERSON AND A BRUSSELS STREET ADDRESS. European organisations lobbying their own governments on behalf of East African herders, with an African focal point holding half the leadership. If a European aid programme or import rule is harming your rangeland, that coalition is the channel to the capital that decides it — and there is a named person and address to write to. IT ALSO NOTES THAT A SOLIDARITY ALLIANCE ISSUES A NEWSLETTER PROVIDING UPDATES ON WHAT IS HAPPENING TO COMMUNITIES IN TWO NAMED AREAS. WHO IT SUITS: pastoralist communities and youth groups in the Karamoja cluster and across East Africa, and anyone facing plantation or mining pressure on rangeland. CAVEATS: COALITIONS AND RESEARCH INSTITUTES — they lobby and advise rather than litigate or buy land. For communities registering their commons in northern Uganda, the LEMU entry; for Tanzania's 53-organisation pastoralist coalition with its Arusha address, PINGO's Forum; for the continental indigenous network, South Africa's IPACC entry.

trackers.name: Southern Africa Litigation Centre (SALC)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional litigation centre supporting and co-counselling cases across Angola, Botswana, DR Congo, Eswatini, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe. Its socio-economic rights work challenges large-scale agricultural and extractive land use that dispossesses customary landholders without adequate consent, consultation or compensation, and covers mining, pollution and climate justice — live matters include a Zambian community's pollution claim against copper processors and San and Bayei claims to ancestral land in Botswana. WHO IT SUITS: in-country lawyers and community organisations who need a partner with regional capacity and resources; SALC generally works through local counsel and partners rather than taking clients directly. SALC RESOURCES A LAWYER — IT DOES NOT REPLACE ONE.
