trackers.name: Cedar forest reserve run by a committee of municipalities and ministries — chaired by the local mayor, across four villages
trackers.desc: THIS PAYLOAD KEEPS ASKING WHO ACTUALLY GOVERNS A PROTECTED AREA. HERE THE ANSWER IS A COMMITTEE THAT INCLUDES THE MUNICIPALITIES THEMSELVES: UNDER AN ENVIRONMENT MINISTER'S DECISION OF OCTOBER 2025 APPOINTING THE RESERVE'S ADMINISTRATIVE BODY, THE NAMES OF THE REPRESENTATIVES OF THE MINISTRIES, THE MUNICIPALITIES AND THE BODIES CONCERNED WITH MANAGING THIS NATIONAL NATURAL RESOURCE WERE FIXED. THE APPOINTED MEMBERS THEN MET, QUORUM WAS CONFIRMED, AND A BALLOT WAS HELD TO ELECT THE EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE - WITH A LAWYER ELECTED AS CHAIRMAN WHO IS ALSO THE HEAD OF THE LOCAL MUNICIPALITY. A RESERVE COMMITTEE CHAIRED BY THE MAYOR OF THE VILLAGE IT SITS IN IS THE ARRANGEMENT THIS FILE HAS BEEN LOOKING FOR ACROSS TWENTY-THREE COUNTRIES: THE PROTECTION AND THE LOCAL AUTHORITY IN THE SAME HANDS, WITH MINISTRY REPRESENTATIVES AT THE TABLE RATHER THAN ABOVE IT. THE GROUND IT COVERS IS SUBSTANTIAL AND SHARED: ABOUT SIX SQUARE KILOMETRES ESTABLISHED BY A LAW OF FEBRUARY 1999, LYING ACROSS SEVERAL HILLS WITHIN FOUR VILLAGES, WITH CEDAR MAKING UP ABOUT EIGHTY PER CENT OF THE AREA AND ONE ACCOUNT PUTTING THE NUMBER OF TREES AT ABOUT A MILLION AND A HALF. FOUR VILLAGES SHARING ONE RESERVE IS ALSO FOUR MUNICIPALITIES WITH A REASON TO COOPERATE - AND THIS PAYLOAD RECORDS SEPARATELY THAT MUNICIPALITIES IN THIS COUNTRY MAY FORM UNIONS AND ESTABLISH JOINT SERVICES BETWEEN THEM. WHAT IS INSIDE IT IS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ARGUING FOR ANY FOREST: MORE THAN FIVE HUNDRED SPECIES OF WILD PLANT, THOUSANDS OF INSECTS AND MORE THAN A HUNDRED SPECIES OF BUTTERFLY; MORE THAN TWENTY TREE SPECIES INCLUDING JUNIPER, WILD PLUM, WILD APPLE, PEAR, HAWTHORN AND OAK; ABOUT EIGHTY-SEVEN FUNGI, SOME EDIBLE AND SOME POISONOUS; TWENTY-SIX MAMMALS; AND EIGHTY MIGRATORY AND RESIDENT BIRDS. A CEDAR FOREST DESCRIBED SPECIES BY SPECIES IS AN INVENTORY, AND AN INVENTORY IS WHAT TURNS A BELOVED PLACE INTO A DEFENSIBLE ONE. THE WILD FRUIT TREES AND THE FUNGI MATTER PARTICULARLY: THEY ARE WHAT LOCAL PEOPLE USE, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT THAT REACHES BEYOND CONSERVATION. IT IS ALSO BUILT FOR VISITORS IN A WAY THAT SPREADS THE BENEFIT: A TRAIL NETWORK OF ABOUT FORTY-EIGHT KILOMETRES, PART SET ASIDE FOR WALKING ALL YEAR AND PART FOR WALKING ON SNOW IN WINTER. IN JUNE 2026 THE COMMITTEE OPENED A TRAIL DESIGNED FOR PEOPLE WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENTS, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH A MOUNTAIN TRAIL ASSOCIATION, A COMPANY AND THE MUNICIPALITY - WITH A PROVINCIAL GOVERNOR, A BISHOP, SEVERAL MUNICIPAL HEADS AND VILLAGE MUKHTARS ATTENDING. AN ACCESSIBLE TRAIL OPENED WITH THE GOVERNOR AND THE NEIGHBOURING MAYORS PRESENT IS A CHEAP AND DURABLE WAY TO PUT A PROTECTED AREA UNDER THE PROTECTION OF EVERYONE WHO MATTERS LOCALLY. THE THREATS IT HAS SURVIVED ARE INSTRUCTIVE TOO: THE FOREST HAD BEEN THREATENED BY AN INSECT THAT KILLED ITS TREES AND WAS RID OF THE PEST, AND A NATIONAL CAMPAIGN FOR THE PREVENTION OF FIRES WAS LAUNCHED FROM THE RESERVE, WITH THE FIRES THAT HAD BROKEN OUT AROUND IT REVIEWED AND MEASURES CALLED FOR TO PREVENT THEIR REPETITION. AND WHAT THE COMMITTEE ASKS FOR IS THE MODEL SENTENCE FOR ANY COMMUNITY TALKING TO DONORS: ITS PRIORITY IS A SCIENTIFIC AND REALISTIC PLAN OBSERVING ENVIRONMENTAL, TOURISM AND NATURAL PRINCIPLES, AND ITS CHAIRMAN SAID THAT THE PEOPLE OF THE TOWN AND THE RESERVE COMMITTEE ARE READY, AND WHAT THEY WANT FROM THE STATE AND FROM FRIENDLY FOREIGN AND LOCAL DONORS IS TO PUT THAT PLAN INTO EFFECT. WE HAVE THE PLAN AND THE PEOPLE, WE NEED THE MONEY TO EXECUTE IT IS A STRONGER POSITION THAN ASKING FOR HELP - AND IT IS AVAILABLE TO ANY COMMUNITY WILLING TO DO THE PLANNING FIRST. THE LIMITS: THIS IS ONE RESERVE'S GOVERNING COMMITTEE, NOT A SERVICE OTHER COMMUNITIES CAN CALL ON - IT MANAGES ITS OWN FOREST, AND NOTHING RECORDED HERE SHOWS IT ADVISING ELSEWHERE OR OPPOSING A DEVELOPMENT OUTSIDE ITS BOUNDARY. ITS MEMBERS ARE APPOINTED BY MINISTERIAL DECISION, SO THE LOCAL MAJORITY DEPENDS ON WHO A MINISTER NAMES, AND THE COMMITTEE HAS BEEN RECONSTITUTED MORE THAN ONCE WITH DIFFERENT PEOPLE NAMED AS CHAIRMAN IN REPORTS OF DIFFERENT YEARS. WHETHER RESIDENTS OF THE FOUR VILLAGES ELECT ANY OF ITS MEMBERS, HOW ITS BUDGET IS RAISED AND WHETHER ITS MEETINGS ARE OPEN WERE ALL NOT ESTABLISHED. THE TREE COUNT DIFFERS BETWEEN SOURCES - ONE SAYS ABOUT A MILLION AND A HALF, ANOTHER MORE THAN FOUR MILLION - AND THE ACCOUNT COMES FROM LEBANESE NEWS SITES, AN ARMY INFORMATION PAGE AND AN ENCYCLOPAEDIA ENTRY DATED BETWEEN 2014 AND JUNE 2026. trackers.name: RTI Portal (India)
trackers.desc: You CAN get: any record, file noting, order, inspection report or status report held by a public authority, under the Right to Information Act 2005, on payment of a ₹10 fee — waived for BPL applicants. Any Indian citizen may ask; you do not have to say why. The Public Information Officer must ordinarily answer within 30 days. Know which site does what: rti.gov.in is the GATEWAY — use it to identify the right PIO and First Appellate Authority and to read proactive disclosures. Filing happens at rtionline.gov.in. You CAN'T get: state records through that filing portal. It covers CENTRAL ministries, departments and public authorities only, and an application wrongly filed there against a state body — including the Government of NCT of Delhi, which runs its own portal — is returned WITHOUT REFUND. State authorities need the relevant state portal or a postal application. An online first appeal can only follow an online application. For activists: this is how you get an environmental clearance file, a public-hearing record or project correspondence from MoEFCC or a central regulator — but a State Pollution Control Board is a state body, so check the tier before paying. If the PIO misses the 30 days or answers badly, appeal to the First Appellate Authority within 30 days, then to the Central Information Commission within 90; the Commission can order disclosure and fine the officer.

trackers.name: NALSA (Legal Services Authority)
trackers.desc: Constitutional body providing free legal aid to weaker sections, cascading to State and District Legal Services Authorities. · Find here: India's National Legal Services Authority — free legal aid and Lok Adalats. INDIA GATES ON THE PERSON, NOT THE CASE — which is the opposite of England and Wales, recorded separately in this map. NALSA states it in terms: ‘there is hence NO BAR AS TO WHICH KIND OF CASES one can apply and not apply for. All kinds of cases are included as long as the individual satisfies the eligibility under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.’ So the question is never whether an environmental case is covered — it is whether the person qualifies. AND TWO SECTION 12 CATEGORIES REACH ENVIRONMENTAL HARM DIRECTLY: eligibility is not based on income alone and includes members of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe and victims of a mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster. Flood, drought and industrial disaster are named eligibility grounds — a community harmed by an industrial release or displaced by flooding qualifies on that basis irrespective of income. Income thresholds otherwise vary by state (for example ₹3 lakhs per annum in Delhi for civil cases in the High Court). THE MERITS FILTER IS LIGHT: under section 13(1) you are entitled provided the institution is satisfied you have ‘a genuine case to prosecute or defend’ — far below a prospects-of-success test. APPLY AT DISTRICT OR TALUKA LEVEL, NOT TO NALSA: District Legal Services Authorities and Taluka Legal Services Committees handle applications; NALSA sets policy. WHAT IS PAID FOR IS BROADER THAN A LAWYER: section 2(c) covers proceedings before any court OR OTHER AUTHORITY OR TRIBUNAL, and inclusions cover process fees, witness expenses, and preparation of pleadings and paper books including document translation and printing — often decisive in a technical environmental case, where expert and document costs defeat claimants more than fees do. Aid runs from the lowest court to the Supreme Court, and you may apply at any stage. ON CHOOSING YOUR LAWYER, READ TWO RULES TOGETHER: regulation 7(6) of the 2010 Regulations lets the Member-Secretary consider a named preference from the panel — but aid can be withdrawn where the person engages a legal practitioner other than the one assigned. Express a preference among panel lawyers; bringing in an outside practitioner ends the aid.

trackers.name: National Green Tribunal — file an application
trackers.desc: THE FORUM TO FILE IN: established under the NGT Act 2010 and functioning since 4 July 2011. STANDING IS OPEN — you do not need to be directly affected; anyone with an interest in protecting the environment may bring a case, which removes the barrier that stops most communities elsewhere. It is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure 1908 and is guided by principles of natural justice, so a case is less likely to die on pleading technicalities, and it is mandated to dispose of applications within 6 months of filing. Applications may be filed online after registering, or offline. It can review violations and also orders or decisions of Government under the Schedule I laws. THE JURISDICTIONAL HOLE, CHECK IT BEFORE YOU FILE: the NGT has no jurisdiction over the Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972, the Indian Forest Act 1927, or state forest and tree-preservation laws — a tree-felling or forest matter under those Acts must instead go as a Writ Petition by Public Interest Litigation to the State High Court or Supreme Court, or as an original suit before the civil judge in the taluk where the project lies. PRECEDENT WORTH CITING: the NGT has held that an entire dam proposal must be placed before the village council for approval under the Forest Rights Act — consent over the whole project, not a fragment of it.

trackers.name: CSR funding and the CSR-1 gate
trackers.desc: INDIA'S BIGGEST REALISTIC FUNDING CHANNEL IS CORPORATE, AND IT IS STATUTORY. Under Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013, companies above a threshold (net worth ₹500 crore, turnover ₹1,000 crore, or net profit ₹5 crore) must spend at least 2 percent of average net profit on CSR, and Schedule VII lists environmental sustainability and conservation among its 14 permitted categories. Roughly ₹25,000–30,000 crore is spent yearly across more than 18,000 companies. THE GATE IS ABSOLUTE: no NGO can legally receive CSR money from any company without CSR-1 registration with the Registrar of Companies on the MCA portal, mandatory since 1 April 2021. AND THE 2025 CHANGE MATTERS MOST TO NEW GROUPS: from 14 July 2025, only NGOs with valid 12A registration and a 3-year track record can register on CSR-1 — a group formed to fight a specific development cannot register and must work through an already-eligible implementing partner. WHAT CSR-1 NEEDS: Trust, Society or Section 8 form; trust deed or incorporation certificate, 12A, 80G if held, PAN; a Class 3 DSC belonging to someone formally authorised in the trust deed or board resolution (old DSCs of former trustees cause rejections); and certification by a practising CA, CS or CMA. Your last 3 years of activities must be mapped specifically to Schedule VII categories — ‘activities not clearly mapped to Schedule VII’ is a stated rejection reason. PRACTICALITIES: the money must be spent within India, a foreign NGO needs a registered Indian partner, administrative costs are capped by agreement at roughly 5–10 percent, and expect 3–6 months from first approach to first disbursement.

trackers.name: Right of Passage — four models for securing a corridor
trackers.desc: FOUR WAYS LAND GETS SECURED IN INDIA, from the organisation that has done most of it. Private purchase: buy the land with partners, rehabilitate affected people, then transfer it to the state forest department for legal protection — note the endpoint, the NGO does not keep it, and legal protection comes from the state. Community securement: community-owned land set aside through easements or bilateral benefit-sharing, with no transfer of ownership. Government acquisition: policy advocacy and support to the state. Plus a network of Green Corridor Champions institutionalising community organisations in corridor protection. THE STRUCTURAL POINT, TRANSFERABLE ANYWHERE: Elephant Reserves include areas of human use and, unless they fall inside Reserve Forests or the Protected Area network, are not legally protected habitats — designation on a map is not protection. The project mapped 88 corridors from 2005 and now lists 101. Funders record that purchasing even a small land parcel can be highly effective when done meticulously by a body that works well with local communities. NOW THE OTHER HALF, AND READ IT BEFORE COPYING THE MODEL: peer-reviewed research in Environmental Management describes a conservation-agrarian squeeze in South India — farmers whose land was identified for acquisition were already facing state neglect of agriculture, rising debt and unstable weather; the concept note proposed acquisition or a land-for-land deal, but farmers said only monetary compensation was provided; and the plan opened with ‘entry point activities’ such as a health camp. If you secure land this way, land-for-land must be delivered and not merely offered.

trackers.name: District Legal Services Authority — free lawyer in every district
trackers.desc: A FREE LAWYER, IN EVERY DISTRICT, BY STATUTE. Under the Legal Services Authorities Act 1987 — given force by Article 39A of the Constitution — legal services institutions run from national down to taluka level, and the District Legal Services Authority exists in every district. ELIGIBILITY IS BY WHO YOU ARE, NOT WHAT THE CASE IS. Under Section 12 the entitled include: a member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe; a woman — irrespective of income or financial status; a child under 18; a mentally ill or disabled person; a person in custody; a victim of trafficking; and anyone affected by a mass disaster, ethnic or caste violence, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster. Otherwise, anyone below the income ceiling set by their State Government (below Rs 5 lakh for a Supreme Court case) — and under Section 13(2) an affidavit of income is generally enough proof. THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR A LAND FIGHT: Section 13(1) means there is no bar on the type of case — all kinds are included so long as the person qualifies and the institution is satisfied there is a genuine case to prosecute or defend. An environmental or land matter is not excluded; only the applicant's status is tested. WHAT YOU GET: representation by an advocate; process fees and witness expenses paid; pleadings and memos of appeal prepared, including printing and translation of documents; drafting of legal documents and special leave petitions; certified copies of judgments and evidence. Available at any stage and from the lowest court to the Supreme Court — and you can seek a second opinion from panel lawyers even while using a private lawyer.

trackers.name: Community Forest Resource rights — Form C and two pieces of evidence
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE THAT SHIFTS GOVERNANCE, NOT JUST TENURE. Section 3(1)(i) of the Forest Rights Act 2006 vests in a community the right to protect, regenerate, conserve or manage any community forest resource it has traditionally protected — defined in section 2(a) as customary common forest land within the village's traditional boundaries, including reserved and protected forests, accessed before 13 December 2005. Recognition moves forest management from the Forest Department to the Gram Sabha. THE PROCEDURE: the Gram Sabha resolves to initiate and elects a Forest Rights Committee of 10 to 15 members; the FRC demarcates the customary boundary and prepares maps, which may include reserved forest, protected forest, national park or sanctuary; the claim goes on Form C. EVIDENCE — AT LEAST 2 FORMS ARE REQUIRED UNDER RULE 13: gazetteers, revenue and forest records, elders' statements, traditional structures, and physical features such as sacred groves or burial grounds. Forest and Revenue officials shall be present at site verification and shall sign the proceedings with their designation — get those signatures. Then Gram Sabha resolution → SDLC → DLC under the District Collector, which is the final authority. WHO MAY CLAIM: Scheduled Tribes depending on the forest, and others resident for 3 generations (75 years) before the cut-off.

trackers.name: FRA in practice — rejection rates, and check who is on your FRC
trackers.desc: KNOW THE FAILURE MODES BEFORE YOU FILE. Only Forest Rights Committees and the Gram Sabha may receive, reject or modify a claim at block, panchayat, forest or range level — and in Chhattisgarh, patwaris and forest guards were illegally included in FRCs to manipulate decisions at Gram Sabha level. Check your FRC's composition against the Rules. REJECTION IS THE NORM, NOT THE EXCEPTION: in Karnataka in 2021, of 2.81 lakh applications about 1.8 lakh were rejected; in Shivamogga district 44,016 of 97,074. Recurring causes: rejection of OTFD claims for failing to produce written 75-year evidence, rejection without reasons or a hearing, weak revenue surveys blocking demarcation, and forest department resistance to handing over CFR governance. WHERE IT HAS WORKED: in Vidarbha, Maharashtra, much of the region's potential CFR was recognised in the name of Gram Sabhas — attributed to Gram Sabhas acting collectively together with NGOs, grassroots organisations and state implementing agencies. AND A STRUCTURAL UPGRADE TO PUSH FOR: Maharashtra, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh have recognised Gram Sabhas as body corporates under PESA 1996, giving them legal personality as self-governing institutions.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: National Green Tribunal — its own FAQ says you do not need an advocate
trackers.desc: The Tribunal states that engaging an advocate is not necessary and that an aggrieved party may approach it in person by submitting an application in the required format — which makes this the cheapest serious forum for stopping a project anywhere in South Asia. Orders bind, and are enforceable with the powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure 1908. The gap that ends cases at the door: Schedule I lists only seven statutes — Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) 1974, the Water Cess Act 1977, Forest (Conservation) 1980, Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) 1981, Environment (Protection) 1986, Public Liability Insurance 1991 and Biological Diversity 2002. The Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 and the Indian Forest Act 1927 are not on it, so a felling or wildlife-specific grievance has to be taken to a High Court by writ instead. Appeals against orders of the appellate authorities under those seven Acts do belong here. Capacity is stated by the Tribunal itself: where the Chennai, Pune, Bhopal and Kolkata benches lack full judicial and expert strength, the Principal Bench in New Delhi hears their applications remotely by video conference. From inception to 30 June 2026 it recorded 55,619 matters instituted, 49,740 disposed and 5,879 pending. It is an open court and hearings can be attended in person. e-filing runs through ngtonline.nic.in; a letter petition may also be sent, and the Tribunal publishes the status of letter petitions. Review lies to the Tribunal, then to the Supreme Court within ninety days. Registry: Faridkot House, Copernicus Marg, New Delhi 110001, 011-23043528.

trackers.name: AERF — pays private forest owners to keep the trees standing, because buying land in India is hard
trackers.desc: What it offers a landowner is income from standing forest instead of income from felling it. AERF signs conservation agreements with private forest owners and communities in the northern Western Ghats — open-access forest outside the protected area system, with no legal protection available — and pays incentives against an undertaking not to cut. Its MyForest programme, begun in 2008 on a Rufford small grant, is described by the International Land Conservation Network as India's first and only initiative of its kind; the pilot aimed at about 40 hectares, and the first two community agreements in 2008 and 2009 covered roughly ten. World Land Trust, which funds some of the agreements, records a ten-year agreement signed in 2018 over 17.5 hectares in the Kuyle–Phansavale corridor. The reason the model is an agreement rather than a purchase is legal. Indian land ceiling rules cap how much land a person may hold and restrict what may be done with forest and agricultural land, which is why conservation here is built on payments and undertakings rather than on a trust taking title — worth knowing before spending months raising a purchase price that could not lawfully be spent. The second route is the supply chain. AERF uses FairWild certification for species harvested from sacred groves, among them Terminalia bellirica, which raised the price paid to villages for the fruit and drew overseas herb buyers into forest conservation — so a grove with a marketable non-timber product has an option a bare woodlot does not, and the first question to ask is what grows on your land that somebody certified already buys. Ask for current coverage rather than trusting a published figure. Totals from AERF's own partners disagree sharply — one gives over 300 agreements across 50 villages and 10,000 acres, another 15,000 acres across 150 villages in three districts — and AERF's own site gives no total at all. Founded 1995 and based in Pune; the work has extended to mangrove conservation on the Maharashtra coast and, since 2019, to value-chain projects in Chhattisgarh.

trackers.name: CPCB directory of State Pollution Control Boards — find the body that must consent before construction
trackers.desc: One official directory routes you to the state board that has to consent before anything is built, instead of hunting thirty-five separate sites — the Central Pollution Control Board publishes a dated directory of every State Pollution Control Board and every Union Territory Pollution Control Committee, the current version being as on 1 April 2026. The consent is the chokepoint, and it falls before the ground is broken. Under section 25 of the Water Act 1974 nobody may, without the previous consent of the State Board, establish or take any steps to establish any industry, operation, process or treatment and disposal system likely to discharge sewage or trade effluent into a stream, well, sewer or onto land, bring a new or altered discharge outlet into use, or begin a new discharge; under section 21 of the Air Act 1981 nobody may establish or operate an industrial plant in an air pollution control area without the Board's previous consent. In practice that is two permissions: Consent to Establish before construction, and Consent to Operate before commercial running, renewed periodically. Finding out whether a Consent to Establish has been applied for or granted is the earliest useful thing a community can do. This joins straight to the tribunal entry. The Water Act 1974 and the Air Act 1981 are both in Schedule I of the National Green Tribunal Act, so a state board's consent order is an appealable decision and the Tribunal is the appellate forum — which is why identifying the right board matters even where you expect to end up in Delhi. Standards run one way only: a state board may not set limits more lenient than the Central Board's, and the Central Board does not itself issue consents to individual industries except in Union Territories that have no board of their own. Two honest limits. Counts differ between sources — 28 state boards and either seven or eight Union Territory committees, depending who is counting — so take the current list from the directory rather than from any summary. And the boards have long been criticised over vacant scientific posts, laboratory backlogs and slow consent processing, in Comptroller and Auditor General reports and in Tribunal orders; the shift towards self-certification for low-polluting White-category units moves part of the scrutiny onto the operator, which is worth knowing before assuming there is a file to inspect.

trackers.name: People's Science Institute — the Environmental Quality Monitoring Group takes the samples
trackers.desc: India's answer to the measurement problem: an independent institute with its own Environmental Quality Monitoring Group, which samples and reports rather than campaigning. The model to study is its Ganga work at Haridwar, reported in the Indian press: its scientists took samples from ten drains discharging into the river at the start of the Maha Kumbh, plus river water at three locations, and found faecal coliform in the drain discharges ranging from 2.35 million to 40.6 million per 100 millilitres, with the Jagjeetpur sewage treatment plant outfall releasing around 129 million litres a day at about 34 million per 100 millilitres. The conclusion drawn was that the river did not meet the Central Pollution Control Board's standards for outdoor bathing. That last sentence is the whole point of independent sampling. A number is only useful against a standard, and the standard is set nationally — so read this alongside the Central Board's directory, because the Board sets the limits a state board must enforce and may not relax, and alongside the tribunal entry, because the Water Act 1974 sits in Schedule I and a consent order made against those limits is appealable. Measurement, standard and forum are three separate things and a community needs all three. It trains people rather than only serving them. The monitoring group has run workshops for voluntary groups on taking over and monitoring drinking water schemes, on the reasoning that where the state has not secured safe water the community can monitor it — the same reproducible logic as Thailand's bucket brigade, arrived at independently. Know its shape before writing. Established in 1988 and based in Dehradun, its work spans participatory groundwater and springshed management, fluorosis mitigation and agro-ecology as well as environmental quality monitoring, across villages in several states. It is a research and field institute rather than a litigator, so pair it with counsel. ITBP Road, P.O. Kanwali, Dehradun 248001, Uttarakhand.

trackers.name: Goa Foundation — the citizens' body that stopped a state's mining industry in the Supreme Court
trackers.desc: One writ petition by a citizens' foundation stopped mining across an entire Indian state. Its petition, WP(C) 435 of 2012, built on a commission of inquiry's findings and asked the Supreme Court to direct termination of mining leases where mining had been carried out in breach of the Forest (Conservation) Act 1980, the Mines and Minerals Act 1957 and its concession rules, the Environment (Protection) Act 1986, the Water Act 1974, the Air Act 1981 and the Wild Life (Protection) Act 1972 — and to appoint an independent authority with full powers to control, supervise and regulate mining in the state. On 5 October 2012 the Court disallowed any restart of mining in Goa and restrained anyone in the state from trading or transporting mineral ore. The pleading is the lesson. It did not run on a single statute; it listed seven, and it asked for an institutional remedy rather than only an injunction. Where a project or an industry is in breach of several regimes at once, pleading them together is what makes the scale of the failure legible to a court, and asking for a supervising authority is what survives after the order. The remedy went further than stopping the harm. The case produced the first judicially instigated Permanent Fund for Goa, taking money from every sale invoice for minerals and sequestering it for future generations — a remedy addressed to what the resource is worth rather than to what the damage costs. Anyone facing extraction rather than construction should read how that was argued. It publishes the record, which is rare and useful. A day-by-day account of the proceedings, the arguments made on both sides and the full text of the judgment that declared five years of mining illegal is available in book form, so the file is reconstructable by anyone preparing something similar. Founded in Goa in 1986; its site carries the mining record alongside its other work.

trackers.name: District Mineral Foundation — money already collected for mining-affected people, and the gram sabha approval that governs it
trackers.desc: This is not money to be raised; it has already been collected, and much of it is unspent. Every mining lease holder pays into the district foundation on top of royalty — 30 per cent of the royalty amount for leases granted before the 2015 amendment and 10 per cent for leases auctioned after it. By November 2024 the foundations held cumulative collections of about 1.02 lakh crore rupees nationally, of which about 87,357 crore had been sanctioned across 3.6 lakh projects and about 54,892 crore actually spent. A district with mining near you almost certainly has a fund, and a balance. The gram sabha lever is the one to know. Decisions, including the identification of beneficiaries, are to be taken in consultation with the gram sabhas of the villages concerned — and in Fifth and Sixth Schedule areas, gram sabha approval is mandatory for all plans, programmes and projects under the national scheme and for the identification of beneficiaries. Where a village sits in a Scheduled Area the fund cannot lawfully spend on it without that approval, which makes the gram sabha resolution the instrument rather than the petition. Environment is a named priority sector, not an afterthought. Revised guidelines issued in January 2024 require at least 70 per cent of funds to go to directly affected areas and high priority sectors, which include environment preservation and pollution control measures alongside drinking water, health care, education, sanitation, skill development and livelihood generation. Restoration work, monitoring equipment, and water supply where a mine has taken the water all sit inside that mandate. Ask for four things in writing. The composition of the foundation, the funds collected, the list of areas classified as directly affected, and the list of beneficiaries. A parliamentary committee has recommended that exactly these be made public, national and district portals have been developed, and the accounts are subject to audit — so the request is for documents that are supposed to exist. Whether your village is on the directly-affected list is the single fact that determines your share.

trackers.name: Forest Rights Act claims — the gram sabha is the authority, and rejected claims can be revisited
trackers.desc: Only the forest rights committee and the gram sabha may receive, reject or modify a claim. The ministry's own answers state that a committee including persons who are not members of the gram sabha cannot assist it in discharging its functions on recognition and vesting of forest rights, and that any decision or action by such a committee would be void and have no legal basis. Where a forest guard, a range office or an ad hoc committee has turned a claim away, that is not a rejection in law, and saying so is the first move rather than the last. The route and the clock are fixed. The gram sabha constitutes a forest rights committee, verifies claims, prepares maps delineating each claim, passes a resolution and forwards its recommendation to the sub-divisional level committee, which examines and consolidates and sends it to the district level committee, whose decision the Act makes final and binding. Appeals run both ways and must be filed within sixty days of the decision challenged, and no appeal may be disposed of against an aggrieved person without giving them a hearing. A rejection for weak evidence is not the end, and there is a circular saying so. The ministry, relying on the rule on the sub-divisional committee's duties, issued a circular in July 2015 recording that claims rejected on grounds of insufficient or incomplete evidence can be revisited, and urging those committees to assist gram sabhas by supplying forest, revenue and geo-referenced maps. A community told its claim failed for want of documents should quote that circular and ask for the maps. What a community forest resource title gives is management, not just recognition. Published guidance records that once title is granted the gram sabha may constitute a committee for the protection of wildlife, forest and biodiversity and prepare and implement a conservation and management plan for the area, retaining oversight and the power to modify it or add restrictions for conservation; that claims are made on the dedicated form introduced by the 2012 amended rules; that at least two forms of evidence are required, which may include gazetteers, revenue and forest records, statements of elders, traditional structures and physical features such as sacred groves or burial grounds; and that the title is neither transferable nor saleable.

trackers.name: Legal Services Authorities — a free panel advocate in every district, up to the Supreme Court
trackers.desc: Free representation runs from the lowest court to the Supreme Court, and there is no restriction on the kind of case. Under the 1987 statute a state authority exists in every state with institutions below it, panel and retainer advocates are available for court representation at magistrate, sessions, high court and Supreme Court level, and entitlement arises where an applicant meets one of the statutory criteria and the authority is satisfied there is a genuine case to prosecute or defend. The authorities themselves state that all kinds of cases are included so long as eligibility is met. You may name your lawyer, and you may apply at any stage. Under the 2010 regulations, where an applicant expresses a choice of a lawyer already on the panel, the secretary may allow it — so a community that knows which advocate it wants can ask for that person rather than accept an allocation. Aid may also be sought at any stage of a case, including on appeal, even where a private lawyer acted earlier. A group that has run out of money halfway through a matter is not shut out. Eligibility is personal rather than organisational, and that changes how you file. The criteria are set by category and by income, with the annual income ceiling revised to 1,25,000 rupees for Supreme Court matters and 1,00,000 rupees for high court matters, alongside categories that include women and children. A village association will not qualify as an entity; the affected individuals within it may, so the application should be made in the names of people who meet the criteria. Start with the para legal volunteer, and understand the Lok Adalat trade. The authorities engage volunteers drawn from retired teachers and government servants, non-governmental organisations, self-help groups, anganwadi workers and panchayats to work at village level as a bridge to the legal services institutions, and that is the first person to ask for. Land and property disputes are actively steered toward Lok Adalat and mediation, where court fees paid are refunded on a compromise settlement — but no appeal lies against a Lok Adalat award, so a dispute settled there is finally disposed of.

trackers.name: Air pollution complaints — a 24-hour redressal expectation, and proof of action posted back where you filed
trackers.desc: What it is, and its honest limit. The board's citizen guidelines describe an application through which anyone in the national capital region can lodge an air pollution complaint: register a mobile number and email address, choose the public complaint option, add photographs, and give your name and telephone number. The same application publishes hourly national air quality index values across the country, but the complaint and redressal machinery described in the guidelines is built for the capital region, and an entry that implied nationwide coverage would mislead. Twenty-four hours, with the proof posted back where you filed. After a complaint is received, the nodal agencies are expected to redress it within twenty-four hours, and the action taken, along with documentary evidence or visual proof, is uploaded on the same medium on which the complaint was lodged. A complainant is therefore entitled to look at a photograph of what was actually done. Nothing else recorded in this file promises evidence back to the person who reported. Naming the source correctly decides who receives it. Complaints are forwarded to the nodal agency matching the problem reported — traffic police, the transport department, public construction agencies and others according to the type of pollution. Describing the source in the terms the system uses is what sends the complaint to the body with the power to act, which is the same instruction recorded for the Thai system that tells complainants to go to the authority with direct power. Delays are monitored centrally. A separate application exists for the nodal agencies to act on lodged complaints, and a central control room monitors the daily status of redressal and notifies agencies of delays. An unresolved complaint is therefore a visible item in a monitored system rather than a letter that vanished — quote the twenty-four hour expectation and the central monitoring when following up. Read this with the state board directory and the tribunal entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: DILRMP citizen services — the record of rights, the cadastral map, and revenue court case tracking
trackers.desc: What can be obtained, and from whom. Under the national land records modernisation programme the department lists the services a citizen can obtain: the record of rights, the cadastral map, spatial data, registration of land and deeds, revenue court case monitoring and transliteration of the record of rights into another language. The programme's stated aims are to modernise land record management, minimise the scope of land and property disputes, enhance transparency and move eventually toward guaranteed conclusive titling. The records themselves are maintained by each state or union territory revenue department, in textual and spatial form — so the state portal is the door, and the national scheme is the standard behind it. Revenue court case monitoring sits on that list. A community can follow the revenue proceedings that decide mutations and boundaries, rather than only reading the ownership entry after the fact. Nothing else recorded in this file offers case tracking as a land service, and for a household whose plot is the subject of a live proceeding it is the difference between learning the outcome and watching the process. The record can be transliterated. A multilingual record of rights is a listed service. For a household whose record is written in a script it cannot read — the ordinary situation for migrants and for minority language speakers across a country of many scripts — that is the difference between holding a document and understanding it. Check how far the work has actually reached. The department's own figures put computerisation of records of rights and of registration offices at around ninety-four per cent, digitisation of maps at about seventy-six per cent, and geo-referencing of cadastral maps as completed for roughly half the country's villages, with a fourteen-digit unique parcel identifier based on the geo-coordinates of the parcel's corners rolled out across most states and territories. Ask whether your village has been geo-referenced before relying on a digital map, and compare the cadastral map against what is on the ground. Read this with the legal services authorities, pollution board and tribunal entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: RTI — free if they miss the deadline, and a per-day penalty on the officer
trackers.desc: Ten rupees, thirty days, and forty-eight hours where life or liberty is at stake. Under the 2005 act a citizen may request information from any public authority on written request or by electronic means, with a nominal application fee and no fee at all for applicants below the poverty line. Information is to be provided within thirty days in the ordinary case, and within forty-eight hours where what is sought concerns the life or liberty of a person; five days are added where the application comes through an assistant public information officer or is transferred to the authority that holds the records, and forty days apply where a third party's information is involved. Late means free. Where the information is not provided within the time limit, it must be provided without charge. A community kept waiting stops paying for copying, and the officer's delay becomes the authority's cost. No other regime recorded in this sweep converts delay into a fee waiver. The officer can be fined by the day. The penalty for refusing to receive an application for information, or for not providing information, is two hundred and fifty rupees per day, up to a total of twenty-five thousand rupees. Two countries in this file now put the sanction on the individual officer rather than the institution — this one and Pakistan, where the penalty is measured in days of the officer's own salary. Naming the penalty provision when a deadline passes is part of the follow-up letter. If you cannot write it, the officer must write it for you. Where an applicant is unable to make the request in writing, the public information officer is to render reasonable assistance to reduce the request into writing. And the ladder is short: silence past the deadline is a deemed refusal which opens a first appeal to an officer senior to the public information officer within thirty days, to be decided within thirty days and at most forty-five, with a second appeal to the information commission within ninety days. Read this with the land record services, the legal services authorities, the pollution boards and the tribunal entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Land Conflict Watch — report your conflict into a verified national database, and look up the comparable ones
trackers.desc: You can report a conflict into it. The project maintains a database of more than a thousand ongoing land conflicts across the country, with conflicts that are no longer active kept separately as closed, and its site carries a route to report a conflict. For a community whose dispute exists only in local memory and a pile of letters, being recorded in a verified national database means the conflict becomes citable by lawyers, journalists and researchers who have never been to the village. What gets recorded is what an objector needs written down. Published descriptions of the methodology record that each entry captures the location of the conflict, the reasons behind it, the number of people affected, the area affected, the land type — whether private, common or forest — the names of the government and corporate agencies involved, and a narrative summary. Every data point is cross-checked against other documents, including police reports, memos submitted to local authorities by communities and transcripts of public consultations for development projects, and where no document exists the researchers go to the people on the ground. That list of fields is, in effect, a template for how a community should be assembling its own record. The comparable conflicts come with numbers attached. Published analyses give sectoral totals — mining conflicts counted with the number of people affected, the hectares involved and the value of the investment at stake, drawn from investment figures already published by governments and companies — alongside analyses of forced evictions, a field-verified database on conflicts arising from renewable energy projects, and studies of legislation, high court judgments and state policies on the commons. Knowing that a class of project has already produced dozens of documented conflicts, with investment values, changes how a case is argued and who will listen. What it is, and is not. It is an independent network of interdisciplinary researchers spread across the country, combining reportage with academic method, publishing quarterly analytics, policy briefs and newsletters. It documents and analyses; it does not litigate, represent or organise. Read it with the legal services authorities, the green tribunal, the forest rights claim and the district mineral foundation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Bhuvan — free satellite data, thematic land-use layers, and tools to make your own shapefile
trackers.desc: Free satellite data, downloadable by period and resolution. The national geoportal provides services and applications built on satellite remote sensing data for public use, including visualisation, three-dimensional exploration of imagery, and free download of satellite datasets for a specified period and resolution; it has run since 2009 and is offered in English, Hindi, Tamil and Telugu. Imagery of a site from before a project began is the single most useful piece of evidence a community can hold, and here it is downloadable rather than merely viewable. The thematic layers are the ones a land case actually turns on. The portal serves thematic maps at scales of one in ten thousand, one in fifty thousand and one in two hundred and fifty thousand covering land use and land cover, wasteland, geomorphology, lineament, urban land use, soil and salt-affected land, generated with the state remote sensing centres and available through standard open geospatial web services. What a piece of land was classified as, at a stated scale and date, is precisely what a tribunal or an appraisal committee asks for, and it is often the fact a project's own documents quietly restate. It has tools for making evidence, not only for looking at it. The published list of user services includes creating a shapefile, viewing and downloading satellite data, creating a colour composite for use in mapping software, building a choropleth map, tagging locations and seeing what is nearby, with video tutorials. A community can therefore produce its own map file of a boundary, a cleared area or a spread of affected households — a document rather than an assertion. Resolution, registration and limits. Published accounts record imagery at about two and a half metres for the country as a whole with higher resolution coverage for roughly two hundred cities, and note that military installations are excluded from the imagery; some services require a free registration. Read this with the land records portal, the pollution control board directory, the green tribunal and the forest rights claim entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Registered valuers — three asset classes, a searchable register showing status, and the number that must be on the report
trackers.desc: Land and building is its own registered class. Under the registered valuers and valuation rules of 2017, with the insolvency and bankruptcy board specified as the authority by the central government under the companies legislation, registration as a valuer is granted by asset class — land and building, plant and machinery, and securities or financial assets — each with its own eligibility requirements and its own examination, and a registered valuer may undertake valuation only for the class of asset for which they are registered. A valuer without the land and building registration is therefore not the right person to value land, however senior or well known they are, and that is a point a community can make on paper. Registration runs through a recognised organisation. An individual is eligible if they are a fit and proper person, hold the prescribed qualification and experience, are a valuer member of a registered valuers organisation, have completed that organisation's recognised educational course, have passed the board's valuation examination, and are recommended by the organisation for registration; individuals, registered partnership entities and companies may apply subject to the rules. Those organisations act as frontline regulators and publish lists of their own registered valuer members, which is a second directory to search. The register is searchable, and it shows status. Published guidance records that the board's site allows a search of registered valuers by name or registration number, showing each valuer's status — active, cancelled or surrendered — and the asset class they are registered for. A status check before instructing anyone, and a second check before relying on a report that has been produced against you, is the whole of the protection this system offers, and both take minutes. The registration number belongs on the report. Guidance is explicit that the registration number should appear on the valuation report itself, and that a valuer who cannot supply a number, or whose status shows as cancelled, surrendered or suspended, should not be engaged for statutory valuation work. Ask for the number, then check it against the register rather than against the letterhead. Read this with the state land records portals, the green tribunal, the legal services authorities and the national satellite data portal entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Recognised environmental laboratories — the section 12 lists, the named government analyst, and what a tribunal will accept
trackers.desc: The central board publishes state-wise lists of recognised laboratories. Two sets are maintained: private environmental laboratories recognised under section 12(1)(b) of the environment protection legislation of 1986 with valid recognition, and government, semi-government, public sector and educational institution laboratories recognised under the same provision. The power to grant that recognition was delegated to the central board by gazette notification in June 2021, with an amending notification in June 2024. The first step for any community is the list for its own state, and the first check is whether the recognition is still current. Recognition carries named analysts and an expiry date. Recognition notifications list the approved government analysts responsible for testing each group of environmental parameters, and state the date up to which the laboratory's recognition is valid, with the listed analysts serving until the end of their official tenure. A report signed by someone who is not a listed analyst, or issued after the recognition expired, is a report with a hole in it — and that is a cheaper thing to find before relying on it than after. Accreditation is the precondition, and the directory is searchable. Laboratories seeking recognition must hold accreditation to the international testing and calibration standard from the national accreditation board and take part in proficiency testing for the parameters concerned; that board maintains a searchable directory by state, city and type of testing, and state pollution control boards publish their own approved laboratory lists. Search the accreditation directory for a laboratory within reach, then check the same name against the recognised list. Scope decides what the report can prove. Recognitions name the media a laboratory may test — water, wastewater, soil, sludge, sediment, solid waste, hazardous waste, ambient air, stack emissions, noise and meteorological conditions — and the categories of test, from physical and inorganic through organic, biological, microbiological and toxicological. Practitioner guidance records that reports from laboratories without accreditation are generally not accepted as compliance evidence, while an accredited laboratory's report is accepted by state boards and as technical evidence in tribunal proceedings. Match the parameter to the scope before the sample is taken, not afterwards. Read this with the green tribunal, the state pollution control board directory, the national satellite data portal and the legal services authority entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: NHRC complaints — free, tracked by diary number, with a name-display choice and a focal point for defenders
trackers.desc: Free, online, tracked, and in your own language. Filing a complaint carries no fee. The online system lets the complainant choose whether the matter goes to the national commission or to the state human rights commission for the state where the incident occurred, verifies the mobile number by one-time password, takes the complainant's and victim's details and the incident, allows supporting documents to be uploaded as PDFs, and on submission issues a unique diary number with which the complaint's status can be tracked. The commission's own answers record the complaint system operating in the twenty-two languages of the constitutional schedule, alongside a helpline number and a walk-in facility at its office. You choose whether your name appears on the website. Before submission the portal asks whether the complainant's and the victim's names are to be displayed publicly. For a household facing a local company, a contractor or an official, that single choice is often the difference between a complaint being filed and no complaint at all, and it is worth knowing about before opening the form. There is a focal point for defenders, published as available around the clock. The commission's law division records a dedicated focal point for human rights defenders, stated to be available at all hours and reachable through published channels including a mobile number. When the risk has shifted from the river to a person — surveillance, threats, a false case — that is the number rather than the general complaint queue. What it can do, and what it will not take. Established in 1993 under the human rights protection legislation, it is a recommendatory quasi-judicial body with the powers of a civil court, able to call for any document and summon any person, and its recommendations run both to relief for the victim and to action against those responsible; its law division handles on the order of a hundred thousand cases a year. Complaints commonly concern authorities failing to take lawful action. But matters already before a court or before another commission are outside its scope, and published guidance records a general limit of one year from the incident. File early, keep the complaint clear of anything already in litigation, and quote the diary number in every follow-up. Read this with the legal services authorities, the green tribunal, the land conflict database and the forest rights claim entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Prohibited and regulated areas around protected monuments — a hundred metres of no construction, then two hundred needing an NOC
trackers.desc: A hundred metres in every direction: no new construction. Under the monuments legislation as amended in 2010, the area within a hundred metres of the boundaries of a centrally protected monument is a prohibited area in which no permission is granted for construction, public or private. Repair and renovation of buildings already standing in that band may be permitted, and the competent authority may allow existing structures including houses to be strengthened in their original form, but reconstruction of an existing building is not permitted. Where a project sits inside that band, the question is not what conditions apply but whether it can lawfully proceed at all. The next two hundred metres: nothing without a no-objection certificate. The area beginning at the limit of the prohibited area and running two hundred metres further in all directions is the regulated area, and the national monuments authority's own published answers state that any individual, firm or government organisation intending to carry out construction or reconstruction on property falling within it must apply for a no-objection certificate before proceeding, the certificate being granted by the competent authority on the authority's recommendation. Asking for the certificate number, and for the date it was granted, is therefore a concrete test that a community can apply to any project in that band. Who decides, what is filed, and how long it takes. The central government has designated the commissioners or directors of the state archaeology departments as competent authorities for centrally protected monuments. Published guidance on the process records that the applicant files a first form, the state competent authority verifies it and completes a second, the application then goes to the national authority, and the decision appears on the applicant portal or reaches the competent authority within fifteen to thirty days; that a covering letter from the competent authority and multiple copies of the first form are required; that a built-up area above two thousand square metres triggers an additional schedule of information; and that a small number of monuments fall outside the satellite colour-coded zonal map, so that applications concerning them are filed on paper. Scale, and the pressure to change the rule. Reporting records that all three thousand six hundred and ninety-six protected monuments carry the prohibition, and that a parliamentary committee has criticised the uniform restrictions as illogical, recommending that prohibited and regulated areas be decided case by case and noting that residents of a regulated area must seek permission even for filling cracks, whitewashing or replacing windows; amendments have been proposed to relax the zones around smaller monuments such as statues, cemeteries and cannons while retaining them for world heritage sites. Check the rule as it stands before relying on the distances. Read this with the green tribunal, the state pollution control boards, the land records services and the satellite data portal entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Fair compensation and resettlement law — consent thresholds, a social impact assessment before acquisition, and entitlements for families without land
trackers.desc: Consent is required where land is acquired for private companies or public-private projects. The fair compensation and transparency legislation of 2013 replaced the colonial-era acquisition statute and applies both to acquisition for the government's own use and to acquisition whose ultimate purpose is transfer to private companies or use in public-private partnership projects. Published official summaries record that acquisition for the second category may take place only with the consent of eighty per cent of affected families, and for the third with the consent of seventy per cent; and that once stated for such a project, the public purpose cannot afterwards be changed. Establishing which of the three categories a project falls into therefore decides whether consent is required at all, and it is the first question to put in writing. A social impact assessment comes before the acquisition, not after it. The Act's structure places the determination of social impact and public purpose ahead of the notification and acquisition provisions, and carries a separate chapter safeguarding food security; the rehabilitation and resettlement award, the procedure for rehabilitation and resettlement, a national monitoring committee and the authority hearing disputes follow. The assessment is a document that exists before the notification, which makes asking for it an early and concrete request. Compensation and entitlements sit in separate schedules. The first schedule sets out compensation for landowners; the second sets out the elements of rehabilitation and resettlement for all affected families — expressly including both landowners and families whose livelihood is primarily dependent on the land acquired — in addition to what the first schedule provides; and the third provides for infrastructure amenities. A family that owns nothing but works the land is therefore inside the second schedule, and a claim that stops at the landowner leaves those entitlements unclaimed. Timelines, and what happens when land is not used. Published summaries of the Act record timelines for the process, special provisions for scheduled castes and scheduled tribes, an enhanced role for gram sabhas, provisions for tenants and sharecroppers, offences and penalties, and a retrospective effect provision; a fourth schedule lists the enactments regulating acquisition that sit outside the main scheme, which is why a project proceeding under a sector-specific statute needs checking against that list. Read this with the forest rights claims and the gram sabha's authority, the district mineral foundation, the legal services authorities and the land conflict database entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Milaap — no platform fee, no minimum target, and the foreign contribution rule that decides who may donate
trackers.desc: The platform charges nothing on donations received. Its own pricing and campaign pages state that there are no upfront or fixed fees and no platform fee on donations, with only actual payment processing charges and a voluntary tipping model applying; that there is no time limit on a fundraiser, which can be paused or stopped at any time; that there is no minimum goal to receive funds, so the campaigner receives whatever is raised net of payment gateway fees; and that withdrawals can be made whenever wanted, in one or more instalments. For a community raising toward legal costs or a purchase price over months, instalment withdrawal without a target threshold is the practical shape it needs. Verification is document-based, and refunds exist. The platform states that when a fundraiser is started its team contacts the campaigner for supporting documents to confirm the cause and recipient are legitimate, that the verification team collects identity documents for know-your-customer checks, and that funds are transferred to the beneficiary or next of kin or to a relevant entity such as a hospital, non-governmental organisation or vendor. It states that where a fundraiser is found to be fraudulent it will refund the donation. Withdrawal requests can be raised after the campaign is approved, with funds transferred net of fees and applicable taxes. The foreign contribution rule is the constraint that catches campaigns out. Its terms state that a non-governmental organisation must be registered or approved under the foreign contribution legislation to receive foreign donations, and that otherwise foreign contributions will be restricted on the campaign; that a campaigner must hold the necessary regulatory permissions for contributions from outside the country; and that foreign donations can only be routed to a registered foreign contribution bank account or to a qualifying overseas charity. Decide at the outset whether the campaign is domestic only, because a diaspora appeal without that registration will not reach you. Tax and accountability sit with the campaigner. The terms record that campaigners bear any tax liabilities on funds raised, that the platform gives no tax or legal advice beyond its published material, and that campaigners are accountable for completing the project by the deadline they set and for keeping funders updated on delays. Read this with the environmental litigators, the green tribunal, the legal services authorities and the judgments portal entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Coastal Regulation Zone — the state authority, the management plan that fixes the map, and the no development zone distances
trackers.desc: Every coastal state has an authority whose job includes examining project proposals and preventing violations. Published legal material records that each coastal state and union territory has a state coastal zone management authority, responsible for monitoring compliance, examining project proposals, recommending clearances, preventing violations and updating the coastal zone management plan. One such authority's own site records that clearance applications are filed through the national environmental clearance portal, publishes the notice of a public hearing on its draft management plan, and describes itself as the regulatory body for protecting and improving the quality of the coastal environment and preventing and abating coastal pollution in its area. That authority is the addressee for a complaint about coastal construction. The management plan is the document that decides everything else. The same material records that management plans are the official maps identifying the zone categories within each state, used to identify ecologically sensitive areas, determine permissible activities and guide development planning — and states plainly that no major coastal development can properly be assessed without reference to the applicable plan. The zone generally covers land up to 500 metres from the high tide line, plus the area between low and high tide lines, and tidal water bodies as identified in the plan; the notification records that along tidal influenced water bodies connected to the sea it applies from the high tide line to 50 metres or the width of the creek, whichever is less, with the distance up to which tidal effects are experienced determined by salinity of five parts per thousand measured in the driest period and demarcated in the plan. Get the plan sheet for your stretch before arguing about a project on it. The no development zone distances are stated, and they depend on the plan being approved. Published summaries record that in the rural category with population density above the stated 2011 census threshold the zone extends 50 metres from the high tide line where the management plans have been approved, and 200 metres where they have not; that the less populated sub-category keeps 200 metres; and that the 2019 notification delegated approval powers for two of the categories to the state authorities. The notification itself records that no construction is permitted within that zone in the rural category except repairs or reconstruction of an existing authorised structure not exceeding existing floor space index, plinth area and density, and permissible activities including dwellings within traditional rights and customary uses such as existing fishing villages; and that temporary tourism facilities are permissible only if the tourism plan features in the approved management plan framed with due consultative process or public hearing, keeping a minimum distance of 10 metres from the high tide line. Read this with the tribunal entry, the pollution boards directory, the environmental laboratories and the compensation law entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Tree Officer permission and the heritage tree — fifteen days before any felling, an objection triggers a hearing, and compensatory planting equal to the tree's age
trackers.desc: In a state with this urban trees legislation, no tree may be felled without the Tree Officer's prior permission — including on the owner's own land. The Act provides that once it is in force in an urban area, notwithstanding any custom, usage, contract or law, no person shall fell a tree or cause one to be felled on any land, whether of his ownership or otherwise, within that area except with the previous permission of the Tree Officer. Ask whether the permission exists before arguing about anything else. Fifteen days must pass, and an objection buys a hearing. The Act provides that no tree shall be felled until fifteen days after permission is given; that permission shall not be refused where in the authority's opinion the tree is dead, diseased or windfallen, constitutes a danger to life or property or obstructs traffic; and that where an objection is received against a permission, the matter shall be placed before the Tree Authority for reconsideration and decided within two weeks after giving a hearing to the person who raised the objection. That fifteen-day gap is the window the objection has to reach. The Act also requires a report of felling permissions to be submitted to the urban local authority at least once every six months, and provides that if the authority fails to inform the applicant of its decision within sixty days the application is treated as it prescribes. Heritage trees, and what felling one costs. Reporting of the 2021 amendment records that a tree of estimated age fifty years or more is defined as a heritage tree, species to be notified from time to time; that anyone felling one must plant trees equal in number to the tree's age, each six to eight feet tall at planting, ensure their survival for seven years and geo-tag them, with economic valuation payable where compensatory plantation is not possible; and that the amending Act requires the authority to refer an application to fell a heritage tree, and any application to fell more than two hundred trees aged five years or more, to the state tree authority, which may allow it with or without conditions or refuse it. Those numbers change what a project must budget. The census and the composition are the standing hooks. Reporting records that local tree authorities must carry out a tree census every five years including enumeration of heritage trees, that tree experts are to be part of local tree authorities, and that fines were proposed up to a stated maximum per tree. The Act's own contents list includes responsibility for preservation of trees and power to take a deposit for compliance, a tree authority fund, accounts and audit, tree cess, the requirement that permission for development of land be given with the Tree Officer's approval, powers of direction and prevention of felling, and power of entry. Read this with the green tribunal, the pollution boards directory, the coastal zone entry and the compensation law entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Groundwater NOC conditions — the standard terms attached to an abstraction permission, the over-exploited bar, and the meters that must report
trackers.desc: The conditions attached to a groundwater permission are published, which makes them checkable against what a project is actually doing. A no objection certificate for groundwater abstraction, published with a project's clearance documents, carries standard conditions including that no additional abstraction or de-watering structures shall be constructed without the authority's prior approval; that the proponent shall seek prior permission for any increase in the quantum of abstraction beyond what the certificate permits; that proponents who built artificial recharge structures and took the rebate in abstraction or restoration charges shall continue to regularly maintain them; and it names industries likely to cause groundwater pollution — tanning, slaughterhouses, dye, chemical and petrochemical works, coal washeries, pharmaceutical and other hazardous units. Ask for the certificate, then count the bores. In an over-exploited area, a new major industry does not get one. Published guidance material records that no new major industry is granted a certificate in over-exploited assessment units except as per policy, that new packaged water industries are not granted one in over-exploited areas even in the small enterprise category, and that for infrastructure projects a certificate is granted only where the local government cannot supply the quantity required. It records exemptions for individual domestic users, rural drinking water supply schemes and armed forces establishments, and records that saline groundwater use is exempt from abstraction and restoration charges but still needs a certificate, with no certificate for a new major industry in an over-exploited unit whatever the water quality. Establish the category of the assessment unit first. Charges and rebates are tied to that category. The same material records that industries, mining and infrastructure projects drawing groundwater in safe, semi-critical and critical units pay abstraction charges based on quantum and unit category, with restoration charges applying in over-exploited units, and a rebate of up to half where recharge structures are functional and verified. Metering is a condition with a clock. Published compliance material records requirements to install tamper-proof digital flow meters with real-time telemetry on all abstraction structures within thirty days of grant, with annual calibration by accredited agencies and certificates uploaded to the online portal within seven days; and records that users drawing groundwater without a valid certificate are directed to apply through that portal, with projects abstracting without one liable to fines and environmental compensation as decided by the national tribunal. That tribunal is already recorded in this bucket. Read this with the tribunal entry, the pollution boards directory, the coastal zone entry and the recognised laboratories entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Eco-sensitive zones — the buffer round a national park or sanctuary, the sixty-day objection window on the draft notification, and the one-kilometre mining bar
trackers.desc: Mining is barred within one kilometre of a national park or sanctuary, by order of the Supreme Court. Published legal analysis of the 2023 modification records that mining within a national park or wildlife sanctuary, and within an area of one kilometre from its boundary, shall not be permissible; that the earlier blanket direction does not apply to zones for which draft and final notifications have issued or proposals have been received, nor to protected areas on inter-state borders or sharing common boundaries; and that the ministry must strictly follow the 2011 guidelines and the provisions of the zone notification for the particular protected area on prohibited, regulated and permitted activities, and must follow a named 2022 office memorandum when granting environment and forest clearances in the zone and other areas outside protected areas. That one-kilometre bar is a bright line to measure from a boundary. The draft notification carries a sixty-day objection window. Published description of the procedure records that a state forest department prepares a proposal delineating the zone boundary around a park or sanctuary, accompanied by a zonal master plan mapping land use, settlements, water bodies and corridors, which goes to the environment ministry; that the ministry examines it and issues a draft notification inviting objections from the public within sixty days; that boundaries and rules are finalised after considering suggestions; and that a monitoring committee is then formed including the district collector, the divisional forest officer, local non-governmental organisations and village representatives. Press reporting of one tiger reserve's draft records exactly that sixty-day period being opened for objections. The activity categories are what a project is tested against. The same description records commercial mining, stone quarrying, major polluting industries, commercial use of firewood and new saw mills as prohibited; felling of trees, hotels and resorts, erection of electric cables, road widening and commercial water extraction as regulated, requiring prior permission and conformity with the zonal master plan; and ongoing agriculture, horticulture, rainwater harvesting and renewable energy as permitted. Know the gap between notification and practice. Published analysis records that many proposals stall at state level under pressure from real estate, mining and tourism interests, and that many notified zones have neither a functional monitoring committee nor a current zonal master plan, leaving the regulation on paper; the guidelines' indicative ten kilometre extent is applied with site-specific variation. Asking whether the committee has met, and whether the master plan exists, is therefore the practical test. Read this with the coastal zone entry, the tribunal, the tree felling permission and the forest rights entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Community reserves and conservation reserves — land declared on the community's own volunteering, a management committee that can block land use change, and ownership left intact
trackers.desc: A community reserve is declared because the community volunteered, not because the state took the land. The wildlife legislation provides that the State Government may, where the community or an individual has volunteered to conserve wildlife and its habitat, declare any private or community land not comprised within a national park, sanctuary or conservation reserve as a community reserve, for protecting fauna, flora and traditional or cultural conservation values and practices. Published description records that ownership remains with the community or individuals, that use of natural resources is regulated by the conservation plan, and that hunting, tree felling and habitat destruction are prohibited without authorisation. For a village holding land it wants kept intact, that is a designation it can ask for rather than resist. Once declared, land use cannot change without the committee and the State.
