The Act provides that after the notification no change in the land use pattern shall be made within the community reserve except in accordance with a resolution passed by the management committee and approval of the same by the State Government, and applies stated sanctuary provisions to the reserve. That double lock is the operative protection against a later project. The committee is composed locally, and it writes the plan. The Act provides for a community reserve management committee as the authority responsible for conserving, maintaining and managing the reserve, consisting of not less than five representatives nominated by the village panchayat, or where none exists by the members of the gram sabha, plus a forest or wildlife department representative; that where the reserve is on private land the committee comprises the owner, a department representative and a representative of the panchayat or tribal community; and that the committee is the competent authority to prepare and implement the management plan and take steps to protect wildlife and habitat. The neighbouring category, and the honest limits. Published commentary records the conservation reserve as the parallel category on government-owned land, administered through its own committee advising the chief wildlife warden, both categories preserving existing land use rights and serving as corridors between fragmented habitats; and records the criticism that community reserves have only limited potential for recognising community conserved areas, and cannot be created inside national parks and sanctuaries. Read this with the eco-sensitive zone entry, the forest rights entry, the tribunal and the coastal zone entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Wetlands Rules 2017 — the state authority's dated duties, the Brief Document with mapped boundaries, objections before notification, and the activities banned inside a wetland and its zone of influence
trackers.desc: The state authority's duties come with deadlines a community can hold it to. The 2017 rules provide that the state or union territory wetlands authority shall prepare a list of all wetlands in the state within three months of publication of the rules; prepare a list of wetlands to be notified within six months, taking into account any existing list under state Acts; recommend identified wetlands, on the basis of their Brief Documents, for regulation; and prepare a comprehensive digital inventory of all wetlands within one year, uploaded to a dedicated national web portal and updated every ten years; and that it develops the list of activities to be regulated and permitted inside notified wetlands and their zones of influence. Asking whether those lists and that inventory exist for a given state is a concrete question. The Brief Document carries the boundary, and objections are heard before notification. The rules provide that the concerned state department shall, within one year, prepare a Brief Document for each wetland identified for notification, providing demarcation of the wetland boundary supported by accurate digital maps with coordinates and, among other contents, the list of site-specific activities to be regulated within the wetland and its zone of influence; and that the state shall, after considering the objections, if any, from the concerned and affected persons, notify the wetland in the official gazette within not more than two hundred and forty days from the authority's recommendation. That objection step is where a community's evidence enters. The prohibited list reaches the zone of influence, not just the water. Published description records that inside notified wetlands and their zones of influence the rules ban conversion for non-wetland uses including encroachment of any kind, setting up of any industry and expansion of existing industries, manufacture, handling, storage or disposal of construction and demolition waste, solid waste dumping, and discharge of untreated wastes and effluents from industries, cities, towns, villages and other human settlements, with permanent construction also barred; and records regulated activities such as water withdrawal, resource harvesting and dredging requiring prior approval. Know the limits and the litigation. The rules do not apply to wetlands covered by the forest, wildlife, forest conservation and coastal zone instruments — three of which are already recorded in this bucket. Published material records the national inventory mapping over seven hundred and fifty thousand wetlands totalling some fifteen million hectares, about 4.63 per cent of the country; records criticism that the 2017 rules diluted the 2010 version and that most states had not notified their wetlands; and records the Supreme Court invoking the public trust doctrine and, in December 2024, directing states to ground-truth around thirty thousand further wetlands. Read this with the eco-sensitive zone, the coastal zone, the tribunal and the community reserve entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Consent to Establish and Consent to Operate — the two permissions no industry may start or run without, the online system where their status is searchable, and the imprisonment term for operating without them
trackers.desc: Two consents gate an industry, and both are searchable online. The state boards' online consent management and monitoring systems carry a search status page, letting anyone check the state of a consent application, and explain the framework in their own words: that consent means the board's sanction for the discharge of sewage or trade effluent into a stream, well, sewer or on land, or for the emission of air pollutants into the atmosphere; that under the water legislation no person shall, without the previous consent of the state board, establish or take any steps to establish any industry, operation or process, or any treatment and disposal system or any extension or addition to it, likely to discharge sewage or trade effluent, or bring into use any new or altered outlet; and that under the air legislation no person shall, without the previous consent of the state board, establish or operate any industrial plant in an air pollution control area. Ask which consents a plant holds, and check the status yourself. The consent file contains the documents a community most wants. A state board's own page lists what must accompany a consent application: land documents or lease agreements; a project report with total investment; a site plan map showing the proposed site and its surroundings in detail; a layout plan indicating processes and the point sources of effluent discharge, air emission, solid waste and hazardous waste, with the position of the stack and the treatment plant; and the manufacturing process for each product with flow diagram, chemical reactions and material balance with water budget — with a non-agricultural land certificate required specifically for brick kilns and stone crushers. Renewal is a pressure point with dates. The same page records that a renewal application must be submitted in the fourth month before the consent order expires, that action follows under the named sections if it is made after expiry, and that a fresh application is needed if renewal is not sought in time. A board records that where stringent legal action such as prosecution or a final closure direction was given in the past year, renewal cases are referred to a higher authority. Published material records 2025 guidelines creating a common application across the air, water and hazardous waste regimes, with timelines by industry category and referral to a state level monitoring committee, deciding within thirty days, where the board misses them. Operating without consent is a prison offence. Published legal material records contravention punishable with imprisonment of not less than one year and six months, extendable to six years, with fine, under both statutes, and an additional daily fine after conviction. Read this with the pollution boards directory, the air pollution complaint entry, the recognised laboratories and the tribunal entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Forest Survey of India — forest cover assessed every two years to district and forest division level, the canopy density classes it uses, and fire alerts sent to registered users by SMS and email
trackers.desc: Forest cover is assessed biennially and published down to district and forest division. The survey's own report records that it gives forest cover of the country at state, district and forest division level, and changes in forest cover against the previous assessment; that it reports forest cover inside and outside the recorded forest area, in hill districts, in the north-eastern states, and mangrove; that for the first time a forest cover change matrix inside and outside forest areas was provided separately for clarity; and that the latest edition covers 751 districts against 636 in the previous one, on district boundaries received from the national survey body. Where a project's assessment claims no loss of forest, that is the independent series to set it against — and the same district in two editions is a comparison anyone can make. The canopy density classes are the vocabulary of the argument. Published description records the report tracking changes in forest cover classified into very dense forest above seventy per cent canopy density, moderately dense forest between forty and seventy, and open forest between ten and forty, alongside tree cover outside recorded forest areas, mangrove extent, growing stock and carbon stock estimates. Knowing which class a patch falls in decides whether its clearing counts as a loss of dense forest. Fire alerts go to registered users, not just to officials. The survey records forest fire monitoring by named satellite sensors, with pre-fire alerts, near-real-time alerts and fire risk zonation delivered by short message and email, and lists among its functions alerting state forest departments and registered users of forest fire; it records a geoportal as the one-stop source for forest fire data, a deforestation alert system among its services, and a fire danger rating system based on a weather index with estimation of fire-affected areas. Very high resolution imagery is used for encroachment and illegal mining. The survey records itself working with very high resolution data for monitoring of assets and activities such as illegal mining and encroachments, and lists access to high resolution satellite imagery with ground details of forest cover among its functions. Headline forest cover figures are also republished on the national open data platform. Read this with the satellite geoportal, the forest rights claims, the eco-sensitive zones and the tree officer entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The Habitats Trust Grants — three grant tiers with stated durations, one open to individuals and one written for grassroots conservationists outside any registered body, and the screening a proposal goes through
trackers.desc: A grant programme funds habitat conservation, and one tier is open to individuals. The trust records the grants as recognising and supporting conservation organisations and individuals who work to conserve the country's natural habitats and native species, especially the lesser-known species and neglected habitats, aiming to support holistic, innovative and replicable conservation projects. Published material records three tiers: a conservation grant open only to organisations, administered for three years and given to two shortlisted applicants; an action grant open to organisations and individuals working towards on-ground action on species or habitats needing urgent intervention, administered for two years and given to three shortlisted applicants; and a seed grant for an urgent and critical gap in conservation action, administered for up to one year, covering interventions such as rapid assessments, development or testing of methodologies, and protection of critical habitats from threats. One tier is written for people outside the sector's institutions. Published guidance records a grant seeking to support grassroots conservationists who are not currently full-time employees of any registered not-for-profit entity — society, trust or the named company form — and who are not on the board of trustees or management committee of any such entity; and records the action grant's own rules as open to organisations and individuals, only for projects carried out in the country, with grassroots conservationists encouraged to apply. That is a funding route that does not require an institution first. The tests a proposal must pass are published. The same guidance records that grants are only for conservation of native species and natural habitats, with projects on non-native and exotic species disqualified; that projects must be structured for long-lasting outcomes, with measurable impacts and appropriate indicators; that evaluation covers applicant strength, capacity to deliver, project relevance, status of the target habitat or species, objectives, activity plan, methodology, outcomes, impact and budget; and that the international red list is the primary guide to a species' conservation status. The trust records applications screened by external auditors for eligibility, evaluated by a sub-jury of experts, with field-level evaluation and verification visits to shortlisted applicants' project sites, and records that it accepts applications only through its online portal, does not fund documentary films, and encourages re-use of equipment bought with grant money. Read this with the corridor land purchase, the private forest payments, the crowdfunding platform and the community reserve entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Kalpavriksh and the community conserved areas work — a registered action group started by students to save a forest, its CCA documentation portal, and its petitions against orders restricting rights inside protected areas
trackers.desc: A community's own conserved area can be documented and defended, and one organisation does that work. The group records community conserved areas as natural ecosystems — forest, marine, wetlands, grasslands or others — containing significant wildlife and biodiversity value, conserved by communities for cultural, religious, livelihood or political purposes, using customary laws or other effective means; and records that such areas often remain invisible, face multiple pressures and receive little policy support. It records itself engaged since the late 1990s in research, documentation, advocacy, awareness-building and dialogue facilitation to strengthen them, and records a web portal on community conserved areas run with other organisations that showcases such areas across the country. For a community whose protection of a patch is customary rather than legal, being on that portal is the first step to being visible. It is a registered body with a stated origin and stated locations. Published description records it as a non-profit organisation working on environmental and social issues, begun in 1979 with a student-led campaign to save a city ridge forest, working at local, national and global levels, registered under the societies registration legislation with its number given, based primarily in one city with members in three other named cities and elsewhere. Its advocacy has gone directly at orders that restrict community rights. Its advocacy pages record a note on the ban on non-timber forest produce collection in protected areas arising from an erroneous interpretation of a Supreme Court order, and a petition to the tribal affairs ministry against an authority's order preventing recognition of rights under the forest rights legislation in tiger reserves. Those are precedents a community can cite when told its rights are extinguished inside a reserve. It has run national-level processes and publishes the material. It records coordinating the national biodiversity strategy and action plan process from 2000 to 2003 under a ministry, setting up a fifteen-member technical and policy core group which commissioned over a hundred groups and individuals to prepare action plans at local, state, ecoregional and thematic levels, with a major focus on inputs from local communities living in or depending on forests, wetlands, seas, grasslands, farms and pastures. Read this with the forest rights claims, the community reserves, the environmental lawyers and the habitat grants entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: HRLN — legal aid centres across the states, more than two hundred lawyers, paralegals and activists, crisis-intervention teams and people's tribunals, and free representation for people with no access to the courts
trackers.desc: A national network of lawyers takes cases free for people who cannot otherwise reach a court. Published description records the organisation, founded in 1989, as having grown from a fledgling law firm to an organisation with legal aid centres in several parts of the country, now a nationwide network of more than 200 lawyers, paralegals and social activists across 26 states and union territories working on access to justice for marginalised individuals and communities. It records the organisation providing pro bono legal services to those with little or no access to the justice system, conducting litigation in the public interest, running helplines, conducting legal awareness programmes, investigating violations, deploying crisis-intervention teams, planning people's tribunals, and publishing know-your-rights materials. Crisis-intervention teams and a helpline are the parts a community can reach in the days after something happens, not months later. Its rights definition covers the environment, and its method is to work through movements. Published description records it defining rights to include civil and political rights as well as economic, social, cultural and environmental rights; records it as collaborating with social movements, human rights organisations and grassroots development groups to enforce the rights of deprived people and communities; and records its major target group as issue-based civil society organisations and social movements, given legal training, advice and support on using the law as a tool for social change. It records the network's own view that large-scale struggles against rights violations have to be waged by social and political movements, the legal system playing a significant supportive role — a limited but crucial instrument. That is an honest statement of what litigation can and cannot do for a campaign. Its legal status and volume are on record. Published description records the parent centre as a non-profit legal aid and education organisation registered under the societies, public trust and foreign contribution legislation, providing free legal assistance to people who lack the capacity to seek a remedy, and records it filing more than 100 petitions each year. Read this with the environmental lawyers, the legal services authorities, the green tribunal and the action group entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: SANDRP — a rivers and dams network publishing weekly and annual overviews of hydropower and pumped storage, court orders on project impacts, and analysis a dam-affected community can cite
trackers.desc: There is a standing network on dams whose published output tracks the projects themselves. The network records itself as an informal network working on issues related to rivers, communities and large scale water infrastructure like dams: their environmental and social impacts, their performance and issues related to governance of rivers and dams, and records its site as an effort to comment on happenings related to dams, rivers and people across the country and beyond and to create a platform for informed debate and discussion. For a community facing a dam, a barrage or a diversion, that is a body already documenting the sector week by week. Its posts record court orders and protests in a form a community can cite. Its published items record a high court taking cognizance of the impact of silt flushing from a named hydropower project on downstream fish, fining the project a stated sum, ordering scientific monitoring of future sediment discharge to be done only after a stated date each year, forming a monitoring committee and asking for compliance reports — noting that the order rested on a state fisheries statute's breeding season and so is not likely to apply to silt flushing by other projects. They record protests by tribal communities affected by a named river-linking project raising concerns about its environmental impact and social costs, with the project proceeding despite questions over its hydrological assessment and its environmental, forest and wildlife clearances, and without the government exploring available cost-effective and better alternatives. Its annual overviews cover the project types being pushed now. It records an annual overview series on dams and hydro projects whose fourth part covers concerns about pumped storage projects, recording that the government push for them in two named mountain ranges has strongly been contested by communities and experts. Its coordinator is quoted that dozens of dam projects are already caught up in litigation due to faulty environmental impact assessments, displacement of people, inadequate compensation, destruction of traditional water and livelihood sources, and loss of biodiversity — a list that doubles as the grounds most often argued. Read this with the assessment notification, the green tribunal, the legal network and the community conserved areas entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: mines, minerals & PEOPLE — a national alliance of mining-affected communities, its work on the district mineral fund that mines must pay into, and the consultations it runs on how that money is used
trackers.desc: Communities living beside mines have a national alliance of their own. The alliance records itself as a growing alliance of individuals, institutions and communities who are concerned and affected by mining, formed because the isolated struggles of different groups pointed to the need for a broad national alliance for combating the destructive nature of mining. For a village facing a lease or a quarry, that is a body whose entire membership is people in the same position. Its central practical subject is the fund the mining company must pay into. Its own records concern the district mineral fund established under the 2015 minerals legislation, recording that despite the Act instructing state governments to form district mineral fund trusts, it took a long time; recording a district level consultation on children in mining areas, illegal mining, the district mineral fund and the future generation fund, held with a partner organisation; and recording suggestions for amendment of the guidelines of the named welfare scheme for effective utilisation of those funds in the districts affected by mining, citing the ministry file number of the January 2024 revised guidelines. Money already earmarked for mining-affected districts is easier to claim than new money, and this alliance works on exactly that. It goes to parliament as well as to districts. It records a delegation representing the alliance submitting a memorandum to parliamentarians to raise issues relating to tribal people; records a dialogue on governance of scheduled areas — the constitution and the path ahead — held in the capital; and records a social media training programme run for its network. Published material records its partner organisation as producing case studies from women in mining-affected communities, compiled with community organisers, researchers, community legal specialists, indigenous peoples' rights activists, and peasant and workers' rights advocates. A government notice records the scale of the fund's spending, with about 18,000 projects completed under the welfare scheme. Read this with the land conflict database, the legal network, the dams network and the environmental action group entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The Environment Monitoring Laboratory — an independent analytical lab for air, water, soil, waste and food contamination, with named instruments, referral services and laboratory training
trackers.desc: There is an independent laboratory whose stated purpose is producing evidence that pollution is man-made. The laboratory records that it was established to document and scientifically validate the evidence showing the anthropogenic nature of environmental pollution and ecological degradation, following the processes of sampling, analysis and public dissemination of information, and continuing to do so; and records its mandate as having expanded from pollution monitoring to overall environmental monitoring, observations, referral services, and designing and validating technologies offering alternatives to conventional mitigation techniques. Published description records it as an independent, analytical laboratory that monitors toxic contamination of the environment and uses the results to advocate for improved regulation of the use of toxins. For a community whose samples have been analysed only by the polluter's consultant, an independent lab that publishes is the counterweight. The instruments and the matrices are listed, which is how a community checks a lab can do its test. Published material records the laboratory equipped for microbiological analysis and for monitoring and analysis of air, water and food contamination, with named instruments including gas chromatograph with mass detector, high performance liquid chromatograph, inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrophotometry, atomic absorption spectrometer, real-time polymerase chain reaction, ultraviolet-visible spectrophotometer and bomb calorimeter; and records its analysis covering environmental pollutants in air, soil, solid waste and water. It records the laboratory's own areas as pollution monitoring in ambient air and at point sources, including noise and radiation; validation of sensor-based pollution monitoring technologies; and testing of toxins and contamination in food commodities. It teaches the methods as well as running them. The laboratory records itself as conducting training on laboratory procedures and practices, and the parent organisation lists open courses including integrated laboratory training on sludge analysis experiments, standards and reuse readiness. It records the laboratory's location on a residential campus in a named district roughly a hundred kilometres from the capital, and publishes the organisation's institutional-area address and telephone numbers. Read this with the accredited laboratories entry, the dams network, the mining alliance and the legal network entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Environment Support Group — a city and state organisation whose lakes petition produced court-ordered lake protection committees, with named trustees, a published address and free support to communities
trackers.desc: A city-based organisation's petition ended with the state ordered to devolve lake regulation to local committees. Published reporting records that its lakes petition, filed in 2008 and heard for several years, was decided on 11 April 2012, directing the state to ensure that local communities were involved in lake rehabilitation and management, and that regulation was devolved to lake protection committees constituted for major urban areas — corporations and councils. It records the high court later issuing a contempt notice on the state chief secretary for not constituting those lake protection committees as directed, and a court committee strongly discouraging commercial involvement in lake management and rejuvenation. A committee in your own municipal corporation, created by court order, is a seat rather than a submission. The organisation says what this work actually takes. It records that saving lakes demands complex research, sourcing of information from multiple agencies, challenging field work, long hours of analysis and committed public interest litigation over years, all done by the small group we are, largely without funding support, and that with support it could help hundreds of communities across the state in reclaiming lakes, canals and ponds. That is an honest account of the cost of a single sustained case. Its remit is the metropolitan area and the state, and its services to communities are listed. It records working out of a named metropolitan area of 14 million and the state, in coordination with similar efforts nationwide, and describes itself as facilitating local communities and civil society groups in their effort to resist socially and environmentally destructive developments, providing research, documentation, training, advocacy and legal support, with campaign support recorded in power sector, mining, environmental decision making, decentralisation and infrastructure. It records working with trade unions advancing labour, occupational and health rights of those handling waste, and with vulnerable communities suffering serious contamination due to waste disposal. Its street address, telephone numbers and trustees' emails are published, and it records welcoming long-term volunteer involvement. Read this with the independent laboratory, the mining alliance, the dams network and the legal network entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: District and taluk legal services authorities — front offices inside the district and taluk courts, panel advocate lists published by district, legal aid clinics in villages, and the right to complain about an assigned lawyer
trackers.desc: Free legal help is delivered from an office inside the district court, and a second one in the taluk court. A district court records that the authority provides legal aid by way of the services of able, efficient advocates, to any person who fulfils the criteria, and that it functions as the district authority at district level and as taluk committees at taluk level. It records that legal aid clinics have been established in all the district and taluka courts of the district, and panel advocates appointed to the front office at district and taluka courts, a senior citizen centre, the district police office, the district prison and village care support centres, to help marginalised people, under-trial prisoners, women and children, scheduled caste and scheduled tribe members, and people with income less than three lakh a year. Village care support centres and a taluk office are the nearest free lawyers most rural communities have. The list of panel advocates is published by district. The same district court publishes a list of trained panel advocates working with the district legal services authority, along with the authority's address at the district court complex, and records that the district authority and taluk committees organise settlement forums. A published list of the actual advocates, by district, is the difference between an entitlement and a name to ask for. Where to apply, and what to bring, is set out. Published guidance records that an application may be made to the taluk committee in the premises of the taluk court, the district authority in the premises of the district court at the district headquarters, the state authority, the high court committee or the supreme court committee, that each has a front office where an application can be moved, and that applications may be made in person, by post, orally or online. It records the documents as proof of identity, a self-declared affidavit of income which the authority may accept unless there is reason to doubt it, and documents for the eligibility category claimed. Two rights inside the system are worth knowing. Published guidance records that a formal complaint can be made about an assigned lawyer, and the authority can withdraw the case from that lawyer and even remove them from the panel; and that an applicant who prefers a particular lawyer on the panel may have that preference considered. Read this with the environmental support group, the independent laboratory, the mining alliance and the legal network entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The gram sabha and its ward-level assemblies — roughly 2.5 lakh village panchayats whose plans and accounts the assembly must approve, a published quorum, seven days' notice, and the social audit
trackers.desc: The village assembly's agenda is the one a community wants to be in the room for. A government economic service record states that the assembly does not have any executive function and operates as a recommending body only, and that it holds meetings normally two to four times a year but can meet as and when necessary, with dates fixed by statute in some states. It records the essential agenda as the annual action plan and budget, the annual accounts and annual report of the village panchayat, selection of beneficiaries for social service programmes, identification of schemes for the annual development plan, consideration of the audit reports and analysis of the panchayat's performance; and records that panchayats, besides grants, receive schematic funds for named programmes and can raise revenue by imposing taxes, fees and penalties as per state rule. Each elected member's own ward has an assembly beneath the village one. The same record describes the area a panchayat member represents as a village parliament, and a village development committee constituted by that body and chaired by its elected panchayat member. Published description of one state's system records that all those on the electoral roll of a ward are members of that ward's assembly; the quorum is ten per cent of the membership, and if a meeting is postponed for want of quorum the second may be held with fifty present; an organising committee is constituted at ward level to distribute the notice to all households; and the ward member and panchayat must give at least seven days' notice, with pamphlets distributed and posters put up. Seven days' notice and a ten per cent quorum are the two numbers to check before a meeting is called valid. The scale and the honest weaknesses are both published. Published description records approximately 2.5 lakh village panchayats, around 6,000 block bodies and more than 540 district bodies; records the assembly as a watchdog over the panchayat where no budget or major development plan can move forward without its approval; and records a parliamentary committee review finding incomplete devolution of functions, funds and functionaries, heavy dependence on state and central grants, shortage of trained support staff, irregular assembly meetings with poor attendance especially among women, and bureaucratic interference. Read this with the district legal services authorities, the environmental support group, the mining alliance and the independent laboratory entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Taluk and sub-registrar offices — the encumbrance certificate that lists every registered transaction, the mutation hearing where neighbours may object, and the information request that forces a stalled file to move
trackers.desc: Two different offices hold the two documents a claim needs. A government guide records that the encumbrance certificate relating to any piece of land can be obtained from the sub-registrar's office, while the ownership certificate — the record of rights — has to be applied for and taken from the corresponding taluk office. Published description records the certificate as a paid service under state registration rules listing registered transactions for a property over a specified period. For a community checking whether a site is mortgaged or attached, that certificate is the search, and the taluk office is where ownership is recorded. The mutation hearing is where a neighbour can object. The government guide records that a person seeking mutation must state the lands already held by him; that the revenue officer acknowledges receipt by a counterfoil, duly filled in, signed and dated, and enters the details in a mutation register; that notice is generated and served on all concerned landholders with a date fixed for hearing; and that any objection received orally or in writing before the date of hearing shall be recorded in the disputed mutation case register. Published description adds that before sanctioning mutation the authority satisfies itself that the acquisition is not in contravention of the land revenue rules, with physical verification and measurement based on the registered deed, to check whether there are unresolved disputes with neighbours regarding borders. A stalled file can be moved with an information request. Published description records that for land records the information officer is the revenue officer at taluk level, the sub-registrar at the registrar's office, or the commissioner or revenue officer at a municipal corporation; that an application should specify the land by survey number, village, taluk and district, the period for the encumbrance certificate, and the record sought; and that the officer must respond within 30 days and provide the records or refuse with reasons. It records that registration offices are public authorities and that encumbrance records, registration entries and officer-level file notings on pending applications are information. Read this with the gram sabha and ward assemblies, the district legal services authorities, the environmental support group and the independent laboratory entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Urban ward committees and area sabhas — the city counterpart of the village assembly, seats reserved for citizens and community organisations in one state, and a study naming the cities where they actually meet
trackers.desc: In one state, the law reserves ward committee seats for citizens and community organisations. A published study records that the state's amended municipal legislation, in a numbered section, gives powers to the state government to nominate seven members to the wards committees — five citizens and one representative each from non-governmental or community-based organisations working in the area. It records a citizens' organisation having organised a public hearing on the municipal legislation before the deadline for passing conformity legislation, where the public endorsed most of the recommendations, and having made informal approaches to members of the municipal corporation to press for the formation of wards committees. Seats set aside for community organisations, and a public hearing on the enabling law itself, are two openings a city group can look for. The constitutional basis and the population threshold are published. Published description records that under a named article, ward committees consisting of one or more wards shall be constituted within the territorial area of all municipalities with a population of three lakh or more, with the state legislature to provide for their composition, territorial area and the manner of filling seats; and records the committees' function as reviewing and suggesting measures for the development of their wards, addressing grievances and overseeing implementation of local projects. A smaller tier exists below the ward, in some states. Published description records a central model proposing to divide each municipal ward into several areas of about 3,000 voters each, whose voting population forms an area assembly — the smallest administrative unit in a local authority — which elects members into the ward committees; and records ward activities as covering planning, budgeting and maintenance of accounts, with a ward finance committee for the annual budget and a ward information and statistics committee compiling the economic scenario, land use and infrastructural developments and requirements. Where they work is recorded, and it is a short list. Published research records area assemblies provided for in seven named states but active only in one named city, and records public participation through ward committee meetings as active only in five named cities among twenty-one studied. Read this with the gram sabha and ward assemblies, the district legal services authorities, the environment support group and the land conflict register entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Sahabat Alam Malaysia (Friends of the Earth Malaysia)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Malaysia's oldest environmental organisation, founded in 1977 — pollution and extractives, land use and planning, deforestation, marine and fisheries, agriculture and Indigenous customary land rights, from a head office in Penang and a field office at Marudi in the Baram, Sarawak. Legal support is one strand of a campaigning organisation rather than a separate law practice: it briefs and backs communities through planning and permit challenges, was closely involved in the litigation over planning permission for the Penang South Reclamation, and publishes plain-language explainers on customary land rights and on the legal classes of Malaysian forest and conservation area. WHO IT SUITS: a community facing a quarry, reclamation, plantation, dam or forest-carbon project — especially in Sarawak, where the Marudi office is the contact point. Expect campaigning support, evidence and referral rather than a retainer.

trackers.name: Friends of the Earth Asia Pacific
trackers.desc: The Asia Pacific regional structure of Friends of the Earth International, formed in 2008, whose member groups work on community-based struggles against destructive projects, particularly mining and other extractive industries, alongside Indigenous peoples, peasant farmers, fisherfolk and trade unions. WHO TO ENLIST: the national member group nearest the project. In this region Friends of the Earth International's own directory names groups in Bangladesh (BELA, the Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers' Association), India, Indonesia (WALHI), Japan, Malaysia (Sahabat Alam Malaysia), Nepal, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines (the Legal Rights and Natural Resources Center), South Korea and Sri Lanka. You CAN: reach an organisation that already works community-side in your own country, and draw regional weight onto a local fight. For activists: in several of these countries the Friends of the Earth affiliate is the most experienced community-side environmental body there is.

trackers.name: Electronic Beneficial Ownership System (e-BOS)
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Malaysia SSM (company register)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); Malaysia SSM (company register) — the official register of companies and legal entities in Malaysia — the primary public record of corporate existence, ownership, directors and filings. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A BENEFICIAL-OWNERSHIP REGISTER: this shows the registered entity, its directors and filings; where a separate beneficial-ownership register exists, use that to reach the real humans behind a shell company.

trackers.name: Selangor Syariah Judiciary Department
trackers.desc: Selangor Syariah Judiciary Department — tribunal (Malaysia).

trackers.name: MACC Asset Declaration Portal (MyDeclaration, Malaysia)
trackers.desc: National asset-declaration registry; the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (SPRM) publishes Government Administrative Members’ asset declarations — Prime Minister, Ministers & Deputy Ministers — on this public portal (launched 2018); a statutory declaration law for all MPs is still pending, Malaysia.

trackers.name: MyProcurement
trackers.desc: Malaysia's Treasury portal disclosing government tenders and awarded contracts. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Malaysia, and for how much.

trackers.name: Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM)
trackers.desc: Malaysia's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Malaysia.

trackers.name: The Malaysian Judiciary
trackers.desc: Official portal of the Malaysian judiciary with court information and judgments/e-services. · Find here: the Malaysian Judiciary's portal with selected judgments and court information.

trackers.name: Malaysiakini
trackers.desc: Malaysian independent news outlet known for corruption and accountability investigations.

trackers.name: Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC / SPRM)
trackers.desc: Malaysia’s anti-corruption agency — investigates and prosecutes corruption in the public and private sectors.

trackers.name: SSM e-Info
trackers.desc: Malaysia's Companies Commission (SSM) official corporate-information portal. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Companies Commission of Malaysia
trackers.desc: registration authority of Malaysia

trackers.name: Department of Syariah Judiciary, Terengganu
trackers.desc: Department of Syariah Judiciary, Terengganu — tribunal in Malaysia (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Native Customary Rights — which state you are in decides everything
trackers.desc: ESTABLISH THE LEGAL GEOGRAPHY FIRST. NCR is an official term in Sabah and Sarawak only: the Sarawak Land Code 1958 and Sabah Land Ordinance 1930 set out how it is acquired and extinguished by the state, and forestry and conservation law in both states provides for extinguishment and compensation when an area is gazetted. IN PENINSULAR MALAYSIA, Orang Asli customary land rights are not mentioned at all by any land, forestry or conservation legislation — a Peninsular community cannot rely on this framework. In Sarawak, Native Customary Land covers land where NCR was created before 1 January 1958 and still subsists, land in a Communal Native Reserve gazetted under section 6, and Interior Area Land where NCR has been created. THE BLUNT POSITION, FROM MALAYSIAN CIVIL SOCIETY: holders of usufructuary rights may use and benefit from the land, but with or without title or reserve status, from the state's perspective the land is still its property — and where transfers are permitted at all they may only be between people legally recognised as members of indigenous communities.

trackers.name: What NCR claims must prove — and how far the courts have retreated
trackers.desc: WHAT IS CLAIMED: Iban claims distinguish temuda (cultivated land) from the wider pemakai menua (communal territorial domain) and pulau — reserved virgin forest kept for domestic needs: timber for boats and houses, fruit trees, medicinal jungle produce, hunting and fishing grounds. THE HIGH POINTS: in Nor Anak Nyawai [2001] 2 CLJ 769 pemakai menua and pulau were recognised as Native Customary Land; and the Federal Court held that NCR pre-existed any statute, so reserving land under the Rajah's Order of 1921 for an oil company did not extinguish it. NOW THE RETREAT, AND IT IS THE REASON TO GET ADVICE BEFORE FILING: in 2016, in Director of Forest, Sarawak v TR Sandah Tabau, the Federal Court held by majority that common law recognition did not extend to the broader pemakai menua; commentary records the courts again declining to uphold Iban claims in 2021. Common law NCR rights have been severely restricted in Sarawak and Sabah, the evidentiary burden falls hardest on orally transmitted cultures, and even recognised NCR land can be reclassified unilaterally into Native Communal Reserves, giving the state discretion over use often without community consent. HELP THAT EXISTS: SACCESS produced a guidebook for Sarawak NCR landowners using the civil courts — which also warns that state surveys of selected NCR land, presented as granting titles and recognition, have been read as an attempt to quiet discontent rather than to recognise rights fully.

trackers.name: Hasanah Micro Grant — open year-round, but only once per organisation
trackers.desc: GRASSROOTS MONEY ON UNUSUALLY GOOD TERMS. Yayasan Hasanah, the grant-making foundation under Khazanah Nasional established 1 July 2015, funds five areas including alam sekitar (environment). The micro grant gives up to RM 50,000 per project over 6 to 12 months. APPLICATIONS ARE OPEN YEAR-ROUND and reviewed quarterly — rare, when most funds in this map have one annual window of a few weeks. Eligible: registered NGOs, non-profits, civil society and community-based organisations active for at least 6 months, one of the shortest track-record requirements anywhere here. TWO RULES THAT DECIDE ELIGIBILITY: organisations that have previously received Yayasan Hasanah funding are not eligible — so this favours newcomers, and an existing grantee should not spend time applying; and you must implement directly, not as an intermediary, managing the project yourself and engaging the community directly. WHAT TO SUBMIT: organisational profile, financial records, and objectives, target communities, approach and expected outcomes. Stated failure causes: previous Hasanah support, missing financial documentation or profile, and proposals lacking clarity, feasibility or a community engagement plan. PILOTS ARE WELCOME — the programme explicitly encourages experimentation. Funded work has included permeable bamboo wave screens installed by a community at Tanjung Kepah, and work with Bateq children of the Orang Asli community — so coastal protection and Orang Asli community work are both in scope. The larger annual Hasanah Grant and the Hasanah Special Grant, run with the Ministry of Finance, cover the same areas.

trackers.name: Sahabat Alam Malaysia — community land mapping and legal support, from two offices only
trackers.desc: Two offices cover the whole country and which one you write to is decided for you: the Penang headquarters handles Peninsular Malaysia, the Marudi office in Baram handles Sarawak, and there is nothing in Sabah. Founded in 1977, registered under the Societies Act 1966 and a Friends of the Earth International member since 1983, SAM works on indigenous customary rights and the natural resources of the tropical rainforests. The service most worth knowing about is the mapping. Friends of the Earth International's account of the Marudi office — a team of four working directly with communities up the Baram — describes territorial land-use mapping alongside legal support, petitions and letters to government, and help constituting indigenous residents' associations. Those community maps are not recognised by the State Land and Survey Department, and that does not make them useless: they can be put before a court or sent to state authorities and to the company, which is how a community without documentary title states its claim in terms the other side has to answer. SAM's own pages do not advertise the mapping, so ask for it by name. Telephone before you travel. SAM's own site gives the Penang address as Jalan Masjid Negeri on one page and Jalan Padang Tembak on another, its older publications give Jalan Air Itam in George Town, and the Marudi number appears as both 758 973 and 756 973. The constants are the Marudi street address — 129A, First Floor, Jalan Tuanku Taha, P.O. Box 216, 98058 Marudi, Baram, Sarawak — and the Penang number +604 827 6930.

trackers.name: PACOS Trust — Sabah: they train you to document settlement history for an NCR claim
trackers.desc: The offer that matters is training in the systematic documentation of indigenous settlement history to support a native customary rights title claim — not a lawyer and not a grant, but the evidence work that decides whether an NCR claim survives, done with a community rather than for it. PACOS also states that it acts as an intermediary between community organisations and outside bodies, whether government agencies, private companies or NGOs, so it will sit between a village and a company rather than leave the village to negotiate alone. The warning on its own site is the thing a community is most likely to need and least likely to be told. Sabah has two kinds of communal title — those grounded in customary tenure, and state-planned communal titles. Under the 2009 amendment to section 76 of the Sabah Land Ordinance, indigenous people are deemed beneficiaries of a communal native title rather than owners under their native customary rights, and the amendment lets whichever party controls the state government declare an area a state-planned communal title. PACOS wants those abolished, and describes the joint venture companies used in the schemes as giving money and asking locals to sign an acknowledgement. Being offered a communal title in Sabah can move you from owner to beneficiary, so establish which kind is on the table before anyone signs anything. Coverage and funding, stated plainly. It supports community organisations in 14 districts across 23 geographical areas and says it hopes to reach all 21 rural districts with at least one community organisation in each — so several districts have none yet. Much of its money comes from outside the country, topped up by research contracts, hosting conferences and in-kind contributions from communities and its own personnel, which makes it exposed to a funding cycle. Registered under the Trustees Ordinance (Sabah) in 1997, working with communities since 1987; office at Taman Flash Gordon, P.O. Box 511, Penampang. Two live domains — the content is at pacostrust.com, while pacostrust.org is a stub. This is the Sabah door: Sahabat Alam Malaysia's two offices cover the peninsula and Sarawak and nothing here.

trackers.name: Jabatan Alam Sekitar — exhibition dates are published, and approving the report is not approving the project
trackers.desc: The Department publishes each EIA report's public exhibition period and comment deadline as a dated notice, so the dates are knowable in advance rather than something you hear about late. Two live examples show the shape: the Penang Mutiara Line LRT segment 2 report was exhibited from 9 March to 7 April 2026 with public comments accepted until 22 April, and the Lynas rare-earth expansion at Gebeng from 10 April to 9 May 2026 with comments until 24 May — roughly a month on display and a further fortnight to write. The distinction that decides your strategy is in the Department's own FAQ: approval of an EIA report is not approval of the project. Under section 34A(3) of the Environmental Quality Act 1974 the Department approves only the report; the project is approved by the approving authority, meaning the State Authority and the local authority. A favourable EIA outcome therefore does not stop the scheme, and an approved EIA still has to pass a planning decision where different arguments and different people apply. Two exclusions to settle before planning around any of this. Activities in the First Schedule of the 2015 prescribed activities order require no public exhibition and no public comment at all unless the Director General directs otherwise in writing, so establish which schedule your project sits in rather than waiting for a notice that will never come. And Sabah and Sarawak run their own state environmental law: prescribed activities there are set by the Environmental Protection (Prescribed Activity) (Environmental Impact Assessment) Order 2005 in Sabah and the Natural Resources and Environment (Prescribed Activities) Order 1994 in Sarawak, not by the federal order. The Department also enforces after approval — site inspections, checks on compliance with the conditions of an approved EIA, verification that the measures set out in the Environmental Management Plan are actually in place, and continuous monitoring through its own digital system — which makes a complaint about breach of conditions a real route rather than a gesture. A project crossing two or more states is processed at headquarters, Menara PETRA, Persiaran Perdana, Precinct 4, Putrajaya. And because a proponent must show the project is consistent with the National Physical Plan, the state Structure Plan and the Local Plan, any conflict with those is a documented inconsistency worth raising in the comment period.

trackers.name: Malaysian Nature Society — stopped a golf course, then got handed the park to run
trackers.desc: The arc worth studying: a state government planned to turn the Kuala Selangor mangrove and mudflat into a golf course, the Society campaigned against it, the area was established as a nature park in 1987 instead, and the Society now manages and runs that park on behalf of the Selangor state government. On its own account this is the only case in Malaysia of a park managed by an NGO for the government. A campaign that ends with the campaigners holding the management agreement is a different outcome from one that ends in a refusal, and it is the outcome to aim at where a state is willing to designate but unwilling to staff. Its conservation division says plainly what it does: see to the effective management of existing protected areas, and establish new ones. Both halves matter — the second is the route for ground with no status yet, the first is what a state government will actually engage with. It also runs the ecoCare Kerteh centre, a field study centre and Dark Cave, so it has a record of taking sites on rather than only arguing about them. The branches are the way in. Founded in 1940 and the country's oldest membership-based, tax-exempt environmental society, it has branches in most states, and those branches run their own local conservation projects and special interest groups. Approach your own state branch rather than the Kuala Lumpur secretariat; membership is open and inexpensive. It works with government agencies, schools, local communities, indigenous peoples and international partners including BirdLife International, IUCN and the Forest Stewardship Council. Two notes. Its site is at mns.my while its e-mail addresses run on mns.org.my, so both domains are live and neither is wrong — take contact details from the site rather than reconstructing an address. And this is a conservation and education society, not a litigator: for legal work in the peninsula or Sarawak go to Sahabat Alam Malaysia, in Sabah to PACOS, and for the federal EIA process to the Department of Environment.

trackers.name: Sarawak NCR — the five acts that create the right, and why a perimeter survey is not a title
trackers.desc: Five acts create the right, and the cut-off date is 1 January 1958. The department's own explanation is that native customary rights may be created by felling virgin jungle and occupying the land cleared, by planting the land with fruit trees, by occupation or cultivation, by use of land for a burial ground or shrine, and by use of land of any class for rights of way — and that rights created by any of those methods are recognised. Native customary land is land in which such rights were lawfully created before 1 January 1958 and still subsist, land in a reserve to which the relevant section applies, and interior area land where rights were created under a permit. Evidence of which of those five acts was done, where, and before that date is the whole of a Sarawak claim. Three different sections do three different things, and communities conflate them. The perimeter survey provision exists to fix boundaries and remove overlapping claims, and gazettes the area as a communal reserve. A separate provision recognises the native territorial domain, capped at a thousand hectares per native community settlement, under which a native communal title can issue. A third provision is the one that produces an individual grant in perpetuity, free of premium and rent, where the director is satisfied that a native has occupied and used unalienated State land under customary tenure amounting to ownership for residential or agricultural purposes. A survey is not a title, and the published figures show the gap. Government statements record millions of acres surveyed and gazetted under the perimeter provision against a few tens of thousands of acres actually titled under the grant provision, and critics of the scheme argue that land gazetted as communal reserve is state land which a minister may later degazette, with no assurance that a surveyed area will proceed to title. Establish which section your land sits under and what the next step to a grant actually is before treating a survey as security. The same inversion appears next door. The Sabah entry recorded here describes a community moving from owner to beneficiary through a communal title; this is the Sarawak version of the same risk, and the two should be read together. For legal help in Sarawak, the Marudi office recorded in this file is the one to approach.

trackers.name: MyBar Pro Bono Hub — where an organisation, not an individual, asks for a lawyer
trackers.desc: The applicant here is the organisation, which solves a problem running through every other legal aid entry in this file. Published accounts of the hub's launch by the bar council's human rights committee record that law firms of any size may register to offer free legal services, that non-governmental organisations submit requests for assistance, and that every case is reviewed by a working group under that committee which matches it with a suitable volunteer firm. Legal aid schemes recorded here for India, Indonesia, Singapore and Bhutan all test the means of individuals, so a village association cannot qualify as an entity and has to file in the names of members. This route is built the other way round. The subject matter is public interest work, not family and tenancy. The platform is described as connecting volunteer law firms with civil society organisations and non-governmental organisations needing legal assistance on public-interest matters — which is the category a development or land dispute actually falls into, and the category most means-tested schemes are least oriented toward. Use the bar's other finding tools before asking for a match. The same site carries directories of lawyers and law firms, firms indexed by area of practice, the bar council legal aid centres, state bar committees, foreign lawyers and law firms, the seniority list, and specialised aid directories. Searching by area of practice first means a request can name the kind of firm needed rather than leaving the matching entirely to the working group. Treat it as new. The hub was launched in December 2025, so intake arrangements, timelines and the scope of matters accepted should be confirmed directly before a community relies on them. In a land or development case the organisations most likely to be making such a request are the two Malaysian bodies already recorded in this file, in Penang and Marudi for the peninsula and Sarawak and in Sabah respectively; approaching them and the hub together is more sensible than either alone.

trackers.name: NAHRIM water quality laboratory — an accredited lab that states it serves the public, and the agency-only lab behind it
trackers.desc: An accredited laboratory that says in its own words that it serves the public. The national water research institute's water quality laboratory offers chemical and microbiological analysis across a range of water matrices — drinking water, surface water, effluent and groundwater — holds a numbered accreditation certificate from the national standards department, and states that alongside supporting the institute's own research it provides analysis services to the general public. Effluent and groundwater being on that list is the part that matters: they are what a community downstream of a plant, a quarry or a landfill actually needs measured, and they are the matrices most private laboratories treat as specialist work. Name the accreditation when you commission, and keep the reference with the result. The laboratory's accreditation is held under a numbered certificate from the standards department. Quoting that certificate and the specific parameters when instructing, and keeping the reference alongside the readings, is what makes a result difficult to wave away later — the same discipline this file records for the accredited houses in Sri Lanka, Nepal and Vietnam. The bigger laboratory network is real but not directly reachable. The national chemistry department runs laboratories across the country with an environmental quality division whose sections cover trace metal analysis, environmental water analysis, oil spill and chemical waste analysis, trace organic compounds and air quality — but it provides its analysis, investigation and scientific consultancy to government agencies rather than directly to members of the public. The way a community reaches that capability is to get the environment department or another agency to send the sample, which is a further reason to make the regulator's complaint the vehicle rather than a parallel track. Sampling decides whether the result stands. The chemistry department publishes sample submission guidelines whose stated purposes include reducing rejected samples and preserving the integrity of samples sent in, and which note that sampling and packaging matter as much as the analysis if the result is to show the true condition of the original sample. Read whichever laboratory's guidance before collecting anything rather than after.

trackers.name: National Conservation Trust Fund and the MySDG Trust Fund — a conservation trust, and a fund with two calls a year
trackers.desc: A national conservation trust fund exists, and its first listed category is protecting particular places. The ministry's national conservation trust fund for natural resources states its purposes as supporting capacity building to meet the country's obligations under multilateral environmental agreements and providing a mechanism to receive and channel funds supporting natural resource management and biodiversity conservation. Among the project categories it funds are those to manage, monitor and protect areas of biodiversity importance and environmentally sensitive areas, and to manage, monitor and protect in-situ biodiversity including ecosystems and species. A community defending a specific place is writing to the fund's first category rather than arguing its way into one. Two categories most applicants overlook. The fund also lists projects to raise public awareness through education, training and capacity building including supporting campaigns for protection and conservation, and projects to foster understanding in the implementation, enforcement and improvement of conservation policies, acts, regulations and guidelines. Campaigning and enforcement literacy are inside the published list rather than adjacent to it, and non-governmental bodies appear among those the fund names as able to apply. A second fund answers the timing problem this file keeps recording. The government's sustainable development trust fund, a collaboration with the United Nations in Malaysia begun with government funding, states that at least two calls for proposals will be run each year and opened to all eligible entities, and that it works with the private sector, non-governmental and civil society organisations, academia and the public. Its stated aims include addressing the climate, biodiversity and pollution crises and their effects on lives and livelihoods, and the inclusion of vulnerable and frequently excluded groups. Two calls a year is a rhythm a community can plan around, unlike the five-day windows recorded elsewhere. Know who decides. That trust fund is governed by a board of trustees drawn from across sectors, with the United Nations resident coordinator an ex-officio member, and its executive committee is co-chaired by the resident coordinator and the Treasury's secretary general. Read this with the land and legal entries already recorded for Malaysia: the file now holds ground, lawyers and money for this country.

trackers.name: Jabatan Bantuan Guaman — a public eligibility calculator, plus mediation and a legal companion service
trackers.desc: You can test your own eligibility before applying. The department, which sits under the prime minister's department, publishes an online means test for legal aid eligibility as a public system, alongside its pages on who qualifies and how to apply. Running that calculator before making an appointment costs nothing and answers the question most communities waste weeks on. Only Korea, among the schemes recorded in this file, offers the same self-check, and in both places it exists precisely because the means rules are hard to read from outside. Four services, not one. The department lists litigation, a mediation service, an advisory service and a legal companion service, with a separate electronic advice system and an online appointment system for booking. That matters where representation may not be granted: a community can still get advice, a mediator, or somebody to accompany it, and those are different offers with different thresholds rather than a single door that is either open or shut. The rules, the charter and the cancellation page are all published. Alongside the legal aid regulations, including their 2021 amendment, the department publishes its client charter, its list of state directors and branch heads, a panel solicitors system and a public complaint management system. It also publishes a page on the cancellation of a legal aid certificate — worth reading before relying on one, because a certificate that can be cancelled is a certificate with conditions attached. Where to go. The head office is in Putrajaya with separate telephone lines for civil and syariah matters, and branches are listed by state with their directors named. Read this with the pro bono hub entry already recorded for this country: that route takes requests from organisations, and this one takes them from individuals — between them a community can be helped whichever way it is constituted.

trackers.name: Carian rasmi and e-Tanah — the title search that carries the registrar's endorsement
trackers.desc: There are two title searches, and only one carries the registrar's signature. A land office distinguishes the private search from the official search: the official search examines, notes or extracts from any register of title, presentation book, correction book or any instrument of dealing or application delivered to the registrar, is applied for on the official search form issued by the registrar's office or the district land office under the national land code, and must be signed by the registrar. The private search carries no such endorsement. For a community that expects to put the result in front of an official or a court, that difference decides which one to buy. What is online differs by state, and the entry says so. The land offices run a public electronic portal on which private searches of land and strata titles can be obtained without attending a counter, application status can be checked, land tax can be checked, paid and a statement generated, and various dealings applied for, with public kiosks provided at every land office and the biometric verification needed only once. But the states differ on the official search: one federal territory portal states that official search applications can be made online with direct debit payment and the certified copy issued in the public portal, while a state portal states that only private searches may be done online and an official search requires attendance at the public counter. Check your own state's portal before travelling or before assuming you can avoid the journey. You need the title particulars, not the owner's name. Published guidance records that a search cannot be run from an owner's name or identity card number: the land office requires the full title details. A community that wants to know who holds a plot must therefore start from the title reference, which is the opposite of the position recorded in this file for Punjab, where a name search is possible. And the search shows the encumbrances. The same guidance records that a title search reveals caveats and charges over the land and whether they remain in force. Where a developer says a plot is unencumbered, or a community wants to know whether a caveat can still be entered, the search is the document that answers it. Read this with the customary rights and conservation trust entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: SPRM and the Whistleblower Protection Act — protection that dies if you go public first
trackers.desc: Going public first destroys the protection. Under the 2010 whistleblower protection act the identity of a person who discloses improper conduct, and the information they give, are confidential and may not be revealed to anyone — including during proceedings in court — and the discloser cannot be subjected to civil, criminal or disciplinary action as a result of the disclosure. Protection attaches at the moment the disclosure is made to an enforcement agency. Published guidance is explicit that a person who tells the public before making a formal report has exposed their own identity and cannot then be protected. For a group whose instinct is to publish first, that fixes the order of operations: report, then take advice about what may be said publicly. Protection can be revoked, and the grounds are listed. It lasts unless revoked under the act, and the grounds include the discloser having taken part in the misconduct themselves, having deliberately made a false statement, having disclosed solely to avoid dismissal or other disciplinary action, or having committed an offence under the act itself. Someone inside a project who was part of what they are reporting should take advice before relying on the protection. Failing to report a bribe is itself an offence. The commission's own material records that under the 2009 act a person who knows of the giving, receiving or offering of a bribe and fails to report it faces a substantial fine or imprisonment or both. A villager offered money to withdraw an objection is therefore not merely being tempted; they are acquiring a reporting duty, and saying so out loud is sometimes enough to end the offer. Channels, tracking and rewards. Reports may be made through the commission's complaint portal and its mobile application, which also allows the status of a submitted report to be checked; the commission accepts information from people who do not identify themselves but states plainly that it often cannot act without a way to make contact, and that reports are screened for whether they involve corruption, whether they can be acted on, and whether the person complained of can be identified. Rewards are paid to public servants whose reports end in conviction, scaled to the value involved. Read this with the official land search, the accredited laboratories, the legal aid department and the water research entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Ketua Audit Negara — reports published project by project, and an auditor who may read classified documents
trackers.desc: Reports are published project by project. The auditor general's report portal carries audits organised by ministry and by named project — among them the management of flood mitigation in the capital, a public private partnership redevelopment of a broadcasting complex, an air traffic control centre project and a government electronic services concession. A community facing a comparable scheme can therefore read how the state's own auditor examined one like it, and cite those findings by name rather than arguing from first principles. The audited universe includes local authorities and government companies. The department's own account lists what it audits: ministries and federal departments, state governments, federal and state statutory bodies, a hundred and forty-nine local authorities, religious councils, trust funds and accounts, and several hundred government companies, meaning those in which the government holds half or more of the equity. The council that approved a project and the company building it can therefore both sit inside the same audit universe. The auditor may read classified documents. The auditor general has power to obtain evidence and examine all records including classified documents, and to see all documents, cash, records, vouchers, stamps, shares, property and store goods subject to audit without interference from any party. Where a community is refused a document on grounds of confidentiality, the auditor is not, and that difference is the reason to route a question through an audit rather than a request. Reporting runs to the legislature, not the executive. Reports are submitted to the head of state — or to the ruler or governor of a state — for consent to be tabled in the federal or state assembly, and are then considered by the public accounts committee; the department records that reporting directly to the legislature rather than to the executive is what secures its independence, and that where elements of misappropriation or corruption appear the matter is notified to the controlling officer, who is expected to report it to the enforcement agencies. Read this with the anti-corruption commission and whistleblower protection, the official land search, the accredited laboratories and the legal aid entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Yayasan Hasanah — a grant programme with an environment window, and published guidelines each cycle
trackers.desc: Environment is one of five named funding areas, not an afterthought. The foundation's published grant guidelines set out a grants programme across five impact areas — education, community development, environment, arts and public spaces, and knowledge — with the stated aim of catalysing social impact at scale. For a community group whose work is environmental but whose case is also about land, livelihoods and a village's future, more than one of those windows may fit, and the guidelines are where the fit is decided. The applicants it expects are civil society organisations and communities. The same guidelines describe working through an ecosystem that includes civil society partner organisations, social enterprises, government and regulatory agencies and the community itself, and state that the ecosystem is intentionally local — a deliberate strategy rather than an incidental preference. A small local organisation is therefore inside the intended applicant pool rather than an exception to it. Read the guidelines for the cycle you are applying in. The foundation issues grant application guidelines for a particular round, with the version and date on the face of the document; eligibility, ceilings, timelines and required documents belong to that round rather than to the programme in general.
