A published profile records a chief who, before appointment, was headwoman of a longhouse of 40 families, and whose responsibilities now encompass oversight of 21 longhouses housing 2,815 families; records her mediating disputes mostly pertaining to land issues, arising where parties are dissatisfied with the decisions made at the longhouse level or the headmen's court; and records the current apex as the native court of appeal, constituted by its president and two members including the head of the state customs council, with a restructuring proposed to add a native supreme court and make the system a fully independent judicial institution. Read this with Sabah's native courts, the Sarawak customary rights acts, the community mapping organisation and the indigenous peoples' network entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Sahabat Alam Malaysia (Friends of the Earth Malaysia)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Malaysia's oldest environmental organisation, founded in 1977 — pollution and extractives, land use and planning, deforestation, marine and fisheries, agriculture and Indigenous customary land rights, from a head office in Penang and a field office at Marudi in the Baram, Sarawak. Legal support is one strand of a campaigning organisation rather than a separate law practice: it briefs and backs communities through planning and permit challenges, was closely involved in the litigation over planning permission for the Penang South Reclamation, and publishes plain-language explainers on customary land rights and on the legal classes of Malaysian forest and conservation area. WHO IT SUITS: a community facing a quarry, reclamation, plantation, dam or forest-carbon project — especially in Sarawak, where the Marudi office is the contact point. Expect campaigning support, evidence and referral rather than a retainer.

trackers.name: Sahabat Alam Malaysia (Friends of the Earth Malaysia)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Malaysia's oldest environmental organisation, founded in 1977 — pollution and extractives, land use and planning, deforestation, marine and fisheries, agriculture and Indigenous customary land rights, from a head office in Penang and a field office at Marudi in the Baram, Sarawak. Legal support is one strand of a campaigning organisation rather than a separate law practice: it briefs and backs communities through planning and permit challenges, was closely involved in the litigation over planning permission for the Penang South Reclamation, and publishes plain-language explainers on customary land rights and on the legal classes of Malaysian forest and conservation area. WHO IT SUITS: a community facing a quarry, reclamation, plantation, dam or forest-carbon project — especially in Sarawak, where the Marudi office is the contact point. Expect campaigning support, evidence and referral rather than a retainer.

trackers.name: Friends of the Earth Asia Pacific
trackers.desc: The Asia Pacific regional structure of Friends of the Earth International, formed in 2008, whose member groups work on community-based struggles against destructive projects, particularly mining and other extractive industries, alongside Indigenous peoples, peasant farmers, fisherfolk and trade unions. WHO TO ENLIST: the national member group nearest the project. In this region Friends of the Earth International's own directory names groups in Bangladesh (BELA, the Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers' Association), India, Indonesia (WALHI), Japan, Malaysia (Sahabat Alam Malaysia), Nepal, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines (the Legal Rights and Natural Resources Center), South Korea and Sri Lanka. You CAN: reach an organisation that already works community-side in your own country, and draw regional weight onto a local fight. For activists: in several of these countries the Friends of the Earth affiliate is the most experienced community-side environmental body there is.

trackers.name: Tansa (Tokyo Investigative Newsroom)
trackers.desc: Tokyo investigative newsroom producing longform expos  s on power and public accountability.

trackers.name: Courts in Japan – Judgments
trackers.desc: Official searchable database of Japanese court judgments (English & Japanese). · Find here: the Japanese courts' English search of precedent-setting judgments.

trackers.name: Courts in Japan – Case Search (裁判例検索)
trackers.desc: Supreme Court's official judgment database — Supreme, High, district, administrative, labour and IP case law, fastest official source. · Find here: the Japanese courts' official case-search of precedent-setting judgments.

trackers.name: National Tax Agency – Corporate Number
trackers.desc: Japan's public corporate-number publication system identifying registered companies. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Corporate Number Publication Site (NTA Japan)
trackers.desc: Japan's official corporate-number registry of registered entities. Here you can trace companies, their directors and filings registered in Japan.

trackers.name: Board of Audit
trackers.desc: body to audit government expenditures of Japan

trackers.name: Board of Audit of Japan
trackers.desc: Constitutionally independent national audit body. Here you can trace public-audit findings on waste, irregularity and misspending in Japan.

trackers.name: Ministry of Finance – Budget
trackers.desc: National public-procurement / budget-transparency portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this shows the specific firms winning specific tenders and contracts — for aggregate budget totals use the open-data/statistics portal, and for findings of waste use the audit body. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Japan.

trackers.name: Ministry of Finance — Budget
trackers.desc: Japan's budget, debt and fiscal data from the finance ministry. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Japan.

trackers.name: Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC)
trackers.desc: Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC) — Japan’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Statistics Bureau of Japan
trackers.desc: Japan's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Japan.

trackers.name: 特別緑地保全地区 — designation that forces a purchase
trackers.desc: A DESIGNATION THAT FREEZES LAND, AND THEN MAKES THE CITY BUY IT. Under Article 12 of the Urban Green Space Act a Special Green Space Conservation District preserves green space in its current state by requiring permission for new building, rebuilding or extension; land reclamation, clearing, quarrying or mining or any change to the form or quality of land; felling of trees and bamboo; and filling or draining water surfaces. Permission comes from the ward or city, or the prefecture for towns and villages. The district is decided by the municipality — or by the prefecture where it is 10 hectares or more and spans 2 or more municipalities. THE PART THAT INVERTS THE USUAL PROBLEM: where the restrictions significantly hinder use of the land, the owner may apply to the ward or city to buy it, and the municipality, prefecture or a designated green space conservation body is required to buy — with JPY 20 million of the transfer income deducted, reducing income tax. Elsewhere conservation depends on persuading an owner to sell; here designation creates a right to compel the purchase. TWO COMPANION TOOLS THAT REDUCE THE BURDEN OF HOLDING LAND: a 管理協定 (management agreement) has the authority carry out the management instead of the owner, and the 市民緑地 scheme opens the land to residents.

trackers.name: 市民緑地制度 — open private land to residents by contract
trackers.desc: A CONTRACT ROUTE WHEN PURCHASE IS NOT POSSIBLE. Under Article 55 of the Urban Green Space Act a local authority or a green space body contracts with a landowner to establish and manage a 市民緑地 — green space or greening facilities on land, artificial ground, buildings or other structures, opened for residents' use. CONDITIONS: land of 300 m² or more inside a city planning area; land inside Special Green Space Conservation Districts and green space conservation areas also qualifies; and the contract term is at least 5 years. Under Article 60 a private body may instead establish and manage one under a citizens' green space plan certified by the mayor. USE IT: this keeps title with the owner while securing public access and management — the middle option between doing nothing and raising a purchase price.

trackers.name: 地球環境基金 — the national grant for environmental NGOs and NPOs
trackers.desc: JAPAN'S STANDING GRANT FOR PRIVATE ENVIRONMENTAL GROUPS, run by ERCA and built from government investment plus corporate and public donations, operating on the investment return with expert committee advice. Its stated aim is to support the autonomy, independence and diversity of environmental NGOs and NPOs. ELIGIBLE FIELDS run to 10 categories, and the useful ones here come first: nature protection, conservation and restoration; forest conservation and greening; environmentally conscious agriculture; air, water and soil environment conservation; comprehensive environmental conservation activity. A borderline classification is not fatal — the activity field may be changed during the review process. THE CYCLE: recruitment is in principle once a year, in the year before the activity year, with timing and eligibility set out in an annual 募集案内; a recorded window ran 14 October to 17 November 2025 with awards announced the following March. Briefings are held across 8 regions, and for online sessions you may attend any region's briefing wherever you are. ERCA also publishes a general list of NGO/NPO grant schemes and a searchable list of past grantees by area and field — a fast way to see who near you has been funded and for what.

trackers.name: Applying — the non-profit-type condition and the system-only submission
trackers.desc: TWO THINGS THAT SINK APPLICATIONS. 1. THE NON-PROFIT-TYPE CONDITION: a 一般社団法人 or 一般財団法人 must meet the 非営利型法人 (non-profit-type corporation) requirements under corporation tax law. If you do not meet them when you apply, transitioning to non-profit type by the grant application submission — around May of the funding year — is a condition of the award decision. So you may apply mid-conversion, but the conversion must complete before the money is confirmed; start it now if it applies to you. 2. THE WORD FILE IS NOT THE SUBMISSION: requests go through the 地球環境基金助成金申請システム online. A Word draft and a submission manual are provided, but the Word file is for drafting only — you must transcribe each item into the system, so budget time for that rather than assuming you can attach the document. Applications are examined by the fund's operating committee and paid under the 交付要綱. Contact: 地球環境基金部, 044-520-9505.

trackers.name: JELF — 400+ environmental lawyers, in all 47 prefectures
trackers.desc: WHO TO CALL, AND THEY ARE EVERYWHERE. JELF has more than 400 lawyers as full members across all 47 prefectures — so it is usable from anywhere, not only the big cities. Many lawyers from Japan's four great pollution lawsuits, the origin of its environmental law, remain members, and successors have worked on dioxin and asbestos. IT LITIGATES AGAINST LARGE PUBLIC WORKS: the Isahaya Bay reclamation in Nagasaki, the Henoko base in Okinawa and the Linear Shinkansen, framing its aim as stopping environmental destruction from wasteful public investment. Ecosystem cases are core — including litigation with the Amami rabbit as plaintiff, and cases for the Ezo pika and Blakiston's fish owl. BE REALISTIC: its own news records losses — in the Kadoku beach ‘rights of nature’ case on Amami Ōshima the Supreme Court declined to accept the plaintiffs' appeal on 23 May 2025, leaving the rejections below standing.

trackers.name: JELF local government support — get your municipality to act
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE MOST COMMUNITIES DO NOT KNOW EXISTS. JELF runs a project team supporting municipalities to protect the local natural and living environment, whose members serve as in-house municipal lawyers, municipal advisers and members of councils and expert committees. It offers drafting of ordinances (条例策定) and legal advice, firm handling of illegal operators carrying out fly-tipping of waste and construction spoil, and sharing of advanced cases and know-how across its national network — and it invites municipalities to consult freely. It expressly names the problem as developers acting without regard to local conditions, citing large-scale disorderly renewable energy development destroying natural and living environments. THE TACTIC: if your group cannot litigate itself, persuading your municipality to seek this help — and to enact a local ordinance — may be the stronger route, because the ordinance binds future developments rather than fighting one at a time.

trackers.name: 日弁連 公害対策・環境保全委員会 — opinion papers that get revisited
trackers.desc: THE BAR FEDERATION TREATS POLLUTION HARM AS A HUMAN RIGHTS ISSUE. The JFBA began with a special committee inside its human rights committee, established an independent pollution committee in May 1969, and renamed it to its present form in 1985. It now has 7 sub-committees plus project teams, working through research, 意見書 (opinion papers), symposia and publications to advance national and local environmental policy and prevent environmental destruction. A METHOD WORTH COPYING: a project team formed in March 2014, before approval of the Linear Chuo Shinkansen construction plan, issued an opinion that approval should not be given until environmental concerns were resolved — then went back 5 years later, in 2019, to investigate Ōshika village in Nagano where the South Alps tunnel generates vast spoil, and Kasugai in Aichi where disposal of spoil containing naturally occurring arsenic and fluorine is contested, and held a public session on which predicted harms had materialised — returning again in November 2022. An objection is worth far more when someone documents, years later, that it was right.

trackers.name: National Trust Activity Grant — pays the purchase price, but the pot is ¥5m a year
trackers.desc: This is money to buy the land, not money to campaign about it — the joint grant of the Pro Natura Foundation Japan and the Association of National Trusts in Japan covers the purchase price, lease payments, the cost of standing up a trust body, and maintenance including signs, fencing and paths. Items 3 and 4 are only available to an applicant also taking item 1 or 2, so there is no maintenance-only grant. Read the size before planning around it: the 22nd round has a total annual pot of ¥5,000,000 and expects to make one or two grants, with a per-organisation cumulative ceiling of ¥8,000,000 across years and a one-year wait after reaching it. There is no closing date — the round opens on 1 April and ends the moment the pot is exhausted, so what you are racing is other applicants rather than a deadline. Three bars catch people: the applicant must be an incorporated body (NPO hōjin, ippan or kōeki zaidan hōjin), so an unincorporated residents' group has to incorporate first; the landowner must already have agreed to the sale or lease; and the title must carry no third-party rights, a mortgage included. A further inversion: land inside a strongly regulated zone under the Natural Parks Act or similar may be ruled outside the scheme, so existing designation can disqualify you rather than help. Applications go by post, two copies of each, with the certificate of registered title, the cadastral map, the fixed-asset tax certificate, articles, officer list and latest accounts; the Association asks to be contacted for an eligibility check first. Screening is documents, then a site inspection, and no progress enquiries are answered. Grantees must present at the Pro Natura results meeting in Tokyo in late November or early December, in person. Awards have stopped megasolar (Hatoyama, Kiritappu), landfill (Jūnigata) and road works (Trust Sarun Kushiro): Jūnigata took 1.6 ha for ¥3,325,000 covering purchase, transfer registration and a sign. No grants at all were made in rounds 6 to 10, or in round 19. 2-30-20 Nishi-Ikebukuro, Toshima-ku, Tokyo 171-0021, 03-5979-8031.

trackers.name: Association of National Trusts in Japan — directory of local land-buying trusts
trackers.desc: Before founding anything, check whether a trust already exists near you: the Association keeps a link list of the trust bodies operating in more than 50 regions of Japan, and an existing body with legal personality can apply for purchase funding that an ad-hoc neighbourhood group cannot. What these bodies do is become the owner — citizens raise subscriptions, take gifts or bequests, or contract, and hold the land themselves rather than petitioning the state to designate it; the Association's own explainer is at ntrust.or.jp/about_ntrust/q1_ans.html. Treat the page as a routing tool, not a register of holdings: it links organisations and does not state which parcels each one owns, or whether any of them can take on a new site now — that has to be asked of the body directly. Association office: 2-30-20 Nishi-Ikebukuro, Toshima-ku, Tokyo 171-0021, 03-5979-8031, office@ntrust.or.jp.

trackers.name: JELF 日本環境法律家連盟 — environmental lawyers nationwide, and they defend you when the developer sues back
trackers.desc: The answer most worth having is in its own FAQ: Japanese procedural law does not allow wildlife to be a plaintiff. The celebrated Amami rabbit 'rights of nature' case was in substance an injunction sought by local residents against turning the rabbit's forest into a golf course, with the animal serving as the campaign's symbol. Plan a residents' injunction and use the species for the public argument, not for the pleadings. The federation says the same of its own role: local environments are defended by residents standing up, and the lawyers' job is to support that legally. That support explicitly includes being sued back. The FAQ names defamation claims and unjust damages suits brought as pressure against residents' movements among the things its members handle, which makes this one of the few entries here where counter-litigation against a campaign is treated as an expected part of the work rather than a catastrophe. The second offer is drafting the rule, not only fighting the project. JELF lawyers act as advisers and outside experts to municipalities, help write local ordinances and give legal support on illegal dumping of waste and construction spoil; the federation names large-scale, badly sited renewable energy development as a current driver of destruction, which is the shape many Japanese local fights now take. Where a municipality is sympathetic but unsure of its powers, this is a route through the council rather than around it. Its membership includes lawyers from Japan's four great pollution lawsuits, and its case record runs from the Isahaya Bay reclamation and Henoko to the maglev line and suits over the Ezo pika and Blakiston's fish owl. It publishes what it learns. A newsletter five times a year written by the lawyers running the cases, plus an annual journal — the closest thing Japan has to a running record of environmental litigation. Expect losses in it: the Kadoku Beach 'rights of nature' case ended on 23 May 2025 when the Supreme Court declined to take the appeal. The office is in Nagoya, not Tokyo — 6F East, Sanko Nishiki Building, 3-5-30 Nishiki, Naka-ku, Nagoya 460-0003, 052-746-9006, jelf@green-justice.com.

trackers.name: 日本環境測定分析協会 JEMCA — search for a measurement laboratory by region and by what you need tested
trackers.desc: One searchable directory instead of hunting laboratories: members can be searched by region and by the kind of analysis needed. The association's own guidance is addressed to exactly the person who does not know where, or what, to commission. Its members' listed categories cover ambient air and exhaust gas, river water, groundwater and wastewater, soil and bottom sediment, dioxins under the specified-concentration scheme, noise, vibration, odorous substances and odour index, workplace environment, asbestos in building materials or in air, low-concentration PCBs in insulating oil, radioactivity, PFAS and microplastics. Two of those are worth noticing. Asbestos in building materials or in air, and PFAS, are the two questions most likely to arise from a demolition or a contaminated site and least likely to be answerable by a general laboratory — here they are listed categories you can search on directly. The association runs proficiency testing, which is the thing to ask a laboratory about. Its scheme compares a laboratory's results against other laboratories to detect bias between them, and analyses duplicate samples to detect variability within one laboratory. Asking whether a laboratory takes part, and what its results were, is a sharper question than asking whether it is accredited, because it goes to whether this laboratory's numbers agree with everybody else's. The environment ministry publishes a manual on quality control when analysis is outsourced, and the association links to it. Read that before commissioning, because the decisions that determine whether a result is usable — sampling points, preservation, chain of custody, choice of method — are made by whoever writes the instruction, not by the laboratory. The search covers a member's registered address only, so a member with other branches must be checked on its own site, and printable member lists have been withdrawn in favour of the search. Association office in Edogawa, Tokyo; 03-3878-2811.

trackers.name: プロ・ナトゥーラ・ファンド — grants for local groups, including a small-group window and an emergency one
trackers.desc: The window built for small local groups is the one to read first. Alongside its general domestic activity grant, the fund runs a locally rooted citizens' activity category for organisations with at least two years of activity behind them, working on their own local natural environment with local residents as the main participants; the foundation states it is intended for relatively small organisations. Grants run for a year, or two years in some categories, at one million yen and two million in some categories, and applications from ordinary members of the public and from students are explicitly welcomed. One condition disqualifies a great many campaigns, so check it before drafting. The domestic activity grant covers conservation together with dissemination and awareness work, and the foundation states that activities without a dissemination or awareness component fall outside it. A project that is purely protective with no public-facing element will not qualify as framed, and adding a genuine explanatory or educational strand is the difference between eligible and not. It runs an emergency grant as well as an annual round. Recent emergency awards have gone to work such as studying early vegetation and pollinator recovery in a wetland after a fire, at a million yen. Almost nothing else in this file offers a route for a situation arising between funding rounds, which is when most damage happens. This is the same foundation that runs the National Trust activity grant recorded here for buying land. A group can move between a research or activity grant and the grant that helps pay a purchase price without changing funder, which is worth knowing when a campaign turns into an acquisition. Other categories cover domestic research, overseas work in developing regions, annual special themes — recent ones on endangered plants and on estuarine and coastal biodiversity — and a longer-term category for continuing projects. Deadlines are enforced to the minute and no changes are accepted after submission.

trackers.name: 公害等調整委員会 — causation adjudication, built for victims who cannot prove causation
trackers.desc: The instrument worth knowing about is causation adjudication. Alongside liability adjudication, which decides whether damages are owed and how much, the system provides a separate procedure in which the adjudication committee determines the causal relationship itself. The commission's own material explains that this exists to make up for a victim's insufficient ability to prove causation and to resolve complex cases quickly; it can be applied for in parallel with a conciliation already under way, so that a stalled conciliation where the parties disagree fundamentally about cause can be unblocked, and a court may also commission it. For a community that is certain a plant is responsible but cannot prove it, that is the procedure the system was designed around. Try the cheaper door first, and the commission says so. Two systems exist: pollution complaint counters at municipal and prefectural level, where staff investigate the facts, liaise with the relevant agencies and advise the parties on improvement measures through a simple procedure; and the dispute resolution system proper. The commission's own guidance advises that depending on the nature and degree of harm, a complaint to the local counter may resolve matters comparatively easily and quickly, and to start there. Four procedures, and a board in most prefectures. Mediation, conciliation, arbitration and adjudication are all available, and in principle all begin on a party's application; conciliation and adjudication account for almost all cases. Thirty-seven prefectures maintain a standing pollution examination board of between nine and fifteen members, and prefectures without one appoint a panel of candidate examiners and constitute a body for each case as it arises. Know the cost and the burden before filing. Application fees apply, and fees for conciliation at prefectural level vary by prefecture, so ask the prefecture's pollution section in advance. The procedure follows civil litigation in form: the applicant's burden is reduced but assertions, proof and evidence remain the applicant's own work. Forms are published for download, some documents may be submitted by e-mail, hearings may be held by web conference, and a consultation line exists for questions before an application is made.

trackers.name: National park land purchase and scenic land protection agreements — the ministry buys, or a body manages in the owner's place
trackers.desc: The ministry buys private land inside national parks, on the owner's own application. Japan's national parks are designated regardless of who owns the land, so they contain a great deal of private property — published figures put ownership inside the parks at roughly sixty per cent national, thirteen per cent public and twenty-six per cent private — and the ministry states that where private land holds outstanding nature it purchases that land at the owner's request. A quarter of the national park estate is therefore in private hands and potentially in scope. An owner who will not sell can still hand over the management. Where management by the landowner is inadequate and there is a risk that the protection of the landscape cannot be achieved, the environment minister, a local authority or an approved park management organisation may conclude a scenic land protection agreement with the owner and manage the land in the owner's place. Two approved agreements are published, one held by a public interest foundation in a national park in Kyushu since 2004 and one by a non-profit organisation in a park in central Japan since 2011 — so this is a route with named precedents rather than a theoretical power. The reason the purchase system exists is the argument to make. Because parks are designated over private land, owners inside special protection zones and first-class special areas carry heavy restrictions: felling trees and putting up new structures are in principle prohibited, and in a special protection zone even taking fallen leaves or stones is forbidden. The purchase system was created to relieve that burden, funded historically through bonds issued by prefectures with national subsidy. An owner arguing for purchase is arguing that the restriction on their land is the point. Establish the zone first, because it governs everything. Special protection zone, first, second or third class special area each carry different restrictions and different permitting authorities; building or forming land inside a special area needs permission judged against national rules and the area's own management plan, and typically takes one to three months. Since April 2022 applications go directly to the ministry rather than through the prefecture, though checking the correct destination in advance is advised.

trackers.name: 公害苦情相談窓口 — a free complaint desk in every municipality, and the national survey that counts them
trackers.desc: Every municipality and prefecture has a pollution complaint desk, and the commission publishes the whole national list. Consultation is free, and can be made in person at the desk, by telephone, by letter, or by email where the local desk accepts it. The instruction from the national commission itself is to start with the desk in your own city, ward, town or village rather than with the commission, because everyday pollution problems are most often resolved there. In larger cities the post of pollution complaint counsellor is a mandatory one rather than a discretionary appointment. The desk's output is directed at the operator. The desk investigates the facts, contacts the relevant agencies where necessary, and where a pollution phenomenon is recognised gives the source of it advice and guidance on improvement measures, working toward resolving the complaint. That is a different thing from filing a report: the counsellor's job ends with somebody being told to change what they are doing. Bring three things. The commission states what the counsellor needs — the cause of the pollution, its degree, and the state of the damage — and that the counsellor will ask in detail in order to handle the matter properly. Preparing those three before the call is the whole of the preparation, and it is the same discipline this file records for reporting lines elsewhere. The national survey is what makes the system checkable. Each year the commission surveys the pollution complaints received at local government desks across the country and publishes a report on how many were received and how they were handled, with the statistical tables carried on the government statistics portal and an annual white paper on pollution dispute processing alongside. A community can therefore see how many complaints of its kind its prefecture receives and what became of them before deciding what to expect — and where the desk cannot resolve matters, the commission's own mediation and adjudication procedures and the prefectural examination boards are the next step, which is the entry already recorded here for causation adjudication.

trackers.name: 法テラス — three free consultations, fee advances repaid monthly, and a means test waived after a designated disaster
trackers.desc: Three free consultations on the same matter, and you may change lawyer. The centre provides free legal consultation with lawyers or judicial scriveners, at its own offices across the country and at the offices of practitioners under contract with it. Consultations are by appointment and run thirty minutes, and the same matter can be taken up to three times — with a different lawyer at the second appointment if the first was not a fit. Criminal matters fall outside this route and go to the bar association instead. Fee advances turn on three conditions, one of which is the merits. Where a lawyer or scrivener must actually be instructed, the centre advances the fees and expenses. The conditions are that income and assets fall at or below the means standard, that it cannot be said there is no prospect of winning, and that the case suits the purpose of civil legal aid. Advances are repaid to the centre in monthly instalments of a few thousand yen; where the assisted person is receiving public assistance, repayment may be deferred until the aid case concludes, and exemption from an unpaid balance may be applied for once all aid cases have ended. Two access provisions decide whether the scheme is usable at all. Consultations away from the office, and interpreter services, are both available to people meeting stated conditions with prior approval. For a village at the end of a bus route, or for a resident who does not speak Japanese, that is the difference between a scheme that exists and one that can be reached — and both must be arranged in advance rather than asked for on the day. After a designated large-scale disaster the means test does not apply. Free consultation is available without the means standard to people who, on the date of the disaster, had an address, residence or place of business in a municipality where the disaster relief law was applied. Practical points: bring the documents received from the court or from the other side, bring a written note of what you want to say because the time is short, arrive about ten minutes early to complete the application form, and file the consultation application with the office within a month of the consultation. Read this with the environmental lawyers' federation and pollution complaint desk entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 登記事項証明書 — anyone may obtain the register for any parcel, without the owner's consent
trackers.desc: Anyone may obtain it, and no permission is required. Published guidance records that a registry certificate can be obtained by any person on payment of the fee, without the consent of the owner or the company representative, apart from certain privacy-related information, and that this follows deliberately from a registration system built on public notice: the ownership of land is published so that dealings are safe. Reported practice is that nothing beyond the application form is required — no identification document and no seal. A community can therefore establish who holds the ground it is fighting over without asking anybody's permission and without explaining why it wants to know. Three ways to ask, and the online one is cheaper and open later. Certificates for land and buildings, and map and plan certificates, may be requested at a registry office counter, by post, or online through the ministry's registration and deposit application system. Counter hours run on weekdays to the early evening while online requests are accepted until nine at night, and the fee for an online request is lower than the counter fee. Payment is made by internet or mobile banking or at a Pay-easy enabled cash machine, so no revenue stamps need to be bought. You choose where it arrives. A certificate requested online can be posted to an address the requester gives, or collected at a registry office the requester nominates — which need not be the office holding the record. For anyone outside a city that is the difference between a request and a day's travel. Bring the lot number rather than the address. Reported guidance notes that identifying the land by its lot number, or a building by its house number, makes the request straightforward, and that both can be found on a property tax notice or on an older certificate. A separate registration information service supplies an inquiry number that can be attached in place of the certificate when filing electronically with government agencies. Read this with the pollution complaint desk and legal aid entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 情報公開 — anyone may request for a small fee, and a review board that reads the withheld document itself
trackers.desc: Anyone may request, for three hundred yen a document. The disclosure law allows any person to request disclosure of administrative documents — individuals, corporations, associations, minors and foreign nationals alike — on payment of a request fee of three hundred yen per document, paid by revenue stamp. What can be asked for is an administrative document: something an agency's officers created or obtained in the course of their duties and hold for organisational use, as it exists at the time of the request. Thirty days, extendable by thirty, with a separate route for very large files. The decision to disclose, partly disclose or refuse is made within thirty days of the request, extendable by up to thirty more for justifiable reasons with notice to the applicant; where the documents are extremely voluminous the agency may take longer, but must notify that within the first thirty days. Time spent correcting a defective request form does not count against the period. The review board reads the withheld documents itself. Where a review request is made against a refusal or partial disclosure, the head of the agency must consult the information disclosure and personal information protection review board, which may require the documents in question to be produced for examination in camera and may require an index classifying and organising the information recorded in them by a method the board specifies, as well as hearing the applicant's statement. A body that can look at the document being withheld is a different proposition from one that can only read the reasons for withholding it. And the lawsuit can be filed near you. An information disclosure action may be brought in the district court at the seat of the high court with jurisdiction over the plaintiff's own address, rather than only where the agency sits. Two further points worth knowing: a further disclosure request may be made within thirty days of the first disclosure, and an agency may refuse without confirming whether a document exists where answering that question would itself reveal exempt information — so a refusal to confirm or deny is a recognised category rather than evasion. Read this with the registry certificate, the pollution complaint desks and the legal support centre entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 会計検査院 — send information about a subsidised project, and search seventy years of findings
trackers.desc: A subsidised local project is inside the audit scope, and anyone may send information about it. The board of audit accepts information concerning the bodies it examines — the state, corporations in which the state has invested capital, and the prefectures, municipalities and other bodies which receive subsidies from the state — where their business or their accounting appears inappropriate, uneconomical, inefficient or insufficient in its effect, and states that such information is used as a reference in its audits. It provides an encrypted web form for this and sets out a privacy policy. Where a road, an embankment or a facility near a community is built with a national subsidy, the recipient body is inside the audit scope, which is the sentence most people do not know. The findings are searchable back to the 1940s. The board maintains a database of its audit reports covering every year from the late nineteen forties to the most recent, browsable by year and searchable by keyword across the full text. A community can look up how the same class of project, subsidy or works contract was treated in earlier findings before it drafts a single sentence of objection. The report must record what broke the law or the budget. The audit report is required to carry eight categories of item, among them matters found to violate law, cabinet order or the budget or to be improper, and it is sent to the cabinet and submitted from there to the legislature; the board also makes ad hoc reports and reports on audits requested by the legislature. Follow-up names what was not fixed, and who was disciplined. Later reports record the state of corrective measures for improper items carried in earlier reports, including items from years before which remained uncorrected at a stated date, and the board ascertains what disciplinary action the responsible ministries took against the supervisors and the officers involved in those items. An uncorrected item with a date on it, and a record of who was disciplined, are the two documents that make an audit bite. Read this with the information disclosure route, the registry certificate, the pollution complaint desks and the legal support centre entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: ハザードマップポータル — flood, landslide, landform classification and disaster monuments on one map, and the limits it publishes
trackers.desc: Several risks appear on one map, for anywhere in the country. The portal is run by the national survey authority with the transport ministry and brings together, in a single consistent presentation, the inundation areas and depths for river flooding, inland water, storm surge and tsunami, landslide warning zones, landform classification, monuments recording past disasters and designated emergency evacuation places, with a companion service for searching the hazard maps published by individual municipalities. A separate ministry download service publishes the underlying national datasets — terrain, land use, city planning and land prices among them — as downloadable geographic data, which is where the layers behind this map can be obtained in bulk. It is free, and it needs no request. Anyone can search by address, place name or coordinates and read the risk layers for a specific site without applying to anybody, which means a community can establish what the state already says about a piece of ground before the first public meeting rather than after it. Landform classification and the disaster monuments are what an objector should reach for first. The classification describes how a piece of land was formed and therefore the natural disaster risk it inherently carries; the monuments are stones and markers recording the scale and damage of disasters that already happened there. Against a proposal that treats a site as a blank rectangle, those two layers are counter-evidence that predates the developer's own study by decades or centuries. The portal publishes its own limits, and they should be quoted accurately. Mesh sizes, drawing methods and legends may not match the maps produced by the originating agencies; some locations have no risk information prepared at all; the national overlay uses a uniform presentation and can sometimes be zoomed further than the source data's accuracy supports; address search results and the background map contain error; and it is expressly not the statutory municipal hazard map used in property transaction disclosure. For the latest and most detailed position, the municipality's own hazard map governs. Read this with the pollution complaint desks, the register copies, the information disclosure route and the board of audit entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 農地中間管理機構（農地バンク） — the prefectural body that takes farmland on lease, keeps it farmed, and gives it back
trackers.desc: One body per prefecture, under public control. The farmland intermediary management organisation is a corporation funded by the prefecture, municipalities and agricultural bodies, designated by the governor as the single such organisation in that prefecture, and in some places called the farmland bank or simply the corporation. Under the area plans given statutory footing by the 2023 amendment to the farm management foundation strengthening law, it borrows farmland from owners — expressly including idle land and land whose owners cannot be identified — and lends it on to those farming in the area, in order to consolidate holdings. Leasing to it keeps the land farmed, and the land comes back. Published summaries of the arrangement record that rent is paid reliably through the bank rather than depending on the tenant, that the land does not fall into abandonment, that at the end of the contract period the land returns to the owner, that deferral of inheritance and gift tax continues where the prescribed procedure is followed, that a lease to the bank counts as succession for the farmers' pension, and that if the tenant becomes unable to continue farming the bank works with the relevant bodies to find another and maintains the land itself in the meantime. For an owner who wants neither to keep farming nor to sell to a developer, that is a third option, and it is the one this file has been looking for in country after country. The transfer runs on a published plan. Rights move when the governor gives public notice of the land use allocation plan the bank has determined, which removes the need for separate permission from the agricultural committee under the farmland law, or alternatively when the mayor gives notice of a municipal consolidation plan. Those plans are public documents, and they are where to look to see which parcels are moving and to whom. To rent land from it, answer the public call. Anyone wishing to borrow farmland from the bank must apply through its open recruitment; the method and the forms differ between prefectures, and the municipality, the agricultural committee or the cooperative can point to the current call. From April 2025 farmland leasing was in principle unified through the bank, with recipients required to be positioned on the target map of the area plan. Read this with the hazard map portal, the registry copies, the pollution dispute boards and the national trust grant entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: クラウドファンディング型ふるさと納税 — the municipality raises money for one named project, and its own residents can give too
trackers.desc: The municipality names the project, the target and the period. A city's own explanation describes crowdfunding conducted through the hometown tax system as a mechanism in which the local authority sets out a specific project aimed at solving a problem and invites donations to that project; people living inside or outside the municipality may donate, and receive the same tax deductions as under ordinary hometown tax giving. For a community that wants a wood, a riverbank, a spring or a stretch of green space bought, restored or maintained, the practical question becomes which municipal project line the work can be attached to — and that is a conversation with the town office rather than a fundraising campaign from nothing. Residents of the municipality can donate, and still receive relief. The platform's own explanation records that donations to the municipality where the donor is registered are possible and remain deductible, with the qualification that no thank-you gift is sent in that case. Local people funding local land is therefore possible here, which is not true of most funding routes recorded elsewhere in this file. A published example is a green space along a river. One city's live projects include conserving the greenery of a named river and restoring its cherry-tree avenue, with the city stating that donations are applied to the specified undertaking, that a thank-you gift goes to non-resident individual donors above a threshold but not to corporations, and that donations cannot be cancelled. A named, purpose-bound, non-cancellable donation is the shape to ask a municipality for, because it is the shape the municipality already knows how to administer. Municipalities can combine, and the underlying scheme is very large. Wide-area government crowdfunding allows several municipalities to raise money together against a problem common to them, and reported figures put total hometown tax donations in a recent year above a trillion yen. The two questions for a town office are which portal it uses and whether it has run a conservation project before. Read this with the national trust activity grant, the directory of local land-buying trusts, the prefectural farmland bank and the pollution complaint desk entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Tansa — no advertising and no subscription, published in two languages, with a standing lawyer
trackers.desc: No advertising, and no subscription fee. The newsroom's published account states that it accepts no advertising revenue from companies or administrative bodies, in order to keep its position independent of sponsors, and that it charges no subscription so that anyone can reach its reporting regardless of their economic circumstances; operations are funded by donations and grants, with monthly supporters, and it describes those donors as companions rather than customers. For a community weighing where to take material, that means nothing it brings can be pulled off by an advertiser, and nothing published about its case will sit behind a paywall where neighbours cannot read it. It publishes in two languages and works across borders. Its articles are released online in Japanese and English, and it states that it places weight on worldwide collaboration as the global standard of the trade, because the state powers and corporations that investigative reporting confronts already operate across national boundaries. Where a project's parent company, financier or buyer sits outside the country, a bilingual newsroom that collaborates internationally is the one that can follow it there. The beat includes contamination. Its published output includes reporting on perfluorinated chemical contamination involving a named manufacturer, and earlier work on the predicament of a town hosting a nuclear plant, alongside series on public money and on labour aboard fishing vessels. A community holding monitoring results and a corporate name is approaching a newsroom that has run precisely that kind of story before. What it is, and one detail worth noting. Launched in February 2017 as a project of a university journalism institute, it became independent with non-profit corporate status in February 2018, opened a training school for investigative journalists in November 2020 and took its present name in March 2021; its stated purpose is to end the abuses of power that create victims and to prevent new harm, and it publishes the name of its standing legal adviser alongside its editor. A newsroom that keeps a lawyer on the masthead is one that expects to be sued, which is a useful signal about what it is prepared to publish. Read this with the municipal pollution complaint desks, the pollution adjudication commission, the environmental lawyers' federation and the national trust grant entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 埋蔵文化財包蔵地 — sixty days' notice before any digging, whatever the scale, and the trial trench that follows
trackers.desc: Sixty days before the ground is broken. Where anyone intends to excavate land known to contain buried cultural property — shell mounds, tumuli and other land publicly recorded as containing buried cultural property — for civil engineering works or any purpose other than investigating that property, the cultural property legislation applies the ordinary notification requirement with the thirty-day period read as sixty days. Municipal guidance records the duty as applying regardless of the type or scale of the works, and lists building construction, building removal, exterior works, land formation, landfill and ground improvement among the works it catches. Whether a site falls inside such an area is published and can be checked in advance, so a community can establish the date by which a notification should already exist and ask whether it does. The agency can require a record-preservation excavation before the digging. Where it is judged particularly necessary for the protection of buried cultural property, the authority may direct that an excavation investigation be carried out to create a record before the excavation proceeds, together with any other necessary matters. Municipal guidance explains that where the works mean the buried property cannot be preserved as it stands, the developer is directed to carry out that record excavation — and that ground improvement works can trigger the same requirement where they affect preservation. Public bodies notify earlier, at the planning stage. Where the works are those of the state or a local authority, the parallel provision requires notice at the time the project plan is drawn up rather than sixty days before the dig, submitted through the municipal board of education to the prefectural board. For a public project, therefore, the question is not whether sixty days' notice was given but whether the planning-stage notice was given at all, and what the prefecture said in reply. Trial trenching, delay, and changing the plan. On receiving a notification the municipality may carry out a confirmatory trial excavation to establish whether the digging will affect buried property; guidance warns that filing immediately before construction causes the start to be delayed, because the reply takes time and its contents may require works to wait, and advises consulting at the planning stage so that the plan can be adjusted to avoid impact on the buried property. Delay and redesign are the practical consequences worth understanding here, and they follow from a rule the project itself has to comply with. Read this with the hazard map portal, the municipal pollution complaint desks, the property register certificate and the information disclosure entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 保安林 — anyone directly benefiting can ask for a protection forest, and objections to a proposed release run thirty days
trackers.desc: A person who benefits from the forest can ask for it to be designated. Under the forest legislation, a person with a direct interest in the designation of a protection forest, or in the release of one, may request in writing, following the prescribed procedure, that a forest be designated as a protection forest or that an existing designation be released. The forestry agency's own notices define who is directly interested: the owner of the forest and others holding rights over its standing trees or land, and also a person who directly receives a benefit from the designation or whose existing benefit would be directly harmed. That second limb is the one that matters downstream — a household whose water supply or slope stability depends on the forest above it can qualify without owning a metre of it. Thirty days to object to a proposed release. Where a public notice is issued of a forest proposed for designation or of a protection forest proposed for release, a person within that same category may submit a written opinion objecting to the content of the notice — to the minister through the prefectural governor in the case of one notice, and to the governor in the case of the other — and the opinion must be delivered to the governor within thirty days of the date of the notice. That is a short, hard deadline attached to a published notice, which makes watching for the notice the practical task. A release for conversion has to buy its way out. Where the release is sought in order to put the land to a non-forest use, the applicant must attach a plan for the project or facility, a plan for the facilities that will perform the functions replacing those the protection forest currently provides, and evidence of any other licences, permits or approvals the works require; the agency's guidance also addresses proof of how the money will be raised, with exceptions for the State and for named expressway and airport companies. The replacement-function plan is the document to read closely, because it is where an application either shows how the lost protection will be reproduced or does not. Municipal and neighbour opinions are collected on a form, and gaps must be explained. Guidance provides that the opinion of the head of the interested municipality and those of directly interested persons are to be confirmed on a prescribed opinion form; and that where the applicant cannot obtain them, it must instead submit minutes showing that sufficient explanation was given, whatever opinions could be obtained, and the course of coordination so far together with the plan for further coordination. An applicant that has not spoken to the neighbours therefore has to file a document saying so. Read this with the national park land purchase and scenic land protection agreements, the national trust grant and directory, the environmental lawyers' network and the hazard map portal entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 土地収用法 — two weeks to file an opinion, a public hearing anyone interested can require, and the record you are asked to seal
trackers.desc: Two weeks of inspection, and an opinion anyone interested can file. Compulsory acquisition runs through project recognition before it reaches compensation. The operator applies for recognition to the recognising authority, which sends the application and the relevant attachments to the mayor of the municipality where the project land lies; the mayor immediately publishes the operator's name, the type of project and the project land, and makes the documents available for public inspection for two weeks. Any person with an interest in the recognition may submit a written opinion to the prefectural governor within that inspection period. The inspection period is short, it is publicised locally rather than nationally, and it is the only point at which the public purpose itself is open to challenge in writing. A public hearing can be required, and objections trigger a third-party body. Prefectural guidance records that where an interested party requests a public hearing during the inspection period, the holding of a public hearing is obligatory; and that where written opinions objecting to the recognition are submitted, the authority is obliged to seek the opinion of a third-party body such as the infrastructure development council. Both consequences follow from documents filed inside those two weeks by ordinary interested parties. Guidance also records an effort obligation to dispose of the application within three months. The record you are asked to sign becomes the basis of the compensation. Before applying for adjudication the operator prepares a land record and, for the vacation ruling, an object record, setting out the condition of each parcel and object and the rights attaching to them, with a measured plan attached. Prefectural guidance states plainly that these records become the basis for calculating the compensation in the later procedure, and that as a rule they require the signature and seal of the landowner and the related persons as well as the operator. Signing without checking the record is therefore signing the foundation of your own compensation figure. The committee is independent, and its papers are inspected too. The adjudicating body is the prefectural expropriation committee, an administrative commission of seven members appointed by the governor with the consent of the prefectural assembly from people experienced in law, economics and administration, exercising their powers independently of the governor and of any other organ. The application for adjudication and the vacation ruling application are themselves made available for inspection for two weeks in the municipality, after which the committee must begin its hearing without delay, ending in a rights-acquisition ruling and a vacation ruling, with compensation paid or deposited before rights pass. Read this with the protection forest designation route, the pollution adjudication commission, the property register certificate and the legal support centre entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 環境アセスメント — anyone may file an opinion, a month and a half to do it, and the project cannot start until the final statement is published
trackers.desc: Anyone may submit an opinion, and the window is a month and a half. The environment ministry's own guide to the assessment system states that the procedure gives the general public three opportunities to put views to the proponent. At the earliest, consideration-document stage, the proponent is to endeavour to hear opinions. At the two main stages — the scoping document setting out what will be surveyed and how, and the draft assessment setting out the results — anyone who has an opinion from the standpoint of environmental conservation may submit it in writing during the month and a half following publication of each document. There is no residence requirement and no standing test: the qualification is having an opinion about environmental conservation. Both documents are inspected for a month, with meetings the proponent must hold. Each document is publicly announced and made available for inspection for one month at local government offices, the proponent's offices and on websites, and the proponent holds explanatory meetings during the inspection period. The 2011 amendment made the meeting compulsory at scoping stage as well, on the reasoning that the documents are long and technical, so that people can hear the explanation before the survey and prediction work is done rather than after; internet publication of the documents was made compulsory at the same time. Filing at scoping is the higher-value moment: it goes to what will be studied. Opinions go into a chain that produces written answers. The proponent compiles a summary of the opinions received and sends it to the prefectural governor and the mayor; at the draft assessment stage it must send its own views on those opinions as well; the governor then gives an opinion to the proponent, taking account of the mayor's and the public's. At the final stage the statement goes to the licensing authority and the environment minister, who may give an opinion, which the licensing authority passes to the proponent before the statement is revised and finalised. A community's written opinion therefore has a documented path to an answer, not just a filing date. Two provisions worth holding on to. The project cannot be implemented until the finalised statement has been publicly announced. And where uncertainty remains in the survey and prediction, follow-up investigation after work begins is provided for, together with the policy for responding if impacts prove significant and a requirement to publish the results — which is what makes a monitoring commitment in the statement something to hold the proponent to later. Read this with the protection forest designation, the pollution adjudication commission, the compulsory acquisition entry and the environmental lawyers' network entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 裁判例検索 — six case collections including an administrative one, full-text PDFs, and the courts' own warning that not everything is there
trackers.desc: Six collections, searchable separately or together. The courts' case search system covers the supreme court reports, the high court reports, the lower court reports and separate collections for administrative cases, labour cases and intellectual property cases, each searchable on its own or through a combined search. The administrative collection is the one to start from for a dispute about a permit, a designation or an official refusal. Results list the date, the court, the branch, the type of decision and, in the administrative collection, the case type; clicking the full-text link opens the whole judgment as a document. The system warns about its own coverage, and so does everyone else. The usage guide states plainly that not all judgments are carried in the system. A national library research guide adds that party names and proper nouns may be omitted or masked and diagrams may be left out, so the text is not necessarily identical to the printed reports; a university guide is blunter still, noting that of the judgments handed down daily across more than five hundred courts, only a small fraction ever appear in reports, journals, databases or on the court website. Treat absence as no evidence either way. Recent decisions are listed separately, and the windows are short. The courts publish lists of recent supreme court and lower court decisions covering the past three months, and recent intellectual property decisions covering the past month. Checking those lists periodically is how a community notices that a comparable case has just been decided, rather than finding out when the other side cites it. Where to point it, and what else exists. Search the administrative collection for the statutes that govern the project — the assessment legislation, the compulsory acquisition statute, forest and river law — and note the decision date and case number of anything useful. The research guide also lists other public databases, including a university-run collection of older decisions and a labour commission database, for material outside the courts' own system. Read this with the compulsory acquisition entry, the assessment participation entry, the environmental lawyers' network and the pollution adjudication commission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 採石法 — the extraction plan approval, the prefecture's published list of approved sites, and the sign at the quarry entrance
trackers.desc: Every quarry needs an approved extraction plan for that specific site. The quarrying legislation requires a registered quarry operator to set an extraction plan for each rock extraction site and obtain the approval of the prefectural governor with jurisdiction over that site. The Act's stated purpose is to prevent disasters accompanying rock extraction and promote the sound development of the industry in the public interest, and it defines the rock types covered — granite, diorite, gabbro, peridotite, porphyry, diabase, trachyte, andesite, basalt, conglomerate, sandstone, shale, slate, tuff, gneiss, serpentinite, crystalline schist, bentonite, acid clay, diatomaceous earth, pottery stone, mica and vermiculite. Gravel extraction runs under separate legislation with its own plan approval, so establish which statute applies. A prefecture publishes the list of approved sites, and asks the public to report the ones not on it. One prefecture's page states that extracting rock without approval of an extraction plan is a violation attracting administrative disposition and penalties, tells anyone who has been extracting without approval to stop work immediately and contact the office, publishes a list of extraction sites approved by its regional bureau, and records that approved sites display an approval sign in a clearly visible position such as near the site entrance. It invites reports where an operator not on the list appears to be extracting. That is a resource and an instruction in one: check the list, look for the sign, report the gap. Which office decides depends on what the rock is for. The same prefecture routes applications by end use — aggregate for roads and concrete, and industrial raw materials for ceramics, casting and civil engineering, to the head office industrial siting section; building and civil engineering materials such as wall stone, pillars, paving and foundations, along with gravestones, lanterns and garden stones including decomposed granite, to the regional bureau's commerce and industry section. It also notes that approval may require procedures under other legislation, including the forest and farmland statutes. The approval test names harm to others. Published guidance records that approval is refused where extraction under the plan is found to cause danger to others, damage to public facilities, or to be contrary to the public welfare; that changes to an approved plan need a change approval, with only minor changes handled by notification; and that operators must file an annual business status report for each site with the regional economy bureau by the end of March covering the previous January to December. Ask for the plan, the change approvals and the annual report. Read this with the environmental lawyers' federation, the pollution adjudication commission, the legal support centre and the judgment search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 都市計画の縦覧 — two weeks to file a written opinion on any city plan, the reasons document beside it, and the earlier hearing stage
trackers.desc: Every city plan decision passes through a two-week public inspection, and anyone affected can file a written opinion. A prefecture's own explanation of the city planning legislation records the reason for the procedure in plain terms: a city plan decides the future shape of the city, has an extremely large effect on residents, and imposes duties and restricts rights in relation to land use, so before it is decided the content must be made widely known to residents and interested persons and their opinions reflected. It quotes the section: when a prefecture or municipality intends to decide a city plan it must give public notice and make the draft plan available for public inspection for two weeks from the date of that notice, accompanied by a document stating the reasons for the intended decision; and residents of the relevant municipalities and interested persons may submit a written opinion by the last day of the inspection period, to the prefecture for a prefectural plan and to the municipality for a municipal one. The reasons document is the part to read first — it is the authority's own justification, in writing, before the decision. Where the opinions go. Municipal pages record that submitted opinions are put before the city planning council as one of the materials for its deliberation when the plan is put to the vote, and that a written opinion needs no prescribed form but must state the name and address of the person — for a body, its name, representative and principal office — and the name of the plan being commented on. Prefectural pages publish the current inspection notices, with the drafts posted online as well as available at the counter. Watch that page rather than the noticeboard. There is an earlier stage, and it is where the shape is still open. Published explanations record that at the drafting stage the deciding body shall, where it considers it necessary, take measures to reflect residents' opinions, such as holding a public hearing; that for district plans a municipal ordinance requires the opinions of landowners and others to be sought in preparing the draft; and that where the municipal ordinance so provides, residents and interested persons may themselves propose the content of a district plan to the municipality. Explanatory meetings are commonly held, but the formal route is the written opinion. Two special cases worth knowing. The same material records that for a special block plan the consent of persons with prescribed interests must be obtained, and that for an idle land conversion promotion district the opinions of landowners and holders of prescribed use or profit rights must be heard. Read this with the assessment opinion window, the expropriation entry, the protection forest entry and the buried cultural property notice entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 保存樹 and 保存樹林 — a mayor may designate a tree or a hedge inside the city planning area, the size criteria, and the categories the law cannot reach
trackers.desc: A municipal mayor can designate a single tree, a group of trees or a hedge for preservation, inside the city planning area. The transport ministry's greenery database records that tree preservation runs both by statute and by local ordinance, and that under the 1962 law on preserving trees to maintain the aesthetic scenery of cities, the mayor designates trees or groups of trees within a city planning area. The Act provides that where the mayor finds it necessary to maintain aesthetic scenery he may designate trees or groups of trees meeting criteria set by cabinet order as a preservation tree or preservation forest, and must notify the owner of the designation. A single tree is designated as a preservation tree; a group of trees or a hedge as a preservation forest, with a marker installed. Ask the city's parks or greenery section whether the tree beside a site is already designated. The criteria are physical, and a hedge counts. A city's published criteria — carried over when designation moved from the national law to a municipal environmental conservation ordinance, with existing designations deemed made under it — record a preservation tree as one that is healthy and of particularly fine appearance and meets any of: a trunk circumference at a height of 1.5 metres of 1.5 metres or more; a height of 15 metres or more; a multi-stemmed tree 3 metres or more in height; or a climbing plant with a branch and leaf area of 30 square metres or more. A preservation forest requires a wooded area of 500 square metres or more, or a hedge forming a group of a stated length. Measure before you argue. Know what the law cannot reach. The Act provides that designation does not apply to trees designated or provisionally designated as cultural properties or forming a unit with one, to protection forests, to landscape-important trees, or to trees owned or managed by the state or a local public body. Those categories are covered by the other instruments already recorded in this country's entries — so if a tree falls outside this law, check those before concluding it is unprotected. Local practice adds reach. A city records that its designations moved to a municipal environmental conservation ordinance for comprehensive environmental protection; another publishes a city tree map of principal preservation trees and natural monuments, distributed at ward offices and service counters. The ministry's page sits inside its urban parks and green space database, which is where the national picture is kept. Read this with the protection forest entry, the city plan reading window, the buried cultural property notice and the national trust land purchase entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 河川法 permissions — taking water, occupying the riverbed, building structures or reshaping the ground all need the river manager's permission, and the four occupancy tests
trackers.desc: Five ordinary project activities inside a river area each require the river manager's permission, and the articles are numbered. A national river office's guidance, published through the ministry's regional bureaux, records that within a river area, permission under the river legislation is required to take water from the river, to use the river exclusively and monopolistically, to extract gravel or reeds, to install a structure in the river, and to change the shape of the river land — with the corresponding articles named for each. A prefecture's page adds permission for acts in a river conservation zone, and a city that manages its own rivers publishes the application forms and the rule that private or profit-making use outside the statutory categories is not available, with a separate temporary-use notification for short small events that leave the place usable by others. Where a project is abstracting, dredging, bridging or filling, the question is which of those permissions it holds. Occupancy is meant for public use, not private monopoly. The same guidance records that what may be permitted is things provided for general public use, such as parks and sports grounds, or things of high social necessity such as bridges, and that activities by which an individual continuously monopolises and uses the river are not permitted — with a narrow exception for a house entrance where there is no other access, allowed at the minimum. The ministry adds that river land occupancy is in principle limited to public bodies and that business activity is not allowed there, with a 2011 change to the occupancy permission standard letting private operators trade only where stated requirements are met, and publishes the number of such cases nationally. The four tests are the wording to quote. A regional bureau records that occupancy may be permitted only where it is unavoidable and meets the criteria, with the more public use preferred in light of local land use: that it causes no hindrance to flood control or water use; that it does not obstruct free use of the river so far as possible; that it is consistent with what the river improvement plan provides; and that it does not damage the land use situation, the landscape or other natural and social environment of the river and its surroundings. Those four are the grounds on which an objection to a riverbank development is framed. Water use applications must show the arithmetic. A metropolitan handbook on river law permissions records that an application must clarify the relationship between the river's flow volume, the intake volume applied for and the intake of related river users; identify related river users including fishery right holders; address timber floating and the passage of boats and rafts; and, where a dam is to be built, set out the present state of the land to become the reservoir and an outline of measures for those who will suffer loss from the impounding. Ask for those figures. Read this with the city plan reading window, the protection forest entry, the expropriation opinion window and the hazard map entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 漁業権 — the fishery right that lets a local cooperative exclude others from a sea area, the five-yearly fishing ground plan, and the public comment on its draft
trackers.desc: A fishery right is an exclusive right over a defined water area, held by a local body. The fisheries agency records that a fishery right is the right to conduct a specified fishery exclusively in a defined water area for a defined period, in three kinds — set-net, demarcated and common fishery rights — and that rights are established in a fishing ground plan drawn up every five years as a whole plan combining the fishery right system and the coastal fishing ground management system, and acquired by the administrative act of licensing. A prefecture puts it plainly: where a fishery right is set, the local fisheries cooperative can restrict use by people who are not its members, and it publishes the numbers of common and demarcated rights licensed in its waters together with the fishery right maps. Where a project touches inshore water, the first question is which rights cover it and who holds them. The plan is consulted on, and the maps are published. A prefecture records publishing the results of public comment on the draft of its sea-area fishing ground plan, and publishes lists of the rights in force by date; another publishes its inland-water fishery right list and the angling rules of each cooperative. For inland waters, a prefecture records that the governor first hears the opinion of the inland fishing ground management committee in setting the area and the species covered, then licenses the cooperative for that area, with a stated number of cooperatives holding a stated number of rights.
