Those documents identify the right-holder by name and area. The holders carry duties, which is why they are useful allies. Published legislative analysis records that a cooperative licensed with a fifth-kind common fishery right in inland waters is placed under a duty to propagate aquatic animals and plants so the resource is not exhausted, funding stocking and fishing-ground management from angling fees and members' rights-exercise fees; and the fisheries agency records that rights are licensed in preference to existing holders who are using the ground appropriately and effectively, with new licences going, after hearing the opinions of the fishermen concerned, to whoever is judged to contribute most to local fisheries. One official instruction is worth knowing before a reclamation is proposed. The agency's guidance on drawing up sea-area plans records as improper any condition that would limit the licence period in anticipation of future reclamation works, or bar the holder from seeking compensation for fishery damage from such works, as departing from the purposes of the Act. Read this with the river law permissions, the city plan display window, the protection forest entry and the national trust purchase entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 鳥獣保護区 and 特別保護地区 — the reserve anyone can ask for, the special zone where building, reclamation and tree felling need permission, and the public hearing before designation or renewal
trackers.desc: Inside a special protection zone, the acts a project depends on need prior permission. Prefectural guidance records that within a wildlife protection area a special protection zone may be designated, and that in that zone hunting is prohibited and certain development acts are regulated: new construction, reconstruction or extension of structures, reclamation or draining of water surfaces, and felling of trees and bamboo — with the environment ministry adding that these require the designating authority's prior permission. Another prefecture's page records the same list and directs anyone contemplating development to check first whether the site falls inside a regulated area. That check is the first step where a site is near wetland or forest. There are two designating authorities and seven categories of reserve. The guidance records that wildlife protection areas are designated either by the environment minister as national reserves or by the prefectural governor as prefectural reserves; and that reserves come in seven designation categories, of which one prefecture uses three: forest wildlife habitat reserves, reserves for colonial migratory arrival sites protecting migratory birds and marine mammals, and reserves for familiar local wildlife habitat serving the formation of a rich living environment. Naming the category that fits a site is how a designation request is framed. Designation and renewal go through a public hearing, publicly announced. A prefecture publishes its notice of a public hearing on renewal of wildlife protection areas, stating that it is made under the named subsections of the Act governing reserves and special protection zones; another records that a straight renewal without boundary change does not require referral to the nature conservation council, which tells you when the council step applies. Reserves run for a stated maximum term, and the special zone's term sits inside the reserve's. Where to look, and what to file. A metropolitan authority publishes an annual map of wildlife protection areas and restricted hunting-implement zones, sold to the public and issued to registered hunters, alongside the permission criteria and instructions for preparing a permission application in two copies; the ministry's regional offices publish the application windows for acts inside national special protection zones. A birdwatching organisation's summary records the separate species preservation legislation, which designates rare species and habitat protection areas, with duties on landowners and a public proposal system for listing a species. Read this with the protection forest entry, the fishery rights entry, the city plan display window and the river law entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 重要里地里山 — the five hundred sites the ministry selected as important for biodiversity, the nature conservation society that works them, and the new certified activity plans that unlock one-stop procedures
trackers.desc: Five hundred named places are on a national list of secondary landscapes important for biodiversity. The environment ministry records that it positioned the traditional village-and-woodland landscape as an environment to be left to the next generation and selected five hundred sites as important for biodiversity conservation, to make them widely known and to be used in local branding of produce and in tourism; and records that its selection was intended to raise the effectiveness of conservation and use by diverse actors. Its background pages record that these landscapes — farmland, ponds, woodland and grassland between the deep mountains and the city — make up about forty per cent of the national land area and serve food and timber supply, landscape, water source recharge and land conservation, contact with nearby nature and the transmission of culture. If a project's site is on that list, the listing is a documented national judgement about the place. A national conservation society works these landscapes and lobbies on them. The nature conservation society records that it investigates the causes of decline and effective conservation measures, carries out on-site conservation and makes policy proposals; that its survey results show the sharpest decline among farmland species; that it lobbies for support to farming that contributes to biodiversity, including a submission to the agriculture vice-minister on amendment of the food and agriculture basic legislation; and that it runs named local projects, from invasive species removal in reservoir ponds to maintaining and restoring valley paddies for an endangered raptor at the top of that ecosystem. The 2024 framework adds certified plans and agreements with landowners. Ministry material on the new legislation records that a company or other body may draw up an activity plan for maintaining, recovering or creating biodiversity — conserving these landscapes, controlling invasive species, protecting rare species — and have it certified by the competent minister; that a certified body obtains one-stop and simplified procedures under the natural parks, nature conservation, species preservation, wildlife protection, invasive species, forest and urban green space legislation; and that a certified municipality may conclude a biodiversity maintenance agreement with landowners. Those agreements and certifications are a route for a community body to secure ground it does not own. Read this with the national trust grant, the trusts directory, the protection forest entry and the wildlife protection area entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 住民監査請求 and 住民訴訟 — one resident can demand an audit of a local authority's spending, and only someone who did so may then sue to stop it
trackers.desc: One resident, acting alone, can demand an audit of a local authority's financial acts. The ministry's own explanatory material records the system as one whereby residents of a local authority, in respect of illegal or improper financial accounting acts or omissions by its executive organs or staff, prevent or correct them so as to protect the interests of all residents, and records that anyone with legal capacity may make the request, natural person or corporation, and may do so alone — unlike the separate signature-gathering route. The statute provides that a resident who considers there is illegal or improper expenditure of public money, acquisition, management or disposal of property, conclusion or performance of a contract, or assumption of a debt or other obligation — including where such an act is predicted with considerable certainty — or an illegal or improper failure to levy or collect public money or to manage property, may, attaching documents proving it, request the audit commissioners to audit and to take measures to prevent or correct the act, or to make good the loss the authority suffered. Where a project runs on the local authority's money, that is a route that does not require the resident to be personally harmed. The audit request is a precondition to the lawsuit, and the clock is one year. Published material records that only a person who has made the residents' audit request may bring the residents' suit, and that the request cannot be made once one year has passed from the day the act was done or completed, except with justifiable reason — a municipality's own page giving natural disaster cutting off transport as its example. The suit can seek an injunction, and it is filed within thirty days. The statute provides that where the resident is dissatisfied with the commissioners' audit result, recommendation or the authority's measures, or where the commissioners fail to audit within the statutory period, or the authority fails to take the recommended measures, the resident may sue, and lists as the first form of relief a demand that the executive organ or staff member be enjoined from all or part of the act. Published commentary records the thirty-day filing windows tied to each of those triggers; records that the suit lies exclusively in the district court for the authority's office; and records the one limit worth knowing — an injunction may not issue where stopping the act would risk grave harm to human life or body or otherwise seriously obstruct the public welfare. Read this with the audit board entry, the information disclosure entry, the expropriation opinion window and the city plan display entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 生物多様性センター — the national vegetation survey mapped at 1:25,000, the specific plant community survey with its selection criteria, and the databases of giant trees and important wetlands
trackers.desc: The environment ministry's biodiversity centre runs and publishes the national baseline surveys. Its own pages record that it carries out basic surveys and monitoring of the country's vegetation, the distribution of animals and plants, rivers and lakes, tidal flats and coral reefs; its natural environment survey index carries a data usage page to read first, a survey catalogue, and the survey rounds by year. Where a project's assessment claims a habitat is unremarkable, these are the national surveys it should be measured against. The vegetation survey is mapped, and its scale changed part way. The centre records the vegetation survey as producing vegetation maps expressing phytosociologically classified community units on topographic maps; that the original scale for the second through fifth rounds was one to fifty thousand, and one to twenty-five thousand from the sixth round on; that nationwide paper vegetation maps were produced in the second and third rounds, with altered areas surveyed in the fourth and fifth; and that the published data integrates the fourth and fifth rounds' alteration information into the existing vegetation map from the second and third. It records the data viewable through the natural environment information system and in a mapping application format. The specific plant community survey states the criteria a site is judged against. The centre records this survey as selecting plant communities meeting stated criteria, by prefecture and with regional character considered, to grasp their distribution, growth and change; and lists among the criteria virgin forest or near-natural forest, with particular care that evergreen broadleaf forest is not omitted, and plant communities or populations distributed in only a few domestic locations and extremely rare. Where a stand of forest is at issue, those are the words to test it against. The centre's other databases are named and public. Its pages list a giant tree and giant tree forest database, endangered species information, bird breeding information, a seabird colony database, marine biodiversity information, the five hundred important wetlands of the country, animal distribution maps by class, and a creature log and creature map, alongside the monitoring sites programme, with maintenance windows announced. Read this with the important satoyama sites, the protection forest entry, the wildlife protection areas and the protected trees entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The municipalities and greening promotion corporations that buy green space — who is obliged to purchase when an owner demands it, the tax reliefs, and the subsidy that funds the purchase
trackers.desc: Where the designation blocks development, the owner can require the authority to buy the land. A metropolitan authority records that in a special green space conservation district, where the restriction on acts causes marked hindrance to use of the land, the owner may apply to the ward or city — or, in town and village areas, the metropolis — for the land to be purchased, and that the metropolis, the municipality or a green space conservation and greening promotion corporation is then to buy it. A city records the same, arising where a permission application within the district is refused and the land use is markedly hindered. For a community wanting a wooded parcel kept, the route runs through the designation and then the owner's own purchase demand. The tax reliefs are the argument to put to the owner. Published material records that on such a sale twenty million yen of the transfer income is deducted, reducing income tax, a city adding the corporate equivalent of the smaller of the gain or that sum deducted as a loss. It records that designation gives the owner an eighty per cent reduction in inheritance tax valuation for mountain forest and wild land, and property tax reduced by up to one half, and that a management agreement can reduce the burden of managing the land. The citizens' green space contract is the lighter instrument beside it. The tax authority records the scheme as one where, mainly on the application of the landowner, a local authority or a green space conservation and greening promotion corporation concludes a contract with the owner, establishes green space or greening facilities for residents' use on that land and manages them, supporting owners who provide their own land for residents' use; and records that land under a qualifying contract is valued at twenty per cent below the ordinary valuation. Published material records the contract terms as covering the area of land, the method of management, the management period and measures on breach, with a twenty per cent inheritance tax valuation reduction where the contract period is twenty years or more. Public money exists for the purchase itself. The metropolitan authority records a subsidy toward purchase of land in a special green space conservation district including planned designation land, and construction of facilities for conserving and using the green space, at up to one half of eligible costs, administered through a named public interest foundation with published application guidance. Read this with the city plan display, the important satoyama sites, the residents' audit request and the crowdfunding entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 日本自然保護協会 NACS-J — the society founded to stop a dam, its own scientific surveys behind formal opinions, and the observation leader training that has produced tens of thousands of surveyors
trackers.desc: The country's oldest nature conservation body was founded out of a dam fight. Published description records its predecessor formed in 1949 to protect a named marshland threatened with submersion by a hydroelectric dam plan, and the society established in 1951 as the country's first nature protection organisation; and records the trigger for its founding as a sulphur mining proposal inside a national park's planned special protection zone, with the fear that such development would spread nationwide during postwar reconstruction. It records the society since then submitting opinions and policy proposals based on its own independent scientific surveys against environmental destruction across the country. An opinion backed by the organisation's own survey is what a hearing responds to. It trains ordinary people as observation leaders, at scale. The environment ministry's own page records the society's nature observation leader training course, held nationwide since the late 1970s, and records that graduates run observation sessions, conduct surveys and education programmes jointly with local authorities, and that attendance at leader-run observation events is estimated at 1.3 million people a year; published description records more than thirty thousand people having taken the course. The society records that registration makes the person a member, bringing a bimonthly conservation journal and member prices, and that leaders may join prefecture-level training and the society's survey programmes. Its citizen survey programmes are the data side of that. Published description records the society running citizen-participation environmental monitoring surveys in the countryside, a thousand-site monitoring programme's rural survey, and citizen participation surveys of local ecosystem services. It records a named high-speed railway project among its standing issues, and records itself as funded by donations, with a stated monthly giving level, a legacy and estate giving route, and named corporate members. Read this with the national trust grant, the trusts directory, the environmental lawyers and the biodiversity centre entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The bar federation's human rights committee — the body that investigates a complaint and issues warnings to whoever is responsible, with a follow-up inquiry six months later
trackers.desc: A citizen can ask the bar association to investigate and issue a formal opinion against the body responsible. The federation records the procedure as one in which its human rights committee receives applications from victims of, or people connected to, a rights violation, investigates the alleged facts, and — where it finds a violation or a risk of one — takes measures against the violator or its supervising body, aiming at removal or improvement of the violation. It lists the measures as warning (notifying its opinion and strongly demanding appropriate action), recommendation (conveying its opinion and requesting appropriate action), request (conveying its opinion and asking for appropriate action), statement of opinion, advice and cooperation. It states plainly that these measures carry no legal compulsion, but have influence as the legal judgment of the bar, and that the procedure allows a legal judgment to be sought on matters that do not sit easily in court procedure but where the need for relief is high in the light of justice. For a community whose grievance will not fit a lawsuit, that distinction is the reason to use it. The limits and the follow-up are both published. The federation records that, unlike the police, its investigative powers and methods have limits and it cannot compel questioning, but that when it requests an investigation of the necessary people or institutions an answer is obtained in most cases. It records that since April 2009, in cases where a warning, recommendation or request has been issued, it asks each recipient after a set period — currently six months — what action they took, and makes a further inquiry where the answer is insufficient. The filing requirements are light, and the venue rule is stated. Bar associations record that there is no fixed form — handwritten or typed is acceptable — and that the application should set out the specific facts so that when, where, who, what and how are clear; they record that an application should as a rule be made to the bar association where the applicant lives, that cases may be transferred to another prefecture's association where that would handle them better, and that a preliminary investigation and a full investigation each aim to conclude within six months. Read this with the environmental lawyers, the pollution dispute commission, the free consultations and the residents' audit entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 日本野鳥の会の野鳥保護区 — a society that buys breeding habitat outright or protects it by agreement with the owner, with the area, the sites and the species counted
trackers.desc: Buying the land is stated here as the most effective answer to development, and the society has been doing it since 1986. The society records that to protect these birds from extinction and respond quickly to advancing development, securing the breeding grounds by purchase is the most effective method, and that as a non-governmental organisation it began pioneering the movement of buying breeding grounds and making them its own bird protection areas in 1986, with the crane programme from 1987 and the fish owl programme from 2004. It records the reserves as established by land purchase or by agreement with the owner, with alteration of the natural environment and entry strictly restricted and environmental maintenance continuing after designation. For a community weighing whether purchase is realistic, this is a domestic body that has done it repeatedly, and says why. The totals are published and broken down. A published release records that after one purchase the total area of reserves owned or held by agreement reached 3,662 hectares — 2,463 for the crane, 1,167 for the fish owl and 32 other — and that with 132 hectares of important fish owl habitat conserved under memoranda with landowners the conserved area came to 3,794 hectares, described as the largest private nature reserve area in the country for the conservation of endangered species. The society's own pages give the current figure as more than 4,000 hectares nationwide. One reserve programme records, at a stated date, 23 sites totalling 2,799.7 hectares used by 31 breeding pairs. The work continues after the purchase, and one recovery is documented. A sanctuary's pages record a reserve where a pair nested every year until 1993, then stopped from 1994 because upstream hill development and straightening of the river caused sediment to accumulate and alder to spread; records alder felling from 1999 to restore the reed beds suitable for nesting; and records breeding confirmed again from 2002. A national committee's listing records the project as establishing private reserves by purchase or owner agreement at 36 sites nationwide, continuing to target habitat of rare birds that has no legal protection and is at risk from development. Read this with the trust association grants, the green space purchase route, the nature conservation society and the protected species entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 公害弁連 — the national liaison of pollution and public-works legal teams, its member teams named case by case, and the victims' organisations that act with them
trackers.desc: The lawyers who run these cases are organised into one national body, and its member teams are named. The liaison records itself as a cross-cutting organisation of the legal teams behind the movements and lawsuits over pollution, the environment and large public works being fought across the country, and records its founding in 1972, out of a pollution research gathering, to build more practical legal theory suited to court practice, to establish mutual exchange of experience and a support system between legal teams, and to strengthen links with victims, support organisations and researchers. For a community that needs counsel who have run this kind of case before, that is a directory of teams rather than a list of firms. Its published fields show what it has actually litigated. It records having extended from the four great pollution trials and an airport noise case into water pollution, soil contamination, air pollution, airport and base noise, high-speed railway pollution, food contamination, pharmaceutical harm and road pollution, and more recently waste and dioxin problems; and records its work as centred on damages claims and injunction claims aimed at relief for victims and eradication of pollution, latterly with environmental restoration of the places pollution destroyed also in view. Injunctions, not only damages, is the part that matters to a community trying to stop something. Its member teams and the victims' organisations are listed by name. Its own assembly papers list named legal teams with their secretaries — including teams for a cadmium disease, several mercury poisoning suits, a high-speed railway pollution case, a national highway case and a contaminated cooking oil case — and a liaison of plaintiff groups in base noise litigation. A published list of a national victims' action committee records its member organisations by name, including disease countermeasure councils, patients' and families' associations in named cities, asbestos plaintiff groups in four regions and a reclamation-related suit's plaintiffs. The bar federation's own committee — separate from these teams — records treating serious harm to life and body from pollution as a human rights problem, with a committee established in 1969 and renamed in 1985, producing research, written opinions, symposia and publications. Read this with the bar federation's relief procedure, the environmental lawyers, the pollution dispute commission and the nature conservation society entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The IUCN Japan committee's member directory and the conservation organisation links — named national bodies with what each does, including a campaign centre for a single contested bay
trackers.desc: A national committee publishes a directory of its member conservation organisations, each with a line on what it actually does. The committee records itself as the liaison body for domestic organisations belonging to the international conservation union, established in 1980, and its member pages describe organisations one by one: a sea turtle association working on nesting surveys, unified tagging and a national conference, linking individuals, organisations and institutions across the country; a wildlife conservation research group aiming at coexistence, working on conservation theory, prevention of excessive commercial use of wildlife, and wildlife conservation education; and a business federation nature conservation fund supporting non-governmental conservation work at home and abroad and promoting companies' biodiversity efforts. For a community that needs a specialist body rather than a general one, a described directory is the shortcut. One member exists for a single contested bay, which is the model worth noting. The directory records a campaign centre whose stated purpose is demanding that two named governments implement the international union's recommendations and resolutions on protecting the dugong of a named prefecture, and, through establishing a dugong protection area in a named bay, advancing local revitalisation. A single-issue body with an international resolution behind it is a template. The bird society's link page is a second directory, weighted to local groups. It lists, with descriptions, a research organisation collecting nationwide bird information with amateur observers and building protection measures on it; an oceanic wildlife society; a council promoting nature experience activities; a national liaison conference against wild bird poaching with a poaching hotline page; a bird protection federation publishing survey results; and a local club protecting the area around a named wildlife protection area, alongside regional bird societies. Read this with the nature conservation society, the bird reserves, the trust association grants and the pollution legal teams entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: トトロのふるさと基金 — a local trust buying hillside parcels since 1990, with the site count, area and purchase price published, and a petition of 31,255 signatures handed to a city mayor
trackers.desc: A local foundation buys hillside land parcel by parcel, and publishes what each purchase cost. It records beginning national trust activity — buying land — in 1990, and states the difficulty plainly: land prices in these hills close to the capital are high, so the area acquired is by no means large, the aim being to show citizens' conservation work widely to society and, from that beginning, to have a wider area conserved. Published reporting records one purchase of a 6,112 square metre privately owned woodland in a named city for 22 million yen, in an area adjoining a regulating pond built by the prefecture, an oak-dominated coppice where racoon dogs, foxes, and dragonflies and frogs that favour wetland live. For a community weighing whether buying is realistic, a published price per parcel is the most useful number there is. The totals are published and they are modest, which is the point. That reporting records the trust land managed and conserved as 67 sites across one prefecture and the neighbouring metropolis, totalling about 135,700 square metres; an earlier account records more than one billion yen of donations, 56 sites and about 10 hectares at the thirtieth anniversary, when a master plan aiming at conservation of the whole hill range was announced. The managing director is quoted that development pressure is intensifying in the surroundings, so conserving the forest matters for the wetland creatures of the hills. Purchase is followed by survey, then volunteers. The same reporting records that after acquisition the foundation carries out a survey of current conditions including the surrounding environment, decides a management policy, and proceeds with conservation work such as undergrowth cutting with the cooperation of volunteers. Its own pages record a volunteer registration briefing and record it having submitted 31,255 signatures to a named city's mayor to protect a wood and its path. It publishes its postcode, prefecture, city, district and building number with telephone and fax. Read this with the trust association grants, the bird reserves, the green space purchase route and the nature conservation society entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: A prefectural green trust association and its prefectural fund — donations that buy land outright, fourteen conservation sites managed with volunteers, and six donation routes including fee-free bank transfer
trackers.desc: A prefecture runs a trust movement whose whole purpose is buying land with residents' donations. The prefecture records the movement as one that widely solicits donations from residents and uses them as funds to acquire land and other property, so that the prefecture's outstanding natural and valuable historical environments are preserved far into the future as property held in common by residents. It records the association established in 1984 as the promotion body for a movement led by residents, and the fund established in the prefecture the following year as the movement's financial source, the two now working as one. For a community trying to raise money to buy a threatened site, a prefectural fund whose stated pillars are land purchase and conservation management is the nearest instrument recorded in this file. The sites, the area and the acquisition cost are published. The association records having acquired its first site in 1990 and now managing and operating fourteen trust conservation sites within the prefecture together with volunteer staff, and publishes a guide covering every site. Published description records about 75 hectares across fourteen sites acquired as of 2024, and records the first site — a slope forest around a named paddy area — as acquired in 1990 and 1991 at a cost of about 716 million yen. A published figure for what a purchase costs is rare and worth having. Giving is made deliberately easy, and it is tax-deductible. The association records six ways to give to the fund, including a donation application form allowing fee-free transfer at the counter of any nearby financial institution in the prefecture — city banks, regional banks, trust banks, credit unions, credit cooperatives, the prefectural agricultural credit federation, agricultural cooperatives and labour banks; and records that donations to the fund are donations to the prefecture and therefore attract tax deductions. It records the association carrying out conservation management of the sites under commission from the prefecture, alongside a newsletter and nature observation meetings, with volunteers involved from the planning stage. Read this with the citizens' trust entries, the bird reserves, the green space purchase route and the trust association grants entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Prefectural bar association legal consultation centres — around 300 walk-in centres run by the bar associations, some free, with island centres listed by name and a booking line per prefecture
trackers.desc: The bar associations run walk-in consultation centres, and their locations and phone numbers are published one by one. A metropolitan centre list names centres by district — including centres in named wards and suburban cities, and three island centres sharing a single booking number — each with its own telephone line, an online booking marker, and the bar association that runs it. It records that the centres are legal consultation offices operated by the three bar associations established in the metropolis under the lawyers' legislation, and that because a public body runs them and lawyers handle the consultations, they can be used with confidence. For a resident who needs a lawyer and does not know one, an address and a number in their own ward is the whole problem solved. The national scale and the price are stated. The federation records that the centres are operated by the bar associations of which all lawyers in the country are members; that consultations are held at around 300 locations nationwide, beginning with the bar association halls; that a consultation runs roughly 30 minutes; and that the fee varies by area and subject but should be assumed to be around 5,500 yen. It records that some centres make all consultations free, and that depending on the type of consultation and your financial circumstances you may be able to consult without charge. Knowing the default price and that free slots exist is what lets a household decide before it walks in. The booking routes are published for the whole country. The federation records an internet reservation service allowing 24-hour booking at bar association centres, and a single nationwide telephone number that routes a caller to their local bar association's desk, with a business service under which the first 30-minute consultation is free except in named prefectures where it costs 5,500 yen. A prefectural bar association records that lawyers who have taken its designated training handle those consultations, and publishes guides to consultation fees and lawyers' fees. Read this with the pollution legal teams, the bar federation's relief procedure, the legal support centre and the conservation directories entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Prefectural pollution examination boards — mediation, conciliation and arbitration in 37 prefectures with 9 to 15 commissioners, closed hearings, and municipal complaint counters as the step before
trackers.desc: A prefecture's own board handles pollution disputes, and its composition is published. One prefecture records its board as an auxiliary body of the governor established under the pollution dispute settlement legislation for the purpose of processing pollution disputes, composed of ten commissioners including lawyers and people of academic standing, with a named department as secretariat, and records that when conciliation is applied for, commissioners designated by the board chairman form a conciliation committee to handle the dispute. It records the board's jurisdiction as mediation, conciliation and arbitration in disputes other than those handled by the national commission — serious cases, wide-area cases and cross-prefectural cases, defining serious cases to include air or water pollution causing marked harm to human health affecting a considerable number of people, and cross-prefectural cases as those spanning several prefectures, where application is made to any one governor. It records the system as simple, quick and inexpensive compared with civil litigation, and with specialists in law and pollution. The national office publishes how many prefectures have a standing board. The national commission records that under the legislation a prefecture may establish a pollution examination board by ordinance, that these carry out mediation, conciliation and arbitration, that 37 prefectures have established boards with not fewer than 9 and not more than 15 commissioners appointed, and that prefectures without a standing board appoint candidate examiners and keep a list, convening a temporary body whenever a case arises. The step before the board is the municipal complaint counter. The national commission records that pollution complaint counters are established in prefectures and in municipalities, and directs that complaints about pollution should be raised with the counsellor at the municipal or prefectural complaint counter, by telephone or letter. A metropolitan board records the sequence plainly: where a complaint to the ward or city counter has passed a considerable period without prospect of resolution, or where third-party mediation would help talks progress, the prefectural board mediates. It records proceedings as closed, so that parties can speak frankly, and records that conciliation cannot order specific measures. Read this with the pollution legal teams, the bar consultation centres, the prefectural green trust and the bird reserves entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Municipal vacant house and land banks — a council-run matching register listing empty houses and plots, free to list and to browse, with the residency conditions and the legality check spelled out
trackers.desc: Municipalities run registers matching owners of empty houses and land with people who want them. Published description records the scheme as a matching system for vacant houses and vacant land, with information provided by municipalities across the country, in which the responsible department of each local authority acts as the counter connecting owners who want to sell or rent with people who want to buy or rent. It records that in many municipalities, registration on the bank and viewing property information are free, while a licensed real estate agent brokers the actual sale or lease, so the usual brokerage commission applies. For a community trying to bring a derelict building or an empty plot into use, a council-run list with no listing fee is a different starting point from an open market. The legality of the property is checked before listing. The same description records that in principle the property must not violate related legislation such as the building standards law and the city planning law, and recommends confirming in advance with the relevant municipality's building counter or city planning counter whether the building's location and structure are lawful, before applying to register. That check, made at a municipal counter before anything is signed, is the step this file would tell a buyer not to skip. Use may be restricted to incomers, and the steps are published. A ministry page records that some municipalities position the scheme as promoting migration and limit it to applicants from outside the prefecture or municipality, so conditions differ and must be confirmed with each authority. Published description sets out the sequence: search the listings; apply for user registration with the municipality; receive detailed information such as the address and interior condition, released to registered users; view the property, shown by a licensed agent and sometimes with the owner present; submit a negotiation application; then negotiate price and terms through that agent to contract and handover. It records that some municipalities make renovation or demolition subsidies conditional on registration. Read this with the prefectural green trust, the pollution examination boards, the bar consultation centres and the local trust entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The city planning proposal system — residents, landowners and community NPOs can put a plan to the council themselves, with a half-hectare area, two-thirds consent and a prefectural pre-consultation desk
trackers.desc: A community group can propose a city plan rather than only object to one. A prefecture records that, as neighbourhood-building efforts led by local people through community councils have grown, landowners, community-building non-profit corporations and development operators meeting stated requirements may now propose city plans to the prefecture or the municipality. It records the requirements as an integrated area of land of 0.5 hectares or more; conformity with the legal standards on city planning, including the policy for the improvement, development and preservation of the city planning area; and the consent of two-thirds or more of the landowners and holders of comparable rights, counted both by number of people and by area. Proposing the plan is a different posture from objecting to somebody else's. Who counts as a proposer, and what may be proposed, are listed. A city records eligible proposers as persons holding ownership or a registered superficies or lease right for the purpose of owning a building in the area; non-profit corporations and public-interest corporations whose purpose is promoting community building; and bodies with experience and knowledge of community building as defined by ministry ordinance, including named public agencies. Another city records that proposals may cover almost all city planning content except the area master plan, including zoning and district plans, and lists the documents required as a proposal stating the proposer's name and address, and landowners' consent forms with copies of the cadastral map and the land register attached. There is a pre-consultation desk, and a route by which a refusal must still go to the council. A prefecture records that it has set up a consultation desk to make proposal procedures run smoothly, checking proposal requirements, content and conformity with planning standards, and advising proposers to use it at as early a stage as possible. A city records that where a proposal leads to a plan, the city submits the plan and its draft to the city planning council; and that where it decides not to make the plan, it must still put the draft to that council and have the decision not to proceed made there. Read this with the city planning inspection period, the land expropriation opinion window, the municipal vacant house banks and the greening corporations entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Information Disclosure System (open.go.kr)
trackers.desc: South Korea's official information-disclosure portal — public access-to-information requests to executive agencies. — Holds to account: public bodies that hold records — find how to request records and what's been released.

trackers.name: EIASS — Environmental Impact Assessment Support System
trackers.desc: South Korea's public EIA information system, run under the environment ministry: every strategic, full, and small-scale environmental assessment, its documents, and the consultation status — opened to the public without login. You CAN get: the assessment documents for a development near you, real-time consultation progress, and the record of supplements and returns (the environment ministry's returns have stalled projects as big as the Jeju second airport for years). You CAN'T get: the approval agency's internal deliberations. For activists: this is where you read the proponent's own study, find its gaps, and time your opinion submissions to the statutory windows.

trackers.name: Friends of the Earth Asia Pacific
trackers.desc: The Asia Pacific regional structure of Friends of the Earth International, formed in 2008, whose member groups work on community-based struggles against destructive projects, particularly mining and other extractive industries, alongside Indigenous peoples, peasant farmers, fisherfolk and trade unions. WHO TO ENLIST: the national member group nearest the project. In this region Friends of the Earth International's own directory names groups in Bangladesh (BELA, the Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers' Association), India, Indonesia (WALHI), Japan, Malaysia (Sahabat Alam Malaysia), Nepal, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines (the Legal Rights and Natural Resources Center), South Korea and Sri Lanka. You CAN: reach an organisation that already works community-side in your own country, and draw regional weight onto a local fight. For activists: in several of these countries the Friends of the Earth affiliate is the most experienced community-side environmental body there is.

trackers.desc: South Korea's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. trackers.name: Government Public Ethics Committee (PETI) — Property Registration
trackers.desc: National asset-declaration system; South Korea’s Public Ethics Committee runs property registration under the Public Service Ethics Act, with top officials’ assets publicly disclosed, South Korea.

trackers.name: 환경법률센터 — Environmental Law Center
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a dedicated environmental legal centre whose stated purpose is to act as a partner on environmental problems that cannot be solved by an individual alone. THE PART THAT MAKES IT REACHABLE: it sits inside 환경운동연합 (KFEM, the Korean Federation for Environmental Movement) alongside the Citizens' Institute for Environmental Studies, and KFEM has 54 grassroots local organisations across the country — so a community can come to legal help through its own local chapter instead of approaching a law centre cold.

trackers.name: 환경운동연합 (KFEM) — 54 local organisations
trackers.desc: THE NATIONAL BODY WITH LOCAL PRESENCE: KFEM comprises 54 grassroots local organisations across Korea, together with the Citizens' Institute for Environmental Studies and the 환경법률센터 (Environmental Law Center), and works with allied specialist bodies. USE IT: for a site-specific fight, start with the local chapter — it is the route into research and legal support that already has people near the site.

trackers.name: 원고적격 — the standing barrier in Korean environmental cases
trackers.desc: KNOW THIS BEFORE PLANNING A CASE. Korean administrative litigation requires the plaintiff to show a 법률상 이익 — a legally protected interest — and environmental harm characteristically does not crystallise immediately into a concrete infringement, so ordinary standing and ripeness requirements sit badly on environmental cases. ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATIONS DO NOT CURRENTLY HAVE STANDING to sue on behalf of the environment itself. Scholarship proposes granting it to bodies with the expertise and structure to carry it, under statutory criteria and with court permission, and a legislative notice proposed widening 법률상 이익 to 법적 이익 so the constitutional environmental right could ground an administrative remedy — but that is a reform proposal, not present law. The Seoraksan cable car case is the standard illustration of how far current administrative litigation falls short of preventing damage to the natural environment. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: build the case around individually affected residents who can show their own legal interest — an association cannot stand in for nature here, which is the opposite of the German position.

trackers.name: 한국내셔널트러스트 — buy the land with citizens' donations
trackers.desc: AN ORGANISATION WHOSE BUSINESS IS BUYING LAND THAT DEVELOPMENT WOULD OTHERWISE TAKE. The National Trust of Korea exists to preserve natural and cultural heritage at risk of disappearing through development projects, by purchasing or securing the sites with citizens' donations. Its first 시민유산 (citizens' heritage) site was the Maehwamareum colony on Ganghwa Island — a paddy wetland holding an endangered plant, designated a Ramsar site in 2008. By 2020 it held 11 citizens' heritage sites (8 natural, 3 cultural) covering 136,106 square metres, funded by about 7.84 billion won in citizen donations, including the Yeoncheon DMZ crane habitat. THE LEGAL POINT THAT MATTERS MOST: sites secured as citizens' heritage are guaranteed the principle of inalienability (양도불능의 원칙), which makes permanent preservation possible — land bought this way cannot simply be sold on, which is the difference between a purchase and a protection. HOW IT WORKS IN PRACTICE: sites are identified by the organisation or reported by the public, citizen and expert opinion is taken, the board decides, and purchase money is then raised through citizen fundraising campaigns, major donors and corporate sponsorship. You can also donate or entrust land or buildings directly, and donations attract year-end tax deduction as a designated public-interest donation body. Contact 02-3675-3401~2, ntfund@naver.com. Internationally the movement is linked through INTO, founded December 2007 across around 30 countries, though each national trust is independent.

trackers.name: 녹색서울실천사업 — Seoul's green grant, and it bars repeat winners
trackers.desc: A CITY GRANT WHERE CIVIC GROUPS PROPOSE THEIR OWN PROJECTS. Seoul's 일반사업 track is explicitly for civic organisations to put forward original projects for environmental improvement and awareness and to lead them themselves, alongside a designated track on city-chosen themes. Judging is by the city's local subsidy management committee on three criteria: suitability of purpose and content, the organisation's capacity to deliver, and the reasonableness of the budget. THE RULE THAT FAVOURS NEWCOMERS: organisations selected 3 years running, or 4 or more times in 5 years, are excluded — the reverse of the usual pattern where track record is an advantage, and it means a new or small group faces less entrenched competition here than in most schemes. MECHANICS: applications go only through the local subsidy system 보탬e (losims.go.kr) — no paper or email route — in a window of about 3 weeks once a year, with the 2026 round running 12 January to 3 February and results announced in February. WIDER ROUTES: the integrated subsidy portal 보조금통합포털, the Ministry of the Interior and Safety's NPAS support programme for non-profit private organisations, and the Ministry of Environment's open call for nature conservation organisations.

trackers.name: 내셔널트러스트 문화유산기금 — buys the building, and takes tip-offs about threatened ones
trackers.desc: Four routes in, and one of them is simply telling them a place is at risk. The Foundation buys sites and buildings outright and holds them permanently as 시민문화유산, citizen heritage; it finds targets itself or acts on a public tip-off (제보), takes citizen and expert opinion, and its board decides. Purchase money is then raised by citizen fundraising campaigns, by finding individual benefactors and through corporate sponsorship — so what a community has to bring is the case, not the money. The other three routes matter because none of them requires a sale. You can donate a building or site or place it in trust; you can hand over management alone (관리위탁), permanently or for a fixed term, keeping ownership, where a place of high value is one you cannot look after; or you can register as a linked site under a joint preservation agreement. The precedent is exactly this map's situation. 최순우 옛집 in Seongbuk-dong, Seoul had already been contracted to a developer and was about to become a villa block as the district converted to multi-family housing; the family sold to the trust in December 2002 instead, and it opened as the first citizen heritage in 2004 — the Foundation's own office is now inside it. Two limits, both large. This is cultural heritage rather than land, and there are three citizen heritage properties in twenty years — 최순우 옛집, 도래마을 옛집 and 권진규 아틀리에, all buildings. A community trying to hold a forest or a wetland needs a different body, and the natural-environment side of the Korean movement sits at nationaltrust.or.kr, which is behind a bot-detection wall and could not be verified here. Donations attract a year-end tax deduction; the Foundation is a designated public-interest donation body. 02-3675-3401~2, ntfund@naver.com, 9 Seongbuk-ro 15-gil, Seongbuk-gu, Seoul 02880. The site serves over plain http with no TLS, so send nothing sensitive through its forms.

trackers.name: 녹색법률센터 Green Legal Centre — took a Korean wind farm to a German supply-chain regulator
trackers.desc: The move to study is the one it made against a wind farm at Muan. A 200-metre turbine was installed 280 metres from homes in Muan county, South Jeolla, with residents reporting low-frequency noise and shadow flicker. Rather than stopping at the Korean planning and noise route, the centre pursued the German manufacturer that supplied the generator, whose Korean subsidiary holds the management and operation contract, and filed what it describes as the first Korean complaint under Germany's supply chain due diligence law. Where equipment comes from a country with a supply chain due diligence statute, the manufacturer's home regulator is a second forum, and reaching it does not require standing in a Korean court. That is the same lever La'o Hamutuk used from Timor-Leste into an Australian environmental authority, arrived at independently on the other side of the region. Its case record is where to look for precedent. Founded in May 1999 as the litigation centre of Green Korea United, it has run a criminal complaint over the discharge of toxic substances into the Han River, litigation over military airfield noise, golf course litigation and Seoul air pollution litigation; it took the Saemangeum future generations case and has run forums on the rights of nature. For a Korean fight over noise, air or a specific facility there is likely to be a comparable case already argued. It teaches as well as litigates. It runs an environmental law school for citizens and an environment school for lawyers and takes practical training cohorts, which is the route for a community that wants its own people to understand the file rather than depending entirely on counsel. Note that Korea has two separate environmental legal centres with similar names: this one, at greenlaw.or.kr, belongs to Green Korea United, while the Environmental Law Centre at ecolaw.or.kr is affiliated to the Korean Federation for Environmental Movement already recorded here. Both exist and they are not the same body.

trackers.name: EIASS — Korea's assessment system, where scoping decisions and draft reports go on public view
trackers.desc: The scoping decision is published for inspection, which is earlier than almost any other system in this file allows. Alongside public viewing of the draft assessment report, the system's public participation section carries the decision on which assessment items were settled for a project — the document that fixes what the study will and will not examine. Elsewhere a community sees the finished report and argues about what is missing; here the list of what will be looked at is itself on view, at the point when adding to it is still possible. Enforcement is published too. The same section carries the status of administrative dispositions, so penalties imposed in connection with assessment obligations are a matter of public record rather than something to be prised out. Consultation progress, the consultation register and consultation statistics are searchable in the same place. Completed consultations are held in full. The system databases the full text of assessment reports for projects whose consultation is complete, together with the agreed consultation content and the status of the assessment agents who prepared them, with a search over all of it. The register of agents matters for the same reason it does in Thailand — the competence and standing of whoever wrote a report is checkable separately from its conclusions. Health impact assessment has its own section, including the factors by project type. It sets out the procedure, the governing rules, the health assessment factors associated with particular kinds of project, and a spatial information service. Where a community's objection is about health rather than habitat, that is the part to read first, because it names in advance which health factors a project of that type is expected to address. The system also publishes the legislation, the drafting guidelines and links to monitoring network data.

trackers.name: 환경분쟁조정위원회 — a published damages calculation, and anticipated harm is in scope
trackers.desc: Harm that is expected to arise counts, not only harm already done. The statute reaches environmental damage that has occurred or is anticipated from business or other human activity, and the listed heads go well beyond the usual pollutants: air, water, soil and marine pollution, noise and vibration, odour, destruction of natural ecosystems, and also obstruction of sunlight, obstruction of ventilation, obstruction of view and artificial lighting. A construction project's foreseeable effects on a neighbourhood can therefore be brought to a specialist administrative body rather than to court. The commission publishes how the money is calculated, which tells you what to measure. Its damages reference sets excess noise as the measured or evaluated level minus a tolerance-limit reference level, and states plainly that the compensable damage period is the part of the construction period during which the tolerance limit was exceeded rather than the whole build, and that below the tolerance limit there may be no award at all. That converts preparation into a specific task: measure early, measure repeatedly, and keep dated records of the days the threshold was passed. Four procedures, and causation can be decided on its own first. Facilitation, conciliation, adjudication and arbitration are available; a party served with a causation adjudication may then apply for facilitation, conciliation, liability adjudication or arbitration, so the causal question can be settled before the money is argued. On receipt an examiner is assigned, carries out a site investigation and obtains expert evaluation before the adjudication meeting decides. An accepted conciliation proposal is recorded with the same effect as a judicial settlement. Know the thresholds and the clocks. Fees are payable on a scale by claim value; the central commission takes adjudication claims above one hundred million won with local commissions below; a party dissatisfied with a local liability adjudication has sixty days from service to go to the central commission; objections to an interim decision run fourteen days. Claims are barred ten years from the damage and three years from knowledge of it, and an application may be dismissed where a conciliation procedure under another statute has been used or is under way.

trackers.name: 사유림 매수 — the state buys private forest at two appraisers' average, with a ten-year pension option
trackers.desc: Here the buyer is the State, which is the cleanest answer this file has to the question of who will purchase the land. The forest service buys private and public forest every year to expand the national forest estate, and its priorities are shaped by conservation rather than by market value: forest adjoining or enclosed by national forest, forest inside national-forest expansion planning areas, forest needed for national forest management, and forest requiring conservation such as ridge protection areas and forest protection zones, along with land usable as urban and neighbourhood forest. Where ground under development pressure sits beside national forest or inside a protection zone, its owner has a public buyer. The procedure is short and the price is not negotiated by the buyer alone. An owner wishing to sell files a consent-to-sell with the national forest management office for the area; the office checks the documents and inspects the site to decide whether purchase is possible, then notifies the owner and negotiates; the price is set as the arithmetic mean of valuations by two independent appraisers, and a contract follows. Forest carrying private rights such as a mortgage or a superficies, or transferred within the previous year, cannot be bought — clear those before applying. The pension option turns a sale into an income. Under the forest pension arrangement the purchase price is paid monthly across ten years, with the service additionally paying interest and an amount corresponding to land price increases, and up to forty per cent of the price may be paid at contract. Regional purchase price ceilings were abolished and the co-ownership rules relaxed so that jointly owned forest can be sold. For an elderly owner holding land that cannot be developed and costs money to keep, that is a monthly income rather than a windfall, and it is the reason many such owners sell at all. Watch the annual plan and the calendar. Purchase plans are published each year on the service's own notice board, office by office; because site survey and appraisal take time, applications made late in the year may roll into the following year's programme, and once the planned volume for a year is exhausted the purchase waits. Approach the local national forest management office early and read the current year's notice before doing anything else.

trackers.name: 환경신문고 128 — a free reporting line covering national park damage, with anonymity and a result notice
trackers.desc: What it covers is wider than pollution in the ordinary sense. The line takes reports of violations under the air, water, waste, chemical substances, livestock excreta, natural parks and soil environment statutes — including unauthorised discharge of sewage and wastewater, installing or operating emission facilities without permission or notification, abnormal operation of emission or abatement facilities, dumping or leaking contaminated soil, incineration of odour-causing substances, illegal dumping, burning or burial of waste, and damage to nature inside a national park. A community watching earthworks in a park, or a plant that runs its abatement equipment only when inspectors are expected, has a named category to report under. Report it the way the system asks and it gets acted on. State who, when, where and how the act was done, with the reporter's name, address and contact details — and where waste is dumped or buried using a vehicle, give the vehicle number. The line is dialled as 128 without an area code and has been toll-free since December 2019; a call is connected to the environmental management department and duty office of the relevant local government, and a report can equally be filed through the national petition portal or its app. There is a reward, and the local authority pays it. Where the report is confirmed as true and the administrative agency has taken action such as an administrative disposition, the head of the competent local government pays a reward within budget, from thirty thousand won up to three million, and may set a different minimum by ordinance according to its budget. The ministry operates the system while local governments receive the reports and pay the rewards, which is worth knowing when chasing an outcome. Anonymity and a result notice are both stated. The reporter's identity is managed so that it is never disclosed outside, and the local authority verifies the violation by site investigation, takes appropriate administrative action and then informs the reporter of the result. Read this with the environmental dispute commission entry recorded here: this line is the enforcement track and that body is the compensation track, and they run separately.

trackers.name: 대한법률구조공단 — free representation under an income line, and a screening that asks whether you can win
trackers.desc: What it provides, and to whom. The corporation is a legal welfare body set up for people who cannot get adequate protection of the law because they are in economic difficulty or do not know the law, and it provides legal counselling, free preparation of litigation documents, representation in civil and family cases and free defence in criminal cases. Free representation is available to nationals at or below one hundred and twenty-five per cent of the standard median income published by the welfare ministry, and to foreign nationals resident in the country who are victims of crime; basic livelihood recipients, disabled people and workers owed wages are served without charge, with a small charge for those on modest monthly incomes. Traffic accidents involving only property damage are excluded. The screening asks whether the case can be won. An applicant files the prescribed legal aid application at the local office together with material showing they are an eligible person and evidence supporting the facts they assert; the corporation then examines the appropriateness of granting aid, the likelihood of success, and whether any judgment could actually be enforced, before deciding. A community's application therefore has to argue the case and not only the poverty — the opposite emphasis to most of the schemes recorded in this file, where means is the whole test. Apply at the office where the court sits. Counselling can be had at whichever office is nearest to where you live, but the corporation states that for litigation representation, using the office located in the place where the competent court sits will get help faster. Branches, sub-offices and field offices operate across the country, with general consultations at the local branch. Test your eligibility before you apply. Counselling runs on weekdays through a national telephone number reachable without an area code, an international line, the website, video consultation and appointment visits, and the electronic filing system carries a self-diagnosis tool and a median income check so an applicant can see whether they qualify before starting. Read this with the environmental dispute commission and the reporting line entries recorded for this country: those are the compensation and enforcement tracks, and this is the one that puts a lawyer in the room.

trackers.name: 등기사항증명서 — anyone may apply, no form, no documents, issued the same day
trackers.desc: Anyone may apply, and the state says so in the service listing itself. The government's own service entry for a land registry certificate records that anyone may apply, that there is no application form and no supporting documents required, and that processing is immediate — within three hours during working hours. No permission from the owner, no paperwork, and no reason to be given. The certificate proves all or part of the registration record for a piece of land, showing the description of the property and the rights over it, which is where mortgages and other encumbrances appear. Three channels, with the fee published for each. The same listing gives the fee for a request made in person at a registry office and the lower fee for an unattended issuing machine or an internet issue, with the certificate obtained through the supreme court's internet registry office. Published guidance records that inspecting the record on screen costs less than having a certificate issued, that the service runs around the clock, and that a certificate issued over the internet has the same legal effect as one issued at the registry counter. The address or the unique property number is the key. Published guidance records that the lot address or the property's unique number is all that is needed, with no seal and no power of attorney. A community that knows where the site is already holds the identifier the registry wants — the same point recorded for Japan, where the lot number can be taken from a property tax notice. Read it as the registry half of the file for this country. This file already records for Korea the environmental dispute commission that calculates damages, the reporting line that brings enforcement, the state purchase of private forest and the legal aid corporation that tests the merits of a case. The registry certificate is what tells a community who it is arguing with, and what is charged against the ground, before any of those are approached.

trackers.name: 정보공개 — ten days to decide, seven to answer an objection, and original documents on the portal
trackers.desc: Look at the portal before filing anything. A request can be handed in at the public body, posted, faxed or submitted through the national information disclosure portal, and the portal also allows original documents held by public bodies to be read directly. Checking whether the document is already published costs nothing and takes minutes, and a request narrowed by what is already visible is harder to refuse. The clocks are short at every stage. The public body must decide whether to disclose within ten days of receiving the request, extendable by up to ten more where unavoidable; where disclosure is decided it must be carried out within ten days of the decision, with the time, place, method and any fee notified; an objection may be lodged within thirty days of the decision notice or of the day a non-disclosure is deemed to have been made; and the body must decide that objection within seven days, extendable by seven. A refusal must carry the route out of it. Where a body decides not to disclose it must notify the requester in writing without delay, stating the grounds and the methods and procedures for challenging the decision, and where an objection is dismissed it must tell the requester that administrative appeal and administrative litigation are available. The objection stage can also be skipped entirely: a requester may go straight to administrative appeal or to the courts. Two provisions that decide real cases. Where exempt and non-exempt information are mixed but can be separated, disclosure is to be made in the way that meets the purpose of the request — so a blanket partial refusal has to be justified rather than assumed. And where a third party had asked for non-disclosure but the body decides to disclose, at least thirty days must pass between the decision and the actual release, during which that third party may object and seek suspension. Expect that gap whenever the document concerns a company. Read this with the environmental dispute commission, the reporting line, the state purchase of private forest and the legal aid entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 국민권익위원회 — grievance complaints, corruption reports, and protection for the person who reports
trackers.desc: Two doors, and the first is the grievance complaint. A grievance complaint means a complaint about an administrative agency's illegal, unjust or passive disposition, or about an unreasonable administrative system, which infringes a person's rights or causes them inconvenience or burden; it is filed through the national petitions portal. Simple procedural questions and requests to interpret legislation are expressly not grievance complaints. A permit granted unlawfully, or an agency's refusal to act on something it should have acted on, is the grievance form's own subject matter rather than a complaint that has to be forced into some other shape. The corruption report is referred out, and the result comes back. Where a corruption report is received, the commission checks the facts and, where investigation is required, refers the matter to the board of audit and inspection, to investigative agencies or to the supervising agency of the public body concerned, receives the outcome and informs the reporter — and where the investigation result is inadequate it can demand that the matter be investigated again. A referral that comes back for a second look is rare among the complaint routes recorded in this file. Protection is a named package, including relief from the reporter's own liability. The commission operates guarantees of status, confidentiality and personal protection for reporters and for those who cooperate with them, a prohibition on disadvantageous measures, and mitigation or exemption of the reporter's own liability, together with relief payments where a reporter, a cooperator, a relative or a person living with them suffers harm or incurs costs directly related to the report. Liability mitigation is the provision that matters most to someone inside a project: it means reporting need not automatically destroy the person who does it. And there is money attached. Where a report directly recovers or increases public revenue or saves public cost, compensation is paid to the reporter; where there is no direct recovery but the report advances the public interest, an award may be paid up to a published ceiling, decided through a deliberation committee. Time limits run from the confirmation of the underlying legal relationship, so a claim should not be left. Read this with the environmental dispute commission, the information disclosure route, the registry certificate and the legal aid entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 국민감사청구 — three hundred signatures can put a project under state audit
trackers.desc: Three hundred citizens can require the audit board to consider an audit. Under the anti-corruption act, citizens aged eighteen or over, numbering three hundred or more, may request the board of audit and inspection to audit a matter where a public institution's handling of its business significantly harms the public interest through a violation of law or an act of corruption. For a community facing a project it believes was approved unlawfully, that is a threshold measured in neighbours rather than in lawyers, and it is the only provision recorded in this file that lets ordinary people put a state audit in motion. The signature roll is the work. The request form, signed or sealed by the representative of the requesters, must be accompanied by a roll listing each requester's name, telephone number, date of birth, address and occupation, and the board states that the roll must be submitted as an original — scans and copies are not accepted — either in person or by post. It also warns that entering another person's name on the roll amounts to forgery of a private document and is punishable. Collect the roll properly the first time, because a defective roll is the easiest way to lose the request. A committee decides whether to audit, and the clock can be extended. The decision whether to carry out an audit is taken by a committee, and where the audit will take more than sixty days, or where measures under the audit law are required, the period may be extended for a reasonable time, with the reason for the extension and its length notified to the requesters or their representative. A second, more flexible route runs beside it. Alongside the statutory national audit request there is a public interest audit request operated under the board's own directive, which is administered more flexibly; both allow a group of citizens to bring a matter to the board rather than waiting for it to choose the subject itself. Read this with the information disclosure route, the anti-corruption and civil rights commission, the registry certificate and the legal aid entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 자연환경국민신탁 — a statutory trust that acquires and holds land, and the preservation agreement for owners who will not sell
trackers.desc: A statutory trust exists to acquire natural land and hold it permanently. The national trust act on cultural heritage and natural environment assets, enacted in 2006 and in force from 2007, establishes two trust corporations: one to acquire and manage cultural heritage and one to acquire and manage natural environment assets. The natural environment trust acquires assets of conservation value using land, funds and other property donated, gifted or entrusted to it by individuals, companies and organisations, together with membership fees, and preserves and manages them permanently for future generations. Where a community wants a particular hillside, wetland or wood taken out of the development market altogether, this is the body whose statutory purpose is to hold it. An owner who will not sell can sign a preservation agreement instead. The act provides that the owner or occupier of cultural heritage or natural environment assets of high conservation value may conclude a voluntary preservation agreement or a protection pledge with the trust, with the requirements, contents, effects, methods and procedures of such cooperation agreements set out in the trust's articles. That is the instrument for the neighbour who wants the land kept as it is but does not want to part with it — the middle option between selling and doing nothing, and one that few countries in this file offer in statute. The tax treatment is the fundraising argument. Published accounts of the act record that the trusts are exempt from income tax, corporation tax, inheritance and gift tax, registration tax, acquisition tax, property tax and aggregate land tax in respect of trust property, and that residents who donate to a trust may deduct the donation from their income within stated limits. A campaign asking people to give land or money can therefore tell the giver precisely what the gift costs them after tax. The state may fund it, and the members govern it. Central or local government may budget for the creation of a trust and for securing and managing trust property, and may support running costs where the trust cannot cover them from its own activities; governance runs through a general meeting of trust members with a board beneath it, those who entrust property become trust members, and anyone may become an activity member on terms set by the articles. Read this with the heritage trust fund, the state purchase of private forest, the environmental dispute commission and the citizen audit request entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 농지은행 경영회생지원 농지매입 — the public body that buys a farm's land and leases it straight back, with a capped buy-back
trackers.desc: It buys the land and leases it straight back to the same farm. The management recovery programme of the state farmland bank buys farmland, and the agricultural facilities attached to it, from households in financial crisis, and then leases those same assets back to the same farming entity on a long lease with a repurchase right guaranteed, so that the farming can continue without interruption.
