A sale that does not end the farming is a fundamentally different instrument from a sale, and it is the answer to the situation this file has recorded again and again: land lost not to a project directly but to the debt a project's disruption produced. The buy-back price is capped. On repurchase the price for the land is the lower of the appraised value at the time of repurchase or the original purchase price uplifted at the rate the ministry sets — published as three per cent a year — with the corporation bearing the appraisal cost; facilities return at the original purchase price, less prepaid depreciation where the lease was extended. A cap of that kind means a recovering farm cannot be priced out of its own land by a rising market, which is precisely what happens under an ordinary sale and repurchase. Eligibility and terms are published as numbers. The programme is stated to cover farmers and agricultural corporations with disaster damage of fifty per cent or more, or with debt above a published threshold and a debt-to-asset ratio of forty per cent or more; purchase is at appraised value within regional limits per square metre and within stated ceilings for individuals and for corporations, and within the amount of the debt; rent is set as a standard rent within about one per cent of the purchase price; and the lease runs seven years, extendable by up to three more following evaluation. The same bank does more than rescue. It takes farmland from retiring, incapacitated or departing farmers by purchase, lease or trusteeship and passes it to young farmers, new entrants, returning farmers and agricultural corporations by sale or lease; it purchases and stockpiles farmland; and it operates a pension scheme against farmland for older farmers. Applications go to the corporation branch covering the land in question, with programme notices published on the bank's own portal. This is agricultural land only. Read this with the state purchase of private forest, the statutory trust that holds natural land, the environmental dispute commission and the citizen audit request entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 먹는물 수질검사기관 — designated laboratories, published fees per test set, and a certificate in fourteen days
trackers.desc: The laboratories are designated, and the list is published. Drinking water testing institutions are designated under the drinking water management law by the environment ministry's river basin environmental offices, and the designation status — the designating office, the institution's name, its location and its contact number — is published, including as an open dataset on the national public data portal. Designated institutions carry a designation number and the year it was granted, and local government waterworks laboratories appear on the list alongside national and private ones. Check the designation, and which office granted it, before paying anyone. The fees are published per test set. The national water agency's testing centre lists a fifty-nine item set for tap water and a forty-six item set for drinking groundwater, with cheaper sets for household groundwater and for agricultural groundwater, all quoted exclusive of tax with ten per cent added for external requests, and with the selection rules stated: faecal coliform or E. coli is chosen rather than both, and uranium is analysed quarterly and only on raw groundwater. A household can therefore price the exact set it needs before submitting anything. Sampling and turnaround are stated. A designated municipal laboratory records that for permitted or notified groundwater the testing institution itself collects the sample, and that the certificate is posted within fourteen days of the sample being received. A sample collected by the laboratory and a result in a fortnight is the difference between a usable result and one the other side can attack on chain of custody. The statutory cycles tell you what already exists. Published guidance records that drinking groundwater is tested every two years, or every three where daily pumping capacity is thirty tonnes or less, and household, industrial and agricultural water every three years; that the drinking groundwater set runs to forty-six statutory items covering microbiology and health-related inorganic substances; and that separate schedules cover fifty-nine water pollutants and thirty-two specified hazardous water pollutants, with perfluorinated compounds among the monitored items. If a well near a project sits on one of those cycles, earlier results already exist — ask for them before commissioning a new test. Read this with the state purchase of private forest, the farmland bank, the environmental dispute commission and the citizen audit request entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 뉴스타파 / KCIJ — a tip server held outside the country, and what happens after you send something
trackers.desc: The tip server sits outside the country, deliberately. The centre's published answers state that a substantial part of its investigative reporting begins from public-interest disclosures by insiders; that the production team treats protection of a source's identity as central and blocks every possibility by which a source could be inferred during reporting and publication; and that the tip system's server is kept abroad rather than domestically, so that access by investigative agencies is blocked. That last sentence is an architectural decision rather than a promise, and it is the reason to prefer a system like this over an email to a reporter. Two operational facts to know before sending anything. A submitted tip cannot be corrected or deleted afterwards, and the submission page says so plainly — check the content before sending rather than after. And where reporting is being conducted covertly for security reasons, the outlet may not contact the person who sent the material at all; its answers also note that no contact may simply mean reporting has not yet begun or no schedule has been set. Silence is therefore not evidence that the material was discarded, which is worth knowing before sending the same documents somewhere else. It is funded by its readers, which is why it can take on power. The centre describes itself as a non-profit, non-partisan independent press organisation for ordinary citizens; it began broadcasting as a project in January 2012 and reorganised in 2013 as a non-profit civil organisation, sustained by regular supporter members, reported in the tens of thousands. Its own supporter pages state that regular support is what allows it to report steadily without yielding to outside pressure — the funding model is the independence, and a community weighing where to take documents should read it that way. There is a dedicated tip line and a street address. A main telephone number, a separate telephone number for tips, a fax number and a Seoul address are published. For material too sensitive to upload, or for someone without a safe device, a telephone number and a physical address are the alternatives to a web form. Read this with the designated drinking water laboratories, the state purchase of private forest land, the farmland bank and the environmental dispute commission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 공청회 개최 요구 — thirty residents can compel a public hearing, and the window closes seven days after the inspection period
trackers.desc: Thirty residents can compel a public hearing. Under the impact assessment legislation, the authority preparing a development basic plan must publish the draft strategic assessment report for public inspection and hold a briefing session to hear the opinions of residents in the assessment target area — but where residents within the scope set by presidential decree request a public hearing, a public hearing must be held. The decree fixes that scope: a hearing is required where thirty or more residents submit opinions stating that a hearing is necessary, or where five or more do so and they amount to half or more of all the residents who submitted opinions on the draft. The same structure applies to project-level assessments, where the obligation to hold the hearing falls on the project operator. A briefing session is something a proponent runs; a public hearing is something residents can require, and thirty signatures is the threshold that separates them. The window runs from the start of inspection to seven days after it ends. Residents may submit their opinions from the day the inspection period of the draft begins until seven days after that period ends, on the environmental effects expected from the plan and on conservation measures — and the same window governs the demand for a hearing. The seven-day tail is the part most easily missed: the inspection period closing is not the end of the right. Some plans must also hear people who are not local residents. Where a development basic plan covers areas of high ecological conservation value, or areas where environmental damage or change to the natural ecosystem is or may become significant, as prescribed by decree, the authority must also hear relevant experts and other persons who are not residents of the assessment target area. For a site of that kind, outside specialists are not intruders on the process but participants the law requires. The documented weakness, and what to do about it. Published research on the system records that notice of a briefing session or hearing is often given in a way that residents of the assessment area do not learn of it, so that sessions proceed with no affected residents present and the consultation requirement is nonetheless treated as satisfied, and that participation by environmental organisations which are not local residents is limited. The practical response is to watch for the inspection notice, count the days, and collect the thirty signatures inside the window rather than relying on being told. Read this with the assessment information system where scoping decisions and draft reports are published, the environmental dispute mediation commission, the green legal centre and the citizens' audit request entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 수용재결 — two appraisers, thirty days to object, ninety to sue, and the remnant land you can force them to buy
trackers.desc: Fourteen days of notice, then two appraisers. Where negotiation fails and the project operator applies to the land expropriation committee for a ruling, the committee's published procedure runs: public notice and inspection at the city, county or district office for fourteen days with individual notice to owners; the hearing of owners' opinions; review of the opinions submitted by both the owner and the operator together with a factual investigation; valuation commissioned from two appraisal institutions with the compensation calculated on their results; deliberation and the expropriation ruling; and service of the ruling document, with posting at the local office for fourteen days where the recipient cannot be found. The owner's opinion is solicited before the valuation is commissioned, which is the point at which what the appraisers are asked to consider can still be affected. Thirty days to object, ninety to sue, and the objection is optional. A person dissatisfied with the ruling may file a written objection with the central land expropriation committee within thirty days of receiving the ruling document, going through the local committee where that committee ruled; and published guidance records that administrative litigation may be brought within ninety days of receiving the expropriation ruling regardless of whether an objection was filed, or within sixty days of receiving the objection ruling. Legal commentary records that the objection stage is no longer compulsory and that the expropriation ruling itself is the object of the suit. Objecting gets two fresh appraisers. On an objection the central committee re-values, selecting two appraisal institutions that did not carry out the earlier valuations, and where the new figure exceeds the compensation in the expropriation ruling the compensation is changed to the new figure. That is a concrete reason to object even where litigation is also contemplated: the re-valuation is done by people who have not already committed to a number. Who you sue depends on what you are disputing, and the remnant land has its own claim. Where the dispute is about the increase or decrease of compensation, the action is brought against the project operator — or against the owner where the operator sues — and the court determines the compensation itself; where the complaint is that the objection ruling was itself unlawful, the defendant is the central committee. Separately, an owner may require the operator to apply for a ruling, and may claim expropriation of remnant land where negotiation on its purchase has failed — but that claim must be made by the date the project works are completed. Read this with the state purchase of private forest land, the legal aid corporation, the property register certificate and the resident-triggered public hearing entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 사법정보공개포털 — one portal for judgments and case law, free precedent search, and the classes of judgment that are open
trackers.desc: The court's disclosure services were consolidated into one portal. The judiciary's own account records that with the next-generation electronic litigation system built in January 2025, judicial information disclosure services previously spread across several systems were brought together into a single information disclosure portal, offering internet viewing of judgments, supply of copies, in-person viewing, the comprehensive legal information service, information disclosure requests, recent legislation, monthly court statistics, the judicial yearbook, a case search link and a false case number check. Anyone who wishes to view or obtain a judgment may apply through those services. Which judgments are open is defined by date and case type. The same account records that judgments are released after de-identification to protect personal information and the privacy of case participants, that a judgment is withheld where the content is unsuitable for disclosure, and that the classes open are: criminal case judgments finalised on or after 1 January 2013, and civil, administrative and patent case judgments finalised on or after 1 January 2015 or pronounced on or after 1 January 2023. A community searching for administrative decisions on permits, land or compensation is therefore inside the open classes for anything recent. Precedent search is free; copies of judgments are not always. The comprehensive legal information service allows supreme court and lower court precedents, statutes, treaties, supreme court rules, established practice and literature to be searched free of charge, and the internet viewing service lets a member of the public search and read disclosed judgments in finalised cases without a separate viewing application. Court pages for the viewing service also describe a fee payment step and an account transfer payment programme, so budget for a charge where a copy is required rather than a search. The 2019 change that made this usable. The supreme court announced that from 1 January 2019 an integrated internet search and viewing service began: criminal judgments that previously required both a case number and the defendant's name became searchable by free keyword, and judgments that could previously be searched only on the website of the court that decided them became searchable for the whole country in one place. Read this with the expropriation ruling entry, the legal aid corporation, the green legal centre and the environmental dispute commission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 1365 기부포털 — the registration criteria a collection is judged against, the one-registration rule, and the searchable record of every collector
trackers.desc: The portal publishes the tests your collection will be judged against. The national donation portal's guide to collection registration records that, on receiving an application, the registering office checks the documents and then reviews the substance against criteria under the donations legislation: whether the purpose is a business that is not profit-making or political or religious activity and so qualifies as a donation collection project; whether the applicant is a corporation or body established with state or local government investment or contribution; whether the collection purpose matches the objects in the body's articles; whether the collection period is within one year and the use period within two years; whether the body has opened a website for disclosing information about the collection; and whether the method of use is described in concrete terms with a detailed schedule and calculation basis. Draft the application against that list. One fundraising project, one registration. The portal states the basic principle that a single fundraising project must have only one registration, and that the registering office checks whether the same project has been registered with both the central ministry and a metropolitan or provincial office; duplicate registration is a ground for cancellation. Where circumstances change, a variation application can alter the target amount, purpose, method, extension of the collection period, use period, method of use and collection costs — but it must be filed before the collection or use period expires. Where you register depends on the target. A metropolitan authority's guidance records that a collection with a target of one billion won or less registers with that city rather than the ministry, and that applications may be submitted through the integrated donation management system, in person or by post; the government service catalogue records that registration applies to collections of ten million won or more from an unspecified public, with a stated processing period where the target exceeds one billion. Every registered collection is searchable, including its accounts. Published quarterly registration listings record that details for each collector — the collection plan, the use plan, the completion report, the statement of use, the accounting audit report and any approval to dispose of or reuse funds — can be found by searching the body's name on the portal. That is how a community checks an organisation asking for money, and how it sees what a comparable appeal actually raised and spent. Read this with the heritage trust fund, the state forest purchase, the green legal centre and the judicial disclosure portal entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 도시·군관리계획 열람 — fourteen days to read the plan and file an opinion, sixty days for a written answer, and residents may propose a plan themselves
trackers.desc: The plan that decides what may be built has a public reading window, and it is fourteen days. A metropolitan planning portal's own procedure guide records that a draft urban management plan is advertised in two or more daily newspapers and then made available by the district head for public reading for at least fourteen days, with minor matters exempt from the consultation requirement. The implementing decree provides that the main contents are advertised in two or more dailies circulating mainly in the area and on the local authority's website, that anyone with an opinion on the advertised draft may submit a written opinion to the mayor or county head within the reading period, and that where an opinion is to be reflected and the matter is important under the local planning ordinance, the draft must be advertised and opened for reading again. You are entitled to a written answer, within sixty days. The portal records that whether an opinion has been reflected in the plan is notified within sixty days of the end of the reading period, and that submitted residents' opinions are attached when the decision is requested from the higher authority; the decree provides the same sixty-day duty to notify the person who submitted the opinion. That is the document a community keeps: a written statement of what the authority did with its objection, and proof that the objection travelled up with the file. Residents may propose a plan, not only object to one. The planning legislation provides that residents, including interested parties, may propose to the body empowered to draft an urban management plan that it draft one, the proposal being accompanied by the plan drawings and an explanatory statement. A community that wants a designation rather than a refusal — a park, a district unit plan, a protective zoning — has a route to ask for it. The consultation duty is enforceable, and courts examine it. Reported judgments record the statutory duty to hear residents' opinions when drafting an urban management plan, to reflect opinions found to be reasonable, and to hear residents even where a provincial governor drafts the plan directly, by sending it to the relevant mayor or county head with a stated deadline; courts have examined whether the advertisement and reading procedure was complied with, including where a modified plan was re-advertised for a fresh reading period. Note the dates of advertisement and reading, because they are what a challenge to procedure turns on. Read this with the assessment system entry, the public hearing threshold, the expropriation ruling and the judicial disclosure portal entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 골재채취 허가 — five-year maximum extraction periods, spawning season bans on river and sea aggregate, and consultation before a site is designated
trackers.desc: Aggregate extraction is permitted by the local mayor or county head, for a period capped at five years. The aggregate extraction enforcement decree provides that when granting an extraction permit the mayor, county head or district head must set the extraction period within a range of five years, and may not set a period exceeding the designation period of an aggregate extraction complex where the permit is inside one. Aggregate is defined as rock limited to crushing use, sand or gravel occurring naturally in rivers, forests, public waters or otherwise on or under the ground and used as material for concrete and asphalt concrete or as base material for construction works, and the business of extracting, sorting, washing or crushing it for profit must be registered with the same local authority. Ask when the permit period ends. The spawning season can be made a no-extraction period. The decree provides that in setting the extraction period the authority shall consider the assessment result of extraction capability and the time needed to install stockyards and ancillary facilities, and that for river aggregate and sea aggregate the spawning season of major fish species may be set as a period during which extraction is prohibited. Where a river or coastal community depends on a fishery, that provision is the specific thing to ask the permitting authority to apply. Designating a site requires consultation with the river and flood authorities. The decree provides that the provincial governor designates areas needing aggregate extraction as planned extraction sites, either directly or on the application of the local mayor or county head, and that where the intended site is a river area or a flood management area under the rivers legislation, the governor must consult in advance the relevant basin or regional environment office head and the flood control office head. Those offices are bodies a community can approach before designation. Who decides depends on where the aggregate is. The decree routes permits for extraction in the exclusive economic zone to the national ministry and for extraction in an aggregate extraction complex to the provincial governor, and provides that where applications compete they are allocated according to the assessment of extraction capability rather than by open lot. The ministry's own policy page records the five-yearly aggregate supply and demand basic plan, the annual supply and demand plan and the resource survey carried out on the ministry's behalf, which is where the numbers behind a permit come from. Read this with the urban management plan reading window, the environmental dispute adjudication commission, the private forest purchase and the judicial disclosure portal entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 매장유산 지표조사 — the area thresholds that force a survey, the local authority's power to require one below them, and the fourteen-day public notice of a find
trackers.desc: Construction over a stated area must have a buried heritage surface survey before it proceeds. The enforcement decree of the buried heritage protection and survey legislation sets the projects requiring a survey, including construction on the coast under the coastal management legislation where the project area is 30,000 square metres or more, with a higher threshold of 150,000 square metres for aggregate extraction projects on the coast. Ask for the survey report by name for any project over those sizes. Below the threshold, the local authority can still require one — and the grounds are listed. The same decree provides that for construction below the stated areas the head of the local authority may find a survey necessary where the work is in an area where buried heritage was previously excavated or discovered, or in an area judged from historical texts, verified records and academic research to have a high likelihood of buried heritage. That is the provision to cite for a small site next to a known find. The decree also lists the areas treated as buried heritage areas, including land shown as containing buried heritage in an approved survey report, land where heritage was preserved after excavation, land recognised as containing heritage through the discovery notification and confirmation procedure, and land holding designated national, city or provincial heritage, natural monuments or scenic sites. A find becomes public within fourteen days. The enforcement rules provide that on receiving a survey report or notification of completed excavation, the metropolitan or provincial governor shall without delay publish the fact of the discovery or excavation on a noticeboard or website for fourteen days, and report the result of that notice to the heritage administration. Watch the provincial site as well as the developer. Two things a resident can do directly. The rules provide a prescribed form by which a construction project operator, a person seeking excavation permission or the local authority may request disclosure of detailed information about a buried heritage area, with the administration able to disclose within seven days of the request; and the Act provides for compensation to a person who reports a discovery and a reward to a discovery reporter who caused the excavation, the amount decided after review by the heritage committee. Excavation or change of the existing state requires permission applied for to both the local authority and the administration on a prescribed form with a survey plan attached. Read this with the national trust for cultural heritage, the assessment system, the thirty-resident hearing demand and the plan reading window entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 보호수 — nearly fourteen thousand protected trees on a published register, trees outside forests included, and an objection window before any de-listing
trackers.desc: The forest service publishes the count and the designating authority. Its protected tree pages define a protected tree as an old tree, a great tree or a rare tree with historical or academic value that particularly needs protection; record the national total as around fourteen thousand trees at a stated December count; name the designating and de-listing authorities as the regional forest service head or the metropolitan or provincial governor; cite the forest protection legislation's designation article; and note that the yearly species breakdown is updated the following July. A protected tree beside a threatened site is therefore a checkable fact with a named authority behind it. The statute says the tree stays where it is. The legislation provides that the governor or regional forest service head shall designate trees particularly needing protection as protected trees and manage them safely in the place where they presently stand; and that the provisions on forest protection zones apply to designation and de-listing, to restrictions on acts affecting a protected tree, and to purchase or exchange of the land on which a protected tree grows. That land purchase provision is the part worth knowing: the instrument reaches the ground the tree stands on. The criteria go beyond size, and reach trees outside forests. Published summaries of the framework record the designation criteria as covering old, great and rare trees worth preserving or propagating, together with village shrine trees, pavilion trees, riverbank trees, unusually formed trees and scenic trees; and the forest resources legislation defines a protected tree as an old, great or rare tree worth preserving, expressly including one standing outside a forest. A single tree in a village square is inside this scheme. De-listing has to be advertised, and you can object. The enforcement decree provides that before de-listing a protected tree the governor or regional forest service head must publish a notice including specified matters; that the owner or a person with a direct interest in the tree may file an objection within the stated objection period; that the authority must notify the objector of the result within twenty days of receiving it; and that de-listing proceeds only where there was no objection or the objection is found unmeritorious. Watch for that notice, because de-listing is the step that precedes felling. The designating authority may also appoint a manager and order the owner or manager to do what is necessary for protection. Read this with the private forest purchase, the aggregate permit, the buried heritage survey and the plan reading window entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 하천점용허가 — the six acts inside a river area that need permission, the documents an applicant must file, and the pollution conditions that can be attached
trackers.desc: Six kinds of act inside a river area need the river authority's permission, and they are listed. The river legislation provides that anyone intending to do any of the following within a river area must obtain the river management authority's permission, and again for important changes to what was permitted: occupation of land; occupation of river facilities; new construction, reconstruction or alteration of a structure; excavation, filling, cutting or other change to the form and quality of land; extraction of earth and stone, sand and gravel; and other acts prescribed by decree that may obstruct the conservation and management of the river. Ask which of the six a project needs, and whether an important change has been made since the permission issued. Conditions can be attached specifically against pollution. The same provision states that a river occupancy permission may carry ancillary conditions necessary to prevent public nuisance caused by pollution of the river and other dangers to health and hygiene, and that the authority shall take stated matters into account when granting one. A community's submission can therefore ask for conditions, not only for refusal. The application file is public-service documented, which tells you what to request. The government services portal records this as a civil application by any person or corporation seeking to occupy land in a national or local river area, and lists the documents by type of act: a hydraulic calculation sheet — omissible only where the river's cross-section is unchanged and there is nothing to examine — an implementation plan statement, a construction cost calculation and, for a dam, a geological survey report, together with design documents and drawings at stated map scales. The listed activity types include structures, land form change, extraction of earth, sand and gravel, planting of vegetation and operation of vessels. The river area itself is decided, and there is a rule for unplanned rivers. The Act provides that where a linear structure such as a railway or road performs the role of an embankment, the river-side slope head of that structure is treated as the embankment slope head, with the land on the channel side included; and that for a river with no basic river plan, the river area is the land where water continuously flows and land judged, by a prescribed method using terrain, surrounding vegetation and flood traces, to be under water on average at least once a year. Determining or changing a river area requires the water resources management committee's deliberation. Read this with the aggregate extraction permit, the plan reading window, the environmental dispute commission and the assessment system entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 마을어업 — the village fishery licence granted only to a fishing village association, the shoreline band it covers, and the fishing ground management rules that decide who exercises it
trackers.desc: Village fishery is licensed only to the village's own body, and the statute says so. The fisheries legislation provides that village fishery shall be licensed only to a fishing village association or to the district fisheries cooperative, in order to promote the common interests of fishers residing in a certain area; and that the mayor or county head may, where necessary for fishers' common interests and the development of fisheries in a certain area, licence such bodies for fisheries other than village fishery. Where a coastal project touches inshore water, the licensed body is a local association with a statutory purpose, not an absentee holder. The band close to shore is treated specially. The Act's provisions on this licence refer to water within the village fishery ground, and to water within five hundred metres of the shoreline at high tide — one thousand metres on the west coast — where the relevant city, county or district fisheries adjustment committee considers it necessary for fisheries adjustment. That distance is measurable, and the committee is a named body to address. Who may actually fish is set by the fishing ground management rules. The Act provides that a fishery right held by a fishing village association is exercised by its members as provided in the fishing ground management rules, and that a right held by the district cooperative is exercised by members whose address is in the working area of the association adjacent to that ground; that the exercise method, the order of priority, and the adjustment of facility quantities or areas among associations and members are set by ministerial rule; and that the mayor may restrict or prohibit exercise of the right so that members' incomes increase evenly. Ask for the management rules and the priority order. Licences can be refused, and the grounds are listed. The Act provides that a fishery licence shall not be granted to a corporation or organisation not established for fisheries, to a person whose combined existing and applied-for fishing ground area exceeds a prescribed area, or to companies and their affiliates meeting prescribed criteria in named aquaculture fisheries. Implementing rules provide that where a wider group of fishers should be able to take part, the mayor may set a lower limit on the number of people exercising the right, or limit the number of exercises or total exercise period of those who have already exercised it. Read this with the aggregate extraction permit, the river occupancy permission, the protected trees register and the assessment system entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 야생생물 보호구역 — the local wildlife protection area a mayor or governor can designate, the residents' opinion required first, and the endangered species management contract with landowners
trackers.desc: A local authority can designate a wildlife protection area, and must hear residents first. The wildlife protection and management legislation provides that a mayor, provincial governor, county head or district head may designate as a wildlife protection area an area needing protection equivalent to a special protection area, in order to protect endangered wildlife; and that when designating, changing or lifting such an area they shall first hear the opinion of residents under the land use regulation framework legislation, and consult the heads of relevant administrative agencies. The designation, its location, area and date must be publicly notified under environment ministry rules and the local ordinance. That residents' opinion step is both a protection and an opening: it is where a community's evidence enters. The national special protection area is designated after hearing landowners and interested parties. The Act provides that the minister may designate as a wildlife special protection area a region especially needing preservation for the protection and breeding of endangered wildlife, after hearing landowners and other interested parties and the head of the local government, and consulting relevant central agencies; and that the designation must be varied or lifted where the area loses its value or no longer needs preservation for military reasons, natural disaster or other causes, following the same procedure. Location, area and date of designation are notified. Damaging acts inside a special protection area are prohibited outright. The Act contains a section restricting acts in a special protection area, providing that no one shall carry out the listed damaging acts there, and separately penalises setting or using explosives, traps, snares, pits, electric current or nets, or spreading poisons, agrochemicals or similar substances, to capture or kill endangered wildlife. Neighbouring land can be brought in by contract. The Act provides that in a special protection area and in adjacent land that can directly affect it through water pollution and the like, the minister or governor may conclude an endangered species management contract with landowners and occupiers covering changes in cultivation method, reduction of chemical use and other land management measures, or recommend that a central or local authority conclude one. That contract is a tool for the buffer, where designation alone does not reach. Read this with the village fishery licence, the river occupancy permission, the protected trees register and the assessment system entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 습지보호지역 — residents' opinions are a step in the designation procedure, the definition reaches paddies, reservoirs and canals, and the surrounding management area is designated with it
trackers.desc: Hearing residents is a named step in the designation procedure, not an optional consultation. The national biodiversity information system records the procedure for designating a wetland protection area as wetland survey, preparation of the designation proposal, gathering the opinions of the metropolitan or provincial governor and of local residents, consultation with relevant ministries, then designation and public notice; and records that a wetland surroundings management area and a wetland improvement area are included in the area designated. A community that wants a wetland protected can therefore ask for the survey, and knows where its own opinion enters. The statutory definition is wide enough to cover working landscapes. The same source records the wetland conservation legislation defining a wetland as an area whose surface is permanently or temporarily covered by fresh, brackish or salt water, comprising inland and coastal wetlands; records that the rivers and islands adjoining a wetland, and sea within the wetland deeper than six metres at low water, are also taken into account; and records that fish ponds, farm ponds, irrigated farmland, reservoirs and canals are also classified as wetlands. Where a project would fill a pond or a paddy, that classification is the first thing to establish. The selection criteria are stated, and so is the international definition used. The same source records that designation targets areas whose natural state retains its primitive character or which are rich in biodiversity, and records the international convention's definition extending the range of wetland to water up to six metres deep at low tide, covering marsh, fen, peatland and areas of water whether natural or artificial, permanent or temporary, static or flowing. The loss figure is the argument the same page makes. It records that since industrialisation and under development pressure half of the world's wetlands have disappeared since 1900, and that wetlands have historically been treated as objects of use rather than protection — the framing a community can borrow when arguing that a local wetland is not expendable. The law's implementing decree and rules are published alongside it. Read this with the wildlife protection area, the river occupancy permission, the assessment system and the environmental dispute commission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 주민감사청구 and 주민소송 — a signed residents' audit request against a local authority, the three-year limit, and the residents' suit that only an audit requester may bring
trackers.desc: Residents can require a higher authority to audit their own local government, on a joint signature. The government's plain-language legal service records that residents aged eighteen or over may request an audit where a local authority's or its head's handling of a matter within their powers violates statutes or significantly harms the public interest; that the request goes to the competent minister for a metropolitan city or province, and to the mayor or governor for a city, county or autonomous district, with the interior minister taking it where two or more ministries are involved or the competent minister is unclear; that the required number of joint signatures is set by the local government's class, one municipal audit page recording one hundred residents aged eighteen or over for its own case; and that the requesters must choose a representative, who files the request form and receives a representative's certificate. Three years is the outer limit, and prior audits do not always bar it. The same service records that an audit request cannot be made once three years have passed from the day the matter was handled or completed; that certain matters are excluded, including one already the subject of a pending or finally decided residents' suit; but that a matter audited by another body may still be requested where new facts emerge, where an important matter was omitted from that audit, or where it is a matter that may be the subject of a residents' suit. It also records a signature verification stage with public inspection, objections decided within fourteen days by a review council, and a chance to cure a shortfall in signatures. Only an audit requester may bring the residents' suit. The service records that a resident who requested an audit on the listed matters may bring a residents' suit against the head of the local authority — or the head of the body to which the power was delegated — in respect of illegal acts or neglect of duty related to the matter audited; that the listed matters include the conclusion or performance of sale, lease, contract or other agreements to which the authority is a party, and neglect of the imposition or collection of local taxes, user charges, fees and fines; that while such a suit is pending no other resident may bring a separate suit on the same matter; and that the suit is filed in the administrative court for the authority's office, or the district court exercising that jurisdiction. Read this with the national audit request, the information disclosure entry, the public hearing demand and the expropriation adjudication entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 환경공간정보서비스 — the ecological nature map graded under the conservation statute, land cover maps back to the 1980s, and a national environmental suitability map you can query by grade
trackers.desc: The ecological nature map grades land by ecological value, and it is made under a named statute. The environment ministry's spatial information service records the ecological nature map as a map grading the natural environment of mountains, rivers, inland wetlands, lakes and marshes, farmland and cities according to ecological value, naturalness and landscape value, prepared under the stated article of the natural environment conservation legislation; the map viewer records the version in force by ministry notice number, maintained by the national ecology institute, and lets a user find a sheet by sheet name or number, administrative district, drawn area or land lot number. Looking up the grade of a specific lot is therefore a search anyone can run. Land cover maps run from the 1980s to the present, at three levels of detail. The service records the land cover map as a map expressing the state of the land surface from satellite or aerial imagery, published as map services whose named layers include a 1980s broad-class land cover layer; the viewer records the detailed-class map as built on 2022 imagery, so it may differ in part from the present, and warns that what the system displays may differ from actual conditions and should be used for reference. Those two sentences are the honest limits to quote alongside any layer. A separate system grades environmental suitability and lets you download sheets. The service records a national environmental suitability map system run by the ministry with a policy research institute, providing a national environmental map composed of the suitability map and natural asset valuation information, with grade lookup, analysis of an area of interest, and sheet download; and records a more precise second version built for one province with nationwide extension under research. Its guidance records the system used at the assessment stage to check the suitability grade and the designation status of areas designated for environmental conservation through a land use regulation lookup service, and, for small-scale assessments, to record the suitability grade of the project area and its surroundings. Files come by request, and other layers sit alongside. The service records a data request menu providing spatial files, available to logged-in users, searchable by metadata or map, with results added to a request list; and lists environmental thematic maps, nationwide land use zone and district information, national park maps carrying biological, geomorphological and cultural locations with conservation value, and a renewable energy map. Read this with the wildlife protection areas, the wetland protection areas, the assessment system and the protected trees entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 국민신탁 — the two statutory trusts that buy and hold land permanently, the tax exemptions attached, and the duty on planners to account for trust property
trackers.desc: Two statutory trusts exist to buy conservation-worthy land and hold it permanently. The national archives record the 2006 legislation on national trusts for cultural heritage and natural environment assets as prepared because state-led conservation had shown limits in effectiveness through infringement of private property rights and shortage of budget, and as a practical alternative supporting the trust movement in which the private sector purchases, conserves and manages areas of high conservation value; and record the law's purpose as regulating the establishment and operation of the cultural heritage national trust and the natural environment national trust and the support of the state and local governments for them. Published material records the natural environment trust as acquiring conservation-worthy natural environment assets using property and membership fees donated, gifted or entrusted by individuals, companies and organisations, and conserving and managing them permanently for future generations. Where a community can raise or attract the land itself, that is the body that can hold it. The statute names the tax exemptions. The archives record exemptions applying to the trusts across income tax, corporate tax, inheritance and gift tax, and registration tax, among the supports the law provides. That is the case to put to a landowner considering a gift rather than a sale to a developer. Trust property has to be accounted for in planning. Published commentary records that the law defines national trust as citizens donating heritage or natural assets they own, or giving money, so that assets of conservation value are conserved, and records a protective device: when an administrative plan or development project affecting the trust's conservation property is being drawn up, that property must be taken into account. A community whose land adjoins a trust holding therefore has a planning argument attached to it. The movement predates the law, and its purchases are named. The same commentary records a citizens' trust association selecting a named wetland plant colony as its first conservation site, bought and preserved through citizens' donations and contributions, followed by named historic houses, a village, an artist's atelier and forest land in the demilitarised zone area — all held under the name of citizens' heritage, secured either by an owner's donation or by public fundraising. Read this with the ecological nature map, the residents' audit request, the wetland protection areas and the protected trees entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 한국환경회의 and the specialist institutes — a national network of environmental organisations, the litigation centre with salaried lawyers, and the citizen research institute behind the evidence
trackers.desc: A national network of environmental organisations exists, with a named secretariat. The network records itself as composed of environmental movement civic organisations nationwide, working since 2005 on raising public awareness of environmental problems and seeking alternatives, and names a specific organisation as its secretariat, with that body's registration number. Its published output includes press conference statements against development and calls to halt large-scale projects, and statements defending environmental impact assessment against being treated as an obstacle to megaprojects — so a local group has a national body that will issue a statement on its issue. The largest federation is built from local branches with specialist institutes attached. Published description records the country's largest environmental organisation, formed in 1993, as having fifty-four local organisations and being the national member of a global environmental network; and records attached specialist bodies including a citizens' environment research institute, an environmental law centre, an environmental education centre, a monthly magazine and a citizens' environmental information centre. It records the research institute, founded in 1993, as researching a reclamation project's sustainable use and conservation, environmental and residents' health damage from an oil spill, field surveys of a four-river project, asbestos removal and a hydrofluoric acid leak response. That is where the evidence for a case comes from. The law centre was the first civic body with salaried lawyers. Published description records the environmental law centre as beginning as an environmental legal advice room and becoming the first civic organisation body with full-time salaried lawyers, with more than a hundred legal professionals participating as members, and records its cases as including litigation that halted a national project, litigation exposing the illegality of a four-river project, cancellation of a military base relocation and of a road zone decision, and damages suits over cement and humidifier disinfectant. It records the centre's stated aim as making the abstract right to environment a more substantive recognised right and easing the heavy burden of proof on environmental victims. Read this with the green legal centre, the federation, the dispute mediation commission and the residents' audit entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 한국내셔널트러스트 — the citizens' trust association that buys threatened land with donations, its eleven citizens' heritage sites, and the money and area it has actually secured
trackers.desc: A citizens' association buys land threatened by development, and its totals are published. Published description records the association as an organisation that preserves natural environment and cultural heritage at risk of disappearing through development projects, by purchasing or securing conservation targets through citizens' donations and gifts. A published profile records its first citizens' heritage site as a wetland rice-paddy colony of an endangered plant on a named island, later designated a Ramsar wetland in 2008; records it then buying a named historic house and founding a separate heritage foundation which split off; and records further natural sites including a village on a named river and a crane habitat in the demilitarised zone area. It records the totals: eleven citizens' heritage sites acquired — eight natural sites held by the association and three cultural sites by the foundation — 136,106 square metres of conservation land secured, and 7.84 billion won raised in citizens' donations by 2020. Those figures are what a community can put beside a developer's offer. The sister foundation holds the cultural side, and its remit is registered. The foundation records itself as a non-profit foundation which secures cultural heritage worth preserving through citizens' voluntary fundraising, donation and gift, and preserves and manages it permanently as citizens' trust assets, focused on historic houses and traditional villages. The heritage authority's own register of non-profit corporations records its purposes as public fundraising to spread awareness of heritage preservation, discovery and preservation programmes for undesignated heritage, and the preservation and use of citizens' heritage. Undesignated heritage is the gap it exists to fill. That phrase matters: a building or site with no state designation has no protection, and this is the body whose stated purpose is to find and hold exactly those. Read this with the statutory national trusts, the heritage fund, the forest purchase scheme and the environmental federation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 녹색연합 — a field-survey organisation that stayed with sites long enough to stop a cable car, its camera-trap habitat surveys, and its citizen scientist training
trackers.desc: This organisation's record includes stopping a named development outright. Its own history lists, among its milestones, drawing out the environment ministry's decision of non-consent and thereby blocking construction of a named mountain cable car; the first private full survey of the goral's habitat in a named region; opposition to a four-river project with monitoring of the changes it caused, calls for those responsible to be punished and for weir dismantling and renaturalisation; publicising the farmed-bear problem until sterilisation ended the breeding of farmed bears; developing a roadkill reporting and monitoring application which the government's integrated system then cooperated with; and rescuing four farmed bears facing slaughter into a temporary shelter through citizens' fundraising. A community facing a cable car, a road or a resort has a domestic organisation with a blocked project on its record. Its method is presence on the site, and it says so. The organisation records that it finds answers by running on its own feet at the site, and stays at the site to the very last; records that it directly and steadily monitors nature that must be protected and builds protection measures; and records installing unmanned sensor cameras where the goral passes, to survey its habitat and carry out rescue activity, so that government and local authorities take up the case. Camera-trap survey data gathered before a project is what an assessment cannot easily dismiss. It trains citizen scientists and publishes its people. Published description records its plans as including training citizen scientists and using networks to link local field presence with policy expertise, establishing local specialist bodies for ecological survey, education and response, and active citizen-participation programmes; and records it founded in 1991, conserving the country's main ecological axis and the demilitarised zone and protecting wildlife and habitats. Its own staff page publishes named staff with direct telephone numbers and email addresses, and it names its values as respect for life, an ecological circular society, non-violent peace and green autonomy. Read this with the environmental federation, the citizens' trust association, the ecological nature map and the residents' audit entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 정보공개센터 and 참여연대 — an information disclosure organisation that helps citizens use the access law, a watchdog with a public interest law centre, and both refusing government money
trackers.desc: One organisation exists specifically to help people use the information access law. The centre records itself as working for a transparent and accountable society in which every citizen enjoys the right to know; states that it monitors the institutions and practices that threaten the citizens' right to know and fights power that conceals information; and records that it discloses and shares public information and data so that citizens can freely use what they need to protect their daily lives and solve social problems, and that it learns and explores together with citizens so anyone can actively use the information disclosure system and public data, and builds the data society needs together with them. For a community whose first task is prising documents out of an authority, that is a body whose whole purpose is that task. Independence is stated as a financial rule, not a sentiment. The centre records itself founded in 2008 with a financial principle of zero government support, funded by citizens' donations, so it can act freely without any interference; records publishing annual and monthly income and expenditure; and records that its budget approvers — the representative, the director and the secretary general — do not hold the organisation's bankbook or debit card, with monthly income and expenditure reported to a steering committee, an annual audit, and the audit report published. That separation of spending authority from custody of the account is a governance detail worth copying. The larger watchdog beside it runs a public interest law centre. A civic organisation records its purpose as monitoring state power through citizens' voluntary participation, presenting concrete policies and alternatives, and building a participatory democratic society through citizens' monitoring of and participation in the activities of legislative, judicial and administrative organs and citizen action exposing irregularities and corruption. Published description records it operating eleven activity bodies and four affiliated institutions, including a public interest law centre and a whistleblower support centre, and records it as taking no government funding since 1998, funded by members' dues, with monthly income and expenditure published and around 23,000 members. Read this with the environmental federation, the field-survey organisation, the residents' audit request and the citizens' trust entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 민변 — a lawyers' organisation with fifteen committees including one on environment and health, a public interest litigation committee, and a record of group suits by residents harmed by noise and flooding
trackers.desc: There is a lawyers' organisation with a standing committee on environment and health. Published description records it as a progressive legal organisation founded on 28 May 1988 by 51 lawyers, which historically handled political trial defence and various public interest lawsuits to defend basic human rights, and which now works across named fields including international solidarity, labour, media, education, women, children and youth, environment and health, livelihoods, minorities, peace and unification, international trade, past-wrongs settlement, digital information, culture and the arts, welfare and finance, and the judiciary. A community with an environmental harm can therefore ask for a named committee rather than a general enquiry. Its public interest litigation arm and its group cases are recorded. Published description records that as formal democratisation advanced the organisation strengthened public interest litigation, establishing a public interest lawsuit committee, and conducted suits including an airport noise damage case and a group action by residents harmed by flooding. Airport noise and flood damage are the classic forms of harm caused by infrastructure, and both have been litigated as group actions here. It records the organisation as running fifteen committees carrying out defence support in public interest and human rights cases, expressing opinions on laws and policies, proposing alternatives, and shaping public debate, and running a public interest defence centre whose work includes monitoring domestic and foreign legislation and case law, building a database, and researching litigation materials. Its membership and funding are stated. The organisation records itself as run on members' dues, with membership comprising lawyers, law professors, current and graduated law school students, and secretariat staff of the head office and each branch. Published description records it publishing annual legislative watch opinions and holding an annual human rights report meeting at which, with a newspaper, it names stumbling-block and stepping-stone judgments. Read this with the environmental law centre, the public interest litigation records, the information disclosure centre and the environmental federation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 제주곶자왈공유화재단 — an island foundation buying private forest with residents' donations, 115.7 hectares held permanently, sellers cutting their price by up to half, and a provincial hometown-donation channel
trackers.desc: An island-level foundation buys private forest outright and holds it permanently. Published reporting records it as a non-profit foundation established in 2007 so that residents could protect the island's natural asset by their own strength, which has so far put in 14.45 billion won to purchase and permanently conserve 115.7 hectares of privately owned forest across named townships and districts in two cities, with cumulative funds of about 18.2 billion won and a target of 165 hectares shared by 2030, campaigning for donations year-round. For a community trying to take a threatened forest out of the market, this is a provincial body doing exactly that, with the hectares and the money both published. Landowners themselves discounted the price, which is the part worth knowing. Published reporting records a single year's purchase of 72,486 square metres of private forest in eastern and western parts of the island using about 990 million won of the sharing fund donated by residents including kindergarten and primary school children, institutions and organisations, protecting habitats including a globally valuable fern colony; and records that some landowners sold at up to half off the appraised value, giving great strength to the spread of the movement. It records the chair saying the purchases protected habitats of endangered wild species and wetlands from the threat of development. The province runs a parallel donation channel, and the sums are stated. Published reporting records the provincial government running two hometown-love designated donation projects, each raising one billion won, to buy about 40,000 square metres of private forest in each of the two cities, and records it putting in 2.3 billion won in total — one billion raised by designated donation and 1.3 billion of its own funds — to buy four parcels totalling 73,955 square metres. It records the province using the same channel for protecting a named salamander and frog, a dolphin population, volcanic cone guardianship and spring water protection. The foundation publishes its address, telephone, fax and email. Read this with the citizens' trust association, the statutory national trusts, the environmental federation and the field-survey organisation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The metropolitan environmental dispute committee — a city-level body that awards compensation for construction noise, vibration, sunlight and light pollution up to a stated ceiling, with past awards published as precedent
trackers.desc: A city runs its own environmental dispute committee, and its jurisdiction is set by claim size. The metropolitan committee records that it handles disputes over health, property and mental harm caused or expected from business or other human activity through air pollution, water pollution, soil pollution, marine pollution, noise, vibration and odour; disputes related to the installation and management of environmental facilities such as waste treatment plants, sewage treatment plants and night soil treatment facilities; sunlight obstruction by structures not covered by the building legislation; light pollution from artificial lighting; and property damage from changes in groundwater level or flow paths. It records its own remit as arbitration and adjudication of disputes arising within the metropolitan area where the claim amount is 100 million won or less. For residents beside a building site, a city body that can award money is a different instrument from a complaint. Past awards are published for people to check before filing. The committee publishes its case list so that applicants can search similar cases before applying, including a claim of 81.2 million won for mental and structural damage from noise and vibration during church construction, and several inter-floor noise claims of 4 million and 10 million won. A published list of claimed sums against described harms is the nearest thing to a price list a neighbourhood can consult. What counts as environmental harm is defined broadly, and the adjudication route is stated. Published legal guidance records environmental harm as covering fourteen listed causes, including natural ecosystem destruction, obstruction of sunlight, ventilation and view, light pollution, changes in groundwater level or river level, chemical leakage and vibration-induced subsidence, with radioactive contamination excluded. It records that an applicant submits a written application for mediation, conciliation, adjudication or arbitration to the competent committee, that adjudication is conducted by a five-member adjudication panel which must begin proceedings without delay, and that parties may object to an interim decision within 14 days. Read this with the information disclosure centre, the public interest lawyers, the citizens' trust and the environmental federation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The village lawyer and the resident legal home doctor — a free lawyer for villages with none, reachable through the township office, and salaried lawyers posted inside 65 local government offices
trackers.desc: A lawyer is posted inside the local government office, and the service is described as first-tier. The ministry programme records that legal home doctors are currently placed and active in 65 local government bodies, social welfare councils and crime-victim one-stop solution centres across the country, providing first-tier legal services to socially and economically vulnerable people needing legal help, defined as legal consultation, legal education, guidance on litigation procedures, and referral to legal aid corporations and social welfare agencies — litigation itself excluded. It contrasts the model with earlier provision: existing legal aid was temporary, litigation-centred and separated from the local community, a service that waited; the home doctor is a standing, comprehensive legal welfare service joined to the local community that goes out to people, residing in local government and welfare bodies and visiting resident centres and welfare facilities directly to consult. For a household that cannot travel to a law office, a lawyer stationed in the district office is a different proposition. The village lawyer covers places with no lawyer at all, and the contact route runs through the township office. Published description records the village lawyer scheme as linking lawyers willing to donate their skills with townships and villages, so residents can consult free by telephone, fax or email, launched under a 2013 agreement between the justice ministry, the government administration ministry and the bar association; and records that a resident finds their village lawyer's contact by asking the township or village office, asking the local bar association or the ministry, or checking the scheme's own pages. One province records 163 township and neighbourhood consultation points with 199 lawyers assigned. Cities add their own free clinics, with the professions listed. One city records a free legal consultation room in the civil affairs office on the ground floor of city hall, open weekday afternoons, staffed by 25 advisers — four lawyers, three tax accountants, seven labour attorneys, five architects and six licensed real estate agents rotating by day. Another district records village lawyers available at every neighbourhood centre and village judicial scriveners at some, covering property registration, inheritance, auctions and deposits. Read this with the metropolitan environmental dispute committee, the public interest lawyers, the information disclosure centre and the citizens' trust entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The land use plan confirmation certificate and the municipal civil affairs counter — what zones and act-restrictions apply to a parcel, the certified copy only a city, county or district office issues, and the limits printed on the document
trackers.desc: A single certificate tells a community which designations and restrictions sit on a parcel. A provincial land information service records that the certificate confirms the designations of zones, districts and areas under each item of a named article of the land use regulation framework legislation, the restrictions on acts within those zones, districts and areas, and matters prescribed by a named article of its enforcement decree. A national service portal records the purpose of the application as obtaining a certified copy in order to confirm decisions of the urban plan for the land and restrictions on permission for acts within the urban planning zone, and records that it can be handled by visit, by telephone or online, anywhere. For a neighbourhood asking what may lawfully be built next door, that is the document that answers it. The certified copy comes from the city, county or district office. Provincial and metropolitan land information services record that for matters important to the exercise of property rights, the certifying land use plan confirmation certificate should be obtained from the city, county or district comprehensive civil affairs office, warning that the online material may not match the actual content because of programme or data errors, and that the online land use plan data has no effect as a certificate. Another records the same for the individual publicly announced land price certificate, and records that maps shown are reference drawings that cannot be used for surveying or design. The certificate's own limits are printed on it. A metropolitan service records that the certificate does not confirm everything that carries the name of a zone, district or area, and that where a topographical map is not prepared and announced — for cases such as railway protection zones and river areas, whose extent is directly designated by statute or self-government rules without a separate designation procedure — the designation cannot be confirmed. Knowing that a river area or railway protection zone may not appear on the certificate is what stops a community assuming silence means absence. A national portal also publishes public inspection of resident opinion hearings and urban planning statistics. Read this with the village lawyers and legal home doctors, the metropolitan environmental dispute committee, the information disclosure centre and the citizens' trust entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Municipal village community support centres — an intermediary body in each city and county that helps residents draft and run their own proposals, with a named city centre's programme ladder published
trackers.desc: A city runs a support centre whose job is to help residents organise themselves. One city's community support centre records its work as a project promoted to encourage residents to make their own villages, encompassing the discovery of residents' organisations, the strengthening of residents' capacity and the support of residents' activities, and records the centre as supporting various projects for village-making activity. For a neighbourhood that has an idea but no organisation, a municipal centre whose stated purpose is finding and strengthening residents' groups is the first door. The programme ladder runs from diagnosis to a resident-led project. The same city sets out the stages: a basic course in which a village preparing a project works with experts, resident-led, to discover and diagnose the village's resources and themes and draw out development tasks; a stage giving the chance to carry out part of the ideas in a village development plan as a small-scale project, raising residents' willingness to cooperate and building a base for continuing; and a resident-led project in which a village that has built capacity and drawn up a development plan sets and implements concrete goals. It records a national ministry running a village-making contest since 2014 to share and spread the results of resident-led village-making, for bottom-up regional development and capacity building. The structure around these centres is described, and so is its weakness. Published description records a capital's arrangement as a village network as the private partner building cooperative governance with the administration, a village community committee of public and private members deliberating and advising on policy, and a comprehensive support centre as the intermediary body, with resident proposal schemes covering village-making, village media, village enterprises and support for community spaces, in a process where residents lead planning, proposing, implementing and follow-up management. It records that no framework law on village communities has yet been enacted, with several bills introduced. Published research records the intermediary body's role as a group of experts helping community activation, finding and settling local success models, and acting as a local advice office, and records that a legal framework is urgently needed and a strong steering committee is important to secure the body's independence. Read this with the village lawyers, the citizens' trust, the environmental federation and the land use certificate entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Wild at Heart Legal Defense Association (台灣蠻野心足生態協會)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Taiwanese public-interest environmental law association founded by the lawyer Robin Winkler, which litigates against permits and environmental impact assessments rather than only commenting on them. Its cases run to a two-decade Indigenous land-rights dispute in Hualien, the Miramar Resort built on Shanyuan beach on what it argued were illegal construction licences, industrial park developments in central and southern Taiwan, an algae reef off the north-west coast threatened by port development, the Taipei Dome, and challenges to offshore wind-farm permits it says rested on deeply flawed assessments. WHO IT SUITS: a community or Indigenous group facing a permitted project where the EIA is the weak point. It is a small association that takes strategic cases and works alongside allied groups rather than running open legal aid. Note its English-language pages carry markedly older material than the Chinese site.

trackers.name: Constitutional Court
trackers.desc: Constitutional Court — supreme court (Taiwan).

trackers.name: DATA.GOV.TW
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Taiwan.

trackers.name: GCIS Business Registry
trackers.desc: Taiwan's Government Commerce Industrial Services company registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Judicial Yuan – Judgment Search
trackers.desc: Official portal of Taiwan's Judicial Yuan, including the Constitutional Court and a public judgment-search system. · Find here: the Judicial Yuan's judgment search covering Taiwan's courts.

trackers.name: Government e-Procurement (PCC)
trackers.desc: National public-procurement / budget-transparency portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this shows the specific firms winning specific tenders and contracts — for aggregate budget totals use the open-data/statistics portal, and for findings of waste use the audit body. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Taiwan, and for how much.

trackers.name: Taiwan — Lobbying Act register (Ministry of the Interior)
trackers.desc: National lobbying register; under the Lobbying Act (2007) lobbyists must register with the lobbied government agency before lobbying & file annual financial statements — the Ministry of the Interior is the designated competent authority, with public access to registrations, Taiwan. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held.

trackers.name: Fuchien High Court Kinmen Branch Court
trackers.desc: Fuchien High Court Kinmen Branch Court — tribunal in Taiwan (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Fuchien Kinmen District Court
trackers.desc: Fuchien Kinmen District Court — first instance court in Taiwan (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: 環境信託 — permanent protection, but check your land category first
trackers.desc: THE MECHANISM FOR PERMANENT PRIVATE PROTECTION, AND ITS PRICE.
