Under the 信託法 (Trust Act, 1996) an environmental trust is covered only by the catch-all at the end of article 69 — ‘or other trusts for the purpose of public interest’ — its full name being 環境保護公益信託. An owner finds a professional organisation, or acts themselves, as 受託人 (trustee), and the trustee applies to the environment authority with the period set as permanent. WHAT IT COSTS THE OWNER, STATED PLAINLY: the land must be transferred into the trustee's name and marked as trust property; it becomes independent, the original owner no longer owns it and has no power of disposal — and equally the trustee cannot dispose of it at will, which is exactly what makes the purpose permanently enforceable. An owner wanting to manage it themselves uses a 宣言信託 (declaration of trust). CHECK YOUR PARCEL CATEGORY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: under domestic law agricultural land and indigenous reserved land cannot be placed in environmental trust with a legal person not engaged in the relevant field; forest land can. That determines whether this route is open to you at all.

trackers.name: One case in thirty years — the tax reason, and the campaign precedent
trackers.desc: BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE ODDS, AND KNOW WHY. 自然谷環境信託基地 (Natural Valley, Hsinchu, 2011) is Taiwan's first and essentially only successful environmental trust since the Trust Act of 1996 — recognised as such by the environment ministry, and eligible to become an environmental education facility under the 環境教育法. On a 2020 review Taiwan had 281 financial-type public interest trusts worth NT$72.5 billion, but only 1 environment-related affairs-type trust and zero cultural heritage trusts. THE DECISIVE OBSTACLE IS TAX: the organisation behind Natural Valley concluded after years of practice and legal research that public interest trust taxation is unreasonable and unfair — donating land for environmental benefit brings no incentive and still attracts tax. Reform is an active campaign, so check the current position before assuming the cost. THE PRECEDENT WORTH COPYING IS A CAMPAIGN, NOT A COMPLETION: the first attempt was the 濁水溪口海埔地公益信託 over the Zhuoshui estuary tidal flats, launched with the slogan ‘everyone buy a share to guard the white dolphin’ to oppose the Kuokuang petrochemical development after IUCN listed the local white dolphin population as critically endangered. The trust was used as a mobilising instrument against a specific project — share subscription as public organising. WHO TO APPROACH: 台灣環境資訊協會 (TEIA), which set up an environmental trust centre in 2007 on Japanese and British models, and 自然保育與環境資訊基金會 (TNF), which campaigns for trust tax reform.

trackers.name: TNF 自然保育與環境資訊基金會 — will hold your land in trust; only two such trusts exist
trackers.desc: This is the trustee that takes the land itself, so it cannot be sold or developed by a later owner — the successor body to 台灣環境資訊協會 (TEIA), which after 22 years converted from an association into a foundation precisely because the association form's regulatory limits were blocking larger environmental public-interest trusts. It holds 自然谷環境信託基地 at 鹿寮坑, 芎林鄉, Hsinchu County: three people pooled money to buy the hillside in 2008, chose an environmental trust in 2011 with 荒野保護協會 as first trustee, and the trust passed to TEIA in June 2014 — the first environmental public-interest trust in Taiwan, an abandoned orchard now regenerated into low-elevation forest holding pangolin and crab-eating mongoose. The number that tells you how hard this route is: Taiwan has produced two. The second, 明知山有虎環境保護公益信託, is a 200-ping private plot behind 中興新村 in Nantou, donated by a private owner as leopard-cat habitat — a species down to 400–600 animals. The obstacle is tax, and it is unresolved: the Foundation's own 環境資訊中心 has campaigned for years against a 公益信託 tax regime it describes as penalising conservation and heritage trusts while favouring trust companies. That makes this slow rather than closed — approach them before land is sold or bequeathed, not after. Contact service@e-info.org.tw; office 3F, No. 48 Minquan Road, Xindian District, New Taipei City, by Dapinglin MRT.

trackers.name: 環境權保障基金會 ERF — free lawyers for development cases, paid for by a settlement residents won
trackers.desc: It exists because farmers won a settlement and made the government pay for the next community's lawyers. Six Houli farmers challenged the environmental impact assessment for phase three of the Central Taiwan Science Park; the case settled in the Taipei High Administrative Court in August 2014, and the settlement required the science ministry to endow a public-interest foundation with NT$30 million and a further NT$5 million a year for four years. That foundation is ERF. The tactic is worth carrying into any settlement negotiation anywhere: ask for the fund, not only the remedy. What it does for you is assign a lawyer. Anyone who believes a development project will affect their health or their environment can apply; after review, where ERF judges there is room to help, it appoints a lawyer to put the case in the EIA or hearing process, and researches the likely health risks first so that the demands made in that procedure are specific rather than general. Its three declared tasks are environmental rights legal aid, environmental monitoring and community empowerment, and it acts in non-litigation as well as litigation for communities and for indigenous tribes facing a development case. The land expropriation point it has established is the one to carry into any Taiwanese case. Arguing on the Shezidao zone expropriation, ERF holds that the Aerotropolis judgment settled that the public interest of an urban plan is not the same thing as the public interest of a land expropriation, and that the expropriation review panel must weigh the public interest and the necessity of taking each objecting petitioner's land individually rather than in bulk. The Shezidao petition ran to 1,156 residents. Take the addresses from the team page. Older listings still give the Taipei office as Xinsheng South Road and the Taichung office as Taiwan Boulevard; the current ones are 8F-1, No. 306 Guangfu South Road, Da'an, Taipei, 02-2391-5538, erf@erf.org.tw, and 10F-2, No. 4-33, Section 1 Shuangshi Road, East District, Taichung, 04-2329-2372, erftc@erf.org.tw. An English summary sits at erf.org.tw/en.

trackers.name: 地球公民基金會 Citizen of the Earth Taiwan — takes no government money, and has offices where the land fights are
trackers.desc: It was founded by its donors and refuses government funding, which is what lets it oppose a state policy directly. Begun in Kaohsiung in 2007 as an association and constituted as a foundation in January 2011 after merging with the Taiwan Environmental Action Network, it was capitalised by 174 individual donors — the first Taiwanese environmental foundation created by public subscription — and it declines government and corporate support. Offices in Kaohsiung, Taipei and Hualien mean somebody is based in the east, where the land expropriation and tourism development fights are, rather than only in the capital. Its subject is land use rather than a single species or pollutant. Its work runs across mountain and national land planning, eastern Taiwan's development, industrial pollution and energy transition, and it argues these through the spatial planning framework: which land is designated for what, where the exceptions are written, and how designations get broken afterwards. Its own analysis records 45,000 illegal factories on farmland nationwide, and makes the point that a use restriction unsupported by a comprehensive plan is one a developer can always overturn. That is the argument to take into a Taiwanese planning fight. Opposing a project on its merits is weaker than showing the designation it breaches and the plan that designation belongs to — and where the plan is missing, say so, because the absence is the vulnerability. Its method is field investigation and publication, not litigation. It surveys on the ground, publishes, holds press conferences and presses for a rule change, so pair it with the Environmental Rights Foundation when a lawyer is needed and with the Nature Conservation and Environmental Information Foundation when the answer is holding land in trust. All three are recorded here and they do different things.

trackers.name: 荒野保護協會 Society of Wilderness — takes guardianship of land by purchase, lease, donation or entrustment
trackers.desc: It states four ways it takes on land, and a community only needs one of them to work. The association's stated approach to habitat guardianship is to acquire custody and management rights over land by purchase, by long-term lease, by donation, or by accepting entrustment, and then to let the place run itself as far as possible. Where a purchase price cannot be raised, a long lease or an entrustment from a willing owner reaches the same result — and that is the conversation to have with an owner who does not want to sell but does not want the land developed either. Its Wugu wetland history is the model for public land. The association and other civic groups launched a conservation movement there in 2002, and in 2004 it entered an adoption agreement with the New Taipei City authority responsible for the high-beach land, taking on the wetland ecological park. A campaign that converts into a management agreement over public ground is the same ending Malaysia's nature society reached at Kuala Selangor, arrived at independently, and it is worth proposing wherever an agency owns land it cannot staff. The site attracted money once it had a guardian. In August 2025 a bank committed thirty million New Taiwan dollars over three years to a Tamsui river guardianship programme centred on that wetland, covering habitat restoration, scientific survey and environmental education. Securing management first and funding second is the order that worked. Approach the chapter, not the head office. The association runs chapters across Taiwan, each with its own volunteer groups including habitat teams — the Taipei chapter's cover park ecologisation, the Tamsui river, trail maintenance and the coast, while the Taichung chapter has run a guardianship programme on the Fazi river through citizen participation since April 2019. It also campaigns: current statements oppose waste soil being dumped into a port reclamation that would destroy Taiwanese white dolphin habitat, and press for water to be returned to a wetland in Taitung. Membership and volunteering are both open.

trackers.name: 環評書件查詢系統 — meeting notices, minutes and conclusions, and the duty to compare predictions with reality
trackers.desc: The system exists so that the public can see the file, and the ministry says so. Its stated purpose is to give the public a complete and convenient search over environmental impact assessment information, and to have competent authorities at every level, development units and sectoral authorities publish meeting notices, meeting minutes and review conclusions there — with the stated users being the general public and environmental groups following a case, alongside the developers obliged by the assessment statute to publish on the designated site. Meeting minutes and review conclusions together in one searchable place is more than most systems in this file offer. The tracking duty is the strongest post-approval provision recorded here. Under the statute the sectoral authority must track a development during construction and in use, the competent authority must supervise implementation of the statement, the assessment report and the review conclusions, and where necessary the developer may be ordered to submit periodic environmental impact investigation reports. Those reports must compare what happened against what was predicted. The developer is required to survey and analyse environmental conditions before the development and after it is in use, and to check them against the predicted results in its own assessment. A prediction that failed is therefore not something a community has to construct — it is a comparison the developer is obliged to make and file. Two further provisions are worth knowing. Where the authority finds adverse environmental impact it shall order the developer to submit countermeasures within a fixed period and, once those are approved, to carry them out faithfully; and in tracking or supervising a case the authority may exercise police powers. Separately, a review conclusion loses its effect if the sectoral authority revokes the development permit. County and city level documents and committee information sit in the same system alongside the central ones.

trackers.name: 特別景觀區土地價購 — the park administration buys, on the owner's application and in order of queue
trackers.desc: The purchase runs on the owner's own initiative, and the application date is the place in the queue. A national park administration has published operating principles, made under the National Park Act and an agency directive, for buying private land inside a special scenic area in order to carry out that area's purpose and to protect the rights of private landowners. Purchase is processed only where the private owner applies of their own motion and meets the stated conditions; qualifying cases are then recorded and handled year by year in the order of their application date, within the budget approved for each year, and applications already recorded before the principles were revised keep their existing order. Apply early even when the year's budget looks spent, because position carries forward. The statute behind it cuts both ways. Private land inside a national park may be kept in its original use so long as that does not obstruct the national park plan — but where private land is needed to implement the plan, it may be expropriated according to law. Refusing to sell is therefore not always the end of the matter, and an owner weighing an application should understand both limbs before deciding. There is a compensation right that almost nobody claims. To delimit a park or to make or change a park plan, the ministry or a body it has commissioned may send officials onto public and private land to survey — but the landowner or occupier must be notified in advance, and where crops, bamboo, trees or other obstacles are damaged in the course of that survey, compensation must be paid, the amount agreed between the parties and, if they cannot agree, determined by the superior agency. Photograph and record damage at the time it occurs, not afterwards. Check your own park's rules rather than assuming. The principles cited here belong to one park administration; ask the administration for the park covering your land whether it has published equivalent purchase principles, what conditions apply and what budget has been allocated. Read this alongside the Korean and Japanese entries recorded here, where the state also buys protected private land on the owner's application.

trackers.name: 社區林業計畫 — an annual community grant, applications 1–31 October, paid half up front
trackers.desc: The applicant must be a registered body, and there are two tiers. The forestry and conservation agency's community forestry programme, running since 2002, funds partnerships with communities and mountain village settlements to share forest management and nature conservation and to build community self-reliance. Applicants must be legally registered non-profit bodies concerned with community affairs — community development associations, cultural and historical workshops, foundations and cooperatives — with university mountaineering clubs admitted through their institution for the patrol project only. A first-time applicant takes the starter tier; a body that has run a plan before with good results and the capacity for more may be approved by its regional branch for the advanced tier. The calendar is fixed, tight and unforgiving. Proposals go to the local work station between 1 and 31 October; the branch completes preliminary, joint and final approval by 31 December; and implementation and closure normally run from 1 January to 31 October of the following year. One grant per applicant per year is the principle, and the previous year's plan must be completed and closed before the next application is made. A community that misses October waits a year. Half the money arrives up front and half after the report. Fifty per cent is disbursed on approval, the community implements, and the balance follows the results report and final settlement — so the group must be able to carry half the cost until its report is accepted. Work that out before writing the proposal rather than after the first payment. The forest protection chapter asks for what an affected community already does. It covers assisting fire prevention and firefighting and clearing fuel along important trails; patrolling a chosen area and reporting fires and disasters; reporting illegal logging, illegal clearing and poaching; and building a network through which residents proactively report harm to forest and wildlife resources. Other chapters cover environmental resource inventory, ecological conservation, ecotourism, passing on traditional community skills and the under-forest economy. Proposals are submitted through the programme's own application portal.

trackers.name: 環境檢驗測定機構許可資料 — the register of licensed testing laboratories, and the grounds for revoking one
trackers.desc: A published register of every licensed environmental testing organisation, with permit numbers and expiry dates. The ministry publishes permit data for environmental testing and measurement organisations including the permit certificate number, the laboratory code, the organisation name, the permit validity period, and each laboratory's name, address, telephone and fax. Check the permit and its expiry before commissioning anybody — and check the same for whichever laboratory produced the figures in a developer's report. A permit is not a formality. An organisation must hold a permit from the central authority before carrying out testing authorised under the environmental laws, must have a dedicated laboratory with its own instruments, and must employ at least six full-time testing personnel including a laboratory supervisor and quality assurance staff, with a lower threshold of two where the applicant is a government body, alongside a capital or registered asset requirement. Applications are reviewed by the ministry's national environmental research academy through document review, performance evaluation that can include practical examination, blind samples and on-site comparison testing, and system evaluation by two or more on-site expert assessors. The disciplinary grounds are the part a community can use. A permit may be revoked where an organisation fails to submit blind sample results within the period or refuses to take part in sampling technique evaluation or blind testing; where it fails two consecutive evaluations; where it keeps testing after expiry or revocation; where it performs authorised testing without a permit; and — the ground worth remembering — where a sampling trip has been declared but nobody actually attended to take the samples, or the sampling time or place was declared falsely. A community that watches the site and writes down who arrived, when and where they sampled has a specific and named complaint rather than a suspicion. Use it alongside the assessment document system. Once a permit is revoked for a test item the organisation must stop testing that item from the day the decision is served. The environmental impact assessment records already noted in this file name the consultant; this register shows whether its laboratory was licensed and current; and the sampling declaration can be measured against what people on the ground actually saw.

trackers.name: 公害陳情 — one national line, a tracked case number, and a result you can look up on a stated day
trackers.desc: Three routes, and the system publishes every local bureau's number. A national toll-free complaint line answers pollution reports, staffed by the county and city environmental bureaus or by the ministry's northern, central and southern inspection corps; an online reception system takes reports and lets a complainant query a case; and a mobile application files reports with satellite positioning so the address does not have to be typed, using plain pictorial categories for the type of pollution. The system also publishes a table of the report centre telephone numbers for every local environmental bureau in the country. State four things, and understand why the name is asked for. A report should specifically describe the location of the subject complained of, the category of pollution and the state of it, and give a real name and contact details so that inspectors can attend the site. Personal data is kept strictly confidential under the ministry's own confidentiality rules for handling public complaints and under the personal data protection law: the name is there for the inspector, not for the operator. The case number is the part that matters. A report filed online or through the application can be queried by case number to follow its progress; after the ministry receives it, the case is cross-checked over the network connecting it to the local environmental bureaus, the result is returned online, and the complainant is told they may query the outcome on the system after seven working days. Nothing else recorded in this file gives a complainant a tracked case number together with a stated day on which to go and look. Ask to accompany the inspection. A metropolitan environmental bureau's own guidance recommends using the city hotline first, because it is faster and because the inspectors may attend together with the complainant; and the ministry has announced that reports verified as true may be put forward for a reward. Read this with the register of licensed testing laboratories recorded for this country: the report brings an inspector, and the register tells you whether the laboratory behind any resulting figures was licensed for that test.

trackers.name: 法律扶助基金會 — 22 branches, apply at the nearest one, and no agent should ever charge you
trackers.desc: Case type is not the obstacle. The foundation was endowed by the judicial branch under the legal aid act passed at the end of 2003, registered in 2004 and taking applications since that July, and it provides legal consultation and the assignment of a legal aid lawyer to conduct proceedings, draft documents or help settle a dispute. Its own explanation of eligibility states that in principle there is no restriction on the type of case, though some civil, criminal and administrative matters require the consent of the branch director before aid is granted. An environmental or land case is therefore not excluded by category — the question is means and merits, not subject. Apply at the nearest branch, not the branch where the case is. The foundation runs twenty-two branches across the country together with an indigenous peoples legal service centre, and states plainly that the review is carried out by whichever branch is convenient for the applicant to reach rather than the one covering the location of the case. Appointments are made through the national telephone line or the online booking system. That is the opposite of the rule recorded in this file for Korea, where representation moves faster from the office at the competent court — two neighbours, two conventions, and worth checking rather than assuming. Two tests, with waivers and projects. A branch reviews the applicant's means and the merits of the case and a review committee decides. The means review is waived for certain categories, including low income and middle-low income households and families in special circumstances; and an applicant who exceeds the means standard may still fall inside one of the foundation's special assistance projects, which relax it. Bring the household's property holdings list and the past year's income tax data, obtained from the tax bureau, and bring proof of indigenous status or disability if either applies, because other projects may then be available. No agent should ever charge you for this. The foundation states that it has not commissioned any agency company to handle legal aid applications and warns against the sales patter of firms that charge high fees to do so. Applying costs nothing; after approval there may be partial cost-sharing, and where a lawyer's fee is later reduced or cancelled any excess the assisted person has paid is refunded. Read this with the environmental rights foundation entry already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 第二類謄本 — anyone may apply, and a company owner's name is not masked
trackers.desc: Three classes of transcript, and the middle one is open to anybody. Since the land registration rules were amended, a land registration and land value transcript comes in three classes. The first shows the registered holder's full data and may be applied for only by the holder or by others entitled by law. The second may be applied for by anyone, and conceals a natural person holder's date of birth, part of the name and part of the identification number, the debtor and debt ratio and the party granting an encumbrance. The third is for an interested party carrying a legal duty to notify or whose rights are affected. Where the holder is a company, nothing is masked. The concealment in the open class applies to natural persons: the name and unified identification number of a non-natural person are expressly not concealed, and neither are entries recording a restriction on registration. For a community facing a corporate developer that is the whole point — the class of transcript anyone may obtain gives the company's identity in full, and shows whether the land carries a registration restriction. Any land office, for the whole country. Applications may be made at any land office, and a city land office can issue cadastral transcript data for all of the country's counties and cities; electronic transcripts issued through the government certificate and electronic signature mechanism have the same effect as paper ones and can be verified through a published checking service. The first class obtained online requires a citizen or business digital certificate. Ask for the change index, not only the current page. The services extend beyond ownership to land and building registration transcripts, land value transcripts, cadastral map transcripts, building survey result maps, a cadastral change index and change lists, land reference information and building address lookup, alongside a real-time cadastral change notification service. A change index tells a community what has moved and when; the notification service tells it as the change happens. Read this with the environmental assessment records and licensed testing laboratory entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 政府資訊公開法 — public works and procurement contracts are proactive disclosure, and fees waive for public interest
trackers.desc: The contract is on the list that must be published without anyone asking. The act names ten categories of government information which must be disclosed proactively unless a restriction applies: laws and regulations; the interpretive rules and discretionary criteria an agency issues to guide its own decisions; the agency's organisation, address, telephone, fax, website and email; documents relating to administrative guidance; policy plans, business statistics and research reports; budget and final account statements; the results of petitions and the decisions on administrative appeals; written public works and procurement contracts; subsidies paid or received; and the minutes of collegiate bodies. For a community facing a public works project, both the contract and any subsidy sit on that list already. Fifteen days, one extension, and a consultation step for affected parties. An agency must decide whether to grant a request within fifteen days of accepting it, extendable once by no more than fifteen further days. Where the information concerns the rights and interests of a particular individual, legal person or group, the agency must first notify that party in writing to give an opinion within ten days, publishing the notice where their whereabouts are unknown, and may decide without the opinion if none is given in time. Fees can be reduced or waived for research or public benefit. The agency may charge according to the purpose for which the information is sought, and fees may be reduced or waived where the application is for academic research or for a public interest purpose. State the purpose in the application rather than leaving it blank. And the reviewing body may read the withheld documents in secret. Where a dispute over disclosure reaches the administrative appeal authority or the administrative courts, all or part of the government information may be examined in closed proceedings, and public officials who breach the act are subject to discipline according to the seriousness of the breach. Nationals with household registration and domestic legal persons and groups may apply, as may nationals abroad holding a passport, and foreign nationals where their own country does not restrict applications by nationals of this jurisdiction. Read this with the transcript classes, the assessment records, the licensed laboratory register and the community forestry entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 環境法律人協會 EJA — a case application form, fifty-three volunteer lawyers, and their own ninety per cent figure
trackers.desc: There is an application form for a case. The association asks anyone who needs help with pollution of any kind — soil, air, water or chemical — or with an environmental impact assessment, land development, land expropriation, science park development, old trees, cultural assets, urban renewal or urban planning, to complete its public interest litigation case application form and send it back. Filling in a form is a much lower step for a village committee than finding and approaching a lawyer cold, and the categories it lists are precisely the ones a development fight falls into. They publish the odds before they take the case. Their own material states that in administrative litigation people lose as often as ninety per cent of the time, and describes the difficulty plainly: residents without specialist knowledge facing an improper development are a small shrimp against a whale. Their stated task is to assemble a professional team of lawyers, expert scholars and civil society groups to accompany residents through the litigation and through discussion of campaign strategy. An organisation that tells you the base rate first is one a community can actually plan around. The team and the docket are stated. It was founded in 2010 by lawyers who considered that environmental cases sat in a weak position within the public legal aid system; fifty-three lawyers have volunteered in its litigation work. Its matters include assessment revocation suits over a road and a wire factory, an aerotropolis series covering assessment, land expropriation and urban planning together, a land readjustment scheme, an island redevelopment, climate litigation, and a transnational damages action over marine pollution from a steel plant abroad. The expropriation and urban planning matters are the ones that most resemble an ordinary community's fight. They also work on the rules themselves. Their law reform work has covered toxic chemical management, reform of the hearing system, campsite regulation and noise control, pursued through parliamentary lobbying, visits to administrative agencies, local organising, public advocacy and attendance at meetings; and since 2024 they have taken public interest cases beyond the strictly environmental, including a building proposed inside a natural park, an expropriation dispute and a heritage preservation action. Read this with the environmental rights foundation, the legal aid foundation, the assessment document search and the licensed testing laboratory register entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 農地銀行 — a public listing platform, matching through the local farmers' association, and a standard lease contract
trackers.desc: A public platform lists farmland for rent and for sale, and the local association does the matching. The agency describes the farmland bank as a website platform established in 2007 that provides information on farmland for lease and sale, knowledge about buying and selling, the law governing farmland use, and production, marketing and agricultural lending information, with farmers' and fishermen's associations acting as the matchmaking agents for the leasing and sale of farmland; a later rental platform version continues the service, and farmland bank service centres were established across township associations. For an owner under pressure to sell to a developer, a listed tenant found through a public body is the alternative to a buyer, and it is reached without an agent's commission. The procedure is written down, document by document. Under the published scheme rules a landlord brings the title deed or a land registry transcript issued within the last three months, an identity document and a seal, files the prescribed listing application with the association where the land lies, and has the offer posted on the ministry's rental platform; a prospective tenant files the corresponding rental need application; the association then matches the two, confirms the actual cultivable area, the rent, the term and the method of payment, and assists both parties to sign the standard agricultural land lease contract, executed in two originals with a copy retained by the association. A standard contract witnessed by a public body is protection that an informal tenancy does not provide to either side. The money attached is real. Published descriptions of the accompanying policy record interest-free loans for farmland rent and operating loans at one per cent, with a ceiling for individual professional farmers and a higher ceiling for organisational tenants, over terms of up to twenty years, together with disaster recovery lending for organisational tenants after a natural disaster. Money to work land one does not own is the piece most tenancy schemes leave out. Notes and limits. Official guidance records that leasing farmland is not affected by the older statute on rent reduction, which is the fear that keeps many owners from letting land at all; that associations may contact prospective tenants directly for owners who prefer not to join the bank; and that municipal governments separately publish their own city-owned farmland available for lease. Read this with the land title transcript, the environmental rights foundation, the second litigation body and the licensed testing laboratory entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 監察院陳情 and the human rights commission — a duty member every day, confidentiality on request, and corrective measures
trackers.desc: Anyone may report an agency's unlawful act or neglect of duty. The control statute allows the Yuan and its members to receive written statements from the public, and the guidance directs a person who finds an administrative agency or public servant acting unlawfully or neglecting their duties to state the facts in detail and to list the evidence. The published template for a statement asks for the sequence of events set out by person, matter, time, place and thing; the unlawful or improper conduct and how it is to be proved, including which law was broken; the specific request being made; and copies of the relevant evidence and documents, including agency letters and any court decisions. That structure is itself a drafting guide worth following. Confidentiality is available on request. The handling regulations require a statement to carry the complainant's real name and identifying particulars, and those of a legal person or group where one is complaining; but they also provide that where the circumstances make it inappropriate, or where the complainant states that they do not wish their name to be published, the Yuan shall keep it confidential. There is a duty member every weekday, and members take complaints on inspection visits. The published channels are post, which remains the bulk of cases; the complaint reception centre where a rostered member receives people in person each weekday; complaints made to members during their inspection visits to local agencies; an online complaint mailbox; and appointments for counter or video complaints. A body whose members travel to local agencies and take complaints while there is unusual, and asking when the next inspection visit to a county falls is a practical question with a published calendar behind it. Rights infringements are routed to the human rights commission. The regulations direct statements involving torture, infringement of human rights or discrimination to the national human rights commission constituted within the Yuan; that commission operates its own complaint system with separate routes for individuals and for legal persons and organisations, and complaints filed through it can be tracked for progress. The Yuan's own powers include investigation and the issuing of corrective measures to agencies, with investigation reports and corrective case texts published on its site. Read this with the two environmental litigation organisations, the assessment document search, the licensed testing laboratory register and the farmland bank entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 報導者 The Reporter — donor rules that bind the funders, no paywall, and a site that hides click counts
trackers.desc: The ethics rules are published, and they bind the funders rather than the reporters. The foundation behind the outlet has adopted work ethics rules stating that its directors and supervisors may not become involved in or interfere with any news case or news content; that all donors accept three principles — not to own, not to interfere, and not to reclaim — so that no news handling is influenced by a donor; that where either of those rules is engaged a supervisor examines whether independence has been maintained; and that full-time staff may not hold outside paid positions or write for commercial media without the foundation's consent. For a community whose opponent has money locally, those rules are the reason a story cannot simply be bought out of the coverage. The funding excludes the usual pressure points. Its own account records operations funded solely by public donations, with no commercial advertising, no placement marketing, no government tenders and no party or politician sponsorship, and it has declined to build a paywall so that issues can reach as many people as possible, inviting readers to share its content, which is released under an open licence. That matters practically: material published there can be reproduced and circulated by the community itself rather than sitting behind a subscription. The site does not display click counts. Its published description records that no view numbers appear on its reports, so that reporters are not pulled toward traffic and issues followed by fewer people are not neglected. A village dispute with no national audience is precisely the kind of story that policy exists to protect, and it is worth naming when making an approach. What it is, and how it works. Founded in December 2015 as the country's first online media outlet established by a public-interest foundation, with a foundation board, a full-time newsroom of around twenty-five people, and membership of the global investigative journalism network, it describes its method as long field investigation, interviewing the parties with an interest in the events, and thorough verification and follow-up, with its output aimed at supervising government policy and changing rules. A contact address is published. Read this with the environmental law association, the licensed testing laboratory register, the assessment document search and the control yuan complaint entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 文化資產保存法 — an individual or group may report a building, and an emergency listing protects it while the review runs
trackers.desc: An individual or a group may report a building, and the authority then has six months. The cultural heritage preservation legislation requires the competent authority to conduct periodic surveys or to accept reports from individuals or groups of the content and scope of anything having the value of a monument, a historic building, a commemorative building or a settlement building group, and, after review under the statutory procedure, to place it on a tracking list. Where the report comes from an individual or a group, the authority must carry out the review within six months. The same structure applies to historic sites and cultural landscapes, which the municipal or county authority must survey or accept reports on, again with a six-month review, and to antiquities. A single resident may therefore start the process and hold the authority to a date. Emergency listing as a provisional monument, before the review even begins. A building that has entered the designation review procedure is a provisional monument; and where a building of monument value has not yet entered that procedure, the authority may in an emergency list it directly as a provisional monument and notify the owner, the user or the manager. During the review period a provisional monument is treated as a monument and must be managed and maintained. That is the provision to point to when demolition is imminent and no designation exists. Six months, extendable once, and then it lapses. The review period for a provisional monument is limited to six months, extendable once where necessary; the authority must complete the review within the period, and on expiry the provisional status loses its effect. The protection is therefore real but time-bound, and the date the clock started is the thing to record. Where listing as a provisional monument causes loss to the property of a rights-holder, the authority must give reasonable compensation, the amount being fixed by agreement. Inside preservation land, felling and earth-taking need joint handling. Within land or zones designated for monument preservation, applications for the construction, extension, alteration, repair, relocation or demolition of buildings and other works, or other changes to their external form or colour; the formation of housing land, the reclamation of land, the repair or widening of roads and other changes to the form of the land; the felling of bamboo and timber and the extraction of earth and stone; and the erection of advertising structures, must be handled by the purpose-related authority together with the cultural authority. Public buildings and their attached facilities more than fifty years old, and those on public land, must be assessed for cultural asset value by the authority before they are disposed of. Read this with the environmental rights foundation's free lawyers, the assessment document search, the land trust and the control yuan complaint entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 土地徵收條例 — a market-price purchase must be attempted first, thirty days to dispute the price, and a twenty-year right to buy the land back
trackers.desc: A market-price purchase must be attempted before any expropriation. The expropriation statute requires the party needing the land to negotiate a purchase with the owner at market price before applying to expropriate, and only where that negotiation fails may the application be made. Published official commentary records how the market price is to be arrived at: by reference to relevant public government information, to information from real estate agencies, by commissioning a licensed real estate appraiser, or by asking the municipal or county government where the land lies to supply it — and that the acquiring body must explain in detail how the figure was set and make every effort to reach agreement. Asking which of those sources produced the offer is the first question at the negotiation stage. A public hearing is required, and in some cases a formal hearing. The party needing the land must hold a public hearing; and where a project on a special agricultural zone has been approved as a major construction and there is dispute, a formal hearing under the administrative procedure legislation must be held instead. For area expropriation, the local government convenes the public hearing with the needing party and the landowners before the case goes to the central authority for approval. Thirty days from the day after the announcement to dispute the price. Once the central authority approves, the municipal or county government must announce the expropriation publicly for thirty days and notify rights-holders in writing, and pay compensation within fifteen days of the end of that period. A rights-holder objecting to the announced matters may object in writing during the announcement period; but an objection to the amount of compensation must be made in writing within thirty days counted from the day after the announcement period ends. The authority must investigate and notify the outcome in writing, and where the objector is dissatisfied the authority may refer the matter to the land price evaluation committee for reconsideration, after which ordinary administrative remedies follow — and published analysis records that a supreme administrative court resolution treats the reconsideration as a step that cannot be skipped, while a failure by the authority to deal with it can itself be challenged. Two provisions worth knowing before signing anything. Where compensation has been paid in full and three years pass without the land being used according to the expropriation plan, or it is used for something other than the approved undertaking, or use ceases within five years of starting, the original owner may apply within twenty years of the announcement to buy the land back at the original compensation price. And where a low or lower-middle income household that had lived there for a year before the announcement loses its only dwelling, the needing party must draw up a resettlement plan and set it out in the expropriation plan, the resettlement including housing, mortgage interest subsidy or rent subsidy. Read this with the environmental rights foundation's free lawyers, the legal aid foundation's branches, the land register extract and the assessment document search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Checking and hiring an appraiser — the ministry's register of licensed practitioners, and the actual transaction price database behind any figure
trackers.desc: The ministry publishes who is legally allowed to value your land. The land administration department runs a query service covering legally practising land administration agents, real estate appraisers, brokerages and rental housing service businesses together with their employed personnel. Before paying for a valuation to set against an official figure, check that the person appears there: the certificate and practice certificate are what the register records, and the fees for issuing them are themselves set by regulation. Municipal land bureaux run their own sections for appraisers and their own searches for legally operating real estate service businesses, and at least one publishes a roster of commended appraisers, which is a starting point when a community has no way of telling one practitioner from another. The professional bodies are organised nationally. Appraisers are organised in municipal associations under a national federation of appraiser associations, which is the route to a practitioner in a particular city and to the professional standards they work to. Where a dispute needs more than a valuation — appraisers, lawyers, accountants and civil engineers appearing together — the federation is where that combination is assembled. The transaction price database is the evidence behind any number. The ministry also operates the actual transaction price query service, in which registered sale prices are published. That database is what makes an argument about value checkable rather than rhetorical: it is the same source an acquiring body may draw on when it sets a market price, and a community can read it first. How this fits the acquisition entries. The expropriation statute recorded elsewhere in this country's entries requires a market-price purchase to be attempted before any acquisition, and allows the price to be set by reference to public government information or by commissioning a licensed appraiser. This entry is the practical half of that: check the register, use the transaction database, and know what a commissioned appraisal costs before deciding whether to commission one. Read this with the expropriation statute, the land register extract, the environmental testing laboratory register and the legal aid foundation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 法學資料檢索系統 — judgments online within days of service, searchable in full text, with the case number shortcut
trackers.desc: Judgments appear within days, not months. The judicial branch's legal information retrieval system publishes its own timing rules: decisions of the supreme court and the supreme administrative court become searchable one month after the ruling, while for every other court the judgment is available within two days of the clerk preparing the original and serving it on the parties — the preparation itself taking seven days from receipt in criminal cases and ten in civil ones. For a community following a comparable case in a neighbouring county, that timetable means the outcome is readable almost as soon as the parties have it. Full-text search, and a case-number shortcut worth knowing. The system offers full-text searching across judgments alongside the regulations, interpretations and rulings sections, and its own instructions show a compact way to search: typing a case number in short form retrieves that numbered case across all courts. The retrieval service covers regulations administered by the judiciary, adjudication-related regulations, interpretations and rulings, judgment searches, summary case searches and public notice procedures, and it suggests related terms as you type. Read the caveats the system states about itself. It records that the data is for reference and that where it differs from the original judgment the original prevails; and that since a date in 2010, under an amended provision of the courts organisation legislation, the names of natural persons are disclosed, without retrospective effect, under published redaction rules. A judgment printed from the system is a research copy, not a certified one — if a document is to be filed, obtain the official version. Where to point it. Search the administrative court judgments for the subjects that decide local disputes: expropriation and compensation references, the environmental assessment challenges, land registration and heritage designations. The administrative courts publish their own guidance on finding superseded precedents through the same system, which matters when an older authority is being cited at you. Read this with the expropriation statute, the appraiser register and transaction price database, the assessment document search and the legal aid foundation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 公益勸募 — the permit you need before asking the public for money, the 21-day lead time, and the register of approved appeals
trackers.desc: Public fundraising for a public-benefit purpose requires a permit, and only certain bodies can hold one. The charitable fundraising legislation names the bodies that may fundraise: public schools, administrative juridical persons, public-benefit incorporated associations and incorporated foundations. Government agencies may accept unsolicited donations for public purposes but may not initiate an appeal, except in major disasters or international relief. A community group that is not incorporated therefore raises money through a registered association or foundation, not in its own name — establishing that relationship is the first step, not the last. Twenty-one days before you start, with named documents. Official guidance records that an application must be filed at least twenty-one days before the appeal begins, through the ministry's fundraising management system, to the municipal or county authority where the appeal takes place, or to the central authority where it crosses jurisdictions — with an appeal conducted only through media, internet or mailed publicity treated as taking place where the fundraising body is located. A dedicated donation account must be opened at a post office or financial institution and reported to the authority within seven days of the appeal starting. The obligations that follow are the reason donors trust it. An appeal may run for at most one year, after which all fundraising and publicity must stop; receipts must state the permit number, the donor, the amount or goods and the date; public accounting must be published at least every six months covering donors' basic details and the conduct of the appeal, on the body's own website or publication, or in a newspaper or electronic media if it has none; the proceeds must be held in a dedicated account and used only for the stated plan, with a dedicated ledger; and necessary expenses may be met from the proceeds within stated percentage limits, published guidance recording fifteen per cent where proceeds are ten million yuan or below. Penalties, and the boundary of the law. Fundraising by a body not named in the statute, without permission, after a permit is revoked, or beyond the permitted period attracts a fine within a published range, with the responsible person named publicly and repeat penalties possible. Commentary records that the statute governs appeals for public benefit — for the benefit of unspecified persons — and that private appeals fall outside it, while fraud remains punishable under the criminal law. Check who is licensed before you give. The ministry publishes a search of permitted appeals showing the fundraising period, the target amount, the permit number and the plan documents. Read this with the wilderness guardianship, the park land purchase, the appraiser register and the judgment search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 土石採取法 — boundary posts and a site notice board, joint on-site inspection by seven agencies, and the no-extraction zone anyone can ask for
trackers.desc: Approval requires a joint site inspection by named agencies, not a desk review. The soil and rock extraction legislation provides that when a municipal or county authority reviews an application for an extraction permit it must conduct an on-site inspection jointly with the agencies for water resources, fisheries, soil and water conservation, transport, environmental protection, land use and management and other relevant bodies, and may issue the permit only after review finds no breach of the governing laws and the central authority has reviewed it. The extraction plan drawings must be certified by a legally registered mining engineer or other relevant professional engineer, and the boundaries, area and depth of the application area are fixed by survey methods published by the central authority. Each of those agencies is a body a community can write to before the inspection. Boundary posts and a notice board must be in place before the site registration certificate issues. The Act requires the operator to set up boundary posts and a site notice board, to preserve and maintain them, and to apply within six months of receiving the permit for the site registration certificate before starting work, with extension possible twice for good reason; the authority issues that certificate after checking the site facilities match the submitted extraction plan. Extraction must follow the approved plan and carry out soil and water conservation, environmental maintenance, restoration and disaster prevention measures. Posts and board are physical things to check against the plan. Time limits differ by where the extraction is. Permits for extraction in rivers and water bodies run a maximum of three years and may not be extended on expiry; on land, coastal and sea area permits run a maximum of ten years, with extension applications treated the same way. An operator may continue extracting while an extension application is pending decision, which is worth knowing when work continues past an expiry date. A no-extraction zone can be requested by the agency responsible for what is being harmed. The Act allows an agency with responsibility for water sources, water conservancy, traffic safety, urban development, environmental landscape or other public interest needs to apply to the central authority to designate a no-extraction zone, with compensation payable to an operator who suffers loss, and requires the local authority to revoke all or part of a permit for an extraction area inside a designated zone. Persuading the responsible agency to apply is a route a community can take. An environmental maintenance fee is collected when the permit issues, and the Act lists the exemptions from permitting, including small quantities for own use and extraction by indigenous people under the indigenous peoples basic legislation, with land in or around indigenous territory subject to that legislation's consultation provision. Read this with the environmental rights foundation, the legal aid foundation, the indigenous consultation entry and the judgment search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 都市計畫公開展覽 — thirty days and a briefing session before the committee sees the plan, any citizen or group may write in, and the review has a sixty-day clock
trackers.desc: Any citizen or group may write in, and they must be able to, before the committee even considers the plan. The city planning legislation provides that after a main plan is drafted and before it is sent to the competent government's city planning committee for review, it shall be publicly displayed for thirty days at the municipal or county government and at the township, town or county-administered city office, and a briefing session held, with the dates and places of both published in a newspaper or electronic news outlet; and that any citizen or group may, during the display period, submit a written opinion to the competent government stating their name and address, which the city planning committee shall take into account in its review, the review result being reported to the interior ministry together with the main plan for approval. The words are any citizen or group — not only owners, not only residents. Timing, and one trap. The Act provides that the committee's review shall be completed within sixty days, extendable once by a further sixty days in special circumstances; and that where the committee amends the plan in review, or the ministry directs amendment, no further public display or briefing session is required. An amended plan can therefore reach approval without a second display, which is why an opinion filed in the first window matters. A municipal implementing rule records that a written opinion under this section must be delivered before the committee completes its review, that the briefing session is to be held during the display period, and that the government reports the review result, plan documents and drawings to the ministry within forty-five days of the committee finishing. The periodic review is a second window, and it comes round. The Act provides that a plan may not be altered arbitrarily after promulgation, but the drafting authority shall carry out a general review at least once every three or five years, making necessary changes according to development conditions and with reference to people's suggestions, and shall change the use of unnecessary public facility land. The general review regulations require the authority, before the review, to announce the review scope and related documents for thirty days at the same offices and hold a discussion meeting, publishing the comment period and meeting details in the government gazette, on the internet and in a newspaper or electronic news outlet, with groups or people able to submit written opinions stating name and address. Detail plans follow the same route, and can be initiated by owners. The Act applies the same drafting, review, display and promulgation provisions to detail plans, and allows land rights holders to draft or change a detail plan themselves in line with the local district development plan, attaching business and financial plans, with a route to the ministry or county government if refused. Read this with the assessment document system, the expropriation entry, the cultural property reporting entry and the extraction permit entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 受保護樹木 — the five-yearly tree census, the measurable thresholds, in-place retention inside a development, and the public briefing before a transplant
trackers.desc: The local authority must survey the trees in its area and publish a register. The forestry legislation's tree protection chapter provides that the local competent authority shall carry out a census of trees in its jurisdiction, and that clustered bamboo and trees, street trees or single trees with ecological, biological, geographical, landscape, cultural, historical, educational, research, community or other significant meaning, once recognised by that authority as protected trees, shall be listed and publicly announced; and that for announced trees the authority shall give priority to strengthened protection, maintain natural crown growth and tree quality, carry out periodic health checks and maintenance, protect the growing environment and publish their current condition regularly on its own webpage. Community, cultural and historical meaning are grounds in their own right, not only size. The thresholds are published numbers. The recognition standard made under that chapter records that a tree outside a forest qualifies where, at 1.3 metres above ground, a broadleaf has a diameter of 1.5 metres or more or a girth of 4.7 metres or more, or a conifer a diameter of 0.75 metres or more or a girth of 2.4 metres or more; where the crown projection area reaches 400 square metres or more; or where the tree's growing site forms an ecological environment rich in biodiversity. It requires the authority to conduct the census at least once every five years, and sets what must be recorded. Measure the trunk at 1.3 metres before anything else. Inside a development, retention in place is the rule. The legislation provides that where an announced protected tree stands within the scope of land development and use, it shall in principle be retained in place; that without the local authority's permission it may not be arbitrarily felled, transplanted, pruned or damaged in any other way, and its good growing environment must be maintained; and that a developer needing to transplant one must submit a transplanting and restoration plan for review and permission before work may begin. Official material records that breach carries a fine in a stated band, and that pruning, transplanting and management must be handled by qualified forestry and related professionals. A public briefing comes before the move. The ministry's explanation of the chapter records that, in order to gather opinions from all quarters on transplanting a protected tree, the developer must first hold a public briefing session. It also records that the listing and announcement must be notified in writing to the landowner, user or manager, with the register carrying the tree's number, species, Chinese and scientific names, quantity, breast-height diameter and girth, a crown projection overlay map and estimated age; and that an announcement may be revoked where the tree suffers major biological harm, cannot survive natural disaster, threatens public safety or loses its protective meaning. Read this with the extraction permit entry, the city plan display window, the cultural property reporting entry and the land trust entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 水質水量保護區 — eleven activities that can be banned in a water quality and quantity protection zone, the tax relief for restricted land, and the levy that funds the affected village
trackers.desc: Inside a protection zone the statute lists eleven kinds of activity that can be prohibited or restricted. The water supply legislation provides that a water utility may, in addition to applying under the water law, apply to the competent authority to consult relevant agencies and designate and announce a water quality and quantity protection zone, prohibiting or restricting the listed harmful activities: excessive felling of timber or unauthorised land clearance; altering a river course to an extent affecting water's self-purification capacity; earth and rock extraction, prospecting or mining that pollutes the source; discharge of industrial, mining or domestic wastewater above standards or above a total load set by the sectoral authority; polluting factories; setting up a landfill or incinerator, or dumping or abandoning refuse, ash, earth and rock, sludge, manure, waste oil, waste chemicals, animal carcasses or other things able to pollute the source; pig farming in the catchment above an important intake designated by the environmental authority, and other for-profit poultry and livestock keeping; construction or extension of a golf course; development of nuclear or other energy, and construction of radioactive waste storage or treatment sites; and other activities announced as harmful. That list is the first thing to read against a project upstream of an intake. The exception is narrow, and worth quoting alongside. The same provision states that those activities are not prohibited where they are necessary for residents' living or for local public construction and approved by the competent authority — so a commercial project cannot rely on the exception simply because it is local. Restricted land gets tax relief, and there is a levy for the village. The Act provides that where a protection zone is designated as a water source special district through the urban planning procedure, the land shall receive reduction or exemption of land value increment tax, gift tax and estate tax according to the degree of restriction, on standards set jointly by the finance and interior ministries and approved by the executive; and that the water utility shall levy a set proportion on top of the water price to assist local construction in the restricted area or those whose rights are restricted, with a conservation and feedback fee payable by those taking surface or ground water in the zone other than non-profit household and public supply. Designation has published criteria and a marker on the ground. The ministry's operating points record that a zone covers the area drained above the intake and any area below it needing joint protection, the defined area around a spring or groundwater source including geologically sensitive recharge areas, and the catchment above a diversion point where a reservoir's inflow is drawn from another basin; and rules made under the Act record that an application must include a detailed plan with the source's condition, the reason, extent and area of the zone, and a topographic map at a scale no smaller than one in three thousand, with the utility required to erect markers at suitable points on the ground once the zone is announced. Read this with the extraction permit entry, the city plan display window, the environmental rights foundation and the land trust entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 專用漁業權 — the exclusive coastal fishery right held only by a fishermen's association, the eight grounds for revoking it, and the compensation the developer must negotiate
trackers.desc: Only a fishermen's association or a fishery production cooperative may hold the exclusive coastal fishery right. The fisheries legislation defines an exclusive fishery right as the right to use a defined water area as a fishing ground, admitting entry-right holders, to operate fisheries taking or culturing aquatic animals and plants or taking aquatic animals with fixed gear in water up to twenty-five metres deep; and provides that applicants for that right are limited to fishermen's associations or fishery production cooperatives. Reporting records the right as covering waters within three nautical miles of the coast or to twenty-five metres depth, renewable on a ten-yearly cycle. Where an offshore project is proposed, the association holding that right is the local body with a legal seat at the table. The eight grounds for revocation are listed, and compensation follows. The Act provides that the authority may change or revoke approval of a fishery right, or suspend its exercise, for: national defence needs; economic utilisation of land; conservation of aquatic resources; environmental protection needs; navigation and anchoring of vessels; laying of submarine pipelines and cables; prospecting and mining; and other public interest needs; that before doing so it shall first give public notice and notify each fisher concerned; and that where loss results, the sectoral authority or the party requesting the change, revocation or suspension shall negotiate appropriate compensation, the central authority deciding if negotiation fails. Reporting records associations arguing that without this right they lose the standing to assert legal rights in negotiations over gas terminals, offshore wind and submarine cables. Duration, renewal and the fee inside the right. The Act sets the duration at five years for set-net and demarcated rights and ten years for the exclusive right, with the holder having priority to re-apply on expiry; requires the authority's approval before a right is mortgaged, transferred, merged or divided, with fishers and fishery workers given priority as transferees; provides that a co-owner may not dispose of a share without the consent of co-owners holding two-thirds; and allows the exclusive right holder to charge entry fees to entry-right holders, at amounts fixed in the entry rules or contract. Planning is published annually. The Act requires the authority to make an overall plan for fishery-right fisheries in public waters based on production resources and with reference to mining, navigation, water conservancy, environmental protection and other public interests, and to publish that plan periodically each year and accept applications. Read this with the protected trees chapter, the water quality protection zone, the city plan display window and the extraction permit entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 野生動物保護區 — a public hearing in the locality before designation, core, buffer and sustainable-use zoning, thirty days of public display of the maps, and rewards for reporting violations
trackers.desc: A local authority may declare a wildlife refuge over an important habitat, and a hearing comes first. The wildlife conservation legislation provides that the local competent authority may designate as a wildlife refuge an important wildlife habitat environment requiring special protection, drawing up and executing a conservation plan, and may entrust execution to another agency or organisation; and that designation, change or abolition of a refuge shall, where necessary, first hold a public hearing in the locality and fully hear the opinions of local residents, before being reported upward and, with the conservation advisory committee's approval, publicly announced and implemented. Where the case is urgent or necessary the central authority may designate or change a refuge directly with that committee's approval. The conservation plan is where the controls are set. The Act provides that the authority may announce controls in the plan on disturbing, abusing, hunting or killing ordinary wildlife; collecting or felling plants; polluting or destroying the environment; and other prohibited or permitted acts. Pollution and destruction of the environment being a controllable act inside a refuge is the sentence to note where a project sits beside one. Zoning and public display are prescribed by rule. The enforcement rules provide that a refuge may be divided into a core zone, a buffer zone and a sustainable use zone, each with its own conservation plan; that before designation the local authority consults relevant agencies and submits the plan and maps for central approval; that the plan must contain the origin, scope, objectives and planning map, the area's present condition, the zoning and use control matters, the manpower and budget needed, and the minutes of any public hearing held; and that after approval the local authority announces the refuge and sends the maps to the district offices for public display for not less than thirty days, after which they are kept available for inspection. The habitat layer beneath it, and the reward for reporting. The forestry agency records that under this Act thirty-eight important wildlife habitat environments were announced by the agriculture ministry and one by the ocean affairs council — thirty-nine in total — with local governments declaring refuges over those needing special protection. The Act provides for conservation or inspection personnel in refuges, police assistance where necessary, and that enforcement officers, members of the public or groups who take part in or assist with detecting and reporting violations may be rewarded under rules the authority sets. Read this with the exclusive fishery right, the water quality protection zone, the protected trees chapter and the city plan display entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 濕地保育法 — the four-step mitigation ladder ending in off-site compensation, the wetland impact statement with public participation, and the paid search that tells you whether a parcel is inside an important wetland
trackers.desc: The Act forces a project down a four-step ladder before it can compensate its way out. The 2013 wetland conservation legislation, in force since February 2015, provides that off-site compensation is allowed only after avoidance and mitigation measures or alternatives have been considered and difficulty remains such that the impact cannot be reduced, and that other ecological compensation is allowed only where off-site compensation is itself difficult; that the authority shall set the compensation ratio and the restoration benchmark; that compensation must reach the ecological restoration benchmark before development or use of the original land begins, unless the authority assesses that impossible, in which case the off-site area ratio or the functional benchmark is raised; and that where the off-site compensation area is 0.2 hectares or less, a payment in lieu may be made into the wetland fund, earmarked for building a functionally complete wetland. Ask which rung of that ladder a project claims to be on. The wetland impact statement has its own rules on disclosure and public participation. The Act provides that for development or use that must prepare a wetland impact statement, the central authority shall set the criteria for requiring one, the details, information disclosure, public participation and other procedural matters. That is a second participation window, separate from the environmental assessment already recorded in this bucket. Anyone can find out whether a parcel is inside an important wetland, for a small fee. The land management agency publishes a search procedure: a table of important wetlands, their conservation and utilisation plans and provisional local-grade wetlands with the authority to ask, kept current on named sites; an application with the site area, position and cadastral data, with coordinates where the land is in water or unregistered; and a fee of a stated small amount for up to ten parcels, rising by parcel. The grades, the numbers and a live enforcement dispute. Published material records wetlands evaluated as international, national and local grade on ecological diversity and species conservation value, under the principles of wise use and no net loss, with existing uses inside an important wetland allowed to continue; records two international, forty national and fifteen local-grade wetlands announced, with most national conservation plans published; and records a case where a national-grade wetland was filled to build a water slide and pool, the county seeking restoration under the regional planning law at a lower fine while environmental groups argued the wetland law's higher penalty should apply. Read this with the protected trees, the assessment query system, the water quality protection zone and the land trust entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 公民訴訟 — the citizen suit against a regulator that will not enforce, the sixty-day written notice that starts it, and the court's power to order the agency to pay the plaintiff's lawyer and testing costs
trackers.desc: Where the regulator will not enforce, the community can sue the regulator. The waste disposal legislation, published by the environment ministry, provides that where a public or private premises violates the Act or its subordinate orders and the competent authority is lax in enforcement, an injured person or a public interest group may state the specific content of that laxity and notify the competent authority in writing; and that if the authority still fails to enforce within sixty days of service of that written notice, the injured person or public interest group may name that authority as defendant and bring suit directly in the high administrative court over its neglect of duty, seeking a judgment ordering it to enforce. The format of the written notice is publicly announced by the central authority. That sixty-day notice is the document to send and date. The court can make the agency pay the plaintiff's costs. The same provision states that in giving judgment the high administrative court may, on its own authority, order the defendant agency to pay appropriate lawyer's fees, detection and appraisal fees, or other litigation costs to a plaintiff who made a concrete contribution to the effective removal and disposal of the waste. Published commentary records the parallel provision in the environmental basic legislation ordering such payment to a plaintiff who made a concrete contribution to maintaining environmental quality, and explains why it exists: testing environmental harm often takes long periods and large sums beyond the means of an individual or an ordinary group. Who may sue, and against whom.
