The same commentary records that both an injured person and a public interest group may be plaintiffs, that under the administrative litigation legislation and the environmental basic legislation the defendant is an administrative agency, and that the equivalent citizen suit clauses sit in the individual environmental statutes — quoting the air pollution control legislation's identical wording on the written notice and the sixty-day period. The same Act arms the regulator, which is what the suit compels it to use. The legislation provides that the authority may order those responsible to clear waste within a period, may clear and dispose of it itself and recover the necessary costs, with that claim ranking ahead of all other claims and mortgages, may enter premises without the owner's consent to sample and clear, and may publish the location, waste type and quantity of illegally backfilled land and have it annotated on the land register until properly cleaned. Read this with the environmental rights foundation, the pollution complaint line, the licensed testing laboratories and the judgment search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 國土測繪圖資服務雲 and the spatial planning map — free cadastral, orthophoto and land use layers with no application needed, and a planning viewer carrying environmentally sensitive areas and hazard potential
trackers.desc: The mapping centre's cloud is free to use, with no application and no restriction on who uses it. The land surveying and mapping centre records that its map service cloud integrates survey results into a web viewer and publishes network map services, and that the viewer needs only a browser on a computer or mobile device, requires no application, is open to anyone and free. It records the content as including the general electronic map with orthophotos, drone system orthophotos, the national land use survey results, cadastral maps, section outline maps, administrative boundary maps at every level and topographic maps at various scales, plus important layers integrated from the government open data platform, with spatial positioning, land information lookup, multi-layer overlay and analysis, offline maps and map collaboration. Looking up the lot number under your feet is one of its stated functions. The layers are published as standards-compliant services and APIs. The centre records the core layers published as web map tile, web map and web feature services conforming to the relevant open standards, and records APIs for house numbers, cadastral maps, national land use survey results, route planning, open-class and map-platform categories. Published material records that the general electronic map and administrative boundary maps are usable free through those services without application, while cadastral map tiles and their APIs are restricted to government agencies, state enterprises and academic institutions. That split is the thing to know before planning a workflow. A separate planning viewer carries the sensitivity and hazard layers. The national spatial planning geographic information platform records that members of the public may, without logging in, query urban plans, non-urban land, national parks, various environmentally sensitive area layers and hazard potential and disaster prevention layers; that its functions include switching basemaps, querying layer attributes, making statistical maps, calculating zone areas, uploading a local layer, street view, positioning and printing; and that a user may load an external map service by its address, the example given being an important wetlands service. It records that its lookup connects to the mapping centre's cloud and that results are for reference only. Read this with the protected trees, the wetland conservation Act, the city plan display and the water quality protection zone entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The conservation foundation that holds land in trust — indefinite protection contracts with owners, its audited annual accounts, and the tax problem that has stopped others
trackers.desc: A conservation body takes land into trust on an open-ended contract, and reports on it publicly every year. The foundation records that since 2000 it has introduced the national trust concept, signing indefinite land protection contracts with landowners, acquiring the land, applying to the authorities to establish an environmental or conservation public interest trust, and carrying out habitat works; and records that each year it submits the trust affairs report, the annual statement of receipts and payments and the inventory of trust property to the supervising authority and an external supervisor for audit, and publishes them. Its stated work includes creating diverse habitat for local key species with automatic cameras monitoring the ecology, and pushing for amendment of the trust and tax legislation. The one successful case shows how such a site is assembled. Published material records that in 2007 six members of a wilderness conservation association jointly bought a low-altitude forest; that after the financial crisis three withdrew, and the remainder concluded that permanent preservation required placing the land in trust; that they first contracted with that association and, after three years, transferred it permanently to the environmental information association. The environment ministry records the resulting base as the country's first successful environmental trust case, able to be developed into an environmental education facility under the environmental education legislation. Published material records the site as having recorded 83 endemic species and 15 protected animal species, and the forestry agency records the trust base and adjoining land certified in a national conservation-coexistence scheme with a numbered certificate. The legal mechanics are stated, and so is the obstacle. Published commentary records that under the trust legislation and the permission and supervision rules for environmental public interest trusts, environmental protection affairs may be entrusted to a public interest environmental organisation, preventing land or forest from falling into the hands of conglomerates or developers through sale; that trust land must be transferred into the trustee's name and annotated as trust property, the trust property being independent. It records the blockage plainly: campaigners argue the public interest trust tax rules are outdated, that people donating land into an environmental trust are charged gift tax, and call for amendment so that relief follows whether the work is genuinely public interest rather than who administers the trust. Read this with the citizen suit entry, the wetland conservation Act, the protected trees and the environmental data entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The environmental rights foundation's legal assistance — the groups it takes cases for, its lawyers in assessments and hearings, and its contract clinics for landowners
trackers.desc: The categories of applicant a foundation will assist are published, and they are the categories a community falls into. A government platform's record of the environmental rights foundation states that for its environmental rights legal assistance it selects cases whose subjects are residents' groups, environmental organisations, self-help associations or community tribes, providing lawyers and professional helpers for non-litigation procedures such as environmental impact assessment and hearings, and where necessary assistance in litigation — recording fifteen such assistance cases at the stated date. Help inside the assessment and the hearing, before any lawsuit, is what most communities actually need. Its stated purpose is participation, information and remedy together. The same record describes its work as case assistance, environmental monitoring and community capacity building, to guarantee that the public obtains environmental information, has public participation in environmental disputes and the opportunity of judicial remedy; it lists further tasks as monitoring and planning environmental policy and individual cases, research on the constitution and environmental legislation, promoting environmental legal education and building an education platform, and providing legal opinions and consultation to public civic groups. It records six project studies monitoring energy-intensive industrial and science parks on climate issues, and three projects on renewable energy disputes aimed at information disclosure and public participation procedures. Its lawyers hold contract clinics for landowners. A published annual account records the foundation working with the fisheries authority and an agricultural centre on the standard contracts used in combined aquaculture and solar projects, submitting many revisions to the public template contracts and urging the authorities to raise landowners' and farmers' and fishers' legal awareness of contracts; and records its salaried lawyers holding repeated contract briefing sessions in aquaculture production areas across five named regions, advising landowners and farmers what to watch for, alongside legal consultation for fishers and residents. Its origin is a court settlement. The foundation records itself as established in 2016 out of the settlement of a science park assessment lawsuit, endowed by a government ministry, with its charter discussed with named local and environmental organisations and a university law centre. Read this with the environmental jurists, the citizen of the earth foundation, the environmental trust and the citizen suit entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 環境資訊中心 — a daily environmental newsroom running since 2000 that covers assessment hearings and local opposition, and the volunteer and habitat programmes attached to it
trackers.desc: There is a daily environmental newsroom here, and its beat includes the hearings a community appears at. The newsroom records itself as a non-profit online medium operated by a named foundation, formerly the environmental information association, which has issued an environmental information newsletter since 2000, growing from translating international news to building a full editorial and reporting team, and committed to diverse and comprehensive environmental reporting. Its own headlines record items such as a preliminary assessment review of an industrial park where residents travelled to the capital with local produce to protest against the development. For a community whose hearing would otherwise go unreported, a newsroom that already covers assessment reviews is the difference between a local dispute and a national one. Its stated theory of change is why it exists. The association records its belief that people act because they understand, and the environment changes because of action, and that its purpose is to build a harmonious relationship between people and nature through the exchange of environmental information and the promotion of environmental trusts; and records the newsletter and site as speaking for the mountains, wetlands, seas and land that have no vote. The habitat side takes volunteers and publishes what they do. Its trust base pages record activities in four lines — habitat guardianship, with volunteer training courses, volunteer work days, working holidays and regular biological surveys; community participation, including village activities and meetings and a young reporters project; environmental education, with ecological interpretation, guided tours and sustainability courses. It records the base as the first successful environmental trust case since the trust legislation of 1996, established in 2011 after three people of different backgrounds pooled money in 2008 to buy hillside land, held first by a wilderness association and transferred to this body in 2014, and describes it as a learning centre as well as a preserved habitat. Its declared target is a share of the country's land. A government social innovation platform records the body's 2023 transition into a foundation to expand civil conservation capacity and promote more and larger environmental public interest trusts, aiming to safeguard three per cent of the country's habitat — which it equates to four times the capital's area — and to bring a quarter of the population to care about the environment and take action. Read this with the conservation foundation holding land in trust, the environmental jurists, the citizen suit and the assessment register entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 透明足跡 — a citizen-built database of factory emissions and penalties, searchable by map or company with a corporate-group ownership layer, and a reporting route that has produced fines
trackers.desc: Factory pollution data here is assembled and published by a civic organisation, not only by the regulator. The platform records itself as a system to make pollution information genuinely open and transparent, built after the organisation successfully pressed the environment authority to publish stack and wastewater monitoring data, the substances and quantities emitted, the list of serious violators, the reasons violations were penalised, and the state of improvement. Published reporting records the earlier position: each factory's penalty record can now be searched on the site, synchronised with government data, and — after the organisation pushed for it — stating which factory was penalised for exceeding limits on which substance, rather than only a vague record that a company breached some clause. That difference, from clause to substance, is what makes a penalty record usable in a community's case. The search is built for a resident, not an analyst. Published description records that users can search by an environment map or a company list, and filter by factory type, emission type and whether there is a penalty record; that where a user sees continuous exceedances they can share the record; and that people no longer need to file an official request to obtain emissions data — with an internet connection they can check a company's discharges at any time. The scale and the group-ownership layer are published. One account records the database as holding data on 112,103 factories, 87,946 violation records, and 1,487 corporate groups covering 26,648 domestic and overseas companies, with parent-subsidiary relationship charts drawn to pursue parent groups' responsibility; an earlier account gives 30,566 companies, 73,527 factories, 71,336 violation records, and real-time monitoring from 121 air and 376 water discharge factories. It records the site averaging over 30,000 visits a month, and records the organisation having assisted 16 pollution reports, of which 5 resulted in penalties, and having taken part in amendments to more than ten laws and pushed open 15 sets of environmental data. Read this with the assessment register, the environmental newsroom, the citizen suit and the environmental jurists entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 主婦聯盟環境保護基金會 — a foundation founded by householders that spun off three further organisations, works through branch offices, and runs on donations rather than contracts
trackers.desc: An organisation founded by ordinary householders became a permanent institution, and the sequence is documented. Published description records that in early 1987 a group of housewives, unwilling to keep sitting by in the face of the environmental sickness and educational failings around them, resolved to start with themselves, under a motto of daring to speak, quick to act, willing to bear responsibility; that the group was formally registered in 1989 as an incorporated environmental protection foundation; and that a working office in a second city followed in 1990. It records the foundation as the country's first non-profit organisation to advance environmental protection work through the role of women, working long-term on waste sorting, resource recovery, green consumption, sustainable agriculture, water pollution and renewable energy. It created other organisations rather than absorbing the work. The same description records that, through long-term capacity-building of its people, the foundation gave birth to a nature trails association, a national parents' league and a consumer cooperative. Spinning off separate bodies is a growth pattern a community organisation can copy rather than becoming a single crowded institution. It records the foundation as an organisation where participants think together, decide together and execute in groups, giving members a stage on which to build confidence step by step and develop the capacity for cooperative decision-making. Its funding position is stated plainly. Published material records the foundation as an independently operating non-profit whose entire running costs — staff salaries, events and lectures, office rent and utilities — depend on donations raised piece by piece, and publishes a postal giro account number and a credit card authorisation form for donors. It records the foundation's branch working on the sources, budget and rules governing school lunch ingredients, with parents assembled to supervise the responsible authorities. Read this with the environmental newsroom, the pollution database, the citizen suit and the conservation trust entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: City environmental bureaus and their reward schemes — a 24-hour complaint desk handling about 1,800 cases a month, what an inspector needs from a caller, and the city-run reward sites listed by name
trackers.desc: A city bureau publishes how many complaints it gets and what it does with them. One city's environmental protection bureau records its public nuisance complaint and inspection service as operating 24 hours a day, year round, with an average of nearly 1,800 complaints a month over two years — about three an hour, one every twenty minutes, the top three types being air pollution, environmental sanitation and noise, together nearly ninety per cent of cases; and records that over a stated period it issued about 1,200 citations with penalties totalling 12.5 million yuan. For a neighbourhood living beside a source, the city bureau — not the ministry — is the body that counts the complaints and issues the fines. What the inspector needs from the caller is stated plainly. The bureau records the difficulty: an inspector often only smells the odour with no definite pollution location, wind and rising heat carry the smell upward, and burning or illegal dumping sites are usually in suburbs or farmland with no monitoring system available to check. It therefore asks complainants to give concrete pollution facts — the source's location, the pollution category, the situation, the time and the frequency — and contact details, so inspectors can arrive quickly, and records building a hotspot map of illegal dumping. That list is the difference between a complaint that closes unfound and one that produces a citation. The equipment and the reward routes are published too. The city records enforcement using unmanned aerial vehicles carrying infrared thermal imagers, micro-sensors to monitor illegal factory emissions, high-resolution cameras for open burning and water quality monitors to catch illegal discharges. The national complaint system records a toll-free complaint line and a reporting app with GPS location, case-number tracking and direct dialling to the local bureau, and lists eight named cities and counties whose own reward schemes must be used to claim a bounty, with payment governed by each local authority's own rules. Read this with the pollution database, the assessment register, the environmental newsroom and the citizen suit entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The community tree-planting and tree-protection grant — village associations apply through district forest offices, with land consent documents required and a selection panel a quarter of whom must be outside experts
trackers.desc: A village-level association can apply for money to plant and protect trees, and the paperwork is listed. The published grant rules record the third application stage as running from 1 April to the end of May, for community development associations registered nationally or other registered non-profit bodies in that village or borough, and list the documents required: an application letter with its date; a basic data table including a planting schedule; a greening or tree-protection plan; copies of the registration certificate and of the current head's identification; and, for a non-profit body other than the village's own development association, a non-profit affidavit — with the forest office first required to ask whether that village's development association intends to apply this year. That last rule stops an outside group cutting across a village's own association. Land consent is the document that decides the application. The same rules require land proof documents with a cadastral map transcript and land registration transcript in both cases: for public land, an official letter of consent from the owning or managing agency stating the location, period, unit and matters consented to; and for private land, a land use consent from the owner or manager for at least five years. A five-year written consent from the landowner is what turns a planting plan into a funded one. The selection panel's composition is fixed, and outside members are guaranteed. The rules record that each district forest office sets up a community selection panel of seven or more members, of whom local government staff, experts and academics shall not be fewer than one quarter, with the convenor designated by the office head; that the office's accounting section helps check whether the budget is properly drawn; and that work stations begin receiving applications and carry out site inspections and preliminary review. It records payment of a second instalment after the results report passes review. Read this with the community forestry programme, the city bureaus, the pollution database and the conservation trust entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Township and district mediation committees — free mediation at the local office, a quarter of seats reserved for women, and a settlement that carries the force of a final court judgment once approved
trackers.desc: Every township and district office runs a free mediation committee, and the settlement it produces carries a court's force. A county government records that the committees are composed of impartial people within the township or district who have legal or other professional knowledge and enjoy trust and standing, and mediate free of charge for the public in civil disputes and criminal matters prosecutable only on complaint; and records that once mediation is established and approved by the competent court, its effect equals a court judgment, and if one party does not perform, the other may apply to the court for compulsory enforcement. It records the advantages as legal effect, saving time, saving money and meeting the parties' needs. For neighbours in a land or building dispute, that is a binding outcome without a lawsuit. Applying is designed for people who cannot write the papers. The same county records that an application is in principle made in writing, by collecting a mediation application form from the committee and filing it with copies for the other parties, but that an applicant unable or unwilling to write may bring identification and a seal and state the matter orally, with committee staff preparing the record. It lists mediable civil matters as including debt repayment, purchase, construction, lease and occupation of real estate, inheritance and commercial sales, and a district office adds transfer of ownership of unregistered buildings, disputes over the location of land boundaries, mortgages and pledges. The committee's composition and the quarter-share for women are set by law. The published statute records committee members as selected by the township or district head from impartial local people with legal or other professional knowledge and public trust, submitted at double the required number, jointly reviewed by the district court and the district prosecutors office, reported to the county government and appointed for four years; and records that the number of women among mediation committee members shall not be fewer than one quarter. The paperwork after settlement runs on fixed days. The statute records that the office shall send the mediation document and file to the court for review within ten days of settlement, that where mediation fails a certificate of non-settlement shall be issued within seven days of application, and that in civil cases already before a court the plaintiff may apply within three months for the refund of two-thirds of the court fee already paid. Read this with the city environmental bureaus, the community tree-planting grant, the pollution database and the environmental newsroom entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: County and city community planners — professional design teams placed inside neighbourhoods, a bottom-up proposal route with staged support, and the land-use consent a proposal must carry
trackers.desc: A county places planning professionals inside communities and pays for it. A county's urban and rural development department records its community planner scheme as working through professional team mentoring — matching planning, design, landscape and community-building teams to enter communities, provide consultation and accompaniment, and help inventory resources, propose planning concepts and prepare implementation schemes; and records a staged capacity mechanism, dividing communities by maturity into introductory, advanced and integrated types. It records the aims as building communities' own planning and implementation capacity; improving public space and overall environmental quality; integrating local culture, industry and living; and establishing long-term community management and governance mechanisms, with recorded results including reuse of idle space. For a neighbourhood that wants a plan rather than only an objection, this is a designer paid by the county to sit with it. The scheme is national in origin and city-led in practice. A national programme site records the resident-mentoring scheme as having grown from a 2003 national community-building plan, with a pilot in which local community planners and architects provided professional technical assistance and residents jointly planned, designed and built their own community living environment through a hire-labour-and-buy-materials method; records the capital as the first city to propose a community planner scheme; and records that although counties and cities run the work, the ministry conducts annual on-site supervision and evaluation, including spot checks on the maintenance and use of previously completed projects, with poorly maintained communities taken into account in the next year's selection. Proposals must carry written land consent, and the rules say so. One city's youth community planner rules record that a proposing team may propose within a living circle or community; the site must lie within the city; public land with public character and demonstration effect is prioritised; and consent forms must be obtained for both public and private land before a grant. They record that before construction a team must obtain a land use consent form and a maintenance and adoption consent form, and attach a record of consensus coordination among residents within the site, construction drawings, a maintenance and management plan and an open-use covenant, with opening hours and contacts published. Read this with the township mediation committees, the community tree-planting grant, the city environmental bureaus and the pollution database entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The neighbourhood chief's office — an elected unpaid chief with a district-employed clerk, a residents' assembly and a six-monthly work meeting whose minutes go online within a week, and city directories that find yours
trackers.desc: The chief must convene a work meeting twice a year, and the minutes go online within a week. A city's service rules record that the chief shall convene the clerk and the block heads for a neighbourhood work meeting once every half year, one of which may be held at year end, with extraordinary meetings where necessary, to consider the neighbourhood work plan; the tracking and implementation of the residents' assembly, the grassroots construction forum and each proposal; the use of subsidy funds for neighbourhood construction; the execution of matters assigned by the district office; and other activities and construction. It records that the minutes shall be uploaded to the neighbourhood office's website within one week after the meeting, and the district office shall send someone to check the website. A published minute, on a public site, within seven days, is the accountability hook. Who may be summoned to that meeting is listed. The same rules record that the chief presides, and that at the chief's request the following may attend: block heads; the clerk; the parks and street lighting or road lighting engineering teams; the maintenance engineering team; the district health centre; the district household registration office; the local police station; and the district cleaning squad — with others invitable, including pumping station staff, river patrol officers, mountain patrol officers, sewerage staff, and local gas, electricity, telecommunications and water company staff. The office is elected, unpaid, and staffed by the district. A city's rules record that the neighbourhood has a chief, unpaid, elected by residents for a four-year term, renewable, under the direction of the district head, handling neighbourhood public affairs and assigned matters; that blocks have block heads, unpaid, selected by the chief from adult residents and appointed by the district head; and that the neighbourhood office has a clerk who, under the district head's orders and the chief's supervision, handles self-government and assigned matters, with the clerk's post counted in the district office establishment. It records that many chiefs now integrate private resources in the neighbourhood and actively seek government subsidies, with several subsidy schemes requiring a proposal planned through the neighbourhood office. Another city publishes the chief's duties, including convening the residents' assembly, reflecting public sentiment, promoting public construction within the neighbourhood and reporting emergencies; and cities publish searchable directories of chiefs by district. Read this with the community planners, the mediation committees, the tree-planting grant and the city environmental bureaus entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: eFOI — Freedom of Information (Philippines)
trackers.desc: You CAN get: records held by the Philippine EXECUTIVE branch — national departments, bureaus, government-owned and -controlled corporations, state universities and colleges and local water districts — filed online through the portal and tracked there, with agencies required to answer within 15 working days (extendable, with notice, where the request is voluminous or needs consultation). If the agency does not hold the record but another executive agency does, a 2021 memorandum circular requires it to refer your request on rather than deny it. You CAN'T get: anything from Congress or the courts — there is no enabling statute covering all branches, so the order reaches the executive only. Critically for a local fight, LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS ARE MERELY ENCOURAGED to follow it, not bound, so a barangay, municipal or provincial record may need a local FOI ordinance instead. Records are also withheld under national-security, privacy and banking confidentiality exceptions. For activists: this is the route to an EIA, a permit file, a procurement record or project correspondence held by DENR, DPWH or a GOCC. Use it early — a denial can be appealed to the agency head within 15 calendar days, then to the Office of the President or by petition for mandamus, and that clock is slower than most project timetables.

trackers.name: National Secretary of Social Action (NASSA)
trackers.desc: The National Secretary of Social Action was established in 1966 as a humanitarian and advocacy arm of the Catholic Bishops’ Conferences of the Philippines (CBCP). The aim of NASSA is to address poverty alleviation, sustainable agriculture, empowerment of women and children, and ecological protection.

trackers.name: Environmental Legal Assistance Center (ELAC)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Philippine environmental law NGO founded in 1990 — lawyers, paralegals, researchers and community organisers, backed by volunteer lawyers and scientists, working from offices in Palawan, Cebu, Bohol and Leyte. It provides free legal representation in environmental court cases against deforestation, mining and other destructive projects and coastal degradation, trains community paralegals and forest, wildlife and fish wardens, and litigates on forest, coastal and land-tenure disputes. WHO IT SUITS: a community or indigenous group in its coverage areas, especially Palawan, facing an extractive or large development project — it is a small office under political and corporate pressure, so cases are chosen, not queued.

trackers.name: The Samdhana Institute — grants programme
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a Southeast Asian grantmaker giving micro to medium-sized grants, plus urgent-action grants, directly to Indigenous peoples and local communities, community-based and civil-society organisations, informal groups and individual activists — for land and territorial rights, natural-resource governance, and community-led climate and livelihood work. Its own site names offices only in Bogor, Indonesia and in Cagayan de Oro and Quezon City, Philippines, which is where this entry is placed; it describes its remit as Southeast Asia generally, so groups elsewhere in the region should still ask. WHO IT SUITS: groups that cannot get money from conventional donors — Samdhana states its grantmaking principle as funding the "un-fundable", and an unregistered informal group is not disqualified. HOW IT DIFFERS: it supplies environmental conflict mediation and technical support alongside the grant rather than only writing cheques.

trackers.name: Foundation for the Philippine Environment (FPE)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: an endowment-based Philippine grantmaker for biodiversity conservation and sustainable development, with small grants of up to PHP 500,000 and a youth stream of up to PHP 100,000. Its grant framework (CARES) explicitly includes Environmental Defense and advocacy alongside research, constituency building and site work. WHO IT SUITS: civil-society organisations, people's organisations, Indigenous peoples' organisations and academic institutions — not individuals. Much of the money is site-focused: FPE identifies a priority conservation site and invites organisations based there to apply, so check whether your area is currently one before writing anything. HOW IT DIFFERS: FPE has also served as implementing partner for the GEF Small Grants Programme in the Philippines, so one relationship can reach more than one pot.

trackers.name: Forest Foundation Philippines
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a Philippine grantmaker for forest protection, running microgrants for community-led work to reduce deforestation and forest degradation, conserve high-conservation-value forest and improve ecosystem connectivity — concentrated in priority landscapes including the Mindoro and Eastern Mindanao Biodiversity Corridors. WHO IT SUITS: duly registered individuals, organisations and firms — NGOs, social enterprises, professionals and consultancy groups — working on forest protection and conservation in the Philippines. HOW IT DIFFERS: programmes open and close, and the Foundation openly lists past programmes that are no longer accepting proposals, so write to the proposals address and confirm what is live before preparing a submission.

trackers.name: Friends of the Earth Asia Pacific
trackers.desc: The Asia Pacific regional structure of Friends of the Earth International, formed in 2008, whose member groups work on community-based struggles against destructive projects, particularly mining and other extractive industries, alongside Indigenous peoples, peasant farmers, fisherfolk and trade unions. WHO TO ENLIST: the national member group nearest the project. In this region Friends of the Earth International's own directory names groups in Bangladesh (BELA, the Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers' Association), India, Indonesia (WALHI), Japan, Malaysia (Sahabat Alam Malaysia), Nepal, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines (the Legal Rights and Natural Resources Center), South Korea and Sri Lanka. You CAN: reach an organisation that already works community-side in your own country, and draw regional weight onto a local fight. For activists: in several of these countries the Friends of the Earth affiliate is the most experienced community-side environmental body there is.

trackers.name: Legal Rights and Natural Resources Center — Kasama sa Kalikasan (LRC-KsK)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Philippine public-interest law centre founded in 1987 by four young lawyers, one of them now a Supreme Court Justice, working for recognition and protection of the rights of Indigenous peoples and upland rural poor communities to land and natural resources. It runs three programmes — research and policy development, direct legal services, and advocacy and campaigns support — and was instrumental in drafting the Indigenous Peoples' Rights Act of 1997 and defending its constitutionality, the statute under which ancestral domain is recognised in the Philippines. It campaigned to repeal the Mining Act of 1995 and still petitions against it. For partner communities it runs paralegal training and field briefings, supplies documentary research, and files cases in court. WHO IT SUITS: an Indigenous or upland community facing mining, logging or encroachment. The model is supporting a community's own campaign rather than taking a client, so it suits a group that is already organised, and it works through partners rather than open intake.

trackers.name: Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism (PCIJ)
trackers.desc: Philippine center reporting on corruption and public money since 1989.

trackers.name: Open Data Philippines
trackers.desc: National — Philippine government open data portal. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Philippines.

trackers.name: DENR-EMB EIA portal
trackers.desc: The Philippines' Environmental Management Bureau (DENR-EMB) EIA portal. You CAN get: Environmental Impact Statement System filings and Environmental Compliance Certificate (ECC) records. You CAN'T get: files for projects that skipped the system. For activists: check a project's ECC status and its EIA documents.

trackers.name: Supreme Court E-Library
trackers.desc: Official Philippine Supreme Court e-library of decisions and resolutions. · Find here: the Supreme Court of the Philippines' E-Library of decisions and resolutions.

trackers.name: PhilGEPS
trackers.desc: The Philippines' single centralised electronic procurement portal — all government bid notices, awards and contracts. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in the Philippines, and for how much.

trackers.name: Philippine Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (PH-EITI)
trackers.desc: National Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative body — discloses oil, gas and mining revenues, contracts and company ownership in Philippines.

trackers.name: PH-EITI Beneficial Ownership Registry
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC)
trackers.desc: The Philippines' Anti-Money Laundering Council — the national financial intelligence unit and AML/CFT authority. Here you can trace how suspicious transactions are reported and money-laundering intelligence is produced in the Philippines.

trackers.name: Commission on Audit (COA)
trackers.desc: The Philippines' independent constitutional supreme audit institution — audits all accounts and expenditures of government funds and properties. — Holds to account: officials handling public money & power — find audit findings and how public money was spent or lost.

trackers.name: Department of Budget and Management (DBM)
trackers.desc: The Philippine executive agency overseeing the national budget — allocation, release and management of public funds. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Philippines.

trackers.name: Office of the Ombudsman (Philippines)
trackers.desc: Philippine constitutional body investigating and prosecuting graft and corruption by public officials.

trackers.name: Philippine Statistics Authority
trackers.desc: Philippines's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Philippines.

trackers.name: SEC Philippines
trackers.desc: The Philippines' Securities and Exchange Commission corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Writ of Kalikasan — how to file, and who qualifies
trackers.desc: THE REMEDY, NOT AN ORGANISATION. Founded on Section 16, Article II of the Constitution and operationalised by A.M. No. 09-6-8-SC, Rule 7. THERE ARE NO DOCKET FEES — the rules waive them so public-interest litigants can reach the court. File directly with the Supreme Court or the Court of Appeals; it is not filed in the Regional Trial Courts, and a petition lodged in an RTC is in the wrong forum. The petition must be verified (sworn), naming the law violated, your circumstances and the respondents, or stating that their identities are unknown. Procedure is summary: petition, writ, the respondent's Return, a summary hearing, a possible TEPO, then judgment — with liberal admission of evidence and site inspections. Reliefs include injunction, environmental protection orders, rehabilitation and continuing mandamus. TEST THE THRESHOLD FIRST: the harm must transcend personal or property rights and threaten the life, health or property of inhabitants in 2 or more cities or provinces — a single-site development inside one municipality does not qualify however severe, and that disqualifies most local fights. AND WINNING THE WRIT IS NOT WINNING A HALT: in the Sibuyan Island case the Court issued the writ against the miner, DENR and the MGB, gave 10 days to comment and referred the case onward — but denied the temporary environmental protection order; and reporting on the writ's record notes that granted petitions have not always been implemented by local governments.

trackers.name: Public Attorney's Office — district offices nationwide
trackers.desc: THE GOVERNMENT'S OWN LAW OFFICE FOR PEOPLE WHO CANNOT PAY, under Republic Act 9406, with district and field offices nationwide — many inside Halls of Justice, court buildings or local government complexes, so this is a local service rather than a capital-city one. Go to the office covering either your residence or where the case will be filed. TWO TESTS, BOTH MUST BE PASSED. Indigency: published limits are ₱24,000 net monthly income in NCR, ₱22,000 in other cities outside NCR, ₱20,000 in municipalities outside NCR — and owning a modest family home does not by itself disqualify you. Merit: the case must have a genuine legal basis and not be frivolous or harassing. BRING: an Affidavit of Indigency plus an income tax return, payslip, or a Certificate of Indigency from the DSWD, the Municipal Social Welfare Office, or your Barangay Chairman. Filing fees are 90 percent discounted for indigents and fully waived with a PAO certificate. THREE LIMITS. PAO can act for one side only — if your opponent is also indigent, one of you is referred to the Integrated Bar of the Philippines. Caseloads are extreme: a PAO lawyer averaged 458 cases in one recorded year against about 40 for a private lawyer, so expect little time per client and turnover of the lawyer on your case. And for a public-interest environmental matter, also try the IBP provincial and city chapters under Rule 139-A, law school clinics — some of which waive means tests where the case involves environmental protection — and groups such as FLAG and SALIGAN, which take landmark land-rights cases at their discretion.

trackers.name: CBFMA — 25-year tenure, and a consent right over permits
trackers.desc: HOW A COMMUNITY GETS SECURE TENURE OVER FOREST LAND IT DOES NOT OWN. Under EO 263 and DENR AO 96-29, a Community-Based Forest Management Agreement runs between the DENR and a people's organisation for 25 years, renewable for another 25, under the community's own Community Resource Management Framework. It is also the instrument issued to POs in allowable zones within protected areas. THE RIGHT THAT STOPS THINGS: a PO must be informed of and consulted on all government projects in the area — and the PO's consent must be secured by DENR before granting or renewing contracts, leases and permits for extraction and utilisation of natural resources inside it, with an equitable sharing agreement reached first where the grantee is not from the affected community. A consent right inside your own tenure area is far stronger than objecting to someone else's permit from outside. You also receive all income from sustainable use within the area (subject to NIPAS), and exemption from forest charges on plantation products under RA 7161. THE PROCESS TRAP: your LGU must endorse the application before DENR can act — and PENRO/CENRO are mandated to orient local executives about CBFM, so ask DENR field staff to run that orientation rather than lobbying the LGU alone. KNOW WHAT IT IS: CBFM is a production sharing arrangement and communities under it have been oriented toward timber plantation harvesting — it secures tenure, it does not by itself mean preservation. For indigenous peoples the stronger route is ancestral domain recognition under RA 8371 (IPRA).

trackers.name: Forest Foundation Philippines — grants for community projects, but not if you own the land
trackers.desc: The eligibility answer that decides most readers: private individual and family-owned land or farm owners cannot apply. The Foundation says so in its own FAQ — it prioritises community-based projects and refers private owners to a tree-farming guidebook instead. Corporations are also excluded, the stated reason being that they have sufficient resources of their own, and government agencies can only partner rather than apply. Who can: duly registered individuals, NGOs, social enterprises, consultancy groups, and community-based or people's organisations — which is the category most land-defence groups fall into. There is no deadline; proposals are taken on a rolling basis, and evaluation depends on whether the Foundation has funds at the time. Small grants are decided by the Executive Director and evaluated in about a month; medium grants go to the Executive Committee or Board and take about a quarter. Expect several rounds of revision — staff will help you draft, at proposals@forestfoundation.ph. Priority is the four focal landscapes (Sierra Madre, Palawan, Samar and Leyte, Mindanao) plus the named GEF Small Grants sites: Aurora, Quezon, the Calamianes, Catanduanes, the Cluster 6 River Basin in Northern Samar, Siargao and Surigao del Norte. Work outside those goes to the Focused Grant Program, which covers small islands, mangroves and beach forests, and OECMs. Do not take the grant ceiling from a third-party listing — the figures on grant-aggregator sites contradict each other and the Foundation's own pages; take it from the current Request for Proposals. Registered with the SEC as Philippine Tropical Forest Conservation Foundation Inc. Office: 2F Valderrama Building, 107 Esteban St., Legaspi Village, Makati City 1229, (+63 2) 8891 0595.

trackers.name: NCIP — nothing gets a permit in an ancestral domain without its certification, and refusal has a form
trackers.desc: No lease, licence, permit, contract or concession inside an ancestral domain may be issued or renewed without the Commission's Certification Precondition and the community's free and prior informed consent. That is the lever; the rest is knowing how it runs. The proponent files with the regulatory agency, which endorses to the NCIP Regional Office with jurisdiction over the site, so a community does not start this process — it finds out that somebody else has. The first practical step is a verification request to that regional office, asking whether a described parcel overlaps a CADT, a CALT or a pending claim. Refusal has a form, and using it matters. Consent is collective, given through the community's own socio-political structures after a period to deliberate without outside influence, and recorded in a memorandum of agreement. Non-consent must be given in writing with specific grounds, and it produces a denial order from the Commission — an undocumented refusal is not the same thing and does not bind. Three exemptions decide whether any of this applies to you. Leases, permits, licences and concessions already existing or vested when NCIP Administrative Order No. 1 of 1998 took effect are recognised and fall outside FPIC and certification altogether. Any formal written agreement or community resolution issued before that order is deemed to be consent, so a resolution signed decades ago can be produced against a community now. And small-scale use of land, water and natural resources, and small-scale quarrying approved by a local government unit, run under a separate lighter process rather than full FPIC. Learn the two certificates apart. A Certification Precondition attests that the applicant has complied with FPIC; a Certificate of Non-Overlap attests only that the area does not touch an ancestral domain. Both are issued by the Regional Director under the 2006 guidelines, which replaced the 2002 order under which the Ancestral Domains Office issued them, so older material describes a route that no longer operates. Timings: the field-based investigation report reaches the main office within 30 days; certification issues within 7 days where there is no overlap; the applicant is notified of an overlap within 15 days of that report and has 30 days to file an action plan; the Certification Precondition issues within 15 working days. The applicant bears the actual cost of the field-based investigation. The Commission holds visitorial powers over resource utilisation contracts, which is a route back in after approval, and a community's own Ancestral Domain Sustainable Development and Protection Plan is the document to have ready before any of this begins.

trackers.name: CEC–Philippines — technical and scientific support to communities, in its own words
trackers.desc: Its own account of what it added in the 1990s is the reason to record it: field research and technical and scientific support services to communities. That is the function most Philippine communities cannot buy — somebody who will investigate a site, run the study and produce a document the other side has to answer. Founded in 1989 by organisations representing fisherfolk, farmers, indigenous peoples, women, the urban poor and professional sectors, it is based in Quezon City and works nationwide across different ecological contexts, combining community-based research with adult environmental education built to be adapted to a specific socio-economic and ecological setting. It completes a set this file has been assembling. Thailand has EARTH, India the Environmental Quality Monitoring Group, Indonesia has Nexus3 — bodies whose job is to produce the independent finding. This is the Philippine one, and the four together make community-collected, independently-analysed evidence a regional technique rather than a local accident. Pair it with ELAC for the litigation, and with the Commission's certification process where ancestral domain is involved. Understand its position before approaching it. This is a movement-aligned organisation that campaigns in explicitly political terms against what it calls environmental plunder, and runs an annual State of the Philippine Environment forum. That alignment is why it will take on a case nobody else will; it is also why its findings will be read politically by the other side, and a community should decide in advance whether that trade is the one it wants. And it documents the security context itself. Its own site records armed patrolling around a people's barricade at Kasibu in Nueva Vizcaya, with more than five police including the municipal station chief arriving at half past ten at night on a sixth consecutive day. Working with it in a live mining dispute is not a neutral administrative act, and this entry says so because the organisation does.

trackers.name: PRRCFI — bought an island to stop it being wrecked, partly on a development bank loan
trackers.desc: The sequence is the lesson, and it is reproducible. A group of divers who saw an island's tallest trees about to be felled and its reefs being wrecked set out in 1991 to buy it. An outside expert was brought in to assess the site's conservation importance, a marine protection plan was drawn up with a specialist survey partner, and the purchase was completed in 1994 through international fundraising together with the World Land Trust and a loan from the Land Bank of the Philippines — reported to have been that bank's first environment loan. Assessment, then money, then title. The part almost nobody attempts is what followed. The waters around Danjugan are now the largest marine protected area in the Southern Negros Marine Key Biodiversity Area, declared by municipal ordinance on the basis of scientific assessments carried out by the foundation itself and its survey partner. That is the whole chain in one place: an organisation produced its own science and a local government turned it into law. Where a community can reach its municipal council, this is the model to put in front of it. The financing route is the transferable part for anyone raising a purchase price. A state development bank made an environment loan against a conservation purchase. Any community told that conservation land cannot be financed should ask whether its own agricultural or development bank has an environmental lending line, because in the Philippines one did. Two cautions. The island's area is given as 48 hectares on the foundation's own site and 43 hectares by its funding partner, so take the figure from the foundation. And the domain is prrcf.org — the acronym is PRRCFI, so prrcfi.org is the address people construct and it is not where the organisation is. The foundation runs youth marine and wildlife camps begun in 1991 and operates the island on a deliberately low-volume tourism model.

trackers.name: Mine Rehabilitation Fund and CLRF — the money a mine must lodge, and who holds it
trackers.desc: Every operating mining contractor and permit holder must lodge money against its own environmental promises, and failing to do so is expressly sufficient ground to suspend or cancel the operation. The umbrella mechanism is the Contingent Liability and Rehabilitation Fund, comprising the Mine Rehabilitation Fund — itself made up of a Monitoring Trust Fund and a Rehabilitation Cash Fund — together with mine waste and tailings fees and the Final Mine Rehabilitation and Decommissioning Fund. The Mine Rehabilitation Fund exists to guarantee performance of the commitments in the operator's Environmental Protection and Enhancement Program. Three checkable facts follow, and none of them depends on the company. Whether the operator has established its funds at all; whether its annual cash provision was paid within sixty days of approval of its decommissioning plan and on each anniversary since; and whether the deposits sit in a government depository bank, which is where the rules require them to be held. Non-establishment is not a technicality — it is stated as a ground for suspension or cancellation. The documents behind the money are the ones to ask for. The Environmental Protection and Enhancement Program sets out the expected impacts and the life-of-mine protection strategy; the Final Mine Rehabilitation and Decommissioning Plan is the plan for returning the site and affected areas to viable and, where practicable, self-sustaining ecosystems. Both are required by regulation, both are submitted for approval, and both record what the operator has promised in terms it can be held to years later. Know which body to write to. The steering committee, chaired by the bureau's director, approves the programmes and plans, monitors the deposited funds and may consult outside experts on the adequacy of the control and rehabilitation measures, while a separate committee receives the annual cash provisions. An operator whose mine is suspended or in care and maintenance must still establish the decommissioning fund. Approvals are published quarterly.

trackers.name: CBFMA — twenty-five years of tenure over forest land, renewable, held by a people's organization
trackers.desc: It is a production-sharing agreement giving a community organisation twenty-five years of tenurial security over defined forest land, renewable for another twenty-five. The bureau describes it as providing tenurial security and incentives to develop, utilise and manage specific portions of forest lands, and published research puts the programme at roughly 1,954 agreements covering about 1.6 million hectares, much of it ground formerly held under timber licences. For a community with no prospect of buying land, this is the largest tenure instrument in the Philippines that it can hold in its own name. The gate is the local councils, so secure them first. The application requires individual or joint endorsement from the legislative councils of the barangay, the municipality and the province. Those endorsements are political rather than technical, they are obtained in a known order, and a community that starts with the barangay and works upward is doing the application in the sequence that actually determines it. The community writes the management framework itself. The resource management framework defines the terms and procedures for access, use and protection of resources inside the area and must be consistent with the strategy for the whole watershed; it is formulated by the community with assistance from its organisation, the department, the local government or others. The obligations that come with it are substantial: assume responsibility for protecting the entire forest land in the area against illegal logging, unauthorised extraction, slash-and-burn and fire, assist in prosecuting violators, prepare and implement a resource use plan and annual work plans, formulate and implement benefit-sharing among members, and pay forest charges. Keep the map and the record of works from the first year. On renewal the field offices are directed to assist a holder whose agreement is recommended for renewal, and the documents required include the original and any amended agreement together with a mapped record showing the development projects the holder has carried out; a renewed agreement runs a further twenty-five years from the last day of the original, and non-renewal is notified in writing. Published research records roughly a thousand agreements expiring within five years, which makes the renewal file the live issue for most existing holders.

trackers.name: DENR recognized environmental laboratories — they must test for NGOs and individuals, and their signatories are published
trackers.desc: The recognised laboratories are required to analyse samples for individuals and non-governmental organisations, not only for companies. Established under the clean water statute and its implementing rules, the recognition system authorises laboratories to generate environmental data in connection with the environmental impact assessment system, environmental monitoring and research supporting the bureau's policies, criteria, guidelines and regulations — and the bureau states that recognised laboratories shall analyse environmental samples for private companies and individuals, the department, other government agencies, non-governmental organisations and local government units. A community can therefore commission the same class of laboratory that produced the figures in a developer's assessment. The recognised signatories are published, laboratory by laboratory. Each recognised laboratory's entry lists the categories it is recognised for, such as water and wastewater, together with the individuals recognised to sign its reports. A report signed by someone who is not a recognised signatory for that laboratory and that category is defective on its face — so check the signature against the published entry before spending time arguing about the numbers themselves. Nothing else in this file offers a check that cheap. Recognition is granted by stated scope. An applicant laboratory must set out the scope of recognition it seeks, its accreditation record, its technical and support personnel, the scope and nature of its work and its laboratory test report forms. The scope of a laboratory's recognition is therefore a matter of record that can be asked for — and, as the Singapore entry in this file records, recognition and accreditation are both specific to particular tests rather than general. Where to go and who to ask. The bureau's environmental research and laboratory services division publishes the list of recognised environmental laboratories and runs the central office laboratory, with published telephone numbers, a divisional email address and a separate address for recognition concerns; records and reporting for recognised laboratories are being moved onto an online system. Start with the list, then the scope, then the signatory.

trackers.name: Public Attorney's Office — free counsel in administrative and civil cases too, and help before the paperwork clears
trackers.desc: The mandate is wider than criminal defence. Under its governing statute the office independently discharges a mandate to render, free of charge, legal representation, assistance and counselling to indigent persons in criminal, civil, labour, administrative and other quasi-judicial cases, and may be called on by proper government authorities to serve others subject to law. Where a community's fight is an administrative or quasi-judicial proceeding — the shape most development disputes actually take — that is inside the mandate, unlike several of the schemes recorded elsewhere in this file which reach only criminal charges. Cases can be taken provisionally, before the paperwork clears. Public attorneys may accept or handle a case provisionally, pending verification of the applicant's indigency and evaluation of the merit of the case, in stated situations: where a warrant of arrest has issued and help is needed to file a motion to post or reduce bail for provisional liberty; where a person has been arrested or detained and immediate legal action is needed to protect their rights; where a pleading must be filed immediately or an appeal perfected to avoid adverse effects; and where the court appoints the attorney as counsel. For a community whose members are picked up at a barricade on a Friday, that provision is the whole difference. Two tests, and the merit test is one you can write to. Indigency is shown by a certificate of indigency or no income from the barangay chairperson with jurisdiction over the applicant's residence, or by an income tax return, pay slip or social welfare certificate, with attorneys required to exercise prudence in checking it. Merit is defined in the office's own manual: a case is meritorious where an assessment of the law and the evidence on hand discloses that the office's services will assist, be in aid of, or be in furtherance of justice, taking into consideration the interests of the parties and those of society. Owning land does not by itself defeat a claim of indigency. Reported thresholds put monthly net income at around twenty-four thousand pesos in the capital region, twenty-two thousand in other cities and twenty thousand in municipalities outside them, and press guidance records that ownership of real property does not on its own negate indigency — which matters for exactly the landholding families this file is concerned with. Go to the district office nearest the applicant's residence. Read this with the environmental legal assistance and ancestral domain entries recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Certified true copies of land titles — from any computerised registry, or delivered to your door
trackers.desc: You no longer have to travel to the registry that holds the title. Under the anywhere-to-anywhere service a certified true copy of a property title can be obtained at any computerised registry of deeds in the country, rather than only at the office where the title is registered. The authority's own description of the service is that it saves people travelling far and spending time and money to get a copy of their title. For a community whose land sits in a distant provincial registry, that removes the journey which quietly defeats most title checks before they start. Or have it delivered. The authority's online portal accepts a request for a certified true copy without any visit to an office, with payment made online through bank cards, electronic wallets or a payment code, and the copy delivered to a chosen address anywhere in the country; the fee is the same as at the counter and the delivery is stated to carry no additional charge. The status of a request can be followed on the portal's own request page. Expect longer where the title was never computerised. The portal states that manually issued titles require an additional five to seven working days, because the physical government copy has to be validated at the registry that holds it. Ask early: an old, never-computerised title is exactly the kind a community defending long-held land is likely to be checking, and the delay falls on the people least able to absorb it. What the copy is for. The authority lists conducting due diligence for buying, selling and leasing property among the uses of a certified true copy, and the document reproduces the government's own copy held at the registry rather than the owner's duplicate. Get the certified copy before the meeting rather than after it. Read this with the ancestral domain certification and public attorney entries already recorded for this country: the certificate says what the record holds, the certification says whether a domain is affected, and the attorney is who argues it.

trackers.name: eFOI — request the file, with a fifteen-day clock and an appeal when it runs out
trackers.desc: Fifteen working days, extendable once by not more than twenty. The standard processing time for a request under the freedom of information programme is fifteen working days. An agency may need longer and will tell the requester, but the extension shall not be longer than twenty working days. Where the request is granted the documents arrive as an attachment through the portal or by email, or the requester is asked to collect them; where it is refused, the agency must give an explanation for the denial. A refusal with reasons and a clock that has run are both documents a community can use. Every executive office must publish its own people's manual. Under the enabling order each office must prepare a manual setting out the location and contact details of its head, regional, provincial and field offices and the other places where the public can obtain information or submit requests, the person or office responsible for receiving requests, the procedure for filing and processing, the standard forms, the process for disposing of requests and the procedure for administrative appeal against a denial. For a community facing one particular agency, that agency's own manual is the map: it names who receives, who decides and where an appeal goes. Silence is a decision you can appeal against. An appeal goes to the person or office next higher in authority, who must decide within thirty working days of its filing, and failure to decide within that period is deemed a denial — which opens the next step rather than closing the matter. Knowing that the clock running out is itself an outcome changes how a request is followed up. Two duties worth quoting back. Government offices are required to create and maintain accurate and reasonably complete records of important information and to run a records management system that makes them easy to identify, retrieve and communicate; and failure to comply with the order is a ground for administrative and disciplinary sanctions against the officer concerned. The programme covers offices of the executive branch. Read this with the certified title copies, the ancestral domain certification and the public attorney entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Citizen Participatory Audit — citizens on the audit team, with the same document access as state auditors
trackers.desc: Citizens sit on the audit team. The participatory audit is a value-for-money audit carried out by the state audit commission with individuals selected from civil society organisations serving as members of the audit team, on a voluntary and unpaid basis. Published descriptions of the programme record that citizen partners are given the same access to documents as the state auditors themselves. Nothing else recorded in this file puts a member of a community inside the state's own examination of a project, with the papers open on the same terms. The subjects are the projects communities actually fight over. The commission's published participatory audit reports cover local road projects funded from the development fund, farm-to-market roads, a flood control project, tourism road infrastructure, waterworks systems, solid waste management, socialized housing, water sanitation and hygiene works, barangay health centres and school buildings, alongside audits of disaster funds and of the use of pandemic money. A community facing one of those can read how the same class of project was audited elsewhere before it starts asking questions about its own. The rest of the audit output is published as well. Annual audit reports setting out the results of the audit of each agency's accounts and operations, together with recommendations for remedial action, are published on the commission's website, along with annual financial reports, performance audit reports and special audit reports, and a citizens' desk is maintained. The annual report for a particular agency is therefore a document a community can open before deciding whether to ask for anything. And the presence of citizens changed behaviour. Reported assessments of the programme record that audited bodies implemented recommendations faster, sometimes even before receiving the final audit report, and that the commission institutionalised the programme by its own resolution after pilot phases. Read this with the freedom of information route, the certified land title copies, the public attorney's office and the procurement entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Agrarian legal assistance — free government lawyers for farmers, including in land conversion cases
trackers.desc: Free representation, defined by who you are rather than what you can pay. The department's own manual on legal assistance states that it consolidates the law, policies and rules to be observed by its lawyers and legal officers in rendering free legal assistance to tenant farmers, agricultural lessees and other qualified agrarian reform beneficiaries — including members of their immediate farm household — and other stakeholders of the programme, covering agrarian law implementation cases, judicial and quasi-judicial cases and all other agrarian-related cases connected with an agrarian dispute, together with mediation and the rendering of legal opinions. A household that qualifies does not have to prove poverty or find a lawyer; it has to establish its status. Conversion, exemption and retention sit inside the service. Published descriptions of the programme record three case types: judicial cases, quasi-judicial cases before the adjudication board, and agrarian law implementation cases, the last comprising the administrative decisions on exemption, conversion and retention. Conversion is the doorway through which farmland becomes a subdivision, a resort or an industrial estate — and this is a government lawyer, at no cost, on the farmer's side of that application. Few resources in this file sit that precisely on the mechanism that takes agricultural land out of agriculture. Filing can be electronic. Published announcements record that cases involving conversions and exclusions falling under the land use committees may be filed by email to the bureau's official account through the regional office's agrarian assistance division, as may applications for cancellation of emancipation patents and certificates of land ownership award and applications for department clearance, with original or certified true copies required afterwards to establish authenticity, and that mediation conferences, interviews and investigations may be conducted by video conference. For a farming household a day's travel from the provincial office, that is the difference between filing and not filing. The boundary is stated by the department itself. A departmental memorandum records that the field of expertise of these lawyers is agrarian cases, that more harm than good will result if other kinds of case are handled, and that such cases may be endorsed to the public attorney's office; a separate memorandum grants limited authority for these lawyers to appear for clients other than agrarian reform beneficiaries. Establish which office a dispute belongs in before queueing at either. Read this with the public attorney's office, the citizen participatory audit, the certified title copies and the environmental legal assistance entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Commission on Human Rights — complaints filed and tracked online, and the assistance a threatened community can ask for by name
trackers.desc: Complaints can be filed online, and tracked. The commission describes its services as filing a human rights complaint, requesting legal advice or counselling, and applying for a human rights clearance, and it operates an online system through which individuals file complaints, request legal assistance, track requests and access information; published accounts record the online complaints portal becoming operational in July 2024. Its contact page lists office hours and regional offices, so the nearest office is identifiable before travelling. A complaint with a tracking number is the difference between a grievance and a case. Its powers go well beyond investigating. Published descriptions of the mandate record investigation and case management of complaints of violations covering civil and political rights as well as economic, social and cultural rights, together with powers and services in aid of investigation that include legal aid and counselling, visitorial powers over places of detention, the application of forensic techniques, witness protection, and financial assistance to victims. Witness protection and financial assistance are what a threatened family actually needs, and they are worth naming explicitly in the request rather than leaving to be inferred. Threats to life or health are the trigger for using it. Practitioner guidance on reporting environmental violations records that where there is no meaningful response to a serious complaint, a formal written follow-up should go to higher officials, with parallel reports to the ombudsman where officials have failed to act and to this commission where there are threats to life or health. The environmental breach and the threat are two different complaints going to two different bodies, and treating them as one is a common and costly mistake. There is a published guide written for environmental defenders. A practical guide for environmental human rights defenders in this country covers abusive lawsuits brought to silence public participation, a framework for assessing and managing legal risk, the counter-measures available under the rules of procedure for environmental cases, and the processes for filing complaints with this commission. Read that before the first threat arrives rather than after it. Read this with the citizen participatory audit, the agrarian legal assistance, the certified land titles and the investigative newsroom entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Local development councils — a quarter of the seats are reserved for people's organisations, and accreditation is how you take one
trackers.desc: A quarter of the council is reserved. Under the local government code every province, city, municipality and barangay has a development council, and representatives of non-governmental organisations operating in that area must constitute not less than one fourth of the members of the fully organised council. Published guidance adds that the composition is to include duly accredited people's organisations, non-governmental organisations and the private sector operating locally, making up not less than a quarter of the council. That is a seat on the body that sets the direction of local development, not an invitation to a consultation — and the seats exist whether or not anyone claims them. Accreditation is the gate, and the procedure is published. The local council accredits non-governmental organisations subject to the criteria provided by law, and departmental circulars set out guidelines on the accreditation of civil society organisations and the selection of their representatives to local special bodies — the development council, the health board, the school board and the peace and order council — with a departmental circular also establishing a desk to handle civil society concerns. The sequence for a community group is therefore: form or join an organisation, get accredited, then contest the selection of representatives. What the council actually does.
