A SCHEME WITH DEVELOPMENT-BANK MONEY CARRIES OBLIGATIONS ON CONSULTATION, RESETTLEMENT AND ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT THAT EXIST INDEPENDENTLY OF NATIONAL LAW, AND A BODY LIKE THIS ONE CAN TELL YOU WHICH APPLY. WHO RUNS IT MATTERS TOO. THE PRESIDENT IS A CANDIDATE OF BIOLOGICAL SCIENCES AND A JOURNALIST, AUTHOR OF TWENTY-FIVE SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS AND OF DOCUMENTARY FILMS ABOUT THE COUNTRY'S ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL PROBLEMS, AND A MEMBER OF THE ANTI-CORRUPTION CENTRE OF AN INTERNATIONAL TRANSPARENCY ORGANISATION. THE VICE-PRESIDENT EDITS THE SITE AND BELONGS TO THE JOURNALISTS' UNION. A SCIENTIST WHO IS ALSO A JOURNALIST AND SITS INSIDE AN ANTI-CORRUPTION BODY COMBINES THE THREE THINGS THIS FILE KEEPS RECOMMENDING SEPARATELY: EVIDENCE, PUBLICATION AND THE CORRUPTION ANGLE. ASKING SUCH A PERSON WHICH OF THE THREE FITS YOUR CASE IS WORTH MORE THAN ASKING THREE ORGANISATIONS. ONE HABIT OF THEIRS IS WORTH IMITATING WHATEVER COUNTRY YOU ARE IN: THEY PUBLISH THE MINISTRY'S REPLIES TO THEIR OWN ENQUIRIES. AN ANSWER THAT EXISTS ONLY IN YOUR DRAWER CAN BE DENIED LATER; AN ANSWER PUBLISHED WITH ITS DATE CANNOT. THE LIMITS: this is AN INFORMATION AND MONITORING ORGANISATION, NOT A LAW FIRM — it reports, assesses and publishes, and it will not represent you. ITS EXPERT ASSESSMENTS ARE ITS OWN, NOT OFFICIAL EXPERTISE, and carry no formal standing in a permitting process. WHETHER IT TAKES REQUESTS FROM COMMUNITIES, AND WHAT IT CAN COVER GIVEN ITS SIZE, WAS NOT VERIFIED; several of its programme descriptions are of long standing rather than current campaigns. Read it with the ecological law centre, the provincial information centres and the chamber of advocates recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Community subvention programme — state co-financing for irrigation, water and sewerage pipelines, and the falling number of approvals
trackers.desc: THIS IS MONEY A COMMUNITY APPLIES FOR, NOT MONEY IT WAITS FOR. MORE THAN A BILLION AND A QUARTER DRAMS FROM THE 2026 STATE BUDGET WAS ALLOCATED TO THE PROVINCIAL GOVERNORS' OFFICES FOR COMMUNITY ECONOMIC AND INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS. AND THE ELIGIBLE WORKS INCLUDE THE ONES THAT DECIDE WHETHER LAND STAYS USABLE: THE CONSTRUCTION AND REPAIR OF DRINKING WATER, SEWERAGE AND IRRIGATION PIPELINES — ALONGSIDE COMMUNITY BUILDINGS, CULTURE HOUSES AND KINDERGARTENS, NIGHT LIGHTING, GASIFICATION OF SETTLEMENTS, REPAIR OF SHARED PROPERTY IN APARTMENT BUILDINGS, AND ENERGY-SAVING MEASURES. IRRIGATION PIPELINES ARE THE LINE TO AIM AT. THIS FILE HAS RECORDED ACROSS THE REGION THAT LAND IS LOST NOT WHEN IT IS TAKEN BUT WHEN IT STOPS BEING WATERED — AND HERE IS AN ANNUAL BUDGET LINE THAT REBUILDS THE PIPE, AWARDED TO COMMUNITIES THAT ASK. SUBVENTION MEANS CO-FINANCING: THE STATE PAYS A SHARE AND THE COMMUNITY FINDS THE REST, OFTEN WITH A DONOR OR DIASPORA CONTRIBUTION. SO THE PRACTICAL QUESTION TO PUT TO YOUR COUNCIL IS NOT WHETHER THE STATE WILL PAY BUT WHAT SHARE IT REQUIRES AND WHO WILL PUT UP THE MATCH — AND THIS FILE HAS RECORDED DIASPORA AND CROWDFUNDING ROUTES FOR THIS COUNTRY SEPARATELY. NOW THE FIGURE THAT SHOULD SHAPE ANY APPLICATION, BECAUSE NOBODY VOLUNTEERS IT: THE NUMBER OF APPROVED SUBVENTION PROJECTS HAS FALLEN EVERY YEAR — THREE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-THREE IN 2022, TWO HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-THREE IN 2023, TWO HUNDRED AND FORTY-TWO IN 2024, AND TWO HUNDRED AND FOUR IN 2025. A PROGRAMME APPROVING FEWER PROJECTS EACH YEAR IS ONE WHERE APPLICATION QUALITY AND TIMING MATTER MORE, NOT LESS. APPLY EARLY IN THE CYCLE, ASK THE GOVERNOR'S OFFICE WHICH CATEGORIES WERE FUNDED LAST YEAR AND WHICH WERE REFUSED, AND SHAPE THE REQUEST TO THE SURVIVING CATEGORIES RATHER THAN THE MOST AMBITIOUS ONE. THE MONEY IS ROUTED THROUGH THE PROVINCIAL GOVERNORS' OFFICES, WHICH TELLS YOU WHERE THE DECISION SITS. THAT IS A PROVINCIAL OFFICE, NOT A MINISTRY IN THE CAPITAL — AND IT IS A SMALL ENOUGH BODY THAT A DELEGATION FROM A COMMUNITY COUNCIL CAN REACH THE PEOPLE WHO RANK THE APPLICATIONS. ONE FURTHER USE: THE LIST OF FUNDED PROJECTS IS A PUBLIC RECORD OF WHAT NEIGHBOURING COMMUNITIES GOT AND FOR WHAT. ASK FOR IT. A COMMUNITY THAT CAN POINT TO A COMPARABLE VILLAGE'S FUNDED IRRIGATION SCHEME IS MAKING A FAR STRONGER CASE THAN ONE DESCRIBING ITS OWN NEED IN ISOLATION. THE LIMITS: this is A STATE CO-FINANCING PROGRAMME FOR MUNICIPAL INFRASTRUCTURE, NOT A CONSERVATION OR LAND-DEFENCE FUND — it builds pipes and repairs buildings, IT WILL NOT OPPOSE A DEVELOPMENT, and nothing here creates a right to object. THE APPLICATION PROCEDURE, THE REQUIRED CO-FINANCING SHARE, DEADLINES AND ELIGIBILITY WERE NOT VERIFIED — those are the four things to ask the governor's office first, and this entry rests on a news report of a government sitting rather than a programme page. Read it with the environmental information centre, the ecological law centre, the provincial Aarhus centres and the conservation trust fund recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Community grants with environment eligible — twenty-three to ninety thousand dollars in seven regions, and a foundation window open to individuals
trackers.desc: THE GRANT WORTH KNOWING ABOUT HERE PAYS BETWEEN TWENTY-THREE AND NINETY THOUSAND DOLLARS FOR GRASSROOTS PROJECTS IN BORDER AND CONFLICT-AFFECTED COMMUNITIES ACROSS SEVEN NAMED REGIONS, RUNS FOR UP TO SIXTEEN MONTHS PLUS A MONTH FOR FINAL REPORTING, AND LISTS ENVIRONMENT AMONG ITS ELIGIBLE THEMES ALONGSIDE PEACEBUILDING, YOUTH, WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT, DISABILITY INCLUSION, EDUCATION AND COMMUNITY RESILIENCE. ENVIRONMENT SITTING INSIDE A PEACE AND RESILIENCE PROGRAMME IS THE OPENING. THIS FILE HAS RECORDED THAT ENVIRONMENTAL PROPOSALS COMPETE POORLY AGAINST HUMANITARIAN ONES IN HARD-PRESSED PLACES — BUT WHERE A FUNDER HAS ALREADY DECIDED THAT WATER, LAND AND FOREST WORK COUNTS AS RESILIENCE, THE COMPETITION IS DIFFERENT AND THE VILLAGE'S REAL PROBLEM CAN BE NAMED DIRECTLY. APPLICANTS MUST BE REGISTERED ORGANISATIONS — CIVIL SOCIETY BODIES, FOUNDATIONS OR NON-PROFITS — AND THE APPROACH IS DESCRIBED AS COMMUNITY-BASED. SIXTEEN MONTHS IS LONG ENOUGH TO BUILD SOMETHING PHYSICAL AND SEE IT THROUGH ONE FULL SEASON, WHICH SHORTER GRANTS NEVER ARE. A SECOND WINDOW OFFERS FORTY TO EIGHTY THOUSAND POUNDS TO REGISTERED CIVIL SOCIETY AND MEDIA ORGANISATIONS FOR PROJECTS OF UP TO ELEVEN MONTHS — SO A GROUP REFUSED BY ONE PROGRAMME HAS ANOTHER OF COMPARABLE SIZE TO TRY. AND THERE IS SOMETHING RARER STILL: A NATIONAL FOUNDATION'S RAPID RESPONSE GRANTS INVITE NOT ONLY ORGANISATIONS BUT FOR-PROFITS AND INDIVIDUALS, WITH INDIVIDUAL APPLICANTS EXPECTED TO PROPOSE SMALLER PROJECTS MANAGEABLE BY ONE PERSON — WRITING AND PUBLISHING A BOOK, DOING RESEARCH, CREATING MULTIMEDIA PRODUCTS — UNDER A STATED CEILING. AN INDIVIDUAL WINDOW SOLVES THE PROBLEM THIS FILE HAS RECORDED IN EVERY COUNTRY: THAT THE PERSON WHO KNOWS THE VALLEY IS NOT A REGISTERED ORGANISATION. RESEARCH AND PUBLICATION ARE EXACTLY WHAT A DOCUMENTED CASE NEEDS, AND ONE PERSON CAN DELIVER THEM. THE PROCESS DETAIL FROM THAT FOUNDATION IS WORTH PREPARING FOR, BECAUSE IT IS WHERE APPLICATIONS DIE: IT CONDUCTS PRE-AWARD INTERVIEWS WITH KEY STAFF TO ASSESS ORGANISATIONAL CAPACITY AND IDENTIFY RISK FACTORS, AND THE AWARD DECISION MAY BE REVERSED IF THAT INTERVIEW SUGGESTS CAPACITY IS QUESTIONABLE. SO THE MONEY IS NOT WON WHEN THE PROPOSAL IS ACCEPTED. HAVE SOMEBODY WHO CAN ANSWER FOR BOOKKEEPING, PROCUREMENT AND REPORTING READY TO SIT THAT INTERVIEW — AND NOTE THAT SELECTED GRANTEES MUST ATTEND A GRANTS MANAGEMENT SEMINAR COVERING FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT, REPORTING, VISIBILITY AND PROCUREMENT, WHICH IS FREE TRAINING WORTH HAVING WHOEVER FUNDS YOU NEXT. THE LIMITS: MOST OF THESE WINDOWS REQUIRE REGISTRATION, WHICH EXCLUDES THE INFORMAL VILLAGE GROUP UNTIL IT CONSTITUTES ITSELF; THE COMMUNITY PROGRAMME IS RESTRICTED TO NAMED BORDER AND CONFLICT-AFFECTED REGIONS AND WILL NOT REACH THE REST OF THE COUNTRY. THESE ARE PROJECT GRANTS, NOT LEGAL OR LAND-PURCHASE FUNDS, AND WILL NOT PAY FOR AN OBJECTION OR A LAWYER. ALL THE CALLS DESCRIBED HAVE THEIR OWN DEADLINES AND SOME HAVE CLOSED — they are recorded as recurring routes rather than open ones, AND THE AMOUNTS AND TERMS COME FROM AGGREGATOR LISTINGS AND ONE FOUNDATION DOCUMENT rather than from every funder's own current page. Foreign-funded work carries political scrutiny a community should weigh. Read it with the environmental information NGO, the ecological law centre, the community subvention programme and the provincial Aarhus centres recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Agricultural assistance NGO — farmer field schools, seeds given on a pass-on promise, and wild edible plant knowledge
trackers.desc: THE MODEL WORTH COPYING IS IN ONE OF THIS ORGANISATION'S PROJECTS: IT FORMED FARMER GROUPS AND SUPPLIED QUALITY SEEDS, SEEDLINGS, AGRICULTURAL TOOLS, MEANS AGAINST PESTS AND ORGANIC FERTILISERS — AND THE FAMILIES WHO RECEIVED THEM COMMITTED TO GIVE SEEDS TO OTHER WOMEN IN THE COMMUNITY AND TO SHARE THE KNOWLEDGE. A PASS-ON OBLIGATION TURNS ONE DISTRIBUTION INTO A SPREADING ONE, AND IT COSTS THE FUNDER NOTHING. THIS FILE HAS RECORDED SEED AND SEEDLING HANDOUTS IN A DOZEN COUNTRIES THAT ENDED WHEN THE PROJECT DID; A WRITTEN PROMISE TO PASS SEED ON IS THE CHEAPEST DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A HANDOUT AND A SEED SYSTEM. THE ORGANISATION'S METHOD IS THE OTHER REASON TO APPROACH IT: PARTICIPATORY APPROACHES TO RURAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNITY- AND FARMER-DRIVEN RESEARCH, AND THE PRINCIPLE OF EMPOWERING WOMEN, POOR VILLAGERS AND OTHER VULNERABLE GROUPS TO TAKE PART IN THE DECISION-MAKING PROCESS. FARMER-DRIVEN RESEARCH MEANS THE QUESTION IS SET BY THE PEOPLE ON THE GROUND. A VILLAGE THAT WANTS TO KNOW WHY ITS SPRING IS FAILING OR WHICH VARIETY SURVIVES ITS FROSTS IS PROPOSING EXACTLY WHAT THIS BODY EXISTS TO DO — AND THIS FILE HAS RECORDED THAT COMMISSIONED RESEARCH IS THE THING COMMUNITIES CANNOT NORMALLY AFFORD. IT RUNS FARMER FIELD SCHOOLS — INCLUDING THE COUNTRY'S FIRST FOR INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT IN A VINEYARD — ALONGSIDE LOCAL EXTENSION AND RESEARCH GROUPS AND CAPACITY BUILDING FOR FARMER GROUPS ON ORGANIC AND LOW-INPUT AGRICULTURE IN MOUNTAIN REGIONS. A FIELD SCHOOL IS A SEASON-LONG GROUP THAT MEETS ON REAL LAND AND TESTS THINGS, NOT A LECTURE. THAT MATTERS FOR A REASON BEYOND FARMING: IT LEAVES BEHIND A GROUP OF PEOPLE WHO HAVE WORKED TOGETHER ALL SEASON, WHICH IS THE UNIT EVERY FUNDER AND EVERY AUTHORITY LATER ASKS TO DEAL WITH. ITS WORK ON THE RECOGNITION, PROCESSING AND USE OF WILD EDIBLE PLANTS, AND ON MEDICINAL AND EDIBLE PLANT PRODUCTION AND MARKETING, IS THE PART TO ASK ABOUT WHERE THE GROUND ITSELF IS THE ASSET. WILD HARVEST GIVES UNCULTIVATED LAND A DOCUMENTED ECONOMIC VALUE, AND THIS FILE HAS RECORDED THE SAME LOGIC IN OMAN WITH FRANKINCENSE AND IN KYRGYZSTAN WITH FOREST PRODUCTS. A HILLSIDE THAT FEEDS AND EARNS IS FAR HARDER TO WRITE OFF AS WASTE GROUND. IT ALSO COORDINATED NATIONALLY FOR A REGIONAL PROGRAMME ON SUSTAINABLE LAND MANAGEMENT TO MITIGATE LAND DEGRADATION AND REDUCE POVERTY, AND PARTNERED IN A CLIMATE ADAPTATION AND BIODIVERSITY PROJECT WITH THE REGIONAL NGO NETWORK RECORDED SEPARATELY IN THIS FILE — SO ONE APPROACH CAN REACH BOTH. ON SCALE AND ACCESS: IT HAS COMPLETED OVER A HUNDRED PROJECTS WITH A SMALL STAFF, AND WORKS WITH FIVE HUNDRED MEMBERS AND SOME THREE THOUSAND FARMERS, MOST OF THEM LOW-INCOME RURAL FAMILIES WHO CANNOT AFFORD MEMBERSHIP FEES — SO INABILITY TO PAY IS PLAINLY NOT A BAR TO BEING WORKED WITH. THE LIMITS: this is AN AGRICULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL DEVELOPMENT NGO, NOT AN ADVOCATE OR A LITIGATOR — IT WILL NOT OPPOSE A MINE, A ROAD OR A QUARRY, and its work is delivered through donor-funded projects that start and stop. MANY OF THE PROJECTS LISTED ARE OLD, AND CURRENT CAPACITY, GEOGRAPHIC COVERAGE AND WHETHER IT IS TAKING NEW COMMUNITIES WERE NOT VERIFIED — the membership and farmer numbers come from an interview several years ago. Read it with the environmental information NGO, the ecological law centre, the community subvention programme and the community grants with environment eligible recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Diaspora fund with affiliates in sixteen countries — it builds village water networks, and its money comes from telethons
trackers.desc: THIS PAYLOAD HAD NO DIASPORA FUNDRAISING ROUTE ANYWHERE, THOUGH IT IS HOW A GREAT DEAL OF VILLAGE INFRASTRUCTURE IN THIS REGION ACTUALLY GETS PAID FOR. THIS FUND IS THE CLEAREST EXAMPLE: ESTABLISHED IN 1992 BY PRESIDENTIAL DECREE, WITH AFFILIATE ORGANISATIONS IN SIXTEEN COUNTRIES AND NINETEEN SUBSIDIARIES AROUND THE WORLD. WHAT IT BUILDS IS EXACTLY WHAT A THREATENED VILLAGE NEEDS AND CANNOT AFFORD: A 2026 ANNOUNCEMENT RECORDS THE UNVEILING OF A WATER NETWORK AND A COMMUNITY CENTRE IN A NAMED VILLAGE. A WATER NETWORK CHANGES WHETHER PEOPLE STAY. THIS FILE HAS RECORDED ACROSS TWENTY-THREE COUNTRIES THAT DEPOPULATION DOES THE WORK NO DEVELOPER HAS TO DO — EMPTY VILLAGES LOSE THEIR LAND WITHOUT A FIGHT. INFRASTRUCTURE THAT KEEPS FAMILIES IN PLACE IS THEREFORE LAND DEFENCE, EVEN THOUGH NOBODY FILES IT THAT WAY. ITS STATED POLICY IS TO GO BEYOND BRICKS AND MORTAR TO PROVIDE SUSTAINABILITY FOR THE PROJECTS IT SPONSORS — SO A PROPOSAL SHOULD SAY WHO WILL OPERATE AND MAINTAIN WHAT IS BUILT, WHICH IS THE QUESTION THIS FILE HAS SEEN SINK MORE VILLAGE SCHEMES THAN ANY OTHER. HOW IT RAISES MONEY IS THE PART WORTH STUDYING RATHER THAN JUST NOTING: TELETHONS BROADCAST FROM ABROAD, AND A FOUR-DAY PHONEATHON RUNNING TWELVE HOURS A DAY STAFFED BY VOLUNTEERS — ONE OF WHICH RAISED ABOUT A MILLION AND A HALF EUROS IN A SINGLE YEAR. THAT IS AN ORGANISED ASK ON A FIXED DATE WITH A PUBLISHED TARGET, RUN BY PEOPLE WHO LEFT AND STILL CARE. ANY COMMUNITY WITH RELATIVES ABROAD HAS THE SAME RAW MATERIAL — AND THIS FILE RECORDED SEPARATELY THAT CROWDFUNDING CAMPAIGNS IN THIS REGION UNDERPERFORM WHEN THEY TARGET NEIGHBOURS RATHER THAN THE DIASPORA. IT ALSO ACCEPTS NON-MONETARY DONATIONS ALONGSIDE BANK TRANSFERS, WHICH IS THE LINE TO USE WHEN WHAT A PROJECT NEEDS IS PIPE, PUMPS OR A VEHICLE RATHER THAN CASH. AND IT PUBLISHES A TRANSPARENCY SECTION CARRYING REPORTS AND REPORTING FILMS. READ THOSE BEFORE APPROACHING: THEY SHOW WHICH VILLAGES WERE CHOSEN AND WHAT WAS BUILT, WHICH TELLS YOU WHETHER YOUR REGION IS INSIDE ITS PATTERN AND WHAT SIZE OF ASK IT ENTERTAINS. FOR RURAL WORK SPECIFICALLY THERE IS A SECOND BODY WORTH KNOWING: A RURAL DEVELOPMENT FOUNDATION OPERATING IN SIXTY-FOUR RURAL COMMUNITIES ACROSS SIX OF THE COUNTRY'S ELEVEN PROVINCES, SERVING OVER A HUNDRED THOUSAND PEOPLE, WITH COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT, CAPACITY BUILDING, ADVOCACY AND YOUTH EMPOWERMENT AMONG ITS METHODS. ADVOCACY APPEARING IN A RURAL FOUNDATION'S OWN LIST OF METHODS IS UNUSUAL AND WORTH TESTING — ASK WHAT IT HAS ADVOCATED FOR, AND WHETHER IT WILL SPEAK FOR A COMMUNITY RATHER THAN ONLY BUILD IN ONE. THE LIMITS: this is A NATIONAL AND DIASPORA DEVELOPMENT FUND CLOSELY TIED TO THE STATE — IT WAS CREATED BY PRESIDENTIAL DECREE AND THE GOVERNMENT HAS CONTRIBUTED TO IT, SO IT WILL NOT FINANCE OPPOSITION TO A STATE OR MUNICIPAL PROJECT. ITS PRIORITIES HAVE BEEN DOMINATED BY WAR AND POST-WAR NEEDS, WHICH SHAPES WHICH REGIONS AND WHICH KINDS OF PROJECT GET FUNDED, and one profile notes it had at times received less support than it needed to meet its goals. WHETHER VILLAGES CAN APPLY DIRECTLY, AND THROUGH WHICH OFFICE, WAS NOT ESTABLISHED - approach through the local authority or an affiliate and ask. THE FIGURES AND HISTORY COME FROM ENCYCLOPAEDIA ENTRIES, AN EMBASSY PAGE AND THE FUND'S OWN NEWSROOM, several years apart. Read it with the community grants with environment eligible, the agricultural assistance NGO's field schools, the community subvention programme and the ecological law centre recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Extractive transparency secretariat and the beneficial ownership register — who stands behind the mining company
trackers.desc: THE PREVIOUS ENTRIES IN THIS FILE TELL A COMMUNITY HOW TO FIND OUT WHO HOLDS THE LICENCE. THIS ONE ANSWERS THE HARDER QUESTION: WHO STANDS BEHIND THE COMPANY THAT HOLDS IT. FROM 2020 THE NATIONAL EXTRACTIVE TRANSPARENCY SECRETARIAT BEGAN PUBLISHING BENEFICIAL OWNERSHIP DATA FOR EXTRACTIVE COMPANIES, AND THE GOVERNMENT ESTABLISHED AN ONLINE REGISTER THE FOLLOWING YEAR, WITH MINING PILOTED FIRST BEFORE EXTENSION TO OTHER SECTORS. WHY IT WAS BUILT IS THE PART TO QUOTE WHEN USING IT: TO HELP IDENTIFY CONFLICTS OF INTEREST WHEN AN OFFICIAL OWNS A COMPANY; TO HELP IDENTIFY MONOPOLY SITUATIONS WHEN COMPANIES SHARE THE SAME ULTIMATE OWNER; AND TO ENSURE PROPER TAX COLLECTION BY REVEALING OFFSHORE OWNERSHIP. AN OFFICIAL WHO OWNS THE COMPANY IS THE SINGLE MOST USEFUL FACT A COMMUNITY CAN ESTABLISH ABOUT A PROJECT. THIS FILE HAS RECORDED PERMIT AFTER PERMIT GRANTED BY BODIES THAT SEEMED INEXPLICABLY WILLING — AND A REGISTER BUILT EXPRESSLY TO SURFACE THAT RELATIONSHIP IS THE FIRST PLACE TO LOOK BEFORE ASSUMING INCOMPETENCE. SHARED ULTIMATE OWNERS MATTER JUST AS MUCH IN A SMALL COUNTRY: TWO COMPANIES BIDDING FOR THE SAME LICENCE, OR A CONTRACTOR AND ITS SUPPOSED COMPETITOR, MAY TRACE TO ONE PERSON — AND THAT IS SOMETHING THE REGISTER IS DESIGNED TO REVEAL. THE SECTOR IS BIG ENOUGH THAT THE DATA IS WORTH THE EFFORT: METAL MINING ACCOUNTED FOR SOME SEVEN PER CENT OF GOVERNMENT REVENUES AND MORE THAN A QUARTER OF EXPORTS IN 2024, WITH COPPER, MOLYBDENUM, ZINC, GOLD AND SILVER THE MAIN PRODUCTS — SO ALMOST EVERY RURAL LAND CONFLICT IN THIS COUNTRY EVENTUALLY MEETS A MINING COMPANY. THE SECRETARIAT ITSELF IS STILL ACTIVE, MEETING ON ITS WORKING PLAN IN FEBRUARY 2026 — SO THERE IS A NAMED OFFICE TO WRITE TO, NOT ONLY A DATABASE. AND HERE IS THE HONEST PROBLEM, STATED BY THE PEOPLE WHO BUILT IT: DESPITE A LARGE NETWORK OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS AND JOURNALISTS WHO WOULD BENEFIT FROM IT, THE REGISTER REMAINS RELATIVELY UNUSED, WHICH IS WHY TRAINING WORKSHOPS WERE RUN WITH A FREEDOM OF INFORMATION CENTRE TO PROMOTE UNDERSTANDING AND USE OF THE DATA. AN UNUSED REGISTER IS AN OPPORTUNITY RATHER THAN A DISAPPOINTMENT. THE INFORMATION IS SITTING THERE, THE PEOPLE WHO MAINTAIN IT WANT IT USED, AND A COMMUNITY THAT ASKS FOR HELP READING IT IS ASKING FOR SOMETHING THE SECRETARIAT AND THE INFORMATION CENTRE HAVE ALREADY ORGANISED TRAINING TO PROVIDE. TWO PRACTICAL LIMITS TO PLAN AROUND. THE DATA IS PUBLISHED IN AN OPEN, MACHINE-READABLE FORMAT BUT ONLY ON AN INDIVIDUAL PER-RECORD BASIS RATHER THAN AS A BULK DATASET — SO YOU CAN LOOK UP A COMPANY, BUT NOT EASILY SCAN THE WHOLE SECTOR FOR PATTERNS WITHOUT HELP. AND THE TRANSNATIONAL AGGREGATOR THAT ONCE CARRIED THIS COUNTRY'S MINING OWNERSHIP DATA ALONGSIDE OTHER COUNTRIES' HAS SINCE BEEN CLOSED — SO THE NATIONAL REGISTER, NOT THE INTERNATIONAL ONE, IS NOW THE PLACE TO LOOK, AND ANY GUIDE POINTING ELSEWHERE IS OUT OF DATE. THE LIMITS: THIS IS A TRANSPARENCY INITIATIVE INVOLVING GOVERNMENT, COMPANIES AND CIVIL SOCIETY TOGETHER - IT PUBLISHES DATA, IT DOES NOT INVESTIGATE, ADJUDICATE OR OPPOSE A PROJECT, AND ITS MEMBERSHIP INCLUDES THE INDUSTRY IT REPORTS ON. BENEFICIAL OWNERSHIP DECLARATIONS ARE SELF-REPORTED AND THEIR ACCURACY DEPENDS ON ENFORCEMENT THIS ENTRY DID NOT VERIFY. WHETHER THE REGISTER IS SEARCHABLE BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC WITHOUT REGISTRATION, AND WHETHER IT NOW COVERS ALL SECTORS OR STILL ONLY THE PILOTED ONES, WERE NOT ESTABLISHED. THE ACCOUNT COMES FROM AN OPEN GOVERNMENT COMMITMENT PAGE, TRANSPARENCY ORGANISATIONS' BLOGS OF EARLIER YEARS AND THE INITIATIVE'S OWN COUNTRY PAGE. Read it with the ecological law centre, the community grants with environment eligible, the diaspora fund's village water networks and the public defender's office recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Cadastre committee's electronic counter — cadastral maps, surveying, the restrictions list, the valuers list and the building permits platform
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE COUNTER WHERE EVERY LAND QUESTION IN THIS COUNTRY IS ANSWERED, AND MOST OF IT IS ONLINE: STATE REGISTRATION, A UNIFIED REFERENCE ON A UNIT OF IMMOVABLE PROPERTY, PROVISION OF INFORMATION, COPIES OF DOCUMENTS, DOCUMENT VIEWING, APPLICATION SUBMISSION AND STATUS, SURVEYING, A CADASTRAL MAP REQUEST, MAPS BY PROVINCE, CORRECTED CADASTRAL MAPS AND A LIST OF THEM. THREE ITEMS IN THAT LIST ARE WORTH MORE THAN THE REST TO ANYONE FACING A PROJECT, AND THE FIRST IS THE LIST OF RESTRICTIONS. RESTRICTIONS ARE WHAT SIT ON A PARCEL BESIDES OWNERSHIP — EASEMENTS, PROTECTED ZONES, MORTGAGES, SERVITUDES, PROHIBITIONS. A COMMUNITY THAT LEARNS WHAT IS ALREADY REGISTERED AGAINST THE GROUND A DEVELOPER WANTS OFTEN FINDS THE OBSTACLE IT NEEDED, AND THIS FILE HAS RECORDED THE SAME LESSON IN THE SUBSOIL ATTACHMENTS OF ANOTHER COUNTRY. THE SECOND IS A LIST OF VALUERS. WHEN COMPENSATION IS OFFERED, THE ONLY ANSWER THAT MEETS A STATE VALUATION ON ITS OWN TERMS IS A SECOND VALUATION BY SOMEBODY QUALIFIED — AND HERE THE QUALIFIED PEOPLE ARE LISTED IN ONE PLACE RATHER THAN FOUND BY RUMOUR. THE THIRD IS AN ONLINE PLATFORM FOR BUILDING PERMITS, SITTING INSIDE THE SAME SYSTEM AS THE MAPS. PERMITS AND PARCELS IN ONE SYSTEM MEANS THE QUESTION WHO WAS ALLOWED TO BUILD WHAT, AND WHERE, HAS A SINGLE ADDRESS. CHECK IT BEFORE ASSUMING A SITE IS AUTHORISED — THIS PAYLOAD HAS RECORDED UNPERMITTED WORKS DISCOVERED ONLY BECAUSE SOMEBODY LOOKED. THERE IS ALSO PRECISE POSITIONING TO BE HAD: THE SYSTEM CARRIES A REGISTRATION APPLICATION TO USE THE REFERENCE STATIONS — THE SAME KIND OF SATELLITE INFRASTRUCTURE RECORDED FOR A GULF COUNTRY IN THE PREVIOUS ROUND, WHICH FIXES A BOUNDARY POINT TO CENTIMETRES RATHER THAN TO A DESCRIPTION. PRICES ARE PUBLISHED, WHICH MATTERS BEFORE YOU START: THE STATE DUTY RATES FOR REGISTRATION, THE LIST OF SERVICE FEES FOR REGISTRATION, AND THE LIST OF SERVICE FEES FOR PROVIDING INFORMATION ARE ALL SET OUT, ALONGSIDE AN IMMOVABLE PROPERTY TAX CALCULATOR. THE VALUATION GEOGRAPHY IS PUBLISHED TOO: TERRITORIAL VALUATION ZONES AND LAND-CADASTRAL VALUATION DISTRICTS FOR THE WHOLE COUNTRY, THE CAPITAL'S LAND VALUATION ZONES USED TO CALCULATE LAND TAX, AND VALUATION ZONES FOR BUILDINGS AND STRUCTURES. THOSE ZONES ARE THE OFFICIAL VIEW OF WHAT GROUND IS WORTH, BY AREA. A HOUSEHOLD ARGUING THAT AN OFFER IS TOO LOW CAN CHECK WHICH ZONE ITS LAND SITS IN BEFORE PAYING ANYONE FOR AN OPINION. ONE PUBLICATION IS ODD ENOUGH TO BE WORTH A LOOK: THE COMMITTEE PUBLISHES LISTS OF CERTIFICATES NOT DELIVERED TO CITIZENS — DOCUMENTS ISSUED BUT NEVER COLLECTED. PEOPLE LOSE RIGHTS BECAUSE PAPER SAT UNCOLLECTED IN AN OFFICE. IF A FAMILY EVER APPLIED FOR REGISTRATION AND HEARD NOTHING, THAT LIST IS THE FIRST PLACE TO LOOK, AND IT COSTS NOTHING. THE LIMITS: THIS IS THE STATE REGISTRY, NOT AN ALLY - IT RECORDS WHAT THE LAW AND THE AUTHORITIES DECIDE, INCLUDING EXPROPRIATIONS AND STATE ALLOCATIONS, AND IT SUPPORTS THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE REAL ESTATE MARKET AS ONE OF ITS OWN STATED PURPOSES. WHICH SERVICES ARE OPEN TO NON-OWNERS, WHAT THE FEES ACTUALLY COME TO, AND WHETHER THE RESTRICTIONS LIST AND PERMIT PLATFORM CAN BE SEARCHED BY A THIRD PARTY WERE NOT ESTABLISHED - those decide whether a neighbour can check somebody else's plot, which is the whole value here. THE SERVICE NAMES COME FROM THE ELECTRONIC SYSTEM'S OWN MENUS AND THE FEE AND ZONE LISTS FROM THE COMMITTEE'S INFORMATION PAGES, READ IN ARMENIAN, AND MENU LABELS DO NOT ALWAYS DESCRIBE WHAT A SERVICE DOES IN PRACTICE. Read it with the public defender's office and its respondent exception, the extractive transparency beneficial ownership register, the community grants with environment eligible and the ecological law centre recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Communities association and inter-community unions — the municipalities' own membership body, chaired by a mayor
trackers.desc: WHEN ONE VILLAGE CANNOT MOVE A MINISTRY, THE ANSWER IN THIS COUNTRY IS THAT THE COMMUNITIES HAVE THEIR OWN UNION: A COMMUNITIES ASSOCIATION FOUNDED BY THE COMMUNITIES THEMSELVES, WHOSE GOVERNING BOARD IS CHAIRED BY THE MAYOR OF THE CAPITAL AND WHICH HAS RECENTLY OPENED A NEW OFFICE. WHY A COMMUNITY JOINS IS WRITTEN INTO THE LOCAL SELF-GOVERNMENT LAW ITSELF: THE COUNCIL OF ELDERS DECIDES ON JOINING UNIONS FOUNDED BY COMMUNITIES AND PAYING THEIR MEMBERSHIP FEES IN ORDER TO COORDINATE THE ACTIVITIES OF COMMUNITIES AND TO REPRESENT AND DEFEND THEIR COMMON INTERESTS. TO REPRESENT AND DEFEND THEIR COMMON INTERESTS IS THE PHRASE A VILLAGE SHOULD QUOTE WHEN ITS OWN COUNCIL ASKS WHY IT SHOULD PAY A MEMBERSHIP FEE. A SINGLE SMALL COMMUNITY ARGUING WITH A MINISTRY LOSES; SIXTY OF THEM WITH A SHARED SECRETARIAT AND A MAYOR AT THE HEAD DO NOT. THE SAME LIST GIVES VILLAGES A SECOND, SMALLER OPTION THAT NEEDS NO NATIONAL BODY AT ALL: THE COMMUNITY HEAD SUBMITS TO THE COUNCIL THE DRAFT DECISION ON CREATING AN INTER-COMMUNITY UNION. TWO OR THREE NEIGHBOURING VILLAGES FACING THE SAME QUARRY, THE SAME RIVER OR THE SAME ROAD CAN FORM A UNION BETWEEN THEMSELVES. THAT IS THE CHEAPEST COLLECTIVE STRUCTURE IN THIS PAYLOAD AND IT IS ALREADY PROVIDED FOR. THE POWERS SITTING BESIDE IT ARE WORTH KNOWING TOGETHER: THE COMMUNITY HEAD CONCLUDES COOPERATION AGREEMENTS WITH COMMUNITIES OF THIS AND OTHER STATES AND SUBMITS THEM FOR RATIFICATION, AND CONCLUDES THE CONTRACTS LEASING OUT COMMUNITY PROPERTY IN THE MANNER THE COUNCIL ESTABLISHES, WHILE THE COUNCIL DECIDES ON ATTRACTING LOANS AND OTHER FUNDS. AGREEMENTS WITH COMMUNITIES OF OTHER STATES IS A TWINNING POWER, AND TWINNING IS HOW SMALL PLACES REACH FOREIGN MONEY AND FOREIGN ATTENTION WITHOUT A NATIONAL INTERMEDIARY. LEASING COMMUNITY PROPERTY IS THE POWER TO WATCH IN THE OTHER DIRECTION - IT IS HOW COMMON LAND LEAVES LOCAL HANDS. THERE IS ALSO MONEY AT THIS LEVEL: MORE THAN 1.25 BILLION IN NATIONAL CURRENCY IS TO GO FROM THE 2026 BUDGET TO COMMUNITIES' SUBVENTION PROGRAMMES, WHICH HAVE RUN SINCE 2018 AND FINANCE WORKS DEVELOPING COMMUNITY INFRASTRUCTURE. THE REASON THE EXTRA MONEY WAS NEEDED IS THE USEFUL PART: IT COVERS FINANCIAL OBLIGATIONS TOWARDS CONSTRUCTION ORGANISATIONS ARISING UNDER PROGRAMMES APPROVED BETWEEN 2022 AND 2025 AND STILL UNDER IMPLEMENTATION - WHICH MEANS UNFINISHED COMMUNITY PROJECTS ARE BEING PAID FOR NOW, AND A COMMUNITY WITH A STALLED SCHEME SHOULD ASK WHETHER ITS CONTRACT IS IN THAT QUEUE. THE UNION IS ALSO BEING DELIBERATELY STRENGTHENED FROM OUTSIDE: AN INTERNATIONAL PROGRAMME AIMS AT THE GOVERNMENT CONSULTING LOCAL AUTHORITIES PROPERLY ON MATTERS DIRECTLY CONCERNING THEM, AT THE ASSOCIATION OPERATING AS A RELIABLE AND STABLE STRUCTURE, AND AT CITIZENS HAVING THE OPPORTUNITY TO PARTICIPATE IN DEMOCRATIC DECISION-MAKING AT LOCAL LEVEL. A PROGRAMME WHOSE STATED TARGET IS THAT THE GOVERNMENT MUST CONSULT LOCAL AUTHORITIES PROPERLY IS A STANDARD A COMMUNITY CAN INVOKE WHEN A PROJECT ARRIVES WITHOUT CONSULTATION - AND THE ASSOCIATION IS THE BODY THAT CARRIES IT. THE LIMITS: THIS IS AN ASSOCIATION OF LOCAL AUTHORITIES, NOT OF RESIDENTS - A VILLAGER CANNOT JOIN IT, ONLY THE COMMUNITY CAN, AND ITS BOARD IS CHAIRED BY A SERVING MAYOR OF THE CAPITAL, WHICH TIES IT TO NATIONAL POLITICS. IT WILL NOT TAKE A CASE AGAINST A COMMUNITY'S OWN COUNCIL, AND WHERE THE COUNCIL ITSELF IS LEASING OUT THE LAND THE ASSOCIATION IS ON THE OTHER SIDE. MEMBERSHIP NUMBERS, FEES, SERVICES OFFERED TO MEMBER COMMUNITIES AND WHETHER RESIDENTS MAY ATTEND ITS EVENTS WERE ALL NOT ESTABLISHED. THE POWERS COME FROM THE LOCAL SELF-GOVERNMENT LAW AS PUBLISHED ON THE PARLIAMENT'S SITE, THE SUBVENTION FIGURE FROM A LEGAL NEWS OUTLET, AND THE CAPACITY-BUILDING AIMS FROM A EUROPEAN ORGANISATION'S PROGRAMME PAGE - NOT FROM THE ASSOCIATION'S OWN ACCOUNT OF WHAT IT DOES FOR MEMBERS. Read it with the wildlife refuge that leases village land, the cadastre's restrictions list and valuers list, the public defender's office and the community grants with environment eligible recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Pan-national foundation's village agriculture programmes in two border provinces, and the grantmakers that publish their amounts
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S BORDER VILLAGES ARE WHERE LAND IS LOST FASTEST, AND THE LARGEST DIASPORA-FUNDED FOUNDATION IS WORKING IN EXACTLY TWO OF THOSE PROVINCES: ITS MULTI-SECTOR AGRICULTURAL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMMES IN THE RURAL COMMUNITIES OF TWO NAMED PROVINCES CONCERN THE ORGANISATION OF LIVESTOCK KEEPING BY THE NEWEST METHODS, THE INTRODUCTION OF NEW CROPS, AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF GREENHOUSE FARMS. GREENHOUSES, NEW CROPS AND BETTER LIVESTOCK ARE WHAT KEEP A BORDER VILLAGE POPULATED. THIS PAYLOAD HAS RECORDED, IN THE SAME COUNTRY, A FOUNDATION THAT LEASES LAND FROM VILLAGES AND PAYS INTO THEIR BUDGETS - THE TWO TOGETHER ARE AN ARGUMENT FOR STAYING PUT THAT NO CAMPAIGN CAN MAKE ALONE. THE FOUNDATION IS REACHABLE AT THE TOP: ITS BOARD OF TRUSTEES INCLUDES MEMBERS WHO MEET THE HEAD OF STATE, AND AT ONE SUCH MEETING THE WORK IT CARRIES OUT ON COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT WAS SINGLED OUT AS IMPORTANT. IT IS ALSO MOVING INTO HOUSING: PROGRAMMES ARE PLANNED IN COOPERATION WITH THE GOVERNMENT FOR THE SUPPORT OF PEOPLE FORCIBLY DISPLACED FROM A NEIGHBOURING TERRITORY AND FOR SOLVING THEIR HOUSING PROBLEMS. A FOUNDATION BUILDING HOUSING FOR DISPLACED FAMILIES IS DECIDING WHICH VILLAGES GROW AND WHICH EMPTY. A COMMUNITY WITH LAND, WATER AND A SCHOOL SHOULD BE IN THAT CONVERSATION EARLY RATHER THAN READING ABOUT THE DECISION AFTERWARDS. ALONGSIDE IT SITS SOMETHING THIS FILE VALUES MORE THAN SIZE - A GRANTMAKER THAT PUBLISHES ITS AMOUNTS. A DEMOCRACY DEVELOPMENT FOUNDATION LISTS INDIVIDUAL GRANTS WITH SUMS AND PURPOSES, INCLUDING ONE OF TWENTY-FOUR MILLION FOUR HUNDRED AND TWENTY THOUSAND IN NATIONAL CURRENCY TO HELP AN ORGANISATION PRODUCE RELIABLE RESEARCH ON IMPORTANT SOCIO-POLITICAL QUESTIONS AND PROMOTE POLICY DIALOGUE, AND ANOTHER OF TWENTY-TWO MILLION TWO HUNDRED AND SIXTY THOUSAND TO STRENGTHEN THE INTEGRITY AND TRANSPARENCY OF ELECTIONS AT REPUBLICAN AND LOCAL LEVELS THROUGH LONG-TERM OBSERVATION. PUBLISHED GRANT AMOUNTS TELL AN APPLICANT WHAT SCALE OF PROPOSAL IS REALISTIC BEFORE THEY WRITE A WORD - AND THE SECOND GRANT SHOWS THAT LOCAL ELECTIONS ARE A FUNDED SUBJECT HERE, WHICH MATTERS IN A COUNTRY WHERE COMMUNITY COUNCILS DECIDE ON LEASING COMMON LAND. ONE OF THOSE GRANTS ALSO INCLUDES SOMETHING RARE: THE SUPPORT WILL HELP THE GRANTEE MAKE THE INSTITUTIONAL CHANGES NEEDED TO RAISE ITS RESILIENCE AND THE EFFECTIVENESS OF ITS WORK. MONEY THAT PAYS FOR AN ORGANISATION TO BECOME STRONGER, RATHER THAN ONLY FOR ITS NEXT PROJECT, IS WHAT THIS FILE HAS FOUND MISSING ALMOST EVERYWHERE. IT IS WORTH ASKING FOR BY NAME. AND THE STRUCTURE THAT SPEAKS FOR ALL THE VILLAGES IS OLDER THAN EITHER: THE UNION OF COMMUNITIES OF THE COUNTRY WAS FOUNDED IN 1997, UNITING ALL THE RURAL AND URBAN COMMUNITIES, AND HAVING FIRST OPERATED AS A PUBLIC ORGANISATION WAS REORGANISED IN 2009 INTO A UNION OF LEGAL PERSONS. ONE FURTHER RESOURCE IS RECORDED IN A DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME'S OWN DOCUMENT: LOCAL CLIMATE RISK MAPPING AND GUIDELINES, AND TECHNOLOGIES FOR INTEGRATING CLIMATE RISKS INTO COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMMES, HAVE BEEN PILOTED AND THEIR COST-EFFECTIVENESS PROVEN. A COMMUNITY THAT WANTS ITS FLOOD, HAIL OR LANDSLIDE EXPOSURE ON PAPER SHOULD ASK FOR THAT MAPPING BY NAME RATHER THAN COMMISSIONING A STUDY - IT EXISTS AND HAS BEEN TESTED. THE LIMITS: THE PAN-NATIONAL FOUNDATION IS A LARGE DIASPORA-FUNDED BODY WORKING THROUGH GOVERNMENT PARTNERSHIPS AND ITS OWN PRIORITIES - IT IS NOT A GRANT WINDOW A VILLAGE CAN APPLY TO, AND HOW COMMUNITIES ARE SELECTED FOR ITS AGRICULTURAL PROGRAMMES WAS NOT ESTABLISHED; ITS CLOSENESS TO THE STATE MEANS IT WILL NOT FUND OPPOSITION TO A GOVERNMENT PROJECT. THE RE-GRANTER'S PUBLISHED GRANTS ARE FOR RESEARCH AND ELECTION OBSERVATION RATHER THAN LAND OR ENVIRONMENT, AND ITS ROUNDS DEPEND ON THE FOREIGN PROGRAMMES FINANCING THEM. THE ACCOUNT COMES FROM A NEWS AGGREGATOR'S REPORT OF A PRESIDENTIAL MEETING, A FOUNDATION'S OWN APRIL 2026 GRANT LISTINGS, A CIVIL SOCIETY MAP ENTRY AND A DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME DOCUMENT - NOT FROM THE PAN-NATIONAL FOUNDATION'S OWN CURRENT PUBLICATIONS, AND NO CONTACT ROUTE OR APPLICATION PROCESS WAS SEEN FOR ANY OF THEM. Read it with the communities association and inter-community unions, the wildlife refuge that leases village land, the cadastre's restrictions list and the public defender's office recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Urban foundation and the forty-five community plans — trainers for local governments, and plans written with the residents themselves
trackers.desc: THE PREVIOUS ROUND RECORDED, IN A NEIGHBOURING COUNTRY, AN ORGANISATION THAT HELPS COMMUNITIES WRITE DEVELOPMENT PLANS RATHER THAN OBJECT TO THEM AFTERWARDS. THIS COUNTRY HAS THE SAME CAPABILITY AND A PROGRAMME TO SHOW FOR IT: INTEGRATED COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT PLANS ELABORATED FOR FORTY-FIVE BORDER COMMUNITIES THROUGH DIRECT ENGAGEMENT AND PARTICIPATION OF THE LOCAL POPULATION, WITH TWENTY-EIGHT COMMUNITIES ALREADY HELPED TO CREATE THEIRS. A PLAN WRITTEN WITH THE VILLAGE IN THE ROOM IS THE CHEAPEST PROTECTION A VILLAGE CAN OBTAIN. IT FIXES ON PAPER, BEFORE ANY DEVELOPER ARRIVES, WHAT THE COMMUNITY SAYS ITS LAND IS FOR. WHAT CAME WITH THOSE PLANS SHOWS THEY WERE NOT PAPER ALONE: FIFTY-SIX GREENHOUSES, NINETEEN SMALL-SCALE AGRO-PRODUCTION UNITS INCLUDING FRUIT DRYERS, WINERIES, A BAKERY AND A SEWING SHOP, COLLECTION CENTRES, WATER-SAVING TECHNOLOGIES AND WORK ON ACCESS TO SAFE DRINKING WATER. COLLECTION CENTRES APPEAR HERE AGAIN, AS THEY DID IN THE NEIGHBOURING COUNTRY LAST ROUND. THAT REPETITION IS ITSELF THE FINDING: THE THING RURAL COMMUNITIES MOST OFTEN LACK IS NOT PRODUCTION BUT THE SHARED POINT AT WHICH SMALL HARVESTS BECOME A SALEABLE QUANTITY. THE ORGANISATION BEHIND MUCH OF THIS WORK HAS BEEN OPERATING SINCE 2004 AND IS THE LEGACY BODY OF A FOREIGN INSTITUTE THAT RAN A LARGE EARTHQUAKE ZONE RECOVERY PROGRAMME - WITH OVER A HUNDRED PROJECTS SINCE, ON INFRASTRUCTURE, POLICY AND LEGISLATION IMPROVEMENT AND ACCESS TO ESSENTIAL COMMUNITY SERVICES. ITS OWN ACCOUNT OF WHAT THOSE PROJECTS DID IS THE PART TO QUOTE: INITIATIVES IN COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT AND CAPACITY BUILDING THAT HAVE EMPOWERED LOCAL RESIDENTS TO ACTIVELY PARTICIPATE IN SHAPING THEIR NEIGHBOURHOODS, FOSTERING A SENSE OF OWNERSHIP AND RESPONSIBILITY - AND WORK IN ARCHITECTURAL AND CULTURAL HERITAGE PRESERVATION THAT HAS SAFEGUARDED HISTORICAL SITES. ITS METHOD IS EVIDENCE-BASED PLANNING, USING DATA AND RESEARCH TO INFORM STRATEGIES AND ENSURE LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY, WORKING CLOSELY WITH GOVERNMENT AGENCIES, LOCAL MUNICIPALITIES AND INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS. THE TRAINING SIDE IS WHERE A COMMUNITY CAN GET SOMETHING WITHOUT A PROJECT OF ITS OWN: A CORE STAFF OF SEVEN, A TRAINING COMPONENT IN ALMOST ALL ITS PROJECTS, MORE THAN TEN TRAINING MODULES DEVELOPED FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, A POOL OF TRAINERS COVERING LOCAL GOVERNMENT, HOUSING, ENVIRONMENT, MUNICIPAL SERVICES, MEDIA AND HUMAN RIGHTS, AND ABOUT A HUNDRED TRAINEES A YEAR DRAWN FROM LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, ORGANISATIONS, YOUTH, WOMEN AND STUDENTS. TEN MODULES WRITTEN FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENTS ARE TEN DOCUMENTS A COUNCIL CAN BE ASKED WHETHER IT HAS READ - AND A HUNDRED TRAINEE PLACES A YEAR IS A SEAT WORTH ASKING FOR BY NAME. ITS REACH IS NATIONAL BUT LOCAL IN SHAPE: A LARGE NETWORK OF PARTNER ORGANISATIONS, LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, LOCAL MEDIA AND CIVICALLY ACTIVE GROUPS IN ALL REGIONS OF THE COUNTRY, AND A BOARD SEAT ON A LOCAL DEMOCRACY AGENCY. AND WHAT IT HAS BUILT IS LISTED PLAINLY: CONCRETE MECHANISMS FOR CIVIL PARTICIPATION, MODELS FOR YOUTH EDUCATION, A REGIONAL YOUTH NETWORK, RESEARCH IN HOUSING POLICY, AND GREEN TECHNOLOGIES INVESTED IN THE COMMUNITIES - UNDER A STATED VISION OF A DIGNIFIED LIFE IN A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT. THE LIMITS: THIS IS A DEVELOPMENT AND CAPACITY ORGANISATION WORKING WITH GOVERNMENT AND MUNICIPALITIES, NOT AGAINST THEM - IT WILL NOT LITIGATE, BUY LAND OR OPPOSE A PROJECT, AND SEVEN CORE STAFF MEANS ITS CAPACITY RISES AND FALLS WITH WHICH PROJECT IS FUNDED. THE FORTY-FIVE COMMUNITY PLANS WERE PRODUCED UNDER A FOREIGN-FUNDED PROGRAMME IN ONE BORDER REGION IN PARTNERSHIP WITH A MINISTRY, NOT BY THIS FOUNDATION, AND WHETHER THOSE PLANS WERE ADOPTED, WHETHER THEY ARE STILL IN FORCE AND WHAT HAPPENED IN THE SEVENTEEN COMMUNITIES NOT YET COVERED WERE ALL NOT ESTABLISHED - THAT PROJECT'S PAGES ARE SEVERAL YEARS OLD. THE FOUNDATION'S STAFF AND TRAINING FIGURES COME FROM A NETWORK MEMBER PROFILE OF 2017 AND A CIVIL SOCIETY DIRECTORY OF 2019, WITH ONLY ITS HISTORY PAGE CURRENT, SO CURRENT SIZE AND ACTIVITY SHOULD BE CHECKED. Read it with the communities association and inter-community unions, the wildlife refuge that leases village land, the pan-national foundation's village agriculture programmes and the cadastre's restrictions list recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Territorial development fund's resettlement standard and replacement village — and the participatory budget that grew from four communities to fifty-two
trackers.desc: THIS PAYLOAD HAS RECORDED DOZENS OF COMMUNITIES LOSING GROUND TO RESERVOIRS AND ALMOST NEVER FOUND THE STANDARD THAT IS SUPPOSED TO APPLY WHEN THEY DO. HERE IT IS WRITTEN DOWN: THE AIM OF THE PROGRAMME IS TO RESTORE THE LIVING CONDITIONS AND QUALITY OF LIFE OF AFFECTED PERSONS AT LEAST TO THE LEVEL THEY HAD BEFORE THE PROGRAMME BEGAN. AT LEAST TO THE PRE-PROJECT LEVEL IS THE TEST TO QUOTE AT ANY DAM, MINE OR ROAD THAT MOVES PEOPLE. IT MEANS COMPENSATION IS NOT A PAYMENT BUT A RESTORATION, AND THAT A FAMILY LEFT WORSE OFF HAS A STATED BENCHMARK TO POINT AT. WHAT THAT LOOKS LIKE IN PRACTICE IS SPECIFIED IN DETAIL, AND THE DETAIL IS THE USEFUL PART: BECAUSE PART OF ONE VILLAGE WILL BE SUBMERGED BY A RESERVOIR, A DECISION WAS TAKEN TO MOVE THE VILLAGE ENTIRELY AND BUILD A NEW ONE - FINANCED BY THE GOVERNMENT WITH A TOTAL BUDGET OF NEARLY FIVE BILLION IN NATIONAL CURRENCY, CONSTRUCTION BEGINNING IN 2024 AND COMPLETION FORESEEN FOR 2027. THE SPECIFICATION IS THE THING TO COPY: A MASTER PLAN AND A FORWARD-LOOKING DEVELOPMENT PLAN, SEVENTY-FOUR INDIVIDUAL HOUSES, TWENTY-FOUR-HOUR WATER SUPPLY, A SEWERAGE SYSTEM, GAS SUPPLY, AN ENTIRELY NEW EDUCATION COMPLEX WITH A SPORTS HALL AND AN OPEN-AIR SPORTS COMPLEX, A NEW CULTURE AND ADMINISTRATIVE COMPLEX, AND A SEPARATE PRODUCTION AREA OF FOUR HECTARES. A PRODUCTION AREA OF FOUR HECTARES INSIDE A RESETTLEMENT PLAN IS THE LINE MOST COMMUNITIES NEVER THINK TO DEMAND. A NEW VILLAGE WITH HOUSES BUT NO PLACE TO WORK IS A DORMITORY THAT EMPTIES IN A DECADE. THE COMPENSATION FORMULA IS EQUALLY QUOTABLE: HOUSE FOR HOUSE, THE STATE PROVIDING RENOVATED MODULAR HOUSES THAT ARE SEISMIC-RESISTANT AND ENERGY-SAVING, WITH THE VILLAGE TO HAVE A PEDESTRIAN PATH AND A LIVESTOCK ROAD. A LIVESTOCK ROAD WRITTEN INTO THE PLAN OF A REPLACEMENT VILLAGE IS PROOF THAT SOMEBODY ASKED THE HERDERS. THIS FILE HAS RECORDED RESETTLEMENTS ELSEWHERE WHERE ANIMALS HAD NOWHERE TO PASS AND THE HERDS WERE SOLD WITHIN TWO YEARS. THE FUND BEHIND THIS WORK HAS OBJECTS WORTH KNOWING SEPARATELY: ASSISTING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF TERRITORIAL GOVERNANCE REFORMS - IN PARTICULAR ASSISTING THE EXPANSION OF INTER-COMMUNITY COOPERATION AND PROMOTING THE CONSOLIDATION OF COMMUNITIES - AND ASSISTING THE ELABORATION OF COMPREHENSIVE PROGRAMMES FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF COMMUNITIES AND TERRITORIES, WITH ITS BENEFICIARIES CONSIDERED TO BE NATURAL AND LEGAL PERSONS. BENEFICIARIES BEING NATURAL PERSONS, NOT ONLY COUNCILS, IS UNUSUAL AMONG THE MUNICIPAL FUNDS THIS FILE HAS RECORDED - AND INTER-COMMUNITY COOPERATION IS THE OBJECT TO CITE WHEN NEIGHBOURING VILLAGES WANT SOMETHING TOO BIG FOR ONE OF THEM. ALONGSIDE IT RUNS A PARTICIPATORY BUDGET WHOSE GROWTH IS THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT IN THIS ENTRY: IN 2024 IT OPERATED IN FOUR COMMUNITIES WITH SEVENTEEN CITIZEN PROPOSALS AND EIGHT PROJECTS BROUGHT TO LIFE; IN 2025 IN TWENTY-ONE COMMUNITIES WITH THIRTY-NINE PROPOSALS AND THIRTY-ONE PROJECTS IMPLEMENTED; IN 2026 IT IS BEING IMPLEMENTED IN FIFTY-TWO COMMUNITIES COVERING ALL THE REGIONS OF THE REPUBLIC. THE VOTING FIGURES ARE MORE STRIKING THAN THE MONEY: MORE THAN A HUNDRED AND NINETY THOUSAND CITIZENS HAD ALREADY VOTED IN 2026, AGAINST SEVEN THOUSAND IN 2024. A TWENTY-SEVENFOLD RISE IN TWO YEARS MEANS THE PROGRAMME IS STILL EXPANDING AND STILL ADDING COMMUNITIES. A VILLAGE NOT YET AMONG THE FIFTY-TWO IS ASKING TO JOIN SOMETHING THAT IS GROWING, NOT TO OPEN A CLOSED DOOR - AND THE STATE PAID 740 MILLION OF THE 1.2 BILLION SPENT IN 2025, SO ROUGHLY THE OTHER HALF CAME FROM ELSEWHERE. THE SUBVENTION LIST SHOWS WHAT SUCH MONEY BUYS, AND IT IS THE LIST THIS FILE'S COMMUNITIES ASK FOR: MORE THAN 1.25 BILLION FROM THE 2026 BUDGET FOR PROGRAMMES RUNNING SINCE 2018 THAT FINANCE THE IMPROVEMENT OF STREETS, GARDENS AND PARKS, PLAYGROUNDS, COMMUNITY BUILDINGS, CULTURE HOUSES AND KINDERGARTENS, THE CONSTRUCTION AND REPAIR OF DRINKING, SEWERAGE AND IRRIGATION WATER LINES, NIGHT LIGHTING, GASIFICATION OF SETTLEMENTS, AND REPAIR OF THE COMMON PROPERTY OF APARTMENT BUILDINGS WITH ENERGY-SAVING MEASURES. IRRIGATION WATER LINES SIT IN THAT LIST BESIDE PLAYGROUNDS. A FARMING VILLAGE SHOULD BE ASKING FOR THE CHANNEL, NOT THE SWINGS - AND BOTH ARE ELIGIBLE. THE LIMITS: THIS IS A STATE FUND IMPLEMENTING GOVERNMENT AND LENDER PROGRAMMES, NOT AN ADVOCATE - IN THE CASE DESCRIBED IT IS THE BODY CARRYING OUT A RESETTLEMENT CAUSED BY A RESERVOIR, NOT ONE RESISTING IT, AND A PUBLISHED RESTORATION STANDARD IS A PROMISE RATHER THAN PROOF OF WHAT AFFECTED FAMILIES ACTUALLY RECEIVED - NOTHING HERE RECORDS THEIR OWN ACCOUNT, WHETHER LAND WAS REPLACED AS WELL AS HOUSES, OR HOW DISPUTED VALUATIONS WERE HANDLED. THE NEW VILLAGE WAS DESCRIBED AS READY IN SPRING 2026 IN ONE REPORT AND AS COMPLETING IN 2027 IN THE FUND'S OWN, SO THE TIMETABLE HAS SLIPPED OR THE ACCOUNTS DIFFER. HOW A COMMUNITY JOINS THE PARTICIPATORY BUDGET, WHO SELECTS THE FIFTY-TWO AND WHAT THE NON-STATE HALF OF THE FINANCING IS WERE ALL NOT ESTABLISHED. FIGURES COME FROM A STATE NEWS AGENCY, A LEGAL NEWS SITE AND THE FUND'S OWN PAGES BETWEEN MARCH AND JULY 2026. Read it with the communities association and inter-community unions, the urban foundation and the forty-five community plans, the pan-national foundation's village agriculture programmes and the cadastre's restrictions list recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: EPBC Act Public Portal — federal referrals
trackers.desc: Australia's public list of every project referred for federal environmental approval under the EPBC Act (administered by the new National EPA from mid-2026), with each referral's documents and a public comment window. You CAN get: every proposed action touching nationally protected matters — the proponent, location, documents, decisions, and 10 business days to comment on whether it's a 'controlled action'. You CAN'T get: projects with only state-level impacts — those sit with state EPAs. For activists: the comment window opens the moment a referral is published, so watching this portal for your region is how campaigns get ahead of a mine or development while the federal decision is still open.

trackers.name: Australian Government Register of Lobbyists
trackers.desc: Federal register of third-party lobbyists under the Lobbying Code of Conduct. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held.

trackers.name: Australian Government Register of Lobbyists
trackers.desc: Public register of third-party lobbyists and clients who contact Australian Government ministers and officials. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held.

trackers.name: Foreign Influence Transparency Scheme
trackers.desc: Register giving the public visibility of activities undertaken on behalf of foreign principals to influence government and politics. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find foreign influence, funding and agents.

trackers.name: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)
trackers.desc: Australia's independent regulator for freedom of information and privacy — FOI reviews and complaints. — Holds to account: public bodies that hold records — find information-commissioner decisions and appeals.

trackers.name: AustLII
trackers.desc: Australasian Legal Information Institute: free primary legal materials including decisions of courts and tribunals. · Find here: free Australian legislation and the full case-law of federal, state and territory courts and tribunals (AustLII).

trackers.name: National Legal Aid (Australia)
trackers.desc: Peak body representing the eight state and territory Legal Aid Commissions, with national access-to-justice data. · Find here: the network of Australia's state and territory legal-aid commissions. IT DOES NOT TAKE APPLICATIONS — go to your state or territory commission. National Legal Aid represents the eight independent Legal Aid Commissions and their directors; the commissions are independent statutory bodies and NLA is a peak body for policy, advocacy and national projects. The national name is the most findable and the least useful — the same pattern recorded here for Canada's 13 provincial plans. THE FINDING THAT MATTERS FOR LAND WORK: NLA's own budget submission records that disaster response legal assistance has become a specialised area and an expansive area of law, expressly including insurance, housing and tenancy, grants, environmental and planning issues and income support. That is a named, separately funded stream in which planning and environmental matters are an express component — where general civil legal aid would not reach an environmental question, a post-disaster framing may. New South Wales, Victoria and Western Australia have received funding to deliver disaster response legal services, each state delivering differently on a place-based approach. BUT THE FUNDING IS DESCRIBED AS TEMPORARY and only three states are named — ask whether a service is currently operating. FOR NON-DISASTER ENVIRONMENTAL WORK, ASK ABOUT COMMUNITY LEGAL CENTRES: some CLCs specialise in particular areas of law, including environmental law, and the commissions administer the Community Legal Services Program funding — Victoria Legal Aid alone funds 42 CLCs. Ask your commission which CLC in your state specialises in environmental law; it administers the funding and will know — a more productive question than asking it to take the case. WHO WILL DO THE WORK: over 70 percent of approved legal aid cases are assigned to external practitioners under a mixed delivery model — but there are falling rates of private practitioners willing to take legal aid work due to disproportionately low remuneration, especially in regional and remote communities, which is where most land disputes are. The Justice on the Brink report found $484 million more per year is needed and the commissions critically under-resourced for over a decade.

trackers.name: Right To Know — FOI requests (AUS)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); Right To Know — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: Bush Heritage Australia — buying land for conservation
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a national not-for-profit that BUYS bushland outright to protect it permanently — 44 reserves covering over 1.4 million hectares, bought, gifted or bequeathed, each locked down with a conservation covenant that binds every future owner in perpetuity (no subdivision, no clearing, no building). USE IT: if land you are trying to save has outstanding conservation value, pitch it to them as an acquisition target, or partner with them on a purchase.

trackers.name: Australian Government (DCCEEW) — conservation organisations directory
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the federal environment department's own list of the conservation organisations that buy and manage land for the National Reserve System — Bush Heritage, Australian Wildlife Conservancy, Tasmanian Land Conservancy, Trust for Nature and others. USE IT: the official starting point for finding which body might acquire or covenant the land you are defending.

trackers.name: Environmental Defenders Office (EDO) — public-interest environmental law
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the largest environmental legal centre in the Australia-Pacific and an accredited Community Legal Centre — runs litigation for community groups defending their area from destructive development, and gives free expert legal advice. Its lawyers have fought some of Australia's biggest environmental battles, from the Adani mine to drilling in the Great Australian Bight. WHO IT SUITS: community groups, farmers, Traditional Owners and residents anywhere in Australia or the Pacific — never proponents. If you are not yet at the litigation stage, their online Legal Help Gateway carries free fact sheets.

trackers.name: Australian Wildlife Conservancy (AWC)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: acquires land and partners with other landholders to establish sanctuaries for threatened wildlife — the largest private owner and manager of land for conservation in Australia, covering 31 sanctuaries and partnership sites across more than 6.5 million hectares. USE IT: pitch a threatened parcel with high wildlife value as an acquisition or partnership target.

trackers.name: National Native Title Tribunal — future acts and Indigenous land use agreements
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Tribunal mediates and arbitrates the FUTURE ACT process — the statutory procedure triggered when a government proposes to grant a mining tenement, exploration licence or other interest over land where native title exists or is claimed. Native title parties get procedural rights: notification, a right to be consulted, and in defined cases a right to negotiate, with s. 31 agreements recorded. WHO IT SUITS: this is a right to be AT THE TABLE and to negotiate, not a general veto — be precise about which it is in a given case. The Tribunal also publishes dedicated guidance for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, mining and exploration, cultural heritage and land acquisitions.

trackers.name: GrantConnect via DCCEEW — how to catch every Commonwealth environment grant
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: individual Australian environment grant rounds open and close constantly — the Environment Restoration Fund ran 2019-2023, the Communities Environment Program closed in 2019 — so chasing a named programme is the wrong strategy. ALL Australian Government grant opportunities are published on GRANTCONNECT, the Commonwealth's grants information system, where you can register free and set a self-defined notification profile covering both live and FORECAST opportunities. WHO IT SUITS: any Australian community or environment group. HOW IT DIFFERS: the forecast feed is the real advantage — it tells you a round is coming before it opens, which is the only way to have a proposal ready in time. Funding continues through the Natural Heritage Trust, a $1.1 billion commitment running to the end of 2027-28.

trackers.name: National Landcare Program — Environment Small Grants
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: grants of $5,000 to $50,000 for projects improving the local environment through natural resource management, COVERING UP TO 100% OF PROJECT COSTS — no matching contribution required, which is unusual and makes this reachable for groups with no reserves. Eligible activities include weed treatment, pest and disease management, fencing, erosion management, revegetation, access management, community education, Indigenous land and sea country planning, and recording Indigenous ecological knowledge. WHO IT SUITS: community and environment groups. HOW IT DIFFERS: the 100% cost coverage and the explicit inclusion of Indigenous knowledge and country planning set it apart from co-funded programmes. Check the current guidelines — rounds and amounts change.

trackers.name: Landcare Australia — grants
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a national body that works with governments, corporate partners, philanthropic organisations and donors to build grants programmes for hands-on environmental projects — habitat restoration, sustainable land management, biodiversity. WHO IT SUITS: landcare and community groups doing on-ground work rather than campaign or legal work. HOW IT DIFFERS: rounds are intermittent and the site states plainly when nothing is open, so subscribe to the newsletter rather than checking hopefully; the money is raised from partners, so timing follows their cycles, not a government calendar.

trackers.name: DCCEEW — revolving funds by state and territory
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the federal environment department's own directory of the state-based revolving funds — the bodies that buy conservation land, covenant it and sell it on so the capital can be reused. Lists the responsible organisation and contact details for New South Wales, Queensland, South Australia, Tasmania and Victoria. USE IT: the fastest way to find the acquiring body for your state, and the route to South Australia's Nature Foundation, which is named here. ONE CAUTION: the directory carries at least one transposed web address for a listed fund, so use the phone numbers and email addresses to confirm, or search the organisation's name directly, rather than typing a URL straight off the page.

trackers.name: Bush Heritage — what a conservation covenant actually prohibits
trackers.desc: READ THIS BEFORE SIGNING OR PROPOSING A COVENANT: a conservation covenant prohibits subdivision, building (except in very limited locations), removal of native vegetation, interference with native animals and their habitats, disposal of non-degradable waste, and interference with natural watercourses and wetlands. It also compels the owner to protect ecological integrity, control feral animals and weeds, manage fire and erosion, carry out ongoing monitoring, and use local seed stock for any revegetation — so it is an obligation as well as a shield. Where land is held on a long-term Crown lease the covenant holds for the life of the lease and is easily renewed, which makes it substantial protection rather than a gesture. USE IT: the prohibition on subdivision and building is what stops a future owner developing the land, and it binds them, not just the person who signs.

trackers.name: Tasmanian Land Conservancy Revolving Fund — buy, covenant, resell
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a science-based non-government organisation running a revolving fund. It buys property with significant natural values on the open market, registers a Conservation Covenant on the title under the Tasmanian Nature Conservation Act 2002 in perpetuity, then puts the property back up for sale, with the proceeds returning to the fund to buy the next one. Properties reaching the market come through two channels: the TLC Revolving Fund, funded principally by the Australian Government's Forest Conservation Fund with contributions from the King Island NRM group and the state department, and the New Leaf Project of the Elsie Cameron Foundation. USE IT: the design detail that makes the whole thing work is the one to carry into an argument. Each covenanted property has one or more areas deliberately excluded from the covenant so a future owner can build a house and live there normally, subject to council approval. Inside the covenanted area, track maintenance, boundary fencing and ecological burning remain permitted, along with walking and birdwatching, and only activities that would damage the conservation values are restricted. That is the answer to anyone who says nobody will buy land they cannot use — and it means a community does not have to raise the purchase price permanently, only find a buyer willing to own a covenanted block. Mitchelmores Creek, 95 hectares of swift parrot habitat near Little Swanport holding old-growth remnants in a heavily cleared district, sold to a private buyer in 2021 on exactly those terms. NOTE ON FIGURES: published totals for how much the revolving funds have protected differ by source and date, so treat the mechanism as the reliable part rather than any single hectare figure.

trackers.name: Australian Communities Foundation grant rounds — and the money that goes to groups WITHOUT DGR status
trackers.desc: WHAT THIS PAGE IS: the running list of open and closed grant rounds at AUSTRALIA'S ONLY NATIONALLY FOCUSED COMMUNITY FOUNDATION, each with its ceiling, its region and its closing date. Australia had 56 filed entries but only THREE on funding, all government or Landcare. A national community foundation is the door for a group too small or too local for a Commonwealth programme, and its rounds are regional, not thematic. AND THE ONES THAT FIT A LOCAL CAMPAIGN: grants between $5,000 AND $10,000 to support STRONGER COLLABORATIONS, FOSTER CREATIVE IDEAS, ADVOCACY, AND ORGANISATIONAL SUSTAINABILITY, and grow community connection, SHARED LOCAL IDENTITY and greater social inclusion; a giving circle offering grants of up to $5,000 to support women and/or gender-diverse people LEADING ENVIRONMENTAL AND CLIMATE ACTION; and an Aboriginal foundation's future fund whose grants are OPEN YEAR ROUND to Traditional Owners and community-controlled organisations. Advocacy is named as a fundable purpose alongside collaboration — and a year-round window matters more than the amount when a project appears without warning. AND THE SCALE BEHIND IT: in one year the foundation distributed $37.4 MILLION, including $22 million of re-granting in partnership with a named philanthropic foundation, TO 698 ORGANISATIONS AND INDIVIDUALS across Australia.

trackers.name: A council's Environment Levy grants — the shire itself pays groups to protect its own environment
trackers.desc: WHERE THE MONEY COMES FROM, and this is the model worth checking in every Australian shire: $50,000 has been allocated FROM THE SHIRE COUNCIL'S ENVIRONMENT LEVY to enhance the local environment through a Community Environment Grants Program, with a maximum of $6,000 available for any one project through a competitive process. A council that levies ratepayers for the environment and then grants the money back to community groups is a funder inside the same building as the planning department — and the programme has run SINCE 2011. AND THE ELIGIBILITY, which is the lowest bar recorded in this file: a group must be NOT FOR PROFIT; be based in the shire and deliver a project that benefits the area; and have an ABN and be incorporated — OR BE AUSPICED BY AN ORGANISATION THAT HAS AN ABN AND INCORPORATION STATUS. Being auspiced by an incorporated body means an unincorporated group of neighbours can hold grant money through a friendly local organisation — no registration, no waiting years. AND WHAT IT IS FOR: to support community groups to ENHANCE, PROTECT AND RESTORE THE NATURAL ENVIRONMENTAL ASSETS OF THE SHIRE, to INCREASE COMMUNITY AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING of environmental assets, and to support conservation strategies currently undertaken by Council. A named grants administration officer, phone number and email are published.

trackers.name: The Revolving Fund — buy the property, covenant it, SELL IT ON, and buy the next one
trackers.desc: THE MECHANISM THAT LETS ONE POT OF MONEY SAVE PROPERTY AFTER PROPERTY: the trust BUYS PROPERTIES THAT ARE ON THE MARKET AND HAVE CONSERVATION VALUE. WE THEN RESELL THEM TO BUYERS WHO AGREE TO PUT CONSERVATION COVENANTS ON THEM, and it also BUYS, HOLDS AND SELLS LAND OF CONSERVATION VALUE THROUGH OUR REVOLVING FUND. Australia had five acquisition entries against 58 total. A revolving fund recycles the same money indefinitely, so a community raising it once funds every purchase after — the covenant stays on the title while the cash comes back. AND WHAT THE COVENANT DOES, which is why the resale is safe: it is A VOLUNTARY LEGAL AGREEMENT... TO PERMANENTLY PROTECT AND CONSERVE PRIVATE LAND, REGISTERED ON TITLE, MAKING IT LEGALLY BINDING FOREVER — EVEN WHEN THE PROPERTY IS SOLD OR PASSED ON TO NEW OWNERS. AND WHAT THE OWNER KEEPS AND GAINS: YOU'LL CONTINUE TO OWN THE LAND AND BE RESPONSIBLE FOR ITS MANAGEMENT, with the trust providing a STEWARDSHIP PROGRAM and experts to DEVELOP A LAND MANAGEMENT PLAN. Financially: MANY REGIONAL AND RURAL COUNCILS IN VICTORIA OFFER SOME FORM OF RATE REBATE OR CONCESSION TO COVENANTORS. PLUS, FROM 1 JANUARY 2024, LAND PROTECTED BY A CONSERVATION COVENANT IS EXEMPT FROM LAND TAX. Rate rebates and a land-tax exemption make protection cheaper than owning the land unprotected — the same argument as the Latvian tax relief in batch554.

trackers.name: Why several DIFFERENT buyers matter — and how each Australian body was founded
trackers.desc: HOW EACH MAJOR AUSTRALIAN LAND-BUYER CAME INTO BEING, which is the encouraging part: one state trust was established in 1972 after initiatives by a premier and a private trust, with THE VICTORIAN GOVERNMENT RESPONDING BY ENACTING LEGISLATION TO ENABLE THE ESTABLISHMENT OF AN ENVIRONMENTAL TRUST TO PURCHASE CONSERVATION LAND. A national body EMERGED TWO DECADES LATER FROM AN INITIATIVE OF THE GREENS SENATOR BOB BROWN TO FACILITATE THE GROUP'S FIRST PROPERTY PURCHASE THROUGH THE MORTGAGE OF HIS OWN HOME. THE RESULTING SUPPORT SHOWED THAT PRIVATE CONSERVATION EFFORTS WERE VIABLE. A third was THE VISION OF A PHILANTHROPIST WHO DONATED SUBSTANTIAL FINANCIAL RESOURCES TO ESTABLISH THE FUND. One of Australia's national land trusts began with a single person mortgaging his own house — the lowest-capital origin recorded anywhere in this file. AND WHY A COMMUNITY SHOULD APPROACH MORE THAN ONE, since they do not want the same things: one HAS A PRIMARY INTEREST IN CONSERVING ALL ECOSYSTEMS, OF OUTSTANDING ECOLOGICAL SIGNIFICANCE; another FOCUSES ON ACQUISITIONS FOR THREATENED WILDLIFE AND THREATENED ECOSYSTEMS; and a third FOCUSES ON TRANSFORMING RURAL LANDHOLDING COMMUNITIES IN DECLINING SOCIOECONOMIC AND ECOLOGICAL REGIONS. A refusal from one buyer is not a refusal from the category, and there are SIX STATE-BASED GROUPS alongside the national ones.

trackers.name: NSW Biodiversity Conservation Trust — private land conservation
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a statutory body under the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016 that negotiates in-perpetuity conservation agreements with private landholders AND PAYS THEM to manage the land for conservation. It holds 2,644 agreements over 2.17 million hectares, with 616,494 hectares protected forever; NSW has invested more than $356 million, and the median annual payment is about $102.50 per hectare. USE IT: more than 80% OF NSW LAND IS PRIVATELY MANAGED, so a private agreement often reaches ground that national-park designation never will. Payment eligibility is geographic — the Biodiversity Conservation Investment Strategy ranks NSW into five priority investment areas, and land in a high-priority area attracts funding support. BE AWARE OF THE CONFLICT: the same Trust also runs a biodiversity OFFSETTING service that compensates for biodiversity lost to development elsewhere, so it sits on both sides of the development ledger. That does not make an agreement any less permanent, but know it before you treat the BCT as an ally against a specific project.

trackers.name: NSW BCT — pathways to a private land conservation agreement (which type to ask for)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: compares the three agreement types, which is the decision that matters. CONSERVATION AGREEMENTS are permanent and attract either annual payments under the Conservation Management Program or grants under the Conservation Partners Program. WILDLIFE REFUGE AGREEMENTS are the entry-level option for a landholder who wants to protect biodiversity but is NOT ready to commit permanently. BIODIVERSITY STEWARDSHIP AGREEMENTS are permanent and let the landholder generate and sell biodiversity credits under the Offsets Scheme. USE IT: if a sympathetic owner is hesitating, the wildlife refuge route is the low-commitment way in — get the land into the system now and the permanent agreement can follow.

trackers.name: EDO advice line — Sydney office
trackers.desc: WHO TO CONTACT, AND WHEN: EDO lawyers give up to 15 minutes of free legal advice on certain planning and environmental law matters, and they state plainly that you should get in touch early so the matter can be dealt with in time — planning objections run on deadlines that expire, and a free consultation is worth nothing after the window closes. The Sydney office is at Suite 8.02, Level 8, 6 O'Connell Street, Sydney NSW 2000. EDO is an accredited community legal service and a member of the National Association of Community Legal Centres, formed in 2019 from the merger of 8 state and territory offices and working since 1985, with offices in Adelaide, Brisbane, Cairns, Canberra, Darwin, Hobart, Perth and Sydney. It acts for individuals, community groups, farmers, conservation groups and Traditional Owners.

trackers.name: Trust for Nature (Victoria) — permanent protection on private land
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: Victoria's statutory private-land conservation body — places permanent conservation covenants on private property and works on strategic conservation planning and on-ground protection. USE IT: if the parcel under threat is private Victorian land, a covenant is the instrument that protects it without a sale.

trackers.name: Environmental Justice Australia — legal support (Victoria)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Victoria's public-interest environmental law organisation (formerly EDO Victoria), acting for communities on environmental and planning matters. WHO IT SUITS: Victorian residents and community groups — outside Victoria, go to EDO instead. Their legal-support page also routes you to the other bodies that take these cases if they cannot act for you themselves.

trackers.name: Queensland Trust for Nature — the Revolving Fund
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: runs a REVOLVING FUND — it buys ecologically significant land, restores it, locks it down with a conservation covenant as a legally binding nature refuge, then RESELLS it on the private market and recycles the capital into the next purchase. Operating since 2004, over 100,000 hectares protected. USE IT: two reasons this matters in Queensland. First, about 85% of the state is privately owned or managed, so public reservation reaches very little of it. Second, the economics are extraordinary — because the money revolves, QTFN reports preserving roughly 104,000 hectares at an effective cost of about $1.32 per hectare, against single National Park acquisitions in Queensland that generally exceed $28 per hectare. If you are arguing for public money to save a Queensland site, that comparison is your strongest card. They also list properties currently for sale, so a sympathetic buyer can acquire land that is already covenanted.

trackers.name: National Trust WA — Conservation Covenant and Stewardship Program
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a statutory authority running WA's longest-established private-land covenanting scheme — begun in 1999, now 189 covenants protecting more than 18,000 hectares of bushland, registered over 340 land titles. Covenants bind the land, not just the current owner. USE IT: for WA bushland on private title, this is the route with the most experience behind it, and stewardship support continues after signing rather than ending at registration. BE AWARE WA HAS FIVE OVERLAPPING COVENANT PROGRAMMES delivered by three different bodies — this one, DBCA's Nature Conservation Covenant Program, Land for Wildlife, the Biodiversity Conservation Covenant Program and DPIRD's Soil Conservation Covenant Program. They are not interchangeable, and the same parcel can end up under more than one. Ask which fits before committing.

trackers.name: DBCA — Nature Conservation Covenant Program (Western Australia)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the WA Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions negotiates voluntary, legally binding covenants registered ON THE LAND TITLE, restricting activities that would threaten the land's conservation values. Each one is INDIVIDUALLY NEGOTIATED between the department and the landowner, so terms can reflect how the owner actually uses the land. USE IT: the reason to pick the departmental route over a trust is stated on the page — the department provides ongoing management advice, advocacy, AND ENFORCEMENT AS A LAST RESORT. If you expect the covenant to be tested by a future owner or a neighbouring development, a covenant the State will enforce is the stronger instrument. Contact the Species and Communities branch direct.

trackers.name: Nature Foundation — Bushbank Revolving Fund (South Australia)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: South Australia's revolving fund — it BUYS properties with conservation value, rejuvenates them, then sells them to new owners who are OBLIGED TO MAINTAIN THEM UNDER CONSERVATION STATUS, recycling the proceeds into the next purchase. Run by Nature Foundation (est. 1981), South Australia's largest private land conservancy, which also owns and manages seven nature reserves totalling over 500,000 hectares. USE IT: two routes in. Pitch a threatened South Australian property as an acquisition target; or, if someone in your network is looking to buy rural land, buying THROUGH the fund puts a conservation obligation on the title permanently and frees the Foundation's capital to save the next site. Donated land works the same way — the donor knows it stays protected and the proceeds buy more.

trackers.name: Tasmanian Land Conservancy — buying land for protection
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: conserves and protects Tasmania's natural environment by PURCHASING and managing land, holding it as private reserve. Has deductible-gift-recipient status, so donations toward an acquisition are tax-deductible. USE IT: to propose a threatened Tasmanian parcel for purchase, or to channel fundraising into an actual buy.

trackers.name: Conservation Council ACT Region
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the peak environment body for the ACT, advocating and campaigning on local environmental issues and acting as the umbrella for Canberra's environment groups — ParkCare and similar community groups sit under it, and it runs the annual ACT Environment Awards. WHO IT SUITS: anyone facing development in the ACT. In a jurisdiction this small the peak body is close to the ground, engaging directly on specific sites and on ACT Government budget and policy decisions, so it is a realistic first call rather than a national office to petition.

trackers.name: Environment Centre NT (ECNT)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the peak community-sector environment organisation in the Northern Territory, working since 1983 on land clearing, mining rehabilitation, biodiversity and stronger environmental legislation. TWO THINGS THAT MAKE IT USABLE. First, it is LEGALLY REPRESENTED — Environmental Justice Australia acts for ECNT, so its objections arrive as legal submissions rather than letters. Second, NT Environment Protection Authority guidance on stakeholder engagement treats ECNT as a body proponents SHOULD consult on referrals, which means a proponent that has not contacted them has a visible gap in its process. USE IT: for NT land clearing and mining referrals, get ECNT engaged early enough to be inside the assessment process, not commenting after it.

trackers.name: Office of the Privacy Commissioner
trackers.desc: Office of the Privacy Commissioner — New Zealand’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: NZLII
trackers.desc: New Zealand Legal Information Institute: free judgments and legislation. · Find here: free New Zealand legislation and court and tribunal decisions (NZLII).

trackers.name: Office of the Ombudsman (NZ)
trackers.desc: Independent officer handling complaints under New Zealand's Official Information Act. · Find here: New Zealand's Ombudsman — complaints and Official Information Act reviews.

trackers.name: Māori Land Court
trackers.desc: Māori Land Court — tribunal (New Zealand).

trackers.name: FYI — FOI requests (NZL)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); FYI — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: QEII National Trust (Ngā Kairauhī Papa) — open space covenants
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: an independent STATUTORY body (QEII National Trust Act 1977) that protects private land forever by registering an open space covenant — the landowner keeps and manages the land, and the protection binds every future owner even after sale. Over 5,000 covenants protect more than 180,000 ha. Roughly 70% of New Zealand is privately owned, so this is the main instrument for protecting lowland habitat. USE IT: if a sympathetic owner holds the threatened land, a covenant locks it down without anyone having to buy it. There are 30 QEII regions each with a local rep.

trackers.name: Environmental Defence Society (EDS)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a not-for-profit founded in 1971 by law students and scientists, combining law, science and planning, with a long record of litigating environmentally significant cases under the Resource Management Act — and it publishes its case studies. Its landmark win, EDS v New Zealand King Salmon [2014] NZSC 38, established that the New Zealand Coastal Policy Statement sets FIRM ENVIRONMENTAL BOTTOM LINES that must be given effect to, displacing the earlier 'overall broad judgment' approach under which environmental harm could simply be balanced away against economic benefit. WHO IT SUITS: cases with precedent value, especially coastal and landscape matters — if a decision-maker is balancing away an outstanding natural landscape, King Salmon is the authority to cite.

trackers.name: Forest & Bird (Royal Forest and Bird Protection Society)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: New Zealand's largest independent conservation organisation, which litigates — jointly with EDS it filed High Court judicial review proceedings challenging 99 of the Minister of Conservation's decisions on West Coast stewardship land, covering roughly 365,345 of the 644,000 hectares reviewed, on the ground that the Minister issued bare 'proceed / do not proceed' decisions with no reasons. WHO IT SUITS: public conservation land and species matters. USEFUL TO KNOW: about 30% of public conservation land is held as STEWARDSHIP land — over 2.7 million hectares, 9% of New Zealand's land area — a weaker protective category than national park, and the category most exposed to reclassification and disposal.

trackers.name: Ngā Whenua Rāhui Fund — protection of indigenous biodiversity on Māori land
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a contestable Ministerial fund (established 1991, administered by the Department of Conservation) that funds voluntary protection of indigenous biodiversity on Māori-owned land while honouring the rights guaranteed under Te Tiriti o Waitangi. Covers remnant forest, waterways and riparian margins, wetlands, tussock, coastal dunes and saltmarsh on Māori freehold, customary land, Māori reservation, or General land owned by Māori. WHO IT SUITS: Māori landowners — the fund's design point is that owners KEEP full ownership and management, and retain their tikanga and tino rangatiratanga; a kawenata is a 25-year renewable agreement tailored to the whenua, not a transfer. HOW IT DIFFERS: three statutory instruments are available and which one applies depends on the land's management structure — Ngā Whenua Rāhui Kawenata (s77A Reserves Act 1977 or s27A Conservation Act 1987) for long-term protection of Māori freehold land, and an Agreement for the Management of Land (s29 Conservation Act 1987) for smaller blocks. Funding also covers pest and weed control and landowner capability.

trackers.name: Waitangi Tribunal — claims process
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a standing commission of inquiry under the Treaty of Waitangi Act 1975 that hears claims that the Crown has breached the Treaty through an Act, regulation, policy, practice, act or omission, and that Māori suffered prejudice as a result. ANY MĀORI MAY SUBMIT A CLAIM. Registered claims receive a 'Wai' number, and the Crown and other interested parties are notified. WHO IT SUITS: where the harm traces to Crown action or inaction rather than a private developer — resource consents, statutory regimes, and Crown land and water decisions. CRUCIALLY: once a claim is registered it becomes ELIGIBLE FOR LEGAL AID, applied for through the Legal Aid Services Treaty team by a legal representative. That funding route is the practical reason to register early rather than late.

trackers.name: Te Puni Kōkiri — whenua Māori resources
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the Ministry of Māori Development's directory of the agencies and tools that bear on Māori land — Ngā Whenua Rāhui and Mātauranga Kura Taiao funds at DOC; Kāhui Taiao at the Ministry for the Environment, which advises on Treaty issues in environmental and resource-management policy and on Waitangi Tribunal claims involving natural resources; and the Environmental Protection Authority's Treaty obligations. USE IT: as the map of who to approach before committing to one route. It also points to Māori Land Online, the Ministry of Justice's definitive ownership, trustee and block record for land under the Māori Land Court's jurisdiction per Te Ture Whenua Māori Act 1993 — the place to establish who actually holds a block.

trackers.name: Companies Office
trackers.desc: New Zealand's official register of companies and their directors. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Office of the Auditor-General
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of New Zealand, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: New Zealand Companies Office
trackers.desc: New Zealand's official company register. Here you can trace companies, their directors and filings registered in New Zealand.

trackers.name: High Court of New Zealand
trackers.desc: High Court of New Zealand — tribunal in New Zealand.

trackers.name: Courts of New Zealand
trackers.desc: Official Supreme Court and senior-courts judgments. · Find here: judgments of the Supreme Court of New Zealand.

trackers.name: data.govt.nz
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in New Zealand.

trackers.name: GETS – Govt Electronic Tenders
trackers.desc: National public-procurement / budget-transparency portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this shows the specific firms winning specific tenders and contracts — for aggregate budget totals use the open-data/statistics portal, and for findings of waste use the audit body. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in New Zealand, and for how much.

trackers.name: Register of Pecuniary Interests
