trackers.desc: Federal Patent Court of Switzerland — tribunal (Switzerland).

trackers.name: Switzerland Zefix (company register)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); Switzerland Zefix (company register) — the official register of companies and legal entities in Switzerland — the primary public record of corporate existence, ownership, directors and filings. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A BENEFICIAL-OWNERSHIP REGISTER: this shows the registered entity, its directors and filings; where a separate beneficial-ownership register exists, use that to reach the real humans behind a shell company.

trackers.name: Swiss Federal Statistical Office
trackers.desc: Switzerland's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Switzerland.

trackers.name: Swiss Federal Audit Office (EFK)
trackers.desc: Switzerland's supreme financial-supervisory body — audits the federal administration's finances and management. — Holds to account: officials handling public money & power — find audit findings and how public money was spent or lost.

trackers.name: Lobbywatch
trackers.desc: Independent civil-society database (since 2014) mapping Swiss parliamentarians' interest ties and which lobbyists they grant building access — roughly 48,000 records.

trackers.name: Register of Accredited Persons (Zutrittsberechtigte)
trackers.desc: Switzerland has no full lobby register; instead Parliament publishes the official list of persons each member accredits for access to the Federal Palace — the country's main formal lobbying-transparency artifact (public since 2012).

trackers.name: Public Eye
trackers.desc: Swiss research-and-advocacy NGO exposing the abuses of Swiss-based multinationals and the policies that enable them. — Holds to account: officials handling public money & power — find research into corporate power, commodity trading and regulation.

trackers.name: SIMAP (Public Procurement)
trackers.desc: National public-procurement / budget-transparency portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this shows the specific firms winning specific tenders and contracts — for aggregate budget totals use the open-data/statistics portal, and for findings of waste use the audit body. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Switzerland, and for how much.

trackers.name: Court of Arbitration for Sport
trackers.desc: Court of Arbitration for Sport — tribunal in Switzerland.

trackers.name: Independent Complaints Authority for Radio and Television
trackers.desc: Independent Complaints Authority for Radio and Television — tribunal (Switzerland).

trackers.name: Federal Patent Court of Switzerland
trackers.desc: Federal Patent Court of Switzerland — tribunal in Switzerland (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Zefix (Central Business Index)
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Zefix — Central Business Name Index
trackers.desc: Official Swiss company register. Here you can trace companies, their directors and filings registered in Switzerland.

trackers.name: Verbandsbeschwerderecht — object first, or lose the appeal
trackers.desc: THE RIGHT THAT LETS AN ORGANISATION TEST A PROJECT IN COURT, in place since 1966: recognised environmental organisations can have an independent court examine whether nature and environment law is actually being complied with. THE TRAP THAT DESTROYS THE RIGHT BEFORE YOU USE IT: in some cantons an Einsprache — an objection at permit stage — is a mandatory precondition of lodging a Beschwerde later. Miss that window and the appeal is gone. Check your canton's rule the moment a project is published, not when you decide to fight it. AND KNOW ITS LIMIT: a Beschwerde cannot prevent a project — it can only have its lawfulness reviewed by the next instance. It has been attacked repeatedly, and a popular initiative to abolish it was clearly rejected at the ballot box in 2008. It works: planned construction interventions in the Aletschwald were averted through it. The Stiftung Landschaftsschutz Schweiz — founded 1970 by Pro Natura, Schweizer Heimatschutz, EspaceSuisse, the Alpen-Club and the Tourismus-Verband — also holds the right.

trackers.name: Buying land in Switzerland — a shared-purchase model, and a closing door
trackers.desc: OVER 800 NATURE RESERVES are held by Pro Natura, from small ponds to large wilderness areas — an organisation founded in 1909 specifically to raise money for Switzerland's first national park, created in 1914. A TACTIC WORTH COPYING: in Villnachern (AG) a building plot at the edge of the building zone held a species-rich Magerwiese; two neighbouring homeowners acted when development plans emerged but could not afford the whole parcel, so Pro Natura Aargau joined the purchase — partly because it already owned land on the same slope. Private neighbours plus a conservation body splitting a purchase is replicable anywhere. AND A LOSS THAT STILL PAID: Pro Natura Uri bid for part of a site to create a reserve, did not get the land, but was brought into all work stages early with a right of say — intervening in a sale was worth it even in defeat. THE DOOR MAY BE CLOSING: a revision of the bäuerliches Bodenrecht would let conservation organisations acquire agricultural land outside protection zones only where a protected plant or rare species is present. Pro Natura Luzern says projects like its Horüti site — over 8 hectares bought to build a large pond landscape on former gravel workings — could then simply not be realised. Check the current state of that law before planning a purchase. FOUR DOORS, NOT ONE: in Pro Natura's own words, some parcels are gifted, others bequeathed, or it buys them — and in other cases it concludes contracts over the use and care of land. An owner who will not sell can still gift, bequeath or contract, and the bequest route is the one nobody thinks to raise with an elderly owner. AND THE CASE THAT ANSWERS THE COMMONEST OBJECTION: Pro Natura bought the farm Hof Waldenstein in the Solothurn Jura and leased it to a farmer, so biodiversity is promoted through continued farming — which is the answer to ‘protection takes the land out of use’. It did not.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: KVU — your cantonal environment office, and the regional conference above it
trackers.desc: THE REGIONAL CONFERENCE IS A LEVER A SINGLE CANTONAL OFFICE IS NOT. KVU (Konferenz der Vorsteher der Umweltschutzämter, Haus der Kantone, Speichergasse 6, 3001 Bern) publishes a per-canton address directory — this link — and coordinates three regional conferences: CREPE for French-speaking Switzerland, USK Nordwestschweiz, and the Zentralschweizerische Konferenz, whose stated purpose includes harmonising enforcement across the region, producing joint position statements (gemeinsame Stellungnahmen), and carrying out joint actions, monitoring and controls. Where a development crosses cantonal boundaries, or one canton is more willing than its neighbours, that is the level to address. KVU also runs a named contact point for basic water-protection controls outside agriculture. WHAT THE CANTONAL OFFICE IS: cantonal ordinances implementing the federal USG define the Amt für Umwelt as the kantonale Umweltschutzfachstelle im Sinne des Bundesrechts, tasked with controlling the environmental measures of the canton, the municipalities, private parties and other obliged persons — it controls private parties, not only public bodies. THE ACCESS PROVISION IS WORTH CITING BY NAME: Nidwalden's ordinance states ‘alle Umweltdaten sind öffentlich, sofern nicht überwiegende Interessen entgegenstehen’ — all environmental data are public unless overriding interests oppose — with results held in Kataster, Inventare, Kartenwerke oder Berichte. Ask for the Kataster by name; a presumption of publicity with named document types beats a general information request. BUT THAT WORDING IS NIDWALDEN'S — each canton has its own implementing law and the wording differs, so check your own canton's kUSV. NAME THE RIGHT FEDERAL ORDINANCE: noise (LSV), air (LRV), soil (VBBo), contaminated sites (AltlV), major accidents (StFV), waste (TVA, VeVA), non-ionising radiation (NISV) and impact assessment (UVPV) each have their own instrument — naming the right one beats a general environmental objection.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Schweizer Heimatschutz — will object on your behalf (Switzerland)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Swiss Heritage Society, founded 1905, one of the national organisations designated to lodge Einsprache and Beschwerde against building projects, at cantonal and federal level. It has cantonal sections, a Rechtsdienst of its own, and it commissions short expert opinions so a section can take a founded position quickly. Villa Patumbah, Zollikerstrasse 128, 8008 Zurich. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES, IN ITS OWN NUMBERS: it publishes its case record every year. In 2024 it closed 29 cases — 8 upheld, 12 rejected, 7 withdrawn without agreement and 2 moot because the project was abandoned; in 2023 it closed 14. In 2020 it closed 21, of which 8 were upheld and 2 partly upheld. It objects in about two or three dozen cases a year for the whole country, and loses more than it wins. Approach it with that in mind: it is not a service, it selects. WHAT WORKS BETTER THAN THE OBJECTION: it states that its Bauberatungen and negotiations frequently produce agreements and improvements without any court being involved — and its own tally shows cases withdrawn once an agreement was reached. Going to the section early, before positions harden, is the route it says works. SCOPE: built heritage and Ortsbilder — historic buildings and the character of places. For open land and habitat the Swiss counterpart is Pro Natura.

trackers.name: Stiftung Ferien im Baudenkmal — takes over buildings facing demolition (Switzerland)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a foundation that takes over listed buildings anywhere in Switzerland which are decaying or threatened with demolition, restores them carefully, and gives them a secure future by running them as holiday accommodation open to the public at reasonable prices. This is the Swiss answer to a threatened building nobody will buy: an organisation that will take the building itself. AND IF IT CANNOT TAKE YOURS: together with Schweizer Heimatschutz it runs two things worth knowing. The Rote Liste publishes endangered objects of building-cultural value and public interest, with the stated aim of saving them — getting a site listed there puts it in front of the people who care and invites public participation while the case is live. And Marché Patrimoine, launched in 2020, is a platform placing historic buildings with buyers who want them, on the reasoning that many worth saving stand empty and decaying while the people who would restore them never see the offer, because such buildings vanish as niche products in the property market. WHO IT SUITS: a community whose fight is over a building rather than a field, and one that has worked out that the winning move may be finding the right owner rather than blocking the wrong one.

trackers.name: Fonds Landschaft Schweiz (FLS) — money for local landscape projects, on application
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a grant-making fund created in 1991 which supports local and regional projects to conserve and restore near-natural cultural landscapes. It is financed by federal money plus voluntary contributions from cantons, communes, business and private individuals, and it is independent of the administration in how it decides — a commission chosen by the Federal Council rules on applications. Applications may be made by private or public bodies, and it supports voluntary efforts from below on application rather than distributing top-down. Its own description of the principle is that it rewards the willingness of local and regional sponsors to help themselves. SCALE, AND THE ONE THING TO GET RIGHT: more than 2,600 projects supported since 1991 with about CHF 150 million, and 236 projects with CHF 7.76 million in 2021 and 2022 alone. Roughly 80% of its contributions benefit agriculture directly or indirectly, so a project that keeps farmers working the landscape is squarely what it funds. Submission deadlines are binding and it states plainly that no extension is possible — find the date before you start writing. WHAT AN APPLICATION MUST CONTAIN: a clear objective, demonstrated feasibility, a cost overview and a financing plan. It funds integral projects covering all the important landscape elements of an area with concrete improvement measures, and will also fund public information work where that is tied to a project it is already supporting. ONE RISK WORTH KNOWING: its legal basis has been extended repeatedly and currently runs to mid-2031, but a federal relief package proposed abolishing the fund outright and it survived with a budget cut. Treat its continuation as secure for now and not indefinitely.

trackers.name: Stiftung Landschaftsschutz Schweiz (SL-FP) — the last slice of the funding, and a guarantor
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: it regularly supports regional sponsors — foundations, cooperatives, associations — as well as cantons and communes, on projects that repair, maintain or improve characteristic and valuable cultural landscapes. READ THE LIMIT FIRST, BECAUSE IT DEFINES THE USE: it has only limited funds of its own and therefore participates primarily in residual financing — the last slice, once the rest is assembled. That is not a weakness if you know it going in. Most community budgets fail at the final gap rather than the first, and a body whose specialism is closing that gap is worth approaching after the main funder rather than before. THE OTHER THING IT WILL DO, WHICH MAY BE WORTH MORE THAN THE MONEY: it can recommend suitable large landscape projects for sponsorship, and in doing so it vouches for the quality of the implementation. A small association asking a company for money is one thing; a small association carrying a national foundation's endorsement is another. It also states that landscape work needs expertise and public awareness rather than money alone, and does not confine itself to passing on funds. USE IT WITH THE FONDS LANDSCHAFT SCHWEIZ, not instead of it: the Fonds is the larger grant-maker on application, this is the residual financier and the guarantor. Different roles, similar names, and a community will otherwise write to one and assume it has covered both.

trackers.name: Schweizer Alpen-Club (SAC) — a recognised appellant body with 110 sections
trackers.desc: THE STATUS THAT MATTERS: with the introduction of the Natur- und Heimatschutzgesetz in 1966 the SAC received recognition as an organisation entitled to appeal. Switzerland's Verbandsbeschwerderecht is already in this file through Pro Natura; this is a second holder of it, and a very different one. THE SCALE: around 180,000 members in 110 sections and 22 sub-sections operating 153 mountain huts owned by the sections. The sections are legally independent associations and may group into regions. Founded 1863. AND ITS PURPOSE HAS INCLUDED THIS SINCE 1906: protection of the mountain world from excessive development was written into its statutes that year, with the preservation of beauty and statements against disfigurement of the high mountains added in 1907, in response to numerous mountain-railway projects. Opposing alpine development is a statutory object more than a century old, not a modern add-on. WHAT IT DOES NOW: it defines unerschlossene Landschaft — undeveloped landscape — as valleys and terrain units of uniform natural or cultural character containing no larger infrastructure, and works on tourism expansion, renewable energy installations in alpine landscapes and mountain aviation. It says solutions come through political dialogue, that it cooperates with national and cantonal authorities on nature-sport and nature-protection concepts, and that it engages nationally through the central association — as in the consultation on revising the nature and heritage protection act — and at cantonal and communal level through the sections. TWO HONEST CAVEATS. First, its own guidance is that Mitsprache should be sought before Einsprache — participation before objection. Second, and it says so itself: local sections sometimes favour development projects with an eye to jobs and regional economic promotion, while the central association takes a more critical line. Do not assume the local section shares your position — ask. And note it has itself objected to the ENLARGEMENT of a nature reserve where a path requirement would have ended ice climbing.

trackers.name: InfoSpecies and info fauna — one application form, free for conservation associations
trackers.desc: THE STRUCTURE: InfoSpecies is the umbrella of Switzerland's national data and information centres and of the species-promotion coordination offices. Within it, info fauna is the national data and information centre for Swiss fauna, recognised as such by the Federal Office for the Environment — a private-law non-profit foundation formed in 2010 from the merger of the amphibian and reptile coordination office (karch, 1979) and the Swiss centre for fauna cartography (CSCF, 1990). Info Flora covers plants; moss, lichen and fungus records are forwarded to the centres responsible for those groups. InfoSpecies shares data through GBIF. WHY THIS MATTERS, in info fauna's own words: high-quality observation data form the basis for all planning — building projects, settlement areas — as well as for the upkeep of protected areas and habitats worth protecting. The observation data are used by federal, cantonal and municipal bodies and their contractors, including the ecological consultancies and self-employed biologists who write the reports, and are decisive for the national Red Lists. HOW TO GET DATA FOR YOUR SITE, which is the practical core: requests for fauna, flora and cryptogam data go through a single written application form to InfoSpecies, which forwards it to the relevant data centres, stating the species groups and the resolution you need. Delivery takes at least five working days and longer for point-precise data, and arrives as a printed or Excel list. The service is free for the federation, cantons, public research bodies, nature conservation organisations and other associations and foundations with non-commercial purposes; a reduced tariff applies to municipalities and to contractors of the federation or cantons. So a non-commercial association gets precise data at no charge — and on request info fauna will also produce individual expert reports, for example potential-distribution maps for species. AND HOW TO PUT RECORDS IN: report through Webfauna and its app, ornitho.ch for birds, FlorApp for plants and InvasivApp for invasive neophytes. Records go straight to the responsible centre, are checked there, and are published as distribution maps. Determination keys in the Webfauna app are free.

trackers.name: Reymond & Associés (Lausanne) — environment law in almost every planning and permit file
trackers.desc: WHY THIS CLOSES A REAL GAP: Switzerland's 24 filed entries contained no resource naming the Suisse romande, Ticino or any canton — in a country where building and planning law is cantonal and the procedures differ canton by canton. A French-speaking community had nothing. WHAT THE ETUDE DOES: it assists both upstream, for example in obtaining a permis de construire, and at the contentious stage, in a field it describes as very complex and technical where opposition and appeal procedures have become almost systematic. It is specialised in questions of environmental law, which it says is of determining importance in almost every planning and building permit file — noise protection, air protection, waste. Its lawyers include an FSA specialist in construction and real property law. AND A CAUTION, RECORDED HONESTLY: the firm also assists many public collectivities in their role as planners, at cantonal and communal level. Check for conflicts. ALSO IN THE ROMANDIE BAR: a Lausanne practice whose partner publishes the annual review of the Cour de droit administratif et public of the cantonal Tribunal's case law on spatial planning, public building law, permis de construire and environmental protection, and has written on neighbour rights and protection of trees, and the qualité pour recourir. Another Swiss firm names experience in the federal Act on the Protection of Nature and Cultural Heritage and in noise protection orders near airports, railway lines and motorways.

trackers.name: Swiss land purchase in practice — sections that own 300 hectares, and the neighbours who bought the field
trackers.desc: THE PRECEDENT A COMMUNITY CAN COPY DIRECTLY: in a small Aargau commune two private individuals bought 600 m² of ecologically valuable land with dry meadows and hedges, right next to where they themselves live, together with Pro Natura — so the three parties became owners of the meadow worth preserving, and the field is now a protected area. The organisation then applied to the commune to have the area assigned to the nature protection zone AT THE NEXT REVISION OF THE ZONING PLAN. Neighbours buying the field next door, jointly with a national organisation, then getting it rezoned — that is the whole sequence, and it happened. THE CANTONAL SECTION AS THE PARTNER: the Aargau section now owns 300 hectares, buys land regularly, and finances it from the contributions of its more than 17,000 members and from donations, with no annual budget for it — more or less money flows depending on the target. For areas of lesser importance the section must fund it alone; for important protected areas the national body can help financially. THE LIMIT, RECORDED HONESTLY: the national spokesman says they do not intend to acquire building land systematically — it is simply too expensive for us — and a canton reports that nature and landscape purchases were only six per cent of approved applications in one year, always requiring the consent of the existing owners. A separate note: the Swiss ornithological institute's purchase of farmland in a Valais commune improved protection for the scops owl.

trackers.name: SL-FP's Geschäftsstelle — it seeks improvements with owners first, and appeals as a last valve
trackers.desc: HOW IT WORKS, and the sequence is the lesson: the foundation pursues its aims above all through CONSULTATIONS, EXPERT OPINIONS (Gutachten), TRAINING, PUBLICATIONS AND PROJECT WORK, working closely with authorities and organisations in nature protection, townscape and monument protection, tourism, spatial planning and regional policy. It speaks up wherever landscape values are at stake and, IN BUILDING PROJECTS, SEEKS LANDSCAPE IMPROVEMENTS TOGETHER WITH OWNERS AND AUTHORITIES. As a 'LAST VALVE' it must also, now and then, make use of the right of appeal. Expert opinion first, negotiated improvement second, appeal last — from an organisation that holds the appeal right and still puts it third. Its office: Schwarzenburgstrasse 11, 3007 Bern, 031 377 00 77. WHO FOUNDED IT, which tells a community who else to call: it was established in 1970 by Pro Natura, the Schweizer Heimatschutz, the spatial planning association EspaceSuisse, the Swiss Alpine Club and the Swiss Tourism Association. A tourism association among the founders of a landscape protection foundation is an alliance most campaigns never think of. AND THE COURT RULING THAT MATTERS FOR NEW BUILDING ZONES: the Federal Court held that the foundation, like other nature and heritage protection organisations, CAN USE THE ASSOCIATION APPEAL AGAINST NEW REZONINGS (Neueinzonungen), and has made clear to the cantons that they must apply a strict standard in enforcing the revised spatial planning act.

trackers.name: Stiftung Natur & Wirtschaft — 400 near-natural areas on company land, quarries and golf courses
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES, and it is the entry point this file has been missing on the corporate side: the foundation works for more biodiversity in the SETTLEMENT AREA, and has 400 near-natural areas ON COMPANY SITES, IN GRAVEL PITS, around residential buildings and ON GOLF COURSES, awarding a certificate and aiming to make it better known among the decision-makers who matter. A gravel pit or a company yard next to your site is a candidate for certified near-natural management — and the certificate gives the operator a reason to say yes. Mühlenplatz 4, 6004 Luzern, 041 249 40 00. AND THE DIRECTORY IT SITS IN, which is the free artefact: a published overview of the Swiss institutions active in nature and landscape protection, with addresses, phone numbers and emails — naming among others BirdLife Schweiz, whose priorities are NATURE PROTECTION IN THE MUNICIPALITY, protection of birds and their habitats, the landscape foundation above, and the working group on invasive neobiota set up by the conference of cantonal environmental officers and the CONFERENCE OF OFFICERS FOR NATURE AND LANDSCAPE PROTECTION, with the cantonal foresters', agriculture offices' and plant protection services' conferences. Where a country's conservation work is cantonal, the conference of cantonal officers is the body that coordinates it — and it is named here with its partners.

trackers.name: Fonds Landschaft Schweiz — federally financed but ADMINISTRATION-INDEPENDENT, and it advises too
trackers.desc: WHAT MAKES IT UNUSUAL: it is a funding instrument FINANCED BY THE CONFEDERATION but, in its implementation, INDEPENDENT OF THE ADMINISTRATION, supporting VOLUNTARY MEASURES that serve to preserve and restore near-natural cultivated landscapes. A commission chosen by the Federal Council grants financial contributions ON APPLICATION. Switzerland had 28 filed entries and three funders. Public money handed out by a body outside the administration is worth knowing about when the administration is the problem. WHO IT SERVES AND WHAT ELSE IT GIVES: it continues with ADVICE AND financial support for PRIVATE INDIVIDUALS, ORGANISATIONS, MUNICIPALITIES AND CANTONS — and it notes that the FLS is perceived as A SEAL OF QUALITY WITH SIGNAL EFFECT. A grant that also works as an endorsement is worth applying for even at small sums. WHAT IT PAYS FOR: measures to preserve the biological and structural diversity of the landscape — adapted management and care of near-natural cultivated landscapes, and the GENTLE RENEWAL AND RESTORATION OF LANDSCAPE-DEFINING ELEMENTS, with tree planting in the open landscape given as an example. And a hard rule worth noting: the submission dates are BINDING; an extension is not possible.

trackers.name: Plattform Renaturierung — a Swiss overview of the foundations and funds, fund by fund
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a published overview of foundations and funds for restoration projects, each described by what it supports and who may apply — the free artefact this file has found most useful across eighteen countries. AND THE CANTONAL FUND IT NAMES, which is the reachable one: a canton's RENATURIERUNGSFONDS has, as a special financing, around 4 MILLION FRANCS ANNUALLY. It supports and RELIEVES MUNICIPALITIES AND PRIVATE PERSONS who carry out mature restoration projects, and applications for contributions can be made BY NATURAL AND LEGAL PERSONS domiciled in the canton — with the procedure running in several stages and possibly taking several months. A standing cantonal fund of four million a year, open to a private person, is closer than any national scheme — and the honest warning about timescale is published with it. AND A PRIVATE FOUNDATION SHOWING THE SHAPE TO LOOK FOR: one supports nature protection projects with ONE-OFF OR REGULAR CONTRIBUTIONS, covering existing or general environmental protection projects in one named municipality, in its canton, OR IN SWITZERLAND, provided they are of public benefit, and can also support bodies working for clean water, for the forest and nature, and for human health. Regular contributions, not just one-off grants, are what a small association should ask about.

trackers.name: Faunaberna's Landkaufprojekte — a small association that bought THREE HECTARES and keeps going
trackers.desc: WHAT A SMALL SWISS ASSOCIATION ACTUALLY DID: in a WORKING GROUP we are acquiring land IN ORDER TO UPGRADE IT ECOLOGICALLY AND PLACE IT UNDER PROTECTION. This then belongs NOT TO JUST ANYONE, BUT TO THE ASSOCIATION itself. Switzerland had two land-acquisition entries filed; this is the one a village-sized group can copy. AND THE SAFEGUARD IN ITS OWN STATUTES, which is the detail that makes the purchase permanent: in the unlikely event of the association being dissolved, THE LAND PASSES, ACCORDING TO THE STATUTES, TO a named national conservation body. A dissolution clause naming who inherits the land is what stops a small association's purchase unravelling when the association does — and it costs nothing to write into the statutes at the start. AND THE TARGET AND THE RESULT: by 2030 we wanted to buy 3 HECTARES OF LAND IN DIFFERENT HABITATS, as our contribution to the international '30 BY 30' BIODIVERSITY TARGET. WE ACHIEVED THIS IN 2026, BUT WE ARE CARRYING ON. Donations are invited to finance the purchase of new parcels DIRECTLY. Three hectares is a target a local group can actually hit, and hitting it early is an argument for the next appeal.

trackers.name: Buying building land for nature — and the country's LARGEST PRIVATE LANDOWNER
trackers.desc: THE SCALE OF WHAT PRIVATE CONSERVATION HOLDS IN SWITZERLAND: the largest conservation body is THE BIGGEST PRIVATE LANDOWNER IN SWITZERLAND, with 61 km² of land AT PRESENT, COMPLETELY UNDER PROTECTION — plus further areas likewise protected and looked after by it, amounting in total to a good 1,000 km². Every year it secures additional areas or BUYS NEW PARCELS, for better protection or to round out and upgrade nature reserves. AND THE TACTIC THIS RECORDS, which is unusual and directly anti-development: a cantonal section BID FOR A PART-PARCEL OF BUILDING LAND with the intention of creating a nature reserve. It did not get the land, but was brought into all the working steps early AND HAD A RIGHT OF CONSULTATION — so intervening in the land sale was worth it anyway. Bidding and losing still bought a seat in the process, which is worth knowing before a group decides an auction is beyond it. Elsewhere, when one body could not afford the whole area, a second section joined the purchase — NOT LEAST BECAUSE IT ALREADY OWNED LAND ON THE SAME SLOPE — and THREE PARTIES BECAME OWNERS of the valuable meadow. Buying jointly with whoever already owns next door is how a parcel gets afforded.

trackers.name: The TWENTY-THREE organisations entitled to appeal — the Swiss roster, named
trackers.desc: THE LIST A SWISS COMMUNITY SHOULD WORK THROUGH, because in this country the right to challenge a project belongs to named organisations: the platform names AQUA VIVA, ARCHAEOLOGY SWITZERLAND, DOCTORS FOR ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION, THE ALPINE INITIATIVE, EQUITERRE, GREENPEACE, THE GREINA FOUNDATION, HELVETIA NOSTRA / FONDATION FRANZ WEBER, MOUNTAIN WILDERNESS, NATURE FRIENDS SWITZERLAND, PRACTICAL ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION SWITZERLAND, PRO NATURA, THE RHEINAUBUND, THE SWISS ALPINE CLUB, THE SWISS ENERGY FOUNDATION, THE SWISS FISHERIES ASSOCIATION, THE SWISS SOCIETY FOR SPELEOLOGY, SWISS HERITAGE, SWISS HIKING TRAILS, THE FOUNDATION FOR LANDSCAPE PROTECTION, BIRDLIFE SWITZERLAND, THE TRANSPORT AND ENVIRONMENT ASSOCIATION, and WWF. Switzerland is among the least-worked buckets in this file. Twenty-three named bodies hold the right to bring a case, and a hiking club, a fishing association, a caving society and a doctors' group are among them — so a community whose site is a river, a cave, a footpath or a health matter has a specialist entitled to act, not only the general conservation bodies. AND WHAT THE RIGHT DOES: WITH THE ASSOCIATION APPEAL RIGHT, NATURE RECEIVES A VOICE. PROJECTS PARTICULARLY DELICATE FOR NATURE CAN THUS BE EXAMINED FOR THEIR COMPATIBILITY WITH THE NATURE AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION LEGISLATION. HONEST LIMIT: the site states it IS NOT CURRENTLY BEING UPDATED BUT SERVES AS AN ARCHIVE AND INFORMATION PLATFORM, so the roster should be checked against a current source before a group relies on any single name.

trackers.name: The appeal right being narrowed — small projects inside the building zone carved out
trackers.desc: A RESOURCE BEING TAKEN AWAY, which a community needs to know before it plans around it: ASSOCIATIONS SUCH AS PRO NATURA, GREENPEACE, THE FONDATION FRANZ WEBER OR ALSO THE FOUNDATION FOR LANDSCAPE PROTECTION WILL NO LONGER BE ABLE TO PROCEED AGAINST SMALLER INDIVIDUAL PROJECTS WITHIN THE BUILDING ZONE. Switzerland is among the least-worked buckets in this file. AND THE THRESHOLD, which is the number to check a site against: anyone intending to build a house WHOSE FLOOR AREA IS SMALLER THAN 400 SQUARE METRES need not concern themselves with A POSSIBLE OBJECTION FROM ENVIRONMENTAL OR HERITAGE-PROTECTION ORGANISATIONS. Below four hundred square metres inside the building zone, the organisational appeal right no longer reaches — so a Swiss community facing incremental small-scale infill cannot rely on the national bodies and must object in its own name. AND THE POLITICAL FRAMING, worth knowing because it is the argument a community will meet: the sponsor called his motion DAVID AGAINST GOLIATH, casting the small builder as David and the conservation associations as Goliath. The appeal right is being narrowed by presenting the objectors as the powerful party, and the parliamentary chamber adopted the initiative BY A CLEAR MAJORITY.

trackers.name: Autorité de protection des données (APD/GBA)
trackers.desc: Autorité de protection des données (APD/GBA) — Belgium’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Juportal
trackers.desc: Official Belgian portal for published case law of the courts and tribunals. · Find here: the official portal of Belgian court judgments (Juportal).

trackers.name: Commission for Access to Administrative Documents (CADA/CTB, Belgium)
trackers.desc: Commission for Access to Administrative Documents (CADA/CTB, Belgium) — independent body overseeing the right of access to public information.

trackers.name: Transparencia — FOI requests (BEL)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); Transparencia — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: Natuurpunt — aankoop van natuurgebieden (Flanders)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: buys land outright and holds it as nature reserve across Flanders, at real scale — 798.5 hectares bought in 2024 alone for €32.6M, bringing the area under its management to just under 30,000 hectares. Roughly 70 percent of a purchase comes from Flemish acquisition subsidy and 30 percent from its own funds. It also takes land by gift: a parcel next to an existing reserve becomes reserve, and one elsewhere can seed a new reserve or be exchanged for strategically located ground. USE IT: but read the limit it states plainly itself — the subsidy tapers away as the price rises, so it CANNOT outbid farmers, developers or estate agents, and can only really act on parcels less attractive for other uses. If a developer wants your site badly, this is not the tool. Its local afdelingen buy in their own right and it trains volunteers in how to do it, so approach the afdeling, not only the head office.

trackers.name: Natuur en Bos — subsidie aankoop gronden (Flanders)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the Flemish government's nature agency runs the public subsidy scheme behind most private nature-reserve purchases in the region — money to buy land with a view to its recognition as a nature reserve. This is the primary source sitting underneath what the conservation associations do, so it is worth reading directly rather than through them. USE IT: to check the current scheme and conditions for yourself before assuming an association can act, and to see what a municipality or other public body could apply for. Flanders only — Wallonia and Brussels run their own arrangements.

trackers.name: Natagora — achat de réserves naturelles (Wallonie & Bruxelles)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: buys land and holds it as nature reserve across Wallonia and Brussels — over 6,200 hectares on more than 200 protected sites — and says openly that it often has to move fast to buy ground that is threatened or left to speculators. The economics are favourable: Wallonia funds half the purchase price of land destined to become a réserve naturelle agréée, and gifts to Natagora carry a Belgian tax deduction, so a donation buys more reserve than its face value. It buys jointly with the Département de la Nature et des Forêts on some programmes. USE IT: the direct route is the one it advertises — if you are SELLING land that could host biodiversity and become a reserve, contact them before you list it. For a community, that means finding the owner and getting Natagora in front of them early, because once a site is on the open market the timetable belongs to someone else.

trackers.name: Council for Permit Disputes
trackers.desc: Council for Permit Disputes — administrative court (Belgium).

trackers.name: Belgium UBO Register
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Access restricted to authorities/obliged entities.

trackers.name: Belgian Court of Arbitration for Sport
trackers.desc: Belgian Court of Arbitration for Sport — tribunal in Belgium.

trackers.name: Belgium company database (company register)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); Belgium company database (company register) — the official register of companies and legal entities in Belgium — the primary public record of corporate existence, ownership, directors and filings. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A BENEFICIAL-OWNERSHIP REGISTER: this shows the registered entity, its directors and filings; where a separate beneficial-ownership register exists, use that to reach the real humans behind a shell company.

trackers.name: Belgian Court of Cassation
trackers.desc: Belgian Court of Cassation — supreme court (Belgium).

trackers.name: Crossroads Bank for Enterprises (KBO/BCE)
trackers.desc: Belgium's official public company register. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Statistics Belgium (Statbel)
trackers.desc: Belgium's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Belgium.

trackers.name: Constitutional Court of Belgium
trackers.desc: Constitutional Court of Belgium — supreme court (Belgium).

trackers.name: Court of Audit
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Belgium, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Belgian Financial Intelligence Processing Unit (CTIF-CFI)
trackers.desc: Belgium's independent administrative FIU, analysing suspicious facts and transactions linked to money laundering and terrorist financing. Here you can trace how suspicious transactions are reported and money-laundering intelligence is produced in Belgium.

trackers.name: Cumuleo
trackers.desc: Independent Belgian mandate transparency platform cataloging over 1 million mandates, functions, and professions held by politicians. Tracks conflicts of interest and promotes public access to government documents. Cited in EU Commission Rule of Law reports and nominated for TI Belgium Integrity Award. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies, top officials & cabinet, officials handling public money & power — find their conflicts of interest with the state; their assets, interests and integrity declarations; corruption cases, sanctions and integrity data.

trackers.name: Registre des lobbies / Lobbyregister
trackers.desc: Belgium's Chamber of Representatives lobby register (since 2019) — a public database of interest representatives seeking to influence the legislative process, bound by a code of conduct.

trackers.name: Belgium e-Procurement
trackers.desc: Belgium's federal public e-procurement platform. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Belgium, and for how much.

trackers.name: Antwerp Labor Court
trackers.desc: Antwerp Labor Court — tribunal (Belgium).

trackers.name: Vlaams Sporttribunaal
trackers.desc: Vlaams Sporttribunaal — tribunal (Belgium).

trackers.name: Council for Alien Disputes
trackers.desc: Council for Alien Disputes — administrative court in Belgium (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Does your appeal stop the works? — suspensive effect in Wallonia and Brussels
trackers.desc: YOUR OWN APPEAL WILL NOT STOP THE MACHINERY — BUT SOMEONE ELSE'S WILL. In the Walloon Region, an administrative appeal against a permis d'environnement or permis unique has no suspensive effect, except when lodged by the technical officer. In Brussels-Capital, appeals against first-instance environmental permit decisions before the Environmental College likewise have no suspensive effect — unless the appeal is brought by the local authority, by Bruxelles Environnement / Leefmilieu Brussel, or by the competent land use planning officer (fonctionnaire délégué / gemachtigde ambtenaar), and is duly motivated by serious danger or irreparable harm. Then the president of the Environmental College, or a member assigned by them, suspends the decision within 5 working days after hearing the parties. THE TACTIC THAT FOLLOWS: the fastest way to halt a Brussels site is not to appeal yourself but to persuade your commune or the regional environment administration to appeal, with serious danger or irreparable harm documented — that is the difference between a paper objection and a stopped site.

trackers.name: Bruxelles Environnement subsidies — do not start before notification
trackers.desc: THE RULE THAT VOIDS A GRANT BEFORE IT STARTS: since 01/01/2025, under the ordinance of 04/04/2024 bearing the Public Finances Code of the Brussels-Capital Region, no activity may be subsidised before formal notification of the grant — the only exception being subsidies beginning on 1 January. Begin the work early and it cannot be funded. PLAN THE LEAD TIME: allow 4 to 6 months between applying and official notification; all discretionary subsidies go to the Inspection des Finances for opinion and those over EUR 4,000 must be validated by the government. CHECK WHICH CALL IS YOURS: the call aimed at communes and CPAS expressly does not address communal schools, asbl linked to local authorities, groups of citizens, or businesses — separate calls exist for those audiences, and local authorities must co-fund at least 10 percent. USE THE HELP OFFERED: pre-accompaniment in drafting the final dossier is strongly recommended and mandatory for some thematic objectives, and an intention note judged too far from the call's objectives can be redirected rather than refused.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Natuurpunt and Natagora — they buy land, and the local branch starts the purchase
trackers.desc: BUYING LAND IS LISTED FIRST IN WHAT THEY DO — these are not campaigners who occasionally acquire. BirdLife describes both Belgian partners' aim as protecting what remains ‘through buying and managing land’, then species protection, then lobbying. PICK THE RIGHT ONE: in Flanders and Brussels it is Natuurpunt (130,000+ members, 500 nature areas, and by its own account around 2 percent of Flemish territory); in Wallonia and Brussels it is Natagora (26,000 members), which works daily on acquiring new spaces to turn into nature reserves and in 2022 alone converted more than 200 hectares, reaching 5,800 hectares protected. Both are active in Brussels, so in the capital either may be the right call. THE MOST USEFUL THING TO KNOW ABOUT NATUURPUNT: it is a volunteer and membership association with about 170 local divisions, active in every Flemish municipality, and ‘the volunteers take the initiative for the purchase, management and opening up of nature areas’, backed by professional teams. The initiative for a purchase comes from the local branch, not head office — so if you want land bought in your municipality, the division in your municipality is who starts it. That is a far shorter path than petitioning a national body. IT ALSO SUPPLIES EVIDENCE: more than 120 study working groups and the waarnemingen.be observations database, which Natuurpunt says provides the scientific basis for government nature policy — so a record of species at your site, in the database the government itself relies on, is evidence you can build BEFORE a development is proposed. Note a published discrepancy: hectare totals for Natuurpunt are given as both 23,000 and 28,000 in different sources; check the current figure. AND THERE IS A FUNDED BUYER ACTIVELY LOOKING RIGHT NOW: LIFE ArdennEislek (January 2025 to 2031), led by Natagora with the Fondation Hëllef fir d'Natur and natur&ëmwelt, will restore over 450 hectares in the Belgian and Luxembourg Ardenne — including 110 hectares of NEW ACQUISITIONS. If your site is in that area and is meadow, heath or biodiversity-rich forest, there is an EU-funded budget running now with land still to buy. A second project, LIFE ToadAlly, coordinated by Natuurpunt Beheer, covers Limburg and Liège.

trackers.name: LDR Advocaten in Omgevingsrecht, Ghent — specialist planning and environmental counsel
trackers.desc: WHO TO CALL: a Flemish law firm founded in 1997 by Isabelle Larmuseau and Peter De Smedt and built entirely around omgevingsrecht — planning and environmental law — with twenty-seven lawyers each working in one or more specific fields within it. Kasteellaan 141, 9000 Ghent, +32 9 234 29 16, info@ldr.be. WHAT IT COVERS THAT MATTERS HERE: it runs the administrative appeal procedures before the authority itself and the judicial routes at the Raad van State and the Grondwettelijk Hof, and it also takes environmental matters through the civil and criminal courts and courts of appeal. That combination is the point: an objection, an annulment action and a nuisance or criminal complaint over the same site are three different doors, and most general practices only know one. The firm also set up LDR Opleidingen and initiated the Vlaamse Vereniging voor Omgevingsrecht, so its people are the ones teaching this material in Flanders. THE QUESTION TO ASK IN THE FIRST EMAIL: this is the largest specialist practice in the field in Flanders, and I could NOT establish from its own material that it acts for objecting residents rather than for applicants and authorities. It may well act for both. So name the developer, the project and the consenting authority up front and ask directly whether the firm is free to act for you. Do that before you send your history.

trackers.name: Fondation Roi Baudouin / Koning Boudewijnstichting — funds land purchase, and takes informal groups
trackers.desc: WHY THIS ONE MATTERS FOR LAND: it does not only fund activities, it funds acquisition. It has run support specifically for acquiring nature reserves in the Hautes-Fagnes, aimed at extending existing reserves or creating new ones; it hosts a fund that buys land outright to protect birds and wildlife; and its 2026 acquisition round backed Terre-en-Vue's purchases of several farms and help buying land for organic farming projects. A Belgian community with a willing seller and no money has somewhere to apply. AND IT WILL TAKE AN UNINCORPORATED GROUP: its Vis mon village! call is open to village residents who have come together either formally as an asbl or informally — an association de fait, a group of inhabitants, a neighbourhood committee. Across this whole file that is rare: most funders require a constituted legal body first. Note the mirror-image exclusion, that projects carried by municipal administrations and their services are not considered in that call. THE OTHER TOOL, WHICH IS NOT A GRANT: a compte de projet, a project account it manages on an association's behalf so the association can raise money with the Foundation's recognition behind it. The conditions are specific and worth reading before you start: name the Foundation's support and the object of the project in your communications, submit fundraising material for its express approval, do not use bought, rented or exchanged data, do not let other organisations collect on your behalf, treat the fundraising ethics code as a minimum, and announce the start of the collection in local media. PRACTICALITIES: three calls for projects a year, spanning environment, climate, biodiversity and heritage among other fields. One current example of scale — its Vent de Nature fund offers up to €50,000 a year, or €100,000 over two years under conditions, for work on the interaction between wind development and biodiversity. Applications must come from the association or organisation that will be supported, not from a third party on its behalf.

trackers.name: Terre-en-vue — citizen savings buy the farmland, the farmer rents it (Belgium)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a movement founded in 2011 and now made up of three bodies — a cooperative, an asbl and a foundation — whose purpose is to buy agricultural land in Belgium and put it beyond speculation, then make it available to agroecological, organic and local farms. The cooperative is the buying instrument: ordinary people put part of their savings into shares, and the cooperative buys land with the proceeds and leases it to farmers. Around 5,000 people have taken shares and more than €9.5 million has been assembled that way. It began with 7.5 hectares at Rochefort, bought when a farmer's rented land was sold off as building plots and he could not buy it himself. WHY A COMMUNITY SHOULD KNOW ABOUT IT: this is the answer when the threat to a field is that it will be sold and built on, and the farmer who works it cannot outbid a developer. For its recent Ferme des Arondes project the whole of the farm's land and buildings was financed through share subscription, and 16% of the million euros needed came in within a week. A campaign here is a share issue, not an appeal, and people get an asset rather than a receipt. Governance is one person one vote regardless of holding, and it says it wants local groups to have as much autonomy and responsibility as possible. UNDERSTAND WHAT YOU ARE ASKING PEOPLE TO BUY: it states that the cooperative has no employees and delegates its management to the asbl, that its income is very limited and lower than its land-purchase spending, and that there is no dividend. This is capital placed for a social and environmental return, not an investment that pays. Say that plainly when you ask neighbours to subscribe, or it will be said for you. SCOPE: Wallonia and Brussels, with De Landgenoten as its counterpart in Flanders. Farmland with an agroecological project attached — not woodland, and not land without a farmer waiting for it. The asbl also advises farmers, citizens and public or private landowners on access to land, so an approach can start with a question rather than a purchase.

trackers.name: De Landgenoten — collective land purchase for Flemish organic farmers
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a foundation and a cooperative — the name is Dutch for fellow countrymen — which buys agricultural land collectively and makes it available to professional agroecological farmers in Flanders. It is the Dutch-speaking counterpart of Terre-en-vue, which covers Wallonia and Brussels; between them Belgium has a farmland buyer on each side of the language border, and a community should approach the one for its region rather than the one it has heard of. WHY IT EXISTS, IN NUMBERS THAT MAKE THE ARGUMENT FOR YOU: Flemish farmland prices rose 28.7% between 2015 and 2019, to an average of about €63,000 a hectare. Access to land is the main threshold for farmers trying to start, secure, expand or hand on a farm, because the capital needed keeps rising and many owners are reluctant to grant new leases. If your fight is over a Flemish field, those figures are the reason the farmer working it cannot simply buy it, and they are worth quoting. It has also published its own report on the obstacles in the Flemish land system, which is the document to ask for before a meeting with a commune. SOURCING: verified on the Access to Land network's own member profile rather than the organisation's own website. The network is the body these organisations founded and belong to, so the profiles are close to first-hand, but confirm current figures directly.

trackers.name: Natuurpunt and Natagora — 400+ reserves, 17,147 hectares, acquired by local branches
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: Belgium's two BirdLife partners, split along the language border — Natuurpunt for Flanders and Brussels with over 54,000 members, Natagora for Wallonia and Brussels with nearly 11,000, the latter formed in 2003 from the merger of Réserves Naturelles RNOB and the ornithological society Aves. Between them they own or manage more than 400 nature reserves covering 17,147 hectares. THE SENTENCE THAT TELLS YOU HOW TO APPROACH THEM: their own partner page states that the work of volunteers and the support of the regional government are essential for acquiring, managing and monitoring the reserves. Acquisition here is not a head-office decision funded from a central pot — it runs through more than 150 local branches and antennas, and it depends on people willing to do the management afterwards. A Belgian community that arrives with a site and a group of people prepared to maintain it is offering the two things the model actually needs, which is the same lesson as the Austrian entry in this file. WHAT ELSE THEY RUN: an active education department and a museum at Turnhout; Natagora runs the Aquascope Virelles visitor centre with WWF-Belgium beside a 140-hectare reserve. Both spend more than 30% of their annual budget on communication with members, volunteers and the public — which is worth knowing if what your campaign needs is reach rather than money. NOTE ON OVERLAP: this file already holds Natuurpunt for its land acquisition work. Treat this as the pair entry covering Natagora and the branch structure, or merge the two.

trackers.name: PNRR projet 97 — 22 million euro buying land in Wallonia, through nine named associations
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: under the national Recovery and Resilience Plan, Wallonia runs project 97 to strengthen the protected area network, with a budget of 22 million euro, implemented by SPW Agriculture, Ressources naturelles et Environnement. Its stated aim is the survival of rare and threatened species by protecting and restoring their habitats, and it works through the acquisition, restoration and ecological valorisation of land of high biological value. AND HERE ARE THE NINE BODIES THAT DELIVER IT — the most useful thing on the page: les Cercles des Naturalistes de Belgique, Natagora, la Ligue Royale Belge pour la Protection des Oiseaux, Ardenne & Gaume, Patrimoine Nature, Les Amis de la Fagne, Les Amis du Parc de la Dyle, Le Génévrier and Virelles Nature. Nine nature conservation associations, named, currently holding public money to buy and restore ground in Wallonia.
