A community with a threatened site should approach whichever of them works its region. WHAT THE MONEY DOES BEYOND BUYING: ecological restoration on recently acquired land or in existing nature reserves — mowing, sod-cutting, digging ponds, blocking drains, fencing for extensive grazing — plus public valorisation with interpretive panels, walking circuits, boardwalks and observatories. WHERE THE REST OF THE WALLOON MONEY SITS: the Direction de la Nature et des Espaces verts handles the creation, acquisition and management of nature reserves, Natura 2000, implementation of the European nature restoration regulation, and the administrative follow-up of subsidies; it also subsidises the acquisition and layout of public green spaces, supervises Plan de Relance calls on the ecological network, protected areas and national parks, and follows the LIFE programmes. AND A PUBLIC DATABASE WORTH OPENING: Wallonia publishes a centralised database of biodiversity projects and subsidies where each project sheet gives the funding framework, the partners, the objectives, the year and downloadable results including scientific studies and technical reports. SCALE NOTE FOR ARGUMENT: nature reserves in Wallonia are increasing but barely 1 per cent of the territory.

trackers.name: Advocaat zoeken Vlaanderen — 24 firms and 100+ lawyers listed by omgevingsrecht speciality
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a directory listing 24 law firms and more than 100 lawyers working in omgevingsrecht, milieurecht and ruimtelijk ordeningsrecht across Flanders and Brussels, searchable by region, with a parallel listing for omgevings- en verkavelingsvergunningen — environmental and subdivision permits, permit disputes and filing objections. Belgium's bucket had LDR Advocaten and nothing else on the legal side; this is a hundred more names, sorted by the exact subject. WHY A DIRECTORY AND NOT ONE FIRM: Flemish permit fights are decided regionally — at the Deputatie, then the Raad voor Vergunningsbetwistingen, then the Raad van State — and the practitioner you want is one who appears there and knows your province. A national pick would be worse than a filtered list. WHAT THE FIRMS ON IT ACTUALLY OFFER A NEIGHBOUR, from their own pages: drafting bezwaarschriften during openbare onderzoeken; assistance when a project appears in your immediate surroundings that you are not happy with; administrative appeals and defence before the Raad voor Vergunningsbetwistingen and the Raad van State; and submitting reasoned objections when new Ruimtelijke Uitvoeringsplannen are being made, for clients potentially disadvantaged by them. TWO CAPABILITIES WORTH ASKING FOR BY NAME: a beroep tot schorsing bij uiterst dringende noodzakelijkheid — suspension on grounds of extreme urgency — before the Raad voor Vergunningsbetwistingen or the Raad van State, which is what stops works already starting; and one firm's own technical capacity to take samples and draw up screening reports, with close contacts to study bureaus and remediation companies.

trackers.name: OmniRecht — an intake desk, seven days a week, into 58+ independent Belgian lawyers
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a platform of more than 58 self-employed and independent Belgian advocates, with an Intakebalie — intake desk — offering eerstelijnsadvies, first-line advice, reachable seven days a week by contact form, with an office-hours phone line. A first conversation without choosing a firm first is a different proposition from cold-calling chambers, and it is the second entry-point of this kind in the file after Croatia's green phone. WHAT ITS LAWYERS COVER, in their own description: they stand with you from the preparatory conversations with the municipality through to challenging a permit refusal. AND THE CLASSIFICATION POINT THAT DECIDES WHO DECIDES YOUR CASE: since 1 January 2018 the omgevingsvergunning replaced the separate building, environmental and subdivision permits. Under VLAREM, the Flemish environmental permit regulation, activities are graded — the heaviest require a permit from the PROVINCE, less heavy ones from your MUNICIPALITY, and the lightest need no permit but carry a duty to notify. The platform's own warning: it is crucial that your activities are classified correctly, and a wrong assessment can lead to problems or even sanctions. For a community that means checking whether a project has been classified into the lightest class to avoid a permit and a public inquiry altogether.

trackers.name: Gautier Melchior — the Walloon and Brussels side, which the Flemish listings do not cover
trackers.desc: WHY THIS CLOSES A REAL GAP: all three of Belgium's filed legal resources are Flemish — LDR in Ghent, the Vlaanderen directory, and a platform reachable in Dutch. A community in Wallonia or Brussels would find none of them useful. This advocate practises in both the Brussels Region and the Walloon Region, specialised in droit de l'urbanisme et de l'environnement. WHAT HE DOES, AND THE FIRST ITEM IS THE ONE MOST FIRMS OMIT: legal accompaniment in the framework of a PUBLIC INQUIRY and of a project announcement — that is, help while the enquête publique is running, before any decision exists to appeal. Getting the objection right at the inquiry stage is what this file has repeatedly found to matter, and few practices sell it. THEN THE REST: administrative appeals concerning permis d'urbanisme and permis d'environnement; legal assistance in pursuing the regularisation of a property; taking on appeals against permit refusal decisions; and bringing annulment actions before the Conseil d'État with, where appropriate, A REQUEST FOR SUSPENSION — the remedy that stops works rather than merely condemning them. He also defends attacked permits before the Conseil d'État, so check for conflicts. AND HE PUBLISHES ON THE RULES AS THEY CHANGE, including new Brussels Government decrees on changes of use subject to permis d'urbanisme, and administrative fines under the Brussels Housing Code.

trackers.name: Bond Beter Leefmilieu — 130+ member organisations, and a named contact to join them
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a network organisation that unites nature and environmental organisations and strengthens the voice of sustainable frontrunners in Flanders, working with citizens, social organisations, businesses and authorities. Belgium's bucket held eight acquirers and four lawyers — this is the body that connects a local group to the rest. THE NUMBERS AND THE DOOR: more than 130 organisations from the network are affiliated as members. Together we reach more than A MILLION FLEMINGS, thousands of businesses and the most important decision-makers in Flanders — and for membership information it publishes a named network worker and her email address. A named human being to write to about joining beats any general contact form, and membership is governed openly: each member association may send ONE DELEGATE to the general assembly, which is the highest authority and determines policy, meeting each spring on the annual plan, budget, financial report and the admission of new members. AND THE MUNICIPAL ARM: Gemeente voor de Toekomst is the network of BBL member organisations that works TOGETHER WITH CITIES AND MUNICIPALITIES on the shift to a sustainable society, again with a named network worker as your point of contact. Where the same network reaches both the councils and the local groups, one introduction serves both.

trackers.name: The Belgian appeal-rights fight — seven organisations that went to the Constitutional Court for citizens
trackers.desc: WHO WENT, AND WHY IT MATTERS TO A RESIDENT: Natuurpunt, BBL, Greenpeace and four further named organisations went to the Constitutional Court because a decree change restricted citizens' appeal rights. Seven organisations willing to litigate on behalf of the public's right to object is a standing alliance a Belgian community can appeal to. WHAT CHANGED, and it is the practical warning every Flemish resident needs: previously every citizen or local association could appeal to the higher authority against a building project's permit application. Henceforth ONLY CITIZENS WHO SUBMITTED AN OBJECTION DURING THE FIRST PUBLIC INQUIRY will still be able to appeal. MISSED THE YELLOW NOTICE BOARD OF THE PUBLIC INQUIRY? THEN SILENCE COUNTS AS CONSENT — the time to react to a new building project is suddenly reduced to the 30 DAYS of the public inquiry. AND THE UNFAIRNESS THEY NAME, worth quoting anywhere the same rule appears: during those 30 days there is often FAR LESS INFORMATION AVAILABLE than during the appeal period that applied until now — the later stage being when you would see administrations' advice on the environmental impact, the municipality's arguments, or information about POSSIBLE CONFLICTS OF INTEREST, all summarised in the permit decision in objective and comprehensible language.

trackers.name: Gezocht: grond te koop — a branch asking the public for TIPS on land coming up for sale
trackers.desc: THE ASK, AND IT IS THE MOST DIRECTLY COPYABLE PAGE IN THE BELGIAN BUCKET: WE DO NOT KNOW EVERYTHING. FAR TOO OFTEN VERY VALUABLE PARCELS ARE SOLD WITHOUT OUR KNOWING ABOUT IT. GIVE US THAT ONE GOLDEN TIP. And do not too quickly think 'surely they will already know' — followed by a named secretary, his email address and HIS MOBILE NUMBER. A land-buying organisation publicly admitting it misses sales, and asking neighbours to phone in tips, turns every resident into part of the acquisition system. WHAT THE BRANCH DOES WITH A TIP: we buy valuable nature parcels to secure the nature and heritage values FOR POSTERITY. We are open to GIFTS AND WILLS — which may even allow your estate to be fiscally optimised, so that your heirs keep more of it. AND THE THIRD THING IT WANTS, which is unusual and useful: WE ARE ALSO LOOKING FOR EXCHANGE LAND, to swap with, or 'relocate', FARMERS AND OWNERS OF VALUABLE NATURE. Offering a farmer equivalent land elsewhere, rather than asking them to sell up, is how a conservation buyer gets ground a farmer will not otherwise part with.

trackers.name: Who paid for a 142-hectare purchase — the region 3.5m, the association 450,000
trackers.desc: THE FUNDING SPLIT ON A REAL PURCHASE, published to the euro: an association BOUGHT AN AREA OF 142 HECTARES FROM A NOBLE FAMILY, and ALMOST FOUR MILLION EURO WAS PUT ON THE TABLE FOR THE PURCHASE. OF THAT, THE REGION PAYS 3.5 MILLION EURO AND THE ASSOCIATION 450,000 EURO. Belgium is the least-worked bucket in this file. The association put up about one euro in nine, and public subsidy covered the rest — which is the ratio a community should ask about before assuming a purchase is beyond it. AND WHY THE FAMILY CAME TO THEM, which is the sentence worth engineering: THE GROUNDS WERE IN THE HANDS OF THE FAMILY. THE FAMILY WANTED TO KEEP THE DOMAIN AS A WHOLE AND CAME TO US. An owner who wants the estate kept intact will approach a conservation buyer rather than split it between developers — the same route as the Czech meadow in batch582. AND THE COHERENCE GAIN: the association already owned the adjoining reserve, so the combination EXPANDS IT TO ALMOST 250 HECTARES. Its income shows how this is possible: of 70.6 million euro, ALMOST 71 PER CENT CONSISTED OF PURCHASE AND OPERATING SUBSIDIES, with membership fees, gifts and sponsorship at 16%.

trackers.name: Owners RANG THE ASSOCIATION offering four hectares — and what a first reserve does for a branch
trackers.desc: THE APPROACH CAME FROM THE SELLERS, IN A CITY WHERE THAT NEVER HAPPENS: A YEAR AND A HALF AGO THE BRANCH GOT A TELEPHONE CALL FROM A WOMAN REPRESENTING SEVERAL OWNERS. SHE PROPOSED SELLING AN AREA OF FOUR HECTARES TO the association, and the report notes THAT A NATURE ASSOCIATION IN A CITY IS APPROACHED WITH A PIECE OF LAND ON OFFER IS EXCEPTIONAL. Even in a city where nature is losing ground to property projects, owners sometimes ring the conservation body first — so a branch that is visible and contactable is doing acquisition work before it has any money. AND WHAT OWNING GROUND DOES TO A LOCAL GROUP, which is the argument for a branch buying even a small parcel: for the city branch IT IS INTERESTING TO HAVE ITS OWN RESERVE, BECAUSE THAT PUSHES THE ORGANISATION FORWARD. IT IMMEDIATELY ATTRACTS VOLUNTEERS — IT IS CONCRETE AND TANGIBLE. PEOPLE INDICATE THAT THEY FEEL THEIR MEMBERSHIP FEE IS BEING USED USEFULLY. OTHERS SEIZE ON IT TO MAKE A GIFT. Requests from SCHOOLS OR COMPANIES to organise activities together become easier to say yes to. Owning one small reserve recruits the volunteers and donors that make the next purchase possible. The report also notes that in the capital, unlike the two regions with one large body each, conservation is MUCH MORE FRAGMENTED, WITH NUMEROUS SMALL ASSOCIATIONS by municipality.

trackers.name: Commission for Personal Data Protection (CPDP)
trackers.desc: Commission for Personal Data Protection (CPDP) — Bulgaria’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Cassation
trackers.desc: Official site of Bulgaria's Supreme Court of Cassation with published acts and decisions. · Find here: the judgments of Bulgaria's Supreme Court of Cassation.

trackers.name: Justice and Environment — European green-law network
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the European network of environmental-law NGOs, whose national member here is Bluelink. Its fifteen members act as the environmental-law service point in their own countries, taking cases and intervening in legislative processes, while the network defends communities and nature in court and lodges infringement complaints against member-state governments. Its standing themes are access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, environmental assessment and pollution control. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who does not yet know which lawyer to call — knock on Bluelink's door first, and use the network only if your problem crosses a border. The network itself does not take individual cases; its members do. YOUR NATIONAL MEMBER IS Bluelink (bluelink.net) — go to them, not to the network. J&E members serve as environmental law ‘service points’ in their countries, handling cases, participating in legislative processes and sometimes providing legal analyses and consultations for national governments. The network has 11 full and 4 associate members, and can launch infringement proceedings against faulty governments — a route a national body alone does not have. CURRENT SCOPE: access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, climate, environmental assessments, and the Environmental Liability Directive. It previously worked on waste, transport, health and Natura 2000, so an older document may overstate what it covers today.

trackers.name: Bluelink
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Bulgaria's member organisation in the Justice and Environment network of European environmental-law NGOs. WHO IT SUITS: anyone in Bulgaria needing an environmental-law starting point; note that the link the network publishes for it is malformed, so the working domain could not be confirmed and the scope of work it accepts is not stated. Domain unverified this session — reach them through the member list on justiceandenvironment.org. It builds civic complaint tooling as well as running the network: Signali.bg helps citizens direct complaints to the right institution, and separate platforms take reports of illegal deforestation and urban environmental problems. BlueLink is a member of Justice and Environment, the European network of environmental law organisations, so it is a route to legal help and not only to publicity. Founded 1998 by Bulgarian environmental NGOs, with the foundation following in 1999; office at 20 Serdika Street, floor 2, 1000 Sofia, +359 8888 16830, office@bluelink.net.

trackers.name: Bulgaria Registry Agency (company register)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); Bulgaria Registry Agency (company register) — the official register of companies and legal entities in Bulgaria — the primary public record of corporate existence, ownership, directors and filings. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A BENEFICIAL-OWNERSHIP REGISTER: this shows the registered entity, its directors and filings; where a separate beneficial-ownership register exists, use that to reach the real humans behind a shell company.

trackers.name: National Audit Office
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Bulgaria, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: CAIS EOP
trackers.desc: Bulgaria's centralised electronic public-procurement platform. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Bulgaria, and for how much.

trackers.name: Bulgaria Open Data Portal
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Bulgaria.

trackers.name: Commercial Register
trackers.desc: data about Bulgarian companies

trackers.name: Bulgaria Commercial Register
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Bivol.bg
trackers.desc: Bulgarian investigative outlet (OCCRP partner) exposing high-level corruption and fraud.

trackers.name: National Statistical Institute
trackers.desc: Bulgaria's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Bulgaria.

trackers.name: Registry Agency
trackers.desc: executive agency of Bulgaria under the Ministry of Justice maintaining public registers including the Commercial Register, Property Register, and BULSTAT Register

trackers.name: Supreme Administrative Court
trackers.desc: Supreme Administrative Court — supreme court in Bulgaria (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: ПУДООС — its declared priorities are waste and water, not nature
trackers.desc: KNOW WHAT IT SAYS IT FUNDS BEFORE YOU WRITE. Bulgaria's environmental management enterprise has a board that adopts the priorities for financing and the requirements for applying — and those priorities were adopted for the sectors waste management and water management. A habitat proposal is therefore arguing outside the declared priorities unless a specific call says otherwise, so frame accordingly or wait for the right call. The requirements and the list of documents needed are published in the Документи section of pudoos.bg — start there, not from a news item. IT DOES FUND NATURE WORK CASE BY CASE, and the winning argument is worth copying: a foundation received an annual subsidy of BGN 50,370 for a tortoise breeding and rehabilitation centre on the stated grounds that it actively assists implementation of the Biological Diversity Act and serves the needs of RIOSV offices across the whole country — not ‘our work is valuable’ but ‘we are the only body able to do something the state is legally obliged to do’. ПУДООС also runs the recurring campaign «За чиста околна среда» for municipalities and кметства, the smallest administrative units.

trackers.name: RIOSV — the permitting body that can also be your funding applicant
trackers.desc: APPROACH YOUR REGIONAL INSPECTORATE FOR BOTH THINGS. RIOSV offices provide the material, technical and staffing support to protected territories — and they act as beneficiary on restoration projects themselves, for example improving the structure and functions of priority habitats in a maintained reserve, and limiting the negative influence of invasive species by afforestation with local species, on projects running 36 months. So the body you go to about a threat is also the body that can apply for the money to fix it, which makes it worth bringing a documented problem plus a proposed remedy rather than a complaint alone. AND TRACK THE ЗАПОВЕД: protection status is changed by ministerial order — one territory was recategorised as a maintained reserve by an order of the Minister of Environment and Waters with a recorded number and date. Status can move by order, so watch for orders affecting your site. HONEST GAP: what could be verified for Bulgaria is the national enterprise, its priorities, case-by-case nature financing and the municipal campaign — not a standing open call with published eligibility for independent NGOs on nature protection. Bulgarian NGOs appear here as partners and subsidised service providers rather than as addressees of a general call.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Fund for Wild Flora and Fauna — buys farmland and keeps it farmed (Bulgaria)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Bulgarian conservation organisation, founded in 2000 and working at fwff.org, that buys agricultural land and then keeps it in production. Under its Bright Future for Black Vulture project it purchased 93 hectares and folded them into agro-sylvo-pastoral complexes to hold the feeding habitat of the black vulture colony in the eastern Balkan Mountains. It runs a sheep farm at Kotel of more than 600 head grazing the core area, and project herds of native cattle supporting the Byala Reka and Kresna sites. USE IT: this is the counter to the objection that protection takes land out of use — the grazing is the management rather than an exception to it, so a grazier or a farming neighbour becomes an argument for the purchase instead of against it. Understand its shape before you write: it is a species-reintroduction organisation that acquires ground where that work needs it, not a land trust with a standing acquisition budget open to any site. Bring it a parcel that connects to vulture or raptor habitat, and bring the grazing arrangement with it.

trackers.name: Fondaciya EkoObshtnost — Bulgarian Environmental Partnership Foundation
trackers.desc: WHAT THE CONSORTIUM IS: the Environmental Partnership Association, headquartered in Brno, is a consortium of six independent national foundations in central and eastern Europe that give grants to community projects protecting the environment. It grew out of a programme begun in 1990 by the C.S. Mott Foundation, the German Marshall Fund and the Rockefeller Brothers Fund, and the national foundations were established as independent bodies in the early 1990s. Alongside grants they run education programmes, provide professional services and build the capacity of civic initiatives — which is the part a new local group needs most. THE BULGARIAN MEMBER: Fondaciya EkoObshtnost, founded 2003 and the last to join the consortium, at bepf-bg.org. Bulgaria has a land buyer in this file and no funder. SOURCING: the consortium and its six national foundations are documented on the Environmental Partnership Association's own site; the national figures and founding dates come from consortium and partner material rather than each foundation's own pages. Confirm current grant rounds with the national foundation directly.

trackers.name: Sdruzhenie Balkanka — takes Bulgarian river and mine cases to Brussels and the treaty bodies
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Bulgarian non-profit working to protect the country's rivers, based at Челопешко шосе 26, Sofia, info@balkanka.bg. It publishes named regional contacts with direct email addresses for Burgas, Veliko Tarnovo, Kazanlak, Plovdiv, Sofia, Stara Zagora and Yambol — so a Bulgarian community can reach a person in its own region rather than a national inbox. It also runs a public dams map and an open forum. WHAT IT DOES THAT ALMOST NOTHING ELSE IN THIS FILE DOES: it takes cases to the international treaty bodies itself. It has filed a complaint with the Implementation Committee of the Espoo Convention over the Ada Tepe gold mine and the new Tintyava mine in the Eastern Rhodopes, and it files complaints to the European Commission. For a community whose national ministry has stopped listening, this is an organisation that has already used the routes above the ministry and knows how they are drafted. ITS CASELOAD: fighting nine planned large hydropower projects and dams plus several small hydropower plants in Bulgaria; monitoring plants already operating; and supporting local people against small hydropower in Serbia and North Macedonia, against mining developments, against planned river channelisation, and against illegal gravel extraction and riverbank deforestation. It has monitored EBRD and EIB financed hydropower in Macedonia in the field, visiting six mountain rivers and nine small dams. Its work has prompted scientific studies of hydropower impacts on river ecosystems. IT ALSO DOES THE UNGLAMOROUS WORK: river clean-ups over hundreds of kilometres, restocking fish, green schools, and current monitoring of Balkan trout habitat in the Aegean catchment, funded through a long-running corporate partnership. A community that wants to build a relationship before it needs one can start there. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer, not a funder, not a law firm — though it acts as procedural representative in its own complaints. Bulgaria's other entries here are a farmland buyer and a grant-making foundation; this is the rivers and mining leg.

trackers.name: Zeleni Balkani — bought 50 ha, manages over 100, and investigates illegal logging reports
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: the Federation of nature conservation associations Green Balkans — national, non-profit, non-governmental, non-political, founded 1988 and the oldest nature conservation NGO in Bulgaria, registered for public benefit activity in the central register of non-profit legal persons. Its named directions include habitat restoration, sustainable management of natural resources, and improving conservation policy and legislation. Bulgaria already had a farmland buyer and a river watchdog in this file; this is the oldest and broadest body. IT BUYS AND IT GRAZES: for one species' breeding areas around 50 hectares of land have been purchased, and in total more than 100 hectares — mainly pastures — are managed by Green Balkans to secure hunting grounds, buffer zones around nests, and places for planting new poplars. Buying the nest surroundings, not just the nest, is the practical shape of that. AND IT INVESTIGATES WHAT CITIZENS REPORT: its programme directions include investigation of reports of illegal logging and construction, and combating illegal capture of and trade in wild songbirds, alongside conservation, restoration and sustainable management of wetlands. If you have seen felling or building that should not be happening, there is a national organisation whose stated work is checking such reports. WHAT IT CAN MOBILISE: hundreds of volunteers and experts; for one campaign it coordinated the work of over 150 experts drawn from the institutes of the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences, NGOs and universities. It runs a Wild Animal Rescue Centre in Stara Zagora and a conservation centre at Pomorie Lake, and publishes open volunteer tasks — brigades at Pomorie Lake, cleaning, photo-archive work — so a supporter can start immediately. IT IS ALSO A MEMBER of the For the Nature coalition, which is the Bulgarian sector's shared front.

trackers.name: Za da ostane priroda — an unregistered coalition your group can join by letter
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: 'For Nature to Remain in Bulgaria' — an independent, non-party coalition of citizens' groups and non-governmental organisations fighting to protect Bulgarian nature by encouraging civil society and compliance with legislation. It began from the ecological idea but covers a much wider circle: health, legislation, sustainable tourism, corruption, administrative capacity and work with institutions, volunteering, social responsibility. AND CITIZENS' GROUPS ARE MEMBERS, NOT JUST NGOs: the coalition is informal and not registered — what matters, it says, is working together with better coordination and united forces. To join you submit a written request briefly describing your motivation. There is a screening rule worth noting: people and organisations for whom there is available information about participation in environmentally damaging activities or a conflict of interest are not admitted. WHAT MEMBERSHIP GIVES YOU, stated plainly: your organisation's name will be written under all joint statements, alerts, press releases and other documents issued in the coalition's name. The duties are equally plain — take part in a closed mailing list which should be followed daily, and organise or attend coalition meetings and take on tasks you can actually complete. A small group gains a national signature and owes real work; both halves are stated. WHAT THE COALITION HAS ACTUALLY DONE: positions on the state of nature in Natura 2000 zones with a petition sent to the European Commission; a complaint lodged with the Commission over the lack of protection in the Irakli-Emine and Rila Natura 2000 zones; meetings with MEPs and questions asked in the European Parliament; numerous alerts to institutions; on-site inspections with photographs and films; and participation in public discussion with a submitted position on the general development plan of Strandzha nature park. One member group reports over 200 actions including on-site action to stop illegal construction works. PRACTICAL: contact@forthenature.org; the coalition forms working groups and asks for volunteers.

trackers.name: National Trust EcoFund — 515 projects, NGOs among the beneficiaries, and a lighter process
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: Bulgaria's Natsionalen doveritelen ekofond, established 1995 and listed by the environment ministry as the official national trust ecofund. Over thirty years it has financed 515 projects by municipalities, schools, universities, companies, institutes of the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences, NGOs and others, in over 150 municipalities. Bulgaria's bucket held the Environmental Partnership foundation and Green Balkans; this is the state-linked fund behind them. THE NUMBERS THAT LET YOU JUDGE A BID: total project value over 270 million BGN, of which grant funding of about 121 million BGN, with an average grant rate around 46 per cent — minimum 19, maximum 85. So expect to find roughly half the cost yourself, and know before applying that the top rate exists but is rare. No other fund in this file publishes its own average grant rate. AND THE CLAIM WORTH TESTING, from its own director: when managing projects financed by the fund, the administrative burden is lower compared to other programmes, and work is done directly with the beneficiaries, who are described as partners. For a volunteer group choosing between funders, administrative burden is often the deciding factor. WHAT IT ACTUALLY RUNS: energy efficiency of municipal schools and kindergartens; a Climate Micro Projects programme under a bilateral agreement, now ended; a predefined project on innovative climate mitigation and adaptation measures in Bulgarian municipalities under the BGENVIRONMENT programme; and the 'Mimi Pramatarova' nature conservation competition for students. Read the current programme list — the climate and municipal lines are the consistent ones. AND A SECOND BULGARIAN BODY SURFACED, worth recording: the Wilderness Fund, founded 30 October 1989 in Sofia, a charitable trust for the conservation, research and restoration of the environment, an IUCN member awarded the Ford Foundation prize for natural heritage protection in 1997, working by lobbying, research and consultancy.

trackers.name: SDP Balkani — it supports initiative committees solving local environmental problems
trackers.desc: THE SENTENCE THAT PUTS THIS IN THE FILE: alongside its conservation projects, the association applies its knowledge in public activities including work on drafting nature protection legislation, participation in joint campaigns with other organisations — and supporting initiative committees in resolving local ecological problems. Supporting a residents' committee is stated as one of its own activities, not inferred. WHO THEY ARE: a non-profit working in the public benefit for the study, protection and restoration of flora and fauna in natural ecosystems. Work began in 1988; registered as a legal person in 1992 under the name Zeleni Balkani – Sofia, and renamed Sdruzhenie za diva priroda BALKANI in 2000 — so it is a separate body from Green Balkans, already filed here, despite the shared origin. office@balkani.org. Its people say that more than 25 years on, the active participants in those early activities are now experts in their field. WHAT IT CAN ACTUALLY DO FOR A SITE: it drew up the management plan for Vrachanski Balkan Nature Park. Across eleven designation countries the management plan and the expert study have been the bottleneck; this is a Bulgarian NGO that has written one. It also does scientific research on mammals and large carnivores using genetics, telemetry, direct observation and field signs, using that data to determine which territories are key for protection and what the threats to a species are. AND IT IS IN A LIVE INFRASTRUCTURE FIGHT: its site tracks the Kresna gorge and the Struma motorway, reporting that the Bern Convention and the European Commission will keep following the case at least until construction of the two carriageways outside the Kresna gorge begins. A community facing a road scheme can see how an international convention body is kept engaged over years. PRACTICAL: two education centres open to visitors, at Dragoman and in the village of Vlahi; it works with WWF Bulgaria at the Dragoman Marsh wetland conservation centre; and it is a member of the For the Nature coalition already filed here.

trackers.name: BBF's Spešen fond — emergency money for 'hot' conservation problems, and land purchase by SMS
trackers.desc: WHY THE FUND EXISTS, in its own words: at present there are no financial mechanisms in Bulgaria to support urgent nature conservation activities, and because of insufficient funds, Bulgarian citizens and NGOs often have no way to react to threats to biodiversity that arise. The foundation created a Spešen fond — Emergency Fund for biodiversity — to allow urgent measures to be taken. Its stated uses include protection of important ecosystems and THE PURCHASE OF VALUABLE NATURAL TERRITORIES, and conservation work in a named Natura 2000 zone and maintained reserve. An emergency fund that supports NGOs OR CITIZENS facing a hot conservation problem is the rarest funding shape in this file — almost every other fund runs to an annual call. AND THE FUNDRAISING MECHANISM WORTH COPYING: the foundation raises money for the purchase of valuable natural territories through a single national donation SMS — DMS PRIRODA — and has run campaigns of the form 'send 1 SMS, save 1 m² of nature' at about 1.20 leva a message, alongside direct bank donation. THE CLAUSE THAT MAKES THE PURCHASE STICK: in every contract (notarial deed) for the purchase of land, an express condition is written that these lands will retain their designation and be used only for a conservation purpose. Write the restriction into the deed itself — the cheapest permanent protection recorded in this file. The foundation was created in 1997, is registered in public benefit, and reports annually in the public register.

trackers.name: BSPB's land purchase for the souslik — grazing farmers as the management, mini-reserves as the tool
trackers.desc: THE MODEL, and it answers the question every purchase raises — who will look after it afterwards: conservation and restoration of the pastures will be done with the help of LOCAL FARMERS AND STOCKBREEDERS, who will take on the care of these territories through grazing domestic animals and mowing. That keeps the optimal height of the grass cover for the sousliks, while the domestic animals get secured pasture. The purchase is paid for once; the grazier maintains it for free, in his own interest. AND THE UNIT OF PROTECTION FOR THE SMALLEST FEATURES: lands with single trees and groups of trees will be protected as MINI-RESERVES in which no activity at all will be carried out, while newly planted trees are given special care and protection by the organisation's team and LOCAL VOLUNTEERS. A mini-reserve around a single tree is a designation small enough for a village to propose — and this file has recorded Portugal's Milvoz as the other body working at that scale. Bulgaria's bucket held Green Balkans, the For the Nature coalition and Balkani; this is the bird protection society, and the land-buying side of Bulgarian conservation.

trackers.name: WWF Bulgaria — in the country since 2006, on forests, rivers and PROTECTED TERRITORIES
trackers.desc: WHAT IT COMMITS TO, in its own words: we are dedicated to the protection of Bulgaria's FORESTS, RIVERS AND PROTECTED TERRITORIES, working to limit climate change and to defend emblematic species such as the brown bear and the Danube sturgeons, and drawing young Bulgarians into environmental education and innovation. It has worked in Bulgaria since 2006. A national office of the largest conservation organisation in the world, whose stated remit includes protected territories, is a partner a Bulgarian community can name in a submission — and this file has recorded WWF affiliates elsewhere co-writing designation studies (Montenegro), buying private reserves with partners (Poland) and holding regional offices across eight countries (the Balkans). THE FIGURE IT PUTS AT THE TOP OF ITS OWN PAGE, which a campaign can quote directly: WE HAVE LOST 73 PER CENT OF WILD ANIMALS IN JUST 50 YEARS. URGENT ACTION IS NEEDED IF WE WANT TO STOP THE LOSS OF NATURE. AND HOW IT IS FUNDED, recorded so a community knows who it is dealing with: internationally the organisation is financed 55 per cent by individuals and 19 per cent by intergovernmental and governmental structures, and it has faced various criticisms. It also runs public donation appeals — including one for fighting forest fires.

trackers.name: Asociạciạ na parkovete — it answers citizens' signals and picks the cases that change the law
trackers.desc: WHAT IT OFFERS, in its own account, and both halves matter: striving to respond to the NUMEROUS CITIZENS' SIGNALS ON A GREAT VARIETY OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROBLEMS WHICH WE RECEIVE, we provided support in two directions — CITIZEN TRAINING, and ASSISTANCE ON EMBLEMATIC CASES WHICH WOULD ALLOW US TO CHANGE THE REGULATORY BASE (green advocacy). An organisation that both trains ordinary complainants and picks the strongest cases to litigate is the pairing this file has looked for repeatedly — and it says plainly it already receives more signals than it can answer, so bring it a case that could set a precedent. ITS STATED AIM: to improve the possibilities for DIRECT PARTICIPATION OF CITIZENS IN LOCAL SELF-GOVERNMENT, by raising awareness and CREATING SKILLS TO DEFEND THEIR INTERESTS in a clean environment and preserved nature, working in partnership with a named wildlife society. AND THE HANDBOOK IT PUBLISHES: HOW DO WE PROTECT THE PROTECTED TERRITORIES? — which sets out the duty of ACTIVE PROVISION OF INFORMATION, where institutions publish on their own initiative, noting that for environmental information this has undoubted priority, since timely information about what is happening to the environment can very often protect the health and property of many people, and sometimes even save a human life. It also records that where persons or organisations outside those chosen by the developer declare a written interest, the developer must hold consultations with them too.

trackers.name: Fondaciạ Kolektivūt — it turns derelict urban ground into public space, with the residents
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a foundation created in 2020 with the aim of TURNING DERELICT URBAN PLOTS INTO LIVING PUBLIC SPACES, working with young people, students, volunteers, artists and design specialists in different parts of the country. Its line: the cities belong to everyone, and together we create their future. Occupying and improving a neglected plot is the strongest answer to a proposal to build on it — this file recorded the same logic in Montenegro, where a clean-up was followed by furniture, cameras and signs. WHAT IT ACTUALLY RUNS: a programme that OPENS DERELICT URBAN PLOTS TO PEOPLE AND FILLS THEM WITH GREENERY AND CULTURE — in districts where shared spaces are lacking, we awaken public life in unusual locations, carried out together with the residents of a named housing estate. AND THE RIVERS PROGRAMME, which is a model for any town with a neglected watercourse: a long-term initiative aiming to transform the relationship of cities with THEIR RIVERS, which began with a festival in the capital and has since spread to more and more towns in the country, building around itself an ecosystem of like-minded people at local, national and EUROPEAN level.

trackers.name: Obzhalvane na aktove na obshtina — you do NOT have to appeal to the region first
trackers.desc: THE PROCEDURAL POINT THAT SAVES MONTHS, set out by a Bulgarian practice: administrative appeal runs by complaint to the SUPERIOR administrative body — where a MAYOR'S act is contested, the superior body is THE REGIONAL GOVERNOR, and the complaint is addressed to the regional administration and LODGED THROUGH THE MUNICIPALITY that issued the contested act. Bulgaria's legal entries were courts and a network; this is the practice side. AND THEN THE PART MOST PEOPLE GET WRONG: IT IS NOT OBLIGATORY TO CONTEST THE ACT BY THE ADMINISTRATIVE ROUTE FIRST — that is, WE CAN GO DIRECTLY WITH A COMPLAINT BEFORE THE COMPETENT COURT. Skipping the internal appeal is allowed, and knowing that stops a community losing months waiting on the body that issued the decision. AND WHAT MUNICIPAL ACTS ARE AT ISSUE: mayors, as administrative bodies of executive power, issue MANY INDIVIDUAL ADMINISTRATIVE ACTS AFFECTING THE LEGAL SPHERE OF CITIZENS, and the most common are those under THE SPATIAL PLANNING ACT. The same practice notes that where an order is issued for the REMOVAL OF AN UNLAWFUL STRUCTURE, you must appeal WITHIN THE DEADLINES of the administrative procedure code and the planning act, BEFORE THE ADMINISTRATIVE COURT of the location.

trackers.name: A Bulgarian environmental-law practice — it will CHALLENGE A PERMIT REFUSAL, and write the OVOS request
trackers.desc: WHAT IT OFFERS, listed as a service: consultations, LEGAL DEFENCE AND ASSISTANCE, AND PROCEDURAL REPRESENTATION on ecological-legal questions; consultation and representation when applying for licences and permits; and CONTESTING BEFORE THE COURT REFUSALS to issue licences and permits. A practice that names contesting a permit decision in court is one a community can approach about a permit that was granted, not only one refused — the same courtroom either way. AND THE TECHNICAL WORK IT DOES, which is the half a community usually cannot produce: drawing up the INFORMATION (REQUEST) FOR ASSESSING THE NEED FOR AN ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT (OVOS) under a named annex and article of the ordinance; ASSESSMENT OF THE IMPACT of various objects on the environment, INCLUDING DRAWING UP OVOS REPORTS; the NOTIFICATION of investment proposals; and the REQUEST FOR ASSESSMENT OF THE NEED to carry out an OVOS. The request that forces a screening decision on whether an impact assessment is needed is a document a lawyer will draft, and it is often the earliest formal step available against a project. It also offers DEFENCE DURING INSPECTIONS AND CONTROL by the environment ministry and the REGIONAL ENVIRONMENT AND WATER INSPECTORATES.

trackers.name: The state forest enterprises BUY PRIVATE FOREST — applications open ALL YEAR ROUND
trackers.desc: THE PUBLIC BUYER A BULGARIAN OWNER CAN APPROACH: the state forest enterprises run a standing PROCEDURE FOR THE PURCHASE OF PROPERTIES — FOREST TERRITORIES, under published ministerial orders and RULES FOR THE PURCHASE OF FOREST TERRITORIES BY THE STATE ENTERPRISES, with TELEPHONE NUMBERS FOR EXPLANATIONS AND CONTACT WITH THE STAFF, an office address, an email and stated working hours. Bulgaria is joint-smallest bucket in this file. A state body that will buy a private wood, with a named procedure and a phone number, is the buyer a community should point a willing owner at — no fundraising required. AND THE CHANGES THAT WIDENED IT: the campaign-style intake of applications from owners IS ABOLISHED — THE INTAKE PROCEDURE WILL BE OPEN ALL YEAR ROUND, and the scope of eligible properties now admits not only properties of NATURAL PERSONS but also THOSE OF MUNICIPALITIES AND LEGAL PERSONS. A year-round window and municipalities admitted as sellers together mean a council can put a threatened wood to the state at any time. AND THE MONEY BEHIND IT: the funds for the purchase and its accompanying costs are provided from the TARGETED FUND 'INVESTMENTS IN FORESTS', which accumulates revenue from the activity of the enterprises. The site archives every year's procedure and its orders.

trackers.name: The priority rule — OLD-GROWTH forest is bought first, and the owner no longer names the price
trackers.desc: THE PRIORITY THAT DECIDES WHICH WOOD GETS BOUGHT: for properties owned by municipalities, PREFERENCE IN THE PURCHASE IS GIVEN TO THOSE IN WHICH PLANTATIONS WITH THE CHARACTERISTICS OF A 'FOREST IN THE PHASE OF OLD AGE' PREDOMINATE. The stated aim is that the state should manage and protect THE OLD FORESTS, IN WHICH NO ECONOMIC ACTIVITY HAS BEEN CARRIED OUT IN RECENT DECADES, following the European forest strategy to 2030. Old-growth character moves a wood to the front of the state's buying queue — so documenting that a threatened stand has been unlogged for decades is worth doing before approaching anyone. AND THE PROCEDURAL CHANGE THAT PROTECTS THE SELLER: the requirement that the owner, when submitting the documents, SHOULD THEMSELVES STATE A PURCHASE PRICE IS REMOVED. An owner no longer has to name a figure and risk undervaluing their own land. AND THE PURPOSE THE STATE GIVES: purchase is carried out to INCREASE AND CONSOLIDATE the forest territories and to create conditions for their MORE EFFECTIVE MANAGEMENT, PROTECTION AND THE MAINTENANCE OF GOOD HEALTH AND VITALITY. Owners apply by a standard-form application to the state enterprise OR to the state forestry or hunting holding IN WHOSE AREA OF ACTIVITY THE PROPERTY LIES.

trackers.name: BlueLink — the foundation that HOSTS Bulgarian civic campaigns, with its address published
trackers.desc: THE INFRASTRUCTURE UNDER BULGARIAN ENVIRONMENTAL CAMPAIGNING: a named Sofia foundation, running since 1998, which hosts the coalition's presence and publishes for it a standing set of sections — NEWS, CALENDAR, POSITIONS (STANOVISHTA), DOCUMENTS, CAMPAIGNS, PETITIONS and BLOGS — alongside its own PROJECTS, ACTIVITIES, HISTORY, THE PEOPLE IN BLUELINK, and WORK AND VOLUNTEERING. A campaign that has somewhere to publish its formal positions and its petitions, without building a site, starts with the half most local groups never finish — and the positions archive is itself a record of what has been argued before. AND THE CONTACT DETAILS, which is what makes this usable: the foundation publishes ITS STREET ADDRESS AND FLOOR IN SOFIA, A TELEPHONE NUMBER, AND AN OFFICE EMAIL. HONEST LIMIT ON THIS ENTRY: what this page gives is the foundation's identity, its published sections and its contact details — not a description of services offered to outside communities. It is filed as A ROUTE IN AND A PLACE TO PUBLISH, not as a body documented here as taking on casework.

trackers.name: Zeleni zakoni — a watchdog that publishes the FILING ADDRESSES for a live case
trackers.desc: A MONITORING INITIATIVE THAT PUBLISHES THE PRACTICAL DETAIL OTHER SITES OMIT: on a live Supreme Administrative Court case it prints how to file ELECTRONICALLY, WITH A QUALIFIED ELECTRONIC SIGNATURE, giving the court's own e-mail address, the environment ministry's address, and even the address of the lawyer representing the appealing companies. Bulgaria is among the least-worked buckets in this file. Publishing the exact filing addresses turns a reader into a party — and naming the developers' own lawyer means a community can see who it is actually against. AND THE PATTERN IT DOCUMENTS, which is the one to watch for locally: for a plan that in principle requires an environmental assessment, THE REGIONAL INSPECTORATE FOR ENVIRONMENT AND WATER ONCE AGAIN ATTEMPTS TO DECLARE THAT IT JUDGES THAT PRECISELY FOR THIS PLAN NO ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT WILL BE CARRIED OUT. The commonest way a plan escapes scrutiny is a screening decision that no assessment is needed, and that decision is itself challengeable. It also records that THE EXCHANGED FORESTS CARRY A BUILDING PROHIBITION IMPOSED BY THE FORESTRY ACT SINCE 2011.

trackers.name: When the right to go to court is itself under attack — and taken to an international body
trackers.desc: AN ATTACK ON THE COURT ROUTE ITSELF, appealed above the national level: the report records that THE ATTACKS ON ACCESS TO JUSTICE IN BULGARIA ARE BEING APPEALED AT INTERNATIONAL LEVEL, and that THE CHANGES TO THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEDURE CODE HAVE THE AIM OF SPEEDING UP CONTESTED INVESTMENT PROJECTS, BY DRASTICALLY REDUCING THE POSSIBILITIES FOR THEIR ADEQUATE ASSESSMENT AND CONTROL, INCLUDING THROUGH THE COURT. Bulgaria is among the least-worked buckets in this file. Procedural-code reform is how the objection route is closed without ever mentioning the environment — the same shape as the Swiss appeal-right narrowing in batch605 and the Kosovar rezoning council in batch608, and a community should read code amendments as project news. AND WHAT CAN BE DONE WITH IT: the response was to appeal the change AT INTERNATIONAL LEVEL, which is the route available when a national parliament has already voted. AND THE BACKGROUND CONDITION IT RECORDS: THE COUNTRY SUFFERS FROM UNREGULATED POLLUTION, AND SEVERAL COAL-FIRED POWER STATIONS ALSO BURN WASTE, DESPITE CASES HAVING BEEN BROUGHT. The organisation also offers HELP FOR STRENGTHENING ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION IN SCHOOLS and runs three-day trainings INCLUDING SIMULATIONS CLOSE TO REALITY.

trackers.name: Andmekaitse Inspektsioon (Estonian DPA)
trackers.desc: Estonia's Andmekaitse Inspektsioon (AKI) is a dual-mandate body: it supervises both the Public Information Act and personal-data protection, handling access challenges and privacy complaints and publishing rulings, guidance and complaint channels. USE IT: one office covers both a refused records request and a data-protection complaint about how a body handled your details.

trackers.name: Riigi Teataja
trackers.desc: Official State Gazette of Estonia, publishing legislation and court decisions online. · Find here: Estonia's official State Gazette — legislation and court decisions (Riigi Teataja).

trackers.name: Estonian Environmental Law Center (Keskkonnaõiguse Keskus)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Estonia's dedicated environmental-law NGO, running a legal-aid service and publishing guidance written specifically for people living beside planned mining areas — what impacts to raise, and how to become a party to the extraction-permit procedure. Also produced guidance on public participation and disclosure of environmental information under the Aarhus Convention, and works on Natura 2000 conflicts between communities, landowners and officials. WHO IT SUITS: a community or landowner facing a quarry, mine or Natura-area restriction and needing to get standing in the permit proceeding. A small team — expect triage, not unlimited representation.

trackers.name: Justice and Environment — European green-law network
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the European network of environmental-law NGOs, whose national member here is the Estonian Environmental Law Center. Its fifteen members act as the environmental-law service point in their own countries, taking cases and intervening in legislative processes, while the network defends communities and nature in court and lodges infringement complaints against member-state governments. Its standing themes are access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, environmental assessment and pollution control. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who does not yet know which lawyer to call — knock on the Estonian Environmental Law Center's door first, and use the network only if your problem crosses a border. The network itself does not take individual cases; its members do. YOUR NATIONAL MEMBER IS Estonian Environmental Law Center (EELC) (k6k.ee) — go to them, not to the network. J&E members serve as environmental law ‘service points’ in their countries, handling cases, participating in legislative processes and sometimes providing legal analyses and consultations for national governments. The network has 11 full and 4 associate members, and can launch infringement proceedings against faulty governments — a route a national body alone does not have. CURRENT SCOPE: access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, climate, environmental assessments, and the Environmental Liability Directive. It previously worked on waste, transport, health and Natura 2000, so an older document may overstate what it covers today.

trackers.name: National Audit Office (Riigikontroll)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Estonia, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: e-Business Register
trackers.desc: Estonian government database

trackers.name: e-Business Register (Estonia)
trackers.desc: Estonia's official e-business company register. Here you can trace companies, their directors and filings registered in Estonia.

trackers.name: Riigihanked
trackers.desc: Estonia's public-procurement register. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Estonia, and for how much.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Estonia
trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Estonia — supreme court (Estonia).

trackers.name: Statistics Estonia
trackers.desc: Estonia's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Estonia.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Estonia
trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Estonia — supreme court in Estonia (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: KIK looduskaitse programm — up to 100 percent, if your põhikiri says so
trackers.desc: ESTONIA FUNDS NON-PROFITS AT UP TO 100 PERCENT OF ELIGIBLE COSTS — for both sihtasutused and mittetulundusühingud, under the environment minister's määrus on support from the Keskkonnaprogramm. That puts it alongside Hungary at the generous end of this map. THE GATE IS YOUR STATUTE: associations and foundations may apply if their põhikiri provides for nature or environmental protection activity — making Estonia the sixth country here, with Finland, Italy, Poland, Greece and Hungary, where the eligibility test is the wording of your own constitution. Treat that as a rule of thumb across Europe. THE EXCEPTION TO BUDGET FOR: acquiring livestock and equipment for maintaining semi-natural communities is capped at 85 percent with at least 15 percent own financing, and per-animal caps apply — EUR 1,500 per horse, 835 per head of cattle, 165 per sheep or goat. Also not eligible: building construction and repair, and vehicle purchase. Local governments, companies, public-law legal persons and sole proprietors may also apply. Applications go through the E-toetuse keskkond, no longer KIKAS, using ID-card or Mobiil-ID.

trackers.name: The sub-programme that pays for documenting an undocumented site
trackers.desc: IF YOUR SITE HAS NO EVIDENCE BEHIND IT, THIS IS THE ROUTE. The looduskaitse programme's first sub-programme funds planning long-term conservation development — expressly including inventories (inventuurid) and applied research to identify protected or little-studied habitats and species, culturally valuable natural objects, ecosystems and ecosystem services. Documenting an unstudied place is fundable in its own right, which is what most campaigns lack before they can argue for protection. The other sub-programmes cover maintenance and protection of habitats, protected areas, hoiualad and single objects including species action plans, and nationwide conservation infrastructure such as observation towers and information points. A LIVE ROUND FOR SHAPE: over EUR 655,000 for species and habitat protection, covering first and second protection category and critically endangered species, with preference for projects on invasive species, express welcome for projects testing new methods of controlling non-native slugs, support for organising looduskaitsetalgud (volunteer conservation work days), mowing equipment for wooded meadows, and repairing roads or culverts needed to maintain heritage meadows.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen.
