The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Keskkonnaõiguse Keskus (KOK) — environmental lawyers for communities (Estonia)
trackers.desc: WHO TO CALL: the Estonian Environmental Law Centre, an independent public-interest expert foundation operating since November 2007, founded by the Estonian Fund for Nature together with three environmental lawyers and grown out of that fund's legal work from 2001. Its lawyers work only in environmental law including planning and building, and it says it has advised hundreds of clients in both administrative and court proceedings. Its stated client list includes community societies and private individuals alongside local authorities, companies and environmental organisations. WHAT IT COVERS: spatial plans, building and use permits, noise, odour nuisance, mineral extraction, nature-protection restrictions, forestry and waste. Named lawyers carry declared specialisms — one covers species and habitat protection, wind farms, mining, forestry including forest drainage, planning and environmental impact assessment, which between them are most of what a rural Estonian community ever faces. It is a member of the Justice and Environment network. WHAT TO EXPECT, AND IT IS NOT WHAT IT ONCE WAS: KOK began by giving free legal aid only, and now funds itself through paid services and project grants as well. Ask about cost in the first message rather than assuming. It also states that because court proceedings are long and expensive it tries where possible to settle disputes without going to court, by helping the parties reach agreement — useful if that is what you want, and worth knowing if it is not. AND RUN THE CONFLICT CHECK: its clients include companies and local authorities as well as residents. Name the developer and the deciding body in your first message and ask whether it is free to act for you.

trackers.name: Eesti Erametsaliit — the private forest owners' union, and the way to reach an owner (Estonia)
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: the Estonian Private Forest Union, a non-commercial, non-profit association of Estonian private forest owners, and one of eighteen partners in the LIFE ENPLC European private land conservation project. Its Latvian counterpart in the same project is the Latvian Forest Owners association, LMIB. WHY A COMMUNITY WOULD GO TO A FOREST OWNERS' BODY: Estonia has no conservation land buyer that three searches in this file could find, and its allies are a legal centre and a research NGO. What it does have is an organised body representing the people who actually own the forest. A conservation approach to an Estonian private owner is far more likely to land if it comes with, or through, the association that owner already belongs to and trusts — and this one has committed itself to a European project whose explicit purpose is engaging private landowners in voluntary conservation, including through conservation easements. It has, in other words, already agreed in principle that its members might do this. HOW TO USE IT: ask whether it will make an introduction, whether it has members in your area who have taken part in the ENPLC work, and what instrument it thinks an Estonian owner would actually sign. That last question matters, because the project's own survey found European practitioners reporting a shortage of adequate legal tools for this. BE CLEAR WHAT IT IS NOT: it is a forest owners' representative body, not a conservation organisation. Its members' interest is in managing and harvesting their forests, and it will not campaign against a development. It is a door to owners, not an ally against a project. SOURCING: described here from the LIFE ENPLC partner page, which sets out each partner's nature and role. Confirm current contact details directly.

trackers.name: Pärandkoosluste Kaitse Ühing (PKÜ) — holds the inventory of Estonia's meadows
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Estonian Seminatural Community Conservation Association, founded 1997, at Wilhelm Struve 2, 51003 Tartu, pky@pky.ee, register code 80006985. It works on semi-natural communities — wooded meadows, alvars, floodplain meadows, coastal meadows and other meadows and pastures maintained only by grazing and mowing. Anyone can join for ten euros a year, and its membership already includes students, scientists, farmers, conservationists and landowners. For a community with no standing and no budget, that is the cheapest route into an established Estonian organisation I have found. THE REASON TO RING IT FIRST: it holds the inventory. Working with the Estonian Fund for Nature it inventoried most of Estonia's alvars and wooded, coastal and floodplain meadows in 1999–2000, inventoried the whole of Läänemaa county with the Southwest Finland regional environment centre, and has added the surveys of every area subject to maintenance and restoration compensation — all collected into one continuously updated database. If your ground is semi-natural grassland, somebody has probably already surveyed it and the record is here. That is the third country in this file where the answer to what lives on a site already exists, after Turkey and North Macedonia. WHAT IT ALSO DOES: it delivers restoration training, and under the Estonian-Latvian LIFE wooded meadow project it has been restoring overgrown wooded meadows — 74 hectares returned by 2025 with a further 70 in progress in Estonia, and 55 hectares plus 11 more in Latvia, against a 700-hectare target. It publishes detailed English-language management and restoration guidance for each habitat type, including the practical detail that sheep beat cattle for clearing juniper because sheep eat the saplings. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer, not a funder and not a law firm. Estonia still has no acquirer. What this gives a community is the survey record, the restoration know-how, and membership of a national body for the price of a meal.

trackers.name: Eesti Ornitoloogiaühing — the bird record, and a hundred years of it (Estonia)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: BirdLife Estonia, founded 1 May 1921 and continuously active since, a full BirdLife partner from 2000, at Veski 4, Tartu 51005, eoy@eoy.ee, +372 742 2195. It describes itself as a voluntary association of people interested in birds, bird study and conservation, working to achieve favourable condition for Estonia's birds through bird studies, habitat conservation and public awareness. WHAT TO ASK IT: what is recorded on your site, and whether the species there carry protection consequences. A century of continuous recording makes it the deepest bird dataset in the country. That question — who already surveyed this — is now answered in seven countries in this file, and Estonia's answer differs by habitat: for semi-natural grassland the inventory sits with the heritage communities association already filed here; for birds it sits with this one. Ask the right holder. IT IS A VOLUNTARY ASSOCIATION, which is the practical way in for a community with people rather than money — the same route as the ten-euro membership of Estonia's grassland body. WHAT IT IS NOT, CHECKED SPECIFICALLY: not a land buyer. I looked for evidence that it purchases or holds land and found none, unlike the Belgian, Polish and Slovenian BirdLife partners. Estonia still has no conservation land buyer in this file — its allies are a legal centre, a grassland inventory and restoration body, a private forest owners' union as the door to landowners, and now the bird record.

trackers.name: KÜSK — Estonia's civil society endowment, and a grant to write your own plan
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: Sihtasutus Kodanikuuühiskonna Sihtkapital, the National Foundation of Civil Society, whose stated main aim is to increase the capacity of associations acting in the public interest in Estonia, mainly through application rounds and competitions letting an association seek support for developing either itself or its community. It also awards stipendiums to organisations it notices itself, and it is the Estonian contact point for the European Commission's CERV programme. Estonia had no funder in this file. THE ROUND THAT SUITS A SMALL GROUP BEST: the arenguhüpet ettevalmistav — development-leap preparation — round, maximum €4,000, with no co-financing required. It pays an association to analyse what it has been doing and plan what comes next: a development plan, an action plan, a communications plan or a business plan, produced with the organisation's own target group and stakeholders involved. During the project the association brings in a development expert to advise it. A grant to write your own plan, with an expert attached and nothing to match, is close to ideal for a village committee that has just constituted itself and does not yet know what it is doing. The follow-on arenguhüppe round then funds carrying that plan out, up to €25,000. THE ELIGIBILITY, WHICH IS STRICT AND CHECKABLE: a non-profit association or foundation acting in the public interest with public activity; registered in the Estonian register for at least one year at the deadline; not under the controlling influence of the state, a local authority, a political party or a company; no KÜSK grant from the same round in the last three years; annual reports filed on time; and no tax debt beyond a small threshold. Applications are scored out of 100 with a funding threshold of 70 points and awards made in rank order until the budget runs out. OTHER ROUNDS TO WATCH: an international cooperation round, and a Kogukonnafond — community fund — round aimed at increasing the crisis preparedness of communities and apartment associations and developing cooperation for it.

trackers.name: Eestimaa Looduse Fond — may own property, funds others' projects, and turns out for work parties
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: the Estonian Fund for Nature, a non-profit foundation founded 1991 and now more than three decades old, describing itself as a civic association that provides society with the expertise nature conservation needs and comes to help where state bodies and the private sector do not reach. Its team holds species and habitat experts as well as people researching the causes of environmental problems. Estonia had no acquirer in this file. THE STATUTE IS WHY THIS IS FILED AS AN ACQUIRER: its assets arise from donations, gifts, bequests, earmarked allocations and other lawful income, and ELF may own any property necessary to achieve its statutory aims whose acquisition does not conflict with law. So an Estonian owner who wants ground protected after death, or a community that raises a purchase price, has a body that can hold it. AND IT IS ALSO A FUNDER: the statute provides that ELF supports nature and environmental protection projects carried out by others and awards stipends. Second Estonian funder in this file, and this one is conservation-specific. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES ON THE GROUND: protects old-growth forest, restores wooded meadows and mires, saves frogs dying on roads, and speaks into climate decisions. Its loodustalgud — nature work parties — run 3 to 5 days and sometimes up to 10, restoring and maintaining habitats: cutting scrub, making hay, tending the habitat of a protected species such as the natterjack toad or the black stork, with a local nature expert on hand. A tradition running since 1998. If your ground needs physical work rather than money, that is a standing volunteer force. IT ALSO MAPS: a recent anniversary appeal collected donations specifically for mapping the natural values of forests — the survey capability this file keeps finding is decisive. PRACTICAL: ELF is on the Estonian list of non-profits eligible for income tax relief, so donations are tax-free up to a limit; there is a donations coordinator for company giving; and bank details are published for direct transfer.

trackers.name: EKO — ten Estonian organisations, and it publishes every submission it has made
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Estonian Council of Environmental NGOs, an informal, politically independent cooperation network formed in 2002, now ten non-governmental environmental organisations — Baltic Environmental Forum, Estonian Fund for Nature, Estonian Green Movement, Estonian Ornithological Society, SEI Tallinn, the Seminatural Community Conservation Association, Tartu Student Nature Protection Circle, the students' society Sorex, Läänerannik, and the Society Against Nõmme Road. Members have worked jointly mainly on making Estonian forestry, agriculture and energy policy and planning decisions more environmentally friendly. WHY THE PAGE ABOVE IS THE RESOURCE: EKO publishes its public addresses and positions, case by case and dated. The archive includes its positions on extending a quarry's mining permit and expanding the quarry, with proposals for supplementing the environmental impact assessment programme; on fish passes at four named dams; on the EIA programme for offshore wind in north-west Estonian coastal sea; and an address stating that EKO understands the concern of local residents and local governments about growing pressure from the state and developers on the quality of the living environment. A community facing a quarry, a dam or a wind farm can read what a ten-organisation coalition already argued about the same kind of case. AND IT NAMES NAMES ONCE A YEAR: since 2004 EKO chooses the year's most environmentally beneficial act — the environmental deed — and the most hostile, the environmental axe. In 2023 the deed was the creation of the Sõrve nature protection area near the capital; the axe went to the agriculture and food board for continuing to permit drainage practices damaging natural values. IT ALSO DID THE WORK OF SAYING WHICH AREAS SHOULD BE PROTECTED: Estonian environmental organisations produced an analysis in 2023 of which areas could additionally be taken under protection, and EKO made its own proposals mainly on mires and heritage meadows, with map layers published, and further proposals on forests and marine areas in preparation. If your ground is a mire or a semi-natural meadow, check whether it is already on that map.

trackers.name: KIK — nine programmes funded by pollution charges, and MTÜs can apply
trackers.desc: WHERE THE MONEY COMES FROM: the Keskkonnainvesteeringute Keskus distributes the keskkonnaprogramm, funded from environmental charges under the keskkonnatasude seadus, across nine fields: fisheries, water management, NATURE CONSERVATION, forestry, circular economy, marine environment, subsurface, air protection and environmental awareness. Part of the charge income also funds keskkonnalaenud — earmarked loans for carrying out an environmental project. Third country in this sweep where polluters fund the repair, after Czechia and Romania — and the first offering loans as well as grants. WHO MAY APPLY: local authorities, companies, bodies dealing with environmental protection, mittetulundusühingud (non-profit associations), sihtasutused (foundations), public-law legal persons and sole traders. Applications go through the e-toetuse environment with ID-card or Mobiil-ID login. WHAT THE NATURE CONSERVATION ROUND ACTUALLY FUNDED, which is the practical core: a 655,290 euro looduskaitse round supporting studies on protected areas, control of alien species, ORGANISING TALGUD — volunteer work parties — and investments connected with maintaining heritage meadows. Named eligible items included acquiring the mowing machinery needed for wooded meadow management and repairing the roads or culverts needed to maintain heritage meadows. Priority went to first and second protection category and critically endangered species and habitats, and to projects on invasive species. Machinery, access roads and volunteer work parties are all fundable line items — the most concrete list of eligible costs in this sweep. HOW IT IS RUN, AND THE HONEST NOTE: the programme has been opened as nine sectoral rounds rather than one large one, each with its own budget and an expert evaluation committee, with the state naming the priority activities in each — done, in KIK's words, to set the focus and avoid needless waste of applicants' time given the small budget. Rounds do not all open every year; check which programme is currently open before writing.

trackers.name: Maa-amet — the State MUST buy land whose use is significantly restricted by protection
trackers.desc: THE DUTY, AND IT IS AN OBLIGATION NOT AN OFFER: the State buys land with nature protection restrictions under the looduskaitseseadus where the owner's use of the land is significantly restricted because of nature protection, AT ITS MARKET VALUE — and, from a change in the law, if the owner of a property with significant protection restrictions wishes to sell, THE STATE MUST BUY IT. Purchases are decided in the order the owners' applications arrive. Where the state must buy, an owner facing a developer has a guaranteed buyer at market value — and this file has recorded pre-emption rights in six countries, but Estonia's is a duty to purchase, not merely a first refusal. THE HONEST QUEUE, RECORDED PLAINLY, BECAUSE IT DECIDES WHETHER THIS IS ANY USE TO YOU: at one point 184 applications were in the acquisition queue worth some 15.3 million euro, with properties at the head of the queue in process since 2007, and elsewhere 735 properties were waiting, some applications going back seven years. The agency states it has capacity to acquire about 80 protected properties a year; one extra government allocation of 1 million euro was expected to buy 30 protected properties totalling over 230 hectares. The ministry itself says such a long waiting time rightly causes great resentment among landowners and is not fair to them. WHICH LAND QUALIFIES: properties containing a protected individual natural object, or lying entirely within a protected area, a conservation area or a permanent habitat — where the owner cannot use the land as they wish or earn income from managing it.

trackers.name: Eestimaa Looduse Fond — it helped form three of Estonia's protected areas
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: a sihtasutus — a foundation, the Estonian form that can hold property — founded in 1991 by 41 founding members and a foundation since January 1999, described as an independent civic organisation that protects nature using the best expert knowledge, innovative solutions and everyone's help. Estonia had one acquirer filed; this is the national foundation. THE TRACK RECORD THAT MATTERS TO A COMMUNITY: the fund has been involved in the FORMATION of Soomaa and Karula national parks and the Alam-Pedja nature protection area. An organisation that has helped form three protected areas is one you can ask to help form a fourth — the same test applied in Latvia, where the body had founded a nature park. WHAT ELSE IT RUNS: it works to protect threatened species and their habitats and the natural landscapes and communities characteristic of Estonia, helps with sustainable use of natural resources, and steps in where the work of state institutions, research bodies and companies needs to be joined up. It runs two nature schools and awards a Young Nature Conservationist prize and a Young Nature Farmer prize. Its emblem animal is the flying squirrel.

trackers.name: Keskkonnaõiguse Keskus — it advises AND represents landowners and local associations in court
trackers.desc: WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES, from its own published casework, and every line is a community's situation: KOK advises and REPRESENTS IN COURT landowners near whose homes an industrial complex is planned — the complex sited on farmland rather than on land designated for industry, for which the local authority AMENDED THE VALID COMPREHENSIVE PLAN. The landowners contested the amendment as unnecessary and unjustified. KOK advised them in the detailed plan procedure and represents them in the court dispute. Its named jurists are published. An organisation that will both advise you through the planning procedure and then take the case to court is the whole route in one instruction. Estonia had 22 filed entries. MORE OF ITS CASELOAD, so a group can see the range: it represents a LOCAL ASSOCIATION in court over a housing development IN A TOWN PARK; and it advises an NGO through three county planning procedures determining a rail corridor's location, and — IN COOPERATION WITH A LAW FIRM — represents it in contesting the established plans in court. AND WHAT IT PUBLISHES FREE: a web guide FOR CITIZENS AND CITIZENS' ASSOCIATIONS on participating in environmental decision-making; a handbook on strategic environmental assessment; work on appropriate assessment and Natura 2000 areas; recommendations for INCLUSIVE SPATIAL PLANNING in local authorities; and an analysis of the organisation of building significant-impact objects.

trackers.name: KIK's funded-projects register — every grant since 2011, updated daily
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a public register of projects financed from the structural funds SINCE 2008, projects financed from the environment programme SINCE 2011, and emissions trading projects since 2017, with data drawn automatically from the e-support environment and UPDATED ONCE EVERY 24 HOURS. A daily-updated list of who got environmental money, for what, and how much, is the best application guide a group will ever read — and it doubles as intelligence: it shows which organisations in your county are already funded and therefore worth approaching as partners. AND THE HONEST LIMIT, published with it: in accordance with data protection rules, grants given to PRIVATE INDIVIDUALS are not found here; private forestry recipients sit in a separate portal, and the studies KIK has funded are listed on their own page. A separate list of funded STUDIES tells a community which surveys already exist before it pays for another. Alongside these the fund publishes its open calls for businesses and open supports for LOCAL AUTHORITIES AND RELATED BODIES as standing pages, and supports applicants in submitting project ideas to an EU innovation fund.

trackers.name: Koosloodus — 25 euro secures 50 square metres, and there is a FORM FOR SELLING IT YOUR LAND
trackers.desc: THE PRICE AND THE MECHANISM: every 25 EURO donation secures the preservation of about 50 SQUARE METRES OF FOREST, and all our forest purchases are planned together with nature scientists and specialists in the field. Estonia had three land-holding bodies filed; this one buys woodland outright. AND THE SENTENCE A THREATENED OWNER NEEDS: ARE YOU A LANDOWNER AND DO YOU WANT TO SELL YOUR LAND TO KOOSLOODUS? Please fill in the form on this page and we will contact you TO ESTABLISH THE NATURE CONSERVATION VALUE OF THE LAND. A published form for offering your own land to a conservation buyer is the shortest route from a threatened parcel to a protected one. AND ITS PUBLISHED PURCHASE PREFERENCES, so a community knows whether its site qualifies: forest SURROUNDING a woodland key habitat or permanent habitat; forest needing additional protection or extension IN A LIMITED-MANAGEMENT ZONE, A CONSERVATION AREA OR THEIR NEIGHBOURHOOD; forest surrounding INDIVIDUAL NATURAL OBJECTS; OLD NATURAL OR PRIMEVAL FOREST NOT YET UNDER PROTECTION; and other unique natural objects and communities worth saving. Though it prefers old forest, it says the restoration of clear-cuts and young forest for future generations is equally important.

trackers.name: Eesti Looduskaitse Selts — a named person and mobile number for EVERY local branch
trackers.desc: WHAT THIS PAGE IS: the society's branch list, and it publishes FOR EACH LOCAL BRANCH A NAMED CONTACT PERSON, A MOBILE TELEPHONE NUMBER AND AN EMAIL ADDRESS — branch after branch across the country, plus the head office secretary with her own number. A named neighbour with a mobile number in your own district is worth more than any national office, and this file has looked for exactly this artefact in forty countries. Several branches share a contact person, so one call can reach two districts. AND WHAT THE SOCIETY OFFERS: join the Estonian Nature Protection Society as a member and take part in nature conservation activities IN YOUR OWN HOME AREA OR ACROSS ESTONIA. Its structure is published in full — board and audit committee, branches, statutes, history, honorary members, FOUNDING MEMBERS AND SUPPORTING MEMBERS — along with a FOREST COMMITTEE, a named declaration, cooperation with a green schools programme, and its own library and art collection. A society with a standing forest committee is the body to bring a felling question to, and membership is the way in.

trackers.name: Loodushoiu Fond — a fund built specifically for PRIVATE LANDOWNERS who want to keep their land
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS AND WHO IT IS FOR: founded in 2021, a UNIQUE ASSOCIATION OF PRIVATE LANDOWNERS FOR NATURE CONSERVATION. It works with landowners who are interested in preserving biodiversity ON THEIR OWN LAND, creating in cooperation opportunities for GREEN CORRIDORS or on a per-property basis — for example creating habitats for protected species or RESTORING WETLANDS. Its aim is invigorating VOLUNTARY nature conservation and creating opportunities for it. An owner who does not want to sell but does want the land kept is the commonest case in this file, and this is the first fund built entirely around them. AND THE FIGURE THAT EXPLAINS WHY IT EXISTS: private landowners currently find it VERY DIFFICULT to find money for conservation work. Of 620 MILLION EURO in the statistics office's review of environmental protection financing, ONLY 54 MILLION reaches the field of preserving biodiversity and protecting the landscape — and of that money, only a small part reaches conservation ON PRIVATE LAND. HOW IT RUNS ITSELF, published: it has never used a membership scheme, preferring regular donations because administering a membership takes considerable time and money; its economic activity is entirely public and, unlike many charitable funds, it publishes summaries of its finances on its website so everyone can see where their money actually goes; and wherever possible it secures THE SUPPORT OF THE LOCAL AUTHORITY. In its forest renewal programme 10 euro is the average cost of one tree, covering not only planting but all project and programme costs.

trackers.name: Eestimaa Looduse Fond — expertise where the state and the private sector do not reach
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS FOR, in its own words, and it is the clearest statement of a gap in the file: it is a free association which PROVIDES SOCIETY WITH THE EXPERTISE NECESSARY FOR NATURE CONSERVATION AND COMES TO HELP WHERE STATE INSTITUTIONS AND THE PRIVATE SECTOR DO NOT REACH. An organisation whose stated purpose is filling the gap left by the state is the one to approach when the agency will not act, and it protects nature relying on ECOLOGY — the science of species and their habitats. THE CONTACT DETAILS, in full: a street address in Tartu, a registry code, an email address, TWO TELEPHONE NUMBERS and TWO BANK IBANs. It adds an honest note: our people are often out in the bog, at sea, in the forest or in a home office, so please contact us in advance to meet at the Tartu office. AND WHAT ITS NAMED STAFF ACTUALLY DO, which tells a community what to ask for: one expert has organised INVENTORY PROJECTS of natural forests, wetlands and other communities, PARTICIPATED IN DRAWING UP PROTECTED-AREA DOCUMENTATION, AND INITIATED THE ESTABLISHMENT OF NEW PROTECTED AREAS, and is now devoted to renewing the fund's NATURE CONSERVATION DATABASE. Donations are tax-deductible — it is entered on the list of non-profit associations receiving income tax relief — and with them the fund and its volunteers restore and maintain endangered meadows and damaged wetlands.

trackers.name: Kaitsealuse maa riigile müük — the state MUST buy protected land when the owner asks
trackers.desc: THE RULE, from the agency's own page: land located in a protected area, limited-conservation area, species protection site or containing an individual protected natural object CAN BE SOLD TO THE STATE if the protection regime restricts the intended use of the land to a significant degree. AND THE OBLIGATION, as stated by the ministry: since last August the law provides that IF THE OWNER OF A PROPERTY WITH A SIGNIFICANT NATURE-PROTECTION RESTRICTION WISHES TO SELL THEIR LAND, THE STATE MUST BUY IT. Where the state is obliged to buy restricted land on request, a designation stops being a loss to the owner and becomes an exit — which is the argument to put to a neighbour who fears protection. AND THE TWO ROUTES, side by side: the state and the owner may agree either that the protected property is EXCHANGED FOR ANOTHER PROPERTY BELONGING TO THE STATE — a swap THE OWNER HAS THE RIGHT TO INITIATE by application — or that it is bought outright. Land is bought according to its MARKET VALUE, and purchases are decided in the order in which owners' applications arrive. AND THE HONEST WARNING, from the state's own figures: 735 properties are currently waiting in the purchase queue, some applications going back seven years; at an earlier count 184 applications worth nearly 15.3 MILLION EURO were queued, with the front of the queue in process since 2007. The agency itself calls such waiting justifiably infuriating to landowners and not fair to them.

trackers.name: Erametsakeskus — the private forest centre that tells owners how to sell restricted land
trackers.desc: WHAT IT PUBLISHES FOR OWNERS: THE STATE HAS UNDERTAKEN AN OBLIGATION TO BUY OUT, FROM THE OWNER, LAND WITH SIGNIFICANT NATURE-PROTECTION RESTRICTIONS, IF THE OWNER EXPRESSES THE WISH. To start this process, a PROPOSAL SHOULD BE MADE TO THE ENVIRONMENT AGENCY for the acquisition of the restricted land. A forest-owners' body that tells its members how to make the state buy their land is the friendliest door into that process, and Estonia's bucket already holds the state fund and the private-landowner fund; this is the advice desk between them. AND THE DUTY IT SPELLS OUT, which turns any walker into a protection trigger: if a forest owner OR ANY OTHER PERSON discovers a NEST TREE, they are obliged under the nature conservation act to inform the environment agency WITHIN THREE DAYS AND NIGHTS. Anyone who finds a nest tree can start a protection process with a phone call, and the law requires it. AND THE AUTOMATIC BUFFER IT RECORDS: when new individual natural objects are taken under protection, a limited-management zone is ADDED AUTOMATICALLY WITHIN A RADIUS OF 50 METRES, until the boundaries are specified by protection rules. It also links the nature conservation act, the Natura pages, and an agency presentation on concluding contracts for the protection of valuable habitats.

trackers.name: The restrictions support — payable the moment PROTECTION PROCEEDINGS ARE OPENED, before any designation
trackers.desc: THE PAYMENT AN ESTONIAN OWNER CAN CLAIM, and its timing is the point: the support exists for THE COMPENSATION OF NATURE-PROTECTION RESTRICTIONS ON PRIVATE FOREST AREAS SITUATED OUTSIDE THE NATURA 2000 NETWORK, its purpose being THE PRESERVATION AND IMPROVEMENT OF ECOLOGICAL CONDITION AND THE COMPENSATION TO THE PRIVATE FOREST OWNER OF INCOME NOT RECEIVED BECAUSE OF COMPLIANCE WITH THE RESTRICTIONS. Estonia is joint-smallest bucket in this file. AND THE ELIGIBILITY LINE THAT MATTERS MOST TO A SITE UNDER THREAT: the forest land qualifies if it LIES IN THE LIMITED-USE ZONE of a protected area, conservation area or permanent habitat — OR LIES IN AN AREA IN RESPECT OF WHICH PROCEEDINGS FOR TAKING IT UNDER PROTECTION HAVE BEEN INITIATED within the meaning of a named section of the Nature Conservation Act. Money becomes claimable when the protection procedure is merely opened, not when it is finished — so an owner is not asked to bear the restriction unpaid while the designation grinds on. AND THE THRESHOLD, which is low: the forest land must be AT LEAST 0.3 HECTARES, must be entered in the national nature information system, and the eligible area INCLUDES a road, ditch, firebreak or strip in an electricity-installation protection zone UP TO FOUR METRES WIDE, AND A CLEARING OF UP TO 0.10 HECTARES. Three tenths of a hectare qualifies, which puts this within reach of ordinary smallholdings.

trackers.name: The new contract route — the state PAYS TO PROTECT NATURE OUTSIDE protected areas
trackers.desc: A ROUTE FOR GROUND THAT WILL NEVER BE DESIGNATED, which is most of the land a community fights over: the amendments ENABLE THE STATE TO CONCLUDE A CONTRACT WITH A PRIVATE FOREST OWNER IN ORDER TO PROTECT NATURAL VALUES ALSO OUTSIDE PROTECTED AREAS. THE PROTECTED NATURAL VALUE MUST BE ENTERED IN THE STATE DATABASE. A paid contract to protect a site the state has not designated is the fallback when a designation campaign fails — and the trigger is simply getting the value recorded in the database. The LIST OF NATURAL VALUES, THE BASES FOR CALCULATING THE USE-RIGHT FEE, AND THE CONTENT AND PROCEDURE OF THE CONTRACT are set by ministerial regulation. AND THE COMPENSATION RULES CREATED ALONGSIDE: the amendments CREATE RULES FOR THE PROTECTION OF AREAS DESIGNATED TO COMPENSATE FOR DAMAGE CAUSED TO NATURE. THOSE AREAS ARE DESIGNATED EITHER BY THE ENVIRONMENT BOARD (where a protected natural value is damaged) OR BY THE PREPARER OF THE PLANNING DOCUMENT OR THE APPLICANT FOR THE PERMIT, WHO MUST COMPENSATE THE DAMAGE CAUSED TO NATURE. The permit applicant is the one who must find and secure the compensating ground — a cost and an obligation a community can hold a developer to. AND ONE WARNING WORTH READING BEFORE BUYING: an exception is added that THE STATE AS A RULE DOES NOT ACQUIRE AN IMMOVABLE WHERE THE PERSON ALREADY KNEW AT THE MOMENT OF ACQUISITION THAT IT WAS INTENDED TO BE TAKEN UNDER NATURE PROTECTION.

trackers.name: A published CASE RECORD — who the environmental lawyers represented, and against what
trackers.desc: A CASEBOOK RATHER THAN A MISSION STATEMENT, which lets a community judge whether this body takes its kind of fight: a town council ADOPTED A THEMATIC PLAN PROVIDING FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A LIQUEFIED NATURAL GAS TERMINAL — PORT FACILITIES, A TANK FARM AND OTHER ASSOCIATED STRUCTURES, on a site PARTLY WITHIN THE NATURA 2000 NETWORK AREA. Estonia is among the least-worked buckets in this file. AND WHAT THE LAWYERS DID: the nature fund and the ornithological society CHALLENGED THE THEMATIC PLAN, BECAUSE THEY WERE CONCERNED ABOUT THE IMPACT OF THE PLANNED LNG TERMINAL ON THE SURROUNDING ENVIRONMENT, and the centre REPRESENTED both organisations IN THE COURT DISPUTE OVER BOTH THE THEMATIC PLAN AND THE DETAILED PLAN. The challenge was brought against the PLAN, not the later permit — the earliest stage at which a terminal can be stopped, and the point most communities reach only after it has passed. AND THE OTHER CASE SHAPE RECORDED: the centre also ADVISED THE ORNITHOLOGICAL SOCIETY IN DETAILED PLAN AND MUNICIPAL COMPREHENSIVE PLAN PROCEEDINGS AND IN THE COUNTY GOVERNOR'S SUPERVISORY PROCEEDINGS, ANALYSING AMONG OTHER THINGS WHETHER THE STRATEGIC ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT REPORT AND ITS PROCEDURE COMPLIED WITH LEGISLATION, IN PARTICULAR THE HABITATS DIRECTIVE. A supervisory proceeding before the county governor is a route short of court, and it is used here in parallel with the planning process.

trackers.name: What the environmental law centre is for — watching whether the laws WORK IN PRACTICE
trackers.desc: A BODY WHOSE JOB IS TO CHECK THE LAW AGAINST REALITY, which is a different service from advising on a single case: the centre is AN INDEPENDENT PROFESSIONAL ORGANISATION DEALING WITH ENVIRONMENTAL LAW, WHICH CREATES, GATHERS, MEDIATES AND USES ENVIRONMENTAL-LAW EXPERT KNOWLEDGE IN ORDER TO ADVANCE THE DEVELOPMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL LAW AND TO HELP IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF ENVIRONMENTAL DECISIONS AND LEGISLATION AT DIFFERENT LEVELS, and ITS PRINCIPAL AIM IS TO STUDY AND MONITOR HOW ENVIRONMENTAL LAWS WORK IN PRACTICE. Estonia is among the least-worked buckets in this file. An organisation that monitors whether the laws work is where a community takes the observation that a rule was ignored in its own case — that observation is this body's raw material rather than an inconvenience. AND THE PURPOSES IT NAMES, each of which a local group can point to when asking for help: it acts on THE PUBLIC INTEREST IN HELPING IMPROVE ESTONIA'S ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITION, PREVENTING ABUSES IN THE USE OF NATURE, ADVANCING SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT, AND SUPPORTING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PRINCIPLES OF THE AARHUS CONVENTION IN ESTONIA. Naming the Aarhus Convention as something it exists to implement makes it the body to approach when information is withheld or participation is denied — the two failures this file has recorded most often across the region.

trackers.name: Office of the Data Protection Ombudsman
trackers.desc: Office of the Data Protection Ombudsman — Finland’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Transparency Register (avoimuusrekisteri)
trackers.desc: Finland's national lobbying register, launched 2024 — reports of lobbying to Parliament and ministries. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held.

trackers.name: Finlex
trackers.desc: Official Finnish legal database with legislation and Supreme Court / Supreme Administrative Court case law. · Find here: Finland's official database of legislation and case-law (Finlex).

trackers.name: Suomen luonnonsuojeluliitto — ympäristöjuristi ja piirit
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Finland's national nature-conservation league, which keeps an environmental lawyer on staff and an environmental-law committee, and whose districts appeal permits and win — the Supreme Administrative Court quashed the environmental and water permits for the Sokli mine and returned them wholly for fresh consideration with the Lapland district among the appellants, and the Vaasa administrative court annulled an airfield's environmental permit on noise grounds partly on a district's and a local association's appeal. WHO IT SUITS: anyone facing a mine, quarry, airfield or forestry decision anywhere in Finland — roughly 160 local associations across 15 districts means there is almost certainly one covering your municipality, and the districts, not the national office, carry most casework.

trackers.name: Suomen Luonnonsuojelun Säätiö (Finnish Nature Conservation Foundation)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a Finnish foundation that makes grants from its funds for research, nature study and environmental communication — and, unusually for a grantmaker, BUYS LAND to establish protected areas. WHO IT SUITS: the grant side reads as research- and communication-oriented rather than campaign funding, so pitch the evidence you need gathered rather than the fight itself; the land-purchase side is worth approaching directly if a specific parcel is at risk and a purchase would settle it. HOW IT DIFFERS: most conservation funders will pay for a survey but not for the ground. Domain unverified this session — it is administered from the Suomen luonnonsuojeluliitto office and named on sll.fi, which is where to reach it. Founded 1962 and funded largely by donations, it has given nearly EUR 1.4 million to Finnish nature conservation, currently about EUR 60,000–80,000 a year across roughly 30 projects. Typical grants are EUR 1,000–5,000; larger cost grants run EUR 3,000–5,000 and the board may award 1 or 2 of EUR 5,000–10,000 for especially significant work, with a half-year doctoral working grant at EUR 13,200. THE WINDOW IS NARROW AND ANNUAL: 1 December to 31 January, decided at the spring board meeting at the turn of March–April; the next stated round is 1.12.2026–31.1.2027. An applicant may be an individual, a working group or a registered organisation, so a community group can apply. Grants come from 3 named funds — Itämeri-rahasto (Baltic catchment ecosystems, including NGO Baltic cooperation), Luonnonsuojelurahasto (threatened species and habitat types) and the Rafael Kuusakoski memorial fund — plus general funds. The stated primary criterion is conservation effectiveness. Competition is real: 202 applications for 26 awards in the 2025 round. NOTE: this is the säätiö (foundation), a separate body from Suomen luonnonsuojeluliitto, the membership association at sll.fi.

trackers.name: Finland PRH (company register)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); Finland PRH (company register) — the official register of companies and legal entities in Finland — the primary public record of corporate existence, ownership, directors and filings. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A BENEFICIAL-OWNERSHIP REGISTER: this shows the registered entity, its directors and filings; where a separate beneficial-ownership register exists, use that to reach the real humans behind a shell company.

trackers.name: National Audit Office (VTV)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Finland, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Rovaniemi Court of Appeal
trackers.desc: Rovaniemi Court of Appeal — appellate court (Finland).

trackers.name: Labour Court
trackers.desc: Labour Court — tribunal (Finland).

trackers.name: Finland Register of Companies
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Access restricted to authorities/obliged entities.

trackers.name: Eduskunta – MP Declarations of Interests
trackers.desc: Legislator / public-official financial interest & asset declarations.

trackers.name: Hilma
trackers.desc: Finland's public-procurement notices portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Finland, and for how much.

trackers.name: Finnish Trade Register
trackers.desc: public register that contains information on traders and businesses

trackers.name: Statistics Finland
trackers.desc: Finland's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Finland.

trackers.name: National Non-Discrimination and Equality Tribunal of Finland
trackers.desc: National Non-Discrimination and Equality Tribunal of Finland — tribunal in Finland (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: PRH / Business Information System
trackers.desc: Finland's company register, including beneficial-ownership filings. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find who really owns and controls them; their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: PRH / Business Information System (Finland)
trackers.desc: Finland's official business information system (PRH and Tax Administration). Here you can trace companies, their directors and filings registered in Finland.

trackers.name: National Non-Discrimination and Equality Tribunal of Finland
trackers.desc: National Non-Discrimination and Equality Tribunal of Finland — tribunal (Finland).

trackers.name: Valitusoikeus — your rules are the standing document
trackers.desc: WHO MAY APPEAL A FINNISH ENVIRONMENTAL PERMIT: a registered association or foundation whose purpose is promoting environmental, health or nature protection or the pleasantness of the living environment, and on whose rule-defined area of operation the environmental effects in question appear. BOTH HALVES ARE DRAFTING INSTRUCTIONS: you must be registered (ry), not an informal group; and the area of operation in your own rules determines where you can appeal — so write it to cover the site before there is a dispute. Courts also weigh Aarhus Article 9(2) and its aim of wide access to justice. WHO TO WORK WITH: Suomen luonnonsuojeluliitto has about 150 local associations and 15 district organisations, which bring these appeals themselves and employ environmental lawyers. ITS STRATEGY IS WORTH COPYING: appeal only after careful consideration, where environmental effects were not sufficiently taken into account in the permit or the plan — the point is to make existing regulation actually apply. It reports winning most often on peat extraction permits. WHAT WINS: in the Sokli appeal the grounds were procedural — material relevant to the application was gathered but not publicly notified, so affected people and associations had no real chance to object (YSL 43§); no opinion was sought from the municipality or its health authority (YSL 42§); and fishers and reindeer herders were not heard. Consultation defects are the most reliable ground.

trackers.name: The appeal right is being narrowed — check before you rely on it
trackers.desc: A WARNING TO VERIFY BEFORE PLANNING A CASE. Parliament has moved to restrict associations' right to appeal building projects: associations would be able to appeal building exemption permits, planning-need decisions and so-called clean transition siting permits only where the project is large enough to require a statutory environmental impact assessment. Suomen luonnonsuojeluliitto warns the effect would be that a solar field of under 200 hectares, or 9 wind turbines, or a data centre could be placed in a local forest of recreational or natural value with no possibility for environmental organisations to intervene. Its director notes that courts around the country have overturned unlawful municipal decisions precisely because SLL districts and associations appealed them. CONFIRM THE CURRENT LAW — if the restriction is in force, the association route may be closed for your project size and an affected landowner becomes the necessary appellant instead.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Snowchange Cooperative — buys damaged land on the open market and rewilds it (Finland)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Finnish cooperative that buys peatlands and forests damaged by peat production and intensive forestry, on the open market, and restores them. Its Landscape Rewilding Programme began in 2018 and its own account by 2025 is 8,500 hectares owned outright and land concessions offered over more than 60,000 hectares, across five main catchment areas — with a later figure of 10,000 hectares owned. Over 178 sites, including Sámi sites. THE CASE THAT SHOWS THE WHOLE ROUTE, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL SINGLE EXAMPLE IN THIS FILE: Linnunsuo was a former peat production site responsible for fish kills in the Jukajoki river in 2010 and 2011. Snowchange bought the 110 hectares from Vapo, Finland's largest peat industry company, in April 2017 after a year of negotiation, funded by a €75,000 loan from Rewilding Europe Capital. It became a strict IUCN protected area that November. A second loan of €200,000 in late 2018 paid for a further 72 hectares next door, taking the site to 182. A community bought a damaged site from the company that damaged it, with borrowed money, and had it protected within seven months. WHY IT WORKS WITHOUT DISPLACING PEOPLE: Linnunsuo is co-managed so that a limited harvest of water birds by Selkie hunters continues, and the hunters help control invasive mink and raccoon dog. Its sites are registered as Indigenous and Community Conserved Areas, its stated method is that communities guide the work through collaborative management, that Indigenous women lead decision-making on their own territory, and that no decision is made without the consent of the affected community. Where it does not own, it negotiates land use agreements with private owners on what restoration will happen. WHAT TO BRING IT: drained peatland, a ditched forest, a river catchment damaged by peat extraction or forestry — and ideally one where the damage is documented, because that is what made the Vapo purchase possible. Finland has over five million hectares of drained peatland; this is the organisation that treats that as a supply of buyable sites rather than a loss.

trackers.name: Laji.fi — anyone can request the hidden data, and you can attach a map of the planning area
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Suomen Lajitietokeskus (FinBIF), which assembles observations from many Finnish species databases — from individual enthusiasts, citizen science projects, authorities and collections — and publishes them openly. Records can be entered through Vihko and Mobiilivihko, which take single observations with photographs and fetch place and time automatically. Finland's bucket held a funder, an acquirer and a legal service, and nothing on the record. THE TWO-TIER STRUCTURE, and it is the part that decides whether you find anything: sensitive records are karkeistettu — blurred — according to a list compiled by an authority working group, covering some but not all threatened species, chosen by assessing how much threat disturbance or collecting poses. For blurred records the public portal does not show the exact place, the date, the observer's name or several other fields; in some cases both place and time are coarsened, to 10 km and one year. A closed data store holds the exact, unblurred detail of every observation, browsable by Finnish authorities that have signed an agreement for the authority portal. AND HERE IS THE ROUTE MOST COMMUNITIES WILL NOT KNOW ABOUT: anyone can make a data request (aineistopyyntö) for sensitive data, from the public portal, giving a justified reason — and the owner of each dataset decides case by case. The request system asks the applicant to state the justification, and an applicant can be asked to complete the application by attaching, for example, a map of the planning area (kaavoitusalue). Land-use planning is written into the process as a reason people ask. You can choose to receive the data as a table or via an API for three months or one year. THE LEGAL BASIS TO CITE OR EXPECT: the blurring rests on the Finnish Act on the Openness of Government Activities, section 24, which makes secret documents containing information on threatened animal or plant species or on the protection of valuable natural areas if disclosure would endanger the protection of that species or area. That is the test — endangering protection — so a request aimed at protecting the site is arguing with the grain of the exemption, not against it.

trackers.name: Kunta- ja Järjestö-Helmi — 95 per cent if volunteers do the work (paused, read on)
trackers.desc: STATUS FIRST, BECAUSE IT MATTERS: there was no application round in 2025 and one is probably not being held in 2026–2027 either. The scheme is filed anyway because the Helmi programme runs to 2030, rounds are opened by ministry decision as need arises, and the terms below are the clearest statement of what a Finnish volunteer group can be paid for. THE CLAUSE THAT IS UNIQUE IN THIS SWEEP: the standard grant share can be raised — for special reasons up to 95 per cent — and the guidance names as a justification the project's measures being carried out to a significant extent by voluntary work, such as talkoot organised by associations. Significant natural values requiring urgent management also count. Volunteer labour raises the grant rate rather than reducing it. No other fund in twenty-eight says so. WHO MAY APPLY: municipalities, joint municipal authorities and other municipally owned actors, associations and foundations, water cooperatives, and joint water area shareholders' collectives. Joint projects are allowed, the grant going to a lead applicant who administers on everyone's behalf — though all participants must meet the requirements. WHAT IT PAYS FOR, INCLUDING THE PAPERWORK: concrete restoration, repair and nature management — and projects may include inventories, plans and permit processes that firmly support the management measures, where those measures are also carried out in the project or have other demonstrable funding and timetable. Purchased services, equipment and supplies are eligible. THE LIMITS, RECORDED PLAINLY: the grant is directed primarily at land owned by municipalities; sites on other owners' land are possible but need arrangements securing the management and its continuation. In forested habitats the grant is given only on protected areas. Built stormwater wetlands are excluded, as is overlap with agri-environment contract obligations. AND THE PROGRAMME BEHIND IT: Helmi 2021–2030 protects and restores mires, birdwaters, traditional biotopes, forest habitats and small waters, and its measures rest on landowners' voluntariness. One round drew 70 applications; 42 were funded with 2.35 million euro.

trackers.name: ymparistolaki.fi — a Finnish firm specialised in environmental and property law since 1994
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: a specialised Finnish asianajotoimisto with experience in environmental and real property law at national and EU level, acting for companies, public bodies and private property owners, providing legal services since 1994. THE SERVICE LIST, WHICH READS LIKE A COMMUNITY'S PROBLEM SET: kaavakonsultointi (plan consultancy), KAAVAVALITUKSET (appeals against plans), rakennusluvat, poikkeusluvat (exemption permits), and the legal problems of shoreline building; permit applications and valitusasiat — appeal matters — and compensation questions relating to permits and damage situations; plus compensation for environmental damage, and soil and groundwater remediation liabilities. Finland had a Vilnius-style legal clinic route and the Laji.fi data body but no named practitioner; this is one, and appeals against plans is its second listed service. WHY THAT MATTERS IN FINLAND SPECIFICALLY: the plan — maakunta-, yleis- or asemakaava — is where land use is settled, and this firm sells consultancy on the plan as well as litigation against it.

trackers.name: Finnish planning-appeal reality — only 6–10 per cent of appeals change anything
trackers.desc: THE NUMBER A COMMUNITY SHOULD KNOW BEFORE SPENDING MONEY: a Finnish firm publishes that, on statistical evidence, appeals to the administrative court succeed poorly — generally only about 6 to 10 per cent of hallinto-oikeus appeals lead to changes, with wide case-by-case variation. AND THE CONCLUSION IT DRAWS, WHICH IS THE ADVICE: because of both the real possibility of influence and the risks inherent in the chances of an appeal succeeding, it is especially important to take part in the planning process at its EARLY STAGE, when the possibilities of influence are better. Where a maakunta-, yleis- or asemakaava is being drawn up over your land, follow its preparation closely and try to affect its content at the earliest possible preparation phase. This file has recorded Iceland's scoping-stage comment window and Czechia's published assessment of municipal plans. Finland supplies the arithmetic for why they matter: the appeal at the end fails nine times in ten. PRACTICAL, from other Finnish firms: building permit matters often cause conflicting views with neighbours and are frequently appealed to the administrative court; environment and land-use appeals are heard in the maaoikeus and hallinto-oikeus; and one firm's plain advice is that if the matter is complex or the other side has hired a lawyer, you should get one too.

trackers.name: METSO — the owner offers, keeps the deed, and the compensation is tax free
trackers.desc: WHAT TO PUT IN FRONT OF A FINNISH LANDOWNER: under the METSO programme the forest owner may apply to have their forest protected, receives a TAX-FREE COMPENSATION, and chooses the option that suits them. Permanent protection can be done by establishing a PRIVATE protected area, in which case the area REMAINS IN THE OWNER'S OWNERSHIP; the alternative is to sell the area to the State. Temporary protection runs as a protection agreement of up to 20 years, or a 10-year environmental support agreement. AND THE STEPS, which a community can walk an owner through: anyone interested can contact their own regional centre, the forest centre or other forestry actors, who pass applications on; an expert establishes the site's natural values and its suitability for the programme; and if accepted, the centre makes an offer of protection to the owner. THE SCALE AND THE HONEST PROPORTION: the target is 96,000 hectares offered voluntarily by landowners, plus 82,000 hectares of commercial forest nature sites secured through environmental support and nature management projects — but Finland has 22.8 million hectares of forest, so that is only a little over 0.4 per cent. A WORKED COMPENSATION EXAMPLE: for permanent protection where the owner keeps the land, the compensation in one calculation was a rauhoituskorvaus of about 40,600 euro — and when a private protected area is established the value of the ground itself is not compensated, only the loss. On METSO sites the timber value is set as an average over three years, to level out fluctuations in stumpage prices.

trackers.name: Establishing a Finnish protected area — and the entry in the property register that makes it permanent
trackers.desc: WHO CAN START IT: a protected area can be established either on the LANDOWNER'S INITIATIVE OR ON THE AUTHORITY'S, and the decision is taken by the regional centre. The owner may apply for a protected area on land they own, or give consent to a proposal made by the authority. Almost 7,800 nature protection areas already exist on private land. THE GROUNDS ON WHICH ONE CAN BE ESTABLISHED — which is the checklist for a site: an endangered, rare or declining species, community, habitat type or ecosystem; a breeding or resting place of a species requiring strict protection; the need to maintain or achieve favourable conservation status; special significance for the ability of habitat types or species TO ADAPT TO THE EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE; or being otherwise so representative or typical as to warrant it. AND THE TWO FACTS THAT MAKE IT STICK: the decision establishing a nature protection area is PERMANENT, and an entry is made in the PROPERTY REGISTER — so it binds the land, not the owner. In protection by agreement land ownership does not change. The State may alternatively buy land areas at market price, and in both cases possibilities for recreational use of the area generally remain unchanged. ONE LIMIT, RECORDED PLAINLY: the decision may not be issued unless the owner and the centre have agreed the protection rules and the compensation — except where the area is already inside a government-approved protection programme, in which case the centre may act without the owner's application or consent.

trackers.name: Luonnonperintösäätiö — it publishes its PURCHASE CRITERIA, and most offers come from owners
trackers.desc: WHAT IT BUYS, in its own published criteria, so you can judge your site before writing: it seeks forest areas that are NOT actively managed commercial forest but have significance for diversity protection in one way or another; areas should preferably be AT LEAST 4–5 HECTARES; the regional emphasis is the southern half of the country but proposals are worth making from the whole of Finland — THE FURTHER NORTH, THE MORE NATURAL THE AREA MUST BE. Besides forests it has acquired mires, wetlands, small waters, islands, rock outcrops and traditional environments. AND THE LINE THAT MATTERS MOST TO AN OWNER: a large part of the forest areas bought now come to our knowledge THROUGH CONTACTS MADE BY THE FOREST OWNERS THEMSELVES. The owner writes to them, not the other way round. IT BUYS THE LAND OUTRIGHT AND LOCKS IT: founded in 1995 with a fisherman-writer's donated savings, it acquires areas of significant natural value into its OWNERSHIP with donated funds and secures for them PERMANENT protection under the nature conservation act, buying forests together with their ground — by purchase, BY EXCHANGE, or through donations. It holds over 200 conservation areas totalling more than 7,000 hectares. AND WHAT IT WILL TAKE THAT OTHERS WON'T: partly commercial-forest areas are acceptable if there are natural values there — we have also bought old commercial forests; they return to old-growth fairly quickly — including forests left with little management by estates of deceased owners.

trackers.name: The regional and specialist Finnish land foundations — PLUPS, the wildlife fund, and the volunteers
trackers.desc: WHY A REGIONAL ONE MATTERS: PLUPS is a lake-region nature heritage foundation that ACCEPTS DONATIONS FROM PRIVATE INDIVIDUALS AND COMPANIES and has assembled holdings piece by piece — two parcels bringing its area at one mire to about 150 hectares, a 73-hectare forest bought in one December, and a 3.5-hectare forest and farm DONATED in another village. AND THE DETAIL WORTH COPYING ANYWHERE: a local branch of the national conservation association DONATED a small island property to the foundation for conservation purposes. One organisation giving land to another that can hold it permanently is a move a local group with a parcel should know about. Its donation account is published openly. TWO MORE FINNISH BODIES ON THE SAME PAGE OF THE PICTURE: a national conservation foundation that owns protected areas acquired IN ACCORDANCE WITH DONORS' WISHES — including some 420 hectares of valuable mire and forest across two municipalities and a 21-hectare area of mostly old forest — and which runs a PREDATOR PROTECTION FUND supporting the protection of predators and their habitats by research, surveys, training, communication, POLITICS AND LAW. AND THE VOLUNTEER ARM: a friends-of-old-growth association concentrates on VOLUNTEER HELP and organising activity such as work parties and excursions on the foundation's protected areas, with joint campaigns run since 2008 with a regional ornithological society and a conservation district.

trackers.name: Luonnonperintösäätiö — over 200 reserves and 7,000 hectares, bought with donations
trackers.desc: WHAT IT HOLDS AND HOW IT GOT IT: a foundation established in 1995 which ACQUIRES INTO ITS OWNERSHIP, WITH DONATED FUNDS, AREAS OF SIGNIFICANT NATURAL VALUE, AND SECURES FOR THEM PERMANENT PROTECTION UNDER THE NATURE CONSERVATION ACT. It has acquired MORE THAN 200 NATURE PROTECTION AREAS, TOTALLING OVER 7,000 HECTARES. Two hundred separate reserves assembled by donation is the largest privately built protected network in this file. AND THE THREE ROUTES BY WHICH IT TAKES LAND: the foundation acquires forests BY BUYING, BY EXCHANGING, OR THROUGH DONATIONS — and it protects forests as untouched as possible from different parts of Finland, with most areas in the south but, in recent years, acquisitions in the north as well. AND THE DOUBLE LOCK, which is the detail worth carrying: in the foundation the forests are IN DOUBLE SAFETY, since they are protected BY THE NATURE CONSERVATION ACT AND BY THE FOUNDATIONS ACT. Land held by a foundation is protected twice over — by conservation law and by the law governing what a foundation may do with its assets — which is why a foundation is a safer holder than an association. Named older and newer reserves are listed individually, some as small as 7 hectares, one later expanded from 13 to 17.5 hectares.

trackers.name: Suomi.fi on appealing a decision — the court fee is WAIVED if you win, and legal aid removes it
trackers.desc: THE COST RULE THAT DECIDES WHETHER A FINNISH COMMUNITY CAN AFFORD TO APPEAL: a court fee is charged on most administrative court decisions, and its size is set annually. IF THE ADMINISTRATIVE COURT CHANGES THE DECISION IN THE APPELLANT'S FAVOUR, THE COURT FEE IS NOT CHARGED. And separately: if a person has received public legal aid, they do not have to pay the administrative court's handling fee. Winning costs nothing, and being poor costs nothing — which removes the fee objection from most Finnish planning appeals. AND WHERE TO GET HELP: if you need more detailed help you can buy it from private advocates or law firms. IF YOU HAVE LITTLE MEANS, YOU MAY HAVE THE RIGHT TO HELP FROM A LEGAL AID OFFICE. AND THE WARNING ABOUT WHAT CANNOT BE APPEALED, which saves a wasted filing: preparatory or implementing decisions cannot be appealed — for example PREPARATORY DECISIONS CONCERNING THE PLANNING OF A MUNICIPALITY'S AREA. The preparatory stage of a plan is not appealable, so a community must object within the process rather than wait to litigate it. The page adds that the decision document usually states at its end HOW AND TO WHOM the decision may be appealed, and that almost all decisions of municipal, wellbeing-region and state authorities can be appealed.

trackers.name: The Finnish hallintopakko demand — ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATIONS can force an inspection
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE WHEN A COMPANY IS BREAKING THE RULES: when a private person wants to make another private operator comply with its environmental obligations, IT IS USUALLY EASIEST TO CONTACT THE COMPETENT MUNICIPAL OR STATE AUTHORITY TO MAKE A DEMAND FOR ADMINISTRATIVE ENFORCEMENT (hallintopakko). AND WHY THAT IS THE ROUTE RATHER THAN A CHOICE: private supervision and enforcement of public-law obligations IS NOT POSSIBLE — private persons cannot directly demand in court that another private operator answer for breaches of public-law environmental obligations. In Finland a community cannot sue the polluter directly; it must make the regulator act — which changes where the effort goes. AND WHO MAY START ONE: the right to initiate an enforcement matter depends on the substantive law, but under the Environmental Protection Act it belongs to the parties concerned, ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATIONS, certain municipal and state authorities, AND THE SÁMI PARLIAMENT. An environmental organisation has standing to demand enforcement even where an individual might not, which is a reason to route a complaint through one. And the teeth: the supervisory authority can generally reinforce its order with A CONDITIONAL FINE, or with the threat that the omitted measure WILL BE CARRIED OUT AT THE DEFAULTER'S EXPENSE. Anyone at all may contact the authority and report possible breaches.

trackers.name: What the Finnish forest foundation will accept — INCLUDING former commercial forest
