It is a facilitator and expert body that works with administrations, so bring it analysis, planning input and stakeholder process — not a confrontation.

trackers.name: Latvijas Zaļā kustība — gives consultations and joins specific problem cases
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Latvian Green Movement, founded 2004 on the base of eight branches of the former Environmental Protection Club, an open and democratic membership organisation bringing together environmental activists, volunteers and experts who want to work actively to improve environmental quality and to prevent criminal offences against the environment. Over 100 individual members and five regional groups. Latvia had no legal or casework ally in this file. THE SERVICE THAT MATTERS, in its own words: defence of the public interest and promotion of effective participation by giving consultations and becoming involved in resolving specific problem situations relating to urban environment, construction, protective zones (aizsargjoslas), waste management and environmental impact assessment. That is casework, named as such, for exactly the kinds of dispute this file exists to serve. AND AT LOCAL LEVEL IT DOES THE REST: active participation in policy planning processes on city development planning and environmental impact assessment, the fight against illegal construction and criminal offences against the environment, and involving local residents in environmental protection activities. It also runs coastal dune protection through public control and involvement in territorial planning — useful in a country whose coast is its most contested ground. IT HAS EXPERTS ON CALL: it has established an Expert Council of specialists in their fields who give it qualitative advice and help it plan its activities. For a community that needs a specialist opinion, that council is the reason to approach this organisation rather than a campaign group. ITS STANDING: member of the Environmental Advisory Council, which brings together 20 national environmental NGOs, represented on the Green Investment Scheme advisory board and other advisory bodies, a CEE Bankwatch Network member group, and part of a consortium coordinating NGO participation in EU funds planning. Facebook: ZalaKustiba.

trackers.name: Vides konsultatīvā padome — 20 organisations elected annually, and the list is published
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Environmental Consultative Council, established under Cabinet regulation no. 209 of 27 March 2007, a consultative coordinating institution whose purpose is to promote public participation in the development and implementation of environmental policy, made up of 20 associations and foundations whose aim is environmental protection. Though it formally sits under the environment ministry, its own members describe it as an independent association of non-governmental organisations and a long-standing partner of the ministry and other state institutions in ensuring environmental protection interests are observed on society's behalf. WHY IT IS THE BEST DIRECTORY LATVIA HAS: the composition changes every year through elections, and the ministry publishes the elected list by name of organisation and representative. One published round named Baltijas krasti, Baltijas Vides Forums, the Biḱernieki forest protection society, the Ecodesign competence centre, the Ḳemeri National Park foundation, the Latvian Waste Management Association, the Latvian Botanists' Society, Latvijas Dabas fonds, the Latvian natural resources monitoring group, the Latvian Anglers' Association, the Latvian Ornithological Society, Pasaules dabas fonds, Teiči Nature Foundation, Vides aizsardzības klubs, Vides fakti, Zaļā brīvība, Zero Waste Latvija and a district development society. That is a current, state-published, name-by-name roll of Latvia's active environmental sector. THE FILTER THAT TELLS YOU WHAT COUNTS: one organisation was not advanced to the elections because the aims stated in its statutes did not meet the requirements of section 14, first paragraph, of the Environmental Protection Law. Latvia therefore has a published statutory test for what an environmental organisation is — and a group drafting its own statutes should read that section before filing them. AND THE SCALE OF THE SECTOR BEHIND IT: as at 1 January 2016, 129 associations and foundations working in environmental protection held public benefit organisation status, and that is only part of all environmental NGOs in the country. Organisations not elected to the council are expressly invited to keep taking part in the ministry's policy-making.

trackers.name: Emro — contests and appeals the būvvalde's administrative acts
trackers.desc: WHAT THEY DO, in their own words: prepare submissions to the būvvalde — the building authority — and other institutions, advise on building permits, acceptance of a construction proposal and its conditions, and contest and appeal the administrative acts of the būvvalde and other institutions. They represent clients in state and municipal institutions and in courts of all instances in civil and administrative proceedings. HOW THEY SAY THEY START, which is what a community needs from a first meeting: with an assessment of the situation and a clear opinion on the client's legal position and options, then a practical plan of action — whether that is contesting an institution's decision or representation in a dispute. Filed because contesting the būvvalde's administrative act is precisely the step the Supreme Court's digest identifies as the one moment a third party can act.

trackers.name: NVO fonds — Latvia's largest civil-society programme, with a micro tier
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Sabiedrības integrācijas fonds runs the largest programme supporting non-governmental organisations in Latvia, aimed at strengthening sustainable civil society development and democracy. In one year the available funding approached 2 million EUR, and the ceilings were set at up to 10,000 EUR for micro-projects and up to 33,000 EUR for macro-projects. WHY IT IS FILED FOR A NATURE CAMPAIGN: the fund records that its supported projects have comparatively often touched on nature, environment, climate and animal protection alongside civil society development, and that it has deliberately given NGOs freer hands in choosing project topics. The number of supported organisations rose from 31 to 87 across four years, so that funding reaches as wide a circle of organisations as possible rather than concentrating in a few. A new group's chances here are better than at a specialist environmental fund. AND A SEPARATE PROGRAMME WORTH KNOWING: the same fund runs co-financing for NGO participation in projects financed by foreign funds — in one round nearly 287,000 EUR across ten applications, with environmental protection among the listed eligible fields. That is the 20 per cent an international grant will demand of you.

trackers.name: Pasaules dabas fonds — it founded a nature park, and it fought the small hydro dams
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a Latvian-registered sabiedriskā labuma organizācija — public benefit organisation — operating since November 1991 and registered in 2005 as the NODIBINĀJUMS 'Pasaules dabas fonds'. Latvia's bucket held Latvijas Dabas fonds but no second land-holding body; a nodibinājums is the Latvian foundation form, which can hold property. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY DONE ON THE GROUND: working with institutions, NGOs and businesses it has created forest management and wetland DEMONSTRATION TERRITORIES; FOUNDED THE 'PAPE' NATURE PARK; and returned large herbivores to Latvia — wild horses, aurochs and bison. An organisation that has founded a nature park is one a community can ask to do it again. AND THE CAMPAIGN THAT MATCHES A DEVELOPMENT FIGHT: it has run river protection measures AGAINST THE CONSTRUCTION OF SMALL HYDROPOWER PLANTS, alongside salmon, Baltic Sea and forest protection campaigns, work to eradicate illegal use of timber resources, and development of FSC certification. Small hydro is the classic small-scale development that a village cannot fight alone, and this is a national body with a record of doing so. HOW TO USE IT: it runs education programmes for FOREST OWNERS — useful where the person to persuade is the landowner — takes volunteers into national and international conservation campaigns, and states that donations go to forest, sea and freshwater protection projects and to restoring the large herbivore populations in Pape nature park.

trackers.name: Latvijas zemes fonds — the state land fund that buys, and its reverse-lease option
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the state development finance institution operates a land fund that BUYS agricultural land, and buys land WITH LEASE AND REPURCHASE RIGHTS — reverśā noma, reverse lease — as well as leasing and selling land, with an e-auction process and a line for land for young farmers. WHY A COMMUNITY SHOULD KNOW IT: this file has recorded state land banks as a THREAT elsewhere — a Portuguese association warned its country's new Banco de Terras could hand public agricultural and forest land to the pulp industry by direct award. The same institution read the other way is a buyer of last resort: where an owner must sell and the alternative is a developer, a state fund that purchases with a repurchase right keeps the land in agricultural use and keeps a route back. Reverse lease is the mechanism to name: the owner sells, continues to farm under lease, and retains the right to buy back. It is the closest thing in this file to a pause button on a distressed sale. HONEST NOTE: this is an agricultural land instrument, not a conservation one. It will not protect habitat by itself — but it can stop the parcel reaching a developer while a protection route is arranged.

trackers.name: Mikroliegumi — ANY PERSON can apply to protect 0.1 to 30 hectares, and it is far quicker
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE, AND IT IS THE FASTEST DESIGNATION RECORDED ANYWHERE IN THIS FILE: a person submitting the first part of the application and inventory form for a specially protected species or biotope micro-reserve MAY ATTACH A SECOND PART PREPARED BY AN EXPERT, containing the information on the proposed territory. Applications for micro-reserves on non-forest land go to the nature conservation agency, which then informs the municipality and the landowner or lawful possessor in writing. Compared with a specially protected nature territory, creating a micro-reserve is MUCH SIMPLER AND FASTER, and they run 0.1 to 30 hectares — bird micro-reserves with their buffer zone reaching up to 500. Latvia had 2,655 micro-reserves covering 45,789 hectares, about 0.7 per cent of the country. WHO WRITES THE OPINION: the expert giving the opinion must be CERTIFIED under the 2010 regulation, and the register of certified experts is published on the agency's own website — so you can find and hire one. The decision then includes the individual protection and use requirements THAT THE CERTIFIED EXPERT SPECIFIED IN THE OPINION. AND WHO MANAGES IT AFTERWARDS: the landowner, or failing that the tenant, lawful possessor, a person hired by them, THE MUNICIPALITY, or the agency, according to the expert's opinion. The species lists in the annexes cover birds, mammals, amphibians, reptiles, invertebrates, fish, vascular plants, mosses, algae, lichens and fungi. Anyone can check whether a micro-reserve exists on a property through the public nature data system.

trackers.name: The Latvian compensation fight — 160 euro a hectare, an 83 per cent success rate, and the buy-back
trackers.desc: WHAT THE OWNER GETS, and it is the number that decides whether they cooperate: a landowner is entitled to apply for an annual compensation of 160 EURO PER HECTARE PER YEAR for the economic restrictions a micro-reserve imposes. And there is a second route: to request compensation in the form of LAND BUY-BACK, the owner or heir submits the application form under the 2013 regulation to the nature conservation agency, which decides whether the request is justified, sets the land price under the law on alienation of property needed for public purposes, and if the owner agrees prepares the papers for a Cabinet order authorising the buy-back. The state can be asked to buy the restricted land outright. THE EFFECTIVENESS FIGURE WORTH QUOTING: a species protection plan found micro-reserve creation 83 per cent effective — in 83 cases out of 100 the bird continues to nest there after the micro-reserve is made, and builds new nests. AND THE CONFLICT, RECORDED HONESTLY BECAUSE A COMMUNITY WILL MEET IT: forest owners' representatives and the national nature fund BOTH AGREE THE COMPENSATION IS INSUFFICIENT; a forest owners' association petitioned the government to halt the creation of new protected territories and micro-reserves until a fair compensation system exists, objecting that proposals are prepared without informing the landowner, who learns of the decision only after the Cabinet has taken it. The fund's own ornithologist warns that while compensation is unresolved there will be continuous tension and conflict situations that provoke actions incompatible with nature protection.

trackers.name: Atlācis un Partneri — a bar-registered practice listing VIDES TIESĪBAS and būvniecības tiesības
trackers.desc: WHY THIS ONE: its published practice areas begin with VIDES TIESĪBAS — environmental law — alongside BŪVNIECĪBAS TIESĪBAS (construction law), administrative law and administrative offence cases, LIETU TIESĪBAS (property law), and public procurement. Latvia had 22 filed entries and two legal resources; this is a bar-registered practice naming environmental law first. AND THE SERVICES THAT MATTER TO A RESIDENTS' GROUP, in its own list: consultations and the provision of legal assistance; REPRESENTATION OF THE CLIENT'S INTERESTS; preparation of OPINIONS; and LEGAL ASSISTANCE AND REPRESENTATION IN THE ADMINISTRATIVE PROCESS BOTH BEFORE THE AUTHORITY AND IN COURT — plus representation before the CONSTITUTIONAL COURT. Representation at the authority stage, before anything reaches a courtroom, is the cheap half of the fight, and it is listed as a distinct service. A CONFLICT NOTE, RECORDED PLAINLY: the same firm offers legal assistance both to construction clients in disputes with contractors AND to contractors in disputes with clients, subcontractors and general contractors, and its lawyers have broad experience with FIDIC conditions. Ask whose side it usually takes. Note also that the site records two partners whose practice was suspended by decision of the Latvian Council of Sworn Advocates in 2024 — check the current bar roll before instructing.

trackers.name: Latvian administrative-law practices — and the free consultation week every March
trackers.desc: WHEN TO CALL, in a practice's own words: if you want to CONTEST a decision of a state or municipal institution; if the institution's action causes losses or infringes your rights; if you need help preparing or understanding administrative acts; IF CONFLICTS ARISE WITH STATE ADMINISTRATION BODIES; or if you need legal representation in the administrative courts. AND THE PROBLEM IT NAMES FIRST AMONG THE COMMONEST: CONFLICTS WITH CONSTRUCTION AUTHORITIES OVER BUILDING PERMITS, alongside contesting administrative penalties, wrongly applied taxes or charges, complaints about public procurement, and data protection breaches by state bodies. It also notes that many people have difficulty understanding or accepting decisions taken by state or municipal institutions — which is the honest starting point. AND THE FREE WEEK NOBODY ADVERTISES TO OUTSIDERS: another Latvian practice records that traditionally, during Advocacy Days in March, residents can receive FREE LEGAL CONSULTATIONS in various branches of law. A national free-advice week is the cheapest legal opinion a community will ever get — and it is worth timing a question to it. That firm also works in cooperation with partner law offices across Europe and worldwide, and says clients hire it when a non-standard solution is needed because of the complexity or specificity of the problem.

trackers.name: Latvijas vides aizsardzības fonds — the state environment fund, and it names NGOs as applicants
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a body of state budget funds for implementing environmental protection measures and projects, whose purpose is to promote sustainable development so as to secure the inhabitants' RIGHT TO LIVE IN A QUALITY ENVIRONMENT, and to ensure sufficient measures for the CONSERVATION OF BIOLOGICAL DIVERSITY AND THE PROTECTION OF ECOSYSTEMS. Latvia had 24 filed entries and three funders. THE MONEY AND WHO GETS IT: the environmental projects sub-programme runs at indicatively 2,070,323 EURO EACH YEAR; one named competition for cooperation projects had 850,000 euro available with a MAXIMUM OF 60,000 EURO PER PROJECT and was announced with NGOs INVITED TO SUBMIT. A recurring state fund that names non-governmental organisations among its applicants is the first door for a Latvian group, and its published competition rules and annexes sit on the administration's own page. AND WHAT IT PAYS FOR BESIDES PRACTICAL WORK: DATA ACQUISITION, ANALYSIS AND DIGITISATION for environmental policy formation, implementation and evaluation, and informative and educational measures aimed at SPECIFIC TARGET GROUPS about compliance with environmental requirements — alongside practical activities and multisectoral environmental protection projects OF NATIONAL SIGNIFICANCE.

trackers.name: The Vides konsultatīvā padome — twenty named environmental organisations in one statutory council
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the ENVIRONMENTAL CONSULTATIVE COUNCIL, and its membership is published in full — five FOUNDATIONS (the nature fund, an environmental education fund, the WWF affiliate, A NATIONAL PARK FOUNDATION and a named reserve foundation) and fifteen ASSOCIATIONS (the ornithological society, an environmental facts body, THE ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION CLUB, the anglers' association, a lakes association, a green freedom body, an ecodesign centre, THE BOTANISTS' SOCIETY, a waste management association, a coasts body, a zero waste body, an environmental management association, THE PERMACULTURE SOCIETY, a corporate sustainability institute and a Baltic environmental forum). Latvia had 25 filed entries. Twenty named organisations sitting in one statutory council is twenty doors, and the list tells a community which specialist to write to. The presence of a national park foundation and a single-reserve foundation shows Latvia has bodies attached to individual sites. AND THE STANDING ALLIANCE INSIDE IT: a named barometer project is run by Latvia's most influential environmental non-governmental organisations — the ornithological society, the nature fund, the green freedom body, the organic farming association and the WWF affiliate, who together address political parties before parliamentary elections. Where five organisations already write jointly to the parties, a local campaign has a ready-made coalition to join.

trackers.name: Latvijas Ornitoloģijas biedrība — project managers with mobile numbers, and a citizen-participation fund
trackers.desc: WHAT ITS PROJECT PAGE GIVES YOU, and it is unusually direct: for each project it publishes the period, THE IMPLEMENTER, THE FINANCER, THE PLACE, AND A NAMED PROJECT MANAGER WITH AN EMAIL ADDRESS AND A MOBILE TELEPHONE NUMBER. A named project manager with a mobile number, listed per project, means a community writes to the person who actually does that work rather than to a general inbox. AND THE PROJECT THAT MATTERS MOST TO A COMMUNITY: one funded by THE ACTIVE CITIZENS FUND with the aim of ensuring the participation of the society AND OF THE WIDER PUBLIC IN STRATEGICALLY IMPORTANT DECISIONS regarding nature protection and the sustainable management of natural resources. A national NGO funded specifically to get the public into strategic nature decisions is an ally with a mandate, not just an opinion. AND WHAT ELSE IT DOES ON THE GROUND: a project financed by the state environmental protection fund AND DONORS, carried out ON LANDS IN THE POSSESSION OF THE NATURE CONSERVATION AGENCY, to implement a species protection plan by placing ARTIFICIAL NESTING SITES for an owl, aiming for more than two fledged young per successful nest. Its registered address and number are public.

trackers.name: Kompensācijas — the buy-back and the annual payment, from the agency that runs both
trackers.desc: THE TWO THINGS AN OWNER CAN ASK FOR, on one agency page. First, the land owner can DEMAND THE BUY-BACK OF THE LAND if the property is UNDEVELOPED and lies in a nature reserve, or in the reserve zone, STRICT REGIME ZONE or REGULATED REGIME ZONE of a specially protected nature area. Where an owner can demand that the state buy restricted land, the designation carries its own way out — the same shape recorded in Estonia this session. SECOND, THE ANNUAL PAYMENT: compensation in the form of an ANNUAL SUPPORT PAYMENT for restrictions on economic activity can be applied for by a land owner whose property lies in a specially protected nature area or a MICRORESERVE that is not a Natura 2000 area, or in a microreserve outside Natura where the owner's area in the microreserve is NOT LESS THAN 0.1 HECTARE. A tenth of a hectare is the floor — which means a very small protected patch still carries a yearly payment to the person who keeps it. AND WHAT THE PAYMENT COVERS: agricultural restrictions including where PLOUGHING AND CULTIVATION ARE PROHIBITED and where ALL TYPES OF ECONOMIC ACTIVITY ARE PROHIBITED. The service is free of charge, requested by submitting an application to the agency under a numbered Cabinet regulation.

trackers.name: The Latvijas zemes fonds in practice — what it buys, and the parcels it turns down
trackers.desc: WHEN THE STATE LAND FUND IS THE BUYER OF LAST RESORT, in a fund manager's own words: CLIENTS CHOOSE TO SELL LAND TO THE LAND FUND WHEN THEY CANNOT FIND ANOTHER BUYER FOR THEMSELVES. The fund has operated since JULY 2015 and BUYS REAL PROPERTY THROUGHOUT THE WHOLE TERRITORY OF LATVIA. A public buyer that exists precisely for land nobody else will take is the one to point an owner at when a developer is the only other offer on the table. AND THE LIMIT, stated honestly and worth knowing before anyone gets their hopes up: in one region the fields are not consolidated — there are SCRUB, FORESTS, DITCHES AND ABANDONED BUILDINGS, and the areas offered to the Land Fund are often small. IF A PERSON WANTS TO SELL A THREE-HECTARE PLOT AROUND THEIR HOUSE, THE LAND FUND DOES NOT BUY SUCH PROPERTIES. Small house plots are refused; consolidated farmland is what it takes — so this is a route for a field, not a garden. AND WHAT THE SELLER KEEPS: a named farmer leasing 31.9 HECTARES from the fund values that THE LAND REMAINS WITH THE STATE, WITH THE POSSIBILITY FOR THE FARMER AS TENANT TO BUY IT BACK LATER IF NEEDED, and that IT HAS NOT GONE TO SPECULATORS.

trackers.name: Latvijas Dabas fonds — its FIVE PROGRAMMES, and the one that plans protected territories
trackers.desc: WHAT LATVIA'S LARGEST CONSERVATION BODY ACTUALLY DOES, broken into the programmes a community can ask for by name. It is a NON-GOVERNMENTAL nature protection organisation FOUNDED IN 1990 with the aim of preserving the diversity of Latvia's nature, and to that end it WORKS ON THE PRACTICAL PROVISION OF NATURE PROTECTION, DRAWING UP PROTECTION PROJECTS FOR RARE AND THREATENED SPECIES AND FOR SPECIALLY PROTECTED NATURE TERRITORIES, ATTRACTING THE FINANCING AND ENSURING ITS REALISATION. Drawing up the protection project AND raising the money for it are named as the same body's work — which is the pairing a community usually has to assemble from two places. AND THE PROGRAMME THAT MATTERS MOST TO A SITE UNDER THREAT: the FIFTH PROGRAMME is SPECIALLY PROTECTED NATURE TERRITORIES, whose main aim is TO CARRY OUT THE PLANNING AND MANAGEMENT OF SPECIALLY PROTECTED NATURE TERRITORIES AND TO INVOLVE SOCIETY IN THOSE ACTIVITIES. The fourth covers PROTECTED SPECIES AND BIOTOPES, aiming at FAVOURABLE PROTECTION STATUS for threatened biotopes and species; the third covers BIODIVERSITY AND ECOSYSTEMS IN FORESTS, THE AGRICULTURAL LANDSCAPE, THE COAST, BOGS AND FRESH WATERS. AND THE POLITICAL SIDE, stated plainly: it PARTICIPATES IN THE FORMATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY, DIRECTLY LOBBYING THE LEGISLATIVE PROCESS. Its office address is published. An organisation that says it lobbies legislation is one that can carry a local case upward.

trackers.name: Cilvēktiesību gids — a guide to WHICH Latvian organisation can help, and with what
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY BUILT ROUND THE QUESTION A COMMUNITY ACTUALLY ASKS: THIS GUIDE WILL INTRODUCE YOU TO VARIOUS ORGANISATIONS THAT WORK IN THE FIELD OF HUMAN RIGHTS IN LATVIA, AND WILL EXPLAIN WHAT HELP THESE ORGANISATIONS CAN GIVE YOU IN CASES WHERE IT IS POSSIBLE THAT YOUR HUMAN RIGHTS HAVE BEEN INFRINGED. Latvia is joint-smallest bucket in this file. A directory that says what each body can do, rather than only listing names, is the difference between a phone list and a route — and it tells a person which door to try first. AND WHAT IT SAYS THOSE BODIES OFFER: MOST ORGANISATIONS DEALING WITH HUMAN RIGHTS QUESTIONS ARE BASED ON PRIVATE INITIATIVE. THEY USUALLY SPECIALISE IN SOME PARTICULAR FIELD, IN ORDER TO DEFEND CERTAIN GROUPS OF SOCIETY AND TO PROTECT THE RIGHTS IMPORTANT TO THOSE GROUPS. THESE ORGANISATIONS CAN USUALLY PROVIDE LEGAL HELP, AS WELL AS PRACTICAL, SOCIAL OR PSYCHOLOGICAL SUPPORT TO THOSE WHOSE HUMAN RIGHTS HAVE BEEN INFRINGED. Legal help is named first among what these bodies provide, and the guide invites people to TURN TO THESE ORGANISATIONS OR INSTITUTIONS IN ORDER TO RECEIVE HELP IN A SPECIFIC SITUATION. HONEST LIMIT ON THIS ENTRY: this is a HUMAN RIGHTS directory, not an environmental or planning one. It is filed because a Latvian community fighting a project will need free legal help and this is a mapped, plain-language route to bodies that give it — but a group should expect to explain its case in rights terms (property, information, participation) rather than as a planning objection.

trackers.name: State Data Protection Inspectorate (VDAI)
trackers.desc: State Data Protection Inspectorate (VDAI) — Lithuania’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Transparency Register (skaidrumas)
trackers.desc: Lithuania's official lobbying/transparency register. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held.

trackers.name: Register of Lobbyists
trackers.desc: National lobbying register. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Lithuania
trackers.desc: Official case law of the Lietuvos Aukščiausiasis Teismas. · Find here: the judgments and case-law of the Supreme Court of Lithuania.

trackers.name: Lietuvos gamtos fondas (Lithuanian Fund for Nature)
trackers.desc: Lithuania's long-standing nature-conservation NGO, founded in 1991 and based in Vilnius, working on rare and endangered species and their habitats, on the management and restoration of natural habitats, and on the protection and restoration of the country's wetlands and peatlands. It helped build Lithuania's ecological network and works alongside state and municipal institutions, research bodies and other organisations rather than against them. WHO TO ENLIST when the site at issue is a bog, wetland or habitat of a protected species and you need someone who can say authoritatively what is there and what it is worth. For activists: no verified litigation record, so treat this as expertise, survey capacity and a route into official consultation processes — not as counsel. If you need a lawyer in Lithuania, this is not yet answered in this file.

trackers.name: CVP IS (Central Procurement)
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Lithuania, and for how much.

trackers.name: Vilnius Court of Commercial Arbitration
trackers.desc: Vilnius Court of Commercial Arbitration — tribunal (Lithuania).

trackers.name: Registrų centras
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Information System of Legal Entities Participants (JADIS)
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Statistics Lithuania
trackers.desc: Lithuania's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Lithuania.

trackers.name: National Audit Office
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Lithuania, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Chief Official Ethics Commission (VTEK)
trackers.desc: Legislator / public-official financial interest & asset declarations.

trackers.name: Supreme Administrative Court of Lithuania
trackers.desc: Supreme Administrative Court of Lithuania — supreme court in Lithuania (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: SAARSP — municipal money funded by environmental fines
trackers.desc: MUNICIPAL ENVIRONMENTAL MONEY, AND ENFORCEMENT FEEDS IT. Under a draft law, fines for breaches of environmental and natural resource law imposed by municipal officials would be transferred to the SAARSP of the very municipality whose officials imposed them — so pressing your municipality to enforce directly funds local environmental work. The same draft would establish participation by representatives of the public in allocating SAARSP funds, for transparency and public involvement in decisions; ask your municipality whether that is in force, because it is a seat at the table over the money. WHAT IT FUNDS: environmental activity by target groups including NGOs and communities, implementation of environmental programmes and projects, and preparation of the documentation needed to implement those measures — plus protection, management, monitoring, creation and inventory of green spaces, and preparation of green space projects. A PRECISE EXCLUSION WORTH KNOWING: money from game animal resource use goes to measures by owners, managers and users of land plots, and hunting clubs are not owners, managers or users — so it cannot fund hunting club measures.

trackers.name: Anyone can propose a Natura 2000 site — including a private person
trackers.desc: THE PROPOSAL RIGHT IS UNUSUALLY OPEN. Proposals to the Environment Ministry to designate territories meeting Natura 2000 criteria may be submitted by scientific institutions, by non-governmental organisations — named examples being LOD, Baltijos aplinkos forumas and Lietuvos gamtos fondas — by protected area directorates, and by private persons. Proposals cover new sites and changing the boundaries of existing ones, and are often made when ecosystem restoration work has given a location higher conservation value meeting the criteria. So restoration you carry out can itself become the basis for designating the site — a sequence worth planning for deliberately. Selection criteria are approved by ministerial order. FUNDING CONTEXT: the national AARP programme allocated EUR 907,200 across 2014–2018 to protecting natural resources, monitoring protected species and restoring landscape complexes in Natura 2000 territories; AARP also pays compensation for damage caused by bison and, since 2019, wolves.

trackers.name: Compensation for farming restrictions — and the default mowing regime
trackers.desc: WHAT MAKES PROTECTION ACCEPTABLE TO A LANDOWNER. Natural and legal persons holding land in Lithuanian protected areas where agricultural activity restrictions apply may apply for financial support — the answer to the landowner who says designation costs them their livelihood. THE DEFAULT REGIME, WHERE TERMS ARE NOT OTHERWISE SET by the special land use conditions law, protected area regulations, planning documents or protection agreements with private landowners: mowing begins 15 June and cut grass must be removed from the field by 30 October inclusive; where livestock graze, no grazing term is set. Knowing the default matters, because a protection agreement can specify different terms — which is the negotiating space between a conservation body and an owner.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Paramėlio gamtos atkūrimo fondas — buys forest plots in southern Lithuania
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a small restoration fund set up with German partners to protect the so-called Paramėlis island and the valuable ground around it in southern Lithuania, near the Čepkeliai mire and Dubičiai. Much of the wetland there was drained, the hydrology disrupted, and biodiversity-important forest cut and still being cut. Its response is to buy the surrounding forest: in the autumn it bought its first two forest plots outright for conservation. BE CLEAR ABOUT THE SCALE: two plots is where this one stands, not two thousand hectares. It is a young fund, not a national trust, and a community bringing it a large block will be disappointed. But for a small parcel of Dzukija forest with a willing seller it is a real buyer, in a country that otherwise has none I could find, and small buyers grow by being brought good sites. HOW TO WORK WITH IT: it runs annual volunteer work parties clearing the scrub encroaching on the Katra valley meadows, and asks people to join those, offer their skills, donate, or assign the 1.2 per cent income-tax designation. That is the same shape as the Austrian and Slovak entries — the money for the next purchase comes from people, so a community that can bring both a site and a crowd is worth more to it than one bringing only a site.

trackers.name: Gamtos paveldo fondas — does the restoration work and owns the survey kit (Lithuania)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a non-profit environmental organisation founded in 2001, at A. Vivulskio g. 41-113, LT-03114 Vilnius, which carries out practical habitat work — meadow and mire restoration, removal of invasive plants, conservation of protected species. WHY IT IS WORTH KNOWING ABOUT WHEN YOU ARE FIGHTING SOMETHING: it owns survey equipment and says so — a Topcon HiPer SR GNSS receiver used for planning and carrying out hydrological restoration, and a drone for photographing terrain that cannot be reached on foot and for assessing how water spreads during floods. A community arguing that a scheme will alter drainage or flooding is usually arguing without evidence, because surveying costs money nobody has. This is a Lithuanian organisation that already has the instruments and the people who use them. WHAT IT IS NOT: it is a practical conservation body, not a legal one and not a land buyer. Ask it for fieldwork, mapping and a hydrological view; ask somebody else for the objection.

trackers.name: Baltic Environmental Forum Lithuania — coordinates the country's environmental NGO coalition
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an environmental NGO at Užupio 9/2-17, 01202 Vilnius, +370 5 213 8155, info@bef.lt, director Žymantas Morkvėnas. Its declared fields are biodiversity protection, agri-environment, rural development, nature tourism and sustainable development. It coordinates the activities of the Lithuanian Environmental NGO Coalition, which makes it the single call that reaches the country's environmental sector rather than one organisation in it — the most useful fact in this entry for a community that does not know who to approach. It joined Eurosite, already in this file, in 2024. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY DELIVERED ON THE GROUND: management recommendations for Lithuanian Natura 2000 sites; mechanisms to secure good quality open habitats in Nemunas Delta regional park; the Baltic grassland viability project; an inventory of marine species and habitats to develop the Natura 2000 network in Lithuania's offshore waters; and since 2016 a ten-year aquatic warbler conservation project running to 2026. If a Lithuanian site is a wet meadow, a delta habitat or offshore, this organisation has probably already surveyed or written management guidance for that habitat type. ITS OWN FRAMING, WHICH TELLS YOU HOW TO PITCH: it says nature should be protected not from people but together with them, and that only through personal experience in nature does someone understand why it needs protecting. It also participates in the Committee of Rural Affairs. A case argued as excluding people will not fit; one argued as keeping people in the landscape will. THE GROUP IT BELONGS TO: the BEF Group, established out of a 1995 technical assistance project of the Baltic environment ministries, Germany and the European Commission, now with offices in Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia and Germany. Its Latvian sister is filed separately in this file. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer, not a funder and not a law firm, and it describes itself as a small organisation. Bring it habitat expertise questions and use it as the door to the coalition.

trackers.name: Aplinkosaugos koalicija — the environmental coalition, and the ministry's own NGO list
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Lithuanian environmental coalition, an association whose stated purpose is systematic representation of the public interest in environmental matters through planned advocacy, partnerships and long-term cooperation, together with strengthening its members' capacity and community. Lithuania's existing entries in this file are two land-holding foundations and a legal body; this is the sector's shared voice. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY WORKED ON, which tells you what it can help with: continued participation in the National Forest Agreement and an assessment of the draft agreement; a position on the EU Nature Restoration Regulation; proposals to the National Water Sector Development Plan 2022–2027; and proposals on the draft Law on Protected Territories and accompanying bills. If a Lithuanian case turns on forest policy, water planning or protected-area law, this is the body that has already filed positions on all three. AND IT DID THE FIELDWORK ON LIVING NEXT TO POLLUTION: it prepared and presented to institutions a qualitative study assessing the quality of life of people living with industrial pollution — odour, noise and dust — using Klaipėda as the case. A community suffering an operating plant rather than a proposed one has, in that study, evidence gathered from people in the same position and already put in front of the authorities. THE OTHER THING THIS OPENS: the Ministry of Environment publishes a list of environmental NGOs as its social partners — among them the environmental policy centre, the environmental management and audit institute, the environmental information centre, the Aplinkosaugos koalicija itself, Gyvo Žalio, Idėjų lysvė and a Klaipėda citizens' initiative for democracy. For a Lithuanian community that is the sector directory, published by the ministry. WHAT IT IS NOT: a coalition and an advocate, not a land buyer, not a funder and not a law firm. It works on project funding, so ask what it currently has capacity for.

trackers.name: Vilnius University Law Clinic — primary legal aid for NGOs, and the standing rules to check
trackers.desc: WHO GIVES FREE LEGAL HELP: the European Commission's own country page for Lithuania states plainly that primary legal aid to non-governmental organisations is provided by VšĮ „Vilniaus universiteto Teisės klinika“ — the Vilnius University Law Clinic. Lithuania was the only country in this region missing both a funder and a legal ally; this is the legal one, and it is free. The same page notes there are no other financial mechanisms. THE STANDING TEST, so you know what to establish before you go: the administrative court accepts only complaints seeking to defend a person's infringed right. But the Supreme Administrative Court applies the Aarhus Convention directly and decides legal standing on the basis of the Convention, and has held that for non-governmental organisations the requirements are that they must be actively operating in the field of environmental protection and meet other national requirements. 'Interested public' status is determined under the Environmental Protection Act and the Act on environmental impact assessment of proposed economic activity. Being demonstrably active in environmental protection before the dispute is what creates standing. THE COST WARNING, WHICH IS BLUNT: the general rule is that the losing party pays all costs, including the court fee and the costs of initiating proceedings, and must also reimburse the winning party's costs. Court fees, expert costs and other costs are usually paid in full; representation costs are reduced by reference to recommendations approved by the Minister of Justice and the Bar, but those are recommendations only and depend on the complexity of the case. Budget for losing before you file. TWO USEFUL FACTS ABOUT THE COURTS: environmental cases are a small share of the caseload — one to two per cent of appeals reaching the Supreme Administrative Court — but environmental aspects are built into many other fields including territorial planning, construction, restitution of property rights, taxes, transport and energy, so your case may be an environmental one under another name. And a prosecutor can bring proceedings defending the public interest: one such action by a Vilnius prosecutor, with a community association and local schools as interested parties, secured the annulment of a pollution permit.

trackers.name: Aplinkosaugos koalicija — twelve organisations, open to new members, and the ministry lists it
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: an umbrella organisation bringing together Lithuania's non-governmental environmental organisations, begun in 2004 on a joint activity agreement and formalised in 2011. It unites twelve organisations working in the environmental field. Its stated mission is to unite organisations' knowledge, experience and resources and take part together in forming and implementing environmental protection policy, and its stated ambition is to become the public environmental competence centre that is turned to first when the non-governmental sector's position is sought. AND IT IS OPEN: the coalition states plainly that it is open to new members. After the Bulgarian coalition that admits unincorporated groups by letter, this is the second national platform in this file a community can actually enter. WHERE TO FIND THE WIDER LIST: the Lithuanian environment ministry publishes its environmental NGO social partners, and the list runs far beyond the coalition — the environmental policy centre, the environmental management and audit institute, the environmental information centre, the coalition itself, and named citizens' associations including one formed by Klaipėda residents. A Lithuanian community can see, on a government page, which organisations the ministry itself recognises as partners. IT IS ALSO INSIDE THE NATIONAL NGO STRUCTURE: the coalition is a member of the Nacionalinė NVO koalicija alongside the youth council, the local community organisations union, the human rights coalition and others — and members' annual activity and financial reports are published. You can read a prospective ally's accounts before approaching it. THE CONTEXT IT ITSELF NAMES: on World NGO Day the national coalition wrote publicly that in Lithuania and in Europe there are increasing attempts to diminish the name of non-governmental organisations and spread doubts about their aims and transparency. Eighth jurisdiction in this chat recording pressure on the sector itself.

trackers.name: APVA — and the municipal environmental programme funded by pollution charges next door
trackers.desc: THE NATIONAL AGENCY: the Aplinkos projektų valdymo agentūra, Labdarių g. 3-102, 01120 Vilnius, administers projects financed from the Aplinkos apsaugos rėmimo programa, whose purpose is to finance environmental protection and other measures set out in the Act on that programme. It also administers the Klimato kaitos programa and the Lithuanian Environmental Investment Fund programme, which funds environmental investment projects reducing the negative impact of economic activity and securing a continuing environmental effect. AND THE PART A COMMUNITY SHOULD ASK ABOUT FIRST: there is a separate savivaldybių aplinkos apsaugos rėmimo specialioji programa — a municipal special environmental protection programme — governed by its own Act, whose funding sources are the pollution charges and state natural resources tax paid in that municipality. Money raised from polluting your district is held by your own council under a statute that says what it may be spent on, and the Supreme Administrative Court has published a summary of case law on challenging decisions about how those funds are used. That is the closest fund to a Lithuanian community and the one with a local decision-maker. A WORKED EXAMPLE OF WHAT NGOs GET: a project of the Aplinkosaugos koalicija — already filed here — received 85,856.43 EUR, of which 7,200 EUR to the coalition as partner, financed from the Klimato kaitos programa administered by APVA, to implement its long-term strategy and strengthen members' capacity so they can more effectively represent the environmental public interest. Its planned work included reviewing its advocacy and monitoring strategies against institutions' legislative plans and members' pressing topics. A state climate fund paying an NGO coalition to do advocacy and monitoring is unusual enough to record, and it tells a Lithuanian group which door its national allies already use. PRACTICAL: the ministry publishes the AARP funds usage rules and the list of projects that received AARP financing; ministry at A. Jakšto g. 4, 01105 Vilnius, info@am.lt.

trackers.name: Teisės vartai — Lithuanian law offices listed with Aplinkos apsaugos teisė as a named practice
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a directory of Lithuanian advokatų kontoros — law offices — with each firm's practice areas listed, its address, and the advocates' names, the year each began practice, telephone and email. The practice-area lists include Aplinkos apsaugos teisė (environmental protection law), Administracinė teisė ir procesas, and Nekilnojamojo turto ir statybų teisė (real property and construction law) — the three labels a community needs to filter on. WHY A DIRECTORY: Lithuania's bucket held the Vilnius University Law Clinic, which gives free primary legal aid to NGOs, and the Aarhus-style route — but no way to find a paid specialist when the clinic's help runs out. A named list with practice areas and the year each advocate qualified lets a community pick on experience rather than on advertising. WHAT LITHUANIAN FIRMS SAY THEY DO IN THIS FIELD: representation in dealings with municipalities and with the State Territorial Planning and Construction Inspectorate; advice on the lawfulness of construction and on change of use purpose; pre-trial dispute resolution; and court representation. Others list reconciliation of the interests of neighbouring plot owners — plot boundaries, building at the boundary, planting, insolation and surface water run-off — and restrictions on property rights including special land use conditions.

trackers.name: Lithuanian environmental standing — the suinteresuota visuomenė may demand action and punishment
trackers.desc: WHAT THE LAW GIVES A COMMUNITY, stated on the EU's own access-to-justice pages: one or more natural or legal persons, and the suinteresuota visuomenė — the interested public — have the right to lodge a complaint or application demanding that appropriate action be taken to avoid or reduce damage to the environment or to restore the environment to its original state, and demanding the punishment of persons guilty of harmful effects on the environment and of officials whose decisions, acts OR INACTION infringed the rights or legally protected interests of citizens, the interested public, or other persons. Inaction is expressly covered, and so is restoration to the original state — not merely stopping further harm. Second country in this sweep after Cyprus where an omission is actionable. AND A SEPARATE ROUTE ON INFORMATION: there is a right to apply to court where a request made under the rules on access to environmental information was unlawfully refused, answered partially or improperly, or not properly taken into account. A refused information request is itself a case. THE STATUTE BEHIND IT: the Aplinkos apsaugos įstatymas regulates relations in environmental protection and sets the basic rights and duties of legal and natural persons in preserving biological diversity, ecological systems and landscape features, alongside Articles 53 and 54 of the Constitution.

trackers.name: Municipal aplinkosaugos competitions — schools, kindergartens and bendruomenės can apply
trackers.desc: WHERE THE LOCAL MONEY ACTUALLY IS: Lithuanian municipalities run their own environmental competitions from the funds of the savivaldybių aplinkos apsaugos rėmimo specialioji programa — the municipal special environmental protection programme already recorded in this file, fed by the pollution charges paid in that municipality. This is the application portal where those calls appear. WHO MAY APPLY, and it is broader than any national fund: non-governmental organisations, public institutions, BENDRUOMENĖS — communities — SCHOOLS AND KINDERGARTENS. A neighbourhood community and a village school are named applicants, which no national environmental fund in this file allows. WHAT THE PROGRAMME IS FOR, in its own words: to involve city residents in protecting the environment of their own place of residence, develop ecological thinking and responsibility, increase awareness of environmental problems, and encourage residents' activity and partnership in solving environmental questions. AND A SECOND MUNICIPAL LINE WORTH ASKING FOR: a parallel competition implements the Law on the Development of Community Organisations in culture, sport, social affairs, ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION and youth policy, to widen NGO involvement in meeting local community needs. PRACTICAL: smaller municipalities publish their own budgets — one district allocated 38,000 euro to NGOs and communities, covering three lines including co-financing of up to 5 per cent of the compulsory contribution to EU or national programme projects and operating costs. Ask your own municipality what it has budgeted and whether co-financing is one of the lines.

trackers.name: Aktyvių piliečiụ fondas — 9 million euro, with at least 80 small local organisations targeted
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Active Citizens Fund in Lithuania, financed under the EEA financial mechanism — at least 10 per cent of that mechanism's funds go to strengthening civil society through the fund, by agreement between the EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway — allocating 9 million euro across a five-year period in Lithuania. It is administered by a consortium of three named NGOs. THE TARGET THAT MATTERS TO A VILLAGE GROUP: the fund plans to involve more than 250 civil society organisations, INCLUDING AT LEAST 80 SMALL ORGANISATIONS OPERATING AT LOCAL LEVEL, to finance at least 180 projects, and to engage about 10,000 people directly. A published target for small local organisations is a commitment you can hold a funder to. THE TWO PROJECT SIZES: small-scale projects from 5,000 to 15,000 euro, and medium-scale projects above 15,000 and up to 80,000 euro. In one call the fund received 157 concept applications — only 16 per cent for the small tier, so the small window is the less crowded one. AND A DETAIL ABOUT PARTNERSHIP WORTH COPYING: two thirds of applications had partners, 179 partners in total across the round, with one applicant naming eleven. Partnering is the norm here, not a bonus.

trackers.name: Anyone can propose a gamtos paveldo objektas — and the agency lists exactly what to send
trackers.desc: THE INVITATION, IN THE AGENCY'S OWN WORDS: if you have noticed a valuable natural object — for example a rare species, an impressive stone or a unique landscape — assessed it against the criteria and think it should be protected, YOU CAN SUBMIT A PROPOSAL. For a state-protected object or natural heritage object, send it to the protected areas service; for a MUNICIPAL protected object, apply to the relevant municipal administration, whose contacts are published. Two tiers, one form, and a published contact list for both — Lithuania had one land acquirer filed and this is the route by which a resident gets a single feature protected. WHAT TO PUT IN THE PROPOSAL, listed by the agency so nothing is guessed: the exact location — municipality, eldership, COORDINATES; quantitative features where applicable such as height, length, AGE, diameter; and qualitative features such as form, composition, transparency, AESTHETIC VALUE and NATURALNESS. The object must meet at least two of the criteria, one being naturalness — whether the object and its surroundings are unaffected by human activity. AND THE SCALE THAT SHOWS IT IS ROUTINE: Lithuania had 701 state-protected natural heritage objects, 155 of them declared natural monuments, AND 232 MUNICIPALITY-PROTECTED ONES. The agency also publishes a handbook on the general and special principles of managing such objects.

trackers.name: The Lithuanian municipal NGO funds — money for improving public spaces, council by council
trackers.desc: WHAT ONE DISTRICT PUBLISHES, and every Lithuanian council runs something comparable: a call inviting NGOs to submit applications for PART-FINANCING from the municipal budget under a multi-year non-governmental organisations activity funding programme, with 20,000 EURO allocated and a stated application window. Eligible applicants are NGOs registered AND OPERATING IN THE DISTRICT'S TERRITORY. AND WHAT THE MONEY CAN BE SPENT ON, from another municipality's rules, which is the part that matters to a group defending a place: funds may be awarded competitively for INITIATIVES INTENDED TO IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF PUBLIC SPACES AND THE ENVIRONMENT — the fitting out of PARKS, sports and recreation grounds, AND OTHER REST AND RECREATION PLACES IN THE LOCAL COMMUNITY'S TERRITORY; for strengthening NGO cooperation with other public legal persons, developing partnership and SOLVING QUESTIONS RELEVANT TO THE LOCAL COMMUNITY; and for strengthening the organisation's own activity and cohesion. Priority goes to organisations holding formal NGO status — and the exclusions are published too: no funding for organisations that failed to report on earlier municipally-funded projects, for everyday running costs or salaries, or for premises repair and equipment UNRELATED TO THE PROJECT.

trackers.name: Lietuvos ornitologų draugija — the country's largest conservation membership body, and it does the fieldwork
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a non-governmental organisation operating for 40 years, uniting Lithuanian people who care about the protection of living nature, who look after and observe birds and their environment, care for environmental preservation and public ecological education, AND PARTICIPATE AS CITIZENS IN FORMING ENVIRONMENTAL AND BIODIVERSITY PROTECTION POLICY. It is THE MOST NUMEROUS CONSERVATION MEMBERSHIP ORGANISATION IN THE COUNTRY. Lithuania had one land-holding body filed. AND WHO CAN JOIN, which is the resource: any citizen who pays the membership fee can be a member. The society unites people of varied interests — professional researchers, bird watchers, naturalists, FARMERS, FORESTERS, teachers, schoolchildren, students and other citizens not indifferent to Lithuanian nature. A membership body that already contains farmers and foresters is one that can talk to the landowners around your site, rather than only to officials. AND WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES ON THE GROUND: it CARRIES OUT GAMTOTVARKA WORKS — practical habitat management — conducts SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH into bird populations and monitoring, and PUBLICLY CONTROLS THE MAKING AND IMPLEMENTATION OF LAWS regulating environmental and biodiversity protection. Since 1994 it has represented BirdLife International in Lithuania. Its Vilnius street address and email are published.

trackers.name: The Lithuanian park directorates — 36 staff, a street address and a phone, per protected area
trackers.desc: WHO ACTUALLY RUNS A LITHUANIAN PROTECTED AREA, and it is a body with a door: the directorate of a named national park and state nature reserve is A BUDGETARY INSTITUTION EMPLOYING 36 STAFF, with a street address in a named town, a website and a direct telephone number. The park covers 58,519 hectares — one of the largest protected territories in Lithuania. AND ITS DUTIES, which tell a resident exactly what to ask it for: it organises the natural science RESEARCH AND OBSERVATIONS of the park and reserve and ACCUMULATES INFORMATION ABOUT THE STATE AND CHANGE OF THEIR NATURAL ENVIRONMENT COMPONENTS; protects natural and cultural heritage values; creates conditions for recreational activity; carries out ecological education; and fosters the region's cultural traditions, crafts and trades. A directorate that accumulates information on the changing state of its own area is the body holding the baseline data your objection needs — and it is a public institution obliged to answer. AND THE INTERNATIONAL LAYERS ON ITS GROUND, each a separate lever: the reserve is declared a NATURA 2000 territory and entered on the list of the RAMSAR CONVENTION protecting wetlands of international importance, and the wider area is one of thirteen European PAN Parks. It also holds a European Solidarity Corps quality label, so it takes volunteers.

trackers.name: The new Saugomų teritorijų įstatymas — individual notice, and compensation for EVERY owner
trackers.desc: TWO CHANGES A LITHUANIAN LANDOWNER SHOULD KNOW, recorded by the forest owners' association that argued for them. First: it is established that BEFORE ESTABLISHING OR DESIGNATING NATURA 2000 TERRITORIES, LANDOWNERS MUST BE INFORMED INDIVIDUALLY. Until now this was done only in the case of establishing national protected areas. Individual written notice before a Natura designation is what stops an owner learning about it from a neighbour, and this file recorded in Turkey that failure to notify villagers was alone sufficient to annul a decision. SECOND, AND IT REACHES PEOPLE WHO WERE PREVIOUSLY EXCLUDED: from now on, compensation for activity restrictions on a specific land or forest plot can be received by ALL OWNERS WHO HAVE NOT YET RECEIVED COMPENSATION, not only those who recovered or acquired the holding BEFORE the protected area was established. Under the old rule, if the land or forest in an existing protected area was bought by another owner, that owner LOST THE RIGHT to the compensation due for the environmental restrictions. Someone who bought into a protected area after designation may now be owed money they were previously refused — worth checking before assuming nothing is available. The association states it actively participated in the deliberations, submitting comments and proposals so the regulation would reflect forest and land owners' interests.

trackers.name: NŽT — the pre-emption list for farmland, and the fees for getting onto it
trackers.desc: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN FARMLAND IS SOLD, and it is the part a community wanting to buy needs: if a person received information from the land service about an AGRICULTURAL LAND PLOT FOR SALE, it means they are on THE LIST OF PERSONS HOLDING A PRE-EMPTION RIGHT to acquire it, the categories being set out in the land acquisition act. A statutory list of who gets first refusal on farmland is a queue a community body may be able to join before the land ever reaches the open market. AND THE CLOCKS AND FEES, published: having received the notice, a person has 15 WORKING DAYS to submit their consent to buy; the seller's notification-and-certificate service costs 47 EURO, and the land service's consent to acquire agricultural land costs 11 EURO for a private person. Eleven euro and fifteen working days is the whole cost of standing in the queue — which makes it worth registering before a sale is announced rather than after. AND THE RULE FOR EVERYONE ELSE: buying an agricultural plot WITHOUT a pre-emption right is possible only if ALL persons holding that right have refused, and only AT THE PRICE STATED IN THE SELLER'S ORIGINAL NOTICE. A person without the right must apply to the service on their own initiative for consent.

trackers.name: Baltijos aplinkos forumas — 20 staff, and it works on WIN-WIN SOLUTIONS with farmers
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: founded in 2003 as a NON-GOVERNMENTAL, NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION, described as one of the strongest and most efficient environmental NGOs in Lithuania, with 20 EMPLOYEES, among them SOME OF THE LEADING EXPERTS ON AGRI-ENVIRONMENTAL MEASURES MANAGEMENT IN THE COUNTRY. AND WHAT IT DOES THAT A COMMUNITY CAN USE: defining the most valuable priority areas for targeted species conservation; EVALUATION OF CONSERVATION STATUS AND MANAGEMENT NEEDS; INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITY BUILDING OF PROTECTED AREAS ADMINISTRATIONS; and STAKEHOLDER DIALOGUE. An organisation that will evaluate a site's conservation status is the one that turns a village's worry into a document a ministry must answer, and it publishes its team, their expertise and its Vilnius office location. AND THE APPROACH WORTH BORROWING WHERE FARMERS ARE THE OBSTACLE: it raises awareness BY ENSURING ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL MOTIVATION to foster WIN-WIN SOLUTIONS FOR AGRICULTURE AND ENVIRONMENT, by achieving CONCRETE BENEFIT FOR THE FARMERS in a long-term perspective, and works in collaboration with local environmental authorities. One named staff member coordinates communication and NATURE TOURISM, supervises VOLUNTEERS, and runs a named public initiative.

trackers.name: Lithuania's court fee — 30 EURO to file, 15 to appeal, and NOTHING where the authority delays
trackers.desc: THE PRICE OF GOING TO COURT, published by the supreme administrative court itself: the court fee for lodging a complaint with the FIRST-INSTANCE court is currently 30 EURO. For lodging an APPEAL to the Supreme Administrative Court, a fee of 15 EURO is paid. Thirty euro to start an administrative case is the cheapest court access recorded in this file — against a 600-dollar New Zealand appeal and a 200-euro Greek deposit. AND THE EXEMPTION THAT MATTERS MOST, from the same system: the Law on Administrative Proceedings provides several exemptions from the court fee, FOR EXAMPLE COMPLAINTS OR APPLICATIONS CONCERNING THE DELAY BY PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION ENTITIES IN PERFORMING ACTS WITHIN THEIR COMPETENCE. Challenging an authority for sitting on a decision costs nothing at all, which is the cheapest lever a Lithuanian community has when a permit is being allowed to slide through. AND THE COURT'S PRACTICAL DETAIL: its Vilnius street address, telephone, MOBILE NUMBER and email are published with its opening hours, and on Mondays and Wednesdays from 17.00 to 17.30 the court accepts applications and complaints from PERSONS WHO HAVE REGISTERED IN ADVANCE. It also warns that the court has the right to require payment of the fee IF PERSONS ABUSE THE RIGHT TO JUDICIAL DEFENCE.

trackers.name: Free primary legal aid in Lithuania — the municipality must see you WITHIN FIVE DAYS
trackers.desc: THE ENTITLEMENT, and it has no means test: the law gives EVERY PERSON LAWFULLY RESIDENT IN LITHUANIA THE RIGHT TO FREE PRIMARY LEGAL AID — a legal consultation. Free first advice for everyone, regardless of income, is a starting point most communities never use, and it is delivered locally rather than in the capital. WHO GIVES IT: municipal administration officials and employees, AND ALSO ADVOCATES OR SPECIALISTS FROM PUBLIC INSTITUTIONS with whom the municipality has signed a contract. They will personally advise HOW TO RESOLVE THE DISPUTE WITHOUT A COURT, inform you about the legal system, laws and other legal acts, HELP TO PREPARE A SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND TO FILL IN THE APPLICATION FOR SECONDARY LEGAL AID. AND THE TIMING GUARANTEE, which is unusually firm: primary legal aid must be given to you IMMEDIATELY. If that is not possible, you will be told the next reception time, WHICH MUST BE NO LATER THAN 5 DAYS from your approach. A five-day statutory maximum wait for free legal advice is worth quoting when an office tries to put a resident off. Applicants must approach the municipality OF THEIR DECLARED PLACE OF RESIDENCE.

trackers.name: Lithuania's compensation for restrictions — the state pays for the FOREST PLAN too
trackers.desc: WHAT AN OWNER GETS FOR ACCEPTING RESTRICTIONS, and it is the offer that persuades a Lithuanian landowner: compensation may be ONE-OFF OR ANNUAL, calculated INDIVIDUALLY FOR EACH FOREST PLOT, taking into account THE VALUE OF THE TIMBER LEFT UNCUT, with the figures set by the preparer of the forest management project. Lithuania had two land-acquisition entries filed. AND THE DETAIL THAT REMOVES THE LAST OBSTACLE: together with the compensation for the restrictions, the forest owner MAY ASK FOR THE COSTS OF PREPARING THE FOREST MANAGEMENT PROJECT TO BE COMPENSATED. The state pays for the very document needed to calculate the payment, so an owner is not out of pocket for finding out what they are owed. AND WHERE THE MONEY COMES FROM WHEN THE SITE IS EUROPEAN: most Lithuanian protected areas OVERLAP with Natura 2000 sites, and in those cases private forest owners' losses ARE COMPENSATED FROM EUROPEAN UNION FUNDS under a named rural development programme — with payments made TO PRIVATE FOREST OWNERS OR THEIR ASSOCIATIONS where felling is forbidden or restricted. An owners' association can receive the payment collectively, which is the fourth community-landholding route recorded in this region. Protected areas cover about 17.5 PER CENT of the country.

trackers.name: The Suvalkija national park plan — owners are offered compensation OR A BUY-OUT
trackers.desc: WHAT HAPPENS TO PRIVATE LAND WHEN A NEW LITHUANIAN NATIONAL PARK IS PLANNED: during the planning process, land owners will, under the provisions of the law, HAVE THE POSSIBLE COMPENSATION preliminarily calculated FOR LOSSES CAUSED BY RESTRICTIONS ON ECONOMIC ACTIVITY, OR THEY MAY BE OFFERED THE BUY-OUT OF THE PRIVATE LAND. A buy-out is offered as an alternative to compensation when a park is created — so designation is itself a route by which private land inside a threatened area can pass into public hands. AND THE SCALE AND STAGE: the government approved the start of preparation of the planning scheme and the planning objectives for a park that could occupy UP TO 35,000 HECTARES. AND THE POINT THAT SHAPES ANY OBJECTION: national parks are NOT protected areas with a single uniform environmental regime — the boundaries and the internal zones are settled during planning, which is when a community's submission has effect. The protected-areas service also publishes NATURE OBJECTS IN PROTECTED AREAS RECENTLY ADAPTED FOR VISITING, which is what gives a designation local support.

trackers.name: Pelkių fondas — a fund for ONE habitat type, and what a single-habitat body is for
