AND THE HONEST CONTEXT A SLOVENIAN GROUP SHOULD KNOW, published by a Slovenian environmental organisation: environmental NGOs receive only 1.18 per cent of all state funds allocated to NGOs, covering environment, nature and spatial planning together; organisations with public-interest status in environment and nature received only 0.8 per cent of all income-tax designation donations in one year; and at local level environmental protection sits right at the tail of all fields. There are more than 200 environmental NGOs in Slovenia, of which 78 hold public-interest status in environmental protection and nature conservation. Expect competition and small sums, and apply widely rather than deeply.

trackers.name: Stičišče Središče — it reads the call for you before you submit
trackers.desc: WHAT IT OFFERS, and it is unusual: a regional NGO support hub that asks directly whether you are looking for a call suitable for financing your activities, wonder whether a call is right for you, are looking for partners in Slovenia or abroad, have doubts about developing the project idea, are stuck on parts of the application form, or WOULD LIKE SOMEONE TO CHECK THE QUALITY OF YOUR APPLICATION BEFORE YOU SUBMIT IT — and offers its project advisers if the answer to any is yes. Free pre-submission review is the cheapest way to raise a bid's chances, and few countries in this file have it named. AND IT EXPLAINS THE TWO THINGS THAT DISQUALIFY MOST APPLICATIONS: co-financing — if a call funds up to 80 per cent, you must fund at least 20 per cent from other sources: another call, donations, membership fees, earned income; and eligibility of applicants, where wording matters — some calls say broadly 'legal persons in the Republic of Slovenia', which admits any NGO, public institution or company, while others restrict to 'societies acting in the public interest in the field of the environment'. IT ALSO POINTS TO NON-MONEY RESOURCE: an organisation that places international volunteers with local groups working on protection of natural and cultural heritage — you apply to their call and normally provide food and accommodation.

trackers.name: The state's predkupna pravica on protected land — and the duty to notify before selling
trackers.desc: THE PROVISION THAT CATCHES A SALE: under the Zakon o ohranjanju narave, the State is the PRE-EMPTION HOLDER on the purchase of immovable property in protected areas for which it has adopted a protection act, REGARDLESS of the provisions of other laws governing pre-emption on agricultural, forest, water or building land — and the owner MUST NOTIFY the manager of the protected area AND THE MINISTRY of an intended sale, with an offer containing the property details, the price and the other conditions of sale. Inside a Slovenian protected area, a sale cannot proceed quietly — the manager is entitled to know first, and a community that knows the manager will hear of it. Fifth country in this file with a statutory pre-emption, after Iceland's listing-triggered right. AND THE POWERS A LOCAL COUNCIL HOLDS, which are set out in the same act: matters of LOCAL importance are the responsibility of the local community — programming and planning for the protection of natural values of local importance, ADOPTING PROTECTION MEASURES for them, providing local public services of nature conservation, and popularising their protection — and the local community ensures the protection of plant or animal species that are LOCALLY THREATENED OR IMPORTANT, on the basis of an expert proposal from the organisation competent for nature conservation. A council can adopt protection measures for a locally threatened species on an expert proposal — and the State must act if the existence of a natural value of local importance is in danger. There is also a register of natural values.

trackers.name: Sklad kmetijskih zemljišč — the state land fund buys for nature-protection functions too
trackers.desc: WHAT IT BUYS, and the clause that matters: the state agricultural land and forest fund gives priority to buying co-ownership shares in land partly already owned by the State, boundary and NEIGHBOURING land, and land in complexes — and, among special kinds of purchase of agricultural land and forests, ARE PURCHASES OF LAND WITH EMPHASISED NATURE-PROTECTION and other strategic functions important from the State's standpoint. A community whose site adjoins state land, or whose site has nature-protection value, has a state buyer whose own rules name both. Restrictions on such transactions are set in special laws including the nature conservation act and the forest act. It also buys larger estates returned in denationalisation and leases them to farmers who are financially too weak to buy, and smaller areas that can be attached to neighbouring farms. AND AN HONEST WARNING ABOUT DEALING WITH IT, recorded from a public account: a buyer valued a parcel at 900 euro on the official register and offered four times that, but the fund would have sold it only at auction, after a written request, at a far higher figure. Ask on what terms the fund sells before assuming a state seller is the cheap route. SEPARATELY, on the other side of the same coin: where public infrastructure is built on land compulsorily taken, the owner is entitled to appropriate compensation OR REPLACEMENT IN KIND, and the owner has 30 days to reply to an offer or agree different terms before the State or municipality may begin expropriation.

trackers.name: IPoP — a consulting and research institute that supports COMMUNITIES on spatial planning
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a non-profit, non-governmental CONSULTING AND RESEARCH organisation that supports communities comprehensively in the sustainable ordering of space, cooperating with civil society, LOCAL COMMUNITIES, educational and public institutions and private companies in Slovenia and other European countries. Slovenia's bucket held the free green advice line, funders and litigators — this is the body that helps with the planning itself. IT DESCRIBES ITS OWN ROLE PRECISELY: we are the connecting link between these organisations and the inhabitants, and so we encourage inclusive practices, cross-sector cooperation, and the spread of experience and knowledge that create SPACES WITH PEOPLE AND FOR PEOPLE. Cooperation is our basic working principle and tool. AND ITS DEFINITION OF WHO THE PUBLIC IS, which a community can quote back at a council that consulted only landowners: in the ordering of space, the public are most often THE LOCAL INHABITANTS, whom the planning, construction, use or renewal of an area directly concerns — and among local inhabitants may be included TEMPORARY RESIDENTS, TENANTS, and so on. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES: expert support in preparing strategic documents and local policies, especially on sustainable mobility, reviving town centres, MANAGEMENT OF PUBLIC GREEN SURFACES and parking policy, connecting local needs with international practice; it is the Slovenian contact point for two European urban programmes; and it has run a project expressly on SUPPORT FOR LOCAL INITIATIVES — the potentials and problems of local initiatives in actively co-shaping the local environment.

trackers.name: Mreža za prostor — the Slovenian spatial-justice network, member by member
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a published network of Slovenian organisations working on space, each member described by what it actually does — the free artefact this file has found most useful in eighteen countries. WHO IS ON IT AND FOR WHAT, in their own descriptions: an institute for the space of culture that works on EXPERT SUPPORT TO LOCAL INITIATIVES, innovative inclusion of heritage, and applying permaculture principles in practice; an institute for social responsibility working on the development of eco-settlements and FRIENDLY CONSTRUCTION — building with natural materials: wood, straw, stone, clay and similar — and establishing dialogue between companies, government services, TRADE UNIONS, civil society organisations and other stakeholders; and the Slovenian foundation for sustainable development, an expert organisation striving for sustainable development in national policies and for establishing balance between people and the environment. A network whose members include a permaculture institute, a natural-building institute and a national sustainability foundation gives a community three different kinds of help from one page. AND THE PARTNERSHIP PATTERN WORTH NOTING: the same organisations — a sustainable development society, the sustainability foundation, the legal-information centre for NGOs and IPoP — have run joint projects together, so an approach to one is an introduction to the others.

trackers.name: DOPPS — it OWNS a 66-hectare nature reserve, and holds public-interest status twice over
trackers.desc: WHAT IT OWNS: the Ormož Lagoons nature reserve measures a little over 66 HECTARES AND IS IN THE OWNERSHIP AND MANAGEMENT OF DOPPS. Slovenia had three land-holding bodies filed; this is one that owns outright rather than manages for the state. AND THE TWO STATUSES THAT MATTER WHEN IT SIGNS A SUBMISSION: in 2001 it received the status of a society ACTING IN THE PUBLIC INTEREST OF NATURE CONSERVATION, and in 2009 the status of a society acting IN THE PUBLIC INTEREST IN THE FIELD OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION in the Republic of Slovenia. Public-interest status in two separate fields is what gives an organisation standing in Slovenian procedures — and a local group with neither can ask this one to act with it. THE BODY: probably the largest and one of the oldest non-governmental nature protection organisations in Slovenia, founded 1979, with around 1,000 members, THREE OFFICES — central in the capital and TWO REGIONAL — and 20 to 24 employed experts. Full partner of BirdLife International. Its bank account, VAT number, registration number and each office's telephone are published, along with a named president and her mobile. AND THE VOLUNTEER ROLE IT RUNS: STORK GUARDIANS — individuals who look after stork nests, follow the course of nesting or help the storks in any way, gathered at a meeting marking 25 years of national stork census.

trackers.name: The Ormož Lagoons reserve — volunteers replanted a meadow, species by species
trackers.desc: WHAT HAPPENED ON THE GROUND, and it is a template a community can copy on any degraded patch: within a named seeds project, VOLUNTEERS AND VISITORS PLANTED 1,230 SEEDLINGS OF 22 DIFFERENT PLANT SPECIES ON AN AREA OF 0.4 HECTARES — the species named individually in the report — having first been shown the seeds of plants characteristic of that type of meadow and the different methods of restoration. About 40 visitors from near and far took part. A named seed list, a measured area and a counted number of seedlings is the kind of record that turns a volunteer day into evidence. AND WHAT ELSE THE SOCIETY PUTS ON THE CALENDAR, so a resident can meet it in person: European birdwatching day events at a reservoir, at two of its own reserves, at a named floodplain and at fishponds, each with a published meeting point and time — car parks, a railway station, a cemetery car park. Where an organisation publishes its meeting points, joining it costs nothing but turning up. The reserve itself carries surfaces dedicated to the restoration of DRY MEADOWS.

trackers.name: The predkupna pravica queue — seven ranks of first refusal, published on the state portal
trackers.desc: THE ORDER OF FIRST REFUSAL on farmland, forest or a farm, in the statutory rank order: 1. the CO-OWNER; 2. an entitled person under a named article; 3. A FARMER WHOSE OWN LAND ADJOINS THE LAND FOR SALE; 4. THE TENANT of the land for sale; 5. another farmer; 6. an agricultural organisation or sole trader who needs the land for agricultural or FORESTRY activity; 7. the state farmland and forest fund, for the Republic. A neighbour whose land touches the parcel, and a tenant already on it, both outrank every outside buyer — so a community's first question is whether one of its own members already sits in ranks 1, 3 or 4. AND THE TIE-BREAK WITHIN A RANK: 1. the farmer for whom farming is the ONLY OR MAIN activity; 2. the farmer who works the land THEMSELVES; 3. the farmer chosen by the seller — with farming counted as the main activity if the produce or income from it is that person's principal means of subsistence. AND THE FALL-BACK, which is the deadline that matters: if none of the pre-emption holders exercises the right, the seller may sell to anyone who accepted the offer IN TIME AND IN THE PRESCRIBED MANNER, subject to approval by the administrative unit.

trackers.name: How to buy farmland and forest — the offer goes on the administrative unit's noticeboard
trackers.desc: WHERE A SALE IS ANNOUNCED, and it is a place a community can watch: the seller lodges the offer to sell agricultural land, a farm or forest IN THREE COPIES with the administrative unit in whose area the greater part of the land lies. THE ADMINISTRATIVE UNIT PUBLISHES THE OFFER ON ITS PHYSICAL NOTICEBOARD AND ON THE ELECTRONIC NOTICEBOARD of the administrative units. Every farmland and forest sale in the country is posted on a public noticeboard before it completes — which is where a group watching a valley learns that ground is changing hands. AND THE CLOCK: the buyer must send a WRITTEN STATEMENT ACCEPTING THE OFFER to the seller AND to the administrative unit within 15 DAYS. AND THE FOREST-SPECIFIC RANKING, which this file has not recorded elsewhere: the priority holders in the purchase of FORESTS are the Republic of Slovenia, IF THE FOREST IS A PROTECTIVE FOREST OR A FOREST WITH A SPECIAL PURPOSE. Where a wood is classed as protective or special-purpose, the state itself moves to the front of the buying queue — so getting that classification recognised changes who can buy it. The article also records that the status of a protected farm has been abolished in transactions between the living, surviving only in inheritance proceedings.

trackers.name: Eko sklad's NVO calls — 20,000–30,000 EURO per project, and you must have existed TWO YEARS
trackers.desc: THE MONEY AND THE ELIGIBILITY BAR, both published: the amount of co-financing is FROM 20,000 TO 30,000 EURO, and project duration is AT LEAST 10 AND AT MOST 12 MONTHS. Slovenia had three funding entries filed. AND THE CONDITION THAT DECIDES WHETHER A NEW GROUP CAN APPLY AT ALL: applicants and their project partners must all be LEGAL PERSONS OF PRIVATE LAW with a seat in the Republic of Slovenia, registered under the law governing SOCIETIES, the law governing FOUNDATIONS, or the law governing INSTITUTES; be non-governmental organisations under the NGO act; AND HAVE BEEN REGISTERED AS SUCH AT LEAST TWO (2) YEARS BEFORE THE DAY THIS CALL WAS PUBLISHED. A two-year registration requirement means a group formed to fight a project cannot fund itself from this call — so a community should either register early, before there is a threat, or apply through an established society as partner. AND THE CONTENT AREAS IT PAYS FOR, which are broader than they look: awareness, education and promotional projects on themes including ADAPTATION TO CLIMATE CHANGE, INCLUDING NATURE-BASED SOLUTIONS AND STRENGTHENING BIODIVERSITY, delivered through awareness-raising and education of TARGET GROUPS to improve understanding of the problem and readiness to change behaviour and decision-making.

trackers.name: Zagovorniki okolja — the Slovenian environmental advocates, and WHO MAY BE A PARTY
trackers.desc: A BODY WHOSE SUBJECT IS LEGAL REMEDIES IN ENVIRONMENTAL AND SPATIAL CASES, publishing both the remedies and the case law, and — on the same site — a named HANDBOOK FOR CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS IN SPATIAL PLANNING. Slovenia is joint-smallest bucket in this file. AND THE LIST THAT DECIDES WHETHER A COMMUNITY IS IN THE ROOM AT ALL, which it sets out in full: those with legal interest include THE OWNER OF THE PROPERTY AND A PERSON WITH PERMANENT RESIDENCE IN THE AFFECTED AREA SHOWN IN THE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT; ANOTHER PERSON, IF THEY SHOW THAT THE INTENDED CONSTRUCTION COULD AFFECT THEIR RIGHTS AND LEGAL INTERESTS BECAUSE OF THE ENVIRONMENTAL BURDENS FORESEEN DURING AND AFTER CONSTRUCTION; A NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATION WITH THE STATUS OF ACTING IN THE PUBLIC INTEREST in environmental protection or nature conservation; AND A CIVIL INITIATIVE, IF IT COLLECTS THE SIGNATURES OF 200 ADULT NATURAL PERSONS WITH PERMANENT RESIDENCE IN THE AREA OF THE MUNICIPALITY WHERE THE INTENDED CONSTRUCTION IS. Two hundred signatures turns an unincorporated group of neighbours into a party to the proceedings — no registration, no association, no lawyer needed to reach the threshold. AND WHAT COUNTS AS LEGAL INTEREST, which tells an objector what to write about: THE INTENDED USE OF THE LAND OR BUILDING, MEASURES TO REDUCE EMISSIONS, DISTANCES FROM PLOT BOUNDARIES AND NEIGHBOURING BUILDINGS, MEASURES TO PREVENT THE SPREAD OF FIRE, ACCESS AND SURFACES FOR FIREFIGHTING AND RESCUE, AND THE MECHANICAL RESISTANCE AND STABILITY OF THE PROPERTY.

trackers.name: Združenje ROVO — a volunteer environmental association acting on its NGO SUPERVISORY RIGHT
trackers.desc: A NAMED NATIONAL VOLUNTEER BODY: THE NON-GOVERNMENTAL ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATION ROVO ACTS AND IS FOUNDED ON THE VOLUNTARY MEMBERSHIP OF ENVIRONMENTALISTS IN OUR COUNTRY. THE ROVO ASSOCIATION CARRIES OUT VARIOUS ORGANISATIONAL AND EXPERT TASKS OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURE PROTECTION UNDER ITS NGO SUPERVISORY RIGHT ACROSS THE TERRITORY OF THE REPUBLIC OF SLOVENIA, NAMELY BY PROTECTING THE WEAKEST LINKS IN OUR SOCIETY. An organisation that describes its work as a supervisory right exercised across the whole country is one that can look at a project it has no local connection to — which is what a village without its own experts needs. AND HOW IT FRAMES THE WORK: WE ARE AWARE THAT THE PROBLEM OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION IS BY ITS NATURE COMPLEX, ITS STUDY INTERDISCIPLINARY, AND ITS SOLUTION CONNECTED WITH THE COORDINATED AND ACTIVE PARTICIPATION OF DIFFERENT FACTORS SUCH AS THE ECONOMY AND ITS INFLUENCES ON ENVIRONMENTAL DECISION-MAKING POLICY. HONEST LIMIT ON THIS ENTRY: what this page gives is the association's self-description, its national scope and its volunteer basis — not a documented casework record, a fee position, or named staff. It is filed as A SECOND NATIONAL DOOR TO TRY, not as a body whose track record is evidenced here.

trackers.name: Commissioner for Personal Data Protection
trackers.desc: Commissioner for Personal Data Protection — Cyprus’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Cyprus — Independent Authority Against Corruption (Lobbyists Register)
trackers.desc: National lobbying register; the IAAC maintains the mandatory public Register of Lobbyists under the 2022 Lobbying Law (registrants’ names, sectors & represented interests posted online), Cyprus. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held.

trackers.name: CyLaw
trackers.desc: Free database of the Cyprus Institute of Legal Information: Supreme Court judgments (1883–) and legislation, no registration. · Find here: free Cyprus case-law and legislation (CyLaw).

trackers.name: Terra Cypria — The Cyprus Conservation Foundation
trackers.desc: Cyprus's conservation foundation, a charitable NGO since 1992, and the one body here with a seat inside the assessment process itself: with BirdLife Cyprus it sits on the Ad hoc committee that carries out the Appropriate Assessment of projects and plans affecting Natura 2000 areas. WHO TO ENLIST when a development touches a Natura 2000 site, a coastal stretch or a wetland. You CAN: use the European route it has already opened, which is the useful thing when domestic channels stall — it petitioned the European Parliament over Akamas and the Petitions Committee kept the case open for follow-up, the Commission acknowledged the area is not sufficiently protected, and in March 2024 the Commission decided to take Cyprus to the Court of Justice over repeated failure to issue the decrees that safeguard Natura 2000 sites. For activists: it monitors approved plans for later relaxation rather than declaring victory at approval, and it argues for transfer-of-development-rights legislation as the fair way to handle private land locked inside protected areas — the argument to make when landowners are the obstacle.

trackers.name: Audit Office
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Cyprus, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Cyprus Register of Beneficial Owners
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Access restricted to authorities/obliged entities.

trackers.name: Registrar of Companies
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: eProcurement
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Cyprus, and for how much.

trackers.name: ΜΕΟΑ — environmental organisations sit on the assessment committee
trackers.desc: A SEAT AT THE TABLE, NOT A CONSULTATION RIGHT. Every appropriate assessment for a project affecting a Cypriot Natura 2000 site is evaluated by the Department of Environment within an ad-hoc committee that includes the Forests Department, Game and Fauna Service and Fisheries — and environmental organisations: the Federation of Environmental Organisations of Cyprus, Terra Cypria and BirdLife Cyprus. Elsewhere in this map civil society comments from outside and hopes to be weighed; here three named bodies sit inside the assessing committee. A local group's fastest route to influence is through one of those three, and the Federation is the umbrella smaller groups reach that table through. WHAT THE ASSESSMENT MUST CONTAIN — hold the developer to it: data on the area, habitats and protected species; evaluation of impacts on the conservation objectives and on the integrity of habitats and species; a study of alternative solutions; and proposed mitigation measures. A submission with no alternatives study, or one assessing impact without reference to the site's conservation objectives, is incomplete on its face. AND ASK ABOUT SCREENING: the Department also runs an informal pre-screening procedure for small projects where specialised studies may not be required — which is exactly where a small but locally significant development can pass unexamined.

trackers.name: Ask whether conservation objectives were set — and get the shapefile
trackers.desc: TWO CONCRETE MOVES. 1. THE QUESTION THE CJEU MADE DECISIVE: a Court of Justice of the European Union ruling reported as a landmark for Natura 2000 puts in doubt permits issued for protected areas without specific conservation objectives — the message being that protection is not a formal procedure nor a policy choice but a substantive legal obligation, and that projects such as LNG installations, hydrocarbon extraction, wind farms and tourist developments must be assessed against site-specific conservation objectives. So ask first whether objectives have been set for your site; if not, the assessment has nothing lawful to measure against. 2. GET THE BOUNDARY DATA: data.gov.cy publishes Natura 2000 area boundaries as a shapefile — machine readable, so you can check a development footprint against the boundary yourself rather than relying on a developer's map. Cypriot SPA, SCI and SAC information is published under Article 4 of Directive 92/43/EEC and the Birds Directive, and official data goes to the EU annually via the EIONET repository, moving to Reportnet3 from 2026 — so EU-held copies are a cross-check on national statements. Each site also has a standard data form, the legal reference for assessing favourable conservation status, available through the Natura 2000 Viewer.

trackers.name: Cyprus Environment Foundation — grants for equipment and monitoring
trackers.desc: A CYPRIOT GRANT-MAKER, and what it funds tells you how to pitch. A recorded grant gave technical support to the LIFE-Vultures project, implemented with the Game and Fauna Service, Terra Cypria and vulture partners, working toward the Griffon Vulture's favourable conservation value of 65 pairs (or 200 individuals) within 25 years. The funded activities were equipment and monitoring capability — CCTV on an acclimatisation aviary and GPS transmitters placed on young vultures in the nest to track the post-fledgling period, so that remote monitoring can alert authorities to intervene in good time and prevent losses. TWO THINGS TO TAKE FROM THAT: it will fund kit and monitoring, not only activity; and the grant was framed as work that complements ongoing EU-funded efforts rather than duplicating them — so pitch a proposal as filling a gap beside an existing LIFE project, which in Cyprus is a realistic description of most conservation funding.

trackers.name: Terra Cypria — sits on parliamentary AND technical assessment committees
trackers.desc: A ROUTE INTO TWO DIFFERENT ROOMS. Terra Cypria — the Cyprus Conservation Foundation, established 1992 — states its first objective as the application of pressure for better environmental protection, and it participates in Parliamentary Committees of the House of Representatives and in governmental technical committees assessing the environmental impact of projects and programmes in protected areas. A body sitting on both the political and the technical-assessment side is unusual and worth approaching early. It monitors 6 Natura 2000 sites and researches government environmental decisions. THE REACH THAT MATTERS MOST: it has been an NGO participant in the proceedings of the Standing Committee of the Bern Convention since 1997, is an IUCN member, and sits on the board of the European Environmental Bureau and Eurosite — the Bern Convention route means a Cypriot case can be raised at Council of Europe level. Funding comes from an annual A.G. Leventis Foundation grant, project grants and course contributions; it runs the Cyprus Environmental Studies Centre at Kritou Terra since 1995 and offers scholarships. Recorded work includes a report on the economic impact on tourism of failing to stop illegal bird trapping — more than 2.5 million birds are trapped yearly. OTHER PARTNERS TO KNOW: BirdLife Cyprus (2003, Nicosia), the Cyprus Wildlife Society and the Federation of Environmental Organisations of Cyprus, all partners in a 10-year EU project covering all 63 Natura 2000 sites.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: BirdLife Cyprus — the island's most active conservation organisation
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an environmental NGO formed in 2003 from the merger of two Cypriot ornithological societies, with offices at Kato Deftera, Nicosia, and the national BirdLife partner. It describes itself as the most active non-governmental nature conservation organisation in Cyprus, working through monitoring, conservation and education. WHY IT MATTERS FOR A SITE UNDER THREAT: its core work is the designation and protection of Important Bird Areas as Special Protection Areas. That is the practical question to bring it — is our ground an Important Bird Area, what is recorded there, and can it be pushed towards designation. Cyprus is one of the emptiest buckets in this file, with no land buyer, no funder and no named counsel that I could find; an organisation that runs the island's bird monitoring and pursues site designation is the closest thing to an evidence base a Cypriot community can reach. It also runs a long campaign against illegal bird trapping and poaching, so it has experience of pressing enforcement authorities. USE IT ALONGSIDE TERRA CYPRIA, NOT INSTEAD OF IT: the other Cypriot entry in this file goes and checks whether works match the consent and holds a Bern Convention seat. This one holds the species and site data. The two escalated the Akamas case together, along with the Cyprus Wildlife Society and the Cyprus Natural Coastline Initiative — four organisations on one letter, which is how Cypriot cases appear to get moved. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer, not a funder, not a law firm.

trackers.name: Enalia Physis Environmental Research Centre — the survey capacity Cyprus lacks
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Cypriot non-profit formed in 2009 conducting biological and environmental research in marine and terrestrial ecosystems, at Acropoleos 2, Nicosia, +357 22331660, own site enaliaphysis.org.cy. It collaborates with organisations in Cyprus and internationally, and its stated mission is research alongside public education. WHAT IT CAN ACTUALLY DO FOR A CASE: it has worked on the designation of a marine protected area network taking account of ecological characteristics and sustainable yield for fishing; on assessing deep-water caves and deep-water corals as areas of ecological research value; on by-catch of vulnerable species and mitigation measures; and it runs standing monitoring schemes around Cyprus covering invasive species, coral colonies against nutrient levels, the effect of disturbance on marine habitats, and fouling communities on artificial reefs. For a coastal or marine development this is an organisation that already holds survey data and knows how designation arguments are built in Cyprus. WHY IT MATTERS HERE: Cyprus has no land buyer, no funder and no named counsel in this file, and its two existing entries are a compliance checker and a bird-data holder. Most Cypriot development pressure is coastal. This is the missing marine and coastal science. SOURCING CAVEAT: verified through the European Youth Portal's accredited-organisation listing, which reproduces the centre's own description and contact details, rather than from a page on its own site. Confirm current activity at enaliaphysis.org.cy before relying on it. AND IT IS NOT ALONE: five Cypriot environmental organisations signed a joint open letter to the President in May 2026 over Akamas — BirdLife Cyprus, Terra Cypria, the Cyprus Wildlife Society, Friends of the Earth Cyprus and the Cyprus Natural Coastline Initiative — calling for roadworks in the national forest park to cease and for information, transparency and accountability. Cypriot cases move when organisations sign together; ask whoever you reach who else will put their name on it.

trackers.name: NGO Support Centre — runs the Active Citizens Fund, and workshops open to informal groups
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: the NGO Support Centre, which with GrantXpert Consulting was selected through open competitive tender as Fund Operator of the Active Citizens Fund in Cyprus. Cyprus had no funder in this file. THE DETAIL THAT MATTERS MOST FOR A RESIDENTS' GROUP: its information workshops for potential applicants were addressed to civil society organisations including non-governmental organisations, informal groups, and public and private entities in Cyprus, with the same sessions run across the island so applicants anywhere could attend. An unincorporated residents' group is inside the audience the Fund Operator writes for — and, given Cyprus's small sector, the workshop is also where you meet everyone else applying. AND THE PROGRAMME PREFERS THE PLACES USUALLY MISSED: it states that it encourages applications from entities based in rural, under-served regions of the island, and towards under-served and hard-to-reach target groups, with particular attention to less experienced, smaller organisations. Third funder in this file to prefer the periphery to the capital, after Montenegro and Serbia. THE SHAPE OF THE MONEY: the Cypriot Active Citizens Fund was supported by a €1.5 million grant from Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway under the EEA and Norway Grants 2014–2021, run through an open call with a budget of about €1.2 million and three outcomes, two of them offering both small and large grants — increased citizen participation in civic activities, empowering vulnerable groups, and a mandatory third on the capacity and sustainability of civil society. Seventeen projects were funded from the 2021 open call. BE REALISTIC ABOUT FIT: its named areas of support are democracy and human rights, and social justice and inclusion, with emphasis on youth and on bi-communal cooperation. A Cypriot land case should be framed as citizen participation in a public decision. A SECOND, LARGER DOOR ON THE SAME ISLAND: the European Commission's Cypriot Civil Society in Action grant programme, in its tenth edition, has committed €19.78 million to civil society in Cyprus since 2007 with more than 160 organisations funded; its recent call ran over €2 million in three lots, was restricted with concept notes submitted first, and offered online and on-site information sessions.

trackers.name: OPOK — the federation of 19 to 20+ Cypriot organisations, and it sits in parliament committees
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Omospondia Perivallontikon Organoseon Kyprou (OPOK) — the Federation of Environmental and Ecological Organisations of Cyprus, founded 1988, described as a network of 19 non-governmental organisations active in the fields of environment and culture, and elsewhere as a non-party body uniting more than 20 independent environmental organisations. It coordinates and supports the actions of its members where those align with its founding principles. For a Cypriot community, one letter reaches the sector. WHERE IT ACTUALLY APPEARS, which is the reason to enlist it rather than a single NGO: it has taken part in sittings of the parliamentary Environment Committee and the parliamentary Interior Committee, held meetings with the Environment Commissioner, and organised a protest event for the protection of the Akamas peninsula. It has publicly demanded that hunting be banned in a particular area, warned that a proposal could adversely affect the safety of drinking water and public health, described a municipality's action as provocative, and called something a dangerous precedent. AND IT WATCHES THE EU INFRINGEMENT ROUTE: it has expressed strong concern about infringement procedures against Cyprus under Union nature protection law. Combined with the Akamas petitions already recorded for this country, that is a federation which follows what Brussels is doing to its own government — useful to a community whose case rests on an EU directive. HOW TO USE IT: ask the federation which of its members works on your kind of site, and ask whether it will co-sign. The Cypriot pattern in this file is joint statements — Terra Cypria, BirdLife Cyprus and this federation acting together — so a single organisation's support is worth less than the federation's.

trackers.name: Cyprus EIA public register — read the developer's own impact study for your village
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Department of Environment's public portal for ΜΕΕΠ — environmental impact assessment studies — listed by project, giving the type of installation, the owner, and the community and district it sits in. A live example on the portal is an EIA for the construction and operation of an intensive poultry rearing unit, naming the owner, the community of Orounta and the Nicosia district. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ANY GRANT: every entry in this file about objecting, surveying or designating rests on knowing what the developer said about your ground. In Cyprus the developer's own study is published, by village, before the decision. Terra Cypria — already filed here — is recorded as checking works against the ecological assessment; this is the portal that assessment lives on, so a resident can do the first check themselves. WHAT TO DO WITH IT: find your community's name, read what the study claims about habitats, water and neighbours, and take the specific claims to BirdLife Cyprus, Terra Cypria or Enalia Physis — all three already in this file — or to the OPOK federation. A study that omits a species or a watercourse is a far stronger basis for an objection than a general concern. A CURRENT DEVELOPMENT TO WATCH, RECORDED PLAINLY: the Department of Environment has prepared a draft Regulation for the rationalisation of environmental impact assessment procedures. Rationalising an assessment procedure can mean fewer projects assessed or shorter windows to respond — read the draft rather than assume. AND WHERE THE RULES FOR THE COUNTRYSIDE SIT: the Republic's policy statement for the regulation and control of development outside development boundaries carries named chapters on protection of nature, landscape and forests, on change of use of a building or other immovable property, and on waste deposition from industrial, livestock, quarrying and construction activity.

trackers.name: Demetriou & Demetriou LLC — runs recourse against zoning changes and permit conditions
trackers.desc: WHY THIS CLOSES A REAL GAP: Cyprus was the only country of the forty-three in this file with no legal resource of any kind — it had BirdLife Cyprus, Terra Cypria, Enalia Physis and the OPOK federation, and nobody to run a case. WHAT THE FIRM SAYS IT DOES: it specialises in cases concerning state interference with the right of property and states it is currently handling many such cases. Its named work covers recourse against decisions of the Administration on compulsory expropriation of property, requisitioning, imposition of restrictions on property, CHANGES OF PLANNING ZONES, return of property expropriated but not used for the purpose of the expropriation, and THE IMPOSITION OF CONDITIONS ON PLANNING PERMITS. Changes of planning zones and conditions on planning permits are exactly the two moments a community loses ground, and this is a Cypriot firm that names both as its practice. It describes handling cases from compulsory expropriations and planning zone changes through to planning restrictions, and representing clients whether filing a recourse against the Administration or negotiating compensation.

trackers.name: Article 146 recourse — the Cypriot route for challenging an unlawful decision or omission
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE, NAMED: Cypriot administrative-law practices describe challenging unlawful state decisions, acts OR OMISSIONS under Article 146 of the Constitution — the recourse that takes a public body's decision to the Administrative Court. An omission is challengeable, not only a decision, which matters when an authority simply fails to act on a breach. WHAT ELSE THE CYPRIOT BAR OFFERS A COMMUNITY: firms state experience in challenging decisions of public bodies and appearing before all courts of the Republic; and on the enforcement side, practices describe injunction applications in planning-violation cases, noting that courts require clear evidence of ongoing violations or risks and that both sides must avoid unnecessary delay. If unauthorised works are under way, an injunction is the named remedy and the evidence standard is stated. PRACTICAL: to practise in the Republic an advocate must be entered on the Register of Advocates kept by the Chief Registrar of the Supreme Court and hold an annual practising licence from the Cyprus Bar Council — so a community can verify anyone it is about to instruct.

trackers.name: Cyprus funding opportunities portal — every co-financed call in one table
trackers.desc: WHY IT EXISTS: to guarantee transparency and immediate information for potential beneficiaries about the funding opportunities offered, the calls for proposals issued by the responsible bodies under each grant or incentive scheme are posted on the funding information portal. In batch 286 I searched for a Cypriot environmental grant scheme and found none; this is the index where such calls appear when they open, and it is the honest answer for a country whose money arrives through co-financed programmes rather than a standing nature fund. AND THE PARALLEL LISTING WORTH OPENING ALONGSIDE IT: Cypriot advisers maintain a summarised table of the programmes through which beneficiaries can draw European or state funds — grants and subsidies co-financed by both EU and Republic of Cyprus funds — for businesses AND OTHER ORGANISATIONS, published as calls are announced by the competent Cypriot bodies. WHAT ELSE IS ON THE MONEY MAP HERE: the European Commission has awarded 15 new grants amounting to over 2 million euro to support the actions of civil society organisations throughout Cyprus; and the Active Citizens Fund programme, run under the EEA and Norway Grants by a consortium including the NGO Support Centre — already filed here — gave particular emphasis to bi-communal cooperation and intercultural dialogue and to strengthening bilateral relations between Cypriot NGOs and organisations in Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway. AND THE OFFICE TO KNOW: Cyprus has a Commissioner for Volunteerism and NGOs, with a standing dialogue between the Minister of the Interior and voluntary organisations. Where a state has a commissioner for the sector, that office is the route to ask which scheme fits.

trackers.name: BirdLife Cyprus — it runs a nature reserve, and it got 69 villas refused
trackers.desc: WHAT IT HOLDS, which closes Cyprus's acquirer gap: Thkio Mosfilies, its first nature reserve and outdoor learning space, in the Famagusta district near the villages of Frenaros, Avgorou and Vrysoulles — its first targeted effort to create and maintain a rich and diverse habitat, nestled in a mosaic of pine woodland, carob scrub and open habitats, and an outdoor education space for the local communities. THE WINS IT RECORDS, which tell a community what is achievable: the Department of Environment REJECTED a proposal for a large-scale development of 69 LUXURY VILLAS at the entrance of Akamas, near a named beach; a landmark legal appeal for safeguarding the wild coastline of another named place; the first recorded breeding attempt among released griffon vultures; and completion of Cyprus's Article 12 bird status report. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND BIRDS: it defined 34 Important Bird Areas following BirdLife International's methodology, and IBAs have been recognised by the European Court of Justice as a scientifically sound basis for determining Special Protection Area boundaries — though in one case only 55 per cent of the IBA is covered by the current SPA boundaries. Where the designated boundary is narrower than the scientific one, the gap is itself the argument. Founded 2003 from the merger of two ornithological societies; offices in Kato Deftera, Nicosia.

trackers.name: The Cyprus environmental front — eight organisations on one Bern Convention complaint
trackers.desc: THE ROSTER, which is the free artefact Cyprus offers: a complaint on the Akamas peninsula to the Bern Convention was supported by the Federation of Environmental Organisations of Cyprus, BirdLife Cyprus, the Cyprus Wildlife Society, the Ecological Movement of Cyprus, Enalia Physis Environmental Research Centre, Friends of Akamas, Friends of the Earth Cyprus and the Initiative for the Protection of the Natural Coastline. A separate joint statement to the President was signed by five of them. Eight named organisations including a FEDERATION and a site-specific 'Friends of' group — the model for a community that wants its own name on the list. AND THE INTERNATIONAL LEVER THEY USED: the Bern Convention's Standing Committee recommends that the Government declare the whole of the Akamas peninsula a national park, a biosphere reserve or a protected area with comparable international protected status, managing it as a whole, including terrestrial and marine parts, in a sustainable, integrated way. A Bern Convention recommendation is a standing instruction to a government that a community can cite — this file has recorded the same lever working in Montenegro. AND WHAT THE MOVEMENT ASKS FOR BEYOND DESIGNATION: the setting up of a SPECIAL ENTITY FOR THE INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT of the peninsula, drawing on the experience of other Natura 2000 sites that are being properly managed. Their complaint notes that current laws are frequently disregarded as construction proceeds without the required permits.

trackers.name: Coucounis Law — and the mistake that got a neighbour's whole case thrown out
trackers.desc: THE ERROR IT DOCUMENTS, which would cost a Cypriot community everything: an owner of neighbouring property challenged a municipality's decision to authorise an apartment building — but filed the recourse ONLY against the town planning permit and failed to challenge the building permit. If he files only against the town planning permit, THE BUILDING PERMIT REMAINS VALID AND LEGAL and consequently the recourse is considered incomplete and DISMISSED AS INADMISSIBLE. Every affected person must file against BOTH the town planning and the building permit, and the firm cites a 2022 Administrative Court judgment showing exactly how the affected neighbour must act. The same applicant also failed to specify the existing or certainly upcoming damage from the construction. AND THE DUTY IT NAMES, which is the ground to run: the town planning authority is OBLIGED BY LAW to ensure that the independent operation, the comfortable possession and enjoyment of the development will not substantially affect THE AMENITIES OF THE AREA OR THE NEIGHBOURING PROPERTIES; and the issue of a town planning permit in disregard of the rights of the neighbour entitles him to invoke a LEGITIMATE INTEREST to apply for annulment. The authority must consider the applicable development plan and any other essential factor, BUT NOT EXTERNAL ones.

trackers.name: Cypriot environmental and planning practices — the 75-day clock, and who else to call
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE AND WHAT THEY COVER: a Cyprus-based boutique firm with offices in Nicosia and Paphos, publishing on environmental enforcement — including appeals against a regulator's decision NOT to grant an environmental permit, or against the CONDITIONS contained in one, and the enforcement powers of environmental regulators, where criminal liability and sanctions apply to anyone operating an installation or performing activities contrary to a requirement to obtain an environmental permit. THE CLOCK EVERY CYPRIOT OBJECTOR NEEDS: the right of recourse may be exercised within 75 DAYS from the date the decision is notified to the interested person, and some laws provide for a HIERARCHICAL REVIEW as an intermediary step before filing. AND THE ROUTE WHEN INFORMATION IS REFUSED: any person not content with the response, or lack of response, to a request for disclosure of ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION is entitled to apply for hierarchical review and/or lodge an administrative recourse. A refused information request is itself actionable — the same rule this file recorded in Lithuania. ALSO ON THE MAP: a Cypriot practice records a criminal appeal concerning use and alteration of a property's approved purpose without authorisation, where a municipality sought an injunction to suspend a business, and notes that courts can issue interim orders to halt unauthorised construction — a firm of 16 legal professionals. And a national land-use-and-zoning lawyer directory lists practices by city.

trackers.name: The Laona Foundation — it was set up to prove that mass tourism was not the answer
trackers.desc: WHY IT EXISTS, and it is the clearest founding story in this file: by the mid-1980s concern for the fate of the unspoilt western peninsula made Friends of the Earth realise that SPECIFIC ACTION WAS NECESSARY IN ORDER TO DEMONSTRATE TO LOCALS AND GOVERNMENT ALIKE THAT MASS TOURISM DEVELOPMENT WAS NOT A SOLUTION TO THE ECONOMIC PROBLEMS OF THE AREA, BUT RATHER THE PRESERVATION OF ITS NATURAL BEAUTY AND TRADITIONAL CULTURE. A planning consultant was brought in, an EU-funded project set up in 1989, and three years later it became a foundation aiming to support rural communities. Arguing that conservation IS the economic case, rather than a cost, is the argument a village facing a resort needs — and here an organisation was built specifically to prove it. WHAT IT STANDS FOR NOW, in its own list: regenerating the Cypriot countryside sustainably and SUPPORTING ITS COMMUNITIES; preserving the natural and cultural heritage, especially landscape, architecture and traditions; protecting distinctive areas such as the Akamas peninsula and THE TERRACED LANDSCAPES of Cyprus; CONFRONTING DESERTIFICATION and preserving the soil; encouraging sustainable tourism AS AN OPPORTUNITY, NOT AS A PANACEA; and sharing expertise with NGOs in Cyprus and abroad. It participates as an observer in the meetings of the LANDSCAPE CONVENTION at the Council of Europe, and works with Friends of the Earth Cyprus and a named environmental institute.

trackers.name: The Cyprus Environmental Directory — the island's green organisations, one by one
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a compiled directory of Cypriot environmental organisations, each entered with its aims, activities and contact details — the kind of artefact this file has found most useful in every country, because it turns one fight into a list of possible allies. WHAT ITS ENTRIES CARRY, from the ones visible: a research centre described as a non-governmental, non-profit organisation headquartered in the capital which, THROUGH RESEARCH, IN-DEPTH SCIENTIFIC STUDY AND EDUCATION, aims at effective contribution to the protection of the LAND AND MARINE environment, and which takes part in EU programmes for NGOs as well as BI-COMMUNAL PROGRAMMES; and a body whose stated purpose includes contributing to the study, protection and advertisement of the NATURAL BEAUTIES AND HISTORICAL MONUMENTS of Cyprus. An organisation that already does in-depth scientific study is the one to ask for the survey a planning objection needs — and the directory says which those are. AND THE FUNDER NAMED THROUGHOUT IT: a private foundation dedicated to the preservation of the cultural and natural heritage of Greece and Cyprus, which awards every year a number of educational grants and is recorded elsewhere in this file as the annual funder behind the island's conservation foundation.

trackers.name: Friends of the Earth Cyprus — a registered charity since 1993, with its bank details published
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: a non-governmental, non-political, non-profit environmental organisation established in 1993 and based in Limassol, which is A REGISTERED ASSOCIATION AND A RECOGNISED CHARITY IN THE REPUBLIC OF CYPRUS, with roughly 300 to 500 members and a youth section. Registered charity status is what lets a body receive a legacy or a donation of land, and this one publishes its full bank account number, IBAN and SWIFT code on its own site so money can be sent without an intermediary. ITS PLACE IN THE ISLAND'S NETWORK, which is the practical value: it is a member group of Friends of the Earth Europe and Friends of the Earth International, and also of THE FEDERATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND ECOLOGICAL ORGANISATIONS OF CYPRUS and the European Environmental Bureau. Where a country has a federation of environmental organisations, one letter reaches all of them. AND ITS STATED GOAL, in its own words: to raise awareness on the importance of preserving the natural environment and to campaign for solutions to environmental and social problems by promoting sustainable policies, envisioning a society built upon peoples' sovereignty and participation. Its address, telephone and fax are published by its international federation.

trackers.name: The Cyprus Department of Forests — it holds TEN national forest parks, with a phone and a PO box
trackers.desc: WHAT IT HOLDS, and this is the answer to Cyprus's thin land bucket: TEN NATIONAL FOREST PARKS, each with a founding year, district and area — running from a 26-hectare park near a coastal resort and a 45-hectare park inside the capital's suburbs, up to a 4,523-hectare mountain park and a 9,147-hectare park in the Troodos range, with a national park proposed for the Akamas peninsula. A state department that has already turned ten separate places into national forest parks, including small urban ones, is the body to bring a neighbourhood site to — the 26- and 45-hectare parks show the floor is low. AND ITS STATED FIELDS OF WORK: afforestation and silviculture; production of timber and non-wood products; PROTECTION AGAINST FIRES AND OTHER HAZARDS; CONSERVATION OF ECOSYSTEMS, FLORA, FAUNA AND HERITAGE; LOCAL PLANS AND VILLAGE DEVELOPMENT; and institutional reform and capacity building — with a mission to serve the Government AND THE PEOPLE, for the benefit of all sections of society. A forest department with a standing programme line for LOCAL PLANS AND VILLAGE DEVELOPMENT is one a village can approach about its own surroundings. Its Nicosia PO box, telephone and fax are published, and it has district offices; it also holds and runs the aerial firefighting contracts.

trackers.name: The Akamas action plan — four named authorities, two million euro, and an open complaint file
trackers.desc: WHAT EXISTS AND WHO RUNS IT: an action plan for the peninsula developed by the Department of Environment as beneficiary, to be implemented ALONG WITH OTHER COMPETENT AUTHORITIES — the DEPARTMENT OF FORESTS, THE DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES AND MARINE RESEARCH, AND THE GAME AND FAUNA SERVICE — with an estimated budget of 2 MILLION EURO and actions already being implemented, eligible for co-funding from the European Regional Development Fund. Four named authorities on one plan is four doors, and a community should write to the one whose remit its own problem falls under. AND WHAT THE MONEY BUYS, which a community can ask to have extended to its site: MONITORING THE GOOD CONSERVATION STATUS of the habitats and species — populations of important species of PLANTS, AMPHIBIANS, REPTILES, BATS, MAMMALS, SEA TURTLES, FISH, SEALS, BIRDS AND ARTHROPODS — alongside management actions. Consistent and coordinated conservation measures are implemented in ALL NESTING BEACHES of the peninsula and a neighbouring Natura site, through a yearly marine turtle programme. AND THE STANDING FILE THIS SITS IN: a Council of Europe complaint case-file remains OPEN on Cyprus concerning the peninsula, and campaigners' demands recorded there include declaring the whole peninsula a national park, a biosphere reserve or a protected area with comparable international protected status.

trackers.name: Terra Cypria on the Akamas — it names the UNUSED TOOL for landowners inside a protected area
trackers.desc: THE INSTRUMENT IT POINTS AT, which exists on paper and is not being used: the foundation, expressing concern for the future of the peninsula if the proposed Local Plan takes effect, PROPOSES THE PASSAGE OF A 2011 BILL FOR THE TRANSFER OF DEVELOPMENT RIGHTS. Transferring the right to build off a protected parcel and onto another site pays the owner without anything being built where it matters — the answer to the owner who says they cannot afford to leave their land alone. The foundation's headline is that these are TOOLS AVAILABLE FOR LANDOWNERS THAT THE GOVERNMENT HAS LEFT UNUSED. AND THE GROUNDS IT ARGUES ON: the peninsula is one of the most important and most beautiful natural areas of Cyprus. Part of it belongs to the European NATURA 2000 network of protected areas because of the VERY IMPORTANT BIODIVERSITY it hosts. For that reason it requires PARTICULAR LOCAL MANAGEMENT precisely because of the environmental particularities of the area, TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE NEEDS OF THE INHABITANTS OF THE SURROUNDING COMMUNITIES. Arguing for local management that names residents' needs is what separates a durable designation campaign from one the village will fight. A companion page records the foundation's judgment on the same area after two years: inaction, non-implementation of decisions and a complete absence of accountability.

trackers.name: The Cyprus Lands and Surveys apallotriosi page — A COMMUNITY ASSEMBLY can be the expropriating authority
trackers.desc: WHO CAN EXPROPRIATE IN CYPRUS, published by the Department of Lands and Surveys itself: subject to a named article of the Constitution and the Compulsory Acquisition Law of 1962, ANY PROPERTY MAY BE COMPULSORILY ACQUIRED FOR PURPOSES OF PUBLIC BENEFIT, and the acquiring authority may be (a) THE REPUBLIC, (b) A MUNICIPAL AUTHORITY, (c) A COMMUNITY ASSEMBLY, or (d) A LEGAL PERSON OF PUBLIC LAW OR A PUBLIC-BENEFIT ORGANISATION to which the right is granted. Cyprus had two land-acquisition entries filed. A community assembly is named as an expropriating authority in its own right — so in Cyprus the village body itself, not only the state, can acquire land for public benefit. And a public-benefit organisation can be granted the same right, which is the route for a conservation body that has no purchase money of its own. AND WHY THE PAGE MATTERS BOTH WAYS: the same law and the same authorities govern a taking a community may want to resist, so the statute and its article numbers are the first thing to read whether the acquisition is wanted or fought. The department publishes it as a standing reference alongside its other land procedures.

trackers.name: The five Cypriot environmental organisations that act together — named, and still active
trackers.desc: THE FIVE BODIES A CYPRIOT COMMUNITY CAN APPROACH, named together in a joint action: TERRA CYPRIA, BIRDLIFE CYPRUS, FRIENDS OF THE EARTH CYPRUS, THE CYPRUS WILDLIFE SOCIETY, and CYPRUS NATURAL COASTLINE — the INITIATIVE FOR THE SALVATION OF THE NATURAL COASTS, calling on the President to take immediate action for the substantive protection of nature, and to keep his environmental commitments under the governing programme. Five organisations that already act as a bloc are five doors that open on one knock — and a local group joining an existing coalition inherits its access. AND THE ASSESSMENT ONE OF THEM GAVE ON NATIONAL RADIO, which is the language a community can borrow: speaking for one of the organisations, a named representative stressed that THE ENVIRONMENT IS UNDER ATTACK FROM EVERY SIDE, while THE MINISTRY HAS FAILED IN ITS TASK, and the President must now intervene. AND WHAT THEIR JOINT LETTER RESTS ON, which is the strongest available lever in Cyprus: the need for IMMEDIATE COMPLIANCE WITH THE EUROPEAN ENVIRONMENTAL ACQUIS, since CYPRUS CONTINUES TO FACE SERIOUS INFRINGEMENT PROCEEDINGS, PARTICULARLY IN RELATION TO THE NATURA 2000 NETWORK. A live infringement proceeding against the state is a pressure a local objection can attach itself to. They ask for THE ADEQUATE DESIGNATION, EFFECTIVE PROTECTION AND INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT of Natura 2000 areas, and the IMPROVEMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES.

trackers.name: Cyprus Natural Coastline — a CITIZENS' initiative fighting for the coast, 6,000 strong
trackers.desc: A NAMED CYPRIOT CITIZENS' BODY, and the only one of the five coalition members that is not a professional organisation: it describes itself as A CITIZENS INITIATIVE DEMANDING AND FIGHTING FOR THE PROTECTION OF THE NATURAL COASTLINE IN CYPRUS, with 6,080 followers. A citizens' initiative that sits at the table with the national conservation foundations is proof that an unincorporated group of residents can hold that seat — it is the model a new local campaign should look at before deciding it must first become a registered association. AND WHERE IT HAS REACHED: it is named as a co-signatory, alongside TERRA CYPRIA, BIRDLIFE CYPRUS, FRIENDS OF THE EARTH CYPRUS and the CYPRUS WILDLIFE SOCIETY, of open letters sent TO THE PRESIDENT OF THE REPUBLIC over the protection of a named peninsula and the Natura 2000 network. HONEST LIMIT ON THIS ENTRY: the initiative's public presence found here is a social-media page giving its purpose and its following, not a constitution, an office or a contact procedure. It is filed as A ROUTE INTO AN ACTIVE COASTAL CAMPAIGN, not as an incorporated body a community can instruct.

trackers.name: Selling your building rights instead of your land — the transfer route, and the bill for it
trackers.desc: A ROUTE THAT PAYS AN OWNER WITHOUT ANYONE BUYING THE LAND, which is the missing answer wherever protection strands a landowner: a bill PROVIDES FOR PRIVATE PROPERTY OWNERS WHO HAVE BUILDING RIGHTS BUT CANNOT UTILISE THEM FOR VARIOUS REASONS, TO SELL THEM OR TRANSFER THEM TO GOVERNMENT-OWNED LAND ELSEWHERE, IN AREAS SPECIFIED BY THE INTERIOR MINISTRY. Cyprus has one of the smallest bases in this file. The owner sells the right to build, keeps or gives up the land, and the building happens somewhere the state chooses — which converts an objector's opponent into a compensated party without a purchase fund. AND THE PRECEDENT THAT SHOWS IT WORKS: A SIMILAR PRACTICE ALREADY EXISTS FOR OWNERS OF LISTED BUILDINGS WHERE STRICT DEVELOPMENT CONDITIONS EXIST. UNDER A 2002 ACT, OWNERS CAN SELL THEIR THEORETICAL BUILDING RIGHTS TO BUILD AN EXTRA FLOOR OR ROOM, FOR EXAMPLE, TO PROPERTY OWNERS IN OTHER AREAS NOT BOUND BY SUCH RESTRICTIONS. The heritage sector has run this since 2002, so a community can point at a working domestic precedent rather than a foreign one. AND THE COMPLAINT THAT MAKES IT URGENT, from the foundation's named executive director: they see A BILL LYING DORMANT SINCE 2011 AND CONSTANT GOVERNMENT STATEMENTS ABOUT FINALISING THE LOCAL PLAN WITHIN MONTHS, WITHOUT THE EXISTENCE OF RELEVANT LEGISLATION TO TRANSFER THE DEVELOPMENT RIGHTS.

trackers.name: A foundation that sits on the government's OWN assessment committees
trackers.desc: A CONSERVATION BODY WITH A SEAT INSIDE THE PROCESS, not only outside it: WE ALSO PARTICIPATE IN VARIOUS PARLIAMENTARY COMMITTEES OF THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES, AS WELL AS GOVERNMENTAL TECHNICAL COMMITTEES ASSESSING THE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT OF PROJECTS AND PROGRAMMES. Cyprus has one of the smallest bases in this file. A body that sits on the technical committee assessing a project's environmental impact is in the room where the assessment is written — earlier than any objection, and the earliest point of entry recorded anywhere in this file. AND HOW IT DESCRIBES ITS FIRST OBJECTIVE, which tells a community what to ask it for: THE FIRST OBJECTIVE OF THE FOUNDATION IS THE APPLICATION OF PRESSURE FOR BETTER ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION. OUR POLICY ACTIONS ARE ACHIEVED THROUGH CONTINUOUS COMMUNICATION AND AWARENESS OF PEOPLE IN KEY POSITIONS WHO CAN INFLUENCE OUR DAILY LIVES, SUCH AS POLITICIANS AND TECHNOCRATS. THIS IS DONE THROUGH LETTERS, MEETINGS, PUBLICATIONS, SEMINARS AND EXHIBITIONS. Naming technocrats alongside politicians as the target is unusual and correct, because the official who drafts the assessment decides more than the minister who signs it. Founded in 1992 AS A CHARITABLE, NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION, it also runs a field studies centre for schools and universities.

trackers.name: Pakistan Information Commission (PIC)
trackers.desc: National right-to-information authority; the Pakistan Information Commission is the independent federal enforcement body under the Right of Access to Information Act 2017 — deciding complaints and directing federal bodies (provinces have separate commissions), Pakistan.

trackers.name: Punjab Information Commission (Pakistan)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI oversight body); Punjab Information Commission (Pakistan) — the national authority overseeing citizens’ right of access to public information (ICIC member).

trackers.name: Punjab Lok Sujag
trackers.desc: Pakistani investigative outlet reporting on governance and public resources.

trackers.name: Pakistan Information Commission
trackers.desc: Federal commission enforcing the Right of Access to Information Act — appeals against denials by executive bodies. — Holds to account: public bodies that hold records — find information-commissioner decisions and appeals.

trackers.name: Election Commission – Asset Declarations
trackers.desc: Legislator / public-official financial interest & asset declarations.

trackers.name: Justice Project Pakistan (JPP)
trackers.desc: Lahore legal-action NGO representing prisoners facing the death penalty and torture; maintains an open death-penalty database and data-driven research on executions, detention and prison conditions in Pakistan.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Pakistan
trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Pakistan — supreme court (Pakistan).

trackers.name: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics
trackers.desc: Pakistan's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Pakistan.

trackers.name: PPRA
trackers.desc: Pakistan's Public Procurement Regulatory Authority tender notices. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Pakistan, and for how much.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Pakistan
trackers.desc: Official Supreme Court judgments and case information. · Find here: judgments and case information of the Supreme Court of Pakistan.

trackers.name: SECP
trackers.desc: Pakistan's Securities and Exchange Commission corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Pakistan
