trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Pakistan — supreme court in Pakistan (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Find your province's act first — there is no national one
trackers.desc: WILDLIFE AND ENVIRONMENT ARE PROVINCIAL SUBJECTS, so no single national statute governs your site. In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa it is the KP Wildlife and Biodiversity Act 2015, replacing the NWFP Wildlife Act 1975 — and it must be read with the KP Province Forest Ordinance 2002, because where the two conflict on ‘acts prohibited’ the Forest Ordinance prevails. WHAT THE ACT GIVES YOU: a Wildlife Board chaired by the Chief Minister with the Environment Secretary as its Secretary, so the escalation point is political and named; provisions on protected areas and expressly on participatory management; power to constitute a Conservancy, which is the community-facing designation to ask about; and power to demarcate a National Park. HOLD THEM TO THE DEADLINE: an application to the Wildlife authority is to be disposed of within 60 days of receipt. A DIRECT PRECEDENT FOR URBAN ENCROACHMENT: Parliament passed the Islamabad Nature Conservation and Wildlife Management Act 2023 specifically to strengthen protection of Margallah National Wildlife Park against unregulated urban expansion.

trackers.name: Two warnings — unresolved ownership, and unstandardised management plans
trackers.desc: 1. A DESIGNATION DOES NOT SETTLE OWNERSHIP. Chitral Gol National Park was declared on 18 October 1984 — yet the case of ownership of the Park and of rights and privileges was recorded as still sub judice, with the technical team supplying the Wildlife Department scenarios for different court outcomes. Establish who owns the land and who holds customary rights before relying on a designation, because protection can sit on top of an unresolved title for decades. 2. THERE IS NO CODE FOR PROTECTED-AREA MANAGEMENT PLANS. Forest working plans follow an approved Forest Working Plan Code nationwide, but protected-area management planning is not yet institutionalised or standardised by provincial wildlife departments — so a designation may arrive with no enforceable management plan behind it, and asking for the plan is a fair and awkward question. AN ALLY FOR FOREST-RIGHTS HOLDERS: forest communities have criticised successive national forest policies as contrary to their rights and interests, and the Forest Ordinance 2002 has been targeted as exploitative by Sarhad Awami Forestry Itehad, representing small forest holders from Dir-Kohistan, Swat and other regions. AND A NEGOTIATED WIN: at Chitral Gol, communities agreed not to graze goats inside the park, with some villages giving up goats entirely — recorded as the cornerstone of community integration in the park's conservation.

trackers.name: WWF-Pakistan Small Grants — an individual can apply
trackers.desc: RUNNING SINCE 1986, and unusually open. It supports grassroots level organisations, research-based institutions, researchers and students — and its stated value is enabling small-scale conservation work and field projects by individual scientists as well as by institutions. Very few funds in this map admit an individual, which matters where no registered organisation exists yet: you can start the evidence work before you have a constitution. Its purpose also includes building the capacity of small grassroots organisations, not just funding outputs. PRIORITIES TO NAME IF THEY FIT YOUR SITE: marine turtles, snow leopards, the Indus River dolphin, sharks and vultures; and the critical ecosystems — mangrove forests, the Indus River Delta and coniferous forests. ALSO IN PAKISTAN: the GEF Small Grants Programme funds CSOs and CBOs directly with special focus on Indigenous Peoples, women and youth, and the share flowing directly to community organisations was raised to 72 percent for GEF-8 core projects, up from 62 in GEF-7.

trackers.name: PPAF Small Grants — funding to build your governance documents
trackers.desc: THE ANSWER TO A BARRIER THAT RECURS ACROSS THIS MAP. Finland, Italy, Poland, Greece and Hungary all gate environmental funding on the wording of your own constitution — and PPAF's Small Grants Project exists precisely to give technical assistance to small or new partner organisations to define their role and develop SOPs, by-laws and internal control systems, enhancing their capability rather than funding a single output. It is money to become fundable. PPAF is Pakistan's leading poverty reduction agency, receiving large annual government allocations alongside corporate and individual contributions. CHECK YOUR DISTRICT IS IN SCOPE — coverage is targeted at vulnerable areas, recorded as Balochistan (Khuzdar, Chagai, Kech, Zhob, Panjgur, Barkhan) and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Torghar, Kohistan, Buner, Lower Dir, Upper Dir, Bannu, Battagram, Mohmand, Kurram). PPAF works through partner organisations: MGPO, a non-profit working with mountain communities since 2001, has run community management and flood relief with PPAF support in Gilgit-Baltistan and maintains its own flood fund for District Ghanche.

trackers.name: Shehri-CBE — Karachi amenity plots, and they have had buildings sealed
trackers.desc: The case that shows what this outfit can make happen: in February 1998 it petitioned over the unlawful construction of 35 buildings near the Quaid's Mazar, and the Chief Justice converted the complaint into Constitutional Petition No. 160/1998 and ordered all 35 sealed. Formed in 1988 and registered under the Societies Registration Act XXI of 1860, Shehri-CBE works on urban land management and governance in Karachi — the conversion of amenity plots, parks, playgrounds and public land into commercial development — and it files public interest litigation rather than only campaigning. Other results on its own record: Constitutional Petition D-1571/2000 against the commercialisation of 11 Karachi Transport Corporation and 15 Sindh Road Transport Corporation bus depot plots; stopping encroachment on a Clifton road by Glass Towers; and saving Gutter Baghicha park through advocacy and litigation together. The timescale is the warning. Its Makro case produced a judgment in December 2009 and the associated civil review petition was still being disposed of in February 2024 — fifteen years between winning and finishing, which is the horizon to plan for, not the exception. Its scope is one city. This is Karachi, and largely the formal urban fabric of it: amenity plots, housing society land, bye-law violations, illegal commercialisation of residential zones. A rural or coastal fight elsewhere in Sindh needs a different organisation. Shehri-CBE, 88-R, Block-2, PECHS, Karachi; info@shehri.org; +92(21)34530646 and 34382298.

trackers.name: Pakistan Fisherfolk Forum — the coastal and delta ground Shehri's entry sends you away from
trackers.desc: This is a membership movement, and the number is the point: the Forum puts its membership at over 100,000 across the country with a minimum 35 per cent women's ratio, organised democratically among fisherfolk and peasants rather than run as a service you apply to. What it brings a community is people, a national platform and standing engagement with district and provincial government — not a lawyer, so pair it with counsel rather than expecting it to litigate for you. Its ground is water and the land beside it: fishing rights and historical fishing rights over entire water bodies for indigenous fishers, abolition of the contract system over inland waters, rehabilitation of the Indus Delta, marine pollution and deep-sea trawling, and the detention of fishermen. Agrarian and land reform sit on the same agenda, and the Forum opposes coal power projects and argues for renewables in their place, which is the shape most coastal Sindh development fights take. It also holds real disaster capability — early warning, rescue and evacuation, emergency response and recovery — which matters where a project's effect arrives as a flood rather than a bulldozer. Founded 1998; it holds the chair of the World Forum of Fisher People. Treat the membership figure with care. The Forum's own site says over 100,000, while partner networks publish 20,000 formal members with a governing board of 14 elected directors, and 25,000 volunteers. Ask what the figure means in your own district before relying on it. Two navigation notes. Go to pff.org.pk/about-pff rather than the homepage, which currently leads with seasonal food-donation appeals and says nothing about the campaigning work. And this is the Sindh and Balochistan coastal and delta organisation — an urban Karachi amenity-plot fight belongs with Shehri-CBE instead, and the two barely overlap. Secretariat at Ibrahim Hyderi, Karachi; info@pff.org.pk.

trackers.name: PCRWR — 24 water laboratories open to the public, and one of them is ISO 17025 accredited
trackers.desc: Twenty-four laboratories, and they take samples from the general public. The Council runs water quality laboratories across the three main hydrological units of the country, with analytical capability spanning microbiological, inorganic and organic contaminants for drinking, irrigation and industrial use, and its own description says they provide testing and advisory services to the general public, academia, industry, NGOs and local service providers. The escalation path is stated, which is unusual and useful. Where a district laboratory cannot run the test you need, samples can be sent up to the regional laboratory or to the National Water Quality Laboratory in Islamabad, so a community in a small district is not stuck with whatever the nearest bench can do. That national laboratory is ISO 17025 accredited and Pak-EPA certified; its stated parameter capability differs between the Council's own pages, one giving more than 200 parameters and another more than 114 for drinking, irrigation and wastewater, so ask for the current scope rather than assuming either. Eight regional centres sit at Lahore, Bahawalpur, Tandojam, Quetta, Peshawar, Gilgit, Muzaffarabad and Karachi, with district laboratories including Sialkot, Sahiwal, Multan, D. G. Khan, Sargodha, Faisalabad, Mianwali, Gujranwala, Hyderabad, Nawabshah, Badin, D. I. Khan, Loralai and Abbottabad. Its published monitoring is evidence you do not have to pay for. The National Water Quality Monitoring Programme report for 2020–21 put safe drinking water at 39 per cent of samples against 31 per cent in 2015 across 29 cities, and concluded that on that trajectory fewer than half the population would have safe water by 2030. City-level water quality profiles are published on the Council's site, so establish what is already on the record for your city before commissioning anything new. Its method statements are worth copying too. The February to March 2025 Islamabad monitoring sampled 267 sources — 97 tube wells, 88 filtration plants, 6 water works, 23 sumps and 53 household taps — with the sampling team drawn from the accredited national laboratory, joint sampling alongside the city water supply directorate, and analysis to the American Public Health Association Standard Methods, 24th edition. This is a federal research council rather than an advocate: it will measure and advise, and it will not campaign.

trackers.name: Environmental Protection Tribunals — a private person can complain, after thirty days' notice
trackers.desc: A private individual can bring a complaint against a polluter directly, without waiting for the agency to act. The tribunals were constituted under the Environmental Protection Act 1997, and the ministry describes them as the final fact-finding authority in environmental matters, entertaining both complaints and appeals against the agency's own actions, with private individuals able to seek relief against alleged polluters. The gate is a thirty-day notice, and missing it ends the complaint. An aggrieved person may complain only after giving not less than thirty days' notice to the federal or provincial agency, stating the alleged contravention and the intention to complain to the tribunal. That notice is the first document to write, it starts a clock, and it should be sent in a form that proves receipt. Appeals against an order or direction of the agency run to the tribunal within thirty days of communication, and an appeal from a final order or sentence of the tribunal goes to the High Court within thirty days, to be heard by a bench of not fewer than two judges. Two features cut in opposite directions. No other court may exercise jurisdiction over a matter within the tribunal's jurisdiction, which removes any choice of forum and makes getting the forum right unusually important. And where the tribunal finds a complaint false and vexatious to the complainant's knowledge, it may order the complainant to pay compensatory costs of up to one hundred thousand rupees — a real exposure for an individual, and a reason to assemble the evidence before filing rather than after. Check which Act applies to your province. Environmental protection is devolved and provinces have their own Acts mirroring the 1997 federal statute, so the tribunal, the notice period and the costs provision should be read from the provincial legislation covering your site rather than from the federal text. Lesser contraventions are tried by judicial magistrates of the first class specially empowered as environmental magistrates by the High Court.

trackers.name: Snow Leopard Foundation — community guards, forest closures and rangeland restoration across 50 sites
trackers.desc: The practical offer is a village-level conservation arrangement and the money to run it. Founded in 2008 and working at more than fifty sites across Gilgit-Baltistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Azad Jammu and Kashmir, its programmes include livestock vaccination, predator-proof corrals and community-based livestock insurance — the arrangements that make it worth a herding community's while to stop killing predators. Where the problem is that conservation costs the community something, that is the gap these schemes are built to close. Its ground work is land protection, not only species work. Under the national snow leopard and ecosystem programme, some 350 hectares of degraded rangeland and pasture in Chitral and Neelum were protected through reseeding, exclusion of livestock grazing and water harvesting; improved fodder was demonstrated across 50 hectares in eight valleys; community forest guards were engaged to secure regeneration in ten forest closures; and 42 community wildlife guards were engaged. A forest closure with a paid local guard is a concrete, replicable arrangement for ground a community wants left alone. It holds primary data on tourism impact. The foundation states it has primary data on how tourism has affected snow leopard habitat in Gilgit-Baltistan, gathered since 2008, and has run a conservation tourism pilot with camping infrastructure and a village information centre. For a community facing a tourism or road proposal in the northern mountains, that is an existing evidence base rather than a study to commission. Know the shape of the money. This is a research and conservation foundation working in partnership with provincial wildlife departments and community organisations and delivering donor-funded programmes; it is not a litigator, and it is not a grant window a village applies to directly. Separately, and reported rather than stated on its own site, communities in Gilgit-Baltistan and Chitral receive about eighty per cent of trophy hunting permit revenue through village conservation committees, which is the region's main community-controlled conservation income and worth establishing for your own valley. Contact info@slf.org.pk; programme presence is concentrated in Gilgit and Chitral.

trackers.name: Community-based trophy hunting programme — the 80 per cent community share and the formula that governs it
trackers.desc: Eighty per cent of the revenue goes to the community of the hunt area, and the guidelines that say so are published by the department itself. Under the guidelines for streamlining the community-based sustainable trophy hunting programme, the community share is eighty per cent, with the balance retained by the forest, parks and wildlife department. Reported accounts record the arrangement beginning in one valley in 1990, single exportable permits auctioned for sums in the hundreds of thousands of dollars, and one community receiving a cheque of more than forty-six million rupees for three hunts in a season. This is the largest community-controlled conservation income recorded anywhere in this research. The split inside that share is prescribed, not left to the village to decide. Ten per cent of the revenue is allocated to habitat management and the remaining seventy per cent to social and development sectors — and a conservancy that fails to use the revenue according to the prescribed formula may be punished, including by being deferred from trophy permits for up to five years. The formula is what stops the habitat money being absorbed into general village spending, and the penalty is what makes it real. The accounts are the application. A conservancy seeking permits must submit a progress report on how the current year's eighty per cent share was used across conservation, social and development sectors, its plans for using the coming year's share in the same sectors, and a completed criteria sheet, and must maintain proper accounts throughout. A community's bookkeeping is therefore not administrative housekeeping; it is what secures the next season's income. Three documents to ask the department for. The current guidelines, the criteria sheet, and the last utilisation report of the conservancy covering your area — together those show whether a conservancy exists near you, what it received and how it spent it. Applications are assessed on a scientific and technical basis under the published guidelines, and the programme is administered province by province, so terms and figures differ between Gilgit-Baltistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

trackers.name: Legal Aid and Justice Authority — free panel counsel, and the case-type limit to check before you apply
trackers.desc: Four steps, set out by the authority itself. Check whether you qualify on the income criteria and the case type; complete the application form online or visit the nearest legal aid office; submit the required documents for verification; and a panel advocate is assigned to handle the case. The authority states that special preference is given to disadvantaged women and children, and that it also promotes non-adversarial dispute resolution and advises the government on justice reform. Check the case type before the income, because that is where this route narrows. The statute establishing the authority is framed around providing legal, financial and other assistance for access to justice to poor and vulnerable people in criminal cases and matters ancillary to them. This is therefore the door when a confrontation over land has produced charges against residents — a common turn in the disputes recorded throughout this file — rather than the route for the underlying civil claim to the land itself. An entry that implied otherwise would send people to the wrong office at the worst moment. The panels are the machinery, and they are policed. The authority establishes panels of advocates and volunteers for each of its offices, may add to or remove from a panel any advocate or volunteer where it is satisfied that they have been derelict in duty or that removal is in the interest of justice, prescribes a code of conduct for panel advocates and volunteers, and prescribes the structure of fees payable for legal aid work. If an assigned advocate does nothing, dereliction of duty is a ground the authority itself holds — ask for the code of conduct and address the complaint to the authority rather than to the advocate. There is a statutory fund behind it. A legal aid and justice authority fund vests in the authority and is to be used for the purposes of the act, including the provision of legal, financial or other assistance, with the authority able to delegate its powers to its director-general and directors. Read this with the environmental tribunal entry already recorded for this country: that is where a community takes its complaint, and this is who defends the people who made it.

trackers.name: Punjab Land Records Authority — the fard, from a district record centre or online
trackers.desc: One authority holds the province's computerised record of rights. The land records authority operates under the provincial board of revenue as the body for digital land records and services, established under its own 2017 act after the long computerisation of the province's registers. The document it issues, the fard or record of rights, is what a sale, a loan, an inheritance claim or a court case rests on — and in this file's terms it is also what decides whether a household has standing to object to what is planned for a piece of ground. Where to get it, and what to do when you lack the numbers. Published guidance describes record centres in each district issuing fards and registering mutations, alongside an online portal and mobile applications for checking records and obtaining a fard, with search by owner name, father's name and identity number where the plot's khasra or khewat number is not known. A community that has never had the numbers is therefore not shut out: the record centre can search on a name. Two limits worth carrying, as reported. First, only records digitised into the system appear online, and older entries may exist solely in the tehsil office. Second, a view-only extract is not the certified copy that banks, courts and government offices require, and mutation entries can lag the main register, so a previous owner's name may still stand in the ownership column until the record is updated. Ask for the certified fard, and read the mutation entries rather than only the ownership column. Outside this province, ask the provincial board of revenue. Land records in Pakistan are provincial, and the equivalent record is held by each province's own board; this entry describes the Punjab system because it is the one with a published digital service and district centres. Read this with the environmental tribunal, legal aid authority and community trophy hunting entries already recorded for this country. This entry rests partly on published guidance rather than the authority's own text, and is recorded on that footing.

trackers.name: SECP eServices — a free company profile search, and the entities it does not cover
trackers.desc: One central registry, and the basic search is free. The securities and exchange commission maintains the country's central company registry under the 2017 companies act, and its electronic services portal provides the public search, document download and registration services. Published guides record that a basic company profile search costs nothing and returns the incorporation date, the registered office address, the incorporation number and the company's status, while certified extracts carry a modest fee. For a community, that is a name, an address and a date against the entity behind a project, obtained before any meeting. Know what is not in it. Partnerships and sole proprietorships are not registered with the commission at all; they register with provincial authorities under provincial law. A search that returns nothing therefore does not establish that an operator does not exist — it may mean the operator is a sole proprietor, or that the name was mis-spelled, and the next question is which provincial register applies. Treating an empty result as proof of nothing existing is the commonest way to misread a registry. Non-profits and foreign branches are in the same register. Alongside private and public limited companies the commission registers single-member companies, holding companies, non-profit companies formed under section 42 of the act, and the branches of foreign companies. Where a project is fronted by a local charitable company or by the branch office of a foreign parent, both are findable here rather than somewhere else. Carry the incorporation number. The company incorporation number is the identifier that follows a company through every other filing, and published guides advise searching the distinctive part of a name rather than its full legal form. Read this with the environmental tribunal, the water laboratories, the land records authority and the legal aid entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Pakistan Information Commission — a free appeal, civil court powers, and a penalty measured in days of salary
trackers.desc: The appeal is free, and silence starts the clock. Under the 2017 access to information act an appeal lies to the commission within thirty days after receiving a decision, or after the time limit for such a decision has passed, and the appeal is free of charge. A public body that simply does not answer has therefore started the appeal period running rather than closing the matter. The act also states that its provisions have effect notwithstanding other laws. The commission has civil court powers, and can fine by the day. After examining a complaint and the evidence, the commission may exercise the powers of a civil court to issue summons for witnesses or for records. Where an official is found to have acted wilfully to obstruct something the act requires, the commission may impose a penalty equal to that official's salary for one day, for a maximum of one hundred days. A sanction measured in the officer's own pay, day by day, is the sharpest personal penalty recorded anywhere in this file. Refusing to receive a request is itself a listed ground of complaint. The commission lists the matters it acts on as wrongful denial of access, non-provision of information within the stipulated time, refusal to receive and process a request from an applicant, and furnishing false, misleading or incomplete information. Two countries in this file now make the handling of a request, rather than the answer to it, a complaint in its own right — here and in the Maldives, where failing to give a receipt is appealable. The rules make the refusal letter work for you. Where a designated officer cannot provide the information within the prescribed time, the rules require an explanation in sufficient detail and in writing of the reasons for total or partial denial or delay, together with information about the remedy of complaint to the commission and its timeline; and public bodies must keep records indexed, catalogued and managed so that they are promptly available. Destroying a record which is at the time the subject of an application or appeal, or obstructing access with intent to prevent disclosure, is an offence. Read this with the land records authority, the environmental tribunals, the legal aid authority and the company registry entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: NAB — a notarised complaint with an undertaking attached, and the whistleblower statute beside it
trackers.desc: The jurisdiction reaches private persons, not only officials. The bureau states that its jurisdiction is not limited to public officials but extends to all those who engage in corrupt practices impacting public interests as defined in the accountability ordinance, and that it investigates and prosecutes corruption, money laundering, embezzlement, misappropriation of public funds, illegal assets, the cheating of members of the public at large and other financial crimes involving public officials or private individuals. A company that has obtained something at the public's expense is inside that description, which is not true of every anti-corruption body recorded in this file. Verification comes before anything else. The published process begins with a complaint from a citizen or an authority and then a complaint verification stage at which the bureau decides the merits, and since January 2024 a central complaint cell has handled complaints under a revised standard operating procedure, with the stated aim of focusing on legally cognizable complaints. Knowing that a filter sits at the front means a community should send its strongest material first rather than an outline. The filing requirements are heavy, and the undertaking is the sting. Published guidance on filing records that a complaint must fall within the corruption section of the ordinance, must set out details and attach relevant proofs, must carry the complainant's national identity card number and contact details, must be attested by a notary public, must state that the matter is not sub judice or under investigation elsewhere, and must include an undertaking that if the complaint is found after inquiry to have been wrong or made to defame or harm somebody the matter may be referred to a court which can impose imprisonment or a fine. That is the highest bar to entry recorded anywhere in this anti-corruption thread: prepare the evidence before filing, not after. A separate whistleblower statute sits beside it. Published accounts record a whistleblowers protection and vigilance commission act which protects those who report corruption and establishes a commission to investigate complaints, alongside provincial anti-corruption establishment acts and the prevention of corruption act. Ask which route carries protection before choosing where to file. Read this with the environmental tribunals, the water laboratories, the land records authority and the company registry entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Auditor-General — your district's own audit report, and the ladder from the DAC to the Public Accounts Committee
trackers.desc: Your district has its own published audit report. The auditor-general's office publishes reports on the accounts of district governments and local councils, of local government and housing departments, of metropolitan corporations and water and sewerage boards, of district education authorities and of public sector enterprises, each prepared by a directorate general of audit for that region or sector. A community can download the report covering its own district and read what was found, with sums attached to particular failures — one such report records water supplied without the membrane essential to purification, quantified in millions of rupees. Lender-financed projects are audited inside those same reports. Sections of local government audit reports cover projects financed by international lenders, listed under their loan and grant numbers — a water and sewerage services improvement project appears that way. Where a scheme is paid for by a development bank rather than from the provincial budget, its audit sits in the same document as the council's own. The escalation ladder is written into the report itself. The reports state that less significant observations are annexed and pursued with the principal accounting officer at departmental accounts committee level, and that in all cases where that officer does not initiate appropriate action the observation will be brought to the notice of the public accounts committee through the next year's audit report. A finding that goes unanswered therefore escalates on a schedule, and quoting that sentence back to an official who is sitting on a response is a lever a community can use without any further permission. Thematic audits of named projects appear as chapters. Reports include thematic audits of particular projects in named districts, and are laid before the national or provincial assembly and discussed by the public accounts committee; the auditor's budget is charged expenditure rather than voted, which is what secures the independence of the office. One limit worth knowing: the main body of a report carries only systemic issues and findings above a stated value, so a smaller local loss may sit in the annexes rather than the body. Read this with the accountability bureau, the environmental tribunals, the water laboratories and the land records entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Land records beyond Punjab — the Sindh and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa systems, and why a fard is not proof of title
trackers.desc: This file already had Punjab; these are the other systems. The board of revenue in Sindh operates a computerised land administration and revenue management system together with an electronic deed registration service, introduced on its own account to overcome the shortcomings of the manual process, improve the capture and storage of data and shorten registration processing time, with deed registration described as protecting property rights and forming one of the largest sources of provincial revenue. In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa the revenue and estate department runs its own land records portal offering online service delivery centre appointments, with the stated aim of improving land record service delivery and contributing to long-lasting tenure security. Establish which province's system holds the parcel before spending a day at the wrong counter. A fard is evidence of the record, not proof of title. Published legal explanations state the distinction plainly: ownership passes through a registered sale deed and the subsequent mutation, and the fard reflects that chain rather than establishing it. A developer producing a fard has shown a record entry, not a title — and the same limit applies to the community's own paper, which is why the underlying deed and mutation are what a dispute eventually turns on. Ask for the certified copy, and for the written statement about pending entries. Practical guidance published for purchasers is to request a certified copy of the fard and written confirmation of whether any pending mutation or court order is attached to the record, and to do this in person for high-value land and for any parcel that has changed hands more than once in a decade. A pending mutation is precisely what a quiet acquisition looks like in the record before anyone announces a project. Coverage is uneven, and that is the risk to plan around. Reported figures describe digitisation across nearly six thousand revenue units in Sindh, a geographic information programme digitising deh maps and integrating them with the digital records, and the identification of tens of thousands of acres of encroached state land; but the same accounts note that rural districts may not yet be fully digitised. An absent online record is therefore not evidence that no record exists — it is a reason to go to the district office. Read this with the Punjab land records, the environmental tribunals, the information commission and the auditor general entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The banks' association panel of approved valuers — a dated public list, three panels, and a recommended limit per firm
trackers.desc: A public, dated list of vetted valuation firms. The central bank entrusted the enlistment and monitoring of professional valuers to the banks' association, and under the prudential regulation on classification and provisioning the realisable value of mortgaged or pledged assets must be assessed by independent valuers on that association's panel. The association publishes its list of approved valuers as a dated document giving each firm's name, address, telephone number and principal executive, reissued as the panel changes. For a household or community that needs an independent valuation of land, that is a vetted directory with contact details, free to consult, in a country where finding any qualified professional is otherwise a matter of word of mouth. Three panels, and land sits in the first. The published guidelines divide the list into three: the first covering land and buildings — agricultural, residential and commercial land, and residential and commercial structures, excluding industrial plants and infrastructure; the second covering industrial plant and machinery and infrastructural construction such as telecommunication networks, roads and highways, railway tracks, water and sewerage lines and oil and gas transportation networks; and a third panel of industry and commodity specialists introduced in 2013. Matching the panel to the thing being valued matters: a firm valuing outside its panel is a point that can be made in writing. Each firm carries a recommended limit, and its performance is reviewed. Enlistment runs on a point-based criterion, and each valuer is assigned a recommended limit — the size of exposure against which a bank may accept that firm's reports, tied since 2013 to the total value of assets valued for a borrower. Enlisted valuers must submit data monthly on the valuations they carry out for the banking industry, are reviewed annually with limits recalculated, and non-compliance leads to de-listing. When a valuation is produced against a community, the questions are which panel the firm sits on and what its recommended limit is. What the panel does not cover. The association states that enlistment is not required for valuation reports which will not be used by the local banking industry, and that institutions not regulated by the central bank need not use enlisted valuers — so a report produced for a developer or a provincial body may sit entirely outside this system. All valuations must be signed by a professionally qualified valuer holding at least a graduate degree in the relevant field. Read this with the provincial land records, the environmental tribunals, the legal aid authority and the information commission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: NCHR — a complaint address in every province, civil-court investigative powers, and the power to join a case
trackers.desc: Each province has its own complaint address and email. The commission publishes member offices for the four provinces with street addresses, telephone numbers and dedicated provincial complaint email addresses, alongside a head office complaint cell number and a central complaints address. A complaint sent to the province's own member goes to a named office rather than a general national inbox, which matters in a country where distance from the capital is itself an obstacle. An online complaint cell has existed since 2014. It can join a case in court. Its published powers under the 2012 legislation include inquiring into and investigating complaints of human rights violations, submitting an application to a court to become a party to a case involving human rights, visiting places of detention, and recommending the amendment or adoption of laws; published reporting records that its investigative powers are equivalent to those of a civil court, and that the same Act provides for human rights courts to expedite the trial of offences related to violations. A body that can apply to join proceedings is a materially different ally from one that can only write a report. Negligence in prevention counts, not only the act itself. The commission is competent to receive petitions, to take notice on its own motion, and to inquire into violations of human rights or the abetment of them, or into negligence in the prevention of such violation by a public servant. Where an agency knew what was happening and did nothing, that inaction is a complaint in its own right — which is precisely the situation most communities in this file find themselves in. Independence, and volume. The commission is stated to work independently of government and to be directly accountable to the national parliament, with its financial and performance reports presented there annually; published reporting records more than seven thousand nine hundred complaints and own-motion actions handled and over a hundred and seventy visits to jails and detention areas. Read this with the environmental protection tribunals, the legal aid authority, the provincial land records and the approved valuers' panel entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Sujag — an outlet whose beat is the rural districts, and which asks readers to help develop a story
trackers.desc: Its stated beat is the districts the national press has left. Founded in 2015 and based in Lahore, with roots in a non-profit registered in the late 1990s doing cultural and political activism, the platform describes itself as reporting from rural districts and small towns that the mainstream media tend to ignore, and places itself in the space that established media either never covered or have vacated as they cut reporting networks and concentrated in a few metropolitan areas. A village dispute over land, water or a public works contract is therefore inside its beat rather than an exception to it, which is the opposite of the position a community occupies when it approaches a national daily. Readers are invited to help develop a story. Its published account of its own model asks supporters to visit regularly, to engage and share opinions and ideas, to take part in its events online and offline, to help develop a story, or to support it financially. That invitation is the practical opening for a community holding documents: it does not have to persuade an outlet to take an interest in a subject it has already said it wants. Ad-free, long-form, and in the language people read. Its business model is stated not to revolve around advertising revenue but around the support of its reader community; published profiles describe it as the country's only media organisation publishing long-form public interest journalism in Urdu, working from a modest office with a network of around ten freelance reporters engaged story by story across the country. Long-form reporting in the language most people actually read is what makes a rural case legible nationally rather than a paragraph in a city paper. It states its own stance. Its editors have said publicly that their journalistic ethos prioritises siding with the marginalised over neutrality, and its published work includes multi-part investigative series on the conditions of stigmatised workers and on district-level public services and health provision. Know that stance before approaching: it means the outlet will not present a community's case as one side of a balanced argument, and it also means an opponent will say so. Read this with the amenity plots organisation, the fisherfolk forum, the environmental protection tribunals and the national human rights commission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Antiquities protection — two hundred feet, a seventy-five year test, and the list your site may not be on
trackers.desc: Two hundred feet is the number to measure first. The antiquities legislation of 1975, amended in 1990, prohibits new construction and excavation around protected monuments within a distance of two hundred feet. That provision has been invoked in public argument over a metro line running past protected monuments, alongside the provincial premises preservation legislation, so it is a live provision rather than a dormant one. Where a project is near a protected antiquity, the distance from the boundary is the first fact to establish and the easiest to establish independently. Seventy-five years, and even the owner may not renovate. The Act redefined antiquities as objects older than seventy-five years. The owner of a protected immovable antiquity may not make any alteration or renovation in, or addition to, the antiquity, and may make only minor adjustments with the permission of the director; a protected immovable antiquity may not be used for any purpose inconsistent with its character or for any purpose other than one directly related to its administration and preservation; and no person may destroy, break, damage, alter, injure, deface or mutilate an antiquity, scribble, write or engrave any inscription or sign on it, or take manure from a protected antiquity. Protection reaches the adjoining ground and the way in. The protection extends to such portion of the land or water adjoining the site of an immovable antiquity as is reasonably required for fencing, covering or otherwise preserving it, and to the reasonable means of access to, and convenient inspection of, the antiquity. A project that blocks the approach to a monument is therefore within the Act's reach even where it does not touch the structure. Land containing an antiquity can be acquired, and the province is now the authority. Where the federal government has reasonable grounds to believe that any land contains an antiquity, it may direct the provincial government to acquire that land under the land acquisition legislation. Since the constitutional devolution of 2011, monuments, historical and archaeological sites and museums, with their staff, budgets and administrative powers, have sat with the provinces, each of which has its own statute — a special premises act, a cultural heritage preservation act, an antiquities ordinance, a heritage foundation act and a walled city act among them. Reporting on one province records roughly sixteen hundred sites protected under its own preservation act against a hundred and twenty-nine under the federal Act there, with some twelve hundred sites discovered over the years still awaiting registration. The question for any given site is therefore which list it is on, provincial or federal, and whether it has been registered at all. Read this with the amenity plots organisation, the provincial land records portals, the information commission and the rural investigative outlet entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Land acquisition — thirty days to object, six weeks to go to court, and the urgency clause that can switch the objection off
trackers.desc: Thirty days from the notification to object, in writing, with a hearing. Under the acquisition legislation still in force, a notification is published in the official gazette where land in a locality appears to be needed for a public purpose. Any person interested in land so notified may object to the acquisition within thirty days from the date of publication of that notification. The objection must be made to the collector in writing, and the collector must give the objector an opportunity of being heard — in person, by a person authorised by them, or by a pleader — and must then, after hearing the objections and making any further inquiry considered necessary, make a report. The date of the notification also fixes the point at which market value is assessed, so it is the single most important date in the file. The urgency provision can switch that right off. Where the commissioner is of opinion that the urgency provisions apply, the commissioner may direct that the objection provisions shall not apply at all, in which case the declaration may be made at any time after the notification. A community told that there is no objection period should ask, in writing, whether such a direction has been made and on what date — because the answer is either a document or a concession that the thirty days is still running. Six weeks to require a reference to the court, on four possible grounds. A person interested who has not accepted the award may apply in writing to the collector requiring the matter to be referred to the court, whether the objection is to the measurement of the land, the amount of compensation, the person to whom it is payable, or the apportionment among those interested; the application must state the grounds. It must be made within six weeks of the award where the applicant was present or represented when the award was made, and otherwise within six weeks of receiving the collector's notice or six months from the award, whichever expires first. Case law records that a dispute about who owns the land may be referred by the collector under a separate provision, but that the amount of compensation cannot be raised that way — the reference is the route for quantum. Fifteen per cent on top, and interest on what was withheld. In addition to market value the court awards a sum of fifteen per centum on that value in consideration of the compulsory nature of the acquisition, and reported judgments record awards of compulsory acquisition charges together with additional compensation and simple interest on the excess amount where compensation was enhanced. Provinces have amended the Act separately, so check the provincial version that applies. Read this with the provincial land records systems, the banks' association panel of approved valuers, the legal aid and justice authority and the information commission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Katchi abadi regularisation — proprietary rights for people already living there, a survey list to be on, and equal title for husband and wife
trackers.desc: The settlement itself can be declared, and the declaration carries proprietary rights. Provincial legislation provides for the regularisation, development and improvement of informal settlements: the director-general prepares schemes for development, improvement or regularisation, including the grant of proprietary rights to the dwellers, and those schemes take effect on being sanctioned by government. The schemes are also required to deal with the rehabilitation of occupants — in the same settlement, or where that is not possible in another area — and with community facilities including water supply, sewerage, electricity, gas and other utilities. For a settlement facing clearance, the question to put in writing is whether it has been declared, and if not, what is needed for declaration. Being on the survey list is the qualifying fact. The executing authority's own published account of the procedure records that it carries out site verification and re-verification of the record for enlisted and declared settlements; that demand notices are issued to eligible dwellers on the criteria that the dweller's name exists in the survey list and the dweller furnishes proof of continuous occupation; that it then processes the grant of proprietary rights and recovers the cost of land and development charges at notified rates; and that it takes action against later encroachers. Two documents therefore decide everything: the survey entry, and the evidence of continuous occupation. Both are worth assembling before a scheme is announced. Thresholds, cut-off dates and equal title. Reporting on the provincial amendment of 2012 records criteria including the existence of at least forty dwelling units for a settlement to be considered, surveys by the district and town administrations, and evaluation of the revenue record and the settlement map; it also records that the amendment grants equal proprietary rights to husband and wife or wives. The eligibility cut-off matters as much as the threshold: the original Act reached those who had built on state land before the end of 2006, and the amendment extended the date to 2011, other provinces having their own dates. In the southern province the right takes the form of a long lease. A high court order describes the parallel system there: regulations made under the 1987 Act set the criteria for declaring an area a katchi abadi, and once a scheme is developed, proprietary rights are conferred on persons in possession within the declared area, those rights taking the form of a lease for ninety-nine years. Read this with the urban amenity plots organisation, the provincial land records systems, the legal aid authority and the acquisition procedure entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: IEE and EIA review — thirty days between the newspaper notice and the hearing, and the published timeline for every step
trackers.desc: The hearing cannot be held sooner than thirty days after the notice. The provincial environmental department publishes the approval process as a timeline, step by step against the regulation that governs each. It records that public participation runs on a thirty-day clock: the date of the public hearing shall not be earlier than thirty days from the date the notice is published in one local and one national daily newspaper. A hearing convened at shorter notice is therefore convened contrary to the published procedure, and the notice date is the fact to fix first. The rest of the timeline is published too. The same document sets out preliminary scrutiny within ten working days, at which the agency may accept the report, require the proponent to make good shortcomings, or return it for revision; the proponent's reply to those shortcomings; then the review process itself, which runs forty-five days for a preliminary examination and ninety days for a full assessment. The application must be filed with the prescribed number of paper and electronic copies, the schedule form and the fee receipt. Knowing the stage a project has reached tells a community how long it has, and a delay against the published timeline is a question with an addressee. Which report a project needs is decided by schedule. The environmental legislation of 1997 requires either a preliminary examination or a full assessment, and the review regulations of 2000 set the procedure for report review, public hearing and monitoring, with one schedule listing the project categories requiring the preliminary examination and another those requiring the full assessment. Checking which schedule a project falls under is the first substantive argument available: the difference decides whether a hearing happens at all and how long the review takes. What the agency must do with comments, and the documented weakness. Published analysis of the regulations records that the notice of availability of the report for public inspection fixes the date, time and place of the hearing; that the agency shall collate, tabulate and duly consider all comments before deciding; and that there is no requirement for it to publish a response to those comments. The same body of commentary records the practical weakness — hearings advertised in newspapers whose readership may not be equipped to assimilate a technical notice, with recommendations that hearings be held in regional languages at accessible venues and that assessment documents be freely available on agency websites. Since environmental powers were devolved to the provinces in 2010, check the version of the regulations your province applies. Read this with the environmental protection tribunals, the provincial land records, the information commission appeal and the acquisition procedure entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Judgment search and case status — the supreme court's own search, and the provincial high court's reported judgments
trackers.desc: The supreme court runs its own judgment search and case status pages. Alongside a judgment search, the court publishes latest judgements, a judgements category, cause lists, online case status and case information pages, all reachable from its own site. For a community whose dispute has reached or may reach the highest court, that combination answers two different questions: what the court has decided on this kind of point, and where a particular case has got to. Case status is the practical half. The online case status and case information pages let a case be followed by its own identifiers rather than through a lawyer's report, which matters where a community is affected by litigation it is not itself conducting — a challenge by a developer to a refusal, or a neighbouring village's petition on the same scheme. The court also publishes cause lists, so a hearing date can be confirmed independently. The provincial high court publishes reported judgments separately. The largest provincial high court maintains a reported judgments section listing judgments approved for reporting, with a search form and a latest-reported listing. Approved-for-reporting is a meaningful filter: those are the judgments the court itself considers to have precedential value, which is what a community wants when it is trying to establish a point rather than to follow a case. Note the court's own copyright statement on its materials before reproducing anything beyond ordinary use. How to work it. Search the high court of your own province first, because most land, acquisition and permit disputes are decided there; use the supreme court search for the general principle; and record the case number, the year and the bench for anything useful. The acquisition entry recorded elsewhere in this country's entries turns on a six-week reference and on which schedule a project falls under — both points on which reported judgments will exist. Read this with that entry and with the environmental protection tribunals, the legal aid authority and the information commission entries already recorded here.

trackers.name: Provincial charity commissions — the officer who sanctions a collection depends on its reach and its length
trackers.desc: Charity registration and the sanctioning of collections are provincial, and the level of officer depends on how far and how long you collect. The largest province's charities legislation of 2018 established a commission to register and regulate charities, fund-raising appeals and the collection of charitable funds. Registration authority is tiered: the commission where a charity's operation extends to the whole province or two or more districts; the deputy commissioner where it does not extend beyond the district; the assistant commissioner where it extends only to a tehsil. Sanctioning a collection is tiered the same way, with the commission sanctioning where the collection is proposed from the whole province or two or more districts, or for a period of more than twelve months, and the deputy and assistant commissioners sanctioning smaller collections. A village appeal for six months is therefore an assistant or deputy commissioner matter, not a provincial one. Misapplication is presumed against everyone involved. The Act provides that where any part of donations collected for a charitable fund is used for a purpose other than that for which it was collected, or is otherwise misapplied or misappropriated, every person concerned with the collection or administration — promoter, collector or recipient — is deemed to have committed the misapplication unless they prove it happened without their knowledge and that they used all due diligence to prevent it. Custody of a charitable fund may not be transferred to another person without prior written approval of the commission or the sanctioning authority. Keep the fund in named hands, keep the purpose narrow, and keep records. What registration requires, and where it is done. Every organisation required to register must provide the registering authority with the objectives of the charity, the source or sources of its income, the nature of its spending and other prescribed documents; the province operates an online registration portal, with registration rules and inspection and audit rules of 2023 cited alongside the Act as the governing framework. A charity trustee must prepare an annual statement of accounts, and tampering with, concealing or destroying collection records carries a penalty. Other provinces have their own. Neighbouring provinces have enacted their own charities legislation and commissions with comparable registration and reporting duties, so check the province the collection will run in rather than assuming a national rule. The commission also publishes information for donors to check registered charities. Read this with the katchi abadi regularisation, the environmental protection tribunals, the legal aid authority and the reported judgments entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Provincial mining concessions — minor minerals auctioned in the press, five-year leases, and a one-month objection window on occupying land
trackers.desc: Surface minerals are auctioned publicly, and the department says so. The largest province's mines and minerals department states that its work includes granting and regulating mining concessions, monitoring concessions periodically through field offices, defending litigation in the high court and the apex court, and monitoring the auction committee and deciding offered bids according to the potential of the area; and that surface minerals such as silica sand, fireclay and bentonite are granted through open auction for five years after due publicity in the press, renewable for further five-year terms on satisfactory performance. A community can therefore watch the press notices for an auction over land near it, and can ask what the concession's five-year term and renewal record are. The rules name who decides by the size of the project. The concession rules of 2002 provide that for major minerals the director general decides projects with capital of three hundred million rupees or above and the director decides smaller ones, while minor minerals are decided by the director or a delegated authority; and they define minor minerals to include ordinary sand, ordinary stone, limestone, sandstone, building stone and decorative stone. Practitioner material records that minor mineral leases are granted through open auction with a stated application fee credited to a named government receipt account, that royalty is paid on the quantity dispatched from the leased area at rates in named rules and periodically notified, and that a notification requires concessions for specific minerals to be granted through competitive bidding or sealed tenders. A neighbouring province's rules give a written objection window before land is occupied. Its concession rules provide that a holder of a mineral title must give the licensing authority one month's previous notice in writing specifying the land proposed to be occupied and the purpose, and that the authority may within one month state objections on grounds of public interest, with the holder barred from proceeding until those objections are dealt with. Where that rule applies, the notice period is the moment to put the public interest argument in front of the licensing authority. There is an appeal ladder, and courts expect it to be used. Reported judgments record a petition dismissed as non-maintainable because the petitioner had not exhausted the appeal and revision remedies provided under named rules, and record the authorities' discretion to depart from first-come-first-served and to allocate by sealed bid or open auction, and to cancel an auction. Exhaust the internal remedies before going to court. Read this with the katchi abadi regularisation, the environmental protection tribunals, the charity commissions and the reported judgments entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Land use classification and reclassification rules — objections in two national and one local newspaper, a public hearing on a fixed date, and proceedings kept for five years
trackers.desc: Reclassifying land for a project requires a published invitation to object and a hearing, and the record must be kept. The province's land use classification, reclassification and development rules provide that before a land use re-classification scheme for a project area is approved the city district government or tehsil municipal administration shall invite objections or suggestions by public notice indicating the salient features of the draft scheme on its website, to the key stakeholders of the area, and in at least two leading national and one local newspaper; shall arrange a public hearing on a specified date, time and place; and shall maintain the record of proceedings for a minimum of five years after approval. The same three steps apply to a draft peri-urban structure plan. Ask for that record: it is the evidence of what was said at the hearing, and it must exist for five years. Objections have to be taken into account before signature. The rules provide that the chief metropolitan planner signs and stamps the draft re-classification scheme prepared after taking into consideration the public objections and suggestions, before the director general forwards it onward. A scheme signed without that consideration is defective on the face of the rules. The notified plan is obtainable, and a park proposal has its own notice. The rules require the authority to notify an approved peri-urban structure plan within seven days of approval, and provide that a person may, on payment of a fee, obtain a certified copy of the notified plan; they also provide that a proposal to establish a recreational park requires the district planning and design committee's approval and publication of the proposal in a leading daily newspaper and on the website, inviting public objections and suggestions. The area between the external limits of the peri-urban area and of the controlled area is to be notified as agriculture area. Who holds the power now. The local government legislation of 2022 provides that a local government shall, subject to any special law on preparation and approval of regional, master and land use plans, approve spatial plans, zoning and land use plans including classification and reclassification of land as per the approved master plan; enforce building control; prepare, approve, execute and manage development plans; regulate development and management of site development and housing schemes; and undertake landscape, parks, monuments and municipal ornamentation. Read this with the amenity plots entry, the assessment hearing entry, the land acquisition entry and the land records entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Joint Forest Management rules and guzara forests — a village committee with a plan the department must implement with it, and forests most of which communities already own
trackers.desc: A province has rules that put a village committee inside forest management. The joint forest management community participation rules of 2004, made under named sections of the provincial forest ordinance and published in the provincial code, provide for a village development committee with a general body, an annual general body meeting and extraordinary meetings confined to the issue for which they are convened; for the committee to elect a chairperson, secretary and treasurer from among themselves; for a women's organisation alongside it; and for the general body to extend the committee's tenure for a limited further period. They provide that a plan is prepared for the forest management unit falling within the village's jurisdiction, that the plan shall be part of the village plan, and that the joint forest management committee and the women's organisation shall implement and monitor it under a partnership arrangement with the department. A village that wants a say in what happens to the forest above it is asking to constitute these bodies. Most of the forest is already community-owned, and that is officially reported. Press reporting citing a conservation union assessment records that the provincial forest department owns only a small share of forests, mostly reserve forests, while the great majority are owned by individual landowners, communities and joint owners — protected forests concentrated in one division and guzara forests mostly in another. It records that local communities and individual owners earned royalty from protected and guzara forests when harvesting took place, and that since harvesting was banned owners have been deprived of that share. Ownership is therefore usually the starting point in this province, not a claim to be established. The ordinance names the guzara rights and their limits. The forest ordinance's own contents include rights in guzara forests and wastelands, management of guzara forests and wastelands, management of wastelands at the request of owners, apportionment of net profit, power to acquire a guzara forest or wasteland, treatment of encroachment on common land, and acts prohibited in guzara forests and wastelands. A legal summary records that landowners of a village whose boundaries include guzara forests and wastelands may use trees and forest produce free of charge but may not sell any tree, timber or other forest produce growing on such lands. Know that limit before agreeing to any deal with a contractor. The settlement machinery is where rights are recorded. The ordinance provides for a forest settlement board with powers of inquiry, orders on claims to rights of pasture or forest produce, a record to be made by the board, commutation of rights, and appeals from its orders — with notifications declaring a forest reserved published in translation in the neighbourhood of the forest. Read this with the snow leopard community guards, the trophy hunting share, the land records and the mining concession entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Provincial Water Act 2019 — abstraction and disposal licences for groundwater, a public register of every licence granted, and enforcement orders owed to affected persons
trackers.desc: Caution on scope: this is a provincial Act, in force in one province only, and a body with a near-identical name exists across the border — the sources here are this country's own. A public register lists every abstraction and disposal licence granted. The Act provides that the authority shall maintain, in paper and electronic form, a register including details of abstraction licences or disposal licences granted to water undertakers and sewerage undertakers. That register is the document to ask for when a factory or scheme is drawing groundwater beside a village. Licences are time-limited and conditional, and sub-licences are counted against the parent limit. The Act provides that every abstraction and disposal licence shall be in the prescribed form and valid for a fixed duration, which may or may not be extendable, subject to terms and conditions the commission prescribes; and that where an undertaker allows a person a sub-licence to abstract water within or near its premises for domestic purposes only, the water so abstracted forms part of the overall abstraction limit granted to that undertaker. A sub-licence therefore cannot be used to enlarge the total. An enforcement order is owed to affected persons, not only to the regulator. The Act provides that an order shall specify the acts or omissions which in the authority's opinion constitute or would constitute contravention of conditions or requirements, and any other fact justifying it; that it shall require the undertaker to do or not do specified things and take effect at the earliest practicable time; that it may be revoked or modified; and that the obligation to comply with a final or provisional order is a duty owed both to the authority and to any person who may be affected by the contravention. That last clause is what gives a neighbour standing to insist on compliance. What the commission controls, and the older rule it displaces. Published analysis records that the commission's remit covers surface water resources as defined in the 1873 canal and drainage legislation, water in lakes or reservoirs, water in drains and groundwater resources, with authority to issue licences for abstraction and disposal of groundwater for agricultural, domestic, industrial and mining purposes; that previously the right to use groundwater rested on colonial easement law tying abstraction to land ownership, so most users needed no licence; and that questions remain about how the licensing system will be set up in practice. Ask under which regime an existing tubewell claims its right. Read this with the water laboratories, the environmental tribunals, the land use reclassification rules and the provincial mining concession entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Provincial fisheries ordinances — the power to declare any water a sanctuary for fish, the explosives and poisoning offences, and the abolition of the contract system on one province's freshwater bodies
trackers.desc: Caution on scope: fisheries here are provincial, so the applicable statute depends on the province — the two described below are one province's ordinance and another's ordinance as amended. Any water can be declared a sanctuary for fish. One province's 1961 fisheries ordinance lists among its sections the power to declare any water to be a sanctuary for fish, alongside the appointment of inspectors of fisheries, the power to lease out the right to catch fish in any water other than private water for a period not exceeding three years, the lessee's power to issue permits, quality control, and the powers to compound offences and make rules. Asking for a sanctuary declaration over a threatened stretch uses a power the statute already names. Explosives, poison and undersized fish are separate offences. The same ordinance provides that no person shall use dynamite or other explosive substance in any water with intent to catch or destroy fish; that no person shall put any poison, lime or noxious material into any water with such intent; that no person shall kill, capture or possess a species listed in the schedule below the size specified against it; and that nets, fixed engines and traps may not be used without a permit or licence. It provides for a magistrate's search warrant where an offence is believed to have been, or be likely to be, committed, for search and arrest without warrant, for a duty on village headmen and watchmen, and makes inspectors public servants. The district officer holds the water inside the district. The ordinance's explanation records that the district fisheries officer is responsible for conservation, management and development of district water areas and is empowered to lease out fishing rights of water confined within the district boundary. That is the office to approach about a particular lake or reach. In another province, the contract system on freshwater bodies was abolished after a long campaign. Reporting of a fisherfolk organisation records that after a ten-year struggle the provincial government abolished the contract system on freshwater bodies by amending its 1980 fisheries law; that the provincial fisheries department maintains a numbered list of over a thousand water bodies, with district lists beneath it; and that fishermen hold licences issued under the amended Act and the 1983 rules by named district and directorate offices, in a case where landlords were said to be barring them from a lake. Read this with the water act licences, the environmental tribunals, the water laboratories and the land reclassification entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Provincial wildlife and biodiversity Act — eight categories of protected area including the site of special scientific interest and the conservancy, a refuge where all hunting is prohibited, and facilities tied to the assessment
trackers.desc: Caution on scope: wildlife here is provincial, so which Act applies depends on the province; the one described is one province's 2015 statute. Eight categories count as protected areas, and the list itself is the menu. National reporting of eleven new notifications under the Act records that under it the national park, conservancy, wildlife sanctuary, site of special scientific interest, wildlife refuge, biosphere reserve, national natural heritage site and game reserve are all called protected areas; that the forestry, environment and wildlife department declared thousands of hectares across named divisions as protected areas by separate notifications, raising the province's protected area coverage from just over ten per cent to almost fifteen; and that administration of sanctuaries, parks, biosphere reserves, conservancies and scientific sites was shifted to a named conservator, with demarcation to follow. Where a site does not fit a national park, one of the other seven may. A wildlife refuge bans hunting outright, by gazette notification. The Act provides that the government or an authorised officer may, by notification in the official gazette, declare any area to be a wildlife refuge where hunting of all wild animals shall be prohibited, managed as prescribed or as provided in the management plan. That is the simplest designation to ask for over a defined area. Facilities inside protected areas must conform to the assessment's recommendations. The Act provides that any facility provided under the stated subsections shall be in conformity with the recommendations of the environmental impact assessment or initial environmental examination under the provincial environmental protection legislation — the same assessment process already recorded in this bucket with its thirty-day notice and hearing. What the Act sets up, and what can go wrong. Published description records the Act consolidating wildlife law with chapters on wildlife organisations, hunting, possession and display, trade and traffic, protected areas, participatory management and ex-situ conservation; establishing a wildlife force and a wildlife and biodiversity board to advise on policy and oversee the fund, with audit by the auditor-general; prohibiting set guns, explosives, automatic weapons, sedative projectiles and electrical devices for hunting; and stating among its aims securing benefits for local communities and conservation through community participation. Published material records one national park declared in 2022 facing a proposed de-notification — the reminder that designation can be undone. Read this with the trophy hunting share, the joint forest management rules, the assessment review and the fisheries ordinances entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Public interest litigation and the green benches — relaxed standing that lets a citizen go straight to a High Court, the 1994 holding that made environment a right to life question, and the commission a court created to force implementation
trackers.desc: Standing was relaxed so that a citizen can approach a High Court or the Supreme Court directly. Published analysis records that from 1993 the most important environmental claims have been decided by the High Courts and the Supreme Court in their constitutional jurisdiction under the broad head of public interest litigation, and that expansion of the scope of fundamental rights and relaxation of the rules of standing have allowed litigants to approach those courts directly, to challenge state action as well as state inaction. Inaction being challengeable is the part that matters where a community's complaint is that nothing is being done. The 1994 holding is the one to cite. Published reporting records that the first environmental public interest case, in 1990, was brought against a government building and its stone crushing activity in a national park; and that the watershed came in 1994, when the Supreme Court held that the right to a clean and healthy environment was part of the fundamental right to life guaranteed in the constitution, a lawyer quoted saying that since then the whole judiciary has moved in the direction of protecting that right. A farmer's own petition produced orders against the government.
