Case material records a farmer filing public interest litigation alleging that government inaction and delay in implementing the national climate policy violated fundamental rights to life and dignity; that the High Court's green bench declared the matter a clarion call for the protection of fundamental rights, in particular of the vulnerable and weak segments of society who are unable to approach this Court; and that although the right to a healthy environment was not explicitly in the constitution, the court recognised it as part of the rights to life and human dignity and tied those rights to the government's duty to undertake mitigation and adaptive measures. What the court did next is the practical model. Reporting records that within a month of hearing the case the judge had summoned the country's main officials, appointed named focal points for each government department, addressed departments' individual capacity needs, and appointed a named commission to ensure implementation of the framework, with the commission tasked to produce implementation targets by a stated date; later analysis records the court issuing directions to federal and provincial governments to comply with their responsibilities. Read this with the environmental tribunals, the judgment search, the legal aid authority and the assessment review entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Provincial air quality index — a dated agency order setting how the index is calculated and disseminated, forty-one stations across seventeen districts, and a live dashboard by city and pollutant
trackers.desc: Caution on scope: environment is provincial here, and what follows is one province's order and network. The index has a dated, numbered order behind it, made under named statutory powers. The provincial environmental protection agency's 2025 order, issued under stated subsections of the 1997 provincial environmental protection legislation, provides for the calculation and dissemination of the air quality index of the province's different districts; recites that the environment and climate change department has established a network of forty-one air quality monitoring stations in seventeen districts providing continuous ambient data calculated on criteria pollutant concentrations; and recites that, under the 2017 smog policy and action plan read with the 2023 provincial clean air policy, the index is calculated on twenty-four hourly or eight hourly average concentrations of those criteria pollutants whose measured values are available — coarse and fine particulates, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide and ozone. Where a reading is quoted at you, that order states what it is and how it was made. The dashboard is public, by city, station and pollutant. The provincial index dashboard carries live readings across named cities and districts, listing more than thirty by name, with selectable views for the index, fine and coarse particulates, nitrogen oxides, sulphur dioxide, carbon monoxide and ozone, a twenty-four hour series, a seven-day heatmap and station-level data; published network listings record the provincial network appearing as a named real-time sensor network. That is the record a community sets its own readings against. The index's own history includes a challenge to it. Published material records that after a court order the provincial environment council approved a smog action plan and adopted an index classification in 2017; records that classification criticised as too lax and underreporting severity, with a stated concentration read as satisfactory on the provincial scale while an international scale reads it as unhealthy; and records that in November 2019 three children asked a court to declare the provincial index illegal and unreasonable. It records that at that time authorities published no real-time fine particulate data, all data coming from non-government sensors and a foreign mission, with ten stations then planned for the provincial capital. Read this with the environmental approval timeline, the environmental tribunals, the green benches and the provincial water Act entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: PILAP — a public interest law association with pro bono lawyers, a research-then-information-request-then-litigation method, and a record of taking issues proposed by citizens and local campaigns
trackers.desc: A registered association of lawyers takes public interest cases, and its method is published in order. The association records itself as non-profit and apolitical, established by a group of concerned citizens in 2011 and registered under the societies registration legislation, funded by members through fees and donations, and supported by a team of pro bono lawyers alongside an operations team. It records its method as first detailed research on a public interest issue, then advocacy, then litigation; and other published material sets the same sequence out as research, then filing right to information requests, then pursuing the litigation front. For a community with an issue but no case yet, that order is the useful part: the information request comes before the lawsuit. Its issue list is chosen partly from what citizens and local campaigns propose. Published material records that the association files numerous information requests each year on issues of public interest, and that topics are often selected through partnerships with organisations — recording one expressway request proposed by a named concerned citizen and a climate group, and another on a storm drain proposed by a named local movement to assist its advocacy — and otherwise chosen from current events, giving as examples drainage project details sought after urban flooding and a national park request filed in light of reports of encroachment on public lands. A community with a documented problem can therefore propose the request rather than only ask for a lawyer. Its recorded results include a river commission and a court-ordered deadline. Published material records among its achievements a river commission on the discharge of untreated sewage and waste, with the high court ordering the commission to oversee progress and set up treatment plants before water enters the river; and records an intervener application before the Supreme Court in a petition questioning unregulated encroachments and the failure of authorities to maintain and develop public parks and amenity plots. A litigation database records its 2022 constitutional petition over the government's failure to implement the 2017 climate legislation, in which a three-judge Supreme Court bench ordered the federal government to establish the climate authority within fourteen days and complete establishing the climate fund. Read this with the amenity plots organisation, the green benches, the information commission and the environmental tribunals entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The climate justice alliance and its member organisations — a named network including a legal collective and research institutes, and the coalitions that have marched against coal and canal projects
trackers.desc: There is a named alliance for energy transition disputes, and its members are listed. Published material records an alliance for climate justice and clean energy as a network organisation working toward the country's just energy transition, running a people's tribunal campaign, and names its member organisations as including a humanitarian, environmental and development consortium, an alternative law collective, a knowledge forum, a policy research institute for equitable development, and a rural news outlet — the outlet already recorded in this bucket. A community fighting a power or mining project therefore has a coalition with a lawyer collective inside it. The coalitions that turn out for these fights are named too. The same material records a climate march joined by more than 3,000 people, organised by named farmer, peasant, labour education, railway workers', women workers' and fisherfolk organisations; records a separate march in the port city organised by the fisherfolk forum with the consortium, the research institute, a railway workers' union, a political party and a brick kiln workers' union; records the fisherfolk forum running a six-week campaign demanding a coal phaseout and an end to coal mining in a named desert district; and records a group working for scheduled caste communities organising a protest over human rights violations in coal mining. It records a provincial community foundation established in 2001 supporting outreach to young people, women and girls, low-income urban residents and rural communities, in a disaster risk reduction network and accredited with an international climate fund. Water disputes have their own bodies, and one drafted a citizens' policy. A water foundation records promoting multi-stakeholder participatory platforms on water, and records a think tank platform which developed recommendations for a national water policy framework, recognised as the first citizens' water policy, plus a universities-for-water network of nine member universities compiling water-related degree programmes. Reporting records a students' alliance and a women's movement among those mobilising against a canal project, and a concerned citizens' alliance convening water experts against it. Read this with the fisherfolk forum, the amenity plots organisation, the public interest lawyers and the rural newsroom entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The Legal Aid Society and the free-legal-aid directories — a toll-free 24/7 legal advice line, community legal clinics with field advocates, and published lists of pro bono providers by city
trackers.desc: There is a toll-free legal advice line that runs around the clock. The society publishes a 24-hour, seven-day legal helpline with a toll-free number, and records that the call centre has provided legal guidance and support to thousands of people seeking clarity and assistance on everyday justice needs. It publishes its floor, building and street address in a named city, with two telephone numbers. For someone whose land problem starts at night or in a village far from a court, a free number that answers is the first practical resource. Its clinics bring advocates to the community rather than the reverse. Published description records community legal awareness sessions conducted across targeted districts, where community members in small groups, with an emphasis on male and female participation, are educated on their legal rights through materials in their native languages and then given legal advice by field advocates who accompany the field trainers; and records those clinics used across its thematic streams, including legal property rights for women and alternative modes of dispute resolution. It records building a network of paralegals to create sustainable, community-led legal support, and outreach ranging from SMS and social media to rickshaw and door-to-door campaigns. Its remit and reach are stated. The society records itself as a not-for-profit non-governmental organisation active since 2013, whose mission is to connect vulnerable and disempowered end users of justice with effective and expedient services, working with actors in the justice system to improve their capacity to address citizens' grievances; and records its teams' collective experience as extending across all parts of the country, including three named regions, with one stated goal responding to societal needs aggravated through climate emergencies and establishing foundational knowledge at grassroots levels. Directories list the alternatives by city. A published directory of free or subsidised legal help records twenty-seven organisations nationally and fifteen in one named city, describing each — including a trust running legal aid alongside water and trafficking work, and a women lawyers' body whose members provide pro bono help to marginalised women — and notes which run hotlines. Read this with the public interest law association, the rights commission, the fisherfolk forum and the amenity plots entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Hisaar Foundation — eleven urban and rural water partnerships, a women and water network with chapters and 250-plus members, and university and professional databases a community can draw expertise from
trackers.desc: Water partnerships have been built at local level, and the count is published. The foundation records having worked over fourteen years on building cooperation to change the water paradigm through its water partnerships and women and water network, and records forming 11 urban and rural water partnerships at different levels and 12 women and water networks across the country. It records 14 emergency support campaigns responding to droughts, floods, earthquakes and other disasters, and cooperation with 25 implementing partner organisations and 34 sponsoring partner organisations, including rural support programmes, universities, banks and companies, a chambers of commerce federation, and non-governmental and community-based organisations. For a community in a water dispute, a standing local partnership is a table that already exists. The women's network is a membership body a resident can join. The foundation records the networks as a tool that seeks to highlight women's problems, perceptions, perspectives and needs in the water sector, aiming to bring in women from all sectors of society so that their voice can be effectively channelled into mainstream policies, discussions and actions relating to water, and records itself as host of a national network with over 250 members and several chapters across the country, itself part of a regional network. It records the first urban water partnership launched in April 2007. Its databases are where a community finds an expert. Published description records a universities network of nine member universities, which has developed a compendium of universities offering degrees, departments or disciplines related to water, a database of water professionals and academics, and a database of research institutes that work on water in the country. It records the foundation set up in 2003, originating in 1999 when a group of concerned citizens responded to a drought crisis, and gives its house, block and postcode address in a named city. Its own diagnosis is blunt. It records that the country does not have an agreed water policy to guide water management and conservation, resulting in inconsistent and ad hoc handling of water systems and operations, mediated largely by power play among entrenched interests. Read this with the climate justice alliance, the fisherfolk forum, the public interest law association and the legal aid society entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Sungi Development Foundation — a rights-based organisation registered under the societies legislation, the provincial forestry advocacy network it founded, and the national coalitions it belongs to
trackers.desc: An organisation that combines village-level work with policy advocacy publishes both its offices. Its contact page gives a plot, street and sector address in the capital and a second address at a named hill location beside a forest check post in a northern city. Published description records it as a non-profit registered under the societies legislation, a rights-based national organisation working in both development and humanitarian sectors since 1989, led by a board of governors of professionals from diverse backgrounds, and records it as having deep roots in the north with country-wide presence through local partners and networks. Its stated mission is changing policy by organising the people affected. Published description records the mission as bringing about policy and institutional changes by mobilising marginalised communities to transform their lives through equitable and sustainable use of resources, without discrimination as to social origin, sex, race, caste or religion, working by organising and enhancing the capacities of poor and marginalised communities on human rights, poverty alleviation and sustainable livelihood, access to social services, equitable distribution and conservation of natural resources, and promoting good governance at local and national levels; and records its approach as combining advocacy work with grassroots development. It built a forestry advocacy network and got a policy changed. Published description records that it initiated and established a provincial-level advocacy network for forest protection, which successfully advocated for a pro-poor forest policy, subsequently approved by the provincial government; and records it as having played a large role in policy formulation in the forest and water sectors, disaster management, food security, labour rights and peace. A community wanting a policy changed rather than a single permit refused has a precedent here. The coalitions it sits in are named. The same description lists its memberships, including a human rights unity, a sustainable agriculture action group, a joint action committee, provincial and national NGO forums, election observation networks, a national rivers and dams platform, and home-based workers' networks — a map of national coalitions a local group can be introduced into. Read this with the water partnerships, the climate justice alliance, the legal aid society and the fisherfolk forum entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Community, village and union council organisations — the three-tier structure the rural support programmes have built, with counts by province and a portal listing the union-council federations
trackers.desc: There is a three-tier structure of community institutions, and each tier is defined by the level it sits at. The network records the structure as community organisations, neighbourhood level community groups; village organisations, village level federations of those; and local support organisations, union council level federations of the village organisations, and publishes a portal for the last tier. For a community that needs an existing body rather than a new committee, this names the one at its own neighbourhood, village and union council. The counts are published province by province, and they are large. Published material records over 520 local support organisations across the country fostered by the rural support programmes in all provinces and two territories at one date, and a total of over 1,457 formed to date at another. A provincial programme records 1,412,351 poor households organised through a three-tier women-led social mobilisation approach in the form of 78,785 community organisations, 13,859 village organisations and 589 local support organisations in 15 outreach districts of one province. A northern programme records more than 3,700 village and women organisations, most federated into more than 70 local support organisations, with earlier counts of 67 and 75. What these bodies do with government is the point. Published material records that the union council federations are forging direct partnerships with government departments, local development partners, donors and private sector actors to increase the scope and outreach of services for their member communities, and that the community organisations behind them have established patterns of local governance that are participatory, democratic, transparent and accountable to their members. A village organisation that already partners with district departments is a different negotiating position from a new protest committee. The delivery record shows what they can build. Published material records one programme's community organisations as having built more than 4,000 small infrastructure projects including bridges, roads, irrigation channels and hydropower units, with a cadre of more than 50,000 community activists and nearly five million dollars of village savings mobilised; and records another as having organised over 21,000 community organisations covering 500,000 households, a third of members being women, with over 7,000 small-scale infrastructure schemes. Read this with the water partnerships, the legal aid society, the development foundation and the climate justice alliance entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Union council conciliation panels — a free settlement forum of local conciliators selected by an elected committee, removable for partiality, whose written settlement courts can refer cases to
trackers.desc: A union council has a panel of conciliators, and using it costs nothing. Published legislation records that the union head, the members of a justice committee and the conciliators shall use their good offices to achieve the amicable settlement of disputes amongst the people in the union through mediation, conciliation and arbitration, whether or not any proceedings have been instituted in a court of law, provided all parties to the dispute agree, and that no fee shall be charged for such settlement, with dispute defined as covering matters whether of civil or criminal nature. For neighbours in a boundary or water quarrel who cannot afford a case, a free forum inside the union council is the nearest one there is. Who picks the conciliators, and how one is removed, is published. The same legislation records the union council electing a justice committee responsible for the selection of the panel of conciliators for out of court amicable settlement of disputes; and provincial rules record that the committee may, on its own or on the application of a resident of the union, and subject to show cause, remove a conciliator on the grounds of consistent partiality. A removal route that any resident can trigger is the safeguard that makes such a panel usable. The conduct rules and the paperwork are stated. The rules record that proceedings are guided by the principles of fairness, justice, impartiality and equity, giving due consideration to the rights and obligations of the parties as well as the specific circumstances of the dispute; that parties shall be asked to enter and participate in good faith with an explicit intention of settling the dispute amicably; and that the report of the settlement shall be reduced in writing and signed or thumb marked by the members, with the union council secretary attesting the final report. Courts can send a case here, and the honest limits are recorded. The legislation records that any court of competent jurisdiction may refer a matter to the panel through the union head for settlement. Published analysis records that panels went largely unimplemented in one province because rules of business were not properly formulated, and estimates that under later provincial legislation only about 20 per cent of people can benefit. Read this with the three-tier community institutions, the legal aid society, the development foundation and the water partnerships entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Provincial environmental agencies and their regional directors — a public complaints cell with complaints counted by region, a named regional director, and a provincial environmental tribunal in the same department
trackers.desc: A province's environmental agency publishes its regional director's office address. The agency's contact page gives the regional director for the largest city at a numbered plot in a named sector of an industrial area. Published reporting names the director for that city's region, three deputy directors, the department's complaints cell coordinator and three assistant directors as attending a complaints meeting — a list of the people a community's complaint actually passes through. Complaints are counted by region, which shows where the agency is being used. Published reporting records the agency as having disposed of 217 complaints of environmental violations received from people across the province, with 112 from the largest city's region, 24 each from two named cities, 14 from another, 12 from another and 31 from elsewhere, and records 76 more complaints of similar nature in the process of disposal. It records that before disposal, the complaints were technically and legally examined, paving the way for the most appropriate action under the province's 2014 environmental protection legislation, and records the secretary directing officials to expedite disposal because non-disposal is not only adverse for the environment but equally harmful for human health. Twelve complaints from a district is a small enough number that one community's file is visible. The department holds the tribunal as well as the agency. The provincial department records itself as established on 17 May 2016 and as comprising the environmental protection agency, an environmental protection tribunal, a coastal development authority and climate change, with more than 350 employees, working to implement the environmental laws according to the 2014 legislation. A business services portal lists the agency's counters as including a licence for handling hazardous substances and approval of initial environmental examinations, impact assessments and environmental clearances. Read this with the union council conciliation panels, the three-tier community institutions, the water partnerships and the legal aid society entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Tehsil land record centres — a centre in every tehsil issuing the record of rights, biometric verification at the counter, correction petitions accepted locally, and the same appeal chapter as the revenue law
trackers.desc: The law requires a record centre in every tehsil. A province's 2017 land records legislation records that the authority shall establish one or more land record centres in each tehsil, and may designate any notified place or facility to provide prescribed services; that it may establish offices or deploy human resource for the transmission of land records maintained by any other body established under law; and that it may levy fees or charges for provision of services, and collect fees on behalf of government or other entities. It records that the appeal, review and revision provisions of a named chapter of the 1967 land revenue legislation apply to appeals filed in this system. For a smallholder, the record and the appeal route are both anchored at tehsil level. What a centre does is wider than issuing records. Published description records each centre as equipped to provide advisory guidance to legal heirs, issuance of the record of rights, mutation processing, cadastral record verification, and acceptance of correction petitions, all connected to the authority's central repository; and records that before these centres people had to rely on revenue clerks for access to land records and travel long distances to record offices, whereas now a record-related request can usually be completed the same day at the closest centre. Accepting a correction petition locally is the part that matters when a record is wrong. The counter process and its identity checks are published. Published description records that a citizen can obtain the record of rights by presenting an identity card and land details such as the estate name and survey number; that at the centre the applicant gives name and parentage, need not recall the holding number, can obtain the record by identity card number, has a thumb impression and photograph taken, and receives a printed challan to pay the fee at a named bank; and that an online copy may be obtained for personal records, while any other purpose requires attending in person because biometric verification is required. The network is counted, and so is the earlier rollout. Published description records approximately 151 centres established across the province, an earlier account giving centres operational in 143 tehsils and sub-tehsils, with records computerised in 30 districts and 92 centres linked online by an earlier date. Read this with the provincial environmental agencies, the union council conciliation panels, the three-tier community institutions and the legal aid society entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Village and neighbourhood councils in one province — 2,996 rural and 505 urban councils that approve their own scheme-wise development budget, identify development needs for the tehsil, and settle disputes
trackers.desc: The lowest council approves its own scheme-by-scheme development programme. A provincial local government department records the functions of the village and neighbourhood council as including identifying development needs of the area for use by the tehsil local government in prioritising development plans for the tehsil; registering births, deaths, marriages and divorces; and considering and approving the annual budget, including the scheme-wise annual development programme and provision for other functions performed by the local council. It records secretariat duties including assisting the chairman in making arrangements for the amicable settlement of disputes as provided in a named section of the legislation, and ensuring formulation of a profile of the respective council in consultation with all relevant stakeholders, annually updated and displayed with the council's approval. A scheme-wise budget approved at village level, and a displayed profile updated yearly, are two documents a resident can ask to see. The tier structure and the counts are published. Published description records three tiers in each case — the neighbourhood council, town council and city district council in urban areas, and the village council, tehsil council and district council in rural areas, with the village or neighbourhood council the lowest tier; and records 2,996 village councils and 505 neighbourhood councils in the province. The 2013 legislation lists among its provisions functions of the village council or neighbourhood council, establishment of local funds and public accounts, budget preparation and approval, ownership of property, use and disposal of properties, personal responsibility with regard to loss and waste, and imposition, notification and enforcement of taxes. The province's supervisory powers are recorded alongside. Published description records that the provincial government has authority to exercise general supervision and control over local councils, including inspection, audit of accounts, issuing directions, suspension of council heads and control over budget, and records that reserved seats at village and neighbourhood level are explicitly set in the law, unlike at higher tiers. Read this with the union council conciliation panels, the three-tier community institutions, the tehsil land record centres and the provincial environmental agencies entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: District public safety and police complaints commissions — a district body that can order a police officer suspended, half its members elected, a 48-hour reporting rule, and the honest record that many were never constituted
trackers.desc: A district commission can direct that a police officer be suspended. The published police order records the district commission's powers on complaints as including directing the district police officer in writing to enquire into a complaint of neglect and take appropriate action and report within a specified period; conducting a fact-finding enquiry through two or more of its members and, where the complaint is found correct, sending its report and directing the district police officer to suspend the defaulting police officer and take departmental action; and reporting the matter to the provincial police officer, provincial government or the police complaints authority where the district police officer does not submit a report or act on its direction. Where the district head has reason to believe an official has committed an act of neglect, failure or excess, the order requires a report on action taken within forty-eight hours. Half the seats are elected and the independent members are chosen by a panel a judge chairs. The order records the government as establishing a district commission in each district consisting of eight, ten or twelve members depending on the area, with half elected; and records the selection panel for independent members as the district and sessions judge as chairperson with one nominee each of the provincial government and the provincial commission, provided the nominee is not an elected representative. It records the chairperson as elected by the members from amongst themselves annually, alternating between independent and elected members. The annual report is public-facing, and the failure rate is recorded. The order records the commission as required to approve an annual local policing plan prepared by the head of district police and to submit an annual report containing an abstract of its own performance, a report on the functioning of the district police, and a report on matters connected with law and order in the district. Published research records that provincial commissions in one province were assessed as dysfunctional or non-functional, and that except in one named district, no commissions had been set up under that province's 2017 police legislation. Read this with the union council conciliation panels, the provincial environmental agencies, the human rights commission and the ombudsman entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
trackers.desc: Sub-national government portal (Pakistan) — entry point to this unit's budget, procurement and finance information. Formerly listed as North-West Frontier Province, renamed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2010.

trackers.name: Centre for Environmental Justice (CEJ)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Sri Lanka's most active environmental litigator — files fundamental-rights and writ petitions in the Supreme Court and Court of Appeal against deforestation, sand mining, quarrying, wetland filling, hazardous waste, coastal reclamation and defective land-use decisions, and publishes its ongoing and completed case lists. It forced the return of illegally imported waste containers to the UK and litigates the X-Press Pearl marine pollution disaster. It also files comments on EIAs and runs a scoring tool for reading them. WHO IT SUITS: a Sri Lankan community facing clearing, mining, filling or a project approved on a weak EIA — CEJ takes strategic cases, usually as petitioner or co-petitioner, and is not a general legal-aid service.

trackers.name: Environmental Foundation (Guarantee) Limited (EFL)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Sri Lanka's oldest environmental litigator, founded in 1981 and incorporated under the Companies Act precisely so that it would have standing to sue in its own name — a paired legal and science operation in which researchers build the technical case the lawyers then argue. Its own site records more than 100 cases filed; reported wins include keeping Galle Face Green a public space, the Eppawala phosphate and Kandalama hotel cases, and the air-pollution case that made vehicle emissions testing mandatory. WHO IT SUITS: a community whose fight turns on evidence as much as argument. EFL is known for a deliberately neutral, non-campaigning posture, which serves a technical challenge well and an outright confrontation less well than a movement litigator would.

trackers.name: Friends of the Earth Asia Pacific
trackers.desc: The Asia Pacific regional structure of Friends of the Earth International, formed in 2008, whose member groups work on community-based struggles against destructive projects, particularly mining and other extractive industries, alongside Indigenous peoples, peasant farmers, fisherfolk and trade unions. WHO TO ENLIST: the national member group nearest the project. In this region Friends of the Earth International's own directory names groups in Bangladesh (BELA, the Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers' Association), India, Indonesia (WALHI), Japan, Malaysia (Sahabat Alam Malaysia), Nepal, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines (the Legal Rights and Natural Resources Center), South Korea and Sri Lanka. You CAN: reach an organisation that already works community-side in your own country, and draw regional weight onto a local fight. For activists: in several of these countries the Friends of the Earth affiliate is the most experienced community-side environmental body there is.

trackers.name: National Audit Office (Sri Lanka)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Sri Lanka — audits government accounts and public money.

trackers.name: CIABOC — Declaration of Assets & Liabilities
trackers.desc: National asset-declaration authority; Sri Lanka’s Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption is the Central Authority for assets & liabilities declarations under the Anti-Corruption Act No. 9 of 2023 — publishing a redacted public registry of officials’ declarations at ads.ciaboc.lk, Sri Lanka.

trackers.name: Center for Investigative Reporting, Sri Lanka
trackers.desc: Sri Lankan investigative-reporting center covering corruption and governance.

trackers.name: Registrar of Companies
trackers.desc: Sri Lanka's online company registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Data Protection Authority of Sri Lanka
trackers.desc: Data Protection Authority of Sri Lanka — Sri Lanka’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Department of the Registrar of Companies (Sri Lanka)
trackers.desc: Sri Lanka’s official company register — incorporation records and online search (eROC).

trackers.name: LawNet Sri Lanka
trackers.desc: Official legal-information system of Sri Lanka with legislation and Supreme Court / appellate judgments. · Find here: Sri Lanka's official legal-information system — legislation and case-law (LawNet).

trackers.name: Parliamentary Commissioner for Administration (Ombudsman)
trackers.desc: Sri Lanka’s Parliamentary Ombudsman, investigating citizens’ complaints against public authorities.

trackers.name: Right to Information Commission (RTIC)
trackers.desc: National right-to-information authority; Sri Lanka’s RTI Commission is the statutorily independent oversight, policy-making and second-appellate body under the RTI Act No. 12 of 2016, Sri Lanka.

trackers.name: Department of Census and Statistics
trackers.desc: Sri Lanka's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Sri Lanka.

trackers.name: Transparency International Sri Lanka (TISL)
trackers.desc: Transparency International's Sri Lanka chapter. Anti-corruption research and advocacy, runs Advocacy and Legal Advice Centres, and works on right-to-information, election integrity and public-procurement transparency.

trackers.name: Sri Lanka — Ministry of Finance / Treasury
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Department of National Budget prepares and publishes budget documents, estimates & the annual budget speech, Sri Lanka. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Sri Lanka.

trackers.name: Legal Aid Commission — 77 centres, focused on litigation
trackers.desc: SEVENTY-SEVEN CENTRES, AND THEY LITIGATE. The Legal Aid Commission was established by Legal Aid Law No. 27 of 1978 and runs 77 legal aid centres island-wide including the Colombo centre under head office — and the stated main focus of the centres is litigation, not advice alone, which is what separates it from a helpline. Its 9 members are 3 nominated by the justice ministry and 6 by the Bar Council of Sri Lanka, so the profession holds the majority. THRESHOLD, AND WHY TO ASK ANYWAY: legal aid goes to ‘deserving persons’ with monthly income of Rs 15,000 or less — but the Commission states the income level is relaxed in special circumstances, for example representation of women seeking maintenance. Do not self-exclude on income without asking.

trackers.name: Land Acquisition Act — the objection right and the 14-day window
trackers.desc: WHEN THE STATE IS TAKING YOUR LAND, THIS IS THE SEQUENCE. A section 2 notice is exhibited in conspicuous places in Sinhala, Tamil and English saying land in the area is required for a public purpose. The section 4 notice is your objection point: it must state that written objections may be made to the specified Secretary to the Ministry and must allow not less than 14 days. THE HEARING IS A RIGHT, SO ASK FOR IT: under section 4(4) the Secretary must consider objections and must give every person who objects an opportunity to be heard before recommending to the Minister. Later, a section 7 notice is gazetted in all three languages — and in newspapers where the value is thought to exceed 500 rupees — stating that compensation claims may be made to the named Acquiring Officer. WATCH THE URGENCY SECTIONS: sections 38 and 38A allow immediate possession on grounds of urgency at any time after the section 2 notice is first exhibited — so act on the section 2 notice, not the section 4 one, because urgency can overtake the ordinary objection window.

trackers.name: Compensation, inquiries and the gap to raise in your objection
trackers.desc: A HANDBOOK ON THE ACT from the Law & Society Trust, plus the details that decide compensation. KEEP EVERY ENVELOPE: where a compensation inquiry is adjourned and cannot resume on the notified date, notice of the new date must be sent by registered post to reach claimants at least 7 days before — service dates are how procedural challenges get built. VALUATION follows the Land Acquisition Regulations 2008, approved 17 March 2009 and applying where intention to acquire was published on or after that date; where part of a land is taken and the remnant is worth proportionately less on its own, compensation should be proportionate to the value of the main land. TAKE ADVICE BEFORE ACCEPTING ANY PAYMENT — the timing of accepting tendered compensation relative to appealing matters, and a question of law goes to the Court of Appeal by written petition. THE ARGUMENT TO PUT IN YOUR OBJECTION: the Act contains no requirement for impact assessments before section 2 or section 4 notices are issued — the Minister may allow investigation afterwards but has no duty to assess impact before selecting the land, which analysts identify as a principle of the National Involuntary Resettlement Policy never written into the legislation.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants Programme — direct to CBOs, but only in three landscapes
trackers.desc: MONEY THAT GOES DIRECTLY TO COMMUNITY ORGANISATIONS, not through an intermediary — up to USD 50,000, though in practice the average is USD 20,000–25,000 and SGP usually asks for 50 percent co-funding, so budget for that before planning around the headline. Focus areas include biodiversity, climate adaptation and land degradation and sustainable forest management. THE STEP MOST APPLICANTS MISS: a national CBO or NGO contacts the SGP National Coordinator to receive the guidelines and forms — there is no generic download route, the country team is the entry point, alongside a National Steering Committee. A proposal must show how it meets GEF SGP criteria, how it aligns with the SGP Country Programme Strategy, and that it comes from a national CBO or NGO. SRI LANKA IS GEOGRAPHICALLY TARGETED — CHECK THIS FIRST: Operational Phase 7 supports 3 landscapes only — the Colombo urban wetlands, the Knuckles conservation forest and World Heritage site, and the coastal region from Mannar island to Jaffna. Outside those, a project does not fit the current phase. SCALE OF A ROUND: one signing entered 29 agreements with community organisations — 20 community grants plus 3 capacity development, 3 knowledge management and 3 social enterprise grants. Sri Lanka is an upgraded country programme, and special consideration goes to indigenous peoples, women and youth. Grievances about the programme, including fund management, go to the National Coordinator.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Rainforest Protectors Trust — buys privately held rainforest before it is clearcut
trackers.desc: A registered land trust that buys the actual parcel — privately held forest adjoining Sinharaja that is on the market and at risk of clearing for tea or oil palm, held permanently rather than leased or covenanted. Thirty acres of primary and riverine forest adjoining Sinharaja have been protected this way, and in 2025 the Trust bought a property on the route to Sinharaja's main entrance for its first Rainforest Conservation and Education Centre. The argument it makes for buying rather than replanting is the one to borrow if you are raising money: conserving standing unprotected forest is cheaper than reforestation, which in the sub-montane terrain around Sinharaja means rough slopes, hand labour and years of invasive-species removal. Purchase is also the only route to riverine forest there, because Sinharaja's rivers now run outside the reserve through private land. Sri Lanka has lost more than 95 per cent of its original rainforest in the past century, which is the scale being worked against. Know which of the two bodies you need: the Trust, registered with the Land Registry, holds title and takes donations towards purchase; Rainforest Protectors of Sri Lanka, a separate non-profit sharing the name, does the fieldwork on the Trust's land — reforestation, research, running the centres. Ask the Trust to hold land; ask the organisation for people on the ground. Donors may visit the conservation lands and walk the trails, which is a practical way to confirm the land exists before giving.

trackers.name: WNPS — a statutory advisory seat, plus PLANT, its land-securing trust
trackers.desc: Two things here that no other Sri Lankan body in this file has. The first is PLANT, the Preserving Land and Nature Trust, a WNPS subcommittee whose stated purpose is securing land and restoring habitat corridors for long-term conservation. The second is a seat at the table: representatives of the Society are invited to sit on the statutory Fauna and Flora Protection Advisory Committee constituted under the Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance, and a body with a statutory advisory seat can raise your site inside the process rather than only outside it. Its record is that it has had land proclaimed. Founded on 23 May 1894 in Colombo as the Ceylon Game Protection Society, it paid for the first game watchers out of its own funds, and Yala and Wilpattu were proclaimed as reserves under the Forest Ordinance after sustained pressure from the Society. It is the oldest conservation organisation in Sri Lanka and the third oldest in the world. ROAR is the working model for degraded land beside a reserve. The Reforestation of a Rainforest project at Diyakothakanda, on degraded land near Sinharaja, uses relay floristics — planting pioneer and early successional species first to shelter the primary forest species that follow — and it set up the Diyakothakanda Conservation Society expressly so the Dikhena village community had a structure to take part through. Sambar, mouse deer, wild boar, pangolin and porcupine have returned to the site. Membership is gated, which matters if you were planning to join to gain standing. Life membership requires five years as an ordinary member in good standing, and an application must be endorsed by two current members with at least a year's membership, or by the General Committee. Its committee structure covers rapid response, science advice, fundraising, publications and legal guidance, and the Marine subcommittee runs proactive legal advocacy alongside its research. Office in Battaramulla; take contact details from wnpssl.org. For land near Sinharaja that is on the market rather than degraded, the Rainforest Protectors Trust buys and holds title — the two are not substitutes for each other.

trackers.name: ITI — Sri Lanka's accredited testing house, including stack emissions and waste leaching
trackers.desc: A government-owned laboratory that sells testing to anyone, accredited to ISO 17025:2017 by the Sri Lanka Accreditation Board. Successor to the Ceylon Institute of Scientific and Industrial Research, it is the country's principal analytical services centre for chemical, physical and microbiological testing. Its water and wastewater laboratory analyses potable water, effluent and process water, industrial water, and environmental water — ground, surface, river and sea — as well as industrial chemicals, waste and sludge. It also samples, which is the harder half. That same unit carries out sampling and analysis of wastewater, ambient air, stack emissions and solid waste specifically to establish compliance with national environmental requirements and regulations. Stack emission sampling is not something a community can improvise and very few bodies in this region offer it at all, so if the dispute is about what a chimney is putting out, this is the entry point. The test to know by name is USEPA 1311. The residue laboratory runs leaching and migration analysis of elements in soil, sludge, fly ash and bottom ash by that method, which is the standard procedure for establishing whether a waste is hazardous. For a fight over an ash pile, a landfill, or the reuse of industrial residue as fill, that single test can decide the question, and it is available here. The same laboratory offers over 230 residue-level tests accredited against EFSA, EU-SANCO, USFDA, USEPA, CODEX and ISO reference standards, and a separate soil and fertiliser laboratory works to AOAC, ISO, Sri Lanka Standards Institution or client-specified methods. Check which ministry it now sits under before quoting it. Its current pages place it under the Ministry of Industries while older pages on the same site still say the Ministry of Science, Technology and Research, and some of those older pages cite the superseded ISO 17025:2005 accreditation. Take the accreditation from the current pages, and ask for the scope in writing — an accredited result is only accredited for the parameters inside that scope.

trackers.name: Central Environmental Authority — thirty working days on the EIA, and the one-mile reserve trigger
trackers.desc: Thirty working days, and the authority publishes the reports currently open. An EIA report must be kept open for public inspection and comment for a mandatory thirty working days; notice goes into the national newspapers and onto the website, and any member of the public may send comments to the authority or to the approving agency within that period. The public may obtain copies of the report from the approving agency on paying copying charges, and a public hearing may be held at that agency's discretion where it would be in the public interest. Your comments must be answered, and there is a clock on it. Comments received are forwarded to the project proponent within six days of the consultation period closing, the proponent must respond in writing making every effort to improve the project, and the approving agency must have regard to the comments and to anything elicited at a hearing when deciding whether to approve. A submission here is not filed and forgotten — it generates a written reply from the proponent that becomes part of the record. Two triggers and one exemption decide whether any of this applies. Under the fauna and flora legislation, any development activity of any description proposed within one mile of the boundary of a National Reserve requires an EIA and written approval from the Director-General of the Department of Wildlife Conservation, so measure the distance before assuming a small project escapes. Initial environmental examinations carry no mandatory comment period, though the report is a public document open to inspection. And where a state agency is itself the project proponent, it cannot act as the approving agency for that project. The authority also runs the complaints line and does the measuring. Complaints on industrial pollution, hazardous waste, impacts from development projects and damage to protected areas are taken by hotline, website, e-mail and letter, and its own teams carry out water quality, air quality, noise and vibration measurement. Separately, the environmental protection licence is applied for at a provincial or district office thirty days before an activity starts, and a refusal may be appealed in writing to the ministry secretary within thirty days of notification.

trackers.name: Lanka Environment Fund — grants to local community organisations, with advocacy and activism named as eligible
trackers.desc: The applicant it wants is a local body. The fund states that local non-profit organisations working towards environmental conservation are highly recommended to apply, and that associations, clubs, social cooperatives and other local community-based organisations are encouraged to apply for grants. The problem recorded again and again in this file — that money reaches large institutions with administrative capacity rather than the people on the ground — is answered here on the eligibility page itself rather than left to be discovered. Advocacy and activism are named categories, not things to be disguised. The eligible activity types include information and awareness-raising campaigns, policy and advocacy work, calls to action and activism activities, alongside research and monitoring, conservation services, rehabilitation and restoration, signage, education and training, capacity building, public events and exhibitions, voluntary activities, the exchange and replication of good practice, bridging people, businesses, non-governmental organisations and associations, study visits and dissemination. A community can therefore ask for the campaign itself instead of dressing it as nature education, which is what most funds quietly require. Equipment, studies and consultancy are fundable lines. The fund lists the provision of appropriate equipment, study development and consultancy among what it supports. Where a community needs a monitoring instrument or an expert report — the thing every measurement entry in this file ends up requiring — that is a line it can ask for rather than an overhead it has to absorb. Know the size of what you are approaching. The fund records having mobilised over a million dollars toward sixteen conservation projects since its inception in 2019, and forms part of a wider network of locally focused environmental foundations. That makes it a small and deliberate grant-maker rather than a large institution, so ask about typical grant size and the current round before drafting, and read it with the accredited testing and litigation entries recorded for this country — the fund can pay for the evidence those routes need.

trackers.name: Legal Aid Commission — 77 centres island-wide, advice regardless of means, representation under an income line
trackers.desc: Advice and representation are two different offers, and the first door is wider. The commission's own statement of what it does is to give free legal advice to any person deserving of support, at any economic level; legal aid in the sense of a lawyer conducting your case is given to deserving persons whose monthly income falls at or below the figure the commission applies. So a community uncertain whether it qualifies should ask for advice first, because that is available on a broader footing than representation, and the advice will tell it whether representation is worth applying for. The centres exist to litigate, and there are seventy-seven of them. The justice ministry records that the main focus of the commission's centres is litigation, and that there are seventy-seven legal aid centres island wide including the Colombo centre directly under head office. For a community outside the capital that means a local office whose declared business is court work rather than referral. The income line can be relaxed, and it is. Aid goes to persons whose monthly income is at or below the stated figure, but the ministry's own description records that under special circumstances the income level is relaxed, giving as its example court representation for women seeking maintenance for themselves or their children irrespective of income. An application from a household a little over the line is therefore not automatically dead, and the relaxation is worth asking about explicitly rather than assuming. A statutory commission with a statutory fund behind it. The 1978 legal aid law establishes both the commission and a legal aid fund into which money is granted and from which it is disbursed, which is why the network has outlasted the projects that come and go around it. Head office sits in the high court complex in Colombo. Read this with the environmental foundation entry already recorded for this country: that is the specialist environmental litigator with its own science team, and this is the state network with an office near you.

trackers.name: Land registry searches — anyone may search the register, at a published fee
trackers.desc: Searching the register is a public service with a published price. The department states that members of the public may apply to search the land register or the duplicate of deeds, on a standard application form available at the land registries and downloadable, and it publishes the fee for copies of or extracts from any folio relating to any land at one hundred and twenty rupees. A community can therefore read the register for the ground next to it for about the price of a bus fare, without needing a lawyer, a reason or anyone's permission. Go to the registry for the place where the land lies. Documents are tendered to the land registry for the area in which the land is situated, and land lying in more than one district may be presented to the Registrar General. The department operates fifty land registries, fourteen district assistant registrar general's offices, seven regional deputy registrar general's offices and four central record rooms, and publishes a finder for identifying which registry holds a given area. Copies can be requested online where the electronic system has reached. The department publishes an online service for requesting deed copies and extract copies, and reports installing that system registry by registry across the country. Ask whether the registry holding your area is on the system before making the journey, because the answer differs by district and the department's own notices record the rollout as still in progress. Get the description right, and remember what the copies are for. Where inaccuracies are found in the documents requested, the registrar of lands rejects the application, so the particulars matter more than the urgency. The department's stated mission is to register documents relating to property and to register titles, to preserve them, and to issue certified copies on request, thereby assisting people to protect their rights. Read this with the environmental litigation and legal aid entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Registrar of Companies — the public search, and the published list of companies that have not filed
trackers.desc: The department publishes the companies that have not filed. Among its own notices is a list of companies which have not submitted annual returns up to a stated year according to its electronic system, published with the date to which it is current. Nothing else recorded in this sweep across the region publishes the defaulters rather than leaving a searcher to infer them company by company. A company promoting a project while absent from its own statutory filings is a fact that can go into a letter, an objection or a question at a public meeting, and it costs nothing to check. What the register covers. The department registers private and public limited liability companies, foreign companies, off-shore companies, unlimited companies, quoted companies, guarantee companies and associations, and registers auditors and company secretaries; under the societies ordinance it is also responsible for the registration of societies. A foreign company operating in the country is therefore registered in the same place as a domestic one, which is not true everywhere in this region. The search works, with one caution. A simple public search of company names and registration numbers is available through the department's online system, returning the registration number against the name. Published descriptions of the register note spelling inconsistencies in recorded names, so search several variants of a name before concluding that a company is not there — the same caution this file records for other registries where an empty result is easy to misread. The accountability documents are published too. The department publishes a citizen and client charter, the companies and societies fees orders as amended by extraordinary gazette, and its office address, opening hours and telephone numbers, with certified copies obtainable through the online system for companies registered through it. Ask for the charter's own timeframes when a request is slow. Read this with the land registry searches, the legal aid commission and the environmental litigation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: RTI Commission — the appeal ladder, the public interest override, and the oral request they must write down
trackers.desc: The ladder, and the clock on each rung. An information officer must decide a request as expeditiously as possible and in any case within fourteen working days of receiving it, either to provide the information on payment of the scheduled fee or to refuse it on one of the statutory grounds, communicating that decision to the citizen; public authorities describe the period as extendable to a maximum of twenty-one days in certain circumstances. An appeal then lies to the designated officer, who is the first appellate authority inside the public authority and must decide within three weeks of receiving it. A second appeal lies to the commission within two months of the response or the non-response. Failure to decide is itself a ground of appeal, and a vacant post is no defence. The commission lists both dissatisfaction with a designated officer's decision and failure to obtain a decision from that officer as grounds for appealing to it. Where no designated officer has been appointed, a government circular provides that the head of the department or body becomes the designated officer, so a public authority cannot stall a request by leaving the post empty; the appeal to the designated officer is compulsory before the commission can be approached. The public interest override applies to every exemption. Where the public interest in disclosing the information is greater than the interest in refusing it, the information should be provided, and this exception applies to all of the exemptions in the act. An objection to a project is a public interest argument, and the statute invites it to be made rather than treating it as an irrelevance. Duties owed to the person asking. The information officer must give all possible assistance: a written acknowledgement of the request, a response in time, notice if an extension is needed, the taking down of an oral request in written form, the keeping of records of requests, and the enlisting of other officers to answer properly. For someone who cannot write the request themselves, the duty to write it down for them is the one that matters. The right belongs to citizens, and a body counts as a citizen where not less than three-quarters of its members are citizens. Read this with the land registry searches, the legal aid commission and the company registrar entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: CIABOC — asset declarations open to the public, and reasons for closing a case
trackers.desc: Asset declarations are published for the public to read. Under the 2023 anti-corruption act the commission has published the declarations of assets and liabilities of the officers and persons required to make them, in the order of precedence of government and in the order received, in a redacted form which excludes the categories the act itself specifies, and has opened them to the general public through a dedicated declarations site. Where an official's part in a land decision, a permit or a contract looks wrong, the declaration is a document a community can open rather than one it must request. No other entry in this file records a published declarations register. The law now reaches the private sector. Published accounts of the act record that it consolidated three older statutes, came into operation in September 2023 with the reconstituted commission beginning work in January 2024, and for the first time clearly reaches bribery in the private sector alongside new offences including bribery of a foreign public official and trading in influence, with strengthened protection for whistleblowers and witnesses. A community's complaint about a company's conduct is therefore not automatically outside the commission's reach. Reasons must be given for closing a case. Among the reforms recorded in published accounts of the act's passage is a requirement binding the commission to provide justification for the closure of a case when the complainant asks for it. A closure with reasons is a document that can be argued with; a closure without one is a silence, and across this file silence is what most often ends a complaint. The enforcement record is published across ranks. The commission publishes arrests and case outcomes ranging from a beat forest officer and hospital staff through a deputy mayor to former ministers, a corporation chairman and senior officials, alongside the act itself, the declaration circulars and the gazetted declaration format. A record that visibly reaches both ends of the ladder is how a community judges whether this route will touch the people it is actually worried about. Read this with the right to information commission, the land registry, the legal aid commission and the company registrar entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: National Audit Office — the surcharge on a named officer, and the certificate that makes it recoverable
trackers.desc: A person can be surcharged personally for a loss. The national audit act provides for the surcharge of those responsible, and for a committee to hear and determine the appeals of anyone aggrieved by such a decision — a body made up of members experienced in auditing, law, public finance management, public administration and engineering, from which the auditor general is excluded and which acts independently — with a further appeal to the Court of Appeal. Where a project causes a loss of public money, liability can therefore attach to named officers rather than only to an institution. And a certificate makes the sum recoverable. The act provides that where immediate action is necessary for the recovery of such a sum, and no appeal is pending before the committee or the Court of Appeal, the audit service commission may issue a certificate containing the particulars of the sum to be recovered. A surcharge backed by a recovery certificate is the strongest personal consequence recorded anywhere in this file, and it is the reason the audit route here is worth more than a report. Local authorities are inside the scope, and management reports must be considered. The audit reaches government departments, the offices of the cabinet, the judicial and public service commissions, the parliamentary commissioner for administration, the elections commissioner, local authorities, public corporations and business or other undertakings vested in the government; and the act requires the chief accounting officer of an audited body to consider the detailed management audit report submitted by the auditor general. A community's own local authority is therefore an audited entity with a report its own officers are obliged to address. Leaning on the auditors is an offence. The act makes it an offence to influence or attempt to influence a decision of the commission or of an officer of the state audit service. That is a protection for the audit and a limit on how anyone, including a community, may approach it. One caution: an amending act of 2025 renamed the appeal body and changed its composition, so check the current form before relying on the procedure. Read this with the bribery and corruption commission, the right to information commission, the land registry and the legal aid commission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The Government Valuation Department and the Institute of Valuers — who fixes a compensation figure, and who can rebut it
trackers.desc: The state's valuation work sits in one named department. The government valuation department is the public body whose officers carry out valuations for the state, publishing in all three languages, with an institutional history running back to the 1940s and a professional degree in estate management and valuation established at national universities from 1972. When a compensation figure reaches a household, it comes from an officer of this department — which means it has an author, a date and a method, all three of which can be asked for in writing rather than argued about in the abstract. Practising valuers are registered under a statute. The institute of valuers was created by an act of parliament in 1975 and established in 1979; published guidance from practising valuers states that in order to pursue the profession of property valuer lawfully in the country a valuer must be registered with that institute. Two questions follow: whether the person who signed the state's report is a member, and whether anyone the community instructs is one. Private chartered valuers advertise the specific service. Firms in the market list consultancy on compensation for government acquisitions among their services, alongside valuation of agricultural property including tea, rubber, coconut and other land, machinery valuation, and work as panel valuers for banks. An independent report is what converts disagreement into a documented rebuttal — the same point the valuers' register entry recorded for another country in this file, reached here through a different institution. Two practical notes. Valuation is described by practitioners themselves as the interpretation of the market forces that determine value rather than the invention of a figure, so the questions that matter are which comparable sales were used and at what dates, and whether the trees, crops, wells and buildings standing on the land were counted and at what rates. And the department has been recruiting assistant valuers in large numbers, which is a fair indication that delay is a structural feature rather than an accident. Read this with the two public interest litigation organisations, the accredited testing house, the land registry and the environment fund entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Groundviews and its sister sites — where a community publishes its own account, in all three languages
trackers.desc: Citizens write the account themselves. The site describes itself as a citizens' journalism website based in the country, created as the first attempt here to make a means through which people in civil society could set down their own perspectives, call attention to humanitarian emergencies, give information on conditions on the ground and present alternatives to the status quo. For a village whose dispute no newsroom will send a reporter to, that is a route to a published, searchable record written by the people who live there rather than a summary written by someone who visited once. The family covers all three languages. The parent policy organisation anchors three civic media initiatives — this English-language site together with a Sinhala and a Tamil one — with the stated purpose of giving fullest expression to narratives by citizens otherwise marginal to, and erased from, mainstream media. Publishing in the language of the district as well as the language of the capital changes who reads a case, and which officials feel it. It is built to document, not only to comment. Its own description records the use of applications, technologies and web and mobile platforms to bear witness to violence, document rights violations and record corruption, alongside critical debate and academic commentary anchored in ground reality that would not find expression in mainstream outlets; the site has won international awards for its journalism. Responsibility sits with the author, and that cuts both ways. The published disclaimer states that content is the sole responsibility of the respective authors and does not necessarily reflect the position of the parent organisation or its staff. A community that publishes its own account therefore carries the risk of what it writes: keep to documents, dates, photographs and what was actually seen, and leave inference to the reader. Read this with the two public interest litigation organisations, the anonymous environmental reporting application, the accredited testing house and the state valuation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: HRCSL — imminent violations count, someone may complain for you, and it can summon documents
trackers.desc: Imminent violations count, not only completed ones. The commission's statutory functions include inquiring into and investigating complaints regarding infringements or imminent infringements of fundamental rights, and providing for their resolution by conciliation and mediation, as well as inquiring into complaints about procedures with a view to ensuring compliance with the constitutional provisions on fundamental rights. A community can therefore complain before the harm has landed, which no other complaint route recorded in this file states so plainly in its own founding statute. Someone else may complain for you, and the commission can act with no complaint at all. Its published guidance records that a complaint may be made by an affected or aggrieved person or group, or by a person or group acting on behalf of them; that the commission may investigate and inquire into fundamental rights violations on its own motion; and that where a matter is reported in the media or the commission otherwise receives information, it can intervene even without a specific complaint from a victim. Publishing the facts can therefore itself put the matter in front of the commission. Free forms, five ways to lodge, and redirection if you pick the wrong door. Complaint forms are available free of charge from the head office, from the regional offices or from the commission's website, and a complaint may be lodged in person, sent by post, by email or by fax, or made by giving information through the commission's hotline. If a complaint falls outside the commission's mandate it will not be accepted, but where it falls within another body's mandate the complainant is directed to that body — so a misdirected complaint produces a signpost rather than silence. The powers behind it, and the remedy available. For the purposes of an inquiry or investigation the commission may procure and receive evidence written or oral, examine persons as witnesses, require evidence to be given on oath or affirmation as in a court, and summon any person residing in the country to attend, to give evidence or to produce any document or other thing in their possession, with penalties where a person fails without reasonable cause to appear, refuses to be sworn, refuses to answer, or fails to comply with a notice, order or direction. Published accounts record that it may grant suitable redress including compensation, and that it has access to inspect and monitor places where people are held. Name the documents you want produced when you complain. Read this with the two public interest litigation organisations, the assessment comment window, the legal aid commission and the government valuation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Antiquities protection — a quarter-hectare triggers an archaeological assessment, and building can be banned within 400 metres
trackers.desc: A quarter of a hectare triggers an archaeological impact assessment.
