The archaeology department's own account records that it is mandatory to obtain an archaeological impact assessment for any proposed development project to be carried out on land of more than a quarter of a hectare in extent, and that procedural orders published in the gazette in 2004, made under the antiquities legislation, require the written permission of the department before the listed types of project are carried out. That is the smallest project-size trigger recorded anywhere in this file, and it means the question for most local developments is not whether an assessment is required but whether one was obtained. Within four hundred metres of a declared monument, building, quarrying, mining and blasting may be banned. Orders may be made under the ordinance with the object of preventing threats to the antiquities and archaeological value of declared monuments, taking into consideration the sites and their neighbouring environment; and within a prescribed distance of four hundred metres the erection of buildings, quarrying, mining and blasting may be prohibited. Where a project sits near a declared monument, the distance and the terms of any such order are the first things to establish. The hundred-year test, and what can be declared. Ancient erections of historical and archaeological value which are over a hundred years old are declared ancient monuments under the amending legislation; ancient buildings on state lands, and ancient trees growing on state or private land, may be declared ancient monuments in order to give them safety and protection; and declarations are made by the minister by notification published in the gazette. An ancient tree on private land being declarable is the provision least likely to be known locally and most likely to matter. A stop-work power, and the finder's share. The ordinance empowers the director-general to cause a scheme or project to be stopped forthwith, and provides that where a scheme or project has been stopped, work shall not commence until the condition or alteration subject to which the approval or permission was granted has been adequately complied with by the sponsors and written permission has been obtained. Separately, an antiquity is not the property of a landowner merely because it was discovered on their land: where the state retains a discovered antiquity, half its market value is payable to the finder and half to the owner of the land, or the whole to one person where they are the same. Read this with the assessment comment window, the two public interest litigation organisations, the legal aid commission and the human rights commission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Registering to raise money — which secretariat registers you depends on how far you operate, and foreign funding changes it
trackers.desc: The tier that registers you is decided by your reach, not your size. The national secretariat's own notice sets out the split: it registers international organisations registered outside the country, any local organisation receiving foreign funding, any local organisation operating in more than one administrative district, and organisations registered under the companies legislation. An organisation operating within a single administrative district registers at district level, and one operating within a divisional secretariat area registers there — the examples given being member welfare societies, mutual aid societies and death relief societies. A single-village group therefore registers locally, but the moment it takes foreign money or works across districts it moves up to the national secretariat. Foreign funding is the trigger to plan around. The secretariat records that organisations receiving foreign funding in addition to domestic funding are categorised as foreign-funded, and that under the voluntary social service organisations legislation of 1980 every voluntary organisation is to be registered, with national and international level organisations required to register at the secretariat under a numbered presidential circular of 1999 concerning money from foreign sources. Decide before accepting a foreign grant whether the group is willing to move into that regime. What the qualifying criteria require. The secretariat states that the organisation must be voluntary, non-profit and non-governmental; that profits or surpluses generated through fundraising must not be shared among members; that it may be maintained by public contributions, charity, grants, domestic or foreign donations or government contribution; that its goals must not be used for personal, political or religious ends; and that its constitution and activities must sit within the legal framework and social values of the country. On dissolution, assets and funds may not be distributed among members or office bearers. Know the current state of the law before relying on this. Reporting records mandatory registration and re-registration introduced by regulation in 2024, with clearance from defence and foreign affairs before a permanent certificate issues, and a leadership vacuum that halted registrations for six months until an appointment in September 2025; and civil society monitoring records a draft bill circulated in 2026 to repeal and replace the 1980 Act with a competent authority holding powers of warrantless entry, document seizure and deregistration, an alignment-with-government-policy requirement and substantially higher penalties. Check what is in force before organising around this. Read this with the rainforest trust, the environmental foundation, the legal aid commission and the acquisition appeal entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Development permits — the coastal zone permit, the UDA clearance, and the list of other agency clearances a project needs
trackers.desc: Inside the coastal zone, nothing may be built without a permit from one named official. The coast conservation legislation of 1981 provides that no person shall engage in any development activity other than a prescribed activity within the coastal zone except under the authority of a permit issued by the Director of Coast Conservation. The zone is defined as the area within 300 metres landward of the mean high water line and 2 kilometres seaward of the mean low water line, with the landward boundary extending 2 kilometres along rivers, streams, lagoons and other waters connected to the sea. A community can therefore ask, for any project near the shore, a single question with a documentary answer: what is the permit number. The permit guidance tells you what needs a major permit, and what it costs. The department's published developers' guide lists activities requiring a major permit, including dwelling houses and related structures of 1,000 square feet or more, breaching of sand bars, and any other development activity that will alter the physical nature of the coastal zone; it publishes fee figures by size, records that all public works within the zone are subject to the permit procedure so public institutions must consult before starting, and records that each application receives a special number in a stated format which must be quoted in all future correspondence, followed by a site inspection and screening by the department's planning committee before a permit is granted with conditions. Two statutory conditions govern issue: consistency with the coastal zone management plan, and no adverse effect on the stability, productivity and environmental quality of the zone. Away from the coast, the local authority issues the permit and the development authority clears it. The development authority's approval process pages record processing times of seven working days for applications in the capital's municipal area and twelve for others, that development permits are issued by the local authority once documents and regulations are in order, and that an enforcement division supervises and monitors local authorities on planning and subdivision approvals, with a named contact for complaints. Planning and building regulations under the 1986 gazette are sold in booklet form. The clearance list is where objections attach. A municipal council's published instructions list the clearances a permit application must carry — from the coast conservation department for development within 300 metres of the coastline, from the railway department within railway reservations, from the road development authority where roads are affected — and the one-stop unit's guidelines add water and drainage clearance, street and building line certificates, an approved base survey plan, and special treatment where land is plantation land or lies in an archaeological conservation area, high security zone, hazard area or conservation area. Each of those is a separate authority that can be asked whether it cleared the project, and on what basis. Read this with the environmental authority's assessment window, the antiquities trigger, the environmental litigators and the land registry search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: GSMB mining licences — the category thresholds, the one-application-per-land rule, and a national line for illegal mining
trackers.desc: The bureau's own licensing pages set out the categories, and the thresholds are numbers you can check on the ground. Under the minerals legislation and its 2009 amendment the bureau issues licences for exploration, mining, transport, processing, storage, trading and export. Its published category description records that Category A includes conditions such as a borehole depth of less than 1.5 metres, monthly production of not less than 100 and not more than 600 cubic metres, and no machinery used; other categories carry their own conditions. A community watching a pit can therefore compare what is happening — machinery on site, volumes trucked out, depth of excavation — against the category the operator claims to hold. Who cannot hold a licence is published. The same pages record that a person who is an undischarged insolvent or bankrupt under the law of this or any other country, or who is a member of parliament, of a provincial council or of a local authority, is not eligible to apply; nor is an applicant who in the bureau's opinion lacks the financial capacity and technical qualifications for the activity, or who fails to pay the prescribed fee. A licence held by a sitting local councillor is a documented disqualification, not merely a conflict of interest. Where the land is not the applicant's, a lease must be produced. The application guidance records that an applicant who is not the land owner must provide a lease deed or agreement from the owner, with an identity card for an individual applicant or a business registration certificate for a corporate one — so a community that owns or holds the land can ask on what document the operator claims access to it. Environmental clearance is separate, and the category decides it. The bureau records that all mining projects in the top industrial mining category are not treated as prescribed projects, with the environmental authority issuing an environmental protection licence or an environmental recommendation as clearance, and notes that the recommendation route has not been legalised under the environmental legislation. Litigation has been brought precisely on the footing that mining and transport proceeded without prior approval from the bureau as project approving agency with the environmental authority's concurrence, citing named sections of both statutes. There is a national complaints line, and the bureau is not above scrutiny. The environment ministry's page for the bureau publishes its address, telephone numbers and a three-digit line for complaints about illegal mining of rocks, sand, soil or any mineral. Press reporting records bureau employees calling for an inquiry into licence irregularities, including acceptance of a second application over the same land contrary to the rule that only one application per land may be accepted, with the file reference quoted. Read this with the environmental authority's assessment window, the development permit clearances, the environmental litigators and the land registry search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Development plans — the draft plan stage, the gazette that fixes street and building lines, and the guide that explains both
trackers.desc: A civil society guide explains land and development plans in plain terms, and it is the starting document. A legal organisation's published guide to land and development plans sets out how development plans work alongside the acquisition process, recording that the local government statutes empower acquisition of lands or buildings for general public purposes under the acquisition legislation with due compensation to the owner or occupier or any person whose legal rights are affected; that a notice must specify the ministry secretary to whom objections go and a period for objections of not less than fourteen days from the date the notice is given; that after considering objections the minister may make a declaration published in the gazette; and that the acquiring officer evaluates compensation after an inquiry, on market value, with a route onward for a claimant dissatisfied with that decision. Read it before the notice arrives, not after. The plan itself passes through a draft stage. The consolidated urban development authority law provides for preparation of a draft development plan, with a duty on the authority on preparing one, for advisory committees established by ministerial order for each development area, and for a planning committee whose conduct of business may be governed by rules. Published plans record the sequence in the gazette: a plan prepared under one named section, approved by the minister under another, and public notice given under a third — with the approval date, the plan period and the named councils and sabha areas covered all stated. Those notices identify exactly which local authority areas a plan binds. Draft plans have legal effect before approval, which is the point most people miss. The published planning and building regulations record that constructions must comply with the street lines, building lines or other road reservation specified in the relevant gazetted development plan, draft development plan or development guide plan, or as prescribed by the relevant authority; that development zone requirements are drawn from the draft development plan schedules; and that where a gazetted development plan is not available a named form's requirements apply instead. A line drawn on a draft plan can therefore already govern what may be built — and where an owner agrees to gift the land falling within a street line, the regulations provide for that too. Ask the local authority which plan is in force for your area, whether a draft is pending, and what the street and building lines are on your road. Read this with the development permit clearances, the acquisition inquiry, the environmental authority's assessment window and the land registry search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Forest Conservation Ordinance — the prohibited acts a resident can report, village forests, and the department that holds the boundary
trackers.desc: The prohibited acts are listed in the statute, which makes a report specific rather than general. The consolidated ordinance lists, for the protected categories, acts including felling a tree or cutting or dragging timber, causing damage by negligence, intentionally stripping bark or leaves, girdling, lopping, tapping or burning a tree or doing any act to damage or destroy one; blocking any waterway within the forest, or drawing water from it by pipeline or other device, or polluting or poisoning water, or polluting the forest environment by dumping and disposing of garbage; transporting, removing, uprooting or destroying any plant or part of it, or selling or exposing for sale any plant found within the forest; permitting cattle to trespass; and killing, catching, trapping, molesting or disturbing any bird, animal or reptile or offering any part for sale. For a conservation forest it further provides that no person may enter except under a permit issued by the Conservator General of Forests or an authorised person, and only for scientific research, observing the fauna and flora, or implementing activities prescribed in the management plan. Quote the paragraph that matches what is happening. Village forests are a distinct category with their own rules. The forests law provisions record the constitution of village forests, that trees listed in a named schedule within a village forest are state property, the acts prohibited in a village forest, the minister's power to make regulations for village forests, and a saving of private rights, alongside reserved trees and their protection. Reserved forests are declared by order published in the gazette over resumed land, land declared state property or land acquired for public purposes, with the orders published in both national languages. Ask which category the land beside you falls in and where the declaring order is. Who to write to, and what they say their job is. The forest department, established in 1887, states that the ordinance of 1907 with its 1966 and 2009 amendments is the main legislative tool empowering forest officers to protect forests and plant resources, that the ordinance was substituted as the forest conservation ordinance from 2009, and that its aim includes conserving forests for posterity with particular regard to biodiversity, soils, water, and historical, cultural, religious and aesthetic values. Those last words are usable in a submission about a site that matters locally for reasons other than timber. Read this with the rainforest purchase trust, the environmental authority's assessment window, the development permit clearances and the antiquities trigger entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance — a one-mile assessment trigger around any national reserve, a hotel ban inside it, and sanctuaries that can include private land
trackers.desc: Any development within one mile of a national reserve boundary needs an assessment and the wildlife director general's written approval. The environmental authority's own account of the assessment framework records that under the fauna and flora legislation as amended, any development activity of any description whatsoever proposed to be established within one mile from the boundary of any national reserve is required to be subject to an environmental impact assessment, and written approval must be obtained from the director general of the wildlife department before the development is implemented. Measure the distance from the reserve boundary first: inside a mile, that approval is a document that must exist. There is a specific ban on tourist hotels within a mile. The ordinance's own arrangement of sections includes a ban on tourist hotels within one mile of a national reserve, alongside the essential features of strict natural reserves, jungle corridors, national parks, refuges, marine reserves, buffer zones and sanctuaries; restriction of entry into strict natural reserves; acts prohibited in strict natural reserves, national parks, nature reserves and jungle corridors; acts prohibited in national reserves and sanctuaries; protected trees; and the wildlife preservation fund. Name the reserve class in a complaint, because the prohibitions differ by class. A sanctuary can include private land, and the declaration route is the gazette. The wildlife department publishes the ordinance's text, which provides that the minister may by order published in the gazette declare any specified area of state land a national reserve, and may declare any specified area of land other than a national reserve to be a sanctuary — a sanctuary being able to include both state land and land other than state land; and that the minister may likewise alter limits, or declare that a reserve or sanctuary, or part of it, ceases to be one, or that a reserve of one class becomes another. A community with private land worth protecting has a category that can cover it — and a community facing de-protection should watch the gazette for the reverse order. Know the gap between the categories and the ground. The department's protected areas pages record that a buffer zone must comprise state-owned land extending from the outer border of a national park, and that no buffer zone has been declared so far, with human influence curtailed instead through the named section that carries the one-mile rule; and that marine reserves have likewise not been declared, while the first marine national park was declared under the ordinance, with activities carried out by law, custom, usage or traditional practice before its establishment allowed subject to conditions. Read this with the forest conservation ordinance, the environmental authority's assessment window, the development permit clearances and the environmental litigators entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Water Resources Board — written permission for deep agro wells and commercial tube wells, registration of drilling companies, and communal conflict resolution over groundwater
trackers.desc: The board says in its own words that it regulates groundwater, and lists the services a community can ask for. Its groundwater management and regulation page records that the board, established under the 1964 legislation with its 1999 amendment and a gazette notification of March 2017, is mandated with regulating the country's groundwater resources; that its work includes addressing assessment studies relevant to groundwater impact with guidelines and recommendations for protection and conservation; communal conflict resolution on groundwater utilisation; and monitoring and regulation of commercial scale groundwater abstractions. Communal conflict resolution is the phrase to use when a village's wells are failing beside an industrial bore. Written permission is required for named well types, and there is a monthly ceiling. Press reporting of the gazetted regulation records that the board's chairman said the regulation would be implemented island-wide to protect groundwater; that written permission of the board must be obtained for agro wells of four metres depth or more, and for wells or tube wells for commercial agriculture and industry; that all government, local government and non-government organisations and institutions, including individual users, must submit detailed reports of their water requirements as projects to obtain approval; and that a monthly ceiling in the tens of thousands of litres was stated for what may be tapped from the ground. The same reporting records the chairman citing coastal groundwater levels dropping several metres below normal, complete drainage and seawater intrusion in one northern district and effects in another. Drillers and industrial users must register, and the notices are current. Published notices record that all drilling companies, owners of drilling machines and individuals engaged in tube well construction must register with the board under the March 2017 extraordinary gazette on groundwater extraction and deep tube well construction, with registration required for the current year and legal action for non-compliance; and that all industries using groundwater — tube wells, open wells and natural springs — must register with the board. Asking whether the operator and its driller are registered is therefore a checkable question. The Act's own duties reach further than wells. A summary of the Act records the board's duty to advise the minister on control, conservation and utilisation of water resources; irrigation, drainage, flood control and hydraulic power schemes; promotion of afforestation; control of soil erosion; prevention of freshwater pollution; and national policy on water. Reporting records that the Act is to be amended to expand the board's mandate over misuse and excessive extraction of groundwater and the surface water generated from it. Read this with the wildlife one-mile rule, the environmental authority's assessment window, the mining licences and the testing house entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Fisheries management areas and fisheries committees — lagoons and reservoirs declared area by area in the gazette, with a registered committee for each and the regulations listed in one place
trackers.desc: The department publishes, in one place, every regulation, order and notification it has made under the fisheries legislation. Its regulations page lists them by year — orders declaring named lagoons and reservoirs as separate fisheries management areas, and notifications establishing and registering fisheries management committees for those areas, each with its gazette extraordinary number and date; alongside the fishing operations regulations and their amendments, recreational fishing management regulations, rules on departure and arrival of mechanised boats, satellite vessel monitoring requirements, and regulations on import and export of cultured coral species. For a community on a named lagoon, the question is whether an order and a committee already exist — and the gazette reference is on that page. The Act's own structure names the tools. The consolidated Act's contents include fisheries management areas; fisheries committees; a register of fishermen; the minister's power to declare closed or open seasons; declaration of fisheries reserves and acts prohibited in them; leasing of State lands; licensing of aquaculture enterprises; settlement of fishing disputes and interim orders in respect of them; powers of authorised officers; offences, forfeiture and compounding; a reward fund; and regulation-making powers. Published summaries record that a fishing licence is valid for at most one year, renewable but not transferable, and that in a fisheries reserve it is prohibited to fish or damage the ecosystems except under a permit. The prohibited methods are listed, and enforcement has been local. Published analysis records that the Act prohibits the use or possession of poisonous or explosive substances and prohibited fishing gear and methods, with enhanced penalties for destructive fishing, and empowers the minister to prohibit export or import of species to protect biodiversity and to declare management areas, reserves and closed seasons, with orders published in the gazettes. Research records five methods prohibited in these waters — push nets; harpooning of marine mammals such as dolphins, dugong and whales; moxi and trammel nets; gill nets in coral reefs or rocky areas; and monofilament nets — and records a district office acting since 2010 against artificial fishing devices built from mangrove logs, concrete pillars, stones and old car bodies, against dynamiting, and against tree branches used for squid fishing, following repeated complaints by small-scale fishing communities. Read this with the wildlife one-mile rule, the forest conservation ordinance, the coastal permit clearances and the groundwater board entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Environmental Protection Licence — no prescribed activity without one, four schedules deciding whether the authority or your own local council issues it, and monitoring against measured standards
trackers.desc: No prescribed activity may be carried on without a licence, and that is the statutory sentence to start from. The environmental authority records that the licence is a regulatory tool under the 1980 national environmental legislation, and that the Act states that no person shall carry out any prescribed activity except under the authority of an environmental protection licence — a legal authorisation, on conditions, to discharge effluents, deposit wastes, emit smoke, gases, fumes or vapour, or make excessive noise or vibration. Where an operation beside a community is discharging or making noise, the first question is whether it holds one, and on what conditions. Four schedules decide who issues and who monitors, and one of them is your own council. The authority records that prescribed industries are published in a named 2008 gazette notification in categories, with high, medium and low polluting activities counted in each; that licences for the higher categories are issued by the authority's provincial and district offices, that the lowest category is delegated to the relevant local authority — municipal council, urban council or pradeshiya sabha — which issues licences and carries out follow-up, monitoring and law enforcement, and that activities registered with the investment board are licensed by that board. Published material records a further list of low-polluting activities delegated to local authorities. Knowing which schedule an activity falls in tells you which office holds the file. Monitoring is against measured parameters, by recognised laboratories. The authority records that the issuing institutions carry out monitoring at regular intervals to check compliance with the licence conditions, using quality analysis reports from laboratories and institutions registered or recognised by the authority, for waste water, air emissions, noise and vibration and final disposal, and that ground vibration and air blast overpressure from machinery and explosions are covered. Published material records that the authority has published standards for effluent quality, air quality, noise and interim standards for vibration. That is what a community's own reading can be set against. Refusal, suspension and appeal are dated. The authority records that under a 1994 gazette notification, where a licence is refused, refused renewal, suspended or cancelled, the industrialist may appeal to the ministry secretary within thirty days; that application forms for new and renewed licences are published in a named gazette schedule and downloadable; and that licences for the higher categories run for a maximum of one year from their effective date. One province operates under its own provincial environmental statute rather than the national Act. Read this with the assessment window, the accredited testing house, the mining licences and the development permit entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: National Wetland Directory and the capital's wetland regime — a 342-page site-by-site directory with coordinates, the wetland management division that made the case, and the no-development treatment that followed
trackers.desc: There is a national wetland directory, site by site, with coordinates. The environmental authority publishes the national wetland directory, produced with a conservation union and a water management institute, running to three hundred and forty-two pages and covering lagoons, mangroves, estuaries, tanks, flood plains, reservoirs, lakes and marshes; entries carry the site's coordinates and its position relative to a named town and district. It records the steering committee, its research committee and a technical review panel behind the document, and cites earlier inventories and a wetland atlas. Where a project sits on or beside a wetland, that directory is the first document to check the site against. The capital's wetlands were assessed and then treated as no-development zones. Published material records that in August 2018 the government approved recommendations to protect and restore the urban wetlands of the capital, following a study by the wetland management division of the land reclamation and development corporation with an international bank and a wetlands trust consultancy; that the study valued the benefits as flood damage mitigation, climate regulation with wetlands averaging ten degrees cooler than hard urban surfaces at the hottest time of day, freshwater supply, water cycle regulation including waste water treatment, food security for the urban poor, erosion regulation, pollination and carbon sequestration; and that the analysis gave decision-makers confidence that the most robust decision was to treat the wetland areas as no-development zones. Those are the numbers and the phrasing to borrow. The policy machinery is named, including local committees. Published research records the 2006 national wetland policy with four levers — better spatial zonation, institutional coordination through local wetland management committees and the re-established national wetland steering committee, integration of wetland management into sectoral planning, and research and education — and records the wildlife department as the convention focal point, responsible for reporting changes in the ecological character of national sites. What the strategy achieved, and what it did not. The same research records achievements since 2016 including improved wetland zoning, wetland city accreditation, new protected areas, recreational parks, a ban on wetland filling and awareness campaigns, while fifty-nine per cent of surveyed respondents perceived a reduction in wetland extent and forty-three per cent a deterioration in wetland health since then. Read this with the environmental protection licence, the assessment window, the fisheries management areas and the forest ordinance entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The fundamental rights application — a case filed directly in the Supreme Court over imminent infringement, the standing holding that collective rights do not disqualify you, and the costs the state was ordered to pay
trackers.desc: The application goes straight to the Supreme Court, and imminent infringement is enough. Published case material records that the constitution gives the Supreme Court sole and exclusive jurisdiction to hear and determine any question relating to the infringement or imminent infringement by executive or administrative action of any fundamental right; that villagers of a mining area — cultivators, landowners and the chief incumbent of a temple — filed a fundamental rights application alleging imminent violation over a mineral investment agreement with a foreign company; and that the court held the proposed agreement posed an imminent infringement of named rights. Where a project is agreed but not yet begun, that is the jurisdiction to use. The standing holding is the part to quote. The judgment records the court's answer to the argument that this was public interest litigation: that the petitioners, as individual citizens, have a constitutional right to be before the court, and are not disqualified because their rights happen to be linked to the collective rights of the citizenry — rights they share with the people of the country; and that they are not non-suited by joining in one application, the article not precluding joinder where individual rights are the basis. A community bringing one petition together is therefore not defeated by the shape of the case. What the court did, and what it cost. Reporting of the judgment records the court exercising its powers to grant relief, with the state ordered to pay costs to each petitioner and two company respondents ordered to pay a further sum to each; published material records a writ prohibiting the agreement proceeding without proper legal and environmental process, and records the case establishing the public trust doctrine, sustainable development, the public's right to object, and the requirement that proper legal procedure be followed when development projects are carried out. A domestic organisation supplied the science and the legal aid. The same material records that a non-profit which institutes and assists public interest litigation — the organisation already recorded as this bucket's own entry — supported the petitioners with scientific and legal research, and contemporary reporting records that the case was filed with legal aid provided by that organisation, naming the counsel who appeared. It records a twelve-scientist national foundation committee report submitted months earlier as part of the evidential ground. Read this with the environmental foundation entry, the assessment window, the environmental protection licence and the wildlife ordinance entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The national spatial data infrastructure and the open data portal — the state's own statement that spatial information is a national resource citizens have a right to access, and the departments that hold the maps
trackers.desc: The geoportal states the principle a community can quote when a map is withheld. The national spatial data infrastructure's geoportal records that the country has built a rich base of map information through systematic topographic surveys, geological surveys, soil surveys, cadastral surveys, natural resources inventory programmes and remote sensing imagery; that with high-resolution satellite imagery organised through geographic information systems and satellite positioning the accuracy and information content of these datasets is high; and that encapsulating them into a national infrastructure places emphasis on information transparency and sharing, with the recognition that spatial information is a national resource and citizens, society, private enterprise and government have a right to access it. That sentence is the state's own. The open data portal is the second route, and it names its operator. Published description records the portal as the government's initiative making a number of datasets freely available to the public, operated by the information and communication technology agency, providing datasets, application programming interfaces and visualisations across agriculture, demography, economy, infrastructure, transport and information technology, including geographic datasets for mapping, and complemented by the spatial data infrastructure for authoritative geographic services; the portal groups datasets by the department that produced them, including the census and statistics department. The statistics department publishes a route for data it has not published. The department records itself as the central government agency producing official statistics, serving government, agencies, the private sector and the general public in their data and information needs; records a microdata catalogue where household survey sample data files are available for downloading, licensed microdata obtainable by submitting a completed request form, project proposal and recommendation letter; and records that data other than that published on the website, including microdata and geospatial data, may be requested by email to two named addresses. The survey department is the mapping authority, and the land use maps are a priced publication. Published description records the survey department, established in 1800 under a named statute, as responsible for national surveying and mapping and as the national focal point for geographic information and remote sensing; the land use policy planning department records a land use and land cover data and maps publication available at its head office at a stated price. Read this with the wetland directory, the environmental protection licence, the assessment window and the mining licence entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Emergency conservation funding — a rapid-response fund that paid for a hillside purchase here, what the money bought, and the local not-for-profit set up to hold land
trackers.desc: An emergency fund paid for land here, and the transaction is described in figures. A rapid response fund for nature records that in 2020, against a backdrop of massive land grabs and forest destruction, the country's oldest conservation society set up a not-for-profit company to preserve land and nature, with a named land project; and records that its own funding, with two partner organisations, paid for the purchase of 12.14 hectares of land in an ecologically sensitive wilderness area, becoming a catalytic trigger for other donors and partners to feel confident about the project. It records the result: 44 acres of land, including stream reservations, brought under a conservation umbrella for the first time, protecting a critical hillside corridor for animal movement, at a location where over 145 endemic species have been listed, more than forty of them on the international red list. For a community trying to raise money quickly for a parcel about to be cleared, that is a documented example of what a first grant can unlock. The structure is the transferable part. The account records the society creating a separate not-for-profit vehicle for the land holding, rather than holding it itself, and records the fund's own representatives joining the team on a field visit under extreme weather conditions — the pattern of a funder verifying on the ground. Published description records the society as the third oldest nature protection society in the world, formed in 1894, working through awareness, advocacy, litigation, lobbying and research, and instrumental in setting up two of the country's national parks; it records its own milestones as intertwined with the country's conservation milestones, and lists a reforestation programme, a schools' nature club programme, a youth wing and a wild cat subcommittee among its structures. Legal capacity is being built deliberately, and the gaps are named. A charity's account of its partnership with a public interest litigation organisation records funding environmental law internships to train young lawyers to engage in public environmental litigation, and records what its legal officers described as the difficulties: the difficulty of finding like-minded lawyers, the absence of experienced practitioners willing to take environmental cases pro bono or at reduced rates, and frequent lack of sympathy or hostility from judges. Read this with the rainforest land trust, the environmental foundation, the environmental justice centre and the fundamental rights entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Ruk Rakaganno — a volunteer tree society founded out of a logging fight, registered as a charity, and running a multi-party restoration of degraded forest beside a world heritage rainforest
trackers.desc: A volunteer society exists that does hands-on work as well as advocacy. The society records itself as a volunteer-based non-governmental organisation founded in 1975, implementing hands-on projects to conserve nature and advocating to protect and conserve the environment, and records recent activities including a members' gathering at a named wetland park, an educational programme for a school, and a sustainable landscape plan shaped for a named institution. A community wanting planting done, not just letters written, has a body that does both. Its origin was government-sanctioned logging, and it registered to last. Published reporting records the society's genesis in government-sanctioned logging of trees in a rainforest, which prompted campaigning by nature organisations and individuals; records the society registered as a charitable organisation in 1985 and as a government-approved charity in 1988; and records its fiftieth anniversary, its patron and founder member, and a longstanding tree identification publication updated and reprinted after twenty-seven years and available in bookshops. Its current restoration is a documented multi-party arrangement. Published material records the society, with the forest department, a company foundation and a hotel group, restoring a degraded plot allocated by the forest department in a named village about 1.5 kilometres from a road into the world heritage rainforest, one account giving the plot as 20 hectares and another as 59 acres; records the project initiated in June 2021 and relaunched in 2022 to reforest the degraded land with native vegetation to grow into forest habitat; and records a scientific partner providing ecological guidance, with the society's president named among those guiding volunteer planting. A university group records such restoration sites as living laboratories where tropical research could flourish, and records joining to start research activities there. That combination — department land, corporate money, a volunteer society, and a research partner — is the model a community can propose for a degraded patch near it. Read this with the rainforest land trust, the nature protection society, the forest ordinance and the emergency funding entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The federation of environmental organisations — a registered trust that charges affiliates nothing, exists to respond to threats as one voice, and takes new member organisations
trackers.desc: A federation exists for conservation organisations, and affiliation is free. The federation records itself as a registered trust governed by a board of conservationists committed to working with all relevant agencies and organisations to support them in addressing crucial environmental issues affecting the country's natural heritage, and records that it does not charge a fee from affiliate organisations, relying entirely on sponsorships, partnerships and fundraising for its own operations. For a small community group with no budget, a national body that costs nothing to join is the difference between being connected and being alone. Its stated purpose is to make one voice out of many. It records its objects as forming an umbrella organisation for the conservation community that will report, prioritise and lobby for effective conservation and be capable of countering all threats to the country's environment as a single, unified voice; forming an organisation representative of the majority of the conservation community; and responding consistently to threats to the environment. It describes itself as a national power base of environmental organisations working collaboratively, and publishes pages for getting involved and for partners. Where a single village group's objection is easy to dismiss, a federation that reports and prioritises threats is the route to having it carried nationally. Its committees are where the national organisations meet, which is how to reach them. Published material records a conservation fund's co-founder — the fund already recorded in this bucket — as sitting on the policy and advocacy committees of the federation, alongside co-chairing a mangrove conservation and sustainable livelihoods forum comprising several local conservation organisations. That is the practical map: the same people sit across the fund, the forum and the federation, so an approach to one is an approach to the network. Read this with the environmental foundation, the environment fund, the nature protection society and the tree society entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Sarvodaya Shramadana — a village-society network with 26 district and 325 divisional centres and more than 3,000 legally independent village societies, and the conservation partnership it signed
trackers.desc: There is a village-society network with legal standing at village level, and its scale is published. A conservation society's partner page records the movement as the country's most broadly embedded community-based development organisation network, working with 26 district centres, 325 divisional centres and over 3,000 legally independent village societies in districts across the country. For a village facing a project, a society that already exists, already has legal personality and already sits inside a national structure is worth more than a committee formed in a hurry. The conservation partnership shows what such a network can be used for. The same page records that in March 2022 a land trust programme and the nature protection society — both already recorded in this bucket — signed a collective memorandum of understanding with the movement, and records that the partnership brought many acres of land under the trust programme's coverage, the three parties working together to protect and further develop the forest ecosystem and biodiversity, carry out research, assess progress, publish findings, and conduct training programmes to educate communities from the movement and neighbouring villages to ensure sustainability. A village society signing a memorandum with a conservation body is a route to protecting land that does not depend on the state. The wider environmental sector is listable, and one more field organisation is named. A published category listing of the country's environmental organisations names, among others, a field ornithology group, a green movement, a marine research organisation, a coastal protection group, an ecotourism foundation and this movement, alongside bodies already recorded here. A wildlife conservation society records itself founded in 1995 and registered both in the country and abroad, committed to the protection of biodiversity in priority areas, the promotion of sustainable use of biodiversity, and the strengthening of rural institutions and promoting cooperative governance and community involvement in conservation; it records habitat loss threats including clearing of forest for subsistence agriculture and mega development projects, and records paying and training local people as field assistants. Read this with the nature protection society, the tree society, the federation and the environment fund entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Centre for Policy Alternatives — a body that files public interest petitions and information appeals in its own name, its published litigation record, and its guide to the case law
trackers.desc: An organisation here files public interest cases in its own name, which matters when residents cannot. Its litigation pages record petitions filed by the centre and its executive director, including an application to intervene in a Supreme Court special determination, a petition challenging the constitutionality of a senior police appointment and a petition challenging a bill tabled in parliament, and record it raising concerns about another bill and challenging certain clauses in the Supreme Court. For a community whose members fear being named as petitioners, an institutional petitioner is the difference between a case and no case. It publishes the case law rather than only its own cases. It has published a volume on salient aspects of public interest litigation jurisprudence in the country, and records an attorney who has, since January 2012, supported public interest litigation cases on constitutional law, administrative law and human rights law filed by the centre, authoring policy briefs, advocacy documents and basic guides. Its street address in the capital is published on its filings. It also uses the information law, and the commission's own record shows how. The information commission's case list records appeals brought by this centre against a named armed force and against a named ministry, alongside appeals by an environmental justice organisation already recorded in this bucket and by individuals against a mineral corporation, a provincial authority, a development company and a wildlife authority — a public record of who has been compelled to release what. The commission publishes practitioner material too. It records publishing a practitioner's guide to its orders covering 2017 to 2021, with legal commentaries on selected orders, and records appeal hearings and public sittings held in named district and provincial offices rather than only in the capital, with provincial advocacy workshops listed by date. Read this with the environmental justice centre, the environmental foundation, the federation and the information law entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Nagenahiru Foundation — a district-level community organisation running mangrove restoration with village societies, a named contact, and a field laboratory and education centre beside a sanctuary
trackers.desc: A district-level organisation exists whose method is building the villages' own capacity. The foundation records itself as a community-based non-profit operating since 1991, registered with the government, whose mission is to facilitate, assist and promote the improvement of the innate capacities and strength of the rural communities while protecting, conserving and restoring the natural environment and biodiversity, especially where those communities live in sensitive ecological areas, running programmes towards capacity building of disadvantaged rural communities to identify and address their own development needs. It records recent objectives spanning poverty, food security, health, small business development, employment generation, ecological restoration and environmental education. For a coastal village, an organisation working at district scale with a named contact is more reachable than a national body. The restoration work is tied to a sanctuary and to livelihoods. Published material records its objective as facilitating the sustainable community management of mangrove ecosystems of a named lake wildlife sanctuary, an area recorded as containing 10 major wetland vegetation types and 303 species of plants; and records its task as promoting communities to protect and conserve their environment through strong educational, training and action programmes coupled with the introduction of environmentally sustainable livelihood options for people from poor socio-economic backgrounds, including post-tsunami restoration of mangrove ecosystems and rebuilding of livelihoods. It runs a field laboratory and an education centre, and its staff numbers are published. Its achievements pages record a mangrove field laboratory, conservation of a natural carbon sink and solar lamps for night fishing; and its education centre records activities including eco-camping in a mangrove forest, travelling upstream by traditional catamaran through mangrove tunnels, awareness on wetland flora and fauna, and planting mangrove plants in a restoration project, alongside printing and publishing educational materials and community awareness programmes on biodiversity. A published organisation profile records activities spread all over a named south-western coastal district, gives the president as the key person to contact, and records five permanent and twelve temporary staff. Its own pages record that more than 50 per cent of the country's mangrove forests have been destroyed irrecoverably in the past 30 years. Read this with the tree society, the federation, the village society network and the environment fund entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The district consortia network — fifteen district-level consortia binding 40-plus organisations and 120 community-based organisations, and the local authorities a village petitions
trackers.desc: A national body works through consortia at district level, and the counts are published. The organisation records itself as established in 1987, a nationally recognised non-profit committed to addressing poverty and inequality through participatory, community-driven development, and records that it currently operates within a robust network of 15 district consortia, over 40 non-governmental organisations and 120 community-based organisations, emphasising capacity building, gender equity, environmental stewardship and the empowerment of marginalised groups. A district consortium is a level a village organisation can actually join; a national office is not. It records engaging marginalised populations through strategic partnerships with self-help groups, community-based organisations, non-governmental organisations and district-level networks, with work grounded in community empowerment, rights-based approaches, advocacy, and evidence-informed, policy-driven strategies. It acts at district level when disaster hits. It records launching, after a named severe storm, a humanitarian operation with a focus on one named district, supporting the most vulnerable communities — which is the test of whether a district network exists in practice. The local authority a village petitions is the third tier, and it is numerous. Published description records 276 rural local authorities as the legislative bodies that preside over the third tier municipalities, introduced in 1987 under a named constitutional amendment and made a devolved subject under the provincial councils, collectively governing approximately 16,726,000 people with 3,624 councillors in total, ranging from 5 to 23 per council, many with their own published websites. It records one district as containing 16 divisional secretariats, 650 village officer divisions, one municipal council, one urban council and ten rural local authorities, headed by a district secretary. Knowing your council has between five and twenty-three councillors, and that the district has a secretary above it, is the map of who to lobby first. Read this with the village society network, the federation of environmental organisations, the district mangrove foundation and the public interest litigation centre entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Regional legal aid centres — dozens of centres island-wide with permanent salaried lawyers and a thousand panel lawyers from regional bar associations, an income test, and a stated preference for a lawyer of your choice
trackers.desc: There is a state-funded network of legal aid centres across the island, and litigation is what they do. The justice ministry records the commission as established by a named 1978 law to provide legal aid to deserving persons, its role being to provide legal advice and free assistance of lawyers to low income groups and to create awareness in the entire society on legal procedures. It records 77 legal aid centres island-wide including the capital centre under the head office, and states that the main focus of the centres is litigation. Other published accounts give 84 and 85 centres at later dates. A centre that litigates, rather than only advises, is the difference for a community facing a developer with counsel. The staffing is published, and it is substantial. Published description records the commission as having over 120 permanent legal officers and over 1,000 panel lawyers from the regional bar associations, and as the main institution dealing with access to equitable justice in the country. An assessment records it administering regional legal aid centres spread all across the country, supported by permanent staff on the public payroll, including lawyers and their assistants operating from those centres, as the only state-funded legal aid service provider, an independent corporate body fully funded by government. The income test and its exceptions are stated. The ministry records aid as given to persons whose monthly income is a stated ceiling or less, with the income level relaxed in special circumstances, giving maintenance claims by women as an example. The founding law tells a community two things worth using. The published law records the commission's power to establish such number of regional or district committees or clinics as it considers necessary, to make legal aid available to as many persons as possible, and requires it to set guidelines taking into account the need to maintain the independence of the legal profession and the desirability of an assisted person being referred to an attorney-at-law of his choice. An annual report records appearances in every magistrate's court, district court, high court, provincial court of appeal, court of appeal and supreme court, and before named tribunals. Read this with the district consortia, the public interest litigation centre, the environmental justice centre and the information commission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Community mediation boards — one in each of 329 divisional secretariat areas, 8,600 volunteer mediators, a five-rupee stamp as the only cost, and no lawyers permitted before the board
trackers.desc: The only cost is a five-rupee stamp, and lawyers are excluded by law. The programme records that the only cost involved is a five-rupee stamp on a letter sent by a disputant to the chairperson of the local community mediation board to register a dispute, and the statute records that no attorney-at-law, agent or other person shall be entitled or permitted to appear on behalf of any disputant in any matter before a board. For a household that cannot pay counsel, a forum where the other side cannot bring counsel either changes the balance. They sit in every divisional secretariat area, and the volunteer count is published. The programme records 329 community mediation boards at community level across the island, assisted by more than 8,600 well-trained volunteer mediators, 27 per cent of them women, dealing on average with more than 250,000 disputes a year with a settlement rate exceeding 65 per cent; the ministry gives approximately 8,266 mediators assisting on a voluntary basis. It records the boards as covering 329 divisional secretariat areas, and records special mediation boards set up for particular subjects including land disputes and financial disputes. The clock is fixed and so is the panel. The programme records that boards must resolve disputes within 60 days, or minor offences within 30 days, of the board being constituted, typically over two or three sessions, with the dispute referred to a panel of three mediators. It records four referral routes — voluntary referral by the parties; mandatory referral for civil disputes on property, debt, damage or demand not exceeding a stated ceiling; mandatory referral of certain offences including property offences, assault, trespass and defamation; and referral by a court where both parties agree. The certificate is the gate, and there is an exception worth knowing. It records that a certificate of settlement issues on success and a certificate of non-settlement on failure, the latter providing a valid legal base to proceed with litigation, and that a party may not have an application entertained where the other disputant is a public officer acting in that capacity, where the dispute relates to recovery of property, money or other dues. Read this with the regional legal aid centres, the district consortia, the public interest litigation centre and the local authorities entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Divisional secretariat land branches — free certification of grant forms at the divisional office, the named village officer and divisional secretary to contact, and the provincial land department that answers the questions
trackers.desc: The paperwork on a state land grant can be certified at the divisional office, free. A provincial land department's published questions and answers record that a holder should visit the land branch of the divisional secretariat and ask for information, will be given three copies of a named form, and should forward the completed forms with stamps to the land registrar's office of the relevant district. It records that the forms may be certified by a notary public, a justice of the peace or the registrar of land, that this work can be done at the divisional secretariat easily and free of charge, and that the document will be registered at the land registry and one copy given to the holder, to be kept carefully. For a household on a state grant, that is the nearest counter and it costs nothing. Who to contact is named by office. The same source directs holders to the village officer of their division and the divisional secretary for further details, records that permission for a mortgage is obtained by forwarding documents to the divisional secretary, and records that where a nomination is re-registered, the previous nomination is cancelled. It records the limits candidly: a grant can be transferred only to a relative under a named schedule, or to a person of the farming class without loss to the holder's family; ownership may be given only to a spouse, children or blood relations; and where a loan is not redeemed, the land will be confiscated by the lending institution, which may sell it to recover the amount. Search and copy services sit at the district land registry. The registrar general's department records fees for copies of or extracts from any folio relating to any land and for inspecting the duplicate of a deed or the land register, records that an instrument should be tendered to the relevant land registry where the land is situated, with land in more than one district presented centrally, and records that the registrar rejects an application where inaccuracies are found, directing enquirers to the registrar of lands in the relevant registry. Read this with the community mediation boards, the district consortia, the regional legal aid centres and the local authorities entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Divisional councils — 257 of them created to widen participation in local decisions, a minute book whose certified copy is court evidence, and a guide telling members their duty runs to the community, not the government
trackers.desc: The councils' own founding purpose is participation in local decisions. The legislation's long title records it as an act to provide for the establishment of divisional councils with a view to providing greater opportunities for the people to participate effectively in the decision-making process relating to administrative and development activities at a local level, and to specify the powers, functions and duties of such councils. Published description records that in 1987 district development councils were abolished and replaced by these bodies, and that 257 councils started functioning on 1 January 1988, generally matching the divisional secretariat divisions. The minute book is evidence in court. The legislation records that all proceedings, decisions, orders and acts shall be entered in a book of minutes, and upon their confirmation with such amendments as may be necessary at the next succeeding meeting, shall be signed by the chairman; and that a copy certified by the chairman of any record so entered and signed shall be admissible in evidence in any court or tribunal. A certified minute that a court must accept is the strongest paper a resident can obtain from a council meeting. The powers reach roads, buildings, nuisances and land. The legislation records the council as the authority for thoroughfares and communications other than principal thoroughfares within its administrative limits, and, subject to ministerial direction, the administrative authority for the protection of any principal thoroughfare within its area, able to exercise the powers in numbered sections relating to buildings along thoroughfares, obstructions, encroachments, injuries to thoroughfares and nuisances on thoroughfares. Its listed provisions include compulsory acquisition of lands and buildings; the council fund and its application; rates and acreage tax; assessment of property and the procedure in case of objections to assessment; and the power to appoint committees. A guide for members states where their duty lies. Published guidance records that members are selected by the people and that their prime responsibility is not towards the government, the provincial council or any other agency, but towards the community who selected them, because the council is a people's council. Read this with the divisional secretariat land branches, the community mediation boards, the regional legal aid centres and the development plans entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Friends of the Earth Asia Pacific
trackers.desc: The Asia Pacific regional structure of Friends of the Earth International, formed in 2008, whose member groups work on community-based struggles against destructive projects, particularly mining and other extractive industries, alongside Indigenous peoples, peasant farmers, fisherfolk and trade unions. WHO TO ENLIST: the national member group nearest the project. In this region Friends of the Earth International's own directory names groups in Bangladesh (BELA, the Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers' Association), India, Indonesia (WALHI), Japan, Malaysia (Sahabat Alam Malaysia), Nepal, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines (the Legal Rights and Natural Resources Center), South Korea and Sri Lanka. You CAN: reach an organisation that already works community-side in your own country, and draw regional weight onto a local fight. For activists: in several of these countries the Friends of the Earth affiliate is the most experienced community-side environmental body there is.

trackers.name: Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers Association (BELA)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the organisation whose 1997 case persuaded Bangladesh's Supreme Court to recognise public-interest litigation at all, opening standing to representative civil-society organisations and to individual public-interested litigants. That precedent is the single most important lever in the country for anyone without a personal stake in a project. Founded in 1992, BELA has filed more than 350 PILs on river and industrial pollution, wetland encroachment, hill cutting, ship-breaking and compensation for losses inflicted by development projects, and was joint winner of the Tang Prize in Rule of Law in 2020. WHO IT SUITS: individuals or communities affected by an environmental problem — and unusually, there is a published intake route. Its legal cell takes applications by email, replies within 15 days, then meets the applicant, scrutinises documents and conducts a field verification before deciding whether to file. Screened, but genuinely open.

trackers.name: Comptroller and Auditor General
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Bangladesh, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust (BLAST)
trackers.desc: Bangladesh’s largest legal-aid NGO (founded 1993), providing representation from magistrates’ courts to the Supreme Court and maintaining a public-interest-litigation repository alongside institutional-reform advocacy.

trackers.name: Information Commission (Bangladesh)
trackers.desc: Bangladesh's Information Commission is the independent statutory body under the Right to Information Act 2009, hearing appeals on denied access, with further appeal to the courts. USE IT: exhaust the Commission first — the court route runs through it.

trackers.name: RJSC
trackers.desc: Bangladesh's Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics
trackers.desc: Bangladesh's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Bangladesh.

trackers.name: Comptroller and Auditor General of Bangladesh
trackers.desc: Bangladesh's supreme audit institution — audits public accounts and the executive's financial management. — Holds to account: officials handling public money & power — find audit findings and how public money was spent or lost.

trackers.name: e-GP Bangladesh
trackers.desc: Bangladesh's national e-government-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Bangladesh, and for how much.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Bangladesh
trackers.desc: Official Supreme Court judgments, cause lists and case information. · Find here: judgments and cause lists of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh.

trackers.name: District and Union Legal Aid — free lawyer down to union level
trackers.desc: THE STRUCTURE REACHES BELOW THE DISTRICT. District Legal Aid Offices sit inside district judge court buildings across Bangladesh, and Union Legal Aid Committees operate at union level — the lowest administrative tier — expressly to reach grassroots communities, which is rare anywhere. There is also a Supreme Court Legal Aid Office (from 2015) and Labour Law Legal Aid Cells at the labour courts in Dhaka and Chattogram. It is run by NLASO, a statutory body under the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs. INCOME THRESHOLDS under clause 2 of the Legal Aid Services Policy: annual income under Tk 1.5 lakh for a Supreme Court case, under Tk 1 lakh for other courts — and those receiving income-related benefits may also qualify. CHECK A 2025 CHANGE FIRST: from 1 July 2025 mandatory mediation was introduced under 9 laws listed in the schedule to the Legal Aid Services (Amendment) Ordinance 2025, so for those matters mediation comes before litigation. NON-STATE OPTIONS if you do not qualify or want a second route: Ain o Salish Kendra, BLAST, the Bangladesh National Women Lawyers' Association, Madaripur Legal Aid Association and BRAC.

trackers.name: Khas land — the award is the easy part, possession is not
trackers.desc: GOVERNMENT LAND THE LANDLESS CAN CLAIM. Khas land covers agricultural, non-agricultural and water bodies, owned by the Ministry of Land with Collectors as custodians. Research puts distributable khas land above 10 million bighas against a landless population of more than 68 percent — district averages of roughly 1.14 acres per landless household, 0.37 acres for agricultural khas alone, with at least 14 of 64 districts above that. NOW THE PART THAT DECIDES OUTCOMES: receiving khas land and holding it are different things. In one documented case a woman was properly enlisted and received 0.34 acres with proper documents but could not take possession — the plot had long been cultivated by a local rich farmer, who on learning of the award sold it without documents to another influential person. Research records a complicated mechanism with high risk of mismanagement, landless people often not involved in the listing process while local influentials were, and a network of influentials as the main threat to proper distribution. PLAN FOR POSSESSION, NOT JUST THE PAPER — the literature's own conclusion is to organise a community movement for access rather than applying individually, and to press for proper identification of khas land, periodic survey and maintained public records of what is available. Note also that under the 1995 non-agricultural policy, religious and charitable organisations settle at 10 percent of determined market price.

trackers.name: Social forestry — planting on state land under a benefit-sharing agreement
trackers.desc: THE OTHER ROUTE ONTO STATE LAND. The Forest Department involves landless people, including women, in planting on forest land, marginal government land and roadside strips under participatory benefit sharing agreements, under which participants have received their share. It grew through tripartite agreements with Zila Parishads and the Roads and Highway Department for roadside plantation — the model to copy for strip land, since it settles in advance who signs and who benefits. THE CONTEXT THAT EXPLAINS THE PRESSURE: forest land managed by the Forest Department, Land Ministry and private owners is about 2,460 thousand hectares, 16.85 percent of the country — but actual forest cover does not exceed 6 percent, and per capita forest land at 0.022 ha is the lowest in the world. BE REALISTIC: benefit-share distribution has been described as small-scale, segmented and at an early stage with little published documentation, so get the sharing terms written into the agreement rather than relying on precedent.

trackers.name: BCCTF NGO window — apply through PKSF, not the Trust
trackers.desc: THE NATIONAL CLIMATE FUND, PAID FROM BANGLADESH'S OWN BUDGET. Established under the Climate Change Trust Act 2010 under the environment ministry, BCCTF was the first national climate fund created by a least developed country and is resourced entirely from national revenue rather than donor pledges. 66 percent is earmarked for resilience-building projects and 34 percent reserved for responding to climate-induced disasters, so two thirds is the realistic project pot. WRITE TO THE BCCSAP: projects must contribute to implementing the Bangladesh Climate Change Strategy and Action Plan 2009 — its priority actions, not general environmental aims. A Technical Committee headed by the ministry reviews proposals, with expert sub-committees for highly technical ones, and the Trustee Board approves. IF YOU ARE AN NGO, THE ENTRY POINT IS PKSF, the government-owned foundation that oversees the NGO window — not the Trust directly. Both governmental and non-governmental institutions working in Bangladesh are eligible.

trackers.name: PKSF — what the NGO window actually pays, and what disqualifies you
trackers.desc: THE RECORD OF AN ACTUAL ROUND, so you can judge the effort. BCCTF provided about BDT 25.06 crore to PKSF for 63 NGOs; PKSF disbursed about BDT 23.85 crore to 61 of them for plantation, sanitation, food security, capacity building and research, with 57 receiving the full sanctioned amount in 3 instalments. BE READY FOR THE REPORTING BURDEN: those 57 submitted a Project Completion Report and Audit Report, and government auditors audited activities at both PKSF and NGO level. A DISQUALIFIER WORTH CHECKING BEFORE YOU APPLY: two NGOs received no disbursement at all because they were defaulters under a Bangladesh Bank housing loan project — an unrelated financial default blocked their climate funding entirely, and undisbursed money from six problematic NGOs was refunded to the Trust. THE OTHER WINDOW: the donor-funded BCCRF put 90 percent into public sector projects and 10 percent through NGOs, again via PKSF, financing community-based adaptation on food security, social protection, health, disaster management and infrastructure. RECORDED HONESTLY: Bangladeshi civil society was strongly critical of the multi-donor model, preferring a state-run board, with concerns about 10–15 percent management fees charged by World Bank consultants and about democratic access to adaptation funding.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas.
