THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: ALRD — khas land: training, legal aid and a route into the local land administration
trackers.desc: The thing it does that little else in Bangladesh does at scale: it takes on khas land — state-owned land that landless families are entitled to be allocated and that local influentials routinely occupy instead. Established in January 1991 as a rights-based national advocacy and networking organisation on land rights and agrarian reform, it has provided technical support since 1993 in four forms: training, legal aid, linkage with the local land administration, and linkage with media. Its own case record shows what that combination achieves. At Beel Kuralia in Chatmohar, more than four hundred acres of agricultural khas land had been held illegally by local influentials for decades; 230 landless families took possession in 1992 and organised across 15 villages through a local partner organisation, and in 2005 the government demarcated 371 acres of khas land and 101 acres of water body. The finding inside that case is worth more than the acreage: the khas land distribution policy contains a provision denying allocation to a widow with no able son, and many widows there nevertheless obtained allocation in their own names — the bar is in the policy and it has been got round in practice. ALRD works through local partner organisations across the country rather than its own branch offices, so the first question to ask is which partner covers your upazila. It is in Lalmatia, Dhaka; take the street address from alrd.org itself, because third-party profiles give at least two different house numbers.

trackers.name: Nijera Kori — the landless people's own organisation; it will not act for you
trackers.desc: It gives nothing away, and that is the point. Nijera Kori — the name means 'we do it ourselves' — has refused micro-credit and every other form of service delivery since 1980, on the reasoning that raising consciousness and building the poor's own autonomous organisation, rather than distributing goods, is what shifts a rural power structure. What a village gets is help forming a landless group of its own, sized at a minimum of 16 and a maximum of 30 members, formed separately for women and men at the start and integrated at committee level once capacity is built. Read the limit it states about itself before relying on it. Its own account of how it works says that in protests and struggles for the physical occupation of khas land, decisions on how to act have to be made by the groups themselves and not by staff. It will not lead your occupation, choose your tactics or represent you — so pair it with ALRD, which supplies the legal aid, the training and the linkage into the local land administration that Nijera Kori deliberately does not. It publishes its own weaknesses, which is rare enough to be worth using. Its 2021 annual report records that levels of consciousness and capacity across the landless organisations remain uneven, that some staff have been found wanting in accountability, that recruiting people with strong critical reasoning has become difficult, and that communities affected by major infrastructure projects are still not treated as parties who count. It also warns that the funding space for this kind of partnership may shrink. The membership figure depends which page you read. The 2021 annual report gives 11,129 landless groups and 225,601 members; the organisation's own About page still carries a March 2008 count of 275,782; a partner network gives 202,077 across 1,168 villages. Take the annual report. Registered with the NGO Affairs Bureau, registration no. 66.

trackers.name: ESDO — the testing methodology to copy, written out in full
trackers.desc: The published method is the most useful thing here, because it is the template for making a community's own testing hard to dismiss. For its lead in paints study with Instiglio and the Lead Exposure Elimination Project, ESDO collected 161 paint samples — decorative, industrial and spray — from major markets in Dhaka and Chattogram, selected on brand popularity, colour variation and product type; prepared them on a dry-weight basis; and had them analysed at an internationally accredited laboratory by ICP-OES following NIOSH method 7303. Forty-two per cent exceeded the national 90 ppm limit. Sampling frame, preparation, accredited laboratory, named analytical method, named standard, result — that sequence is what turns a set of numbers into evidence, and it is reproducible for water, soil or air anywhere in this region. Its findings also show what a standard does not cover. Screening 70 toy samples by X-ray fluorescence from Chawkbazar in Dhaka, the country's largest toy distribution hub, it found lead, cadmium, chromium, mercury, arsenic, antimony, chlorine and bromine — and established that the 90 ppm lead limit set for decorative paint does not extend to industrial paints or to plastics, and that only an estimated eight factories nationwide hold any environmental clearance, which in any case covers emissions rather than the chemical safety of products. An earlier study found four paints carrying a lead-free logo that nonetheless contained lead. It has changed a standard and it has litigated. Its advocacy from 2008 preceded the Bangladesh Standards and Testing Institution setting a mandatory 90 ppm limit for household paint in 2018, and on 6 January 2020 it joined eleven other organisations in filing a writ petition to the High Court Division seeking a ban on single-use plastics in coastal areas, hotels, motels and restaurants within a year. Its campaign from 1995 to 2002 preceded the two-stroke vehicle ban in Dhaka and other major cities. Its domain is esdo.org, not esdo.org.bd — the country-code form is the one people construct, and it is not where the organisation is. Head office in Dhaka.

trackers.name: Arannayk Foundation — a forest fund whose grantees are mostly community organisations
trackers.desc: The record shows who actually gets the money: 167 grants worth about US$5.99 million, to 71 NGOs and research institutions and 558 community-based organisations. A community organisation is not an unusual grantee here; it is the majority of them. Established in 2003 through a bilateral agreement between the governments of Bangladesh and the United States, the foundation exists to fund and facilitate the conservation, protection, restoration and sustainable management of tropical forest, and it has run more than a hundred projects. One of its stated objectives is unusual and worth reading twice. Among them is developing conservation partnerships between non-governmental bodies, government and the private sector concerning forest conservation on privately owned or leased tea estates. Very little in this file addresses forest on privately held commercial estates at all; where your ground sits inside a tea lease, this is the fund whose own objectives already contemplate it. Its results are reported in a form you can hold it to. Twenty-five thousand hectares of degraded protected area brought under improved management jointly with the Forest Department, nine co-management organisations established with that department, over a million native trees of fifty threatened species planted by more than nineteen thousand households across more than twenty funded projects, sixty-seven threatened native tree species held in ex-situ conservation, and 14.8 million taka saved by the community organisations themselves. Women make up 48 per cent of executive committee members of the community organisations its projects have formed. Know that it is both funder and implementer. It makes grants and it also runs projects of its own, so an applicant may find the foundation already working in the landscape it is being asked to fund. Establish which role it is taking on your site before applying, because the two are not the same relationship.

trackers.name: DoE Environmental Clearance Certificate system — verify whether the operator actually holds one
trackers.desc: There is a public certificate verification tool, and it answers the first question a community should ask. The department's clearance system lets anyone check a certificate, and the department's own guidance directs people to that verification option. Whether the operator on your ground holds a valid clearance, in what category, and when it expires are therefore checkable facts rather than assertions — and operating without a valid certificate is a different and far simpler argument than disputing an assessment. The category decides everything that follows. Projects are classified by pollution and health impact, and for the higher categories a location clearance must be obtained before the environmental clearance, with no development of land or construction permitted for the establishment of such a unit until the location clearance is held. Projects inside export processing zones, economic zones and small and cottage industry estates are exempt from location clearance and need only the environmental clearance. Certificates expire, and the renewal date is a pressure point. Validity runs by category, shortest for the highest-impact categories, and renewal must be applied for at least thirty days before expiry. A lapse, or a renewal application filed late, is a matter for the department and a moment when conditions can be revisited. Published summaries of the 2023 rules also record an appeal to the environmental appellate authority within thirty days of a refusal, on payment of a fee. And a person who has suffered loss from pollution can apply directly. Those same summaries record a provision under which any person who has suffered loss due to environmental pollution may apply, with the application to be disposed of within thirty working days — a deadline that makes silence itself a fact worth recording. Two cautions: the category names and validity periods changed between the 1997 and the 2023 rules, so older guidance describing Orange-A and Orange-B categories or a three-year green validity may be out of date and both should be taken from the current rules. Application forms are published on the department's own portal.

trackers.name: Protected area co-management — the tiers, the seats, and the revenue share that is not always paid
trackers.desc: Entry is through the lowest tier, and it is open to households rather than to organisations. Co-management around a protected area is built in three levels: village conservation forums made up of enlisted forest-dependent households, a people's forum formed at forest range level as the apex of those forums, and a co-management general committee as the formal body, drawn from a range of stakeholders. A household that depends on the forest enlists at the bottom; the seats above are filled from there. Whether you are inside the landscape decides whether you have a seat at all. The co-management structure operates within a defined landscape around each protected area — delineated as one kilometre around the northern sites and two kilometres around the southern ones — with a conservation council of up to fifty members meeting twice a year under the divisional or assistant conservator of forests, and a co-management committee of around fifteen to twenty members elected by that council. Establish which side of the landscape boundary your village falls on before anything else. The revenue share is the reason this matters financially. The 2017 protected area management rules, with earlier government orders, set the benefit-sharing percentages from government revenue to the co-management organisations; published accounts record committees receiving half of ecotourism fees and concessions and all of the fees collected for non-timber forest produce extraction, and the finance ministry approving entry fee collection with half the revenue to the committee. Confirm before relying on any of it. Published evaluation records that the forest department paused a revenue-sharing provision and convened a review committee on financial responsibility under those rules, that funds may not be released directly to the community organisations, and that entry fees and revenue sharing had not been established at several protected areas. A seat on the committee is real; the money attached to it has to be checked site by site, and the question of whether a share has ever actually been paid at your protected area is the one to ask first.

trackers.name: Department of Environment complaints — a named grievance officer, a named appeal officer, and a published performance report
trackers.desc: Complaints can be filed online, and from the office that covers your ground. The department offers online complaint submission as a published electronic service, and the same facility appears on its divisional and district office sites rather than only on the national one. A community can therefore lodge its complaint with the office whose officers would have to drive to the site, which is not the same thing as sending it to the capital and hoping it travels back down. Every office names a grievance redress officer and an appeal officer. Alongside the online complaint facility, the department's offices publish their grievance redress system, the designated grievance settlement officer and the designated appeal officer, and the officer designated to provide information under the information law. Ask for the matter to be registered under the grievance redress system, keep the reference, and if it stalls take it to the named appeal officer. A complaint with an owner and an appeal route is a different object from a letter, which is the same lesson this file records for registered pro bono cases in Mongolia. The department reports on its own grievance handling. It publishes an annual performance agreement report on grievance redress management alongside its policies and guidelines, so a complainant can see what the department has committed to and cite that standard when following up rather than asking for a favour. Two adjuncts worth knowing. The department publishes a daily air quality index report, which gives a dated public record for the before-and-after comparison this file keeps recommending; and district office pages note that complaints seeking redress of social problems may be submitted to deputy commissioners and upazila executive officers, which is the local administrative route when the environmental one stalls. The named information officer is the route for documents. Read this with the clearance and public interest litigation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Legal aid — applications received at union and upazila level, not only at the district
trackers.desc: The intake tier goes below the district, which is the finding. The organisation publishes forms and registers for union and upazila legal aid committees covering both their awareness work and their receipt of legal aid applications, alongside a combined form for the two. That means a villager applies at the union committee — the nearest tier of the state to a homestead — rather than finding the fare to the district town first. Across this file the recurring failure of legal aid schemes is distance; here the state has put the application desk inside the union. There is a toll-free helpline, and the site carries two numbers. The organisation's current homepage and a 2024 notice give 16430 as the toll-free legal aid helpline, to be called within office hours, while other pages of the same site still display 16699. Both are published by the organisation itself. Try the number shown on the current homepage first and the other if it fails, and treat this entry as reporting the site as it stands rather than resolving a contradiction the organisation has not resolved. Named officers, and a charter to hold them to. District legal aid officers file monthly work statements on a numbered form, and the organisation publishes its citizen's charter, its list of officers and its focal point and monitoring arrangements. Address correspondence to the named district legal aid officer and ask for the charter's commitments — the same instrument recorded in this file for the environment department's grievance officers in this country and for published service standards elsewhere. Mediation is part of the work, and the organisation has responded to waves of cases before. Its notices record legal aid and mediation activity organised district by district, and a 2024 notice invited people facing false and harassing criminal cases filed during a stated period to call the helpline for legal assistance. Where a set of prosecutions follows a protest — the turn this research keeps recording — this is a body that has treated that pattern as a category before. Read this with the department of environment complaints entry already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Khatian and mouza map online — search by plot or by owner's name, and the address that changed
trackers.desc: What can be obtained, and where. The land ministry's records and maps system carries the survey khatians of each series and the mutation khatians, together with mouza maps, selected by division, district, upazila or thana, survey type and mouza, and by sheet number for a map. From the same record an applicant can apply for an online copy or a certified copy, paying the fee electronically and receiving the document by post or collecting it. For a community that has never seen the paper record of the ground it lives on, this is the first place to look before anybody is asked for anything. You can search by plot number or by the owner's name. Published guidance on using the system records an advanced search which accepts the plot number or the name of the owner, so a household that knows neither the khatian number nor the plot can still reach the record. That places this country with Punjab, where a name search is offered, and against Hong Kong, where the register is closed by name, Japan, where the practical key is the lot number, and Malaysia, where the full title particulars are required. The rule this file has arrived at holds: who may search, and on what key, has to be established country by country. The address has changed, and the old one no longer serves. Services formerly provided through the earlier portal have been consolidated into the ministry's records and maps system, and published guides record the older address as no longer providing khatian and map services. Check the current host before sending anybody to look, because a dead link is how a community concludes that a record does not exist. Know which copy you need. The guidance distinguishes the online copy from the certified copy, and it is the certified copy that land offices, banks and courts will expect. Applying calls for the mouza and district together with the khatian or plot number. Read this with the khas land route, the clearance certificate verification and the union-level legal aid entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: e-GP — the annual procurement plan searchable by office, and variation orders tracked after the award
trackers.desc: The annual procurement plan is searchable by office. Before any individual tender is advertised, procuring entities prepare an annual procurement plan inside the national electronic procurement system, and the portal carries a search for those plans by office. A community can therefore see what its own district or municipal office intends to buy in the year ahead rather than learning of a project when the machinery arrives. Only one other entry in this procurement sweep offers a forward-looking record of that kind. The tendering phase covers the whole run to award. The procurement authority describes the electronic tendering phase as covering centralised user registration, preparation of the annual procurement plan, preparation of the tender or proposal document, invitation of tenders, sale of tender documents, online pre-tender meetings, collection of tender securities, online submission, tender opening and evaluation, negotiation where applicable, and contract award. Each of those leaves a record, and the pre-tender meeting in particular is a point at which questions were asked and answered. Variation orders are tracked after the award. The contract management side of the system covers preparation and submission of the work plan, the defining of milestones, the tracking and monitoring of progress, and variation orders. A variation order is the document that explains why a project grew, changed or cost more than the contract said, and it sits inside the same system rather than in a file nobody outside the agency has seen. Manual procurements are listed as well. Where a tender or a contract award was handled on paper, the portal still lists it, noting that the document must be bought from the procuring entity's office and that the same information appears on the procurement authority's own website. Read this with the land record and map services, the information commission, the union-level legal aid and the environmental clearance verification entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Comptroller and Auditor General — local authorities audited, and 'special issue based' is a published report category
trackers.desc: Local authorities, public enterprises and statutory bodies are auditable. The office's constitutional mandate is to audit the receipts and expenditure of government and to give an opinion on whether they are duly accounted for and comply with the financial rules and regulations established by the government, and a further statute gives it authority to audit statutory public authorities, public enterprises and local authorities. The union parishad, the municipality or the development authority behind a project is therefore an audited body in its own right, not merely a spender of somebody else's money. Nobody can narrow the scope. The constitution guarantees the auditor complete independence in determining the scope and extent of the audit. A request that a particular scheme be examined therefore goes to a body which the government cannot instruct to look away — which is not true of most of the complaint routes recorded in this file, and is the reason a written request here is worth making even without a guarantee of a reply. Special issue based audit is a published category. The office's reports are published and filterable by category: compliance audits, financial audits, performance audits and special issue based audits. A single project, scheme or event can therefore be the subject of a report of its own, and the existence of that named category is what makes such a request askable rather than fanciful. The reports reach parliament, and performance is the test. The auditor submits reports to the president, who causes them to be laid before parliament, where the public accounts committee discusses them; and alongside traditional financial and compliance work the office conducts performance audits evaluating the economy, efficiency and effectiveness with which public resources are managed. A help desk for service recipients has also been established at the office. Read this with the electronic procurement system, the land record and map services, the information commission and the union-level legal aid entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: BELA's legal cell — a published intake procedure, a fifteen-day reply, and field verification before a case is taken
trackers.desc: The intake procedure is published, and it runs on a clock. The organisation operates a legal cell that provides legal assistance to individuals or communities affected by environmental problems, headed by a coordinator, with applications sent to a single published address for the cell; it states that a response is sent to the applicant within fifteen days of receipt, that it then contacts the applicant for further information, documents and a meeting, and that after scrutiny of the documents its team carries out a field verification. A visit to the ground before anything is filed is the step that separates a case which survives from a complaint which does not, and it is written into the published procedure rather than left to chance. The record is a list, not a claim. Published accounts record more than three hundred and fifty public interest cases on river pollution, industrial and vehicular pollution, encroachment on wetlands, hill cutting, relocation of industries, labour welfare and compensation for losses inflicted by development projects; the organisation's own site carries the list of its cases, the judgments and orders obtained, and collections of the laws, policies and rules. Before the first meeting, find the case closest to your own and take it with you. Public interest litigation exists here partly because of this organisation. Published accounts record that following a case it initiated in 1997 the Supreme Court recognised the concept of public interest litigation, opening the formal justice system to representative civil society organisations and to individual public-interested litigants. Founded in the early 1990s by a lawyer whose successors have led it since, it has been recognised by national and international awards. Its evidence standard, and one question to ask. Its research is described as using satellite images, high resolution photographs and community testimonies — the same three kinds of material this file has recorded communities assembling across the region — alongside training delivered to government officials, local government representatives, judicial officers and civil society, and a right to information focal point. One caution: published material records that a former chief executive is now serving as environment minister in the interim government, with an acting chief executive in post. A community bringing a case against a government body should ask directly how that is handled. Read this with the legal aid, the clearance certificate system, the land rights organisation and the information commission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Public health engineering water laboratories — a published price per parameter, and which tests only the central lab can do
trackers.desc: The price list is published, parameter by parameter. The department's water quality monitoring and surveillance circle publishes a laboratory testing cost schedule setting a unit cost against each parameter — pH, colour, temperature, taste, odour, turbidity, conductivity, salinity, alkalinity and the rest — and a separate microbiological set covering biochemical and chemical oxygen demand, E. coli and faecal and total coliforms, each listed with the national standard beside the fee and a stated total for the set. A household or a village committee can therefore add up the cost of exactly the tests it needs before leaving home, which is the step at which most attempts at independent evidence in this region quietly stop. The schedule says which laboratory can do which test. Every parameter in the published list is marked either as available at the central and zonal laboratories or as central laboratory only — temperature and taste appear as central-only. Knowing that before the journey is the difference between a sample that gets analysed and a sample that is turned away at the counter after a day's travel. There is a zonal laboratory network, and the locations are named. The schedule is issued under the office of the senior chemist of the zonal laboratory and lists laboratories at Mymensingh, Comilla, Rajshahi, Khulna, Rangpur, Barisal, Sylhet, Tongi, Bogra, Jhenaidah, Noakhali, the Chittagong Hill Tracts and Gopalganj, alongside the central laboratory. Four of those were the original zonal laboratories, strengthened from 1998 when further laboratories were established with external support. The department's own arsenic record is why the network exists. Its published account records that it first confirmed arsenic contamination of groundwater in a northern district in late 1993, that from 1997 it investigated jointly with the geological survey using both laboratory and field test kit methods, and that groundwater in sixty-one of the country's sixty-four districts and two hundred and forty-nine of four hundred and seventy upazilas was found contaminated above the fifty parts per billion threshold. A department that has published a national contamination finding of that scale about the water it is responsible for is one whose test results carry weight in an argument. Read this with the environmental clearance certificate, the pollution complaint route, the environmental lawyers' legal cell and the information commission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Netra News — an investigative outlet publishing from outside the jurisdiction, and what that changes
trackers.desc: It publishes from outside the country, and that is the point. Founded in December 2019 and based abroad, the newsroom describes itself as defending democracy through public interest journalism, publishing investigations that expose corruption and human rights abuses alongside analysis, interviews and opinion, and treating its watchdog role as the core of its work. Published accounts record that its first investigation rested on a whistleblower's tip and that access to the site was blocked domestically within days of publication. Where domestic outlets are constrained, a newsroom outside the jurisdiction can publish what one inside cannot — and the blocking is itself evidence of how much that difference is worth. It withholds bylines for security. Its editor has stated publicly that the newsroom does not give bylines because of security considerations, that the reporting is done by professional journalists and freelance collaborators working from the ground, and that digital hygiene is the most important protection for reporters inside the country. For anyone weighing whether to hand over documents, the absence of bylines is the relevant operational fact: no reporter's name goes on the story either. It builds databases, not only articles. Published accounts record a 2024 data journalism award for work documenting the scale of extrajudicial executions through a database of thousands of cases involving security forces, and a 2025 journalism award recognising its investigations into high-level corruption and abuses. A newsroom that builds datasets can absorb a stack of documents and make something of it, which is not true of every outlet a community might approach. What that means practically, and the caution. The publisher has said he is personally liable for everything the outlet publishes, which is precisely why documentary evidence matters more to it than allegation; and the site has been blocked domestically, so reaching its material from inside the country may require a different route. This is a channel for evidence, not a source of protection: no outlet can shield anyone from local consequences, and that should be weighed before any approach rather than after. Read this with the environmental lawyers' legal cell, the information commission, the auditor general and the public water laboratory entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Acquisition compensation — a forty-five day arbitration clock, ten per cent interest, and a bar on going to court instead
trackers.desc: The clock that decides everything is forty-five days. Under the acquisition legislation of 2017, where there is any question about the award of compensation the person entitled must apply for arbitration within forty-five days of the notice; the arbitration appellate tribunal must then dispose of an appeal within sixty working days and inform the deputy commissioner in writing. Missing that forty-five day window ends the argument about value before it starts, so the date on the notice is the first thing to record and the first thing to check against the calendar. Interest runs at ten per cent from the original award. Where compensation is increased on arbitration or appeal, published summaries record that the awardee receives the compensation plus any applicable increase together with ten per cent annual interest, running from the date the initial award was made public or given under objection until the revised payment is made or ordered. Delay by the acquiring side therefore has a price, and that price belongs in the application rather than being left for someone else to notice. The courts are barred except where the Act allows. A court may not grant an injunction against any action taken or to be taken under the Act, and may not accept a complaint or petition against an order or action made under it, unless expressly authorised by the Act itself. The arbitration route is therefore not one option among several — it is the route, and treating it as a fallback loses the case. What the process looks like, and the gaps commentators name. The deputy commissioner publishes a preliminary notice at convenient places on or near the property where it appears needed for a public purpose; a joint list of owners and interested parties is prepared; objections are heard by the deputy commissioner, who reports upward for the final decision; compensation takes into account the market value of the property at the date the notice was published, with agencies reported as required to pay three times market value for private land, calculated on official mouza rates; and the property vests only once compensation has been paid or is deemed paid. Altering the nature of a property in order to obstruct acquisition is prohibited. Published legal commentary records the Act's weaknesses plainly: no resettlement provision, a short period for filing objections, no return of acquired land left unused, and no definition of what counts as a public purpose. Read this with the environmental lawyers' legal cell, the land records portal, the legal aid entry and the information commission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Antiquities Act — a street or square can be declared an antiquity, and an owner can hand over guardianship without losing title
trackers.desc: A street, a square or a group of buildings can be declared an immovable antiquity. The antiquities legislation's definition of immovable antiquity extends to any urban site, street, group of buildings or public square of special value which the government, being of the opinion that its preservation is a matter of public interest by reason of its arrangement, its architecture or its materials of construction, declares by notification in the official gazette to be an immovable antiquity. That is a neighbourhood-scale power rather than a single-monument one, and the three stated grounds — arrangement, architecture, materials — are the headings a submission should be written under. Natural features, the adjoining ground and the access are all inside the definition. The definition also reaches any rock, cave or other natural object of historical, archaeological, artistic or scientific interest, or containing sculpture, engraving, inscription or painting of such interest; anything attached or fastened to an immovable antiquity, from a gate or window to wall-painting, woodwork, ironwork or sculpture; such portions of land or water adjoining the site as are reasonably required for fencing, covering or otherwise preserving it; and the reasonable means of access to, and convenient inspection of, the antiquity. A project that blocks the approach is therefore within the Act even where it leaves the structure untouched. The hundred years is a rolling test. An amending ordinance of 1976 replaced the fixed historical date in the definition with the words 'the preceding hundred years', so what qualifies moves forward with each passing year rather than being frozen at a nineteenth-century cut-off. Guardianship by agreement, with compensation written into it. The owner of any immovable antiquity or protected antiquity may by written agreement constitute the director its guardian, and the director may accept that guardianship with the government's prior sanction; where he does, the owner retains the same right, title and interest in the antiquity as if no guardian had been constituted. The agreement may provide for the facilities allowed to persons deputed for inspection and maintenance, the expenses of preservation and who pays them, and compensation for any loss sustained by the owner, the occupier or any other person as a result of enforcing or observing the agreement; its terms may be altered with government sanction and the owner's consent, and it may be terminated on six months' written notice by either side. For an owner who wants the protection but fears losing control of the property, that is the provision to read first. The Act separately provides for compulsory acquisition of a protected immovable antiquity, for the protection of a place of worship from misuse, and for restrictions on the use of a protected immovable antiquity; the archaeology directorate administers it, and its head chairs the advisory committee constituted under the Act. Read this with the environmental lawyers' legal cell, the land records portal, the acquisition compensation clock and the information commission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: কৃষি খাস জমি বন্দোবস্ত — settlement of government land to landless families, including families made landless by acquisition
trackers.desc: A family made landless by acquisition is a listed category. Under the agricultural khas land management and settlement policy gazetted in 1997, any landless family may apply on the prescribed form to the assistant commissioner (land) for settlement of government khas land. The application form itself asks the applicant to tick which class of landless they fall into, and the classes include a distressed freedom fighter's family, a family displaced by river erosion, a widow or abandoned wife with a capable son, a family with neither agricultural land nor a homestead — and a family that has become landless as a result of acquisition. A household whose land has just been taken for a project is therefore inside this policy by its own terms, which is a different claim from compensation and can be pursued alongside it. What the application requires. Two photographs attested by the ward member or union parishad chairman — a joint photograph of husband and wife — a citizenship certificate from the union parishad chairman, a certificate of landlessness from the chairman, proof of permanent residence, and the prescribed form. The joint photograph is not incidental: the settlement is made to the couple, and the deed is executed by them together. An open meeting, a list, and a twenty-one day step. The upazila agricultural khas land management and settlement committee verifies the applications — official process descriptions record verification through a public meeting — prepares the list of genuine landless families and fixes how much land each is to receive; the assistant commissioner (land) then proceeds within twenty-one days. The deed is executed and registered, with the deputy commissioner accepting it on behalf of government, and the family pays a salami of one taka per acre or part of an acre together with the current year's rent through the revenue receipt at the tahsil office. The nominal salami is the point worth knowing: the obstacle here is the list, not the price. Irregular settlements can be challenged. The policy provides that where agricultural khas land was settled irregularly after 1972, the local committee may on specific complaint and evidence recommend cancellation to the district committee, whose decision is final; and where the service itself fails, the published redress officer is the deputy commissioner or the district committee. The governing instruments are the 1997 policy together with the tenancy legislation of 1950, the land management manual of 1990 and the land reforms ordinance of 1984. Read this with the landless people's own organisation, the land rights organisation's khas land work, the khatian and mouza map search and the acquisition compensation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Public interest disclosure protection — identity withheld without consent, and the discloser cannot be made a witness
trackers.desc: A statute exists specifically to protect the person who discloses. The public interest information disclosure protection legislation of 2011 was enacted to give legal protection to someone who discloses information relating to the public interest. Its core protection is stated directly: where a discloser makes a correct disclosure of public interest information under the Act, that person's identity may not be revealed without their consent. For a village resident who knows what an inspector did not write down, or a contractor's employee who has seen the test results, that clause is the difference between a document reaching an authority and nobody being willing to hand it over. The protection extends into court, which is where most informal promises fail. The Act provides that information published under its disclosure provision shall not be taken as evidence in any civil or criminal case, that the discloser shall not be made a witness in such a case, and that nothing shall be revealed in the proceedings by which the person's identity is or could be disclosed — with provision for material in books, documents or papers forming part of the evidence that would have that effect. Anonymity that survives litigation is a materially stronger promise than anonymity offered by an official at the counter. There is a penalty attached to false disclosure, and it cuts both ways. The Act provides a punishment for a person who discloses information knowing it to be false. That is worth reading before disclosing: the protection is for correct disclosures made under the Act, so the practical discipline is to disclose what can be evidenced and not what is suspected. Rules under the Act were issued in 2017 and set out the procedure. Know the conflict before you rely on it. Published legal commentary records that provisions of the colonial-era official secrets legislation are argued to conflict with both the constitutional guarantee and this Act — a live question rather than a settled one. Anyone disclosing official documents should take advice on which statute the authority is likely to invoke, and should route the disclosure through the Act's own procedure rather than informally. Read this with the information commission appeal ladder, the environmental clearance verification, the legal aid route and the environmental lawyers' association entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Supreme Court case search and the daily cause lists — find whether a case exists, and when and before whom it is listed
trackers.desc: The court runs a case search, and publishes its daily lists. The supreme court's own site carries a case search page alongside the daily cause lists of both divisions. Published guidance on using them records that the court publishes a separate list for the appellate division and for the high court division each working day, usually the evening before the hearing day; that each list is organised bench by bench with the presiding judges named; that within a bench cases are numbered in the order they will be called; and that lists are occasionally revised after publication. For a community following a case that affects it — its own, or one brought by a neighbouring village against the same developer — that is how to find out when it will actually be heard. Search by case number or by party name. The guidance advises opening the list for the relevant division, finding the bench hearing the matter, and searching the page for the case number or a party's name, or using the case search portal. Party name search is the useful one when you know a company or an agency is in litigation but not the case number. Bench assignments can change between hearing dates, so the list must be checked afresh each time rather than assumed. Know which division you are in. The high court division hears appeals from lower courts and tribunals and has original jurisdiction in limited classes including writ jurisdiction under the constitution, company and admiralty matters; the appellate division hears appeals from the high court division and is the final court. A challenge to an official decision or an authority's failure to act starts, in the ordinary case, in the high court division. What this does not give you. A cause list tells you a case exists and when it is listed; it does not give the judgment. Where the reasoning is needed, apply through the court's own channels or ask the organisations recorded elsewhere in this country's entries — the environmental lawyers' association and the legal aid route — to obtain it. Read this with those entries and with the acquisition compensation and antiquities entries already recorded here.

trackers.name: Foreign donations regulation — registration then project-by-project approval, and what counts as a foreign donation
trackers.desc: Money from a relative abroad counts as a foreign donation. The foreign donations legislation of 2016 defines a foreign donation as funds, goods or any other grant or assistance given in any form by a foreign government or organisation, or by an expatriate citizen of this country, in favour of an organisation, a registered body or an individual, to conduct voluntary or charitable activities inside the country. A village committee funded by relatives working overseas is therefore inside this regime, not outside it — the single most common mistake a community makes when it starts raising money. Registration first, then approval for each project. The Act requires an organisation conducting voluntary activities with foreign donations to obtain prior approval, with an application stating the amount of the donation, the source of its availability and the utilisation of the fund. Where the application and information appear correct, the director general issues a registration certificate valid for ten years, renewable, subject to the opinion of the home ministry and the bank and financial institution department of the finance ministry. Published guidance records this as registration with the bureau followed by project-specific approval, with renewal due six months before expiry, and a further requirement of prior approval to use a volunteer or staff member from outside the country. Voluntary activities are defined broadly, and environmental work is inside. The Act's definition covers non-profit social, religious, cultural, economic and educational activities, healthcare, drinking water and sewerage, relief and rehabilitation, agriculture and agricultural infrastructure, public awareness, poverty alleviation, women's empowerment, democracy and good governance, human rights, research, and activities related to the development and protection of ethnic groups. Frame the project within those words. Know the grounds for cancellation before you write anything. The Act lists offences that may cause registration to be cancelled or withheld, including anti-state activities, making malicious and derogatory statements against the constitution and constitutional bodies, subversive activities, financing terrorism, and trafficking. Monitoring organisations record a 2021 regulation allowing cancellation where a body is inactive for five years without foreign funding. Domestic-only routes exist. Welfare organisations may register with the social services department under the 1961 ordinance, and bodies may incorporate as societies or non-profit companies under the respective legislation — but bureau registration remains a parallel requirement for anyone accepting foreign funds. Read this with the public interest disclosure protection, the environmental lawyers' association, the khas land settlement and the case search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: বালুমহাল ইজারা — sand quarries are leased by the district administration under one statute, amended in 2023
trackers.desc: Sand and soil extraction runs on a lease from a single named authority. The sand quarry and soil management legislation of 2010, published on the official law database, was enacted to resolve complications about the granting of sand quarry leases, to provide for planned extraction and marketing of sand and soil from sand quarries and its control, to suppress offences committed in connection with it, and to fix a single authority for sand quarry management. Its definitions record a lessee as a person or institution taking a sand quarry lease from the district commissioner, and lease value as the money paid to the government in exchange for extracting sand or soil. For a riverside community, that means the question is answerable at the district office: is this stretch leased, to whom, and for what value. Mineral sand is treated separately by definition. The Act defines mineral sand by reference to sand enriched with heavy minerals in quantities determined by the energy and mineral resources division, naming zircon, rutile, ilmenite and monazite among them — a different category from ordinary construction sand, and one that brings a different department into the picture. Establish which is being taken. The Act was amended in 2023, and the land ministry publishes both. The amending Act of 2023 is published on the same database and lists the sections of the 2010 Act it amends or substitutes, and the land ministry's own notices and law page carry the amendment for download alongside the land offences prevention and remedy legislation of 2023, the land reform legislation of 2023 and the immovable property acquisition and requisition legislation of 2017. Check the amended text rather than the original, and note that the acquisition statute recorded elsewhere in this country's entries sits in the same list. District administrations publish the Act themselves. District portals carry the sand quarry legislation on their law and policy pages under the district commissioner and district magistrate, which is the office that grants the lease and the office to which a complaint about unleased or out-of-boundary extraction is addressed. Read this with the public interest disclosure protection, the khas land settlement, the environmental lawyers' association and the case search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Environmental clearance under the 2023 rules — four colour categories, no utilities without location clearance, and a thirty-working-day pollution damage claim
trackers.desc: Anyone harmed by pollution can apply for remedy, and the department has thirty working days. The environment conservation rules of 2023 provide, in their opening rules, for application by any person who has suffered loss due to environmental pollution, to be disposed of within thirty working days; and set out the form of notice to an owner, occupier or agent for collection of samples of air, water, soil or other substances. The rules also provide that on application the department shall supply an analysis report of samples of water, liquid waste, air and sound together with the information or data derived from it, on payment of the prescribed fee. That combination — a damage claim with a clock, and a right to buy the department's own analysis — is the practical core of this entry. Four categories decide what a project must produce. Industrial units and projects are classified by activity, pollution and potential harm to environment and health into green, yellow, orange and red categories. Published guidance records that red category projects require an environmental impact assessment and orange category an initial environmental examination, that higher categories need a location clearance certificate before the clearance certificate itself, and that a public hearing features in the red category process. Establish the colour first; it tells you which document should exist. No location clearance means no land development and no utilities. Guidance on the rules records that for yellow, orange and red categories a location clearance certificate must be obtained before the clearance certificate, that without it no development of land or construction of infrastructure is allowed for the establishment of the unit, and that utility providers are forbidden to give electricity, gas or water connections without it. Where a project has started work, ask which certificate it holds and when it was issued. Validity is short, and renewal is a recurring opening. A green category certificate runs five years, yellow two years, and orange and red one year, each renewable at the same interval on a prescribed form and fee, with renewal to be applied for before expiry. Where clearance is refused, an appeal lies to the environmental appellate authority within thirty days, with a further application to the authority if the appeal is rejected, and the certificate continues to be granted and renewed until the appeal is settled. Enforcement guidance records inspection priorities that include red and orange category facilities, establishments without a certificate or without renewal in the previous year, recurring polluters and clusters of high polluting industries. Read this with the sand quarry lease, the environmental lawyers' association, the public interest disclosure protection and the case search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Ward Shava and the open budget session — statutory meetings where residents set the project list, with the documented ways they get captured
trackers.desc: The lowest tier of local government must hold open meetings where residents put projects on the list. Published studies of the 2009 union council legislation record two statutory forums for citizen engagement: the ward assembly and the open budget meeting. The ward assembly is a gathering of everyone on the ward's voter list; each of the nine wards in a union council is required to hold at least two open meetings a year, open to all adult residents without restriction, presided over by the elected ward member and typically convened before the budget is set, at which participants identify community needs and propose development projects. Its recorded functions include prioritising the demands of citizens that are to become schemes or projects in their areas. That is the meeting at which a community's own priority — a drain, a protected common, a road not widened — enters the official list. The chair, the adviser and the timing are prescribed. The same material records that the council chairperson must ensure the ward-level open budget meeting is held, that it must be chaired by the ward member concerned and that the member holding the reserved seat acts as adviser to the meeting, and that a council is required to organise two open budget sessions each year, in stated months, inviting community people to participate irrespective of gender, caste or class. If the meeting has not been called, that is a failure of a named officer's duty. The same reforms brought three other tools. Published accounts record that mandatory citizen participation mechanisms introduced with the 2009 legislation included citizen charters, ward assemblies, five-year plans and the right to information — the last already recorded in this file — and that standing committees are formed at ward level for particular functions with the ward member as convener. Ask for the council's citizen charter and its five-year plan alongside the budget. Know how these meetings are captured, because that is documented too. Studies record that council representatives often place development agendas themselves and select beneficiaries from their own patronage; that large majorities of surveyed residents did not engage in the initial and final phases of the budget process; and that although councils are legally obliged to arrange ward assemblies, open budget meetings and standing committees, these often function as symbolic events controlled by powerful local actors, with elite domination, political interference and weak enforcement named as the barriers. Attend in numbers, record what is proposed, and put the demand in writing. Read this with the environmental clearance categories, the sand quarry lease, the information commission appeal and the environmental lawyers' association entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Social forestry and the participatory benefit sharing agreement — the written share of the harvest, the committees with a women's quota, and the tree farming fund
trackers.desc: The share of the harvest is written into an agreement, and the percentages are published. Published accounts of the forest department's social forestry work record that after the final harvest the participants receive forty-five per cent of the revenue, the government forty-five per cent and ten per cent goes to a tree farming fund for future plantations; one worked example records an investment on one hundred hectares allocated to fifty members returning a multiple of the outlay. Research records the participatory benefit sharing agreement between participants and the forest department, made under the 2004 social forestry rules as amended, as the key component of the programme — the document that reduces uncertainty and gives participants a form of ownership, and that establishes the right to participate in departmental plantation activities and to claim the agreed share after harvest. Ask to see the agreement before joining a scheme, and keep a copy. Different plantation types carry different splits. A study of one forest division records a strip plantation split among the forest department, local citizens, the tree farming fund, the land-owning agency and the local union council, with the largest share to local citizens — so where a road, embankment or railway strip is involved, the land-owning agency and the union council are parties too, and their shares are known. Establish which plantation type is proposed: strip, agroforestry or woodlot. The committees are named, and a third of the seats are women's. Research records three committees formed among participants in a social forestry area — a management committee, an advisory committee and a fund management sub-committee — with at least one third of committee members drawn from women participants, the management committee responsible for overall management of the plantation and the trees and for handling conflicts during and after implementation. That is a governance structure a community can ask to have constituted properly. Know the documented failure modes. Published evaluation records low individual returns where plantations were felled before maturity or long after the planned rotation, and records participants doubting during the first rotation whether the department would fell the plantation or hand over the agreed share; it also records that where the fund cannot cover its share of replanting costs, participants are asked to contribute voluntary labour. Read this with the forest fund, the protected area co-management, the khas land settlement and the ward assembly entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Water Act 2013 — potable water as the highest priority right, prior permission before anything impedes natural flow, and protection orders even over private land
trackers.desc: Drinking water is declared the highest priority right, in the Act's own words. A published text of the 2013 legislation records that, subject to the Act, the right to potable water and to water for hygiene and sanitation shall be treated as the highest priority right; that water resources are defined to include surface, ground and rain water and also the water of an estuary, aquifer, flood-plain, wetland, water source, foreshore and coast; and that a water resource development project means any activity or programme for developing water resources, including hydraulic infrastructure for irrigation, flood control and drainage, river bank protection and dredging. That definition matters because it decides what counts as a project under this Act. Rights over surface water on private land stay with the owner — but a protection order can still issue. The same text records that all rights over surface water on any private land remain with the owner and continue to be enjoyed subject to the Act, provided that the executive committee may, to prevent wastage and misuse of water and for its protection and conservation, issue a protection order to the owner of such private land without discrimination. A pond or watercourse inside a private boundary is therefore not beyond the Act's reach. Nothing may impede natural flow without prior permission. Published review of the Act records that without prior permission of the executive committee no individual or organisation may extract, distribute, use, develop, protect or conserve water resources, nor build any structure that impedes the natural flow of water; that management of water resources in rivers, creeks, reservoirs, flood flow zones and wetlands is assigned to that committee under the water ministry; and that draining of wetlands that support migratory birds is prohibited, with named exceptions — dredging for navigability, land reclamation by filling wetlands, and flood and erosion control structures — still requiring prior permission. Ask which permission a structure across a khal holds. The bodies and the planning organisation are named. Summaries record the Act creating the national water resources council and the water executive committee with stated duties, including promoting the national water policy and planning, monitoring and evaluation, ensuring integrated development under the national water resources plan, and disseminating data exchange and analysis on water resources; and the Act defines the water resources planning organisation, whose officers have taken part in public discussion of the law alongside the environmental lawyers' association and the land rights organisations already recorded in this bucket. Read this with the environmental clearance categories, the sand quarry lease, the ward assembly and the environmental lawyers' entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Protection and Conservation of Fish Act — the rule-making powers that can close a water body, declare a fish sanctuary, and stop dewatering or effluent killing a fishery
trackers.desc: The Act's rule-making powers are the list of things a community can ask the government to do for a particular water body. The legislation empowers rules to prohibit the destruction of fishes by poisoning of waters, or the depletion of fisheries by pollution by trade effluents or otherwise; to prescribe seasons in which killing or catching a prescribed species is prohibited; to set a minimum size below which a species may not be killed or sold; to prohibit all fishing in all waters or in any specified waters for a specified period; to prohibit the destruction of fishes by drying or dewatering of any fishery; and to declare a fish sanctuary. Where a project drains, dries or discharges into a water body, the dewatering and effluent limbs are the ones to name. The definition of a fishery is broad enough to cover the waters people actually use. The Act defines a fishery as any water body, natural or artificial, open or closed, flowing or stagnant — river, haor, baor, beel, floodplain, canal and so on — where activities for growing, conserving, developing, breeding, exploiting or disposing of fish are undertaken, and defines fish to include prawn, shrimp, amphibians, tortoises, turtles, crustaceans, molluscs, echinoderms and frogs at all stages of their life history. That breadth matters when the water in question is a seasonal floodplain rather than a river. The offences carry imprisonment, and the officers are public servants. The Act provides that breach of a rule made under the rule-making section, or of a prohibition notified under the sale-prohibition section, is punishable with rigorous imprisonment of not less than one year and up to two years, or a fine, or both; contains a separate prohibition on the monofilament net known as current jal, with its own penalties for manufacture, fabrication, import, marketing and storage; and provides for confiscation, arrest without warrant, officers being deemed public servants, and the trial of offences. The measures in force show what the powers are used for. Published analysis records juvenile hilsa up to a stated size banned from catch, transport, marketing, sale and possession between November and May each year; a twenty-two day national ban on hilsa fishing enforced across named districts, with a designated breeding zone of thousands of square kilometres; and area closures, gear restrictions, seasonal restrictions and vessel regulations built on this Act, its 1982 amending ordinance and the 1985 rules. It also records a move away from leasing water estates and a policy commitment to involve poor and traditional fisherfolk in managing open and closed water bodies. Read this with the water Act, the environmental clearance categories, the ward assembly and the environmental lawyers' entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Ecologically Critical Areas — the declaration power, the 2016 rules with committees down to village level, the prohibited activity list, and the record of what has been allowed inside one anyway
trackers.desc: The government may declare an area ecologically critical where its ecosystem has reached or is threatened to reach a critical state. Published legal analysis records that the 1995 environment conservation legislation empowers the government to declare an area facing an environmentally critical situation to be an ecologically critical area, on being satisfied that because of environmental degradation the area's ecosystem has reached or is threatened to reach a critical state; and that the amended definition covers an area rich in unique biodiversity, or environmentally significant, needing protection or conservation from destructive activities. It records that such an area may include both public and private property, which is what makes the management complex. Asking for a declaration is therefore available where degradation is documented rather than only where a species is listed. The declaration itself names what may not continue there. Published description records that the government shall specify, in the declaring notification or a separate one, which operations or processes cannot be initiated or continued in the area; and reporting records the prohibitions in practice as including establishing industries that pollute soil, water, air or by noise, activities harmful to fish and other aquatic animals, discharge of sewage and liquid waste, and disposal of solid waste, with any development work threatening biodiversity and ecology strictly prohibited. The 2016 rules build committees down to village level. Published analysis records that the ecologically critical areas management rules of 2016, made under the Act, provide for committees at national, district, upazila, union and village level, with government officials, civil society representatives, non-governmental organisations and professional societies as members, list the prohibited and banned activities including restrictions on changing land use types, and require the national committee to consider the area's naturalness and biodiversity status and identify causes of deterioration and potential threats. That village-level committee is the nearest entry point. What has been declared, and what has been allowed inside anyway. Reporting records thirteen areas declared since 1999 — named beaches, islands, haors, an oxbow lake, two city lakes, the ten kilometre belt around a reserved forest, and four rivers around the capital declared in 2009; and records that an industrial belt and a large coal-fired power plant were set up in that ten kilometre belt, and that a 2017 amendment to the definition of hazardous industries exempted a number of gas plants there from conditions including environmental impact assessment. Published analysis records public interest litigation by the environmental lawyers' association already recorded in this bucket prompting the High Court Division to direct protective measures for a named island and the forest. Read this with the environmental lawyers' entry, the clearance categories, the fish protection Act and the water Act entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Environment Court Act 2010 — the sixty-day rule that lets a citizen into court when the inspector does nothing, the compensation suit filed directly, and how few courts exist
trackers.desc: The inspector's written report is the gate — and sixty days of inaction is the way through it. The 2010 legislation provides that no special magistrate court shall take cognizance of an offence except on the written report of an inspector of the environment department, and that no environment court shall receive a claim for compensation except on such a report; but that where the court is satisfied on an application that the inspector was requested to accept the complaint and took no necessary action within the next sixty days, or that there are reasonable grounds for accepting the complaint, it may — after giving the inspector or the director general a reasonable opportunity of being heard — take cognizance without that written report, or direct the inspector to investigate. Put the request to the inspector in writing and date it, because that date is what opens the door. A compensation suit is filed directly with the environment court. The Act provides that a suit for compensation under environmental law shall be filed directly with the environment court, and that cases received from the special magistrate for trial are tried by that court; and the 1995 conservation legislation provides that where a person, a group of persons or the public suffers loss from a violation, that person, group or the public — or the director general on their behalf — may file a suit for compensation before the environment court. What the court can order goes beyond a fine. The Act provides that the special magistrate court may pass any sentence prescribed under environmental law, order confiscation or disposal of any equipment, transport used in the offence or article involved, and in appropriate cases pass an order or decree for compensation, making further orders in the same judgment; and material records the magistrate court limited to offences punishable by less than five years or a stated fine, with alternative dispute resolution available during a pending case. Know the two structural weaknesses before relying on it. Published analysis records that environmental law for these courts means the 1995 Act and such other laws as the government specifies by gazette, and that no such notification has been issued in years, leaving the jurisdiction narrow; and records that only two environment courts and one appellate court have been established. Read this with the environmental lawyers' association, the ecologically critical areas, the clearance categories and the fish protection Act entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The air quality monthly reports — station-by-station monthly analysis published as a series, the daily index for each city, and the calibration record kept for every station visit
trackers.desc: The environment department publishes a monthly air quality report, month after month, on its own portal. Each edition records that data from the continuous stations is automatically collected in a central server and disseminated through the department's website, that an air quality index for each city is calculated and published online daily to notify the public of the status in their city, and that the report provides an overview and analysis of air quality monitoring data for the month; the reports carry the station abbreviations, the national ambient air quality standard against which readings are set, and note which stations are refurbishment stations. Successive months are posted as separate documents on the same portal path, which is what makes a series out of them. The quality control record is itself a resource. The reports record that quality assurance and control methods are implemented with full documentation and validated through an international certified calibration reference laboratory, and that forms and log sheets document every activity at the monitoring stations, including all maintenance, calibration, operation and every visit. Where a reading is disputed, those log sheets are the thing to ask for. The network and its history are documented. Published material records the department having established eleven continuous air monitoring stations in eight major cities, with plans for further stations and compact units; records the monitoring programme as begun under a donor-funded project now run entirely by the department, producing quality data since 2014, accessible through its website without cost, with a monthly report giving specific values for each parameter at all eleven stations; and records the parameters monitored as fine and coarse particulates, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide and ozone among others. The index thresholds follow a stated external scale, and other bodies monitor too. Published material records that the department's index breakpoints are the same as the United States environmental agency's, as set out at named pages of the national air quality management plan for 2024 to 2030; and records other public and private organisations monitoring in their own capacity, including a research institute running its own monitor and publishing a daily value for its own area of the capital. Read this with the ecologically critical areas, the environment courts, the clearance categories and the water Act entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Community-based fisheries management — community organisations holding water bodies on ten-year agreements, the committee structure the arrangement requires, and the published account of where it fails
trackers.desc: Communities have held government water bodies under agreements, and the scale is documented. A published legal review of the programme records community control established over 116 water bodies across 48 sub-districts in 22 districts, with 130 community-based organisations formed, the communities given responsibility for management of government-owned fisheries and privately owned seasonal water bodies — closed and open depressions, river sections and others; it sets out the classification of fisheries for leasing and management and the leasing arrangements attaching to each, and records the framework as descending from a public trust doctrine under which government-owned fisheries became an estate that cannot be retained under private ownership. Another study records community organisations holding access rights over a government water body through ten-year agreements, and others managing common fisheries on seasonal floodplains largely of private land without needing recourse to government authority. The committee structure is specified. Published research records that the arrangement devolves the right of fishing in inland fisheries to poor, landless traditional fishers living permanently around the fishery, and requires forming a fishery user group and a beel management committee — a nine-member decision-making body serving two years — with rules on meetings, conflict management, involvement of fishers in catching and selling, distribution of benefits and conservation of sanctuaries, the committee being the formal body enforcing them. A community organising around a water body has a documented shape to copy. The published record of failure is as useful as the model. The same research examines constraints on enforcing those rules, and the absence of mechanisms to address them. A conflict study records that the land administration, not the fisheries department, ultimately controls decisions on property and use rights, and that an open-access policy increased competition rather than improving access for traditional fishers, with local landowners gradually winning that struggle. Other material records a higher lease value affecting fishers' access, fishers lacking the credit to acquire a licence and depending on moneylenders, water bodies above a stated size leased by tender, and subleasing strictly prohibited on pain of cancellation. Read this with the fish conservation Act, the ecologically critical areas, the landless settlement and the co-management entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The national environment movement and the riverkeepers — program committees by issue, district committees and named local conveners, and its stated practice of helping local organisations form where none exist
trackers.desc: A national movement organises by issue, and says it helps local organisations form where there are none.
