For a community, the plan is the document that decides what may be built next to it for years, and this is the window in which its own words enter the file. Know what a petition can and cannot ask for. Reporting on a later posting records officials stating that interested members of the public may petition but cannot obtain a change to land use or to the plan's colour zoning — except where the petition is for the common good and public benefit, the example given being a request to add green space as additional public park. Frame a petition as a public benefit, not as a private preference, and ask for the designation you want rather than only objecting to the one proposed. Deadlines move, and movement is public. Reporting records a petition window opened for one month and then extended by public announcement after criticism that the plan favoured developers, with the extension tied to the statutory right to petition for amendment, change or revocation under a named section of the Act. Watch for extensions rather than assuming the first published closing date is final — and note that comprehensive plans are described as normally revised on a five-year cycle, so the window recurs. What the new Act added. Published summaries record that the 2019 Act replaced the 1975 legislation after forty-four years, taking effect one hundred and eighty days after publication in the gazette, and that a comprehensive plan now carries six maps rather than four — among them the land use classification map, the open space map, the transport and communications projects map and the public utilities and facilities projects map. Those maps are the documents to request and read. Read this with the environmental law foundation, the justice fund, the expropriation entry and the solicitation licence entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: ประทานบัตร — thirty days' posting at the district office, the sub-district office and the village head's house, and a public hearing
trackers.desc: The mining department's own paper sets out three participation steps, and the first is disclosure. Its published material on mining and human rights records that the minerals legislation of 2017, in force from 29 August 2017, was written with participation provisions in several sections, and that participation by affected people or communities has three principal steps: first, the information in the mining lease application and related information must be disclosed, with a notice posted for the public for not less than thirty days; second, there must be an opportunity to be heard. A community's entitlement therefore begins with a document it can demand to see, not with a meeting it must be invited to. Where the notice must be posted is specified, and those are places you can check. Published analysis of the Act records that for every class of mining lease application the notice must be posted openly in the area applied for — at the district office, the sub-district administrative organisation and the village head's house — for not less than thirty days, and that a public hearing must be held to take the opinions of the community in the area where mining is to be done. Three named posting points mean three places to look and photograph, and a missing notice at any of them is a documented procedural failure. Know which authority decides which permit. Legal commentary from an environmental law foundation records that the Act shortened the consideration of prospecting and lease applications: the minister's approval power over prospecting licences was removed, with local administrative organisations deciding ordinary prospecting licences within ten days, while exclusive and special prospecting licences are decided by the department's director-general, the process beginning with an application to the local mineral industry officer who compiles the documents and opinions. Faster decisions mean shorter windows, which makes the posted notice the thing to watch for. The subsidiary rules carry the numbers. The department publishes the subsidiary legislation made under the Act, including rules on compensation for underground mining — the criteria for the compensation amount and the steps for claiming and paying it — and rules on licences to buy, store, possess and transport controlled minerals, with transport licence validity set by reference to the distance from origin to destination, and provisions stated to be for protecting the environment, safety and health. Ask for the specific subsidiary rule that governs the activity in front of you. Read this with the comprehensive plan petition window, the environmental law foundation, the justice fund and the judgment search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: ศาลปกครอง — you may draft and file the case yourself, generally without court fees, and there is a dedicated environmental division
trackers.desc: The court's own guidance says a person may write the complaint without a lawyer. The administrative court's cautions on preparing a complaint state that in an administrative case a claimant can prepare the complaint themselves, without needing a lawyer or a person with legal knowledge to prepare it — while warning that a claimant who has not studied the rules and conditions for bringing an administrative case under the establishing legislation risks getting them wrong. For a village facing a licence or a permit it disagrees with, that is the difference between a remedy that exists on paper and one that can actually be used. What the complaint must contain, and how to file it. Published guidance on the procedure records that there is no prescribed form but the complaint must be in writing, not oral, in polite terms, and must include the items in the named section: the name and address of the claimant and of the respondent, the facts or circumstances of the act giving rise to the case, the relief sought and the claimant's signature, with relevant evidence attached and copies of the complaint and evidence made for each respondent. Filing may be done in person, through an authorised person, or by registered post. Exhaust the specific procedure first — that is the commonest trap. The court records that a claimant does not have the right to sue immediately upon suffering harm: they must first consider whether a law prescribes steps or methods for remedying that harm, and if a specific law does, those steps must be followed first. Published case digests record the supreme administrative court treating a complaint letter that contested an order as an appeal against it even though no formal appeal had been lodged, and record that where an appeal committee decides after its consideration period, that decision is a new administrative order which may be challenged within thirty days of notification under the building control legislation. Keep every letter you send; it may itself be the appeal. Two features that lower the cost. Practitioner material records that filing an administrative case is in principle free of court fees, except where the claim is for payment of money or delivery of property under named provisions. Academic work records that the president of the supreme administrative court announced in June 2011 the establishment of an environmental case division in both the supreme and the first-instance administrative courts, giving specialist consideration to environmental cases. Read this with the environmental law foundation, the justice fund, the comprehensive plan petition window and the mining lease posting entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: รุกขมรดกของแผ่นดิน — the culture department's tree register, its stated purposes, and how a local tree gets nominated into it
trackers.desc: The culture department publishes selection criteria for a national register of significant trees. Press reporting records that the department of cultural promotion, under the culture ministry, announced the criteria for selecting trees for the land's arboreal heritage programme, with the stated purposes of searching out and collecting information on trees of local cultural and historical importance, using that information for dissemination and learning, promoting such trees as cultural tourism sites, and encouraging children, young people and the public to see the importance of trees and take part in conserving and caring for them. A tree with a local story therefore has a national channel that is about documentation rather than felling permits. The scale is published, and it is competitive. Reporting of one selection round records that around eight hundred trees were considered and sixty-three selected nationwide, and names an individual example: a two hundred and fifty year old tree on private land in a named sub-district whose owner said publicly that he would conserve it for life. Nomination of a tree in a private garden is therefore an established practice, not an exception. What the register records, and why that matters. A library description of the programme's published book records that it gives each tree's history with English captions, a travel map and geographic coordinates locating where the tree stands, illustrated by named photographers, and describes the trees as large and generally around one hundred years old or more. Coordinates and a published photograph are exactly what a community needs when a tree is later said to have been diseased or already gone. Read it for what it is. Published descriptions of the general concept record heritage trees as large trees of value or historical importance whose distinctive character cannot be replaced, with age, rarity and size the basic criteria alongside aesthetic, botanical, ecological and historical value, and note that some countries have legislated to protect nationally significant trees. This programme is a cultural register rather than a felling control, so pair it with the monument precinct entry and the comprehensive plan petition window already recorded in this country's entries — a documented cultural tree strengthens a submission made through those routes. Read this with the monument precinct entry, the comprehensive plan window, the environmental law foundation and the community forest registration entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: องค์กรผู้ใช้น้ำ — neighbours in one basin can register a water user organisation, and one member per organisation can sit on the basin committee
trackers.desc: People who use water near each other in the same basin have a statutory right to register an organisation. The national water office records that the 2018 water resources legislation builds management at three levels — a national committee chaired by the prime minister, basin committees chaired by a provincial governor selected from within the basin, and water user organisations, formed by natural or juridical persons who use water in nearby areas within the same basin, registering together for shared benefit in the use, development, management, maintenance, restoration and conservation of water resources among their members. A parliamentary summary of the Act records the same right in the section on water user organisations. That is a vehicle a village can create before a dispute, not during one. Registration buys a seat at basin level. The same office records that beyond managing water among their own members, one member per organisation may stand for selection as a basin committee member representing water user organisations, with a stated number of such seats in each basin drawn from the sectors using water. Ministerial regulations of 2021 govern how those representatives, the local administrative organisation representatives and the qualified members are obtained, and a published handbook sets out the registration steps, the application form, the meaning and powers of a water user organisation, and the registrar's power to dissolve one. Get the handbook and the form before the basin committee seats are next filled. The first category of use needs no licence, and that is stated plainly. The office records that first category water use — the use of most people in the country — requires no licence and no water use fee, though users must give information to the state so that overall demand can be analysed for supply planning; and that farmers growing crops, rice farming and livestock keeping are unaffected by the ministerial regulation, except that groundwater use continues to require a licence under the groundwater law, with fees payable for some groundwater activities. Know which category a project claims before arguing about its licence. Consultation is built into the national plan. The parliamentary summary records that the national committee must arrange to hear the opinions of the public, water user organisations, stakeholders, state agencies and relevant local administrative organisations, and must monitor and evaluate implementation and review or improve the water management action plans to match actual conditions. Read this with the Mekong consultation window, the community forest registration, the comprehensive plan petition and the pollution complaint entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: องค์กรชุมชนประมงท้องถิ่น and the coastal sea zone — the registered local fishing community, the provincial fisheries committee that must carry its proposals, and the three-mile line
trackers.desc: A registered local fishing community organisation has its proposals carried upward by statute. The 2015 fisheries emergency decree provides that the provincial fisheries committee's powers and duties include gathering suggestions and proposing approaches for promoting fishing occupations, and for the management, maintenance, conservation, restoration and use of aquatic resources by local fishing community organisations in its area of responsibility, for submission to the national committee for policy purposes; and considering and proposing approaches for developing or resolving fisheries problems, and for managing, maintaining, conserving, restoring and using fishing grounds in its area, for submission to the minister, the committee or the director general. It records among the decree's purposes protecting and assisting or supporting small-scale local fisherfolk. Registering the community organisation is how a coastal village gets a standing route into that committee. The coastal sea zone is defined, and it can be adjusted on the provincial committee's proposal. The decree defines coastal sea as the sea in the kingdom three nautical miles from the shoreline, with a ministerial regulation able to set the zone in a given area at less or more than three miles but not less than 1.5 and not more than 12 nautical miles, accompanied by a map of the boundary; and where the physical character of the coast makes it necessary, the zone may be set as proposed by the provincial fisheries committee. That map is a document to ask for, and the committee is the body that can propose moving the line. Inland public waters need the provincial committee's permission. Published material on amendment of the decree records that a person wishing to fish in fresh water in fishing grounds that are public property of the state within a province must obtain permission from the provincial fisheries committee, which sets the criteria. The committee's composition includes outside expertise. The decree provides for members with knowledge or experience in fisheries or in natural resources and the environment, up to a stated number, alongside the official members. Read this with the community forest registration, the water user organisation, the comprehensive plan petition and the pollution complaint entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: เขตห้ามล่าสัตว์ป่า and the hearing before an area is fixed — the department's own legal page, the ministerial notification on stakeholder and community participation, and the reserved species schedule
trackers.desc: There is a ministerial notification specifically on hearing opinions before a wildlife area is fixed, extended or revoked. The national parks and wildlife department's legal affairs page lists, among the subordinate instruments made under the 2019 wildlife conservation and protection legislation and published in the government gazette, a ministry notification on hearing opinions and the participation of stakeholders, related communities and the public in determining the area of, extending, or revoking a wildlife sanctuary and a non-hunting area. Where a boundary is being drawn or removed near a village, that notification is the instrument to cite by name. The same page carries the Act itself in Thai and English and the other subordinate rules, including a royal decree designating certain wild animals and the notification on officers' identity cards. The Act's structure shows where the two area types sit. A parliamentary library summary records the Act as one hundred and twenty-one sections in nine chapters — wild animals; zoos; the wildlife conservation and protection committee; wildlife sanctuaries; service or compensation fees; non-hunting areas; use of biodiversity; control of officers; and penalties — with fee rates and a schedule of reserved wild animals appended. It records the schedule as nineteen species, listing among the mammals the kouprey, Sumatran and Javan rhinoceros, marbled cat, dugong, Eld's deer, serow, goral, Bryde's whale, Omura's whale, tapir and Schomburgk's deer, and among the birds the sarus crane, white-eyed river martin and Gurney's pitta. Establishing that a listed species uses the site is the first fact to fix. The master plan for sanctuaries and non-hunting areas needs the committee's approval. Published legal commentary records that the Act provides for a master plan for the administration and conservation of wildlife species, wildlife sanctuaries and non-hunting areas, which must be approved by the wildlife conservation and protection committee; and records the criticism made of the Act at passage, that it went through without an opportunity for public comment, two weeks before a general election. Knowing that history is useful when the participation notification is invoked. Read this with the local fishing community organisation, the community forest registration, the administrative court entry and the comprehensive plan petition entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The wetland register and the cabinet conservation measures — sixty-nine internationally important and hundreds of nationally important wetlands listed by name, location and coordinates, with an open data set
trackers.desc: Wetlands here are protected by cabinet resolution rather than by a dedicated statute, and the register is the instrument. The policy and planning office records that the rules directly governing wetland management are the cabinet resolutions of 1 August 2000 and 3 November 2009, which approved the register of wetlands — sixty-nine of international importance and a further set of national importance — together with the wetland conservation measures; and records that the office has been reviewing and updating the register, its boundaries and the conservation measures, because the status and use of each wetland has changed, which affects enforcement of the related rules. Asking which resolution and which register version applies to a site is therefore the first step, not the last. The list itself is published with names, levels, locations and coordinates, as open data. The same office publishes a list of the country's important wetlands under those two resolutions, giving the wetland's name, its level of importance — national or international — its location and its coordinates, and offers the wetlands data as an open data set. That is a checkable answer to whether a project site sits on or beside a listed wetland. The convention obligations behind the measures are stated. A parliamentary library account records that the country joined the wetlands convention in 1998 with the policy and planning office as national focal point, and that the main obligations of parties are to select important wetlands for inclusion in the international register, promote wetland conservation, plan the wise use of wetlands, and run activities to build knowledge and awareness of their importance. It records wetlands as among the most productive ecosystems, sources of biodiversity, and water storage that prevents flooding and reduces topsoil erosion. An earlier inventory gives the baseline numbers. Published material records a national wetland inventory of over four hundred pages listing sixty-one internationally important, two hundred and eight nationally important and further locally important wetlands, with the water resources department maintaining its own wetlands pages carrying the convention text. Read this with the water user organisation, the local fishing community organisation, the assessment search system and the community forest registration entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Air4Thai and the environmental open data catalogue — hourly station readings, a downloadable back-history for every station, and the same data as a public API
trackers.desc: The national air quality data is published as an open dataset with a public interface, not only as a dashboard. The environment ministry's data catalogue publishes hourly and daily fine particulate averages measured at the pollution control department's automatic monitoring stations, offering the air quality data from stations nationwide as an application programming interface in both machine-readable formats, and separately for the capital and its surrounding provinces, with download counts shown for each. A community with its own sensor can therefore compare against the official series programmatically, rather than screenshotting a map. The back-history is downloadable station by station. The department's own portal carries a history page which downloads past air quality data for all stations, and displays past data by chosen parameter and time period. Where a project is blamed for a change in local air quality, a dated series from before it began is what makes the comparison. The station network is documented, region by region. Published official material records the permanent monitoring stations counted by area — a stated number in the capital, in the five surrounding provinces, in named central, northern, north-eastern and eastern provinces, with mobile measuring vehicles as well — and records the capital's own separate network of permanent stations alongside the national ones. Knowing which station covers a district, and how far it is from the site, is the first check on any figure quoted at a hearing. The same data reaches the public through an app and a broadcaster's page. Published material records the department's free application reporting the national air quality index with hourly data for some stations, daily data, seven-day back graphs and a station map, published for the general public particularly during haze crises; and the public broadcaster republishes the same departmental data as a nationwide real-time report with health guidance by risk level. Read this with the pollution complaint system, the assessment search system, the administrative court entry and the community sampling entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: GISTDA open data and the water department's layer downloads — satellite imagery and burn-scar, flood and soil moisture layers with update dates, plus watershed class and community forest boundaries
trackers.desc: The space agency runs an open geoinformation catalogue, and each dataset carries its update date. The agency's open data system describes itself as a geoinformation data warehouse search system of the public organisation for space technology and geoinformatics, offering satellite imagery and basemaps; its listings name datasets including burn scar boundary data (latest), soil moisture data for the country, repeatedly flooded area data, and satellite imagery at two-metre detail (latest), each shown with the date it was updated and a view count. A community documenting burning or repeated flooding beside a project can therefore cite a dated national layer rather than its own photographs alone. The water department publishes downloadable layers produced by other agencies. The water resources department's geographic information system carries a downloads page listing layers with the date each was last edited and the agency that produced it — including watershed quality class from the policy and planning office, and community forest boundaries updated by the forest department. Those two layers matter directly to entries already in this bucket: the community forest registration route, and the catchment classification a project must be checked against. Provincial soil and land use information is assembled into ready-made maps. A government service catalogue records the land development department's provincial soil resource information system as integrating its own data — soil group, land use, soil suitability for crops, permanent forest boundary, problem soils, drought impact and economic crop suitability zones — into ready-made maps including a land use map, a problem soil map, a permanent forest boundary map and crop suitability maps. The national parks department publishes its own land use map data page. Parcel-level data sits in the national data catalogue. The government data catalogue records the land parcel search system as letting a person find, without travelling to a land office, the parcel shape, its position, its area, the site as seen from satellite imagery and street view, the land office coordinates, the appraised value per parcel, fees, taxes, survey costs and the survey waiting queue — the system already recorded in this bucket, here with its catalogue entry. Read this with the land office entry, the community forest registration, the wetland register and the assessment search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: เทใจ — a Thai crowdfunding platform for community and environmental projects, its published ten per cent fee and how it is added, and the foundation that receives the donations for tax purposes
trackers.desc: A crowdfunding platform exists for groups that are not registered organisations. The platform records its origin as wanting to help people who want to do good things for society — including non-profit organisations, groups of people and social enterprises — so they can make those things happen and scale them. Published description records it as a social crowdfunding platform founded by a foundation and a social innovation organisation, which screens projects against criteria including creativity, measurable impact and feasibility, publishes them, lets donors follow progress, and assures transparent use of the money. A village group with no legal form can therefore still raise money publicly. The fee is published, and so is how it is added. The platform records a ten per cent service fee on the amount a project receives, used for system maintenance, financial transaction costs and monitoring and verification of projects; and records that the fee is added on top of the target — a project seeking ten thousand baht is displayed as eleven thousand, the extra thousand being the fee, so the amount the project needs is not reduced. It records what happens on a shortfall: where a project does not reach its target but is ready to proceed, the team transfers the donations anyway; where the project owner cannot proceed, the team handles it otherwise. Knowing the fee is added rather than deducted is what makes the target realistic. Donations run through a named foundation, which is what makes them deductible. The platform's terms record the service as operated by a named company with a named royally-sponsored rural reconstruction foundation as the recipient of donations for the various projects, and record that a donor wanting the deduction must supply the specified information in full and correctly. Its questions record that donating through the platform is deductible at one times the amount whichever project is supported, because projects sit under that foundation, and records the earlier requirement to submit the receipt to the revenue department for donations before a stated date. Published material records the general limit that donations, combined, must not exceed ten per cent of assessable income after deductions. Read this with the environmental fund, the community forest registration, the wetland register and the assessment search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: มูลนิธิศูนย์ข้อมูลชุมชน — a legal aid foundation for community rights cases, its office address published, and its stated grounding in community, human and environmental rights
trackers.desc: A second legal aid organisation exists for community rights, alongside the environmental law foundation already recorded here. Published description records the centre as a non-profit non-governmental organisation providing legal aid to communities on community rights, human rights and environmental rights, grounded in the constitution and in the international covenants on civil and political rights and on economic, social and cultural rights; and records it as a watchdog on the implementation of those two covenants. Where a case is about a community's rights rather than a pollution measurement, that framing is the one that fits. Its address is published, which is what makes it reachable. Its own page gives a street address with soi and junction numbers, district and postcode in the capital, and published listings record it in a national human rights commission's own organisation network directory — the commission already recorded in this bucket — so a community can find it through the state body it may already be complaining to. Its stated purpose is access to justice for a liveable environment. The organisation's own description states its aim as ensuring access to justice so that people may live in a good and peaceful environment, and records it as committed to protect and promote human rights, community rights and the environment. Two things follow for a community: the covenants give arguments that do not depend on domestic environmental legislation alone, and a watchdog role on covenant implementation means the organisation has standing reasons to document what happened, not only to litigate it. Read this with the environmental law foundation, the human rights commission, the justice fund and the administrative court entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The volunteer placement foundation and its organisation directory — profiles of community organisations by issue, with addresses and volunteer vacancies, including land and ethnic-rights bodies
trackers.desc: A volunteer placement foundation publishes profiles of the community organisations it places people with, and those profiles double as a directory. Each entry records the organisation's name, the issues it works on, its stated objectives, its current projects, its address and, where applicable, how many volunteers it is taking. For a community looking for an organisation that already works on its issue nearby, that is a list with contacts attached rather than a national abstraction. The profiles name land and resource rights bodies directly. One profile records a northern development foundation whose issues are rights in the management of land and resources, and the rights of ethnic groups, with the stated objective of strengthening networks of small-scale farmers and people's movements to push for solutions on rights in land and natural resources, and campaigning to raise social awareness of participation in creating fairness; and records its goal as helping poor farmers both inside and outside forest areas to have strong organisations and networks, aware of and confident in community rights, able to be self-reliant and to access land and other resources as factors of production. Another records a highland community development foundation working on rights and status for stateless elders and people without rights, strengthening communities, youth health, and supporting networks including a river basin people's network, publishing its street address, village, sub-district and province and its own website. The rights commission's own network register carries the same kind of material. A national human rights commission organisation register — the commission already recorded in this bucket — publishes organisation profiles including named contact people with street addresses, districts, postcodes, telephone numbers and emails; one profile records northern organisations meeting in 1991 after contests over land, water and forest in which local people had no power against capital and politicians did not listen, and deciding to build joint rural-urban working so that rural work would not be too isolated. Read this with the community rights legal aid foundation, the human rights commission, the community council and the community organisations institute entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Who to call after a chemical release — three organisations that issue joint statements on industrial accidents, the demands they make of the agencies, and the sampling programme behind them
trackers.desc: Three named organisations act together on industrial accidents, and their joint statement shows what to demand. A joint statement records that after a chemical leak from a named polyester factory in a named district spread a foul smell over a wide area on a stated date — with local people reporting it to a regional pollution control office — an environmental law foundation, an ecological recovery foundation and an international campaigning organisation, which work together, issued a joint statement. It records their demands on the state agencies: that the pollution control department and the industrial works department must investigate the leak and explain the information to the public quickly and straightforwardly, take legal measures against the polluter, and follow up, gather data and provide assistance to those affected. A community with a plant on its doorstep now knows which two agencies to name, and which three organisations already write to them. The ecological foundation's remit is supporting the people harmed. That foundation records itself as an independent non-profit organisation whose mission focuses on academic work and on supporting communities affected by pollution and hazardous substances to obtain justice, particularly those close to the risk or on the margins, who face health, environmental and economic hardship from the expansion of industry, and supporting those affected to receive help, remedy or fair compensation. It records itself registered under the law in August 2009, after operating from earlier as a named industrial pollution study and campaign group. Its sampling programme is the evidence engine. A joint statement with a foreign association records the two organisations having gone into areas affected by industrial pollution in several regions of the country to collect environmental samples, then sent the samples for analysis in laboratories in Europe, with results showing contamination by several types of hazardous pollutants, especially heavy metals and persistent organic pollutants, in a number of areas; and records the project's aim as advancing the public's right of access to information, especially for communities affected by industrial pollution. Read this with the pollution map, the environmental law foundation, the community rights legal aid foundation and the human rights commission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: นักสืบสายน้ำ and นักสืบสายลม — citizen bio-indicator surveys a village can run itself, reading water quality from stream invertebrates and air quality from lichens on bark
trackers.desc: A community can read its own water quality without a laboratory, and the method is published. A foundation records launching a water detective project from about 1996 to 2003, inviting children and adults to read the health of streams from the community of small freshwater animals — the aquatic insect larvae living on stones and sand beneath the water — which can be used as biological indicators of water quality, assessed together with other physical characteristics of the stream, such as bankside vegetation, bankside animal communities, sinuosity, colour, temperature and flow speed. For a community upstream or downstream of a project, a repeatable survey it can run itself is a baseline nobody can withhold. The air version reads pollution off tree bark. The same foundation records that air quality can be known more precisely than by smell by observing lichens, explaining that lichens are half fungus and half alga and are fragile because they take in pollution easily, unlike plants whose leaves have a waxy coating, so that where there is much pollution there may be few lichens, or in severe cases none at all. It names the pollution sources it is read against — vehicle exhaust, factory stacks, construction dust, waste burning and, in some areas, agricultural chemicals. The method has been taught to villagers and schools, with the tools listed. Published reporting records training in which participants act as wind detectives, examining lichens on trees to see air quality; water detectives, finding aquatic insects and animals to see water quality; and soil detectives, taking soil samples to measure acidity and alkalinity, using a magnifying glass and a manual to survey and record. It records a public health research institute supporting eight communities and schools in a named district to build a network for monitoring natural change that ordinary people can carry out themselves, with about forty villagers and teachers from named villages in two sub-districts surveying soil, water, air and living things over three days. Read this with the pollution map, the ecological recovery foundation, the community rights legal aid foundation and the volunteer placement directory entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: BioThai — a registered foundation supplying data and technical backing to farmers and local networks on biological resources, with a published address, telephone and email
trackers.desc: A foundation exists specifically to supply information and technical support to farmers and local communities on biological resources. It records that, because work on biodiversity and local knowledge had widened, there ought to be an organisation that permanently supports farmers, local communities and the networks working on those issues with data, academic and other backing, and that it therefore registered formally as a foundation in 2006, continuing a line of work begun in 1995 and since widening to food security, monitoring the role of corporations and fair trade. For a community facing a plantation, a seed contract or a contamination question, a body whose stated job is supplying the evidence is the ally to find first. Its objects and activities are listed, and they are usable. A directory records its objects as research on biological resources, agriculture, food, and farmers' and community rights, and promoting and disseminating knowledge on those subjects to the general public; and lists its activities as supporting the role and strength of farmers, local communities and people's networks in conserving, restoring, developing and sustainably using biological resources; campaigning on and publicising impacts on biological resources, such as movement against biopiracy; driving policy and law to protect biological resources and local wisdom through legislation of a distinct, purpose-built kind; and following the overall picture of free trade agreements the country negotiates with other countries, with responsibility for tracking and analysing those issues. Free trade agreement text is where seed and plant-variety rules are often set, and someone is reading them. It is contactable and it has a physical base. It publishes a house number, lane, road, village, sub-district, district, province and postcode, a telephone number and an email address. Published material records the foundation sharing a new base with a sustainable agriculture foundation on a plot of about two rai, described as a space for communicating food security issues in policy, problems of eating, and access to good chemical-free food, alongside a learning area on the processes of cultivating, cooking and eating. Read this with the community rights legal aid foundation, the citizen bio-indicator surveys, the ecological recovery foundation and the volunteer directory entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The eastern people's network and a city municipality's complaint system — a provincial coordinator who calls in the district chief and provincial industry office, and the eleven communities that sued and won a pollution control zone
trackers.desc: Eleven communities around one industrial estate sued together, and the case is dated. Published reporting records that on 1 October 2007, 27 representatives of residents from 11 communities around the industrial estate jointly filed suit against the national environment board at the provincial administrative court, on the ground that it had neglected its duty by not declaring the area a pollution control zone in order to control, reduce and eliminate pollution. A named provincial administrative court, eleven named communities and a specific duty is the shape of a case a neighbourhood can actually bring. A provincial network exists and its coordinator is the person villagers write to. Published reporting records residents of a numbered village in a named sub-district and district writing to the coordinator of the eastern people's network to ask him to get state agencies to verify the facts of a gas leak, and records that he coordinated with the provincial industry office and the district chief, after which the cause was found to be sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and lead vapour from factories in a named industrial zone, with nearby trees withering and dying and residents' breathing affected. Knowing that one named coordinator can pull in the provincial industry office and the district chief is worth more than a national hotline. The network's own methods and its allies are recorded. Published material records the network campaigning with residents of a named district against the expansion of an industrial estate using a loudspeaker vehicle and distributing leaflets, and submitting a letter to five senate committee members who had previously visited the area and found many irregularities, asking them to examine a government announcement made without regard to impacts on people. A local group's own history lists its partners as the eastern people's network, a council of work-related patients' groups and an international campaigning organisation, each with a named contact. The city municipality runs its own complaint system. The municipality covering the estate publishes a complaints and grievances system with an online form, case status checking, and separate channels for reporting corruption, alongside its street address. Read this with the pollution map, the joint statements on chemical releases, the community rights legal aid foundation and the citizen bio-indicator surveys entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Provincial natural resources and environment offices — the ministry's representative in each province, with environmental complaints named as a duty, published addresses and phone numbers, and a separate corruption channel
trackers.desc: Each province has an office of the environment ministry, and handling complaints is one of its listed duties. A provincial office publishes its powers and duties, which include coordinating, advising, promoting, publicising and disseminating knowledge on environmental quality management, pollution control and environmental protection through the participation of all sectors; handling environmental complaints; and acting under the national environmental quality promotion and conservation legislation and other related laws. For a village whose complaint has stalled with a district office, the provincial office is the next named door — and complaints are its job, not a favour. Its standing as the ministry's provincial representative is stated in a ministerial regulation. Another provincial office records that under a 2017 ministerial regulation on the ministry's permanent secretary office, the provincial office is to act as the ministry's representative in the region in directing, implementing, supervising, promoting, supporting and coordinating natural resources and environment work within the provincial area. Knowing the office speaks for the ministry inside the province tells a community what weight its letter carries. The offices publish addresses, telephone and fax numbers, and their internal divisions. One provincial office publishes a house number, village, road, sub-district, district, province and postcode with two telephone lines and a fax number; another publishes a water resources division with its own email, telephone and fax. Several publish a service manual for people coming to the office. A separate corruption channel is published alongside. The same offices record guidelines and procedures for handling complaints of corruption and misconduct, a channel for reporting corruption and misconduct, and statistical data on such complaints, alongside a code of ethics for state officials and a provincial anti-corruption operations centre. Read this with the pollution complaint system, the eastern people's network, the community rights legal aid foundation and the citizen bio-indicator surveys entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Damrongtham centres — a complaint desk in every provincial hall and every district office, a 24-hour hotline, mobile rapid units, and per-province contact lists including the governor's direct line
trackers.desc: There is a complaint desk in every provincial hall and every district office. Published notices record five channels: filing in person at the ministry centre, at the provincial centre in every provincial hall, and at the district centre in every district office; filing by post to a named post box or to the address of any provincial or district centre; the 1567 hotline, available 24 hours; and further electronic channels. The ministry centre records its purpose as being a hub for integrating the cooperation of government agencies of every ministry and state enterprises in serving the public efficiently, equitably, with quality and speed. For a village whose complaint has gone nowhere with the responsible agency, the district office already holds a desk whose job is to route it. Each province publishes its own contact list, and it goes beyond a switchboard. A published compilation of provincial centre contacts lists, for each province, items including filing in person at the provincial hall with the floor given, postal address, the 24-hour hotline, a mobile rapid unit, a complaints box, an email address, office telephone and fax, and a direct telephone line to the provincial governor, noting for each province whether a social media page, a messaging account, the national services application or a municipal reporting platform is available. A published direct line to the governor, listed beside the hotline, is an unusual thing to have in writing. Provincial centres also publish their complaint statistics and their own reporting routes. One province's page lists complaint and grievance filing through the provincial centre, electronic services, annual statistical data on corruption complaints, a service satisfaction survey report and the provincial internal audit unit, alongside a messaging-platform channel where a resident types the problem, photographs it, selects the problem type and shares the location. Another province's centre publishes its street address on the first floor of the provincial hall with the hotline, two telephone numbers and a fax, and records its establishment under a 2014 national order requiring every province to set up a centre. Read this with the provincial environment offices, the eastern people's network, the pollution complaint system and the community rights legal aid foundation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Provincial, branch and district land offices — where a boundary survey is applied for, which office holds which kind of title, the queue-ticket steps, and the private licensed surveyor option
trackers.desc: A boundary survey is applied for at the land office where the land lies, and the counter steps are published. A government service register records that an applicant must submit documentary evidence to the competent officer at the land office in the area where the land is located, contacting the public relations officer first on the day of application, to have documents checked initially and to take a queue ticket, to await the application and examination in order, and a second time on the day of registration, to take a queue ticket and await registration in order. It lists the types of subdivision survey that may be requested, including subdivision in the original name, division of co-ownership, division by gift, division by sale, division on expropriation, division deducting land for public benefit, division of land acquired by possession under named sections of the civil and commercial code, division under a court judgment, and division for land allocation. Division deducting land for public benefit, named in the same list, is the entry point a community should look for. Which office to approach depends on the kind of document held. Published description records that an application may be filed at the provincial land office, a provincial branch land office, or the district land office where the land is located, and that for a full title deed the provincial or branch office is the one to contact, while for a certificate of utilisation it is the district land office, unless the district chief's authority has been revoked, in which case the provincial or branch office applies. It records the applicant as needing to state the condition of the land — paddy, orchard, field or residential. A private licensed surveyor may be named in the application. The same service register records a route in which the applicant files the survey application specifying the private licensed survey office that is to carry out the work, to the provincial, branch or sub-branch land office where the land is located, with the registry section receiving the application; and records the identity documents required, including a power of attorney where someone acts for a person or juristic person. The department publishes announced survey costs. Read this with the Damrongtham centres, the provincial environment offices, the eastern people's network and the community rights legal aid foundation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Sub-district administrative organisations and the village assembly that feeds their plan — a legal person with its own council, roughly 6,500 of them, and a local development plan that must be built through a people's assembly
trackers.desc: The sub-district body is a legal person with its own council and its own plan. A sub-district organisation's published statement of powers records its duties under the decentralisation legislation as including preparing its own local development plan; providing and maintaining land routes, waterways and drainage; providing and controlling markets, piers, ferry landings and parking; public utilities and other construction; promotion of training and occupations; commerce and investment promotion; tourism promotion; education; social welfare and quality of life for children, women, the elderly and the disadvantaged; and maintenance of local arts, traditions, local wisdom and culture, along with improvement of congested community areas. It records a numbered section requiring that budgeting, procurement, auditing, performance evaluation and disclosure of information follow the law and the criteria set by the interior ministry. For a village, that is the body that holds the local plan and the budget behind it. The plan must be built through a people's assembly. A published planning manual records that the local development plan is made from the needs of the people in the community, through the participation of the people in the community by holding a people's assembly, taking account of the financial position and the urgency of the local authority's needs; and records that under a named section of the 1999 decentralisation legislation, municipalities, the special city and sub-district administrative organisations have the power and duty to prepare their own local development plans. The parts of the body are set out, with residents named as one of them. A sub-district organisation records its working structure as the council as the legislative side; the chief executive as the executive side; sub-district officials as the permanent civil service side; the people in the area as the centre of development who take part in implementation; and the supervisory side. Published description records an executive of one chief executive and two deputies, directly elected, and records approximately 6,500 such organisations at one date. Read this with the Damrongtham centres, the provincial environment offices, the community organisation councils and the district land offices entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: WALHI — Wahana Lingkungan Hidup Indonesia (Friends of the Earth Indonesia)
trackers.desc: Indonesia's largest and oldest environmental advocacy network, founded 1980, uniting several hundred member NGOs and individuals with independent offices in most provinces. WHO TO ENLIST: the provincial WALHI office nearest the project — the organisation works on agrarian conflict over natural resources, indigenous and peasant rights, coastal and marine issues, deforestation, mining and pollution. You CAN: plug into an existing regional campaign, get help arranging legal representation for a community, and draw on WALHI's record of pushing law enforcement in environmental crime cases and forcing the primary-forest, peatland and oil-palm moratoria. For activists: the fastest route to allies who already know the province and the company.

trackers.name: The Samdhana Institute — grants programme
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a Southeast Asian grantmaker giving micro to medium-sized grants, plus urgent-action grants, directly to Indigenous peoples and local communities, community-based and civil-society organisations, informal groups and individual activists — for land and territorial rights, natural-resource governance, and community-led climate and livelihood work. Its own site names offices only in Bogor, Indonesia and in Cagayan de Oro and Quezon City, Philippines, which is where this entry is placed; it describes its remit as Southeast Asia generally, so groups elsewhere in the region should still ask. WHO IT SUITS: groups that cannot get money from conventional donors — Samdhana states its grantmaking principle as funding the "un-fundable", and an unregistered informal group is not disqualified. HOW IT DIFFERS: it supplies environmental conflict mediation and technical support alongside the grant rather than only writing cheques.

trackers.name: Friends of the Earth Asia Pacific
trackers.desc: The Asia Pacific regional structure of Friends of the Earth International, formed in 2008, whose member groups work on community-based struggles against destructive projects, particularly mining and other extractive industries, alongside Indigenous peoples, peasant farmers, fisherfolk and trade unions. WHO TO ENLIST: the national member group nearest the project. In this region Friends of the Earth International's own directory names groups in Bangladesh (BELA, the Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers' Association), India, Indonesia (WALHI), Japan, Malaysia (Sahabat Alam Malaysia), Nepal, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines (the Legal Rights and Natural Resources Center), South Korea and Sri Lanka. You CAN: reach an organisation that already works community-side in your own country, and draw regional weight onto a local fight. For activists: in several of these countries the Friends of the Earth affiliate is the most experienced community-side environmental body there is.

trackers.name: Badan Pemeriksa Keuangan (BPK RI)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Indonesia, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: AHU Online
trackers.desc: Indonesia's Ministry of Law company registry (AHU). — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: AMDALNET — national environmental assessment system
trackers.desc: Indonesia's national AMDAL (environmental impact assessment) system, run by the environment ministry (launched Feb 2023). You CAN get: environmental-assessment filings and permit processing routed through the national platform. You CAN'T get: older paper-era files not migrated. For activists: check whether a project has lodged its AMDAL, and follow the documents.

trackers.name: Beneficial Ownership Register
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Satu Data Indonesia
trackers.desc: National — Indonesian government open data portal. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Indonesia.

trackers.name: INAPROC / LKPP
trackers.desc: Indonesia's national public-procurement platform run by the LKPP procurement agency. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Indonesia, and for how much.

trackers.name: Indonesian Parliamentary Center (IPC)
trackers.desc: Indonesian parliament-monitoring CSO (since 2005) — tracks transparency of DPR lawmaking using published proceedings, advocates freedom-of-information (UU KIP), and drives Open Parliament Indonesia. Part of the international PMO network.

trackers.name: Komisi Informasi Pusat (Central Information Commission)
trackers.desc: Indonesia's independent central information commission, resolving public-information disputes through mediation and non-litigation adjudication and setting public-information service standards under the Public Information Openness Law.

trackers.name: Wamena District Court
trackers.desc: Wamena District Court — tribunal (Indonesia).

trackers.name: Direktori Putusan Mahkamah Agung
trackers.desc: Official Supreme Court directory of Indonesian court decisions — one of the world's largest open judgment databases. · Find here: Indonesia's official directory of Supreme Court and lower-court judgments (Direktori Putusan).

trackers.name: Publish What You Pay Indonesia
trackers.desc: National civil-society coalition of the global Publish What You Pay campaign — advocates for transparency in oil, gas and mining revenues in Indonesia.

trackers.name: Seknas FITRA (Indonesian Forum for Budget Transparency)
trackers.desc: National coalition (founded 1999) that builds databases and accessible analysis of Indonesia's national and regional budgets and campaigns for budget transparency. Here you can trace how Indonesia's national and regional budgets allocate money, in FITRA's budget-transparency databases and analysis.

trackers.name: Calang District Court
trackers.desc: Calang District Court — tribunal (Indonesia).

trackers.name: BPS – Statistics Indonesia
trackers.desc: Indonesia's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Indonesia.

trackers.name: ICEL — Indonesian Center for Environmental Law
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a non-profit foundation established 19 July 1993, working specifically on environmental law through research, advocacy and building the legal capacity of communities. THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR PEOPLE AT RISK: ICEL files amicus curiae briefs supporting environmental defenders who are themselves prosecuted for opposing land control and company operations, working with the Center for Environmental Law and Climate Justice at the University of Indonesia and with ELAW, the Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide — so there is a route here for a defender facing criminal charges, not only for a community challenging a permit. It also publishes Jurnal Hukum Lingkungan Indonesia and a compendium of selected environmental judgments. Offices in Jakarta.

trackers.name: IUPHHK-RE — holding forest through a restoration concession
trackers.desc: HOW LAND GETS HELD HERE, AND IT IS A WORKAROUND. Conservation groups cannot readily buy and own Indonesian forest; instead they take a timber concession licence over production forest and use it to restore rather than log. The first, to PT REKI under SK Menhut SK.293/Menhut-II/2007 of 28 August 2007, covered 52,170 hectares in Musi Banyuasin, South Sumatra; a second in 2010 added 46,385 hectares in Jambi — together Hutan Harapan, about 98,554 hectares. THE TRANSFERABLE LESSON: a production-forest concession must be held by a legally constituted company, so the BirdLife consortium (Burung Indonesia, RSPB, BirdLife International) formed a foundation AND had to incorporate PT REKI as a corporate vehicle to hold the licence. Holders may manage water services, biodiversity protection, nature tourism, carbon, and non-timber products such as rattan, sago, nipah and bamboo. KNOW WHAT YOU ARE TAKING ON. The licence is legally still an HPH, so logging remains permitted on a restoration concession — researchers have called for that rule to be removed. Allocated areas are not clean and clear: tenurial conflict may be unresolved, and sites face encroachment, illegal logging and illegal mining. Fees are charged at the same rate as commercial concessions despite no timber revenue, permitting does not run through a market mechanism, and local government support has been weak. And community work is not optional — one concession protects its ecosystem by working with 900 communities through village forest management, small enterprise and loans, because without alternative income, encroachment and land-clearing fires continue whatever the licence says.

trackers.name: Hutan adat — customary forest is not state forest (MK 35/2012)
trackers.desc: THE RULING THAT CHANGED OWNERSHIP. Before it, customary forest was state forest whose management could merely be handed to the community — leaving the community as, in effect, a proxy of the state with only a right to manage. Constitutional Court decision 35/PUU-X/2012 split forest into three categories — hutan hak, hutan negara and hutan adat — and placed hutan adat within hutan hak, forest encumbered with land rights, not state forest. That now sits in Article 5(1)(b) of Forestry Law 41/1999 as amended by Law 6/2023. In hutan adat the customary community is both owner and manager, the main actor rather than a partner, and the forest keeps its conservation, protection and/or production functions. CRITERIA FOR DESIGNATION: the area lies within the customary territory, is forested with clear boundaries, is managed according to the community's local wisdom, and there is still forest-product gathering nearby for daily needs. Hutan adat is one of 5 social forestry schemes, alongside Hutan Kemasyarakatan, Hutan Desa, Kemitraan Kehutanan and Hutan Tanaman Rakyat.

trackers.name: Applying for hutan adat — the Perda first, and a 180-day clock
trackers.desc: THE SEQUENCE DEFEATS MOST APPLICANTS. Recognition of hutan adat is an accessory act — it must be preceded by recognition of the customary community itself. If the community is inside state forest area, that means a Peraturan Daerah; if outside, a regulation of the regional head. So the first fight is at the kabupaten or provincial legislature, not the ministry. THE APPLICATION goes to the Minister of Environment and Forestry, copied to regional parties including the regional head, and the Dirjen Perhutanan Sosial dan Kemitraan validates and verifies the documents. REQUIREMENTS SPLIT IN TWO: syarat mutlak (absolute) — identity of the community, a map of the customary territory, and a statement letter signed by its head — and syarat toleransi, which is where the Perda or regional head decision sits, so field verification can proceed while that is still outstanding. WATCH THE 180-DAY CLOCK: if requirements are incomplete or incorrect the application is returned, and if not completed within 180 days it is rejected. EXPECT RESISTANCE: roughly 40 million hectares was at stake after the ruling, and a 2013 ministry circular (SE.1/Menhut-II/2013) said release of hutan adat from state forest required regional government agreement — read by commentators as institutional self-preservation — while related rules demand written proof of claims over land held customarily.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: WALHI regional offices — 29 named directors, and the nine provinces with none
trackers.desc: One page routes you to a named person in your own province instead of a national inbox — the Eksekutif Daerah directory lists 29 regional offices with the director's name, street address, telephone and email, grouped as Banumapa (Bali, Maluku Utara, NTB, NTT, Papua), Jawa (Jabar, Jakarta, Jateng, Jatim, Yogyakarta), Kalimantan (Kalbar, Kalsel, Kalteng, Kaltim), Sulawesi (Gorontalo, Sulteng, Sulbar, Sulsel, Sultra, Sulut) and Sumatera (Aceh, Babel, Bengkulu, Jambi, Lampung, Riau, Sumbar, Sumsel, Sumut). WALHI is Friends of the Earth Indonesia and litigates as well as campaigns. Nine of Indonesia's 38 provinces have no office on this list: Kepulauan Riau, Banten, Kalimantan Utara, Maluku, Papua Barat, Papua Barat Daya, Papua Selatan, Papua Tengah and Papua Pegunungan — if you are in one of those, the nearest listed office is the route in, and there is no local number to hunt for. The Gorontalo entry carries no street address and a placeholder telephone, so treat it as unverified and go through the national office at Jln. Tegal Parang Utara No 14, Jakarta Selatan 12790, +62-21-79193363. Read the directory on walhi.or.id itself: several provincial WALHI sites republish this exact page, Bali address included, and those copies are not the canonical source.

trackers.name: YLBHI–LBH — 18 legal aid offices, and 'structural legal aid' is why they take land cases
trackers.desc: Eighteen LBH branch offices in eighteen provinces, and the consultation page tells you to write to the nearest one by e-mail, with the full list published there — Banda Aceh, Medan, Padang, Palembang, Bandar Lampung, Jakarta, Bandung, Semarang, Yogyakarta, Surabaya, Bali, Makassar, Manado, Papua, Pekanbaru, Palangka Raya, Samarinda and West Kalimantan. The foundation was set up on 28 October 1970 on Adnan Buyung Nasution's initiative with the backing of the then Governor of Jakarta. The doctrine is the reason a land case gets taken at all. LBH works on bantuan hukum struktural — structural legal aid, meaning assistance given to the poor and the weak through efforts to change the unequal social, political, economic and cultural structure around them rather than casework alone. A community losing land to a concession is a structural case in exactly that sense, which is why these offices litigate against plantations, mines and evictions rather than only defending individuals. The gate is a poverty certificate, and the village issues it. Where aid is drawn under the state-funded scheme, an accredited legal aid organisation requires an application, written or spoken, giving the applicant's identity and the substance of the problem; the documents in the case; and a surat keterangan miskin, a certificate of indigence from the lurah, kepala desa or an official of equivalent rank where the applicant lives. Understand that early, because in a land conflict the village head may be aligned with the project, and the person who signs your certificate can be the person you are fighting — so ask the LBH office directly whether it can take the case outside the state scheme. Coverage is uneven, and the gap is filled elsewhere. Eighteen provinces of thirty-eight leaves Maluku, Nusa Tenggara, most of Sulawesi and several of Papua's newer provinces writing to another region — but WALHI's regional directory covers most of exactly those places, so the two networks' blank spots barely overlap and a community should check both. Head office: Jl. Diponegoro No. 74, Menteng, Central Jakarta 10320.

trackers.name: AMAN — map your customary territory before somebody else maps it
trackers.desc: The instruction its own organisers give is the whole point: map your customary territory before another party maps it. AMAN and BRWA, the Customary Territory Registration Agency, run participatory mapping of adat territory, and by 2015 member communities had mapped 7.4 million hectares that way. The alliance runs mapping training continuously — six adat communities in Lebak, Banten took a six-day course from 23 to 28 December 2024 — and the sequence it teaches is to assemble the social data and a written history of territorial ownership first, hold the deliberation with neighbouring clans second, and only then walk the boundary. Check the eligibility test before writing, because it is specific and it excludes people. Membership is open to adat communities only, not to organisations and not to local communities in general, and a community must be able to evidence five things: its history of origin, its customary territory, its customary institutions, its customary law and adjudication, and its cultural practice. A community that cannot evidence all five is masyarakat lokal rather than masyarakat adat, and this is not its door. You will be dealing with a structure, not a head office. There are roughly 20 regional boards at about provincial level and some 110 to 115 district boards, several of which run their own sites as subdomains of aman.or.id; case services are handled by PPMAN, the alliance's own legal defence body, and mapping through its UKP3 unit — so ask for the district board and for PPMAN by name rather than writing to the centre. Membership stood at 2,279 adat communities in May 2016. Be clear what a map is and is not. A participatory map is the evidence base, not the recognition: state recognition comes through a district-level regulation or decree, and only once that exists can customary forest designation follow. The alliance's own news carries examples of those decrees being made, which is what a completed sequence looks like. Board counts differ between AMAN's own documents, so take the current figure from the alliance rather than from any single publication.

trackers.name: Yayasan KEHATI — Indonesia's biodiversity grant fund, and the costs it may not cover
trackers.desc: This is where the money is: an endowment-backed foundation whose entire mandate is to raise, manage and disburse grants for biodiversity, which has worked with more than a thousand local organisations from Aceh to Papua and moved over US$200 million. It was created on 12 January 1994 out of the Rio Earth Summit and the 1993 Tokyo Declaration, with the founding American grant held as an endowment invested in shares and bonds so that the returns pay for the grants; further money comes from bilateral and multilateral donors, companies, philanthropy and crowdfunding. Its three priority ecosystems are agriculture, forest, and coastal and small islands. Who can apply, from its own programme guidelines: environmental, forestry and conservation NGOs established and operating in Indonesia; local community groups and adat law communities, including those whose livelihoods depend on forest resources; the Indonesian arms of qualifying international or regional bodies; and universities. Who cannot is the part to read twice. Government institutions, agencies, departments, regional government and kelurahan offices are excluded, with state universities the only exception — so a village administration cannot apply and the community group has to be the applicant. The programme administrator, the fund's depository, Conservation International and KEHATI itself are also barred from applying to the funds KEHATI administers. Grants go out by call for proposals in numbered cycles rather than continuously, so the thing to watch is the current call; it runs the TFCA-Sumatera and TFCA-Kalimantan debt-for-nature funds as administrator, each with its own eligibility and its own cycle. One warning about what the money is for. An older KEHATI grant FAQ circulating online states that its grants may not be used to buy or own land or buildings, nor for construction, renovation, vehicles or equipment. That has not been confirmed on the foundation's current site, so ask before building a land purchase plan around this fund, because the answer decides whether it is your fund at all. Grantees go through institutional due diligence and are then trained: the 2025 SOLUSI cohort spent five days in Bogor on grant management and reporting, on free, prior and informed consent, and on gender and social inclusion. Its forest programme includes Taman Kehati, genetic reserve areas outside the forest estate managed jointly by local government and local communities, which is a route for land sitting outside the forest zone.

trackers.name: Nexus3 Foundation — takes the samples, and funds communities to take their own
trackers.desc: The only body in this file that both produces the measurement and pays for communities to produce their own. Its grant programme, run with Arnika and IPEN, explicitly funds environmental sampling and pollution monitoring alongside media investigation, community organising and capacity building, and is open to initiatives concerning mining, mineral processing and smelters. Applicants are encouraged to combine two or three activity types in one proposal. It does not fund commercial or profit-oriented activity, illegal or violent activity, personal benefits or vehicle purchase. No other fund recorded here will pay for sampling — Thailand's Environment Fund and KEHATI both fund building and managing instead — so where the thing you need is a number, this is the window to read. Its own testing work shows what the pipeline actually involves. For its mercury study it collected samples in Tapanuli Selatan and Mandailing Natal in North Sumatra and in Sukabumi in West Java between March and November 2024, and sent them to the national research agency's laboratory at Tanjung Bintang in Lampung for total mercury analysis — carrying a domestic wildlife transport permit issued by the local conservation office for the whole journey from the sampling site to the laboratory. That permit step is the kind of thing that stops an unprepared community at the roadside, and it is worth asking about before any biological sample is collected. The Weda Bay work shows what independent results can establish. With Universitas Tadulako, fieldwork in July 2024 around the nickel mining and processing area of Weda Bay in Central Halmahera found mercury and arsenic in fish samples, and among residents' blood samples 47 per cent contained mercury while 32 per cent showed arsenic above safe limits; the findings were presented publicly in May 2025. Grant calls open and close, so check the current one rather than relying on a page date. +62 811 3995464, nexus3@nexus3foundation.org.

trackers.name: Hutan Harapan / PT REKI — the licence route that takes production forest off the conversion track
trackers.desc: The instrument is a licence, not a purchase, and it is open to anyone who can form a company. Under Indonesian forestry rules, ecosystem restoration in production forest is carried out through an IUPHHK-RE permit. In 2005 the forestry minister designated about 101,355 hectares straddling Jambi and South Sumatra as the country's first ecosystem restoration area; a consortium of bird conservation organisations formed a foundation and then — because a production forest concession must be held by a legally constituted company — incorporated PT Restorasi Ekosistem Indonesia specifically to hold the permit. Permits followed for South Sumatra in 2007 and for Jambi in 2010, together covering roughly 98,555 hectares. That incorporation step is the transferable lesson.
