trackers.desc: Each province's ministry office publishes the accredited legal aid organisations in that province, with names and addresses. A provincial ministry office records that legal aid institutions provide legal services free of charge to recipients who are unable to pay, and lists accredited offices with the name of the head, the office address including street, village and regency, and social media or email contacts. For a community in one province, a provincial list of accredited offices beats a national organisation's switchboard. The two kinds of help are distinguished, and the non-court side is the wider one. The same office records the scope as litigation aid, covering accompaniment of a case at investigation and trial stages, and non-litigation aid, covering accompaniment of a case outside court, mediation, negotiation, legal counselling, community empowerment, drafting of legal documents and case investigation. Drafting documents and investigating a case, free, is what most land disputes actually need. The application requirements are published, and one of them is issued by the village. Provincial ministry pages record that an applicant must submit a request orally or in writing containing at least the applicant's identity and a brief description of the matter; hand over documents relating to the case; and attach a certificate of poverty from the lurah, the village head, or an official of equivalent level at the applicant's place of residence; and record that within at most three working days after the request is declared complete, the legal aid institution must give an answer accepting or rejecting it, and where accepted provides aid on the basis of a special power of attorney from the recipient. Knowing the village head issues the qualifying letter, and that the answer is due in three working days, is what turns a right into an appointment. The nationwide network behind it is provincial by design. The national foundation records branch offices established in the regions after the first city office, naming more than a dozen cities, and records that it now has 18 branch offices in 18 provinces. A published directory gives, for each branch, street address, telephone, fax, email and website. Read this with the legal companions, the customary territory register, the fisherfolk coalition and the environmental forum entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Village forest management bodies — formed by village deliberation, appointed by the village head's decision, with duties listed one by one, and the district facilitators who help them apply
trackers.desc: A village forest body is created by the village's own regulation and its members appointed by the village head's decision. One village's published decision records the body established under a village regulation of 2018 on the formation of the village forest management body, appoints named office-holders as its committee, and lists their duties: strengthening the body; drawing up the village forest management plan; marking the boundaries of the village forest working area; developing village forest enterprises; developing the institution; protecting and securing the working area; and formulating the arrangement for sharing the results and benefits of management by deliberation and consensus. A village decision letter with seven listed duties is a template any other village can copy. What the body is, and who forms it, is stated by a provincial forestry service. A provincial forestry department records the body as an organisation formed by the village community through deliberation to manage the village forest sustainably and fairly, whose main functions are planning, implementing and supervising village forest management; regulating the fair use of forest resources; and being a forum for community communication and collaboration, with roles including protecting the forest from damage and illegal activity. Published material records that the body is formed by the village government and connects with the forest management unit, the provincial forestry service and the ministry, and is usually accompanied by a third party, naming four villages that appointed one organisation as their facilitator. The permit route and the verification are recorded through one village's case. Published material records a village body formed in 2017 to apply to the ministry with a proposed area of about 9,332.97 hectares, records the villagers' proposal as verified by a regional social forestry and environmental partnership office, and records the verified qualifying area as about 2,758 hectares in permanent production forest. It records support from named organisations for permit processing, capacity training, potential surveys, boundary marking and drawing up the village forest management plan, and a regional office supplying a river boat for ecotourism. Read this with the customary territory register, the provincial legal aid offices, the deforestation data foundation and the indigenous alliance entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The village consultative body — a village-level legislature elected by territorial representation, whose agreement a village regulation needs, with thirteen listed tasks and a budget line of its own
trackers.desc: A village regulation cannot pass without this body's agreement. Published village and ministry material records the body's functions under a named article of the 2014 village legislation as discussing and agreeing draft village regulations together with the village head; receiving and channelling the aspirations of the village community; and supervising the performance of the village head. For a hamlet whose land is about to be committed by a village regulation, the body that must agree it is the first place to be heard. Its tasks are listed one by one, and they include convening the village assembly. A village's own page records thirteen tasks under a named 2016 ministerial regulation, including digging out, receiving, managing and channelling community aspirations; convening the body's own deliberation and the village assembly; forming the village head election committee; convening a special assembly for an interim village head election; discussing and agreeing draft village regulations with the village head; supervising the village head's performance; evaluating the report on the conduct of village government; and creating a harmonious working relationship with the village government and other village institutions. Who sits on it, and how many, follows the village's own map. The same page records that members represent the village population on the basis of territorial representation, determined democratically, that the number of members takes into account the population and the village's financial capacity, and that the territories represented are the hamlets, neighbourhood associations and community units within the village. A seat allocated to a named hamlet is a seat a hamlet can fill. It has its own operating money and a stated right to give an opinion. Published material records that the operational cost of carrying out the body's tasks and functions comes from the village income and expenditure budget, and records its rights as including stating an opinion on the conduct of village government, the implementation of village development, community guidance and community empowerment. It records the body as convening the village assembly with participants including the village head, village apparatus, groups and community figures. Read this with the village forest management bodies, the customary territory register, the provincial legal aid offices and the deforestation data foundation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: District and city land offices — the counter that re-marks a boundary on request, the complaint form that opens a dispute file, the receipt that proves it, and mediation before any court
trackers.desc: A city land office publishes a service for re-marking a boundary, and the counter steps are listed. A public services register records a city land office's service for measurement of a land parcel for the restoration of boundaries, with the applicant instructed to come to the land office with a complete file and requirements, bringing a photocopy of the identity card and family card of the applicant and of any authorised representative; take a queue number and wait to be called by the relevant counter officer; and have the application file received and examined by the counter officer, with the office's street address, postcode and telephone published, and an online service noted. For a household whose boundary marker has gone, that is the exact counter and the exact document list. The office's stated jobs include dispute handling, not only registration. Published description of one city office records its main tasks as implementing technical policy in the land field, including land registration, determination of rights, data maintenance, measurement and mapping, and the resolution of land disputes; and records it as active in mediation and conflict resolution and as providing open land information services so the public can access data on the status and legality of land. District office service lists record measurement and mapping, transfer of title on sale, gift, inheritance or exchange, mediation and facilitation of land conflict settlement, online file status checking, downloadable application forms and a complaints channel. The complaint route produces a document a claimant should keep. Published legal commentary records that after initial consultation a claimant fills in the land dispute complaint form provided by the land office, covering the identities of the parties, the location of the disputed land, the chronology of the dispute and the demands made, and that on submission the officer verifies the documents and issues a receipt as proof that the report has been received, which can be used to follow up. It records the office as holding a complete database of land ownership history, including historical documents the disputing parties may not have. Published guidance records that where mediation succeeds, the result is set out in a peace deed that can be registered with the court so it has binding legal force. Read this with the village consultative bodies, the village forest management bodies, the customary territory register and the provincial legal aid offices entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Musrenbang — the annual village planning forum held by the fourth week of January, its four required forms, the sub-district delegates who escort a proposal upward, and the indicative budget ceiling announced at it
trackers.desc: The village planning forum has a deadline and a paper trail. A village's own guidance records that the village planning forum is held every year, at the latest in the fourth week of January, and lists the administrative outputs that must be produced and reported to the sub-district as the minutes of the deliberation, a priority problems list form, a priority activities form and a proposed activities list form, each numbered. It records the preparation stage as beginning with formation of an organising team of three to five people appointed by decision of the village head, responsible for the whole process from preparation through implementation to follow-up. A dated deadline and four named forms is what turns attendance into a claim on next year's budget. The money available is announced at the meeting. Published description records that at the forum the village head presents an evaluation of the previous year's village work plan, and the sub-district head or a representative conveys the indicative budget ceiling for the village and for the sub-district area, together with sectoral development from the district or province to be carried out in the village that year. It records the outputs as an inventory of priority activities to be financed from the village allocation fund and the village fund, and an inventory of problems falling to the district or province, to be proposed for financing through the district or provincial budget. The sub-district stage chooses people to escort the proposal. Published description records the sub-district forum as convened to discuss, agree and verify proposed activities from villages that are priorities for the sub-district area; align community proposals with regional development policy; set priorities not covered at village level; and choose sub-district representatives to escort the proposals to the sectoral agency forum and the district planning forum. Other description records the chain as running from village or urban ward, to sub-district, to district or city, to province, to national level, and records the sectoral agency forum as strategically important because it brings together sectoral and spatial community groups. Read this with the village consultative body, the village fund, the village forest management bodies and the spatial conformity document entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Village-owned enterprises — a legal body the village creates by assembly decision and village regulation, capitalised from separated village wealth and from residents' own capital, to manage assets and natural resources
trackers.desc: A village can create its own enterprise, and the decision is taken at the village assembly. A district community empowerment office records the 2014 village legislation as providing that a village may establish a village-owned enterprise; that it is managed in a spirit of kinship and mutual cooperation; and that it may run businesses in the economic field or in public services; and that its establishment is agreed through the village assembly and set out in a village regulation. It records the implementing regulation defining it as a business entity whose capital is wholly or largely owned by the village through direct participation from separated village wealth, in order to manage assets, service provision and other businesses for the greatest welfare of the village community. A body a village creates by its own regulation, to hold assets, is the vehicle this brief keeps asking about. The capital can include the residents' own money. A finance ministry office records the enterprise as a legal entity established by a village or jointly by villages to manage businesses, make use of assets, develop investment and productivity, provide services and provide other business types; records village capital participation as the separation of village wealth from the village budget to become the enterprise's capital; and records the capital as consisting of village capital participation, capital participation by the village community, and a share of profits determined in the village assembly to add to capital. Separating the enterprise from the village government is treated as the safeguard. A district record notes management as democratic and technocratic, with democracy visible not only in the village assembly component but also in accountability, and records that separation of both the organisation and the assets of the enterprise from the village government is an important component for maintaining accountability. It records formation conditions as the initiative of the village government or the community based on a village assembly; existing community economic potential; conformity with community needs; and available village resources not yet optimally used, especially village wealth. Read this with the village consultative body, the village fund, the village forest management bodies and the planning forum entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Gugatan Warga Negara — the citizen lawsuit route (Jakarta)
trackers.desc: THE MECHANISM RESIDENTS HAVE ACTUALLY USED: a gugatan warga negara (citizen law suit) lets residents sue their own government. An alliance of capital residents brought one in 2019 over Jakarta's air pollution at the Central Jakarta District Court — case 374/Pdt.G/LH/2019/PN.Jkt.Pst. This ICEL compendium of selected environmental judgments sets it out alongside criminal judgments and, more useful for a land fight, hak uji materil (judicial review) rulings that struck at regulations themselves, including Putusan No. 77 P/HUM/2019 and Putusan No. 29 P/HUM/2019 against a provincial governor's regulation. USE THAT: judicial review of a subordinate regulation is the tool when the spatial-planning rule itself was written for the developer. BE REALISTIC ABOUT TIME: LBH Jakarta's advocacy team has publicly criticised how slowly the Jakarta air pollution citizen lawsuit moved through the Central Jakarta District Court compared with similar cases elsewhere. The route exists and has been used — it is not fast.

trackers.name: Syariah Court of Singapore
trackers.desc: Syariah Court of Singapore — tribunal (Singapore).

trackers.name: ACRA
trackers.desc: Singapore's accounting and corporate regulatory authority; company registry. Here you can trace companies, their directors and filings registered in Singapore.

trackers.name: Singapore ACRA (company register)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); Singapore ACRA (company register) — the official register of companies and legal entities in Singapore — the primary public record of corporate existence, ownership, directors and filings. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A BENEFICIAL-OWNERSHIP REGISTER: this shows the registered entity, its directors and filings; where a separate beneficial-ownership register exists, use that to reach the real humans behind a shell company.

trackers.name: ACRA BizFile
trackers.desc: Singapore's official company register — free searches of company profiles and officers. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: GeBIZ
trackers.desc: Singapore's central government e-procurement portal for public-sector tenders and awards. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Singapore, and for how much.

trackers.name: Singapore Courts – Judgments
trackers.desc: Official Supreme Court and State Courts judgments and case summaries. · Find here: judgments and grounds of decision of the Singapore courts.

trackers.name: Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC)
trackers.desc: Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) — Singapore’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Singapore Department of Statistics
trackers.desc: Singapore's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Singapore.

trackers.name: ACRA Register
trackers.desc: Electronic register of legal entities and public accountants.

trackers.name: Parks and Trees Act — and check what the designation covers underground
trackers.desc: READ THIS BEFORE ASSUMING A DESIGNATION SETTLES ANYTHING. Nature reserve protection runs through the Parks and Trees Act 2005, successor to the Nature Reserves Ordinance (1951), the Nature Reserves Act (1985) and the National Parks Act (1990). An NUS Asia-Pacific Centre for Environmental Law working paper examines the PTA's nature reserve provisions specifically so they may be given their intended effect — and frames the problem as relentless pressure and improving capability to develop subterranean space, noting Singapore has ‘left no stone unturned, and now look set to leave no granite undrilled either’. UNDERGROUND DEVELOPMENT BENEATH A PROTECTED SURFACE IS A LIVE QUESTION HERE: establish what your site's designation covers vertically, not just its boundary on a map. BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE ROUTE — Singapore has no community forest mechanism, no land trust tradition, no NGO standing regime and no land-defence grant fund; the decisive channel is evidence plus direct engagement, not litigation.

trackers.name: Chek Jawa, Dover, Kranji — what has actually changed decisions
trackers.desc: THE METHODS WITH A TRACK RECORD. CHEK JAWA IS THE PRECEDENT: in December 2001 individuals campaigning to save it were invited to a closed-door meeting at the National Development Ministry, where the minister announced the site would not be reclaimed; in January 2002 two new nature reserves at Labrador Park and Sungei Buloh were gazetted. That is the shape of a win here — technical evidence and direct engagement, with the decision announced rather than litigated. CITIZEN EVIDENCE THAT WORKED: a secondary school teacher documented older and endangered species in Dover Forest by measuring the girth of tree trunks and examining droppings on the forest floor — girth is a cheap, defensible proxy for tree age that anyone can gather; and Global Forest Watch satellite monitoring let citizens track land-use change and surface unreported developments, which is how the clearing of Kranji woodland came to light. THE STRATEGIC SHIFT: an area once needed endangered species present before conservation could be argued, and authorities could dismiss a society as having a limited following — but they cannot brush aside a sympathetic general public. Broad support is now the lever where species rarity used to be the only one. ALIGN WITH A PUBLISHED PLAN: the Singapore Terrestrial Conservation Plan names sites to elevate to Nature Park status and to restore — a site campaign is stronger inside it than alone — and the Friends of Sungei Buloh model shows a standing volunteer body is the recognised way to stay attached to a site.

trackers.name: Nature Society (Singapore) — the seat already at the agency table
trackers.desc: Singapore offers no third-party objection route against a land-use decision, so the practical question is who is already in the room — and that is the NSS Conservation Committee, which states that it regularly takes part in engagements with the Housing and Development Board, JTC, the Land Transport Authority and the Public Utilities Board, and with private developers such as Mandai Wildlife Group, to press for the retention of corridors and refugia. Where a development raises greater concerns it prepares a position paper documenting those concerns and its recommendations. Its published record is both the evidence that it engages at project level and the model to copy: a proposal on the Brookvale Park Road project, feedback on HDB's Tengah baseline review, feedback on the HDB Dover–Ulu Pandan forest baseline study, a position paper on the Cross Island Line, a position paper on the Mandai development plan, and the Kranji Marsh work. Its Marine Conservation Group separately reviews environmental impact assessments and responds on foreshore development. The single most useful thing to hand them is data, and to hand it over early. The Committee's stated functions are to identify and propose conservation of important terrestrial and marine areas, to give authorities feedback on land-use plans and policies, and to run the biodiversity surveys that underpin those proposals — so a documented species record from your site is worth more than a letter of objection, and worth most before an agency commissions its own baseline study. Set expectations honestly. This is a volunteer-run membership society working through consultation rather than litigation, and it argues for retention and mitigation within a development at least as often as against the development itself. Use www.nss.org.sg: the same pages are also served from preview. and mobile. subdomains, which are not the canonical host.

trackers.name: Singapore Heritage Society — the other submission-writer, and what a Singapore campaign actually wins
trackers.desc: Singapore has two organisations that write formal submissions on development, and this is the other one. Founded in 1987 as an independent non-profit, the Society works on rediscovering forgotten histories, sustaining living heritage such as the Pulau Ubin island community, cultural authenticity in districts such as Chinatown, and conservation of built heritage, particularly modern architecture from the 1920s to the 1970s. A threatened building, burial ground or historic landscape belongs here, where a forest belongs with the Nature Society. As a general principle it opposes the destruction of heritage, and holds that any decision affecting heritage must take account of the relevant stakeholders and of all possible conservation alternatives. Bukit Brown is the case to read before planning a Singapore campaign, including its ending. On 12 September 2011 the Land Transport Authority, the Urban Redevelopment Authority and the National Parks Board announced a dual four-lane road through a cemetery of roughly 100,000 graves, the largest Chinese cemetery outside China, with construction to begin in the first quarter of 2013. The Society published a position paper on 5 February 2012, still hosted on its own site, arguing for consultation that started from whether the road was needed at all and putting a heritage park as the alternative. The road went ahead. What the campaign obtained was a year-long documentation project funded at $250,000 and a bridged segment of the highway sparing part of the site, and the Society's own page records that the impact on physical and cultural heritage and on ecology remained, in its words, not properly addressed. Expect mitigation and a permanent record rather than a cancellation, and say so to your own people early. The lever that did travel was the international listing. Campaigners nominated the site and it entered the 2014 World Monuments Watch, the first Singapore site to do so, putting the decision in front of an audience the state does mind about. That is the same move the Maldives entry records against UNESCO's biosphere framework: where no domestic objection route exists, an international list the government has signed up to is the one that does. The Society publishes its position papers and the newspaper reference databases compiled behind them, and both are the model to copy.

trackers.name: URA Master Plan — Singapore's leverage point is the five-yearly plan, not the individual application
trackers.desc: Singapore gives an objector very little against a specific development, and a great deal against the designation that permits it. The Master Plan is the statutory land use plan under the Planning Act, guiding development over the next ten to fifteen years, reviewed every five years, and showing the permissible use and density for every parcel. Development that departs from it needs planning permission; development consistent with it is very hard to resist. The five-yearly draft goes on public exhibition before it is gazetted, and that is the window. The 2025 plan was exhibited from November 2024 and gazetted on 1 December 2025, with the authority collecting views through surveys, workshops and guided exhibition tours during the exhibition period; the 2019 plan was gazetted in November 2019. Between full revisions the authority issues amendments for particular plots or zones, so a parcel can be rezoned outside the cycle and that is worth watching for. Reported analysis puts the number of parcels whose designation changed between the 2019 and 2025 plans at 1,243. Read the Written Statement, not only the map. The map shows which zone a parcel sits in; the Written Statement is the legislative document defining each zoning category and the development control standards that apply to it. An argument about what a zone permits is an argument about the Written Statement, and citing the map alone will not carry it. Check the parcel before anything else. The authority's online space portal shows the land use zone, gross plot ratio and development control conditions for any address across the fifty-five planning areas, free and immediately. Establishing what the plan already permits on the ground you are worried about is the first five minutes of any Singapore campaign — and where the permitted use is itself the problem, the remedy is the next plan review rather than the next application. Pair this with the Nature Society and the Heritage Society, which are the two bodies that write submissions into these processes.

trackers.name: Legal Aid Bureau — advice without a merits test, and a provisional grant when proceedings are already running
trackers.desc: Advice is much easier to obtain than representation, and most people never learn that. For legal advice the bureau applies only a preliminary means test — no merits test and no statement taking — with an appointment made through the ministry's portal to see the duty lawyer. For representation in court both the means test and the merits test must be passed. A community that wants a professional read on where it stands, before deciding whether to litigate at all, is asking for the cheaper of the two things. If proceedings have already started, say so immediately. In urgent cases, for example where court proceedings are running, the bureau may represent an applicant under a provisional grant of aid before the merits test has been passed, continued or renewed until the board decides the case. Applicants are told to inform the bureau if proceedings have been commenced by them or against them, or if the matter needs urgent attention. Without that, a fairly straightforward application usually takes around four months from statement taking to a decision. Three limits decide whether this is available at all. The scheme covers civil matters and not criminal proceedings; it is for citizens and permanent residents of limited means; and the Director may refuse aid even where both tests are passed if it appears unreasonable in the circumstances of the case, including where a third party's interest is involved — which is worth weighing where several neighbours are affected by the same development. Check that the proceeding intended falls within the Act's scope before relying on the scheme. Disclosure is a legal duty with a penalty attached. An applicant must make full and frank disclosure of means and must tell the Director of any change in them; knowingly making a false statement or failing to disclose is an offence carrying a fine of up to five thousand dollars or imprisonment of up to six months or both. Cases are taken by the bureau's in-house lawyers and by private solicitors assigned to them, and a discretionary route exists for applicants who narrowly fail the means test in defined circumstances.

trackers.name: SAC-SINGLAS accreditation — a laboratory is accredited for specific tests only, which is the thing to check
trackers.desc: Accreditation here means assessed technical competence, judged by peers. The national accreditation council administers the laboratory accreditation scheme, which assesses and recognises the technical competence and the management processes of a laboratory and its staff. Assessment works on a peer basis, with technical experts drawn from industry, government bodies and tertiary institutions examining laboratories in their own fields of testing and calibration. The scheme is voluntary and open to all laboratories, and those accredited include commercial firms, research bodies, manufacturers and government departments, with the accreditation recognised across scores of economies. The scope is the point, and it is where most people go wrong. Accreditation is granted only for specific tests and calibrations in specific fields, and a laboratory may issue accredited reports only for the tests and calibrations it is accredited for. So a laboratory saying that it is accredited has not answered the question. Ask which tests fall inside its scope, check that the parameters you need are among them, and require that the report covering those parameters be issued as an accredited report. The environmental parameters a community needs are inside the scheme. The council's programmes reach testing for water, waste and energy management, chemical and biological testing such as verifying the purity of treated water, air and soil testing, and toxicity studies. A community that needs a discharge, a well or a soil sample examined is not looking for an exotic service. Ask for the measurement uncertainty, because the requirement is published. The council publishes its accreditation process, its checklist against the international testing standard, requirements on the traceability of measurement, policies on proficiency testing, and guidance on evaluating and expressing measurement uncertainty. Requesting the uncertainty alongside the figure is therefore asking for something the scheme already requires, and it is what stops a borderline reading being argued in whichever direction suits. Read this with the other measurement entries recorded in this file.

trackers.name: SG Eco Fund — a year-round small grant and an annual large one, with two traps in the terms
trackers.desc: Two doors, with very different burdens. The ministry's fifty million dollar fund, launched in November 2020, supports ground-up projects that involve the community and advance environmental sustainability, including climate change mitigation, waste reduction and the conservation of nature and biodiversity, and it takes applications from individuals, teams and organisations. The smaller category is open all year round, was introduced to shorten and simplify the process, and asks for a pitch deck with a short presentation to an evaluation committee if shortlisted. The main category opens annually from 1 May to 31 August, runs to a maximum of a million dollars and requires a written proposal. A community can use the year-round route to fund a first piece of work while preparing for the annual round. What the fund means by community is stated, not implied. Its published answers record that a company's employees are not considered part of the community; that a project need not be new, but an applicant must explain the need and show what additional environmental benefit a repeat would bring; and that reasonable profit is permitted where it supports the project's continued operation. Read those answers before writing, because they define the thing being funded. Two traps sit in the terms. An applicant may not receive funding from more than one government grant scheme for the same project, though non-government funding is allowed and must be declared in the form — so taking one government grant can foreclose another. And the grant recipient and the fund's board of trustees co-own all intellectual property arising from the project, which matters where the project is a survey, a dataset or a map that a community may later want to use in an objection or a case. Mechanics and scale. Applications close at 23:59 on the stated deadline and cannot be amended once submitted; individuals and teams log in with the national digital identity and organisations with the corporate equivalent; the secretariat may, but need not, contact applicants for clarification. The fund reports having awarded around thirteen million dollars to over three hundred individuals and organisations since launch, so the typical award is small and the number of recipients large.

trackers.name: Reporting to NEA — an app that routes to the right agency, and a warning that you may be the witness
trackers.desc: You do not have to know which agency is responsible. The national municipal feedback application routes a report to the relevant town council or agency, working across ten government agencies and seventeen town councils, and states in terms that the person reporting need not indicate which body is responsible. The environment agency's own feedback form performs the same triage in reverse: construction site noise stays with the agency, renovation noise inside public housing goes to the housing board, animal matters to the parks board, food matters to the food agency. For a community that has been passed between offices, that routing is the practical value. Construction and industrial noise is regulated against published limits. The agency regulates noise from construction sites and industrial operations against permissible noise limits and sets vehicle noise emission standards, and feedback on construction noise can be given on a toll-free line or through the agency's environment application. Contractors must apply for permits to carry out quieter categories of work on specified Sundays and public holidays, so what is permitted on a given day is a matter of record that can be checked before a complaint is made. The agency says what evidence it needs, and warns you may have to testify. For a littering offence committed from a vehicle it asks for full particulars, a contact number, the date, time, location and vehicle number, and photographic or video evidence clear enough to identify the vehicle — and states plainly that the person reporting may be required to assist officers in further investigations and, if the case proceeds to trial, to appear as a witness. No other reporting channel recorded in this file tells the reporter that in advance, and it is the sentence a community should read before deciding who signs the report. There is a documentary trail on the other side. The agency's portal receives environmental impact assessment reports and pre-consultation traffic noise impact assessments, and an environmental impact study is required where a new residential or noise-sensitive development is built close to an existing nuisance-causing development, or the reverse. Disputes with a neighbour rather than an operator run through grassroots leaders, then the community mediation centre, then the tribunal. Read this with the master plan and environmental fund entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: INLIS land titles search — the registered owner from an address, and the pending instruments it will not show
trackers.desc: The registered owner can be found from the address. The land authority states that the particulars of the registered owner of a private property can be obtained through the property ownership information service on its integrated land information portal, searchable by property address among other keys. The same portal sells survey plans and, drawing on three other agencies, road line plans, railway protection plans, borehole information and utilities information — so the ownership question and the infrastructure question can be answered in one place. No subscription fee is required, and fees are paid by card or bank debit. What it does not show is stated plainly, and it matters more than what it does. The authority notes that this product does not include information on instruments pending registration which may affect ownership. A dealing already lodged but not yet registered is therefore invisible here — the same gap that Hong Kong fills with a published list of unposted instruments, disclosed in Singapore as a limitation rather than closed by a service. Where the answer has to be current, ask the registry directly rather than relying on the search alone. Check the address against the lot number before you search. The registry's records run on survey district and lot numbers; property addresses are not maintained by the registry but have been incorporated for reference, and the authority cautions users to confirm that the address and the lot number correlate before proceeding, and to search the plans filed with the survey division to obtain the lot and survey district number where they do not. Two systems, and a route into the deep history. Land here sits under either the deeds register or the titles register. For unregistered land a lot particulars search comes first, and where the transactions registered are not enough for a fifteen year title search, a lot history printout traces the subdivision and amalgamation of the lot with the land book and caveat book references. Where records are not available online a manual search at the registry remains available. Read this with the reporting and routing entry and the environmental fund entry already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Bizfile — entity, people and industry searches, and what the free tier shows
trackers.desc: Four searches, and two of them are unusual. The regulator's register offers four public search functions: entity, people, industry and reserved names. The industry search finds live businesses by their business activity — the authority's own example is finding all the active cafes in the country — and the people search follows individuals rather than companies. Nothing else recorded in this sweep offers either. For a community trying to map who actually operates a particular kind of works in its area, an activity search is a different instrument from looking up one name at a time. Existence and status cost nothing; the officers cost a little. The entity search takes a name or the unique entity number, including a previous number, with keyword match types for containing, starting with and exact match, and advanced filters for entity type and status. Published guidance records that the free result shows the entity name, the identifier, the current status and the registered address, while the directors, shareholders and filing history sit behind a modestly priced business profile. Establishing that a company exists and is live is therefore free, and the deeper question is cheap rather than closed. The intermediary is checkable too. Where an entity is a registered corporate service provider, its registration details appear at the bottom of its own entity profile, and the advanced filters include a corporate service provider number. The firm that incorporated or administers a company can therefore be looked up in the same register as the company itself. Carry the unique entity number. It is the single identifier the entity uses across government, it stays with the entity for its life, and searching on it removes the ambiguity that similar company names create. Bulk datasets are published separately through the national open data portal for anyone doing wider research. Read this with the master plan, the land titles search and the reporting entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: GeBIZ and the awarded contracts dataset — who won, for how much, and who else bid
trackers.desc: One portal carries the public sector's tenders and quotations. The government's electronic procurement portal is where the public sector's invitations to quote and invitations to tender are posted, apart from security-sensitive contracts, with the tender documentation downloadable and bids submitted through the same system. Agencies also publish their annual procurement opportunities each year, which is a forward plan of what is going to be bought rather than a record of what already has been. The award result names the winner and the other respondents. The portal's own guidance on viewing awarded results describes finding out who a business opportunity was awarded to and who the other respondents were. For a community, that answers both halves of the question: who is doing the work, and who else was in the field. The awarded contracts are published as open data, without a login. The national open data portal carries a government procurement dataset drawn from the system, covering the tender number, the procuring agency, the awarded supplier, the awarded amount and the award date, refreshed on a rolling basis and reachable without an account or a key. That makes the record searchable in bulk — by supplier across years, or by agency across a category — which no other procurement record in this sweep allows. Ask for the sole-source notice where nothing was advertised. Alongside quotations and tenders the portal publishes period contracts, which are framework agreements for recurring needs, and sole-source notices, where a supplier is approached without open competition. Where a project has appeared with no tender having been advertised, the sole-source notice is the document to look for. Read this with the master plan, the land titles search, the business registry searches and the reporting entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: CPIB — the court must black out your name, and a government contract raises the stakes
trackers.desc: The court itself must conceal the informer's identity. Under the protection of informers provision of the corruption act, complaints of an offence are not admissible in evidence in any civil or criminal proceeding, no witness is obliged or permitted to disclose the name or address of an informer or to state anything that might lead to their discovery, and where books or documents in evidence contain an entry naming or describing an informer the court must have those passages concealed from view or obliterated so far as is necessary. Across this file confidentiality is usually an agency's promise; here it is a duty placed on the court. The exception is stated as plainly: where the court finds the informer wilfully made a material statement they knew to be false, or where justice cannot otherwise be done between the parties, disclosure may be required. A government contract raises the penalty and shifts the burden. Where a corrupt transaction is proved to relate to a contract or a proposal for a contract with the government, the penalties are substantially higher, and gratification given to or received by a person in the employment of the government or a public body is presumed corrupt, with the burden of rebutting that presumption resting on them. For a community objecting to a contract rather than to a private arrangement, the presumption is the provision that matters. What an actionable report contains. The bureau publishes what it needs: where, when and how the alleged corrupt act happened, who was involved and what their roles were, what was given and what favour was shown in return, with identities, amounts, dates, times, places and the mode of the transaction. It also states that a complaint which is too vague may not be capable of being acted on. This is the clearest published specification in this file of what a corruption report has to contain to be usable. Anonymous reports are looked into, and the clock is short. The bureau states that it looks into all corruption reports including anonymous ones, that an electronic report takes minutes to complete and is processed within ten working days, and that knowingly giving false or misleading information is itself an offence. Where an investigation shows no criminal offence but a breach of service conduct rules, the officer is referred to their own department for disciplinary action. Read this with the master plan, the land titles search, the business registry and the procurement entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Auditor-General's Office — checks that arise from complaints, and the follow-the-dollar audit
trackers.desc: A complaint can start a check. The auditor-general's published report records that, alongside its planned audits, the office carried out checks arising from matters that came to its attention through observations from past audits, through feedback, and through complaints. Among the audit bodies recorded in this file, few say plainly that outside complaints feed the audit programme; here it is stated in the report itself, which makes a letter to the office a documented input rather than a hopeful one. Selective audits look for irregularity, excess, extravagance and gross inefficiency. Beyond the annual financial statement audits, the office conducts selective audits — checks on selected areas for financial irregularity, excess, extravagance or gross inefficiency — on statutory boards in rotation, choosing them by factors such as the materiality of the public funds they manage, and aiming to audit the larger boards at least once every five to seven years. Naming the statutory board behind a project, and the scale of the funds it handles, is therefore how a request to the office should be framed. The follow-the-dollar audit traces money out of government. The auditor-general may conduct an audit tracing public monies beyond government agencies to the non-government bodies which receive them, where the finance minister directs it, and the minister may direct it only if satisfied that doing so is in the public interest. Where a grant or a subsidy leaves the state for a company or an organisation running a project, there is a named instrument that follows it out. The report goes to the president and parliament, and lapses get called in. The report is presented to parliament, where the public accounts committee deliberates on it and may call public sector entities to account for lapses; the observations selected for the report are those indicating malfeasance, lapses with significant financial impact, or systemic or common lapses that would seriously weaken financial governance if uncorrected, and agencies have filed police reports where possible irregularities were found. Read this with the corrupt practices bureau, the master plan, the land titles search and the business registry entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Pro Bono SG — guidance clinics, and a non-litigation service for organisations including property matters
trackers.desc: There is a service aimed at organisations, not only individuals. The legal guidance pages record support for non-profit organisations seeking legal guidance on non-litigation matters, and list property law — lease terms are the example given — among the fields covered, with a dedicated address for enquiries. A residents' committee, a registered society or a community group with a lease, a tenancy, a licence or a constitutional question therefore has a free route to a lawyer. That matters because almost every legal clinic recorded elsewhere in this file is built for individuals with personal problems, and a community group is neither. For individuals: register first, then the appointment is arranged. Free basic legal guidance is offered to people who have never sought legal advice or cannot afford a lawyer, by video conference or at named physical clinics with fixed evening hours in several parts of the island, and the organisation states plainly that there may be a one to two week wait, so alternative dates should be held in mind. Plan around that rather than arriving in the week a deadline falls. It publishes the list of the other clinics, with their rules. Its compilation of legal clinics notes that most are dedicated to personal legal matters only, that some require documents to be submitted in advance when booking, that identification and supporting documents should be brought, and that appointments should be made ahead. Knowing which clinic takes which kind of matter is what saves a wasted trip and a lost week. The limits are stated by the clinics themselves. Guidance at these sessions is basic guidance and not a substitute for legal advice or legal action; volunteer lawyers are bound not to act further for those they see at a free clinic; sessions are short; and business, corporate and investment matters are outside scope. Representation, where it is available, is a separate service subject to assessment. Read this with the legal aid bureau, the master plan, the land titles search and the accreditation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Appraiser's licence and the surveyors' institute — only licensed appraisers may value land, and every licence expires in December
trackers.desc: Valuing land here requires a licence. The revenue authority states plainly that anyone who appraises lands and buildings in the country must apply for an appraiser's licence. The first check on any valuation put in front of a household is therefore whether the person who signed it holds one, and that is a narrower and more answerable question than whether they are qualified or experienced. Every licence expires on the thirty-first of December, whenever it was granted. The published conditions record that all appraisers' licences expire on 31 December of each calendar year regardless of when the licence was approved, with renewal to be made by 21 December. A valuation signed early in a year by someone who did not renew is therefore a document worth questioning, and the check costs nothing but a date comparison. Institute membership is a precondition, and the entry route is documented. An applicant for the licence must be a member or fellow of the surveyors and valuers institute — probationer membership has not been sufficient since the start of 2014 — and must provide a testimonial from a licensed appraiser verifying that the applicant can perform appraiser work independently, supported by three valuation reports carried out under that appraiser's supervision; self-employed applicants must additionally be up to date on their statutory medical savings contributions before an application is processed. That chain of conditions is what a licence actually represents, and it is worth knowing when weighing one report against another. Compensation is a named service of the profession. The institute's own description of valuation services covers all types of land and buildings — commercial, industrial, residential, recreational and special use — for letting, purchase, sale, investment, mortgage, insurance, taxation and compensation. A household facing acquisition is therefore asking for work the profession already does at a market rate, not for a favour, and asking several firms produces a fee comparison as well as a value. Read this with the land titles search, the master plan, the free legal guidance and the audit entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Environmental studies — published reports, a roughly month-long window, and proximity to a sensitive area as the trigger
trackers.desc: Proximity to a sensitive area is the trigger. The planning authority's own account records that proposed development projects near sensitive areas — nature reserves, nature areas, marine and coastal areas, other areas of significant biodiversity, or projects with potential trans-boundary impact — are subject to greater scrutiny, with the technical agencies for parks, environment, ports and food consulted more extensively to determine whether a more thorough environmental study is required. The first question about any project is therefore whether the site falls near one of those categories, and where the agencies answer that it does not, that answer is itself the thing to contest, with the categories quoted back. The reports are published, and feedback is invited. Environmental study reports are stated to be publicly available online unless there are specific reasons to maintain confidentiality, such as security considerations; the studies are carried out by independent environmental consultants and reviewed by the technical agencies and the planning authority; and the findings are considered in consultation with community stakeholders, including the extent of potential impact and the adequacy of the proposed mitigation measures. Reported practice is release on the authority's website with a feedback window of roughly a month — one recent case ran from the tenth of July to the sixth of August 2026, with a heritage impact assessment published alongside the environmental ones. Mitigation and monitoring are where a submission bites. The agencies expressly weigh the adequacy of proposed mitigation measures, and the housing authority records that an environmental management and monitoring plan may be developed for each site to manage potential impact. A submission that answers the mitigation chapter and the monitoring plan engages the framework on its own terms, where one that argues only about the loss of the site does not. The known weaknesses, stated plainly. There is no standalone assessment statute; published commentary records that the mode of engagement remains at the authorities' discretion, that a select group from the nature community is typically consulted before reports are released publicly, and that the reports are highly technical enough to defeat an untrained reader. The environment agency centrally manages assessment consultancy processes for private developers and has issued biodiversity impact assessment guidelines. Get the report on the day it appears, split the reading between people, and answer the mitigation chapter. Read this with the master plan, the nature society, the heritage society and the laboratory accreditation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: National monument preservation — open spaces now qualify, a notice of intention is published, and an enforcement notice can stop work
trackers.desc: Open spaces and inland waters can now be preserved, not only buildings. The preservation legislation originally allowed the preservation of buildings and structures and of sites containing the remains of one. Amendments expanded the definition of monument to include any site, including open spaces and inland waters, so that a place of national significance with no structure on it can be preserved — the change that allowed a well-known open recreation ground to be gazetted. A field, a green, a padang or a stretch of water is therefore now within the statute's reach, which is not true of most heritage regimes recorded in this file. Anyone may make submissions at any time, and intentions are published. Ministerial statements in the legislature record that when a site or building is being considered a notice of intention is filed and published, so that members of the public know in advance that something is proposed for gazetting; and that this does not stop anyone with an interest from making submissions or giving feedback to the heritage board at any time, which has happened. The practical instruction is to write before there is a notice, and to write again once there is one. A proposed monument already carries protection. Reported practice records that proposed monuments receive the same legal protections as gazetted ones, with penalties for alterations that compromise historical character; and the amended Act allows the board to serve an enforcement notice to stop any operation or activity where it makes the professional assessment that the activity places a monument at risk of being destroyed, removed, damaged or altered. That notice is the thing to ask for when machinery is already on site. Objections are considered, and the decision is a preservation order. The preservation of sites and monuments division assesses an identified site and recommends to government whether it should be preserved; the minister then decides whether to issue a preservation order placing it under the Act's protection, which is published in the government gazette. In a case gazetted in December 2025 the minister acted on the advisory board's assessment and the heritage board's recommendation, and the published decision expressly recorded that a written objection from an interested party had been taken into consideration. Both sides are read, and both are recorded. Read this with the master plan, the environmental studies feedback window, the nature society and the heritage society entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Land acquisition compensation — the inquiry where you file your claim, and the assessors you may object to
trackers.desc: The inquiry is where a claim is filed, and it has a date on the notice. Acquisition is governed by the land acquisition legislation and administered by the land authority, which states that owners whose land is acquired are paid market value compensation. Its published account of the process records that owners receive a notice giving the particulars of the property to be acquired and the date of the collector's inquiry; that at the inquiry the collector obtains the information needed to assess compensation and owners may submit their own claims; that the collector's award is the document stating the sum awarded; that payment is made when the collector takes possession; and that an owner dissatisfied with the award may lodge an appeal with the appeals board. The inquiry, not the appeal, is the first place a valuation of your own can be put on the record. What the board may consider, and what it may not. The appeals board publishes the statutory list of matters it takes into consideration in determining compensation, and the provision states that it shall consider those matters and no others. Market value is deemed not to exceed the price a bona fide purchaser might reasonably be willing to pay after taking into account the zoning and density requirements and any other restrictions imposed under the planning legislation as at the date of acquisition, and any restrictive covenants in the title; and no account is taken of any potential value for a use more intensive than the planning rules then permitted. The date of acquisition is the date the declaration notification is published. Anyone arguing value on the basis of what the land could become is arguing something the board is not permitted to weigh. You may object to the assessors. The appeals board regulations provide that where the board sits with two assessors, the commissioner selects them from a panel at least fourteen days before the hearing, the registrar supplies them with the available information about the appeal, and the parties may object to either or both assessors within seven days after receiving the notice of hearing and apply for their substitution, which the commissioner may allow if sufficient grounds are shown. Conflict of interest, apparent bias or lack of relevant expertise are the grounds that clause exists for, and the seven days runs from the notice. The board can go and look, including at comparable land. The regulations also allow the board to enter and inspect the land in the proceedings and, where practicable, comparable land, on notice, with the collector and the appellant able to be present. A community that has identified genuinely comparable transactions can therefore ask for them to be seen rather than merely cited. Read this with the master plan, the appraiser's licence and surveyors' institute, the land titles search and the legal aid entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Garden City Fund — the charity money route into conservation on state green space, with a 2.5 times tax deduction
trackers.desc: Where land cannot be bought, this is the money route. Almost all green space here is state land, so the acquisition question a community faces elsewhere becomes a funding question: how to put money and effort into protecting a specific habitat that is not yours. The parks board established a registered charity with institution of a public character status, managed independently as a charity, to take donations from individuals and organisations for conservation, research, outreach and education. Its stated purposes are the development of amenities and features in green spaces, community activities and programmes covering nature and ecology, landscape and horticulture, animal and greenery management, animal health and welfare and conservation, and citizen involvement in the care of those spaces. The deduction is two and a half times the donation. Donations qualify for a tax deduction of two and a half times the amount given, with a valid identity or business registration number, and the details are filed with the revenue authority so the deduction appears automatically in the following year's assessment. For a group approaching a company to fund work on a threatened site, that multiplier is the argument that makes the ask concrete. Named programmes you can direct money to. Published programme pages record donations directed to coral reef research and restoration, marine turtle protection and species recovery, the seed bank preserving regional plant species against climate change and urban development, and the botanic gardens; and a tree-planting programme under which a donation of three hundred dollars plants a tree in a parks-board-managed green space, with general donations pooled and planted the following year and private plantings of fifty or more trees arranged directly. Corporate donations recorded in the annual report have funded conservation and education at a marine park and scaled up coral restoration. Directing a donation to a named programme, rather than to general funds, is what ties the money to a place. What it is not. This is not a body that buys land or holds it in trust; it channels money into work on land the state already manages. A community whose site is privately owned needs the master plan and heritage routes recorded elsewhere in this country's entries; a community whose site is public green space can use this to fund the survey, the restoration or the planting that makes the case for keeping it. Read this with the eco fund's grants, the master plan review window, the heritage society and the national monument preservation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Jom — a subscriber-funded weekly that runs essays taking months, in a media landscape where long-form is rare
trackers.desc: A reader-funded magazine that publishes on a fixed weekly rhythm. Founded in 2022, Jom describes itself as a weekly digital magazine covering arts, culture, politics, business and technology in Singapore, independent and with no affiliation to any party, corporate interest or organisation, run by three co-founders. Every Friday it publishes three pieces: a free newsletter, a paid weekly update giving its view of the week's most important stories, and a paid essay. The essays, it states, take months to research, write and edit. For a community whose case only makes sense at length — a land use decision, a heritage loss, a displaced trade — the existence of a slot that is designed for months of work is the thing worth knowing. Its funding model is the independence claim, and it says so. The magazine's own account of why it exists is blunt about the landscape: mainstream outlets have decent editorial standards and regular coverage but lack political and corporate independence, and non-mainstream outlets have more independence but are not set up for consistent long-form work. Its answer is a reader-funded subscription model, chosen expressly to secure editorial independence. A community weighing where to take a story can read that reasoning and judge it, which is more than most outlets offer. What it is not. It is a general-interest magazine, not an environmental or investigative newsroom, and it publishes weekly rather than on breaking developments. A hearing date next week is not what this outlet is for; the pattern behind a decade of decisions is. Pitching accordingly — the long arc, the documents, the people who lived it — is the difference between a piece it can take and one it cannot. Use it alongside the official windows. The master plan review, the heritage nomination route and the national monument preservation entries recorded for this country are where a case is formally made; coverage is what makes those windows matter to anyone outside them. Read this with those entries and with the heritage society and eco fund entries already recorded here.

trackers.name: Fund-raising permits — the police licence, the charity exemption, the seven-day disclosure and the unmanned-box carve-out
trackers.desc: Whether you need a police licence depends on who benefits, not on what you are raising for. House to house and street collections remain licensed by the police, except where the collection is by or for a registered or exempt charity, or is a foreign-purposes appeal by a person approved by the charities commissioner. So a public appeal for a charitable cause that is not for the benefit of a registered or exempt charity still needs the police licence — which is exactly the position of an unincorporated residents' group raising for itself. Applicants must represent a registered business, company, society or organisation, the purpose must be charitable, and the application asks for supporting approvals including consent from the manager or owner of the premises where the appeal is held. The unmanned box carve-out is the one to know. The police state that the legislation does not apply to collections made using unmanned collection boxes, so no licence is required under the relevant section where nobody uses face-to-face means to actively encourage donations at the box. A staffed table needs a licence; a sealed box left with a willing shopkeeper does not — while the charities legislation still applies. Charities file a disclosure instead, seven working days ahead. Since October 2023 registered and exempt charities and valid foreign-purposes permit holders are exempt from the police licence but must submit details of each public appeal through the charity portal at least seven working days before it starts: the purpose, duration and method of collection, the locations, and a contact number and email for public queries. That disclosure is also how a donor checks a collector, alongside the portal's permit search. Foreign causes need a permit, thirty days ahead. Anyone conducting or participating in an appeal for foreign charitable purposes needs a permit from the commissioner regardless of whether the appeal is public or private, online or offline, applied for at least thirty days before it begins, with proof that the beneficiary is a bona fide organisation in its own country, a letter from that beneficiary acknowledging the appeal in its name, and its governing instrument. Accounts of the appeal must be audited by a public accountant where more than ten thousand dollars is raised, and the amount transmitted abroad and the recipient must be recorded. Two rules that shape the budget. Published guidance records that charities must keep the ratio of fund-raising expenses below thirty per cent, and that a person under sixteen may not act as a collector without the commissioner's permission, with the charity and any third-party fundraiser jointly responsible for briefing collectors. Read this with the master plan window, the legal aid bureau, the pro bono hub and the judgments entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Tree conservation areas and the Heritage Tree scheme — one metre of girth needs written approval, five metres and anyone can nominate
trackers.desc: Inside a tree conservation area, felling a mature tree needs written approval even with no development going on. The parks agency records that developers and private property owners wishing to fell any mature tree with a girth exceeding one metre must seek written approval from the Commissioner of Parks and Recreation, even if no developmental works are currently in progress. Published dataset material records that two areas in the south central and eastern parts of the country were gazetted as tree conservation areas in August 1991 to control indiscriminate felling; that mature trees are defined as those with girth more than one metre measured half a metre from the ground; and that the requirement applies to developers and to owners of private property alike. The same approval requirement is recorded as applying to vacant land. Measure the girth before you argue about anything else. The applicant must show there was no alternative. Published guidance records that submission plans must clearly state the species, girth and height of existing trees, that a professional arborist's report may be required, and that a developer must show there are no alternative designs or technical solutions to retain the tree affected by the works; a non-development application by a house owner must state the reasons for felling and may need an arborist's report. Ask to see the alternatives analysis. Anyone can nominate a Heritage Tree. The scheme's own site records that anyone may nominate a tree, that the nominee should be more than five metres in girth or noted for botanical, historical, social, cultural or aesthetic significance, that nominated trees are inspected before consideration by a Heritage Tree Panel of varied expertise, and that an endorsed tree receives greater attention and care including a lightning protection system and special protection from construction impact during development works, sometimes with interpretive signage. A funded conservation programme supports that work. Nomination is a route a resident can start alone, before any application is filed. The statute names more than trees. The parks and trees legislation contains a part on conservation of trees and plants covering tree conservation areas, the prohibition on cutting or damaging a tree of more than one metre girth, tree conservation notices, heritage road green buffers and their maintenance, the prohibition on cutting trees or plants in such a buffer, applications for approval to cut, reinstatement notices and notices to plant or replant. Reported enforcement records a company fined and ordered to pay a substantial sum in compensation to the state for felling a rare tree in a conservation area. Read this with the master plan window, the environmental studies entry, the monument preservation entry and the acquisition compensation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Planning permission — provisional versus written permission, the two-year validity, the exemption list, and the status check anyone can run
trackers.desc: Work cannot lawfully begin until the final permission is in hand, and the two stages have different names. The planning authority records that planning permission is required for development and building works including changing the use of premises, that some proposals can be registered under plan lodgment for instant approval, and that an exemption list sets out works needing no permission; published guidance records that provisional permission is a conditional approval subject to conditions such as payment of the land betterment charge and submission of further documents, that written permission is granted only once those conditions are fulfilled, and that work cannot legally begin until written permission is in hand. Asking which of the two a developer holds is a sharper question than asking whether it has approval. The scope of development is broad, and a change of use counts. Guidance records that the legislation defines development to cover erecting new buildings, additions or extensions, and any material change in the use of land or buildings, so that converting a retail unit to a restaurant needs approval even with no structural work. Where a use has quietly changed next door, that is the provision to check. Permissions expire, and applications can be tracked. Published guidance records that written permission is valid for two years from issue and that permissions carry an expiry date which must be extended or renewed before it passes; and the authority provides an online status check for a submitted application. Diary the expiry date of a permission affecting your area, because a lapsed permission means a fresh application. Test-the-water applications are public-facing too. The authority records an outline application allowing a property owner, a prospective buyer with the owner's consent, or a developer to test a proposed land use, plot ratio or building height before making a formal application — used in particular where the proposed intensity or height is beyond approved control parameters or the proposal does not conform with intended master plan land uses, generally assessed in twenty working days. An outline application is therefore an early signal that someone intends to exceed the plan. It also records that an applicant who is not the owner must first obtain written consent from the owner or from the land authority where the premises are state-owned, and that the lot and survey numbers can be found through the land information service already recorded in this file. Read this with the master plan entry, the environmental studies entry, the land titles search and the monument preservation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Construction noise control — the no-work rule within 150 metres, noise meters the contractor must install at your building, and the limits that tighten at night
trackers.desc: The contractor has to put noise meters at the nearest affected buildings — which may be yours. The environment ministry records that the environment agency sets maximum permissible noise limits for construction sites to protect public health, taking reference from the world health body's guidelines and tailoring them locally; that limits are differentiated by time band with more stringent limits at night and on Sundays and public holidays; and that to measure the noise generated from their worksites, construction companies must install noise meters at the nearest affected buildings and monitor the levels regularly. Ask where the meters are and what they have recorded. The subsidiary regulations under the environmental protection legislation are the instrument, published in full on the statutes site. The no-work rule turns on distance, and 150 metres is the number. Published summaries of the rule record that for construction sites within 150 metres of residential premises and noise sensitive premises, no work is allowed from ten at night on a Saturday or the eve of a public holiday until seven in the morning of the following Monday or the day after the holiday. Measure the distance from the site to the nearest home or noise-sensitive building; inside that radius the weekend prohibition applies. Quieter work on Sundays needs a permit, and the conditions are public. A government information sheet records that since 2017 sites at the architectural or project completion stage may carry out quieter forms of work on specific Sundays and public holidays from a published list, that contractors must apply through the agency's portal for a permit to do so, and that the permit is subject to stringent conditions specified in the application form and any others the agency imposes. If work is happening on a Sunday, there is a permit to ask about — and a list that says what kinds of work it can cover. Limits are tiered by who is being protected. Published practitioner material records that the framework sets tiered limits by the sensitivity of the receiving premises and its distance from the site, with hospitals, schools and homes for the aged given the strictest protection, residential buildings within 150 metres next, and other buildings in a looser category; that limits tighten in the evening and overnight; and that compliance involves pre-construction baseline surveys and calibrated meters, with escalating fines and possible prosecution for exceedances. Read this with the reporting entry, the environmental studies entry, the planning permission entry and the master plan entries already recorded for this country.
