trackers.name: Earth Control Measures — silty discharge from a construction site is reportable to a 24-hour line, with CCTV on larger sites and prosecutions on record
trackers.desc: Silty water running off a construction site into a drain is a reportable offence, and the reporting line is published. The water agency records that the public can report sightings of silty discharge in drains and canals to its twenty-four hour call centre, giving the location and any photographs or videos; that financial penalties and stop work orders may be imposed on errant contractors; and that under the sewerage and drainage legislation offenders are liable to prosecution and may be fined up to a stated maximum. It records that the drainage network conveys rainwater to the country's freshwater reservoirs across thousands of kilometres of drains, canals and rivers, and that two-thirds of the country's land area is water catchment — which is why a muddy drain is treated as a water supply problem rather than an aesthetic one. Larger sites must watch themselves, and the threshold is published. The agency records that all construction sites of 0.2 hectares and above are required to install CCTV to monitor treated water discharge into public drains, with the feed analysed in real time and automatic alerts sent to the project manager and the site's control officer; that it encourages treatment systems with an auto-intervention feature stopping operations when discharge exceeds a stated limit of total suspended solids; and that inspection frequency is increased ahead of the monsoon. Ask whether the site next to you is above that size, and whether the camera is there. The plan exists before work starts, and it is approvable. Agency material records that before earthworks begin a contractor must engage a qualified erosion control professional to design the measures, obtain a clearance certificate from the agency and implement them on site, covering erosion control to minimise bare earth and sediment control to collect, store and treat silty water during rain; that the plan must be submitted for approval before construction commences; and that contractors must operate, maintain and monitor the measures and stop any silty discharge immediately on detection. That approved plan is a document to ask for. Enforcement is documented case by case. Reported prosecutions record a contractor fined after silty water was discharged into a public drain from its treatment machine for two hours, detected by an image-analytic silt detection system that had already alerted the contractor; and the agency has published lists of fined contractors alongside the requirements. Read this with the construction noise entry, the reporting entry, the environmental studies entry and the tree conservation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Marine park protection under the parks legislation — fishing, coral collection and mooring made offences without approval, and the jurisdiction gap that made the amendment necessary
trackers.desc: Adding a marine park to the parks legislation made three specific acts offences without approval. The parliamentary record of the 2017 amendment states that by adding a definition of marine park and adding it as a type of public park, the protection of the parks legislation is applied to the designated foreshore as well as the marine areas of the marine park — so that it is an offence to fish, collect corals or moor boats there without the parks board's approval; and that the amendment enables the board to make subsidiary rules regulating human activities in the marine park to keep it as a sanctuary for marine life, for example restricting diving and the dropping of anchors at ecologically sensitive locations. Those three acts are the ones a visitor can photograph and report. The jurisdiction gap it fixed is the useful part of the record. The same debate records that earlier notices had attempted to designate a wetland area by demarcating points in the sea and declaring them under the parks legislation, but that with no corresponding amendment to the Act, the board still had to send every reported misdemeanour beyond the high water mark to the maritime authority to enforce, and could not act itself against blatant misbehaviour in daylight inside the designated wetland — including the laying of fish nets. Where a marine or foreshore area is said to be protected, the question is therefore which Act covers it and which agency can act, not whether a notice exists. What the park covers, and what protection level applies. The record and published analysis state that the park covers about forty hectares around the named islands and the reefs off two others; that with the amendment offences in the marine park attract the same penalties as public parks, which are lower than for national parks and nature reserves; and that the Act allows designation of a national park or nature reserve for the purpose of protection and conservation of biodiversity in that area, which is the route by which a higher status could be sought. The parliamentary record also notes a civil-society plan listing many further islands and reefs of high marine biodiversity adjacent to the park. One general prohibition worth knowing alongside it. Published material on the 2020 wildlife legislation records that a person must not intentionally feed any wildlife in any place, or intentionally release any wildlife in any place, without the director-general's written approval, and must comply with the approval's conditions. Read this with the tree conservation entry, the earth control measures, the master plan window and the environmental studies entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Nature reserves and nature park networks — the four reserves conserved by statute, the buffer parks around them, and the offence of releasing animals into watercourses that flow in
trackers.desc: Four nature reserves are conserved under the parks legislation, and the largest doubles as the water catchment. The parks agency records that the country's four nature reserves are conserved under the parks and trees legislation, are primary providers of ecosystem services helping clean air and water, and hold native flora and fauna including rare and endangered species; that the largest covers some three thousand hectares, with over two thousand hectares of forest cover including scattered patches of primary lowland dipterocarp forest and the last remaining primary freshwater swamp forest; and that it serves as the catchment for four named reservoirs located within it. Where a project sits near a reserve, that catchment function is a second argument alongside the biodiversity one. The nature park networks are the buffers, and they are named. The agency records nature park networks that buffer the reserves and support ecological connectivity — one network buffering a wetland reserve with extensions east, west and south, plus named marshes and a mangrove and mudflat, strengthening wetland biodiversity conservation in that part of the island; and another of over two hundred hectares developed from the ecological profile of the area with input from a scientific advisory panel of academics and domain experts from the nature community. Asking which network or nature area a site falls in is how its status gets fixed. Penalties inside reserves are higher, and one offence reaches outside them. Published academic material records that the legislation introduced heritage road green buffers and enhanced penalties for offences committed in national parks, nature reserves and tree conservation areas. The parliamentary record of the amending Bill records that it became an offence to release or abandon animals into watercourses outside the nature reserves where the person knows or ought to know that those watercourses flow into the reserves, with signage at key watercourses; and that parks not managed by the agency, such as an independently run garden, were brought under the Act's protection with enforcement powers delegable to their staff. The gap that the same literature names. The academic guide records examples where nature reserves and nature areas were lost to development without any opportunity for public participation, and identifies wide discretion over land use without adequate transparency, and the absence of mandatory environmental impact assessment legislation, as deficiencies in an otherwise relatively comprehensive framework. Read this with the master plan entry, the environmental studies window, the tree conservation areas and the marine park entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The wetland reserve and its nature park network — gazettement under the parks legislation, a 400-hectare network built on ecological connectivity research, and enforcement teeth against poaching
trackers.desc: The decision to safeguard the buffer habitats was made on ecological connectivity research, and the agency says so. The parks agency records that a new nature park network was announced to extend natural capital along the northern coasts, and that the decision to safeguard buffer zones and complementary wetland habitats around the wetland reserve was determined through extensive research that established the ecological connectivity and complementarity between the sites; that the reserve and a named mangrove and mudflat park are important refuelling sites for migratory shorebirds along a named flyway; and that wetland habitats serve as a food source and nursery ground for marine organisms, store carbon and mitigate coastal erosion. Where a site is argued to be separate from a protected area, connectivity research is the counter-argument, and here it is the government's own. The network is more than triple the reserve, and its components are named. The agency records the network as covering over four hundred hectares, more than triple the size of the wetland reserve, comprising the reserve, other core habitats including the mangrove and mudflat and named marshes, nature parks, eco-corridors and named nature areas, safeguarding mangroves, mudflats and freshwater marshes; and records two hundred and seventy-nine bird species recorded in the reserve and surrounding complementary habitats. That count is the kind of figure an objection can cite. Gazettement is what changed the legal position. Published material records the site opened as a nature park in 1993, gazetted as a nature reserve under the parks and trees legislation on 1 January 2002 with full nature reserve status and enhanced legal protections, expanded to two hundred and two hectares in 2014, declared the country's first regional heritage park in 2003, and inducted into an international shorebird site network. Nature park status carries enforcement, not just a label. Reporting of the mangrove and mudflat designation records that the new status would allow the agency to better monitor and protect threatened species of mangrove, crustaceans and migratory shorebirds, and would give it teeth to enforce anti-poaching laws under the parks and trees legislation; and records the seventy-three hectare park as state land comprising a mangrove forest with sixteen threatened mangrove species and a mudflat, with radio-tracking confirming that shorebirds roosting in the reserve at high tide fly to feed on the mudflat at low tide — the interdependence that justified protecting both. Read this with the nature reserves entry, the marine park entry, the master plan window and the environmental studies entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The public consultation portal — every ministry's open consultations in one place, roughly four weeks each, with the summary of responses published afterwards
trackers.desc: Every ministry's consultations are posted in one place, and feedback goes straight to the agency. The government's citizen engagement department records that the public may let their views be heard by participating in the public consultations posted by ministries and government agencies, and that the feedback goes directly to the agencies concerned; its pages are organised year by year, with the archive reaching back well over a decade, and it also publishes the summary of responses for past consultations. Where a decision that will shape a project is still at policy stage, that is the one page to watch rather than each ministry's own site. The window is about four weeks, and the agency sets it. A ministry's parliamentary answer records that agencies decide the duration of their own consultations on the portal, but that it typically lasts four weeks, and that one hundred and twenty-six public consultations were hosted on the site over the past five years. That number is what a community should weigh against its own capacity: a consultation missed is not reopened. Individual agencies mirror the same practice, with closing times and published outcomes. Agency material records consultations launched on the portal with stated open and close dates — one on the country's decarbonisation journey, its climate ambition and transition measures, running about four weeks — and records another closing at a stated hour on a stated date, with the agency later publishing a report summarising the key feedback received during the consultation period and the draft instrument alongside. A regulator's own consultations page records inviting feedback on draft amendments before the closing date and publishing its official response to the public feedback received. Read this with the master plan window, the environmental studies window, the reporting entry and the nature society entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: OneMap and the open data portal — the national map with over a hundred thematic layers and a public API, and datasets published in mapping formats under an open licence
trackers.desc: The national map publishes its interfaces for members of the public, not only for agencies. The land authority's map documentation records the platform as the authoritative national map, and records that it publishes a variety of interfaces in a standard data format for government agencies, businesses, associations, third party developers, researchers and members of the public, providing authoritative, localised and granular map and map-related data, with registration required to use them. The authority's own page records the map as usable to obtain street-level geospatial information, or narrowed to specific queries such as land ownership, nearest schools and demographic data at or around a location. Land ownership at a point is the query that matters when a project's site boundary is unclear. More than a hundred thematic layers sit on it. The authority records the platform, launched in 2010, as built on open-source platforms, offering location information, navigation services and developer interfaces, and records it as used in over a hundred government and private applications, with more than a hundred and ten thematic layers. Published guidance records the interfaces as including search, reverse geocoding, coordinate conversion between the global and national systems, a themes interface listing query names and retrieving a theme, and demographic data at planning area and subzone level, with open-source client libraries published by the authority and by third parties. The open data portal carries the datasets in mapping formats, under a named licence. Published description records the government's open data portal as publishing datasets across planning boundaries, transport, environment and the economy, with geospatial datasets commonly offered in two named mapping formats and licensed under the national open data licence, free for reuse with attribution. A published guide records the portal carrying datasets at planning area and subzone level from different years, including households by income and size and resident population by planning area, dwelling type, age and ethnic group, joinable to geospatial layers through those same areas; records the current master plan datasets as superseding the previous ones, which remain available for historical comparison; and records the entire cadastral map as published by the land authority. Read this with the land titles search, the master plan window, the environmental studies entry and the acquisition compensation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The wider nature movement — the campaigns that got a reclamation deferred and a rail alignment reopened, the roundtable where groups and agencies meet, and the volunteer groups a resident can join
trackers.desc: Campaigns here have changed decisions, and the record names which ones. The national library's own account records the leading conservation organisation as having campaigned successfully for the preservation of many nature areas, including a named wetland reserve, a named shore and freshwater wetlands now managed as marshes, with origins reaching back to a natural history society formed in 1921. The organisation itself records being widely consulted by the government for numerous developments, naming a shore, a rail line, a forest town and a woodlands site. Published reflection by two participants records the shore campaign's success as coming from the groundswell of public opinion garnered through outreach programmes, where the public was totally convinced of the value of the habitat, with the internet instrumental in gathering that support. The reasons the campaign worked are set out by the people who ran it. The same reflection records the lessons: that younger volunteers who are conversant with the medium should be at the forefront; that there is still a need to be professional in conservation work, most volunteer conservationists being non-scientists who are passionate but not always well versed with the technicalities of the habitat and its associated flora and fauna; and that working closely with government agencies and academia is crucial. That is an assessment written from inside a campaign that won. A standing roundtable exists where groups and agencies meet. Published material records a biodiversity roundtable initiated by the parks agency, the university and a nature website, at which the parties meet a few times a year to update one another on conservation initiatives, exchange ideas and raise issues for discussion, and which started an annual public biodiversity festival; it records the origins of several groups traced to the year news broke that a shore was due for reclamation, the public protesting and the government eventually deferring it. The groups a resident can actually join are listed. A published list records a movement coordinating a month-long series of events over a proposed rail line through a nature reserve with a social media campaign, a marine conservation group that is a special interest group of the nature society, volunteer guiding groups running public walks on the shores, and museum volunteer programmes. Read this with the nature society entry, the heritage society, the environmental studies window and the nature reserves entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The natural history museum's reference collections — specimens catalogued with collection dates and locations, a herbarium of the region's plants, and a hundred thousand field notes and photographs
trackers.desc: The national reference collection is the record of what used to live where. The museum records itself as housing the national and reference collection of preserved zoological specimens and the university herbarium, used for comparative research on the country's and the region's flora and fauna, and describes the specimens as the preserved physical records of the region's biodiversity. Published description records the zoological collection as listing over 560,000 catalogued lots and over a million specimens in total, one of the largest of Southeast Asian animals in the region, and records the herbarium as established in 1955 and now documenting the region's botanical resources by preserving evidence of its surviving plant diversity, with published counts by group including flowering plants, ferns, mosses, liverworts and marine algae. Where an assessment claims a site holds nothing notable, dated specimen records from that place are the contradiction. The value for a community is the collection date and locality on each specimen. Published description records the collection as meticulously catalogued with collection dates and locations, providing an irreplaceable historical baseline used to track changes in species distribution and abundance over time and assess the impact of human activities, and notes that historical records can reveal whether a species once common is now gone. A separate collection holds the paperwork, not the animals. The museum records a biodiversity histories collection of over 100,000 non-specimen objects — field notes and journals, photographic slides and prints, and oral history materials — documenting the study of natural history in the country and region and providing context on how biodiversity knowledge has been produced, recorded and interpreted over time. Field notes name places and dates, which is what an old record needs to be usable. It records its researchers running expeditions and contributing to the natural sciences. Published description records the collections' origin in an 1849 museum collection, transferred by the government in 1972 to a university zoology department and later rehoused. Read this with the nature society, the wider nature movement, the environmental studies window and the nature reserves entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: ACRES — a wildlife rescue hotline with published hours and what to report, an animal crime investigation unit taking wildlife-crime reports by email, and the government line for the hours it no longer covers
trackers.desc: When clearance starts on a site, displaced animals need a number that answers, and this is it. The organisation records a wildlife rescue hotline as the first point of contact for an injured bird, a trapped snake or a displaced wild animal in urban areas, with calls answered by trained staff who assess the situation and dispatch a rescue team when needed, publishing the number and its hours of 7am to 1am daily. It records what a caller should have ready: the exact location or nearest landmark, the type of animal, its condition — injured, trapped, unconscious — and whether it is still present and visible, with photographs, video and a pinned location by messaging app if the line is busy. It advises describing size, colour and distinct markings and noting whether other animals are nearby. The organisation is candid about its own capacity, which matters when planning who to call. It records operating a single rescue van and a motorbike, with an average caseload of three per hour, so it may not always respond immediately and may ask the caller to transport a safely containable animal; it records having one full-time veterinarian and sometimes recommending the parks agency instead. Published reporting records the hotline ceasing to run around the clock due to a lack of funding and an increase in rescues, and records the organisation stating it received about 1,200 calls monthly against operating costs of about eighty thousand dollars a month at that time. Outside those hours, and for wildlife crime, it names the alternatives. It publishes the parks board's animal response centre number as a 24-hour alternative, and records an animal crime investigation unit taking reports of prohibited pet keeping, sale of wild animals or parts, and abuse, by a published email address, alongside a separate whistleblowing address about the organisation itself. It records itself registered as a society in 2001 and under the charities legislation as an institution of a public character, with both registration numbers published, and records that removing wild animals from their natural habitat is a criminal offence for most species here. Read this with the wildlife protection entries, the nature society, the pollution reporting line and the natural history collections entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The specialist species societies and the sector directory — a volunteer herpetological society that runs surveys and holds a student grant, and a published list of the country's nature and environment organisations
trackers.desc: Specialist volunteer societies exist for particular groups of animals, and they do survey work. A herpetological society records itself as a volunteer-run group of enthusiasts passionate about the conservation, appreciation and study of reptiles and amphibians in the country and the wider region, stating that it believes in ethics, rigour and outreach; and records that it regularly supports herpetofauna surveys and conducts research, inviting anyone working on reptiles and amphibians in the country and region to make contact. For a site where the species at issue is a frog or a snake, a specialist society is the body with the identification skill a general nature group may lack. Its members work alongside the state agency on species recovery. The parks agency records that, with assistance from members of the society, tadpoles of a frog species listed as vulnerable in the national red data book were introduced at two sites on a named island in June 2024 and March 2025, supported by artificial habitats, with adults translocated from mainland nature reserves in July 2025 and tadpoles and a clutch of eggs observed the following month, indicating breeding. That is documented volunteer participation in a recovery programme, not advocacy. The society also puts money into the next generation of surveyors. Its published notices record a student grant with an application deadline, and its site records guided walks at a named wetland reserve, member-produced identification posters, and members attending regional biodiversity workshops. A published directory lists the sector, which is how a community finds the right specialist. A green landscape directory describes named organisations one by one — including an all-volunteer eco-education non-profit advocating protection of natural heritage, a herpetological society, an urban farming pioneer, an international conservation body's local arm working through community engagement, environmental education and capacity development, and an environmental awareness society. A separate published list records an annual coastal cleanup conducted by more than 4,000 volunteers from some 60 schools, institutions, government bodies and private organisations, coordinated by museum volunteers, which collects data on debris and submits it to government and international organisations. Read this with the nature society, the wider nature movement, the natural history collections and the wildlife rescue entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Ecological restoration specialists a community can hire or work with — a firm doing mangrove propagule nurseries and shoreline restoration, and the university labs producing threatened-species planting stock
trackers.desc: There is a private firm whose ordinary business is restoring habitat, and its services are listed. A university lecture notice records the firm as established in 2007, operating at the intersection of biodiversity science, ecological design and landscape architecture, whose habitat enhancement and restoration work merges conservation with functional landscape planning across diverse ecosystems from freshwaters to degraded shorelines; and records its coastal restoration services as covering nursery propagation of mangrove propagules, shoreline protection, and restoration strategies grounded in coastal engineering and hydrological studies. It records the firm's plant specialist as a master horticulturalist who consults on development projects and co-authored a widely referenced guide to the country's garden plants, with experience in native plant restoration and habitat classification, and records its mangrove restoration work at named islands. For a community proposing restoration instead of clearance, a firm that can price and design it is what turns a demand into a proposal. The public planting stock for threatened species is produced in a university laboratory. Published material records a university plant systematics laboratory working with the parks agency to develop planting material from threatened species in the country, which are being tested for planting; records the agency's forest restoration programme as having planted over 17,000 trees since the 1990s in the nature reserves to help rehabilitate forest fragments and forest gaps; and records that most trees initially planted in the urban programme were non-native, with the agency having started diversifying the planting stock by including more native species, though often of foreign provenance. Provenance is the question to ask about any replanting offer. The volunteer route into the same work is documented. A university record describes students joining a mangrove rehabilitation project at a named island living laboratory, tagging, measuring and recording information for over 77 plants in the vegetation monitoring phase of a replanting project, data used in assessing the success of the habitat enhancement project. Read this with the natural history collections, the specialist societies, the wetland reserve and the tree conservation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Waterways Watch Society and the Friends of Ubin Network — volunteer patrols on the rivers with three park offices, and a standing network where villagers sit alongside nature and heritage groups
trackers.desc: Volunteers patrol the rivers here on a fixed schedule, and the society has offices inside the parks. The society records itself as a non-governmental and non-profit environmental organisation committed to foster appreciation and promote conservation of the environment, especially the waterways, established in 1998 with only 27 members and grown to about 700 volunteers, aged between 5 and 80. It records its main office within a named riverside park since 1999, under a named bridge, a first branch office opened in February 2014 at a waterway park under a named bridge to reach residents of a new town, and a second branch at a lake gardens in June 2019. It records starting with volunteers patrolling three named rivers by boat at weekends to fish out any litter they could find. A standing patrol on the water, with a base in the park, is the kind of presence that notices a discharge before anyone reports it. Its results and its funding are stated. The society publishes the kilograms of trash collected from a named reservoir during clean-up programmes and volunteer patrols across three financial years and the number of environmental awareness programmes conducted, and records that as a charity it relies primarily on the support of donors and sponsors to fund its work fighting pollution in the waters. Published material records a staff member overseeing corporate clean-up programmes and a schools programme. The island network is the model where villagers sit at the same table. The parks agency records a friends network as composed of individuals representing the different aspects of a named island, from its rich culture and heritage to its biodiversity, whose members are as varied as the groups they represent — nature groups, heritage groups, villagers, academics and passionate stakeholders, and records that since its formation in 2014 it has led and contributed to several ground-up initiatives, including a proposal for an educational and research centre on the island for heritage and biodiversity conservation and a reunion bringing together close to 140 current and former island residents and their families. A youth network profile records a biodiversity voices group aiming to empower youths to have a voice in the decision-making process for biodiversity locally and globally. Read this with the nature society, the specialist societies, the restoration specialists and the wildlife rescue entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The free legal clinic directory and the regulator's lawyer search — clinics listed by region with addresses, hours and eligibility, and a searchable database of every registered solicitor by practice area
trackers.desc: Every free legal clinic in the country is listed in one place, sorted by region. The directory groups clinics as central, east, north-east, north, west, online and various, plus Shariah and walk-in categories, with counts for each region, and gives for each clinic the address, the days and hours it runs, the eligibility rule and a telephone number. Its entries show how narrow the eligibility can be — Singaporean or permanent resident at some, income eligibility per the website at a university clinic, women residing in the country who pass a means test at another. A community group can therefore find the nearest clinic and know before travelling whether its members qualify. What a clinic session actually is, and is not, is published. Published material records community legal clinics accepting appointments from residents who need legal advice on personal matters, investment, business and professional matters not being applicable, open only to people who have never sought legal advice before and who are not represented by lawyers, offering a volunteer lawyer for 20 minutes on a strictly confidential basis; and records that the volunteer lawyers are bound by law not to act any further for the attendees of these free legal clinics, the guidance being basic guidance and comfort only. That limit is the reason to treat a clinic as a first step, not a representation route. Twenty-one clinics sit inside the local council structure. A district councils body records that a memorandum with the law society's pro bono arm established a community legal pro bono services network, under which 21 community legal clinics have been established at community development councils and community centres or residents' committees across five districts, with one telephone number and email for appointments across all of them. And the regulator publishes a searchable list of every registered lawyer. A published referral list records the legal services regulatory authority as maintaining a database of all solicitors and law practices registered with it, allowing the public to conduct a search by areas of practice and specialisations. Read this with the legal aid bureau entry, the pro bono guidance, the nature society and the planning objection entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Town councils and the municipal coordination office — seventeen estate-level bodies that control common property and keep their own accounts, and the reporting route that names which one is responsible
trackers.desc: Seventeen estate-level bodies control the common property residents live on, and their duties are published. A government explainer records 17 town councils managing common property in public housing estates, which control, manage, maintain and improve the common property of the residential and commercial properties within their towns, with common property including linkways, gardens, lifts, corridors and void decks. It records their work as covering routine repairs such as lift servicing, conservancy and cleaning, upgrading of facilities such as playgrounds, and cyclical maintenance like electrical re-wiring, and records them as responsible for the financial management of their towns, keeping proper accounts and records of transactions and ensuring proper financial control over payments, expenditure and assets. It states plainly that residents may approach their town councils and elected members of parliament on feedback regarding their estates. For a resident, the body that controls the ground outside the front door is this one, and it keeps accounts that can be asked about. A coordinating office exists precisely because responsibility is split. Published description records a municipal services office set up on 1 October 2014 to improve the government's overall coordination and delivery of municipal services, envisioned as a coordinating body bringing together government agencies, town councils and community partners, covering maintenance of greenery and local infrastructure such as roads and footpaths and the cleanliness of public areas, and partnering agencies to share and monitor complaints on municipal matters. The reporting route names the responsible body for you. Published material records an application that routes a report to the appropriate agency or town council to resolve the issue and provide timely responses, with reportable categories including facilities maintenance in housing estates, illegal parking, cleanliness, roads and footpaths, animals and birds, pests and smoking in prohibited places; records the office as partnering 17 town councils and 10 named government agencies, including the building authority, the housing board, the transport authority, the environment agency, the parks board, the water agency, the land authority and the planning authority; and records chatbot channels added for messaging platforms. Read this with the planning master plan, the environmental feedback channel, the legal clinic directory and the wildlife rescue entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The five district Community Development Councils — mayors and district offices with their own local assistance schemes, a per-resident government grant, and freedom to fundraise
trackers.desc: Five district councils sit between residents and the government, and they design their own schemes. A ministry records that the councils and mayors form a bridge between residents and the government and function not only as the hands and legs to implement programmes for the community, but also as the eyes and ears to identify emerging needs and gaps in social support, being nimble and close to the ground with the ability to aggregate local needs and resources, build capabilities in their partners, and connect communities together. It records that the councils have developed and administered over 100 local assistance schemes, forming about 40 per cent of all their programmes, tailored to meet the respective district's needs and priorities. A district body that writes its own schemes is a place a neighbourhood proposal can actually land. Their money comes partly per head, and partly from their own fundraising. Published description records the councils as receiving an annual government grant directly proportional to the number of residents within their district, calculated at a rate of one dollar per person, and as encouraged to conduct their own fundraising activities. Knowing the grant is per resident tells a community roughly what its district council has to work with. Their boundaries, leadership and size are published. Published description records five districts — central, north east, north west, south east and south west — established in 1997 as nine and consolidated into five in 2001; records each council as governed by a chairman designated as mayor of the district, with between 12 and 80 other members, in practice 17 to 25 seats; and records boundaries as formed by grouping electoral constituencies, fluid and subject to change with every general election, and not to be confused with town councils. It records one district as covering more than 551,000 residents and another as about 220,000 households with over 750,000 residents, with a high concentration of industrial estates. Each council publishes its own website and general manager. Read this with the town councils and municipal office, the legal clinic directory, the restoration specialists and the planning master plan entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The Community Mediation Centre and the neighbour tribunal — free mediation at 21 locations islandwide, a relations unit that chases a non-responding neighbour, and a tribunal that can order an apology
trackers.desc: Mediation is free, and it happens near where people live. The centre records itself as a centre under the law ministry offering mediation to residents facing relational and community disputes, with no cost for the service; records in-person mediation at 21 locations islandwide, with virtual mediation an option for less complex disputes; records a session as about two to four hours, available Mondays to Fridays and Saturday mornings; and records that matters discussed and the identity of the parties are kept confidential. Elsewhere it records its main premises with a street address and unit number, plus 18 satellite mediation locations. For a household in a noise, obstruction or drainage quarrel, a free session in its own town is the first move. What happens if the other side ignores the invitation is now answered. The centre records that for neighbour disputes, where the respondent declines or fails to respond to a mediation invitation, a resident can seek the assistance of a community relations unit on a stated hotline between 9am and 9pm on weekdays, and that in other towns an outcome letter is issued, after which a claim may be filed at the neighbour tribunal. A ministry records that a mediation direction framework and that unit are being expanded nationwide from a stated date. Knowing there is a body whose job is to chase a neighbour who will not come is what makes the voluntary route usable. The tribunal behind it has real orders and a low filing fee. Published legal description records that the tribunal hears claims between neighbours living in the same building or within 100 metres of each other; that the filing fee for a neighbour dispute claim is a stated small sum paid through the community justice and tribunals system; that lawyers are not allowed to appear unless every party agrees and the tribunal permits it, so most people run their own case; and that the tribunal can order damages, an injunction, specific performance, a written or spoken apology, and any ancillary order needed, with claims capped at a stated amount. It records that once a claim is filed, the registrar or tribunal judge can order the parties to attend mediation with or without their consent. Read this with the town councils, the district community development councils, the legal clinic directory and the restoration specialists entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The heritage society's position paper as a template — a document that asked whether the road was needed at all, its recommendations, and what the campaign around it actually won
trackers.desc: A position paper on one cemetery road is a usable template for opposing a road anywhere. The society's published paper is structured as a position on the road; a section on cost-benefit analysis, environmental impact assessment and transparency with best practices elsewhere; a section on genuine consultation, the reality of the consultation process, decisions made without consultation and the value of consultation; and recommendations. Its recommendations are to gazette the site as a heritage site, to fully document the cemetery, and to turn it into a heritage park. It records the site as the largest Chinese cemetery outside China, with approximately 100,000 graves, a remarkable historical space even in international terms. Naming an alternative — documentation plus a park — rather than only objecting is the move this file keeps recording as effective. The paper's central question is the one most campaigns forget to ask. Published material records the society arguing that a consultation should take as a starting point the fundamental question of whether a road through the cemetery is needed in the first place, and records its stated stance that while it understands the need to provide public housing and relieve traffic congestion, it does not believe enough effort has been invested in the search for a solution. It records the society as open to working with all interested parties to document the heritage of the cemetery as well as to discuss innovative ways to preserve it in situ, and as opposing destruction of heritage as a general principle, with decisions requiring due consideration of the relevant stakeholders and all possible conservation alternatives. What the campaign won is recorded, and it was partial. Published research records that amid growing public debate the government made two small concessions: allocating funds for a year-long documentation project and planning a bridge segment as part of the highway to preserve some of the site's biodiversity; and records that, dissatisfied, activists nominated the site for world heritage status and got it onto a 2014 international monuments watch list, while development plans for the site remained. Read this with the heritage society, the nature society, the national monument preservation and the planning permission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Citizens' Consultative Committees — the constituency-level grassroots body that recommends amenities and facilities, administers two welfare funds at the community club, and can refer a rejected application onward
trackers.desc: One of these committees' stated functions is recommending what gets built in the constituency. Published description records the committees, under the statutory community association, as the umbrella bodies of all grassroots organisations, with functions to promote good citizenship; disseminate information and relay public feedback on government policies and actions; direct and carry out projects and activities at constituency and national level; and make recommendations on the provision of amenities and facilities in the constituency. The association records them as the apex grassroots organisations, which plan and lead major grassroots activities within the constituency, oversee local assistance programmes, and organise major fund-raising projects. A body whose written job includes recommending amenities is a body worth putting a proposal to. Two welfare funds are applied for at the community club. A ministry records that the committees help administer a community development and welfare fund and a community care fund; that a committee appointed by the consultative committee manages and oversees disbursement of the first, whose applicants must be residents of the constituency or division the committee serves and citizens or permanent residents; and that the second offers interim assistance to residents needing urgent and temporary financial relief, granted up to three months per application at a stated monthly cap. It records that residents can apply for both at the community centres or clubs, and that where an application does not meet the criteria, the committee may seek help elsewhere, with longer-term needs referred to the ministry's social service offices. The scale, and the criticism, are both on record. A published speech records 1,800 grassroots organisations and almost 40,000 grassroots leaders. Published description records a parliamentary criticism that town councils historically had to seek community improvement project funding through these committees, typically chaired by advisers affiliated with the governing party — a practice reformed in 2021 — and records a national audit report having flagged lapses in governance. Read this with the town councils, the district community development councils, the community mediation centre and the fund-raising permits entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: URCDP — Unidad Reguladora y de Control de Datos Personales
trackers.desc: URCDP — Unidad Reguladora y de Control de Datos Personales — Uruguay’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Unidad de Acceso a la Informacion Publica (UAIP, Uruguay)
trackers.desc: Unidad de Acceso a la Informacion Publica (UAIP, Uruguay) — oversight body for the right of access to public information.

trackers.name: Qué Sabés — FOI requests (URY)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); Qué Sabés — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: CAinfo (Centro de Archivo y Acceso a la Información Pública)
trackers.desc: Uruguayan civil-society organisation promoting the right of access to public information and transparency. Publishes the Active Transparency Online Index (ITAeL) assessing public bodies' compliance, and monitors press freedom and freedom of expression.

trackers.name: Vida Silvestre Uruguay — Refugios de vida silvestre
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a civil association founded in 1995 running the Refugios de vida silvestre programme since 2011 — a national network of voluntary private reserves, which matters in Uruguay because almost all the natural grassland, native woodland, wetland, sierra and coast sits on private land outside the state protected-area system. Refugios now protect over 500 plant, 300 invertebrate and 362 vertebrate species, many of them in no SNAP area at all. USE IT: if you own or work rural land in Uruguay and want it recognised and mapped as a refugio; the programme has its own sign-up route and works with landowners who keep farming.

trackers.name: REDES — Amigos de la Tierra Uruguay
trackers.desc: Founded in 1988 and the Friends of the Earth member group in Uruguay, working alongside the social movements affected by a project rather than for them. What it supplies is capacity and evidence: participatory research run jointly with faculties of the Universidad de la República, training and institutional strengthening for affected movements, and — through its Programa Uruguay Sustentable with the Comisión Nacional en Defensa del Agua y la Vida — a territorial GIS information system built for water-basin campaigning. It has fought the Neptuno-Arazatí water project, arguing the contract breached the Escazú Agreement on access to information and participation, and offshore hydrocarbon prospecting. WHO IT SUITS: organised groups already in a fight who need research, mapping and national coordination. It campaigns and researches; it does not litigate.

trackers.name: Tribunal de Cuentas de la República
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Uruguay's external audit body (supreme audit institution), created by the 1934 Constitution and governed by Section XIII, the TOCAF and articles 210, 211 and 212. Under article 211 literal B it intervenes preventively in state spending and payments — before the money moves — solely to certify legality, recording observaciones where it finds a problem, so an objection to a public works contract or land purchase lands at the approval stage rather than afterwards. KNOW THE LIMIT: it was given no jurisdictional or sanctioning powers and acts administratively — it observes, reports and denounces, it does not decide or punish. USE THE ESCALATION: where an ordenador reiterates a spend the Tribunal has observed and the Tribunal maintains the observation, it can have the matter flagged de urgente consideración when communicated to the General Assembly or the relevant Junta Departamental — which puts a contested departmental contract in front of the elected body that can act. Its resolutions are published and searchable, naming the contracting authority and the procurement, including intendencias. Contact: Juan Carlos Gómez 1324, 11100 Montevideo, 2916 1032/36, tribunal@tcr.gub.uy.

trackers.name: Base de Jurisprudencia Nacional
trackers.desc: Official free database of Uruguayan court decisions (Supreme Court from 1989; appellate and lower courts more recently), no registration required. · Find here: Uruguay's National Jurisprudence Database of court rulings.

trackers.name: Compras Estatales (ARCE)
trackers.desc: Uruguay's state procurement agency and tender portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Uruguay, and for how much.

trackers.name: Dirección General de Registros
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Instituto Nacional de Estadística
trackers.desc: Uruguay's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Uruguay.

trackers.name: Fondo Uruguay Socioambiental — funds rights defence, not just conservation
trackers.desc: A FUND WHOSE OBJECT IS THE THING THIS MAP IS FOR. Its stated purpose is strengthening the defence of socio-environmental rights in Uruguay through financial and technical support to community groups and civil society initiatives. Note both halves of that framing: it says grupos comunitarios, not registered NGOs — so an unincorporated neighbourhood group is within the intended audience — and it says defence of rights, not conservation projects. Most funders in this map finance conservation activity and are uneasy about advocacy; naming rights defence as the object is unusual and worth using in how you frame an application. Technical support is offered alongside the money, which matters for a group applying for the first time.

trackers.name: Vigilancia Ambiental — a citizen platform wired into the ministry
trackers.desc: CIVIL SOCIETY ASKED TO BE PLUGGED INTO THE STATE, AND WAS — a model worth copying elsewhere. The Red Uruguaya de ONG Ambientalistas, an asociación civil de segundo grado grouping environmental organisations and professionals, built Plataforma de Vigilancia Ambiental, where any person can file an environmental report and georeference it, developed with support from AGESIC, the digital government agency. IT POINTS BOTH WAYS: the Ministry of Environment's own complaints service page links out to the Red's citizen monitoring platform, and the platform provides access back to the ministry's complaints system. The Red reports interconnection with several departmental intendencias including Salto, Soriano, Colonia and Rocha. Under an open government commitment, a single national environmental complaints system was to integrate the state's Sistema Único de Respuesta with Vigilancia Ambiental — and interconnection with the civil society reporting system was added at the express request of the Red. The commitment states the aim that civil society play a fundamental role in oversight and enforcement of environmental regulation. ALSO: Denuncias Ambientales UY, an app built by COENDU, carries reporting tools to report breaches to the police and to the ministry.

trackers.name: Mapeo de la Sociedad Civil — find the group already working on your place
trackers.desc: A CATEGORISED DIRECTORY OF URUGUAYAN ORGANISATIONS, including conservación ambiental and organisations of promoción de derechos e incidencia — the fastest way to find whether someone is already working on your site, and to find co-applicants for the funds that require partnership. WHAT THE LISTINGS SHOW IS ITSELF USEFUL: the entries include a balneario neighbours' association formed around a single beach with the slogan ‘recuperemos nuestra playa’, an interdisciplinary group of biologists, geographers, sociologists, writers and naturalists working on one sierra range, and a group focused on a triple-border area. Small single-place groups are the norm here, not the exception — worth knowing if you are wondering whether your own group is too small or too local to count as an organisation.

trackers.name: Uruguay's basin commissions and regional water councils - civil society holds seven of twenty-one seats by decree, four reserved for delegates from the basin commissions, which may issue opinions on their own initiative
trackers.desc: CIVIL SOCIETY HOLDS A THIRD OF THE SEATS ON THE REGIONAL WATER COUNCILS BY DECREE — SEVEN DELEGATES OF TWENTY-ONE. The three regional water resources councils ARE INTEGRATED IN A TRIPARTITE AND EQUITABLE MANNER WITH 7 DELEGATES OF GOVERNMENT, 7 DELEGATES OF THE USERS AND 7 DELEGATES OF CIVIL SOCIETY, TOTALLING 21 DELEGATES PER REGIONAL COUNCIL; of the civil society seats THREE SHALL BELONG TO SOCIAL OR NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS WITH NATIONAL REPRESENTATION AND THE REMAINING FOUR SHALL COME FROM THE EXISTING BASIN COMMISSIONS; delegates MUST HAVE INTEREST AND/OR ACTIVITY IN THE THEMATIC OF WATER RESOURCES and are proposed by TECHNICAL OR TEACHING INSTITUTIONS, NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS and WORKERS' UNIONS, the ministry choosing them SO AS TO ASSURE THE HIGHEST POSSIBLE DEGREE OF REPRESENTATIVITY. Four of the seven civil society seats are reserved for people who come up through the basin commissions. Join the commission for your own basin and the regional seat is the next step, not a separate campaign. WHAT THE BASIN COMMISSIONS ARE FOR: they exist TO GIVE SUSTAINABILITY TO THE LOCAL MANAGEMENT OF THE NATURAL RESOURCES AND TO ADMINISTER THE POTENTIAL CONFLICTS OVER THEIR USE, and their competences include collaborating in the basin water resources plan, LINKING THE EXECUTIVE POWER WITH THE ACTORS INVOLVED, advising the regional council and the ministry IN THE LOCAL MANAGEMENT OF THE NATURAL RESOURCES, PROPITIATING THE STRENGTHENING AND EFFECTIVE EXERCISE OF THE RIGHT OF CITIZEN PARTICIPATION, and ISSUING AN OPINION ON ITS OWN INITIATIVE OR AT THE REQUEST OF THE AUTHORITY. Issuing an opinion on its own initiative is the power to use. A basin commission can put a written view on a project onto the record without waiting to be consulted. WHICH COMMISSIONS EXIST AND HOW ONE IS CREATED: commissions have been operating for a named aquifer, a stream, two lagoons and several rivers, and each regional council RESOLVES THE CONFORMATION OF THE BASIN COMMISSIONS ON THE BASIS OF THE NEEDS AND EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST IN THE TERRITORY; the regional council DEFINES THE DEFINITIVE INTEGRATION of each commission, and commissions are made up of the water directorate, local representatives of national and departmental government, users and ORGANISED CIVIL SOCIETY. Expressions of interest from the territory are what create a commission. If your basin has none, a letter from local organisations to the regional council is the recorded starting point. THE ROUTE UPWARD WHEN A DISPUTE CANNOT BE SETTLED LOCALLY: the regional council is competent to UNDERSTAND MATTERS RAISED TO IT BY THE BASIN OR AQUIFER COMMISSIONS, PROPOSING MECHANISMS OF SOLUTION OF CONTROVERSIES LINKED TO THE USE OR EXPLOITATION OF WATER RESOURCES, and it formulates the regional water resources plan. A conflict over water use has a named forum above the commission that must propose a solution. Raise it formally through the commission so that it arrives as a council matter rather than a complaint. THE CONSTITUTIONAL BACKING WORTH CITING: the participation of users and civil society in planning, management and control of water resources was written into the constitution by popular initiative plebiscite, and the basin is the UNIT OF ACTION FOR THE PLANNING, CONTROL AND MANAGEMENT OF THE WATER RESOURCES; a national advisory commission on water and sanitation is likewise tripartite. Participation here rests on a constitutional article approved by referendum. That is a stronger footing than a ministerial policy, and it is worth quoting in the first letter.

trackers.name: Uruguay's 125 municipios and their national plenary - five elected members for any locality above 2,000 people, a multiparty body of nine mayors training municipal officials, and a constitutional congress of intendants that can sign interdepartmental service agreements
trackers.desc: ANY LOCALITY OF MORE THAN TWO THOUSAND PEOPLE IS ENTITLED TO ITS OWN ELECTED MUNICIPAL COUNCIL. The constitutional rule is that THERE WILL BE A LOCAL AUTHORITY THAT WILL BE CALLED MUNICIPIO, CONFIGURING A THIRD LEVEL OF GOVERNMENT AND ADMINISTRATION, that EVERY POPULATION OF MORE THAN TWO THOUSAND INHABITANTS WILL CONSTITUTE A MUNICIPIO, and that its territory MUST FORM A UNIT, WITH SOCIAL AND CULTURAL PERSONALITY, WITH COMMON INTERESTS THAT JUSTIFY THE EXISTENCE OF REPRESENTATIVE POLITICAL STRUCTURES AND THAT FACILITATE CITIZEN PARTICIPATION. There are now 125 MUNICIPIOS, each governed by a council of five directly elected members, 125 MAYORS AND 500 COUNCILLORS alongside nineteen intendants and five hundred and eighty-nine departmental board members. Five elected people for a town of two thousand. Where your locality has no municipio, the population threshold is the argument for creating one — and departmental governments have created dozens since 2013. THE NATIONAL BODY OF THE MAYORS: a plenary of municipios was created within the intendants' congress, representing THE 125 MUNICIPIOS OF THE COUNTRY and represented by A MULTIPARTY EXECUTIVE TABLE MADE UP OF NINE MAYORS ELECTED IN PLENARY, produced by an inter-party agreement TO ORIGINATE A SPACE THAT WOULD REPRESENT THE GENERAL INTERESTS OF ALL THE MUNICIPIOS; it runs WORKSHOPS OF STRENGTHENING OF COMPETENCES FOR OFFICIALS OF DEPARTMENTAL AND MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENTS. A multiparty body of nine mayors that trains municipal officials. Where one mayor alone will not move, this is the room where the other hundred and twenty-four sit. THE DEPARTMENTAL CONGRESS ABOVE IT: the constitution provides for a congress of intendants WITH THE PURPOSE OF COORDINATING THE POLICIES OF THE DEPARTMENTAL GOVERNMENTS, which MAY ALSO CELEBRATE THE AGREEMENTS by which departmental governments arrange THE ORGANISATION AND PROVISION OF SERVICES AND ACTIVITIES PROPER OR COMMON, BOTH IN THEIR RESPECTIVE TERRITORIES AND IN A REGIONAL OR INTERDEPARTMENTAL FORM, and which WILL COMMUNICATE DIRECTLY WITH THE POWERS OF THE GOVERNMENT. Departments may agree to run a service regionally, and the congress can sign that agreement. For a river or a coast crossing two departments, that is the instrument to ask for. THE HONEST LIMITS ON THE THIRD TIER: the municipal organs ARE TOTALLY SUBORDINATED TO THE DEPARTMENTAL ONES: ALL THEIR ACTS, GENERAL OR PARTICULAR, MAY BE APPEALED BEFORE THE INTENDANTS, SO THEY CANNOT RESOLVE ABSOLUTELY ANYTHING WITH DEFINITIVE CHARACTER; municipios DO NOT HAVE JURIDICAL PERSONALITY, WHICH LIMITS THEIR ACTION; THE CREATION OF THE MUNICIPIOS DEPENDS ON THE WILL OF THE DEPARTMENTAL GOVERNMENTS; and NEITHER MAYORS NOR COUNCILS HAVE THEIR OWN RESOURCES: THE FUNDS COME FROM DEPARTMENTAL ALLOCATIONS AND FROM THE FUND OF INCENTIVE TO MUNICIPAL MANAGEMENT, WHICH IS DISTRIBUTED FROM THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT. Analysts note a recorded tension between the second and third tiers. A municipal decision can be appealed to the intendant, so a favourable vote in your municipio is a step rather than an outcome. Get the same position adopted by the departmental board, and ask about the national incentive fund, which is the money the municipio actually has.

trackers.name: FLACMA - the Latin American federation of cities and municipal associations, open to affiliation by ANY INDIVIDUAL MUNICIPALITY, whose assembly passes resolutions signed by mayors across eighteen countries
trackers.desc: ANY CITY OR MUNICIPALITY IN THE REGION MAY AFFILIATE DIRECTLY, NOT ONLY THROUGH ITS NATIONAL ASSOCIATION. Its membership rule is that MEMBERS ARE ALL THE CITIES, MUNICIPALITIES, NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND MUNICIPALIST INSTITUTIONS OF LATIN AMERICA THAT HAVE EXPRESSED THEIR WILL TO AFFILIATE; it is AN ORGANISATION OF FREE ADHESION THAT REPRESENTS THE 16,132 MUNICIPALITIES, INTENDANCIES AND PREFECTURES, THE CITIES AND THE ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, NETWORKS AND GUILDS OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, and it is the regional section of the world organisation of local governments. A single municipality may join in its own right. Where your national association is captured or inactive, that is a way for one sympathetic town hall to reach the regional table on its own. WHOSE PRESIDENTS SIT ON IT: its published leadership is drawn from the presidents of the national municipal bodies of the region — the federation of municipalities of one southern country, the association of municipalities of another, the Brazilian association of municipalities, the congress of intendants of another, the national federation of municipalities of one large federal country and the association of municipalities of an Andean one — each of them a serving mayor. The people who chair your own national municipal association sit here. A matter raised through that association can be carried into a regional assembly by the same person. WHAT IT SAYS IT IS FOR: TO BE THE VOICE OF LATIN AMERICAN MUNICIPALISM, TO CONSOLIDATE THE LATIN AMERICAN MUNICIPAL ASSOCIATIVE MOVEMENT, TO REPRESENT AND SERVE AS INTERLOCUTOR OF ALL THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND THEIR NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES, and TO PROMOTE IN LATIN AMERICA AUTONOMOUS, STRONG AND DEMOCRATIC LOCAL GOVERNMENTS; it ADHERES TO AND PROMOTES THE WORLD AND REGIONAL CONVENTIONS THAT THE NATIONAL STATES OF THE REGION SUBSCRIBE. Promoting the conventions the states have signed is written into its purpose. Where your country has signed an environmental or rights convention and a municipality is being told to ignore it, that is a body with a standing commitment to the opposite. THE PRECEDENT THAT SHOWS IT TAKES POSITIONS: its general assembly has approved unanimously a declaration on a territorial sovereignty dispute, signed by the president and BY MUNICIPAL AUTHORITIES AND HEADS OF ASSOCIATIONS AND FEDERATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES of eighteen named countries of the region, which also REAFFIRMED THE LEGITIMATE RIGHTS... OVER THE NATURAL RESOURCES OF THE AREA IN QUESTION. The assembly passes resolutions that name natural resources and get signed by mayors across eighteen countries. A community campaign that can be framed as a municipal cause has a forum that has done exactly that before. THE OTHER REGIONAL NETWORKS BESIDE IT: regional analysis names, among the principal associations and networks of local and regional governments with EXPERIENCES, IDEAS AND RESOURCES TO FOSTER INITIATIVES AND PROJECTS LINKED TO SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AT LOCAL LEVEL, a network of Mercosur cities alongside this federation, and global initiatives with regional presence for local sustainability and for city climate action; various cities have prepared VOLUNTARY LOCAL REPORTS on implementing the global development agenda in their territories. A voluntary local report is a document a municipality writes about itself. Getting your community's situation named in one is cheap, public and lasting. THE HONEST NOTE ON REPRESENTATION: the region's representation in the world body has been the subject of negotiations between this federation, the Mercosur cities network and the world organisation to form A LATIN AMERICAN REPRESENTATION THAT IS PLURAL, DIVERSE AND PARTICIPATORY. More than one body claims to speak for the region's municipalities. Approach both this federation and the Mercosur cities network rather than assuming one covers the other.

trackers.name: Mercociudades - a South American city network whose cooperation calls admit UNIVERSITIES AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS as partners alongside two or more municipalities, with an environment and sustainable development unit coordinated by a member city
trackers.desc: UNIVERSITIES AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS CAN BE PARTNERS IN THE COOPERATION PROJECTS THIS CITY NETWORK FUNDS. Its south-south cooperation call is open to MEMBER CITIES AND ASSOCIATED STATES, to universities of a regional university association, and to ORGANISATIONS OF CIVIL SOCIETY; THE PROJECT MUST INVOLVE AT LEAST TWO MEMBER LOCAL GOVERNMENTS OR ASSOCIATED STATES, and THE UNIVERSITIES AND SOCIAL ORGANISATIONS MAY PARTICIPATE AS PARTNER ENTITIES ALONGSIDE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, each city able to stand as coordinator of one proposal and partner in another. Two municipalities and your organisation is a fundable consortium. Where a threatened area straddles two towns, or two towns face the same developer, that is the shape the call is written for. THE THEMATIC UNIT THAT COVERS LAND AND WATER: among its seventeen thematic units and four working groups is one for ENVIRONMENT AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT, coordinated by a city with sub-coordinating cities, which has run exchanges on waste, sustainability and circular economy and marked world water day, and has opened AN OPPORTUNITY OF COOPERATION TOGETHER WITH THE UNITED NATIONS ENVIRONMENT PROGRAMME FOR THE STRENGTHENING OF LOCAL CAPACITIES; other units cover AUTONOMY, MANAGEMENT AND PARTICIPATION, HUMAN RIGHTS, URBAN DEVELOPMENT, PLANNING AND METROPOLITAN AREAS and BORDER INTEGRATION. A coordinating city runs each unit, and it is a city like yours rather than a secretariat. Write to the coordinator of the environment unit with your case: that is a mayor's office, not an agency. WHAT THE NETWORK COMMITS ITSELF TO DO: among its statutory objectives are TO CARRY OUT STUDIES AND COLLABORATE IN THE ELABORATION OF PLANS AND STRATEGIES IN THE URBAN-ENVIRONMENTAL AREA, WITH THE OBJECTIVE OF HARMONISING AND COORDINATING THE ACTIONS IN THIS AREA, TO COLLABORATE IN THE PLANNING OF THE POLICIES AND PLANS OF DEVELOPMENT OF THE CITIES, TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE NEED TO IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF LIFE, TO ADVOCATE AND RAISE AWARENESS ABOUT CITIZEN PARTICIPATION AND SOCIAL INCLUSION, and TO IDENTIFY THE CAUSES OF ACCENTUATION OF THE SOCIAL INEQUALITIES, IN ORDER TO PROPOSE AND SUPPORT SOLUTIONS POSSIBLE TO BE EXECUTED BY THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS. Collaborating in city development plans is a stated commitment. A municipality revising its plan can ask the network for that collaboration rather than paying a consultancy. WHO ELSE MAY TAKE PART: THE OTHER INSTANCES OF THE SUB-NATIONAL GOVERNMENTS OF THE COUNTRIES of the two regional blocs THAT EXPRESS THEIR WILL TO DO SO AND WHOSE GOVERNMENTS HAVE BEEN DEMOCRATICALLY ELECTED may participate as collaborators, and COOPERATION WITH CONSORTIA AND ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES WILL BE CARRIED OUT BY MEANS OF AGREEMENTS. Provinces, departments and municipal consortia can join as collaborators. Where the decision sits above the town hall, that tier can be brought to the same table. THE PLATFORM THAT MATCHES NEEDS TO SOLUTIONS: its cooperation programme runs an interactive platform DESIGNED SPECIALLY TO SHARE LOCAL SOLUTIONS... AND TO INTERWEAVE STRENGTHS AND TECHNICAL NEEDS OF CITIES OF ALL SOUTH AMERICA, with a directory of good practices through which member cities HAVE THE POSSIBILITY OF EXCHANGING WITH THE REFERENTS OF SOLUTIONS OF THE CITIES. Post the technical need rather than the complaint. A city that has already solved the same problem is what the platform is built to find.

trackers.name: ICLEI - a sustainability network open to individual councils AND to associations of local governments, giving fee-paying members year-round telephone and email support on designing environment and water projects, plus local biodiversity planning tools and an environmental award
trackers.desc: MEMBERSHIP OF THIS GLOBAL SUSTAINABILITY NETWORK IS OPEN TO ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AS WELL AS TO INDIVIDUAL COUNCILS, AND THE FEE SCALES WITH POPULATION AND NATIONAL INCOME. Its membership page states that AFFILIATION IS OPEN TO ALL LOCAL AND REGIONAL GOVERNMENTS, AS WELL AS TO THEIR WORLD, REGIONAL, NATIONAL AND SUBNATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS, that members MAY VOTE AND PARTICIPATE IN THE GOVERNING ORGANS OF THE WHOLE NETWORK, and that they CONTRIBUTE AN ANNUAL AFFILIATION FEE THAT VARIES REGIONALLY AND ACCORDING TO POPULATION AND GROSS NATIONAL INCOME PER CAPITA. A small municipality pays a small fee and votes in the same network as a capital city. Where a national association is the member, ask whether your council is covered by it already. WHAT A MEMBER ACTUALLY GETS, IN THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT'S OWN WORDS: it SUPPORTS ITS PARTNERS TO FIND SUSTAINABLE SOLUTIONS THROUGH PROJECTS, INITIATIVES AND PROGRAMMES, offers cities and states A PLATFORM TO INTERACT WITH OTHER LOCAL GOVERNMENTS and provides RESOURCES AND TOOLS TO PROMOTE POSITIVE ENVIRONMENTAL, ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL CHANGES; support runs DURING THE YEAR THAT THE FEE LASTS, PERMANENTLY, BY TELEPHONE OR BY EMAIL, and covers THE DESIGN OF PROGRAMMES AND PROJECTS OF SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN THEMES SUCH AS: ENVIRONMENT, WATER, PUBLIC SERVICES, ENERGY EFFICIENCY, SOLID WASTE. Joining requires A REQUEST TO THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT addressed to the named regional secretary, plus a membership form. Permanent telephone and email support on designing water and environment projects, for one annual fee. That is a standing technical helpline for a town hall that has none. THE BIODIVERSITY WORK THAT MATTERS FOR LAND: its recorded local biodiversity work is TO PROMOTE THE BIODIVERSITY STRATEGIES OF THE STATE AND MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENTS, AS WELL AS THEIR ACTION PLANS, AND ALSO TO REINFORCE THE CAPACITIES OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS TO INCORPORATE BIODIVERSITY INTO THE PLANNING PROCESSES, and it notes that MORE MONETARY RESOURCES ARE INVESTED GLOBALLY IN BIODIVERSITY AT LOCAL AND SUBNATIONAL LEVEL THAN AT NATIONAL LEVELS; a member municipality has launched an urban biodiversity index, and a global initiative on NATURE IN URBAN PLANNING is promoted through the network. Incorporating biodiversity into planning processes is the exact point at which a project is stopped or waved through. Ask the secretariat which of its tools your municipality can adopt in its next plan revision. THE RECOGNITION THAT GIVES A COUNCIL A REASON: the regional secretariat runs an award for local governments THAT HAVE CARRIED OUT ACTIONS IN FAVOUR OF THE PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT IN THEMES OF CLIMATE CHANGE, BIODIVERSITY, ENERGY EFFICIENCY, MOBILITY, AMONG OTHERS, open to municipalities, city boroughs and federal entities. An award with a biodiversity category. A council weighing whether to protect a site has a public reason to do so, and the application is a deadline you can work to. THE OFFICES THAT COVER THIS REGION: there is a secretariat for one large federal country together with Central America and the Caribbean, and a separate South American secretariat, each publishing member lists that include municipalities of several countries. Two regional offices cover the whole file. Write to the one for your subregion rather than to the global body.

trackers.name: Fundo Casa Socioambiental - a small-grants fund for community groups across South America that funds groups WITHOUT LEGAL PERSONALITY through a partner organisation, with calls prioritising repeatedly rejected and newly formed groups
trackers.desc: A GROUP WITH NO LEGAL PERSONALITY AT ALL CAN RECEIVE A GRANT, BY BORROWING ANOTHER ORGANISATION'S. The fund's calls state that ORGANISATIONS THAT DO NOT POSSESS a registered company number ARE ALSO ELIGIBLE AND MAY SEND PROJECTS IN THIS CALL; the partner organisation field MUST ONLY BE FILLED IN IN THE CASES IN WHICH THE PROPOSING ORGANISATION DOES NOT POSSESS one, that partner being THE NON-PROFIT INSTITUTION THAT CEDES ITS LEGAL STRUCTURE TO THE GROUPS and THE LEGAL RESPONSIBLE FOR THE PROJECT, receiving the resource in an institutional bank account; one organisation may be PROPOSER OF ONE PROJECT OF ITS OWN AND PARTNER FOR UP TO ONE OTHER GROUP WITHOUT JURIDICAL PERSONALITY. An unincorporated village committee can be funded tomorrow if one registered neighbour signs as partner. That single rule removes the obstacle that blocks most community groups in this file. WHO THE FUND IS AND HOW SMALL THE GRANTS ARE: it is A NON-GOVERNMENTAL, NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION THAT FINANCES SMALL PROJECTS, AND CAPACITY STRENGTHENING, FOR SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL INITIATIVES OF NGOs AND COMMUNITY GROUPS IN SOUTH AMERICA, whose strategy is THE SUPPORT OF MANY PROJECTS WITH SMALL AMOUNTS INSTEAD OF SUPPORTING FEW PROJECTS WITH LARGE AMOUNTS; founded in 2005, its mission is TO PROMOTE CONSERVATION AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY, DEMOCRACY AND SOCIAL JUSTICE THROUGH THE SUPPORT AND STRENGTHENING OF CAPACITIES AND INITIATIVES OF CIVIL SOCIETY IN SOUTH AMERICA, with experience supporting POPULAR ORGANISATIONS, SOCIAL MOVEMENTS, NETWORKS AND ARTICULATIONS; recorded totals run from more than three thousand projects in ten countries to almost five thousand. Many small grants rather than a few large ones. A group asking for a few thousand is inside this fund's model rather than beneath its notice. WHAT A CALL ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE: one recorded call supported UP TO 24 PROJECTS OF UP TO R$ 35,000.00 in named river regions and one state, open to LOCAL ASSOCIATIONS AND COMMUNITY GROUPS WITH AN ANNUAL BUDGET OF UP TO R$ 150 THOUSAND, its priority publics being TRADITIONAL COMMUNITIES SUCH AS INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, QUILOMBOLA, RIVERSIDE AND EXTRACTIVIST COMMUNITIES; a later edition raised the ceiling to fifty thousand per project and expanded from thirty-four approved projects to fifty-seven after two hundred and thirty-three applications arrived. Another call prioritises ORGANISATIONS RECENTLY CREATED, IN AN INITIAL STAGE OF ACTIVITIES OR RESUMING THEIR ACTIVITIES AFTER A PERIOD OF PARALYSIS, and INITIATIVES OF ORGANISATIONS THAT HAVE NOT YET ACCESSED RESOURCES from the fund or that have applied three or more times without success. Applying and failing repeatedly is itself a stated priority criterion. If your group has been rejected three times, say so in the next application. THE THREE-COUNTRY ALLIANCE BEHIND THE AMAZON CALLS: one initiative unites this fund with a Colombian and a Peruvian socio-environmental fund, aiming TO PROMOTE GREATER CONTRIBUTION OF DIRECT RESOURCES TO INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, QUILOMBOLA COMMUNITIES AND OTHER TRADITIONAL PEOPLES IN THE AMAZON OF BRAZIL, PERU AND COLOMBIA, ESPECIALLY IN THE BORDER REGION, supporting twenty-four, fourteen and nineteen projects respectively in one year; all members of a southern socio-environmental funds alliance WILL LAUNCH CALLS IN THEIR COUNTRIES, each publishing its own. Border regions are named as a priority rather than a complication. Look up the member fund for your own country and read its call, not only this one. THE RULES THAT CATCH PEOPLE OUT: resources may not be spent before the contract is signed; funds from other budget lines may not be moved to pay consultancies; groups with PENDING ACCOUNTS from a previous grant are not accepted; and where a group hires advice it MUST SEEK PEOPLE OF TRUST, with the project ELABORATED TOGETHER WITH THE COMMUNITY and its final version OF WIDE KNOWLEDGE OF THE COMMUNITY. Do not spend a peso before signature, and do not let a consultant write the proposal alone. Both are stated grounds for losing the grant.

trackers.name: The GEF Small Grants Programme - grants of up to $50,000 DIRECT to community organisations, with a national coordinator in each country who helps write the concept paper, planning grants, and a companion window of up to $300,000
