WHO PAID, AND HOW THE MATCH WORKED: the purchase was made WITH THE SUPPORT OF a bird conservation organisation, an international conservation fund, a national branch of a conservation union and a land purchase trust; a dedicated fund was established by the supporter's family with the association and the bird organisation, with DONATIONS RECEIVED IN 2018... MATCHED DOLLAR FOR DOLLAR UP TO $100,000, providing VITAL LONG-TERM SUPPORT FOR THE NEST BOX PROGRAM AS WELL AS HABITAT CONSERVATION AND RESERVE MANAGEMENT. Four funders on one purchase, plus a matched fund for the running costs. A single donor rarely covers a reserve; assembling several is the work. WHAT IT DOES ON THE LAND IT OWNS: published annual objectives include ENLARGING THE... RESERVE TO PROTECT IMPORTANT FEEDING HABITATS, experimenting with silage from stored natural grasses as dry-season forage, improving riverbank short-grass habitat with irrigation, and CONTROLLING THE FERAL PIG POPULATION BY TRADITIONAL HUNTING METHODS LED BY COMMUNITIES; the reserve runs a sustainable cattle model, and since 2013 a lodge OFFERS A SERVICE TO OBSERVE WILDLIFE, WHILE THE INCOME CONTRIBUTES TO THE SUSTAINABILITY OF THE CONSERVATION PROGRAMME. Community-led hunting of feral pigs inside a private reserve, and cattle kept rather than banished. A reserve that keeps local livelihoods on the land is the kind neighbours defend. THE RECOGNITION AND THE THREAT IT FACED: in 2015 the site was classified as a place of regional importance in a hemispheric shorebird reserve network, THE FIRST OF the country; and press records that the species and the reserve SCORED A TRIUMPH OVER AN ILLEGAL SETTLEMENT IN ITS HABITAT. Even a bought, registered reserve faced an illegal settlement. Ownership is the beginning of protection, not the end of it — budget for the guarding as well as the purchase.

trackers.name: Instituto de Acceso a la Información Pública (IAIP)
trackers.desc: National right-to-information authority; El Salvador’s IAIP is the guarantor body under the LAIP (2011) — resolving access appeals, training officials and overseeing the Portal de Transparencia, El Salvador.

trackers.name: FIAES — Fondo de la Iniciativa para las Américas El Salvador
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a debt-for-nature fund created by Legislative Decree 585 of 1993 under the Enterprise for the Americas agreement with the United States and extended in 2001 by the Tropical Forest Conservation Act. It funds work in protected areas, the coastal-marine ecosystem and their buffer zones, prioritising by national poverty index as well as biodiversity. WHO IT SUITS: NGOs and ADESCOs — legally recognised community development associations — acting as organizaciones ejecutoras; individuals cannot apply. HOW IT DIFFERS: its council is chaired by the environment minister, so it is quasi-public money with published operating manuals you can read before applying.

trackers.name: UNES — Unidad Ecológica Salvadoreña
trackers.desc: El Salvador's principal environmental organisation working alongside community groups defending territory — indigenous communities in resistance in the Sensunapán-Banderas river basin, mangrove management on the coast, and the long fight over metallic mining. It accompanies and strengthens local committees rather than acting for them, and it articulates nationally with the Juzgado Ambiental, the human rights ombudsman (PDDH) and municipal governments, which is the practical value: it knows which of those doors to use. It has also run a strategic environmental litigation diploma with the Universidad de El Salvador. WHO IT SUITS: organised community committees and campesino and indigenous groups; UNES accompanies and trains, it does not litigate your case for you.

trackers.name: El Faro
trackers.desc: Salvadoran investigative newsroom reporting on corruption, organized crime and power.

trackers.name: El Salvador — Centro Nacional de Registros (CNR)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the Registro de Comercio registers companies & commercial entities (consultable online) alongside property & IP registries, El Salvador. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: COMPRASAL
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in El Salvador, and for how much.

trackers.name: Corte de Cuentas de la República
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of El Salvador. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in El Salvador.

trackers.name: Juzgados Ambientales — they order remedies; plan to fight for the compliance record
trackers.desc: SPECIALIST ENVIRONMENTAL COURTS THAT HAVE ORDERED REMEDIAL MEASURES AGAINST MINING DAMAGE — few countries in this map have one. The Juzgado Ambiental de San Miguel ordered in 2019 a series of measures to reduce the damage caused by mining at San Sebastián. BUT RECORD WHAT HAPPENED NEXT, BECAUSE IT DEFINES THE LIMIT: on 31 January the Ministry of Environment (MARN) declared as reserved information the compliance with those court-ordered measures, refusing to release it and stating the data would stay reserved until the case concludes in February 2030. So the order exists and the compliance record is sealed for years. If you win an order from an environmental court here, assume you will have to fight separately for the compliance information, and build the access-to-information request into the litigation plan rather than treating it as a follow-up. NOTE ALSO the cost-recovery provision from the 2017 law: MARN was required, at the cost of the responsible persons, to close old metallic mines and recover affected regions — worth checking whether an equivalent survives in the current law.

trackers.name: The 2017 mining ban — a model statute, and a lesson about durability
trackers.desc: THE STRONGEST CITIZEN-WON ENVIRONMENTAL LAW IN THIS MAP — AND IT WAS REPEALED. In March 2017 El Salvador became the first country in the world to prohibit metallic mining in all its forms, after a citizen campaign backed by environmental organisations, the Catholic Church and local communities. THE DRAFTING IS THE MODEL: art. 2 definitively prohibits exploration, extraction, exploitation and processing in any possible form, and bans toxic chemicals such as cyanide and mercury in any mining process; art. 3 reaches terrestrial, maritime and subterranean mining; and art. 9 declares the law special, of national interest, prevailing over any other that contradicts it — a supremacy clause inside an environmental statute is rare and is the feature to copy. Artisanal miners and güiriseros got 2 years to convert to another activity, so subsistence work was transitioned rather than criminalised. IT WAS REPEALED IN DECEMBER 2024 by the Ley General de Minería Metálica; the Dirección General de Energía, Hidrocarburos y Minas is now the principal authority, with MARN and the Autoridad Salvadoreña del Agua overseeing environmental and water conditions, and the reglamento due within one year. Opponents including UNES, the Church and the UCA warn the Río Lempa could receive toxic waste; a campaign for a million signatures to have the law declared unconstitutional is running, though its own leaders judge a favourable response very unlikely. THE LESSON FOR THE WHOLE MAP: a law won by citizens, carrying a supremacy clause, was still repealed by a later legislature. Durability comes from constitutional entrenchment or treaty status, not from statutory language however strong.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: El Salvador's communal development associations - legal personality granted by the town hall within fifteen days, a municipal officer sent to help constitute them, power to receive cooperation funds, and a new registration deadline to check
trackers.desc: A NEIGHBOURHOOD CAN OBTAIN LEGAL PERSONALITY THROUGH ITS OWN TOWN HALL, AND THE COUNCIL MUST ANSWER WITHIN FIFTEEN DAYS. The municipal code provides that THE COMMUNAL ASSOCIATIONS SHALL HAVE LEGAL PERSONALITY GRANTED BY THE RESPECTIVE COUNCIL, that associations SHALL PRESENT AN APPLICATION FOR REGISTRATION AND GRANT OF LEGAL PERSONALITY TO THE COUNCIL, ATTACHING THE STATUTES, AND IT SHALL RESOLVE AT THE LATEST WITHIN THE FIFTEEN FOLLOWING DAYS, and that the approval agreement and statutes SHALL BE PUBLISHED IN THE OFFICIAL GAZETTE; associations MAY PARTICIPATE IN THE SOCIAL, ECONOMIC, CULTURAL, RELIGIOUS, CIVIC, EDUCATIONAL FIELD AND IN ANY OTHER THAT IS LEGAL AND BENEFICIAL TO THE COMMUNITY. Fifteen days for a decision, and legal personality granted locally. That is the entry ticket every funder, court and ministry in this file asks for, obtainable at your own town hall. HOW IT IS ACTUALLY DONE, STEP BY STEP: the community approaches the municipal DEPARTMENT OF COMMUNAL DEVELOPMENT so that a representative accompanies it; a GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF NEIGHBOURS is held in the neighbourhood in that representative's presence, at which the board is elected; at a following assembly a council representative SWEARS IN THE BOARD AND THEY CAN BEGIN TO WORK, minutes being kept throughout. From twenty-five attendees a BOARD OF ELEVEN PEOPLE is chosen, including a president, a legal officer, a treasurer and four members-at-large; the association ends up holding CREDENTIALS OF THE BOARD, A COPY OF THE OFFICIAL GAZETTE, THE AGREEMENT OF LEGAL PERSONALITY, THE TAX NUMBER OF THE ASSOCIATION AND CERTIFICATION OF THE CONSTITUTIVE ACT. Twenty-five neighbours at one meeting, a municipal officer present, and a second meeting to swear in the board. Ask the communal development department to send that officer — accompanying you is their job. WHAT THESE ASSOCIATIONS DO AND HOLD: they are described as bodies that WORK TOGETHER WITH THE MAYORALTIES AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS FOR THE PROMOTION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF PROJECTS in health, education, WATER, infrastructure and housing, that CONVOKE COMMUNITY ASSEMBLIES TO DISCUSS PUBLIC AFFAIRS AND THE NEEDS OF THE CITIZENS, AND MEDIATE BETWEEN CITIZENS AND AUTHORITIES, some having created working commissions linking members, specialists and local governments; they RECEIVE AND ADMINISTER FUNDS COMING FROM NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL COOPERANTS. They can receive and administer cooperation funds directly. Where an outside funder asks who will hold the money, this is the answer that does not require an intermediary. THE CHANGE IN PROGRESS, WHICH MUST BE CHECKED BEFORE ANYONE RELIES ON THIS: reforms would mean the council WOULD CONTINUE GRANTING THE AGREEMENT OF RECOGNITION, BUT THE LEGAL PERSONALITY WOULD ONLY BE PERFECTED WITH INSCRIPTION IN THE new communal associations registry within the national registry centre, and ALL EXISTING COMMUNAL ASSOCIATIONS WILL HAVE TO REGISTER OBLIGATORILY... WITHIN THE PERIOD OF ONE YEAR, TO CONSERVE THEIR LEGAL PERSONALITY; councils would keep supervision powers and could pursue sanctions where obligations are unmet. Associations may be constituted in NEIGHBOURHOODS, COLONIES, CANTONS AND HAMLETS. If your association was recognised only by the municipality, the one-year registration deadline is the thing to check first. An unregistered association loses the standing everything else in this file depends on.

trackers.name: FLACMA - the Latin American federation of cities and municipal associations, open to affiliation by ANY INDIVIDUAL MUNICIPALITY, whose assembly passes resolutions signed by mayors across eighteen countries
trackers.desc: ANY CITY OR MUNICIPALITY IN THE REGION MAY AFFILIATE DIRECTLY, NOT ONLY THROUGH ITS NATIONAL ASSOCIATION. Its membership rule is that MEMBERS ARE ALL THE CITIES, MUNICIPALITIES, NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND MUNICIPALIST INSTITUTIONS OF LATIN AMERICA THAT HAVE EXPRESSED THEIR WILL TO AFFILIATE; it is AN ORGANISATION OF FREE ADHESION THAT REPRESENTS THE 16,132 MUNICIPALITIES, INTENDANCIES AND PREFECTURES, THE CITIES AND THE ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, NETWORKS AND GUILDS OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, and it is the regional section of the world organisation of local governments. A single municipality may join in its own right. Where your national association is captured or inactive, that is a way for one sympathetic town hall to reach the regional table on its own. WHOSE PRESIDENTS SIT ON IT: its published leadership is drawn from the presidents of the national municipal bodies of the region — the federation of municipalities of one southern country, the association of municipalities of another, the Brazilian association of municipalities, the congress of intendants of another, the national federation of municipalities of one large federal country and the association of municipalities of an Andean one — each of them a serving mayor. The people who chair your own national municipal association sit here. A matter raised through that association can be carried into a regional assembly by the same person. WHAT IT SAYS IT IS FOR: TO BE THE VOICE OF LATIN AMERICAN MUNICIPALISM, TO CONSOLIDATE THE LATIN AMERICAN MUNICIPAL ASSOCIATIVE MOVEMENT, TO REPRESENT AND SERVE AS INTERLOCUTOR OF ALL THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND THEIR NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES, and TO PROMOTE IN LATIN AMERICA AUTONOMOUS, STRONG AND DEMOCRATIC LOCAL GOVERNMENTS; it ADHERES TO AND PROMOTES THE WORLD AND REGIONAL CONVENTIONS THAT THE NATIONAL STATES OF THE REGION SUBSCRIBE. Promoting the conventions the states have signed is written into its purpose. Where your country has signed an environmental or rights convention and a municipality is being told to ignore it, that is a body with a standing commitment to the opposite. THE PRECEDENT THAT SHOWS IT TAKES POSITIONS: its general assembly has approved unanimously a declaration on a territorial sovereignty dispute, signed by the president and BY MUNICIPAL AUTHORITIES AND HEADS OF ASSOCIATIONS AND FEDERATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES of eighteen named countries of the region, which also REAFFIRMED THE LEGITIMATE RIGHTS... OVER THE NATURAL RESOURCES OF THE AREA IN QUESTION. The assembly passes resolutions that name natural resources and get signed by mayors across eighteen countries. A community campaign that can be framed as a municipal cause has a forum that has done exactly that before. THE OTHER REGIONAL NETWORKS BESIDE IT: regional analysis names, among the principal associations and networks of local and regional governments with EXPERIENCES, IDEAS AND RESOURCES TO FOSTER INITIATIVES AND PROJECTS LINKED TO SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AT LOCAL LEVEL, a network of Mercosur cities alongside this federation, and global initiatives with regional presence for local sustainability and for city climate action; various cities have prepared VOLUNTARY LOCAL REPORTS on implementing the global development agenda in their territories. A voluntary local report is a document a municipality writes about itself. Getting your community's situation named in one is cheap, public and lasting. THE HONEST NOTE ON REPRESENTATION: the region's representation in the world body has been the subject of negotiations between this federation, the Mercosur cities network and the world organisation to form A LATIN AMERICAN REPRESENTATION THAT IS PLURAL, DIVERSE AND PARTICIPATORY. More than one body claims to speak for the region's municipalities. Approach both this federation and the Mercosur cities network rather than assuming one covers the other.

trackers.name: ICLEI - a sustainability network open to individual councils AND to associations of local governments, giving fee-paying members year-round telephone and email support on designing environment and water projects, plus local biodiversity planning tools and an environmental award
trackers.desc: MEMBERSHIP OF THIS GLOBAL SUSTAINABILITY NETWORK IS OPEN TO ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AS WELL AS TO INDIVIDUAL COUNCILS, AND THE FEE SCALES WITH POPULATION AND NATIONAL INCOME. Its membership page states that AFFILIATION IS OPEN TO ALL LOCAL AND REGIONAL GOVERNMENTS, AS WELL AS TO THEIR WORLD, REGIONAL, NATIONAL AND SUBNATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS, that members MAY VOTE AND PARTICIPATE IN THE GOVERNING ORGANS OF THE WHOLE NETWORK, and that they CONTRIBUTE AN ANNUAL AFFILIATION FEE THAT VARIES REGIONALLY AND ACCORDING TO POPULATION AND GROSS NATIONAL INCOME PER CAPITA. A small municipality pays a small fee and votes in the same network as a capital city. Where a national association is the member, ask whether your council is covered by it already. WHAT A MEMBER ACTUALLY GETS, IN THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT'S OWN WORDS: it SUPPORTS ITS PARTNERS TO FIND SUSTAINABLE SOLUTIONS THROUGH PROJECTS, INITIATIVES AND PROGRAMMES, offers cities and states A PLATFORM TO INTERACT WITH OTHER LOCAL GOVERNMENTS and provides RESOURCES AND TOOLS TO PROMOTE POSITIVE ENVIRONMENTAL, ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL CHANGES; support runs DURING THE YEAR THAT THE FEE LASTS, PERMANENTLY, BY TELEPHONE OR BY EMAIL, and covers THE DESIGN OF PROGRAMMES AND PROJECTS OF SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN THEMES SUCH AS: ENVIRONMENT, WATER, PUBLIC SERVICES, ENERGY EFFICIENCY, SOLID WASTE. Joining requires A REQUEST TO THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT addressed to the named regional secretary, plus a membership form. Permanent telephone and email support on designing water and environment projects, for one annual fee. That is a standing technical helpline for a town hall that has none. THE BIODIVERSITY WORK THAT MATTERS FOR LAND: its recorded local biodiversity work is TO PROMOTE THE BIODIVERSITY STRATEGIES OF THE STATE AND MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENTS, AS WELL AS THEIR ACTION PLANS, AND ALSO TO REINFORCE THE CAPACITIES OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS TO INCORPORATE BIODIVERSITY INTO THE PLANNING PROCESSES, and it notes that MORE MONETARY RESOURCES ARE INVESTED GLOBALLY IN BIODIVERSITY AT LOCAL AND SUBNATIONAL LEVEL THAN AT NATIONAL LEVELS; a member municipality has launched an urban biodiversity index, and a global initiative on NATURE IN URBAN PLANNING is promoted through the network. Incorporating biodiversity into planning processes is the exact point at which a project is stopped or waved through. Ask the secretariat which of its tools your municipality can adopt in its next plan revision. THE RECOGNITION THAT GIVES A COUNCIL A REASON: the regional secretariat runs an award for local governments THAT HAVE CARRIED OUT ACTIONS IN FAVOUR OF THE PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT IN THEMES OF CLIMATE CHANGE, BIODIVERSITY, ENERGY EFFICIENCY, MOBILITY, AMONG OTHERS, open to municipalities, city boroughs and federal entities. An award with a biodiversity category. A council weighing whether to protect a site has a public reason to do so, and the application is a deadline you can work to. THE OFFICES THAT COVER THIS REGION: there is a secretariat for one large federal country together with Central America and the Caribbean, and a separate South American secretariat, each publishing member lists that include municipalities of several countries. Two regional offices cover the whole file. Write to the one for your subregion rather than to the global body.

trackers.name: Fundación DEMUCA - a foundation for strengthening local governments across Central America and the Caribbean, working through the national municipal associations, with a work line covering ENVIRONMENTAL AND RISK MANAGEMENT and cohorts of twenty municipalities
trackers.desc: A FOUNDATION EXISTS WHOSE WHOLE PURPOSE IS STRENGTHENING LOCAL GOVERNMENTS IN CENTRAL AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, AND IT WORKS THROUGH THE NATIONAL MUNICIPAL ASSOCIATIONS. It is described as AN INSTRUMENT OF TECHNICAL AND FINANCIAL COOPERATION of a national development agency THAT PROMOTES THE STRENGTHENING OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS IN CENTRAL AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, its work focused on THE DESIGN OF STRATEGIES AND THE EXECUTION OF NATIONAL AND REGIONAL PROJECTS AIMED AT IMPROVING THE MANAGEMENT CAPABILITIES OF MUNICIPALITIES AND THEIR VARIOUS FORMS OF ASSOCIATION; it SUPPORTS THE NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES IN THE GENERATION OF STRATEGIC POLICY PROPOSALS and COLLABORATES IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPROVEMENT OF THE MEANS AND INSTRUMENTS OF ADMINISTRATION OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS. It is a foundation constituted under the law of one member country in 1995, with a delegation registered in the cooperating country. Where a national municipal association is weak, this is the body that funds and staffs its policy work. Ask your association what it currently receives, and whether your municipality is in the next cohort. THE THREE WORK LINES, ONE OF WHICH COVERS ENVIRONMENT: the cooperation is channelled through this foundation in three lines — TAX REFORM AT LOCAL LEVEL, TO STRENGTHEN THE FINANCIAL CAPACITY OF THE MUNICIPALITIES WITH THEIR OWN RESOURCES TO IMPLEMENT THEIR POLICIES; implementation of the municipal administrative career statute FOR THE STABILITY OF THE HUMAN RESOURCE AND OF THE MUNICIPAL PLANS; and STRENGTHENING OF CAPACITIES OF THE MUNICIPALITIES AND ASSOCIATIONS, TO PROMOTE MUNICIPAL ASSOCIATIVISM, LOCAL ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, POLICIES AND PLANS OF EQUALITY, ENVIRONMENTAL AND RISK MANAGEMENT, STRENGTHENING OF THE SOCIAL FABRIC AND THE PREVENTION OF VIOLENCE. Environmental and risk management sits inside the third line, alongside strengthening the social fabric. A request framed as municipal capacity on environmental management fits the existing programme rather than asking for something new. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DELIVERS, FROM RECORDED EXAMPLES: with a national municipalities corporation and a state municipal development institute it launched a second phase of implementation FOR 20 NEW MUNICIPALITIES AT NATIONAL LEVEL; TO WHICH TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE WILL BE GIVEN TO STRENGTHEN THEIR CAPACITIES through LABOUR TECHNIFICATION, PERMANENT TRAINING AND THE CREATION, DESIGN AND APPLICATION OF TOOLS AND INSTRUMENTS; it co-published a guide for the internal functioning of plural municipal councils; and it produced a model to improve municipal tax management, described by its own technician as A SIMPLE GUIDE DIRECTED TO STRENGTHENING MUNICIPAL AUTONOMY, WHICH CAN BE IMPLEMENTED WITHOUT HAVING EXTERNAL TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, piloted in ten named municipalities with external financing of twenty-seven thousand dollars. Twenty municipalities in one cohort, and a tax guide a town hall can apply on its own. Both are the kind of thing a small municipality can be nominated for without a budget of its own. THE REGIONAL BODY IT SITS BESIDE: the federation of municipalities of the Central American isthmus is one of the organisations from which the Latin American municipal federation was formed, and has appeared as a regional counterpart in municipal research and in Mesoamerican biological corridor work. Verify whether that federation is currently active before relying on it; the foundation above is the better documented door at present.

trackers.name: Alianza Socioambiental Fondos del Sur - the alliance listing each country's own grassroots socio-environmental fund, several of which pay for MOBILISATIONS IN DEFENCE OF RIGHTS and run joint cross-border calls
trackers.desc: EVERY MAJOR COUNTRY IN THIS REGION NOW HAS ITS OWN SMALL-GRANTS FUND RUN BY LOCAL ENVIRONMENTALISTS, AND THEY ARE LISTED IN ONE PLACE. The alliance names among its members funds in BRAZIL — a socio-environmental fund founded in 2005, an institute of society, population and nature with its own ecos fund, and a Brazilian fund for environmental education — plus MEXICO, CENTRAL AMERICA, BOLIVIA, PERU, COLOMBIA, ECUADOR and, in ARGENTINA, a rural communities network and a socio-environmental fund; each fund is A NATIONAL OR REGIONAL ENTITY DEDICATED TO PROVIDING GRANTS AND OTHER FORMS OF SUPPORT TO LOCAL GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS THAT PROPOSE JUST AND SUSTAINABLE ALTERNATIVES TO PROTECT THE RIGHTS AND ECOSYSTEMS OF COMMUNITIES, and all were FOUNDED BY LOCAL SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTALISTS. One page lists the fund for your country. Start there rather than with an international donor, because these funds exist precisely because grassroots groups cannot reach the large external financiers. WHY THESE FUNDS EXIST, IN THEIR OWN WORDS: they attend to how THE MOST VULNERABLE POPULATIONS FACING ENVIRONMENTAL CHALLENGES ARE ALSO THE MOST EXCLUDED FROM PHILANTHROPIC SUPPORT, whose RIGHTS ARE CONSTANTLY VIOLATED AND WHO IN GENERAL CANNOT ACCESS A LARGE EXTERNAL FINANCIER. Being too small for the big funders is the qualifying condition here, not a disqualification. WHAT THE COLOMBIAN FUND SAYS IT DOES, AS A TEMPLATE: it is AN ALLY OF THE GRASSROOTS COMMUNITIES, WHICH WORKS TO STRENGTHEN AND AMPLIFY THEIR AUTONOMY, KNOWLEDGE AND CAPACITIES IN THE DEFENCE OF LIFE, TERRITORIES AND COMMON GOODS, functioning as A MECHANISM OF FINANCIAL, POLITICAL AND ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT TO COMMUNITY AGENDAS THAT PROTECT ECOSYSTEMS, HUMAN RIGHTS AND SOCIAL JUSTICE AT LOCAL LEVEL, responding IN AN AGILE MANNER TO COMMUNITY PROJECTS AND ACTIONS, INCLUDING EMERGENT NEEDS SUCH AS MOBILISATIONS IN DEFENCE OF RIGHTS; since 2020 it has SUPPORTED 280 GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS... AND MOBILISED MORE THAN US$1,000,000 IN SMALL DONATIONS. Mobilisations in defence of rights are named as fundable. Very few funders in this file will pay for that, and this one says so on its own page. THE CENTRAL AMERICAN FUND, WHICH COVERS SEVERAL COUNTRIES AT ONCE: it gives STRATEGIC ACCOMPANIMENT AND AGILE AND TIMELY DONATIONS TO INDIGENOUS, PEASANT AND AFRO-DESCENDANT ORGANISATIONS, IN THEIR PROCESSES OF IMPROVING THEIR SOCIAL, ECONOMIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESILIENCE IN CENTRAL AMERICA. For the Central American countries there is one regional door rather than seven national ones. Address it as a regional fund and say which country and territory you are in. WHAT THE ALLIANCE ADDS ON TOP OF THE INDIVIDUAL FUNDS: members run joint calls across borders, publishing separate deadlines per country for the same initiative, and have documented the experience in a case study on how one project PROMOTED COLLABORATION AMONG LOCAL FUNDS OF BRAZIL, COLOMBIA AND PERU IN THE AMAZON BORDER REGION; the alliance also includes a youth-led global thematic fund. The same call closes on different dates in each country. Check your own fund's deadline rather than the one you saw quoted elsewhere.

trackers.name: The GEF Small Grants Programme - grants of up to $50,000 DIRECT to community organisations, with a national coordinator in each country who helps write the concept paper, planning grants, and a companion window of up to $300,000
trackers.desc: THERE IS A NAMED NATIONAL COORDINATOR IN YOUR COUNTRY WHOSE JOB INCLUDES HELPING YOU WRITE THE APPLICATION. The programme's own procedure is that THE PROJECT PROPONENT — A NATIONAL CBO OR NGO — CONTACTS THE SGP NATIONAL COORDINATOR TO RECEIVE PROJECT APPLICATION GUIDELINES AND FORMS, and that WITH ASSISTANCE FROM THE NATIONAL COORDINATOR, THE PROPONENT PREPARES A BRIEF PROJECT CONCEPT PAPER; the coordinator pre-screens it, and if eligible the proponent prepares a full proposal — IN SOME CASES, THIS STEP MAY BE SUPPORTED BY A PLANNING GRANT — which goes to a national steering committee that accepts, rejects or returns it for further work. A planning grant to write the proposal, and an official whose job is to help you write it. Contact the coordinator before drafting anything, because the concept paper is short and they will tell you whether it fits. WHAT IT PAYS AND TO WHOM: the programme PROVIDES GRANTS OF UP TO $50,000 DIRECTLY TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES INCLUDING INDIGENOUS PEOPLE, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS AND OTHER NON-GOVERNMENTAL GROUPS, for projects in BIODIVERSITY, CLIMATE CHANGE MITIGATION AND ADAPTATION, LAND DEGRADATION AND SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT, INTERNATIONAL WATERS AND CHEMICALS, with SPECIAL CONSIDERATION FOR INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, WOMEN, AND YOUTH; it COMPLEMENTS THE LARGE AND MEDIUM-SIZED facility funding BY PROVIDING A WINDOW FOR THE DIRECT PARTICIPATION OF NGOs, LOCAL COMMUNITIES, AND OTHER GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS. Since 1992 it has supported CLOSE TO 30,000 GRANTS, ADMINISTERING $1.54 BILLION... ACROSS 136 COUNTRIES. Fifty thousand dollars, paid direct to a community organisation, on biodiversity or land degradation. That is the largest routine sum in this file available without an intermediary. HOW IT IS RUN LOCALLY: it operates IN A DECENTRALIZED AND COUNTRY-DRIVEN MANNER THROUGH COUNTRY PROGRAM TEAMS COMPOSED OF A NATIONAL COORDINATOR, OFTEN A PROGRAM ASSISTANT, AND A NATIONAL STEERING COMMITTEE IN EACH PARTICIPATING COUNTRY, each country publishing a country programme strategy that proposals must align with. In one small island state an operational phase was advertised with A GRANTS PORTFOLIO OF APPROXIMATELY US$750,000... FOR COMMUNITY-BASED ENVIRONMENTAL PROJECTS. Download your country's programme strategy before writing. Proposals are judged against that document, and it names the priorities and often the specific landscapes. THE THREE AGENCIES THAT NOW RUN IT: the core programme is implemented by a development programme, an agriculture organisation and a conservation organisation, the second bringing expertise in AGRICULTURE, FISHERIES, FORESTRY, BIOENERGY, CLIMATE-RESILIENT PRACTICES, LIVESTOCK, AND LAND & WATER to thirteen countries; national coordinator posts in some small states are contracted through the conservation organisation, working alongside a Caribbean islands biodiversity hotspot fund. Which agency runs your country's programme changes who you write to. Check the country page rather than assuming it is the development programme. THE LARGER WINDOW BESIDE IT: a civil society challenge programme led by a conservation union SUPPORTS COMPETITIVE OPPORTUNITIES FOR LOCAL CSOs TO ACCESS FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL RESOURCES TO SCALE UP INNOVATIVE ENVIRONMENTAL SOLUTIONS, OFFERING GRANTS OF UP TO $300,000. Three hundred thousand for an organisation that has already proved something small works. Treat the fifty-thousand grant as the step that qualifies you for it.

trackers.name: Pro Bono Network of the Americas and its national clearinghouses - non-profits in 16 countries that place SOCIAL ORGANISATIONS with volunteer law firms free, plus free representation for cases at the merits stage before the inter-American commission
trackers.desc: THERE IS A CLEARINGHOUSE IN MOST OF THESE COUNTRIES WHOSE JOB IS TO FIND A LAW FIRM WILLING TO ACT FOR YOUR ORGANISATION FREE. Its members are NON-PROFIT ENTITIES THAT FACILITATE THE PROVISION OF FREE LEGAL SERVICES TO PEOPLE OF SCARCE RESOURCES, SECTORS OR GROUPS IN A CONDITION OF VULNERABILITY, ENTREPRENEURS AND SOCIAL ORGANISATIONS, WITH A VIEW TO IMPROVING ACCESS TO JUSTICE AND THE DEFENCE OF THE PUBLIC INTEREST; the network born in 2011 HAS NOW BECOME THE MAIN INSTITUTIONAL HOME OF THE PRIMARY PRO BONO CLEARINGHOUSES IN THE REGION and INCLUDES MORE THAN 20 ORGANIZATIONS, REPRESENTING 16 COUNTRIES, coordinated jointly by a New York bar association centre and a national pro bono foundation. Social organisations are named alongside individuals as eligible. A community association fighting a project is exactly the kind of client these clearinghouses were built to place. HOW A CASE ACTUALLY REACHES A LAWYER: one national foundation RECEIVES REQUESTS FOR PRO BONO CASES THROUGH ITS WEB PLATFORM OR OTHER ENTITIES, and ARTICULATES AND CHANNELS FREE LEGAL ADVICE, CARRIES OUT WORKSHOPS AND INFORMATIVE TALKS AND SEEKS TO GENERATE PUBLIC INFLUENCE; another states that cases ARRIVE AT THE FOUNDATION THROUGH the regional centre, the regional network, or national NGOs in contact with member firms and university professors, and that WHOEVER HAS A CASE OR A PROJECT FOR WHICH THEY NEED PRO BONO ADVICE MAY PRESENT IT BY SENDING AN EMAIL to a published address. One email with the case attached. That is the whole entry procedure in at least one country, and the others run a web form. THE HONEST LIMIT, STATED BY THE CLEARINGHOUSE ITSELF: one alliance RESERVES THE RIGHT TO EVALUATE AND DECIDE WHETHER A REQUEST MAY BE CONSIDERED A PRO BONO CASE; THE PRESENTATION OF A REQUEST DOES NOT GUARANTEE ITS ACCEPTANCE, NOR THE ASSIGNMENT OF A LAWYER OR FIRM; it ACTS ONLY AS AN INTERMEDIARY BETWEEN THE PERSON OR ORGANISATION REQUESTING AND THE VOLUNTEER LAWYERS, and taking a case DEPENDS EXCLUSIVELY ON THE VOLUNTARY DECISION OF THOSE LAWYERS OR FIRMS, WITHOUT ANY OBLIGATION OF SPONSORSHIP EXISTING. No guarantee, and no obligation on any firm. Apply to more than one clearinghouse, and make the request specific enough that a commercial firm can see the discrete piece of work being asked for. WHAT THE NETWORK COORDINATES BEYOND SINGLE CASES: volunteer lawyers and firms work on PARTICIPATION BEFORE THE INTER-AMERICAN SYSTEM OF HUMAN RIGHTS, COOPERATION TO SOCIAL ORGANISATIONS THAT REQUIRE LEGAL SUPPORT, THE ELABORATION OF THEMATIC REPORTS AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT TO INITIATIVES; under a collaboration agreement with the inter-American human rights commission the network PROVIDES PRO BONO LEGAL REPRESENTATION TO PEOPLE WITH CASES AT THE MERITS STAGE, the commission notifying petitioners of that opportunity. Free representation for a case already before the inter-American commission, arranged through this network. If a matter has reached that stage, ask the commission and the network at the same time. THE REGIONAL PROGRAMME AIMED AT SMALL ORGANISATIONS: under a civic space strengthening project the network HAS DECIDED TO JOIN FORCES TO SUPPORT THE NON-PROFIT INITIATIVES OF CENTRAL AMERICAN COUNTRIES BY MEANS OF ITS NETWORK OF LAWYERS TO PROVIDE FREE ADVICE TO APPLICANTS, with an application form; it also runs law student competitions and internship placements across member organisations. For the Central American countries there is a dedicated window rather than only the national clearinghouse. Use it, and note that the same network places law students who can do the document work.

trackers.name: Fondo de Acción Urgente para América Latina y el Caribe - rapid response grants of up to $5,000 decided in NO MORE THAN 10 WORKING DAYS for defenders under threat, plus a strategic window for organisations defending territories and common goods
trackers.desc: A REQUEST IS STUDIED IN NO MORE THAN TEN WORKING DAYS AND THE MONEY MOVES THREE DAYS AFTER APPROVAL. The fund's rapid response grants are A UNIQUE, FLEXIBLE, AND SHORT-TERM FINANCING MODEL... TO PROVIDE TIMELY AND STRATEGIC SUPPORT FOR ACTIONS THAT RESPOND TO SITUATIONS OF RISK OR THREATS THAT IMPACT THE SECURITY OF WOMEN ACTIVISTS AND DEFENDERS, THEIR COLLECTIVES, OR ORGANIZATIONS, or that TAKE ADVANTAGE OF OPPORTUNITIES TO ADVANCE OR DETER SETBACKS TO THE RIGHTS; ONCE A REQUEST IS RECEIVED, IT IS STUDIED DURING NO MORE THAN 10 WORKING DAYS. IF IT IS APPROVED, IT TAKES AT LEAST THREE WORKING DAYS TO TRANSFER THE RESOURCES, depending on each country's banking requirements. Applicants REGISTER their COLLECTIVE OR ORGANIZATION IN OUR ONLINE SYSTEM and make the request through it. Two weeks from request to money. When a defender has to leave home tonight or a hearing is next month, that is the only timescale in this file that matches the emergency. WHAT IT PAYS AND FOR HOW LONG: the support comprises FLEXIBLE RESOURCES (UP TO AN ALLOCATION OF 5,000 DOLLARS), GRANTED TO SUPPORT THE ACTIVISTS AND THEIR ORGANISATIONS IN A STRATEGIC AND TIMELY MANNER IN THE FACE OF UNFORESEEN AND UNPLANNED SITUATIONS THAT REQUIRE AN IMMEDIATE INTERVENTION, for a maximum of three months; THESE ACTIONS CANNOT BE ACTIVITIES OF PROGRAMMES AND/OR PROJECTS, and applicants MUST DEMONSTRATE THE URGENT CHARACTER OF THE UNFORESEEN AND UNPLANNED SITUATION. It will not pay for anything already in your workplan. Frame the request around what changed this month — the threat, the eviction date, the hearing — and nothing else. THE SECOND WINDOW, WHICH IS ABOUT TERRITORY: alongside the rapid grants the fund gives STRATEGIC SUPPORTS: TO STRENGTHEN THE PROCESSES OF RESISTANCE AND THE STRATEGIES OF THE ORGANISATIONS LED BY WOMEN, TRANS, NON-BINARY OR GENDER-DISSIDENT PEOPLE, THAT PROMOTE IN AN INTEGRATED MANNER THE PROTECTION OF THE TERRITORIES, THE COMMON GOODS AND THE RIGHTS; one recorded call was directed at LOCAL, DEPARTMENTAL OR NATIONAL ORGANISATIONS AND COLLECTIVES OF WOMEN AND/OR FEMINISTS THAT HAVE PERMANENT WORK AROUND THE DEFENCE OF THE TERRITORIES AND NATURE, and at MIXED COMMUNITY, INDIGENOUS, AFRO-DESCENDANT, RAIZAL AND PEASANT ORGANISATIONS THAT HAVE A SPECIFIC LINE OF WORK ON WOMEN'S RIGHTS LINKED TO ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE, AND IN WHICH WOMEN HAVE SIGNIFICANT LEADERSHIP. Mixed community, indigenous and peasant organisations qualify for the territorial window, not only women's organisations, provided women lead a strand of the work. That is a wider door than the fund's name suggests. WHO IT IS AND WHERE IT REACHES: it is THE REGIONAL FEMINIST FUND FOR SPANISH-SPEAKING LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, created in 2009 in one national capital as part of a global urgent action fund founded in 1997 that regionalised IN ORDER TO UNDERSTAND LOCAL CONTEXTS BETTER AND TO BE CLOSER TO THE WORK SITES OF GRASSROOTS ACTIVISTS, now AN INTERNATIONAL ALLIANCE OF THREE AUTONOMOUS SISTER FUNDS. Spanish-speaking countries only for this fund. If you are in Brazil, Guyana, Suriname, Haiti or the English-speaking Caribbean, ask which sister fund covers you before applying. WHAT IT FUNDS THE MONEY FOR: recorded lines are PROTECTION AND SECURITY, RESPONDING TO SITUATIONS OF RISK OR THREAT AGAINST THE SECURITY OF ACTIVISTS AND DEFENDERS, THEIR COLLECTIVES OR ORGANISATIONS, and opportunity grants that let a movement act before a window closes. Security costs — relocation, a lawyer's retainer, travel to a hearing — are exactly what this covers, and they are the costs that no project grant in this file will pay.

trackers.name: Protection grants for defenders at risk - up to €7,500 for LEGAL FEES OF THOSE BEING JUDICIALLY HARASSED, physical and digital security, medical and family costs, with a 24-hour hotline, plus emergency, relocation, trial-monitoring and respite programmes
trackers.desc: THESE GRANTS PAY THE LEGAL FEES OF SOMEONE BEING SUED OR PROSECUTED FOR DEFENDING LAND. The protection grants programme, launched in 2001 TO PROVIDE RAPID AND PRACTICAL FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS AT RISK, pays for IMPROVING PHYSICAL SECURITY OF AN ORGANISATION OR INDIVIDUAL, DIGITAL SECURITY AND COMMUNICATION SECURITY; SUPPORTING LEGAL FEES FOR HRDs WHO ARE BEING JUDICIALLY HARASSED; PAYING FOR MEDICAL FEES FOR HRDs WHO HAVE BEEN ATTACKED OR WHO HAVE SUFFERED A MEDICAL CONDITION AS A RESULT OF THEIR PEACEFUL HUMAN RIGHTS ACTIVITIES; PROVIDING FAMILY ASSISTANCE FOR IMPRISONED HRDs OR FAMILY MEMBERS WHO ARE AT RISK BECAUSE OF A HRD'S ACTIVITIES, up to a maximum of €7,500. Applications CAN BE SUBMITTED ANYTIME VIA THEIR ONLINE SYSTEM, and there is a 24-HOUR EMERGENCY HOTLINE. A criminal complaint or a defamation suit filed by a developer is judicial harassment, and the legal fees are payable. That is the single most common attack on land defenders in this file, and this is the grant written for it. WHAT IT WILL NOT FUND, WHICH DECIDES HOW YOU WRITE IT: the programme excludes RETROSPECTIVE FUNDING, INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS, ORGANISATIONS THAT HAVE APPLIED OR ARE ALREADY RECEIVING FUNDING FOR THE SAME PURPOSE ELSEWHERE, PROJECTS WHICH FOCUS ON BROADER HUMAN RIGHTS ISSUES RATHER THAN THE SPECIFIC SITUATION OF HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, COSTS FOR HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS WHO ARE ALREADY IN EXILE and ongoing office running costs; grants ARE GENERALLY NOT AWARDED FOR 100% OF THE PROPOSED BUDGET, and applicants must commit to return the grant if the work does not go ahead or is funded elsewhere. Write about the named people at risk, not about the campaign. A proposal that describes the environmental issue rather than the threat to specific defenders is refused on its own terms. THE OTHER EMERGENCY FUNDS THAT COVER THE SAME GROUND: a European defenders mechanism provides EMERGENCY GRANTS UP TO 10,000€ and runs a TEMPORARY RELOCATION PROGRAMME that funds a host organisation to relocate a defender, responding to AN INCREASED RISK, AN ANTICIPATED INCREASED RISK OR FOR A HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDER WHO HAS BEEN WORKING IN A DIFFICULT ENVIRONMENT FOR A PROLONGED PERIOD OF TIME AND WHO NEEDS A BREAK, covering REST AND RESPITE, PROFESSIONAL CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT... EMOTIONAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL WELL-BEING, FAMILY SUPPORT; a civil society lifeline fund covers LEGAL REPRESENTATION, PRISON VISITS, TRIAL MONITORING, TEMPORARY RELOCATION, EQUIPMENT REPLACEMENT, applying by email after describing a secure contact method, in several languages including Spanish; and a federation offers SECURE TRANSPORTATION, LEGAL SUPPORT, MEDICAL SUPPORT... HUMANITARIAN ASSISTANCE... URGENT RELOCATION, URGENT MONITORING. Trial monitoring is fundable, and so is a paid observer at the hearing. Where a case is being heard in a small town, an outside monitor changes how it is conducted. THE RESPITE OPTIONS WHEN SOMEONE MUST LEAVE: recorded schemes include a protective fellowship allowing UP TO TEN DEFENDERS PER YEAR to join a university centre FOR THE PURPOSES OF TRAINING, NETWORKING, AND REST, a foundation offering A YEAR LONG RESPITE PROGRAMME, a refuge for journalists forced to flee providing ADMINISTRATIVE, LEGAL AND SOCIAL ASSISTANCE, and a cities of refuge network offering PHYSICAL SAFETY AND ECONOMIC SECURITY FOR A TWO-YEARS FIXED PERIOD. Leaving for a year is not the end of a campaign if someone else can hold the file. Identify who that is before the threat arrives, because these programmes take applications from the person at risk and their host, not from a court. THE SECURITY WARNING BUILT INTO THE APPLICATION: applicants are asked to ENSURE THAT THE METHOD OF CONTACT YOU ARE PROVIDING IS SECURE AND THAT IT IS OK TO BE CONTACTED IN THAT WAY, and one fund asks applicants to describe HOW it CAN CONTACT YOU SECURELY BEFORE SENDING SENSITIVE INFORMATION. Do not send the details from a shared community email account. The application itself can expose the person it is meant to protect.

trackers.name: Inter-American Foundation grants - CURRENTLY PAUSED - direct grants of $25,000-$400,000 to grassroots organisations with no sector calls, no deadline, five application languages, and LAND AND LABOUR accepted as counterpart
trackers.desc: THIS FUNDER IS CURRENTLY PAUSED — CHECK BEFORE SPENDING TIME ON IT. Its own application page states: WE ARE CURRENTLY PAUSING GRANT FUNDING IN ALIGNMENT WITH EXECUTIVE ORDER REEVALUATING AND REALIGNING UNITED STATES FOREIGN AID. CHECK THIS PAGE FOR FURTHER UPDATES. It is AN INDEPENDENT AGENCY of that government. Everything below describes how it worked when open, and is recorded because the terms are unusual enough to be worth watching for. Read the page before writing anything. A funder under a foreign aid review can reopen with different rules, and the counterpart and eligibility terms are the first things such reviews change. WHY IT MATTERED: IT FUNDED GRASSROOTS GROUPS DIRECTLY, WITH NO INTERMEDIARY: it ONLY SUPPORT[S] COMMUNITY-LED PROJECTS SUBMITTED BY LOCAL AND GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS THAT ARE BASED IN INDEPENDENT COUNTRIES OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, requiring proof that YOUR ORGANIZATION HAS A HISTORY OF WORKING TOGETHER AS A GROUP AND IS CAPABLE OF EFFECTIVELY USING GRANTS FUNDS; it DOES NOT IDENTIFY PROBLEMS OR SUGGEST PROJECTS; INSTEAD IT RESPONDS TO INITIATIVES PRESENTED, and PROJECTS ARE SELECTED FOR FUNDING ON THEIR MERITS RATHER THAN BY SECTOR. Grants ran FROM US$25,000 TO $400,000 OVER ONE TO FOUR YEARS, with proposals accepted 365 DAYS A YEAR in SPANISH, PORTUGUESE, ENGLISH, FRENCH, OR HAITIAN CREOLE. No sector calls, no themes, no deadline. A community proposing its own solution in its own language is the entire model, and it is worth having a proposal ready if the pause lifts. THE COUNTERPART RULE, WHICH IS THE PART TO UNDERSTAND: all funded organisations must COMMIT RESOURCES TO ADVANCE THEIR DEVELOPMENT INITIATIVES, called counterpart; COUNTERPART FUNDING MUST BE A COMPONENT OF THE BUDGET... BUT NO MINIMUM AMOUNT IS REQUIRED. HIGHER COUNTERPART FUNDING MAKES A PROPOSAL MORE ATTRACTIVE, and it MAY BE IN CASH DONATIONS OR IN KIND, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, LAND, SUPPLIES, INFRASTRUCTURE, LABOR, AND OFFICE, STORAGE AND MEETING SPACE. Salaries are A LEGITIMATE EXPENSE. Land and volunteer labour count as counterpart. A community that owns the site and works it has already met the requirement without spending anything. WHAT IT LOOKED FOR IN A PROPOSAL: CREATIVE USE OF THE COMMUNITY'S RESOURCES; A DIVERSE ARRAY OF COMMUNITY VOICES IN PROJECT DEVELOPMENT AND EXECUTION; SUBSTANTIAL BENEFICIARY ENGAGEMENT in identifying the problem, choosing the approach, designing the project and managing it; PARTNERSHIPS WITH LOCAL GOVERNMENT, THE BUSINESS COMMUNITY AND OTHER CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS; feasibility, sustainability, measurable results and EVIDENCE OF BENEFICIARIES' ENHANCED CAPACITY FOR SELF-GOVERNANCE; its recorded interests included COMMUNITY CONSERVATION; AND LOCAL MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES (FORESTS, FISHERIES, ETC.). Partnership with the local government is a scoring criterion. That is the argument for bringing your municipality into the proposal rather than fighting it. THE EXCLUSIONS AND THE FIELD OFFICE RULE: support was limited to independent countries of the region, with recorded exclusions of two countries and a period when FUNDING IN THE CARIBBEAN was RESTRICTED TO three named states; public universities could not apply directly BUT MAY PARTNER WITH AN ORGANIZATION THAT IS ELIGIBLE; and an organisation headquartered abroad could apply only if its field office CAN DEMONSTRATE LOCAL LEADERSHIP. Local leadership had to be demonstrated, not asserted. Where an outside NGO offers to apply on your behalf, insist that your own organisation is the applicant.

trackers.name: RedLAC - the network of 32 national and regional ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS in 20 countries, permanent conservation trust institutions financing protected areas and local communities, with a published member list by country and zone
trackers.desc: THIRTY-TWO NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS IN TWENTY COUNTRIES, AND THE NETWORK PUBLISHES WHICH ONE COVERS YOURS. It GROUPS 32 ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS FROM 20 COUNTRIES OF THE REGION, UNITING EFFORTS TO PROTECT THE RICH BIODIVERSITY OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, with its member list filterable by zone — Caribbean, Mesoamerica and South America — alongside regional funds; more than twenty-five years old, it counts MORE THAN 100 ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS WORLDWIDE. Find the fund for your country on that member page. These are permanent national institutions with endowments, not project offices that close when a grant ends. WHAT THESE FUNDS DO, IN THE NETWORK'S WORDS: they HAVE DEMONSTRATED TO BE A KEY MECHANISM IN THE SUSTAINABLE FINANCING OF BIODIVERSITY AND IN THE STRENGTHENING OF PROTECTED AREAS AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, with a role in THE PROTECTION OF NATURAL AREAS AND THE SUPPORT TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES, described as MULTIDIMENSIONAL FUNDS, WITH APPROACHES THAT INTEGRATE PROTECTION OF BIODIVERSITY, CLIMATIC RESILIENCE AND COMMUNITY EMPOWERMENT. Support to local communities is named alongside protected areas. A community managing land next to a park is inside the mandate, not adjacent to it. SOME OF THE MEMBERS BY NAME AND KIND: recorded members include a Caribbean biodiversity fund, a national forever-protection association in one Central American country, an action fund and a Pacific foundation in one Andean country, a nature fund in one southern country, an island life fund and a regional marine fund — the last two showing that funds exist for a single archipelago and for a shared sea as well as for whole countries. There are funds scoped to one archipelago and to one reef system. If your site sits in either, that narrower fund is a better fit than the national one. WHAT THE NETWORK ITSELF OFFERS ITS MEMBERS: joining gives funds THE OPPORTUNITY TO CONNECT AND COLLABORATE WITH OTHER MEMBERS OF THE NETWORK THROUGHOUT THE REGION, to SHARE KNOWLEDGE, RESOURCES AND EXPERIENCES TO IMPROVE THEIR CAPACITIES, and ACCESS TO A WIDE VARIETY OF RESOURCES AND TOOLS, with TRAINING AND ADVICE ON DIVERSE THEMES, FROM PROJECT MANAGEMENT TO COMMUNICATION AND ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION. Where your country has no environmental fund, this network is where one would be built, and it trains new members. That is a long project, but it is the route. WHY THEY MATTER FOR PERMANENT PROTECTION: these funds are conservation trust funds — institutions holding capital whose returns finance protected areas and community work year after year, and the network works alongside a global environment facility, an African funds consortium and a large conservation finance initiative on that model. An endowment pays for wardens and monitoring long after a campaign ends. Where a protected area has just been declared, the next question is which of these funds can endow its running costs.

trackers.name: The ICCA Consortium and the international register of territories of life - a community-reviewed register open to any well-defined community with its own governance, plus national catalytic organisations, documentation workshops and life plan support
trackers.desc: A COMMUNITY CAN PUT ITS OWN TERRITORY ON AN INTERNATIONAL REGISTER, REVIEWED BY OTHER COMMUNITIES RATHER THAN BY OFFICIALS. The international register IS A TOOL DEVELOPED TO SERVE AS SUPPORT AND RECOGNITION TO THOSE COMMUNITIES WITH OUTSTANDING VALUES IN GOVERNANCE AND CONSERVATION OF NATURE, run by a United Nations environment body with the consortium and a commons organisation; its PEER REVIEW PROTOCOL is A CONSENSUS DOCUMENT IN WHICH THE DIFFERENT STEPS THAT EACH COMMUNITY MUST TAKE IN ORDER TO FORM PART OF THE REGISTER ARE DESCRIBED, including SUBMITTING TO A PROCESS OF REVIEW OF THE CANDIDATURE BY ANONYMOUS MEMBERS (REVIEWERS) OF OTHER SIMILAR COMMUNITIES THAT ALREADY FORM PART OF THE REGISTER. Other communities judge the application, and the protocol is published so you can read the test before applying. Registration is a public record of who governs the land, made without asking the state's permission. WHAT QUALIFIES AS ONE OF THESE TERRITORIES: they exist IN ANY TYPE OF CULTURE AND ECOSYSTEM WHERE THERE IS A COMMUNITY LINKED TO A TERRITORY, WITH ITS OWN SYSTEM OF GOVERNANCE, AND THAT GIVES POSITIVE RESULTS IN TERMS OF CONSERVATION OF NATURE AND LIVELIHOODS FOR THE COMMUNITY; the first defining characteristic is that THE AREA OR TERRITORY MUST HAVE A WELL DEFINED COMMUNITY, WITH A CLEAR LINK TO A TERRITORY ALSO WELL DEFINED. A well defined community and a well defined territory. Neither a formal title nor a state designation is in that test. WHO THE CONSORTIUM IS AND WHAT ITS MEMBERS DO: it is AN INTERNATIONAL NON-PROFIT ASSOCIATION DEDICATED TO SUPPORTING INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES THAT GOVERN AND CONSERVE THEIR LANDS, WATERS AND TERRITORIES, its members from more than eighty countries acting on themes including THE DOCUMENTATION, SUSTAINING AND DEFENCE OF THE TERRITORIES OF LIFE, and comprising ALMOST 180 MEMBERS (ORGANISATIONS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND COMMUNITY ORGANISATIONS, TOGETHER WITH THE CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS THAT SUPPORT THEM) AND MORE THAN 420 HONORARY MEMBERS. Community organisations are members in their own right, alongside the NGOs that support them. Ask the national focal point how your organisation joins. WHAT THE REGIONAL NETWORK ACTUALLY DELIVERS: the Latin American network runs workshops WITH THE AIM OF SHARING KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERIENCES COMING FROM THE TERRITORIES, including a practical workshop on the register itself, a case study workshop drawing on one country's experience, and one on a GUIDE OF SELF-STRENGTHENING: A GUIDE FROM COMMUNITIES FOR COMMUNITIES; communities are recorded pursuing PROCESSES OF DOCUMENTATION, THE CONSTRUCTION OF LIFE PLANS, THE register AND THE STRENGTHENING OF THEIR OWN GOVERNANCE. A life plan is the document that states what a community will and will not permit on its land. Building one is the work these workshops exist to support. WHAT IT HAS SUPPORTED ON THE GROUND: in one country an observatory and a named indigenous community organised A WORKSHOP OF EXCHANGE OF KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERIENCES, ATTENDED BY TWENTY-FIVE REPRESENTATIVES OF TEN INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, TO EXCHANGE ABOUT LEGAL AND NON-LEGAL STRATEGIES OF TERRITORIAL DEFENCE AND PROTECTION; in another, five indigenous peoples, an Afro-descendant community and a coastal community met with a foundation and the small grants programme TO DEBATE AND DECIDE ON THE WORLD REGISTER; national members have planned A STUDY OF THE EXISTING LEGAL FRAMEWORK ON CONSERVATION AND RIGHTS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, ACTIONS FOR COMMUNITY STRENGTHENING AND A NATIONAL ADVOCACY STRATEGY; a global support initiative works through NATIONAL CATALYTIC ORGANISATIONS in more than twenty-six priority countries. Ask which organisation is the national catalytic body for your country. It is the one already funded to accompany communities through documentation and registration.

trackers.name: Mapeo and its successor - a free, offline, open-source mapping and evidence toolset built with Amazonian indigenous partners, where ALL DATA IS OWNED BY THE COMMUNITY, exporting shapefiles and reports for lawsuits and land claims
trackers.desc: A FREE OFFLINE APP THAT TURNS A PHONE INTO AN EVIDENCE RECORDER, AND THE COMMUNITY KEEPS THE DATA. It is A FREE DIGITAL TOOLSET FOR DOCUMENTING, MONITORING, AND MAPPING MANY TYPES OF DATA, OFFLINE-FIRST OPEN-SOURCE TECHNOLOGY needing NO INTERNET OR SPECIAL HARDWARE... TO COLLECT, VIEW, OR SHARE DATA; WITH THE PUSH OF A BUTTON, CONTRIBUTORS CAN GATHER MAP DATA BY LINKING GPS POINTS, PHOTOS, AND NOTES, and ALL DATA IS COMPLETELY OWNED BY THE COMMUNITIES THEMSELVES, exchanged between phones by a peer-to-peer sync that works OVER A LOCAL WIFI NETWORK WITHOUT NEEDING A CONNECTION. No signal, no server, no subscription, and nobody else holds the file. For a community watching a road survey or a clearing crew, that is the difference between a rumour and an exhibit. WHAT IT WAS BUILT TO BE USED FOR: it was CO-DESIGNED AND DEVELOPED WITH INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES WHO FACE THREATS TO THEIR LAND SUCH AS ILLEGAL GOLD MINING, OIL CONTAMINATION AND POACHING, and built TO SUPPORT THEM TO DOCUMENT THESE ACTIVITIES IN ORDER TO TAKE COMMUNITY ACTION AGAINST THEM, TO REPORT THEM TO AUTHORITIES, FILE LAWSUITS, LAUNCH MEDIA CAMPAIGNS, OR CREATE MAPS FOR LAND CLAIMS; it allows USERS TO COLLECT EVIDENCE IN THE FIELD, SUCH AS PHOTOGRAPHS AND GPS POINTS, AND ORGANIZE THIS DATA FOR ACTIONS SUCH AS WHISTLEBLOWING AND CLAIMING LAND RIGHTS. Filing a lawsuit and making a map for a land claim are the stated purposes. Set up the categories to match what a court or a ministry will ask for, before the incursion happens. THE CASE THAT SHOWS WHAT IT IS WORTH: in one country OVER TWENTY indigenous COMMUNITIES DEFENDED THEIR TERRITORY... AGAINST THE IMPOSITION OF DEVASTATING OIL EXPLORATION PROPOSED BY THE GOVERNMENT, having USED the tool FOR OVER FOUR YEARS TO RECORD TERRITORIAL DATA ...AND MAPS, WHICH THEY USED AS EVIDENCE AGAINST THE government; the account records: THEY WON! Four years of routine recording before the case existed. The evidence that wins these cases is gathered long before anyone knows there will be a case. WHAT COMES OUT OF IT, AND IN WHICH LANGUAGES: export options include PDF OR PRINT REPORT, GEOJSON, CSV OR SHAPEFILE from the desktop version and direct sharing from the phone; the interface IS AVAILABLE IN LOCAL LANGUAGES, AND ALSO HAS AN IN-BUILT TRANSLATION FEATURE, supporting THE UNDERSERVED DIALECTS OF INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES; one community leader records that IT IS SO EASY TO USE THAT EVEN OUR ELDERS — WHO DO NOT SPEAK SPANISH — USE IT. A newer version adds audio, tracks and routes. A shapefile is what a planning office and a court will accept. Elders who do not speak the national language can gather it themselves, which also answers the objection that the data was collected by outsiders. THE SUPPORT AROUND THE TOOL: the developers publish TRAINING AND TECHNICAL RESOURCES, a COMPLETE REFERENCE GUIDE... ON PLANNING AND IMPLEMENTING PROJECTS and customisation of the tools, and a defenders toolkit site; a dedicated version was built with a United Nations monitoring centre and a forest peoples organisation so that custodian communities can MAP, MONITOR AND SUPPORT THEIR TERRITORIES OF LIFE ON THEIR TERMS and may, SHOULD THEY WISH TO, CONTRIBUTE TO GLOBAL CONSERVATION DATABASES. Contributing to the global database is optional and separate. Decide as a community what stays local before the first survey, because that choice is hard to reverse once data is shared.

trackers.name: Global Forest Watch - free near-real-time deforestation alerts by email for any drawn area, an offline field app that walks patrols to the clearing, and a small grants fund whose examples include GETTING CONCESSIONS REVOKED and compiling evidence for formal complaints
trackers.desc: YOU CAN SUBSCRIBE TO EMAIL ALERTS FOR A SINGLE PLOT OF FOREST AND BE TOLD WITHIN DAYS WHEN TREES ARE CUT. The platform is FREE AND SIMPLE TO USE, ENABLING ANYONE TO CREATE CUSTOM MAPS, ANALYZE FOREST TRENDS, SUBSCRIBE TO ALERTS, OR DOWNLOAD DATA FOR THEIR LOCAL AREA OR THE ENTIRE WORLD, providing NEAR-REAL-TIME ALERTS SHOWING SUSPECTED LOCATIONS OF RECENT TREE COVER LOSS; it moved BEYOND ANNUAL DATA ON FORESTS to MONTHLY AND WEEKLY DEFORESTATION ALERTS, with EMAIL SUBSCRIPTIONS bringing them DIRECTLY INTO THE HANDS OF USERS. Users CAN SIGN UP FOR ALERTS AND DOWNLOAD DATASETS WITHOUT ANY SUBSCRIPTION OR LICENSING FEE. Draw the boundary of the land you are defending and subscribe. From then on the clearing tells you rather than the other way round, and the date stamp is independent of anything the developer says. THE FIELD APP THAT WORKS WITHOUT SIGNAL: a companion mobile application ALLOWS RANGERS TO ACCESS the data and alerts OFFLINE, WHICH IS CRITICAL IN AREAS WITH LIMITED TO NO CELL SIGNAL; USING CACHED DATA, THE APP DIRECTS USERS TO NEARBY FOREST CLEARING AND ENABLES THEM TO CAPTURE PHOTOS AND FILL OUT FORMS ABOUT DEFORESTATION, WHICH ARE UPLOADED NEXT TIME THEIR DEVICE CONNECTS, so that patrols KNOW EXACTLY WHERE TO LOOK... AND STOP THE ILLEGAL ACTIVITY BEFORE IT GETS OUT OF CONTROL; it is FREE, OPEN SOURCE, AND AVAILABLE IN ENGLISH, SPANISH, PORTUGUESE, FRENCH, AND BAHASA INDONESIAN. The alert gives the coordinates and the app walks you to them. A ground photograph taken at a satellite-flagged point, on a known date, is the evidence a prosecutor can use. THE GRANT ATTACHED TO IT, AND WHAT IT HAS PAID FOR: a small grants fund SEEKS TO BUILD THE CAPACITY OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS TO EFFECTIVELY USE the tools TO REDUCE ILLEGAL OR UNPLANNED DEFORESTATION; funded project types include USING DATA AND IMAGERY... ALONGSIDE COMMUNITY TERRITORIAL MAPS TO ADVOCATE FOR LAND TITLES AND OTHER STRENGTHENED LAND RIGHTS; CROWDSOURCING, COMPILING AND PUBLISHING DATA ON CONCESSIONS THAT OVERLAP WITH ANCESTRAL COMMUNITY LANDS, AND SUPPORT COMMUNITIES IN APPLYING PUBLIC PRESSURE TO GET THESE CONCESSIONS REVOKED; DEVELOPING THE CAPACITY OF FOREST MONITORING BRIGADES TO CONDUCT FIELD VERIFICATIONS OF NEAR-REAL TIME ALERTS; and SUPPORTING INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES IN DEVELOPING RESPONSE PROTOCOLS, FORMULATING LEGAL STRATEGIES AND COMPILING EVIDENCE OF ILLEGAL DEFORESTATION INCLUDING SATELLITE IMAGERY, DATA AND ANALYSES, AND SUBMITTING IT TO LAW ENFORCEMENT THROUGH FORMAL COMPLAINTS OR OTHER LEGAL PROCESSES. Getting concessions revoked and compiling evidence for formal complaints are funded project types, written into the fund's own examples. THE DEADLINE DISCIPLINE: the fund runs an annual call, and the platform states of a recent round: THE CALL FOR APPLICATIONS HAS CLOSED AS OF THE DEADLINE... WE CANNOT GRANT ANY EXTENSIONS, advising applicants to PREPARE FOR THE NEXT CALL FOR APPLICATIONS BY REVIEWING the current materials, while noting that SOME ITEMS IN THE GUIDELINES FOR APPLICANTS MAY CHANGE YEAR TO YEAR. One deadline a year, strictly enforced. Download this year's guidelines now and write the proposal before the next call opens. WHO ELSE IS ALREADY USING IT: the platform serves GOVERNMENTS, THE PRIVATE SECTOR, NGOs, JOURNALISTS, UNIVERSITIES, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC, and is convened as a partnership of OVER 200 ORGANIZATIONS; a fellowship accompanies the grants. Your municipality and your national forest agency can subscribe to the same alerts you do. Sending them the alert with a covering letter turns your observation into their file.

trackers.name: Public Lab and the open science hardware community - free open-source, low-cost instruments and toolkits communities build themselves for water, air, soil and land use, plus BALLOON AND KITE AERIAL MAPPING with stitching software and an open question forum
trackers.desc: THE INSTRUMENTS ARE OPEN SOURCE AND CHEAP ENOUGH THAT A COMMUNITY CAN BUILD ITS OWN, INCLUDING AERIAL PHOTOGRAPHY FROM A KITE. RANGING FROM WATER QUALITY SENSORS TO INDOOR AIR QUALITY AND KITE MAPPING KITS; its tools and data are CREATED BY THE community, OPEN SOURCE, AND TYPICALLY INEXPENSIVE TO USE. Its earliest technique was LOW-ALTITUDE AERIAL MAPPING WITH BALLOONS AND KITES with software to stitch the photographs into a map. That is how you show what a hillside looked like before the machines arrived. Before, during and after is the sequence that wins arguments about damage. Start the baseline photographs now, while there is still a before. WHAT THE PLATFORM ACTUALLY GIVES YOU: it is A PLATFORM FOR COMMUNITY SCIENCE PRACTITIONERS WORKING ON ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES TO DOCUMENT THEIR WORK, SHARE TOOLS FOR ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING AND ADVOCACY, AND CONNECT WITH EACH OTHER; THE COMMUNITY IS OPEN AND FREE FOR ANYONE TO JOIN, members CAN ADD THEIR OWN PROJECT PAGE TO DOCUMENT THEIR METHODS AND SHARE EXPERTISE, and users CAN BROWSE LOW-COST ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING TOOLS FOR APPLICATION AREAS SUCH AS AIR QUALITY, LAND USE, STORMWATER, alongside ADVOCACY METHODS, AND ACTION TOOLKITS BY SCIENCE TOPICS covering WATER, SOIL, AIR, INDUSTRY, CLIMATE, ORGANIZING, AND MONITORING; COMMUNITY MEMBERS CAN ASK OR ANSWER QUESTIONS. Post the question with your site's details. Somebody has usually measured the same pollutant with the same cheap instrument and will say what went wrong the first time. THE KINDS OF INSTRUMENT PEOPLE HAVE BUILT: recorded tools include a spectrometer made from LEGO OR CARDBOARD, WEBCAMS OR RASPBERRY PI CAMERAS, RECYCLED DVDs so that SPECTROSCOPY IS A RESEARCH METHOD THAT ANYONE CAN EXPLORE; a SIMPLE AIR SENSOR whose REALTIME READOUT CHANGES COLOR WHEN THE SENSOR READS DIFFERENCES IN AIR QUALITY, usable WITHOUT HAVING TO LEARN HOW TO PROGRAM; a low-budget water kit with probes MEASURING TEMPERATURE, DISSOLVED OXYGEN AND CONDUCTIVITY, developed to measure sewage outfalls after storms; a DIY device to TEST FOR HEAVY METALS IN WATER; DIY infrared cameras; and a marine microplastics trawler. Dissolved oxygen, conductivity and heavy metals are the readings that show a river has been damaged. A community that takes them weekly for a year has a record no consultant's single sample can rebut. WHAT THE WIDER COMMUNITY ADDS: a water data collaborative HELPS GUIDE COMMUNITY GROUPS ON HOW TO ADOPT DIY, OPEN HARDWARE METHODS FOR COLLECTING THE QUALITY OF WATER DATA THEY NEED TO ACHIEVE THEIR OUTCOMES, alongside research centres publishing open hardware loggers, and an annual gathering for open science hardware makes tools ACCESSIBLE THROUGH OPEN-SOURCE LICENSING; recorded projects include WATER MONITORING IN THE AMAZON. Decide what outcome the data is for before choosing the instrument. A reading that will go to a court needs a different protocol from one that will go to a public meeting, and these groups will tell you which.

ARE BOTH FROM AND IN LATIN AMERICA and UNDERSTAND THE LEGAL AND POLITICAL CONTEXT OF THE REGION BECAUSE they WERE BORN AND LIVE IN LATIN AMERICA. It has MORE THAN 25 YEARS OF EXPERIENCE. International human rights law applied to a local environmental case. Where the national courts have closed, that is the route this organisation was built to open. Its method is to work through a national organisation rather than around it. Approach it together with the environmental lawyers already in your country, which makes acceptance more likely. WHO IT IS AND WHERE ITS PARTNERS ARE: founded in 1998 by five environmental law groups from four Latin American countries and one northern one TO BUILD AND EXTEND THE CAPACITIES OF NATIONAL DEFENDERS, it WORKS WITH PARTNERS IN COUNTRIES SUCH AS ARGENTINA, CANADA, CHILE, COLOMBIA, COSTA RICA, ECUADOR, MEXICO AND PERU, with recorded legal work also in Brazil; it is a member of an international land coalition. Ask which national organisation is its partner in your country. That is the door, and the partner list is published by the coalitions it belongs to. THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT, IMPLEMENTATION AND EFFECTIVE ENFORCEMENT OF NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL LAW, and it seeks to ensure that INTERNATIONAL POLICIES, LAWS AND FINANCIAL FLOWS CONTRIBUTE TO THE PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT; it runs legal internships placing law students on country work. Financial flows are named among its targets. Where a project depends on an international bank or investor, that is a second front this organisation already works on.

trackers.name: Accountability Counsel - free support for communities complaining to the accountability offices of banks financing a harmful project, taking cases ONLY WHERE THE COMMUNITY ASKS, plus a searchable global complaints database and a resource guide

IS PERPETUATED BY THE STATE IN ALLIANCE WITH THE CORPORATIONS WITH INTEREST IN THEIR TERRITORIES, and another with AN ALARMING DISPOSSESSION OF LANDS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND AFRO-DESCENDANT COMMUNITIES, BECAUSE OF THE EXPANSION OF THE AGRICULTURAL FRONTIER. An independent index that contradicts the government's own monitoring, country by country. Quote your country's score back at the ministry that claims consultation works. THE LAND DEAL DATABASE AND ITS REGIONAL FOCAL POINT: a global land acquisitions observatory names a regional focal point organisation for Latin America and coordinates national pilot land observatories in several countries with the coalition. If a large land acquisition has been announced near you, check whether it is already recorded there — and if it is not, the focal point is who records it. WHAT ITS OWN ANALYSIS SAYS ABOUT THIS REGION: land IS AT THE CENTRE OF DIVERSE CONFLICTS IN THE REGION, WHERE THE HIGHEST NUMBER OF ATTACKS AGAINST THE PEOPLE WHO DEFEND IT IS RECORDED, LINKED IN GREAT MEASURE TO THE EXTRACTIVE INDUSTRIES; the coalition works THROUGH THE PROMOTION OF REGIONAL PLATFORMS AND NATIONAL COALITIONS... SO THAT THE WOMEN, MEN AND COMMUNITIES WHO LIVE ON AND FROM THE LAND HAVE DECISION-MAKING POWER OVER THEIR LANDS AND TERRITORIES. The region with the most attacks on land defenders is the one you are in. Read this entry with the protection funds and the pro bono routes already filed.

trackers.name: Rainforest Foundation US - land titling accelerated with regional government agrarian offices (75,000 acres for 20 communities in months), 400+ trained and financed community patrollers monitoring 19.6M acres, and support to strengthen organisations' capacity to manage funds
trackers.desc: WHAT HISTORICALLY TOOK YEARS WAS DONE IN MONTHS: TWENTY COMMUNITIES TITLED 75,000 ACRES IN ONE INITIATIVE. The foundation records that, working IN CLOSE PARTNERSHIP with a national indigenous federation and a regional government agrarian directorate, it WAS ABLE TO SIGNIFICANTLY ACCELERATE THE TITLING PROCESS, MEANING WHAT HISTORICALLY TOOK YEARS WAS ACCOMPLISHED IN JUST MONTHS; through that initiative 20 COMMUNITIES... SECURED LEGAL TITLES IN RECORD TIME FOR 75,000 ACRES OF THEIR ANCESTRAL LANDS, and in another year SIXTEEN INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES it supported RECEIVED LEGAL TITLE TO THEIR ANCESTRAL LANDS; separately it supported titling initiatives AIMING TO SECURE LAND TENURE FOR MORE THAN 11M ACRES ACROSS three countries and advanced tenure security for NEARLY 300,000 ACRES with two peoples in another. Titling accelerated by working with the regional government office that issues the titles, not around it. That is the partnership shape to copy. THE MODEL, STEP BY STEP: its PROVEN LAND-TITLING MODEL is that COMMUNITIES MAP THEIR ANCESTRAL BOUNDARIES, STRENGTHEN THEIR GOVERNANCE, AND USE REAL-TIME MONITORING TOOLS... TO DETECT THREATS; INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS, FEDERATIONS, REGIONAL GOVERNMENTS and the foundation HAVE JOINED FORCES TO MAP AND TITLE INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' LANDS. Mapping, governance and monitoring are done together rather than in sequence. A community that starts mapping while its governance documents are weak will stall at the titling office. THE MONITORING PROGRAMME AND ITS SCALE: it has TRAINED AND FINANCED OVER 400 COMMUNITY-BASED PATROLLERS TO MONITOR AND PROTECT 19.6 MILLION ACRES OF THEIR LANDS ACROSS four countries, using a programme in which INDIGENOUS FOREST MONITORS USE SMARTPHONES, SATELLITE IMAGERY, AND DRONES TO DETECT THREATS AND PREVENT DEFORESTATION against ILLEGAL LOGGING, MINING, AND CRIMINAL ACTIVITY; an earlier year recorded 307 COMMUNITY-BASED FOREST PATROLLERS ACROSS 129 COMMUNITIES. In one country it supports AROUND 114 INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, FIVE INDIGENOUS FEDERATIONS, AND ONE REGIONAL INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' ORGANISATION to run it. Patrollers are trained and paid. Community monitoring fails when it depends on volunteers, and this programme treats it as work. THE MONEY IT MOVES TO COMMUNITIES: it UNLOCKED OVER $10.5 MILLION IN FUNDING FROM AROUND THE WORLD TO FUEL INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES' FOREST PROTECTION WORK in one year, and supports partners to STRENGTHEN ORGANIZATIONAL GOVERNANCE AND THEIR CAPACITY TO MANAGE FUNDS AND PROJECTS FOR THE COMMUNITY'S BENEFIT; its forward plan is to STRENGTHEN 67 INDIGENOUS AND LOCAL ORGANIZATIONS AND INCREASE THEIR ACCESS TO FUNDING. Capacity to manage funds is what unlocks direct financing. Ask for that support before asking for a grant, because the audit trail is what most community organisations lack. WHO IT WORKS THROUGH, AND THE DEFENDER RISK: its named partners include a Central American regional forest peoples alliance, a national umbrella organisation of one large country's indigenous peoples, a district council representing one people, and two national congresses representing peoples inside and outside a comarca; it records that THE AMAZON IS THE MOST DANGEROUS REGION IN THE WORLD FOR ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDERS and collaborates with a national federation TO IMPLEMENT PREVENTIVE MEASURES, ENABLING COMMUNITIES TO BE BETTER PREPARED AGAINST THESE THREATS. It works through representative organisations, not with communities directly. Approach through your federation or council — and note that it also plans titling for communities next to territories reserved for peoples in voluntary isolation, to build a protection corridor.

trackers.name: Business & Human Rights Resource Centre - invites companies to answer a community's allegation and PUBLISHES THE NON-RESPONSE on the company's own page, with regional researchers, investor escalation and published policy and benchmark data on 10,000+ companies
trackers.desc: A COMPANY'S REFUSAL TO ANSWER A COMMUNITY'S ALLEGATION IS ITSELF PUBLISHED, ON ITS OWN PAGE. The centre INVITE[S] COMPANIES TO RESPOND TO ALLEGATIONS OF MISCONDUCT AND PUBLISH[ES] THEIR COMMENTS, doing so WHEN WE FIND NO EVIDENCE THAT THEY HAVE OTHERWISE RESPONDED TO THE CONCERNS; the process ENCOURAGES COMPANIES TO PUBLICLY ADDRESS HUMAN RIGHTS CONCERNS, AND PROVIDES THE PUBLIC WITH BOTH THE ALLEGATIONS AND THE COMPANY'S COMMENTS. It states plainly: WE INDICATE RESPONSE RATES IN THE COMPANY SECTIONS OF THE SITE, and IF A COMPANY IS LISTED AS HAVING FAILED TO RESPOND TO A PARTICULAR ALLEGATION, BUT IT HAS IN FACT ISSUED A RESPONSE... PLEASE LET US KNOW. A permanent public record that the company was asked and said nothing. For a developer that presents itself as responsible to lenders and buyers, that line on its own page is a cost. THE SCALE AND WHO DOES THE ASKING: it collects evidence on MORE THAN 10,000 COMPANIES IN MORE THAN 180 COUNTRIES and takes up ALLEGED ABUSE QUICKLY AND DIRECTLY WITH COMPANIES, INVITING THEM TO RESPOND TO SPECIFIC ALLEGATIONS (OVER 1,500 PER YEAR); a network of regional researchers BUILD LONG TERM RELATIONSHIPS WITH HUMAN RIGHTS ADVOCATES ON THE GROUND, BRINGING UNDERSTANDING OF THE DYNAMICS IN THE COUNTRIES THEY COVER, and WHERE THERE IS AN ALLEGATION OF CORPORATE HUMAN RIGHTS ABUSE THAT HAS NO PUBLIC RESPONSE, THEY REACH OUT TO THE COMPANY. Its site runs in several languages including Spanish and Portuguese. There is a researcher for your region who already knows the local advocates. Send the documented allegation to them rather than to a general address. WHAT IT DOES BEYOND PUBLISHING: its recorded practice is that DIALOGUES CAN EXTEND FURTHER AND OCCASIONALLY WE TAKE AN ACTIVE ROLE IN SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES AND NGOs; in one recorded case concerning an imprisoned indigenous leader who HAD LED THE OPPOSITION TO A PROPOSED... MINE IN HIS COMMUNITY'S TERRITORY, it POSTED THE ALLEGATIONS ON OUR WEBSITE AND SOUGHT RESPONSES FROM TWO COMPANIES WHO DID NOT RESPOND, AND ASSISTED THE LOCAL VILLAGERS IN SUBMITTING THE CASE TO THE UN SPECIAL REPRESENTATIVE ON HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, then CONTACTED PUBLIC INVESTORS... AND INVITED THEM TO COMMENT, of whom two responded and ONE COMMITTED TO RAISING THE ISSUE WITH ITS CLIENTS WHO ARE INVESTED in the company. Going up the chain to the investors is the step that moves a company. Identify who holds the shares or the loan before you send the allegation, and ask that they be invited to comment too. THE HONEST NUMBERS: the centre records a response rate averaging 43% on one page and 60% on another, and its own field acknowledges criticism about WEAK AND TANGENTIAL COMPANY RESPONSES and about the LACK OF REMEDY AND THE INEQUITY IN ARMS FOR THOSE AFFECTED BY ABUSE; a published analysis notes that A COMPANY RESPONSE TO A CRITICAL CIVIL SOCIETY REPORT IS NOT NECESSARILY A POSITIVE SIGN. Roughly half of companies answer, and an answer is not a remedy. Treat this as a public record and a pressure point, not as a complaint procedure that decides anything. WHAT IT ALSO PUBLISHES ON EACH COMPANY: company pages carry news, allegations, KEY DATA POINTS BASED ON CORPORATE POLICIES, AND SCORES FROM PROMINENT CIVIL SOCIETY BENCHMARKS, and its stated goals include a SAFE AND ENABLING ENVIRONMENT IN WHICH COMMUNITIES AND WORKERS CAN ADVOCATE FOR THEIR RIGHTS AND INTERESTS, INCLUDING THROUGH FREE AND FAIR NEGOTIATIONS. Read the company's page before your first meeting with it. Its own published policies and benchmark scores are the standard you can hold it to at the table.

trackers.name: Fundación Avina - a Latin American foundation with staff in up to 19 countries, six programmes including WATER and BIOMES, a record of SEED GRANTS to organisations that became leading deforestation monitors, and convening offered alongside money
trackers.desc: A FOUNDATION WITH STAFF LIVING IN NINETEEN LATIN AMERICAN COUNTRIES THAT HAS MOVED MORE THAN A BILLION DOLLARS THROUGH LOCAL ALLIES. It is A REGIONAL NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION WITH A MANDATE TO SUPPORT SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN THE LATIN AMERICAN REGION, whose activities cover ACCESS TO WATER AND ENERGY, RESOURCE MANAGEMENT and which works THROUGH A BROAD NETWORK OF GRASS-ROOTS AND COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS, NATIONAL AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS, THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY AND THE PRIVATE SECTOR; one account records 75 FULL-TIME STAFF MEMBERS BASED IN 19 COUNTRIES IN LATIN AMERICA and another 95 STAFF MEMBERS ACROSS 15 COUNTRIES, with OVER $500 MILLION ACROSS 13,000 INITIATIVES mobilised on one count and OVER USD 1.21 BILLION since 1994 on another. Staff who live in the country rather than visit it, and grant-making measured in thousands of small initiatives. Ask who the country contact is before writing to any regional address. THE PROGRAMME LIST THAT TELLS YOU WHERE A LAND CASE FITS: it works through SIX KEY PROGRAMS — CLIMATE, CIRCULAR ECONOMY, LABOR INNOVATION, BIOMES, DEMOCRACY, AND WATER, and elsewhere describes KEY AREAS INCLUDING CLIMATE ACTION, DEMOCRATIC STRENGTHENING, INCLUSIVE CIRCULAR ECONOMIES, BIOMES CONSERVATION, WATER MANAGEMENT, AND LABOR INNOVATION, with SUPPORT FOR LOCAL INITIATIVES. Biomes and water are separate programmes with their own staff. A watershed case goes to the water programme and a forest or savannah case to biomes — sending it to the wrong one is how a request gets lost. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DID FOR MONITORING ORGANISATIONS: a foundation officer records that in one phase it USED GRANTMAKING... TO MOBILIZE FUNDS WITH PARTNERS TO ORGANIZATIONS IN PAN-AMAZON, NOT ONLY IN THE BRAZILIAN AMAZON, WHICH IS OFTEN THE FOCUS, BUT THE PAN-AMAZON AND THE CHACO REGION, TO STRENGTHEN THEIR ABILITIES TO MONITOR DEFORESTATION, and that MANY OF THE ORGANIZATIONS THAT NOWADAYS ARE LEADING ORGANIZATIONS IN THIS AREA HAVE BEEN SUPPORTED AS A SEED GRANT. Seed grants to organisations that later became the leading monitors. If your group is at the beginning, that is the stage this foundation has repeatedly funded — and the Chaco, usually ignored beside the Amazon, is named.
