HOW IT DESCRIBES ITS OWN ROLE, WHICH SHAPES WHAT TO ASK FOR: it works AS A BROKER, CO-INVESTOR AND FACILITATOR, its PRIMARY CONTRIBUTION TO ITS ALLIES IS THE PROMOTION OF COLLABORATIVE ACTION THROUGH SERVICES AND FINANCIAL SUPPORT, and it BRINGS ITS ABILITIES AND RESOURCES TO THE TABLE AS A PEER INSTITUTION, providing ITS ABILITY, SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE, CONTACTS, RESOURCES, STRATEGIES, AND TOOLS TO WORK TOWARDS A COMMON CAUSE. Contacts and convening are offered alongside money. Where a case needs a mayor, a ministry and a company in one room, that is the service to ask for rather than a grant. THE UNITED STATES ENTITY, AND WHAT IT FUNDS: a separate United States non-profit MOBILIZES RESOURCES AND PARTNERSHIPS FROM THE UNITED STATES TO SUPPORT AND EXPAND THE IMPACT OF THIS MISSION and SUPPORTS INITIATIVES ALIGNED WITH THE FOUNDATION'S PRIORITIES ACROSS THREE INTERCONNECTED PILLARS... DEMOCRATIC INNOVATION, CLIMATE ACTION, AND A JUST AND REGENERATIVE ECONOMY, having COME TO EMBRACE FEMINIST PRINCIPLES THAT CENTER THE IMPORTANCE OF BUILDING COLLECTIVE POWER. Two legal entities, two funding routes. Which one can pay you depends on where your organisation is registered, so ask that first. THE HONEST NOTE ON ORIGIN AND COMPANY: it was FOUNDED IN 1994 BY a Swiss industrialist, is headquartered in one Central American capital with a northern office, works BY ENCOURAGING ALLIANCES BETWEEN SOCIAL AND BUSINESS LEADERS, and its recent activities include projects with a named water technology company in one country's semi-arid region. Its model is explicitly to put business leaders at the table with social ones. Decide whether that suits your fight before joining a programme, and read who co-funds it.

trackers.name: Protected area co-management by municipalities and NGOs in Honduras and El Salvador - a ten-area agreement signed by THIRTEEN TOWN HALLS, a park co-managed by three municipalities and the forest institute, and municipal accords bringing an ecological foundation in to run a park
trackers.desc: THIRTEEN TOWN HALLS SIGNED ONE CO-MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT FOR TEN PROTECTED AREAS, AND IN ANOTHER COUNTRY TWO MUNICIPALITIES BROUGHT AN NGO IN BY FORMAL RESOLUTION. In one country, a system was instituted BY THE SIGNING OF THE CO-MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT OF THE TEN PROTECTED AREAS OF THE GULF, SIGNED BETWEEN a flora and fauna defence committee, the state forestry administration AND THIRTEEN MUNICIPAL TOWN HALLS OF THE DEPARTMENTS OF two named regions; in another, two municipalities SUBSCRIBED THE DOCUMENT OF AGREEMENT OF TECHNICAL COOPERATION BETWEEN THE MUNICIPALITIES OF two named towns FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF THE PROTECTED NATURAL AREA, and in the same month EMITTED AN ACCORD TO GIVE PARTICIPATION TO a named ecological foundation FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND EXECUTION OF THE MENTIONED AGREEMENT AND TO FACILITATE THE PROCESS OF PLANNING, MANAGEMENT AND HANDLING of the park. An inter-municipal agreement first, then a separate accord bringing in the technical organisation. Two documents, both from the council chamber, and no land changes hands. WHO IS ELIGIBLE TO CO-MANAGE, WHICH IS BROADER THAN EXPECTED: a regional study of shared management records participation by ORGANISATIONS, GROUPS AND INSTITUTIONS CO-MANAGING IN THE COUNTRY, AMONG THEM MUNICIPALITIES, PEASANT GROUPS, INDIGENOUS GROUPS AND NGOs, and finds across the region AN UNEQUIVOCAL TENDENCY TOWARDS AN ACCELERATED GROWTH OF THE SHARED MANAGEMENT OF PROTECTED AREAS; another regional review tabulates co-management experiences country by country across seven countries plus one large neighbour. Peasant groups and municipalities co-manage protected areas alongside NGOs. If your community has no legal association yet, a town hall or an existing peasant group may be the eligible party. WHAT ONE AREA'S ARRANGEMENT LOOKS LIKE: a hill reserve spanning THREE MUNICIPALITIES is CO-MANAGED BY THE FOREST CONSERVATION INSTITUTE and THE THREE MUNICIPAL TOWN HALLS WITH INFLUENCE IN THE AREA; the ten-area gulf system connects BY EXTENSIVE WETLANDS AND MANGROVE ECOSYSTEMS with a central seat in one named town. Three town halls sharing one reserve, with the national institute. Where a hill or wetland straddles municipal boundaries, that is the standing arrangement to ask for by name. WHAT AN NGO GETS AND KEEPS: a ministry record lists four further similar agreements for named protected areas held by named associations, noting that of the initial NGOs three STILL REMAIN WITH PRESENCE IN THE AREA THROUGH AN AGREEMENT; instruments include AGREEMENTS OF TECHNICAL COOPERATION OR LETTERS OF UNDERSTANDING and LETTERS OF ENDORSEMENT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF PROJECTS IN PROTECTED AREAS, and the environment law ESTABLISHES THE JURIDICAL BASES FOR THE DELEGATION OF THE MANAGEMENT of protected areas by the state, with the number of organised civil society groups participating having increased. A letter of endorsement is what lets an outside organisation run a project inside a protected area. Ask which instrument your ministry issues, because the lightest one may be enough. THE COST THIS WORK HAS CARRIED, RECORDED PLAINLY: the director of one co-managing foundation WAS ASSASSINATED ON 6 FEBRUARY 1995 FOR HER EFFORTS TO PROTECT THE PARK AGAINST THE PALM PLANTATIONS IN THE REGION; the following month the park was added to an international wetlands list, it now bears her name, and THE PARK IS NOW ADMINISTERED BY THE same FOUNDATION. The foundation kept the co-management after its director was killed, and the park carries her name. Read this entry alongside the defender protection funds already filed before putting anyone's name on a public campaign.

trackers.name: Fundación Moisés Bertoni — reservas bajo dominio privado
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: works with landowners who want part of their property declared a private nature reserve recognised by the Paraguayan state, handling the technical justification, the declaration and the subsequent management. Private conservation became a formal category with the SINASIP in 1994; the Reserva Natural del Bosque Mbaracayú was created by Ley 112/91 as Paraguay's first private reserve, and Reserva Tapytá was recognised by Decreto 5831 of 2005 as protected in perpetuity. USE IT: to convert threatened Atlantic Forest, Cerrado or Chaco land into a declared reserve — the technical dossier is the bottleneck, and this is who writes it.

trackers.name: Guyra Paraguay — Conservación de Sitios
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: has been acquiring land for conservation in perpetuity since 2001 and now runs four conservation units, including the Guyra Retã complex of over 6,000 hectares inside the Tekoha Guasu / San Rafael national park reserve, Cañada El Carmen created by Ley 2073/05, Campo Iris and Tobich in the Chaco. Its private reserve category runs under Resolución SEAM 200 of 2001 within Ley 352/94 on protected areas. Critically, it buys land for Indigenous territorial reclamation as well as for conservation: in 2008 it bought 548 hectares in socio-environmental condominium under a deed committing it to cede the land outright after ten years, and in 2023 it transferred that title to the Mbya Guaraní community of Tapy Kanguekua–Arroyo Morotí. USE IT: where an Atlantic Forest or Chaco property is for sale over ancestral territory and the community needs a buyer that will hand the title on.

trackers.name: FAPI — Federación por la Autodeterminación de los Pueblos Indígenas
trackers.desc: An autonomous third-level Indigenous federation of 13 member organisations across both regions of Paraguay, registered since 2007 and recognised as a legitimate interlocutor before the Paraguayan state. Its most directly usable output is tierrasindigenas.org.py, the interactive platform it coordinates with UCINY, CLIBCH, Tierraviva, GAT and others, which maps Indigenous lands and territories against forest-change and fire data — most Indigenous territory is absent from official maps, so the platform exists to make it visible and to drive territorial restitution. Its member associations also drafted the national free, prior and informed consent protocol over nine years. WHO IT SUITS: Indigenous communities in Paraguay working through their own association — FAPI acts through its 13 members, not for individual claimants.

trackers.name: Contraloría General de la República
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Paraguay, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: DNCP – Contrataciones Públicas
trackers.desc: Paraguay's procurement agency, an open-contracting pioneer publishing all state tenders. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Paraguay, and for how much.

trackers.name: Administrative Registry of Final Beneficiaries
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Access restricted to authorities/obliged entities.

trackers.name: Poder Judicial del Paraguay
trackers.desc: Official judiciary portal with jurisprudence and case search. · Find here: the portal, case search and rulings of Paraguay's Judiciary.

trackers.name: Paraguay — Dirección General de los Registros Públicos (DGRP)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the Judiciary’s DGRP maintains the Registro Público de Comercio & Registro de Personas Jurídicas with an online registral-information service, Paraguay. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Artículo 38 — any person, alone, may demand measures from the authorities
trackers.desc: THE BROADEST STANDING PROVISION IN THIS MAP. Article 38 gives toda persona the right, individually or collectively, to claim measures from the public authorities for the defence of the environment, the integrity of the habitat, public health, national cultural heritage and other interests that by their nature belong to the community and relate to quality of life and collective patrimony. FOUR THINGS TO USE: any person — no residence, ownership or membership requirement; individually — you do not need an organisation, unlike Mongolia where a missing charter clause defeated an NGO's standing; integrity of the habitat is named separately from the environment, so it is its own protected interest; and the right is to claim measures from the authorities, making it a demand on the state rather than only a defence against a private party. IT SITS BESIDE TWO OTHERS: article 40, the right to petition authorities ‘individual o colectivamente y sin requisitos especiales’ in writing, to which they must respond within the period set; and article 39, the right to just and adequate compensation for damage caused by the State.

trackers.name: Supervisión de cumplimiento — the stage after judgment, and it works
trackers.desc: PARAGUAY IS WHERE THE INTER-AMERICAN INDIGENOUS LAND DOCTRINE WAS BUILT — Yakye Axa (2005), Sawhoyamaxa (2006) and Xákmok Kásek (2010), in each of which the Court ordered restitution of ancestral lands and required the State to supply basic goods and services in the interim. The doctrine, with Moiwana and Saramaka: property under article 21 of the American Convention is not limited to the Western concept and covers communal property of traditional peoples, including natural resources on their lands as a means of maintaining religion, agriculture, hunting, fishing and their way of life. THE STAGE MOST CAMPAIGNS OVERLOOK: after judgment the Court opens supervisión de cumplimiento, and it is active — in Sawhoyamaxa it issued supervision resolutions in 2015 and 2019, recorded the 2014 law expropriating the community's traditional lands as a concrete advance, and in 2017 sent a delegation on an in situ visit to the Paraguayan Chaco. A judgment is not the end of the case; supervision is where implementation is argued. WHAT PRODUCED THE RESULT was the combination: court supervision, plus monitoring with periodic meetings with the community and with Congress, plus public campaigning. BE REALISTIC: Amnesty assessed the 2005 and 2006 violations as not addressed and therefore continuing, with state action insufficient — roughly two decades passed between expulsion and concrete restitution.

trackers.name: Ley 3001 art. 11 — roads, dams and pipelines must buy environmental certificates
trackers.desc: A LAW THAT MAKES DEVELOPERS PAY THOSE WHO CONSERVE. Ley 3001/2006 creates a certification mechanism for environmental services, with economic valuation attached. Article 2 defines environmental services as those generated by human activities of management, conservation and recovery of ecosystem functions — so it pays for activity, not merely for owning intact land, and recovery of a degraded ecosystem is inside the definition. ARTICLE 11 IS THE OPERATIVE PROVISION: works of high environmental impact — construction and maintenance of roads, hydraulic works, power plants, electricity transmission lines, pipelines, port works, high-emission industries, and discharge of urban and industrial effluents — must include within their investment scheme the compensation for environmental services through acquisition of Certificados de Servicios Ambientales, expressly without prejudice to other mitigation and conservation measures. So a road, dam, transmission line or pipeline must buy certificates, separately from and additional to its ordinary mitigation obligations. TWO QUESTIONS FOLLOW: if a listed project is near you, has it acquired certificates, and from whom? And if you hold or manage conserved land, you may be the counterparty rather than only the objector. Covered categories include protection of water resources and biodiversity; transactions are made once only.

trackers.name: CONADERNA's compliance list — a map of who is supposed to enforce it
trackers.desc: A PARLIAMENTARY COMMISSION URGING COMPLIANCE IS EVIDENCE THAT COMPLIANCE HAS BEEN PATCHY — and its address list is a map of who is meant to enforce Ley 3001. The Senate's Comisión Nacional de Defensa de los Recursos Naturales presented a Declaration urging full compliance in high-impact works, directed to MADES, the Ministry of Public Works (MOPC), INFONA, the binational hydroelectric entities Itaipú and Yacyretá, ANDE, the national public procurement directorate (DNCP), the Central Bank, the Banco Nacional de Fomento, private banks, PETROPAR, the Contraloría General, the Supreme Court and the Ministerio Público. Note the procurement authority and the banks are on that list — which means a financing or tender route exists alongside the environmental one. AND THE LAW IS STILL BEING STRENGTHENED: on 30 September 2025 the Cámara de Diputados gave media sanción to a bill making certificate acquisition obligatory for all public institutions and state enterprises for high-impact works, through tender processes. Check its current status — media sanción is one chamber only, not enactment. ALSO RECORDED, AS A PROPOSAL ONLY: a Fondo Ambiental was presented at a workshop run by Proyecto Paraguay Biodiversidad and opened by Itaipú Binacional and the environment minister. This entry does not assert that fund exists — verify before relying on it; the Ley 3001 obligation on Itaipú and Yacyretá is the firmer hook.

trackers.name: Paraguay's neighbourhood commissions and communal boards - recognised by resolution of the intendant, able to file a draft ordinance backed by 30% of neighbours which passes by SILENCE after three months, with municipally funded elections
trackers.desc: THIRTY PER CENT OF THE NEIGHBOURS CAN FORCE THE MUNICIPAL COUNCIL TO CONSIDER AN ORDINANCE, AND SILENCE FOR THREE MONTHS MEANS IT PASSES. The municipal statute provides that the creation, fusion and modification of the limits of the communal boards of neighbours SHALL BE DONE BY MUNICIPAL ORDINANCE, that THE DRAFT ORDINANCE MAY BE PRESENTED BY THE NEIGHBOURS OF THE ZONE, HAVING TO BE ENDORSED BY THIRTY PER CENT OF THEM, and that THE MUNICIPAL COUNCIL MUST OBLIGATORILY CONSIDER THE PROJECT AND IF IT DOES NOT PRONOUNCE WITHIN THE PERIOD OF THREE MONTHS THE SAME SHALL BE TAKEN AS SANCTIONED. Silence approves it. That is the strongest lever a community holds over a reluctant council in this file — collect the signatures, file the draft and diarise the ninety days. WHAT THESE NEIGHBOURHOOD BODIES ARE: communal boards of neighbours, ALSO CALLED NEIGHBOURHOOD COMMISSIONS, are ASSOCIATIONS OF NEIGHBOURS THAT FUNCTION IN DELIMITED URBAN OR RURAL ZONES OF THE MUNICIPALITIES, INTEGRATED FREELY BY THE CITIZENS OF THE ZONE AND GOVERNED BY MUNICIPAL ORDINANCE, with their own administrative organisation; their functions include ASSISTING THE MUNICIPALITY IN THE REALISATION OF WORKS OF COMMUNITY INTEREST AND IN THE PROVISION OF BASIC SERVICES. Recognition of commissions created SHALL BE EFFECTED BY RESOLUTION OF THE MUNICIPAL INTENDANCY, and it is among the intendant's duties TO AUTHORISE THE CREATION AND FUNCTIONING OF COMMISSIONS OF COMMUNAL PROMOTION AND COMMUNAL BOARDS OF NEIGHBOURS. Rural zones are expressly included. One resolution of the intendant recognises the body, and after that the community has a named counterpart inside the municipality. WHAT THE MUNICIPALITY OWES THEM: municipalities SHALL PROMOTE THE PARTICIPATION OF THE INHABITANTS OF THE MUNICIPALITY IN MUNICIPAL MANAGEMENT AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE CITIZEN ASSOCIATIONS; citizens MAY GIVE THEMSELVES THE FORMS OF ORGANISATION THEY CONSIDER MOST APPROPRIATE; and the municipality SHALL BE OBLIGED TO PROVIDE ALL PUBLIC INFORMATION THAT IT HAS CREATED OR OBTAINED within the statutory period. Promulgated ordinances must be sent monthly to the municipal council, the interior ministry and the departmental government. The information duty is the one to use first. Ask the municipality in writing for the file on the project — it must answer, and the answer becomes your evidence. HOW THE COMMISSIONS ARE ORGANISED IN PRACTICE: a capital regulation defines them as ORGANISED GROUPINGS OF PERSONS RESIDENT IN A DETERMINED TERRITORY... PLURALIST, DEMOCRATIC AND INFLUENTIAL ASSOCIATIONS, NON-PROFIT, THAT DO NOT ADMIT PARTY OR RELIGIOUS PROSELYTISM NOR DISCRIMINATION OF ANY TYPE; the rules set the agenda for constitutive, ordinary and extraordinary assemblies, the MINIMUM AND MAXIMUM NUMBER OF BLOCKS for a commission, the forms to be sent to the coordinating body and the municipality, an obligatory independent electoral tribunal for each coordinator, whose election materials MUST BE COVERED IN THEIR TOTALITY BY THE MUNICIPAL BUDGET, and the possibility of youth and older persons' commissions. The municipality pays for the commission's elections. Ask for that budget line rather than funding a ballot yourselves. THE TAX POINT THAT CATCHES PEOPLE OUT: the revenue authority records that temporary neighbourhood commissions recognised by a municipality or governorate DO NOT POSSESS PATRIMONY NOR THEIR OWN LEGAL PERSONALITY, ONLY THE RECOGNITION OF THE MUNICIPALITY, and that they MUST REGISTER WITH THE TAXPAYER REGISTRY IN ORDER TO RECEIVE THE CONTRIBUTIONS OF THE MUNICIPALITY FOR THE EXECUTION OF COMMUNITY PROJECTS. Recognition is not legal personality here. If the plan is to hold money or sign for land, you need a different vehicle — but the tax registration is what unlocks municipal contributions for a project.

trackers.name: Paraguay's association of municipal boards, association of departmental boards, council of governors and women officeholders' network - with an NGO that has trained councillors on budget scrutiny, and an honest warning about the inter-municipal organisation
trackers.desc: THE MUNICIPAL COUNCILLORS HAVE THEIR OWN NATIONAL ASSOCIATION, AND AN NGO HAS TRAINED THEM ON HOLDING THE MAYOR'S BUDGET TO ACCOUNT. A local management association records a PROGRAMME OF TRAINING FOR MUNICIPAL COUNCILLORS AND MAYORS ON RENDERING OF ACCOUNT OF THE MUNICIPAL BUDGETARY MANAGEMENT, AGREEMENT OF COOPERATION BETWEEN THE ASSOCIATION OF MUNICIPAL BOARDS OF PARAGUAY AND itself, and a further PROGRAMME OF TRAINING FOR MUNICIPAL INTENDANTS AND MUNICIPAL COUNCILLORS ON THE FORMULATION OF THE MUNICIPAL BUDGET, TO SUPPORT THE MANAGEMENT OF THE PARAGUAYAN LOCAL GOVERNMENTS; it has also run a public dialogue forum with authorities and civil society on a municipal development agenda. Councillors, not the mayor, vote the budget and the ordinances. An organisation that has already trained them on budget scrutiny is the one to ask for a session in your own council. THE FIVE BODIES THAT SIT IN THAT SPACE: a recorded decentralisation project was sponsored by the COUNCIL OF GOVERNORS OF PARAGUAY, the ASSOCIATION OF DEPARTMENTAL BOARDS OF PARAGUAY, the inter-municipal cooperation organisation, the ASSOCIATION OF MUNICIPAL BOARDS OF PARAGUAY and the NETWORK OF WOMEN MUNICIPAL OFFICEHOLDERS OF PARAGUAY, in DAYS OF INFORMATION AND DIALOGUE ON DECENTRALISATION AND REFORM WITH DEPARTMENTAL CANDIDATES FOR PUBLIC OFFICE. Governors, departmental boards, municipal boards and a women officeholders' network each have a national body. Where a mayor is unmoved, the departmental board or the councillors' association is a separate door into the same territory. THE INTER-MUNICIPAL ORGANISATION, AND THE HONEST WARNING ABOUT IT: it presents itself as A NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATION THAT BRINGS TOGETHER THE MUNICIPALITIES OF THE COUNTRY, publishes an address, telephones and email in the capital, and runs training including a programme of democratic leadership for young people. But press reporting records that it WAS BORN AS A PUBLIC OFFICE DEPENDENT ON THE EXECUTIVE POWER IN 1964 and left the public sphere on changing its statutes in the 1990s BUT MAINTAINS ALL THE FUNCTIONS AND ATTRIBUTIONS OF A STATE INSTITUTION; that it acts as an OBLIGATORY INTERMEDIARY in vehicle and driving licence procedures and in real estate transfer matters; that ENTIRE MUNICIPALITIES ARE DEPENDENT ON it for their charging and document systems and it HAS EVEN SUSPENDED TRANSFERS IF THE COMMUNES DO NOT COMPLY WITH ITS CONDITIONS; and that the national comptroller has published an audit report on it. Treat that body as a service provider with leverage over your municipality rather than as an ally. If a town hall says it cannot act because of its obligations to that organisation, ask which contract it means and get it in writing. WHERE THE TRAINING MONEY HAS COME FROM: the recorded programmes were run under cooperation agreements and for a national reform programme financed through an international development agency, with the sponsorship of the bodies named above. Councillor training here has historically been externally financed. Ask the councillors' association which cooperation programme is currently funding its work, and whether your council can be included in the next round.

trackers.name: FLACMA - the Latin American federation of cities and municipal associations, open to affiliation by ANY INDIVIDUAL MUNICIPALITY, whose assembly passes resolutions signed by mayors across eighteen countries
trackers.desc: ANY CITY OR MUNICIPALITY IN THE REGION MAY AFFILIATE DIRECTLY, NOT ONLY THROUGH ITS NATIONAL ASSOCIATION. Its membership rule is that MEMBERS ARE ALL THE CITIES, MUNICIPALITIES, NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND MUNICIPALIST INSTITUTIONS OF LATIN AMERICA THAT HAVE EXPRESSED THEIR WILL TO AFFILIATE; it is AN ORGANISATION OF FREE ADHESION THAT REPRESENTS THE 16,132 MUNICIPALITIES, INTENDANCIES AND PREFECTURES, THE CITIES AND THE ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, NETWORKS AND GUILDS OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, and it is the regional section of the world organisation of local governments. A single municipality may join in its own right. Where your national association is captured or inactive, that is a way for one sympathetic town hall to reach the regional table on its own. WHOSE PRESIDENTS SIT ON IT: its published leadership is drawn from the presidents of the national municipal bodies of the region — the federation of municipalities of one southern country, the association of municipalities of another, the Brazilian association of municipalities, the congress of intendants of another, the national federation of municipalities of one large federal country and the association of municipalities of an Andean one — each of them a serving mayor. The people who chair your own national municipal association sit here. A matter raised through that association can be carried into a regional assembly by the same person. WHAT IT SAYS IT IS FOR: TO BE THE VOICE OF LATIN AMERICAN MUNICIPALISM, TO CONSOLIDATE THE LATIN AMERICAN MUNICIPAL ASSOCIATIVE MOVEMENT, TO REPRESENT AND SERVE AS INTERLOCUTOR OF ALL THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND THEIR NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES, and TO PROMOTE IN LATIN AMERICA AUTONOMOUS, STRONG AND DEMOCRATIC LOCAL GOVERNMENTS; it ADHERES TO AND PROMOTES THE WORLD AND REGIONAL CONVENTIONS THAT THE NATIONAL STATES OF THE REGION SUBSCRIBE. Promoting the conventions the states have signed is written into its purpose. Where your country has signed an environmental or rights convention and a municipality is being told to ignore it, that is a body with a standing commitment to the opposite. THE PRECEDENT THAT SHOWS IT TAKES POSITIONS: its general assembly has approved unanimously a declaration on a territorial sovereignty dispute, signed by the president and BY MUNICIPAL AUTHORITIES AND HEADS OF ASSOCIATIONS AND FEDERATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES of eighteen named countries of the region, which also REAFFIRMED THE LEGITIMATE RIGHTS... OVER THE NATURAL RESOURCES OF THE AREA IN QUESTION. The assembly passes resolutions that name natural resources and get signed by mayors across eighteen countries. A community campaign that can be framed as a municipal cause has a forum that has done exactly that before. THE OTHER REGIONAL NETWORKS BESIDE IT: regional analysis names, among the principal associations and networks of local and regional governments with EXPERIENCES, IDEAS AND RESOURCES TO FOSTER INITIATIVES AND PROJECTS LINKED TO SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AT LOCAL LEVEL, a network of Mercosur cities alongside this federation, and global initiatives with regional presence for local sustainability and for city climate action; various cities have prepared VOLUNTARY LOCAL REPORTS on implementing the global development agenda in their territories. A voluntary local report is a document a municipality writes about itself. Getting your community's situation named in one is cheap, public and lasting. THE HONEST NOTE ON REPRESENTATION: the region's representation in the world body has been the subject of negotiations between this federation, the Mercosur cities network and the world organisation to form A LATIN AMERICAN REPRESENTATION THAT IS PLURAL, DIVERSE AND PARTICIPATORY. More than one body claims to speak for the region's municipalities. Approach both this federation and the Mercosur cities network rather than assuming one covers the other.

trackers.name: Mercociudades - a South American city network whose cooperation calls admit UNIVERSITIES AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS as partners alongside two or more municipalities, with an environment and sustainable development unit coordinated by a member city
trackers.desc: UNIVERSITIES AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS CAN BE PARTNERS IN THE COOPERATION PROJECTS THIS CITY NETWORK FUNDS. Its south-south cooperation call is open to MEMBER CITIES AND ASSOCIATED STATES, to universities of a regional university association, and to ORGANISATIONS OF CIVIL SOCIETY; THE PROJECT MUST INVOLVE AT LEAST TWO MEMBER LOCAL GOVERNMENTS OR ASSOCIATED STATES, and THE UNIVERSITIES AND SOCIAL ORGANISATIONS MAY PARTICIPATE AS PARTNER ENTITIES ALONGSIDE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, each city able to stand as coordinator of one proposal and partner in another. Two municipalities and your organisation is a fundable consortium. Where a threatened area straddles two towns, or two towns face the same developer, that is the shape the call is written for. THE THEMATIC UNIT THAT COVERS LAND AND WATER: among its seventeen thematic units and four working groups is one for ENVIRONMENT AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT, coordinated by a city with sub-coordinating cities, which has run exchanges on waste, sustainability and circular economy and marked world water day, and has opened AN OPPORTUNITY OF COOPERATION TOGETHER WITH THE UNITED NATIONS ENVIRONMENT PROGRAMME FOR THE STRENGTHENING OF LOCAL CAPACITIES; other units cover AUTONOMY, MANAGEMENT AND PARTICIPATION, HUMAN RIGHTS, URBAN DEVELOPMENT, PLANNING AND METROPOLITAN AREAS and BORDER INTEGRATION. A coordinating city runs each unit, and it is a city like yours rather than a secretariat. Write to the coordinator of the environment unit with your case: that is a mayor's office, not an agency. WHAT THE NETWORK COMMITS ITSELF TO DO: among its statutory objectives are TO CARRY OUT STUDIES AND COLLABORATE IN THE ELABORATION OF PLANS AND STRATEGIES IN THE URBAN-ENVIRONMENTAL AREA, WITH THE OBJECTIVE OF HARMONISING AND COORDINATING THE ACTIONS IN THIS AREA, TO COLLABORATE IN THE PLANNING OF THE POLICIES AND PLANS OF DEVELOPMENT OF THE CITIES, TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE NEED TO IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF LIFE, TO ADVOCATE AND RAISE AWARENESS ABOUT CITIZEN PARTICIPATION AND SOCIAL INCLUSION, and TO IDENTIFY THE CAUSES OF ACCENTUATION OF THE SOCIAL INEQUALITIES, IN ORDER TO PROPOSE AND SUPPORT SOLUTIONS POSSIBLE TO BE EXECUTED BY THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS. Collaborating in city development plans is a stated commitment. A municipality revising its plan can ask the network for that collaboration rather than paying a consultancy. WHO ELSE MAY TAKE PART: THE OTHER INSTANCES OF THE SUB-NATIONAL GOVERNMENTS OF THE COUNTRIES of the two regional blocs THAT EXPRESS THEIR WILL TO DO SO AND WHOSE GOVERNMENTS HAVE BEEN DEMOCRATICALLY ELECTED may participate as collaborators, and COOPERATION WITH CONSORTIA AND ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES WILL BE CARRIED OUT BY MEANS OF AGREEMENTS. Provinces, departments and municipal consortia can join as collaborators. Where the decision sits above the town hall, that tier can be brought to the same table. THE PLATFORM THAT MATCHES NEEDS TO SOLUTIONS: its cooperation programme runs an interactive platform DESIGNED SPECIALLY TO SHARE LOCAL SOLUTIONS... AND TO INTERWEAVE STRENGTHS AND TECHNICAL NEEDS OF CITIES OF ALL SOUTH AMERICA, with a directory of good practices through which member cities HAVE THE POSSIBILITY OF EXCHANGING WITH THE REFERENTS OF SOLUTIONS OF THE CITIES. Post the technical need rather than the complaint. A city that has already solved the same problem is what the platform is built to find.

trackers.name: ICLEI - a sustainability network open to individual councils AND to associations of local governments, giving fee-paying members year-round telephone and email support on designing environment and water projects, plus local biodiversity planning tools and an environmental award
trackers.desc: MEMBERSHIP OF THIS GLOBAL SUSTAINABILITY NETWORK IS OPEN TO ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AS WELL AS TO INDIVIDUAL COUNCILS, AND THE FEE SCALES WITH POPULATION AND NATIONAL INCOME. Its membership page states that AFFILIATION IS OPEN TO ALL LOCAL AND REGIONAL GOVERNMENTS, AS WELL AS TO THEIR WORLD, REGIONAL, NATIONAL AND SUBNATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS, that members MAY VOTE AND PARTICIPATE IN THE GOVERNING ORGANS OF THE WHOLE NETWORK, and that they CONTRIBUTE AN ANNUAL AFFILIATION FEE THAT VARIES REGIONALLY AND ACCORDING TO POPULATION AND GROSS NATIONAL INCOME PER CAPITA. A small municipality pays a small fee and votes in the same network as a capital city. Where a national association is the member, ask whether your council is covered by it already. WHAT A MEMBER ACTUALLY GETS, IN THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT'S OWN WORDS: it SUPPORTS ITS PARTNERS TO FIND SUSTAINABLE SOLUTIONS THROUGH PROJECTS, INITIATIVES AND PROGRAMMES, offers cities and states A PLATFORM TO INTERACT WITH OTHER LOCAL GOVERNMENTS and provides RESOURCES AND TOOLS TO PROMOTE POSITIVE ENVIRONMENTAL, ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL CHANGES; support runs DURING THE YEAR THAT THE FEE LASTS, PERMANENTLY, BY TELEPHONE OR BY EMAIL, and covers THE DESIGN OF PROGRAMMES AND PROJECTS OF SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN THEMES SUCH AS: ENVIRONMENT, WATER, PUBLIC SERVICES, ENERGY EFFICIENCY, SOLID WASTE. Joining requires A REQUEST TO THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT addressed to the named regional secretary, plus a membership form. Permanent telephone and email support on designing water and environment projects, for one annual fee. That is a standing technical helpline for a town hall that has none. THE BIODIVERSITY WORK THAT MATTERS FOR LAND: its recorded local biodiversity work is TO PROMOTE THE BIODIVERSITY STRATEGIES OF THE STATE AND MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENTS, AS WELL AS THEIR ACTION PLANS, AND ALSO TO REINFORCE THE CAPACITIES OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS TO INCORPORATE BIODIVERSITY INTO THE PLANNING PROCESSES, and it notes that MORE MONETARY RESOURCES ARE INVESTED GLOBALLY IN BIODIVERSITY AT LOCAL AND SUBNATIONAL LEVEL THAN AT NATIONAL LEVELS; a member municipality has launched an urban biodiversity index, and a global initiative on NATURE IN URBAN PLANNING is promoted through the network. Incorporating biodiversity into planning processes is the exact point at which a project is stopped or waved through. Ask the secretariat which of its tools your municipality can adopt in its next plan revision. THE RECOGNITION THAT GIVES A COUNCIL A REASON: the regional secretariat runs an award for local governments THAT HAVE CARRIED OUT ACTIONS IN FAVOUR OF THE PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT IN THEMES OF CLIMATE CHANGE, BIODIVERSITY, ENERGY EFFICIENCY, MOBILITY, AMONG OTHERS, open to municipalities, city boroughs and federal entities. An award with a biodiversity category. A council weighing whether to protect a site has a public reason to do so, and the application is a deadline you can work to. THE OFFICES THAT COVER THIS REGION: there is a secretariat for one large federal country together with Central America and the Caribbean, and a separate South American secretariat, each publishing member lists that include municipalities of several countries. Two regional offices cover the whole file. Write to the one for your subregion rather than to the global body.

trackers.name: Fundo Casa Socioambiental - a small-grants fund for community groups across South America that funds groups WITHOUT LEGAL PERSONALITY through a partner organisation, with calls prioritising repeatedly rejected and newly formed groups
trackers.desc: A GROUP WITH NO LEGAL PERSONALITY AT ALL CAN RECEIVE A GRANT, BY BORROWING ANOTHER ORGANISATION'S. The fund's calls state that ORGANISATIONS THAT DO NOT POSSESS a registered company number ARE ALSO ELIGIBLE AND MAY SEND PROJECTS IN THIS CALL; the partner organisation field MUST ONLY BE FILLED IN IN THE CASES IN WHICH THE PROPOSING ORGANISATION DOES NOT POSSESS one, that partner being THE NON-PROFIT INSTITUTION THAT CEDES ITS LEGAL STRUCTURE TO THE GROUPS and THE LEGAL RESPONSIBLE FOR THE PROJECT, receiving the resource in an institutional bank account; one organisation may be PROPOSER OF ONE PROJECT OF ITS OWN AND PARTNER FOR UP TO ONE OTHER GROUP WITHOUT JURIDICAL PERSONALITY. An unincorporated village committee can be funded tomorrow if one registered neighbour signs as partner. That single rule removes the obstacle that blocks most community groups in this file. WHO THE FUND IS AND HOW SMALL THE GRANTS ARE: it is A NON-GOVERNMENTAL, NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION THAT FINANCES SMALL PROJECTS, AND CAPACITY STRENGTHENING, FOR SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL INITIATIVES OF NGOs AND COMMUNITY GROUPS IN SOUTH AMERICA, whose strategy is THE SUPPORT OF MANY PROJECTS WITH SMALL AMOUNTS INSTEAD OF SUPPORTING FEW PROJECTS WITH LARGE AMOUNTS; founded in 2005, its mission is TO PROMOTE CONSERVATION AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY, DEMOCRACY AND SOCIAL JUSTICE THROUGH THE SUPPORT AND STRENGTHENING OF CAPACITIES AND INITIATIVES OF CIVIL SOCIETY IN SOUTH AMERICA, with experience supporting POPULAR ORGANISATIONS, SOCIAL MOVEMENTS, NETWORKS AND ARTICULATIONS; recorded totals run from more than three thousand projects in ten countries to almost five thousand. Many small grants rather than a few large ones. A group asking for a few thousand is inside this fund's model rather than beneath its notice. WHAT A CALL ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE: one recorded call supported UP TO 24 PROJECTS OF UP TO R$ 35,000.00 in named river regions and one state, open to LOCAL ASSOCIATIONS AND COMMUNITY GROUPS WITH AN ANNUAL BUDGET OF UP TO R$ 150 THOUSAND, its priority publics being TRADITIONAL COMMUNITIES SUCH AS INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, QUILOMBOLA, RIVERSIDE AND EXTRACTIVIST COMMUNITIES; a later edition raised the ceiling to fifty thousand per project and expanded from thirty-four approved projects to fifty-seven after two hundred and thirty-three applications arrived. Another call prioritises ORGANISATIONS RECENTLY CREATED, IN AN INITIAL STAGE OF ACTIVITIES OR RESUMING THEIR ACTIVITIES AFTER A PERIOD OF PARALYSIS, and INITIATIVES OF ORGANISATIONS THAT HAVE NOT YET ACCESSED RESOURCES from the fund or that have applied three or more times without success. Applying and failing repeatedly is itself a stated priority criterion. If your group has been rejected three times, say so in the next application. THE THREE-COUNTRY ALLIANCE BEHIND THE AMAZON CALLS: one initiative unites this fund with a Colombian and a Peruvian socio-environmental fund, aiming TO PROMOTE GREATER CONTRIBUTION OF DIRECT RESOURCES TO INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, QUILOMBOLA COMMUNITIES AND OTHER TRADITIONAL PEOPLES IN THE AMAZON OF BRAZIL, PERU AND COLOMBIA, ESPECIALLY IN THE BORDER REGION, supporting twenty-four, fourteen and nineteen projects respectively in one year; all members of a southern socio-environmental funds alliance WILL LAUNCH CALLS IN THEIR COUNTRIES, each publishing its own. Border regions are named as a priority rather than a complication. Look up the member fund for your own country and read its call, not only this one. THE RULES THAT CATCH PEOPLE OUT: resources may not be spent before the contract is signed; funds from other budget lines may not be moved to pay consultancies; groups with PENDING ACCOUNTS from a previous grant are not accepted; and where a group hires advice it MUST SEEK PEOPLE OF TRUST, with the project ELABORATED TOGETHER WITH THE COMMUNITY and its final version OF WIDE KNOWLEDGE OF THE COMMUNITY. Do not spend a peso before signature, and do not let a consultant write the proposal alone. Both are stated grounds for losing the grant.

trackers.name: The GEF Small Grants Programme - grants of up to $50,000 DIRECT to community organisations, with a national coordinator in each country who helps write the concept paper, planning grants, and a companion window of up to $300,000
trackers.desc: THERE IS A NAMED NATIONAL COORDINATOR IN YOUR COUNTRY WHOSE JOB INCLUDES HELPING YOU WRITE THE APPLICATION. The programme's own procedure is that THE PROJECT PROPONENT — A NATIONAL CBO OR NGO — CONTACTS THE SGP NATIONAL COORDINATOR TO RECEIVE PROJECT APPLICATION GUIDELINES AND FORMS, and that WITH ASSISTANCE FROM THE NATIONAL COORDINATOR, THE PROPONENT PREPARES A BRIEF PROJECT CONCEPT PAPER; the coordinator pre-screens it, and if eligible the proponent prepares a full proposal — IN SOME CASES, THIS STEP MAY BE SUPPORTED BY A PLANNING GRANT — which goes to a national steering committee that accepts, rejects or returns it for further work. A planning grant to write the proposal, and an official whose job is to help you write it. Contact the coordinator before drafting anything, because the concept paper is short and they will tell you whether it fits. WHAT IT PAYS AND TO WHOM: the programme PROVIDES GRANTS OF UP TO $50,000 DIRECTLY TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES INCLUDING INDIGENOUS PEOPLE, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS AND OTHER NON-GOVERNMENTAL GROUPS, for projects in BIODIVERSITY, CLIMATE CHANGE MITIGATION AND ADAPTATION, LAND DEGRADATION AND SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT, INTERNATIONAL WATERS AND CHEMICALS, with SPECIAL CONSIDERATION FOR INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, WOMEN, AND YOUTH; it COMPLEMENTS THE LARGE AND MEDIUM-SIZED facility funding BY PROVIDING A WINDOW FOR THE DIRECT PARTICIPATION OF NGOs, LOCAL COMMUNITIES, AND OTHER GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS. Since 1992 it has supported CLOSE TO 30,000 GRANTS, ADMINISTERING $1.54 BILLION... ACROSS 136 COUNTRIES. Fifty thousand dollars, paid direct to a community organisation, on biodiversity or land degradation. That is the largest routine sum in this file available without an intermediary. HOW IT IS RUN LOCALLY: it operates IN A DECENTRALIZED AND COUNTRY-DRIVEN MANNER THROUGH COUNTRY PROGRAM TEAMS COMPOSED OF A NATIONAL COORDINATOR, OFTEN A PROGRAM ASSISTANT, AND A NATIONAL STEERING COMMITTEE IN EACH PARTICIPATING COUNTRY, each country publishing a country programme strategy that proposals must align with. In one small island state an operational phase was advertised with A GRANTS PORTFOLIO OF APPROXIMATELY US$750,000... FOR COMMUNITY-BASED ENVIRONMENTAL PROJECTS. Download your country's programme strategy before writing. Proposals are judged against that document, and it names the priorities and often the specific landscapes. THE THREE AGENCIES THAT NOW RUN IT: the core programme is implemented by a development programme, an agriculture organisation and a conservation organisation, the second bringing expertise in AGRICULTURE, FISHERIES, FORESTRY, BIOENERGY, CLIMATE-RESILIENT PRACTICES, LIVESTOCK, AND LAND & WATER to thirteen countries; national coordinator posts in some small states are contracted through the conservation organisation, working alongside a Caribbean islands biodiversity hotspot fund. Which agency runs your country's programme changes who you write to. Check the country page rather than assuming it is the development programme. THE LARGER WINDOW BESIDE IT: a civil society challenge programme led by a conservation union SUPPORTS COMPETITIVE OPPORTUNITIES FOR LOCAL CSOs TO ACCESS FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL RESOURCES TO SCALE UP INNOVATIVE ENVIRONMENTAL SOLUTIONS, OFFERING GRANTS OF UP TO $300,000. Three hundred thousand for an organisation that has already proved something small works. Treat the fifty-thousand grant as the step that qualifies you for it.

trackers.name: World Land Trust and its 52 local partners - raises the money for LAND PURCHASE but leaves the title with the local organisation, funds reserve rangers and watershed buy-outs, and has signed shared-management agreements with an environment ministry
trackers.desc: THIS IS A FUNDER THAT PAYS FOR LAND PURCHASE AND THEN PUTS THE TITLE IN A LOCAL ORGANISATION'S NAME, NOT ITS OWN. It DOESN'T OWN ANY OF THE LAND ITSELF, which IS ALL OWNED BY ITS LOCAL NGO PARTNERS, so that THE LAND IS IN THE CONTROL OF LOCAL CONSERVATION PARTNERS; it HELPS RAISE THE FUNDS TO PURCHASE THE LAND AND THEN PROVIDES ASSISTANCE TO THE LOCAL ORGANIZATION IN MANAGING AND PROTECTING it, with ownership ENTRUSTED TO CONSERVATION ORGANISATIONS RUN BY LOCAL PEOPLE WHO TAKE ON THE RESPONSIBILITY OF PROTECTING THE LAND, MONITORING THE WILDLIFE AND BIODIVERSITY ON THE RESERVE, AND EMPLOYING PARK WARDENS. Money for the purchase, and the deed stays local. For a community group with a willing seller and no capital, this is the closest thing in this file to a buyer. WHERE IT WORKS IN THIS REGION: partners and projects are recorded in ARGENTINA... BELIZE, BOLIVIA, BRAZIL, COLOMBIA, ECUADOR, GUATEMALA, HONDURAS... MEXICO, PARAGUAY, PERU... VENEZUELA among other countries, with 52 active conservation partners after five new ones joined in one year. Twelve countries in this file already have a partner. Find the partner nearest you and approach it, because the funder works through partners rather than taking applications from communities directly. WHAT THE PURCHASE PROGRAMME ACTUALLY DOES: its land purchase appeal RAISES FUNDS SO THAT partner organisations CAN PURCHASE LOCAL LAND AND CREATE RESERVES TO PROTECT THE LOCAL HABITAT AND WILDLIFE IN PERPETUITY; recorded cases include funding a partner to expand an existing reserve by hundreds of hectares, and a purchase that was THE CULMINATION OF 16 YEARS OF NEGOTIATIONS. Cumulatively the trust and its partners have been INSTRUMENTAL IN THE PURCHASE AND PROTECTION OF MORE THAN 3,312,183 ACRES of threatened habitat. Sixteen years of negotiation ended in a purchase. If the owner is not ready to sell yet, that is not a reason to stop asking — it is the normal timescale. WHAT ELSE IT FUNDS BESIDES THE PURCHASE: partnerships encompass LAND PURCHASE, LAND PROTECTION through a carbon scheme and FUNDING FOR RESERVE RANGERS, and recorded projects include WATERSHED PROTECTION BY PURCHASING KEY AREAS TO SAFEGUARD WATER SUPPLIES and work WITH LOCAL COMMUNITIES TO PRESERVE CULTURAL TRADITIONS; one Amazon corridor project proceeded THROUGH LAND PURCHASE, WORKING WITH LOCAL indigenous COMMUNITIES, RESTORATION, MONITORING AND MANAGEMENT. Ranger salaries are funded, not only the acquisition. A reserve nobody can afford to guard is the usual failure, and this is one of the few sources that pays for the guarding. THE AGREEMENT MODEL WORTH COPYING: in one country the trust signed A SHARED-MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT WITH its partner organisation AND THE MINISTRY OF THE ENVIRONMENT, aiming TO ENSURE THE PROTECTION OF RESERVES TOTALLING OVER 2.5 MILLION ACRES. A three-way agreement between funder, local organisation and the environment ministry. Where the state owns land it cannot manage, that is the arrangement to propose. THE PARTNERS THEMSELVES ARE THE ROUTE: named partners include foundations protecting foothill and cloud forests and páramo whose RESERVES PROTECT LOCAL CENTRES OF ENDEMISM THAT ARE NOT PROTECTED BY the country's NATIONAL PARKS OR PROTECTED AREAS, a habitat and development foundation in one southern country, a body creating protected areas while PROMOTING THE PARTICIPATION OF LOCAL STAKEHOLDERS, and a multi-country organisation supporting PUBLIC, COMMUNAL AND PRIVATE PROTECTED AREAS with a team of local conservationists, legal professionals and mapping experts. One partner explicitly supports communal protected areas and employs its own lawyers and mappers. Where a community holds land collectively and needs title work or a boundary map, ask that partner first.

trackers.name: Rainforest Trust - FEASIBILITY AWARDS of about $10,000 to fund the legal pathway study and species survey, then uncapped creation awards for land purchase, community land titling or converting extractive concessions into protected areas
trackers.desc: THERE IS A GRANT OF AROUND TEN THOUSAND DOLLARS JUST TO FIND OUT WHETHER PROTECTING A SITE IS POSSIBLE. The funder provides FEASIBILITY AWARDS TO ASSESS THE POTENTIAL FOR CREATING OR EXPANDING PROTECTED OR CONSERVED AREAS, INTENDED TO ADDRESS SPECIFIC INFORMATION GAPS... AS PRECURSORS TO APPLYING FOR a full award; these can SUPPORT DEVELOPING A LEGAL PATHWAY TO PROTECT A PROPOSED SITE, OR FIELD SURVEYS TO DETERMINE THE PRESENCE AND ABUNDANCE OF CRITICALLY ENDANGERED OR ENDANGERED SPECIES, at typical funding of about US $10,000 and up to about US $20,000 in exceptional cases, ACCEPTED ON A ROLLING BASIS. Ten thousand dollars to pay for the legal pathway study and the species survey — the two documents every protection file needs and no community can afford. Apply for this before applying for anything else. WHAT THE MAIN AWARD BUYS: primary awards SUPPORT THE CREATION AND EXPANSION OF PROTECTED OR CONSERVED AREAS, ON LAND OR SEA, BE IT THROUGH DESIGNATION, LAND TITLING, PURCHASE OR ANY OTHER RECOGNIZED METHODOLOGY; tools named include LAND PURCHASE; DESIGNATION AS NATIONAL PARKS; NATURE RESERVES; COMMUNITY RESERVES; AND CONVERSION OF LOGGING, MINING, OR OTHER TYPES OF EXTRACTIVE CONCESSIONS TO FORMALLY PROTECTED AREAS. Applications above a quarter of a million dollars have fixed deadlines; smaller ones MAY BE SUBMITTED ON A ROLLING BASIS THROUGHOUT THE YEAR, and THERE IS NO FIXED UPPER LIMIT. Converting an existing logging or mining concession into a protected area is a named, fundable route. Where a concession has already been granted over the land you are defending, that is the door rather than a dead end. THE COMMUNITY LAND TENURE TRACK: for projects where indigenous or community land tenure is the primary strategy, the funder looks for cases where LAND OWNERSHIP, I.E. LAND TITLE, IS GRANTED TO A COMMUNITY RATHER THAN TO AN INDIVIDUAL OR AN NGO, or SUBSTANTIAL MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY OF THE AREA WILL BE LED BY THE INDIGENOUS PEOPLES OR LOCAL COMMUNITY, or THE GRANT IS DIRECTLY MANAGED BY AN INDIGENOUS OR LOCAL COMMUNITY-LED ORGANIZATION, including designation as A MULTIPLE-USE TERRITORY WITH MANAGEMENT (OR CO-MANAGEMENT) BY THE INDIGENOUS OR LOCAL COMMUNITY; such organisations are STRONGLY ENCOURAGED TO APPLY. Title to the community rather than to an NGO is a funding criterion here, not a complication. If your aim is communal title, this funder prefers it. WHEN PURCHASE IS THE STRATEGY, THE TEST IS URGENCY: for land purchase projects the funder asks that LAND IS LIKELY TO BE CONVERTED IN THE NEAR FUTURE IF PURCHASE IS NOT COMPLETED, that AN ALTERNATIVE PROTECTION STRATEGY IS NOT POSSIBLE, MORE EXPENSIVE, OR SIGNIFICANTLY LESS EFFECTIVE, and that CONSERVATION VALUE IS GREATER THAN EXPECTED BASED ON THE COST. Imminent conversion is the argument that wins a purchase grant. Document the threat — the permit application, the clearing, the road survey — as carefully as the biodiversity. WHO MAY APPLY, AND THE WARNING ABOUT MIDDLEMEN: ALL APPLICANTS MUST BE LEGALLY REGISTERED, NON-GOVERNMENT ORGANIZATIONS THAT ARE AUTHORIZED TO CONDUCT WORK IN THE COUNTRY, and partners SHOULD BE NGOs BASED IN THE COUNTRY OF THE PROPOSED PROTECTED AREA; the funder states plainly: YOU NEVER NEED TO PAY A CONSULTANT OR INTERMEDIARY TO APPLY FOR its funding, it ONLY REVIEW[S] APPLICATIONS SUBMITTED DIRECTLY BY ELIGIBLE ORGANIZATIONS, and WE WILL WORK WITH YOU TO REFINE YOUR PROPOSAL. Beyond acquisition it HELPS BUILD THE CAPACITY OF ITS PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS, including TRAINING FOR EMPLOYMENT AS FOREST GUARDS, WILDLIFE MONITORS AND ECO-GUIDES. Anyone offering to broker this application for a fee is to be refused. The funder says so itself, and it will help refine the proposal free.

trackers.name: Pro Bono Network of the Americas and its national clearinghouses - non-profits in 16 countries that place SOCIAL ORGANISATIONS with volunteer law firms free, plus free representation for cases at the merits stage before the inter-American commission
trackers.desc: THERE IS A CLEARINGHOUSE IN MOST OF THESE COUNTRIES WHOSE JOB IS TO FIND A LAW FIRM WILLING TO ACT FOR YOUR ORGANISATION FREE. Its members are NON-PROFIT ENTITIES THAT FACILITATE THE PROVISION OF FREE LEGAL SERVICES TO PEOPLE OF SCARCE RESOURCES, SECTORS OR GROUPS IN A CONDITION OF VULNERABILITY, ENTREPRENEURS AND SOCIAL ORGANISATIONS, WITH A VIEW TO IMPROVING ACCESS TO JUSTICE AND THE DEFENCE OF THE PUBLIC INTEREST; the network born in 2011 HAS NOW BECOME THE MAIN INSTITUTIONAL HOME OF THE PRIMARY PRO BONO CLEARINGHOUSES IN THE REGION and INCLUDES MORE THAN 20 ORGANIZATIONS, REPRESENTING 16 COUNTRIES, coordinated jointly by a New York bar association centre and a national pro bono foundation. Social organisations are named alongside individuals as eligible. A community association fighting a project is exactly the kind of client these clearinghouses were built to place. HOW A CASE ACTUALLY REACHES A LAWYER: one national foundation RECEIVES REQUESTS FOR PRO BONO CASES THROUGH ITS WEB PLATFORM OR OTHER ENTITIES, and ARTICULATES AND CHANNELS FREE LEGAL ADVICE, CARRIES OUT WORKSHOPS AND INFORMATIVE TALKS AND SEEKS TO GENERATE PUBLIC INFLUENCE; another states that cases ARRIVE AT THE FOUNDATION THROUGH the regional centre, the regional network, or national NGOs in contact with member firms and university professors, and that WHOEVER HAS A CASE OR A PROJECT FOR WHICH THEY NEED PRO BONO ADVICE MAY PRESENT IT BY SENDING AN EMAIL to a published address. One email with the case attached. That is the whole entry procedure in at least one country, and the others run a web form. THE HONEST LIMIT, STATED BY THE CLEARINGHOUSE ITSELF: one alliance RESERVES THE RIGHT TO EVALUATE AND DECIDE WHETHER A REQUEST MAY BE CONSIDERED A PRO BONO CASE; THE PRESENTATION OF A REQUEST DOES NOT GUARANTEE ITS ACCEPTANCE, NOR THE ASSIGNMENT OF A LAWYER OR FIRM; it ACTS ONLY AS AN INTERMEDIARY BETWEEN THE PERSON OR ORGANISATION REQUESTING AND THE VOLUNTEER LAWYERS, and taking a case DEPENDS EXCLUSIVELY ON THE VOLUNTARY DECISION OF THOSE LAWYERS OR FIRMS, WITHOUT ANY OBLIGATION OF SPONSORSHIP EXISTING. No guarantee, and no obligation on any firm. Apply to more than one clearinghouse, and make the request specific enough that a commercial firm can see the discrete piece of work being asked for. WHAT THE NETWORK COORDINATES BEYOND SINGLE CASES: volunteer lawyers and firms work on PARTICIPATION BEFORE THE INTER-AMERICAN SYSTEM OF HUMAN RIGHTS, COOPERATION TO SOCIAL ORGANISATIONS THAT REQUIRE LEGAL SUPPORT, THE ELABORATION OF THEMATIC REPORTS AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT TO INITIATIVES; under a collaboration agreement with the inter-American human rights commission the network PROVIDES PRO BONO LEGAL REPRESENTATION TO PEOPLE WITH CASES AT THE MERITS STAGE, the commission notifying petitioners of that opportunity. Free representation for a case already before the inter-American commission, arranged through this network. If a matter has reached that stage, ask the commission and the network at the same time. THE REGIONAL PROGRAMME AIMED AT SMALL ORGANISATIONS: under a civic space strengthening project the network HAS DECIDED TO JOIN FORCES TO SUPPORT THE NON-PROFIT INITIATIVES OF CENTRAL AMERICAN COUNTRIES BY MEANS OF ITS NETWORK OF LAWYERS TO PROVIDE FREE ADVICE TO APPLICANTS, with an application form; it also runs law student competitions and internship placements across member organisations. For the Central American countries there is a dedicated window rather than only the national clearinghouse. Use it, and note that the same network places law students who can do the document work.

trackers.name: The Alliance of Environmental Legal Clinics of Latin America and the Caribbean - more than 30 university clinics in 10 countries taking REAL, COLLECTIVE public-interest environmental cases free, with dam-affected and mining-affected communities among their clients
trackers.desc: MORE THAN THIRTY UNIVERSITY LEGAL CLINICS IN TEN COUNTRIES TAKE REAL ENVIRONMENTAL CASES FOR COMMUNITIES, FREE. The alliance ARTICULATES MORE THAN 30 CLINICS IN 10 COUNTRIES and has, since 2019, brought together universities WITH THE OBJECTIVE OF PROMOTING CLINICAL EDUCATION IN ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS AND STRENGTHENING THE FORMATION OF STUDENTS IN THE DEFENCE OF THE ENVIRONMENT AND HUMAN RIGHTS; one member clinic states that its course USES THE CLINICAL METHOD OF TEACHING LAW, BASED ON THE PRACTICE OF THE STUDENTS ON REAL AND NOT SIMULATED CASES, and that THESE CASES MUST ALWAYS BE OF PUBLIC INTEREST. Real cases, not exercises, and public interest is the entry condition. A community with a dispute and no money is what these clinics need in order to teach. WHAT THEY ARE, IN A CLINIC DIRECTOR'S WORDS: they are INSTANCES OF FORMAL TEACHING AND LEARNING AND AT THE SAME TIME OF SERVICE TO THE COMMUNITY AT A MOMENT WHEN THERE EXISTS A GREAT BARRIER OF ACCESS TO JUSTICE IN GENERAL; the initiative FOCUSES ON COLLECTIVE CASES AND EXERCISES THE DEFENCE OF ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS IN CASES OF PUBLIC INTEREST, seeking TO BALANCE THAT ASYMMETRY IN THE DEFENCE OF THE RIGHTS RELATED TO THE ENVIRONMENT. Collective cases are the speciality. Where the harm is shared by a whole village, that is the shape these clinics prefer, not a weakness in the claim. WHAT THEY HAVE ACTUALLY CARRIED: one university clinic CARRIES 22 CASES TO RESOLVE SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL AND PUBLIC HEALTH CONFLICTS in its country, including SUPPORT TO THE COMMUNITIES AFFECTED BY a named large dam, and a claim over mercury contamination from mining harming indigenous peoples; another works on mercury in the Amazon; students of two universities prepared AN AMICUS CURIAE in an unprecedented case on climate change and indigenous childhood; and in 2023 the network filed a report before the inter-American human rights court in an advisory opinion request on climate emergency, EXPRESSLY CITED IN THE FINAL DECISION. Twenty-two live cases in one clinic, and dam-affected communities among the clients. Ask the nearest clinic for its current case list before describing your own. THE OLDER NETWORK BESIDE IT, AND WHAT IT USES: a Latin American network of legal clinics aims TO STRENGTHEN CLINICAL TEACHING AND THROUGH THIS INSTRUMENT TO INTERVENE IN THE DEFENCE OF THE PUBLIC INTEREST AND HUMAN RIGHTS BY MEANS OF STRATEGIC LITIGATION AS A TOOL, its membership including named university clinics paired with human rights and environment centres in several cities. Some clinics are paired with an established rights centre. That combination gives a case both student capacity and an experienced litigating partner. HOW THEY WORK WITH COMMUNITIES: the method promotes ACTIVE LEARNING FROM THE APPROACH TO STATE ACTORS, CIVIL SOCIETY, LOCAL COMMUNITIES, EXPERTS... TO STRENGTHEN THE STRATEGIES OF APPROACHING THE CASES FROM EXPERIENCE; since 2022 the alliance also collaborates with a global network promoting STRUCTURED COLLABORATION BETWEEN UNIVERSITIES AND COMMUNITIES, sharing EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING, PARTICIPATORY PLANNING and social transformation. Structured collaboration between a university and a community is a defined programme, not a favour. Ask the clinic's coordinator which faculty course could adopt your case this term — the academic calendar, not the litigation calendar, decides when they can start.

trackers.name: Fondo de Acción Urgente para América Latina y el Caribe - rapid response grants of up to $5,000 decided in NO MORE THAN 10 WORKING DAYS for defenders under threat, plus a strategic window for organisations defending territories and common goods
trackers.desc: A REQUEST IS STUDIED IN NO MORE THAN TEN WORKING DAYS AND THE MONEY MOVES THREE DAYS AFTER APPROVAL. The fund's rapid response grants are A UNIQUE, FLEXIBLE, AND SHORT-TERM FINANCING MODEL... TO PROVIDE TIMELY AND STRATEGIC SUPPORT FOR ACTIONS THAT RESPOND TO SITUATIONS OF RISK OR THREATS THAT IMPACT THE SECURITY OF WOMEN ACTIVISTS AND DEFENDERS, THEIR COLLECTIVES, OR ORGANIZATIONS, or that TAKE ADVANTAGE OF OPPORTUNITIES TO ADVANCE OR DETER SETBACKS TO THE RIGHTS; ONCE A REQUEST IS RECEIVED, IT IS STUDIED DURING NO MORE THAN 10 WORKING DAYS. IF IT IS APPROVED, IT TAKES AT LEAST THREE WORKING DAYS TO TRANSFER THE RESOURCES, depending on each country's banking requirements. Applicants REGISTER their COLLECTIVE OR ORGANIZATION IN OUR ONLINE SYSTEM and make the request through it. Two weeks from request to money. When a defender has to leave home tonight or a hearing is next month, that is the only timescale in this file that matches the emergency. WHAT IT PAYS AND FOR HOW LONG: the support comprises FLEXIBLE RESOURCES (UP TO AN ALLOCATION OF 5,000 DOLLARS), GRANTED TO SUPPORT THE ACTIVISTS AND THEIR ORGANISATIONS IN A STRATEGIC AND TIMELY MANNER IN THE FACE OF UNFORESEEN AND UNPLANNED SITUATIONS THAT REQUIRE AN IMMEDIATE INTERVENTION, for a maximum of three months; THESE ACTIONS CANNOT BE ACTIVITIES OF PROGRAMMES AND/OR PROJECTS, and applicants MUST DEMONSTRATE THE URGENT CHARACTER OF THE UNFORESEEN AND UNPLANNED SITUATION. It will not pay for anything already in your workplan. Frame the request around what changed this month — the threat, the eviction date, the hearing — and nothing else. THE SECOND WINDOW, WHICH IS ABOUT TERRITORY: alongside the rapid grants the fund gives STRATEGIC SUPPORTS: TO STRENGTHEN THE PROCESSES OF RESISTANCE AND THE STRATEGIES OF THE ORGANISATIONS LED BY WOMEN, TRANS, NON-BINARY OR GENDER-DISSIDENT PEOPLE, THAT PROMOTE IN AN INTEGRATED MANNER THE PROTECTION OF THE TERRITORIES, THE COMMON GOODS AND THE RIGHTS; one recorded call was directed at LOCAL, DEPARTMENTAL OR NATIONAL ORGANISATIONS AND COLLECTIVES OF WOMEN AND/OR FEMINISTS THAT HAVE PERMANENT WORK AROUND THE DEFENCE OF THE TERRITORIES AND NATURE, and at MIXED COMMUNITY, INDIGENOUS, AFRO-DESCENDANT, RAIZAL AND PEASANT ORGANISATIONS THAT HAVE A SPECIFIC LINE OF WORK ON WOMEN'S RIGHTS LINKED TO ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE, AND IN WHICH WOMEN HAVE SIGNIFICANT LEADERSHIP. Mixed community, indigenous and peasant organisations qualify for the territorial window, not only women's organisations, provided women lead a strand of the work. That is a wider door than the fund's name suggests. WHO IT IS AND WHERE IT REACHES: it is THE REGIONAL FEMINIST FUND FOR SPANISH-SPEAKING LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, created in 2009 in one national capital as part of a global urgent action fund founded in 1997 that regionalised IN ORDER TO UNDERSTAND LOCAL CONTEXTS BETTER AND TO BE CLOSER TO THE WORK SITES OF GRASSROOTS ACTIVISTS, now AN INTERNATIONAL ALLIANCE OF THREE AUTONOMOUS SISTER FUNDS. Spanish-speaking countries only for this fund. If you are in Brazil, Guyana, Suriname, Haiti or the English-speaking Caribbean, ask which sister fund covers you before applying. WHAT IT FUNDS THE MONEY FOR: recorded lines are PROTECTION AND SECURITY, RESPONDING TO SITUATIONS OF RISK OR THREAT AGAINST THE SECURITY OF ACTIVISTS AND DEFENDERS, THEIR COLLECTIVES OR ORGANISATIONS, and opportunity grants that let a movement act before a window closes. Security costs — relocation, a lawyer's retainer, travel to a hearing — are exactly what this covers, and they are the costs that no project grant in this file will pay.

trackers.name: Protection grants for defenders at risk - up to €7,500 for LEGAL FEES OF THOSE BEING JUDICIALLY HARASSED, physical and digital security, medical and family costs, with a 24-hour hotline, plus emergency, relocation, trial-monitoring and respite programmes
trackers.desc: THESE GRANTS PAY THE LEGAL FEES OF SOMEONE BEING SUED OR PROSECUTED FOR DEFENDING LAND. The protection grants programme, launched in 2001 TO PROVIDE RAPID AND PRACTICAL FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS AT RISK, pays for IMPROVING PHYSICAL SECURITY OF AN ORGANISATION OR INDIVIDUAL, DIGITAL SECURITY AND COMMUNICATION SECURITY; SUPPORTING LEGAL FEES FOR HRDs WHO ARE BEING JUDICIALLY HARASSED; PAYING FOR MEDICAL FEES FOR HRDs WHO HAVE BEEN ATTACKED OR WHO HAVE SUFFERED A MEDICAL CONDITION AS A RESULT OF THEIR PEACEFUL HUMAN RIGHTS ACTIVITIES; PROVIDING FAMILY ASSISTANCE FOR IMPRISONED HRDs OR FAMILY MEMBERS WHO ARE AT RISK BECAUSE OF A HRD'S ACTIVITIES, up to a maximum of €7,500. Applications CAN BE SUBMITTED ANYTIME VIA THEIR ONLINE SYSTEM, and there is a 24-HOUR EMERGENCY HOTLINE. A criminal complaint or a defamation suit filed by a developer is judicial harassment, and the legal fees are payable. That is the single most common attack on land defenders in this file, and this is the grant written for it. WHAT IT WILL NOT FUND, WHICH DECIDES HOW YOU WRITE IT: the programme excludes RETROSPECTIVE FUNDING, INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS, ORGANISATIONS THAT HAVE APPLIED OR ARE ALREADY RECEIVING FUNDING FOR THE SAME PURPOSE ELSEWHERE, PROJECTS WHICH FOCUS ON BROADER HUMAN RIGHTS ISSUES RATHER THAN THE SPECIFIC SITUATION OF HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, COSTS FOR HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS WHO ARE ALREADY IN EXILE and ongoing office running costs; grants ARE GENERALLY NOT AWARDED FOR 100% OF THE PROPOSED BUDGET, and applicants must commit to return the grant if the work does not go ahead or is funded elsewhere. Write about the named people at risk, not about the campaign. A proposal that describes the environmental issue rather than the threat to specific defenders is refused on its own terms. THE OTHER EMERGENCY FUNDS THAT COVER THE SAME GROUND: a European defenders mechanism provides EMERGENCY GRANTS UP TO 10,000€ and runs a TEMPORARY RELOCATION PROGRAMME that funds a host organisation to relocate a defender, responding to AN INCREASED RISK, AN ANTICIPATED INCREASED RISK OR FOR A HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDER WHO HAS BEEN WORKING IN A DIFFICULT ENVIRONMENT FOR A PROLONGED PERIOD OF TIME AND WHO NEEDS A BREAK, covering REST AND RESPITE, PROFESSIONAL CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT... EMOTIONAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL WELL-BEING, FAMILY SUPPORT; a civil society lifeline fund covers LEGAL REPRESENTATION, PRISON VISITS, TRIAL MONITORING, TEMPORARY RELOCATION, EQUIPMENT REPLACEMENT, applying by email after describing a secure contact method, in several languages including Spanish; and a federation offers SECURE TRANSPORTATION, LEGAL SUPPORT, MEDICAL SUPPORT... HUMANITARIAN ASSISTANCE... URGENT RELOCATION, URGENT MONITORING. Trial monitoring is fundable, and so is a paid observer at the hearing. Where a case is being heard in a small town, an outside monitor changes how it is conducted. THE RESPITE OPTIONS WHEN SOMEONE MUST LEAVE: recorded schemes include a protective fellowship allowing UP TO TEN DEFENDERS PER YEAR to join a university centre FOR THE PURPOSES OF TRAINING, NETWORKING, AND REST, a foundation offering A YEAR LONG RESPITE PROGRAMME, a refuge for journalists forced to flee providing ADMINISTRATIVE, LEGAL AND SOCIAL ASSISTANCE, and a cities of refuge network offering PHYSICAL SAFETY AND ECONOMIC SECURITY FOR A TWO-YEARS FIXED PERIOD. Leaving for a year is not the end of a campaign if someone else can hold the file. Identify who that is before the threat arrives, because these programmes take applications from the person at risk and their host, not from a court. THE SECURITY WARNING BUILT INTO THE APPLICATION: applicants are asked to ENSURE THAT THE METHOD OF CONTACT YOU ARE PROVIDING IS SECURE AND THAT IT IS OK TO BE CONTACTED IN THAT WAY, and one fund asks applicants to describe HOW it CAN CONTACT YOU SECURELY BEFORE SENDING SENSITIVE INFORMATION. Do not send the details from a shared community email account. The application itself can expose the person it is meant to protect.

trackers.name: Inter-American Foundation grants - CURRENTLY PAUSED - direct grants of $25,000-$400,000 to grassroots organisations with no sector calls, no deadline, five application languages, and LAND AND LABOUR accepted as counterpart
trackers.desc: THIS FUNDER IS CURRENTLY PAUSED — CHECK BEFORE SPENDING TIME ON IT. Its own application page states: WE ARE CURRENTLY PAUSING GRANT FUNDING IN ALIGNMENT WITH EXECUTIVE ORDER REEVALUATING AND REALIGNING UNITED STATES FOREIGN AID. CHECK THIS PAGE FOR FURTHER UPDATES. It is AN INDEPENDENT AGENCY of that government. Everything below describes how it worked when open, and is recorded because the terms are unusual enough to be worth watching for. Read the page before writing anything. A funder under a foreign aid review can reopen with different rules, and the counterpart and eligibility terms are the first things such reviews change. WHY IT MATTERED: IT FUNDED GRASSROOTS GROUPS DIRECTLY, WITH NO INTERMEDIARY: it ONLY SUPPORT[S] COMMUNITY-LED PROJECTS SUBMITTED BY LOCAL AND GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS THAT ARE BASED IN INDEPENDENT COUNTRIES OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, requiring proof that YOUR ORGANIZATION HAS A HISTORY OF WORKING TOGETHER AS A GROUP AND IS CAPABLE OF EFFECTIVELY USING GRANTS FUNDS; it DOES NOT IDENTIFY PROBLEMS OR SUGGEST PROJECTS; INSTEAD IT RESPONDS TO INITIATIVES PRESENTED, and PROJECTS ARE SELECTED FOR FUNDING ON THEIR MERITS RATHER THAN BY SECTOR. Grants ran FROM US$25,000 TO $400,000 OVER ONE TO FOUR YEARS, with proposals accepted 365 DAYS A YEAR in SPANISH, PORTUGUESE, ENGLISH, FRENCH, OR HAITIAN CREOLE. No sector calls, no themes, no deadline. A community proposing its own solution in its own language is the entire model, and it is worth having a proposal ready if the pause lifts. THE COUNTERPART RULE, WHICH IS THE PART TO UNDERSTAND: all funded organisations must COMMIT RESOURCES TO ADVANCE THEIR DEVELOPMENT INITIATIVES, called counterpart; COUNTERPART FUNDING MUST BE A COMPONENT OF THE BUDGET... BUT NO MINIMUM AMOUNT IS REQUIRED. HIGHER COUNTERPART FUNDING MAKES A PROPOSAL MORE ATTRACTIVE, and it MAY BE IN CASH DONATIONS OR IN KIND, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, LAND, SUPPLIES, INFRASTRUCTURE, LABOR, AND OFFICE, STORAGE AND MEETING SPACE. Salaries are A LEGITIMATE EXPENSE. Land and volunteer labour count as counterpart. A community that owns the site and works it has already met the requirement without spending anything. WHAT IT LOOKED FOR IN A PROPOSAL: CREATIVE USE OF THE COMMUNITY'S RESOURCES; A DIVERSE ARRAY OF COMMUNITY VOICES IN PROJECT DEVELOPMENT AND EXECUTION; SUBSTANTIAL BENEFICIARY ENGAGEMENT in identifying the problem, choosing the approach, designing the project and managing it; PARTNERSHIPS WITH LOCAL GOVERNMENT, THE BUSINESS COMMUNITY AND OTHER CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS; feasibility, sustainability, measurable results and EVIDENCE OF BENEFICIARIES' ENHANCED CAPACITY FOR SELF-GOVERNANCE; its recorded interests included COMMUNITY CONSERVATION; AND LOCAL MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES (FORESTS, FISHERIES, ETC.). Partnership with the local government is a scoring criterion. That is the argument for bringing your municipality into the proposal rather than fighting it. THE EXCLUSIONS AND THE FIELD OFFICE RULE: support was limited to independent countries of the region, with recorded exclusions of two countries and a period when FUNDING IN THE CARIBBEAN was RESTRICTED TO three named states; public universities could not apply directly BUT MAY PARTNER WITH AN ORGANIZATION THAT IS ELIGIBLE; and an organisation headquartered abroad could apply only if its field office CAN DEMONSTRATE LOCAL LEADERSHIP. Local leadership had to be demonstrated, not asserted. Where an outside NGO offers to apply on your behalf, insist that your own organisation is the applicant.

trackers.name: RedLAC - the network of 32 national and regional ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS in 20 countries, permanent conservation trust institutions financing protected areas and local communities, with a published member list by country and zone
trackers.desc: THIRTY-TWO NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS IN TWENTY COUNTRIES, AND THE NETWORK PUBLISHES WHICH ONE COVERS YOURS. It GROUPS 32 ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS FROM 20 COUNTRIES OF THE REGION, UNITING EFFORTS TO PROTECT THE RICH BIODIVERSITY OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, with its member list filterable by zone — Caribbean, Mesoamerica and South America — alongside regional funds; more than twenty-five years old, it counts MORE THAN 100 ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS WORLDWIDE. Find the fund for your country on that member page. These are permanent national institutions with endowments, not project offices that close when a grant ends. WHAT THESE FUNDS DO, IN THE NETWORK'S WORDS: they HAVE DEMONSTRATED TO BE A KEY MECHANISM IN THE SUSTAINABLE FINANCING OF BIODIVERSITY AND IN THE STRENGTHENING OF PROTECTED AREAS AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, with a role in THE PROTECTION OF NATURAL AREAS AND THE SUPPORT TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES, described as MULTIDIMENSIONAL FUNDS, WITH APPROACHES THAT INTEGRATE PROTECTION OF BIODIVERSITY, CLIMATIC RESILIENCE AND COMMUNITY EMPOWERMENT. Support to local communities is named alongside protected areas. A community managing land next to a park is inside the mandate, not adjacent to it. SOME OF THE MEMBERS BY NAME AND KIND: recorded members include a Caribbean biodiversity fund, a national forever-protection association in one Central American country, an action fund and a Pacific foundation in one Andean country, a nature fund in one southern country, an island life fund and a regional marine fund — the last two showing that funds exist for a single archipelago and for a shared sea as well as for whole countries. There are funds scoped to one archipelago and to one reef system. If your site sits in either, that narrower fund is a better fit than the national one. WHAT THE NETWORK ITSELF OFFERS ITS MEMBERS: joining gives funds THE OPPORTUNITY TO CONNECT AND COLLABORATE WITH OTHER MEMBERS OF THE NETWORK THROUGHOUT THE REGION, to SHARE KNOWLEDGE, RESOURCES AND EXPERIENCES TO IMPROVE THEIR CAPACITIES, and ACCESS TO A WIDE VARIETY OF RESOURCES AND TOOLS, with TRAINING AND ADVICE ON DIVERSE THEMES, FROM PROJECT MANAGEMENT TO COMMUNICATION AND ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION. Where your country has no environmental fund, this network is where one would be built, and it trains new members. That is a long project, but it is the route. WHY THEY MATTER FOR PERMANENT PROTECTION: these funds are conservation trust funds — institutions holding capital whose returns finance protected areas and community work year after year, and the network works alongside a global environment facility, an African funds consortium and a large conservation finance initiative on that model. An endowment pays for wardens and monitoring long after a campaign ends. Where a protected area has just been declared, the next question is which of these funds can endow its running costs.

trackers.name: The ICCA Consortium and the international register of territories of life - a community-reviewed register open to any well-defined community with its own governance, plus national catalytic organisations, documentation workshops and life plan support
trackers.desc: A COMMUNITY CAN PUT ITS OWN TERRITORY ON AN INTERNATIONAL REGISTER, REVIEWED BY OTHER COMMUNITIES RATHER THAN BY OFFICIALS. The international register IS A TOOL DEVELOPED TO SERVE AS SUPPORT AND RECOGNITION TO THOSE COMMUNITIES WITH OUTSTANDING VALUES IN GOVERNANCE AND CONSERVATION OF NATURE, run by a United Nations environment body with the consortium and a commons organisation; its PEER REVIEW PROTOCOL is A CONSENSUS DOCUMENT IN WHICH THE DIFFERENT STEPS THAT EACH COMMUNITY MUST TAKE IN ORDER TO FORM PART OF THE REGISTER ARE DESCRIBED, including SUBMITTING TO A PROCESS OF REVIEW OF THE CANDIDATURE BY ANONYMOUS MEMBERS (REVIEWERS) OF OTHER SIMILAR COMMUNITIES THAT ALREADY FORM PART OF THE REGISTER. Other communities judge the application, and the protocol is published so you can read the test before applying. Registration is a public record of who governs the land, made without asking the state's permission. WHAT QUALIFIES AS ONE OF THESE TERRITORIES: they exist IN ANY TYPE OF CULTURE AND ECOSYSTEM WHERE THERE IS A COMMUNITY LINKED TO A TERRITORY, WITH ITS OWN SYSTEM OF GOVERNANCE, AND THAT GIVES POSITIVE RESULTS IN TERMS OF CONSERVATION OF NATURE AND LIVELIHOODS FOR THE COMMUNITY; the first defining characteristic is that THE AREA OR TERRITORY MUST HAVE A WELL DEFINED COMMUNITY, WITH A CLEAR LINK TO A TERRITORY ALSO WELL DEFINED. A well defined community and a well defined territory. Neither a formal title nor a state designation is in that test. WHO THE CONSORTIUM IS AND WHAT ITS MEMBERS DO: it is AN INTERNATIONAL NON-PROFIT ASSOCIATION DEDICATED TO SUPPORTING INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES THAT GOVERN AND CONSERVE THEIR LANDS, WATERS AND TERRITORIES, its members from more than eighty countries acting on themes including THE DOCUMENTATION, SUSTAINING AND DEFENCE OF THE TERRITORIES OF LIFE, and comprising ALMOST 180 MEMBERS (ORGANISATIONS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND COMMUNITY ORGANISATIONS, TOGETHER WITH THE CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS THAT SUPPORT THEM) AND MORE THAN 420 HONORARY MEMBERS. Community organisations are members in their own right, alongside the NGOs that support them. Ask the national focal point how your organisation joins. WHAT THE REGIONAL NETWORK ACTUALLY DELIVERS: the Latin American network runs workshops WITH THE AIM OF SHARING KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERIENCES COMING FROM THE TERRITORIES, including a practical workshop on the register itself, a case study workshop drawing on one country's experience, and one on a GUIDE OF SELF-STRENGTHENING: A GUIDE FROM COMMUNITIES FOR COMMUNITIES; communities are recorded pursuing PROCESSES OF DOCUMENTATION, THE CONSTRUCTION OF LIFE PLANS, THE register AND THE STRENGTHENING OF THEIR OWN GOVERNANCE. A life plan is the document that states what a community will and will not permit on its land. Building one is the work these workshops exist to support. WHAT IT HAS SUPPORTED ON THE GROUND: in one country an observatory and a named indigenous community organised A WORKSHOP OF EXCHANGE OF KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERIENCES, ATTENDED BY TWENTY-FIVE REPRESENTATIVES OF TEN INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, TO EXCHANGE ABOUT LEGAL AND NON-LEGAL STRATEGIES OF TERRITORIAL DEFENCE AND PROTECTION; in another, five indigenous peoples, an Afro-descendant community and a coastal community met with a foundation and the small grants programme TO DEBATE AND DECIDE ON THE WORLD REGISTER; national members have planned A STUDY OF THE EXISTING LEGAL FRAMEWORK ON CONSERVATION AND RIGHTS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, ACTIONS FOR COMMUNITY STRENGTHENING AND A NATIONAL ADVOCACY STRATEGY; a global support initiative works through NATIONAL CATALYTIC ORGANISATIONS in more than twenty-six priority countries. Ask which organisation is the national catalytic body for your country. It is the one already funded to accompany communities through documentation and registration.

trackers.name: Mapeo and its successor - a free, offline, open-source mapping and evidence toolset built with Amazonian indigenous partners, where ALL DATA IS OWNED BY THE COMMUNITY, exporting shapefiles and reports for lawsuits and land claims
trackers.desc: A FREE OFFLINE APP THAT TURNS A PHONE INTO AN EVIDENCE RECORDER, AND THE COMMUNITY KEEPS THE DATA. It is A FREE DIGITAL TOOLSET FOR DOCUMENTING, MONITORING, AND MAPPING MANY TYPES OF DATA, OFFLINE-FIRST OPEN-SOURCE TECHNOLOGY needing NO INTERNET OR SPECIAL HARDWARE... TO COLLECT, VIEW, OR SHARE DATA; WITH THE PUSH OF A BUTTON, CONTRIBUTORS CAN GATHER MAP DATA BY LINKING GPS POINTS, PHOTOS, AND NOTES, and ALL DATA IS COMPLETELY OWNED BY THE COMMUNITIES THEMSELVES, exchanged between phones by a peer-to-peer sync that works OVER A LOCAL WIFI NETWORK WITHOUT NEEDING A CONNECTION. No signal, no server, no subscription, and nobody else holds the file. For a community watching a road survey or a clearing crew, that is the difference between a rumour and an exhibit. WHAT IT WAS BUILT TO BE USED FOR: it was CO-DESIGNED AND DEVELOPED WITH INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES WHO FACE THREATS TO THEIR LAND SUCH AS ILLEGAL GOLD MINING, OIL CONTAMINATION AND POACHING, and built TO SUPPORT THEM TO DOCUMENT THESE ACTIVITIES IN ORDER TO TAKE COMMUNITY ACTION AGAINST THEM, TO REPORT THEM TO AUTHORITIES, FILE LAWSUITS, LAUNCH MEDIA CAMPAIGNS, OR CREATE MAPS FOR LAND CLAIMS; it allows USERS TO COLLECT EVIDENCE IN THE FIELD, SUCH AS PHOTOGRAPHS AND GPS POINTS, AND ORGANIZE THIS DATA FOR ACTIONS SUCH AS WHISTLEBLOWING AND CLAIMING LAND RIGHTS. Filing a lawsuit and making a map for a land claim are the stated purposes. Set up the categories to match what a court or a ministry will ask for, before the incursion happens. THE CASE THAT SHOWS WHAT IT IS WORTH: in one country OVER TWENTY indigenous COMMUNITIES DEFENDED THEIR TERRITORY... AGAINST THE IMPOSITION OF DEVASTATING OIL EXPLORATION PROPOSED BY THE GOVERNMENT, having USED the tool FOR OVER FOUR YEARS TO RECORD TERRITORIAL DATA ...AND MAPS, WHICH THEY USED AS EVIDENCE AGAINST THE government; the account records: THEY WON! Four years of routine recording before the case existed. The evidence that wins these cases is gathered long before anyone knows there will be a case.
