Replacement land is a stated option, and its quality is specified. The statute speaks of exchanging as well as taking back, and requires prior agreement on the replacement plot's location, size, condition and quality — not merely its existence. Where an exchange is offered, those four attributes are the ones to get written down, because a plot of equal area on worse ground is the commonest form of a bad settlement. The constitutional frame, and the phrase everything turns on. The constitution provides that the state may, on the basis of state special needs, exchange or take back land with compensation, and may confiscate land used in a manner harmful to public health, the protection of nature or national security; and that where the state or its competent body requisitions private property on the basis of overriding public need, it shall pay compensation and price. The operative phrase is state special needs: ask which special need is being invoked, and where and by whom it was declared, before arguing about the money. The owner's entitlement appears in the rights section too. Among the rights of an owner the law lists the right to receive compensation as provided by the law where the land is exchanged or taken back for state special needs, and a separate article deals with the guarantees of the citizen's ownership right in exactly that situation. Read this with the local protection route through the soum council, the human rights commission and its defenders committee, the national environmental NGO council and the inspection agency entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Соёлын өвийг хамгаалах — protection zones set with professional bodies, a building rule inside them, and rewards for citizens who act
trackers.desc: Protection zones are set jointly with professional organisations, and submitted upward. The cultural heritage protection law makes it the duty of the local administrative bodies to carry out, together with professional organisations, the work of establishing the protection zones of world and national cultural heritage sites, and to submit that work to the competent authority. For a community, the practical consequence is that the zone boundary is produced locally with expert input before it is confirmed elsewhere — so the moment to be heard about where the line runs is at the aimag or soum stage, not after a national confirmation. Inside a protection zone, building is allowed only in a form that does not damage the monument. The revised text provides that, in order to improve the conservation and protection of an immovable monument within the protection zone of a historical and cultural site, new buildings may be erected and used for research and promotional purposes only in a form that causes no damage to the monument's original appearance and integrity, with the criteria for height limits approved jointly by the government members responsible for urban development and for culture. A height limit approved by two ministries is a concrete document to ask for when a structure is proposed near a monument. Citizens who act are to be rewarded, and illegal digging stopped. Among the duties of the responsible bodies are rewarding citizens, enterprises and organisations that have taken an active and initiative-taking part in protecting cultural heritage, halting illegal excavation of immovable historical and cultural monuments, and acting on information about cultural heritage violations; local authorities are also to support the work of the protection administrations of world and national heritage sites, and to take measures to rescue, restore and conserve heritage in danger of destruction or damage. Two further provisions worth knowing. Soum and district protected historical and cultural sites may be given to tourism organisations for use under contract — so where a site is being commercially used, there is a contract to ask for. And an owner of a valuable or invaluable historical and cultural item must immediately notify the cultural heritage register, the governor and the police if it is lost, must offer any invaluable item first to the state if selling, and may not transfer such an item into the ownership of a foreign citizen, foreign legal person or stateless person. Read this with the local protection route through the soum council, the professional inspection agency, the bar association's public interest committee and the land for state special needs entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Иргэнд газар өмчлүүлэх — one free allocation per family, joint ownership on request, and a governor who must record the minute your application arrived
trackers.desc: There is a state guide that walks through the allocation. The land relations guide published for citizens sets out the ownership route step by step — who may own, how much, where to apply and what the application must say — and reproduces the statutory sizes. It is the page to read before the statute. Land can only be owned by citizens, and each family gets one free allocation. The constitution provides that land other than pasture, common-tenure land and land for state special needs may be given into ownership only to citizens; foreigners and stateless persons hold use rights only. The allocation statute that followed gives each citizen one free allocation for family needs, sized by location: published summaries record up to 0.07 hectares in the capital, up to 0.35 in an aimag centre, up to 0.5 in a soum centre or village, and up to 0.07 along the state roads linking the capital to aimag centres. Pasture, forest and water fund land, land for special needs and public-use land in settlements — streets, squares, roads, recreation and sports areas, parks, cemeteries, waste and treatment sites — are outside the scheme. Citizens can ask to own jointly, and the request goes in the application. The application is made to the soum or district governor, and the statute lists what it must contain: each family member's names and civil registration number, the applicant's address and telephone, the administrative unit where the land lies, the purpose and size sought — and, where citizens wish to own the land together or as a group, a request to that effect. That last item is the one worth knowing: joint ownership by several households is something the application form itself contemplates, not a special arrangement to be argued for afterwards. Your place in the queue is a recorded fact. On receiving the application the governor records the order of receipt and the year, month, day, hour and minute. Where allocations in an area are contested or limited, that record is the document to ask for. The citizen's own obligation is to have a cadastral map made of the parcel. And the state must negotiate before taking it back. Among the central land authority's duties is to agree in advance with the owner, on the government's behalf, on exchanging or taking back citizen-owned land for state special needs with compensation — so once land is owned, the route to it runs through a negotiation with the owner rather than a unilateral decision. The authority also consolidates the proposals of aimag and capital governors on the location, purpose and size of land to be allocated and registers them soum by soum, which is where to look for what is actually available locally. Read this with the nökhörlöl partnership route, the local protection designation by the soum khural, the parcel information system and the state special needs compensation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Licensed valuers — the finance ministry's list, the contract the valuation runs on, and the annual return naming who did the work
trackers.desc: The finance ministry publishes who holds a valuation licence. Valuation of assets is a licensed activity: the statute defines a valuer as the holder of a special licence to carry out asset valuation, and the ministry publishes lists of licence holders together with guidance for those applying. Where a household or a community is confronted with an official figure for land or property, the first check is whether the person who produced it is on that list, and the second is whether the community can commission someone from it who is not connected to the other side. Licence holders are issued a certificate on a form approved by the finance minister, and a valuation firm may operate branches, each of which must have at least one full-time licensed valuer. The valuation runs on a contract, and the statute says what goes in it. Valuation is carried out on the basis of a contract agreed between the client and the valuation legal entity, and the law sets out the matters that contract must contain. Valuation itself is defined as the independent activity of the valuer directed at establishing the value of the object, with the resulting value being the monetary amount established, arrived at on a stated valuation basis — market or non-market. Asking which basis was used, and requiring it to be stated, is the most direct way to test a figure that seems low without needing to be a valuer oneself. Who did the work is reported annually. A valuation legal entity must submit electronically to the professional valuation body the list of valuations it carried out during the year together with the names of the valuers, experts and assistants who took part. That return is a record that connects a named individual to a particular piece of work, which matters when the same handful of firms value everything in a district. The statute also carries conflict-of-interest provisions reaching the officials and influential persons of a client's parent and subsidiary companies. Where this fits. The compensation entry recorded for this country turns on six matters that must be agreed before land is taken, including the quality of any replacement plot; the figure behind that agreement comes from a valuer. Read this with the state special needs compensation entry, the citizen land allocation route, the parcel information system and the state central laboratory entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The investigative newsroom, the press institute behind it, and the reporters' association — where a resource story goes here
trackers.desc: There is a nonprofit investigative newsroom, and an institute that trains into it. Reporting by the global investigative journalism network records that the country's first international investigative reporting conference, held in the capital and drawing over a hundred attendees from ten countries, launched the Mongolian Centre for Investigative Journalism — described as the first nonprofit investigative newsroom in Central Asia. The conference was organised by the Press Institute of Mongolia, itself a member of that network, with a German broadcaster's academy and a local television station. For a community sitting on documents about a licence, a concession or a rehabilitation account, those two bodies are the addressees: a newsroom built for long-form investigation, and an institute that trains and convenes the reporters who do it. The network behind it is wider than one newsroom. The same account records that the conference grew out of roundtables convened by journalists who had attended the global investigative conference abroad, that those meetings sparked stories across nineteen media outlets in the country, and that they established a network of journalism educators and reporters intent on expanding investigative work. Separately, an association of investigative journalists was formed after a foundation-run training workshop, acting as a support network for people working in the field. A story rejected by one outlet is therefore not a dead end: the same network runs through many newsrooms. The beat context is resources. The reporting sets the scene plainly — a country of about three million people with vast mineral resources, a multinational race to develop them, and corruption ranked poorly on the international perception index at the time. That is the reason an investigative newsroom exists here, and it is also why mining licences, rehabilitation guarantees and land allocations are the stories these newsrooms are equipped to follow. Check the current position before relying on this. The founding account dates from 2017; newsroom names, staffing and even survival change, and this entry does not verify the centre's present state. Confirm who is publishing now before sending material, and ask what protections they offer sources. Read this with the transparency account portal, the environmental rehabilitation guarantee, the corruption complaint route and the local development fund entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The court decisions database — read how similar claims were decided, and the evidence standard for a public-interest claim
trackers.desc: Court decisions are published and searchable, case by case. The judiciary operates an electronic database of court decisions, with individual judgments available on their own pages and filters by date and court category. For a community deciding whether to litigate, that database answers the question that matters most before spending money: how have courts here actually treated a claim like this one, and on what did those claims turn. Reading three decisions in the relevant category is cheaper than an opinion and more concrete than advice. An administrative case in the database shows both the target and the standard. One published decision concerns oversight of a governor's compliance with obligations undertaken by law and by contract to protect and rehabilitate the environment, to protect public health and to remit payments to the local budget — recording that compliance with those obligations had been supervised and enforced. The same decision records the court's approach to standing on public interest grounds: it notes that an administrative contract is a construction or investment carrying out state functions for the common benefit, and that the claimant had brought the claim without proving by well-founded evidence that public rights and interests had been violated or might be violated. That sentence is the practical instruction. A public-interest claim here is not defeated by the subject matter; it is defeated by arriving without evidence that the public right is engaged. Before filing, assemble the specific documents that show the harm or the risk — the contract obligation that was not performed, the payment not made, the monitoring result, the inspection finding — rather than relying on the general public interest in the environment. How to use the database. Search the administrative category for decisions involving local governors, mining licences, land allocation and rehabilitation obligations; note which claims failed for want of evidence and which succeeded and on what documents; and take those decisions to whichever lawyer you engage, so the conversation starts from the court's own reasoning. Read this with the bar association's public interest committee, the state legal aid centre, the environmental rehabilitation guarantee account and the transparency account portal entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Filing the annual activity report online — the registration authority's channel, and the donor tax relief that no longer exists
trackers.desc: The activity report a non-governmental organisation must file can now be sent through the national digital services system. The state registration authority announces that non-governmental organisations may submit their activity reports through the government's electronic services system, alongside the registration legislation and package of registration laws it publishes. For a community body that has registered in order to hold donations, filing that report is the obligation that keeps the registration alive, and doing it online removes the trip to the capital that used to be part of it. Keep the file the report is built from. The same authority publishes transparency headings that show what a reporting body is expected to be able to produce: the previous year's budget performance, the current year's budget and next year's draft, budget execution together with half-yearly and full-year financial statements and audit conclusions, explanations of savings and overruns, goods and services purchased at or above a stated value with the supplier's name and address, and income and expenditure movements at or above that value other than salary costs. Build the bookkeeping around those categories from the start and the report writes itself. Donor tax relief was removed, and that changes the pitch. A justice ministry study on renewing the non-governmental organisations legislation records that the regulation giving donors a tax concession was repealed. A community asking local businesses for money should therefore not promise a deduction; the case has to be made on the project itself. The same study describes the sector as working in wide cooperation with government, the private sector and donor organisations, and as playing a complementing role where public policy has not reached a group. What this is and is not. This entry is the reporting and filing side of holding money, not a permit to solicit from the public; the search for a general public collection statute for this country did not establish one, and this file does not assert what it could not verify. The conservation finance package and the citizen land allocation entries recorded elsewhere in this country's entries remain the two routes to money that are documented here. Read this with those entries, the bar association's public interest committee and the court decisions database entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: OT Watch and the herder complaint route — a national NGO that files to lenders' grievance mechanisms and trains herders to do it
trackers.desc: A national organisation exists whose work is filing community complaints against financed projects. Published profiles record a non-profit established around 2009 and 2010 whose stated purpose is compliance monitoring of the mining industry, protection of human rights, restoration of violated rights, research, training and advocacy; that it works with communities affected by projects financed by the development banks and the international finance institution in the extractive, energy and infrastructure sectors; that it focuses on indigenous peoples, land rights, rural communities and women in relation to dams, energy, infrastructure, mining, natural resources and water; and that it supports nomadic herders through capacity building and training in applying international environmental and human rights standards to their own community cases. That last point is the one that matters most: it teaches communities to run the complaint, not only to be represented in it. The route it uses is the lender's grievance mechanism, and it has produced results. Reported accounts record that in 2012 and 2013 herders, assisted by a local organisation and this one, filed complaints to the finance institution's ombudsman about involuntary resettlement and economic displacement, and about the diversion of a seasonal river through the mining lease and its effects on water systems, pasture yields and traditional livelihoods; and that a further series of complaints went to a development bank's project complaint mechanism about pasture fragmentation, dust and road and infrastructure impacts. Reporting records that after several years and three independent expert reviews, damages were established and a tripartite council signed a complaint resolution agreement of sixty items in 2017, the ombudsman closing the complaint in 2019 on the promise of implementation. The limits are recorded too. Herders reported that a bank compliance review did not discuss the personal experiences they had relayed to the expert during the site visit; the agreement still required implementation; and reporting records that the organisation's director has faced criminal charges connected to her advocacy. Treat these mechanisms as slow, and the personal risk to named advocates as real. Who else is in the coalition. Reported accounts name a coalition including a centre for human rights and development, a citizens' alliance centre, a steppes organisation and local groups such as a soil-focused body based in the affected soum, alongside international accountability organisations. Read this with the court decisions database, the bar association's public interest committee, the conservation finance package and the rehabilitation guarantee entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Байгаль орчны нөлөөллийн үнэлгээ — the detailed assessment must formally collect residents' views, and the assessment database is open to the public
trackers.desc: The company doing the detailed assessment must formally take residents' views while it is still drafting. The environmental impact assessment legislation provides that the legal entity carrying out a project's detailed assessment shall, during preparation of the report, officially collect proposals from the administration of the territory where the project will be implemented and from local citizens and residents affected by it, and organise a discussion. It further provides that the central state administrative body decides whether the project may proceed on the basis of the detailed assessment report, the expert's and professional council's conclusions, and those collected views. Getting a written submission into the report while it is being drafted therefore reaches the decision file, not just the public record. The proponent must present the report to affected residents. The Act provides that the project implementer and the professional organisation that carried out the assessment shall jointly organise the presentation of the detailed assessment report to local residents affected by the project, and that public participation is regulated by a procedure approved by the minister responsible for the environment. Ask when that presentation is scheduled and who is being invited. The assessment database is open, and its contents are listed. The assessment procedure provides that the database contains all legal documents relating to assessment, brief presentations of assessment reports, the verification conclusion together with measures taken on it and their implementation, the annual environmental management plan, report and special account guarantee information, and state inspectors' inspection information with the measures taken and their implementation. Companies that carried out a detailed assessment must enter the report presentation into the database, with the original report kept in the central body's archive for five years. A resident can ask the local governor for more. Amending provisions record that assessments of projects being implemented in a territory are held openly in the assessment database, and that a citizen has the right to submit a request to the governor of the aimag, capital, soum or district for additional information on the state of subsoil resource use, environmental impact, rehabilitation, and the measures being implemented by authorised state bodies in the course of supervision. The Act also places a duty on banks, financial and investment organisations not to finance or lend for production or services harmful to the environment, society or human health, and requires the assessing entity to insure the risks connected with its assessment work. Read this with the herder complaint route, the court decisions database, the conservation finance package and the bar association's public interest committee entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Pasture rules in the Land Law — the bag assembly decides pasture disputes first, camps may be held jointly by a hot ail, and no one may hold pasture alone
trackers.desc: A pasture dispute is decided first by the bag's own citizens' assembly. Official guidance on the land legislation records the provision that any dispute arising over pasture use is discussed and settled by the bag citizens' general assembly, and if no agreement is reached, decided by the soum governor. That is the first forum, it is inside the community, and it is cheaper and faster than anything above it. The same guidance records that herders have the right to use pasture in common. Winter and spring camps can be held jointly, but not by one household alone. The law provides that land beneath winter and spring camps may be held jointly by citizens as a hot ail — the traditional household cluster. Published analysis of court reasoning records that there is no provision at all in the law for winter, spring, summer or autumn pasture to be granted to any person to possess alone. That single sentence is the answer to a claim that someone has acquired exclusive rights over a customary camp. The soum governor sets the dates, and the bag's proposal is the basis. The law provides that the dates for clearing livestock from and returning them to winter and spring pasture are set by the soum or district governor, taking account of that year's pasture yield and citizens' proposals, with bag and khoroo governors and citizens implementing them; and that in order to protect specific winter and spring pastures from degradation and to restore them, the soum governor may allow herders to use them in groups under conditions and an agreement, taking account of regional characteristics, the tradition of pasture use, and the land's carrying capacity, on the basis of a proposal from the bag citizens' general assembly. Getting the bag assembly to make that proposal is the mechanism. Boundaries are fixed with the neighbours present. Guidance on possession records that the land office or the soum land officer determines access and boundaries in the presence of the applicant and the owners, possessors and users of neighbouring parcels, fixing turning point coordinates to cadastral mapping accuracy, drafting the governor's order where there is no conflict and returning the file with a written reply where there is; and that no person may possess land without a valid certificate of right. It also records that where pasture problems sharpen, herders can act through public organisations, herder groups and partnerships. Read this with the partnership entry, the local development fund, the soum khural protection route and the herder complaint entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Water Law protection zones and the basin council — the ordinary protection zone's prohibitions, the thousand-metre urban band, and the citizens' assembly that sets the boundary
trackers.desc: The basin council exists to put residents' views into water decisions, and its powers are listed. The water legislation provides that a basin council shall have citizens' proposals reflected in decisions on protecting and rationally using water; give opinions on projects to accumulate or use water resources, to run large mining operations, and to build dams and canals; monitor implementation of the basin administration's water management plan and refer detected breaches to the competent body for correction and liability; monitor whether a water user is fully performing its contract obligations, and whether it is fully performing the duties accepted in its environmental impact assessment to reduce adverse impact, remedy damage caused and rehabilitate; and monitor observance of the special and ordinary protection and sanitary zone regimes and protect the headwaters and surroundings of water sources. That monitoring duty is the thing to invoke when an operator's assessment commitments are not being met. The protection zones are set by the local citizens' representatives' assembly. Official guidance records that the law establishes special and ordinary protection zones and sanitary zones for water resources, with certain activities prohibited in them, and that such a zone is determined by the citizens' representatives' assembly of the province, capital, soum or district on the basis of the environment ministry's opinion. A community can therefore ask its own khural to set a zone, not only ask the ministry. The ordinary zone's prohibitions are specific. A joint ministerial order records that in the ordinary protection zone it is prohibited to prospect for or extract widely distributed minerals; to build or use structures discharging waste water without treatment facilities or not connected to sewerage; to store petroleum products, chemicals or radioactive substances; and to build or use substandard waste water pits or latrines; that extraction of less widely distributed minerals in that zone is decided specially, on the basis of an environmental impact assessment conclusion, taking account of the water body's resources, regime and hydrogeological conditions; and that in the territory of state and provincial-grade towns the zone extends up to one thousand metres from the shore of a water body. A separate statute bars mining outright in headwater and water protection areas. A published court decision records the law prohibiting prospecting and mining for minerals in river headwater formation areas, in the protection zones of water bodies, and in forest areas, and records a company returning the overlapping part of its licensed area after the government resolution fixing those boundaries. Read this with the pasture rules, the rehabilitation guarantee, the soum-level protection route and the inspectors entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Law on Fauna — the soum citizens' assembly fixes the hunting zones, a commercial hunting contract needs its decision first, and hunting territory is defined to include land, forest and water
trackers.desc: The local citizens' assembly decides where hunting may happen at all. The law on fauna provides that the soum or district citizens' representatives' assembly establishes the hunting zones within the distribution territory of game animals, on the basis of the hunting management plan; and that the habitat territory of game animals covers the land, forest and water where conditions for those animals to live are present. That definition matters because it brings forest and water into a wildlife question, and the assembly that fixes the zones is the same local body already recorded in this bucket for pasture and protection zones. A commercial hunting contract requires the assembly's decision as a precondition. The law provides that the soum governor concludes a contract for commercial hunting or capture only with a legal entity that satisfies stated conditions: a decision of the soum citizens' representatives' assembly; professional staff and hunters; and a plan of measures to protect and propagate game animals, with the financial capacity to implement it. Asking to see those three things is how a commercial hunting operation is tested locally. Parts of a hunting zone may be given to citizens or legal entities to hold under contract for protecting and sustainably using the resource. Rare animals are defined, and the categories decide what is possible. The law defines a rare animal as one whose numbers have fallen in its distribution territory, with a small stock and at risk of extinction, and provides for biotechnical measures for animals' living and feeding conditions. Published policy material records the state approach: taking named species into special protection, prohibiting or restricting use of depleted animals and their parts, prohibiting the export of one product and the hunting of another species, and setting annual limits for hunting and capture; and records that hunting is to be carried out only within hunting zones, with rare animals huntable only under special permit for scientific or stated purposes, listed by a 2012 government resolution. Household hunting runs through the local governor. Published reporting records that a citizen hunting for household purposes pays the statutory fee and hunts under a permit issued by the soum or local governor, excluding the very rare and rare species; and records that hunting inside a state special protected area, or keeping or trading what is taken there, is a criminal matter, with permission obtained from the soum or provincial governor. Read this with the water protection zones, the pasture rules, the rehabilitation guarantee and the inspectors entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The herder NGOs and the ombudsman complaint — a Khanbogd herders' body formed over a river diversion, the international complaint it filed, and the tripartite committee that came out of it
trackers.desc: Herders affected by a mine formed their own organisation and used an international complaint mechanism. Published case material records that in February 2013 a soum-based organisation representing a group of local herders, assisted by a second national watchdog organisation, filed a complaint against the mining company to the compliance advisor ombudsman — a mechanism for communities to voice concerns where they believe they are adversely affected by projects supported by the international finance corporation and the investment guarantee agency; that the complaint concerned a seasonal river running through the lease that was diverted to stop it flooding the open pit; and that the ombudsman found the complaint eligible for assessment, after which the parties agreed to work within its dispute resolution function. Where a project is financed by a development institution, that route exists alongside the domestic ones already recorded in this bucket. The outcome was a standing committee with elected herders on it. The same material records that a tripartite committee involving representatives of local government, elected herders as the complainants, and the company was established in 2015, with the memorandum of understanding and the committee's bylaw written collaboratively by the parties to ensure the initial complaints were adequately addressed and a broad dialogue maintained. A community can ask for that structure by name and by precedent. What the organisations argued is on the record, in their own words. Published accounts record the two organisations describing how diverting the river would deteriorate pastureland yields along it, causing irreversible damage to herders' livelihoods, and their letter describing the company as monopolising the scarce water supply through the diversion; and record an independent expert panel finding in 2015 that herders' water resources would be severely affected, with the complete loss of a named spring, fencing that would lengthen herders' journeys to water, and watershed impacts leading to loss of summer pasturelands. The wider river movement, and what it cost. Published accounts record a river movement founded in 2001 over a river system reduced from over four hundred kilometres to a fraction, its successor movement and a coalition uniting eleven movements; record a 2009 statute protecting river headwaters, protected zones of water reservoirs and forested areas, designed to shield a large share of natural ecosystems from mining, which the movements later went to court to enforce; and record that after a 2013 protest at parliament activists were detained and prosecuted, while the law was not overturned. Read this with the water protection zones, the rehabilitation guarantee, the pasture rules and the inspectors entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The environmental database — detailed assessment reports posted publicly by law, the local citizens' assembly minutes that must be inside them, and the parliamentary audit that says what is missing
trackers.desc: Detailed assessment reports are required by law to be posted publicly on a named database. A parliamentary evaluation of the assessment legislation records that the report is to be placed openly to the public on the environmental information database at its named web address. That database is the country's environmental information store, and it is where a community should look first for the report on a project near it — before asking the proponent for a copy. The report must contain the local people's assembly minutes. The assessment legislation, already recorded in this bucket for other provisions, requires the detailed assessment report to include the opinion and minutes of the public assembly of the local citizens affected by the project, and of the administration of the territory where it will be implemented, along with the historical and cultural values of the project site and other matters tied to the project's character; and provides that the legal entity carrying out the detailed assessment shall, while preparing the report, officially obtain opinions from the territorial administration and from the local citizens and residents affected, and organise a discussion, with public participation regulated by a rule the environment minister approves. A report without those minutes is incomplete on its face. The parliamentary evaluation also records what is missing, which is usable. The same evaluation records that there are no detailed assessment reports that fail to incorporate those opinions — and, separately, that there is no detailed data on independent oversight following decisions of the body that carried out the general assessment. It records that for projects inside specially protected areas the opinion of that area's protection administration is obtained, but that differences of understanding and conflicts of interest among affected citizens complicate the arrangement. Annual management plan performance is assessed by a working group appointed by the governor. The evaluation records that enterprises' environmental management plan implementation reports for the year are assessed by a working group appointed by order of the provincial governor, and the next year's plan is approved on the basis of that assessment document; and records that inspections are organised in response to complaints and information from local administrative bodies and citizens, with results conveyed to the relevant bodies and the public. Read this with the assessment law entry, the inspectors, the basin council and the rehabilitation guarantee entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The conservation trust fund and the community-based conservation programmes — grants that go directly to community organisations, the grazing management rights they are meant to secure, and the household target
trackers.desc: A permanent conservation trust fund exists to make grants, and community organisations are named among its grantees. Published material records the fund as adopting detailed policies and procedures for transparent and equitable grantmaking, science-based monitoring, technical and audited financial reporting, and development of new financial solutions to increase funding for conservation; and records it designed to be a permanent player supporting the implementation of the country's public policies and commitments and financing project implementers, established with input from a foreign development agency, a wildlife conservation organisation, a biodiversity foundation, a development programme's finance initiative, a citizenship council and public bodies including the finance ministry and the central bank. A separate account records the trust fund making grants to community-based organisations, non-governmental organisations and government agencies. What the money is for is stated in terms a herder group can use. That account records the fund providing technical and financial support directly to community-based organisations so they can strengthen their management of natural resources, including securing management rights on grazing grounds, developing management plans for sustainable grazing practices, and promoting activities that encourage lower herd sizes; and records the programme's targets as safeguarding an additional fourteen million hectares toward a national goal of protecting thirty per cent of the country by 2030, strengthening management of protected areas covering forty-seven million hectares, and helping twenty-four thousand herder households implement community-managed practices in areas surrounding protected areas. Securing management rights on grazing ground is exactly the instrument recorded in this bucket's pasture and partnership entries. A second organisation runs community programmes with named partners. A conservation society's own pages record community-based natural resource use and management herder groups in protected areas and their buffer zones receiving training and education materials, funded by a named children's development fund and a foreign government, with events run in a named provincial centre; and record its work extending across borders on the shared steppe, naming the three main threats as illegal and unsustainable hunting and wildlife trade, habitat fragmentation and degradation from poorly planned development and overgrazing, and wildlife and livestock disease transmission. Read this with the finance mechanism entry, the partnership route, the pasture rules and the local protection entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The rivers and lakes movement — the herder-led coalition that got the headwaters mining ban passed, the Supreme Court order to enforce it, and the record of how the ban was then hollowed out
trackers.desc: A herder-led movement forced a national mining ban through parliament, and the sequence is documented. Published material records the movement's founder as awarded an international environmental prize in 2007 for having successfully pressured thirty-five of thirty-seven mining operations working in one river basin; records that new companies then received new licences over the same areas, so activists concluded they could not win all local battles unless special national legislation was passed; and records the resulting law as designed to protect up to twenty-five per cent of the country's natural ecosystems from destruction by mining. It records that when parliament was slow and the draft was near being scrapped, the movement organised a hunger strike in front of the parliament house which triggered the law's adoption in July 2009; and that the movement then cooperated with the government to delineate the actual protection zones and negotiate them with local populations. The lesson recorded is that local wins needed a national instrument. The court route was used, and won. The same material records that in May 2011, to demand implementation, the movement brought thousands of nomadic herders to the capital's central square in a camp; and that in October 2011 the Supreme Court ordered the government to enforce the ban on mining in river and forest areas, following an appeal by activists. Published reporting records the movement returning to that route, its leader deciding to sue the government for inaction after a request to implement the law was refused, creating the precondition for a case. What happened next is recorded too, and it matters more than the victory. Reporting records that at least half of the seventeen hundred licences that had to be cancelled were restored, that deposits given strategic status are exempt from the law's requirements, and that a mining company director personally warned the movement that the mining association and corporations were working to pass a new law to neutralise the 2009 ban. A published fact-finding mission by two human rights organisations collected testimonies on mining impacts and highlighted shortcomings in national legislation enabling operations to circumvent conservation provisions. A directory records the movement's own contact details in a named province with a representative office in the capital. Read this with the water law protection zones, the herder organisations, the local protection route and the mining bond entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The human rights organisation that runs fact-finding missions on mining — testimonies collected from herders, authorities and companies, and recommendations addressed to named provinces, districts and firms
trackers.desc: A domestic rights organisation runs documented fact-finding missions into mining areas. A published mission report records a team including a domestic centre for human rights and development and an interpreter, and records that the mission interviewed 30 men and 19 women — 21 local community and herder representatives, 21 local authority officials and five mining company representatives. Interviewing all three sides and publishing the count is what makes a report hard to dismiss. The report records that despite threats and intimidation, human rights defenders, local communities and even local authorities continue to mobilise, demanding respect for their constitutional right to live in a safe and healthy environment, citing the constitutional article by number. The recommendations are addressed to named bodies, which is what a community can hold up. The report records recommendations directed to the national government, a named province, three named districts, three named mining companies, and a United Nations special rapporteur. The organisation behind it records its mission as contributing to a country where everyone enjoys human rights without discrimination and its vision as a society where people can participate freely, actively and meaningfully in development processes they benefit from. Published analysis names why these cases fail, and it is not for lack of law alone. Published material records civil society organisations as having handled most of the public interest litigation cases in the country since 2000, most involving environmental and human rights abuses from irresponsible mining; and records root causes as laws too general and weak to enhance public participation in environmental decision-making or to strengthen local communities' capacity to protect their rights; environmental laws dedicated only to protecting plants or animals without considering the individual's right to land, safety and security; and international operating standards not implemented while domestic standards are poor and outdated. It records a licensing figure — 3,692 special licences covering 22.3 million hectares in one year — and one district where eleven companies hold licences over 1.1 of 2.8 million hectares, making herding difficult. Read this with the rivers movement, the accountability complaint, the assembly minutes and the audit request entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The herders' pasture user federation and the environmental consortium — a national body representing herder communities, an alliance of fourteen research institutes and organisations, and their published addresses
trackers.desc: Herders have a national federation of their own pasture user groups. Published description records the federation as a national organisation representing the vital interests of the country's herders and engaged in activities to preserve and promote pastoralism with its nomadic traditions of managing natural resources; records its objectives as to empower, enable and support herder communities in their endeavour to eliminate poverty and achieve sustainable development; and publishes a named contact person with a street address in the capital. It records the federation's aim as maintaining the ecological and societal well-being of rangeland-based livestock herding. Where a project threatens pasture, that is the body that already speaks for pasture users nationally. The principles it works to include recognition of local land users' authority. The same network records the commitments its members work to, including respecting and protecting the inherent land and territorial rights of indigenous peoples as set out in the international labour convention and the United Nations declaration, and enabling the role of local land users in territorial and ecosystem management, recognising that stewardship is best achieved through participatory decision-making at territorial level, empowering local land users and their communities with the authority, means and incentives to carry out this responsibility. Those are the words to quote when a plan treats herders as bystanders. A research consortium sits beside it, and its purpose is coordination. Published description records a nature and environmental consortium as an alliance of fourteen nature and environment conservation research institutes, centres and organisations, committed to joining their efforts and coordinating activities, whose stated mission is coordinating and facilitating the activities of environmental research organisations and non-governmental organisations in nature conservation and sustainable use of natural resources, and which seeks to improve the technical and scientific basis for decision making on environmental issues through honest investigations; its postal address is published. A further listing records an environmental citizens' council with a room, building and district address in the capital. Read this with the rivers movement, the fact-finding organisation, the conservation trust fund and the environmental database entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Steps Without Borders and the participatory environmental monitoring committees — herders, companies and local government monitoring a mine together, and the organisation that sets the committees up
trackers.desc: Committees exist here on which herders monitor a mine alongside the company and the authorities, and a named organisation sets them up. Published material records participatory environmental monitoring committees as a tool to address the root causes of social conflicts and help integrate environment and human rights protection into mining governance, and quotes the head of a domestic organisation that their establishment relied on partnerships with stakeholders ranging from rural communities and herders to mining companies, government partners and civil society organisations. For a community that cannot stop a mine, a standing seat at its monitoring is the next thing worth having. The organisation's own mission is participation by the people usually left out. It records its corporate mission as developing democratic civil society and increasing the participation of civil society organisations and marginalised people in order to support rural development and social justice; records monitoring the implementation of a mining sector transparency programme; and records an intention to conduct surveys on the issues facing those living in rural and marginalised areas in order to define their needs, and to protect and implement the rights guaranteed to them by national laws. Its director is named in published research partnerships. Published research states the herders' legal position plainly. A university record describes mobile pastoralist communities as an often-excluded group, living on state land without legal rights but with customary protections, and describes mitigating mining's social impact on them as extremely complex. Published analysis records limited enforcement of environmental protections and inadequate recognition of traditional communal land use practices, with mining expansion causing land degradation and water contamination and herders frequently displaced with minimal compensation; it names this organisation and a human rights centre among the domestic bodies working on it. Where an agreement exists, monitoring it is its own job. Reporting records a named domestic watchdog and a local organisation supporting vulnerable herders to raise their voices and hold a large mine accountable, and records a report finding 35 per cent of the agreement's commitments complete, with 1.2 million dollars distributed in compensation packages to herder families while the most important parts remained outstanding. Read this with the rivers movement, the fact-finding organisation, the herders' federation and the accountability complaint entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The human rights defenders committee and the rights centre — a statutory protection body with named seats for the bar and for non-profits, risk assessments for defenders, and the participation rules NGOs can invoke
trackers.desc: The participation rules are written into more than one statute, and an organisation can invoke them. A civic space monitor records that the law on non-governmental organisations provides that organisations may be involved in drafting and implementing decisions; that the law on development policy, planning and management requires the equal participation of all parties to ensure proper public-private partnerships and the transparency of development policy documents; and that a law on the resolution of complaints from citizens to government organisations and officials regulates the process and the rights and responsibilities of the parties. It records public participation regulations included in different sectoral rules, around public councils and working groups, public discussions, public monitoring, and public information and awareness, and describes the legal environment for civil society organisations as generally enabling while noting overlapping and sometimes conflicting regulations. There is a statutory committee for protecting defenders, and its seats are allocated. Published description records a human rights defenders committee that identifies the necessity to protect human rights defenders and conducts a risk assessment determining the danger level and risk faced by defenders, their families, guardians, partners, immediate relatives and legal representatives; submits concluding reports based on those assessments; monitors implementation of the law on human rights defenders; and creates a database for complaints and information. It records the committee as seven members — four from non-profit organisations, a commissioner in charge of human rights defenders, and one member each from the bar association and the advocates' association. A community whose organiser is being threatened has a named body with a risk-assessment function. A rights centre works the same ground, and the risks are documented. A network profile records a centre whose mission is a country where everyone enjoys human rights without discrimination and whose vision includes people being able to participate freely, actively and meaningfully through development processes they benefit from. Published material records that defenders promoting corporate accountability in the extractive sector face threats and intimidation from government and corporate actors, judicial harassment, vilification and smear campaigns, and that organisations criticising policy often become victims of defamation suits. Read this with the herders' federation, the fact-finding organisation, the monitoring committees and the rivers movement entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Soum-level herder communities and forest user groups — co-management contracts signed with bag and soum governors, the named local bodies in one community's network, and the application route through the district governor
trackers.desc: A herders' group can hold a co-management contract with its own district governor, and two dated examples are recorded. A community registry records that a named herders' group had a co-management contract with the district governor in 2005 and 2019 to ensure the responsible use of pastures and natural resources, and that the group's activities have been documented in a database while it awaits certification. It records another community's co-management contract approved by the citizens' representative assembly of the sub-district and the sub-district governor. Contracts at sub-district and district level, not national, are where herders' use of pasture is actually settled. The local bodies that make up one community's network are listed by name. The registry records that network as including the community focus group, a larger local community group, the district governor's office, the sub-district governor, the district meteorological station, a named strictly protected area administration, a named natural reserve, the community association of the district, herders, and the district environmental ranger. That list is a map of who a community actually deals with — including the ranger and the protected area administration. It records the district's total land area and animals per family, and names concentration of animals around settlement centres and water sources as the pasture problem. Forest user groups apply through the district, and the route upward is stated. Published material records that licences are not granted to individual households; instead households must band together and collectively apply as a forest user group at the district level, after which the district governor takes the request up to the provincial governor and finally submits it to the environment ministry, which takes the final decision. It records that such groups can collect deadwood and non-timber forest products such as berries and nuts, and in certain cases may apply for a licence to practise thinning. Published assessment records that these communities were accepted as rural civil society organisations in the civil code following a member of parliament's initiative, which allowed contracts on communal land management to be made between local government and the communities, and records herders who managed to make the district governor listen to them and influenced pasture management plans. Read this with the pasture users' federation, the monitoring committees, the defenders committee and the rivers movement entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The Local Development Fund and the bag meeting that feeds it — where a herder proposes a project, who shortlists it, who sits on the district council, and the citizen monitoring groups formed to watch the spending
trackers.desc: A project starts at the sub-district meeting, and the route upward is described by an official. Published reporting records that community meetings are held in the smallest rural administration unit, where proposals are put forward and chosen, and quotes an official describing the levels: community members gather at the sub-district meeting and speak about the projects they propose for the following year; a shortlist is sent to the district governor's council for consideration; the district council discusses which three or four projects can be implemented in the year and sends that on to the province for financing. It records that when funding is short, remaining proposals are carried to the following year. For a herding community that wants a well, a fence or a road rather than only to stop something, that is the sequence and the calendar. Who sits on the district council is published, and it includes a herder representative. The same reporting records council members as the governor, the government office director, the school principal, the social worker, the head of the hospital, a herder representative and members from non-governmental organisations. Knowing there is a herder seat and an organisation seat tells a community whose ear to seek before the shortlist is made. The fund itself is described as the only direct forum, and its share is stated. Published description records the integrated budget law, in force from January 2013, as the first law to prescribe public consultation in government decision-making and arguably the country's first attempt to decentralise development planning to local government, with the fund as the only forum for citizens to directly voice their opinion on local expenditures and its share of the national budget significant at five per cent. Citizens' monitoring groups were created to watch the money. A published commitment records the aim of establishing citizen monitoring groups at every sub-district, urban sub-district and district to monitor fund projects, because public access to information on implementation and budget allocation is currently limited, so citizens cannot monitor or hold government accountable. Read this with the herder communities and forest user groups, the pasture users' federation, the participatory monitoring committees and the defenders committee entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: State attorneys and the legal aid centre — free advocates for indigent citizens under a named statutory duty, the two delivery routes, and where people actually go for advice in the provinces
trackers.desc: Free defence attorneys exist as a state status, not a favour. A published conference paper records that the state has provided the conditions and opportunities for indigent defendants to defend their rights and receive legal aid by appointing them defence attorneys with the status of state attorney, and records the duty in a numbered article of the law on the legal status of lawyers, to organise provision of advocacy services to indigent citizens. It records the two delivery routes as a legal aid centre and a legal aid and advocacy services provider for the indigent. For a herding household facing a case it cannot pay for, the entitlement is written into the lawyers' statute rather than left to charity. The centre appears in official commitments alongside the bar and civil society. A published government commitment lists the legal assistance centre, all levels of public administrative agencies, the bar association, an open society foundation, the national broadcaster and other media and non-governmental organisations as supporting institutions for public legal education, with the objective of creating conditions that programmes providing legal education to citizens are implemented in an equal, accessible and human rights based manner, including a special programme taking account of target group needs and a legal guide system built on existing capacity. Where people actually go for advice is recorded, and it is not a law firm. A published legal system overview records that, given the country's history, there seems to be no tradition of seeking professional advice and little regard for its potential usefulness, that advice is rarely sought before entering into a contract, and that general legal advice is sought from places such as the general prosecutor's office, local governments and ministries, with an expectation that advice will be free. It records that chief prosecutors at the province and capital city level must have five years of professional experience, and that legal acts may be issued by the governors of the provinces, the capital city, districts, sub-districts and urban sub-districts, called ordinances, which must conform to national law. Read this with the local development fund, the herder communities, the defenders committee and the monitoring committees entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Soum land officers and district land offices — the local official who marks boundaries and keeps the land database, the 15-day certificate renewal decision, and the bag governor's letter an applicant needs
trackers.desc: The official who marks a boundary on the ground works at soum level. Published legislation records that the land supervisor of the soum and the district land office shall respectively carry out demarcation and marking of the boundaries of privately owned land on the ground, registration of boundary changes and entry into the land database, as well as control activities. It records that certificate holders must register the acquired land in the state registry of cadastral and property rights, and register transfers of ownership or use and pledge agreements in the registry of immovable property. For a household whose boundary is disputed, the person who can mark it is in the soum office, not the capital. Applications go to the local governor or land office, and the documents are listed. Published legal commentary records that citizens submit application materials to the local governor or land development office, and lists the requirements as including notarised copies of birth certificates of family members under 16; a letter of confirmation by a khoroo or bag governor on the status of the family and the number of its members; copies of the land possession certificate or a notarised copy of the possession contract where land is already possessed; and an outlining map showing the location and size of the land. It records that on the governor's decision, the local immovable property registration office registers the ownership status and issues a registration certificate. A letter from the sub-district governor about who is in the household is the document most likely to be missing. Renewal and termination both run through the same governors, on a stated clock. Published legislation records that on receiving a request for extension of a certificate, governors of aimags, the capital city, soums or districts shall review and determine within 15 days whether the person has met the conditions to preserve the right, after which the governor extends the certificate and the soum land officer or the aimag, capital city or district land department makes the relevant registration. It records that governors of aimags, the capital city, soums and districts terminate certificates where the holder has consistently or seriously violated obligations under the land legislation and the contract. Read this with the local development fund, the herder communities and forest user groups, the pasture users' federation and the state attorneys entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The bag and khoroo citizens' public assembly — every resident attends in person, it nominates the governor, reviews his report and can move to dismiss him, and it decides anything not reserved to a higher body
trackers.desc: At the lowest tier the resident attends in person, not through a delegate. The local administration legislation, as published by a province, records the public assembly of the bag or khoroo as having the general powers to discuss and decide matters pertaining to the bag or khoroo where these are not specifically assigned by law or by a decision of the competent higher state body; to decide the rules of its own sessions and other organisational questions; to elect and release the chair of its session; to nominate a candidate for governor of the bag or khoroo; to discuss the governor's report on the implementation of the assembly's decisions and give an assessment of his work; to propose the governor's dismissal on grounds provided by law; where specially empowered by law, to adopt administrative normative acts consistent with legislation and have them entered in the state register; and other powers provided by law. A residual power to decide anything not reserved higher up is unusual at this level. The citizen's own participation rights are set out separately. The same legislation records that a citizen has the right to take part in exercising local self-government directly or through representative bodies, and specifically to be elected to and to elect the citizens' representative assemblies of the province, sum, capital and district; to take part in person in the public assembly of the bag or khoroo; to submit petitions and complaints to local self-governing bodies and have them resolved; and to receive information under the procedures set by law. It records that after each regular election of the sum or district representative assembly, the session of the bag or khoroo public assembly is convened once the new governor has been appointed. The complaint duty runs the other way too. The constitution records that a citizen has the right to submit petitions and complaints to state bodies and officials and have them resolved, and that state bodies and officials have the duty to resolve citizens' petitions and complaints in accordance with law. Read this with the local development fund, the herder communities, the soum land officers and the state attorneys entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Auditor General's Office
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Maldives, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Information Commissioner’s Office (Maldives)
trackers.desc: Information Commissioner’s Office (Maldives) — the Maldives’ independent Information Commissioner’s Office overseeing the Right to Information Act and adjudicating access-to-information appeals. — Holds to account: the Maldives’ public bodies on disclosure — find RTI appeal decisions, guidance and annual reports.

trackers.name: Information Commissioner’s Office (ICOM, Maldives)
trackers.desc: National right-to-information authority; the Maldives’ Information Commissioner’s Office is the independent oversight & appeal body under the Right to Information Act (2014) — ruling on access complaints (its decisions appealable to the courts), Maldives.

trackers.name: Maldives — Ministry of Finance
trackers.desc: National budget authority; prepares & publishes the national budget (and a dedicated budget portal) under the Fiscal Responsibility Act, Maldives. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Maldives.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Maldives
trackers.desc: Official site of the Maldivian Supreme Court with judgments. · Find here: information and judgments of the Supreme Court of the Maldives.

trackers.name: Maldives — Ministry of Economic Development & Trade (Business Registration)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the trade regulator provides company & business-name registration services and maintains the business register, Maldives. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Protected Areas Regulation 2018/R-78 — consultation is a stated objective
trackers.desc: QUOTE THE REGULATION'S OWN OBJECTIVES BACK. Regulation No. 2018/R-78 lists six objectives, and two are about community involvement in designation: to ensure the process of protected area declaration is consultative and transparent, and to enhance awareness and participation of community in protected area designation and management. Where a designation process has excluded a community, that departs from the regulation's own stated purpose — cite those two limbs. It also aims to enlist environmentally significant areas, and it covers areas already declared and areas protected before or after it came into force, so it applies to existing sites too. THE ACT BEHIND IT, Law 4/93 (ratified 19 April 1993): the ministry identifies protected areas and reserves (s.4); an impact assessment must be submitted before any development project that may have a potential impact on the environment (s.5) — note that low threshold, not ‘significant’ impact; and the ministry has authority to TERMINATE any project that has an undesirable impact. Termination, not conditions or fines — and the test is ‘undesirable’, not ‘unlawful’. The Act declares the natural environment a national heritage.

trackers.name: Farukolhu — designation used instead of an airport, and the paper-parks answer
trackers.desc: A PRECEDENT AND A REBUTTAL. Sh. Farukolhu was designated a protected area under Act 4/93 in 2018 — recorded as a major victory because the island had previously been considered for development of an airport to boost tourism infrastructure. Its reefs are nurseries for endangered hawksbill turtles and vulnerable sicklefin lemon sharks; its mangroves and wetlands are bird nesting grounds. Designation is a demonstrated alternative to an airport in this jurisdiction. AND THE ANSWER TO ‘IT WILL NEVER BE MANAGED ANYWAY’: 93 sites have been designated in recent years while management has not kept pace — but as a conservationist puts it, paper parks are not always a bad thing, because declaring them helps earmark and preserve them rather than allocating them for industrial or tourism development. A designated site is one not allocated to something else. WHERE MONEY IS COMING FROM: the CATENATE project, US$2 million from the GEF plus US$7.5 million co-funding from the ministry, Sh. Funadhoo Council and the earlier USAID-funded REGENERATE, to manage Farukolhu and 14 other protected areas in the same atoll. An island council is a named co-funder — local councils can put money into protected area management. A CANDID NOTE: a legal handbook records that the Maldivian judiciary ‘has not yet taken an activist role in environmental management’, so administrative and designation routes are likely to outperform litigation here.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Save Maldives Campaign — went for an injunction, and works through island councils
trackers.desc: It has gone to court. Human Rights Watch records that in September 2021 the campaign sought a civil injunction to halt the government's Gulhifalhu lagoon reclamation, arguing it would destroy environmentally protected areas in breach of Maldivian law — which makes this the Maldivian body on record attempting to stop a project by legal process rather than by statement alone. Its stated way of working is through the local authority rather than around it: the campaign says it collaborates with NGOs, community-based organisations, island councils and government bodies to protect sensitive ecosystems, so a community's route in is usually to bring its island council along, not to bypass it. The model to copy is on its own site. Project ThimaaVeshi's open letter of 19 October 2025 to the Minister of Tourism and Environment, over the downsizing and rezoning of Addu Nature Park's core protected area, was endorsed by 18 civil society organisations and 7 local tourism actors and led by young people from Addu; it argued the rezoning conflicts with UNESCO's Seville Strategy and Statutory Framework for Biosphere Reserves because the buffer zones around the core area are no longer clear. Naming an international framework the state has signed, and recruiting tourism operators as co-signatories, is where the leverage came from. Two limits. This is a citizen-led campaign of individuals rather than an incorporated body with staff and an office, so it coordinates and acts collectively rather than representing you. And an environmental refusal here is not final: reporting from Malé records the planning ministry overturning the Environmental Protection Agency's rejection of the Maafaru airport development in early 2020, so a favourable EPA decision is a stage rather than an ending.

trackers.name: Environmental Regulatory Authority — ten working days to comment, and no right to enforce the outcome
trackers.desc: The comment window is ten working days from the day the report becomes available for public viewing, and the EIA Regulation directs that comments be accepted from the public as well as from ministries and authorities — so the date to watch is the publication of the assessment, not any notice you will be sent. The trap sits at the other end: the regulation contains no provision allowing citizens or NGOs to enforce the terms and conditions of an Environmental Decision Statement. You can shape the conditions and you cannot make anyone keep them. So build the case around getting the conditions written correctly, and around the monitoring reports the proponent must file at two-month intervals through site preparation, construction and decommissioning, because those are the only routine record of compliance. Know which body you are writing to now. The Environmental Protection Agency, created in December 2008, was replaced in 2025 by the Environmental Regulatory Authority, working under the Ministry of Climate Change, Environment and Energy from Henveiru, Malé; material naming the EPA — including older guidance still hosted on the Authority's own site — refers to its predecessor. Screening decides your route: projects listed in Schedule D require a full EIA, and for everything else the proponent files a screening form and the ministry decides between an EIA, an initial environmental examination and an environmental management plan, so establish first which of the three your project received. Two developments to check before relying on any of this. The minister has long held the power to overturn the regulator's refusal on appeal, and did so for the Kulhudhuffushi airport in 2017, which destroyed part of that island's mangrove, and for the Noonu Maafaru runway extension in 2020.
