Published reporting records a nationwide expedition series completing the first archipelago-wide survey of the country's coral reefs across 26 atolls, its data to support marine spatial planning. Read this with the dredging conditions, the protected area designation, the fisheries regulation and the environmental authority entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Maldives Coral Institute — coral relocated ahead of a harbour project, community restoration with island councils, and measured recovery figures from a named island
trackers.desc: Coral in the path of a harbour project has been physically moved out of the way here, and the operation is on record. The institute records that in 2020, in collaboration with a named local organisation and the island community, it installed a silt screen and relocated 5,000 colonies of coral on a named island that were in danger of being destroyed from a harbour development project. For a community whose reef is about to be dredged, relocation with a silt screen is a concrete demand to put to the developer, and there is a domestic body that has done it. The restoration results are measured, which is what makes them arguable. It records a low-technology, community-based restoration method used from 2021, with over 400 square metres of reef grown representing 32 species of coral, a 40.24 per cent increase in coral cover and a 730.77 per cent increase in fish abundance within two years. Published material records the same method applied after land reclamation and harbour developments left reefs degraded and local communities vulnerable to erosion and flooding, with the project working closely with the island council and engaging the local population. Its stated objects include supporting protection, not only restoration. The institute records aims to identify areas of greater coral resilience and vulnerability and direct protection and management measures to those places; to develop and trial methods of reef restoration to promote recovery of degraded reefs; to support the design, implementation and management of a national network of protected areas to better safeguard critical coral reef habitats; and to identify threats to corals and seek means to ameliorate them through legislation, regulation and community action. It records creating a coral gene bank from bleaching-resilient colonies. Island councils are inside the work, and the training is counted. Its project pages record stakeholder training at a state marine laboratory attended by 27 representatives from 16 organisations, including 21 stakeholders from five regions in four atolls, with secretariats from six named island and atoll councils in the stakeholder network; and published description records work with a named island council to establish community-managed conservation areas safeguarding grouper spawning grounds and manta ray cleaning stations. Read this with the marine research institute, the dredging conditions, the island councils and the green fund entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Maldives Whale Shark Research — a Maldivian NGO whose data underpinned a marine protected area declared with island councils, and a citizen-science volunteer programme that funds it
trackers.desc: A domestic research NGO's data was the basis for declaring a protected area, working with the island councils. Published material records the organisation as principal data provider for the implementation of the largest marine protected areas in the country, created to protect the whale sharks near a named atoll, and records that by working closely with the local island councils and the government, the area was assigned its protected status in June 2009, protecting the largest and most consistent aggregation of whale sharks in the country. For a community that wants a site protected, this is the sequence in reverse order from the usual: long-term data first, councils second, designation third. It is Maldivian-registered and states where its money goes. The organisation records itself as a Maldivian non-governmental organisation that carries out whale shark research and fosters community-focused conservation initiatives, having begun as a research expedition in 2006 and grown into the only long-term organisation dedicated to studying the species in the country, seeking to advance the field and to advocate for sound conservation policy by encouraging and valuing community and industry stakeholder participation. Published description records the volunteer programme as Maldivian-led, with 70 per cent of revenue spent directly in local communities, running for over ten years. That revenue split is the test to put to any research or eco-tourism operation working near a community. Its data comes from ordinary people on the water. Published material records that much of its data now comes from citizen scientists and local contributors ranging from liveaboards, resort excursions and guesthouses, without whose assistance its register of individual sharks would not exist; records volunteers surveying, photographing, observing and identifying sharks over ten-day placements, entered by application assessed on interest, experience and training; and records the atoll as one of a few aggregation sites where the species can be encountered year-round, with one of the highest re-sighting rates in the world. It records schools work on the island where it is based. Read this with the coral institute, the marine research institute, the protected area designation and the island councils entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Zero Waste Maldives — expertise offered directly to island councils on collection and segregation, waste audits across a whole atoll, and a social enterprise model built because grant funding failed others
trackers.desc: An island council can hire this organisation's expertise, and the offer is published. The organisation records that it offers its expertise to island councils, resorts and guesthouses that would like to optimise their collection systems and add waste segregation to the model, so that the community can get the most out of the waste it puts out, noting that each island is unique in its waste generation and physical make-up and thus requires a customised approach. For a council facing a waste facility it did not choose, an organisation that will redesign collection instead is a different option. Its critique of the standard model is the argument to borrow. It records that the practice of building island waste management centres keeps the community disengaged from the waste that is generated, so they see waste as someone else's problem, in most cases the local councils, and that only by changing the perception of waste to that of a resource can value be extracted from it. Published material records the organisation's view that land is still reclaimed in ways that impact coral reefs, naming a waste-to-energy incinerator project, and that the government keeps pushing mega projects which are not impacting people in a good way — land reclaimed to build houses people cannot afford. It works at atoll scale with councils, and the work is named. An atoll council records collaborating with the organisation to conduct waste audits across all 13 islands of the atoll, funded by the environment ministry, focused on hazardous waste management, and records the council's own view that effective waste management requires addressing root causes, fostering collective action, and ensuring solutions are inclusive and long-lasting. Its funding model exists because grants were not enough. Published description records the organisation started in 2018 and registered in 2019, with the founder noting that the mechanism of operating a non-governmental organisation here is difficult and most die because of lack of funding, so it began a social entrepreneurship model, selling zero-waste alternatives that were not available locally, and now has 15 to 20 contributors — specialists in economics, communications and engineering — working on different projects on a volunteer basis. Read this with the green fund, the atoll conservation fund, the environmental regulator and the transparency organisation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The Baa Atoll Biosphere Reserve Office and the atoll and island councils — lease payments flowing into an atoll conservation fund that built housing on every island, and the expired community management agreement
trackers.desc: Lease payments for a protected area go into an atoll-level fund, and the money has been spent on the islands. Published reporting records that areas protected as biosphere reserves can be leased and the payment goes into the atoll biosphere reserve conservation fund, and that the fund has been used to build two-room apartments on each island of the atoll, directly benefiting local councils. An atoll-level fund fed by leases, spending on every island in the atoll, is the clearest local conservation-finance loop in this bucket. It records the reserve office conveying its own constraints to a minister, including the lack of a proper office building and storage space, and records the atoll designated in 2011 and re-designated for ten more years in September 2021 after reports on ecological surveys of coral reefs, islands and sandbanks. The island councils were named as co-managers, and the agreement lapsed. Published reporting records that one protected zone in the atoll was to be managed by two named islands together with the atoll council and the biosphere reserve office, but that a memorandum signed between the parties for the community-based conservation model expired four years ago and has not been renewed. It records an audit highlighting the longstanding problem of unclear mandates in managing the country's 93 protected areas, with the responsibilities of the environment ministry, the regulatory authority and local councils, which have jurisdiction over some protected areas, not clearly defined. A community relying on a co-management memorandum should check its expiry date. The obstacle at council level is stated by an assessment. A published project document records that most protected areas outside three named atoll and island areas lack management plans, converting them into paper parks, and records lack of capacity in local island councils to implement the broad mandate of natural resource management specified in the decentralisation legislation as a key concern, with formal authority and resources continuing to be retained by the national ministries. Published description records that atoll and island councils play a role in enforcement at the local level alongside the national agency and police. Read this with the atoll conservation fund, the coral institute, the marine research institute and the waste organisation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Island councils and Women's Development Committees — council size set by island population, a third of seats reserved for women, a directly elected committee president, and lease revenue kept by the council
trackers.desc: Every inhabited island elects a council, and its size follows the island's population. Published reporting records that councils serving islands with fewer than 2,000 inhabitants comprise three councillors including one female member, and islands with 2,000 or more comprise five councillors including two female members, with a named city council allocated a member for each of its eight districts plus a mayor and the capital's council matching its number of parliamentary representatives. For an island community, the body that plans and consents to development is a handful of people its own residents elect. A parallel committee exists on every island, and it now elects its own president. Published material records that women's development committees mirror the size of the island or city council — an island with three councillors has three committee members — and that the committee president, previously chosen from among elected members at the first meeting, becomes its own directly elected position. Reporting records that for the first time, committee president positions, one per island or city, were decided by direct vote at the most recent local elections. It records one city's committee as ten members, five from one district and five from the others. What the committee is mandated to do is broader than what it usually does. Published material records that the decentralisation legislation mandates the committees to advise the island council on matters related to island development and municipal services provided by the council, while recording their primary activities in practice as cleaning programmes, social awareness programmes, sports events, fundraising and courses. An assessment records that 70 per cent of committees agreed they received some level of support from their island council, that 74 per cent said their members had not contested local council elections nor considered running, and identifies capacity needs in project proposal writing, budgeting, facilitation skills and fundraising strategies. The money question is the one to ask a council. Published description records that amendments provided a quota reserving one third of seats for female councillors and that revenue generated from leasing land, islands and lagoons stays with the councils. Read this with the atoll reserve office and island councils, the atoll conservation fund, the waste organisation and the coral institute entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Petitioning your own island council — a 370-person island where two petitions halted a project, the authority that intervened and convened the agencies, and the training institute for councillors
trackers.desc: On one island of 370 people, petitions stopped a project and forced an intervention. Published commentary records that on a named island with a population of just 370 and 284 eligible voters, collecting the signatures for both petitions would have been an arduous task even in a bigger island, and that the numbers drove home the seriousness of the issue to the community and the intensity of the division, in which the council was also accused of being biased; and records that as the debate escalated, the project was halted and the local government authority intervened. For a small island, that is the clearest recorded example in this bucket of a community's own signatures changing an outcome. The same commentary records the authority convening the agencies around one waste dispute. It records that on the authority's request a meeting was convened at the environment ministry bringing together the city council, the waste management company, the environmental protection agency, the health protection agency, the ministry and the authority, and that with proper communication and collaborative efforts agreed upon, the issue was resolved and misunderstandings clarified, leading to more favourable arrangements for all parties — adding that sometimes all it takes is an effort to find common ground between authorities of the central government and local government, but this crucial step is often not taken when and how it is needed. The authority's own remit, and its new power over councillors, are published. Published description records the authority as established under the decentralisation legislation to regulate, oversee and develop the local governance system, mandated to monitor that councils function in accordance with the constitution and the law, coordinate councils at national level, harmonise standards and procedures, formulate rules of procedure for women's development committees and conduct their elections. Reporting records that under recent amendments the authority can immediately suspend a council member based on the findings of an initial inquiry, where previously it had to seek ministerial permission, warn and report first. Its training institute publishes capacity-building for councils. Read this with the island councils and women's development committees, the atoll reserve office, the waste organisation and the transparency organisation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: City and island council land services — a gazetted land register a resident can audit, a council digital portal with e-permits, and the recorded gaps between allocations announced and allocations listed
trackers.desc: A council land register can be published and then checked against what was announced. Published commentary records that a city council released its long-awaited land register on 20 November 2025, 678 days later than expected, and records the writer examining the allocations for one constituency and finding that six of the nine projects that had been announced, publicly bid and officially awarded were missing from the published list, while other projects appeared under the names of individuals close to the council leader. It records two allocations that did appear with their terms — a 5,000 square foot plot for 25 years under the council's development plan, and a children's park allocation for 25 years — and records a further agreement, made with a company owned by a relative of the mayor which had not submitted a bid, where the land was reportedly handed over but is not included in the register. A published register that residents compare against council minutes is the audit tool this bucket has been missing. The council's own service portal replaces paper permits. A city council records a digital services portal enabling about 90 per cent of council services to be accessed online, designed to cut repetitive submissions and reduce paperwork, replacing traditional paper-based permits with e-permits verifiable by code, and covering permits to close roads for events or construction work, birth and residential registrations, and booking of parks and recreational facilities. It records the council's stated aspiration as efficient land allocations for residential, social and commercial needs. Who may issue a land registration has widened, and the plan comes first. Published reporting records that the authority to issue land registrations within a city now includes the city council of that city, the prevailing land registry authority, or an authority designated by government for land development. A national service portal records that an approved land use plan is required before land allocation in the islands and cities, under a named amendment to the decentralisation legislation. Read this with the island councils and women's development committees, the local government authority, the atoll reserve office and the waste organisation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Island magistrate courts — a court on every inhabited island under a named section of the judicature legislation, a resident magistrate where the population reaches 500, and a neighbouring magistrate where it does not
trackers.desc: There is a court on the island itself, not only in the capital. The supreme court records the subordinate courts as the five superior courts based in the capital — criminal, civil, family, juvenile and drug — and the magistrate courts in each inhabited island. Published legal description records that under a named section of the judicature legislation there shall be a magistrate court in each inhabited island except in the capital where superior courts exist, and records that divisions of superior courts may be established in other inhabited islands, with one such civil court division already created. For an island community, that means a filing counter without a boat journey. A resident magistrate arrives at a population threshold. Published description records 146 magistrates hearing misdemeanours, civil and family cases; records that all inhabited islands that do not have a superior court should have a magistrate court, and every island with a population of at least 500 people has a resident magistrate; and records that cases from islands without a magistrate are heard by a magistrate from a neighbouring island. A stated population threshold, and a neighbouring magistrate below it, is the practical answer to whether a small island has a judge of its own. The appeal route and the jurisdiction schedule are published. Published description records the high court as comprising eleven judges, hearing appeals from the superior courts, the employment tribunal and the magistrate courts, with power to review a lower court decision for constitutional and legal validity and to overturn it, and to rule on the constitutional validity of any law or part of a law. The judicature legislation carries a numbered schedule setting out the jurisdiction of magistrate courts, alongside separate schedules for each superior court. Read this with the state legal aid, the judicial administration department, the island councils and the bar council registers entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: EcoPeace Middle East
trackers.desc: Founded in 1994 as Friends of the Earth Middle East and still a member of Friends of the Earth International, EcoPeace is staffed and directed jointly by Jordanians, Palestinians and Israelis, with its own offices in Amman, Ramallah and Tel Aviv and a national director in each. WHO TO ENLIST: the office in your own country. Its Good Water Neighbors programme works with communities on either side of a shared water problem, pairing them across the border rather than treating each in isolation. You CAN get community-level organising support and technical and advocacy weight on water, sewage and Jordan Valley development. You CAN'T get a litigator — EcoPeace works by cross-border cooperation, research and advocacy, not by suing proponents, so a community that needs a permit or an approval challenged in court should look elsewhere. For activists: in Jordan and Palestine this was the only substantial environmental organisation with an office and a named national director that could be verified on its own domain.

trackers.name: Palestine — Ministry of National Economy (Companies Registry)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the MNE Companies Registry (Companies Controller) registers & regulates companies and business entities in the State of Palestine. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: State Audit & Administrative Control Bureau
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Palestine, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Palestine — Ministry of Finance & Planning
trackers.desc: National budget authority; controls public expenditure, prepares the budget, and publishes fiscal & financial reports, State of Palestine. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Palestine.

trackers.name: Supreme Constitutional Court of the State of Palestine
trackers.desc: Supreme Constitutional Court of the State of Palestine — supreme court (Palestine).

trackers.name: Establish your area classification first — it decides who has authority
trackers.desc: THE QUESTION THAT COMES BEFORE EVERY OTHER ONE. Of the 18 protected areas transferred to the Palestinian Authority under the Oslo agreements, only 8 are under actual Palestinian control, totalling less than 15 km²; the remaining 10 lie within Area C or overlapped areas. So establish your site's area classification before approaching any authority — the answer differs site by site, not governorate by governorate, and approaching the wrong body costs months. THE BODY THAT MANAGES RESERVES: the Directorate of Forests, Rangelands and Wildlife in the Ministry of Agriculture, with 4 divisions — forestry, nature reserves, rangelands and nurseries — and offices in all governorates of the West Bank, plus 40 rangers patrolling protected areas and natural forests. A governorate office with a rangelands division is the practical door, and rangelands matters where grazing land rather than forest is at issue. The Environment Quality Authority is the separate regulator, established 10 December 1996. NOTE THE LAYERED LEGAL HISTORY: Jordanian environmental laws applied in the West Bank and Egyptian in Gaza until 1967, so statutes of Jordanian origin may still be relevant — this map records Jordan's environment law separately.

trackers.name: Inspect your land physically — the appeal window is 10 days
trackers.desc: A PROCEDURAL RULE TO DIARISE. Demolition orders in the relevant administrative system are, under the rules, to be issued 10 days prior to action and are subject to appeal — and reporting records that orders are not always effectively communicated to those affected. The practical consequence is the same either way: inspect your land regularly and physically, because an order you do not find is an appeal window lost, and the window is short. THE ENFORCEMENT CHAIN THAT DOES WORK, for wildlife cases: EQA inspectors alongside the Environmental Police handed 29 illegally captured or nest-poached mammals and birds to the Nature Palestine Society in a single year — including 5 Palestine mountain gazelles, critically endangered globally — with rehabilitation at Tamoun Nature Reserve and a named EQA governorate office (Jenin) in the chain. If your issue is capture or poaching, that is a working route with named participants. TRAINING EXISTS: Nature Palestine Society has run environmental law training for young environmentalists covering national law, international conventions and the challenges that impede their enforcement. Since 2009 a sectoral working group on environment has brought together donors and national stakeholders, monitoring projects and giving environmental approvals.

trackers.name: CEPF Mediterranean Basin — Palestine is named eligible in current calls, and this is the first funding route recorded here
trackers.desc: PALESTINE IS NAMED AS AN ELIGIBLE COUNTRY IN CEPF'S OWN CURRENT CALLS FOR PROPOSALS, IN BOTH THE SMALL AND LARGE GRANT WINDOWS. The small-grants call ran from 9 February to 15 March 2026, offering twenty to fifty thousand US dollars from a total of five hundred and forty thousand, restricted to conservation of threatened freshwater biodiversity, with projects starting 1 August 2026 and completing by 30 September 2027; the regional implementation team scheduled its English-language webinar with a session time given specifically for Palestine. The large-grants window opened 1 July 2026 and closes 18 September 2026, offering fifty thousand to a hundred and eighty thousand dollars under two directions: traditional land use practices, and preservation of threatened plant species. LOCAL AND NATIONAL NGOS ARE EXPLICITLY PRIORITISED in the small-grants call. ELIGIBILITY: applicants must be legally registered entities holding their own bank accounts with authorisation under national law to receive charitable funding; individuals cannot apply directly but may work with a qualifying organisation. Letters of inquiry are submitted through the ConservationGrants portal in English or French; the regional implementation team is BirdLife International together with DOPPS. WHY THIS ENTRY NAMES NO PALESTINIAN ORGANISATION: this map treats Palestine as a context where recording local bodies can expose the people in them, so it records international instruments only. That is a deliberate limit rather than a finding that no Palestinian organisations exist, and a reader should understand it as such. CEPF'S OWN 2024 ECOSYSTEM PROFILE STATES THAT THE SECURITY AND GEOPOLITICAL SITUATION, PARTICULARLY IN PALESTINE AND LEBANON, HAS IMPACTED INHABITANTS AND ORGANISATIONS — the fund is operating with that on the record, and anyone weighing an application should read the current call document rather than this entry for what is presently possible.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants Programme — UNDP's Palestinian programme runs its own calls, inviting NGOs and community organisations directly
trackers.desc: UNDP'S PROGRAMME OF ASSISTANCE TO THE PALESTINIAN PEOPLE PUBLISHES ITS OWN SMALL GRANTS CALLS, INVITING NON-GOVERNMENTAL AND COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS TO SUBMIT PROPOSALS ADDRESSING LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL PRIORITIES, with a stated emphasis on youth and women. This is the second funding route recorded for Palestine and it is structurally different from the first: where the Mediterranean hotspot fund runs on periodic regional calls decided abroad, this one is administered through a country programme with its own coordinator. THE ACCESS SEQUENCE IS WHAT TO LEARN, BECAUSE IT IS NOT A SINGLE APPLICATION: you approach the National Coordinator first, who provides the guidelines and forms; you submit a short concept paper; the coordinator pre-screens it against the programme's criteria and the Country Programme Strategy; if it passes you prepare the full proposal, in some cases supported by a planning grant; and the National Steering Committee then accepts it, rejects it, or returns it for more work. A concept paper is a far smaller investment than a full proposal, so the screening step is a genuine protection against wasted effort. MONEY COMES IN THREE INSTALMENTS — up front, mid-term against a satisfactory progress report, and a final payment on the completion report — which a community with no reserves must plan around. Grants under the core programme run up to seventy-five thousand US dollars, with up to a hundred and fifty thousand for strategic projects; older material widely quotes a fifty thousand ceiling. Focal areas are biodiversity, climate change mitigation and adaptation, land degradation and sustainable forest management, international waters and chemicals. THIS ENTRY NAMES NO PALESTINIAN ORGANISATION, DELIBERATELY: this map records only international instruments for Palestine, because naming local bodies can expose the people in them. That is a limit on what is written here, not a statement about what exists. Confirm the current call status and the coordinator before preparing anything, and read the country strategy first. AN UNREGISTERED VILLAGE GROUP CAN BE FUNDED DIRECTLY. The programme states that, in cooperation with UNOPS, it has developed Memoranda of Agreement allowing grants to be awarded to community-based groups that are not formally registered, without going through an intermediary non-governmental organisation. Where registering an association is slow, costly or impossible, that is the difference between a community being fundable and not, and it distinguishes this programme from the hotspot fund also recorded here, which requires a registered entity with its own bank account. Raise it with the coordinator directly. Note too that National Coordinators and programme staff are UN-contracted rather than government-employed, expressly to protect their neutrality and objectivity in awarding grants.

trackers.name: Prince Albert II of Monaco Foundation — Mediterranean basin funding, with a short pre-application
trackers.desc: THE MEDITERRANEAN BASIN IS ITS FIRST STATED PRIORITY AREA, and its domains cover BIODIVERSITY PROTECTION and WATER RESOURCES AND DESERTIFICATION alongside climate and renewable energy — water being the frame that fits most land disputes here. ENTRY IS CHEAP: an annual call open for one month in June, starting with a SHORT ONLINE PRE-APPLICATION rather than a full proposal, so testing whether an idea interests them costs little. IT SETS NO CEILING ON THE GRANT BUT WILL NOT EXCEED HALF THE PROJECT BUDGET — the other half must come from elsewhere. This file recorded a neighbouring case where this foundation provided additional support for a plan that another fund had already initiated; sequencing funders that way is how the fifty per cent condition is normally met, and the hotspot fund recorded separately for this country is the obvious first step in that sequence. ITS PRE-APPLICATION FORM ACCEPTS ASSOCIATIONS, COMPANIES, PUBLIC ORGANISATIONS AND INDIVIDUALS, and it makes grants to civil society organisations, foundations, public and international bodies and enterprises alike — an unusually wide range of eligible applicants. THE LIMITS: no project here was found among those it publishes, and it funds environmental work rather than objection, litigation or advocacy. It advises grant seekers to study its funded projects as the guide to its interests, which is the first thing to do before writing anything.

trackers.name: MedPAN — the network of Mediterranean protected-area managers, and you can join before you have an area
trackers.desc: MEMBERSHIP IS OPEN TO ORGANISATIONS CONTRIBUTING TO THE CREATION OF A MARINE PROTECTED AREA, NOT ONLY TO THOSE ALREADY MANAGING ONE — its own invitation asks whether your organisation manages a protected area OR is contributing to the management or creation of one. A community trying to get a stretch of coast designated therefore qualifies before it has won anything, which is unusual and is the single most useful fact here. IT GATHERS AROUND EIGHTY TO A HUNDRED MEMBER ORGANISATIONS — institutions and NGOs across the Mediterranean that either run protected areas or are creating them — which makes its membership A DIRECTORY OF PEOPLE WHO HAVE ALREADY DONE WHAT YOU ARE TRYING TO DO. This file has found repeatedly that the hardest thing to find is someone who has already succeeded at the same task nearby; a network of practitioners is that. IT ALSO GIVES MONEY, AND THIS TERRITORY IS ON ITS PUBLISHED ELIGIBLE LIST: calls for small projects of up to around twenty-five thousand euros for a single area, or up to around forty-five thousand where three or more areas cooperate on one project. Applications go by a grant application form to a published secretariat email, with a rules document setting eligibility and an online question session before the deadline. CRUCIALLY, THE CALLS ARE OPEN NOT ONLY TO THE BODY MANAGING THE AREA BUT TO OTHER ORGANISATIONS — NGOs, scientific institutions, private companies — WORKING WITH THE AUTHORITIES RESPONSIBLE FOR IT. A community organisation partnering with the relevant authority can apply. AND IT TRAINS: it runs courses to build the operational capacity of protected-area managers and holds regional workshops drawing hundreds of participants. It manages a Mediterranean protected-areas database and publishes a status report on them every four years, which is where to check what already exists along this coast. THE LIMITS: marine and coastal areas only; earlier calls required the applicant to match around a quarter of the cost; and it funds and trains management rather than opposition or litigation. Created in 2008 to coordinate a managers' network that had existed since the 1990s, non-profit, with a permanent secretariat.

trackers.name: Palestinian Hydrology Group — it monitors the water, and it builds the alternative
trackers.desc: IT HAS RUN A WATER, SANITATION AND HYGIENE MONITORING PROGRAMME SINCE 2002, AND IT MONITORS, ANALYSES AND REPORTS ON WATER QUALITY, WATER ACCESS, POLLUTION AND INFRASTRUCTURE, developing information systems including GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEMS. Every other entry recorded for this territory is a foreign fund, a foreign network or a state portal. THIS IS THE EVIDENCE LAYER, AND IT IS DOMESTIC — more than two decades of systematic monitoring by an organisation with offices in Ramallah, Gaza, Hebron, Jerusalem and Nablus, working across SIXTEEN GOVERNORATES. IT ALSO BUILDS THE ALTERNATIVE RATHER THAN ONLY DOCUMENTING THE PROBLEM: rainwater harvesting cisterns, SPRING DEVELOPMENT AND REHABILITATION, groundwater well rehabilitation, rain-fed catchment systems, biogas units for wastewater, and school sanitation — over eight hundred projects reaching more than three hundred thousand people. This file has recorded across the region that a worked alternative plan beats objection alone; here is a body that has built eight hundred of them. NOTE HOW IT COUNTS PEOPLE, BECAUSE IT IS THE MOST COPYABLE THING HERE: in one named village it describes 140 RIGHT HOLDERS — 69 women and girls, 71 men and boys — facing daily problems of water access. Not beneficiaries, RIGHT HOLDERS, counted and disaggregated by sex. A community that can state how many right holders a scheme affects, with the breakdown, has produced the one number an authority has to answer; an unquantified complaint has not. IT CAN BE JOINED AND STEERED: its GENERAL ASSEMBLY IS COMPOSED OF PROFESSIONALS REPRESENTING LOCAL COMMUNITIES, and that assembly ELECTS A BOARD OF DIRECTORS EVERY THREE YEARS — founded, in its own account, on citizens' right to associate for the development of resources. Very few bodies in this payload are membership organisations with elected leadership, and those that are can be influenced from below rather than merely petitioned. ITS FRAMING IS RIGHTS-BASED AND WORTH BORROWING: it works to promote the right of individual access to clean water, EQUAL AND JUST ALLOCATION of water, the involvement of marginalised groups and especially women in decision-making, and good governance in the water sector. THE LIMITS: its subject is water, sanitation and environmental resources — a land dispute unconnected to water fits it poorly. It is a development and monitoring organisation, not a litigator, and it works alongside the water authority rather than against it. Use it for the monitoring record, the mapping, the count of affected right holders and the technical alternative; take an objection to the accountability and legal routes recorded separately here.

trackers.name: ARIJ — village profiles for every locality, and the mapping that shows what official figures miss
trackers.desc: YOUR VILLAGE MAY ALREADY HAVE A PROFILE, FREE AND ONLINE, IN ARABIC AND ENGLISH. This institute publishes detailed profiles for the localities of named governorates — fact sheets, maps and aerial photographs, location and physical characteristics, history, religious and archaeological sites, population, education, health, economic activities, THE LOCAL INSTITUTIONS AND ASSOCIATIONS THAT EXIST THERE, and LOCALITY DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES AND NEEDS — alongside fact sheets for every governorate. A community facing a scheme usually has no baseline document about itself. Check whether one already exists before commissioning anything. AND ONE THING IN THOSE PROFILES IS WORTH MORE THAN THE REST. Its own mapping survey found MORE AGRICULTURAL LAND THAN THE OFFICIAL STATISTICS DID — because the official survey defined agricultural area BY LAND OWNERSHIP and counted only actual holdings, EXCLUDING FRAGMENTED SMALL SEASONAL PLOTS AND HOME GARDENS, which its own survey found in high proportion. If your land is dismissed as not agricultural, the official figure may be measuring something different from what you grow. That is a checkable, documented discrepancy, and it is the kind of argument that changes what a plan is allowed to do with land. ITS GEO-INFORMATICS DEPARTMENT IS A FULL MAPPING CAPABILITY: it acquires and analyses SATELLITE IMAGES, MONITORS LAND USE CHANGE, maintains and updates a geographical database, runs tracking systems using satellite positioning, and produces atlases, interactive maps and the GIS-based village profiles themselves. CRUCIALLY IT WILL WORK FOR OTHERS RATHER THAN ONLY FOR ITSELF: it states that it supports national organisations with reports, geographical records and maps, and that it TRAINS MUNICIPALITIES AND LOCAL COUNCILS ON THE JOB in geo-informatics to improve their performance in natural resource management. A council that can produce its own maps argues differently with a developer than one that cannot, and this file has recorded across the region that councils are often the decisive actor. ITS WIDER WORK COVERS LAND USE, WATER RESOURCES, WASTEWATER AND SOLID WASTE, BIODIVERSITY AND DESERTIFICATION, ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING INCLUDING POLLUTION AND MODELLING, and the empowerment of local communities including capacity building in good governance, transparency and accountability. It monitors land use change, land expropriation and demolitions, and runs a long-standing joint monitoring project with another Palestinian land research body, funded externally, which publishes its findings publicly. THE LIMITS: it is a research and mapping institute, not a law practice or an objector — it produces the evidence and the maps, and somebody else must use them. Its village profiles vary in age, so check the date on any profile before relying on its figures. Use it with the water and sanitation organisation recorded separately here: between them they cover the mapping and the monitoring that this territory's foreign entries cannot supply.

trackers.name: Land Research Center — documents land and housing rights violations, and sits inside a pro bono legal consortium
trackers.desc: ITS ENTIRE SUBJECT IS LAND. It exists to DOCUMENT VIOLATIONS OF LAND AND HOUSING RIGHTS AND DESTRUCTIVE ACTS DIRECTED AT AGRICULTURE AND THE ENVIRONMENT, and to develop the land and the capacities of the people affected by them. Founded in 1986 and registered as an independent non-governmental body in 1999 under a numbered licence, it is a member of the international conservation union. THE MOST USEFUL THING ABOUT IT IS WHAT IT BELONGS TO: a FOUR-ORGANISATION HUMAN RIGHTS CONSORTIUM formed in 2019 with a three-year European Union grant, whose three stated components are PRO BONO LEGAL AID, COUNSELLING AND REPRESENTATION; local and international ADVOCACY TARGETING EUROPEAN UNION INSTITUTIONS AND MEMBER STATES; and capacity building — aimed at protecting marginalised communities. The other three members are legal aid and counselling organisations, including a long-established legal aid and human rights centre. This territory previously had no route to a lawyer recorded in this map at all; a documentation body that sits at the same table as three legal aid organisations is the way in. IT CAN BE JOINED AND ITS LEADERSHIP CHANGED: a GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF TWENTY-FOUR MEMBERS drawn from different professional fields, which elects a SEVEN-MEMBER BOARD EVERY THREE YEARS. That is the second Palestinian membership body recorded here in three rounds, and membership bodies can be influenced from below rather than only petitioned. KNOW WHERE IT ACTUALLY IS BEFORE YOU TRAVEL: its main Jerusalem headquarters HAS BEEN CLOSED SINCE FEBRUARY 2002 BY A MILITARY ORDER THAT IS AUTOMATICALLY RENEWED EVERY SIX MONTHS. Its working branches are in Hebron, Bethlehem and Nablus, with a published telephone number and email. IT ALSO CO-RUNS THE LONG-STANDING MONITORING PROJECT DESCRIBED IN THE ENTRY FOR THE MAPPING INSTITUTE RECORDED SEPARATELY HERE — the two work together, and a community needing both maps and documented violations should approach them as a pair. ONE THING TO WEIGH BEFORE APPROACHING IT: this organisation and its funding partners are the subject of contested characterisations by groups that monitor non-governmental bodies, including allegations about a partner organisation's political affiliations. This file records what a body does and publishes; it does not adjudicate such disputes. Read the competing accounts yourself, and understand that association with a contested organisation can itself become an argument used against a community — which this payload has recorded happening in Georgia and Kyrgyzstan in different forms.

trackers.name: JLAC — free lawyers for demolition, displacement and land confiscation cases, with mobile clinics
trackers.desc: IT TAKES PRO BONO CASES ON HOUSE DEMOLITION, FORCED DISPLACEMENT AND LAND CONFISCATION, and has done so for more than forty years. That is this map's subject stated as an organisation's core practice, and until this round the territory had no route to a lawyer recorded here at all. IT REACHES BEYOND ITS OFFICES: branches in Ramallah, Jerusalem and Salfit, PLUS MOBILE LEGAL CLINICS IN THE NORTHERN WEST BANK. This file has now recorded travelling legal services in three countries — the pattern is that where communities cannot reach a lawyer, the lawyer who matters is the one who comes to the district. AND IT WILL ACT AGAINST WHOEVER IS RESPONSIBLE, INCLUDING ITS OWN AUTHORITY. Its own pages state that the cases it adopts are NOT LIMITED to violations by the occupying power but ALSO INCLUDE VIOLATIONS BY THE PALESTINIAN NATIONAL AUTHORITY in areas under its jurisdiction, naming arbitrary dismissal from public service and political detention. A community whose own government has granted the permit, sold the land or ignored the objection needs a lawyer who will sue that government; very few bodies in this payload will, and fewer still say so in writing. IT HAS WON THE KIND OF CASE A COMMUNITY ACTUALLY FACES: its legal department overturned a DEMOLITION AND REMOVAL ORDER FOR A 1,200-METRE PRIMARY WATER PIPELINE serving a residential community of more than ten housing units. Infrastructure saved by litigation is a rarer outcome than a scheme delayed, and it shows the work reaches beyond individual homes to the services a community depends on. IT COMBINES INDIVIDUAL CASES WITH PUBLIC INTEREST LITIGATION, LEGAL REFORM, COMMUNITY AWARENESS AND ADVOCACY, and it targets poor and marginalised groups and communities specifically. Through the consortium it anchors, it and three partner organisations describe themselves as the largest providers of pro bono legal assistance in East Jerusalem, together serving around thirteen hundred people a year and having taken on 125 HOUSE DEMOLITION CASES, 370 residency cases and 525 social and economic rights cases; the consortium publishes its own telephone number and email. ITS RECORD IS CHECKABLE: it publishes factsheets, legal interventions, legal papers, and annual and financial reports. ONE THING TO WEIGH: this organisation is the subject of contested characterisations by groups that monitor non-governmental bodies, including about its funding origins and its advocacy positions. This file records what a body does and publishes and does not adjudicate such disputes — read the competing accounts, and note that association with a contested organisation can itself be used against a community, as this payload has recorded happening elsewhere in the region.

trackers.name: PARC — it builds and trains the cooperatives, which are how land gets held
trackers.desc: IT WORKS WITH FORTY-ONE COOPERATIVES, EACH OF TWENTY TO EIGHTY MEMBERS — a farmer network of something like one to three thousand households — and it TRAINS THEM AND HELPS BUILD THEM. This file established in the Jordanian case that a cooperative is the vehicle a village uses to keep its land: members agree to sell only inward, and the body holds what would otherwise be sold away. AN ORGANISATION THAT BUILDS COOPERATIVES IS THEREFORE BUILDING THE THING THAT HOLDS LAND, and it has been doing it since 1983. IT BUILDS THEM ON STATED PRINCIPLES OF DEMOCRATIC PARTICIPATION, TRANSPARENCY AND ACCOUNTABILITY, which is the difference between a cooperative that can safely hold an asset and one that cannot. THE TRAINING IS PRACTICAL RATHER THAN RHETORICAL: WATER TREATMENT SYSTEMS, STORAGE FACILITIES, quality control testing of produce, fertilisation and harvesting, FINANCING, marketing, packaging, shipping and export — delivered with its own trading arm. A cooperative that can store, test and sell its crop has an income, and this file has recorded repeatedly that a community body with its own revenue outlasts one that depends on grant cycles. ITS FOUNDING PURPOSE WAS THE LAND ITSELF: it was formed in 1983 by agronomists, agricultural engineers, pioneer farmers and veterinary doctors out of the voluntary movement, who held that specialised agricultural groups would serve farmers and THE NATIONAL GOAL OF PROTECTING THE LAND. Its work spans LAND DEVELOPMENT, WATER RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENT, poverty reduction, women's empowerment and olive oil marketing, and it reaches the West Bank including the Jordan Valley, and Gaza. TWO OF ITS PUBLISHED STRATEGIC OBJECTIVES ARE DIRECTLY USABLE: CREATING AN ENABLING LEGAL ENVIRONMENT AND GOVERNMENT POLICIES for agricultural and rural development, and ENHANCING THE ROLE OF AGRICULTURAL COOPERATIVES AND GRASSROOTS INSTITUTIONS. A community that wants its cooperative recognised, or a rule changed, is asking for something this body already works on. ITS OWN STATEMENT OF PURPOSE IS TO MOBILISE RURAL PEOPLE SO AS TO ENABLE THEM TO CONTROL THEIR RESOURCES — which is the whole of what this map is for. THE LIMITS AND THE CAUTION. It is a development organisation, not a law practice: it will not litigate, and its legal work is policy rather than casework. Its self-description is politically framed, and it is the subject of published criticism by organisations that monitor non-governmental bodies, including scrutiny of its donors. This file records what a body does and publishes and does not adjudicate such disputes — read the competing accounts, and understand, as this payload has recorded elsewhere, that association with a contested organisation can itself become an argument used against a community.

trackers.name: ACAD — agricultural micro-credit, and it lends to cooperatives as well as to farmers
trackers.desc: NOTHING ELSE IN THIS MAP LENDS FARMERS MONEY. This body is specialised in MICRO-CREDIT and business support for poor and low-income producers, and between 1988 and the end of 2013 it financed 14,773 PROJECTS WITH THIRTY-FOUR MILLION DOLLARS — AND THIRTY COOPERATIVE SOCIETIES WITH A FURTHER HALF A MILLION. THAT SECOND FIGURE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS HERE. This file has established that a cooperative is the vehicle through which a community holds land — a village keeps its fields by having members sell only inward. A COOPERATIVE THAT CAN BORROW CAN BUY, BUILD, STORE AND SURVIVE A BAD SEASON; and a farmer who can borrow is a farmer who does not have to sell. IT WAS FOUNDED FOR EXACTLY THAT PURPOSE: established in 1988 to build the economic capacity of small farmers who were at risk of collapse, through IN-KIND FINANCING, starting in the Jordan Valley and extending to the central and northern West Bank, with a Gaza branch from 1996 and branches now in all West Bank governorates. Its support services reach beyond loans to INFRASTRUCTURE, WATER, and the strengthening of baseline organisations and COOPERATIVE SOCIETIES in marginalised rural areas. ITS STATED OBJECTIVES INCLUDE ENCOURAGING AND SUPPORTING THE DEFENCE OF THE RIGHTS OF INDIVIDUAL FARMERS AND FARMING GROUPS, and it is recorded by the land coalition it belongs to under LEGAL ASSISTANCE, LEGAL EMPOWERMENT AND ACCESS TO JUSTICE and under EFFECTIVE ACTIONS AGAINST LAND GRABBING. AND IT CARRIES THE NATIONAL LAND COALITION'S PROGRAMME, WHICH IS THE MOST CONCRETE LIST OF LAND DEFENCE MEASURES IN THIS ENTIRE MAP: awareness sessions on land governance, youth and women's empowerment, THE FENCING OF AGRICULTURAL LANDS TO RESIST EXPANSION, and THE CREATION OF COOPERATIVES. Fencing and forming a cooperative are cheap, physical and available to any village — this file recorded fencing once before, as the first protective act taken at sacred sites in Kyrgyzstan. NOW THE CAUTION, AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF THE RISK: CREDIT IS DEBT. A loan secured against land is one of the commonest ways land is finally lost, and a borrower who cannot repay in a bad year can end up handing over the very field the loan was meant to save. Ask what security is required, whether land can be taken, what happens in a season of drought or closure, and whether the cooperative rather than the household can carry the obligation. THE OTHER LIMITS: it is a lender and development organisation, not a law practice — its legal work is empowerment and advocacy rather than casework; and it operates in a contested environment where donors and organisations are subject to public scrutiny. Use it for finance, for cooperative formation, and for the fencing programme; take a case to the legal routes recorded separately for this territory.

trackers.name: Hebron University legal clinics — including one on housing rights and eviction
trackers.desc: THERE IS A CLINIC HERE SPECIFICALLY ON HOUSING RIGHTS, GIVING LEGAL ADVICE TO OWNERS AND TENANTS ON RENT INCREASES, REPAIRS AND EVICTION. In a payload of nearly three hundred entries, that is the closest thing to a property clinic anywhere in this region — every other legal body recorded in this file handles land questions incidentally, as part of a general practice, or not at all. IT IS NOT ONE CLINIC BUT A SET, EACH ORGANISED BY SUBJECT: family law, covering divorce, custody, ill-treatment and INHERITANCE; anti-violence; HOUSING RIGHTS; human rights; labour law, on workers' and employers' rights and conditions; criminal law, run in partnership with an international legal institution; women's rights, covering discrimination, education and violence; ACADEMIC FREEDOM; and juvenile and children's rights. A community can therefore approach the clinic whose subject actually fits, rather than a general enquiry desk. THE COLLEGE STATES ITS OWN AIM PLAINLY: PROVIDING FREE LEGAL AID SERVICES TO THE MARGINALISED CLASSES OF SOCIETY THROUGH THE LEGAL CLINICS — alongside moot trials, FIELD VISITS, workshops and training courses, and comparative research and international conferences on the law here and elsewhere. Field visits matter: a clinic that goes out is one that can see a site. ITS TRAINING PURPOSE IS ALSO THE COMMUNITY'S GAIN: the clinics exist to give students practice before graduation, which means supervised people with time — the resource a community usually cannot buy. AND IT SITS AT THE CENTRE OF SOMETHING LARGER: this clinic anchors a union of SIX PALESTINIAN UNIVERSITY LEGAL CLINICS formed in 2012 across the West Bank and Gaza, and has been described as a model for clinics in this territory and across the region. If this one cannot help, five others exist. The university itself is the first Palestinian university, founded in 1971, and its college of law was the first of its kind here. THE LIMITS. It is a teaching clinic, so its rhythm is academic and its capacity finite; several of its specialised clinics are advisory rather than representative. Land and planning disputes against public authorities are not among the named subjects — the housing clinic's stated scope is landlord and tenant. And the university's own record includes closures by military order lasting months and, at one point, years, so continuity cannot be assumed. Put the question to the housing clinic first, and ask whether the human rights clinic will take a land matter.

trackers.name: Independent Commission for Human Rights — an ombudsman office that handles thousands of complaints a year
trackers.desc: IT HANDLES BETWEEN TWO AND A HALF AND THREE THOUSAND COMPLAINTS EVERY YEAR — by conducting investigations, collecting the necessary data and information, following up with the concerned authorities, and settling them as quickly as possible. Almost nothing else recorded in this map states what it actually processes. A published caseload tells you the door is open, that complaints are handled rather than filed, and roughly how long a queue you are joining. IT IS THE NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS INSTITUTION HERE AND IT OPERATES AS AN OMBUDSMAN OFFICE — the state-facing complaints body this territory's listing in this file did not have, despite twelve other entries. Established by presidential decree in 1993 under an article of the Basic Law providing for exactly such a commission, published in the official gazette in 1995, and working since 1994. ITS FUNCTIONS ARE FOUR, AND TWO ARE DIRECTLY USABLE IN A LAND DISPUTE: receiving and following up COMPLAINTS; LEGISLATIVE OVERSIGHT; PROVIDING LEGAL ADVICE; and monitoring places of deprivation of liberty. Legislative oversight means a rule or a draft law can be put to it, not only an individual grievance. AND THE MANDATE MOST WORTH ASKING IT TO USE IS ITS REPORTING POWER: it may REPORT WITHOUT RESTRICTION on the human rights situation — on SPECIFIC MATTERS or through THEMATIC REPORTS — and make recommendations to the government, to parliament and to other competent bodies. A community facing a pattern rather than a single decision can ask for a thematic report; this file has recorded repeatedly that a pattern documented in an official publication moves institutions that ignore individual letters. ON INDEPENDENCE THERE IS AN EXTERNAL VERDICT RATHER THAN THIS FILE'S OPINION: IT HOLDS FULL ACCREDITATION WITHIN THE GLOBAL ALLIANCE OF NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS INSTITUTIONS, and it belongs to Arab, Asia-Pacific and Mediterranean networks of such institutions. It has maintained that standing while operating across a territorial and political division that has produced two administrations since 2007, and it works on both sides of it. NOW THE LIMIT THAT DECIDES WHETHER IT IS THE RIGHT DOOR AT ALL: ITS COMPLAINTS RUN AGAINST PALESTINIAN OFFICIAL BODIES. A demolition order, a land seizure or a permit refusal issued by the occupying authority is a different target, and the international accountability routes, the land documentation bodies and the legal aid organisations recorded elsewhere in this file are the ones for that. Use this commission where the decision-maker is a Palestinian ministry, municipality or authority — and note that it advises and recommends rather than representing you in court.

trackers.name: Legal Empowerment Fund — core funding for the kind of legal work this territory already does
trackers.desc: IT GIVES THE RAREST KIND OF MONEY: FLEXIBLE, RENEWABLE, LONG-TERM CORE FUNDING. The emergency fund recorded elsewhere in this file states plainly that core costs and programme costs are NOT covered; this one provides them. Core funding pays the salary of the person who answers the telephone, keeps a clinic open between cases and lets an organisation say no to work that does not fit. This payload has recorded body after body whose real weakness is that it exists only between grants. IT IS THE FIRST GRANTMAKING INITIATIVE CREATED SOLELY TO SUPPORT GRASSROOTS LEGAL EMPOWERMENT, established in 2021 and hosted by an international human rights fund, and it backs strategies of ADVOCACY, EDUCATION AND LITIGATION — describing legal empowerment as combining law with organising to build power among people affected by injustice. THAT DESCRIPTION FITS WHAT ALREADY EXISTS HERE. This map records for this territory university legal clinics organised by subject including one on HOUSING RIGHTS AND EVICTION, a union of six such clinics, a pro bono legal aid organisation working on demolition and land confiscation, a land research body and an agricultural association whose objectives include creating an enabling legal environment. Those are grantee-shaped organisations, and this is the fund built for them. KNOW THE ODDS BEFORE YOU SPEND WEEKS ON AN APPLICATION, BECAUSE THE FUND PUBLISHES THEM: a recent round gave FORTY-TWO GROUPS IN TWENTY-FOUR COUNTRIES a total of one and a half million dollars in two-year grants — AND IT RECEIVED APPLICATIONS FROM ONE HUNDRED AND FIFTY-THREE COUNTRIES REQUESTING OVER TWO HUNDRED AND THIRTY-THREE MILLION. Demand outruns supply by something like a hundred and fifty to one. Apply, but do not plan around it. TWO PRACTICAL POINTS. IT RUNS THEMATIC CALLS, including one for groups working at the intersection of legal empowerment and LAND AND ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE — watch for one covering this region rather than only the open rounds. AND ANONYMITY IS POSSIBLE: two grantees were omitted from a published list because of the sensitive nature of their work. THE LIMITS: it funds ORGANISATIONS rather than individuals or unregistered committees; grants are modest, averaging some tens of thousands of dollars over two years; and it is a foreign fund, which in a contested environment is a fact that can be used against a recipient — this file has recorded that pattern here already.

trackers.name: Palestinian Bar — a searchable lawyer directory, and a duty the bar president can invoke for someone who cannot pay
trackers.desc: TWO INSTRUMENTS, AND THE SECOND IS THE ONE PEOPLE DO NOT KNOW ABOUT. THE FIRST IS A SEARCHABLE DIRECTORY OF PALESTINIAN LAWYERS on the bar's unified portal — so a community can verify that the person it is dealing with is admitted, and find lawyers by name before instructing anyone. THE SECOND IS A DUTY WRITTEN INTO THE BAR'S OWN INTERNAL REGULATION. THE HEAD OF THE BAR MAY ASSIGN ANY LAWYER TO PROVIDE ONE FREE PROFESSIONAL SERVICE EACH YEAR, AND A LAWYER WHO REFUSES WITHOUT ACCEPTABLE REASON, OR WHO NEGLECTS THE DUTY OF DEFENDING FAITHFULLY, IS EXPOSED TO DISCIPLINARY PENALTIES. AND ONE OF THE PERMITTED FORMS OF THAT SERVICE IS DEFENDING A PERSON WHOM THE HEAD OF THE BAR HAS ESTABLISHED TO BE POOR AND UNABLE TO PAY ANY LAWYER'S FEES. So the route is not to ask a lawyer for charity but TO ASK THE HEAD OF THE BAR TO ESTABLISH POVERTY AND ASSIGN COUNSEL. That is the fourth country in this file where the bar, rather than the courts, holds a power to put a lawyer on a case. NOW THE CATCH, AND IT DECIDES WHETHER THE REQUEST WORKS. THE DUTY IS ONCE PER LAWYER PER YEAR, AND THE LIST OF QUALIFYING SERVICES ALSO INCLUDES GIVING A LECTURE TO TRAINEES, ADVISING TRAINEES, PREPARING LESSONS, ORGANISING CONFERENCES AND WRITING LEGAL ARTICLES. A lawyer can therefore discharge the entire obligation by delivering one lecture. ASK EXPLICITLY FOR THE SERVICE TO BE PROVIDED IN THE FORM OF REPRESENTATION, cite the clause on defending a person of established poverty, and put the request in writing to the head of the bar rather than to an individual advocate. KNOW WHAT IT WILL AND WILL NOT REACH: the person's poverty must be ESTABLISHED TO THE HEAD OF THE BAR, so prepare that evidence first; and one assigned service is one service, not an ongoing retainer for a long land dispute. PRACTICAL NOTE ON REACHING THEM: the bar's main website is currently under maintenance while technical and operational updates are carried out, but the unified portal and a separate lawyer services gateway operate alongside it, and the association publishes a telephone, a fax and an email address. The bar was established in 1973 and states its aim as promoting the rule of law and defending the legal rights of Palestinians. THE LIMITS: a directory confirms admission and not competence, and shows no specialism; the assignment duty is discretionary in the head of the bar and thin in volume; and the bar regulates lawyers rather than advocating for clients. Use it with the university housing rights clinic, the union of six legal clinics and the pro bono legal aid organisation recorded separately for this territory — those hold the subject expertise this route does not guarantee.

trackers.name: Engineers Association — the licence application, compulsory supervision, and how to check an engineer
trackers.desc: START WITH THE RULE IT STATES PLAINLY: UNDER THE BUILDINGS REGULATION, ANYONE INTENDING TO CARRY OUT ANY CONSTRUCTION PROJECT MUST SUBMIT AN APPLICATION TO THE COMPETENT COMMITTEE, ON THE PRESCRIBED FORM, TO OBTAIN A LICENCE. That gives a community two things at once: A NAMED BODY THAT HOLDS THE FILE for any scheme near it, and a test — if no application was made on that form, the works are unlicensed, and that is a different and simpler argument than disputing the merits of a permit. SECOND, ENGINEERING SUPERVISION OF CONSTRUCTION PROJECTS IS COMPULSORY, AND THE INSTRUMENTS ARE NAMED. A cabinet decision of 2020 amended the BUILDINGS AND PLANNING REGULATION FOR LOCAL AUTHORITIES of 2011 and brought its supervision requirement into force; supervision protocols were then signed with the municipalities of a governorate; and engineering offices are bound by the supervision instructions set out in the association's CONSULTANCY WORK MANUAL. CITE THE REGULATION BY NUMBER AND YEAR. This file has found across four countries that a named, licensed supervising engineer is the most consistent accountability handle available — that person is identifiable, their standing is checkable, and their professional body can receive a complaint about their conduct EVEN WHERE THE PERMIT ITSELF CANNOT BE TOUCHED. THIRD, YOU CAN CHECK THE ENGINEER. The association operates a lookup against its practice-of-engineering department: enter a name and verify standing before engaging anyone — or before accepting that the person supervising the site next door is entitled to be doing it. FOURTH, AND THIS IS THE SPECIALISM TO ASK FOR BY NAME: THE EVALUATION AND REHABILITATION OF EXISTING BUILDINGS AND STRUCTURES IS A LISTED FIELD WITHIN STRUCTURAL ENGINEERING. When excavation, piling or heavy vehicles crack a neighbouring house, that is the engineer who assesses it — not a general contractor, and not a lawyer. Other listed fields cover roads, traffic systems, ports, airports, railways, bridges and tall buildings, so the specialism can be matched to the project being resisted. THE ASSOCIATION IS ONE OF THE OLDEST AND LARGEST PROFESSIONAL BODIES IN THE TERRITORY, licensed in 1958 with two centres and operating from this one since 1963, grown from dozens of members to thousands, with its headquarters address published. THE LIMITS: it regulates engineers and will not object to a project on your behalf; engaging an office costs money; registration categories differ between local and Jordanian membership, which affects which funds a member belongs to but not the services above. And supervision protocols were signed with the municipalities of one governorate — ASK WHETHER THEY APPLY WHERE YOU ARE. Use it with the university housing rights clinic, the union of legal clinics and the bar's poverty-assignment route recorded separately here: the engineer establishes what is happening physically, and those carry it.

trackers.name: Registry of historic buildings — look up your own village, and the organisation that documented 50,320 buildings before anyone threatened them
trackers.desc: THE SINGLE MOST USEFUL THING IN THIS ENTRY IS THAT YOUR VILLAGE MAY ALREADY BE DOCUMENTED. THIS ORGANISATION'S REGISTRY OF HISTORIC BUILDINGS RECORDED 50,320 HISTORIC BUILDINGS IN 422 VILLAGES AND TOWNS, compiled between 1994 and 2007 and published as three volumes of detailed histories, maps and photographs covering some 420 villages across sixteen districts — AND IT IS BROWSABLE BY DISTRICT AND TOWN ON THE ORGANISATION'S OWN SITE, down to individual houses, their vaults, their courtyards and what they are used for now. DOCUMENTATION MADE BEFORE A THREAT EXISTS IS WORTH MORE THAN ANY SURVEY COMMISSIONED AFTER ONE. A record compiled years ago by architects, archaeologists and historians cannot be dismissed as got up for the dispute — GO AND SEE WHETHER YOUR OWN BUILDINGS ARE IN IT BEFORE YOU COMMISSION ANYTHING, and if they are, that entry is your starting evidence and it costs nothing. THE ORGANISATION IS A NON-PROFIT FOUNDED IN JUNE 1991 WHOSE STATED AIM IS PROTECTING AND DEVELOPING ARCHITECTURAL HERITAGE, AND IT IS DISTINGUISHED BY ITS FOCUS ON RURAL AREAS — which is where this map's work almost always is, and where heritage bodies almost never are. In thirty years it has completed MORE THAN ONE HUNDRED RESTORATION PROJECTS, including monuments in the old city of Jerusalem and the renovation of historic streets in Bethlehem, and it has been recognised internationally, including a 2006 award for best practices in improving the living environment. THE STRATEGIC INSIGHT IN ITS OWN WORK IS WORTH COPYING ANYWHERE: ITS DATA SHOWED THAT REHABILITATING FIFTY VILLAGES WOULD SAVE ROUGHLY HALF THE ARCHITECTURAL HERITAGE OF THE WHOLE COUNTRY, so it built a fifty-village programme around that finding. WHEN YOU HAVE A REGISTRY, YOU CAN WORK OUT WHERE EFFORT BUYS THE MOST — and argue for your village on that basis rather than on sentiment. AND SINCE 2001 IT HAS RUN RESTORATION AS JOB CREATION, which answers the argument every community faces: that protection costs jobs while development brings them. RESTORATION WORK EMPLOYS PEOPLE LOCALLY, AND THIS ORGANISATION HAS TWO DECADES OF EVIDENCE FOR IT. Its work also aims at community and cultural centres for marginalised groups, so a building saved becomes a building used. THE LIMITS: it is a heritage organisation and will speak to the architectural and cultural value of a place, not to its ecology or to planning law — pair it with the land research and legal bodies recorded separately here. The registry closed in 2007, so a building put up or lost since then will not appear, and buildings in it have been threatened by demolition and conflict in the years since. IT DOES NOT HOLD LAND OR PROVIDE LAWYERS.

trackers.name: Heritage award now open here — a regional fund for tangible and intangible heritage projects
trackers.desc: IN FEBRUARY 2026 A HERITAGE AWARD RUN FROM A NEIGHBOURING COUNTRY WAS EXPANDED TO INCLUDE THIS ONE. That matters because it is money and recognition for heritage work, from a source that was previously closed to organisations here. WHAT IT FUNDS: INNOVATIVE PROJECTS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO SAFEGUARDING TANGIBLE AND INTANGIBLE CULTURAL HERITAGE, aiming to promote best practice in that work. It is run by the region's oldest national heritage organisation — a non-governmental non-profit founded in 1989 — in partnership with the European Union's delegation, two banks including one operating here, and a private donor. PREVIOUS EDITIONS RAN IN 2024 AND 2025 AND HONOURED COMPLETED HERITAGE WORK, and the 2025 round had a published application deadline extended into late July — SO EXPECT AN ANNUAL CYCLE WITH A FIXED CLOSING DATE AND WATCH FOR IT, because the expansion to this country is new and the first local round is the least contested one you will ever enter. THIS FITS EXACTLY WHAT THIS COUNTRY ALREADY HAS. This file records here a registry documenting more than fifty thousand historic buildings across four hundred and twenty-two villages, compiled before any present dispute. A REGISTRY ENTRY IS THE EVIDENCE BASE; THIS AWARD IS A WAY TO FUND DOING SOMETHING WITH IT — surveying, stabilising, restoring or recording the practices attached to a place. AND INTANGIBLE HERITAGE IS EXPRESSLY WITHIN SCOPE, which is the opening for communities whose claim rests on crafts, seasonal land use, terracing, water practices or oral knowledge rather than on a listed building. THE LIMITS: it is an award decided competitively by an organisation based in another country, oriented to heritage rather than to land tenure or planning disputes, and it will not fund opposition to a scheme as such — frame the work as safeguarding, documentation or restoration. Confirm the current cycle, the eligibility rules for applicants here and the deadline before building a plan around it.

trackers.name: Documentation organisation — it takes affidavits about land loss, publishes them with legal analysis, and its law library is open to the community
trackers.desc: THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE IS THE METHOD, NOT THE REPUTATION. THIS ORGANISATION'S DOCUMENTATION OF LAND LOSS RUNS ON AFFIDAVITS TAKEN FROM THE PEOPLE IT HAPPENED TO. A published case on the confiscation of TWENTY-NINE DUNUMS of village land rests on AN AFFIDAVIT GIVEN TO IT BY THE HEAD OF THE VILLAGE COUNCIL, recording that the land was fertile and under cultivation and setting out his own account of the circumstances — published alongside analysis against the property provisions of international instruments. THAT IS A ROUTE THIS FILE HAS NOT RECORDED ANYWHERE ELSE IN TWENTY-THREE COUNTRIES: A VILLAGE COUNCIL HEAD OR AN AFFECTED LANDOWNER CAN GIVE A SWORN STATEMENT TO AN ESTABLISHED ORGANISATION AND HAVE IT PUBLISHED, DATED AND ANALYSED. The affidavit is evidence that exists outside your own files, held by a body that will still have it in ten years. THE ORGANISATION IS AN INDEPENDENT PALESTINIAN NON-GOVERNMENTAL HUMAN RIGHTS BODY BASED IN RAMALLAH, ESTABLISHED IN 1979 — among the oldest in the region — AND IN SPECIAL CONSULTATIVE STATUS WITH THE UNITED NATIONS ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL COUNCIL SINCE 2000. That status is what allows it to appear before international bodies, which is the second half of what it offers: documentation that goes somewhere. ITS STATED METHOD IS WORTH QUOTING WHEN APPROACHING IT: IT DOCUMENTS VIOLATIONS OF THE INDIVIDUAL AND COLLECTIVE RIGHTS OF PALESTINIANS IRRESPECTIVE OF THE IDENTITY OF THE PERPETRATOR, and seeks to end them through advocacy before national and international mechanisms. COLLECTIVE RIGHTS ARE NAMED ALONGSIDE INDIVIDUAL ONES — which matters for a village whose loss is communal grazing, water or access rather than one family's title. AND THERE IS A PHYSICAL RESOURCE MOST PEOPLE DO NOT KNOW ABOUT: IT KEEPS A SPECIALISED INTERNATIONAL LAW LIBRARY FOR THE USE OF ITS STAFF AND THE LOCAL COMMUNITY. A LAWYER OR A STUDENT WORKING ON A LAND CASE CAN USE IT. This file has told communities across the region to find legal materials without ever naming a library open to them. IT ALSO WORKS WITH PALESTINIAN CIVIL SOCIETY AND GOVERNMENTAL INSTITUTIONS to bring international standards into local law and policy, and prepares research, studies and interventions. THE LIMITS: it is a documentation and advocacy organisation — IT DOES NOT BUY LAND, FUND COMMUNITIES OR PROVIDE ROUTINE LEGAL REPRESENTATION, and this country's listing records separate bodies for legal aid, land research and village profiles that do those things. International advocacy produces findings and pressure over long periods, not orders that return land. AND IT OPERATES UNDER SUSTAINED PRESSURE ITSELF, INCLUDING LITIGATION AND MEASURES AGAINST IT ABROAD — which is worth knowing before relying on it as a permanent fixture.

trackers.name: Land settlement and registration — be there on survey day, and what counts as proof
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING HELD A BUILDING REGISTRY, VILLAGE PROFILES, FREE LAWYERS FOR DEMOLITION CASES AND AN ORGANISATION THAT DOCUMENTS LAND VIOLATIONS — AND NOTHING ON HOW TO GET LAND REGISTERED IN THE FIRST PLACE, WHICH IS THE STRONGEST PROTECTION THERE IS. Settlement is run by a LAND AND WATER SETTLEMENT AUTHORITY established in 2016 to SECURE AND CONFIRM PRIVATE AND PUBLIC OWNERSHIP and to RESOLVE DISPUTES OVER BOUNDARIES, OWNERSHIP, DISPOSAL AND USUFRUCT. AND THE AUTHORITY'S OWN GUIDANCE CONTAINS THE SINGLE MOST ACTIONABLE SENTENCE IN THIS ENTRY: YOUR PRESENCE ON YOUR LAND AND AT YOUR HOUSE ON THE DAY IT IS SURVEYED AND ITS BOUNDARIES ARE DEMARCATED IS A FUNDAMENTAL FACTOR IN PRESERVING YOUR RIGHTS. BE THERE ON SURVEY DAY. Boundaries are fixed by what the surveyor is shown and told on the ground; an absent owner is a boundary decided by whoever did turn up. THIS FILE RECORDED FOR ANOTHER COUNTRY THAT NEIGHBOURS' PLOTS ARE NOT MEASURED AT THE SAME TIME AND THAT OVERLAPS FOLLOW — the same risk applies here, so agree lines with neighbours BEFORE the survey and stand on the ground during it. WHAT TO BRING IS SPECIFIED: EVERY DOCUMENT YOU HOLD, INCLUDING AN EXTRACT FROM THE PROPERTY TAX REGISTER, AND ANY OTHER PAPERS SUPPORTING THE CLAIM. NOTE WHAT THAT MEANS — A TAX RECORD IS TREATED AS EVIDENCE OF OWNERSHIP. Households without a deed are not without proof, and this payload has now found tax receipts named as evidence in two separate countries. SETTLEMENT ORDERS ARE PUBLISHED AS PUBLIC ANNOUNCEMENTS, so the start of settlement in an area is knowable in advance rather than a surprise. WATCH FOR THE ORDER COVERING YOUR VILLAGE AND TELL EVERY HOUSEHOLD IN IT — a settlement round is the one moment when unregistered land can be brought onto the register cheaply and lawfully, and it does not come round often. THE PROGRAMME IS ACTIVE: THIRTY-FIVE THOUSAND DUNUMS WERE REGISTERED IN THE NORTHERN GOVERNORATES USING MODERN TECHNIQUES, a SECOND REGISTRATION PROJECT is under discussion with an international bank mission, and the authority has run training on applying ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL MANAGEMENT PROCEDURES WITHIN SETTLEMENT WORK — which is a hook for anyone whose land has environmental or social sensitivities. AND ONE FACT MATTERS ENORMOUSLY FOR THE DISPLACED: THE AUTHORITY STATES THAT IT RETAINS OFFICIAL COPIES OF THE REGISTERS OF THE SOUTHERN TERRITORY, AND WARNS AGAINST ANY DISPOSAL OF OR TAMPERING WITH PRIVATE AND PUBLIC PROPERTY. IF LOCAL RECORDS ARE DESTROYED OR INACCESSIBLE, COPIES EXIST ELSEWHERE — which is the answer to the assumption that a lost registry means a lost claim. THE LIMITS: settlement proceeds where the authority is able to operate, and registration under this system does not resolve claims arising under another authority's control — the documentation and legal bodies recorded separately here handle those. Fees, timetables and the governorates currently under settlement were not verified in this round; confirm before travelling. And a settlement round is also when weak claims are tested, so prepare documents before the surveyor arrives rather than after.

trackers.name: ARC-WH — a Palestinian site came OFF the Danger List in 2019, and the centre runs the meetings on how that is done
trackers.desc: THE DANGER LIST HAS AN EXIT, AND A PALESTINIAN PROPERTY IS THE WORKED EXAMPLE: the centre's own record of a regional meeting on World Heritage in Danger highlights the successful removal of the Bethlehem property from the Danger List in 2019, together with the lessons learned from that experience. That matters because a Danger listing is often treated as a verdict rather than a process. It is a process, with a defined route out — the meeting addressed the mechanisms and procedures of the List, the preparation of the desired state of conservation for removal, and the corresponding corrective measures. FOR A COMMUNITY, THE POINT IS THAT DANGER LISTING IS A LEVER WITH DOCUMENTED CONSEQUENCES AND A DEFINED PATH, not a label — and this is the body that convenes the site managers and focal points who administer it. IT ALSO TRAINS PEOPLE IN ASSESSING WHAT A DEVELOPMENT WOULD DO TO A PROTECTED SITE: a regional workshop on impact assessment in a World Heritage context, run with the international conservation and restoration bodies, supported twenty-three site managers and stakeholders from fifteen member states in identifying, evaluating and MITIGATING POTENTIAL NEGATIVE IMPACTS OF DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS on World Heritage properties. WHAT IT IS: a Category 2 Centre under the auspices of UNESCO, established by Bahrain, based in Manama, assisting nineteen Arab States Parties with the 1972 Convention, and providing information, assistance, and logistical and financial support. It works on inventories and Tentative Lists covering both cultural and natural sites. THE LIMIT: it serves States Parties rather than communities and cannot be commissioned by a village — the approach runs through the national heritage authority or a body already working with the centre. This is Palestine's third entry and the first concerning heritage or designation; the other two are funding windows.

trackers.name: The environmental NGO network — one approach that reaches about fifteen organisations
trackers.desc: THIS FILE HAS RECORDED SEVERAL PALESTINIAN ORGANISATIONS ONE AT A TIME — A RESEARCH INSTITUTE, A LAND DOCUMENTATION CENTRE, A HYDROLOGY GROUP, AN AGRICULTURAL RELIEF BODY, A HERITAGE RESTORATION ORGANISATION. THEY ARE COORDINATED BY A NETWORK, AND THE NETWORK IS THE FASTER DOOR.
