For 500+ members, 1,500 wildlife clubs and nine branches, Malawi's WESM and CURE entry; for mining and EIA review, CEPA; for savings-based land purchase, CCODE and the federation entry; for land disputes and representation, the Legal Aid Bureau entry; for the national land network, LandNet Malawi.

trackers.name: SERI (Socio-Economic Rights Institute of South Africa) — a public interest law centre representing communities and social movements free — with a whole work theme devoted to defending the space to assemble and protest without arrest, rural land tenure litigation, and a free guide on opposing and resisting eviction
trackers.desc: ONE OF ITS THREE THEMES IS DEFENDING YOUR RIGHT TO ORGANISE AT ALL — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S MAURITIUS ENTRY COVERS THE CLEARING HOUSE THAT VETS CLIENTS AND REFERS THEM OUT; ITS MAURITANIA ENTRY THE ACTIVIST ECOSYSTEM LAWYERS AND THE MEANS TEST; ITS MOZAMBIQUE ENTRY THE COMMERCIAL ENVIRONMENTAL FIRM; ITS SOUTH AFRICA BUCKET CARRIES A CENTRE FOR ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS HOST, A LEGAL RESOURCES CENTRE HOST AND A LAWYERS FOR HUMAN RIGHTS HOST. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE THIRD THEME, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT SEEKS TO PROTECT THE SITES WITHIN WHICH PEOPLE CAMPAIGN FOR THE PROTECTION AND ADVANCEMENT OF THESE RIGHTS — WORKING TO PROTECT THE POLITICAL SPACES IN WHICH SOCIO-ECONOMIC RIGHTS ACTIVISTS, SOCIAL MOVEMENTS, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS AND TRADE UNIONS ARE ABLE TO EXPRESS THEMSELVES FREELY, ASSEMBLE AND PROTEST WITHOUT UNJUSTIFIED STATE INTERFERENCE, AND BE FREE FROM ARBITRARY ARREST AND DETENTION. A law centre that treats the right to organise as its own subject rather than a precondition somebody else handles. This file has recorded the sequence repeatedly: the community organises, the organisers are arrested, and the land case collapses because there is nobody left to run it. Here the arrest is the case too, and the same lawyers carry both. THE CONVICTION IT WORKS FROM, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IT IS THE PEOPLE WHO ARE ON THE RECEIVING END OF POVERTY AND INEQUALITY WHO ARE BEST PLACED TO DEVISE AND IMPLEMENT STRATEGIES TO CHALLENGE THEM. That is a statement about who directs the strategy, not who benefits from it. A community that arrives with its own plan is being taken at its word, which is the opposite of the arrangement this file has recorded where the lawyer decides what the fight is about. WHO THE CLIENTS ARE: A PUBLIC INTEREST LAW CENTRE PROVIDING DEDICATED SOCIO-ECONOMIC RIGHTS ASSISTANCE TO INDIVIDUALS, COMMUNITIES AND SOCIAL MOVEMENTS — PROVIDING LEGAL ADVICE AND REPRESENTATION, RESEARCH SERVICES AND ADVOCACY SUPPORT. SOCIAL MOVEMENTS as a client category, alongside individuals and communities. An unregistered movement is not outside the client list. THE THREE THEMES: SECURING A HOME; MAKING A LIVING; AND EXPANDING POLITICAL SPACE. THE RIGHTS IT LITIGATES, INCLUDING ONE THAT MATTERS HERE: HOUSING, WATER, HEALTHCARE SERVICES, FAIR LABOUR PRACTICES, ELECTRICITY, SANITATION, A CLEAN AND HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT, EDUCATION AND VARIOUS CHILDREN'S RIGHTS — ALL GROUNDED IN THE COUNTRY'S CONSTITUTION. A CLEAN AND HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT is on the list, litigated as a constitutional socio-economic right rather than as environmental law. For a community facing pollution or a dump, that framing reaches a different bench and a different set of remedies than an environmental appeal does. THE RURAL LAND TENURE WORK: MUCH OF ITS WORK IS CONCENTRATED IN THE MAJOR CITIES, BUT IT ALSO WORKS IN A NAMED RURAL PROVINCE SUPPORTING THE FAMILIES OF THE VICTIMS OF A MASSACRE, AND IN TWO OTHER NAMED RURAL PROVINCES RESEARCHING, ADVOCATING AND LITIGATING FOR LAND TENURE RIGHTS. Rural land tenure litigation, named as current work in named provinces. The urban weighting is real and recorded, but the rural land practice exists — and supporting massacre victims' families is the clearest possible signal about what kind of opponent it will take on. THE GEOGRAPHIC REACH: ACTIVE IN SEVEN OF NINE PROVINCES, BUT WITH NO PARTICULAR GEOGRAPHICAL FOCUS — AND WORKING WITH COMMUNITIES, SOCIAL MOVEMENTS, INDIVIDUALS AND OTHER NON-PROFIT ORGANISATIONS IN THE COUNTRY AND BEYOND. AND BEYOND is worth testing if you are outside South Africa: the stated reach is not strictly national. THE EVICTION WORK IT NAMES: PREVENTING EVICTIONS WHICH LEAD TO HOMELESSNESS, PRESSING FOR THE IN SITU UPGRADING OF INFORMAL SETTLEMENTS, AND PREVENTING UNFAIR WATER AND ELECTRICITY DISCONNECTIONS — ALSO PROTECTING RESIDENTIAL TENANTS AND PREVENTING UNFAIR BANKING PRACTICES WHICH MAY RESULT IN THE LOSS OF A HOME. IN SITU UPGRADING is the demand to make instead of relocation. A settlement improved where it stands keeps the land, the livelihoods and the networks; relocation loses all three, and this file has recorded relocation offered as though it were the only humane option. THE SUB-THEMES UNDER SECURING A HOME: INFORMAL SETTLEMENTS; INNER CITY EVICTIONS AND ACCESS TO ALTERNATIVE ACCOMMODATION; BANK REPOSSESSIONS AND SALES-IN-EXECUTION; AND SPATIAL JUSTICE. BANK REPOSSESSIONS AND SALES-IN-EXECUTION. Land is lost to a bank far more often than to a developer, and it is lost quietly — this is one of the few free legal services in this file that names that route explicitly. THE FREE EVICTION GUIDE AND WHAT IT COVERS: WHAT AN EVICTION IS, WHAT THE LAW SAYS ABOUT EVICTIONS, WHEN AN EVICTION IS UNLAWFUL, THE LAWFUL PROCESS FOR AN EVICTION, HOW TO OPPOSE A LAWFUL EVICTION, AND HOW TO RESIST AN UNLAWFUL EVICTION — ONE OF THE RESOURCES IN A NAMED TOOLKIT AIMED AT INFORMING INDIVIDUALS, COMMUNITIES AND COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS OF THEIR RIGHTS. HOW TO OPPOSE A LAWFUL EVICTION is the section most guides omit. An eviction can be procedurally correct and still be delayed, conditioned or defeated on what happens to the people afterwards — and a community that knows this does not give up when told the papers are in order. THE TENANT GUIDE AND HOW IT WAS BUILT: DEVELOPED WITH A UNIVERSITY URBANISM AND BUILT ENVIRONMENT CENTRE, STRUCTURED IN THREE SECTIONS COVERING THE START, DURATION AND END OF THE LANDLORD-TENANT RELATIONSHIP — BUILT AROUND THE QUESTIONS TENANTS HAVE ACTUALLY ASKED WHEN THEY CAME FOR SUPPORT. Written from the questions clients asked rather than from the statute. That is why it can be handed to somebody without a lawyer present. AND THE RESEARCH IT PUBLISHES FOR OTHERS TO USE: AN INFORMAL SETTLEMENT RESEARCH SERIES OF THREE SITE-BASED REPORTS AND A SYNTHESIS REPORT — NOTING THAT A NATIONAL UPGRADING PROGRAMME PROVIDES A STRONG POLICY FRAMEWORK BUT THAT THERE ARE FEW IF ANY EXAMPLES WHERE MUNICIPALITIES HAVE UPGRADED INFORMAL SETTLEMENTS IN KEEPING WITH THE POLICY. A published finding that the policy exists and is not being followed. That is the sentence to put to a municipality that says upgrading is impossible — sourced, and written by lawyers who litigate against municipalities. WHO IT SUITS: South African communities, settlements and social movements facing eviction, disconnection, repossession or arrest for organising — and rural communities litigating land tenure. CAVEATS: SOUTH AFRICA-CENTRED WITH ITS WEIGHT IN THE CITIES, AND IT TAKES SELECTED PUBLIC INTEREST CASES RATHER THAN OPERATING A WALK-IN SERVICE — for daily walk-in help and document preparation, Mauritius' entry; for the means test on free environmental representation, Mauritania's entry.

trackers.name: Abahlali baseMjondolo — a membership movement of 180,000+ people in 90+ branches whose published constitution makes every shack dweller and informal worker automatically eligible — it occupies land, resists evictions, provides legal support, and bars partnership with any political party
trackers.desc: A MOVEMENT WITH A CONSTITUTION, A CARD, AND A RULE AGAINST PARTIES — method and adjacency declared first: A UGANDAN LAND-EVICTION LEGAL AID ORGANISATION WAS CHECKED FIRST THIS ROUND AND FOUND ALREADY FILED UNDER UGANDA, ON A COALITION HOST RATHER THAN ITS OWN DOMAIN; ALL THREE OF ITS OWN HOSTS WERE ABSENT AND THE SUBJECT CHECK CAUGHT IT, SO IT WAS NOT DUPLICATED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK FOR THIS ENTRY RAN THE SHIPPED HOST AND FIVE SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL ABSENT. THIS FILE'S MOZAMBIQUE ENTRY COVERS THE SAVINGS FEDERATION AND ITS FINANCE AGENCY; ITS MAURITANIA AND MAURITIUS ENTRIES NAME A TENANTS' MOVEMENT WITHOUT DESCRIBING IT OR SHIPPING ITS HOST. NONE IS RESTATED. WHO CAN JOIN, FROM THE CONSTITUTION, WHICH IS THE FIND: ALL SHACK DWELLERS LIVING IN THE COUNTRY, AS WELL AS ALL PEOPLE WORKING IN THE INFORMAL ECONOMY, ARE AUTOMATICALLY ELIGIBLE FOR MEMBERSHIP — AND AN APPLICATION FOR MEMBERSHIP CONSTITUTES AN AGREEMENT TO ABIDE BY THE CONSTITUTION. AUTOMATICALLY ELIGIBLE. No vetting, no invitation, no registered organisation required — the two categories this file has recorded as least able to access anything are the two the constitution admits by right. And note the inversion: people who are NOT poor can join only by special invitation, which is the opposite of every membership body recorded here. THE THREE MEMBERSHIP TYPES AND THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: INDIVIDUAL, BRANCH AND SETTLEMENT — AND IN THE SETTLEMENTS WHERE THERE IS NOT DEMOCRATIC GOVERNANCE, THAT IS WHERE LEADERS ARE NOT SUBJECT TO ANNUAL FREE AND FAIR ELECTION, OR WHERE THERE IS NO GENERAL DESIRE TO AFFILIATE, PEOPLE MAY JOIN AS INDIVIDUAL MEMBERS; INDIVIDUAL MEMBERS ARE WELCOME TO STAND FOR ELECTION TO THE SECRETARIAT. The route around a captured settlement leadership, written into the rules. This file has recorded repeatedly that a community's own committee can be the obstacle — bought, appointed, or simply first to arrive. Here a resident can join alone, without the committee's permission, and can rise to national office doing it. THE FEE AND THE CARD: AN ANNUAL MEMBERSHIP FEE AT AN AMOUNT DETERMINED BY THE SECRETARIAT IS PAYABLE AND CARDS WILL BE ISSUED TO ALL MEMBERS, SOLD AT A RATE APPROVED AT THE ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING. Members pay, and the rate is set by the members' own meeting. That is what independence from donors costs and buys. THE MONEY RULES WRITTEN INTO THE CONSTITUTION: THE TREASURER SHALL KEEP DAY TO DAY RECORDS OF ALL INCOME AND EXPENDITURE, REPORTED ON AT EVERY MEETING; ALL BANK ACCOUNTS MUST HAVE THREE SIGNATORIES, ONE OF WHOM MUST BE THE CHAIR, AND THE CHAIR AND ONE OTHER MUST SIGN ALL TRANSACTIONS. Three signatories and accounts read aloud at every meeting. Copy those two clauses directly into any community organisation's constitution — they are the cheapest protection against the capture this file records destroying community bodies once money arrives. THE PARTY RULE: IT WILL NOT ENTER INTO ANY PARTNERSHIPS WITH ANY POLITICAL PARTY AND IS INDEPENDENT OF ALL PARTY AND ELECTORAL POLITICS — IT WILL NOT TAKE MEMBERSHIP OF A PARTY OR JOIN A PARTY, KEEPING ITS AUTONOMY SEPARATE FROM PARTY DECISION-MAKING STRUCTURES. Written into the constitution rather than left to judgement. A land movement that can be delivered to a party at election time stops being a land movement, and this is the clause that prevents it. THE FOUR THINGS IT SAYS IT DOES: BUILDING BRANCHES AND CREATING SPACES FOR THINKING AND RESISTING TOGETHER; RESISTING EVICTIONS AND REPRESSION, ORGANISING PROTESTS, PROVIDING LEGAL SUPPORT, AND ENGAGING THE MEDIA; OCCUPYING LAND TO CREATE PLACES FOR PEOPLE TO LIVE AND BUILD COMMUNITIES; AND ESTABLISHING WORKING COMMUNES AND FOOD GARDENS. OCCUPYING LAND, stated openly as a method alongside legal support. Recorded plainly: this is a movement that takes ground as well as defends it, which carries consequences a community should weigh before joining. THE FARMLAND DEMAND: WE DEMAND THE RIGHT TO FARMLAND IN AND CLOSE TO OUR COMMUNITIES, AND THE RIGHT TO PRODUCE AND ACCESS HEALTHY FOOD. An urban movement demanding farmland inside the city. Worth noting for any settlement negotiating an upgrade: land to grow on is a separate ask from land to live on, and is rarely put on the table unless someone puts it there. THE SIZE AND ITS GROWTH: FORMED IN 2005 BY 32 REPRESENTATIVES FROM 12 INFORMAL SETTLEMENTS AFTER AROUND 750 RESIDENTS OF ONE SETTLEMENT BLOCKADED A MAJOR ROAD — NOW MORE THAN 180,000 MEMBERS IN 93 BRANCHES ACROSS FOUR PROVINCES, WITH A LATER FIGURE OF MORE THAN 100 BRANCHES ACROSS FIVE; AN EARLIER RECORDED FIGURE WAS 30,000 MEMBERS IN 40 SETTLEMENTS. Thirty-two people from twelve settlements. The starting size is the useful figure here, not the current one. WHO ELSE HAS JOINED: MEMBERSHIP INITIALLY OF URBAN SHACK DWELLERS HAS EXPANDED TO RURAL AND URBAN COMMUNITIES; IT ALSO WORKS WITH STREET TRADERS, WITH FURTHER BRANCHES OF STREET TRADERS, AND HAS MEMBERS IN AREAS WHERE PEOPLE LIVE IN POOR QUALITY HOUSES RATHER THAN SHACKS, WHO JOINED BECAUSE THEIR COMMUNITIES ARE ADJACENT TO SHACK SETTLEMENTS. Neighbouring communities joined because they were adjacent. That is how a settlement stops being isolated — the standard precondition for clearance recorded throughout this file. THE DECISION RULE IT STATES: EVERYONE HAS THE RIGHT TO PARTICIPATE IN ALL DISCUSSIONS AND DECISION-MAKING RELEVANT TO THEM, AND NO ONE SHOULD THINK OR DECIDE FOR US — WITH A COLLECTIVE DECISION AT A GENERAL ASSEMBLY RECORDED AS BINDING ONLY ON THE PROVINCE WHOSE MEMBERSHIP TOOK IT. A national body that limits its own decisions to the province that voted. Federating without surrendering local control, stated in practice rather than principle. THE REPRESSION IT RECORDS AGAINST ITSELF: THREATS, ASSASSINATIONS, UNLAWFUL EVICTIONS AND MANY INSTANCES OF POLICE VIOLENCE — WITH ONE LAND OCCUPATION ATTACKED BY A NAMED MUNICIPAL UNIT THAT DEMOLISHED AND BURNT 76 HOMES IN A SINGLE DAY, AND NAMED MEMBERS ARRESTED AND GRANTED BAIL. Filed without softening. Twenty years of organising has cost members their lives, and a municipality maintains a standing unit for demolishing occupations. Anyone weighing this route should read that first, alongside the protection resources filed under the Republic of Congo and Comoros. AND THE OBSERVATION ABOUT SETTLEMENT POWER THAT EXPLAINS THE MEMBERSHIP RULE: A SETTLEMENT MAY BE CONTROLLED BY ELITES — PEOPLE THERE WITH MONEY, POLITICAL CONNECTIONS, OR SIMPLY THOSE WHO GOT THERE FIRST — OR BY AUTHORITARIAN PARTY MEMBERS MAINTAINED IN CONTROL IN EXCHANGE FOR PETTY FAVOURS TO DELIVER THE SETTLEMENT AS A VOTE BANK; ITS ANSWER IS A HOMEMADE POLITICS THAT EVERYONE CAN UNDERSTAND AND FIND A HOME IN. DELIVER THE SETTLEMENT AS A VOTE BANK names the transaction precisely. A community whose leaders keep promising that the councillor will sort it out is describing that arrangement, and the individual-membership clause above is the designed escape from it. WHO IT SUITS: shack dwellers, informal workers and settlements in this country wanting to join an existing mass movement — and organisers elsewhere looking for constitutional clauses on membership, money and party independence worth copying. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY, AND A MOVEMENT RATHER THAN A SERVICE — IT ORGANISES, OCCUPIES AND SUPPORTS RATHER THAN REPRESENTING YOU AS A CLIENT; ITS METHODS INCLUDE LAND OCCUPATION AND PROTEST, AND ITS MEMBERS HAVE FACED SUSTAINED VIOLENCE. For the savings federation that won a joint planning process instead, Mozambique's entry; for the accredited free law clinic, Mauritania's entry.

trackers.name: Southern Africa Litigation Centre (SALC)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional litigation centre supporting and co-counselling cases across Angola, Botswana, DR Congo, Eswatini, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe. Its socio-economic rights work challenges large-scale agricultural and extractive land use that dispossesses customary landholders without adequate consent, consultation or compensation, and covers mining, pollution and climate justice — live matters include a Zambian community's pollution claim against copper processors and San and Bayei claims to ancestral land in Botswana. WHO IT SUITS: in-country lawyers and community organisations who need a partner with regional capacity and resources; SALC generally works through local counsel and partners rather than taking clients directly. SALC RESOURCES A LAWYER — IT DOES NOT REPLACE ONE. It provides technical and monetary support to local and regional lawyers and organisations litigating human rights and rule of law cases, working primarily through strategic litigation and capacity-strengthening support to lawyers and grassroots organisations. So the ask is not ‘please take my case’ but ‘please back my lawyer’ — come with a local lawyer or local organisation. It also trains human rights lawyers and facilitates networks across the region, so it is a route to finding counsel too. THE SECOND FORUM MOST PEOPLE MISS: SALC supports litigation in South African courts that advances human rights in the southern African region — so where your own courts are slow, captured or hostile, there may be another venue, and SALC is the body that supports using it. NAME THE RIGHT CLUSTER WHEN YOU APPROACH: its themes are criminal justice, civil and political rights, socio-economic rights, international criminal justice, business and human rights and equality rights — ‘environment’ is not one of them, so frame a land-defence case as business and human rights or socio-economic rights. Established 2005 in Johannesburg out of the International Bar Association and OSISA. It has also run open calls for small organisational development grants to emerging CBOs in Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe — periodic, so watch for them.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a pan-African feminist rapid-response fund with reach across all 54 African countries — small grants released quickly for unanticipated, time-critical situations rather than planned programme work, covering safety and protection needs when defenders are threatened and short windows for advocacy after an unexpected event. WHO IT SUITS: women's rights organisations, feminist collectives and movements in which women or gender-diverse people are the primary decision-makers. It does NOT fund individuals, and the action must be strategic, genuinely unanticipated, and completable in under three months. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is emergency money for a moment, not a budget for a campaign — decisions are fast and grants are modest.

trackers.name: ITIE Moçambique
trackers.desc: National Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative body — discloses oil, gas and mining revenues, contracts and licences in Mozambique.

trackers.name: Mozambique — Serviço Nacional de Registo (SNR)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the SNR portal handles online company name reservation & registration via the Conservatória do Registo das Entidades Legais (with Balcão de Atendimento Único one-stops), Mozambique. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Mozambique — Ministério da Economia e Finanças (MEF)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; designs, formulates & executes economic & social development policy and the State budget, Mozambique. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Mozambique.

trackers.name: Constitutional Council (Mozambique)
trackers.desc: Constitutional Council (Mozambique) — supreme court in Mozambique (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: SADC Protocol on Wildlife Conservation and Law Enforcement
trackers.desc: A REGIONAL TREATY WHOSE DEFINITIONS DO REAL WORK. The SADC Protocol on Wildlife Conservation and Law Enforcement (1999, in force 2003) defines ‘taking’ as hunting, killing, injuring, capturing, harassing, collecting, picking, uprooting, digging up, cutting, destruction and removal of any wildlife species. So clearing vegetation for a development is ‘taking’ under this definition, not merely site preparation — that reframing is the most useful thing here. It defines community based wildlife management as management by a community which has the right to manage the wildlife AND to receive the benefits from that management, giving a benefit-sharing argument a treaty source; and ‘conservation’ to include rehabilitation and restoration, so restoration sits inside the defined term. THE CROSS-BORDER HOOK: States Parties must cooperate to manage shared wildlife resources as well as any transfrontier effects of activities within their jurisdiction or control — a mine, dam or plantation whose effects cross a border engages a treaty duty on the state that authorised it. Article 4 objectives include enforcing wildlife laws within, between and among States Parties and facilitating community-based natural resources management. CHECK YOUR STATE HAS RATIFIED — the Protocol is legally binding only for countries that have signed and ratified it, and this entry does not assert that your state has. ON TFCAs: they encompass protected areas as well as multiple resource use areas, so they are not exclusion zones; a TFCA practitioners network founded September 2013 has membership open to all stakeholder groups. And SADC's own 2023–2033 TFCA programme names the marginalisation of communities living in and around protected areas as a problem it exists to address — quotable against the body that wrote it.

trackers.name: Centro Terra Viva — Mozambican environmental lawyers who sit with communities through consultation and resettlement, and train women paralegals
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Mozambican non-profit founded in 2002 — Estudos e Advocacia Ambiental, environmental studies and advocacy — with lawyers on staff, some of them registered with the Mozambican bar. Its published work is the exact sequence a community faces when a project arrives: legal advice to rural communities to secure their land tenure, land delimitation, accompanying community and public consultation processes when land use rights are being granted to private investors, and monitoring resettlement. It works on the licensing processes in Palma and Montepuez in Cabo Delgado — gas and rubies — and has done community land delimitation in Inhambane. WHY DELIMITATION IS THE THING TO ASK FOR FIRST: in Mozambique the land itself cannot be sold or mortgaged, and communities hold rights of use and benefit rather than title, so what protects you is a delimited, documented community right recorded before an investor's application, not a purchase — which is why the resource classes that work in Kenya do not transfer here. THE PART WORTH COPYING ANYWHERE: CTV builds associations of women paralegals — it has trained and organised one in Massingir district in Gaza, and works in Ile in Zambézia — so that the people in resettlement villages can press their own claims after the lawyers leave. It also publishes reports on resettlement, land delimitation, logging and artisanal mining, and runs environmental education programmes. WHO IT SUITS: rural and coastal communities facing extractive projects, concessions or resettlement, and local associations that want their own paralegals trained. CAVEATS: no published intake route, case-selection criteria or fee information; much of the fieldwork sits inside donor-funded projects in named districts, so whether CTV can reach your district depends on which project is running. It is an advocacy and legal-assistance organisation, not a litigation firm, and no land purchase capacity exists here — in Mozambican law there is nothing to buy.

trackers.name: Justiça Ambiental (JA!) — stands with Mozambican communities that refuse the compensation offered, and goes after the projects' financiers
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: JA! / Amigos da Terra Moçambique, a Mozambican civil society organisation based in Maputo that works directly with communities displaced by the gas and coal megaprojects. It visits and works regularly with named villages — Milamba, Senga and Quitupo in the Rovuma basin area — and its documentation of what happened there is the specific kind a reader needs: the project took people's farmland and gave compensatory land that is far from their homes and in many cases not arable. THE MOMENT IT MATTERS MOST: JA! has publicly reported that communities at Maganja affected by the gas project were called in by the police after refusing to accept monetary compensation for their land, and named that as intimidation. Refusing a compensation offer is a legitimate act, and a community that does it needs a national organisation willing to say so out loud on the day the police call. WHAT ELSE IT DOES: it has documented resettlement in the Tete coal province into areas without access to agriculture, with rising food insecurity; it questions operators directly at their own shareholder and public meetings; and with international partners it works the money — raising the responsibilities of the French operator over Mozambique LNG since 2019, and pressing financial institutions, including over a development bank loan to a floating LNG project that UN-appointed human rights experts had raised concerns about. That is the same financier-pressure route this file records in Senegal and Guinea, run from inside the affected country. WHO IT SUITS: Mozambican communities facing displacement, resettlement or compensation offers from gas, coal or hydropower projects, especially in Cabo Delgado and Tete. CAVEATS: an advocacy and campaigning organisation — not a law firm and not a compensation negotiator; for legal assistance, delimitation and paralegal training Mozambique's Centro Terra Viva entry is the one to use. Cabo Delgado is an active conflict zone, and JA!'s own reporting records intimidation of communities that resist.

trackers.name: Centro de Integridade Pública — publishes what the resettlement contracts and mining deals actually say, and names the irregularities
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Centro de Integridade Pública (CIP), a Mozambican non-profit association created in 2005, independent and non-party, working on transparency, anti-corruption and integrity — and, for a community, the organisation that goes after the CONTRACT and the MONEY behind a project rather than the project's fence line. WHAT IT HAS DONE ON RESETTLEMENT AND EXTRACTION: monitoring reports on mining activity in Moma, Moatize, Manica and Sussundenga; documentation of the conflict between resettled families and the coal company at Cateme in Tete; and published exposure of a heavy-sands company installation in Zambézia “laden with irregularities”, dangers to a forest reserve, and a problematic resettlement on Olinda island, Inhassunge district — including impositions and negotiations conducted in the name of the population rather than with it. It has also criticised mining companies' conduct toward host communities nationally, and analysed a parliamentary inquiry into hazardous chemical use in gold mining in Manica, noting mercury pollution, habitat destruction, lost livelihoods and public health harm. THE FIGHT IT PICKED THAT MATTERS MOST TO AN AFFECTED VILLAGE: it stated publicly that the government was seeking to keep the contracts SECRET. A resettlement is governed by documents — the concession contract, the resettlement plan, the environmental licence — and a community that cannot read them is negotiating blind; an organisation whose whole purpose is prising those documents loose is a resource, not a commentator. WHO IT SUITS: Mozambican communities facing resettlement by mining, gas or heavy-sands projects who need the terms, the licence conditions and the money flows made public. CAVEATS: a research, transparency and advocacy organisation — not a law firm, not a paralegal service and not a fund; it publishes, it does not represent you. For delimitation, DUAT documentation and paralegals, Mozambique's Centro Terra Viva entry; for contesting the project and its financiers, JA!.

trackers.name: ORAM — Mozambique's rural mutual-aid association, founded 1992, which walks communities through delimitation to a DUAT certificate
trackers.desc: WHO GETS YOU THE CERTIFICATE: the Associação Rural de Ajuda Mútua (ORAM), a non-profit Mozambican membership association founded in 1992 whose stated mission is to defend the rights and interests of peasants and rural communities and secure sustainable tenure and use of land and natural resources — with the working aim of turning rights of access to land into actual benefits for rural communities. It has PROVINCIAL DELEGATIONS, including a Nampula delegation created in 1996 that extended into Cabo Delgado from 2008, so this is not a capital-city-only organisation. Head office: Rua da Resistência 1518, Maputo; open Monday to Friday, 7:30 to 15:30. WHAT THE PROCESS PRODUCES, AND AT WHAT SCALE: once a delimitation application is authorised, the DUAT certificate is issued and handed to the community at a ceremony attended by the provincial land service, the district government, local authorities, ORAM, partners and community leaders — a public handover, which matters because everyone who might later dispute the boundary is standing there. Documented community delimitations in this work include Muirite and Muilo in Chapa administrative post, Mueda district, Cabo Delgado, at 35,702 and 47,488 hectares respectively. ORAM also works on the alternative to full titling — local mapping and declaration of acquired DUAT rights, producing LOCALLY REGISTERED DECLARATIONS instead of formal titles, which is faster where the cadastre cannot cope. ASK WHICH YOU ARE GETTING: a delimitation certificate for the community, a locally registered declaration, or an individual DUAT — they are not the same document. WHO IT SUITS: Mozambican rural communities and peasant associations seeking delimitation, a community DUAT, or documentation before an investor applies over their land. CAVEATS: an associative rural development organisation, not a law firm; researchers note that the share of forest fees returning to communities has tended to create small local elites and that local government has at times interfered in managing those funds — ask how the money will be governed before it arrives. For paralegals and resettlement monitoring, Mozambique's CTV entry; for contesting a project and its financiers, JA!; for the contracts behind it, CIP.

trackers.name: IPAJ — Mozambique's constitutional free-lawyer service, with provincial AND district delegations, itinerant assistance and new counters inside administrative posts
trackers.desc: WHAT THE CONSTITUTION GUARANTEES: the Instituto do Patrocínio e Assistência Jurídica (IPAJ), created in 1994 under the justice ministry to satisfy the constitutional requirement that the state provide legal assistance and representation — the guarantee sits in Article 62 of the Constitution. A SECOND ENTITLEMENT MOST PEOPLE NEVER INVOKE: the statutes of the Mozambican Bar Association (Ordem dos Advogados de Moçambique) say that members MUST provide free legal representation as one of their duties. So if IPAJ has no capacity, a private advocate still carries a professional obligation — ask the Ordem, not only the Institute. HOW IT IS STRUCTURED AND WHERE IT IS GOING: IPAJ operates through PROVINCIAL AND DISTRICT DELEGATIONS, with provincial delegates subordinated centrally while coordinating with the provincial government; it marked 30 years in 2025, emphasising ITINERANT legal assistance and international partnerships, with the government identifying support to displaced populations of CABO DELGADO as a priority area for it. Reported for one year: more than 300,000 people to benefit from free legal assistance. AND THE ACCESS PATTERN WORTH CHECKING LOCALLY: in Sofala, three new IPAJ service counters were planned for the administrative posts of Munhava, Manga and Inhamízua in Beira district, explicitly to make attendance easier for citizens in need. Ask whether a balcão has opened at your administrative post — the same pattern as Malawi placing legal aid desks inside existing government buildings, and it is how a service reaches people who cannot travel. WHO IT SUITS: Mozambicans without means who need representation — including in land, DUAT and resettlement disputes — and displaced people in Cabo Delgado. CAVEATS: A STATE INSTITUTE under the justice ministry, means-tested and heavily loaded with criminal work; it will not campaign against a licensed project. For delimitation and paralegals, Mozambique's CTV entry; for community DUAT certificates, ORAM; for contesting a project and its financiers, JA!; for the contracts behind it, CIP.

trackers.name: ORAM and Mozambique's community land organisations — the body that walks a village through delimitation to a certificate, with paralegal associations and the peasants' union
trackers.desc: WHO GETS THE TITLE ISSUED: the ORGANIZAÇÃO RURAL DE AJUDA MÚTUA (ORAM) exists to DEFEND THE RIGHTS AND INTERESTS OF CAMPONESES, contributing to associative and community development, and its work is the delimitation of community land. ITS NAMPULA DELEGATION WAS CREATED IN 1996 AND EXPANDED INTO CABO DELGADO FROM 2008, HAVING IMPLEMENTED SEVEN THREE-YEAR STRATEGIC PLANS, with delegations in other provinces including Zambézia. THE RESULT, WITH THE HECTARES: the communities of MUIRITE AND MUILO, Posto Administrativo de Chapa, Distrito de Mueda, Cabo Delgado, RECEIVED THEIR DELIMITATION CERTIFICATES over areas of 35,702 HECTARES AND 47,488 HECTARES respectively. Two neighbouring villages holding certificates over eighty thousand hectares between them is what this organisation actually produces — ask ORAM's provincial delegation to start a delimitation before an investor arrives, not after. AND THE CERTIFICATE IS HANDED OVER AT A CEREMONY ATTENDED BY THE PROVINCIAL LAND SERVICES, THE DISTRICT GOVERNMENT, LOCAL AUTHORITIES, ORAM, PARTNERS AND COMMUNITY LEADERS AND MEMBERS. Insist on the public ceremony. Getting the district government and the land services to hand you the certificate in front of your own community is how the boundary becomes something officials have personally acknowledged. THE REST OF THE NAMED NETWORK, which works alongside ORAM on community land: the UNIÃO NACIONAL DE CAMPONESES (UNAC), the national peasants' union; the FUNDAÇÃO INICIATIVA PARA TERRAS COMUNITÁRIAS (iTC-F), dedicated to community lands; the ASSOCIAÇÃO DE APOIO E ASSISTÊNCIA JURÍDICA ÀS COMUNIDADES (AAAJC), which provides legal support to communities; the ASSOCIAÇÃO DE PARALEGAIS DE CABO DELGADO (ASPACADE); the ASSOCIAÇÃO NACIONAL DE EXTENSÃO RURAL (AENA); the ORDEM DOS ADVOGADOS DE MOÇAMBIQUE; and the CENTRO DE FORMAÇÃO JURÍDICA E JUDICIÁRIA (CFJJ), which trains the justice sector. A paralegal association based in your own province is the cheapest continuous legal presence available to a Mozambican community — ASPACADE for Cabo Delgado, AAAJC nationally. Paralegals live nearby; lawyers visit. A recorded outcome from this network: a local community and an investor established a partnership after conflict mediation by the environmental-law centre. WHO IT SUITS: Mozambican rural communities seeking delimitation, a certificate, paralegal support or mediation with an investor. CAVEATS: NGOs AND ASSOCIATIONS — confirm which have a delegation in your province. For environmental lawyers who sit on the councils, Mozambique's Centro Terra Viva entry; for communities that refuse, Justiça Ambiental; for the resettlement contracts, Centro de Integridade Pública; for the free-lawyer service, IPAJ.

trackers.name: Livaningo and the ombudsman complaint six Mozambican organisations filed together — the incinerator a two-year campaign stopped, and the lender's grievance office that took the smelter case
trackers.desc: THE PLANT THEY STOPPED, AND WHERE SIX ORGANISATIONS FILED TOGETHER: A GRASSROOTS CAMPAIGN BEGUN IN 1998 AGAINST A DANISH-BACKED WASTE INCINERATION PLANT NEAR MATOLA, THE INDUSTRIAL HUB NEAR MAPUTO, HALTED THE PROJECT AFTER A TWO-YEAR STRUGGLE, with its named leader and a team of activists supported by an international environmental organisation. Her account of the starting point is the one to hold onto: WHEN WE BEGAN, THERE WERE NO ORGANISATIONS IN MOZAMBIQUE FIGHTING FOR THESE CAUSES — SO WE CREATED A MOVEMENT. WE MOBILISED PEOPLE, REACHED OUT INTERNATIONALLY AND CONNECTED WITH GROUPS IN SOUTH AFRICA AND THE US, AND GRADUALLY OUR NETWORK GREW. An incinerator was stopped by people who had no organisation when they started. If nothing exists where you are, that is not a reason to wait — it is what she did. AND THE LESSON THE VICTORY TAUGHT, WHICH IS THE STRATEGIC POINT OF THIS ENTRY: IT TAUGHT THE POWER OF HOLDING TRANSNATIONAL CORPORATIONS RESPONSIBLE IN THEIR HOME COUNTRIES — and it inspired communities across Mozambique to make contact for help against disastrous development projects in their own regions. The company's home country is a second front. A foreign-backed project has a parent, a lender and a government behind it that answer to their own publics and their own regulators — find out whose money it is before you decide where to fight. That campaign led to LIVANINGO BEING CO-FOUNDED IN 1998. THE MECHANISM, WITH THE DATE AND THE FILING PARTIES: IN OCTOBER 2010 A COALITION OF LOCAL AND NATIONAL NGOs, REPRESENTING THEMSELVES AND OTHER LOCALLY AFFECTED PEOPLE, FILED A COMPLAINT TO THE COMPLIANCE ADVISOR/OMBUDSMAN CONCERNING AN ALUMINIUM SMELTER 20 KM WEST OF MAPUTO WITH A PRODUCTION CAPACITY OF 250,000 TONNES A YEAR — ON AIR EMISSIONS, COMMUNITY HEALTH AND SAFETY, CONSULTATION, INFORMATION DISCLOSURE AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT PLANS. SIX MOZAMBICAN ORGANISATIONS ARE NAMED AS COMPLAINANTS TOGETHER, INCLUDING A HUMAN RIGHTS LEAGUE AND A DEVELOPMENT NGO ALONGSIDE THE ENVIRONMENTAL BODIES. A lender's own grievance office accepted a complaint from Mozambican NGOs on behalf of affected people. Note the five heads it was filed under — air emissions, health and safety, consultation, information disclosure, environmental management plans. Those are the grounds a project financed by a development lender can be challenged on, and CONSULTATION and INFORMATION DISCLOSURE are the two most communities can prove. And note who filed: environmental organisations, a human rights league and a development NGO in one complaint. A coalition spanning three sectors is harder to characterise as a single interest group — recruit outside your own sector before you file. WHAT THE LEADING ORGANISATIONS DO NOW: one PROVIDES LEGAL SUPPORT TO COMMUNITIES IMPACTED BY MEGAPROJECTS AND CARRIES THEIR VOICES TO THE MEDIA AND TO GOVERNMENT BODIES, WHILE WORKING TO PUT FORWARD DEVELOPMENT ALTERNATIVES AND STRENGTHEN A CULTURE OF CIVIC ACTION, and it monitors named cases including a coal mine in Tete province recorded as taking NEARLY 40,000 HECTARES OF LAND AND CUTTING OFF ACCESS TO THE RIVER ON WHICH MANY RESIDENTS DEPEND, and a dam project on the Zambezi of which 60% OF THE POWER IS INTENDED FOR EXPORT AND 40% FOR MOZAMBIQUE'S OWN NEEDS. Sixty per cent for export is the number to put in front of a community being asked to accept a dam. Ask for the export share of any energy project on your river before you are told what it will do for you. Contacts are published: Rua Kamba Simango nr 184, Maputo, tel +258 21 496668; and an environmental advocacy association in Maputo publishes its own street address and telephone. WHO IT SUITS: Mozambican communities facing a lender-financed megaproject, a mine or a dam. CAVEATS: ADVOCACY ORGANISATIONS — they support, they do not replace counsel. For the certificates over tens of thousands of hectares and the ceremony rule, Mozambique's ORAM entry; for what the resettlement contract says, Centro de Integridade Pública.

trackers.name: Mozambique's Conselhos Comunitários de Pesca — fishing community councils managing natural resources — plus the published menu of legal services to rural communities, the resettlement monitoring, and the Maputo street addresses
trackers.desc: A COUNCIL OF THE FISHERS THEMSELVES, AND A LAWYER WHO SITS IN THE CONSULTATION: A BIODIVERSITY AND PROTECTED AREAS PROGRAMME SUPPORTS, THROUGH A MOZAMBICAN ENVIRONMENTAL LAW ORGANISATION AND A NAMED NATIONAL PARK, A PROJECT ON THE MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES BY THE CONSELHOS COMUNITÁRIOS DE PESCA — THE FISHING COMMUNITY COUNCILS — WITH THE OBJECTIVE OF IMPROVING THE RESILIENCE OF THE ECOSYSTEMS AND THE LIVELIHOODS OF THE FISHING COMMUNITIES ALONG THE PARK'S WESTERN COAST. A fishing community council is a body the fishers themselves sit on, and in Mozambique it is the recognised form for managing the resource. If you fish inside or beside a protected area, that is the structure to ask about by name — and note that a law organisation and a national park are jointly supporting it, which means the council has both legal backing and the park's recognition. THE SERVICE MENU, PUBLISHED BY PERIOD, AND IT READS AS A LIST OF THINGS YOU CAN ASK FOR: FROM 2013 TO 2017 THE WORK WAS LEGAL ADVISORY ACTIVITIES TO RURAL COMMUNITIES FOR REINFORCING THE SECURITY OF LAND TENURE AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF BENEFICIAL PARTNERSHIPS BETWEEN COMMUNITIES AND INVESTORS; MASS ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION AND INFORMATION; THE ACCOMPANIMENT OF COMMUNITY AND PUBLIC CONSULTATION PROCESSES FOR THE ATTRIBUTION OF LAND USE RIGHTS TO PRIVATE INVESTORS; AND THE MONITORING OF RESETTLEMENT PROCESSES. ACCOMPANIMENT OF THE CONSULTATION is the one to underline. In Mozambique a private investor cannot get land use rights without a community consultation, and that consultation is where communities lose — outnumbered, unadvised, signing a record they did not write. An organisation whose stated service is sitting in that meeting with you is the single most useful thing on this list. Ask for it BEFORE the consultation is scheduled, not after. AND THE MONITORING OF RESETTLEMENT PROCESSES is the other half: somebody watching what was promised against what is delivered, after everyone else has gone home. THE EARLIER PERIOD SHOWS THE OTHER CAPABILITY: FROM 2009 TO 2012 THE FOCUS WAS ADVOCACY FOR GOOD ENVIRONMENTAL GOVERNANCE IN THE LAND AND FORESTS SECTOR WITH A RURAL FOCUS, TURNING TO CAPACITY-BUILDING AND TECHNICAL-LEGAL SUPPORT REINFORCED BY APPLIED RESEARCH ON LAND AND FOREST MANAGEMENT AND ADMINISTRATION AT PUBLIC AND COMMUNITY LEVEL. THE STAFF FORM WORTH COPYING: A REGIONAL DELEGATE FOR THE NORTH FOCUSED ON SUPPORTING LOCAL COMMUNITIES IN THE MANAGEMENT OF LAND AND OTHER NATURAL RESOURCES, THROUGH THE PROVISION OF SOCIAL PREPARATION ACTIVITIES FOR ENVIRONMENTAL LICENSING PROCESSES, TRAINING AND MONITORING — AND PRODUCED AND PUBLISHED SEVERAL REPORTS ON RESETTLEMENT. SOCIAL PREPARATION FOR LICENSING is a named service: getting a community ready before the licensing process begins rather than reacting to it. A regional delegate posted in the north, not the capital, is what makes that possible — ask whether the organisation you approach has anyone stationed in your province. THE ADDRESSES, SO YOU CAN WALK IN: BAIRRO CENTRAL B, RUA DA IGREJA Nº 4, 2º DIREITO, MAPUTO, WITH TWO TELEPHONE NUMBERS; AND FOR THE OTHER ORGANISATION, RUA KAMBA SIMANGO NR 184, MAPUTO, WITH A TELEPHONE NUMBER. THE MONITORING PRECEDENT, AND IT STARTED WITH ONE PERSON SPEAKING UP: MOVED BY AN ASTONISHING DENUNCIATION MADE IN MAPUTO DURING A SEMINAR ON CORPORATE RESPONSIBILITY, AN ORGANISATION DECIDED TO BEGIN MONITORING THE SOCIAL IMPACTS OF A NAMED FOREIGN AGRICULTURE COMPANY'S PROJECT IN A NAMED IRRIGATION SCHEME. Somebody stood up at a workshop, said what was happening on their land, and an organisation started monitoring because of it. That is how most of the cases in this file began. If there is a seminar, go and speak — the people who can act are in the room. THE REGIONAL GATHERING TO KNOW ABOUT: ACTIVISTS FROM SOCIAL MOVEMENTS AND ORGANISATIONS IN MOZAMBIQUE, SOUTH AFRICA, LESOTHO, MALAWI, NAMIBIA, ZAMBIA AND ZIMBABWE PARTICIPATED IN A PEOPLES' SUMMIT HELD ALONGSIDE THE REGIONAL BLOC'S OWN SUMMIT — BRINGING TOGETHER FARMERS, FISHERFOLK, LANDLESS PEOPLES AND RURAL PEOPLE. A parallel summit, in the same city, in the same week as the heads of state. Seven countries' movements in one room, and the press already there for the official meeting. When your region's leaders next gather, that is the cheapest platform available. AND THE JOURNALISTS, WITH THE RISK STATED: A GATHERING WAS HELD WITH JOURNALISTS FROM ACROSS MOZAMBIQUE, WHO ARE ALSO BEING TARGETED AND ARE FEARFUL OF WRITING THE TRUTH — WITH A PLAN TO CONTINUE INTERACTING WITH THEM AND GIVING THEM SUPPORT TO PUBLISH THE FACTS. Reporters are frightened too, and supporting them is treated as part of the work rather than a favour. If the local paper will not print your story, the question may not be indifference. WHO IT SUITS: Mozambican fishing and rural communities facing a consultation, a licence or a resettlement. CAVEATS: DEMAND FOR THESE SERVICES EXCEEDS SUPPLY — approach early. For the environmental lawyers who sit with communities, Mozambique's Centro Terra Viva entry; for the organisation that stands with communities refusing a project, Justiça Ambiental; for what the resettlement contracts actually say, Centro de Integridade Pública; for the body that walks communities through delimitation, ORAM; for the ombudsman complaint filed by six organisations, the Livaningo entry.

trackers.name: No-fee data and technology help that explicitly prioritises organisations with no technical staff — a half-hour intake call, one day a month for one to four months, sub-Saharan Africa named as a focus region, and a deeper partnership by application
trackers.desc: THEY PRIORITISE THE GROUPS WITH NOBODY TECHNICAL ON STAFF — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S MALI ENTRY COVERS THE PRINTABLE TOOLKIT AND TRAINERS' MANUAL, ITS LESOTHO ENTRY THE FULLY FUNDED HOLISTIC SECURITY SUPPORT, ITS LIBYA ENTRY THE TWO-HOUR DIGITAL HELPLINE, AND ITS BURKINA FASO ENTRY AN INVESTIGATIVE DATA HOST. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHO IS PRIORITISED, WHICH IS THE FIND: WE PRIORITISE ORGANISATIONS THAT ARE UNDER-RESOURCED OR WHO LACK IN-HOUSE TECH/DATA CAPACITY — AND SUPPORT IS PROVIDED TO ORGANISATIONS OR INDIVIDUALS WITH RESOURCE CONSTRAINTS, WHETHER THAT BE FUNDING OR INTERNAL CAPACITY. Having nobody who understands the technology is the reason you qualify, not the reason you are turned away. This file has recorded that gap repeatedly — a committee holding mapping data, membership lists and witness statements with no idea whether any of it is safe — and here it is the stated entry condition. THE PROGRAMME AND ITS PRICE: LIGHTWEIGHT, NO-FEE SUPPORT TO ORGANISATIONS AND INDIVIDUALS WHO HAVE QUESTIONS ABOUT USING DATA OR TECHNOLOGY IN THEIR SOCIAL JUSTICE WORK. INDIVIDUALS as well as organisations, and no fee. A single organiser with a question qualifies. THE PUBLISHED INTAKE STEPS, SO YOU KNOW EXACTLY WHAT HAPPENS: IT STARTS WITH YOU REACHING OUT WITH A SPECIFIC QUESTION OR CHALLENGE; STEP ONE, A BRIEF INTAKE SURVEY; STEP TWO, A HALF-HOUR INTRODUCTORY CALL — AND IT WILL USUALLY INCLUDE AT LEAST ONE FOLLOW-UP CALL ALONGSIDE SPECIFIC RECOMMENDATIONS AND RESOURCES, AND MIGHT ALSO INCLUDE TECHNICAL FEEDBACK OR CONNECTIONS TO OTHER ORGANISATIONS OR EXPERTS. A SPECIFIC QUESTION is what starts it. Not a proposal, not a project plan — which means the work of getting help is one email describing the problem you actually have. THE TIME COMMITMENT, STATED SO YOU CAN JUDGE IT BEFORE AGREEING: CHALLENGES THAT CAN BE TACKLED TOGETHER WITHIN ONE TO FOUR MONTHS OF LIGHTWEIGHT ENGAGEMENT — FOR EXAMPLE ONE DAY PER MONTH. One day a month. This file has recorded capacity-building programmes that quietly consume a small organisation's entire staff time; publishing the expected burden up front lets a committee decide honestly whether it can carry it during a live land dispute. WHO THE PARTNERS ARE: A WIDE ARRAY OF ORGANISATIONS, USUALLY WITHIN LATIN AMERICA AND SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA, VARYING IN TECHNICAL BACKGROUND — SOME WANT SPECIFIC, TECHNICAL ADVICE, WHILE OTHERS ARE LESS FAMILIAR WITH DIGITAL STRATEGIES AND DATA OR TECHNOLOGY PROCESSES BUT ARE EAGER TO LEARN. WHAT THE SUPPORT CAN COVER: RETHINKING YOUR INTERNAL TECH AND DATA PRACTICES; STRENGTHENING ORGANISATIONAL SECURITY; ADOPTING NEW TOOLS; BUILDING INTERNAL TECHNICAL CONFIDENCE; AND ENSURING THAT YOUR TECH CHOICES MATCH YOUR VALUES. ADOPTING NEW TOOLS is the practical one for this file's readers: before a community organisation commits to a mapping platform, a case-management system or a survey app, somebody independent will look at whether it fits — and this file has recorded plenty of tools adopted because a donor supplied them rather than because they suited the work. THE DEEPER PROGRAMME AND ITS TERMS: IN-DEPTH, NO-COST SUPPORT FOR PARTNERS IN LATIN AMERICA AND SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA THROUGH A NAMED PROGRAMME, WHICH TAKES SIX TO NINE MONTHS AND MUST BE APPLIED FOR — DESCRIBED ELSEWHERE AS THREE TO SIX MONTHS WITH TARGETED RESEARCH, MATCHMAKING AND TAILORED RECOMMENDATIONS, AND ELSEWHERE AGAIN AS A YEAR-LONG PARTNERSHIP TO DESIGN, MANAGE AND IMPLEMENT DATA AND TECHNOLOGY PROJECTS. The published duration varies across their own pages, so ask what is on offer this cycle rather than assuming. What is consistent: it is applied for, it is free, and sub-Saharan Africa is one of two named regions. THE ANNUAL VOLUME: CONTEXTUAL SUPPORT TO OVER 80 ORGANIZATIONS IN ONE YEAR THROUGH THE LIGHT-TOUCH PROGRAMME AND LONGER-TERM PARTNERSHIPS, PLUS IN-DEPTH TECH STRATEGY AND INFRASTRUCTURE SUPPORT TO A FEW SELECTED GROUPS. Eighty on the light programme, a few on the deep one. The odds on the quick route are far better, and it is the one to use first. WHO RUNS IT: A GLOBAL MAJORITY-CENTRED ORGANISATION, AS ITS PROGRAMMES CENTRE COMMUNITIES FROM A GLOBAL MAJORITY CONTEXT, AND AS ITS STAFF IS MOSTLY FROM A GLOBAL MAJORITY CONTEXT, INCLUDING ITS LEADERSHIP. Stated about the leadership, not only the programmes. That is a checkable claim rather than a value statement, and this file has recorded the difference mattering when advice has to fit a place the adviser has never worked in. THE CONTEXT IT NAMES FOR THIS WORK: ACROSS LATIN AMERICA AND AFRICA, CIVIL SOCIETY FACES INFORMATION DISORDERS, SHRINKING CIVIC SPACE, RESTRICTIVE GOVERNMENT POLICIES, AND COLLABORATION BETWEEN BIG TECH COMPANIES AND GOVERNMENTS THAT ENABLES INCREASED SURVEILLANCE — WITH ELECTIONS TAKING PLACE AMID ANTI-NGO LEGISLATION, RESTRICTIVE CYBERSECURITY LAWS, AND USES OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE THAT PUT CIVIL SOCIETY UNDER PRESSURE. RESTRICTIVE CYBERSECURITY LAWS named as a threat to civil society rather than a protection for it. A community organisation prosecuted over a post or a leaked document is usually charged under one, and this file's legal entries are the other half of that problem. THE NAMED TOOL AND THE OPEN CALL: PARTNERS ARE SUPPORTED IN NAVIGATING DIGITAL SECURITY AND RESPONSIBLE DATA CHALLENGES THROUGH A CYBERSECURITY ASSESSMENT TOOL AND THE LIGHT-TOUCH PROGRAMME — AND AN OPEN CALL FOR SUPPORT WAS LAUNCHED TO HELP ORGANIZATIONS AND COLLECTIVES PREPARE FOR A CRITICAL ELECTION PERIOD. An assessment tool you can run against your own organisation. Watch for the open calls: they are time-bound and they are how a group with no existing relationship gets in. AND THE FUNDER-FACING GUIDE IT CO-WROTE, WHICH IS THE ONE TO SEND UPWARD: FUNDERS OFTEN WANT TO BE TRANSPARENT ABOUT THE PROGRAMMING THEY SUPPORT, BUT IN A CLIMATE THAT IS HOSTILE TO CIVIL SOCIETY, PUBLISHING GRANTEE INFORMATION CAN TURN ORGANISATIONS INTO TARGETS — SO IT WORKED WITH TWO NAMED PARTNERS TO PUBLISH A CONVERSATION GUIDE FOR FUNDERS ON SHARING DATA RESPONSIBLY, ADDRESSING DATA COLLECTION, STORAGE AND SHARING. Your funder's transparency page can be the thing that names you to your opponents. Very few grantees think to raise that, and there is now a guide written for the funder rather than for you — which makes the conversation easier to start. WHO IT SUITS: African community organisations and activists with a concrete data or technology question and nobody in-house to answer it. CAVEATS: ADVICE AND CAPACITY, NOT FUNDING, EQUIPMENT OR INCIDENT RESPONSE, AND THE DEEPER PROGRAMME RUNS BY APPLICATION IN CYCLES — for an attack in progress use the helpline. For the two-hour digital helpline, Libya's entry; for fully funded support with no registration requirement, Lesotho's entry; for printable material in your own language, Mali's entry.

trackers.name: Cullinan & Associates Inc., Cape Town and Durban — a named environmental law firm of ten specialists that represents community groups as well as companies — published practice areas covering mining, water licences, heritage and planning, an injunction won against a seismic survey, and offices in two cities
trackers.desc: AN ENVIRONMENTAL LAW FIRM WITH ITS PRACTICE AREAS AND ITS CASES PUBLISHED — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S MALI ENTRY RECORDS THAT THIS FIRM REPRESENTED THE APPLICANTS IN THE OFFSHORE CASE WITHOUT NAMING OR DESCRIBING IT; ITS MADAGASCAR ENTRY THE INTERNATIONAL PROGRAMME THAT PARTNERED ON THOSE CASES; ITS SOUTH AFRICA BUCKET CARRIES A CENTRE FOR ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS HOST AND A LEGAL RESOURCES CENTRE HOST, AND ITS GHANA BUCKET A LEGAL RESOURCES CENTRE NAME. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. WHAT THE FIRM IS, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT PRACTISES EXCLUSIVELY IN THE FIELD OF ENVIRONMENTAL, SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AND GREEN BUSINESS LAW, AND ITS TEAM OF TEN ENVIRONMENTAL LAW SPECIALISTS IS PROBABLY THE LARGEST IN SOUTH AFRICA — A LEADER IN ITS FIELD FOR MORE THAN 20 YEARS. The standing question across this whole file is where a community finds an attorney who actually does this work. Here is a private firm that does nothing else, with ten specialists, named directors and two offices — not a legal aid clinic dependent on grant cycles, and not an international NGO working through partners. WHO IT ACTS FOR: THE PRACTICE REPRESENTS CORPORATE CLIENTS, COMMUNITY GROUPS AND NGOs — AND ALSO ACTS FOR MUNICIPALITIES, NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS AND PRIVATE INDIVIDUALS. COMMUNITY GROUPS and PRIVATE INDIVIDUALS are named client categories alongside corporates and municipalities. Recorded plainly: a firm that also acts for companies will run a conflict check, so name your opponent at first contact — the point made in this file's São Tomé entry about clearinghouses applies just as much to a commercial firm. THE CASE ON RECORD, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE FIRM REPRESENTED GREENPEACE AFRICA AND NATURAL JUSTICE IN AN INJUNCTION APPLICATION TO THE HIGH COURT TO PREVENT A SEISMIC SURVEY FOR THE EXPLORATION OF OIL AND GAS. An injunction application to stop a survey already under way. That is the emergency remedy communities most often need and least often know how to ask for — and it is on this firm's public record. THE PUBLISHED PRACTICE AREAS, WHICH ARE THE MENU A COMMUNITY CAN POINT AT: ADMINISTRATIVE LAW, AGRICULTURE, CLIMATE CHANGE AND CARBON TRADING, CONSERVATION AND WILDLIFE, CONSTITUTIONAL, DUE DILIGENCE AUDITS, ENERGY LAW, FISHING INDUSTRY, FORESTRY, HERITAGE LAW, HIGH COURT PRACTICE, HUNTING, LEGISLATIVE DRAFTING, CIVIL AND HIGH COURT LITIGATION, LOCAL GOVERNMENT LAW, MARINE LIVING RESOURCES, MINERAL LAW AND RIGHTS, MINING, MUNICIPAL LAW, PLANNING LAW, POLLUTION AND WASTE, PROVINCIAL GOVERNMENT, TOWN PLANNING, WASTE LAW AND WATER LAW. HERITAGE LAW, PLANNING LAW and MINERAL RIGHTS in the same list. Most land fights in this file are simultaneously a planning objection, a heritage question and a mineral rights problem, and communities are usually told to find three different specialists. THE WATER PRACTICE IN DETAIL: WATER USE LICENCES AND RIGHTS, REGISTRATION, EFFLUENT, WETLANDS, AND WATER TRIBUNAL APPEALS. A WATER TRIBUNAL APPEAL is a specific, named forum. Where an operation has been granted a licence to take water a community depends on, that is the venue — and knowing the forum exists is most of the battle. THE RIGHTS-OF-NATURE PRACTICE: AT THE FOREFRONT OF DEVELOPING INNOVATIVE MEANS OF RESPECTING THE LAWS OF NATURE, INCLUDING PROTECTING LAND AND SACRED SITES FROM DEVELOPMENT. SACRED SITES named as a practice area rather than a sentiment. Communities whose strongest claim is a burial ground, grove or spring usually cannot find a lawyer who treats that as a legal argument. THE RENEWABLE ENERGY PRACTICE AND WHAT IT INCLUDES: INDEPENDENT POWER PRODUCER GUIDANCE, SITE ACQUISITION, LEGAL STRUCTURES, COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION, AND FINANCING AGREEMENTS. SITE ACQUISITION and COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION are the same practice. A firm that structures land deals for developers understands exactly how they are assembled — which is worth knowing both as a risk and as an asset when the community is the client. THE ASSESSMENT WORK IT IS KNOWN FOR: MATTERS RELATING TO WASTE MANAGEMENT AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENTS, WITH AN IMPRESSIVE TRACK RECORD IN HIGH-PROFILE LITIGATION — AND EXPERTISE IN ENVIRONMENTAL DUE DILIGENCE, COASTAL AND MARINE ISSUES, RENEWABLE ENERGY AND CONTAMINATION. ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENTS are where nearly every project in this file is either stopped or waved through, and a firm that both prepares and challenges them knows what a defective one looks like. THE CONTINENTAL REACH DESCRIBED BY OTHERS: IT HAS ITS EAR TO THE GROUND FOR WHAT IS HAPPENING IN SOUTH AFRICA AND OTHER COUNTRIES, WITH PASSION AND A CONTINENTAL NETWORK. A CONTINENTAL NETWORK is the reason to write from outside South Africa. The firm cannot appear in your national court, but a referral to someone who can is a reasonable thing to ask for. WHO IS IN IT AND WHERE: DIRECTORS ARE THREE NAMED ATTORNEYS, SUPPORTED BY THREE SENIOR ASSOCIATES, ONE ASSOCIATE AND THREE CANDIDATE ATTORNEYS, WITH OFFICES IN CAPE TOWN AND DURBAN — AND A LEAD DIRECTOR WHO HAS WORKED IN MORE THAN 30 COUNTRIES AND DRAFTED ENVIRONMENTAL TREATIES, LAWS AND POLICIES FOR GOVERNMENTS IN ASIA, AFRICA, EUROPE AND SOUTH AMERICA. THE POLICY AND DRAFTING SIDE: IT WORKS CLOSELY WITH ENACT INTERNATIONAL, A SPECIALIST ENVIRONMENTAL LAW AND POLICY CONSULTANCY STAFFED BY THE FIRM'S LAWYERS AND LED BY A GOVERNANCE SPECIALIST PARALEGAL WITH 25 YEARS OF EXPERIENCE — WITH EXPERIENCE DRAFTING NATIONAL, PROVINCIAL AND MUNICIPAL LEGISLATION ON ENVIRONMENTAL AND LAND USE ISSUES. MUNICIPAL LEGISLATION drafting. Where a district or municipality is willing to protect an area but does not know how to write the by-law, that is a service that exists — and this file has recorded sympathetic local authorities failing for exactly that reason. AND THE RELATED BODIES ITS LEAD DIRECTOR SITS IN: A WILD LAW INSTITUTE THAT PIONEERS ECO-CENTRIC LAWS AND GOVERNANCE SYSTEMS, AND A FOUNDING NON-EXECUTIVE DIRECTORSHIP OF A BIODIVERSITY LAW CENTRE. A BIODIVERSITY LAW CENTRE is a separate non-profit worth tracing on its own — the non-commercial route to some of the same expertise. WHO IT SUITS: South African community groups, co-operatives and land committees needing a specialist attorney — and organisations elsewhere in Africa seeking a referral into that network. CAVEATS: A COMMERCIAL LAW FIRM THAT ALSO ACTS FOR CORPORATES AND MUNICIPALITIES — EXPECT A CONFLICT CHECK AND EXPECT FEES; IT IS ADMITTED IN SOUTH AFRICA, SO IT CANNOT APPEAR IN OTHER NATIONAL COURTS. For the organisation that files these cases with fishers as co-applicants, Mali's entry; for pro bono routes where fees are impossible, this file's São Tomé, Eswatini and Ethiopia entries.

trackers.name: Muungano wa Wanavijiji — a federation of about 1,000 settlement groups with over 100,000 members and its own finance agency — which got a 650-acre settlement of 300,000 people declared a special planning area, so the county had to plan it jointly with residents rather than clear it
trackers.desc: THEY GOT THE COUNTY TO PLAN THE SETTLEMENT INSTEAD OF CLEARING IT — method and adjacency declared first: THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THE SHIPPED HOST AND FIVE SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; THE HOST AND FOUR SPELLINGS ARE ABSENT, AND ONE GENERIC WORD APPEARS IN THREE DESCRIPTIONS ON OTHER HOSTS. THIS FILE'S GHANA, ZAMBIA, ZIMBABWE, TOGO AND DJIBOUTI BUCKETS CARRY FEDERATION AND URBAN-POOR-FUND HOSTS OR MENTIONS OF THE SAME GLOBAL NETWORK; ITS NIGERIA BUCKET A PARALEGAL ORGANISATION AND ITS MALI ENTRY THE EVICTION-LAW TRAINER. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PLANNING DECLARATION, WHICH IS THE FIND: A SLUM BELT OF ALMOST 650 ACRES, HOME TO AT LEAST 300,000 PEOPLE, BECAME THE SITE OF LARGE-SCALE COLLABORATIVE COMMUNITY PLANNING JOINTLY LED BY THE COUNTY GOVERNMENT AND COMMUNITY RESIDENTS — A RECOGNITION BY LOCAL GOVERNMENT THAT CONVENTIONAL PLANNING PROCESSES CANNOT ADEQUATELY ADDRESS SUCH SETTLEMENTS' CHALLENGES, AND THAT COMMUNITIES' INPUT IS CRITICAL; AN INTEGRATED DEVELOPMENT PLAN HAS BEEN DRAWN UP, SECTOR PLANS FINALISED WITH THE COUNTY, AND IMPLEMENTATION BEGAN IN MARCH 2020. The opposite outcome to every eviction recorded in this file. Three hundred thousand people on land somebody wanted, and instead of demolition the county was brought into a joint planning process the residents co-led. That is the single most useful precedent here for a settlement facing clearance: the alternative to being removed is being planned WITH, and it has been done at scale. WHAT THE DECLARATION TOOK, AND WHO WAS IN IT: THE RESULT OF MANY YEARS' WORK, ACTION-BASED RESEARCH AND INTERACTIONS BETWEEN THE COUNTY, THE COMMUNITY AND THE MANY ORGANISATIONS THE COMMUNITY WORKED WITH — INCLUDING A RESEARCH PARTNERSHIP INVOLVING A CONSTITUTIONAL LAW INSTITUTE, TWO NATIONAL UNIVERSITIES AND A FOREIGN ONE — WITH THE ALLIANCE MOBILISING THE COMMUNITY, ORGANISING THE CONSULTATION, AND COORDINATING THE 40+ ORGANISATIONS DRAWING UP THE PLAN. MANY YEARS, and forty organisations coordinated by the community's own alliance rather than by the county. Both halves are the honest cost: it is slow, and the community has to be the convener. THE STATUTORY FUNDING POINT, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE CITY COUNTY GOVERNMENT IS STATUTORILY MANDATED WITH FINANCING PUBLIC PARTICIPATION ACTIVITIES LIKE THIS PROCESS. The government must pay for the consultation. Communities are routinely told that meaningful participation is unaffordable; where such a duty exists, the money for meetings, mapping and facilitation is the county's obligation, not a favour. Find out whether your own law says the same. THE STRUCTURE THAT MADE IT POSSIBLE: THE COMMUNITY HAD ORGANISED ITSELF INTO PLATFORMS WHERE IT COULD ARTICULATE ITS DEMANDS AND ADDRESS THE RELEVANT AUTHORITIES; SAVINGS GROUPS ARE A KEY PLATFORM, AND THE PROCESS PLACED RELIANCE ON THOSE EXISTING NETWORKS TO MOBILISE PARTICIPATION — AN IMPORTANT PRECONDITION FOR SUCCESS. The savings groups came first and the planning victory came out of them. A community with no standing structure has nothing for a process like this to rest on, which is the argument for starting the groups long before the threat arrives. THE SIZE OF THE FEDERATION: AROUND 1000 SLUM-BASED GROUPS THROUGHOUT THE COUNTRY WITH MORE THAN 100,000 MEMBERS, CENTRALLY FACILITATED BY NATIONAL LEADERS DRAWN FROM THE SETTLEMENT GROUPS — EACH GROUP AUTONOMOUS. Leaders drawn from the settlements, and each group autonomous. Federating does not mean surrendering control of your own settlement's decisions. WHAT IT FEDERATES AROUND: ISSUES AFFECTING ENTIRE SETTLEMENTS — SECURING RIGHTS TO THE LANDS THEY OCCUPY, OR IMPROVING HOUSING AND DELIVERY OF SERVICES — WITH GROUPS NOT A PROXY FOR THEIR COMMUNITIES BUT A CATALYST FOR RESIDENTS' COLLECTIVE ACTION, AND MEMBERSHIP INCLUDING SHACK OWNERS AND THEIR TENANTS, BUSINESSES, SCHOOLS, HEALTH CENTRES AND RELIGIOUS ESTABLISHMENTS. OWNERS AND THEIR TENANTS in the same body. This file has recorded that split being used to break settlements apart during an eviction; including both by design removes the wedge. THE FINANCE AGENCY IT CREATED: A HOUSING DEVELOPMENT AND FINANCE AGENCY ESTABLISHED IN 2003 BY THE FEDERATION ITSELF, RAISING AND STRUCTURING CAPITAL TO ACHIEVE COMMUNITY AND INDIVIDUAL PLANS, OPERATING ACROSS 14 COUNTIES THROUGH ABOUT THIRTY REGIONAL NETWORKS — ITS PRIMARY CLIENTELE BEING WOMEN WHO LIVE IN INFORMAL SETTLEMENTS. The residents built their own finance house. That is the standing brief's raise-the-money item answered from inside the community rather than by a foreign grant — and it is owned by the federation, so the capital serves the members' plans rather than a donor's programme. WHAT THAT AGENCY PROVIDES BESIDES MONEY: ACCESS TO FINANCE AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, INCLUDING TRAINING IN FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT, HOUSING DEVELOPMENT AND BUSINESS MANAGEMENT. THE METHOD, SYSTEMATISED: BUILDING CITY SLUM PROFILES, FEDERATING SAVING GROUP NETWORKS, AND WORKING WITH CITY AUTHORITIES TO DESIGN PROJECTS, UNDERTAKE POLICY CHANGES AND SECURE CITY FUNDING — USING COMMUNITY SAVINGS, RESIDENT ASSOCIATIONS, SETTLEMENT- AND CITY-WIDE DATA COLLECTION, PEER EXCHANGES, COMMUNITY-LED PROJECT DESIGN AND PARTNERSHIPS WITH COUNTY AND CENTRAL GOVERNMENT. SECURE CITY FUNDING is listed as an outcome of the method, not a hope. The sequence is: count yourselves, organise, then go for the public money. THE EXCHANGE PRINCIPLE: WHEN ONE SAVINGS GROUP HAS INITIATED A SUCCESSFUL INCOME-GENERATING PROJECT, RE-PLANNED A SETTLEMENT, OR BUILT A TOILET BLOCK, THE ALLIANCE ENABLES GROUPS TO COME TOGETHER AND LEARN FROM INTRA-NETWORK ACHIEVEMENTS — ON THE LOGIC THAT DOING IS KNOWING, CHALLENGING THE NOTION THAT DEVELOPMENT SOLUTIONS MUST COME FROM PROFESSIONALS, SO COMMUNITIES BEGIN TO VIEW THEMSELVES AS HOLDING THE ANSWERS TO THEIR OWN PROBLEMS. Read beside the travel grants recorded in this file's Burundi entry: the same conclusion reached independently, that a community learns most from another community that has already done it. THE IN-SITU POSITION: ITS KEY OBJECTIVE IS TO DRIVE THE IN-SITU APPROACH, USING SIMPLE AND AFFORDABLE BUILDING TECHNOLOGIES BASED ON COMMUNITY-ATTESTED BUILDING PLANS, DESIGNS AND CODES — WITH HOUSE IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS IN THREE NAMED SETTLEMENTS ACROSS THREE MUNICIPALITIES IN PARTNERSHIP WITH COUNTY GOVERNMENTS FOR PRECEDENT SETTING. IN-SITU means upgrading where people already are, which is the direct answer to relocation. And COMMUNITY-ATTESTED BUILDING CODES matter: settlements are often cleared on the ground that their housing fails the official standard, so a code the community wrote and the county accepted removes that pretext. AND ITS ORIGIN AND THE DATA IT PRODUCES: IT EMERGED AS A RESPONSE TO FORCED EVICTIONS BY THE GOVERNMENT, BRINGING THOUSANDS OF WOMEN-LED SAVINGS GROUPS TOGETHER INTO A FEDERATION DRIVEN AND GOVERNED BY MEMBERS — PROFILING AND MAPPING SETTLEMENTS AND USING THEIR SAVINGS AND KNOWLEDGE TO PLAN AND IMPLEMENT UPGRADING; ITS SURVEYS SERVE AS AN ANCHOR FOR BOTTOM-UP PLANNING, AND ITS PROFILING REVEALED THE HIGHEST POPULATION DENSITIES IN THE CITY AND A HIGH POVERTY PENALTY WHERE ACCESS TO BASIC SERVICES IS CONTROLLED BY CARTELS. The community's own count is what made the negotiation possible — a settlement that has enumerated itself cannot be described as empty, temporary or small by anyone else. WHO IT SUITS: African settlements facing clearance who want the planning route instead, community savings groups, and organisations looking for a federation-and-finance-agency model built by residents. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY'S FEDERATION AND ITS COUNTY GOVERNMENTS — THE MODEL TRANSFERS, THE ORGANISATION DOES NOT; THE PLANNING DECLARATION TOOK MANY YEARS AND 40+ PARTNER ORGANISATIONS, AND ITS FOCUS IS URBAN SETTLEMENTS RATHER THAN RURAL OR CONSERVATION LAND. For the organisation teaching the laws behind eviction, Mali's entry; for community paralegals, Nigeria's entry.

trackers.name: Customary Land Rights Act 2022 — 60 percent written consent, no sector exempt
trackers.desc: THE STRONGEST CONSENT PROVISION IN THIS MAP. Section 28: no investment shall take place on customary land unless the investor obtains the written, informed consent of at least 60 percent of the male and female adult members of the family or a fair representation of the community with rights to the land. Written consent, not consultation; a numerical threshold, not an undefined ‘community view’ a chief can assert on your behalf; and male and female adults expressly. Section 31 requires investors to sign lease agreements before the investment starts. AND NO SECTOR IS EXEMPT, INCLUDING MINING — where FPIC is codified elsewhere it is typically limited to Indigenous peoples, watered down to ‘consultation’, and usually excludes mining. OTHER OPERATIVE TERMS: industrial development — mining, plantations, farming, housing — is banned in protected, conserved or ecologically sensitive areas, naming wetlands, wildlife habitats, steep slopes and old-growth forests; leasehold may not exceed 50 years; citizens hold a 10 percent minimum share in all large-scale land-based investments; local land use committees must be at least 30 percent women; and all customary land must be registered before it can be acquired for investment. Discrimination in owning or using land by gender, tribe, religion, age, marital, social or economic status is prohibited.

trackers.name: Licence conditions become contract terms — and how the law was won
trackers.desc: THE PROVISION TO REACH FOR WHEN A LICENCE IS BREACHED. The Act incorporates public environmental licence conditions into binding legal agreements between communities and companies — so a licence condition becomes a term of the community's own contract, and breach is actionable by the community itself rather than only by the regulator. That converts a regulatory failure into a contractual claim you control. HOW THE LAW WAS WON, WHICH IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART: it grew from a decade of local fights against land grabs and pollution, with its provisions on consent, women's land rights and responsible investment each stemming from specific grassroots struggles. Communities that had shaped the bill's contents then led a nationwide movement to get it passed — organising regional consultations, submitting inputs, and writing to the President to ask that the laws be sent to Parliament. Both Acts passed unanimously in August 2022. THE CASES THAT DROVE IT: an oil palm company obtained over 74,000 acres from government between 2011 and 2013; and in 2012 an investor took over 30,000 hectares through a one-sided deal with traditional authorities behind closed doors — a holding the size of a chiefdom, including homes and communal spaces. THE HONEST NOTE: Sierra Leonean civil society has said explicitly it needs international support to monitor implementation. A strong statute is not self-executing.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Legal Aid Board — the statute promises a paralegal in every chiefdom; roughly two thirds of chiefdoms have none
trackers.desc: SIERRA LEONE IS THE ONE COUNTRY IN THIS GROUP WHERE FREE HELP WITH A LAND DISPUTE IS MEANT TO REACH THE VILLAGE RATHER THAN THE DISTRICT TOWN, AND THE GAP BETWEEN THE STATUTE AND THE STAFFING IS THE WHOLE STORY. Section 14(2) of the Legal Aid Act 2012 requires the Board to appoint at least one paralegal to each chiefdom. There are 190 chiefdoms. The Board has reported placing paralegals in about a third of them, with a complement in the order of 65 paralegals and volunteer paralegals, and offices in 29 towns — 16 in district headquarter towns and 13 in chiefdom headquarter towns. What makes it worth approaching anyway: the Act endorses paralegals, university law clinics, civil society organisations and NGOs alongside practising lawyers as legal aid providers, the service is free and open regardless of nationality, and mediation is offered as a service in its own right rather than only as a step before litigation — paralegals routinely handle land disputes and conflicts with authorities, and monitor local and informal courts, including checking that fines imposed by a Local Court do not exceed the statutory ceiling and that clients are refunded where they have. URL NOT VERIFIED: no canonical domain for the Board was located, and no page for it was found on a Sierra Leonean government domain; the figures above come from the Board's own country report as circulated through Harvard Law School's Access to Justice programme, from Sierra Leone's Open Government Partnership commitment record, and from HiiL's case study. Approach through a district office in person rather than online, and treat the chiefdom-level presence as something to confirm locally before relying on it.

trackers.name: EPA-SL environmental impact assessment — 14 days to comment, addressed to the Executive Chairman, counted from the last publication
trackers.desc: THE COMMENT WINDOW IS FOURTEEN DAYS AND IT DOES NOT START WHEN YOU HEAR ABOUT THE PROJECT. Under the Environment Protection Agency Act 2022, once an applicant files an environmental impact assessment the Agency publishes it on its website or in a newspaper for inspection and comment by the public, government ministries, professional bodies and NGOs, and comments must reach the Executive Chairman within 14 days of the last publication. Two consequences follow. First, publication in a Freetown newspaper starts the clock for a chiefdom that will never see that newspaper, so the practical protection is to ask the Agency in writing to be notified of filings in your district rather than to watch for a notice. Second, because the period runs from the last publication, establish which of the website posting and the newspaper notice came later before assuming you are out of time. The Executive Chairman then submits the assessment with an environmental public disclosure report to the Board, which considers it within 30 working days. An EIA licence is a statutory requirement for the activities listed in the schedule of the Agency's founding legislation, licences are monitored for deviation from their terms, and the Act provides an appeal against the Agency's decision. Head office is 38 Freetown Road, Wilberforce Village, Freetown; info@epa.gov.sl; +232-88-908-951; open 08:00 to 16:45, Fridays to 15:30. CAVEAT ON THE ADDRESS: at least one intergovernmental directory still lists the Agency at 20E Fifth Road, Juba Hill — use the Agency's own contact page. The section numbering and the two time limits above were read from the Act as published on SierraLII, the national legal information institute, not from the Agency's site, which does not set out the comment procedure.

trackers.name: Green Scenery — documents Sierra Leonean land deals from the field, backs the affected landowners' association, and has been sued twice for defamation for doing it
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Freetown-based environmental and human rights organisation that monitors land grabbing nationally and works alongside MALOA, the Malen Affected Landowners and Users Association, the community's own body in the country's best-documented land conflict. THE FACT THAT DECIDES MOST SIERRA LEONEAN LAND DISPUTES, and which Green Scenery's work turns on: outside Freetown land is owned by individual families, and a paramount chief has no right to sell it — yet the leases at issue were arranged between the chief, government officials and the company. More than 80 per cent of one chiefdom's arable land was leased for palm oil, over 18,000 hectares, on a 50-year term, without the free, prior and informed consent of the landowners. Ask who signed, and whether they had the right to. A High Court ruling elsewhere in the country ordered the restoration of 1,486 acres belonging to over 70 families sold to a company without the owners' informed consent — the principle is enforceable. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES: field fact-finding missions producing published reports — including a 13-page report corroborating the arrest of 57 citizens in the chiefdom — monitoring of arrests and intimidation of land rights defenders, and challenges to the sustainability certification granted to the company despite the conflict. AND THE RISK IT CARRIES SHOULD BE UNDERSTOOD BY ANYONE WHO PUBLISHES: the company filed defamation complaints against Green Scenery in 2013 and again in 2019 over its reports; the first was dropped, and in the second a default judgment was reportedly obtained that the organisation says was never served on it or its lawyer. Community members have fared worse — MALOA members were jailed after a protracted trial, and two people were shot dead in a 2019 escalation. WHO IT SUITS: Sierra Leonean families and communities facing agro-industrial leases, and anyone needing the land deal documented rather than argued about. CAVEATS: a research, documentation and advocacy organisation, not a law firm — Sierra Leone's Legal Aid Board entry covers paralegal coverage, though its civil-representation gate is narrow. MALOA, the community association itself, may merit its own entry.

trackers.name: Namati Sierra Leone — paralegals who renegotiate leases already signed, including a 21,000-hectare deal covering dozens of villages
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Sierra Leone country programme of the legal empowerment organisation Namati, staffed by Sierra Leonean paralegals and lawyers. WHY IT ANSWERS THE SITUATION MOST COMMUNITIES ARE ACTUALLY IN: it works with communities who have seen the entire land of their villages signed away by elders and chiefs who did not have the whole community's best interests at heart — and it renegotiates.
