In one case it worked to renegotiate an inequitable 21,000-hectare lease with a Swiss biofuels company that had taken control of all the land of dozens of villages, leaving them nothing to grow food on, and where necessary it litigates to strike down deals that are manifestly unjust. A signed lease is not the end of the matter. REPORTED RESULTS IN A SINGLE HARD YEAR: paralegals supported six communities to negotiate equitable land lease agreements and four others to harmonise their boundaries, and got a Dutch agricultural company to replant 2,600 trees it had cut down without community consent. Farming families in Nimiyama Chiefdom defended their land rights in a landmark case against local leaders and a foreign company with paralegal support. WHAT ELSE TO KNOW: the paralegal model here is written into law — Sierra Leone's 2012 legal aid act recognised community paralegals and called for them to operate in EVERY CHIEFDOM, though coverage has never matched what the law envisaged. Namati's Sierra Leone team leaders were later contracted by the Ministry of Lands, as independent lawyers, to draft two model land laws, and the resulting land bills were signed into law. WHO IT SUITS: Sierra Leonean communities whose land has been leased over their heads, who want a lease renegotiated, boundaries harmonised, or environmental damage remedied. CAVEATS: an international organisation running a national programme, not a Sierra Leonean NGO; paralegal coverage is uneven; and for local documentation of a land deal, Sierra Leone's Green Scenery entry, or the Legal Aid Board for the statutory service.

trackers.name: Conservation Society of Sierra Leone — the organisation that helped pass the 2022 land laws, fought the Lake Sonfon mining, and built Gola into a £10m benefit-sharing park
trackers.desc: WHAT THE LAW NOW GIVES YOUR COMMUNITY: on 7 September 2022 Sierra Leone enacted the CUSTOMARY LAND RIGHTS ACT and the NATIONAL LAND COMMISSION ACT, which GRANT ALL LOCAL COMMUNITIES THE RIGHT TO FREE PRIOR INFORMED CONSENT OVER ALL INDUSTRIAL PROJECTS ON THEIR LANDS, BAN INDUSTRIAL DEVELOPMENT — INCLUDING MINING, TIMBER AND AGRIBUSINESS — IN OLD-GROWTH FORESTS AND OTHER ECOLOGICALLY SENSITIVE AREAS, INCORPORATE PUBLIC ENVIRONMENTAL LICENCE CONDITIONS INTO BINDING LEGAL AGREEMENTS between communities and companies, and ESTABLISH LOCAL LAND USE COMMITTEES, mandated to be AT LEAST 30% WOMEN. Two things make this the strongest community-land statute in this file: FPIC is granted to ALL communities rather than only those a state classifies as indigenous, and MINING IS NOT EXEMPTED — elsewhere governments claim the subsoil and carve mining out. Landowners can veto a project affecting their land. And the licence clause is the quiet weapon: environmental conditions written into a public permit become terms of a contract you can enforce yourself, instead of waiting for a regulator. WHO HELPED PASS IT AND CAN HELP YOU USE IT: the CONSERVATION SOCIETY OF SIERRA LEONE (cs-sl.org), which contributed evidence-gathering, public awareness and community engagement to the campaign, led work against mining pressure at LAKE SONFON and the Pampana River, and played a foundational role in establishing the GOLA RAINFOREST NATIONAL PARK — 71,070 hectares, enacted by Parliament in December 2010, now a UNESCO World Heritage site — whose REDD+ programme has generated over £10 MILLION with a BENEFIT-SHARING MODEL. WHAT COMMUNITIES HAD ALREADY WON BEFORE THE ACT: Tonkolili district communities won a court judgment against the nation's largest iron mine, with damages and flooding remedies partially paid; and in the Gola region communities INVALIDATED AN ILLEGITIMATE 30,000-HECTARE PALM OIL CONCESSION negotiated without community consent. WHO IT SUITS: Sierra Leonean landowning families and communities facing a mining, plantation or timber project. CAVEATS: A NEW STATUTE STILL BEDDING IN — implementation depends on the land committees actually being constituted, and research records that outcomes differ sharply depending on whether decisions sit with landowning families or the paramount chief. For the committee procedure and the statute text itself, this file's Sierra Leone community land committees entry; for paralegals who renegotiate leases already signed, the Namati entry.

trackers.name: Environmental Foundation for Africa and ENFORAC — a national NGO that puts planting contracts out to community organisations by catchment area, and a 16-member environmental coalition
trackers.desc: THE CATCHMENT CONTRACTS AND THE SIXTEEN-MEMBER COALITION: the ENVIRONMENTAL FOUNDATION FOR AFRICA (EFA, efasl.org), ESTABLISHED 1992 to inspire and enable COMMUNITY-LED PROGRAMMES for sustainable environmental management as a basis for poverty alleviation, whose Sierra Leone arm IS REGISTERED IN SIERRA LEONE AS A NATIONAL NGO, at 1 BEACH ROAD, LAKKA, PMB 34, Freetown Peninsula (tel +232 76 611410), with a BIODIVERSITY AND RENEWABLE ENERGY LEARNING CENTRE at 16 MAIN PENINSULA ROAD, SUSSEX. THE PART A COMMUNITY GROUP CAN ACT ON: in the Freetown urban greening campaign EFA implemented, a season's planting of 300,000 TREES, GRASSES AND SHRUBS OF 52 VARIETIES ACROSS 13 CATCHMENT AREAS AND 76 REFORESTATION AREAS WAS PUT OUT FOR BID DIVIDED INTO THE 13 CATCHMENT AREAS — AND INTERESTED COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS COULD EXPRESS INTEREST OR BID TO MANAGE ONE OR MORE. Planting work broken into catchment lots that CBOs bid for is paid conservation work a village association can win. Ask EFA and the city council when the next expression of interest opens, and register your CBO before it does. WHAT IT HAS BUILT WITH COMMUNITIES: on TIWAI ISLAND AND ITS EIGHT HOSTING COMMUNITIES, and at SUSSEX on the Freetown Peninsula, work included construction of social facilities in the Tiwai communities and SKILLS TRAINING FOR COMMUNITY PEOPLE; elsewhere it formed ECO-CLUBS AND ENVIRONMENTAL ACTION GROUPS IN SCHOOLS AND COMMUNITIES along the coast and supported development of a curriculum integrating environmental education nationally. Its own stated diagnosis: LESS THAN 10% OF SIERRA LEONE'S FOREST COVER REMAINS, contributing to dry-season water shortages and to flooding and landslides in the rains, and FOREST PROTECTION AND REPLANTING EFFORTS ARE INADEQUATE AND YET TO BECOME A PRIORITY IN SIERRA LEONE. AND THE COALITION TO JOIN: THE ENVIRONMENTAL FORUM FOR ACTION (ENFORAC) IS A COALITION OF 16 ENVIRONMENTAL NGOs, COMMUNITY GROUPS AND ACADEMIC INSTITUTIONS that came together AS A UNITED VOICE to protect and advocate for Sierra Leone's natural resources, FORMED 2004 AND LAUNCHED APRIL 2006, REGISTERED WITH THE CORPORATE AFFAIRS COMMISSION AS A NOT-FOR-PROFIT COMPANY LIMITED BY GUARANTEE ON 24 AUGUST 2020. A coalition that admits COMMUNITY GROUPS alongside NGOs and universities is one your village association can actually join — and being registered as a company limited by guarantee means it can hold assets and contract in its own name. Ask about membership, not just support. WHO IT SUITS: Sierra Leonean community organisations wanting paid restoration work, a coalition, or training. CAVEATS: A CHARITY WITH A FOREIGN PARENT and a coalition; neither is a law firm. For land deals documented from the field and the two defamation suits that followed, Sierra Leone's Green Scenery entry; for paralegals who renegotiate existing leases, Namati; for the organisation behind the Customary Land Rights Act, the Conservation Society of Sierra Leone entry; for the 14-day comment window, the EPA-SL entry.

trackers.name: Timap for Justice and the community paralegal method — built when Sierra Leone had 100 lawyers in the whole country — plus the free guidance note written specifically for defending community rights in land acquisition cases
trackers.desc: ONE HUNDRED LAWYERS FOR THE WHOLE COUNTRY — that is the condition this method was invented for, and it is the condition most communities in this file are in: AT THAT POINT, THERE WERE JUST 100 LAWYERS IN ALL OF SIERRA LEONE — AND A NAMED ORGANISATION TRAINED A FRONTLINE OF PARALEGALS IN MEDIATION, ADVOCACY, EDUCATION, AND ORGANIZING. If waiting for a lawyer is not a plan where you live, this is the alternative that was designed for exactly that. And note what the training covers: not just law, but mediation, organising and education. A paralegal is a negotiator and an organiser who happens to know the rules. WHAT A COMMUNITY PARALEGAL IS: A GRASSROOTS ADVOCATE WHO USES THEIR KNOWLEDGE OF THE LAW TO SEEK CONCRETE SOLUTIONS TO INSTANCES OF INJUSTICE, EMPLOYING SUCH TOOLS AS MEDIATION, COMMUNITY ORGANIZING, EDUCATION, AND ADVOCACY BEFORE FORMAL OR CUSTOMARY AUTHORITIES. BEFORE FORMAL OR CUSTOMARY AUTHORITIES — both. In most of the countries in this file the decision that matters is taken by a chief, an elders' council or a district officer, not a judge. A paralegal works in those rooms; a lawyer often cannot. THE PRINCIPLE, AND IT IS THE TEST TO APPLY TO ANYONE OFFERING YOU HELP: RATHER THAN TREATING AFFECTED PEOPLE LIKE VICTIMS REQUIRING AN EXPERT SERVICE — I WILL SOLVE THIS PROBLEM FOR YOU — COMMUNITY PARALEGALS BUILD POWER AMONG THE PEOPLE WITH WHOM THEY WORK. That sentence names the difference between a service and an organising strategy. When the case ends, one leaves you where you were and the other leaves you with people who know how to do it again. THE RECORD, WITH NUMBERS: 195 SUPPORTED COMMUNITY PARALEGALS INITIATED ALMOST 6,000 NEW CASES AND SERVED MORE THAN 13,000 CLIENTS ACROSS SIX COUNTRIES IN A SINGLE YEAR — AND IN TWO COUNTRIES A TEAM SUPPORTED INDIVIDUALS FROM HISTORICALLY-EXCLUDED COMMUNITIES TO SECURE MORE THAN 3,000 LEGAL IDENTITY DOCUMENTS, ENABLING THEM TO SEEK FORMAL EMPLOYMENT AND GOVERNMENT SERVICES. Thirteen thousand clients from 195 paralegals. That ratio is why the model scales where lawyers do not — and identity documents matter to this file specifically, because a person without papers cannot register a claim to land. AND THE DISCIPLINE THAT MAKES IT ARGUABLE: PARALEGALS TRACK DATA ON THE PROCESS AND RESULTS OF EVERY CASE, AND THE LESSONS ARE TRANSLATED INTO LARGE-SCALE CHANGES TO LAWS AND SYSTEMS. Every case recorded. A hundred logged cases of the same failure is a policy argument; a hundred remembered ones are anecdotes. If you start a paralegal programme, start the casebook on day one. THE FREE DOCUMENT TO ASK FOR BY NAME: A GUIDANCE NOTE ON PARALEGAL INTERVENTION IN DEFENDING COMMUNITY RIGHTS IN LAND ACQUISITION CASES WAS PREPARED IN RESPONSE TO A REQUEST FOR MORE GUIDANCE. A curriculum written for exactly the situation this whole file is about — a community whose land is being acquired — and written because practitioners asked for it. That is the first training document to obtain. THE COMPARATIVE RESEARCH THAT TELLS YOU WHAT WORKS: A SIX-COUNTRY RESEARCH PROJECT ON COMMUNITY PARALEGALS, WITH RESEARCH COMPLETED IN SIERRA LEONE, KENYA, INDONESIA, SOUTH AFRICA, LIBERIA AND THE PHILIPPINES, COMPARATIVELY ASSESSING PROGRAMMES' IMPACT ON INDIVIDUALS, HOUSEHOLDS, AND PATTERNS OF LOCAL GOVERNANCE — AND ALSO ASSESSING THEIR SCALE, SUSTAINABILITY AND THEIR RELATIONSHIP TO THE STATE. RELATIONSHIP TO THE STATE is the variable to read before designing anything: whether paralegals are recognised, tolerated or resisted decides how the programme must be built, and it differs sharply between the countries in this file. THE HISTORY, WHICH IS OLDER THAN MOST PEOPLE ASSUME: THE APPROACH DATES BACK TO AT LEAST THE 1950s, WHEN A NAMED ORGANISATION AND OTHERS DEPLOYED PARALEGALS TO HELP NON-WHITE SOUTH AFRICANS NAVIGATE AND DEFEND THEMSELVES AGAINST THE APARTHEID REGIME. Seventy years of practice, invented under a government that was actively hostile. That matters where civic space is closing: the method was built for exactly those conditions. AND THE REGIONAL PICTURE: KENYAN NGOs AND FAITH INSTITUTIONS HAVE TRAINED COMMUNITY PARALEGALS SINCE THE EARLY 1990s, MOST WORKING AS VOLUNTEERS AND ADDRESSING LAND CLAIMS, INHERITANCE, LABOR RIGHTS AND MONITORING — AND THE FIRST CONTINENT-WIDE MEETING OF GRASSROOTS LEGAL ADVOCATES TOOK PLACE IN KAMPALA IN JULY 2012. FAITH INSTITUTIONS as trainers is worth noting: a church, mosque or diocese may already run paralegal training in your area, and it is often the most durable host because it does not depend on project funding. AND A MEMOIR OF A DECADE AS A COMMUNITY-BASED PARALEGAL IN SIERRA LEONE HAS BEEN WRITTEN, USING CASE STUDIES AND STORIES TO EXPLAIN THE MULTIPLE, FLEXIBLE AND INNOVATIVE WAYS GRASSROOTS ADVOCATES CAN BRING JUSTICE TO PLACES AND PEOPLE THAT LAWYERS AND THE LAW DO NOT REACH. A working paralegal's own account, in case studies. That is the training text to put in the hands of the person you are asking to do the job. WHO IT SUITS: any African community with no reachable lawyer, and anyone setting up or funding a paralegal programme. CAVEATS: PARALEGALS ARE NOT LAWYERS — some matters need counsel, and recognition varies by country. For paralegals who renegotiate leases already signed, Sierra Leone's Namati entry; for the organisation that helped pass a named act, the Conservation Society of Sierra Leone entry; for the flexible grants and the country-by-country brief on how paralegal work is funded by government, Kenya's Grassroots Justice Network entry.

trackers.name: The Bench Marks Foundation's Community Monitoring School — a school that trains residents of mining-affected communities to document what the company is doing — 40+ communities trained, 33 locations, 8 facilitators, feeding a six-country network, with the model published and already copied by another organisation in a further country
trackers.desc: THEY TRAIN RESIDENTS TO DOCUMENT THE MINE, AND THE MODEL IS PUBLISHED — method and adjacency declared first: THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THE SHIPPED HOST AND FIVE SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; THE HOST AND FOUR SPELLINGS ABSENT, WITH ONE GENERIC PHRASE APPEARING IN ONE ENTRY ON ANOTHER HOST. THIS FILE'S GAMBIA ENTRY COVERS THE FREE FILMING AND EVIDENCE GUIDES AND ITS NIGER ENTRY THE COMMONAGE ACQUISITIONS. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE SCHOOL AND WHO IT TRAINS, WHICH IS THE FIND: A COMMUNITY MONITORING SCHOOL INITIATED IN 2016 TO SUPPORT COMMUNITIES LOCATED NEAR MINING OPERATIONS IN MONITORING AND DOCUMENTING THE NEGATIVE IMPACTS OF MINING — WHICH HAS MOBILISED AND TRAINED OVER FORTY COMMUNITIES TO MONITOR CORPORATE ACTIVITY, CAPACITATING THEM TO TELL THEIR STORIES AND ENGAGE MINING AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT. Every funder, court and complaints desk in this file assumes the community arrives with a documented record. Almost none of them explains how that record gets made, or pays anyone to make it. This is a standing school that trains residents — not researchers — to produce it, and it has been running since 2016. WHAT THE TRAINING ACTUALLY TEACHES, IN A MONITOR'S OWN WORDS, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: WHENEVER YOU SEE SOMETHING THAT IS WRONG YOU HAVE TO STOP AND CAPTURE IT — WE NOW KNOW HOW TO IDENTIFY ISSUES IN THE COMMUNITIES, CAPTURING THE EVIDENCE AND HOW TO BRING THEM OUT. STOP AND CAPTURE IT. The whole discipline in five words, and the reason most communities have nothing to show a year later: the moment passed and nobody recorded it. THE LIMIT THE MONITORS THEMSELVES IDENTIFIED, AND WHAT WAS ADDED: BUT WE ALSO REALISED THAT REPORTING IS NOT ENOUGH — SOMETHING NEEDED TO FOLLOW TO CREATE CHANGE; THE QUESTION WAS HOW DO YOU SOLVE THE PROBLEMS THAT YOU FIND, AND A NAMED PROBLEM-SOLVING TRAINING ASSISTED ACTIVISTS WITH KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS AROUND IDENTIFYING AND SOLVING PROBLEMS, SO THEY NOW KNOW WHO TO APPROACH. The monitors said documentation alone changed nothing and the programme was rebuilt around that. Worth carrying into any evidence-gathering effort: decide in advance who the record is going TO, or it accumulates and does nothing. THE CHANGE MONITORS REPORT IN THEIR COMMUNITIES: OUR COMMUNITY IS STARTING TO BE MORE CONSCIOUS AND AWARE OF THE ISSUES THAT ARE AFFECTING THEM — IF YOU RAISE AN ISSUE AS A MONITOR NOW, THEY ARE RESPONSIVE. THE REPORTING CHAIN, WHICH IS PRACTICAL AND COPYABLE: PROVINCIAL COMMUNITY MONITOR COORDINATORS CONSOLIDATE THE STORIES AND POST THEM ON THE ACTION VOICES ALERTS WHATSAPP GROUP, WHICH ACTS AS A RESOURCE BASE TO DRAW FROM FOR FURTHER POSTING ON THE WEBSITE AND SOCIAL MEDIA. A WhatsApp group as the intake layer, with coordinators consolidating upward. That is a reporting system a coalition can build this month with no budget and no software — and it is how a scattered set of villages becomes one visible record. THE SIX-COUNTRY NETWORK IT FEEDS: A BROADER SOUTHERN AFRICAN NETWORK WHOSE NAME MEANS WE ARE WATCHING, A PLATFORM WHERE MINING AFFECTED COMMUNITIES SHARE THEIR DAILY STRUGGLES — THE COUNTRIES BEING ANGOLA, THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, MOZAMBIQUE, ZAMBIA, ZIMBABWE AND SOUTH AFRICA. Six countries, and often the same companies operating across them. A community can find out what a mining company did to the last village it dealt with, in a neighbouring country, before negotiating with it. THE CURRENT FOOTPRINT, WITH ITS STAFFING: COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS ACROSS 6 PROVINCES, OPERATING IN 33 LOCATIONS WITHIN 14 LOCAL MUNICIPALITIES, COORDINATED BY 8 FACILITATORS — ALL DIRECTLY AFFECTED BY LARGE-SCALE MINING OPERATIONS; ALSO PRESENT IN SIX OTHER AFRICAN COUNTRIES AND IN FOUR MORE. Eight facilitators for 33 locations. That ratio is the honest measure of what this costs to run, and it is low enough for a national coalition to consider replicating. THE MODEL BEING COPIED BY SOMEONE ELSE: NORWEGIAN CHURCH AID IN TANZANIA DEPLOYS THE SAME COMMUNITY MONITORING SCHOOL MODEL TO STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY CAPACITY THERE. Already transplanted by an unrelated organisation. That is the proof the model travels — and the reason to ask for the curriculum rather than only for help. THE RESEARCH SERIES IT PUBLISHES: A FEARED POLICY GAP SERIES — A CRITICAL RESEARCH ANALYSIS OF CORPORATIONS' CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY POLICIES, SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT REPORTING AND PRACTICES, AGAINST THE LIVED EXPERIENCE OF COMMUNITIES IMPACTED UPON. The method is the comparison: what the company's own report claims, set beside what the residents record. A community with a monitor's log and the company's sustainability report has the two halves of that argument already. WHAT IT SAYS IT IS FOR: ADDRESSING SKEWED POWER RELATIONS BETWEEN COMMUNITIES AND CORPORATIONS THROUGH INTERVENTION THAT LEVELS THE PLAYING FIELD, LEADING TO COMMUNITY AGENCY AND CHANGE — AND MONITORING MULTINATIONAL CORPORATIONS TO ENSURE THEY MEET MINIMUM SOCIAL, ENVIRONMENTAL AND ECONOMIC STANDARDS. THE FREE PUBLICATIONS THE MONITORS THEMSELVES PRODUCED: BOOKLETS AND VIDEOS FROM THE ACTIVIST TRAINING PROGRAMME, INCLUDING AN INVESTIGATION BY THE ACTIVISTS INTO FOOD PRICE INCREASES AND HOW THEY AFFECTED POOR COMMUNITIES LIVING NEAR MINES, AND ONE ON DEALING WITH FOOD INSECURITY AND MAKING FOOD GARDENS — ON THE STATED BELIEF THAT GROWING FOOD IS LIKE PRINTING OWN MONEY; TARGET GROUPS ARE THE MINING COMMUNITIES THEMSELVES, INCLUDING YOUNG WOMEN AND LEARNERS, WITH A SECONDARY TARGET OF SCHOOL PRINCIPALS, TEACHERS, MINES AND GOVERNMENT DEPARTMENTS. The trained residents write the booklets, and the second audience is the school principal and the mine. Material produced by the affected community and aimed at the local officials is a different instrument from a report written about them for donors abroad. AND THE QUESTION THAT SHAPED THE PROGRAMME, PLUS THE MEDIA POSITION: IT ASKED ITSELF WHAT CAN WE LEARN FROM THE EXPERIENCES OF THESE ACTIVISTS ABOUT THE CAPACITIES NEEDED BY COMMUNITIES — DEVELOPING THE SCHOOL BECAUSE OF A VACUUM OF KNOWLEDGE; IT HOLDS A STRONG MEDIA VOICE IN MAINSTREAM MEDIA AND GIVES VOICE TO COMMUNITIES USING SOCIAL AND MAINSTREAM MEDIA, WITH THE SLOGAN LET THEM TALK. The curriculum was derived from asking existing activists what they had needed. Any organisation building training should start there rather than with an expert's syllabus. WHO IT SUITS: communities living beside large-scale mining who need their own documented record — and coalitions anywhere wanting a published, already-transplanted model for training resident monitors. CAVEATS: ITS FRAME IS MINING AND CORPORATE ACCOUNTABILITY RATHER THAN LAND PURCHASE OR LITIGATION, AND IT TRAINS AND PUBLISHES RATHER THAN REPRESENTING COMMUNITIES; ITS DIRECT PRESENCE IS CONCENTRATED IN ONE COUNTRY WITH LIGHTER COVERAGE ELSEWHERE. For the free guides on filming so footage stands as evidence, Gambia's entry; for the mining-affected community network with a peoples' charter, Niger's entry.

trackers.name: SERAP (Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project), Lagos — files for named villages, took the Abule Egba pipeline community to the African Commission, and sued Nigeria plus nine oil defendants including ExxonMobil in the ECOWAS Court
trackers.desc: THEY FILE FOR THE VILLAGE, AND THE PAPERS SHOW WHAT THE STATE WILL ARGUE BACK — method and adjacency declared first: FIRST OF THE NAMED-ATTORNEY ROUNDS, AFTER NINE ACQUISITION ROUNDS MOVED THE AFRICA-WIDE MEDIAN ON LAND ACQUISITION FROM ONE TO TWO. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN FOUR HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; THE SUBJECT'S OWN HOST AND ALL SIX FACTS ABSENT, WITH ONE UNRELATED COALITION HOST IN TWO BUCKETS. THIS FILE'S ERITREA ENTRY COVERS THE CONTINENTAL COMMISSION'S COMPLAINT PROCEDURE AND ITS EGYPT ENTRY THE REGIONAL COURT'S NO-EXHAUSTION RULE — PROCEDURAL BODIES, NOT COUNSEL. THIS IS THE ORGANISATION THAT APPEARS BEFORE THEM. NONE IS RESTATED. WHO IT FILES FOR, WHICH IS THE FIND: A COMMUNICATION RECEIVED BY THE CONTINENTAL COMMISSION'S SECRETARIAT FROM THIS ORGANISATION ON BEHALF OF THE PEOPLE OF THE AWORI COMMUNITY OF ABULE EGBA, LAGOS STATE, AGAINST THE FEDERAL REPUBLIC — ALLEGING VIOLATION OF THEIR RIGHTS FOLLOWING A PIPELINE EXPLOSION WHICH RESULTED IN LOSS OF LIVES, PHYSICAL AND PERMANENT INJURIES, DESTRUCTION OF PROPERTIES AND ENVIRONMENTAL DEGRADATION. ON BEHALF OF THE PEOPLE OF a village named in the case title. This file has recorded the complaint procedures at length; this is the organisation that actually carries a village into them, with the community named in the case title rather than represented in the abstract. THE DEFENCE THE STATE RAN, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND AND THE THING TO ANTICIPATE: THE STATE ARGUED THE COMPLAINT DID NOT FULFILL THE EXHAUSTION OF LOCAL REMEDIES REQUIREMENT, THAT THE INCIDENT IS EFFECTIVELY COVERED BY LOCAL LEGISLATION PROVIDING FOR LOCAL REMEDIES, AND THAT THE COMPLAINANT DID NOT ATTEMPT ANY FORM OF UTILIZATION OF SUCH LOCAL REMEDIES — CITING THE DOMESTIC LAW OF TORT AND SECTION 11(5) OF THE OIL PIPELINES ACT LFN 2004. Every community going to a regional body will meet this argument, and here it is in the state's own words with the statutes it cited. Prepare the answer before filing: what was tried domestically, when, and what happened. This file's Eritrea entry records the escape clause that exists for exactly this. THE CONSTITUTIONAL PROVISIONS THE STATE ITSELF POINTED TO: THAT UNDER FIVE NAMED SECTIONS VICTIMS HAVE THE UNFETTERED RIGHT OF ACTION, AND THAT ONE EXPRESSLY MANDATES THE STATE TO PROVIDE FOR IT. The government, defending itself, listed the constitutional routes its own citizens can use. That admission is quotable straight back in a domestic case — a state that says the remedies exist cannot easily say they do not apply to you. THE REGIONAL COURT CASE AND WHO IT NAMED: A COMPLAINT IN THE REGIONAL COMMUNITY COURT OF JUSTICE AGAINST THE GOVERNMENT — AND AGAINST MULTINATIONAL CORPORATIONS OPERATING IN THE NIGER DELTA, WITH EXXONMOBIL CORPORATION AS THE NINTH DEFENDANT. NINE DEFENDANTS, the state and the companies together in one action. Suing the government and its investors in the same proceeding removes the usual answer that the harm was somebody else's doing. THE TREATIES IT PLEADED: THAT THE GOVERNMENT IS A STATE PARTY TO THE COVENANT ON ECONOMIC, SOCIAL AND CULTURAL RIGHTS, THE COVENANT ON CIVIL AND POLITICAL RIGHTS, AND THE AFRICAN CHARTER — AND THAT THE DEFENDANTS HAVE FAILED INDIVIDUALLY AND/OR COLLECTIVELY TO REMEDY THE SITUATION. WHAT IT IS, IN THE COURT PAPERS' OWN WORDS: A HUMAN RIGHTS NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATION REGISTERED UNDER NATIONAL LAWS, WHOSE MANDATES INCLUDE THE PROMOTION OF RESPECT FOR SOCIO-ECONOMIC RIGHTS THROUGH LITIGATION, RESEARCH AND PUBLICATIONS, ADVOCACY AND MONITORING. LITIGATION named first in its own objects. When choosing between organisations that offer help, the founding documents show which ones actually go to court. THE STANDING FIGHT IT WON, WHICH RECURS IN EVERY SUCH CASE: THE GOVERNMENT FILED TWO PRELIMINARY OBJECTIONS CONTENDING THAT THE ORGANISATION LACKED STANDING TO SUE AND THAT THE LAWSUIT WAS STATUTORILY BARRED, AND THAT THE FREEDOM OF INFORMATION LAW DOES NOT APPLY RETROACTIVELY. LACKED STANDING is the first objection filed against almost every public-interest case in this file. An organisation that has already survived it in the national high court is worth more to a community than one that has not, and is a fair question to ask any prospective counsel. THE ORDER IT OBTAINED AND AGAINST WHOM: IT SUCCESSFULLY OBTAINED THE COURT'S PERMISSION TO SUE FOR THE RELEASE OF DOCUMENTS ON THE SPENDING OF RECOVERED PUBLIC STOLEN FUNDS — THE ORDER FOR LEAVE FOR AN ORDER OF MANDAMUS GRANTED AGAINST THE ACCOUNTANT-GENERAL AND THE ATTORNEY-GENERAL, BOTH NAMED. MANDAMUS is the order that compels an official to do their duty, and it was granted against the two most senior legal and financial officers of the federation. Where a ministry will not answer a records request about a project, this is the instrument — and there is now an organisation with a record of obtaining it. THE ARGUMENT IT MADE FOR DISCLOSURE: THAT DISCLOSURE WILL GIVE THE GENERAL PUBLIC A TRUE PICTURE AND A CLEAR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW THE SPENDING HAS IMPACTED ON THE LIVES OF THE POOR AND INDIGENT AND OTHER DISADVANTAGED CITIZENS. The public-interest framing that satisfied the court, worth copying into a records request: not curiosity, but the effect on named disadvantaged people. THE RECORDS WORK BEHIND THE LITIGATION: IT SUPPORTS FREEDOM OF INFORMATION REQUESTS ON ASSET RECOVERY, PUBLIC PROCUREMENT AND CONSTITUENCY PROJECTS, AND ANALYSES THE AUDITOR GENERAL'S REPORTS ON FEDERAL APPROPRIATIONS — THEN LITIGATES ON THE INFORMATION GATHERED, AND TRANSLATES REPORTS INTO SHORT, ACCESSIBLE FORMATS. Records first, then the case built on them. The Auditor General's report is a published document in most countries and almost nobody reads it — it is where a project's money appears before the project does. WHAT IT SAYS ABOUT RESOURCES: DEDICATED TO PROMOTING TRANSPARENCY AND ACCOUNTABILITY IN THE USE OF THE COUNTRY'S NATURAL RESOURCES, BELIEVING ITS LARGE NATURAL RESOURCE BASE SHOULD BE USED TO MEET THE BASIC NEEDS OF ITS POPULATION. AND WHAT IT DOES BETWEEN CASES: ESTABLISHED IN 2004, PROMOTING RIGHTS AND ACCOUNTABILITY THROUGH TRAINING, ADVOCACY, RESEARCH AND STRATEGIC LITIGATION — PUBLICLY URGING NAMED PRESIDING OFFICERS OF BOTH LEGISLATIVE CHAMBERS ON SPECIFIC MATTERS, AND FILING SUIT AGAINST THE NATIONAL ELECTORAL COMMISSION, WITH ITS ACTIONS PUBLISHED ON ITS OWN SITE. The actions are posted publicly, which means a community can see what is currently being litigated and whether its own grievance already sits inside a live case. WHO IT SUITS: communities harmed by pipelines, spills or extractive projects who need someone to file for them domestically and regionally — and anyone who needs a ministry compelled to release project records. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY'S ORGANISATION, WITH A CORRUPTION-AND-TRANSPARENCY FRAME RATHER THAN LAND OR PLANNING; IT SELECTS STRATEGIC CASES RATHER THAN ACTING AS A GENERAL LEGAL AID SERVICE, AND SEVERAL OF THE PROCEEDINGS CITED ARE OLDER — CHECK ITS CURRENT DOCKET. For the continental commission's complaint procedure without a lawyer, Eritrea's entry; for the regional court that requires no exhaustion of domestic remedies, Egypt's entry.

trackers.name: Natural Justice: Lawyers for Communities and the Environment
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an African public-interest law organisation — lawyers and paralegals working with communities facing mining, oil and gas, logging and large infrastructure, combining legal empowerment, community protocols, policy work and litigation. Hubs in Cape Town, Nairobi and Dakar, staff in Madagascar, Botswana and Guinea, and country programmes in Burkina Faso, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Namibia, Nigeria, Senegal and South Africa. It also runs the Environmental Lawyers Collective for Africa and an EIA Process Tracker. WHO IT SUITS: an Indigenous or rural community whose land, water or customary rights are threatened by an extractive or infrastructure project. It takes selected cases and works project-to-project outside its programme countries, so expect an approach-and-assess conversation rather than open intake. IS THERE AN OFFICE NEAR YOU? STAFF, NOT A HUB — Botswana. The 3 hubs are Cape Town, Nairobi and Dakar; here there are additional staff, so expect a smaller presence and a longer route into casework. WHAT IT DOES: founded 2007 in Cape Town, it supports communities to know the law, use the law and shape the law — access to land and governance of natural resources, the struggle against harmful extractive and infrastructure developments, traditional knowledge and benefit sharing, community rights within conservation, and climate action. ITS SIGNATURE TOOL IS THE COMMUNITY PROTOCOL — a documented instrument letting a community set out its biological, cultural and spiritual resources, norms and values, and assert existing rights under customary, domestic and international law, aimed squarely at laws and projects developed by government and industry without consultation. Ask for it by name. Contact: 63 Hout Street, Cape Town 8001; +27 21 426 1633; info@naturaljustice.org.

trackers.name: African Environmental Defenders Fund (emergency grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the African Environmental Defenders Fund — an emergency grant fund run by Natural Justice with the International Land Coalition Africa, ICCA Consortium, PACJA, Oxfam Novib, FEMNET and others, giving up to US$5,000 to land and environmental defenders anywhere in Africa who are under threat because of their activism. It can cover the cost of legal representation where a defender is arrested, summoned or prosecuted, plus relocation and other short-term transitional costs. WHO IT SUITS: an individual frontline defender who is a citizen or legal resident of an African country, facing an imminent threat, and not already supported by another body — it is not project or core funding, and routine office and administrative costs are excluded. HOW IT DIFFERS: applications are rolling, by email or helpline, not to a grant round. Natural Justice's own site names Burkina Faso, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Namibia, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa and Botswana as its country programmes, which is where this entry is placed; the fund's stated eligibility is any African country, so apply from elsewhere on the continent too.

trackers.name: Southern Africa Litigation Centre (SALC)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional litigation centre supporting and co-counselling cases across Angola, Botswana, DR Congo, Eswatini, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe. Its socio-economic rights work challenges large-scale agricultural and extractive land use that dispossesses customary landholders without adequate consent, consultation or compensation, and covers mining, pollution and climate justice — live matters include a Zambian community's pollution claim against copper processors and San and Bayei claims to ancestral land in Botswana. WHO IT SUITS: in-country lawyers and community organisations who need a partner with regional capacity and resources; SALC generally works through local counsel and partners rather than taking clients directly. SALC RESOURCES A LAWYER — IT DOES NOT REPLACE ONE. It provides technical and monetary support to local and regional lawyers and organisations litigating human rights and rule of law cases, working primarily through strategic litigation and capacity-strengthening support to lawyers and grassroots organisations. So the ask is not ‘please take my case’ but ‘please back my lawyer’ — come with a local lawyer or local organisation. It also trains human rights lawyers and facilitates networks across the region, so it is a route to finding counsel too. THE SECOND FORUM MOST PEOPLE MISS: SALC supports litigation in South African courts that advances human rights in the southern African region — so where your own courts are slow, captured or hostile, there may be another venue, and SALC is the body that supports using it. NAME THE RIGHT CLUSTER WHEN YOU APPROACH: its themes are criminal justice, civil and political rights, socio-economic rights, international criminal justice, business and human rights and equality rights — ‘environment’ is not one of them, so frame a land-defence case as business and human rights or socio-economic rights. Established 2005 in Johannesburg out of the International Bar Association and OSISA. It has also run open calls for small organisational development grants to emerging CBOs in Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe — periodic, so watch for them.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a pan-African feminist rapid-response fund with reach across all 54 African countries — small grants released quickly for unanticipated, time-critical situations rather than planned programme work, covering safety and protection needs when defenders are threatened and short windows for advocacy after an unexpected event. WHO IT SUITS: women's rights organisations, feminist collectives and movements in which women or gender-diverse people are the primary decision-makers. It does NOT fund individuals, and the action must be strategic, genuinely unanticipated, and completable in under three months. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is emergency money for a moment, not a budget for a campaign — decisions are fast and grants are modest.

trackers.name: Companies and Intellectual Property Authority
trackers.desc: CIPA is Botswana's registrar of companies and a parastatal of Botswana Government.

trackers.name: Online Business Registration System (OBRS)
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Botswana — Ministry of Finance
trackers.desc: National budget authority; formulates financial & economic policy, administers the treasury, and publishes the national budget & budget speeches, Botswana. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Botswana.

trackers.name: Office of the Auditor General
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Botswana, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: SAFLII – Botswana
trackers.desc: Free judgments of the High Court of Botswana (1999– ), the Court of Appeal (1981– ) and the Industrial Court, via the Southern African Legal Information Institute. · Find here: free Botswana and Southern-African case-law and legislation (SAFLII).

trackers.name: Botswana CBNRM — a policy directive, not a legal right
trackers.desc: KNOW WHAT YOUR RIGHT RESTS ON BEFORE YOU RELY ON IT. Comparative legal analysis sets Botswana against its neighbours: in Namibia law grants communities the right to set up conservancies and retain all income from game; in Mozambique the Forest and Wildlife Law 1999 gives communities rights to obtain logging licences and concessions, to participate in granting licences to logging companies and to receive a share of public revenues. Those are rights granted through legislation — and, in the analysis's words, this contrasts with Botswana's CBNRM framework, where access to resources by local communities is only through policy directives. A policy directive can be revised by the department that issued it; a statutory right cannot. Treat CBNRM here as an administrative permission rather than a legal entitlement, and document everything, because there is no statutory floor beneath it. THE VEHICLE is a registered community trust with a board of trustees as supreme governing body — 105 registered trusts operate as viable entities generating and distributing revenue, and at its recorded peak CBNRM covered 150 villages in ten districts and more than 135,000 people, about 10 percent of the population.

trackers.name: Two documented failure modes — agree the trust's purpose in writing
trackers.desc: RECORDED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED OVER, because both are avoidable if anticipated. 1. ELITE CAPTURE: an evaluation of Botswana's CBNRM framework found governance gaps, elite capture and limited capacity undermining equitable benefit sharing — so the trust's constitution and benefit-distribution rules are where the real fight is, not the wildlife quota. 2. MISMATCHED EXPECTATIONS: a study of communities next to Chobe National Park found general incongruence between community perceptions and expectations of the purpose and roles of Community Trusts and those of the wildlife authorities — after 2 decades, significant confusion translating into unfulfilled expectations and frustration. AGREE IN WRITING, WITH THE AUTHORITY, WHAT THE TRUST IS FOR AT THE OUTSET, including what revenue is expected and who decides its use. A CBNRM policy drafted for the Department of Wildlife and National Parks was intended to set specific objectives and implementation guidelines and to include a section on relations between protected areas and neighbouring communities — check whether it is in force, since that is the document that would govern a buffer-zone dispute.

trackers.name: Land Tribunal — it hears planning appeals as well as land board appeals, and a public body that ignores its ruling commits an offence
trackers.desc: MOST PEOPLE KNOW THIS AS THE PLACE YOU CHALLENGE A LAND BOARD. THE HALF THAT GETS MISSED IS THAT IT ALSO HEARS APPEALS FROM PLANNING AUTHORITIES — it is constituted under both the tribal land legislation and the town and country planning legislation, which makes it the forum for a planning permission you want to stop, not only for a plot allocation you want back. It is a court of law and equity, its judgments go on appeal to the High Court, and it sits in four divisions — Gaborone, Francistown, Palapye and Maun — with circuit sittings arranged for outlying areas. THE CLOCK: thirty days from the date you became aware of the land board's decision — awareness, not service, which cuts both ways and is worth pinning down in writing early. WHAT TO WALK IN WITH, because an incomplete filing is the common failure: the land board or planning authority resolution you are challenging; a notice and grounds of appeal lodged with the Clerk of Court giving full names, addresses and contacts of every party, the grounds, and the relief you want; a list of any witnesses; certified copies of your identity document or passport and of the certificate of customary land grant, lease or title deed; and a sketch plan showing the area in dispute. You then file an affidavit of service, and the respondent has one month from service to file a notice of intention to defend with its reasons. THE PROVISION NOBODY QUOTES: under the tribunal's own Act, a public body or party that without reasonable excuse fails to comply with or enforce a determination commits an offence, punishable by a fine of up to P10,000 or two years' imprisonment, and up to P20,000 for a body corporate — so a land board that simply ignores a ruling is not merely in breach, it is liable. CAVEAT: the thirty-day limit and the offence provision were read from the tribal land legislation and the tribunal's Act rather than from this services page, which sets out the filing steps but no deadline.

trackers.name: Land board allocation — demarcate within three months or the board can take the plot back through the tribunal, with no compensation
trackers.desc: THE GRANT IS STRONG AND THE FORFEITURE IS FAST, WHICH IS AN UNUSUAL COMBINATION AND THE REASON THIS ENTRY EXISTS. Tribal land is allocated by twelve main land boards and forty-one subordinate land boards; any citizen aged eighteen or over may apply for unallocated tribal land in any tribal territory, not only their own, on the ministry's customary land rights application form, submitted during the window stated in the allocation announcement — miss the announcement and you wait for the next one. A successful applicant receives a deed of customary land grant, and those rights are held in perpetuity and pass from one generation to the next. Allocation is to be completed within three months of the land becoming available. THEN THE TRAP: an allocated plot must be demarcated promptly, and a land board has publicly warned that failure to demarcate within three months of allocation can lead to cancellation — the board applies to the Land Tribunal to recover the land, and where it succeeds there is no compensation. Holders already occupying land under an older certificate were separately required to apply for a deed within six months of the 2018 Act commencing. ONE ACCESSIBILITY POINT WORTH KNOWING: an appeal from a subordinate land board to the main tribal land board may be lodged verbally or in writing with the clerk, and the clerk must then supply the board with the reasons for the decision and serve a copy of those reasons on you — ask for the written reasons, because they are what an appeal to the Land Tribunal is built on. Ministry of Land Management, Water and Sanitation Services toll free 0800 600 737; offices open 07:30 to 12:45 and 13:45 to 16:30 on weekdays. CAVEATS: the demarcation warning comes from the government news service reporting a land board briefing, not from a regulation quoted here, and the verbal-appeal provision from the subsidiary legislation rather than this page — confirm both at your land board, and treat three months as the working assumption rather than a certainty.

trackers.name: DITSHWANELO — Botswana's human rights centre, gives free advice on civil matters, and sat on the negotiating team the Kalahari communities mandated
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: DITSHWANELO — Setswana for “rights” — the Botswana Centre for Human Rights, founded in 1993 by Alice Mogwe, and the first non-state body in this country's entry list: everything else here is a tribunal, a land board or a registry. It offers free advice on civil judicial matters, supports San communities, and states that it deliberately takes the issues least supported by others. THE PRECEDENT THAT MATTERS FOR ANY COMMUNITY FACING RELOCATION: when the government moved to relocate residents of the Central Kalahari Game Reserve, the First People of the Kalahari mandated a negotiating team — community representatives, FPK, a regional indigenous peoples' network, DITSHWANELO and the church council — to deal with government on their behalf, from 1996. That is the same instrument Ghana's mining communities used: a written community mandate naming who speaks for you. AND THE LESSON IS WHAT HAPPENED NEXT: the negotiations collapsed when government refused to move, and the residents then went to court — 244 former CKGR residents mounted a legal challenge in 2002, and in 2006 the High Court at Lobatse ruled the eviction from their ancestral land unlawful, and the refusal of permits to return unconstitutional. Negotiation and litigation are sequential, not alternative; the negotiating record is what makes the later case. DITSHWANELO is the secretariat of the CKGR NGO Coalition and of the UPR NGO working group, so it is also the route into Botswana's reporting to international human rights bodies — useful when domestic remedies stall. Private Bag 00416, Gaborone. WHO IT SUITS: Botswana communities facing relocation, loss of land access or discrimination in access to justice; San communities in particular. CAVEATS: a human rights advocacy organisation offering free civil advice, not a dedicated environmental or land law firm; its published priorities are broad; and the CKGR litigation itself was carried by outside counsel and an international campaigning organisation, not by DITSHWANELO. FIRST PEOPLE OF THE KALAHARI, the community's own body that mandated the negotiating team, was founded in 1991, registered in 1992, officially recognised in 1993, received an international award in 2005 — and had dissolved as an organisation by 2013, so it is not a door that can be knocked on today. WHAT IT ACTUALLY PROVIDES, LISTED: free PARALEGAL COUNSELLING; a Domestic Workers Association giving legal and mediation assistance in labour matters; awareness-raising through workshops, school lectures and an annual human rights film festival in Gaborone; and accountability work that includes monitoring state actions and submitting SHADOW REPORTS to the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights and to UN Special Procedures and the Universal Periodic Review. A shadow report is a route a community can feed into without a lawyer or a filing fee — ask DITSHWANELO when the next Botswana review cycle is and what evidence it needs. It states that it deliberately focuses on issues least supported by others, including ex-Botswana miners who worked in apartheid-era gold mines and domestic workers, and it works in partnership with Botswanan organisations on gender equality, freedom of expression and information, children and youth, and indigenous peoples. It is the secretariat of the Central Kalahari Game Reserve NGO Coalition, the UPR NGO Working Group, and a southern African civil society solidarity coalition covering Zimbabwe, Eswatini, human rights defenders and migration. For regional strategic litigation, the Southern Africa Litigation Centre is already recorded in this file.

trackers.name: Botswana's community trusts — Khwai, Sankuyo, Habu, Kuru and Khama Rhino, the registered bodies through which a village holds a concession, plus Kalahari Wildlands Trust
trackers.desc: THE TRUSTS THAT HOLD THE CONCESSION — in Botswana a community does not act as a village, it acts as a REGISTERED TRUST, and these are the named ones: KHWAI DEVELOPMENT TRUST, FOUNDED APRIL 2000, a community-based natural resource management organisation representing the interests of the community of KHWAI VILLAGE, LOCATED IN A WILDLIFE CONCESSION BORDERING MOREMI GAME RESERVE AND CHOBE NATIONAL PARK, through which the community plays an active role in the use of natural resources WHILE ENSURING TOURISM BENEFITS ARE DISTRIBUTED TO ALL HOUSEHOLDS AND RESIDENTS; SANKUYO TSHWARAGANO MANAGEMENT TRUST in north-western Ngamiland; HABU COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT TRUST in western Ngamiland, working with the Habu, Tubu and Nokaneng communities alongside the NGO WILD ENTRUST AFRICA; KURU DEVELOPMENT TRUST in Ghanzi; and KHAMA RHINO SANCTUARY TRUST, FOUNDED 1992. Register the trust first. It is the legal person that signs the concession, receives the tourism revenue and distributes it — and the distribution rule belongs in the trust deed, because Khwai's stated commitment is to ALL households and residents, not to a committee. THE LESSON FROM KHWAI'S OWN DELAY, RECORDED HONESTLY: Khwai was among the FIRST villages encouraged to join the programme and among the LAST in Ngamiland to implement it — because residents were unsure whether they would remain permanently in the village, and because the dominant San community wanted a model giving them FULL CONTROL of land and resources, and a concession for San people alone, which government would not accept as it would exclude other ethnic groups. THE TRUST'S REGISTRATION WAS DELAYED BY THAT DISAGREEMENT. Settle who is inside the trust before you file it. An unresolved question about which people the trust represents will hold up registration for years, and years is exactly how long a concession stays available. AND THE FAILURE MODE, STATED PLAINLY: the 2014 TROPHY-HUNTING BAN cost these communities INCOME AND EMPLOYMENT, because their revenue rested on a single licence class. Build a trust with more than one income line. A NATIONAL BODY WORKING OUTSIDE THE PARKS: KALAHARI WILDLANDS TRUST, formed 2016 and based in MAUN, exists to CONSERVE AND REHABILITATE HABITAT FOR FREE-RANGING WILDLIFE ESPECIALLY IN AREAS OUTSIDE BOTSWANA'S PROTECTED AREA NETWORK, and to support the most needy rural communities in those areas, with experience in land use planning and community based resource management; its founders' earlier work contributed to government decisions REMOVING 258 KILOMETRES OF VETERINARY FENCING across wildlife migration routes in northern Botswana between 1998 and 2008. An organisation that has had 258 km of fencing taken out is one that has moved this government before. WHO IT SUITS: Botswana villages in or near a wildlife management area, and communities outside the protected-area network. CAVEATS: TRUSTS DEPEND ON CONCESSION AND LICENCE POLICY, which has changed abruptly. For free advice from the human rights centre, Botswana's DITSHWANELO entry; for planning appeals as well as land board appeals, the Land Tribunal entry; for the three-month demarcation rule, the land board entry.

trackers.name: BOCONGO and Somarelang Tikologo — Botswana's 300-member NGO umbrella with a code of conduct, the Registrar of Societies door, and a member-based environmental NGO founded by three university lecturers
trackers.desc: THE REGISTRATION DOOR AND THE 300-MEMBER UMBRELLA — the two things a Botswana community group needs before anything else: THE BOTSWANA COUNCIL OF NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS (BOCONGO) WAS ESTABLISHED IN 1995 AS THE NATIONAL COORDINATING BODY, AND HAS A MEMBERSHIP BASE OF OVER 300 NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS ACROSS THE COUNTRY, MAKING IT THE LARGEST AND MOST REPRESENTATIVE CIVIL SOCIETY COORDINATION PLATFORM IN BOTSWANA, operating as a MEMBERSHIP-DRIVEN APEX BODY that coordinates NGOs, FACILITATES DIALOGUE WITH GOVERNMENT, strengthens capacity and increases MEMBERS' CAPACITY TO BE EFFECTIVE ADVOCATES FOR POLICY DEVELOPMENT BOTH INDIVIDUALLY AND AS A SECTOR. AND IT HAS SET OUT AN NGO CODE OF CONDUCT to ensure transparency and accountability among Botswana-based NGOs. A published code of conduct is a standard you can hold an organisation to. Before you let a body speak for your village, ask whether it is a BOCONGO member and whether it signs the code — and if it will not, ask why. THE DOOR ITSELF, STATED PLAINLY: NGOs WANTING TO BECOME RECOGNISED BY THE GOVERNMENT CAN REGISTER WITH THE REGISTRAR OF SOCIETIES IN GABORONE — and the government, through the NATIONAL NGO POLICY (2012), RECOGNISES THE IMPORTANT ROLE PLAYED BY CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, PROVIDING FOR A COORDINATED APPROACH AND ENHANCING COMMUNICATION AND PARTNERSHIPS BETWEEN GOVERNMENT, STAKEHOLDERS AND CSOs. Registrar of Societies, Gaborone: that is where a Botswana community group becomes a legal person. A national policy that names CSOs as partners is the document to cite when a district office treats your association as an intruder. THE MEMBER-BASED ENVIRONMENTAL NGO: SOMARELANG TIKOLOGO — ENVIRONMENT WATCH BOTSWANA — WAS FOUNDED IN 1991 BY THREE LECTURERS AT THE UNIVERSITY OF BOTSWANA, at PRIVATE BAG 00376, GABORONE, tel +267 391 3709 (somatiko.org.bw), aiming to promote SUSTAINABLE ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION BY EDUCATING, DEMONSTRATING AND ENCOURAGING BEST PRACTICES IN ENVIRONMENTAL PLANNING, RESOURCE CONSERVATION AND WASTE MANAGEMENT, and operating THROUGH FOUR SUBCOMMITTEES: ENVIRONMENTAL PLANNING, RESOURCE CONSERVATION, WASTE MANAGEMENT, AND PR AND FUND-RAISING. Fundraising as a standing subcommittee rather than an afterthought is why a volunteer organisation survives thirty years. Copy the structure: put the money committee alongside the work committees, not below them. IT HAS NEARLY 100 MEMBERS AND DONORS, INCLUDING GOVERNMENT AGENCIES, BANKS, PRIVATE COMPANIES AND MULTINATIONALS, and it holds A COLLECTION OF HAND-MADE GREEN CRAFTS FROM LOCAL PRODUCERS. Banks and multinationals inside the membership cuts both ways: it is access to the people who finance projects, and it is a constraint on what the organisation will say. Ask which of its members has an interest in the scheme you are fighting before you rely on it. ALSO NAMED, WITH POSTAL ADDRESSES: KALAHARI CONSERVATION SOCIETY (PO Box 859, GABORONE, kcs.org.bw); KHWAI DEVELOPMENT TRUST (PO Box 657, MAUN); KURU FAMILY OF ORGANISATIONS (PO Box 219, GHANZI); KWENENG RURAL DEVELOPMENT ASSOCIATION (Private Bag 7, MOLEPOLOLE); and THE BOTSWANA SOCIETY (PO Box 1950, Gaborone, botsoc.org.bw). An Okavango programme has also been described as combining environmental education, policy dialogue, enterprise development, ecotourism and research, OPERATING WITH LOCAL GOVERNANCE SUPPORTED BY A NATIONAL ADVISORY COUNCIL CHAIRED BY A CABINET-LEVEL MINISTER. Local governance with a national council chaired by a minister is the pairing worth demanding: the village runs it, and a cabinet minister has to attend the meeting where it is reviewed. WHO IT SUITS: Botswana community groups registering, seeking an umbrella, or looking for the organisation nearest them. CAVEATS: AN APEX BODY AND A MEMBERSHIP NGO with corporate members — neither is a litigator. For the community trusts that hold concessions and the 258 km of fencing removed, Botswana's community trusts entry.

trackers.name: Community Leaders Network of Southern Africa — a network whose members are rural community leaders themselves, with named officers and a fundraising coordinator, plus Botswana's Ngamiland district NGO council (regional body, filed here because the file has no regional key)
trackers.desc: THE MEMBERS ARE THE LEADERS, NOT THE NGOs — and a placement note first: THIS IS A REGIONAL BODY SPANNING A DOZEN COUNTRIES, FILED UNDER BOTSWANA ONLY BECAUSE THE FILE HAS NO REGIONAL KEY AND THE NAMED DISTRICT NGO COUNCIL BELOW IS BOTSWANAN. If you are in Angola, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe or Madagascar, it applies to you. THE COMMUNITY LEADERS NETWORK OF SOUTHERN AFRICA (CLN) IS A COLLABORATIVE GROUPING OF RURAL REPRESENTATIVES FROM ANGOLA, BOTSWANA, MALAWI, MOZAMBIQUE, NAMIBIA, SOUTH AFRICA, TANZANIA, ZAMBIA AND ZIMBABWE — established bringing together OVER 50 REPRESENTATIVES OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES ENGAGED IN COMMUNITY BASED NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, and later described as REPRESENTING OVER 20 MILLION INDIVIDUALS ACROSS TWELVE SOUTHERN AFRICAN NATIONS. Representatives of communities, not of organisations. Almost every network in this file is a network of NGOs; this one seats the people who actually hold the resource. If your community runs a conservancy, a community forest or a trust, its leader is the category of person CLN is made of — ask what membership requires, because you may already qualify without an NGO in between. WHERE IT CAME FROM, AND WHY THAT MATTERS: CLN WAS BORN AFTER THE INAUGURAL AFRICAN WILDLIFE SUMMIT HELD AT VICTORIA FALLS, ZIMBABWE IN 2019, AT WHICH COMMUNITY LEADERS NOTED THE NEED TO HAVE ONE VOICE WHEN DEALING WITH COMMUNITY RIGHTS ON NATURAL RESOURCES IN SOUTHERN AFRICA — AND IT WAS FORMALISED AT A FIVE-DAY WORKSHOP IN WINDHOEK FROM 18 TO 22 OCTOBER, bringing together CBNRM representatives from Zambia, Namibia, Malawi, Zimbabwe, Tanzania, Botswana and Mozambique alongside support and technical staff. A summit, then two years, then a five-day formalisation workshop. That is the same sequence this file recorded in Bangui — convene, agree the need, then meet for long enough to write the constitution. Five days is the number: a network is not formalised in an afternoon. ITS MISSION AND VISION ARE THE WORDING TO BORROW: TO STRENGTHEN NATIONAL COMMUNITY-BASED NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT PROGRAMMES SUCH THAT SOUTHERN AFRICAN LOCAL COMMUNITIES INFLUENCE POLICIES AND DECISIONS THAT AFFECT THEIR LIVELIHOODS AT ALL LEVELS OF GOVERNANCE; AND RESILIENT LOCAL COMMUNITIES WHOSE RIGHTS TO MANAGE NATURAL RESOURCES ON THEIR LAND ARE RESPECTED NATIONALLY AND INTERNATIONALLY. At all levels of governance, and respected NATIONALLY AND INTERNATIONALLY. That second phrase is the whole point of a regional network: a decision taken in a foreign parliament about your wildlife or your timber is a decision you have no vote on, and a regional body is the only structure that can answer it in the room where it is taken. WHO TO WRITE TO: CLN HAS A NAMED CHAIRMAN, A NAMED EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR APPOINTED IN JANUARY 2026, AND A NAMED COORDINATOR WHO IS THE KEY GO-TO PERSON RESPONSIBLE FOR COORDINATING ACTIVITIES OF THE MEMBER COUNTRIES INCLUDING MAINTAINING LIAISON, AND MANAGING ADVOCACY CAMPAIGNS AND FUNDRAISING EFFORTS — with a country focal person in Botswana whose stated interests are INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, HUMAN RIGHTS, LAND RIGHTS, CLIMATE CHANGE, ENVIRONMENTAL CONSERVATION AND BIODIVERSITY. A coordinator whose job description includes FUNDRAISING is the person to ask about money, and a country focal person whose listed interests include LAND RIGHTS is the one to ask about a taking. Ask for the focal person for your country by name. THE DISTRICT-LEVEL BODY, WHICH IS THE UNIT MOST COMMUNITIES ACTUALLY NEED: THE NGAMILAND COUNCIL OF NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS (NCONGO) CONVENES IN COLLABORATION WITH CLN AND A GOVERNMENT MINISTRY. A DISTRICT council of NGOs, convening alongside a regional network and a ministry in the same room. That is the full ladder in one sentence — district, region, state — and it is the ladder to ask about wherever you are: is there a district NGO council, and does it meet with the ministry? THE SUPPORT ORGANISATION BEHIND IT: an organisation with over twenty years in East and Southern Africa states that it WORKS CLOSELY WITH NATIONAL NETWORKS OF COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS THAT PRACTISE CBNRM AND THEIR REGIONAL FORUM, THE CLN, and that its strategies were TO ENSURE THE PERSPECTIVES OF MARGINALISED RURAL COMMUNITIES WERE HEARD AND INFLUENCED POLICY PROCESSES. CAVEATS: CLN CAMPAIGNS ACTIVELY AGAINST TROPHY HUNTING IMPORT BANS, and communities differ sharply on hunting — this file records that plainly rather than hiding it, and you should know the network's position before you join it. For the community trusts that hold concessions, Botswana's community trusts entry; for the 300-member national umbrella with an NGO code of conduct and the Registrar of Societies, BOCONGO and Somarelang Tikologo.

trackers.name: Volunteer lawyers who train prosecutors and judges on wildlife and trafficking crime, observe trials neutrally, draft legislation — and run multi-year programmes strengthening the technical legal skills of named local civil society organisations
trackers.desc: THEY TRAIN THE PROSECUTORS, AND THEY TRAIN YOUR LAWYERS TOO — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ETHIOPIA ENTRY COVERS THE SENIOR LAWYERS PROJECT NAMED ALONGSIDE THIS ORGANISATION IN PRO BONO DIRECTORIES, ITS ERITREA ENTRY A BROKER WITH A FINITE-PROJECT TEST, ITS SÃO TOMÉ ENTRY THE CLEARINGHOUSE CIRCULATING MATTERS TO 800 LAWYERS, AND ITS ESWATINI ENTRY THE LEGAL MARKETPLACE WHOSE PARENT FOUNDATION HAS SUPPORTED THIS ORGANISATION FOR DECADES. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE COMMUNITY WORK IT NAMES, WHICH IS THE FIND: COMMUNITY WORK IS FOCUSED UPON ACCESS TO JUSTICE ISSUES AND HAS INCLUDED THEMES OF CIVIC PARTICIPATION AND ENGAGEMENT, RIGHTS-BASED EDUCATION IN PARTNERSHIP WITH LOCAL (IN-COUNTRY) NGOs, AND RIGHTS-BASED EDUCATION EMBEDDED IN SUPPORTED AND MANAGED MICRO-ENTERPRISE. RIGHTS EDUCATION EMBEDDED IN MICRO-ENTERPRISE is the unusual one: the legal training arrives inside a savings or income programme people were joining anyway, rather than as a workshop they must be persuaded to attend. This file has recorded rights training failing on attendance more than on content; that design solves it. WHO IT WORKS TO REACH: WE WORK TO MAKE JUSTICE ACCESSIBLE FOR INDIVIDUALS AND COMMUNITIES, PARTICULARLY THOSE WHO TRADITIONALLY MAY NOT ENGAGE THE FORMAL JUSTICE SYSTEM — AND WE RAISE INDIVIDUALS' AWARENESS OF THEIR RIGHTS UNDER THEIR LEGAL SYSTEMS, ENABLING THEM TO SEEK JUSTICE AND ADVOCATE FOR CHANGE. THE AFRICAN WILDLIFE-CRIME PROGRAMME ON RECORD: IN TANZANIA, PRO BONO ATTORNEYS HELPED DESIGN AND DELIVER TRIAL ADVOCACY TRAINING FOR PROSECUTORS HANDLING HUMAN TRAFFICKING AND WILDLIFE CRIME CASES. Prosecutors trained to run environmental cases properly. This file has recorded again and again that a case collapses not because the law is absent but because nobody in the courtroom knows how to prove it — and where a state prosecutor could act on illegal logging, poaching or pollution, this is who upgrades them. THE OTHER AFRICAN PROGRAMMES NAMED: IN KENYA, LEGAL TEAMS SUPPORTED THE CREATION OF A NATIONAL PROSECUTION TRAINING INSTITUTE, DEVELOPED CASE MANAGEMENT TOOLS, AND PROVIDED HANDS-ON COURTROOM TRAINING FOR PROSECUTORS AND JUDGES; AND IN LIBERIA, LAW FIRM PARTNERS CONTRIBUTED LEGAL RESEARCH AND LEGISLATIVE DRAFTING FOR REFORMS. LEGISLATIVE DRAFTING, contributed free. When a community coalition has agreed what a forest or land act should say, somebody has to render it in statutory language — and that is the step most campaigns cannot buy. THE THREE-YEAR CIVIL SOCIETY PROGRAMME, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: FUNDED BY A NAMED LAW FIRM FOUNDATION, A THREE-YEAR PROGRAM SUPPORTS TWO ZAMBIAN CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS IN STRENGTHENING THEIR CAPACITY — ENHANCING THE TECHNICAL LEGAL SKILLS OF PARTNER NGOs TO ADVOCATE FOR RIGHTS AND ACCESS TO JUSTICE, THROUGH CAPACITY BUILDING AND INSTITUTIONAL ENGAGEMENT. Two named national organisations, three years, funded by a law firm's own foundation. The model is worth knowing about even where the subject differs: a large firm can fund a multi-year legal-skills programme for African NGOs, and this is the shape such a programme takes. An organisation wanting one should be asking a firm's foundation, not only its pro bono desk. THE PROGRAMME AREAS BEYOND TRAINING: NEUTRAL TRIAL OBSERVATION; ASSESSMENT AND EVALUATION; TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE COVERING ROADMAPS, MANUALS, LEGAL ANALYSIS, RESEARCH AND LEGISLATIVE DRAFTING; AND COMMUNITY OUTREACH. NEUTRAL TRIAL OBSERVATION is the one to request when defenders are prosecuted. An independent observer in the courtroom, whose neutrality is the organisation's stated mandate, changes how a hearing is conducted — and produces a record that survives the verdict. This file has documented land defenders tried on fabricated charges with nobody watching. THE TRAINING FORMAT: A WEEK-LONG INTENSE TRAINING USING MOCK SCENARIOS, IN CONTEXTS INCLUDING CRIMINAL LAW GENERALLY, TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS, INHERITANCE AND SUCCESSION, AND GENDER-BASED AND DOMESTIC VIOLENCE. INHERITANCE AND SUCCESSION is a land subject in everything but name. Widows and daughters losing land at a death is the single most common dispossession this file records, and it is a listed training context. WHO IT PARTNERS WITH INSTITUTIONALLY: COURTS, GOVERNMENT AGENCIES, AND LEGAL BODIES, TO DEVELOP FAIR, EFFECTIVE, AND INDEPENDENT GOVERNMENT INSTITUTIONS — IMPLEMENTING PROGRAMS TO COMBAT CORRUPTION, STRENGTHEN DUE PROCESS, AND ENSURE LEGAL PROTECTIONS ARE UPHELD. THE STATED METHOD AND MANDATE: WE CONNECT VOLUNTEER LEGAL EXPERTS WITH LOCAL PARTNERS TO DELIVER PRACTICAL, SUSTAINABLE SOLUTIONS, WORKING ALONGSIDE LOCAL PARTNERS TO ENSURE CONTEXTUAL AND SUSTAINABLE SUPPORT — WITH A MANDATE OF NEUTRALITY AND INDEPENDENCE. NEUTRALITY is both the strength and the limit. It is what lets them into a ministry and a courtroom; it also means they will not be your advocate against the state. Use them for the training, the observation and the drafting — and the entries under Chad and Seychelles for the confrontation. THE VOLUNTEER BASE AND ITS GEOGRAPHY: LAWYERS VOLUNTEER INDIVIDUALLY OR THROUGH THEIR EMPLOYERS — USUALLY A LAW FIRM OR AN IN-HOUSE DEPARTMENT — WITH THE LARGEST NUMBERS COMING FROM THE UNITED STATES, CANADA, THE UNITED KINGDOM AND AUSTRALIA. Recorded plainly: the volunteers are overwhelmingly anglophone and northern, which shapes both the language of delivery and whose legal tradition the training reflects. Francophone and lusophone African organisations should ask about that before committing. THE SCALE: MORE THAN 5,000 WORKSHOPS AND PROGRAMS DELIVERED, AND OVER THE PAST DECADE MORE THAN 86,500 HOURS OF PRO BONO SERVICE VALUED AT MORE THAN $36.5 MILLION — WITH PROJECTS IN AFRICA, ASIA, THE CARIBBEAN AND CENTRAL AND SOUTH AMERICA, ACROSS 25 YEARS. AND HOW IT IS FUNDED, RECORDED BECAUSE IT SHAPES WHAT IT WILL DO: FUNDED THROUGH A VARIETY OF FEDERAL GRANTS AND DONATIONS, INTEGRATING PRO BONO RESOURCES AND VOLUNTEERS WITH THE SELF-FUNDED PARTICIPATION OF HIGHLY SKILLED LAWYERS IN NEARLY ALL OF ITS PROGRAMMING. Government grants fund much of it, which is another reason the mandate is neutrality. Ask early whether a proposed programme's funder has a view on the subject you need help with. WHO IT SUITS: African civil society organisations wanting technical legal skills, communities needing trial observation when defenders are prosecuted, and coalitions that need a law drafted. CAVEATS: NEUTRAL AND INSTITUTION-FACING RATHER THAN ADVERSARIAL, LARGELY ANGLOPHONE VOLUNTEERS, AND IT WORKS THROUGH PROGRAMMES RATHER THAN TAKING CASES — it will not litigate against a government for you. For senior lawyers on attorney-client terms, Ethiopia's entry; for cases built outside the jurisdiction, Chad's entry; for operational legal work by a clearinghouse, São Tomé's entry.

trackers.name: Avocats sans frontières Canada (ASFC) — a francophone legal cooperation organisation whose published focus opens with community and customary land rights — working only through local partners, on multi-year projects, and stating plainly that it does not litigate in its own name
trackers.desc: FRANCOPHONE LAWYERS WHOSE FIRST LISTED FOCUS IS CUSTOMARY LAND RIGHTS — adjacency and disambiguation declared first: TWO SEPARATE ORGANISATIONS SHARE THE LAWYERS-WITHOUT-BORDERS NAME. THIS ENTRY IS THE CANADIAN ONE, CREATED BY CANADIAN LAWYERS IN 2002 AND WORKING IN FRENCH. A BELGIAN ORGANISATION OF THE SAME NAME, CREATED IN 1992 AND BASED IN BRUSSELS, IS A DIFFERENT BODY; THIS FILE'S BOTSWANA BUCKET ALREADY CARRIES A THIRD, DIFFERENTLY-NAMED TRAINING ORGANISATION. DO NOT CONFUSE THEM WHEN WRITING. THIS FILE'S EGYPT BUCKET CARRIES AN ENVIRONMENTAL LAW ALLIANCE HOST, ITS ETHIOPIA BUCKET A SENIOR LAWYERS PROJECT HOST, ITS ERITREA BUCKET AN INTERNATIONAL DEVELOPMENT ADVOCATES HOST. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE FOCUS LIST, WHICH IS THE FIND: ITS PUBLISHED FOCUS COVERS COMMUNITY AND CUSTOMARY LAND RIGHTS, CRIMINAL JUSTICE, EDUCATION, GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE, GENERALIST LEGAL SERVICES, GOVERNANCE, ACCOUNTABILITY AND TRANSPARENCY, PEACE-BUILDING AND TRANSITIONAL JUSTICE, AND WOMEN'S RIGHTS. COMMUNITY AND CUSTOMARY LAND RIGHTS at the head of the list, from an organisation that works in French. Almost every legal resource in this file operates in English, which leaves francophone West and Central Africa — where most of the land conflicts recorded here sit — reading translations or nothing at all. Customary tenure is also precisely the category that national law treats as absence. THE LIMIT IT STATES ABOUT ITSELF, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: GENERALLY IT DOES NOT DEFEND HUMAN RIGHTS ITSELF IN THE COUNTRIES IN WHICH IT OPERATES — ITS MISSION IS MORE TO INCREASE THE CAPABILITIES OF ITS PARTNERS. Filed prominently because it prevents a wasted approach: a community writing here for representation will not get a lawyer in court. What it will get, through a local partner organisation, is that partner's capacity paid for. Identify the national organisation you would work with FIRST, then approach together. HOW EVERY PROJECT IS BUILT: ALL OF THE ORGANISATION'S PROJECTS ARE DEVELOPED AND IMPLEMENTED IN CLOSE COOPERATION WITH ONE OR MORE LOCAL PARTNERS — GROUPS OF HUMAN RIGHTS LAWYERS, CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS, GOVERNMENT AGENCIES. GROUPS OF HUMAN RIGHTS LAWYERS as a partner category. In a country where the bar association is weak or captured, an independent grouping of lawyers is the body this organisation would resource — which is an argument for forming one. THE PRINCIPLE THAT GOVERNS WHAT IT WILL DO: THIS APPROACH ALWAYS RESPECTS THE NEEDS EXPRESSED BY LOCAL STAKEHOLDERS. Written as a constraint on itself rather than an aspiration. Hold it to that: the project should be the one the community asked for, not the one that fits an existing programme. WHAT THE WORK CONSISTS OF: LEGAL AID, JUDICIAL ASSISTANCE, STRATEGIC LITIGATION OF EMBLEMATIC CASES OF HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS, ADVOCACY FOR CHANGE, TRAINING AND THE REINFORCEMENT OF LOCAL CAPACITIES — THROUGH OUTREACH LEGAL WORK, PARTICULARLY IN STRATEGIC LITIGATION, LEGAL AID SERVICES AND LEGAL ASSISTANCE. EMBLEMATIC CASES is the selection standard, the francophone equivalent of the impact-at-scale test recorded in this file's Mauritania and Seychelles entries. A case that would settle a question for many communities is the one to put forward. THE CONDITIONS IT WORKS IN: PROJECTS ARE OFTEN CARRIED OUT OVER A NUMBER OF YEARS IN COMPLEX ENVIRONMENTS — CONFLICT, POST-CONFLICT, POST NATURAL DISASTER. Conflict and post-conflict settings named as normal operating conditions. Communities in the Sahel and Central Africa, where this file has recorded land disputes tangled with armed conflict, are inside the remit rather than too difficult for it. WHOM IT EXISTS TO STRENGTHEN: CREATED BY LAWYERS IN 2002, IT AIMS AT EMPOWERING LOCAL ASSOCIATIONS AND ADVOCATES WITH THE GOAL OF ADVANCING JUSTICE AND HUMAN RIGHTS FOR ALL, ESPECIALLY PERSONS IN SITUATIONS OF VULNERABILITY. THE THREE THINGS IT SEEKS: CLOSE PARTNERSHIPS WITH LEGAL PROFESSIONALS AND CIVIL SOCIETY TO OBTAIN TANGIBLE BENEFITS FOR PEOPLE IN VULNERABLE SITUATIONS; CONCRETE AND SUSTAINABLE RESULTS WITHIN THE COMMUNITIES WHERE IT CARRIES OUT COLLABORATIVE PROJECTS; AND TO MAKE THE LAW AN INSTRUMENT FOR INCLUSION, CHANGE AND DEVELOPMENT. THE DEFENDER-PROTECTION STRAND: ITS STATED CONTRIBUTIONS INCLUDE STRENGTHENING THE SECURITY AND INDEPENDENCE OF LAWYERS WHO DEFEND HUMAN RIGHTS, THE HOLDING OF FAIR TRIALS, AND THE CONTINUING TRAINING OF JUSTICE ACTORS AND MEMBERS OF CIVIL SOCIETY — ALONGSIDE THE FIGHT AGAINST IMPUNITY. THE SECURITY OF THE LAWYERS THEMSELVES. This file has recorded communities losing their case when their advocate was threatened, struck off or arrested; an organisation whose programme includes protecting the lawyer is addressing the failure point rather than the symptom. THE LEGAL FIELDS IT NAMES: HUMAN RIGHTS, ACCESS TO JUSTICE, VOLUNTARY COOPERATION, STRATEGIC LITIGATION, TRANSITIONAL JUSTICE, LEGAL AID AND JUDICIAL ASSISTANCE, CIVIL AND POLITICAL RIGHTS, INTERNATIONAL LAW, ECONOMIC, SOCIAL AND CULTURAL RIGHTS, INTERNATIONAL JUSTICE, WOMEN'S RIGHTS, AND PEACE AND SECURITY. ECONOMIC, SOCIAL AND CULTURAL RIGHTS is the heading under which land, water and livelihood claims are argued in the francophone system — worth naming in that language when approaching. WHERE IT WORKS, INCLUDING IN AFRICA: ACTIVE IN MORE THAN 15 COUNTRIES SINCE 2002, WITH A COUNTRY LIST NAMING MALI ALONGSIDE SEVERAL LATIN AMERICAN AND CARIBBEAN STATES — AND A NAMED MALI PROJECT, FUNDED BY A CANADIAN GOVERNMENT DEPARTMENT, AIMED AT WOMEN, GIRLS AND OTHER PEOPLE IN SITUATIONS OF VULNERABILITY MAKING THEIR HUMAN RIGHTS A REALITY. Recorded honestly: its African footprint on the public record is Mali, with the weight of its work in Latin America and the Caribbean. A francophone West African organisation is nonetheless approaching a body that already runs a project in the region and in its language. AND THE PUBLISHED CONTACT AND PRO BONO ROUTE: A PUBLISHED GENERAL EMAIL ADDRESS, A PARTNERSHIP PAGE INVITING ORGANISATIONS TO BECOME PARTNERS, AND A NAMED PRO BONO STRAND ALONGSIDE ITS PARTNER PROGRAMME — WITH A PROGRAMMATIC AND LEGAL TEAM PLACED ON SITE IN THE COUNTRY OF OPERATION. A PRO BONO strand and an open become-a-partner page, with staff placed in-country rather than managing remotely. Write in French, name the partner you already work with, and describe the case as emblematic. WHO IT SUITS: francophone African human rights lawyers' groups and civil society organisations working on customary land rights, seeking capacity, training and support for strategic cases. CAVEATS: IT DOES NOT LITIGATE IN ITS OWN NAME AND WORKS ONLY THROUGH LOCAL PARTNERS, SO A COMMUNITY NEEDS AN ORGANISATION TO APPROACH WITH; ITS PUBLISHED AFRICAN PRESENCE IS NARROW, AND PROJECTS ARE MULTI-YEAR AND DONOR-FUNDED RATHER THAN RESPONSIVE TO AN URGENT CASE. For lawyers who build cases from outside the jurisdiction, Chad's entry; for the pro bono clearinghouse circulating matters to 800+ lawyers, São Tomé's entry.

trackers.name: UNHCR Botswana's published legal assistance list — naming Ditshwanelo, BONELA and the Law Society of Botswana as the bodies giving free legal help to people who cannot pay, and saying what each one actually does
trackers.desc: A PUBLISHED LIST OF WHO WILL ACT FOR YOU WHEN YOU CANNOT PAY — method and adjacency declared first: NINTH NAMED-ATTORNEY ROUND. A NATIONAL HEALTH AND HIV RIGHTS NETWORK IN THE SAME COUNTRY WAS WITHDRAWN THIS ROUND BEFORE WRITING — ITS FOCUS IS ACCESS TO HEALTH SERVICES RATHER THAN LAND OR PROJECTS, AND THE STANDING BRIEF SAYS NOT TO VEER. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN TWO HOSTS AND FOUR DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; BOTH HOSTS AND ALL FOUR FACTS ABSENT. THIS BUCKET ALREADY CARRIES THE NAMED RIGHTS CENTRE ON ITS OWN HOST — THAT ENTRY IS THE ORGANISATION, THIS IS THE DIRECTORY THAT PLACES IT AMONG THE COUNTRY'S OTHER FREE-LEGAL OPTIONS. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHO THE LIST IS FOR, WHICH IS THE FIND: IF YOU ARE IN THE COUNTRY AND NEED FREE LEGAL ASSISTANCE OR COUNSELLING, OR ARE INTERESTED TO LEARN ABOUT YOUR RIGHTS AND HELP YOUR COMMUNITY TO ACCESS LEGAL SUPPORT, THE ORGANISATIONS LISTED MAY BE ABLE TO HELP YOU. The commonest failure in this file is not that no free lawyer exists but that nobody knows which one. A short maintained list, published by an agency with no interest in promoting any particular organisation, answers that — and it is the kind of page worth finding for your own country before you need it. THE SECOND HALF OF THAT SENTENCE, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE LIST IS ADDRESSED NOT ONLY TO A PERSON WITH A PROBLEM BUT TO SOMEONE WHO WANTS TO HELP THEIR COMMUNITY ACCESS LEGAL SUPPORT — SO IT IS WRITTEN FOR THE ORGANISER AS WELL AS THE CLIENT. Explicitly addressed to the person doing the organising. That is unusual and it is the right audience: one person who learns which four organisations exist can route an entire settlement's problems to the right door. WHAT ONE LISTED BODY DOES: PROVIDES FREE LEGAL SERVICES TO MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC WHO CANNOT AFFORD PRIVATE LEGAL SUPPORT. WHAT A SECOND LISTED BODY DOES: EDUCATES, RESEARCHES, COUNSELS AND MEDIATES ON ISSUES OF HUMAN RIGHTS WITH SPECIFIC REFERENCE TO THE MARGINALIZED AND DISEMPOWERED — AND CAN ACT AS A MEDIATOR BETWEEN A GOVERNMENTAL AGENCY AND AN INTERNATIONAL AGENCY. MEDIATES, and can mediate between a government agency and an international one. Where a community's problem is that two institutions are pointing at each other, an organisation that will sit between them is doing something neither a lawyer nor an activist does. WHAT A THIRD LISTED BODY DOES: PROVIDES LEGAL SUPPORT TO PEOPLE WHO CANNOT AFFORD IT, WITHIN A HEALTH AND HUMAN RIGHTS MANDATE. Recorded with its mandate attached so nobody arrives with a land case at the wrong door. The list's value is partly in showing which organisations will NOT take your matter. THE REFERRAL AND TRACKING SYSTEM ONE OF THEM RUNS, WHICH IS THE THIRD FIND: SINCE 2014 IT HAS USED A LEGAL AID DATABASE TO REFER AND TRACK HUMAN RIGHTS ABUSE CASES AGAINST MARGINALISED PEOPLE. A database that both REFERS and TRACKS. Referral alone is how cases disappear — a community told to go to another organisation and never followed up. A tracked referral is a different service, and it is a cheap thing for any coalition to build for itself. THE REGISTRATION IT HELPED ACHIEVE: IN 2016 THE TEAM SUPPORTED THE SUCCESSFUL REGISTRATION OF THE COUNTRY'S FIRST ORGANISATION OF A PREVIOUSLY UNREGISTERED COMMUNITY — A REGISTRATION FIGHT WON THROUGH THE COURTS. Registration itself won in court. This file records the registration barrier blocking communities at nearly every funder; here is a domestic precedent that a refusal to register can be overturned, and an organisation that has done it. WHO ELSE SITS IN THE SAME NETWORK: NAMED PARTNERS INCLUDING THE COUNTRY'S NGO UMBRELLA COUNCIL, A NETWORK OF AIDS SERVICE ORGANISATIONS, A NETWORK OF PEOPLE LIVING WITH HIV, THE NATIONAL LAW SOCIETY, A YOUTH GROUP, A NAMED HUMAN RIGHTS CENTRE, AND REGIONAL LITIGATION AND RIGHTS ORGANISATIONS INCLUDING A SOUTHERN AFRICA LITIGATION CENTRE AND A SOUTHERN AFRICAN OPEN SOCIETY FOUNDATION. THE NATIONAL LAW SOCIETY inside a civil society network, as this file's Central African Republic entry records for another country. That is the reachable door to the private bar: the law society is where pro bono is coordinated, and a community that reaches the network reaches the society. THE CAPACITY IT HAS BUILT IN OTHER ORGANISATIONS: OVER 32 CIVIL SOCIETY AND COMMUNITY BASED ORGANIZATIONS TRAINED ON HUMAN RIGHTS PROGRAMMING TO FACILITATE MORE FOCUSED, SUSTAINABLE, COMMUNITY-LEVEL AND PEER-LED INTERVENTIONS, SUPPORTING BROADER PARTICIPATION OF COMMUNITIES FOR POLITICAL ENGAGEMENT AND LOBBYING FOR LAW AND POLICY REFORMS AT COMMUNITY LEVEL. THE JOINT ASSESSMENT IT CO-FACILITATED WITH THE STATE: A NATIONAL LEGAL ENVIRONMENT ASSESSMENT CO-FACILITATED WITH A GOVERNMENT MINISTRY AND A UN DEVELOPMENT AGENCY, WHICH IDENTIFIED KEY LEGAL AND POLICY GAPS CREATING BARRIERS FOR VULNERABLE POPULATIONS. A LEGAL ENVIRONMENT ASSESSMENT run jointly with the ministry that would have to fix the gaps. Worth naming as an instrument: a government that co-signed the finding cannot easily dispute it later. THE FARM COMMUNITIES ITS OWN RESEARCH DESCRIBES: REMOTE FARM COMMUNITIES USUALLY ONLY ACCESSIBLE WITH FOUR-WHEEL-DRIVE VEHICLES, WHERE OFTEN ONE FAMILY MEMBER WORKS FOR THE FARMER AND THE ENTIRE FAMILY STAYS ON THE FARM, SO THAT OVER THE YEARS INFORMAL SETTLEMENTS HAVE COME INTO EXISTENCE ON THOSE FARMS — RESIDENTS ONLY ABLE TO ACCESS GOVERNMENT SERVICES BY MOBILE OUTREACH THAT IS NOT COMPREHENSIVE OR RELIABLE, SOME GOING MANY MONTHS WITHOUT A SINGLE VISIT. This is the farm dweller situation recorded in this file's Eswatini and Seychelles entries, described here from another country: the whole family resident because one member is employed, and an informal settlement forming on private land over years. Where that is the pattern, the housing claim and the employment claim are the same fact, and both are lost together. AND THE ACCESS FIGURE THAT MAKES THE POINT: ALTHOUGH THE MAJORITY OF PEOPLE IN THE COUNTRY HAVE ACCESS TO A FACILITY WITHIN A 15 KILOMETRE RADIUS, IN ONE NAMED DISTRICT THIS IS ONLY THE CASE FOR 60% OF THE POPULATION.
