National averages hide the districts that need the service most. Ask for the figure by district before accepting that provision is adequate. WHO IT SUITS: anyone in this country who needs a free lawyer and does not know where to begin, and organisers looking for the shape of a national free-legal directory to build or find at home. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY, AND A SHORT AGENCY-MAINTAINED LIST RATHER THAN A COMPREHENSIVE REGISTER — SEVERAL LISTED BODIES HAVE HEALTH, REFUGEE OR HIV MANDATES RATHER THAN LAND OR PLANNING, SO CHECK THE MANDATE BEFORE APPROACHING; CONTACTS AND OPERATIONAL STATUS CHANGE, SO VERIFY BEFORE TRAVELLING. For the mapping tool that shows the nearest free legal office in another country, Mauritius' entry; for the rights centre itself, this bucket's own entry.

trackers.name: Mauritian Wildlife Foundation (MWF)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the only Mauritian NGO working solely on conservation of the island's endemic plants and animals, founded in 1984 and operating under a memorandum of agreement with government since 1994. Beyond species work it holds and manages land: it runs hands-on restoration on the Mauritian mainland, the offshore islets and Rodrigues, and manages nature reserves including Île aux Aigrettes and Grande Montagne. An IUCN member and BirdLife International partner. USE IT: as the body in Mauritius with the standing and the field capacity to take on a site and actually manage it, and as a partner if land you are trying to protect needs an institution behind it. Note what it is not: MWF is a conservation manager working closely with government, not a campaigning or litigating organisation, so it is the wrong door for opposing a project and the right one for securing what survives.

trackers.name: Companies & Business Registration (CBRD)
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Data Protection Office (Mauritius)
trackers.desc: Data Protection Office (Mauritius) — Mauritius’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Mauritius e-Procurement
trackers.desc: Mauritius' public e-procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Mauritius, and for how much.

trackers.name: National Audit Office
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Mauritius, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Mauritius
trackers.desc: Official judgment search of the Supreme Court of Mauritius, browsable by year. · Find here: the judgment search of the Supreme Court of Mauritius.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: Environment and Land Use Appeal Tribunal — one forum for six Acts
trackers.desc: A SINGLE SPECIALIST TRIBUNAL COVERS MOST OF WHAT A DEVELOPMENT TOUCHES. The Environment and Land Use Appeal Tribunal hears appeals under the Act's listed relevant Acts: the Building Act, the Environment Protection Act, the Local Government Act, the Morcellement Act (land subdivision), the Town and Country Planning Act, and any other Act prescribed. A development is usually challengeable under more than one of those, and they all go to the same forum — so identify every relevant Act before choosing a ground. The Tribunal comprises a Chairperson, Vice-chairperson and members, may include an appointed expert under section 3(4), and may sit in divisions. ‘Party’ in proceedings before it expressly includes the State. THE HONEST PICTURE, from the Tribunal's own chair at an Aarhus Convention task force: after the AHRIM judgment, in practice the only recourse objectors have is judicial review of the local authority's decision — a long and costly process — with objectors, often immediate neighbours or environmental NGOs, constrained by the technicality of judicial review. Plan for that, and see the Eco-Sud entry for the standing position.

trackers.name: Eco-Sud (JCPC 2023-0070) — Privy Council authority for liberal standing
trackers.desc: THE CASE TO CITE ON STANDING. The Minister granted an EIA licence under section 23 of the Environment Protection Act 2002 for a residential development on two plots close to a designated Ramsar wetland. The NGO Eco-Sud appealed, and the Tribunal held it lacked standing under section 54(2) — not aggrieved, no undue prejudice. The Supreme Court of Mauritius allowed Eco-Sud's appeal, holding that test too restrictive and that environmental appeals require a more liberal approach to standing, following Walton v The Scottish Ministers [2012] UKSC 44 — and the Privy Council firmly rejected the Minister's appeal, taking a purposive approach to statutory construction. THE REASONING TO QUOTE: the Board accepted the purpose of the standing rule was to stop ‘busybodies interfering in things which do not concern them’, but held it ‘is to be understood within the larger purpose of the EPA 2002 which remains the protection of the environment’. A restrictive standing provision read in light of the statute's protective purpose — now Privy Council authority, binding in Mauritius and persuasive across other JCPC jurisdictions, several of which appear in this map. Note section 2 of the EPA, a general duty of care on the citizens of Mauritius, in force without amendment. BUT CHECK THE CURRENT TEXT: Act No. 7 of 2020 added further criteria qualifying who may appeal against the Minister — older commentary may be out of date. Mauritius has been a Ramsar party since 2002; appeals reach the JCPC under section 81 of the Constitution.

trackers.name: Eco-Sud — won the Privy Council case that lets Mauritian citizens challenge an EIA licence without proving personal injury
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Mauritian environmental NGO whose 2018 challenge to an EIA licence granted for a hotel in a sensitive zone produced the single most useful precedent on this island. THE POINT OF LAW, WHICH DECIDES WHETHER YOU CAN FIGHT AT ALL: the Environment Tribunal applied a locus standi test — requiring the challenger to show it was personally injured and would suffer undue personal prejudice — and rejected the case on that basis. The Supreme Court held that the interpretation of standing must be widened because the environment is everyone's concern, and the Privy Council confirmed it: you cannot be required to claim a personal impact when challenging a matter concerning the environment and the benefits nature provides to all living things. If someone tells your group it has no standing to contest a licence in Mauritius, that is now wrong, and this is the case to cite. WHO IT SUITS: Mauritian residents, associations and collectives wanting to challenge an environmental clearance or EIA licence, especially in coastal and wetland zones. CAVEATS: winning standing is not winning the case — it opens the door to the Environment and Land Use Appeal Tribunal, and campaigners note that legislation has been repeatedly amended since 2016 to make legal contestation harder; Eco-Sud is an NGO, not a law firm, and litigation there required years and instructed counsel.

trackers.name: Platform Moris Lanvironnman — a coalition of about fifteen Mauritian NGOs that takes apart developers' EIA reports in public, at length
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: PML, created in December 2009, bringing together around fifteen Mauritian NGOs and committed individuals around an environmental charter, formed so that separate campaigns could coordinate, share information and back each other. WHAT IT ACTUALLY PRODUCES, and it is the most transferable habit in this entry: detailed public commentary on developers' Environmental Impact Assessment reports, filed with the environment ministry and then published — in one case a 150-page critique, including preliminary expert opinions, of an EIA that had been written in six very short weeks, together with a French-language summary so residents could read it. It has done the same for oil bunkering EIAs in the port and for an industrial battery anode facility near an estuary, arguing that report did not comply with the relevant environmental legislation. THE ARGUMENTS IT MAKES ARE THE ONES TO REUSE: that a project claiming only a small share of buildings will be “green” is masking that over 80 per cent of a site's terrestrial area — forest and other ecosystems — would be destroyed; that a 30-metre buffer around wetlands is derisory relative to their function; and that calling a forest “unusable” reveals ignorance of its ecological, economic and social role. ITS OWN STRATEGIC ADVICE, from a spokesperson: civil society must mobilise experts AND a legal team from the start — contestations fail either because the odds are legally stacked or because the objectors' files are not well enough built, or both. It also notes a win: the contestation of one project was successful despite the promoters and government having a head start. WHO IT SUITS: Mauritian communities and collectives facing smart-city, hotel, marina or industrial projects, especially on the coast. CAVEATS: a coalition and information-sharing platform, not a legal service or a fund; its site is a modest association page and much of its output appears via national press; and for the standing point that makes contestation possible, the Eco-Sud entry is the companion.

trackers.name: MACOSS — the recognised Mauritian NGO umbrella with 204 member organisations since 1965, the government NGO Unit, and named local chambers a community can instruct
trackers.desc: THE UMBRELLA AND THE NAMED CHAMBERS — this file's Mauritius record has been all environmental organisations and no membership body or lawyer: the MAURITIUS COUNCIL OF SOCIAL SERVICE (MACOSS), FOUNDED NOVEMBER 1965, is THE RECOGNISED UMBRELLA BODY FOR NGOs IN MAURITIUS, WITH A MEMBERSHIP OF 204 ORGANISATIONS, whose role is to FOSTER CO-OPERATION BETWEEN NGOs, GOVERNMENT DEPARTMENTS AND THE INTERNATIONAL COMMUNITY; it is JOINTLY FUNDED, INCLUDING BY AN EXTERNAL DEVELOPMENT PARTNER, and has evolved from a social service coordinating body into a Council of NGOs dedicated to social services and sustainable social development, promoting voluntary and charitable activities, COMMUNITY AND SOCIAL DEVELOPMENT, by BRINGING TOGETHER REPRESENTATIVES OF STATUTORY BODIES AND VOLUNTARY ORGANISATIONS. Two hundred and four member organisations is the whole organised Mauritian sector in one place — and a body whose stated function is bringing statutory bodies and voluntary organisations to the same table is who a village association asks to convene a meeting with a ministry. AND THERE IS A GOVERNMENT NGO UNIT WHOSE PUBLISHED FUNCTION IS TO PROVIDE SUPPORT AND GUIDANCE TO NGOs. If you are forming an association, the NGO Unit is the free advisory desk before you pay anyone — ask it what registration your intended activity requires. THE LAWYERS, BY NAME AND STRUCTURE, because Mauritius separates barristers from attorneys and that changes who you instruct: 5 ST JAMES COURT, THE CHAMBERS OF RAVINDRA CHETTY S.C., ESTABLISHED 2010, a set REGROUPING SELF-EMPLOYED BARRISTERS WHO SHARE THE SAME ETHICS AND VALUES — all sole practitioners, BUT OFTEN INSTRUCTED TOGETHER AS PART OF A TEAM, listed under civil and human rights work; and ETUDE DYA GHOSE, ATTORNEYS, FOUNDED 1971 by an attorney-at-law and now a family practice of FOUR ATTORNEYS, among the leading sets. A chambers whose barristers can be instructed TOGETHER is what a community case needs — one silk and a team, briefed through an attorney. Ask an attorney's set to instruct the chambers; that is the order the Mauritian profession works in. The published guidance for a rights problem in Mauritius is to contact a specialised lawyer OR SEEK FREE CONSULTATIONS FROM LEGAL AID SERVICES, report the issue to the HUMAN RIGHTS COMMISSION for advice and intervention, and reach out to NGOs. WHO IT SUITS: Mauritian community associations needing a sector body, a registration advisor or counsel. CAVEATS: AN UMBRELLA AND PRIVATE CHAMBERS — fees apply to the latter; confirm current listings. For the Privy Council case that lets citizens challenge an EIA, Mauritius' Eco-Sud entry; for the fifteen-organisation environmental coalition, Platform Moris Lanvironnman; for the foundation that manages islands, the Mauritian Wildlife Foundation entry.

trackers.name: How MWF co-manages land in Mauritius — separate MOUs with the government and the Rodrigues Regional Assembly, a jointly run sanctuary, its own visitor income, and the ACTogether NGO finder
trackers.desc: THE NGO THAT CO-MANAGES STATE LAND UNDER AN MOU — which is the transferable part, not the birds: the MAURITIAN WILDLIFE FOUNDATION IS A REGISTERED CHARITY, No. 2143, ESTABLISHED 1984, WITH ITS ACCREDITATION NUMBER WITH THE NATIONAL SOCIAL INCLUSION FOUNDATION ALSO PUBLISHED, headquartered at GRANNUM ROAD, VACOAS, with a branch at SOLITUDE, RODRIGUES. IT WORKS CLOSELY WITH THE GOVERNMENT OF MAURITIUS AND WITH THE RODRIGUES REGIONAL ASSEMBLY, WITH FORMALISED AGREEMENTS IN PLACE — SET OUT IN SEPARATE MEMORANDUMS OF UNDERSTANDING. Separate MOUs with the national government and with an island's own regional assembly is the arrangement to ask for: it means the island body signs in its own right rather than through the capital. If your territory has a regional assembly, insist it be a party, not a spectator. WHAT THAT LETS IT DO WITH LAND: FROM 1996 MWF EXPANDED ITS OPERATIONS INTO HABITAT RESTORATION, INCLUDING THE MANAGEMENT OF NATIVE FORESTS AND SMALL ISLANDS AROUND MAURITIUS AND IN THE OUTER ISLANDS — an evolution FROM A FUNDING-AND-ADMINISTRATION ORGANISATION TO A HANDS-ON CONSERVATION AGENCY, marked by the change of name that year — AND A NAMED SANCTUARY IS RUN JOINTLY BY THE NATIONAL PARKS AND CONSERVATION SERVICE AND MWF, with an international trust's help. A charity that began by administering funds and became the manager of forests and islands is the growth path a local association can follow. Jointly run by the parks service and the NGO is the phrase to put in your own agreement. AND HOW IT PAYS FOR ITSELF, WHICH IS THE PART MOST COMMUNITIES SKIP: ONE OF ITS STATED OBJECTIVES IS TO SECURE THE FUTURE OF MAURITIAN SPECIES THROUGH INCOME GENERATED AND SOUND MANAGEMENT OF HUMAN, FISCAL AND CAPITAL RESOURCES — and it operates ECOTOURS OPEN TO THE PUBLIC on a named islet and a named mountain, plus A BOUTIQUE at Mahébourg listed as the last stop of the visit. Income generated is written into the objectives, and the shop is placed at the END of the tour. That is a deliberate design: a protected site that sells something to the people who have just seen it funds its own wardens. ITS OTHER STATED AIMS include SHARING KNOWLEDGE GAINED THROUGH RESTORATION PROGRAMMES WITH FELLOW MAURITIAN AND INTERNATIONAL CONSERVATIONISTS and SHARING THE JOYS AND BENEFITS OF NATIVE WILDERNESS AND WILDLIFE WITH THE MAURITIAN PEOPLE; it has run workshops for FISHERMEN IN THE NORTH OF MAURITIUS under an islet-protection project, and its education programme covers Mauritius and Rodrigues. THE OTHER NAMED ORGANISATIONS: REEF CONSERVATION, ECOSUD, ASSOCIATION DU DÉVELOPPEMENT DURABLE and the BIODIVERSITY ENVIRONMENT INSTITUTE, all recorded as active in the non-formal sector; and Mauritius protects biodiversity through a mix of national parks, forest and nature reserves, offshore islet protections and marine protected areas, PLUS SOME PRIVATELY MANAGED CONSERVATION AREAS. Privately managed conservation areas exist in Mauritius. That is the category to ask about if the ground you want protected is in private hands — the mechanism already has precedent here. AND TO FIND ANY OF THEM: A PUBLIC FIND-AN-NGO DIRECTORY (actogether.mu) CARRIES MAURITIAN NGOs WITH THEIR ADDRESSES, ACCREDITATION NUMBERS AND PROGRAMMES. WHO IT SUITS: Mauritian and Rodriguan communities seeking co-management, a private conservation arrangement, or a self-funding visitor model. CAVEATS: A CONSERVATION CHARITY WORKING UNDER GOVERNMENT AGREEMENTS — not a litigator. For 204 member organisations and the NGO Unit, Mauritius's MACOSS entry; for chambers and a firm dating to 1971, the attorney entry.

trackers.name: Voluntary Marine Conservation Areas — the Mauritian model where coastal communities and fishermen establish a conservation area themselves — plus sixty mooring buoys, a free daily education centre in a donated public building, and MMCS's 40 years
trackers.desc: A CONSERVATION AREA THE FISHERMEN DECLARE THEMSELVES — and that is the Mauritian idea worth taking anywhere: SINCE 2009, A MAURITIAN NGO HAS BEEN DEVELOPING THE INNOVATIVE CONCEPT OF VOLUNTARY MARINE CONSERVATION AREAS IN MAURITIUS, WORKING WITH COASTAL COMMUNITIES AND FISHERMEN TO ESTABLISH VOLUNTARY CONSERVATION AREAS. VOLUNTARY means the community and the fishermen agree the area and observe it, without waiting for a legal designation. This file records again and again that formal protection takes years and often never comes. A voluntary area can start this season, it is the fishermen's own rule so they enforce it themselves, and it builds the record that a later legal designation rests on. If your coast needs protecting now, that is the form to ask about by name. WHO RUNS IT: A NON-PROFIT, CHARITABLE, PROJECT-BASED NGO REGISTERED WITH THE REGISTRAR GENERAL SINCE 2004 AND ACCREDITED WITH THE NATIONAL CORPORATE RESPONSIBILITY FOUNDATION SINCE 2009. Accreditation with a national corporate responsibility foundation is the domestic funding route in Mauritius — it makes the organisation eligible for company CSR money rather than foreign grants. Ask whether your own country has an equivalent register, because that is where local corporate funds are legally required to go. THE ENGINEERING, AND THE REASON FOR IT: SIXTY PERMANENT MOORING BUOYS WERE INSTALLED ALONG THE MAURITIAN COASTS AND THE RODRIGUES MARINE RESERVE, IN A PROJECT LAUNCHED IN 2000 WITH TWO NAMED PARTNERS — BECAUSE WHEN A BOAT DROPS ANCHOR ON THE REEF, THE DAMAGE CAUSED TO ANIMAL AND VEGETAL LIFE CAN BE PARTICULARLY DRAMATIC, AS THE SWELL AND THE WIND CAUSE THE CHAIN TO SCOUR THE SEABED WITHIN THE BOAT'S SWINGING SPACE, AND IT TAKES YEARS FOR THE CORALS TO GROW AGAIN. A single anchor chain sweeping a circle of reef, every time a boat stops. Sixty fixed buoys is a physical fix that requires no enforcement and no prosecution — the boats use them because they are there. Where tourist or fishing boats anchor on your reef, that is the intervention to cost first. THE BUILDING, WHICH IS THE PART TO COPY: A PUBLIC BUILDING ON A NAMED BEACH WAS DONATED AND RENOVATED BY A BEACH AUTHORITY, AND THE NGO USES IT AS A PLATFORM FOR EDUCATION ON MARINE ECOLOGY — WITH BOOKS, DVDs AND VARIOUS GAMES ON THE DISCOVERY OF THE MARINE HABITAT AVAILABLE FREE OF CHARGE, AT A FACILITY OPEN EVERY DAY OF THE YEAR. A public authority donated and renovated a building, and a community organisation runs it. Ask your own beach, forest or municipal authority what buildings it holds that stand empty — the premises are usually the hardest thing for a village association to obtain, and here a state body supplied them. AND THE MOBILE VERSION FOR EVERYWHERE ELSE: A MOBILE UNIT OPERATING SINCE SEPTEMBER 2014 EXTENDS AWARENESS AND EDUCATION ACTIVITIES TO ALL REGIONS OF THE ISLAND, PRIMARILY TARGETING SCHOOLS — and the organisation is THE NATIONAL COORDINATOR FOR MAURITIUS AND RODRIGUES OF AN INTERNATIONAL ECO-SCHOOLS PROGRAMME, WITH NEARLY 100 SCHOOLS PARTICIPATING TODAY. A hundred schools in a small country is most of them. If you want a generation that will defend a reef, the schools programme is the mechanism — and there is an international programme with a national coordinator already in place. THE JOBS: IT RUNS AN ECO-GUIDE TRAINING PROGRAMME FOR OUT-OF-SCHOOL UNEMPLOYED YOUTH, AND WORKS IN COLLABORATION WITH THE MINISTRY OF FISHERIES TO REINFORCE THE CAPACITY OF MARINE PROTECTED AREAS. Out-of-school unemployed youth named as the target for guide training. That is the group most likely to be blamed for pressure on the resource and least likely to be offered a wage from it. THE OLDER SOCIETY: A MAURITIUS MARINE CONSERVATION SOCIETY HAS OPERATED FOR MORE THAN 40 YEARS, WHOSE LONG-TERM MARINE MAMMAL IDENTIFICATION STUDY BROUGHT ABOUT THE CREATION OF A BETTER MANAGEMENT PLAN FOR THE DOLPHIN WATCHING TOURISM INDUSTRY, AND WHOSE CORAL REEF MONITORING PROGRAMME PROVIDES DATA ON THE HEALTH AND DIVERSITY OF THE CORALS — with the motto CONSERVATION THROUGH EDUCATION, and work on UNDERWATER CULTURAL HERITAGE AND ARCHAEOLOGY. A long-term identification study that produced a management plan for a tourism industry. That is the sequence: count the animals for years, and the count becomes the rule the operators follow. If a tourism industry is pressing on your wildlife, the counting has to start before the argument does. AND UNDERWATER CULTURAL HERITAGE is a category worth knowing — a wreck or a submerged site can carry heritage protection that the water around it does not. Also named: AN ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AND CONSERVATION ORGANISATION WORKING TO CONSERVE MAURITIUS' BIODIVERSITY AND DECREASE VULNERABILITY TO CLIMATE CHANGE. WHO IT SUITS: Mauritian and Rodriguan coastal communities and fishermen, and anyone whose reef is being anchored on or whose young people need paid guide work. CAVEATS: A VOLUNTARY AREA HAS NO LEGAL FORCE — it rests on the fishermen's own agreement, so it is only as strong as their consensus. For separate MOUs with the government and the Rodrigues Regional Assembly, Mauritius' MWF entry, which also carries the actogether.mu NGO finder.

trackers.name: The Earth Defenders Toolkit — a toolkit co-created by eight frontline organisations with an interactive tool finder, guides to building your own wireless network where no operator will, and free offline software for a community website carrying your land plan
trackers.desc: BUILT SO YOU NEED THEM LESS, NOT MORE — declared adjacency first: THE PREVIOUS ENTRY IN THIS FILE, UNDER EQUATORIAL GUINEA, NAMED THIS TOOLKIT IN A SINGLE LINE. THE EIGHT CO-CREATORS, THE TOOL FINDER, THE GUIDES AND THE SUPPORT ROUTE BELOW ARE NOT IN IT. WHAT IT IS: A COLLABORATIVE SPACE FOR EARTH DEFENDERS AND THEIR ALLIES, PROVIDING A GROWING COLLECTION OF RESOURCES AND TRAINING MATERIALS FOR COMMUNITIES ON THE FRONTLINES OF THE STRUGGLE TO DEFEND CRITICAL ECOSYSTEMS AROUND THE WORLD, AND COMMUNITY NETWORKS FOR USERS TO CONNECT AND SHARE THEIR EXPERIENCES — CO-CREATED BY EIGHT NAMED ORGANISATIONS, INCLUDING A FOREST PEOPLES ORGANISATION AND AN INDIGENOUS DISTRICT COUNCIL. A district council among the co-creators, not just NGOs. A community body helped design the toolkit, which is a different provenance from a product built for communities and handed over. THE MISSION, AND IT IS THE TEST TO APPLY TO EVERY TECHNOLOGY OFFER YOU RECEIVE: TO PROVIDE AND PROMOTE APPROACHES TO USING TECHNOLOGY IN A WAY THAT SUPPORTS LOCAL AUTONOMY AND OWNERSHIP OVER TOOLS AND DATA, AND REDUCES RELIANCE ON OUTSIDE SUPPORT — AIMING TO SERVE COMMUNITY NEEDS WITHOUT SEEDING A RELATIONSHIP OF DEPENDENCY ON OUTSIDE SUPPORT. WITHOUT SEEDING A RELATIONSHIP OF DEPENDENCY. Ask any organisation offering your community software what happens when their funding ends. If the answer is that the system stops, it was never yours. THE TOOL FINDER, WHICH IS WHERE TO START: AN INTERACTIVE TOOL FINDER HELPS USERS FIND OUT WHAT IS AVAILABLE AND PARSE IT FOR WHAT MIGHT BE MORE ALIGNED TO THEIR GOALS. You describe what you are trying to do and it narrows the options. That is the step communities usually skip — adopting whichever tool an outsider arrived with rather than the one that fits the task. WHY IT EXISTS, AND THE PATTERN IS FAMILIAR FROM THIS FILE: THREATS AGAINST INDIGENOUS AND OTHER FRONTLINE DEFENDERS INCREASED; FOR MANY PARTNERS THE PANDEMIC BROUGHT DUAL THREATS OF DISEASE AND INCREASED INVASION OF THEIR TERRITORIES BY ILLEGAL LOGGERS AND MINERS; AND MORE AND MORE COMMUNITIES WERE REACHING OUT TO REQUEST SUPPORT AND TRAININGS ON HOW TO USE TECHNOLOGY TO PROTECT THEIR LAND — SO IT WAS CREATED TO SHARE SUCCESS STORIES AND BEST PRACTICES, ADVICE ON HOW TO DETERMINE WHAT TOOLS ARE RIGHT FOR A PARTICULAR PROJECT, AND FOSTER COMMUNITY BETWEEN FRONTLINE DEFENDERS. Invasion rose precisely when outsiders could not travel. Whenever attention leaves — a pandemic, an election, a war elsewhere — the loggers arrive. That is the argument for a community's own monitoring rather than a visiting one. THE UNMET NEEDS THEY NAME, WORTH READING AS A LIST OF WHAT OTHER COMMUNITIES ASK FOR: BESPOKE TOOLS TO SUPPORT SECURE COMMUNICATIONS, SOCIAL NETWORKS, LANGUAGE REVITALIZATION AND ACTIVISM, OFFLINE NETWORKING, MEDIA DISTRIBUTION AND ADVOCACY. THE TWO CONNECTIVITY GUIDES, WHICH ARE THE FIND: A COMMUNITY NETWORK GUIDE COMPILING SUGGESTED STEPS, RESOURCES AND QUESTIONS TO SUPPORT A COLLECTIVE PROCESS BEHIND THE DEPLOYMENT AND MAINTENANCE OF A COMMUNITY NETWORK; AND A SECOND GUIDE FEATURING FREE HARDWARE AND FREE SOFTWARE TOOLS CREATED SPECIFICALLY TO EMPOWER COMMUNITIES TO MANAGE THEIR OWN NETWORKS — NOTING THAT COMMUNITY NETWORKS HAVE BECOME A SELF-PROVIDING SOLUTION TO THE CONNECTIVITY GAP THAT GOVERNMENTS AND CORPORATIONS HAVE FAILED TO PROVIDE TO RURAL AND REMOTE COMMUNITIES. Build your own network where no operator will come. For a village that cannot report anything because there is no signal, this is the underlying fix rather than a workaround — and the guides are free, with free hardware designs. AND THE OPTION MOST PEOPLE DO NOT KNOW EXISTS: OTHER COMMUNITIES PREFER TO USE A COMMUNITY NETWORK THAT IS NOT CONNECTED TO THE INTERNET. A local network with no internet at all — messages, maps and files shared across a village, unreachable from outside. Where surveillance is the danger, that is safer than connectivity, and it still solves the problem of getting a map from one end of the territory to the other. THE HONEST FRAMING IN THE GUIDE: THERE IS NO SUCH THING AS A RECIPE TO FOLLOW, BUT WE CAN LEARN MANY LESSONS AND RECOMMENDED STEPS FROM EXISTING EXPERIENCES IN DIVERSE GEOGRAPHIES. THE WEBSITE SOFTWARE: DEVELOPED FOR LOCAL COMMUNITIES WHO WANTED WEBSITES TO SHOWCASE THEIR WAY OF LIFE AND TO PUBLISH NEWS AND STORIES ABOUT THE THREATS AND CHALLENGES THEY FACE — OPEN-SOURCE SOFTWARE FOR CREATING AND LAYING OUT A LOCAL WEBSITE WHILE OFFLINE, WHICH CAN ALSO BE UPLOADED TO AN ONLINE SERVER IF THE COMMUNITY CHOOSES; USEFUL FOR COMMUNITIES WHO WANT TO MAINTAIN INFORMATION ABOUT THEMSELVES OR THEIR LAND, LIKE A LAND OR MANAGEMENT PLAN. IT IS FREE AND OPEN-SOURCE, BUT YOU NEED TO REQUEST AN ACCOUNT FROM THE ADMINISTRATOR. Build the site offline, publish only if and when you decide. A community land plan or management plan hosted under your own name is the document to point an investor or a ministry at — and this file has recorded repeatedly that the community with a written plan is treated differently from the one without. AND THE ORAL-HISTORY APP: AN APP FOR COMMUNITIES TO MAP, PROTECT AND SHARE STORIES ABOUT THEIR LAND, CONNECTING AUDIO OR VIDEO CONTENT TO PLACES ON A MAP. For a claim resting on what people remember rather than on paper, this turns memory into a located record. Record the elders now; that window closes on its own. WHO IT SUITS: African communities choosing what technology to adopt, villages with no connectivity, and anyone wanting a community website or an oral-history map. CAVEATS: TOOLS AND GUIDES, NOT FUNDING OR LEGAL HELP — and the website software needs an account requested from an administrator. For the free offline mapping tools where the community owns the data, Equatorial Guinea's entry; for the free system for rights neither registered nor registerable, Comoros' entry; for free weekly deforestation alerts, the Republic of Congo's entry.

trackers.name: Publish What You Pay (PWYP) — the global coalition of 1,000+ civil society organisations on oil, gas and mining that a national coalition joins by completing one form — with an Africa Charter, regional coordinators, a published governance manual and a recent change of name
trackers.desc: A FORM AND AN EMAIL, AND YOU ARE IN A THOUSAND-ORGANISATION COALITION — declared adjacency first: NATIONAL TRANSPARENCY INITIATIVES ARE ALREADY FILED IN THIS FILE AS BARE ORGANISATION NAMES UNDER GHANA, LIBERIA, NIGERIA, TANZANIA, SIERRA LEONE AND ZAMBIA, AND ONE NATIONAL COALITION CHAPTER UNDER NIGERIA. NONE DESCRIBES THE GLOBAL COALITION, ITS MEMBERSHIP ROUTE, ITS AFRICA CHARTER OR ITS RENAMING. AND THE RENAMING MATTERS PRACTICALLY: THE NETWORK NOW OPERATES UNDER A NEW NAME, HAVING FORMERLY BEEN REGISTERED UNDER ITS ORIGINAL ONE. Searching the old name will find history rather than the current network; this file records both so nobody looks in the wrong place. THE JOINING ROUTE, WHICH IS THE FIND: BECOMING A MEMBER MEANS JOINING MORE THAN 1000 OTHER CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS IN OVER 50 COUNTRIES ACROSS THE WORLD — AND IF YOU ARE PART OF A NATIONAL COALITION WHICH WOULD LIKE TO JOIN OR AFFILIATE, COMPLETE A FORM AND EMAIL IT TO THE RELEVANT REGIONAL COORDINATOR. One form to a named regional coordinator. That is the entire barrier between a national land or mining coalition and a thousand organisations that have fought the same companies — and this file has recorded repeatedly that the community meeting a mining firm for the first time is meeting a firm that has met a hundred communities. NOTE THE UNIT: it is national coalitions that affiliate, not individual villages. So the practical step for a single community is to find or build the national coalition — and this file's national entries under Ghana, Nigeria, Liberia, Tanzania, Sierra Leone and Zambia are where several already exist. WHAT IT IS: A GLOBAL COALITION OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS UNITED IN THEIR CALL FOR AN OPEN AND ACCOUNTABLE EXTRACTIVE SECTOR, SO THAT OIL, GAS AND MINING REVENUES IMPROVE THE LIVES OF WOMEN, MEN AND YOUTH IN RESOURCE-RICH COUNTRIES, AND THAT EXTRACTION IS CARRIED OUT IN A RESPONSIBLE MANNER THAT BENEFITS COUNTRIES AND THEIR CITIZENS — FORMED IN 2002. THE AFRICAN GOVERNING DOCUMENT: AN AFRICA CHARTER IS THE INSTITUTIONAL DOCUMENT THAT GUIDES THE ACTIVITIES OF THE NETWORK IN AFRICA AND PROMOTES ITS VISION AND VALUES ON THE AFRICAN CONTINENT. A charter written for Africa specifically, not a translation of the global one. Read it before joining — it is what your coalition would be signing up to, and it is the document to hold the network to afterwards. THE GOVERNANCE: A GOVERNANCE MANUAL OUTLINES ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES AND IS INTENDED TO BE A LIVING DOCUMENT — AND THE NETWORK HAS BEEN A REGISTERED LEGAL ENTITY IN THE UNITED KINGDOM SINCE APRIL 2015. A published governance manual is rarer than it should be. This file's IPACC entry records the same virtue: when the rules of a network are written down, a member organisation can tell whether it is being outvoted fairly. WHO ELSE IS IN IT: OPEN SOCIETY FOUNDATIONS, A GLOBAL INVESTIGATIVE ORGANISATION, DEVELOPMENT AND FAITH-BASED AGENCIES, A GLOBAL ANTI-CORRUPTION MOVEMENT, A HUMAN RIGHTS ORGANISATION, AND A NUMBER OF GROUPS FROM DEVELOPING COUNTRIES. Several of those already have their own entries here. Joining one coalition therefore puts your organisation in the same room as the funders, the investigators and the legal networks filed separately across this file — which is the compounding value of a coalition over a grant. THE BACKLASH REPORT, WHICH IS THE ONE TO CITE WHEN YOUR MEMBERS ARE THREATENED: IT PUBLISHED A REPORT TOGETHER WITH A GLOBAL CIVIL SOCIETY ALLIANCE ABOUT THE BACKLASH THAT NATURAL RESOURCE ACTIVISTS FACE. Somebody has documented that resisting extraction gets people attacked, as a pattern rather than a series of incidents. That report is evidence for a protection application. THE TRANSITION MINERALS WORK, WHICH IS WHERE AFRICAN LAND PRESSURE IS HEADING: MEMBERS AND PARTNERS SHARE EXPERIENCES OF USING COLLECTIVE ACTION TO AMPLIFY VOICES AND OPEN UP PARTICIPATION OF COMMUNITIES AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS IN TRANSITION MINERALS ADVOCACY IN AFRICA. The minerals for batteries and grids are under African ground, and the next decade of concessions will be granted over communities who have never heard the phrase. Getting into that conversation before the licences are issued is worth more than any objection afterwards. THE RAW MATERIALS GUIDELINES: A COALITION IT SITS IN IS DEEPLY CONCERNED ABOUT THE POTENTIAL FOR A RAW MATERIALS REGULATION TO INCREASE EXTRACTION AND HARM NATURE AND PEOPLE, AND HAS DEVELOPED COMPREHENSIVE GUIDELINES URGING DECISION-MAKERS TO IMPLEMENT IT IN A WAY THAT MINIMISES THESE HARMS — FOCUSING ON A SIGNIFICANT REDUCTION IN RAW MATERIAL CONSUMPTION AND A GENUINE COMMITMENT TO CIRCULAR ECONOMY PRINCIPLES. The demand side named as the answer. A community objecting to a mine is usually told the mineral is needed; guidelines arguing that consumption itself should fall give that objection an economic argument rather than only a local one. AND THE FREE PUBLICATION: A REPORT ON WHAT THE MOVEMENT LEARNED IS FREELY AVAILABLE IN ENGLISH, FRENCH AND RUSSIAN. WHO IT SUITS: African national coalitions and organisations working on oil, gas, mining or transition minerals, and communities looking for the coalition in their own country. CAVEATS: MEMBERSHIP IS FOR NATIONAL COALITIONS AND ORGANISATIONS RATHER THAN INDIVIDUAL COMMUNITIES, AND THE NETWORK HAS CHANGED ITS NAME — search both. For the national initiatives already filed, Ghana's, Liberia's, Nigeria's, Tanzania's, Sierra Leone's and Zambia's entries; for the contract repository holding extractives agreements, Mauritania's entry; for the trackers naming the financier behind a project, Guinea's entry.

trackers.name: Land documentation technology, hardware and training under a published data sovereignty policy where the community owns the records — trained in a single afternoon for people who have never used a smartphone, with a printed-paper-map route where there are no devices
trackers.desc: THE FOUNDATION DOES NOT CLAIM OWNERSHIP — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE ALREADY CARRIES COMMUNITY-OWNED OFFLINE MAPPING TOOLS UNDER EQUATORIAL GUINEA, A FREE RECORDING SYSTEM FOR UNREGISTERED RIGHTS UNDER COMOROS, MAPPING MICROGRANTS UNDER BURUNDI, AND STATUTORY-DEED FORMALIZATION UNDER THE REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO. THIS IS A DIFFERENT OFFER — A HOSTED PLATFORM WITH HARDWARE AND A PUBLISHED DATA-GOVERNANCE POLICY. THE OWNERSHIP CLAUSE, AND IT IS THE FIND: DATA BELONGS TO THE PEOPLE WHO CREATE IT — PARTNERS AND THE COMMUNITIES THEY REPRESENT OWN THEIR DATA AND DECIDE WHO CAN ACCESS IT AND UNDER WHAT CONDITIONS. THE FOUNDATION DOES NOT CLAIM OWNERSHIP. COMMUNITIES HAVE THE RIGHT TO GOVERN DATA ACCORDING TO THEIR OWN LAWS, CUSTOMS AND VALUES. Written as policy, on a page you can print. The offline-tools entry in this file gives you data that never leaves your phones; this one is the opposite arrangement — the records sit on somebody's cloud — and the protection is contractual rather than technical. Both are legitimate; know which you are accepting. Ask any organisation offering to map your land to show you the equivalent page, and if there isn't one, that is your answer. THE FRAMEWORKS IT BINDS ITSELF TO: A UNITED NATIONS DECLARATION ON THE RIGHTS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES; FREE, PRIOR AND INFORMED CONSENT; AND A NAMED SET OF PRINCIPLES FOR INDIGENOUS DATA GOVERNANCE — COLLECTIVE BENEFIT, AUTHORITY TO CONTROL, RESPONSIBILITY, AND ETHICS. AUTHORITY TO CONTROL is the clause to quote. Those four words are a published standard a community can hold any data project to, including a government one. THE RISK IT NAMES OUT LOUD RATHER THAN BURIES: LAND AND RESOURCE DATA CAN CARRY REAL RISKS IF MISUSED, PARTICULARLY WHEN IT REFLECTS COLLECTIVE RIGHTS, CUSTOMARY GOVERNANCE SYSTEMS, OR SENSITIVE TERRITORIAL CLAIMS — STRONG DATA GOVERNANCE HELPS ENSURE THAT DATA STRENGTHENS COMMUNITY RIGHTS RATHER THAN EXPOSING COMMUNITIES TO NEW VULNERABILITIES. A map of who lives where, in a contested area, is a targeting list in the wrong hands. This file has recorded evictions that followed a survey. An organisation that says so before it starts is behaving correctly. THE TRAINING STANDARD, STATED PLAINLY: WE ROUTINELY TRAIN PEOPLE WHO HAVE NEVER EVEN USED A SMARTPHONE BEFORE TO USE OUR TECHNOLOGY TO DOCUMENT THEIR LAND RIGHTS IN A SINGLE AFTERNOON. One afternoon, from no smartphone experience. That is the benchmark to hold any trainer to — and it means the people who walk the boundary can record it themselves rather than escorting a technician. THE PAPER ROUTE FOR PLACES WITH NO DEVICES: TECHNOLOGY THAT ALLOWS USERS TO PRINT PAPER MAPS, ANNOTATE THOSE MAPS WITH PEN, AND THEN TAKE A PICTURE OF THOSE ANNOTATIONS WITH THEIR PHONE AND UPLOAD THEM TO BE TRANSCRIBED. Draw on a printed map with a pen, photograph it, done. Elders who will not use an app will mark a map, and one phone in the village converts the whole exercise — which is the cheapest participatory mapping method in this file. THE OTHER COLLECTION OPTIONS: GPS-ENABLED SMARTPHONES AND TABLETS, PAPER-BASED FORMS COMBINED WITH SATELLITE IMAGERY TO IDENTIFY PROPERTY BOUNDARIES, OR HAND-HELD GPS DEVICES — AND IT CAN ALSO STORE DATA ALREADY COLLECTED THROUGH TRADITIONAL PAPER-BASED SURVEYS AND MAPS. Your existing paper records can be brought in. Decades of village registers, minute books and hand-drawn boundaries do not have to be redone. WHAT THE PLATFORM INCLUDES: MOBILE, OFFLINE-READY TOOLS TO MAP LAND PARCELS, FORESTS AND COMMUNITY RESOURCES; REAL-TIME DASHBOARDS AND INTERACTIVE MAPS TO TRACK PROGRESS AND INFORM ADVOCACY; SECURE CLOUD SYSTEMS TO MANAGE RECORDS AND PROTECT SENSITIVE DATA; AND ROLE-BASED ACCESS THAT ENABLES COLLABORATION WITH GOVERNMENTS, CIVIL SOCIETY AND DONORS WHILE ENSURING COMMUNITY CONTROL OF DATA. ROLE-BASED ACCESS is the practical mechanism behind the ownership promise: the ministry can be shown the boundary without being shown the names. THE SHORTAGE IT EXISTS TO ANSWER: A CRITICAL SHORTAGE OF SURVEYORS IS SLOWING DOWN THE DOCUMENTATION OF LAND AROUND THE WORLD — AND IN MUCH OF THE WORLD, PARTICULARLY IN AFRICA, LAND IS MANAGED BY CUSTOMARY TENURE SYSTEMS THAT ARE NOT PART OF ANY FORMAL STATUTORY SYSTEM. This file's Eritrea entry covers the volunteer surveyor programme; this is the other half of the same problem — methods that need fewer surveyors at all. THE SCALE: ONE-THIRD OF PEOPLE ON THE PLANET DO NOT HAVE DOCUMENTED RIGHTS TO THE LAND ON WHICH THEY RELY; AN ESTIMATED 70% OF PROPERTY IN EMERGING ECONOMIES IS UNDOCUMENTED; AND AN ESTIMATED 25% OF THE WORLD'S URBAN POPULATION LIVE IN HOMES TO WHICH THEY HAVE NO LEGAL RIGHT. THE WORKED RESULTS: ONE PARTNER, AFTER A SHORT TRAINING COURSE, REACHED MORE THAN 13,000 FAMILIES BY MIGRATING THEIR EXISTING DATA AND CONTINUING WITH FIELD COLLECTION; AND WITH ANOTHER PARTNER A COMMUNITY REGISTERED OVER 100,000 FAMILY PLOTS UNDER ITS OWN LAND POLICY, SECURING RIGHTS AND PROTECTING FORESTS AMID POLITICAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL THREATS. UNDER ITS OWN LAND POLICY — a community's own rules, not the state's, with a hundred thousand plots recorded against them. Where a government will not recognise customary tenure, a community register built to its own policy is still the document that exists when the argument comes. THE GOVERNMENT ANGLE, WHICH IS AN ASK YOU CAN MAKE: WHEN GOVERNMENTS OPEN THEIR DATA ON LAND USE AND CONCESSIONS, CONSERVATIONISTS CAN SEE WHAT LAND IS PROTECTED AND WHAT IS UNDER THREAT, AND INDIVIDUALS AND COMMUNITIES CAN CHECK THAT THEIR RIGHTS ARE PROPERLY DOCUMENTED — AND WHERE LANDOWNERS NEED PROTECTION, GOVERNMENTS CAN OPEN THEIR LAND RECORDS WITHOUT DISCLOSING THE NAMES OF INDIVIDUAL OWNERS. That last clause defeats the standard refusal. When a ministry says concession data cannot be published because of privacy, the answer is that boundaries can be opened while names stay closed. AND THE MAINTENANCE POINT: GOVERNMENTS ADOPTING THE PLATFORM DO NOT NEED TO HIRE SPECIALLY TRAINED STAFF TO MANAGE THE UPKEEP OF THESE RECORDS. WHO IT SUITS: African communities and the organisations documenting their land — especially where records are on paper, devices are few and the risk of exposure is real. CAVEATS: IT WORKS THROUGH PARTNER ORGANISATIONS AND THE PLATFORM IS HOSTED, SO THE PROTECTION IS POLICY RATHER THAN TECHNICAL — for data that never leaves your own phones, Equatorial Guinea's entry. For the free system recording rights neither registered nor registerable, Comoros' entry; for grants that buy the devices, Burundi's entry.

trackers.name: Marine grants of €1–3 million where the lead must be an international or regional NGO but consortia including national NGOs and local implementing partners are welcomed — with a published 25% match, a concept-note first stage, and 23 African coastal countries named in one call
trackers.desc: THE LEAD MUST BE INTERNATIONAL. THE PARTNER LIST IS WHERE YOU GET IN — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S MAURITANIA ENTRY COVERS THE TERRESTRIAL LANDSCAPE FUND THAT NAMES THIS ONE AS A PARTNER TRUST FUND, ITS CÔTE D'IVOIRE ENTRY THE BIODIVERSITY HOTSPOT FUND, ITS TANZANIA ENTRY A RAINFOREST FUNDER, AND ITS LIBYA AND BURUNDI ENTRIES A BIRD CONSERVATION HOST. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE CONSORTIUM RULE, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT WELCOMES APPLICATIONS BY CONSORTIA OF NGOs LED BY INTERNATIONAL AND/OR REGIONAL NGOs, AND THAT INCLUDE NATIONAL NGOs OR OTHER LOCAL IMPLEMENTING PARTNERS — AND IT OPERATES THROUGH GRANTS TO NGOs THAT TYPICALLY WORK IN PARTNERSHIPS WITH VARIOUS LOCAL ACTORS. Read the two halves together: a fishers' association or coastal community organisation cannot lead, but the fund expects it to be in the consortium. So the practical move is not to apply — it is to find out which international or regional NGO is preparing a bid on your coast and to be named in it on terms you set. This file has recorded the alternative repeatedly: the project arrives already designed, and the community is a beneficiary rather than a partner. WHO MAY LEAD, RECORDED WITH ITS INCONSISTENCY: ELIGIBLE APPLICANTS ARE INTERNATIONAL OR REGIONAL NGOs WITH PROVEN EXPERIENCE IN COASTAL AND MARINE CONSERVATION IN THE AREA — THOUGH ANOTHER STATEMENT DESCRIBES FUNDING FOR THE ACTIVITIES OF NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS. The sources differ on whether a national NGO can lead. That is worth asking directly rather than assuming the stricter reading — a large national organisation may have more room than the summary suggests. THE MATCH REQUIREMENT: NGOs MUST PROVIDE MATCH FUNDING OF AT LEAST 25% OF THE TOTAL PROJECT COSTS. A quarter of a one-to-three-million-euro project has to come from somewhere else. That is the number that decides who can realistically lead, and it is the reason the lead is an international NGO. THE GOVERNMENT CONDITION: PROJECTS MUST HAVE THE APPROVAL OF THE APPROPRIATE AUTHORITY OR AUTHORIZED BODY OF THE COUNTRY OR REGION WHERE THE PROJECT IS LOCATED. Your fisheries or environment ministry holds a veto. If a community wants a marine protected area that the ministry is lukewarm about, that approval is the obstacle to work on first — and it is also the leverage point if a community opposes a badly designed one. THE GRANT SIZE AND THE VOLUME PER CALL: GRANTS OF €1–3 MILLION, WITH ONE CALL ANTICIPATING PROJECTS TOTALLING APPROXIMATELY EUR 15 MILLION AND ANOTHER EXPECTING FOUR TO SIX GRANTS WITH A TOTAL VOLUME OF UP TO EUR 12 MILLION. Four to six grants for a whole coastline. The odds are long, and knowing that early is worth more than optimism. THE APPLICATION SHAPE: NO UNSOLICITED PROPOSALS — GRANTS ARE AWARDED ON OPEN CALLS ONLY. EACH CALL DEFINES A STRATEGIC AND GEOGRAPHIC FOCUS ALONG WITH GRANT SIZE AND NUMBER OF GRANTS; CONCEPT NOTES ARE SUBMITTED BEFORE A DEADLINE, AND SHORT-LISTED APPLICANTS ARE THEN ASKED TO ELABORATE FULL PROPOSALS USING A PRESCRIBED TEMPLATE. A CONCEPT NOTE FIRST, which is short. The full proposal is only written by those invited, so the cost of trying is low — and a community partner should ask to see the concept note before it is submitted, because that is the document that fixes who does what. WHAT IT FUNDS: NEWLY ESTABLISHED OR BETTER MANAGED MARINE PROTECTED AREAS OR NETWORKS OF THEM, AS WELL AS OTHER EFFECTIVE AREA-BASED CONSERVATION MEASURES; AND ENHANCED LIVELIHOOD CONDITIONS IN COASTAL COMMUNITIES, INCLUDING SUSTAINABLE LIVELIHOODS IN COMMUNITIES DEPENDENT ON THOSE AREAS AND THEIR BUFFER ZONES. OTHER EFFECTIVE AREA-BASED CONSERVATION MEASURES is the category to reach for. A community's own closed season, sacred reef or customary fishing restriction can qualify as conservation without becoming a state protected area — which is the difference between a community keeping control and losing it. THE PREFERENCE IT STATES: IT FAVORS PROJECTS THAT INTEGRATE MARINE PROTECTION WITH POVERTY REDUCTION, SUSTAINABLE AND EQUITABLE USE OF MARINE RESOURCES, AND COMMUNITY-BASED PROTECTION — AND PROJECTS SHOULD LOOK BEYOND INDIVIDUAL PROTECTED AREAS TO CONSIDER SYSTEMS AND/OR PROMOTE REGIONAL APPROACHES, SHOWING EARLY RESULTS, AND BEING SCALABLE AND TRANSFORMATIVE. COMMUNITY-BASED PROTECTION named as a stated preference. Quote it when a proposed design would exclude fishers from their own grounds: the fund's own criteria favour the opposite. THE AFRICAN COUNTRIES NAMED IN ONE ATLANTIC CALL: MOROCCO, MAURITANIA, SENEGAL, THE GAMBIA, CAPE VERDE, GUINEA-BISSAU, GUINEA, SIERRA LEONE, LIBERIA, CÔTE D'IVOIRE, GHANA, TOGO, BENIN, NIGERIA, CAMEROON, EQUATORIAL GUINEA, GABON, SÃO TOMÉ AND PRÍNCIPE, THE REPUBLIC OF CONGO, THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO, ANGOLA, NAMIBIA AND SOUTH AFRICA. Twenty-three countries in a single call, the whole Atlantic seaboard. If your coast is on that list, the question is which organisation applied and whether your community appeared in it. THE OTHER AFRICAN REGION AND THE CALL HISTORY: IN AFRICA, INITIATIVES TARGET THE ATLANTIC COAST AND WESTERN INDIAN OCEAN, INCLUDING MOZAMBIQUE, TANZANIA, MADAGASCAR AND SOUTH AFRICA — WITH CALLS FOR THE WESTERN INDIAN OCEAN IN 2018, 2020 AND 2021, AFRICA'S ATLANTIC COAST IN 2021, AND ASIA-PACIFIC IN 2023. Africa has had four of the named calls. The pattern suggests African coasts are a recurring rather than occasional focus, which makes preparing a consortium in advance worthwhile. WHY IT EXISTS AND WHO FOUNDED IT: FOUNDED IN 2016 BY A GERMAN FEDERAL MINISTRY IN COOPERATION WITH A DEVELOPMENT BANK AS A RESPONSE TO THE FUNDING GAP FOR MARINE BIODIVERSITY CONSERVATION, IN PARTICULAR WITH A VIEW TO NETWORKS OF MARINE PROTECTED AREAS AND TRANSBOUNDARY CONSERVATION MEASURES. TRANSBOUNDARY is worth noting: a fishery or reef shared with a neighbouring country is a feature here rather than a complication. AND THE CURRENT STATUS: CURRENTLY THERE IS NO OPEN CALL FOR PROPOSALS, WITH APPLICANTS ASKED TO CAREFULLY CONSULT THE GRANT PROGRAMME DOCUMENTS TO SEE IF THEIR PROJECT CONCEPT WILL MEET ALL REQUIREMENTS AND MEASURABLY CONTRIBUTE TO THE PRESCRIBED INDICATORS. Closed at the time of writing. The programme documents stay published between calls, so the requirements can be read and a consortium assembled now rather than in the weeks a call is open. WHO IT SUITS: African coastal communities, fishers' associations and national organisations on the Atlantic seaboard or Western Indian Ocean — as consortium partners rather than lead applicants. CAVEATS: NO UNSOLICITED PROPOSALS, INTERNATIONAL OR REGIONAL LEAD, 25% MATCH, GOVERNMENT APPROVAL REQUIRED, AND NO OPEN CALL AT PRESENT — this is a door you prepare for, not one you knock on today. For the terrestrial equivalent paying a million a year for decades, Mauritania's entry; for the hotspot fund that reaches smaller local organisations, Côte d'Ivoire's entry.

THE WALK-IN HELP DESKS IN THE TOWNSHIPS: HELP DESKS RUN THROUGHOUT THE WEEK AT VARIOUS VENUES, INCLUDING FOUR GENERAL ADVICE HELP DESKS IN FOUR NAMED AREAS — LOCATED IN AREAS WHICH PREDOMINANTLY HOUSE PEOPLE FROM PREVIOUSLY DISADVANTAGED BACKGROUNDS AND CATER TO THE MOST MARGINALISED MEMBERS OF THE COMMUNITY. The desks are in the townships rather than only in the city centre. Deliberately placed where the people are, which removes the transport cost that this file has recorded ending more legal matters than any legal argument. WHY THE SPECIALIST DESKS MATTER: THEY ARE STAFFED BY ATTORNEYS WHO ARE USUALLY EXPERTS IN THEIR FIELD, AND THEY CAN ASSESS AND GIVE ADVICE ON THE MERITS OF A CASE ON THE SPOT — ENSURING MATTERS ARE DEALT WITH AS SPEEDILY AS POSSIBLE. MERITS ASSESSED ON THE SPOT. Knowing within one visit whether a case is worth pursuing saves months, and a negative answer given early is itself worth having. THE WALK-IN REALITY: ITS CITY-CENTRE LOCATION ENSURES IT IS READILY ACCESSIBLE TO ANYBODY WHO MAY NEED ITS SERVICES, AS PUBLIC TRANSPORT IS ALWAYS AVAILABLE — SO IT HAS A NUMBER OF CLIENTS WHO WALK IN OFF THE STREET ON A DAILY BASIS. THE THREE OFFICES AND THEIR CONTACTS: A JOHANNESBURG HEAD OFFICE AT A NAMED CONSTITUTIONAL SITE WITH A PUBLISHED TELEPHONE NUMBER AND EMAIL, A KWAZULU NATAL REGIONAL OFFICE IN DURBAN WITH ITS OWN NUMBER AND EMAIL, AND A WESTERN CAPE REGIONAL OFFICE IN CAPE TOWN WITH ITS OWN NUMBER AND EMAIL. Three cities, each with a direct number and address published. Write to the regional office rather than the head office. THE MATTERS IT COVERS AND THE SCALE: CIVIL LAW MATTERS SUCH AS CHILD LAW, DIVORCES, DOMESTIC VIOLENCE, DECEASED ESTATES, REFUGEE LAW, CONSUMER LAW, WILLS AND HOUSING — WITH ONE OFFICE RECORDING OVER 3,000 CLIENTS CONTACTING IT IN A YEAR, AND WORKSHOPS HELD THROUGHOUT THE YEAR FOR BOTH ATTORNEYS AND COMMUNITIES. Recorded plainly: the named clinic subjects are civil and family matters, not environmental or land-rights litigation. DECEASED ESTATES and WILLS are the land connection that matters most in practice — this file has repeatedly found that families lose land at a death rather than to a company, and this is a free service that addresses exactly that. AND THE WIDER SERVICES IT LISTS: GENERAL LEGAL ASSISTANCE, STRATEGIC IMPACT LITIGATION, PARTNERSHIPS AND CO-OPERATION AGREEMENTS, AND INTERNATIONAL LEGAL NETWORKS AND ADVICE — WITH AN ATTORNEY SIGNUP FORM PUBLISHED FOR LAWYERS WHO WANT TO JOIN THE PANEL. STRATEGIC IMPACT LITIGATION sits alongside the daily clinics, so a matter that outgrows the help desk does not necessarily have to leave. And the attorney signup form is worth passing to any sympathetic lawyer you know — the panel is how the supply of free representation grows. WHO IT SUITS: South African community organisations needing legal help for themselves, and residents facing eviction, estate or documentation problems — with three city offices and township desks. CAVEATS: SOUTH AFRICA ONLY, AND ITS CLINIC SUBJECTS ARE CIVIL, FAMILY, HOUSING AND REFUGEE MATTERS RATHER THAN ENVIRONMENTAL LITIGATION — for a project or permit fight, use it to get your organisation in order and go to the specialist entries. For the activist ecosystem lawyers and the means test, Mauritania's entry; for a named commercial environmental firm, Mozambique's entry.

THE COURT INSTRUCTION, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: WHEN YOU GO TO COURT IT IS EXTREMELY IMPORTANT THAT YOU ARE ABLE TO PROVE TO THE JUDGE OR MAGISTRATE THAT YOU HAVE MADE AN EFFORT TO FIND LEGAL REPRESENTATION — SO MAKE SURE TO REQUEST WRITTEN RESPONSES FROM ALL THE LEGAL CLINICS YOU HAVE APPROACHED. This file has recorded many people turned away and none of them keeping the letter; from here, keep every one. THE FOLLOW-UP ADVICE IT GIVES: FOLLOW UP REGULARLY — EMAIL OR PHONE THEM, OR GO TO THEIR OFFICES IN PERSON AND REQUEST AN UPDATE; PUTTING PRESSURE ON THEM CAN SPEED UP THE PROCESS AND MEAN THAT YOU FIND LEGAL REPRESENTATION FASTER. Unusually blunt for a legal guide: the clinics are overloaded, and the person who keeps arriving in person gets seen. Said plainly rather than politely. THE DISTINCTION IT DRAWS THAT PEOPLE GET WRONG: LEGAL ADVICE IS WHEN A QUALIFIED LAWYER CONSULTS WITH YOU AND ADVISES ON YOUR OPTIONS — BUT THEY ARE NOT YOUR LAWYER AT THAT POINT; ONCE A LAWYER HAS OFFICIALLY TAKEN ON YOUR MATTER YOU BECOME THEIR CLIENT AND THEY CAN GO TO COURT AND REPRESENT YOU. WHO HAS THE RIGHT: EVERYONE, INCLUDING FOREIGN NATIONALS, HAS THE RIGHT TO A LAWYER — AND NON-CITIZENS CAN APPROACH THE LEGAL PRACTICE COUNCIL AND ANY FREE LEGAL CLINICS FOR ASSISTANCE. Migrants and refugees are among the most evicted people recorded in this file and the most often told they have no standing. Stated here as a right, with named bodies to approach. THE CONSTITUTIONAL POINT IT BUILDS ON: THE CONSTITUTION STATES THAT NO PERSON IN THE COUNTRY, INCLUDING FOREIGNERS LIVING THERE, SHOULD BE EVICTED INTO HOMELESSNESS, AND IT IS WITH THIS IN MIND THAT THE COURTS SHOULD ADJUDICATE EVICTION MATTERS. EVICTED INTO HOMELESSNESS is the operative test rather than who holds title. Where the state cannot say where the family will go, the eviction fails on that ground alone — which is why the relocation-camp offer recorded in this file's Mauritania entry gets made. WHEN TO ACT: IF YOU HAVE RECEIVED A NOTICE OF MOTION FOR YOUR EVICTION, SEEK LEGAL REPRESENTATION OR ADVICE AS SOON AS POSSIBLE. THE ANSWERS IT PUBLISHES TO THE COMMONEST LANDLORD TACTICS: IT IS NOT LEGAL FOR A LANDLORD TO CUT OFF YOUR WATER, AND YOU HAVE THE RIGHT TO BASIC AMENITIES INCLUDING WATER; IF DENIED ENTRY TO YOUR HOME YOU CAN CONTACT THE POLICE OR SEEK LEGAL ASSISTANCE TO REGAIN ACCESS; A NOTICE TO VACATE CAN BE APPEALED THROUGH THE RENTAL HOUSING TRIBUNAL OR A LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE; AND NEGOTIATION AFTER A NOTICE OF MOTION IS POSSIBLE, BUT SHOULD BE DONE THROUGH LEGAL REPRESENTATION, WITH ANY AGREEMENT FORMALIZED IN WRITING AND SUBMITTED TO THE COURT. Cutting the water and changing the locks are the two moves that precede most evictions in this file, and both are answered here with what to do the same day. And an agreement reached with a landlord is worth nothing unless it goes into the court file. THE DOWNLOADABLE VERSION: THE COMPLETE GUIDE FOR TENANTS CAN BE DOWNLOADED AND READ ANYWHERE, ON ANY DEVICE, FOR FREE. Downloadable matters where data is expensive: one download in a place with signal, then read and shared in a settlement without it. WHY IT EXISTS AND HOW IT GREW: BUILT IN PARTNERSHIP WITH A CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATION AND A TENANTS' SOCIAL MOVEMENT, IT ORIGINALLY FOCUSED ON ONE PROVINCE FOR LACK OF CAPACITY — THEN FAMILIES CAME TO THE SITE COMPLAINING OF UNLAWFUL EVICTIONS AND INTIMIDATION FROM UNSCRUPULOUS LANDLORDS AND ASKED FOR LEGAL SERVICES IN OTHER PROVINCES; IT NOW COVERS ALL NINE. The users asked and the tool expanded. Worth recording as a model: a directory of who will help, built by a data organisation rather than a law firm, is cheap and any national coalition could build one. AND THE OPEN INVITATION THAT KEEPS IT ALIVE: IF YOU ARE A LAWYER, WHETHER FROM A LAW CLINIC OR ELSEWHERE, THAT PROVIDES FREE OR AFFORDABLE EVICTION SUPPORT AND WOULD LIKE YOUR DETAILS UP ON THE WEBSITE, LET THEM KNOW BY EMAIL — WITH A PUBLISHED CONTACT ADDRESS FOR SUGGESTING A LEGAL SUPPORT OFFICE, AN ADMISSION THAT SOME CATEGORIES ARE STILL EMPTY IN SOME PROVINCES, AND A NOTE THAT RESEARCH INTO NON-GOVERNMENTAL LAW CLINICS IS ONGOING. The gaps are admitted rather than hidden, and anyone can fill them — including a community organisation that knows a local lawyer the database does not. WHO IT SUITS: tenants and communities in this country who need to find a free lawyer near them today — and organisations elsewhere wanting a cheap, copyable model for a national directory of free legal help. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY, AND AN INFORMATION TOOL RATHER THAN A LAWYER — IT STATES ITSELF THAT IT DOES NOT REPLACE LEGAL ADVICE FROM A QUALIFIED LAWYER; SOME CATEGORIES ARE STILL UNPOPULATED IN SOME PROVINCES, AND ITS SCOPE IS TENANCY AND EVICTION RATHER THAN RURAL OR CONSERVATION LAND. For the accredited clinic behind it, Mauritania's entry; for the clearing house that vets clients before referring them free to panel attorneys, this bucket's own earlier entry.

trackers.name: Natural Justice: Lawyers for Communities and the Environment
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an African public-interest law organisation — lawyers and paralegals working with communities facing mining, oil and gas, logging and large infrastructure, combining legal empowerment, community protocols, policy work and litigation. Hubs in Cape Town, Nairobi and Dakar, staff in Madagascar, Botswana and Guinea, and country programmes in Burkina Faso, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Namibia, Nigeria, Senegal and South Africa. It also runs the Environmental Lawyers Collective for Africa and an EIA Process Tracker. WHO IT SUITS: an Indigenous or rural community whose land, water or customary rights are threatened by an extractive or infrastructure project. It takes selected cases and works project-to-project outside its programme countries, so expect an approach-and-assess conversation rather than open intake. IS THERE AN OFFICE NEAR YOU? NO — this is project-to-project country. Natural Justice's 3 hubs are Cape Town, Nairobi and Dakar, with additional staff in Antananarivo, Botswana and Guinea; elsewhere it works across African countries on a project-to-project basis. So you are asking them to take on a project, not walking into an office — approach with a defined case and expect that answer to depend on their current programme. Its team page does list staff and fellows beyond the hub countries. WHAT IT DOES: founded 2007 in Cape Town, it supports communities to know the law, use the law and shape the law — access to land and governance of natural resources, the struggle against harmful extractive and infrastructure developments, traditional knowledge and benefit sharing, community rights within conservation, and climate action. ITS SIGNATURE TOOL IS THE COMMUNITY PROTOCOL — a documented instrument letting a community set out its biological, cultural and spiritual resources, norms and values, and assert existing rights under customary, domestic and international law, aimed squarely at laws and projects developed by government and industry without consultation. Ask for it by name. Contact: 63 Hout Street, Cape Town 8001; +27 21 426 1633; info@naturaljustice.org.

trackers.name: African Environmental Defenders Fund (emergency grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the African Environmental Defenders Fund — an emergency grant fund run by Natural Justice with the International Land Coalition Africa, ICCA Consortium, PACJA, Oxfam Novib, FEMNET and others, giving up to US$5,000 to land and environmental defenders anywhere in Africa who are under threat because of their activism. It can cover the cost of legal representation where a defender is arrested, summoned or prosecuted, plus relocation and other short-term transitional costs. WHO IT SUITS: an individual frontline defender who is a citizen or legal resident of an African country, facing an imminent threat, and not already supported by another body — it is not project or core funding, and routine office and administrative costs are excluded. HOW IT DIFFERS: applications are rolling, by email or helpline, not to a grant round. Natural Justice's own site names Burkina Faso, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Namibia, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa and Botswana as its country programmes, which is where this entry is placed; the fund's stated eligibility is any African country, so apply from elsewhere on the continent too.

trackers.name: Cour des comptes
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Burkina Faso, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: data.gov.bf
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Burkina Faso.

trackers.name: Burkina Faso — Maison de l’Entreprise (eCreation / CEFORE)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the MEBF one-stop CEFORE & eCreation online platform handle company creation, modification & RCCM registration, Burkina Faso. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: Groupement de Gestion Forestière — the only village-level concessionaire
trackers.desc: THERE IS NO ALTERNATIVE VEHICLE. FAO's account of the Projet Aménagement des Forêts Naturelles states that the Groupement Villageois de Gestion Forestière (GGF), sponsored by a Commission villageoise de gestion de terroir or not, is the only concessionaire considered by the State at village scale for forest management — and that groupements can in some cases cover several villages, so a multi-village grouping is expressly possible. The model rests on three stated foundations: participation of the populations (erected as the base principle), economic sustainability and ecological sustainability. THE FUND BEHIND IT: the Fonds d'Aménagement Forestier, established 1987 to relay external financing with a permanent domestic system. Government texts later officially recognised the forest fund and extended it to all forest products across the whole territory — recorded as reducing unfair competition between products from managed and unmanaged zones. That competition problem is the one to understand: without the extension, wood from unmanaged forest undercut wood from managed forest, penalising exactly the communities doing the management work.

trackers.name: Five recognised access routes — and hunting zones put you on equal footing
trackers.desc: THE NATIONAL PROSPECTIVE DOCUMENT LISTS FIVE WAYS COMMUNITIES LAWFULLY ACCESS FOREST RESOURCES: (1) droits d'usage — traditional gathering rights, in both classed and protected forest; (2) concessions to groupements de gestion forestière through management plans, authorising commercial valorisation; (3) partnership agreements between neighbouring populations and hunting-zone concessionaires; (4) village management of hunting zones, which makes rural communities concessionaires on the same footing as private operators; and (5) commercial exploitation in unmanaged zones. Route 4 is the strongest — equal legal footing with commercial operators is rare. HOW A chantier d'aménagement forestier is built, per its cahier des charges: a social component (the UGGF), a conseil de gestion, a comité de contrôle interne, a commission de contrôle, a direction technique and the Fonds d'Aménagement Forestier. NOTE THERE ARE TWO SEPARATE CONTROL BODIES — internal committee and control commission — so where a CAF is failing, those are the named internal remedies before anything external. DOCUMENTS YOU CAN ASK FOR: an annual work plan based on expected receipts and quarterly physical and financial progress reports. BUT CHECK IT EXISTS: newer CAFs in the Centre-Nord were recorded as having neither a technical direction nor monitors yet — the structure on paper is not always the structure on the ground. A noted tension: foresters sometimes repress herders in the forests.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: ORCADE — the first Burkinabè NGO to take on the mining sector, and it explains the mining code to the councillors who have to apply it
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an organisation created in 2001 after a rights-based advocacy workshop in Ghana persuaded participants to set up bodies at home to accompany communities through rights-based advocacy against mining companies. It was the first NGO in Burkina Faso to work on the mining sector and is generally treated as the lead one. WHAT IT DOES THAT A VILLAGE CAN USE: it investigates the causes of conflict between mining companies and neighbouring communities, and its programme staff report that compensation for people who lost the assets and livelihoods taken for mining operations is the recurring grievance — so its research is the documentary base for a compensation claim. It has published a state-of-play study on artisanal and small-scale mining and an assessment of how the new mining code is being implemented. AND THE PART THAT IS UNUSUAL AND WORTH ASKING FOR: ORCADE runs workshops for local elected officials on the mining code and its implementing decrees, including the fund financed by levies on mining companies and placed at the disposal of communes — because a mayor who does not know the fund exists cannot claim it for your village. If your council is the body that should be defending you and does not understand the instrument, this is who trains it. ORCADE sits on the steering committee of the extractive industries transparency initiative in Burkina Faso, leads its civil society capacity-building working group, and has held the national chair of Publish What You Pay. 09 BP 675 Ouagadougou 09; secretariat@orcade.org. WHO IT SUITS: communities beside industrial or artisanal gold operations, and local councils in mining communes. CAVEATS: advocacy, research and training — not litigation, and no legal service or intake route was found; the security situation across much of Burkina Faso constrains field access, and published contact numbers vary between listings.

trackers.name: MBDHP — free legal clinics run by a human rights movement with sections in all 45 provinces and committees down to village level
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Mouvement Burkinabè des Droits de l'Homme et des Peuples, founded in February 1989, and structurally the most far-reaching organisation in this country's entry list: sections in all 45 provinces, around a hundred sub-sections at department level, and sectoral and VILLAGE committees as a third tier. That structure is the point — in a country where the practical barriers to justice are ignorance, poverty, social and cultural obstacles and an under-resourced justice ministry, an organisation with a committee in the village is reachable in a way a Ouagadougou office is not. WHAT IT PROVIDES: it operates boutiques de droit — legal clinics — in a number of localities including Ouagadougou, Kongoussi, Tenkodogo, Dédougou, Banfora and Yako, and it is the UN refugee agency's partner for legal assistance in the country. ITS SERVICES ARE STATED TO BE FREE. WHAT TO KNOW BEFORE YOU GO: the documented legal-aid partnership is framed around deprivation of liberty and the situation of displaced and stateless people rather than land or environmental cases, so ask directly whether the local section will take a land dispute or a compensation claim — the structure is there, the mandate is broad (promoting and protecting citizens' rights and freedoms), but the advertised specialism is not land. Burkina Faso also maintains a state fonds d'aide juridique for the poor, which civil society including MBDHP has pressed to make accessible; ask about it if a case needs filing fees. WHO IT SUITS: Burkinabè households and communities — including in mining and displacement-affected areas — who need a lawyer and cannot pay for one. CAVEATS: a general human rights movement, not an environmental or land law specialist — for mining-sector work Burkina Faso's ORCADE entry is the complement; and the security situation across much of the country constrains what any organisation can reach.

trackers.name: FIAN Burkina Faso — took the failures of the rural land law to the UN review, and documents the attestation route smallholders are supposed to use
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Burkinabè section of the international right-to-food organisation, working on land and food rights, which has submitted evidence to the United Nations Universal Periodic Review on the difficulties of securing rural land possession in Burkina Faso — taking a domestic implementation failure to an international forum is a route most communities do not know exists, and this is an organisation that has used it. THE INSTRUMENT IT DOCUMENTS, WHICH ANY BURKINABÈ FARMER SHOULD ASK ABOUT: under the rural land law of 2009 customary rights are officially recognised and can be formalised through an Attestation de Possession Foncière Rurale (APFR), issued by the rural land service of your own commune, land management having been transferred to the rural communes. Any rural landholder may request recognition of their possession, individually OR COLLECTIVELY; the attestation passes by inheritance and may be transferred, with transfers entered in the commune's rural land transactions register. Loans of land can also be registered — a verbal loan is declared to the village land commission and written down on a form supplied by the commune, which is the protection for someone farming land they do not own. Communities may also adopt local land charters, validated by deliberation of the municipal council. WHAT FIAN SAYS IS WRONG, and it is what to check before relying on any of it: implementation requires rural land services staffed and equipped in every commune, and the material, financial and human means committed have been very weak, so the law is only partly applied. Reporting from communes near the capital bears that out — one had issued no attestations at all and was instead selling amicable transfer deeds by the hectare, another applied the law in only nine of its 26 villages. Ask whether your commune has a functioning rural land service before assuming the route is open. WHO IT SUITS: Burkinabè smallholders, women and collective landholders seeking documented possession, and communities losing land to real-estate expansion. CAVEATS: an advocacy and documentation organisation, not a law firm or a land agency; the security situation constrains fieldwork across much of the country; for mining-affected communities Burkina's ORCADE entry is the other route, and for free legal help its MBDHP entry.

trackers.name: NATUDEV and Burkina Faso's APACs — 53,858 community-conserved sites identified, 951 documented, and the documentation is the defence
trackers.desc: WHAT TO DOCUMENT, AND WHY IT COSTS ALMOST NOTHING: an APAC — aire ou territoire du patrimoine autochtone et communautaire, a “territory of life” — is land a community ALREADY conserves by custom: village forests, sacred woods, sacred water points, pastoral areas. You are not buying, leasing or transferring anything; you are getting what you already protect INVENTORIED, MAPPED AND WRITTEN DOWN so it can be defended when someone else wants it. THE ORGANISATION: Association Nature et Développement (NATUDEV) started the APAC dynamic in Burkina Faso in 2016 and is described as the reference NGO for it; the Burkina section of the global APAC consortium supports communities through inventories, mapping, studies, and the installation of boundary signage and PERIMETER FIREBREAK TRACKS to reduce bush-fire risk. THE SCALE, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT TO PUT IN FRONT OF ANY AUTHORITY: 53,858 sites identified covering 721,527.98 hectares, of which 951 are documented — 69 village forests, 89 communal pastoral spaces, 121 sacred water points and 672 sacred woods. Named examples include the Kalwaka sacred wood (82 ha) in Centre-Ouest and the village conservation zones of Sadpenga (226 ha) and Saro (861 ha). THE THREATS IT IS AGAINST are the ones this file records everywhere: artisanal gold mining, real-estate promotion, extensive agriculture, charcoal burning, poaching and bush fires. NATUDEV has also commissioned a LEGAL STUDY on APACs to support advocacy for their formal legal recognition — which is the honest state of play. WHO IT SUITS: Burkinabè villages with a sacred wood, pasture or water point under pressure, and communities anywhere wanting a no-cost first step toward defending customary conservation. CAVEATS: APAC STATUS IS NOT YET A LEGAL TITLE IN BURKINA FASO — recognition is being advocated for, so documentation gives you evidence and visibility rather than enforceable ownership; and the security situation limits fieldwork in much of the country. For an attestation of possession, Burkina's FIAN entry; for mining communities, ORCADE; for free legal help, MBDHP.

trackers.name: Burkina Faso's Fonds d'Assistance Judiciaire — 27 commissions in the high courts, an UNSTAMPED written request, and you may apply before, during OR AFTER the trial
trackers.desc: WHERE TO APPLY: under décret n°2016-185/PRES/PM/MJDHPC/MINEFID of 11 April 2016, assistance judiciaire is the benefit granted to people who, because their resources are insufficient, cannot exercise their rights in court — EITHER AS CLAIMANT OR AS DEFENDANT; the FONDS D'ASSISTANCE JUDICIAIRE (FAJ), a public establishment created in 2016, pays. Burkinabè law makes justice itself free — what costs money is the advocate, the bailiff and the expert, and that is exactly what the FAJ covers. THE PROCEDURE, STATED EXACTLY, AND IT IS THE CLEAREST IN THIS FILE: address a WRITTEN, UNSTAMPED request (demande écrite non timbrée) to the president of the commission d'assistance judiciaire installed at the Tribunal de Grande Instance OF YOUR PLACE OF RESIDENCE. Unstamped means you do not need to buy a fiscal stamp to ask for help — the commonest way a poor applicant is turned back at a counter. AND THE TIMING RULE IS THE MOST USEFUL SENTENCE HERE: the request may be made BEFORE, DURING OR AFTER the trial — the last covering enforcement measures. So a judgment you cannot afford to ENFORCE is still within reach; most people assume the moment has passed. WHAT YOU GET: if TOTAL, all costs occasioned by the trial are covered, including the entirety of advocate's fees; if PARTIAL, the decision fixes the state's contributory share. WHO QUALIFIES: physical persons of Burkinabè OR FOREIGN nationality (subject to reciprocity), with certain categories entitled as of right on request — including children who are victims of trafficking or in conflict with the law, unassisted children and children of indigent parents, and victims of attacks on life or bodily integrity including acts of torture by state agents in the exercise of their functions.
