COVERAGE: the Fund is operational through 27 commissions d'assistance judiciaire sitting at the seats of the Tribunaux de Grande Instance across the territory, and it trains civil society organisations on the mechanism precisely because they are in direct contact with people on the ground. WHO IT SUITS: Burkinabè and foreign residents who cannot pay an advocate, bailiff or expert in a land, compensation or mining dispute. CAVEATS: A STATE FUND with an indigence assessment, and the security situation restricts access to several regions. For mining communities, Burkina's ORCADE entry; for free legal clinics, MBDHP; for attestations of rural possession, FIAN; for community-conserved areas, NATUDEV.

trackers.name: NATURAMA, Tiipaalga, Terre Verte and CERDE — Burkina Faso's nature foundation, the village agroforestry associations with named contacts, and an environmental-law research centre
trackers.desc: THE FOUNDATION, THE VILLAGE MODEL AND THE LAW CENTRE: NATURAMA — FONDATION DES AMIS DE LA NATURE (naturama.bf) works on RESTORATION OF DEGRADED LAND AND PROTECTION OF BIODIVERSITY IN BURKINA FASO, with named partners including a German bird and nature conservation league, a Swiss ornithological station and a German development agency. WHAT IT ACTUALLY PUTS ON THE GROUND: at the village of SILEMBA it implements A FENCED ONE-HECTARE MARKET-GARDEN PERIMETER WORKED BY 25 WOMEN PRODUCERS, and it runs MISE EN DÉFENS (MED) SITES, under a project for the small green wings of the Sahel, alongside a model-villages approach. A fenced hectare worked by twenty-five named women is the smallest unit of protected land in this file that pays for itself. Ask for the perimeter AND the fence — a mise en défens without a fence is a hope. ASSOCIATION TIIPAALGA, with a named coordinator, runs THE IMPLEMENTATION AND PROMOTION OF A VILLAGE MODEL OF SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL DEVELOPMENT IN NORTHERN BURKINA FASO, which SINCE 2016 HAS ENABLED MORE THAN FORTY WOMEN TO TAKE OWNERSHIP OF JARDINS NUTRITIFS in the Centre-Nord region. TERRE VERTE'S INTER-VILLAGE ASSOCIATION TIPWEOGO, east of GOURCY, with a named contact and email, is establishing an AGRO-SYLVO-PASTORAL BOCAGE SYSTEM ACROSS FIFTEEN ASSOCIATED VILLAGES — Bascorma, Bèda, Danaoua, Kalcé, Kindibo, Lèbenga, Ramessé, Raoundé, Rasko, Ridimbo, Roba, Toémigo, Tougo, Ziré and Zondoma. Fifteen villages in one association is the scale at which a rural bloc becomes hard to ignore, and the model is a hedged, enclosed landscape — which means boundaries that are physically visible on the ground. Also named: ASSOCIATION TIND YALGÉ at BOUSSÉ with a named president and mobile number, supporting agriculture, livestock, beekeeping and youth training in the villages of the Kourwego and a member of a national organic agriculture council; and the FONDATION NATURE ET VIE at OUAGADOUGOU. AND THE ONE TO KNOW BEFORE A DISPUTE: CERDE — THE CENTRE D'ÉTUDES ET DE RECHERCHES SUR LE DROIT DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT — a Burkinabè environmental-law study and research centre, recorded as a partner on participatory management of sustainable development in the periphery of the PONASI protected-area landscape. An environmental-law research centre inside your own country is who reads the decree before you sign anything. Burkina Faso has one; most countries in this file do not. Recorded results from assisted natural regeneration of village forests in Burkina Faso include 225 HECTARES PRESERVED while generating income for rural communities. WHO IT SUITS: Burkinabè villages restoring degraded land, women's producer groups, and communities on the edge of a protected area. CAVEATS: SMALL ASSOCIATIONS operating under a difficult security situation. For 53,858 hectares of community-conserved APACs, Burkina Faso's NATUDEV entry; for the first NGO to take on the mining sector, ORCADE; for free legal clinics, MBDHP; for the rural land law failures taken up formally, FIAN Burkina Faso.

trackers.name: SPONG — Burkina Faso's national NGO umbrella since 1974, with an ethics committee, a stated credibility label, and a member holding the civil society seat on the national water council
trackers.desc: THE ETHICS COMMITTEE AND THE SEAT ON THE WATER COUNCIL: THE SECRÉTARIAT PERMANENT DES ORGANISATIONS NON GOUVERNEMENTALES (SPONG, spong.bf) WAS CREATED ON 30 OCTOBER 1974 AND IS THE FIRST NATIONAL FAÎTIÈRE — UMBRELLA — OF NGOs, DEVELOPMENT ASSOCIATIONS AND FOUNDATIONS IN BURKINA FASO, born in the context of THE GREAT SAHELIAN DROUGHT OF THE 1970s, FACED WITH THE NECESSITY OF BETTER COORDINATING HUMANITARIAN AND DEVELOPMENT ACTION. IT BEGAN WITH 17 NGOs AND NOW FEDERATES SOME 329 MEMBER ORGANISATIONS, NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL, including foundations, research and training centres, youth movements and thematic networks, at 01 BP 131 OUAGADOUGOU 01, tel 00 226 25 47 35 66, with named staff. Seventeen organisations became three hundred and twenty-nine. Different sources give 165, 277, 319 and 329 for different years — treat the number as a range and ask SPONG for the current count and the member list, because that list is the answer to who is actually operating in your province. THE TWO THINGS THAT MAKE IT A RESOURCE RATHER THAN A DIRECTORY. FIRST: IT DESCRIBES ITSELF AS A LABEL DE CRÉDIBILITÉ FOR BURKINABÈ NGOs AND DEVELOPMENT ASSOCIATIONS, AND IS RECORDED AS THE BODY THAT CREDIBILISES THEM. Membership of SPONG is a credential. If an organisation approaches your village offering to represent it, ask whether it is a SPONG member — and if you are forming one, joining is how you become legible to the state and to funders at the same time. SECOND: ITS STATUTORY AND FUNCTIONAL ORGANS ARE AN ANNUAL GENERAL ASSEMBLY, A CONSEIL D'ADMINISTRATION, A COORDINATION UNIT — AND A COMITÉ D'ÉTHIQUE. An ethics committee inside the umbrella is a place to take a complaint about a member organisation. That is rare in this file: almost everywhere else, a community that has been badly treated by an NGO has nowhere to go. Ask what the committee can hear and who sits on it before you need it. WHAT IT IS FOR, IN ITS OWN TERMS: TO PROVIDE A FRAMEWORK OF CONCERTATION ALLOWING CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS TO KNOW ONE ANOTHER, TO ACT IN THE FIELD WITH MORE COHERENCE AND TO GO TOGETHER INTO DIALOGUE WITH THE STATE AND THE TECHNICAL AND FINANCIAL PARTNERS; TO ANIMATE AND FAVOUR DIALOGUE BETWEEN CIVIL SOCIETY, THE STATE AND THOSE PARTNERS; AND TO CARRY PROXIMITY ASSISTANCE TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES THROUGH THE PROJECTS AND PROGRAMMES IMPLEMENTED BY ITS MEMBERS. Going together into dialogue with the state is the function. One village association arriving alone at a ministry is a petitioner; the same association arriving inside a 329-member platform is a sector. AND THE SEAT WORTH KNOWING ABOUT: A NAMED PERSON LISTED THROUGH SPONG IS EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR OF NATURAMA AND THE REPRESENTATIVE OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS ON THE CONSEIL NATIONAL DE L'EAU, AS WELL AS A MEMBER OF THE NATIONAL WATER PARTNERSHIP AND OF A BASIN STAKEHOLDERS' FORUM. Civil society holds a designated seat on Burkina Faso's national water council, and it is held by the head of a conservation NGO. If your problem is a dam, an irrigation scheme, a borehole or a polluted watercourse, that seat is the shortest route from your village to the national body — and the person holding it already runs an organisation that works on nature. SPONG is ENGAGED IN THE PRINCIPAL NATIONAL PLANNING PROCESSES, CONTRIBUTING TO THE DESIGN AND REVISION OF MAJOR STRATEGIC DOCUMENTS AND SECTORAL POLICIES, and belongs to REGIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL NETWORKS INCLUDING A WEST AND CENTRAL AFRICAN NGO PLATFORM NETWORK AND A SAHEL DESERTIFICATION NETWORK. Its members' recognised competences span health, education, water and sanitation, sustainable agriculture, environment, humanitarian action, governance, human rights and social inclusion. Ask the umbrella for a member with the competence you need rather than searching for one yourself — that is what a concertation framework is for. WHO IT SUITS: Burkinabè associations seeking credibility, a complaint route, a partner with specific competence, or a way into national water policy. CAVEATS: AN UMBRELLA AND CONCERTATION BODY, not a funder or a litigator; confirm current membership figures. For the first Burkinabè NGO to take on the mining sector, ORCADE; for free legal clinics with sections in all the provinces, MBDHP; for 53,858 community-conserved sites identified, NATUDEV and the APACs entry; for the fenced hectare worked by 25 women, NATURAMA and Tiipaalga; for 27 commissions in the high courts, the Fonds d'Assistance Judiciaire entry.

trackers.name: Both ENDS, Amsterdam — the organisation that co-founds and connects small grants funds for 500+ partners — where recipients always decide themselves what the money is spent on, and the same funds can move fast enough to get a threatened defender to safety
trackers.desc: YOU DECIDE WHAT THE MONEY IS SPENT ON — RECIPIENT ORGANISATIONS ALWAYS DECIDE FOR THEMSELVES WHAT THEY SPEND THE MONEY ON. One sentence, and it separates this whole category of funding from the rest of this file. Almost every grant recorded here arrives attached to a workplan written months earlier and a budget line that cannot be moved when the situation changes. Unrestricted money is what lets a community pay a lawyer in March when the plan said trees in June — and when you are comparing offers, this is the question to ask first. WHY THESE FUNDS EXIST, STATED PLAINLY: SMALL GRANTS FUNDS OFFER AN EFFECTIVE, ALTERNATIVE WAY TO CHANNEL BIG MONEY FROM LARGE DONORS AND FUNDS TO LOCAL GROUPS AND ORGANISATIONS THAT ARE STRIVING FOR A SUSTAINABLE AND JUST SOCIETY — POWERFUL ALTERNATIVE FINANCING MECHANISMS FOR INITIATIVES STEMMING FROM A GRASS ROOT LEVEL, AND FOR CITIZENS' INITIATIVES IN AREAS THAT ARE GETTING LESS AND LESS CONVENTIONAL FUNDING. Big donors cannot give $5,000 to a village committee; the paperwork costs more than the grant. A small grants fund is the intermediary built to solve exactly that, which is why the money a community can actually reach usually arrives through one. WHAT THEY GIVE BESIDES MONEY: SMALL GRANTS FUNDS NOT ONLY PROVIDE FINANCING, BUT ALSO SHARE INFORMATION AND KNOWLEDGE, HELP BUILD NETWORKS AND CONDUCT JOINT LOBBY ACTIVITIES. JOINT LOBBY ACTIVITIES is the underused half. A fund with fifty grantees in your country can put a joint position to a ministry that no single grantee could — ask yours whether it does, and whether your issue can be on the list. THE EMERGENCY CAPACITY, WHICH IS WHY THIS BELONGS BESIDE THE PROTECTION ENTRIES IN THIS FILE: SMALL GRANTS FUNDS CAN RESPOND PROMPTLY AND EFFECTIVELY TO CRISES, FOR EXAMPLE WHERE ENVIRONMENTAL AND HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS COME UNDER THREAT — WITH SMALL AMOUNTS OF MONEY, THESE PEOPLE CAN QUICKLY BE BROUGHT TO SAFETY. A fund you already have a relationship with is faster than an emergency fund you have never met. That is an argument for taking a small grant before you need one — the relationship is the asset, not the amount. THE ORGANISATION ITSELF: IT ENVISIONS AN ENVIRONMENTALLY JUST WORLD IN WHICH PEOPLE AND ECOSYSTEMS THRIVE AND ALL PEOPLE CAN LIVE IN DIGNITY — IT STRENGTHENS AND CONNECTS CIVIL SOCIETY ACTORS GLOBALLY AND COLLABORATES WITH MORE THAN 500 PARTNER ORGANISATIONS WORLDWIDE. ITS ROLE WITH THE FUNDS, AND WHY IT IS WORTH APPROACHING RATHER THAN THE FUNDS ALONE: IT IS THE CO-FOUNDER OF A NUMBER OF SMALL GRANTS FUNDS AND WORKS CLOSELY WITH FUNDS THAT FOCUS ON ENVIRONMENTAL AND HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS — THEIR EXPERIENCE HAS TAUGHT THEM THESE FUNDS ARE INDISPENSABLE IN GETTING DONATED MONEY TO THE RIGHT PLACE AND IN GENERATING MAXIMUM IMPACT WITH MINIMUM RESOURCES; AND THEY HELP THESE FUNDS DELIVER ON THEIR COMMITMENT OF OFFERING PRO-POOR SUPPORT IN AN INCLUSIVE AND PARTICIPATORY MANNER. An organisation that connects rather than competes. For a community that does not know which of the dozen funds in this file fits its situation, a connector with 500 partners is a better first letter than a guess at a funder. THE NAMED ALLIANCE AND ITS MEMBER FUNDS, WHICH IS THE MAP OF WHERE TO LOOK: A GLOBAL ALLIANCE FOR GREEN AND GENDER ACTION — A STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIP OF A CENTRAL AMERICAN WOMEN'S FUND, THIS ORGANISATION AND A NAMED WOMEN'S FUND, WITH A NETHERLANDS MINISTRY — WORKING WITH VARIOUS WOMEN'S AND ENVIRONMENTAL SMALL GRANTS FUNDS INCLUDING A GLOBAL GREENGRANTS FUND, A SOUTH ASIA WOMEN'S FUND AND A GLOBAL URGENT ACTION FUND. GREEN AND GENDER together in one alliance. A women's group defending land can apply as either, and the alliance exists precisely because those two categories of funder used to send applicants back and forth. This file's Global Greengrants and Urgent Action entries are both inside it. THE CLIMATE FINANCE WORK: A THREE-YEAR $562,000 GRANT POSITIONS THIS ORGANISATION AND TWO OTHERS TO ADVOCATE FOR LOCAL COMMUNITIES TO BENEFIT FROM A LARGE CLIMATE FUND — BY STRENGTHENING THE CAPACITIES OF WOMEN'S, INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' AND GRASSROOTS GROUPS, CONNECTING LOCAL VOICES TO THE NATIONAL AND GLOBAL POLICIES AND PROCESSES THAT GOVERN CLIMATE FUNDING. Somebody is paid to argue that the big climate money should reach communities rather than ministries. If a large climate project is being planned over your area, these are the people whose job includes asking who benefits. THE DRYLANDS FINDING, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT FOR PASTORALIST AND FARMING COMMUNITIES: EFFECTIVE LOCAL ACTION BY LAND-USING COMMUNITIES IS AT THE HEART OF ACHIEVING LAND DEGRADATION NEUTRALITY GLOBALLY — HOWEVER, THEIR CONTRIBUTIONS ARE OFTEN NOT WELL RECOGNIZED OR ADEQUATELY SUPPORTED BY GOVERNMENTS AND OTHER AGENCIES. Your government has a land degradation target it reports on. A community already restoring its own land is delivering against that target unrecognised — saying so, in those words, converts your work from a local matter into a national commitment your ministry needs help meeting. AND THE QUESTION IT PUTS TO DONORS: HOW DONORS, FOUNDATIONS AND OTHER FUNDERS CAN BETTER SUPPORT WOMEN-LED INITIATIVES — FOCUSING ON CHALLENGES, COLLABORATION, AND OPPORTUNITIES FOR IMPROVED MATCHMAKING — ALONGSIDE A DEMAND FOR INTERNATIONAL INVESTMENT FRAMEWORKS ALIGNED WITH ECONOMIC JUSTICE, SOCIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY, AND THE NEEDS OF COMMUNITIES WORLDWIDE. WHO IT SUITS: African community organisations that need unrestricted money, or that do not know which fund fits them. CAVEATS: IT IS A CONNECTOR AND CO-FOUNDER OF FUNDS RATHER THAN AN OPEN GRANT WINDOW — approach it to be routed, not to be funded directly. For the $500–$5,000 and $5k–$15k windows, South Africa's Global Greengrants entry; for the three application windows and 72-hour review, Mauritania's rapid-response fund entry; for the fund naming land and environmental groups a priority, Tunisia's embattled-organisation entry.

trackers.name: OCCRP Aleph — a billion searchable records including land registries, company registries and court files — open to activists as well as journalists, free to browse without an account, self-hostable for sensitive work, and with a published warning that your searches are logged
trackers.desc: LAND REGISTRIES AND COMPANY RECORDS, SEARCHABLE, AND ACTIVISTS CAN GET IN — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S BENIN ENTRY COVERS A FOLLOW-THE-MONEY RESEARCH SERVICE AND GUINEA'S COVERS TWO INVESTOR TRACKERS. NEITHER CARRIES A SEARCHABLE ARCHIVE A COMMUNITY ORGANISATION CAN QUERY ITSELF. WHO MAY HAVE IT, AND IT IS THE FIND: ACCESS IS GRANTED ON A CASE-BY-CASE BASIS TO JOURNALISTS AND ACTIVISTS — AND ACCESS TO PROTECTED MATERIALS CAN BE GRANTED TO INVESTIGATIVE JOURNALISTS, ACTIVISTS, OR RESEARCHERS. CIVIL SOCIETY MEMBERS CAN REQUEST ACCESS THROUGH THE WEBSITE, AND EACH REQUEST IS REVIEWED BY A STAFF MEMBER. ACTIVISTS, named alongside journalists in the access rules. A land committee's researcher is inside that category and does not need a press card — which is unusual enough to be worth an application even without a specific case in hand. WHAT IS IN IT, AND ONE ENTRY IN THE LIST MATTERS MORE THAN THE REST: A VAST INDEX OF COMPANY REGISTRIES, SANCTION LISTS, PERSON-OF-INTEREST LISTS, LAND REGISTRY DATA, AIR AND MARITIME REGISTRIES, PROCUREMENT DATABASES, COURT RECORDS AND OFFSHORE LEAKS — MORE THAN A BILLION RECORDS FROM OVER 300 DATASETS ACROSS MORE THAN 180 COUNTRIES. LAND REGISTRY DATA and COURT RECORDS in one searchable place. The title on the parcel next to yours, the company that holds it, and any case it has been in — this file has recorded communities paying lawyers to establish exactly that, and it may be one search away. THE TIERED ACCESS, STATED PLAINLY SO YOU KNOW WHAT COSTS NOTHING: SOME DATASETS ARE RESTRICTED TO A FEW VETTED REPORTERS AND OTHERS ARE AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC DIRECTLY ON THE WEBSITE WITHOUT SIGNING UP. NO ACCOUNT IS NECESSARY TO BROWSE — BUT EXPORTING RESULTS OR CREATING RESEARCH SPACES REQUIRES A FREE ACCOUNT, WHICH REQUIRES EVIDENCE OF RELEVANT PREVIOUS WORK, THE NAME OF THE ORGANIZATION YOU ARE AFFILIATED WITH, AND YOUR ROLE THERE. Browse first, apply later. Anyone can search the public layer today; the account is only needed to export or collaborate — and EVIDENCE OF PREVIOUS WORK is where a published report, a filed complaint or a community study earns its second use. THE CROSS-REFERENCING FEATURE, WHICH IS THE ONE TO LEARN: USERS CAN UPLOAD THEIR OWN DOCUMENTS — SUCH AS FREEDOM OF INFORMATION RECORDS OR LEAKS — AND CROSS-REFERENCE THEM AGAINST THE ENTIRE CORPUS TO UNCOVER HIDDEN LINKS. Your own documents, checked against a billion records at once. A list of names from a compensation register or a concession notice, uploaded, may surface the company behind them without you knowing what to look for. AND THE OWNERSHIP CLAUSE ON WHAT YOU UPLOAD: YOU RETAIN CONTROL OVER YOUR UPLOADED DATA AND CAN DECIDE WHO CAN ACCESS IT — OR KEEP SUCH DOCUMENTS IN YOUR OWN PRIVATE SPACE. THE REGIONAL ARCHIVE FOR NORTH AFRICA: A REGIONAL ARCHIVE MAKES MILLIONS OF RECORDS AVAILABLE IN ARABIC — GOVERNMENT JOURNALS AND DATA ON COMPANY OWNERSHIP AND PROCUREMENT FROM ALGERIA, EGYPT, LIBYA, MOROCCO AND TUNISIA AMONG OTHERS — WITH THE SOFTWARE ITSELF TRANSLATED INTO ARABIC AND A PUBLISHED CONTACT FOR ACCESS. THE OPERATIONAL SECURITY WARNING, AND IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT PRACTICAL LINE HERE: YOUR SEARCH QUERIES ARE LOGGED ON THE ORGANISATION'S SERVERS — IF INVESTIGATING ENTITIES THAT MIGHT MONITOR THEIR OWN EXPOSURE, YOUR SEARCH PATTERN COULD REVEAL YOUR INTEREST. CONSIDER WHAT QUERIES YOU RUN AND WHEN, AND USE THE CROSS-REFERENCING FEATURE TO BATCH-COMPARE YOUR DATA RATHER THAN RUNNING INDIVIDUAL NAME SEARCHES. Searching for a powerful man by name, repeatedly, is itself a signal. Batch your queries instead of typing them one at a time, and decide as a group who does the searching — this file's digital-security entries under Morocco cover the rest. THE SELF-HOSTED OPTION FOR SENSITIVE WORK: THE OPEN-SOURCE VERSION CAN BE RUN ON YOUR OWN INFRASTRUCTURE — IT IS FULLY OPEN SOURCE AND SELF-HOSTABLE. THE VERIFICATION RULE THE ORGANISATION STATES ITSELF: THE DATA COMES FROM VARIOUS SOURCES AND ANY FINDINGS BASED ON IT MUST BE INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED — LEAKED DATASETS BY NATURE ARE NOT ALWAYS COMPLETE, AND ARE THUS IMPERFECT SOURCES. Never put a finding from here into a submission without a primary document behind it. A name in a leak is a lead, not evidence — and a wrong accusation costs a community more than silence would have. WHERE THE DATA COMES FROM: LEAKED OR HACKED DATASETS ARE INCLUDED, EACH UNDERGOING AN ETHICAL REVIEW TO DETERMINE PUBLIC INTEREST — AND THE RESEARCH AND DATA TEAM COLLABORATES WITH LOCAL PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS TO GATHER COMPANY REGISTRIES AND GOVERNMENT FILINGS. LOCAL PARTNERS SUPPLY THE REGISTRIES. If your country's company register is not in there, a national organisation can offer to help put it there — which turns your own government's records into a permanent public resource. THE TRAINING AND THE PRICE NOTE, RECORDED AS FOUND: VIRTUAL TRAINING SESSIONS ON ADVANCED FEATURES ARE OFFERED REGULARLY AND A COMMUNITY FORUM EXISTS — AND THE UPDATED PLATFORM WILL BE FREE FOR NON-PROFIT JOURNALISM AND AT-COST FOR OTHER PUBLIC INTEREST GROUPS. Check the current terms before planning around free access; the model has been changing. WHO IT SUITS: African community organisations and their researchers trying to establish who owns the land, the company or the concession beside them. CAVEATS: ACCOUNTS REQUIRE EVIDENCE OF PRIOR WORK, SOME DATA IS RESTRICTED, FINDINGS MUST BE VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, AND YOUR SEARCHES ARE LOGGED. For research done for you on request, Benin's entry; for the two investor trackers, Guinea's entry; for the free digital-security helpline, Morocco's entry.

trackers.name: Environmental Paper Network (EPN) — a 350-organisation coalition against pulp, paper and biomass whose regional working groups are joined by emailing a named staff member — with a common vision document demanding community ownership that a company can be asked to sign
trackers.desc: THE WORKING GROUP PUBLISHES AN EMAIL ADDRESS. THAT IS THE WHOLE JOINING PROCESS — adjacency and scope declared first: THIS FILE'S BURUNDI ENTRY COVERS THE FOREST FINANCE DATABASE THAT TRACKS PULP AND PAPER CREDIT FLOWS, ITS ANGOLA ENTRY THE COMMERCIAL BANK CAMPAIGNING ORGANISATION, AND ITS SOMALIA ENTRY THE FOREST NETWORK WITH NATIONALLY-OWNED MEMBERS. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. AND THE HONEST LIMIT: THE NETWORK'S OWN REGIONAL PAGES NAME SOUTH AMERICA, NORTH AMERICA, ASIA AND EUROPE — AFRICA IS NOT A NAMED REGION. IT IS FILED HERE FOR THE PLANTATION AND BIOMASS EXPANSION AFRICAN COMMUNITIES ALREADY FACE, AND FOR THE JOINING ROUTE. THE JOINING ROUTE, WHICH IS THE FIND: EACH REGIONAL WORKING GROUP PUBLISHES A NAMED STAFF MEMBER'S EMAIL ADDRESS TO JOIN IT — ONE MEETS VIRTUALLY EVERY TWO MONTHS TO SHARE STRATEGIES AND DEVELOP PROJECTS, AND ANOTHER REGION PUBLISHES A SEPARATE NAMED CONTACT FOR ITS COHORTS, COALITIONS AND AD HOC GROUPS. A person's name and address, and a call every two months. No application, no registration, no fee — and an African organisation writing to ask whether a group exists for its region is exactly how one gets started. This file has recorded that the absence of an African chapter is usually nobody's decision; it is that nobody asked. THE SIZE: A COALITION OF OVER 350 NONPROFITS WORKING TO TRANSFORM THE FOREST, PULP AND PAPER, AND BIOMASS INDUSTRIES — FOUNDED IN 2002, TODAY UNITING NEARLY 200 ORGANIZATIONS ACROSS REGIONS. WHAT MEMBERSHIP ACTUALLY GIVES: IT CONNECTS ORGANIZATIONS ACROSS CONTINENTS TO ACT COLLECTIVELY, AND SHARES RESEARCH, TOOLS AND INTELLIGENCE TO STRENGTHEN CAMPAIGNS. INTELLIGENCE, named as something shared between members. A community facing a pulp company usually knows only what that company says locally; a network member learns what the same company did in three other countries and what stopped it. THE COMMON VISION DOCUMENT AND ITS FIRST DEMAND, WHICH IS THE ONE TO PUT TO A COMPANY: PROMOTE COMMUNITY-OWNERSHIP, WORKER-OWNERSHIP AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF PAPER MANUFACTURING FACILITIES SCALED APPROPRIATELY FOR LOCAL COMMUNITIES, AND A DIVERSITY OF SMALL- AND MEDIUM-SIZED ENTERPRISES IN THE PAPER SECTOR; AND RESPECT AND SUPPORT LOCAL ECONOMIES ON THE BASIS OF A LONG-TERM SOCIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL VISION BUILT WITH LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND BUSINESSES. SCALED APPROPRIATELY FOR LOCAL COMMUNITIES is the alternative to a single vast mill, and it is written down and endorsed by hundreds of organisations. A community is not obliged to argue only against the project; it can table a signed industry vision describing what it would accept instead. THE SOURCING DEMANDS IN THE SAME DOCUMENT: END SOURCING OF FIBRE FROM UNKNOWN AND ILLEGAL SOURCES; END THE USE OF FIBRE FROM SUPPLIERS ASSOCIATED WITH LOSS OF ENDANGERED FORESTS AND HIGH CONSERVATION VALUE FORESTS, ECOSYSTEMS AND HABITATS; END THE USE OF FIBRE ASSOCIATED WITH CONVERSION OF NATURAL FORESTS OR OTHER HIGH CONSERVATION VALUE ECOSYSTEMS INTO PLANTATIONS FOR PAPER FIBRE; AND END THE USE OF FIBRE ASSOCIATED WITH LOSS OR DEGRADATION OF PEATLANDS AND HIGH CARBON STOCK FORESTS. CONVERSION OF NATURAL FORESTS INTO PLANTATIONS, named as the thing to end. That is the exact operation this file has recorded arriving in African forest districts under the language of reforestation — a plantation replacing a forest is a conversion, not a restoration, and here is the industry-facing standard that says so. THE PRECAUTIONARY DEMAND MEMBERS ENDORSE: THEY CALL UPON THE INDUSTRY TO ADOPT THE PRECAUTIONARY PRINCIPLE WITH REGARD TO USE OF NATURAL RESOURCES AND CHEMICALS THROUGHOUT THE PRODUCTION PROCESS, AND TO REFRAIN FROM ACTIVITIES THAT COULD CAUSE IRREPARABLE HARM TO HUMAN HEALTH AND THE ENVIRONMENT. THE INDUSTRY DESCRIPTION IT PUBLISHES, WHICH IS THE PARAGRAPH TO QUOTE: THE PULP AND PAPER INDUSTRY IS ONE OF THE MOST POLLUTING AND WATER-INTENSIVE INDUSTRIES ON THE PLANET; IT CONSUMES AROUND FOUR PERCENT OF GLOBAL ENERGY AND RELIES HEAVILY ON TOXIC CHEMICALS WHICH POLLUTE RIVERS AND HARM ECOSYSTEMS; AND, PERHAPS MOST STARKLY, IT DISPLACES COMMUNITIES AND DAMAGES LOCAL LIVELIHOODS THROUGH THE EXPANSION OF MONOCULTURE TREE PLANTATIONS. WATER-INTENSIVE, said first. A pulp mill's water draw is the impact that reaches furthest from the fence line and is least often assessed — the same point this file records under the plantation-and-water entries. THE PATTERN IT DOCUMENTS ELSEWHERE, WHICH TRANSFERS DIRECTLY: A MASSIVE NEW PULP MILL ALONGSIDE A DEVELOPMENT-BANK-SUPPORTED STRATEGY TO ACCELERATE EUCALYPTUS PLANTATION EXPANSION, DESCRIBED AS A REPLICATION OF HISTORICAL COLONIAL EXTRACTIVIST MODELS — AND, ELSEWHERE, COMMUNITIES NEAR LARGE PULP COMPLEXES FACING POLLUTION, FOREST DEGRADATION AND CONFLICTS OVER WATER AND LAND, WORSENING AS BIOMASS POWER STATIONS ARE INTEGRATED INTO PULP MILLS — OFTEN PRESENTED AS A RENEWABLE ENERGY SOLUTION, BUT ACTUALLY INTENSIFYING EXTRACTIVISM AND GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSIONS. A DEVELOPMENT BANK SUPPORTING THE PLANTATION STRATEGY WHILE THE MILL IS BUILT. Two arms of the same project, and the bank arm is the one with a complaint mechanism — which this file's Nigeria and Burundi entries supply. AND THE BIOMASS WARNING: a power station burning plantation wood is counted as renewable energy and funded as climate action. If an energy project near you is fuelled by trees, that framing is contested by a 350-organisation coalition, in writing. THE INEQUALITY IT NAMES: IN HIGH-INCOME COUNTRIES PAPER IS OFTEN USED FOR DISPOSABLE PACKAGING THROWN AWAY AFTER A SINGLE USE, WHILE IN LOWER-INCOME REGIONS MANY PEOPLE STILL LACK ESSENTIAL PAPER-BASED GOODS LIKE BOOKS, HYGIENE PRODUCTS AND LEARNING MATERIALS. THE WIN ON RECORD: AFTER A LONG BATTLE, IT BECAME CLEAR THAT A NEW PULP MILL WOULD NOT BE BUILT BY A NAMED EUROPEAN PAPER COMPANY — DESCRIBED AS A SUCCESS STORY OF POPULAR RESISTANCE AGAINST PULP PLANTATIONS AND FOR FOREST CONSERVATION. A mill stopped. Worth reading in full before anyone tells your community that a project of that size cannot be refused. AND THE DEFENDER CASE IT CARRIES: POLICE ATTEMPTED TO FORCIBLY ARREST A NAMED TRADITIONAL HEAD OF A HAMLET WHOSE COMMUNITY HAD FOR YEARS RESISTED ENCROACHMENT ON ITS CUSTOMARY LAND AND THE DEFORESTATION THAT FOLLOWED. A customary leader named and defended internationally within days. That is what network membership buys when the arrests start — and this file's defender-protection entries under Benin and Morocco are the faster routes. WHO IT SUITS: African communities facing a pulp mill, a eucalyptus or acacia plantation, or a biomass power project — and national organisations wanting to open an African working group. CAVEATS: AFRICA IS NOT CURRENTLY A NAMED REGION OF THE NETWORK, AND IT IS A CAMPAIGNING COALITION RATHER THAN A FUNDER OR LEGAL SERVICE — the published emails are the way to ask. For the credit flows behind these companies, Burundi's entry; for the organisation that will feature your project before bankers, Angola's entry; for the forest network whose African members own themselves, Somalia's entry.

trackers.name: Download your own country's checklist of tree species with endemism and conservation status attached — plus a plant-assessment database that records national listings, not only global ones, and a team that will troubleshoot an assessment you have produced yourself
trackers.desc: DOWNLOAD YOUR COUNTRY'S TREE LIST, WITH ENDEMISM AND STATUS ATTACHED — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S SOMALIA ENTRY COVERS THE TREE FUNDER THAT REQUIRES A GLOBAL THREAT LISTING AND NAMES THIS BODY'S ASSESSMENT PROGRAMME; ITS NIGER AND SUDAN ENTRIES THE SPECIES FUNDS; ITS BURUNDI ENTRY THE CONSERVATION EVIDENCE DATABASE; AND A CONSERVATION UNION IS A HOST UNDER MOROCCO AND CAPE VERDE. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE COUNTRY CHECKLIST, WHICH IS THE FIND: ON THE COUNTRY PAGES YOU CAN DOWNLOAD A COUNTRY CHECKLIST WITH ASSOCIATED INFORMATION ON ENDEMISM AND CONSERVATION STATUS — AND ON THE SPECIES PAGES YOU CAN EXPLORE TREE SPECIES DISTRIBUTION, CONSERVATION STATUS (GLOBAL AND NON-GLOBAL) AND CONSERVATION ACTIONS. One download tells you which trees occur in your country, which occur nowhere else, and which are listed as threatened. For a community facing clearance, that is the fastest way to find out whether anything on the ground has a status worth citing — and ENDEMISM is the column that carries weight, because a species found only in your country cannot be replaced by protecting it somewhere else. THE ASSESSMENT DATABASE AND ITS CRUCIAL SCOPE: A GLOBAL DATABASE OF ALL KNOWN CONSERVATION ASSESSMENTS OF PLANTS, CONTAINING GLOBAL, REGIONAL AND NATIONAL ASSESSMENTS — OVER 300,000 ASSESSMENTS REPRESENTING OVER 180,000 TAXA, WITH THE SCOPE OF EACH ASSIGNED AS GLOBAL, NOT GLOBAL OR UNKNOWN, AND OLDER NON-DIGITAL SOURCES BEING ADDED. NATIONAL assessments recorded alongside global ones, and the scope of each is labelled. Read this beside the tree funder filed under Somalia, which accepts a national assessment where no global one exists but demands a public reference: this database is where that reference is found, and the scope label tells you which kind you are holding before you cite it. THE TROUBLESHOOTING OFFER, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: HAVE YOU PRODUCED RED LIST ASSESSMENTS FOR TREES WHICH ARE NOT FEATURED IN THE DATABASE? THE ASSESSMENT TEAM ARE ABLE TO PROVIDE TROUBLESHOOTING SUPPORT FOR TREE CONSERVATION ASSESSMENTS — WITH A CONTACT ROUTE PUBLISHED. They will help you fix an assessment you have already made. A national botanist, a university department or a community organisation that has documented a tree's decline can get that work checked and brought into the record — which is how an unlisted species becomes a listed one, and how the funding gate filed under Somalia opens. THE REASSESSMENT GUIDANCE: GUIDANCE OUTLINING THE STEPS NEEDED TO COMPLETE A REASSESSMENT OF A TREE SPECIES, WHETHER YOU ARE REASSESSING A SINGLE TAXON OR COORDINATING A LARGER REASSESSMENT INITIATIVE. A REASSESSMENT is the route when a species was assessed years ago as secure and the forest has since gone. An out-of-date listing is used against communities as evidence that nothing is at stake; the published steps for correcting it are here. THE PORTAL AND WHAT IT COMBINES: ACCESS TO INFORMATION ON THE WORLD'S NEARLY 60,000 TREE SPECIES, WITH A GLOBAL OVERVIEW OF SUMMARY STATISTICS — LINKING FOUR EXISTING DATABASES, AND WITH A CONSERVATION ACTION TRACKER THAT ENABLES THE MONITORING OF CONSERVATION ACTIONS FOR EACH TREE SPECIES. THE ACTION TRACKER shows what is already being done for a species, and by whom. That is how you find the organisation already working on your tree — or establish that nobody is, which is itself the case for funding. THE TREE DATABASE ITSELF: THE ONLY GLOBAL DATABASE OF ALL KNOWN TREE SPECIES AND THEIR COUNTRY-LEVEL DISTRIBUTIONS, FIRST PUBLISHED IN 2017, CONTINUOUSLY UPDATED — 58,076 TREE SPECIES AT ONE RECORDED DATE, WITH OVER 6,700 GEOGRAPHIC UPDATES IN A SINGLE YEAR REFLECTING FEEDBACK FROM PARTNERS AND TAXONOMIC PROGRESS. Six thousand seven hundred corrections in one year, from partners. The distribution record is editable in practice: if a tree grows in your country and the database does not say so, that is a correction somebody wants. WHAT IT IS MEANT TO BE USED FOR: MONITORING AND MANAGING TREE SPECIES DIVERSITY, FORESTS AND CARBON STOCKS ON A GLOBAL, REGIONAL OR NATIONAL LEVEL — AND IT ENABLES A GAP ANALYSIS TO BE PERFORMED, TO IDENTIFY WHERE CONSERVATION ASSESSMENTS ARE LACKING. A GAP ANALYSIS names the unassessed species in your country. This file's Niger entry records a fund that treats data-deficient species as a priority — the gap analysis produces exactly that list. THE DATA REQUEST ROUTE FOR WHAT IS NOT ONLINE: IF YOU REQUIRE INFORMATION NOT AVAILABLE THROUGH THE ONLINE DOWNLOADS YOU CAN FILL OUT A DATA REQUEST FORM — THE FORM ENABLES ADVICE AND A DETERMINATION OF WHAT DATA WILL BE MOST USEFUL TO YOU AND YOUR PROJECT, AFTER WHICH A MEMBER OF STAFF REVIEWS IT AND FOLLOWS UP BY EMAIL. A person reads the request and advises. Say what the project is rather than only what the dataset is; the form is designed for that. THE FIGURE THEY PUBLISH, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT: 30% — 17,500 — OF TREE SPECIES ARE CURRENTLY AT RISK OF EXTINCTION, MEANING THERE ARE TWICE THE NUMBER OF THREATENED TREE SPECIES GLOBALLY THAN THREATENED MAMMALS, BIRDS, AMPHIBIANS AND REPTILES COMBINED. More threatened trees than all threatened mammals, birds, amphibians and reptiles put together. Conservation attention and money follow animals; that single comparison is the counter, and it is published by the body that counted. THE PROGRESS FIGURE: SINCE 2015 THERE HAS BEEN A FOUR-FOLD INCREASE IN THE NUMBER OF ASSESSMENTS FOR TREE SPECIES PUBLISHED ON A NAMED RED LIST, WITH SEVERAL NEW RED LIST PUBLICATIONS FOR COMPLETE TREE GROUPS AND REGIONAL TREE FLORAS PRODUCED. THE OTHER DATABASES AND THE EXPERTISE DIRECTORY: FOUR GLOBALLY UNIQUE AND PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE DATABASES COVERING PLANT COLLECTIONS, BOTANIC GARDENS, PLANT ASSESSMENTS AND TREE SPECIES — PLUS A DIRECTORY OF EXPERTISE, AND A TOOL LETTING RESEARCHERS AND PRACTITIONERS ACCESS AND SHARE PLANT MATERIAL AND ASSOCIATED DATA, IDENTIFYING AND FLAGGING MATERIAL SUBJECT TO ACCESS AND BENEFIT-SHARING, BIOSAFETY AND TRADE-CONVENTION REGULATIONS. ACCESS AND BENEFIT-SHARING flagged on the material itself. Where a plant from community land has commercial or medicinal value, those are the rules that decide whether the community sees anything from it — and a tool that flags them is where to start checking. AND THE CITATION AND USE TERMS: A PUBLISHED CITATION FORMAT NAMING THE DATABASE, THE ORGANISATION, THE PLACE AND THE DATE ACCESSED, WITH USERS ASKED TO REFER TO A DATA USER AGREEMENT WHEN DOWNLOADING. Cite it properly with the access date. A submission that names its source precisely is far harder to wave away than one that asserts a species is rare. WHO IT SUITS: African communities, botanists and organisations needing to establish what trees grow on land under threat and whether any of them are formally listed. CAVEATS: TREES AND PLANTS ONLY, DATA RATHER THAN FUNDING OR LEGAL HELP, AND COVERAGE DEPENDS ON WHAT HAS BEEN ASSESSED — an unassessed species is not a secure one. For the funder that requires the global listing this database records, Somalia's entry; for the fund that treats data-deficient species as a priority, Niger's entry.

trackers.name: Game Rangers Association of Africa (GRAA) — a ranger association community and government rangers can join, whose accidental death, disability and medical evacuation cover costs $30 per ranger per year — with ranger teams admitted as corporate members and legal support among its published demands
trackers.desc: THIRTY DOLLARS A YEAR COVERS A RANGER'S DEATH AND EVACUATION — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S BURUNDI ENTRY COVERS THE CHARITY THAT FUNDS RANGER TEAMS AND RUNS A CRISIS APPEAL FOR RANGER SALARIES, WITHOUT NAMING THIS ASSOCIATION; ITS SOUTH SUDAN ENTRY THE CONSERVANCY WHOSE RANGERS WENT UNPAID; ITS ZIMBABWE ENTRY THE CO-MANAGEMENT FOUNDATION THAT APPOINTS RANGERS. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE INSURANCE AND ITS PRICE, WHICH IS THE FIND: THROUGH A JOINT INITIATIVE WITH A NAMED INSURANCE BROKER, IT SUPPORTS THE ACCIDENTAL DEATH, DISABILITY AND MEDICAL EVACUATION COVER OF OVER 1,500 — AND IN A LATER FIGURE OVER 3,000 — RANGERS ACROSS AFRICA, COSTING JUST $30 PER RANGER PER YEAR, PROVIDING FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO THE FAMILIES. Thirty dollars. A community conservancy with twenty rangers can cover the lot for six hundred dollars a year, which is within reach of almost every small grant recorded in this file and is the kind of line item a funder will rarely refuse. It is also the difference between a family destitute after a death in service and a family compensated. THE GAP THAT MAKES IT NECESSARY, WITH ITS NUMBERS: 40% OF THOSE SURVEYED WERE NOT COVERED BY HEALTH INSURANCE, 50% HAD NO LIFE INSURANCE AND 60% HAD NO LONG-TERM DISABILITY INSURANCE. Sourced figures to put in a budget justification. Half of Africa's rangers have no life cover while doing a job that involves armed confrontation. WHO CAN JOIN AND HOW, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: PROSPECTIVE MEMBERS CHECK WHICH CATEGORY SUITS THEM AND RETURN A MEMBERSHIP FORM BY EMAIL — WITH A PROFESSIONAL CATEGORY FOR ANY PERSON WHO HAS EARNED THEIR LIVING IN GAME RANGING FOR AT LEAST FIVE CONTINUOUS YEARS, AND A SEPARATE CATEGORY FOR ANY PERSON EARNING THEIR LIVING IN THE PROFESSION WHO DOES NOT YET QUALIFY; FEES ARE IN LINE WITH THE APPLICANT'S CURRENT GRADE OF EMPLOYMENT, WHETHER GAME RANGER OR FIELD RANGER. Fees scaled to the grade of employment, which means a field ranger pays a field ranger's fee. That is the design decision that makes a continental professional association reachable by the lowest-paid people in it — and a form returned by email is the whole application. AND ENTITIES CAN JOIN TOO: RANGER TEAMS AND OTHER ENTITIES CAN JOIN AS A CORPORATE MEMBER AND RECEIVE MEMBERSHIP BENEFITS — AND SUPPORTERS WHO ARE NOT RANGERS CAN JOIN AS A SUPPORTER MEMBER OR VOLUNTEER THEIR SKILLS. A whole team joins at once. A community conservancy's ranger unit can be enrolled as a body rather than person by person, which is the practical route to getting the insurance in place. THE DEMANDS IT PUBLISHES ON BEHALF OF RANGERS: IMPROVEMENT IN SUPPORT STRUCTURES FOR ALL RANGERS INCLUDING GOVERNMENT, COMMUNITY AND PRIVATE SECTOR RANGERS — INCLUDING MEDICAL AND LIFE INSURANCE SCHEMES, LEGAL SUPPORT, TRAUMA RESPONSE FOR MEDICAL EMERGENCIES AND PROFESSIONAL COUNSELLING SERVICES, TO SUPPORT RANGERS AND THEIR FAMILIES. COMMUNITY RANGERS named in the same breath as government ones. A community's own scouts are inside this association's definition, not an informal category outside the profession — and LEGAL SUPPORT is on the list of what they should have, which matters where rangers face prosecution or where their own conduct is in question. THE EMPLOYMENT DEMANDS: THE RIGHTS OF ALL RANGERS TO JOB SECURITY, FAIR REMUNERATION, CAREER DEVELOPMENT AND PROGRESSION AS A WAY TO IMPROVE RESILIENCY AGAINST DEMORALISATION AND CORRUPTION — ALONGSIDE ACTION TO ENHANCE RANGER EMPLOYMENT AND WELFARE CONDITIONS, AND GREATER RECOGNITION FOR THE FAMILIES OF RANGERS. Corruption framed as a consequence of poor pay rather than a character failing. That is the honest version of a problem this file has recorded communities blaming individuals for, and it points at the remedy. THE TRAINING AND KIT IT PROVIDES: IT TRAINS RANGERS IN REMOTE AREA FIRST AID AND PROVIDES THEM WITH FIRST AID KITS TO ENSURE THEY ARE SAFE IN THE FIELD. WHAT THE JOB ACTUALLY INVOLVES, IN ITS OWN DESCRIPTION: RANGE MANAGEMENT, COLLECTION OF RESEARCH DATA, MONITORING, COMBATTING ILLEGAL WILDLIFE TRADE, WILDLIFE CAPTURE, POPULATION MANAGEMENT, FIRE MANAGEMENT, MAINTENANCE, ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION AND IMPORTANTLY WORKING WITH COMMUNITIES. COLLECTION OF RESEARCH DATA and MONITORING are ranger work. A community that employs scouts already has the people who can gather the evidence the funders and courts elsewhere in this file require. HOW THE ROLE IS CHANGING: MORE TIME IS DEVOTED TO SOCIAL ISSUES BROUGHT ABOUT BY HUMAN WILDLIFE CONFLICT AND SYNDICATED POACHING — RANGERS ARE BECOMING AN IMPORTANT INTERFACE BETWEEN NATURAL RESOURCES AND COMMUNITIES THAT DEPEND ON THEM, BRINGING A NEW AND COMPLEX DIMENSION TO THE WORK. The association names the tension honestly: the ranger stands between the community and the resource, and this file has recorded that position turning violent in both directions. Training and support for that interface is what the demands above are asking for. THE CONDITIONS IT DESCRIBES: PATROLS IN RUGGED TERRAIN AND ALL WEATHER, WITH THE RISK OF ENCOUNTERING DANGEROUS ANIMALS, WELL-ARMED POACHING GANGS OR MILITIA GROUPS — AND MARINE PROTECTED AREA RANGERS PROTECT HABITATS THAT PROVIDE SUSTAINABLE RESOURCES FOR MANY IMPOVERISHED COASTAL COMMUNITIES, OFTEN WORKING WHERE PIRATES AND EXTREMIST GROUPS OCCUR. Marine rangers are covered too, which matters for the coastal and fishing communities recorded throughout this file. THE STANDING IT HOLDS: FOUNDED IN 1970, THE OLDEST, LARGEST AND MOST REPRESENTATIVE RANGER ASSOCIATION IN AFRICA, WITH OVER 1,800 MEMBERS SINCE 1970 ACROSS MORE THAN 26 COUNTRIES AND A LATER FIGURE OF OVER 2,500 RANGERS IN 20 COUNTRIES — A MEMBER OF AN INTERNATIONAL RANGER FEDERATION AND A GLOBAL CONSERVATION UNION, WITH RECOGNISED CHAPTERS IN SIX NAMED COUNTRIES. AND THE PROTOCOL THAT BINDS ITS SIGNATORIES: AT A WORLD CONGRESS IN 2000, A MEMORANDUM OF AFRICAN CONTINENTAL UNDERSTANDING WAS SIGNED BY ALL THE AFRICAN DELEGATES PRESENT — A PROTOCOL WHICH ACKNOWLEDGES THE ASSOCIATION AS THE VOICE OF THE RANGER IN AFRICA AND BINDS THE SIGNATORIES INTO FORMING NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS WITHIN THEIR OWN COUNTRIES. A signed continental protocol committing delegates to form national ranger associations. Where no such association exists in your country, that commitment is the lever — and forming one is a recognised route to representation rather than an invention. WHO IT SUITS: African community conservancy scouts, government and private rangers, and the organisations employing them — for insurance, first aid training and professional representation. CAVEATS: A PROFESSIONAL ASSOCIATION FOR RANGERS, NOT A FUNDER, A LAW FIRM OR A COMMUNITY ORGANISATION; MEMBERSHIP CARRIES FEES AND THE INSURANCE IS A PAID PRODUCT; AND ITS FRAME IS WILDLIFE PROTECTION INCLUDING ENFORCEMENT, WHICH COMMUNITIES IN CONFLICT WITH RANGERS WILL WEIGH. For the charity that funds ranger teams and runs a crisis appeal, Burundi's entry; for the collapse that leaves rangers unpaid, South Sudan's entry.

trackers.name: ACJPS (African Centre for Justice and Peace Studies), Sudan — founded in 2009 after the foreign NGOs were expelled; its Legal Programme litigates strategically and filed jointly with PLACE before the African Committee of Experts on the Rights and Welfare of the Child
trackers.desc: THEY BUILT IT AFTER THE FOREIGN NGOs WERE THROWN OUT — method and adjacency declared first: THIRD NAMED-ATTORNEY ROUND. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN FOUR HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; THE SUBJECT'S OWN HOST, ITS ACRONYM AND FOUR FACTS ABSENT. ONE NETWORK HOST APPEARS UNDER DR CONGO; ONE GENERIC PHRASE MATCHED A SUDAN ENTRY ABOUT A UNIVERSITY CENTRE ACTING AS CO-APPLICANT, READ IN FULL AND A DIFFERENT SUBJECT — THAT ENTRY IS THE CO-APPLICANT SIDE, THIS IS A NATIONAL ORGANISATION. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE LEGAL PROGRAMME AND WHAT IT DOES, WHICH IS THE FIND: ITS LEGAL PROGRAMME MONITORS LEGAL DEVELOPMENTS AND CONDUCTS LEGAL RESEARCH, AND CONDUCTS STRATEGIC LITIGATION TO PURSUE EFFECTIVE REMEDIES FOR HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS AND TO INFLUENCE LAW, POLICY AND PRACTICE. A standing legal programme inside a monitoring organisation, which is the combination that matters: the same body that documents the violation can carry it into a forum. Many organisations in this file do one or the other. THE JOINT FILING AND THE BODY IT WENT TO, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IT SUBMITTED A COMPLAINT TOGETHER WITH PLACE (PEOPLE'S LEGAL AID CENTRE) TO A CONTINENTAL COMMITTEE OF EXPERTS ON THE RIGHTS AND WELFARE OF THE CHILD — CHALLENGING PROVISIONS IN THE NATIONALITY LAW THAT AUTOMATICALLY REVOKE NATIONALITY WITHOUT DUE PROCESS, THE MATTER RECORDED IN THAT COMMITTEE'S OWN NUMBERED LIST OF COMMUNICATIONS NAMING BOTH ORGANISATIONS AGAINST THE GOVERNMENT. A THIRD continental forum, alongside the Commission and the Court recorded elsewhere in this file. It takes communications and it publishes them numbered, and where a project's harm falls on children — schooling lost to a relocation, a settlement cleared with families in it — that is a route almost nobody uses. And it was filed jointly by two national organisations, neither of them foreign. THE FOUR OBJECTIVES IT STATES: TO DOCUMENT VIOLATIONS AND PROTECT THOSE AT RISK; TO HOLD PERPETRATORS OF SERIOUS VIOLATIONS AND INTERNATIONAL CRIMES TO ACCOUNT; TO ENSURE EFFECTIVE ACCESS TO JUSTICE AND OBTAIN REPARATION FOR VICTIMS; AND TO STRENGTHEN RESPECT FOR HUMAN RIGHTS IN GOVERNANCE, SOCIETY AND CULTURE. REPARATION named as an objective rather than only accountability. A community wants the loss made good, and organisations differ on whether they pursue that or stop at the finding. WHY IT EXISTS, WHICH IS WORTH RECORDING: CREATED IN 2009 IN RESPONSE TO THE EXPULSIONS AND SUSPENSIONS OF INTERNATIONAL AND NATIONAL CIVIL SOCIETY GROUPS IN THE COUNTRY AFTER THE ARREST WARRANT FOR PRESIDENT AL-BASHIR. Founded because the foreign organisations were removed. This file has repeatedly recorded communities losing support when an international NGO withdraws or is expelled; here is the answer built deliberately — a national body designed from the outset to survive that. THE LAND CONFLICT IT DOCUMENTS: LONGSTANDING TENSIONS BETWEEN TWO NAMED COMMUNITIES HAVE REPEATEDLY ERUPTED INTO VIOLENCE OVER LAND OWNERSHIP, ACCESS TO RESOURCES, AND DISPLACEMENT-RELATED GRIEVANCES — EARLIER CLASHES RESULTING IN DEATHS, DISPLACEMENT AND THE OCCUPATION OF AGRICULTURAL LANDS, LEAVING UNDERLYING DISPUTES UNRESOLVED DESPITE MEDIATION EFFORTS. Land ownership and displacement recorded as the driver, not the consequence. An organisation that names the land question inside a conflict it is documenting is one that will recognise a land claim when a community brings it. HOW IT COLLECTS WHAT IT PUBLISHES: INFORMATION COLLECTED DIRECTLY FROM INTERNALLY DISPLACED PERSONS RESIDING IN TAWILA CAMP — INCLUDING WOMEN AND GIRLS REPORTING THAT INDIVIDUALS WORKING FOR HUMANITARIAN ORGANIZATIONS ALLEGEDLY DEMANDED SEXUAL FAVOURS IN EXCHANGE FOR ASSISTANCE, REGISTRATION FOR AID PROGRAMMES AND EMPLOYMENT. It publishes allegations against aid organisations, not only against the state. A monitor willing to report the conduct of the humanitarian sector is more likely to report honestly on a conservation body or a project developer too. WHAT IT PUBLISHES AND HOW OFTEN: MONTHLY REPORTS DOCUMENTING THE HUMAN RIGHTS AND HUMANITARIAN SITUATION AMIDST ONGOING ARMED CONFLICT — AND IT REGULARLY PRODUCES HIGH QUALITY, EVIDENCE-BASED PUBLICATIONS. Monthly, through an active war. Where a community needs its situation on a dated public record, a monthly national report is a place to get it entered. THE REPUTATION IT HAS BUILT AND WHAT IT RESTS ON: IT HAS PERFORMED VITAL MONITORING AND PROTECTION FUNCTIONS AND BUILT A SOLID REPUTATION FOR THE CREDIBILITY, IMPARTIALITY AND PROFESSIONALISM OF ITS WORK. WHAT IT OFFERS OTHER ORGANISATIONS, WHICH IS THE THIRD FIND: IT HAS PLAYED A VITAL ROLE IN PROVIDING TECHNICAL SUPPORT AND TRAINING TO NEW CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS AND INFORMAL ACTIVIST NETWORKS. INFORMAL ACTIVIST NETWORKS, explicitly — not only registered NGOs. The registration barrier this file records at nearly every funder does not apply to being trained, and a village committee with no legal status can still ask. WHO IS ON ITS BOARD AND WHY THAT MATTERS: A LATE INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS EXPERT WHO WAS A LAWYER, POLICY ANALYST, LAW PROFESSOR AND ADVOCATE WITH THIRTY-FIVE YEARS ACROSS ACADEMIC, JUDICIAL, GOVERNMENTAL, REGIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL LEVELS; A LAW LECTURER SPECIALISING IN INTERNATIONAL CRIMINAL LAW; A SENIOR RESEARCHER AT AN INTERNATIONAL WATCHDOG AND FORMER UN MISSION HUMAN RIGHTS OFFICER; AND AN EXPERT WHO ADVISED JOINT UN AND AFRICAN UNION MEDIATION TEAMS AND SERVED AS AN INDEPENDENT COMMISSIONER IN A UN COMMISSION OF INVESTIGATION INTO POST-ELECTION VIOLENCE. The board is the capability. Reading who sits on an organisation's board tells you which forums it can actually reach — here, criminal law, UN mediation and a continental treaty body, all present. THE NETWORKS IT SITS IN: A MEMBER OF AN INTERNATIONAL ANTI-TORTURE NETWORK, LISTED AMONG HUMAN RIGHTS ORGANISATIONS WORLDWIDE BY AN INTERNATIONAL FEDERATION, A MEMBER OF A GRASSROOTS JUSTICE NETWORK, A CITIZENSHIP RIGHTS INITIATIVE AND AN ANTI-GENOCIDE ALLIANCE. Five routes to reach it where a national site is intermittent, which in a conflict it will be. AND WHAT IT SAYS IT IS AIMING AT: A COUNTRY WHERE ALL PEOPLE CAN LIVE AND PROSPER FREE FROM FEAR AND WANT, IN WHICH ALL PERSONS AND GROUPS ARE GRANTED THEIR RIGHTS TO NON-DISCRIMINATION, EQUALITY AND JUSTICE. WHO IT SUITS: communities displaced by conflict or land seizure who need their situation documented monthly and carried into a continental forum — and unregistered local groups that need training rather than money. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY, OPERATING THROUGH AN ACTIVE ARMED CONFLICT, WITH A CIVIL AND POLITICAL RIGHTS FRAME RATHER THAN LAND OR PLANNING; IT DOCUMENTS, TRAINS AND LITIGATES STRATEGICALLY RATHER THAN ACTING AS A GENERAL LEGAL AID SERVICE. For the university centre that acts as co-applicant before the African Court and Commission, Sudan's entry; for the continental commission's own complaint procedure, Eritrea's entry.

trackers.name: Natural Justice: Lawyers for Communities and the Environment
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an African public-interest law organisation — lawyers and paralegals working with communities facing mining, oil and gas, logging and large infrastructure, combining legal empowerment, community protocols, policy work and litigation. Hubs in Cape Town, Nairobi and Dakar, staff in Madagascar, Botswana and Guinea, and country programmes in Burkina Faso, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Namibia, Nigeria, Senegal and South Africa. It also runs the Environmental Lawyers Collective for Africa and an EIA Process Tracker. WHO IT SUITS: an Indigenous or rural community whose land, water or customary rights are threatened by an extractive or infrastructure project. It takes selected cases and works project-to-project outside its programme countries, so expect an approach-and-assess conversation rather than open intake. IS THERE AN OFFICE NEAR YOU? STAFF, NOT A HUB — Antananarivo. The 3 hubs are Cape Town, Nairobi and Dakar; here there are additional staff, so expect a smaller presence and a longer route into casework. WHAT IT DOES: founded 2007 in Cape Town, it supports communities to know the law, use the law and shape the law — access to land and governance of natural resources, the struggle against harmful extractive and infrastructure developments, traditional knowledge and benefit sharing, community rights within conservation, and climate action. ITS SIGNATURE TOOL IS THE COMMUNITY PROTOCOL — a documented instrument letting a community set out its biological, cultural and spiritual resources, norms and values, and assert existing rights under customary, domestic and international law, aimed squarely at laws and projects developed by government and industry without consultation. Ask for it by name. Contact: 63 Hout Street, Cape Town 8001; +27 21 426 1633; info@naturaljustice.org.

trackers.name: African Environmental Defenders Fund (emergency grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the African Environmental Defenders Fund — an emergency grant fund run by Natural Justice with the International Land Coalition Africa, ICCA Consortium, PACJA, Oxfam Novib, FEMNET and others, giving up to US$5,000 to land and environmental defenders anywhere in Africa who are under threat because of their activism. It can cover the cost of legal representation where a defender is arrested, summoned or prosecuted, plus relocation and other short-term transitional costs. WHO IT SUITS: an individual frontline defender who is a citizen or legal resident of an African country, facing an imminent threat, and not already supported by another body — it is not project or core funding, and routine office and administrative costs are excluded. HOW IT DIFFERS: applications are rolling, by email or helpline, not to a grant round. Natural Justice's own site names Burkina Faso, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Namibia, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa and Botswana as its country programmes, which is where this entry is placed; the fund's stated eligibility is any African country, so apply from elsewhere on the continent too.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a pan-African feminist rapid-response fund with reach across all 54 African countries — small grants released quickly for unanticipated, time-critical situations rather than planned programme work, covering safety and protection needs when defenders are threatened and short windows for advocacy after an unexpected event. WHO IT SUITS: women's rights organisations, feminist collectives and movements in which women or gender-diverse people are the primary decision-makers. It does NOT fund individuals, and the action must be strategic, genuinely unanticipated, and completable in under three months. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is emergency money for a moment, not a budget for a campaign — decisions are fast and grants are modest.

trackers.name: High Constitutional Court of Madagascar
trackers.desc: High Constitutional Court of Madagascar — supreme court (Madagascar).

trackers.name: EDBM – Guichet Unique
trackers.desc: National — company registration one-stop (RCS); publishes company constitution notices, Madagascar. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Madagascar — Ministère de l’Économie et des Finances
trackers.desc: National budget authority; coordinates the preparation & execution of the State budget and publishes public-finance information, Madagascar. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Madagascar.

trackers.name: SADC Protocol on Wildlife Conservation and Law Enforcement
trackers.desc: A REGIONAL TREATY WHOSE DEFINITIONS DO REAL WORK. The SADC Protocol on Wildlife Conservation and Law Enforcement (1999, in force 2003) defines ‘taking’ as hunting, killing, injuring, capturing, harassing, collecting, picking, uprooting, digging up, cutting, destruction and removal of any wildlife species. So clearing vegetation for a development is ‘taking’ under this definition, not merely site preparation — that reframing is the most useful thing here. It defines community based wildlife management as management by a community which has the right to manage the wildlife AND to receive the benefits from that management, giving a benefit-sharing argument a treaty source; and ‘conservation’ to include rehabilitation and restoration, so restoration sits inside the defined term. THE CROSS-BORDER HOOK: States Parties must cooperate to manage shared wildlife resources as well as any transfrontier effects of activities within their jurisdiction or control — a mine, dam or plantation whose effects cross a border engages a treaty duty on the state that authorised it. Article 4 objectives include enforcing wildlife laws within, between and among States Parties and facilitating community-based natural resources management. CHECK YOUR STATE HAS RATIFIED — the Protocol is legally binding only for countries that have signed and ratified it, and this entry does not assert that your state has. ON TFCAs: they encompass protected areas as well as multiple resource use areas, so they are not exclusion zones; a TFCA practitioners network founded September 2013 has membership open to all stakeholder groups. And SADC's own 2023–2033 TFCA programme names the marginalisation of communities living in and around protected areas as a problem it exists to address — quotable against the body that wrote it.

trackers.name: Madagasikara Voakajy — a Malagasy organisation that is now the legal manager of seven protected areas, with communities in the governance
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Malagasy conservation organisation, founded 2005, that creates protected areas with communities and then holds the legal mandate to manage them. In 2025 the environment ministry formally entrusted it with seven protected areas — Mangabe-Ranomena-Sahasarotra, Mahialambo, Ampanangandehibe-Behasina, Analalava, Analabe-Betanatanana, Ambatofotsy and Ampotaka — signed by the Director General of Environmental Governance with the organisation's executive director. Sixteen protected area managers had their mandates renewed at the same ceremony after seven years without official recognition, which tells you how long the paperwork can stall and why an established delegate matters. WHY THIS IS THE MALAGASY VERSION OF BUYING LAND: nobody purchases forest here — protection runs through management transfer to a community body, the Vondron'Olona Ifotony or VOI, with an organisation like this one holding the delegated management contract and building the VOI's capacity to govern the resource. Its stated programme is strengthening VOI governance, restoration inside protected areas and management transfer zones through agroforestry and native species, five village nurseries producing about 15,000 seedlings each a year run with ten VOI in the Moramanga district, and income-generating activities so that conservation pays. WHO IT SUITS: communities in or beside forest who want a management transfer secured and defended, particularly around Moramanga, Bobaomby and the named protected areas. CAVEATS: this is a species-led conservation organisation — the case that wins its attention is endemic biodiversity, not the injustice of a project; it names degradation of the Mangabe protected area and damage to restoration sites by incomers among its own challenges; and no intake route, application form or fee information was found.

trackers.name: Fondation Tany Meva — a Malagasy foundation whose entire purpose is funding community environmental projects, about 1,850 of them so far
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: created in 1996 and recognised as being of public utility, Tany Meva is the first Malagasy environmental foundation and one built specifically for communities — its stated mission is to mobilise and manage funds for local initiatives to protect and sustainably manage natural resources, with communities at the centre of its financing. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY PAID OUT: by its thirtieth anniversary it reported more than US$20 million in grants across roughly 1,850 local projects throughout Madagascar, reaching over 415,000 households, with supported projects covering more than a million hectares of land and over 200,000 hectares of marine area managed or conserved, more than 10,000 hectares reforested or restored, and 20,000 hectares of forest under community management through natural resource management transfers (TGRN) — the Malagasy instrument by which a community takes over management of forest, which this file records elsewhere. WHAT IT FUNDS: biodiversity conservation and natural resource management, forest restoration and reforestation, ecotourism, climate adaptation, renewable energy and energy efficiency, environmental education, and income-generating activities that take the pressure off the resource — the last is the category most community groups underuse. HOW THE MONEY REACHES YOU NOW: under its 2023-2027 strategic plan it works through landscape partnerships, selecting established support organisations to work alongside local community organisations, prepare them for autonomy and keep the project running after the grant ends — for example four community projects around the Ankarafantsika protected area and three around Anjozorobe funded for three to five years. It has also signed agreements covering mangrove degradation in Boeny and the management of REDD+ carbon revenues with the environment ministry. WHO IT SUITS: Malagasy community organisations — including VOI holding a management transfer — that need money for the work rather than a lawyer for the fight. CAVEATS: a grant-maker for conservation and livelihoods, not a defence fund — nothing here pays for litigation or for opposing a project; financing now flows through selected landscape partners in named regions rather than by open national application, so ask which partner covers your area; and its stated alignment is with public policy, though it says it decides autonomously.

trackers.name: Collectif TANY — raises money specifically to pay for the legal defence of Malagasy farmers facing land grabs and prosecution
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Collectif pour la Défense des Terres Malgaches (TANY), a non-profit of Malagasy-origin members formed to oppose the dispossession of Malagasy citizens and farmers. Its stated activities are precise and unusual: collecting information on land-grab cases; sending missions into the field to conduct investigations and interviews; and the LEGAL DEFENCE of farmers or activists imprisoned or prosecuted. It runs public fundraising campaigns for named struggles — including one to fund legal assistance to communities in the Ihorombe region affected by land grabbing by a foreign agri-company. Money raised abroad to pay a specific community's lawyer is a resource almost nothing else in this file provides. THE FACT IT KEEPS PUTTING IN FRONT OF GOVERNMENT, which every Malagasy household should know: the great majority of Malagasy live on their land WITHOUT a land title, and more than 1,000 of Madagascar's 1,693 communes have no guichet foncier — the communal land desk that alone can issue a certificat foncier. Obtaining a title takes much time and much money. So TANY argues for strengthening in law the recognition of the legitimate rights of local communities EVEN WHERE THEY HOLD NEITHER TITLE NOR CERTIFICATE, legalising the rights of occupants of land with obsolete status, and halting allocations to investors by long lease or concession. It has also opposed provisions allowing foreigners to own titled land and criticised the state investment board for accelerating investors' paperwork while ordinary families queue. WHO IT SUITS: Malagasy farming communities facing land grabs, long leases or prosecution for defending their land. CAVEATS: ITS MEMBERS AND OFFICERS ARE BASED IN FRANCE — this is an advocacy and support collective working with partner farmer associations in Madagascar, not a walk-in office or a law firm; it funds and accompanies defence rather than conducting it. For protected-area management transfers, Madagascar's Voakajy entry; for community grants, Tany Meva.

trackers.name: Buying hectares by the acre — the fund that paid for 200 ha at Ankarabolava-Agnakatrika, and how a local partner gets it
trackers.desc: WHERE THE PURCHASE MONEY COMES FROM: a UK-based land-purchase trust runs a “Buy an Acre” programme that funds LAND ACQUISITION by LOCAL partner organisations — it does not buy or hold land itself — the in-country partner buys, and the partner holds the title. WHAT IT HAS PAID FOR IN MADAGASCAR: the expansion of the Ankarabolava-Agnakatrika forest by 200 hectares, reported as home to over 50 threatened species including a critically endangered lemur, secured by a botanical garden's Madagascar programme. A SECOND WORKED EXAMPLE, because it shows how long this takes: in South Africa a renosterveld conservation trust secured a 497-hectare property — the culmination of SIXTEEN YEARS OF NEGOTIATIONS — with the fund paying for 150 hectares of that purchase. Note what that means in practice: the fund covered under a third of the parcel, so the local organisation had to raise the rest — external purchase money is usually a CONTRIBUTION toward a deal you are already assembling, not the whole price. Reported programme-wide output includes protection of 152,205 hectares of priority land in a single reporting period, nearly half of it solely funded by the trust. HOW TO USE THIS: identify the parcel, get a local organisation with legal personality to be the buyer and future titleholder, price it, then approach acre-based funders for a share — and expect the negotiation with the seller to outlast the fundraising. WHO IT SUITS: Malagasy conservation organisations and community partners with a specific parcel in view and no capital, and organisations elsewhere studying how purchase money is actually assembled. CAVEATS: THIS IS A FOREIGN FUNDER WITH ITS OWN PRIORITIES — it funds land of high biodiversity value, so it will not pay for a parcel that matters to you for other reasons; it works through vetted partner organisations rather than with individuals or unregistered groups; and title rests with the partner, not automatically with neighbouring communities. For Malagasy community grants see the Tany Meva entry, for protected-area management transfers Voakajy, and for legal defence funding Collectif TANY.

trackers.name: Madagascar's land-law clinics — five cliniques de droit foncier in five regions, run with four Malagasy NGOs, plus Trano Aro Zo at Ihosy since 2011
trackers.desc: WHERE TO WALK IN: FIVE CLINIQUES DE DROIT FONCIER — land-law clinics — have been set up in five regions, IN COLLABORATION WITH FOUR MALAGASY NGOs, under a justice-governance programme supported by the UN development programme and USAID. Their stated purpose is prevention of land conflicts, awareness-raising on land legislation, civic education of the population, and DECONGESTING THE CIVIL COURTS — that is, resolving land disputes before they become cases. A SECOND, OLDER CLINIC WITH A NAME TO ASK FOR: at IHOSY the clinic Trano Aro Zo, established with European Union support in 2011 and run by a Malagasy NGO, provides advice, orientation, CONCILIATION and accompaniment of vulnerable people in protecting their rights. Conciliation and accompaniment are the two words to listen for: someone who will sit with you through the procedure is worth more in Madagascar than advice alone, because the file this country records elsewhere is that most communes have no land desk at all. WHAT ELSE THE SAME PROGRAMME PUT IN PLACE, because it changes what a court visit looks like: standardised JUSTICE INFORMATION KIOSKS at first-instance courts, equipment for the courts of five regions, renovation of eight first-instance courts in the south, and civil and commercial training for 51 magistrates and 141 court clerks. A judge quoted in that work describes the current context as marked by RECURRENT LAND DISPUTES, and notes the difficulty caused by texts issued without implementing decrees — the same gap this file records across the region. Madagascar has also launched a free online case-law platform at the justice ministry. WHO IT SUITS: Malagasy households and communities with a land dispute, boundary problem or inheritance claim, especially in the five programme regions and around Ihosy. CAVEATS: NO STANDALONE SITE FOR THE CLINICS — this entry points at the programme's published account; the clinics are donor-funded and programme-bound, so ask whether yours is still operating and which NGO runs it. They conciliate and orient rather than litigate. For legal-defence fundraising, Madagascar's Collectif TANY entry; for community grants, Tany Meva; for protected-area transfers, Voakajy.

trackers.name: Fanamby and the FAPBM — the Malagasy association that holds delegated management of five protected areas under numbered contracts, and the foundation that signs financing conventions with named managers
trackers.desc: HOW A NON-STATE BODY COMES TO MANAGE A PROTECTED AREA IN MADAGASCAR: FANAMBY — the word means CHALLENGE in Malagasy — A NON-PROFIT ASSOCIATION CREATED IN 1997, is THE DELEGATED MANAGER (GESTIONNAIRE DÉLÉGUÉ) OF FIVE PROTECTED AREAS: ANJOZOROBE ANGAVO in Analamanga; MENABE ANTIMENA and the ALLÉE DES BAOBABS in Menabe; LOKY MANAMBATO (Daraina) in SAVA; and ANDRAFIAMENA ANDAVAKOERA in DIANA. THE PAPERWORK IS PUBLISHED AND IT IS THE MODEL TO ASK FOR: the Menabe Antimena site was CLASSED BY ARRÊTÉ N°4532-06/MINENVF OF 28 MARCH 2006 GRANTING TEMPORARY PROTECTION, AND THE MANAGEMENT WAS THEN HELD UNDER CONTRAT DE DÉLÉGATION DE GESTION N°1058/06/MINENVF DATED 24 AUGUST 2006. Temporary protection first by arrêté, then a numbered management delegation contract — that is the two-step sequence by which a Malagasy site gets protected and a non-state body gets to run it. Ask for both documents by number, and note that the temporary protection came FIVE MONTHS BEFORE the management contract: the classing is what buys the time. ITS STATED MISSION IS TO PRESERVE NATURAL RESOURCES BY INVOLVING AND MAKING RESPONSIBLE ALL ACTORS AND THOSE CONCERNED, NOTABLY THE COMMUNAUTÉS DE BASE, IN THE WHOLE PROCESS, with its founder identifying protected areas AS PLATFORMS FOR SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT through income-generating activities in the service of communities — sustainable tourism and bio-equitable supply chains. THE PART A VILLAGE CAN COPY: in 2008 it launched THE FIRST COMMUNITY TOURISM PROJECT IN MADAGASCAR with the full involvement of a named local entity; and IN 2010, AT THE REQUEST OF THAT ENTITY AND OF LOCAL ASSOCIATIONS, FANAMBY CREATED AN ECONOMIC INTEREST GROUPING, professionalising communities and integrating them into an association or federation strong enough to hold its own on international markets. A groupement d'intérêt économique created AT THE COMMUNITIES' OWN REQUEST is the shape to ask for: the conservation body holds the management contract, the community holds the trading vehicle. ON THE GROUND at Menabe Antimena the delegated manager and sub-delegates work with local communities through NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT TRANSFERS, a LOCAL MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE, FIRE OFFICERS and a DINA EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE, against clearings, fires and uncontrolled migratory movements. THE MONEY BEHIND IT: THE FONDATION POUR LES AIRES PROTÉGÉES ET LA BIODIVERSITÉ DE MADAGASCAR (FAPBM, fapbm.org), Lot VX 13 Andrefandrova, ANTANANARIVO, SIGNS ANNUAL FINANCING CONVENTIONS WITH PROTECTED-AREA MANAGERS — in one year covering 17 areas run by the national parks agency and 18 more run by NINE OTHER NAMED ORGANISATIONS INCLUDING FANAMBY. The foundation funds whoever holds the management — so securing the delegation is what unlocks the endowment. ALSO NAMED: NY TANINTSIKA, BP 1345, FIANARANTSOA 301, with published telephone numbers and email. WHO IT SUITS: Malagasy communities seeking protection for a site, a community tourism or trading vehicle, or a delegated manager. CAVEATS: DELEGATION IS A MINISTERIAL CONTRACT — the community is a partner, not the holder, unless it forms its own vehicle. For a Malagasy organisation that became legal manager of its area, Madagascar's Madagasikara Voakajy entry; for a foundation that funds communities directly, Fondation Tany Meva; for money for legal defence, Collectif TANY; for hectares bought outright, the Ankarabolava entry; for five land-law clinics, the cliniques de droit foncier entry.

trackers.name: Bongolava Maitso — Tafo Mihaavo, the community association managing 70,000 hectares across 54 fokontany, and the Alliance Voahary Gasy platform that co-signs letters to the President
trackers.desc: THE VILLAGE ASSOCIATION THAT HOLDS 70,000 HECTARES: THE ASSOCIATION BONGOLAVA MAITSO — TAFO MIHAAVO HAS BEEN MANAGER OF THE BONGOLAVA MAITSO PROTECTED AREA FOR MORE THAN TEN YEARS, COVERING 70,000 HECTARES BETWEEN PORT-BERGÉ AND MAMPIKONY — AND IT RECALLS THAT IT IS ITSELF AT THE ORIGIN OF THE CREATION OF THE SITE, which is distinguished by its RICHNESS IN BIODIVERSITY, NOTABLY PALISSANDRE AND LEMURS LOCALLY CALLED AKOMBA, AS WELL AS BY THE PRESENCE OF SACRED CULTURAL SITES. A community association that created the protected area and has managed it for a decade is the strongest form in this file: not consulted, not partnered — the manager. And note what it protects: rosewood, lemurs AND sacred sites in the same designation, so the cultural claim and the biological one are carried by one instrument. ITS STRUCTURE IS THE PART TO COPY: THE ORGANISATION RESTS ON A DECENTRALISED GOVERNANCE COVERING 54 FOKONTANY AND SEVERAL COMMUNES. Fifty-four fokontany inside one association. That is how a body large enough to hold seventy thousand hectares stays accountable to the people living on it — governance decentralised to the smallest administrative unit, not concentrated in a committee at the district town. AND THE WARNING, WHICH THIS FILE HAS NOW SEEN TWICE: FACING THE EXPIRY OF ITS MANAGEMENT CONTRACT, THE ASSOCIATION REQUESTED AN AUDIENCE WITH THE DIRECTION GÉNÉRALE OF THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN ORDER TO CLARIFY THE MODALITIES FOR RENEWING ITS MANDATE. A ten-year community management contract came to its end date and the renewal terms were not clear. This file recorded the same failure at a Chadian community hunting reserve whose mandate simply lapsed. Put the renewal mechanism in the founding document: who renews it, by when, and what happens if they do not answer. Ask for that clause before you sign, not in year ten. THE PLATFORM: THE ALLIANCE VOAHARY GASY IS AN ENVIRONMENTAL PLATFORM GROUPING ABOUT THIRTY MEMBERS, ALL ACTORS WORKING IN THE SECTOR, WITH A NAMED CHAIRMAN OF ITS BOARD — its membership including a national foundation for protected areas and biodiversity, a community foundation, A NATIONAL GROUPING OF FOREST OPERATORS, AN ASSOCIATION OF JOURNALISTS FOR THE ENVIRONMENT, AN ASSOCIATION OF MALAGASY FOREST ENGINEERS, A NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL ACTION ASSOCIATION and A NATIONAL CONFEDERATION OF FARMER ASSOCIATIONS. Forest operators, journalists, forest engineers and farmers in the same platform as the conservation foundations. That mix is the point: the people who cut, the people who report, the people who certify and the people who farm, all reachable through one door. WHAT THE PLATFORM DOES WITH ITS MEMBERS: THE ALLIANCE AND SEVEN OTHER NAMED ORGANISATIONS — INCLUDING A CITIZENS' COLLECTIVE, A CITIZEN MOVEMENT, TWO NAMED NGOs AND A TRANSPARENCY ORGANISATION — ADDRESSED AN OPEN LETTER TO THE PRESIDENT OF THE REPUBLIC, THE MINISTER OF JUSTICE, THE PRESIDENT OF THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY AND THE PRESIDENT OF THE HIGH CONSTITUTIONAL COURT, DENOUNCING ATTEMPTS TO RELEASE A SITTING MEMBER OF PARLIAMENT WHO HAD BEEN SENTENCED TO FIVE YEARS' FIRM IMPRISONMENT FOR THE DESTRUCTION OF THE FOREST OF A NAMED PROTECTED AREA. An MP convicted and imprisoned for destroying a protected forest, and eight organisations writing jointly to four heads of institution to keep him there. That is what a platform is for. Note the four addressees — head of state, justice minister, speaker and constitutional court — and copy the list. ALSO NAMED among Malagasy environmental bodies: a biodiversity network, a primate study and research group, a service for support to environmental management, a scientific association and several named conservation organisations; and the traditional Malagasy assembly of the inhabitants of a given collectivity is recorded as an existing form of civil society. WHO IT SUITS: Malagasy communities managing or seeking to manage a protected area, and anyone needing a national platform. CAVEATS: A CONTRACT-BASED MANAGEMENT MODEL — the renewal risk is real and documented. For the two-step arrêté-then-delegation sequence, Madagascar's Fanamby entry; for the foundation that funds whoever holds the management, FAPBM; for money for legal defence, Collectif TANY; for hectares bought outright, the Ankarabolava entry; for five land-law clinics, the cliniques de droit foncier entry.

trackers.name: Madagascar's regional platforms of protected-area managers — DIANA and SAVA joining forces against cross-border fishing pressure — and the fund line that pays for local development around the areas, not just the areas
trackers.desc: THE MANAGERS FORMED THEIR OWN PLATFORM — and this file has not recorded that form anywhere else in Africa: A PLATFORM OF PROTECTED AREA MANAGERS IN THE DIANA REGION OPERATES AS AN ADVOCACY FORCE, WORKING CLOSELY WITH OTHER INSTITUTIONS — A MARINE CONSERVATION ORGANISATION, THE NGO MIHARI, A THIRD BODY AND THE NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL CIVIL SOCIETY PLATFORM — TO ENSURE THAT THE MANAGERS' VOICE IS HEARD IN THE EFFORT TO CONSERVE NATURAL RESOURCES, WHICH IS DESCRIBED AS AN ENGINE OF SOCIO-ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT FOR LOCAL POPULATIONS AND THE REGION. The people who actually run protected areas organising themselves as a bloc. Everywhere else in this file the managers are individual grantees dealing separately with a ministry and a funder; here they federated. If your community manages an area under a transfer or a co-management contract, you are a MANAGER — and a platform of managers is a body you can be a member of in your own right. AND IT SPREAD, WHICH IS THE PART TO COPY: INSPIRED BY THE OTHER REGIONS MAKING UP A NAMED NORTHERN TRIANGLE, A PLATFORM OF MANAGERS WAS RECENTLY CREATED IN THE SAVA REGION WITH THE SAME OBJECTIVES — AND THE TWO NOW INTEND TO JOIN FORCES IN ORDER TO MITIGATE INTER-REGIONAL PRESSURES. One region formed a platform, the neighbouring region copied it, and now the two are combining. That is a growth path a community group can follow deliberately: found it, document it, tell the next district, then federate. THE PROBLEM THEY FORMED TO SOLVE IS NAMED PRECISELY, AND IT IS THE COMMONEST KIND: FISHERMEN FROM ONE REGION GO FISHING ILLEGALLY WITHIN THE LIMITS OF A NAMED PROTECTED AREA ON THE OTHER REGION'S SIDE AT THE TIME OF A NAMED SEASONAL WIND OR AT THE FISHING SEASON OPENING — AND VICE VERSA ON THE OTHER SIDE. And vice versa is the honest part. This is not outsiders against locals; it is two neighbouring communities each crossing into the other's protected water, seasonally. No enforcement by either side alone can fix that — only an agreement between the two, which is exactly what a joint platform is for. If your conflict has that shape, the answer is a body that both sides sit in, not more patrols. AND THE PLATFORM'S OWN ASSESSMENT IS RECORDED WITHOUT VARNISH: CHALLENGES REMAIN FOR THE PLATFORM TO ACHIEVE THE VISION — TO BE A PLATFORM OF SOLIDARITY, EFFICIENT AND RECOGNISED AT REGIONAL AND LOCAL LEVEL. Recognised at regional AND LOCAL level. Note which one is harder: a platform can be known to the region's officials and still not be trusted by the villages it covers. Build the local recognition first. WHAT IS AVAILABLE TO A MANAGER, WITH THE COVERAGE FIGURE: IN 2022 THE NATIONAL BIODIVERSITY TRUST FUND SUPPORTED 48 PROTECTED AREAS OUT OF THE 123 AREAS WITH DEFINITIVE STATUS IN THE EXISTING NETWORK, FINANCING BOTH THE AREAS MANAGED BY THE STATE PARKS AGENCY AND THE NEW PROTECTED AREAS MANAGED BY NGOs AND/OR CONSERVATION ASSOCIATIONS. Forty-eight of a hundred and twenty-three. Well under half the network is funded, which means the competition is real and the question worth asking is what the other seventy-five do for money — but it also means an association-managed new protected area is explicitly eligible, not just the state agency.
