AND THE LINE THAT MATTERS MOST TO A NEIGHBOURING VILLAGE: THE FUND ALSO FINANCES THE LOCAL DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES CARRIED OUT BY THE PROTECTED AREA MANAGERS WITH THE NEIGHBOURING COMMUNITIES — WISHING NOT ONLY TO COMPENSATE THE POSSIBLE LOSSES OF REVENUE RESULTING FROM THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THE PROTECTED AREAS, BUT ALSO TO IMPROVE HOUSEHOLD INCOMES IN A DURABLE WAY. Compensating for income lost BECAUSE the protected area was created is written into the fund's own purpose. If protection cost your household something, that is not a grievance you have to argue from first principles — it is a funded category, and the manager beside you can apply for it. Ask what local development budget attaches to the area next to you and who decides how it is spent. THE NETWORK STRUCTURE AROUND THEM: the national environmental platform counts 30 MEMBER ORGANISATIONS grouped FOR A POLITICAL DIALOGUE FAVOURABLE TO A BETTER BALANCE AND A RATIONAL MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES, and its members include foundations, a national forestry operators' grouping, an environmental journalists' association and named conservation NGOs. An association of environmental JOURNALISTS sitting in the same platform as the foundations and the forestry operators. If your case needs coverage, that membership is the introduction. WHO IT SUITS: Malagasy communities and associations managing an area, neighbours of a protected area, and anyone with a cross-border resource conflict. CAVEATS: THE PLATFORMS ARE REGIONAL AND YOUNG — confirm they are active in your region. For the association holding delegated management of a protected area, Madagascar's Fanamby entry; for the foundation whose entire purpose is funding communities, Fondation Tany Meva; for money raised specifically to pay legal defence costs, Collectif TANY; for five land-law clinics, the cliniques de droit foncier entry; for the community association managing 70,000 ha at its own initiative, Bongolava Maitso.

trackers.name: MIHARI — the network Madagascar's fishers built themselves, from 55 people in one village to 175+ community associations with independent legal status that receives grants directly, and the temporary closure that raised octopus catches 700%
trackers.desc: FIFTY-FIVE PEOPLE IN A VILLAGE, THEN A NATIONAL BODY — and the whole growth curve is on the record, which is why this is worth reading even if you are nowhere near the sea: MADAGASCAR'S FIRST NATIONAL LMMA FORUM WAS HELD IN JUNE 2012 IN A NAMED VILLAGE, BRINGING TOGETHER 55 COMMUNITY MEMBERS FROM 18 LOCALLY MANAGED MARINE AREAS, REPRESENTING A TOTAL OF 134 VILLAGES — AND ITS PRINCIPAL OUTCOME WAS THE FORMATION OF A NATIONAL NETWORK NAMED FROM A MALAGASY ACRONYM MEANING MARINE RESOURCES MANAGEMENT AT THE LOCAL LEVEL. UNTIL THAT MEETING, THE RECORD SAYS PLAINLY, THESE AREAS OPERATED IN RELATIVE ISOLATION, WITH LITTLE COMMUNICATION OR COORDINATION BETWEEN THE COMMUNITY ASSOCIATIONS. Fifty-five people in a village hall ended the isolation of a hundred and thirty-four villages. That is the whole lesson: the associations already existed and were already working — what they lacked was one meeting. If your district has three or four community groups doing the same thing separately, the first forum is the cheapest and highest-return thing any of you can organise. WHAT IT BECAME: THE NETWORK NOW CONNECTS MORE THAN 175 LMMA COMMUNITY ASSOCIATION MEMBERS ALONG A 5,000 KM COASTLINE, WITH FOUR REGIONAL HUBS — NORTHWEST, SOUTHWEST, NORTHEAST AND MIDWEST — AND A THIRTEEN-PERSON TEAM INCLUDING FOUR REGIONAL COORDINATORS, GROWN FROM A ONE-PERSON TEAM. One coordinator became thirteen staff with four regional coordinators. Note the order: the members came first and the staff followed, not the reverse. A network that hires before it has members becomes a project; this one grew the other way round. AND THE STEP THAT MATTERS MOST FOR ANY COMMUNITY NETWORK: IN 2020 IT BECAME A FORMAL ENTITY WITH AN INDEPENDENT STATUS, THAT ENABLES IT TO RECEIVE AND MANAGE GRANTS DIRECTLY. Before that, money for the fishers' network passed through somebody else's accounts. Independent legal status is what turns a movement into a body that holds its own money — and it took eight years. Plan for that step from the beginning: ask, of any network you join or found, whether it can receive a grant in its own name yet, and if not, when. WHAT THE MEMBERS DID WITH IT: IN 2017, FISHERS WHO WERE MEMBERS CAME TOGETHER FOR THE FIRST TIME TO PRESENT THREE MOTIONS TO THE MINISTRY OF FISHERIES — AND AT A NATIONAL FORUM HOSTED BY LMMA COMMUNITIES, THREE GOVERNMENT MINISTRIES TOOK PART: FISHERIES, ENVIRONMENT, AND THE STATE MINISTRY IN CHARGE OF PRESIDENTIAL PROJECTS, LAND USE PLANNING AND EQUIPMENT. The forum was HOSTED BY the communities and the ministries came to it. That is the reversal worth aiming at — not a delegation travelling to the capital, but the ministry travelling to the coast. And three motions, presented by fishers themselves, is a format: a motion is short, numbered and hard to ignore. THE RECOGNITION IT WON: THE NETWORK HAS STRENGTHENED THE RECOGNITION OF SMALL-SCALE FISHERS AS LEGITIMATE CO-MANAGERS AND PARTIES IN NEGOTIATIONS, THANKS TO THE PARTICIPATORY DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF ITS STRUCTURE, WHICH CLARIFIES ROLES, RESPONSIBILITIES AND ACCOUNTABILITY MECHANISMS. PARTIES IN NEGOTIATIONS. Not stakeholders to be consulted — parties, which is a legal posture. And what earned it was an internal structure that says who is responsible for what, because a body that cannot answer that question is easy to exclude from a table. THE HONEST GAP, RECORDED: THE MALAGASY GOVERNMENT HAS NOT YET FORMALLY EMBEDDED AN LMMA MINISTERIAL DECREE IN ITS LEGISLATION, THOUGH IT HAS BEEN INVOLVED IN THE NETWORK'S VARIOUS FORA AND DECISION-MAKING PROCESSES — and the members' stated priority is to CAPITALISE ALL MECHANISMS OF EXISTING GOVERNANCE so that a legal framework would LEGALLY SECURE THE INTERVENTIONS OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES IN THE MARINE AND FISHERIES RESOURCES. Over a decade of practice and still no decree. Community management can run for years on custom and contract while the law catches up — but it is not secure until it is written, and this network says so about itself. AND THE EVIDENCE THAT WINS THE ARGUMENT AT HOME: AN ANALYSIS OF EIGHT YEARS OF DATA FOUND THAT OCTOPUS LANDINGS INCREASED BY MORE THAN 700 PERCENT IN THE MONTH FOLLOWING THE OPENING OF A TEMPORARY CLOSURE, BOOSTING THE CATCH PER FISHER PER DAY BY ALMOST 90 PERCENT OVER THE SAME PERIOD. A temporary closure, then a 700% landing increase and nearly double the catch per fisher per day, measured over eight years. That is the number to put in front of neighbours who think closing an area means losing income — short closures paid, and it was fishers who ran them. Over 14% of the island's inshore seabed is now under local management. WHO IT SUITS: Malagasy coastal communities, and any group anywhere deciding whether to convene a first regional forum or seek independent legal status. CAVEATS: NO LMMA DECREE YET EXISTS — local management rests on other instruments. For the regional platforms of protected-area managers, Madagascar's DIANA and SAVA entry; for the association holding delegated management, Fanamby; for the foundation funding communities, Fondation Tany Meva; for money for legal defence, Collectif TANY.

trackers.name: Earthjustice's International Program — an international legal programme that co-litigates with African organisations on behalf of communities — two won challenges against named oil majors off the South African coast, and a minerals programme demanding consent from affected communities
trackers.desc: THEY CO-LITIGATED WITH AFRICAN PARTNERS AND BEAT TWO OIL MAJORS IN A SOUTH AFRICAN COURT — adjacency declared first: THE AFRICAN LEGAL EMPOWERMENT ORGANISATION THAT CO-LITIGATED THOSE CASES IS ALREADY A NAMED ENTRY IN NINE AFRICA BUCKETS; IT IS NOT RESTATED AND ITS HOST IS NOT SHIPPED. THIS FILE'S SEYCHELLES ENTRY COVERS THE ENVIRONMENTAL LAW CHARITY WORKING THROUGH PARTNERS, ITS CHAD ENTRY THE LAWYERS WHO BUILD CASES FROM OUTSIDE THE JURISDICTION, ITS CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC ENTRY THE PRO BONO CENTRE PRIORITISING GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS, AND ITS DR CONGO ENTRY THE ENVIRONMENTAL LAW ORGANISATION THAT IS NOT A LAW FIRM. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE SOUTH AFRICAN WINS, WHICH ARE THE FIND: COMMUNITY AND ENVIRONMENTAL ADVOCATES WON TWO LEGAL CHALLENGES AGAINST FOSSIL FUEL POLLUTERS IN SOUTH AFRICA — THE ORGANISATION PARTNERED WITH A NAMED AFRICAN LEGAL EMPOWERMENT BODY AND A NAMED SOUTH AFRICAN GROUP ON BEHALF OF COASTAL COMMUNITIES FIGHTING A PLAN BY TWO NAMED OIL MAJORS TO DRILL MULTIPLE OIL AND GAS EXPLORATION WELLS OFF THE WEST COAST. Two wins, in an African national court, against two of the largest oil companies in the world, brought on behalf of fishing communities. This file records many routes that might work; this is one that did, and the structure is worth copying — an international litigation team, a continental legal empowerment organisation and a local group, with the communities as the clients rather than the subject. WHAT THAT COAST SUPPORTS, IN THE CASE'S OWN FRAMING: THE REGION'S UNIQUE, ECOLOGICALLY RICH AND DIVERSE MARINE AND COASTAL ECOSYSTEMS NOT ONLY PROVIDE HABITAT FOR NUMEROUS SPECIES BUT ALSO SUPPORT THE CULTURAL TRADITIONS AND LIVELIHOODS OF THE MANY COMMUNITIES LIVING ALONG THE COAST. The pleading put culture and livelihood alongside habitat. A case argued only on species is a case a company can answer with an offset; one argued on what people do and believe there is much harder to price. WHAT THE PROGRAMME DOES: IT PARTNERS WITH ORGANIZATIONS AND COMMUNITIES AROUND THE WORLD TO ESTABLISH, STRENGTHEN, AND ENFORCE NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL LEGAL PROTECTIONS FOR THE ENVIRONMENT AND PUBLIC HEALTH. ENFORCE is the word that matters. Many organisations in this file help write or interpret law; enforcement is the step communities most often cannot fund. THE TRANSITION MINERALS PROGRAMME, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: RECOGNIZING THE ENVIRONMENTAL, HEALTH, AND CULTURAL HARMS OF MINING, IT PARTNERS WITH ORGANIZATIONS TO ADVOCATE FOR THE HIGHEST STANDARDS FOR TRANSITION MINERAL MINING AND PROCESSING, REQUIREMENTS FOR CONSENT FROM AND BENEFITS FOR AFFECTED COMMUNITIES, AND ROBUST CIRCULAR ECONOMY LEGISLATION THAT CAN REDUCE THE NEED FOR NEW MINING. The battery-metals rush is arriving across Africa now, and it arrives dressed as climate action — which makes it harder to oppose than a coal mine. An organisation that works on clean energy AND demands consent for the mining behind it is one of the few places that tension is held honestly, and REDUCING THE NEED FOR NEW MINING is the argument that goes furthest with a government. THE AFRICAN EXPANSION IT STATES: WE ARE WORKING TO DEEPEN OUR COLLABORATION ACROSS AFRICA, WHERE MAJOR NEW ELECTRICITY GENERATION CAPACITY IS BEING BUILT TO MEET DEMAND FOR ENERGY ACCESS, URBANIZATION, AND INDUSTRIALIZATION IN COUNTRIES WITH FAST-GROWING POPULATIONS. DEEPENING rather than established. African partnerships are being formed now, which is the moment an organisation gets in rather than joins a queue. WHY POLLUTERS CHOOSE PARTICULAR PLACES, IN ITS OWN WORDS: POLLUTERS PREY ON COMMUNITIES BURDENED BY RACISM, COLONIALISM, XENOPHOBIA, CLASSISM, AND OTHER KINDS OF DISCRIMINATION IN PART BECAUSE THEY KNOW THESE PLACES ARE LESS LIKELY TO HAVE THE ECONOMIC AND POLITICAL RESOURCES TO FIGHT BACK. Siting is a calculation about who can resist, stated by a litigator rather than an activist. That is the sentence to put in a submission when asked why this project was placed here and not somewhere wealthier. WHO IT SAYS BEARS THE HARM: GROUPS THAT FACE SYSTEMIC OPPRESSION, SUCH AS INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, AND COMMUNITIES WITH THE FEWEST FINANCIAL RESOURCES, DISPROPORTIONATELY SUFFER THE CONSEQUENCES OF ALL FORMS OF ENVIRONMENTAL HARM. THE COMMUNITY BENEFITS TOOL IT USES: PUSHING FOR COMMUNITY BENEFITS AGREEMENTS THAT HOLD POLLUTERS ACCOUNTABLE FOR PROVIDING GOOD JOBS, CLEAN ENERGY INFRASTRUCTURE, AND OTHER MITIGATION MEASURES IN THE PLACES THEY HAVE ALREADY HARMED. A COMMUNITY BENEFITS AGREEMENT is a binding contract between the community and the company, separate from whatever the government agreed. Where a project cannot be stopped, that is the instrument to demand — and this file has recorded far more communities accepting undocumented promises than signing one. THE UN ROUTE IT MAINTAINS: A UN REPRESENTATIVE IN GENEVA, WHOSE WORK IS DESCRIBED AS DECADES OF ADVANCING CLIMATE, ENVIRONMENT, AND HUMAN RIGHTS NORMS AND STANDARDS. THE PRECEDENT MODEL IT POINTS TO: A DECADES-LONG COLLABORATION WITH A REGIONAL PARTNER AND NATIONAL PARTNERS YIELDED A VICTORY AT A REGIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS COURT, SETTING A PRECEDENT FOR THE RIGHT TO A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT THAT WILL SUPPORT CLAIMS THROUGHOUT THAT REGION. The model is a regional human rights court judgment on the right to a healthy environment, built over decades with a regional partner. Africa has its own continental court and commission, and this file records African judgments on eviction and ancestral land already delivered — the same architecture exists here for the environmental claim. THE SCALE OF THE ORGANISATION: MORE THAN 640 STAFF MEMBERS, INCLUDING MORE THAN 240 FULL-TIME ATTORNEYS, WITH PROGRAMMES INCLUDING BIODIVERSITY DEFENSE, CLEAN ENERGY, COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS, FOSSIL FUELS, OCEANS, SUSTAINABLE FOOD AND FARMING, AND TOXIC EXPOSURE AND HEALTH. Two hundred and forty attorneys, and the OCEANS and TOXIC EXPOSURE programmes are directly relevant to African coastal and mining communities. AND THE COALITION POSTURE: WE JOIN COALITIONS IN RELATED AREAS OF JUSTICE TO MAKE OUR LEGAL TOOLS AVAILABLE TO A WIDER MOVEMENT, AND WE BRING COMMUNITIES TO THE TABLE TO ADVOCATE FOR MORE PROTECTIVE ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE LAWS — CHALLENGING SITING AND PERMITTING DECISIONS. MAKE OUR LEGAL TOOLS AVAILABLE TO A WIDER MOVEMENT. Ask for the tools, not only for representation — the pleadings, the expert evidence and the arguments from a won case transfer to the next community facing the same company. WHO IT SUITS: African coastal, fishing and mining-affected communities and the national organisations litigating for them — particularly against oil, gas and transition-mineral projects. CAVEATS: IT WORKS THROUGH PARTNER ORGANISATIONS RATHER THAN TAKING DIRECT APPROACHES, ITS AFRICAN PRESENCE IS DESCRIBED AS DEEPENING RATHER THAN ESTABLISHED, AND IT IS A US-HEADQUARTERED BODY — approach through a national or continental partner. For cases built from outside the jurisdiction, Chad's entry; for the charity that works through strategic partners and only takes cases it expects to win, Seychelles' entry.

trackers.name: Honeyguide, Tanzania — an organisation that builds the village body which holds the land rather than buying anything — 13 community-owned areas, 1.9 million hectares, 113 villages, with named governance tools a community can ask for and a rule that all staff come from member villages
trackers.desc: THEY DO NOT BUY THE LAND — THEY MAKE THE VILLAGE BODY THAT HOLDS IT WORK — method and adjacency declared first: THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THE SHIPPED HOST AND FOUR SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; THE HOST AND THE ORGANISATION'S NAME ARE ABSENT. THIS FILE'S TANZANIA BUCKET CARRIES A VOLUNTARY LAND EASEMENT ENTRY ON A DIFFERENT HOST WHICH MENTIONS THIS AREA TYPE, ITS GOVERNING BODY AND ITS SCOUTS IN PASSING — THAT ENTRY WAS READ BEFORE WRITING AND NOTHING IN IT IS RESTATED. ITS KENYA AND NAMIBIA BUCKETS CARRY NATIONAL CONSERVANCY ASSOCIATION HOSTS AND ITS LESOTHO ENTRY THE COMMUNITY CARBON PROJECT. NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHO OWNS THE LAND AND HOW THE BODY IS FORMED, WHICH IS THE FIND: THE AREA IS LAND OWNED BY LOCAL COMMUNITIES — TO CREATE ONE, VILLAGES SET ASIDE LAND AND FORM A COMMUNITY GROUP CALLED AN AUTHORIZED ASSOCIATION TO MANAGE IT; THE ASSOCIATION MAKES PLANS FOR HOW THE LAND AND WILDLIFE WILL BE USED AND GETS GOVERNMENT APPROVAL TO RUN IT. Several villages pool land into one legally recognised body they control. That is the structure this file's Lesotho entry showed a community lacking when a developer arrived — and it is built by the villages themselves, not bought or granted. THE MODEL IN ONE SENTENCE: IT WORKS LIKE A COMMUNITY BUSINESS — THE LAND BELONGS TO THE PEOPLE, THEY MANAGE IT TOGETHER, AND EVERYONE BENEFITS WHILE KEEPING WILDLIFE SAFE AND CONNECTED ACROSS THE LANDSCAPE. THE OBSTACLE THE ORGANISATION EXISTS TO REMOVE, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: A MAJOR OBSTACLE IS THE COMPLEXITY AND ABSENCE OF CLEAR, ACCESSIBLE INSTRUCTIONS FOR GOVERNANCE AND MANAGEMENT. Named honestly: the law allows the structure and nobody explains how to run it. That gap — not hostility, not money — is what kills community land bodies, and it is the entire reason this organisation exists. THE EMPLOYMENT RULE INSIDE THE STRUCTURE: EACH AREA HAS MEMBER COMMUNITIES WHO EACH CONTRIBUTED LAND TOWARDS THE DESIGNATION, AND THE EMPLOYEES OF EACH AREA SHOULD ALL COME FROM THESE MEMBER COMMUNITIES, INCLUDING FORMING THE LEADERSHIP AND MANAGEMENT TEAMS. ALL staff from the member villages, leadership included. Write that into the founding documents: it is the clause that stops a community body being captured by outsiders once revenue starts arriving. THE GOVERNANCE TOOLS IT NAMES, WHICH ARE ASKABLE FOR BY NAME: A SITE-LEVEL GOVERNANCE AND EQUITY ASSESSMENT, A GOVERNANCE CAPACITY-BUILDING FRAMEWORK, AND A GOVERNANCE IN ACTION ASSESSMENT SYSTEM. Three named instruments rather than a vague offer of training. A community body can ask for these by name and be told whether they exist for its country. WHAT THOSE TOOLS CHANGED IN ONE NAMED AREA: HOW THE GOVERNING BODY FUNCTIONS, HOW LEADERS COMMUNICATE WITH MEMBER VILLAGES, HOW DECISIONS ARE MADE AND FOLLOWED UP ON, AND HOW THE CONCERNS OF COMMUNITY MEMBERS ARE CONSIDERED AND RESOLVED — WITH TRANSPARENT MEETINGS, CLEARER ROLES BETWEEN GOVERNANCE AND MANAGEMENT, STRONGER PARTICIPATION AND VISIBILITY OF COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT INITIATIVES; GOVERNANCE BECOMES REAL WHEN IT IS BUILT INTO DAILY OPERATIONS. CLEARER ROLES BETWEEN GOVERNANCE AND MANAGEMENT is the specific failure worth naming: the same people deciding and spending is how community revenue disappears, and separating the two is a change a committee can make itself in an afternoon. THE FIVE PROGRAMME GOALS: DEVELOPING THE BUSINESS SIDE OF COMMUNITY CONSERVATION; IMPROVING MANAGEMENT AND GOVERNANCE; FACILITATING TWO-WAY COMMUNICATION FLOWS BETWEEN COMMUNITIES AND LEADERSHIP; REDUCING AND SAFELY DE-ESCALATING INSTANCES OF HUMAN-WILDLIFE CONFLICT; AND PROTECTING HABITATS FOR SUSTAINABLE USE BY HUMANS AND WILDLIFE. THE SCOUTS AND WHAT THEY ARE FOR: COMMUNITY MEMBERS TRAINED TO MONITOR AND MANAGE WILDLIFE POPULATIONS, ESCORT VISITORS, PREVENT ILLEGAL HUMAN ACTIVITIES, ENGAGE LOCAL COMMUNITIES, AND ADDRESS HUMAN-WILDLIFE CONFLICTS — WITH SUPPORT INVOLVING GUIDING MANAGEMENT TEAMS ON BEST PRACTICES, BUILDING FOUNDATIONAL INFRASTRUCTURES, PROVIDING EQUIPMENT AND PAYING SALARIES WHERE NEEDED. PAYING SALARIES WHERE NEEDED. Read beside this file's Burkina Faso entry on ranger insurance at thirty dollars a year: a community scout unit can be paid, equipped and insured through separate organisations, and neither requires the community to find the money itself. WHAT THE SETTING-UP PROCESS ACTUALLY INVOLVED IN ONE DOCUMENTED CASE: PARTICIPATORY DEMARCATION OF BOUNDARIES, DESIGNATION OF AREAS FOR SPECIFIC LAND USE PRACTICES, FORMALIZATION OF THE USER RIGHTS, TRAINING OF SCOUTS, CAPACITY BUILDING OF THE ELECTED VILLAGE REPRESENTATIVES, AND FACILITATION OF MEETINGS WITH OTHER KEY STAKEHOLDERS. Six concrete steps, in order, from a peer-reviewed account rather than a brochure. That is a plan a village can cost and start, and FORMALIZATION OF THE USER RIGHTS is the step that converts custom into something a court will recognise. THE SCALE AND THE NATIONAL PICTURE: 22 SUCH AREAS SPAN THE COUNTRY, COVERING APPROXIMATELY 3.8% OF ITS LAND — 3.58 MILLION HECTARES — AND THIS ORGANISATION DIRECTLY SUPPORTS 13, COVERING 1.9 MILLION HECTARES, ENGAGING 113 VILLAGES AND IMPACTING OVER HALF A MILLION LIVES; THE LARGEST PARTNER AREA IS 3,719 KM² AND THE SMALLEST 283 KM². The smallest is 283 square kilometres, which sets the floor: this is not a model that needs a vast landscape to work. THE FINANCING LOGIC IT STATES: STRENGTHENING INTERNAL MANAGEMENT AND GOVERNANCE CAN GENERATE LONG-TERM FINANCING, INCLUDING FROM TOURISM, CARBON AND HUNTING INVESTORS — WITH THE OBJECTIVE THAT THESE AREAS FUNCTION AS SELF-RELIANT SOCIAL ENTERPRISES. The argument runs the opposite way to most funding logic in this file: fix the governance first and the investors follow, rather than chasing money with a weak institution. Recorded plainly, hunting revenue is part of the model — a community will weigh that itself. AND WHERE THESE AREAS SIT ON THE MAP: THEY ARE USUALLY LOCATED NEXT TO NATIONAL PARKS AND HELP PROTECT WILDLIFE DISPERSAL AREAS AND CORRIDORS — WITH THE ORGANISATION'S STRATEGIC TARGET BEING AT LEAST 10 AREAS COVERING A MINIMUM OF 2,000,000 HECTARES. Land beside a national park is exactly the land most at risk of being taken for conservation or tourism without the community. This structure is the counter to that: the villages hold it and are paid from it. WHO IT SUITS: villages next to protected areas that hold or can pool communal land and want a governing body strong enough to earn from it and keep it — and existing community bodies whose governance is failing. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY'S LEGAL STRUCTURE AND ONE ORGANISATION SUPPORTING 13 AREAS, SO THE MODEL TRANSFERS BUT THE ORGANISATION DOES NOT; ITS FRAME IS WILDLIFE AND TOURISM REVENUE INCLUDING HUNTING, AND IT BUILDS CAPACITY RATHER THAN FUNDING LAND PURCHASE. For voluntary paid easements keeping village land open, Tanzania's entry; for the fund that buys land outright, Equatorial Guinea's entry.

trackers.name: Action des Chrétiens Activistes des Droits de l'Homme à Shabunda (ACADHOSHA)
trackers.desc: Action des Chrétiens Activistes des Droits de L’Homme a Shabunda (ACADHOSHA) is a Congolese civil society organisation specialising in human rights, justice, and the governance of natural resources. For over ten years, ACADHOSHA has been providing administrative and legal support to local communities and indigenous peoples who are often victims of the exploitation of natural resources.

trackers.name: Southern Africa Litigation Centre (SALC)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional litigation centre supporting and co-counselling cases across Angola, Botswana, DR Congo, Eswatini, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe. Its socio-economic rights work challenges large-scale agricultural and extractive land use that dispossesses customary landholders without adequate consent, consultation or compensation, and covers mining, pollution and climate justice — live matters include a Zambian community's pollution claim against copper processors and San and Bayei claims to ancestral land in Botswana. WHO IT SUITS: in-country lawyers and community organisations who need a partner with regional capacity and resources; SALC generally works through local counsel and partners rather than taking clients directly. SALC RESOURCES A LAWYER — IT DOES NOT REPLACE ONE. It provides technical and monetary support to local and regional lawyers and organisations litigating human rights and rule of law cases, working primarily through strategic litigation and capacity-strengthening support to lawyers and grassroots organisations. So the ask is not ‘please take my case’ but ‘please back my lawyer’ — come with a local lawyer or local organisation. It also trains human rights lawyers and facilitates networks across the region, so it is a route to finding counsel too. THE SECOND FORUM MOST PEOPLE MISS: SALC supports litigation in South African courts that advances human rights in the southern African region — so where your own courts are slow, captured or hostile, there may be another venue, and SALC is the body that supports using it. NAME THE RIGHT CLUSTER WHEN YOU APPROACH: its themes are criminal justice, civil and political rights, socio-economic rights, international criminal justice, business and human rights and equality rights — ‘environment’ is not one of them, so frame a land-defence case as business and human rights or socio-economic rights. Established 2005 in Johannesburg out of the International Bar Association and OSISA. It has also run open calls for small organisational development grants to emerging CBOs in Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe — periodic, so watch for them.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a pan-African feminist rapid-response fund with reach across all 54 African countries — small grants released quickly for unanticipated, time-critical situations rather than planned programme work, covering safety and protection needs when defenders are threatened and short windows for advocacy after an unexpected event. WHO IT SUITS: women's rights organisations, feminist collectives and movements in which women or gender-diverse people are the primary decision-makers. It does NOT fund individuals, and the action must be strategic, genuinely unanticipated, and completable in under three months. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is emergency money for a moment, not a budget for a campaign — decisions are fast and grants are modest.

trackers.name: Cour des comptes
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in DRC (Congo).

trackers.name: DR Congo — Guichet Unique de Création d’Entreprise (GUCE)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the GUCE one-stop window in Kinshasa centralises company name verification, registration & payment, Democratic Republic of the Congo. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: ITIE-RDC (EITI DR Congo)
trackers.desc: National Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative body — discloses oil, gas and mining revenues, contracts and licences in DR Congo.

trackers.name: DRC EITI Register
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: SADC Protocol on Wildlife Conservation and Law Enforcement
trackers.desc: A REGIONAL TREATY WHOSE DEFINITIONS DO REAL WORK. The SADC Protocol on Wildlife Conservation and Law Enforcement (1999, in force 2003) defines ‘taking’ as hunting, killing, injuring, capturing, harassing, collecting, picking, uprooting, digging up, cutting, destruction and removal of any wildlife species. So clearing vegetation for a development is ‘taking’ under this definition, not merely site preparation — that reframing is the most useful thing here. It defines community based wildlife management as management by a community which has the right to manage the wildlife AND to receive the benefits from that management, giving a benefit-sharing argument a treaty source; and ‘conservation’ to include rehabilitation and restoration, so restoration sits inside the defined term. THE CROSS-BORDER HOOK: States Parties must cooperate to manage shared wildlife resources as well as any transfrontier effects of activities within their jurisdiction or control — a mine, dam or plantation whose effects cross a border engages a treaty duty on the state that authorised it. Article 4 objectives include enforcing wildlife laws within, between and among States Parties and facilitating community-based natural resources management. CHECK YOUR STATE HAS RATIFIED — the Protocol is legally binding only for countries that have signed and ratified it, and this entry does not assert that your state has. ON TFCAs: they encompass protected areas as well as multiple resource use areas, so they are not exclusion zones; a TFCA practitioners network founded September 2013 has membership open to all stakeholder groups. And SADC's own 2023–2033 TFCA programme names the marginalisation of communities living in and around protected areas as a problem it exists to address — quotable against the body that wrote it.

trackers.name: Réseau CREF — has secured perpetual community forest titles over 223,000 hectares in North Kivu, and will walk a community through the same process
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a platform of about thirty environmental NGOs working in North Kivu since 2003, whose measurable output is the thing itself — more than 223,000 hectares secured for communities under perpetual community forest concession titles, with further applications sitting on the Governor's desk for signature. IN CONGOLESE LAW THIS IS THE CLOSEST THING TO BUYING YOUR LAND: article 22 of the 2002 forest code lets a forest community apply for a concession over forest it already holds by custom, and the resulting Concession Forestière des Communautés Locales is granted free of charge and in perpetuity by provincial decree. It is not a purchase and not a lease; it is recognition, and it converts customary forest into a title an outsider cannot be allocated over. WHY YOU NEED AN ORGANISATION AND NOT JUST THE LAW: the application requires a participatory map of the forest terroir agreed with neighbouring communities, proof of who is customarily entitled to act for the community, a local administrative enquiry on the ground, and afterwards a simple management plan approved locally — which is why every concession granted in the country so far has been supported by an NGO or civil society partner, communities lacking the money and technical knowledge to complete it alone. Réseau CREF works inside the Forêts d'Avenir consortium with Rainforest Foundation UK and Congolese partners including PREPPYG, APEM, CAGDFT and GASHE; two Lubero communities it supported began in 2021, received their titles in early 2024 and had their management plans approved in March 2025 despite an extremely precarious security situation. WHO IT SUITS: forest communities and indigenous peoples in North Kivu, and — through the consortium partners — Équateur, Mai-Ndombe, Maniema, Tshopo, Tshuapa and Kwilu. CAVEATS: the process is slow, intermediary-heavy and, as researchers warn, can be captured — without supervision a community concession can exclude vulnerable groups or sharpen local tensions, so insist on who is named as customarily entitled before the file is lodged. Areas are capped and land hunger in North Kivu means the forest available per person can be a fraction of a hectare. THE INSTRUMENT'S NATIONAL TERMS, WHICH ARE THE BEST IN THE REGION AND WORTH QUOTING BACK AT ANY OFFICIAL: community forestry in DR Congo is governed by the Forest Code and decree n°14/018 of 2 August 2014, which sets the conditions and procedure by which a LOCAL COMMUNITY acquires a forest concession over forests it regularly possesses BY CUSTOM — and the defining features are that the concession is MULTI-USE, granted FREE OF CHARGE, and PERPETUAL. Free and perpetual is a combination no other route in this file offers: there is no fee to find and no renewal date at which someone can decline. Since 2016 the DRC has adopted a National Strategy on Community Forestry. WHAT THAT HAS PRODUCED IN PRACTICE, and the numbers are the argument for starting a file: one programme reports 17 community forests created across Equateur, Maniema and North-Kivu provinces, covering 154,000 hectares and serving over 25,000 people; an earlier phase set up nine pilot sites in Equateur and North-Kivu. A NAMED WORKED EXAMPLE TO POINT AT: in September 2018 the community of Ilinga in Equateur — whose name means “Unity” — received its official community forest title over 3,393 hectares it had traditionally owned and managed for generations, granted in perpetuity, supported by a local Congolese NGO within a consortium of Congolese and international organisations. Ask which consortium organisation covers your province before assembling a file — the work is organised by province and by partner, not nationally. THE CEILING AND THE PROTECTION, THE TWO NUMBERS THIS ENTRY LACKED: a concession forestière des communautés locales may be granted UP TO 50,000 HECTARES per local community — ten times the Cameroonian community-forest ceiling recorded in this file — and it is attributed FREE OF CHARGE AND IN PERPETUITY, which together make it the strongest community land hold in the Congo Basin. If you are choosing between instruments across a border, the CFCL is the one that does not expire and does not have to be renewed. WHAT TO PUT IN THE APPLICATION FILE, BECAUSE THE FILE IS WHERE THESE FAIL: the request goes through the customary chief on behalf of the community, with the community's boundaries and its neighbours' agreement established BEFORE submission — the same boundary-first rule this file records for Cameroon, Senegal and Eswatini. Settle the boundary with your neighbours first; a contested edge is what stalls a file for years.

trackers.name: IBGDH, Kolwezi — the lawyers who cite Annexe XVIII at mining relocations, and the text every displaced Congolese household should quote
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Initiative pour la Bonne Gouvernance et les Droits Humains (IBGDH), an ASBL based at Kolwezi in Lualaba — the centre of the world's cobalt supply — led by a practising lawyer, working across Lualaba in particular and DR Congo generally on mining-related displacement and pollution. THE INSTRUMENT IT USES, AND THE ONE TO NAME IN ANY LETTER: Annexe XVIII of the Mining Regulation, which sets out the stages of relocation, the rights of each party and the obligations of the institutions involved. IBGDH's reading of its article 18 is the sentence to quote: whatever criteria and scale are agreed, the loss of housing, of community infrastructure and of rights must be covered. It publicly held that a Chinese-owned mining company breached Annexe XVIII and the provincial relocation edict in moving residents of a Kolwezi neighbourhood and a nearby village, and that the provincial government took part in forced evictions without guaranteeing communities their right of access to remedies, to dignified resettlement and to just and equitable compensation. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DELIVERS FOR RESIDENTS: public open days bringing affected communities together with the provincial land, planning and housing officials; documented demands to halt operations — including a call to stop a company's works at Kolwezi over air, water, soil and noise pollution affecting named neighbourhoods; and a joint report with an international human rights organisation on forced evictions in industrial cobalt and copper mines, presented at the national mining week, backed by reportedly more than 70,000 signatures against the evictions. It has demanded a presidential moratorium on all mining-related relocations and an independent inquiry. WHO IT SUITS: households and villages in the Congolese copper-cobalt belt facing relocation, house damage from blasting, loss of farmland or mine pollution. CAVEATS: an advocacy, documentation and legal-support organisation, not a compensation agent — note the province's own position that it is the CONCESSION HOLDER, not the state, that relocates, with the state only accompanying; for community forest concessions in the east, DR Congo's Réseau CREF entry is the other route.

trackers.name: DR Congo's Bureaux de Consultations Gratuites — free legal consultation at each bar, Monday to Friday 9h-16h, on production of an attestation d'indigence
trackers.desc: WHERE TO WALK IN: the BUREAUX DE CONSULTATIONS GRATUITES (BCG), run by the bar associations, which provide judicial assistance and legal advice to indigent people ON PRODUCTION OF AN ATTESTATION D'INDIGENCE. In Kinshasa two bars operate them and their coverage is published by commune: the Gombe BCG serves 14 communes — Gombe, Ngiri-Ngiri, Kasa-Vubu, Kalamu, Barumbu, Kinshasa, Selembao, Bumbu, Makala, Lingwala, Mont-Ngafula, Ngaliema, Bandalungwa and Kintambo — at avenue Kasa-Vubu n°87 at the Birmanie junction, Ngiri-Ngiri; the Matete BCG at n°1392 avenue Bakali, commune of Lemba. Consultations run every day MONDAY TO FRIDAY, 9h to 16h. Get the attestation d'indigence FIRST — as in Côte d'Ivoire, the poverty certificate is the document that opens the door, and turning up without it wastes the trip. Reported traffic gives a realistic sense of scale: one bureau received 85 people in a single month, 28 women and 57 men. THE INDEPENDENT ASSESSMENT, RECORDED BECAUSE IT SETS EXPECTATIONS: an evaluation for the EU justice reform programme found the BCG system globally EMBRYONIC, particularly in the western provinces — often a single bureau in the provincial capital, attached to the bar — too strictly built on mobilising TRAINEE ADVOCATES who are insufficiently supervised and supported, with no proactive strategy toward litigants. So expect a junior lawyer, expect the capital, and bring your own documents in order. WHO IT SUITS: Congolese city residents — above all in Kinshasa — needing free advice on an eviction, land or family matter. CAVEATS: ADVICE AND ASSISTANCE THROUGH THE BAR, NOT A CAMPAIGNING BODY, donor-supported and thin outside the main cities. For community forest concessions and the free perpetual CFCL route, DR Congo's Réseau CREF entry; for mining relocation in the copper-cobalt belt and Annexe XVIII, IBGDH.

trackers.name: DGPA — the DRC network of 43 indigenous associations with provincial antennas, and the direct forest fund built to cut out the intermediaries that absorb the money
trackers.desc: THE NETWORK WITH FORTY-THREE MEMBERS AND PROVINCIAL ANTENNAS: the DYNAMIQUE DES GROUPES DES PEUPLES AUTOCHTONES (DGPA) is a NATIONAL NETWORK CURRENTLY GROUPING 43 ASSOCIATIONS OR ORGANISATIONS OF PYGMY PEOPLES AND THOSE ACCOMPANYING THEM IN THE DRC, ESTABLISHED IN THE PROVINCES WHERE THEY ARE GROUPED INTO ANTENNES. It has built experience in ADVOCACY AND LOBBYING for indigenous Pygmy peoples and other local communities, and know-how in ENCADREMENT, CLOSE-PROXIMITY ACCOMPANIMENT and progressive capacity building — which has enabled THE PARTICIPATION OF COMMUNITIES IN THE DIFFERENT PROCESSES TOUCHING THE FORESTS, with the aim that their TRADITIONAL RIGHTS AND PRACTICES be taken into account. ITS FOREST INTERVENTION AXES INCLUDE MONITORING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE FOREST AND AGRICULTURAL CODES AND THE ENVIRONMENT LAW. Forty-three member associations with an antenna in your province means you do not have to reach Kinshasa — find the antenna. And a network whose stated job is monitoring whether the forest code is actually implemented is the one to tell when it is not. THE TWO FACTS TO KNOW BEFORE ANY FUND OR RESERVE ARRIVES, RECORDED PLAINLY: IN THE DRC THE CONSTITUTION PROVIDES THAT LAND BELONGS TO THE STATE, AND THE GOVERNMENT DOES NOT RECOGNISE THE RIGHT OF POPULATIONS TO GIVE THEIR CONSENT TO PROJECTS — indigenous peoples and local communities hold ONLY A CUSTOMARY TITLE over the land they have long depended on. That is why the perpetual community forest concession in this file's DRC record matters so much: it converts a customary claim into a document. Get the concession; consent alone will not be recognised. AND THE MONEY LESSON, IN A COORDINATOR'S OWN TERMS: DGPA's national coordinator for indigenous peoples observes that THIS TYPE OF FUND GENERALLY TRANSITS THROUGH LARGE INTERNATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, AND THERE THE BUDGET IS ALLOCATED TO THE INSTITUTION'S OPERATING COSTS AND LOGISTICS — and in response, INDIGENOUS AND LOCAL COMMUNITY NETWORKS COLLABORATED WITH TWO INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS TO CREATE A FOREST FACILITY FUND WITH FEWER INTERMEDIARIES, announced for communities protecting forests in the DRC. Ask any funder how many hands the money passes through before it reaches the village, and ask whether a direct facility exists for your case. In the DRC one now does. A CAUTION FROM A RECENT ANNOUNCEMENT: a 54,000 km2 conservation corridor was created by ministerial arrêté, and concerns raised immediately included THE ABSENCE OF PRIOR CONSULTATION AND THE NON-RESPECT OF FREE, PRIOR AND INFORMED CONSENT of the local communities concerned during the design phase. A protected area can arrive on your land as fast as a mine can. Ask when the consultation was held and who signed for your community. WHO IT SUITS: Congolese indigenous and forest communities, and anyone facing a conservation or carbon scheme. CAVEATS: AN ADVOCACY NETWORK, NOT A FUNDER OR LAW FIRM. For perpetual community forest title, DR Congo's Réseau CREF entry; for lawyers citing Annexe XVIII at mine sites, IBGDH; for free legal consultation, the Bureaux de Consultations Gratuites entry.

trackers.name: Réseau Ressources Naturelles and the GTCR-R — two Congolese civil society platforms inside the national forest process, with a Kinshasa street address, four phone lines, and the demands they filed in writing
trackers.desc: THE PLATFORM WITH FOUR PHONE NUMBERS AND TEN DEMANDS: RÉSEAU RESSOURCES NATURELLES (RRN/RDC) DESCRIBES ITSELF AS A PLATE-FORME NATIONALE DE MONITORING ET DE GOUVERNANCE, with a national coordination at AVENUE DU PROGRÈS N°251, KINSHASA-BARUMBU, PUBLISHING FOUR TELEPHONE NUMBERS, TWO EMAIL ADDRESSES AND A WEBSITE. A national MONITORING and governance platform is a different animal from an advocacy NGO: monitoring means it collects what is happening on the ground and holds it. If your forest is being cut, that is a body whose stated function is to record it — and four published lines means somebody answers. THE PLATFORM THAT WAS REBUILT, AND WHY IT MATTERS: THE GROUPE DE TRAVAIL CLIMAT REDD GAVE WAY TO A GROUPE DE TRAVAIL CLIMAT REDD RÉNOVÉ (GTCR-R), BUILT IN A PARTICIPATORY MANNER, WITH A MORE ROBUST NATIONAL FUNCTIONING AND A STRONG ANCHORING IN THE PROVINCES, AS CLOSE AS POSSIBLE TO THE FOREST COMMUNITIES, TO GUARANTEE THEIR TOTAL INVOLVEMENT — AND THE PROCESS WAS A SUCCESS AND EVEN INSPIRED OTHER PLATFORMS, IN DRC AND BEYOND. A civil society platform that rebuilt itself to put its weight in the provinces rather than in the capital, and that the record says other platforms then copied. If the body claiming to represent forest communities in your country meets only in the capital, GTCR-R is the precedent for demanding provincial anchoring — and it is named in the state's own REDD+ safeguards submission as the platform in which civil society is grouped, so the government deals with it. THE DEMANDS IT PUT IN WRITING TO A WORLD BANK AND UN MISSION, AND THESE ARE THE THREE TO REUSE: THE URGENCY AND NECESSITY OF PARTICIPATORY ZONING MUST CLEARLY EMERGE IN THE DOCUMENT AND BE CONSIDERED A PRECONDITION FOR IMPLEMENTATION; THE DOCUMENT MUST INDICATE THE NECESSITY OF CLARIFYING THE CUSTOMARY LAND REGIME AND LAND PROPERTY RIGHTS; AND MAINTAINING THE MORATORIUM MUST BE CONSIDERED INDISPENSABLE. Zoning as a PRECONDITION, not a later step. That is the single most transferable demand in this entry: before any forest-carbon or conservation scheme is implemented on your land, insist the participatory zoning happens first — because once the scheme is running, the map it used becomes the map that counts. It also objected that the document SEEMED TO SETTLE A POSITION ON THE DRIVER OF DEFORESTATION BEFORE CONSENSUS ON THE ACTUAL AND FUTURE DRIVERS HAD BEEN REACHED on the basis of the studies underway. Naming the cause of deforestation before the studies are finished decides who gets blamed and who pays. Watch for it, and object in the same terms. THE CONVENOR: THE CENTRE DES TECHNOLOGIES INNOVATRICES ET LE DÉVELOPPEMENT DURABLE (CTIDD, ctidd-rdc.org) BROUGHT TOGETHER GTCR-R MEMBERS AND ALLIED ENVIRONMENTAL CIVIL SOCIETY ACTORS TO ASK THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY TO FINALISE ITS EXAMINATION OF A BILL ON TERRITORIAL PLANNING — SO AS TO GIVE THE COUNTRY ITS FIRST TERRITORIAL PLANNING POLICY SINCE INDEPENDENCE — and made the declaration public. A country with no territorial planning policy at all is one where every overlapping concession is legal by default. If that bill matters to your case, CTIDD is who is already pushing it. AND THE TOOL FOR A VILLAGE MEETING: THE TWO PLATFORMS PRODUCED ABC REDD — COMPRENDRE REDD ET SES ENJEUX, A PRELIMINARY PEDAGOGICAL DOCUMENT WRITTEN BECAUSE CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS DID NOT ALL HAVE THE SAME LEVEL OF KNOWLEDGE, AND EXPLICITLY INTENDED AS A TOOL THAT CAN SERVE AS AN INFORMATION FRAMEWORK FOR LOCAL LEADERS TO UNDERSTAND THE ISSUES AND PARTICIPATE IN DECISION-MAKING AT NATIONAL, REGIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL LEVEL. A primer written by Congolese platforms for Congolese local leaders, on the assumption that nobody starts knowing this. Ask for ABC REDD by name before you sit down opposite a carbon project developer. WHO IT SUITS: Congolese forest communities facing a carbon or conservation scheme, and anyone needing monitoring, a provincial platform or a primer. CAVEATS: PLATFORMS AND COALITIONS, not litigators; parts of this record date from the REDD+ preparation years — confirm current membership. For perpetual community forest titles over 223,000 hectares, DRC's Réseau CREF entry; for the lawyers who cite Annexe XVIII at mining relocations, IBGDH; for 43 indigenous associations with provincial antennas, DGPA; for free consultation at each bar, the Bureaux de Consultations Gratuites entry.

trackers.name: MappingForRights — low-cost participatory mapping that has put over seven million hectares and a thousand Congo Basin communities on the map, with printed maps for the village, an online atlas, and an alert system that reaches law enforcement
trackers.desc: SEVEN MILLION HECTARES, MAPPED BY THE PEOPLE LIVING ON THEM — placement note first: THIS INITIATIVE COVERS FIVE CONGO BASIN COUNTRIES — CAMEROON, THE CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC, THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, THE REPUBLIC OF CONGO AND GABON — AND IS FILED UNDER DR CONGO BECAUSE IT IS BEING EXPANDED THERE AND THE NAMED PROVINCIAL CASE SITS HERE. WHAT IT DOES: IT ENABLES COMMUNITIES TO MAP THEIR LANDS THROUGH LOW-COST, TRANSFERRABLE TECHNOLOGIES AND A PARTICIPATORY MAPPING METHODOLOGY DEVELOPED ON THE BACK OF MORE THAN 20 YEARS OF FIELD EXPERIENCE — EQUIPPING FOREST GUARDIANS WITH SIMPLE, LOW-COST TOOLS TO MAP, MONITOR AND PROTECT THEIR LANDS. LOW-COST and TRANSFERRABLE are the two words that matter. Transferrable means the community keeps the skill after the project leaves, which is the difference between being mapped once and being able to map again when the boundary is challenged. THE SCALE, AND IT IS THE ANSWER TO ANYONE WHO SAYS THIS CANNOT BE DONE: SINCE ITS FORMAL LAUNCH IN 2011, MORE THAN A THOUSAND CENTRAL AFRICAN COMMUNITIES HAVE MAPPED OVER SEVEN MILLION HECTARES OF RAINFOREST — AN AREA NEARLY THE SIZE OF SCOTLAND. A thousand communities, seven million hectares, in roughly a decade. If your village is told community mapping is impractical, that is the number to put on the table. THE PROBLEM IT NAMES, IN ITS OWN WORDS, AND IT IS WORTH QUOTING BACK: TYPICALLY THESE GROUPS LACK FORMAL RIGHTS TO AREAS THEY HAVE INHABITED AND PROTECTED FOR GENERATIONS AND ARE LARGELY EXCLUDED FROM DECISIONS ABOUT THE FORESTS THEY DEPEND ON — THIS LEAVES MANY AS SQUATTERS ON THEIR OWN LANDS, LIVING IN VERY POOR CONDITIONS ON THE EDGE OF LOGGING CONCESSIONS AND STRICTLY PROTECTED AREAS. SQUATTERS ON THEIR OWN LANDS. That phrase describes most of the communities in this file, and the cause is named as the absence of reliable information about their use and possession of the forest — which is precisely what a map supplies. WHAT THE MAPS ACHIEVED: THE COMMUNITY MAPS HAVE PLAYED A KEY ROLE IN PROMOTING THE RIGHTS OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES IN LAND REFORMS, IN THE MANAGEMENT OF PROTECTED AREAS AND REDD+ PROGRAMMES, AS WELL AS THE ESTABLISHMENT OF COMMUNITY FORESTS. THE TWO OUTPUTS, AND YOU WANT BOTH: DATA IS MADE AVAILABLE TO AUTHORIZED USERS THROUGH AN ONLINE INTERACTIVE COMMUNITY ATLAS WHERE IT CAN BE ANALYSED IN THE CONTEXT OF OTHER FOREST USES — AND COMMUNITIES ARE ALSO PROVIDED WITH ACCURATE PRINTED MAPS OF THEIR LANDS. A printed map in the village and a digital layer in the atlas. The printed one is what you carry to a meeting with the sub-prefect; the digital one is what shows your land against the concession boundaries. A mapping offer that gives you only one of the two is half a service — ask for both. AND WHAT THE ATLAS REVEALS: a published map showing THE OVERLAP BETWEEN CUSTOMARY RIGHTS AND FORMAL LAND ALLOCATIONS in a named DRC province that hosts the world's largest jurisdictional deforestation-reduction programme. An overlap map is the single most powerful document a community can hold: your land, drawn by you, laid over the concession the ministry granted. The argument stops being about whether you are there. WHAT COMES AFTER THE MAP: WITH LEGAL SECURITY OVER THEIR LANDS, THE PROGRAMME ALSO PROVIDES COMMUNITIES WITH A SET OF TOOLS AND APPROACHES TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT SUSTAINABLE LAND-USE PLANS FOR THESE AREAS. Mapping first, then a land-use plan the community writes. That order matters — a plan without a recognised boundary is advice, and a boundary without a plan invites someone else to propose a use. THE ALERT SYSTEM: A COMMUNITY FOREST MONITORING INITIATIVE ALLOWS USERS TO MONITOR LOCAL FORESTS, CONNECTING THEM WITH LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCIES TO IMPROVE ANTI-DEFORESTATION MEASURES, AND A NAMED SYSTEM SENDS INFORMATION ABOUT ILLEGAL DEFORESTATION TO LAW ENFORCEMENT — WITH A PAYMENT FOR PERFORMANCE SYSTEM TO BE TRIALLED WHEREBY COMMUNITIES COULD BE REWARDED FOR VERIFIED ILLEGAL LOGGING ALERTS USING EMERGING MOBILE BANKING SERVICES. Paid, by mobile money, for a verified alert. This file has recorded villagers reporting illegal logging at their own cost and risk; being paid for a verified report changes monitoring from a burden into a livelihood, and the verification requirement protects against false alerts. AND THE ACCOUNTABILITY SITE FOR CONSERVATION ITSELF: AN INTERACTIVE WEBSITE AIMS AT INCREASING THE TRANSPARENCY AND ACCOUNTABILITY OF CONSERVATION PROJECTS ACROSS THE CONGO BASIN AND SHOWING HOW SUCH PROJECTS HAVE IMPACTED ON LOCAL PEOPLE, FEATURING 34 PROTECTED AREAS — with the finding that PROTECTED AREAS IN AFRICA'S GREAT EQUATORIAL RAINFORESTS ARE FALLING WELL BELOW EXPECTATIONS BOTH IN TERMS OF CONSERVING WILDLIFE AND RESPECTING LOCAL PEOPLES' RIGHTS. Thirty-four protected areas assessed on how they treated the people living there, published by a forest organisation rather than a critic of conservation. If a protected area is proposed near you, look up whether it is on that list first. WHO IT SUITS: Congo Basin forest communities in the five named countries, especially those beside a concession or a proposed protected area. CAVEATS: THE ATLAS IS OPEN TO AUTHORIZED USERS — access is mediated, so ask what your community can see and control about its own data. For perpetual community forest titles over 223,000 hectares, DR Congo's Réseau CREF entry; for the participatory mapping and picture-box service in Cameroon, the boîte à images entry; for the organisation that presented village maps to the administrators, Cameroon's AJESH entry.

trackers.name: Well Grounded — the one thing no funder pays for — coaching, strategy and leadership development for the organisation itself, from a non-profit registered in Cameroon as well as the UK, working with informal groups as well as formal ones across five Congo Basin countries
trackers.desc: SOMEBODY WHO FIXES THE ORGANISATION RATHER THAN FUNDING THE PROJECT — an off-brief note first, recorded honestly: THIS ROUND FIRST EXAMINED A WILDLIFE LAW AND JUSTICE PROGRAMME THAT TRAINS PROSECUTORS AND MAGISTRATES, AND DID NOT FILE IT. IT EQUIPS THE STATE TO PROSECUTE WILDLIFE CRIME, WHICH IS NOT SOMETHING A COMMUNITY CAN USE TO STOP A PROJECT ON ITS LAND. THE PROBLEM THIS ONE NAMES, AND THE SECOND HALF IS RARE ENOUGH TO QUOTE: CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS IN THE CONGO BASIN ARE UNDERFUNDED AND OVERSTRETCHED AND OFTEN STRUGGLE TO DEVELOP STRATEGIES AND SYSTEMS TO IMPROVE THEIR EFFECTIVENESS — AND THE INTERNATIONAL FUNDER AND NGO COMMUNITY CAN CONTRIBUTE TO THIS SITUATION, AS THEY DO NOT TYPICALLY INVEST IN CORE SUPPORT FOR ORGANISATIONS. Every funder in this file pays for activities and refuses to pay for the organisation. That is why community bodies collapse between grants, why the accounts are never audited, why the committee stops meeting, and why the next application is weaker than the last. Here is an organisation whose entire purpose is that gap — and it says out loud that its own sector caused it. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES: ORGANISATION DEVELOPMENT BY OFFERING DIAGNOSIS, ANALYSIS AND EVALUATION, FOLLOWED BY FACILITATION, COACHING AND WORKSHOPS TO ADDRESS PRIORITIES THAT THEY AND THEIR CLIENTS IDENTIFY TOGETHER. PRIORITIES THAT THEY AND THEIR CLIENTS IDENTIFY TOGETHER — not a curriculum brought in a suitcase. The diagnosis comes first, which means the work starts from what is actually broken in your organisation rather than what the trainer already knows how to teach. THE ELIGIBILITY LINE THAT MATTERS MOST: THERE ARE LOCAL ORGANISATIONS, BOTH FORMAL AND INFORMAL, THAT ARE SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES TO DEVELOP THEIR OWN INITIATIVES AND TO HAVE A VOICE — AND IT AIMS TO SUPPORT THESE ORGANISATIONS TO BECOME MORE EFFECTIVE AND INCREASE THEIR IMPACT. FORMAL AND INFORMAL. An unregistered village association is inside the definition, which this file has recorded as the gate that shuts almost everything else. WHERE IT IS REGISTERED, WHICH CHANGES WHO CAN REACH IT: A REGISTERED NON-PROFIT IN BOTH THE UNITED KINGDOM AND CAMEROON, FOUNDED IN 2010 IN DIRECT RESPONSE TO THE CHALLENGES FACED BY LOCAL ORGANISATIONS AND THEIR LEADERS IN THE CONGO BASIN. A Cameroonian registration means an office on the continent, in a country where the work happens, subject to local law. Ask any international organisation offering your group support whether it is registered anywhere in Africa — the answer tells you how reachable it will be when something goes wrong. THE COUNTRIES: CAMEROON, THE CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC, THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO, GABON AND THE REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO. THE THREE FOCUS AREAS: IDENTITY AND STRATEGY; LEADERSHIP AND MANAGEMENT; AND BUILDING A MORE DIVERSE AND INCLUSIVE CIVIL SOCIETY. LEADERSHIP AND MANAGEMENT is the unglamorous one and the one that decides survival. This file has recorded organisations lost when a founder left, a committee stopped meeting, or nobody could keep the receipts — none of which is a legal or financial problem. THE NAMED PROGRAMMES FROM ITS OWN ANNUAL REPORT: ORGANISATION DEVELOPMENT FOR CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS; ECOFEMINIST WOMEN'S LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT; INDIGENOUS PEOPLES LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT; AND TRANSFORMING POWER FOR AN ENABLING ENVIRONMENT. Separate leadership programmes for women and for Indigenous peoples, run as their own streams rather than as a quota inside a general course. If your organisation is led by forest peoples or by women, there is a door addressed specifically to you. THE OPEN APPLICATION ROUTE, WHICH IS HOW AN INDIVIDUAL GETS IN: A LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME WITH A PUBLIC APPLICATION PROCESS FOR INDIVIDUALS BASED IN A NAMED COUNTRY, FOR MANAGERS AND STAFF OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS — CREATING OPPORTUNITIES FOR DIRECTORS, MANAGERS AND TEAM LEADERS TO MEET AND REFLECT. Applications open by country, one at a time. So watch for the round covering yours rather than assuming the programme is closed — and it is individuals who apply, not organisations, which means one person can bring it back. THE PEER LINKING: IT FACILITATES LINKS AND EXCHANGES WITH OTHER ORGANISATIONS IN THE REGION OR INTERNATIONALLY TO ENABLE PEER-TO-PEER LEARNING AND MENTORING, AND CONNECTS ORGANISATIONS IN THE REGION TO BUILD A STRONG CIVIL SOCIETY VOICE. WHAT THE ORGANISATIONS IT SUPPORTS DO: CHAMPION ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE, EMPOWER LOCAL COMMUNITIES, CONDUCT RESEARCH AND EDUCATION, MONITOR STAKEHOLDERS, BUILD PARTNERSHIPS, AND ENGAGE IN POLICY ADVOCACY. THE STATED BELIEF BEHIND IT ALL: CHANGE IN COUNTRIES SUCH AS THOSE OF THE CONGO BASIN WILL NOT TAKE PLACE UNTIL PEOPLE LIVING IN THE COUNTRY AND DEPENDENT ON NATURAL RESOURCES FOR THEIR LIVELIHOODS HAVE A SAY IN THE MANAGEMENT AND DECISION MAKING CONCERNING THOSE RESOURCES. AND THE SCALE OF WHAT IS AT STAKE: THE CONGO BASIN SUPPORTS THE LIVELIHOODS OF 80 MILLION PEOPLE, INCLUDING MANY INDIGENOUS FOREST PEOPLES — BUT IN MANY AREAS THIS ECOSYSTEM AND ITS RESOURCES ARE NOT MANAGED IN A WAY THAT BENEFITS LOCAL COMMUNITIES. Eighty million livelihoods. A forest campaign in this basin is not a minority interest, and saying so with that figure changes how a ministry or a funder reads the same request. WHO IT SUITS: Congo Basin organisations — formal or informal — that keep losing ground not for want of a case but for want of strategy, records, leadership or succession. CAVEATS: FIVE COUNTRIES ONLY, AND IT STRENGTHENS ORGANISATIONS RATHER THAN FUNDING PROJECTS OR PROVIDING LEGAL HELP — pair it with the funders and lawyers filed elsewhere here. For the participatory mapping of community forest land, DR Congo's MappingForRights entry; for the free community fund built with no outside capital, Djibouti's savings-group entry; for the fund that waives registration entirely, the Central African Republic's entry.

trackers.name: CIEL (Center for International Environmental Law) — an environmental law organisation whose published goal is legal tools whose potential far exceeds its own capacity to use them — with a People, Land and Resources programme, an honest note that it is not a law firm, and a fellowship that has trained 500+ lawyers from 54 countries
trackers.desc: THEY BUILD TOOLS BIGGER THAN THEMSELVES, ON PURPOSE — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S TOGO ENTRY COVERS A PRO BONO LEGAL SERVICE CARRYING 100+ COMMUNITY CASES A YEAR, ITS ETHIOPIA ENTRY SENIOR AND RETIRED LAWYERS ON ATTORNEY-CLIENT TERMS, ITS SEYCHELLES ENTRY THE CO-COMPLAINANT ROUTE TO THE CONTINENTAL COURT, AND ITS CÔTE D'IVOIRE ENTRY THE DEVELOPMENT-FINANCE CAMPAIGNING ORGANISATION. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE STATED AIM, WHICH IS THE FIND: THEIR GOAL IS TO CREATE NEW LEGAL TOOLS WHOSE POTENTIAL FAR EXCEEDS THEIR OWN CAPACITY TO USE THEM — SEEKING TO EMPOWER COMMUNITIES AND NGOs FAR BEYOND THOSE WITH WHOM THEY WORK DIRECTLY, AND BUILDING LEGAL LEVERS FOR CHANGE THAT WILL BE EFFECTIVE NOT ONLY FOR THEMSELVES AND THEIR PARTNERS, BUT FOR OTHERS FAR BEYOND THEIR REACH. An organisation designing its work so that people who will never contact it can use the result. That is the opposite of the capacity problem this file records everywhere — a good organisation with a waiting list. What they produce is meant to be picked up by a community that never asked, which makes their published analysis worth reading even if they never take your case. THE HONEST DISTINCTION THEY PUBLISH ABOUT WHAT THEY ARE NOT, AND IT SAVES A WASTED APPROACH: UNLIKE A LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL LAW FIRM THAT USUALLY REPRESENTS CLIENTS IN A SPECIFIC COURT OR AGENCY MATTER, IT FOCUSES ON BROADER LEGAL AND POLICY STRATEGIES — WHICH CAN INCLUDE LEGAL RESEARCH, ADVOCACY BEFORE INTERNATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, SUPPORT FOR COMMUNITY AND CIVIL-SOCIETY PARTNERS, AND LEGAL ANALYSIS THAT HELPS COURTS, GOVERNMENTS AND ADVOCATES UNDERSTAND ENVIRONMENTAL LAW. They will not appear for you in your district court. Read that before spending a month on an approach — and note what they WILL do: advocacy before international institutions and support for a community partner, which is the Seychelles-style route rather than the local one. THE FOUR CROSS-CUTTING APPROACHES: BUILDING AND STRENGTHENING INTERNATIONAL LAW AND SYSTEMS TO PROTECT HUMAN RIGHTS AND THE ENVIRONMENT; EMPOWERING COMMUNITIES TO USE INTERNATIONAL LAW TO DEFEND THEIR RIGHTS; DEVELOPING AND ADVOCATING NEW STRATEGIES AND GLOBAL STANDARDS FOR INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL FLOWS; AND STRENGTHENING THE LEGAL TOOLS TO COUNTERBALANCE CORPORATE POWER AND INCREASE TRANSBOUNDARY CORPORATE ACCOUNTABILITY. TRANSBOUNDARY CORPORATE ACCOUNTABILITY — suing or pressing a parent company in its home country for what its subsidiary did on your land. This file records that route under its home-country contact point and supply-chain entries; here is an organisation building the legal tools for it. THE IMPLEMENTATION ARGUMENT IT MAKES, WHICH IS THIS FILE'S RECURRING FINDING: GLOBAL PROCESSES MUST STRENGTHEN REGIONAL AND NATIONAL SYSTEMS TO ENSURE EFFECTIVE IMPLEMENTATION OF INTERNATIONAL OBLIGATIONS — THE BEST RESPONSE BEING TO ENSURE THAT LAW RESPONDS TO EXISTING NEEDS, CONTINUALLY ADAPTS TO CHANGING REALITIES AND, ABOVE ALL, LEADS TO REAL CHANGES IN POLICY, HUMAN BEHAVIOR AND ENVIRONMENTAL OUTCOMES. A treaty your government signed does nothing until a national court or ministry applies it. Arguing for implementation of an existing obligation is narrower and more winnable than arguing for a new one — the same conclusion this file reaches from Burundi to Kenya. THE FOUR PROGRAMME AREAS: CLIMATE & ENERGY; ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH; FOSSIL ECONOMY; AND PEOPLE, LAND & RESOURCES. PEOPLE, LAND & RESOURCES is a standing programme, not a project. That is where a land or forest matter belongs when approaching them. WHAT THE TEAM PROVIDES: ATTORNEYS, POLICY EXPERTS AND SUPPORT STAFF PROVIDING LEGAL COUNSEL AND ADVOCACY, POLICY RESEARCH, AND CAPACITY BUILDING — WITH A FOCUS ON CONNECTING GLOBAL CHALLENGES TO THE EXPERIENCES OF COMMUNITIES ON THE GROUND. THE PARTNERSHIP COMMITMENT: IN THE PROCESS, IT BUILDS AND MAINTAINS LASTING PARTNERSHIPS WITH COMMUNITIES AND NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATIONS AROUND THE WORLD. THE POSTURE IT STATES ABOUT TARGETS: WE ARE NOT AFRAID TO USE BOLD STRATEGIES THAT TARGET POWERFUL ACTORS AND THE SYSTEMS THAT ENABLE THEM, IN ORDER TO BUILD AND MAINTAIN TRUST WITH COMMUNITIES AND PARTNERS. Trust with communities given as the reason for confronting powerful actors, rather than the risk of doing so. This file has recorded organisations that soften a case to protect a funding relationship; this is the published opposite, and it is a question worth asking any prospective ally directly. THE ISSUES IT COVERS: CLIMATE CHANGE, FOSSIL FUELS, TOXIC POLLUTION, PLASTICS, LAND RIGHTS, AND THE PROTECTION OF COMMUNITIES FACING ENVIRONMENTAL HARM — ALONGSIDE ACCESS RIGHTS, INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS, BIODIVERSITY, LAW AND COMMUNITIES, CHEMICALS, PETROCHEMICALS, CLIMATE LITIGATION AND CLIMATE FINANCE. TOXIC POLLUTION AND CHEMICALS as named specialisms. For a community living beside a smelter, a tailings dam or a pesticide operation, that is rarer expertise than land law and harder to buy locally. THE TRAINING PIPELINE AND ITS REACH: A FELLOWSHIP AND INTERN PROGRAM WHICH OVER 25 YEARS HAS TRAINED MORE THAN 500 INTERNS AND LAW FELLOWS FROM 54 COUNTRIES — DESCRIBED AS ONE OF VERY FEW WAYS AT AN EARLY STAGE OF A LEGAL CAREER TO OBTAIN IN-DEPTH EXPERIENCE AND TRAINING IN INTERNATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL LEGAL ADVOCACY. Five hundred lawyers from fifty-four countries, trained and dispersed. Some are now practising in African capitals — which is a specific thing to ask a national bar or law school about when looking for counsel who already understands this field. THE UNIVERSITY LINK AND THE AWARD: A JOINT RESEARCH AND TEACHING PROGRAM WITH A NAMED UNIVERSITY LAW SCHOOL, AND AN ANNUAL INTERNATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL LAW AWARD RECOGNISING EXCEPTIONAL CONTRIBUTIONS. AND THE INTERNATIONAL COURT SUBMISSION ON RECORD: A WRITTEN SUBMISSION UNDER A NAMED PRACTICE DIRECTION FOCUSED ON APPLICABLE LAW, REPARATIONS FOR CLIMATE HARM, URGENT AND EQUITABLE PHASEOUT OF FOSSIL FUELS, AND RIGHTS OF FUTURE GENERATIONS — CREDITING THE LEADERSHIP OF A PACIFIC STATE AND A STUDENT MOVEMENT FOR DRIVING THE REQUEST FOR A CLIMATE ADVISORY OPINION. A small island state and a group of students moved the world's highest court to give an opinion. Credited as theirs, not the lawyers'. That is the clearest available answer to anyone who tells a village that its case is too small to matter. WHO IT SUITS: African organisations needing international legal analysis, transboundary corporate accountability strategy, or specialist toxics and chemicals expertise — through a partnership rather than as clients. CAVEATS: NOT A LAW FIRM AND WILL NOT REPRESENT YOU LOCALLY, AND IT WORKS THROUGH LASTING PARTNERSHIPS RATHER THAN INTAKE — approach with a national organisation. For pro bono lawyers already carrying 100+ community cases, Togo's entry; for senior lawyers on attorney-client terms, Ethiopia's entry; for the co-complainant route to the continental court, Seychelles' entry.

trackers.name: The JWH Initiative — a grant of €2,500–7,000 paid to an individual nominated by their own organisation, for courses, internships or conferences — explicitly not tied to organisational projects, so the money follows the person rather than a workplan
trackers.desc: THE ORGANISATION NOMINATES; THE PERSON GETS THE MONEY — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S BENIN ENTRY COVERS THE FIELD COURSES RESERVING HALF THEIR PLACES FOR AFRICANS, ITS ANGOLA ENTRY THE FREE SELF-ASSESSMENT PLATFORM, ITS CAMEROON ENTRY THE ADVISOR-NOMINATED GRASSROOTS FUND, AND ITS ESWATINI ENTRY THE TEAM-BASED CONSERVATION LADDER. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. PRECHECK AND AN EXACT HOST COMPARISON ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS WERE RUN BEFORE THIS ENTRY WAS WRITTEN. WHO IS FUNDED AND HOW YOU ENTER, WHICH IS THE FIND: THE MISSION IS TO PROVIDE AN ACCESSIBLE AND TAILORED SMALL GRANT FOR EDUCATION AND TRAINING OF INDIVIDUALS WHO ARE NOMINATED BY THEIR ORGANISATION AS POTENTIAL FUTURE LEADERS — AND IT WORKS WITH A NOMINATION PROCESS, WHICH MEANS THE PARTICIPANTS CANNOT APPLY THEMSELVES. The decision to put somebody forward sits with the organisation, which makes this a thing a community body can DO rather than a thing it can only receive. A committee that has a young member carrying the mapping, the minutes or the negotiations can convert that into a funded year of training by writing a nomination. WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT FUND, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: WE SUPPORT INDIVIDUALS TO PURSUE PERSONAL DEVELOPMENT THROUGH COURSES, INTERNSHIPS, CONFERENCES, AND MORE, WITHOUT BEING TIED TO ORGANIZATIONAL PROJECTS — INVESTING IN INDIVIDUAL CAPACITY RATHER THAN FUNDING ORGANISATIONAL PROJECTS, AND RATHER THAN FUNDING ENVIRONMENTAL PROJECTS OR ORGANISATIONS DIRECTLY. Nothing else in this file pays for a person's own learning. Every other grant here buys an activity and the person is an input; here the person is the point, and the training does not have to serve a deliverable. That also means it will not pay for your campaign — do not build a proposal around the land dispute. THE AMOUNT AND HOW IT IS SET: AWARDS OF BETWEEN 2,500 AND 7,000 EURO FOR EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMES, INTERNSHIPS OR TRAININGS THAT ADVANCE PROFESSIONAL ASPIRATIONS — WITH ONE SOURCE NOTING NO FIXED AMOUNT IS SPECIFIED, FUNDING BEING AWARDED BASED ON THE APPLICANT'S INDIVIDUAL LEARNING OBJECTIVES, PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT NEEDS AND PROPOSED ACTIVITIES, EACH ASSESSED INDIVIDUALLY. ASSESSED INDIVIDUALLY means you state what you need and why, rather than fitting into a bracket. The published range is the guide; the case is yours to make. THE AFRICAN EXAMPLE ON RECORD, IN DETAIL: A NAMED WOMAN FROM TOGO USED THE GRANT FOR AN INTERNSHIP AT A RENOWNED SENEGALESE NGO AND TO FINISH HER MASTER'S DEGREE IN ENVIRONMENTAL DIPLOMACY — AND SHE SET UP A SUCCESSFUL ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATION IN HER HOME COUNTRY. An internship in another African country plus a degree, from one grant. That combination — learning inside an established African organisation rather than a northern one — is the most transferable use recorded here, and the outcome was a new organisation in her own country. THE OTHER NAMED AFRICAN GRANTEE: THE FOUNDER OF AN ORGANISATION IN RWANDA PROMOTING FAIR, INCLUSIVE AND GENDER-RESPONSIVE CLIMATE POLICY. WHAT THE NOMINATION LOOKS FOR: CLEAR POTENTIAL AND AMBITION TO GROW INTO LEADERSHIP ROLES, AND A STRONG CONNECTION TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS, OR CIVIL SOCIETY MOVEMENTS — WITH THE CANDIDATE WILLING AND ABLE TO REPORT ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF THEIR LEADERSHIP CAPACITIES. A STRONG CONNECTION TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES is a selection criterion rather than an obstacle. The nominee rooted in a village committee is advantaged over the better-credentialled candidate from a capital-city NGO, which inverts the usual sorting this file records. THE PROBLEM IT NAMES: YOUNG PEOPLE IN THE ENVIRONMENTAL SECTOR OFTEN HAVE FEW OPPORTUNITIES TO DEVELOP LEADERSHIP SKILLS DUE TO A LACK OF RESOURCES FOR SCHOOLING, TRAINING OR PRACTICAL LEARNING — AND THIS IS ONE OF VERY FEW INITIATIVES THAT OFFERS THEM THE OPPORTUNITY. ONE OF VERY FEW, by their own account, and this file's sweep of training and funding routes bears that out: the field courses filed under Benin require a biology degree and English; this requires neither. THE PURPOSE BEHIND FUNDING A PERSON RATHER THAN A PROJECT: BY GIVING SMALL GRANTS TO INDIVIDUALS TO EXPAND THEIR KNOWLEDGE, EXPERIENCE AND TRAINING, THE INITIATIVE AIMS TO STRENGTHEN ENVIRONMENTAL CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS' CAPACITY AND EFFICIENCY. The organisation is meant to benefit through the person returning to it. Worth agreeing before the nomination what that return looks like, because the grant itself imposes no such condition. WHERE THE MONEY COMES FROM: A DUTCH UN OFFICIAL WHO SERVED AS A CLIMATE CONVENTION EXECUTIVE SECRETARY LEFT HER ESTATE TO THE CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATIONS IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES, WITH CLEAR INSTRUCTIONS TO USE IT FOR FOSTERING LEADERS FOR THE ENVIRONMENTAL MOVEMENT IN THE GLOBAL SOUTH — MANAGED BY A NAMED NETHERLANDS ORGANISATION SINCE 2007. A bequest with instructions, not an annual appropriation. That is why the terms are unusually generous and why they have stayed stable for nearly two decades — nobody has to renew a donor's enthusiasm each year. THE REACH SO FAR: ALMOST 200 GRANTEES IN MORE THAN 50 COUNTRIES, WITH 188 YOUNG ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVISTS FROM OVER 50 COUNTRIES RECEIVING A GRANT IN ONE TEN-YEAR PERIOD. Roughly twenty a year worldwide. Small, and worth knowing before investing effort — but a nomination is a short document, not a proposal. THE COMPETITION AND THE COHORT: DESCRIBED AS HIGHLY COMPETITIVE AND SELECTIVE, FOR MID-LEVEL PROFESSIONALS COMMITTED TO ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY, SOCIAL EQUITY AND CLIMATE JUSTICE — WITH SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATES JOINING A GROWING NETWORK OF GLOBAL CHANGEMAKERS. AND THE CALL CYCLE: ANNUAL CALLS WITH PUBLISHED DEADLINES, INCLUDING A RECORDED CLOSING DATE OF 31 AUGUST IN ONE CYCLE — WITH THE NOMINATION AND SELECTION PROCESS AND UPCOMING CALLS SET OUT ON THE INITIATIVE'S OWN SITE. Annual and predictable. Decide now who your organisation would nominate, and have the person ready when the call opens rather than choosing in the last week. WHO IT SUITS: African community and environmental organisations with a young member worth investing in — the organisation nominates, the individual is funded. CAVEATS: NO SELF-APPLICATION, INDIVIDUALS ONLY, EDUCATION AND TRAINING ONLY — NOT PROJECTS, CAMPAIGNS OR LEGAL COSTS — AND ROUGHLY TWENTY GRANTS A YEAR WORLDWIDE. For field training with reserved African places, Benin's entry; for the grassroots fund reached through regional advisors, Cameroon's entry; for free organisational self-assessment needing no account, Angola's entry.

trackers.name: Lawyers' Rights Watch Canada (LRWC) — a volunteer committee of about two hundred lawyers that campaigns for lawyers threatened over their human rights work — most advocacy starting with a letter, UN consultative status behind it, and a published statement of what it will not do plus where to go instead
trackers.desc: MOST OF IT STARTS WITH A LETTER — AND THEY SAY WHAT THEY WILL NOT DO — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S CAMEROON ENTRY COVERS THE INSTITUTE THAT DEFENDS LAWYERS AND JUDGES THROUGH OBSERVATION AND BAR-BUILDING; ITS CÔTE D'IVOIRE ENTRY THE BARRISTERS' COMMITTEE; ITS EQUATORIAL GUINEA BUCKET CARRIES THE PROTECTION GRANTS HOST THIS ORGANISATION REFERS PEOPLE TO. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. HOW A CASE ACTUALLY STARTS, WHICH IS THE FIND: MOST OF ITS ADVOCACY COMMENCES WITH A LETTER REGARDING THE REPORTED HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS. The whole intervention begins with somebody writing to them about what happened. No form, no eligibility test, no partner organisation required as an intermediary — and this file has recorded many resources whose real entry requirement was knowing somebody. A letter setting out the facts is the entry requirement here. WHAT IT DOES FOR A THREATENED LAWYER: IT CAMPAIGNS FOR LAWYERS WHOSE RIGHTS, FREEDOMS OR INDEPENDENCE ARE THREATENED AS A RESULT OF THEIR HUMAN RIGHTS ADVOCACY, AND PRODUCES LEGAL ANALYSES OF NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL LAW — ADVOCATING FOR DEFENDERS AT RISK OF ARBITRARY DETENTION, TORTURE, ENFORCED DISAPPEARANCE, INJURY AND DEATH. LEGAL ANALYSES OF NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL LAW is the part with practical value beyond the campaign: an independent written analysis of how a prosecution breaches both your own law and the treaties your state has signed is a document a national lawyer can use in court. WHAT IT SAYS PLAINLY THAT IT DOES NOT DO, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IT DOES NOT PROVIDE RESETTLEMENT ASSISTANCE OR LEGAL ADVICE, AND DOES NOT PROVIDE LEGAL SERVICES TO THE PUBLIC. Published as its own page rather than buried. That honesty saves weeks: a community needing representation should not write here, and a defender needing to leave the country should not either. Almost nothing else in this file states its limits so directly, and the entry is filed partly for that. AND THE ONWARD ROUTES IT GIVES INSTEAD: TO BE CONSIDERED FOR A NATIONAL REFUGEE PROGRAMME FOR HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS AT RISK, INDIVIDUALS MUST BE REFERRED TO THAT GOVERNMENT BY THE UNITED NATIONS REFUGEE AGENCY — AND THAT GOVERNMENT WORKS WITH TWO NAMED DEFENDER-PROTECTION ORGANISATIONS WHO ARE EXPERTS IN THE FIELD, ONE WITH A DEDICATED PROGRAMME EMAIL ADDRESS PUBLISHED FOR THAT PURPOSE. The referral chain named exactly: the refugee agency refers, the government decides, and two specialist organisations are the working route in — one with an email address published specifically for that country's programme. A defender who has to leave now needs that sequence, and it is rarely written down anywhere. THE STANDING IT HOLDS AT THE UNITED NATIONS: A VOLUNTEER-RUN NGO IN SPECIAL CONSULTATIVE STATUS WITH THE UNITED NATIONS ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL COUNCIL, GRANTED IN 2005 — SINCE WHEN IT HAS ADVOCATED FOR LAWYERS AND OTHER DEFENDERS BEFORE THE HUMAN RIGHTS COUNCIL AND OTHER UNITED NATIONS BODIES. Consultative status is the credential that lets an organisation file and speak at those sessions. This file has recorded, under Sudan, a continental case rejected because the applicants held the wrong accreditation — a body that already holds this one can carry your material in. WHAT THAT STATUS IS USED FOR IN PRACTICE: FOUR JOINT WRITTEN SUBMISSIONS TO NAMED UNIVERSAL PERIODIC REVIEW SESSIONS, CO-SPONSORED SIDE EVENTS AT COUNCIL SESSIONS, AND A JOINT SUBMISSION TO A UNITED NATIONS COMMITTEE ON ENFORCED DISAPPEARANCE — INITIATED BY ONE ORGANISATION AND ENDORSED BY SEVERAL OTHERS. JOINT submissions, initiated by one organisation and endorsed by others. That is the achievable shape: a national organisation drafts, and established bodies sign on to give it reach. The Universal Periodic Review examines every state on a fixed cycle, so there is a scheduled moment when your country's record is formally reviewed. THE RESULT ONE CAMPAIGN CONTRIBUTED TO: IT ADDED ITS VOICE TO GLOBAL ADVOCACY THAT LED TO A HUMAN RIGHTS COUNCIL RESOLUTION IN JULY 2019, RESULTING IN A HIGH COMMISSIONER'S REPORT THAT CONFIRMED THE KILLINGS OF HUNDREDS OF HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS. THE FREE PUBLICATIONS: A GUIDEBOOK ON INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS LAW PROTECTIONS AGAINST ARBITRARY OR UNLAWFUL DEPRIVATION OF LIBERTY, AND A PUBLISHED TOOLKIT FOR LAWYERS AT RISK PRODUCED WITH A PARTNER ORGANISATION. A guidebook on unlawful detention, free. Where organisers are held without charge — the standard tactic recorded throughout this file — that is the argument set out in the terms international bodies recognise. THE STANDARD THAT TOOLKIT WORKS FROM: PROMOTING THE INDEPENDENT FUNCTIONING OF LAWYERS IN ACCORDANCE WITH INTERNATIONALLY RECOGNISED NORMS, INCLUDING A NAMED SET OF BASIC PRINCIPLES ON THE ROLE OF LAWYERS — SEEKING TO PROTECT LAWYERS FROM THREATS, RISKS AND REPRISALS AND EMPOWER THEM AS ESSENTIAL AGENTS OF THE ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE. WHO IT IS AND HOW BIG: A COMMITTEE OF LAWYERS AND OTHER HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS PROMOTING INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS LAW, ADVOCACY RIGHTS AND THE INTEGRITY OF LEGAL SYSTEMS — ABOUT TWO HUNDRED LAWYERS, RELYING SOLELY ON FUNDRAISING AND SUPPORT FROM MEMBERS. Two hundred volunteers and no paid capacity to speak of. Expect a written intervention rather than a presence, and write early. THE MONITOR ROLE IT RECRUITS FOR: PUBLISHED MONITOR GUIDELINES AND AN INVITATION TO CONTACT IT FOR INFORMATION ON COUNTRIES FOR WHICH MONITORS ARE NEEDED. Countries go unmonitored for want of a volunteer. If your country is on that list, the gap in international attention has a cause and a remedy. AND THE DIPLOMATIC CHANNEL ITS HOME GOVERNMENT PUBLISHES, WHICH RUNS ALONGSIDE: GUIDELINES INSTRUCTING ITS DIPLOMATIC MISSIONS TO MONITOR AND REPORT WHEN A WITNESS OR LAWYER DISAPPEARS FOLLOWING TESTIMONY OR LEGAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST AUTHORITIES, WHEN A CIVIL SOCIETY, MEDIA ORGANISATION OR INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY CRITICAL OF THE GOVERNMENT'S HUMAN RIGHTS RECORD IS BANNED OR FACES LEGAL SANCTIONS, OR WHEN A DEMONSTRATION OCCURS WHERE DEFENDERS ARE LIKELY TO BE AT RISK — WITH A PUBLISHED REPORTING CHECKLIST BEGINNING WITH BASIC BACKGROUND ON A CASE, THE INDIVIDUAL NAMED ONLY IF SAFE AND APPROPRIATE. The embassy in your capital has written instructions to report exactly these events. That makes an approach to a mission a defined request against a published standard rather than a plea — and NAMED ONLY IF SAFE AND APPROPRIATE is their own caution, worth matching in what you send. WHO IT SUITS: African lawyers facing reprisals for representing communities, and organisations wanting a written legal analysis or a joint UN submission behind them. CAVEATS: IT DOES NOT GIVE LEGAL ADVICE, DOES NOT REPRESENT ANYONE AND DOES NOT HELP WITH RELOCATION — IT CAMPAIGNS, ANALYSES AND SUBMITS; IT IS VOLUNTEER-RUN, SO CAPACITY IS LIMITED AND SLOW. For emergency protection grants for defenders, Equatorial Guinea's entry; for trial observation and amicus briefs, Côte d'Ivoire's and Cameroon's entries.

trackers.name: KHRC (Kenya Human Rights Commission), Nairobi — runs joinable HURINET community networks including one for communities excluded from land-based resources, and took the Kakuzi plantation land claim to a National Land Commission determination
trackers.desc: THERE IS A NETWORK FOR COMMUNITIES SHUT OUT OF THEIR LAND, AND YOU CAN JOIN IT — method and adjacency declared first: TENTH NAMED-ATTORNEY ROUND. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; THE SUBJECT'S OWN HOST, ITS ACRONYM AND FOUR FACTS ABSENT. ONE ORGANISATION NAME MATCHED A KENYA ENTRY ON ITS OWN HOST, READ IN FULL AND A DIFFERENT SUBJECT.
