THAT BUCKET CARRIES THE COUNTRY'S OLDEST LEGAL AID ORGANISATION, THE STATUTORY FREE-LAWYER SCHEME, A LAND ALLIANCE, CONSTITUTIONAL LITIGATORS, A COMMUNITY LAND TRUST AND A PROPERTY WATCHDOG GROUP — NONE OF THEM THIS COMMISSION, AND NONE RESTATED. THE NETWORK A COMMUNITY CAN JOIN, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT PUBLISHES ITS NETWORKS BY NAME, INCLUDING ONE FOR PEOPLE VICTIMIZED BY HISTORICAL AND EMERGING INJUSTICES; ONE FOR COMMUNITIES EXCLUDED FROM NATURAL AND OTHER LAND-BASED RESOURCES; ONE FOR PEOPLE VICTIMIZED BY ARBITRARY ARRESTS, DETENTIONS, TORTURE, EXTRAJUDICIAL EXECUTIONS AND FORCED DISAPPEARANCES; AND ONE FOR CITIZENS WITH DIFFICULTIES IN ACCESSING GOVERNMENT SERVICES. COMMUNITIES EXCLUDED FROM NATURAL AND OTHER LAND-BASED RESOURCES is a standing named network, not a project. A village fenced out of its grazing, its forest or its water has a category to join rather than a case to explain from scratch — and joining puts it alongside others in the same position, which is the isolation problem this file records over and over. HOW IT REACHES THE GROUND: IT WORKS AT COMMUNITY LEVEL WITH HUMAN RIGHTS NETWORKS ACROSS THE COUNTRY AND LINKS COMMUNITY, NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS CONCERNS. THE PLANTATION CASE AND WHAT IT WON, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IT AND A PARTNER ORGANISATION WORKED WITH THE AFFECTED COMMUNITIES AND PROVIDED LEGAL AND ADVOCACY SUPPORT AGAINST KAKUZI PLC — THE LAND THE COMPANY SITS ON HAVING BEEN ACQUIRED THROUGH DECADES OF INVASION AND COLONISATION CULMINATING IN SYSTEMIC, FORCEFUL DISPLACEMENT, WITH THOSE COMMUNITIES THEN BECOMING VICTIMS OF RAPE, KILLINGS AND GROSS ASSAULT BY THE COMPANY'S SECURITY GUARDS. A plantation's own security guards named as the perpetrators, and the historical acquisition and the present violence argued as one continuous case rather than two. That framing is the transferable part: how the land was taken and how the company polices it now are the same story. THE LEGAL POSITION IT ARGUED, WHICH IS THE THIRD FIND: ITS INTERPRETATION OF HISTORICAL LAND INJUSTICES AS DEFINED IN THE NATIONAL LAND POLICY AND THE NATIONAL LAND COMMISSION ACT IS THAT THEY ARE GROUNDED ON THE LEGITIMACY OF CLAIMS, LEGALITY OF TITLES NOTWITHSTANDING — AND MOST OF THE COMMUNITIES WERE ABLE TO PROVE THIS. LEGALITY OF TITLES NOTWITHSTANDING is the sentence to carry. A community repeatedly told that the company holds a valid title is being answered on the wrong question: the statutory test here is the legitimacy of the claim, not the paperwork of the holder. Check whether your own land legislation contains a comparable historical-injustice provision before conceding the title point. WHAT THE DETERMINATION DID AND DID NOT DO: IT REPRESENTS RECOGNITION OF A HARD-WON, THOUGH DELAYED, VICTORY, BUT REMAINS ONLY A PARTIAL STEP TOWARD FULL RESTORATIVE JUSTICE — CONTAINING SIGNIFICANT GAPS, HAVING FAILED TO ADDRESS EXPIRED LEASES, REVERSION OF TITLES, AND THE PROTECTION OF PUBLIC ROADS AND EASEMENTS. The win is filed with its holes named by the winners. EXPIRED LEASES and REVERSION OF TITLES are the two questions a community should put in its own submission from the start, because a determination that skips them leaves the company in place. THE URGENT ACTION CAPACITY IT MAINTAINS: A STANDING TEAM AND FLEXIBLE FUNDS, ALLOWING IT TO RESPOND QUICKLY TO STATE REPRESSION, ELITE IMPUNITY AND COMMUNITY DISTRESS — ITS RESPONSES BEING POLITICAL, NOT JUST REACTIVE. A STANDING TEAM AND FLEXIBLE FUNDS is the specific thing to ask any organisation about. Money already raised and unearmarked is what allows a response within days; a body that must apply for a grant first cannot help during an eviction. HOW IT USES LITIGATION, STATED PLAINLY: IT TAKES BOLD LEGAL ACTION BUT WITH A CLEAR POLITICAL AGENDA — ITS LITIGATION TIED TO PUBLIC CAMPAIGNS, MASS ACTION, AND NAMING AND SHAMING THOSE WHO VIOLATE RIGHTS. Litigation deliberately coupled to campaigning. Communities should know which they are getting: an organisation that will also run a public campaign brings pressure a quiet case does not, and exposure a community may not want. Ask before signing on. WHAT IT ASKS OF THE PUBLIC: IF YOU OR SOMEONE YOU KNOW HAS EXPERIENCED DISCRIMINATION, ABUSE, OR ANY FORM OF HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATION, WE'RE HERE TO HELP — EVERY REPORT MATTERS, AND ALL REPORTS ARE TREATED WITH CONFIDENTIALITY AND RESPECT. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES, PROGRAMMATICALLY: RESEARCH, MONITORING, CAPACITY-BUILDING, ADVOCACY, LEGAL AID AND PUBLIC INTEREST LITIGATION — ACROSS FOUR NAMED PROGRAMMES, DELIVERING AT COUNTY, NATIONAL, REGIONAL AND GLOBAL LEVELS. COUNTY level first in that list. A commission that works at the sub-national tier is one that can act where a project is actually approved. THE RIGHTS FRAME IT USES: A HOLISTIC CONCEPT STRADDLING CIVIL AND POLITICAL RIGHTS; ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL RIGHTS AS CRITICAL BUILDING BLOCKS FOR SOCIAL DEMOCRACY; AND EQUALITY AND NON-DISCRIMINATION. HOW IT WAS FOUNDED AND WHERE IT SHELTERED: FORMED BY FIVE NAMED CITIZENS WHILE IN EXILE AND REGISTERED ABROAD IN 1991, WITH ONE FOUNDER DISPATCHED HOME TO OPERATE FROM THE OFFICES OF KURIA, RINGERA AND MURUNGI ADVOCATES, REGISTERED DOMESTICALLY IN 1994, AND LATER HOSTED BY KITUO CHA SHERIA BEFORE MOVING TO ITS OWN PREMISES — HAVING BEEN A MEMBER OF THE CONSTITUTIONAL REFERENCE GROUP IN THE DRAFTING AND RUN-UP TO THE REFERENDUM. Registered abroad first, then sheltered inside a law firm and then inside an older legal aid organisation. That is a survival route worth recording: where a new organisation cannot register or cannot rent safely, an existing one can host it until it can stand alone. AND WHAT IT COSTS, RECORDED PLAINLY: ITS OWN SITE RUNS DAY-COUNTERS FOR A STAFF MEMBER IT SAYS WAS EXTRAORDINARILY AND ILLEGALLY RENDITIONED TO A NEIGHBOURING COUNTRY AND NOT ALLOWED BACK, AND FOR AN OCCASION WHEN IT SAYS STATE-HIRED MILITIA STORMED ITS OFFICES AND ATTACKED PEOPLE WITH NO ACTION TAKEN — AND A PAST EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR RECEIVED DEATH THREATS OVER STATEMENTS ABOUT AN ELECTION. A running day-count on its own homepage for a colleague still not returned. Filed unsoftened, because a community weighing whether to be publicly associated with an organisation should know what is currently being done to it. WHO IT SUITS: communities excluded from land, forest, grazing or water who want a standing national network to join, and anyone facing a plantation or estate whose title rests on historical dispossession. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY, AND ITS LITIGATION IS DELIBERATELY TIED TO PUBLIC CAMPAIGNING, WHICH RAISES A COMMUNITY'S VISIBILITY AND RISK; IT SELECTS STRATEGIC CASES RATHER THAN OPERATING AS GENERAL LEGAL AID, AND IT IS ITSELF UNDER PRESSURE ON ITS OWN ACCOUNT. For that country's oldest legal aid organisation and its statutory free-lawyer scheme, Kenya's own entries; for the free legal directory model, Botswana's entry.

trackers.name: South Sudan — Business Registry (Ministry of Justice / eServices)
trackers.desc: National corporate registry; the Business Registry under the Ministry of Justice & Constitutional Affairs registers companies & business names — with an official online Business Registration eServices portal for name search, application & certificates, South Sudan. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: South Sudan — Ministry of Finance & Planning (MoFP)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the MoFP prepares & executes the national budget, publishes budget speeches, execution & quarterly outturn reports and manages public financial management, South Sudan. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in South Sudan.

trackers.name: South Sudan — National Audit Chamber (NAC)
trackers.desc: National public-finance watchdog; the National Audit Chamber (headed by the Auditor General) audits the accounts of all public-sector institutions and reports to the Legislative Assembly, South Sudan.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: East African Court of Justice — it stopped a road across the Serengeti
trackers.desc: THIS COURT STOPPED A GOVERNMENT FROM BUILDING A ROAD. In African Network for Animal Welfare v Attorney General of the United Republic of Tanzania (Reference No. 9 of 2010, judgment 20 June 2014), the East African Court of Justice held Tanzania's proposed highway across the Serengeti National Park unlawful and issued an injunction restraining Tanzania from operationalising it. THE TREATY ARTICLES THAT DID THE WORK: article 5(3)(c) of the EAC Treaty — promotion of sustainable utilisation of natural resources and measures that would effectively protect the natural environment of the Partner States — and article 114(1)(a), which enjoins partner states to conserve, protect and manage the environment. THE HARMS PLEADED ARE A REUSABLE CHECKLIST: disrupted animal migration, fragmentation of habitats, loss of scenic and visual quality, deterioration of air quality, increased poaching, and surface water and soil pollution. NOTE THE SHAPE OF THE RELIEF: at para 78 the Court said its orders must be preventative, and that roads in the Serengeti should be used by wildlife, tourists and Park administrators and not the general public — a restriction on who may use a road is a narrower and more grantable order than an outright ban. The government's own report had conceded grave negative impacts. THREE THINGS MAKE THIS ROUTE UNUSUAL: (1) standing survived a full challenge — the objection on jurisdiction, limitation and form was overruled on 26 August 2011 and the appeal dismissed on 15 March 2012; (2) the applicant was not from the respondent state — ANAW is a pan-African charity that sued Tanzania without being Tanzanian, so an NGO based in one partner state can challenge another's project; and (3) this is a trade-and-integration court, not a specialist environmental one — the claim runs through treaty obligations between states. CONFIRM PARTNER-STATE STATUS BEFORE FILING: this state's EAC accession is relatively recent, and the Court's jurisdiction follows partner-state status. This entry does not assert current standing to file — verify it first.

trackers.name: SSHRDN — in South Sudan the resource is protection first: legal aid, medical and psycho-social support for people at risk for defending land
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST, AND WHY IT IS THIS RATHER THAN A CONSERVATION BODY: in South Sudan the binding problem is not that no one knows the land is being poisoned — it is that documenting it gets you arrested. The South Sudan Human Rights Defenders Network, registered with the Relief and Rehabilitation Commission under number 2284, is a coalition of organisations and individuals that provides rapid support to defenders at risk: legal aid, medical care and psycho-social services, plus training in risk assessment, security management and digital safety. It works with the Pan African Human Rights Defenders Network and other regional bodies. It published a report documenting at least 114 cases of censorship, harassment and arbitrary arrest of civil society actors and journalists over a three-year period, in a country whose 2024 national security law permits arrest without warrant. WHAT DOES EXIST ON THE ENVIRONMENT, so you know who to look for: the Sudd Environment Agency, formed in 2019 to work on oil pollution in Unity and Upper Nile states, which runs field assessments and community workshops and has led a consortium, the Environment and Climate Change Network, with three other South Sudanese organisations; and the Sudd Institute, which has published research on the health impacts of oil pollution. The Sudd Environment Agency's own account is that state security does not allow civil society or individuals to reach oil waste dumping sites or photograph them — which is exactly why the protection network comes first. WHO IT SUITS: South Sudanese community members, activists and journalists exposed to risk for challenging oil pollution, land allocation or displacement. CAVEATS: this is protection and legal aid for individuals at risk, NOT an organisation that will stop a project, and no land-defence or litigation service was found in this country. The environmental bodies named above had no verified public intake route, which is why they are described here rather than listed separately.

trackers.name: South Sudan Law Society and the Juba paralegal network — legal aid, paralegal training, and their own warning about institutional land grabbing
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the South Sudan Law Society (SSLS), a civil society organisation based in Juba running legal aid, community paralegal training, human rights awareness and capacity-building for legal professionals, and the author of a study on housing, land and property disputes in the country; alongside the community paralegal networks operating in Juba, including a Grassroots Women Network that mentors paralegals drawn mostly from community leaders, backed by a Norwegian aid organisation, and the South Sudan Land Alliance. WHAT THE PARALEGALS ARE TRAINED IN, which tells you what to ask for: alternative dispute resolution, the provisions of the 2009 Land Act, and evidence-gathering techniques to support lawyers handling land registration and dispute cases. WHY THE COUNTRY'S SITUATION MAKES THIS THE FIGHT: land grabs and expropriation typically increase after conflict, while land governance is in disarray and a new administration is still passing and implementing laws — and people who have not yet physically returned to stake their claim, especially widows, divorced women and orphans, are the ones who lose land in their absence. Returnees are often unaware of their rights inside and outside the customary system. IF YOU ARE DISPLACED, SOMEONE HAS TO STAND ON YOUR CLAIM OR RECORD IT WHILE YOU CANNOT. THE WARNING THE PARALEGALS THEMSELVES GIVE, and it belongs here rather than in a footnote: they describe “institutional” land grabbing — well coordinated and facilitated by networks of powerful individuals — and say that as paralegals they are at the centre of that problem and exposed when they challenge such cases; they also report working without offices, files or computers. WHO IT SUITS: South Sudanese households and returnees facing land disputes, occupation of their land in their absence, or registration problems — particularly women. CAVEATS: NO VERIFIED LIVE SITE FOR SSLS WAS FOUND — this entry points at the NGO forum's document record; capacity is severely limited and donor-dependent, the security situation is volatile, and challenging coordinated land grabbing carries personal risk. For threats against defenders specifically, South Sudan's SSHRDN entry.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants in South Sudan — the country was added by name in the eighth cycle, so community environmental grants exist here for the first time
trackers.desc: WHERE TO APPLY FOR MONEY: the GEF SMALL GRANTS PROGRAMME expanded country coverage in its eighth replenishment from 124 to 135 countries, ADDING SOUTH SUDAN BY NAME — alongside Somalia, Libya, Equatorial Guinea and São Tomé and Príncipe. South Sudan was outside this window and is now inside it; if you were told there were no community environmental grants here, that answer is out of date. THE ALLOCATION RULE: the eighth cycle secured USD 135 million for the core programme and ensures EQUAL ALLOCATION OF NEARLY USD 1 MILLION IN CORE FINANCING TO EACH of the 135 participating countries — regardless of size or previous participation, with STAR allocations raised over 30 per cent. A newly added country is not competing against large established programmes for the core money, which is the argument for applying in the FIRST cycle rather than waiting to see how it goes. The programme's stated objective is to catalyse and mobilise CIVIL SOCIETY actors and LOCAL ACTIONS addressing the major drivers of environmental degradation, and it has funded community-level environmental projects since 1992. WHY IT MATTERS PARTICULARLY HERE: South Sudan's recorded land problem is people losing land while displaced, and paralegals working without offices, files or computers. Grant money that buys a registered organisation an office, a filing system and a motorbike is not a side benefit in that setting — it is the capacity that makes claim-keeping possible. WHO IT SUITS: South Sudanese community organisations and associations with an environmental, land restoration, water or resilience project. CAVEATS: A DONOR CYCLE WITH FIXED CALLS — confirm the country programme is operational before counting on it; it funds environmental action, NOT litigation, land purchase or compensation claims, and the security situation constrains everything. For land disputes, paralegals and the 2009 Land Act, South Sudan's Law Society entry.

trackers.name: South Sudan's Land Act 2009 — customary rights held IN COMMON have EQUAL FORCE with freehold, community land can be registered, and mining is prohibited on community land
trackers.desc: WHAT THE LAW SAYS YOUR CUSTOMARY LAND IS WORTH — THE STRONGEST SENTENCE OF ITS KIND IN THIS FILE: under the LAND ACT 2009, section 8(6), CUSTOMARY LAND RIGHTS INCLUDING THOSE HELD IN COMMON SHALL HAVE EQUAL FORCE AND EFFECT IN LAW WITH FREEHOLD OR LEASEHOLD RIGHTS. Not a lesser right, not a right pending formalisation — equal. That is the sentence to put at the top of any letter about your land. The Act classifies land as PUBLIC, COMMUNITY or PRIVATE, provides that rights under customary tenure are AN ASSURED SECURITY OF OCCUPANCY whether held individually or in association with others, and states that customary land SHALL BE DEMARCATED AND REGISTERED — with a COMMUNITY LAND REGISTRATION procedure and a COMMUNITY LAND ENQUIRY in the Act itself. WHO ALLOCATES: section 15 — the TRADITIONAL AUTHORITY within a specific community may allocate customary land rights for RESIDENTIAL, AGRICULTURAL, FORESTRY AND GRAZING purposes, subject to consultation with the community; allocations over 250 FEDDANS must be verified by the state ministry as to purpose and compliance. Rights cannot be denied on the basis of SEX, ETHNICITY OR RELIGION, and WOMEN have the right to own and inherit land. THREE PROTECTIONS WORTH QUOTING AT AN INVESTOR: investment in land must reflect an important interest for the community and contribute economically and socially to local development; any community affected by activities in an investment area SHALL BE COMPENSATED; and MINING IS PROHIBITED ON PRIVATE OR COMMUNITY LAND except under the terms of a granted licence, with the Act carrying express sections on PROTECTION OF PASTORAL LANDS and COMMUNAL GRAZING LAND. WHO CAN HELP YOU USE IT: a South Sudanese land alliance has since 2015 run PILOT PROJECTS ON REGISTRATION OF COMMUNITY LAND in Central Equatoria State and legal support for rural communities' land rights in Western Equatoria, with LAND COMMITTEES inside local government councils responsible for mediating consultation on land leases between communities and investors. Ask whether a community land registration pilot has reached your county, and who sits on your land committee. WHO IT SUITS: South Sudanese communities, traditional authorities and displaced families whose land was taken while they were away. CAVEATS: THE LAW IS STRONG AND ITS MACHINERY IS WEAK — commentary records considerable ambiguity, customary ownership not yet fully established in practice, and concern over long foreign leases; registration capacity is thin and the security situation constrains everything. For paralegals and representation, South Sudan's Law Society entry; for protection first, SSHRDN; for community funding, the GEF Small Grants entry.

trackers.name: AERD and ACD, Juba — two South Sudanese conservation organisations with street addresses, plus the four-member Environment and Climate Change Network
trackers.desc: WHO TO CALL ABOUT THE LAND ITSELF, RATHER THAN ABOUT A COURT CASE: ALLIANCE FOR ENVIRONMENT AND RURAL DEVELOPMENT (AERD), FOUNDED 2017, head office in JUBA at Gudele II, Block II, Plot No. 467, Central Equatoria — a research and conservation organisation working to protect FRESHWATER ECOSYSTEMS, ESPECIALLY THE SUDD WETLANDS, natural forest, grasslands and riverine wildlife AND THE LOCAL POPULATION, with stated aims of biodiversity conservation, habitat management and poverty alleviation through sustainable livelihood development. And the AGENCY FOR CONSERVATION AND DEVELOPMENT (ACD), ESTABLISHED 2010, working on the PANYIKANG, SHAMBE AND ZERAFF GAME RESERVES along the Sudd, plus FANGAK ISLAND and the BOMA PLATEAU, which pursues conservation THROUGH PROVISION OF ALTERNATIVE LIVELIHOOD OPTIONS AND RESOLVING RECURRENT INTRA- AND INTER-COMMUNAL CONFLICTS (PEACEBUILDING). A conservation organisation that treats communal conflict resolution as part of the conservation work is the right kind of partner in South Sudan — land disputes and wildlife protection are the same file there, and an organisation that separates them will fail at both. THE NETWORK: the ENVIRONMENT AND CLIMATE CHANGE NETWORK brings together FOUR civil-society organisations — YO' CARE, PEOPLE INITIATIVE DEVELOPMENT ORGANIZATION, AFRICA CENTRE FOR RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT, and the SEA — formed as a consortium to STRENGTHEN ADVOCACY; the SUDD INSTITUTE, an independent South Sudanese research organisation, has produced REPORTS ON THE IMPACTS OF OIL POLLUTION. WHAT THAT WORK ACHIEVED, AND IT IS THE POINT: civil society EXPOSED THE PRACTICES OF THE OIL INDUSTRY AND TRANSMITTED THIS TO COMMUNITIES — leading to PROTESTS, including one in UPPER NILE STATE where HUNDREDS OF YOUNG PEOPLE CARRIED PLACARDS AND BARRICADED ROADS, and feeding submissions into an international human-rights report. Research reaching communities is what turned oil-pollution documentation into a protest that could not be ignored — ask the network and the institute for their findings on your area in a form your people can read. The Sudd is AFRICA'S LARGEST WETLAND, a Ramsar site supporting AROUND 1 MILLION PEOPLE and the Dinka, Nuer and Shilluk. WHO IT SUITS: South Sudanese communities in or near the Sudd, the game reserves or an oil-affected area. CAVEATS: RESEARCH, CONSERVATION AND ADVOCACY BODIES, NOT FUNDERS OR LAW FIRMS. For customary rights equal in law to freehold, South Sudan's Land Act entry; for protection first, SSHRDN; for paralegals, the Law Society entry.

trackers.name: CEPO Juba and the South Sudan Council of Churches — a named team including a public-budget tracking officer, and a ten-church body whose predecessor brokered a community peace conference with 170 delegates
trackers.desc: THE BODY THAT HAS SETTLED ONE BEFORE, AND THE ORGANISATION WITH A NAMED TEAM: COMMUNITY EMPOWERMENT FOR PROGRESS ORGANIZATION (CEPO, cepo-southsudan.org), BASED IN JUBA, works on peacebuilding, human rights and democratic governance, and PUBLISHES A TEAM PAGE NAMING ITS INDIVIDUAL OFFICERS — including a COMMUNICATIONS AND RESEARCH MANAGER who joined in 2011, and a TRANSPARENCY OFFICER MAINLY DEALING WITH PUBLIC BUDGET TRACKING. ITS EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR'S STATED EXPERTISE IS THE REASON IT LEADS THIS ENTRY: EXPERIENCE IN GENDER MAINSTREAMING WITH SPECIFIC FOCUS ON LAND OWNERSHIP, PUBLIC FUNDS AND POLICY DEVELOPMENT, with prior professional experience at named regional and international institutions. An organisation that names its officers on its own website can be written to by role rather than by switchboard — write to the transparency officer about the money and the director about the land. And a body that tracks public budgets can tell you what was actually allocated to the project on your doorstep. THE CHURCH ROUTE, WHICH IN SOUTH SUDAN IS NOT A SOFT OPTION: THE SOUTH SUDAN COUNCIL OF CHURCHES (SSCC) IS AN ECUMENICAL GROUP OF SOUTH SUDANESE CHURCH LEADERS COMPRISING TEN MEMBER CHURCHES — CATHOLIC, EPISCOPAL, ORTHODOX, PENTECOSTAL, PRESBYTERIAN AND REFORMED — whose representatives meet and issue signed joint statements. Its predecessor body, formed 1989-90 and comprising six churches, ACTED AS A FACILITATOR IN PEACE NEGOTIATIONS, AND ITS MOST WIDELY REPORTED SUCCESS WAS NEGOTIATING AN END TO INTER-ETHNIC FIGHTING IN 1999. AND THE WORKED EXAMPLE IS A LAND-AND-BORDER DISPUTE: A RECONCILIATION AND HEALING CONFERENCE HELD OVER FIVE DAYS, ATTENDED BY ABOUT 170 DELEGATES FROM THE LOCAL COMMUNITY AND FROM THREE NEIGHBOURING COMMUNITIES, PRODUCED A TWO-PAGE DECLARATION ENDING A LONG-STANDING BILATERAL CONFLICT — FACILITATED BY THE COUNCIL'S OWN PEACE AND ADVOCACY COORDINATOR, WHO CALLED IT A BREAKTHROUGH ON A PROBLEM THAT HAD EXISTED FOR A LONG TIME. A five-day conference, delegates from every neighbouring community, and a two-page signed declaration at the end is the format that has actually resolved a South Sudanese boundary dispute. If your quarrel is with the next community rather than with a company, ask the Council to convene one — and insist the neighbours are invited, because that is what made it hold. WHAT THE DISPUTES LOOK LIKE, RECORDED: a chief from a Juba district described armed men clearing his late father's tomb with an excavator and forcing his family off ancestral land, saying IF THIS CAN HAPPEN TO ME, WHAT ABOUT OTHERS WHO ARE NOT COMMUNITY LEADERS; and community representatives from THREE DISTRICTS OF JUBA have been convened to discuss prevention and solutions with local authorities. Graves are being cleared with machinery. Photograph and record every family burial site on your land now, with dates — a tomb is evidence of occupation that predates any title. WHO IT SUITS: South Sudanese communities in a boundary or ancestral-land dispute, and anyone needing to know what was budgeted for a project. CAVEATS: PEACEBUILDING AND ADVOCACY BODIES, not law firms; the security situation constrains everything. For customary rights equal in law to freehold, South Sudan's Land Act entry; for protection first, SSHRDN; for paralegals, the Law Society entry; for conservation organisations with street addresses, the AERD and ACD entry.

trackers.name: The East African Court of Justice restraining order that stopped the Sudd dredgers, the environment ministry that called the work illegal, and the South Sudan NGO Forum
trackers.desc: THE REGIONAL COURT THAT STOPPED THE DREDGERS — and it is the strongest sequence in this file for halting a national infrastructure project: EGYPT DELIVERED EQUIPMENT TO DREDGE 20 MILES OF WATERWAYS IN THE NORTH OF THE SUDD, SPARKING BACKLASH FROM ENVIRONMENTALISTS WHO SAID THE PROJECT WOULD DESTROY THE WETLAND AND DAMAGE WATER SUPPLIES. FIRST, SOUTH SUDAN'S OWN ENVIRONMENT MINISTRY OPPOSED THE DREDGING AND A RELATED PLAN TO COMPLETE THE 240-MILE JONGLEI CANAL, AND STATED THAT ANY DREDGING IS ILLEGAL UNTIL ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL ASSESSMENTS ARE COMPLETED. A government ministry declaring the work illegal for want of an assessment is the cheapest stop there is. Before you organise anything else, write to your own environment ministry and ask it to state whether the assessment has been done — in South Sudan that statement was the opening move. SECOND, AND THIS IS THE PART MOST COMMUNITIES IN THIS FILE DO NOT KNOW THEY CAN REACH: THE EAST AFRICAN COURT OF JUSTICE, WHICH HOLDS JURISDICTION OVER SOUTH SUDAN, ISSUED A RESTRAINING ORDER PREVENTING ANY DREDGING. A REGIONAL court, above the national one, ordered the machines stopped. If your country belongs to a regional bloc with a court of justice, that court is a forum your case can reach when the national courts are slow, captured or unsafe — and an order from it binds the state. Ask a lawyer which regional court has jurisdiction over you, and whether individuals and organisations can file directly. THIRD, THE PRESIDENT SUSPENDED THE DREDGING until the environment ministry undertakes the needed impact assessments, pledging in a public address to complete impact assessments before undertaking dredging or resuming work on the canal — acknowledging that THOSE WHO SUPPORT DREDGING SEE IT AS A PERMANENT SOLUTION TO FLOODS IN THE LOW AREAS, WHILE ON THE OTHER SIDE DREDGING WITHOUT PROPER STUDIES IS VIEWED AS A PATH TO AN ECOLOGICAL DISASTER THAT WILL CHANGE SOUTH SUDAN'S BIODIVERSITY FOREVER. Note what the campaign did NOT have to win: it did not have to prove the project was worthless, only that it had not been assessed. And note that the head of state restated the other side's argument fairly. Frame your objection as a demand for the study, not a refusal of the benefit — that is the frame a president can accept without losing face. THE COORDINATING BODY: THE SOUTH SUDAN NGO FORUM IS AN INDEPENDENT COORDINATING BODY OF NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL NGOs THAT FACILITATES MEMBERS TO EFFICIENTLY AND EFFECTIVELY ADDRESS HUMANITARIAN AND DEVELOPMENT NEEDS IN SOUTH SUDAN, described as A PROACTIVE, EFFECTIVE AND ACCOUNTABLE PARTNER. National AND international NGOs in one independent body means a Juba-registered community organisation sits alongside the agencies with the budgets. Independent is the word that matters — it is not a government structure. AND THE BASELINE DOCUMENT TO ASK FOR BY NAME: A COUNTRY ENVIRONMENTAL PROFILE FOR SOUTH SUDAN, commissioned in June 2021 to identify and assess key environmental and climate change issues and INTENDED AS BASELINE INFORMATION FOR DECISION MAKERS — which concludes that THE CONSERVATION STATUS OF THE ECOSYSTEMS AND ANIMAL AND PLANT SPECIES IS EXTREMELY POOR, WITH FEW THREATENED SPECIES ADEQUATELY CONSERVED UNDER THE CURRENT SYSTEM, and that POLLUTION FROM EXTRACTIVE INDUSTRIES, DEFORESTATION DUE TO UNREGULATED CHARCOAL PRODUCTION AND CONSTRUCTION, AND INADEQUATELY CONTROLLED AND ILLEGAL EXTRACTION OF TIMBER, IVORY AND BUSHMEAT IS RAMPANT AND ON-GOING. ITS RECOMMENDATIONS NAME COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION, MECHANISMS FOR DISPUTE RESOLUTION, LAND TENURE ISSUES AND LAND MANAGEMENT, AND WEALTH-SHARING ARRANGEMENTS. An official baseline that already says conservation is extremely poor and extraction is rampant is evidence you do not have to gather. Cite the profile rather than arguing the point — and note that community participation, dispute resolution and wealth-sharing are its own recommendations, so asking for them is asking the state to do what its commissioned study told it to. WHO IT SUITS: South Sudanese communities facing a canal, dredging, extraction or charcoal clearance, and organisations seeking a coordinating body. CAVEATS: THE SUSPENSION IS A SUSPENSION, NOT A CANCELLATION, and the country remains under external pressure to complete the project — treat it as time bought. For protection first, legal aid and medical support, South Sudan's SSHRDN entry; for paralegals in Juba, the South Sudan Law Society entry; for two conservation organisations with street addresses, AERD and ACD; for customary rights held IN COMMON with EQUAL FORCE, the Land Act 2009 entry.

trackers.name: South Sudan's Justice and Confidence Centres for legal aid, the Terekeka cooperative a community formed with help, county FM radio, and the East African civil society seat a South Sudanese body holds
trackers.desc: A CENTRE FOR LEGAL AID, AND A COOPERATIVE THAT NOW EXISTS — two concrete things from a Juba organisation this file already holds, neither of them in its existing entry: AT ITS INCEPTION THE ORGANISATION WAS MAINLY LOOKING AT THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A JUSTICE AND CONFIDENCE CENTRE FOR THE PROVISION OF LEGAL AID SERVICES, AND PEACE BUILDING AND CONFLICT TRANSFORMATION THROUGH PEACE DIALOGUES. A named centre whose purpose is providing legal aid, founded before anything else the organisation does. Ask whether a Justice and Confidence Centre operates in your state — in a country where this file records almost no reachable legal help, a standing centre is the first thing to look for by name. AND THE OUTCOME THAT IS EXACTLY ON BRIEF: ITS LIVELIHOODS PROGRAMME, IMPLEMENTED IN TEREKEKA COUNTY OF CENTRAL EQUATORIA STATE, HELPED THE COMMUNITY OF GEMEIZA TO FORM A COOPERATIVE ASSOCIATION. A named community in a named county now has a cooperative association it did not have before, and an organisation helped it constitute one. This file has recorded the same shape in Angola and Equatorial Guinea: the cooperative is the legal person a community can actually get, and somebody will walk you through forming it. Ask for that help by naming Gemeiza — it has been done once, so the route exists. THE OTHER OUTCOME, STATED MODESTLY AND WORTH READING: THE COMMUNITY PEACE DIALOGUES ORGANISED IN LAKES STATE HAVE CREATED A SPACE OF OPENNESS BETWEEN THE CITIZENS AND LAKES STATE GOVERNMENT AUTHORITIES. A space of openness between citizens and their state government is not a small thing where the alternative is no contact at all. If your grievance cannot yet be framed as a legal claim, a dialogue that puts citizens and state authorities in the same room is the step before it can be. THE ORIGIN, WHICH IS A TEMPLATE ANY GROUP OF YOUNG PEOPLE CAN COPY: IT WAS FORMED TO ENGAGE UNIVERSITY STUDENTS AND FRESH GRADUATES IN BUILDING THEIR RESPECTIVE COMMUNITIES ON A VOLUNTARY BASIS — INITIALLY FORMED IN KHARTOUM IN 1999 CONSISTING MOSTLY OF UNIVERSITY STUDENTS, ITS SCOPE BROADENING AFTER IT WAS ESTABLISHED IN JUBA AS A SEPARATE ENTITY, AND REGISTERED BY THE MINISTRY OF JUSTICE ON 17 NOVEMBER 2010. Students, volunteering, in exile, in 1999 — and a registered national organisation eleven years later. Note the registering body: the MINISTRY OF JUSTICE, not the interior ministry. Where an organisation registers tells you what the state thinks it is, and it changes who you deal with afterwards. THE CONTACTS ARE PUBLISHED: A NAMED EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR, AN EMAIL ADDRESS AND TWO TELEPHONE NUMBERS. THE COMMUNICATION INFRASTRUCTURE IT BUILDS: an internal meeting was held for THE PROCUREMENT AND INSTALLATION OF FM RADIO FOR TWO NAMED COUNTIES. County FM radio, procured and installed by a civil society organisation. This file has recorded the same thing in Uganda, where listeners' clubs demanded a full station. A county with its own transmitter can hold a public conversation about a project; a county without one cannot. ITS OTHER WORK NAMES THE ROOMS IT CAN REACH: it issues ANNUAL ALTERNATIVE REPORTS ON THE STATUS OF GOVERNMENT, PRIVATE AND NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS ON PROMOTING TRANSPARENCY AND THE FIGHT AGAINST CORRUPTION, runs CORRUPTION EDUCATION THROUGH PUBLIC EVENTS, RADIO AND TV TALK SHOWS, and is THE NATIONAL CHAPTER OF THE EAST AFRICAN CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS' FORUM, having held a NATIONAL CONSULTATION WITH STAKEHOLDERS ON THE ROLE OF CIVIL SOCIETY IN THE EAST AFRICAN COMMUNITY AND HOW CSOs CAN CONTRIBUTE TO THE INTEGRATION PROCESS. An ALTERNATIVE report is the document you write when the official one is wrong. And the East African chapter seat matters for a specific reason recorded elsewhere in this file: the East African Court of Justice issued a restraining order that stopped Sudd dredging. The regional route exists, and here is the national body seated in the regional civil society forum. AND THE RISK, RECORDED PLAINLY BECAUSE ANY SOUTH SUDANESE READER NEEDS IT: MEMBERS OF THE ORGANISATION HAVE BEEN ARRESTED ON BASELESS ACCUSATIONS THAT THEY ARE FOREIGN AGENTS TRYING TO TOPPLE THE GOVERNMENT, AND ITS FOUNDER HAS BEEN THREATENED AND HARASSED, BEATEN AND ABUSED, ARRESTED AND DETAINED — AND HAS NOT BEEN DETERRED. Foreign agents is the accusation used against civil society across this file's record. Two defences worth preparing in advance: keep your funding sources and your statutes documented and consistent, and be a member of a domestic network that will say publicly that you are what you say you are. This file's emergency-fund entries exist for the moment those fail. WHO IT SUITS: South Sudanese communities needing legal aid, wanting to form a cooperative, or seeking a dialogue with state authorities. CAVEATS: OPERATING CONDITIONS ARE DANGEROUS and this entry says so rather than pretending otherwise. For the named team and the Council of Churches, South Sudan's CEPO entry; for protection first — legal aid, medical and relocation — SSHRDN; for the regional court that stopped the dredging, the East African Court of Justice entry; for the independent coordinating body of national and international NGOs, the South Sudan NGO Forum entry.

trackers.name: Who pays the lawyer when a company sues the person who reported on it — legal defence funding for bloggers and citizen journalists, applications accepted from family or a support organisation, and funded legal aid units in East, West and Southern Africa
trackers.desc: THEY PAY THE LAWYER FOR THE PERSON WHO WROTE IT DOWN — WHO COUNTS, AND IT IS BROADER THAN ALMOST ANYONE ASSUMES: THEY SUPPORT JOURNALISTS INCLUDING CITIZEN JOURNALISTS, BLOGGERS, BROADCASTERS, PHOTOJOURNALISTS, CARTOONISTS OR FACT-CHECKERS — AND NEWS OUTLETS — WHEN THEY ARE CONFRONTED WITH LEGAL ACTION AS A RESULT OF THEIR REPORTING. AS THEY PUT IT: JOURNALISM IS A FUNCTION SHARED BY A WIDE RANGE OF ACTORS. A CITIZEN JOURNALIST OR BLOGGER qualifies. So does the community member who posted the photographs of the clearance. This file has recorded companies suing the villager who filmed rather than the newspaper that printed it — and that villager is inside this definition. WHO MAY APPLY, WHICH REMOVES THE USUAL OBSTACLE: USUALLY APPLICATIONS ARE MADE BY THE LAWYER HANDLING THE CASE, BUT THEY CAN ALSO BE MADE BY THE JOURNALIST, THE FAMILY OR FRIENDS OF THE JOURNALIST, OR A RELEVANT SUPPORT ORGANISATION. Family or friends can apply. If the person is already detained and cannot write, somebody else can start it — which is exactly the situation in which help is needed and least likely to be sought. THE THREE THINGS ON OFFER: WE CAN PROVIDE FUNDING FOR YOUR LEGAL DEFENCE; WE CAN HELP YOU FIND A LAWYER; AND OUR LEGAL TEAM CAN PROVIDE TECHNICAL LEGAL SUPPORT TO YOUR LAWYER. Money, a lawyer, or expertise for the lawyer you already have. Most communities in this file need the third as much as the first: a competent local advocate who has never argued a free-expression case can be backed by specialists who have. AND THE FOURTH, WHICH IS OFFENSIVE RATHER THAN DEFENSIVE: WE CAN ALSO HELP YOU BRING LEGAL ACTION TO COMPEL THE STATE TO PROTECT YOUR RIGHTS IF THEY HAVE BEEN VIOLATED, INCLUDING TO INVESTIGATE ABUSES AND BRING PERPETRATORS OF ATTACKS TO JUSTICE. Not only defending the charge but forcing an investigation into the attack. Where a beating or a burning was never investigated, that is a case somebody will fund. THE PROBLEM NAMED IN THEIR OWN WORDS: THE LAW CAN BE USED AGAINST JOURNALISTS TO STOP THEM REPORTING; THOSE FACING LEGAL ACTION OFTEN CANNOT AFFORD A LAWYER, AND THERE IS A SHORTAGE OF LOCAL LEGAL CENTRES AND LAWYERS ABLE TO DEFEND THEM FREE OF CHARGE. DEFAMATION LAWS ARE REGULARLY ABUSED TO INTIMIDATE THE MEDIA AND STIFLE LEGITIMATE CRITICISM OF PUBLIC FIGURES AND INSTITUTIONS — AND THE THREAT OF HARSH CRIMINAL SANCTIONS, EXPENSIVE LITIGATION AND HIGH CIVIL DAMAGE AWARDS EXERTS A POWERFUL CHILLING EFFECT ON FREEDOM OF EXPRESSION. THE TACTIC WITH A NAME: STRATEGIC LAWSUITS AGAINST PUBLIC PARTICIPATION ARE A FORM OF LEGAL HARASSMENT DESIGNED TO INTIMIDATE JOURNALISTS AND SILENCE CRITICAL REPORTING — AND THEY HELP JOURNALISTS RESIST THESE ABUSIVE TACTICS. Learn the name and use it. A company suing a community group for objecting is not pursuing a grievance, it is running a recognised tactic — and calling it by its name in public, and to funders, changes how the case is understood. This file has recorded the same suits against land committees across the continent. THE PRIORITY RULE, SO YOU KNOW WHERE YOU STAND: SPECIAL PRIORITY IS GIVEN TO CASES IN WHICH AN INDIVIDUAL JOURNALIST IS THREATENED WITH IMPRISONMENT OR BANKRUPTCY, AS WELL AS MATTERS THAT THREATEN THE EXISTENCE OF A MEDIA OUTLET. BANKRUPTCY ranks alongside prison. A damages claim designed to ruin somebody is treated as seriously as a criminal charge — say so plainly in the application. THE AFRICAN CAPACITY WORK, WHICH IS THE DURABLE PART: THEY BUILD LOCAL LEGAL CAPACITY BY TRAINING LAWYERS AND FUNDING LOCAL LEGAL CENTRES THAT CAN REPRESENT JOURNALISTS FREE OF CHARGE, AND RUN REGIONAL LITIGATION SURGERIES TO STRENGTHEN THE CAPACITY OF LAWYERS WHO DEFEND THE MEDIA — CURRENTLY IN EAST, WEST AND SOUTHERN AFRICA. THEY PROVIDE FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE AND PRACTICAL SUPPORT TO ORGANISATIONS THAT EITHER HAVE, OR WISH TO ESTABLISH, A LEGAL AID UNIT. OR WISH TO ESTABLISH. If your organisation wants its own legal aid unit, this is a funder for exactly that — which is a far bigger prize than one case paid for. THE PRECEDENT ALREADY WON ON THIS CONTINENT: THEY SUPPORTED THE FIRST FREE SPEECH CASE BEFORE THE AFRICAN COURT OF HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS, WHICH RULED THAT THE IMPRISONMENT FOR DEFAMATION OF A JOURNALIST FROM A NAMED AFRICAN COUNTRY VIOLATED HIS RIGHTS. A continental ruling that jailing someone for defamation breaches their rights. That judgment is citable in any African court, and it exists because somebody funded one journalist's appeal. THE OTHER NAMED ROUTES: A LEGAL DEFENCE FUND GIVING FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO JOURNALISTS WHO FACE PROSECUTION OR IMPRISONMENT AND WHO ARE UNABLE TO AFFORD A LAWYER OR TRIAL COSTS, WITH A PUBLISHED EMAIL ADDRESS AND TELEPHONE NUMBER; A NONPROFIT PROVIDING PRO BONO REPRESENTATION THROUGH A NETWORK OF MORE THAN 600 LAWYERS AROUND THE WORLD; AND A NEARLY 300-PAGE DEFENCE HANDBOOK FOR JOURNALISTS AND BLOGGERS COVERING REPUTATION AND DEFAMATION, RIGHT TO PRIVACY, PUBLIC ORDER AND MORALITY, AND NATIONAL SECURITY AND STATE SECRETS. A free handbook with a chapter on each charge actually brought against people who publish. PUBLIC ORDER and NATIONAL SECURITY are the two most often used against land campaigners in this file — read those before you publish, not after the summons. WHO IT SUITS: African community members, bloggers and local outlets sued or charged over reporting on land, mining or environmental disputes. CAVEATS: THE THRESHOLD IS THAT THE LEGAL ACTION ARISES FROM REPORTING — a pure land dispute needs a different route. For the free brokerage that finds any organisation a pro bono firm, the Central African Republic's entry; for the centre giving rapid legal support when defenders are criminalized, Kenya's Strategic Legal Response Centre entry; for the fund naming land and environmental groups a priority, Tunisia's embattled-organisation entry.

trackers.name: The Oakland Institute — the think tank that publishes the purchase contracts, business plans and maps behind African land deals — free to reuse for advocacy and campaigning, indexed country by country, with informants' names deliberately withheld
trackers.desc: THEY PUT THE CONTRACT ITSELF ON THE INTERNET — adjacency declared first: A LAND-DEAL REPORTING SITE IS ALREADY A SOURCE HOST UNDER GABON, AND AN INTERNATIONAL LAND COALITION UNDER GHANA, LIBERIA AND MALAWI. NEITHER CARRIES THE CONTRACTS ARCHIVE DESCRIBED HERE. WHAT THEY PUBLISH, AND IT IS THE FIND: THE REPORTS ARE BASED ON THE ACTUAL MATERIALS FROM THESE LAND DEALS AND INCLUDE INVESTIGATION OF INVESTORS, PURCHASE CONTRACTS, BUSINESS PLANS AND MAPS NEVER RELEASED BEFORE. The purchase contract, the business plan and the map. This file has recorded community after community negotiating against a document they have never seen — and the Mauritania and Sudan entries give two other repositories. This one is different in kind: it publishes the investor's own BUSINESS PLAN, which states what the company told its financiers it would do, in numbers, before it told you anything. WHY THEY RELEASE THEM: WHAT IS DISCONCERTING ABOUT THE CURRENT LARGE-SCALE LAND INVESTMENTS IN AFRICA IS THE LACK OF TRANSPARENCY OF THE DEALS — SO THEY MAKE AVAILABLE THE DETAILED INFORMATION AND DOCUMENTATION COLLECTED IN THE COURSE OF THEIR RESEARCH, WITH ALL AVAILABLE REPORTS, LAND DEAL BRIEFS, CONTRACTS AND ADDITIONAL MATERIALS, VIEWABLE AS FULL DOCUMENTATION BY COUNTRY. FULL DOCUMENTATION BY COUNTRY is how to search it. Open your own country's page before commissioning any research — the deal on your land may already be documented, with the paperwork attached. THE COUNTRIES COVERED: A SEVEN-COUNTRY CASE STUDY PROJECT ON LAND INVESTMENT DEALS IN AFRICA — ETHIOPIA, MALI, MOZAMBIQUE, SIERRA LEONE, SUDAN, TANZANIA AND ZAMBIA — WITH RESEARCH ALSO COVERING SOUTH SUDAN. THE METHOD, WHICH ANY NATIONAL ORGANISATION COULD COPY: A THOROUGH EXAMINATION OF THE ACTUAL AGREEMENTS AND THE EXTENT AND DISTRIBUTION OF SPECIFIC LAND DEALS; FIELD RESEARCH INVOLVING EXTENSIVE DOCUMENTATION AND INTERVIEWS WITH LOCAL INFORMANTS; EXAMINATION OF SOCIAL, POLITICAL, ECONOMIC AND LEGAL IMPACTS; AND MEETINGS WITH GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS, CIVIL SOCIETY, INVESTORS AND THE LOCAL COMMUNITIES AFFECTED. They met the investors as well as the villagers. A study that has heard both sides is harder for a ministry to dismiss than one that has only heard yours — and asking the company for a meeting is free. THE REUSE LICENCE, WHICH IS WHY THIS MATTERS TO A COMMUNITY RATHER THAN A LIBRARY: THE TEXT MAY BE USED FREE OF CHARGE FOR THE PURPOSES OF ADVOCACY, CAMPAIGNING, EDUCATION AND RESEARCH, PROVIDED THE SOURCE IS ACKNOWLEDGED IN FULL — THE COPYRIGHT HOLDER REQUESTS THAT ALL SUCH USES BE REGISTERED WITH THEM FOR IMPACT ASSESSMENT PURPOSES, AND FOR OTHER COPYING, REUSE, TRANSLATION OR ADAPTATION, PERMISSION MUST BE SECURED BY EMAIL TO A PUBLISHED ADDRESS. FREE FOR ADVOCACY AND CAMPAIGNING, and translation permitted on request. So a community handbook can lift the findings wholesale, in the local language, provided the source is named — and registering the use costs one email and tells them their work reached somebody. THE SOURCE-PROTECTION PRACTICE, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE MODEL TO DEMAND: A SPECIAL APPRECIATION TO ALL THOSE WHO WERE COURAGEOUS ENOUGH TO SHARE THEIR STORIES DESPITE THE OBVIOUS RISKS TO THEIR OWN SAFETY AND SECURITY — THEIR NAMES HAVE NOT APPEARED IN THIS REPORT TO ENSURE THEIR SAFETY. Names withheld on purpose, and the reason printed. Before you give testimony to any researcher, ask what will appear under your name and who decides — this file has recorded defenders exposed by a published report they were never shown. THE SCALE: IN 2009 ALONE NEARLY 60 MILLION HECTARES — AN AREA THE SIZE OF FRANCE — WAS PURCHASED OR LEASED IN THESE LAND GRABS. THE PATTERN THEY FOUND, AND IT IS THE FINDING TO QUOTE IN AN OBJECTION: THESE LARGELY UNREGULATED LAND PURCHASES ARE RESULTING IN VIRTUALLY NONE OF THE PROMISED BENEFITS FOR NATIVE POPULATIONS, BUT INSTEAD ARE FORCING MILLIONS OF SMALL FARMERS OFF ANCESTRAL LANDS AND SMALL, LOCAL FOOD FARMS IN ORDER TO MAKE ROOM FOR EXPORT COMMODITIES, INCLUDING BIOFUELS AND CUT FLOWERS. VIRTUALLY NONE OF THE PROMISED BENEFITS, across seven countries, examined against the contracts. When a company promises your village jobs, a clinic and a road, that promise has been made before and measured afterwards — and this is the evidence that it was not kept. Put the finding in writing at the consultation and ask for the promises to be written into a binding schedule instead. THE MECHANISM NAMED: SPECULATORS TAKING OVER AGRICULTURAL LAND WHILE SMALL FARMERS, VIEWED AS SQUATTERS, ARE FORCIBLY REMOVED WITH NO COMPENSATION — TAKING THESE AWAY WHILE PROMISING PROGRESS THAT NEVER HAPPENS. VIEWED AS SQUATTERS is the legal move that does the damage, and it is why the land-recording entries in this file matter before an investor arrives rather than after. AND THE NAMED CASE STUDIES THAT FOLLOWED: A BRIEF ON VILLAGERS PAYING FOR A BIOFUELS INVESTMENT DISASTER; A REPORT ON A BROKEN DEVELOPMENT MODEL IN THE SAME COUNTRY; A REPORT ON THE HUMAN RIGHTS IMPACT OF LAND INVESTMENTS ON INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES IN A NAMED REGION; AND A REPORT ON PLANTATION FORESTRY AND CARBON VIOLENCE IN AN EAST AFRICAN COUNTRY. CARBON VIOLENCE, documented in a plantation forestry case years before the current wave of offset projects. Read it beside the carbon-developer training filed under Togo — together they are the warning and the preparation. WHO IT SUITS: African communities facing an agricultural, biofuel, plantation or carbon land deal who need the deal's own paperwork and a documented record of what such promises are worth. CAVEATS: A RESEARCH ARCHIVE RATHER THAN A SERVICE, AND MUCH OF THE CORE MATERIAL DATES FROM AN EARLIER WAVE OF DEALS — check dates before quoting figures. For the extractives contract repository, Mauritania's entry; for the community-investor guides and agreements collection, Sudan's entry; for the training that prepares a community before a carbon developer arrives, Togo's entry.

trackers.name: Grants of US$20,000–100,000 paid straight to producer organisations, spendable on hiring consultants and buying equipment — with a published instalment schedule, a 10–20% cash match, and 67% of the whole budget reaching the grassroots against a sector average under 2%
trackers.desc: SIXTY-SEVEN PERCENT REACHED THE GRASSROOTS. THE SECTOR AVERAGE IS UNDER TWO — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S SOMALIA ENTRY COVERS A FOREST NETWORK THAT NAMES THE HORN PASTORAL PARTNER, AND ITS LIBYA AND MALI ENTRIES COVER THE FOOD SOVEREIGNTY ALLIANCE AND THE FARMERS' FORUM. NONE CARRIES THIS GRANT PROGRAMME AND NONE OF THEIR HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE GRASSROOTS SHARE, STATED BY THE PROGRAMME ITSELF AS A COMPARISON, AND IT IS THE FIND: SIXTY-SEVEN PERCENT OF THE BUDGET DIRECTLY SUPPORTED FOREST AND FARM PRODUCER ORGANIZATIONS IN ONE YEAR — A LEVEL OF GRASSROOTS DELIVERY DESCRIBED AS EXTRAORDINARILY HIGH COMPARED WITH OTHER CLIMATE AND DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMMES, WHERE GENERALLY LESS THAN 2 PERCENT OF TOTAL BUDGETS GOES DIRECTLY TO THE GRASSROOTS. Under two percent is the number to carry out of this entry. It is the honest measure of nearly every climate and development fund a community will ever be told about — published by a UN-hosted programme about its own sector. Ask any funder approaching your community what share of its budget reaches organisations like yours, and use that figure as the benchmark. THE GRANT RANGE AND WHO RECEIVES IT: USD 20,000 TO USD 100,000, PROVIDED DIRECTLY TO SUCCESSFUL BENEFICIARY ORGANIZATIONS IN THREE SEPARATE INSTALMENTS DEPENDING ON THE SIZE OF THE GRANT, THE NATURE OF ACTIVITIES, THE HISTORY OF COLLABORATION AND THE OUTCOME OF THE TECHNICAL ASSESSMENT. Twenty thousand at the floor, paid to the organisation rather than through an intermediary. That is several times the size of most community grants in this file. WHAT THE MONEY MAY ACTUALLY BE SPENT ON, WHICH ALMOST NO OTHER FUND ALLOWS: A FLEXIBLE MECHANISM THAT ALLOWS PRODUCER ORGANISATIONS TO BUILD THEIR INTERNAL CAPACITIES BY HIRING CONSULTANTS AND PURCHASING NECESSARY EQUIPMENT. HIRING CONSULTANTS AND BUYING EQUIPMENT. This file has recorded that the thing nobody funds is the organisation itself — the lawyer, the accountant, the vehicle, the computer. Here that is the stated purpose, not a hidden overhead line to be argued over. THE CO-CONTRIBUTION RULE, PUBLISHED EXACTLY SO YOU CAN PLAN FOR IT: THE FACILITY SUPPORTS FROM 80% UP TO 90% OF THE INVESTMENTS IN THE WORK PLAN. THE MINIMUM BENEFICIARY CONTRIBUTION IS 10% IF INVESTMENTS ARE BELOW USD 10,000 AND 20% IF ABOVE — AND THE ORGANISATION COMMITS TO MATCH IN CASH. IN CASH is the trap to read twice. Your labour, your land and your buildings do not count — a fifth of the investment must be money you have. Plan the work plan's investment total around what your savings group can actually put up, because crossing USD 10,000 doubles the share you must find. THE PAYMENT SCHEDULE: FIRST PAYMENT 30% OF THE AWARD ON SIGNATURE; SECOND 50% ON CLEARANCE OF THE FIRST NARRATIVE AND FINANCIAL REPORTS; AND A THIRD AND FINAL PAYMENT AFTER THAT. Thirty percent up front, which is unusually generous — but half the money waits on your first financial report being accepted. An organisation without someone who can produce accounts will stall at that gate, so fix the bookkeeping before applying, not after. HOW TO APPLY AND HOW LONG THE PROJECT RUNS: THE PROPOSED DURATION SHOULD BE WITHIN 12 MONTHS FROM ASSIGNMENT OF THE GRANT; APPLICATIONS SHALL BE SUBMITTED THROUGH THE COUNTRY OFFICE OF THE HOSTING UN AGENCY; AND THE DEADLINE IS SPECIFIED IN EACH CALL, WITH LATE APPLICATIONS NOT CONSIDERED. THROUGH THE COUNTRY OFFICE. There is a UN agricultural office in your capital and it is the route — which means a visit, a phone call and a named officer, rather than an online portal. WHO IS ELIGIBLE: FOREST AND FARM PRODUCER ORGANIZATIONS REPRESENTING SMALLHOLDERS, RURAL WOMEN'S GROUPS, YOUTH, AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES. THE AFRICAN CORE COUNTRIES: GHANA, KENYA, MADAGASCAR, TOGO, TANZANIA AND ZAMBIA — WITH ADDITIONAL NETWORK COUNTRIES FOR WHICH FUNDING IS ACTIVELY BEING SOUGHT INCLUDING GAMBIA AND LIBERIA. ACTIVELY SEEKING FUNDING for named countries not yet covered. If yours is on that second list, the programme wants to arrive and is looking for money to do it — which makes a letter of demand from national producer organisations useful to them rather than a nuisance. THE FIRST-PHASE RESULTS, AND ONE CLAUSE MATTERS MOST: PRODUCER ORGANISATIONS THEMSELVES LEVERAGED MORE THAN $100 MILLION IN ADDITIONAL FINANCE, PRESSED THROUGH 51 POLICY CHANGES — INCLUDING LONG-STALLED HANDOVERS OF FOREST LAND RIGHTS — AND ATTRACTED 158 NEW FINANCIAL INVESTMENTS IN 262 BUSINESSES. LONG-STALLED HANDOVERS OF FOREST LAND RIGHTS, unblocked by producer organisations with small grants behind them. This file records those handovers stalling for decades; the lever that moved them was organised producers, not litigation. THE ADVOCACY OUTCOME IT FUNDS EXPLICITLY: MORE ENABLING POLICY AND LEGAL FRAMEWORKS DELIVERED THROUGH MORE INCLUSIVE GOVERNANCE AND CROSS-SECTORAL PROCESSES — WITH A STATED OUTPUT THAT THE ORGANISATIONS HAVE CLEAR ADVOCACY AGENDAS THAT REPRESENT ALL THEIR MEMBERS' INTERESTS, ALONGSIDE STRENGTHENING ORGANISATIONAL MANAGEMENT CAPACITY AND EMPOWERING WOMEN WITHIN THE ORGANISATIONS. Advocacy named as a fundable output. Compare the indigenous-led fund filed under Chad, which excludes political campaigns — the two are complementary, and which one you approach should depend on how the work is framed. THE PROBLEM IT NAMES: MANY PRODUCERS STRUGGLE TO ACCESS FINANCE FROM BANKS AND MICROFINANCE INSTITUTIONS, GOVERNMENT SUPPORT PROGRAMMES OR PRIVATE-SECTOR PARTNERS — SO TO IMPROVE ACCESS TO MARKETS AND FINANCE, INDIVIDUALS WORK TOGETHER TO ESTABLISH PRODUCER ORGANISATIONS. AND THE ILLEGALITY WORK ON RECORD: WOOD FUEL VALUE CHAINS HAVE BEEN AT THE CENTRE OF ITS EFFORTS, WITH SUCCESSFUL COUNTRY INITIATIVES TO TACKLE ILLEGALITY HOTSPOTS IN SIX NAMED AFRICAN COUNTRIES. Charcoal and firewood, treated as a value chain worth organising rather than a nuisance to police. For communities blamed for deforestation they did not cause, that framing is itself useful. WHO IT SUITS: organised African forest and farm producer groups, women's and youth producer organisations, in or near the named countries. CAVEATS: A CASH MATCH OF 10–20% IS REQUIRED, HALF THE MONEY DEPENDS ON AN ACCEPTED FINANCIAL REPORT, AND CALLS RUN BY COUNTRY WITH FIRM DEADLINES — unregistered groups will struggle. For the fund that waives registration and bank account entirely, the Central African Republic's entry; for the savings model that builds the cash match from nothing, Djibouti's entry; for the farmer-owned forum a group joins first, Mali's entry.

trackers.name: The Ramsar Convention Secretariat — a treaty secretariat that can open a collaborative process on a threatened wetland from information it receives, and send a technical advisory mission — with the consent limits and the published criticisms of the mechanism set out
trackers.desc: THE SECRETARIAT CAN ACT ON WHAT IT LEARNS. THE LISTING NEEDS YOUR GOVERNMENT — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S SEYCHELLES ENTRY CARRIES A WETLANDS ORGANISATION HOST, ITS ERITREA ENTRY THE CIVIL SOCIETY REPORTING ROUTE TO THE WORLD HERITAGE COMMITTEE — A DIFFERENT CONVENTION WITH A DIFFERENT MECHANISM — AND ITS MAURITANIA ENTRY THE LANDSCAPE FUND. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE SECRETARIAT'S POWER TO ACT ON INFORMATION, WHICH IS THE FIND: IF THE SECRETARIAT BELIEVES A SIGNIFICANT CHANGE HAS OR IS LIKELY TO OCCUR, THE SECRETARIAT CAN BEGIN A COLLABORATIVE PROCESS TO TRY TO FIND A SOLUTION AND CAN PROVIDE ADVICE AND ASSISTANCE — AND IF THIS PROCESS WILL NOT READILY YIELD A SOLUTION, THE SECRETARIAT MUST NOTIFY THE STANDING COMMITTEE, WHICH WILL ALSO ATTEMPT TO WORK OUT AN ACCEPTABLE SOLUTION. What triggers it is the Secretariat BELIEVING a change is likely — the text does not restrict where that belief comes from. A community with photographs, water measurements and dates of a drainage scheme or a dam has something to send, and the escalation to the Standing Committee is written as a MUST rather than a discretion. This file's world heritage entry under Eritrea is the parallel route for a different convention; this is the wetlands one. THE TREATY DUTY THAT SITS UNDER IT: ARTICLE 3.2 OBLIGES EACH CONTRACTING PARTY TO ARRANGE TO BE INFORMED AT THE EARLIEST POSSIBLE TIME IF THE ECOLOGICAL CHARACTER OF ANY WETLAND IN ITS TERRITORY HAS CHANGED, IS CHANGING, OR IS LIKELY TO CHANGE AS A RESULT OF TECHNOLOGICAL DEVELOPMENTS, POLLUTION, OR OTHER HUMAN INTERFERENCE. Your own government has undertaken to ARRANGE TO BE INFORMED. A formal letter telling the ministry what is happening is not a nuisance — it is the mechanism by which it discharges a treaty obligation, and that is the framing to use when writing it. THE ADVISORY MISSION: AT THE REQUEST OF A CONTRACTING PARTY, THE SECRETARIAT MAY ORGANIZE AN ADVISORY MISSION TO ANALYZE THE SITUATION AT ONE OR MORE SITES AND PROVIDE ADVICE ON MEASURES — A TECHNICAL SUPPORT MECHANISM FORMALLY ADOPTED BY THE CONVENTION. Independent international experts on your wetland, paid for by the treaty, but only if the government asks. Asking costs the government nothing and is framed as technical assistance rather than scrutiny, which makes it a realistic thing to lobby a ministry for. THE CONSENT LIMIT, RECORDED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT DECIDES WHAT IS POSSIBLE: SITES MAY ONLY BE ADDED TO OR WITHDRAWN FROM THE RECORD WITH THE CONSENT OF THE CONTRACTING PARTIES IN WHOSE TERRITORY THEY ARE LOCATED — DISTINGUISHING THE MECHANISM FROM A PUNITIVE OR SUPERVISORY LISTING. You cannot list a site over your government's objection. Every use of this route runs through persuading the ministry, so treat it as an argument to win at home rather than a complaint to file abroad. THE CRITICISM PUBLISHED ALONGSIDE IT: THE RELATIVELY SMALL NUMBER OF SITES ON THE RECORD — FAR FEWER THAN THE DOCUMENTED CASES OF ECOLOGICAL CHANGE — REFLECTS THIS CONSENT-BASED DESIGN; AND CRITICS NOTE THAT DELISTING CAN BE DRIVEN BY POLITICAL AND REPUTATIONAL CONSIDERATIONS AS MUCH AS BY VERIFIED ECOLOGICAL RECOVERY. Recorded so nobody spends a year on a false expectation: most damaged wetlands never appear, and removals are not proof of recovery. Check whether a site near you was quietly delisted and on what evidence. THE FRAMING OFFERED TO GOVERNMENTS, WHICH IS THE PERSUASION ANGLE: FAR FROM BEING A BLACKLIST OR A NEGATIVE MARK FOR A COUNTRY, THE REGISTRY IS AN OPPORTUNITY FOR GOVERNMENTS TO DEMONSTRATE THEIR ACCOUNTABILITY FOR PROTECTING NATURAL RESOURCES THAT REQUIRE URGENT ATTENTION. That sentence is the one to put in the letter. A ministry refuses what looks like an accusation and considers what looks like a chance to show competence — and this framing comes from the system itself, not from you. HOW A GOVERNMENT PUTS A SITE ON: IT MUST FORMALLY SOLICIT THE SECRETARIAT AND COMPLETE A QUESTIONNAIRE WITH INFORMATION ABOUT THE WETLAND — AND IF INCLUSION IS DETERMINED NECESSARY, AN ADVISORY MISSION FOLLOWS TO PROVIDE SUPPORT AND TECHNICAL ADVICE. A questionnaire is the whole administrative burden, and a community that has already gathered the water, species and land-use evidence can hand the ministry most of the answers. That is the cheapest way to make a yes likely. THE ROUTE BACK OFF: THE COUNTRY MAY REQUEST REMOVAL ONCE THE THREATS ARE GONE, REQUESTING A NEW ADVISORY VISIT AND COMPLETING A SURVEY TO SHOW THE PROGRESS MADE. THE CONVENTION'S OWN HIERARCHY FOR DAMAGE, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT TO QUOTE AT A HEARING: MAINTAINING OR RESTORING ECOLOGICAL CHARACTER WHEREVER POSSIBLE; ONLY IF THAT IS NOT POSSIBLE SHOULD ANY CONSIDERATION OF RESTRICTING OR DELISTING A SITE BE CONSIDERED; AND IF UNPREVENTABLE LOSS OR DETERIORATION DOES OCCUR, MITIGATION IS EXPECTED, WITH COMPENSATION MEASURES AS A LAST-RESORT OPTION WHERE THE CHANGE IS IRREVERSIBLE. Compensation is the LAST resort, not the opening offer. This file has recorded project after project arriving with a compensation package as the first and only conversation; the convention your government signed puts avoidance first, restoration second, mitigation third, and money last. THE TRANSBOUNDARY OPTION: MANY INTERNATIONALLY IMPORTANT WETLANDS EXTEND AS ONE ECOLOGICALLY COHERENT WHOLE ACROSS NATIONAL BORDERS, AND PARTIES CAN AGREE TO ESTABLISH SITES ON THEIR TERRITORY AS PARTS OF A BIGGER TRANSBOUNDARY SITE. A river, swamp or floodplain shared with a neighbouring country can be listed as one thing. Where the harm comes from upstream in another state, that is the structure that makes it a shared obligation rather than somebody else's problem. AND THE DESIGNATION ROUTE AND SCALE: DESIGNATION OCCURS WHEN PARTIES NOMINATE SITES MEETING AT LEAST ONE OF NINE CRITERIA — SUCH AS CONTAINING REPRESENTATIVE OR UNIQUE WETLAND TYPES, OR SUPPORTING VULNERABLE SPECIES OR LARGE POPULATIONS OF WATERBIRDS — UNDER A TREATY IN FORCE SINCE 1975, WHOSE PARTIES GREW FROM ABOUT 90 IN THE MID-1990s TO OVER 170, WITH TARGETED OUTREACH TO DEVELOPING NATIONS PARTICULARLY IN AFRICA. ONE of nine criteria is enough. A wetland does not have to be famous — being a representative example of a wetland type in its region can be sufficient, which puts designation within reach for far more places than communities assume. WHO IT SUITS: African communities whose marsh, floodplain, lake or delta is threatened by drainage, damming, pollution or conversion — working through their own environment ministry. CAVEATS: EVERYTHING RUNS THROUGH GOVERNMENT CONSENT, THE REGISTER IS SMALL RELATIVE TO THE DAMAGE, AND THE CONVENTION ADVISES RATHER THAN ENFORCES — pair it with the domestic legal routes. For the world heritage reporting route that accepts civil society reports directly, Eritrea's entry; for the landscape fund paying long-term management money, Mauritania's entry.

trackers.name: Wild Landscapes International — an organisation that buys the land outright — a 1,425-acre farm acquired with a local trust and placed into conservation, two adjoining farms being bought next, and an open invitation for partners to send in their own projects
trackers.desc: THEY BOUGHT THE FARM, AND THEY ARE BUYING THE TWO NEXT DOOR — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S SOMALIA ENTRY COVERS THE ZERO-OVERHEAD WILDLIFE FUNDER WHOSE RHINO FUND IS NAMED ALONGSIDE THIS ORGANISATION IN ONE PROJECT; ITS KENYA BUCKET CARRIES A WILDLIFE FOUNDATION AND A RANGELANDS TRUST HOST; ITS TANZANIA BUCKET A RAINFOREST TRUST AND A NATURE CONSERVANCY HOST; ITS MAURITANIA ENTRY THE LANDSCAPE FUND WITH A 2,000 SQUARE KILOMETRE MINIMUM. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. A SCAN OF ALL 53 BUCKETS FOUND LAND PURCHASE TO BE THE THINNEST THEME IN THIS FILE; THIS ENTRY IS WEIGHTED TO IT. THE PURCHASE ITSELF, WHICH IS THE FIND: IN COLLABORATION WITH A NAMED LOCAL CONSERVATION TRUST, IT IS PROTECTING A RARE VEGETATION TYPE BY ACQUIRING A NAMED FARM SPANNING 1,425 ACRES — A PURCHASE THAT DOUBLES THE SIZE OF AN EXISTING RESERVE AND PLACES THE LAND INTO CONSERVATION, SAFEGUARDING THE LARGEST REMAINING AREA OF ONE OF THE WORLD'S MOST CRITICALLY ENDANGERED AND BIODIVERSE ECOSYSTEMS. Bought, not campaigned over. Where a threatened piece of land is privately owned and for sale, the shortest route to saving it is a buyer, and this file has had almost nothing to say about who that buyer might be. Here is a body that does it, with the acreage and the local trust named — and note the structure: an international organisation with the money, a LOCAL trust that will hold and manage it. AND IT IS NOT A ONE-OFF: WORK IS UNDERWAY TO ACQUIRE TWO ADJOINING FARMS TO FURTHER EXPAND AND SECURE THAT ECOSYSTEM — WITH THE PURCHASE ALSO OFFERING THE POSSIBILITY OF CREATING A WILDLIFE CORRIDOR THAT CONNECTS TO A NATIONAL PARK. Buying adjoining parcels one at a time until they connect to protected land. That is a strategy a local trust can pursue over years, and it means the first purchase does not have to be the whole landscape. THE OPEN INVITATION, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: WE ARE ALWAYS EAGER TO EXPLORE NEW OPPORTUNITIES TO COLLABORATE AND MAKE A MEANINGFUL IMPACT — WE WELCOME PROSPECTIVE PARTNERS TO REACH OUT AND SHARE THEIR PROJECTS. An explicit invitation to write to them with a project. Most organisations in this file that hold real money say nothing of the kind, and an unprompted approach with a specific parcel, a price and a local partner is exactly what this asks for. THE GAP IT SAYS IT EXISTS TO FILL: WITHOUT CONNECTIONS TO GOVERNMENT FUNDING OR PHILANTHROPY HUBS IN NAMED WEALTHY CENTRES, ORGANISATIONS STRUGGLE TO SECURE THE SUPPORT NEEDED TO PROTECT GLOBALLY SIGNIFICANT LANDSCAPES — AND IT ADDRESSES THIS BY OFFERING EXPERTISE IN FUNDRAISING, PUBLIC FINANCE, AND LANDSCAPE CONSERVATION. PUBLIC FINANCE expertise offered to partners. Land is often bought with a mix of philanthropy and government money, and knowing how to assemble that mix is the specialist skill a local trust almost never has. WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: WE ARE NOT A PROGRAMME-BASED ORGANISATION — EVERY PROJECT WE SUPPORT IS INTENDED TO HAVE A BEGINNING, A MIDDLE, AND AN END; OUR ROLE IS TO HELP SET THINGS IN MOTION: TO FILL A GAP, BUILD CAPACITY, REMOVE A BOTTLENECK, AND THEN STEP BACK. An end date, stated in advance. Ask what the exit looks like at the first conversation — a partner that plans to leave is easier to work with than one that plans to stay, provided the handover is written down. THE HANDOVER IT AIMS AT: WHERE POSSIBLE WE HAND OVER TO OTHERS, OR HELP BUILD THE FOUNDATIONS FOR LONG-TERM SUCCESS — STRONGER INSTITUTIONS, BETTER GOVERNANCE, CLEARER FUNDING PIPELINES, AND MORE RESILIENT PARTNERSHIPS; A MORE SUSTAINABLE MODEL THAT DOES NOT RELY INDEFINITELY ON EXTERNAL DONORS OR LARGE INTERNATIONAL NGOs, BUT THAT CAN STAND ON ITS OWN FEET. THE LOCAL ENTITY IT BUILT: AN EAST AFRICA AFFILIATE FOUNDED IN 2024 TO STRENGTHEN AND EXPAND ITS WORK IN TWO NAMED COUNTRIES AND THE WIDER REGION — ESTABLISHED BECAUSE, TO BE EFFECTIVE IN A LANDSCAPE, YOU NEED PEOPLE WHO KNOW IT WELL, WHO UNDERSTAND NOT ONLY THE ECOLOGY BUT THE POLITICS, THE PEOPLE, THE CLIMATE, AND THE WAY DECISIONS ACTUALLY GET MADE. A regional office founded on the continent is the address to write to rather than the head office. THE RESCUE ON RECORD, AND THE WARNING IN IT: WHEN MAJOR SOURCES OF OUTSIDE FUNDING COLLAPSED IN 2024, A NAMED COMMUNITY CONSERVANCY FACED ITS GREATEST TEST — RANGER TEAMS WENT UNPAID, PATROLS FALTERED, AND THE SANCTUARY ITSELF WAS IN JEOPARDY; THE AFFILIATE AND OTHER PARTNERS STEPPED IN TO BRIDGE THE GAP. IT WAS A STARK REMINDER THAT EVEN THE MOST SUCCESSFUL COMMUNITY PROJECTS REMAIN VULNERABLE WITHOUT STEADY SUPPORT. A successful community conservancy nearly collapsed in one year when its donor went. Winning the land is not the end of the problem, and any community taking on land should ask what happens the year the money stops — which is the argument for the revenue model below and for the unrestricted funders elsewhere in this file. THE REVENUE MODEL IT IS BUILDING AT THAT SITE: A PARTNERSHIP WITH A COMMUNITY AND A TOURISM FOUNDATION TO ESTABLISH A NEW SAFARI LODGE, DESIGNED TO GENERATE LONG-TERM REVENUE FOR SPECIES PROTECTION, COMMUNITY LIVELIHOODS, AND RANGELAND MANAGEMENT. Recorded plainly because it cuts both ways: a lodge is income the community controls, and it is also a tourism operator on community land. The terms of that agreement decide which — and this file's Cape Verde entry on conditions for engagement with external actors is the document to have written before signing one. THE CORRIDOR AT SCALE: IN PARTNERSHIP WITH LOCAL CONSERVANCIES IN A NAMED KENYAN COUNTY, IT IS WORKING TO CREATE A 556,000-ACRE RHINO CORRIDOR WITH A SWAHILI NAME. WHO IT SAYS IT WORKS THROUGH: COMMUNITIES, CONSERVATIONISTS, INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, RANCHERS, FORESTERS, FISHERFOLK, AND GOVERNMENT AGENCIES — THROUGH A ONE-OFF, PROJECT-BASED APPROACH THAT STRENGTHENS LONG-TERM LOCAL STEWARDSHIP. AND ITS SIZE AND APPETITE: FOUNDED IN 2018, A SMALL, DEEPLY EXPERIENCED TEAM, NIMBLE AND EFFICIENT, WITH LOW OVERHEADS AND LITTLE BUREAUCRACY — WHICH IT SAYS PUTS IT IN A BETTER POSITION TO TAKE ON AMBITIOUS, HIGHER-RISK PROJECTS, WHERE THE STAKES ARE HIGHER BUT THE RETURN IS EVEN MORE MEANINGFUL. HIGHER-RISK PROJECTS, volunteered. A parcel that larger conservation organisations have declined as too complicated is the kind of thing worth putting to them. WHO IT SUITS: African local trusts, conservancies and community organisations with a specific parcel that needs buying, and no route to the money or the transaction expertise. CAVEATS: A SMALL ORGANISATION DOING SELECTED ONE-OFF PROJECTS, NOT A STANDING ACQUISITION FUND WITH AN APPLICATION WINDOW; ITS AFRICAN WEIGHT IS IN EAST AFRICA AND ONE SOUTHERN AFRICAN ECOSYSTEM, AND IT EXPECTS A CAPABLE LOCAL PARTNER TO HOLD THE LAND AFTERWARDS — arrange that partner first. For the fund naming community conserved areas as eligible grantees, Mauritania's entry; for the zero-overhead funder, Somalia's entry.

trackers.name: Masifundise Development Trust — a trust that sued the national fisheries minister and won an out-of-court agreement obliging the government to write a new policy for 30,000 small-scale fishers — and built the 4,000-member fisher organisation, with elected branch committees, that holds it to account
trackers.desc: THEY SUED THE FISHERIES MINISTER AND GOT A NEW NATIONAL POLICY OUT OF IT — method and adjacency declared first: THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THE SHIPPED HOST AND FIVE SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; THE HOST AND FOUR SPELLINGS ABSENT. THIS FILE'S SOMALIA ENTRY NAMES A COASTAL LINKS ORGANISATION IN A LIST OF EIGHT MOVEMENTS WITHOUT DESCRIBING IT OR SHIPPING THIS HOST; ITS NIGER AND RWANDA ENTRIES USE THE RIGHT-TO-SAY-NO PHRASE IN OTHER ENTRIES; ITS MALI ENTRY THE FISHERS' CO-OPERATIVE LITIGATION. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE COURT CASE AND WHAT IT FORCED, WHICH IS THE FIND: IN 2004 LEGAL ACTION WAS LAUNCHED AGAINST THE MINISTER CONCERNED, CITING CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHTS TO FOOD SECURITY, CULTURE, AND THE RIGHT TO OCCUPATIONS AND LIVELIHOODS — AND IN 2007 THE MINISTER SIGNED AN OUT OF COURT AGREEMENT THAT OBLIGED THE GOVERNMENT TO DEVELOP A NEW FISHERIES POLICY ACCOMMODATING THE SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC RIGHTS OF 30,000 SMALL-SCALE FISHER PEOPLE. Not damages for one community — a national policy, written because a fishers' organisation sued. Three years from filing to settlement, and the remedy was legislative. That is the largest ratio of effort to outcome recorded in this file, and the grounds are worth copying: FOOD SECURITY, CULTURE, AND OCCUPATION, rather than property. A community with no title has all three. THE STRUCTURE OF THE ORGANISATION THEY BUILT, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: ESTABLISHED IN 2003, WITH OVER 2,000 MEMBERS ACROSS 89 COASTAL TOWNS IN FOUR PROVINCES IN ONE ACCOUNT AND 4,000 IN ANOTHER — WITH PROVINCIAL, REGIONAL, SUB-REGIONAL AND BRANCH STRUCTURES; EACH BRANCH HAS A COMMITTEE WITH ELECTED OFFICIALS WHO REPRESENT THEM ON THE REGIONAL COMMITTEE, AND A REGION ELECTS A REGIONAL SECRETARY AND CHAIRPERSON. Four tiers, every one elected from below. That is the constitutional shape to copy for any scattered set of villages: the branch elects its committee, the branch committee sits regionally, the region elects its own officers. Nobody is appointed downward, which is what this file records going wrong when a national body speaks for communities it did not consult. THE APPEAL COURT RULING BEHIND IT: A 2018 SUPREME COURT OF APPEAL RULING RECOGNISED THE RIGHTS OF SMALL-SCALE FISHERS TO CONTINUE CUSTOMARY FISHING PRACTICES. Customary practice recognised by an appellate court — the same argument this file's Guinea-Bissau entry records being made about customary land, won here on water. THE TRIBUNAL AND WHAT IT WAS FOR: A FISHER PEOPLE TRIBUNAL HELD OVER THREE DAYS IN A NAMED CHURCH, THE COUNTRY'S FIRST PEOPLE'S TRIBUNAL FOCUSED ON FISHING COMMUNITIES — ATTEMPTING TO DOCUMENT AND EXPOSE OCEAN GRABBING AND THE VIOLATIONS OF FISHING COMMUNITIES' RIGHTS, AND TO CHECK IF THEIR RIGHTS ARE BEING MET; A JURY VERDICT WAS LAUNCHED PUBLICLY AFTERWARDS. A people's tribunal with a jury and a published verdict, held in a church hall over three days. It has no legal force, and that is the point: where the state will not hold a hearing, the community holds its own, on the record, with testimony that can then be used elsewhere. Cheap, and entirely within a coalition's own control. WHAT THE CAMPAIGNING ACTUALLY CONSISTED OF: STREET CAMPAIGNS, MEDIA COVERAGE, DIPLOMATIC MEETINGS WITH LOCAL AND NATIONAL GOVERNMENT, AND THE COURT CASE — WHICH LED TO ONE OF THEIR MOST SIGNIFICANT VICTORIES. Four instruments used together. The litigation is listed last and did not stand alone. THE THREATS THE MEMBERSHIP ORGANISATION NAMES: THE PRIVATISATION OF COASTAL LAND THAT LIMITS ACCESS TO THE SEA; ASSERTING COMMUNAL AND CUSTOMARY RIGHTS; RECOGNITION AND PROTECTION OF TRADITIONAL FISHING PRACTICES; GENDER EQUITY AND THE ROLE OF WOMEN AND YOUTH; PARTICIPATION IN CO-MANAGEMENT; STRENGTHENING LOCAL BRANCHES AND DISSEMINATING THE POLICY AT BRANCH LEVEL; AND AN IMPROVED EXEMPTION ALLOCATION UNTIL THE POLICY IS IMPLEMENTED. PRIVATISATION OF COASTAL LAND THAT LIMITS ACCESS TO THE SEA is the fishing equivalent of enclosure: the water is still public, but the road to it is not. Worth naming early wherever a coastal development is proposed. WHAT MAKES FISHING UNVIABLE, IN ITS OWN LIST: CORPORATE MONOPOLIES, OVERFISHING, POLLUTION OF THE OCEANS AND GOVERNMENT ACTION — WITH MANY POOR COMMUNITIES DENIED ACCESS BY ELITE GROUPS WHO PLACE NARROW COMMERCIAL INTERESTS ABOVE THE RIGHT OF FISHERS TO EARN A LIVING. THE INLAND EXTENSION, WHICH IS RARELY COVERED: IN 2017 IT TURNED ITS ATTENTION TO ASSISTING INLAND FISHING COMMUNITIES, WITH CURRENT LEGISLATION NOT RECOGNISING SMALL-SCALE FISHING FOR LIVELIHOODS IN RIVERS AND DAMS — WORKING ON A DAM FISHERY PROJECT, HELPING COMMUNITIES SET UP COMMITTEES IN NAMED TOWNS AND ENGAGING GOVERNMENT, RECREATIONAL FISHERS AND A UNIVERSITY. River and dam fishers are invisible in law almost everywhere, and this file has recorded dam projects displacing them with no category to claim under. An organisation that has taken that on, and works with the recreational fishers rather than against them, is a rare model. WHAT IT DOES BEYOND CAMPAIGNS: IT FACILITATES THE FORMATION AND GROWTH OF MASS BASED COMMUNITY ORGANISATIONS IN POOR COASTAL AREAS, AND DEVELOPS DISCUSSION PAPERS THAT SPEAK IN THE VOICE OF TRADITIONAL SMALL-SCALE FISHERS AND CRITICALLY ANALYSE CONCEPTS AND DEFINITIONS RELATED TO FISHERY POLICY. DEFINITIONS is where these fights are won or lost: who counts as a small-scale fisher decides who gets a permit, and the definition is written in policy documents most communities never read. THE PROGRAMME'S FOUR OBJECTIVES: EMPOWERMENT FOR SOCIAL ACTIVISM ESPECIALLY YOUTH; DEMONSTRATING FOOD SOVEREIGNTY THROUGH PROVINCIAL AND MICRO-PROJECTS; SYSTEMIC CHANGE THROUGH ACCOUNTABLE LEGAL AND INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORKS COMMITTED TO PARTICIPATORY GOVERNANCE; AND GLOBAL SOLIDARITY AMONGST SMALL-SCALE FOOD PRODUCERS. THE CONSERVATION ARGUMENT IT MAKES: SMALL-SCALE FISHERS ARE THE CUSTODIANS OF NATURAL RESOURCES BECAUSE THEY DEPEND ON THESE RESOURCES IN ORDER TO SURVIVE — WITH A STAFF MEMBER TRAVELLING COMMUNITY TO COMMUNITY, REACHING THREE OF THE FOUR COASTAL PROVINCES AT LEAST TWICE IN A SINGLE YEAR. The counter-argument to conservation-by-exclusion, made by the people excluded. And the travel figure is the honest cost of holding a coastal membership together. AND THE ALLIANCES ON RECORD: MEMBERS HAVE PARTICIPATED IN INTERNATIONAL FORUMS INCLUDING A UNITED NATIONS FOOD AND AGRICULTURE BODY; THE ORIGINAL LITIGATION WAS RUN WITH A HUMAN RIGHTS LITIGATION ORGANISATION; THE TRUST CO-FOUNDED A NATIONAL RURAL EDUCATION COLLECTIVE IN 1980; AND IT ISSUES JOINT PRESS RELEASES WITH A CAMPAIGN ASSERTING COMMUNITIES' RIGHT TO REFUSE OIL AND GAS DEVELOPMENT ON A NAMED STRETCH OF COAST. The fishers did not litigate alone: a public-interest law organisation ran the case with them. That pairing — a membership organisation plus a litigation partner — is the combination behind most of the wins recorded in this file. WHO IT SUITS: coastal and inland fishing communities losing access to water or shore, and any scattered membership wanting a four-tier elected structure or a people's tribunal model. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY, WITH A FISHERIES AND FOOD-SOVEREIGNTY FRAME RATHER THAN LAND PURCHASE; IT ORGANISES, RESEARCHES AND CAMPAIGNS AND LITIGATES THROUGH LEGAL PARTNERS RATHER THAN AS A LAW CENTRE. For the organisation that builds rural bodies before the land claim, Somalia's entry; for the co-operative named as co-applicant in offshore litigation, Mali's entry.

trackers.name: Natural Justice: Lawyers for Communities and the Environment
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an African public-interest law organisation — lawyers and paralegals working with communities facing mining, oil and gas, logging and large infrastructure, combining legal empowerment, community protocols, policy work and litigation. Hubs in Cape Town, Nairobi and Dakar, staff in Madagascar, Botswana and Guinea, and country programmes in Burkina Faso, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Namibia, Nigeria, Senegal and South Africa. It also runs the Environmental Lawyers Collective for Africa and an EIA Process Tracker. WHO IT SUITS: an Indigenous or rural community whose land, water or customary rights are threatened by an extractive or infrastructure project. It takes selected cases and works project-to-project outside its programme countries, so expect an approach-and-assess conversation rather than open intake. IS THERE AN OFFICE NEAR YOU? NO — this is project-to-project country.
