Natural Justice's 3 hubs are Cape Town, Nairobi and Dakar, with additional staff in Antananarivo, Botswana and Guinea; elsewhere it works across African countries on a project-to-project basis. So you are asking them to take on a project, not walking into an office — approach with a defined case and expect that answer to depend on their current programme. Its team page does list staff and fellows beyond the hub countries. WHAT IT DOES: founded 2007 in Cape Town, it supports communities to know the law, use the law and shape the law — access to land and governance of natural resources, the struggle against harmful extractive and infrastructure developments, traditional knowledge and benefit sharing, community rights within conservation, and climate action. ITS SIGNATURE TOOL IS THE COMMUNITY PROTOCOL — a documented instrument letting a community set out its biological, cultural and spiritual resources, norms and values, and assert existing rights under customary, domestic and international law, aimed squarely at laws and projects developed by government and industry without consultation. Ask for it by name. Contact: 63 Hout Street, Cape Town 8001; +27 21 426 1633; info@naturaljustice.org.

trackers.name: African Environmental Defenders Fund (emergency grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the African Environmental Defenders Fund — an emergency grant fund run by Natural Justice with the International Land Coalition Africa, ICCA Consortium, PACJA, Oxfam Novib, FEMNET and others, giving up to US$5,000 to land and environmental defenders anywhere in Africa who are under threat because of their activism. It can cover the cost of legal representation where a defender is arrested, summoned or prosecuted, plus relocation and other short-term transitional costs. WHO IT SUITS: an individual frontline defender who is a citizen or legal resident of an African country, facing an imminent threat, and not already supported by another body — it is not project or core funding, and routine office and administrative costs are excluded. HOW IT DIFFERS: applications are rolling, by email or helpline, not to a grant round. Natural Justice's own site names Burkina Faso, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Namibia, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa and Botswana as its country programmes, which is where this entry is placed; the fund's stated eligibility is any African country, so apply from elsewhere on the continent too.

trackers.name: Southern Africa Litigation Centre (SALC)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional litigation centre supporting and co-counselling cases across Angola, Botswana, DR Congo, Eswatini, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe. Its socio-economic rights work challenges large-scale agricultural and extractive land use that dispossesses customary landholders without adequate consent, consultation or compensation, and covers mining, pollution and climate justice — live matters include a Zambian community's pollution claim against copper processors and San and Bayei claims to ancestral land in Botswana. WHO IT SUITS: in-country lawyers and community organisations who need a partner with regional capacity and resources; SALC generally works through local counsel and partners rather than taking clients directly. SALC RESOURCES A LAWYER — IT DOES NOT REPLACE ONE. It provides technical and monetary support to local and regional lawyers and organisations litigating human rights and rule of law cases, working primarily through strategic litigation and capacity-strengthening support to lawyers and grassroots organisations. So the ask is not ‘please take my case’ but ‘please back my lawyer’ — come with a local lawyer or local organisation. It also trains human rights lawyers and facilitates networks across the region, so it is a route to finding counsel too. THE SECOND FORUM MOST PEOPLE MISS: SALC supports litigation in South African courts that advances human rights in the southern African region — so where your own courts are slow, captured or hostile, there may be another venue, and SALC is the body that supports using it. NAME THE RIGHT CLUSTER WHEN YOU APPROACH: its themes are criminal justice, civil and political rights, socio-economic rights, international criminal justice, business and human rights and equality rights — ‘environment’ is not one of them, so frame a land-defence case as business and human rights or socio-economic rights. Established 2005 in Johannesburg out of the International Bar Association and OSISA. It has also run open calls for small organisational development grants to emerging CBOs in Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe — periodic, so watch for them.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a pan-African feminist rapid-response fund with reach across all 54 African countries — small grants released quickly for unanticipated, time-critical situations rather than planned programme work, covering safety and protection needs when defenders are threatened and short windows for advocacy after an unexpected event. WHO IT SUITS: women's rights organisations, feminist collectives and movements in which women or gender-diverse people are the primary decision-makers. It does NOT fund individuals, and the action must be strategic, genuinely unanticipated, and completable in under three months. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is emergency money for a moment, not a budget for a campaign — decisions are fast and grants are modest.

trackers.name: Namibia e-Procurement
trackers.desc: Namibia's government e-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Namibia, and for how much.

trackers.name: NamibLII
trackers.desc: Namibia Legal Information Institute: free judgments and legislation. · Find here: free Namibian judgments and legislation (NamibLII / Laws.Africa).

trackers.name: Office of the Auditor-General
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Namibia, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Business and Intellectual Property Authority (BIPA)
trackers.desc: Namibia’s official registry of businesses and intellectual property — company incorporation and registration numbers.

trackers.name: BIPA Beneficial Ownership Register
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Namibia
trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Namibia — supreme court in Namibia (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: High Court of Namibia
trackers.desc: High Court of Namibia — supreme court in Namibia (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Communal conservancies — the community defines the area
trackers.desc: THE STRONGEST COMMUNITY LAND MODEL IN THIS MAP, AND THE REASONS ARE STRUCTURAL. A communal conservancy holds conditional rights to use the wildlife within a self-defined area, with fixed boundaries agreed with adjacent conservancies, communities or landowners — negotiated laterally with neighbours, not drawn by a ministry and handed down. It is a self-governing, democratic entity run by members through an elected committee, and it is recognised by the ministry but not governed by it: MEFT facilitates registration and monitors compliance, and may de-register a non-complying conservancy, but does not run it. AND IT REVERSED A CRIMINAL STATUS: before independence, residents on communal land who hunted game were treated as poachers; as legal entities with wildlife utilisation plans, conservancies were allowed to hunt under quotas based on annual game counts carried out by the ministry and the conservancies together. TO ESTABLISH ONE: an elected committee meets the requirements set under the 1996 amendment of the 1975 Nature Conservation Ordinance, then the Minister declares it in the Government Gazette. Obligations: wildlife management plans, annual general meetings and financial reports. SCALE: from 4 gazetted in 1998 to 86 conservancies and 43 community forests over 180,083 km² — community conservation areas now cover 20 percent of Namibia.

trackers.name: CCFN — a conservation fund that pays your legal costs
trackers.desc: THE WINDOW ALMOST NOTHING ELSE IN THIS MAP OFFERS. Alongside Minimum Support Packages and Payments for Ecosystem Services, CCFN provides financial aid to communities to meet their legal costs in pursuing their contract liberties and realising their benefits from contracts relating to their rights over their natural resources — expressly for conservancies that have been disadvantaged and/or shortchanged in contractual or other legally recognised arrangements. A conservation fund paying a community's legal fees to enforce a bad joint-venture contract is rare anywhere. Separate application forms exist for Conservancy Grants and JV Grants; check the Project Guidelines under Resources. There is also a human-wildlife conflict window — Germany through KfW announced a N$72.5 million HWC grant for communal conservancies, with the 43 worst-affected registered conservancies qualifying plus the Kyaramacan Association in Bwabwata National Park. LONG-TERM: ‘Namibia for Life’ secured N$1 billion in long-term financing with CCFN, NACSO, WWF and Enduring Earth. BUT KNOW THE TRANSITION: the movement is described as moving from a largely donor-funded development phase to a longer-term maintenance phase, with conservancy numbers expected to plateau around 90–100 — so new registrations are nearing a ceiling and the money is shifting toward sustaining what exists.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Environmental Clearance Certificate portal — an appeal costs N$1,000, more than three applications, and only registered parties may comment
trackers.desc: TWO NUMBERS DECIDE WHETHER ORDINARY PEOPLE USE THIS SYSTEM. AN APPLICATION FOR A CLEARANCE CERTIFICATE COSTS N$300; AN APPEAL COSTS N$1,000. Objecting is priced higher than applying, and the same N$1,000 applies to a transfer of certificate. Fees are not payable online: they must be paid by affixing a revenue stamp or a revenue franking impression to the document, so budget the trip as well as the money. THE SECOND GATE IS REGISTRATION, AND IT CLOSES QUIETLY: under the assessment regulations only a registered interested and affected party is entitled to comment in writing on submissions made to the Environmental Commissioner. Registering on a project's register is not a formality you do when you have something to say — it is the thing that gives you standing to say it, and it has to be done while the consultation is open. WHAT THE PORTAL ACTUALLY OFFERS, WHICH IS MORE THAN MOST IN THE REGION: online registration and application with status tracking against your email address; a Report Environmental Noncompliance form that lets you attach a photograph and lets you withhold your own details unless you want to be contacted; a screening questionnaire that tells you whether a project needs an assessment at all; a list of activities that may not be undertaken without a certificate; and a plain-language guide to the environment Act that carries section numbers so you can find the provision itself. There is also a Public Comments on new Projects list with a validity date against each project — that list rendered empty when this entry was written, so check it in a browser rather than assuming nothing is open. CAVEATS: the Commissioner is required to acknowledge an application within three days and to notify a decision within seven days of finalising review, and an appeal lies to the Minister — those timings and the registration rule were read from the assessment regulations and from a legal-alliance summary of them, not from this portal, which publishes fees and FAQs rather than deadlines. Note also that whether a public hearing happens at all is discretionary.

trackers.name: NACSO — how a Namibian community becomes a registered conservancy or community forest, which is the strongest community land right in this region
trackers.desc: WHERE THE RIGHT COMES FROM: Namibia wrote environmental protection into its constitution after independence and then, by legislation in the mid-1990s, established the right of people on communal land to organise themselves as conservancies and benefit directly from managing the natural resources there. The first conservancies were registered in 1998 and the first community forests in 2006. This is devolution to the community itself — not, as in Zimbabwe, to the district council — and it is why Namibia is usually described as Africa's leading case of devolved rights and responsibilities. WHAT EXISTS NOW: by the end of 2017 there were 83 registered communal conservancies and 32 registered community forests, plus one community association inside a national park, covering 166,267 km²; the count has since grown to around 87 conservancies with more communities electing to self-organise. Over seven million hectares of communal land are managed as conservancies. WHO TO ENLIST AND WHAT TO ASK: the environment ministry facilitates registration and monitors compliance; NACSO is the umbrella of the support organisations that help communities through it — technical assistance, governance support, the annual game counts, monitoring, and policy advocacy. Ask them what your area would have to do to register, because a registered conservancy is a legally recognised entity with rights to manage the resources in its defined jurisdiction, which is a far better position from which to refuse a project than being residents with no standing. Income comes from tourism, conservation hunting, meat and crafts, and a national fund has been established to move conservancies off donor dependence. In October 2024 a National Communal Conservancies and Community Forest Alliance was launched as the umbrella body representing conservancies and community forests at national policy level. WHO IT SUITS: communal-area communities in Namibia that want legal standing over their land and resources before a project arrives. CAVEATS: registration is a process with the ministry, not a purchase, and it takes time and organisation; conservancy income depends on tourism and hunting markets; and NACSO is a support and coordination association, not a legal service — for an objection to a specific project, Namibia's environmental clearance portal entry is the route.

trackers.name: Shack Dwellers Federation of Namibia and NHAG — a community-managed revolving fund that lends to its own savings groups, and has secured land for thousands of families
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY AND BUY LAND: the Shack Dwellers Federation of Namibia (SDFN), founded in October 1998 by around 30 grassroots housing groups active since the late eighties, a national network of housing savings schemes open to people who are unemployed or earn less than about N$5,000 a month; and the Namibia Housing Action Group (NHAG) Trust, established 1992 as its support organisation. THE INSTRUMENT: in 1996 communities established the Twahangana Fund, a COMMUNITY-MANAGED REVOLVING development fund that lends to the savings groups themselves — members' savings combined with government and international contributions. Each saving group manages its own savings and holds its own bank account. Community savings have been used to secure land and to leverage additional government contributions. WHY IT EXISTS IN THOSE TERMS: the federation's own account is that 89 per cent of Namibians do not qualify for conventional home loans and cannot access commercial housing — so the savings group is not a supplement to the mortgage market, it is the replacement for it. REPORTED SCALE, AND THE FIGURES VARY BY SOURCE AND DATE: from 605 schemes with 20,400 members, land secured for roughly 6,230 families and 3,488 houses built, up to over 1,000 saving groups, 30,000–33,000 members, savings above N$34 million, and 7,000–7,700 brick houses, each with its own toilet and water connection. About two-thirds of members are women, and the negotiation with authorities has been driven mainly by women. A member's account of the route is exact: save small amounts regularly, then buy a plot, then build. Town councils have partnered with NHAG to open land for low-income buyers. WHO IT SUITS: Namibians in shacks, rented rooms or without accommodation who cannot borrow commercially, and groups wanting to buy land collectively rather than individually. CAVEATS: this is slow and incremental — members describe consolidation of the erven delaying construction for years — and Namibia's housing backlog is reported above 300,000 against this output. It secures and develops land for members; it is not a defence against a project, and for communal conservancy registration Namibia's NACSO entry is the route.

trackers.name: Legal Assistance Centre, Windhoek — a land and environment law project with a paralegal phone line and published walk-in hours
trackers.desc: WHO TO INSTRUCT: the Legal Assistance Centre (LAC), Namibia's public interest law organisation, whose Land, Environment and Development (LEAD) project covers inheritance, conservancies, ILLEGAL FENCING, environmental issues and issues affecting especially disadvantaged groups including the Himba and the San. HOW TO REACH IT, WHICH IT PUBLISHES PLAINLY: phone a paralegal on +264-61-22-3356, or come to the office at 4 Marien Ngouabi Street, Windhoek — open for basic advice Monday to Friday, 08h00–11h30 and 14h00–16h00, closing 15h00 on Fridays. THE FIGHT IT IS BUILT FOR, and the numbers explain why: about 39 per cent of Namibia's land area is communal, with the 2013/2014 agricultural census recording 169,984 agricultural households — 907,715 people — holding tenure rights in communal areas; and LAC's own analysis identifies ELITE LAND GRABBING in communal areas and ILLEGAL PRIVATE ENCLOSURES that reduce communal grazing and worsen overgrazing, at a time when traditional authorities' ability to enforce customary tenure has weakened. Illegal fencing is the quiet way communal land is taken — no permit, no notice, just posts — and this is the organisation that has litigated and published on it. It also trains Communal Land Boards in environmentally sound decision-making and conflict management, runs workshops for communities and for traditional leaders, police and officials on the Communal Land Reform Act and conservancy legislation, and comments publicly on live disputes including a mining conflict framed as a test of constitutional environmental rights. THE REGIONAL DOOR IT OPENS: LAC belongs to the Southern African Legal Assistance Network (SALAN), a network of legal aid and legal assistance NGOs spanning South Africa, Lesotho, Botswana, Mozambique, Malawi, Zambia, Zimbabwe and Tanzania — so a community in any of those countries can ask LAC who its national equivalent is. WHO IT SUITS: Namibians facing illegal fencing, communal land allocation disputes, inheritance problems or environmental harm — and southern African communities looking for the nearest legal aid organisation. CAVEATS: a public interest law organisation with finite capacity, and it notes shrinking resources for civil society; the walk-in service is basic advice, not automatic representation. For conservancy registration, Namibia's NACSO entry; for savings-based land purchase, the Shack Dwellers Federation.

trackers.name: Namibian Chamber of Environment and the Namibia Nature Foundation — 63 member NGOs whose council is the members themselves, grants with no overhead deduction, and a foundation that will hold and administer funds for a community
trackers.desc: THE CHAMBER, THE ZERO-OVERHEAD GRANTS AND THE TRUST: the NAMIBIAN CHAMBER OF ENVIRONMENT (NCE, n-c-e.org), A MEMBERSHIP-BASED AND MEMBER-DRIVEN UMBRELLA ORGANISATION ESTABLISHED AS A VOLUNTARY ASSOCIATION UNDER NAMIBIAN COMMON LAW, currently holds 63 FULL MEMBERS — NAMIBIAN REGISTERED NGOs whose main business is environmental matters in Namibia — AND 13 ASSOCIATE MEMBERS. ITS GOVERNANCE IS THE POINT: THE MEMBERS CONSTITUTE THE COUNCIL, WHICH IS THE HIGHEST DECISION-MAKING ORGAN, AND THE COUNCIL ELECTS THE EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE AT AN AGM. An umbrella where the members ARE the governing body cannot be steered over their heads. If your organisation joins, you get a vote in the chamber, not just a newsletter. AND THE MONEY ARRANGEMENT IS UNUSUAL ENOUGH TO COPY: CORE FUNDING FOR THE NCE IS PROVIDED BY A SINGLE CORPORATE DONOR, WHICH MEANS ALL ADDITIONAL FUNDING RECEIVED IS INVESTED DIRECTLY INTO ENVIRONMENTAL PROJECTS AND PROGRAMMES — THERE ARE NO OVERHEAD COSTS — AND THE NCE DELIBERATELY FOCUSES ON CORPORATE SUPPORT AND AVOIDS TARGETING FUNDING SOURCES THAT MAY COMPETE WITH ITS MEMBERS. A grant-maker whose overheads are already paid passes on every kwacha it raises, and one that refuses to chase its own members' donors is not a rival. Ask what it funds: emphasis is placed on LEGACY INITIATIVES WITH TANGIBLE OUTCOMES. Its secretariat is two people, only one full-time — so approach with a specific, finished proposal. ITS MEMBERS, published with descriptions, include a nature trust established to manage and conserve the land hosting a named lodge, a conservancy association whose stated purpose is TO REPRESENT AS MANY PROPERLY ESTABLISHED CONSERVANCIES AS POSSIBLE AND ACT AS THEIR COORDINATING BODY, a desert lion research project, DEVELOPMENT WORKSHOP NAMIBIA on informal settlements and disadvantaged communities, and the NAMIBIAN ENVIRONMENT AND WILDLIFE SOCIETY, an NCE founding member whose potential partners are ALL ORGANISATIONS IN NAMIBIA with conservation, environmental research or environmental education as their main aim. A nature trust formed to hold the land under a lodge is a template: a private landholding placed inside a non-profit that exists to conserve it. THE FOUNDATION THAT WILL HOLD YOUR MONEY: THE NAMIBIA NATURE FOUNDATION (NNF, nnf.org.na), 76-78 Frans Indongo Street, WINDHOEK, FOUNDED 1987 AND REGISTERED UNDER A DEED OF TRUST WITH THE MASTER OF THE NAMIBIAN HIGH COURT, one of Namibia's oldest and largest homegrown environmental organisations and an IUCN member since 1991, whose stated objects include RAISING FUNDS FOR CONSERVATION AND ENVIRONMENTAL INITIATIVES AND ADMINISTERING AND MANAGING FUNDS FOR PARTNERS, DONORS, PRIVATE SECTOR, GOVERNMENT, COMMUNITIES AND PROJECT IMPLEMENTERS. A registered trust that will administer funds on a community's behalf solves the problem that stops most village groups being funded at all — no bank account, no audit history. And one partner records that through NNF's technical support their team MANAGED TO ESTABLISH A FULLY REGISTERED NGO. Ask NNF for that support before asking anyone for money. WHO IT SUITS: Namibian community groups needing registration, a fiscal host, a grant or an umbrella. CAVEATS: SMALL SECRETARIATS; NCE core funding comes from a mining company — know that before you approach. For how a community becomes a registered conservancy, Namibia's NACSO entry; for land bought through community savings, the Shack Dwellers Federation and NHAG entry; for the land and environment lawyers, the Legal Assistance Centre entry; for the appeal against a clearance certificate, the ECC portal entry.

trackers.name: IRDNC — forty years of Namibian community conservation that trains and employs villagers as rangers — and the four-country KAZA consortium roster with a law centre inside it
trackers.desc: RANGERS HIRED FROM THE VILLAGE, AND A LAW CENTRE IN THE CONSORTIUM: INTEGRATED RURAL DEVELOPMENT AND NATURE CONSERVATION (IRDNC, irdnc.org.na) IS A NAMIBIAN NGO WITH MORE THAN 40 YEARS OF EXPERIENCE IN SUSTAINABLE NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT AND COMMUNITY-DRIVEN CONSERVATION, based at WINDHOEK WEST, WINDHOEK. ITS METHOD IS THE POINT: BY TRAINING AND EMPLOYING LOCAL COMMUNITY MEMBERS AS RANGERS, IT PROTECTS DESERT-ADAPTED ELEPHANTS, LIONS AND BLACK RHINOS WHILE SAFEGUARDING LIVELIHOODS AND STRENGTHENING LONG-TERM COEXISTENCE BETWEEN PEOPLE AND WILDLIFE, working to reduce human-wildlife conflict in the north-west. Forty years, and the ranger is a person from the village on a wage. That is the difference between a conservation project and a local institution: the salary stays in the community and the knowledge does not leave when the funder does. If an organisation proposes protection on your land, ask how many of the posts will be filled locally and at what pay — IRDNC is the Namibian precedent for the answer being all of them. THE ROSTER THAT MATTERS MOST, BECAUSE IT NAMES WHO TO APPROACH IN FOUR COUNTRIES FOR ONE LANDSCAPE: the consortium partners for a sustainable wildlife management programme in the KAVANGO-ZAMBEZI TRANSFRONTIER CONSERVATION AREA — THE WORLD'S LARGEST — ARE THE ASSOCIATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL CONSERVATION AND INTEGRATED RURAL DEVELOPMENT (ACADIR) IN ANGOLA; ECOEXIST IN BOTSWANA; IRDNC; THE KAZA SECRETARIAT; THE LEGAL ASSISTANCE CENTRE; THE NACSO NATURAL RESOURCE WORKING GROUP; THE NAMIBIA NATURE FOUNDATION; THE NAMIBIA DEVELOPMENT TRUST; SAVE THE RHINO TRUST; TRAFFIC; AND WWF ZAMBIA AND WWF ZIMBABWE. A LEGAL ASSISTANCE CENTRE sitting inside a wildlife consortium is the detail to take away. It means the legal capacity is already at the table with the conservation bodies, so a community inside KAZA does not have to find a lawyer separately — ask the consortium which partner handles the land and rights questions, and note that the answer is a named public interest law firm. And a transfrontier consortium means an Angolan, Botswanan, Namibian, Zambian or Zimbabwean community facing the same landscape has counterparts named in the same document. ACADIR in Angola is a body this file's Angolan record does not otherwise hold — an association combining environmental conservation AND integrated rural development is exactly the pairing a southern Angolan village needs. THE PROGRAMME'S OWN OBJECT IS WORTH QUOTING BACK: TO RECONCILE THE CHALLENGES OF WILDLIFE CONSERVATION WITH THOSE OF FOOD SECURITY, PROMOTING SUSTAINABLE AND LEGAL USE OF RESILIENT ANIMAL POPULATIONS BY INDIGENOUS RURAL POPULATIONS, WHILE INCREASING AND DIVERSIFYING THE PROTEIN SUPPLY. Food security and protein supply written into a conservation programme's object is the counter to the argument that protection means going hungry. Cite it. THE SCALE AND WHERE THE MONEY GOES, ON THE RECORD: a global environment facility grant of USD 7.1 MILLION FORMED PART OF A TOTAL OF USD 32.43 MILLION for scaling up community-based ecosystem management, covering a conservancy network then numbering 29 REGISTERED CONSERVANCIES WITH 150,000 RESIDENTS ACROSS 75,000 SQUARE KILOMETRES — and an earlier USD 26.5 MILLION in donor support went to the same programme, under which LOCAL COMMUNITIES WERE GRANTED RIGHTS TO MANAGE THE LAND AND REAP THE BENEFITS FROM TOURISM, WITH ANY INCOME GENERATED PAID OUT DIRECTLY TO INDIVIDUAL MEMBERS OF CONSERVANCIES OR POOLED TO PAY FOR NECESSITIES LIKE WATER TANKS, WIND PUMPS AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF LOCAL INFRASTRUCTURE. Paid out directly to individual members, OR pooled for water tanks and wind pumps — and the conservancy chooses which. That is the clause to write into your own constitution before the first revenue arrives, because the argument about how income is split is the one that breaks community bodies. Decide it while there is still nothing to divide. The programme's activities are also named: COMMUNITY-BASED TOURISM FACILITIES INCLUDING JOINT VENTURES WITH THE PRIVATE SECTOR, TROPHY HUNTING, GAME MEAT PRODUCTION, THE COMMERCIALISATION OF INDIGENOUS PLANTS AND CRAFT PRODUCTION. Commercialisation of indigenous plants is the quiet earner on that list, and the one least likely to divide a community. WHO IT SUITS: Namibian communal communities, anyone inside the KAZA landscape in five countries, and conservancies deciding how to split income. CAVEATS: TROPHY HUNTING IS PART OF THIS MODEL and communities differ sharply on it — decide before you join a programme built around it. For how a community becomes a registered conservancy or community forest, Namibia's NACSO entry; for 63 member NGOs governing the council themselves with no overhead on grants, the Namibian Chamber of Environment and NNF entry; for a land and environment law project, the Legal Assistance Centre entry; for a community-managed revolving fund, the Shack Dwellers Federation entry.

trackers.name: Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a regional environmental endowment established in 2012, managing an endowment plus a sinking fund for Ecosystem-based Adaptation, which it disburses mainly through partner National Conservation Trust Funds rather than directly — it helped establish several of them, including the Dominica, Grenada, Jamaica, St Kitts & Nevis, St Lucia and St Vincent funds. Its EbA window runs open calls for proposals. WHO IT SUITS: organisations doing on-the-ground ecosystem work that reduces climate vulnerability. Check whether your country has a national trust fund first — that is usually the door, and the CBF itself is the wholesaler behind it. HOW IT DIFFERS: endowment income committed for the long term, so it funds sustained protected-area management rather than a campaign. APPLY TO YOUR NATIONAL FUND, NOT TO CBF — for most of the money. CBF is a regional umbrella: at national level the partner National Conservation Trust Funds (NCTFs) lead the grantmaking process, with endowment proceeds held in country-based subaccounts and channelled through them. So for the Conservation Finance stream, the regional body is the wrong door — find your NCTF. THE EXCEPTION IS THE EbA FACILITY, which awards through competitive calls for proposals and is a direct route. THE NUMBERS: EbA medium grants USD 250,000–1 million, large grants up to USD 2 million — large by the standards of most funds here, and not aimed at a small unincorporated group acting alone. Eligible recipients expressly include NCTFs, NGOs, community-based organisations, government agencies, universities and the private sector. SCOPE CHECK: the EbA Facility covers the marine and coastal zone of the insular Caribbean, so an inland project must show its connection to marine and coastal ecosystems. IF YOU ARE TOO SMALL FOR EbA: CBF partners with GEF SGP across 12 shared countries — that is the sibling route for community-scale grants, and it is recorded separately in this map. Endowment disbursements go to NCTFs that have signed agreements with CBF, the first in 2016 with Fondo MARENA in the Dominican Republic.

trackers.name: Cour supérieure des comptes et du contentieux administratif (Haïti)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Haiti — audits government accounts and the use of public money.

trackers.name: Haiti — Ministère du Commerce et de l’Industrie (Guichet MCI)
trackers.desc: National corporate registry; the Ministry of Commerce & Industry registers businesses — via the online Guichet MCI platform (launched 2024) issuing a secure certificate, with company-name antecedent search & application tracking, Haiti. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Haiti — Ministère de l’Économie et des Finances (MEF)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; coordinates preparation & execution of the general State budget and manages the treasury, Haiti. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Haiti.

trackers.name: Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund (CEPF)
trackers.desc: A FUND WHOSE SMALL-GRANT APPLICATION IS A SINGLE LETTER. CEPF (founded 2000; a joint initiative of the French Development Agency, Conservation International, the EU, the GEF, the Government of Japan, the MacArthur Foundation and the World Bank) has funded more than 2,500 grantees. FOR SMALL GRANTS THE LETTER OF INQUIRY IS THE ENTIRE APPLICATION — no longer project proposal is required — reviewed by the hotspot's Regional Implementation Team, with an offline template provided in the call's languages. Large grants go through the ConservationGrants portal and only then invite a full proposal. Reported averages: small grants around US$15,000, large around US$150,000; the small/large threshold varies by call (US$20,000 and US$50,000 both recorded), so read it. TIMING: calls run 6–8 weeks and notification comes several months after closing — but CEPF stops accepting letters once the designated funds are committed, so an open call can close early. WHO IS DISQUALIFIED: individuals cannot apply — you need a legally registered organisation with its own bank account — and government cannot apply. Community groups, farmers' cooperatives, Indigenous Peoples' organisations and women's groups all can, and CEPF welcomes first-time applicants. TWO RULES THAT SINK GOOD APPLICATIONS: your letter must aim at one single strategic direction; and site-based directions are geographically bound — community management work must be in a listed priority KBA, corridor work in a named corridor, while civil-society strengthening can be anywhere in the hotspot. THE STEP MOST PEOPLE SKIP: CEPF encourages you to contact RIT staff to discuss the idea before submitting — free, and the cheapest way to learn whether it fits.

trackers.name: ANAP — it approves plans AND must follow their implementation
trackers.desc: A THREE-PART DUTY WORTH SEPARATING OUT. The Agence Nationale des Aires Protégées was created by the décret-cadre published in Le Moniteur, 26 January 2006, its mission drawn from article 54: protect biodiversity and manage the Système National des Aires Protégées. The decree requires it to elaborate and approve the plans d'aménagement for protected areas in its jurisdiction and follow their implementation — so a plan that exists but is not being followed engages the same body that approved it. Other statutory functions: coordinating preparation and implementation of the national protected areas management plan, and protecting biodiversity in situ and ex situ. THE ENFORCEMENT ARM: the Brigade de Sécurité des Aires Protégées (BSAP) is an operational direction of ANAP for environmental surveillance of protected area units and ecological sites, and also provides support to control bodies — the named body if your issue is unlawful activity inside a protected area. THE DEFINITION IS BROAD: a protected area is any zone delimited, regulated OR managed for conservation of biodiversity and associated natural and cultural resources — regulation alone can suffice. FOR A SMALL SITE, CATEGORY III (monument ou élément naturel) covers a topographic feature, a mountain, an underwater cavern, a grotte, or even a living element such as an ancient wooded islet, and these are generally quite small areas. ANAP became a Direction Générale by presidential arrêté of 10 May 2017.

trackers.name: The capacity gap is documented — and so is the shared-responsibility principle
trackers.desc: PLAN FOR THE MINISTRY NOT ACTING UNAIDED. A USAID-commissioned Biodiversity and Tropical Forest Assessment records that responsibilities at the heart of the MDE's mandate as set forth in the decree are generally not addressed by the MDE due to a lack of resources — with delineation of national parks among the functions listed. A statutory duty undischarged for want of resources is still a statutory duty, and that assessment is a citable source for the gap — but a campaign depending on unaided ministry action is likely to stall. Note too that before 2012 ANAP was a technical direction barely operational. THE OPENING FOR PARTICIPATION IS IN THE SYSTEM'S OWN FOUNDING PRINCIPLE: the National Environmental Management System proceeds from collective responsibility, to be shared between sectoral ministries and between the Government and citizens. WHERE A DEVELOPMENT CROSSES SECTORS: the Comité Interministériel d'Aménagement du Territoire (CIAT), led by an Executive Secretariat and composed of the Ministries of Planning, Agriculture, Environment, Public Works and Interior, is where those ministries sit together. CONTEXT: protection efforts date from 1926; the SNAP and ANAP were created in 2006; post-earthquake the PSDH treats biodiversity as a pillar through the Programme pour la Protection de l'Environnement and the Programme de Gestion des Bassins Versants. Parc national La Visite covers 30 km².

trackers.name: Haiti's communal section councils and assemblies elected by universal suffrage, the municipal assembly that oversees the mayor's spending, and the three national federations including the mayors' body brokering foreign town-hall cooperation
trackers.desc: THE SMALLEST TERRITORIAL AUTHORITY IN THE COUNTRY IS ELECTED BY UNIVERSAL SUFFRAGE, AND IT IS THE ONE CLOSEST TO RURAL LAND. Communal sections are THE SMALLEST EXISTING TERRITORIAL ENTITIES AND ARE ADMINISTERED BY THREE MEMBERS ELECTED BY UNIVERSAL SUFFRAGE FOR FOUR YEARS who form the communal section administrative council, assisted by an ASSEMBLY OF THE COMMUNAL SECTION whose members receive no salary but a fee per QUARTERLY MEETING, an incentive to hold that quarterly meeting of the council with the assembly. The assembly is described as A LINK BETWEEN THE POPULATION AND THE DIFFERENT STRUCTURES OF LOCAL GOVERNANCE which, BEING CLOSE TO THE REALITIES OF THE GROUND, HELPS IDENTIFY THE PRIORITIES OF THE COMMUNITY AND FAVOURS CONCERTATION BETWEEN THE CITIZENS, THE LOCAL ORGANISATIONS AND THE AUTHORITIES CONCERNED. Three elected people and an assembly that meets quarterly, in your own rural section. Getting a project onto that quarterly agenda is the first formal step available, and local organisations are named as parties to the concertation. HOW THE PYRAMID CONNECTS UPWARD: the municipal council is required to have the support of a municipal assembly MADE UP OF REPRESENTATIVES FROM THE COMMUNAL SECTIONS; DECISIONS MADE BY THE section councils MUST BE APPROVED BY THE section assemblies; each section elects a representative to the municipal assembly, and that assembly OVERSEES THE MAYOR'S USE OF RESOURCES. There are 146 COMMUNES and ten departments subdivided into 42 ARRONDISSEMENTS. The body that oversees the mayor's spending is built from your section's own representative. If the town hall is backing a project, the municipal assembly is where that can be questioned by someone your section elected. THE THREE FEDERATIONS THAT SPEAK NATIONALLY: THREE NATIONAL FEDERATIONS DEFEND THE INTERESTS OF THE TERRITORIAL COLLECTIVITIES — the federation of commune mayors, CURRENTLY THE MOST ACTIVE, the federation of communal section administrative councils, and the federation of communal section assemblies. The mayors' federation states its aims as promoting ACCOUNTABILITY AND GOOD LOCAL GOVERNANCE, strengthening cooperation between town halls and their departmental associations, and acting for DECENTRALISATION AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT, with work including TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND DECENTRALISED COOPERATION BETWEEN HAITIAN AND FOREIGN TOWN HALLS and post-disaster support. Decentralised cooperation between Haitian and foreign town halls is a real funding channel. A twinned foreign municipality can pay for work your own commune cannot, and the federation is where those links are brokered. THE HONEST STATE OF THESE BODIES: a national forum of the section assemblies has been convened by the interior ministry with section council members and city delegates present; but analysts record that in some sections the council DOES NOT EVEN HAVE AN OFFICE, LET ALONE STAFF WHO COULD ENSURE THE FOLLOW-UP OF A FILE OR KEEP THE INSTITUTIONAL MEMORY when members change at elections, with small monthly operating funds; the departmental level IS NOT FUNCTIONAL AS THE CONSTITUTION PROVIDES, the ten departments operating as administrative deconcentration instead; and five of the 146 communes were not yet effectively in place. Assume no institutional memory. Give the section council a written file it can keep, with copies to the assembly and the federation, because the people who receive it may not be there next year. WHAT THE MONEY LOOKS LIKE: transfers to territorial collectivities are fixed annually in the budget, and in one year 87% WERE ALLOCATED TO THE FUNCTIONING OF THE TOWN HALLS, THE COMMUNAL SECTION COUNCILS AND THE COMMUNAL SECTION ASSEMBLIES, the remainder to unspecified projects in those collectivities. Nearly all the transfer pays salaries and running costs, so do not expect the section council to fund anything. Ask it for standing, minutes and a resolution instead — those cost nothing and are what outside funders and courts look for.

trackers.name: FLACMA - the Latin American federation of cities and municipal associations, open to affiliation by ANY INDIVIDUAL MUNICIPALITY, whose assembly passes resolutions signed by mayors across eighteen countries
trackers.desc: ANY CITY OR MUNICIPALITY IN THE REGION MAY AFFILIATE DIRECTLY, NOT ONLY THROUGH ITS NATIONAL ASSOCIATION. Its membership rule is that MEMBERS ARE ALL THE CITIES, MUNICIPALITIES, NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND MUNICIPALIST INSTITUTIONS OF LATIN AMERICA THAT HAVE EXPRESSED THEIR WILL TO AFFILIATE; it is AN ORGANISATION OF FREE ADHESION THAT REPRESENTS THE 16,132 MUNICIPALITIES, INTENDANCIES AND PREFECTURES, THE CITIES AND THE ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, NETWORKS AND GUILDS OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, and it is the regional section of the world organisation of local governments. A single municipality may join in its own right. Where your national association is captured or inactive, that is a way for one sympathetic town hall to reach the regional table on its own. WHOSE PRESIDENTS SIT ON IT: its published leadership is drawn from the presidents of the national municipal bodies of the region — the federation of municipalities of one southern country, the association of municipalities of another, the Brazilian association of municipalities, the congress of intendants of another, the national federation of municipalities of one large federal country and the association of municipalities of an Andean one — each of them a serving mayor. The people who chair your own national municipal association sit here. A matter raised through that association can be carried into a regional assembly by the same person. WHAT IT SAYS IT IS FOR: TO BE THE VOICE OF LATIN AMERICAN MUNICIPALISM, TO CONSOLIDATE THE LATIN AMERICAN MUNICIPAL ASSOCIATIVE MOVEMENT, TO REPRESENT AND SERVE AS INTERLOCUTOR OF ALL THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND THEIR NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES, and TO PROMOTE IN LATIN AMERICA AUTONOMOUS, STRONG AND DEMOCRATIC LOCAL GOVERNMENTS; it ADHERES TO AND PROMOTES THE WORLD AND REGIONAL CONVENTIONS THAT THE NATIONAL STATES OF THE REGION SUBSCRIBE. Promoting the conventions the states have signed is written into its purpose. Where your country has signed an environmental or rights convention and a municipality is being told to ignore it, that is a body with a standing commitment to the opposite. THE PRECEDENT THAT SHOWS IT TAKES POSITIONS: its general assembly has approved unanimously a declaration on a territorial sovereignty dispute, signed by the president and BY MUNICIPAL AUTHORITIES AND HEADS OF ASSOCIATIONS AND FEDERATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES of eighteen named countries of the region, which also REAFFIRMED THE LEGITIMATE RIGHTS... OVER THE NATURAL RESOURCES OF THE AREA IN QUESTION. The assembly passes resolutions that name natural resources and get signed by mayors across eighteen countries. A community campaign that can be framed as a municipal cause has a forum that has done exactly that before. THE OTHER REGIONAL NETWORKS BESIDE IT: regional analysis names, among the principal associations and networks of local and regional governments with EXPERIENCES, IDEAS AND RESOURCES TO FOSTER INITIATIVES AND PROJECTS LINKED TO SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AT LOCAL LEVEL, a network of Mercosur cities alongside this federation, and global initiatives with regional presence for local sustainability and for city climate action; various cities have prepared VOLUNTARY LOCAL REPORTS on implementing the global development agenda in their territories. A voluntary local report is a document a municipality writes about itself. Getting your community's situation named in one is cheap, public and lasting. THE HONEST NOTE ON REPRESENTATION: the region's representation in the world body has been the subject of negotiations between this federation, the Mercosur cities network and the world organisation to form A LATIN AMERICAN REPRESENTATION THAT IS PLURAL, DIVERSE AND PARTICIPATORY. More than one body claims to speak for the region's municipalities. Approach both this federation and the Mercosur cities network rather than assuming one covers the other.

trackers.name: ICLEI - a sustainability network open to individual councils AND to associations of local governments, giving fee-paying members year-round telephone and email support on designing environment and water projects, plus local biodiversity planning tools and an environmental award
trackers.desc: MEMBERSHIP OF THIS GLOBAL SUSTAINABILITY NETWORK IS OPEN TO ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AS WELL AS TO INDIVIDUAL COUNCILS, AND THE FEE SCALES WITH POPULATION AND NATIONAL INCOME. Its membership page states that AFFILIATION IS OPEN TO ALL LOCAL AND REGIONAL GOVERNMENTS, AS WELL AS TO THEIR WORLD, REGIONAL, NATIONAL AND SUBNATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS, that members MAY VOTE AND PARTICIPATE IN THE GOVERNING ORGANS OF THE WHOLE NETWORK, and that they CONTRIBUTE AN ANNUAL AFFILIATION FEE THAT VARIES REGIONALLY AND ACCORDING TO POPULATION AND GROSS NATIONAL INCOME PER CAPITA. A small municipality pays a small fee and votes in the same network as a capital city. Where a national association is the member, ask whether your council is covered by it already. WHAT A MEMBER ACTUALLY GETS, IN THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT'S OWN WORDS: it SUPPORTS ITS PARTNERS TO FIND SUSTAINABLE SOLUTIONS THROUGH PROJECTS, INITIATIVES AND PROGRAMMES, offers cities and states A PLATFORM TO INTERACT WITH OTHER LOCAL GOVERNMENTS and provides RESOURCES AND TOOLS TO PROMOTE POSITIVE ENVIRONMENTAL, ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL CHANGES; support runs DURING THE YEAR THAT THE FEE LASTS, PERMANENTLY, BY TELEPHONE OR BY EMAIL, and covers THE DESIGN OF PROGRAMMES AND PROJECTS OF SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN THEMES SUCH AS: ENVIRONMENT, WATER, PUBLIC SERVICES, ENERGY EFFICIENCY, SOLID WASTE. Joining requires A REQUEST TO THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT addressed to the named regional secretary, plus a membership form. Permanent telephone and email support on designing water and environment projects, for one annual fee. That is a standing technical helpline for a town hall that has none. THE BIODIVERSITY WORK THAT MATTERS FOR LAND: its recorded local biodiversity work is TO PROMOTE THE BIODIVERSITY STRATEGIES OF THE STATE AND MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENTS, AS WELL AS THEIR ACTION PLANS, AND ALSO TO REINFORCE THE CAPACITIES OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS TO INCORPORATE BIODIVERSITY INTO THE PLANNING PROCESSES, and it notes that MORE MONETARY RESOURCES ARE INVESTED GLOBALLY IN BIODIVERSITY AT LOCAL AND SUBNATIONAL LEVEL THAN AT NATIONAL LEVELS; a member municipality has launched an urban biodiversity index, and a global initiative on NATURE IN URBAN PLANNING is promoted through the network. Incorporating biodiversity into planning processes is the exact point at which a project is stopped or waved through. Ask the secretariat which of its tools your municipality can adopt in its next plan revision. THE RECOGNITION THAT GIVES A COUNCIL A REASON: the regional secretariat runs an award for local governments THAT HAVE CARRIED OUT ACTIONS IN FAVOUR OF THE PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT IN THEMES OF CLIMATE CHANGE, BIODIVERSITY, ENERGY EFFICIENCY, MOBILITY, AMONG OTHERS, open to municipalities, city boroughs and federal entities. An award with a biodiversity category. A council weighing whether to protect a site has a public reason to do so, and the application is a deadline you can work to. THE OFFICES THAT COVER THIS REGION: there is a secretariat for one large federal country together with Central America and the Caribbean, and a separate South American secretariat, each publishing member lists that include municipalities of several countries. Two regional offices cover the whole file. Write to the one for your subregion rather than to the global body.

trackers.name: Fundación DEMUCA - a foundation for strengthening local governments across Central America and the Caribbean, working through the national municipal associations, with a work line covering ENVIRONMENTAL AND RISK MANAGEMENT and cohorts of twenty municipalities
trackers.desc: A FOUNDATION EXISTS WHOSE WHOLE PURPOSE IS STRENGTHENING LOCAL GOVERNMENTS IN CENTRAL AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, AND IT WORKS THROUGH THE NATIONAL MUNICIPAL ASSOCIATIONS. It is described as AN INSTRUMENT OF TECHNICAL AND FINANCIAL COOPERATION of a national development agency THAT PROMOTES THE STRENGTHENING OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS IN CENTRAL AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, its work focused on THE DESIGN OF STRATEGIES AND THE EXECUTION OF NATIONAL AND REGIONAL PROJECTS AIMED AT IMPROVING THE MANAGEMENT CAPABILITIES OF MUNICIPALITIES AND THEIR VARIOUS FORMS OF ASSOCIATION; it SUPPORTS THE NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES IN THE GENERATION OF STRATEGIC POLICY PROPOSALS and COLLABORATES IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPROVEMENT OF THE MEANS AND INSTRUMENTS OF ADMINISTRATION OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS. It is a foundation constituted under the law of one member country in 1995, with a delegation registered in the cooperating country. Where a national municipal association is weak, this is the body that funds and staffs its policy work. Ask your association what it currently receives, and whether your municipality is in the next cohort. THE THREE WORK LINES, ONE OF WHICH COVERS ENVIRONMENT: the cooperation is channelled through this foundation in three lines — TAX REFORM AT LOCAL LEVEL, TO STRENGTHEN THE FINANCIAL CAPACITY OF THE MUNICIPALITIES WITH THEIR OWN RESOURCES TO IMPLEMENT THEIR POLICIES; implementation of the municipal administrative career statute FOR THE STABILITY OF THE HUMAN RESOURCE AND OF THE MUNICIPAL PLANS; and STRENGTHENING OF CAPACITIES OF THE MUNICIPALITIES AND ASSOCIATIONS, TO PROMOTE MUNICIPAL ASSOCIATIVISM, LOCAL ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, POLICIES AND PLANS OF EQUALITY, ENVIRONMENTAL AND RISK MANAGEMENT, STRENGTHENING OF THE SOCIAL FABRIC AND THE PREVENTION OF VIOLENCE. Environmental and risk management sits inside the third line, alongside strengthening the social fabric. A request framed as municipal capacity on environmental management fits the existing programme rather than asking for something new. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DELIVERS, FROM RECORDED EXAMPLES: with a national municipalities corporation and a state municipal development institute it launched a second phase of implementation FOR 20 NEW MUNICIPALITIES AT NATIONAL LEVEL; TO WHICH TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE WILL BE GIVEN TO STRENGTHEN THEIR CAPACITIES through LABOUR TECHNIFICATION, PERMANENT TRAINING AND THE CREATION, DESIGN AND APPLICATION OF TOOLS AND INSTRUMENTS; it co-published a guide for the internal functioning of plural municipal councils; and it produced a model to improve municipal tax management, described by its own technician as A SIMPLE GUIDE DIRECTED TO STRENGTHENING MUNICIPAL AUTONOMY, WHICH CAN BE IMPLEMENTED WITHOUT HAVING EXTERNAL TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, piloted in ten named municipalities with external financing of twenty-seven thousand dollars. Twenty municipalities in one cohort, and a tax guide a town hall can apply on its own. Both are the kind of thing a small municipality can be nominated for without a budget of its own. THE REGIONAL BODY IT SITS BESIDE: the federation of municipalities of the Central American isthmus is one of the organisations from which the Latin American municipal federation was formed, and has appeared as a regional counterpart in municipal research and in Mesoamerican biological corridor work. Verify whether that federation is currently active before relying on it; the foundation above is the better documented door at present.

trackers.name: The GEF Small Grants Programme - grants of up to $50,000 DIRECT to community organisations, with a national coordinator in each country who helps write the concept paper, planning grants, and a companion window of up to $300,000
trackers.desc: THERE IS A NAMED NATIONAL COORDINATOR IN YOUR COUNTRY WHOSE JOB INCLUDES HELPING YOU WRITE THE APPLICATION. The programme's own procedure is that THE PROJECT PROPONENT — A NATIONAL CBO OR NGO — CONTACTS THE SGP NATIONAL COORDINATOR TO RECEIVE PROJECT APPLICATION GUIDELINES AND FORMS, and that WITH ASSISTANCE FROM THE NATIONAL COORDINATOR, THE PROPONENT PREPARES A BRIEF PROJECT CONCEPT PAPER; the coordinator pre-screens it, and if eligible the proponent prepares a full proposal — IN SOME CASES, THIS STEP MAY BE SUPPORTED BY A PLANNING GRANT — which goes to a national steering committee that accepts, rejects or returns it for further work. A planning grant to write the proposal, and an official whose job is to help you write it. Contact the coordinator before drafting anything, because the concept paper is short and they will tell you whether it fits. WHAT IT PAYS AND TO WHOM: the programme PROVIDES GRANTS OF UP TO $50,000 DIRECTLY TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES INCLUDING INDIGENOUS PEOPLE, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS AND OTHER NON-GOVERNMENTAL GROUPS, for projects in BIODIVERSITY, CLIMATE CHANGE MITIGATION AND ADAPTATION, LAND DEGRADATION AND SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT, INTERNATIONAL WATERS AND CHEMICALS, with SPECIAL CONSIDERATION FOR INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, WOMEN, AND YOUTH; it COMPLEMENTS THE LARGE AND MEDIUM-SIZED facility funding BY PROVIDING A WINDOW FOR THE DIRECT PARTICIPATION OF NGOs, LOCAL COMMUNITIES, AND OTHER GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS. Since 1992 it has supported CLOSE TO 30,000 GRANTS, ADMINISTERING $1.54 BILLION... ACROSS 136 COUNTRIES. Fifty thousand dollars, paid direct to a community organisation, on biodiversity or land degradation. That is the largest routine sum in this file available without an intermediary. HOW IT IS RUN LOCALLY: it operates IN A DECENTRALIZED AND COUNTRY-DRIVEN MANNER THROUGH COUNTRY PROGRAM TEAMS COMPOSED OF A NATIONAL COORDINATOR, OFTEN A PROGRAM ASSISTANT, AND A NATIONAL STEERING COMMITTEE IN EACH PARTICIPATING COUNTRY, each country publishing a country programme strategy that proposals must align with. In one small island state an operational phase was advertised with A GRANTS PORTFOLIO OF APPROXIMATELY US$750,000... FOR COMMUNITY-BASED ENVIRONMENTAL PROJECTS. Download your country's programme strategy before writing. Proposals are judged against that document, and it names the priorities and often the specific landscapes. THE THREE AGENCIES THAT NOW RUN IT: the core programme is implemented by a development programme, an agriculture organisation and a conservation organisation, the second bringing expertise in AGRICULTURE, FISHERIES, FORESTRY, BIOENERGY, CLIMATE-RESILIENT PRACTICES, LIVESTOCK, AND LAND & WATER to thirteen countries; national coordinator posts in some small states are contracted through the conservation organisation, working alongside a Caribbean islands biodiversity hotspot fund. Which agency runs your country's programme changes who you write to. Check the country page rather than assuming it is the development programme. THE LARGER WINDOW BESIDE IT: a civil society challenge programme led by a conservation union SUPPORTS COMPETITIVE OPPORTUNITIES FOR LOCAL CSOs TO ACCESS FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL RESOURCES TO SCALE UP INNOVATIVE ENVIRONMENTAL SOLUTIONS, OFFERING GRANTS OF UP TO $300,000. Three hundred thousand for an organisation that has already proved something small works. Treat the fifty-thousand grant as the step that qualifies you for it.

trackers.name: Protection grants for defenders at risk - up to €7,500 for LEGAL FEES OF THOSE BEING JUDICIALLY HARASSED, physical and digital security, medical and family costs, with a 24-hour hotline, plus emergency, relocation, trial-monitoring and respite programmes
trackers.desc: THESE GRANTS PAY THE LEGAL FEES OF SOMEONE BEING SUED OR PROSECUTED FOR DEFENDING LAND. The protection grants programme, launched in 2001 TO PROVIDE RAPID AND PRACTICAL FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS AT RISK, pays for IMPROVING PHYSICAL SECURITY OF AN ORGANISATION OR INDIVIDUAL, DIGITAL SECURITY AND COMMUNICATION SECURITY; SUPPORTING LEGAL FEES FOR HRDs WHO ARE BEING JUDICIALLY HARASSED; PAYING FOR MEDICAL FEES FOR HRDs WHO HAVE BEEN ATTACKED OR WHO HAVE SUFFERED A MEDICAL CONDITION AS A RESULT OF THEIR PEACEFUL HUMAN RIGHTS ACTIVITIES; PROVIDING FAMILY ASSISTANCE FOR IMPRISONED HRDs OR FAMILY MEMBERS WHO ARE AT RISK BECAUSE OF A HRD'S ACTIVITIES, up to a maximum of €7,500. Applications CAN BE SUBMITTED ANYTIME VIA THEIR ONLINE SYSTEM, and there is a 24-HOUR EMERGENCY HOTLINE. A criminal complaint or a defamation suit filed by a developer is judicial harassment, and the legal fees are payable. That is the single most common attack on land defenders in this file, and this is the grant written for it. WHAT IT WILL NOT FUND, WHICH DECIDES HOW YOU WRITE IT: the programme excludes RETROSPECTIVE FUNDING, INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS, ORGANISATIONS THAT HAVE APPLIED OR ARE ALREADY RECEIVING FUNDING FOR THE SAME PURPOSE ELSEWHERE, PROJECTS WHICH FOCUS ON BROADER HUMAN RIGHTS ISSUES RATHER THAN THE SPECIFIC SITUATION OF HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, COSTS FOR HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS WHO ARE ALREADY IN EXILE and ongoing office running costs; grants ARE GENERALLY NOT AWARDED FOR 100% OF THE PROPOSED BUDGET, and applicants must commit to return the grant if the work does not go ahead or is funded elsewhere. Write about the named people at risk, not about the campaign. A proposal that describes the environmental issue rather than the threat to specific defenders is refused on its own terms. THE OTHER EMERGENCY FUNDS THAT COVER THE SAME GROUND: a European defenders mechanism provides EMERGENCY GRANTS UP TO 10,000€ and runs a TEMPORARY RELOCATION PROGRAMME that funds a host organisation to relocate a defender, responding to AN INCREASED RISK, AN ANTICIPATED INCREASED RISK OR FOR A HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDER WHO HAS BEEN WORKING IN A DIFFICULT ENVIRONMENT FOR A PROLONGED PERIOD OF TIME AND WHO NEEDS A BREAK, covering REST AND RESPITE, PROFESSIONAL CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT... EMOTIONAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL WELL-BEING, FAMILY SUPPORT; a civil society lifeline fund covers LEGAL REPRESENTATION, PRISON VISITS, TRIAL MONITORING, TEMPORARY RELOCATION, EQUIPMENT REPLACEMENT, applying by email after describing a secure contact method, in several languages including Spanish; and a federation offers SECURE TRANSPORTATION, LEGAL SUPPORT, MEDICAL SUPPORT... HUMANITARIAN ASSISTANCE... URGENT RELOCATION, URGENT MONITORING. Trial monitoring is fundable, and so is a paid observer at the hearing. Where a case is being heard in a small town, an outside monitor changes how it is conducted. THE RESPITE OPTIONS WHEN SOMEONE MUST LEAVE: recorded schemes include a protective fellowship allowing UP TO TEN DEFENDERS PER YEAR to join a university centre FOR THE PURPOSES OF TRAINING, NETWORKING, AND REST, a foundation offering A YEAR LONG RESPITE PROGRAMME, a refuge for journalists forced to flee providing ADMINISTRATIVE, LEGAL AND SOCIAL ASSISTANCE, and a cities of refuge network offering PHYSICAL SAFETY AND ECONOMIC SECURITY FOR A TWO-YEARS FIXED PERIOD. Leaving for a year is not the end of a campaign if someone else can hold the file. Identify who that is before the threat arrives, because these programmes take applications from the person at risk and their host, not from a court. THE SECURITY WARNING BUILT INTO THE APPLICATION: applicants are asked to ENSURE THAT THE METHOD OF CONTACT YOU ARE PROVIDING IS SECURE AND THAT IT IS OK TO BE CONTACTED IN THAT WAY, and one fund asks applicants to describe HOW it CAN CONTACT YOU SECURELY BEFORE SENDING SENSITIVE INFORMATION. Do not send the details from a shared community email account. The application itself can expose the person it is meant to protect.

trackers.name: Inter-American Foundation grants - CURRENTLY PAUSED - direct grants of $25,000-$400,000 to grassroots organisations with no sector calls, no deadline, five application languages, and LAND AND LABOUR accepted as counterpart
trackers.desc: THIS FUNDER IS CURRENTLY PAUSED — CHECK BEFORE SPENDING TIME ON IT. Its own application page states: WE ARE CURRENTLY PAUSING GRANT FUNDING IN ALIGNMENT WITH EXECUTIVE ORDER REEVALUATING AND REALIGNING UNITED STATES FOREIGN AID. CHECK THIS PAGE FOR FURTHER UPDATES. It is AN INDEPENDENT AGENCY of that government. Everything below describes how it worked when open, and is recorded because the terms are unusual enough to be worth watching for. Read the page before writing anything. A funder under a foreign aid review can reopen with different rules, and the counterpart and eligibility terms are the first things such reviews change. WHY IT MATTERED: IT FUNDED GRASSROOTS GROUPS DIRECTLY, WITH NO INTERMEDIARY: it ONLY SUPPORT[S] COMMUNITY-LED PROJECTS SUBMITTED BY LOCAL AND GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS THAT ARE BASED IN INDEPENDENT COUNTRIES OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, requiring proof that YOUR ORGANIZATION HAS A HISTORY OF WORKING TOGETHER AS A GROUP AND IS CAPABLE OF EFFECTIVELY USING GRANTS FUNDS; it DOES NOT IDENTIFY PROBLEMS OR SUGGEST PROJECTS; INSTEAD IT RESPONDS TO INITIATIVES PRESENTED, and PROJECTS ARE SELECTED FOR FUNDING ON THEIR MERITS RATHER THAN BY SECTOR. Grants ran FROM US$25,000 TO $400,000 OVER ONE TO FOUR YEARS, with proposals accepted 365 DAYS A YEAR in SPANISH, PORTUGUESE, ENGLISH, FRENCH, OR HAITIAN CREOLE. No sector calls, no themes, no deadline. A community proposing its own solution in its own language is the entire model, and it is worth having a proposal ready if the pause lifts. THE COUNTERPART RULE, WHICH IS THE PART TO UNDERSTAND: all funded organisations must COMMIT RESOURCES TO ADVANCE THEIR DEVELOPMENT INITIATIVES, called counterpart; COUNTERPART FUNDING MUST BE A COMPONENT OF THE BUDGET... BUT NO MINIMUM AMOUNT IS REQUIRED. HIGHER COUNTERPART FUNDING MAKES A PROPOSAL MORE ATTRACTIVE, and it MAY BE IN CASH DONATIONS OR IN KIND, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, LAND, SUPPLIES, INFRASTRUCTURE, LABOR, AND OFFICE, STORAGE AND MEETING SPACE. Salaries are A LEGITIMATE EXPENSE. Land and volunteer labour count as counterpart. A community that owns the site and works it has already met the requirement without spending anything. WHAT IT LOOKED FOR IN A PROPOSAL: CREATIVE USE OF THE COMMUNITY'S RESOURCES; A DIVERSE ARRAY OF COMMUNITY VOICES IN PROJECT DEVELOPMENT AND EXECUTION; SUBSTANTIAL BENEFICIARY ENGAGEMENT in identifying the problem, choosing the approach, designing the project and managing it; PARTNERSHIPS WITH LOCAL GOVERNMENT, THE BUSINESS COMMUNITY AND OTHER CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS; feasibility, sustainability, measurable results and EVIDENCE OF BENEFICIARIES' ENHANCED CAPACITY FOR SELF-GOVERNANCE; its recorded interests included COMMUNITY CONSERVATION; AND LOCAL MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES (FORESTS, FISHERIES, ETC.). Partnership with the local government is a scoring criterion. That is the argument for bringing your municipality into the proposal rather than fighting it. THE EXCLUSIONS AND THE FIELD OFFICE RULE: support was limited to independent countries of the region, with recorded exclusions of two countries and a period when FUNDING IN THE CARIBBEAN was RESTRICTED TO three named states; public universities could not apply directly BUT MAY PARTNER WITH AN ORGANIZATION THAT IS ELIGIBLE; and an organisation headquartered abroad could apply only if its field office CAN DEMONSTRATE LOCAL LEADERSHIP. Local leadership had to be demonstrated, not asserted. Where an outside NGO offers to apply on your behalf, insist that your own organisation is the applicant.

trackers.name: RedLAC - the network of 32 national and regional ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS in 20 countries, permanent conservation trust institutions financing protected areas and local communities, with a published member list by country and zone
trackers.desc: THIRTY-TWO NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS IN TWENTY COUNTRIES, AND THE NETWORK PUBLISHES WHICH ONE COVERS YOURS. It GROUPS 32 ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS FROM 20 COUNTRIES OF THE REGION, UNITING EFFORTS TO PROTECT THE RICH BIODIVERSITY OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, with its member list filterable by zone — Caribbean, Mesoamerica and South America — alongside regional funds; more than twenty-five years old, it counts MORE THAN 100 ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS WORLDWIDE. Find the fund for your country on that member page. These are permanent national institutions with endowments, not project offices that close when a grant ends. WHAT THESE FUNDS DO, IN THE NETWORK'S WORDS: they HAVE DEMONSTRATED TO BE A KEY MECHANISM IN THE SUSTAINABLE FINANCING OF BIODIVERSITY AND IN THE STRENGTHENING OF PROTECTED AREAS AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, with a role in THE PROTECTION OF NATURAL AREAS AND THE SUPPORT TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES, described as MULTIDIMENSIONAL FUNDS, WITH APPROACHES THAT INTEGRATE PROTECTION OF BIODIVERSITY, CLIMATIC RESILIENCE AND COMMUNITY EMPOWERMENT. Support to local communities is named alongside protected areas. A community managing land next to a park is inside the mandate, not adjacent to it. SOME OF THE MEMBERS BY NAME AND KIND: recorded members include a Caribbean biodiversity fund, a national forever-protection association in one Central American country, an action fund and a Pacific foundation in one Andean country, a nature fund in one southern country, an island life fund and a regional marine fund — the last two showing that funds exist for a single archipelago and for a shared sea as well as for whole countries. There are funds scoped to one archipelago and to one reef system. If your site sits in either, that narrower fund is a better fit than the national one. WHAT THE NETWORK ITSELF OFFERS ITS MEMBERS: joining gives funds THE OPPORTUNITY TO CONNECT AND COLLABORATE WITH OTHER MEMBERS OF THE NETWORK THROUGHOUT THE REGION, to SHARE KNOWLEDGE, RESOURCES AND EXPERIENCES TO IMPROVE THEIR CAPACITIES, and ACCESS TO A WIDE VARIETY OF RESOURCES AND TOOLS, with TRAINING AND ADVICE ON DIVERSE THEMES, FROM PROJECT MANAGEMENT TO COMMUNICATION AND ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION. Where your country has no environmental fund, this network is where one would be built, and it trains new members. That is a long project, but it is the route. WHY THEY MATTER FOR PERMANENT PROTECTION: these funds are conservation trust funds — institutions holding capital whose returns finance protected areas and community work year after year, and the network works alongside a global environment facility, an African funds consortium and a large conservation finance initiative on that model. An endowment pays for wardens and monitoring long after a campaign ends. Where a protected area has just been declared, the next question is which of these funds can endow its running costs.

trackers.name: Global Forest Watch - free near-real-time deforestation alerts by email for any drawn area, an offline field app that walks patrols to the clearing, and a small grants fund whose examples include GETTING CONCESSIONS REVOKED and compiling evidence for formal complaints
trackers.desc: YOU CAN SUBSCRIBE TO EMAIL ALERTS FOR A SINGLE PLOT OF FOREST AND BE TOLD WITHIN DAYS WHEN TREES ARE CUT. The platform is FREE AND SIMPLE TO USE, ENABLING ANYONE TO CREATE CUSTOM MAPS, ANALYZE FOREST TRENDS, SUBSCRIBE TO ALERTS, OR DOWNLOAD DATA FOR THEIR LOCAL AREA OR THE ENTIRE WORLD, providing NEAR-REAL-TIME ALERTS SHOWING SUSPECTED LOCATIONS OF RECENT TREE COVER LOSS; it moved BEYOND ANNUAL DATA ON FORESTS to MONTHLY AND WEEKLY DEFORESTATION ALERTS, with EMAIL SUBSCRIPTIONS bringing them DIRECTLY INTO THE HANDS OF USERS. Users CAN SIGN UP FOR ALERTS AND DOWNLOAD DATASETS WITHOUT ANY SUBSCRIPTION OR LICENSING FEE. Draw the boundary of the land you are defending and subscribe. From then on the clearing tells you rather than the other way round, and the date stamp is independent of anything the developer says. THE FIELD APP THAT WORKS WITHOUT SIGNAL: a companion mobile application ALLOWS RANGERS TO ACCESS the data and alerts OFFLINE, WHICH IS CRITICAL IN AREAS WITH LIMITED TO NO CELL SIGNAL; USING CACHED DATA, THE APP DIRECTS USERS TO NEARBY FOREST CLEARING AND ENABLES THEM TO CAPTURE PHOTOS AND FILL OUT FORMS ABOUT DEFORESTATION, WHICH ARE UPLOADED NEXT TIME THEIR DEVICE CONNECTS, so that patrols KNOW EXACTLY WHERE TO LOOK... AND STOP THE ILLEGAL ACTIVITY BEFORE IT GETS OUT OF CONTROL; it is FREE, OPEN SOURCE, AND AVAILABLE IN ENGLISH, SPANISH, PORTUGUESE, FRENCH, AND BAHASA INDONESIAN. The alert gives the coordinates and the app walks you to them. A ground photograph taken at a satellite-flagged point, on a known date, is the evidence a prosecutor can use. THE GRANT ATTACHED TO IT, AND WHAT IT HAS PAID FOR: a small grants fund SEEKS TO BUILD THE CAPACITY OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS TO EFFECTIVELY USE the tools TO REDUCE ILLEGAL OR UNPLANNED DEFORESTATION; funded project types include USING DATA AND IMAGERY... ALONGSIDE COMMUNITY TERRITORIAL MAPS TO ADVOCATE FOR LAND TITLES AND OTHER STRENGTHENED LAND RIGHTS; CROWDSOURCING, COMPILING AND PUBLISHING DATA ON CONCESSIONS THAT OVERLAP WITH ANCESTRAL COMMUNITY LANDS, AND SUPPORT COMMUNITIES IN APPLYING PUBLIC PRESSURE TO GET THESE CONCESSIONS REVOKED; DEVELOPING THE CAPACITY OF FOREST MONITORING BRIGADES TO CONDUCT FIELD VERIFICATIONS OF NEAR-REAL TIME ALERTS; and SUPPORTING INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES IN DEVELOPING RESPONSE PROTOCOLS, FORMULATING LEGAL STRATEGIES AND COMPILING EVIDENCE OF ILLEGAL DEFORESTATION INCLUDING SATELLITE IMAGERY, DATA AND ANALYSES, AND SUBMITTING IT TO LAW ENFORCEMENT THROUGH FORMAL COMPLAINTS OR OTHER LEGAL PROCESSES. Getting concessions revoked and compiling evidence for formal complaints are funded project types, written into the fund's own examples. That is the grant to cite when describing what you intend to do. THE DEADLINE DISCIPLINE: the fund runs an annual call, and the platform states of a recent round: THE CALL FOR APPLICATIONS HAS CLOSED AS OF THE DEADLINE... WE CANNOT GRANT ANY EXTENSIONS, advising applicants to PREPARE FOR THE NEXT CALL FOR APPLICATIONS BY REVIEWING the current materials, while noting that SOME ITEMS IN THE GUIDELINES FOR APPLICANTS MAY CHANGE YEAR TO YEAR. One deadline a year, strictly enforced. Download this year's guidelines now and write the proposal before the next call opens. WHO ELSE IS ALREADY USING IT: the platform serves GOVERNMENTS, THE PRIVATE SECTOR, NGOs, JOURNALISTS, UNIVERSITIES, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC, and is convened as a partnership of OVER 200 ORGANIZATIONS; a fellowship accompanies the grants. Your municipality and your national forest agency can subscribe to the same alerts you do. Sending them the alert with a covering letter turns your observation into their file.

trackers.name: Public Lab and the open science hardware community - free open-source, low-cost instruments and toolkits communities build themselves for water, air, soil and land use, plus BALLOON AND KITE AERIAL MAPPING with stitching software and an open question forum
trackers.desc: THE INSTRUMENTS ARE OPEN SOURCE AND CHEAP ENOUGH THAT A COMMUNITY CAN BUILD ITS OWN, INCLUDING AERIAL PHOTOGRAPHY FROM A KITE. The network is DEVOTED TO EMPOWERING COMMUNITIES AND CITIZEN SCIENTISTS TO MONITOR THEIR OWN ENVIRONMENTS THROUGH THE USE OF INEXPENSIVE DIY TECHNIQUES, hosting AN IMPRESSIVE CATALOG OF OPEN SOURCE TOOLKITS... RANGING FROM WATER QUALITY SENSORS TO INDOOR AIR QUALITY AND KITE MAPPING KITS; its tools and data are CREATED BY THE community, OPEN SOURCE, AND TYPICALLY INEXPENSIVE TO USE. Its earliest technique was LOW-ALTITUDE AERIAL MAPPING WITH BALLOONS AND KITES with software to stitch the photographs into a map. A kite, a camera and free stitching software produce a dated aerial photograph of a site at a resolution no public satellite gives you. That is how you show what a hillside looked like before the machines arrived. WHY IT EXISTS, AND WHAT THAT PRECEDENT MEANS: it was founded in 2010 FOLLOWING THE BP OIL DISASTER IN THE GULF OF MEXICO... TO ADDRESS AN ENORMOUS GAP IN COMMUNITY KNOWLEDGE ABOUT THE IMPACTS OF THE SPILL, launching AS AN OPEN SOURCE PLATFORM, COLLECTING DATA AND MAPS OF THE COASTLINE OVER TIME TO SHOW THE COAST BEFORE, DURING, AND AFTER THE SPILL. Before, during and after is the sequence that wins arguments about damage. Start the baseline photographs now, while there is still a before. WHAT THE PLATFORM ACTUALLY GIVES YOU: it is A PLATFORM FOR COMMUNITY SCIENCE PRACTITIONERS WORKING ON ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES TO DOCUMENT THEIR WORK, SHARE TOOLS FOR ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING AND ADVOCACY, AND CONNECT WITH EACH OTHER; THE COMMUNITY IS OPEN AND FREE FOR ANYONE TO JOIN, members CAN ADD THEIR OWN PROJECT PAGE TO DOCUMENT THEIR METHODS AND SHARE EXPERTISE, and users CAN BROWSE LOW-COST ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING TOOLS FOR APPLICATION AREAS SUCH AS AIR QUALITY, LAND USE, STORMWATER, alongside ADVOCACY METHODS, AND ACTION TOOLKITS BY SCIENCE TOPICS covering WATER, SOIL, AIR, INDUSTRY, CLIMATE, ORGANIZING, AND MONITORING; COMMUNITY MEMBERS CAN ASK OR ANSWER QUESTIONS. Post the question with your site's details. Somebody has usually measured the same pollutant with the same cheap instrument and will say what went wrong the first time. THE KINDS OF INSTRUMENT PEOPLE HAVE BUILT: recorded tools include a spectrometer made from LEGO OR CARDBOARD, WEBCAMS OR RASPBERRY PI CAMERAS, RECYCLED DVDs so that SPECTROSCOPY IS A RESEARCH METHOD THAT ANYONE CAN EXPLORE; a SIMPLE AIR SENSOR whose REALTIME READOUT CHANGES COLOR WHEN THE SENSOR READS DIFFERENCES IN AIR QUALITY, usable WITHOUT HAVING TO LEARN HOW TO PROGRAM; a low-budget water kit with probes MEASURING TEMPERATURE, DISSOLVED OXYGEN AND CONDUCTIVITY, developed to measure sewage outfalls after storms; a DIY device to TEST FOR HEAVY METALS IN WATER; DIY infrared cameras; and a marine microplastics trawler. Dissolved oxygen, conductivity and heavy metals are the readings that show a river has been damaged. A community that takes them weekly for a year has a record no consultant's single sample can rebut. WHAT THE WIDER COMMUNITY ADDS: a water data collaborative HELPS GUIDE COMMUNITY GROUPS ON HOW TO ADOPT DIY, OPEN HARDWARE METHODS FOR COLLECTING THE QUALITY OF WATER DATA THEY NEED TO ACHIEVE THEIR OUTCOMES, alongside research centres publishing open hardware loggers, and an annual gathering for open science hardware makes tools ACCESSIBLE THROUGH OPEN-SOURCE LICENSING; recorded projects include WATER MONITORING IN THE AMAZON. Decide what outcome the data is for before choosing the instrument. A reading that will go to a court needs a different protocol from one that will go to a public meeting, and these groups will tell you which.

trackers.name: Accountability Counsel - free support for communities complaining to the accountability offices of banks financing a harmful project, taking cases ONLY WHERE THE COMMUNITY ASKS, plus a searchable global complaints database and a resource guide
trackers.desc: IT ONLY TAKES CASES WHERE THE COMMUNITY ASKS FIRST, AND IT SAYS WHY. It states: TO ENSURE THAT WE DO NOT REPLICATE THE POWER DYNAMIC WE SEEK TO UPEND AND ARE A TRUSTED, WANTED PARTNER IN COMMUNITIES, WE ONLY TAKE CASES IN WHICH COMMUNITIES REQUEST OUR SUPPORT; assistance BEGINS WITH A REQUEST FOR SUPPORT FROM THE COMMUNITY ITSELF OR A LOCAL CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATION, and NEARLY ALL CASES COME TO US THROUGH REFERRALS THROUGH CIVIL SOCIETY NETWORKS, OFTEN WITH ONLY ONE OR TWO DEGREES OF SEPARATION; it asks that a case INVOLVE A TRUSTWORTHY LOCAL PARTNER WITH WHOM WE CAN CLOSELY COLLABORATE, and weighs THE LIKELIHOOD OF A COMPLAINT LEADING TO A POSITIVE RESULT AT THE COMMUNITY LEVEL and of CREATING SYSTEMIC CHANGE AT THE INSTITUTIONAL LEVEL. Ask through an organisation that already knows you. One or two degrees of separation is the stated norm, so the introduction matters more than the application. WHAT IT DOES: it ASSIST[S] COMMUNITIES TO DEFEND THEIR RIGHTS THROUGH COMPLAINTS TO ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICES TIED TO PROJECTS THAT CAUSE HARM, specialising in NON-JUDICIAL COMPLAINT OFFICES ESTABLISHED TO RECEIVE COMMUNITY COMPLAINTS; its case work RANGES FROM INTENSIVE AND COMPREHENSIVE ASSISTANCE TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND THEIR PARTNERS THROUGHOUT A COMPLAINT PROCESS, TO PROVIDING MORE TARGETED SUPPORT WITH DAILY CASE WORK CONDUCTED PRIMARILY BY LOCAL PARTNERS, and it CONDUCT[S] TRAININGS IN LOCAL COMMUNITIES ABOUT ALL OPTIONS FOR ADDRESSING HUMAN RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL ABUSES ASSOCIATED WITH INTERNATIONALLY FINANCED PROJECTS. A complaint to a bank's own accountability office runs alongside any court case rather than replacing it. Ask for the training even if you never file: it maps every route available against a financed project.
