THE UNITED STATES ENTITY, AND WHAT IT FUNDS: a separate United States non-profit MOBILIZES RESOURCES AND PARTNERSHIPS FROM THE UNITED STATES TO SUPPORT AND EXPAND THE IMPACT OF THIS MISSION and SUPPORTS INITIATIVES ALIGNED WITH THE FOUNDATION'S PRIORITIES ACROSS THREE INTERCONNECTED PILLARS... DEMOCRATIC INNOVATION, CLIMATE ACTION, AND A JUST AND REGENERATIVE ECONOMY, having COME TO EMBRACE FEMINIST PRINCIPLES THAT CENTER THE IMPORTANCE OF BUILDING COLLECTIVE POWER. Two legal entities, two funding routes. Which one can pay you depends on where your organisation is registered, so ask that first. THE HONEST NOTE ON ORIGIN AND COMPANY: it was FOUNDED IN 1994 BY a Swiss industrialist, is headquartered in one Central American capital with a northern office, works BY ENCOURAGING ALLIANCES BETWEEN SOCIAL AND BUSINESS LEADERS, and its recent activities include projects with a named water technology company in one country's semi-arid region. Its model is explicitly to put business leaders at the table with social ones. Decide whether that suits your fight before joining a programme, and read who co-funds it.

trackers.name: 环境民事公益诉讼 — who may sue, and on what evidence
trackers.desc: THE STANDING TEST, FROM THE SUPREME PEOPLE'S COURT'S OWN INTERPRETATION (adopted 8 December 2014, in force 7 January 2015). Under Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law a social organisation may sue over pollution or ecological destruction harming the public interest if it is registered with the civil affairs department of a government at or above the level of a city divided into districts, and has engaged specifically in environmental protection public interest activities continuously for more than 5 years with no record of violation. If those are met the court shall accept the case; the organisation must not seek economic benefit from the suit. WHAT THE TERMS MEAN: social groups, private non-enterprise units and foundations all count. YOUR CHARTER DECIDES WHAT YOU CAN SUE ABOUT — the test is met where the charter states that the purpose and main business scope is protecting the social public interest, and the public interest at stake in the suit must be related to that stated scope. ‘No violation record’ means no administrative or criminal penalty in the course of business in the 5 years before filing. HAVE THIS READY WHEN YOU FILE: registration certificate, charter, the annual work reports or annual inspection reports for the 5 consecutive years before suit, and a signed and stamped declaration of no violation record. Article 9 lets the court invite you to add claims such as ceasing the infringement and restoring the original state if what you asked for is too narrow to protect the public interest. THE LIMIT: this is the CIVIL route. Environmental administrative public interest litigation — challenging a government decision — can be brought only by the procuratorate, so a challenge to an approval must go through persuading it to act.

trackers.name: CEPF — Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund grants
trackers.desc: MONEY THAT REACHES SMALL GROUPS. CEPF funds civil society organisations of all sizes — farmers' cooperatives and community groups as much as universities and international NGOs. Small grants average about USD 15,000 and large grants about USD 150,000; in the Indo-Burma Phase IV call, which listed China among its eligible countries, small grants ran to USD 50,000 and large grants USD 50,000–250,000. ITS STATED PREFERENCES FAVOUR YOU: priority goes to projects showing a leading role for local organisations or building local civil society capacity, and to projects supporting Indigenous and local communities in community-based or co-management conservation — explicitly including actions that enhance local communities' tenure and resource use rights. Small grant applications in that call were accepted in Chinese and other regional languages, not only English. HARD CONDITIONS: your organisation needs its own bank account and must be able to receive charitable contributions under national law; the project must sit inside a biodiversity hotspot where CEPF currently works and support at least one strategic direction in that hotspot's ecosystem profile — read the profile before writing anything. Excluded: anything that could adversely affect critical habitat, introduce invasive non-indigenous species, or remove or alter tangible cultural heritage. CHECK THE CURRENT CALL: eligible countries are listed per call and windows are fixed — Indo-Burma Phase IV ran 2 February to 16 March 2026. Since 2000 CEPF has given over USD 300 million to more than 2,700 organisations across more than 112 countries.

trackers.name: 社会公益型保护地 — a 50-year management agreement instead of a purchase
trackers.desc: YOU CANNOT BUY THE LAND, SO YOU CONTRACT FOR IT. In 2011, with Sichuan provincial support, China's first civil nature reserve was created at Laohegou, Pingwu County — core giant panda habitat and a migration corridor that sat in no legally protected area system, with management limited to basic patrol and fire prevention while poaching, snaring and poison-fishing were common. THE MECHANISM: a 50-year entrusted management agreement (委托管理协议) with the county gave the Taohuayuan Foundation long-term management rights over three forest parcels within 110 km², with the foundation raising social funds and taking full responsibility for establishment, management and financing. YOU NEED A REGISTRABLE LOCAL ENTITY: a 民办非企业 private non-enterprise unit, the Pingwu Laohegou Nature Conservation Centre, was registered to run it. The model is described as more flexible than government reserves, able to work where government cannot, and able to bring collective and individual land into protection at relatively low cost — made possible by collective forest tenure reform. Recognised by the State Forestry Administration, it has been replicated at Bayuelin (Leshan, Sichuan) and Xicaohai (Heqing, Yunnan).

trackers.name: 保护地役权 and 社区协议保护 — easements and community agreements
trackers.desc: TWO CONTRACT ROUTES, WITH THEIR LIMITS STATED. Conservation easements (保护地役权): Qianjiangyuan National Park and others have piloted collective forest and moso bamboo easements, and Article 22 of the Hainan Tropical Rainforest National Park Regulations (Trial) expressly lets the park authority manage collectively owned natural resources through easement contracts. BUT LEGAL SCHOLARSHIP RECORDS REAL WEAKNESSES: subjects, rights, creation procedures and registration requirements differ widely between localities and lack internal consistency; practice is usually led by the protected-area authority or local government, emphasising public objectives with little attention to protecting private property rights; and some localities hold back over doubts about the legal basis under the Civil Code. Community conservation agreements (社区协议保护) follow a clear sequence: first establish who owns the resource and who can authorise — reserve authority for state reserves, the village for collective land; then mobilise, choosing communities with genuine willingness and organisational capacity; then negotiate and sign, drafting a conservation plan and a development plan together. At Longge village in Sanjiangyuan this took about 5 months of discussion and produced a cooperative joined by all 53 herding households. AND THE APPROACH THAT MADE IT WORK NEAR LAOHEGOU: the foundation did not start by policing hunters — it asked what the community's own grievance was, found it was outsiders digging medicinal herbs, and villagers amended their own 村规民约 to bar them. Only then did protection extend to wildlife, and the community accepted it.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: 自然之友 Friends of Nature — send them the case; they are the plaintiff
trackers.desc: There is a public-interest-litigation hotline and a separate address for submitting pollution and ecological-destruction leads — +86 10 65232040 and gyss@fonchina.org — and that is the shape of the route: the organisation sues, and what a community supplies is the case. The count as at 31 December 2024: 64 environmental public interest suits brought, 57 accepted for docketing, 47 concluded. The gap between 64 and 57 is the honest number, because getting a case 立案 is its own gate before any argument on the merits. Coverage spans soil, air and water pollution, ecological destruction, marine protection and climate. The precedent to cite when a project has not been built yet is the green peafowl case — the country's first preventive environmental public interest litigation for wildlife protection, brought over habitat a hydropower scheme would have flooded, which establishes that the harm does not have to have happened first. Others: the first climate case, over curtailed wind and solar in Gansu; the Changzhou contaminated-land case; and a vehicle-emissions case against Hyundai settled by agreement to place the damages in a public-interest trust so restoration money is actually spent on restoration. Several have been listed as typical or guiding cases by the Supreme People's Court and by provincial high courts. The organisation states its own constraint: social organisations bringing this litigation face shortages of specialist staff and limited funding, which is why it has argued the work should be brought within the legal aid system. Expect selection, and expect years — one Hunan case took five to a first-instance win. It began pressing for the litigation route in 2005 and had its first case docketed in 2011. Office: Room 2106, Block B, Hualong Building, Building 3, Courtyard A29, North Third Ring Road Middle, Beijing; office@fonchina.org.

trackers.name: 中国绿发会 CBCGDF 保护地 — apply to have your own site made a conservation area
trackers.desc: The route in is an application from whoever knows the site, and it has been open to individuals. The foundation runs a network of civil-society conservation areas, each numbered in a CCAfa series that had passed 178 by late 2021, and each headed by a local director with volunteers who patrol it. In May 2016 the scientist who discovered the Ili pika submitted an application to establish a conservation area for it at Jinghe; the foundation took it up, built a cooperative protection mechanism with the Xinjiang environmental department, the Bortala prefecture and Jinghe county governments, the county environment bureau and the state forest administration, declared the area on International Biodiversity Day that month with three sub-stations across the core range, and launched an online public fundraising campaign to pay for its work — which is what makes this more than a label. In September 2021 an individual's application to protect an endangered local pig breed in Fujian was approved on the same footing. Be clear what the designation is and is not. It is made by a foundation, not the state: it confers structure, a named director, volunteers, a fundraising channel and a national organisation's attention, but no statutory protection and no title. Its force comes from the cooperation agreements the foundation then builds with provincial and county authorities, so where the local government will not engage the designation is largely nominal — establish that early rather than late. Existing areas run from giant panda habitat at Conglinggang, declared December 2018, to wetland on the Hutuo river from June 2020, great bustard wintering and breeding grounds at Changyuan and Tumuji, and spotted seal habitat at Lüshun. An annual conference brings the directors together; the 2021 meeting ran online with more than 24,000 viewers and was listed in the China Association for Science and Technology's guide to significant academic conferences, which is the kind of standing that matters when a local official asks who you are. Two site cautions. The foundation runs both cbcgdf.org and cbcgdf.org.cn, and both serve over plain http with no TLS, so send nothing sensitive through their forms. Telephone 010-68485952.

trackers.name: SEE基金会 — unrestricted money for new and growing Chinese environmental groups
trackers.desc: The money is unrestricted, which is the rarest feature of any fund in this file. Its start-up programme was created in 2012 to address the shortage of grassroots environmental organisations in China; by mid-2016 it had run six rounds and given 150 newly formed organisations 15 million yuan in unrestricted funding. Its growth-stage programme, begun in December 2012 and co-funded with three other Chinese foundations, gives a partner organisation three consecutive years of unrestricted funding totalling 300,000 yuan. Unrestricted means it pays for rent, salaries and the year in which nothing is achieved — the costs no project grant covers, and the ones that close small organisations. The second half of the growth programme is a mentor, not a cheque. Partners are matched with a mentor team drawn from the foundation's entrepreneur members and other specialists, working on the organisation's core business, the professionalisation of its team and the diversification of its funding. By mid-2017 it had 43 partner organisations across nineteen provinces, regions and municipalities. For a group that has an issue and no institution, the sequence of start-up grant and then growth grant with mentoring is the path this foundation is built to run. Know its shape before applying. Founded in 2008 by an association of entrepreneurs formed in 2004, it became a public fundraising foundation at the end of 2014 and reports having supported more than 900 Chinese grassroots environmental organisations or individuals directly or indirectly. Its declared fields are desertification control, climate change and business sustainability, ecological conservation and nature education, and marine protection. This is conservation and pollution funding from a business-founded platform, not litigation money, and its posture is collaborative rather than adversarial — read it alongside the Friends of Nature entry, which is where a case goes. Check the current round. The figures above come from the programmes' own published records of 2016 and 2017; rounds open and close, and the site serves over plain http without TLS, so send nothing sensitive through it.

trackers.name: 12369 environmental reporting — sixty days to conclude, and the status is checkable
trackers.desc: The deadlines are written into the administrative measures, and so is the standard. A report belonging to a lower-level authority must be assigned to it through the reporting system within three working days, and a report must be concluded within sixty days of acceptance; a complex case may be extended only with the approval of the responsible head, the reporter must be told the reason, and the extension may not exceed a further thirty days. The measures state the standard plainly: every report received is to be accepted, every violation investigated, every matter to have a result and every case a reply. Published performance tells you what to expect. The ministry's own national reporting for 2017 recorded 618,856 reports, an average of 3.7 days to accept and 22.8 days to close, about a tenth not accepted because the information given was insufficient or the matter fell outside environmental management, and roughly seven in ten accepted reports found substantiated. Of substantiated cases the commonest outcome was an order to rectify within a time limit, with on-site correction, suspension of production for treatment and closure together making up most of the rest. The most reported sector was construction, largely night-time noise. Say the four things that keep a report out of the rejected tenth. The time, the precise location with a landmark or coordinates, a plain description of what is being discharged, and where possible the full name of the enterprise, with photographs kept as evidence — and ask the operator to record that you want the outcome reported back to you. Where a local reward scheme applies, the reporter must give real identity and contact details and say expressly that they are claiming under it; such schemes grade cases by severity and are made by provincial and municipal authorities rather than nationally. The handling status can be checked afterwards. A national query service for the progress of a 12369 report is published through the government service portal, and reports may be made by telephone, through the ministry's online reporting platform, through its public reporting account, or by letter. No lawyer, organisation or fee is required at any point, which makes this the lowest threshold route recorded for China.

trackers.name: 森林生态效益补偿 — an annual payment per mu for keeping public-benefit forest standing
trackers.desc: If the forest is designated national-level public benefit forest, there is an annual payment, and it is higher for collectives and individuals than for the state. Central finance provides forest ecological benefit compensation for the protection and management of national-level public benefit forest, delineated under national rules and graded into three protection levels. The published measures set different standards by ownership: the state-owned category at a lower rate per mu per year, and collective and individually owned national public benefit forest at a materially higher one, of which the larger part is management subsidy and a small fixed part is public management expenditure. Rates have been revised upward over time, so ask the county forestry bureau for the current standard rather than relying on any figure. For collectives and individuals the money is explicitly economic compensation, not only wages. Policy explanation of the collective and individual share divides it into economic compensation to the collective and individuals for keeping the forest, a labour subsidy for organised management work, and a small allowance for facilities and equipment. That first component is the one that matters to a household deciding whether to keep trees standing rather than convert the land. It runs on a contract, so ask for the contract. Forestry authorities must conclude management contracts with the state units, collectives and individuals undertaking the work; those parties perform the obligations in the contract and are paid according to how they perform it. Reading the obligations before signing tells a household exactly what it is being paid to do and what would put the payment at risk. There is an archive, and you can ask whether you are in it. County forestry departments and forest management units must establish resource archives for national public benefit forest containing per-household registration cards, resource status and change tables and maps, the forest tenure ledger and the management agreements, and provincial authorities must build databases, remote sensing image libraries and management information systems. Whether a household is registered, over what area and at what grade is therefore a checkable fact. Payments can also be suspended, reduced or cancelled for poor management or breach, and interception or misappropriation of the funds by others is pursued at county level, so both under-payment and misuse have a named forum.

trackers.name: 检察公益诉讼 — the procuratorate takes leads from the public and can order the regulator to act
trackers.desc: Cases begin from leads given by members of the public. A published case records a district procuratorate receiving a lead reported by a public interest litigation volunteer, opening a case after preliminary investigation, and then establishing the facts through site visits, obtaining documentary evidence and questioning witnesses — finding that a company had unlawfully emitted volatile organic compounds, harming the environment and the public interest. Reporting to the procuratorate is a different act from reporting to the environment bureau: this file already records the ministry's own reporting line, and this is the body that supervises whether that bureau did its job. The pre-litigation recommendation is the instrument to ask for. The procuratorate may issue a pre-litigation procuratorial recommendation to the administrative organ carrying supervisory duties, urging it to perform those duties according to law — in the published case, recommending that the environment bureau promptly investigate and deal with the company's unlawful emissions, and serving alongside it a note on enforcement points the bureau should watch in that industry. Where a community's complaint was accepted and then went nowhere, that inaction is precisely what this procedure exists to correct. It escalates, and the targets include developers. Where an administrative organ has opened an ecological damage compensation procedure, the procuratorate continues to supervise the consultation and the restoration, and where consultation fails to produce an agreement it may commence civil public interest litigation. Published cases include unlawful hill excavation and mining organised under the cover of emergency risk removal and site levelling for a health and tourism project, with assessed losses of national mineral resources in the tens of millions of yuan and a separately assessed loss of ecosystem service function. What to give them, and how to reach them. Published reporting describes basin work in which procuratorates at three levels handled dozens of public interest cases, pushed more than a hundred mines into ecological restoration, ordered hundreds of mining firms to treat pollution and closed scores of temporary yards unlawfully occupying land, and a river special project that screened hundreds of leads. The procuratorial service line and the online procuratorial platform are the public channels. Give the same four things an environmental report needs — the time, the precise location, a plain description of what is happening and the operator's full name — and add which agency has already been told and has not acted.

trackers.name: 法律援助 — environmental damage compensation is a listed legal aid matter, with a seven-day decision
trackers.desc: Compensation for environmental pollution and ecological destruction is a named category. The legal aid law provides that a party who, because of financial difficulty, has not appointed a representative may apply to a legal aid institution in a list of matters — and claims for compensation for environmental pollution and ecological damage sit on that list, alongside work injury, traffic, food and drug safety and medical accident claims. A community asking for a lawyer to pursue damage to its land or water is therefore asking for something the statute already names, not for an exception to be made. The timetable is statutory, and a refusal has to be in writing. The institution must examine an application within seven days of receiving it and decide whether to grant aid; where it grants aid it must assign a legal aid provider within three days of the decision; and where it refuses it must notify the applicant in writing, with reasons. Where the papers are incomplete it must tell the applicant in one notification what is missing, and an applicant who does not supply it is treated as having withdrawn. A written refusal carrying reasons is a document — and a document can be questioned, appealed and shown to other people. Some applicants skip the means check entirely. Applicants who hold material showing that they are minors, elderly people or disabled people without a fixed source of living, or recipients of social assistance, judicial assistance or preferential treatment, or migrant workers claiming unpaid labour remuneration or work injury compensation, are exempt from verification of financial difficulty. The threshold is provincial, and the state must tell you the right exists. The standard of financial difficulty is set by each provincial-level government according to local economic conditions and adjusted over time, so the figure is local rather than national. Courts, procuratorates, public security organs and relevant departments are required to inform parties promptly of their right to apply. Cities run legal aid centres with workstations at labour arbitration bodies, courts, procuratorates and in worker neighbourhoods, with duty lawyers giving free consultation on working days, and applications may be made at the nearest institution, through the provincial government service network, or through the national legal service hotline. Read this with the reporting line and procuratorial public interest litigation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 不动产登记资料查询 — what someone intending to sue may ask before they can prove an interest
trackers.desc: Who may look, and where. Under the ministerial measures on searching real estate registration records, the people who may query and copy the records are the rights holder and an interested party, either of whom may entrust a lawyer or another agent to do it for them. The query is made at the registration body of the city or county where the property lies, and a body approached in the wrong place must tell the applicant which body to go to. An application form and identity documents are required, and an agent must produce both parties' identity documents and an authorisation which itself fixes the scope of what may be searched and copied. A dispute counts as an interest, not only a deal. An interested party may apply to query the registration result where the interest arises from a sale, exchange, gift, lease or mortgage of the property — and also where a civil dispute exists over the property and litigation or arbitration has already been commenced. The contracts, or the proceedings, are the proof to bring. And someone who intends to sue but cannot yet prove the interest may still ask four things. The same measures allow a person who intends to buy, lease or mortgage, or to bring litigation or arbitration, but who cannot produce the interest documents, to query whether the register records the natural condition of the property, whether it is co-owned, whether there is a mortgage registration, advance notice registration or objection registration, and whether there is a seizure registration or another restriction on disposal. A lawyer instructed by such a person may in addition ask the registry to verify whether the name of the rights holder given matches the register, the form of co-ownership, and the name of the authority that ordered the seizure or the restriction on disposal. For a community that has not yet started proceedings, that is the door: it can learn whether the ground is encumbered, frozen, or subject to an objection already lodged by somebody else. On the spot, or within five working days. Where the conditions are met and the applicant needs a certificate of the query result or copies of the records, the registration body must provide them immediately, and where special reasons prevent that, within five working days; self-service terminals capable of verifying identity and issuing result certificates may also be provided. Read this with the legal aid, procuratorial public interest litigation and reporting line entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: CMA qualification — check the laboratory behind a monitoring report, and the scope it is approved for
trackers.desc: Environmental monitoring institutions are required by law to hold the qualification. The market regulator's own service page for the qualification of inspection and testing institutions cites, among its legal bases, the central policy on deepening environmental monitoring reform to improve the quality of monitoring data, under which environmental monitoring institutions must obtain a testing institution qualification certificate, together with the metrology law and the certification and accreditation regulation. A monitoring report produced by a body that does not hold that certificate is therefore defective before anybody argues about its contents. Anyone can check the certificate and the approved scope. The national certification and accreditation information platform allows a search of institutions holding national or provincial qualification by certificate number, institution name or address, and shows the testing capability each has been approved for. When a report arrives bearing the qualification mark, the question is not only whether the laboratory holds a certificate but whether that certificate covers the parameter reported. This file records that scope point for Singapore, Brunei and Taiwan; here it is checkable by anybody, from outside, without asking the laboratory anything. Expired and out of scope are the two failures to look for. Published guidance on using the platform describes precisely those cases: a qualification that has lapsed, and a report covering items outside the approved range. Both are visible on the platform and both defeat the report, and guidance also notes that a suspected false qualification report can be reported to the market regulation authorities. The same check applies to an expert relied on in court. The regulator's page records that bodies carrying out judicial appraisal must have laboratories that have passed metrological certification or laboratory accreditation. Where a community's evidence, or the other side's, is heading into proceedings, the qualification of the laboratory behind it is a matter of public record. Read this with the legal aid, procuratorial public interest litigation and reporting line entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 政府信息公开 — an oral application the office must write up, and township land compensation as priority disclosure
trackers.desc: If writing is genuinely difficult, you may apply orally and the office must fill in the form. Applications for government information are made to the agency's information disclosure working body in written form, including electronic data messages — and where the applicant genuinely has difficulty using written form, the application may be made orally and the receiving body completes the application on the applicant's behalf. Agencies must establish and improve their application channels, and must compile and publish a disclosure guide and catalogue giving the name, office address, office hours, telephone, fax and email of that working body. Township governments must give priority disclosure to land takings and compensation. Among the matters a township government is required to disclose as a priority are the expropriation or requisition of land and the demolition of houses, together with the payment and use of the compensation and subsidy fees, alongside the township land use master plan and the examination and approval of homestead land. For a village facing acquisition that is a named category of proactive disclosure at the tier closest to it, so the first question is not whether the information can be obtained but why it has not already been published. Twenty working days, at both ends. Information falling within the scope of proactive disclosure must be made public within twenty working days of being formed or changed. On application, published agency procedure describes registration on receipt with a receipt issued to the applicant, transfer to the handling department, and a written reply issued before the twentieth working day. Remedies, and the report that counts them. A person who considers that an agency has infringed their lawful rights in its disclosure work may complain or report to the next higher agency or to the competent disclosure department, and may apply for administrative reconsideration or bring administrative litigation; an agency that has failed to establish sound disclosure systems is to be ordered to correct by the higher agency, with discipline for the responsible leaders and directly responsible personnel in serious cases. The annual disclosure report must record applications received and handled and the reconsiderations and lawsuits arising from disclosure work, so an agency's own report shows how often it is challenged. Read this with the legal aid, procuratorial public interest litigation, testing qualification and land record entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 12388 — report at the right level, and what real-name reporting buys
trackers.desc: Report at the right level, or it goes nowhere. The discipline inspection and supervision organs run a single national reporting telephone and website, with separate reporting sites for each province and for central government organs. The site's own notice for online reporting states the principle of graded responsibility and tells reporters to choose the site corresponding to the locality and the rank of the person being reported. For a village complaint about a county official, the county level channel is the one that matters, and a report filed at the wrong level loses time rather than gaining attention. Real-name reporting buys priority and an answer. The rules governing how these organs handle reports encourage reporting under one's own name; online reporting requires identity authentication; and a report which carries a signature that is not the reporter's true name, or which cannot be verified, is handled as anonymous. Real-name reports are given priority in handling and disposal and receive a reply, and the organs are required to keep the reporter's name, unit, address and telephone number, and the content of the report, strictly confidential, and to protect real-name reporters from unlawful harm. Receipt is notified and the outcome is fed back. The same rules state both duties in terms: the fact of acceptance is to be communicated, and the result of the handling is to be reported back. A route which confirms that it has taken a case and then says what came of it is uncommon among the complaint channels recorded in this file, and it is worth quoting when following up. The scope names the waste of state assets. Reports may concern breaches of party discipline by organisations and members, and, for the six categories of public officials covered by the supervision law, failure to perform duties according to law, breaches of the rules on the impartial exercise of power and on integrity, and suspected corruption, bribery, abuse of power, dereliction of duty, rent-seeking, transfer of benefits, favouritism and the wasting of state assets. One caution sits in the same rules: false accusation and framing are themselves investigated, so a report should rest on what can be shown. Read this with the government information disclosure route, the testing qualification check, the legal aid and the land record entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 领导干部自然资源资产离任审计 — the outgoing audit of a leader's environmental record
trackers.desc: A departing official is audited on their environmental record. Under regulations issued in 2017 and operating as a regular system since 2018, audit bodies carry out outgoing — and in some cases mid-term — audits of leading officials' performance of their responsibilities for managing natural resource assets and protecting the ecological environment, commissioned by the organisation departments as officials are rotated or leave office. When the official who approved a project moves on, there is therefore an audit whose subject is precisely what happened to the land, the water and the air during their term. The audit is grounded in physical change. The regulation directs that the audit be based on natural resource asset balance sheets, or on departmental management data, reflecting the changes in the physical quantities of natural resource assets and in ecological environment quality. The measurable state of a place across a term of office is the baseline, which is a different and harder test than whether procedures were followed. Inspection reports and rectification status must be handed over. The audited official's locality, department and other relevant units must provide the target responsibility agreements signed and how far they were met, the appraisals and any rewards or penalties, the routine and special inspections carried out by higher authorities together with their inspection reports and conclusions, and the rectification undertaken by the local party committee, government and departments. A community that has complained before will find the paper trail of its own complaint inside that bundle. Accountability is lifelong, and publication is directed. Problem leads transferred by the audit must be investigated, and the responsible persons are subject to lifelong accountability whether or not they have since been transferred, promoted or retired, under the party accountability rules and the measures on accountability for ecological damage by leading cadres; the regulation also directs party committees and governments at all levels gradually to explore and implement a system of publishing the results of these audits. An audited official who disagrees may appeal within a stated period, with review and a final decision at the higher level. Read this with the government information disclosure route, the reporting platform, the testing qualification check and the land record entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 房屋征收评估办法 — the households choose the valuation firm, and ten days to take the review to an expert committee
trackers.desc: The people whose homes are being taken choose the valuation firm. The measure on valuation for the expropriation of houses on state-owned land provides that the real estate price valuation institution is selected by the expropriated persons themselves, by consultation within a prescribed period; and that where they cannot agree in time, the expropriation department organises them to decide by majority vote, or determines the firm by lot or random draw, with provinces setting the detailed procedure. The choice of valuer therefore belongs to the households rather than to the department taking the property — which is the opposite of the arrangement most people assume they are stuck with. Disagree with the review, and there are ten days. Where the expropriated person or the expropriation department objects to the review result issued by the original valuation firm, they must apply to the real estate price valuation expert committee for adjudication within ten days of receiving that review result. The window is short and it is counted from receipt, so the date on the envelope matters: missing it forecloses the route entirely. Non-cooperation must be written into the report. The measure requires that where the expropriation department or the expropriated person does not cooperate or does not provide the relevant materials, the valuation firm state that fact in the valuation report; during adjudication the firm must explain the valuation to the expert committee, and where on-site inspection and investigation of the house is required, the relevant units and individuals must assist. A refusal to hand over documents therefore becomes part of the written record rather than an unprovable complaint. Independence, recusal, and the comparison standard. Valuation firms, appraisers and committee members must carry out expropriation valuation and adjudication independently, objectively and impartially and are responsible for the opinions they issue; no unit or individual may interfere; anyone with an interest in the matter must recuse themselves; and firms may not solicit this work by catering to improper demands of the parties, false advertising or maliciously low fees. Real estate similar to the expropriated house is defined as that which is the same or similar in location, use, nature of rights, grade, degree of newness, scale and building structure — the definition on which a comparison can be challenged. Housing administration and other departments must facilitate queries of ownership and related transaction information needed for the valuation, review and adjudication. Read this with the government information disclosure route, the civic protected area entry, the reporting platform and the natural resource audit entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 中央生态环境保护督察 — a team stationed for a month, a hotline from eight to eight, and published referral tables
trackers.desc: A national inspection team stations in the province for a month, and publishes how to reach it. Each stationing announcement carries the same four facts: the dates of the visit, a dedicated duty telephone number, a dedicated postal box address in the provincial capital, and the hours during which the hotline receives reports — published in the rounds recorded here as eight in the morning to eight at night, every day of the stationing period. Those four facts are the entire access route, they are announced at the start of the visit, and they expire with it. For a community whose complaints have been circling the same local offices for years, this is a month in which a body from outside the province is taking calls. What it takes, and what it hands back. The announcements state that the team mainly receives letters and calls concerning ecological and environmental protection in the province being inspected, and that reports falling outside that scope are transferred to the inspected locality to handle under the applicable rules. The practical consequence is blunt: frame the matter as an ecological or environmental protection problem in that province, or it is handed back down to the very authorities the complaint is trying to get above. Referrals and rectification are published in numbered batches. Provincial, municipal and district governments publish tables of public letters and complaints transferred by the inspection team together with the rectification carried out while the inspection continues, issued batch by batch and archived afterwards. A published batch table is evidence that a complaint was referred and a place to check what the response was — which is more than most complaint routes in this file provide. The published focus list tells you which framing lands. Announced priorities for recent rounds have included illegal occupation of protected natural areas, development that breaks through the ecological protection red line, damage to shorelines, ecological destruction of cultivated land, curbing the blind launch of high-energy and high-emission projects, environmental infrastructure, agricultural non-point source pollution, solid waste including construction waste, protection of important lakes and tributaries, rectification of problems found in earlier inspections, and prominent ecological and environmental problems raised by the public. Match the complaint to a listed priority and quote that priority back. Read this with the government information disclosure route, the reporting platform, the civic protected area and the expropriation valuation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 不可移动文物 — county-level registration, the four things a protection unit must have, and the building ban inside the scope
trackers.desc: Registration happens at county level, and that is the first rung. Under the cultural relics protection law, immovable cultural relics that have not yet been approved and published as cultural relic protection units are to be registered and published by the cultural relics administration department of the county-level government. A village with an old bridge, an ancestral hall, a kiln, a well or a temple therefore does not have to reach for national listing first: registration by the county department is the fastest step and it puts the thing on a public list. A protection unit must have four things, and each is checkable. For protection units at each level, the responsible governments delineate the necessary scope of protection, put up markers with explanations, establish record archives, and designate either a dedicated body or a named person responsible for management. Asking which of those four exist for a given site is a concrete question with a documentary answer, and a unit whose protection scope has never been delineated is one whose boundary can be argued about when a project arrives. Inside the protection scope, building is prohibited. The law provides that within the protection scope of a cultural relic protection unit no construction works other than cultural relic protection works may be carried out, nor any blasting, drilling or excavation; where special circumstances require such works, the safety of the unit must be assured and approval must be obtained from the government that approved and published that unit, with the prior agreement of the cultural relics department one level higher — and for a national key unit, approval by the provincial-level government with the agreement of the State Council's relics department. That is a prohibition with a named approver, not a consultation. Planning must absorb the protection, and participation is expressly invited. When governments draw up plans they must first agree protection measures for immovable relics with the relics department and incorporate them into the plan; county-level and higher departments organise protection plans for the immovable relics in their area, approved and published by the same-level government and filed with the department one level up. The law also directs relics departments to guide and encourage grassroots mass self-governing organisations and volunteers to take part in protecting immovable cultural relics — a written basis for a village committee to be involved rather than informed. Read this with the entrusted management of protected areas, the government information disclosure route, the central environmental inspection team and the expropriation valuation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 环境损害司法鉴定 — registered institutions that produce court-usable environmental evidence, and the ones that do not charge in advance
trackers.desc: There is a registered profession whose whole job is producing environmental evidence for court. The national classification rules define environmental damage judicial appraisal as the activity, in litigation, of appraisers applying environmental science or specialist knowledge — through monitoring, testing, site investigation, experimental simulation or comprehensive analysis — to identify and judge the specialist questions raised in pollution or ecological destruction proceedings, and to give an appraisal opinion. These are not consultants a community hires informally: they are registered with the justice administration, and their opinions are the evidence courts work from. Four questions they are authorised to answer. The rules list what the appraisal resolves: the nature of the pollutants; the nature, scope and degree of the damage to the ecological environment; the assessment of causation; and the assessment of pollution treatment and operating costs together with the measures or plans needed to prevent the damage spreading and to restore the environment. Separate categories cover solid waste identification, and hazardous waste identification including determining lawful disposal methods and estimating disposal costs. Causation and restoration cost are the two a community usually cannot establish on its own, and they are inside the scope by name. The numbers, and where the institutions are. Official publications record 287 institutions and 5,098 appraisers registered with the justice administration nationally, handling upwards of twenty thousand appraisals a year, with coverage reported across every province from 2023 after growth from 220 institutions and 3,810 appraisers. Registration runs through joint rules of the justice and ecology ministries setting the review procedure, the scoring, the professional capability required and the laboratory and equipment a body must have — so being on the register is itself a statement about capability. Some do not charge before they work. Because the cost of appraisal was identified as an obstacle in environmental public interest litigation, the justice ministry and the supreme procuratorate established a no-advance-fee arrangement in 2019 under which institutions appraise first and charge afterwards, beginning with 58 institutions and later expanded to 141. The arrangement was built for procuratorial public interest cases, so the practical route for a community is usually through the procuratorate rather than direct — but knowing the list exists is what makes that approach concrete. Read this with the entrusted management conservation route, the pollution complaint channels, the environmental information disclosure and the corporate penalty search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 环境影响评价公众参与办法 — disclosure seven working days after the assessor is hired, and the questioning opinions that force a hearing
trackers.desc: Disclosure starts seven working days after the assessor is appointed, not when the report is finished. The public participation measures require the construction unit, within seven working days of determining who will prepare the environmental impact report, to publish on its own website, on local public media sites or on local government sites the project name, the siting or routing, the construction content and, for rebuilding, expansion or relocation projects, the existing works and their environmental protection situation. From that point on, throughout the preparation of the draft for comment, the public may submit opinions relating to the assessment to the construction unit, using a public opinion form whose content and format the ministry prescribes. That early window is the one most often missed: it opens before there is a report to react to, and it is when the scope is still being set. Questioning opinions trigger meetings, and which meeting depends on what is questioned. Where a project attracts many questioning opinions on its environmental impacts, the measures split the response in two. If the questions centre on the impact prediction conclusions, the environmental protection measures or the risk prevention measures, the construction unit must convene a public symposium or a hearing, and must invite representatives of the public who may be environmentally affected. If they centre on the technical methods, guidelines or theory used in the assessment, it must convene an expert argumentation meeting, with affected public representatives invited to attend. Framing an objection deliberately — as a challenge to conclusions and measures, or as a challenge to method — therefore determines which forum the rules require. Ten working days' notice, and minutes published within five. Where such a meeting is to be held, the unit must announce the time, place and theme, the categories of public who may register and how to register, at least ten working days beforehand, through the network platform and by posting notices where local people will readily see them. Within five working days after the meeting it must compile the minutes or the expert conclusions from the on-site record and publish them, faithfully recording the various opinions expressed. The participation explanation is a document with a prescribed format. The unit must adopt reasonable opinions relating to the project's environmental impact and have the report revised accordingly, and must prepare a public participation explanation covering the process, scope and content of participation, the collection and analysis of opinions, and which opinions were adopted — or not adopted, with the reasons and how that was fed back to the public. The ministry issued the format for that explanation and the public opinion form as companion documents. Asking to see the explanation, and checking your own submitted opinion against it, is the most direct test of whether participation happened. Read this with the judicial appraisal institutions, the pollution complaint channels, the environmental information disclosure and the entrusted conservation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 舆论监督 — the environmental law's own duty on news media, and the failures it lists as actionable against officials
trackers.desc: The environmental law itself puts a duty on news media. Article 9 of the environmental protection law as revised in 2014 provides that governments at all levels shall strengthen publicity and popularisation of environmental protection, encouraging grassroots self-governing organisations, social organisations and environmental volunteers to publicise environmental laws and knowledge; that education authorities and schools shall include environmental knowledge in teaching; and that news media shall carry out publicity of environmental protection laws and knowledge and conduct public opinion supervision of environmental violations. A community approaching an outlet is therefore not asking for a favour outside the system: scrutiny of environmental violations is a function the statute assigns to the press. The law also lists what officials can be held to have done wrong. The same statute enumerates the failures for which responsible officials face sanction, and the list is the most useful part of it for anyone framing a complaint or a story: granting an administrative licence contrary to the conditions; shielding environmental violations; failing to order a business to suspend or close where the law requires it; failing to investigate promptly on discovery or on receiving a report of excessive discharge, discharge by means evading supervision, environmental accidents or ecological destruction from unimplemented protection measures; unlawfully sealing or seizing an operator's facilities and equipment; falsifying monitoring data or directing others to do so; failing to disclose environmental information that must be disclosed; and diverting collected discharge fees. Each of those is a specific, checkable allegation rather than a general complaint about a project. Two of them are the ones that matter most on the ground. Failure to investigate after a report has been received turns a community's own complaint into the evidence of the official failure; and failure to disclose information that must be disclosed connects directly to the disclosure duties recorded elsewhere in this country's entries. Both are the kind of specific, documented lapse that gives a newsroom something it can stand behind. How to use it. File the complaint first and keep the receipt, request the information and keep the refusal, then take the pair to an outlet: the story is no longer that a project is unwelcome but that a named duty was not performed. Read this with the assessment participation measures, the judicial appraisal institutions, the pollution complaint channels and the environmental information disclosure entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 举报奖励 — rewards for reporting environmental violations, insider reporting encouraged, and confidentiality rules for the reporter
trackers.desc: Reporting an environmental violation is a rewarded act, and insiders are named as the people to do it. The ecology ministry issued guidance in April 2020 directing provinces and cities to build and operate reward systems for reports of environmental violations, requiring provincial and prefecture-level departments to have such systems in place by the end of that year. The guidance encourages reporting under the reporter's real name and, in terms, encourages reporting by people inside the enterprise who know what is happening. Where a report is verified and the reporter qualifies, a reward is to be given unless the reporter expressly refuses it. The department that pays is generally the one that made the penalty decision, in principle at prefecture level. Confidentiality is written into the guidance and into local rules. The guidance specifically stresses protection of the reporter: localities are to strengthen responsibility and confidentiality awareness, collect less unnecessary personal information, keep the reporter's personal information strictly confidential, and pay the reward in a way that protects them. Municipal implementing measures published since go further — one requires strict confidentiality through acceptance, verification and investigation, forbids disclosure of the reporter's name, contact details, identity information or the content of the report without their written consent, and provides that units and individuals who leak that information or retaliate against the reporter will be dealt with seriously. Read the local measures, not only the national guidance: the operative confidentiality rule is the municipal one. The amounts are real and published. Ministry case bulletins record provincial schemes paying set ranges — one province from one thousand to twenty thousand yuan by severity, another operating a provincial online platform handling acceptance, registration, verification and payment electronically with rewards from one thousand up to five hundred thousand yuan — and record nationwide totals of nearly fourteen thousand rewarded cases in a single year. Heavy rewards are envisaged where a report prevents a major violation, removes a major safety hazard, or assists in investigating a serious case. What is excluded, and the risk of getting it wrong. Municipal measures list situations attracting no reward: an unclear target, unclear facts or clues too vague to check; a violation already accepted by an authority or exposed in the media before the report; a reporter who deliberately committed the violation or fabricated materials; and serving staff of the environmental system. Fabricating facts, malicious reporting or false accusation attracts legal liability. Report what can be checked, name the target and the conduct, and keep the submission record. Read this with the pollution complaint channels, the central inspection team, the judicial appraisal institutions and the assessment participation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 公开募捐 — only a qualified charity may appeal to the public, the ten-day filing, and the designated internet platforms
trackers.desc: A community group cannot appeal to the public on its own — it must act with a qualified charity. The public fundraising management measures, published in the state gazette, provide that a charitable organisation holding public fundraising qualification may cooperate with an organisation or individual that does not hold it, provided the activity is for charitable purposes and the qualified organisation bears the corresponding legal responsibility; a non-qualified partner may not conduct public fundraising by itself in any form. So the practical route for a village or a residents' group is a partnership agreement with a registered charity that holds the qualification, with the charity carrying the compliance burden. Ten days before, the plan is filed. The measures require the fundraising plan to be filed with the civil affairs department where the charity is registered at least ten days before the activity starts; where the activity runs outside that department's jurisdiction, a further filing is required ten days ahead with the county-level or higher civil affairs department where it takes place, submitting the plan, a copy of the qualification certificate and an explanation of why it is genuinely necessary to fundraise locally. Guidance records that a plan covers the purpose, start and end dates and area, the person responsible and office address, how donations are accepted, the bank account, the beneficiaries, the use of funds raised, the fundraising costs and the treatment of any surplus. For emergencies, the law allows the filing to be completed within ten days after the activity begins. Internet appeals must run on designated platforms. The measures provide that a charitable organisation fundraising through the internet must do so on an internet public fundraising service platform designated by the central civil affairs department, and may simultaneously publish the information on its own portal website, official microblog, official messaging account and mobile client; the activity name and other information published must remain consistent with the filed plan and may not be changed at will. What must be displayed, and what the media must check. At the fundraising site or prominently on the activity's carrier, the organisation must publish its name, the public fundraising qualification certificate, the plan, contact details and how to look up fundraising information; it must keep an information file with a detailed ledger of receipts and vouchers for inspection by authorities and donors. Separate platform service measures require broadcasters, publishers, network service providers and telecoms operators to verify the registration and qualification certificates before providing platform services, and prohibit them from accepting donated property on the charity's behalf. Read this with the reporting rewards, the entrusted reserve management, the judicial appraisal institutions and the judgment documents entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 矿业权人勘查开采信息公示 — every licence holder files annual information publicly, and the abnormal list is the pressure point
trackers.desc: Every holder of an exploration or mining licence must file annual information and publish it to society. The public disclosure measures for mining rights holders' exploration and extraction information, made under the mineral resources legislation and the enterprise information disclosure regulation, require that anyone holding a mineral exploration permit or a mining permit fills in annual information on mineral exploration and extraction and publishes it as required, filing between 1 January and 31 March each year for the previous year, with errors correctable during the filing period and both the original and corrected information published. A mining right created less than six months before year end joins the following year's cycle. The stated purposes include strengthening credit constraints, improving supervision and expanding social oversight — the last of which is what a community is exercising when it reads the filing. Where to read it. The ministry and provincial natural resources departments carry a dedicated column for the disclosure system on their portals, and holders file through the provincial portal for the place where the exploration project or mine is located. Administrative penalty information about a holder, and management information on the abnormal list and the serious violation list, are entered and published by the department that made the decision. Information that cannot be published for confidentiality reasons is reported directly to the provincial department instead. Random inspection is built in, and results are made public. Departments draw a proportion of exploration projects and mines by random lot to check the published information, with the ministry managing national spot checks and provinces organising their own. A ministry notice records that provinces must determine and publish the random inspection list by the end of April, that any mining right already on the abnormal list must be checked on the ground at least once, that inspectors are selected at random, complete a verification form and publish the results promptly, and that clues to illegality found during verification are transferred to the responsible section. The consequences are concrete. The same notice records that the abnormal list and serious violation list are to be brought into local government credit platforms, that credit status is to be consulted in natural resources administration and in the allocation and use of government funds, and that a holder on the serious violation list is not to be granted approval and registration of a new exploration or mining right. Ministry practice records removal decisions from the abnormal list being published for a five working day comment period, during which anyone may report orally or in writing that the conditions for removal are not met. That comment window is a direct point of entry. Read this with the procuratorate public interest litigation, the reporting rewards, the judgment database and the property registration search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 文物保护法 2024 — survey before land is transferred, twenty-four hours to reach a find, and seven days for a decision
trackers.desc: Anyone who finds a relic during construction or farming can start a clock that the authority must keep. The cultural relics protection legislation as revised in 2024 provides that where any unit or individual discovers a relic or a suspected relic in construction work, agricultural production or other activity, they shall protect the scene and immediately report to the local cultural relics administrative department; that the department shall reach the scene within twenty-four hours of receiving the report and put forward handling opinions within seven days; that it shall take measures to protect the scene and may where necessary notify the public security organs or maritime enforcement authority to assist; and that where an important relic is found it shall be reported immediately to the national department, which shall give handling opinions within fifteen days. Those three periods are the ones to note in writing when making the report. Survey comes before the land is transferred, not after the digger arrives. The Act provides that in areas where underground relics may exist, before a local government at or above county level transfers or allocates land, the provincial cultural relics department shall arrange for a qualified archaeological unit to carry out survey and exploration; and that the areas where underground relics may exist are delimited and dynamically adjusted by that department. Where a large-scale basic construction project, or a project inside the protection scope or construction control zone of a protected unit, has not had that survey done, the construction unit must first apply for it. Commentary records this as the survey-before-construction and archaeology-before-transfer system introduced by the revision, alongside new regimes for underground relic burial areas and underwater relic protection areas. Ask whether the survey was done before the land changed hands. Who pays, and what happens if relics are found. The Act provides that the costs of archaeological survey, exploration and excavation needed for basic and production construction are included in the construction project budget by the construction unit, with governments able to support the work; and that where relics are found in survey or exploration, the provincial department and the construction unit jointly agree protection measures, important discoveries going to the national department, with a procedure for handling losses caused to the construction unit by stoppage or delay. Named offences, and a pollution provision. The Act lists among violations proceeding without approved on-site protection measures for an immovable relic, unauthorised relocation or demolition, unauthorised repair obviously changing the original state, rebuilding on the original site without authority, working without a relic conservation qualification certificate, and carrying out a large project or work inside a protection scope or control zone without the lawful archaeological survey — with fines calculated on unlawful gains. It also provides that building facilities that pollute a protected unit and its environment inside the protection scope or construction control zone is punished by the ecology and environment authorities. Read this with the mining rights disclosure, the procuratorate public interest litigation, the reporting rewards and the judgment database entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 古树名木保护条例 2025 — protection zones drawn round each tree and fed into the planning system, in-place protection as the rule, and fines per tree
trackers.desc: A protection zone is drawn around each listed tree and put into the land planning system. The 2025 state council regulation, published in the gazette, provides that authorities at or above county level shall establish an archive for each old or famous tree, set up protection markers, build protective facilities and take protective measures; that the county government shall delineate the tree's protection zone and publish it according to law; and that once delineated the protection zone shall be promptly incorporated into the territorial spatial planning implementation supervision information system. A tree that has been listed therefore carries a mapped exclusion that a project must plan around, not merely a plaque. In-place protection is the rule, and moving one requires a two-stage approval. Published official explanation records that old and famous trees are in principle protected in place and may not be transplanted; that where transplanting is genuinely necessary in listed circumstances the construction unit must submit an application with transplanting and maintenance plans; and that it must be reviewed by the department at or above county level that recognised the tree — according to the highest protection grade involved — and reported to that level of government for approval. Ask which grade the tree carries and who approved any move. The grades, and what a breach costs per tree. The same explanation records grading by age: first-grade protection above five hundred years, second grade three hundred to five hundred, third grade one hundred to three hundred; that provinces may raise city trees a grade; and that all famous trees receive first-grade protection regardless of age. The regulation provides that on a breach of the relevant article the department shall order the unlawful conduct stopped, order restoration or other remedial measures within a time limit and confiscate unlawful gains, with fines calculated per tree — the highest band for first-grade trees and famous trees, lower bands for second and third grade — and that compensation, public security penalties or criminal liability follow where applicable. Those are numbers a report can quote. Two more things worth knowing. The regulation provides that where public interests such as ecological protection damage the lawful rights of a tree's rights-holder, the government at or above county level shall compensate, and may take measures to reasonably accommodate the interests of units and individuals where collectively or privately owned trees are involved; and that where a listed tree dies, the recognising department organises confirmation, investigates the cause and reports handling opinions. Officials also record city practice: full satellite positioning of every tree with a matching code, plaques on all registered trees, and instrument-based health assessment. Read this with the immovable cultural relics entry, the reporting rewards, the public interest litigation and the relics protection law entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 渔业法 — underwater blasting and construction must be negotiated with the fisheries authority beforehand, damages ordered where resources are lost, and the priority rules for aquaculture certificates
trackers.desc: Underwater blasting, survey and construction work has to be settled with the fisheries authority in advance. The fisheries legislation provides that where underwater blasting, prospecting or construction operations will seriously affect fishery resources, the operating unit shall consult in advance with the fisheries administrative authority at or above county level and take measures to prevent or reduce harm to fishery resources; and where losses to fishery resources are caused, the relevant government at or above county level shall order compensation. For a bridge, dredging, cable or reclamation project in fishing water, that is both a step the project must have taken and an order a community can ask the government to make. Reclamation of lakes is banned, and coastal flats need approval. The Act provides that reclaiming lakes for farmland is prohibited; that coastal tidal flats may not be reclaimed without the approval of a government at or above county level; and that important seed bases and aquaculture sites may not be reclaimed at all. Establishing that a stretch of flats is an important seed base or farming site therefore changes the answer outright. The certificate has priority rules that favour people who live from the water. The revised Act provides that units and individuals using state-owned waters and flats for aquaculture apply to the county-level fisheries authority, which issues an aquaculture certificate fixing a reasonable term; and that in issuing certificates the government shall give priority to local fishery producers who take aquaculture on waters or flats as their main source of livelihood, who have converted from capture fishing under industry restructuring, or who need alternative waters because the aquaculture waters plan has been adjusted. Collectively owned waters and flats may be contracted to individuals or units for aquaculture. Withdrawal of a certificate is compensable, and the environment duties run both ways. The Act provides that where a local government at or above county level varies or withdraws an aquaculture certificate for public interest and thereby causes property loss, it shall give fair and reasonable compensation, expropriation of collectively owned waters and flats following the land administration legislation; that governments shall protect and improve the ecological environment of fishery waters and prevent pollution, with supervision and investigation of fishery pollution accidents under the marine environment and water pollution statutes; and that aquaculture operators must not cause environmental pollution or ecological damage, with discharge of farming tail water meeting pollutant discharge standards. Read this with the pollution reporting hotline, the assessment publicity, the protected trees regulation and the heritage survey entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 野生动物保护法 — named project types must route around protected areas and important habitats, the wildlife authority must be consulted on the assessment, and passages or fish ways where avoidance is impossible
trackers.desc: The Act names the project types that must avoid protected areas and important wildlife habitats. The 2022 revision provides that the siting and routing of construction projects — airports, railways, roads, waterways, water conservancy and hydropower, wind power, photovoltaics, cofferdams and sea reclamation — shall avoid nature reserves and other important wildlife habitats and migration and spawning corridors; and that where avoidance is genuinely impossible, measures such as building wildlife passages and fish passage facilities shall be taken to eliminate or reduce the adverse effects on wildlife. Where one of those project types is proposed, that list is the first sentence to quote. The wildlife authority must be consulted before the assessment is approved. The Act provides that where a construction project may affect a protected area, another important wildlife habitat or a migration corridor, the department approving the environmental impact assessment documents shall seek the opinion of the wildlife protection authority — the national department where nationally protected wildlife is involved, the provincial department where locally protected wildlife is involved. Asking whether that opinion was sought, and what it said, is a documentary question about an approval already granted. Corridors have their own published boundaries. The Act provides that during migration and spawning, hunting is prohibited within migration corridors outside the protected areas and other activities obstructing wildlife breeding are strictly limited, and that the county-level government or its wildlife authority shall prescribe and publish the extent of those corridors and the content of the obstructing activities. Published commentary records that provincial and higher governments are to incorporate important wildlife habitats into national parks, nature reserves and other protected areas. The lists are revised on a cycle, and the hunting rules run through named certificates. Published legal analysis records that protection covers wildlife on the national key protected list, the list of terrestrial wildlife of important ecological, scientific and social value, and local key protected lists, with those lists adjusted every five years on assessment, or sooner where protection needs require; that hunting nationally protected wildlife is prohibited save under a special hunting licence from the national or provincial authority; that taking listed terrestrial species needs a hunting licence from a county-level or higher authority subject to quota; and that hunters must keep to the species, number, place, tools, methods and period stated and file a report of the hunt with the issuing authority afterwards. Read this with the fisheries law, the protected trees regulation, the pollution reporting hotline and the assessment publicity entries already recorded for this country.
