trackers.name: 环境民事公益诉讼 — the two qualifications a social organisation needs to sue, the presumption against a defendant who withholds its emission data, and the court's duty to collect evidence
trackers.desc: A registered social organisation can sue over pollution or ecological destruction, on two stated qualifications. The environmental legislation provides that a social organisation may bring such an action where it is registered with the civil affairs department of a government at or above the level of a city divided into districts, and has been specially engaged in environmental protection public interest activities continuously for five years or more with no record of unlawful conduct; that where it meets those conditions the court shall accept the case; and that the organisation must not seek economic benefit through the litigation. The supreme court's interpretation records that social groups, private non-enterprise units and foundations so registered qualify; that an organisation whose charter purpose is protecting the public interest and which carries out environmental public interest activities meets the test, provided the public interest at issue is related to its purpose and scope of business; and that no administrative or criminal penalty for unlawful business activity in the previous five years satisfies the clean-record requirement. The evidential rules favour the plaintiff on the defendant's own data. The interpretation provides that where a plaintiff asks the defendant to produce the names of its main pollutants, discharge method, concentration and total volume, any excess discharges and the construction and operation of its pollution control facilities, and law or regulation requires the defendant to hold that information or there is evidence it holds it but refuses to produce it, the court may presume the plaintiff's assertion on those facts to be established; and that the court shall itself investigate and collect evidence it considers necessary. Those are the two provisions that make a case winnable without the plaintiff owning a laboratory. Support from other bodies is provided for, and the case is notified to the regulator. The interpretation provides that procuratorates, departments with environmental supervision duties, other organs, social organisations and enterprises may support a social organisation's action by giving legal advice, submitting written opinions and assisting with investigation and evidence gathering; and that within ten days of accepting the case the court shall notify the department responsible for supervising the defendant. First-instance cases go to an intermediate or higher court where the conduct occurred, where the harm resulted, or where the defendant is domiciled. Read this with the judgment database, the pollution reporting hotline, the assessment publicity and the wildlife project avoidance entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 排污许可证管理信息平台 — the public end where any discharge permit can be looked up, the emission information the holder must publish itself, and the five-year ledger it must keep
trackers.desc: The permit platform has a public end, and it is searchable by anyone. A district government's guidance records that the national discharge permit management information platform's public end can be used to look up the permit information of permit-holding units and of registered discharging units, giving the direct address, and records the separate enterprise end where holders file. A national service portal carries the same lookup as a national discharge permit public information query, provided by the environment ministry, searchable by province, prefecture and industry category. Where a plant is discharging near a community, its permit is a public document that can be pulled up by name. The holder must publish its own emission information on that platform. A municipal bureau's compliance guide records that a discharging unit must, in accordance with the information disclosure provisions of its permit's duplicate copy, truthfully publish its pollutant discharge information on the platform, and that this must include the types of pollutants discharged, their concentrations and quantities, the construction and operation of pollution control facilities, the permit implementation report and self-monitoring data; and that where water pollutants enter the municipal drainage network, it must also include the location and manner of that connection. That is a self-published record a community can check against its own observations. Exceedances must be recorded and reported, and count toward the total. The same guide records that on finding discharges exceeding the standard or other abnormal conditions, the unit must immediately take measures to eliminate or reduce the harm, record it truthfully in the environmental management ledger, and report to the environmental authority with an explanation; and that pollutant discharges under such abnormal conditions are counted into the unit's discharge quantity. It records the ledger being kept in both electronic and paper form for not less than five years, on the platform's own template. What the platform covers, and its known weaknesses. Published description records the platform divided into public, enterprise and management ends; records permitted totals for air and water able to be filed month by month, and functions for noise and solid waste applications; and records candidly that the public end has suffered page access failures and enforcement report pages not displaying data, with provinces reporting saving failures and delayed data. Read this with the public interest litigation entry, the pollution reporting hotline, the assessment publicity and the judgment database entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 中华保护地 (CCAfa) — a non-state protected-area network a volunteer team or community can apply to join, with published construction and assessment rules, and boundaries that move with the species
trackers.desc: A foundation runs a protected-area system outside the state reserve network, and communities can apply into it. Published material records the foundation launching the system in April 2016 to follow biodiversity and environmental protection quickly, effectively and dynamically, covering natural species resources, ecological environment and cultural relics, and to make up for problems in the existing national park system it names as vertical modularity, large funding requirements and operational difficulty; and records it encouraging and supporting volunteers, non-governmental organisations, relevant institutions and communities to join. Other published description records the system as gathering non-governmental environmental organisations, local government bodies and research institutions, focused on endangered species and habitat protection, complementing the national park and nature reserve systems from outside them. The defining feature is that the boundary is not fixed by survey. The same material records the core characteristic as a horizontal, dynamic community-people protection system centred on a particular species, whose scope is not bound by reserve boundary demarcation and approval, and can change with the species' migration routes and habitat shifts. For a community whose case is about an animal that moves, that is a protection route that moves with it. The application route is documented by example. Published material records an individual submitting an application to establish a named protected area for a local pig breed, the application passing review and the foundation's research office undertaking to support the protected area's construction; records another established by ceremony with a forestry administration; and records an annual declaration round for exemplary protected area public-welfare projects, open to any protected area or volunteer team working on construction, biodiversity, green development or volunteer service. The foundation's own site carries the system's pages and a published standardised construction and management assessment method, and records it formally approving an individual protected area application by name. The scale and subjects are recorded, and the counts differ by date. Published material records more than 130 protected areas by late 2019, more than 140 by end-2019, more than 160 in a later account across more than thirty provinces and regions, and 224 by the end of 2024; recorded subjects include dark night skies, ancient trees, cultural relics, desert wetlands, corals, dolphins and seals, with two dark-sky sites entered into an international dark-sky listing. Read this with the public interest litigation entry, the environmental information platform, the wildlife protection law and the nature reserve entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 污染受害者法律帮助中心 — a university-based centre with a free hotline for pollution victims, lawyers advanced for major or poor cases, and litigation and appraisal fees paid up front
trackers.desc: Caution on currency: much of the centre's published record dates from earlier years, so check whether the hotline is still staffed before relying on it. A free hotline exists for pollution victims, and its usage was counted. Published description records the centre, established in October 1998 at a law university and recorded with the justice ministry, as providing free environmental legal consultation to the public by hotline telephone, receiving visitors and replying to letters; and records that from the hotline's opening in November 1999 to December 2006 it answered 9,482 consultation calls from across the country, received 512 visits and replied to 332 letters, with callers coming from almost every province and region. Published material gives the centre's street address, office and hotline numbers and email. That is a phone number for a person whose water or air has been damaged. It pays the costs that stop a case, not just the advice. The same description records that for major and typical environmental cases, and cases where the party is especially poor, the centre provides lawyer representation and advances part or all of the litigation fees and appraisal fees to help pollution victims defend their lawful environmental rights. Appraisal fees are the expense that defeats most pollution claims, and this is a body that fronts them. It trains the people who will handle the case. The centre records providing free practical legal training to lawyers, judges, environmental officials and members of environmental organisations, to improve their ability to handle environmental cases, enforce environmental law strictly and participate in environmental management; and records its wider work as research, international exchange and popularising environmental law knowledge to raise public environmental legal awareness. Its case record shows what it supports. The centre's own pages record legal assistance to a named fish pond water pollution case, a case in which 68 village households sued a copper company over air pollution, mobile environmental rights consultation activities in central and western regions, recruitment of environmental public interest trainee lawyers, and its role supporting an organisation's air pollution public interest suit against a chemical company. Read this with the public interest litigation entry, the environmental organisations, the permit platform and the protected area network entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: IPE 蔚蓝地图 — a public database of enterprise environmental supervision records, penalties and complaints, built from thirty-one provinces' and hundreds of cities' published data
trackers.desc: The regulator's record on a specific company is searchable in one place. The centre records itself as a public interest environmental research institution registered in the capital, founded in June 2006, which collects, organises and analyses environmental information published by government and enterprises and runs a database and map platform. It records the database as comprehensively collecting environmental quality, emissions and pollution source supervision records published by the governments of 31 provinces and hundreds of prefecture-level cities, together with enterprise disclosures made compulsorily or voluntarily under regulations and corporate responsibility requirements. Its data description lists the record types held, including environmental supervision records, environmental administrative penalties, environmental complaints and reports, orders for rectification within a time limit, enterprise responses, key regulated units, supervisory monitoring of discharging units, enterprise carbon emissions data and listed company environmental disclosure, drawn from named authorities across environment, emergency management, maritime, urban management, water, industry, development, natural resources, housing, meteorology, transport, market regulation and financial regulation. For a community that has been told a plant is compliant, the penalty record is the check. Its history shows what such a database does to a company. Published description records the centre compiling the country's first public interest water pollution database in June 2006, listing more than 2,500 polluting enterprises, then an air pollution map naming close to 5,000; forming a green choice alliance with other environmental organisations in 2007 to expose pollution in supply chains; and publishing with a foreign organisation a pollution information transparency index rating cities' disclosure of pollution source supervision information. It records a mobile application released in June 2014 giving real-time air quality from more than 2,000 stations in over 390 cities and water quality from more than 7,000 monitoring sections. The removal route is also documented, which matters both ways. Published material records a mechanism by which an enterprise may address a supervision record through information disclosure or a third-party audit — so a community should check whether a record has been cleared as well as whether it exists. Read this with the pollution victims' legal centre, the public interest litigation, the environmental information platform and the ratings entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 中华环保联合会法律中心 — a national federation's legal centre with a published direct line and room number, whose stated job is bringing environmental public interest suits and pollution supervision
trackers.desc: A national federation runs a legal centre whose stated duties include bringing public interest suits, and it publishes a direct telephone number. The federation records the centre as responsible for publicity, education and training on environmental rights defence and for research on environmental law theory and policy recommendations, and for organising environmental public interest litigation, pollution supervision and other environmental rights-defence practice, so as to protect the environmental rights and interests of the public and society. It publishes the centre's own telephone number and its room and floor in a named building, alongside the federation's main telephone, fax and street address. For a community whose complaint has stalled with a local bureau, a national body whose written remit is organising public interest litigation and pollution supervision is a different door. Its identity is verifiable in the public registers. A national standards body's register of social organisations records the federation with its unified social credit code, legal representative and organisation grade, and records counts of the standards it has issued. That is how a community checks that the body it is writing to is the registered national federation and not a similarly named one. The federation is one of two national bodies with the standing that matters, and the other is a grant-making foundation. The environmental protection foundation — a separate national body — publishes its founder and named vice-chairs, and is the counterpart on the funding side rather than the litigation side. Read this with the public interest litigation entry, the pollution victims' legal centre, the enterprise records database and the environmental complaints entries already recorded for this country, and note the standing rules recorded there: only organisations meeting the statutory conditions may bring these suits, which is why the identity check above matters before a community relies on any organisation offering to sue on its behalf.

trackers.name: 创绿家 — startup grants for brand-new environmental groups, the counts of teams funded, and the civil society directory where organisations, jobs and funding calls are listed
trackers.desc: A grant exists specifically for environmental groups that have just formed. Published material records the programme as launched by a named foundation in 2012, specifically to support environmental public interest teams in their start-up period, aiming to discover and cultivate new forces in the environmental public interest field and help founders who care about the environment and their home places get through the start-up stage more successfully, so the sector becomes healthier and more diverse. It records the foundation as having introduced the idea of angel funding into the environmental field. For a village group that has just formed, most grant schemes are closed; this one is built for exactly that stage. The counts are published and they differ by date, which shows the growth. One account records the programme, after six rounds, as having supported 150 environmental public interest start-up teams with more than 15 million yuan, spread across 28 provinces and cities, working on pollution prevention, biodiversity protection and waste sorting; an earlier account records 90 teams and 10.27 million yuan; and a later one records that by the end of 2022 the programme had funded 511 start-up environmental organisations with more than 43.22 million yuan. It records a companion programme supporting organisations beyond the start-up stage. The foundation behind it publishes its own scale. Published description records it established in 2008 by a named ecological association, dedicated to funding and supporting the growth of civil environmental public interest organisations, upgraded in 2014 to a foundation permitted to raise funds publicly, and records it as having directly or indirectly supported the work of more than 900 civil environmental organisations or individuals. The directory carrying all this is itself the resource. The civil society brief that publishes these records also carries organisation profiles, job listings and funding-call listings for the sector — which is where a new group looks for the next round, the next hire and the organisations already working on its issue. Read this with the entrepreneurs' foundation entry, the protected area network, the public interest litigation and the pollution victims' centre entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 山水自然保护中心 — conservation agreements signed between a village and a nature reserve, community patrol teams with published patrol counts, and field stations in eleven named places
trackers.desc: A village and a nature reserve can sign a conservation agreement, and the case that started it is documented. Published description records a village nearest the natural resources that had been a natural protector but, unable to benefit from protecting the environment, turned to short-term gain, with heavy logging that damaged the local environment and steadily lowered the quality of the tea that was its main livelihood. It records the organisation running multiple rounds of negotiation in the village and supporting the reserve and the village to sign a conservation agreement, under which the reserve authorised the village to patrol and protect the hills and checked the results periodically, with funding and policy help to raise livelihoods; and records forest destruction dropping sharply, the village's farmer patrol team winning a conservation award, and the agreement approach being run in 17 villages like it. That is a signed instrument between a community and a protected area, not a consultation. The patrol work is counted. Published material records that in one year it supported community conserved areas' patrol and monitoring across 9 communities, with effectively protected area totalling over 450 square kilometres, 683 person-times of forest patrol and 1,333 river patrols; records support for eco-friendly industries including bees, tea, medicinal fruit, nature education and ecological experience, with community benefit of a stated sum; and records five human-wildlife conflict defence pilots and compensation reaching over ten households. It is registered, and its field stations are published. It records itself established in 2007, registered with a district civil affairs bureau with a named supervising authority, focused on species and habitat protection and working hand in hand with local communities, with systematic research based on citizen science. Its recruitment page lists eleven offices and field stations, including ones in a township and a village committee building. Read this with the entrusted reserve management entry, the protected area network, the ecological compensation payments and the enterprise records entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The daily incinerator emissions platform and a city volunteer association — five pollutants and furnace temperature published every day per plant, and a municipal association that monitors the plant beside it
trackers.desc: Every waste incineration power plant publishes yesterday's emissions, plant by plant, every day. The platform records that, under named environmental legislation and a specific regulation on automatic monitoring data at these plants, since 2 January 2020 the previous day's daily averages for five pollutants — particulates, nitrogen oxides, sulphur dioxide, carbon monoxide and hydrogen chloride — together with the furnace temperature curve and related data marks, are published daily. It records that the plant is the responsible subject for the disclosure and is responsible for the truthfulness, accuracy, completeness and validity of the automatic monitoring data it publishes, and that under a marking rule manual marking of the previous day's data must be completed before noon each day, failing which the operator is deemed to have no objection to the validity of the automatic monitoring data. For a neighbourhood beside an incinerator, a daily per-plant series with the operator on the hook for its accuracy is the strongest routine data in this file. A municipal volunteer association works the same subject at city level. A city environmental protection volunteers' association publishes a telephone number, an email address, microblog and messaging accounts, and a full street address including district, road, building, unit and room. Its published material records that burning plastics also emits some new pollutants that are not yet well regulated, so the environmental and health risks brought by waste incineration plants still cannot be ignored, and that monitoring of ambient environmental quality around the plants still faces many difficulties, needing more attention from the environmental authorities and the enterprises to reduce the plants' effect on surrounding environmental quality. The city's own bureau publishes the enforcement and complaint route. The municipal ecology and environment bureau records its enforcement detachment as exercising administrative punishment powers for pollution prevention, ecological protection and nuclear and radiation safety across the city, including enforcement over construction projects' compliance and automatic monitoring equipment operation, and as responsible for accepting, transferring, supervising and investigating the city's environmental complaint letters and visits and for coordinating the resolution of larger and cross-district pollution disputes; its address and telephone are published. Read this with the enterprise records database, the pollution victims' centre, the community conservation agreements and the public interest litigation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 村务监督委员会 — the village supervision committee residents elect to audit the village's own accounts, who is barred from sitting on it, and the annual review that can end a village official's term
trackers.desc: Villagers elect a small committee whose job is auditing the village's own money and land decisions. A provincial implementing measure records that a village shall establish a village affairs supervision committee responsible for democratic financial management and for supervising the implementation of village affairs disclosure, accountable to the villagers' assembly and the villagers' representative assembly. It records the committee's duties as including supervising democratic decision-making on village-level affairs; supervising the exercise of powers by villagers' committee members; democratic supervision of the items, content, timing, procedure and form of village affairs disclosure; participating in reviewing the collective's financial plans and financial management systems; auditing accounts; and, when entrusted by villagers, examining and auditing collective financial accounts the villagers have questioned and requiring the persons concerned to explain. For a village whose land compensation or contract terms are in doubt, that audit-on-request is the closest internal check available. Who may not sit on it is spelled out. The same measure records the committee as three to five members including a chair, elected by the villagers' assembly or representative assembly from villagers with voting rights, and required to include people with accounting and management knowledge, serving the same term as the villagers' committee; and bars villagers' committee members and their spouses, parents, children, siblings, grandparents and grandchildren from membership. National guidance adds that the village accountant, the village clerk and the head of the village collective economic organisation may not serve, and that no organisation or individual may designate or appoint members. Its powers are listed as five named rights. National guidance records the committee and its members as holding the right to be informed, by attending villagers' committee, small group, representative and joint meetings; the right to question village affairs and financial matters villagers feel strongly about and require explanation; the right to audit; the right to make recommendations, including to the township party committee and government where necessary; and the right to preside over democratic review. It records that a villagers' committee member rated unsatisfactory in two consecutive reviews has their post terminated, and that meetings are held at least quarterly. Read this with the community conservation agreements, the incinerator data platform, the enterprise records database and the city bureau entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Township justice offices and the village legal adviser — public legal service stations in every township, a one-office-six-stations layout, and an adviser whose brief names land acquisition and environmental disputes
trackers.desc: The township justice office is the base for public legal services, and the counts are published. A ministry record describes one province as having established, on the base of township justice offices, 2,460 township or street public legal service stations, and, on the base of village and community people's mediation committees, 51,700 village or community public legal service rooms. It describes the offices' one office, six stations layout as comprising a legal aid work station, a notarisation assistance point, an arbitration liaison point, an administrative reconsideration consultation point, an administrative enforcement opinion collection point and a legislative opinion collection point, to provide convenient and inclusive public legal services. It records that in nine months of one year the province's justice offices answered more than 250,000 public legal consultations, accepted 4,290 first-instance legal aid applications and guided 5,959 notarisation matters, and records 2,578 township mediation committees and 51,700 village committees with 54,100 full-time and part-time mediators, with 518,100 disputes investigated and resolved to that date. For a village, the nearest legal counter is in its own township. The village legal adviser's brief names land acquisition and environmental disputes. A city justice bureau records the adviser's duties as including providing legal consultation and legal aid, answering legal questions arising in daily production and life, and providing necessary legal help to those meeting legal aid conditions; accepting commissions to draft and revise legal documents and, from village or residents' committees or the public, to take part in litigation, with fees reduced or waived as appropriate; and taking part in people's mediation at the invitation of grassroots mediation organisations, providing legal opinions on disputes arising from medical matters, traffic accidents, land acquisition and demolition, labour and capital, and environmental protection, with rural and less developed areas named as the programme's priority. One district shows how the pieces connect. A district record describes 27 township justice offices directing mediation committees into district governance centres, 2,615 mediators, and specialist committees stationed there connecting with court case-filing judges so that judicial confirmation and court-referred mediation join up. Read this with the village supervision committees, the community conservation agreements, the incinerator data platform and the city bureau entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: County and district property registration centres — an interested party's right to search the register, what counts as proof of interest, the lawyer route, and one city's four service halls with telephone numbers
trackers.desc: A person with a legitimate interest — not only the owner — can search the property register. National rules record that county-level and above government registration bodies are responsible for managing registration record enquiries, that rights holders and interested parties may enquire into and copy registration records, and that they may entrust a lawyer or other agent to do so. The rules record the principles as lawfulness, convenience for the people and efficiency, and require bodies to provide necessary enquiry premises and assign dedicated staff responsible for enquiry, copying and issuing enquiry result certificates, and to improve access through internet technology, self-service enquiry terminals and enquiry ports in relevant premises. For a community trying to establish who holds a site, an interested-party search with a lawyer's help is the route the rules themselves describe. What must be produced is listed. A city registration centre's service guide records the materials as an enquiry application form stating the purpose and the interest; the applicant's identity documents; for an agent, the power of attorney and the agent's identity documents; for an interested party, materials proving the interest; and for state organs acting on duty, assistance materials and staff credentials; and records timing as same-day service, with other special cases completed within five working days and batch enquiries within a set period. Another city records that a rights holder using a self-service terminal in the registration hall need not submit those materials. The result is a document with a verification code. A municipal centre records the enquiry result as an authoritative certificate issued by the registration body reflecting the natural and property-rights status of the property, with legal effect, used for proof of title, house purchase, schooling points, mortgage lending and judicial control; and records that the result is labelled by enquirer type — including an interested party without supporting documents who is a lawyer — and carries a verification code valid for three months. One city publishes four service halls with addresses and telephone numbers. Read this with the village supervision committees, the township justice offices, the incinerator data platform and the enterprise records database entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The village collective economic organisation — the body that holds collective land, a member's right to copy the accounts, reports circulated ten days before the members' meeting, and audits by the county and township
trackers.desc: A member may read and copy the organisation's books, and the reports must circulate before the meeting. The 2024 legislation records members' rights as including attending the members' meeting or members' representative meeting under the law and the organisation's charter and voting on major matters; consulting and copying the organisation's financial and accounting reports, meeting minutes and other materials, and learning the relevant circumstances; supervising the organisation's production and management activities and the distribution and use of collective income, and putting forward opinions and suggestions; and contracting rural land let by the organisation. It records that the organisation shall prepare an annual operating report, an annual financial accounting report and an income distribution plan, and provide them to members for inspection ten days before the members' meeting or members' representative meeting is held. Ten days' notice and a right to copy the minutes is the combination that makes scrutiny possible. This is the body that actually holds the village's land. The legislation records the organisation as a regional economic organisation based on collective ownership of land which represents its members in exercising ownership, existing at township, village and group level; records that collective property is collectively owned by the members and the organisation exercises ownership on their behalf, and may not be divided among individual members; and records its functions as including letting rural land; handling homestead applications and use; rationally developing, using and protecting arable land, forest land and grassland and supervising that use; using collectively operated construction land or transferring it by sale or lease; distributing and using collective income; and distributing and using land compensation fees where collective land is requisitioned. Audit is by the county department and the township. The legislation records that the organisation shall accept audit supervision according to law, with the county-level agriculture and rural department and the township government or subdistrict office carrying out regular and special audits as circumstances require, and the state audit organs auditing the truthfulness, legality and effectiveness of its receipt and use of fiscal funds. It records that the charter must be filed with the township government or subdistrict office and the county agriculture department. Read this with the village supervision committees, the township justice offices, the property registration centres and the village conservation agreements entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Urban residents' committees under the 2025 revision — a legal person for a community of one to three thousand households, a lowered threshold for residents to convene the assembly, and disclosure that must stay up fifteen days
trackers.desc: The committee is a legal person and its chair is the legal representative. The 2025 revision of the urban residents' committee legislation records the committee as a grassroots mass self-governing organisation for residents' self-management, self-service, self-education and self-supervision, which is responsible to and reports to the residents' assembly and the residents' representative assembly; and records that it has the legal person status of a grassroots mass self-governing organisation, with the committee chair as its legal representative, and may carry out civil activities needed to perform its functions, but may not provide guarantees. It records committees as generally established within a range of one thousand to three thousand households, with the area called a community, and their establishment, abolition or resizing proposed by the subdistrict office and approved by the district or city government. For an urban neighbourhood, that is a body with legal personality at its own scale. The quorum for residents to call the assembly was deliberately lowered. The legislature's explanatory note records that, given that community sizes are now generally large, the legal number required to propose convening the residents' assembly is reduced, to make it easier for the assembly to be held, and that a representative assembly system is added; it records new provisions on the subjects, participants, forms and procedures of deliberation and consultation, and the implementation of consultation results. The legislation records consultation as taking deliberative meetings, hearings and discussion meetings, with government departments, the subdistrict office, mass organisations, social organisations, people's congress deputies, political consultative conference members and relevant professionals invited as needed. What must be published, and for how long, is stated. The legislation records a public affairs disclosure system requiring prompt publication of matters discussed and decided by the residents' assembly or representative assembly and their implementation; the management and use of government-allocated funds and accepted social donations; and the management and use of facilities owned and used by the committee; requires a disclosure board, with publication for not less than fifteen days and the committee guaranteeing the truthfulness of what it publishes; and records that where it fails to publish or publishes untruthfully, residents may report to the district or city government, its departments or the subdistrict office, which must investigate and order lawful publication. It records the committee's duties as including guiding and assisting the establishment of owners' assemblies and the election of owners' committees, and helping mediate property disputes. Read this with the village collective economic organisations, the village supervision committees, the township justice offices and the property registration centres entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: National Judicial Rulings System (سامانه ملی آرای قضایی)
trackers.desc: Judiciary Research Institute's official public database of Iranian court rulings — trial, appeal, unification-of-precedent, Supreme Court & Administrative Justice Court. · Find here: Iran's national database of court rulings — trial, appeal, unification-of-precedent and apex courts (Judiciary Research Institute).

trackers.name: Supreme Audit Court (Divan Mohasebat)
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of Iran. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Iran.

trackers.name: Sherkat – Company Registration Portal
trackers.desc: National — official company registration & public company-information search, Iran (Persian). — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Iran
trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Iran — supreme court in Iran (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Kuwait Regional Convention (ROPME) — and its Judicial Commission
trackers.desc: THE ONE BINDING ENVIRONMENTAL INSTRUMENT COVERING ALL EIGHT GULF STATES. The Kuwait Regional Convention for Cooperation on the Protection of the Marine Environment from Pollution was signed 24 April 1978 and entered into force 1 July 1979 — 30 articles, described as the basic legal instrument binding the eight States of the Region. ALL EIGHT ARE FULL PARTIES: ROPME records ‘no signatories without ratification, acceptance, approval or accession’, so unlike some regional instruments there is no signed-but-unratified state to argue about. ARTICLE II fixes the Sea Area by coordinates, from Ras Dharbat Ali (16°39'N, 53°3'30"E) to Ras Al Fasteh (25°04'N, 61°25'E) — a treaty boundary you can check a project location against. Use the term ‘ROPME Sea Area’: it was coined by the Plenipotentiaries to achieve unanimity, cooperating in spite of existing geopolitical boundaries, and it is the name all eight accepted. THE ORGAN MOST PEOPLE DO NOT KNOW EXISTS: alongside the Council and Secretariat, ROPME has a Judicial Commission, established March 1989, of 6 nationals of Member States highly qualified in international law. In a region with almost no environmental litigation route, a standing judicial commission under a ratified convention is the most significant legal fact available — though this entry does not assert that individuals may petition it; establish who may seise it first. AN EVIDENCE SOURCE THAT NEEDS NO SITE ACCESS: ROPME's scientific bodies include a Remote Sensing Unit, alongside RIIS and MEMAC. WHICH PROTOCOL FITS YOUR ISSUE: oil-spill emergency response; land-based sources of pollution — the limb for a coastal development, discharge or reclamation; and transboundary movement of hazardous wastes. Development is named as a stressor in ROPME's own statement of purpose. At stake: over 20 species of dolphin and whale, all five subtropical turtle species, and more than 1,000 fish species, most endemic.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants Programme Iran — a Tehran office, a twelve-member steering committee, and grants that go straight to community organisations
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE FIRST RESOURCE IN THIS MAP FOR IRAN THAT GIVES SOMETHING RATHER THAN MERELY RECORDS SOMETHING — every other Iranian entry here is a court or a registry. The programme maintains an office in Tehran, hosted with UNDP at Shahrzad Boulevard in Darrous, Pasdaran, and awards grants directly to community-based and non-governmental organisations rather than through government. DECISIONS ARE MADE BY A TWELVE-MEMBER NATIONAL STEERING COMMITTEE DRAWN FROM IRANIAN CIVIL SOCIETY, ACADEMIA AND GOVERNMENT AGENCIES, SERVING VOLUNTARILY, with the programme's guidelines requiring a majority of such committees to come from the non-governmental sector. That composition is the reason a community proposal can succeed here: the people assessing it are not solely officials. THE ROUTE MOST RELEVANT TO DEFENDING LAND IS THE ONE FOR COMMUNITY CONSERVED AREAS: the Iran programme has run work under the global support initiative for territories and areas conserved by Indigenous Peoples and local communities — a designation route for land that a community already manages by custom, which is precisely the situation of many Iranian pastoral and village territories. Ask about that stream specifically rather than about general environmental grants. HOW TO APPROACH IT: contact the National Coordinator first, obtain the guidelines, submit a short concept paper, and only prepare a full proposal if it passes pre-screening against the programme's criteria and the Iran Country Programme Strategy; the steering committee then accepts, rejects or returns it. Grants are paid in three instalments — on signature, on a satisfactory mid-term report, and on completion — so a group with no working capital must plan for the gap. Focal areas are biodiversity, climate change, land degradation and sustainable forest management, international waters and chemicals. THE SAFETY POINT, AND IT IS NOT A FORMALITY IN THIS COUNTRY: this map records only international instruments for Iran and names no Iranian organisation or individual, because naming them can expose them. Anyone considering an application should weigh what association with foreign-funded environmental work may mean for the people whose names appear on it, and should take current guidance from the programme office rather than from this entry. Confirm the office, the coordinator and the current call before acting; the country page reached carries material of uncertain currency. AN UNREGISTERED VILLAGE GROUP CAN BE FUNDED DIRECTLY. The programme states that, with UNOPS, it has developed Memoranda of Agreement allowing grants to community-based groups that are not formally registered, without an intermediary non-governmental organisation. For pastoral and village communities that manage land by custom rather than through a constituted association — the situation the community conserved areas stream is designed around — that removes the step most likely to be impossible. Ask about a Memorandum of Agreement rather than assuming registration is required first. National Coordinators are UN-contracted rather than government-employed, expressly to protect neutrality and objectivity in grant-making.

trackers.name: Copernicus Browser — free satellite imagery you can compare across dates, from any browser
trackers.desc: PICK YOUR AREA, PICK TWO DATES, AND SEE WHAT CHANGED. This free service lets anyone browse and download FULL-RESOLUTION imagery from the European Copernicus satellite missions, COMPARE IMAGES SIDE BY SIDE, and CREATE TIMELAPSES DIRECTLY IN THE BROWSER — which is how change over months or years becomes something you can show rather than assert. Imagery refreshes every five to ten days. THIS COUNTRY HAS TWO ENTRIES IN THIS ENTIRE MAP, AND THIS IS THE ONLY ONE THAT REQUIRES NO ORGANISATION, NO INTRODUCTION AND NO PERMISSION — a browser and a free account. Where naming a domestic body could put people at risk, a tool one person uses alone is not a convenience but the whole of what is available. WHAT IT IS ACTUALLY USED FOR, ACCORDING TO AN INVESTIGATIVE RESEARCH TOOLKIT: TRACKING CONSTRUCTION PROJECTS, MINING OPERATIONS AND LAND DEVELOPMENT, and documenting environmental degradation — with the timelapse function singled out as particularly valuable for creating visual evidence of change. A dam wall rising, a wetland shrinking, a quarry spreading, a road cut through a slope: all of them are visible from orbit on dates you choose. BEYOND PLAIN PHOTOGRAPHS IT OFFERS PROCESSED VIEWS THAT ANSWER SPECIFIC QUESTIONS: false-colour composites, a VEGETATION index for plant health and a WATER index for surface water, plus atmospheric and air quality data from a dedicated mission. A lake or marsh contracting year on year shows in the water index even when a photograph looks ambiguous. THE PRACTICAL LIMITS: a free account is currently required; resolution is moderate rather than the sub-metre imagery people expect from commercial services, so small structures may not be legible; cloud cover blocks optical images, though radar imagery from another mission in the same collection sees through it; and the interface takes some learning. AND A WARNING ABOUT OLD GUIDES: THE PREDECESSOR VIEWER WAS SHUT DOWN IN FEBRUARY 2025 and its functions moved here. Any tutorial, bookmark or training material naming the older tool is pointing at a dead service.

trackers.name: Digital Security Helpline — emergency help when devices or accounts are compromised
trackers.desc: IT IS FREE, IT RUNS AROUND THE CLOCK, AND IT ANSWERS EVERY REQUEST WITHIN TWO HOURS. A helpline for civil society worldwide — activists, community groups, journalists and human rights defenders — with support in ten languages including RUSSIAN and ARABIC. This country has three other entries in the whole of this map, all of them tools or instruments requiring no local organisation; THIS IS THE FIRST THAT PUTS A PERSON ON THE OTHER END. IT DOES TWO DIFFERENT JOBS. Before anything happens, it walks you through ASSESSING THE RISKS YOUR WORK ACTUALLY CREATES and deciding what to secure first. Once you are under attack, it provides RAPID-RESPONSE EMERGENCY ASSISTANCE — and it helps ANALYSE, DOCUMENT AND EXPOSE advanced attacks including SPYWARE and targeted phishing. That last part is the one to remember: a technically documented intrusion becomes evidence that an international body can act on, where an unverified suspicion cannot. IT SECURES INFRASTRUCTURE, WEBSITES AND SOCIAL MEDIA ACCOUNTS, and provides guidance materials, training and referrals onward to others who can help. REACH IT BY EMAIL AT A PUBLISHED ADDRESS. It is an accredited member of a civil society computer emergency response body, and it publishes both a data usage policy and terms of service for the helpline — read them first, and think about which device and connection you use to make contact. THE LIMITS ARE IMPORTANT HERE: it handles digital security and nothing else. It will not take up an environmental case, fund anything or represent anyone, and it cannot change the conditions that make the work dangerous. Use it alongside the satellite imagery and corporate ownership tools recorded separately in this file — those are exactly the activities that draw the attention this helpline exists to defend against, and the two belong together.

trackers.name: iNaturalist — photograph what lives on the ground, and it becomes a scientific record
trackers.desc: THIS IS HOW A COMMUNITY CREATES THE SPECIES RECORD IT CANNOT FIND. Photograph a plant, animal or fungus with a free app, or record a sound; an automated system suggests what it is; a global community of naturalists then reviews it; and WHEN THEY AGREE THE OBSERVATION BECOMES RESEARCH GRADE AND IS AUTOMATICALLY SHARED WITH THE GLOBAL BIODIVERSITY DATABASE. This file recorded that database separately and warned that an under-surveyed district looks empty in it — and that a developer can cite that emptiness. THIS IS THE ANSWER TO THAT PROBLEM, and it costs nothing. OLD PHOTOGRAPHS COUNT. If you know roughly when and where a picture was taken, it is welcome — so photographs a family already has of a valley, a spring or an orchard can become dated, located species records without anyone going back into the field. AND THE PRIVACY SETTING IS THE ONE TO UNDERSTAND BEFORE YOU START: observations can be public, private, or OBSCURED — obscured randomises the location to protect sensitive species or habitats, and you can grant exact coordinates only to users you specifically trust. In a country where this file records no domestic organisation that can safely be named, publishing precise coordinates of what you are documenting, and of where you were, is a decision to take deliberately rather than by default. Use it with the digital security helpline recorded separately here. IT WORKS OFFLINE FOR CAPTURE: photographs and location are stored on the phone without a connection and uploaded when you have one. PRACTICAL POINTS THAT DECIDE WHETHER A RECORD IS USABLE: turn on location so coordinates are logged; take SEVERAL PHOTOGRAPHS FROM DIFFERENT ANGLES of a single individual, because that is what lets the community identify it to species; and add sounds where the animal is easier heard than seen. THE LIMITS. Identification depends on other people, so a rare or difficult organism may sit unidentified. Uploading needs a connection. And research-grade records are HARVESTED PERIODICALLY rather than fixed — if an identification is later contested and changed, the record can drop out of the global database. Once your observations reach research grade, download and cite them from that database, where a download carries a permanent identifier that cannot be revised away.

trackers.name: OSME Conservation Fund — small grants to nationals, three times a year, about half funded
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY HAS FIVE ENTRIES IN THIS ENTIRE MAP AND NO FUNDING ROUTE. THIS IS ONE, AND ITS CRITERIA ARE WRITTEN IN FAVOUR OF PEOPLE WHO LIVE HERE: projects should be INITIATED AND CARRIED OUT BY NATIONALS of the region, and/or engage local communities, and/or include TRAINING OF LOCAL COUNTERPARTS — while applications carrying significant international airfare costs are unlikely to be approved. A fund that discourages flying in outside experts is one that expects local people to do the work and be paid for it. THE TERMS: THREE DECISION ROUNDS A YEAR, with deadlines of 31 January, 31 May and 30 September; typical awards of one to three thousand pounds and NO STATED MAXIMUM; and a published funding rate of AROUND FIFTY PER CENT. Few funders in this payload disclose their success rate at all. WHAT IT WILL PAY FOR MATTERS MORE THAN THE SUM, BECAUSE IT INCLUDES GETTING A PLACE RECOGNISED: INVESTIGATING POTENTIAL NEW IMPORTANT BIRD AREAS or ornithologically little-known areas; strengthening the record of EXISTING important bird areas through breeding censuses and systematic counts; investigating the status of threatened species; and STUDIES OF ILLEGAL BIRD KILLING AND UNSUSTAINABLE HUNTING. This file has recorded repeatedly that a place with an internationally recognised designation is defended on different terms from a place without one, and that a community's central problem is proving its ground is not ordinary. This fund pays for exactly that proof. TWO OTHER GRANTS RUN ALONGSIDE IT: a threatened species research award of up to five thousand pounds annually, with a deadline around 1 December, and a youth fund of one to two thousand pounds for bird camps and education projects for sixteen to twenty-five year olds, LED FROM WITHIN THE REGION. The society publishes a country profile for this country, and a major international bird reference platform is now freely accessible throughout its region. THE LIMITS, AND ONE IS SPECIFIC TO HERE: it funds ornithological conservation and research only; the sums are modest; specimen collection needs justification and all necessary local authorisations; and it is a scientific society that will not oppose a project. Consider also what an international grant application discloses about you and your work — read it alongside the digital security helpline recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: ICCA Consortium — you do not need to be a registered organisation to join it
trackers.desc: ITS MEMBER ORGANISATIONS DO NOT NEED TO BE FORMALLY RECOGNISED BY STATE GOVERNMENTS. Eligible members expressly include traditional tribes, nations and peoples AND THEIR CUSTOMARY NETWORKS, ASSOCIATIONS AND FEDERATIONS, traditional local communities and their customary networks, and SELF-INITIATED GROUPINGS. This file has established across the region that the commonest barrier between a community and land, money or standing is not merit but the absence of a registered legal entity. THIS IS THE FIRST BODY RECORDED IN THIS ENTIRE MAP THAT SETS THAT BARRIER ASIDE — a village that has never registered anything can be a member in full standing. AND IT ALREADY HAS A NAME FOR WHAT YOU HAVE. The concept it works with — territories and areas conserved by Indigenous peoples and local communities, or territories of life — expressly covers systems called QOROQ and QOROQ-E BUMI, alongside himas and a dozen others from around the world. A community here is not asking to import a foreign model; the international framework already has a place for the one that exists. IT IS AN ASSOCIATION RATHER THAN AN AGENCY: an international membership organisation of Indigenous peoples, local communities and supporting organisations DOCUMENTING, SUSTAINING AND DEFENDING those territories, with over a hundred and sixty member organisations and some four hundred honorary members from eighty countries, plus regional coordinators and national focal points to approach. IT SETS OUT A ROUTE, IN ORDER: understand and strengthen your territory; communicate it; CREATE A CRITICAL MASS OF SUPPORT; REGISTER IT; and SECURE LEGAL OR POLICY RECOGNITION. That sequence is the closest thing in this payload to a plan for a community that holds land by custom and wants that holding acknowledged. THE REGISTRY IS RUN BY A UNITED NATIONS CONSERVATION MONITORING CENTRE AND SUBMISSION IS VOLUNTARY BY THE CUSTODIANS THEMSELVES, and a registered territory can be listed among the world's recognised protected and conserved areas. NOW THE CAUTION, AND IN THIS COUNTRY IT IS THE WHOLE OF THE DECISION: REGISTERING A TERRITORY MEANS PUBLISHING WHERE IT IS AND WHO LOOKS AFTER IT. This file has recorded for this country a digital security helpline and a mapping tool whose locations can be deliberately obscured; read those first, decide what to disclose and to whom, and note that the consortium's own steps put registration late in the sequence rather than first. THE OTHER LIMITS: it is not a funder and not a law practice; members must be not-for-profit and for-profit bodies are excluded; and recognition it helps pursue is granted by states, not by it.

trackers.name: Judicial Assistance Office — a free lawyer, and refusing the case is a disciplinary offence
trackers.desc: IT PROVIDES FREE REPRESENTATION AND LEGAL ADVICE TO PEOPLE WHO CANNOT PAY A LAWYER'S FEE, AND THE OBLIGATION ON LAWYERS IS NUMBERED. Every advocate must accept AT LEAST THREE ASSISTANCE CASES A YEAR referred by the bar's judicial assistance institution — A LEGAL DUTY, not a request — and a lawyer who refuses or neglects one HAS A DISCIPLINARY OFFENCE RECORDED AGAINST HIM. This country had no route to a lawyer anywhere in this map. This is one, it is old, and it has teeth. AND YOU WILL NOT BE GIVEN A TRAINEE: referral of assistance cases to trainee lawyers is PROHIBITED by the regulation. IT REACHES CIVIL MATTERS, WHICH IS THE QUESTION THAT DECIDES WHETHER IT IS ANY USE FOR LAND. Officials have said publicly that CLAIMANTS AND DEFENDANTS — not only the accused — should be able to have a lawyer, and that because judges may not gather evidence for the parties, the assistance unit exists to fill exactly that gap. A dispute over a plot, a permit or compensation is a civil matter, so ask for assistance on that basis rather than assuming the office is only for criminal defence. IT IS RUN BY THE PROFESSION, NOT BY THE STATE: the office receives NO GOVERNMENT BUDGET and is carried at the lawyers' own expense, and providing this service has been a statutory duty of the bar since 1936. In a country where this file records no domestic organisation it can safely name, a service funded by the profession rather than the treasury is a meaningful distinction. THE STRUCTURE AND WHAT TO EXPECT: the institution has a secretariat, a petitions branch and a judicial branch; it MAY INVESTIGATE YOUR APPLICATION and summon you by letter for further explanation or documents; and free legal consultation is given to callers at the office — at one recent event SEVEN HUNDRED LAWYERS provided free consultations in a single day. THE COST FALLS ONLY IF YOU WIN: where the assisted client succeeds, the lawyer collects ONE FIFTH OF THE FEE and pays it into the bar's fund, unless he proves collection is legally impossible. Nothing is due from a case that fails. THE LIMITS. It is means-tested and you must show you cannot pay. Capacity is finite — three cases per lawyer is a floor for the profession, not a promise to every applicant. The independent provincial bars run their own assistance rather than routing everything through the centre, so apply to the bar for YOUR province. And an application is a disclosure of your dispute to an institution — read this alongside the digital security helpline recorded separately for this country before you write.TWO FEATURES OF THIS OFFICE WERE NOT RECORDED HERE, AND BOTH CHANGE HOW A COMMUNITY SHOULD USE IT. FIRST, THERE IS NO DIFFERENCE BETWEEN PLAINTIFF AND DEFENDANT — EITHER SIDE MAY APPLY IF UNABLE TO PAY. A COMMUNITY DOES NOT HAVE TO WAIT TO BE SUED. IF THE RIGHT MOVE IS TO BRING THE CLAIM — OVER A WATERCOURSE, A BOUNDARY, A LEASE, A DAMAGED ORCHARD — THE FREE-COUNSEL ROUTE IS OPEN TO THE ONE STARTING THE CASE, NOT ONLY TO THE ONE DEFENDING IT. SECOND, IF THE APPOINTED LAWYER DOES NOT PURSUE THE MATTER PROPERLY, THE APPLICANT MAY DEMAND THAT THE ASSISTANCE OFFICE HOLD THEM ACCOUNTABLE. FREE REPRESENTATION THAT COMES WITH A COMPLAINT CHANNEL AGAINST THE REPRESENTATIVE IS RARE ANYWHERE IN THIS FILE. SO KEEP DATED NOTES FROM THE FIRST MEETING OF WHAT WAS AND WAS NOT DONE. THAT RECORD IS THE WHOLE BASIS OF SUCH A COMPLAINT, AND A COMMUNITY THAT KEEPS IT HAS A REMEDY THAT PAYING CLIENTS OFTEN LACK. THE OFFICE IS ORGANISED WITH A SECRETARIAT, A PETITIONS BRANCH AND A JUDICIAL BRANCH; AND THE MINISTRY IS SEPARATELY CHARGED WITH GIVING LEGAL GUIDANCE TO PEOPLE ATTENDING THE COURTS AND THE DEEDS REGISTRATION OFFICES — WHICH IS WHERE MOST LAND QUESTIONS BEGIN, AND WHERE A COMMUNITY WITHOUT A LAWYER CAN ASK FIRST. THE SERVICE IS RUN WITHOUT ANY GOVERNMENT BUDGET, AT THE EXPENSE OF AND BY THE ADVOCATES THEMSELVES. A SERVICE THE PROFESSION PAYS FOR ITSELF DOES NOT DISAPPEAR WHEN A MINISTRY CHANGES ITS PRIORITIES — BUT IT ALSO MEANS CAPACITY IS FINITE, SO APPLY EARLY RATHER THAN ON THE EVE OF A HEARING.SIX THINGS ABOUT THIS SYSTEM WERE NOT RECORDED HERE, AND THE FIRST IS THE TEST YOU MUST MEET: UNDER ARTICLE 24 OF THE ADVOCACY LAW, THOSE WHO LACK THE MEANS TO PAY A LAWYER'S FEE MAY REQUEST ASSISTANCE FROM THE BAR — PROVIDED THE CLAIM HAS A BASIS AND RELATES TO THE APPLICANT PERSONALLY. RELATES TO THE APPLICANT PERSONALLY IS THE CLAUSE THAT SHAPES HOW A COMMUNITY APPLIES. A VILLAGE CANNOT ASK COLLECTIVELY — THE HOUSEHOLD WHOSE LAND, WATER OR HOUSE IS AT STAKE APPLIES IN ITS OWN NAME, AND SEVERAL HOUSEHOLDS CAN APPLY SEPARATELY ABOUT THE SAME PROJECT. SECOND, SOMEBODY ELSE DECIDES WHETHER YOU ARE POOR ENOUGH: DETERMINING WHETHER A PERSON IS WITHOUT MEANS OR UNABLE TO PAY RESTS WITH THE COURT HEARING THE CASE, AND IN A CASSATION COMPLAINT WITH THE COURT THAT ISSUED THE JUDGMENT COMPLAINED OF. THIRD, AND THIS IS THE PROTECTION NOBODY EXPECTS: ALTHOUGH A RETAINER IS ORDINARILY A PERMISSIVE CONTRACT A LAWYER MAY RESIGN FROM AT WILL, THAT RULE DOES NOT APPLY TO ASSISTANCE REPRESENTATION, BECAUSE ACCEPTING IT IS A DUTY THE LEGISLATOR PLACED ON THE LAWYER. A LAWYER WHO CANNOT WALK AWAY IS WORTH MORE THAN A WILLING ONE WHO CAN. THIS FILE HAS RECORDED CASES ACROSS THE REGION COLLAPSING WHEN COUNSEL WITHDREW UNDER PRESSURE — HERE, WITHDRAWAL IS NOT AT THE LAWYER'S DISCRETION. FOURTH, WHAT IT COSTS: THE ASSISTANCE LAWYER TAKES NOTHING FROM THE CLIENT AS FEE OR CONSULTATION CHARGE APART FROM THE STAMP DUTY; IF THE CLIENT RECOVERS THEIR RIGHTS IN COURT THEY PAY AT A TARIFF LOWER THAN OTHER LAWYERS CHARGE; AND IF THEY RECOVER NOTHING, THE BAR ASSOCIATION PAYS. FIFTH, THERE ARE TWO DOORS, NOT ONE: CASES ARE REFERRED EITHER BY THE BAR'S JUDICIAL ASSISTANCE INSTITUTION OR BY THE JUDICIARY'S CENTRE FOR LAWYERS AND EXPERTS ESTABLISHED UNDER ARTICLE 187 — SO A REFUSAL AT ONE IS NOT THE END OF THE ROAD. SIXTH, CHECK WHO IS ASSIGNED TO YOU: TRAINEE LAWYERS AND LAW GRADUATES WITHOUT A LICENCE MAY NOT TAKE THESE CASES, AND THE LAWYER'S LICENCE MUST BE VALID AND NOT SUSPENDED. AND THE MONEY IS BUDGETED RATHER THAN CHARITABLE: THE JUDICIARY'S BUDGET DEPARTMENT IS OBLIGED EACH YEAR TO INCLUDE IN THE BUDGET BILL THE CREDIT NEEDED FOR ASSIGNED AND ASSISTANCE REPRESENTATION FEES, AS ESTIMATED AND PROPOSED BY THE CENTRAL BAR — WHICH MEANS ASKING FOR AN ASSISTANCE LAWYER IS CLAIMING SOMETHING ALREADY PAID FOR, NOT ASKING A FAVOUR.

trackers.name: The Article 90 Commission — a written complaint parliament is obliged to answer
trackers.desc: THE CONSTITUTION GIVES EVERY PERSON A WRITTEN COMPLAINT ROUTE, AND MAKES ANSWERING IT COMPULSORY. Anyone with a complaint about THE MANNER OF WORK of the assembly, the executive or the judiciary may submit it IN WRITING to the assembly, which is OBLIGED to examine it and give a SUFFICIENT ANSWER — and where the complaint concerns the executive or the judiciary, to require examination and a sufficient answer FROM THEM and to announce the result within an appropriate period. This country's listing in this map has held no domestic complaints channel at all. AND THE ENFORCEMENT CLAUSE IS UNLIKE ANYTHING ELSE RECORDED ANYWHERE IN THIS FILE. The commission may summon officials of the three branches or correspond with them directly AND THEY ARE OBLIGED TO COMPLY — and where an offence is proven for failing to answer or failing to give a convincing answer, THE OFFENDER FACES IMPRISONMENT OF THREE MONTHS TO ONE YEAR AND DISMISSAL FROM STATE SERVICE FOR SIX MONTHS TO ONE YEAR. Elsewhere in this payload an ignored complaint is simply ignored. Here silence by an official is itself an offence. AND THERE IS A SECOND DUTY WORTH FRAMING YOUR COMPLAINT AROUND: IN INDIVIDUAL MATTERS THE COMMISSION'S DUTY IS TO GIVE A SUFFICIENT ANSWER, BUT IN MATTERS OF PUBLIC CONCERN ITS DUTY IS TO INFORM THE GENERAL PUBLIC. A scheme affecting a whole district, a water source or a shared pasture is a matter of public concern, and saying so in the complaint invokes a duty of publication rather than merely of reply. WHAT IT COVERS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. Its subject is THE MANNER OF WORK of the three branches and their officials — how a decision was taken, whether procedure was followed, whether an authority answered — rather than the merits of the decision itself. An interpretation of the constitutional council confirms it examines the manner of work of CURRENT officials. Complaints about bodies affiliated to the executive or judiciary must first go through the channels the law provides for them, so this is the LAST avenue rather than the first. The commission has a unit dedicated to examining manners of work and received complaints, staffed by member deputies, advisers and experts, and it may summon both the complainant and the party complained of to explain. THE LIMITS, PLAINLY. It is not a court: courts must rule on every complaint, whereas this commission's obligation is a sufficient answer or public information, not a judgment or a remedy. It cannot reverse a permit or stop a project. It sits inside the legislature, and A WRITTEN COMPLAINT IS A DISCLOSURE OF YOUR NAME AND YOUR DISPUTE TO A STATE INSTITUTION — read this alongside the digital security helpline recorded separately for this country before writing. Use it where an authority has failed to follow its own procedure or has refused to answer, and use the bar's judicial assistance office recorded separately here for the case itself.

trackers.name: Free seedlings from the natural resources offices — and the coordinates that make it a record
trackers.desc: THE SEEDLINGS ARE FREE AND THE REQUEST IS A TELEPHONE CALL. Provincial natural resources departments supply the seedlings applicants need at no charge under the national tree-planting programme, with requests taken through a national telephone number and a national system; in the capital a separate city system operates alongside NINETY-THREE FLOWER AND PLANT TRAINING CENTRES distributing both fruit and non-fruit trees, and under one scheme staff attend homes, plant the seedling and leave written care instructions. BUT THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR LAND IS THE CONDITION ATTACHED. REGISTRATION OF THE PLANTING AREA IN THE STATE SYSTEM IS MANDATORY, AND AN APPLICANT MUST GO TO THE DISTRICT NATURAL RESOURCES AND WATERSHED OFFICE CARRYING THE COORDINATES OF THE PLANTING SITE IN ORDER TO RECEIVE THE TREES. This file has established across three countries that a state service can find land UNUSED and reallocate it, and that dated, witnessed evidence of use is the cheapest answer to that finding. HERE THE STATE ITSELF RECORDS, DATES AND GEO-REFERENCES YOUR PLANTING AS A CONDITION OF GIVING YOU THE TREES — the proof is created by the authority that would otherwise make the finding, and it costs nothing. AND A COMMUNITY BODY CAN APPLY AS AN INSTITUTION RATHER THAN AS INDIVIDUALS. The scheme names as participants not only nature-lovers and volunteers but COMPANIES, INDUSTRIES AND MINES, CITY AND VILLAGE COUNCILS AND VILLAGE ADMINISTRATORS, AND ASSOCIATIONS AND NATURAL-RESOURCE COOPERATIVES. A village council or a cooperative requesting seedlings for a named area, with coordinates, is doing something the scheme expressly invites. THE SUPPLY IS REAL AND SUITED TO DRY GROUND: production runs through 126 STATE NURSERIES COVERING NEARLY THREE THOUSAND HECTARES, plus around thirteen DESERT NURSERIES producing desert species, alongside private nurseries; hundreds of millions of seedlings are prepared for the planting week, and desert species such as haloxylon and atriplex are planted on natural-resource land. Ask for species suited to your ground rather than accepting whatever is offered. THE LIMITS, AND THE FIRST IS A DECISION. GIVING COORDINATES REGISTERS YOUR SITE AND YOUR NAME IN A STATE SYSTEM — that is what makes the record valuable and also what makes it a disclosure; read this with the digital security helpline recorded separately for this country. The distribution is SEASONAL, concentrated around the natural resources week in late winter, so the window is short. And officials themselves note that seedlings taken in previous years were often badly planted, unattended and died — A DEAD SEEDLING PROVES NOTHING, so plan the watering before you collect the trees.

trackers.name: UNESCO Chair on Water Reuse — a named professor with a telephone number
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY HAS THE FEWEST RECORDED RESOURCES OF ALL TWENTY-THREE IN THIS FILE, AND ALMOST NONE OF THEM CAN BE TELEPHONED. THIS ONE CAN: a UNESCO chair established in 2014 at the principal national university, WITH A NAMED CHAIRHOLDER AND TWO WORK TELEPHONE NUMBERS PUBLISHED. ITS SUBJECT IS WATER REUSE — the science of treated wastewater and recycled water — AND THAT IS MORE USEFUL THAN IT SOUNDS. Schemes across this region justify their water demand by promising to recycle, to treat and reuse effluent, or to return water to the system. A chair whose entire field is water reuse is the person who can say whether a particular claim of that kind is technically credible, at what quality, and with what residue. This file has found in nearly every country that the decisive gap is the cost of expert analysis; here is a named academic in the field, reachable directly. THE PROGRAMME THAT ESTABLISHED IT DESCRIBES ITS CHAIRS AS THINK TANKS AND BRIDGEBUILDERS BETWEEN ACADEMIA, CIVIL SOCIETY, LOCAL COMMUNITIES, RESEARCH AND POLICY-MAKING, so an approach from residents is within the post's stated purpose rather than an imposition on it. ASK A TECHNICAL QUESTION ABOUT A SPECIFIC SITE: what happens to the treated water, what it contains, where it goes, and whether the volumes stated in a proposal are achievable. Do not ask for support against a project — a chair cannot represent anyone and will not take sides. THE LIMITS, AND THE SECOND ONE IS A DECISION FOR YOU. It is an academic post inside a state university, so it is not independent of the administration; its output is research and teaching. AND IN THIS COUNTRY ANY APPROACH IDENTIFIES YOU AND YOUR INTEREST — an enquiry framed as a technical question about water quality is a quieter thing than a complaint, but it is still a disclosure, and this file's guidance on that for this country applies here too. The listing reached sits on a UNESCO water information platform rather than the university's own page, so confirm the current holder and the numbers before calling.

trackers.name: Provincial engineering organisation — the supervisor's duty to report violations, and where the report goes
trackers.desc: EVERY BUILDING HERE HAS SUPERVISING ENGINEERS UNDER A STATUTORY DUTY, AND THE DUTY IS THE OPENING A COMMUNITY NEEDS. They are obliged to supervise the works CONTINUOUSLY for conformity with the specifications in THE PERMIT AND THE APPROVED DRAWINGS, and at completion to CERTIFY that the building conforms to the permit, the drawings and the technical calculations. AND WHERE THE WORKS DEPART FROM THE APPROVED DRAWINGS, THE SUPERVISOR MUST PREPARE A REPORT OF THE VIOLATIONS AND DELIVER IT TO THE PROVINCIAL ORGANISATION AND TO THE PERMIT-ISSUING AUTHORITY — AND IF THE VIOLATIONS ARE NOT REMEDIED, THE MATTER IS REFERRED TO THE MUNICIPALITY'S ARTICLE 100 COMMISSION. That is a complete chain with a body at every step, and it changes the question entirely. A COMMUNITY DOES NOT HAVE TO PROVE THE WORK IS UNLAWFUL. IT HAS TO ASK WHETHER THE SUPERVISOR HAS FILED A REPORT — and if a departure from the drawings is visible and no report exists, the failure lies with a named licensed professional. THE DOCUMENTS ALSO ALREADY EXIST. A COORDINATING SUPERVISOR — an architect or civil engineer holding a supervision licence — is responsible for coordinating all the supervisors on a building or complex AND SUBMITTING STAGE REPORTS TO THE MUNICIPALITY, THE PROVINCIAL ORGANISATION AND OTHER RELEVANT AUTHORITIES. Stage reports are not something a community must commission; they are produced for every project, and they are held by two bodies. ASK WHICH LICENCE AND WHICH GRADE. Licences are split three ways: by DISCIPLINE — seven building disciplines including SURVEYING, URBAN PLANNING and TRAFFIC; by COMPETENCY — supervision, execution, and design or calculation, WITH A SEPARATE LICENCE ISSUED FOR EACH; and by GRADE, which limits the scale of work a person may take. Someone may hold a supervision licence and no design licence, or a grade too low for the project they are signing. TWO INTEGRITY RULES ARE WORTH KNOWING: A SUPERVISOR MAY NOT BE THE CLIENT OR THE CLIENT'S LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE ON THE SAME PROJECT, and a final disciplinary conviction of degree three or above disqualifies a professional from receiving referred supervision work. The provincial organisation checks competence and capacity before referring work, and its board sets the geographic area within the province in which a supervisor may operate. THE STRUCTURE IS PROVINCIAL: EACH PROVINCE HAS ITS OWN ORGANISATION WITH ITS OWN SITE, established under the building engineering and control law and described as non-governmental. FIND YOUR OWN PROVINCE'S ORGANISATION — the one linked here is a single provincial example. THE LIMITS. It regulates engineers rather than assisting residents, and in the statutory chain the complainant is the SUPERVISOR, not the neighbour — a community's route is to ask the provincial organisation whether reports were filed and to raise a supervisor's failure with it. Engaging services costs money. And any approach identifies you; read this with the digital security guidance recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Endowments organisation — a single tree can be endowed, and several people can endow together
trackers.desc: THE SMALLEST UNIT OF PERMANENT PROTECTION THIS FILE HAS FOUND IN THREE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-THREE ROUNDS IS HERE: ENDOWED TREES. In one province alone there are more than FIVE HUNDRED ENDOWED ORCHARDS, together with agricultural land, residential, administrative and industrial endowments — AND INDIVIDUAL ENDOWED TREES. A community that cannot conceivably buy a valley can still place a grove, a spring-side plot or a single old tree permanently outside the market. AND SEVERAL PEOPLE MAY ENDOW TOGETHER. A province has launched its first PARTICIPATORY ENDOWMENT, expressly using COLLECTIVE FINANCING to build a permanent financial base — which confirms in a second country the joint form this file recorded a round earlier. Many small contributions can become one endowment. THE SCALE MEANS THIS IS ORDINARY, NOT EXOTIC: there are MORE THAN TWO HUNDRED THOUSAND ENDOWMENTS in the country, and the organisation is establishing ENDOWMENT ADVISORY OFFICES. THE ENDOWER'S INTENTION IS ENFORCED, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE INSTRUMENT. All intentions and endowment deeds are registered and categorised in a comprehensive system SO THAT THE INCOME OF EACH ENDOWMENT IS SPENT IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE INTENTION OF ITS ENDOWER. AND YOU CAN NAME YOUR OWN WATCHDOG. A SUPERVISOR APPOINTED BY THE ENDOWER OVERSEES THE TRUSTEE'S WORK AND THE PRECISE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE DEED. This payload assembled across four endowment entries that the endower's conditions are the entire protection; HERE THE ENDOWER MAY ALSO APPOINT THE PERSON WHO POLICES THEM. Draft the deed to describe the land, the permitted uses and what may never be done — then name a supervisor who will outlive the argument. THERE IS ALSO A NEW ROUTE FOR DISPUTED ENDOWED LAND: a legal framework and integrated system now allows OWNERSHIP CLAIMS OVER ENDOWMENTS TO BE REGISTERED AND PURSUED, and the organisation has publicly invited anyone with such a claim to bring it — the facility being open to the public as well as to the organisation itself. Endowed ground that was taken or transferred is therefore contestable through a named channel. THE LIMITS, AND TWO ARE SERIOUS. THE ORGANISATION IS MOVING DELIBERATELY FROM TRADITIONAL ADMINISTRATION AND LEASING TOWARDS INVESTMENT, so endowed land may be developed rather than left alone — the deed's conditions are the only brake. ITS TAKING OF A SUPERVISION FEE FROM ENDOWMENT INCOME HAS BEEN QUESTIONED IN LEGAL SCHOLARSHIP AND BEFORE THE ADMINISTRATIVE JUSTICE COURT, so the cost of state administration is contested rather than settled. It is a state organisation with broad powers over endowments lacking a trustee. And in this country any dealing with an institution identifies you — read this with the digital security guidance recorded separately here.

trackers.name: Village administration and elected council — who holds the plan, who issues the permit, who must prosecute
trackers.desc: IF A SCHEME IS GOING UP ON RURAL LAND HERE, FOUR BODIES STAND BETWEEN IT AND LAWFULNESS, AND A RESIDENT CAN CHECK EVERY ONE OF THEM. FIRST, THE PLAN. EVERY VILLAGE'S DEVELOPMENT IS GOVERNED BY A RURAL GUIDE PLAN PREPARED BY A NATIONAL HOUSING FOUNDATION, AND YOU OBTAIN IT FROM THE VILLAGE ADMINISTRATION — WHOSE OFFICIALS ARE OBLIGED TO PROVIDE YOU WITH ITS DETAILS. That is a duty owed to an ordinary resident, and the plan shows whether a given plot lies inside or outside the built fabric. Ask neighbours who know the village too; the plan's boundary is the fact everything else turns on. SECOND, THE PERMIT. THE VILLAGE ADMINISTRATOR FORMS THE FILE AND ISSUES THE BUILDING PERMIT FOR STRUCTURES WITHIN THE VILLAGE'S LEGAL BOUNDARY — BUT ONLY AFTER COORDINATING WITH THE HOUSING FOUNDATION AND OBTAINING ITS TECHNICAL OPINION, AND ONLY WITHIN THE FRAMEWORK OF THE APPROVED GUIDE PLAN. A separate duty covers files for buildings, installations AND THE SUBDIVISION OF LAND, which are referred onward for the permit to issue. So the questions are simple and answerable: is there a permit, was the housing foundation's technical opinion taken, and does the work match the guide plan. THIRD, AND THIS IS THE STRONGEST LINK: BEFORE ANY ACTION, THE PERMIT-ISSUING AUTHORITY MUST OBTAIN THE OPINION OF THE COMMISSION UNDER THE LAW ON PRESERVING THE USE OF AGRICULTURAL LAND AND ORCHARDS. A permit granted without that opinion is defective on its face — and even where a village has NO approved guide plan, construction still needs a permit from the village administration and the land REMAINS SUBJECT TO THE AGRICULTURAL LAND PRESERVATION LAW. FOURTH, CHANGING WHAT LAND MAY BE USED FOR IS NOT A LOCAL DECISION: ANY LAND-USE CHANGE INSIDE A GUIDE PLAN REQUIRES THE AGREEMENT OF THE NATIONAL LAND AFFAIRS ORGANISATION. A developer promising that farmland will be reclassified is describing a decision that a national body must make.
