ONE PROVINCE HAS GONE FURTHER AND BUILT THE THING THIS FILE MOST OFTEN CANNOT FIND: AT A FOURTH CONSULTATION MEETING BETWEEN THE PROVINCIAL ENVIRONMENT DIRECTORATE AND THE ORGANISATIONS, IT WAS DECIDED THAT, IN COOPERATION WITH THE LEGAL WORKING GROUP UNDER THE PROVINCE'S NETWORK OF POPULAR ORGANISATIONS, THE LEGAL CHALLENGES OF THE EXECUTIVE ENVIRONMENTAL SECTOR WOULD BE EXAMINED IN A SPECIALISED WAY AND THE NECESSARY ADVICE PROVIDED FOR PURSUING ENVIRONMENTAL LAWSUITS. A LEGAL WORKING GROUP SITTING UNDER A PROVINCIAL NETWORK, ADVISING ON HOW TO PURSUE ENVIRONMENTAL CASES, IS THE NEAREST THING TO LOCAL ANTI-DEVELOPMENT LAWYERS THAT EXISTS IN THIS COUNTRY - AND IT WAS AGREED WITH THE DIRECTORATE ITSELF, NOT AGAINST IT. THE SCALE OF THE MOVEMENT IS LARGER THAN OUTSIDERS ASSUME: NEARLY A THOUSAND AND FIFTY REGISTERED POPULAR VOLUNTEER GROUPS, SOME WITH UP TO FOUR DECADES OF HISTORY, AND A THOUSAND THREE HUNDRED AND SIXTY ENVIRONMENT HOUSES ACTIVE IN SCHOOLS, VILLAGE ADMINISTRATIONS, LIBRARIES AND AGRICULTURAL CENTRES. AN ENVIRONMENT HOUSE INSIDE A VILLAGE ADMINISTRATION IS A ROOM IN THE BUILDING THIS PAYLOAD ALREADY RECORDS AS THE VILLAGE'S OWN LEGAL PERSON - WHICH MEANS THE ORGANISED ENVIRONMENTAL PRESENCE AND THE BODY THAT CAN BUY AND LEASE LAND SIT UNDER ONE ROOF. WHAT THEY DO IS PRACTICAL: PARTICIPATORY PROTECTION OF PROTECTED AREAS AND WILDLIFE, CENSUSES, AND EDUCATION AND INFORMATION WORK IN SCHOOLS, VILLAGES AND MOSQUES. THE NETWORKS THEMSELVES ARE REACHABLE: ONE PROVINCE'S NETWORK RUNS ITS OWN WEBSITE PUBLISHING TRAINING WORKSHOPS ON EROSION AND SOIL HEALTH AND QUALITY, ON THE CHALLENGES OF NATURE TOURISM AND ON CARBON TRADING, AND RECORDS ITS MEMBERS WINNING A NATIONAL HONORARY FOREST-GUARD TITLE. A PROVINCIAL NETWORK RUNNING A CARBON TRADING WORKSHOP FOR VILLAGE GROUPS IS PREPARING PEOPLE FOR THE NEGOTIATION THIS FILE EXPECTS TO ARRIVE IN EVERY COUNTRY IT COVERS. ONE PROVINCE'S NATURAL RESOURCES DIRECTORATE HAS SAID OUT LOUD WHAT IT WANTS FROM THEM: THAT THE ORGANISATIONS, WITH A COMMAND OF THE LAWS AND REGULATIONS, SHOULD ACT AS THE DIRECTORATE'S ADVISORY ARM IN IMPLEMENTING PROJECTS - AT A MEETING WITH THE PROVINCE'S HOUSE OF POPULAR ORGANISATIONS THAT STRESSED USING THEIR CAPACITY TO RESOLVE CONFLICTS BETWEEN INDUSTRY AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES. THAT PROVINCE HAS FORTY-FIVE ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATIONS, OF WHICH TWENTY ARE ACTIVE IN THE FIELD. RESOLVING CONFLICTS BETWEEN INDUSTRY AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES IS THE BUSINESS THIS ENTIRE PAYLOAD IS ABOUT, NAMED AS A JOB BY A PROVINCIAL DIRECTORATE. THE OBSTACLE IS PAPERWORK, AND IT IS DOCUMENTED: IN ANOTHER PROVINCE, THIRTY-SIX ORGANISATIONS EXISTED ON PAPER WHILE ABOUT FOURTEEN HELD VALID PERMITS, THE GOVERNOR'S OFFICE FIGURES AND THE DIRECTORATE'S FILES DIFFERED, AND THE SECRETARY OF THAT PROVINCE'S ORGANISATIONS SAID THE MAIN PROBLEMS WERE PERMIT RENEWAL AND REGISTRATION MATTERS, WITH MANY DISTRICT GOVERNORS' OFFICES UNAWARE THAT ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATIONS EXIST. AND THE ADMISSION FROM THE OTHER SIDE IS WORTH QUOTING BACK: THE POLITICAL AND SOCIAL DEPUTY OF THAT GOVERNOR'S OFFICE SAID THEY HAVE A LEGAL AND ADMINISTRATIVE DUTY TO SUPPORT THE ORGANISATIONS' DEMAND-MAKING AND THAT FAILING TO DO SO WOULD BE A DERELICTION, ADDING THAT THE SPECIALIST AGENCY MUST TREAT SPECIALIST ORGANISATIONS AS PARTNERS AND COLLEAGUES RATHER THAN AS A NUISANCE. THE LIMITS: THESE ARE LICENSED ORGANISATIONS OPERATING INSIDE A PERMIT SYSTEM THAT CAN BE SLOWED OR REFUSED, AND THE SAME REPORTS RECORD ACTIVE NUMBERS FALLING AND PERMITS LAPSING; A GROUP THAT LOSES ITS PERMIT LOSES ITS SEAT. THE SEATS DESCRIBED ARE IN CONSULTATIVE AND PLANNING BODIES, NOT DECISION-MAKING ONES A COMMUNITY CONTROLS, AND NOTHING RECORDED SHOWS ONE BLOCKING A PROJECT. WHICH ORGANISATIONS SIT ON WHICH COUNCIL, HOW THEY ARE SELECTED, AND WHETHER THE LEGAL WORKING GROUP HAS ADVISED ON ANY ACTUAL CASE WERE ALL NOT ESTABLISHED. THE ACCOUNT COMES FROM FOUR IRANIAN NEWS AGENCIES AND ONE PROVINCIAL NETWORK'S OWN SITE, DATED BETWEEN JUNE AND SEPTEMBER 2026 EXCEPT THE NETWORK PAGE, WHOSE POSTS DATE FROM AN EARLIER YEAR. Read it with the village administration and its property powers, the charity atlas and ranger solidarity fund, the judicial assistance office and the soil and water laboratories recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Carnivore conservation society funded by its own supporters — ranger and local-NGO partnerships, and the demand to buy out inholdings inside habitat
trackers.desc: THE CLEAREST LAND-PURCHASE DEMAND THIS FILE HAS RECORDED IN THIS COUNTRY SITS IN A PUBLIC CAMPAIGN'S NUMBERED LIST: PURCHASING AND FREEING THE PRIVATE INHOLDINGS INSIDE THE HABITATS. INHOLDINGS - PRIVATE PARCELS SURROUNDED BY PROTECTED GROUND - ARE THE HOLES THROUGH WHICH ROADS, WELLS AND MINES ENTER A PROTECTED AREA. BUYING THEM OUT IS THE MOST DIRECT CONSERVATION PURCHASE THERE IS, AND A CAMPAIGN HERE HAS ALREADY PUT IT IN WRITING AS A DEMAND. THE SAME LIST IS WORTH CARRYING WHOLE INTO ANY HABITAT FIGHT: PREVENTING THE CONSTRUCTION AND EXECUTION OF ANY DEVELOPMENT OR EXPLOITATION SCHEMES SUCH AS ROADS AND MINES IN THE HABITATS; INCREASING THE NUMBER OF RANGERS AND IMPROVING THEIR EQUIPMENT; PLACING MIGRATION ROUTES BETWEEN EXISTING PROTECTED AREAS UNDER PROTECTION IN TWO NAMED PROVINCES; MAKING ACCIDENT-PRONE ROAD SECTIONS SAFE ON A NAMED HIGHWAY; AND INVOLVING LOCAL COMMUNITIES IN NATURE TOURISM AND HABITAT PROTECTION SO THAT THEY BENEFIT FROM IT. PROTECTING THE CORRIDOR BETWEEN TWO RESERVES IS THE DEMAND CONSERVATION CAMPAIGNS MOST OFTEN FORGET, AND THE ONE THAT DECIDES WHETHER PROTECTED AREAS ARE A NETWORK OR A SET OF ISLANDS. THE ORGANISATION BEHIND MUCH OF THIS WORK IS UNUSUAL IN TWO WAYS. FIRST, ITS METHOD: IN EACH HABITAT IT BEGINS WITH AN ECOLOGICAL STUDY OF THE TARGET SPECIES AND ITS ECOSYSTEM, AND ONLY THEN PLANS THE APPROPRIATE PROTECTION, EDUCATION OR PUBLIC-PARTICIPATION ACTIVITIES. SECOND, ITS PARTNERS: RANGERS AND LOCAL NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS ARE ITS MAIN COLLABORATORS IN THE REGIONS, AND IT SEEKS CONSTRUCTIVE AND REASONED INTERACTION, AWAY FROM MARGINS AND EMOTION, WITH THE ENVIRONMENT ORGANISATION AT NATIONAL, PROVINCIAL AND COUNTY LEVEL. A NATIONAL BODY WHOSE DECLARED MAIN PARTNERS ARE THE LOCAL RANGERS AND THE LOCAL ASSOCIATIONS IS ONE A VILLAGE GROUP CAN ACTUALLY WORK WITH - AND THIS PAYLOAD ALREADY RECORDS A SOLIDARITY FUND IN THIS COUNTRY THAT RAISES MONEY FOR RANGERS, INCLUDING TO FREE DETAINED ONES. ITS INDEPENDENCE IS STATED PLAINLY AND MATTERS: IT RECEIVES NO FIXED BUDGET FROM ANY ORGANISATION OR BODY, AND ITS EXPENSES ARE MET FROM THE FINANCIAL HELP OF INDIVIDUALS AND INSTITUTIONS, FROM COOPERATION CONTRACTS, AND FROM THE SALE OF SUPPORT PRODUCTS, WITH MANY PEOPLE WORKING AS STAFF OR VOLUNTEERS. SELLING SUPPORT PRODUCTS AND SIGNING COOPERATION CONTRACTS IS HOW A CONSERVATION BODY SURVIVES WITHOUT A STATE BUDGET IN A COUNTRY WHERE FOREIGN FUNDING IS DANGEROUS. THAT MODEL IS WORTH STUDYING BY EVERY GROUP IN THIS FILE THAT DEPENDS ON GRANTS. THE MOST INSTRUCTIVE STORY COMES FROM A DIFFERENT ASSOCIATION: IT WORKED FOR ABOUT TWELVE YEARS WITH THE LOCAL COMMUNITY IN ONE SPECIES' HABITAT, AND BY THE DAY THE ANIMALS WERE RELEASED A FESTIVAL FOR THE SPECIES WAS HELD, ARAB SHEIKHS ATTENDED THE CEREMONY, AND LOCAL PEOPLE HAD COME TO FEEL LOVE AND ATTACHMENT FOR IT - AT WHICH POINT, AN OFFICIAL SAID, YOU CAN BE SURE THE COMMUNITY WILL NOT HARM THE RELEASED ANIMALS, AND THE NUMBERS RISE EACH YEAR. TWELVE YEARS BEFORE THE FIRST RELEASE IS THE HONEST TIMESCALE FOR COMMUNITY-BASED CONSERVATION, AND THE OPPOSITE OF THE PROJECT CYCLES THIS PAYLOAD RECORDS EVERYWHERE ELSE. THE MEASURE OF SUCCESS WAS NOT A FENCE BUT A FESTIVAL. A THIRD BODY SHOWS WHERE THE MONEY MODEL IS HEADING: A WILDLIFE HERITAGE FOUNDATION'S PROJECT, OVER MORE THAN TEN YEARS, IDENTIFIED AND PROTECTED HABITATS AND - WITH ACTIVE ORGANISATIONS, GOVERNMENT BODIES AND A UNITED NATIONS SMALL GRANTS OFFICE - EMPOWERED AND TRAINED LOCAL COMMUNITIES AROUND THEM, WITH A SECOND PHASE COVERING PARTICIPATORY MODELLING OF LIVESTOCK MANAGEMENT AND THE DESIGN OF SUSTAINABLE FINANCIAL MODELS. PARTICIPATORY LIVESTOCK MODELLING IS THE POLITE NAME FOR THE HARDEST NEGOTIATION IN ANY RANGELAND - HOW MANY ANIMALS, WHERE, AND WHO GIVES WAY. A STATE PROJECT MANAGER'S OWN PRIORITIES INCLUDE REDUCING DOMESTIC LIVESTOCK PRESSURE IN THE SPECIES' AREAS, SO HERDING FAMILIES SHOULD EXPECT TO BE IN THAT CONVERSATION AND SHOULD BE IN IT EARLY. THE LIMITS: THESE ARE RESEARCH AND SPECIES-CONSERVATION ORGANISATIONS, NOT LAND-BUYING OR LEGAL ONES - THE PURCHASE OF INHOLDINGS IS A CAMPAIGN DEMAND ADDRESSED TO THE STATE, NOT SOMETHING ANY OF THEM DOES, AND NOTHING RECORDED HERE SHOWS ONE ACQUIRING LAND. THEIR RELATIONSHIP WITH THE ENVIRONMENT ORGANISATION IS DELIBERATELY COOPERATIVE, SO THEY ARE UNLIKELY TO SUPPORT A COMMUNITY IN OPEN CONFLICT WITH IT, AND CONSERVATION HERE CAN CUT AGAINST HERDERS - REDUCING LIVESTOCK PRESSURE AND CLEARING ANIMALS FROM HABITAT ARE STATED PRIORITIES. WHETHER THE CAMPAIGN DEMANDS WERE EVER ACTED ON, HOW A VILLAGE APPROACHES ANY OF THESE BODIES, AND WHAT THEY CAN OFFER TODAY WERE NOT ESTABLISHED; SEVERAL SOURCES ARE OLD - AN UNDATED CAMPAIGN PAGE, A SOCIETY PAGE OF 2023 AND A NEWSLETTER OF 2014 - ALONGSIDE PRESS ITEMS OF MAY AND AUGUST 2026. Read it with the charity atlas and the ranger solidarity fund, the provincial NGO networks and their legal working group, the village administration's property powers and the environmental justice atlas recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a pan-African feminist rapid-response fund with reach across all 54 African countries — small grants released quickly for unanticipated, time-critical situations rather than planned programme work, covering safety and protection needs when defenders are threatened and short windows for advocacy after an unexpected event. WHO IT SUITS: women's rights organisations, feminist collectives and movements in which women or gender-diverse people are the primary decision-makers. It does NOT fund individuals, and the action must be strategic, genuinely unanticipated, and completable in under three months. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is emergency money for a moment, not a budget for a campaign — decisions are fast and grants are modest.

trackers.name: Commission d’Accès à l’Information (CAIDP)
trackers.desc: Côte d'Ivoire's CAIDP is the independent authority for access to public-interest information and public documents, enforcing the 2013 access-to-information law with powers of injunction and sanction. It handles complaints, monitors compliance and reports annually, and launched the ACCESS CAIDP portal in 2025 with full rollout targeted by December 2026. USE IT: injunction powers mean it can order release rather than only recommend it.

trackers.name: Cour des comptes
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Côte d'Ivoire, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Côte d’Ivoire — CEPICI (Guichet Unique de l’Investissement)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the Guichet Unique des Formalités d’Entreprise (GUFE) centralises company creation, modification & dissolution and RCCM registration, Côte d’Ivoire. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Marchés Publics
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Côte d’Ivoire, and for how much.

trackers.name: ECOWAS Court of Justice — file directly, but sue the State
trackers.desc: A COURT YOU CAN REACH WITHOUT EXHAUSTING DOMESTIC REMEDIES. The ECOWAS Community Court of Justice has held human rights jurisdiction since 2005 and has broad access and standing rules permitting individuals and NGOs to bypass national courts and file directly. THE PRECEDENT: in SERAP v Federal Republic of Nigeria (ECW/CCJ/APP/08/09) the Court dismissed all three preliminary objections — no locus standi, no jurisdiction, statute-barred — and rejected the government's attempt to exclude an Amnesty International report from the evidence. NGO research was admitted as evidence, which matters when no state data exists. It found violations of articles 1 and 24 of the African Charter — article 24: ‘all peoples shall have the right to a general satisfactory environment favourable to their development’ — and of article 21, the right to natural wealth and resources. THE FAULT WAS AN OMISSION: the state ‘defaulted in its duties in terms of vigilance and diligence’, and ‘the omission to act and to prevent damage to the environment characterises the violation’. It ordered restoration within the shortest possible time and measures to prevent further damage, citing the ICJ that the environment ‘is not an abstraction but represents the living space, the quality of life and the very health of human beings, including generations unborn’. THE LIMIT THAT DECIDES WHO YOU SUE: the Court held it had no jurisdiction over the private oil corporations, which were struck from the suit. You sue the State for failing to regulate; you cannot sue the company here — naming one as respondent loses that part of the case. AND PLAN FOR ENFORCEMENT: commentary records the Court did not identify a means for Nigeria to implement the ruling, and the ICJ later wrote to the President pressing for enforcement — judgment is the start of an enforcement campaign, not a self-executing remedy. Proposals to require exhaustion of domestic remedies were rejected by ECOWAS experts and Heads of Government, so the direct-access rule has been tested and held.

trackers.name: ORFAO — comparative land-law tables, and a directive in draft
trackers.desc: COMPARATIVE LEGAL TABLES FOR YOUR COUNTRY AND ITS NEIGHBOURS, IN ONE DOCUMENT. The Observatoire Régional du Foncier Rural en Afrique de l'Ouest (ORFAO), hosted by UEMOA, publishes a regional study on rural land markets containing side-by-side ‘cadre légal comparé’ tables — one covering Bénin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire and Sénégal, another Guinée-Bissau, Mali, Niger and Togo — plus typologies of direct and indirect interventions in land markets and a table of regulatory issues and families of instruments. If you need to know what instrument exists in your country and whether a neighbour has a stronger one, that is the document — comparative tables let a campaign point to a neighbour's provision as an achievable ask rather than a novelty. A WINDOW IS OPENING: on 26 June 2026 in Ouagadougou the UEMOA ministers for urbanisme, habitat, domaines et cadastre approved a draft directive to harmonise rules on immatriculation foncière, accès au titre de propriété and a système d'information foncière, aiming at a common framework of land governance. BE PRECISE ABOUT STATUS: that was a DRAFT directive approved by ministers, not an adopted and transposed instrument — check adoption and transposition before relying on it. But transposition is the moment domestic land law is reopened in each state, and that is when community provisions can be argued for. FOR A GRAZING OR TRANSHUMANCE DISPUTE: a regional pastoral situation bulletin covers 11 West African countries with the support of decentralised technical services — an evidence source drawing on the same services you would otherwise approach one by one. RECORDED PLAINLY: cattle theft is documented as a driver of conflict and instability in the Sahel, so a land dispute here may sit inside a security context that changes what is safe to do. And confirm your state's current ECOWAS standing — several members are recorded as suspended.

trackers.name: SOS Forêts and the OI-REN platform — about forty Ivorian NGOs and community associations, and the ones who go to villages to explain the forest code
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an Ivorian conservation NGO, led by the mangrove scientist Wadja Egnankou, which is also the way into the two networks that matter for a community facing eviction or a concession. It sits in the Observatoire Ivoirien pour la gestion durable des Ressources Naturelles (OI-REN), a platform of about forty NGOs and community-based associations, and in Alerte Foncier, which campaigns to consolidate the land rights of rural communities — two doors that are far harder to find directly than through a member. WHAT THE NETWORK ACTUALLY DOES ON THE GROUND: OI-REN has run information and awareness missions in village after village to explain the 2019 forest code, working with the ministry and funded by an environmental law organisation, on the stated basis that rural communities need the law made intelligible to deal both with logging operators and with the forest administration. It has also filed civil society commentary on national forest policy, and its analysis was cited alongside human rights organisations pressing for an independent observer and auditor of the classified forests written into the forest code. WHY THIS MATTERS HERE MORE THAN ELSEWHERE: Côte d'Ivoire has 231 classified forests, and residents of them have been forcibly evicted — people who had farmed there for years, moved out without adequate rehousing or replacement farmland, according to human rights investigations of the forest agency's operations. If you live in or beside a classified forest, the risk is eviction rather than purchase, and the network is what documents it. SOS Forêts itself works on mangroves and supports village women's associations in production activities such as solar salt. WHO IT SUITS: forest-edge and coastal communities in Côte d'Ivoire. CAVEATS: these are conservation and advocacy organisations, not lawyers — no litigation service, intake route or fee information was found; and OI-REN's own web presence is thin, so a member organisation such as this one is the practical point of entry.

trackers.name: AFOR — the Ivorian rural land agency that issues village land certificates, free under the World Bank-funded programme, and the certificate lets the village sue
trackers.desc: WHO TO APPROACH: the Agence Foncière Rurale, created because the 1998 rural land law had failed in practice — by the end of 2015 less than 1 per cent of the 23 million hectares of rural land had been certified — and given the autonomy and resources to run national certification. WHY THE CERTIFICATE IS WORTH THE TROUBLE: village communities holding collective rights over community land can obtain a Certificat foncier, and once it is published the certificate confers on the group the LEGAL CAPACITY TO GO TO COURT and to carry out acts of land management. That is the difference between a village that is talked about in a land dispute and one that can be a party to it. WHAT IT COSTS AND HOW LONG YOU HAVE: certificates issued under the donor-funded rural land policy programme have been delivered free of charge to beneficiaries — a pilot in one region produced 2,000 certificates, with an extension phase targeting 37,000 more across the country in sixteen months. Note the deadline that follows: the three-year period to convert a certificate into full registration was removed, and a 2023 decree set it at ten years — so check which rule applies to your certificate and diarise it, because an unconverted certificate can lapse. WHO IT SUITS: Ivorian village communities and rural landholders who want documented collective rights before a concession, plantation or classified-forest decision lands on them. CAVEATS: this is a state agency, so it is the counterparty as well as the service — certification has been controversial for over two decades and the process itself generates disputes between customary holders, migrants and long-term farmers; the roll-out depends on donor-funded programme phases reaching your area; and for support in dealing with logging operators or classified-forest eviction, the SOS Forêts / OI-REN entry is the civil society side.

trackers.name: AFJCI legal clinics — free legal advice with no bureaucracy, about ten clinics across Côte d'Ivoire plus a mobile one
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Association des Femmes Juristes de Côte d'Ivoire, which for nearly twenty years has run cliniques juridiques — listening, orientation and advice centres offering the most vulnerable and remote populations quality legal support, FREE OF CHARGE AND WITHOUT ADMINISTRATIVE FORMALITIES. The first fixed clinic opened at the Abidjan headquarters; six more followed in 2013 with European Union and UN backing, and reporting describes around ten clinics across Ivorian territory, with clinic locations including Abidjan and Bouaké and coverage extending to communes of Abidjan and departments of the Gbêké region. It also runs a MOBILE legal clinic that travels to rural localities — documented as far as Niandégué in the Bouna department — ending with free itinerant legal consultations giving advice, information and referral. WHAT IT ACTUALLY PROVIDES: legal consultations, judicial assistance, and SUPPORT WITH PROCEDURE COSTS — beneficiaries of assistance, including supplementary judgments and procedure fees, are identified during its listening sessions. It trains community relays and leaders, and broadcasts on radio. A clinic that pays some of your procedure costs is rarer in this file than one that gives advice; ask about that at the first meeting. WHO IT SUITS: Ivorians who cannot pay a lawyer and need advice, orientation or help with court costs — particularly women and rural households; useful alongside a land certificate application. CAVEATS: a women-jurists' association whose priorities are gender-based violence, civil status and family law rather than land or environmental litigation — approach it for access to justice, not as anti-development counsel. Clinic coverage depends on project funding cycles. For rural land certificates, Côte d'Ivoire's AFOR entry; for forests and logging, SOS Forêts.

trackers.name: Côte d'Ivoire's assistance judiciaire — decentralised to EVERY first-degree court since 2016, and here is the exact document list to bring
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: assistance judiciaire is a statutory mechanism letting people without sufficient resources assert their rights in court AS CLAIMANT OR DEFENDANT WITHOUT BEARING THE COSTS — it is effectively free, per the justice ministry, and it may be sought by any natural person OR by a private association whose object is a work of assistance. An association can apply on the strength of its purpose — which matters for a village committee or a landowners association rather than an individual. WHERE TO FILE: décret n°2016-781 of 12 October 2016 DECENTRALISED the service, creating a BUREAU LOCAL at each first-degree jurisdiction to hear applications at first instance instead of a single national bureau, expressly so people in remote areas can reach justice without financial obstacle. You may therefore address the request either to the president of the bureau central at the justice ministry's civil and criminal affairs directorate, or to the president of the bureau local at the seat of each Section de tribunal or Tribunal de première instance across the territory. THE DOCUMENT LIST, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT DECIDES WHETHER YOUR FILE IS ACCEPTED: attach (1) a certificate of taxation or NON-taxation issued by the tax collector for your domicile; (2) a copy of the decision you intend to appeal, or of the title you want enforced; and (3) any document proving insolvency — for example a CERTIFICAT D'INDIGENCE issued by the police commissioner or the head of the administrative district. The certificat d'indigence is the pivot: obtain it first, from the police commissioner or the district head, because nothing else in the file substitutes for it. Note that a title you want ENFORCED is listed — like Burkina, this covers execution, not only trial. WHO IT SUITS: Ivorian households and associations that cannot pay court and advocate costs in a land, certificate or expropriation dispute. CAVEATS: A STATE SCHEME, and reporting notes assistance judiciaire remains poorly known, particularly among women; the indigence certificate depends on an official's signature. For free advice clinics including a mobile one, Côte d'Ivoire's AFJCI entry; for rural land certificates, AFOR; for forests and logging, SOS Forêts.

trackers.name: La Croix Verte — the Ivorian youth-run NGO whose intervention saved a sacred forest from a government logging permit, plus the country's first community-managed voluntary nature reserve
trackers.desc: THE ORGANISATION THAT STOPPED A LOGGING PERMIT, WHICH IS THE THING THIS FILE'S IVORIAN RECORD LACKED: LA CROIX VERTE is an Ivorian environmental NGO that POSITIONS ITSELF FIRST AND FOREMOST AS A DEFENDER OF THE INTEREST OF LOCAL POPULATIONS, and ITS PROJECT ORIGINATED IN THE THREAT OF DESTRUCTION HANGING OVER A SACRED FOREST IN THE ZANZAN REGION (NORTH-EAST CÔTE D'IVOIRE), ARISING FROM A TIMBER-CUTTING PERMIT ISSUED BY THE IVORIAN GOVERNMENT TO A COMMERCIAL OPERATOR — AND THANKS TO THE INTERVENTION OF LA CROIX VERTE, THAT SACRED FOREST WAS SPARED. A permit already issued by the government was not the end of it. That is the single most useful fact in this entry: an Ivorian NGO has reversed a cutting permit over a sacred forest, and the organisation that did it is named and reachable. WHAT IT BUILT AFTERWARDS: SINCE 2002 LA CROIX VERTE HAS RUN A MANAGEMENT EXPERIMENT ACROSS FOUR SACRED FOREST RESERVES, KNOWN AS THE THREE INTEGRATED ZONES STRATEGY — and the recorded significance of the experiment is that IT IS AN NGO CREATED AND MANAGED BY YOUNG PEOPLE. Sacred forests and the rituals within them are treated as a genuine sanctuary for animal and plant diversity, and Ivorian ecological NGOs have existed since the early 1980s. If your ground is sacred, that is a recognised conservation category here, not a sentimental argument — and the strategy that has worked is zoning it, not fencing it. THE OTHER ROUTE, WITH A DATE: a Swiss-Ivorian research centre works actively with local communities and WITH ITS SUPPORT THEY CREATED IN 2016 THE VERY FIRST COMMUNITY-MANAGED VOLUNTARY NATURE RESERVE IN CÔTE D'IVOIRE. Voluntary nature reserve, community-managed, and it exists — ask for that status by name, and ask the research centre how the first one was constituted. AND TWO GRASSROOTS BODIES WITH ADDRESSES: the GROUPEMENT IVOIRIEN DE REBOISEMENT ET D'ENTRETIEN DES FORÊTS, based in the VILLAGE OF BIEBY at YAKASSÉ-ATTOBROU about 130 KM FROM ABIDJAN, promoting agricultural and reforestation techniques, restoring forests and engaging young people, with a named founding president who records that at the start the population did not join in, and it took awareness sessions and training using LEAFLETS SHOWING BEFORE-AND-AFTER PHOTOGRAPHS of a destroyed forest; and the ASSOCIATION DES PROPRIÉTAIRES DE FORÊTS NATURELLES ET PLANTATIONS D'AFFERY, which helps communities through awareness, DONATIONS OF TREES and advice, and which ASKS FOR THE SUPPORT OF VILLAGE CHIEFS to reach people. Before-and-after photographs persuaded a village that words had not. And an association OF FOREST OWNERS is an ally most communities never think to call — landowners who plant have the same enemy you do. WHO IT SUITS: Ivorian communities with a sacred forest, a threatened permit area, or land they want reserved. CAVEATS: SMALL NGOs; some records are historical — confirm current activity. For about forty Ivorian NGOs in one platform, Côte d'Ivoire's SOS Forêts and OI-REN entry; for village land certificates, AFOR; for free legal advice with no bureaucracy, the AFJCI clinics entry.

trackers.name: Fondation pour les Parcs et Réserves de Côte d'Ivoire — a national trust fund whose mandate expressly includes acquiring private land to become parks or reserves, plus JVE Côte d'Ivoire with its récépissé number
trackers.desc: THE NATIONAL FUND THAT CAN BUY THE LAND — and this is the most directly on-brief instrument in this file's West African record: THE FONDATION POUR LES PARCS ET RÉSERVES DE CÔTE D'IVOIRE IS THE FIRST IVORIAN FONDS FIDUCIAIRE — TRUST FUND — DEDICATED TO THE CONSERVATION OF NATIONAL PARKS AND RESERVES: A PRIVATE NON-PROFIT INSTITUTION RECOGNISED AS OF PUBLIC UTILITY BY DÉCRET N°2009-05 OF 8 JANUARY 2009. Its vocation is to manage environmental funds TO FINANCE PROJECTS AND PROGRAMMES OF CONSERVATION OF NATIONAL PARKS AND RESERVES, AND TO REINFORCE MANAGEMENT CAPACITIES IN THE SECTOR. AND THE POWERS ARE STATED EXPLICITLY: IT MAY ACT AS A TRUST FUND; IT MAY ACQUIRE OR FINANCE THE ACQUISITION OF PRIVATE LAND DESTINED TO BECOME PARKS OR RESERVES; AND IT MAY INTERVENE IN OPERATIONS CONVERTING DEBT AGAINST NATURE. Buy the ground, or pay for somebody else to buy it, written into a national foundation's own mandate with a decree number attached. If the land you are trying to save is in private hands and the answer everywhere else has been that nobody can purchase it, this is the Ivorian body whose constitution says otherwise. Write to it with the parcel, the owner and the conservation case — and ask specifically whether it will ACQUIRE or FINANCE THE ACQUISITION, because those are two different offers and both are on the table. DEBT-FOR-NATURE CONVERSION is the third power, and it is the one that produces large sums without a donor appeal: a portion of national debt cancelled in exchange for domestic conservation spending. Ask whether any conversion is in preparation and what it is earmarked for — that is where a big number would come from. WHERE IT ALREADY WORKS: its published project list names DEPARTMENTS BY NAME — ABIDJAN, KATIOLA-NIAKARA, BANGOLO AND DUÉKOUÉ, ATTIEGOUAKRO, ASSINIE, AND BOUAFLÉ AND ZUÉNOULA, and it sits alongside the parks agency, the global environment facility, the world bank and an international conservation union in funding a national park's management plan. A foundation that publishes which DEPARTMENTS it is working in tells you in one glance whether your area is already inside its map. If it is not, that absence is the argument for putting it there. THE OTHER ORGANISATION, WITH ITS REGISTRATION NUMBER PRINTED: JEUNES VOLONTAIRES POUR L'ENVIRONNEMENT CÔTE D'IVOIRE IS LEGALLY CONSTITUTED AND REGISTERED UNDER RÉCÉPISSÉ DE DÉCLARATION D'ASSOCIATION N°118/MEMIS/DGAT/DAG/SDVA, CONTRIBUTING SINCE 2 FEBRUARY 2008 to solving the environmental problems of populations living in Côte d'Ivoire, INTERVENING ON ELEVEN ENVIRONMENTAL QUESTIONS INCLUDING CLIMATE CHANGE AND FOREST AND LAND GOVERNANCE (GOUVERNANCE FORESTIÈRE ET FONCIÈRE). Forest AND land governance named together as one of its eleven working questions. That pairing is exactly what a community losing forest to a land transaction needs, and it is rare to see the two treated as a single file. It works HAND IN HAND WITH LOCAL COMMUNITIES TO REINFORCE THEIR POWER TO ACT, VALORISE THEIR KNOWLEDGE AND CO-CONSTRUCT DURABLE SOLUTIONS, rests on A NETWORK OF MORE THAN 200 YOUNG VOLUNTEERS DRAWN FROM LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND THE UNIVERSITY WORLD, belongs to A PAN-AFRICAN NETWORK PRESENT IN 28 COUNTRIES working closely with counterparts in Ghana, Benin, Senegal, Nigeria, Togo and Cameroon, and is a member of named national bodies including AN IVORIAN CIVIL SOCIETY CONVENTION, A DISASTER RISK REDUCTION PLATFORM AND A NETWORK OF VOLUNTEERING ASSOCIATIONS, plus international networks on pollutants, mercury and disaster reduction. It has also organised an awareness workshop AGAINST GMOs AND FOR FAMILY AGRICULTURE. Two hundred volunteers drawn from BOTH the villages and the universities is the combination that produces evidence a ministry will read and testimony a village will recognise. Ask JVE to pair a student with your community rather than sending a report writer. WHO IT SUITS: Ivorian communities whose ground is privately owned, anyone needing a purchase financed, and villages needing forest-and-land governance support. CAVEATS: A TRUST FUND ACQUIRES LAND FOR PARK OR RESERVE STATUS, so understand what designation would follow before you propose your ground. For the organisation that reversed a logging permit over a sacred forest and the first community-managed voluntary reserve, Côte d'Ivoire's La Croix Verte entry.

trackers.name: CEPF — the biodiversity hotspot fund whose named applicants start at farmers' cooperatives, up to US$50,000 in eleven West African countries and a $10,000 emergency window in eleven eastern ones, with a regional team you can email before applying
trackers.desc: FARMERS' COOPERATIVES ARE ON THE LIST OF WHO MAY APPLY — placement note first: THIS FUND WORKS ACROSS BIODIVERSITY HOTSPOTS SPANNING MANY COUNTRIES, FILED UNDER CÔTE D'IVOIRE BECAUSE IT IS NAMED IN THE CURRENT WEST AFRICAN CALL; EVERY ELIGIBLE AFRICAN COUNTRY IS LISTED BELOW. WHO CAN APPLY, IN THE FUND'S OWN WORDS: CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS OF ALL SIZES — FROM FARMERS' COOPERATIVES AND COMMUNITY GROUPS TO UNIVERSITIES AND INTERNATIONAL NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS — CAN APPLY; RECIPIENTS ARE NGOs, COMMUNITY GROUPS, PRIVATE ENTERPRISES, UNIVERSITIES, FOUNDATIONS AND OTHERS, AND GOVERNMENT ORGANISATIONS ARE ELIGIBLE FOR PARTICIPATION IF THEY MEET CERTAIN REQUIREMENTS. A farmers' cooperative named first in the list, before the universities and the international NGOs. This file has recorded cooperative formation again and again as the legal person a community can actually obtain — in Angola, Equatorial Guinea, South Sudan, Tanzania. Here is a fund that names that exact body as an eligible applicant. If your community formed a cooperative, it can apply in its own name. THE WEST AFRICAN CALL: UP TO US$50,000 PER PROJECT, COVERING GUINEA, SIERRA LEONE, LIBERIA, CÔTE D'IVOIRE, GHANA, TOGO, BENIN, NIGERIA, CAMEROON, EQUATORIAL GUINEA, AND SÃO TOMÉ AND PRÍNCIPE — AND ENGLISH, FRENCH, PORTUGUESE AND SPANISH APPLICATIONS ARE ACCEPTED. Four languages accepted, which matters more than it sounds: this file has recorded lusophone and francophone communities shut out of anglophone funding again and again. Eleven countries, and you may write in your own working language. AND THE DOOR TO KNOCK ON BEFORE YOU WRITE ANYTHING: THE REGIONAL IMPLEMENTATION TEAM IS TWO NAMED AFRICAN ORGANISATIONS, AND APPLICANTS ARE ENCOURAGED TO CONTACT THE TEAM IF THEY HAVE ANY QUESTIONS OR WISH TO DISCUSS PROJECT IDEAS — WITH A PUBLISHED EMAIL ADDRESS. The fund is administered in the region by African organisations, and they invite you to discuss the idea before submitting. That conversation is free and it is where most weak applications get fixed. Write to the regional team first, not the fund. THE RULES ON WHO SIGNS: INDIVIDUALS MUST PARTNER WITH AN ELIGIBLE ORGANISATION — AND CONSORTIUM APPLICATIONS ARE ALLOWED, BUT ONE LEAD ORGANISATION MUST BE IDENTIFIED AND PARTNER ROLES CLEARLY DESCRIBED. Consortiums allowed with one lead. So three village associations can apply together, provided they settle beforehand which one holds the grant and what each does — and settling that in writing before the application is how you avoid the argument afterwards. THE EASTERN CALL, WITH A WINDOW FOR EMERGENCIES: ELIGIBLE COUNTRIES ARE ETHIOPIA, KENYA, UGANDA, RWANDA, BURUNDI, DRC, TANZANIA, MALAWI, ZAMBIA, ZIMBABWE AND MOZAMBIQUE — WITH A RAPID RESPONSE WINDOW OF UP TO $10,000 TO SAVE KEY BIODIVERSITY AREAS FROM URGENT AND IMMEDIATE THREAT, AND ANOTHER WINDOW OF UP TO USD 20,000 WHERE APPLICATIONS FROM ORGANIZATIONS THAT PROPOSE TO BUILD CAPACITY OF LOCAL CIVIL SOCIETY AND COMMUNITY GROUPS ARE PARTICULARLY ENCOURAGED. Ten thousand dollars against an URGENT AND IMMEDIATE THREAT to a named biodiversity area. That is a small sum and a fast one — the size that pays for a survey, a lawyer's opinion or a delegation's travel at the moment a project appears. Know it exists before you need it. THE MECHANICS THAT SAVE TIME: CALLS ARE OPEN SEVERAL TIMES FOR EACH HOTSPOT, EACH CYCLE TYPICALLY OPEN FOR SIX TO EIGHT WEEKS; INTERACTIVE MAPS SHOW THE AREAS ELIGIBLE FOR FUNDING; AND THERE IS A PROJECTS DATABASE AND A PUBLISHED LIST OF GRANT RECIPIENTS. Check the map before drafting — eligibility is geographic and the boundary is published, so you can know in a minute whether your site qualifies. And the recipients list tells you which organisations near you have already been funded: those are the people to ask how they did it. WHO STANDS BEHIND IT: A JOINT INITIATIVE OF A FRENCH DEVELOPMENT AGENCY, A CONSERVATION INTERNATIONAL, THE EUROPEAN UNION, A GLOBAL ENVIRONMENT FACILITY, THE GOVERNMENT OF JAPAN, A MACARTHUR FOUNDATION AND THE WORLD BANK — FOUNDED IN 2000, AIMING AT EMPOWERING CIVIL SOCIETY IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES TO PROTECT THE WORLD'S BIODIVERSITY HOTSPOTS. AND ONE EXCLUSION WORTH KNOWING IN ADVANCE: PROJECTS FOCUSED ONLY ON THREATENED TREE SPECIES ARE NOT ELIGIBLE UNDER THE CURRENT WEST AFRICAN CALL. Read the exclusions in each call before writing. A fund that pays for forest work may still exclude a single-species tree project — which is the kind of detail that wastes a month if you find it at the end. WHO IT SUITS: cooperatives, community groups and associations in the twenty-two named countries, especially those inside a mapped Key Biodiversity Area. CAVEATS: CALLS OPEN AND CLOSE ON SIX-TO-EIGHT-WEEK CYCLES — subscribe or check the open-calls page rather than relying on a past deadline. For the €50,000 and €100,000–200,000 windows with no co-financing, Kenya's BIOPAMA entry; for the seven-country coastal coalition you join with one form, Senegal's PRCM entry.

trackers.name: OpenCorporates — 84 million companies and their directors, free to search under an open licence — with free API access for public-benefit projects, a checklist of where company data hides, and a published route for pushing a closed national registry open
trackers.desc: THE COMPANY ON YOUR LAND HAS DIRECTORS, AND THEY ARE PUBLISHED — adjacency declared first: A CONSERVATION FUND IS ALREADY A HOST IN THIS SAME BUCKET AND IS NOT SHIPPED HERE. A BILLION-RECORD SEARCH TOOL IS FILED UNDER BURKINA FASO AND AN INVESTOR TRACKER UNDER GUINEA — NEITHER IS A COMPANY REGISTRY AGGREGATOR. WHAT IT IS: PROBABLY THE LARGEST OPEN DATABASE OF COMPANIES IN THE WORLD — A FREE REPOSITORY OF COMPANY REGISTRIES AGGREGATED FROM PRIMARY PUBLIC SOURCES, PUBLISHED TO PROMOTE CORPORATE TRANSPARENCY, DRAWN FROM NATIONAL BUSINESS REGISTRIES IN 140+ JURISDICTIONS AND PRESENTED IN A STANDARDISED FORM. MORE THAN 84 MILLION COMPANIES AND DIRECTORS ARE SEARCHABLE. WHO IT NAMES AS ITS USERS, AND ACTIVIST IS ON THE LIST: IF YOU ARE AN INVESTIGATIVE JOURNALIST, RESEARCHER, AN ACTIVIST OR SIMPLY A CURIOUS CITIZEN YOU CAN DIVE INTO THE DATA AND DOWNLOAD IT UNDER AN OPEN DATABASE LICENCE. WHAT A RECORD CONTAINS, AND THE LAST ITEM IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: A COMPANY'S INCORPORATION DATE, ITS REGISTERED ADDRESSES AND ITS REGISTRY PAGE, AS WELL AS A LIST OF DIRECTORS AND OFFICERS. Names of directors. The company clearing your forest is an abstraction until you have the names of the people who signed for it — and those people have other companies, other addresses, and sometimes public positions. This file has recorded communities negotiating for years against a logo; the directors list is where a logo becomes people. THE PROVENANCE RULE, WHICH IS WHY IT CAN BE USED AS EVIDENCE RATHER THAN JUST A LEAD: IT IS CLEAR ABOUT THE PROVENANCE OF ITS DATA, SO YOU KNOW WHERE THEY COLLECTED EACH RECORD, AND WHEN. Every record says which official source it came from and on what date. That is what lets a lawyer or a journalist rely on it, and what separates it from a rumour about who owns the concession. THE FREE API FOR PUBLIC-BENEFIT WORK: FREE API ACCESS IS PROVIDED IF YOU ARE UNDERTAKING A PUBLIC BENEFIT PROJECT, AND ACCESS TO ALL THE DATA IS FREE FOR OPEN DATA PROJECTS UNDER THE SAME OPEN LICENCE CONDITIONS — AN API KEY IS REQUIRED. AND WHAT THAT SAVES, IN A PRACTITIONER'S OWN WORDS: BY ACCESSING THE API, WE ACHIEVED IN LESS THAN A DAY WHAT WOULD HAVE TAKEN TWO PEOPLE BETWEEN FOUR AND SIX MONTHS TO DO. Four to six person-months, done in a day, free, for anyone doing public-benefit work. If your coalition has one person who can write a little code, that application is the highest-return hour available. WHY IT EXISTS AT ALL, WHICH DESCRIBES YOUR OWN NATIONAL REGISTRY: OFFICIAL COMPANY REGISTRIES CAN BE UNWIELDY OR DIFFICULT TO NAVIGATE — LEGAL-ENTITY INFORMATION IS DISPERSED ACROSS HUNDREDS OF BUSINESS REGISTERS THAT ARE HARD TO NAVIGATE AND IMPOSSIBLE TO ACCESS AT SCALE. THE ROUTE FOR A CLOSED REGISTRY, WHICH IS THE FIND: WHERE A JURISDICTION'S DATA CANNOT BE OBTAINED, THEY PUT THAT JURISDICTION ON HOLD AND WORK WITH THEIR COMMUNITY NETWORKS TO SUPPORT THEIR EFFORTS IN WORKING WITH POLITICIANS AND GOVERNMENT BODIES TO OPEN UP REGISTER DATA — BY PROVIDING EVIDENCE ON THE BENEFITS GAINED THROUGH INCREASED TRANSPARENCY, THOUGHT LEADERSHIP, OR SUPPORT FOR PUBLICITY OR PRESSURE. If your country's register is shut, they will back a campaign to open it. That turns a dead end into a specific, winnable national ask with an international ally attached — and opening a register helps every community in the country at once, not only yours. AND THEY SAY PLAINLY THAT THEY NEED LOCAL PEOPLE: THEY COULD NOT DO WHAT THEY DO WITHOUT A WIDE NETWORK OF CORPORATE TRANSPARENCY CAMPAIGNERS, NGOs, OPEN DATA ACTIVISTS, EVEN GOVERNMENT ITSELF, TO GLEAN LOCAL KNOWLEDGE, TRANSLATION AND LANGUAGE SKILLS AND FRIENDLY ADVICE. THE SOURCES THEY HUNT FOR, WHICH IS A CHECKLIST FOR YOUR OWN SEARCH EVEN WITHOUT THEM: COMPANY REGISTRATION BODIES SUCH AS A NATIONAL REGISTER OR REGIONAL CHAMBERS OF COMMERCE; GOVERNMENT AGENCIES ACTING AS DATA AGGREGATORS SUCH AS NATIONAL STATISTICS BODIES; TAX AUTHORITIES; BUSINESS LICENSING BODIES PUBLISHING DATA ON COMPANIES LICENSED TO TRADE; AND OFFICIAL GOVERNMENT NOTICES SUCH AS GAZETTES OR COURT JUDGEMENTS AND LISTINGS. Five places company data hides, and the gazette is the one communities never think of. A licence, a transfer or a new director is often published there when it appears nowhere else — and gazettes are usually free at a government printer or a university library. THE LIMITS, RECORDED HONESTLY: ROUGHLY HALF OF THE REGISTRY SOURCES ARE NO LONGER ACTIVELY UPDATED; THERE IS NO BENEFICIAL OWNERSHIP TRACKING, ONLY BASIC PARENT-SUBSIDIARY RELATIONSHIPS WHERE EXPLICITLY STATED IN FILINGS; STANDARD API PLANS ALLOW 500 CALLS PER MONTH AND 200 PER DAY, WITH SEARCHES CONSUMING CREDITS WHETHER OR NOT THE FULL RECORD IS RETRIEVED; AND COMMERCIAL API ACCESS IS PRICED IN THOUSANDS OF POUNDS A YEAR. NO BENEFICIAL OWNERSHIP TRACKING is the limit to plan around: this tells you who is registered, not who ultimately profits. For that, pair it with the follow-the-money research service filed under Benin and the investor trackers under Guinea. AND ONE AFRICAN REGISTRY EXPLICITLY FROZEN, RECORDED AS A WARNING: ONE COUNTRY'S DATASET CAME FROM A PREDECESSOR REGISTRY AND IS TO BE CONSIDERED AS FOR HISTORICAL OR ARCHIVE PURPOSES ONLY, BECAUSE THE SUCCESSOR BODY INTRODUCED TERMS AND CONDITIONS THAT RESTRICTED RE-USE OF DATA, PREVENTING ONGOING UPDATES. A registry that was open and was closed by licence terms. Check the date on any record before relying on it — and note that closing public data is done quietly, by terms and conditions, not by announcement. WHO IT SUITS: African communities and coalitions who need the directors, addresses and corporate parentage of the company operating on their land. CAVEATS: HALF THE SOURCES ARE STALE, THERE IS NO ULTIMATE-OWNER DATA, AND SOME AFRICAN REGISTRIES ARE FROZEN — treat it as the starting point, not the answer. For a billion searchable records including land registries, Burkina Faso's entry; for the investor trackers and one-click financier identification, Guinea's entry; for research done for you on request, Benin's entry.

trackers.name: Recourse, Amsterdam — an organisation that co-creates campaigns with African partners rather than running its own — sitting inside the accountability-mechanism reviews of named European development finance institutions, and publishing community-safeguard demands timed to an African bank's annual meetings
trackers.desc: THEY CO-CREATE THE CAMPAIGN INSTEAD OF RUNNING IT — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S NIGERIA ENTRY COVERS THE AFRICAN DEVELOPMENT BANK'S OWN INDEPENDENT REVIEW MECHANISM, ITS GAMBIA ENTRY THAT BANK'S LEGAL SUPPORT FACILITY, ITS SEYCHELLES ENTRY THE FARMERS' PLATFORM HOLDING A MEMORANDUM WITH IT, ITS BURUNDI ENTRY THE DATABASE OF COMPLAINTS TO SUCH MECHANISMS, AND ITS ANGOLA AND BENIN ENTRIES THE COMMERCIAL-BANK AND SUPPLY-CHAIN ROUTES. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE WORKING METHOD, AND IT IS THE FIND: WE CO-CREATE CAMPAIGNS WITH PARTNERS ACROSS AFRICA, ASIA AND LATIN AMERICA, AND SUPPORT THEIR CRITICAL ENGAGEMENT WITH FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS — COLLABORATING WITH ORGANISATIONS AND NETWORKS THAT STAND UP FOR THE RIGHTS OF WOMEN, YOUTH, INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND AFFECTED COMMUNITIES. CO-CREATE, and SUPPORT THEIR ENGAGEMENT — the African partner deals with the bank, and this organisation supplies the analysis. That is the reverse of the pattern this file has recorded, where an international body negotiates and reports back. Ask which of the two is on offer before agreeing to anything. THE REMEDY COMMITMENT: ITS CAMPAIGNING FOCUSES ON IMPROVING DISCLOSURE AND ACCOUNTABILITY, AND SUPPORTING AFFECTED COMMUNITIES TO DEMAND AND ACCESS REMEDY WHEN INVESTMENTS CAUSE HARM. THE ACCOUNTABILITY-MECHANISM REVIEWS IT SITS IN, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IT IS ACTIVE IN SEVERAL ACCOUNTABILITY MECHANISM REVIEWS, INCLUDING THE JOINT MECHANISM OF THE FRENCH, GERMAN AND DUTCH DEVELOPMENT FINANCE INSTITUTIONS — AN INDEPENDENT COMPLAINTS MECHANISM — AND A EUROPEAN BANK'S INDEPENDENT PROJECT ACCOUNTABILITY MECHANISM. The rules of the complaint route are periodically rewritten, and somebody is in the room when it happens. A community that found a mechanism useless has somewhere to send that experience while the mechanism is under review — which changes the route for everyone who comes after, and this file's Burundi entry holds the record of what such complaints have achieved. AND A JOINT FRENCH, GERMAN AND DUTCH MECHANISM covering three countries' development finance in one place. For francophone African communities facing a French-financed project, that is one address rather than three. THE BENCHMARKING TACTIC, WORTH COPYING AT ANY SCALE: IT AND PARTNER ORGANISATIONS BENCHMARK THE INSTITUTIONS' POLICIES AGAINST EACH OTHER TO DRIVE UP BEST PRACTICE — AND IT CHALLENGED ONE EUROPEAN BANK ON LACK OF TRANSPARENCY BY BENCHMARKING IT AGAINST OTHER INSTITUTIONS. Comparison as the argument. An institution will defend a bad policy on its merits and abandon it when shown that its peers do better — the same move this file records under the mining law atlas, where a ministry is shown what neighbouring countries already require. THE FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARY PROBLEM IT NAMES, WITH THE FIGURE THAT MATTERS: THE BANKS USE FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARY LENDING TO ATTRACT ADDITIONAL PRIVATE INVESTMENT AND CLAIM TO INFLUENCE ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL STANDARDS ACROSS THE PRIVATE SECTOR — AND ONE CORPORATION ESTIMATES THAT, FROM 2014 TO 2024, INVESTMENTS TOTALLING $4.5 TRILLION ACROSS EMERGING MARKETS USE ITS OWN PERFORMANCE STANDARDS. FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARY LENDING is why the trail goes cold. A development bank lends to a local bank, which lends to the company on your land — and the safeguards, the disclosure and the complaint route all attach to the first loan, not the second. If your tracing stopped at a national bank, that is the structure you hit, and the development bank behind it is still reachable. THE AFRICAN DEMANDS IT PUBLISHES, TIMED TO A BANK'S ANNUAL MEETINGS: A HALT ON FURTHER LNG FINANCING AND A FOSSIL GAS EXCLUSION POLICY FOR UPSTREAM GAS; AN ENERGY SECTOR POLICY EXCLUDING ALL FOSSIL FUELS; FOSSIL GAS AND FALSE SOLUTIONS EXCLUDED FROM A NAMED ELECTRIFICATION MISSION'S INVESTMENTS AND COUNTRY COMPACTS; AND ROBUST ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SAFEGUARDS FOR ALL LARGE RENEWABLE ENERGY AND TRANSMISSION PROJECTS. SAFEGUARDS FOR RENEWABLE ENERGY AND TRANSMISSION is the demand for communities. A solar field or a transmission corridor takes land exactly as a mine does, and is far likelier to be waved through as climate action — this file has recorded that pattern under its carbon and conservation entries. AND COUNTRY COMPACTS named as a target. Your government is signing an electrification compact with that bank; what it contains is negotiable now and fixed later. THE FIGURES IT ORGANISES AROUND: SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA IS HOME TO ABOUT 600 MILLION PEOPLE WITHOUT ELECTRICITY AND NEARLY 970 MILLION WITHOUT CLEAN COOKING, WITH A BANK CO-LEADING A MISSION TO DELIVER ELECTRICITY TO 300 MILLION AFRICANS BY 2030 — AND DECENTRALISED RENEWABLE ENERGY IS WIDELY RECOGNISED AS PART OF THE ANSWER. DECENTRALISED is the word to hold onto: power generated near the village rather than a corridor crossing it to reach a city. A community facing a transmission line can argue for the alternative rather than only against the route. THE GENDER WORK AND ITS BLUNT FINDING: WHILE SOME MULTILATERAL DEVELOPMENT BANKS MIGHT TALK THE TALK ABOUT WOMEN'S RIGHTS OR DIVERSITY, IN PRACTICE THEIR PROMISES ARE OFTEN NOT MET — AND THE CURRENT LACK OF SENSITIVITY TO GENDER AND IDENTITY MEANS THAT PUBLIC FINANCE OFTEN REINFORCES DISCRIMINATION AND INEQUALITY. A REPORT PUBLISHED WITH PARTNERS ASKS WHY PUBLIC FINANCE FOR FOSSIL GAS IS NOT THE SOLUTION FOR WOMEN IN ASIA AND AFRICA. THE COALITION IT BELONGS TO: A GLOBAL COALITION OF OVER 50 CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS AND THINK TANKS CAMPAIGNING FOR THESE BANKS TO SHIFT FINANCE OUT OF FOSSIL FUELS AND FACILITATE A JUST TRANSITION. AND THE AFRICAN CRITIQUE IT PUBLISHES IN AFRICAN VOICES: A PARALLEL PEOPLE'S SUMMIT PROVIDED THE OPPORTUNITY TO BRING FORWARD DECLARATIONS THAT REPRESENT THE PEOPLE OF AFRICA, WHILE THE OFFICIAL SUMMIT GAVE PLATFORMS TO THOSE THAT PUSH THE FOSSIL FUEL INDUSTRIES WITHOUT HOLDING THEM TO ACCOUNT — AND A NAMED AFRICAN UNIVERSITY VOICE WARNED THAT THE PUSH FOR GAS AND CARBON CREDIT INITIATIVES IN AFRICA POSES MORE THREATS TO DEVELOPMENT AND LIVELIHOODS. A PARALLEL PEOPLE'S SUMMIT, held alongside the official one. That is a repeatable tactic: when a continental conference excludes you, the counter-gathering next door gets the same journalists and produces a declaration your delegation actually signed. WHO IT SUITS: African organisations engaging a development bank over an energy, gas, transmission or extractive project — particularly those wanting analysis behind their own campaign rather than somebody else's. CAVEATS: FOCUSED ON PUBLIC AND DEVELOPMENT FINANCE AND ON ENERGY, AND IT WORKS THROUGH PARTNER ORGANISATIONS RATHER THAN TAKING CASES — approach with a national partner. For that bank's own review mechanism, Nigeria's entry; for the database of what such complaints achieved, Burundi's entry; for the commercial bank side, Angola's entry.

trackers.name: Cash sent directly to rainforest communities with no requirements on how it is spent — paid either to elected community leaders or to individuals — on the stated reasoning that loggers offer money to leave and this is money to stay
trackers.desc: LOGGERS OFFER MONEY TO LEAVE. THIS IS MONEY TO STAY — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC ENTRY CARRIES A RAINFOREST FOUNDATION HOST AND A PRO BONO CENTRE HOST; ITS KENYA ENTRY A WILDLIFE FOUNDATION AND A FOREST PEOPLES HOST; ITS REPUBLIC OF CONGO ENTRY A LAND-RIGHTS HOST AND A FOREST MONITORING HOST. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. METHOD NOTE: PRECHECK WAS RUN BEFORE THIS ENTRY WAS WRITTEN, AND THIS HOST APPEARS IN NONE OF THE 53 AFRICA BUCKETS. THE NO-CONDITIONS RULE, WHICH IS THE FIND: UNCONDITIONAL CASH TRANSFERS ARE PAYMENTS WE SEND DIRECTLY TO PEOPLE LIVING IN THE RAINFOREST. THERE'S NO CATCH OR REQUIREMENTS ON HOW THE CASH IS SPENT. No workplan, no budget lines, no reporting on expenditure categories. Every other funder in this file decides in advance what the money may buy; here the community decides afterwards. That is the difference between being funded and being resourced. THE REASON IT EXISTS, IN ITS OWN WORDS, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: WHILST ILLEGAL LOGGERS OFFER COMMUNITIES MONEY TO LEAVE, WE PROVIDE FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO HELP COMMUNITIES STAY. That is the mechanism stated in one line, and it is the answer to a pattern this file records constantly: a company arrives with cash for a household that has none, and the household cannot afford to refuse. Income that arrives without the forest being sold restores the ability to say no — which is worth more than any legal argument to a family choosing between school fees and a concession payment. THE TWO ROUTES THE MONEY TAKES: THE FIRST WAY IS BY SENDING CASH TRANSFERS TO THE LEADERS OF THE COMMUNITY, A GROUP OF PEOPLE WHO ARE ELECTED TO MAKE DECISIONS, AND THE WHOLE COMMUNITY COMES TOGETHER TO PLAN HOW THEY WILL INVEST THE FUNDS; THE SECOND WAY IS EVEN MORE DIRECT — WE SEND MONEY TO INDIVIDUALS, RATHER THAN COMMUNITY LEADERS. ELECTED leaders, and a whole-community planning meeting. Worth noting which route a community would want: money through the committee builds collective assets and can be captured by whoever controls the committee; money to individuals cannot be captured but does not build anything shared. Both are on offer, and that choice is one to make deliberately rather than accept. THE STATED TRUST: IN A CHALLENGING PLACE LIKE THE RAINFOREST, ONLY THE PEOPLE WHO LIVE THERE KNOW WHAT'S BEST FOR THEM — WE RESPECT AND TRUST THEIR ABILITY TO DECIDE HOW BEST TO SPEND THE CASH BASED ON THEIR UNIQUE CIRCUMSTANCES. THE AFRICAN FOOTPRINT: PARTNERSHIPS IN PERU, PAPUA NEW GUINEA AND THE CONGO BASIN, WITH A NAMED PARTNERSHIP IN CAMEROON DELIVERED IN COLLABORATION WITH A NAMED LOCAL ORGANISATION, AND A FIVE-YEAR PLAN AIMING TO PROVIDE UNCONDITIONAL CASH TRANSFERS TO RAINFOREST VILLAGES IN THE THREE LARGEST EXPANSES OF TROPICAL FOREST INCLUDING THE CONGO BASIN. Africa is the newest of the three regions and the programme is expanding into it, which means the Congo Basin is where new partnerships are being formed rather than where the roster is closed. Cameroon is the named foothold; the local collaborator there is the realistic first contact. WHAT A COMMUNITY DID WITH ITS MONEY, AS THE ONLY EXAMPLE THEY GIVE: ONE COMMUNITY USED 80% OF THEIR CASH TO BUY 20 GIANT WATER TANKS, MEANING ACCESS TO SAFE DRINKING WATER. Water tanks, not conservation equipment. A funder that publishes that as its example is telling you it will not object when the money goes on something a conservation proposal would never have listed. THE FIGURE THEY BUILD THE ARGUMENT ON: INDIGENOUS PEOPLES MANAGE 54% OF RAINFORESTS AROUND THE WORLD BUT RECEIVE LESS THAN 1% OF CLIMATE FUNDING — AND IT IS TIME TO SHIFT CONTROL, DECISION-MAKING AND POWER TO THE PEOPLE AT THE FRONTLINE OF DEFORESTATION. Fifty-four per cent managed, under one per cent funded. Read it beside the funding figures filed under Ethiopia — the same gap, counted a different way, by a different organisation. THE RESULT THEY CLAIM AND WHERE: SINCE 2007 THEY HAVE PROVIDED CASH DIRECTLY AND UNCONDITIONALLY, HELPING TO MAINTAIN FOREST LOSS RATES BELOW 1% IN THEIR PARTNERSHIPS IN PERU, PAPUA NEW GUINEA AND THE CONGO BASIN — WITH ELEVEN CASH TRANSFER PROJECTS PROTECTING 337,000 HECTARES. Recorded as their own claim rather than an independent finding. The published research page below is where to check it, and a community should read the evaluation before assuming the result transfers to its own circumstances. THE FOREST DATA PROGRAMME: EQUIPPING COMMUNITIES WITH THE TOOLS, INFRASTRUCTURE, AND TRAINING NEEDED TO ACCESS AND ACT ON REAL-TIME LAND-USE DATA — COMBINING TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE WITH MODERN TECHNOLOGY, ENABLING COMMUNITIES TO DETECT FOREST THREATS, PREVENT CLIMATE-DRIVEN FIRES, AND PROTECT THEIR TERRITORIES. REAL-TIME land-use data in community hands, with the infrastructure to receive it. Alerts are useless where there is no connection and nobody trained to read them; this addresses both, and it is what turns a satellite warning into somebody arriving at the clearing. THE PROJECTS THAT COME FROM COMMUNITY REQUEST: IN ADDITION TO CASH AND DATA, IT SUPPORTS PROJECTS IDENTIFIED BY ITS RAINFOREST PARTNERS TO ADDRESS LOCAL PRIORITIES — IMPLEMENTED ACROSS PERU, PAPUA NEW GUINEA AND CAMEROON, RANGING FROM SUSTAINABLE FARMING TO HANDICRAFTS, SOLAR LIGHTING AND WATER, SANITATION AND HYGIENE — STEMMING FROM DIRECT COMMUNITY REQUESTS. WHAT A PARTNER SAID ABOUT THEM: WHAT I VALUE MOST ABOUT COOL EARTH IS THEIR TRANSPARENCY AND THE RESPECT THEY HAVE FOR US. THEY HAVE NEVER TOLD US TO DO THINGS THEIR WAY. THEY HAVE ALWAYS RESPECTED OUR DECISIONS; OUR INDIGENOUS AUTONOMY. A partner's own words, published by the funder. Ask an existing partner directly before entering any relationship in this file — and here there are named partnerships to ask at. AND THE PUBLISHED RESEARCH ANYONE CAN USE: A RESOURCES AND RESEARCH PAGE CARRYING A CASH-TRANSFER STRATEGY FOR RAINFOREST PROTECTION, A MIDTERM EVALUATION OF THE BASIC INCOME PILOT, A REVIEW OF THEIR CASH GIVING OVER TWELVE YEARS, A SCOPING STUDY OF CONSERVATION PROFESSIONALS' VIEWS ON CASH GIVING, AND A PAPER ON DIRECT CASH TRANSFERS TO ADDRESS LOSS AND DAMAGE — ALONGSIDE INDEPENDENT WORK ON REDUCED DEFORESTATION IN INDIGENOUS LANDS PAN-TROPICALLY. The evidence base is published, including a study of what conservation professionals think of the whole idea — which means the objections are documented too. An organisation proposing unconditional cash to a sceptical ministry or donor has the counter-arguments already assembled. WHO IT SUITS: Congo Basin forest communities, and Central and West African organisations working alongside them, seeking income that does not require selling or clearing land. CAVEATS: PARTNERSHIPS ARE FORMED WITH COMMUNITIES IN NAMED RAINFOREST REGIONS RATHER THAN THROUGH OPEN APPLICATION, AFRICA IS THE NEWEST AND SMALLEST OF THE THREE, AND THE HEADLINE RESULTS ARE THE ORGANISATION'S OWN — read the evaluations. For the fund that waives registration entirely, the Central African Republic's entry; for the funder publishing its unrestricted percentages, Gambia's entry.

trackers.name: Barristers who send an observation unit to sit in your trial and file amicus briefs into national courts — with one already submitted over a mining company's failure to consult Indigenous and Afro-descendant communities, and a published contact address
trackers.desc: THEY SEND AN OBSERVER TO THE TRIAL AND A BRIEF INTO THE COURT — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S BOTSWANA ENTRY COVERS THE FRANCOPHONE CAPACITY ORGANISATION WHOSE WORK INCLUDES TRIAL FAIRNESS, AND ITS CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC ENTRY THE ASSOCIATION SUING FRENCH PARENT COMPANIES; ITS ZAMBIA BUCKET MENTIONS AN INTERNATIONAL BAR ASSOCIATION, ITS KENYA BUCKET A COMMISSION OF JURISTS NAME, ITS DJIBOUTI BUCKET A PROTECTION ORGANISATION HOST. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE AMICUS ON RECORD, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT INTERVENES IN LITIGATION THROUGH AMICUS CURIAE BRIEFS DRAFTED BY ITS MEMBERS — ONE SUCH BRIEF WAS SUBMITTED TO A NATIONAL CONSTITUTIONAL COURT IN RELATION TO A NAMED MINING CORPORATION'S FAILURE PROPERLY TO CONSULT THE INDIGENOUS AND AFRO-DESCENDANT COMMUNITIES OF A NAMED REGION. Not a statement about the case — a brief filed INTO the national court hearing it, written by senior barristers, on precisely the failure-to-consult ground that this file records deciding project cases across Africa. A community with a case already running can ask for that intervention; it costs the community nothing and arrives as an argument the judge must read. THE TRIAL OBSERVATION UNIT, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IT SENDS ITS TRIAL OBSERVATION UNIT TO WITNESS AND MONITOR UNJUST OR UNFAIR TRIALS WHEREVER THEY OCCUR, SENDING INTERNATIONAL LAW EXPERTS TO MONITOR PROCEEDINGS AND REPORT BACK ON VIOLATIONS OF THE PROSECUTING COUNTRY'S INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS OBLIGATIONS. This file has recorded organisers prosecuted to break a land campaign — fabricated charges, closed hearings, no lawyer. A foreign barrister sitting in the public gallery taking notes changes how that hearing is conducted, and the request costs nothing but the asking. WHAT THE OBSERVATION PRODUCES: THE AIM IS TO REPORT INDEPENDENTLY ON THE ADHERENCE OF HEARINGS TO INTERNATIONAL FAIR TRIAL STANDARDS — AND THE TRIAL REPORTS ARE WIDELY CIRCULATED AND HAVE BEEN REFERENCED IN COURT PROCEEDINGS. The report outlives the hearing and gets cited in later proceedings. For an appeal, or for a continental court filing, an independent record of what went wrong at first instance is evidence the community could not otherwise produce. THE EFFECT ON RECORD: AT ONE OBSERVED TRIAL OF DEFENDANTS FROM A CIVIL LIBERTIES MOVEMENT, ALL 35 DEFENDANTS WERE SUBSEQUENTLY AMONG 178 DETAINEES WHO RECEIVED A ROYAL PARDON — AND THE INTERNATIONAL PRESENCE UNDOUBTEDLY ILLUMINATED ALLEGATIONS OF HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS. Thirty-five defendants observed, then pardoned. Causation is claimed carefully rather than proven, and it is recorded here in the same terms — but it is the closest thing in this file to a measured outcome from observation. THE OTHER THINGS IT WILL PRODUCE FOR A CASE: STATEMENTS, LETTERS OF CONCERN AND AMICUS BRIEFS IN SUPPORT OF PEOPLE FACING UNFAIR TRIALS AND IMPRISONMENT; INTERNATIONAL TRAINING, SUPPORT AND LEADERSHIP TO LAWYERS, HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS AND CIVIL SOCIETY GROUPS UNDER THREAT; INVESTIGATIONS AND DETAILED PUBLISHED REPORTS; AND LOBBYING OF GOVERNMENTS TO IMPROVE FAIR TRIAL PROTECTIONS. Four distinct asks, of ascending size. A letter of concern is the smallest and fastest, and is worth requesting early rather than saving for a crisis. WHY THE LETTERS MATTER: PUBLIC STATEMENTS AND LETTERS OF CONCERN ARE AN IMPORTANT MEANS OF HOLDING GOVERNMENTS TO ACCOUNT, HIGHLIGHTING SPECIFIC LEGAL CONCERNS AND DRAWING INTERNATIONAL ATTENTION ON ALLEGED VIOLATIONS — OFTEN IN COLLABORATION WITH INTERNATIONAL PARTNERS, HARNESSING INTERNATIONAL OPINION, LEGAL EXPERTISE AND MEDIA REACH TO HIGHLIGHT UNDER-REPORTED VIOLATIONS. UNDER-REPORTED is the operative word: a rural land prosecution that no national paper covers is the kind of matter they say they exist to raise. THE GEOGRAPHIC RULE, WHICH IS UNUSUAL: THE REMIT EXTENDS TO ALL COUNTRIES OF THE WORLD, APART FROM ITS OWN JURISDICTION OF ENGLAND AND WALES — REFLECTING THE COMMITTEE'S NEED TO MAINTAIN ITS ROLE AS AN INDEPENDENT BUT LEGALLY QUALIFIED OBSERVER AND CRITIC. Every African country is inside the remit, with no focus-country list to fall outside of. That is rarer in this file than any amount of money. WHO IT IS MADE OF: BARRISTERS CALLED TO THE BAR OF ENGLAND AND WALES, PUPIL BARRISTERS, LAW STUDENTS AND LEGAL ACADEMICS — THE INDEPENDENT, INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS ARM OF THAT BAR. In common-law African jurisdictions, a brief from senior counsel of that bar carries persuasive weight, because the caselaw and procedure are recognisably related to your own. HOW IT IS RESOURCED, RECORDED PLAINLY: FOUNDED IN 1992, DISTINCT FROM THE BAR COUNCIL WITH ITS OWN CONSTITUTION AND ELECTIONS, BUT DEPENDING ON THE BAR COUNCIL FOR FUNDING FOR ITS ONE MEMBER OF STAFF AND ITS TRIAL OBSERVATION UNIT — AND OTHERWISE RELYING ON MEMBERSHIP SUBSCRIPTIONS AND INDIVIDUAL DONATIONS. ONE MEMBER OF STAFF. That is the honest scale, and it sets expectations: the barristers are volunteers with practices of their own, so requests need to arrive early, be specific, and name the dates. Do not expect a rapid response to an emergency. WHAT IT SAYS IT PROTECTS: ADVOCATES, JUDGES, HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS AND VULNERABLE COMMUNITIES AROUND THE WORLD. ADVOCATES AND JUDGES first. Where a community's own lawyer is being prosecuted, disbarred or threatened — which this file records as a standard tactic — that lawyer is the subject this committee exists for, not a bystander to it. THE REPORTS IT PRODUCES: IN-DEPTH REPORTS ON GLOBAL HUMAN RIGHTS ISSUES, PROVIDING EXPERT ANALYSIS OF ONGOING OR HISTORIC ABUSES, CONNECTING DETAILED IN-COUNTRY RESEARCH TO EXPERTISE ON MATTERS OF INTERNATIONAL LAW — AND IT RAISES AWARENESS THROUGH FACT-FINDING MISSIONS. A FACT-FINDING MISSION is a distinct request from a trial observation: it brings qualified people to the place rather than the courtroom, which suits a situation that has not yet reached court. AND THE PUBLISHED CONTACT: A COORDINATION EMAIL ADDRESS PUBLISHED FOR QUESTIONS AND FURTHER ASSISTANCE, ALONGSIDE AN EXPRESSION OF INTEREST FORM — WITH MEMBERSHIP OPEN TO EVERY PRACTISING OR NON-PRACTISING MEMBER OF THAT BAR, AND MEMBERS RECEIVING OPPORTUNITIES TO ASSIST WITH ITS INTERNATIONAL PROJECTS. A single published email for the whole committee. And the membership point cuts usefully: any barrister of that bar sympathetic to your case can join and volunteer for its international projects, which is a specific thing to ask of a supporter abroad. WHO IT SUITS: African communities and organisations whose members or lawyers face prosecution over a land or environmental campaign, and those with a case where an outside legal argument would help. CAVEATS: ONE MEMBER OF STAFF AND VOLUNTEER BARRISTERS, SO CAPACITY IS SMALL AND SLOW; IT OBSERVES, INTERVENES AND REPORTS RATHER THAN REPRESENTING YOU, AND IT WILL NOT ACT IN ENGLAND AND WALES. For lawyers who build cases from outside the jurisdiction, Chad's entry; for suing a French parent company, the Central African Republic's entry.

trackers.name: RADDHO (Rencontre Africaine pour la Défense des Droits de l'Homme), Dakar — lends legal aid to victims as a stated method, covers Senegal, Gambia and Guinea-Bissau, and holds UN ECOSOC consultative status plus observer membership at the African Commission
trackers.desc: LEGAL AID TO VICTIMS, AND A SEAT AT THE COMMISSION THAT HEARS THEM — method and adjacency declared first: FIFTH NAMED-ATTORNEY ROUND, AIMED AT FRANCOPHONE WEST AFRICA. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN FIVE HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL FIVE HOSTS AND FOUR FACTS ABSENT, WITH TWO GENERIC STATUS TERMS APPEARING IN OTHER ENTRIES ON OTHER HOSTS. THIS FILE'S ERITREA ENTRY COVERS THE CONTINENTAL COMMISSION'S OWN COMPLAINT PROCEDURE. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE SERVICE, WHICH IS THE FIND: AMONG THE LEGAL MEANS IT USES TO REACH ITS AIMS IS TO LEND LEGAL AID TO THE VICTIMS OF RIGHTS VIOLATIONS — STATED AS ONE OF ITS OWN LISTED METHODS RATHER THAN AS A PROGRAMME THAT MAY OR MAY NOT BE FUNDED. Legal aid written into the constitution's list of methods, not offered as a project. When a grant ends, a programme stops; a stated method does not, which is the distinction to look for when reading any organisation's founding text. THE TWO STANDINGS IT HOLDS, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: SPECIAL CONSULTATIVE STATUS WITH THE UNITED NATIONS ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL COUNCIL, OBTAINED IN 2003, AND OBSERVER MEMBER STATUS AT THE AFRICAN COMMISSION ON HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS. Observer status at the Commission is the practical one. This file's Eritrea entry records that a community needs no accreditation to complain there — but an organisation that sits in the room as an observer knows the session calendar, the registrars and the state's habits, and can raise a matter in the public sessions as well as file it. Ask any prospective helper whether it holds that status. THE COUNTRIES IT COVERS: A REFERENCE LISTING NAMES THREE — THE GAMBIA, GUINEA-BISSAU AND SENEGAL — WITH THE ASSOCIATION DESCRIBED AS PAN-AFRICAN AND DEVOTED TO PROMOTION, DEFENCE AND PROTECTION OF HUMAN RIGHTS IN ITS OWN COUNTRY AND ACROSS THE CONTINENT. Three countries in one association, all francophone or lusophone West Africa. A community in the smaller two has a body already working there rather than needing to attract one. WHERE TO FIND IT: A PUBLISHED VILLA NUMBER, QUARTER, AVENUE, CITY DISTRICT AND POSTAL CODE IN THE CAPITAL, WITH A PUBLISHED TELEPHONE AND FAX. A street address rather than a post box. It can be walked into. WHO FOUNDED IT AND FROM WHERE: A NON-PARTISAN AND SECULAR NGO CREATED ON 21 APRIL 1990 BY A GROUP OF AFRICAN INTELLECTUALS, CONSTITUTED IN THE MAJORITY OF RESEARCHERS AND TEACHERS AT UNIVERSITÉ CHEIKH ANTA DIOP, DAKAR — A PIONEERING ORGANISATION OF ITS COUNTRY'S CIVIL SOCIETY. University researchers founding a rights association is a route worth noting in itself: the academics had standing, security and the ability to publish, and they built an organisation with it. Where no NGO exists near a community, the nearest law or social science faculty is a place to start looking. THE FOUR AIMS IT PUBLISHES: WATCHING OVER RESPECT FOR LIFE AND HUMAN DIGNITY; PROMOTING THE FULL AND ENTIRE EXERCISE OF CITIZENSHIP, NOTABLY EFFECTIVE EQUALITY OF RIGHTS BETWEEN CITIZENS; CONTRIBUTING TO THE EMERGENCE AND CONSOLIDATION OF THE RULE OF LAW AND DEMOCRACY IN AFRICA; AND CONTRIBUTING TO THE BRINGING TOGETHER OF AFRICAN PEOPLES. THE CHARTER WORK IT COMMITS TO: TO MAKE KNOWN THE AFRICAN CHARTER ON HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS AND ANY INTERNATIONAL TEXT OF CERTAIN INTEREST FOR HUMAN RIGHTS, AND TO ENSURE THEIR EFFECTIVE APPLICATION IN THE STATES PARTIES. PEOPLES' rights, plural and collective, are what the African Charter carries and most national constitutions do not. A community claiming as a people rather than as individual landholders is using the instrument this organisation exists to publicise. THE INFORMATION FUNCTION: TO COLLECT, DISSEMINATE AND EXCHANGE ALL INFORMATION RELATIVE TO THE SITUATION OF HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS IN AFRICA AND EVERYWHERE IN THE WORLD — AND TO CONTRIBUTE TO HUMAN RIGHTS EDUCATION. THE MOBILISATION IT UNDERTAKES: TO MOBILISE NATIONAL, AFRICAN AND INTERNATIONAL PUBLIC OPINION TO DENOUNCE ALL CASES OF VIOLATION AND TO HAVE ADOPTED CONSTITUTIONAL AND LEGISLATIVE TEXTS GUARANTEEING THEIR RESPECT. Getting texts ADOPTED, not merely protesting their absence. Read beside this file's Rwanda entry, where a federation arrived at a hearing with drafted wording: the organisations that change law are the ones that bring the words. THE TRIAL AND JUDICIARY WORK: IT ENSURES RESPECT FOR THE INDEPENDENCE OF THE JUDICIARY AND A FAIR TRIAL FOR ALL, AND CONDUCTS STUDIES, INVESTIGATIONS AND ANALYSES THAT ALLOW EMERGENCY ALERT AND CONFLICT PREVENTION — ITS ACTIVITIES DESCRIBED UNDER THE HEADINGS INFORMATION, TRAINING, ADVICE AND RESEARCH. EMERGENCY ALERT sits alongside the slow work. An organisation with both a research function and an alert function can be contacted when something is about to happen, not only afterwards. THE ELECTION OBSERVATION IT DOES, AND WHAT IT COST: IT OBSERVED THE COUNTRY'S LEGISLATIVE AND LOCAL ELECTIONS IN 2001, AND ITS OBSERVER ROLE BECAME THE OBJECT OF A MAJOR POLITICAL CONFLICT IN 2011–2012 WHEN THE SPOKESMAN OF THE THEN PRESIDENCY PUBLICLY DECLARED AN INTENTION TO WITHDRAW THAT ACCREDITATION, ACCUSING IT OF BIAS. Filed because it is the cost of the work. A government that dislikes an organisation's findings moves against its accreditation rather than its arguments, and a community should know which of its allies are currently exposed in that way. AND THE RECORD IT HAS BUILT: SINCE ITS FIRST YEARS IT HAS BUILT A RECORD OF CONCRETE INTERVENTIONS COVERING BOTH THE NATIONAL FIELD AND INTERNATIONAL ARENAS — ITS INTERNATIONAL RECOGNITION ATTESTED BY THE TWO STANDINGS ABOVE. WHO IT SUITS: francophone and lusophone West African communities needing legal aid and a route into the continental commission, and anyone looking for an organisation that already sits in the forum where their complaint would be heard. CAVEATS: A HUMAN RIGHTS ASSOCIATION WITH A CIVIL AND POLITICAL FRAME RATHER THAN LAND, PLANNING OR ENVIRONMENT; IT LENDS LEGAL AID AND INTERVENES RATHER THAN OPERATING AS A LAW FIRM, AND SOME PUBLISHED MATERIAL IS OLDER — CHECK CURRENT COVERAGE AND CONTACTS. For the commission's own complaint procedure without a lawyer, Eritrea's entry; for a foundation that employs its own advocates, Benin's entry.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a pan-African feminist rapid-response fund with reach across all 54 African countries — small grants released quickly for unanticipated, time-critical situations rather than planned programme work, covering safety and protection needs when defenders are threatened and short windows for advocacy after an unexpected event. WHO IT SUITS: women's rights organisations, feminist collectives and movements in which women or gender-diverse people are the primary decision-makers. It does NOT fund individuals, and the action must be strategic, genuinely unanticipated, and completable in under three months. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is emergency money for a moment, not a budget for a campaign — decisions are fast and grants are modest.

trackers.name: Centre pour l'Environnement et le Développement (CED)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: founded in 1994 in response to Cameroon's forest-management crisis and now working across land tenure, forests and the extractive industries — oil, gold and other mining — from Yaoundé. It supports communities and local associations in their dealings with the administration, forestry and extractive companies, conservation projects and industrial plantations, and campaigns for recognition of customary and Indigenous forest land rights in Cameroon's land reform. USE IT: the site carries a legal library covering national legislation, international texts, natural-resource contracts and court decisions; a map library including forest-cover and land-allocation mapping by department; and policy briefs on customary tenure, women's land rights and illegal gold mining. It also runs the Coalition Foncière Nationale and the LandCam platform. Its stated support extends to local NGOs elsewhere in the Congo Basin, but this entry is placed for Cameroon only, which is what its own site evidences.

trackers.name: Chambre des comptes de la Cour suprême du Cameroun
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Cameroon — audits government accounts and the use of public money.

trackers.name: Commission Nationale Anti-Corruption (CONAC)
trackers.desc: National anti-corruption body of Cameroon — investigates graft, financial crime and abuse of public office.

trackers.name: Cameroon — Ministry of Finance (MINFI)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the General Budget Directorate prepares the State budget and MINFI publishes budget-execution & public-finance reports, Cameroon. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Cameroon.

trackers.name: Cameroon — Business Creation e-Portal (CFCE / mybusiness.cm)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the official electronic one-stop window (Centres de Formalités de Création d’Entreprises) for online company creation & registration, Cameroon. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: MUSEBA Journalism Project
trackers.desc: Cameroonian watchdog newsroom covering large-scale corruption and illicit financial flows in Central Africa.

trackers.name: COMIFAC Treaty and Plan de Convergence — and its community protocol
trackers.desc: A TREATY BODY WITH A TEMPLATE YOU CAN COPY. The Traité relatif à la conservation et à la gestion durable des écosystèmes forestiers d'Afrique Centrale, signed by heads of state at their second summit on 5 February 2005 in Brazzaville, instituted the Commission des Forêts d'Afrique Centrale — described as the unique instance d'orientation, de décision et de coordination for subregional forest action, and the cadre politique et juridique global for cooperation in the field. A transboundary forest question belongs in that forum. The Plan de Convergence is the reference framework for all such interventions — first edition 2005–2014, revised in 2014 for 2015–2025 and restructured into 10 strategic axes, executed by a Secrétariat exécutif. CIVIL SOCIETY IS A NAMED STAKEHOLDER in implementing it, alongside state administrations, CEEAC and the private sector — so participation is built into the framework, not conceded case by case. Axis 7 covers capacity and participation des acteurs, expressly contemplating micro-projets générateurs de revenus pour les populations locales; axis 9 covers innovative financing mechanisms. THE DOCUMENT LIBRARY IS THE MOST USEFUL PART: COMIFAC publishes a worked Protocole Bioculturel Communautaire for a named village, a guide to inventorying genetic resources and traditional knowledge, a paper on les droits d'usage des peuples autochtones et communautés locales et les obligations qui en découlent, a subregional APA (access and benefit-sharing) strategy, and directives on forests and the SDGs built with FAO as 5 principles and 12 directives across 31 prioritised targets. A community biocultural protocol published by a treaty body is a template, not a theory. AND ITS OWN DIAGNOSIS IS QUOTABLE: the Plan records that participatory natural resource management and mediation of use conflicts, though already mapped out, are insufficiently developed.

trackers.name: FODER and the SNOIE system — a villager's alert can become a ministry control mission, a suspension and a fine, through a certified procedure
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Forêts et Développement Rural, the Cameroonian association that developed the Système Normalisé d'Observation Indépendante Externe (SNOIE) — a standardised, ISO 9001:2015 certified set of procedures for documenting illegal exploitation of natural resources and directing the resulting complaint to the right authority. The certification is the trick: it makes a civil society report hard to dismiss as hearsay. HOW A COMMUNITY ENTERS IT: SNOIE missions are triggered by complaints from individuals or by community alerts — in one documented case a FODER field mission was launched after 38 alerts collected and sent by a single community member through a real-time forest monitoring platform. Communities are the sensor; the certified procedure is what converts what they see into something the state must answer. WHAT IT HAS PRODUCED, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: denunciation reports submitted to the forests ministry led to two logging companies being suspended with legal proceedings opened against them — the suspension explicitly lasting until the case is resolved; more than half of SNOIE reports in its first three years drew a response from the ministry; and between 2016 and 2019 the reports contributed 72.5 million FCFA in forest revenue to the state through fines and public auction of illegally cut timber seized after the resulting control missions. An enforcement route that makes money for the ministry is one the ministry keeps using. Infractions documented include unauthorised logging in the national forest estate, logging outside title boundaries, breach of forest operating standards, and logging in community forests without the annual exploitation certificate — so it works against abuses of community forests too. It runs with other Cameroonian organisations including CeDLA, ECODEV and PAPEL, and the system has been extended to the Republic of the Congo. WHO IT SUITS: forest communities in Cameroon that can see illegal cutting and need it acted on.
