A minuted count of who disagreed, certified by the affected people's own representatives, is the document a community should insist on. Representatives of the affected people sit on the council itself. Published legal description records the council's membership as including a representative of the land users whose land is recovered, a representative of the people's council, a representative of the fatherland front committee at district level, representatives of socio-political organisations, and other members decided by the district committee, and records that the district people's committee is the authority that decides to establish the council. Other published analysis records that the appearance of a representative of those whose land is taken, usually one or two people, is a notable legislative step forward, while noting that effectiveness depends on that representative's capacity and that in many cases they need training or legal support to take real part in technical matters such as land prices or the resettlement plan. The posting period is fixed. Published description records the posting period as at least 30 days under a named article of the 2024 land legislation, and records that the approved plan must be sent to each person whose land is recovered, stating the level of compensation and support, any resettlement housing or land, and the time and place of payment. Read this with the district land registration branches, the commune inspection board, the community supervision board and the provincial legal aid centres entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Commune-level fatherland front committees — the body that picks issues people are angry about each year, chairs a social criticism conference, and issues written recommendations it then has to chase
trackers.desc: Each year the committee picks the issues people are angry about, and that choice is the plan. A joint resolution records that, annually, the front committee chairs a consultation with the socio-political organisations at the same level to select the issues that the people are concerned about and angry about, and to determine the appropriate forms of oversight and social criticism, in order to build the oversight and social criticism plan. For a community whose grievance is widely shared, getting onto that annual list is the opening. Oversight ends in a written recommendation that goes in two directions. The same resolution records that, based on the oversight results, the front committee or socio-political organisation chairing the oversight shall conclude on the content and issue a written recommendation to the body, organisation or individual subject to oversight and to the competent authority, and at the same time send it to the front committee or organisation at the immediately higher level. A recommendation copied upward is harder to shelve than one sent only to the body complained of. The methods of social criticism include a direct dialogue. The published regulation lists the methods as holding conferences of the leading bodies of the front committee and the executive boards of the socio-political organisations at each level; collecting critical opinions through organisations, individuals and members within their own systems, or sending the draft document to relevant bodies, organisations and individuals for critical opinions; and, when necessary, organising direct dialogue between the critics and the body or organisation whose draft document is being criticised. It records oversight as carried out through implementation of the legal documents on grassroots democracy, the activity of the people's inspection board and the community investment supervision board. Published reporting on one sector records the commune-level committee as issuing conclusions and specific recommendations, reporting to the party committee, coordinating with the authorities to follow up and urge acceptance, explanation and correction, and periodically announcing results so the people know and can continue to supervise. Read this with the commune people's inspection board, the community investment supervision board, the provincial legal aid centres and the compensation council entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Royal Audit Authority
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Bhutan, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Bhutan — Ministry of Finance
trackers.desc: National budget authority; prepares & publishes the national budget and budget reports, Royal Government of Bhutan. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Bhutan.

trackers.name: Anti-Corruption Commission of Bhutan (ACC)
trackers.desc: Bhutan’s lead anti-corruption body — investigates and prosecutes graft, runs asset declaration and corruption prevention.

trackers.name: Bhutan — Corporate Regulatory Authority (CRA)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the CRA (formerly Office of the Registrar of Companies, upgraded 2024) incorporates companies and runs the online single-window company registry & compliance system, Bhutan. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Every Bhutanese is a trustee — the clause an individual can cite
trackers.desc: THE STRONGEST CONSTITUTIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL PROVISION IN THIS MAP. Article 5 of the 2008 Constitution requires that a minimum of 60 percent of Bhutan's total land be maintained under forest cover for all time — a permanent safeguard, not a policy target. AND IT VESTS A DUTY PERSONALLY: Article 5 states that every Bhutanese is a trustee of the Kingdom's natural resources and environment. That trusteeship clause is what an individual cites — stronger than the diffuse-interest provisions this map records for Paraguay and the Dominican Republic, because it is framed as a duty held personally rather than an interest shared collectively. HEADROOM: actual forest cover is around 71–72 percent and more than 51 percent of the country is protected across 10 national parks and sanctuaries — the largest protected share of any Asian country — so the 60 percent floor is not currently the binding constraint. BUT DO NOT MISUSE THE MANDATE: the World Bank's Bhutan Forest Note records that public debate is ‘prone to the misconception that sustainably managed forests do not count toward forest cover’. Arguing that management per se breaches the 60 percent mandate will fail — argue degradation, conversion or biodiversity impact instead. Only about 3.5 percent of land is managed for commercial production.

trackers.name: Community forests run on a certificate — and rule 63 can cancel it
trackers.desc: TWO THINGS TO READ BEFORE YOU NEED THEM. The Forest and Nature Conservation Rules and Regulations 2017 govern Community Forests with named provisions on sale of surplus forest produce (r.61), royalty (r.62), cancellation of the Community Forest Certificate (r.63), formation of CF network and association (r.64) and monitoring and evaluation (r.65). Your community forest exists by certificate, and rule 63 provides for cancelling it — read the grounds now, not later. And rule 64 gives community forest groups a statutory basis for forming a network and association, so groups can organise together rather than each negotiating alone. The 2017 Rules supersede all earlier government notifications, circulars, orders and rules. THE TENURE RULE: under rule 12, private registered land acquired by the Government for national interest becomes State Reserved Forest Land from the date of acquisition — conversion is automatic on that date. CHECK WHICH ACT YOU ARE READING: the Forest and Nature Conservation Act 2023 replaces the 1995 Act and both circulate; its 11 chapters cover State Reserved Forest Land, nature conservation, soil, water and waste, forest-based industry and offence and penalty, with powers in the Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources and the Department of Forests and Park Services. Your local contact is the Divisional Forest Office in the dzongkhag.

trackers.name: Bhutan Trust Fund — individuals and unregistered groups can apply
trackers.desc: NO LEGAL PERSONALITY REQUIRED — which removes the commonest barrier in this map. The Bhutan Trust Fund for Environmental Conservation, established 1991 as the world's first environmental trust fund by the Royal Government with UNDP and WWF and a US$20 million endowment, incorporated under Royal Charter in 1996 and renewed in 2021, is autonomous of government, with a Management Board fully Bhutanised in May 2001. ANY AGENCY, INSTITUTION, COMMUNITY OR INDIVIDUAL THAT IS BHUTANESE IS ELIGIBLE — recorded applicant types include communities and non-registered citizen groups, individuals, NGOs, subnational government and towns and municipalities. THE PAPERWORK IS WHERE GOOD PROPOSALS FAIL: small grant proposals may be submitted at any time of year in the prescribed template (with a separate annual call for larger grants); proposals from an agency must be approved by their head and carry an official forwarding letter; and an individual working in any agency, public or private, needs a No Objection Letter from it. Get the forwarding letter or NOL before drafting, not after. Fundable sectors include land management, sustainable rural livelihoods, community development and eco-tourism; thematic windows have included managing development impacts — expressly reducing environmental harm caused by development activities. It is also accredited to the Adaptation Fund (since 2018, valid to 6 February 2029) and the Green Climate Fund (2020), so it is a route to international climate finance too. Contact: Post Box 520, Genyen Lam, Thimphu; 975-2-33981.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Bhutan Trust Fund small grants — an individual can apply, and the window never closes
trackers.desc: The eligibility list is wider than almost anyone in Bhutan believes: the Small Grants Window is open to community-based organisations, civil society organisations, youth groups, academic institutions, private sector entities, government agencies and individuals. The national broadcaster reported from a 2023 networking event that many civil society organisations had assumed only government bodies could apply, and that the Fund's managing director told them anyone can, provided the proposal serves the greater interest of society. Two figures set the scale honestly: up to Nu 1.0 million per project against an annual small-grants allocation of up to Nu 6.0 million — roughly half a dozen small grants a year for the whole country, so a strong proposal still competes. There is no deadline on this window. It stays open all year, proposals go in at any time on the prescribed Small Grant Proposal Template, and they are screened quarterly, which makes it the route to use when a threat appears mid-year rather than conveniently before an annual call. The larger money runs differently: large grants, advocacy grants and programme-related investments go through an annual call for proposals with a thematic focus set for that cycle, so read the current call before writing to that window instead of assuming your subject is in scope. The Fund was established on 6 March 1991 by the Royal Government of Bhutan with UNDP and WWF, holds a Royal Charter first granted in 1996 and renewed in 2021, and was the first Bhutanese entity accredited to the Adaptation Fund, in 2018, and to the Green Climate Fund, in 2020 — which matters because it can channel international climate money as well as its own endowment.

trackers.name: RSPN — Bhutan's one nationwide conservation NGO, and how it paid for the benign option
trackers.desc: There is essentially one of these in Bhutan, so knowing what it will and will not do matters more than usual. The Royal Society for Protection of Nature was established in 1987 under the Royal Command of the Fourth King as a citizen-based NGO, is registered with the Civil Society Organizations Authority as a Public Benefit Organization, is governed by a seven-member board with an executive director running day-to-day affairs, and holds the Royal Patronage of the Queen. It describes itself as a complementary partner to the Royal Government rather than a counterweight to it, so expect conservation weight, research and funding brought into a decision — not litigation against the state. The Phobjikha electrification case is the transferable one. More than five hundred households in the valley, black-necked crane habitat where RSPN has worked for over two decades, were lighting with pine resin and kerosene. The valley needed electricity; its sensitivity as a conservation area mattered to both the government and RSPN; and environmentally sensitive electrification cost more than the government could carry. RSPN ran a pilot from 2003 to 2005 putting solar lighting into 198 households and 22 institutions, funded by the Solar Electric Lighting Fund and the UN Environment Programme. That is the move worth copying: where the damaging option is cheap and the benign one is not, the fight is often about who pays the difference, and a conservation body with international funders can answer that question when no planning argument will. RSPN also runs the Black-necked Crane Information Centre in Phobjikha and holds a MacArthur Award for Creative and Effective Institutions. Take the domain from the Society, not from its partners. At least one partner directory publishes its website as rspnbhutan.com; it is rspnbhutan.org. Programme counts differ between sources too — its own history page says eleven flagship programmes and a partner says six focus areas — so ask which are currently running rather than assuming yours is covered.

trackers.name: National Environment Commission — the clearance a project needs, and the paper your community signs
trackers.desc: Two documents in the application file are about your community, and one of them you sign. An application for environmental clearance must include a record of public consultation carried out under Chapter VI of the 2016 clearance regulation, signed by the members of the local authority present, plus written consent from any person whose property the activity directly affects, authenticated by the local authority. Published project documentation describes how this runs in practice: the local government summons the affected community, the proponent explains the development, the process to follow, the potential impacts and the intended mitigation, questions and discussion follow, and at the end of the meeting community members sign the clearance the proponent has prepared, which the local administration co-signs. That signature is the consent, and it is given at the end of the first meeting. Anyone attending should know before arriving that the paper being passed round is part of the clearance file, that nobody is obliged to sign it, and that objections are worth more recorded in the minutes than left as an unsigned sheet. Ask for the document in advance. Where the application goes depends on a colour-coded list. Red category projects require full environmental impact assessment and are reviewed by the commission's secretariat; projects on the district committee's list are cleared by the district environment committee, which is the competent authority under the 2007 environment protection Act and is also responsible for monitoring compliance with clearance conditions and acting on non-compliance; projects on neither list are assessed at initial examination level by the secretariat. Districts publish both the exempted list and the district-competence list, and a private applicant must route the application through the gewog or dungkhag, which reviews and verifies it before it reaches the committee chairman. Operating without clearance carries a fine of ten times the application fee, and clearances expire and must be renewed with a penalty for late renewal — so whether a project holds a current clearance, and whether it was ever granted one, are both checkable questions to put to the district committee. The commission's own site serves over plain http without TLS.

trackers.name: National Legal Aid Centre and the Bar Council — advice as of right, representation only where justice requires it
trackers.desc: In a civil matter, expect advice and assistance rather than a lawyer in court. The national legal aid centre, established at the Supreme Court complex and funded by the State, provides legal advice, assistance and representation — but reported accounts of its terms record that in civil cases only advice and assistance are provided as a matter of course, with representation granted only where the interest of justice genuinely requires it. A community should therefore go in expecting help to understand and to draft, and should be ready to argue the interest-of-justice point separately if it wants counsel in the courtroom. The means assessment reaches the household, and the form carries an oath. Under the legal aid rules the centre may assess the net worth of disposable capital accessible to the applicant and to the applicant's household, and the designated officer decides to grant or refuse aid on the basis of a report, or may seek further examination first. The application form includes a declaration on oath, and a false declaration means aid is denied or revoked immediately. Assemble the household's position honestly before filing rather than after a question is asked. There is a second door, and it is narrow. The bar council's own stated functions include providing pro bono legal aid to indigent persons in addition to the funding support given by the State, and facilitating access to jabmi services across the country. Requests are screened by the legal aid centre before they reach the council: of eighty-five recorded requests for pro bono aid, sixteen were granted, from a body of around three hundred registered attorneys. Plan for a low grant rate and apply early rather than at the point of crisis. Where to go, and what to cite. The centre sits at the Supreme Court complex in Thimphu and the bar council is based at the Office of the Attorney General; the constitutional provision to quote is the undertaking that the State shall endeavour to provide legal aid to secure justice, which shall not be denied to any person by reason of economic or other disabilities. Read this with the environmental clearance entry recorded here: the consultation meeting, where the community is asked to sign, is the moment advice is worth most.

trackers.name: Water quality testing — the reference laboratory, the district network, and a private environmental lab
trackers.desc: The national reference point for drinking water sits in the health service. The disease control centre's non-infectious disease laboratory strengthens the country's capacity to monitor drinking water quality and carries out assessment of compliance with the national drinking water quality standard by service providers. For a community that suspects its supply has been affected by works upstream, that is the laboratory whose findings the rest of the system already treats as authoritative. Testing capacity is distributed, which matters in a country of long roads. The published drinking water quality standards allocate roles across the centre, dzongkhag hospitals, ten-bedded hospitals and primary health centres, thromde and dzongkhag municipal offices and gewog administrations — including undertaking urban water quality testing, providing water quality testing support to the health facilities within a jurisdiction, and compiling data with an annual report to the water department. A village should ask its dzongkhag hospital or health centre first rather than assuming the only door is in Thimphu. Get the standard before you get the result. Compliance is assessed against the published drinking water quality standard, and that same document sets out which body does what. A measurement means nothing without the limit it is being measured against, and in Bhutan both the limits and the responsibilities are in one published place. For parameters outside drinking water, there is a private route. An environmental testing and calibration laboratory established in 2016 describes its work as covering pollution monitoring in air, water, soil, flue gas and noise together with calibration of scientific devices, working to international standards and to the national standards bureau's standards. Bhutan's testing landscape is small, so apply the instruction recorded elsewhere in this file before commissioning anyone: ask what the laboratory is accredited or recognised for, confirm your parameters are inside that scope, and ask for the measurement uncertainty with the figure. Read this with the environmental clearance entry recorded here, where the consultation record is the moment a measurement becomes useful.

trackers.name: Dzongkhag Environment Committee — the district body that clears projects, monitors the conditions and must act on breach
trackers.desc: For many projects the clearing authority is the district, not the capital. The dzongkhag environment committee is a competent authority constituted under the national environment protection act, issuing environmental clearance for the projects within its competence under the environmental assessment act, its regulation and the colour-coded project categorisation list. Its published duties include compliance monitoring of the conditions of environmental clearance and taking necessary action for non-compliance, and making recommendations to ministries, local governments or the commission secretariat on measures needed to protect environmental quality. A community with a complaint about conditions should address the committee that imposed them rather than starting in Thimphu. The conditions have teeth, and the meter runs daily. The clearance regulation provides for fines according to the severity of the offence, and where an offence is repeated in violation of an order issued under the assessment act, an additional fine of twenty thousand ngultrum may be imposed for every day the offence continues after the expiry of the time limit. A continuing breach is therefore a daily liability rather than a single penalty, and that is the language to use when reporting one. Green category does not mean unregulated. A project in the green category is not subjected to the environmental assessment process, but the exempted activity must still obtain the approvals, clearances and development consents required from the concerned agencies under other legislation. Where a developer says its project needs no assessment, the question that follows is which consents it does hold and from whom. There is a paper trail upward, and an appeal. The competent authority must submit to the commission secretariat a list of the activities and projects it has screened and issued clearance for, so the district's list of clearances is a document that exists and can be asked for; and the regulation provides for appeal against a decision. Read this with the environmental clearance and water quality testing entries already recorded for this country: the clearance sets the conditions, the district committee monitors them, and the laboratory tells you whether they are being met.

trackers.name: National Land Commission — the lagthram, a thirty-day cooling period, and land dispute settlement
trackers.desc: One agency holds the record, and the certificate has a name. The land commission has been the autonomous authority for land registration, cadastral survey and mapping since the 2007 land act, working across all twenty dzongkhags and the thromdes, and a nationwide cadastral resurvey of every parcel was completed in 2010. The land ownership certificate is the lagthram, issued through the dzongkhag survey and land sector, whose published functions include providing information on registered land to landowners. Before contesting what may happen to a plot, get the record for it from the office that issues the certificate. There is a thirty-day cooling period, and the timelines are published. A rural land transaction runs thirty days of cooling period plus fifteen days at the gewog, thirty days including field survey at the dzongkhag, and seven days at the commission; the municipal route carries a mandatory thirty-day cooling period plus fifteen days including field survey. A cooling period is a window in which a transfer can be questioned before it completes, and no other entry in this file names one. Family land needs the family's no objection. Where the land under transaction is family land, no objection from family members above eighteen is required, and the same consent is required where land is to be registered as individual land. A transfer completed without it is questionable on the face of the paperwork, which makes the consent documents worth asking for. Substitute land and dispute settlement are listed services. Alongside transactions the commission lists land use certificates, land acquisition and substitute land, land exchange, land leases, cadastral survey licensing and land dispute settlement among the services it provides. Where land is being acquired, ask for the substitute land route by name. The online transaction portal shows the total cost of the land, the demarcation, subdivision and certificate fees and the revenue receipt number and date to the applicant and to every official processing the file, with a message sent at each change of status. Read this with the district environment committee and environmental clearance entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Reporting waste and unclearanced projects — five places to report, and a tenfold penalty
trackers.desc: Five addresses for a report, and one of them is the police. Under the waste prevention and management regulation, a person who knows of anyone releasing waste of any nature into the environment other than by the prescribed procedures may report it to the nearest local authority or to the Royal Bhutan Police. The reporting page adds that illegal waste activity may be reported directly to the concerned gewog administration, the dzongkhag administration, the thromde or the environment commission secretariat, or through the online incidence report form itself. A community ignored at one tier therefore has four others named on the same page, which is the widest set of alternative addressees recorded in this file. Do not touch the waste. The same page warns that waste may contain syringes, toxic substances or asbestos, and that exposure to improperly handled waste can damage health. Photograph it, write down where and when, and leave it where it lies. It is the only safety instruction to the reporter recorded anywhere in this research, and it belongs in any guidance built from these entries. A project without clearance faces ten times the application fee. District environment pages state that a fine or penalty equivalent to ten times the application fee is imposed for establishing, commencing or carrying out a project without the required environmental clearance, that a late renewal penalty applies, and that clearance must be renewed before it expires. Ask a project for its clearance and for the expiry date on it: an expired clearance is a live liability rather than a technicality. A field verification report exists for most cleared projects. The district route is published: a private applicant routes the application through the gup or dungkhag, which forwards it after review and verification; the environment officer reviews it, may seek additional documents and coordinates a site visit with the relevant stakeholders; the visiting team compiles a field verification report for endorsement, or for deliberation by the district environment committee, which may endorse, reject, or direct re-verification or a joint field visit. That report is a document, and a community that knows it exists can ask for it. Read this with the district environment committee, land commission and water quality testing entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: e-GP — the tender, the corrigendum and the contract award, published in one place
trackers.desc: Three documents, and the award is the one that names the contractor. The government's electronic procurement system exists so that all procuring agencies publish their tenders, any corrigendum to them, and the notification of contract award. For a community watching a project take shape, those three answer different questions: the tender says what was asked for, the corrigendum says what was changed after the request went out, and the award says who is doing the work and under what reference. Awards can be searched on their own. The portal carries a contract listing separate from the tender listing, with an advanced search across tenders, and it publishes the standard bidding documents used across government. That means the terms a contractor signed up to are readable in their standard form, which is a different starting point from asking an agency what the contract says. Manual tenders and manual awards are listed as well. Where a procurement was run on paper rather than through the system, the portal still lists it, noting that the tender document must be bought from the procuring agency's office and that the same information is available from the procurement policy division's own site. A project let outside the electronic system is therefore still announced, and this entry names the second place to look rather than leaving a gap. Read it beside the clearance and the reporting line. This file already records for this country the dzongkhag environment committee which issues environmental clearance and monitors its conditions, the land commission, and the waste reporting route with its five addressees. The clearance says what was permitted, the award says who is carrying it out, and the reporting line is where a breach of the conditions goes — three records that between them describe a project from permission through to performance.

trackers.name: Anti-Corruption Commission — a complaint you can track by number, and the asset declarations behind an official
trackers.desc: Complaints cover private bodies as well as public ones, and the offence list is published. The commission states that it accepts complaints and information about corrupt conduct involving or affecting authorities and officials, whether public or private, and lists the offences under the 2011 act: bribery, embezzlement, trading in influence, abuse of functions, possession of unexplained wealth, false claims, failure to declare a conflict of interest, abuse of privileged information and money laundering. For a community watching a local project, failure to declare a conflict of interest is usually the one that fits, and it is a named offence rather than a suspicion. You get a registration number, and you can track it. The commission acknowledges receipt of a complaint and may come back for further information, and its mobile application allows a complainant to report corruption and then track the status of the complaint using the unique registration number issued when it was lodged. The commission also states the cost of anonymity plainly: where a complaint is made anonymously it cannot contact the complainant or discuss the matter with them. Asset declarations are a standing system with their own portal. Public officials have declared assets since 2006 on an annual cycle, with published notifications of each filing deadline and a penalty for non-declaration, and a gift rule prohibits solicitation, restricts acceptance and sets procedures for disclosing and managing gifts. Where an official's involvement in a project looks wrong, the declaration regime is the instrument that already exists to test it. A pattern can be the subject, not only a person. The commission conducts system studies examining the practices, procedures and systems of public or private entities that are conducive to corruption, which means a recurring problem in how projects are approved can be raised as a system question rather than as an accusation against an individual. Published accounts add a round-the-clock toll-free complaint line, an annual report giving the numbers of complaints, investigations, prosecutions and assets recovered, and statutory protection for the identity of informants and witnesses, with knowingly false and malicious reporting itself an offence. Read this with the district environment committee, the land commission, the waste reporting route and the procurement entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Royal Audit Authority — irregularities named by agency and project, and the balance still unsettled years later
trackers.desc: Irregularities are published by category and by agency. The authority's annual audit report groups its findings into fraud and corruption, non-compliance with laws, rules and regulations, and shortfalls, lapses and deficiencies, and attributes amounts to named bodies. Reporting of recent years records district administrations, state corporations and a hydroelectric project among those carrying the largest figures in their categories. For a community facing a particular project, the annual audit report is the document in which that project's own failures are quantified in money, by a body whose job is to say so. Performance audit is a mandate, not a favour. The authority derives its mandate from the constitution and from the audit act to audit and report on the economy, efficiency and effectiveness in the use of public resources, and to carry out performance audits examining selected schemes, themes or topics as it considers necessary, alongside financial audits testing whether appropriated amounts were spent on the specified programmes within approved limits, and compliance audits. A scheme can therefore be proposed to it as a subject rather than merely complained about. The follow-up is published as well. Review reports show, agency by agency, which irregularities have been settled and what balance remains unsettled as at a stated date, including items previously reported to Parliament which are still outstanding years later; amounts recovered through the audits are recorded, and cases are forwarded to the anti-corruption commission where warranted, with the outcomes for individuals noted. An unsettled balance carried for years, with a date attached, is a harder fact than an allegation. The reports go to Parliament. Published accounts record that audit reports are tabled in Parliament, where the public accounts committee reviews them and holds hearings with the audited entities, and that audited bodies must respond to findings within a set time with evidence of corrective action. Read this with the anti-corruption commission, the district environment committee, the electronic procurement system and the land commission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: PAVA compensation rates — the 120-day notice, the published adjustment factors, and the banks' rival rate
trackers.desc: The notice period is a hundred and twenty days, and approval comes before it. The published compensation rate document sets out the acquisition sequence: on the decision of an agency or project to acquire land, the proposal is submitted to the land commission secretariat for formal approval, which conveys its decision within two weeks; subject to that approval, the district or municipal committee must notify the landowner of the government's intention to acquire the land at least a hundred and twenty days before the acquisition; and a landowner who prefers substitute land is dealt with under the land act. Four months is the planning window a household actually has — and where that notice never came, the omission is itself the first argument. The adjustment factors are published, and they can be checked. The rate schedule states that the compensation rate reduces by five per cent where there is no water at the land under assessment, and by ten per cent where the land is unstable, marshy or prone to landslides, with parallel deductions in urban areas where there is no road connection or the soil is unstable. A household can therefore check whether the deductions applied to its own plot are the ones the schedule allows, rather than accepting a figure with no workings behind it. The agency and the revision cycle are named. The property assessment and valuation agency was established in 2008 under the finance ministry, in line with the land act, to assess and fix land and collateral property values and to facilitate the fixing of land and property taxes, lease rents and compensation rates; published accounts of its work record that under the land act compensation rates are to be revised only once every three years, and the ministry publishes each revision by notification. Establishing which rate year governs a particular acquisition is therefore the first question to ask. There is a rival published rate. The association of financial institutions developed a common land base rate for valuation across lenders, adopting one bank's rates as the base and stating that the system addresses drawbacks in the compensation rate, with local area names and descriptions added to remove ambiguity. Where a compensation offer sits far below what a lender would value the same land at, both figures now have a published source, which is a far stronger objection than a household's own sense of the market. Read this with the national land commission, the district environment committee, the audit authority and the legal aid entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: NSDI, the geo-portal and the cadastral division — where maps come from, and the datum that changed in 2026
trackers.desc: There is a national spatial data platform, and the public is named among its users. The national spatial data infrastructure is described as a joint initiative of the land commission secretariat and a foreign development agency, begun in early 2015 with the production of topographic maps at one in twenty-five thousand covering some nine thousand eight hundred and fifty square kilometres of the southern region, and developed since into a centralised platform for government agencies, academic institutions, consultants and the public, offering access to accurate and reliable geospatial data and supporting a single authoritative source across contributing agencies. A community asking for data is therefore inside the stated user group rather than making an unusual request. Cadastral maps come from a named division. The cadastral information division manages all cadastral surveying and mapping and provides cadastral maps, acts as the focal point for surveyors in every dzongkhag, has led three nationwide cadastral surveys since the chain survey of the 1960s, and is upgrading its system to an internationally standard coordinated cadastre using satellite positioning and geographic information technology. The two questions to put to it are for the cadastral map of the parcel and for which of those surveys the map derives from. A separate geo-portal carries downloadable layers and their metadata. Developed by the centre for geo-information with the land commission and international support, the portal allows maps, data and metadata to be shared with a data viewer and a download function, with the stated aim of improving awareness of what data exists and access to it. The metadata is the part that matters in a dispute: it carries the date and the accuracy of a layer, and a map quoted without them is worth little. The datum changed in 2026, and that matters more than it sounds. The commission announced a new national geodetic datum in 2026, alongside a consent management module for land transactions and new strata rules, describing the datum as a modern and accurate foundation for surveying, mapping, infrastructure development and land administration. Coordinates expressed in an old datum and a new one do not line up, so when an old plan is compared against a recent one, establish which datum each uses before drawing any conclusion about a boundary. Read this with the land commission's title and cooling-period entry, the community forest route, the compensation rate schedule and the environmental clearance entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The Bhutanese — the independent paper that reported a land case, and the constraints it works under
trackers.desc: An independent paper exists, and it has reported a land case. Founded in February 2012 by an investigative journalist, conceived the year before as a newspaper that would focus on in-depth and investigative journalism, its own account records impact in reporting on corruption and abuse of power and also across hydropower, economic, political and social stories. Its coverage of a township land allotment case became a national controversy which the prime minister of the day answered publicly, stating that he had asked the anti-corruption commission for a thorough investigation and had made himself available for questioning. A community holding documents about a land allotment therefore has an outlet that has already run precisely that kind of story to a national conclusion. The pressure it has faced is documented, and worth knowing before approaching. Published accounts record a licensing process running from October 2011 to February 2012, described as extraordinarily long with the cabinet of the day intervening to delay the licence; and an advertising ban in August 2012, months after launch, characterised as an economic embargo in retaliation for its investigative coverage, with the government accused of reducing advertising revenue. What an outlet has already survived is a fair guide to what it can carry. The market context is thin. The state-owned daily remains the only daily newspaper, in two language editions; several papers launched in the late 2000s have since closed for financial reasons; the advertising market is small and most public-body advertising is allocated to public media; and journalist attrition is high, with experienced reporters leaving for better-paid work. An approach should assume a small newsroom with limited capacity and arrive with the documents already organised, dated and indexed. The legal weather, stated plainly. Published assessments record that the media regulator's five members are appointed directly by government, that journalists report difficulty obtaining access to state-held information, and that a national security provision penalising attempts to create misunderstanding or hostility between the government and the people acts as a brake on journalism. Bring facts, documents and dates rather than characterisations, and let the paper decide what it can say. Read this with the anti-corruption commission, the royal audit authority, the community forest route and the land commission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Heritage sites inventory — getting a site documented is what makes planners consider it
trackers.desc: The inventory is the lever, because it is what feeds planning. Published accounts record that the culture department launched an inventory database system for heritage sites, documenting sixty-eight sites — twenty-six in one central dzongkhag and twenty-two and twenty in two eastern ones — and training five young architects and researchers in documentation and analysis. The stated purpose of that system is to play a role in the registration, designation and value-based protection of heritage sites, and to allow government to give greater consideration to cultural heritage sites when planning future infrastructure projects such as hydroelectric dams, or when designating economic zones. Getting a site documented into that inventory is therefore the practical move available to a community: the inventory is what planners consult, and a site absent from it is invisible at exactly the moment it matters. A named division does the surveys and the documentation. The heritage sites and archaeology division within the culture department carries out nationwide surveys, documentation and inventory of cultural heritage sites alongside conservation and archaeological work, has deputed assessment teams to dzongkhags after earthquake damage, and publishes its own studies of monuments selected from the national inventory on stated criteria such as being established before the seventeenth century or having greater historical and architectural significance. Approach it with photographs, dates, names and the site's history: that is what documentation consists of, and a community can assemble most of it. Movable heritage is inventoried separately, including in private hands. The antiquities division prepares a comprehensive inventory of relics and religious articles housed in dzongs, temples and monasteries including private collections, conserves and restores cultural properties, and administers export control and permits for non-antique products. Where a project threatens a temple, its contents are a separate matter from its walls. Custodians are inside the process, and the general law is still pending. The division's stated vision involves religious congregations and monks, as the custodians of heritage sites, in major renovation projects and in discussions of policies and programmes; its own publication states that it is the responsibility of every citizen to safeguard individual heritage sites and the cultural landscape in general; and reported accounts record that a comprehensive cultural heritage bill, long in preparation, has yet to bind sites, artefacts and intangible heritage into a single law. Until it does, the inventory and this division's process are the protection that exists. Read this with the land commission's title and cooling-period entry, the community forest route, the environmental clearance and the compensation rate entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Corporate Regulatory Authority — company verification is public, the shareholder detail is not, and the filing agent has a number
trackers.desc: There is a company verification tool, and that is what is public. The corporate regulatory authority operates the online company system, which carries a company verification function alongside registration and the migration of existing companies into the system. Commercial registry services record honestly what such a search returns in this country: typically a confirmation that a named company is incorporated or registered under the companies legislation, with fuller information described as not publicly available or supplied for a fee, and extracts obtained through agents taking one to two weeks. Expect confirmation that an entity exists, not a shareholder list — and plan the rest of the research around that limit rather than against it. What the companies legislation covers, and what it does not. Companies are registered under the companies legislation of 2016, and the authority's published guidance records that the mode of incorporation is by registration only, that a company may be formed only for lawful profit-oriented business, and that non-governmental organisations and other forms of association are not registered under that Act at all. An operator presenting itself as a company may therefore not be one, and a body absent from this register may still exist under another regime — which is a reason to check the association and licensing records rather than concluding that nothing exists. Filing agents are certified and carry a number. Under the 2024 regulations for company secretaries and filing agents, certified filing agents may register companies, and the application requires the agent to enter their unique registration number and verify it. Asking which certified filing agent incorporated a company, and for that number, gives a second named party connected to the operator behind a project. The mechanics, and where to go when the register stops. Published guidance sets out the registration fee, the approval email from the registrar, and the issue of the certificate and articles of incorporation electronically once payment is made; it records that a company forming a subsidiary must own more than half the shares of the new company and have control over its management accordingly, and that shareholders' liability is limited to any amount unpaid on their shares. Where the register will not disclose ownership, the published procurement awards, the audit reports and the environmental clearance file often name the same parties. Read this with the electronic procurement contract awards, the royal audit authority, the environment commission clearance and the anti-corruption commission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Land Kidu and the rehabilitation programme — a named coordinator in your own gewog, and land granted to people farming without a thram
trackers.desc: There is a coordinator for this in your own gewog. The land commission's own account of the national rehabilitation programme, instituted in 2011 to rehabilitate landless and socio-economically disadvantaged households, records that the process was made proactive: the royal secretariat and its regional offices identify and verify the landless for land grants through dzongkhag and gewog kidu coordinators. For a household with no land or with land it cannot register, that means there is a named official at local level whose job is to identify them — the approach is to that coordinator, not to the capital. What the programme is for, and what the commission does. The stated objectives are to increase the productive asset base of beneficiaries by providing adequate land with complementary support, and to create and enhance income-generating opportunities. The commission's own role is to spearhead identification of potential sites and ground verification jointly with the dzongkhags, to coordinate feasibility studies with a multi-sector task force drawn from various ministries and agencies, and to coordinate plotting for land allotment and demarcation through cadastral survey. A community asking for land is therefore asking for a site to enter that pipeline, and the feasibility study is the step where an unsuitable site is filtered out. Land held without papers can be registered. Reporting on the grants records that people cultivating land without a thram — the land record — were granted kidu allowing the land to be registered in their name, and that where excess land was held bona fide the recipients did not have to pay for it. That is the provision for a household whose occupation is real but undocumented, and it follows the nationwide cadastral resurvey rather than preceding it. The scale, and the older resettlement track. Published reporting records the first grants after the resurvey in 2009 and, by the end of one later year, cumulative grants of some 123,000 acres in 133 gewogs to over 102,000 beneficiaries across thirteen dzongkhags since 2010. A separate and earlier resettlement programme, running from 1997 in five dzongkhags over nine phases, granted land to the landless, the near-landless and households dependent on shifting cultivation, resettling roughly 4,600 households. Read this with the national land commission's title and cooling-period entry, the community forest route, the heritage sites inventory and the compensation rate entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Bhutan Ecolab — a private laboratory for air, flue gas, soil and noise, where the state reference lab covers drinking water
trackers.desc: The state reference laboratory covers drinking water; this covers the rest. The water quality entry already recorded for this country points to the national reference laboratory, whose mandate is drinking water and compliance with the national drinking water standard. What it does not cover is the emissions and noise side of a project. An environmental pollution testing and calibration laboratory established in 2016, with backing from a foundation and a national holding company, offers monitoring across air, water, soil, flue gas and noise, together with calibration of measuring instruments. For a community beside a quarry, a plant or a road project, that combination — stack emissions, ambient air, noise — is the measurement set the reference laboratory was never set up to provide. It works to national and international standards, which is what makes a result usable. The laboratory states that it works to both international standards and those of the national standards bureau, covering quality management and laboratory testing, with the stated aim of results that are reliable, traceable and unbiased. Traceability is the property that matters in a dispute: a result that can be tied back to a calibrated instrument and a documented method is far harder to wave away than a reading from an unknown device. What to establish before commissioning. Which specific tests the laboratory is competent and equipped for, since a laboratory offering five media rarely holds the same depth in all of them; how samples or measurements must be taken for the result to stand, particularly for noise, where duration, position and background readings decide whether a figure means anything; and whether the laboratory also carries out the proponent's own compliance monitoring for the same project, which is worth knowing before the two sets of numbers are compared in public. Where the results go. The environmental clearance route and the district environment committee recorded elsewhere in this country's entries are where monitoring evidence has somewhere to be lodged, and the waste and unclearanced-project reporting channel is where a discrepancy can be raised. Read this with those entries and with the water quality testing entry, which this one is written to sit beside rather than repeat.

trackers.name: Judgments of the Supreme Court and High Court — a selection published, plus the codes and forms that govern a case
trackers.desc: Some judgments are published, and research guides point to where. A foreign law research guide maintained by a national library lists, among the free online legal resources for this country's judicial branch, the judiciary's own site and a page of supreme court judgments. A separate legal system overview records that some of the judgments of the supreme court and the high court can be found on the judiciary's site, together with the judicial forms used in proceedings. The word to hold onto is some: this is a selection, not a complete record, and a community should not read absence as meaning no comparable case exists. The procedural codes are published in full, and they matter more here than case law. Descriptions of the judiciary's site record that legislation relevant to the courts is provided in full text, including the civil and criminal procedure code, the penal code, the evidence act and the judicial service act, alongside sections on court procedures. In a system where only a selection of judgments is published, the procedural code is the document that tells a litigant what the court must do — how a case is begun, what a summons requires, what happens on non-appearance. What the court can order. The same overview records that the court issues orders in the form of directions, writs, injunctions and compliance orders under the procedure code, and issues summons requiring a litigant to appear on a specified date, with failure to honour a summons potentially leading to dismissal, a default judgment or liability for contempt. For a community, the injunction and compliance categories are the ones worth understanding before seeking relief against works already under way. Statistics, and where else to look. The judiciary publishes annual reports whose central content is case statistics for courts across the country, useful for showing how many cases of a kind are brought and how they end. Where a judgment is needed and is not published, ask through the court that decided it or through the legal aid route recorded elsewhere in this country's entries. Read this with the national legal aid centre and bar council, the land commission's cooling period, the anti-corruption reporting and the compensation rate entries already recorded here.

trackers.name: Civil Society Organizations Authority — the two categories, the endowment thresholds, and the offence of unlawful collection
trackers.desc: Registration is the gateway, and there are only two categories. The civil society organisations legislation of 2007, amended in 2022, established an authority which reviews and approves all registration applications, approves accreditation of foreign organisations, and monitors compliance with the Act and with each organisation's own articles or charter. Local organisations are either public benefit or mutual benefit organisations, and published material records a total of sixty-four registered with fifty-two active — forty public benefit and twelve mutual benefit. A community wanting to hold and spend donated money for a land or environmental purpose is looking at public benefit registration. The endowment threshold is the barrier to plan around. The authority's guidelines set minimum endowment fund limits of three million ngultrum for a public benefit organisation and one and a half million for a mutual benefit organisation, held with the monetary authority as fixed deposits earning returns to finance activities, with separate guidance sections on endowment funds, social enterprise and fundraising, and a fundraising report template annexed. That threshold is why most communities will raise through an existing registered organisation rather than forming their own. Collecting without conforming to the Act is an offence. The Act provides that a person or organisation is guilty of unlawful collection if they collect any donation or charity without conforming to its provisions; that any charity or donation to any institution must be recorded regardless of quantity or value; and that collections may be made only on the volition of the donor. Any person may give movable or immovable property to any institution, private or government, provided it accords with the Act. Foreign money is routed through a bank, and governance is prescribed. Donations, grants, subsidies, financial assistance, contributions and bequests from foreign sources, public or private, must be routed through an authorised financial institution of the country. Each organisation is governed by a board electing a chairperson, a secretary and a treasurer from among its members, responsible for the management and use of donated property, for ensuring property and income are used only for purposes authorised by the articles, and for honouring any donor agreement that further restricts use. Accredited organisations submit annual reports with audited financial statements, and accreditation is reviewed every three years. Read this with the community forest and land kidu entries, the anti-corruption reporting protection and the published judgments entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The Legal Aid Centre and its regional offices — advice and assistance for all, representation only where justice requires it
trackers.desc: A national legal aid centre exists, and the limits on what it provides are stated. Reporting on its establishment records that the national legal institute set up a legal aid centre at the supreme court in October 2022, funded by the state, providing legal advice, assistance and representation in civil and criminal cases — but with representation in civil cases granted only where the interest of justice genuinely requires it, while in criminal cases all three services are available, initially to needy accused charged with felony offences. A community in a land or environmental dispute is in civil territory, so the realistic expectation is advice and assistance, with representation as an argued exception rather than an entitlement. It is reaching outward from the capital. Development agency reporting records a regional legal aid centre opened in a busy border commercial town, sitting in the district court there, as an extension of the national centre and offering legal counsel, representation and referrals; it is one of two regional centres established in 2025 under a funded access to justice project. Ask whether a regional centre now covers your district before assuming a trip to the capital. Local leaders are trained to be the first stop. The same reporting records sensitisation workshops run for gewog and village-level leaders on what constitutes legal aid, the eligibility criteria and the procedures for accessing it, with the aim of reaching hard-to-reach rural communities; village representatives describe mediating disputes themselves and resolving some internally and some in court. Your tshogpa or gup may already have been trained on how to refer a case. Mediation is institutional here, not informal. The institute's own mediation reports record court-annexed mediation units in the courts other than the apex court, with minor civil disputes referred to them by presiding judges, and record thousands of local government leaders trained in mediation skills across the gewogs and chiwogs, alongside bench clerks and paralegal service providers. For a dispute with a neighbour or a small contractor that is not the main fight, that route is faster and cheaper than litigation. Read this with the legal aid centre and bar council entry, the community forest certificate, the anti-corruption reporting protection and the published judgments entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Department of Geology and Mines — the mineral portal's legislation and guidelines, the community development fund, and who issues surface collection permits
trackers.desc: The mineral portal publishes the whole rulebook in one place. The department's legislation page lists the statutes and rules that govern mining here — the mines and minerals management regulations, the regulation for environmental clearance of projects, the forest and nature conservation rules, the land lease rules and the waste prevention and management regulation, alongside the forest and nature conservation legislation and the taxes and levies legislation — and the guidelines beneath them, including the mineral prospecting and exploration guideline, the guideline for leasing mines and quarries, guidelines for preparing the project feasibility study and guidelines for preparation of an environmental management plan for mining projects. A community can read the exact document the operator's plan is supposed to satisfy. Every mining company contributes to a community development fund, and the uses are named. The mineral development policy of 2017 requires all mining companies to contribute to a community development fund to be used specifically for drinking water schemes, water source protection, social forestry schemes and renovation of religious sites belonging to the community, among other schemes. It also provides that mine allocation shall take account of the environmental carrying capacity of each mining area and avoid unnecessary proliferation, and that public consultation shall focus on the effects of the proposed mining and related matters under consultation guidelines. Ask which fund the mine beside you pays into, and what it has financed. Reclamation is funded in advance, not promised. Reporting on the policy records that mining environmental standards are to be strengthened through adequate environmental assessment and a properly designed mine plan and environmental management and mitigation plan before a lease issues; that mines are to be supervised by qualified professionals; that post-mining reclamation is to be ensured by collecting a sufficient environmental reclamation fund to implement the mine closure and reclamation plan at the end of the lifecycle; and that leaseholders must manage and mitigate adverse impacts on affected communities with adequate grievance mechanisms and procedures in place for them. Those are the three things to ask for: the plan, the fund, the grievance procedure. Know which department issues the permit you are questioning. Reporting records that the mines legislation and the forest and nature conservation legislation, enacted on the same day in 1995, both conferred authority over surface collection, so that two departments issue permits and monitor collection, and that an audit authority criticised the forest department issuing permits for surface collection and dredging of riverbed materials directly; a pending bill would resolve the conflict. Until it does, riverbed sand and boulder collection may sit with either department. Exploration permit copies are recorded as being circulated to the local gewog administration and the forest officer, which means the local office should hold one. Read this with the community forest certificate, the legal aid centre, the anti-corruption reporting protection and the civil society authority entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Chiwog zomdu, Gewog Tshogde and Dzongkhag Tshogdu — where a project enters the plan, the agenda notification, and the six-monthly session
trackers.desc: The planning cycle starts at a village-level meeting, and that is the earliest door. The local development planning manual records that local governments are empowered to formulate and implement their own plans and programmes through a planning cycle, and that a chiwog planning exercise is carried out with its outcome presented at the chiwog zomdu for deliberation and prioritisation. A project that is going to appear in the five-year plan will pass through that meeting first, which is where a community's own priority — or its objection — is cheapest to insert. Know the three bodies and what each decides. The local governance department records that local government here means the district councils of the twenty dzongkhags, the gewog councils of two hundred and five gewogs and the thromde councils of four thromdes, all made up of locally elected community representatives who discuss and decide local issues; that the district council is the consultative decision-making body at district level, consulting members of other local governments and senior officials of the district administration and regional offices when deciding an agenda item; and that its decisions are implemented by the district administration. Published summaries record the district council as the highest decision making body in the district, tasked among other things with reviewing gewog regulations and ordinances and empowered to enforce rules on health and public safety and to regulate environmental pollution. Sessions are scheduled, and the agenda is opened by notification. A district administration's published procedure records that the council meets at least once every six months for regular sessions, with up to three special sessions in emergencies; that the chairperson confirms the session date under a named section of the local government legislation; and that on confirmation a notification issues under another named section inviting proposals from members for inclusion in the agenda. Getting your gup or tshogpa to file the item during that window is the mechanism, and the dates are published. Plans are built from the bottom and approved upward. Published policy material records that local government plans are formulated under the local government legislation, the plan preparation guidelines, the local development planning manual, thromde structural plans and local area plans, with close consultation with communities to assess needs and aspirations, and are discussed at the gewog councils, district councils and thromde councils before being finalised and approved. Read this with the community forests entry, the district environment committee, the land commission and the compensation rates entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Water Act and Water Regulation — an environment clearance before any abstraction, river basin committees, water user associations, and upstream-downstream sharing of watershed costs
trackers.desc: Abstracting or using water requires an environment clearance, and the regulation makes the permit general. Summaries of the 2011 water legislation record that it sets out procedures for obtaining an environment clearance in order to be allowed to abstract or use water, provides for prevention and control of water pollution, and carries specific requirements for drinking water, irrigation water and water resources in forests and wetlands, along with construction and safety of water infrastructure, water emergencies, dispute settlement and appeals, and offences and penalties. Summaries of the 2014 regulation record that, except for activities existing before it, any water abstraction activity requires a permit from the concerned authority, and that groundwater abstraction may be considered permissible only where there is no other alternative surface water source. Ask which clearance and permit an abstraction holds, and whether a surface alternative was ruled out. Upstream and downstream share the cost of protecting the catchment. A published account of the Act records that it stipulates payments for watershed conservation must be shared by both upstream inhabitants and downstream users, created requirements for water use in drinking, irrigation, forests and wetlands, established the implementing bodies and paved the way for the national integrated water resources management plan. That sharing rule is the basis for a village upstream of a town asking who pays for keeping its catchment intact. River basin committees and water user associations are the two bodies to ask about. The Act mandates the environment commission to form river basin committees to manage and develop water resources and defines their organisation and functions, and provides for the formation and functions of water users' associations; the regulation adds water user rights, the right to a water facility for land and a house, effluent discharge, property damage and compensation, timber extraction from a watershed area and community settlement within a watershed area. The Act declares the country's water resources to be state property, with the river basin approach as the leading principle. The live implementation questions are on the record. National reporting of an environmental officers' conference records officers from twenty districts and four municipalities discussing classification of abstraction from riverbanks, restriction of activities within the buffer zone — defined as the area within a stated distance of any water body — and districts receiving water disputes without a gewog-level resolution first; with a proposal that assessment be compulsory for activities inside the buffer zone, including those otherwise exempt from clearance, and that drinking and irrigation be served as first priority. Take a water dispute to the gewog first, because districts are recorded as receiving them without that step. Read this with the local council planning cycle, the environment commission clearance, the community forests and the water testing entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Forest and Nature Conservation Rules 2023 — the community forest management plan and its ten-year certificate, tree marking before any felling, and the by-laws a group must adopt
trackers.desc: The 2023 rules set out what a community forest management group must produce and what it gets in return. Made under the 2023 forest and nature conservation legislation, they provide that a community forest management group shall prepare and adopt by-laws observing good governance principles such as participation, transparency, accountability, equity and inclusiveness; that it shall maintain proper records of forest resource utilisation and financial management; that the management plan is prepared through consultation and collaboration and submitted for review and approval, with an ownership certificate in a prescribed annexure; and that the community forest management plan is valid for ten years and may be revised based on performance. Those are the documents to ask a group for, and the standard to hold it to. No tree comes down until it is marked. The rules provide that in a community forest the harvesting of any tree shall be allowed only after marking by the responsible authority, and that the group is entitled to forest produce for other stated uses. Marking before felling is a check anyone can see on the ground. Leased forest land can be taken back, in consultation with the district and the land commission. The rules provide that the department may revert leased State Reserve Forest Land after expiry of the term or annulment of the term, in consultation with the Dzongkhag and the National Land Commission Secretariat. Where a lease over reserved forest is the basis of a project, its term and its annulment conditions are therefore worth reading. Fire, monitoring and the Act's own chapters. The rules provide for an inter-agency forest fire coordination group and community-based forest fire management groups, which on receiving information of a fire shall immediately activate suppression in coordination with the department, with reporting through a digital platform; and provide for corrective measures and strengthened monitoring of division and park offices. Published summaries record that the Act and these rules run to eleven chapters covering State reserved forest land, forest management and protection, nature conservation, soil, water and waste management, allotment of timber and non-wood forest produce, forest-based industry, trade and transport of forest produce, and offences and penalties, and that they cover inland fisheries and fishing authorisation as well. Read this with the community forests entry, the environment commission clearance, the district environment committee and the water act entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Payment for ecosystem services — the signed contract between an upstream community forest group and a downstream town's water users, and the two later schemes aimed at hydropower
trackers.desc: An upstream community forest group has been paid, under contract, to protect a downstream town's drinking water. Published research records that after a 2009 feasibility study by the watershed management division with an international agency, the country's first scheme was signed in 2010 between the community forest management group of an upstream village, as the environmental service provider, and the downstream town's water users, with operation beginning in 2011 and technical support from an international organisation; that the watershed management division acted as intermediary alongside the district administration and the forest department; and that the contract ran three years, was renewed for a further five on successful completion, with increased fees and an additional service user added. Contemporary reporting records the community undertaking to preserve the drinking water source in return for a stated annual payment. That is a template a community can point at rather than invent. The trigger was a complaint that went up through the district meeting. The same research records that the downstream town's residents had already sensed forest degradation in the upland area, that the issue was raised in the district meeting and its verdict conveyed to higher authorities, leading to the scheme. That is the route by which a catchment problem became a contract. The money is held by the group, and the honest limits are recorded. A published assessment records that the scheme income is kept in a group savings account, but that although significant relative to what the community forest generated on its own, the fund was not yet substantial enough to assess investment in community development or poverty reduction. Research also records that the watershed protection zone inside that community forest was reduced in area after 2020, and argues that in-depth watershed data on recharge capacity, discharge rate and water table is needed, with payment strategy set on evidence rather than estimation. Two further schemes were designed around different payers. Published material records a scheme planned to compensate communities in a valley for the development constraints of living in a conservation area through increased local capture of tourism revenues, that valley being the country's largest habitat for a globally threatened crane and an important natural wetland; and records basin work assessing the ecosystem services a river basin provides to downstream hydropower projects, to enable a payment mechanism, with modelling showing that degrading even a small upstream area sharply increases soil erosion.
