Read this with the community forests entry, the water act, the trust fund small grants and the district environment committee entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: National Environment Protection Act — the right to be informed while all options are open, the right to challenge substantive and procedural legality, and the caveat written next to the consultation right
trackers.desc: The public must be informed while all options are still open — the Act says so in those terms. The 2007 national environment protection legislation provides that the public concerned shall be informed in a timely and effective manner, either by public notice or individually as appropriate, of any environmental decision-making procedure, when all options are open and effective public participation can take place. That phrasing is the sentence to quote when a consultation is held after the decision is effectively made. Three participation rights are listed, and one carries a caveat worth knowing. The Act lists among the public's rights consultation during the environmental impact assessment process before an environmental clearance is issued — provided that the larger interest of the community or country shall prevail over individual interest — and commenting on draft legislation or regulations under preparation to implement the Act. Knowing that proviso in advance is better than meeting it for the first time in a hearing. The appeal right reaches procedure as well as substance. The Act provides that any person aggrieved by a decision taken under it may appeal to the Commission, and that the person aggrieved may challenge the substantive and procedural legality of any decision, act or omission, with that right of access to a review procedure applying in particular to any person who so considers. An omission is expressly included, which matters where an authority has simply not acted. The clearance regime it sits over is named, with monitoring and compensation powers. The commission's assessment and compliance division records its mandates under this Act, the 2000 assessment legislation and the 2016 clearance regulation as reviewing, assessing and deciding on issuance, rejection or renewal of environmental clearances; monitoring, controlling and enforcing the terms of a clearance attached to a development consent, including ordering sanctions and compensation for environmental damage; and preparing regulations on reporting, on the information an application must contain, and on monitoring and emergency response. Published material records the commission's power to adopt regulations on public information, consultation, mediation and appeals, on compensation for environmental damage from cleared projects, and to bring complaints for prosecution; and records six sectoral assessment guidelines published for mining, roads, industries, hydropower, transmission lines and forestry. Read this with the environment commission entry, the district environment committee, the reporting entry and the water act entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Water Quality Standards 2018 — the classes a river is assigned, the hydrology centre that must monitor ambient quality at its stations, and the duty to add stations on request
trackers.desc: Ambient river and stream monitoring is a named duty of a named body, at named stations. The 2018 water quality standards, made under the environment framework and approved at a numbered commission meeting, set out roles and responsibilities, providing that the national hydrology and meteorology centre shall conduct ambient water quality monitoring of rivers and streams along with other hydrological observations at all the hydrological stations it operates; install additional water quality monitoring stations or sites in consultation with the environment commission secretariat; and provide technical support to the secretariat and other agencies on monitoring. Asking for a station on a stretch a project will affect is therefore a request with a stated route and a stated body. The standards classify water by intended use, with limits attached. The document records parameter tables with limits by class — including a drinking water source class requiring conventional treatment, and a class for irrigation, industrial cooling and similar uses — and records bacteriological parameters among them, with the note that the generic standard applies unless otherwise stated. Establishing which class a stream is assigned to fixes the numbers a discharge must meet, before any argument about whether it is polluting. The amendment changed reporting, not the limits, and that distinction is recorded. The document records an amendment concerning the data reporting system to the commission, and states expressly that the amendment will not change the existing table of parameters and its limits, approved at a dated meeting. Knowing that the limits survived a revision is what lets an older reading still be compared. The air side is thinner, and the entry says so. Published research records air quality observatories established in this country with an international mountain research centre and the environment commission, giving measured mean concentrations of coarse and fine particulates at two named sites; a later factsheet records itself as the first consolidated national overview based on ground measurements, atmospheric models and satellite observations, presenting trends, seasonal patterns and spatial distribution. Published material records four monitoring stations and a recorded drop in particulate matter during a national lockdown. Read this with the water quality testing entry, the private laboratory, the water act and the environment commission entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Bhutan for Life and the trust fund's main grant window — the protected-area finance programme with its declining transition payments, and who may apply to the fund besides registered organisations
trackers.desc: A dedicated legal entity finances the protected area network, and its goals are published. The programme's own pages record it as a legal entity established under a royal charter granted in July 2018 to support a robust network of protected areas through long-term financing, and record its goals as a protected area network and biological corridors representing more than half the country; socio-economic wellbeing of communities in and near the protected area system enhanced by climate-informed natural resources management; stable populations of key species; habitat and ecosystem contiguity; and support for the government to develop new sources of financing. The second of those goals is the one a community near a park can quote. The financing structure is stated, including where the money is meant to come from afterwards. The same pages record donated funds placed in a transition fund making annual payments, starting high and declining to zero over a fourteen-year project period, while the government increases its own funding by roughly five to seven per cent annually, after which the country funds its protected areas alone; and record the identified internal sources as a green tax on vehicle imports, payment for ecosystem services from hydropower, and revenue from eco-tourism in the protected areas — the second of which is the instrument already recorded in this bucket. Published material records the mechanism as combining a stated donor fund with a larger government contribution over that period. The trust fund's main grant window names community groups and individuals among eligible applicants. A finance resource database records the trust fund — established by the government with a development programme and a conservation organisation — as running an annual call for applications for grants and project-related investment, with eligible applicants including communities and non-registered citizen groups, individuals, non-profit and civil society organisations, subnational government, scholarly institutions, and towns and municipalities, across ecosystems including forest, freshwater, wetland, mountains and human-changed areas, on a thematic focus set for each funding cycle. That an unregistered citizen group is listed is the operative fact. The fund's own standing and mission are published. Its site records it as the world's first environmental trust fund, established in 1991, with a renewed royal charter granted in 2021, and as the first entity in the country accredited to two named international climate funds; published description records its mission as funding conservation of flora, fauna, ecosystems and biodiversity and addressing the adverse effects of development on the natural environment. Read this with the small grants entry, the ecosystem services contract, the conservation NGO and the community forest entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Bhutan Ecological Society — a domestic non-profit doing field research and restoration with communities, its published programme areas, and the four-party restoration agreement it sits inside
trackers.desc: There is a domestic scientific non-profit that works with communities, and its programme areas are published. The society records itself as focusing on climate resilience, renewable energy, sustainable food and water systems, landscape restoration and conservation, working through research, education and policy advocacy; and records that it works with communities and partners to restore degraded forests and farmlands, expand native tree cover, strengthen livelihoods and support climate resilience, and that it conserves and enhances water systems, improves access and protects biodiversity. Published description records it as connecting education, science, praxis, business and policy, delivering field-based environmental education in partnership with the national university and a foreign field studies school, and states its intention to pilot, demonstrate and upscale climate adaptation strategies in collaboration with communities, academia, civil society and the government. For a community that needs field science rather than advocacy, that is a domestic body that does it. It publishes and awards, which is how evidence becomes usable. The society records a programme that documents its projects, develops learning opportunities and shares research that turns environmental evidence into public understanding and better decisions, running trainings and symposia, publishing a peer-reviewed journal and supporting a named environmental stewardship award. Its address and post box in the capital are published. It is one of four parties to a national restoration agreement, with stated targets. A conservation organisation's press release records a 2025 four-party agreement between the government, that organisation, the environmental trust fund already recorded in this bucket and this society, under a named regional initiative, aiming to restore up to fifty thousand hectares of degraded land over the next decade; records the trust fund's managing director saying it will align national ambition with global support; records the agreement as intended to empower Bhutanese organisations and communities to lead implementation of restoration plans; and quotes the society's executive director on working hand in hand with communities to bring degraded forests back to life, with a financing package and national restoration roadmap to follow. A grant record notes the society awarded a regional competitive block grant to tackle plastic waste and river pollution. Read this with the trust fund entry, the conservation society, the community forests and the payment for ecosystem services entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The Bar Council and pro bono legal aid — a statutory duty to provide free legal aid to indigent people, a merits screen run by the legal aid centre, and about three hundred registered attorneys
trackers.desc: The bar's own published functions include free legal aid and getting lawyers into the districts. The council lists among its functions providing pro bono legal aid to an indigent person, in addition to funding support from the state, and facilitating access to lawyer services across the country, alongside promoting legal education, assisting the courts in expediting cases and conducting general meetings. Access across the country is the problem in a mountain state, and it is named as a duty rather than an aspiration. The route to a free lawyer runs through a merits screen, and it is described. Published reporting records the council urging members to provide free legal services more often to marginalised and vulnerable people, records 300 attorneys registered with the council, and records that before cases arrive at the council they undergo scrutiny from the national legal aid centre to see if they merit pro bono services. It records an attorney describing colleagues' initial reluctance and growing interest in taking such cases. Knowing the screen exists tells an applicant where the decision is actually made. The council is statutory, and its composition is published. Published description records the council constituted under a 2016 amendment to the 2003 legal practitioners legislation, with a named royal president and an inaugural ceremony in May 2017; and records its members as an independent representative, the attorney general as ex-officio member, two retired justices — one of the high court and one of the supreme court — and three members elected from among the lawyers. The statute itself records the council's duties as including determining, maintaining and enhancing standards of professional practice and ethical conduct; determining the maximum number of cases a lawyer may handle at one time; regulating and checking the time taken for each case; and entertaining and determining cases of misconduct against lawyers on its roll. Those last duties are the complaint route if representation goes wrong. Published material records that no person may practise unless enrolled with the council, and that eligibility requires citizenship, a recognised legal qualification, the national legal course and the bar selection examination. Read this with the ecological society, the trust fund, the community forests and the assessment entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Tarayana Foundation — a registered public benefit organisation with its registration number, field officers reaching remote villages, and self-help groups where the community decides what changes
trackers.desc: A registered organisation works in the villages that are hardest to reach, and its registration is public. Published description records it as a civil society organisation and public benefit organisation registered with the country's civil society organisation authority, with its registration number given, founded in 2003 and governed by a board of directors and executive committees, its secretariat managing programmes through a network of programme and field officers. It records its focus as remote, rural villages, bridging the gaps between larger national initiatives and local grassroots requirements, noting that difficult terrain and the scattered nature of communities make it very challenging for many communities to access social services and markets. For a scattered settlement facing a project, an organisation whose whole method is reaching such places is the realistic ally. Communities make the decisions, and that is the stated method. Published description records it focusing on social mobilisation, capacity building and empowerment processes wherein communities make the main decisions for change they want effected in their villages; and records its interventions in four areas beginning with community mobilisation through awareness raising, capacity building, collective action through self-help groups — mostly women — and promoting volunteerism in the community and in schools, alongside access to basic needs and services, education support, and rural livelihoods. Its own pages record work across social, economic, environment and climate development, and research, advocacy and network. Its delivered numbers show the scale it operates at. Published reporting records a housing improvement programme as its flagship, with 244 new houses constructed, 31 renovated and 64 under construction in a single year across thirteen named districts, and 229 new and improved pour-flush toilets constructed with 30 under construction; and records food security support to 39 villages in 12 districts to cultivate vegetables on approximately 150 acres, with youths laid off during the pandemic taking part. An award assessment records its role as a grassroots facilitator bringing together stakeholders to achieve a common goal, and records that involving grassroots in project design, management and implementation improved the relevance of the interventions. Read this with the ecological society, the trust fund, the bar council and the community forest entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Bhutan Transparency Initiative — a civil society organisation supporting victims and witnesses of corruption, working alongside the named state bodies, and the journalists' association beside it
trackers.desc: Supporting the people who report corruption is a stated programme here, not an afterthought. Published description records the organisation's work as including supporting the victims and witnesses of corruption and institutionalising civil society accountability standards in all registered civil society organisations in the country. For someone who has reported a bribe over a land decision, an organisation whose written remit covers victims and witnesses is the difference between reporting alone and reporting with support. It names the institutions it works with, which is how a community knows where a case can travel. The same description records it working closely with the national anti-corruption commission, the department of local governance of the home affairs ministry, the royal audit authority, the royal court of justice, the office of the attorney general, civil society organisations, local governments, relevant private organisations and the communities at large — several of those bodies already recorded in this bucket — and records it working with individuals from diverse backgrounds including vulnerable and marginalised groups. Its structure is published, which is what makes it checkable. It records a board of trustees of seven members from diverse backgrounds, the executive director as member secretary to the board, and three divisions — operations, programme, and communication and resource management; and records that since its inception in 2014 it has established itself as the leading civil society organisation for anti-corruption and governance in the country. The journalists' association is the other body worth knowing. It records itself as non-political and non-profit, launched in February 2012 and registered as a mutual benefit civil society organisation under the civil society organisations legislation on 10 November 2014, with mandates including upholding freedom of expression and media, protecting and promoting the right to information, and protecting journalists from hazards such as threats, harassment and litigation, managed by a secretariat headed by an executive director answerable to a board. Read this with the anti-corruption commission, the audit authority, the civil society authority and the independent newspaper entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The civil society brief and the registered organisations it profiles — how many bodies exist, what they do, how they are funded, and the two registration categories a new group must choose between
trackers.desc: A published brief describes the country's registered civil society sector organisation by organisation. The publisher records the brief as explaining how the country's civil society organisations have evolved since the 1980s, delving into their funding, and showing how they work alongside government to provide basic services and assistance to vulnerable groups, and as detailing the work of some of the country's 54 registered organisations, whose activities range from environmental protection to supporting entrepreneurs; other material records 47 legally registered organisations at an earlier date, alongside numerous voluntary groups. For a community deciding whether to form a body or join one, a profile of the whole sector is the map. The registration rules are located by chapter, which is what a new group needs. The brief records that the constitution commits the state to endeavour to create a civil society free of oppression, discrimination and violence, based on the rule of law, protection of human rights and dignity; and records that Chapter 5 of the civil society legislation provides for registration and establishment, that Chapter 7 of the rules and regulations sets out the requirements for registration, and that Chapter 8 sets out the grounds for refusal. Knowing that refusal grounds are written down, and where, is the difference between an application and a guess. The regulator's own account gives the dates and the duties. The authority records the legislation enacted on 20 June 2007 to promote the establishment and growth of civil society organisations, its own formation in 2009 with a secretariat from 2010, and the Act amended in 2022; and lists its duties as reviewing and approving registration applications that satisfy the Act, approving accreditation of foreign organisations, monitoring organisations' compliance with the Act and their own charters, and liaising with government agencies. It records itself as the bridge between government and civil society, and records a quarterly meeting held to enhance networking among organisations. Published description records the oldest conservation society — already in this bucket — as registered as one of the public benefit organisations, the category that matters for a body intending to serve the wider public rather than its own members. Read this with the civil society authority entry, the ecological society, the rural foundation and the transparency initiative entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Community forest management groups and the divisional forest office — ten households can form a group, the range post at block level is the nearest forestry service point, and the district administration approves the plan
trackers.desc: Ten households are enough to form a group, and the approval sits at district level. Published material records that a group of at least ten households willing to establish, control and manage a forest area as a community forest can form a community forest management group, and that the group is authorised to control the management of the community forest in accordance with the management plan prepared by the group and approved by the district administration on the recommendation of the divisional forest officer. For a village facing loss of the forest it uses, ten households and a district approval is a smaller threshold than most routes in this file. What the plan must contain is listed, and the difficulty is stated plainly. The same material records that the plan needs maps of the boundary and various compartments, management objectives, descriptions of forest types and species, an assessment of the forest condition and an inventory of the forest areas, and records that it is often difficult for local people to provide such information for a management plan — which is precisely where a mapping or forestry ally is needed. Published rules record that the group shall prepare and adopt by-laws observing good governance principles such as participation, transparency, accountability, equity and inclusiveness. The nearest forestry office is at block level, and the field structure is published. Published material records the forest department as having, at field level, 14 territorial divisions, 10 national parks and wildlife sanctuaries, with several range posts providing service to local communities at block level, and records the divisional forest office as the custodian of forest resources in the districts, catering forestry services to the people. The scale shows this is a well-used route, and one practical benefit is recorded. Published material records 781 community forests in 2018 covering about 92,165 hectares, roughly 3 per cent of forested area, benefiting about a third of the rural population, an earlier count giving 36 forests over 2,914 hectares with 1,664 households; and records that communities can get the wood they require from the nearby community forest simply by using a local permit issued by the group's executive committee members. Read this with the civil society brief, the ecological society, the rural foundation and the forest legislation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The District Environment Committee and the district environment officer — the district body that issues or refuses clearance, the route an application must travel through the block head, and the site visit a community can ask for
trackers.desc: The body that grants or refuses environmental clearance for smaller projects sits in the district, not the capital. A district administration records its environment section as functioning under the aegis of the district environment committee, constituted under a named section of the environment protection legislation, and records the committee as the competent authority at district level, whose duties are issuing environmental clearance for projects within the district's competence; reviewing non-listed projects before forwarding them to the national commission secretariat or another competent authority; compliance monitoring of the conditions of clearance and taking necessary action for non-compliance; gathering and forwarding environmental information; and monitoring the quality of the environment. For a village facing a quarry, a farm road or a small plant, the decision-maker has an office in the district town. The route an application must travel runs through the block head. A district administration records that private applicants and individuals must route their application through the concerned block head or sub-district office, which forwards it with the complete set of required documents to the district administrator, chairman of the committee, after proper review and verification; that the applicant pays the fee to the district revenue section; and that the environment officer reviews the application, may seek additional documents, and coordinates a site visit programme with relevant stakeholders where deemed necessary, with the visiting team compiling a field verification report that the committee may endorse, reject, or return with directives such as re-verification, a joint field visit, further documents or a halt. Knowing the block head sees the file first, and that a joint field visit can be ordered, is where a community's evidence lands. Operating without clearance is expensive, and the forms are downloadable. The same administration records that a fine equivalent to ten times the application fee is imposed for establishing, commencing or carrying out a project without the required environmental clearance, with a late renewal penalty, and records assessment forms uploaded to the district website for download. Published description records the assessment legislation defining concerned people as individuals, groups and communities whose interests may be affected by a project. Read this with the community forest groups, the civil society brief, the transparency initiative and the ecological society entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Thromde municipal offices — the elected town council that levies land and property taxes, the division that issues and polices building permits, and the named approval chain a construction file must climb
trackers.desc: The office that issues building permits also polices them, and its mandate says both. A capital municipality records its compliance and enforcement division's mandates as ensuring planned development in compliance with the structure plan, the development control regulation and other relevant regulations; issuance of development, building and demolition permits within the municipality; upholding traditional architecture; promoting a safe and habitable built environment; inspection and monitoring of developments to ensure compliance as per approved drawings; delivering public services on building valuations, queries and conflicts; monitoring unauthorised constructions, squatter settlements and encroachment on state land; and facilitating commercial activities within the municipality in line with that regulation. For a resident watching a building rise past its approved drawings, the inspection duty is written down in the same list as the permit power. The approval chain is published step by step, with named posts. The municipality records that an applicant files a construction application with the land ownership record copy, two sets of architectural, structural, electrical and sanitary drawings, and the design team's certificate, pays a registration fee at customer care, receives a construction approval identification number, and has the drawings forwarded to an architect who approves or rejects and informs the client by telephone; that basement and attic questions go to the mayor; that approved drawings go on to a structural engineer and an electrical engineer, then require power clearance from the national power corporation; and that final approval is generated by the chief of the development regulation division, the executive secretary and the mayor before scrutiny, service and amenity fees are paid. A second municipality publishes the same chain, and a service portal lists construction permits, water supply, sewer connection, occupancy certification and vacuum tanker services together. The council above them is elected and can tax. Published description records municipalities as a second-level administrative division codified under a named 2009 local government legislation, administered independently by a municipal council of seven to ten elected members headed by a mayor where sufficiently developed, and records those councils as empowered to regulate advertising, enforce public health and safety rules, and levy taxes on land, property and property transfer. Read this with the district environment committee, the community forest groups, the civil society brief and the local governance entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: District and sub-district courts — a court in each of twenty districts plus sub-district benches, a civil court fee of fifty ngultrum, and a jabmi rather than a lawyer to speak for you
trackers.desc: The court fee for a civil case at district and sub-district level is fifty ngultrum. A published legal system guide records that parties in a civil case pay only 100 ngultrum as court fee in the High Court, while court fees in the district and sub-district courts are only 50 ngultrum. For a household weighing whether a claim is affordable, that is the whole filing cost at first instance. There is a court in every district and a lower bench below it. The same guide records a district court in each of the twenty districts, the first established in 1960 or 1961, usually of one bench and sometimes with division benches, exercising original jurisdiction in all cases within its territorial jurisdiction and hearing appeals from an order or judgment of a sub-district court, presided over by a district judge assisted by one or more registrars. It records the sub-district court, established in 1978, as the lowest formal court in the country, with three such courts having original jurisdiction in all cases within their territorial jurisdiction. Published legislation records that a sub-district court exercises original jurisdiction where the original jurisdiction of the High Court and the district court does not apply, and that a case shall be registered with the registry of the court. A jabmi speaks for a party, and hearings are uninterrupted. The guide records that judges allow uninterrupted hearing to the litigants or their jabmis, that parties are given opportunity to make presentation to the court and answer questions posed by the judges, and that the plaintiff and defendant or their jabmis can submit evidence to substantiate their legal contentions, with courts deciding on the facts and issues submitted by the parties and a civil claimant proving the case by a fair preponderance of the credible evidence. Published legislation records that the court shall allow the parties or their jabmi rebuttal. Orders travel between courts automatically. The legislation records that where a court issues a warrant, order or judgment to be carried out in another court's territory, the issuing court shall request by court order the receiving court to take necessary action, and the receiving court shall ensure it is carried out fully. Read this with the district environment committee, the thromde municipal offices, the community forest groups and the bar council entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The block office and its administrative officer — 205 blocks, a council of five to eight elected ward representatives, a chief executive who must observe whether decisions comply, and a no-confidence petition route
trackers.desc: The block office is the counter that handles the paperwork a rural household actually needs. Published description records that the block office, made up of the head, the deputy and ward representatives, is where officials put up proposals for rural infrastructure in the five year plans, organise local projects, gather community labour, process a lot of paperwork from census to wood permit, settle disputes, and decide the use of community resources like land; and records that governments have sought to strengthen this institution through appointment of block administrative officers, building modern block offices, and decentralising budget and administrative powers. Deciding the use of community land, and issuing wood permits, are the two functions a community will meet first. The council is small, elected ward by ward, and removable. Published description records 205 blocks, averaging about 230 square kilometres, divided into wards for elections; records the council as the head, the deputy and between five and eight democratically elected ward representatives, serving five-year terms; and records that the local electorate may petition for an election by a simple majority of the voting population to vote no confidence in the local government, carried by at least two-thirds. It records the council as holding powers to regulate resources, manage public health and safety, and levy taxes on land, grazing, cattle, entertainment and utilities, and as meeting to approve the block's annual plan and budget, manage community resources, pass local regulations and resolve disputes. The chief executive has a compliance duty written into the legislation. The local governance legislation records that the block administrative officer shall be the chief executive of the block and the executive secretary; that the chief executive shall observe whether the local government is acting in accordance with prescribed requirements; and that the chief executive shall implement the decisions of the local government, with the block administration submitting reports to the district. Read this with the local governance councils, the district environment committee, the community forest groups and the municipal offices entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Block and district development grants — a fixed annual sum each block and district can spend on what it chooses, allocated by a published resource formula, with an assessment of how that discretion is used
trackers.desc: Local governments get a fixed sum they may direct themselves. A study prepared for the upper house records that plan formulation has been based on activities identified by people at block level, with the allocation of formula-based annual grants to local governments to fund their plans, and records that the grants system is generally seen to provide objectivity and certain predictability over resources for local governments. It records that local governments now have access to block development grants, a system which provides greater financial flexibility over a fixed sum. Money whose use the block itself decides is the difference between a plan and a wish. The formula and the tiers are published. Published reporting records that the planning commission allocates budget based on a resource allocation formula, described as a framework for sharing and allocation of capital resources in the form of five-year and annual grants to districts, blocks and municipalities to fund their expenditure, responsibilities and functions; and records an official saying the formula-based grants provide resource predictability from the central government and flexibility in terms of priority-setting discretion, enhancing ownership, transparency and accountability and encouraging greater people's participation in development and decision-making. It records the formula as introduced for districts and blocks in one plan period and for the four municipalities later, and records that checks and balances are determined by regular monitoring and audits by the national audit authority. The district grant has a stated annual figure. A finance ministry account records a district-level development grant of a stated annual sum per district, with government having identified the broad areas in which the grant should be used; records the block grant initiative as having encouraged greater community participation and vitality in identifying pressing needs; and records the annual grant to blocks as the sum total of all financial resources allocated to blocks to achieve their planned programmes and activities as per their needs and priorities, and to maintain existing service infrastructure. Read this with the block offices, the local governance councils, the district environment committee and the municipal offices entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Associação Projecto Vitó
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Cape Verdean environmental association that began on Fogo as a volunteer effort after a sea-turtle rescue and now works on Fogo, Brava, Santo Antão, São Nicolau and Santiago, and in the Reserva Natural Integral dos Ilhéus do Rombo. It supports management of the Parque Natural do Fogo and the operationalisation of the Fogo Biosphere Reserve, working through citizen science and transferring technical knowledge to civil society. The first environmental NGO awarded Cape Verde's Medal of Merit, First Class. USE IT: as the organisation with standing and field presence inside Cape Verde's protected-area network — the route to getting a site monitored, documented and argued for. It is a conservation and education body, not a campaigning or legal one.

trackers.name: Biosfera
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Cape Verdean NGO working on coastal and marine species and their habitats from São Vicente, with long-running field operations on the uninhabited island of Santa Luzia. It states a dual mission — conservation, and mobilising Cape Verdean civil society for the protection of the environment — and its strategic objectives include protecting coastal and marine habitats, promoting responsible artisanal fishing and reducing pollution that disturbs species and habitats. USE IT: as the coastal counterpart to the protected-area bodies. It is the organisation to approach about a shoreline, a fishery or a marine habitat under pressure, and the one in Cape Verde that most explicitly treats mobilising the public as part of its job.

trackers.name: Cabo Verde. Supremo Tribunal de Justiça
trackers.desc: Cabo Verde. Supremo Tribunal de Justiça — supreme court (Cabo Verde).

trackers.name: Tribunal de Contas
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Cabo Verde, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Cabo Verde — Ministério das Finanças
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the DGPOG prepares & publishes the State Budget (Orçamento do Estado) and provisional accounts, Cabo Verde. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Cabo Verde.

trackers.name: Cabo Verde — Casa do Cidadão (Porton di nos Ilha / Empresa no Dia)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the Casa do Cidadão portal handles company name reservation (Certificado de Admissibilidade de Firma) & the “Empresa no Dia” incorporation regime (IRN), with beneficial-ownership disclosure via CENTIF, Cabo Verde. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: Conselho Assessor — a statutory council per island, or per protected area
trackers.desc: A NAMED BODY WHOSE STATED PURPOSE IS POPULATION PARTICIPATION. Article 22(1) of Decreto-Lei n.º 3/2003 of 24 February provides that the government department responsible for the environment may create a Conselho Assessor for each island or, exceptionally, for a single protected area, with the object of facilitating management through the participation of the population and cooperation. TWO QUESTIONS FOLLOW: does a Conselho Assessor exist for your island or your area — and if not, can one be requested? The composition is set out in the Boletim Oficial, I Série n.º 44 of 23 July 2014, with certain representatives designated by the respective members of Government, so the balance between state and community seats is checkable in the gazette rather than a matter of practice. This is the route into management decisions short of litigation, and in a small-island jurisdiction it is likely to be the more productive one.

trackers.name: Six categories — and two of them have never been used
trackers.desc: PICK YOUR CATEGORY KNOWING WHICH ARE EMPTY. Decreto-Lei n.º 3/2003 creates the typology of protected areas and gives them juridical content, configures the Rede Nacional das Áreas Protegidas as an open system into which declared areas are progressively integrated, and articulates the public participation guaranteed in the Lei de Bases da Política do Ambiente. ‘An open system’ is the phrase to use — the network is designed to keep admitting areas, so a proposal works with the statute's logic; and the participation guarantee lives in the Lei de Bases, so cite both. THE SIX: Reserva Natural (15 sites, in integral, parcial and temporal subcategories — a ‘temporal’ reserve is protection for a defined period); Parque Nacional — no sites have been decreed; Parque Natural; Monumento Natural; Paisagem Protegida — zones where the integrated action of man and nature has created aesthetic or cultural value, protection centred on maintenance and restoration, so this is the category for a worked, inhabited landscape; and Sítio de Interesse Científico — places generally of reduced dimension holding populations threatened with extinction, of which none have yet been designated. For a small site with a threatened population that category is unused rather than unavailable — being first is harder, but it exists and is designed for small sites. Coverage exceeds 10 percent of the country, about 632.09 km²; Parques and Reservas Naturais are at least 75 percent of the network. Responsible body: Direção Nacional do Ambiente.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: ADAD, Praia — Cape Verde's oldest environmental association, and the 2020 decree that gives you an EIA to comment on
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Associação para a Defesa do Ambiente e Desenvolvimento (ADAD), a legally constituted NGO created in 1991 in Praia, Santiago, and published in the official gazette — the country's long-standing national environmental association, working on sustainable practice, biodiversity protection and environmental justice, alongside education and engagement with decision-makers. It is a member of the international conservation union and of regional marine and coastal networks, so a small island community has a route through it to outside technical and legal attention. Address: Avenida Cidade Lisboa, Fazenda, Praia, Santiago. THE LEGAL HOOK TO NAME, and it is recent enough that many people do not know it exists: Decreto-Lei n.º 27/2020 approves the legal regime for environmental impact assessment of PUBLIC AND PRIVATE projects likely to produce significant effects on the environment, published in the official bulletin of 19 March 2020, with requirements for impact studies and assessment processes aligned to established good practice. If a hotel, quarry, marina or road is proposed near you in Cape Verde, ask which EIA was done under the 2020 regime, and ask to see it — that document is the only formal opening most residents will get. WHO IT SUITS: Cape Verdean residents and community associations facing coastal development, quarrying or infrastructure, and island groups needing a national body with international network reach. CAVEATS: NO VERIFIED LIVE SITE OF ITS OWN WAS FOUND — this entry points at the conservation union's member record, and the association's public presence is largely through social media; it is an environmental association, not a law firm or a fund. For Sao Vicente and marine reporting, Cape Verde's Biosfera entry.

trackers.name: Cape Verde — free legal assistance is a state-assured right delivered by STATE-APPOINTED ADVOCATES, with an access-to-law institute alongside
trackers.desc: WHAT YOU ARE ENTITLED TO: in Cape Verde access to free legal assistance is a right ASSURED BY THE STATE, so that every citizen regardless of economic condition can have adequate legal representation — and the service is delivered by ADVOCATES APPOINTED BY THE STATE who act in judicial proceedings AT NO COST to the beneficiary. The mechanism is appointment, not application to a fund: what you are asking for is the nomination of an advocate, and the phrase to use is apoio jurídico / assistência jurídica gratuita. THE INSTITUTION NAMED ALONGSIDE IT: the Instituto de Acesso ao Direito e à Justiça (IADJ), described as a principal instrument of legal support, offering ORIENTATION and LEGAL REPRESENTATION to citizens; the Ordem dos Advogados de Cabo Verde sits beside it, running continuing training for advocates. The barriers the same account names are the familiar pair — lack of financial resources and the COMPLEXITY OF LEGAL PROCEDURES — with government and NGOs running free or reduced-cost assistance programmes to mitigate them. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ISLAND LAND DISPUTE: Cape Verde's development pressure is coastal and touristic, and the country's environmental impact regime — recorded separately in this file — gives a resident a document to contest; a state-appointed advocate is how an ordinary household actually contests it, because the EIA route is worthless if nobody can file. WHO IT SUITS: Cape Verdeans without means facing an expropriation, coastal development, inheritance or property dispute on any island. CAVEATS: THIS ENTRY IS SOURCED FROM A CAPE VERDEAN LEGAL-SECTOR PUBLICATION RATHER THAN A GOVERNMENT PORTAL — confirm the current procedure and the IADJ's contact details with the Ordem dos Advogados de Cabo Verde before relying on specifics; appointment depends on advocate availability across a nine-island archipelago. For the EIA regime and the national environmental association, Cape Verde's ADAD entry; for Sao Vicente marine reporting, Biosfera.

trackers.name: Fundo do Ambiente, Cape Verde — a public institute that finances environmental preservation projects, and it funds MUNICIPALITIES directly
trackers.desc: WHERE TO APPLY FOR MONEY: the FUNDO DO AMBIENTE, a Cape Verdean PUBLIC INSTITUTE whose current statute was approved by Decreto-lei nº59/2020 of 5 August, developing the regulatory norms foreseen in the Lei de Bases da Política do Ambiente and establishing the fundamental principles for managing and protecting the environment against all forms of degradation. The financing regime for projects relating to environmental preservation activity sits in Decreto-Lei nº40/2013. A dedicated financing decree plus a public institute means the money is not discretionary charity — cite the decree number when you ask what the current window is. WHO IT ACTUALLY PAYS, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART: documented disbursements go to MUNICIPAL COUNCILS — the Câmara Municipal de São Miguel received a rotating excavator to give effect to its projects, and a new urban solid waste collection truck, and a memorandum of understanding was signed between the Fund, that municipal council and the island water utility. Equipment and works through your own câmara municipal is how island environmental money actually lands — so the lever, as in Mali, is the municipal council rather than a direct community application. Ask your câmara what it has requested from the Fundo do Ambiente and what it received; both sides of that are public. WHO IT SUITS: Cape Verdean municipalities, associations and communities with an environmental preservation, waste or water project on any island. CAVEATS: A STATE FINANCING INSTITUTE — it funds environmental preservation, NOT litigation, land purchase or opposition to a licensed development, and the documented flow is to municipal councils rather than to villages directly; confirm the current window and eligibility before relying on it. For the 2020 EIA regime and the national environmental association, Cape Verde's ADAD entry; for a state-appointed advocate, the legal assistance entry; for Sao Vicente marine reporting, Biosfera.

trackers.name: Cape Verde's protected areas and their Conselho Assessor — article 22 lets a council be created FOR A SINGLE PROTECTED AREA, to secure local community participation
trackers.desc: THE SEAT AT THE TABLE AND HOW TO GET IT: Cape Verde's protected areas sit in the REDE NACIONAL DE ÁREAS PROTEGIDAS under DECRETO-LEI Nº3/2003 of 24 February, with categories including Parque Natural, Reserva Natural and Reserva Natural Integral, each delimited by its own decreto-regulamentar. ARTICLE 22 IS THE PROVISION TO QUOTE: the government department responsible for the environment MAY CREATE A CONSELHO ASSESSOR FOR EACH ISLAND OR, EXCEPTIONALLY, FOR A SINGLE PROTECTED AREA, to facilitate management THROUGH THE PARTICIPATION OF THE POPULATION and cooperation between administrative bodies — and where such a council has been created its stated objects are TO SUPPORT AND ENSURE THE PARTICIPATION OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND PARTNER ENTITIES, and TO PROPOSE DIRECTIVES AND ACTIONS. A council can be created for ONE protected area, and its job is your participation — that is the cheapest formal standing available in Cape Verde: ask the environment department to constitute a Conselho Assessor for the area you live beside. WHAT THE DECLARATIONS ARE BUILT ON, which tells you what argument works: the Boa Vista Parque Natural do Norte was declared to conserve natural values AND THEIR INTERACTION WITH THE SOCIOECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT OF LOCAL POPULATIONS, THROUGH THE STRENGTHENING OF TRADITIONAL ACTIVITIES. Traditional activity is written into the ground of declaration — so a fishing or salt-working practice is an argument FOR protection, not an obstacle to it. WHAT THESE AREAS FACE, DOCUMENTED ON SAL: the Ponta do Sinó reserve is ALMOST ENTIRELY SURROUNDED BY RESORTS, its size reduced not only by government decrees but by the loss of sand migration, with dunes that have disappeared; threats listed are vehicle traffic across the dunes, coastal development, light and noise pollution, and disturbance of nesting and feeding sites. The Baía da Murdeira reserve, created 2003, is the ONLY officially designated MARINE reserve in Cape Verde — about 2,067 hectares; Costa da Fragata covers 2,693 hectares, 346 on land and 2,347 marine. Local conservation work is run as COOPERATIVE MANAGEMENT of the protected areas — training, trail delimitation, codes of conduct, dune restoration, and community outreach including GUIDE TRAINING AND SUSTAINABLE LIVELIHOODS FOR FISHERS AND RESIDENTS. WHO IT SUITS: Cape Verdean island communities beside a protected area or facing resort expansion. CAVEATS: STATE-DECLARED AREAS WITH ADVISORY COMMUNITY BODIES, NOT COMMUNITY TENURE — the council is assessor, and decrees have themselves reduced reserve areas. For the EIA regime, Cape Verde's ADAD entry; for money, the Fundo do Ambiente entry; for a state-appointed advocate, the legal assistance entry.

trackers.name: Cape Verde's island-by-island conservation organisations — FMB on Maio, BIOS.CV on Boa Vista, Projeto Biodiversidade on Sal, Lantuna nationally, and the honest gap in community management
trackers.desc: WHICH ORGANISATION IS ON YOUR ISLAND — the only question that matters in a ten-island archipelago: FUNDAÇÃO MAIO BIODIVERSIDADE (FMB, fmb-maio.org), A CABO VERDEAN NON-PROFIT FOUNDED 2010 ON MAIO ISLAND, running four programmes — TURTLE PROTECTION, MARINE CONSERVATION, TERRESTRIAL CONSERVATION, and SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AND ECOTOURISM — with projects characterised by COMMUNITY-BASED STRATEGIES, strong scientific foundations and extensive outreach. WHAT IT ACHIEVED, WHICH IS WHY IT LEADS THIS ENTRY: work with FMB AS LOCAL PARTNER DELIVERED THE DESIGNATION OF A UNESCO BIOSPHERE RESERVE AND THE APPROVAL OF CABO VERDE'S FIRST PROTECTED AREAS MANAGEMENT PLAN, plus a GUARDIANS OF THE SEA initiative. A single-island foundation that produced the country's first protected-areas management plan is proof the instrument can start locally and end nationally — and FMB records that RANGERS deliver more than half the objectives of the biodiversity plan, so ask about ranger posts, which are jobs as well as protection. THE OTHERS, BY ISLAND: BIOS.CV, a Cabo Verdean NGO BASED ON BOA VISTA, TWENTY YEARS in environmental conservation — habitat protection for threatened turtles and birds, HUMPBACK WHALE MONITORING, environmental education for local people AND VISITORS, and TRAINING YOUNG PEOPLE in conservation of protected species and habitats; PROJETO BIODIVERSIDADE, a Cabo Verdean non-profit ON SAL ISLAND, protecting wildlife THROUGH COMMUNITY-LED ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION PROGRAMMES; and LANTUNA (lantuna.org), A CABO VERDEAN NGO CONSTITUTED 2013, for study, conservation and protection of the archipelago's environment, contributing to the sustainable development of RURAL AND URBAN COMMUNITIES and to ecotourism, working on the PARQUE NATURAL DA BAÍA DO INFERNO E DO MONTE ANGRA, and stating that it ACTS WITH AUTONOMY, guided by impartiality and merit, FREE OF EXTERNAL INFLUENCES, with a commitment to the collective interest and to making all essential information about its projects accessible. An organisation that publishes an independence clause is telling you it can act against an interest. Ask for that clause in writing from whoever offers to help you. AND THE STRUCTURAL GAP, RECORDED HONESTLY: UNLIKE OTHER WEST AFRICAN COUNTRIES, THERE IS NO PRACTICE OF COMMUNITY MANAGEMENT IN CABO VERDE — THOUGH A VARIETY OF COMMUNITY ASSOCIATIONS ACROSS THE ISLANDS REPRESENT FISHERS' INTERESTS, and partners are supporting those groups toward CO-MANAGEMENT OF MARINE RESOURCES AND COMMUNITY-LED PROTECTED AREAS. There is no established community-management route here yet — which means the fishers' associations that already exist are the vehicle, and the first community-led protected area is still unclaimed. WHO IT SUITS: Cabo Verdeans on any island, especially fishing communities and those near a natural park. CAVEATS: SMALL ISLAND NGOs, donor-dependent. For the oldest environmental association and the EIA route, Cape Verde's ADAD entry; for public financing, the Fundo do Ambiente entry; for the advisory council a protected area may create, the Conselho Assessor entry; also Projecto Vitó and Biosfera.

trackers.name: Plataforma das ONG de Cabo Verde — 724 registered organisations, a published roster of associations by island and concelho with phone numbers, and the 1987 law associations are formed under
trackers.desc: THE ROSTER BY ISLAND AND CONCELHO — which is what a Cape Verdean on one island actually needs: the PLATAFORMA DAS ONG DE CABO VERDE (platongs.org.cv) IS AN INDEPENDENT NON-PROFIT NGO WITH FINANCIAL, ADMINISTRATIVE AND PATRIMONIAL AUTONOMY, with a NAMED PRESIDENT, TWO PUBLISHED TELEPHONE NUMBERS AND AN EMAIL, whose mission is TO CONTRIBUTE TO STRENGTHENING AND IMPROVING THE LEVEL OF INTERVENTION OF ITS MEMBER ORGANISATIONS, and whose stated purpose has always been CREATING CONDITIONS THAT FAVOUR DIALOGUE, PARTICIPATION AND THE EMPOWERMENT OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, IN STRICT RESPECT FOR THEIR AUTONOMY. Patrimonial autonomy means it can hold property in its own right, and strict respect for members' autonomy is written into its purpose — an umbrella that says so is one your association can join without being absorbed. WHAT IT HOLDS: A BASE OF 724 ORGANISATIONS REGISTERED, and it has sought to take on FROM THE JUSTICE MINISTRY THE FUNCTION OF REGISTERING LEGAL PERSONS — arguing that because it is on the ground it could record each successive change within every association and so say AT ANY MOMENT HOW MANY ASSOCIATIONS EXIST IN CABO VERDE WITH EFFECTIVE FUNCTIONING, HOW MANY DO NOT FUNCTION, AND HOW MANY FUNCTION ILLEGALLY. Seven hundred and twenty-four organisations on one register, and the umbrella itself says the hard part is knowing which are actually working. Ask the Plataforma whether the association offering to help you is functioning — that is precisely the question it built the base to answer. AND IT PUBLISHES THE LIST: A GUIA DAS ONG AND A MAPEAMENTO DA SOCIEDADE CIVIL CABO-VERDIANA, PLUS A ROSTER OF CABO VERDEAN NGOs AND ASSOCIATIONS ARRANGED BY ISLAND AND BY CONCELHO WITH POSTAL ADDRESSES AND MOBILE AND LANDLINE NUMBERS — including, on Santiago, NAMED ASSOCIATIONS OF FISHERS AND FISHWIVES AND OF FARMERS AND LIVESTOCK KEEPERS at concelho level. An association of fishers and fishwives with a phone number in your own concelho is the ally a coastal project affects directly. Producer associations are already organised, already local, and already have a reason to object. THE NUMBERS THAT TELL YOU WHAT TO EXPECT: in one named concelho the survey records 18 CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, OF WHICH 14 ARE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT ASSOCIATIONS, WITH AN ASSOCIATIONAL PENETRATION RATE OF 16% AND FEMALE PARTICIPATION AROUND 47% — AND ONLY TWO OF THE SEVENTEEN AFFILIATED TO THE PLATAFORMA. Community development association is the dominant form in Cabo Verde, and most are NOT affiliated to the national platform. So the roster is where you find them, and affiliation is a step you can help a local association take. THE LAW THEY ARE FORMED UNDER IS NAMED: the associations law published in 1987, LEI Nº 78/III/87, is recorded alongside independence in 1975 and the political opening as one of the main references of Cape Verdean civil society's development. The Plataforma also records the sector's honest weakness: ONGs AND OTHER CSOs FACE NUMEROUS DIFFICULTIES, BEGINNING WITH THEIR LIMITED INSTITUTIONAL CONDITIONS AND INTERNAL CAPACITY TO PROPERLY MANAGE THE RESOURCES THEY OBTAIN FROM NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL PARTNERS. Capacity to manage money, not lack of money, is named as the first constraint. If you are raising funds for a local association, budget for its administration too. WHO IT SUITS: Cape Verdeans on any island seeking the association nearest them, and groups wanting to form or verify one. CAVEATS: A PLATFORM AND A DIRECTORY — not a funder or a law firm. For the local partner that delivered a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and the country's first protected areas plan, Cabo Verde's FMB entry; for the organisations on Boa Vista and Sal, BIOS.CV and Projeto Biodiversidade; for the independence clause, Lantuna.

trackers.name: AfricanDefenders (Pan-African Human Rights Defenders Network) — five sub-regional members with their own country lists, seven named Ubuntu Hub host cities from Kampala to Accra, and national coalitions it will help you build
trackers.desc: SEVEN CITIES WHERE YOU CAN GO AND STILL SPEAK THE LANGUAGE — placement note first: THIS IS A PAN-AFRICAN NETWORK, FILED UNDER CAPE VERDE BECAUSE THIS BUCKET CARRIED NO DEFENDER-NETWORK RESOURCE. ITS FIVE SUB-REGIONS COVER THE WHOLE CONTINENT. THE SEVEN HOST CITIES, NAMED: KAMPALA IN UGANDA; ABIDJAN IN CÔTE D'IVOIRE; TUNIS IN TUNISIA; JOHANNESBURG, PRETORIA AND CAPE TOWN IN SOUTH AFRICA; AND ACCRA IN GHANA — THE SEVENTH ADDED TO HOST ADDITIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS FROM WEST AFRICA. Seven actual cities with actual housing. This file's round on protection funds named the relocation programme in one line; here are the places it goes. Anglophone, francophone and arabophone options, which means for almost any African defender there is a destination where the language and the paperwork are familiar. AND WHAT THE RELOCATION IS FOR, IN ITS OWN TERMS: TEMPORARILY RELOCATING ARTISTS, BLOGGERS, JOURNALISTS OR OTHER HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS FACING VIOLENCE OR THREATS IN THEIR HOME COUNTRY — MOVING THESE ACTIVISTS TO A SAFE HOST CITY WHERE THEY SPEAK THE LANGUAGE AND REMAIN CONNECTED TO LOCAL ORGANIZATIONS, HELPING THEM CONTINUE THEIR IMPORTANT WORK — AND IN ADDITION TO PROVIDING HOUSING, THE NETWORK WORKS WITH LOCAL PARTNERS TO PROVIDE MEDICAL SUPPORT AND SERVICES. CONTINUE THEIR WORK, not stop it. That is the difference between relocation and exile: the point is to keep organising from somewhere safer, which is why the language and the connection to local organisations are stated as design features rather than conveniences. THE STRUCTURE, WHICH TELLS YOU HOW TO REACH IT: A NETWORK OF FIVE AFRICAN SUB-REGIONAL ORGANISATIONS, NATIONAL COALITIONS FOR HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, AND INDIVIDUAL DEFENDERS — SO AN INDIVIDUAL IS A CATEGORY OF MEMBER, NOT ONLY AN ORGANISATION. THE EAST AND HORN MEMBER, WITH ITS COUNTRY LIST: IT ESTABLISHES AND SUPPORTS NATIONAL COALITIONS OF HRDs IN VARIOUS COUNTRIES THROUGH WHICH HRDs CAN COME TOGETHER AND CLAIM THEIR RIGHTS AT THE NATIONAL LEVEL — AND SERVES AS SECRETARIAT OF A SUB-REGIONAL NETWORK DRAWING MEMBERSHIP FROM BURUNDI, DJIBOUTI, ERITREA, ETHIOPIA, KENYA, RWANDA, SOMALIA TOGETHER WITH SOMALILAND, SOUTH SUDAN, SUDAN, TANZANIA AND UGANDA, REPRESENTING MORE THAN 100 HRDs, BOTH INDIVIDUALS AND ORGANISATIONS. ESTABLISHES AND SUPPORTS NATIONAL COALITIONS is a service, not a description. If your country has no defenders' coalition, this is the body whose stated job is helping you build one — and note the country list: Djibouti, Eritrea, Somalia, Sudan and South Sudan are all in it, which are among the thinnest buckets in this entire file. THE CENTRAL AFRICA MEMBER: BASED IN DOUALA, CAMEROON, IT ACCOMPANIES AND REINFORCES THE WORK OF HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS WITH THE AIM TO MITIGATE THEIR VULNERABILITIES AND RISKS, AND TO RAISE AWARENESS OF THE HUMAN RIGHTS SITUATION IN THE SUB-REGION — ITS VISION BEING TO PROMOTE, TRAIN AND SUPPORT DEFENDERS, FOSTER SOLIDARITY AMONG THEM, AND DEFEND THEIR RIGHTS WHENEVER THESE ARE UNDER PRESSURE. THE WEST AFRICA MEMBER: CREATED IN MAY 2005, COMPOSED OF NATIONAL COALITIONS FOR HUMAN RIGHTS AND INDIVIDUALS. AND THE SOUTHERN AFRICA MEMBER, WITH ITS OWN NINE-COUNTRY ASSEMBLY: DELEGATES FROM ANGOLA, BOTSWANA, THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, ESWATINI, LESOTHO, MALAWI, SOUTH AFRICA, ZAMBIA AND ZIMBABWE. Four sub-regional bodies with published country lists between them. Find which one covers you, then ask it which national coalition exists in your country — that is a two-step route to the nearest organised protection, and it works from anywhere on the continent. THE PRACTICE WORTH REQUESTING BY NAME: THE NETWORK AND ITS MEMBERS ISSUE UNDERSIGNED REGIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL CALLS — INCLUDING ONE DEMANDING THE IMMEDIATE AND UNCONDITIONAL RELEASE OF A NAMED DEFENDER AND THE WITHDRAWAL OF HIS PROSECUTION, AND ONE OVER A RESTRICTION IMPOSED ON A MEMBER NETWORK'S ABILITY TO OPERATE THROUGHOUT A COUNTRY. A joint statement signed by regional and international organisations, naming a prosecution and demanding its withdrawal. That costs the network nothing and can cost a government a great deal. It is one of the fastest things to ask for when somebody is arrested — ask for the statement before you ask for money. THE RECOGNITION: A SHIELD AWARDS RECOGNISING OUTSTANDING DEFENDERS FOR THEIR IMPACT ON THE PROTECTION AND PROMOTION OF HUMAN RIGHTS. An award is protection. A named, publicly honoured defender is measurably harder to disappear quietly, and nominations are usually open. AND THE NOTE ON WHY ONE HOST CITY WORKS: THE HOST COUNTRY HAS LONG BEEN HOSTING REFUGEES COMING FROM ACROSS THE REGION, AND ITS REFUGEE POLICY HAS BEEN PRAISED AS ONE OF THE MOST OPEN IN THE WORLD. The relocation programme sits where the immigration rules already permit it. When considering where to move someone, the legal question is as important as the distance — and that is why these seven cities and not others. WHO IT SUITS: African land and environmental defenders under threat, and anyone in a country with no national defenders' coalition. CAVEATS: RELOCATION IS TEMPORARY and demand exceeds places. For the 24-hour helpline, the protection grants and the two directories, Benin's defender protection entry; for the 48-hour emergency fund, Liberia's African Defenders Emergency Fund entry; for the three application windows including a protection grant, Mauritania's rapid-response fund entry.

trackers.name: Farm Radio International — free radio scripts, dramas and interview questions already translated into local African languages, for the 1,300+ stations in 38 countries that have signed up — plus a published method that lets the community choose the topic and measured uptake of up to 48%
trackers.desc: THE SCRIPTS ARE FREE, AND OFTEN ALREADY IN YOUR LANGUAGE — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ETHIOPIA ENTRY COVERS THE COMMUNITY RADIO ASSOCIATION, MEMBERSHIP AND THE LICENSING ARGUMENT; ITS CHAD ENTRY COVERS A FUND THAT PAYS FOR TRANSMITTERS AND EQUIPMENT. NEITHER CARRIES THE FREE PROGRAMME RESOURCES, THE LOCAL-LANGUAGE SCRIPTS OR THE PARTICIPATORY METHOD BELOW. WHAT THEY GIVE, AND THE LANGUAGE CLAUSE IS THE FIND: RADIO RESOURCES LIKE BACKGROUNDERS, DRAMA SCRIPTS AND SUGGESTED INTERVIEW QUESTIONS — OFTEN AVAILABLE IN LOCAL AFRICAN LANGUAGES — PLUS INFORMATION PACKAGES WITH SCRIPTS, INTERVIEWS AND DRAMAS, A WEEKLY NEWS SERVICE ABOUT RURAL COMMUNITIES IN AFRICA, AND ONLINE DISCUSSIONS BETWEEN BROADCASTERS AND SUBJECT EXPERTS IN ENGLISH AND FRENCH. A station with a transmitter and nothing to broadcast is the commonest failure this file could record. Here is a library of finished programmes — dramas, interviews, background briefings — already written and often already in the language your listeners speak, free, and the site lets you save and edit a resource as a Word document so it can be rewritten for your own valley. SUGGESTED INTERVIEW QUESTIONS is the item to notice. A volunteer presenter facing a district officer or a company representative for the first time does not need courage so much as a page of the right questions. THE NETWORK, AND WHAT IT DELIBERATELY IS NOT: MORE THAN 1,300 RADIO STATIONS IN 38 AFRICAN COUNTRIES HAVE SIGNED UP AS BROADCASTING PARTNERS — AND, IN THEIR OWN WORDS: WE DON'T OWN RADIO STATIONS, WE DON'T EQUIP, OPERATE OR FINANCE THEM. WE WORK WITH AFRICAN RADIO STATIONS TO PROVIDE THE COMMUNICATION SERVICES THAT AFRICAN FARMERS, ENTREPRENEURS AND RURAL COMMUNITIES NEED. They do not own or run anything, which means the station stays yours. Read that beside this file's warnings about outside organisations arriving with their own agenda — an organisation that supplies content and refuses ownership is a different kind of partner. THE MEASURED SCALE: IN ONE YEAR, 154 RESOURCES PROVIDED TO 3,420 BROADCASTERS; 33 PROJECTS WITH 259 PARTNERS; 256 STATIONS HELPED TO INTERACT WITH MORE THAN 401,470 OF THEIR LISTENERS — REACHING AN ESTIMATED 24.5 MILLION PEOPLE ACROSS RURAL AFRICA. THE EVIDENCE THEY PUBLISH ABOUT THEIR OWN METHOD: PARTICIPATORY FARM RADIO PROGRAMMING, WHEN IT MEETS STANDARDS OF QUALITY AND CONSISTENCY, LEADS TO REMARKABLE GAINS IN KNOWLEDGE — AND SPECIALIZED, CAREFULLY DESIGNED PROGRAMS CAN LEAD TO UPTAKE OF MORE EFFECTIVE PRACTICES BY UP TO 48%, ON AVERAGE 21%, OF FARMING FAMILIES IN LISTENING AREAS, AT A COST OF PENNIES PER PERSON. A fifth of families in the listening area actually changing what they do, measured. If you are trying to get a whole district to adopt a boundary rule, a closed season or a testing routine, that is the benchmark to hold your own communications to — and the qualifier QUALITY AND CONSISTENCY is doing the work: one broadcast changes nothing. AND THE HONEST ORIGIN OF THAT EVIDENCE, WHICH IS RARER STILL: PRIOR TO THE RESEARCH INITIATIVE, INVESTMENTS IN RADIO PROGRAMS FOR FARMERS HAD ASSUMED THAT, BECAUSE RADIO IS THE MOST ACCESSIBLE AND RELEVANT MEDIUM FOR FARMERS IN SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA, AGRICULTURAL INFORMATION PROVIDED ON THE RADIO WAS MEANINGFUL AND HELPFUL — BUT THERE WAS VERY LITTLE HARD EVIDENCE TO BACK UP THIS CLAIM. They went and tested an assumption their whole sector was built on. Ask the same of anything offered to your community: who measured it, and against what. THE PARTICIPATORY PRINCIPLE, WHICH IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART: THE APPROACH ACKNOWLEDGES THAT FARMERS UNDERSTAND AND CAN EXPRESS THEIR OWN NEEDS, CAN EVALUATE OPTIONS IF THEY HAVE THE RIGHT INFORMATION, AND CAN MAKE DECISIONS TO ADOPT — OR NOT TO ADOPT — A PARTICULAR PRACTICE. IT ACTIVELY ENGAGES FARMERS IN IDENTIFYING AND CHOOSING THE THEME OF THE CAMPAIGN, AND FEATURES THEIR VOICES, PERSPECTIVES, CONCERNS AND QUESTIONS. OR NOT TO ADOPT. A method that treats refusal as a legitimate outcome is the opposite of the consultations this file records, where the decision was made before the meeting and the meeting existed to record consent. THE FIRST TWO STEPS, SO A STATION CAN RUN IT WITHOUT THEM: COMMUNITY RAPID APPRAISALS IN 100 COMMUNITIES, FOUR PER PARTICIPATING STATION, EACH TYPICAL OF THE AREA SERVED — GATHERING WHAT FARMERS NEED AND HOW FARMERS USE RADIO; THEN IMPROVEMENT SELECTION, ENGAGING KNOWLEDGE PARTNERS SUCH AS AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH INSTITUTIONS AND UNIVERSITY EXTENSION SERVICES. HOW FARMERS USE RADIO, asked before anything is broadcast — what hour, on whose set, with whom listening. A campaign aimed at a time when the women who do the work are in the fields reaches nobody. THE SPILLOVER FINDING: WHEN EVEN A SMALL NUMBER OF FARMERS ARE ENGAGED BY A RADIO STATION ON A CONTINUOUS, INTERACTIVE BASIS, LISTENERS IN OTHER COMMUNITIES BENEFIT BY LEARNING ABOUT AND INTRODUCING PRACTICES THEMSELVES. Engage a few properly and the rest overhear. That is the argument for depth in one village rather than a thin campaign across twenty. THE OFFICES: OPERATIONS BEGAN IN ONE EAST AFRICAN COUNTRY, WITH OFFICES IN MALAWI, UGANDA, GHANA, MALI, BURKINA FASO AND MOZAMBIQUE. AND THE LIMIT THEY STATE THEMSELVES: NOT ALL OF THE RADIO STATIONS WHO RECEIVE OUR RESOURCES PARTICIPATE IN OUR RADIO PROJECTS. Two different things: the free resources, open to any partner station, and the funded projects, which are selected. Sign up for the first without expecting the second. WHO IT SUITS: African community and rural radio stations, and the farming or fishing communities who want their issue on air in their own language. CAVEATS: RESOURCES ARE AIMED AT BROADCASTERS AND SKEW AGRICULTURAL — a station or a partner organisation is the route in, and funded projects are selective. For the association a station joins and the licensing argument, Ethiopia's entry; for grants that pay for transmitters and equipment, Chad's entry; for legal defence when a broadcaster is sued, South Sudan's entry.

trackers.name: SOMO (Centre for Research on Multinational Corporations) — a research centre running since 1973 that files complaints to accountability mechanisms on behalf of people harmed by financed projects — with a complaint-tools website covering the African development bank, and the published finding that fear of reprisal is what stops communities using these routes
trackers.desc: THEY FILE THE COMPLAINT THEMSELVES, ON YOUR BEHALF — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S CHAD ENTRY COVERS THE NATIONAL CONTACT POINTS, ITS BURUNDI ENTRY THE DATABASE OF COMPLAINTS TO ACCOUNTABILITY MECHANISMS AND THE REQUEST-ONLY LEGAL NON-PROFIT, ITS NIGERIA ENTRY THE AFRICAN DEVELOPMENT BANK'S OWN REVIEW MECHANISM, AND ITS COMOROS ENTRY THE CARBON GRIEVANCE REVIEW WHICH CITES THIS CENTRE'S RESEARCH. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHAT IT DOES FOR AFFECTED PEOPLE, AND IT IS THE FIND: IT SUPPORTS THOSE PEOPLE ADVERSELY AFFECTED BY DEVELOPMENT-FINANCE-INSTITUTION-FINANCED ACTIVITIES BY FILING COMPLAINTS TO THE INDEPENDENT ACCOUNTABILITY MECHANISMS. Not a guide to filing — the filing itself. This file holds several entries explaining how these mechanisms work; this is an organisation that will draft and lodge the complaint, which is the step where most communities stop. THE COMPLAINT-TOOLS WEBSITE IT PROVIDES: A WEBSITE PROVIDING INFORMATION AND TOOLS TO FILE COMPLAINTS AGAINST A COMPANY, BUSINESS OR MULTINATIONAL CORPORATION IN ORDER TO PREVENT, STOP AND SEEK JUSTICE FOR NEGATIVE IMPACTS CAUSED BY THEIR BUSINESS ACTIVITIES — WITH THE MECHANISMS COVERED INCLUDING THOSE OF AN AFRICAN DEVELOPMENT BANK. PREVENT and STOP, not only seek justice afterwards. The African bank's mechanism is covered on the same site as the corporate routes, so one page compares the option against your government's financier with the option against the company itself. THE HONEST FINDING ABOUT WHY THESE ROUTES GO UNUSED, WHICH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING HERE: RESEARCH CARRIED OUT WITH PARTNERS SHOWS THAT VICTIMS OF HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS ARE AFRAID TO SPEAK OUT AGAINST THOSE VIOLATIONS, AND EXPRESSED THAT THIS FEAR PREVENTED THEM FROM RAISING A COMPLAINT WITH INTERNATIONAL NON-JUDICIAL GRIEVANCE MECHANISMS. Every complaint route in this file assumes somebody is willing to be named. Researchers asked why they were not being used and the answer was fear, not ignorance — which means the first question before any filing is who will be exposed, and whether the mechanism accepts a complaint lodged by an organisation on the community's behalf. That is exactly what this centre does. THE AFRICAN CASE IT RECORDS: ALSO IN LIBERIA, IT WAS OBSERVED THAT THE COMMUNITIES THAT EXPRESSED COMPLAINTS OR GRIEVANCES TO A NAMED STEEL MULTINATIONAL RECEIVED THREATS FROM BOTH THE COMPANY AND FROM LOCAL OFFICIALS. FROM BOTH THE COMPANY AND FROM LOCAL OFFICIALS. The district administration and the concession holder responded together — which is why this file's defender-protection entries under Benin and Morocco belong in the plan before the complaint is lodged, not after. THE SERVICES IT OFFERS: CUSTOM-MADE SERVICES — RESEARCH, CONSULTING AND TRAINING — TO NON-PROFIT ORGANISATIONS AND THE PUBLIC SECTOR, AND STRENGTHENING COLLABORATION BETWEEN CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS THROUGH ITS WORLDWIDE NETWORK. CUSTOM-MADE RESEARCH for non-profits. A national organisation can commission the corporate investigation it cannot do itself — and this file's Benin entry covers a second organisation doing the same on request. HOW IT DESCRIBES ITS OWN PLACEMENT: COOPERATING WITH HUNDREDS OF ORGANISATIONS AROUND THE WORLD, IT ENSURES THAT ITS RESEARCH LANDS WHERE IT HAS THE MOST IMPACT — FROM COMMUNITIES AND COURTROOMS TO THE DESKS OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, MEDIA, AND POLITICIANS.
