COURTROOMS listed second. Research produced to evidentiary standard is a different product from a campaign report, and worth specifying when commissioning. THE NETWORKS IT HOSTS: DOZENS OF THEMATIC GLOBAL NETWORKS, AND IT HOSTS SEVERAL — INCLUDING A GOOD ELECTRONICS NETWORK, A RESPONSIBLE BUSINESS PLATFORM, AN OECD WATCH, AND A TAX JUSTICE NETWORK. AN OECD WATCH hosted here. That is the network monitoring the national contact points filed under Chad — so the same address reaches both the route and its watchdog. THE SECTORS IT RESEARCHES: ELECTRONICS, ENERGY AND WATER, MINERALS, AGRICULTURE AND FOOD, CLOTHING, PHARMACEUTICALS AND FINANCIAL SECTORS — AND ON CORPORATE ACCOUNTABILITY IT TRACKS SUPPLY CHAINS, TAX AVOIDANCE, LEGAL LOOPHOLES AND ABUSES OF CORPORATE POWER. ENERGY AND WATER as a named sector. Water concessions and utility privatisations rarely get corporate-research attention, and a community fighting one has few places to ask. THE ADVOCACY SUPPORT IT NAMES: SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES, UNIONS AND NGOs IN STRATEGIC CAMPAIGNS FOR JUSTICE AND REGULATION. THE LETTERBOX PRECEDENT ON RECORD, WHICH IS THE TACTICAL FIND: A NATIONAL CONTACT POINT ACCEPTED A COMPLAINT FILED BY INDIGENOUS GROUPS AGAINST AN OIL MULTINATIONAL — THE FIRST TIME A COMPLAINT AGAINST A LETTERBOX COMPANY HAD BEEN DECLARED ADMISSIBLE. A LETTERBOX COMPANY — a shell with an address and no operations, used to hold a concession at one remove from the parent. Communities are told repeatedly that the entity on their land has no reachable owner. That defence has now failed once, on the record, in a case brought by indigenous groups. THE REGULATORY STRATEGY IT PUBLISHES: PROMOTING BINDING LEGISLATION AND SELECTIVELY SUPPORTING POWERFUL SOFT LAW STANDARDS THAT CAN PAVE THE WAY FOR HARD RULES; ALIGNING CLOSELY WITH PARTNERS TO ADVANCE MORE ROBUST REGULATIONS OR ENFORCEMENT; SUPPORTING STRONG MANDATORY HUMAN RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL DUE DILIGENCE AT NATIONAL AND EUROPEAN LEVELS; AND STRENGTHENING AND STRATEGICALLY USING THE OECD GUIDELINES. MANDATORY DUE DILIGENCE laws in Europe require companies to check their supply chains for harm. When those laws bite, the evidence they need is exactly what an African community already holds — and knowing which organisations feed that machine is how your case gets into it. AND THE CRITIQUE IT RECORDS OF THE FINANCE SIDE: NGOs CRITICIZED A FINANCE CORPORATION'S POOR RECORD IN SANCTIONING COMPANIES IT FINANCES FOR NON-COMPLIANCE WITH ITS STANDARDS IN CONFLICT-AFFECTED AND FRAGILE ENVIRONMENTS. Standards that are not enforced against the financed company. Filed honestly: expect the mechanism to find in your favour and the money to keep flowing, and plan the campaign accordingly. WHO IT SUITS: African communities and national organisations facing a multinational or a financed project, particularly where naming individual complainants would be dangerous. CAVEATS: AMSTERDAM-BASED AND WORKING THROUGH PARTNERS RATHER THAN INTAKE, AND ITS OWN RESEARCH SHOWS THESE MECHANISMS OFTEN FAIL — pair with legal and protection support. For the national contact points, Chad's entry; for what such complaints have actually achieved, Burundi's entry; for research done on request, Benin's entry.

trackers.name: An African conservation NGO that incubates emerging non-profit organisations, publishes a named officer's direct email, and asks anyone with a specific project to write in — plus community training that has ended in paid internships
trackers.desc: THEY INCUBATE NEW NON-PROFITS, AND THEY PUBLISH AN EMAIL ADDRESS — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S TOGO ENTRY COVERS THE 12-COUNTRY CONSERVATION IMPLEMENTER, ITS SEYCHELLES ENTRY THE TAX DEDUCTION, ITS SÃO TOMÉ ENTRY THE SERVITUDE TRUST, ITS SOUTH SUDAN ENTRY THE LAND BUYER, ITS CHAD ENTRY THE TRUST-FUND LIBRARY. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE INCUBATION LINE, WHICH IS THE FIND: AMONG THE THINGS IT DOES — ALONGSIDE LANDSCAPE WILDERNESS MANAGEMENT, DEVELOPING YOUNG LEADERS FROM DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES, DIRECT ACTION ANTI-POACHING AND ADVOCACY AT A GOVERNMENT LEVEL — IS THE INCUBATION OF EMERGING NON-PROFIT ORGANISATIONS. Incubating new organisations, stated as ordinary work. This file has recorded registration, governance and a bank account as the gate that keeps community groups out of every fund in it — and has repeatedly had to advise finding a fiscal sponsor. An established body that will host and grow a new organisation is the direct answer, and almost nothing else here offers it. THE OPEN DOOR, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IF THERE IS A SPECIFIC PROJECT THAT YOU WOULD LIKE TO GET INVOLVED IN, PLEASE SEND US A MESSAGE AND WE WILL GET IN TOUCH WITH YOU TO DISCUSS ALL THE OPTIONS. An invitation to write in about a specific project, published on their own site. Write with the project, not with a request for support in general — that is the shape they asked for. THE NAMED CONTACT: A CHIEF OPERATIONS OFFICER FOR CONSERVATION IS NAMED WITH A DIRECT EMAIL ADDRESS AGAINST THE SPECIES PROGRAMME. A named senior officer with a working email, not a contact form. That is the difference between a message that reaches a person and one that reaches an inbox nobody owns. THE TRAINING THAT ENDED IN PAID WORK, WITH ITS NUMBERS: AN EMPLOYABILITY, WELLNESS AND LEADERSHIP TRAINING COURSE, FUNDED BY A NAMED COMMUNITY CONSERVATION FUND, INCLUDED YOUTH FROM COMMUNITIES AROUND A NAMED WILDLIFE RESERVE — 20 GRADUATES COMPLETED THE TRAINING, AND TWO NAMED GRADUATES EARNED PAID INTERNSHIPS AT THAT RESERVE THANKS TO A NAMED CONSERVATION FUND. Twenty trained, two into paid work, reported honestly with the names of the funders who paid for each part. That ratio is worth knowing before a community invests its young people's time — and the funders named are themselves two more doors, since a course like this is arranged between an NGO and a fund rather than applied for. WHAT THE SOCIAL PROGRAMMES ARE FOR: IT IS ONE OF THE FEW CONSERVATION NGOs IN ITS COUNTRY CURRENTLY INVOLVED IN ACTIVE, SUSTAINABLE SOCIAL INTERVENTION PROGRAMMES — THROUGH WHICH YOUNG PEOPLE ARE EMPOWERED TO BECOME FINANCIALLY INDEPENDENT ENTREPRENEURS AND BREADWINNERS FOR THEIR FAMILIES. THE FLAGSHIP-SPECIES METHOD IT PUBLISHES: A PROGRAMME USES ICONIC WILDLIFE SPECIES AS FLAGSHIPS TO DRAW ATTENTION TO CHALLENGES FACING CONSERVATION AND WILDERNESS AREAS — INTERVENTIONS DIRECTED TOWARDS THESE SPECIES RESULT IN THE PROTECTION OF LANDSCAPES AND THE ASSOCIATED WILDLIFE, AND THE PROMOTION OF BENEFICIATION TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES. The method stated plainly: pick the animal that attracts money and attention, and the landscape is protected behind it. A community whose land holds a well-known species has a lever that a community with only rare plants does not — which is worth knowing when deciding how to frame an appeal, and worth naming as the reason obscure ecosystems go unfunded. WHAT A SPECIES INITIATIVE CONTAINS IN PRACTICE: THE ESTABLISHMENT OF NEW POPULATIONS IN SUITABLE HABITAT, LAW ENFORCEMENT SUPPORT, AND DEMAND REDUCTION WORK IN THE CONSUMER COUNTRY — WITH A CAMPAIGN USING LOCALLY GENERATED INFORMATIVE MATERIAL, SOCIAL MEDIA, EVENTS, SEMINARS, PRESENTATIONS, COMPETITIONS AND FIRST-HAND WILDLIFE EXPERIENCES TO WORK ALONGSIDE YOUTH IN THAT COUNTRY. DEMAND REDUCTION IN THE CONSUMER COUNTRY. Work aimed at the buyers thousands of kilometres away, run alongside the field work — the same logic as the investment-chain entries elsewhere in this file. WHAT IT SAYS IT DOES OVERALL: IT PROTECTS AND SUSTAINS LANDSCAPES THROUGH AN AGILE AND INNOVATIVE APPROACH, INTEGRATING SPECIES, SPACES AND PEOPLE — INCLUDING BUILDING CLIMATE RESILIENCE. THE RECURRING-DONATION AND BANKING DETAIL IT PUBLISHES: FULL BANK ACCOUNT DETAILS INCLUDING BRANCH CODE, ACCOUNT NUMBER AND SWIFT CODE, AN INSTANT MOBILE DONATION APP OPTION WITH INSTALLATION GUIDANCE, AND MONTHLY, QUARTERLY OR ANNUAL RECURRING CONTRIBUTIONS. Recorded because it is a template rather than a service: publishing full banking details, a mobile app route and a recurring option is how a small African organisation makes itself payable from anywhere. Most community organisations in this file cannot receive money even when someone wants to send it. ITS AGE AND STANDING: OVER 45 YEARS OF RESULTS AND A FIFTY-YEAR EXPERIENCE, WITH THE WORK RECEIVING A NAMED INTERNATIONAL AWARD FOR ENTERPRISE IN 2008, AND A LEADERSHIP HANDOVER IN 2000 FROM ITS FOUNDING FIGURE. THE ALLIANCE IT CO-FOUNDED: IN 2015 IT CO-FOUNDED AN INTERNATIONAL ALLIANCE OF ACTION-ORIENTED ORGANISATIONS WHO UNDERSTAND THAT WILDERNESS AREAS HAVE LOCAL MEANING AND GLOBAL SIGNIFICANCE — WHOSE FOUNDING MEMBERS ARE THIS FOUNDATION AND TWO NAMED NORTHERN ORGANISATIONS, WITH A LEADERSHIP SCHOOL FOUNDED IN 1957 AS A PATRON PARTNER. An African organisation as a founding member of a northern alliance rather than a grantee of one. Worth noting as the structure to ask for when an international body proposes a partnership. AND THE POLICY BODY IN THAT ALLIANCE: A WILDERNESS SPECIALIST GROUP OF A WORLD COMMISSION ON PROTECTED AREAS WHICH ASSURES GLOBAL WILDERNESS POLICY AND LEGISLATION THAT SAFEGUARDS THE IRREPLACEABLE LIFE SUPPORT SERVICES OF WILD NATURE AND PROVIDES DIRECT CULTURAL AND SOCIAL BENEFITS TO HUMAN COMMUNITIES. A specialist group inside the body that sets protected-area standards internationally. Where a designation is being drafted over your land, that is where the definitions are argued. WHO IT SUITS: African community groups that need to become an organisation, and southern African communities near reserves seeking training, work or a landscape partner. CAVEATS: SOUTH AFRICA-BASED WITH ITS FIELD WORK CONCENTRATED THERE; IT IS A CONSERVATION IMPLEMENTER RATHER THAN A FUNDER OR A LAW FIRM, AND ITS SPECIES PROGRAMMES INCLUDE ANTI-POACHING LAW ENFORCEMENT SUPPORT, WHICH SOME COMMUNITIES WILL WEIGH CAREFULLY. For the 12-country implementer with free assessment tools, Togo's entry; for the fund that has bought land, Eswatini's entry.

trackers.name: An encrypted reporting app with automatic GPS, built with communities facing illegal logging — plus an investigation dashboard and a storytelling tool, designed around low literacy, weak networks and surveillance, with credentials issued on request by email
trackers.desc: AN ENCRYPTED APP THAT STAMPS THE GPS ON YOUR EVIDENCE — method and adjacency declared first: A NATIONAL CIVIL SOCIETY LAND COALITION WAS CHECKED FIRST THIS ROUND AND FOUND ALREADY FILED UNDER GHANA BY NAME AND BY FACT, SO IT WAS NOT DUPLICATED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS THE FULL NAME AND DESCRIPTION TEXT OF ALL 53 BUCKETS; THE SHIPPED HOST AND FIVE FACTS ARE ABSENT, AND ONE GENERIC PHRASE MATCHED ONE ENTRY, READ IN FULL AND A DIFFERENT SUBJECT. THIS FILE'S GAMBIA ENTRY COVERS THE FREE GUIDES ON FILMING SO FOOTAGE STANDS AS EVIDENCE AND ITS SIERRA LEONE ENTRY THE SCHOOL THAT TRAINS RESIDENTS TO DOCUMENT A MINE. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHAT THE APP RECORDS AND HOW IT PROTECTS IT, WHICH IS THE FIND: GPS AUTOMATICALLY RECORDS LOCATION; RECORD VIDEO, AUDIO OR TAKE PHOTOS; END-TO-END ENCRYPTION; AUTOMATIC LOGOUT AFTER 5 MINUTES; COMPATIBILITY WITH A TOR PROJECT PROXY; A RECORD OF ALL REPORTS KEPT IN THE APP; AND EXPORT OF AN ENCRYPTED ZIP FILE TO SD CARD — WITH BUILT-IN VIDEO TUTORIALS. Every funder, court, complaints desk and petition in this file assumes the community arrives with a dated, located, credible record. This is the instrument that makes one. AUTOMATIC LOGOUT AFTER 5 MINUTES and TOR COMPATIBILITY are the details that matter where phones get taken at roadblocks — and EXPORT TO SD CARD means the evidence survives the phone being confiscated. THE THREE TOOLS AND WHAT EACH IS FOR, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: A REPORTING APP FOR SIMPLE, SECURE AND SYSTEMATIC REPORTING FROM THE FRONTLINE; AN INVESTIGATION DASHBOARD TO FIND CONNECTIONS BETWEEN EVENTS AND INDIVIDUALS OVER SPACE AND TIME; AND A STORYTELLING TOOL TO SHARE EMBEDDABLE MULTIMEDIA NARRATIVES. The dashboard is the part communities rarely have: fifty separate incidents become one pattern across space and time, which is what turns a list of complaints into an argument a regulator or a court can act on. This file's Sierra Leone entry records monitors concluding that reporting alone changed nothing — the dashboard is the answer to that. HOW TO GET IT: IT IS A CLOSED APPLICATION — TO GET CREDENTIALS THAT ALLOW YOU TO USE THE APP, GET IN TOUCH VIA A PUBLISHED EMAIL ADDRESS. Closed by design rather than by gatekeeping: an open reporting app is an open target. One email gets an organisation credentialed, and that is the whole application process. WHERE IT CAME FROM AND WHO BUILT IT: FIRST DEVELOPED TO TARGET ILLEGAL LOGGING IN ONE WEST AFRICAN COUNTRY, FOUNDED BY A FILMMAKER AS A RESULT OF WORK WITH A TEAM OF ACTIVISTS FROM A NAMED NATIONAL INSTITUTE — APPLYING THE KNOWLEDGE OF JOURNALISTS, SCIENTISTS, TECHNOLOGISTS, DESIGNERS AND SECURITY EXPERTS. WHAT IT WAS DESIGNED AROUND, WHICH IS UNUSUAL: THE TEAM STARTED FROM SQUARE ONE, BUILDING THE SYSTEM TO WITHSTAND THE DIFFICULTIES OF RUNNING A TECHNOLOGY PROJECT IN THE REGION — TAKING INTO ACCOUNT INFRASTRUCTURE AND NETWORK CHALLENGES, AS WELL AS LIMITATIONS IN LITERACY AND SECURITY CONCERNS; THE SYSTEM WAS DESIGNED TO FIT THE NEEDS OF A GIVEN COMMUNITY. LITERACY named as a design constraint alongside network and security. Most reporting tools in this file assume a user who can read a form in English; this one was rebuilt from nothing because that assumption failed. THE TIMING ARGUMENT: REAL-TIME REPORTING MEANS USERS CAN PREVENT ILLEGAL LOGGING BEFORE THE FIRST TREE IS FELLED — WITH THE AIM OF DELIVERING ACTIONABLE REPORTS THAT TRIGGER ACTION FROM GOVERNMENT AND POLICYMAKERS. BEFORE THE FIRST TREE IS FELLED. Read beside the development bank's complaint desk filed under Morocco, which accepts complaints while a project is still under preparation: the two together are a route to stopping something rather than documenting its aftermath. WHAT IT WAS FUNDED TO ACHIEVE: A SECURE AND EFFECTIVE MECHANISM FOR EVIDENCE-BASED REPORTING OF ENVIRONMENTAL CRIMES — ENABLING CITIZENS TO HOLD BUSINESSES AND GOVERNMENT TO ACCOUNT AND ENSURE COMMUNITIES' VOICES ARE CENTRAL TO DIALOGUES ON WHAT HAPPENS TO THE COUNTRY'S LAND AND RESOURCES. THE SECURITY BENEFIT ITS USERS REPORTED, IN THEIR OWN WORDS: IT HAS HELPED WITH OUR SECURITY. Users found the tool made them safer, not more exposed — which is the opposite of what documenting a powerful operation usually costs, and worth weighing against the risks this file records elsewhere. WHAT THE TEAM SAID IT STILL WANTED: TO FIGURE OUT HOW TO MAKE THESE TECHNOLOGIES SAFER, MORE ACCESSIBLE, SCALABLE AND FREE — INTENT ON INTEGRATING REPORTING SYSTEMS INTO MAINSTREAM MEDIA, LOCAL AND NATIONAL GOVERNANCE AND JUSTICE SYSTEMS, AND ENSURING THERE ARE FEEDBACK MECHANISMS TO COMMUNITIES THAT LACK EVEN BASIC PHONE NETWORK. FEEDBACK TO COMMUNITIES THAT LACK EVEN BASIC PHONE NETWORK is the honest limit stated by the builders themselves: a village with no signal can still be reported ABOUT but struggles to be told what happened next. Plan a physical route back — a printed summary carried to the meeting. WHO USES IT AND WHERE: USED EXTENSIVELY IN AFRICA AND SOUTHEAST ASIA, PARTICULARLY BY CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS BUT ALSO SOME INDIGENOUS GROUPS — AND CUSTOMISED FOR ISSUES BEYOND FORESTS, INCLUDING ENVIRONMENTAL CONSERVATION IN ONE SOUTH AMERICAN COUNTRY AND WOMEN'S HEALTH IN ONE EAST AFRICAN COUNTRY. Not a forestry tool. The same suite has been reconfigured for health reporting, which means a community can use it for evictions, pollution, water levels or violence without waiting for a purpose-built version. THE PROJECT THAT SCALED IT AND THE TRAINING BEHIND IT: A PRIZE-WINNING NATIONAL ACTIVIST USING IT TO MONITOR ILLEGAL LOGGING AND DESTRUCTIVE OIL PALM PLANTATION EXPANSION, WITH HIS WORK TO TRAIN LOCAL COMMUNITIES TO USE THE APP SUPPORTED BY A PRIZE GRANT PROGRAMME AND A NAMED FOUNDATION — THE PROJECT STILL EXPANDING TWO YEARS AFTER ITS ORIGINAL FUNDING ENDED. Still growing two years after the grant stopped, which this file has recorded as the rare exception rather than the rule. The training was the thing that lasted, not the funding. AND THE SEPARATE NATIONAL TOOL PUBLISHED ALONGSIDE IT: A FREE MOBILE APP IN ANOTHER WEST AFRICAN COUNTRY DESIGNED TO COMBAT ILLEGAL MINING, LETTING ANYONE REPORT INCIDENTS BY PROVIDING LOCATION COORDINATES, UPLOADING PHOTOS AND ADDING COMMENTS — WITH INCIDENTS STORED ON A SERVER AND VIEWABLE ON A MAP, AND AN OPTION TO REPORT ANONYMOUSLY; ITS PUBLISHED PRIVACY NOTICE STATES THAT CONTACT INFO AND IDENTIFIERS MAY BE COLLECTED AND LINKED TO YOUR IDENTITY. Recorded together deliberately, because the contrast is the lesson: a free open app that offers anonymous reporting while its own privacy notice says identifiers may be linked to you. Read the privacy notice of any reporting app before a community uses it — the promise on the download page and the disclosure in the store listing can say different things. WHO IT SUITS: community organisations documenting logging, mining, eviction or pollution who need evidence that is located, dated, encrypted and defensible — and anyone weighing which reporting app is safe to use. CAVEATS: A TOOL AND ITS MAKERS, NOT A FUNDER, A LAWYER OR AN ORGANISER; ACCESS IS BY CREDENTIAL ON REQUEST RATHER THAN OPEN DOWNLOAD, IT NEEDS SMARTPHONES AND SOME NETWORK, AND ITS BUILDERS NAME FEEDBACK TO OFF-NETWORK COMMUNITIES AS AN UNSOLVED PROBLEM. For the free guides on filming so footage stands as evidence, Gambia's entry; for training residents to monitor a mine, Sierra Leone's entry.

trackers.name: The Kitengela Wildlife Conservation Lease, Kenya — run by FoNNaP then The Wildlife Foundation, paying landowners about US$4 per acre a year to keep land unfenced and unsold; with IFAW's US$1.2m/year Kitenden lease alongside it
trackers.desc: FOUR DOLLARS AN ACRE TO KEEP IT OPEN — AND WHAT THAT BOUGHT — method and adjacency declared first: FOURTH ACQUISITION-ONLY ROUND, AND THE FIRST COVERING THE ROUTE WHERE NO LAND CHANGES HANDS. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL HOSTS AND FOUR FACTS ABSENT. TWO GENERIC PHRASES MATCHED TWO ENTRIES, BOTH READ IN FULL: A SIERRA LEONEAN STATUTE PAGE, AND A KENYAN UMBRELLA MEMBERSHIP BODY WHICH MENTIONS A LEASING INCOME MODEL IN A SINGLE LINE WITHOUT ITS PRICE, CONTRACT TERMS OR OUTCOME. THIS ENTRY IS THE LEASE PROGRAMME ITSELF; NEITHER IS RESTATED AND NEITHER HOST IS SHIPPED. THIS FILE'S TANZANIA BUCKET CARRIES A VOLUNTARY LAND EASEMENT ENTRY AND ITS LESOTHO ENTRY THE CARBON ROUTE WHERE COMMUNITY LAND STAYS IN TITLE. THE PRICE AND WHAT IT BUYS, WHICH IS THE FIND: LANDOWNERS WERE PAID KSh 300 PER ACRE PER YEAR, ROUGHLY US$4, IN RETURN FOR AGREEING TO LEAVE THEIR LAND OPEN AND NOT ENGAGE IN QUARRYING, FENCING, LAND SUBDIVISION AND SALE OR POACHING — WITH THE AVERAGE ANNUAL PAYMENT AROUND US$400 TO US$800 PER HOUSEHOLD. The three acquisition rounds before this one were about getting land into community hands. This is the opposite arrangement and often the only one available: the household keeps its title and is paid not to develop. Four dollars an acre is the number to start any such negotiation from — it is what was actually paid, not what was asked. THE FOUR RESTRICTIONS, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: QUARRYING, FENCING, SUBDIVISION AND SALE, AND POACHING — THE CONTRACT NAMING SUBDIVISION AND SALE ALONGSIDE THE PHYSICAL USES. SUBDIVISION AND SALE inside the same clause as quarrying is the operative part. A payment that only stops fencing leaves the owner free to sell to a developer next year; this one buys the parcel's continuity, which is what a community trying to hold a corridor together actually needs. Copy those four words into any such agreement. THE PAYMENT TIMING: PAYMENTS ARE SCHEDULED SEVERAL TIMES PER YEAR TO COINCIDE WITH SCHOOL PAYMENT TIME — WITH PARTICIPANTS REPORTED AS SENDING THEIR CHILDREN TO SCHOOL, INCLUDING SECONDARY SCHOOL. Paid when school fees fall due. A small design choice that decides whether a household stays enrolled, because the alternative to the lease payment is selling an acre in the same week. HOW SMALL IT STARTED AND HOW FAR IT GOT: BEGUN AS A PILOT IN 2000 LEASING SEVERAL HUNDRED ACRES FROM 11 PARTICIPANTS, WITH ONE IMPLEMENTER STATING IT STARTED WITH 214 ACRES AND 2 FAMILIES — EXPANDING TO 8,545 ACRES FROM 117 FAMILIES BY LATE 2003, THEN 417 FAMILIES AND 60,000 ACRES, WITH AN EVALUATION TABLE REPORTING 61,067 ACRES BY 2012; 115 HOUSEHOLDS WERE ON A WAITING LIST. Two families to sixty thousand acres. And a waiting list is the detail worth carrying to a funder: demand from landowners outran the money, which is the opposite of the usual problem. WHO RAN IT AND WHO PAID: INITIATED BY A LOCAL CONSERVATION NGO OF PARK SUPPORTERS WITH SUPPORT FROM A US WILDLIFE TRUST, THE FIRST PHASE FUNDED BY A DEVELOPMENT BANK'S GLOBAL ENVIRONMENT FACILITY, THE SECOND IMPLEMENTED BY A NATIONAL WILDLIFE FOUNDATION — WITH THE STATE WILDLIFE SERVICE PAYING AN ANNUAL KSh 900,000, ABOUT US$13,235, AND US$64,000 OVER FIVE YEARS. A local volunteer association started it and the state and the development bank followed. The sequence matters: nobody funded the idea until a small group had proved it on 214 acres. WHO ACTUALLY HELD THE POWER, STATED PLAINLY: THE MOST IMPORTANT ACTORS ON THE GROUND WERE THE PASTORALIST LANDOWNERS, BECAUSE THEY CONTROLLED THE ACTUAL DISPERSAL LAND — THE ENTIRE PROGRAMME DEPENDED ON THEIR WILLINGNESS TO ACCEPT PAYMENTS AND MAINTAIN OPEN RANGELAND USE ON PRIVATE LAND. Worth quoting back at any conservation body arriving with a plan: the people with the title are the ones who decide, and the scheme exists at their discretion. THE MAPPING THAT MADE IT WORK, DONE WITH THE LANDOWNERS' OWN ASSOCIATION: SUCCESS DEPENDED ON SPATIAL INFORMATION ABOUT WHERE FENCES HAD BEEN PUT UP AND WHERE LAND REMAINED UNFENCED — THE MAPS DEVELOPED TOGETHER BY MEMBERS OF THE KITENGELA ILPARAKUO LANDOWNERS ASSOCIATION (KILA) AND SCIENTISTS AT ILRI, SHOWING PARCELS ALREADY ENROLLED AND THOSE ON THE WAITING LIST, AND USED TO TARGET PRIORITY AREAS AND ATTRACT MORE FUNDING. A fence map, made by the landowners with researchers, that then attracted the money. Read beside the resident drone-mapping filed under Somalia: in both cases the community's own map was the asset that unlocked everything after it. THE GAP BETWEEN WHAT WAS PAID AND WHAT WAS ASKED: A SURVEY FOUND THE AVERAGE ANNUAL COMPENSATION DEMANDED PER HOUSEHOLD WAS KSh 60,022, ROUGHLY US$920, PER ACRE — AGAINST THE KSh 300 PER ACRE ACTUALLY PAID, WITH THE RANGE OF RESPONSES SO LARGE THAT THE VALUATION METHODOLOGY WAS DEEMED QUESTIONABLE. Landowners named a figure roughly two hundred times what they were eventually paid. Recorded because it is the honest measure of what these payments are: not compensation for the land's value, but a small annual sum against the temptation to sell. A community should go in knowing that. WHAT THE PROGRAMME WAS RACING: THE FIRST GROUP RANCH WAS SUBDIVIDED IN 1986 INTO PRIVATE PARCELS AVERAGING 255 ACRES, DECLINING TO 154 ACRES MAINLY AS A RESULT OF LAND SALES. Average holdings fell by 40% through sales. Subdivision converts collective land into parcels that leave one by one, and this file has recorded the same sequence in several countries. THE OUTCOME, RECORDED WITHOUT SOFTENING: THE CORE PERIOD RAN FROM 2002 AND EXPANDED AFTER 2008 — AND OVER THE SAME DECADES WILDEBEEST IN THE ECOSYSTEM DECLINED FROM 38,000 IN 1978 TO ABOUT 10,000 BY 2012, WITH ANOTHER ACCOUNT RECORDING A FALL FROM 30,000 TO 8,000 IN TWENTY YEARS. Sixty thousand acres enrolled and the population still collapsed. Filed unsoftened because a community weighing this route deserves it: the lease held some land open, and it did not on its own reverse what was happening around it. THE LARGER LEASE ON RECORD ALONGSIDE IT: A FIVE-YEAR AGREEMENT PRESENTED TO ROUGHLY 9,000 LANDOWNERS AT AN ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING, WITH AROUND 1,600 SIGNING UP AND ANOTHER THOUSAND ON RENEWAL, SECURING 26,000 ACRES AND LATER OVER 55,000 — A US$1.2 MILLION PER YEAR AGREEMENT INCLUDING SCHOLARSHIPS, A MANAGEMENT PLAN, LIVELIHOOD PROJECTS FOR WOMEN, AND EMPLOYMENT FOR COMMUNITY GAME SCOUTS INCLUDING ONE OF THE FIRST ALL-WOMEN COMMUNITY RANGER UNITS, WITH A BANK DRIVEN INTO THE VILLAGES TO OPEN ACCOUNTS. The contrast is the lesson: the same instrument at $1.2 million a year carried scholarships, jobs and a management plan. Ask for the package, not the per-acre rate alone — and note that only 1,600 of 9,000 landowners signed initially, so a lease presented at a general meeting does not need unanimity to start. AND THE PUBLISHED WARNING ABOUT WHO BENEFITS: THE SUBDIVISION OF THESE RANGELANDS HAS TENDED TO BENEFIT ELITES, AND THIS TREND IS REINFORCED IN LAND-BASED SCHEMES SUCH AS THESE — LAND LEASES DO HOWEVER KEEP THE LANDS THEY COVER TOGETHER; BUT CONSIDERATION MUST BE GIVEN TO ADJACENT COMMUNITIES THAT MAY FACE NEGATIVE KNOCK-ON EFFECTS, AND LEASES MAY NOT OFFER AS MUCH TO LANDOWNERS IN OTHER AREAS OR BE FINANCIALLY SUSTAINABLE ACROSS VAST AREAS. Payments flow to whoever holds title, so where subdivision already favoured the well-connected, the lease pays them again. And the displaced pressure lands on the neighbouring community. Both belong in the discussion before a village signs. WHO IT SUITS: landowning communities asked to keep land open rather than sell it, and anyone negotiating a payment-for-conservation agreement who needs real prices, real contract terms and a real failure on record. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY AND ONE ECOSYSTEM, WITH FIGURES SPANNING 2000–2012 AND VARYING BETWEEN SOURCES — THESE ARE PRECEDENTS AND NUMBERS TO NEGOTIATE FROM, NOT AN OPEN PROGRAMME TO JOIN; PAYMENT DEPENDS ON DONOR FUNDING THAT WAS NEVER PERMANENT. For a body a village organisation can actually join, Kenya's entry; for a voluntary easement with the village keeping the land, Tanzania's entry.

trackers.name: Judiciary of The Republic of The Gambia
trackers.desc: Judiciary of The Republic of The Gambia — supreme court (Gambia).

trackers.name: The Gambia — Companies Department (Registrar of Companies, MoJ)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the Registrar of Companies (Attorney General’s Chambers & Ministry of Justice) administers the Companies Registry under the Companies Act 2013 & Single Window Business Registry Act, The Gambia. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: National Audit Office
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of The Gambia. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Gambia.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: ECOWAS Court of Justice — file directly, but sue the State
trackers.desc: A COURT YOU CAN REACH WITHOUT EXHAUSTING DOMESTIC REMEDIES. The ECOWAS Community Court of Justice has held human rights jurisdiction since 2005 and has broad access and standing rules permitting individuals and NGOs to bypass national courts and file directly. THE PRECEDENT: in SERAP v Federal Republic of Nigeria (ECW/CCJ/APP/08/09) the Court dismissed all three preliminary objections — no locus standi, no jurisdiction, statute-barred — and rejected the government's attempt to exclude an Amnesty International report from the evidence. NGO research was admitted as evidence, which matters when no state data exists. It found violations of articles 1 and 24 of the African Charter — article 24: ‘all peoples shall have the right to a general satisfactory environment favourable to their development’ — and of article 21, the right to natural wealth and resources. THE FAULT WAS AN OMISSION: the state ‘defaulted in its duties in terms of vigilance and diligence’, and ‘the omission to act and to prevent damage to the environment characterises the violation’. It ordered restoration within the shortest possible time and measures to prevent further damage, citing the ICJ that the environment ‘is not an abstraction but represents the living space, the quality of life and the very health of human beings, including generations unborn’. THE LIMIT THAT DECIDES WHO YOU SUE: the Court held it had no jurisdiction over the private oil corporations, which were struck from the suit. You sue the State for failing to regulate; you cannot sue the company here — naming one as respondent loses that part of the case. AND PLAN FOR ENFORCEMENT: commentary records the Court did not identify a means for Nigeria to implement the ruling, and the ICJ later wrote to the President pressing for enforcement — judgment is the start of an enforcement campaign, not a self-executing remedy. Proposals to require exhaustion of domestic remedies were rejected by ECOWAS experts and Heads of Government, so the direct-access rule has been tested and held.

trackers.name: Department of Forestry — and 66 parks demarcated since the 1950s
trackers.desc: A DOCUMENTARY STARTING POINT MOST COUNTRIES IN THIS MAP CANNOT OFFER. Between 1950 and 1954 a forestry adviser identified and demarcated 66 forest parks for conservation and production — timber, bamboo and rhun palms — so if your site is one of them, the demarcation record exists. The colonial administration's own conclusion that total protection for all the parks was impractical is the origin of the participatory turn that followed. The Department's operational mandate rests on the Forest Regulation of 1978, with the Forest Act 1998 and Regulations legally requiring communities to participate in fire prevention and participative forest management — note that participation is a legal requirement on communities, not only an entitlement, which cuts both ways before an approach. The Department works to the Gambian Forest Management Concept, developed with the Gambian-German Forest Project since 1980. Current policy: the National Forest Policy 2023–2032. The parent ministry is the Ministry of Environment, Climate Change and Natural Resources.

trackers.name: Community Forest Committee — the state transfers ownership, after probation
trackers.desc: THE GAMBIA TRANSFERS OWNERSHIP, NOT A CONCESSION — and that is rare enough to cite across borders. The community forestry concept foresees an ownership transfer of forest land from the State to an interested community: not a management agreement, not a use right. COMPARE WHAT THIS MAP RECORDS ELSEWHERE: Cambodia's community protected areas give management rights but not exclusion rights; Burkina Faso's GGF is a concession; Guinea classifies forest ‘to the benefit of’ a collectivity. Where a neighbouring community is negotiating a concession, The Gambia is the comparator. The Gambia is recorded as one of the first countries in Africa to introduce community forestry nationwide, the concept being the flagship of the 1995 Forest Policy and the 1998 Forest Bill. THE ROUTE RUNS THROUGH A COMMITTEE YOU FORM AND ELECT: communities establish Community Forest Committees or Village Development Committees whose members are elected by the local population, trained by implementing partners and then responsible for planning, coordinating and managing delivery — including natural resource-based income-generating activities. THE STEP MOST APPLICANTS UNDERESTIMATE: the community must go through a training and probation period, which is then evaluated, with the final aim being reservation of the forestland as a gazetted Community Forest. Plan for probation and assessment, not an application — the gazettal comes at the end, not the beginning. The programme also provides literacy and basic skills, civic and health education, so the route carries adult education with it rather than assuming it.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: NEA Inspectorate — 26 inspectors for the whole country, and every enforcement notice on record fell inside Greater Banjul
trackers.desc: WHERE A POLLUTION REPORT GOES, AND HOW FAR THE AGENCY CAN ACTUALLY REACH. The Inspectorate of the National Environment Agency enforces ten instruments, including the National Environmental Management Act 1994, the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations 2014, the Environmental Discharge (Permitting) Regulations 1999 and the Environmental Quality Standards Regulations 1999. Its first response is administrative, not judicial: an Improvement Notice or a Demand for Compliance, with litigation held back as a last resort. As at 4 January 2022 it had served 121 such notices, all of them within the Greater Banjul Area, against a national inspectorate of 26 people — one acting principal inspector, nine senior inspectors and sixteen inspectors. Up-country, the absence of a notice against a site is not evidence that the site is clean; it is more likely evidence that no inspector has been there. The page names the unit and its statutory basis but gives no complaint form, no email address and no service standard for responding to a report, so a written complaint to the Agency's head office in Kanifing, copied to the relevant regional office, is the route that exists rather than the route that is advertised.

trackers.name: NEA environmental assessment programme — the Class A / B / C screening decision is the one worth contesting early
trackers.desc: THE SCREENING CLASS DECIDES HOW MUCH SCRUTINY A PROJECT EVER RECEIVES, AND IT IS SET BEFORE ANY STUDY BEGINS. The Agency's own explainer describes three classes: Class A requires a mandatory assessment, Class B a limited one, and Class C none at all on the basis that the impacts are treated as negligible. A project placed in Class C generates no assessment document to comment on, which makes the classification, not the report, the thing to challenge. The explainer also names the lead-institution arrangement — for oil and gas the Public Utilities Regulatory Authority leads, with lands and survey, parks and wildlife, physical planning, water resources and the affected community brought in as stakeholders — so the body holding the file may not be the environment agency at all. Terminology note for searching the register: the Agency now writes ESIA rather than EIA, and older documents use the earlier term. This is a published programme description hosted on the Agency's own domain; it is not a procedure manual and it states no comment deadline, and no public register of screening decisions was located on the site.

trackers.name: NALA will advise you on a land case and will not represent you in one — and the same page carries the two bodies that can act
trackers.desc: CHECK THE CIVIL GATE BEFORE BUILDING A PLAN AROUND FREE COUNSEL. The Ministry of Justice's own description of the National Agency for Legal Aid states that it provides legal advice as well as legal representation in criminal matters in court, at police stations and in prisons. Advice is general; representation is criminal. A community facing an acquisition or a nuisance can therefore get an opinion from NALA but should not expect an advocate from it. Headquarters in Banjul with centres at Basse and Farafenni; the West Coast Region and Central River Region centres are described as still being established. Three telephone numbers are published and no email address, no means test and no application form. The same page lists the two bodies that can actually act on a land dispute without counsel: the Alternative Dispute Resolution Secretariat, headquartered at Fajara with pilot centres at Farafenni and Basse, which runs arbitration, conciliation and mediation as an alternative to the courts; and the National Human Rights Commission at Kotu, which holds the powers of the High Court at trial — to hear complaints, summon and examine witnesses on oath, and enforce its decisions, including measures to protect the life and safety of an individual. NALA maintains no website of its own; this is the State's canonical page for it, not a third party's description.

trackers.name: IHRDA, Banjul — pro bono counsel that takes community cases to the African regional courts, and publishes a case intake form
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Institute for Human Rights and Development in Africa, founded in Banjul in 1998 by two lawyers who had worked inside the Secretariat of the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights and concluded the regional system was profoundly underused. It provides pro bono legal counsel to victims of human rights violations, before national courts and before the African regional bodies — the African Commission, the African Court, the ECOWAS Community Court of Justice, the East African Court of Justice and the SADC Tribunal — and filed the first case ever brought before the African Commission. WHY IT BELONGS IN A MAP ABOUT LAND: the regional system is where African communities have won the landmark land rulings. The Endorois decision held that an indigenous community's rights to property, culture, religion, disposal of natural resources and development had been violated by their removal — a precedent any dispossessed community's lawyer should know exists. IHRDA maintains Africa's most comprehensive human rights case law database, free to search, which is where you find what has already been won. AND — UNUSUALLY IN THIS FILE — IT PUBLISHES A CASE INTAKE FORM: it says plainly that it is a small organisation with substantial work, that it prioritises cases with the potential to benefit wider communities and achieve systemic change, and that it provides legal expertise only and NOT financial or material assistance. It also runs country-specific litigation workshops to get civil society actors filing cases themselves, and mentions a legal defence fund supporting litigants. 949 Brusubi Layout, AU Summit Highway, P.O. Box 1896, Banjul. WHO IT SUITS: communities anywhere in Africa whose domestic remedies are exhausted or blocked, especially indigenous and minority communities facing dispossession. CAVEATS: entered under The Gambia because that is where it is based and registered — its work is continental. Regional cases take years and produce decisions that states must then be pressed to implement; it does not fund your costs; and its stated focus areas are refugees, minority rights, children and economic and social rights rather than environmental law as such.

trackers.name: Gambia Environmental Alliance — the union of 50+ community environmental groups with regional representatives, plus TANGO the NGO umbrella since 1983
trackers.desc: THE UNION A GAMBIAN VILLAGE GROUP CAN ACTUALLY JOIN: the GAMBIA ENVIRONMENTAL ALLIANCE (GEA), established and registered in 2021, describes itself as THE FIRST GOVERNING GROUP FOR ALL ENVIRONMENTAL COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS IN THE GAMBIA, and has grown to OVER FIFTY ORGANISATIONAL GROUPS, with MORE THAN SIX REGIONAL REPRESENTATIVES WORKING VOLUNTARILY, FROM BANJUL TO THE CENTRAL RIVER REGION. A union of community groups with a representative in your region is the thing a single village committee most lacks — fifty groups speaking together is a different weight of letter than one, and GEA exists to be joined. ITS STATED MISSION IS THE PART TO QUOTE BACK: to conserve flora, fauna, marine and coastal ecosystems, TO PROMOTE LOCAL PEOPLE'S INTERESTS OVER PROFIT for sustainable growth, and to complement government and partner efforts in policies, human resources and nature-based solutions. Its declared fields of action include ADVOCACY FOR LAND AND WATER RIGHTS, ECOSYSTEM PROTECTION AND RESTORATION, ACCESS AND BENEFIT SHARING AGREEMENTS, INNOVATIVE FINANCING MECHANISMS, POLICY INFLUENCE, and SOCIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE, across forests, drylands, oceans and coasts, wetlands and rivers; it states it works with government departments and agencies, the private sector, academic institutions, media houses and THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY OF THE GAMBIA. An organisation that already has a route to the National Assembly is how a village question becomes a national one — ask GEA to carry it, and ask about access and benefit sharing before you sign anything with a company. THE OLDER UMBRELLA: TANGO — THE ASSOCIATION OF NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS IN THE GAMBIA (tango.gm), FOUNDED 1983 — is the umbrella body for NGOs operating in the country, running national civil-society awards and validating internal policies for its members. Forty years of continuous existence makes TANGO the register of who is real in Gambian civil society: ask it whether an organisation approaching your village is actually a member. TWO MORE NAMED GAMBIAN BODIES: the STAY GREEN FOUNDATION, recorded in national climate-adaptation planning, and the WEST AFRICA BIRD STUDY ASSOCIATION (WABSA). WHO IT SUITS: Gambian village committees, community forest groups and coastal communities seeking allies, national voice or a benefit-sharing check. CAVEATS: VOLUNTEER-STAFFED MEMBERSHIP BODIES, NOT FUNDERS OR LAW FIRMS. For the community forest that becomes yours outright, The Gambia's Department of Forestry entry; for the 26-inspector enforcement reality and the A/B/C screening classes, the NEA entries; for counsel that will actually represent you, the IHRDA entry.

trackers.name: The Gambia's environment funding door — the Operational Focal Point at Environment House with phone and email, the concept-paper-first small grants route, and a labour-as-cost-share window
trackers.desc: THE FUNDING DOOR WITH AN ADDRESS ON IT — and this closes the last funding gap in this file's Gambian record: the country's OPERATIONAL FOCAL POINT for global environment financing is the EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR OF THE NATIONAL ENVIRONMENT AGENCY, at ENVIRONMENT HOUSE, JIMPEX ROAD, KANIFING, BANJUL — tel +220 4399423 / 4399425, with a published nea.gm email address. The Operational Focal Point ENDORSES which focal area a project's funds come from — biodiversity, climate change or land degradation — so that one office decides whether your file is even sent onward. Go there with your concept, and ask which focal area it should be filed under. THE SEQUENCE, WHICH IS WHERE MOST COMMUNITY APPLICATIONS DIE: for the small-grants window, a national community-based organisation or NGO CONTACTS THE NATIONAL COORDINATOR to receive application guidelines and forms; WITH THE COORDINATOR'S ASSISTANCE the proponent prepares A BRIEF PROJECT CONCEPT PAPER; the coordinator REVIEWS AND PRE-SCREENS it against the criteria and the country programme strategy; AND ONLY IF JUDGED ELIGIBLE does the proponent prepare a full proposal — a step that IN SOME CASES MAY BE SUPPORTED BY A PLANNING GRANT. Do not write a full proposal first. A short concept paper, prepared WITH the national coordinator's help, is the whole first stage — and there may be a grant to pay for writing the proposal itself. Grants run up to USD 50,000 directly to local communities, including indigenous peoples, community-based organisations and other non-governmental groups. A SECOND, SMALLER WINDOW WORTH KNOWING FOR ITS TERMS: a diplomatic mission in Banjul runs small grants to GAMBIAN COOPERATIVES improving basic economic or social conditions locally, maximum about USD 15,000 per project, projects completed within one year, applications encouraged FROM ALL PROVINCES, eligibility limited to cooperatives REGISTERED WITH THE GAMBIAN COOPERATIVE AGENCY — and REQUIRING COST SHARING IN THE FORM OF CASH, LABOUR OR MATERIAL PROVIDED BY THE LOCAL COMMUNITY. Labour counts as your contribution. A village with no cash still has a match to offer — and registering as a cooperative is the eligibility step that unlocks this one. WHO IT SUITS: Gambian village committees, community forest groups and cooperatives seeking project money. CAVEATS: WINDOWS ON APPLICATION CYCLES — confirm current calls and deadlines; the second is a foreign mission's programme. For the union of fifty community groups that can help you apply, The Gambia's GEA and TANGO entry; for the community forest that becomes yours outright, the Department of Forestry entry; for the 26-inspector enforcement reality, the NEA Inspectorate entry.

trackers.name: WABSA and the community bird sanctuary — a Gambian NGO with a published registration number that has built six community sanctuaries counting toward the national 15% protected-land target
trackers.desc: THE COMMUNITY SANCTUARY THAT COUNTS TOWARD THE NATIONAL TARGET — which is the strongest argument in this file for creating one, because the government needs it: the WEST AFRICAN BIRD STUDY ASSOCIATION (WABSA, wabsa.org) WAS FORMED IN APRIL 1994 BY INDIGENOUS GAMBIAN YOUTHS, CONCERNED CITIZENS SEEKING TO PRESERVE THE COUNTRY'S FLORA AND FAUNA, AND IS REGISTERED AS A CHARITABLE AND NON-PROFIT CONSERVATION NGO UNDER NGO REG N° 77, with its programmes DIRECTED BY THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS AND THE GENERAL MEMBERSHIP. Directed by the board AND the general membership means members vote on the programme, not just on the accounts. Ask whether the organisation working on your land is directed by its members — and note WABSA prints its NGO registration number, which is the document to demand from anyone. THE UNIT IT BUILDS: WABSA ESTABLISHES COMMUNITY SANCTUARIES THAT PROVIDE HABITATS FOR RESIDENT AND MIGRATORY BIRDS, WITH MAJOR COMMUNITY PROJECTS AT MARAKISSA, BRUFUT, KARTONG, BAMBALI, KUTIRR AND SIFOE COMMUNITY BIRD SANCTUARY — AND IT STATES THAT IT CONTRIBUTES THROUGH THE ESTABLISHMENT OF COMMUNITY BIRD SANCTUARIES TO THE GOVERNMENT TARGET OF 15% OF THE LAND AS PROTECTED AREAS. Six named village sanctuaries, and the government's own 15% target is met partly by them. Put it to your ministry that way: a community sanctuary on your ground is not a request, it is a contribution to a national commitment the state has already made. Ask which national target your protection would count toward — every country in this file has one. WHAT MAKES THE VILLAGERS KEEP IT: WABSA PROMOTES ALTERNATIVE SUSTAINABLE LIVELIHOOD ACTIVITIES THROUGH VEGETABLE GARDEN SCHEMES, AQUACULTURE AND CASHEW PROCESSING, AND ITS WORK HAS INCLUDED THE RESTORATION OF OYSTER FARMS — creating livelihood activities for INDIGENOUS PEOPLE LIVING NEARBY THE RESTORED AND COMMUNITY BIRD SANCTUARY AREAS. A sanctuary with a vegetable scheme and an oyster farm beside it is one the neighbours defend. Oysters in particular: the mangrove that shelters the birds is the mangrove the oysters grow on, so protection and income are the same act. THE OUTCOMES IT CLAIMS, WITH FIGURES: the restoration work HAS CONTRIBUTED TO HALTING AND REVERSING SALINE INTRUSION IN THE INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY FARMLANDS AND WETLANDS, WITH ECOSYSTEM SERVICES IMPROVED AND BIODIVERSITY SPECIES RECOVERED — AND IT IS ESTIMATED THAT WABSA'S RESTORATION ACTIVITIES CONTRIBUTE 0.15% OF THE GAMBIA'S TOTAL CLIMATE CHANGE MITIGATION REQUIRED BY 2030. Saline intrusion into farmland reversed is the outcome a farmer cares about; the carbon figure is what a funder cares about. Quote whichever one you are speaking to — the same mangrove does both. ITS OTHER WORK: establishing BIRD STUDY CLUBS IN SCHOOLS, research on LOCAL NAMES OF BIRDS, mangrove conservation through REDD+, and restoration at NIUMI, JOKADU, KIANG WEST and TANBI WETLAND national parks, the BAO BOLONG WETLAND RESERVE, the TANJI BIRD RESERVE and PIRANG BONTO FOREST — with a GEF small grants project on Niumi National Park, and tree planting with the national youth council and the red cross society WITH TECHNICAL SUPPORT FROM THE DEPARTMENTS OF FORESTRY AND OF PARKS AND WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT. Research on the LOCAL NAMES of birds is quiet but useful: a species recorded under the name your elders use is evidence that your community has known it for generations. WHO IT SUITS: Gambian villages wanting a sanctuary that earns, mangrove and oyster communities, and schools. CAVEATS: A SMALL MEMBERSHIP NGO dependent on project grants. For 50+ organisations and six regional representatives, The Gambia's GEA entry; for the GEF focal point at Environment House with its published telephone, the Jimpex Road entry.

trackers.name: RAMPAO — the West African marine protected areas network founded by fifteen MPAs themselves, now eight countries and 38 areas, which publishes a management-effectiveness evaluation of its own members and lets you reproduce it free
trackers.desc: FIFTEEN PROTECTED AREAS FOUNDED IT THEMSELVES — placement note first: THIS IS AN EIGHT-COUNTRY REGIONAL NETWORK, FILED UNDER THE GAMBIA BECAUSE IT IS A MEMBER COUNTRY WITH NO MARINE-NETWORK ENTRY IN THIS FILE. THE MEMBERS ARE BENIN, CABO VERDE, MAURITANIA, THE GAMBIA, GUINEA, GUINEA-BISSAU, SENEGAL AND SIERRA LEONE. HOW IT WAS MADE, AND IT IS THE PART TO COPY: FOLLOWING A LONG PROCESS OF REFLECTION AND CONCERTATION BETWEEN MPA MANAGERS AND THE DIFFERENT INSTITUTIONS INVOLVED IN THE MANAGEMENT OF MARINE AND COASTAL RESOURCES, THE REGIONAL NETWORK WAS CREATED OFFICIALLY BY FIFTEEN MEMBER MARINE PROTECTED AREAS. The areas themselves founded it — fifteen of them, after their managers had talked for a long time first. Not a donor programme with members recruited afterwards. This file recorded the same shape in Madagascar, where regional platforms of protected-area managers federated; here it happened at continental-coast scale, and the managers include community-managed areas. WHAT IT IS NOW: IT BRINGS TOGETHER 8 COUNTRIES AND OFFICIALLY COUNTS 38 MARINE PROTECTED AREAS, WITH AROUND FIFTY IN A WIDER COUNT — AND IT IS EXPANDING, WITH LIBERIA, CÔTE D'IVOIRE, GHANA, TOGO, BENIN AND NIGERIA BEING TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT IN A CONSULTATION ON EXTENSION TO THE OTHER COASTAL COUNTRIES OF THE REGION. Six more countries under consultation. If your coast is in one of those six and you manage or want a protected area, the network is actively looking for you — which is the easiest moment to join anything. WHAT MEMBERSHIP ACTUALLY PROVIDES, LISTED: SUPPORTING AND FURNISHING SERVICES TO THE MEMBERS OF THE NETWORK — THE NETWORKING OF A SET OF REPRESENTATIVE MPAs, THE REHABILITATION AND RESTORATION OF CRITICAL HABITATS, EXCHANGE AND MUTUAL LEARNING BETWEEN MEMBERS, AND TECHNICAL CAPACITY BUILDING. REHABILITATION AND RESTORATION OF CRITICAL HABITATS is a service, not a slogan — meaning the network brings resources to repair damaged ground, not only to protect intact ground. A community whose mangrove or seagrass has already been cut is still eligible; damage is not disqualifying. AND THE UNUSUAL THING IT DOES: IT PRODUCED AND PUBLISHED AN EVALUATION OF THE MANAGEMENT EFFECTIVENESS OF THE MARINE PROTECTED AREAS OF ITS OWN NETWORK — AND THE REPRODUCTION OF THE TEXT FOR NON-COMMERCIAL PURPOSES, NOTABLY EDUCATIONAL, IS PERMITTED WITHOUT PRIOR WRITTEN AUTHORISATION, PROVIDED THE SOURCE IS DULY CITED. A network that publishes how well its own members are performing, and lets anyone copy the report free for teaching. Two uses: it tells you which areas in the region are actually managed well so you know whom to visit and ask; and the free-reproduction clause means you can print the relevant pages for your own community meeting without asking anyone. THE REFERENCE PUBLICATION: a state-of-the-marine-protected-areas report is to be EDITED EVERY 3 YEARS, deepening elements of conservation including OTHER EFFECTIVE AREA-BASED CONSERVATION MEASURES, and is described as A USEFUL AND OPERATIONAL DECISION-SUPPORT TOOL and THE RESULT OF A PARTICIPATORY AND INCLUSIVE ELABORATION PROCESS WHICH BENEFITS UPSTREAM FROM THE CONTRIBUTION OF THE PRACTITIONERS WHO ARE THE ACTORS IN THE COUNTRIES CONCERNED. Written with the practitioners upstream, not about them afterwards. If you manage an area, contributing to the next edition puts your site into the reference document that ministries and funders consult — ask when the next three-yearly cycle opens. THE OBSERVATORY BEHIND IT: AN OBSERVATORY FOR BIODIVERSITY AND PROTECTED AREAS IN WEST AFRICA IS IMPLEMENTED IN THE SIXTEEN STATES OF WEST AFRICA BY A CONSORTIUM OF FOUR NAMED INSTITUTIONS — AN ECOLOGICAL MONITORING CENTRE, THIS NETWORK, A UNIVERSITY REGIONAL MARINE CENTRE AND A REGIONAL AGRO-HYDRO-METEOROLOGY CENTRE — UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF A REGIONAL ECONOMIC UNION AS INSTITUTIONAL HOST, WITH THE OBJECTIVE OF IMPROVING THE LONG-TERM MAINTENANCE OF BIODIVERSITY THROUGH THE PROMOTION OF THE BEST SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE AND DATA AND THE REINFORCEMENT OF CAPACITIES TO SUPPORT POLICIES AND DECISION-MAKING. Two universities and a meteorological centre inside the same consortium as the MPA network, hosted by the region's economic union. The data on your coast is being assembled there — which means a community can ask that consortium what is already recorded about its own waters before commissioning anything. AND THE PURPOSE, STATED IN THE NETWORK'S OWN TERMS: IT WORKS CLOSELY WITH MPA MANAGERS TO PROMOTE THE CONSERVATION OF MARINE BIODIVERSITY FOR THE BENEFIT OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES. FOR THE BENEFIT OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES, written into the network's own description of itself. Hold it to that sentence. WHO IT SUITS: Gambian and other West African coastal communities managing or seeking a marine protected area, and anyone in the six expansion countries. CAVEATS: A NETWORK OF AREA MANAGERS — a community joins through the area it manages or co-manages, so the prior step is getting that recognition. For the seven-country coastal coalition any organisation can join with one signed form, Senegal's PRCM entry; for the coastal infrastructure training that included the financiers, Guinea's entry.

trackers.name: Story grants of $500 to $10,000 that pay a reporter's travel to cover mining, land and environmental harm — freelancers and social media creators eligible, editorial mentorship included, and organisational grants to start a reporters' network where none exists
trackers.desc: SOMEBODY WILL PAY A REPORTER TO COME AND LOOK — declared adjacency first: THIS FILE'S SOUTH SUDAN ENTRY COVERS LEGAL DEFENCE FOR JOURNALISTS ONCE THEY ARE SUED. THIS ENTRY IS THE MONEY AND TRAINING THAT GETS THE STORY REPORTED IN THE FIRST PLACE. THE MONEY: STORY GRANTS, WHICH OFTEN COVER REPORTING OR TRAVEL COSTS, RANGING FROM $500 TO AS HIGH AS $10,000 FOR INDIVIDUAL OR SMALL GROUPS OF JOURNALISTS. The reason no journalist has covered your case is usually the bus fare and the three days away, not indifference. This file has recorded again and again that a single published article is the entry ticket to everything else — the Environmental Justice Atlas requires one, funders read them, and a documented case travels. Travel money for a reporter is therefore one of the cheapest things that changes a community's position, and somebody already funds it. THE FOUR KINDS OF SUPPORT: FUNDING, TRAINING, RESOURCES, AND MENTORSHIP — WITH GRANTEES PAIRED UP WITH A VETERAN JOURNALIST OR EDITOR WHO HELPS THEM THROUGH THE COURSE OF THE INVESTIGATION AS THEY PURSUE ANGLES AND TRACK DOWN INFORMATION. A mentor attached to the story is what turns a local reporter's first investigation into something a national outlet will run. Ask any journalist you approach whether they have applied. THE AFRICAN MINING ROUND, WITH ITS EXACT TERMS: A THREE-DAY VIRTUAL WORKSHOP FOR JOURNALISTS IN FOUR NAMED AFRICAN COUNTRIES ON MINING, THE ENVIRONMENT AND HUMAN RIGHTS — UP TO 40 PARTICIPANTS, CONDUCTED IN ENGLISH AND FRENCH WITH SIMULTANEOUS INTERPRETATION — FOLLOWED BY 10 STORY GRANTS OF US$2,000 EACH FUNDING TRAVEL, REPORTER STIPENDS AND MULTIMEDIA ELEMENTS, ALONGSIDE ONE-TO-ONE EDITORIAL MENTORSHIP AND TRAINING ON REPACKAGING REPORTING FOR SOCIAL MEDIA. MINING, ENVIRONMENT AND HUMAN RIGHTS as one subject, taught together. That is precisely the intersection most of this file's cases sit at, and the round exists because reporters were covering one strand without the other two. WHO IS ELIGIBLE, AND IT IS BROADER THAN PEOPLE ASSUME: JOURNALISTS IN ANY MEDIUM AND SOCIAL MEDIA CONTENT CREATORS WITH EXPERIENCE COVERING MINING, ENVIRONMENTAL OR HUMAN RIGHTS ISSUES; FREELANCERS AND EARLY-CAREER REPORTERS ARE ELIGIBLE; AND GROUP SUBMISSIONS ARE ALLOWED UNDER A SINGLE LEAD APPLICANT RESPONSIBLE FOR COMMUNICATIONS AND FUND MANAGEMENT. SOCIAL MEDIA CONTENT CREATORS qualify. The young person in your community who already posts video of the clearances is inside this definition — they do not need a press card, and this file's video-as-evidence entry is what makes their footage usable in court as well as online. THE ACCESS PROVISION, WHICH IS RARE: A LIMITED NUMBER OF COMMUNICATIONS STIPENDS ARE OFFERED TO PARTICIPANTS WITH UNSTABLE INTERNET ACCESS, AND ALL WHO COMPLETE THE WORKSHOP RECEIVE A CERTIFICATE. They pay for your data bundle so you can attend. Almost no training in this file accounts for the cost of being online for three days. WHO TEACHES: JOURNALISTS LEARN FROM RESEARCHERS, ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTISTS, MINING LAW EXPERTS, HUMAN RIGHTS ADVOCATES, CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES WORKING AT THE INTERSECTION OF MINING, ENVIRONMENT AND HUMAN RIGHTS IN AFRICA. LOCAL COMMUNITIES listed among the teachers. If your committee has fought a mine, offer yourselves as a session — being in the room where forty reporters are trained is worth more than any single article. THE ORGANISATIONAL GRANTS, FOR GROUPS RATHER THAN INDIVIDUALS: MEDIA GRANTS ARE MADE TO ORGANIZATIONS IN ORDER TO ESTABLISH NETWORKS OF ENVIRONMENTAL JOURNALISTS IN COUNTRIES WHERE THEY DON'T EXIST, AND BUILD THEIR CAPACITY WHERE THEY DO — INVITING APPLICATIONS FROM MEDIA ORGANIZATIONS, JOURNALISM NETWORKS, UNIVERSITIES AND JOURNALISM SCHOOLS; NGOs AND RESEARCH INSTITUTES WILL ALSO BE CONSIDERED, BUT ONLY THOSE WITH STRONG MEDIA AND COMMUNICATION PROGRAMS. WHERE THEY DON'T EXIST. If your country has no environmental reporters' network, funding to start one is a named purpose — and a university journalism school is an eligible applicant, which is often an easier host than an NGO. WHAT THOSE GRANTS FUND: TRAINING JOURNALISTS THROUGH WORKSHOPS, FIELD TRIPS AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF REPORTING RESOURCES; INNOVATING STORYTELLING THROUGH MAPPING TOOLS, DATA VISUALIZATION AND NEW PLATFORMS; AND STRENGTHENING JOURNALIST NETWORKS. FIELD TRIPS. Getting reporters physically to the site is fundable as a category — so a community can propose hosting one rather than waiting to be found. THE THEMES IT NAMES, AND THE LAST IS THE UNUSUAL ONE: WILDLIFE TRAFFICKING, ENVIRONMENTAL CRIMES, URBAN CONSERVATION, BIODIVERSITY CREDITS, GREEN AND BLUE ECONOMIES, INNOVATIVE CONSERVATION EFFORTS, THE IMPACT OF NEW POLICIES OR EMERGING THREATS — AND UNINTENDED HARMFUL EFFECTS OF CONSERVATION MEASURES. UNINTENDED HARMFUL EFFECTS OF CONSERVATION MEASURES is funded as a story theme. A community evicted by a park or squeezed by a carbon project has a subject an editor is already looking for — which this file has recorded from Kenya's conservation land purchases to Tanzania's carbon contracts. THE GEOGRAPHIC PRIORITY: A FOCUS ON BIODIVERSITY-RICH REGIONS AND UNDERREPRESENTED COUNTRIES, INCLUDING THOSE IN WEST AFRICA. AND THE TOOL IT POINTS REPORTERS AT: A WILDLIFE CRIME TRACKING TOOL DEVELOPED BY A SOUTH AFRICAN INVESTIGATIVE ENVIRONMENTAL JOURNALISM ORGANISATION. WHO IT SUITS: African communities who need their case reported, and the local reporters, freelancers and content creators who would cover it if the travel were paid. CAVEATS: GRANTS GO TO JOURNALISTS AND MEDIA ORGANISATIONS, NOT TO COMMUNITIES — the use to a community is bringing the opportunity to a reporter. Calls are irregular and posted several times a year. For legal defence once the story is published, South Sudan's media defence entry; for making community footage court-ready, Niger's video-as-evidence entry; for the register that requires one media story to list your case, Algeria's Environmental Justice Atlas entry.

trackers.name: The African treaty body in Abidjan whose stated job is that your government is not out-lawyered by an investor — with a free online academy any African civil servant can join by email, a legal hotline, and a roster of specialised firms members may use
trackers.desc: A TREATY BODY WHOSE JOB IS THAT YOUR GOVERNMENT IS NOT OUT-LAWYERED — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ETHIOPIA ENTRY NAMED THIS FACILITY IN ONE LINE WHILE DESCRIBING A SENIOR-LAWYERS NETWORK, AND NIGERIA CARRIES THE SAME DEVELOPMENT BANK'S INDEPENDENT REVIEW MECHANISM. NEITHER DESCRIBES THE ACADEMY, THE HOTLINE, THE ROSTER OR THE MEMBERSHIP ROUTE. THE STATED PURPOSE, WHICH IS THE FIND: THE GOAL OF THE FACILITY IS TO REMOVE ASYMMETRIC TECHNICAL CAPACITIES AND LEVEL THE FIELD OF LEGAL EXPERTISE AMONG PARTIES TO LITIGATION AND NEGOTIATIONS — A CORE PILLAR OF ITS MANDATE IS TO REBALANCE NEGOTIATING POWER BETWEEN AFRICAN STATES AND PRIVATE INVESTORS BY ENSURING THAT GOVERNMENTS HAVE ACCESS TO WORLD-CLASS LEGAL EXPERTISE WHEN FACING COMPLEX TRANSACTIONS. An African institution that exists because African governments lose at the table. This file has recorded community after community discovering that their own ministry signed a contract it did not understand — and this is the body that ministry was supposed to call. Knowing it exists is itself leverage: a community can ask, in public and in writing, whether the facility was consulted before the deal was signed. WHY IT EXISTS, STATED PLAINLY: THE DEBT CRISES OF THE 1980s AND 1990s HAD EXPOSED THE DEARTH OF LEGAL AND TECHNICAL CAPACITY WHICH RESULTED IN POORLY NEGOTIATED CONTRACTS AND UNSUCCESSFUL LITIGATION OUTCOMES FOR AFRICAN GOVERNMENTS. WHERE IT SITS AND WHO ASKED FOR IT: AN INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATION HOSTED BY AN AFRICAN DEVELOPMENT BANK GROUP IN ABIDJAN, ESTABLISHED BY TREATY IN FORCE FROM 22 DECEMBER 2008 AT THE REQUEST OF AFRICAN COUNTRIES, OPERATIONAL FROM 2010 — WITH THE INITIAL REQUEST MADE BY AFRICAN FINANCE MINISTERS IN 2003. THE FREE ACADEMY, AND EXACTLY HOW A CIVIL SERVANT GETS IN: A VIRTUAL ACADEMY LAUNCHED IN 2017, A PORTAL DEDICATED TO CONTINUING TRAINING, WITH AN ONLINE REGISTRATION PLATFORM, INDUSTRY EXPERTS AND PRACTICAL CASE STUDIES SO PARTICIPANTS UNDERSTAND HOW TO APPLY THEORETICAL KNOWLEDGE IN CONCRETE SITUATIONS. THE COURSE IS FREE FOR AFRICAN GOVERNMENTS — AND A CIVIL SERVANT IN AN AFRICAN GOVERNMENT WHO WISHES TO TAKE A COURSE SHOULD CONTACT A PUBLISHED EMAIL ADDRESS FOR A COUPON CODE. Free, online, and one email away for anyone employed by an African government. The district lands officer, the environment ministry lawyer and the local council legal adviser your community deals with can all take contract-negotiation training at no cost — and telling them so is a cheap, non-confrontational thing a community organisation can do that raises the competence of the people deciding its case. THE THREE SERVICES: LEGAL ADVISORY SERVICES TO GOVERNMENTS IN THE STRUCTURING AND NEGOTIATION OF COMPLEX COMMERCIAL TRANSACTIONS RELATING TO EXTRACTIVES AND NATURAL RESOURCES, INFRASTRUCTURE, PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIPS, POWER AND SOVEREIGN DEBT — TO ENSURE AFRICAN COUNTRIES BENEFIT FROM TRANSACTIONS THAT ARE FAIR AND EQUITABLE; CAPACITY BUILDING FOR AFRICAN LAWYERS AND GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS, INCLUDING TRAINING PROGRAMS AND PLATFORMS AND LEGAL HOTLINES; AND CREDITOR LITIGATION ASSISTANCE, PARTICULARLY AGAINST VULTURE FUNDS. LEGAL HOTLINES for government lawyers. INFRASTRUCTURE and PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIPS are named alongside extractives — so the road, the port and the power plant crossing your land fall inside the mandate, not only the mine. THE MEMBERSHIP BENEFITS, PUBLISHED AS A LIST: PRIORITY ASSISTANCE WITH CAPACITY BUILDING SEMINARS ON DEBT MANAGEMENT AND LITIGATION, ASSETS RECOVERY, COMPLEX COMMERCIAL AND BUSINESS TRANSACTIONS, NEGOTIATION, NATURAL RESOURCES AND EXTRACTIVE INDUSTRIES MANAGEMENT, INVESTMENT AGREEMENTS AND INTERNATIONAL ARBITRATION; INDIVIDUALIZED AND REGIONAL TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE; USE OF A ROSTER OF SPECIALIZED LAW FIRMS AND LEGAL EXPERTS TO REPRESENT MEMBERS; AND USE OF A DATABASE SYSTEM ON PAST AND CURRENT TRENDS. A ROSTER OF SPECIALIZED LAW FIRMS the state may draw on. When a ministry pleads that it cannot match the investor's counsel, that roster is the answer — and the excuse is checkable. THE MEMBERSHIP RULE AND THE GAP IT IMPLIES: MEMBERSHIP IS OPEN TO ALL SOVEREIGN NATIONS AND INTERNATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS — AND IT ORGANISES MASTERCLASSES ON THE MEMBERSHIP RATIFICATION PROCESS UNDER ITS TREATY TO RAISE MEMBERS' AWARENESS OF THE NECESSITY TO COMPLETE MEMBERSHIP. It has to run classes reminding countries to finish ratifying. So check whether your own country has completed membership — an unratified treaty is a concrete, winnable national ask, and a state that has not joined is negotiating without help it could have had for nothing. THE MEASURED RESULT: IT IS ESTIMATED THAT ITS INTERVENTIONS HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO SAVINGS AND REVENUES FOR GOVERNMENTS OF APPROXIMATELY USD 15 BILLION. THE WORKED COUNTRY EXAMPLE: OPERATIONS IN ONE NAMED WEST AFRICAN COUNTRY BEGAN IN 2013 WITH A $400,000 GRANT AGREEMENT FOR LEGAL SUPPORT ON INDEPENDENT ENERGY PROJECTS AND THE MODERNIZATION OF TRANSMISSION AND DISTRIBUTION IN A METROPOLITAN AREA — AND SINCE THEN THE FACILITY HAS RECEIVED MORE THAN 10 REQUESTS FROM THAT COUNTRY FOR ADVISORY SERVICES IN THE EXTRACTIVE SECTOR AND CAPACITY BUILDING IN SOVEREIGN DEBT AND INFRASTRUCTURE. Ten requests from one small country, on the public record. Requests are traceable — which means a community can ask whether the facility was asked about the project on its land, and the absence of a request is itself a finding. THE CONVENING FUNCTION, WHICH IS THE OPENING FOR CIVIL SOCIETY: ITS INTERVENTIONS ALSO FACILITATE NATIONAL DIALOGUE AND CONSULTATION BETWEEN AND WITHIN GOVERNMENT INSTITUTIONS AND THE PRIVATE SECTOR TO DEVELOP COHERENT POLICIES AND LEGAL FRAMEWORKS FOR NATIONAL DEVELOPMENT. AND THE SCOPE: THE FULL LIFECYCLE OF TRANSACTIONS AND DISPUTES, FROM PROJECT STRUCTURING AND CONTRACT NEGOTIATION TO SETTLEMENT SUPPORT. SETTLEMENT SUPPORT at the far end. A dispute already underway is still within their remit, which matters where a concession has soured and the state is being sued. WHO IT SUITS: African national coalitions and community organisations pressing their own government to negotiate competently — and any African civil servant who can take the free training. CAVEATS: ITS CLIENTS ARE STATES, NOT COMMUNITIES — a village cannot instruct it. The uses here are the free academy, the membership question, and asking publicly whether it was consulted. For the same bank's review mechanism one person can now trigger, Nigeria's entry; for senior and retired lawyers working on attorney-client terms, Ethiopia's entry; for the contract repositories, Mauritania's and South Sudan's entries.

Two decimal places, published by the funder about itself. Every funder in this file says it supports local leadership; this one states the share and can be held to it. Ask any prospective funder for those two figures — what proportion of your grantees are led by the people affected, and what proportion of your money is unrestricted — and the answer, or the refusal, tells you what you are dealing with. A published grantee list is itself a resource: it is a directory of indigenous-led organisations that have already passed this funder's assessment, searchable by anyone looking for a peer, a partner or a referee. THE GRANT RANGE AND TERM: MOST GRANTS RANGE FROM US$50,000 TO US$100,000 FOR ONE OR TWO YEARS — WITH LARGER GRANTS OVER LONGER PERIODS AVAILABLE GENERALLY BY INVITATION ONLY AND TO PREVIOUS GRANTEES OR ESTABLISHED LOCAL PARTNERS. And INQUIRIES are invited: a question before applying is a normal step here, not an imposition. THE AFRICAN REGIONAL PROGRAMME NAMED: AN AFRICAN RIFT VALLEY PROGRAMME, ESPECIALLY SOUTHWEST ETHIOPIA AND ALSO NORTHERN KENYA — COVERING A WIDE RANGE OF PEOPLES AND LIVELIHOODS IN SOUTHERN ETHIOPIA AND NORTHERN KENYA. WHERE GRANTS GO WITHIN A REGION: GENERALLY TO ORGANIZATIONS BASED WITHIN THOSE REGIONS OR, WHERE APPROPRIATE, TO INTERNATIONALLY BASED ORGANIZATIONS WORKING IN SUPPORT OF THE EFFORTS OF PEOPLE AND INSTITUTIONS ON THE GROUND. Based within the region, first. The foreign organisation is the exception rather than the default — the inverse of the pattern this file has recorded across most international funding. THE ELIGIBLE ORGANISATION TYPES: DEVELOPMENT NGOs, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, GOVERNMENT UNITS, UNIVERSITIES, MUSEUMS AND OTHER TYPES OF NON-PROFIT — PRIMARILY WORKING WITH PROJECTS THAT ASSIST PEOPLES AND COMMUNITIES IDENTIFIED AS INDIGENOUS, TRIBAL AND MINORITY. MUSEUMS AND UNIVERSITIES are eligible alongside community organisations. A community holding cultural material, an archive or an oral-history project has an institutional partner route that most environmental funders in this file do not offer. THE STRATEGY IT STATES: SUPPORTING AND STRENGTHENING INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' EFFORTS TO SECURE AND EXERCISE THEIR RIGHTS TO THEIR LAND, TERRITORIES, RESOURCES, AND SOVEREIGN SYSTEMS OF GOVERNANCE. SOVEREIGN SYSTEMS OF GOVERNANCE — the council of elders, the customary authority, the grazing committee. Funding the institution rather than a project run around it is what this file has repeatedly found decides whether anything survives the grant. THE SUBJECT IT FUNDS: THE INTERFACE BETWEEN NATURAL ENVIRONMENTS AND HUMAN CULTURES — THE BICULTURAL, DESCRIBED AS THE RICH BUT NEGLECTED ADAPTIVE INTERWEAVE OF PEOPLE AND PLACE, CULTURE AND ECOLOGY. A community defending a sacred grove, a fishing calendar or a herding route does not have to translate that into a species-conservation proposal here. The culture and the ecology are one subject, which is the framing most conservation funders force applicants to abandon. WHAT IT DOES BESIDES GRANTMAKING: GRANT MAKING, CAPACITY BUILDING, NETWORKING AND OTHER INTERVENTIONS — AND FINANCIAL AND LOGISTICAL SUPPORT FOR INDIGENOUS-LED AND COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS. LOGISTICAL SUPPORT is unusual and worth asking about: help with the mechanics rather than only the money. THE ISSUES ITS PARTNERS WORK ON: A GLOBAL NETWORK OF INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES AND ORGANIZATIONS TACKLING ISSUES RANGING FROM CLIMATE CHANGE AND LAND SOVEREIGNTY TO GENDER JUSTICE. AND THE CHANGE OF APPROACH, RECORDED BECAUSE IT AFFECTS ELIGIBILITY: THE FUNDER RECONFIGURED ITS GRANTMAKING AND MOVED AWAY FROM THE REGIONAL APPROACH OF ITS PREVIOUS WORK TOWARD A BROADER, RIGHTS-BASED STRATEGY — SO GRANTSEEKERS WHO WERE PREVIOUSLY EXCLUDED DUE TO GEOGRAPHIC RESTRICTIONS MAY WANT TO TAKE A SECOND LOOK. The old African programme covered two countries; the geographic gate has since been loosened. If your organisation was told years ago that it was outside the region, that answer may no longer hold — and this file has recorded funders' published country lists going stale more often than any other detail. WHO IT SUITS: African indigenous, pastoralist and minority organisations working where culture and ecology are the same subject — especially those needing unrestricted money for their own institutions. CAVEATS: A PRE-PROPOSAL WINDOW WITH A LIMITED NUMBER INVITED ON, THE LARGER TIER BY INVITATION ONLY, AND ITS GEOGRAPHIC FOCUS HAS CHANGED — check the current programme pages before writing. For the no-pass-or-fail funder, Ethiopia's entry; for the fund that waives registration, bank account and ID, the Central African Republic's entry; for the indigenous-led fund accepting video applications, Chad's entry.

trackers.name: The WITNESS Library — free downloadable guides on filming so the footage stands up as evidence, including a section for community documenters of environmental crimes and one on recording who ordered the act rather than only the act — in Arabic, French and Portuguese, licensed for adaptation
trackers.desc: FILM IT SO IT COUNTS IN COURT, AND FILM WHO ORDERED IT — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S LIBYA ENTRY CARRIES A GLOBAL WITNESS HOST, A DIFFERENT ORGANISATION WITH A SIMILAR NAME, NOT RESTATED AND NOT SHIPPED; ITS EQUATORIAL GUINEA ENTRY THE FREE OFFLINE MAPPING AND EVIDENCE TOOLS; ITS MALI ENTRY THE PRINTABLE SECURITY TOOLKIT; ITS ETHIOPIA ENTRY THE DEVELOPMENT PROJECT DATABASE. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE ENVIRONMENTAL SECTION, WHICH IS THE FIND: A GUIDE THAT WILL SUPPORT COMMUNITY-BASED DOCUMENTERS TO COLLECT VISUAL EVIDENCE OF ENVIRONMENTAL HUMAN RIGHTS CRIMES AND VIOLATIONS SO THAT IT CAN BE EFFECTIVELY USED IN ADVOCACY AND ACCOUNTABILITY PROCESSES. Written for community documenters, not for journalists or lawyers. A village that films a bulldozer, a spill or an eviction is usually producing something that proves an event happened but proves nothing about who is responsible or whether it was lawful — which is why so much of the footage in this file's cases never became evidence. THE LINKAGE EVIDENCE SECTION, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: CAPTURING LINKAGE AND NOTICE EVIDENCE CAN BE INCREDIBLY IMPORTANT FOR LONG-TERM JUSTICE AND ACCOUNTABILITY — LEARN HOW TO DOCUMENT WHO COMMITTED THE CRIME AND HOW THEY DID IT, IN ADDITION TO DOCUMENTING THE CRIME ITSELF. LINKAGE is the whole difference between a video of a cleared forest and a case against a company. Filming the vehicle markings, the licence plates, the uniforms, the signage, the paperwork handed over and the person giving instructions is what connects an act to the entity that ordered it — and NOTICE evidence proves they knew. A community filming without that in mind is documenting its own loss rather than building a claim. THE SCENE GUIDANCE: HOW TO SAFELY AND EFFECTIVELY GATHER VIDEO DOCUMENTATION AT THE SCENE OF AN ALLEGED VIOLATION, INCLUDING DEVELOPING A FILMING PLAN, CAPTURING DETAILS AND VARIOUS ANGLES, AND FILLING OUT A CAMERA REPORT — PLUS TIPS ON ADDING NARRATION DURING FILMING SO THAT THE WORK IS EASIER TO VERIFY. A CAMERA REPORT and spoken narration are the two cheapest things that make footage verifiable: who filmed, when, where, and what is being shown, said aloud on the recording. Neither costs anything, and both are usually missing. WHAT THE FIELD GUIDE IS AND WHO IT WAS BUILT WITH: BASIC AND ADVANCED PRACTICES DRAWN FROM CONVERSATIONS WITH ATTORNEYS, INVESTIGATORS, ANALYSTS, LEGAL SCHOLARS, FUNDERS AND PEERS WORKING ON THE GROUND WHERE THE VIOLATIONS HAPPEN — AIMING TO MOVE VIDEO FROM CAPTURE TO THE COURTROOM. THE LANGUAGES EACH SECTION IS ISSUED IN: SECTIONS ARE DOWNLOADABLE IN ENGLISH, ARABIC, FRENCH, SPANISH, UKRAINIAN AND RUSSIAN DEPENDING ON THE SECTION — AND THE ORGANISATION MAINTAINS SITES IN ARABIC, FRENCH, PORTUGUESE AND SPANISH. French, Arabic and Portuguese all covered, though not every section in every language — check which sections exist in yours before planning a training around them. THE LIBRARY AND ITS SIZE: OVER 250 LEARNING MATERIALS, FREE AND ADAPTABLE, INCLUDING VIDEO AND PDF DOWNLOADS OF CORE TRAINING MATERIALS AND HOW-TO GUIDES. THE LICENCE: THE ARCHIVING GUIDE IS LICENSED UNDER A CREATIVE COMMONS ATTRIBUTION-NONCOMMERCIAL-SHAREALIKE LICENCE. You may translate it into your own language and hand it out. That is explicit permission to adapt, which almost nothing else in this file grants — a national organisation can produce a version in the local language without asking. THE ARCHIVING GUIDE AND WHO IT IS FOR: IF YOU ARE A HUMAN RIGHTS ACTIVIST, A SMALL OR GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATION, OR MEDIA COLLECTIVE, CREATING OR COLLECTING DIGITAL VIDEO, AND YOU WANT TO MAKE SURE IT CAN BE USED FOR ADVOCACY, AS EVIDENCE, FOR EDUCATION OR HISTORICAL MEMORY — NOT JUST NOW BUT INTO THE FUTURE — BUT YOU ARE NOT SURE WHERE TO BEGIN, THEN THIS GUIDE IS FOR YOU. Land cases take years. Footage on a phone that is lost, sold or broken before the hearing is the ordinary outcome, and archiving is the unglamorous step that decides whether the evidence still exists when it is finally needed. THE COMMUNITY ARCHIVING COLLECTION: A TOOLKIT FOR ACTIVISTS AND COMMUNITY DEFENDERS LOOKING TO PRESERVE HUMAN RIGHTS DOCUMENTATION — INCLUDING GUIDANCE ON DOCUMENTING AND SAFEGUARDING AGAINST MANIPULATION BY OPPRESSIVE FORCES WHILST MAINTAINING THE INTEGRITY OF HISTORICAL NARRATIVES AND LIVED REALITIES. THE SHUTDOWN COLLECTION: RESOURCES TO SUPPORT ACTIVISTS IN PREPARING AND NAVIGATING INTERNET SHUTDOWNS — TIPS AND TACTICS TO PREPARE, DOCUMENT AND PRESERVE FOOTAGE DURING A SHUTDOWN.
