WHAT IT IS AND WHERE ITS PEOPLE ARE: it is A REGIONAL, NON-PROFIT TECHNICAL INSTITUTE WITH MORE THAN 30 YEARS OF DEDICATED EXPERIENCE ACROSS THE COUNTRIES AND TERRITORIES OF THE CARIBBEAN REGION, headquartered in one island capital with staff based in three further countries; it CHAMPION[S] LOCALLY LED APPROACHES TO USING AND MANAGING NATURAL RESOURCES THAT PUT THE NEEDS OF COMMUNITIES FIRST, ESPECIALLY THOSE WHICH ARE OFTEN OVERLOOKED, and promotes CARIBBEAN SOLUTIONS FOR CARIBBEAN CHALLENGES, RECOGNISING THAT THE REGION'S UNIQUE ISSUES REQUIRE HOMEGROWN RESPONSES. Staff living in four countries, not a distant headquarters. For the small islands, where most entries in this file point to bodies far away, this is the regional organisation that is actually present. THE TECHNICAL SERVICES IT SELLS OR PROVIDES: named areas include DEVELOPMENT OF TOOLKITS AND TRAINING IN FACILITATING PARTICIPATORY APPROACHES, PARTICIPATORY FOREST POLICY DEVELOPMENT, SITE PLANNING AND COMMUNITY FORESTRY, PARTICIPATORY PROTECTED AREA POLICY DEVELOPMENT, PLANNING AND MANAGEMENT, CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONAL CAPACITY BUILDING, SUPPORTING DEVELOPMENT OF SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITY SMALL AND MICRO-ENTERPRISES and DEVELOPMENT OF COMMUNICATION STRATEGIES AND PRODUCTS such as case studies and policy briefs. Site planning and protected area management planning are services you can commission. Where a community has been told to produce a management plan it cannot write, this is who writes it with them. WHAT THE MICRO-GRANTS LOOK LIKE: one programme assisted SIX CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS WITH TECHNICAL SUPPORT AND MICRO-GRANTS TO SCALE UP ECOSYSTEM-BASED SOLUTIONS... IN SIX HIGH-RISK COMMUNITIES across three island states, covering HILLSIDE, RIVERBANK, MANGROVE, AND COASTAL VEGETATION RESTORATION; a recent advocacy facility awarded grants RANGING FROM $1,500 TO $8,000 to six organisations for work from recognising women in agriculture and fisheries to DOCUMENTING THE IMPACTS OF HURRICANES and advocating equitable resilience. Fifteen hundred dollars is a real grant here. Hillside and riverbank restoration is exactly the work a community does after a development has destabilised a slope. WHAT IT HAS BUILT WITH OTHERS: it convenes a regional climate justice alliance, implements a forest sector project IN PARTNERSHIP WITH two named national organisations in one island, and has run a project to STRENGTHEN THE TECHNICAL AND FINANCIAL CAPACITY OF SELECTED CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS and to improve understanding of THE INSTITUTIONAL REQUIREMENTS FOR EFFECTIVE CIVIL SOCIETY PARTICIPATION IN NATURAL RESOURCE GOVERNANCE; earlier work included SAFEGUARD[ING] WATERSHEDS THROUGH TARGETED PAYMENTS and participatory forest management across seven islands. It works through national member organisations. Find which one in your island already partners with it, and approach through them.

trackers.name: Business & Human Rights Resource Centre - invites companies to answer a community's allegation and PUBLISHES THE NON-RESPONSE on the company's own page, with regional researchers, investor escalation and published policy and benchmark data on 10,000+ companies
trackers.desc: A COMPANY'S REFUSAL TO ANSWER A COMMUNITY'S ALLEGATION IS ITSELF PUBLISHED, ON ITS OWN PAGE. The centre INVITE[S] COMPANIES TO RESPOND TO ALLEGATIONS OF MISCONDUCT AND PUBLISH[ES] THEIR COMMENTS, doing so WHEN WE FIND NO EVIDENCE THAT THEY HAVE OTHERWISE RESPONDED TO THE CONCERNS; the process ENCOURAGES COMPANIES TO PUBLICLY ADDRESS HUMAN RIGHTS CONCERNS, AND PROVIDES THE PUBLIC WITH BOTH THE ALLEGATIONS AND THE COMPANY'S COMMENTS. It states plainly: WE INDICATE RESPONSE RATES IN THE COMPANY SECTIONS OF THE SITE, and IF A COMPANY IS LISTED AS HAVING FAILED TO RESPOND TO A PARTICULAR ALLEGATION, BUT IT HAS IN FACT ISSUED A RESPONSE... PLEASE LET US KNOW. A permanent public record that the company was asked and said nothing. For a developer that presents itself as responsible to lenders and buyers, that line on its own page is a cost. THE SCALE AND WHO DOES THE ASKING: it collects evidence on MORE THAN 10,000 COMPANIES IN MORE THAN 180 COUNTRIES and takes up ALLEGED ABUSE QUICKLY AND DIRECTLY WITH COMPANIES, INVITING THEM TO RESPOND TO SPECIFIC ALLEGATIONS (OVER 1,500 PER YEAR); a network of regional researchers BUILD LONG TERM RELATIONSHIPS WITH HUMAN RIGHTS ADVOCATES ON THE GROUND, BRINGING UNDERSTANDING OF THE DYNAMICS IN THE COUNTRIES THEY COVER, and WHERE THERE IS AN ALLEGATION OF CORPORATE HUMAN RIGHTS ABUSE THAT HAS NO PUBLIC RESPONSE, THEY REACH OUT TO THE COMPANY. Its site runs in several languages including Spanish and Portuguese. There is a researcher for your region who already knows the local advocates. Send the documented allegation to them rather than to a general address. WHAT IT DOES BEYOND PUBLISHING: its recorded practice is that DIALOGUES CAN EXTEND FURTHER AND OCCASIONALLY WE TAKE AN ACTIVE ROLE IN SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES AND NGOs; in one recorded case concerning an imprisoned indigenous leader who HAD LED THE OPPOSITION TO A PROPOSED... MINE IN HIS COMMUNITY'S TERRITORY, it POSTED THE ALLEGATIONS ON OUR WEBSITE AND SOUGHT RESPONSES FROM TWO COMPANIES WHO DID NOT RESPOND, AND ASSISTED THE LOCAL VILLAGERS IN SUBMITTING THE CASE TO THE UN SPECIAL REPRESENTATIVE ON HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, then CONTACTED PUBLIC INVESTORS... AND INVITED THEM TO COMMENT, of whom two responded and ONE COMMITTED TO RAISING THE ISSUE WITH ITS CLIENTS WHO ARE INVESTED in the company. Going up the chain to the investors is the step that moves a company. Identify who holds the shares or the loan before you send the allegation, and ask that they be invited to comment too. THE HONEST NUMBERS: the centre records a response rate averaging 43% on one page and 60% on another, and its own field acknowledges criticism about WEAK AND TANGENTIAL COMPANY RESPONSES and about the LACK OF REMEDY AND THE INEQUITY IN ARMS FOR THOSE AFFECTED BY ABUSE; a published analysis notes that A COMPANY RESPONSE TO A CRITICAL CIVIL SOCIETY REPORT IS NOT NECESSARILY A POSITIVE SIGN. Roughly half of companies answer, and an answer is not a remedy. Treat this as a public record and a pressure point, not as a complaint procedure that decides anything. WHAT IT ALSO PUBLISHES ON EACH COMPANY: company pages carry news, allegations, KEY DATA POINTS BASED ON CORPORATE POLICIES, AND SCORES FROM PROMINENT CIVIL SOCIETY BENCHMARKS, and its stated goals include a SAFE AND ENABLING ENVIRONMENT IN WHICH COMMUNITIES AND WORKERS CAN ADVOCATE FOR THEIR RIGHTS AND INTERESTS, INCLUDING THROUGH FREE AND FAIR NEGOTIATIONS. Read the company's page before your first meeting with it. Its own published policies and benchmark scores are the standard you can hold it to at the table.

trackers.name: Bahamas National Trust
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: an independent statutory body created by the Bahamas National Trust Act 1959, modelled on the British National Trust and given the job of ACQUIRING LAND and managing protected areas nationwide; it now holds and runs 32 national parks covering over two million acres, and its governing council seats government, private-sector and scientific representatives. Park rules are made under section 24 of the Act, so its bylaws carry legal force on trust property. USE IT: to propose a threatened Bahamian site for national-park status or trust acquisition, and to check whether land a developer wants already sits inside a park boundary.

trackers.name: Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a regional environmental endowment established in 2012, managing an endowment plus a sinking fund for Ecosystem-based Adaptation, which it disburses mainly through partner National Conservation Trust Funds rather than directly — it helped establish several of them, including the Dominica, Grenada, Jamaica, St Kitts & Nevis, St Lucia and St Vincent funds. Its EbA window runs open calls for proposals. WHO IT SUITS: organisations doing on-the-ground ecosystem work that reduces climate vulnerability. Check whether your country has a national trust fund first — that is usually the door, and the CBF itself is the wholesaler behind it. HOW IT DIFFERS: endowment income committed for the long term, so it funds sustained protected-area management rather than a campaign. APPLY TO YOUR NATIONAL FUND, NOT TO CBF — for most of the money. CBF is a regional umbrella: at national level the partner National Conservation Trust Funds (NCTFs) lead the grantmaking process, with endowment proceeds held in country-based subaccounts and channelled through them. So for the Conservation Finance stream, the regional body is the wrong door — find your NCTF. THE EXCEPTION IS THE EbA FACILITY, which awards through competitive calls for proposals and is a direct route. THE NUMBERS: EbA medium grants USD 250,000–1 million, large grants up to USD 2 million — large by the standards of most funds here, and not aimed at a small unincorporated group acting alone. Eligible recipients expressly include NCTFs, NGOs, community-based organisations, government agencies, universities and the private sector. SCOPE CHECK: the EbA Facility covers the marine and coastal zone of the insular Caribbean, so an inland project must show its connection to marine and coastal ecosystems. IF YOU ARE TOO SMALL FOR EbA: CBF partners with GEF SGP across 12 shared countries — that is the sibling route for community-scale grants, and it is recorded separately in this map. Endowment disbursements go to NCTFs that have signed agreements with CBF, the first in 2016 with Fondo MARENA in the Dominican Republic.

trackers.name: Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund (CEPF)
trackers.desc: A FUND WHOSE SMALL-GRANT APPLICATION IS A SINGLE LETTER. CEPF (founded 2000; a joint initiative of the French Development Agency, Conservation International, the EU, the GEF, the Government of Japan, the MacArthur Foundation and the World Bank) has funded more than 2,500 grantees. FOR SMALL GRANTS THE LETTER OF INQUIRY IS THE ENTIRE APPLICATION — no longer project proposal is required — reviewed by the hotspot's Regional Implementation Team, with an offline template provided in the call's languages. Large grants go through the ConservationGrants portal and only then invite a full proposal. Reported averages: small grants around US$15,000, large around US$150,000; the small/large threshold varies by call (US$20,000 and US$50,000 both recorded), so read it. TIMING: calls run 6–8 weeks and notification comes several months after closing — but CEPF stops accepting letters once the designated funds are committed, so an open call can close early. WHO IS DISQUALIFIED: individuals cannot apply — you need a legally registered organisation with its own bank account — and government cannot apply. Community groups, farmers' cooperatives, Indigenous Peoples' organisations and women's groups all can, and CEPF welcomes first-time applicants. TWO RULES THAT SINK GOOD APPLICATIONS: your letter must aim at one single strategic direction; and site-based directions are geographically bound — community management work must be in a listed priority KBA, corridor work in a named corridor, while civil-society strengthening can be anywhere in the hotspot. THE STEP MOST PEOPLE SKIP: CEPF encourages you to contact RIT staff to discuss the idea before submitting — free, and the cheapest way to learn whether it fits.

trackers.name: BPAF is Registrar of 123 protected areas — start with the register
trackers.desc: THE FIRST PLACE TO ESTABLISH WHETHER YOUR SITE IS PROTECTED, AND UNDER WHICH LAW. The Bahamas Protected Areas Fund Act 2014 (No. 28) requires the Board to establish and maintain a Register of Protected Areas, and BPAF is the Registrar of 123 protected areas. That matters because the system draws on four different statutes: forest reserves, protected forests and conservation forests under the Forestry Act; and areas declared under the Fisheries Resources (Jurisdiction and Conservation) Act, the Bahamas National Trust Act, and the Wild Birds Protection Act. Identify which of the four applies before arguing — the powers, decision-maker and appeal route differ by statute, and the Wild Birds Protection Act is an unexpected route to area protection. THE MANDATE IS BROADER THAN PARKS: carbon sinks, water resources, wetlands, blue holes, degraded ecosystems and climate adaptation areas are all named. GOVERNANCE IS PUBLISHED AND CHECKABLE: a board of at most 11 — 5 appointed by Government, one each by the Bahamas National Trust and The Nature Conservancy, four co-opted — with 4-year maximum terms, members including expertise in law, and a stated position that only two directors are employed by, affiliated with or controlled by Government. Check that statement against the current board. Grantees include Waterkeepers Bahamas, the Bahamas National Trust and the University of The Bahamas.

trackers.name: Bahamas Protected — a coalition proposal became a gazetted expansion
trackers.desc: A DOCUMENTED PATH FROM CIVIL SOCIETY PROPOSAL TO GOVERNMENT INSTRUMENT, WITH A REALISTIC TIMESCALE. The coalition Bahamas Protected — The Nature Conservancy, the Bahamas National Trust and BREEF with national stakeholders, funded by Oceans 5 — made a written proposal to expand marine protected areas in September 2018. In July 2021 the Government gazetted an expansion adding 5,254,179 acres to the 13.9 million already protected, bringing the country to 20 percent of its marine and coastal habitat. Roughly three years from proposal to gazettal — that is the interval to plan for. THE METHOD IS COPYABLE: a marine gap analysis engaging about 40 scientists and practitioners from more than 26 organisations across three consultations, identifying priority areas of interest for further vetting — evidence assembled collectively, then a specific written ask. It also worked with the BEST Commission and the Department of Marine Resources. CONTEXT: the first Bahamian protected area dates from 1892 and the Exuma Cays Land & Sea Park (1958) was the first of its kind — a managed no-take zone. Bahamas National Trust: P.O. Box N-4105, Nassau.

trackers.name: The Bahamas' district councils, town committees and STATUTORY BOARDS FOR TOWN PLANNING appointed by the councils - monthly public meetings, statutory town area meetings, and a January budget deadline
trackers.desc: THERE IS A LOCAL STATUTORY BOARD FOR TOWN PLANNING ON EACH FAMILY ISLAND, AND ITS MEMBERS ARE APPOINTED BY THE DISTRICT COUNCIL. The local government department records that STATUTORY BOARDS WERE ESTABLISHED TO MANAGE SPECIFIC AREAS OF GOVERNANCE WITHIN THE FAMILY ISLANDS, that THESE BOARDS HAVE AUTHORITY IN AREAS SUCH AS THE PORT, ROAD TRAFFIC, TOWN PLANNING AND HOTEL LICENSING, and that they are COMPOSED OF MEMBERS APPOINTED BY THE DISTRICT COUNCIL, WHO PROVIDE GUIDANCE AND REGULATORY OVERSIGHT. Town planning and hotel licensing are decided by a board your own elected district council appoints. On an island facing a resort proposal, that appointment is the single most consequential thing the council does. THE ELECTED BODIES, AND HOW MANY PEOPLE HOLD THEM: the country is divided into local government districts — thirteen larger-island districts WITH TOWN COMMITTEES, DISTRICT COUNCILS AND STATUTORY BOARDS and a further twenty that have district councils only; the founding statute established administrators, districts, councillors and town committees so that THE VARIOUS ELECTED LEADERS could GOVERN AND OVERSEE THE AFFAIRS OF THEIR RESPECTIVE DISTRICTS WITHOUT THE INTERFERENCE OF CENTRAL GOVERNMENT, with elections EVERY THREE YEARS, ONE HUNDRED AND TEN COUNCILLORS AND TWO HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-ONE TOWN COMMITTEE MEMBERS. Nearly four hundred elected local officials across the islands, each of whom is RESPONSIBLE FOR THE PROPER USE OF PUBLIC FUNDS FOR THE MAINTENANCE AND DEVELOPMENT OF THEIR DISTRICT. On a small island that is a person you can find. THE MEETINGS AND THE PUBLIC'S PLACE IN THEM: the current statute requires that COUNCIL AND TOWN COMMITTEE MEETINGS SHALL BE HELD AT LEAST ONCE A MONTH, and provides for ADMISSION OF THE PUBLIC TO MEETINGS and for TOWN AREA MEETINGS; a member absent for THREE CONSECUTIVE MEETINGS without written consent vacates office. Councils and committees are APPROVED AUTHORITIES, with their own funds, annual budgets and appointed local government auditors, and there is a RIGHT OF APPEAL TO THE MINISTER against council decisions. A town area meeting is a statutory forum of residents, not a courtesy. Ask the committee to convene one, and note that a right of appeal exists against what the council decides. THE OFFICIAL WHO SITS AT THE CENTRE OF IT: the family island administrator works in partnership with the elected council, holds PORT AUTHORITY FUNCTIONS and COMMISSIONER FUNCTIONS under the statute, and councillors and committee members serve as EX OFFICIO JUSTICES OF THE PEACE. The administrator is the one office that touches ports, permits and public order on the island. Where a project needs a jetty or dredging, that is the desk it crosses. THE BUDGET MOMENT TO DIARISE: every town committee must, DURING THE MONTH OF JANUARY IN EACH FINANCIAL YEAR, SUBMIT TO THE COUNCIL OF THE DISTRICT ESTIMATES OF THE INCOME AND EXPENDITURE OF THE COMMITTEE for the following year. January is when the committee decides what it will spend on. A request made in December is in the estimates; one made in June waits a year.

trackers.name: Caribbean Association of Local Government Authorities - open to individual LOCAL AUTHORITIES AND MINISTRIES where no national association exists, sharing an office with the ministers' forum and the Commonwealth local government body
trackers.desc: WHERE A CARIBBEAN COUNTRY HAS NO NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF LOCAL AUTHORITIES, THE INDIVIDUAL COUNCILS AND THE MINISTRY JOIN THE REGIONAL BODY DIRECTLY. Its membership COMPRISES MAINLY NATIONAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT ASSOCIATIONS, AND, LOCAL AUTHORITIES AND MINISTRIES RESPONSIBLE FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT WHERE THERE ARE NO NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS; it is A NOT FOR PROFIT ORGANISATION ESTABLISHED TO FACILITATE THE FURTHER DEVELOPMENT OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT WITHIN THE CARIBBEAN REGION, founded in 1992 and incorporated in 2012 under the companies statute of one member country, with its secretariat accommodated by a borough corporation. A single village or town council in a country with no national association can belong in its own right. For the small islands, where local government is weakest, that is the only regional table available. WHO ACTUALLY TURNS UP: recorded meetings have brought together local government representatives from THE BAHAMAS, BELIZE, DOMINICA, GUYANA, ST LUCIA AND TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO, and a wider regional event drew central and local government from ANTIGUA AND BARBUDA, THE BAHAMAS, BELIZE, DOMINICA, GUYANA, JAMAICA, ST KITTS AND NEVIS, ST LUCIA, AND TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO, alongside private sector partners; one meeting included A TRAINING SESSION ON INSTITUTIONAL STRENGTHENING OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT SYSTEMS and a segment on women in local leadership. Nine or ten countries in one room, with a university academic who has supported the body since its founding. If your island's councils are weak, the comparison with a neighbouring island that has stronger ones is the most persuasive material available. THE PROGRAMME THAT PUT MONEY INTO LOCAL AUTHORITIES: a regional local economic development programme was A SIX-YEAR $23.2 MILLION PROJECT IN WHICH LOCAL GOVERNMENTS WILL UTILIZE ASSETS AND HUMAN CAPITAL TO STIMULATE ECONOMIC GROWTH, CREATE JOBS AND DEVELOP THE BUSINESS SECTOR, funded by a national development agency and implemented by a federation of municipalities IN PARTNERSHIP WITH the ministers' forum, this association and the commonwealth local government forum; it aimed TO PARTNER WITH 50 LOCAL GOVERNMENT AUTHORITIES TO SUPPORT THE GROWTH AND DEVELOPMENT OF 500 MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES. Fifty local authorities were partnered in one programme. Ask whether a successor programme is running, and whether your council was among the fifty — the material and contacts from it will still be in the office. THE OTHER REGIONAL BODIES BESIDE IT: a forum of local government ministers convenes the responsible ministers, and a commonwealth local government forum opened A SMALL REGIONAL OFFICE FOR THE CARIBBEAN, WHICH IS CO-LOCATED WITH this association; European funding has supported SUPPORTING AND STRENGTHENING LOCAL GOVERNMENT ASSOCIATIONS AT THE REGIONAL AND NATIONAL LEVELS, with five partnership agreements signed with local government umbrella organisations TO FURTHER SUPPORT THE CONTRIBUTION OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT TO GOVERNANCE AND ACCOUNTABILITY, ADVANCING DEVELOPMENT, AND PROMOTING GENDER EQUITY. Three regional bodies share one office. One letter reaches the association, the ministers' forum and the commonwealth body at the same address. THE HONEST HISTORY: its own background records that between 2008 and 2012 the secretariat was relocated and DURING THAT TIME NO OFFICE WAS SET UP, the presidency lapsing when its holder ceased to be a local government representative, before another government arranged accommodation for the secretariat. This body has been dormant before. Confirm it is currently staffed and meeting before routing anything important through it.

trackers.name: FLACMA - the Latin American federation of cities and municipal associations, open to affiliation by ANY INDIVIDUAL MUNICIPALITY, whose assembly passes resolutions signed by mayors across eighteen countries
trackers.desc: ANY CITY OR MUNICIPALITY IN THE REGION MAY AFFILIATE DIRECTLY, NOT ONLY THROUGH ITS NATIONAL ASSOCIATION. Its membership rule is that MEMBERS ARE ALL THE CITIES, MUNICIPALITIES, NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND MUNICIPALIST INSTITUTIONS OF LATIN AMERICA THAT HAVE EXPRESSED THEIR WILL TO AFFILIATE; it is AN ORGANISATION OF FREE ADHESION THAT REPRESENTS THE 16,132 MUNICIPALITIES, INTENDANCIES AND PREFECTURES, THE CITIES AND THE ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, NETWORKS AND GUILDS OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, and it is the regional section of the world organisation of local governments. A single municipality may join in its own right. Where your national association is captured or inactive, that is a way for one sympathetic town hall to reach the regional table on its own. WHOSE PRESIDENTS SIT ON IT: its published leadership is drawn from the presidents of the national municipal bodies of the region — the federation of municipalities of one southern country, the association of municipalities of another, the Brazilian association of municipalities, the congress of intendants of another, the national federation of municipalities of one large federal country and the association of municipalities of an Andean one — each of them a serving mayor. The people who chair your own national municipal association sit here. A matter raised through that association can be carried into a regional assembly by the same person. WHAT IT SAYS IT IS FOR: TO BE THE VOICE OF LATIN AMERICAN MUNICIPALISM, TO CONSOLIDATE THE LATIN AMERICAN MUNICIPAL ASSOCIATIVE MOVEMENT, TO REPRESENT AND SERVE AS INTERLOCUTOR OF ALL THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND THEIR NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES, and TO PROMOTE IN LATIN AMERICA AUTONOMOUS, STRONG AND DEMOCRATIC LOCAL GOVERNMENTS; it ADHERES TO AND PROMOTES THE WORLD AND REGIONAL CONVENTIONS THAT THE NATIONAL STATES OF THE REGION SUBSCRIBE. Promoting the conventions the states have signed is written into its purpose. Where your country has signed an environmental or rights convention and a municipality is being told to ignore it, that is a body with a standing commitment to the opposite. THE PRECEDENT THAT SHOWS IT TAKES POSITIONS: its general assembly has approved unanimously a declaration on a territorial sovereignty dispute, signed by the president and BY MUNICIPAL AUTHORITIES AND HEADS OF ASSOCIATIONS AND FEDERATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES of eighteen named countries of the region, which also REAFFIRMED THE LEGITIMATE RIGHTS... OVER THE NATURAL RESOURCES OF THE AREA IN QUESTION. The assembly passes resolutions that name natural resources and get signed by mayors across eighteen countries. A community campaign that can be framed as a municipal cause has a forum that has done exactly that before. THE OTHER REGIONAL NETWORKS BESIDE IT: regional analysis names, among the principal associations and networks of local and regional governments with EXPERIENCES, IDEAS AND RESOURCES TO FOSTER INITIATIVES AND PROJECTS LINKED TO SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AT LOCAL LEVEL, a network of Mercosur cities alongside this federation, and global initiatives with regional presence for local sustainability and for city climate action; various cities have prepared VOLUNTARY LOCAL REPORTS on implementing the global development agenda in their territories. A voluntary local report is a document a municipality writes about itself. Getting your community's situation named in one is cheap, public and lasting. THE HONEST NOTE ON REPRESENTATION: the region's representation in the world body has been the subject of negotiations between this federation, the Mercosur cities network and the world organisation to form A LATIN AMERICAN REPRESENTATION THAT IS PLURAL, DIVERSE AND PARTICIPATORY. More than one body claims to speak for the region's municipalities. Approach both this federation and the Mercosur cities network rather than assuming one covers the other.

trackers.name: ICLEI - a sustainability network open to individual councils AND to associations of local governments, giving fee-paying members year-round telephone and email support on designing environment and water projects, plus local biodiversity planning tools and an environmental award
trackers.desc: MEMBERSHIP OF THIS GLOBAL SUSTAINABILITY NETWORK IS OPEN TO ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AS WELL AS TO INDIVIDUAL COUNCILS, AND THE FEE SCALES WITH POPULATION AND NATIONAL INCOME. Its membership page states that AFFILIATION IS OPEN TO ALL LOCAL AND REGIONAL GOVERNMENTS, AS WELL AS TO THEIR WORLD, REGIONAL, NATIONAL AND SUBNATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS, that members MAY VOTE AND PARTICIPATE IN THE GOVERNING ORGANS OF THE WHOLE NETWORK, and that they CONTRIBUTE AN ANNUAL AFFILIATION FEE THAT VARIES REGIONALLY AND ACCORDING TO POPULATION AND GROSS NATIONAL INCOME PER CAPITA. A small municipality pays a small fee and votes in the same network as a capital city. Where a national association is the member, ask whether your council is covered by it already. WHAT A MEMBER ACTUALLY GETS, IN THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT'S OWN WORDS: it SUPPORTS ITS PARTNERS TO FIND SUSTAINABLE SOLUTIONS THROUGH PROJECTS, INITIATIVES AND PROGRAMMES, offers cities and states A PLATFORM TO INTERACT WITH OTHER LOCAL GOVERNMENTS and provides RESOURCES AND TOOLS TO PROMOTE POSITIVE ENVIRONMENTAL, ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL CHANGES; support runs DURING THE YEAR THAT THE FEE LASTS, PERMANENTLY, BY TELEPHONE OR BY EMAIL, and covers THE DESIGN OF PROGRAMMES AND PROJECTS OF SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN THEMES SUCH AS: ENVIRONMENT, WATER, PUBLIC SERVICES, ENERGY EFFICIENCY, SOLID WASTE. Joining requires A REQUEST TO THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT addressed to the named regional secretary, plus a membership form. Permanent telephone and email support on designing water and environment projects, for one annual fee. That is a standing technical helpline for a town hall that has none. THE BIODIVERSITY WORK THAT MATTERS FOR LAND: its recorded local biodiversity work is TO PROMOTE THE BIODIVERSITY STRATEGIES OF THE STATE AND MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENTS, AS WELL AS THEIR ACTION PLANS, AND ALSO TO REINFORCE THE CAPACITIES OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS TO INCORPORATE BIODIVERSITY INTO THE PLANNING PROCESSES, and it notes that MORE MONETARY RESOURCES ARE INVESTED GLOBALLY IN BIODIVERSITY AT LOCAL AND SUBNATIONAL LEVEL THAN AT NATIONAL LEVELS; a member municipality has launched an urban biodiversity index, and a global initiative on NATURE IN URBAN PLANNING is promoted through the network. Incorporating biodiversity into planning processes is the exact point at which a project is stopped or waved through. Ask the secretariat which of its tools your municipality can adopt in its next plan revision. THE RECOGNITION THAT GIVES A COUNCIL A REASON: the regional secretariat runs an award for local governments THAT HAVE CARRIED OUT ACTIONS IN FAVOUR OF THE PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT IN THEMES OF CLIMATE CHANGE, BIODIVERSITY, ENERGY EFFICIENCY, MOBILITY, AMONG OTHERS, open to municipalities, city boroughs and federal entities. An award with a biodiversity category. A council weighing whether to protect a site has a public reason to do so, and the application is a deadline you can work to. THE OFFICES THAT COVER THIS REGION: there is a secretariat for one large federal country together with Central America and the Caribbean, and a separate South American secretariat, each publishing member lists that include municipalities of several countries. Two regional offices cover the whole file. Write to the one for your subregion rather than to the global body.

trackers.name: Fundación DEMUCA - a foundation for strengthening local governments across Central America and the Caribbean, working through the national municipal associations, with a work line covering ENVIRONMENTAL AND RISK MANAGEMENT and cohorts of twenty municipalities
trackers.desc: A FOUNDATION EXISTS WHOSE WHOLE PURPOSE IS STRENGTHENING LOCAL GOVERNMENTS IN CENTRAL AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, AND IT WORKS THROUGH THE NATIONAL MUNICIPAL ASSOCIATIONS. It is described as AN INSTRUMENT OF TECHNICAL AND FINANCIAL COOPERATION of a national development agency THAT PROMOTES THE STRENGTHENING OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS IN CENTRAL AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, its work focused on THE DESIGN OF STRATEGIES AND THE EXECUTION OF NATIONAL AND REGIONAL PROJECTS AIMED AT IMPROVING THE MANAGEMENT CAPABILITIES OF MUNICIPALITIES AND THEIR VARIOUS FORMS OF ASSOCIATION; it SUPPORTS THE NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF MUNICIPALITIES IN THE GENERATION OF STRATEGIC POLICY PROPOSALS and COLLABORATES IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPROVEMENT OF THE MEANS AND INSTRUMENTS OF ADMINISTRATION OF LOCAL GOVERNMENTS. It is a foundation constituted under the law of one member country in 1995, with a delegation registered in the cooperating country. Where a national municipal association is weak, this is the body that funds and staffs its policy work. Ask your association what it currently receives, and whether your municipality is in the next cohort. THE THREE WORK LINES, ONE OF WHICH COVERS ENVIRONMENT: the cooperation is channelled through this foundation in three lines — TAX REFORM AT LOCAL LEVEL, TO STRENGTHEN THE FINANCIAL CAPACITY OF THE MUNICIPALITIES WITH THEIR OWN RESOURCES TO IMPLEMENT THEIR POLICIES; implementation of the municipal administrative career statute FOR THE STABILITY OF THE HUMAN RESOURCE AND OF THE MUNICIPAL PLANS; and STRENGTHENING OF CAPACITIES OF THE MUNICIPALITIES AND ASSOCIATIONS, TO PROMOTE MUNICIPAL ASSOCIATIVISM, LOCAL ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, POLICIES AND PLANS OF EQUALITY, ENVIRONMENTAL AND RISK MANAGEMENT, STRENGTHENING OF THE SOCIAL FABRIC AND THE PREVENTION OF VIOLENCE. Environmental and risk management sits inside the third line, alongside strengthening the social fabric. A request framed as municipal capacity on environmental management fits the existing programme rather than asking for something new. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DELIVERS, FROM RECORDED EXAMPLES: with a national municipalities corporation and a state municipal development institute it launched a second phase of implementation FOR 20 NEW MUNICIPALITIES AT NATIONAL LEVEL; TO WHICH TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE WILL BE GIVEN TO STRENGTHEN THEIR CAPACITIES through LABOUR TECHNIFICATION, PERMANENT TRAINING AND THE CREATION, DESIGN AND APPLICATION OF TOOLS AND INSTRUMENTS; it co-published a guide for the internal functioning of plural municipal councils; and it produced a model to improve municipal tax management, described by its own technician as A SIMPLE GUIDE DIRECTED TO STRENGTHENING MUNICIPAL AUTONOMY, WHICH CAN BE IMPLEMENTED WITHOUT HAVING EXTERNAL TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, piloted in ten named municipalities with external financing of twenty-seven thousand dollars. Twenty municipalities in one cohort, and a tax guide a town hall can apply on its own. Both are the kind of thing a small municipality can be nominated for without a budget of its own. THE REGIONAL BODY IT SITS BESIDE: the federation of municipalities of the Central American isthmus is one of the organisations from which the Latin American municipal federation was formed, and has appeared as a regional counterpart in municipal research and in Mesoamerican biological corridor work. Verify whether that federation is currently active before relying on it; the foundation above is the better documented door at present.

trackers.name: The GEF Small Grants Programme - grants of up to $50,000 DIRECT to community organisations, with a national coordinator in each country who helps write the concept paper, planning grants, and a companion window of up to $300,000
trackers.desc: THERE IS A NAMED NATIONAL COORDINATOR IN YOUR COUNTRY WHOSE JOB INCLUDES HELPING YOU WRITE THE APPLICATION. The programme's own procedure is that THE PROJECT PROPONENT — A NATIONAL CBO OR NGO — CONTACTS THE SGP NATIONAL COORDINATOR TO RECEIVE PROJECT APPLICATION GUIDELINES AND FORMS, and that WITH ASSISTANCE FROM THE NATIONAL COORDINATOR, THE PROPONENT PREPARES A BRIEF PROJECT CONCEPT PAPER; the coordinator pre-screens it, and if eligible the proponent prepares a full proposal — IN SOME CASES, THIS STEP MAY BE SUPPORTED BY A PLANNING GRANT — which goes to a national steering committee that accepts, rejects or returns it for further work. A planning grant to write the proposal, and an official whose job is to help you write it. Contact the coordinator before drafting anything, because the concept paper is short and they will tell you whether it fits. WHAT IT PAYS AND TO WHOM: the programme PROVIDES GRANTS OF UP TO $50,000 DIRECTLY TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES INCLUDING INDIGENOUS PEOPLE, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS AND OTHER NON-GOVERNMENTAL GROUPS, for projects in BIODIVERSITY, CLIMATE CHANGE MITIGATION AND ADAPTATION, LAND DEGRADATION AND SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT, INTERNATIONAL WATERS AND CHEMICALS, with SPECIAL CONSIDERATION FOR INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, WOMEN, AND YOUTH; it COMPLEMENTS THE LARGE AND MEDIUM-SIZED facility funding BY PROVIDING A WINDOW FOR THE DIRECT PARTICIPATION OF NGOs, LOCAL COMMUNITIES, AND OTHER GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS. Since 1992 it has supported CLOSE TO 30,000 GRANTS, ADMINISTERING $1.54 BILLION... ACROSS 136 COUNTRIES. Fifty thousand dollars, paid direct to a community organisation, on biodiversity or land degradation. That is the largest routine sum in this file available without an intermediary. HOW IT IS RUN LOCALLY: it operates IN A DECENTRALIZED AND COUNTRY-DRIVEN MANNER THROUGH COUNTRY PROGRAM TEAMS COMPOSED OF A NATIONAL COORDINATOR, OFTEN A PROGRAM ASSISTANT, AND A NATIONAL STEERING COMMITTEE IN EACH PARTICIPATING COUNTRY, each country publishing a country programme strategy that proposals must align with. In one small island state an operational phase was advertised with A GRANTS PORTFOLIO OF APPROXIMATELY US$750,000... FOR COMMUNITY-BASED ENVIRONMENTAL PROJECTS. Download your country's programme strategy before writing. Proposals are judged against that document, and it names the priorities and often the specific landscapes. THE THREE AGENCIES THAT NOW RUN IT: the core programme is implemented by a development programme, an agriculture organisation and a conservation organisation, the second bringing expertise in AGRICULTURE, FISHERIES, FORESTRY, BIOENERGY, CLIMATE-RESILIENT PRACTICES, LIVESTOCK, AND LAND & WATER to thirteen countries; national coordinator posts in some small states are contracted through the conservation organisation, working alongside a Caribbean islands biodiversity hotspot fund. Which agency runs your country's programme changes who you write to. Check the country page rather than assuming it is the development programme. THE LARGER WINDOW BESIDE IT: a civil society challenge programme led by a conservation union SUPPORTS COMPETITIVE OPPORTUNITIES FOR LOCAL CSOs TO ACCESS FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL RESOURCES TO SCALE UP INNOVATIVE ENVIRONMENTAL SOLUTIONS, OFFERING GRANTS OF UP TO $300,000. Three hundred thousand for an organisation that has already proved something small works. Treat the fifty-thousand grant as the step that qualifies you for it.

trackers.name: Protection grants for defenders at risk - up to €7,500 for LEGAL FEES OF THOSE BEING JUDICIALLY HARASSED, physical and digital security, medical and family costs, with a 24-hour hotline, plus emergency, relocation, trial-monitoring and respite programmes
trackers.desc: THESE GRANTS PAY THE LEGAL FEES OF SOMEONE BEING SUED OR PROSECUTED FOR DEFENDING LAND. The protection grants programme, launched in 2001 TO PROVIDE RAPID AND PRACTICAL FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS AT RISK, pays for IMPROVING PHYSICAL SECURITY OF AN ORGANISATION OR INDIVIDUAL, DIGITAL SECURITY AND COMMUNICATION SECURITY; SUPPORTING LEGAL FEES FOR HRDs WHO ARE BEING JUDICIALLY HARASSED; PAYING FOR MEDICAL FEES FOR HRDs WHO HAVE BEEN ATTACKED OR WHO HAVE SUFFERED A MEDICAL CONDITION AS A RESULT OF THEIR PEACEFUL HUMAN RIGHTS ACTIVITIES; PROVIDING FAMILY ASSISTANCE FOR IMPRISONED HRDs OR FAMILY MEMBERS WHO ARE AT RISK BECAUSE OF A HRD'S ACTIVITIES, up to a maximum of €7,500. Applications CAN BE SUBMITTED ANYTIME VIA THEIR ONLINE SYSTEM, and there is a 24-HOUR EMERGENCY HOTLINE. A criminal complaint or a defamation suit filed by a developer is judicial harassment, and the legal fees are payable. That is the single most common attack on land defenders in this file, and this is the grant written for it. WHAT IT WILL NOT FUND, WHICH DECIDES HOW YOU WRITE IT: the programme excludes RETROSPECTIVE FUNDING, INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS, ORGANISATIONS THAT HAVE APPLIED OR ARE ALREADY RECEIVING FUNDING FOR THE SAME PURPOSE ELSEWHERE, PROJECTS WHICH FOCUS ON BROADER HUMAN RIGHTS ISSUES RATHER THAN THE SPECIFIC SITUATION OF HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, COSTS FOR HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS WHO ARE ALREADY IN EXILE and ongoing office running costs; grants ARE GENERALLY NOT AWARDED FOR 100% OF THE PROPOSED BUDGET, and applicants must commit to return the grant if the work does not go ahead or is funded elsewhere. Write about the named people at risk, not about the campaign. A proposal that describes the environmental issue rather than the threat to specific defenders is refused on its own terms. THE OTHER EMERGENCY FUNDS THAT COVER THE SAME GROUND: a European defenders mechanism provides EMERGENCY GRANTS UP TO 10,000€ and runs a TEMPORARY RELOCATION PROGRAMME that funds a host organisation to relocate a defender, responding to AN INCREASED RISK, AN ANTICIPATED INCREASED RISK OR FOR A HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDER WHO HAS BEEN WORKING IN A DIFFICULT ENVIRONMENT FOR A PROLONGED PERIOD OF TIME AND WHO NEEDS A BREAK, covering REST AND RESPITE, PROFESSIONAL CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT... EMOTIONAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL WELL-BEING, FAMILY SUPPORT; a civil society lifeline fund covers LEGAL REPRESENTATION, PRISON VISITS, TRIAL MONITORING, TEMPORARY RELOCATION, EQUIPMENT REPLACEMENT, applying by email after describing a secure contact method, in several languages including Spanish; and a federation offers SECURE TRANSPORTATION, LEGAL SUPPORT, MEDICAL SUPPORT... HUMANITARIAN ASSISTANCE... URGENT RELOCATION, URGENT MONITORING. Trial monitoring is fundable, and so is a paid observer at the hearing. Where a case is being heard in a small town, an outside monitor changes how it is conducted. THE RESPITE OPTIONS WHEN SOMEONE MUST LEAVE: recorded schemes include a protective fellowship allowing UP TO TEN DEFENDERS PER YEAR to join a university centre FOR THE PURPOSES OF TRAINING, NETWORKING, AND REST, a foundation offering A YEAR LONG RESPITE PROGRAMME, a refuge for journalists forced to flee providing ADMINISTRATIVE, LEGAL AND SOCIAL ASSISTANCE, and a cities of refuge network offering PHYSICAL SAFETY AND ECONOMIC SECURITY FOR A TWO-YEARS FIXED PERIOD. Leaving for a year is not the end of a campaign if someone else can hold the file. Identify who that is before the threat arrives, because these programmes take applications from the person at risk and their host, not from a court. THE SECURITY WARNING BUILT INTO THE APPLICATION: applicants are asked to ENSURE THAT THE METHOD OF CONTACT YOU ARE PROVIDING IS SECURE AND THAT IT IS OK TO BE CONTACTED IN THAT WAY, and one fund asks applicants to describe HOW it CAN CONTACT YOU SECURELY BEFORE SENDING SENSITIVE INFORMATION. Do not send the details from a shared community email account. The application itself can expose the person it is meant to protect.

trackers.name: RedLAC - the network of 32 national and regional ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS in 20 countries, permanent conservation trust institutions financing protected areas and local communities, with a published member list by country and zone
trackers.desc: THIRTY-TWO NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS IN TWENTY COUNTRIES, AND THE NETWORK PUBLISHES WHICH ONE COVERS YOURS. It GROUPS 32 ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS FROM 20 COUNTRIES OF THE REGION, UNITING EFFORTS TO PROTECT THE RICH BIODIVERSITY OF LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, with its member list filterable by zone — Caribbean, Mesoamerica and South America — alongside regional funds; more than twenty-five years old, it counts MORE THAN 100 ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS WORLDWIDE. Find the fund for your country on that member page. These are permanent national institutions with endowments, not project offices that close when a grant ends. WHAT THESE FUNDS DO, IN THE NETWORK'S WORDS: they HAVE DEMONSTRATED TO BE A KEY MECHANISM IN THE SUSTAINABLE FINANCING OF BIODIVERSITY AND IN THE STRENGTHENING OF PROTECTED AREAS AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, with a role in THE PROTECTION OF NATURAL AREAS AND THE SUPPORT TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES, described as MULTIDIMENSIONAL FUNDS, WITH APPROACHES THAT INTEGRATE PROTECTION OF BIODIVERSITY, CLIMATIC RESILIENCE AND COMMUNITY EMPOWERMENT. Support to local communities is named alongside protected areas. A community managing land next to a park is inside the mandate, not adjacent to it. SOME OF THE MEMBERS BY NAME AND KIND: recorded members include a Caribbean biodiversity fund, a national forever-protection association in one Central American country, an action fund and a Pacific foundation in one Andean country, a nature fund in one southern country, an island life fund and a regional marine fund — the last two showing that funds exist for a single archipelago and for a shared sea as well as for whole countries. There are funds scoped to one archipelago and to one reef system. If your site sits in either, that narrower fund is a better fit than the national one. WHAT THE NETWORK ITSELF OFFERS ITS MEMBERS: joining gives funds THE OPPORTUNITY TO CONNECT AND COLLABORATE WITH OTHER MEMBERS OF THE NETWORK THROUGHOUT THE REGION, to SHARE KNOWLEDGE, RESOURCES AND EXPERIENCES TO IMPROVE THEIR CAPACITIES, and ACCESS TO A WIDE VARIETY OF RESOURCES AND TOOLS, with TRAINING AND ADVICE ON DIVERSE THEMES, FROM PROJECT MANAGEMENT TO COMMUNICATION AND ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION. Where your country has no environmental fund, this network is where one would be built, and it trains new members. That is a long project, but it is the route. WHY THEY MATTER FOR PERMANENT PROTECTION: these funds are conservation trust funds — institutions holding capital whose returns finance protected areas and community work year after year, and the network works alongside a global environment facility, an African funds consortium and a large conservation finance initiative on that model. An endowment pays for wardens and monitoring long after a campaign ends. Where a protected area has just been declared, the next question is which of these funds can endow its running costs.

trackers.name: Global Forest Watch - free near-real-time deforestation alerts by email for any drawn area, an offline field app that walks patrols to the clearing, and a small grants fund whose examples include GETTING CONCESSIONS REVOKED and compiling evidence for formal complaints
trackers.desc: YOU CAN SUBSCRIBE TO EMAIL ALERTS FOR A SINGLE PLOT OF FOREST AND BE TOLD WITHIN DAYS WHEN TREES ARE CUT. The platform is FREE AND SIMPLE TO USE, ENABLING ANYONE TO CREATE CUSTOM MAPS, ANALYZE FOREST TRENDS, SUBSCRIBE TO ALERTS, OR DOWNLOAD DATA FOR THEIR LOCAL AREA OR THE ENTIRE WORLD, providing NEAR-REAL-TIME ALERTS SHOWING SUSPECTED LOCATIONS OF RECENT TREE COVER LOSS; it moved BEYOND ANNUAL DATA ON FORESTS to MONTHLY AND WEEKLY DEFORESTATION ALERTS, with EMAIL SUBSCRIPTIONS bringing them DIRECTLY INTO THE HANDS OF USERS. Users CAN SIGN UP FOR ALERTS AND DOWNLOAD DATASETS WITHOUT ANY SUBSCRIPTION OR LICENSING FEE. Draw the boundary of the land you are defending and subscribe. From then on the clearing tells you rather than the other way round, and the date stamp is independent of anything the developer says. THE FIELD APP THAT WORKS WITHOUT SIGNAL: a companion mobile application ALLOWS RANGERS TO ACCESS the data and alerts OFFLINE, WHICH IS CRITICAL IN AREAS WITH LIMITED TO NO CELL SIGNAL; USING CACHED DATA, THE APP DIRECTS USERS TO NEARBY FOREST CLEARING AND ENABLES THEM TO CAPTURE PHOTOS AND FILL OUT FORMS ABOUT DEFORESTATION, WHICH ARE UPLOADED NEXT TIME THEIR DEVICE CONNECTS, so that patrols KNOW EXACTLY WHERE TO LOOK... AND STOP THE ILLEGAL ACTIVITY BEFORE IT GETS OUT OF CONTROL; it is FREE, OPEN SOURCE, AND AVAILABLE IN ENGLISH, SPANISH, PORTUGUESE, FRENCH, AND BAHASA INDONESIAN. The alert gives the coordinates and the app walks you to them. A ground photograph taken at a satellite-flagged point, on a known date, is the evidence a prosecutor can use. THE GRANT ATTACHED TO IT, AND WHAT IT HAS PAID FOR: a small grants fund SEEKS TO BUILD THE CAPACITY OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS TO EFFECTIVELY USE the tools TO REDUCE ILLEGAL OR UNPLANNED DEFORESTATION; funded project types include USING DATA AND IMAGERY... ALONGSIDE COMMUNITY TERRITORIAL MAPS TO ADVOCATE FOR LAND TITLES AND OTHER STRENGTHENED LAND RIGHTS; CROWDSOURCING, COMPILING AND PUBLISHING DATA ON CONCESSIONS THAT OVERLAP WITH ANCESTRAL COMMUNITY LANDS, AND SUPPORT COMMUNITIES IN APPLYING PUBLIC PRESSURE TO GET THESE CONCESSIONS REVOKED; DEVELOPING THE CAPACITY OF FOREST MONITORING BRIGADES TO CONDUCT FIELD VERIFICATIONS OF NEAR-REAL TIME ALERTS; and SUPPORTING INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES IN DEVELOPING RESPONSE PROTOCOLS, FORMULATING LEGAL STRATEGIES AND COMPILING EVIDENCE OF ILLEGAL DEFORESTATION INCLUDING SATELLITE IMAGERY, DATA AND ANALYSES, AND SUBMITTING IT TO LAW ENFORCEMENT THROUGH FORMAL COMPLAINTS OR OTHER LEGAL PROCESSES. Getting concessions revoked and compiling evidence for formal complaints are funded project types, written into the fund's own examples. That is the grant to cite when describing what you intend to do. THE DEADLINE DISCIPLINE: the fund runs an annual call, and the platform states of a recent round: THE CALL FOR APPLICATIONS HAS CLOSED AS OF THE DEADLINE... WE CANNOT GRANT ANY EXTENSIONS, advising applicants to PREPARE FOR THE NEXT CALL FOR APPLICATIONS BY REVIEWING the current materials, while noting that SOME ITEMS IN THE GUIDELINES FOR APPLICANTS MAY CHANGE YEAR TO YEAR. One deadline a year, strictly enforced. Download this year's guidelines now and write the proposal before the next call opens. WHO ELSE IS ALREADY USING IT: the platform serves GOVERNMENTS, THE PRIVATE SECTOR, NGOs, JOURNALISTS, UNIVERSITIES, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC, and is convened as a partnership of OVER 200 ORGANIZATIONS; a fellowship accompanies the grants. Your municipality and your national forest agency can subscribe to the same alerts you do. Sending them the alert with a covering letter turns your observation into their file.

trackers.name: Public Lab and the open science hardware community - free open-source, low-cost instruments and toolkits communities build themselves for water, air, soil and land use, plus BALLOON AND KITE AERIAL MAPPING with stitching software and an open question forum
trackers.desc: THE INSTRUMENTS ARE OPEN SOURCE AND CHEAP ENOUGH THAT A COMMUNITY CAN BUILD ITS OWN, INCLUDING AERIAL PHOTOGRAPHY FROM A KITE. The network is DEVOTED TO EMPOWERING COMMUNITIES AND CITIZEN SCIENTISTS TO MONITOR THEIR OWN ENVIRONMENTS THROUGH THE USE OF INEXPENSIVE DIY TECHNIQUES, hosting AN IMPRESSIVE CATALOG OF OPEN SOURCE TOOLKITS... RANGING FROM WATER QUALITY SENSORS TO INDOOR AIR QUALITY AND KITE MAPPING KITS; its tools and data are CREATED BY THE community, OPEN SOURCE, AND TYPICALLY INEXPENSIVE TO USE. Its earliest technique was LOW-ALTITUDE AERIAL MAPPING WITH BALLOONS AND KITES with software to stitch the photographs into a map. A kite, a camera and free stitching software produce a dated aerial photograph of a site at a resolution no public satellite gives you. That is how you show what a hillside looked like before the machines arrived. WHY IT EXISTS, AND WHAT THAT PRECEDENT MEANS: it was founded in 2010 FOLLOWING THE BP OIL DISASTER IN THE GULF OF MEXICO... TO ADDRESS AN ENORMOUS GAP IN COMMUNITY KNOWLEDGE ABOUT THE IMPACTS OF THE SPILL, launching AS AN OPEN SOURCE PLATFORM, COLLECTING DATA AND MAPS OF THE COASTLINE OVER TIME TO SHOW THE COAST BEFORE, DURING, AND AFTER THE SPILL. Before, during and after is the sequence that wins arguments about damage. Start the baseline photographs now, while there is still a before. WHAT THE PLATFORM ACTUALLY GIVES YOU: it is A PLATFORM FOR COMMUNITY SCIENCE PRACTITIONERS WORKING ON ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES TO DOCUMENT THEIR WORK, SHARE TOOLS FOR ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING AND ADVOCACY, AND CONNECT WITH EACH OTHER; THE COMMUNITY IS OPEN AND FREE FOR ANYONE TO JOIN, members CAN ADD THEIR OWN PROJECT PAGE TO DOCUMENT THEIR METHODS AND SHARE EXPERTISE, and users CAN BROWSE LOW-COST ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING TOOLS FOR APPLICATION AREAS SUCH AS AIR QUALITY, LAND USE, STORMWATER, alongside ADVOCACY METHODS, AND ACTION TOOLKITS BY SCIENCE TOPICS covering WATER, SOIL, AIR, INDUSTRY, CLIMATE, ORGANIZING, AND MONITORING; COMMUNITY MEMBERS CAN ASK OR ANSWER QUESTIONS. Post the question with your site's details. Somebody has usually measured the same pollutant with the same cheap instrument and will say what went wrong the first time. THE KINDS OF INSTRUMENT PEOPLE HAVE BUILT: recorded tools include a spectrometer made from LEGO OR CARDBOARD, WEBCAMS OR RASPBERRY PI CAMERAS, RECYCLED DVDs so that SPECTROSCOPY IS A RESEARCH METHOD THAT ANYONE CAN EXPLORE; a SIMPLE AIR SENSOR whose REALTIME READOUT CHANGES COLOR WHEN THE SENSOR READS DIFFERENCES IN AIR QUALITY, usable WITHOUT HAVING TO LEARN HOW TO PROGRAM; a low-budget water kit with probes MEASURING TEMPERATURE, DISSOLVED OXYGEN AND CONDUCTIVITY, developed to measure sewage outfalls after storms; a DIY device to TEST FOR HEAVY METALS IN WATER; DIY infrared cameras; and a marine microplastics trawler. Dissolved oxygen, conductivity and heavy metals are the readings that show a river has been damaged. A community that takes them weekly for a year has a record no consultant's single sample can rebut. WHAT THE WIDER COMMUNITY ADDS: a water data collaborative HELPS GUIDE COMMUNITY GROUPS ON HOW TO ADOPT DIY, OPEN HARDWARE METHODS FOR COLLECTING THE QUALITY OF WATER DATA THEY NEED TO ACHIEVE THEIR OUTCOMES, alongside research centres publishing open hardware loggers, and an annual gathering for open science hardware makes tools ACCESSIBLE THROUGH OPEN-SOURCE LICENSING; recorded projects include WATER MONITORING IN THE AMAZON. Decide what outcome the data is for before choosing the instrument. A reading that will go to a court needs a different protocol from one that will go to a public meeting, and these groups will tell you which.

trackers.name: Accountability Counsel - free support for communities complaining to the accountability offices of banks financing a harmful project, taking cases ONLY WHERE THE COMMUNITY ASKS, plus a searchable global complaints database and a resource guide
trackers.desc: IT ONLY TAKES CASES WHERE THE COMMUNITY ASKS FIRST, AND IT SAYS WHY. It states: TO ENSURE THAT WE DO NOT REPLICATE THE POWER DYNAMIC WE SEEK TO UPEND AND ARE A TRUSTED, WANTED PARTNER IN COMMUNITIES, WE ONLY TAKE CASES IN WHICH COMMUNITIES REQUEST OUR SUPPORT; assistance BEGINS WITH A REQUEST FOR SUPPORT FROM THE COMMUNITY ITSELF OR A LOCAL CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATION, and NEARLY ALL CASES COME TO US THROUGH REFERRALS THROUGH CIVIL SOCIETY NETWORKS, OFTEN WITH ONLY ONE OR TWO DEGREES OF SEPARATION; it asks that a case INVOLVE A TRUSTWORTHY LOCAL PARTNER WITH WHOM WE CAN CLOSELY COLLABORATE, and weighs THE LIKELIHOOD OF A COMPLAINT LEADING TO A POSITIVE RESULT AT THE COMMUNITY LEVEL and of CREATING SYSTEMIC CHANGE AT THE INSTITUTIONAL LEVEL. Ask through an organisation that already knows you. One or two degrees of separation is the stated norm, so the introduction matters more than the application. WHAT IT DOES: it ASSIST[S] COMMUNITIES TO DEFEND THEIR RIGHTS THROUGH COMPLAINTS TO ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICES TIED TO PROJECTS THAT CAUSE HARM, specialising in NON-JUDICIAL COMPLAINT OFFICES ESTABLISHED TO RECEIVE COMMUNITY COMPLAINTS; its case work RANGES FROM INTENSIVE AND COMPREHENSIVE ASSISTANCE TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND THEIR PARTNERS THROUGHOUT A COMPLAINT PROCESS, TO PROVIDING MORE TARGETED SUPPORT WITH DAILY CASE WORK CONDUCTED PRIMARILY BY LOCAL PARTNERS, and it CONDUCT[S] TRAININGS IN LOCAL COMMUNITIES ABOUT ALL OPTIONS FOR ADDRESSING HUMAN RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL ABUSES ASSOCIATED WITH INTERNATIONALLY FINANCED PROJECTS. A complaint to a bank's own accountability office runs alongside any court case rather than replacing it. Ask for the training even if you never file: it maps every route available against a financed project. WHAT IT HAS ACHIEVED, INCLUDING IN THIS REGION: recorded results include supporting communities TO PREVENT ABUSES IN MEXICO and elsewhere, TO COMPEL REDESIGN OF A PROJECT in one country and TO REACH HISTORIC AGREEMENTS in others including one Caribbean state; its impact includes REDESIGNED PROJECTS THAT NOW REFLECT COMMUNITY NEEDS, HARM STOPPED AND PREVENTED TO DEFEND WATER RESOURCES, AND AGREEMENTS RESULTING IN COMPENSATION. Redesign, prevention and compensation are the realistic outcomes. A complaint of this kind rarely cancels a project outright, and knowing that before starting keeps a community's expectations intact. THE DATABASE AND GUIDE ANYONE CAN USE: it runs THE WORLD'S MOST COMPREHENSIVE COMMUNITY COMPLAINT DATABASE — SEARCH BY REGION, SECTOR, INSTITUTION, TYPE OF HARM, and a comparison of accountability policies ACROSS SIXTEEN INSTITUTIONS; its resource guide contains INFORMATION ABOUT TOOLS FOR REDRESSING HUMAN RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL VIOLATIONS BY INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS, EXPORT PROMOTION AGENCIES, AND PRIVATE CORPORATE ACTORS, intended TO ASSIST COMMUNITY LEADERS, LAWYERS, NGOs, AND INDIVIDUALS IN DETERMINING WHAT RIGHTS THEY HAVE AND HOW TO FILE A COMPLAINT, and it also covers INFORMATION DISCLOSURE RULES at those institutions. Search the database for your sector before writing anything. Someone has complained about a comparable project and the outcome tells you what to ask for. WHICH OFFICES EXIST, AND WHERE THE GAPS ARE: the offices it works with include those of the regional development bank for this continent, the world bank's public and private arms, a climate fund, a development programme's compliance unit and one national development bank's ombudsperson; it records that THERE ARE MANY COMMUNITIES THAT LACK AN AVAILABLE ACCOUNTABILITY OPTION BECAUSE NO SUCH ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICE EXISTS AT THE INSTITUTION(S) FINANCING A PROJECT, and works to open avenues where investment has none, INCLUDING IMPACT INVESTMENT, PRIVATE EQUITY, AND FINANCING FROM CHINESE INSTITUTIONS; its advocacy removed a requirement that complainants cite specific policy violations, since PREVIOUSLY A COMPLAINT COULD BE REJECTED IF IT DID NOT CONTAIN THIS TECHNICAL INFORMATION. Identify the financier before assuming there is a complaint office. Where the money is private equity or a Chinese lender there may be none, and that absence is itself worth publicising.

trackers.name: Caribbean Natural Resources Institute (CANARI) - a regional technical institute with staff in four countries that COACHES community organisations to write proposals and then manages the grants, and sells participatory forest, site planning and protected area management services
trackers.desc: IT COACHES COMMUNITY ORGANISATIONS TO WRITE THE PROPOSAL, THEN ADMINISTERS THE GRANT — 68 ORGANISATIONS AND 77 GRANTS IN EIGHT COUNTRIES IN ONE PROGRAMME. Its record states that it SUPPORTED 68 CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS TO IMPLEMENT 77 GRANTS IN EIGHT COUNTRIES, and that ONCE A PROJECT CONCEPT WAS APPROVED, it COACHED CSOs TO HELP THEM DEVELOP PROPOSALS THAT WERE WELL ALIGNED TO the funder's STRATEGY, MET LOCAL NEEDS AND HELPED FULFIL THE INDIVIDUAL CSO'S MANDATES; the same programme leveraged AT LEAST US$2 MILLION IN ADDITIONAL FUNDING. Among its listed services is MANAGEMENT OF GRANT PROGRAMMES. Coaching on the proposal, not just a form to fill in. For a small island organisation with no grant writer, that coaching is worth more than the grant. WHAT IT IS AND WHERE ITS PEOPLE ARE: it is A REGIONAL, NON-PROFIT TECHNICAL INSTITUTE WITH MORE THAN 30 YEARS OF DEDICATED EXPERIENCE ACROSS THE COUNTRIES AND TERRITORIES OF THE CARIBBEAN REGION, headquartered in one island capital with staff based in three further countries; it CHAMPION[S] LOCALLY LED APPROACHES TO USING AND MANAGING NATURAL RESOURCES THAT PUT THE NEEDS OF COMMUNITIES FIRST, ESPECIALLY THOSE WHICH ARE OFTEN OVERLOOKED, and promotes CARIBBEAN SOLUTIONS FOR CARIBBEAN CHALLENGES, RECOGNISING THAT THE REGION'S UNIQUE ISSUES REQUIRE HOMEGROWN RESPONSES. Staff living in four countries, not a distant headquarters. For the small islands, where most entries in this file point to bodies far away, this is the regional organisation that is actually present. THE TECHNICAL SERVICES IT SELLS OR PROVIDES: named areas include DEVELOPMENT OF TOOLKITS AND TRAINING IN FACILITATING PARTICIPATORY APPROACHES, PARTICIPATORY FOREST POLICY DEVELOPMENT, SITE PLANNING AND COMMUNITY FORESTRY, PARTICIPATORY PROTECTED AREA POLICY DEVELOPMENT, PLANNING AND MANAGEMENT, CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONAL CAPACITY BUILDING, SUPPORTING DEVELOPMENT OF SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITY SMALL AND MICRO-ENTERPRISES and DEVELOPMENT OF COMMUNICATION STRATEGIES AND PRODUCTS such as case studies and policy briefs. Site planning and protected area management planning are services you can commission. Where a community has been told to produce a management plan it cannot write, this is who writes it with them. WHAT THE MICRO-GRANTS LOOK LIKE: one programme assisted SIX CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS WITH TECHNICAL SUPPORT AND MICRO-GRANTS TO SCALE UP ECOSYSTEM-BASED SOLUTIONS... IN SIX HIGH-RISK COMMUNITIES across three island states, covering HILLSIDE, RIVERBANK, MANGROVE, AND COASTAL VEGETATION RESTORATION; a recent advocacy facility awarded grants RANGING FROM $1,500 TO $8,000 to six organisations for work from recognising women in agriculture and fisheries to DOCUMENTING THE IMPACTS OF HURRICANES and advocating equitable resilience. Fifteen hundred dollars is a real grant here. Hillside and riverbank restoration is exactly the work a community does after a development has destabilised a slope. WHAT IT HAS BUILT WITH OTHERS: it convenes a regional climate justice alliance, implements a forest sector project IN PARTNERSHIP WITH two named national organisations in one island, and has run a project to STRENGTHEN THE TECHNICAL AND FINANCIAL CAPACITY OF SELECTED CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS and to improve understanding of THE INSTITUTIONAL REQUIREMENTS FOR EFFECTIVE CIVIL SOCIETY PARTICIPATION IN NATURAL RESOURCE GOVERNANCE; earlier work included SAFEGUARD[ING] WATERSHEDS THROUGH TARGETED PAYMENTS and participatory forest management across seven islands. It works through national member organisations. Find which one in your island already partners with it, and approach through them.

trackers.name: Business & Human Rights Resource Centre - invites companies to answer a community's allegation and PUBLISHES THE NON-RESPONSE on the company's own page, with regional researchers, investor escalation and published policy and benchmark data on 10,000+ companies
trackers.desc: A COMPANY'S REFUSAL TO ANSWER A COMMUNITY'S ALLEGATION IS ITSELF PUBLISHED, ON ITS OWN PAGE. The centre INVITE[S] COMPANIES TO RESPOND TO ALLEGATIONS OF MISCONDUCT AND PUBLISH[ES] THEIR COMMENTS, doing so WHEN WE FIND NO EVIDENCE THAT THEY HAVE OTHERWISE RESPONDED TO THE CONCERNS; the process ENCOURAGES COMPANIES TO PUBLICLY ADDRESS HUMAN RIGHTS CONCERNS, AND PROVIDES THE PUBLIC WITH BOTH THE ALLEGATIONS AND THE COMPANY'S COMMENTS. It states plainly: WE INDICATE RESPONSE RATES IN THE COMPANY SECTIONS OF THE SITE, and IF A COMPANY IS LISTED AS HAVING FAILED TO RESPOND TO A PARTICULAR ALLEGATION, BUT IT HAS IN FACT ISSUED A RESPONSE... PLEASE LET US KNOW. A permanent public record that the company was asked and said nothing. For a developer that presents itself as responsible to lenders and buyers, that line on its own page is a cost. THE SCALE AND WHO DOES THE ASKING: it collects evidence on MORE THAN 10,000 COMPANIES IN MORE THAN 180 COUNTRIES and takes up ALLEGED ABUSE QUICKLY AND DIRECTLY WITH COMPANIES, INVITING THEM TO RESPOND TO SPECIFIC ALLEGATIONS (OVER 1,500 PER YEAR); a network of regional researchers BUILD LONG TERM RELATIONSHIPS WITH HUMAN RIGHTS ADVOCATES ON THE GROUND, BRINGING UNDERSTANDING OF THE DYNAMICS IN THE COUNTRIES THEY COVER, and WHERE THERE IS AN ALLEGATION OF CORPORATE HUMAN RIGHTS ABUSE THAT HAS NO PUBLIC RESPONSE, THEY REACH OUT TO THE COMPANY. Its site runs in several languages including Spanish and Portuguese. There is a researcher for your region who already knows the local advocates. Send the documented allegation to them rather than to a general address. WHAT IT DOES BEYOND PUBLISHING: its recorded practice is that DIALOGUES CAN EXTEND FURTHER AND OCCASIONALLY WE TAKE AN ACTIVE ROLE IN SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES AND NGOs; in one recorded case concerning an imprisoned indigenous leader who HAD LED THE OPPOSITION TO A PROPOSED... MINE IN HIS COMMUNITY'S TERRITORY, it POSTED THE ALLEGATIONS ON OUR WEBSITE AND SOUGHT RESPONSES FROM TWO COMPANIES WHO DID NOT RESPOND, AND ASSISTED THE LOCAL VILLAGERS IN SUBMITTING THE CASE TO THE UN SPECIAL REPRESENTATIVE ON HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, then CONTACTED PUBLIC INVESTORS... AND INVITED THEM TO COMMENT, of whom two responded and ONE COMMITTED TO RAISING THE ISSUE WITH ITS CLIENTS WHO ARE INVESTED in the company. Going up the chain to the investors is the step that moves a company. Identify who holds the shares or the loan before you send the allegation, and ask that they be invited to comment too. THE HONEST NUMBERS: the centre records a response rate averaging 43% on one page and 60% on another, and its own field acknowledges criticism about WEAK AND TANGENTIAL COMPANY RESPONSES and about the LACK OF REMEDY AND THE INEQUITY IN ARMS FOR THOSE AFFECTED BY ABUSE; a published analysis notes that A COMPANY RESPONSE TO A CRITICAL CIVIL SOCIETY REPORT IS NOT NECESSARILY A POSITIVE SIGN. Roughly half of companies answer, and an answer is not a remedy. Treat this as a public record and a pressure point, not as a complaint procedure that decides anything. WHAT IT ALSO PUBLISHES ON EACH COMPANY: company pages carry news, allegations, KEY DATA POINTS BASED ON CORPORATE POLICIES, AND SCORES FROM PROMINENT CIVIL SOCIETY BENCHMARKS, and its stated goals include a SAFE AND ENABLING ENVIRONMENT IN WHICH COMMUNITIES AND WORKERS CAN ADVOCATE FOR THEIR RIGHTS AND INTERESTS, INCLUDING THROUGH FREE AND FAIR NEGOTIATIONS. Read the company's page before your first meeting with it. Its own published policies and benchmark scores are the standard you can hold it to at the table.

trackers.name: Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a regional environmental endowment established in 2012 which disburses mainly through partner National Conservation Trust Funds and runs open calls under its Ecosystem-based Adaptation window. WHO IT SUITS — READ THIS FIRST: this country is NOT a core eligible country for the EbA facility. CBF's own trustee report lists it among territories that can benefit ONLY where they are included in a regional project in which eligible countries form a three-quarters majority. So the realistic route is joining a regional consortium led from an eligible country, not applying alone. HOW IT DIFFERS: long-horizon endowment money for sustained ecosystem management, not campaign funding. APPLY TO YOUR NATIONAL FUND, NOT TO CBF — for most of the money. CBF is a regional umbrella: at national level the partner National Conservation Trust Funds (NCTFs) lead the grantmaking process, with endowment proceeds held in country-based subaccounts and channelled through them. So for the Conservation Finance stream, the regional body is the wrong door — find your NCTF. THE EXCEPTION IS THE EbA FACILITY, which awards through competitive calls for proposals and is a direct route. THE NUMBERS: EbA medium grants USD 250,000–1 million, large grants up to USD 2 million — large by the standards of most funds here, and not aimed at a small unincorporated group acting alone. Eligible recipients expressly include NCTFs, NGOs, community-based organisations, government agencies, universities and the private sector. SCOPE CHECK: the EbA Facility covers the marine and coastal zone of the insular Caribbean, so an inland project must show its connection to marine and coastal ecosystems. IF YOU ARE TOO SMALL FOR EbA: CBF partners with GEF SGP across 12 shared countries — that is the sibling route for community-scale grants, and it is recorded separately in this map. Endowment disbursements go to NCTFs that have signed agreements with CBF, the first in 2016 with Fondo MARENA in the Dominican Republic.

trackers.name: CANARI — Caribbean Natural Resources Institute
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional technical non-profit founded in 1989, headquartered in Trinidad and legally registered as a non-profit in this country, working with grassroots and community-based organisations directly involved in natural resource management. What it actually supplies is capacity rather than representation: coaching, mentoring and training of trainers, facilitated multi-stakeholder dialogues for planning and policymaking, participatory research, and unusual practical tools — participatory GIS mapping, three-dimensional modelling, participatory video and photojournaling — for communities that need to evidence their own case. It also channels funding and technical support to civil society organisations. WHO IT SUITS: community organisations and CSOs that need to be equipped to hold their ground in a planning or policy process. It is not a litigator, and its re-granting runs through time-limited donor projects rather than a standing open call — ask what is currently running. IS YOUR SITE A KBA? CHECK BEFORE YOU WRITE ANYTHING. CANARI publishes the CEPF Caribbean Islands Biodiversity Hotspot Ecosystem Profile, which identifies 45 Key Biodiversity Areas and 6 conservation corridors covering 28 KBAs as priorities for funding support, with maps — formulated through a process engaging over 200 stakeholders from more than 160 organisations. A campaign whose site is a KBA, or sits in one of the six corridors, has a materially stronger funding case and should say so explicitly. CORRECTED — AND THIS STREAM IS CLOSING. CEPF returned for a Phase II running August 2021 to July 2027, and CANARI is once again the Regional Implementation Team, managing US$11.8 million. THE ELEVENTH AND FINAL SMALL-GRANT CALL offers USD 5,000–50,000 for projects of up to 12 months between April 2026 and March 2027, and the tenth call was the final open call for large grants in the region — so treat the current call as the last scheduled opportunity, not one of many, though targeted solicitations may still fill portfolio gaps. ELIGIBILITY NARROWED IN PHASE II: the Phase I list of 11 countries no longer applies; Phase II calls name Antigua and Barbuda, The Bahamas, the Dominican Republic, Jamaica, Saint Lucia, and St Vincent and the Grenadines, with CEPF stating 7 countries initially eligible. BUT THE SITE TEST CAN OUTRANK THE COUNTRY TEST: applicants based outside the eligible countries may submit provided activities focus on a conservation need within a priority corridor or site. THREE RULES: applicants must not be a government agency (government-owned bodies qualify only with independent legal personality and authority to receive private funds); joint projects are eligible with one lead organisation; and NGOs, community groups, universities and private enterprises may all apply. ASK BEFORE YOU DRAFT: RIT Manager Nicole Brown, caribbeanrit@canari.org — applicants uncertain about eligibility are expressly encouraged to make contact first. A Grievance Redress Mechanism exists for concerns about a funded project. WHAT CANARI ITSELF IS: a non-profit technical institute of thirty years' standing that acts as a conduit, channelling funding, information and technical support to CSOs — not a standing grant fund. Its project pattern is small grants plus technical coaching for partner CSOs to run participatory community vulnerability assessments and then design a project from the results.

trackers.name: Barbados Audit Office
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of Barbados. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Barbados.

trackers.name: Barbados — Corporate Affairs & Intellectual Property Office (CAIPO)
trackers.desc: National company registry; registers & regulates companies and business names (with an online corporate registry) and administers IP rights, Barbados. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: CommonLII – Barbados
trackers.desc: Free judgments of the Court of Appeal (1958– ), High Court (1960– ) and Supreme Court of Barbados, plus Privy Council decisions, via the Commonwealth Legal Information Institute. · Find here: free Barbadian case-law (CommonLII / BAILII).

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Judicature
trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Judicature — supreme court in Barbados (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Caribbean Court of Justice (CCJ)
trackers.desc: YOUR FINAL COURT OF APPEAL — this is one of only 5 states that have acceded to the CCJ's Appellate Jurisdiction, replacing the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council for civil and criminal appeals: Barbados, Belize, Dominica, Guyana and Saint Lucia. Everywhere else in the Eastern Caribbean the final court remains the Privy Council, so do not assume the CCJ is your appeal route from a neighbouring jurisdiction's practice. BE CLEAR WHAT THE OTHER JURISDICTION DOES NOT COVER: in its Original Jurisdiction the CCJ interprets the Revised Treaty of Chaguaramas on freedom of movement of people, goods, services, capital and the right of establishment — it does not extend to human rights generally, and it is not an environmental forum. A land-defence claim does not fit there unless it has a cross-border economic dimension, such as a project licensed to a company from another CARICOM state. WHERE IT DOES FIT, INDIVIDUALS CAN GET IN: under Article 222 a natural or juridical person may seek special leave, granted where the Treaty intended the right to enure to the benefit of individuals, the applicant has been prejudiced, and the member state entitled to espouse the claim omitted or declined to. 35 such cases have been brought, so the route is used rather than theoretical — Trinidad Cement Ltd v Republic of Guyana [2009] CCJ 1 (OJ) established that individuals and companies can use the Treaty to make their own state comply. The Court sits as a court of first instance there, its rulings immediately binding in international law, and hearings are broadcast live.

trackers.name: Barbados National Trust — holds nature reserves, parks and coastal land
trackers.desc: A LAND-HOLDING CONSERVATION BODY, founded 1960, working to preserve the natural and artistic heritage of Barbados. Its holdings include nature reserves, park areas and coastal areas alongside gardens, historic houses and windmills, and it runs museums and an education programme. WHY THE INTERNATIONAL LINKS ARE PRACTICALLY USEFUL: it maintains working relationships with National Trusts in Canada, Scotland, England, Ireland, Wales and the United States — and the National Trust model carries a large body of transferable practice on conservation covenants, endowment and visitor management that a small Caribbean trust can draw on through those relationships. COMPARE THE SAINT LUCIA TRUST, recorded separately in this map: that one is a statutory body with an express power to acquire property and to make by-laws over what it holds. If you are approaching a national trust in this region, establish first whether it is statutory or voluntary, because that determines what it can do with land once it has it.

trackers.name: Barbados' public planning register and TREE PRESERVATION ORDER objection window, the Planning and Development Board that now decides major applications, and the 30 appointed constituency councils
trackers.desc: A TREE PRESERVATION ORDER MUST BE ADVERTISED FOUR TIMES AND OBJECTIONS TAKEN FOR AT LEAST 28 DAYS, AND EVERY OBJECTION MUST BE CONSIDERED. The planning statute requires that before such an order is made A NOTICE SHALL BE PUBLISHED ONCE IN THE OFFICIAL GAZETTE AND AT INTERVALS OF NOT LESS THAN FOUR DAYS IN AT LEAST THREE ISSUES OF A NEWSPAPER, stating the grounds, and that OBJECTIONS AND REPRESENTATIONS MAY BE MADE IN WRITING TO THE MINISTER WITHIN... NOT LESS THAN 28 DAYS FROM ITS PUBLICATION; EVERY OBJECTION OR REPRESENTATION RECEIVED SHALL BE CONSIDERED BEFORE AN ORDER IS MADE. Tree preservation orders exist here as a live instrument with a public objection window. The same machinery that lets a developer object can be used to ask the minister to make one over a stand of trees. THE REGISTER THAT IS OPEN TO ANYONE: the planning head SHALL KEEP A REGISTER... WITH RESPECT TO APPLICATIONS FOR PLANNING PERMISSION MADE TO HIM, INCLUDING INFORMATION AS TO THE MANNER IN WHICH SUCH APPLICATIONS HAVE BEEN DEALT WITH, and EVERY REGISTER SHALL BE AVAILABLE FOR INSPECTION BY THE PUBLIC AT ALL REASONABLE HOURS; when a development plan is approved, notice goes in THREE ISSUES OF THE GAZETTE AND OF AT LEAST ONE NEWSPAPER and copies SHALL BE MADE AVAILABLE FOR INSPECTION AND PURCHASE BY THE PUBLIC. The register records not only the application but how it was dealt with. That is where you find out whether conditions were imposed and whether they were met. WHO DECIDES NOW, AFTER THE REFORM: the planning office was renamed the planning and development department, the post of chief town planner REPLACED WITH THAT OF DIRECTOR OF PLANNING AND DEVELOPMENT, and THERE IS A PLANNING AND DEVELOPMENT BOARD TO HANDLE APPLICATIONS FOR PLANNING PERMISSION, EXCEPT THOSE REFERRED TO THE MINISTER, THUS REMOVING THE TASK FROM THE ONE PUBLIC OFFICER PREVIOUSLY ASSIGNED; the board MUST DETERMINE MAJOR AND COMPLEX APPLICATIONS AS PRESCRIBED but may delegate lesser ones to the director, and the appeal panel's decision timeframe was increased FROM 14 TO 28 DAYS. Members of the board are publicly named on appointment. Major applications are now decided by a named board rather than one official. A board has minutes, members and a chair — all of which can be written to. THE LOCAL BODIES THAT DO EXIST: the country is A PARLIAMENTARY DEMOCRACY WITHOUT ELECTED LOCAL GOVERNMENT, but a 2009 statute CREATED 30 APPOINTED CONSTITUENCY COUNCILS, overseen by a constituency empowerment department, which PROVIDE A WIDE RANGE OF SERVICES BASED ON THE NEEDS OF THEIR CONSTITUENTS and are EXPECTED TO EFFECTIVELY AND EFFICIENTLY ASSIST IN THE MANAGEMENT OF NATIONAL GOVERNMENT RESOURCES ASSIGNED FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF EACH CONSTITUENCY. Each receives a fixed annual allocation, and council spending is around 0.07% OF TOTAL GOVERNMENT EXPENDITURE; they must be audited annually, and are described as existing MAINLY TO COMMUNICATE LOCAL OPINION TO LARGER BODIES IN THE CENTRAL GOVERNMENT. Communicating local opinion upward is their stated purpose, and there are thirty of them with a chairperson each. Small budget, but a formal channel and a named chair for every constituency. THE PLAN THAT FRAMES EVERY DECISION: the planning office uses the PHYSICAL DEVELOPMENT PLAN AS A BROAD ADMINISTRATIVE POLICY TOOL TO CHART SETTLEMENT, GROWTH PATTERNS AND THE ALLOCATION OF LAND TO VARIOUS USES, while noting that THIS DOCUMENT IS NOT THE SOLE DETERMINANT OF THE DECISION MAKING PROCESS, and the planning head IS ALSO REQUIRED BY STATUTE TO CONSULT WITH VARIOUS AGENCIES OF GOVERNMENT. Ask which agencies were consulted on the application and what each said. Those consultations are required, so their absence is itself a ground of complaint.

trackers.name: Caribbean Association of Local Government Authorities - open to individual LOCAL AUTHORITIES AND MINISTRIES where no national association exists, sharing an office with the ministers' forum and the Commonwealth local government body
trackers.desc: WHERE A CARIBBEAN COUNTRY HAS NO NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF LOCAL AUTHORITIES, THE INDIVIDUAL COUNCILS AND THE MINISTRY JOIN THE REGIONAL BODY DIRECTLY. Its membership COMPRISES MAINLY NATIONAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT ASSOCIATIONS, AND, LOCAL AUTHORITIES AND MINISTRIES RESPONSIBLE FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT WHERE THERE ARE NO NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS; it is A NOT FOR PROFIT ORGANISATION ESTABLISHED TO FACILITATE THE FURTHER DEVELOPMENT OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT WITHIN THE CARIBBEAN REGION, founded in 1992 and incorporated in 2012 under the companies statute of one member country, with its secretariat accommodated by a borough corporation. A single village or town council in a country with no national association can belong in its own right. For the small islands, where local government is weakest, that is the only regional table available. WHO ACTUALLY TURNS UP: recorded meetings have brought together local government representatives from THE BAHAMAS, BELIZE, DOMINICA, GUYANA, ST LUCIA AND TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO, and a wider regional event drew central and local government from ANTIGUA AND BARBUDA, THE BAHAMAS, BELIZE, DOMINICA, GUYANA, JAMAICA, ST KITTS AND NEVIS, ST LUCIA, AND TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO, alongside private sector partners; one meeting included A TRAINING SESSION ON INSTITUTIONAL STRENGTHENING OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT SYSTEMS and a segment on women in local leadership. Nine or ten countries in one room, with a university academic who has supported the body since its founding. If your island's councils are weak, the comparison with a neighbouring island that has stronger ones is the most persuasive material available.
