THE CONFIDENTIALITY POINT, WHICH IS THE DETAIL MOST GUIDES OMIT: IT OVERVIEWS THE MAIN INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS FRAMEWORKS DEFINING BANKS' RESPONSIBILITIES ON GRIEVANCE MECHANISMS AND REMEDY, INCLUDING GUIDANCE AROUND THE EXTENT AND LIMITS OF BANKS' DUTIES OF CONFIDENTIALITY. Banking secrecy is the standard refusal when you ask whether a bank funds the project on your land. Knowing where that duty stops is what turns the refusal into a question they must answer. THE CHANNEL IT RUNS ITSELF WHERE THE INDUSTRY HAS NONE: WHILE A NAMED INDUSTRY STANDARD HAS NO OFFICIAL GRIEVANCE MECHANISM, COMPLAINTS RELATING TO A BANK'S FINANCING OF PROJECTS UNDER THAT STANDARD CAN BE FILED THROUGH ITS OWN WEBSITE. A civil society organisation built the complaints channel the industry declined to build. Signatory banks answer to it by reputation rather than by rule — weaker than a legal route, and available when nothing else is. THE AFRICA BENCHMARK AND A SCORED AFRICAN BANK: REGIONAL BENCHMARKS PUBLISHED FOR AFRICA IN 2021, ASIA IN 2022 AND LATIN AMERICA IN 2024, ALONGSIDE A GLOBAL BENCHMARK — WITH ONE NAMED AFRICAN BANK ASSESSED AS A LAGGARD, TOTAL SCORE 2.5 OUT OF 14: POLICY 0.5 OF 3, DUE DILIGENCE 2 OF 5, REPORTING 0 OF 3, REMEDY 0 OF 3. African banks scored on remedy, and one scoring zero. When the lender behind a project is African rather than European, that benchmark is where to look first — and a published zero on remedy tells you the internal route is not worth your months. THE RESPONSE DATABASE AND ITS HONEST FINDING: A DATABASE COVERING INSTANCES IN WHICH CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS SOUGHT RESPONSES FROM BANKS ON ALLEGED HUMAN RIGHTS IMPACTS OF THEIR FINANCE — AND AN UPDATE SHOWING UNDER 5% OF BANKS RESPONDED CONSTRUCTIVELY TO RECENT ISSUES RAISED, WITH RESPONSES GETTING WORSE, NOT BETTER. UNDER FIVE PERCENT, published by the organisation whose whole method is writing to banks. Plan on the letter being ignored and design the campaign around what follows it — and record your own attempt in that database, because the count is the argument for regulation. THE PRECEDENT THAT CREATED ONE MECHANISM, WHICH IS THE TACTIC TO COPY: A BANK INTRODUCED ITS HUMAN RIGHTS GRIEVANCE MECHANISM IN 2021 FOLLOWING A 2018 RECOMMENDATION FROM ITS COUNTRY'S NATIONAL CONTACT POINT, WHICH URGED IT TO ESTABLISH A GRIEVANCE RESOLUTION PROCESS — AND BEFORE PUBLISHING IT CONDUCTED AN 18-MONTH CONSULTATION WITH LEADING HUMAN RIGHTS ORGANISATIONS. A complaint to a national contact point produced a permanent mechanism at the bank, three years later. That is a bigger win than the original case: the route now exists for everyone the bank finances. WHO MAY FILE UNDER IT: AFFECTED PEOPLE AND THEIR NOMINATED LEGITIMATE REPRESENTATIVES — FOR EXAMPLE CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS WORKING WITH AFFECTED PEOPLE — ANYWHERE IN THE WORLD, CONCERNING ANY OF THE BANK'S PAST OR CURRENT FINANCE. ANYWHERE IN THE WORLD, and PAST finance. A project already built, financed years ago, is still inside scope. AND THE DEAL DATABASE: A DODGY DEALS DATABASE SHOWING LINKS TO COMPANIES IN MINING, STEEL AND OIL AND GAS WHOSE OPERATIONS HAVE BEEN CONNECTED TO SERIOUS HUMAN RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL VIOLATIONS, PLUS PER-BANK PROFILE PAGES COVERING FINANCE AND POLICIES. WHO IT SUITS: African communities facing a project financed by a commercial bank — and the national organisations supporting them who need the bank named and reached. CAVEATS: COMMERCIAL BANKS ONLY, CAMPAIGNING RATHER THAN LEGAL ACTION, AND ITS OWN DATA SHOWS BANKS RARELY ANSWER — use it alongside the statutory routes. For research identifying the financier on request, Benin's entry; for the database of what complaints to development banks achieved, Burundi's entry; for the home-country contact points, Chad's entry.

trackers.name: Capacity for Conservation — a free multilingual self-assessment platform for conservation organisations that needs no account to use — 12 management themes, a development plan template, an indicator list, training courses, and a library the community adds to
trackers.desc: NO ACCOUNT, NO APPLICATION, NO PARTNER. JUST THE TOOLS — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S TOGO ENTRY NAMES THE CO-FOUNDING CONSERVATION ORGANISATION AND POINTS AT THIS SITE WITHOUT DESCRIBING IT; ITS CÔTE D'IVOIRE ENTRY THE HOTSPOT FUND THAT PART-FUNDS IT; ITS LIBYA AND BURUNDI ENTRIES A BIRD CONSERVATION HOST THAT CO-BUILT IT; AND ITS SÃO TOMÉ ENTRY THE MID-CAREER AWARD WHOSE USEFUL-LINKS PAGE RECOMMENDS IT. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. NO ACCOUNT NEEDED, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT IS NOT NECESSARY TO CREATE AN ACCOUNT OR LOG IN TO USE THIS WEBSITE — THOUGH A FREE ACCOUNT ENABLES YOU TO COMPLETE AN ORGANISATIONAL ASSESSMENT WITH YOUR COLLEAGUES, SEE COMBINED RESULTS, DEVELOP AN ONLINE DEVELOPMENT PLAN, AND ADD RESOURCES OR CASE STUDIES TO THE COMMUNITY LIBRARY. Almost every strengthening resource in this file requires a partnership, an application or a grant relationship first. This one requires nothing at all: a committee in a village with an internet connection can open it today, read the material and take what it needs. That is the rarest access condition in the whole list. THE ASSESSMENT AND HOW MUCH OF IT YOU MUST DO: THE ASSESSMENT IS SPLIT INTO 12 THEMES; YOU CAN COMPLETE THE FULL ASSESSMENT, OR YOU CAN COMPLETE JUST THE SECTIONS THAT ARE RELEVANT TO YOUR ORGANISATION — AND ONCE SUBMITTED YOU CAN VIEW YOUR RESULTS AND THE AVERAGE FOR THE WHOLE ORGANISATION, WHICH HELPS YOU PRIORITISE. Answer only the sections that apply. A small organisation with no staff, no vehicles and no grants does not have to pretend otherwise to get a usable result. WHAT THE RESULT IS FOR: THE RESULTS GIVE A GOOD BASELINE OF THE INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITY OF YOUR ORGANISATION AND CAN BE USED TO INFORM ORGANISATIONAL PLANNING — AND IF REPEATED EVERY YEAR, TRENDS IN CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT CAN BE SEEN. A BASELINE is the practical use. Funders across this file ask what an organisation's capacity is and whether it is improving; a dated self-assessment, repeated annually, answers that in the funder's own language and costs nothing to produce. THE MULTI-PERSON DESIGN: DESIGNED TO BE APPLICABLE FOR ANY INDIVIDUAL AT ANY LEVEL OF THEIR CAREER, IT RECOMMENDS INVITING AS MANY STAFF AS POSSIBLE TO GET A BROADER PICTURE, AND INVOLVING THE RELEVANT STAKEHOLDERS FOR EACH AREA — WITH MULTIPLE LEVELS OF PERMISSIONS SELF-MANAGED BY ORGANISATIONS, AND SPREADSHEET EXPORTS AND ON-SCREEN CHARTS AND TABLES. ANY LEVEL OF THEIR CAREER means a field assistant's assessment counts alongside the director's, and the tool shows where they disagree. That disagreement is usually the most useful thing it produces — and PERMISSIONS ARE SELF-MANAGED, so the organisation controls who sees what. WHAT THE RESULTS POINT YOU TO: THE HEALTH CHECKS INDICATE AREAS WHERE ORGANISATIONS COULD CONSIDER IMPROVING, ALONG WITH RECOMMENDATIONS FOR TOOLS ON THE WEBSITE — AN ORGANISATION THAT NEEDS TO WORK ON ITS FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT, FOR EXAMPLE, WOULD BE DIRECTED TO OVER 25 RESOURCES, RANGING FROM A GUIDE TO BUDGETARY MANAGEMENT TO A DOCUMENT ABOUT RISK ANALYSIS. The weakness comes with the remedy attached. Financial management is the gate this file has recorded most often — the grant that stalls on an unaccepted financial report, the fund that requires audited accounts — and there are 25 free documents behind that one heading. THE PLANNING TOOL AND THE INDICATORS: AN ORGANISATIONAL DEVELOPMENT PLANNING GUIDE AND TEMPLATE — AND AN INDICATOR LIST COVERING 12 KEY CAPACITY AREAS THAT CAN BE ADAPTED FOR YOUR OWN NEEDS, WITH THE ADVICE THAT IT IS GOOD PRACTICE TO USE MULTIPLE METHODS OF MONITORING. An indicator list you may adapt. Rather than accepting a funder's indicators, an organisation can arrive with its own — which is a small shift in who defines success and one this file has recorded mattering. THE OTHER SECTIONS: A RESOURCE LIBRARY OF TOOLS AND CASE STUDIES; A GROWING LIBRARY OF INTERACTIVE TRAINING COURSES IN AN eLEARNING HUB; AND AN ARCHIVE OF PAST ORGANISATIONAL RESILIENCE WEBINARS. THE LANGUAGES: THE WHOLE SYSTEM WAS MADE TO BE MULTILINGUAL, WITH A RESOURCE LIBRARY THAT CAN BE CONTRIBUTED TO BY THE COMMUNITY. Built multilingual from the start rather than translated later — check for your working language before assuming English only. THE CONTRIBUTION INVITATION: SHARE YOUR ORGANISATIONAL DEVELOPMENT EXPERIENCES BY COMPLETING A CASE STUDY OR ADDING RESOURCES THAT HAVE BEEN BENEFICIAL TO YOU — IT AIMS TO BE A USER-LED COMMUNITY PROMOTING MUTUAL EXCHANGE AND LEARNING, AND IT DEPENDS ON YOU TO RATE AND REVIEW THE RESOURCES AND TO SHARE YOUR OWN. An African organisation that solved a registration, governance or funding problem can put the answer where the next one will find it. That is also how the library stops being written entirely by people who have never run an organisation in these conditions. WHO BUILT AND FUNDS IT: A COLLABORATIVE PROJECT OF A BIRD CONSERVATION BODY, A FAUNA AND FLORA ORGANISATION, A TROPICAL BIOLOGY ASSOCIATION AND A UNIVERSITY GEOGRAPHY DEPARTMENT — FUNDED BY A CAMBRIDGE COLLABORATIVE FUND, A NAMED ARCADIA FUND, A NAMED FOUNDATION AND A CRITICAL ECOSYSTEM PARTNERSHIP FUND. Four conservation bodies and four funders behind a free tool, which is why it has no fee and no gatekeeper. AND WHO IT WAS BUILT FOR, IN A USER'S OWN WORDS: NATIONAL AND LOCAL CONSERVATION ORGANISATIONS IN BIODIVERSITY-RICH DEVELOPING COUNTRIES REQUIRE IT — AND ONE USER WROTE THAT THE OPEN ACCESS LEARNING CENTRE IS A VALUABLE RESOURCE FOR INDIVIDUALS AND ORGANIZATIONS COMMITTED TO CONSERVATION, ESPECIALLY FOR LOCAL CONSERVATIONISTS LIKE MYSELF, AND THAT ITS FREE ACCESSIBILITY CONTRIBUTES SIGNIFICANTLY TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF SELF-LED ORGANIZATIONS. SELF-LED is the phrase to hold onto. This is a tool for an organisation improving itself without anyone's permission, which is what the funder and partner entries elsewhere in this file all quietly assume you have already done. WHO IT SUITS: any African conservation, land or community organisation wanting to strengthen itself before approaching funders — no partnership, application or fee required. CAVEATS: A SELF-LED TOOLKIT, NOT FUNDING, TRAINING DELIVERY OR A PARTNERSHIP, AND IT NEEDS AN INTERNET CONNECTION — download what matters while you have one. For the organisation whose partners set the terms, Togo's entry; for the funder with no pass-or-fail screen, Ethiopia's entry; for core organisational support in the Congo Basin, DR Congo's entry.

trackers.name: The Rufford Foundation Small Grants — a funder with no deadlines at all — applications any day of the year from individuals and small groups, £7,000–18,000, willing to cover 50–100% of a project's cost, with the eligible-country list, the exclusions and the reference rules published
trackers.desc: NO DEADLINES, AND THEY WILL PAY THE WHOLE COST — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ETHIOPIA BUCKET CARRIES A SYNCHRONICITY HOST, ITS SÃO TOMÉ BUCKET A WHITLEY HOST; ITS ZIMBABWE ENTRY THE CO-MANAGEMENT FOUNDATION, ITS CAPE VERDE ENTRY THE INCUBATING FOUNDATION, ITS SOMALIA ENTRY THE ZERO-OVERHEAD FUNDER. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE ABSENCE OF DEADLINES, WHICH IS THE FIND: THERE ARE NO DEADLINES — APPLICATIONS CAN BE SUBMITTED AT ANY TIME OF YEAR, AND UNSUCCESSFUL APPLICANTS MAY RE-APPLY AFTER 12 MONTHS, WITH APPLICATIONS REVIEWED WITHIN 3 MONTHS. Almost every fund in this file runs on an annual call, which means a threat arriving in March waits until the following year for money. Here the application goes in the week the problem appears and is answered within three months. For anything urgent, that timing is the whole difference. THE PROPORTION OF COSTS IT WILL COVER, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IDEALLY, WE SHOULD PROVIDE BETWEEN 50 AND 100% OF THE COSTS OF THE PROJECT — AND WHERE THE FOUNDATION IS NOT THE ONLY FUNDER, EVIDENCE OF CO-FUNDING IS REQUIRED. UP TO 100%. No match, no co-financing requirement, no gap to fill from somewhere else — which is the condition that has sunk more applications in this file than any assessment of merit. WHO CAN APPLY: INDIVIDUALS AND SMALL GROUPS LOCATED IN THE DEVELOPING COUNTRIES — FOR FIELD PROJECTS THAT HAVE CLEAR CONSERVATION OBJECTIVES. An individual can hold the grant. No registration, no constitution, no organisation required — one person in a village with a defined field project is the intended applicant. THE LADDER AND THE AMOUNTS: A STAGED PROCESS WITH FOUR LEVELS — A FIRST GRANT, A SECOND GRANT, A BOOSTER GRANT AND A COMPLETION GRANT — WITH GRANTS RANGING FROM £7,000 TO £18,000, AND A MINIMUM OF 12 MONTHS BETWEEN A FIRST AND SECOND APPLICATION. Four rungs, so a first small grant is the entry to a decade of funding rather than a one-off. Plan the first project as the foundation of the second. THE CONDITION ON MOVING UP THE LADDER: APPLICANTS CANNOT APPLY FOR A SECOND GRANT UNLESS THEY HAVE ALREADY RECEIVED A FIRST, AND MUST HAVE SUBMITTED INTERIM REPORTS AND A FINAL REPORT — WITH A NEW BUDGET REQUIRED, AND AT LEAST ONE OF THE THREE REFEREES DIFFERENT FROM THE PREVIOUS APPLICATION. Reporting is the gate to the next grant, and it is the cheapest thing to get right. A different referee each round also forces the applicant to keep widening their circle, which is useful in itself. THE REFERENCE RULES, PUBLISHED PLAINLY: AT LEAST ONE REFERENCE MUST COME FROM A WELL-ESTABLISHED INSTITUTION — A MAJOR CONSERVATION NGO, UNIVERSITY OR GOVERNMENT BODY — ON OFFICIAL LETTERHEAD; IT IS UNACCEPTABLE FOR AN APPLICANT TO DRAFT A REFERENCE FOR A REFEREE TO SIGN, THOUGH IT IS ACCEPTABLE TO PROVIDE BACKGROUND INFORMATION ON THE PROJECT TO THE REFEREE. The real barrier, stated. Three referees, one on institutional letterhead, is the requirement a rural applicant is least able to meet — which is the practical argument for building a relationship with a university department or a national NGO before there is anything to apply for. And the line between drafting a reference and briefing a referee is drawn explicitly: giving background is allowed, writing it for them is not. THE FRAUD WARNING: IF AN APPLICANT IS CONSIDERED TO BE USING FRAUDULENT REFERENCES, THE APPLICATION IS AUTOMATICALLY REJECTED, THEY WILL NOT BE ELIGIBLE TO APPLY IN FUTURE, AND THE SUSPECTED FRAUD WILL BE REPORTED TO THE RELEVANT AUTHORITIES. WHO IT PRIORITISES, AND WHO IS BARRED: EARLY-STAGE CONSERVATION CAREERS, WITH PRIORITY TO THOSE UNDERTAKING AN MSc OR PhD OR EQUIVALENT OR WHO GRADUATED IN THE PAST 3 YEARS — OTHERS ARE CONSIDERED IF THEY FIT THE GENERAL CRITERIA, BUT BSc STUDENTS ARE NOT FUNDED, AND ONLY FIELDWORK COSTS ARE CONSIDERED. Recorded plainly: this is weighted toward postgraduates, and OTHERS ARE CONSIDERED is a genuine but narrower door. FIELDWORK COSTS ONLY also means no salaries and no office — budget accordingly. A community organisation's strongest route is often a postgraduate from that community applying with the community's project. WHAT THE PROJECT MAY BE ABOUT: PARTICULAR SPECIES, THREATENED HABITATS OR ISSUES LIKE HUMAN-WILDLIFE CONFLICT OR COMMUNITY EDUCATION — AND IN GENERAL THE FOUNDATION PREFERS PROJECTS AT THE ECOSYSTEM LEVEL RATHER THAN SPECIES WORK. ECOSYSTEM LEVEL PREFERRED OVER SPECIES. The opposite weighting to the flagship-species logic recorded in this file's Cape Verde entry — which means a habitat with no charismatic animal in it is a better fit here than almost anywhere else. THE SPECIES RULE, WITH ITS OPENING: IT CONSIDERS WORK ON ANY SPECIES NOT LISTED AS LEAST CONCERN AT A GLOBAL LEVEL ON THE INTERNATIONAL RED LIST — AND ALSO CONSIDERS SPECIES THAT DO NOT APPEAR ON THE LIST BECAUSE THEY HAVE NOT BEEN ASSESSED BUT ARE THOUGHT TO BE GLOBALLY THREATENED. UNASSESSED SPECIES ARE ELIGIBLE. Most African plants and invertebrates have never been assessed, and this file has recorded that absence being read as absence of value. Here it is explicitly not a bar. WHAT IT WANTS AND WHAT IT WILL NOT FUND: PRAGMATIC PROJECTS THAT WILL MAKE A SUBSTANTIAL AND LONG-LASTING IMPACT AND HAVE A SIGNIFICANT HUMAN ELEMENT — SMALL-SCALE OR PILOT PROJECTS RATHER THAN A SMALL AMOUNT OF FUNDING FOR A LARGE PROJECT; PURE RESEARCH WITH NO OBVIOUS CONSERVATION BENEFIT IS NOT ELIGIBLE. A SIGNIFICANT HUMAN ELEMENT is a stated preference, not a concession. And the warning against using it as a slice of a bigger budget is worth heeding: propose the whole of something small. AND THE PUBLIC RECORD OF EVERY FUNDED PROJECT: FUNDED PROJECTS ARE LISTED BY WORLD REGION AS A GUIDE TO GRANT SEEKERS, AND PROJECT PROFILES AND UPDATES USUALLY INCLUDE EXTENSIVE INFORMATION SUCH AS REPORTS AND CONTACT DETAILS — WITH A PUBLISHED LIST OF WHICH COUNTRIES QUALIFY AND WHICH DO NOT, INCLUDING THOSE UNDER BANKING SANCTIONS. Every funded project published with its report and the grantee's contact details. Read what was funded in your own country, then write to those people — they are the nearest thing to a referee, a collaborator and a worked example of a successful application, all at once. WHO IT SUITS: individual African conservationists and small groups — especially postgraduates from affected communities — needing fieldwork money quickly and without a matching contribution. CAVEATS: FIELDWORK COSTS ONLY, NO SALARIES OR OVERHEADS; WEIGHTED TOWARD MSc AND PhD APPLICANTS, WITH THREE REFEREES REQUIRED AND ONE ON INSTITUTIONAL LETTERHEAD; SOME COUNTRIES ARE EXCLUDED, INCLUDING THOSE UNDER BANKING SANCTIONS — check the published country list first. For a fund that takes video applications and waives registration, Libya's entry; for the zero-overhead funder, Somalia's entry.

trackers.name: CAPPA (Corporate Accountability and Public Participation Africa), Lagos — a pan-African organisation whose communities hold their own water parliaments — fifty local leaders facing the state water corporation directly — and whose two-year campaign made a development bank abandon a public-private water contract
trackers.desc: COMMUNITIES HOLD THEIR OWN WATER PARLIAMENT, AND THE BANK WALKED AWAY — method and adjacency declared first: THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN TWO HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS THE FULL NAME AND DESCRIPTION TEXT OF ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL HOSTS AND ALL SIX FACTS ABSENT. THIS FILE'S ZIMBABWE ENTRY COVERS THE EXTRACTIVES PETITIONER AND ITS UNDERGROUND-WATER POINT; ITS SOMALIA AND SÃO TOMÉ ENTRIES THE LAND-WITH-WATER DEMAND; ITS MOROCCO ENTRY THE DEVELOPMENT BANK'S COMPLAINT DESK. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE WATER PARLIAMENTS, WHICH IS THE FIND: THE CAMPAIGN HAS EMPOWERED COMMUNITIES ALL OVER THE CITY TO HOLD THEIR OWN WATER PARLIAMENTS — THESE COMMUNITIES CARRYING OUT ACTIONS TO OPPOSE PRIVATIZATION AND CALL FOR PUBLIC SOLUTIONS, SOMETIMES IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE LARGER CAMPAIGN AND SOMETIMES ON THEIR OWN. SOMETIMES ON THEIR OWN is the measure of whether an organising model worked. A parliament that only convenes when the NGO arrives is an event; one the neighbourhood calls itself is an institution. Read beside the fishers' tribunal filed under South Sudan: communities holding their own formal hearing when the state will not. WHAT ONE PARLIAMENT ACTUALLY DID: A WATER-FOCUSED COMMUNITY PARLIAMENT WAS ORGANISED AND FACILITATED IN THE CITY WHERE MORE THAN FIFTY LOCAL LEADERS FROM ACROSS THE STATE SPOKE DIRECTLY WITH OFFICIALS OF THE STATE WATER CORPORATION ABOUT THEIR CONCERNS. Fifty leaders and the utility's officials in one room, arranged by the communities' own side rather than as a consultation the utility designed. That is a different thing from being invited to comment, and it is a format any coalition can convene. THE WIN ON RECORD, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: A TWO-YEAR CAMPAIGN CULMINATED IN 2016 WITH A DEVELOPMENT BANK ABANDONING ITS EFFORTS TO SECURE A PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP CONTRACT WITH THE CITY — AND THE CAMPAIGN CONTINUES TO WIN VICTORIES, HOLDING OFF WATER PRIVATIZATION. Two years, and the financier withdrew. This file is full of routes for complaining to development banks after a project starts; this is the rarer record of one being stopped before the contract was signed — and the bank's own complaint desk, filed under Morocco, accepts complaints while a project is still under preparation. WHY THE ORGANISATION EXISTS AT ALL: THE CAMPAIGN WAS SO SUCCESSFUL THAT THE ORGANISERS DETERMINED THEY NEEDED A MORE ROBUST PLATFORM TO CARRY THE WORK BEYOND ONE COUNTRY — AND SO THEY LAUNCHED THIS PAN-AFRICAN ORGANISATION, WHICH HAS ALREADY FORMED PARTNERSHIPS WITH GRASSROOTS AND LABOUR ORGANISATIONS IN NEARLY A DOZEN COUNTRIES. A continental body created out of a won local campaign rather than founded first and populated afterwards. The organisational history is the credential. THE ANNUAL CONTINENTAL EVENT: AN AFRICA WEEK OF ACTION AGAINST WATER PRIVATIZATION, IN ITS FOURTH CONSECUTIVE YEAR — OPENING WITH A PRESS CONFERENCE AT WHICH ACTIVISTS BRIEFED THE PRESS, INCLUDING ON THE IMPACTS OF ILLEGAL MINING ON WATER, FROM EXPOSURE TO NONCOMMUNICABLE DISEASES TO LOSS OF FISH AND WILDLIFE. A fixed annual week is a date a local group can plan a launch or a march around, with continental press attention already arranged. Mining is on the agenda alongside privatisation, so a community fighting a mine over water has a place in it. WHO SIGNS THE JOINT STATEMENTS: A NATIONAL WATER JUSTICE NETWORK, TWO NAMED WATER AND ENERGY WORKERS' UNIONS, A REVENUE MOBILISATION ORGANISATION, AN ADVOCACY CENTRE, A BIODIVERSITY AND BIOSAFETY ASSOCIATION, AN ECUMENICAL WATER NETWORK, A NETWORK OF WATER RIGHTS INITIATIVES AND A CITIZENS' SERVICE FORUM — WITH ACTIVISTS FROM CAMEROON, GABON, GHANA, KENYA, MOZAMBIQUE, NIGERIA, SENEGAL, TANZANIA AND UGANDA. WATER AND ENERGY WORKERS' UNIONS on the same statement as community groups. The people who run the pipes have the most to lose from privatisation too, and a community campaign that has the utility's own union alongside it is far harder to dismiss as outside agitation. THE POSITION STATEMENT AND ITS BACKING: A POSITION STATEMENT OPPOSING WATER PRIVATISATION AND VOICING DEMANDS TO GOVERNMENTS, CORPORATIONS AND INSTITUTIONS, ENDORSED BY OVER 100 ORGANISATIONS FROM AROUND THE WORLD. A drafted position endorsed by a hundred organisations, free to sign. A local group facing a water contract does not need to write its own text from nothing. WHAT THE COALITION DEMANDS INSTEAD: THAT GOVERNMENT LEADERS INVEST IN PUBLIC WATER SYSTEMS THAT INCLUDE MEANINGFUL PUBLIC PARTICIPATION IN WATER GOVERNANCE, WITH PARTICULAR FOCUS ON THE PERSPECTIVES OF THOSE TYPICALLY LEFT OUT, INCLUDING WOMEN, LOW-INCOME PEOPLE AND RURAL COMMUNITIES. The demand is not simply no; it is public investment plus participation. Opposing without an alternative is the position this file records being dismissed most easily. WHO IT SAYS BENEFITS FROM PRIVATISATION: LARGE MULTINATIONAL CORPORATIONS, TWO NAMED FIRMS, AND THE SHAREHOLDERS THEY SERVE ARE THE PRIMARY BENEFICIARIES OF CORPORATE CONTROL SCHEMES LIKE PRIVATISATION AND SO-CALLED PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIPS, WHICH EXTRACT RESOURCES FROM THE CONTINENT AND FUNNEL THEM INTO FOREIGN BANK ACCOUNTS — DESCRIBED AS A DETRIMENT TO THE COMMUNITY, THE WORKERS AND THE STATE ITSELF. Two named firms, which is checkable. When a public-private partnership is proposed for your water, finding out which company is behind the bid is the first research task — and it may be one already documented here. HOW IT WORKS, IN ITS OWN WORDS: STRENGTHENING LOCAL COMMUNITIES, ORGANISING AND MOBILISING CITIZENS AND PUBLIC SERVICE UNIONS — WORKING CLOSELY WITH THE MEDIA AND PARTNERING WITH A STRONG NETWORK OF JOURNALISTS TO AMPLIFY COMMUNITY VOICES; ITS APPROACH IS TO STAND WITH COMMUNITIES AND BUILD THEIR CAPACITY TO INFLUENCE STATE AND CORPORATE POLICIES. A STRONG NETWORK OF JOURNALISTS is a resource in itself, and it is why a small campaign in one city produced continental coverage. THE FREEDOM OF INFORMATION ROUTE IT USES: IT HAS FILED A FREEDOM OF INFORMATION REQUEST WITH THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY DEMANDING COMPREHENSIVE LEGISLATIVE RECORDS — AND IT RUNS A JOURNALISM FELLOWSHIP, PUBLISHING AN ANNUAL REPORT DOCUMENTING ITS CAMPAIGNS. A freedom of information request to the legislature itself. Where a water or land contract is being approved quietly, the records of the approval are requestable — and this file's Eswatini entry records the same tactic used on a ministry with an answer of none. AND ITS STATED VISION AND ADDRESS: THAT AFRICA'S DEVELOPMENT PATH BE DESIGNED, MODELLED AND EXECUTED BY AFRICANS, WHILE RESPECTING HUMAN RIGHTS, PROMOTING SOCIAL JUSTICE AND PROTECTING THE ENVIRONMENT — NURTURING MOVEMENTS OF AFRICAN COMMUNITIES AND A NEW GENERATION OF LEADERS DEMANDING DEMOCRATIC COMMUNITY AND NATURAL RESOURCE GOVERNANCE, WITH A FULL STREET ADDRESS PUBLISHED. WHO IT SUITS: communities facing water privatisation, a public-private utility contract, or a mine or plantation taking their water — and coalitions wanting a water parliament format or a ready-endorsed position statement. CAVEATS: AN ADVOCACY AND CAMPAIGNING ORGANISATION, NOT A FUNDER, A LAW CENTRE OR A LAND-PURCHASE BODY; ITS DEEPEST WORK IS IN ONE CITY AND ONE COUNTRY WITH PARTNERSHIPS ELSEWHERE, AND ITS BROADER PROGRAMME COVERS FOOD, TOBACCO AND CIVIC SPACE ALONGSIDE WATER. For the complaint desk of the financier itself, Morocco's entry; for the parliamentary petition route on extractives, Zimbabwe's entry.

trackers.name: Church Land Programme, Pietermaritzburg — audits church landholdings diocese by diocese and helps resident communities negotiate transfer; the audits were also run by Nkuzi Development Association and the Surplus People Project
trackers.desc: ASK THE CHURCH WHAT LAND IT OWNS — AND WHO AUDITS IT — method and adjacency declared first: SEVENTH ACQUISITION-ONLY ROUND; THE AFRICA-WIDE MEDIAN ON THIS TAG HAS RISEN FROM ONE TO TWO OVER THE SIX ROUNDS SO FAR. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL HOSTS AND FOUR FACTS ABSENT, WITH TWO MATCHES UNDER MADAGASCAR AND SIERRA LEONE READ IN FULL AND FOUND TO BE A LEGAL DEFENCE FUND, LAND-LAW CLINICS AND A PARALEGAL METHOD. THIS FILE'S NIGER ENTRY COVERS THE COMMONAGE ACQUISITIONS BY ONE OF THE AUDIT ORGANISATIONS NAMED BELOW AND ITS SEYCHELLES ENTRY ANOTHER'S EVICTION SURVEY — NEITHER ABOUT CHURCH LAND, WHICH IS COVERED NOWHERE ELSE IN THIS FILE. NONE IS RESTATED. THE ASSET NOBODY ASKS ABOUT, WHICH IS THE FIND: A NATIONAL PROGRAMME INITIALLY FOCUSED ON CHURCH OWNED LAND WHILE ALSO CHALLENGING THE CHURCH TO ENGAGE IN THE NATIONAL LAND QUESTION — ITS WORK LATER SHIFTING TOWARD COLLABORATING WITH COMMUNITIES ON LAND AND HOUSING REFORM. Six acquisition rounds have gone to funders, lenders, savings federations and the state. The churches are the landowner nobody in this file has approached, and across Africa they hold a great deal — mission farms, diocesan estates, land occupied for generations by people with no title to it. A community living on church land is dealing with an owner that has to answer a moral argument as well as a legal one. THE AUDIT MECHANISM AND WHO RAN IT, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: DIOCESAN LAND AUDITS CARRIED OUT BY NAMED INDEPENDENT ORGANISATIONS — ONE DIOCESE'S AUDIT CONDUCTED BY A RURAL DEVELOPMENT ASSOCIATION, ANOTHER FACILITATED BY A LAND RIGHTS PROJECT, A THIRD CONTRACTED TO A PROVINCIAL AGENCY WHICH COULD NOT COMPLETE THE TASK, AND TWO FURTHER DIOCESES WHERE THIS PROGRAMME ITSELF IMPLEMENTED THE AUDIT. A LAND AUDIT is the instrument, and it is the first ask: what does this diocese own, where, and who lives on it. The audits were done by independent organisations rather than by the church itself, which is what made the answers usable — and one contracted agency simply failed to deliver, so who conducts it matters. THE TRANSFER COMMUNITIES ASKED FOR: BEFORE 1998, COMMUNITIES ON CHURCH-OWNED LAND AT MARIANNHILL MISSION OPENED NEGOTIATIONS WITH THE ORDER WITH THE IDEA OF TAKING TRANSFER OF THE LAND THAT THEY OCCUPIED AND USED FOR RESIDENTIAL PURPOSES AND AGRICULTURAL ACTIVITIES. The communities opened the negotiation themselves. There is no application form for this and no fund to apply to — the route is a direct approach to the order or diocese holding the title, and it has worked. A DOCUMENTED PARTIAL WIN AND ITS LIMIT: IN 1990 A CHURCH AGREED THAT 50 FAMILIES COULD SETTLE ON CHURCH LAND AT CLARKSON, TSITSIKAMMA AS A FIRST STEP TO RESTITUTION — BUT THAT CHURCH HAS BEEN UNWILLING TO GIVE RESIDENTS ON ITS LAND TITLE DEEDS TO THEIR HOUSES, AND ALSO LEASES LARGE PARTS OF ITS LAND TO COMMERCIAL FARMERS. Filed with the limit attached, because it is the pattern to expect: permission to occupy granted, title withheld, and the better land still leased commercially. Settlement without a deed is what this file records collapsing a generation later. Ask for the deed at the start, and ask what the church's other land is currently earning. THE MOVE TO WATCH FOR: OTHER CHURCHES SOLD THEIR LAND IN ANTICIPATION OF THE LAND REFORM PROGRAMME. Sold ahead of the reform. Where a claim or a policy is coming, the holder can dispose of the asset first — which is an argument for getting the audit done and the claim lodged before the intention becomes public. THE CHURCH BODY SET UP TO HANDLE IT: A REGIONAL CATHOLIC BISHOPS CONFERENCE ESTABLISHED A LAND DESK IN AID OF AND IN COOPERATION WITH THE GOVERNMENT'S REDISTRIBUTION PROGRAMME, WITH COORDINATOR PHILANI MKHIZE — THE CHURCH RECOGNISING THAT IT IS NOT JUST AN ACT OF HANDING OVER LAND TO COMMUNITIES, BUT THAT THE ESSENTIAL IMPARTING OF SKILLS IS CRUCIAL. A standing LAND DESK inside a bishops' conference covering several countries. That is an office a community or its priest can write to by name, and it exists to do exactly this. WHAT THAT DESK CONCLUDED WAS MISSING: SEED, IRRIGATION, CONNECTING SMALL-SCALE FARMERS TO THE MARKET AND THE IMPARTING OF SKILLS ARE ESSENTIAL TO THE SUCCESS OF LAND REDISTRIBUTION — AND THESE ELEMENTS ARE ALL TOO OFTEN COMPLETELY ABSENT. The same four-item gap this file recorded under Niger, reached independently by a church land office. Two separate bodies auditing two different programmes found the same thing, which makes it the strongest evidence in this file for demanding post-transfer support in writing. THE ASSUMPTION IT WARNS AGAINST: THERE IS AN ASSUMPTION THAT JUST BECAUSE A COMMUNITY HAS BEEN WORKING ON A FARM, OR LIVES IN A RURAL AREA, THAT THEY WILL HAVE AN INNATE ABILITY TO FARM — A TRIP TWO YEARS EARLIER HAVING PROVED HOW INCORRECT THIS ASSUMPTION IS. Worth saying plainly to any community about to accept land: farm labour and farm management are different trades, and the training has to be negotiated as part of the transfer rather than assumed. THE ALTERNATIVE INSTRUMENT IT POINTS TO: LONG-TERM LEASE AGREEMENTS WORK WELL IN MANY PARTS OF THE CONTINENT, ONE NEIGHBOURING COUNTRY BEING THE CLOSEST AND MOST OBVIOUS WORKING EXAMPLE. Where a church will not transfer the freehold, a long lease is the fallback to name — and it is what is already normal in several African land systems. HOW THE PROGRAMME WORKS WITH PEOPLE: THROUGH A PROCESS OF ANIMATION WITH GROUPS OF POOR PEOPLE TO CREATE UNIQUE RESPONSES TO THEIR UNIQUE SITUATIONS, AND TO AFFIRM, LEARN FROM AND JOURNEY WITH THOSE WHO ARE SYSTEMATICALLY EXCLUDED, SUPPORTING PEOPLE'S STRUGGLES TO REGAIN THEIR COLLECTIVE POWER — WITH A PUBLISHED STREET ADDRESS, TELEPHONE NUMBER AND EMAIL. WHO FOUNDED IT AND FROM WHERE: INITIATED IN 1996 AS A JOINT PROJECT BETWEEN A RURAL ADVANCEMENT ASSOCIATION AND A CHRISTIAN SOCIAL AWARENESS AGENCY, INDEPENDENT FROM 1997 — THE SECOND FOUNDER FORMED IN 1979 BY WHITE CHRISTIANS TO EDUCATE WHITE CHURCHES ON THE EFFECTS OF APARTHEID ON BLACK PEOPLE. Two existing organisations spun out a third to do one job. Worth noting as a structure: where a task sits awkwardly inside both, a joint project given its own registration can do what neither could. AND THE PUBLISHING ARM IT RUNS: AN INITIATIVE BEGUN IN 2010 AS AN EMAIL LIST TO PROVIDE AND SHARE RESOURCES, SINCE EXPANDED, WHOSE MATERIAL IS MEANT TO BE SEASONAL, LOCALLY-GROUNDED AND NUTRITIOUS — THE ORGANISATION DEVELOPING ITS OWN MATERIALS TO RAISE AWARENESS ON THE LAND DEBATE. An email list is what it started as, and it cost nothing. WHO IT SUITS: communities living on mission, diocesan or other church-held land anywhere in Africa who want an audit done and a transfer negotiated — and organisers who have not yet asked who owns the land their settlement sits on. CAVEATS: THE PROGRAMME ITSELF IS ONE COUNTRY'S AND THE CASES ARE FROM ITS LAND REFORM ERA, THOUGH CHURCH LANDHOLDING AND DIOCESAN LAND DESKS EXIST WIDELY; IT ANIMATES, AUDITS AND ACCOMPANIES RATHER THAN FUNDING PURCHASES OR LITIGATING, AND ONE DOCUMENTED CASE ENDED IN OCCUPATION WITHOUT TITLE. For the commonage acquisitions and the post-transfer failure rate, Niger's entry; for the eviction survey that found only 1% went through a court, Seychelles' entry.

trackers.name: Ligue Iteka
trackers.desc: Burundi’s oldest human-rights organization, founded in 1991 and forced into exile since the 2015 crisis — through a network of monitors inside the country it documents killings, torture, enforced disappearances, arbitrary arrest and illegal detention, and catastrophic prison conditions (national prisons running at over 300% of capacity), publishing weekly ‘Iteka n’Ijambo’ bulletins and quarterly and annual human-rights reports even as the government brands it an ‘enemy of the nation’ and refuses to recognize its findings.

trackers.name: Cour des comptes du Burundi
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Burundi — audits government accounts and the use of public money.

trackers.name: Burundi — Ministère des Finances, du Budget et de l’Économie Numérique
trackers.desc: National budget authority; designs & implements financial policy and prepares the State budget, Burundi. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Burundi.

trackers.name: Burundi — Agence de Développement du Burundi (Guichet Unique / Registre de Commerce)
trackers.desc: National corporate registry; the Agence de Développement du Burundi (ADB, successor to the API) runs the Guichet Unique de création d’entreprises — the single entry point hosting the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés & business-creation formalities, Burundi. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: COMIFAC Treaty and Plan de Convergence — and its community protocol
trackers.desc: A TREATY BODY WITH A TEMPLATE YOU CAN COPY. The Traité relatif à la conservation et à la gestion durable des écosystèmes forestiers d'Afrique Centrale, signed by heads of state at their second summit on 5 February 2005 in Brazzaville, instituted the Commission des Forêts d'Afrique Centrale — described as the unique instance d'orientation, de décision et de coordination for subregional forest action, and the cadre politique et juridique global for cooperation in the field. A transboundary forest question belongs in that forum. The Plan de Convergence is the reference framework for all such interventions — first edition 2005–2014, revised in 2014 for 2015–2025 and restructured into 10 strategic axes, executed by a Secrétariat exécutif. CIVIL SOCIETY IS A NAMED STAKEHOLDER in implementing it, alongside state administrations, CEEAC and the private sector — so participation is built into the framework, not conceded case by case. Axis 7 covers capacity and participation des acteurs, expressly contemplating micro-projets générateurs de revenus pour les populations locales; axis 9 covers innovative financing mechanisms. THE DOCUMENT LIBRARY IS THE MOST USEFUL PART: COMIFAC publishes a worked Protocole Bioculturel Communautaire for a named village, a guide to inventorying genetic resources and traditional knowledge, a paper on les droits d'usage des peuples autochtones et communautés locales et les obligations qui en découlent, a subregional APA (access and benefit-sharing) strategy, and directives on forests and the SDGs built with FAO as 5 principles and 12 directives across 31 prioritised targets. A community biocultural protocol published by a treaty body is a template, not a theory. AND ITS OWN DIAGNOSIS IS QUOTABLE: the Plan records that participatory natural resource management and mediation of use conflicts, though already mapped out, are insufficiently developed.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: ODEB — Burundi's first environmental civil society organisation, and the route by which local groups sign co-management memoranda over protected areas
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Organisation pour la Défense de l'Environnement au Burundi, created and legally recognised in 1992 — the first civil society organisation in the country working on environmental protection, with its own legal personality and working contacts among official decision-makers and international environmental bodies. Its stated mission includes supporting populations that take initiatives for ecologically sustainable development and conducting relentless advocacy, which is the closest thing Burundi has to a standing environmental defence body. WHAT THE ROUTE ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE HERE, and it is worth knowing before you approach anyone: protected areas are managed by the state environment office, which works with local associations and groupings — community protection support committees have been set up at protected areas, and memoranda of collaboration have been signed between the state office and four local groupings at one forest reserve, under a project run by a consortium of Burundian environmental associations with international small-grants funding. So a village grouping can hold a written co-management relationship over a reserve; the documented path to it runs through an established national association acting as intermediary. Address: 18 avenue des États-Unis, Rohero 2, Bujumbura. WHO IT SUITS: local groupings and associations near forests, wetlands and protected areas in Burundi that want recognition as a management partner rather than to be treated as encroachers. CAVEATS: NO LIVE CANONICAL WEBSITE FOR ODEB WAS VERIFIED — this entry points at the national biodiversity clearing-house record for the organisation, and a domain seen on its social media was not confirmed; treat the organisation as the contact and this as the record. It is an awareness, advocacy and support organisation, not a law firm; no intake route or fee information exists, and Burundian civic space is narrow.

trackers.name: ABO Burundi and the site support groups around Kibira — and the reason an EIA objection in Burundi may have nothing behind it
trackers.desc: WHO WORKS WITH PARK-EDGE COMMUNITIES: the Association Burundaise pour la protection des Oiseaux (ABO), created by ministerial ordinance n°530/231 of 8 April 2000 to protect the natural environment through the study and safeguarding of biodiversity, and working on the preservation and rehabilitation of ecosystems and natural habitats. Around the Kibira National Park it works with the neighbouring population on forestry and fruit-tree activities on the Mutana and Rukoma hills in Kayanza province, and runs awareness work aimed at the environmental police, the local administration and forest guards. THE STRUCTURE TO ASK FOR BY NAME: with an international birds partner it has set up income-generating projects for park-edge residents — goat rearing among them — organised through SITE SUPPORT GROUPS: standing local groups attached to a particular site, which give park-edge residents a recognised collective identity in dealings with the park administration. If you live beside a protected area and have no committee, this is the cheapest structure to form — it exists in law nowhere, but it gives you one name and one voice at the park gate. THE LEGAL PICTURE, STATED HONESTLY BECAUSE IT CHANGES WHAT IS WORTH ATTEMPTING: Burundi's environment code sets out the fundamental rules for protecting and managing the environment, BUT NO DECREE HAS BEEN ISSUED TO APPLY ITS PROVISIONS, INCLUDING ON ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT; and the land code contains no provision favouring conservation of natural areas and conflicts with the forest code on the cession or concession of wooded land. So an EIA objection in Burundi may have no implementing decree behind it — ask what instrument the decision is actually being made under before you build a case on the code. Protected areas themselves are administered by the national environment and nature conservation institute. WHO IT SUITS: Burundian communities living beside Kibira or other protected areas, seeking a recognised group and livelihood support rather than confrontation. CAVEATS: NO VERIFIED SITE OF ITS OWN — this entry points at the international partner's Burundi page; ABO is a conservation association, NOT a legal service, a fund or an advocate against a project, and Burundian civic space is tightly constrained. For the country's first environmental civil society organisation, Burundi's ODEB entry.

trackers.name: Burundi's legal clinics — free advice AND representation for people who could otherwise never reach a court, in a country where land conflicts are the common case
trackers.desc: WHERE TO GET FREE LEGAL HELP: legal clinics established in Burundi over recent years to bring justice closer to citizens, which provide FREE LEGAL ADVICE AND REPRESENTATION to people who would otherwise have no means of accessing the courts — a documented clinic operates at RUYIGI, in the east. WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT RESOURCE FOR BURUNDI SPECIFICALLY, in the reporting's own terms: access to justice remains fraught with obstacles despite progress; CONFLICTS OVER LAND ARE COMMON; and EVEN EDUCATED BURUNDIANS OFTEN LACK UNDERSTANDING OF LEGAL PROCEDURES and the requirements involved. That last point is the one to take seriously — if literate, schooled people cannot navigate the procedure, the barrier is the procedure, and what you need first is somebody who has done it before, not a better argument. The documented case is exactly the kind this file exists for: a woman in her seventies whose struggle to reclaim her late parents' land was long and painful, and who reached the clinic when nothing else was open to her. Inheritance is how most Burundian land disputes begin, and a widow or daughter contesting a family claim is the commonest client — go early, before the parcel is re-occupied. WHO IT SUITS: Burundians with a land, inheritance or succession dispute and no money for a lawyer, particularly older women and returnees. CAVEATS: THE CLINICS HAVE NO STANDALONE SITE — this entry points at the supporting organisation's published account, which names Ruyigi; coverage is by clinic rather than national, so confirm the nearest one and its days. Burundian civic space is tightly constrained and the national land commission recorded elsewhere in this file withdrew from at least one province, so do not count on it. For conservation and park-edge community structures, Burundi's ODEB and ABO entries.

trackers.name: Burundi's GEF small grants programme — 21 civil society organisations funded in the eighth cycle, with an ICCA window for community-conserved territories
trackers.desc: WHERE TO APPLY FOR MONEY: the Programme de Microfinancements du FEM (PMF/FEM) — the Global Environment Facility Small Grants Programme — run in Burundi with the UN development programme. Its EIGHTH OPERATIONAL PHASE was launched on 5 August 2026 in Bujumbura, and TWENTY-ONE CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS received financing agreements for projects on environmental protection, biodiversity conservation and climate adaptation. Twenty-one grants to civil society organisations in one cycle is the largest documented number of community-level environmental grants in any country in this file — this is a real window, not a notional one. WHAT THE NEW CYCLE ADDED, AND IT IS THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR LAND: selection was described as particularly competitive, the retained projects now integrate REINFORCED COMMUNITY RESILIENCE CRITERIA, and the cycle carries unprecedented co-financing under the second phase of the GLOBAL INITIATIVE ON INDIGENOUS AND COMMUNITY CONSERVED TERRITORIES AND AREAS (ICCA-GSI). An ICCA window is money specifically for territories communities already conserve — the same instrument recorded in Burkina Faso's APAC entry, and it is open in Burundi now. THE THREE FINANCING STREAMS BEHIND IT, so you ask for the right one: the global environment facility itself, funding climate, biodiversity, land restoration, international waters and waste; STAR funds mobilised through the environment, agriculture and livestock ministry, promoting sustainable agriculture and HILLSIDE COLLECTIVE IRRIGATION; and the ICCA co-financing. Note also the constraint the national environment office states openly: it lacked the expertise and data to fill in climate-fund application dossiers, and needed training to write concept notes — if the state office found the forms hard, budget for help with yours. WHO IT SUITS: Burundian community organisations and associations with a conservation, restoration, agriculture or climate project — especially one on land the community already protects. CAVEATS: A DONOR-CYCLE PROGRAMME with competitive selection and fixed calls — confirm whether the current phase is open; it funds environmental projects, NOT litigation or land purchase. For park-edge site support groups, Burundi's ABO entry; for the first environmental civil society organisation, ODEB; for free legal advice and representation, the legal clinics entry.

trackers.name: Burundi's forest code — a planted woodlot belongs to whoever made it, if you hold real rights over the land; plus the state woodlots handed to communities to co-manage
trackers.desc: PLANT IT AND IT IS YOURS — WITH ONE CONDITION THAT DECIDES EVERYTHING: Burundi's forest code provides that BOISEMENTS BELONG TO THE NATURAL OR LEGAL PERSONS WHO MADE THEM OR HAD THEM MADE, SUBJECT TO THOSE PERSONS HOLDING REAL RIGHTS OVER THE LAND SO REFORESTED. Establish your right to the ground FIRST, then plant — in that order. Trees planted on land you cannot show a real right to belong to whoever can, and Burundi's forest domain is otherwise included in the PUBLIC DOMAIN of the state and the collectivities. The forest code was REVISED BY LOI N°1/07 OF 15 JANUARY 2016, whose objects include ending the reduction of forest cover, sustainable management, and significantly increasing the area of PROTECTED forest and of sustainably managed forest; protected areas are governed separately by loi n°1/10 of 30 May 2011 on the creation and management of protected areas. WHAT CATEGORY YOUR TREES FALL IN: Burundian forest formations are classed as NATURAL FORMATIONS, and BOISEMENTS that are DOMANIAL (state), COMMUNAL, or PRIVATE — the last including MICRO-BOISEMENTS; agroforestry covers roughly 60,000 ha, and most forest products people actually use come from plantations, wooded islets and agroforestry systems rather than natural forest, of which only about 6.6% of the territory remains. A micro-boisement or a family woodlot is a recognised legal category in Burundi, not an informality — which makes tree-planting one of the cheapest tenure acts available to a household. THE COMMUNITY ROUTE, DOCUMENTED AS A PILOT: the forests minister launched an experimental COMMUNITY MANAGEMENT approach over TWO PILOT STATE WOODLOTS in the north — 65 HA in Gashikanwa commune, Ngozi province, and 30 HA on Ntamba hill — under an instrument establishing PARTICIPATORY MANAGEMENT (AMÉNAGEMENT PARTICIPATIF) OF STATE WOODLOTS to reconcile poverty reduction with sustainable management, requiring the forest administration to RESPONSABILISER local populations in managing forest resources. Ask whether a state boisement near you has been placed under participatory management — the pilots are small and named, so the precedent is concrete. Note that exploitation of state AND COMMUNAL forests requires MANAGEMENT PLANS APPROVED by the forest administration. WHO IT SUITS: Burundian households, hills and communes planting or holding woodlots. CAVEATS: OWNERSHIP OF TREES FOLLOWS RIGHTS IN LAND, and land pressure and inheritance disputes are Burundi's dominant land problem; the code was under revision alongside the land code. For free advice and representation, Burundi's legal clinics entry; for 21 civil-society grants and the ICCA window, the GEF Small Grants entry; for park-edge groups, ABO.

trackers.name: Burundi's land watchdogs — the OAG, which published the land commission's members and their political affiliations, FOCODE, OLUCOME, and the commune land office
trackers.desc: WHO WATCHES THE LAND COMMISSION, in a country whose defining dispute is who gets their hill back: the OBSERVATOIRE DE L'ACTION GOUVERNEMENTALE (OAG), Bujumbura, published an ANALYSIS OF THE ORGANISATION AND FUNCTIONING OF THE COMMISSION NATIONALE TERRES ET AUTRES BIENS (CNTB) — the body that decides restitution claims — subtitled as a thorn in the process of peace consolidation and national reconciliation, and THE OAG PUBLISHED THE LIST OF THE CNTB'S PERMANENT MEMBERS TOGETHER WITH THEIR POLITICAL AFFILIATIONS. An organisation that will publish who sits on the commission deciding your land claim, and which party each of them belongs to, is the most useful kind of ally there is. Ask the OAG for the current membership before your file is heard — knowing who will decide is half of preparing. WHO ELSE SPEAKS ON LAND: the FORUM POUR LA CONSCIENCE ET LE DÉVELOPPEMENT (FOCODE), Bujumbura, issued a public declaration that THE GOVERNMENT MUST GUARANTEE THE CNTB DOES NOT DEVIATE FROM ITS MISSION OF RECONCILING BURUNDIANS; and the OBSERVATOIRE DE LUTTE CONTRE LA CORRUPTION ET LES MALVERSATIONS ÉCONOMIQUES (OLUCOME), an INDEPENDENT NON-GOVERNMENTAL ANTI-CORRUPTION WATCHDOG that INVESTIGATES ALLEGATIONS OF CORRUPTION WITHIN THE BURUNDIAN GOVERNMENT AND BUSINESS SECTORS and is known to be critical of the government. If a land allocation near you smells of money rather than of law, OLUCOME is the body whose stated business is exactly that — and it is independent, which in this file's Burundi record is a short list. THE OFFICE NEAREST YOUR HILL: Burundi has established, by decree, a SERVICE FONCIER COMMUNAL — A LAND SERVICE AT COMMUNE LEVEL — alongside a COMMISSION FONCIÈRE NATIONALE with a permanent secretariat, and an INTERMINISTERIAL STEERING COMMITTEE FOR LAND REFORM chaired by the Second Vice-President. The commune land service is the closest registration desk to a rural family in this file's Burundi record. Ask what it can register and what it charges before assuming a title is out of reach — and note the law defines a SINISTRÉ broadly, covering the returnee, the displaced, the regrouped or dispersed, and THE WIDOW. The widow is named in the statute as a category of claimant. That is worth knowing before anyone tells a widow she has no standing. WHO IT SUITS: Burundians with a restitution or land claim, and communities facing an allocation that looks irregular. CAVEATS: WATCHDOGS AND ANALYSTS, NOT LAW FIRMS — and several records here predate recent political change; confirm current status and whether an organisation is still operating. For free advice AND representation, Burundi's legal clinics entry; for the first environmental organisation, ODEB; for site support groups at Kibira, ABO; for project money through 21 organisations, the GEF small grants entry.

trackers.name: Burundi's protected-area memoranda — four local groupings signed collaboration agreements with the OBPE at Bururi, the three-NGO consortium behind them, and the published register of approved local NGOs
trackers.desc: THE MEMORANDUM FOUR VILLAGE GROUPINGS SIGNED, WHICH IS THE INSTRUMENT TO ASK FOR BY NAME: management of protected areas in Burundi is carried out by the OFFICE BURUNDAIS POUR LA PROTECTION DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT (OBPE), a national institution under the environment ministry, WHICH IS SUPPORTED BY OTHER PARTNERS — NOTABLY LOCAL ASSOCIATIONS AND GROUPINGS, AND NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL NGOs. MÉMORANDUMS DE COLLABORATION BETWEEN THE OBPE AND FOUR LOCAL GROUPINGS WERE SIGNED AT THE RÉSERVE NATURELLE FORESTIÈRE DE BURURI, WITH THE SUPPORT OF A PROJECT IMPLEMENTED BY A CONSORTIUM OF THREE BURUNDIAN ORGANISATIONS — ABN, APRN/BEPB AND FCBN — ON FOREIGN ECOSYSTEM-FUND FINANCING. Four village groupings holding signed memoranda with the state agency that manages the reserve is the closest thing to co-management in this file's Burundian record. Ask the OBPE for a mémorandum de collaboration, and cite Bururi: the precedent is Burundian, recent, and involved four groupings at once rather than one. AND THE STRUCTURE UNDERNEATH IT: COMITÉS D'APPUI À LA PROTECTION HAVE BEEN PUT IN PLACE AT COMMUNITY LEVEL ACROSS THREE PROTECTED AREAS — with the official record itself stating that THESE COMMITTEES DESERVE REDYNAMISATION AND CAPACITY STRENGTHENING TO BETTER FULFIL THEIR MISSION. The state has written down that the community committees are under-supported. That is an admission you can quote when asking for the training and the running costs — you are not requesting a favour, you are asking for what the government's own document says is needed. WHO THE LEAD ORGANISATION IS: the ASSOCIATION BURUNDAISE POUR LA PROTECTION DE LA NATURE (ABN), A NON-PROFIT NGO GOVERNED BY THE DÉCRET-LOI N°1/011 OF 8 FEBRUARY 2000 ON ASSOCIATIONS SANS BUT LUCRATIF AND AGRÉÉE BY ORDONNANCE MINISTÉRIELLE N°530/231 OF 8 APRIL 2000, intervening in PROTECTED AREAS, WATERSHEDS (BASSINS VERSANTS), WETLANDS AND LANDSCAPES, whose aims include GATHERING THE FRIENDS OF NATURE AROUND THE OBJECTIVE OF ITS PRESERVATION, REHABILITATION AND SUSTAINABLE USE, working through local media and ENVIRONMENT CLUBS, WHICH IT CALLS THE SOUNDING BOARD FOR THE MESSAGE. ITS METHOD, WITH THE NUMBERS: a participatory approach in which COMMUNITY ASSOCIATIONS ARE INVOLVED IN IDENTIFYING RESOURCES AND MAJOR THREATS; WORKSHOPS INVOLVING 53 COMMUNITY MEMBERS TO IDENTIFY CHALLENGES AND DEVELOP ADAPTATION PLANS — which named HEAVY RAINS LEADING TO SOIL EROSION, LANDSLIDES, SEDIMENTATION AND WIND DAMAGE TO HOUSES as the most pressing; AND AT LEAST 267 COMMUNITY MEMBERS ENGAGED IN SETTING UP TREE NURSERIES AND GROWING TREES ON THEIR OWN CROPLANDS, with a named executive director stating that ABN supports communities AND the government TO INCREASE LAND PROTECTION THROUGH AGROFORESTRY. Trees grown on people's own croplands rather than on a project plot is why the planting survives — the owner of the land is the owner of the tree. Insist the nurseries go onto members' own ground. ALSO NAMED: ORGANISATION DE DÉFENSE DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT ET DE DÉVELOPPEMENT DURABLE (ODEB), A LOCAL NGO CREATED IN 1992, BUJUMBURA. AND THE REGISTER: BURUNDI'S APPROVED LOCAL NGOs ARE PUBLISHED AS AN OPEN-DATA FILE GIVING EACH ONE'S DATE OF APPROVAL, ORDINANCE NUMBER AND POSTAL ADDRESS — including named commune development associations such as ADECOB for Bururi and ADECOMA for Mabanda. A downloadable list of every approved NGO with its ordinance number lets you verify an organisation in one search, and shows that COMMUNE-level development associations are a registered category in Burundi — that is a form your own commune can take. WHO IT SUITS: Burundian communities beside a reserve, commune associations, and farmers wanting nurseries on their own land. CAVEATS: A DONOR-FUNDED CONSORTIUM PROJECT — confirm which memoranda are current. For the body that published the political affiliations of a land commission's members, Burundi's OAG entry; for the communal land service, the Service Foncier Communal entry.

trackers.name: FORSC — Burundi's principal civil society platform of 146 organisations still publishing on land crises and a forced title reform — and the de-registration of five organisations, with the bar council that refused to strike off their lawyer
trackers.desc: THE BAR COUNCIL REFUSED — hold on to that, because the rest of this entry is about how much pressure Burundian civil society has been under: A NAMED LAWYER FACED NUMEROUS MEASURES OF INTIMIDATION AND REPRESSION INCLUDING AN INTERNATIONAL ARREST WARRANT AND A DEMANDED STRIKING-OFF FROM THE BUJUMBURA BAR — AND THAT DEMANDED STRIKING-OFF WAS REJECTED BY A DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF THE ORDER OF ADVOCATES OF BUJUMBURA. A bar council refusing a government demand to disbar a lawyer is a real and citable act of professional independence. If your advocate is threatened with removal from the roll, the bar's own council is the body that decides — and there is a Burundian precedent of it saying no. THE PLATFORM: FORSC IS THE PRINCIPAL PLATFORM OF BURUNDIAN CIVIL SOCIETY, BRINGING TOGETHER 146 ORGANISATIONS. SET UP IN 2002, IT AROUSED THE INTEREST OF BURUNDIAN CIVIL SOCIETY MEMBERS IN CONCERTED WORK, AND WORKED TO CARRY OUT A DIAGNOSIS OF THE SOCIAL, ECONOMIC, POLITICAL AND SECURITY CONTEXT IN ORDER TO ARRIVE AT A SHARED VISION AND IDENTIFY COMMON ACTIONS TO CARRY OUT. A diagnosis first, then a shared vision, then common actions. That order is the method — and it is why a platform holds together: the members agreed what the situation was before they agreed what to do about it. ITS COMPOSITION IS THE USEFUL PART: ORGANISATIONS OF WOMEN, OF YOUTH, HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, ACTIVISTS WORKING ON GOOD GOVERNANCE, GRASSROOTS COMMUNITY GROUPINGS, JURISTS, TRADE UNIONS, MEDIA, JOURNALISTS AND OTHER ACTORS — AND IT HAS FREQUENTLY LED ADVOCACY ACTIONS TARGETING NATIONAL DECISION-MAKING BODIES. GRASSROOTS COMMUNITY GROUPINGS are a named member category alongside the unions and the jurists. A village grouping is eligible for the same platform as the lawyers — which is the point of a platform rather than a federation of professionals. AND IT STILL PUBLISHES ON LAND, WHICH IS WHY IT IS IN THIS FILE: recent items include A LAND CRISIS AND SUSPICIONS OF ILLEGAL MINING EXPLOITATION UNDER HEAVY MILITARY GUARD IN A NAMED LOCALITY, and A FORCED REFORM OF LAND TITLES IN BURUNDI DESCRIBED AS BETWEEN PRECIPITATION, LEGAL OPACITY AND RISKS OF MASSIVE DISPOSSESSION. A forced title reform carrying risks of massive dispossession is the kind of national change that reaches every rural household at once and is usually noticed too late. If a titling reform is underway where you are, find out who is publishing about it — in Burundi, this platform is. THE RISK THIS FILE OWES YOU, RECORDED PLAINLY: A MINISTERIAL ORDINANCE OF 19 OCTOBER 2016 DEFINITIVELY STRUCK FIVE NAMED BURUNDIAN ORGANISATIONS FROM THE LIST OF NON-PROFIT ASSOCIATIONS — A CIVIL SOCIETY REINFORCEMENT FORUM, A CONSCIENCE AND DEVELOPMENT FORUM, AN ANTI-TORTURE ASSOCIATION, A HUMAN RIGHTS AND DETAINEES ASSOCIATION AND A CITIZENS' NETWORK — AFTER THEIR ACTIVITIES HAD BEEN PROVISIONALLY SUSPENDED ON 23 NOVEMBER 2015. THREE GROUNDS WERE STATED: DEPARTING FROM THE OBJECTIVES SET OUT IN THEIR STATUTES; TARNISHING THE IMAGE OF BURUNDI; AND SOWING HATRED AND DIVISION AMONG THE POPULATION. A FURTHER ORDINANCE FIVE DAYS LATER PROVISIONALLY SUSPENDED OTHERS, INCLUDING AN ELECTORAL MONITORING COALITION, A JOURNALISTS' UNION AND A HUMAN RIGHTS LEAGUE. DEPARTING FROM THE OBJECTIVES SET OUT IN THEIR STATUTES is the ground to notice, because it is the one that turns your own founding document into the weapon. Write your statutes broadly enough to cover what you will actually do, and keep a record showing your activities match them. That is not legalism — it is the specific defence against the specific charge used here. AND THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST: SOME OF THESE ORGANISATIONS CONTINUE TO PRODUCE REGULAR REPORTS ON HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS. Struck from the register and still publishing. De-registration ends the legal person, not the work — and the platform whose site carries current land reporting is one of the five. Where the register is closed to you, documentation is what remains, and it still reaches people. THE ENVIRONMENTAL BODY, FOR THE OTHER HALF OF THE WORK: A BURUNDIAN NATURE PROTECTION ASSOCIATION IS A NON-PROFIT NGO APPROVED BY A NAMED MINISTERIAL ORDINANCE, INTERVENING IN THE PROTECTION OF THE NATURAL ENVIRONMENT — NOTABLY PROTECTED AREAS, WATERSHEDS, WETLANDS AND LANDSCAPES — AND IT BASES ITS ACTIVITIES ON REINFORCED AWARENESS-RAISING OF THE POPULATION AND OF THE POLITICAL AUTHORITIES, THROUGH LOCAL MEDIA AND THROUGH SUPPORT TO ENVIRONMENT CLUBS, WHICH CONSTITUTE THE SOUNDING BOARD FOR THE MESSAGE. Environment clubs as the sounding board, plus local media, plus the political authorities addressed alongside the population. In a constrained space that is a survivable model: clubs are small, local and hard to characterise as political, and they carry a message further than a press release. WHO IT SUITS: Burundian communities facing a title reform, a mine or a land dispute, and any group deciding how to write its statutes. CAVEATS: CIVIC SPACE IN BURUNDI IS SEVERELY CONSTRAINED and several bodies named here have been de-registered — this file records that rather than pretending otherwise; take local advice before contacting anyone. For the four local groupings that signed collaboration agreements at a forest reserve and the association with 267 community members in nurseries, Burundi's ABN and protected-area memoranda entry; for the country's first environmental civil society organisation, ODEB; for 21 civil society organisations funded through small grants, the GEF small grants entry; for the human rights league, Ligue Iteka.

trackers.name: Up to $5,000 to map your own area, from a network with two African regional hubs — funds usable for devices, events and training, no prior affiliation required, and a named person in the region to help before you apply
trackers.desc: ONE BILLION PEOPLE ARE MISSING FROM THE MAP — that is the organisation's own framing, and this file has met the consequence everywhere: WHEN A PLACE IS NOT ON THE MAP, THE MAP AN INVESTOR OR A MINISTRY LOOKS AT SHOWS EMPTY GROUND. THIS FILE'S LANDMARK ENTRY RECORDS THE SAME MECHANISM — UNMAPPED READS AS VACANT. THE MONEY AND WHAT IT BUYS: UP TO $5,000 IS AVAILABLE FOR COMMUNITY MAPPING PROJECTS THAT RESPOND TO A LOCAL CHALLENGE — AND THE FUNDS CAN BE USED TO PURCHASE DEVICES, HOST EVENTS, AND FACILITATE TRAINING TO PROVIDE THE TOOLS AND RESOURCES NEEDED TO COMPLETE THEIR OWN MAPPING PROJECTS. DEVICES is the item that unlocks the rest. Everything else in this file that a community can do with a phone — offline mapping, evidence video, boundary recording, deforestation alerts — assumes somebody owns the phone. This grant buys the handsets, and it is one of very few that will. THE ELIGIBILITY LINE THAT REMOVES THE USUAL OBSTACLE: APPLICANTS DO NOT NEED TO BE CURRENTLY AFFILIATED WITH THE ORGANISATION, BUT PROJECTS MUST CONTRIBUTE BROADLY TO ITS MISSION OF CREATING COMMUNITY-LED OPEN MAP DATA FOR HUMANITARIAN RESPONSE AND SOCIO-ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT. No prior relationship needed. That is rare enough among the funders in this file to be worth stating twice — you are not applying to a club you have to join first. THE TWO AFRICAN HUBS AND THE PERSON IN THEM: FOUR REGIONAL OPEN MAPPING HUBS EXIST, TWO OF THEM EASTERN & SOUTHERN AFRICA AND WEST & NORTHERN AFRICA — AND MICROGRANT RECIPIENTS ARE SUPPORTED THROUGHOUT THEIR PROJECTS BY REGIONAL COMMUNITY MANAGERS BASED IN THESE HUBS, WHO OFFER LOCALISED SUPPORT. THE HUB ENGAGES WITH OPEN MAPPING ORGANIZATIONS AND COMMUNITIES TO FACILITATE THE EXCHANGE OF IDEAS AND EXPERTISE ACROSS THE REGION. A regional community manager whose job is supporting grantees, based on the continent rather than in a distant office. Whether the grant is won or not, that is a person to introduce yourself to. THE OFFER MOST APPLICANTS NEVER TAKE UP: IF THERE IS ANYTHING YOU WOULD LIKE THEM TO SUPPORT YOU WITH IN ORDER TO STRENGTHEN YOUR PROJECT, LET THEM KNOW — FOR EXAMPLE BUILDING RELATIONSHIPS WITH OTHER MAPPING COMMUNITIES, SOURCING UPDATED IMAGERY FOR MAPPING PROJECTS, OR GUIDANCE ON HOW TO USE SOME OF THE TOOLS THEY HAVE CREATED. WRITE NO MORE THAN 150 WORDS. SOURCING UPDATED IMAGERY is buried in that list and is worth the whole application. Current satellite imagery of your area, obtained for you, is what shows the clearing that was not there last year — and communities routinely pay for it or go without. Ask for it in the 150 words. THE COLLABORATION PREFERENCE, WITH AN EMAIL TO HELP YOU MEET IT: PRIORITY WILL BE GIVEN TO APPLICATIONS THAT COLLABORATE WITH OTHER MAPPING COMMUNITIES IN THE REGION — COUNTRY SPECIFIC OR REGIONAL, INCLUDING ESTABLISHED COMMUNITIES, YOUTH MAPPER CHAPTERS, OR OTHER MEMBERS TO HELP WITH TRAINING AND VALIDATION — AND FOR SUPPORT IN SOURCING COLLABORATORS THERE IS A PUBLISHED EMAIL ADDRESS. They will find you the collaborator that their own scoring rewards. Write to that address before writing the application, not after — and note YOUTH MAPPER CHAPTERS: university mapping societies exist in many African countries and will map for a cause without charging. THE FIRST PROJECT PRINCIPLE, WHICH IS ALSO THE TEST OF ANY MAPPING OFFER: COMMUNITY-DEFINED PROJECT GOALS — GOALS WILL BE COMMUNITY-LED AND WILL ALIGN WITH THE COMMUNITY'S LONG TERM VISION, AND THE APPLICANT WILL CLEARLY EXPLAIN HOW THE ACTIVITIES LISTED REFLECT THE PROJECT GOALS. The funder is asking whether the community set the goal. So write the application from the community's decision outward, not from the technology inward — and if an outside organisation is drafting it for you, that is the sentence to check they got right. THE CONDITIONS, STATED PLAINLY: YOU WILL PROVIDE WRITTEN DOCUMENTATION AND RECEIPTS FOR ALL OF YOUR EXPENSES; AND YOU UNDERSTAND THAT THE DECISIONS MADE BY THE MICROGRANTS COMMITTEE ARE FINAL. Receipts for everything. Small grants are lost more often through missing paperwork than misspent money — appoint the person who keeps the receipts on the day the grant lands. THE EMERGENCY WINDOW: RAPID RESPONSE EMERGENCY MICROGRANTS FUND LOCAL MAPPING GROUPS IN PLACES MOST AT-RISK — AND GRANTS HAVE BEEN PROVIDED TO 27 COMMUNITIES ACROSS SEVERAL PROGRAMMES. THE FREE TOOLS AND THE FREE SCHOOL: A COMBINATION OF OPEN MAPPING TOOLS DEVELOPED BY THE OPEN-SOURCE COMMUNITY TO CREATE, ACCESS, MANAGE, ANALYZE AND SHARE OPEN MAP DATA — ALL OF THESE TOOLS AND RESOURCES ARE FREELY AVAILABLE FOR YOU TO USE — ALONGSIDE AN EDUCATIONAL WEBSITE FOR LEARNING THE MAPPING ITSELF. Free tools and a free school. The grant buys the devices and the training; the software costs nothing either way, so a community with two phones and an internet cafe can begin before any money arrives. THE INCLUSION COMMITMENT: BY INVOLVING WOMEN AND GENDER NON-CONFORMING PEOPLE IN MAPPING INITIATIVES, THEY ENSURE THEIR NEEDS ARE PRIORITIZED, ENABLING TARGETED AND EFFECTIVE INTERVENTIONS. Who holds the phone decides what gets mapped. If only men walk the boundary, the water points, gathering grounds and paths that women use will not appear on it — and this file has recorded that omission deciding compensation. WHO IT SUITS: African community groups and mapping societies that need devices, imagery and training to put their own area on the map. CAVEATS: ROUNDS OPEN AND CLOSE, AND ELIGIBLE COUNTRY LISTS VARY BY ROUND — check which is open before planning. For the platform where a boundary becomes a public record, Mali's LandMark entry; for the free offline tools where the community owns the data, Equatorial Guinea's entry; for the free system for rights neither registered nor registerable, Comoros' entry.

trackers.name: Accountability Counsel — the legal non-profit that takes cases only when a community asks first, publishes the criteria it screens by, refers on what it cannot take — and runs a free database of every community complaint ever filed against an internationally financed project
trackers.desc: THEY WILL NOT COME TO YOU. YOU HAVE TO ASK — adjacency declared first: THIS ORGANISATION'S NAME APPEARS INSIDE NIGERIA'S ENTRY ON AN AFRICAN DEVELOPMENT BANK REVIEW MECHANISM, A BANK INFORMATION CENTRE IS A HOST UNDER GUINEA, AND A SMALL-GRANTS CONNECTOR UNDER BURKINA FASO. NONE OF THOSE CARRIES THE REQUEST-ONLY RULE, THE SELECTION CRITERIA, THE REFERRAL PRACTICE OR THE COMPLAINTS DATABASE. THE REQUEST-ONLY RULE, AND IT IS THE FIND: ASSISTANCE BEGINS WITH A REQUEST FOR SUPPORT FROM THE COMMUNITY ITSELF OR A LOCAL CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATION — WE DO NOT SOLICIT COMMUNITIES FOR CASES; COMMUNITIES MUST DEMONSTRATE THAT WE ARE A WANTED AND TRUSTED PARTNER BY REACHING OUT TO US. An organisation that refuses to arrive uninvited. This file has recorded the opposite pattern repeatedly — outside bodies selecting a community as a case, running it their way, and leaving. Here the initiative must be yours, which means nothing happens unless somebody writes. Waiting to be found is the commonest way a community never gets help at all. HOW COMMUNITIES ACTUALLY REACH THEM: NEARLY ALL CASES COME THROUGH REFERRALS THROUGH CIVIL SOCIETY NETWORKS, OFTEN WITH ONLY ONE OR TWO DEGREES OF SEPARATION BETWEEN LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND THE ORGANISATION. One or two degrees. The national coalition, the paralegal group or the law clinic already working with you almost certainly knows somebody who knows them — so the practical step is asking your existing partner to make the introduction rather than writing cold. THE PUBLISHED SELECTION CRITERIA, SO YOU CAN JUDGE YOUR OWN CASE BEFORE ASKING: REQUESTS ARE SCREENED ON WHETHER THERE CAN BE A POSITIVE OUTCOME FOR THE COMMUNITIES AND WHETHER LESSONS FROM THE CASE CAN BE TRANSLATED INTO SYSTEMIC CHANGE; CASES MUST INVOLVE A TRUSTWORTHY LOCAL PARTNER WITH WHOM THEY CAN CLOSELY COLLABORATE; AND A CODE OF ETHICS IS PUBLISHED ALONGSIDE. A TRUSTWORTHY LOCAL PARTNER is a condition, not a nicety. Building that relationship first is therefore the preparation — and the code of ethics is published, which means you can read in advance what they will and will not do in your name. WHAT HAPPENS WHEN THEY CANNOT TAKE THE CASE, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: WE DO NOT HAVE THE CAPACITY TO TAKE ON EVERY REQUEST, SO WE ALSO SERVE AS A RESOURCE HUB — TRAINING COMMUNITIES AND ADVOCATES ON WHAT ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICES ARE AND HOW TO USE THEM, SHARING LESSONS FROM OUR CASES PUBLICLY, AND CONNECTING PEOPLE WITH ORGANIZATIONS WHO MAY BE BETTER ABLE TO SUPPORT THEM. A refusal comes with a referral. So the downside of asking is close to nothing: the worst outcome is being pointed at somebody better suited, which is itself the thing most communities in this file are missing. THE RANGE OF SUPPORT: FROM DEEP, MULTI-YEAR ACCOMPANIMENT THROUGH A COMPLAINT PROCESS AND ITS FOLLOW UP, TO A MORE LIMITED REVIEW OF KEY DOCUMENTS. A REVIEW OF KEY DOCUMENTS is the small ask worth making. Having someone experienced read the agreement, the resettlement plan or the impact assessment before you sign or object is a few hours of their time and can change everything — and it is far likelier to be granted than years of representation. THE WORKED OUTCOME, AND ITS CONTENTS ARE THE MODEL FOR WHAT TO DEMAND: HUNDREDS OF FARMERS AND THEIR FAMILIES, REPRESENTING NEARLY 4,000 PEOPLE, REACHED AN HISTORIC NEGOTIATED AGREEMENT WITH THEIR GOVERNMENT AND A DEVELOPMENT BANK CONCERNING THE TAKING OF THEIR FARMLAND FOR AN INDUSTRIAL PARK — PROVIDING REMEDIAL SUPPORT WITH A COMBINATION OF LAND, EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES, AGRICULTURAL EQUIPMENT AND TRAINING, AND SUPPORT FOR MICRO-ENTERPRISE FOCUSED ON WOMEN AND THE MOST VULNERABLE MEMBERS OF THE COMMUNITY. LAND, not only cash. That is the distinction this file has recorded communities losing again and again: compensation is spent and gone, replacement land is not. Ask for the settlement in the shape above — land first, then equipment and training, with a share ring-fenced for women and the poorest. OTHER RECORDED RESULTS: SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES TO PREVENT ABUSES IN TWO NAMED COUNTRIES, TO COMPEL REDESIGN OF A PROJECT IN A THIRD, AND TO REACH HISTORIC AGREEMENTS IN TWO OTHERS. COMPEL REDESIGN is worth noting as an outcome distinct from stopping or accepting. A project moved, re-routed or rescoped is a win, and it is the one most often available. THE FREE DATABASE: AN INTERACTIVE DATABASE OF EVERY COMMUNITY COMPLAINT EVER FILED TO EVERY ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICE — WITH TOOLS TO UNDERSTAND HOW AND WHY COMMUNITIES ARE HARMED AND TO IDENTIFY THE MAIN ROADBLOCKS AND BOTTLENECKS IN REACHING EFFECTIVE REMEDY, PLUS BENCHMARKING TOOLS TO COMPARE POLICIES AND PRACTICES ACROSS FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS. AND WHAT IT IS EXPLICITLY FOR: IF YOU ARE SEEKING JUSTICE FOR HARM CAUSED BY INTERNATIONALLY FINANCED PROJECTS, IT PROVIDES UNPARALLELED INSIGHT INTO WHAT OUTCOMES A COMPLAINT PROCESS CAN ACHIEVE, THE LIMITATIONS, AND HOW A PROCESS CAN DIFFER ACROSS MECHANISMS — SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES IN FILING MORE EFFECTIVE COMPLAINTS. Every complaint ever filed, searchable, with outcomes. Before spending years on one route, look up what communities like yours actually got from it — and which financier's office produced results. That is a decision this file has repeatedly recorded being made blind. THE TRAINING: THEY TRAIN LOCAL, REGIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS ON HOW TO EFFECTIVELY USE THESE OFFICES, AND THE GROUPS THEY TRAIN GO ON TO CONTINUE ADVOCACY IN THEIR COMMUNITIES, REGIONS AND COUNTRIES. AND THE AFRICAN STATUS, RECORDED HONESTLY: A GLOBAL TEAM WORKING FROM FOUR REGIONS DIVIDED EQUALLY BETWEEN THE GLOBAL SOUTH AND NORTH, WITH A REGIONAL PRESENCE IN ASIA AND BUILDING A PRESENCE IN AFRICA. BUILDING, not built. African coverage is the thinnest part of their footprint — so expect referral and training more often than representation, and treat the database and the training as the reliable offer. WHO IT SUITS: African communities harmed by a project financed by a development bank or international investor, working with a local organisation that can partner on the case. CAVEATS: REQUEST-ONLY, CAPACITY-LIMITED, AND THE AFRICAN PRESENCE IS STILL BEING BUILT — approach through your existing partner. For the review mechanism one person can now trigger, Nigeria's entry; for the trackers naming the financier behind a project, Guinea's entry; for the home-country complaint route against a foreign firm, Chad's entry.

trackers.name: An open database of bank credit flows and policy scores covering Central and West Africa — which publishes exactly why its African coverage is weak, names the gap in the company registers, and tells you what to do instead
trackers.desc: IT PUBLISHES WHY IT CANNOT SEE YOUR REGION, WHICH IS THE MOST USEFUL THING IN IT — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ANGOLA ENTRY COVERS THE COMMERCIAL BANK CAMPAIGNING ORGANISATION THAT LISTS THIS COALITION AMONG ITS PROJECTS; ITS BENIN ENTRY THE FOLLOW-THE-MONEY RESEARCH SERVICE; ITS GUINEA ENTRY THE INVESTOR TRACKERS; AND A NAMED INVESTIGATIVE ORGANISATION IS A HOST UNDER LIBYA. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PUBLISHED ADMISSION, AND IT IS THE FIND: MANY OF THE ACTORS THAT DRIVE DEFORESTATION IN CENTRAL AND WEST AFRICA DO NOT REQUIRE LARGE SYNDICATED FINANCING THAT IS USUALLY RECORDED IN THE FINANCIAL DATABASES. MOREOVER, THEY HAVE NOT LISTED COMPANIES AND THE COMPANY REGISTERS IN THE RELEVANT JURISDICTION DO NOT MAKE SUFFICIENTLY DETAILED COMPANY-LEVEL DATA AVAILABLE. THIS MAKES ACCESS TO INFORMATION ON FINANCIAL RELATIONSHIPS MORE DIFFICULT TO OBTAIN COMPARED TO COMPANIES THAT ARE LISTED OR REGISTERED IN COUNTRIES WHERE COMPANY REGISTERS PROVIDE DETAILED INFORMATION. A financial watchdog stating in public that it cannot see your region properly, and why. That is worth more to an African community than the database itself: it explains why every investor-tracing tool in this file comes back empty on the logging company next door — the company is unlisted, the loan is small, and the national register holds nothing. The failure is structural, not your research. AND IT NAMES THE OTHER HALF: MANY COMPANIES ACTIVE IN CENTRAL AND WEST AFRICA ALSO OBTAIN FINANCE FROM SOURCES THAT ARE NOT COVERED BY THIS DATASET, SUCH AS FROM INDIVIDUAL FINANCIERS. INDIVIDUAL FINANCIERS — a person, not an institution. No campaign against a bank reaches them, and no benchmark scores them.
