Where that is the case, the leverage is the buyer of the timber or the permit-issuing ministry instead, which this file's supply-chain and register entries address. WHAT IT TELLS YOU TO DO INSTEAD, PLAINLY: IF YOUR BANK IS NOT INCLUDED IN THIS EVALUATION, YOU COULD CHECK YOUR BANK'S WEBSITE OR ASK THEM DIRECTLY. Ask them directly. Unsatisfying, and it is the honest answer — and a written question creates a record of refusal that is itself usable. WHAT THE ASSESSMENT COVERS: 50 FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS SELECTED WITH THE MOST SIGNIFICANT EXPOSURE TO THE FOREST-RISK SECTOR IN SOUTHEAST ASIA, CENTRAL AND WEST AFRICA AND PARTS OF SOUTH AMERICA — WITH A LATER ASSESSMENT COVERING 200 INSTITUTIONS EXPOSED TO COMPANIES IN AREAS AT RISK OF DEFORESTATION. THE SCORING RESULT, STATED BLUNTLY: THAT ASSESSMENT SCORED 59% OF THEM UNDER ONE OUT OF TEN — DESCRIBED AS A SIGN OF AN ABJECT FAILURE TO MITIGATE ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL AND GOVERNANCE RISKS. Nearly six in ten scoring below one out of ten. When a bank tells your ministry it applies rigorous environmental standards, that figure is the sector-wide answer — and the scores are per-institution, so the specific claim is checkable. WHAT THE POLICY CRITERIA INCLUDE, WHICH DOUBLE AS QUESTIONS TO PUT TO A LENDER: WHETHER OPERATIONS IN PRIMARY FORESTS ARE PROHIBITED, AND WHETHER THE BANKS ARE SIGNATORIES TO THE MAIN INTERNATIONAL COVENANTS RELATED TO FOREST AND LAND ISSUES. Two questions any community can put in a letter. A bank that has not prohibited primary forest operations has said so by omission, and the omission is on the record. THE DATASET AND ITS SECTORS: UPDATED CREDIT FLOWS AND INVESTMENT HOLDINGS, ANALYZING 300 COMPANIES ACROSS SIX TROPICAL FOREST-RISK COMMODITY SECTORS — BEEF, PALM OIL, PULP AND PAPER, RUBBER, SOY AND TIMBER — OPERATING IN SOUTHEAST ASIA, SOUTH AMERICA, AND CENTRAL AND WEST AFRICA. RUBBER AND PULP beside palm oil and timber. Plantation crops this file has recorded arriving on African community land are all inside the definition, so search by sector when the company name yields nothing. THE HEADLINE FIGURE: OVER $395 BILLION DIRECTED TO THESE SECTORS SINCE A NAMED CLIMATE AGREEMENT, WITH $77 BILLION IN A SINGLE YEAR AND A HALF — AND FINANCING TO SECTORS LINKED TO DEFORESTATION CONTINUES TO RISE DESPITE INTERNATIONAL COMMITMENTS AIMING TO HALT AND REVERSE BIODIVERSITY LOSS BY 2030. The money went up after the agreements were signed. That is the counter to any assurance that global commitments have changed the lending — and it is measured rather than asserted. HOW THE DATA IS BUILT, WHICH TELLS YOU ITS LIMITS: FINANCIAL DATA FROM TWO NAMED COMMERCIAL TERMINALS AS WELL AS PUBLICLY AVAILABLE COMPANY REPORTS, TO IDENTIFY CORPORATE LOANS, CREDIT AND UNDERWRITING FACILITIES — RUN BY A COALITION OF CAMPAIGN AND RESEARCH ORGANIZATIONS INCLUDING A RAINFOREST ACTION NETWORK AND A DUTCH NOT-FOR-PROFIT FINANCIAL ANALYST ORGANISATION. Built from the same paid terminals a community cannot afford, then published free. That is the same barrier and the same answer as the open financial tools filed under Benin. ITS STATED PURPOSE: ESSENTIALLY AN EFFORT TO BRING MORE TRANSPARENCY AND ACCOUNTABILITY TO FOREST-RISK SECTOR FUNDING. THE REGULATION ASSESSMENT ADDED LATER: EXAMINING WHETHER CURRENT FINANCIAL SECTOR REGULATIONS ARE ADEQUATE TO STOP THE TIDE OF FINANCING FROM THE BANKS AND INVESTORS MOST RESPONSIBLE FOR TROPICAL DEFORESTATION, COVERING INSTITUTIONS IN FIVE NAMED JURISDICTIONS. AND THE POSITION IT ARGUES FROM: VOLUNTARY SOCIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL POLICIES ARE NOT ENOUGH TO STOP BANKS PROVIDING FINANCIAL SERVICES TO LAND-GRABBING COMPANIES OR FOREST-RISK COMPANIES. Said by the people who spent a decade scoring voluntary policies. Treat a bank's published commitment as a document to hold it to, not as protection — and put the regulatory demand to your own government alongside the campaign against the lender. WHO IT SUITS: Central and West African forest communities trying to identify who finances a plantation, logging or agribusiness operation — and those needing to understand why that search keeps failing. CAVEATS: ITS OWN CONTACT PAGE SAYS AFRICAN COVERAGE IS THE WEAKEST PART, MANY LOCAL FINANCIERS ARE OUTSIDE THE DATASET, AND IT IS A DATABASE RATHER THAN A SERVICE — pair it with research done on request. For that research service, Benin's entry; for the organisation that will feature your project in front of bankers, Angola's entry; for company directors and registries, Côte d'Ivoire's entry.

trackers.name: Conservation Evidence — a free database of which conservation actions actually work, each study summarised in one jargon-free paragraph — with a companion journal that is free to publish in, open access, and accepts papers as short as a page from practitioners
trackers.desc: FREE TO PUBLISH IN, AND A PAPER CAN BE ONE PAGE LONG — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ANGOLA ENTRY COVERS THE FREE ORGANISATIONAL SELF-ASSESSMENT PLATFORM, AND ITS SÃO TOMÉ ENTRY THE AWARD WHOSE USEFUL-LINKS PAGE RECOMMENDS BOTH. NEITHER IS RESTATED AND NEITHER HOST IS SHIPPED. THE JOURNAL THAT COSTS NOTHING TO PUBLISH IN, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT RUNS A PRACTITIONER-FOCUSED JOURNAL PUBLISHING THE RESULTS OF TESTING INTERVENTIONS; IT IS FREE TO PUBLISH IN THE JOURNAL, AND ALL PAPERS ARE OPEN ACCESS SO THAT OTHER CONSERVATIONISTS CAN READ THEM. Publication fees are what keep African practitioners out of the scientific record — hundreds or thousands of dollars per paper, which is why work done on this continent is so often written up by somebody else, elsewhere. Free to publish and free to read removes both halves of that. WHO IT IS FOR AND HOW SHORT A PAPER MAY BE: PAPERS CAN BE AS SHORT AS A PAGE AND THE EMPHASIS IS ON TESTING INTERVENTIONS, NOT ON SCIENTIFIC NOVELTY — HELPING CONSERVATION PRACTITIONERS WHO MIGHT NOT PUBLISH IN TRADITIONAL SCIENTIFIC JOURNALS TO SHARE THEIR WORK WITH OTHERS. One page, and novelty is not required. A community group that tried a fence design, a fire break, a grazing rotation or a nursery method and measured what happened has a publishable paper. That matters twice over: the knowledge travels, and the organisation acquires a citable publication — which every funder entry in this file treats as evidence of capacity. WHAT THE DATABASE IS: A FREE, AUTHORITATIVE INFORMATION RESOURCE DESIGNED TO SUPPORT DECISIONS ABOUT HOW TO MAINTAIN AND RESTORE GLOBAL BIODIVERSITY — SUMMARISING EVIDENCE FROM THE SCIENTIFIC LITERATURE ABOUT THE EFFECTS OF ACTIONS TO CONSERVE WILDLIFE AND ECOSYSTEMS. THE SCALE OF WHAT HAS BEEN READ FOR YOU: OVER 600 EXPERTS HAVE SUMMARISED THE EVIDENCE FOR THE EFFECTIVENESS OF OVER 4,000 CONSERVATION INTERVENTIONS ACROSS 29 SPECIES GROUPS, HABITATS OR OTHER ISSUES — SCANNING OVER 1.2 MILLION PAPERS IN MORE THAN 670 JOURNALS. Before designing anything, look up whether it has been tested. This file has recorded communities and funders repeating methods that were shown not to work years ago, because the literature sits behind paywalls nobody local can pass. THE NON-ENGLISH SEARCH, WHICH DETERMINES WHAT IS IN THERE: 53 MEMBERS OF A NAMED TRANSLATION PROJECT SEARCHED JOURNALS IN 16 NON-ENGLISH LANGUAGES, AND OVER 330 NON-ENGLISH-LANGUAGE JOURNALS HAVE BEEN SEARCHED, SO ADDITIONAL STUDIES WILL BE ADDED TO SYNOPSIS UPDATES. Deliberately looking beyond English. Worth checking whether francophone and lusophone African journals are among them — and if the work from your region is absent, that is an argument for publishing it in the free journal rather than assuming it does not count. HOW EACH STUDY IS PRESENTED: FOR EACH INTERVENTION, EACH SCIENTIFIC PAPER IS SUMMARIZED IN A SINGLE, JARGON-FREE PARAGRAPH, AND THE KEY MESSAGES ARE EXTRACTED FROM ALL PAPERS TO PROVIDE A QUICK OVERVIEW. JARGON-FREE, one paragraph per study. That is what makes this usable by a committee member rather than only by a scientist — and quotable in a submission to a ministry without a translator. THE EFFECTIVENESS RATING: A COMPANION ASSESSMENT PROVIDES EXPERT ASSESSMENTS OF THE EFFECTIVENESS OF ACTIONS, WITH 231 ADDITIONAL EXPERTS GENERATING A GENERALIZED, OVERALL EFFECTIVENESS CATEGORY FOR EACH ACTION. A category per action means you can say, on record, that a proposed mitigation measure is rated as having no evidence of benefit. When a developer's impact assessment promises to offset the harm by planting or relocating, that rating is the check — and this file has recorded such promises going unexamined for want of exactly this. WHAT A SYNOPSIS COVERS: THE EFFECTIVENESS OF ALL ACTIONS YOU COULD TAKE TO CONSERVE A SPECIES GROUP OR HABITAT OR TO TACKLE A SPECIFIC CONSERVATION ISSUE — SUBJECTS SO FAR INCLUDING AMPHIBIANS, BIRDS, MAMMALS, FORESTS, PEATLAND AND CONTROL OF FRESHWATER INVASIVE SPECIES. FORESTS and PEATLAND are both covered, which is directly relevant where a plantation, a drainage scheme or a restoration project is proposed on community land. THE FORMATS IT COMES IN: SYNOPSES ARE AVAILABLE INDIVIDUALLY, ONLINE — BOTH AS A DOWNLOADABLE PDF AND AS A SEARCHABLE DATABASE — AND SOME IN PRINT, AND ARE COMBINED AS A SEARCHABLE DATABASE COVERING ANY HABITAT AND TAXON, ANYWHERE IN THE WORLD. DOWNLOADABLE PDF, so it can be taken offline and read where there is no connection. Download the synopsis for your habitat once and keep it. HOW TO SEARCH IT, IN ITS OWN WORKED EXAMPLE: SEARCH A SPECIES NAME TO SEE WHAT ACTIONS HAVE BEEN TESTED FOR IT; SEARCH THE WIDER GROUP TO SEE WHAT HAS BEEN LEARNED THAT YOU MAY WANT TO APPLY; OR SEARCH AN ACTION PHRASE TO SEE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF DIFFERENT METHODS. The middle one is the trick for African species with little literature: search the genus or family rather than the species, and apply what was learned elsewhere. THE CORRECTION ROUTE: IF YOU THINK EVIDENCE HAS BEEN MISSED, EMAIL THE PROJECT WITH THE DETAILS AND ATTACH IT — BUT IT HAS TO BE WORK THAT SCIENTIFICALLY QUANTIFIES THE CONSEQUENCES OF INTERVENTIONS, AND INTERVENTIONS ARE PERIODICALLY REVIEWED AND UPDATED USING SUGGESTIONS AND FURTHER LITERATURE REVIEWS. SCIENTIFICALLY QUANTIFIES is the bar, and it excludes an unmeasured account however true. Which is the argument for measuring: a community that counts before and after has something the database will take. AND HOW IT WAS BUILT: 290 ADVISORY BOARD MEMBERS — PRACTITIONERS, ACADEMICS AND POLICY MAKERS REPRESENTING THE GEOGRAPHIC RANGE AND EXPERTISE COVERED — REFINED THE SCOPE AND STRUCTURE OF EACH SYNOPSIS, ADDED ACTIONS AND SOURCES, AND REVIEWED THE PROTOCOL AND NEAR-FINAL SYNTHESIS, WITH COLLABORATORS LARGELY PROVIDING THEIR TIME FOR FREE. PRACTITIONERS on the boards alongside academics, giving their time free. That is why the actions listed are things somebody could actually do, rather than only things somebody could study. WHO IT SUITS: African community organisations, conservancies and practitioners deciding what to do — and any group with a measured result worth publishing free. CAVEATS: SCIENTIFIC EVIDENCE ON CONSERVATION ACTIONS, NOT LAW, FUNDING OR LAND RIGHTS, AND COVERAGE IS UNEVEN BY REGION AND TAXON — absence of evidence is not evidence of failure. For the free organisational self-assessment platform, Angola's entry; for the species funds that pay for the work itself, Niger's and Sudan's entries.

trackers.name: Tusk Trust — a grant-maker that says plainly it runs no open application process and works only through vetted partnerships — prioritising African-led organisations, paying travel grants for partners to visit each other, and awarding £225,000 by nomination to winners' own organisations
trackers.desc: NO OPEN APPLICATION — SO GET VETTED, AND GET NOMINATED — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ANGOLA ENTRY COVERS THE NO-DEADLINE SMALL-GRANTS FUNDER, ITS SOMALIA ENTRY THE ZERO-OVERHEAD FUNDER, ITS CAPE VERDE ENTRY THE INCUBATING FOUNDATION, ITS ZIMBABWE ENTRY THE CO-MANAGEMENT FOUNDATION. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE SELECTION ROUTE, STATED HONESTLY, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT DOES NOT OPERATE AN OPEN GRANT APPLICATION PROCESS; RATHER, IT IDENTIFIES AND DEVELOPS STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS WITH VETTED ORGANISATIONS. Filed precisely because it saves the wasted month. An organisation that reads the size of this fund and drafts a proposal is drafting into nothing — there is no form. Being found is the only route, which makes the visibility work below the actual application: symposia, awards, partner referrals and published results are how a small organisation becomes findable. WHAT IT SAYS IT PRIORITISES: LOCAL LEADERSHIP AND EXPERTISE — AFRICAN-LED ORGANISATIONS WITH IN-DEPTH KNOWLEDGE OF LOCAL CONTEXTS; COMMUNITY INTEGRATION — PROJECTS THAT SUCCESSFULLY ENGAGE COMMUNITIES AND USE CONSERVATION TO ALLEVIATE POVERTY; AND HIGH IMPACT. AFRICAN-LED as the first stated criterion, and poverty alleviation named as a conservation purpose rather than a side benefit. A community organisation is the target here, not the subcontractor. THE COLLABORATION FUND, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IT HAS FUNDED 35 COLLABORATION VISITS AND TRAVEL GRANTS BETWEEN ITS PROJECT PARTNERS OVER SIX YEARS — WITH ONE FULLY FLEDGED COLLABORATION PROJECT BETWEEN TWO NAMED PARTNERS ARISING FROM A SYMPOSIUM, AND FOUR MORE HOPED FOR. Money to go and see how another organisation does it. This file has recorded again and again that the most useful thing available to a community organisation is another community organisation that has already been through the same fight — and travel is what makes that real rather than an email. Thirty-five funded visits is a working precedent to point at when asking any funder for the same line item. THE AWARDS AND WHERE THE MONEY GOES: AWARDS TOTALLING £225,000 — A £100,000 AWARD FOR LIFETIME ACHIEVEMENT, A £75,000 AWARD FOR CONSIDERABLE COMMITMENT AND SIGNIFICANT IMPACT, AND A £30,000 WILDLIFE RANGER AWARD FOR FIELD-BASED INDIVIDUALS — WITH GRANTS PAID TO THE WINNERS' REGISTERED ORGANISATIONS OVER THREE YEARS. The money goes to the organisation, not the individual, and it is spread over three years. That makes an award a funding stream rather than a prize — and the ranger award reaches the people this file has recorded as least likely to be funded directly. THE NOMINATION RULE: SELF-NOMINATIONS ARE EXCLUDED ACROSS ALL AWARD CATEGORIES, AND RANGERS ARE ELIGIBLE IF ACTIVELY ENGAGED IN CONSERVATION OR ENFORCEMENT WITHIN PROTECTED AREAS — WITH RANGER JUDGING CRITERIA OF LEADERSHIP, INTEGRITY, COURAGE, RESILIENCE, COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND SUSTAINED TEAMWORK. You cannot nominate yourself, so somebody else must. That is a specific, small favour to ask of a partner organisation, a university contact or a national NGO — and it is the same relationship-building the reference requirement in this file's Angola entry demands. THE FOUNDING PREMISE: ITS FOUNDER ENVISIONED AN ORGANISATION THAT WOULD SUPPORT AND AMPLIFY PROGRESSIVE, LOCALLY-DRIVEN CONSERVATION INITIATIVES RATHER THAN IMPOSING TOP-DOWN SOLUTIONS. THE PROBLEM IT NAMES: IN-COUNTRY, COMMUNITY-DRIVEN ORGANISATIONS OFTEN REMAIN UNDER-RECOGNISED AND LACK THE RESOURCES NEEDED TO GROW — SO ITS WORK BOLSTERS LOCAL AFRICAN LEADERSHIP AND INCREASES THE PROFILE OF ORGANISATIONS AND THEIR TEAMS. PROFILE treated as a deliverable. Being unknown is diagnosed here as a funding problem in itself, which is worth naming when asking any supporter for help with communications rather than only with fieldwork. WHAT PARTNERS ACTUALLY RECEIVE: DIRECT GRANTS TO PARTNER NGOs AND RANGER TEAMS SUPPORTING HABITAT PROTECTION, ANTI-POACHING OPERATIONS AND COMMUNITY-BASED CONSERVATION, ALONGSIDE ADVOCACY AND CAPACITY BUILDING — AND, THROUGH ONE NAMED PARTNERSHIP, EQUIPMENT, TRAINING, MENTORING AND COLLABORATIVE DATA EXCHANGE TO PLAN, TRAIN, INITIATE OR ENHANCE FIELD DATA COLLECTION, ANALYTICS, INFORMATION MANAGEMENT AND REPORTING CAPABILITIES. Funding aimed specifically at an organisation's ability to collect and manage its own data. That capability is what turns a community's observations into the evidence every other entry in this file assumes it already has. THE CRISIS FUNDING ON RECORD: COLLABORATIVE FUNDRAISING INCLUDING A RANGER CHALLENGE CAMPAIGN PROVIDING CRISIS FUNDING — WITH RELIEF GRANTS RAISED THROUGH A CRISIS APPEAL SUPPORTING ONE NAMED CONSERVANCY WHEN TOURISM REVENUE COLLAPSED, ENSURING RANGERS COULD CONTINUE WORK WITHOUT FEAR OF BEING LAID OFF. Read beside the collapse recorded in this file's South Sudan entry, where a conservancy's rangers went unpaid when its donor went. Somebody runs a standing appeal for exactly that emergency. THE SCALE: FOUNDED IN 1990, MORE THAN £130 MILLION GENERATED, OVER 250 LOCAL PARTNER ORGANISATIONS AND RANGER TEAMS ACROSS MORE THAN 25 AFRICAN COUNTRIES — CURRENTLY SUPPORTING APPROXIMATELY 80 COMMUNITY-BASED PROJECTS ACROSS 24 COUNTRIES, PROTECTING OVER 50 MILLION HECTARES AND SUPPORTING OVER 9,000 RANGER LIVELIHOODS. THE BREADTH OF WHAT IT WILL BACK: THE FULL SPECTRUM OF AFRICA'S LANDSCAPES AND THREATENED SPECIES, FROM ICONIC MAMMALS TO A SEAGRASS-EATING MARINE MAMMAL OF THE INDIAN OCEAN AND AN ELUSIVE PRIMATE OF WESTERN AFRICA'S TROPICAL RAINFOREST — WITH PARTNERS RESOLVING THOUSANDS OF HUMAN-WILDLIFE CONFLICTS EACH YEAR. Marine and rainforest work alongside savanna, so coastal and forest communities are not outside the frame. AND THE US DONATION ROUTE IT USES: THROUGH A NAMED INTERMEDIARY, FOREIGN CHARITABLE ORGANISATIONS CAN RAISE FUNDS FROM UNITED STATES DONORS WHILE AVOIDING THE COMPLEXITIES OF ESTABLISHING A UNITED STATES CHARITY, SOLICITING TAX-DEDUCTIBLE DONATIONS WITH DEDICATED SUPPORT. The same problem solved a second way. This file's Somalia entry records a funder receiving American donations on an African organisation's behalf; here is a dedicated intermediary that exists to do only that. An African organisation with willing American supporters has two routes rather than none. WHO IT SUITS: established African-led conservation organisations and ranger teams seeking long-term partnership, travel money to learn from peers, or nomination for a funded award. CAVEATS: NO OPEN APPLICATION PROCESS AND NO FORM — PARTNERSHIP IS BY VETTING AND AWARDS BY THIRD-PARTY NOMINATION; ITS FRAME IS WILDLIFE AND SPECIES CONSERVATION, INCLUDING ANTI-POACHING ENFORCEMENT, SO A PURE LAND-RIGHTS OR POLLUTION FIGHT WILL NOT FIT. For a funder with no deadlines and an open form, Angola's entry; for the one that pays the bank fees, Somalia's entry.

trackers.name: IBJ (International Bridges to Justice), Geneva — country programmes in Burundi and DR Congo providing free defence counsel and monitoring police cells, and JusticeMakers fellowships of US$2,000–5,000 awarded to individual lawyers and defenders
trackers.desc: A LAWYER IN THE FIRST HOURS CUTS TORTURE BY UP TO 80% — method and adjacency declared first: TWO CANDIDATES WERE WITHDRAWN THIS ROUND BEFORE DRAFTING, BOTH ALREADY FILED — A TANZANIAN COLLECTIVE-TITLE ORGANISATION UNDER TANZANIA AND A CONGOLESE FREE LEGAL CLINIC UNDER THE REPUBLIC OF CONGO, THE SECOND WITH THE SAME FINDS ALREADY WRITTEN OUT. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL ABSENT. THIS FILE'S REPUBLIC OF CONGO ENTRY COVERS THE 24/7 DEFENDER HELPLINE AND EVACUATION GRANTS, ITS COMOROS ENTRY THE AFRICA-BASED DEFENDERS NETWORK, ITS CAMEROON ENTRY THE BODY DEFENDING LAWYERS AND JUDGES WHO ARE THEMSELVES HARASSED. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE TIMING FINDING, WHICH IS THE FIND: ITS EXPERIENCE HAS DEMONSTRATED THAT LEGAL ADVICE DURING THE INITIAL PHASES OF CRIMINAL DEFENCE REDUCES CASES OF TORTURE BY UP TO 80% — SO IT WORKS JOINTLY WITH DUTY COUNSEL AND COURT-APPOINTED LAWYERS. This file has recorded land defenders arrested again and again, and has answered with protection funds, helplines and relocation. None of them addresses the first night in a cell, which is when the damage is done. A lawyer present in the initial phase is the intervention, and the figure is the argument for spending money on duty counsel rather than on a campaign after the fact. WHAT IT PROVIDES AND WHERE: THROUGH ITS 8 COUNTRY PROGRAMMES IT OFFERS DIRECT LEGAL ASSISTANCE, TRAINS LAWYERS, ORGANISES ROUND TABLES FOR JUSTICE SECTOR OFFICIALS AND RUNS INFORMATION CAMPAIGNS ON LEGAL RIGHTS — WITH OFFICES INCLUDING FOUR NAMED COUNTRIES, TWO OF THEM AFRICAN. THE FREE ASSISTANCE IN ONE NAMED AFRICAN COUNTRY: SINCE 2016 IT HAS GRANTED FREE LEGAL ASSISTANCE TO ORDINARY ACCUSED AND CHARGED PERSONS WHO ARE INDIGENT OR VULNERABLE, AND/OR VICTIMS OF TORTURE — ACCOMPANIED BY MONITORING OF CELLS AND LOCK-UPS, PARTICIPATION IN PEACEKEEPING TASKFORCE MEETINGS, AND SUPPORT TO MILITARY JUSTICE; CARRIED OUT BY A LOCAL AFFILIATED ENTITY. MONITORING OF CELLS AND LOCK-UPS is the part worth knowing about: an organisation that already visits the places detainees are held has a route to a person the family cannot reach. And MILITARY JUSTICE matters where defenders are arrested by soldiers rather than police. THE SEED GRANTS AND WHO CAN APPLY: AN ACCESS TO JUSTICE COMPETITION AWARDING FELLOWSHIPS TO LAWYERS AND HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS FOR THE MOST INNOVATIVE AND SUSTAINABLE PROJECTS — US$2,000 IN ONE ROUND AND US$5,000 IN OTHERS, WITH A DETAILED PROPOSAL REQUIRED AND WINNERS CONNECTED TO A GLOBAL NETWORK OF SUPPORT; ONE ROUND WAS OPEN TO ANY FEMALE COMMUNITY ACTIVISTS, LAWYERS AND HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS. Money to an individual lawyer rather than to an organisation. Most funds in this file require a registered body with audited accounts; this one is a competition an individual defence advocate can enter alone, which is the shape that fits a country where the lawyer willing to take these cases is one person. THE AFRICAN ROUND ON RECORD: A COMPETITION FOR PREVENTION OF TORTURE IN FRANCOPHONE AFRICA AWARDED 10 DEDICATED LAWYERS, HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS AND LEGAL ACTIVISTS WITH FELLOWSHIPS — AND FELLOWS TO DATE HAVE INCLUDED INDIVIDUALS FROM 37 COUNTRIES. A francophone Africa round, run in French. This file has recorded francophone Central Africa as its thinnest region for legal help; this is a route that has already been opened there once. THE SIX JUDGING CRITERIA, PUBLISHED: INNOVATION; RELEVANCE; URGENCY; PRACTICABILITY; EFFICACY, MEANING THE PROJECT IS DESIGNED TO PRODUCE THE DESIRED IMPACT WITHIN A ONE-YEAR TIME FRAME; AND COLLABORATION, MEANING THE PROJECT WORKS JOINTLY WITH DOMESTIC GROUPS, INSTITUTIONS, LEGAL WORKERS, JUDGES, PROSECUTORS, POLICE, PRISON OFFICIALS AND PRISON GUARDS. The criteria are published, so a proposal can be written against them directly. Note that COLLABORATION explicitly includes police and prison guards — an application framed purely as opposition will score badly, which is worth knowing before writing one. THE WORKED EXAMPLES IT PUBLISHES FOR APPLICANTS: PLACE LEGAL AID LAWYERS AT POLICE STATIONS TO ENSURE ACCUSED PERSONS HAVE ACCESS TO COUNSEL; ESTABLISH CHILDCARE AT THE COURTHOUSE SO WOMEN DEFENDANTS CAN ATTEND PROCEEDINGS; DEVELOP A MOBILE ARRAIGNMENT COURT; CREATE ALTERNATIVES TO CUSTODIAL SENTENCING; AND ESTABLISH A MICROFINANCE LEGAL INSURANCE PRODUCT SO PEOPLE HAVE FUNDING TO SECURE COUNSEL. Five funded project shapes, published as examples. A LAWYER STATIONED AT THE POLICE STATION is the one that maps directly onto a community where arrests at a project site are routine, and LEGAL INSURANCE is a genuinely unusual idea: a village paying small sums in advance against the day someone is detained. THE FREE REFERENCE LIBRARY: A CRIMINAL DEFENSE WIKI BRINGING CASE LAW, CODES, TREATIES AND OTHER RESOURCES TO LAWYERS IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES — WITH ITS ELEARNING PROGRAMME AND THE WIKI RECORDING 15,276,212 INTERACTIONS BY THE END OF 2019, REACHING 106 COUNTRIES. Free codes and case law for a lawyer who cannot afford a subscription. Where a defender's advocate is working from an outdated printed code, this is the fix. THE PRO BONO PARTNERSHIP FOR LAW FIRMS: A LAWYER-TO-LAWYER PROGRAMME WHOSE BASELINE COMMITMENT IS TO CREATE AT LEAST ONE COUNTRY-SPECIFIC ELEARNING COURSE AND DEFENDERS MANUAL FOR PUBLIC DEFENDERS — THE ORGANISATION PROVIDING A TEMPLATE AND RESOURCES, THE PARTNER DEVELOPING THE COURSE WITH INPUT FROM LOCAL AFFILIATES, THEN WORKING WITH THE LOCAL BAR ASSOCIATION TO OBTAIN CERTIFICATION. BAR ASSOCIATION CERTIFICATION is the detail that makes it stick: a course that counts toward a lawyer's professional requirements gets taken, and one that does not gets ignored. Any organisation building legal training should seek that accreditation from the start. WHAT IT SAYS THE PARTNERSHIP GIVES THE FIRM: WORK ALLOWING LAWYERS IN THE POOREST AND MOST REMOTE REGIONS TO BUILD THE SKILLS TO PROTECT THEIR CLIENTS FROM CRUEL AND UNUSUAL PUNISHMENT; AND HIGH-LEVEL NETWORKING, SINCE EACH PROGRAMME REQUIRES THE FIRM TO BUILD CONTACTS WITH GOVERNMENTS, BAR ASSOCIATIONS AND LAWYERS. The pitch to the firm is stated openly, including what the firm gets out of it. Useful for any group approaching a commercial firm for pro bono help: name the benefit rather than only the need. THE THREE RIGHTS IT NAMES: THE RIGHT TO COMPETENT LEGAL REPRESENTATION, THE RIGHT TO BE PROTECTED FROM CRUEL AND UNUSUAL PUNISHMENT, AND THE RIGHT TO A FAIR TRIAL FOR EVERY MAN, WOMAN AND CHILD — IN FRAGILE OR CONFLICT-AFFECTED COUNTRIES. AND THE PUBLISHED ROUTES IN: AN APPLICATIONS PAGE FOR THE FELLOWSHIP AND A DEDICATED PUBLISHED EMAIL FOR SPECIFIC QUESTIONS — PLUS A ROLLING INTERNATIONAL INTERNSHIP TAKING LAW STUDENTS AND GRADUATES YEAR-ROUND, WHOSE PAST TASKS INCLUDED RESEARCHING CRIMINAL PROCEDURE AND PENAL CODES, SUPPORTING LOCAL PUBLIC DEFENDERS AND ASSISTING IN GRANT WRITING. The internship is a way for a national organisation to get research capacity it cannot pay for — including help writing the grant applications this file records communities failing at for want of a drafter. WHO IT SUITS: land and environmental defenders who have been detained or charged, the lawyers who represent them, and anyone wanting a seed grant an individual advocate can win alone. CAVEATS: ITS FRAME IS CRIMINAL DEFENCE AND TORTURE PREVENTION RATHER THAN LAND, PLANNING OR LAND PURCHASE — IT HELPS WITH THE ARREST, NOT THE PROJECT; ITS DIRECT PROGRAMMES COVER EIGHT COUNTRIES ONLY, THE COMPETITION ROUNDS ARE PERIODIC AND REGION-SPECIFIC, AND SOME FIGURES CITED ARE FROM EARLIER YEARS. For the 24/7 defender helpline and evacuation grants, the Republic of Congo's entry; for trial observation and support to harassed lawyers, Cameroon's entry.

trackers.name: Chad — Agence Nationale des Investissements et des Exportations (ANIE)
trackers.desc: National corporate registry; the ANIE (public agency, Loi 004/PR/07) runs Chad’s Guichet Unique for company creation — the single window registering businesses & handling investment & export formalities, Chad. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Chad — Ministère des Finances et du Budget
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Ministry of Finance & Budget manages public finances, prepares & executes the state budget, treasury & taxation and publishes budgetary information, Chad. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Chad.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: COMIFAC Treaty and Plan de Convergence — and its community protocol
trackers.desc: A TREATY BODY WITH A TEMPLATE YOU CAN COPY. The Traité relatif à la conservation et à la gestion durable des écosystèmes forestiers d'Afrique Centrale, signed by heads of state at their second summit on 5 February 2005 in Brazzaville, instituted the Commission des Forêts d'Afrique Centrale — described as the unique instance d'orientation, de décision et de coordination for subregional forest action, and the cadre politique et juridique global for cooperation in the field. A transboundary forest question belongs in that forum. The Plan de Convergence is the reference framework for all such interventions — first edition 2005–2014, revised in 2014 for 2015–2025 and restructured into 10 strategic axes, executed by a Secrétariat exécutif. CIVIL SOCIETY IS A NAMED STAKEHOLDER in implementing it, alongside state administrations, CEEAC and the private sector — so participation is built into the framework, not conceded case by case. Axis 7 covers capacity and participation des acteurs, expressly contemplating micro-projets générateurs de revenus pour les populations locales; axis 9 covers innovative financing mechanisms. THE DOCUMENT LIBRARY IS THE MOST USEFUL PART: COMIFAC publishes a worked Protocole Bioculturel Communautaire for a named village, a guide to inventorying genetic resources and traditional knowledge, a paper on les droits d'usage des peuples autochtones et communautés locales et les obligations qui en découlent, a subregional APA (access and benefit-sharing) strategy, and directives on forests and the SDGs built with FAO as 5 principles and 12 directives across 31 prioritised targets. A community biocultural protocol published by a treaty body is a template, not a theory. AND ITS OWN DIAGNOSIS IS QUOTABLE: the Plan records that participatory natural resource management and mediation of use conflicts, though already mapped out, are insufficiently developed.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: GRAMPTC — took a complaint against the World Bank's lender on behalf of 25,220 farmers in the Doba oil zone, and got it declared admissible
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Groupe de Recherches Alternatives et de Monitoring du Projet Pétrole Tchad-Cameroun, a non-profit founded in 2001 and registered in December 2001 under folio 1226, working on the environmental, social and economic impacts of oil production. WHAT IT DID, WHICH IS THE LARGEST COMMUNITY COMPLAINT IN THIS FILE: with six other organisations it filed a complaint in October 2011 on behalf of 25,220 farmers from 25 villages of the Doba oil zone against the World Bank Group's private-sector lender, over the land take of the oil installations, pollution damage to crops and livestock, inadequate compensation, restricted movement between villages under a de facto night curfew, and the absence of monitoring. The complaints office found it eligible in January 2012 and held 115 individual and 25 community complaints admissible, then sent a mission to meet the affected people. WHY YOU SHOULD READ ITS RESEARCH BEFORE ACCEPTING ANY COMPENSATION OFFER: GRAMPTC's field studies found that compensation for crops was still being paid at the prices used in the 1995 environmental impact study while market prices had risen sharply, that goods to be destroyed were miscounted or misidentified, and that on the sites it surveyed the restored topsoil was a fraction of the required depth, with some 76 hectares of farmland effectively lost. Compensation frozen at the price list in the original impact study is a pattern worth checking anywhere. It publishes a monthly bulletin, La Lettre de Transparence, and has continued to press on newer operators. B.P. 4021, N'Djaména Moursal. WHO IT SUITS: farming communities in Chad's oil zone facing land take, pollution or a compensation offer. CAVEATS: NO LIVE ORGANISATIONAL WEBSITE WAS VERIFIED, so this entry carries no URL rather than pointing at a third party — its bulletins are mirrored on Chadian research-centre sites. It is a research and monitoring body, not a law firm; the complaint route produced assessment and negotiation, not an order; and much of the published record dates from the 2011-2013 period.

trackers.name: Chad's three legal assistance services — APLFT, the women lawyers' association and the public interest law centre
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: three Chadian organisations that offer legal advice and judicial assistance, from providing information through to assistance BEFORE THE COURTS — the Association pour la Promotion des Libertés Fondamentales au Tchad (APLFT), the Association des Femmes Juristes du Tchad (AFJT), and the Public Interest Law Center (PILC). They were supported together under a two-year access-to-justice programme for people in vulnerable situations, funded by the European Union and run with an international lawyers' organisation. APLFT was founded on 9 June 1991 and recognised in June 1992; it works through standing commissions including “assistance et conseil juridiques” and one on women's and children's rights, publishes a monthly bulletin on fundamental freedoms, and has hundreds of active members in Chadian towns beyond the capital. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR LAND IN CHAD SPECIFICALLY: pressure on land in the far south is severe — farmland expanding onto traditional grazing areas, herders migrating in from neighbouring countries, and agropastoral conflicts that reached unprecedented levels between 2021 and 2024, with more than a thousand people killed and over two thousand injured, in provinces where a majority live below the poverty line. Most Chadian land disputes are not company-versus-village but neighbour-versus-neighbour under demographic pressure, and the resource that fits is a legal advice service, not a campaign. WHO IT SUITS: Chadians facing land disputes, farmer-herder conflict, expropriation or any matter needing advice or representation, especially women. CAVEATS: NO VERIFIED LIVE SITE WAS FOUND FOR ANY OF THE THREE — this entry points at the international lawyers' organisation's published record of the joint programme; some details date from the programme period and should be confirmed locally. These are general legal-aid and human rights services, not land specialists. For the oil zone and the complaint route to a project's financier, Chad's GRAMPTC entry.

trackers.name: Chad's Fonds Spécial en faveur de l'Environnement — calls for proposals open to associations, with training workshops held in the provinces, at a published N'Djamena address
trackers.desc: WHERE TO APPLY FOR MONEY: the Fonds Spécial en faveur de l'Environnement (FSE), created by loi n°014/PR/98 of 17 August 1998 setting the general principles of environmental protection, and made operational in 2012 by décret n°168/PR/PM/MERH/2012, under the environment ministry. Its mission is to mobilise, manage and allocate finance for concrete projects of protection, restoration and valorisation of the environment across the whole national territory, and it expressly supports initiatives carried by LOCAL AUTHORITIES, CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, public services and technical partners. Address: Avenue Ngarta Tombalbaye, Klemat, rue de 40m, opposite the two water towers, N'Djamena. HOW THE MONEY IS ACTUALLY OFFERED, AND IT IS THE PART TO WATCH FOR: the FSE runs APPELS À PROPOSITIONS — numbered calls — and holds INFORMATION AND TRAINING WORKSHOPS IN THE PROVINCES before the deadline, explaining the guidelines and the application form to local organisations and associations; a third call was worked through in Moyen-Chari, and it has run workshops in Batha and Ouaddaï to help local actors capture climate financing. If a call is open, the FSE will come and teach you how to fill in the form — attend that workshop; it is the cheapest application training a Chadian association will ever get. WHERE ITS MONEY COMES FROM: state and local-authority subsidies, ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION TAXES, AND FINES COLLECTED FOR DAMAGE CAUSED TO THE ENVIRONMENT — so polluter penalties are meant to fund community projects. THE FUND'S OWN ADMISSION, RECORDED BECAUSE IT SETS EXPECTATIONS: its director general has publicly identified the NON-DISBURSEMENT of FSE money held at the public treasury in recent years as delaying both its activities and its international accreditation. A fund that cannot draw its own money will be slow; ask what has actually been disbursed in the last cycle, not what was allocated. WHO IT SUITS: Chadian associations, local authorities and community organisations with an environmental restoration, desertification or climate project. CAVEATS: A STATE FUND under the environment ministry — it finances environmental action, NOT litigation or land purchase, and its own disbursement record is the constraint. For legal advice and court assistance, Chad's APLFT/AFJT/PILC entry.

trackers.name: Chad's loi 14/PR/2008 — community forests are CLASSED on the Conseil Rural's advice, and a classed forest is inalienable, imprescriptible and unseizable
trackers.desc: THE LAW THAT MAKES YOUR FOREST UNSEIZABLE: loi n°14/PR/2008 of 10 June 2008 on the regime of forests, wildlife and fisheries resources — 336 ARTICLES, and THE FIRST LAW OF ITS KIND IN CHAD SINCE INDEPENDENCE IN 1960. THE TWO PROVISIONS THAT MATTER: COMMUNITY FORESTS ARE CLASSED BY DECISION OF THE MINISTER IN CHARGE OF FORESTS, AFTER THE OPINION OF THE CONSEIL RURAL CONCERNED or the groupement d'intérêt — so the route runs through your rural council, not around it; and CLASSED FORESTS ARE INALIENABLE, IMPRESCRIPTIBLE AND UNSEIZABLE, AND THEY KEEP THEIR NATURE AS CLASSED FOREST EVEN WHEN THEY NO LONGER CARRY FOREST. Cannot be sold, cannot be lost by lapse of time, cannot be seized — and clearing it does not release it. That last clause defeats the commonest tactic in this file: destroy the trees, then argue there is nothing left to protect. Classing does not block buildings, tracks and infrastructure needed for the forest's own management, nor associated forestry activities consistent with the forest's vocation. THE SECOND INSTRUMENT, FOR WILDLIFE COUNTRY: the law introduces many notions of natural-resource management BY COMMUNITIES and expressly provides for RECLASSIFYING CERTAIN CATEGORIES OF PROTECTED AREA — particularly THOSE CURRENTLY PERFORMING BADLY — INTO A ZONE DE GESTION CONCERTÉE DE LA FAUNE, MANAGED BY LOCAL COMMUNITIES in partnership with state services and the private sector; it also allows a protected area to be organised as A CENTRAL CORE surrounded by PERIPHERAL ZONES MANAGED BY THE COMMUNITIES. A failing protected area next to you is an opportunity, not only a burden — the statute names underperformance as a ground for handing management to communities. Ask for reclassification by name. The law's stated policy options include the effective participation and responsabilisation of the population and poverty reduction through local employment and revenue. WHO IT SUITS: Chadian villages and rural councils near forest or a weak protected area. CAVEATS: CLASSING IS A MINISTERIAL DECISION and the recorded field pressures are severe — chronic insecurity, pastoral pressure, organised poaching; note also that Chad banned wood-cutting and charcoal production outright in 2008, which criminalises common village activity. For environmental project money and the provincial training workshops, Chad's Fonds Spécial en faveur de l'Environnement entry; for legal advice, the APLFT entry.

trackers.name: AFPAT, N'Djamena — Mbororo women's organisation working land-conflict resolution and 3D participatory mapping, with parity governance and a published address
trackers.desc: WHO MAPS AND WHO SETTLES LAND CONFLICTS: the ASSOCIATION DES FEMMES PEULES ET PEUPLES AUTOCHTONES DU TCHAD (AFPAT), a Chadian COMMUNITY ORGANISATION OF INDIGENOUS FULANI (MBORORO) WOMEN, CREATED 1999 WITH OFFICIAL AUTHORISATION TO OPERATE FROM 2005, based at Rue de Bouta, N'Djamena (afpat.net). ITS STATED WORKING METHODS ARE THE REASON IT IS IN THIS FILE: AFPAT works on THE DEFENCE OF FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, the creation of economic activities, and THE PROTECTION AND MANAGEMENT OF THE NATURAL RESOURCES ON WHICH NOMADIC HERDING COMMUNITIES DEPEND, using innovative methods for THE RESOLUTION OF LAND CONFLICTS, THREE-DIMENSIONAL PARTICIPATORY MAPPING OF NATURAL RESOURCES, and work against climate change, desertification and biodiversity loss. Land-conflict resolution and 3D participatory mapping in one Chadian organisation is the exact pairing that has won cases elsewhere in this file — Brainforest in Gabon, Action Mines in Guinea. In Chad it is held by a herders' women's association, which means it is reachable by pastoralists rather than only by villages with fixed fields. HOW IT IS GOVERNED, AND THIS IS WORTH COPYING: AFPAT is A STRUCTURE OF PARITY GOVERNANCE — the bureau and the team respect STRICT PARITY — with governance and all projects resting on the participation of women. Parity written into the statutes rather than promised in a proposal is what makes a women's mandate survive a change of leadership. WHERE ITS REACH EXTENDS: AFPAT is a member of the Congo Basin indigenous peoples' network (REPALEAC) and took part in a REGIONAL WORKSHOP ON LAND RIGHTS under a Community of Practice on land tenure in the Congo Basin (October 2025); it is registered in the UN civil-society database; and its coordinator sits as president of an international forest-certification body's Indigenous Peoples council. Its field campaigns run across Logone Occidental, Mayo Kebbi-Ouest and Mayo Kebbi-Est, with a green-entrepreneurship and climate-adaptation training workshop for women trainers held in N'Djamena with the environment ministry. WHO IT SUITS: Chadian pastoralist and Mbororo communities facing land conflict, and anyone needing a terroir mapped or a regional land-rights channel. CAVEATS: AN ADVOCACY AND MAPPING ORGANISATION, NOT A FUNDER OR A LAW FIRM. For the law that makes a classed forest inalienable and unseizable, Chad's loi 14/PR/2008 entry; for environment project money and the provincial calls, the Fonds Spécial en faveur de l'Environnement entry; for legal advice, APLFT.

trackers.name: Chad's community hunting reserve at Binder-Léré — 40,000 ha managed by a local decision body, and the three-year term that was never renewed
trackers.desc: THE COMMUNITY RESERVE THAT EXISTS, AND THE CLAUSE THAT KILLED IT: east of the RÉSERVE DE FAUNE DE BINDER-LÉRÉ (created 1974, 135,000 ha, Mayo-Kebbi Ouest) lies an experimental RÉSERVE DE CHASSE COMMUNAUTAIRE OF 40,000 HECTARES, part of the ZONE AGRO-PASTORALE COMMUNAUTAIRE D'INTÉRÊT CYNÉGÉTIQUE (ZAPIC). It was CLASSIFIED IN 2004 BY ARRÊTÉ N°020/MEE/SG/DCFAP/04, amended by ARRÊTÉ N°071/MEE/SG/DCFAP/05, AND ITS MANAGEMENT WAS ENTRUSTED TO AN INSTANCE LOCALE D'ORIENTATION ET DE DÉCISION (ILOD) FOR A PERIOD OF THREE YEARS — and the record states plainly that it has been NEITHER MODIFIED NOR RENEWED SINCE. THIS IS THE MOST TRANSFERABLE WARNING IN THIS FILE: a community management mandate with a fixed term and no renewal clause simply expires, and nobody tells you. If you are offered a three-year delegation, put the renewal mechanism in the same arrêté — name who renews it, by when, and what happens on silence. Chad's own community reserve has been running on a lapsed mandate for two decades. An ILOD — a LOCAL BODY OF ORIENTATION AND DECISION — is nonetheless the named Chadian vehicle for community management of a classified area: ask for one by name, and ask for the arrêté number. WHY THE RESERVE MATTERS NOW: the ministry delegated management of Binder-Léré to a conservation NGO on the express condition that the reserve's BIODIVERSITY CORE BE UPGRADED TO A NATIONAL PARK, after heavy elephant poaching (89 animals killed in March 2013, 19 in February 2018, 7 in August 2019); the PARC NATIONAL DE ZAH SOO, 815 km2, was created in 2022 as Chad's FOURTH national park, holding the country's third savanna elephant population, Kordofan giraffe and its only manatee population, with the stated aim that RIVERSIDE COMMUNITIES OF BINDER-LÉRÉ BENEFIT FROM INCLUSIVE DEVELOPMENT, making the complex an ISLAND OF INTEGRITY AND GOOD GOVERNANCE. Poaching numbers were what forced the state to act — count and record what is being taken from your area, because that is the evidence that moves a ministry. Chad has around 10.1% of its territory in protected areas, and the assessment notes that state budget for the parks directorate is very limited, with most field action funded by external partners. WHO IT SUITS: Chadian riverside communities near a classified reserve, and anyone negotiating a fixed-term community management delegation. CAVEATS: A LAPSED MANDATE AND AN NGO-DELEGATED PARK — confirm current status before relying on either. For the law that makes a classed forest unseizable and allows reclassification into community management, Chad's loi 14/PR/2008 entry; for land-conflict resolution and 3D mapping, AFPAT; for project money, the Fonds Spécial and Green Climate Fund entries.

trackers.name: Chad's bar and rights bodies — the Ordre des Avocats that suspended work nationwide when two advocates were arrested, the LTDH and ATPDH, the women's league that funds legal assistance, and ADPV in the under-served zones
trackers.desc: THE BAR THAT STOPPED WORK FOR ITS OWN, WHICH TELLS YOU BOTH THE RISK AND THE SOLIDARITY: when two named Chadian advocates were arbitrarily arrested alongside civil society figures after an authorised peaceful march, THE ORDRE DES AVOCATS DU TCHAD DECIDED TO SUSPEND ALL ITS ACTIVITIES ACROSS THE ENTIRE TERRITORY, UNTIL THE DATE SET FOR THE FIRST HEARING OF THE TRIAL OF THE TWO LAWYERS AND THE OTHER ARBITRARILY DETAINED ACTIVISTS. A bar association that shuts the whole country's legal profession to defend two of its members is one that will not abandon a lawyer who takes your case. That is worth knowing before you ask someone to represent you against the state — and it is worth knowing that taking such a case in Chad carries the risk of arrest. THE TWO NATIONAL RIGHTS BODIES, BOTH REACHABLE AND BOTH ON THE RECORD: the LIGUE TCHADIENNE DES DROITS DE L'HOMME (LTDH) and the ASSOCIATION TCHADIENNE POUR LA PROMOTION ET LA DÉFENSE DES DROITS DE L'HOMME (ATPDH), which ISSUE JOINT STATEMENTS WITH AN INTERNATIONAL OBSERVATORY FOR THE PROTECTION OF HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, condemning arrests and calling for immediate and unconditional release. The ATPDH was CO-FOUNDED BY A NAMED CHADIAN LAWYER who returned to Chad after 1990, saw widespread starvation and poverty, AND FOUNDED THE ASSOCIATION TO PREVENT SIMILAR SUFFERING IN FUTURE; its president is a lawyer. Two national rights organisations that can put your case into an international observatory's statement within days is the fastest protection available to a Chadian community leader. Contact them BEFORE anything happens, not after — an organisation that already knows your name acts faster. FOR WOMEN'S CLAIMS: the LIGUE TCHADIENNE DES DROITS DES FEMMES ran a funded project for gender equality in Chad whose components included STRENGTHENING THE KNOWLEDGE AND CAPACITY TO ACT OF GIRLS AND WOMEN AND OF KEY ACTORS, AND LEGAL, PSYCHOLOGICAL AND JUDICIAL ASSISTANCE, financed through a small local-initiatives fund for projects PROPOSED AND IMPLEMENTED BY LOCAL ORGANISATIONS delivering help directly to the local population. A small-initiatives fund that requires the project to be proposed AND implemented by a local organisation is money a Chadian association can actually win — ask the LTDF how it applied. AND FOR THE PLACES NOBODY REACHES: ASSOCIATION POUR LA DÉFENSE DES PERSONNES VULNÉRABLES (ADPV), FOUNDED AND BASED IN N'DJAMENA (adpv-td.org), working on human rights and the protection of women, children, young people and marginalised communities, with SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AND CLIMATE RESILIENCE among its named domains — and which states that it ACTS CLOSEST TO THE COMMUNITIES, NOTABLY IN ISOLATED AND UNDER-SERVED ZONES, MOBILISING LOCAL EXPERTISE AND YOUNG COMMUNITY LEADERS, welcoming volunteers and interns. Isolated and under-served zones is where most Chadian land is. An organisation that names those places as its priority and takes volunteers is one a rural committee can both call and join. HOW THE SECTOR CAME TO EXIST: Chadian civil society was governed by a restrictive 1962 ordinance until THE ADVENT OF DEMOCRACY IN 1990, WHICH BROUGHT A SUBSTANTIAL INCREASE IN CIVIL SOCIETY — IN PARTICULAR HUMAN RIGHTS ASSOCIATIONS, INDEPENDENT UNIONS, UNIONS AND FEDERATIONS AND NETWORKS OF ASSOCIATIONS, AND GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS. WHO IT SUITS: Chadian community leaders at risk, women with a claim, and rural committees in remote areas. CAVEATS: STATE THIS PLAINLY — lawyers and activists have been arbitrarily detained in Chad; approach with care and through an organisation rather than alone. For three legal assistance services, Chad's APLFT entry; for a complaint against a lender on behalf of communities, GRAMPTC; for land-conflict resolution and 3D mapping, AFPAT; for the ILOD vehicle and the lapsed mandate, the community hunting reserve entry.

trackers.name: ADC-Tchad and the Chadian water networks — one named coordinator holding five positions at once, and the associational categories Chadian law recognises
trackers.desc: ONE PERSON, FIVE DOORS — which in a country this file records as thin is worth more than five separate addresses: a NAMED CHADIAN COORDINATOR IS LISTED SIMULTANEOUSLY AS WASH PROGRAMME COORDINATOR; POINT FOCAL FOR THE CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS SIDE OF A SANITATION AND WATER FOR ALL PARTNERSHIP; POINT FOCAL FOR AN AFRICAN ALLIANCE OF WATER AND SANITATION UMBRELLA BODIES; EXECUTIVE SECRETARY OF THE PARTENARIAT NATIONAL DE L'EAU DU TCHAD; AND A MEMBER OF BOTH THE ASSOCIATION POUR LA DÉFENSE DES DROITS DES CONSOMMATEURS (ADC-TCHAD), N'DJAMÉNA, AND THE RÉSEAU DES ASSOCIATIONS D'EAU ET ASSAINISSEMENT DU TCHAD. National water partnership, continental alliance, global partnership focal point, a consumer rights association and a national network of water associations — all reachable through one correspondent. If your problem is a borehole, a dam, a pollution source or a water cut, that is the single letter to write. And note the CONSUMER RIGHTS association in the list: where environmental standing is hard to establish, consumer standing sometimes is not, because you are a paying user of a service. THE CATEGORIES CHADIAN LAW AND PRACTICE ACTUALLY RECOGNISE, WHICH IS WHAT A NEW GROUP NEEDS BEFORE IT CHOOSES A FORM: from just after independence, civil society was governed by A RESTRICTIVE FRAMEWORK UNDER ORDONNANCE N°27/INT-SUR OF 28 JULY 1962, under which RELIGIOUS ASSOCIATIVE MOVEMENTS AND ASSOCIATIONS AND GROUPINGS ORIENTED TOWARDS PRODUCTION ACTIVITIES WERE THE MOST REPRESENTED. THE ADVENT OF DEMOCRACY IN 1990 FAVOURED A SUBSTANTIAL INCREASE IN THE CIVIL SOCIETY FABRIC, WITH THE EMERGENCE OF ASSOCIATIONS FOR THE DEFENCE AND PROMOTION OF HUMAN RIGHTS, CORPORATIONS, TRADE UNIONS INDEPENDENT OF POLITICAL PARTIES, UNIONS AND FEDERATIONS AND NETWORKS OF ASSOCIATIONS, ECONOMIC GROUPINGS, BASE ORGANISATIONS AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT ASSOCIATIONS. Production groupings and religious associations were the forms that survived the restrictive years — which is why, in much of the Sahel, a farmers' grouping or a church body can convene a meeting an advocacy NGO cannot. Pick the form that fits what your community already is, not the one that sounds most like a campaign. AND THE TURNING POINT NAMED IN THE SAME RECORD: THE START OF CHADIAN OIL EXPLOITATION AT THE END OF THE 1990s CONSTITUTED A TURNING POINT THAT FAVOURED THE STRUCTURING of civil society. The oil project is what organised Chadian civil society. That is the pattern worth knowing in advance: a large extractive project creates, as a by-product, the coalitions that will still exist after it. If one is arriving in your area, the organisations forming around it now are the ones you will work with for the next twenty years — join early. THE RIGHTS BODY AND WHO BUILT IT: a Chadian human rights association was founded after the 1990 change by people who, according to a named co-founder, RETURNED TO CHAD FROM ABROAD AND SAW WIDESPREAD STARVATION AND POVERTY AMONG THE PEOPLE, AND WERE MOTIVATED TO FOUND IT TO PREVENT SIMILAR SUFFERING IN THE FUTURE — and its president is a lawyer. A rights association whose president is a practising lawyer is a legal resource wearing an advocacy name. Ask who the president is before assuming an organisation cannot litigate. ALSO USEFUL: the state radio broadcaster reaches the country through transmitters at N'DJAMENA, SARH, MOUNDOU AND ABÉCHÉ AND BROADCASTS IN SEVEN AFRICAN LANGUAGES AS WELL AS FRENCH AND ARABIC. Seven African languages on a national transmitter network is how a rural Chadian community hears something. If your case needs to travel beyond the capital, the language it travels in matters as much as the outlet. WHO IT SUITS: Chadian communities with a water or pollution problem, new associations choosing a legal form, and anyone facing an extractive project. CAVEATS: SOME OF THIS RECORD IS HISTORICAL and Chadian civic space has narrowed since — confirm current status. For a complaint taken against the World Bank's lender on behalf of 25,200 people, Chad's GRAMPTC entry; for three legal assistance services, the APLFT entry; for calls for proposals with a published window, the Fonds Spécial en faveur de l'Environnement; for 40,000 ha managed by a local association and the lapse that followed, the Binder-Léré entry.

trackers.name: OECD National Contact Points (NCPs) — the free government mediation office in the foreign company's own home country — who may file, what it covers, the published complaint form, and the Nigerian flooding case that reached an agreement in twelve months
trackers.desc: THE OFFICE IS IN THEIR COUNTRY, NOT YOURS — and that is the whole point of this entry for a community whose own courts are unreachable: A COMPLAINT CAN BE SUBMITTED BY ANY INDIVIDUAL OR ORGANISATION WITH A LEGITIMATE INTEREST IN REPORTING THAT A BUSINESS, OPERATING IN OR FROM THE TERRITORY OF THE COUNTRY OF THE OFFICE, HAS ALLEGEDLY NOT OBSERVED THE GUIDELINES. If the firm on your land is French, Italian, British, Norwegian or from any other adhering country, there is a government office in that country whose job includes hearing your complaint about what its company did in Africa. You do not travel; you write. THE OFFICES EXIST BY OBLIGATION: ALL GOVERNMENTS ADHERING TO THE GUIDELINES MUST SET UP A NATIONAL CONTACT POINT, WHOSE WORK INCLUDES SERVING AS A MEDIATION AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION PLATFORM. WHO MAY FILE, PUBLISHED PLAINLY BY ONE SUCH OFFICE: ANY INTERESTED PARTY CAN FILE A COMPLAINT — THE COMPLAINANT MAY BE, FOR EXAMPLE, A COMMUNITY AFFECTED BY A COMPANY'S ACTIVITIES, EMPLOYEES OR THEIR TRADES UNION, OR A NON-GOVERNMENT ORGANISATION — AND A COMPLAINANT MAY ACT ON BEHALF OF IDENTIFIED OTHER PARTIES. ANOTHER STATES SIMPLY: ANYONE CAN SUBMIT A COMPLAINT IF THEY BELIEVE THAT A COMPANY VIOLATES THE GUIDELINES. A COMMUNITY AFFECTED BY A COMPANY'S ACTIVITIES is listed first among the examples. No registration, no lawyer, no standing test — and you may file on behalf of named others, so one person can carry the village. WHAT THE GUIDELINES COVER, WHICH IS BROADER THAN PEOPLE EXPECT: DUE DILIGENCE IN THE SUPPLY CHAIN; DISCLOSURE; HUMAN RIGHTS; EMPLOYMENT AND INDUSTRIAL RELATIONS; ENVIRONMENT; WORKING TO STOP BRIBERY; CONSUMER INTERESTS; SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY; COMPETITION; AND TAXATION. ENVIRONMENT and BRIBERY are separate heads, and DUE DILIGENCE IN THE SUPPLY CHAIN means the buyer of the crop or mineral can be complained about, not only the operator on your land. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS: AN INITIAL ASSESSMENT AGAINST ADMISSIBILITY CRITERIA; THEN GOOD OFFICES TO HELP THE PARTIES RESOLVE THE ISSUES, FACILITATING ACCESS TO CONSENSUAL AND NON-ADVERSARIAL MEANS SUCH AS MEDIATION OR CONCILIATION; IF DISPUTE RESOLUTION FAILS, THE OFFICE MAY INVESTIGATE THE ALLEGED BREACHES AND ISSUE RECOMMENDATIONS; AND IT SHOULD PUBLISH A FINAL STATEMENT ABOUT THE COMPLAINT AND ANY RESOLUTION REACHED. SOME OFFICES ASK THE COMPANY AND COMPLAINANT TO REPORT BACK AFTER A PERIOD, USUALLY ONE YEAR, ON PROGRESS IN IMPLEMENTING THE RECOMMENDATIONS. A published final statement is a permanent public record naming the company, which is worth something even when nothing else is won — and the one-year report-back is the follow-up almost no process in this file has. THE WORKED AFRICAN CASE, WITH ITS DATES: A COMPANY HAD DRILLED FOR OIL IN AND AROUND A NAMED NIGERIAN TOWN SINCE THE 1960s. BECAUSE OF ELEVATED ROADWAYS, EMBANKMENTS AND PLATFORMS BUILT BY THE COMPANY, THE COMMUNITY SUFFERED FOR FIVE DECADES FROM VIOLENT ANNUAL FLOODING OF LARGE SWATHES OF FARMLAND AND RESIDENTIAL AREAS — WITH 90% OF HOUSEHOLDS HAVING LOST AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS AND OVER 65% SUFFERING SEVERE HEALTH PROBLEMS. A EUROPEAN OFFICE ACCEPTED THE COMPLAINT IN JULY 2018, OPENED A MEDIATION IN THE PRESENCE OF A THIRD-PARTY CONCILIATOR, AND THE PROCESS LED TO AN AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE PARTIES IN JULY 2019. Fifty years of flooding, and twelve months from filing to agreement once it reached the company's home government. Note what made the complaint strong: percentages. Ninety per cent of households, sixty-five per cent with health effects — somebody counted, door to door. That survey is the work to do before writing. NOW THE HONEST WEAKNESSES, BECAUSE THEY DECIDE WHETHER THIS IS WORTH YOUR TIME: THE QUALITY AND EFFECTIVENESS OF OFFICES VARY WIDELY AND CHANGE OVER TIME. SOME REJECT COMPLAINTS WHEN A COMPANY REFUSES TO ENGAGE IN MEDIATION, EFFECTIVELY ALLOWING THE COMPANY TO UNILATERALLY STYMIE THE COMPLAINT PROCESS. AND SOME HAVE STRICT CONFIDENTIALITY REQUIREMENTS AND WILL DISCOURAGE PUBLIC ADVOCACY ALONGSIDE THE PROCESS — RULES DESCRIBED AS GENERALLY PROBLEMATIC FOR COMMUNITIES SUFFERING ABUSES, AND AS FAILING TO TAKE INTO ACCOUNT THE SERIOUS POWER IMBALANCES BETWEEN COMMUNITIES AND COMPANIES. Filing can buy your silence. Check that office's confidentiality rule BEFORE you file, because agreeing to it may cost you the campaign you already have. AND THE PUBLISHED WORKAROUND: ONE WAY AROUND THIS RESTRICTION IS TO FORM PARTNERSHIPS WITH OTHER CIVIL SOCIETY ALLIES WHO ARE NOT PART OF THE COMPLAINTS PROCESS AND CAN CONTINUE OTHER FORMS OF ADVOCACY. Keep some allies outside the complaint so they can keep speaking. Decide who files and who stays free before anyone signs anything. THE HELP THAT EXISTS: A GLOBAL CIVIL SOCIETY NETWORK IS NAMED AS AN EXCELLENT RESOURCE FOR THIS ROUTE; ONE OFFICE PUBLISHES A GUIDING COMPLAINT FORM AND ASKS FOR WRITTEN AND AS SPECIFIC AND PRECISE DOCUMENTATION AS POSSIBLE; AND SECTOR GUIDANCE DOCUMENTS EXIST FOR THE FINANCIAL, EXTRACTIVE AND AGRICULTURAL SECTORS. A guiding form and sector guidance for extractives and agriculture — the two sectors most of this file's cases sit in. Fill in the form rather than writing a letter from scratch. AND THE SCALE, SO YOU KNOW THIS IS USED: 225 SPECIFIC INSTANCES CONCLUDED BETWEEN 2001 AND 2022, RESOLVED THROUGH CONCILIATION, MEDIATION OR GOOD OFFICES. WHO IT SUITS: African communities harmed by a foreign-owned company, or by a foreign buyer in the supply chain. CAVEATS: THE OFFICES HAVE NO FORCE OF LAW AND ARE NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR JUDICIAL REMEDIES — they can complement courts that are not accessible. For the trackers that identify which foreign company and financier stands behind a project, Guinea's investment chain entry; for the two-person and now one-person bank complaint, Nigeria's and Guinea's entries; for the damage valuation study to bring to mediation, Ghana's Strategic Response Mechanism entry.

trackers.name: GlobalGiving — the crowdfunding platform any registered African non-profit can join — the exact threshold of $5,000 from 40 donors, the 5–12% fee, the full vetting checklist, and its own published warning that it will not bring you a single donor
trackers.desc: FORTY DONORS AND FIVE THOUSAND DOLLARS — AND THEY BRING YOU NEITHER. THE WARNING THEY PUBLISH THEMSELVES, AND IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE ON THE PAGE: THE PLATFORM DOES NOT PROVIDE DONORS TO YOUR PROJECT OR PROMOTE YOUR ACCELERATOR PROJECT. THE CROWDFUNDING CAMPAIGN IS THE FINAL STAGE OF A RIGOROUS VETTING PROCESS — IT HELPS DETERMINE WHETHER YOUR ORGANIZATION HAS A COMMUNITY OF SUPPORTERS THAT CARES ABOUT YOUR WORK. The campaign is a test of the supporters you already have, not a way to find new ones. Communities join these platforms expecting an audience and discover they are the audience. Count your forty people first — diaspora relatives, former colleagues, a church or mosque, a partner organisation abroad — and only then apply. THE THRESHOLD, EXACTLY: YOUR ORGANIZATION MUST RAISE AT LEAST $5,000 FROM 40 UNIQUE DONORS DURING THE CROWDFUNDING CAMPAIGN TO GRADUATE AND BECOME A PERMANENT PARTNER — A THREE-WEEK CAMPAIGN, FOLLOWING AN OPTIONAL ONE-WEEK TRAINING CURRICULUM. Forty unique donors matters more than the sum. An average of $125 each is reachable; forty separate people willing to give is the part to organise, and it is measured on name, email, card, address and IP, so the same person cannot count twice. AND THE SECOND WARNING: IT IS BEST-SUITED FOR ORGANIZATIONS WITH SUPPORTERS WHO CAN DONATE ONLINE. Online donation is the real filter. If your supporters are neighbours with mobile money and no card, this platform is the wrong door and a local mobile-money fundraising service is the right one. THE FEES, STATED: THERE ARE NO COSTS FOR NON-PROFITS TO JOIN, BUT A 5-12% FEE IS RETAINED ON DONATIONS, INCLUDING THE 3% CREDIT CARD TRANSACTION COST, AND A FEE IS DEDUCTED FROM EACH DONATION DURING THE CAMPAIGN. Between five and twelve per cent. Free to join is not free to use — budget the deduction before promising anyone what the money will buy. THE VETTING CHECKLIST, WHICH IS ALSO A LIST OF WHAT TO ASSEMBLE: THEY COLLECT AND REVIEW LEGAL DOCUMENTS, FINANCIAL RECORDS, PROGRAM MATERIALS, AND LISTS OF SENIOR STAFF AND BOARD MEMBERS, TO VALIDATE THAT THE ORGANIZATION IS RUNNING THE PROJECT AS DESCRIBED; THEY EVALUATE CAPACITY TO IMPLEMENT ACTIVITIES AND TO COMMUNICATE ABOUT ITS WORK; THEY RESEARCH THE ORGANIZATION'S RELATIONSHIP WITH PREVIOUS FUNDERS; THEY CHECK THAT IT MEETS LOCAL REQUIREMENTS FOR REGISTRATION WITH ITS LOCAL GOVERNMENT; AND THEY ENSURE COMPLIANCE WITH ANTI-TERROR GUIDELINES AND INTERNATIONAL GUIDELINES FOR PHILANTHROPY. Assemble that folder once and it serves every funder in this file. The registration check appears here as it does everywhere — and the anti-terror screening is the reason organisations in conflict-affected regions get delayed, so allow for it rather than being surprised. THE FIVE SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS, AND THE REFERENCE RULE IS THE ONE PEOPLE FAIL: TWO YEARS OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS SHOWING CLEAR INCOME SOURCES AND EXPENSE ALLOCATION; STRONG REFERENCES — LETTERS FROM FUNDERS, PARTNER ORGANISATIONS, COMMUNITY MEMBERS, OR PROGRAMME BENEFICIARIES WHO HAVE DIRECTLY WITNESSED YOUR IMPACT, WITH REFERENCES FROM FAMILY OR INTERNAL STAFF NOT ACCEPTED; AND ORGANISATIONAL CAPACITY — ABILITY TO MANAGE FUNDS, COMMUNICATE IN ENGLISH, AND MAINTAIN REGULAR DONOR ENGAGEMENT THROUGH QUARTERLY REPORTING. COMMUNITY MEMBERS AND PROGRAMME BENEFICIARIES count as referees. A village committee that has never had a funder can still produce valid references from the people it served — which removes the usual trap of needing a funder to get a funder. But note COMMUNICATE IN ENGLISH, which is a real barrier in francophone and lusophone countries and worth planning a translator for. THE APPROVAL LEVEL, WHICH IS BETTER THAN MOST: IT EVALUATES THE WHOLE ORGANISATION, NOT JUST PROJECTS, WHICH ALLOWS FOR MORE FLEXIBLE FUND USAGE ONCE APPROVED — AND IT CAN DISBURSE FUNDS WITHIN DAYS, NOT MONTHS. Approved once, then flexible. Almost every grant in this file is tied to a project written months earlier; this is unrestricted money you can move when the bulldozers arrive rather than when the workplan said. WHAT GRADUATION BUYS: PERMANENT MEMBERSHIP, INCLUDING ONGOING OPPORTUNITIES TO ATTRACT NEW CORPORATE AND INDIVIDUAL DONORS; INCLUSION IN A PRESS RELEASE ANNOUNCING THE GRADUATES; AND A CUSTOM MEDIA KIT — WITH MATCHING FUNDING AND BONUS PRIZES PROVIDED DURING THE CAMPAIGN, AND DONORS ABLE TO GIVE IN USD OR GBP. MATCHING FUNDING during the campaign means a donation given on the right day is worth more than one given later. Ask which days match, and hold your biggest supporters back for them. THE ELIGIBILITY REACH: ANY REGISTERED NONPROFIT ANYWHERE IN THE WORLD IS ELIGIBLE TO APPLY, WITH VETTED ORGANISATIONS IN 175+ COUNTRIES AND THE PUBLISHED LIST NAMING AFRICAN STATES INCLUDING CHAD, THE CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC, COMOROS, THE CONGO AND THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO. Countries this file has recorded as the hardest to fund are on the eligibility list. The barrier is registration and forty donors, not geography. AND THE SCALE AND STATED COMMITMENT: 1.9 MILLION DONORS HAVE CONTRIBUTED MORE THAN $1 BILLION TO OVER 40,000 PROJECTS — WITH A STATED COMMITMENT TO TRANSFORMING AID AND PHILANTHROPY TO ACCELERATE COMMUNITY-LED CHANGE, WITH PARTICULAR EMPHASIS ON TRUST-BASED GRANTMAKING AND PUTTING DECISION-MAKING POWER IN THE HANDS OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES. WHO IT SUITS: registered African community organisations with a reachable network of forty supporters who can give online. CAVEATS: REGISTRATION, TWO YEARS OF ACCOUNTS AND ENGLISH ARE ALL REQUIRED, AND THE PLATFORM BRINGS NO DONORS — unregistered groups should look at the funds in this file that say so explicitly. For the fund open to unregistered groups of two or more, Tunisia's embattled-organisation entry; for the advisor-nominated small grants where 40% of grantees are first-time, Ghana's African Women's Development Fund entry; for free legal help getting registered, the Central African Republic's pro bono brokerage entry.

trackers.name: Cultural Survival's Keepers of the Earth Fund — an indigenous-led fund run by indigenous staff that pays communities and traditional governments directly — no legal registration required, applications accepted as two pages or a five-minute video, plus a separate fund for community radio in nine named African countries
trackers.desc: TWO PAGES OR FIVE MINUTES OF VIDEO, AND NO REGISTRATION NEEDED — THE APPLICATION FORMAT, WHICH IS THE FIND: A PROPOSAL ANSWERING SEVEN QUESTIONS, LIMITED TO A MAXIMUM OF TWO PAGES OF WRITTEN TEXT OR FIVE MINUTES OF VIDEO — SENT TO A PUBLISHED EMAIL ADDRESS. ONE AFRICAN CALL ACCEPTED PROPOSALS IN ENGLISH, AFRIKAANS, SETSWANA AND KHOEKHOEGOWAB. A five-minute video, in a language the community actually speaks, replaces the proposal document. This file has recorded literacy and English as the two barriers that quietly exclude the communities with the strongest case; here both are answered in the application rules themselves. An elder can make this application on a phone. THE REGISTRATION LINE: LEGAL REGISTRATION IS NOT REQUIRED, BUT APPLICANTS MUST HAVE A BANK ACCOUNT CAPABLE OF RECEIVING INTERNATIONAL TRANSFERS — OR AN EXISTING WRITTEN AGREEMENT WITH A FISCAL SPONSOR. Unregistered groups qualify, and the bank account gate has a published way around it: a fiscal sponsor, meaning another organisation receives and passes on the funds under a written agreement. That single arrangement unlocks several funders in this file, and it is worth setting up with a trusted national body before you need it. WHO HOLDS THE MONEY, WHICH IS UNUSUAL: AN INDIGENOUS-LED FUND MANAGED BY INDIGENOUS STAFF, WITH GRANTS GOING DIRECTLY TO INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, COLLECTIVES, ORGANIZATIONS AND TRADITIONAL GOVERNMENTS, TO SUPPORT PROJECTS DESIGNED BY THEM AND IN ACCORDANCE WITH THEIR INDIGENOUS VALUES. TRADITIONAL GOVERNMENTS named as eligible recipients. A council of elders or a customary authority can hold the grant as itself, without inventing an NGO to sit in front of it — which is rarer in this file than any amount of money. THE AMOUNTS: SMALL GRANTS OF UP TO $12,000; ONE AFRICAN CALL AWARDED UP TO $8,000; AND UPON SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF AN INITIAL GRANT AND REPORTING, APPLICANTS MAY APPLY FOR SUBSEQUENT GRANTS OF UP TO $10,000. THE THEMES ONE AFRICAN CALL PRIORITISED, AND THE ESCAPE CLAUSE AT THE END: CLIMATE CHANGE SUCH AS REFORESTATION, ADAPTATION OF CROPS AND FLOOD PREVENTION; FOOD SOVEREIGNTY SUCH AS SEED BANKS, INDIGENOUS TRADITIONAL FOOD SYSTEMS, AND FISHING AND HUNTING RIGHTS; INDIGENOUS ECONOMIES; INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE SYSTEMS SUCH AS TRANSFER OF KNOWLEDGE FROM KNOWLEDGE KEEPERS TO YOUTH AND CHILDREN; AND INDIGENOUS SPIRITUALITIES — NEVERTHELESS, APPLICANTS ARE ENCOURAGED TO SUBMIT PROPOSALS IN TOPICS OR THEMES IMPORTANT TO THEIR COMMUNITY. FISHING AND HUNTING RIGHTS and SEED BANKS are funded themes, not side interests — and the closing sentence says you may propose whatever your community thinks matters. Very few funders in this file leave that door open in writing. WHAT IT WILL NOT FUND, STATED SO NOBODY WASTES A CYCLE: PROJECTS THAT ARE NOT INDIGENOUS-LED, POLITICAL CAMPAIGNS, RELIGIOUS OR MISSIONARY ACTIVITIES, ACADEMIC RESEARCH, CONFERENCE REGISTRATIONS, INDIVIDUAL WORK, OR GOVERNMENT PROGRAM REPLICAS. POLITICAL CAMPAIGNS excluded, INDIVIDUAL WORK excluded. So frame the work as the community's own development and stewardship rather than as opposition to a project — the same activity, described the way the fund is written to receive it. THE ELIGIBILITY TEST: BE AN INDIGENOUS NON-PROFIT GRASSROOTS COMMUNITY, ORGANIZATION OR GOVERNMENT, WITH COLLECTIVE DECISION MAKING. THE RECORD: SINCE 2017 IT HAS SUPPORTED 392 PROJECTS IN 40 COUNTRIES THROUGH SMALL GRANTS AND A WRAP-AROUND APPROACH, TOTALLING $2,219,369 — AND IT IS USUALLY THE FIRST SOURCE OF FINANCING FOR ORGANIZATIONS OR PROJECTS. USUALLY THE FIRST SOURCE OF FINANCING. That is what a community with no funding history needs and almost never finds — and every later funder in this file wants to see that somebody funded you before. THE CALL CYCLE, WHICH DETERMINES WHETHER YOU CAN APPLY AT ALL: A HYBRID STRATEGY OF ONE YEAR OF PUBLIC CALL FOLLOWED BY TWO YEARS OF APPLICATIONS BY INVITATION — AND THE COMMUNITIES INVITED ARE SELECTED FROM A DATABASE MADE UP OF APPLICANTS WHO SUBMITTED THROUGH THE PUBLIC CALLS. Apply in a public year even if you are turned down, because that is how you enter the database the invitations are drawn from. A rejected application is the entry ticket to the two closed years that follow. THE SECOND FUND, FOR COMMUNITY MEDIA, WITH ITS AFRICAN COUNTRY LIST: GRANTS FOR INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY RADIO STATIONS AND OTHER MEDIA TO STRENGTHEN BROADCAST INFRASTRUCTURE AND SYSTEMS, CAPACITY BUILDING FOR RADIO TEAMS, ADVOCACY, ORGANIZATIONAL STRENGTHENING AND NETWORKS — FROM $1,500 TO $12,000, WITH UP TO $8,000 FOR A SINGLE STATION OR COLLECTIVE AND UP TO $12,000 FOR A NETWORK PROPOSAL INVOLVING THREE OR MORE COMMUNITY MEDIA, COMPLETED WITHIN 6 TO 10 MONTHS. ITS AFRICAN ELIGIBILITY LIST NAMES BOTSWANA, CAMEROON, THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, KENYA, NAMIBIA, SOUTH AFRICA, TANZANIA, UGANDA AND ZIMBABWE. Money for a transmitter, and more of it if three stations apply together. This file's Ethiopia entry covers the association a station joins and the licence argument; this is who pays for the equipment — and the network bonus is a reason for neighbouring stations to apply as one. IT ALSO TRAINS: TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES IN JOURNALISM, BROADCASTING, AUDIO EDITING, TECHNICAL SKILLS AND MORE FOR INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY RADIO JOURNALISTS — AND SINCE 2017 IT HAS AWARDED 227 GRANTS TO COMMUNITY RADIOS AND OTHER OUTLETS IN 24 COUNTRIES, TOTALLING OVER $1,569,348. AND THE RELATIONSHIP APPROACH: THEY AIM TO PERSONALLY VISIT THE MAJORITY OF PROJECTS THEY FUND, AND SEEK LONG-TERM RELATIONSHIPS WITH PARTNERS, LOOKING FOR PROGRESSIVE GROWTH TOWARDS SELF-SUFFICIENCY. They come to you. A funder that visits sees the situation rather than the report, which changes what can be explained — and it is the strongest reason to apply here before applying anywhere that will only ever read your paperwork. WHO IT SUITS: African indigenous communities, collectives and traditional authorities — including unregistered ones — and indigenous community radio stations in the nine named countries. CAVEATS: INDIGENOUS-LED ONLY, NO POLITICAL CAMPAIGNS, AND PUBLIC CALLS RUN ONLY ONE YEAR IN THREE — check which phase the cycle is in. For the fund that waives bank account and ID entirely, the Central African Republic's entry; for the community radio association and licensing argument, Ethiopia's entry; for the cash award to the village group itself, Egypt's entry.

trackers.name: A European lobbying coalition that exists to be instructed from Africa — with an elected Eastern African focal point, named African partners in its core group, free voluntary membership, and a published Brussels contact for reaching EU institutions
trackers.desc: A EUROPEAN LOBBY THAT EXISTS TO BE INSTRUCTED FROM AFRICA — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S SÃO TOMÉ ENTRY COVERS THE AFRICAN-LED HORN PASTORAL ORGANISATION NAMED BELOW AS A CORE-GROUP PARTNER, AND ITS TANZANIA ENTRY A PASTORALIST AND HUNTER-GATHERER COALITION. TWO EUROPEAN MEMBERS NAMED BELOW ARE HOSTS UNDER THE CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC AND ANGOLA. AND THE KENYAN ORGANISATION HOLDING THE EASTERN AFRICAN FOCAL POINT ALREADY HAS ITS OWN ENTRY UNDER KENYA, ON REGISTERING COMMUNITY LAND — IT IS NAMED HERE ONLY AS THE HOLDER OF THAT SEAT. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE DIVISION OF LABOUR IT STATES OPENLY, AND IT IS THE FIND: THE COALITION CAN DO THIS WORK ONLY BY CLOSELY COLLABORATING WITH PARTNERS IN THE FORM OF PASTORALIST NETWORKS, EXPERTS AND ORGANISATIONS WORKING IN EASTERN AFRICA, SINCE THESE ACTORS ARE ABLE TO PROVIDE GRASSROOTS INFORMATION AND FORMULATE THE PROBLEMS AND NEEDS OF PASTORALISM AND PASTORALISTS — CRUCIAL INPUTS FOR THE LOBBYING. AND: THE EASTERN AFRICAN PARTNERS HAVE THE LEGITIMATE RIGHT TO LOBBY THEIR OWN GOVERNMENTS, THE AFRICAN UNION AND OTHER REGIONAL AFRICAN BODIES. A European organisation writing down that it cannot define the problem and that Africans hold the right to lobby African institutions. That is the arrangement this file has recorded almost never happening: the foreign body lobbies its own governments, the African body lobbies its own, and neither speaks for the other. If an international organisation offers to represent your community abroad, this is the division of labour to insist on. WHO IT LOBBIES AND WHERE, WHICH IS THE PRACTICAL VALUE: MEMBERS LOBBY THEIR NATIONAL GOVERNMENTS, EUROPEAN UNION BODIES — COUNCIL, PARLIAMENT AND COMMISSION — AND OTHER POLICY-FORMULATING BODIES IN EUROPE INCLUDING THE EUROPEAN HEADQUARTERS OF THE UNITED NATIONS IN GENEVA AND A UN AGRICULTURE AGENCY IN ROME. Those are the institutions that fund the rangeland projects, the border programmes and the drought responses arriving in the Horn. A pastoralist organisation with a grievance about a European-funded programme has, through this coalition, a route to the people who wrote the cheque. THE STRUCTURE, INCLUDING THE AFRICAN SEAT: MANAGED BY AN ELECTED EUROPEAN FOCAL POINT, CURRENTLY AT A BELGIAN VETERINARY ORGANISATION; AN EASTERN AFRICAN FOCAL POINT, CURRENTLY AT A NAMED KENYAN ORGANISATION; AND A CORE GROUP. An elected African focal point, not an advisory seat. The Kenyan organisation holding it is the address to write to first — nearer, and mandated. THE NAMED CORE-GROUP COMPOSITION: EUROPEAN MEMBERS BEING A GERMAN AGROECOLOGY ASSOCIATION, A UK ENVIRONMENT AND DEVELOPMENT INSTITUTE AND THE BELGIAN VETERINARY ORGANISATION; EASTERN AFRICAN PARTNERS BEING A UGANDAN DEVELOPMENT ORGANISATION, A PASTORALIST FORUM IN ETHIOPIA, A SOMALI ARM OF A HORN PASTORAL NETWORK AND THE KENYAN ORGANISATION; PLUS AN INTERNATIONAL CONSERVATION UNION. Four African organisations named on the core group, from Uganda, Ethiopia, Somalia and Kenya. That list is a directory for a pastoralist community in any of those countries. THE MEMBERSHIP TERMS, WHICH COST NOTHING: PARTICIPATION IS ON A VOLUNTARY BASIS AND IS BASED ON A SHARED COMMITMENT TO AND BELIEF IN THE MISSION STATEMENT — AN INFORMAL COALITION, WITH 25 MEMBER ORGANISATIONS AND 7 PARTNER ORGANISATIONS, ESTABLISHED IN 2009. INFORMAL and VOLUNTARY: no fee, no registration test, no legal statute demanded. For an unregistered pastoralist association, this file has recorded that as the barrier that shuts everything else.
