THE FOUR PRIORITY LOBBYING ISSUES, WHICH ARE THE ARGUMENTS ALREADY BUILT FOR YOU: RECOGNITION OF PASTORALISM AS A VALUABLE AND VIABLE LIVELIHOOD SYSTEM CONTRIBUTING TO NATIONAL AND REGIONAL ECONOMIES, FOOD SECURITY, EMPLOYMENT AND SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES; MOBILITY AS A CRUCIAL CONDITION FOR SUSTAINABLE PASTORALISM AND FOR COMMUNITY SECURITY IN CONFLICT AREAS, ALSO ACROSS NATIONAL BORDERS; AND PASTORALISTS' RIGHTS OF ACCESS TO AND MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES — LAND, VEGETATION, WATER AND OTHERS. MOBILITY, argued as a security condition rather than a nuisance. Fences, ranch boundaries and conservancy lines are what break a herding route, and the case that movement itself is the right — across national borders — is already drafted and lobbied for at EU level. THE WON CAMPAIGN AND ITS SCALE: ON 15 MARCH 2022 THE UNITED NATIONS GENERAL ASSEMBLY DECLARED 2026 THE INTERNATIONAL YEAR OF RANGELANDS AND PASTORALISTS — THE CULMINATION OF A MOVEMENT THAT GREW OVER SEVERAL YEARS INTO A GLOBAL COALITION OF OVER 300 PASTORALIST AND SUPPORTING ORGANISATIONS, WITH THIS COALITION IN ITS CORE TEAM. A designated UN year is a hook every ministry, embassy and donor must respond to. Pastoralist organisations should be putting their own demands under that banner while it is open. THE FIGURES IT ORGANISES AROUND: IN AFRICA, DRYLANDS MAKE UP ABOUT 40% OF THE LAND AREA, WITH PASTORALISM REPRESENTING THE MAIN LIVELIHOOD OPTION FOR APPROXIMATELY 200 MILLION PEOPLE. Forty percent of the continent, two hundred million people. This file has recorded pastoralist land described as empty; those two numbers are the first answer. ITS ARGUMENT ABOUT CLIMATE, STATED AS A REVERSAL WORTH BORROWING: MAN-MADE CLIMATE CHANGE IS CREATING CONDITIONS INCREASINGLY CHARACTERISED BY VARIABILITY AND UNPREDICTABILITY — PASTORALISTS USE VARIABILITY TO THEIR ADVANTAGE, AND THEIR PRODUCTION SYSTEMS GUIDE US TO A SUSTAINABLE FUTURE. Herding is not a system to be modernised out of the way; it is the system already adapted to the conditions everyone else is now facing. That reframing turns a defensive claim into an offer. THE ENGAGEMENT STRATEGY AND THE RECORD: A 2018 ENGAGEMENT STRATEGY TO BETTER STRUCTURE ITS INTERVENTIONS AND IDENTIFY THE PATHWAYS TO ITS COMMUNICATION, ADVOCACY AND KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT OBJECTIVES — PLUS A PUBLISHED SUMMARY OF SIX GLOBAL WEBINARS, EACH ON A SPECIFIC PASTORALISM THEME AND HOSTED BY A MEMBER OR PARTNER. AND THE CONTACT: A NAMED CONTACT PERSON WITH A PUBLISHED BRUSSELS STREET ADDRESS AND EMAIL. A street address in Brussels, five minutes from the institutions. Write to the African focal point first and the Brussels contact second. WHO IT SUITS: pastoralist organisations in Kenya, Ethiopia, Uganda, Somalia and the wider Eastern African drylands with a grievance or an argument that needs carrying to European institutions. CAVEATS: EASTERN AFRICA ONLY, INFORMAL AND VOLUNTEER-RUN, AND IT LOBBIES RATHER THAN FUNDS OR LITIGATES — West and Southern African pastoralists will need a different route. For the African-led Horn pastoral organisation on its core group, São Tomé's entry; for the pastoralist and hunter-gatherer coalition, Tanzania's PINGO's Forum entry; for the continental farmers' seat, Seychelles' entry.

trackers.name: Lawyers and investigators who build cases from outside the country where the harm happens, on behalf of affected communities working with local partners — with a treaty-listed wetland being bulldozed for a resort among their live actions
trackers.desc: THEY BUILD THE CASE OUTSIDE THE COUNTRY WHERE THE HARM HAPPENS — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S KENYA ENTRY NAMES A GRASSROOTS JUSTICE NETWORK OF WHICH THIS ORGANISATION IS A MEMBER; ITS SEYCHELLES ENTRY THE ENVIRONMENTAL LAW CHARITY WHOSE FOREST GOVERNANCE LEAD LATER JOINED THIS TEAM; ITS SOUTH SUDAN ENTRY THE WETLANDS TREATY SECRETARIAT ADDRESSED IN THE CASE BELOW; AND ITS ERITREA ENTRY A PRO BONO BROKER WHOSE MANAGER SITS ON THIS ORGANISATION'S LEGAL ACTION COMMITTEE. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHERE THE CASE IS BUILT, WHICH IS THE FIND: WE DEVELOP LEGAL INTERVENTIONS FROM OUTSIDE THE JURISDICTIONS WHERE INDIVIDUALS AND COMMUNITIES SUFFER INJUSTICE — PURSUING INNOVATIVE LEGAL ACTIONS ACROSS BORDERS, CHALLENGING STATES AND OTHER POWERFUL ACTORS. The whole point is that the forum is somewhere else. Where the national courts are captured, the judges untrained or the lawyers unwilling, this file's other legal entries run into a wall; this one starts on the other side of it — in the company's home country, at a treaty body, or before an international court. WHO IT ACTS FOR AND WITH: IT WORKS WITH AFFECTED COMMUNITIES, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH OTHER INTERNATIONAL AND LOCAL GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS — AND ON BEHALF OF AFFECTED COMMUNITIES, USING CROSS-BORDER LEGAL STRATEGIES TO HOLD PERPETRATORS TO ACCOUNT. ON BEHALF OF. The community does not have to appear in a foreign court itself, which matters where naming individuals is dangerous — the point this file's Cape Verde entry establishes as the reason most complaint routes go unused. WHAT IT IS MADE OF: AN INDEPENDENT ORGANISATION OF LAWYERS AND INVESTIGATORS THAT IDENTIFIES AND PURSUES LEGAL ACTIONS TACKLING POWERFUL ACTORS INVOLVED IN SERIOUS HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS AND ENVIRONMENTAL HARMS — A TEAM SPREAD ACROSS MULTIPLE COUNTRIES, WITH OFFICES IN IRELAND AND THE UK. INVESTIGATORS alongside lawyers. Evidence-gathering is inside the organisation rather than contracted out, which is what makes a case possible when the documents are held abroad. THE COMMITTEE THAT SHAPES THE CASES: WORK IS GUIDED BY A LEGAL ACTION COMMITTEE, A DIVERSE AND SELECT TEAM OF EXPERTS DRAWN FROM LEGAL PRACTICE, ACADEMIA AND INVESTIGATIVE JOURNALISM, WHO VOLUNTARILY PROVIDE THEIR EXPERTISE AND CONNECTIONS. INVESTIGATIVE JOURNALISM on the committee that decides which cases to take. That is unusual and it shapes what gets picked: cases where the facts can be established and published, not only argued. THE INFRASTRUCTURE BEHIND IT: THROUGH AN INTERNATIONAL NETWORK OF MEMBERS, UNIVERSITIES AND GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS IT MOBILIZES INSIGHTS FROM RESEARCH AND PRACTICE — SUPPORTED BY FORMAL CONNECTIONS WITH LEADING LAW SCHOOLS, AN INFRASTRUCTURE THAT ALLOWS IT TO DEVELOP CASES THAT PUSH BEYOND THE LIMITS OF CONVENTIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS LITIGATION. Law schools doing the research means the preparatory work costs nothing and takes as long as it needs. A novel argument that no firm would fund is exactly what this structure exists to produce. THE WETLAND CASE AND WHAT THE COMMUNITY DID, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: ON ONE ISLAND IT IS SUPPORTING COMMUNITY MEMBERS, A NAMED LAND ACTORS GROUP, WHO HAVE ORGANISED TO PROTECT THEIR TREATY-LISTED WETLAND WHICH IS BEING BULLDOZED BY A FOREIGN COMPANY BUILDING A MEGA-RESORT COMPLEX — AND, WITH A NAMED LAND RIGHTS AND RESOURCES COMMITTEE, THEY ARE CALLING ON THE TREATY SECRETARIAT AND TWO GOVERNMENTS TO TAKE URGENT ACTION IN AN OPEN LETTER. Read this beside the wetlands treaty entry filed under South Sudan, which records that the Secretariat can act on information it receives. Here is a community doing exactly that — an open letter to the Secretariat and to the governments, published, with lawyers behind it. That is the mechanism and the worked example in the same file, and the tactic transfers directly to an African wetland facing a resort, a dam or a drainage scheme. THE ARGUMENT IN THAT CASE: IT SHINES A SPOTLIGHT ON THE EXPLOITATION OF TREATY-LISTED WETLANDS AND THE GOVERNMENTS FAILING TO LIVE UP TO THEIR COMMITMENTS TO PROTECT THEM — IN A TIME OF CLIMATE CRISIS, GOVERNMENTS MUST DO ALL THEY CAN TO PROTECT BIODIVERSE WETLANDS, WHICH ALSO ACT AS CRUCIAL CARBON SINKS. THE ISLAND WIN ON RECORD, AND WHAT IT WAS ACTUALLY ABOUT: LAND DEFENDERS WON THEIR APPEAL CHALLENGING A DECISION DENYING THEM THE RIGHT TO FIGHT A DESTRUCTIVE AIRPORT DEVELOPMENT — DESCRIBED AS ALSO A WIN FOR COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE REGION FIGHTING THE EXPLOITATION AND DESTRUCTION OF THEIR ISLAND-HOMES. The win was on standing — the right to bring the challenge at all. This file has recorded case after case dismissed before the merits because the community was held to have no interest; that is the fight before the fight, and it is winnable on appeal. THE AFRICAN EXPERIENCE ON THE TEAM: ONE LAWYER LIVED FOR 16 YEARS IN ANOTHER COUNTRY DEFENDING COMMUNITY LAND RIGHTS IN THE FACE OF FORCED EVICTIONS AND LAND GRABS AND PROMOTING TRANSPARENCY IN ENVIRONMENTAL GOVERNANCE, AND FROM 2020 TO 2024 LED A NAMED CHARITY'S FOREST GOVERNANCE WORK IN LATIN AMERICA, AFRICA AND ASIA. Forced evictions and land grabs are the named specialism of somebody on this team, with African forest governance experience directly. That is who to ask for. THE COMMITTEE'S AFRICAN COURT EXPERIENCE: A COMMITTEE MEMBER'S PRACTICE SPANS THE UN HUMAN RIGHTS COMMITTEE, THE UN COMMITTEE AGAINST TORTURE AND VARIOUS NATIONAL CONSTITUTIONAL COURTS INCLUDING UGANDA, NIGERIA, KENYA AND MALAWI. Four African constitutional courts named. The cross-border strategy is not a substitute for national litigation — the people shaping it have argued in those courts. AND THE CALL TO OTHERS ALONGSIDE THE LITIGATION: THERE ARE ACTIONS WE CAN ALL TAKE, LIKE CONTINUING TO SUPPORT CLIMATE LITIGATION WORK, AND JOINING ONE OF THE MANY ORGANISATIONS FIGHTING FOR GOVERNMENTS AND DECISION MAKERS TO TAKE BOLD CLIMATE ACTION NOW. WHO IT SUITS: African communities facing a foreign company or a state where the domestic courts are closed — approaching through a local or international partner organisation rather than alone. CAVEATS: A SMALL TEAM TAKING SELECTED STRATEGIC CASES FROM IRELAND AND THE UK, NOT A LEGAL AID SERVICE, AND NO AFRICAN OFFICE — the route in is a partner. For the wetlands treaty mechanism this case invokes, South Sudan's entry; for the grassroots justice network it belongs to, Kenya's entry; for pro bono operational legal work, São Tomé's and Eswatini's entries.

trackers.name: The Conservation Finance Alliance — a free library of real conservation trust funds' operations manuals, grant agreements, legal frameworks, feasibility studies and fundraising strategies — tagged by country and language, including African funds in French — plus the African consortium of environmental funds
trackers.desc: THE OPERATIONS MANUALS AND GRANT AGREEMENTS OF REAL FUNDS, FREE — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ESWATINI ENTRY COVERS ONE AFRICAN CAPITAL FUND WHOSE DOCUMENTS APPEAR IN THIS LIBRARY, WITHOUT NAMING THE LIBRARY; ITS SÃO TOMÉ, SOUTH SUDAN AND SEYCHELLES ENTRIES THE SERVITUDE TRUST, THE LAND BUYER AND THE TAX DEDUCTION. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. WHAT IS ACTUALLY IN THE LIBRARY, FREE, WHICH IS THE FIND: OPERATIONS MANUALS, GRANT AGREEMENTS AND NGO AGREEMENTS, GRANTEE REPORTING REQUIREMENTS, BOARD DOCUMENTS AND BOARD COMPOSITION PAPERS, INVESTMENT REPORTS, LEGAL FRAMEWORKS, TERMS OF REFERENCE, ASSET MANAGER SELECTION DOCUMENTS, JOB DESCRIPTIONS, FEASIBILITY STUDIES, FUNDRAISING STRATEGIES AND PROPOSALS — EACH TAGGED BY COUNTRY, REGION, YEAR AND LANGUAGE. The actual signed paperwork of working funds, not guidance about it. An African organisation setting up a trust to hold land, or negotiating a grant agreement with an international NGO, can read what other funds signed before drafting its own — and this file has repeatedly recorded local organisations accepting whatever agreement was put in front of them for want of a comparison. WHAT A CONSERVATION TRUST FUND IS, DEFINED, AND WHO IT PAYS: PRIVATE, LEGALLY INDEPENDENT GRANT-MAKING INSTITUTIONS THAT PROVIDE SUSTAINABLE FINANCING FOR BIODIVERSITY CONSERVATION AND OFTEN FINANCE PART OF THE LONG-TERM MANAGEMENT COSTS OF A COUNTRY'S PROTECTED AREA SYSTEM — RAISING AND INVESTING FUNDS TO MAKE GRANTS TO NGOs, COMMUNITY BASED ORGANIZATIONS AND GOVERNMENTAL AGENCIES. COMMUNITY BASED ORGANIZATIONS named as grantees, and LEGALLY INDEPENDENT of the government that hosts them. A national fund is money that does not stop when the ministry changes, which is the answer to the collapse recorded in this file's South Sudan entry. THE AFRICAN NETWORK IT NAMES, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IT WORKS IN COLLABORATION WITH THE NETWORKS OF CONSERVATION TRUST FUNDS — A LATIN AMERICAN AND CARIBBEAN NETWORK, AN ASIA-PACIFIC NETWORK, AND A CONSORTIUM OF AFRICAN FUNDS FOR THE ENVIRONMENT. An African consortium of these funds exists. That is the single most useful thing here for an organisation that does not know whether its own country has a conservation trust fund — the consortium's membership list answers that question, and a national fund is a domestic grantmaker rather than another foreign application. HOW MANY EXIST: SUCH FUNDS HAVE BEEN ESTABLISHED IN MORE THAN 50 DEVELOPING COUNTRIES AND TRANSITION ECONOMIES — AND THEY CAN SERVE AS AN EFFECTIVE MEANS FOR MOBILIZING LARGE AMOUNTS OF ADDITIONAL FUNDING FROM INTERNATIONAL DONORS, NATIONAL GOVERNMENTS AND THE PRIVATE SECTOR. THE AFRICAN DOCUMENTS ON RECORD: A NAMED IVORIAN PARKS AND RESERVES FOUNDATION'S ASSET MANAGER SELECTION TERMS OF REFERENCE, IN FRENCH; A NAMED SOUTH AFRICAN FUND'S BOARD COMPOSITION PAPERS AND ITS GRANT AGREEMENTS WITH INTERNATIONAL NON-PROFITS; AND A MOZAMBICAN BIODIVERSITY FOUNDATION'S FEASIBILITY STUDY. French-language African material, which most of the resources in this file lack. A francophone organisation can read an Ivorian fund's own terms of reference in French rather than working from an English template. THE START-UP MATERIAL AND WHAT A PROFILE DOES: A WELL-DEVELOPED PROFILE SERVES TO CLARIFY ROLES BETWEEN THE FUND, GOVERNMENT AGENCIES AND NONPROFITS; ATTRACT DONOR ATTENTION; AND PROVIDE A BASIS FOR LEGALLY ESTABLISHING THE ENVIRONMENTAL FUND — WITH ADDITIONAL PROFILES AVAILABLE REFLECTING FUNDS AT DIFFERENT STAGES OF DEVELOPMENT. CLARIFY ROLES BETWEEN THE FUND, GOVERNMENT AGENCIES AND NONPROFITS is the sentence to sit with. Who controls the money and who merely advises is decided in the founding documents, and a community that wants a say should be arguing about board composition at that stage — for which the board composition papers above are the precedent. THE FUNDRAISING WORKSHOP HELD IN AFRICA: A WORKSHOP ON FUNDRAISING STRATEGIES FOR ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS, HELD IN A NAMED EAST AFRICAN COUNTRY, PUBLISHED IN ENGLISH, FRENCH AND SPANISH. THE TYPES OF FUND IT DISTINGUISHES: ENVIRONMENTAL TRUST FUNDS FOR INDIVIDUAL PROTECTED AREAS, REGIONAL GROUPINGS OF PROTECTED AREAS OR ENTIRE PROTECTED AREA SYSTEMS — WHICH CAN BE LOCAL, NATIONAL, OR INCLUDE SEVERAL COUNTRIES. A fund can be LOCAL and cover a SINGLE protected area. A trust set up for one forest, one wetland or one community conservancy is a recognised form, not an oversized ambition — which is the realistic scale for most of the situations in this file. THE RESOURCE-REVENUE VEHICLE IT NAMES: OIL AND GAS AND OTHER NATURAL RESOURCE REVENUE FUNDS — A LEGAL VEHICLE THAT SUPPORTS ENVIRONMENTAL PRIORITIES BY MOBILIZING, BLENDING AND OVERSEEING FINANCIAL ASSETS GENERATED FROM REVENUES OR FEES ASSOCIATED WITH NON-RENEWABLE AND RENEWABLE NATURAL RESOURCES. Where extraction is going ahead anyway, a standing demand with a name: that a share of the royalties be paid into an independent trust rather than into a discretionary budget. This file has recorded many communities promised benefits and few holding the instrument that would deliver them. THE REGIONAL VEHICLE: A LEGAL VEHICLE OPERATING AT REGIONAL LEVEL — WITH EXAMPLES OF REGIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS FOUND IN THE CARIBBEAN, CENTRAL AFRICA AND PACIFIC REGIONS. A Central African regional fund is named as an existing example, which matters for the Congo Basin countries that appear throughout this file. THE PAYMENT MECHANISM IT DEFINES: BENEFICIARIES OR USERS OF AN ECOSYSTEM SERVICE, SUCH AS WATER REGULATION, MAKE A DIRECT OR INDIRECT PAYMENT TO THE PROVIDER OF THAT SERVICE IN EXCHANGE FOR SERVICE PROVISION AND MAINTENANCE. The city downstream pays the community upstream for keeping the catchment intact. Where the land in question feeds a water supply, that is a revenue argument rather than a conservation appeal — and it names the utility as the payer. AND THE WORKING GROUPS BEHIND IT: AN ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS WORKING GROUP OF 122 MEMBERS FROM 33 COUNTRIES, WHOSE MISSION IS KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER AND EXCHANGE AMONG RELEVANT FUNDS, DONORS AND NGOs; AND A PROTECTED AREA FINANCE WORKING GROUP OF 102 MEMBERS FROM 31 COUNTRIES, WHICH SHARES INFORMATION AND BEST PRACTICES TO SUPPORT NATIONAL LEVEL PROTECTED AREA FINANCING SYSTEMS. Two working groups of practitioners, with donors in the room. An African fund or a would-be fund joining them is sitting with the people who capitalise these vehicles. WHO IT SUITS: African organisations and communities that need to find their national conservation trust fund, negotiate an agreement with one, or establish a local fund to hold and finance land. CAVEATS: A PRACTITIONER ALLIANCE AND A DOCUMENT LIBRARY, NOT A FUNDER — IT GIVES NO GRANTS; MUCH OF THE MATERIAL IS TECHNICAL AND SOME IS DATED, AND THE FUNDS THEMSELVES ARE THE BODIES TO APPROACH. For one African capital fund that has bought land, Eswatini's entry; for the tax deduction that rewards protection annually, Seychelles' entry.

trackers.name: Seed Savers Network Kenya — a network that has trained 74,000 smallholders and helped establish 54 community seed banks on a model where one trusted member hosts seeds owned by all — and whose sector won a High Court ruling quashing the law that criminalised saving and exchanging seed
trackers.desc: THE COURT STRUCK DOWN THE LAW THAT MADE SAVING SEED A CRIME — method and adjacency declared first: THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THE SHIPPED HOST AND FIVE SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL ABSENT. THIS FILE'S SÃO TOMÉ ENTRY RECORDS A WOMEN'S MOVEMENT PROMOTING SEED SAVING, SEED SHARING AND SEED BANKS WITHOUT NAMING THIS ORGANISATION OR SHIPPING ITS HOST; ITS LIBYA BUCKET CARRIES A FOOD SOVEREIGNTY ALLIANCE HOST. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE COURT RULING, WHICH IS THE FIND: IN NOVEMBER 2025 THE HIGH COURT QUASHED A LAW THAT HAD CRIMINALIZED THE TRADITIONAL PRACTICES OF SAVING, MULTIPLYING AND EXCHANGING SEEDS — AND THE GOVERNMENT IS NOW REVIEWING THE LAW AND IMPLEMENTING MEASURES TO SUPPORT SEED SAVING. A national law making it a crime for a farmer to keep and swap her own seed, struck down. Check whether your own country has such a provision before assuming the practice is safe — and if it does, there is now a judgment to point at. THE HOSTING MODEL, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: SEED BANK MEMBERS IDENTIFY ONE TRUSTED MEMBER WITH SPACE TO KEEP SEEDS PRODUCED BY ALL OF THEM — SEEDS STORED BELONG TO INDIVIDUAL MEMBERS AND NORMALLY PROVIDE ENOUGH TO PLANT IN THE NEXT SEASON; EACH BANK IS HOSTED BY A COMMUNITY MEMBER WHO VOLUNTEERED TO STORE THE SEEDS ON THEIR LAND. No building, no budget, no registration: a room in someone's homestead and an agreement about whose seed is whose. That is the cheapest institution in this entire file, and ownership staying with the individual member is what keeps it from becoming a fund somebody can capture. THE SCALE AND THE RECORD: SINCE 2009 IT HAS TRAINED OVER 74,000 RURAL SMALLHOLDERS AND WORKED WITH OVER 3,000 FARMER GROUPS, HELPED ESTABLISH 54 COMMUNITY SEED BANKS AND DOCUMENTED 148 LOCAL CROP VARIETIES — WITH A LATER COUNT OF MORE THAN 1,000 SEED VARIETIES STORED ACROSS 140 COMMUNITY SEED BANKS. THE AMBASSADOR MODEL: SEED AMBASSADORS TRAINED BY THE NETWORK, ONE OF WHOM NOW MANAGES FIVE SEED BANKS AND WORKS WITH 100 SMALLHOLDERS — AND IN ONE COUNTY THE NETWORK WORKS WITH OVER 400 FARMERS THROUGH 10 SEED AMBASSADORS. Forty farmers per ambassador, five banks per experienced one. Those ratios let a community cost the thing before starting it. THE TRAINER-TO-TRAINER RULE: FARMERS WHO HAVE BEEN TRAINED CASCADE THE KNOWLEDGE TO THEIR IMMEDIATE NEIGHBOURS AND OTHER FARMERS. The same multiplication principle recorded in this file's Guinea-Bissau entry for paralegals, applied to seed. Two people trained is a village trained, if the cascade is built into the design from the start. THE PROBLEM IT WAS BUILT FOR, IN AN AMBASSADOR'S WORDS: THE BIGGEST PROBLEM WAS FARMERS APPROACHING THE PLANTING SEASON WITHOUT SEEDS TO PLANT BECAUSE THEY HAD CONSUMED EVERYTHING THEY HARVESTED — WITH A FARMER EXPLAINING THAT SEEDS STORED AT HOUSEHOLD LEVEL IN JERRYCANS WOULD ROT, WOULD BE CONVERTED TO FOOD DURING DRY SPELLS, AND WOULD BE GIVEN AWAY TO VISITORS. Precise and unsentimental about why household storage fails: hunger, damp and hospitality. A collective bank solves all three, because eating the seed becomes a decision somebody else witnesses. THE LOSS IT MEASURED FIRST: FOCUS GROUP DISCUSSIONS SHOWED THAT MORE THAN 30 CULTIVARS OF LOCAL CROPS HAD BEEN LOST IN JUST TEN VILLAGES OVER THE LAST 20 YEARS. They counted what had gone before proposing anything. A community biodiversity register is a document a village can compile itself in a few meetings, and it is the evidence base for everything after. HOW IT FINDS THE KNOWLEDGE: IDENTIFYING SENIOR FARMERS WHO STILL USE TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE AND LOCAL VARIETIES — THESE CHAMPION FARMERS BEING MOTIVATED TO SHARE THEIR KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERIENCE WITH OTHER FARMERS. THE TECHNICAL TRAINING: FARMERS' GROUPS ARE TRAINED IN BOTH POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE SEED SELECTION METHODS TO CONTINUOUSLY IMPROVE EXISTING FARMERS' VARIETIES, WITH EACH GROUP STARTING A SEED BANK AT THE END OF THE GROWING PERIOD — AND SEED AMBASSADORS WITH EXPERTS FROM COLLABORATING RESEARCH INSTITUTIONS TEST AND GERMINATE SEEDS TO IDENTIFY THE MOST VIABLE VARIETIES. Farmers' own varieties being deliberately improved rather than merely preserved. That answers the standard argument that indigenous seed means lower yields — selection is a technique, not a technology anyone has to buy. THE ARGUMENT FOR DECENTRALISING IT: IN A SITUATION WHERE ONLY ONE PERSON IS PRODUCING AND SHARING SEEDS, IF HIS VARIETY GETS INFECTED THEN ALL FARMERS WILL SUFFER THE FATE, BUT THE DIVERSITY OF SEED STOCKS IN FARMER-MANAGED SEED SYSTEMS PROVIDES SOME DEGREE OF CUSHION — WITH DEMONSTRATION PLOTS IN TWO ARID COUNTIES SHOWCASING VARIETIES ADAPTED TO DIFFERENT LOCAL CLIMATE ZONES. The case against a single supplier, whether that supplier is a company or a neighbour. Many small stores beat one large one when the failure comes. WHAT ONE BANK ACTUALLY HOLDS, AND WHO IT SERVES: A COMMUNITY SEED BANK HOLDING 13 VARIETIES OF MAIZE, 14 OF BEANS, THREE OF MILLET AND EIGHT OF SORGHUM, LENDING AND RECEIVING DONATIONS FROM ITS OVER 2,000 MEMBERS — ANOTHER STORING SEEDS FOR MORE THAN 100 FARMERS, ESTABLISHED BECAUSE FARMERS NEEDED CHEAPER ALTERNATIVES TO EXPENSIVE HYBRID SEEDS AND DROUGHT-RESISTANT CROPS. Thirty-eight varieties in one village store. That is the concrete answer to the seed-dependency this file's São Tomé entry describes — a household buying commercial seed every season versus a bank it can borrow from. AND THE SPREAD BEYOND ITS OWN COUNTRY, PLUS THE WOMEN'S ENTERPRISE STRAND: THE INITIATIVE HAS BEEN REPLICATED IN OTHER PARTS OF THE COUNTRY BY FARMERS THROUGH A FARMER-MANAGED SEED SYSTEM AND IS GROWING IN OTHER COUNTRIES INCLUDING TWO NAMED ONES — AND BUSINESSES HAVE BEEN DEVELOPED FOR WOMEN FROM SEED BANK TO SEED ENTERPRISES, SINCE WOMEN ARE LOCAL KEY CUSTODIANS OF SEEDS. REPLICATED BY FARMERS THEMSELVES, without the organisation. That is the strongest evidence the model needs no NGO to run it — and the seed enterprise strand turns a store into an income, which is what keeps a volunteer host committed. WHO IT SUITS: farming communities losing local varieties or dependent on bought seed, and anyone wanting a costed, copyable model for a village seed bank that needs no building and no registration. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY'S NETWORK, WITH SPREAD INTO TWO OTHERS; IT TRAINS AND ORGANISES RATHER THAN FUNDING, LITIGATING OR HOLDING LAND, AND THE COURT RULING CITED IS RECENT WITH THE LAW UNDER REVIEW — CHECK ITS CURRENT STATE. For the women's movement that carries seed across borders after disasters, São Tomé's entry; for the collective that builds rural organisations first, Somalia's entry.

trackers.name: Dahari
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the only IUCN member in the Comoros, founded in 2013, with around sixty staff working alongside communities on Anjouan and Grande Comore. Its central instrument is the INDIVIDUAL CONSERVATION AGREEMENT: a farmer contracts with Dahari for a fixed term not to clear forest or cut native trees on their plot, and receives payments calculated by the area preserved, checked by periodic inspection of the parcel. Management of the Moya forest zone has been delegated to Dahari by the national protected-areas network, and it has supported fishers in establishing the country's first permanent community-managed marine reserve. USE IT: if you hold or farm land carrying native forest, the conservation agreement is a way to make leaving it standing pay; if you fish, the marine programme is the route to a community-managed no-take zone.

trackers.name: Comoros — Ministry of Finance & Budget
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Ministry of Finance, Budget & Banking Sector prepares & implements the state finance laws (lois de finances) and budget, and oversees public-spending control via the General Inspection of Finance, Comoros. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Comoros.

trackers.name: Comoros — Agence Nationale pour la Promotion des Investissements (ANPI)
trackers.desc: National corporate registry; the ANPI (est. 2008, under the Ministry of Investment) operates the guichet unique for company creation & permits and maintains a public directory of officially registered Comorian companies, Comoros. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: Parcs nationaux des Comores — check which law governs your site
trackers.desc: TWO REGIMES EXIST AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME. The Comoros has had a loi-cadre relative à l'environnement since 1994, and the first protected area was classified under article 46 of it — a participatory process from January 1999 leading to the 2001 décret creating the Parc marin de Mohéli. Then Loi n° 18-005/AU of 5 December 2018 on the système national des aires protégées, promulgated 26 November 2019, replaced the framework, and on 23 May the head of state signed décrets formally establishing 5 new protected areas. Establish whether your site sits under article 46 of the 1994 loi-cadre or under the 2018 system law — older classifications predate the newer statute. NOTE THE STATUS: the Parc marin de Mohéli is an établissement public à caractère administratif under the environment minister's tutelle — a state body, whatever its community origins. And its founding decree prohibits industrial or commercial activities in the park outright, regulates ecotourism planning and provides for strict application of penalties — a flat prohibition is stronger than a permitting regime, so check whether your area carries the same term. Since 2016 the strategic vision, with UNDP and GEF support, has been a system managing 27 percent of national territory with a community approach.

trackers.name: Mohéli — the two questions the model never answered
trackers.desc: IF YOU ARE OFFERED THE MOHÉLI MODEL, ASK WHAT IT LEFT OUT. The park began as a community effort to protect turtles at Mohéli's south-eastern tip — one of the Indian Ocean's largest green turtle nesting sites — and became the country's first protected area in 2001, winning the Equator Initiative prize at the 2002 Johannesburg Earth Summit. UNDP called it a ‘méthode de cogestion couronnée de succès’ and the state is replicating it across Ngazidja, Ndzuani and Mohéli. BUT SEVERAL UN REPORTS AND SOURCES INTERVIEWED BY MONGABAY RECORD THAT IT IS FAR FROM A TOTAL SUCCESS: it produced no defined plan either for supporting the communities whose traditional rights were restricted by the protected areas, or for sustainable financing of the network. So ask those two questions — what is the defined plan to support people whose traditional rights are restricted, and what is the financing plan? Both gaps are documented in UN reporting, so the questions are evidenced rather than adversarial. AND KNOW THE MISUNDERSTANDING THAT RECURS EVERYWHERE: Hachime Abdéremane of the Comorian NGO Ulanga-Ngazidja, who helped create the park, put it exactly — ‘at the start, officials thought we were going to create a park, install barriers and charge outsiders entry. Whereas for us it was a park at community scale, which meant we were going to work with the residents.’ Principal activities are fishing, agriculture and livestock; dynamite fishing was the practice that first alerted conservationists.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Comoros' FADC — the national community development fund, which finances labour-intensive village works
trackers.desc: WHERE COMMUNITY MONEY COMES FROM: the Fonds d'Appui au Développement Communautaire (FADC), the Comorian national vehicle through which community development money is channelled. A documented transfer shows how it is fed and what it buys: 500 million Comorian francs, part of a budget-support package released by France, were retroceded to the FADC to finance HIGH LABOUR-INTENSITY WORKS (travaux à haute intensité de main d'oeuvre). Labour-intensive works are the form of community money most useful to a village under pressure — the budget is spent on local wages and a physical asset in your own commune, not on a consultancy. WHY THIS ENTRY EXISTS AT ALL, AND IT IS AN HONEST CORRECTION: the Comoros was researched TWICE in this file for a civil-society organisation to stand beside communities — in both cases nothing met the bar, and the country was left with a single conservation entry. The answer turned out not to be an NGO but the fund itself: in a small island state with a thin associative sector, the realistic lever is the national community fund and the commune that applies to it. Ask which FADC-financed works are planned in your commune, who selected them, and whether the labour is being hired locally — those three questions are the whole of community oversight here. WHO IT SUITS: Comorian villages and communal authorities seeking financing for local infrastructure and work programmes, on any of the islands. CAVEATS: SOURCING FOR THIS ENTRY IS THIN — the verified facts are the fund's existence, its purpose and one documented transfer; NO CLAIM is made here about current windows, ceilings or application routes, so confirm those locally before relying on them. The FADC is a state channel, not an advocate, and it will not oppose a project. For community conservation and agriculture agreements, Comoros' Dahari entry.

trackers.name: Comoros — a published attorney list with street addresses, free Supreme Court case law, and the CADI courts that decide village land disputes first
trackers.desc: WHERE TO FIND A LAWYER AND WHICH COURT DECIDES: no Comorian legal aid organisation could be verified for this file, so the practical route is three published things. (1) AN ATTORNEY LIST WITH STREET ADDRESSES IS PUBLISHED for Moroni — including practitioners on the Route de la Corniche, at Immeuble Ridjal, and on Boulevard Karthala facing the Comoros Museum and the Palais de Justice — which in a country with one multi-advocate firm is how you find counsel at all. (2) COMORIAN SUPREME COURT JUDGMENTS ARE PUBLISHED FREE on a francophone case-law database, searchable by chamber — judicial, administrative, social. Free access to your own supreme court's reasoning is not a small thing where government printers charge per page; take the citation of a comparable case with you. (3) THE COURT STRUCTURE A LAND DISPUTE ACTUALLY RUNS THROUGH, and this is the substantive point: the Supreme Court record shows a judgment of the TRIBUNAL DE CADI at Foumbouni — a traditional court — concerning THE VILLAGERS of a named locality being PARTIALLY OVERTURNED by the Moroni Court of Appeal. So a village land case may start before a cadi and be reopened on appeal in the formal courts — losing at the cadi stage is not the end, and the appeal route is documented. A judge of the Moroni commercial court has separately written that the COEXISTENCE OF TRADITIONAL AND FORMAL JUDICIAL SYSTEMS harms efficiency and confidence in justice, and that DIFFICULTIES IN EXECUTING JUDGMENTS are a recognised national problem — plan for enforcement as a separate fight, as in Lesotho and Zambia. WHO IT SUITS: Comorians with a land, inheritance or village boundary dispute on any island, and anyone needing to instruct counsel or cite precedent. CAVEATS: THIN GROUND, STATED HONESTLY — what is recorded here is a directory, a database and a court structure, NOT a legal aid service; the attorney list is a foreign-mission compilation and should be checked as current. For community conservation and agriculture agreements, Comoros' Dahari entry; for community works funding, the FADC entry.

trackers.name: Comoros' accords de cogestion — article 60 of loi 18-105/AU, one agreement PER VILLAGE, village écogardes, and a village committee that handles breaches before any court
trackers.desc: A CO-MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT PER VILLAGE: the Comorian protected-areas system rests on LOI N°18-105/AU on the SYSTÈME NATIONAL DES AIRES PROTÉGÉES, whose ARTICLE 60 governs ACCORDS DE COGESTION — agreements that establish and organise co-management involving the responsibility and participation of named VILLAGE COMMUNITIES, and which are expected to EVOLVE FROM CONSULTATIVE co-management, state-led in its first learning phase, TOWARD COOPERATIVE co-management IN WHICH RESPONSIBILITIES ARE SHARED FOR BOTH TAKING AND APPLYING DECISIONS. Ask in writing which of the two types your agreement is, and what triggers the move from consultative to cooperative — that transition is where real authority passes, and the statute already names it as the direction of travel. HOW IT WORKS ON THE GROUND AT MOHÉLI, the country's first protected area (April 2001, renamed a national park in 2015, a UNESCO biosphere reserve in 2021): EACH VILLAGE HAS ITS OWN SPECIFIC CO-MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT; ANY BREACH OF THE RULES IS DEALT WITH DIRECTLY BY A COMMITTEE OF VILLAGERS, and the case is transferred to the national judicial system ONLY WHERE LOCAL SOLUTIONS CANNOT BE FOUND; and local residents act as ÉCOGARDES responsible for awareness-raising and surveillance, trained with external technical support. One agreement per village and a village committee as the first instance is the strongest co-management design recorded in this file — it keeps enforcement local and cheap, and it means a neighbouring village's failure does not void your agreement. The park covers roughly 400 km2 marine and 200 km2 terrestrial, with 4,404 ha of marine area, protecting green and hawksbill turtle nesting; the model has been described as a successful co-management method and is being replicated across Ngazidja, Ndzuani and Mohéli. THE FAILURE, RECORDED SO YOU NEGOTIATE FOR IT: fourteen years after creation the park had NO DEDICATED OPERATING FINANCE and lived project to project, and THE ECONOMIC IMPACTS THE COMMUNITIES EXPECTED NEVER FOLLOWED; UN reporting found no defined plan either for SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES WHOSE TRADITIONAL RIGHTS WERE RESTRICTED by the protected areas, or for sustainably financing the network. If your traditional rights are being restricted, put the compensation and the funding line in the agreement itself — Mohéli shows that goodwill without a financing clause produces two decades of unmet expectation. WHO IT SUITS: Comorian coastal and forest villages inside or beside a protected area. CAVEATS: CO-MANAGEMENT OF STATE-DECLARED AREAS, NOT TENURE. For village-scale conservation agreements, Comoros' Dahari entry; for community works money, the FADC entry; for the cadi appeal route and the attorney list, the Comoros legal entry.

trackers.name: Ulanga-Ngazidja — the Grande Comore NGO that helped create a national park and signs partnership conventions with park conservators; its head defines what community-scale means
trackers.desc: THE NGO ON THE OTHER ISLAND: ULANGA-NGAZIDJA is a Comorian environmental NGO working on GRANDE COMORE (NGAZIDJA) — the island Dahari does not cover — which publishes its own environmental journal (Habari za Ulanga) and SIGNED A CONVENTION DE PARTENARIAT WITH THE CONSERVATOR OF THE PARC NATIONAL MITSAMIOULI-NDROUDÉ, at a ceremony gathering park members, LOCAL AUTHORITIES and the NGO. The convention fixes the terms of cooperation, both parties undertaking to cooperate on awareness-raising for environmental protection and valorisation, WITH THE STATED AIM OF CONTRIBUTING TO IMPROVING THE LIVING CONDITIONS OF THE COMMUNITIES LIVING IN THE PARK'S ZONES. A signed, publicly reported convention between a village NGO and a park conservator is a template you can ask for by name — it puts community living conditions into the text rather than leaving them to goodwill, which is exactly what Mohéli's twenty years of unmet expectation lacked. WHAT ITS HEAD SAYS, AND IT IS THE CLEAREST STATEMENT OF THE ARGUMENT IN THIS FILE: Hachime Abdéremane, head of Ulanga-Ngazidja, who took part in creating the park, recalls that AT THE START THE OFFICIALS THOUGHT WE WERE GOING TO CREATE A PARK, PUT UP BARRIERS AND CHARGE OUTSIDERS FOR ENTRY — WHEREAS FOR US IT WAS A PARK AT COMMUNITY SCALE, WHICH MEANT WE WERE GOING TO WORK WITH THE RESIDENTS. Say that sentence in your own first meeting. The difference between a fenced park and a community park is decided in the first conversation, not in the management plan. WHAT THE SITE HOLDS AND WHAT THREATENED IT: Ndroudé shelters the ÎLOT AUX TORTUES, a major GREEN TURTLE NESTING SITE unique on Ngazidja, whose reputation had been destroyed by POACHING, with recovery supported since 2011 by a Swiss marine-mammal conservation organisation. The other documented threat across the archipelago is DYNAMITE FISHING — pure dynamite thrown into the water to stun and kill fish en masse, with shockwaves capable of levelling coral reefs. WHO IT SUITS: Ngazidja villages and anyone on Grande Comore needing a domestic environmental partner or a park agreement precedent. CAVEATS: A VOLUNTEER-BASED NATIONAL NGO, not a funder or a legal service. For Anjouan and the village agreements, Comoros' Dahari entry; for the one-agreement-per-village co-management design, the accords de cogestion entry; for community works money, FADC.

trackers.name: Comoros' USD 54 million ecosystem-adaptation initiative — 6,200 ha of mangroves and watersheds, eight communal development plans, 10,000 people trained, and a participatory monitoring system
trackers.desc: THE MONEY THAT IS ALREADY COMING AND WHAT IT BUYS: the Comorian government has launched a climate-resilience initiative worth USD 54 MILLION — a USD 10 MILLION grant from the global environment fund plus USD 44 MILLION in co-financing from partners including a development bank and a bilateral agency — aiming to PROTECT 140,000 COASTAL INHABITANTS through the restoration, protection and sustainable management of 6,200 HECTARES of MANGROVES, BEACHES AND UPPER WATERSHEDS, described as THE ARCHIPELAGO'S NATURAL DEFENCE SYSTEM. WHAT A COMMUNITY GETS OUT OF IT, IN THE COMMITMENTS' OWN TERMS: EIGHT COMMUNAL DEVELOPMENT PLANS WILL BE UPDATED THROUGH INCLUSIVE AND GENDER-TRANSFORMATIVE PROCESSES; 10,000 COMMUNITY MEMBERS WILL BE TRAINED in integrated coastal zone management and climate-resilient planning; and A NEW PARTICIPATORY MONITORING SYSTEM WILL GUARANTEE COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION AND ACCOUNTABILITY, with COMMUNITIES PLAYING A LEADING ROLE in restoring and managing the ecosystems through mangrove and beach rehabilitation and watershed conservation to stabilise soils and improve fresh water availability. Eight communal development plans is a countable number — find out whether yours is one of them, because an updated commune plan is where a community's priorities become the document the money follows. And a participatory monitoring system is the accountability clause Mohéli's park never had: ask to sit on it. THE CATEGORY THE NATIONAL STRATEGY COMMITS TO: alongside the protected-area expansion, national work followed steps toward THE CREATION OF THREE NATIONAL PROTECTED AREAS AND THREE RÉSERVES COMMUNAUTAIRES, with community-engagement projects on Ndzuwani feeding that vision. Community reserve is a named category in the Comorian plan, distinct from national park — ask for that designation by name rather than accepting park status with a consultative role. The pressure behind all this: on Anjouan 80% OF THE FOREST WAS CUT BETWEEN 1995 AND 2014 and most rivers have dried up; Anjouan has 44 WATERSHEDS and Mohéli 25, identified in the national water strategy. WHO IT SUITS: Comorian coastal and watershed communities, and communes seeking their plan updated. CAVEATS: A DONOR-FUNDED GOVERNMENT PROGRAMME — confirm which communes and sites are included before assuming coverage. For the one-agreement-per-village design and the financing lesson from Mohéli, Comoros' accords de cogestion entry; for Anjouan village agreements, Dahari; for Grande Comore, Ulanga-Ngazidja; for community works money, FADC.

trackers.name: ONG AIDE — the Comorian association monitoring coral reef health at 20 sites across all three islands, plus IMANA on deforestation and the protected-area network designed for village co-management
trackers.desc: THE TWENTY MONITORED REEF SITES — and a baseline is what a community needs when a project later claims it caused no damage: ONG AIDE (ASSOCIATION D'INTERVENTION POUR LE DÉVELOPPEMENT ET L'ENVIRONNEMENT), AN ASSOCIATION GOVERNED BY THE 1986 LAW, CREATED IN NOVEMBER 1997 WITH THE SUPPORT OF THE DIRECTION NATIONALE DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT through a regional environment programme, whose overall objective is to contribute to the sustainable development of the Comoros through STUDY AND PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT, with specific objectives of MONITORING NATURAL ENVIRONMENTS, STRENGTHENING ENVIRONMENTAL CAPACITY, AWARENESS AND EDUCATION, AND DEVELOPING ALTERNATIVE SOCIOECONOMIC ACTIVITIES. ITS PROGRAMME IS THE RESOURCE: BIOPHYSICAL MONITORING OF THE STATE OF HEALTH OF CORAL REEFS AT 20 SITES ACROSS MOHÉLI, ANJOUAN AND GRANDE COMORE; SOCIOECONOMIC MONITORING OF THE CORAL REEFS; AND CARTOGRAPHY OF COASTAL BIOTOPES, funded through a regional marine protected areas network and international reef research bodies. Twenty reef sites monitored on all three islands, biophysically AND socioeconomically, is a dated baseline dataset held by a Comorian association. Ask AIDE what its records show for your stretch of coast before a developer's consultant tells you what was there — and note it maps the coastal biotopes, so the habitat boundary is already drawn. Alternative socioeconomic activities is written into its objectives — which means it is equipped to answer the question every coastal project poses: what will people do instead. ALSO NAMED: ONG IMANA, which has worked on the environment in the Comoros for three years and publishes on the causes and effects of deforestation in the archipelago, naming endemic species at risk including LIVINGSTONE'S FLYING FOX AND THE COMORO BLUE PIGEON, and noting that Comorian forests provide essential resources to local communities. THE STATE STRUCTURE THEY WORK ALONGSIDE, WHOSE STATED DESIGN IS THE WHOLE POINT: THE PARCS NATIONAUX DES COMORES AND THE NATIONAL PROTECTED AREAS NETWORK PROJECT WAS TITLED THE DEVELOPMENT OF A NATIONAL NETWORK OF TERRESTRIAL AND MARINE PROTECTED AREAS REPRESENTATIVE OF THE UNIQUE NATURAL HERITAGE OF THE COMOROS AND CO-MANAGED BY LOCAL VILLAGE COMMUNITIES — with a NAMED NATIONAL COORDINATOR, and published management plans running on fixed periods. Co-managed by local village communities is in the project's own title. Quote the title back: the network was not designed to exclude villages, it was designed around them — and each park has a published plan d'aménagement et de gestion with an end date, which is when it is renegotiated. WHO IT SUITS: Comorian coastal and forest communities on any of the three islands, and anyone needing baseline reef or habitat data. CAVEATS: SMALL ASSOCIATIONS AND DONOR-FUNDED PROGRAMMES — several of these records are dated; confirm current activity. For Anjouan village agreements, Comoros' Dahari entry; for Grande Comore and the park-conservator convention, Ulanga-Ngazidja; for the one-agreement-per-village design and the Mohéli financing failure, the accords de cogestion entry; for eight communal plans and a participatory monitoring system, the ecosystem-adaptation entry; for community works money, FADC.

trackers.name: What a Comorian association is and why they fail — the 1901-law model, the three required officers, the audit of assemblies and accounts, and the customary power that outranks the state
trackers.desc: THREE OFFICERS, AND THE THREE THINGS THAT GO WRONG: THE COMORIAN ASSOCIATIVE MODEL DERIVES FROM THE FRENCH LAW OF 1 JULY 1901, AND THE VERY GREAT MAJORITY OF THE ASSOCIATIVE FABRIC IS MADE UP OF VILLAGE ASSOCIATIONS WITH VERY TARGETED PURPOSES — WOMEN'S, SPORTING, CULTURAL OR LOCAL DEVELOPMENT — alongside thematic CSOs, MILITANT ORGANISATIONS, TRADE UNIONS, AND PROFESSIONAL AND ECONOMIC ASSOCIATIONS. THE FIELD OF INTERVENTION OF A CSO DEPENDS ON ITS STATUTES AND MAY BE NATIONAL, INSULAR, REGIONAL OR VILLAGE-LEVEL. Your statutes decide your reach. If you write village-level statutes you cannot later act at island level without amending them — write the scope you will eventually need, not the one you start with. THEY ARE STRUCTURED INTERNALLY BY STATUTES AND A BUREAU, WITH AT MINIMUM A PRESIDENT, A TREASURER AND A SECRETARY-GENERAL. Three officers is the floor. That is the whole formal requirement — a Comorian village can constitute a legal association with three named people and a set of statutes. AND THE AUDIT, WHICH IS THE MOST USEFUL SENTENCE HERE BECAUSE IT NAMES EXACTLY WHAT KILLS THESE BODIES: THE FUNCTIONING OF ASSOCIATIVE INSTANCES RARELY RESPECTS WHAT THEIR OWN INTERNALLY ADOPTED TEXTS PROVIDE — IN PARTICULAR, THE ASSEMBLIES ARE NOT HELD AT THE ADEQUATE INTERVALS OR ACCORDING TO THE ADEQUATE MODALITIES, THE LIST OF MEMBERS AND THE FINANCIAL ACCOUNTS ARE NOT UP TO DATE. Hold the assembly on time, keep the membership list current, keep the accounts current. Those three failures are what a ministry, a court or a funder will point to when it wants to say your association does not really represent anyone — and they are the three cheapest things in this entry to fix. Do them before you need them. THE PARALLEL STRUCTURE, AND ITS WEIGHT: BESIDES THE OFFICIAL AND MODERN STRUCTURES THERE EXIST SEVERAL HUNDRED CUSTOMARY, TRADITIONAL, RELIGIOUS AND COMMUNITY STRUCTURES WHICH PARTICIPATE IN SOCIAL LIFE AND CONCORD BUT WHICH HAVE NO LEGAL STATUS — AND ON GRANDE COMORE, CUSTOMARY POWER IS VERY INFLUENTIAL, AT THE CENTRE OF DECISIONS AT NATIONAL, REGIONAL AND VILLAGE SCALE, WITH DECISIONS TAKEN AT THAT LEVEL MORE RESPECTED THAN THOSE OF THE STATE. More respected than the state, and holding no legal status at all. That is the pairing to work with: take the decision through the customary body, and register an association to give that decision a legal face. Neither alone is enough — the custom carries the village, the statutes carry the paperwork. The same record notes that THE VITALITY OF THE ASSOCIATIVE MOVEMENT AMONG YOUNG PEOPLE AND THE STRICT DISTINCTION OF GENDER BETWEEN ASSOCIATIONS PROBABLY REFLECTS TRADITIONAL STRUCTURES LINKED TO AGE CLASSES AND GENDER. Age-class and gender associations already exist in every village. You do not need to invent a body — ask which ones are already meeting. WHAT THE STATE HAS BEEN BUILDING TOWARDS: a named capacity and volunteering project FOLLOWED STEPS TOWARDS THE CREATION OF THREE NATIONAL PROTECTED AREAS AND THREE COMMUNITY RESERVES, alongside a community engagement project on Anjouan, within a national protected-area expansion strategy whose priorities include A STRATEGY KNOWN AND SHARED BY ALL, A PRAGMATIC STRUCTURE ADAPTED TO NEEDS AND FINANCING, EFFICIENT AND SIMPLE PROCESSES AND PROCEDURES, AND GOOD COOPERATION BETWEEN THE MULTIPLE ACTORS. Three community reserves were an explicit national objective. Ask the protected areas service where that count now stands and whether a slot remains — a state target with an unfilled number is the easiest thing in government to volunteer for. ALSO NAMED: CEDAC, an association for childhood and community development, ran a project on REINFORCING LOCAL GOVERNANCE OF THE COMMUNES, touring Anjouan, Mohéli and Ngazidja to build collaboration between COMMUNES AND BASE ASSOCIATIONS, HANDING POSTERS TO THE MAYORS reading that COLLABORATION AND DIALOGUE BETWEEN THE COMMUNE AND THE ASSOCIATIONS ARE THE KEY TO LOCAL DEVELOPMENT. Somebody has already toured all three islands persuading mayors to work with village associations. If your commune is unresponsive, that campaign and its posters are the precedent to invoke. WHO IT SUITS: Comorian villages constituting or repairing an association, and anyone weighing the customary route against the legal one. CAVEATS: THIS IS A CIVIL SOCIETY ASSESSMENT, not a legal opinion — confirm current registration practice. For one agreement PER VILLAGE under article 60, Comoros' accords de cogestion entry; for the NGO that helped create a national park, Ulanga-Ngazidja; for reef monitoring at 20 sites, ONG AIDE; for the community development fund, FADC; for attorneys with street addresses, the published attorney list entry.

trackers.name: The village Ulanga movement — associations called Nature founded in most Comorian villages on two islands — plus Malezi Mema's first permanent community marine reserve, the Mrémani seedling nursery and 950 metres of anti-erosion lines
trackers.desc: AN ASSOCIATION CALLED NATURE, IN MOST OF THE VILLAGES — and this is the Comorian precedent worth carrying anywhere: ASSOCIATIONS NAMED ULANGA — WHICH MEANS NATURE IN COMORIAN — WERE CREATED ON NDZOUANI AND ON NGAZIDJA, IN MOST OF THE VILLAGES. ALMOST EVERYWHERE, ACTIONS OF REFORESTATION, CLEANING AND AWARENESS-RAISING OF THE POPULATION WERE ORGANISED WITHIN THE COMMUNITIES THANKS TO THE INITIATIVE OF THESE ASSOCIATIONS — AND THIS MOVEMENT SIGNIFICANTLY CONTRIBUTED TO THE COLLECTIVE AWARENESS OF ENVIRONMENTAL STAKES. Village by village, under one name, in the local language, on their own initiative. Not a national NGO opening branches — separate village associations that took the same name because the idea travelled. That is the cheapest form of national movement there is, and the Comorian record says it worked: the environment framework law and the government's sustainable development declaration came AFTER the villages had already organised, not before. WHAT ONE OF THEM ACTUALLY DOES, WITH THE NUMBERS: A NAMED ULANGA ASSOCIATION AT MRÉMANI IS DESCRIBED AS A LOCAL ASSOCIATION SPECIALISING IN THE PRODUCTION OF FOREST AND FRUIT SEEDLINGS, AND WAS ENGAGED TO DELIVER THE TRAINING — WITH 4,098 SEEDLINGS RAISED IN NURSERY IN TOTAL, 80% FOREST SPECIES AND 20% FRUIT SPECIES INCLUDING JACKFRUIT, ORANGE, AVOCADO, MANGO AND BREADFRUIT. A village association that is the SPECIALIST, hired by a bigger organisation to train others. That is the position to aim for: the skill stays in the village and the village gets paid for it. And the 80/20 split is the practical lesson — four fifths forest species for the watershed, one fifth fruit trees so households get something to eat and sell. AND THE EARTHWORKS, MEASURED: 950 LINEAR METRES OF ANTI-EROSION LINES WERE BUILT IN A NAMED WATERSHED, WITH THE STATED PURPOSE OF PROTECTING THE LAND — done with a water management committee and the farmers of the zone. Nine hundred and fifty metres, built with the water committee and the farmers together. If erosion is taking your soil, that is the scale one season's work reaches — and this file has recorded the same technique with published dimensions in Somaliland. THE MARINE FIRST: THANKS TO THE COMMITMENT OF THE MALEZI MEMA ASSOCIATION, THE CREATION OF A PERMANENT MARINE RESERVE AT A NAMED SITE BECAME THE FIRST PERMANENT COMMUNITY MARINE RESERVE IN THE COMOROS — described as an innovative conservation model. The FIRST permanent one, and a village association is named as the reason it exists. If your coast has no protection, somebody has to be first; here is the association that was, and its name is on the record for anyone who wants to ask how. AND THE FISHERS' FORUM THAT FOLLOWED: AROUND FIFTY FISHERMEN FROM 11 COASTAL VILLAGES MET AT A FORUM IN A NAMED TOWN TO STRENGTHEN THEIR COOPERATION ON MARINE RESOURCES. Fifty fishers from eleven villages in one room — the same shape this file recorded in Madagascar, where fifty-five people from eighteen areas founded a national network. The first forum is always small and always the turning point. MORE NAMED BODIES: ADIC, AN NGO SPECIALISED FOR MORE THAN 25 YEARS IN THE IMPROVEMENT OF THE LIVING CONDITIONS OF THE COMORIAN POPULATION, WORKING ANJOUAN AND MOHÉLI; AND A UJAMAA ASSOCIATION IN GRANDE COMORE. THE SCALE OF THE PROBLEM, AND ITS STATED CAUSE: THE COMOROS HAS LOST 28 PERCENT OF ITS FOREST COVER IN THE PAST 20 YEARS AND EROSION HAS CAUSED COASTAL AREAS TO RECEDE BY 30 METRES; POPULATION DENSITY ON ANJOUAN IS AROUND 900 PEOPLE PER SQUARE KILOMETRE — AND THE CAUSE IS NAMED PLAINLY AS INEQUALITIES IN HOW LAND AND RESOURCES WERE ALLOCATED AT INDEPENDENCE, FORCING POORER PEOPLE INTO LIVELIHOODS BASED ON UNSUSTAINABLE RESOURCE EXTRACTION. Deforestation traced to how land was allocated at independence, said by a conservation organisation about its own country. That sentence is the one to reuse wherever a community is blamed for cutting the forest it was pushed onto — the extraction is downstream of the allocation, and somebody credible has written it down. AND THE ARTISTS: an album was released by SOME OF THE BEST KNOWN COMORIAN ARTISTS TO ENCOURAGE THE REFORESTATION OF ANJOUAN, FOLLOWED BY A SERIES OF CONCERTS. Musicians recording an album for a reforestation campaign, then touring it. Where a leaflet reaches nobody, a song reaches everybody — and the artists in your country are approachable in a way a ministry is not. WHO IT SUITS: Comorian villages on any island, coastal communities wanting a reserve, and anyone whose soil is eroding. CAVEATS: SMALL VILLAGE ASSOCIATIONS with limited capacity — this file's separate entry on why Comorian associations fail is worth reading alongside. For the organisation supporting rural communities with individual conservation agreements, Comoros' Dahari entry; for the Grande Comore NGO that helped create a national park, Ulanga-Ngazidja; for coral reef monitoring at 20 sites, ONG AIDE; for article 60 co-management agreements, the accords de cogestion entry; for the national community development fund, FADC.

trackers.name: STDM (Social Tenure Domain Model), GLTN / UN-Habitat — the free open-source system for recording land rights that are neither registered nor registerable — communities draw boundaries on printed satellite images, and it stores photographs, videos and sketches as supporting proof
trackers.desc: PRINT THE SATELLITE IMAGE AND LET PEOPLE DRAW THEIR OWN BOUNDARIES — declared overlap first: THE NETWORK BEHIND THIS TOOL ALREADY APPEARS AS A SOURCE URL IN TWO ENTRIES IN THIS FILE, UNDER LIBYA AND SUDAN. NEITHER DESCRIBES THE TOOL, WHICH IS WHAT THIS ENTRY IS FOR. THE SCALE OF THE PROBLEM, IN ONE FIGURE: UP TO 70% OF LAND USES IN MANY DEVELOPING COUNTRIES IS NOT RECORDED IN NATIONAL LAND REGISTRIES. Seven tenths of land use unrecorded. Your community is not an oversight, it is the norm — and the fix is not waiting for the registry to reach you. WHAT THE TOOL IS FOR, AND IT IS THE EXACT SITUATION MOST COMMUNITIES IN THIS FILE ARE IN: IT FOCUSES ON LAND AND PROPERTY RIGHTS WHICH ARE NEITHER REGISTERED NOR REGISTERABLE, AS WELL AS OVERLAPPING CLAIMS THAT MAY HAVE TO BE ADJUDICATED IN TERMS OF WHO, WHERE AND WHAT RIGHT — SUPPORTING THE DEVELOPMENT AND MAINTENANCE OF RECORDS IN AREAS WHERE REGULAR OR FORMAL REGISTRATION OF LAND RIGHTS IS NOT THE RULE, AND TACKLING THE NEEDS OF NEGLECTED COMMUNITIES SUCH AS PEOPLE IN INFORMAL SETTLEMENTS AND CUSTOMARY AREAS. NEITHER REGISTERED NOR REGISTERABLE. Most tools assume a title exists or could exist; this one is built for the case where neither is true, and it handles OVERLAPPING claims rather than forcing one answer — which is what customary and grazing land actually looks like. AND THE PRINCIPLE: IT ENABLES YOU TO SHOW WHAT CAN BE OBSERVED ON THE GROUND IN TERMS OF TENURE, AS AGREED WITHIN LOCAL COMMUNITIES — REPRESENTING PEOPLE-LAND RELATIONSHIPS INDEPENDENT OF THE LEVEL OF FORMALITY, LEGALITY AND TECHNICAL ACCURACY. AS AGREED WITHIN LOCAL COMMUNITIES is the standard of proof, not a surveyor's certificate. So the record can be built by the people who know the boundaries. IT COSTS NOTHING: A FREE AND OPEN SOURCE PRO-POOR LAND RECORDATION SYSTEM — IT IS OPEN SOURCE, THUS AVAILABLE FREE, HENCE ITS SUSTAINABILITY — A PLUGIN FOR FREE MAPPING SOFTWARE, USABLE ON WINDOWS, LINUX AND MAC, WITH ITS SOURCE CODE PUBLIC AND TWO PUBLIC MAILING LISTS FOR USERS AND ANNOUNCEMENTS. Free forever, with the code public — so no organisation can take the system away when a project ends, and the mailing lists mean you can ask other users when you get stuck. THE METHOD, WHICH IS THE MOST TRANSFERABLE THING HERE AND NEEDS NO SOFTWARE AT ALL: SATELLITE IMAGERY IS USED AS THE BASIS FOR DATA COLLECTION — PEOPLE RECOGNISE IMMEDIATELY THE ROADS AND SPATIAL UNITS ON THE IMAGES; HIGH RESOLUTION IMAGES CAN BE ENLARGED AND PRINTED WITH OVERLAPS WITH NEIGHBOUR PRINTS; AND BASED ON THE IDENTIFICATION OF BOUNDARIES ON THE IMAGES, THE BOUNDARIES CAN BE DRAWN ON THE IMAGE. PEOPLE REALLY UNDERSTAND WHAT THEY SEE ON THE IMAGE — THEY CAN IDENTIFY THE PLACE WHERE THEY LIVE, AND WHERE THEIR NEIGHBOURS LIVE. Print the image large, overlap the sheets, and let people draw. An elder who cannot read a cadastral plan can find their own compound on a photograph in seconds. This file has recorded participatory mapping across the Congo Basin and Cameroon; this is the cheapest version of it, and the printing is most of the cost. WHAT ELSE IT HOLDS AS PROOF: DOCUMENTS THAT SUPPORT SOCIAL TENURES — PHOTOGRAPHS, VIDEOS, SKETCHES, MAPS, OR OTHER DOCUMENTS — ALONGSIDE TITLE DEEDS, NAMES, GENDER AND PROPERTIES. A photograph of the old boundary tree and a video of an elder describing it are storable evidence here. Nothing else in this file treats that material as part of a land record. THE RANGELAND APPLICATION, FOR PASTORALISTS: AS PILOTED BY A NAMED REGIONAL INSTITUTE AND PARTNERS, IT ADDRESSED SECURITY OF TENURE THROUGH PARTICIPATORY COMMON RESOURCE IDENTIFICATION, MAPPING AND DOCUMENTATION — KEY RESOURCES INCLUDING CATTLE DIPS, SALT LICK AREAS AND WATER POINTS — AND MANAGEMENT IMPROVED DUE TO THE RECOGNITION OF BOUNDARIES ANTICIPATORILY DEFINED, LEADING TO THE REVIVAL AND ESTABLISHMENT OF COMMUNITY RESOURCE MANAGEMENT COMMITTEES ESPECIALLY AROUND WATER AND GRAZING LANDS. Mapping the water points and salt licks rather than the plots. For grazing land the resource is the thing to record, not the perimeter — and the mapping itself revived the committees that manage them. THE RECORD: FROM A FIRST PROTOTYPE IN ONE AFRICAN COUNTRY IT SPREAD TO OVER 100 SETTLEMENTS IN DIFFERENT MUNICIPALITIES, MOBILISING COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT, AWARENESS BUILDING, TECHNICAL TRAINING AND DATA GENERATION USING PARTICIPATORY APPROACHES — AND THE SUCCESSES CAUGHT THE ATTENTION OF LOCAL AUTHORITIES, WHO FOUND THE DATA GENERATED VALUABLE INSIGHTS. The authorities came to want the data. A community record that is accurate enough for the municipality to use becomes the municipality's record too, which is a far stronger position than being outside the system. THE EVIDENCE ACROSS THREE CASE STUDIES: A REMARKABLE IMPROVEMENT IN INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS AND COLLABORATION AMONG DIFFERENT INSTITUTIONS, AS WELL AS A NOTABLE REDUCTION IN LAND CONFLICTS OR DISPUTES. AND THE NETWORK'S STATED VALUES, WHICH ARE THE TERMS TO HOLD ANY PARTNER TO: PRO-POOR, EQUITY, AFFORDABILITY, GOOD GOVERNANCE, SUBSIDIARITY, GENDER SENSITIVENESS, SYSTEMATIC LARGE SCALE APPROACH AND SUSTAINABILITY — WITH A PUBLISHED LIST OF IMPLEMENTING ORGANIZATIONS. A published list of implementing organisations is the route in: find the one nearest you rather than starting alone, because the software is free but the first training is not something to improvise. WHO IT SUITS: African communities on customary, grazing or informal land with no registrable title, and organisations helping them record it. CAVEATS: IT NEEDS SOMEONE COMFORTABLE WITH A COMPUTER AND A FIRST TRAINING — the tool is free, the capacity is not. For the participatory mapping that put seven million hectares on the map, DR Congo's MappingForRights entry; for the global platform where a boundary becomes a public record, Mali's LandMark entry; for the free land library and country pages, Guinea-Bissau's entry.

trackers.name: University law clinics as free representation — the network that opened 14 of them, what its clinics actually do for communities, the curriculum other faculties copy, and the continental associations to ask in a country with no clinic yet
trackers.desc: THE LAW FACULTY DOWN THE ROAD HAS A CLINIC — declared adjacency first: THIS FILE ALREADY CARRIES FIVE NATIONAL FREE-LEGAL-CLINIC ENTRIES, UNDER MOROCCO, BURKINA FASO, CÔTE D'IVOIRE, THE REPUBLIC OF CONGO AND MADAGASCAR. NONE DESCRIBES THE CONTINENTAL NETWORKS, THE CURRICULUM, OR HOW A COMMUNITY REACHES A CLINIC IN A COUNTRY WITH NO ENTRY OF ITS OWN. THAT IS WHAT THIS ONE IS FOR. WHAT A LAW CLINIC IS: CLINICAL LEGAL EDUCATION, BY WAY OF LAW CLINICS, TRAINS LAW STUDENTS IN THE SPIRIT OF SOCIAL JUSTICE AND PUBLIC SERVICE, AND PROVIDES DESPERATELY-NEEDED LEGAL SERVICES TO POOR COMMUNITIES AND UNDERPRIVILEGED PERSONS — LAW CLINICS SERVE TO FILL A GAP NOT ADEQUATELY ADDRESSED BY GOVERNMENTAL LEGAL AID PROGRAMMES. A law faculty is a standing pool of supervised legal labour that costs a community nothing and exists in almost every African capital and many provincial cities. It is the nearest free legal help most people have and the one they least often think of — and unlike a busy advocate, a clinic wants the case because the case is the teaching. THE NETWORK: ESTABLISHED IN 2003, A NON-GOVERNMENTAL, NON-PROFIT AND NON-POLITICAL ORGANIZATION COMMITTED TO PROMOTING CLINICAL LEGAL EDUCATION, LEGAL EDUCATION REFORM, LEGAL AID AND ACCESS TO JUSTICE, AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF FUTURE PUBLIC INTEREST LAWYERS — BUILDING A NETWORK OF COHESIVE UNIVERSITY-BASED LAW CLINICS PROVIDING PRO-BONO LEGAL SERVICES TO THE UNDER-SERVED. SINCE 2004, 14 UNIVERSITY-BASED LAW CLINICS HAVE OPENED, INCLUDING AT THE NATIONAL LAW SCHOOL — WITH A NAMED STREET LOCATION IN THE CAPITAL AND PUBLISHED OPENING HOURS, WEEKDAYS 9AM TO 5PM. Fourteen clinics from one organisation in twenty years, and it keeps office hours anyone can walk into. WHAT ITS CLINICS DO, WITH NAMED EXAMPLES WORTH ASKING YOUR OWN FACULTY TO COPY: ONE CLINIC PROVIDES PRO BONO LEGAL AND ADVISORY SERVICES TO THE POOR AND UNDERSERVED MEMBERS OF THE COMMUNITY WITHIN AND OUTSIDE THE UNIVERSITY, AND ENGAGES IN PUBLIC ENLIGHTENMENT AND SENSITIZATION ON THE HUMAN RIGHTS OF THE PEOPLE. ANOTHER ORGANISED A COMMUNITY JUSTICE SPEAK OUT FORUM FOR MEMBERS OF TWO NAMED COMMUNITIES TO INTERACT WITH THE POLICE, THE LEGAL AID COUNCIL AND THE DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC PROSECUTION. ANOTHER CONDUCTED A TWO-DAY PRISON CLINIC AT TWO NAMED PRISONS, INTERVIEWING PRISONERS OF WHOM 36 WERE ON PRE-TRIAL DETENTION. A COMMUNITY JUSTICE SPEAK OUT FORUM is the copyable one: the clinic convened the villagers, the police and the prosecutors in one room, and hosting it as a university event rather than a protest is what made all three come. If your committee cannot get officials to a meeting, ask a law faculty to convene it instead. AND THE PRISON CLINIC matters where land defenders are held: students went in, interviewed, and found thirty-six people on pre-trial detention. Somebody has to count them before anyone can be released. ITS CURRENT WORK NAMES THIS FILE'S SUBJECTS DIRECTLY: IT FOSTERS LEGAL REFORMS, SUPPORTS CIVIC SPACE DEFENDERS, AND PROMOTES ENVIRONMENTAL AND CLIMATE JUSTICE. THE CURRICULUM, WHICH IS THE PART THAT TRAVELS: IT DEVELOPED A CLINICAL LEGAL EDUCATION CURRICULUM FOR UNIVERSITY LAW FACULTIES AND CLINICS, INTRODUCED AS PART OF THE UNDERGRADUATE LAW PROGRAMME, WITH TRAINING WORKSHOPS AND MANUALS FOR TEACHERS — AND IT HOSTED THE FIRST NATIONAL COLLOQUIUM IN PARTNERSHIP WITH A JUSTICE INITIATIVE, WHERE PARTICIPATING LAW FACULTIES SUPPORTED THE INTRODUCTION OF CLINICAL LEGAL EDUCATION. The curriculum and the teachers' manuals already exist. A dean who says a clinic would take years to design can be told the design is written, tested and free — which turns a long argument into a short one. THE OTHER NETWORKS, WHICH ARE THE ROUTE IF YOUR COUNTRY HAS NO CLINIC: AN ASSOCIATION OF UNIVERSITY LEGAL AID INSTITUTIONS, A EUROPEAN NETWORK OF CLINICAL LEGAL EDUCATION, AND A GLOBAL ALLIANCE FOR JUSTICE EDUCATION — THESE NETWORKS PROMOTE TRANSNATIONAL STUDY VISITS AND EXCHANGE PROGRAMS, ENJOY COLLABORATION BETWEEN CLINICAL PROGRAMS AND LEGAL PROFESSIONALS, AND PROMOTE INITIATIVES THAT MIGHT IMPROVE THE COMMUNITY UNDERSTANDING OF THE BENEFITS OF CLINICAL LEGAL EDUCATION. STUDY VISITS AND EXCHANGE PROGRAMS mean a faculty with no clinic can send someone to watch one working. That is the cheapest way a new clinic gets started, and these networks pay for it. THE PUBLISHED JOURNALS: AN AFRICAN JOURNAL OF CLINICAL LEGAL EDUCATION AND ACCESS TO JUSTICE, AND AN INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF CLINICAL LEGAL EDUCATION, WITH AN EDITORIAL BOARD NAMING LAW ACADEMICS AND SENIOR ADVOCATES FROM SEVERAL AFRICAN COUNTRIES. An editorial board is a published list of senior lawyers who have already committed themselves to access to justice in print. This file has repeatedly noted that finding the right advocate is the hard part; that list is a starting point, and writing to a named professor gets answered more often than writing to a firm. AND THE EFFECT RECORDED: THE INTERVENTION BY LEGAL CLINICS IN PROVIDING LEGAL AID, ADVICE AND ACCESS TO JUSTICE HAS BROUGHT RELIEF TO PEOPLE WHO OTHERWISE WOULD NOT HAVE HAD ACCESS TO JUSTICE, DUE TO THE INSUFFICIENCY OF FUNDS AND THE INADEQUACY OF LEGAL AID FACILITIES PROVIDED BY GOVERNMENT. WHO IT SUITS: African communities near any university with a law faculty, and organisations wanting a clinic started in a country that has none. CAVEATS: CLINICS ARE STAFFED BY SUPERVISED STUDENTS AND RUN ON THE ACADEMIC YEAR — they are strong on advice, documentation and convening, weaker on long litigation, and quiet in vacation. For the national clinics already filed, Morocco's, Burkina Faso's, Côte d'Ivoire's, the Republic of Congo's and Madagascar's entries; for the free brokerage that finds a law firm, the Central African Republic's entry; for the community paralegal method where there is no lawyer at all, Sierra Leone's Timap entry.

trackers.name: The Amplio Talking Book — a battery audio device that plays hours of local-language content off-grid and records the community's spoken replies back — no cost to the user, one device serving 100 listeners, with a Ghanaian arm that sets it up and a phone platform for basic handsets
trackers.desc: IT PLAYS THE LAW ALOUD, AND RECORDS WHAT THE VILLAGE SAYS BACK — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO ENTRY NAMES TALKING BOOKS IN ONE LINE AS A TOOL USED BY A LAND-RIGHTS ORGANISATION, AND THE ETHIOPIA AND CAPE VERDE ENTRIES COVER COMMUNITY RADIO. NONE DESCRIBES THE DEVICE, THE FEEDBACK LOOP, THE VOICE PLATFORM OR THE GHANAIAN ARM. WHAT IT IS: A BATTERY-POWERED AUDIO DEVICE DESIGNED WITH AND FOR LOW-LITERATE PEOPLE IN RURAL, REMOTE AND OFF-GRID COMMUNITIES — USING AUDIO PROMPTS AND VISUAL ICONS, EACH ICON EMBOSSED WITH A DOT FOR THE VISUALLY IMPAIRED — DELIVERING HOURS OF CONTENT IN ANY LANGUAGE, WITH MULTIPLE TOPICS AND PLAYLISTS, PLAYED ON DEMAND. THE TWO-WAY CLAUSE, WHICH IS THE FIND AND WHICH ALMOST NOTHING ELSE IN THIS FILE OFFERS: WITH THE BUILT-IN MICROPHONE, USERS CAN RECORD THEIR FEEDBACK DIRECTLY ONTO THE DEVICE — AND EACH DEVICE CAN COLLECT HUNDREDS, OR EVEN THOUSANDS, OF USER FEEDBACK MESSAGES, TYPICALLY RECORDED IN A COMMUNITY'S LOCAL LANGUAGE. Every other information tool here pushes outward. This one comes back with the community's own voice on it, in their own language, unmediated by a form or a translator. For a consultation that was never really held, that is a way of producing the record the developer never took — hundreds of recorded statements from people who cannot write a submission. WHY THAT MATTERS, IN THEIR OWN FRAMING: WHILE IT IS A BEST PRACTICE TO INCLUDE STAKEHOLDERS IN THE EVALUATION PROCESS, IT IS NOT ALWAYS EASY, ESPECIALLY IN RURAL COMMUNITIES — PROJECT TEAMS OFTEN FACE BARRIERS DUE TO GEOGRAPHIC REMOTENESS, ILLITERACY AND LANGUAGE ABILITIES, AND POWER DYNAMICS. POWER DYNAMICS named alongside distance and literacy. People say different things into a device at home than in a meeting with the chief and the company sitting there — which is exactly why a recording made privately is worth more than a show of hands. WHAT PEOPLE ACTUALLY SAID WHEN GIVEN THE CHANCE: ONE PILOT COLLECTED 1,200 USER FEEDBACK MESSAGES IN ABOUT SIX MONTHS — PEOPLE ASKED A WIDE RANGE OF QUESTIONS ABOUT HEALTH SERVICES, THE COST OF HEALTH CARE, CORPORAL PUNISHMENT, CHILD PROTECTION ISSUES AND MORE. Twelve hundred messages in six months, on subjects nobody had put on the agenda. Give a community a way to speak and it raises what it actually cares about, not what the programme was designed around. THE HONEST PROCESSING PROBLEM, RECORDED BECAUSE IT WILL BE YOURS TOO: THE FEEDBACK WAS IN LOCAL LANGUAGES, SO THEY HAD TO WORK WITH LOCAL LANGUAGE SPEAKERS TO SORT AND PROCESS THE RECORDINGS AND FEED THE DATA INTO THE IMPACT ASSESSMENT AND, MORE IMPORTANTLY, INTO THE PROGRAM DESIGN — AND EXISTING SOFTWARE WAS TOO CUMBERSOME FOR AUDIO AND TOO COMPLEX FOR THE LOCAL LANGUAGE SPEAKERS TO NAVIGATE, SO THEY BUILT NEW WEB-BASED SOFTWARE FOR IT. Collecting the voices is the easy half. Budget for the people who will listen to a thousand recordings in the local language and sort them — and note that the tool for doing it was built because the professional software defeated the local speakers, which is a warning about every system handed to a community. WHO MAKES THE CONTENT: LOCAL PARTNERS ABLE TO CUSTOMIZE MESSAGES DEPENDING ON THE CULTURAL CONTEXT — USUALLY SONGS, DRAMAS, INTERVIEWS AND ENDORSEMENTS — PRODUCED WITH SUBJECT EXPERTS, MUSICIANS AND THEATER GROUPS, IN MORE THAN A DOZEN LANGUAGES. SONGS AND DRAMAS, made with musicians and theatre groups from the area. A land law explained as a drama by people the village knows is listened to; the same law read out as a notice is not. THE SHARING RATIO AND THE PRICE: A BUILT-IN SPEAKER ALLOWS FAMILIES AND GROUPS TO LISTEN AND LEARN TOGETHER, AND DEPENDING ON PROGRAM DESIGN A SINGLE DEVICE CAN SERVE 100 LISTENERS OR MORE — AND THERE IS NO COST TO THE END USER. One device, a hundred people. That changes the arithmetic of a funding request from a device per household to a handful per village. THE PHONE PLATFORM FOR EVERYONE WITHOUT A DEVICE: A VOICE PLATFORM LETS TEAMS REACH ENTIRE COMMUNITIES INSTANTLY — TEXT MESSAGES OR AUTOMATED VOICE CALLS TO THOUSANDS OF NUMBERS AT ONCE, INCLUDING BASIC FEATURE PHONES WITH NO INTERNET REQUIRED, DELIVERING CONTENT AND COLLECTING FEEDBACK OVER A REGULAR PHONE CALL. Automated voice calls to thousands of basic handsets. When a hearing date moves or an eviction notice appears, that is how a whole district is told in an hour — and the reply comes back by voice, not by form. THE AFRICAN ARM AND WHAT IT SELLS: A NON-PROFIT GHANAIAN ORGANISATION PARTNERS WITH GOVERNMENT AGENCIES, LOCAL NGOs AND INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS TO PLAN AND DELIVER PROGRAMS IN THE HARDEST-TO-REACH RURAL COMMUNITIES, OFFERING SERVICES FROM TECHNOLOGY SETUP AND TRAINING TO PROGRAM DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION. An African organisation you can contract for the setup rather than importing a team. LOCAL NGOs are named among its partners, so a national organisation supporting your community is an eligible customer. THE MULTI-TOPIC POINT, FROM A GOVERNMENT HEALTH DIRECTOR RATHER THAN THE VENDOR: MOST OF OUR PARTNERS ARE WORKING ON MULTISECTORAL PROJECTS — WITH THE DEVICE WE CAN SHARE KNOWLEDGE ABOUT MANY TOPICS AND ADDRESS CRITICAL, INTERCONNECTED ISSUES, SUCH AS CLIMATE CHANGE AND GENDER EQUITY. THE REACH AND THE AFRICAN DEPLOYMENTS: OVER TWO MILLION PEOPLE IN 14 COUNTRIES SINCE 2007 — INCLUDING A LAND-RIGHTS PROGRAMME IN LIBERIA, AN ADOLESCENT RIGHTS PROJECT IN ZAMBIA, A SMART VILLAGES PROJECT IN NIGER, A 73-COMMUNITY FARMER PROGRAMME IN NORTHERN GHANA, AND A PROJECT THAT ECONOMICALLY EMPOWERED 23,000+ WOMEN FARMERS. A LAND-RIGHTS PROGRAMME IN LIBERIA is the precedent to cite: this exact device has already been used to explain a land law to rural people, which means the use case is proven rather than proposed. AND THE SCALE OF THE GAP: NEARLY 800 MILLION PEOPLE WORLDWIDE CANNOT READ OR WRITE. WHO IT SUITS: African communities where the law, the notice or the contract exists only in writing and only in a foreign language — and organisations that need the community's own answer on record. CAVEATS: SUPPLIED THROUGH PARTNER ORGANISATIONS AND GOVERNMENTS RATHER THAN SOLD TO VILLAGES, AND THE CONTENT AND FEEDBACK PROCESSING MUST BE BUDGETED — the Ghanaian arm is the route for setup. For talking books used in a land-rights programme, the Republic of the Congo's entry; for free radio scripts in local languages, Cape Verde's entry; for the association a station joins, Ethiopia's entry.

trackers.name: They reviewed every carbon standard's complaint system and named the only one that works — with a table of recommendations per standard, a benefit-sharing audit of 47 projects, and complaints filed in their own name on communities' behalf
trackers.desc: THEY REVIEWED EVERY CARBON STANDARD'S COMPLAINT SYSTEM AND NAMED THE ONE THAT WORKS — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S TOGO ENTRY COVERS THE TRAINING THAT PREPARES COMMUNITIES BEFORE A CARBON DEVELOPER ARRIVES, ITS SOUTH SUDAN ENTRY THE CARBON-VIOLENCE PLANTATION REPORT, ITS CHAD ENTRY THE INDIGENOUS-LED FUND, AND ITS TANZANIA AND DJIBOUTI ENTRIES PASTORALIST COALITIONS. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE REVIEW AND ITS SINGLE-NAME FINDING, WHICH IS THE FIND: A REVIEW CONDUCTED ON ITS BEHALF FOUND THAT ONLY ONE STANDARD BODY PROVIDES APPROPRIATE RECOURSE TO FILE GRIEVANCES TO COMMUNITIES AFFECTED BY CLIMATE PROJECTS — THE REMAINING ASSESSED STANDARDS HAVE INADEQUATE OR NON-EXISTENT GRIEVANCE MECHANISMS, LEAVING LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLES VULNERABLE AND INFRINGING ON THEIR ACCESS TO JUSTICE. One out of all of them. Before a community spends a year filing under whichever standard certified the project on its land, this tells it whether that route exists at all — and the briefing names each standard with specific recommendations, so the answer for yours is a table lookup rather than a year of discovery. THE SUBMISSION CHANNELS IT DOCUMENTS, WHICH ARE WHAT TO DEMAND: REQUIREMENTS FOR GRIEVANCE SUBMISSIONS INCLUDE AN ONLINE COMPLAINTS FORM, MAIL, WHATSAPP, EMAIL, VOICE OR VIDEO RECORDING, CALLING A TOLL-FREE HOTLINE, OR AN IN-PERSON MEETING AT THE PLACE WHERE THE COMPLAINANT IS. WHATSAPP, VOICE RECORDING, AND A MEETING WHERE THE COMPLAINANT IS. A grievance system that only accepts a written English form has excluded the people it exists for — and here is a documented list of what an accessible one looks like, usable as the demand when yours does not.
