WHAT DOES EXIST: advocates of the Guinean bar organise VOLUNTEER FREE-DEFENCE PERIODS — women advocates have run a March initiative for successive years, defending accused people without means before the Conakry jurisdictions, with nine accused at the Mafanco first-instance tribunal assisted in one such month. Their own explanation of why it matters names the harm precisely: where a person cannot pay and no counsel is assigned of office, they can remain in detention a long time WITHOUT THEIR FILE BEING DEFENDED. If a family member is detained after a land protest, the bar's volunteer scheme and the NGOs are the whole of the answer — ask the barreau de Guinée when the next initiative runs and which tribunals it covers. Reporting also notes multi-service centres offering care and legal support, and that although a medico-legal report is not legally required to lodge a complaint, in practice it is often demanded — so obtain any medical documentation early, because its absence later becomes an obstacle to conviction. WHO IT SUITS: Guineans without means facing prosecution or detention, including after protests over mining and land, and anyone needing to know that the state route is absent. CAVEATS: VOLUNTEER AND EPISODIC — a month-long bar initiative is not a standing service, and NGO capacity is concentrated in Conakry. For legal aid and human rights casework, Guinea's MDT entry; for evidence and the financier route, CECIDE; for community protocols and mining royalties, Action Mines; for sub-regional solidarity, CGLTE-OA.

trackers.name: Guinea's code forestier L/2017/060 and the Direction Nationale des Eaux et Forêts — the law to cite, the office that runs village nurseries, and the permit-overlap trap in a bauxite country
trackers.desc: THE LAW TO CITE AND THE OFFICE TO ASK: Guinea's forest code is LOI ORDINAIRE L/2017/060/AN OF 12 DECEMBER 2017, adopted in plenary on 24 April 2017. Its opening definitions are the ones to quote in a letter: an AIRE PROTÉGÉE is a clearly defined geographic space, RECOGNISED ACCORDING TO INTERNATIONAL CRITERIA, dedicated and managed BY LEGAL OR OTHER MEANS to favour the LONG-TERM conservation of nature, ecosystem services AND THE CULTURAL VALUES ATTACHED TO THEM; and AMÉNAGEMENT FORESTIER covers technical AND SOCIO-ECONOMIC operations together with legal and administrative measures. Two phrases are worth carrying: BY LEGAL OR OTHER MEANS — which is the opening for a customary arrangement — and CULTURAL VALUES, which puts sacred groves and burial forests inside the statutory definition rather than outside it. THE OFFICE AND WHAT IT ALREADY DOES WITH VILLAGES: the DIRECTION NATIONALE DES EAUX ET FORÊTS, under the environment ministry, runs the ANNUAL NATIONAL REFORESTATION CAMPAIGN across the whole territory through its DECONCENTRATED SERVICES — prefectural and communal sections and the CANTONNEMENTS FORESTIERS — with strong grassroots community involvement; documented activity includes COMMUNITY REFORESTATION with teak in a village of Coyah with technical support from forestry agents, awareness sessions with village communities of the Mambiyah rural commune, Kindia, ON THE IMPORTANCE OF CREATING COMMUNITY FORESTS, and installing a VILLAGE NURSERY at Gogota in Guinée Forestière. The cantonnement forestier is the office to walk into: it already has agents assigned to villages, and a nursery is the cheapest way to start a claim that is visibly yours. THE TRAP, DOCUMENTED FOR THE REGION AND ACUTE HERE: research on community forests in neighbouring Gabon records the SUPERPOSITION of MINING AND LOGGING PERMITS over the space traditionally used by communities applying for a community forest, and calls for territorial planning that ranks land allocation and sets the conditions for coexistence. In a bauxite country, check the mining cadastre over your area BEFORE you invest in a forest application — an overlapping permit is the thing that defeats these files. WHO IT SUITS: Guinean villages and rural communes seeking forest recognition, reforestation support or a nursery. CAVEATS: THE CODE IS THE FRAME, NOT A GRANT — confirm which implementing texts are in force and what the cantonnement requires; state forestry involvement does not by itself secure tenure. For evidence and the financier route, Guinea's CECIDE entry; for community protocols and mining royalties, Action Mines; for legal aid, the no-state-scheme entry.

trackers.name: Guinée Écologie, Conakry — founded 1989 with a published arrêté number and street address, runs local conservation committees at Mont Béro, and owns its own drone and procedures manual
trackers.desc: THE CONSERVATION ORGANISATION GUINEA WAS MISSING FROM THIS FILE: GUINÉE ÉCOLOGIE, headquartered at 210 RUE DI 501, COMMUNE DE DIXINN, BP 3266, CONAKRY (guineeecologie.net), A NON-PROFIT NGO FOUNDED IN 1989 AND OFFICIALLY APPROVED UNDER ARRÊTÉ 7955/MID/CAB/89, whose mission is to act WITH ALL SOCIAL ACTORS in close collaboration with all concerned organisational structures AT EVERY LEVEL, for a Guinea where populations at the base participate effectively and efficiently, supported by governance favourable to sustainable use of natural resources. Founded in 1989 with its approval arrêté printed on its own site: this is the oldest and most verifiable environmental organisation in Guinea in this file, and the file previously had none. WHAT IT DOES ON THE GROUND, WITH THE NUMBERS: since APRIL 2023, with the FOREST CENTRE OF N'ZÉRÉKORÉ and an international partner, it has run a project to restore degraded areas of the FORÊT CLASSÉE DU MONT BÉRO — about 26,850 HECTARES, part of the Guinean montane forests extending into Sierra Leone, Liberia and Côte d'Ivoire — under pressure from DEFORESTATION, ILLEGAL LOGGING AND ENCROACHMENT, targeting 9,597 members of surrounding communities, with villagers at OULÉOUON raising seedlings in nurseries for planting in delimited zones. AND THE VEHICLE IT BUILDS IS THE ONE TO ASK FOR BY NAME: a COMITÉ LOCAL DE CONSERVATION, whose members learn to raise nursery plants AND TO FARM BETTER WITHOUT ENCROACHING ON THE FOREST. A local conservation committee that trains people to farm the edge without cutting into it is the arrangement that survives after the project ends — ask for the committee AND the nursery, because the nursery is what makes the committee useful. WHO IT WORKS WITH AND WHAT IT OWNS: it collaborates with the DIRECTION NATIONALE DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT, the DIRECTION NATIONALE DES EAUX ET FORÊTS and the OFFICE GUINÉEN DES PARCS ET RÉSERVES, with a long list of development partners; it is a FOUNDING MEMBER OF THE FORUM DES ONGs POUR LE DÉVELOPPEMENT DURABLE, a platform of national and international NGOs in Guinea; and it publishes its own capability inventory — an electronic publishing unit, a physical and digital library, a 4x4 vehicle, two trail motorcycles, A DRONE FOR AERIAL VIDEO AND PHOTOGRAPHY, field scientific equipment, a portable generator, and its OWN MANUAL OF ADMINISTRATIVE AND FINANCIAL PROCEDURES. A drone and a 4x4 mean an organisation that can document your site from the air and get there in the rains. Ask what it has photographed near you — aerial imagery from a dated flight is evidence. It has also trained civil society on PRIOR IMPACT STUDIES and environmental management tools for coastal infrastructure — ports, airports, transport, mines and industry. WHO IT SUITS: Guinean forest-edge and coastal communities, and anyone facing a large infrastructure or mining project. CAVEATS: A CONSERVATION AND TRAINING NGO, not a funder or a law firm. For thirteen villages against a lender, Guinea's CECIDE entry; for writing your own protocol, Action Mines Guinée; for the mining cadastre overlap trap, the code forestier entry; and note there is NO free state legal aid in Guinea.

trackers.name: CADES/Guinée and the Coordination des ONG Féminines — a 2007 national development NGO working four regions and women's crop chains, with the mining-company partnership named as a caution, plus a women's NGO coordination with a Kaloum address
trackers.desc: THE NGO PAID BY THE MINE, FILED WITH THE WARNING ATTACHED: CADES/GUINÉE — CENTRE D'APPUI POUR LE DÉVELOPPEMENT ÉCONOMIQUE ET SOCIAL — IS A NATIONAL DEVELOPMENT NGO, APOLITICAL AND NON-PROFIT, CREATED IN 2007 (cades-guinee.org), WITH A NAMED CONTACT, TWO TELEPHONE NUMBERS AND AN EMAIL PUBLISHED. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY DELIVERED, WITH THE PLACES NAMED: CAPACITY BUILDING OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS IN THE REGIONS OF KINDIA, MAMOU, LABÉ AND KANKAN, FINANCED BY THE EUROPEAN UNION AND IMPLEMENTED WITH THREE NAMED PARTNER ORGANISATIONS; PROMOTION OF WOMEN'S ENTREPRENEURSHIP IN AGRICULTURAL CHAINS — PINEAPPLE, MANGO AND GATHERED FRUITS — AT KINDIA, FORÉCARIAH AND CONAKRY; SUPPORT TO THE TRANSFORMATION AND MARKETING OF LOCAL AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS BY WOMEN ENTREPRENEURS; AND PROMOTION OF FINANCIAL INCLUSION AND ENTREPRENEURIAL TRAINING FOR YOUNG PEOPLE AT CONAKRY AND KINDIA. Four regions named, and the crops named. Gathered fruits sitting alongside pineapple and mango in a funded value chain is the detail worth acting on: an income from what the bush already produces is the argument against clearing it, and there is a Guinean organisation that has already built the market for three such products. AND THE ONE TO READ TWICE BEFORE YOU RELY ON IT: CADES HAS RUN AN EDUCATIONAL PROJECT TO STRENGTHEN SCHOOL INFRASTRUCTURE AND TEACHING QUALITY IN MINING ZONES, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH A NAMED MINING COMPANY. An NGO building schools in the mining zone with the mining company's money is both a real resource and a real conflict of interest, and this file will not pretend otherwise. If the organisation offering to help your community is also paid by the operator you are opposing, that is not automatically disqualifying — but you need to know it before the first meeting, not after. Ask every organisation that approaches you: who funds you, and does any of your funding come from this project or its parent? THE OTHER BODY, WITH FULL CONTACTS: THE COORDINATION DES ONG FÉMININES DE GUINÉE (COFEG), IMMEUBLE KÉBÉ, 1ER ÉTAGE, KALOUM, CONAKRY, BP 2176, WITH TWO TELEPHONE NUMBERS AND TWO EMAIL ADDRESSES PUBLISHED. A coordination of women's NGOs with a street address in the administrative heart of Conakry is one call that reaches many organisations. In a country where this file has recorded that free state legal aid does not exist, the bodies that aggregate other bodies are worth more than usual. THE FIGURES THAT SET THE BARGAINING POSITION, AND THEY BELONG IN ANY GUINEAN OBJECTION: IN 2018 THE MINING SECTOR BROUGHT THE GUINEAN PUBLIC TREASURY 544 MILLION US DOLLARS, MORE THAN 30% OF ITS RECEIPTS — AND DESPITE THAT, GUINEA WAS RANKED 178TH OUT OF 189 COUNTRIES ON THE HUMAN DEVELOPMENT INDEX. GUINEA IS THE LARGEST EXPORTER OF BAUXITE TO CHINA, WHICH IS THE WORLD'S LEADING PRODUCER OF ALUMINIUM; AND GUINEA'S OIL POTENTIAL IS PUT AT 22 EXPLORATION BLOCKS IN THE WESTERN REGION OF THE COUNTRY. Thirty per cent of state revenue from mining, and 178th of 189 on human development. Put those two numbers in the same sentence and you have the argument that extraction has not paid for development where it happened. And twenty-two exploration blocks in the west is the notice of what is coming after the bauxite. HOW GUINEAN CIVIL SOCIETY HAS USED THE INTERNATIONAL ROUTE: the record describes QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE ANALYSIS OF THE STATE REPORTS PRESENTED BY GUINEA AND OF THE ALTERNATIVE REPORTS PRESENTED BY GUINEAN CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS TO THE UN COMMITTEES, PRINCIPALLY AT THE UNIVERSAL PERIODIC REVIEW. An ALTERNATIVE report submitted alongside the state's own is a document your organisation can contribute to. The government files its account of your situation on a fixed cycle; the shadow report is where the other account goes. ALSO NAMED, with postal addresses and telephones, in a published civil society directory for Guinea: several national associations including one for the promotion of employment and one for family wellbeing. WHO IT SUITS: Guinean women's producer groups, communities in Kindia, Mamou, Labé, Kankan or Forécariah, and anyone vetting who is offering help. CAVEATS: SEE THE FUNDING WARNING ABOVE — it is the point of this entry, not a footnote. For thirteen villages taken against the IFC, Guinea's CECIDE entry; for community protocols and the local development fund, Action Mines Guinée; for the 26,850-hectare arrêté, Guinée Écologie; for the fact that no free state legal aid exists, the aide juridictionnelle entry.

trackers.name: The West African coastal conservation partnership that trains NGO leaders, journalists, construction executives AND infrastructure financiers together on impact studies — plus Carbone Guinée covering all four regions and the 40 resource people in the countryside
trackers.desc: THE BUILDERS AND THE FINANCIERS WERE INVITED TOO — and that is the detail that makes this worth filing: A REGIONAL PARTNERSHIP FOR MARINE AND COASTAL CONSERVATION IN WEST AFRICA, TOGETHER WITH A NATURE FOUNDATION, FUNDED A PROJECT OF WORKSHOPS TO SENSITISE AND INFORM CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS ON THE IMPACTS OF INFRASTRUCTURE AND ON THE TOOLS OF ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT — AND THE STATED AUDIENCE WAS LEADERS OF NATIONAL NGOs, JOURNALISTS, EXECUTIVES OF THE CONSTRUCTION COMPANIES, AND THE PRINCIPAL FINANCIERS OF THE INFRASTRUCTURE. Four groups in one room: the objectors, the reporters, the builders and the people paying for it. Almost everything in this file is organised the other way — communities trained separately, companies briefed separately, and the two sides meeting only in a dispute. Putting the financier in the same training as the NGO leader is cheap, and it means the person who can cancel a project has heard the objection before it becomes a fight. If you are designing a workshop, that is the invitation list to copy. THE STATED PURPOSE: TO TAKE INTO ACCOUNT THE ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL AND LEGAL ASPECTS, NOTABLY AS REGARDS THE PRIOR IMPACT STUDIES, AND TO INFORM AND TRAIN NON-STATE ACTORS ON THESE MANAGEMENT TOOLS. PRIOR impact studies — the ones done before the work starts, which is the only moment they change anything. Non-state actors being trained on the tools means the tools are not reserved to consultants: an association can learn to read an impact study, and there is a regional programme that teaches it. WHAT THE PARTICIPANTS ACTUALLY DID: OVER TWO DAYS, PARTICIPANTS FROM CIVIL SOCIETY AND THE MEDIA ELABORATED STRATEGIES TO INVOLVE THEMSELVES IN HOW THE SOCIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT STUDIES OF COASTAL INFRASTRUCTURE ARE TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT. Two days, and the output is strategies rather than awareness. A training that ends with a plan for who does what is worth ten that end with a certificate. THE THREATS THE PROGRAMME NAMES, WHICH ARE THE ONES TO WATCH ON ANY AFRICAN COAST: THE COASTLINE IS TODAY ATTACKED BY SEVERAL FACTORS, INCLUDING THE ABUSIVE CUTTING OF THE MANGROVE AND ABOVE ALL BY ENERGY, HOTEL AND PRIVATE INFRASTRUCTURE. Hotels named alongside power plants. Tourism infrastructure takes coastline as surely as a refinery does, and it arrives with more local goodwill — which makes it harder to question. The mangrove goes first in both cases. AND THE STANDING BODY BEHIND IT: A NAMED TECHNICAL ADVISER SERVES AS FACILITATOR OF A CADRE DE CONCERTATION — a standing consultation framework. A facilitator whose job is convening the framework, named and contactable. Ask who facilitates the cadre de concertation in your sector; there usually is one, and the post is the door in. THE STAFFING MODEL WORTH NOTING: THE HOST ORGANISATION RUNS 6 PERMANENT STAFF AT HEAD OFFICE AND 40 ASSOCIATE RESOURCE PERSONS IN THE COUNTRYSIDE. Six paid people and forty associates in the rural areas. That ratio is how a small national organisation covers a whole country — the reach is in the associates, not the office. If an organisation tells you it works nationally, ask how many of its people live outside the capital. THE SECOND ORGANISATION, WITH ITS COVERAGE STATED PLAINLY: CARBONE GUINÉE IS AN ASSOCIATION OF YOUNG PEOPLE OF DIVERSE TRAINING, WHOSE INTERVENTION ZONE IS BASSE GUINÉE, MOYENNE GUINÉE, HAUTE GUINÉE AND GUINÉE FORESTIÈRE — AND ANY LOCALITY REQUESTING OUR INTERVENTION — WORKING ON THE REINFORCEMENT OF THE CAPACITIES OF COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS AND OF DECENTRALISED TERRITORIAL COLLECTIVITIES, ON FOOD SECURITY AND ACCESS TO WATER, HYGIENE AND SANITATION, AND ON THE PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT, WITH AN ADDRESS IN A NAMED COMMUNE OF CONAKRY. ANY LOCALITY REQUESTING OUR INTERVENTION, printed as part of its own coverage statement. That is an open invitation, and all four of Guinea's natural regions are named — so wherever you are in the country, writing to ask is within their published remit. And note the second beneficiary: DECENTRALISED TERRITORIAL COLLECTIVITIES, meaning your own commune or rural council can be the one trained, which is often the body that actually signs away land. ITS STATED AMBITION ALSO NAMES THE METHOD: TO MOBILISE LOCAL AND INTERNATIONAL RESOURCES WITH A VIEW TO ENSURING SUSTAINABLE SELF-DEVELOPMENT, AND TO UNITE ITS FORCES WITH ANY OTHER ASSOCIATION SHARING ITS VISION AND MISSIONS. WHO IT SUITS: Guinean coastal and rural communities, communes facing an infrastructure or hotel project, and journalists covering impact studies. CAVEATS: THESE ARE TRAINING AND CAPACITY BODIES, not litigators or funders of land purchase. For the organisation founded 1989 with a published arrêté number and its Dixinn address, Guinea's Guinée Écologie entry, which also carries the Forum des ONGs pour le Développement Durable.

trackers.name: Free trackers that name the investors behind a project with one click, the organisations that will help you reach them, and the 2024 rule change letting a single person file a complaint against the African Development Bank
trackers.desc: ONE PERSON CAN FILE IT NOW — declared overlap first: THIS FILE ALREADY CARRIES NIGERIA'S ENTRY ON THE AFRICAN DEVELOPMENT BANK'S COMPLAINT MECHANISM, WHICH RECORDS A TWO-PERSON THRESHOLD. THAT THRESHOLD HAS SINCE BEEN LOWERED, AND THE OTHER CHANGES BELOW ARE NOT IN THAT ENTRY. THE CHANGE: THE NEW POLICY STRENGTHENS ACCESSIBILITY FOR COMPLAINANTS BY ALLOWING COMPLAINTS TO BE FILED BY A SINGLE PERSON — AND ENABLES THE MECHANISM TO ADVISE COMMUNITIES ON HOW TO SUBMIT COMPLAINTS IF NEEDED. One person, and the mechanism itself will tell you how to write it. Those two together remove the commonest reasons a complaint never gets filed: nobody else would sign, and nobody knew the format. If you were told you needed a group, that is out of date. THE PROTECTION THAT COMES WITH IT: IT ADOPTS A ZERO-TOLERANCE STANDARD FOR RETALIATION AGAINST COMPLAINANTS, AND REJECTS ANY FORM OF THREAT, INTIMIDATION, HARASSMENT, VIOLENCE, OR DISCRIMINATION TOWARDS THOSE THAT RAISE CONCERNS THROUGH THE MECHANISM. A written retaliation standard gives you something to invoke if pressure follows the filing — report the retaliation to the mechanism as a second complaint, because under this policy that is itself a breach. THE DUTY THAT SHOULD HAVE TOLD YOU ALL THIS ALREADY: IT REQUIRES BANK MANAGEMENT TO MAKE THE MECHANISM BETTER KNOWN AMONG AFFECTED COMMUNITIES BY DISCLOSING INFORMATION ABOUT IT AT A PROJECT LEVEL. If a bank-financed project near you has never told anyone this route exists, that failure is itself now a documented obligation being missed. Ask the project office in writing where the mechanism is disclosed. AND THE POWER THAT DOES NOT NEED YOU AT ALL: IT PROVIDES THE MECHANISM WITH THE ABILITY TO INITIATE COMPLIANCE REVIEW PROCESSES IN CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES WITHOUT A FORMAL COMPLAINT FROM AFFECTED COMMUNITIES. Where filing is too dangerous, the mechanism can start a review on its own. So information reaching it informally still has somewhere to go. THE SCOPE: THE MANDATE COVERS BOTH PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTOR OPERATIONS OF THE BANK GROUP — OPERATIONAL SINCE 2006, WITH OVER 100 COMPLAINTS RECEIVED FROM CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS AND AFFECTED COMMUNITIES. PRIVATE SECTOR OPERATIONS TOO. A company project is in scope if the bank financed it, which is how a community reaches a firm that would otherwise ignore it. NOW THE HARDER HALF, AND IT IS THE FIRST QUESTION: WHO IS ACTUALLY BEHIND THE PROJECT? TWO FREE TOOLS — A SHAREHOLDER TRACKER AND A DEVELOPMENT BANK INVESTMENT TRACKER — ALLOW USERS TO MAP THE INVESTMENT CHAINS BEHIND HARMFUL PROJECTS MORE QUICKLY AND COMPLETELY THAN EVER BEFORE, IDENTIFYING KEY INVESTORS AND FINANCIERS WITH THE CLICK OF A BUTTON. The company clearing your land is often a subsidiary of a subsidiary, and every complaint route in this file depends on knowing which bank, fund or parent stands behind it. These two tools do that lookup for you, free. Run the search before you decide what kind of campaign you are in — a project financed by a development bank has a complaint mechanism attached; one financed privately does not, and needs a different approach. THE ORGANISATION THAT WILL WORK WITH YOU IN AFRICA: IT BUILDS THE CAPACITY OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES THROUGHOUT AFRICA ON MULTILATERAL DEVELOPMENT BANKS — PROVIDING INFORMATION, STRATEGIC ADVICE, AND CONNECTIONS TO DECISION-MAKERS SO THAT THOSE IMPACTED BY THEIR INVESTMENTS CAN VOICE THEIR CONCERNS — AND IT IS A FOUNDING MEMBER OF A CIVIL SOCIETY WORKING GROUP ON THE AFRICAN DEVELOPMENT BANK, A NETWORK OF AFRICAN ORGANIZATIONS AND INTERNATIONAL ALLIES PUSHING THE BANK TO BE MORE SUSTAINABLE, INCLUSIVE, TRANSPARENT, AND ACCOUNTABLE TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES. CONNECTIONS TO DECISION-MAKERS is the offer. A bank director takes a meeting arranged by an organisation they already know; the same request from a village goes unanswered. Ask to be introduced, not just advised. AND THE NUMBERS THAT SHOULD SET YOUR EXPECTATIONS HONESTLY, PUBLISHED BY THE ACCOUNTABILITY GROUPS THEMSELVES: A 231% RISE IN COMPLAINTS BETWEEN 2009 AND 2019 — AND JUST 16.4% OF 1,614 COMPLAINTS FILED SINCE 1994 HAVE REACHED A FORMAL CONCLUSION. Roughly one in six complaints ever concludes formally. That is not a reason to skip filing — a live complaint changes how a project behaves while it is open, and it creates a record — but do not build the campaign on the complaint alone, and do not let anyone tell your community that filing is the plan. AND THE GAP TO KNOW BEFORE YOU HOPE FOR MONEY: MAJOR DEVELOPMENT BANKS HAVE LONG RESISTED COMPENSATING COMMUNITIES IMPACTED BY THE PROJECTS THEY FINANCE, EVEN AS THEY ACKNOWLEDGE DEVELOPERS OFTEN FALL SHORT — POINTING INSTEAD TO AN INDEPENDENT COMPLAINTS PROCESS THAT FACILITATES TALKS BETWEEN PROJECT DEVELOPERS AND COMMUNITIES. The bank offers mediation, not compensation — so the money, if any, comes from the developer at the table. Go into that room with your own damage valuation, which this file's Ghana entry records as a fundable study, and with the investment chain in hand so you know who else is listening. WHO IT SUITS: African communities harmed by any project with development-bank or foreign investor finance behind it. CAVEATS: THE COMPLIANCE ROUTE ASKS WHETHER THE BANK FOLLOWED ITS OWN RULES, NOT WHETHER THE PROJECT IS GOOD — and most complaints do not conclude formally. For the mechanism's basic terms, Nigeria's Independent Review Mechanism entry; for the thirteen villages that took on a bauxite project, Guinea's CECIDE entry; for the damage valuation study shared with community, courts and company, Ghana's Strategic Response Mechanism entry.

trackers.name: Stand For Her Land (S4HL) — a women's land rights campaign that publishes an email address for starting or joining a national coalition — country coalitions built from local grassroots organisations, with African coalitions already running and a named women lawyers association chairing one
trackers.desc: EMAIL THEM AND START THE NATIONAL COALITION YOURSELF — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S GABON ENTRY NAMES THIS CAMPAIGN AS A PLATFORM THE HOUSING ORGANISATION WORKS THROUGH, WITHOUT DESCRIBING IT OR SHIPPING ITS HOST; ITS REPUBLIC OF CONGO BUCKET CARRIES THE SECRETARIAT ORGANISATION'S HOST; ITS LIBERIA AND ZIMBABWE BUCKETS A LAND COALITION HOST AND ITS CAMEROON AND SENEGAL BUCKETS THE NAME. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS RUN ON THE HOST ACTUALLY BEING SHIPPED. THE PUBLISHED DOOR, WHICH IS THE FIND: LEARN MORE ABOUT STARTING OR JOINING A NATIONAL COALITION BY EMAILING THE CAMPAIGN — WITH A CONTACT ADDRESS PUBLISHED, AND THE QUESTION PUT DIRECTLY: IS YOUR ORGANIZATION READY TO BE A PART OF THE INITIATIVE? STARTING, not only joining. Where no national coalition exists in your country, a local organisation can write and propose founding one — which is a different offer from every network in this file that admits members to a structure somebody else already built. The founding organisation shapes what the coalition prioritises. WHAT THE COALITIONS ARE MADE OF: COUNTRY COALITIONS COMPRISE LOCAL GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS, NATIONAL CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS, AND OTHER NON-STATE ACTORS — FACILITATED BY A GLOBAL STEERING COMMITTEE AND LED BY GRASSROOTS AND NATIONAL PARTNERS. LED BY GRASSROOTS AND NATIONAL PARTNERS, with the global body facilitating rather than directing. Test that in the first conversation: ask who sets the coalition's priorities and who holds the money. THE PROBLEM IT NAMES, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE IMPLEMENTATION GAP — THE GULF BETWEEN THE STRONG STANDARDS IN PLACE TO PROTECT WOMEN'S RIGHTS TO LAND AND THE REALIZATION OF THOSE RIGHTS IN PRACTICE; IN MANY COUNTRIES COMMITMENTS LACK INCORPORATION INTO LEGAL AND POLICY FRAMEWORKS, AND EVEN WHERE LAWS ARE EQUITABLE, DEEPLY ENTRENCHED PATRIARCHAL SOCIAL NORMS OFTEN RESULT IN WEAK IMPLEMENTATION. The law being good and the law being followed are different problems. This file has recorded communities told their rights already exist in statute; the campaign exists precisely for the distance between the two. THE ADMISSION FROM A TRADITIONAL AUTHORITY, RECORDED AT A LAUNCH: A NAMED HIGH ROYAL HIGHNESS CONFIRMED THAT CERTIFICATES OF CUSTOMARY OWNERSHIP DO NOT FULLY PROTECT WOMEN. A customary ruler saying in public that customary certificates leave women unprotected. That is the strongest possible evidence for a community weighing whether a certificate of customary ownership secures everyone in it or only the men — and it comes from inside the institution, not from a critic of it. THE AFRICAN COUNTRY COALITIONS ON RECORD: ETHIOPIA, SENEGAL, TANZANIA AND UGANDA, ALONGSIDE COALITIONS OUTSIDE AFRICA — WITH A ZIMBABWE PROGRAMME DISMANTLING GENDER DISCRIMINATION IN RURAL LAND AND RESOURCE ACCESS, OWNERSHIP AND CONTROL. HOW ONE NATIONAL TASK FORCE IS STRUCTURED: 25 CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS AS MEMBERS OF A TASK FORCE CHAIRED BY A NATIONAL WOMEN LAWYERS ASSOCIATION. A women lawyers association chairing the national coalition. That is a working answer to the standing question of where a community finds an attorney — a national association of women lawyers already convened around land, and reachable through the coalition rather than cold. WHAT THAT NATIONAL COALITION SAID IT WOULD DO: WE HAVE PROGRESSIVE LAWS ON LAND, BUT THEY DO NOT REACH THE LOCAL COMMUNITIES — WE WANT TO MAKE THE GOVERNMENTS ACCOUNTABLE AND ALSO AMPLIFY LOCAL BY-LAWS TO ENGAGE THE COMMUNITIES. AMPLIFY LOCAL BY-LAWS. A village or district by-law is the instrument a community can actually get passed, and it binds locally — far more achievable than national reform and recorded here as a deliberate strategy rather than a consolation. THE FIGURE IT CARRIES: WOMEN WITH STRONG LAND RIGHTS AND INHERITANCE EARN UP TO 3.8 TIMES MORE INCOME — AND LARGE-SCALE CLIMATE MITIGATION INTERVENTIONS ARE MORE EFFECTIVE WHEN WOMEN'S LAND RIGHTS ARE FULLY RECOGNIZED. 3.8 times more income, sourced. That is the number for a ministry that treats women's tenure as a social question rather than an economic one. THE SPECIFIC LEGISLATIVE HANDLE ONE COALITION IDENTIFIED: THE CAMPAIGN AS AN OPPORTUNITY TO PUSH FOR THE GAZETTEMENT OF A SUCCESSION AMENDMENT ACT ALREADY PASSED INTO LAW — PUTTING WOMEN'S LAND RIGHTS INTO THE PROCESS OF POLICY REVIEW AND IMPLEMENTATION. An act passed but never gazetted, and therefore not in force. Worth checking in your own country: the reform may already exist on paper and be stuck one administrative step from operating — which is a far smaller campaign than passing a new law. WHAT THE CORE PARTNERS SUPPLY: RESOURCES, TOOLS AND SUPPORT TO NATIONAL AND LOCAL ADVOCACY IN FOCAL COUNTRIES, WHERE COALITIONS OF LOCAL AND NATIONAL-LEVEL ACTORS DRIVE CHANGE ON THE GROUND — WITH A NAMED LAND RIGHTS ORGANISATION SERVING AS SECRETARIAT, PROVIDING COORDINATION AND ADMINISTRATION. THE THREATS AND WHAT IT IS DOING ABOUT THEM: RISING NATIONALISM HAS CUT PUBLIC FUNDING AND SHRUNK THE SPACE FOR CIVIL SOCIETY IN SOME OF THE VERY COUNTRIES WHERE THE CAMPAIGN OPERATES — AND IT IS MEETING THAT BY HELPING ITS COALITIONS BUILD FUNDRAISING CAPACITY, DEVELOP LOCAL LEADERSHIP AND STRENGTHEN THEIR ABILITY TO CONTINUE. FUNDRAISING CAPACITY offered to member coalitions, published as a response to donor withdrawal. Ask for it by name — this file has recorded very few networks offering it. AND WHAT IT SAYS IT LOOKS FOR IN A COUNTRY: GRASSROOTS WOMEN'S LEADERSHIP, VOICE AND AGENCY; COALITION AND MOVEMENT BUILDING; AND THE EFFORT TO BUILD ON EXISTING AND PAST EFFORTS. BUILD ON EXISTING AND PAST EFFORTS is the selection signal: a proposal that starts from what local women's groups have already been doing reads better here than one proposing something new. WHO IT SUITS: African women's groups, land committees and national organisations wanting to found or join a national coalition on women's land rights — and communities looking for lawyers already organised around land. CAVEATS: A CAMPAIGN AND COALITION MODEL, NOT A FUNDER OR A LAW FIRM; ITS AFRICAN COALITIONS ARE IN A LIMITED SET OF COUNTRIES, AND STARTING A NEW ONE IS A NEGOTIATION RATHER THAN AN ENTITLEMENT. For the household-scale route to an occupancy licence, Gabon's entry; for the open campaign requiring no registration at all, Ethiopia's entry.

trackers.name: Awqaf SA (National Awqaf Foundation of South Africa) and AWQAF Africa — the waqf endowment, whose founding deed forbids the land ever being sold or inherited; known as habous across North and West Africa, with state Ministries of Awqaf administering existing holdings
trackers.desc: A DEED THAT FORBIDS THE LAND EVER BEING SOLD — method and adjacency declared first: EIGHTH ACQUISITION-ONLY ROUND. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL HOSTS AND FIVE FACTS ABSENT — WAQF, AWQAF, HABOUS, ISLAMIC FINANCE AND ZAKAT ARE ABSENT FROM EVERY BUCKET IN THIS FILE. ONE GENERIC WORD, ENDOWMENT, APPEARS IN FOUR ENTRIES ON OTHER HOSTS IN UNRELATED SENSES. THIS FILE'S ANGOLA ENTRY COVERS CHURCH LANDHOLDING AND ITS AUDITS, A DIFFERENT RELIGIOUS LANDOWNER AND MECHANISM; ITS SOMALIA ENTRY THE ANTI-SPECULATION CO-OPERATIVE. NONE IS RESTATED. WHAT THE FOUNDING ACT DOES TO THE LAND, WHICH IS THE FIND: LAND TRANSFORMED INTO WAQF, FORBIDDING ITS SALE OR INHERITANCE — ON THE ORIGINAL INSTRUCTION THAT IF YOU WISH, IMMOBILIZE THE CORPUS AND OFFER ITS INCOME IN ALMS. Eight acquisition rounds in, this is the only instrument found that removes land from the market permanently by the terms of its own deed. The co-operative filed under Somalia achieves something similar with a resale clause still being drafted; this has done it for fourteen centuries, is recognised in the law of most Muslim-majority African states, and is absent from all 1,030 Africa entries in this file until now. WHY THAT MATTERS HERE, AND IT IS THE SECOND FIND: DESCRIBED AS AN INALIENABLE CHARITABLE ENDOWMENT — BY ENSURING DECENTRALIZED MANAGEMENT OF ESSENTIAL SERVICES SUCH AS EDUCATION, HEALTH AND SOCIAL ASSISTANCE, IT ENABLED COMMUNITIES TO TAKE COLLECTIVE RESPONSIBILITY FOR THEMSELVES, REINFORCING SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC AUTONOMY. INALIENABLE is the operative word for a community whose danger is not eviction but a future sale — by a chief, a committee, or its own grandchildren. THE NAMED BODIES THAT ESTABLISH THEM: A NATIONAL FOUNDATION IN ONE AFRICAN COUNTRY DESCRIBED AS LEADING THE MOVEMENT AND AS AN INDEPENDENT NON-PROFIT FOUNDED FOR THE SOCIAL, ECONOMIC, POLITICAL, EDUCATIONAL, INTELLECTUAL, MORAL, RELIGIOUS AND SPIRITUAL EMPOWERMENT OF MUSLIM AND HISTORICALLY DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES; A CONTINENTAL BODY RECORDED AS A WAQF SERVING ALL COUNTRIES OF AFRICA; AND AN INTERNATIONAL FUND WITH A PUBLISHED STREET ADDRESS. HISTORICALLY DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES, not only Muslim ones, in the national foundation's own object clause. And a continental body constituted to serve every African country is the one to write to from outside its home state. THE NAMES IT GOES BY, WHICH YOU NEED TO SEARCH THE REGISTER: WAQF, PLURAL AWQĀF, OR ḤABS, ḤUBS, ḤUBŪS, ḤABĪS, PLURAL AḤBĀS IN NORTH AFRICA — KNOWN IN SOME ARABIC COUNTRIES AS HIBSS OR HUBOUSS; THE TERM REFERRING TO THE ACT OF FOUNDING, THE ENDOWMENT ITSELF, AND THE ENDOWMENT INSTITUTION. Practical, not academic: a land register or ministry file will be indexed under one of these spellings, and habous is the one used across North and West Africa. A community searching for what is already endowed near it needs the local word. WHAT THE STATE HOLDS: A MINISTRY OF AWQAF EXISTS IN AT LEAST ONE AFRICAN COUNTRY, ALONGSIDE NAMED BOARDS AND COUNCILS ELSEWHERE — MEANING THERE IS A PUBLIC BODY ADMINISTERING THESE HOLDINGS THAT CAN BE ASKED WHAT IT ADMINISTERS. The same move as the diocesan land audit filed under Angola, in a different tradition: a ministry that holds endowment land can be asked what it holds and who benefits. That is a records request, not a campaign. THE RANGE OF PURPOSES ALREADY ESTABLISHED HISTORICALLY: A WAQF WAS ESTABLISHED FOR VIRTUALLY EVERY ENDEAVOR THAT COULD BE CONSTRUED AS BEING OF SOCIAL BENEFIT — INCLUDING SCHOOLS, MEDICAL FACILITIES, ORPHANAGES, HOUSES FOR THE POOR, FOOD FOR THE POOR, THE BLIND, BATTERED AND ABUSED WOMEN, SOUP KITCHENS, WELLS, WATER PIPES AND FOUNTAINS. WELLS AND WATER PIPES. A community endowment for a water source is squarely within the tradition, which matters where this file has recorded water taken without any land changing hands. WHO ELSE THEY SERVED: WAQF ENDOWMENTS WERE NOT ONLY FOR MUSLIMS — MANY SERVED NON-MUSLIM COMMUNITIES; ONE FOUNDING EXAMPLE BEING SEVEN ORCHARDS BEQUEATHED BY A JEWISH RESIDENT OF MEDINA. Worth knowing before assuming this route is closed to a mixed community. THE MODERN REVIVAL AND WHAT IT REQUIRES: A RECENT INTERNATIONAL TREND FOR REVIVAL AND PROMOTION, WITH CHARITABLE INSTITUTIONS EMPHASIZING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF SOCIAL JUSTICE AND INCLUDING PHILANTHROPIC REFORM IN THEIR DEMOCRATIC AGENDA, LEADING TO IMPROVED GOVERNANCE WITH MODERN ACCOUNTING AND INCORPORATION OF TRUST LAWS. INCORPORATION OF TRUST LAWS is the bridge: the old form registered under modern trust legislation, which is what makes it usable in a secular land registry. HOW IDLE ENDOWMENT LAND GETS DEVELOPED: PUBLISHED CASE STUDIES OF REDEVELOPING IDLE WAQF PROPERTIES INTO PRODUCTIVE LAND TRUSTS, WITH NEW USES INCLUDING SERVICES TO THE COMMUNITY, JOBS, FUNDING SMALL ENTREPRENEURS, HEALTH CARE AND SHELTERING THE POOR AND NEEDY — WITH ONE AFRICAN COUNTRY AMONG THE CASES AND A DEVELOPMENT BANK'S ROLE IN FINANCING THEM EXAMINED. IDLE WAQF PROPERTIES is the opening. Endowment land sitting unused, already inalienable and already dedicated to the poor, is the cheapest land a community will ever find — and there is published guidance on financing its development. HOW MONEY IS RAISED WITHOUT SELLING THE LAND: THE MANAGER CAN COOPERATE IN FINANCING THE MANAGEMENT OF WAQF LAND OR RAISE FUNDS FROM THE COMMUNITY THROUGH CASH WAQF AND SHARE WAQF — WITH MANAGERS THAT ALSO RUN ALMS INSTITUTIONS INTEGRATING THOSE FUNDS TO BROADEN THE FUNDING BASE. CASH WAQF is small contributions pooled into a permanent fund. It is the same shape as the daily savings federation filed under Togo, with the difference that the corpus can never be spent or sold — only its income. THE WOMEN'S ROLE, HISTORICAL AND ARGUED FOR AGAIN: THE POTENTIAL FOR GENDER EQUALITY THROUGH THE ROLE OF WOMEN AS FOUNDERS AND MANAGERS — ONE OF THE OLDEST UNIVERSITIES FOUNDED BY FATIMA AL-FIHRI IN 859 AND SUSTAINED BY PERPETUAL ENDOWMENTS TO OFFER FREE TEACHING; WITH THE OBSERVATION THAT IN MOST POST-COLONIAL MUSLIM SOCIETIES VERY LITTLE HAS BEEN ACCOMPLISHED IN PROMOTING THE ROLE OF WOMEN IN RE-IMAGINING WAQF. Women as founders and managers is a documented precedent, not a modern imposition, which is a useful thing to be able to say inside the tradition. AND THE HONEST ASSESSMENT OF ITS CONDITION TODAY: IN THE MODERN MUSLIM WORLD THIS INSTRUMENT SEEMS TO HAVE LOST ITS VITALITY, VISIBILITY AND EFFECTIVENESS AFTER THE ILL EFFECTS OF MODERNITY AND COLONIALISM — IT IS NOT A PANACEA, BUT HAS THE POTENTIAL TO REKINDLE SOLIDARITY, SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT, PRESERVATION OF BIODIVERSITY, THE COMMON GOOD AND WOMEN'S ECONOMIC AGENCY. Filed with that assessment attached: many national endowment administrations are weak or captured, and PRESERVATION OF BIODIVERSITY appears here as an aspiration rather than a record. Approach the institution knowing it may need reviving locally rather than merely used. WHO IT SUITS: communities in Muslim-majority or mixed societies who want land placed permanently beyond sale, and anyone who has never asked what endowment land already exists near them. CAVEATS: THIS IS A LEGAL FORM PLUS THE BODIES THAT ADMINISTER IT, NOT A FUND THAT WILL BUY LAND FOR YOU; ITS STRENGTH VARIES ENORMOUSLY BY COUNTRY AND MUCH OF THE PUBLISHED CASE MATERIAL IS FROM OUTSIDE AFRICA; AND ITS OWN SCHOLARS DESCRIBE THE INSTITUTION AS DIMINISHED. For church landholding and the audit route, Angola's entry; for the co-operative resale restriction, Somalia's entry.

trackers.name: Tribunal de Contas
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Guinea-Bissau, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Guinea-Bissau — Ministério da Economia e Finanças
trackers.desc: National budget authority; formulates, executes & evaluates financial policy and prepares the State budget, Guinea-Bissau. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Guinea-Bissau.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: ECOWAS Court of Justice — file directly, but sue the State
trackers.desc: A COURT YOU CAN REACH WITHOUT EXHAUSTING DOMESTIC REMEDIES. The ECOWAS Community Court of Justice has held human rights jurisdiction since 2005 and has broad access and standing rules permitting individuals and NGOs to bypass national courts and file directly. THE PRECEDENT: in SERAP v Federal Republic of Nigeria (ECW/CCJ/APP/08/09) the Court dismissed all three preliminary objections — no locus standi, no jurisdiction, statute-barred — and rejected the government's attempt to exclude an Amnesty International report from the evidence. NGO research was admitted as evidence, which matters when no state data exists. It found violations of articles 1 and 24 of the African Charter — article 24: ‘all peoples shall have the right to a general satisfactory environment favourable to their development’ — and of article 21, the right to natural wealth and resources. THE FAULT WAS AN OMISSION: the state ‘defaulted in its duties in terms of vigilance and diligence’, and ‘the omission to act and to prevent damage to the environment characterises the violation’. It ordered restoration within the shortest possible time and measures to prevent further damage, citing the ICJ that the environment ‘is not an abstraction but represents the living space, the quality of life and the very health of human beings, including generations unborn’. THE LIMIT THAT DECIDES WHO YOU SUE: the Court held it had no jurisdiction over the private oil corporations, which were struck from the suit. You sue the State for failing to regulate; you cannot sue the company here — naming one as respondent loses that part of the case. AND PLAN FOR ENFORCEMENT: commentary records the Court did not identify a means for Nigeria to implement the ruling, and the ICJ later wrote to the President pressing for enforcement — judgment is the start of an enforcement campaign, not a self-executing remedy. Proposals to require exhaustion of domestic remedies were rejected by ECOWAS experts and Heads of Government, so the direct-access rule has been tested and held.

trackers.name: ORFAO — comparative land-law tables, and a directive in draft
trackers.desc: COMPARATIVE LEGAL TABLES FOR YOUR COUNTRY AND ITS NEIGHBOURS, IN ONE DOCUMENT. The Observatoire Régional du Foncier Rural en Afrique de l'Ouest (ORFAO), hosted by UEMOA, publishes a regional study on rural land markets containing side-by-side ‘cadre légal comparé’ tables — one covering Bénin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire and Sénégal, another Guinée-Bissau, Mali, Niger and Togo — plus typologies of direct and indirect interventions in land markets and a table of regulatory issues and families of instruments. If you need to know what instrument exists in your country and whether a neighbour has a stronger one, that is the document — comparative tables let a campaign point to a neighbour's provision as an achievable ask rather than a novelty. A WINDOW IS OPENING: on 26 June 2026 in Ouagadougou the UEMOA ministers for urbanisme, habitat, domaines et cadastre approved a draft directive to harmonise rules on immatriculation foncière, accès au titre de propriété and a système d'information foncière, aiming at a common framework of land governance. BE PRECISE ABOUT STATUS: that was a DRAFT directive approved by ministers, not an adopted and transposed instrument — check adoption and transposition before relying on it. But transposition is the moment domestic land law is reopened in each state, and that is when community provisions can be argued for. FOR A GRAZING OR TRANSHUMANCE DISPUTE: a regional pastoral situation bulletin covers 11 West African countries with the support of decentralised technical services — an evidence source drawing on the same services you would otherwise approach one by one. RECORDED PLAINLY: cattle theft is documented as a driver of conflict and instability in the Sahel, so a land dispute here may sit inside a security context that changes what is safe to do. And confirm your state's current ECOWAS standing — several members are recorded as suspended.

trackers.name: IBAP, Bissau — the protected-areas institute has a real address and a switchboard, and its website is carrying injected spam
trackers.desc: THE INSTITUTE IS GENUINE AND ITS WEBSITE IS PARTLY COMPROMISED; BOTH FACTS MATTER BEFORE YOU SEND ANYTHING. The Institute for Biodiversity and Protected Areas was created in 2005 by decree-law and holds administrative, financial and asset autonomy under the minister responsible for the environment, which means it can set conservation policy rather than only implement it. It administers the national protected areas system — around 470,000 hectares, roughly 15 per cent of the territory, of which two-thirds is marine or estuarine — with staff based at the Bissau headquarters and in the protected areas themselves, and an expansion toward 26.3 per cent of national territory is under way. For a coastal or island community this is the body with jurisdiction over the mangrove, the fishing ground and the park boundary. Headquarters: Avenida Dom Settimio Arturo Ferrazzetta, Caixa Postal 70, Bissau; switchboard (245) 320 71 06 and 320 71 07, taken from the institute's own reporting to the biodiversity convention. WARNINGS: the institute's home page currently carries injected spam articles on unrelated medical subjects in German and Portuguese, which means the site has been compromised at some point — the institutional pages and the annual reports still read as authentic, but do not download binaries from it and do not trust anything that asks for credentials. Its supervising ministry is stated differently in different places — the institute's own page says the minister responsible for the environment, while an international conservation union listing puts it under rural development, agriculture, forests and hunting — so confirm the ministry before addressing correspondence. No environmental complaint form, impact-assessment register or objection deadline was located for Guinea-Bissau, and the institute's own annual reporting records that it has operated largely on donor funds rather than budget allocations.

trackers.name: Tiniguena — the Bissau-Guinean NGO the island elders called in, which turned traditional rules into a legally decreed community marine protected area
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Bissau-Guinean NGO founded in 1991 promoting participatory and durable development. THE SEQUENCE IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS ENTRY, because it is the order most communities get wrong: the traditional authorities of three Bijagós islands went to Tiniguena and asked for help; Tiniguena united the groups from the three islands, proposed turning the area into a community marine protected area, and built a management plan drawn from the Bijagó people's own traditional rules of access to and use of land, sea and resources. The plan was then approved at the same time as the government decree creating the area in 2005 — so the custom became the legal management regime rather than being overridden by one. WHAT IT PRODUCED: the Urok community marine protected area, about 54,500 hectares across Formosa, Nago and Chediã, including over 3,000 hectares of mangrove, governed by a management council made up of representatives of every tabanca on the islands, representatives from the wider archipelago, the state biodiversity and protected areas institute, and Tiniguena. The communities set fisheries management plans, reserved marine resources for local subsistence, and patrol their own waters against illegal fishing. In 2019 that council won the UN Development Programme's Equator Prize — the first time a Guinea-Bissau initiative had done so. Tiniguena also works on recognition of community and ancestral heritage areas on the coast, including sacred forests, and on climate-adapted family farming in Urok. WHO IT SUITS: coastal and island communities with living customary rules over their waters and land who want those rules made enforceable. CAVEATS: an NGO and facilitator, not a legal service — no litigation, no intake route, no fee information; the model depends on functioning traditional authority and took years, and Guinea-Bissau's political instability affects everything built through the state. THE ZONING RULE, WHICH IS THE PART ANOTHER COMMUNITY CAN COPY WORD FOR WORD: the area was built on THREE ZONES — a CENTRAL ZONE, essentially mangrove, RESERVED TO RESIDENTS for SUBSISTENCE AND CEREMONIAL fishing; a BUFFER ZONE reserved to residents for COMMERCIAL fishing; and a PERIPHERAL ZONE OPEN TO NON-RESIDENT FISHERS ON CONDITION THEY RESPECT THE RULES IN USE IN THE RESERVE. Naming a zone where outsiders may fish on your terms is what makes the whole scheme defensible — a total exclusion invites the argument that you are privatising a common, while a conditional opening turns every outside fisher into someone bound by your rules. WHAT CO-MANAGEMENT AND PARTICIPATORY SURVEILLANCE PRODUCED: a restoration of biodiversity, particularly MANATEE populations and migratory waterbirds; and the community's SEED GUARDIANS conserve 17 DIFFERENT RICE VARIETIES plus endemic bean and groundnut varieties. The co-management effort has since turned to protecting forests THREATENED BY THE EXPANSION OF CASHEW CULTIVATION, with measures written into the SECOND MANAGEMENT PLAN and the traditional role of the CAMABIS — the Bijagó age class responsible for forest surveillance — revived to carry it. Give the enforcement job to the customary body that already held it; a revived traditional role costs nothing and carries authority a hired guard does not.

trackers.name: Liga Guineense dos Direitos Humanos — the body that went to Varela and wrote down what the heavy-sands mining did there
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Liga Guineense dos Direitos Humanos (LGDH), Guinea-Bissau's human rights league, whose field report on the heavy-sands mining at Varela, in the north-west near the Senegalese border, is the documentation the affected villages had and would otherwise have lacked. WHAT ITS REPORT ESTABLISHED, and why documentation is the whole of the resource here: the communities “have nowhere to take their children and resettle their lives”; the concession over parcel 12 of the Varela sands at Nhinquin ran to 2028 and had passed from a Russian company that held it from 2015 to a company of unknown capital, presumed to originate in a free zone. The mineral at issue is ilmenite, the source of titanium dioxide — demand driven by the same industries that market themselves as sustainable. WHAT THE COMMUNITIES SAY IS WRONG, as set out in a public campaign: the environmental and social impact study was delivered AFTER the concession was granted, contrary to law; the consultancy that produced it was owned by a direct relative of the minister who approved the project; and the promised schools, health centres and roads were never built. The harms listed are forest, dune, mangrove and farmland destruction, salinisation of groundwater making water unfit to drink or irrigate with, coastal erosion, and loss of traditional livelihoods. ASK WHEN THE IMPACT STUDY WAS DATED RELATIVE TO THE CONCESSION, AND WHO OWNED THE CONSULTANCY — in this case both answers were the case. WHAT HAPPENED, STATED PLAINLY: protests led by women of Nhinquin in January halted the activity; more than 100 women protested peacefully and the area was militarised, with arbitrary detentions reported; in April villagers burned the company's installations and 16 people were detained and taken to a military barracks. WHO IT SUITS: Bissau-Guinean coastal communities facing mining concessions, and anyone needing a national human rights body to visit and record what is happening. CAVEATS: NO VERIFIED LIVE SITE FOR LGDH WAS FOUND — this entry points at the newspaper record quoting its report. It documents and reports; it is not counsel and not a fund. This entry records the confrontation and the arrests as reported; it does not recommend them — the transferable move here is the dated, written field report. For the Urok islands model and community management, Guinea-Bissau's Tiniguena entry.

trackers.name: Guinea-Bissau's Centros de Acesso à Justiça — walk in, get a lawyer appointed at no cost and court fees waived; PROPERTY is the commonest problem they see
trackers.desc: WHERE TO WALK IN: the Centros de Acesso à Justiça (CAJ), created in 2011 under Decreto-lei 11/2010 (the legal-aid framework) and Decreto 11/2011, which also set up the justice ministry's Gabinete de Informação e Consulta Jurídica (GICJU) that coordinates them. WHAT A CENTRE ACTUALLY DOES FOR YOU, from a documented case: staff explain the options, then help you REQUEST THE APPOINTMENT OF A LAWYER AT NO COST THROUGH A PARTNERSHIP WITH THE ORDEM DOS ADVOGADOS, and file a request for EXEMPTION FROM COURT FEES. Two separate applications — counsel and fee waiver — and most people know about neither; the centre exists to make both for you. WHY THIS BELONGS IN A LAND MAP: the head of the Bissau Velho centre lists the commonest problems as PROPERTY first, then thefts, physical assault, debts, labour questions, family problems and illegal detention. COVERAGE AND REACH: centres were planned for nine regions; as of February 2018 seven were installed — two in Bissau and five in the regions, and by 2019 the network had assisted about 13,000 people. Rural reach runs through PAS — community-level activists who act as intermediaries between communities and the CAJ, reporting incidents and directing victims to the centres, with named posts in villages across Cacheu region; regional centres schedule meetings with local communities, and urban centres work directly through police stations and courts. THE HONEST LIMIT, RECORDED IN THE SAME EVALUATIONS: the UNDP-bar association partnership FAILED to secure legal representation in the regions because most advocates are concentrated in Bissau and visit the regions only sporadically. Expect the centre to open the door and the fee waiver to work; do not assume a lawyer will physically appear outside the capital. WHO IT SUITS: Bissau-Guineans with a property, inheritance or detention problem and no money, especially outside Bissau. CAVEATS: donor-dependent and unevenly staffed; traditional authorities still resolve many community disputes in practice. For the Varela mining documentation, Guinea-Bissau's LGDH entry; for the Urok islands community-management model, Tiniguena.

trackers.name: BioGuiné Foundation — a national biodiversity endowment whose stated purpose includes EMPOWERING the communities inside and around the protected areas
trackers.desc: WHERE THE LONG MONEY IS: the Fundação BioGuiné (BioGuinea Foundation, FBG), conceived as a DURABLE FINANCING STRATEGY to consolidate conservation work in Guinea-Bissau — and, in its own words, the EMPOWERMENT of the communities resident inside and in the surroundings of the country's PROTECTED AREAS, through appropriation, accountability and capacity-building of the different actors. A conservation endowment that names community empowerment as half its purpose is worth approaching differently from one that funds park management — quote that purpose back at it. The foundation was envisaged from the creation of the protected-areas institute in 2004 and is a pillar of the national protected-areas and biodiversity strategy. HOW THE MONEY REACHES THE GROUND, WHICH DETERMINES WHO YOU TALK TO: FBG funding is CHANNELLED THROUGH IBAP, the public institute responsible for the country's protected areas — so IBAP, already recorded in this file with its Bissau address, is the door, not the foundation directly. It has supported Orango National Park, a marine protected area in the Bijagós Archipelago — 88 islands, 21 inhabited by some 30,000 people, mostly of the Bijagó ethnicity, a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve since 1996. CAPITALISATION, BECAUSE AN ENDOWMENT ONLY MATTERS IF IT IS FUNDED: the government committed a minimum of ONE MILLION EUROS to the seed capital, witnessed by a joint co-financing letter signed by the finance minister and the state secretary for fisheries in December 2014, alongside contributions recorded from a French environment facility and REDD/carbon market sources. Protected areas cover a reported 12.2% of national territory, rising to 33.3% counting the Bolama-Bijagós Biosphere Reserve. WHO IT SUITS: Bissau-Guinean communities inside or bordering protected areas, especially in the Bijagós, seeking long-term financing for management and livelihoods. CAVEATS: AN ENDOWMENT CHANNELLED THROUGH A STATE INSTITUTE — you apply through IBAP, not to the foundation; it funds conservation and community capacity, NOT litigation, land purchase or opposition to a licensed project, and its reach is protected-area geography only. For the Varela mining documentation, Guinea-Bissau's LGDH entry; for community management at Urok, Tiniguena; for a free lawyer and fee waiver, the Centros de Acesso à Justiça.

trackers.name: Guinea-Bissau's eight environmental civil-society organisations — a national diagnostic naming which five work nationwide and which two are Bijagós-only
trackers.desc: THE WHOLE MAP OF WHO WORKS WHERE, WHICH SAVES A COMMUNITY MONTHS: a national diagnostic identified EIGHT CIVIL-SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS INTERVENING IN THE ENVIRONMENTAL DOMAIN in Guinea-Bissau, and — the useful part — SORTED THEM BY REACH. FIVE COVER THE WHOLE NATIONAL TERRITORY: the ORGANIZAÇÃO PARA A DEFESA E DESENVOLVIMENTO DAS ZONAS HÚMIDAS (ODZH), TINIGUENA, ONG PALMEIRINHA, AD (AÇÃO PARA O DESENVOLVIMENTO), ALTERNAG (Associação Guineense Estudos e Alternativas), and KAFO (Unidade de Entreajuda Social Enraizada no Território). TWO ARE REGIONAL AND WORK ONLY IN THE BIJAGÓS ARCHIPELAGO: ADEMA (Associação para a Defesa do Ambiente) and NINJON. Knowing which organisations can actually travel to you is the difference between a letter answered and a letter ignored — if you are on the islands, ADEMA and NINJON are on your doorstep; if you are inland, the five national bodies are the ones to write to. WHAT TWO OF THEM DO IN PRACTICE: ONG PALMEIRINHA (palmeirinha.org), based at the protected-areas institute's premises in Bissau, works on environmental education and communication at national, regional and international level, its stated mission being to inform and educate Guinean society, DECISION-MAKERS AND THE PRIVATE SECTOR so they use natural resources durably in the Protected Areas and generally; it publishes educational books and runs cinema-debate sessions in schools, works on desertification and plastic-bag use, and is mobilised with communities and the institute on POILÃO in the Bijagós, a sea-turtle sanctuary where green turtles nest between August and October. AD (ad-bissau.org), created 9 NOVEMBER 1991 at CABOXANQUE, Tombali region, BY FORMER AGRICULTURE MINISTRY STAFF, works on income-generating activities, environment, HUMAN RIGHTS, education and training, gender, micro-finance, food security and media, builds COMMUNITY SCHOOLS and museums, and runs beekeeping, horticulture in the tabancas of a national park, and a community radio station. An organisation founded by former ministry staff knows which office holds your file — that is worth more than a bigger budget. WHO IT SUITS: Bissau-Guinean communities choosing which national or island organisation to approach. CAVEATS: A DIAGNOSTIC SNAPSHOT — confirm current activity and contacts. For the island elders' route and the Urok zoning, Guinea-Bissau's Tiniguena entry; for the protected-areas institute, IBAP; for a lawyer in one visit, the Centros de Acesso à Justiça entry; for the endowment, BioGuiné.

trackers.name: Federação KAFO, Djalicunda — the Bissau-Guinean peasant federation that has stood up twenty community-managed forests over fifteen years and markets the honey and juice they produce
trackers.desc: THE FEDERATION WITH TWENTY COMMUNITY FORESTS: the FEDERAÇÃO KAFO, a REGIONAL NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATION AND PEASANT FEDERATION, with its SEDE SOCIAL at the CENTRO CAMPONÊS DE DJALICUNDA, SECTOR DE MANSABA, REGIÃO DE OIO, CP 1186 — northern Guinea-Bissau. THE RECORD: IN THE OIO REGION 20 COMMUNITY-MANAGED FORESTS HAVE NOW BEEN IMPLEMENTED FOR FIFTEEN YEARS BY THE KAFO PEASANT FEDERATION, IN WHICH PARTICIPATING LOCAL COMMUNITIES ARE ENGAGED IN SEVERAL SUSTAINABLE PRACTICES AND NATURAL RESOURCE USES BASED ON TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE. Twenty community forests standing after fifteen years is the longest-running community forest programme recorded for Guinea-Bissau in this file — and it is run by a federation of peasants, not by a conservation NGO. If your tabanca wants a community forest, this is the body that has done it twenty times in one region. AND THE PART THAT MAKES THEM LAST: KAFO FURTHER PROMOTES THE MARKETING OF CERTAIN NATURAL PRODUCTS DERIVED FROM THE COMMUNITY FORESTS — FOR EXAMPLE HONEY AND JUICES — AND SEEKS TO EXPAND THE SYSTEM BY IMPLEMENTING ADDITIONAL COMMUNITY FORESTS IN THE REGION. A forest that sells honey pays for its own protection. Ask KAFO how the marketing is organised before you ask anyone for a grant — the buyers and the product lines are the part most community forest schemes in this file never built, and it is why Chad's reserve lapsed and Mohéli's park disappointed. WHY THE MODEL MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY: the federation's work sits alongside Guinea-Bissau's SACRED FORESTS, and the research question its programme was examined against was whether community-managed forests can carry protection forward as the values attached to sacred groves shift. Where a sacred forest is weakening because the people who kept it are gone, a community-managed forest with a product to sell is the successor institution. That is a live argument to put to elders who fear their grove will not survive the next generation. The pressure it works against is documented: CASHEW HAS REPLACED MOST OTHER FORMS OF LAND USE IN GUINEA-BISSAU, ESPECIALLY SINCE THE 1980s, IS THE ONLY CASH CROP OF THE ECONOMY AND ACCOUNTS FOR ABOUT 90% OF ALL EXPORTS, WITH THE QUICK EXPANSION OF CASHEW ORCHARDS HOMOGENISING ONCE HIGHLY COMPLEX BIO-CULTURAL LANDSCAPES. If the thing taking your land is a cashew orchard rather than a company, the counter-offer has to be another crop that pays — which is exactly what the honey and juice lines are for. AND THE OTHER THREAT ON THE HORIZON, RECORDED IN THE FILE: petroleum exploration has covered GUINEA-BISSAU'S ENTIRE COAST, INCLUDING THE BOLAMA-BIJAGÓS ARCHIPELAGO, with early estimates of a substantial resource and the warning that offshore production COULD HAVE HUGE ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS UNLESS NECESSARY SAFEGUARDS ARE DEVELOPED AND IMPLEMENTED. WHO IT SUITS: Bissau-Guinean tabancas in Oio and beyond wanting a community forest that earns, and island communities facing offshore exploration. CAVEATS: A REGIONAL FEDERATION — its twenty forests are in Oio; confirm whether it works your region. For which organisations cover the whole country and which only the Bijagós, Guinea-Bissau's eight environmental organisations entry; for the island elders' route and Urok zoning, Tiniguena; for a lawyer in one visit, the Centros de Acesso à Justiça entry; for the endowment, BioGuiné.

trackers.name: Guinea-Bissau's boundary-dispute machinery — the brigade, the Comissão Fundiária Nacional and participatory demarcation in named sections, plus an eighteen-organisation civil society roster
trackers.desc: WHO SETTLES A TABANCA BOUNDARY, WITH THE SEQUENCE AS IT ACTUALLY RAN: in the SECTION OF PELUNDO, CACHEU REGION, IN THE TABANCAS WHERE THERE HAD BEEN NO CONSENSUS ON THE BOUNDARIES, work resumed with NEW MEETINGS WITH THE BRIGADE, NEGOTIATIONS BETWEEN THE PARTIES IN DISAGREEMENT, AND A MEETING AT THE COMISSÃO FUNDIÁRIA NACIONAL; discussions also opened on the draft REGULAMENTO DA LEI DE ORDENAMENTO TERRITORIAL E URBANO (ROTU) at the Ministry of Public Works, Housing and Urbanism. Brigade first, then negotiation between the parties, then the national land commission — that is the escalation order for a boundary that will not settle, and the commission is a named national body a tabanca can be taken to. Ask for the meeting at the Comissão Fundiária Nacional by name. AND THE OTHER HALF OF THE METHOD, IN THE SECTION OF QUICET, BIOMBO: PARTICIPATORY PLANNING AND DEMARCATION OF COMMUNITY LANDS BEGAN AFTER CONSULTATIONS WITH CENTRAL GOVERNMENT, LOCAL ADMINISTRATION, TRADITIONAL POWER AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, PLUS FIELD VISITS — STARTING WITH A FIRST WORKSHOP PRESENTING THE PROJECT. Traditional power is named as a consulted party in the state's own sequence, alongside central government and local administration. If your elders are not at the table, the sequence is not being followed — say so, and cite Quicet. The work runs across the regions of OIO, CACHEU AND BIOMBO under a project titled peaceful and inclusive management of land. A project whose own title is peaceful and INCLUSIVE land management is one whose terms you can hold it to. THE ROSTER, WHICH IS THE REST OF WHO EXISTS: EIGHTEEN NAMED BISSAU-GUINEAN CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS — including the ASSOCIAÇÃO NACIONAL PARA O DESENVOLVIMENTO LOCAL URBANO (NADEL), the ASSOCIAÇÃO ACADÉMICA DA FACULDADE DE DIREITO DE BISSAU, the COOPERATIVA DOS PRODUTORES AGROPECUÁRIA DE TOMBALI, FAROL DO DIREITO PÚBLICO, the LIGA GUINEENSE DOS DIREITOS HUMANOS, ONG PALMEIRINHA, ODZH, the REDE NACIONAL DAS ASSOCIAÇÕES JUVENIS (RENAJ), the REDE DAS MULHERES OPERADORAS ECONÓMICAS DA GUINÉ-BISSAU (REMOE), TINIGUENA, and VOZ DI PAZ. Two of those are worth singling out for a land case: the law faculty's student association, which is where free research capacity sits, and FAROL DO DIREITO PÚBLICO — a public-law body in a country whose land disputes are public-law disputes. And REMOE is the women traders' network: in a cashew economy, the people who buy and sell the crop are an interest group with weight. WHO IT SUITS: Bissau-Guinean tabancas with a contested boundary, communities in Oio, Cacheu or Biombo, and anyone needing research or a public-law argument. CAVEATS: A DONOR-SUPPORTED LAND PROGRAMME on project cycles — confirm which sections are covered now. For which organisations are national and which Bijagós-only, Guinea-Bissau's eight environmental organisations entry; for twenty community forests that sell honey, the Federação KAFO entry; for the island elders and Urok zoning, Tiniguena; for a lawyer in one visit, the Centros de Acesso à Justiça entry.

trackers.name: Guinea-Bissau's searchable civil society directory, and the profile of AD — founded at Caboxanque in 1991 by former agriculture ministry officials to build base organisations, with micro-finance and human rights among its themes
trackers.desc: THE CITIZEN'S ACTION SHOULD EQUAL THE STATE'S — that is ONG PALMEIRINHA's own stated vision, and it is the sharpest sentence in this file's Bissau-Guinean record: AN ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY TURNED TOWARDS THE CONSERVATION AND RATIONAL USE OF NATURAL RESOURCES IN WHICH THE CITIZEN IS CALLED TO PARTICIPATE, SUCH THAT THEIR ACTION TENDS TO BE ASSUMED AND TO EQUAL THAT OF THE STATE. Not consulted, not heard — equal to the state's. An organisation that writes that into its published vision is one that will back a community claiming a role rather than a hearing. Its mission adds that it exists to inform, educate and communicate to SOCIETY, DECISION-MAKERS AND THE PRIVATE SECTOR, which means it will address the company as well as the ministry. AND THE DIRECTORY THAT MAKES ALL OF THIS REACHABLE: A SEARCHABLE BUSINESS DIRECTORY OF BISSAU-GUINEAN CIVIL SOCIETY CARRIES A FULL PROFILE PER ORGANISATION — founding date and place, founders, stated aims, and a list of priority intervention themes. A directory with founding date, founders and themes for each entry is how you tell a working organisation from a name on a list. Read the themes before you write: an organisation whose themes do not include environment or human rights will not carry your case however friendly it is. THE PROFILE THAT MATTERS MOST, BECAUSE THIS FILE HAS NAMED AD WITHOUT EVER SAYING WHAT IT IS: A ONG ACÇÃO PARA O DESENVOLVIMENTO WAS CREATED AT CABOXANQUE, REGION OF TOMBALI, ON 9 NOVEMBER 1991, ON THE INITIATIVE OF FORMER OFFICIALS OF GUINEA-BISSAU'S MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE. Founded in a village in the south by people who had worked inside the agriculture ministry and left. That combination — rural base, state experience — is why it can navigate both a tabanca meeting and a ministry corridor. Ask AD who in it knows the ministry that is handling your file. ITS AIM, IN ITS OWN WORDS: TO ENCOURAGE AND REINFORCE THE INITIATIVES THAT LEAD TO A DEVELOPMENT ASSOCIATING THE AUTHENTIC PROGRESS OF MAN AND JUSTICE, THROUGH THE CREATION OF STRUCTURES THAT PROMOTE THE DEVELOPMENT OF ORGANIZAÇÕES DE BASE AND THE PROMOTION OF ALTERNATIVE SYSTEMS — AND TO CREATE SOCIOECONOMIC, CULTURAL AND POLITICAL CONDITIONS FAVOURING A DEVELOPMENT THAT IS SOCIALLY JUST, ECONOMICALLY INCLUSIVE AND ENVIRONMENTALLY RESPONSIBLE. Creating STRUCTURES that promote base organisations is a different offer from running projects for them. If your village group needs to become a durable body rather than a beneficiary, that is the organisation whose stated purpose is building the structure. ITS PRIORITY INTERVENTION THEMES ARE PUBLISHED IN FULL: INCOME-GENERATING ACTIVITIES, ENVIRONMENT, HUMAN RIGHTS, EDUCATION AND TRAINING, GENDER, MICRO-FINANCE, HEALTH, FOOD SECURITY, AND SOCIAL COMMUNICATION. Micro-finance, human rights and environment inside one organisation is rare anywhere in this file. It means the same body can lend a women's group working capital, take up a land violation, and argue the conservation case — without three separate introductions. And SOCIAL COMMUNICATION on the list means it can put the story out. Ten years of the assessment authority, a national NGO and an international union working together, with park residents giving evidence. If your community lives inside a protected area, that is the established channel — and residents' testimony is already part of how it works. The same record notes national recognition given in categories including COMMUNICATION AND AWARENESS IN PROTECTED AREAS, PARK GUARD, LOBBYING AND FUNDRAISING, OFFICIALISATION OF THE BIOSPHERE RESERVE, AND ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION. Lobbying and fundraising is an award category. Where a national institute publicly honours those skills, they are skills you can openly ask to be taught. WHO IT SUITS: Bissau-Guinean village groups wanting to become a structure, women's groups needing credit, and communities inside protected areas.
