trackers.desc: SEVENTY-SEVEN THOUSAND DOCUMENTS, FREE, AND A PAGE FOR YOUR COUNTRY — declared overlap first: THIS PLATFORM ALREADY APPEARS AS A SOURCE BEHIND TWO ENTRIES IN THIS FILE, UNDER MOZAMBIQUE AND ESWATINI. NEITHER DESCRIBES THE FOUNDATION ITSELF, WHICH IS WHAT THIS ENTRY IS FOR. THE PROBLEM IT EXISTS TO SOLVE, NAMED BY THE SECTOR ITSELF: PRACTITIONERS AND ORGANIZATIONS IN THE LAND SECTOR COMMONLY VIEW THE INACCESSIBILITY OF LAND INFORMATION AS A KEY IMPEDIMENT TO THE PROMOTION OF POLICIES AND PRACTICES THAT ENSURE RESPONSIBLE LAND GOVERNANCE — POOR VISIBILITY OF WHAT IS BEING DONE TO ADVANCE LAND RIGHTS AT THE COUNTRY LEVEL, COUPLED WITH A LACK OF SYNERGY AND COORDINATION AMONG STAKEHOLDERS, HAS SLOWED THE PROGRESS OF THE LAND GOVERNANCE AGENDA. Not that the information does not exist — that nobody can find it. This file has met that wall in almost every country: a study was done, a law was passed, an organisation already works on this, and none of it is where anyone would look. WHAT IT PULLS TOGETHER: IT FACILITATES THE COLLECTION, SOURCING AND SEARCHING OF OTHERWISE FRAGMENTED AND INACCESSIBLE DATA AND INFORMATION ON LAND GOVERNANCE AND LAND USE FROM DIVERSE SOURCES — PRODUCED BY GOVERNMENTS, ACADEMIA, INTERNATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS, INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS — COMBINING PUBLIC DATA, PUBLISHED INFORMATION, AND FIRST-HAND KNOWLEDGE. INDIGENOUS PEOPLES listed as a source category alongside governments and academia. Community knowledge is treated as data here, not as anecdote. THE COUNTRY PAGE, WHICH IS WHERE TO START: A LAND BOOK PROVIDES COUNTRY AND THEMATIC PAGES WITH STANDARDIZED INDICATOR DATA, DATA VISUALIZATION TOOLS, CURATED COUNTRY AND THEME NARRATIVES, AND ACCESS TO RELEVANT RESEARCH AND PUBLICATIONS — A ONE-STOP SHOP FOR KEY STATISTICS AND RESOURCES ON LAND GOVERNANCE IN EVERY COUNTRY OF THE WORLD. Every country, including the ones with the thinnest coverage in this file. Before commissioning any research, open your country's page: the tenure figures, the laws and the existing studies are already assembled there, and a curated narrative tells you what the picture is. THE LIBRARY: OVER 77,000 RESOURCES LISTED. Search it by your country and your commodity. Somebody has almost certainly already written about the thing on your land, and a report you can cite is worth more in a meeting than an assertion you cannot. THE LICENSING, WHICH MATTERS IF YOU BUILD ANYTHING: IT IS A PIONEERING HUB FOR LINKED OPEN DATA ON LAND, ENABLING THE PUBLICATION OF STRUCTURED DATA IN MACHINE READABLE, STANDARDIZED FORMATS UNDER OPEN LICENSES THAT CAN BE REUSED BY ANYONE — AND IT ESTABLISHES BY DEFAULT OPEN SOURCE LICENSES IN ALL ITS COMPUTER DEVELOPMENTS. Reusable by anyone, by default. A community handbook, a school lesson or a submission can lift from it without asking permission. THE OPEN DOOR: EVERYONE IS WELCOME TO PARTICIPATE — BE IT TO SHARE EXPERIENCES, ASK QUESTIONS, CONTRIBUTE EXPERTISE OR SIMPLY LISTEN-IN AND LEARN MORE — AND GET IN TOUCH IF YOU WANT TO ORGANIZE AN EVENT WITH US. They will co-host an event with you. For an organisation with no platform, a webinar carrying somebody else's audience is the cheapest way to be heard outside your district — and the invitation is standing. THE CAPACITY WORK, WHICH IS THE PART TO ASK FOR: IT EMPOWERED LOCAL ORGANIZATIONS ACROSS THE GLOBAL SOUTH, PARTICULARLY THOSE IN EAST AFRICA, INDIA, THE MEKONG REGION AND LATIN AMERICA, TO ENHANCE THEIR USE AND MANAGEMENT OF LAND INFORMATION AND CONTRIBUTE TO A LAND INFORMATION ECOSYSTEM — AND IT AIMS TO BUILD THE CAPACITIES OF INFORMATION PROVIDERS. Training African organisations to manage their own land information, so the records stay with them. That is a different offer from being studied by someone else. WHAT ONE ONLINE DEBATE ACTUALLY PRODUCED: SOME OF THE IDEAS DISCUSSED THERE, AND THE INTERCHANGE BETWEEN DISCUSSANTS, LATER INFLUENCED CONTRIBUTIONS TO CONSULTATIVE SESSIONS ORGANISED BY A PRESIDENTIAL ADVISORY PANEL ON AGRICULTURE AND LAND REFORM ON THE NEED TO RE-PURPOSE LAND ADMINISTRATION. An online discussion that reached a presidential panel. Taking part in the debates is not decoration — the people writing national land policy read them. AND THE GAP A PARTICIPANT NAMES, WHICH IS AN OPENING FOR YOU: THERE ARE REAL OBSTACLES TO GETTING INFORMATION ON, FOR EXAMPLE, INDIGENOUS AND COMMUNITY LAND RIGHTS AS WELL AS WOMEN'S LAND RIGHTS. The two categories hardest to find data on are exactly the ones most communities in this file hold. If you have that information for your own area, you hold something the sector says is missing — which is leverage as well as a contribution. ITS STATUS: A FOUNDATION REGISTERED IN THE NETHERLANDS IN 2014, A REGISTERED PUBLIC BENEFIT ORGANIZATION WHICH DOES NOT GENERATE PROFITS FROM ITS ACTIVITIES. AND ITS STATED VISION: WHEN IT COMES TO STRENGTHENING THE RIGHT TO LAND, IT IS THE LOCAL COMMUNITIES THEMSELVES THAT HAVE TO GET INVOLVED. WHO IT SUITS: any African community organisation that needs the existing research, law and statistics for its country before it acts. CAVEATS: A KNOWLEDGE PLATFORM, NOT A FUNDER OR A LITIGATOR — and coverage of community and women's land rights is thinner than the rest, by its own account. For the platform mapping community land and concessions, Mali's LandMark entry; for the searchable register of community struggles, Algeria's Environmental Justice Atlas entry; for free legal research across jurisdictions, the Central African Republic's pro bono brokerage entry.

trackers.name: Code for Africa — Africa's largest network of civic-tech and data labs in 20 countries — two free open data and source-document portals, a drone network, air quality sensors, forensic tools and whistleblower encryption for newsrooms, all under an open licence
trackers.desc: SIX MONTHS OF SUPPORT, NOT A WEEK OF CONSULTANTS — declared adjacency first: ONE OF THE INVESTIGATIVE OUTLETS IN THIS NETWORK IS ALREADY FILED UNDER SOUTH AFRICA, AND THE GAMBIA ENTRY COVERS STORY GRANTS. NEITHER COVERS THE DATA PORTALS, THE DOCUMENT REPOSITORY, THE DRONE NETWORK OR THE AIR SENSORS. WHAT IT IS: THE CONTINENT'S LARGEST NETWORK OF CIVIC TECHNOLOGY AND DATA JOURNALISM LABS, WITH TEAMS IN 20 COUNTRIES — BUILDING SOLUTIONS THAT GIVE CITIZENS UNFETTERED ACCESS TO ACTIONABLE INFORMATION THAT EMPOWERS THEM TO MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS, AND WHICH STRENGTHENS CIVIC ENGAGEMENT FOR IMPROVED PUBLIC GOVERNANCE AND ACCOUNTABILITY. THE TWO FREE PORTALS, AND THE SECOND IS THE ONE TO NOTICE: THE CONTINENT'S LARGEST OPEN DATA PORTALS — ONE FOR DATASETS AND ONE FOR SOURCE DOCUMENTS. A source-document repository is where contracts, licences, permits and reports that somebody obtained are held in public. This file has recorded that the concession over your land usually exists on paper somewhere and nobody has looked. That is a place to look, free. AND THE DATA PORTAL COMES WITH PEOPLE: 6,000+ USERS COMPRISING DEVELOPERS WHO USE THE API, JOURNALISTS WHO FIND DATASETS FOR THEIR STORIES AND INVESTIGATIONS, AND RESEARCHERS WHO REQUEST DATA — WITH A TEAM OF DATA ANALYSTS WHO HELP FIND IT, AND A VAST COLLECTION OF READY-TO-USE DATASETS IN VARIOUS FORMATS WHICH USERS CAN DOWNLOAD FOR ANALYSIS AND COMPARISONS. A TEAM OF DATA ANALYSTS WHO HELP FIND IT. You can ask for the data rather than only search for it — which matters when you do not know what the dataset would be called. THE THREE INCUBATED NETWORKS: AN AFRICAN DRONE NETWORK; A FACT-CHECKING INITIATIVE; AND AN AIR QUALITY SENSOR NETWORK. A continental drone network and an air-sensor network are two things communities in this file have needed and paid for separately. An overhead photograph of a clearance and a record of what a plant is putting into the air are both obtainable through people who already own the equipment — and this file's Somalia entry gives the kite-and-balloon alternative where drones are restricted. THE INVESTIGATIVE NETWORK IT MANAGES: IT GIVES THE CONTINENT'S BEST MUCKRAKING NEWSROOMS THE LATEST POSSIBLE FORENSIC DATA TOOLS, DIGITAL SECURITY AND WHISTLEBLOWER ENCRYPTION TO HELP IMPROVE THEIR ABILITY TO TACKLE CROOKED POLITICIANS, ORGANISED CRIME AND PREDATORY BIG BUSINESS — AND IT SPEARHEADED CONTINENT-WIDE PROBES OF A MAJOR LEAKED-DOCUMENTS INVESTIGATION. WHISTLEBLOWER ENCRYPTION is the practical one. If somebody inside the company or the ministry wants to hand over the contract, there is a newsroom equipped to receive it safely — and telling that person such a route exists is something a community member can do. THE MONEY IT MANAGES: A $1 MILLION-A-YEAR INNOVATION FUND AND A $500,000-A-YEAR IMPACT FUND — PLUS SEED FUNDING FOR CROSS-BORDER COLLABORATION AND ONE OF AFRICA'S LARGEST SKILLS DEVELOPMENT INITIATIVES FOR DIGITAL JOURNALISTS. THE WOMEN'S NETWORK: A PAN-AFRICAN NETWORK OF FEMALE JOURNALISTS, DATA SCIENTISTS AND TECHNOLOGISTS WORKING TO CHANGE THE DIGITAL MEDIA LANDSCAPE BY PRODUCING AND PROMOTING DATA-DRIVEN NEWS. THE BOOTCAMP MODEL, AND ITS STATED REASON IS THE MOST USEFUL PARAGRAPH HERE: A $25,000 SUPPORT PROGRAMME GIVES PARTICIPANTS SMALL CASH GRANTS AS SEED FUNDING, ALONG WITH TECHNOLOGY AND BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT MENTORSHIP, SPACE IN LOCAL TECH HUBS, AND ACCESS TO SPECIALIST PAN-AFRICAN COMMUNITIES — DESIGNED TO AVOID THE PROBLEM THAT HIT AND RUN WORKSHOPS ALWAYS HAVE, WHERE A BUNCH OF CONSULTANTS PARACHUTE IN FOR A WEEK AND THEN DISAPPEAR. EVERYONE GETS REALLY EXCITED, BUT QUICKLY FINDS OUT THAT THEIR NEW SKILLS AREN'T MATURE ENOUGH TO ACTUALLY BUILD ANYTHING MEANINGFUL AFTER THE EXPERTS LEAVE — SO THE MODEL GUARANTEES SIX MONTHS OF INTENSIVE SUPPORT. Consultants parachute in for a week and then disappear. Every community in this file has been on the receiving end of that, and here is an organisation that named the problem and redesigned around it. Use the sentence: when someone offers your committee a workshop, ask what happens in month four. THE LICENCE: ALL CONTENT IS RELEASED UNDER A CREATIVE COMMONS ATTRIBUTION LICENSE, AND THE SITE ITSELF IS OPEN SOURCE CODE. Everything reusable with credit. A community handbook, a map or a submission can lift from it without asking. AND THE HONEST SECTOR ASSESSMENT IT PUBLISHES ABOUT ITS OWN FIELD: MANY CIVIC TECH PROJECTS IN AFRICA ARE DONOR-FUNDED, SHORT-LIVED, AND LACK CLEAR MODELS FOR LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY; ACTORS FACE STRUCTURAL OBSTACLES IN SECURING STABLE FUNDING, FORMING LASTING INSTITUTIONAL PARTNERSHIPS AND MAINTAINING USER ENGAGEMENT; AND THE DIGITAL DIVIDE REMAINS A SIGNIFICANT BARRIER, WITH MANY RURAL AND MARGINALISED COMMUNITIES LACKING ACCESS TO THE INTERNET AND DIGITAL LITERACY SKILLS. A civic-tech federation admitting that most civic-tech projects die and that rural communities cannot reach them anyway. Read that before accepting a digital tool as the answer — and pair anything online with the offline routes in this file: the printed satellite image, the community radio, the paralegal who walks. WHO IT SUITS: African communities and their allies looking for datasets, source documents, aerial imagery, air readings or a newsroom that can receive documents safely. CAVEATS: IT SERVES JOURNALISTS, DEVELOPERS AND RESEARCHERS RATHER THAN COMMUNITIES DIRECTLY — the route in is usually a reporter or a local lab. For story grants that pay a reporter's travel, Gambia's entry; for the investigative outlet already filed, South Africa's Oxpeckers entry; for kite-and-balloon aerial mapping where drones are restricted, Somalia's entry.

trackers.name: AMLA (African Mining Legislation Atlas) — the mining laws of all 53 African countries, free and side by side — with a drafting template offering two annotated sample provisions per topic, and training already given to 70 young African law students from 18 countries
trackers.desc: YOUR COUNTRY'S MINING LAW, FREE, BESIDE EVERY OTHER COUNTRY'S — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S GAMBIA ENTRY COVERS THE AFRICAN LEGAL SUPPORT FACILITY THAT CO-IMPLEMENTS THIS PROJECT, AND ITS ETHIOPIA ENTRY NAMES THE ATLAS IN ONE LINE. NEITHER DESCRIBES THE PLATFORM, THE TEMPLATE OR THE TRAINING. WHAT IT GIVES: FREE ONLINE ACCESS TO THE MINING LAWS OF 53 AFRICAN COUNTRIES — A ONE-STOP RESOURCE FOR AFRICA'S MINING LEGAL FRAMEWORK COVERING MINING CODES, REGULATIONS AND RELATED LEGISLATION, WITH INTERACTIVE FEATURES TO PROVIDE COMPARATIVE DATA ACROSS EXISTING LAWS AND REGULATIONS. COMPARATIVE is the word that matters. Any community can eventually find its own mining code; almost nobody can put it beside fifty-two others and see what their country left out. When a ministry says a protection is impossible or unheard of, the atlas shows which African neighbours already have it in force — which turns an objection into a citation. WHY IT WAS BUILT, STATED PLAINLY: A COMPREHENSIVE LEGAL FRAMEWORK IS CRUCIAL FOR THE PROPER GOVERNANCE OF AFRICA'S MINING SECTOR — HOWEVER, ACCESS TO AND KNOWLEDGE OF THE EVOLVING LEGISLATION OF MANY AFRICAN COUNTRIES HAS NOT KEPT PACE. Even the lawyers could not reliably find these laws. If your advocate has never read the current mining code because no copy was accessible, that is a documented continental problem rather than a personal failing — and it is now solved for free. THE DRAFTING TEMPLATE, AND ITS STRUCTURE IS THE FIND: A MINING LAW DRAFTING AND REFERENCE TOOL PROVIDING GUIDANCE ON THE ELEMENTS OF A MINING LAW COVERING ALL POTENTIAL ISSUES, BASED ON AFRICA'S PRESENT REALITIES — EACH TOPIC DESCRIBED WITH ITS ELEMENTS AND ASSOCIATED ISSUES, FOLLOWED GENERALLY BY TWO SAMPLE PROVISIONS, EACH ACCOMPANIED BY AN ANNOTATION EXPLAINING THE CONTEXT, ISSUES, AND USEFUL FEATURES OF THE PRESENTED LANGUAGE. Two drafted alternatives per topic, each with an explanation of why it is worded that way. A community coalition submitting comments on a draft mining law does not have to describe what it wants in general terms — it can propose actual clause text, annotated, and ask why the weaker of the two was chosen. This file has recorded that submissions written in the language of the draft are the ones that survive. WHERE THE SAMPLE LANGUAGE COMES FROM: MOST EXAMPLES ARE DRAWN OR INSPIRED BY CURRENT MINING LAWS WITHIN AFRICA, AND WHERE SUCH EXAMPLES DO NOT EXIST THEY ARE SOURCED FROM MINING LAWS OUTSIDE OF AFRICA OR DRAFTED DE NOVO. African-sourced first. So the answer to a minister who says a clause is foreign and unworkable here is usually the name of the African country whose law already contains it. WHAT IT IS FOR: AN ENHANCED STARTING POINT PROVIDING A CLEAR AND PRACTICAL FOUNDATION ON WHICH USERS CAN THOROUGHLY CONSIDER TOPICAL ISSUES SUPPORTED BY SAMPLE DRAFTING LANGUAGE AS THEY DEVELOP, MODIFY OR SIMPLY ASSESS MINING LEGISLATIVE FRAMEWORKS THAT FIT EACH COUNTRY'S UNIQUE CONTEXT. OR SIMPLY ASSESS. You do not have to be drafting anything to use it — reading your own law against the template shows what is missing, which is the cheapest audit of a mining code available. THE TRAINING AND THE NUMBERS ALREADY DELIVERED: CAPACITY BUILDING THROUGH TRAINING, ON-GROUND AND REMOTELY, OF AFRICAN LEGAL PROFESSIONALS AND ADVANCED LAW STUDENTS — IN THE USE OF THE PLATFORM AND ON OVERALL ISSUES IN MINING LAW. TO DATE THE PROJECT HAS TRAINED 70 YOUNG AFRICAN LAW STUDENTS FROM 18 COUNTRIES. Seventy trained students across eighteen countries, and remote training is offered. Those are early-career lawyers who already know mining law and are cheap to reach — the university law clinics filed under Comoros are where to look for them. WHO BUILT AND RUNS IT: AN INITIATIVE OF A DEVELOPMENT BANK'S LEGAL VICE-PRESIDENCY, IMPLEMENTED WITH AN AFRICAN LEGAL SUPPORT FACILITY AND AN AFRICAN UNION COMMISSION, WITH A NAMED SOUTH AFRICAN UNIVERSITY LAW FACULTY AN INTEGRAL PART FOR SEVERAL YEARS. An African university faculty inside the project. That is a named academic route to expertise your organisation can approach directly, and a place students are being trained. THE FOUR STATED OBJECTIVES: PROMOTING TRANSPARENCY, ACCESSIBILITY AND COMPARISON OF AFRICA'S MINING LAWS; FACILITATING THE PREPARATION, REVISION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF MINING LAWS; PROVIDING A LIVING DATABASE TO CATALYSE RESEARCH AND POLICY DEBATES ON LEGAL AND REGULATORY ISSUES; AND PROMOTING THE DEVELOPMENT OF LOCAL LEGAL EXPERTISE ON AFRICAN MINING LAWS. IMPLEMENTATION is listed beside preparation and revision. A good mining law nobody enforces is the pattern this file has recorded from Burundi to Kenya — and it is named here as part of the job. THE CONTINENTAL ALIGNMENT IT CLAIMS: AFRICA NEEDS TOOLS THAT RESPOND TO AND ARE ALIGNED WITH THE PRINCIPLES OF A CONTINENTAL MINING VISION AND THE ASPIRATIONS OF A CONTINENTAL 2063 AGENDA. Two continental frameworks your own government has endorsed. Quoting them back is how a local demand becomes a national commitment somebody is already accountable for. AND THE ATTACHED TOOLKITS: A TOOLKIT FOR STATE EQUITY PARTICIPATION IN MINING COMPANIES, AND A MINERAL TAXATION TOOLKIT LAUNCHED ALONGSIDE THE ATLAS. STATE EQUITY PARTICIPATION means whether the country owns a share of the mine on its own land, and MINERAL TAXATION means what it collects. Both decide whether anything returns to the region the ore came from — and both now have free toolkits. WHO IT SUITS: African communities, coalitions and lawyers facing a mining project, a draft mining law, or a ministry claiming a protection cannot be written. CAVEATS: MINING LAW ONLY — not oil and gas, not agriculture, not infrastructure — and it gives the law rather than the individual licence or contract. For the contracts themselves, Mauritania's and South Sudan's entries; for the facility that co-implements it and its free academy, Gambia's entry; for senior lawyers who renegotiate resource contracts, Ethiopia's entry.

Both fundable from the same programme, which is rare. AND ITS SECOND PURPOSE, AIMED AT OTHER FUNDERS: TO ATTRACT MORE FUNDING AND INFLUENCE FUNDING PRACTICES TO PRIORITIZE LONG-TERM FLEXIBLE SUPPORT TO GRASSROOTS GROUPS. THE COLLECTIVE SECURITY WORK: SINCE 2017 IT HAS PLAYED A LEADING ROLE IN REDEFINING SECURITY FOR HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS AND PROMOTING COLLECTIVE SECURITY, CO-CREATING AN ONLINE MULTIMEDIA RESOURCE ON DEFENDING RIGHTS IN HOSTILE CONTEXTS, BASED ON INPUT FROM TWO CROSS-SECTOR DIALOGUES WITH COMMUNITY ACTIVISTS, NGOs AND DONORS. COLLECTIVE security rather than individual protection — the whole community's safety planned together instead of a bodyguard for one leader. That is both cheaper and more durable, and there is a free multimedia resource explaining how it is done. AND THE AFRICAN COUNTRIES ON RECORD: OVER THE YEARS IT HAS SUPPORTED HUMAN RIGHTS GROUPS IN SIERRA LEONE, LIBERIA, GUINEA, THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, UGANDA AND BURUNDI — WITH A GLOBAL TEAM OF 65 OR MORE, FOUNDED IN 2002. For the funder publishing its unrestricted percentages, Gambia's entry; for the 24-hour protection helpline, Benin's entry; for the fund waiving registration entirely, the Central African Republic's entry.

HOW MEMBERSHIP WORKS: ITS OBJECTIVES ARE OUTLINED IN ITS CONSTITUTION, AND MEMBERS FORMALLY SUBSCRIBE TO THEM — ADVANCING THOSE OBJECTIVES AT LOCAL, NATIONAL, REGIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL LEVELS. Read the constitution before joining: subscribing to it is the membership act, and it is what you would be bound to. WHAT IT COVERS BEYOND HOUSING, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: ITS WORK FOCUSES ON THE HUMAN RIGHTS LINKED TO HOUSING AND HABITAT — THAT IS, LAND, HOUSING, CLEAN WATER, SANITATION, A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT, ACCESS TO PUBLIC GOODS AND SERVICES SUCH AS HEALTH, EDUCATION, TRANSPORT AND RECREATION, ACCESS TO LIVELIHOOD AND SOCIAL PROTECTION, PLURALISM, AND THE PRESERVATION OF SOCIAL, NATURAL, HISTORIC AND CULTURAL PATRIMONY. LAND, WATER, A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT, LIVELIHOOD and NATURAL AND CULTURAL PATRIMONY are all inside the mandate. A rural community losing farmland, a spring, a grazing route or a sacred site to a project is describing this coalition's subject, not stretching it — which matters because the housing framing puts many rural organisations off approaching. THE PUBLISHED CONTACT ROUTES: A COORDINATION OFFICE FOR THE MIDDLE EAST AND NORTH AFRICA REGIONAL PROGRAMME AT A NAMED STREET ADDRESS IN CAIRO WITH A PUBLISHED TELEPHONE AND FAX NUMBER, AND A UN LIAISON OFFICE IN GENEVA WITH ITS OWN NUMBER — PLUS PUBLISHED EMAIL ADDRESSES FOR BOTH THE HOUSING AND LAND RIGHTS NETWORK AND THE NORTH AFRICA PROGRAMME. An address and a phone number in Cairo, on the continent, in a region this file has few contacts for. And a UN liaison office in Geneva is a route to the treaty bodies that most community organisations have no way of reaching. THE AFRICAN TURNING POINT IN ITS OWN HISTORY: A SEMINAR HELD BY MEMBERS IN LIMURU, KENYA IN 1987 FORMED A TURNING POINT IN THE MEMBERS' COLLECTIVE PHILOSOPHY AND COMPOSITION, COMMITTING ITSELF TO THE SERVICE OF PEOPLE AND COMMUNITIES LIVING IN POVERTY AND DEPRIVATION — BRINGING TOGETHER REPRESENTATIVES FROM OVER 40 NGOs FROM AFRICA, ASIA AND LATIN AMERICA, AND GIVING WAY TO A NEW STRUCTURE AND A CLEAR VISION. The coalition changed its own constitution at a meeting in Kenya, on the initiative of Southern members. That is a precedent worth knowing when weighing whether an international body can actually be moved by its African membership. WHAT IT SEEKS: TO RECOGNIZE, DEFEND AND FULLY IMPLEMENT EVERYONE'S RIGHT TO A SECURE PLACE TO LIVE IN PEACE AND DIGNITY, IN ALL COUNTRIES — ALSO SERVING AS A PRESSURE GROUP IN DEFENCE OF THE RIGHTS OF THE HOMELESS, POOR AND INADEQUATELY HOUSED. WHAT IT DOES: ADVOCACY AND SUPPORT FOR THE POOR, SOLIDARITY NETWORKING, POPULAR MOBILIZATION, DEBATE AND ANALYSIS — EMPHASISING STRENGTHENING THE NETWORK, SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES, AND INFLUENCING PUBLIC POLICY. POPULAR MOBILIZATION named among its own activities. A coalition that expects its members to organise rather than only to be consulted. THE SPECIALIST NETWORK IT RUNS: A HOUSING AND LAND RIGHTS NETWORK WITH A GLOBAL PROGRAMME, WHICH ALSO OPERATES THE COALITION'S PROGRAMME IN THE MIDDLE EAST AND NORTH AFRICA AS WELL AS EMERGING REGIONAL INITIATIVES IN OTHER REGIONS. EMERGING REGIONAL INITIATIVES IN OTHER REGIONS is worth asking about directly: sub-Saharan Africa has no standing regional programme named here, so an organisation approaching now is approaching while the structure is still forming. THE REPARATION MATERIAL IT PUBLISHES: A DOWNLOADABLE WORK ON IMAGINING REPARATION — DATA, NUMBERS AND ENTITLEMENTS FROM PROTRACTED HABITAT RIGHTS VIOLATIONS. DATA, NUMBERS AND ENTITLEMENTS. Communities are routinely offered a compensation figure with no basis they can check; a published method for costing what was actually lost, over years, is the counter-document. ITS ORIGIN AND STANDING: ORGANISED IN 1976 AS A NONGOVERNMENTAL COUNTERPART TO A UN COMMISSION ON HUMAN SETTLEMENTS, BOTH EMERGING FROM THE FIRST UN HABITAT CONFERENCE — AN INDEPENDENT INTERNATIONAL NONPROFIT COALITION OF ORGANISATIONS AND INDIVIDUALS. Fifty years old and constituted as the civil society counterpart to a UN body. That standing is what lets a member organisation's submission reach a forum a village committee could not enter alone. THE OTHER NETWORKS WITHIN IT: A WOMEN AND HABITAT NETWORK, A LATIN AMERICAN PROGRAMME, AND A SOUTH ASIA REGIONAL PROGRAMME, ALONGSIDE THE HOUSING AND LAND RIGHTS NETWORK. AND THE EVIDENCE FROM ITS OWN EVICTION RESEARCH: FOLLOWING ITS CASE STUDIES, VERY FAVOURABLE ADVANCES OCCURRED IN SEVERAL CASES — IN ONE COUNTRY SOME OF THE MOST NOTORIOUS EVICTION DECREES WERE CANCELED AND THE GOVERNMENT BEGAN CALLING ON THE SOCIAL MOVEMENT AND ITS PARTNER ORGANISATIONS TO PARTICIPATE IN DIALOGUE TO DRAFT NEW HOUSING POLICIES, AND IN SOUTH AFRICA A NEW POLITICAL CONTEXT OPENED FRESH HOPES FOR COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION. Eviction decrees cancelled, and the movement afterwards invited to help draft the replacement policy. That second step is the one worth aiming at: stopping the eviction leaves the rule that permitted it intact. WHO IT SUITS: African community organisations, land committees and settlement associations facing eviction or displacement — as members of a coalition rather than subjects of its research. CAVEATS: A COALITION AND A PRESSURE GROUP, NOT A FUNDER OR A LAW FIRM; MEMBERSHIP MEANS SUBSCRIBING TO A CONSTITUTION, AND ITS STRONGEST AFRICAN PRESENCE IS THE NORTH AFRICA PROGRAMME — sub-Saharan structures are described as emerging. For the development project database that warns before financing, Ethiopia's entry; for filming evidence that links an act to who ordered it, Gambia's entry.

trackers.name: WLSA (Women and Law in Southern Africa) — a regional legal network with separately registered chapters in seven southern African countries — legal advice and legal aid, paralegal trainers at community level, and published objects that include strategic litigation and registration of deeds
trackers.desc: SEVEN COUNTRY CHAPTERS, AND ONE OF THEM REGISTERS DEEDS FOR YOU — method and adjacency declared first: AFTER TWO WITHDRAWALS LAST ROUND, THE PRE-WRITE CHECK NOW RUNS FOUR SIBLING HOSTS AND THE SUBJECT NAME AND ITS ACRONYM ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. ALL FOUR HOSTS ABSENT; THE ACRONYM ABSENT; THE FULL NAME APPEARS ONCE, INSIDE A LESOTHO ENTRY ABOUT THAT COUNTRY'S JUSTICE-MINISTRY LEGAL AID DEPARTMENT, AS A PASSING MENTION ON A DIFFERENT HOST AND ABOUT A DIFFERENT BODY. THIS FILE'S GAMBIA ENTRY COVERS THE WOMEN LAWYERS ASSOCIATION WITH A LITIGATION FUND AND ITS GUINEA ENTRY THE COALITION CHAIRED BY SUCH AN ASSOCIATION. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE SEVEN COUNTRIES, WHICH IS THE FIND: A REGIONAL NETWORK OPERATING IN SEVEN COUNTRIES OF SOUTHERN AFRICA — BOTSWANA, LESOTHO, MALAWI, MOZAMBIQUE, ESWATINI, ZAMBIA AND ZIMBABWE — WITH OFFICES IN EACH, EACH REGISTERED SEPARATELY UNDER ITS OWN COUNTRY'S LAW. Seven national organisations rather than one foreign office with seven addresses. Each is registered locally, which means each survives a government expelling foreign NGOs — the exact vulnerability this file recorded when a regional defenders network was barred from operating in one country. THE PUBLISHED OBJECTS OF ONE CHAPTER, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: TO PROVIDE, OR PROCURE PROVISION BY OTHERS OF, ADVISORY OR COUNSELLING SERVICES TO WOMEN WHOSE LEGAL RIGHTS HAVE BEEN ABUSED; TO CONDUCT TRAINING OF TRAINERS (PARALEGALS) FOR LEGAL RIGHTS, GENDER AND HUMAN RIGHTS EDUCATION AT COMMUNITY LEVEL, AND REFER AND LINK BENEFICIARIES WITH HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS AND LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCIES; AND TO PROVIDE STRATEGIC LITIGATION SERVICES INCLUDING REGISTRATION OF DEEDS. REGISTRATION OF DEEDS, written into the objects of a legal NGO. That is the practical end of everything this file has recorded about tenure: not a campaign about title but the clerical act of getting the document lodged. A widow who cannot register the deed to the ground she farms loses it, and this is an organisation whose stated job includes doing that registration. PROCURE PROVISION BY OTHERS is worth noticing too: where the chapter cannot act itself, its object is to find someone who can — a referral duty rather than a polite refusal. TRAINING OF TRAINERS at community level means the paralegals it trains go on to train more. A community organisation that sends two people can end up with its own capacity rather than a dependency. WHAT ITS WORK CONSISTS OF: QUESTIONING AND CHALLENGING THE LAW, INSTIGATING CAMPAIGNS FOR CHANGES IN LAWS, POLICIES AND PLANS OF ACTION, EDUCATING WOMEN AND GIRLS ABOUT THEIR RIGHTS, PROVIDING LEGAL ADVICE, AND GENDER SENSITIZING COMMUNITIES AND LEADERSHIP. GENDER SENSITIZING LEADERSHIP — chiefs and councillors, the people who actually allocate land in most of the situations recorded here. THE LAND ARGUMENT ONE CHAPTER MAKES: SINCE LAND IS STILL THE PRIMARY SOURCE OF WEALTH AND LIVELIHOOD, IT HAS HIGHLIGHTED THE SIGNIFICANT LEGAL, SOCIAL AND POLITICAL PROBLEMS CAUSED BY GENDER INEQUALITIES IN ACCESSING LAND — DEMANDING REMEDIAL LEGAL REFORMS, DEVELOPING CITIZENS' LEGAL AWARENESS, AND SUPPORTING WOMEN'S STRUGGLE TO SECURE LAND RIGHTS. WHAT IT IS FIGHTING, NAMED PLAINLY: DISCRIMINATION, INEQUALITIES AND GENDER VIOLENCE MAINLY RESULTING FROM THE PERSISTENCE OF CUSTOMARY LAWS AND PRACTICES WHICH SOMETIMES JEOPARDISE WOMEN. THE POSITION IT TAKES ON CUSTOMARY LAW: ITS RESEARCH INVESTIGATES BOTH CUSTOMARY LAW AND GENERAL LAW AND THE INTERACTION BETWEEN THE TWO — TAKING THE PERSPECTIVE THAT THE OFFICIAL CUSTOMARY LAW OF SOUTHERN AFRICAN STATES IS A RIGID AND SKEWED VERSION OF WHAT IS PRACTISED. The distinction is usable in an actual dispute. What a court applies as customary law may not be what the community practises — so a woman told that custom bars her can argue that the OFFICIAL version has been hardened against her, and there is a body of research behind that argument. HOW THE RESEARCH IS STAFFED, WHICH IS UNUSUAL: TEAMS OF 6–8 PERSONS IN EACH COUNTRY, TWO EMPLOYED FULL TIME AND THE OTHERS EMPLOYED ELSEWHERE IN RELATED JOBS DOING THE RESEARCH PART-TIME — DESIGNED SO THAT FINDINGS ARE IMMEDIATELY INCORPORATED IN THE WORK OF THE RESEARCHERS. The part-time researchers work inside ministries, courts and universities, and carry the findings back there. That is a deliberate design for getting research used rather than shelved, and it is cheap enough for any national organisation to copy. WHAT ACTION RESEARCH MEANS HERE: WE INFORM, ADVISE AND TAKE ACTION DURING THE RESEARCH — RESEARCH INTENDED TO INFORM AND INFLUENCE ACTION BEING TAKEN. Advice given while the study is running, not after it publishes. A community that agrees to be researched here gets something back during the work. THE SUBJECTS IT HAS RESEARCHED IN SEQUENCE: MAINTENANCE LAW; INHERITANCE LAW; FAMILY AND THE LEGAL STATUS OF WOMEN IN THE FAMILY; THE ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE; AND DELIVERY PROBLEMS AND CONSTRAINTS. Decades of published work on inheritance across seven countries — which is where most individual land loss in this file actually happens, at a death rather than at a concession. WHO FOUNDED IT AND WHEN: SET UP IN 1989 BY FEMALE LECTURERS IN SOUTHERN AFRICAN UNIVERSITIES — ACADEMICS, GENDER ACTIVISTS AND RESEARCHERS — TO RESPOND TO THE SOCIO-LEGAL NEEDS OF WOMEN IN THE REGION; ESTABLISHED AS A RESEARCH AND EDUCATION TRUST IN JUNE 1998 WITH A SEVENTH MEMBER COUNTRY ADDED. Founded by African university staff, from inside the region. Another model requiring no foreign founder, alongside the lawyers' association recorded in this file's Gambia entry. AND THE CONTINENTAL COALITION TWO CHAPTERS BELONG TO: A COALITION ON A CONTINENTAL WOMEN'S RIGHTS PROTOCOL, WHOSE RATIFICATION AND ADVOCACY MISSION IN JUNE 2025 WAS FOLLOWED BY A NAMED STATE DEPOSITING ITS INSTRUMENT OF RATIFICATION IN JULY 2025, BECOMING THE 46TH MEMBER STATE TO DO SO. A ratification mission in June, an instrument deposited in July. Recorded because this file rarely gets to show advocacy and result a month apart — and because the protocol, once ratified, is law a national court can be asked to apply. WHO IT SUITS: women and communities in the seven named southern African countries facing inheritance, customary-law or land-registration problems, and organisations wanting paralegal trainers. CAVEATS: SEVEN COUNTRIES ONLY, AND ITS FRAME IS WOMEN'S AND CHILDREN'S RIGHTS RATHER THAN COMMUNITY OPPOSITION TO A PROJECT; CHAPTERS DIFFER IN CAPACITY AND IN WHAT THEY OFFER — DEED REGISTRATION IS ONE CHAPTER'S PUBLISHED OBJECT, NOT A NETWORK-WIDE SERVICE. Approach the chapter in your own country. For the association with a fund that pays filing fees, Gambia's entry; for the campaign whose coalitions such bodies chair, Guinea's entry.

trackers.name: SCAT (Social Change Assistance Trust), Cape Town — core grants that pay a rural advice office's running costs so its doors stay open, plus a Fundraising Incentive Scheme that rewards money the community raises itself
trackers.desc: THEY PAY THE RENT SO THE ADVICE OFFICE STAYS OPEN — AND MATCH WHAT YOU RAISE YOURSELF — method declared first: THE WORD-BOUNDARY PROBE RAN ONE HOST AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; THE HOST AND ALL SIX FACTS ABSENT. THE FUNDRAISING INCENTIVE SCHEME, WHICH IS THE FIND: ONE OF ITS THREE GRANT TYPES IS A REWARD FOR LOCAL FUNDRAISING — AN INCENTIVE TO ENCOURAGE COMMUNITY-DRIVEN PHILANTHROPY, ALONGSIDE CORE GRANTS AND A DEVELOPMENT FUND FOR TRAINING, WITH MICRO GRANTS AND SPECIAL PROJECT FUNDS ALSO OFFERED. A funder that pays you MORE for money you raised locally. Every other fund in this file asks what you need; this one also asks what you gathered yourself, and rewards it. For a community with a collection tin and no grant history, the tin is now worth more than its contents. WHAT THE CORE GRANT PAYS FOR, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: CORE FUNDS AS A CONTRIBUTION TO THE RUNNING COSTS OF THE LOCAL ORGANISATION — A SMALL CORE GRANT COVERING THE RUNNING COSTS OF AN ADVICE OFFICE SO THE DOORS REMAIN OPEN. RUNNING COSTS, not project costs. This is the gap this file has recorded again and again — organisations that can win money for activities and none for rent, electricity or a phone line. An office that stays open is what a community actually needs from a funder. WHO ITS PARTNERS ARE AND HOW THEY ARE GOVERNED: RURAL COMMUNITY-OWNED DEVELOPMENT ORGANISATIONS IT CALLS LOCAL DEVELOPMENT AGENCIES, MANAGED BY ELECTED MEMBERS OF THE COMMUNITIES THEY SERVE, HELD STRINGENTLY ACCOUNTABLE THROUGH THEIR CONSTITUTION AND ANNUAL GENERAL MEETINGS, WITH COMMITTEE MEMBERS ELECTED AT THAT MEETING. COMMUNITY-OWNED and elected, with accountability running to the village rather than to the funder. That is the governance shape this file records under Malawi's membership movement and Senegal's residents' federation, here as a funding requirement. THE PARALEGAL WORK IT KEEPS ALIVE, WHICH IS THE THIRD FIND: A LONG TRACK RECORD OF FUNDING COMMUNITY-BASED ADVICE OFFICES THAT PROVIDE A PARALEGAL SERVICE WHERE ACCESS TO INFORMATION IS LIMITED AND SERVICE DELIVERY IS POOR — WORKING WITH TWO NAMED NATIONAL ADVICE-OFFICE BODIES TO PROMOTE THE ACCESS TO JUSTICE AGENDA AT THE HIGHEST LEVELS IN GOVERNMENT. This is the funder behind the paralegal layer. This file's Benin entry records the published rule on when a paralegal must escalate a land case; its Central African Republic entry the clinics themselves. Here is who keeps the lights on in the office where that paralegal sits. THE PROBLEM IT NAMES ABOUT THOSE PARALEGALS: IN THIS COUNTRY PARALEGALS ARE OFTEN THE POOR HELPING THE POOR, AND LACK OF FUNDING AND A SUSTAINABLE SOURCE OF INCOME MEANS THEY ARE NOT ADEQUATELY REWARDED FOR THE SERVICE THEY PROVIDE. Said plainly by the funder itself. A community relying on a volunteer paralegal should understand that the person helping them is usually as poor as they are, and that the service is fragile for that reason. WHY IT EXISTS AS AN INTERMEDIARY: IT RAISES FUNDS FROM CORPORATE, GOVERNMENT AND CIVIL SOCIETY FUNDERS WHO SUPPORT SUCH WORK BUT DO NOT HAVE OR WISH TO CREATE THE INFRASTRUCTURE NECESSARY TO MONITOR AND SUPPORT SMALL AND REMOTE INITIATIVES. The honest description of why intermediaries exist: big funders cannot administer small remote grants. A village organisation too small for a direct grant is exactly this body's client. THE FIELD SUPPORT IT SENDS: AN ON-SITE PROGRAMMES TEAM PROVIDING MONITORING, MENTORING AND COACHING FOR THE STAFF AND COMMITTEE OF THE LOCAL AGENCIES. THE TRAINING IT ATTACHES: GOVERNANCE, LOCAL ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, ACCESS TO JUSTICE, LOCAL FUNDRAISING, DEVELOPING PARTNERSHIPS WITH LOCAL AND PROVINCIAL GOVERNMENT, AND ORGANISATIONAL SUSTAINABILITY. LOCAL FUNDRAISING is taught, not just rewarded — which is what makes the incentive scheme reachable rather than decorative. THE TERMS: PARTNERS MUST MEET A SET OF CRITERIA TO QUALIFY, THEN MEET REPORTING AND ACCOUNTABILITY REQUIREMENTS, AND MUST RE-APPLY ANNUALLY — WITH CONTINUATION DEPENDING ON PRESENTATION OF AN ANNUAL REPORT AND AUDITED ANNUAL FINANCIAL STATEMENTS AT AN ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING. AUDITED STATEMENTS EVERY YEAR is a real cost and a real barrier. Budget for the auditor before applying, and note that the training offered covers exactly this. WHAT IT HAS MOVED AND TO HOW MANY: AROUND 50 MILLION RAND RAISED OVER FIVE YEARS, WITH 175 ORGANISATIONS RECEIVING GRANTS AND SUPPORT. WHERE IT WORKS AND SINCE WHEN: ESTABLISHED IN NOVEMBER 1984 BY THREE NAMED TRUSTEES TO CHANNEL FUNDS TO RURAL COMMUNITIES WITH LIMITED ACCESS TO RESOURCES, OPERATING IN FOUR NAMED PROVINCES FROM A PUBLISHED STREET ADDRESS. AND A DOCUMENTED OUTCOME: ONE PARTNER WAS ASSISTED TO FORMALISE ITS OPERATIONS BY EMPLOYING FULL-TIME STAFF AND ACQUIRING PREMISES AND OFFICE EQUIPMENT. ACQUIRING PREMISES. A community organisation that ends up owning its own building is harder to close than one that rents, and this is a funder whose record includes getting one there. WHO IT SUITS: rural community-owned organisations that need rent and salaries covered rather than project money, and any group already raising something locally that wants it matched. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY AND FOUR PROVINCES WITHIN IT; PARTNERS MUST BE COMMUNITY-OWNED AND ELECTED, RE-APPLY ANNUALLY AND PRODUCE AUDITED ACCOUNTS; ITS THEMES ARE ACCESS TO JUSTICE, GENDER EQUALITY, LOCAL ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND YOUTH RATHER THAN LAND OR ENVIRONMENT AS SUCH. For a fund open to unregistered groups with activists deciding, South Africa's EJF entry; for building a permanent endowment instead, Equatorial Guinea's entry.

trackers.name: Seinoli Legal Centre (SLC)
trackers.desc: Lesotho’s first public-interest legal centre (est. 2010) — provides free legal services and strategic litigation for communities affected by large development projects (the Lesotho Highlands Water Project dams, mining, agribusiness), operates a toll-free grievance line, and combines litigation, advocacy and community capacity-building to secure compensation, relocation and access to justice.

trackers.name: Southern Africa Litigation Centre (SALC)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional litigation centre supporting and co-counselling cases across Angola, Botswana, DR Congo, Eswatini, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe. Its socio-economic rights work challenges large-scale agricultural and extractive land use that dispossesses customary landholders without adequate consent, consultation or compensation, and covers mining, pollution and climate justice — live matters include a Zambian community's pollution claim against copper processors and San and Bayei claims to ancestral land in Botswana. WHO IT SUITS: in-country lawyers and community organisations who need a partner with regional capacity and resources; SALC generally works through local counsel and partners rather than taking clients directly. SALC RESOURCES A LAWYER — IT DOES NOT REPLACE ONE. It provides technical and monetary support to local and regional lawyers and organisations litigating human rights and rule of law cases, working primarily through strategic litigation and capacity-strengthening support to lawyers and grassroots organisations. So the ask is not ‘please take my case’ but ‘please back my lawyer’ — come with a local lawyer or local organisation. It also trains human rights lawyers and facilitates networks across the region, so it is a route to finding counsel too. THE SECOND FORUM MOST PEOPLE MISS: SALC supports litigation in South African courts that advances human rights in the southern African region — so where your own courts are slow, captured or hostile, there may be another venue, and SALC is the body that supports using it. NAME THE RIGHT CLUSTER WHEN YOU APPROACH: its themes are criminal justice, civil and political rights, socio-economic rights, international criminal justice, business and human rights and equality rights — ‘environment’ is not one of them, so frame a land-defence case as business and human rights or socio-economic rights. Established 2005 in Johannesburg out of the International Bar Association and OSISA. It has also run open calls for small organisational development grants to emerging CBOs in Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe — periodic, so watch for them.

trackers.name: Office of the Auditor General
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of Lesotho. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Lesotho.

trackers.name: Lesotho — One-Stop Business Facilitation Centre (Registrar of Companies)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the Registrar of Companies (Ministry of Trade & Industry) runs an online companies register with free public company search, Lesotho. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Office of the Auditor General
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Lesotho, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: MNN Centre for Investigative Journalism
trackers.desc: Lesotho's investigative newsroom exposing corruption and misuse of public resources.

trackers.name: LesothoLII
trackers.desc: Lesotho Legal Information Institute: free case law and legislation (AfricanLII network). · Find here: free Lesotho judgments and legislation (LesothoLII / Laws.Africa).

trackers.name: Directorate on Corruption and Economic Offences (DCEO)
trackers.desc: National anti-corruption body of Lesotho — investigates graft, financial crime and abuse of public office.

trackers.name: Compensation over 50 years when the Land Act gives 99 — the argument to make
trackers.desc: THE STRONGEST FORM OF COMPENSATION CHALLENGE, AND IT TURNS ON A PERIOD RATHER THAN AN AMOUNT. Communities affected by the Lesotho Highlands Water Project rejected their scheme because compensation was calculated over 50 years while the Land Act 2010 gives a right to use the land for 99 years — on that basis they called the 50-year plan baseless. Not ‘the amount is too low’ but ‘the period used to calculate it is shorter than the tenure the statute gives me’. The rate was attacked the same way: 86 cents per square metre, described as arbitrarily decided with no basis compared to the actual harvest from the fields. AND LATE PAYMENT IS A BREACH, NOT A DELAY: the LHDA Order of 1986 imposes the primary duty to ensure the standard of living of affected communities does not deteriorate but is maintained or improved, and read with the Land Act it provides for prompt compensation even before entry into the property. ‘Before entry’ is the test — so record the date the project entered and the date any money arrived.

trackers.name: One appeal opened a queue — check whether your second tranche was ever paid
trackers.desc: A PRECEDENT THAT OTHERS IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWED. After a landmark Court of Appeal ruling, the LHDA missed a court-set deadline to pay compensation to communities affected by the Katse Dam — and 21 community associations lodged fresh compensation demands on the back of it. THE STRUCTURE OF THE CLAIM IS THE LESSON: 22 associations downstream of Katse were affected by Phase I; they received initial compensation in 2003 covering a 10-year pilot phase, with a second tranche due in 2013 covering the remaining 40 years of a 50-year lease period — and LHDA failed to pay, triggering over a decade of disputes. If your compensation was structured as a pilot tranche with a later instalment, check whether that instalment was ever paid: a decade-old unpaid tranche proved recoverable, and others in the same position followed. Sums ranged from M500,000 to M3 million, the winning society having received about M2.7 million initially. TWO MORE LEVERS: Phase II rates are adjusted annually by the Lesotho CPI, dwellings compensated at replacement cost, urban valuations certified by the LAA, and a land-for-land option exists; and financing involves the African Development Bank with Standard Bank as an Equator Principles institution, so bank-level grievance mechanisms are a second route. RECORDED HONESTLY: communities report formal complaints unanswered, grievance systems inaccessible, and defenders facing threats and intimidation. NOTE ALSO section 16 of the Land Act: rural landowners may apply for a lease but are not required to register, and Community Councils keep allocation records manually and in silos — get a certified copy of your council's allocation record now, because it may be the only proof and it exists in one place.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: Transformation Resource Centre — field workers living with the dam-affected communities, and it is already working the Polihali phase
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Lesotho NGO that has worked the country's biggest displacement file — the Lesotho Highlands Water Project — for decades, and stations field workers in the affected areas rather than visiting from Maseru: two were posted at Mohale and Ratau to follow resettlement, compensation and development day to day. It helped affected residents put their complaints to the development authority, supported the marches that followed, and worked alongside the community's own body, the Survivors of the Lesotho Dams. Outcomes attributed to that pressure include the compensation period being extended to fifty years and delayed communal compensation being released. IT IS ALREADY ON THE NEXT DAM, WHICH IS THE POINT FOR ANYONE FACING ONE: its Polihali Liaison Community Participation programme works with communities affected by Phase 2 construction, on compensation and resettlement, and investigates whether the social impact assessments the developers commissioned are actually being fulfilled — comparing the promises in the assessment against what is delivered is a documentary exercise a community can start immediately. WHAT ITS RECORD TEACHES ABOUT COMPENSATION, and it is the lesson to carry into any negotiation: TRC's finding was that cash compensation arrives late and only covers debts, that people had been feeding themselves from land before resettlement, and that no land-for-land was offered — so argue for replacement land and for water supply in the resettlement site, not for a figure. TRC publishes its documentation, including a book-length account of the lessons of the project. WHO IT SUITS: Basotho communities facing dam construction, resettlement or downstream flow loss. CAVEATS: TRC is a research, documentation and community-organising body — for litigation Lesotho already has the Seinoli Legal Centre, which acts for dam-affected communities. Its published contact detail is dated, and reported intimidation of people attending dam-affected peoples' meetings is part of the context.

trackers.name: Lesotho's Legal Aid department — 17 lawyers for the whole country, travelling to district courts on scheduled dates, now opening decentralised offices
trackers.desc: WHERE TO GET A FREE LAWYER, AND THE CONSTRAINT STATED FIRST: the Legal Aid department, established by the Legal Aid Act of 1978 and mandated to provide legal REPRESENTATION to indigent Basotho, is one of four departments in the justice ministry. It has A TOTAL OF 17 LAWYERS, and the office is based only in MASERU. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE IS THE THING TO PLAN AROUND: the department's lawyers TRAVEL TO THE DISTRICTS ON SCHEDULED DATES to represent clients in the district courts — so the question is not whether legal aid exists near you, it is WHEN THE CIRCUIT NEXT REACHES YOUR DISTRICT. Find that date and build your case around it. WHAT IS CHANGING: government has begun launching DECENTRALISED LEGAL AID OFFICES in the districts, with one opened at Melele Ground in Qacha's Nek with European Union support, aimed explicitly at vulnerable and remote communities — the elderly, children, people with disabilities and unemployed people in remote areas. The ministry frames this as a constitutional obligation: Lesotho's Bill of Rights covers access to justice, fair hearing and legal representation, and the state says it has a responsibility to provide legal aid nationally. Civil society was present at the launch through WILSA (Women and Law in Southern Africa), whose representative described the office as restoring hope to people who had felt forgotten. Ask whether a decentralised office has opened in your district before assuming you must reach Maseru. WHO IT SUITS: indigent Basotho needing representation in a district court, including in land, inheritance and eviction matters. CAVEATS: SEVERELY UNDER-RESOURCED — 17 lawyers nationally, a Maseru base and a travelling circuit mean delay is structural, not personal; it is a state department and will not act against government policy. For dam-affected communities and the financier-complaint route, Lesotho's TRC entry; for litigation, Seinoli Legal Centre.

trackers.name: Lesotho's dam community associations — the Court of Appeal ordered the second compensation tranche paid, and 21 more associations then filed
trackers.desc: THE MONEY A COURT HAS ORDERED, AND THE VEHICLE THAT CLAIMED IT: villages downstream of the Katse Dam are organised as REGISTERED COMMUNITY ASSOCIATIONS, and one of them — the Ukhopo-Maliba-Matšo Society at Bobete, Thaba-Tseka — took the Lesotho Highlands Development Authority to court and won. On 7 November the Court of Appeal dismissed the LHDA's challenge and upheld a High Court order compelling payment to MORE THAN 600 VILLAGERS, giving the authority 90 DAYS to pay. THE RULING IS THE PART TO CARRY ANYWHERE: the Chief Justice held that the authority CANNOT RELY ON INTERNAL POLICIES OR CONSULTANTS’ TECHNICAL REPORTS TO OVERRIDE ITS CONSTITUTIONAL AND STATUTORY DUTY TO COMPENSATE, that the duty arises from the Constitution, the Treaty and the LHDA Order, and IS NOT A MATTER OF BUREAUCRATIC DISCRETION — and it condemned the failure to consult villagers before unilaterally stopping payment in 2013. If an authority tells you its own policy or a consultant's report has ended your entitlement, that is the finding to put in front of it. THE ARITHMETIC, WHICH EVERY AFFECTED ASSOCIATION SHOULD DO: compensation is based on a 50-YEAR LEASE; associations received an initial tranche in 2003/4 covering a ten-year pilot period, and A SECOND TRANCHE WAS DUE IN 2013 TO COVER THE REMAINING 40 YEARS. Bobete's society had received about M2.7 million for the initial period; other associations were paid between M500,000 and M3 million. WHAT FOLLOWED, AND WHY YOU SHOULD NOT WAIT: after the ruling, 21 further community associations lodged fresh compensation demands, out of 22 representing villages downstream of Katse; separately more than 3,000 individuals and 889 registered businesses have brought a constitutional case alleging unpaid compensation, sums as low as 78 cents per square metre paid years after expropriation, and the failure ever to establish the promised community development fund. The LHDA missed the Court-set deadline. WHO IT SUITS: Basotho villages affected by Katse, Mohale or Polihali, and communities anywhere whose second-tranche or long-term compensation has quietly stopped. CAVEATS: THIS IS LITIGATION, NOT A GRANT WINDOW — it required an advocate and years; the promised community development fund was never established, so do not count on it. For litigation, Lesotho's Seinoli Legal Centre entry; for field-level accompaniment, the TRC entry; for the free-lawyer circuit, the Legal Aid department.

trackers.name: Lesotho's community councils and grazing associations — the council allocates land and controls grazing; only 20% of households hold a registered lease and 39% hold nothing
trackers.desc: WHO ALLOCATES YOUR LAND AND WHAT YOU HOLD: in Lesotho the COMMUNITY COUNCIL is the allocating authority, and its statutory functions include LAND ALLOCATION, GRAZING CONTROL, NATURAL RESOURCE CONTROL, POLLUTION AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONSERVATION, BURIAL GROUNDS and AREA ECONOMIC PLANNING. One elected body near you holds allocation, grazing and natural-resource control together — which means a single council decision can open or close a piece of ground, and the council is therefore the first door, not the ministry. WHAT YOU PROBABLY HOLD, IN NUMBERS: the 2016 census records 20% of households with REGISTERED LEASEHOLDS, 41% with only UNREGISTERED CERTIFICATES OF ALLOCATION, and 39% WITH NEITHER; registered and unregistered parcels alike are predominantly non-agricultural, so extensive cropland and COMMUNAL PASTURE is not formally registered at all. Find out which of the three you are in before a project arrives: a certificate of allocation is not a lease, and 39% of households have no paper whatsoever. Under section 16 of the LAND ACT 2010 an allottee of residential land in a rural area MAY APPLY TO THE COMMISSIONER FOR A LEASE — the lease being the strongest form of title, issued by the national land administration authority — but for non-commercial rural land registration is OPTIONAL, which is why so few register. Councils record allocations MANUALLY and work in silos, with no integration between allocating authorities and the national registry. If your allocation exists only in a council ledger, get a certified copy now; that ledger is the only evidence you have. THE VEHICLE FOR PASTURE, AND THE LIMIT ON IT: Lesotho has a documented history of GRAZING ASSOCIATIONS as the community form for range management — but note that PRINCIPAL CHIEFS, NOT COMMUNITY COUNCILS, are in charge of range management and CATTLE POSTS, and that ALL NATURAL RESOURCES BELONG TO THE STATE and a MINING LEASE DOES NOT REQUIRE A LAND LEASE FIRST. That last rule is the one to plan around: a mining lease can be granted over ground you hold without your lease being touched — so registration protects your occupation, not the minerals under it. WHO IT SUITS: Basotho households and villages wanting to know what they hold, register it, or organise pasture. CAVEATS: ALLOCATION AND LEASEHOLD, NOT FREEHOLD — and the council-to-registry gap is a real risk of loss. For dam-affected communities and the second compensation tranche, Lesotho's community associations entry; for litigation, Seinoli; for the travelling legal-aid circuit, the Legal Aid department entry.

trackers.name: Lesotho's environmental organisations — LEJAC, PELUM, GEM, ESNEL, TED and Advision working as a bloc, under the LCN umbrella that nominates civil society to national bodies
trackers.desc: THE EIGHT THAT WORK TOGETHER, WHICH IS HOW A SMALL COUNTRY'S CIVIL SOCIETY ACTUALLY MOVES: a Lesotho coalition names the organisations working jointly on environment and justice — the LESOTHO ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE AND ADVOCACY CENTRE (LEJAC); PARTICIPATORY ECOLOGICAL LAND USE MANAGEMENT (PELUM) LESOTHO; the GEOGRAPHY AND ENVIRONMENT MOVEMENT (GEM); the ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY NETWORK OF LESOTHO (ESNEL); TECHNOLOGIES FOR ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT (TED); ADVISION LESOTHO; the LESOTHO COUNCIL OF NGOs (LCN); and this file's TRANSFORMATION RESOURCE CENTRE, convened alongside a Catholic justice and peace commission at P.O. Box 200, Maseru 100, tel +266-22324263. Eight organisations that already appear on the same list are eight signatures on the same letter — in a country this size that is most of the sector, and approaching the coalition is faster than approaching them one by one. WHAT LEJAC DOES, AND THE DETAIL THAT MATTERS: it takes A HUMAN RIGHTS APPROACH TO ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES, and in doing so ADDRESSES BREAD-AND-BUTTER ISSUES IN THE LOCAL COMMUNITIES IT SERVES, alongside environmental education work. An environmental organisation that handles bread-and-butter questions is one that will still be there between crises — that is the kind to build a relationship with before you need it. And PELUM is the land-use member: for grazing, cropping and rangeland questions, start there. THE UMBRELLA AND HOW IT IS BUILT: the LESOTHO COUNCIL OF NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS (LCN, lcn.org.ls / lecongo.org.ls), ESTABLISHED MAY 1990, coordinates and supports civil society nationwide through networking, leadership training, information dissemination, capacity building, coordination, ADVOCACY AND REPRESENTATION WHEN DEALING WITH THE GOVERNMENT AND THE INTERNATIONAL COMMUNITY. Its structure: an ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING elects a NINE-MEMBER BOARD OF DIRECTORS, supported by NAMED COMMISSIONS — including a WOMEN AND CHILDREN COMMISSION and an ECONOMIC JUSTICE COMMISSION — and a National Secretariat headed by an Executive Director; it is based at House No. 544, Hoohlo, Maseru, runs an ANNUAL NGO WEEK, and belongs to a regional climate action network and the SADC council of NGOs. THE FUNCTION WORTH USING: LCN FACILITATES SECTORAL REPRESENTATION BY NOMINATING CANDIDATES FOR NATIONAL BODIES, so that community interests sit inside governance processes. If a national body is being formed that will decide something affecting your area, LCN is who nominates the civil society seat. Ask to be put forward, and go to NGO Week where the sector is in one room. WHO IT SUITS: Basotho communities facing rangeland loss, dam impacts or a development project, and local groups seeking a bloc. CAVEATS: MEMBERSHIP AND ADVOCACY BODIES, NOT FUNDERS OR LAW FIRMS. For field workers who live with the displaced, Lesotho's Transformation Resource Centre entry; for the dam-affected associations and the Court of Appeal costs order, the community associations entry; for 17 lawyers nationwide, the Legal Aid entry; for statutory land allocation and grazing control, the community councils entry.

trackers.name: LEJAC's Pro-Poor Property Development project, Serumula's community botanical garden, and the LCN grant window — Lesotho organisations working on land people own but cannot develop
trackers.desc: THE PROGRAMME FOR PEOPLE WHO OWN LAND AND CANNOT DEVELOP IT — which is the exact situation in which land gets lost to a developer, and a Lesotho organisation names it as a programme: LEJAC IS RUNNING PROJECTS ON PRO-POOR PROPERTY DEVELOPMENT, WHICH SEEKS TO PROTECT AND ENFORCE THE LAND RIGHTS OF POOR PEOPLE WHO POSSESS LAND BUT LACK THE REQUISITE RESOURCES TO DEVELOP THEIR LAND, alongside a named STREAM AND VALLEY ENVIRONMENTAL REHABILITATION PROJECT TO RESTORE THE NATURAL ECOSYSTEM OF THE AREA, and it takes A HUMAN RIGHTS APPROACH TO ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES, ADDRESSING BREAD-AND-BUTTER ISSUES IN THE LOCAL COMMUNITIES IT SERVES. Owning land you cannot afford to develop is how families are talked into selling. An organisation whose stated project is protecting exactly those owners is the first call before you sign anything — ask LEJAC what pro-poor property development means for your plot. LEJAC IS ALSO LEADING THE FORMATION OF A CLUSTER TO COORDINATE LESOTHO CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS WORKING ON CLIMATE CHANGE, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE LESOTHO COUNCIL OF NGOs AND PELUM. THE COMMUNITY MODEL AND THE FINDING BEHIND IT: SERUMULA DEVELOPMENT ASSOCIATION, A LOCAL NGO, RUNS A COMMUNITY-BASED ENVIRONMENTAL RESOURCES CONSERVATION PROGRAMME — THE TŠENEKENG BOTANICAL GARDEN AT SEMONKONG — and the assessment of it sets out the contrast plainly: MANY GOVERNMENT CONSERVATION PROGRAMMES HAVE FOLLOWED AN AUTOCRATIC APPROACH THAT IMPOSES PROJECTS ON THE COMMUNITY, WHILE NGOs ARE COMPLIMENTED FOR INCLUDING THE AFFECTED COMMUNITIES IN THE DECISION-MAKING PROCESS THROUGH DIFFERENT PARTICIPATORY METHODS. A botanical garden is the answer to a specific Lesotho problem: medicinal plants harvested from communal land for sale until they are depleted. Growing the plant is what stops the digging of it — if your commonage is being stripped of a species people sell, propagating it is the intervention, not policing. THE OTHER NAMED BODIES, WITH THEIR PLACES: RURAL SELF-HELP DEVELOPMENT ASSOCIATION, based in MASERU, HAS BEEN IMPLEMENTING THE SUSTAINABLE LAND USE PROGRAMME AND OTHER RELEVANT ACTIVITIES IN MAFETENG AND MOHALE'S HOEK DISTRICTS; BETHEL BUSINESS AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT CENTRE (BBCDC), BASED AT MT MOOROSI, WORKING ON SOLAR ENERGY AND SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE AND OFFERING TRAINING COURSES; and an international NGO's country office in Maseru has been involved in a HIGHLANDS COMMUNITY FORESTRY PROJECT NEAR A NAMED DAM. A community forestry project beside a major dam is the precedent to cite if a dam is what threatens you: the offset work already exists in Lesotho, so ask which organisation held it and on what terms. AND THE MONEY: THE LESOTHO COUNCIL OF NGOs IS THE UMBRELLA BODY, BASED IN MASERU, PROVIDING INFORMATION ON ENVIRONMENTAL NGOs — AND IT RECEIVED A GRANT OF EUR 4.5 MILLION TO INCREASE ITS INSTITUTIONAL AND COORDINATION CAPACITY, WHICH ALSO PROVIDES SUPPORT TO OTHER ORGANISATIONS THROUGH FUNDS ALLOCATED UNDER A CALL FOR PROPOSALS — with the stated rationale that LCN'S MAIN AGENDA IS TO EMPOWER ITS MEMBERS, IN PARTICULAR THOSE IN THE DISTRICTS. An umbrella that re-grants to its members through a call for proposals is a funding window disguised as a coordination body. If you are a district CBO, ask LCN when its next call opens — empowering members in the districts is written into why it was funded. WHO IT SUITS: Basotho landholders who cannot develop, commonage communities losing medicinal plants, and district CBOs seeking funds. CAVEATS: SMALL NGOs on donor cycles. For six named organisations under the LCN umbrella and its nomination power to national bodies, Lesotho's LEJAC and LCN entry.

trackers.name: Fully funded security, digital and wellbeing support whose only two published conditions are being purpose-led and having community impact — a loose collective qualifies, with a free one-hour consultation and a protocol in 27 languages
trackers.desc: A LOOSE COLLECTIVE QUALIFIES. THAT IS THE WHOLE TEST — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S LIBYA ENTRY COVERS THE TWO-HOUR DIGITAL SECURITY HELPLINE, ITS EQUATORIAL GUINEA ENTRY THE PROTECTION GRANTS AND A PROTECTIVE ACCOMPANIMENT HOST, AND ITS BENIN AND MOROCCO ENTRIES THE DEFENDER HELPLINE AND PROTECTION CLUSTER. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE TWO ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA, WHICH ARE THE FIND: FULLY-FUNDED HOLISTIC SECURITY SUPPORT TO A WIDE RANGE OF PEOPLE AND ORGANISATIONS AT RISK. YOU MIGHT BE A DEFENDER, ACTIVIST, OR JOURNALIST. OR YOU COULD BE PART OF A COMMUNITY GROUP, LOOSE COLLECTIVE, OR FORMAL NGO. ALL WE ASK IS THAT YOU MEET THE FOLLOWING CRITERIA: PURPOSE-LED — WORKS TOWARDS POSITIVE SOCIAL, POLITICAL, OR ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE; AND COMMUNITY IMPACT — CREATES CHANGE THAT EXTENDS BEYOND THE INDIVIDUAL OR ORGANISATION TO A WIDER COMMUNITY, MOVEMENT, OR CAUSE. LOOSE COLLECTIVE, named as eligible. No registration, no constitution, no bank account, no audit — two conditions any village committee resisting a project already meets. The protection grants filed under Equatorial Guinea require a registered organisation; this door does not, and that is the single most important difference between them. THE FUNDING CONDITION IT NAMES: IT PROVIDES FUNDED SUPPORT TO RIGHTS-BASED CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, COLLECTIVES AND DEFENDERS WORKING IN THE GLOBAL SOUTH THAT CANNOT OTHERWISE FUND THIS SUPPORT. Inability to pay is the qualifying condition, not a disqualifier. THE FREE CONSULTATION: AT-RISK DEFENDERS CAN BOOK A FREE ONE-HOUR PHONE CONSULTATION WITH ONE OF THE TEAM, TO DISCUSS A SAFETY AND SECURITY, DIGITAL SECURITY, OR WELLBEING AND RESILIENCE CONCERN. An hour with a specialist, bookable, costing nothing. This file has recorded communities carrying a threat for months without ever putting it to somebody who assesses threats for a living. THE THREE STREAMS AND THE LANGUAGES EACH IS DELIVERED IN, WHICH DECIDE WHAT YOU CAN ACTUALLY GET: SAFETY AND SECURITY IN ENGLISH, SPANISH, FRENCH, PORTUGUESE AND ARABIC; DIGITAL SECURITY IN ENGLISH, SPANISH AND PORTUGUESE; AND WELLBEING AND RESILIENCE IN ENGLISH, SPANISH, FRENCH, ARABIC AND GERMAN. Note the gap: digital security is NOT offered in French or Arabic here. Francophone and North African groups should take safety and wellbeing from this organisation and digital security from the two-hour helpline filed under Libya, which covers both languages. WHAT PROTECTION AND SECURITY COVERS: PERSONAL SAFETY, HOME AND OFFICE SECURITY, ORGANISATIONAL SECURITY, TRAVEL SECURITY, COLLECTIVE PROTECTION, AND PARTNER SECURITY. PARTNER SECURITY — the risk your allies inherit from working with you. A national organisation that takes a village's case can be targeted through it, and vice versa; almost nobody plans for that direction of harm. THE PROTOCOL AND ITS HANDBOOK: A HOLISTIC SECURITY PROTOCOL FOR HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS — AVAILABLE IN 21 AND LATER 27 LANGUAGES, WITH AN ACCOMPANYING HANDBOOK OFFERING EXTENSIVE GUIDANCE, EXERCISES AND TEMPLATES TO HELP DEFENDERS IMPLEMENT THE 21 HOLISTIC SECURITY MEASURES AND ADAPT THEM TO THEIR SITUATION, WORK AND PROFILE. Twenty-one numbered measures with exercises and templates, free. A committee can work through them at its own meetings without anyone visiting — and the language count has grown, so check for yours even if it was absent before. WHO THE PROTOCOL WAS BUILT WITH: BASED ON EXPERIENCES WORKING WITH DEFENDERS ALL OVER THE WORLD, INCLUDING HIGH-RISK COMMUNITIES SUCH AS WOMEN HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, LGBTI DEFENDERS, AND THOSE DEFENDING LAND, INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS. Land and environmental defenders named among the communities it was built from, not a category it was later extended to. THE ECOSYSTEM MAP, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: DEFENDERS AND OTHER CIVIC ACTORS AT RISK CAN STRUGGLE TO IDENTIFY AND ACCESS THE SUPPORT THAT THEY NEED IN AN EMERGENCY — A PROTECTION ECOSYSTEM MAP HELPS BOTH THOSE AT RISK AND OTHER ORGANISATIONS NAVIGATE THE PROTECTION MECHANISMS, SECURITY GRANTS, AND OTHER SUPPORT THAT MAY BE AVAILABLE. A map of the other doors, published by one of them. That is the thing this file itself is assembling for land projects; for defender protection specifically, somebody has already built it, and it should be read before an emergency rather than during one. THE SCALE AND THE TREND: NEARLY 7,000 HOURS OF SUPPORT IN 68 COUNTRIES IN ONE YEAR, OVER 6,000 HOURS ACROSS 100 COUNTRIES IN ANOTHER, MORE THAN 1,000 ACTIVISTS TRAINED IN 112 WORKSHOPS — AND A 20 PERCENT INCREASE IN REQUESTS FOR SAFETY AND WELLBEING SUPPORT IN ONE YEAR. Demand rising twenty percent in a year. Expect a queue, and ask early. THE REFERRAL NETWORK: MORE THAN 50 REFERRAL PARTNERS WORLDWIDE, INCLUDING A PRESS FREEDOM ORGANISATION, A WORLD ORGANISATION AGAINST TORTURE, AND A EUROPEAN UNION HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS MECHANISM — BY STRENGTHENING THIS ECOSYSTEM, WE CAN REACH MORE PEOPLE IN NEED FASTER AND REDUCE BARRIERS TO ACCESS. REFERRAL PARTNERS CAN REQUEST ON YOUR BEHALF. If a network you already belong to is one of the fifty, that is a faster route in than a cold approach. THE POSITION IT ARGUES ON RELOCATION, WHICH IS WORTH READING BEFORE ANYONE LEAVES: INTERNATIONAL RELOCATION IS ONLY ONE TOOL IN A WIDER SPECTRUM — A PROTECTION CONTINUUM RUNNING THROUGH HOLISTIC SECURITY RISK MANAGEMENT, COLLECTIVE PROTECTION, SOLIDARITY AND ADVOCACY, INTERNATIONAL PROTECTIVE ACCOMPANIMENT, INTERNATIONAL RESPITE, AND DOMESTIC RELOCATION, BEFORE CONSIDERING INTERNATIONAL RELOCATION — WHICH SHOULD BE A STRATEGY OF LAST, NOT FIRST, RESORT, SINCE FAILURE TO DO SO RISKS UNDERMINING SOCIAL MOVEMENTS AND CREATING WHOLE CIVIL SOCIETIES IN EXILE. Six options before leaving the country, listed in order. A leader flown abroad is a campaign decapitated, and the movement rarely recovers — so the question to ask any organisation offering help is which rung of that continuum it is proposing and why the cheaper ones were skipped. AND THE FREE MATERIALS BESIDE THE PROTOCOL: A GUIDE TO COLLECTIVE PROTECTION FOR DEFENDERS AND THEIR ALLIES; AN INFOSHEET ON COMPASSION FATIGUE, VICARIOUS TRAUMA AND BURNOUT FOR THOSE SUPPORTING DEFENDERS; A QUICK REFERENCE CARD SETTING OUT ACTIONS GRANTMAKERS CAN TAKE TO PREVENT AND RESPOND TO SERIOUS ATTACKS AFFECTING THEIR GRANTEES; A GUIDE TO INSURANCE FOR NGOs OPERATING IN VIOLENT ENVIRONMENTS; AND A RISK ASSESSMENT TOOL THAT SETS YOUR RISK THRESHOLD AND AUTOMATICALLY CALCULATES RISK RATINGS. THE CARD FOR GRANTMAKERS is the one to send upward: it tells your funder what it should do when you are attacked, which is a conversation few grantees can start from nothing. WHO IT SUITS: African community groups, collectives and organisations facing threats — including unregistered ones, and including those who need the wellbeing side rather than the security side. CAVEATS: GLOBAL SOUTH GROUPS THAT CANNOT OTHERWISE FUND THE SUPPORT, DEMAND IS RISING, AND DIGITAL SECURITY IS NOT DELIVERED IN FRENCH OR ARABIC — pair it accordingly. For the two-hour digital helpline in French and Arabic, Libya's entry; for grants that buy the equipment, Equatorial Guinea's entry; for the 24-hour defender helpline, Benin's entry.

trackers.name: The Transnational Institute (TNI) — free primers and reports on land and water grabbing written with agrarian movements — including North African extractivism, a pan-African water justice network, and the question of what to do about deals that break no law at all
trackers.desc: THE HARD CASE IS THE DEAL THAT BREAKS NO LAW — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S EGYPT ENTRY COVERS THE PEASANT MOVEMENT; ITS ALGERIA ENTRY THE MOVEMENT FUNDER; ITS ERITREA ENTRY THE FOREST NETWORK WITH AFRICAN-LANGUAGE BOOKLETS; ITS BURKINA FASO AND MADAGASCAR ENTRIES A FOOD RIGHTS ORGANISATION; ITS DJIBOUTI BUCKET CARRIES A SEEDS AND LAND RESEARCH HOST. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES MOST AFRICAN CASES, WHICH IS THE FIND: ACQUISITIONS WHERE FORMAL STATE LAWS ARE SKIRTED ARE CLEARLY GRABS — BUT THEN WHAT ABOUT CASES WHERE THE DEALS DO NOT BREAK FORMAL RULES AND LAWS? THIS IS THE CASE IN MANY AFRICAN COUNTRIES. Most of this file's legal entries assume an illegality to expose. The harder and commoner situation is the concession granted entirely lawfully, because the law already vests the land in the state and treats customary occupation as absence. A community whose lawyer reports that everything was done correctly has not lost the argument — it has discovered that the argument is about the law itself, and this is where that case is set out. THE NORTH AFRICA REPORT: EXTRACTIVISM AND RESISTANCE IN NORTH AFRICA, EXAMINING THE COMMODIFICATION OF NATURE AND PRIVATISATION OF RESOURCES ASSOCIATED WITH OIL AND GAS EXTRACTION IN ALGERIA AND TUNISIA, PHOSPHATE MINING IN TUNISIA AND MOROCCO, AND WATER-INTENSIVE AGRIBUSINESS ALONG WITH TOURISM IN MOROCCO AND TUNISIA — DOCUMENTING CASES THAT TAKE THE FORM OF ACCUMULATION BY DISPOSSESSION. Named countries, named sectors. North Africa is thinly covered by almost everything else in this file, and phosphate, gas and water-intensive agribusiness are precisely the industries taking land there. THE PAN-AFRICAN WATER NETWORK IT REPORTS, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: FROM SILOS TO A PAN-AFRICAN FRONT — THE AFRICA WATER JUSTICE NETWORK, UNITING WATER COMMONING STRUGGLES AGAINST CAPITAL — ALONGSIDE A REPORT ON A DEVELOPMENT BANK'S WATER AND SANITATION POLICIES IN TUNISIA AND PRIVATISATION AT THE EXPENSE OF FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS. A continental network on water specifically, reported by name. Communities losing a river, a borehole or an irrigation system to a private operator have very few allies in this file; that network is the one to trace and join. THE WATER POINT IT MAKES ABOUT AFRICA: AS LAND IS GRABBED AND EARMARKED IN AFRICA FOR SUPPOSED DEVELOPMENT, THERE ARE NEARLY ALWAYS IMPLICATIONS FOR THE WATER NEARBY, FOR LOCAL PEOPLE'S LAND AND WATER RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY. The land deal is also a water deal, and it is rarely written that way in the contract. A community negotiating over hectares should be asking how much water the operation will take and from where — that is the loss that arrives later and is hardest to reverse. WHAT THE PROGRAMME IS: RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS ON THE COLLECTIVE STRUGGLES OF RURAL WORKING PEOPLE TO DEMOCRATISE ACCESS, OWNERSHIP, AND CONTROL OF LAND, WATER AND OTHER NATURAL RESOURCES. WHO THE MATERIAL IS WRITTEN WITH: MANY OF THESE HAVE BEEN PRODUCED WITH TRANSNATIONAL AGRARIAN MOVEMENTS AND PARTNERS ON THE GROUND. Written with movements rather than about them, which is why the primers read as arguments a community can use rather than as findings about it. THE STATED AIM: TO CONTRIBUTE TO STRENGTHENING THE CAMPAIGNS BY AGRARIAN SOCIAL MOVEMENTS IN ORDER TO MAKE THEM MORE EFFECTIVE IN RESISTING LAND AND WATER GRABBING, AND IN DEVELOPING AND ADVANCING ALTERNATIVES SUCH AS LAND, FOOD AND WATER SOVEREIGNTY AND AGRO-ECOLOGICAL FARMING SYSTEMS. THE DEFINITION IT WORKS FROM: A GLOBAL PHENOMENON WHEREBY THE ACCESS, USE AND RIGHT TO LAND AND OTHER CLOSELY ASSOCIATED NATURAL RESOURCES IS BEING TAKEN OVER, RESULTING IN A CASCADE OF NEGATIVE IMPACTS ON RURAL LIVELIHOODS AND ECOLOGIES, HUMAN RIGHTS, AND LOCAL FOOD SECURITY — OFTEN PACKAGED AS LARGE-SCALE INVESTMENT FOR RURAL DEVELOPMENT. PACKAGED AS INVESTMENT FOR RURAL DEVELOPMENT is the phrasing a community will meet in the consultation. Having the counter-framing written down and sourced is what stops a public meeting turning into a discussion of jobs. THE CLIMATE WARNING IT CARRIES: DOMINANT APPROACHES TO CLIMATE CHANGE MITIGATION ARE PUTTING NEW PRESSURES ON SMALL FARMERS AND VILLAGE DWELLERS, JUSTIFYING DISPOSSESSION BY POWERFUL ACTORS — WITH MAINSTREAM NARRATIVES OFTEN INTENSIFYING PRESSURE TO REPLACE SO-CALLED INEFFICIENT USERS OF LAND, INCLUDING SMALL FARMERS AND PASTORALISTS, WITH MARKET-BASED ACTORS. INEFFICIENT USERS OF LAND is the exact language used against pastoralists and shifting cultivators across this file, and it now arrives wrapped in climate justification. Naming that move in advance is half of answering it. THE FRONTLINE VOICES REPORT: COOLING THE PLANET — FRONTLINE COMMUNITIES LEAD THE STRUGGLE, AMPLIFYING THE VOICES OF FRONTLINE COMMUNITIES AND SHARING THE POLITICAL MESSAGES OF 16 SOCIAL MOVEMENT LEADERS CONNECTED TO A GLOBAL CONVERGENCE OF LAND AND WATER STRUGGLES. A GLOBAL CONVERGENCE OF LAND AND WATER STRUGGLES is itself a body worth tracing — sixteen named movement leaders are sixteen possible contacts. THE PRIMERS AND THE PRINT OPTION: A GLOBAL LAND GRAB PRIMER AND A GLOBAL WATER GRAB PRIMER, ALONGSIDE A WATER JUSTICE REPORT INTENDED TO STRENGTHEN STRUGGLES FOR PUBLIC AND COMMUNITY WATER SYSTEMS — WITH PRINT COPIES ORDERABLE AND A MONTHLY NEWSLETTER. PRINT COPIES ORDERABLE. Everything else here is a download; a printed primer can be read at a village meeting by people without devices, which this file has repeatedly identified as the difference between a resource existing and being used. AND THE AFRICAN CASES ITS OWN CITATIONS POINT TO: WORK ON NEW INVESTMENT AND OLD CHALLENGES IN LAND DEALS AND THE WATER CONSTRAINT IN AFRICAN AGRICULTURE, AND ON THE POLITICS OF BIOFUELS AND LAND-WATER GRABBING IN A NAMED MOZAMBICAN CASE — WITH THE INSTITUTE FOUNDED IN 1974. WHO IT SUITS: African farmers' organisations, pastoralist associations and community committees who need the argument and the evidence, especially where the deal against them is lawful. CAVEATS: RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS, NOT FUNDING, LEGAL REPRESENTATION OR ORGANISING SUPPORT; MUCH OF THE MATERIAL IS IN ENGLISH AND ACADEMIC IN REGISTER — the primers are the accessible entry point. For the peasant movement you can join, Egypt's entry; for community booklets in African languages, Eritrea's entry; for the funder whose categories include legal aid, Algeria's entry.

trackers.name: Wildlife Works — a community forest-carbon project where 13 blocks of land stay in the communities' own legal title and locational committees decide the spending — filed with the fieldwork finding that ranch owners hold 30-year contracts while communities have no binding agreement
trackers.desc: INCOME FROM THE LAND WITHOUT SELLING IT — AND GET YOUR AGREEMENT IN WRITING — method and adjacency declared first: A BIRD CONSERVANCY WITH A LARGE LAND-PURCHASE RECORD WAS CHECKED FIRST THIS ROUND AND FOUND TO OPERATE ONLY IN LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN — NOT A RESOURCE AVAILABLE TO AFRICAN LOCALS, SO IT WAS NOT FILED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THE SHIPPED HOST AND THREE SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL ABSENT. THIS FILE'S CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC, DR CONGO, COMOROS AND GAMBIA BUCKETS MENTION FOREST-CARBON SCHEMES AND ITS CÔTE D'IVOIRE, EGYPT, KENYA AND TANZANIA BUCKETS CARBON CREDITS, IN PASSING; NONE IS THIS PROJECT AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. ITS EQUATORIAL GUINEA AND LIBYA ENTRIES COVER THE LAND-PURCHASE FUNDERS. WHO HOLDS THE TITLE, WHICH IS THE FIND: 13 BLOCKS OF LAND OWNED BY INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY OWNERSHIP GROUPS, EACH OWNED BY DIFFERENT LEGAL ENTITIES FORMED YEARS AGO BY THE COMMUNITIES AND THE GOVERNMENT TO HOLD LEGAL TITLE TO THE LAND — 12 LEASEHOLD AND 1 FREEHOLD — WITH CARBON RIGHTS HELD BY THE INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY GROUP OF LANDOWNERS. The land is not bought and not leased away: it stays in community title, and the community holds the carbon rights over it. For a community that cannot afford to buy its ground and does not want to sell it, this is the third option — income from the land while keeping it. CARBON RIGHTS as a separate thing from land rights is the point to settle before signing anything. THE GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE THAT DECIDES THE SPENDING, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: LOCATIONAL CARBON COMMITTEES ARE THE GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE THROUGH WHICH THE COMMUNITIES DIRECTLY ALLOCATE FUNDS — SET UP WITHIN EACH COMMUNITY, DETERMINING HOW THEY WOULD LIKE TO SPEND THEIR CARBON REVENUES, RESULTING IN SCHOLARSHIPS, SCHOOL INFRASTRUCTURE AND WATER INFRASTRUCTURE. A committee per location, not one committee for the whole scheme. That is the structure to insist on: money decided where it lands, by people the neighbours can hold to account. THE PUBLISHED REVENUE TARGET: OUR TARGET IS FOR 50% OR MORE OF PROJECT REVENUE TO GO DIRECTLY TO COMMUNITY PARTNERS — WITH THE MODEL CHANGING BETWEEN PROJECTS DEPENDING ON LOCALISED FACTORS SUCH AS LAND TENURE RIGHTS AND THE HOST GOVERNMENT'S POLICIES. A TARGET, not a guarantee, and it varies by project. Ask what the actual percentage is in the contract in front of you.
