For the fund that grants purchase money and hands over the title, Equatorial Guinea's entry; for the organisation that buys farms itself, South Sudan's entry.

trackers.name: #MineAlert and #GreenAlert (Oxpeckers) — free map-and-alert tools that tell a resident which mining applications, water use licences and environmental impact assessments are live over their own area, with the subscribe-by-area steps published
trackers.desc: FIND OUT WHAT IS BEING APPLIED FOR OVER YOUR OWN GROUND, BEFORE IT IS DECIDED — method and adjacency declared first: FOUND WHILE VERIFYING A PLACEHOLDER IN THIS FILE'S ACCESS INITIATIVE ENTRY. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL HOSTS AND ALL SIX FACTS ABSENT. THE PARENT NAME APPEARS IN TWO BUCKETS: THE SOUTH AFRICA ENTRY, READ IN FULL AND FOUND TO BE A ONE-LINE STUB NAMING NO TOOLS, AND THE GUINEA-BISSAU CODE FOR AFRICA ENTRY, WHICH IS A FUNDER OF THESE TOOLS AND A DIFFERENT SUBJECT. NEITHER IS RESTATED AND NEITHER HOST IS SHIPPED. THE ALERT, WHICH IS THE FIND: A CITIZEN-FOCUSED WEBSITE AND MOBILE APP THAT ALERTS RESIDENTS AND ORGANISATIONS TO MINING APPLICATIONS AND LICENCES IN THEIR REGIONS — AND A SISTER TOOL THAT LETS YOU TRACK AND SHARE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENTS THE SAME WAY. Almost every entry in this file helps a community AFTER it has learned about a project. This one is how it learns. An application is a public document that sits in a register nobody reads; an alert keyed to your own coordinates turns that into a letter arriving before the comment window closes. HOW A PERSON ACTUALLY USES IT, PUBLISHED STEP BY STEP: OPEN THE SITE; USE MY LOCATION TO FIND PROJECTS IN YOUR AREA, OR REGISTER WITHOUT LOCATION SERVICES; OPEN THE MAP; CREATE ALERT; THEN SUBSCRIBE BY AREA, MINE, COMPANY, COMMODITY OR TYPE OF MINE — AND ALERTS ARRIVE AUTOMATICALLY. Five steps, published. SUBSCRIBE BY COMPANY is the one organisers miss: if a company has already taken land in the next district, an alert on its name tells you when it files near you. WHAT ELSE IS ON THE MAP: A MINING LICENCES LAYER FROM SEVERAL COLLATED DATASETS; A WATER LICENCES LAYER SHOWING WATER USE LICENCES AND APPLICATIONS FOR MINING DEVELOPMENTS AGAINST THE COUNTRY'S FRESHWATER PRIORITY AREAS; AND WATER THREATS LAYERS SHOWING THE VULNERABILITY OF FRESHWATER RESOURCES TO MINING, BUILT FROM THE NATIONAL MINE WATER ATLAS COMPILED BY THE WATER RESEARCH COMMISSION. THE WATER LICENCE IS THE SEPARATE PERMISSION, and it is often the weaker one. A mine may hold its mineral right and still need water it has not been granted; a community that can see both applications on one map can object to the one that is actually vulnerable. WHAT IT IS FOR, IN ITS OWN WORDS: TO EQUIP MINING-AFFECTED COMMUNITIES WITH THE RIGHT AMOUNT OF INFORMATION TO MAKE THEIR VOICES HEARD — FREE, FAST AND EASY TO USE, BRIDGING THE TRANSPARENCY GAP BETWEEN GOVERNMENT, ORGANISATIONS RALLYING FOR CHANGE, AND ORDINARY CITIZENS. WHAT A REGISTERED USER GETS: ALERTS ON ALL THE MINING COMPANIES OR GEOGRAPHIES THEY ARE INTERESTED IN, TO USE TO PETITION FOR CHANGE — WITH ACCESS TO MINING LICENCES, WATER USE LICENCES AND SOCIAL AND LABOUR PLANS. SOCIAL AND LABOUR PLANS are the commitments a company made to the community to get its licence — housing, jobs, local procurement. Read beside this file's Republic of Congo entry on the schedule of obligations: the plan is the promise, and almost nobody checks it against what was built. WHY IT WAS BUILT, AND THE GAP IT NAMES: A DRAFT NATIONAL MINING CHARTER WAS SILENT ABOUT THE POLLUTER PAYS PRINCIPLE, SET NO GOALS FOR WATER CONSUMPTION AND DESTRUCTION BY MINES, AND MADE NO PROVISION FOR MINE CLOSURE — WITH GRIEVANCE MECHANISMS FOR LOCAL COMMUNITIES, THEIR RIGHT TO SAY NO TO MINING, AND EASY ACCESS TO RELEVANT EXPERTISE ALSO ABSENT. Four omissions named in a national charter, and the tool was built because of them. That list is a template for reading your own country's mining policy: closure, water, polluter-pays, grievance. If those four are missing, the same gap exists. THE OTHER TOOLS ON THE SAME SHELF: A TRACKER FOR BIODIVERSITY THREATS CAUSED BY MINING LICENCES ACROSS AFRICA; A POWER TRACKER FOR RENEWABLE AND COAL-BASED ENERGY SOURCES; A GLOBAL AND REGIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL-CRIME TRACKER WITH EUROPE AND ASIA EDITIONS; A CLIMATE TRACKER; AND TRACKERS FOR POACHING COURT CASES AND INCIDENTS SINCE 2010. The biodiversity layer is continental, not national — so a community outside the home country still has something to search. WHO BUILDS AND PAYS FOR IT: A PROJECT OF AN INVESTIGATIVE ENVIRONMENTAL JOURNALISM CENTRE, SUPPORTED BY A CONTINENTAL CIVIC-TECH NETWORK AND A NATIONAL OPEN SOCIETY FOUNDATION, DEVELOPED BY A NAMED TECHNICAL PARTNER. WHAT THE PARENT NEWSROOM IS: A CORE NEWSROOM COMBINING TRADITIONAL INVESTIGATIVE REPORTING WITH DATA-DRIVEN JOURNALISM, GEO-NARRATIVE TECHNIQUES AND DIGITAL ENGAGEMENT TOOLS, BOLSTERED BY FELLOWS, WITH SPECIAL DIGITAL PROJECTS DESIGNED TO CREATE PUBLIC RESOURCES TO IMPROVE CITIZEN ACCESS TO ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE. A newsroom that builds public tools rather than only publishing stories. Worth approaching with a documented local problem: they run a fellowship and take investigations. WHAT THE MAPPING IS MEANT TO ENABLE: CITIZENS AND COMMUNITIES PARTICIPATING MEANINGFULLY IN DECISION-MAKING, TRACKING THE PROGRESS OF PROJECTS, NOTIFYING STAKEHOLDERS AND AUTHORITIES IF SOMETHING SEEMS AMISS, AND TAKING PREVENTATIVE MEASURES TO AVOID EXPOSURE TO POSSIBLE RISKS. THE DATA IT WAS BUILT FROM: THE MOST RECENT MINING APPLICATIONS AND LICENCES IN ONE PROVINCE, THE LATEST DATASETS FROM THE MINERALS DEPARTMENT, AND A DATASET FROM AN AFRICAN MINES SOURCE. AND THE HONEST LIMIT: THE ALERTING IS BUILT ON WHATEVER DATASETS THE GOVERNMENT HAS RELEASED, SO COVERAGE FOLLOWS DISCLOSURE — THE MINING AND EIA TOOLS ARE STRONGEST IN ONE COUNTRY, WITH THE BIODIVERSITY LAYER EXTENDING ACROSS AFRICA. Filed with that limit attached: an empty map is not proof that nothing is being applied for near you, only that nothing has been disclosed in a machine-readable form. Where the map is blank, the records request is still the route. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who wants to know what is being applied for over their own ground before it is granted, and organisers who want an alert on a company that is moving through a region. CAVEATS: THE UNDERLYING LICENCE DATA IS STRONGEST IN ONE SOUTHERN AFRICAN COUNTRY; IT ALERTS AND MAPS BUT DOES NOT OBJECT, LITIGATE OR FUND; AND ITS COVERAGE DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON GOVERNMENT DISCLOSURE. For the schedule of obligations a company owes your village, the Republic of Congo entry; for the civic-tech network that co-funds these tools, the Guinea-Bissau entry.

trackers.name: Guamina (Friends of the Earth Mali)
trackers.desc: The Malian member of Friends of the Earth International, based in Bamako. Its work covers desertification, mining, sustainable agriculture, food security and ecological debt, alongside training and literacy courses delivered in local languages and a particular focus on the status of women. WHO TO ENLIST: one of very few points of contact in Mali for a community facing a mining or land-use problem, and a route into the wider Friends of the Earth Africa network. Domain unverified: Guamina appears in Friends of the Earth International's own member directory at foei.org with a Bamako postal address and telephone number but no website listed, so reach it through that entry. Guamina has no website of its own, so the link is Friends of the Earth International's member-group page for Mali, which publishes its address and telephone numbers: Hamdallaye près du pont Diafarana, Rue 42 porte 232, 2744 Bamako, on +223 20 80 01 16 or +223 76 11 83 38. It takes part in FoEI's campaigns on desertification and mining as well as sustainable agriculture, food security and ecological debt, and separately runs training and literacy courses in local languages — which is why it can reach communities a capital-city organisation cannot.

trackers.name: Section des comptes de la Cour suprême du Mali
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Mali — audits government accounts and the use of public money.

trackers.name: ITIE Mali
trackers.desc: National Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative body — discloses oil, gas and mining revenues, contracts and licences in Mali.

trackers.name: Mali — Guichet Unique API-Mali
trackers.desc: National company registry; the API-Mali one-stop window centralises company formalisation & RCCM immatriculation (within 72h) and investment-code approvals, Mali. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Mali — Budget de l’État (budget.gouv.ml)
trackers.desc: National budget-transparency portal of the Ministry of Finance; lets citizens explore the State budget, expenditure & revenue data, Mali. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Mali.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: ECOWAS Court of Justice — file directly, but sue the State
trackers.desc: A COURT YOU CAN REACH WITHOUT EXHAUSTING DOMESTIC REMEDIES. The ECOWAS Community Court of Justice has held human rights jurisdiction since 2005 and has broad access and standing rules permitting individuals and NGOs to bypass national courts and file directly. THE PRECEDENT: in SERAP v Federal Republic of Nigeria (ECW/CCJ/APP/08/09) the Court dismissed all three preliminary objections — no locus standi, no jurisdiction, statute-barred — and rejected the government's attempt to exclude an Amnesty International report from the evidence. NGO research was admitted as evidence, which matters when no state data exists. It found violations of articles 1 and 24 of the African Charter — article 24: ‘all peoples shall have the right to a general satisfactory environment favourable to their development’ — and of article 21, the right to natural wealth and resources. THE FAULT WAS AN OMISSION: the state ‘defaulted in its duties in terms of vigilance and diligence’, and ‘the omission to act and to prevent damage to the environment characterises the violation’. It ordered restoration within the shortest possible time and measures to prevent further damage, citing the ICJ that the environment ‘is not an abstraction but represents the living space, the quality of life and the very health of human beings, including generations unborn’. THE LIMIT THAT DECIDES WHO YOU SUE: the Court held it had no jurisdiction over the private oil corporations, which were struck from the suit. You sue the State for failing to regulate; you cannot sue the company here — naming one as respondent loses that part of the case. AND PLAN FOR ENFORCEMENT: commentary records the Court did not identify a means for Nigeria to implement the ruling, and the ICJ later wrote to the President pressing for enforcement — judgment is the start of an enforcement campaign, not a self-executing remedy. Proposals to require exhaustion of domestic remedies were rejected by ECOWAS experts and Heads of Government, so the direct-access rule has been tested and held. VERIFY MEMBERSHIP BEFORE FILING: this state has been reported as withdrawing from ECOWAS. This entry does not resolve that question — confirm current membership and the Court's jurisdiction over your state before relying on this route, because withdrawal, if effective, would remove it.

trackers.name: ORFAO — comparative land-law tables, and a directive in draft
trackers.desc: COMPARATIVE LEGAL TABLES FOR YOUR COUNTRY AND ITS NEIGHBOURS, IN ONE DOCUMENT. The Observatoire Régional du Foncier Rural en Afrique de l'Ouest (ORFAO), hosted by UEMOA, publishes a regional study on rural land markets containing side-by-side ‘cadre légal comparé’ tables — one covering Bénin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire and Sénégal, another Guinée-Bissau, Mali, Niger and Togo — plus typologies of direct and indirect interventions in land markets and a table of regulatory issues and families of instruments. If you need to know what instrument exists in your country and whether a neighbour has a stronger one, that is the document — comparative tables let a campaign point to a neighbour's provision as an achievable ask rather than a novelty. A WINDOW IS OPENING: on 26 June 2026 in Ouagadougou the UEMOA ministers for urbanisme, habitat, domaines et cadastre approved a draft directive to harmonise rules on immatriculation foncière, accès au titre de propriété and a système d'information foncière, aiming at a common framework of land governance. BE PRECISE ABOUT STATUS: that was a DRAFT directive approved by ministers, not an adopted and transposed instrument — check adoption and transposition before relying on it. But transposition is the moment domestic land law is reopened in each state, and that is when community provisions can be argued for. FOR A GRAZING OR TRANSHUMANCE DISPUTE: a regional pastoral situation bulletin covers 11 West African countries with the support of decentralised technical services — an evidence source drawing on the same services you would otherwise approach one by one. RECORDED PLAINLY: cattle theft is documented as a driver of conflict and instability in the Sahel, so a land dispute here may sit inside a security context that changes what is safe to do. And confirm your state's current ECOWAS standing — several members are recorded as suspended.

trackers.name: CMAT — five farmer and jurist organisations in one convergence against land grabbing, running a legal clinic for the dispossessed
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Convergence Malienne contre les Accaparements de Terres, formed in 2012 and formalised in 2013, which joins five umbrella organisations — the farmers' professional associations (AOPP), the Coalition des Alternatives Africaines (CAD-Mali), the national peasant coordination (CNOP), the association of the dispossessed (UACDDDD), and the Ligue des Jeunes Juristes pour le Développement Humain. That last member is the point: the convergence has lawyers inside it, and one of its stated objectives is to run a legal clinic for victims of expropriation, eviction and land grabbing. ITS STATED AIMS ARE UNUSUALLY OPERATIONAL: enable victims of expropriation and eviction to know and assert their rights; stop evictions and expropriations legally and legitimately; and demand reparation for both material and immaterial damage. It supports named village communities through their disputes, and its own estimate is that more than a million hectares have been grabbed in a country where the agricultural land law it pressed for was finally passed in 2017. It has also run training for communities on the UN declaration on peasants' rights, and published a comparative analysis of Mali's various natural resource codes — useful because, as its own briefing puts it, Mali has no single legal instrument covering agricultural land: the provisions are scattered across many texts, and that vagueness is what makes customary holders easy to dispossess. WHO IT SUITS: villages and urban neighbourhoods facing expropriation, eviction or an investor allocation. CAVEATS: a coalition rather than a service provider — approach is through a member organisation, and no intake route, fee or clinic timetable was published; its own account records severe repression of protesting communities, including arrests and long arbitrary detention, which is context a community should weigh.

trackers.name: CNOP-Mali — supports the village land commissions that let a village delimit its own terroir under the 2017 agricultural land law
trackers.desc: WHO GETS YOUR VILLAGE COMMISSION WORKING: the Coordination Nationale des Organisations Paysannes du Mali (CNOP), created in May 2002 as a framework for exchange and joint action between Malian farmers' organisations, active in policy dialogue with the state and in denouncing land-grab cases, notably in the Office du Niger zone; it hosted the international peasant conference against land grabbing at Nyéléni in November 2011. WHAT IT IS DOING NOW THAT A VILLAGE CAN USE: in February 2025 it convened the first steering committee of a project on SUPPORTING THE LAND AND FOREST SECURITY OF COMMUNITIES THROUGH THE LAND COMMISSIONS (COFO), bringing civil society, ministries and technical services together on the commissions' role in preventing and resolving land conflicts and protecting community land and natural resources. THE INSTRUMENT BEHIND IT: the agricultural land law of April 2017 recognises the land rights of rural communities and puts VILLAGE LAND COMMISSIONS at the centre — for the first time letting villages DELIMIT THEIR OWN TERROIR; a CNOP staffer's diagnosis of why this was needed is exact — the state had never put in place any mechanism for getting customary rights recognised. Implementing decrees were adopted in late March. ASK WHETHER YOUR VILLAGE HAS A COMMISSION FONCIÈRE VILLAGEOISE AND WHETHER IT HAS DELIMITED THE TERROIR — that delimitation is the document that answers an investor's map. THE HONEST WARNING FROM THE MOVEMENT ITSELF: campaigners record that the bill went from 180 articles to 49 during adoption, losing coherence and clarity precisely on the application of customary rights and the roles of the village land commissions — so expect the text to be thinner than the promise, and press for the implementing detail. WHO IT SUITS: Malian villages and farmers' organisations wanting their terroir delimited and their customary rights recognised, especially in the Office du Niger zone. CAVEATS: a farmers' movement and policy organisation, not a law firm — for legal advice and aid it works alongside the jurists' league inside the CMAT convergence, whose entry is also in this file; Mali's security situation constrains fieldwork in much of the country. WHY THIS IS A LAND-HOLDING INSTRUMENT AND NOT ONLY AN ADVISORY ONE: THE DELIMITED TERROIR IS THE ASSET. Once a village has delimited its terroir through the commission, it holds a bounded, officially acknowledged area attached to the village rather than to individuals — which is what an investor, a neighbouring village or a state service must then negotiate against. Delimit before you are approached, not after: every instrument in this file that works — Senegal's reserves, Cameroon's convention, the Congolese CFCL, Ethiopia's Guassa — was in place BEFORE the project arrived, and the ones that failed were attempted after.

trackers.name: ANICT and the FNACT — Mali's national fund for local-authority investment, five windows, 37.9 billion FCFA in one year, and your commune is the applicant
trackers.desc: WHERE THE MONEY FOR LOCAL PROJECTS SITS: the Agence Nationale d'Investissement des Collectivités Territoriales (ANICT), a public administrative establishment created by loi n°0042 of 7 July 2000 to manage the subsidies allocated to local investments carried out UNDER THE PROJECT OWNERSHIP OF THE TERRITORIAL COLLECTIVITIES, and to guarantee certain loans they contract. It runs the FONDS NATIONAL D'APPUI AUX COLLECTIVITÉS TERRITORIALES (FNACT), which has FIVE WINDOWS covering investment, training and support to the collectivities' functioning. THE APPLICANT IS YOUR COMMUNE, NOT YOU — which is exactly why a village should know this exists: the money for a borehole, a road or a market is already allocated to your local authority, and the lever is the mayor and the communal council, not a donor. One window worth naming: the Dotation d'Investissement affectée au Financement du Développement Économique Régional (DIN-DER), placed at the disposal of Regional Councils expressly for projects of economic interest that valorise THE PROTECTION AND VALORISATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES and improve access to goods and services. THE SCALE, PUBLISHED IN ITS OWN ANNUAL REPORT: in 2024 the FNACT was funded to 37,905,274,755 FCFA — the Malian state providing the largest share (22.6 billion for the regions' FNACT budget plus 6.6 billion via the special investment budget), with KfW, Denmark, the World Bank and UNCDF completing it — financing 140 PROJECTS across all regions, with emphasis on Koulikoro, Ménaka and Nioro. Performance-linked grants of 230 to 256 million FCFA per commune have been awarded under a conditional performance programme, and ANICT publishes which dossiers were judged compliant — in one regional round, 32 of 40 submitted. Ask your commune what it submitted, and whether it was judged compliant; the list is public. WHO IT SUITS: Malian villages and communal councillors seeking financing for local infrastructure or natural-resource projects. CAVEATS: THE COLLECTIVITY IS THE BENEFICIARY, NOT THE COMMUNITY DIRECTLY, so this is a lever over your mayor rather than a grant you can win; security conditions restrict verification visits in several regions. For village land commissions and terroir delimitation, Mali's CNOP entry; for the land-grab convergence and its lawyers, CMAT.

trackers.name: Mali's named organisations — AMEDD which brokers between communities and banks, AMRED which holds a government accord-cadre, AMEPANE which counts wildlife with the forestry service, and the women jurists' association
trackers.desc: FOUR MALIAN ORGANISATIONS, EACH DOING SOMETHING DIFFERENT A COMMUNITY NEEDS: ASSOCIATION MALIENNE D'EVEIL AU DÉVELOPPEMENT DURABLE (AMEDD, ameddmali.org), based at KOUTIALA, working SINCE 1998 on ecology, economy and the social, WORKING CLOSELY WITH THE COLLECTIVITÉS TERRITORIALES AND RURAL ORGANISATIONS, ESPECIALLY THEIR UNIONS AT LOCAL AND REGIONAL LEVEL. ITS STATED ROLE IS TO FACILITATE COLLABORATIVE RELATIONS BETWEEN CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, LOCAL ENTREPRENEURS — BANKS, ECONOMIC OPERATORS AND OTHERS — RESEARCH INSTITUTIONS, LOCAL AUTHORITIES AND STATE PUBLIC SERVICES, with four governing principles including THE PARTICIPATION OF LOCAL POPULATIONS and THE PERPETUATION OF PROJECTS AND RESULTS, and a stated objective to CREATE APTITUDES AND KNOW-HOW IN GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS AND THEIR UNIONS FOR AUTONOMOUS AND QUALIFIED DEVELOPMENT OF THEIR OWN POTENTIAL. An organisation whose declared job is to introduce a village union to a BANK is rare in this file — most brokers connect communities to donors. If your group needs credit rather than a grant, that is the door, and AMEDD works through the unions rather than around them. ASSOCIATION MALIENNE DE RECHERCHE SUR L'ENVIRONNEMENT ET LE DÉVELOPPEMENT (AMRED), Rue Nelson Mandela, Immeuble Nyogondeme So, Hippodrome, BAMAKO — which HAS AN ACCORD-CADRE D'ONG WITH THE GOVERNMENT OF MALI, working on environmental problems, drinking water and energy for disadvantaged areas, and socio-economic development including microfinance, through studies and research, support and advice, and training and awareness. A framework agreement with the state is what lets an NGO be received rather than merely heard. ASSOCIATION MALIENNE POUR LA PROTECTION DE LA NATURE (AMEPANE), which with a partner association and IN CLOSE COOPERATION WITH THE DIRECTION NATIONALE DES EAUX ET FORÊTS RAN A PROGRAMME OF FAUNAL INVENTORIES IN THE PROTECTED AREAS OF THE BAFING-FALÉMÉ ZONE, tied to the creation of a transboundary protected area there. Counting the animals alongside the forestry service is how a boundary case gets built — the inventory is the evidence, and doing it WITH the state means the state cannot dispute its own numbers. AND FOR COUNSEL: the ASSOCIATION DES JURISTES MALIENNES (AJM), OFFICIALLY ESTABLISHED 1988, AN APOLITICAL ORGANISATION whose membership is AROUND FIFTY WOMEN LAWYERS, SOLICITORS, MAGISTRATES AND JUDGES, promoting and protecting women's rights in Malian law, and a member of a national women's rights group. Fifty women jurists including sitting magistrates is a professional network, not a charity — for a widow's or a woman's land claim in Mali, this is the first call. WHO IT SUITS: Malian village unions, communities near Bafing-Falémé, and women with a land or inheritance claim. CAVEATS: SMALL NATIONAL NGOs; confirm current operations given the security situation. For the village land commissions and delimiting your terroir before you are approached, Mali's CNOP entry; for five farmer and jurist organisations in one convergence, CMAT; for local-authority money, ANICT.

trackers.name: Sahel Eco, Bamako — a foreign NGO's Mali programme handed over to Malians in 2004, holding a national water-initiative secretariat, plus the CAFO and regional NGO coordinations
trackers.desc: THE NGO THAT WAS HANDED OVER TO MALIANS, WHICH IS A MODEL AS MUCH AS AN ADDRESS: SAHEL ECO IS A MALIAN NGO CREATED IN 2004 BY THE ORGANISATIONAL TRANSFORMATION OF A BRITISH NGO'S MALI PROGRAMME — WHICH HAD WORKED IN THE COUNTRY SINCE 1989 — INTO A NATIONAL AND AUTONOMOUS STRUCTURE, at HAMDALLAYE ACI 2000, RUE 402, BP 259, BAMAKO, with TWO PUBLISHED TELEPHONE NUMBERS and an email. Its stated VISION IS TO BE A REFERENCE AFRICAN NGO IN ENVIRONMENTAL GOVERNANCE, its MISSION TO WORK WITH THE POPULATIONS OF MALI AND OF NEIGHBOURING WEST AFRICAN COUNTRIES TO IMPROVE THEIR STANDARD OF LIVING THROUGH BETTER MANAGEMENT OF THE ENVIRONMENT, its domain ENVIRONMENT AND RURAL ECONOMY, and its slogan simply REVERDIR LE SAHEL. An international programme converted into a Malian-owned organisation is the succession this file keeps finding missing elsewhere. If a foreign body is working on your land, ask what its handover plan is — Sahel Eco is the precedent that it can be done, with the staff and the address kept. WHAT IT HOLDS: SAHEL ECO PROVIDES THE SECRETARIAT OF A WATER INITIATIVE WHOSE PROJECTS ARE IMPLEMENTED BY A CONSORTIUM OF NGOs, working on integrated water management in selected zones, strengthening actor movements at national and regional level, and developing an area of influence beyond the initiative itself to secure impact at larger scale. A Malian NGO holding the secretariat of a multi-NGO consortium is who convenes the others. If you need several organisations behind one question, ask the secretariat, not each member. WHAT IT DOES ON THE GROUND: it runs a TREES FOR LIVELIHOODS PROJECT with a named project chief, supporting NON-TIMBER FOREST PRODUCT ENTREPRENEURS and reporting publicly on THE CONSTRAINTS AND CHALLENGES THOSE ENTREPRENEURS FACE; and it has handed over completed works on HARIMA — PASTORAL HALTING-PLACES (GÎTES D'ÉTAPES) AND WAITING ZONES — IN THE COMMUNE OF SIO. Halting-places and waiting zones are physical infrastructure for herders, built and formally received. In a country whose land conflicts are largely pastoral, a built and handed-over gîte d'étape is a claim on a route that a map alone is not. AND THE STANDING FORUMS, WHICH ARE WHERE A REGIONAL QUESTION IS RAISED: THE COORDINATION RÉGIONALE DES ONGs AND THE COORDINATION RÉGIONALE DE LA CAFO — the coordination of women's associations and NGOs — PROVIDE THE FRAMEWORKS FOR EXCHANGE FOR CIVIL SOCIETY ACTORS IN THE REGIONS, alongside cultural events that carry discussions on integrated water resource management. It is recorded that the first such event was where TRADITIONAL MODES OF WATER RESOURCE MANAGEMENT AND THEIR LINKS WITH MALI'S CURRENT WATER CODE WERE DISCUSSED — A DIALOGUE BETWEEN LOCAL KNOWLEDGE AND MODERN LEGISLATION DESCRIBED AS A MAJOR ELEMENT FOR ACTORS' OWNERSHIP. Regional exchange spaces are few, and cultural festivals double as them. If there is a festival in your region, that is where the water and land conversation actually happens — go to it with your question prepared. ALSO NAMED: MALI FOLKECENTER NYETAA, and SOLIDARITÉ INTERNATIONALE POUR L'AFRIQUE (SIA-Mali), A MALIAN NATIONAL NGO CREATED 2005 UNDER ACCORD-CADRE N°02127, apolitical and non-profit, whose mission is PROMOTING THE ACTIVE AND RESPONSIBLE PARTICIPATION OF RURAL COMMUNITIES IN THEIR OWN DEVELOPMENT, targeting young farmers' organisations and women's groupings. WHO IT SUITS: Malian pastoralists, forest-product producers, women's groupings, and communities needing several NGOs behind one question. CAVEATS: CONFIRM CURRENT OPERATIONS given the security situation. For the broker that introduces a village union to a bank, Mali's AMEDD entry; for fifty women jurists including magistrates, the AJM; for delimiting your terroir before you are approached, CNOP; for local-authority money, ANICT.

trackers.name: CAFO — 2,500+ member associations represented in every region and cercle of Mali, with its Bamako door number, and the interface it runs between members and the public authorities
trackers.desc: TWO THOUSAND FIVE HUNDRED MEMBERS, IN EVERY CERCLE — on the numbers this is the largest membership body recorded anywhere in this file's African record: CAFO, THE COORDINATION DES ASSOCIATIONS ET ONG FÉMININES DU MALI, WAS CREATED ON 20 OCTOBER 1991 BY FOUR WOMEN'S ASSOCIATIONS AND OBTAINED ITS RÉCÉPISSÉ ON 24 MARCH 1992 UNDER N° 0244/MAT-DNAT. IT IS EFFECTIVELY REPRESENTED IN ALL THE REGIONS AND IN ALL THE CERCLES OF THE NATIONAL TERRITORY, AND COUNTED MORE THAN 2,500 MEMBER ASSOCIATIONS AND NGOs, OF WHICH MORE THAN 500 IN BAMAKO. Every cercle. That is the administrative unit below the region, which means CAFO has a presence in the district your village belongs to — not in the capital, in your district. Four founding associations became two and a half thousand in twenty years, and the récépissé number is printed, which is the document this file tells you to demand from anyone. THE ADDRESS IS PUBLISHED TO THE DOOR NUMBER: COURA BOLIBANA, RUE 376, PORTE 63, BP E 194, BAMAKO, WITH A TELEPHONE, A FAX AND AN EMAIL. AND THE TWO FUNCTIONS ARE THE REASON TO WRITE: IT BRINGS TECHNICAL SUPPORT TO ITS MEMBERS THROUGH APPUI-CONSEIL AND ORIENTATION IN THE MATTER OF THE SEARCH FOR FINANCING — AND IT ASSURES THE INTERFACE BETWEEN ITS MEMBERS AND THE PUBLIC AUTHORITIES. Help finding money, and a standing interface with the state. Those are the two things a village women's association cannot build for itself, and CAFO's own description says it supplies both. Join first, then ask — membership is what turns the interface into yours. ITS MISSION IS TO CONTRIBUTE TO VALORISING THE STATUS OF WOMEN BY THE REGROUPING AND COORDINATION OF MEMBERS' ACTIONS AND THE INFLUENCE OF POLICIES, and its first stated objective is TO BRING THE WOMEN OF MEMBER ASSOCIATIONS AND NGOs TO COLLABORATE WITHIN AN ORGANISED, CREDIBLE STRUCTURE SERVING THEM AS A FRAMEWORK OF MOBILISATION, CONCERTATION, TRAINING AND ACTION. It TAKES POSITIONS CLEARLY ON THE GREAT NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL QUESTIONS AND EXERTS PRESSURE ON THE PUBLIC POWERS TO SERVE WOMEN'S INTERESTS. A body that says openly it pressures the public authorities, and has members in every cercle, is a national campaign infrastructure that already exists. If land is being taken and the women of your area are affected, this is the structure that can carry it beyond your commune. AND IT IS HONEST ABOUT ITS OWN MONEY, WHICH IS WORTH READING BEFORE YOU DEPEND ON IT: ITS FINANCING IS CONSTITUTED THROUGH PROJECTS OR ACTION PROGRAMMES AND FOR THE MOST PART CAME FROM A FOREIGN EMBASSY AND A UN AGENCY, WITH MINISTRIES HELPING IMPLEMENT TRAINING SESSIONS — AND A PROGRAMME WAS PUT IN PLACE TO DIVERSIFY THE SOURCES OF FINANCING. Project-based funding from two main donors is a fragility the organisation itself named and acted on. Ask what is currently funded before you plan around it. THE FORMS THAT ALREADY EXIST IN MALI, WHICH IS WHAT A VILLAGE NEEDS BEFORE INVENTING ONE: the national civil society record names, among others, the ASSOCIATION VILLAGEOISE (AV); the ASSOCIATION DE SANTÉ COMMUNAUTAIRE (ASACO); the ASSOCIATION DES ORGANISATIONS PROFESSIONNELLES PAYSANNES (AOPP); the ASSEMBLÉE PERMANENTE DES CHAMBRES D'AGRICULTURE (APECAM); ACTION POUR LA RECHERCHE ET LE DÉVELOPPEMENT DES INITIATIVES LOCALES (ARDIL); the CELLULE D'APPUI AU DÉVELOPPEMENT À LA BASE (CADB); and the COMITÉ DE CONCERTATION ET D'APPUI AUX ORGANISATIONS NON GOUVERNEMENTALES (CCA-ONG). ASSOCIATION VILLAGEOISE is a recognised category with its own acronym in the national record. A Malian village does not need to invent a legal form — the AV already is one, and AOPP is the peasant professional organisation that speaks for farmers nationally. A national directory also lists Malian organisations with STREET ADDRESS TO THE DOOR NUMBER, TELEPHONE, FAX AND EMAIL, sorted by category including CSO and TRAINING AND RESEARCH. WHO IT SUITS: Malian women's associations anywhere in the country, village associations choosing a form, and anyone needing help finding financing. CAVEATS: SOME FIGURES AND CONTACTS DATE FROM PUBLISHED RECORDS OF EARLIER YEARS, AND MALI'S SECURITY SITUATION AFFECTS OPERATIONS — confirm before travelling. For the NGO handed over to Malians in 2004 and the regional coordinations, Mali's Sahel Eco entry; for the broker that introduces a village union to a bank, AMEDD; for fifty women jurists including magistrates, the AJM; for delimiting your terroir before you are approached, CNOP; for local-authority money, ANICT.

trackers.name: LandMark — the global platform that maps community land to prove it is not empty, showing 78.9% of Africa held under customary tenure and only 21% formally recognised, with impact analysis needing no mapping expertise and an open route to submit your boundary
trackers.desc: SEVENTY-EIGHT PER CENT OF AFRICA, AND MOST OF IT UNRECOGNISED — placement note first: THIS IS A GLOBAL PLATFORM, FILED UNDER MALI ONLY BECAUSE THIS FILE HAS NO GLOBAL KEY AND THIS BUCKET CARRIED NO LAND-DATA RESOURCE. IT COVERS EVERY AFRICAN COUNTRY. THE NUMBER: 78.9 PERCENT OF AFRICA'S LAND MASS IS HELD BY INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND COMMUNITIES UNDER CUSTOMARY TENURE — ABOUT 21 PERCENT IS FORMALLY RECOGNIZED, WHILE THE REMAINING 57.9 PERCENT IS NOT. Four fifths of the continent is community land, and more than half of it has no legal recognition at all. That single pair of figures reframes almost every case in this file: your situation is not an exception, it is the majority condition of African land. AND WHY THAT MATTERS, STATED PLAINLY: WHEN INFORMATION ON CUSTOMARY BOUNDARIES IS NOT EASILY ACCESSIBLE OR AVAILABLE, GOVERNMENTS AND PRIVATE DEVELOPERS SEE THOSE PLACES AS VACANT EMPTY LOTS AVAILABLE FOR INVESTMENT — SO THE PLATFORM PROVIDES EVIDENCE THAT THESE LANDS ARE NOT VACANT, IDLE OR NECESSARILY AVAILABLE FOR OUTSIDERS. VACANT EMPTY LOTS. That is how your land appears on the map an investor is shown, and the fix is not an argument but a boundary on a map somebody can look up. This file has recorded that same logic from the Congo Basin to the Comoros; here is the global register where the boundary can sit. THE THREE LAYERS IT CARRIES: THE PHYSICAL BOUNDARIES OF THE LAND; NATURAL ASSETS LOCATED ON THAT LAND, SUCH AS FORESTS, CARBON, AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES; AND CRITICAL THREATS TO COMMUNITY LANDS, SUCH AS CONCESSIONS MADE TO PRIVATE DEVELOPERS. The third layer is the one to open first: concessions granted over community land, drawn against the community boundary. An overlap you can point at ends the argument about whether anyone lives there. THE DISCLAIMER, WHICH IS ITSELF A USEFUL SENTENCE: THE ABSENCE OF DATA DOES NOT INDICATE THE ABSENCE OF INDIGENOUS OR COMMUNITY LAND. Printed on the map itself. THE COVERAGE, HONESTLY STATED: IT HAS MAPPED 36.8% OF THE WORLD'S LAND AS HELD OR USED BY INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, OUT OF AN ESTIMATED 50% OR MORE THAT EXPERTS PROJECT IS ACTUALLY HELD OR USED — with coverage weakest in Africa, the Middle East and much of Asia, where it is currently focusing its attention. It is the main topic. TRADITIONAL JUDGEMENTS THAT ARE FRAUDULENT OR ABUSIVE names something this file has circled repeatedly without a route attached: the customary decision that cannot be appealed. Here is a body that treats a bought verdict as corruption rather than as custom. THE SERVICE: OPERATING IN MORE THAN 50 COUNTRIES — 90+ CENTRES ACROSS 60 — THEY EMPOWER INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES AND COMMUNITIES TO SAFELY REPORT CORRUPTION WHEN THEY SEE IT HAPPEN, PROVIDING FREE AND CONFIDENTIAL ADVICE AND SUPPORT TO VICTIMS AND WITNESSES, ENABLING THEM TO ASSERT THEIR RIGHTS, SEEK REDRESS AND STAND UP FOR JUSTICE. WITNESSES, not only victims. Somebody who saw the payment but did not lose land is inside the definition — and is often the person who can actually prove it. THREE WAYS TO REACH THEM: ONLINE, BY PHONE OR IN-PERSON — AND RECEIVE SUPPORT FROM A TRAINED ADVISOR. HOW FAR THE HELP GOES, WHICH IS FURTHER THAN ADVICE: OFTEN STARTING WITH AN INITIAL CONSULTATION, CENTRES ASSIST CLIENTS IN PURSUING CORRUPTION-RELATED COMPLAINTS — RANGING FROM NAVIGATING BUREAUCRATIC RED TAPE AND SUBMITTING THE RIGHT GOVERNMENT FORM TO CONDUCTING FORMAL INVESTIGATIONS AND PREPARING JUDICIAL CASES. SUBMITTING THE RIGHT GOVERNMENT FORM at one end and PREPARING JUDICIAL CASES at the other. Most land losses in this file begin with a form filed wrongly or not at all; this is free help with the small clerical thing as well as the big legal one. THE MOBILE VERSION, BUILT FOR EXACTLY THIS FILE'S READERS: MOBILE CENTRES BRING FREE LEGAL ADVICE TO RURAL POPULATIONS — BECAUSE OFTEN THE VICTIMS OR WITNESSES ARE ILLITERATE, MARGINALISED AND EXTREMELY VULNERABLE, OR SIMPLY PEOPLE LIVING IN RURAL AREAS VERY FAR FROM LEGAL INFRASTRUCTURE, WHO DO NOT HAVE REAL ACCESS TO LEGAL ADMINISTRATIONS. The lawyer travels to the village. That inverts the arrangement every other legal entry in this file depends on, and it is the only version that reaches people who cannot afford the bus to the district town. THE MOBILE METHOD, STEP BY STEP AND WORTH REQUESTING BY NAME: THE ACTION STARTS WITH A TRAINING SESSION INCLUDING A PUBLIC MEETING ON THEMES THAT MATTER TO THE LOCAL POPULATION — FOR EXAMPLE, CORRUPT PRACTICES IN LAND MANAGEMENT. THE TEAM INFORMS CITIZENS OF LEGISLATION AT THEIR DISPOSAL, INCLUDING THE PENAL CODE, THE CIVIL CODE, OTHER LAWS RELEVANT TO PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION, AND INTERNATIONAL INSTRUMENTS SUCH AS A UN CONVENTION AGAINST CORRUPTION. AFTER THE TRAINING SESSION, THE LEGAL COUNSELLOR AND ASSISTANTS COLLECT THE COMPLAINTS OF CITIZENS WHO ARE WILLING TO SHARE THEM. Public meeting first, then complaints collected. THE RECORD: IN ONE YEAR THE CENTRES WORKED WITH 7,480 VICTIMS AND WITNESSES ACROSS 65 COUNTRIES, MAKING 264 CORRUPTION-RELATED LEGAL SUBMISSIONS TO HOLD WRONGDOERS ACCOUNTABLE. THE WORKED AFRICAN CASE: AFTER COMPLAINTS OF BRIBERY AND EXTORTION AT A HOSPITAL, A CENTRE'S INVESTIGATION UNCOVERED LARGE-SCALE ADMINISTRATIVE CORRUPTION AND PROMPTED A NATIONAL DEBATE AND OFFICIAL ENQUIRIES — DETERRING STAFF FROM DEMANDING BRIBES IN THAT HOSPITAL AND MANY OTHERS ACROSS THE COUNTRY. THE STRUCTURE AND THE LOCAL RULE: MORE THAN 100 CHAPTERS — LOCALLY ESTABLISHED, INDEPENDENT ORGANISATIONS — STAFFED WITH LOCAL EXPERTS AND IDEALLY PLACED TO DETERMINE THE PRIORITIES AND APPROACHES BEST SUITED TO THEIR COUNTRIES, WITH WORK RANGING FROM VISITING RURAL COMMUNITIES TO PROVIDE FREE LEGAL SUPPORT TO ADVISING THEIR GOVERNMENT ON POLICY REFORM. THE CURRENT CASE AND ITS SHAPE: APPLICANTS SEEK A JUDICIAL REVIEW OF AN ENVIRONMENTAL AUTHORISATION GRANTED IN 2023 TO TOTALENERGIES EP SOUTH AFRICA, AFTER AN APPEAL TO THE RELEVANT MINISTER — AND THEY OPPOSED A SECOND OIL MAJOR'S BID TO JOIN THE PROCEEDINGS. Appeal to the minister first, then judicial review. That sequence matters: the internal appeal is usually a precondition, and skipping it can end a case before it starts. WHO IS OPPOSING THEM, NAMED: THE MINISTER AND DIRECTOR-GENERAL OF THE MINERAL RESOURCES AND ENERGY DEPARTMENT, THE MINISTER OF THE FORESTRY, FISHERIES AND ENVIRONMENT DEPARTMENT, AND THE OIL COMPANY ITSELF ALL OPPOSE THE LEGAL CHALLENGE. Two ministries and the company on the other side. Recorded plainly because it is the realistic picture: the environment ministry did not become an ally when the case was filed. THE LAW FIRM NAMED PUBLICLY: THE ORGANISATIONS ARE REPRESENTED BY CULLINAN & ASSOCIATES. Naming the firm in the press release is itself useful to other communities — it is a working answer to the standing question of which attorneys actually run these cases in the country. THE CAMPAIGN THAT SURROUNDS THE LITIGATION: A NAMED OCEANS CAMPAIGN WORKING WITH COASTAL COMMUNITIES WHOSE LIVELIHOODS ARE THREATENED — AIMING TO EMPOWER LOCAL OCEAN-DEPENDENT COMMUNITIES, ENSURING FISHER LIVELIHOODS AND THEIR TOOLS AND KNOWLEDGE ARE SUSTAINED, AND THAT COMMUNITIES ARE ABLE TO ENGAGE WITH DECISION-MAKERS. HOW IT BUILDS THAT: THE CAMPAIGN BUILDS ON EXISTING NETWORKS OF SMALL-SCALE FISHERS AND OTHER COASTAL COMMUNITIES, AS WELL AS ENGAGING CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS WORKING ON CLIMATE AND ENERGY — WITH A COMMUNITY OUTREACH COORDINATOR AND A NAMED LEGACY PROJECT SUPPORTING FISHERS IN A DISTANT COASTAL TOWN. A paid community outreach coordinator, and fishers hundreds of kilometres away brought into the same campaign. The litigation did not create the network; it used one that already existed. THE TRIBUNAL AND THE FINANCE ANGLE: AN OCEANS TRIBUNAL DESCRIBED AS EXPOSING THE DEVASTATING IMPACT OF THE GOVERNMENT'S SECRET DECISIONS, AND COASTAL COMMUNITY MEMBERS FROM THREE NAMED TOWNS CALLING ON THE BANKS NOT TO FUND A POWERSHIP PROJECT — ALONGSIDE CHALLENGES TO ELECTRICITY GENERATION APPLICATION PROCESSES AND TARIFF PLANS. A people's tribunal and a direct appeal to the banks, run alongside the court case rather than instead of it. Where the courts are slow, the financing is the other pressure point — and community members from named towns made that appeal themselves. THE CONTINENTAL FRAMING IT USES: BY EXTENDING THE FIGHT FOR CLIMATE JUSTICE TO OPPOSING DEEP-SEA OIL AND GAS EXPLOITATION, WE WILL SERVE THE COUNTRY AND THE AFRICAN CONTINENT AS A WHOLE, WHILST ACKNOWLEDGING THE COURAGEOUS FIGHT OF A NAMED NIGERIAN PEOPLE AND BUILDING ON A NAMED ACTIVIST'S LEGACY. AND WHAT THE FISHERS THEMSELVES PUT ON RECORD: FOR TRADITIONAL FISHERS, WHO HAVE BEEN LIVING FROM THE OCEAN FOR HUNDREDS OF YEARS, THE OCEAN IS MORE THAN JUST A RESOURCE THAT SUSTAINS OUR LIVELIHOODS — FOR US, WHO HAVE LOST FAMILY MEMBERS AND ANCESTORS AT SEA, THE OCEAN IS PART OF OUR HERITAGE, WHICH WE BELIEVE IS WORTH PROTECTING. Heritage and burial, put into the court record by the fishers rather than by a lawyer. That is the evidence a compensation calculation cannot absorb, and it is the reason to have the community speak in its own words in the papers. WHO IT SUITS: African coastal and fishing communities facing seismic surveys, offshore drilling or port and power projects — and any community organisation looking for a workable litigation structure to copy. CAVEATS: A SOUTH AFRICAN ORGANISATION LITIGATING UNDER SOUTH AFRICAN LAW; THE CASES AND REMEDIES ARE NATIONAL, THOUGH THE STRUCTURE AND GROUNDS TRANSFER — and it is a campaigning body, not a service you apply to. For the international programme that partnered on these cases, Madagascar's entry; for marine funding with community conservation measures, Mauritius' entry.

trackers.name: Spaces for Change, Lagos — an organisation whose legal experts run sessions teaching communities the laws that justify their own eviction — plus field visits after demolitions that publish what compensation was actually offered, and the constitutional argument built from how the demolition was carried out
trackers.desc: THEY TEACH YOU THE LAWS THAT WILL BE USED TO EVICT YOU — method and adjacency declared first: THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THE SHIPPED HOST AND FOUR SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL ABSENT. THIS FILE'S NIGERIA BUCKET CARRIES A COMMUNITY-PARALEGAL ORGANISATION ON A DIFFERENT HOST, READ BEFORE WRITING AND NOT RESTATED; ITS GUINEA-BISSAU ENTRY THE 450-MEMBER EVICTION COALITION AND ITS MALAWI ENTRY THE SOCIO-ECONOMIC RIGHTS INSTITUTE WITH ITS EVICTION GUIDE. NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHAT ITS LAWYERS ACTUALLY TEACH, WHICH IS THE FIND: LEGAL EXPERTS FACILITATED LEARNING SESSIONS THAT EXPLAINED THE LAWS THAT JUSTIFY FORCED EVICTIONS IN THE COUNTRY. Not the laws that protect you — the ones that will be used against you. This file is full of guidance on rights; this is the inverse and rarer service: knowing in advance which statute the notice will cite, what it requires the state to do first, and therefore where the state will fail to do it. That is what turns a demolition into a case. WHY THAT MATTERS TO THE PEOPLE IN THE ROOM: BECAUSE MOST RESIDENTS LACK TITLED LAND DOCUMENTATION, THEY ARE PRONE TO URBAN-INDUCED GENTRIFICATION AND FORCED DISPLACEMENT, IN CONSTANT DANGER OF FORCEFUL EVICTION WITHOUT PROPER COMPENSATION OR RESETTLEMENT. WHAT PARTICIPANTS SAID THEY GOT: THAT THE PARTNERSHIP WAS A SAFE PLACE TO INTERACT WITH STATE AND LOCAL AUTHORITIES AND ALSO MAINSTREAMING THE NEEDS OF INFORMAL COMMUNITIES INTO THE STATE'S HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT AGENDA — WITH LEADERS COMMITTING TO STEP DOWN THE KNOWLEDGE AND TRAINING TO THEIR OWN MEMBERS. A SAFE PLACE TO INTERACT WITH AUTHORITIES is a distinct thing to ask an organisation for: not representation, but a room in which the meeting can happen without the community negotiating alone. And STEP DOWN THE TRAINING is how twenty people become a thousand. THE FIELD DOCUMENTATION IT DOES AFTER A DEMOLITION, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: ON A FIELD VISIT, COMMUNITY MEMBERS DISCLOSED THAT A FORM WAS CIRCULATED BY A LOCAL DEVELOPMENT COMMITTEE PROPOSING A TOKEN PAYMENT OF THREE HUNDRED THOUSAND NAIRA FOR STRUCTURES MADE OF PLANK AND FIVE HUNDRED THOUSAND FOR A PERMANENT STRUCTURE, TO BE DISTRIBUTED AT THE TRADITIONAL RULER'S PALACE — AND, CONTRARY TO NARRATIVES CIRCULATING ON SOCIAL MEDIA, AFFECTED RESIDENTS HAD NOT RECEIVED ANY FORM OF COMPENSATION. Actual figures, and who was handing out the form. Two things follow for any community facing this: the payment is announced through a local committee at a chief's palace rather than through the state, and the announcement circulates publicly long before anyone is paid. Record the offer, record who made it, and record the date nobody received it. THE INJUNCTION THAT WAS IGNORED: THREE DAYS BEFORE THE DEMOLITION THE COURT GRANTED AN INTERIM INJUNCTION RESTRAINING THE STATE GOVERNMENT, THE ATTORNEY GENERAL, THE COMMISSIONER FOR PHYSICAL PLANNING AND A NAMED AGENCY; THE ORDER WAS DULY SERVED AND ACKNOWLEDGED, HOWEVER, IN BLATANT DISREGARD OF THE COURT'S DIRECTIVE, THE DEMOLITION PROCEEDED. An injunction was won, served, acknowledged — and ignored. Filed because it sets an honest expectation about what a court order alone achieves, and because SERVED AND ACKNOWLEDGED is precisely the record that makes the disregard actionable afterwards. Keep proof of service. THE ARGUMENT IT BUILDS FROM THE METHOD: CONDUCTING A DEMOLITION EXERCISE AT NIGHT, ACCOMPANIED BY HEAVILY ARMED POLICEMEN AND THE USE OF TEAR GAS, AMOUNTS TO CRUEL, INHUMAN, AND DEGRADING TREATMENT PROHIBITED UNDER A NAMED SECTION OF THE CONSTITUTION. The manner of the eviction becomes its own constitutional violation, separate from the question of who owns the land. A community that cannot win on title may still win on how it was done — so the time of day, the weapons and the gas are facts worth recording precisely. THE CONTINENTAL INSTRUMENT IT INVOKES DOMESTICALLY: THE AFRICAN CHARTER ON HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS, WHICH HAS BEEN DOMESTICATED INTO NATIONAL LAW, GUARANTEES THE RIGHT TO PROPERTY AND PROTECTION FROM ARBITRARY DISPLACEMENT. DOMESTICATED means the Charter is enforceable in your own national court, not only at the continental bodies filed under Egypt and Eritrea. Establishing whether your country has domesticated it is a single question to a lawyer with a large answer. WHAT ITS HOUSING PROGRAMME COVERS: PROGRAMS AND ACTIVITIES THAT IMPROVE THE SECURITY OF TENURE, REDRESS HOUSING RIGHTS VIOLATIONS, PREVENT FORCED EVICTIONS AND INCREASE PUBLIC PARTICIPATION IN URBAN PLANNING PROCESSES. THE SECOND SECTOR IT MONITORS: SYSTEMATICALLY MONITORING AND EVALUATING THE GAPS BETWEEN POLICY AND PRACTICE IN THE ENERGY SECTOR. THE COMMUNITY CONGRESS FORMAT IT RUNS: A CONGRESS WHOSE 20 PARTICIPANTS WERE DRAWN FROM SIX NAMED COMMUNITIES SHARING A COMMON DENOMINATOR, RUNNING SINCE 2017. Six separate settlements in one room. Communities facing the same government with the same tactic rarely meet; this file has recorded that isolation being the point of how evictions are sequenced. THE PROCEDURAL FAILURES A PARALLEL HOUSING NETWORK DOCUMENTED IN THE SAME COUNTRY: FAILURE TO CONDUCT EFFECTIVE CONSULTATION, FAILURE TO PROVIDE REPARATIONS INCLUDING RESTITUTION AND COMPENSATION, AND THE USE OF FORCE — NOTING THAT NOWHERE DOES NATIONAL LAW REFER TO DEMOLITION AS A REMEDY, AND THAT EVICTIONS WERE TAKING PLACE ON PROPERTIES THAT HAD BECOME PRIME WATERFRONT REAL ESTATE, UNDERTAKEN TO FAVOR PRIVATE INVESTORS. NOWHERE DOES THE LAW REFER TO DEMOLITION AS A REMEDY is a single sentence worth carrying into any meeting: the state is doing something its own statute does not authorise, whatever the justification offered. AND THE EVIDENCE PACKAGE ONE INVESTIGATION ASSEMBLED, AS A MODEL OF WHAT TO KEEP: TWO WITNESS STATEMENTS ON OATH AND A MEMORANDUM TO THE NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS COMMISSION AS PART OF A PUBLIC HEARING ON EVICTION AND DEMOLITIONS; THREE STATEMENTS MADE BY VICTIMS TO THE POLICE; THREE QUIT NOTICES ISSUED BY GOVERNMENT AGENCIES; EIGHT COURT DOCUMENTS INCLUDING FOUR DECISIONS; 23 CORRESPONDENCES; 169 PHOTOGRAPHS AND 52 VIDEOS. That is the itemised list a community should be building from the first quit notice onward — sworn statements, the notices themselves, correspondence, photographs, video. Note also that the national human rights commission held a PUBLIC HEARING on evictions, which is the domestic body this file's Algeria entry records as obliged to take complaints. WHO IT SUITS: urban and peri-urban communities without title facing demolition or resettlement, and community leaders wanting to train their own members in the law before the notice arrives. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY, WITH AN URBAN HOUSING AND ENERGY FOCUS RATHER THAN RURAL LAND OR CONSERVATION; IT RESEARCHES, TRAINS, DOCUMENTS AND ADVOCATES — CHECK WHETHER IT WILL REPRESENT YOU BEFORE ASSUMING IT. For community paralegals in the same country, Nigeria's entry; for the free eviction guide including how to oppose a lawful eviction, Malawi's entry.

trackers.name: Cour des comptes de Mauritanie
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Mauritania — audits government accounts and the use of public money.

trackers.name: CN-ITIE Mauritanie
trackers.desc: National Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative body — discloses oil, gas and mining revenues, contracts and licences in Mauritania.

trackers.name: Mauritania — Agence pour la Promotion des Investissements (APIM, Guichet Unique)
trackers.desc: National corporate registry; APIM’s One-Stop Shop (Guichet Unique, Khidmaty platform) handles company registration — Commercial Registry, tax & social-security registration — for SARLs, SAs, branches & GIEs within 48 hours, Mauritania. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Mauritania — Ministère des Finances
trackers.desc: National budget authority; governs & manages public finances and prepares the national budget, Islamic Republic of Mauritania. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Mauritania.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: African Convention on Nature — check WHICH version binds your state
trackers.desc: THERE ARE TWO AFRICAN CONVENTIONS OF THIS NAME, AND CITING THE WRONG ONE IS THE AVOIDABLE ERROR HERE. The Algiers Convention was signed 15 September 1968, in force 16 June 1969. The revised Maputo Convention was adopted by the Assembly of the Union in Maputo on 11 July 2003 and entered into force 23 July 2016 — thirteen years later. THE OPERATIVE RULE: the 1968 Convention remains in force for those countries that have not ratified the 2003 revisions, so the two coexist and which binds your state depends on its ratification status. Commentary records only about 30 percent of African states had ratified Maputo. This entry does not assert which binds your state — the African Union publishes a Status List alongside the treaty text at au.int. Check it first. WHY THE DELAY IS AN ARGUMENT FOR IT: commentary attributes the thirteen years to the revised text containing strong provisions that could create accountability and also slow down social and economic development — a treaty resisted for creating accountability is one worth invoking where it applies. PROVISIONS TO KNOW: article XXXIX — no reservation may be made to this Convention, so a ratifying state takes all of it; article XL — withdrawal takes effect only one year after written notification; and no instrument of accession to the 1968 Algiers Convention may be deposited any longer, so the older text is closed to new entrants. THE OBJECTIVES ARE BROADER THAN USUAL: conservation, utilisation and development of soil, water, flora and fauna for present and future welfare, from an economic, nutritional, scientific, educational, cultural and aesthetic point of view — so a claim resting on cultural or aesthetic value has a treaty basis. BUT IF THE 1968 TEXT IS WHAT BINDS YOU, EXPECT LITTLE: parties were encouraged to cooperate but were not required to submit regular reports on implementation, and there were no financial mechanisms — no reporting trail, no funding attached. Article XLI also provides for interim secretariat arrangements, so check current institutional capacity. IUCN publishes a commentary on each provision in English and French.

trackers.name: Nature Mauritanie — the national wetlands and waterbird association, and the technical counterweight on the coast where the projects land
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Association Mauritanienne de protection de la nature, founded in 2000 by experts concerned with wetlands and officially recognised by the Mauritanian authorities in 2004 under receipt number 0216. Its work is conservation and sustainable use of Mauritania's wetland biodiversity, waterbirds and their habitats, and fragile ecosystems, and it takes part in the international waterbird censuses on national territory — which is the point for a community, because a census is a dated, comparable, independently collected number, and that is what an objection to a coastal or wetland project has to be built on. WHERE THE PRESSURE IS IN THIS COUNTRY: the wetlands it works in include the Banc d'Arguin national park, a Ramsar site since 1982 and World Heritage site since 1989, covering a third of the Mauritanian coast and inhabited by the Imraguen fishing communities, whose traditional fishery sits inside a protected area that is also a national economic asset — the classic setting for a fisheries, port or extractive dispute in which the residents are the ones treated as the problem. WHO IT SUITS: coastal and wetland communities, especially fishing communities in and around the Banc d'Arguin and the Diawling area, needing survey data, technical argument or a national ally. 6th district, Ilot 70, BP 2647, Nouakchott. CAVEATS: a scientific and conservation association, not a legal or advocacy defence body — no litigation capacity, intake route or fee information was found, and much of its published activity is bird monitoring and awareness rather than casework. Some site content is several years old; confirm current programmes before relying on it.

trackers.name: BACoMaB Trust Fund — a permanent endowment that pays the running costs of Mauritania's coastal protected areas, with a small grants window
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the Banc d'Arguin and Coastal and Marine Biodiversity Trust Fund, created in 2009 as a permanent endowment — capital invested on ethical and socially responsible markets, with the income used to fund conservation and management along the Mauritanian coast. A charitable foundation under English law with a headquarters agreement in Mauritania, recognised there as being of public utility since December 2010. WHY AN ENDOWMENT MATTERS MORE THAN A GRANT: it is designed to cover the RECURRENT costs that donors will not fund — surveillance, shared governance, community development, ecological monitoring, environmental education and capacity building — which is exactly what fails when a project ends. In one year it signed annual grant agreements totalling €860,000 with the Banc d'Arguin national park (€550,000), the Diawling national park, and a monk seal conservation programme (€120,000); its support to the Banc d'Arguin maritime and coastal surveillance system alone rose year on year from €69,000 to €176,500 across four years. THE DOOR FOR A COMMUNITY OR A SMALL ORGANISATION: alongside the park grants, BACoMaB runs a “Petites Subventions” (small grants) window to support other actors working in or for the sustainable management of the beneficiary zones, and its stated funding priorities include support to the livelihoods of people living in or near those zones, in ways compatible with the protection objectives, plus shared environmental governance arrangements. Note the origin of the money, because it is a precedent worth citing elsewhere: the government's initial contribution came from €1.5 million of revenues from the fisheries agreement with the European Union — the first time in Africa that fisheries-agreement money was directed to biodiversity protection. WHO IT SUITS: Mauritanian coastal communities and local organisations working in or beside the protected areas — principally the Banc d'Arguin and Diawling. CAVEATS: this funds conservation and compatible livelihoods, not opposition to a project; the main beneficiaries are the protected-area agencies themselves, and eligibility is tied to officially protected sites, so a community outside one has no claim on it; and it will not pay for legal costs.

trackers.name: Mauritania — aide juridique is provided for in the judicial organisation ordinance on proof of indigence, and the bar association in Nouakchott is who to ask
trackers.desc: WHAT THE LAW PROVIDES: Mauritania's ordinance on judicial organisation states that court fee tariffs are fixed by decree and that AIDE JURIDIQUE MAY BE GRANTED TO PARTIES WHO JUSTIFY THEIR INDIGENCE, in the conditions the law lays down. Proof of indigence is the gate here as in every francophone country in this file — ask which text fixes the criteria and what document is accepted before you assemble anything else. TWO OTHER PROVISIONS OF THAT ORDINANCE WORTH KNOWING IF YOU LIVE FAR FROM A COURT: courts and tribunals MAY HOLD AUDIENCES FORAINES — travelling hearings — within their jurisdiction, which is the same circuit principle recorded in Lesotho; and advocates exercise their ministry FREELY BEFORE ALL JURISDICTIONS, with the guarantee that no one may be removed from their natural judges. WHO TO ASK: the ORDRE NATIONAL DES AVOCATS DE MAURITANIE, the national bar, based in NOUAKCHOTT (+222 45 24 30 30 area; directory contacts +222 2245 47 74 and +222 31 10 00 06), whose own site publishes a list of members and copies of the laws regulating the legal profession, together with full texts of criminal, social, commercial and civil laws — the members list is how you find a named advocate in a country where no legal aid organisation could be verified for this file. Court infrastructure is being extended under a justice reform programme, with new tribunals delivered at Boutilimit, El Mina and Nouakchott-Sud. WHO IT SUITS: Mauritanians without means facing a land, inheritance or expropriation matter, and anyone needing to identify a practising advocate. CAVEATS: THIN GROUND, STATED HONESTLY — no Mauritanian legal aid organisation or clinic could be verified for this file; what is recorded here is a statutory provision and a bar association, not a service with an intake desk, and the bar's site is in Arabic. For the coastal endowment and its small grants window, Mauritania's BACoMaB entry.

trackers.name: Banc d'Arguin — only the resident Imraguen may fish in 1.2 million hectares, and only under sail; an exclusive use right rather than a title
trackers.desc: THE EXCLUSIVE RIGHT AND WHO HOLDS IT: the Parc National du Banc d'Arguin (PNBA), created 24 June 1976 by decree 76-147, covers 1,200,000 HECTARES — a third of the Mauritanian coast and the largest coastal and marine protected area in West Africa, Ramsar 1982 and UNESCO World Heritage 1989. THE PROVISION THAT MATTERS: THE POPULATIONS RESIDENT IN THE PARK ARE THE ONLY ONES AUTHORISED to practise controlled exploitation of the fish stocks, and MOTORISED BOATS ARE STRICTLY FORBIDDEN. About 1,200 Imraguen live permanently in EIGHT COASTAL VILLAGES, fishing from LANCHES — single-sail, engineless boats — which the park administration REGISTERS AND LIMITS IN NUMBER, around a hundred, USABLE ONLY BY THE IMRAGUEN. The park's missions under loi 2000-024 expressly include contributing to the development of those traditional fishing populations. Where a state has abolished collective land title — as Mauritanian land law did — an EXCLUSIVE USE RIGHT tied to residence and to a technology only you possess can hold ground that a deed cannot. The gear restriction IS the protection: it excludes industrial fleets by rule, not by argument. HOW IT CAME ABOUT, which is the transferable part: a conservation funder encouraged the government to BAN MOTORISED GEAR AND GUARANTEE EXCLUSIVE ACCESS TO THE PARK FOR THE IMRAGUEN PROVIDED THEY USED THEIR TRADITIONAL LANCHES — the community's own practice became the condition of its monopoly. From 1997 the park controlled Imraguen fishing activity; from 1998 it policed and repressed outside incursions. THE RECORDED WEAKNESS, so you do not copy the flaw: COMITÉS DE PLAGE (beach committees) were created in 2000 and can set a fishing rule, discipline, monitor and sanction — BUT their decisions bind ONLY THEIR OWN ACTIVE MEMBERS and not outsiders, BECAUSE no fishing terroirs were fixed within which each committee's authority would run. A committee without a defined territory can only govern its own members — fix the boundary of its authority when you create it. Analysts also warn that the gap between lanche-owning and non-owning families is the fault line to watch. WHO IT SUITS: Mauritanian coastal communities, and anyone whose state denies collective title but might grant an exclusive, gear-conditioned use right. CAVEATS: A USE RIGHT INSIDE A STATE PARK, NOT OWNERSHIP — revocable by the same authority that granted it, and dependent on continued enforcement against outside fleets. For the endowment that pays recurrent park costs, Mauritania's BACoMaB entry; for the wetlands association, Nature Mauritanie; for a lawyer, the aide juridique entry.

trackers.name: Mauritania's environment ministry NGO database — the state's own register of environmental organisations, plus AMDH, OMASSAPE, Tenmiya and Ecodev by name
trackers.desc: THE STATE'S OWN LIST OF WHO EXISTS: Mauritania's MINISTÈRE DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT ET DU DÉVELOPPEMENT DURABLE (BP 1666, Nouakchott) MAINTAINS A PUBLISHED BASE DE DONNÉES ONGs — A DATABASE OF ENVIRONMENTAL NGOs — UNDER ITS PARTNERSHIPS SECTION, developed with support from a Sahel resilience programme, listing organisations by locality including NOUADHIBOU. A government-published register of environmental NGOs does two jobs at once: it tells you who works in your wilaya, and it lets you check whether an organisation approaching your village is actually on the ministry's list. Ask for the entry, not just the name. NAMED ORGANISATIONS: ONG TENMIYA, listed in that ministry database and recorded as an implementing partner — with ECODEV — on a project building BASIC COMMUNAL INFRASTRUCTURE in Mauritania. OMASSAPE (ORGANISATION MAURITANIENNE POUR L'ASSISTANCE, LA SOLIDARITÉ SOCIALE ET L'APPUI À LA PROTECTION DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT), ZRE Nord 537, Tevragh Zeina, Nouakchott, tel +222 45 29 02 02, created 2004, with 39 MEMBERS AND 3 SALARIED STAFF, working in FRENCH, ENGLISH AND ARABIC, at LOCAL AND REGIONAL level, a member of the PLATEFORME DES ACTEURS NON ÉTATIQUES DE MAURITANIE, whose president sits as a delegate of that platform to the national steering committee and the small grants programme, working on rural production through the deployment of TRADITIONAL MECHANISMS, with a named commune among its institutional partners. Thirty-nine members and three paid staff is the honest size of a working Mauritanian association — and its president holds a seat on the committee that awards small grants, which is who to speak to before a call closes. AND FOR RIGHTS: the ASSOCIATION MAURITANIENNE DES DROITS DE L'HOMME (AMDH, amdhrim.org), FOUNDED 1991, BASED IN NOUAKCHOTT, A MEMBER OF THE INTERNATIONAL FEDERATION FOR HUMAN RIGHTS, with a published board — president, vice-president, treasurer and secretary general — named on the record. An organisation with named officers and an international federation behind it is one whose letter travels further than its own borders. In a country where this file records aide juridique as provided for but thin, AMDH is the standing rights body. WHO IT SUITS: Mauritanian communities seeking a partner in their region, checking an organisation's bona fides, or needing a rights body. CAVEATS: A MINISTRY DATABASE AND SMALL ASSOCIATIONS — several records are dated; confirm current status. For the wetlands and waterbird association with its récépissé number, Mauritania's Nature Mauritanie entry; for an endowment that pays running costs in perpetuity, BACoMaB; for the Imraguen exclusive sail-only fishing right, the Banc d'Arguin entry.

trackers.name: Association des Amis du Banc d'Arguin and Association Nafore — a friends-of-the-park association defending a named island from the sea, and an environmental association with three published phone lines in Nouakchott
trackers.desc: THE FRIENDS OF THE PARK AND THE ISLAND THEY ARE DEFENDING: THE ASSOCIATION DES AMIS DU BANC D'ARGUIN (AABA) — whose members carry, in collaboration with an international foundation, the national park itself and Nature Mauritanie, THE OBJECTIVE OF DEFENDING THE ÎLE DE NAÏR AGAINST COASTAL EROSION AND THE ADVANCE OF THE SEA. A friends-of-the-park association is a membership body attached to a protected area — the form that lets ordinary people hold a formal relationship to a park they do not manage. If your area has a park and no friends' association, that is a vehicle worth creating; if it has one, join it. AND THE ARGUMENT THEY MAKE FOR ONE SMALL ISLAND IS WORTH LEARNING: RESISTING CLIMATE CHANGE IS POSSIBLE. SAFEGUARDING THE ÎLE DE NAÏR IS IMPORTANT FOR THE PROTECTION OF BANC D'ARGUIN'S BIODIVERSITY — DIFFERENT AFRO-TROPICAL SPECIES NEST ON THE ISLAND, WHICH IS ALSO SOUGHT IN WINTER BY EUROPEAN SPOONBILLS. IF THE ISLAND DISAPPEARS THEY WILL NO LONGER BE ABLE TO JOIN THEIR AFRICAN COUSINS THERE. A site that hosts both resident and migratory populations is a site with an international constituency. Name the species that arrive from elsewhere: it converts a local loss into somebody else's loss too, and that is what brings foreign partners. WHO SPEAKS FOR IT, AND THE DETAIL WORTH NOTING: THE PRESIDENT OF NATURE MAURITANIE IS AN ORNITHOLOGIST AT THE BANC D'ARGUIN NATIONAL PARK — one person holding both the NGO presidency and a post inside the park. Where the same person sits in the park service and leads the association, the two are not adversaries — which means a request can travel between them without a formal letter. Find out who holds both roles near you. THE OTHER NAMED BODIES, WITH THEIR CONTACTS: ASSOCIATION NAFORE — POUR LA PROTECTION DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT, at NOT 677, MOUGHATAA DE TEVRAGH-ZEINA, NOUAKCHOTT, BP 3212, WITH THREE PUBLISHED TELEPHONE NUMBERS, an email and its own site; and the ASSOCIATION POUR LA PROTECTION DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT EN MAURITANIE, BP 5275 NOUAKCHOTT, which AIMS TO COMBAT DEFORESTATION AND DESERTIFICATION BY PROVIDING INFORMATION AND ANIMATION ON PROTECTING THE ENVIRONMENT AND SOIL MANAGEMENT, AND ENCOURAGES THE PARTICIPATION OF WOMEN AND YOUTH. Three phone lines on one small association is unusual and useful — in a country where this file records thin coverage, an organisation that publishes several numbers expects to be called. WHAT THE WORK LOOKS LIKE ON THE GROUND: Nature Mauritanie's REFORESTATION OF A NAMED ROAD AXIS IN THE COMMUNE OF SEBKHA WAS IMPLEMENTED IN COLLABORATION WITH THE MAIRIE OF SEBKHA on foreign development financing, and it also runs RESTORATION AND PROTECTION OF THE MANGROVE OF THE LOWER DELTA OF THE SENEGAL RIVER IN MAURITANIA. An NGO implementing with the mairie means the commune is a co-signer, not a bystander. Bring your mairie into the project from the start — that is how a planting scheme becomes municipal policy rather than one season's work. Mauritania has been represented at continental conservation congresses by THE BANC D'ARGUIN AND DIAWLING NATIONAL PARKS AND THE BACoMaB TRUST FUND TOGETHER. WHO IT SUITS: Mauritanian coastal and delta communities, and anyone near a national park wanting a formal association. CAVEATS: SMALL ASSOCIATIONS — confirm current contacts. For the wetlands and waterbird association with its récépissé number, Mauritania's Nature Mauritanie entry; for the state's own register of environmental NGOs, the ministry database entry; for an endowment paying running costs in perpetuity, BACoMaB; for the Imraguen exclusive sail-only right, the Banc d'Arguin entry.

trackers.name: FONADH, Mauritania's numbered human rights coalition that criticises power and opposition alike, plus a national NGO list with phone numbers and a type-filterable organism database
trackers.desc: THE FORUM THAT CRITICISES BOTH SIDES: THE FORUM DES ORGANISATIONS NATIONALES DES DROITS HUMAINS EN MAURITANIE (FONADH) ISSUES JOINT DECLARATIONS DATED AND PLACED AT NOUAKCHOTT, WITH ITS MEMBER ORGANISATIONS LISTED IN NUMBERED ORDER BENEATH THE TEXT — the first named being the Association Mauritanienne des Droits de l'Homme. A numbered signatory list under a dated declaration is a coalition you can join and a document you can cite. If your community's complaint is a rights complaint, ask FONADH what it takes to be a signatory — the list is the membership. AND WHAT MAKES IT USABLE RATHER THAN PARTISAN: IT RECALLS TO THE STATE ITS CONSTITUTIONAL COMMITMENTS IN MATTERS OF HUMAN RIGHTS, AS WELL AS ITS INTERNATIONAL COMMITMENTS RELATING TO FREEDOM OF THE PRESS, FREEDOM OF DEMONSTRATION, AN INDEPENDENT AND EQUITABLE JUSTICE, AND FREEDOM OF OPINION — AND IT STATES THAT IT OBSERVES THESE DRIFTS AS MUCH IN THE RANKS OF POWER AS IN THOSE OF THE OPPOSITION. A coalition that criticises the government and the opposition in the same declaration is one a village can approach without being annexed to somebody's political side. That neutrality is the practical value: it means the forum's support does not convert your land case into a party matter. Freedom of demonstration named among the commitments is the one that matters when a community wants to gather about a project. THE NATIONAL LIST, WITH NUMBERS TO RING: A PUBLISHED ONG NATIONALES PAGE CARRIES MAURITANIAN ORGANISATIONS WITH BP ADDRESSES, TELEPHONE NUMBERS AND THEIR STATED OBJECTS — including AED-MAURITANIE (ASSOCIATION POUR L'ENFANCE DÉSHÉRITÉE), BP 1488 NOUAKCHOTT; AMPIFSD, WITH A PUBLISHED TELEPHONE; AMSME; AND ENSEMBLE POUR LE DÉVELOPPEMENT ET LA SENSIBILISATION (EDS), with two telephone numbers. AND THE STATED OBJECTS ON THAT PAGE ARE WORTH READING BEFORE YOU CHOOSE WHO TO WRITE TO: REINFORCE THE CAPACITIES OF INDIVIDUALS AND COMMUNITIES TO PARTICIPATE EFFECTIVELY IN LOCAL AND NATIONAL LIFE AND TO RESOLVE THEIR PROBLEMS; PROMOTE, THROUGH APPROPRIATE EDUCATION AND CIVIC TRAINING, FAVOURABLE BEHAVIOUR IN THE DOMAINS OF CIVISM, HUMAN RIGHTS, THE ECONOMY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND HEALTH; AND WORK FOR THE REINFORCEMENT OF THE ECONOMIC, SOCIAL AND CULTURAL RIGHTS OF VULNERABLE OR MARGINALISED GROUPS AND THE CONSOLIDATION OF THE RULE OF LAW. Economic, social and cultural rights of marginalised groups is the legal category a land loss actually falls under — not civil liberties. An organisation that names ESC rights in its own object is one whose mandate already covers what happened to you. THE DATABASE THAT SORTS BY WHAT KIND OF BODY IT IS: A SEARCHABLE ORGANISM DATABASE IS FILTERABLE BY COUNTRY AND BY ORGANISATION TYPE — WITH TYPES INCLUDING ASSOCIATION DE JEUNES, ASSOCIATION DE MIGRANTS, ASSOCIATION DE MAIRES AND ONG — LISTING EACH ENTRY WITH ITS CITY AND REGION. Filtering by TYPE is the useful part, and note the ASSOCIATION DE MAIRES: an association of mayors is a body that can be asked to take a position on a project affecting several communes at once, which no single mayor will do alone. AND FOR THE FOREIGN ORGANISATIONS: A PUBLISHED CONTACT SHEET LISTS THE INTERNATIONAL NGOs PRESENT IN MAURITANIA WITH BP, TELEPHONE AND FAX FOR EACH, AND NAMES A COORDINATION ORGANISATION FOR MOST OF THEM, BASED AT A NAMED SEAT IN NOUAKCHOTT. One coordination body for most of the international NGOs in the country is a single door to the funded organisations. Write there and ask which member works in your wilaya rather than writing to twenty. THE STATE SIDE, NAMED: MAURITANIA HAS A COMMISSARIAT AUX DROITS DE L'HOMME, À L'ACTION HUMANITAIRE ET AUX RELATIONS AVEC LA SOCIÉTÉ CIVILE. Relations with civil society sits inside the same commissariat as human rights and humanitarian action. That is the office an association writes to when it wants the state to acknowledge it — and the pairing tells you the state treats civil society as a rights-and-relief matter, which is the register to write in. WHO IT SUITS: Mauritanian communities with a rights or land complaint, associations seeking a coalition, and anyone needing an organisation in their wilaya. CAVEATS: SOME PUBLISHED CONTACT SHEETS ARE OLDER — confirm numbers before relying. For the state's own register of environmental NGOs, Mauritania's environment ministry NGO database entry; for the friends-of-the-park association defending an island, AABA and Nafore; for the wetlands and waterbird association with its récépissé number, Nature Mauritanie; for an endowment paying running costs in perpetuity, BACoMaB; for the Imraguen sail-only right, the Banc d'Arguin entry.

trackers.name: ResourceContracts.org and OpenLandContracts.org (CCSI, the World Bank and NRGI) — the repository holding 1,300+ land and extractives contracts from 89 countries, the free mapping template and helpdesk behind it, and the African network whose portal review the procurement authority adopted 70% of
trackers.desc: THE CONTRACT OVER YOUR LAND MAY ALREADY BE PUBLISHED — placement note first: THE ANTI-CORRUPTION COALITION DOMAIN IS ALREADY USED UNDER DJIBOUTI, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS FILED IN MAURITANIA AND THAT DOMAIN IS NOT USED HERE. THE REPOSITORY, AND IT IS THE FIND: A GLOBAL CONTRACT REPOSITORY HOSTING OVER 1,300 CONTRACTS AND ASSOCIATED DOCUMENTS FROM 89 COUNTRIES — DISCUSSED IN A SESSION SPECIFICALLY ON HOW TO OPEN UP LAND AND EXTRACTIVES CONTRACTS. Somewhere there is a signed document setting out what the company may do on your land, for how long, at what royalty, and with what obligations to you. This file has recorded community after community negotiating against a contract they have never read. Before commissioning research or hiring anyone, search the repository for your country and the company's name — it may simply be there, free. THE SPATIAL POINT, WHICH MATTERS FOR OVERLAYS: PARTICIPANTS DISCUSSED THE UNIQUE SPATIAL CONSIDERATIONS OF NATURAL RESOURCE INVESTMENTS — AND IMPORTANT STRIDES HAVE BEEN MADE THROUGH EFFORTS TO COLLECT AND ORGANIZE ONE AFRICAN COUNTRY'S CONCESSIONS DATA. Concessions data organised country-wide is what you lay over a community boundary to show the overlap — the exact operation this file's LandMark and MappingForRights entries describe. The boundary is your half; the concession layer is this half. WHO ELSE NEEDS THE SAME DOCUMENT, WHICH IS A USEFUL ARGUMENT: THE MOST IMPORTANT USE CASES CONCERNED HOW GOVERNMENTS COULD BETTER SHARE THIS INFORMATION AMONG THE MANY DIFFERENT AGENCIES — CADASTRAL, TAXATION, ENVIRONMENT AND FINANCE AMONG OTHERS — THAT USE CONTRACT DATA. Even the ministries do not share it with each other. So when a lands officer says he cannot show you the concession, he may genuinely not have it — which changes who you ask rather than whether you ask. THE FREE TECHNICAL HELP: A DATA STANDARD MAPPING TEMPLATE AND A HELPDESK PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE — AND A NAMED PERSON LEADS THE AFRICA PORTFOLIO WITH A PUBLISHED INVITATION TO ASK FOR SUPPORT. THE WORKED AFRICAN CASE, STEP BY STEP, AND IT IS COPYABLE: USING THE MAPPING TEMPLATE AND WITH TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE FROM THE PARTNERSHIP AND THE HELPDESK, A PAN-AFRICAN INFORMATION NETWORK CONDUCTED A MINI-MAPPING OF A GOVERNMENT PROCUREMENT PORTAL TO DETERMINE THE LEVEL OF DISCLOSURE AND HOW IT COULD BE IMPROVED TO ENABLE BETTER MONITORING BY CIVIL SOCIETY. THEY PRESENTED PRELIMINARY FINDINGS TO THE PROCUREMENT AUTHORITY, WHO NOTED THEY WERE THE FIRST ORGANIZATION TO PROVIDE FEEDBACK ON THE PORTAL SINCE IT WAS LAUNCHED TWO YEARS EARLIER, AND ENCOURAGED A FULL MAPPING — AFTER WHICH THE AUTHORITY RESOLVED TO IMPLEMENT OVER 70% OF THE RECOMMENDATIONS. THE FIRST ORGANIZATION TO GIVE FEEDBACK IN TWO YEARS.
