That is the sentence to hold onto: a government portal nobody was using, an agency that welcomed the criticism, and seventy per cent of the recommendations adopted. Reviewing a portal is unglamorous, cheap and available to any organisation with a laptop — and almost nobody does it. AND THE RELATIONSHIP THAT GREW OUT OF IT: HE CONTINUED TO SHARE INFORMATION WITH THE AUTHORITY INFORMALLY BEFORE THEY SIGNED A FORMAL AGREEMENT; WHEN A COALITION OF PROCUREMENT MONITORS WAS ESTABLISHED, THE AUTHORITY BEGAN HOSTING THEIR MEETINGS AND TRAINING THEM ON THE AGENCY'S PROCESSES — AND NOW THEY WORK VERY WARMLY AND VERY OPENLY IN A STRONG PARTNERSHIP. The regulator ended up hosting and training its own monitors. Where confrontation has failed, offering to check the agency's own system is a door that opens — and it produces access no complaint would have won. THE SECOND WORKED CASE, WHICH IS THE TEMPLATE FOR A COMMUNITY WITH NO SPECIALISTS: A NETWORK OF LOCAL CIVIL SOCIETY GROUPS CARRIED OUT A PUBLIC EXPENDITURE TRACKING EXERCISE — AFTER FILING ACCESS TO INFORMATION REQUESTS AND FOLLOWING UP WITH AUTHORITIES, A DISTRICT NETWORK DISCOVERED THAT THE SUPPLIER WHO WON THE CONTRACT HAD ALREADY BEEN PAID DESPITE FAILING TO DELIVER, AND THAT THE COMPANY HAD NO PRIOR EXPERIENCE IN THE FIELD — ITS CORE BUSINESS WAS PHONE AND ELECTRICAL SUPPLIES. THANKS TO THE INVESTIGATION, THE COMPANY HAD TO REFUND THE PAYMENT. Two questions did it: has this been paid for, and has this company ever done this work before. A district network with no lawyers recovered public money by asking them in writing. Ask the same two about whoever holds the contract on your land — a firm whose core business is something else entirely is the commonest sign of a contract awarded for other reasons. THE PAN-AFRICAN NETWORK BEHIND BOTH: A MEMBERSHIP-BASED CIVIL SOCIETY NETWORK AND RESOURCE CENTER PROMOTING THE RIGHT OF ACCESS TO INFORMATION, TRANSPARENCY AND ACCOUNTABILITY ACROSS AFRICA — WHICH HAS WORKED ON DISCLOSURE, PUBLIC PARTICIPATION, EFFICIENCY, VALUE FOR MONEY AND COMPETITION IN PUBLIC CONTRACTING IN FIVE NAMED AFRICAN COUNTRIES. MEMBERSHIP-BASED means your organisation can join it, and access-to-information is its core subject — which is the skill most needed to get the contract in the first place. AND THE ACCELERATOR: AN IMPACT ACCELERATOR THAT HELPS TEAMS OF BOLD PROCUREMENT REFORMERS PROPEL THEIR AMBITIOUS PLANS TOWARD SYSTEMIC CHANGE, SUPPORTING TEAMS AROUND THE WORLD TO USE PUBLIC CONTRACTING TO IMPROVE EFFECTIVE GOVERNANCE AND SUPPORT MORE EQUITABLE AND GREEN OUTCOMES. WHO IT SUITS: African communities and organisations trying to obtain, read or check the contract, concession or permit governing land near them. CAVEATS: COVERAGE IS UNEVEN AND MANY AFRICAN GOVERNMENTS PUBLISH LITTLE OR NOTHING — absence from the repository means unpublished, not non-existent. For the platform showing concessions against community boundaries, Mali's LandMark entry; for the source-document repository and data analysts who help you search, Guinea-Bissau's civic-tech entry; for free advice where a contract was obtained by bribe, Mali's advice centres entry.

trackers.name: ROPPA (Réseau des Organisations Paysannes et de Producteurs de l'Afrique de l'Ouest) — the West African peasant federation founded by a hundred farmer leaders, with 13 named national members and associate members, three published operating principles including regular renewal of mandates, and an open door to the rest of the region
trackers.desc: THIRTEEN COUNTRIES, IN FRENCH, AND THE DOOR IS OPEN — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S MALI ENTRY COVERS THE ANGLOPHONE EASTERN AND SOUTHERN AFRICAN FARMERS' FORUM AND ITS LIBYA ENTRY THE PAN-AFRICAN FOOD SOVEREIGNTY ALLIANCE. THIS IS THE WEST AFRICAN FRANCOPHONE COUNTERPART; NEITHER IS RESTATED AND NEITHER HOST IS SHIPPED. A GLOBAL LAND COALITION IS A HOST UNDER GHANA, LIBERIA AND MALAWI AND IS LIKEWISE NOT SHIPPED. WHOSE INITIATIVE IT IS, AND IT IS THE FIND: AN INITIATIVE PROPER TO THE PEASANT AND AGRICULTURAL PRODUCER ORGANISATIONS OF WEST AFRICA — FORMALLY FOUNDED IN JUNE 2000 AT COTONOU AT A MEETING THAT BROUGHT TOGETHER ABOUT A HUNDRED PEASANT LEADERS MANDATED BY THEIR OWN ORGANISATIONS. MANDATED BY THEIR OWN ORGANISATIONS. Not invited, not selected by a donor — sent, with authority, by the bodies they came from. This file has recorded the difference that makes when a delegation is challenged on who it speaks for. THE THIRTEEN NAMED NATIONAL MEMBERS: BENIN, BURKINA FASO, CÔTE D'IVOIRE, THE GAMBIA, GHANA, GUINEA, GUINEA-BISSAU, LIBERIA, MALI, NIGER, SENEGAL, SIERRA LEONE AND TOGO — PLUS ASSOCIATE MEMBER PEASANT ORGANISATIONS IN CAPE VERDE AND NIGERIA. Both anglophone and francophone countries in one federation, working in French. Almost every continental resource in this file arrives in English; for a farmers' organisation in Niger, Mali or Guinea this is the one that does not need translating. THE OPEN DOOR, STATED: THIS GROUPING IS NOT CLOSED, AND THE MEDIUM-TERM AMBITION IS TO WELCOME PEASANT ORGANISATIONS FROM ALL THE COUNTRIES OF THE WEST AFRICAN ECONOMIC COMMUNITY, WHICH REPRESENTS THE REAL WEST AFRICA. An explicit invitation to countries not yet in. If your national farmers' organisation is absent from that list, joining is a stated ambition of theirs rather than a favour to ask. THE THREE PUBLISHED OPERATING PRINCIPLES, AND THE THIRD IS THE ONE TO COPY: PEASANT SOLIDARITY, WHICH GIVES A PLACE TO EVERYONE BY ASSOCIATING ALL CATEGORIES OF PEASANT AND AGRICULTURAL PRODUCER ORGANISATIONS IN EACH COUNTRY, AND SUPPORTS THEM AND THEIR MEMBERS IN THE RECOGNITION OF THEIR IDENTITY, THEIR RIGHTS AND THEIR ROLES; CONSENSUS, AS THE PREFERRED METHOD FOR DECIDING AND ACTING TOGETHER; AND TRANSPARENCY, BY RENDERING ACCOUNT AND ENSURING THE REGULAR RENEWAL OF MANDATES. REGULAR RENEWAL OF MANDATES, written into the founding principles. This file has recorded again and again that community organisations are lost not to opponents but to leaders who never leave. A federation that names term renewal as one of three principles is showing the clause every village committee should have in its own constitution. ALL CATEGORIES OF ORGANISATION IN EACH COUNTRY is the other clause worth taking. Herders, fishers, women's groups and small growers inside one national body rather than competing for the same ministry's attention. THE DECENTRALISATION APPROACH: AT THE LEVEL OF WEST AFRICAN COUNTRIES IT FOLLOWS AN APPROACH THAT PROGRESSIVELY GIVES MORE RESPONSIBILITY TO THE TERRITORIAL LEVELS AT THE BASE. Power moving downward on purpose. That is the opposite of the pattern this file records, where a national body accumulates the funding and the seats while the villages supply the legitimacy. WHAT IT POSITIONED ITSELF AS: THE INSTRUMENT OF DEFENCE AND PROMOTION OF FAMILY FARMS, WHICH CONSTITUTE THE PRINCIPAL AGRO-SYLVO-PASTORAL PRODUCTION SYSTEM IN WEST AFRICA. AGRO-SYLVO-PASTORAL — farming, forest and grazing treated as one system. That single term is the answer to a land classification that calls a fallow field empty and a grazing range unused, and it is worth using in submissions. ITS PUBLISHED OBJECTIVES: PROMOTE AND DEFEND THE VALUES OF EFFICIENT AND SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE FOR FAMILY FARMS; INFORM AND TRAIN MEMBERS OF PEASANT ORGANISATIONS BASED ON THE RELEVANT EXPERIENCES OF ITS OWN MEMBERS; AND ENCOURAGE AND SUPPORT DIALOGUE AND STRUCTURING OF FARMERS ORGANISATIONS IN EACH COUNTRY FOR PARTICIPATION AND INVOLVEMENT IN THE DEFINITION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF AGRICULTURAL AND RURAL SECTOR DEVELOPMENT POLICIES. TRAIN MEMBERS BASED ON THE EXPERIENCES OF ITS OWN MEMBERS. The curriculum is other West African farmers' cases, not an imported syllabus — which is the same principle the file's Guinea-Bissau and Cape Verde entries record working elsewhere. THE LAND THEMES IT IS INDEXED UNDER BY A GLOBAL LAND COALITION: SECURE TENURE RIGHTS; STRONG SMALL-SCALE FARMING SYSTEMS; AND EQUAL LAND RIGHTS FOR WOMEN. THE INFORMATION RELAY BESIDE IT: A WEST AFRICAN AGROECOLOGY ALLIANCE DESCRIBED AS A COORDINATION AND INFORMATION-RELAY PLATFORM COMPOSED OF PEASANT ORGANISATIONS. AND THE REGIONAL FORUM ON RECORD: A REGIONAL FORUM ON AGROECOLOGY, ORGANIC AGRICULTURE AND CLIMATE-SMART AGRICULTURE IN WEST AFRICA, HELD IN ABUJA FROM 21 TO 24 OCTOBER 2024, ORGANISED BY AN INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATION, A WEST AFRICAN ORGANIC NETWORK AND THAT ALLIANCE — BRINGING TOGETHER MORE THAN 350 PARTICIPANTS FROM REGIONAL INSTITUTIONS, SECTORAL MINISTRIES AND NETWORKS OF PEASANT ORGANISATIONS, WITH A PUBLISHED FINAL COMMUNIQUÉ. Ministries and peasant networks in the same room, with the communiqué published. A document your own ministry's delegation signed is a commitment you can quote back at a district meeting — and it is free to download. WHO IT SUITS: West African farmer, herder and producer organisations, especially francophone ones that find continental resources arriving only in English. CAVEATS: MEMBERSHIP IS FOR NATIONAL PEASANT ORGANISATIONS, NOT INDIVIDUAL VILLAGES OR NGOs, AND IT IS AN ADVOCACY FEDERATION RATHER THAN A FUNDER — a village group joins its national member first. For the eastern and southern African farmers' forum and its district structure, Mali's entry; for the pan-African alliance with an open WhatsApp community, Libya's entry; for the pastoralist coalition and its regional focal points, Tanzania's PINGO's Forum entry.

trackers.name: One million US dollars a year for 15 to 50+ years into a single landscape, with consortia including local community, grassroots and Indigenous organisations strongly encouraged — and community conserved areas named as eligible grantees
trackers.desc: A MILLION DOLLARS A YEAR FOR FIFTY YEARS, AND THEY WANT A COMMUNITY ORGANISATION IN THE CONSORTIUM — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S SOUTH AFRICA AND MADAGASCAR ENTRIES CARRY A LAND-PURCHASE FUNDER HOST, ITS TANZANIA ENTRY A RAINFOREST FUNDER THAT FUNDS LOCAL ORGANISATIONS, ITS KENYA ENTRY A COMMUNITY LAND TRUST, AND ITS ERITREA ENTRY THE WORLD HERITAGE REPORTING ROUTE — SEVERAL SITES BELOW ARE WORLD HERITAGE LISTED. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE CONSORTIUM ENCOURAGEMENT, WHICH IS THE FIND: APPLICATIONS FROM CONSORTIA, SPECIFICALLY THOSE INCLUDING LOCAL COMMUNITY, GRASSROOTS, AND INDIGENOUS ORGANIZATIONS, ARE STRONGLY ENCOURAGED. A community organisation cannot meet these eligibility conditions alone — but its presence in the consortium is something the fund actively wants. That reverses the usual bargaining position this file records, where a village is invited late and told what has been decided. Here the international NGO needs you named on the application, which is the moment to negotiate what your organisation gets, decides and holds. WHO MAY BE A GRANTEE: NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS OR LOCALLY BASED ACTORS — INCLUDING INDIGENOUS AND COMMUNITY CONSERVED AREAS — WITH PROVEN CREDENTIALS. COMMUNITY CONSERVED AREAS named as possible grantees in their own right, not only as consortium members. A community that has already declared and governs its own conserved area is inside the definition. THE SUM AND THE TERM, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: ONE MILLION USD PER YEAR PER LANDSCAPE, EITHER AS A GUARANTEED SUM ANNUALLY FOR AS LONG AS POSSIBLE — CURRENTLY ESTIMATED AT 50+ YEARS — OR, IN APPROVED AFRICAN CASES, FOR AT LEAST 15 YEARS. Fifty years of guaranteed baseline money is a different instrument from every grant in this file. It outlasts governments, donors and staff — and it is the answer to the pattern recorded here again and again, where a protected area is gazetted, funded for three years, then quietly abandoned to whoever wants the timber. WHAT THAT MONEY IS FOR: LONG-TERM, DEPENDABLE BASELINE FUNDING CONTRIBUTING TO THE CORE FINANCING OF MANAGEMENT OF PROTECTED AREAS AND THEIR BUFFER ZONES — ADDRESSING THE LACK OF A SECURED FUNDING SOURCE TO COVER BASIC MANAGEMENT AND PROTECTION COSTS, WIDELY IDENTIFIED AS THE BOTTLENECK. BASELINE AND CORE, not projects. Salaries, patrols, fuel, boundary maintenance — the costs this file has recorded nobody funding. THE PUBLISHED ELIGIBILITY CONDITIONS: A TRACK RECORD OF IMPACTFUL CONSERVATION WORK AT SCALE; EXPERIENCE IMPLEMENTING LARGE GRANTS INCLUDING FINANCIAL AND ADMINISTRATIVE SYSTEMS SUFFICIENT TO MANAGE THEM; A LEGAL BASE TO WORK IN THE COUNTRY AND THE LANDSCAPE, SUCH AS A MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING; FAMILIARITY AND ESTABLISHED TRUSTFUL RELATIONS WITH RELEVANT GOVERNMENT AGENCIES, LOCAL COMMUNITIES, GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS AND LOCAL STAKEHOLDER GROUPS; AND ADHERENCE TO A SOCIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SAFEGUARDS SYSTEM. TRUSTFUL RELATIONS WITH LOCAL COMMUNITIES is a stated eligibility condition. A community that publicly disputes an applicant's conduct is speaking to a criterion the fund has written down — and the SAFEGUARDS SYSTEM is the document to ask for and hold the grantee to once money is flowing. THE SIZE FLOOR THAT DECIDES ELIGIBILITY IMMEDIATELY: A CONTIGUOUS AREA OF AT LEAST 2,000 SQUARE KILOMETRES THAT IS MOSTLY BIOLOGICALLY INTACT; AT LEAST 50% CLASSIFIED IN A NAMED INTERNATIONAL PROTECTED-AREA CATEGORY, WITH SOME RECOGNITION AND LEGAL PROTECTION ESTABLISHED ON THE REMAINDER. AND THE OTHER FLOOR, STATED PLAINLY: LANDSCAPES REQUIRING LESS THAN 1 MILLION USD ANNUALLY ON A SUSTAINED BASIS ARE NOT ELIGIBLE — FOR ADMINISTRATIVE COST REASONS, THE FUND IS DESIGNED TO FOCUS ON LARGER PROJECTS. Two thousand square kilometres, and too small to spend a million a year is a disqualification. Most communities in this file are defending a fraction of that, and should read these two lines first rather than last. The honest use of this entry for a smaller place is the opposite direction: find out whether your land sits inside or beside an existing legacy landscape, because then the money is already there and the buffer zone rules apply to you. THE BUFFER ZONE AND WHAT IT MEANS FOR NEIGHBOURS: THE LANDSCAPE WILL TYPICALLY BE SURROUNDED OR ADJOINED BY A BUFFER ZONE WHERE, EITHER BY REGULATION OR MANAGEMENT PRACTICE, IT IS RECOGNIZED THAT ECONOMIC ACTIVITIES SHOULD BE LIMITED TO THOSE CONSISTENT WITH THE CONSERVATION VALUES OF THE LANDSCAPE — AND ELIGIBLE ACTIVITIES ARE DIRECTED TO THE LANDSCAPE AND ITS BUFFER ZONE. The buffer zone cuts both ways and communities should know which way it is being used near them. It restricts what neighbours may do with their own land — and it also makes them eligible for the grant activities, since spending is explicitly allowed there. If a buffer zone is limiting your farming, ask what share of that million is being spent on your side of the line. WHO IMPLEMENTS ON SITE: CONSERVATION ACTIVITIES ARE IMPLEMENTED JOINTLY BY PROTECTED AREA AUTHORITIES, LOCAL COMMUNITIES, AND EXPERIENCED CONSERVATION ORGANIZATIONS — WITH THE FUND SEEKING COLLABORATIONS OVER AN EXTENDED PERIOD BETWEEN NGOs, AUTHORITIES, LOCAL POPULATIONS AND CO-DONORS. THE AFRICAN COUNTRY LIST FROM ONE PUBLISHED CALL: BENIN, BURKINA FASO, BURUNDI, THE CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC, CHAD, COMOROS, THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO, DJIBOUTI, ETHIOPIA, THE GAMBIA, GUINEA, LIBERIA, MADAGASCAR, MALI, MAURITANIA, NIGER, SENEGAL AND TOGO. Eighteen African countries in one call, several of them places this file has recorded as having almost no conservation finance at all. THE APPROVED AFRICAN SITES ON RECORD: TWO NATIONAL PARKS, ONE IN THE REPUBLIC OF CONGO AND ONE IN ZIMBABWE, WITH CONSERVATION IMPLEMENTED BY TWO NAMED ORGANISATIONS — BOTH LABELLED KEY BIODIVERSITY AREAS AS WELL AS WORLD HERITAGE SITES. World heritage listed, which means the civil society reporting route filed under Eritrea reaches the same sites. A community inside or beside one of these landscapes has both a funded manager to negotiate with and an international body that accepts its own account of what is happening. AND THE PORTFOLIO TARGET AND CALL STATUS: A DIVERSE PORTFOLIO OF 30+ PROTECTED AREAS BY 2030, COVERING AT LEAST 60,000 SQUARE KILOMETRES — WITH CALLS FOR APPLICATIONS CURRENTLY CLOSED AND A PUBLISHED OPEN CALLS PAGE TO CHECK REGULARLY. Closed at the time of writing, with the target not yet met — so more calls are expected, and a consortium assembled in advance is the one that can answer a short window. WHO IT SUITS: African conservation organisations and community bodies at or beside very large protected landscapes — and communities who should know a fifty-year funder may be arriving next door. CAVEATS: 2,000 KM² MINIMUM, A MILLION A YEAR MINIMUM, LARGE-GRANT EXPERIENCE REQUIRED, AND CALLS ARE PERIODIC — small sites are outside it entirely. For a funder that buys land outright, South Africa's entry; for one that funds a local organisation to hold the reserve, Tanzania's entry; for the community land trust model, Kenya's entry.

trackers.name: Activist lawyers using the law to protect ecosystems across Southern Africa in partnership with communities — filed with the published means test that decides who free environmental representation is available to, and the pro bono routes for everyone who fails it
trackers.desc: ACTIVIST LAWYERS, AND THE MEANS TEST THAT DECIDES WHO THEY TAKE — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S SOUTH AFRICA BUCKET MENTIONS THIS CENTRE INSIDE A GREEN TRUST'S PUBLISHED MEMBERSHIP LIST, AND ITS MOZAMBIQUE ENTRY NAMES IT AS A RELATED BODY OF THE LAW FIRM; NEITHER DESCRIBES IT AND NEITHER HOST IS SHIPPED. THE SOUTH AFRICA BUCKET ALSO CARRIES A CENTRE FOR ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS HOST AND A LEGAL RESOURCES CENTRE HOST, AND A SOUTHERN AFRICA LITIGATION CENTRE IS A NAME IN TWELVE BUCKETS. NONE IS RESTATED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. WHAT THEY CALL THEMSELVES, WHICH IS THE FIND: WE ARE ACTIVIST LAWYERS WHO SEEK TO USE THE LAW TO PROTECT AND RESTORE ECOSYSTEMS IN SOUTHERN AFRICA. ACTIVIST LAWYERS, in their own words on their own front page. That is a different proposition from a firm that takes environmental instructions — and it tells a community what kind of case they are looking for before the first conversation. HOW THE HELP REACHES A COMMUNITY: BY PARTNERING WITH COMMUNITIES AND OTHER CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, WE PROVIDE LEGAL ADVICE AND SUPPORT. PARTNERING rather than representing. Worth clarifying at the outset which one is on offer in your case, because advice and support to somebody else's litigation is a different thing from carrying the file. THE LIVELIHOODS CLAUSE IN THE VISION, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE VISION IS OF FLOURISHING INDIGENOUS SPECIES AND ECOSYSTEMS THAT SUPPORT SUSTAINABLE LIVELIHOODS IN SOUTHERN AFRICA. Livelihoods written into a biodiversity organisation's own vision. A community arguing that the wetland or forest feeds it is on-mission here, not making a social argument to a conservation body — which this file has recorded communities being asked to drop. WHERE THEY AIM THE WORK: WE IDENTIFY WHERE LEGAL INTERVENTIONS CAN HAVE THE MOST POWERFUL IMPACTS ON BIODIVERSITY CONSERVATION WITHIN SOUTHERN AFRICA — PRIORITISING INTERVENTIONS THAT WILL HAVE IMPACTS AT SCALE, USING RESPONSES THAT ARE BOTH REACTIVE AND PROACTIVE. IMPACTS AT SCALE is the selection rule, and it is the same one this file records at Seychelles and Central African Republic: a case that changes only one place is the weaker candidate. Frame the request around what the ruling would settle for everyone. WHAT THEY TARGET: LAW, POLICY AND THE INSTITUTIONS THAT FORMULATE AND IMPLEMENT THESE LAWS AND POLICIES — INFLUENCING THE DESIGN OF LAW AND POLICY, INFLUENCING DECISION-MAKING, AND COLLABORATING WITH CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, COMMUNITIES AND OTHER STAKEHOLDERS. THE INSTITUTIONS THAT IMPLEMENT is the part communities feel. A permitting office that always says yes is a target here, not merely a fact of life. THE WETLAND CASE ON RECORD: WE WORK WITH PARTNER ORGANISATIONS TO ADDRESS THREATS TO A NAMED UNIQUE WETLAND OF INTERNATIONAL IMPORTANCE. Read that beside the wetlands treaty mechanism filed under South Sudan and the community open letter filed under Chad: a wetland of international importance has a treaty secretariat, a civil society reporting route AND lawyers in the region working on exactly that category of site. THE REGIONAL SCOPE: SOUTHERN AFRICA RATHER THAN A SINGLE COUNTRY. AND — THE PUBLISHED GATE ANY COMMUNITY MEETS WHEN SEEKING FREE ENVIRONMENTAL REPRESENTATION IN THIS REGION, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE NO OTHER ENTRY IN THIS FILE STATES IT: IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW SOCIETY REQUIREMENTS, CASES ARE ONLY CONSIDERED WHERE THE PERSON OR ORGANISATION REQUESTING ADVICE IS UNABLE TO AFFORD TO ENGAGE THE SERVICES OF PRIVATE ENVIRONMENTAL ATTORNEYS, OR UNABLE REASONABLY TO ACCESS THE RESOURCES REQUIRED TO ENGAGE SUCH SERVICES. The means test is a professional rule, not a preference. A community organisation that has any funding at all should expect to be asked why it cannot pay — and the second limb, being unable REASONABLY TO ACCESS the resources, is the one a rural committee with a small grant should be answering, because distance and capacity count, not only cash. THE SECOND HALF OF THAT GATE: ONLY A LIMITED NUMBER OF STRATEGICALLY SELECTED CASES ARE TAKEN, THOSE WITH THE POTENTIAL TO RESULT IN SYSTEMIC CHANGES PROMOTING ENVIRONMENTAL AND CLIMATE JUSTICE AND THE REALISATION OF CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHTS — WITH BASIC SELF-HELP INFORMATION PUBLISHED FOR EVERYONE ELSE. Two filters, both of which a strong case can fail: too able to pay, or too local to matter. SELF-HELP INFORMATION is what the majority actually receive, and it is published rather than withheld. THE OTHER PUBLISHED ROUTE FOR THOSE WHO DO NOT QUALIFY: A PRO BONO REQUEST FORM DOWNLOADABLE FROM THE LEGAL PRACTICE COUNCIL, WITH A MEANS TEST AND A REQUIREMENT THAT THE LEGAL PROBLEM HAVE MERIT — AND WHERE A REFERRAL IS MADE, THE CLIENT IS RESPONSIBLE ONLY FOR THE COST OF DISBURSEMENTS SUCH AS SHERIFFS' FEES, WITH THE ATTORNEY CHARGING NO FEES. A downloadable form from the statutory regulator of the profession, and the attorney's fees fall away entirely. Disbursements remain, which is the cost the litigation funds elsewhere in this file exist to cover — the two together are a complete answer for a community with no money at all. THE CLEARING HOUSE OPTION RECORDED ALONGSIDE IT: A PRO BONO ORGANISATION RUNNING A GENERAL LEGAL CLEARING HOUSE WHERE CLIENTS ARE CONSULTED, ASSESSED AND REFERRED TO PRIVATE LAWYERS FOR FREE ASSISTANCE, ASSISTING OVER 6,500 CLIENTS PER ANNUM VIA TWO CITY OFFICES AND HOLDING FREE WEEKLY LEGAL CLINICS INCLUDING ONES FOR NGOs AND COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS. A weekly clinic specifically for NGOs and community-based organisations, walk-in. That is the lowest-threshold legal door recorded anywhere in this file. AND THE UNIVERSITY ROUTE: LAW FACULTY LAW CLINICS PROVIDING FREE LEGAL SERVICES TO INDIGENT AND MARGINALISED COMMUNITIES IN THEIR SURROUNDING REGIONS. A university law clinic is permanent, local and free, and its supervising attorneys are qualified. For a community near any law faculty, that is the first call rather than the last. WHO IT SUITS: Southern African communities and organisations facing threats to wetlands, forests and indigenous ecosystems — and anyone needing to know why free environmental representation was refused, and where to go next. CAVEATS: A SMALL SPECIALIST CENTRE TAKING SELECTED HIGH-IMPACT WORK IN SOUTHERN AFRICA, PARTNERING RATHER THAN NECESSARILY REPRESENTING, AND SUBJECT TO THE MEANS TEST ABOVE — the pro bono form, the clearing house and the university clinics are the routes when it says no. For a named commercial environmental firm, Mozambique's entry; for the fishers' co-operative litigation structure, Mali's entry.

trackers.name: Ndifuna Ukwazi Law Centre, Cape Town — an accredited law clinic taking eviction and tenancy cases free, subject only to a basic means test — walk-in Tuesdays and Wednesdays 9am to 3pm, a named paralegal reachable by WhatsApp, a free 12-week course on the laws that govern evictions, and a stated list of what it will not take
trackers.desc: A WALK-IN LAW CLINIC WITH A WHATSAPP NUMBER AND NO FEE — method and adjacency declared first: THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN TWO HOSTS AND FIVE SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL ABSENT. THIS FILE'S SOUTH AFRICA BUCKET CARRIES TWO OTHER NATIONAL PUBLIC-INTEREST LAW HOSTS; ITS MAURITIUS ENTRY THE PRO BONO CLEARING HOUSE, ITS MAURITANIA ENTRY THE PUBLISHED MEANS TEST FOR ENVIRONMENTAL REPRESENTATION, ITS MALAWI ENTRY THE EVICTION GUIDE. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE CLINIC, ITS DAYS AND ITS DOOR POLICY, WHICH IS THE FIND: A HOUSING CLINIC OPEN ON TUESDAYS AND WEDNESDAYS FROM 9AM TO 3PM, WORKING ON A FIRST-COME FIRST-SERVE BASIS TO ACCOMMODATE WALK-INS, BUT ENCOURAGING PEOPLE TO MAKE AN APPOINTMENT THROUGH A NAMED POLITICAL ORGANISER AND PARALEGAL — REACHABLE BY CALL OR WHATSAPP ON A PUBLISHED MOBILE NUMBER OR BY DIRECT EMAIL, ALONGSIDE A PUBLISHED LANDLINE AND CLINIC EMAIL. A named person with a mobile number you can message. Almost every legal resource in this file is an institution with a general inbox; here there is a paralegal whose direct WhatsApp is published, which is the difference between a query that is answered and one that joins a queue. And the walk-in policy means someone with no phone credit can still arrive on a Tuesday. WHAT IT COSTS AND THE ONE CONDITION, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: WE PROVIDE PRO-BONO (FREE) LEGAL ADVICE FOR MATTERS RELATED TO HOUSING AND EVICTION; WE DO NOT CHARGE FOR OUR SERVICES, BUT AN INDIVIDUAL OR HOUSEHOLD MUST MEET THE BASIC MEANS TEST — AND WE DO NOT HAVE ANY ADDITIONAL QUALIFICATION CRITERIA IN ORDER TO BE ASSISTED WITH LEGAL ADVICE ON MATTERS WITHIN OUR EXPERTISE. NO ADDITIONAL QUALIFICATION CRITERIA. One test, stated once, and nothing else hidden behind it — which is worth contrasting with the layered eligibility this file has recorded elsewhere. Bring proof of income and the question is settled in one visit. WHAT IT WILL NOT TAKE, SAID PLAINLY: WE DO NOT PROVIDE ASSISTANCE FOR INHERITANCE OR ESTATE RELATED ISSUES. Filed because it saves a wasted journey, and because it marks a real gap: inheritance is how much of the land loss recorded in this file actually happens, and this clinic is not the place for it. The women lawyers association in this file's Gambia entry handles exactly that. ITS ACCREDITATION AND WHAT THE CLINIC ACTUALLY DOES: ACCREDITED AS A LAW CLINIC IN JUNE 2015 AND OPERATING AS A LAW CENTRE, PROVIDING LEGAL ASSISTANCE — LEGAL ADVICE AND LEGAL REPRESENTATION — TO QUALIFYING INDIVIDUALS, HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES FACING EVICTIONS AND LANDLORD AND TENANT DISPUTES. REPRESENTATION, not only advice, and COMMUNITIES as well as households. Accreditation as a law clinic is what lets it appear in court rather than refer you onward. WHO IT SPECIALISES IN HELPING: TENANTS WHO WOULD BE FACING AN EVICTION APPLICATION, WHO HAVE BEEN ILLEGALLY EVICTED, AND WHO ARE FACING UNFAIR RENTAL PRACTICES LIKE EXORBITANT RENT INCREASES. All three stages: before the application, after an illegal eviction, and the rent squeeze that precedes both. The first is the one people miss — come when the notice arrives, not when the sheriff does. THE FREE COURSE, ITS LENGTH AND ITS VENUE: A FREE 12-WEEK WEEKLY COMMUNITY EDUCATION PROGRAMME OPEN TO ANY MEMBER OF THE PUBLIC, AT A NAMED RECREATION CENTRE ON A NAMED STREET — DESIGNED TO HELP PARTICIPANTS UNDERSTAND THE LAWS THAT GOVERN EVICTIONS AND TENANT-LANDLORD ISSUES, EQUIPPING THEM WITH THE LEGAL AND POLITICAL KNOWLEDGE TO TACKLE UNFAIR PRACTICES OR RESIST UNJUST EVICTIONS, THROUGH BOTH THE LAW AND THE EXPERIENCES OF COMMUNITY MEMBERS AND ACTIVISTS. Twelve weeks, free, open to anyone, in a community hall rather than a lecture theatre. Read beside this file's Mali entry, where lawyers teach the laws that justify eviction: the same instinct, and here it runs as a standing course with a venue and a start date. WHAT THE ASSEMBLY FORMAT IS FOR: THE LAW IS MADE ACCESSIBLE AND PEOPLE ARE LINKED TO COMMUNITY ORGANISING AND ACTIVISM — THROUGH THESE ASSEMBLIES, TENANTS HAVE THE POWER TO PLAN ACTIONS TO RESIST UNLAWFUL AND UNJUST EVICTIONS. The course is also the organising route: people who arrive as individuals with a problem leave as part of a body that can act together. THE FOUR WORKING AREAS: RESISTING EVICTIONS AND DISPLACEMENT; EQUITABLE ACCESS TO LAND AND HOUSING; SECURITY OF TENURE; AND COMMUNITY ORGANISING AND MOVEMENT BUILDING — WITH THE TENURE PROGRAMME AIMED AT SECURING LONG TERM TENURE RIGHTS FOR THE LANDLESS AND HOMELESS. THE THEORY IT WORKS BY: LEVERAGE FOR SOCIAL CHANGE IS CREATED BY BRINGING TOGETHER THE USE OF THE LAW, EVIDENCE-BASED RESEARCH, MEDIA ADVOCACY AND, IMPORTANTLY, A MOVEMENT OF PEOPLE. The law is one of four ingredients and explicitly not sufficient alone. That is the honest reading of every legal resource in this file. WHAT ELSE IT SPECIALISES IN, WHICH IS UNUSUAL FOR A LAW CENTRE: COMMUNITY BASED SOCIAL AUDITING OF SERVICE DELIVERY; ACCESS TO INFORMATION AND PROCUREMENT MONITORING AT THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT LEVEL; BUDGET ANALYSIS AND ADVOCACY; AND ACTIVIST EDUCATION. PROCUREMENT MONITORING AND BUDGET ANALYSIS at municipal level. That is how a community finds out what its council has actually committed to spend and to whom — often the fastest way to establish who benefits from a development before anyone announces it. THE CONDITION IT DOCUMENTS: AS OF 2017, THE CITY OFFERS LITTLE SUPPORT TO RESIDENTS WHO WILL BECOME HOMELESS BECAUSE OF EVICTION, EXCEPT A ONE WAY TICKET TO A RELOCATION CAMP ON THE PERIPHERY OF THE CITY. The relocation camp on the periphery is the standard offer, and naming it early in a negotiation stops it being presented as generosity. AND THE ONLINE TOOL AND THE STUDENT ROUTE: A SEPARATE ORGANISATION HAS DEVELOPED AN ONLINE TOOL TO HELP PEOPLE FIND FREE LEGAL INFORMATION ON EVICTIONS NATIONALLY, WITH A DIRECTORY OF LEGAL SUPPORT OFFICES — AND THE LAW CENTRE RUNS A TWO-WEEK STUDENT VACATION PROGRAMME INCLUDING TOURS OF THE HIGH COURT, MAGISTRATES' COURT AND RENTAL HOUSING TRIBUNAL, WITH STUDENTS SHADOWING ATTORNEYS DURING CLINIC CONSULTATIONS. A national directory of free legal support offices for evictions, searchable, run by someone else — which is the answer for anyone outside this one city. And the student programme is how a law faculty becomes a supply of people who know eviction work. WHO IT SUITS: tenants and communities in this city facing eviction applications, illegal eviction or rent increases — and organisations elsewhere looking for an accredited-clinic-plus-course model to copy. CAVEATS: ONE CITY, ONE COUNTRY, AND A MEANS TEST; IT DOES NOT TAKE INHERITANCE OR ESTATE MATTERS, AND ITS EXPERTISE IS URBAN HOUSING AND TENANCY RATHER THAN RURAL OR CONSERVATION LAND. For inheritance and succession, Gambia's entry; for the clearing house that vets clients before referring them free to panel attorneys, Mauritius' entry.

trackers.name: ROTAB-Niger / Publiez Ce Que Vous Payez
trackers.desc: Nigerien network of civil-society organisations for budget transparency and analysis, and the local Publish What You Pay coalition — scrutinises the national budget and revenues from the extractive (uranium, oil) sector.

trackers.name: Cour des Comptes
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Niger, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: ITIE Niger
trackers.desc: National Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative body — discloses oil, gas and mining revenues, contracts and licences in Niger.

trackers.name: Niger — Ministère des Finances
trackers.desc: National budget authority; prepares & executes the State budget and manages public debt & finances, Niger. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Niger.

trackers.name: Niger — Maison de l’Entreprise (CFE / Guichet Unique)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the Maison de l’Entreprise (under the CCIN) runs the Centre de Formalités des Entreprises one-stop window for company creation, modification, radiation & RCCM registration, Niger. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: ECOWAS Court of Justice — file directly, but sue the State
trackers.desc: A COURT YOU CAN REACH WITHOUT EXHAUSTING DOMESTIC REMEDIES. The ECOWAS Community Court of Justice has held human rights jurisdiction since 2005 and has broad access and standing rules permitting individuals and NGOs to bypass national courts and file directly. THE PRECEDENT: in SERAP v Federal Republic of Nigeria (ECW/CCJ/APP/08/09) the Court dismissed all three preliminary objections — no locus standi, no jurisdiction, statute-barred — and rejected the government's attempt to exclude an Amnesty International report from the evidence. NGO research was admitted as evidence, which matters when no state data exists. It found violations of articles 1 and 24 of the African Charter — article 24: ‘all peoples shall have the right to a general satisfactory environment favourable to their development’ — and of article 21, the right to natural wealth and resources. THE FAULT WAS AN OMISSION: the state ‘defaulted in its duties in terms of vigilance and diligence’, and ‘the omission to act and to prevent damage to the environment characterises the violation’. It ordered restoration within the shortest possible time and measures to prevent further damage, citing the ICJ that the environment ‘is not an abstraction but represents the living space, the quality of life and the very health of human beings, including generations unborn’. THE LIMIT THAT DECIDES WHO YOU SUE: the Court held it had no jurisdiction over the private oil corporations, which were struck from the suit. You sue the State for failing to regulate; you cannot sue the company here — naming one as respondent loses that part of the case. AND PLAN FOR ENFORCEMENT: commentary records the Court did not identify a means for Nigeria to implement the ruling, and the ICJ later wrote to the President pressing for enforcement — judgment is the start of an enforcement campaign, not a self-executing remedy. Proposals to require exhaustion of domestic remedies were rejected by ECOWAS experts and Heads of Government, so the direct-access rule has been tested and held. VERIFY MEMBERSHIP BEFORE FILING: this state has been reported as withdrawing from ECOWAS. This entry does not resolve that question — confirm current membership and the Court's jurisdiction over your state before relying on this route, because withdrawal, if effective, would remove it.

trackers.name: ORFAO — comparative land-law tables, and a directive in draft
trackers.desc: COMPARATIVE LEGAL TABLES FOR YOUR COUNTRY AND ITS NEIGHBOURS, IN ONE DOCUMENT. The Observatoire Régional du Foncier Rural en Afrique de l'Ouest (ORFAO), hosted by UEMOA, publishes a regional study on rural land markets containing side-by-side ‘cadre légal comparé’ tables — one covering Bénin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire and Sénégal, another Guinée-Bissau, Mali, Niger and Togo — plus typologies of direct and indirect interventions in land markets and a table of regulatory issues and families of instruments. If you need to know what instrument exists in your country and whether a neighbour has a stronger one, that is the document — comparative tables let a campaign point to a neighbour's provision as an achievable ask rather than a novelty. A WINDOW IS OPENING: on 26 June 2026 in Ouagadougou the UEMOA ministers for urbanisme, habitat, domaines et cadastre approved a draft directive to harmonise rules on immatriculation foncière, accès au titre de propriété and a système d'information foncière, aiming at a common framework of land governance. BE PRECISE ABOUT STATUS: that was a DRAFT directive approved by ministers, not an adopted and transposed instrument — check adoption and transposition before relying on it. But transposition is the moment domestic land law is reopened in each state, and that is when community provisions can be argued for. FOR A GRAZING OR TRANSHUMANCE DISPUTE: a regional pastoral situation bulletin covers 11 West African countries with the support of decentralised technical services — an evidence source drawing on the same services you would otherwise approach one by one. RECORDED PLAINLY: cattle theft is documented as a driver of conflict and instability in the Sahel, so a land dispute here may sit inside a security context that changes what is safe to do. And confirm your state's current ECOWAS standing — several members are recorded as suspended.

trackers.name: Aghirin'man, Arlit — the mining-town association that got an independent laboratory in, and now owns a radiation meter of its own
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Nigerien association founded in 2002 in Arlit, in the uranium districts of the north, working on education, environmental protection and health in the face of uranium mining. HOW IT STARTED, WHICH IS THE PART EVERY COMPANY TOWN WILL RECOGNISE: it began by asking the operator why people were dying early. According to its president the company answered by threatening to close the mine, which frightened members who feared for their jobs — and then the miners' wives and other civil society organisations joined and carried it. WHAT IT DID NEXT IS THE MODEL: in December 2003 it invited an independent French radioactivity laboratory to come and measure, and the results are why the case exists at all — drinking-water wells at ten times the World Health Organization's uranium guideline while the operator's own communications denied any water contamination, and radioactive waste rock used as road fill outside a hospital reading a hundred times normal background, which was removed only eight months after the laboratory wrote to the company's chief executive, who never replied. AND THEN IT BOUGHT THE INSTRUMENT: with a scintillometer donated by an Austrian foundation, Aghirin'man now takes its own radiation measurements in the town — a community that owns the meter does not have to wait for anyone's permission to know. It also watches new projects, using the rule that Nigerien regulation requires an environmental impact study to be produced and made public BEFORE the public hearings at which residents can question the promoter, and it has written to operators demanding the radiological and bacteriological analyses of drinking-water boreholes. Its stated programme includes training local people in environmental rights and supporting income activities away from contaminated ground. WHO IT SUITS: communities in and around Arlit, Akokan and the newer uranium concessions; and, as a template, any community beside an extractive operation that needs its own measurements. CAVEATS: NO VERIFIED SITE OF ITS OWN — this entry points at the French relay association that supports it and publishes its work; treat that as the route in, not as the organisation. It is a small local association operating under real pressure, its president has described an embargo imposed by the mining companies, and it has no legal service or intake procedure.

trackers.name: Niger's Commissions foncières and the farmers' chamber network — village-level offices that issue written land acts for a few thousand francs
trackers.desc: WHO TO APPROACH: the Commissions foncières (Cofo) — offices established under Niger's Code rural at village and tribe level (Cofob), commune level (Cofocom) and department level (Cofodep) — whose job is to verify people's land rights and issue written acts attesting to them, then archive a copy. Coverage reported: more than 3,000 of about 15,000 villages have a base commission, 145 of 265 communes, and all 36 departments, with a permanent regional secretariat of the Code rural in each of the 8 regions. The Réseau National des Chambres d'Agriculture (RECA) publishes plain-language notes on how to use them, which is why its page is the entry point here. WHAT YOU CAN GET AND WHY IT PROTECTS YOU: the commissions issue attestations of customary holding, of sale, of donation, and formalise contracts of rental, loan and customary pledge — and these acts count as WRITTEN PROOF, usable as evidence if a dispute reaches a court. Crucially, the acts are ADMINISTRATIVE acts, so they can only be challenged by hierarchical appeal or by an action for excess of power before an administrative tribunal — that is what gives them their protective force. In rural areas a full land title from the cadastre service is built on the basis of an attestation of customary holding issued by a Cofo, so the attestation is the first step, not a lesser alternative. Reported cost in one documented case: acts issued after enquiry for 2,500 to 3,000 FCFA, plus the commission members' travel costs, with fees set by each commission's internal rules. Commissions also identify and delimit pastoral areas, passage corridors and water points, and controlled a plateau to check that fields had not been created on land reserved for grazing. If the base commission in your village is not functioning, the commune or department commission can issue the act — and the act has the same legal value whichever level issues it. WHO IT SUITS: Nigerien farmers, herders and villages wanting written proof of a holding, a sale, an inheritance or a shared pastoral resource before a dispute or an allocation arrives. CAVEATS: these are STATE bodies with uneven coverage — the base commissions exist in only a fifth of villages, and the cadastre service may require the attestation to come from commune or department level; disputes between rural operators must first go through an attempt at customary conciliation before a judicial procedure. For the uranium zone and radiation monitoring, Niger's Aghirin'man entry.

trackers.name: ANAJJ Niger — ten legal-aid bureaux sitting inside the high courts, open to ANY person living in Niger, with a rights-NGO representative on each panel
trackers.desc: WHERE TO FILE: the Agence Nationale de l'Assistance Juridique et Judiciaire (ANAJJ), a public administrative establishment created by loi n°2011-42 of 14 December 2011, with statutes fixed by decree in 2012. Its mission is to make ASSISTANCE JURIDIQUE available FREE TO ANY APPLICANT, and ASSISTANCE JUDICIAIRE to vulnerable and indigent persons — the two limbs named in Benin's entry, split explicitly by who qualifies. WHERE THE OFFICES ARE, AND THIS IS THE BEST-DISTRIBUTED FRANCOPHONE NETWORK IN THIS FILE: TEN local bureaux (BAJJ) established INSIDE the Tribunaux de Grande Instance — Agadez, Arlit, Diffa, Dosso, Konni, Maradi, Niamey, Tahoua, Tillabéry and Zinder — so the counter is in the courthouse you would have to attend anyway, including at ARLIT, the uranium town whose community monitoring is recorded separately in this file. WHO SITS ON THE PANEL THAT DECIDES, published and worth knowing: the president of the high court chairs it; the chief clerk is secretary; and it includes a representative of the population ministry, A REPRESENTATIVE OF HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENCE ASSOCIATIONS, and a representative of the advocates or court-appointed defenders. A rights-NGO representative sits on the body deciding your application — if you know that organisation, they are already in the room. WHO CAN APPLY: the Director General states that ANAJJ may be seized for legal or judicial assistance by ANY PERSON LIVING ON NIGERIEN TERRITORY, the law making NO DISTINCTION BY NATIONALITY; detained persons apply through the head of the prison establishment. Note the limit she also draws: the agency can offer legal assistance on its own initiative through awareness sessions and open days, but in a DISPUTE it must be formally seized — nobody will come to you. WHO IT SUITS: anyone living in Niger — citizen or not — facing a land, compensation or pollution dispute and unable to pay. CAVEATS: A STATE AGENCY under the justice ministry, means-tested on the judicial limb, and Niger's security situation restricts movement in several regions. For attestations of customary possession at commune level, Niger's Commissions foncières entry; for uranium-zone radiation monitoring, Aghirin'man. HOW POVERTY IS PROVED, WHICH IS THE GATE EVERY FRANCOPHONE SCHEME IN THIS FILE TURNS ON: Niger is the country that publishes the rule. Décret n°2014-04/PRN/MJ of 3 January 2014 fixes THE CRITERIA AND THE MODES OF PROOF OF INDIGENCE for obtaining assistance judiciaire, made under the 2011 law and the 2012 ANAJJ statutes. Its article 2 defines what you are actually getting: assistance judiciaire subject to the indigence condition is a SET OF SERVICES for an indigent person during a judicial procedure, comprising THE DEFENCE OF THAT PERSON AND THE TAKING IN CHARGE OF ALL COSTS RELATING TO THE PROCEDURE. Defence plus all procedural costs — not advice, not a contribution — so ask for the decree by number if a bureau tries to narrow it. AND THE TRANSFERABLE MOVE: in every francophone country recorded here the application fails or succeeds on the indigence document, so ask your own bureau WHICH TEXT fixes the criteria and what proof it names, before you assemble anything else. Niger's answer is a decree; Côte d'Ivoire's is a certificat d'indigence from the police commissioner or district head; DR Congo's is an attestation d'indigence; Burkina's request is unstamped.

trackers.name: Niger's PMF/FEM small-grants machinery — civil society sits on the deciding committee, grants cover up to 75% of cost, volunteer labour counts as co-financing, and a preparatory grant pays for the baseline study
trackers.desc: THE FRANCOPHONE SMALL-GRANTS MACHINE, SET OUT IN FULL BECAUSE EVERY STEP IS A PLACE A VILLAGE FILE CAN BE HELPED OR LOST — and this closes the last funding gap in this file's Nigerien record: THE PROGRAMME DE MICROFINANCEMENT DU FONDS POUR L'ENVIRONNEMENT MONDIAL (PMF/FEM/NIGER) LAUNCHES APPELS À PROPOSITION DE PROJETS under STAR and CORE fund allocations, awarding small grants to CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, NATIONAL ORGANISATIONS COMMUNAUTAIRES DE BASE AND RESEARCH INSTITUTIONS, to support innovative and inclusive community initiatives that improve socioeconomic conditions and produce positive global environmental impacts, with selected projects required to PROMOTE AND VALORISE THE KNOWLEDGE AND KNOW-HOW OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES in addressing biodiversity loss, land degradation, climate impacts and pollutants. Your own knowledge is a stated selection criterion, not a decoration — write what your community already knows how to do into the proposal. WHO DECIDES, AND WHO SITS THERE: THE NATIONAL COORDINATOR ACTS AS THE PRINCIPAL FOCAL POINT FOR NGOs, ASSOCIATIONS AND ORGANISATIONS COMMUNAUTAIRES DE BASE; the COMITÉ NATIONAL DE PILOTAGE (CNP) IS THE NATIONAL DECISION BODY for both strategy and the award of grants — AND REPRESENTATIVES OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS SIT ON IT alongside state structures and technical and financial partners. Civil society sits on the committee that awards the money. Find out who your sector's representative is and speak to them before the call closes — that is a seat, not a suggestion box. FOUR TERMS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU APPLY: grants represent UP TO 75% OF THE TOTAL COST of the initiative; a separate PREPARATORY GRANT SUPPORTS NECESSARY PRIOR STUDIES — SUCH AS ESTABLISHING THE BASELINE SITUATION or other technical analysis — whose results then ENRICH AND FINALISE the project proposal; the CNP MAY MANDATE ITS OWN MEMBERS OR IDENTIFY RESOURCE PERSONS TO ACCOMPANY organisations in finalising their proposal, AND PRESELECTED PROPONENTS MAY BE INVITED TO PRESENT THEIR INITIATIVE BEFORE THE COMMITTEE; and CO-FINANCING MAY BE IN KIND, INCLUDING VOLUNTEER LABOUR (BÉNÉVOLAT), with project duration not exceeding 24 MONTHS and ONE PROPOSAL PER ORGANISATION. Ask for the preparatory grant first and let it pay for the baseline study — that study is also the evidence you will need later if a project disputes what your land was like before. And eligibility is landscape-bound: projects must sit in the PAYSAGES PRIORITAIRES, so check the country strategy document for whether yours is one. THE WORKED NIGERIEN EXAMPLE: ONG ACTION POUR LE DÉVELOPPEMENT DU NIGER restores degraded land through CASH FOR WORK with conditional transfers to WOMEN AND YOUNG HEADS OF HOUSEHOLD to create productive assets, implemented PARTICIPATIVELY WITH BENEFICIARIES BEFORE restoration activities begin. WHO IT SUITS: Nigerien village committees, women's and youth groups, and community organisations restoring land. CAVEATS: A CYCLE-BASED WINDOW with a landscape restriction — read the current call and the country strategy. For the rural code land commissions, Niger's COFO entries.

trackers.name: ANSEN and Niger's named organisations — regional antennas in three regions, school nurseries owned by the schools that built them, the giraffe association, and the national NGO directory
trackers.desc: THE OWNERSHIP CLAUSE AND THE ANTENNAS: the ASSOCIATION NIGÉRIENNE DES SCOUTS DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT (ANSEN), at PALAIS DES SPORTS PORTE 402, BP 2013, NIAMEY, WITH REGIONAL ANTENNAS IN THE REGIONS OF ZINDER, DOSSO AND AGADEZ, has run AN ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION PROGRAMME SPREAD OVER THE WHOLE SCHOOL YEAR IN CERTAIN NIAMEY SCHOOLS SINCE 1994, with NURSERIES AND SCHOOL GARDENS CREATED INSIDE THE ESTABLISHMENTS CONCERNED. AND ITS OWN STATEMENT OF WHO OWNS THE RESULT IS THE MOST TRANSFERABLE SENTENCE IN THIS ENTRY: THE PROPERTY RIGHTS BELONG EXCLUSIVELY TO ANSEN AND THE SCHOOLS THAT IMPLEMENTED IT; AS FOR THE FINANCIAL PARTNER, IT SIGNED A CONVENTION WITH US, WHICH MEANS THAT THOSE RESPONSIBLE FOR IMPLEMENTATION ARE THE OWNERS. The funder signs a convention; the implementers own the nursery. Write that clause into any agreement you sign — who owns the trees, the fence and the well when the project ends is the question most communities in this file discovered too late. WHAT ELSE ANSEN DOES: tree planting in areas affected by desertification with young people; land recuperation with young people in the national services and young scouts; an ANNUAL YOUTH CAMP FOR THE REHABILITATION OF THE LAND; a project to combat desertification THROUGH THE PRODUCTION OF GUM ARABIC; AND COLLABORATION WITH NIGER'S UNCCD FOCAL POINT ON IMPLEMENTING THE NATIONAL ACTION PROGRAMME TO COMBAT DESERTIFICATION AND MANAGE NATURAL RESOURCES, working with two education ministries and a named foreign NGO. Gum arabic turns anti-desertification planting into a crop with a buyer, and an annual camp is recurring labour that costs nothing. Both are answers to the question of who maintains a restoration after the grant ends. THE OTHERS, NAMED: L'ASSOCIATION DE SAUVEGARDE DES GIRAFES DU NIGER (ASGN), FORMED 1996 WITH THE OBJECTIVE OF SAVING THE LAST POPULATION OF WEST AFRICAN GIRAFFES — WHEN IT WAS FORMED ONLY 50 INDIVIDUALS SURVIVED IN THE COUNTRY — EXPLICITLY INCLUDING PRESERVATION OF THEIR HABITAT IN THE FACE OF AGRICULTURAL EXPANSION, with a named leader. An association founded when fifty animals were left is proof that a last population is still worth organising around. And note the framing: the threat named is agricultural expansion, not poaching — habitat loss is stated as the enemy, which is the framing a community losing land can use. ONG ACTION POUR LE DÉVELOPPEMENT DU NIGER, ESTABLISHED 2018 AS A LEGALLY RECOGNISED NON-PROFIT, INTERVENING IN THE REGIONS OF TILLABÉRY, DIFFA, TAHOUA, ZINDER, MARADI AND DOSSO, WITH A NATIONAL OFFICE IN NIAMEY AND THREE SUB-OFFICES AT TAHOUA/ILLELA, TILLABÉRY/OUALLAM AND DOSSO. Sub-offices in named towns is what distinguishes an organisation that can reach a village from one that can only receive letters in Niamey. A national forum has also convened ONG ADESSA, ONG ADKOUL, ONG AGIR PLUS, ONG KARKARA and others alongside the hydraulics ministry and a research institute. AND TO FIND THE REST: A RÉPERTOIRE DES ONG NATIONALES AU NIGER IS PUBLISHED AS A CURATED HUMANITARIAN RESPONSE RESOURCE. A national NGO directory maintained for emergency coordination is also the most current list of who is actually operating — in a country with a difficult security situation, currency matters more than completeness. WHO IT SUITS: Nigerien communities in Zinder, Dosso, Agadez, Tillabéry, Tahoua, Diffa or Maradi, and schools wanting a nursery they will own. CAVEATS: CONFIRM CURRENT OPERATIONS given the security situation. For the 75% grant, the preparatory grant and the civil-society seat on the national steering committee, Niger's PMF/FEM entry.

trackers.name: Niger's peasant platform, herders' federation and milk cooperatives inside a six-country 55-organisation campaign — plus the Maisons du Paysan with a published management plan for each named village, and DIMOL's Niamey contacts
trackers.desc: THE FARMERS' PLATFORM, AND THE HOUSE IN THE VILLAGE: NIGER'S NAMED MEMBERS OF A SIX-COUNTRY REGIONAL CAMPAIGN INCLUDE THE PLATEFORME PAYSANNE DU NIGER (PFPN); THE FÉDÉRATION NATIONALE DES ÉLEVEURS DU NIGER (FNEN DADO); KARKARA; GAJEL; A NAMED REGIONAL CHAMBER OF AGRICULTURE; A MILK COOPERATIVE AT A NAMED TOWN; TWO NAMED DAIRIES; AND A HYGIENE ENTERPRISE — PART OF A CAMPAIGN INVOLVING 55 MEMBER ORGANISATIONS ACROSS SIX WEST AND CENTRAL AFRICAN COUNTRIES. A national peasant platform and a national herders' federation, both named, both already inside a regional campaign. If you are a Nigerien farmer or herder, you do not need to found anything — those two bodies exist and are already federated across six countries. AND THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN FIGURES ARE THE ARGUMENT, WHICH IS WHY THEY ARE WORTH CARRYING: 2,000 PRODUCERS AFFECTED; 15 MINI-DAIRIES IN THE SIX COUNTRIES UNDER THREAT; 54 DISTRIBUTORS UNDER THREAT; 48 MILLION PASTORALISTS AND AGROPASTORALISTS IN THE SIX COUNTRIES WHOSE SURVIVAL IS AT STAKE; AND 276,892 TONNES OF SKIMMED-MILK-AND-VEGETABLE-FAT POWDER IMPORTED FROM EUROPE INTO WEST AFRICA IN A SINGLE YEAR. Forty-eight million pastoralists against a named tonnage of imported milk powder. That is how a livelihood campaign is built: count your own people, count the imports, and put the two numbers side by side. The campaign's own framing is the model — IF LOCAL MILK IS NOT PROTECTED, IT IS A WHOLE ECOSYSTEM AND ALL ITS ACTORS THAT ARE THREATENED. Substitute your own product and the sentence still works. THE PHYSICAL INSTITUTION THIS FILE HAD NOT RECORDED: MAISONS DU PAYSAN — FARMERS' HOUSES — EXIST AT NAMED NIGERIEN VILLAGES, AND EACH HAS ITS OWN UPDATED PLAN DE GESTION ENVIRONNEMENTALE ET SOCIALE PUBLISHED UNDER A COMMUNITY ACTION PROJECT FOR CLIMATE RESILIENCE, IN SEVEN VOLUMES, ONE PER NAMED LOCALITY, PUBLICLY DISCLOSED. A Maison du Paysan is a building in a village that belongs to the farmers who use it — stores, inputs, a meeting room. And each one has a published environmental and social management plan naming that specific village. Two uses: if your village has one, the plan is a public document you can demand and read; and if it does not, the seven published plans are the template for asking for one. THE ORGANISATIONS WITH CONTACTS: DIMOL, AT BP 13 874, NIAMEY, WITH TWO TELEPHONE NUMBERS, A FAX AND A PUBLISHED EMAIL, WORKING ON THE PROMOTION AND FLOURISHING OF NIGERIEN WOMEN AND ACCREDITED TO A CONTINENTAL HUMAN RIGHTS BODY; ONG-VIE KANDE NI BAYRA, WHOSE COORDINATOR ALSO CHAIRS A CADRE DE CONCERTATION AND WHICH IS DESCRIBED AS THE SAHEL PARTNER NOW GROUPING BENIN, NIGER, CHAD, TOGO AND MALI; AND ONG FAILATOUL HAIRAN, A YOUNG NIGERIEN NON-PROFIT CREATED BY ARRÊTÉ NUMBER 00445 OF THE MINISTRY OF THE INTERIOR ON 16 JULY 2016, WORKING ON ACCESS TO DRINKING WATER, HEALTH, EDUCATION, ENVIRONMENT AND HUMANITARIAN ACTION. An arrêté number and a date is what a Nigerien association's existence rests on — note the form: a numbered ministerial order from the interior ministry. Ask any organisation for its arrêté number, and know that is what yours will look like. AN ACCREDITATION TO A CONTINENTAL HUMAN RIGHTS BODY, as DIMOL holds, means the organisation can appear at that body's sessions. If your case needs to be raised continentally, an accredited national organisation is the vehicle — and there is one in Niamey with a published phone number. THE WOMEN AND LAND QUESTION IS DOCUMENTED: a published Sahel network paper addresses LA FEMME RURALE ET LE PROBLÈME FONCIER AGRICOLE AU NIGER, recording that 80% OF THE POPULATION IS RURAL, that AGRICULTURE IS THE PRINCIPAL ECONOMIC ACTIVITY, and that food insecurity structurally affects more than 30% of households. A paper specifically on rural women and the agricultural land problem in Niger, written through a Sahel network rather than about it from outside. If your dispute involves a woman's claim to farmland, that is the document to have in hand. AND THE STATE INTERLOCUTOR, NAMED: A CONSEIL NATIONAL DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT POUR UN DÉVELOPPEMENT DURABLE HAS AN EXECUTIVE SECRETARIAT IN NIAMEY WITH A NAMED FOCAL POINT. A national environment council with an executive secretariat is the body that receives national environmental questions. One named person, one office. WHO IT SUITS: Nigerien farmers, herders and women's groups, villages with or wanting a Maison du Paysan, and anyone needing a continentally accredited national organisation. CAVEATS: SOME FIGURES AND CONTACTS COME FROM PUBLISHED PROGRAMME AND CAMPAIGN DOCUMENTS — confirm before relying, and note Niger's security situation. For regional antennas in three regions, school nurseries since 1994 and the clause that implementers own the result, Niger's ANSEN entry; for 50 giraffes in 1996 and habitat loss named, ASGN; for the NGO directory, the Niger NGO directory entry.

trackers.name: The free field guide, in French and Arabic, for making phone footage stand up as court evidence — filming plans, camera reports, a collection plan agreed with your lawyer, and a 250-item library on archiving and verification
trackers.desc: THE PHONE FOOTAGE IS ALREADY THERE; THE PROBLEM IS IT WILL NOT STAND UP — anchor note first: THE FILE-WIDE SWEEP FLAGGED THIS ORGANISATION'S DOMAIN AS A SUBSTRING INSIDE LIBYA'S ENTRY, WHICH CITES A DIFFERENT ORGANISATION WITH A SIMILAR NAME. THEY ARE UNRELATED. THE GAP IT EXISTS TO CLOSE, STATED PLAINLY: CITIZENS AND ON-THE-GROUND HUMAN RIGHTS ACTIVISTS ARE BETTER POSITIONED TO COLLECT EVIDENCE OF HUMAN RIGHTS ABUSE THAN PROFESSIONAL INVESTIGATORS, BECAUSE INVESTIGATORS ALMOST ALWAYS ARRIVE AFTER-THE-FACT WHEN EVIDENCE HAS DETERIORATED OR IS GONE — HOWEVER, THE QUALITY OF CITIZEN VIDEO RARELY PASSES THE HIGHER BAR NEEDED TO FUNCTION AS EVIDENCE IN A COURT OF LAW. You were there and the investigator was not. That is an advantage nobody can buy — and it is routinely wasted, because the footage was filmed in a way a court cannot use. This file has recorded evictions, clearances and spills that hundreds of people filmed and nobody could prove. AND THE FIX IS SMALL: WITH SLIGHT MODIFICATIONS, THE FOOTAGE CITIZENS AND ACTIVISTS OFTEN RISK THEIR LIVES TO CAPTURE CAN SERVE AS EVIDENCE IN CRIMINAL AND CIVIL JUSTICE PROCESSES. SLIGHT MODIFICATIONS. Not better cameras, not training courses — a handful of habits. That is the cheapest evidentiary upgrade available to any community in this file. THE GUIDE'S FOUR SECTIONS: THE LAW, COVERING BASIC LEGAL PRINCIPLES AND PROCESSES; BASIC PRACTICES, WITH TIPS FOR CAPTURING VIDEO WITH ENHANCED EVIDENTIARY VALUE; FILMING FOR EVIDENCE, ON FILMING, ORGANIZING AND MANAGING YOUR VIDEOS FOR EVIDENTIARY PURPOSES; AND SHARING AND USING EYEWITNESS VIDEO IN HUMAN RIGHTS REPORTING AND ADVOCACY, WITH TECHNIQUES FOR VERIFYING VIDEO CONTENT AND GUIDELINES FOR USING EYEWITNESS VIDEO ETHICALLY. AND IT IS DOWNLOADABLE IN ENGLISH, ARABIC, FRENCH, SPANISH, UKRAINIAN AND RUSSIAN. French and Arabic cover most of the countries in this file that have no equivalent resource in their own language. Download it before anything happens and give it to whoever holds the camera. THE PIECE ALMOST NOBODY KNOWS ABOUT: HOW A COLLECTION PLAN CAN HELP INVESTIGATORS AND LAWYERS COMMUNICATE THEIR NEEDS TO FRONTLINE ACTIVISTS, SO THE FOOTAGE ACTIVISTS COLLECT CAN BETTER SUPPORT A LEGAL CASE. Ask your lawyer what they will need to prove, before you film it. A collection plan is that conversation written down — and it turns filming from an instinct into an assignment. Communities that do this bring back what the case requires; those that do not bring back an hour of shouting. THE FIELD METHOD, WHICH IS CONCRETE: GUIDANCE ON SAFELY AND EFFECTIVELY GATHERING VIDEO DOCUMENTATION AT THE SCENE OF AN ALLEGED HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATION — INCLUDING DEVELOPING A FILMING PLAN, CAPTURING DETAILS AND VARIOUS ANGLES, AND FILLING OUT A CAMERA REPORT. A CAMERA REPORT is a written note of who filmed, where, when and what — a page in a notebook. Without it, months later nobody can say which valley the clip shows, which is the commonest way good footage becomes useless. THE SAFETY WARNING, PUBLISHED BY THEM RATHER THAN BURIED: FILMING FOR HUMAN RIGHTS CAN BE DANGEROUS. IT CAN PUT YOU, THE PEOPLE YOU ARE FILMING AND THE COMMUNITIES YOU ARE FILMING IN AT RISK. CAREFULLY ASSESS THE RISKS BEFORE YOU PRESS RECORD — NOTHING STATED IN THIS GUIDE IS ABSOLUTE, YOU SHOULD MODIFY THE PRACTICES TO FIT YOUR NEEDS, AND WHEN POSSIBLE, SEEK SUPPORT FROM LOCAL EXPERTS. THE PEOPLE YOU ARE FILMING are put at risk too. A face in your footage is a name for somebody else's file — decide as a community who may be shown before the day arrives, not afterwards. THE LIBRARY: OVER 250 LEARNING MATERIALS TO SUPPORT ACTIVISTS IN USING VIDEO AND TECHNOLOGY FOR HUMAN RIGHTS, INCLUDING AN ACTIVIST'S GUIDE TO ARCHIVING VIDEO AND RESOURCES ON ARCHIVING AND PRESERVATION. ARCHIVING is the half everyone skips. Footage on one phone that gets seized, broken or sold is gone — and the guide on preserving it is free. THE VERIFICATION TIP SHEET: FOUR BASIC STEPS THAT CAN BE TAKEN TO DETERMINE WHETHER OR NOT THE CONTENT OF AN ONLINE VIDEO IS AUTHENTIC, INTENDED TO SUPPORT NEWS MEDIA, HUMAN RIGHTS ADVOCATES, INVESTIGATORS AND ACTIVISTS — ALSO AVAILABLE IN ARABIC. Use it on the other side's material as well as your own. A developer's promotional video of a consultation meeting can be checked for when and where it was actually taken. AND THE FAILURE MODES NAMED FROM PRACTICE, WORTH READING AS A CHECKLIST: STRICT AUTHENTICATION STANDARDS MUST BE MET; FILMMAKERS MAY FACE RISKS WHEN PROVIDING TESTIMONY; IMPROPERLY COLLECTED FOOTAGE CAN CONFLICT WITH WITNESS STATEMENTS; AND WITHOUT PROPER MANAGEMENT, CONFUSION CAN ARISE REGARDING WHERE THE FOOTAGE WAS FILMED AND WHAT IT DEPICTS. FOOTAGE CAN CONFLICT WITH WITNESS STATEMENTS is the danger nobody expects: a video that contradicts your own witness on a small detail damages the case rather than helping it. Take the statements and the film together, and check them against each other before either goes anywhere. WHO IT SUITS: any African community filming an eviction, a clearance, a spill or a police action, and the lawyers working with them. CAVEATS: A GUIDE AND A LIBRARY, NOT LEGAL REPRESENTATION — and their own warning about risk should be read first. For the offline tools where the community owns the footage, Equatorial Guinea's entry; for the free digital security helpline if a device is seized, Morocco's entry; for the organisation that takes evidence communities gathered themselves, Libya's entry.

trackers.name: NRGI (Natural Resource Governance Institute) — two African summer schools that teach civil society to analyse real oil, gas and mining contracts — full scholarships covering travel and tuition, evening one-on-one clinics, a post-course mentorship, and a free index scoring your own country
trackers.desc: THEY TEACH PEOPLE TO READ THE CONTRACT, AND THEY PAY THE FARE — THE FRANCOPHONE AFRICA SCHOOL, WHICH NAMES THIS COUNTRY AMONG ITS OWN: A REGIONAL KNOWLEDGE HUB RUN WITH A CENTRAL AFRICAN UNIVERSITY, WHOSE ANNUAL SUMMER SCHOOL HAS RUN SINCE 2011, USUALLY AROUND AUGUST — ATTRACTING UP TO 40 MEMBERS OF THE MEDIA AND CIVIL SOCIETY FROM 12 DIFFERENT COUNTRIES INCLUDING BURKINA FASO, CAMEROON, THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, GUINEA AND NIGER — TAUGHT BY A DIVERSE TEAM OF EXPERTS WITH PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTOR BACKGROUNDS, MOSTLY FROM ACROSS FRANCOPHONE WESTERN AND CENTRAL AFRICA. Taught in French by francophone Africans, for francophone Africans. Most training in this file arrives in English through an interpreter; this one does not, and it has run every August for over a decade. WHAT IS ACTUALLY PRACTISED THERE, AND IT IS THE FIND: THE SCHOOL PLACES STRONG EMPHASIS ON PRACTICAL ANALYTICAL SKILLS — EACH LESSON PROVIDES PARTICIPANTS WITH THE OPPORTUNITY TO ANALYZE REAL-LIFE CONTRACTS, LEGISLATION AND FISCAL POLICIES, AND ENCOURAGES COMPARISONS BETWEEN COUNTRIES TO DETERMINE BEST PRACTICES. Real contracts, taken apart in a classroom. This file's Mauritania entry records where those contracts can be found; this is where somebody from your organisation learns what the clauses mean. A community that can read its own concession agreement negotiates differently from one that cannot, and the skill stays with the person afterwards. AND THE TWO TRACKS IN ONE ROOM: ATTENDING JOURNALISTS PRACTISE THEIR REPORTING AND WRITING SKILLS UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF A SKILLED EXTRACTIVE SECTOR REPORTER; CIVIL SOCIETY DELEGATES LEARN HOW TO ENGAGE IN CONSTRUCTIVE AND EVIDENCE-BASED POLICY ADVOCACY AROUND EXTRACTIVE SECTOR GOVERNANCE. Reporters and campaigners trained together for two weeks. The relationships formed there are why a journalist later takes your call — and this file's Gambia entry has the money that pays such a reporter to travel to your area. THE MENTORSHIP THAT CONTINUES: ALL PARTICIPANTS CAN SIGN UP FOR A MENTORSHIP PROGRAM THAT MOBILIZES EXPERTS IN SUPPORT OF STUDENTS' RESEARCH AND PROJECTS AFTER THE COURSE. Support that outlasts the fortnight. This file's Guinea-Bissau entry names the opposite pattern — consultants who parachute in and disappear — and a post-course mentorship is the answer to it. THE EVENING CLINICS, WHICH ARE THE MOST DIRECTLY USEFUL HOUR OF THE WHOLE COURSE: PARTICIPANTS CAN SIGN UP FOR ONE-ON-ONE CLINICS IN THE EVENING WITH COURSE EXPERTS TO DISCUSS THE CHALLENGES THEY FACE IN THEIR COUNTRIES AND REQUEST ADVICE. Bring your actual case. Somebody sent by a community can put the real concession, the real compensation offer and the real refusal in front of an expert who has seen fifty of them — free, and without hiring anyone. THE ANGLOPHONE SCHOOL AND ITS PRICE, STATED PLAINLY: A COMPREHENSIVE, INTERMEDIATE-LEVEL TWO-WEEK RESIDENTIAL COURSE COVERING GOVERNANCE ISSUES IN THE DECISION CHAIN OF NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, DEEPENING ANALYTICAL SKILLS IN FISCAL AND REVENUE MANAGEMENT POLICIES, TRANSPARENCY REPORTS, CONTRACTS AND KEY LEGISLATION — OPEN TO GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS, CIVIL SOCIETY ACTORS, JOURNALISTS, PARLIAMENTARIANS AND PRIVATE SECTOR ACTORS, AT APPROXIMATELY $2,500 INCLUSIVE OF ACCOMMODATION, FOOD AND TUITION, WITH A NAMED CONTACT PERSON. THE SCHOLARSHIPS, WHICH ARE WHAT MAKE IT REACHABLE: WITH DONOR SUPPORT, A NUMBER OF SCHOLARSHIPS ARE AVAILABLE TO ELIGIBLE PARTICIPANTS FROM SELECT COUNTRIES — AND FOR THE ADVANCED COURSE, A LIMITED NUMBER OF FULL SCHOLARSHIPS COVERING TRAVEL, ACCOMMODATION AND TUITION ARE AVAILABLE ON A COMPETITIVE BASIS FOR MEMBERS OF GOVERNMENT, CIVIL SOCIETY, PARLIAMENTS AND THE MEDIA FROM SELECTED RESOURCE-RICH COUNTRIES, WITH A RESTRICTED NUMBER OF EXCEPTIONS FOR OUTSTANDING APPLICANTS FROM OTHER COUNTRIES. WOMEN ARE PARTICULARLY ENCOURAGED TO APPLY. TRAVEL INCLUDED, and exceptions made for outstanding applicants from countries not on the list. So a community organisation in a country that is not named should still apply rather than assume exclusion — the exception clause is published for a reason. THE APPLICATION ITSELF IS SHORT: A SHORT ESSAY ON THE GOVERNANCE CHALLENGES ASSOCIATED WITH EXTRACTIVE INDUSTRIES IN THE APPLICANT'S COUNTRY, AND THE APPLICANT'S EXPECTATIONS OF HOW THE COURSE WILL BENEFIT THEM AND THEIR ORGANIZATION. One essay. Somebody who has lived the problem writes that more convincingly than any consultant. THE FREE INDEX ANYONE CAN OPEN TODAY: IT MEASURES THE QUALITY OF GOVERNANCE IN THE OIL, GAS AND MINING SECTORS — A ROBUST, EVIDENCE-BASED TOOL LETTING GOVERNMENTS, CIVIL SOCIETY ACTORS, PRIVATE COMPANIES AND CITIZENS UNDERSTAND HOW THEIR COUNTRIES PERFORM — A FREELY AVAILABLE PUBLIC DATA PRODUCT SERVING AS A GLOBAL BENCHMARK, COUNTRY AND SECTOR DIAGNOSTIC TOOL, AND A ROADMAP FOR POLICY AND PRACTICE REFORM, WITH COUNTRY PROFILES. Your country has a score and a profile setting out exactly which parts of its own system are weak. That is an official-looking document arguing your case before you say a word — and it costs nothing to print. THE TEACHING METHOD: LEARNING THROUGH PARTICIPANTS' OWN EXPERIENCES, USING SUSTAINED DEBATES AND POLICY LABS TO APPLY NEW KNOWLEDGE TO THEIR PROFESSIONAL ROLES, EXAMINING AND DEBATING THE PROS AND CONS OF POLICY DECISIONS FROM VARIOUS ANGLES. AND THE AFRICAN FINDING FROM THE INDEX, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT TO CARRY: A REPORT ON SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA CONCLUDES THAT POLICYMAKERS, PARLIAMENTARIANS, CIVIL SOCIETY, MEDIA AND REGIONAL INSTITUTIONS SHOULD FOCUS MORE ON NARROWING THE IMPLEMENTATION GAP, WHICH WILL HELP RESTORE TRUST BETWEEN GOVERNMENT, COMMUNITIES AND INVESTORS — AND THAT CONSULTING STAKEHOLDERS HELPS GOVERNMENTS DESIGN LAWS ADEQUATE FOR THEIR INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITY, AND ASSESS WHAT IS NEEDED FOR EFFECTIVE IMPLEMENTATION BEFORE LAWS ARE PASSED. THE IMPLEMENTATION GAP, named by the sector's own diagnostic. This file has recorded the same thing from Burundi's unissued decrees to Kenya's unenforced judgment: the law usually exists and is not applied. Arguing for implementation of what is already law is a narrower and far more winnable demand than arguing for new law. WHO IT SUITS: African community organisations, coalitions and journalists facing an oil, gas or mining project who need somebody trained to read the documents. CAVEATS: COURSES RUN ANNUALLY WITH COMPETITIVE SCHOLARSHIPS AND ELIGIBLE-COUNTRY LISTS THAT VARY BY YEAR — and the paid fee is beyond most community budgets without one. For the repository where contracts are published, Mauritania's entry; for the coalition a national body joins with one form, Mauritius' entry; for story grants paying a reporter's travel, Gambia's entry.

trackers.name: The Huairou Commission's Community Resilience Funds — a fund applied for on a form and decided by an independent committee of grassroots women — paying in cash, tools or other resources, monitored locally by the leaders themselves, with named African member organisations and a farmer on the governing council
trackers.desc: A COMMITTEE OF GRASSROOTS WOMEN DECIDES WHO GETS THE MONEY — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE CARRIES A SHACK AND SLUM DWELLERS FEDERATION UNDER SOUTH AFRICA AND GHANA, A NAMED PARTNER OF THE FUND DESCRIBED HERE, AND THE REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO ENTRY NAMES A GLOBAL WOMEN'S LAND CAMPAIGN THIS NETWORK CO-DESIGNS. NEITHER IS RESTATED AND NEITHER HOST IS SHIPPED. WHO DECIDES, AND IT IS THE FIND: TO ACCESS THE FUNDS, MEMBERS COMPLETE A FORM DETAILING THEIR NEEDS AND HOW THEY PLAN TO MAKE USE OF THE RESOURCES — AND AN INDEPENDENT COMMITTEE OF GRASSROOTS WOMEN REVIEWS ALL APPLICATIONS AND DECIDES WHICH GO FORWARD, AND WHETHER SUPPORT WILL BE IN THE FORM OF CASH, TOOLS OR OTHER RESOURCES. Village women reviewing village women's applications. Every other fund in this file is decided by programme officers abroad, however participatory the language on the website — here the panel is the constituency. And the support can arrive as TOOLS rather than money, which sidesteps the bank account, the transfer fee and the argument about who holds the cash. WHAT THE FUND IS: A FLEXIBLE FINANCING MECHANISM THAT HAS OVER TEN YEARS CHANNELED FUNDS TO COMMUNITY RESILIENCE BUILDING INITIATIVES LED BY ORGANIZED GRASSROOTS WOMEN'S GROUPS — DESIGNED WITH GRASSROOTS WOMEN LEADERS AND THEIR TECHNICAL ALLIES. WHAT IT ALSO PAYS FOR, WHICH FEW FUNDS COVER: GRASSROOTS WOMEN'S ABILITIES TO TRANSFER AND AGGREGATE THEIR WORK THROUGH EXCHANGES, BUILD COALITIONS WITH OTHER CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS AND NETWORKS, AND LEVERAGE THEIR WORK TO ADVOCATE WITH GOVERNMENT INSTITUTIONS TO FORMALLY RECOGNIZE AND RESOURCE GRASSROOTS WOMEN'S RESILIENCE PRACTICES. Exchanges and coalition-building as fundable line items. This file has recorded over and over that a village which visits another village learns faster than one that attends a workshop — and that the travel is what nobody will pay for. THE MONITORING ARRANGEMENT: THE FUND IS MONITORED AT LOCAL LEVEL BY LEADERS THEMSELVES, AND AT GLOBAL LEVEL AT ANNUAL REVIEW MEETINGS WHERE IT IS EVALUATED IN TERMS OF SUCCESSES AND RISKS AND OPPORTUNITIES TO FURTHER SCALE. WHAT A MEMBER GROUP ACTUALLY DID WITH IT: ONE KENYAN MEMBER ORGANIZED GRASSROOTS WOMEN IN 5 COMMUNITIES TO MAP RISKS AND COLLECTIVELY PLAN AND DELIVER RESILIENCE BUILDING ACTIONS, ADDING MORE COMMUNITIES IN LATER YEARS — USING THE FUND TO IMPROVE SOIL pH, ACCESS TO CLEAN WATER AND SECURE LAND RIGHTS, AND TO ENHANCE FOOD AND NUTRITION SECURITY, ACCESS TO CLEAN ENERGY AND PARTICIPATION IN FOREST MANAGEMENT. SECURE LAND RIGHTS listed beside soil pH and clean water. A fund that treats tenure as a resilience expense will pay for the survey, the meeting and the paperwork that a conservation or emergency funder would refuse. THE ALTERNATIVE TO MONEYLENDERS: THAT MEMBER OFFERED GRASSROOTS WOMEN ALTERNATIVES TO MICROFINANCE INSTITUTIONS BY HELPING GROUPS SET UP THEIR OWN SAVINGS AND CREDIT SCHEMES — AND IS PLANNING TO ORGANIZE 500 GRASSROOTS WOMEN FARMERS INTO A COOPERATIVE TO LEND LARGER SUMS TO MEMBERS, EXPAND MARKETS FOR FARM PRODUCE, AND ACT AS A BRIDGE BETWEEN GRASSROOTS WOMEN AND MICROFINANCE INSTITUTIONS. A cooperative that can lend more than a savings group and negotiate with lenders as a block. That is the next rung above the no-outside-capital savings model filed under Djibouti, and it is reachable from it. THE AFRICAN MEMBER PROFILE, WITH ITS STRUCTURE PUBLISHED: ONE UGANDAN MEMBER WORKS WITH 53 CONSOLIDATED MEMBERS, 8 AFFILIATED ORGANIZATIONS IN RURAL AREAS, AND 2 MAIN PARTNERS — ENGAGED IN WOMEN'S RIGHTS, GOVERNANCE, HEALTH, LAND AND HOUSING, RESILIENCE AND GIRLS' EDUCATION, PRIORITIZING WOMEN'S LAND RIGHTS, FOOD SECURITY AND COMMUNITY RESILIENCE, AND HOSTING PEER LEARNING AND DISTRICT GENDER NETWORK SESSIONS. THE THEMATIC NETWORKS IT BUILT, WHICH ARE FOUR SEPARATE DOORS: GRASSROOTS WOMEN NETWORKING AROUND LAND AND HOUSING THROUGH A NAMED AFRICAN LAND LINK; CARE-GIVING THROUGH A HOME-BASED CARE ALLIANCE; RESILIENCE THROUGH A COMMUNITY PRACTITIONERS PLATFORM; AND SAFETY THROUGH A SAFER CITIES NETWORK. THE LAND ANALYSIS IT WORKS FROM: INSECURITY OF TENURE CHALLENGES GRASSROOTS WOMEN THE MOST, BECAUSE ACCESS TO AND CONTROL OVER LAND IS LINKED TO THEIR SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC STATUS IN THE COMMUNITY — AND SECURITY OF TENURE BECOMES KEY TO THEIR ECONOMIC, SOCIAL AND CONSEQUENTLY POLITICAL EMPOWERMENT. ITS THREE LAND OBJECTIVES, AND THE FIRST IS THE ONE TO DEMAND LOCALLY: PROMOTE GRASSROOTS WOMEN'S REPRESENTATION WITHIN LAND GOVERNANCE STRUCTURES; ENSURE THEIR ACCESS TO AND CONTROL OVER LAND; AND SUPPORT THEIR GROUPS' INNOVATION IN LAND MANAGEMENT, NUTRITION AND FOOD SECURITY. Representation within the land governance structures themselves — the committee, the board, the allocation panel — not merely consultation by it. That is a specific, checkable ask at a district land office. THE ARGUMENT ONE MEMBER MADE TO OFFICIALS, WHICH IS WORTH BORROWING WHOLE: THE WOMEN SHOWCASED TO LOCAL OFFICIALS HOW SECURE TENURE AND LAND RIGHTS BUILD SELF-SUFFICIENCY AND COMMUNITY RESILIENCE, REDUCING RELIANCE ON RELIEF AND SOCIAL SECURITY FROM GOVERNMENT, MEANWHILE POSITIONING THE GROUP AS A VIABLE PARTNER. Secure our tenure and we will need less from you. That reframes a rights claim as a saving to the district budget, and it is the argument most likely to move an official who is unmoved by everything else. AND THE TOOL NAMED AT A CONTINENTAL LAND CONFERENCE: WOMEN'S GROUPS IN RURAL WESTERN KENYA HAVE ORGANIZED THEMSELVES INTO GROUPS CALLED COLLECTIVE WOMEN FARMERS, WHICH THEY USE AS A TOOL TO FIGHT FOR LAND ACCESS FOR FOOD PRODUCTION — AND ONE MEMBER SECURED A FORMAL AGREEMENT WITH A MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE ENSURING AGRICULTURAL SUBSIDIES REACH IMPOVERISHED HOUSEHOLDS IN DROUGHT-AFFECTED REGIONS. A written agreement with a ministry, obtained by a grassroots women's group. Not a promise at a meeting — a formal agreement, which is the form to insist on. WHO IT SUITS: organised African women's groups needing small flexible money for land, water or food security work, and those wanting a route onto land governance bodies. CAVEATS: THE FUND IS FOR MEMBER GROUPS OF THE NETWORK, SO JOINING OR AFFILIATING COMES FIRST — the African member organisations named on its pages are the way in. For the savings model that needs no outside capital at all, Djibouti's entry; for the federation partner named here, South Africa's entry; for the deed-formalization service and its talking books, the Republic of the Congo's entry.

trackers.name: Up to $25,000 for species work, open to anyone directly involved with no organisation required — three rounds a year, a published 12% success rate, a searchable archive of every grant since 2009, and support-staff salaries in developing countries considered
trackers.desc: ANYONE DIRECTLY INVOLVED CAN APPLY. NO ORGANISATION REQUIRED — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ESWATINI ENTRY COVERS THE TEAM-BASED CONSERVATION LADDER, ITS SÃO TOMÉ ENTRY THE MID-CAREER NATIONAL AWARD, ITS SOMALIA ENTRY THE ROLLING INDIVIDUAL SMALL GRANTS, AND ITS MOROCCO AND CAPE VERDE ENTRIES A CONSERVATION UNION HOST. THIS IS A DIFFERENT FUND WITH DIFFERENT RULES; NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHO MAY APPLY, WHICH IS THE FIND: ANYONE DIRECTLY INVOLVED IN SPECIES CONSERVATION CAN APPLY — WHETHER YOU ARE A FIELD RESEARCHER, A CONSERVATIONIST, A SCIENTIST, OR PART OF AN NGO. ELIGIBILITY EXTENDS TO ALL PLANT, ANIMAL AND FUNGI SPECIES CONSERVATION EFFORTS, WITHOUT DISCRIMINATION ON THE BASIS OF REGION OR SELECTED SPECIES. No registration, no institution, no host organisation named as a condition. A person who knows the animal or plant on their own land, and is doing something about it, is inside the definition.
