The plan is negotiated before the deed is signed, and the NGO is bound to help carry it out. That is what stops a servitude becoming an unfunded obligation the owner resents. THE MONEY THAT COMES WITH IT, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE TEAM PROVIDES SUPPORT INCLUDING INCENTIVE FUNDING TO PROTECT REMAINING PATCHES — INCENTIVISING LANDOWNERS WITH ADVICE AND ASSISTANCE WITH KEY MANAGEMENT INTERVENTIONS. The landowner is paid to protect it, not merely asked. That is the difference between a scheme farmers sign and one they decline, and it is the answer to the question this file keeps running into: why would the owner agree? THE METHOD, PUBLISHED STEP BY STEP: KEY AREAS ARE INITIALLY IDENTIFIED BASED ON DESK-TOP STUDIES AND EXTENSIVE MAPPING; THE LANDOWNERS ARE THEN APPROACHED AND ASKED IF THEIR LAND MAY BE SURVEYED, WITH A THOROUGH SURVEY USUALLY REQUIRING MULTIPLE VISITS AT DIFFERENT TIMES OF THE YEAR. Map first, then ask permission to survey, then negotiate. A local organisation can follow that sequence exactly — and the multiple-visit point matters, because a single dry-season survey misses most of what makes a case. THE LEGAL SIDE-BENEFITS IT NAMES TO LANDOWNERS: SIGNING THE EASEMENT AND THE ASSOCIATED MANAGEMENT PLAN BRINGS YOU IN LINE WITH ALL ENVIRONMENTAL LEGISLATION, PARTICULARLY REGARDING THE LAWS WHICH STATE THAT YOU MAY NOT SELL A PROPERTY CONTAINING INVASIVE ALIEN PLANTS — AND IT FORCES THE NEXT LANDOWNER TO ACKNOWLEDGE WHERE THE VIRGIN LAND IS. Compliance sold as a benefit rather than conservation sold as a duty. An approach that solves a legal problem the owner already has is the one that gets signed. THE ARGUMENT IT PUTS TO THE OWNER: THE IDEA IS THAT YOU YOURSELF WOULD WANT TO PREVENT FUTURE OWNERS FROM DESTROYING OR DEGRADING THE VEGETATION ON YOUR FARM — IT IS THE ONLY WAY TO LEAVE THIS LEGACY. THE RESULTS ON RECORD: FIVE FARMS WITH SIGNED EASEMENTS, BRINGING OVER 1,300 HECTARES INTO CONSERVATION IN PERPETUITY — INCLUDING ONE NAMED FARM WITH 360 HECTARES, AND 370 HECTARES OF THE LARGEST REMAINING AREA OF A NAMED VEGETATION TYPE UNDER THE FIRST SUCH EASEMENT. Five farms, thirteen hundred hectares. Small numbers, permanent effect — which is the honest scale at which this instrument works, one owner at a time. THE PURCHASE PROGRAMME ALONGSIDE IT: A 270-HECTARE STRETCH WAS SECURED THROUGH AN INTERNATIONAL BUY AN ACRE PROGRAMME WHICH ENABLES PEOPLE WORLDWIDE TO FUND LAND PURCHASES FOR THREATENED HABITATS — BUT LAND ACQUISITION IS JUST ONE TOOL. A public buy-an-acre appeal is a real route to the purchase price, and it is run by international partners on behalf of local trusts. That is the fundraising mechanism the standing brief asks about, working, on African ground. THE CORRIDOR STRATEGY: THE TRUST IS BUILDING CONSERVATION CORRIDORS WITH FARMING NEIGHBOURS, INCLUDING A NAMED NEIGHBOURING EASEMENT SITE — SO THAT WILDLIFE, ESPECIALLY POLLINATORS AND INVERTEBRATES, CAN MOVE FREELY AND SAFELY ACROSS NATURAL REMNANT PATCHES IN A HIGHLY TRANSFORMED LANDSCAPE. Neighbouring farms signed one after another add up to a corridor. Each easement makes the next one easier to ask for, because the neighbour has already seen the terms. WHY IT EXISTS AND WHY PRIVATE LAND IS THE WHOLE PROBLEM: THE REMAINING REMNANTS ARE ESSENTIALLY ALL FOUND ON PRIVATELY-OWNED LAND, SO WORKING WITH COMMERCIAL FARMERS IS CRUCIAL TO THE SURVIVAL OF THE ECOSYSTEM — WITH OVER 95% OF THE HABITAT ALREADY CONVERTED FOR AGRICULTURE, AND MOST OF THE COUNTRY'S BIODIVERSITY RESTING IN THE HANDS OF PRIVATE LANDOWNERS. MOST BIODIVERSITY IS ON PRIVATE LAND. State protected areas cannot reach it, which is why an instrument aimed at the title deed matters more than another park. THE THREAT IT IDENTIFIED, WHICH IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE: THE GREATEST THREAT TO WHAT REMAINS IS MISMANAGEMENT — NOT NECESSARILY MALICIOUS MISMANAGEMENT, BUT MORE A CASE OF LANDOWNERS NOT APPRECIATING THE UNIQUENESS AND RARITY OF THESE HABITATS. Worth carrying into any approach: the owner is often not an opponent, and a survey showing them what is on their land is the first move rather than a confrontation. AND THE OTHER MECHANISMS IT SITS AMONG, WITH THE CONSTRAINT NAMED: FROM BIODIVERSITY STEWARDSHIP, TO PROTECTED ENVIRONMENTS, TO PRIVATE NATURE RESERVES, THERE ARE MANY MECHANISMS AVAILABLE FOR LANDOWNERS TO FORMALLY PROTECT THEIR LAND — BUT A CHALLENGE IS LIMITED CAPACITY AND RESOURCES, RESULTING IN CIRCUMSTANCES WHERE THE NEED TO PROTECT BIODIVERSITY OUTWEIGHS THE SUPPLY TO DO SO. Three named alternatives to ask your own country's conservation authority about, and an honest statement that the bottleneck is people to do the paperwork rather than willing owners. WHO IT SUITS: African trusts, community organisations and sympathetic landowners wanting permanent protection registered against land, and anyone looking for a working easement model to copy. CAVEATS: A SMALL REGIONAL TRUST WORKING IN ONE SOUTH AFRICAN ECOSYSTEM WITH COMMERCIAL FARMERS — IT IS A MODEL AND A TOOLKIT FOR ELSEWHERE, NOT A SERVICE THAT OPERATES IN OTHER COUNTRIES, AND WHETHER A SERVITUDE CAN BE REGISTERED THIS WAY DEPENDS ON YOUR OWN PROPERTY LAW. For the body that buys farms outright, South Sudan's entry; for the self-declared community territory registry, Morocco's entry.

trackers.name: The Rural Women's Assembly — a 170,000-member movement of rural women across 11 countries that publishes its membership country by country — with its own charter, a demand worded as land with water rights, and a counter-summit timed against the regional heads of state meeting
trackers.desc: 170,000 WOMEN, COUNTED COUNTRY BY COUNTRY, DEMANDING LAND WITH WATER — method and adjacency declared first: THIS MOVEMENT WAS FOUNDED BY THREE ORGANISATIONS ALREADY IN THIS FILE — THE 48-COMMUNITY FEDERATION UNDER RWANDA, THE SIX-NGO RURAL COLLECTIVE UNDER SOMALIA, AND A FARM WOMEN'S PROJECT. THEIR ENTRIES NAME A RURAL WOMEN'S ASSEMBLY IN PASSING WITHOUT DESCRIBING IT OR SHIPPING THIS HOST, AND NONE IS RESTATED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THE SHIPPED HOST AND FIVE SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL ABSENT. THE PER-COUNTRY MEMBERSHIP, PUBLISHED, WHICH IS THE FIND: 23,000 IN ESWATINI, 2,050 IN MALAWI, 5,000 IN LESOTHO, 9,000 IN ZAMBIA, 9,017 IN SOUTH AFRICA, 65,000 IN ZIMBABWE AND 10,000 IN MOZAMBIQUE — WITH A CLAIMED TOTAL OF NEARLY 170,000 WOMEN IN 11 COUNTRIES. Almost no movement in this file publishes its membership broken down by country, and the breakdown is what makes it usable: a woman in Malawi can see that 2,050 others are already in, and a Zimbabwean chapter of 65,000 is a body a ministry has to answer. The uneven figures are also honest — this is not a movement pretending to be equally strong everywhere. THE DEMAND AS IT IS WORDED, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: TO ADVANCE LAND WITH WATER RIGHTS, FOOD SOVEREIGNTY, CLIMATE JUSTICE, AND WOMEN'S LEADERSHIP. LAND WITH WATER RIGHTS as the phrase, matching the rural collective recorded in this file's Somalia entry — the same correction reached twice, independently. Land granted without water is the failure this file recorded under Niger, and these movements now write the water into the demand itself. THE OWNERSHIP PROBLEM IT NAMES: RELATIVELY FEW WOMEN OWN THE LAND THEY CULTIVATE, LIMITING THEIR DECISION-MAKING POWER — IN A MEMBER'S WORDS, WE HAVE PART-CONTROL OVER SYSTEMS OF PRODUCTION, BUT IF YOU DON'T OWN THE LAND THEN THE INCOME, WHAT YOU PLANT AND HOW YOU PLANT IS OFTEN DECIDED ELSEWHERE. Working the land and controlling it are different things, and the gap between them is where a woman's labour turns into someone else's decision. HOW IT WAS FOUNDED AND BY WHOM: BORN IN 2009 WHEN OVER 250 WOMEN FROM NINE COUNTRIES — PEASANT PRODUCERS, SMALL-SCALE FARMERS, LAND RIGHTS ACTIVISTS AND LABOUR UNIONISTS — MET AT A THREE-DAY GATHERING ORGANISED BY THREE NAMED ORGANISATIONS, WHICH BECAME THE CATALYST FOR A UNIFIED FEMINIST GRASSROOTS MOVEMENT AND PRODUCED ITS CHARTER AND PLATFORM FOR ACTION. One three-day meeting of 250 people produced a charter and a movement now numbering six figures. That is a costable, repeatable act: convene the existing organisations, write the charter in the room, and leave with a platform rather than a communiqué. HOW IT IS STRUCTURED: A SELF-ORGANISED NETWORK OF RURAL WOMEN MOVEMENTS, ASSEMBLIES AND ORGANISATIONS IN DIFFERENT COUNTRIES, WHOSE MISSION IS TO MAKE SURE WOMEN IN THEIR OWN COUNTRIES' CHAPTERS ARE ABLE TO MOBILISE OTHER WOMEN AND ARTICULATE THE ISSUES. THE LEGAL FRAMEWORK IT HAS ADOPTED: A UNITED NATIONS DECLARATION ON THE RIGHTS OF PEASANTS, TAKEN UP AS AN ADVOCACY AND LEGAL FRAMEWORK THAT CAN PUT AUTHORITIES TO TASK AND CREATE ASSESSMENT CRITERIA. A declaration specifically for peasants, adopted deliberately as a measuring stick. This file has recorded communities searching for a standard to hold a government to; this is one written for exactly this constituency, and adopting it formally is a decision any assembly can take. WHAT IT ORGANISES THROUGH: TEACH-INS, WORKSHOPS, RESEARCH AND DOCUMENTATION, AND POLICY ADVOCACY — PROMOTING SEED SAVING, SEED SHARING AND SEED BANKS, SMALL-SCALE FARMING, NATURAL COMPOST AND THE REINTRODUCTION OF INDIGENOUS AND NUTRITIOUS FOODS; IT ALSO ENGAGES IN URGENT ACTION, PROVIDING RESOURCES AND COMFORT FOR SISTERS IN DIFFICULTY. URGENT ACTION for members in difficulty, run by the membership itself rather than by a foreign protection fund. Slower and smaller than the mechanisms filed elsewhere here, but it answers to the women it serves. THE SEED ARGUMENT IT MAKES: WHEN WOMEN LOSE THEIR SEEDS THEY LOSE MORE THAN CROPS — THEY LOSE INDEPENDENCE, NUTRITION, CULTURAL KNOWLEDGE, AND THE POWER TO DECIDE WHAT GROWS IN THEIR FIELDS; ACROSS THE REGION RURAL WOMEN FACE GROWING PRESSURE FROM AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS THAT ENCOURAGE THEM TO BUY COMMERCIAL SEED, FERTILISER AND PESTICIDES EVERY SEASON. Seed dependency as a form of dispossession that takes no land at all. A household buying seed every season has lost something even while holding title. THE CROSS-BORDER SEED PRACTICE, AND THE DEMAND BEHIND IT: WHEN THERE WAS TROUBLE IN ONE COUNTRY, WOMEN FROM OTHER SOUTHERN AFRICAN COUNTRIES CAME BRINGING INDIGENOUS SEEDS TO THE WOMEN OF THE ASSEMBLY THERE — AND IT HAS CALLED FOR THE OPENING OF BORDERS FOR SEED SHARING AND THE PROTECTION OF TRADITIONAL AND INDIGENOUS SEEDS FROM MULTINATIONAL CORPORATIONS. Members carried seed across borders to replant after a disaster. That is a mutual-aid system a network can run itself, and it is worth building the seed banks before the drought rather than after. THE COUNTER-SUMMIT IT HOLDS: A PEOPLE'S SUMMIT TIMED TO COINCIDE WITH THE ANNUAL REGIONAL HEADS OF STATE SUMMIT, WITH CLOSE TO 200 WOMEN GATHERING FROM NINE NAMED COUNTRIES, TRAVELLING AS AN ACT OF SOLIDARITY WITH THEIR SISTERS IN THE HOST COUNTRY. The same timing tactic as the mining counter-gathering recorded in this file's Rwanda entry: hold your assembly in the same city, the same week, while the press and the ministers are already there. THE COLLECTIVE WORK PRACTICE IT HAS REVIVED, AND THE CAMPAIGN NAME: A REVIVED AFRICAN TRADITION OF COLLECTIVE COMMUNITY WORK, IN ONE INSTANCE BRINGING MORE THAN 70 COMMUNITY MEMBERS INCLUDING WOMEN, MEN AND YOUNG PEOPLE TOGETHER TO PREPARE LAND FOR PLANTING — AND A ONE WOMAN, ONE HECTARE CAMPAIGN, ALONGSIDE SEED MULTIPLICATION SITES AND PRACTICAL AGRO-PROCESSING TRAINING SUCH AS MAKING JAM AND CANNING FRUIT. ONE WOMAN, ONE HECTARE is a demand small enough to be granted and specific enough to be counted. And the collective work tradition brings men and young people into a women's movement's activity without diluting who leads it. AND THE CONSULTATION PRINCIPLE IT ASSERTS: WHEN THE GOVERNMENT WANTS TO MAKE CHANGES IT HAS TO GO TO THE GROUND AND CONSULT US, WOMEN — BECAUSE OFTEN, WOMEN ARE NOT CONSULTED WHEN IT COMES TO CLIMATE JUSTICE; IT IS A BOTTOM-UP APPROACH. WHO IT SUITS: rural women farmers anywhere in southern Africa wanting a chapter to join or start, and organisations looking for a charter-plus-platform founding model or a seed-sharing mutual aid system. CAVEATS: A MEMBERSHIP MOVEMENT, NOT A FUNDER, A LAW CENTRE OR A LAND-PURCHASE BODY; ITS STRENGTH IS VERY UNEVEN BETWEEN COUNTRIES ON ITS OWN PUBLISHED FIGURES, AND CHAPTERS ARE SELF-ORGANISED, SO WHAT EXISTS NEAR YOU VARIES. For the federation that litigated against parliament, Rwanda's entry; for the collective that builds rural organisations before the land claim, Somalia's entry.

trackers.name: Nature Seychelles
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the oldest and largest environmental NGO in Seychelles, a registered association since 1998 with a board of trustees and around fifteen full-time staff including protected-area specialists. It manages Cousin Island Special Reserve and the Sanctuary at Roche Caiman, and through its Locally Empowered Area Protection project it has pioneered CO-MANAGEMENT under the country's nature reserve and conservancy legislation — the route by which local people take on protection and management of an area rather than leaving it to government. USE IT: start with LEAP if you want an area near you protected and locally run; use its protected-area staff if you need the technical case for why a site matters. It sits on government committees and taskforces and in the Citizen Engagement Platform Seychelles, so it has standing in consultations — but it works with government rather than against it, and will not fight a project for you.

trackers.name: Seychelles — Financial Services Authority (FSA)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the FSA registers & regulates companies, IBCs, foundations, trusts & securities and maintains the corporate register, Seychelles. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: SeyLII
trackers.desc: Seychelles Legal Information Institute: free judgments and legislation. · Find here: free Seychelles judgments and legislation (SeyLII / Laws.Africa).

trackers.name: Anti-Corruption Commission Seychelles (ACCS)
trackers.desc: National anti-corruption body of Seychelles — investigates graft, financial crime and abuse of public office.

trackers.name: Seychelles — Ministry of Finance, National Planning & Trade
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Finance Department plans & manages the Government budget and runs programme performance-based budgeting, Seychelles. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Seychelles.

trackers.name: Seychelles — Office of the Auditor General (OAG)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution; conducts financial, compliance, performance & special investigative audits per ISSAI and reports to the National Assembly, Seychelles.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: Court of Appeal — the state must clean up, and may owe damages
trackers.desc: A CONSTITUTIONAL DUTY TO ACT AGAINST POLLUTION BY PRIVATE PARTIES. Seychelles' highest court held that Article 38 of the Constitution means the state must act to ensure ‘that private citizens do not pollute the environment’; that it is obliged to take steps to clean up pollution caused to public places like rivers and beaches; and that failure to act could lead to claims for damages. The case was brought by a landowner at Fairview estate against the Minister of Environment, the Minister of Health and the Attorney General over serious E. coli pollution of a river, with the state arguing it was not constitutionally obliged to act. THREE THINGS MAKE THIS UNUSUALLY USEFUL: the duty runs against state passivity, so where a regulator does nothing the inaction is itself the breach; it attaches to public places, rivers and beaches named; and it carries a damages remedy, not merely a declaration. The judgment was unanimous, written by Janak de Silva, a non-resident judge from Sri Lanka — the appellate bench includes non-resident judges, which is why its environmental reasoning draws on wider common-law authority and why the decision is described as potentially influential beyond Seychelles.

trackers.name: EPA 2016 Appeals Board — written procedure, but budget for the fee
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE BELOW THE COURTS. The Environment Protection Act 2016 (No. 18 of 2016), gazetted 5 September 2016, expressly establishes an Appeals Board, and dedicated Appeals Rules of Procedure Regulations exist — so the procedure is written down and obtainable. BUDGET FOR THE FEE: the statutory Memorandum of Appeal requires you to state the grounds of appeal and to certify that a fee in Seychelles Rupees has been paid, with receipt number and date — appeals are not free, so establish the current fee before the deadline, not after. WHAT ELSE THE ACT PROVIDES: the Minister may declare protected coastal zones and prepare an Integrated Coastal Zone Management Plan; may regulate petroleum and mineral exploration in territorial waters and the EEZ; EIA runs by prescribed classes, with an Environmental Appraisal Committee and registered EIA consultants — so a consultant's registration is checkable. THE ADMINISTRATOR MAY SERVE AN ENFORCEMENT NOTICE OR A PROHIBITION NOTICE — ask whether either has been served, because they are documents. Obstructing an inspection is punishable. The Act is live: plastic bag rules 2017, a tourism environmental sustainability levy, effluent standards and laboratory rules all 2023. WHO OPERATES: Nature Seychelles (BirdLife partner) manages the Cousin Special Island Reserve — 27 ha plus waters to 400 m from the high-water mark; Island Conservation Society staffs centres on 6 outer islands under a 2007 agreement with the parastatal Islands Development Company. DO NOT APPROACH the Nature Protection Trust of Seychelles — the first environmental NGO registered here (1992) — it ceased operating in 2011.

trackers.name: SeyCCAT Blue Grants Fund — grant money created by converting national debt, with the application form translated into Creole so locals could actually apply
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the Seychelles Conservation and Climate Adaptation Trust, created in 2015 as an independent, nationally based public-private trust fund to manage the proceeds of the world's first debt-for-nature swap for ocean conservation — US$21.6 million of national debt bought back at a discount, with the redirected debt service capitalising the trust — later joined by proceeds of a sovereign blue bond that raised US$15 million from investors. It runs the Blue Grants Fund. WHAT IT PAYS AND ON WHAT TERMS: reported disbursement rose from about US$286,500 in the first call to roughly US$889,000 across twenty-one projects in the third year, with US$700,000 a year available at that point and more than US$5.3 million distributed in total by 2025. Two windows are described: small-to-medium grants up to SCR 100,000, awarded on an approved concept note, maximum 12 months; and large grants between SCR 100,000 and SCR 1,000,000, shortlisted on a concept note then awarded on a full proposal, maximum 24 months. A concept note first, not a full proposal, is a low-cost way in for a small association. THE PART TO STEAL, BECAUSE IT IS AN ACCESS PROBLEM EVERY FUND IN THIS FILE HAS: the application form was originally in a standard European format that experienced NGOs could handle but local stakeholders could not, so in 2019 SeyCCAT translated the application form into Creole so people could apply in their own language, held public meetings across three islands, and did one-to-one visits with fishing communities, students and young women entrepreneurs. Ask any fund whether its form exists in the language its intended applicants speak. WHO IT SUITS: Seychellois NGOs, fishers' associations and community groups working on marine protection, sustainable fisheries and climate adaptation. CAVEATS: it funds ocean, fisheries and climate work — not litigation, not land purchase, and not opposition to a project; grants run to fixed short terms; and the model depends on debt-conversion and bond proceeds rather than open-ended income.

trackers.name: Seychelles legal aid — EVERY licensed lawyer must take legal aid cases as a condition of their licence, and you apply to the Judiciary
trackers.desc: WHO OWES YOU A LAWYER, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST RULE FOUND ANYWHERE IN THIS FILE: in Seychelles ALL LICENSED LEGAL PRACTITIONERS — UNLESS EXEMPT — MUST, AS A CONDITION OF THEIR LEGAL PRACTITIONER'S LICENCE, TAKE LEGAL AID CASES. Not a voluntary scheme, not a pro bono appeal to conscience: the obligation is attached to the licence itself, so the entire practising profession is the pool. Compare Mozambique and Angola, where the bar's statutes impose a duty, and every other country in this file where legal aid depends on who volunteers. HOW TO APPLY, AND WHERE: applications are filed WITH THE JUDICIARY, which reviews them, notifies the outcome, and ALLOCATES A LAWYER to your case if approved. THE MEANS TEST IS PUBLISHED AS A NUMBER: you must earn LESS THAN SCR 8,000 PER MONTH, and proof of your financial position is required. A published income threshold means you can determine your own eligibility before you go — rarer in this file than it should be. Scale: 784 legal aid applications were filed with the Judiciary in a single year in a country of under 100,000 people. The Registrar of the Supreme Court licenses practitioners under the Legal Practitioners Act, and publishes the roll of licensed lawyers — including suspensions, so you can check who is currently entitled to practise before instructing anyone. WHO IT SUITS: Seychellois who cannot afford a lawyer in a land, property, planning or environmental matter, on any island. CAVEATS: A MEANS-TESTED STATE SCHEME administered by the Judiciary — allocation is to an available practitioner rather than a specialist of your choosing, and the scheme does not fund campaigning; the threshold figure should be confirmed as current. For the coastal and marine conservation route and the Blue Grants Fund, Seychelles' SeyCCAT entry; for standing to litigate environmental matters, the Eco-Sud precedent recorded under Mauritius.

trackers.name: CEPS and the Seychelles NGO directory — the civil society umbrella that publishes every member's address, phone and named focal person, plus TRASS on Praslin and the Islands Foundation
trackers.desc: THE DIRECTORY AND THE ISLAND GROUPS: the CITIZENS ENGAGEMENT PLATFORM SEYCHELLES (CEPS, ceps.sc) is THE UMBRELLA ORGANISATION OF CIVIL SOCIETY IN SEYCHELLES, whose members include this file's Nature Seychelles, and which is recorded as able to take A MONITORING AND WATCHDOG ROLE to ensure CITIZEN CONCERNS ARE NOT BEING NEGLECTED on national engagement platforms; it belongs to the Southern African council of NGOs. THE PART THAT MAKES IT USABLE TODAY: CEPS PUBLISHES A DIRECTORY OF NGOs GIVING EACH MEMBER'S FOUNDING DATE, POSTAL ADDRESS, TELEPHONE NUMBER, EMAIL AND NAMED FOCAL PERSON — including entries for the TERRESTRIAL RESTORATION ACTION SOCIETY OF SEYCHELLES at Baie Ste Anne, Praslin (tel +248 513370, focal person named), SUSTAINABILITY FOR SEYCHELLES (tel +248 422 4072, focal person named, category Environment and Natural Resources), and the SEYCHELLES ISLANDS FOUNDATION at La Ciotat Building, Mont Fleuri, PO Box 853, Victoria. A published directory with a named focal person per organisation removes the hardest step in a small country — you are not writing to an institution, you are writing to a person whose name and number are printed. Start there. THE ISLAND ORGANISATION AND WHAT IT DOES WITH PRIVATE LAND: TRASS is a not-for-profit based on PRASLIN committed to restoring degraded ecosystems, mobilising interested parties for the restoration, enhancement, maintenance and SAFEGUARDING of areas AFFECTED BY FOREST FIRES, and WORKING IN PARTNERSHIP WITH PRIVATE LANDOWNERS, government, the private sector and other NGOs so that degraded land can be fully restored. Fourteen years on it holds a solid group of volunteers — one member records having MOBILISED OVER 200 OTHER VOLUNTEERS — and has opened a second nursery with capacity for TWELVE THOUSAND LOCAL AND RARE FRUIT PLANTS, integrating agroforestry with endemic, native and medicinal planting under a USD 31 MILLION ridge-to-reef project CO-FINANCED BY GOVERNMENT, A UN AGENCY AND CIVIL SOCIETIES. An organisation that partners with PRIVATE LANDOWNERS is the one to bring to a landowner who is wavering — restoration is an alternative to selling, and here it comes with a nursery and two hundred volunteers attached. AND THE TRUST THAT HOLDS WORLD HERITAGE: the SEYCHELLES ISLANDS FOUNDATION (SIF, sif.sc), a NON-PROFIT CHARITABLE ORGANISATION ESTABLISHED AS A PUBLIC TRUST BY THE GOVERNMENT IN 1979, manages ALDABRA ATOLL AND THE VALLÉE DE MAI, governed by a BOARD OF FIFTEEN TRUSTEES, with the local population encouraged to engage through public awareness and outreach. WHO IT SUITS: Seychellois on any island seeking an organisation, a landowner considering restoration, or a community wanting its concern monitored nationally. CAVEATS: A SMALL VOLUNTEER SECTOR; confirm listings. For the island bought in 1968 and the co-management act, Seychelles' Nature Seychelles entry; for grant money from a debt conversion, SeyCCAT; for the duty on every licensed lawyer, the legal aid entry.

trackers.name: Island Conservation Society — signed a 2007 agreement to be conservation manager on a state company's islands and now staffs six of them, plus the island bought outright by a single donor in 1973
trackers.desc: THE ISLAND SOMEBODY BOUGHT, AND THE CONTRACT TO STAFF THE REST: the ISLAND CONSERVATION SOCIETY (ICS) WAS REGISTERED AS AN NGO IN SEYCHELLES ON 25 MARCH 2001, with its head office — THE ISLAND CONSERVATION CENTRE — AT POINTE LARUE, MAHÉ, focusing on THE PROTECTION AND REHABILITATION OF THE SMALL ISLANDS OF SEYCHELLES, PARTICULARLY THE OUTER ISLANDS. THE ARRANGEMENT IS THE RESOURCE: MOST OF THE OUTER ISLANDS ARE GOVERNMENT-OWNED AND MANAGED BY A PARASTATAL COMPANY, AND IN 2007 ICS SIGNED AN AGREEMENT WITH THAT COMPANY TO ACT AS CONSERVATION MANAGERS AND ADVISERS ON ALL ITS ISLANDS — AND ICS NOW EMPLOYS FULL-TIME SCIENTISTS AND RANGERS AT CONSERVATION CENTRES ON SIX OF THEM. A single agreement with the state company that holds the land put paid conservation staff onto six islands. Where a parastatal holds the ground you want protected, the route is a management-and-advice agreement with the company — not a campaign against it. Ask what it would take to be named conservation adviser. ICS records OVER 20 YEARS OF SCIENTIFIC DATA ON THE MARINE AND TERRESTRIAL BIODIVERSITY OF SIX ISLANDS AND ATOLLS, with a presence across ARIDE, ALPHONSE, DESROCHES, PLATE ISLAND, SILHOUETTE and the outer atolls of FARQUHAR, ASTOVE and COSMOLEDO, working seabird monitoring, marine protection, invasive species removal and habitat restoration, with fewer than 50 staff. Twenty years of biodiversity data held by an NGO rather than a ministry is a body of evidence that does not disappear when a government changes. Ask ICS what its series shows for your island. AND THE PURCHASE, WHICH IS THE PLAINEST PRECEDENT IN THIS FILE'S SEYCHELLOIS RECORD: A UK-INCORPORATED WILDLIFE CHARITY PURCHASED ARIDE ISLAND NATURE RESERVE IN SEYCHELLES WITH FUNDS DONATED BY A NAMED INDIVIDUAL IN 1973. An entire island bought outright with one person's donation, and still a nature reserve half a century later. When somebody asks whether buying the land is realistic, Aride is the answer — and the vehicle was a charity incorporated by charter that could hold it in perpetuity. HOW ICS FUNDS ITSELF, WORTH COPYING AND WORTH WATCHING: PARTNERSHIPS HAVE BEEN DEVELOPED FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF HOTELS ON SEVERAL ISLANDS, and a named cosmetics company agreed a TWO-YEAR SPONSORSHIP focused on enhancing the protection of one island's marine environment. Hotel partnerships fund the rangers and also put buildings on the island. Read that arrangement carefully before you copy it: ask what the developer got, and what the NGO can veto. ITS NAMED PARTNERS INCLUDE: the PLANT CONSERVATION ACTION GROUP (PCA), whose mission is to serve as THE PRINCIPAL SOURCE OF ADVICE AND INFORMATION ON THE TECHNICAL ASPECT OF PLANT CONSERVATION IN SEYCHELLES and to mobilise action for species threatened with extinction AND THOSE OF IMPORTANCE FOR HUMAN WELFARE, publishing a newsletter available online; and the MARINE CONSERVATION SOCIETY SEYCHELLES, incorporating a shark research institute. A group that names itself the principal source of technical plant advice is who to ask for the species list before a clearance — and note it counts plants important for HUMAN welfare, not only rare ones. WHO IT SUITS: Seychellois island communities, anyone facing a parastatal landholder, and groups considering outright purchase. CAVEATS: HOTEL AND CORPORATE SPONSORSHIP UNDERPINS SOME OF THIS WORK — check the terms. For the co-management pioneered under the nature reserve and conservancy act, Seychelles' Nature Seychelles entry; for grant money from converted national debt, SeyCCAT; for named focal persons per organisation, the CEPS directory; for a 12,000-plant nursery run by volunteers, TRASS.

trackers.name: The Seychelles Islands Foundation — a public trust whose 14-member board reserves at least five seats for conservation organisations — plus the farmers' and wildlife club members with phone numbers and the schools training programme
trackers.desc: FIVE OF THE FOURTEEN SEATS ARE RESERVED — and that clause is the reason this entry exists: THE SEYCHELLES ISLANDS FOUNDATION IS A PUBLIC TRUST ESTABLISHED IN 1979 BY THE GOVERNMENT, WITH THE PRESIDENT AS PATRON, TO MANAGE AND PROTECT THE COUNTRY'S TWO UNESCO WORLD HERITAGE SITES — AND ITS BOARD OF TRUSTEES, APPOINTED BY THE PRESIDENT, HAS 14 MEMBERS, INCLUDING AT LEAST FIVE REPRESENTATIVES FROM ORGANIZATIONS CONCERNED WITH THE CONSERVATION OF WILDLIFE AND NATURAL HISTORY, OR NATIONAL ACADEMIES OF SCIENCE. At least five of fourteen, written into the trust's own constitution, held by conservation organisations rather than by ministries. That is a minority with a guaranteed floor — and it is the clause to ask for whenever a body is being created to manage land near you: not consultation, not observer status, a stated minimum number of seats for organisations of your kind. Seychelles wrote it in 1979. AND WHY: ITS FORMATION WAS DRIVEN BY THE NEED FOR AN INDEPENDENT, SCIENCE-BASED INSTITUTION TO OVERSEE THE CONSERVATION OF THESE SITES, PARTICULARLY THOSE AT RISK DUE TO THEIR ISOLATION AND SENSITIVITY — and it is described as THE LONGEST ESTABLISHED LOCAL ORGANISATION WORKING IN NATURE CONSERVATION IN SEYCHELLES, having taken a PIONEERING MANAGEMENT APPROACH BY TWINNING THE TWO SITES, and being MANDATED TO ENSURE THEY ARE WELL-MANAGED PROTECTED AREAS WHERE CONSERVATION, RESEARCH, EDUCATION AND TOURISM ARE SUSTAINABLY BALANCED. A public trust rather than a government department, deliberately, so that the science would be independent of the ministry of the day. This file has flagged the trust form repeatedly as the vehicle able to hold land in perpetuity — here it is holding two World Heritage Sites and a nature reserve. THE MONITORING RECORD, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES A CLAIM STICK: SINCE 2014 THE FOUNDATION HAS ANNUALLY MONITORED THE CORAL REEFS OF ONE ATOLL, DOCUMENTING CHANGES THROUGH MAJOR BLEACHING EVENTS IN 2016 AND 2024 AND PROVIDING KEY INSIGHTS INTO THEIR RESILIENCE AND RECOVERY. Ten years of annual monitoring across two bleaching events. A ten-year series is the difference between saying the reef is dying and proving when and how fast — and it only exists because somebody started counting in a year when nothing was happening. THE ENERGY FIGURE WORTH KNOWING FOR ANY REMOTE STATION: A RENEWABLE ENERGY SYSTEM TODAY SUPPLIES 98% OF THE ATOLL'S ELECTRICITY DEMAND WITH SOLAR POWER — IMPLEMENTED OVER FOUR YEARS BY A STAFF MEMBER, AS PART OF HER MSc THESIS. Ninety-eight per cent solar on a remote atoll, and it was somebody's masters project. If your community facility runs on generators and diesel, a student needing a thesis subject is a free engineer — approach the nearest university department, not a contractor. THE TRAINING THAT MEMBER ORGANISATIONS CAN GET: with financial support from a critical ecosystem partnership fund, the national civil society platform ran a FOUR-DAY TRAINING PROGRAMME FOR MEMBERS REPRESENTING A WIDE RANGE OF THEMATIC AREAS, EMPHASISING TECHNICAL CAPACITY-BUILDING WITH A PARTICULAR FOCUS ON CLIMATE RESILIENCE AND ECOSYSTEM-BASED ADAPTATION; A THREE-DAY SESSION FOR SEVEN OF ITS CORE TEAM; AND A THREE-DAY PROGRAMME BRINGING TOGETHER OVER 40 STUDENTS FROM FIVE SECONDARY SCHOOLS — concluding with a site visit to a named bay. Members, staff and schoolchildren trained in the same programme, and the platform trained its own core team too. That last part is the one organisations skip: the umbrella that trains everyone else and never itself becomes the bottleneck. Ask your national platform when it last trained its own staff. TWO MORE MEMBER BODIES WITH CONTACTS, BOTH FILED UNDER AN ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES COMMISSION: WILD LIFE CLUBS OF SEYCHELLES, C/O A NAMED PO BOX IN VICTORIA, MAHÉ, WITH TWO TELEPHONE NUMBERS AND A FOCAL PERSON; AND A VAL D'ANDORRE FARMERS ASSOCIATION, WITH A TELEPHONE NUMBER AND AN EMAIL. A FARMERS ASSOCIATION sitting in the environment and natural resources commission of the national civil society platform. On a small island the farmers and the conservationists are in the same commission by design — which is how a land-use disagreement gets settled between neighbours rather than in a ministry. Also named in the same platform: AN ECOTOURISM SOCIETY OF SEYCHELLES with a named focal person and address, and a SUSTAINABILITY ORGANISATION with a named doctor as focal person and a published telephone, which states it COLLABORATES WITH CITIZENS, THE GOVERNMENT, NGOs AND THE PRIVATE SECTOR and invites people to CONTACT US TO BECOME A VOLUNTEER OR MEMBER. An open invitation to become a member or volunteer, with a phone number. That is the lowest possible barrier to entry, and it is worth taking literally. WHO IT SUITS: Seychellois community groups, farmers' associations and anyone arguing for reserved seats on a management body. CAVEATS: A PRESIDENTIALLY-PATRONED PUBLIC TRUST — independent by design but appointed from the top. For the umbrella and the full NGO directory, Seychelles' CEPS entry; for the organisation that signed a 2007 agreement to manage six outer islands and staffs full-time scientists and rangers, the Island Conservation Society entry.

trackers.name: Wetlands International — the mangrove organisation with African regional offices, small grants for community groups and an eleven-country exchange network — whose whole method is that planting is the part that fails and the water flow is what to fix
trackers.desc: PLANTING IS THE PART THAT FAILS; FIX THE WATER INSTEAD — an off-brief note first, recorded honestly: THIS ROUND FIRST EXAMINED A WETLAND CONVENTION'S ADVISORY-MISSION ROUTE AND DID NOT FILE IT. A SITE CAN BE ADDED TO THAT REGISTER ONLY WITH THE APPROVAL OF THE PARTY IN WHOSE TERRITORY IT LIES, AND THE MISSION COMES ONLY UPON RECEIVING A REQUEST FROM A CONTRACTING PARTY — SO A COMMUNITY CANNOT TRIGGER IT. IT IS A STATE MECHANISM, NOT A RESOURCE AVAILABLE TO LOCALS. THE METHOD, WHICH IS THE FIND: INSTEAD OF FOCUSING SOLELY ON MANGROVE PLANTING, IT WORKS TO RESTORE UNDERLYING HYDROLOGY LIKE THE MIXING OF SALTWATER AND FRESHWATER SO THAT THE MANGROVES REGENERATE NATURALLY — CONSIDERING ADJUSTMENTS TO A DISTURBED AREA'S TOPOGRAPHY, RESULTING IN TRUE ECOSYSTEM RESTORATION WITH A RICHER BIODIVERSITY. Restore the water flow and the mangroves come back on their own. Planting seedlings is what every project does and what most projects lose — the seedlings die because the reason the mangroves went is still there. If somebody offers your community a planting day, ask first what blocked the tidal channel. THE FAILURE DIAGNOSED BY A COMMUNITY MEMBER RATHER THAN THE ORGANISATION: MANY MANGROVE RESTORATION INITIATIVES HAVE BEEN FAILING TO BEAR FRUIT DUE TO A LACK OF KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS ON ECOLOGICAL MANGROVE RESTORATION — IN ONE NAMED PLACE, MOST RESTORATION INITIATIVES HAVE FOCUSED ON PLANTING AND IGNORED THE CRUCIAL ASPECTS OF THE RESTORATION PROCESS: MAINLY BIOLOGICAL, SOCIAL, HISTORICAL AND POLITICAL. SOCIAL, HISTORICAL AND POLITICAL listed as parts of a restoration process. Who used to hold that shoreline, who cut it and why, and who benefits now are restoration questions, not distractions from it. THE TRAINING, AND WHO SITS IN THE ROOM: SINCE 2019 IT HAS PARTNERED WITH A NAMED MANGROVE ORGANISATION TO TRAIN LOCAL COMMUNITIES, FOREST MANAGERS, NATIONAL AND SUB-NATIONAL GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS, ACADEMIA AND RESEARCH INSTITUTIONS, CIVIL SOCIETY AND PRIVATE SECTOR ON THE COMMUNITY-BASED ECOLOGICAL MANGROVE RESTORATION APPROACH — AND IMPORTANTLY, LOCAL MANGROVE COMMUNITIES LEARN TO PERFORM THIS WORK, AND IN THE PROCESS LEARN TO RESTORE, VALUE, AND RESPONSIBLY STEWARD THEIR MANGROVES. Communities and the forest officers who police them, trained together on the same method. That is worth more than the technique itself: after it, both sides are arguing from the same manual. THE MONEY THAT REACHES GROUPS DIRECTLY: SMALL GRANTS FOR COMMUNITY GROUPS HAVE BEEN USED TO SUPPORT MANGROVE ACTIVITIES — AND THE EXCHANGE VISITS SHOWED PRACTICAL EXAMPLES OF COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT THROUGH THE PROVISION OF FUNDING FOR LIVELIHOOD DIVERSIFICATION AND COASTAL PROTECTION. THE STRUCTURE THAT KEEPS IT ALIVE AFTER THE PROJECT: A GROUP OF VOLUNTEERS HAS BEEN RECRUITED AND TRAINED AS FOCAL POINTS TO MAINTAIN RESTORATION ACTIVITIES AS FAR AS POSSIBLE. Named volunteer focal points, as this file has recorded working for pastoralist security training and for park-edge site support groups. The same cheap device keeps appearing because it works: give two or three people a title and the work survives the funding. THE ELEVEN-COUNTRY EXCHANGE NETWORK, WHICH IS THE THING TO ASK TO JOIN: MANGROVE EXCHANGE VISITS BROUGHT TOGETHER PRACTITIONERS REPRESENTING COMMUNITIES, POLICYMAKERS, CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS AND RESEARCHERS FROM KENYA, MADAGASCAR, MOZAMBIQUE AND TANZANIA ON THE WESTERN INDIAN OCEAN SIDE, AND SENEGAL, GUINEA-BISSAU, GUINEA, SIERRA LEONE, LIBERIA, NIGERIA AND GAMBIA ON THE ATLANTIC COAST — WHERE THEY SAW BEST PRACTICES IN SITE SELECTION, COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND RESTORATION METHODS. A REGIONAL PLATFORM FOR AFRICA'S MANGROVE CONSERVATION WAS ESTABLISHED OUT OF IT. Eleven countries and both coasts, with community representatives travelling alongside the officials. A platform that already exists is far easier to join than one you have to build — ask the regional office when the next exchange is and who nominates. THE PROGRAMME'S SIZE: A TEN-YEAR PROGRAMME LAUNCHED IN 2017 AIMS TO SAFEGUARD 1 MILLION HECTARES OF AFRICAN MANGROVES BENEFITTING 2 MILLION PEOPLE, WITH A NEWER PROJECT AIMING AT 65,000 HECTARES IN ONE NAMED REGION AND AN OFFICE OPENED IN A NAMED REGIONAL TOWN, PLUS TRAINING FOR LOCAL STAKEHOLDERS AROUND A GLOBAL MANGROVE WATCH TOOL. An office in a regional town rather than only the capital, and a free monitoring tool taught to local stakeholders. Both are reachability, which is what decides whether a resource is real for a village. WHAT IS ACTUALLY AT STAKE, IN NUMBERS: MORE THAN 100,000 INHABITANTS IN ONE NAMED DELTA DEPEND ON THE AREA'S MANGROVES FOR HONEY PRODUCTION, AGRICULTURE, SALT EXTRACTION AND ECO-TOURISM — AND COASTAL COMMUNITIES CONTRIBUTE TO RESTORATION AND IN RETURN ARE EMPOWERED TO DEVELOP ALTERNATIVE LIVELIHOODS AND SUSTAINABLY USE MANGROVE PRODUCTS LIKE OYSTERS. Honey, salt, oysters and tourism from a mangrove nobody was paying for. Listing what your wetland already produces, with numbers, is the argument against the development that would replace it — and one this file has recorded winning where a bare conservation appeal lost. AND THE OFFICES: A NAMED REGIONAL AFRICA ARM AND A NAMED EAST AFRICA ARM, EACH WITH ITS OWN SITE AND CONTACTS. WHO IT SUITS: African coastal and island communities whose mangroves, deltas or wetlands are degraded or under development pressure. CAVEATS: IT WORKS THROUGH PROGRAMMES AND PARTNERSHIPS, NOT OPEN APPLICATIONS — approach the regional arm nearest you. For the 30-day closure that raised village income 136%, São Tomé's community marine management entry; for the fishers' own national network, Madagascar's MIHARI entry; for the free grants with no co-financing, Kenya's BIOPAMA entry.

trackers.name: The organisation that becomes a co-complainant beside your own community body before the African Commission and Court — with two won land judgments, a published legal-cases site, and an independent 15-year evaluation of whether the approach works
trackers.desc: THEY PUT THEIR OWN NAME ON THE CASE BESIDE YOURS — adjacency declared first: A BANJUL-BASED PRO BONO COUNSEL THAT TAKES COMMUNITY CASES TO THE SAME BODIES ALREADY HAS ITS OWN ENTRY UNDER GAMBIA. THIS IS A DIFFERENT ORGANISATION WITH A DIFFERENT ROLE, CROSS-REFERENCED BELOW. THE STRUCTURAL FIND, AND IT IS ABOUT WHO IS NAMED ON THE PAPERS: IN ONE CASE THE COMPLAINANTS WERE A NATIONAL MINORITY RIGHTS CENTRE AND THIS ORGANISATION, ACTING ON BEHALF OF A COMMUNITY WELFARE COUNCIL. IN THE SECOND, THE THREE ORIGINAL COMPLAINANTS WERE THIS ORGANISATION, THE COMMUNITY'S OWN DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME, AND THE SAME NATIONAL CENTRE. The community's own organisation is a named complainant, not a beneficiary. That is the arrangement to insist on: this file has recorded case after case brought FOR communities in which the community had no standing, no say in settlement and no copy of the file. Here a village-level body sits on the claim alongside a national NGO and an international one — three names, one case. THE ROUTE THOSE CASES TOOK, STATED PLAINLY: AFTER FAILED ATTEMPTS AT NATIONAL LEVEL, INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES RESORTED TO THE AFRICAN COMMISSION AND COURT ON HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS, WHICH BOTH RULED IN FAVOUR OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' LAND RIGHTS, ORDERED THAT MEASURES BE TAKEN FOR LAND RESTITUTION AND COMPENSATION, AND DECLARED THAT THE STATE HAD VIOLATED THEIR HUMAN RIGHTS. AFTER FAILED ATTEMPTS AT NATIONAL LEVEL. Losing at home is a precondition of these routes rather than the end of the road — and communities routinely stop at the point where this actually begins. WHAT THE FIRST DECISION ESTABLISHED, AND IT IS DIRECTLY THIS FILE'S SUBJECT: THE COMMISSION EXAMINED A GOVERNMENT'S EVICTION OF AN INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY FROM ANCESTRAL LAND AROUND A LAKE TO ESTABLISH A GAME RESERVE — FINDING VIOLATIONS OF THE RIGHTS TO RELIGION, CULTURE, PROPERTY, NATURAL RESOURCES AND DEVELOPMENT, AND CALLING FOR RECOGNITION OF THE COMMUNITY'S OWNERSHIP OF ITS ANCESTRAL LAND AND ITS RESTITUTION — AN IMPORTANT PRECEDENT FOR ENSURING EQUITY AND PARTICIPATION IN NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT AND DEVELOPMENT ON INDIGENOUS LANDS. Evicted to make a game reserve, and the eviction was held unlawful. Conservation displacement is not an exception to rights law on this continent — there is a continental decision saying so, and it is citable by any community facing the same. WHAT THE SECOND DID: THE FIRST INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' RIGHTS CASE CONSIDERED BY THE COURT, AND BY FAR THE LARGEST EVER CASE IT HAD TO CONSIDER, FINDING VIOLATIONS OF SEVEN ARTICLES OF THE AFRICAN CHARTER AND CREATING A MAJOR LEGAL PRECEDENT — WITH A REPARATIONS JUDGMENT FOLLOWING THAT CLARIFIED THE SCOPE AND CONTENT OF STATE OBLIGATIONS TO UPHOLD INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' LAND RIGHTS. THE PARTICIPATION MODEL, WHICH IS THE MOST COPYABLE PART: THE LITIGATION ITSELF AND THE COMMUNITY'S PARTICIPATION IN THE VARIOUS STAGES OF THE LEGAL PROCESS PROVIDED A MODEL FOR COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT, THROUGH WHICH THE COMMUNITY WERE EMPOWERED TO BETTER UNDERSTAND AND ADVOCATE FOR THEIR RIGHTS — AND AT THE HEARING, 25 COMMUNITY MEMBERS ATTENDED IN PERSON AND A FURTHER 40 VIEWED IT AT HOME BY LIVESTREAM. Twenty-five people in the courtroom and forty watching at home. Somebody budgeted for that, and it is why the case built a movement rather than only a judgment. If your lawyers are not planning for community attendance, ask them to — it is a line in a grant application, not an impossibility. THE INDEPENDENT EVALUATION OF WHETHER ANY OF THIS WORKS: A COMMISSIONED EVALUATION OF 15 YEARS OF LITIGATION AND LEGAL EMPOWERMENT PROGRAMMES WITH MINORITIES AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLES IN EAST AFRICA FOUND THESE ACTIVITIES TO BE POWERFUL TOOLS THAT CREATE SPACES AND OPPORTUNITIES FOR COMMUNITIES TO UNITE AROUND SHARED STRUGGLES AND MAKE DECISIONS THAT CAN IMPACT POSITIVELY ON THEIR COLLECTIVE RIGHTS — CONSIDERING THREE NAMED EAST AFRICAN COMMUNITIES, FINDING THE PROGRAMMES SUCCESSFUL OVERALL, AND DRAWING LESSONS FOR FUTURE ACTIVITIES. THE FINDINGS ARE STRONGLY BASED ON FEEDBACK DIRECT FROM THE RELEVANT COMMUNITIES, AND THE FULL REPORT IS PUBLISHED. An organisation that paid for an outside review of its own method and published it, with the communities' own verdict in it. Read that before agreeing to be somebody's test case. THE HONEST RECORD ON ENFORCEMENT, WHICH THIS FILE HAS FLAGGED BEFORE: THERE WERE CONTINUING VIOLATIONS OF THE PROVISIONAL MEASURES ORDER, INCLUDING A VIOLENT EVICTION OF APPROXIMATELY 1,000 PEOPLE AND POLICE INTIMIDATION WHILE JUDGMENT WAS AWAITED — AND THE ORGANISATION ITSELF NOTED A HISTORY OF LAX IMPLEMENTATION OF THE EARLIER JUDGMENT. An order in your favour did not stop the evictions. Budget the enforcement fight as a separate campaign with its own years and its own money, as this file's Kenyan strategic-legal entry also records. THE SUPPORTING PRESSURE THAT CAME WITH IT: A UN ANTI-RACISM BODY URGED THE GOVERNMENT TO ENSURE LEGAL ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF THE COLLECTIVE RIGHTS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND TO PREVENT, PUNISH AND SANCTION ACTS THREATENING THEIR SECURITY AND PROPERTY. Two international bodies saying the same thing in the same year. Cases are won in parallel, not in a single forum — and a second body's statement costs far less to obtain than a judgment. THE STAKES AS ITS LEGAL DIRECTOR PUT THEM: THE CASE IS OF FUNDAMENTAL IMPORTANCE FOR INDIGENOUS PEOPLES IN AFRICA, PARTICULARLY GIVEN THE CONTINENT-WIDE CONFLICTS BETWEEN COMMUNITIES SPARKED BY PRESSURES OVER LAND AND RESOURCES — AND ULTIMATELY THE COURT WOULD BE RULING ON THE CRUCIAL ROLE OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES IN THE CONSERVATION OF LAND AND NATURAL RESOURCES. AND THE PUBLISHED RESOURCES: A LEGAL CASES WEBSITE, ACADEMIC ARTICLES ON LITIGATING INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' RIGHTS IN AFRICA INCLUDING ITS POTENTIALS, CHALLENGES AND LIMITATIONS, AND A NAMED WORK ON LITIGATION AS A TOOL FOR COMMUNITY EMPOWERMENT. POTENTIALS, CHALLENGES AND LIMITATIONS — published by the people who won the cases. That is the honest reading list before a community commits years to a case. WHO IT SUITS: African indigenous and minority communities who have exhausted national courts over eviction, land or resource rights, and the national organisations working with them. CAVEATS: A SMALL ORGANISATION TAKING STRATEGIC CASES OVER MANY YEARS, NOT A GENERAL LEGAL SERVICE — approach through a national partner, and expect a decade. For pro bono counsel before the same bodies, Gambia's IHRDA entry; for rapid legal support when defenders are criminalized, Kenya's Strategic Legal Response Centre entry; for university law clinics as free representation, Comoros' entry.

trackers.name: PAFO (Pan-African Farmers Organisation) — the continental platform recognised as the representative body of African farmers' organisations at the highest level — five regional member networks, founded under African Union sponsorship, with signed memoranda giving farmers a named door at a development bank
trackers.desc: THE HIGHEST CONTINENTAL SEAT AFRICAN FARMERS HOLD — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S MAURITANIA ENTRY COVERS THE WEST AFRICAN MEMBER NETWORK IN DETAIL, ITS ESWATINI ENTRY THE ALLIANCE THAT PARTNERS WITH THESE NETWORKS, AND ITS MALI ENTRY THE EASTERN AND SOUTHERN FARMERS' FORUM. THE SAME DEVELOPMENT BANK NAMED BELOW HAS ITS REVIEW MECHANISM UNDER NIGERIA AND ITS LEGAL FACILITY UNDER GAMBIA. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THEIR HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE RECOGNITION, AND IT IS THE FIND: IT IS RECOGNIZED AS THE REPRESENTATIVE BODY OF AFRICAN FARMERS' ORGANIZATIONS AT THE HIGHEST CONTINENTAL LEVEL — A CONTINENTAL ORGANIZATION WHOSE MEMBERSHIP BASE IS REGIONAL FARMERS NETWORKS. There is a recognised continental seat, and farmers hold it. That matters practically rather than symbolically: when a community's issue is bigger than its country — a transboundary concession, a regional trade rule, a continental agriculture policy — there is an existing body with standing to raise it, reachable through your own national organisation. This file has recorded communities trying to build that reach from scratch. THE LADDER, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT USABLE: MORE THAN 80 MILLION FARMERS INTEGRATED INTO NEARLY 70 TO 73 NATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS, UNIONS, FEDERATIONS, COOPERATIVES AND ASSOCIATIONS, PRESENT IN MORE THAN 45 TO 48 COUNTRIES, UNITED IN FIVE REGIONAL NETWORKS — GROUPED WITHIN THE NATIONAL PLATFORMS OF MORE THAN 30 COUNTRIES. Village group to national platform to regional network to continental seat. Four steps, all of them existing, none requiring anybody's permission to begin — and the figures are recorded as found, ranging because different sources count differently. THE FIVE NAMED REGIONAL MEMBER NETWORKS: AN EASTERN AFRICA FARMERS FEDERATION; A REGIONAL PLATFORM OF FARMERS' ORGANIZATIONS OF CENTRAL AFRICA; A NETWORK OF PEASANT AND PRODUCER ORGANISATIONS OF WEST AFRICA; A SOUTHERN AFRICAN CONFEDERATION OF AGRICULTURAL UNIONS; AND A MAGHREB AND NORTH AFRICAN UNION OF FARMERS. A MAGHREB AND NORTH AFRICAN UNION is worth naming separately: North African farmers are inside this structure, which is rare in a file where most continental networks stop at the Sahara. HOW IT WAS FOUNDED, AND BY WHOM, WHICH IS THE MODEL: THE FIVE SUB-REGIONAL NETWORKS HAD BEEN WORKING TOGETHER SINCE 2003 ON ISSUES OF CONTINENTAL INTEREST; THEY MET IN ADDIS ABABA IN MAY 2008 TO DISCUSS THE CONDITIONS FOR CREATING A PLATFORM THAT WOULD UNITE THEIR EFFORTS AND HARMONIZE THEIR CONCERNS; THOSE CONSULTATIONS PRODUCED A DECLARATION; AND THE CONSTITUTIVE ASSEMBLY WAS HELD UNDER AFRICAN UNION SPONSORSHIP IN LILONGWE FROM 27 TO 29 OCTOBER 2010, ON THE SIDELINES OF A CONFERENCE OF AFRICAN MINISTERS IN CHARGE OF AGRICULTURE. Seven years of working together before founding anything, and the constitutive assembly deliberately timed to sit beside the ministers' own conference. Both are tactics: existing collaboration first, and holding your founding meeting where the decision-makers are already gathered costs them nothing to attend. THE FIRST MANDATE GIVEN TO ITS OFFICE: TO SET UP THE EXECUTIVE SECRETARIAT, TO MAKE THE ORGANISATION FUNCTIONAL AND OPERATIONAL, AND TO NEGOTIATE THE PARTNERSHIPS NECESSARY FOR THE LIFE OF THE ORGANIZATION. ITS STATED FUNCTION: A FUNDAMENTAL COORDINATING FUNCTION BOTH WITH ITS MEMBER NETWORKS AND WITH CONTINENTAL AND INTERNATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS — ABLE TO FACILITATE DIALOGUE AND COOPERATION WITH CONTINENTAL AND INTERNATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, AND WITH FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL PARTNERS. WHAT ITS OWN CHIEF EXECUTIVE SAYS IT IS FOR: THE ONLY FARMERS PLATFORM ON A CONTINENTAL SCALE IN THE WORLD — IMPORTANT FOR ADVOCACY AND FOR MAKING THE VOICES OF FARMERS HEARD AT CONTINENTAL AND INTERNATIONAL LEVELS, AND FOR KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT, THE EXCHANGE OF EXPERIENCE AND THE PROMOTION OF THE ACHIEVEMENTS OF FARMERS AND THEIR ORGANIZATIONS. FROM THE BEGINNING, IT HAS TRIED TO UNITE THE FARMERS OF THE CONTINENT AROUND COMMON NEEDS, THEMES AND CHALLENGES THAT BRING THEM ALL TOGETHER. THE HEADQUARTERS AND CONTACTS: HEADQUARTERS IN KIGALI, RWANDA, WITH PUBLISHED MEDIA AND TECHNICAL CONTACT ROUTES. THE DEVELOPMENT BANK RELATIONSHIP AND ITS PAPER TRAIL, WHICH IS THE USABLE PART: A MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING SIGNED WITH AN AFRICAN DEVELOPMENT BANK IN OCTOBER 2023, WITH A DELEGATION LED BY ITS PRESIDENT VISITING THE BANK'S HEADQUARTERS ON 13 DECEMBER 2024 TO ADVANCE ITS IMPLEMENTATION — THE BANK'S DIRECTOR OF AGRICULTURE AND AGRO-INDUSTRY REAFFIRMING COMMITMENT AND HIGHLIGHTING INVESTMENTS THAT HAVE BENEFITED OVER 14 MILLION PRODUCERS. A signed memorandum with the bank that finances the projects arriving on your land, held by the body your farmers' union belongs to. When a bank-funded project harms a member community, that memorandum is a named relationship to invoke — and this file's Nigeria entry holds the same bank's complaint mechanism. THE SECOND SIGNED AGREEMENT AND WHAT IT COVERS: A COOPERATION AGREEMENT WITH A CONTINENTAL AGRICULTURE ALLIANCE TO STRENGTHEN THE CAPACITIES OF AFRICAN FARMERS' ORGANIZATIONS — SUPPORTING THEM TO CONDUCT POLITICAL ADVOCACY AROUND AREAS OF COMMON INTEREST AT CONTINENTAL, REGIONAL AND NATIONAL LEVELS, AND SUPPORTING PROGRAMS ENSURING WOMEN AND YOUNG FARMERS HAVE ACCESS TO RESOURCES THAT ALLOW THEM TO BE MORE PRODUCTIVE, UNHINDERED BY GENDER AND SOCIOCULTURAL NORMS, BARRIERS TO MARKET ENTRY AND OTHER INSTITUTIONAL OBSTACLES. POLITICAL ADVOCACY, named in a signed agreement as fundable. Compare the indigenous-led fund under Chad, which excludes political campaigns outright — knowing which doors treat advocacy as legitimate decides where the same work should be sent. AND THE GLOBAL SEAT: DELEGATIONS ATTEND A FARMERS' FORUM HELD IN ROME ALONGSIDE AN INTERNATIONAL AGRICULTURAL DEVELOPMENT FUND, WITH 80-PLUS FARMERS' LEADERS REPRESENTING MILLIONS OF SMALLHOLDERS AND RURAL PRODUCERS. A standing forum where farmer leaders sit with the fund that lends to their governments. The route there begins at a district meeting. WHO IT SUITS: African farmers' unions, cooperatives and national platforms — and community groups wanting their issue carried above national level through a structure that already exists. CAVEATS: MEMBERSHIP IS REGIONAL NETWORKS, NOT INDIVIDUAL GROUPS, AND IT COORDINATES AND ADVOCATES RATHER THAN FUNDING OR LITIGATING — join your national platform, which joins the regional network. For the West African member network from the inside, Mauritania's entry; for the farmer-governed development agencies, Eswatini's entry; for the same bank's complaint mechanism, Nigeria's entry.

trackers.name: ClientEarth — an environmental law charity that has no African offices and works through named strategic partners instead — with a published rule that it only brings cases it expects to win, and a forest-community result already on record
trackers.desc: IN AFRICA THEY WORK THROUGH PARTNERS. FIND THE PARTNER — adjacency declared first: A COMMUNITY-AND-ENVIRONMENT LAW NON-PROFIT WITH OFFICES IN CAPE TOWN, NAIROBI AND DAKAR IS ALREADY A NAMED ENTRY IN NINE AFRICA BUCKETS, AND AN ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDER LAW CENTRE IS A HOST UNDER SOUTH AFRICA; NEITHER IS RESTATED AND NEITHER HOST IS SHIPPED. THIS FILE'S DR CONGO ENTRY COVERS THE INTERNATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL LAW ORGANISATION THAT IS EXPLICITLY NOT A LAW FIRM. HOW IT OPERATES IN AFRICA, WHICH IS THE FIND AND ALSO THE LIMIT: ITS ENTITIES SIT ACROSS THREE REGIONS — NORTH AMERICA, ASIA AND THE PACIFIC, AND EUROPE — AND IT ADDITIONALLY OPERATES IN LATIN AMERICA AND AFRICA VIA STRATEGIC PARTNERS. There is no African office to write to. Approaching the London headquarters about a case in your district is the wrong door; the right one is the partner organisation in your country, which is a national body with its own staff and its own mandate. Establish who that is before spending effort — and note that the relationship runs the other way too: a national organisation that becomes a strategic partner gains access to a large litigation team. THE NAMED AFRICAN PARTNER, WHICH IS THE CONCRETE ADDRESS: A FOUNDATION FOR COMMUNITY INITIATIVES IN LIBERIA, ONE OF ITS PARTNER ORGANISATIONS, WHOSE EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR HAS SPENT A DECADE WORKING TO IMPROVE WOMEN'S LIVES IN RURAL AREAS BY ADVOCATING FOR THEIR RIGHTS TO LAND OWNERSHIP AND EQUAL PARTICIPATION IN FOREST GOVERNANCE. A named Liberian organisation led by a named woman working on rural land ownership and forest governance. For West African forest communities that is a contact in the region, and it is the kind of partner this charity chooses — which tells you what a candidate partner looks like. THE AFRICAN AIM AS IT STATES IT: WE SUPPORT FOREST COMMUNITIES TO HAVE A SAY IN THE LAWS AFFECTING THEIR LAND BECAUSE WE BELIEVE IT'S THE BEST LONG-TERM APPROACH TO PROTECTING FORESTS. A SAY IN THE LAWS, not only in the project. This file has recorded communities consulted about a concession after the forest code was already written; the work here is upstream of that, at the drafting stage. THE AFRICAN RESULT ON RECORD: IT HAS HELPED COMMUNITIES IN AFRICA'S LAST GREAT RAINFOREST CUT ILLEGAL LOGGING. THE CASE-SELECTION RULE, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND AND SAVES A WASTED APPROACH: WE ONLY BRING CASES WHEN WE STRONGLY BELIEVE WE HAVE A REASONABLE CHANCE OF WINNING, AND THE OUTCOME WILL HAVE POSITIVE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS ON A LARGE SCALE. Two conditions, both hard. A strong claim about one village will not qualify if the ruling changes nothing beyond it. Communities should read that honestly: this is a route for cases that set a precedent, and the file's local legal aid and paralegal entries are the route for cases that matter to one place. THE ACCESS-TO-JUSTICE WORK IT DESCRIBES: IT SUPPORTS THE PEOPLE AND COMMUNITIES MOST AFFECTED BY ENVIRONMENTAL DEGRADATION TO DEFEND THEIR RIGHTS, AND MAKES SURE PEOPLE, PROSECUTORS AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS CAN PARTICIPATE IN ENVIRONMENTAL DECISION-MAKING, AND GO TO COURT WHEN LAWS ARE BROKEN. PROSECUTORS named alongside communities. Where a state prosecutor could act on environmental crime but does not know how, training them is a route that removes the burden from the community entirely — and it is a thing to ask a partner organisation to pursue. THE INFORMATION RIGHT IT WORKS ON: IT MAKES SURE PEOPLE CAN FIND INFORMATION ABOUT THE ENVIRONMENT WHERE THEY LIVE AND WORK, SO THEY CAN TAKE THAT INFORMATION TO COURT WHEN THINGS GO WRONG — PROMOTING THE RIGHT TO INFORMATION AND ACCESS TO JUSTICE. The right to the document comes before the case. This file has recorded again and again that the impact assessment, the permit and the concession map are what a community cannot get; establishing the right to them is the work that makes everything else possible. THE FULL RANGE: INFORMING, IMPLEMENTING AND ENFORCING THE LAW; ADVISING DECISION-MAKERS ON POLICY; AND TRAINING LEGAL AND JUDICIAL PROFESSIONALS — STRENGTHENING THE ENTIRE SYSTEM, FROM HOW LAWS ARE WRITTEN TO HOW THEY ARE APPLIED, INTERPRETED AND ENFORCED BY COURTS AND REGULATORS. TRAINING JUDGES. A court that has never heard an environmental case decides badly through unfamiliarity as often as through bias, and judicial training is a slow intervention that changes every case afterwards. THE OTHER THINGS IT DOES FOR COMMUNITIES: IT DRAFTS LEGISLATION, TRAINS JUDGES, SUPPORTS COMMUNITIES FACING ENVIRONMENTAL HARM AND SHAPES GLOBAL POLICY FRAMEWORKS — WHETHER DEFENDING FORESTS FROM ILLEGAL LOGGING, PROTECTING RIVERS FROM POLLUTION OR CHALLENGING FOSSIL FUEL EXPANSION. ITS STATED THEORY, RECORDED BECAUSE IT SHAPES WHAT IT WILL TAKE ON: THE ENVIRONMENTAL CRISIS IS TOO BIG TO BE ADDRESSED BOTTOM-UP; TO DELIVER CHANGE AT THE RATE NEEDED THERE NEEDS TO BE SYSTEMIC CHANGE, AND TO DO THIS YOU NEED THE LAW — AND IT CHANGES THE SYSTEM FROM WITHIN, WORKING WITH, INSTEAD OF AGAINST, ITS MOST POWERFUL PLAYERS. Recorded plainly because it will not suit everyone: an organisation that says the crisis cannot be addressed bottom-up, and that works with powerful players rather than against them, is a different proposition from the confrontational routes elsewhere in this file. Where a community's whole case is that the powerful player is the problem, weigh that before approaching — and compare the organisation under Egypt, which states the opposite posture. THE TOOLS COMMITMENT: IT GIVES PEOPLE, PARTNERS AND ORGANISATIONS THE TOOLS THEY NEED TO DO THE SAME. AND THE SCALE AND THE CASES IT NAMES: FOUNDED IN 2007, ACTIVE IN OVER 60 COUNTRIES, WITH CASES INCLUDING TAKING A GOVERNMENT TO COURT FOR BREAKING AIR QUALITY LAWS, CONFRONTING A STATE FOR BREACHING THE HUMAN RIGHTS OF ISLANDERS WHOSE HOMES ARE BEING WASHED AWAY BY RISING SEAS, SUING A FOOD MULTINATIONAL OVER PLASTIC WASTE, AND A GREENWASHING CASE AGAINST AN AIRLINE THAT SET A PRECEDENT. ISLANDERS WHOSE HOMES ARE BEING WASHED AWAY, taken as a human rights case against a state. For African coastal and island communities losing land to the sea, that is the closest precedent in this entry — and it was won on rights, not on environmental law. WHO IT SUITS: African national environmental organisations that could become strategic partners, and forest communities whose case would change the law rather than one permit. CAVEATS: NO AFRICAN OFFICES, WORKS THROUGH PARTNERS, TAKES ONLY CASES IT EXPECTS TO WIN WITH LARGE-SCALE IMPACT, AND WORKS WITH POWERFUL ACTORS BY DESIGN — for a single community's dispute, use the national and regional legal entries. For the environmental law organisation that builds tools for others to use, DR Congo's entry; for the confrontational posture, Egypt's entry.

trackers.name: BirdLife South Africa — the organisation that got a biodiversity tax deduction written into national law — communities and communal landowners can deduct the value of land they protect, with the rules, the fact sheets and a named tax specialist published
trackers.desc: PROTECT IT FOR 99 YEARS AND DEDUCT THE VALUE OF THE LAND FROM YOUR TAX — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S SÃO TOMÉ ENTRY COVERS THE SERVITUDE TRUST, ITS ESWATINI ENTRY THE CAPITAL FUND, ITS SOUTH SUDAN ENTRY THE BODY THAT BUYS FARMS; ITS SOUTH AFRICA BUCKET CARRIES A BIODIVERSITY INSTITUTE HOST AND NAME. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. WHAT THE PROJECT PUT INTO LAW, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT INTRODUCED A NEW TAX INCENTIVE, SECTION 37D, INTO THE NATIONAL INCOME TAX ACT — ALLOWING LANDOWNERS AND COMMUNITIES DECLARING NATURE RESERVES AND NATIONAL PARKS TO DEDUCT THE FULL VALUE OF THE LAND DECLARED FROM THEIR TAXABLE INCOME. An NGO wrote a clause into the tax code. Most of this file records organisations arguing against laws; this one added one, and the result pays the people who protect land every year rather than once. When a community asks what it gains by declaring its land protected, this is a number on a tax return. THE COMMUNAL LAND POINT, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE INCENTIVE APPLIES TO PROTECTED AREAS DECLARED ON PRIVATE OR COMMUNALLY OWNED LAND, AND PROVIDES A REDUCTION IN TAX LIABILITY FOR COMMUNAL AND PRIVATE LANDOWNERS — WITH DECLARATIONS MADE BY PRIVATE LANDOWNERS, COMMUNAL PROPERTY ASSOCIATIONS OR OCCUPIERS OF COMMUNAL LAND. COMMUNAL PROPERTY ASSOCIATIONS AND OCCUPIERS OF COMMUNAL LAND named as eligible. Community-held land is inside the scheme, not an exception to it — which is rare in tax law and is the detail worth checking against your own country's code. THE MECHANICS, PUBLISHED: ELIGIBILITY APPLIES TO LAND DECLARED AS A NATURE RESERVE OR NATIONAL PARK UNDER TWO NAMED SECTIONS OF THE PROTECTED AREAS ACT; THE LAND MUST BE SUBJECT TO A TITLE DEED ENDORSEMENT FOR A MINIMUM OF 99 YEARS; THE DEDUCTION IS A 4% STRAIGHT-LINE DEDUCTION ON THE VALUE OF THE LAND DECLARED; IT BECOMES EFFECTIVE IN THE YEAR THE LAND IS DECLARED AND THE ENDORSEMENT IS EFFECTED; AND IT CAN BE SET OFF AGAINST TAXABLE INCOME OR USED TO INCREASE AN ASSESSED LOSS. Ninety-nine years, endorsed on the title deed. Read that beside the servitude filed under São Tomé: both put the protection into the deeds registry, but this one comes with an annual payment attached. 4% straight-line means the full value is recovered over 25 years, which is a serious sum against a farm. THE PENALTY IF IT IS UNDONE: IF THE PROTECTED AREA STATUS IS TERMINATED UNDER THE PROTECTED AREAS ACT, THE TAXPAYER MAY BE LIABLE FOR CERTAIN TAX PENALTIES. A financial cost to reversing the protection, which is the teeth. A future owner who wants to develop the land inherits a tax bill for doing so. WHY THIS IS UNUSUAL AT ALL: GENERALLY, THE VALUE OF LAND IS NOT DEDUCTIBLE FOR TAX PURPOSES — THIS DEDUCTION OFFERS A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO DEDUCT THE VALUE OF LAND. THE PROOF IT WORKS: TESTED AT PILOT SITES ACROSS THE COUNTRY, RESULTING IN THE SUCCESSFUL INCLUSION OF THIS TAX BREAK IN A TAX RETURN IN 2016 — AND ONE NAMED PRIVATE RESERVE RECEIVED THE DEDUCTION, WITH THE TANGIBLE FINANCIAL BENEFIT BOLSTERING ITS CASH FLOW SO THAT ADDITIONAL RESOURCES COULD BE MOBILISED. Claimed, accepted, and on record. That precedent is what a landowner's accountant will want to see before advising them to sign. THE FREE MATERIAL AND THE NAMED CONTACT: THE PROJECT PROVIDES HIGH-LEVEL SUMMARIES AND TECHNICAL TAX OVERVIEWS, WITH UPDATED FACT SHEETS PUBLISHED FOR IMPLEMENTERS, LANDOWNERS AND OTHER VESTED STAKEHOLDERS — WITH A NAMED PROJECT MANAGER AND TAX SPECIALIST GIVEN AS THE CONTACT. A named tax specialist inside a conservation organisation, reachable, with the technical sheets free. That combination does not exist anywhere else in this file, and it is exactly what a community negotiating with a landowner cannot otherwise obtain. THE STATED LIMIT ON THAT MATERIAL: THESE TAX RESOURCES DO NOT CONSTITUTE TAX ADVICE AND MAY NOT BE USED AS SUCH. Recorded plainly — the fact sheets prepare the conversation with an accountant, they do not replace it. THE SCALE OF THE OPPORTUNITY: APPROXIMATELY 75% OF THE COUNTRY IS HELD IN PRIVATE OWNERSHIP; LANDOWNERS BEAR THE RESPONSIBILITY OF MANAGING PROTECTED AREAS AND FACE FINANCIAL COMMITMENTS AS A RESULT — AND THE COST TO THE STATE OF BIODIVERSITY STEWARDSHIP IS A FRACTION OF THE COST OF ACQUIRING AND MANAGING STATE-OWNED PROTECTED AREAS. CHEAPER THAN BUYING IT is the argument that persuades a treasury. Where a government says it cannot afford to protect an area, the counter is that a stewardship declaration costs it a fraction of an acquisition — and this is the sourced version of that claim. HOW THE DECLARATION HAPPENS: THROUGH A GOVERNMENT-LED REGIME OF BILATERAL AGREEMENTS WITH PRIVATE AND COMMUNAL LANDOWNERS TO FORMALLY CONSERVE AND MAINTAIN A PARTICULAR AREA OF LAND — ESTABLISHED THROUGH A NATIONAL BIODIVERSITY STEWARDSHIP INITIATIVE, WHOSE KEY PRINCIPLES INCLUDE FOCUSING ON PRIORITY AREAS, VOLUNTARY COMMITMENT FROM LANDOWNERS, AND WORKING IN PARTNERSHIPS. VOLUNTARY COMMITMENT is the safeguard to check: a community entering such an agreement is contracting with the state, and the terms of that agreement decide whether it keeps its use of the land. THE NATIONAL GUIDELINE THAT EXISTS FOR IT: A BIODIVERSITY STEWARDSHIP GUIDELINE DETAILING EVERY ASPECT OF SECURING HIGH BIODIVERSITY LAND UNDER LONG TERM PROTECTION AND MANAGEMENT, WITH EXPERT INPUT FROM LEADING PRACTITIONERS, PRACTICAL TOOLKITS PER CHAPTER, AND AN EXAMPLE DECLARATION DIAGRAM DEFINING A GEOGRAPHIC AREA OVER A CADASTRE. Toolkits per chapter and a worked declaration diagram over a cadastre. That is the document to hand a lawyer or a provincial official rather than describing what you want. AND THE LESSON THE PROJECT PUBLISHES ABOUT ITS OWN METHOD: ATTEMPTING TO INTRODUCE THE COUNTRY'S FIRST BIODIVERSITY TAX INCENTIVE IN ISOLATION WOULD HAVE BEEN AN ERROR — IT HAD TO BE INTRODUCED INTO THE CONTEXT OF AN EXISTING COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE OF IMPLEMENTERS RANGING FROM NATIONAL AND PROVINCIAL GOVERNMENT TO NGOs AND SPECIALISTS. The tax change succeeded because it was carried by people already running the stewardship programme. Anyone attempting the same in another country should find that existing community of practice first rather than drafting alone. WHO IT SUITS: African communities, communal property associations and sympathetic landowners weighing formal protection — and organisations elsewhere seeking a working model for a biodiversity tax incentive. CAVEATS: THE INCENTIVE IS SOUTH AFRICAN LAW AND DEPENDS ON A DECLARED PROTECTED AREA AND A 99-YEAR TITLE DEED ENDORSEMENT, WHICH IS A PERMANENT COMMITMENT; THE PUBLISHED MATERIAL IS EXPRESSLY NOT TAX ADVICE — take it to an accountant. For binding land through a servitude instead, São Tomé's entry; for the fund that has bought land, Eswatini's entry.

trackers.name: Nkuzi Development Association — the association whose own national survey found 4.18 million people displaced from farms in twenty years with only 1% involving any legal process — and which runs the paralegal service, claim-form help and legal facility that came out of it
trackers.desc: 1.7 MILLION EVICTED, AND ONLY 1% WENT THROUGH A COURT — method and adjacency declared first: THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THE SHIPPED HOST AND FIVE SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL ABSENT. THIS FILE'S SOUTH AFRICA BUCKET CARRIES A RURAL ADVANCEMENT ASSOCIATION WORKING WITH FARM DWELLERS ON A DIFFERENT HOST, ITS ESWATINI ENTRY THE FARM WOMEN'S NGO AND THE TENURE GRANT, ITS RWANDA ENTRY THE 48-COMMUNITY RESTITUTION FEDERATION. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE SURVEY FIGURES, WHICH IS THE FIND: BETWEEN 1984 AND 2004, ABOUT 4.18 MILLION PEOPLE HAD BEEN DISPLACED FROM FARMS, AND ABOUT 1.7 MILLION OF THESE HAD BEEN EVICTED — AND ONLY 1% OF THESE DISPLACEMENTS HAD INVOLVED A LEGAL PROCESS. ONE PER CENT. This file has recorded eviction after eviction described as lawful; here is the measured proportion that ever saw a court, produced by a community organisation's own national survey and presented to a parliamentary committee. Ninety-nine times in a hundred there was no order, which means the first question a farm dweller should ask — where are the papers — is almost always the winning one. WHEN THE EVICTIONS HAPPEN, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: MOST OCCURRED DURING TIMES OF POLITICAL UNCERTAINTY AND TRADE LIBERALISATION, AND TIMES OF DROUGHT — WITH CHILDREN AND WOMEN THE MOST VULNERABLE; A LACK OF INFORMATION AND ACCESS TO LEGAL HELP WAS A GREAT PROBLEM. Evictions cluster around elections, trade shocks and drought. A community can therefore anticipate rather than react: the season to have paralegals trained and contacts in place is the season before the water fails or the political calendar turns. THE PRACTICE THE SURVEY EXPOSED: ONCE IT BECAME CLEAR THAT LAWS RESTRICTING MOVEMENT WOULD BE PHASED OUT, SOME LANDOWNERS STARTED THE PRACTICE OF SHACK FARMING, AND WERE GUILTY OF INFRINGING UPON THE RIGHTS OF WORKERS — WITH SOME WORKERS RECLASSIFIED AS RETRENCHED RATHER THAN EVICTED. RETRENCHED RATHER THAN EVICTED is the relabelling to watch for: end the job and the housing claim is presented as ending with it. Two separate rights, deliberately collapsed into one. WHAT IT DOES ON A CLAIM: ESTABLISHED IN 1997 TO ASSIST COMMUNITIES TO LODGE LAND CLAIMS AFTER A RESTITUTION ACT, WHEN THE CLAIMS COMMISSION'S OFFICES WERE ONLY IN THE CAPITAL — ASSISTING IN THE COMPLETION OF CLAIMS FORMS, FACILITATION OF LAND CLAIMS COMMITTEES, AND DOCUMENTATION OF SUPPORTING EVIDENCE, SO CLAIMANT COMMUNITIES WOULD NOT MISS THE CUT-OFF DATE. The organisation exists because the state put its only claims office in the capital and set a deadline. Filling in forms and gathering evidence is unglamorous work, and it is the difference between a claim lodged and a claim lost to a date — the same barrier this file records under every registration requirement. THE LEGAL FACILITY IT INITIATED: A LAND RIGHTS MANAGEMENT FACILITY ESTABLISHED TO PROVIDE SPECIALISED LEGAL SKILLS AND TO ASSIST LAND DWELLERS AND EVICTEES WITH LEGAL ADVICE — AN INITIATIVE OF THIS ASSOCIATION, WHICH SOUGHT LEGAL ASSISTANCE FOR BENEFICIARIES OF LAND REFORM AFTER THE COURTS RULED THAT INDIGENT FARM DWELLERS ARE ENTITLED TO IT. A court ruled that poor farm dwellers are ENTITLED to legal assistance, and a community organisation then built the facility to deliver it. That is the sequence worth copying: win the entitlement, then construct the thing that supplies it, rather than waiting for the state to. ITS FOUR PROGRAMMES: LAND REFORM IMPLEMENTATION, FARM DWELLER, RESEARCH AND POLICY, AND LEGAL SERVICES — WITH THE FIRST CONTAINING COMMUNITY ORGANIZING AND TRAINING AND SUSTAINABLE LIVELIHOODS SUPPORT. THE FOURTH OBJECTIVE, STATED PLAINLY: FOR QUALITY LEGAL AND PARALEGAL SUPPORT TO BE AVAILABLE TO ENABLE THE POOR AND LANDLESS PEOPLE TO EXERCISE THEIR LAND RIGHTS AND OTHER HUMAN RIGHTS. THE DEPENDENCY IT DOCUMENTS: WHERE FARM DWELLERS RECEIVE SERVICES SUCH AS HOUSING, ELECTRICITY AND SCHOOLING, IT IS OFTEN AT THE MERCY OF LANDOWNERS — IF LANDOWNERS DO NOT WANT THEM TO HAVE A MOBILE CLINIC OR SCHOOLS, THEY WILL NOT GET THEM, WHICH EXPLAINS WHY MOST OF THE CHILDREN OR PEOPLE ON FARMS ARE NOT EVEN DOCUMENTED AND DO NOT EVEN GET SOCIAL GRANTS. Undocumented people cannot claim a grant, register a birth, or prove they lived somewhere for thirty years. The landowner's veto over a clinic becomes, a generation later, the reason a family cannot prove its own occupation — which is why getting documents is land work. THE SCHOOL CLOSURE FINDING: NATIONALLY, MOST OF THE SCHOOLS EARMARKED FOR CLOSURE ARE MOSTLY FARM SCHOOLS, WHICH WILL OBVIOUSLY AFFECT FARM DWELLER CHILDREN'S RIGHT TO EDUCATION. Closing the school is a quieter way of clearing a farm than any eviction notice. ITS ASSESSMENT OF THE OFFICIAL COMMITTEES: DESPITE BEING SIDE-LINED, IT AND OTHER ORGANISATIONS WERE MOBILISING LOCAL COMMUNITIES TO ATTEND THE MEETINGS AND PARTICIPATE — BUT DISTRICT LAND REFORM COMMITTEES DO NOT SEEM TO HAVE POLICIES OR STRATEGIES AIMED AT THE BETTERMENT OF PEOPLE IN RURAL AREAS, AND ONE CANNOT HELP BUT CONCLUDE THAT THE COMMITTEES ARE A SCHEME AIMED AT JUSTIFYING THE EXPENDITURE OF FUNDS BY THE DEPARTMENT. An honest verdict on a participation structure, from an organisation that keeps sending people to it anyway. Both halves are the lesson: attend, and do not mistake attendance for influence. ITS POSITION ON A MORATORIUM: A MORATORIUM ON EVICTIONS, WITHOUT PUTTING MEASURES IN PLACE THAT ENSURE IT IS PROPERLY IMPLEMENTED AND MONITORED, WOULD NOT ACHIEVE WHAT IS INTENDED. A land organisation arguing against the headline demand unless monitoring comes with it. Worth remembering when a government offers a freeze instead of a remedy. AND WHAT IT SAYS IT IS AIMING AT, PLUS HOW IT LEARNS: DISADVANTAGED WOMEN AND MEN ORGANISED AND EMPOWERED TO ASSERT THEIR RIGHTS, BASED ON ACCESS TO SUFFICIENT LAND, SECURE TENURE, BASIC SERVICES AND INTEGRATED LOCAL ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT — WITH LANDLESS PEOPLE EMPOWERED TO DRIVE A LAND REFORM PROCESS WHICH SHIFTS POWER RELATIONS; ITS DIRECTOR, DEPUTY DIRECTOR, FARM DWELLER PROGRAMME MANAGER AND A VOLUNTEER RESEARCHER ATTENDED A WEEK-LONG WORKSHOP ON PARTICIPATORY ACTION RESEARCH, AND IT WAS ASKED TO JOIN A TASK TEAM DRAFTING AN ALTERNATIVE FARM DWELLER POLICY. The senior staff went on a research training course together, and the survey above is what came of it. A community organisation that can produce its own national numbers gets asked to help draft the policy. WHO IT SUITS: farm dwellers and landless communities lodging restitution claims or facing eviction — and organisations anywhere wanting the survey-then-parliament model, or the argument that most evictions never see a court. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY, AND THE HEADLINE SURVEY COVERS 1984–2004, SO THE FIGURES ARE HISTORICAL EVEN THOUGH THE PATTERN PERSISTS; IT ORGANISES, RESEARCHES AND ARRANGES PARALEGAL AND LEGAL SUPPORT RATHER THAN LITIGATING AS A LAW CENTRE. For the statutory grant that buys land for farm dwellers, Eswatini's entry; for the federation that litigated restitution delays, Rwanda's entry.

trackers.name: Somalia — Registrar of Companies (Ministry of Commerce & Industry)
trackers.desc: National corporate registry; the Registrar of Companies at the Ministry of Commerce & Industry registers local & foreign-owned companies & business licences (renewable annually), Somalia. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Somalia — Ministry of Finance
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Federal Ministry of Finance develops economic policy, prepares & executes the federal budget (presented to Parliament each October) and publishes fiscal & revenue reports, Somalia. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Somalia.

trackers.name: Somalia — Office of the Auditor General (OAG)
trackers.desc: National public-finance watchdog; the federal Supreme Audit Institution (strengthened by the 2023 Federal Audit Law) conducts financial, compliance & performance audits of government institutions and reports to Parliament, Somalia.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: East African Court of Justice — it stopped a road across the Serengeti
trackers.desc: THIS COURT STOPPED A GOVERNMENT FROM BUILDING A ROAD.
