Article 4 objectives include enforcing wildlife laws within, between and among States Parties and facilitating community-based natural resources management. CHECK YOUR STATE HAS RATIFIED — the Protocol is legally binding only for countries that have signed and ratified it, and this entry does not assert that your state has. ON TFCAs: they encompass protected areas as well as multiple resource use areas, so they are not exclusion zones; a TFCA practitioners network founded September 2013 has membership open to all stakeholder groups. And SADC's own 2023–2033 TFCA programme names the marginalisation of communities living in and around protected areas as a problem it exists to address — quotable against the body that wrote it.

trackers.name: Yonge Nawe — the Eswatini environmental justice group that sued a minister to the highest court and won civil society a seat on the environment regulator
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an environmental action group founded in 1987, the Friends of the Earth member in Eswatini, working on environmental justice and getting local voices into environmental decisions. THE PRECEDENT IT SET IS THE REASON TO KNOW IT EXISTS: when the environment law was amended in 2002 it required a representative of an environmental NGO to sit on the management board of the national environment authority. The responsible minister ignored that provision and excluded NGOs. Yonge Nawe, then led by the environmental attorney Thuli Brilliance Makama, pressed the point and, when the minister refused to comply, took the minister to the country's highest court rather than let the disobedience become the precedent for every future minister — work for which Makama received the Goldman Environmental Prize in 2010. WHAT THAT MEANS FOR YOU: in Eswatini a civil society seat on the regulator exists in law and had to be litigated into existence, so ask who currently occupies the NGO seat on the authority's board, and take your project to that person. The authority itself has the statutory power to halt developments that have not been properly assessed for environmental impact. Yonge Nawe also works on industrial pollution of rivers and on land rehabilitation projects in communities, and shares a national radio slot with the environment authority and the national trust commission. WHO IT SUITS: Swazi communities facing pollution, land degradation or a development approved without proper assessment. CAVEATS: LEADERSHIP AND CONTACT DETAILS HAVE CHANGED OVER TIME — Makama has long since moved to international work, published email addresses in directories are old, and the website was not verified as live; confirm before relying on it. Eswatini is an absolute monarchy with narrow civic space, and most rural land is held under the King in trust, which shapes what any organisation there can do.

trackers.name: Swaziland Justice Forum — documents Eswatini's evictions, and the communities it works with took their case to the African Commission
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Swazi civil society organisation that documents forced evictions and names those responsible — it alleged that the royal sugar corporation was complicit in the illegal eviction of 33 farmers and their dependents from Vuvulane, following plans to take over the land, vest it in the royal wealth fund and lease it on to the corporation, and argues that the sugar industry has benefited the King and multinationals while displacing Swazi people from plantation land. WHY DOCUMENTATION IS THE ONLY FOUNDATION HERE: most land is Swazi Nation Land held in trust by the King and allocated through chiefs, with no formal legal security of tenure and no uniform official written record of allocations — so a household has nothing to produce when the bulldozers arrive. Recorded evictions include 61 people, more than 30 of them children, made homeless when armed police and bulldozers demolished homes at Embetseni in 2018; over 100 people from at least 20 homesteads cleared at Nokwane, where a 159-hectare science and technology park now stands; and about 106 people served notice by the national provident fund at Madonsa. THE ROUTE THAT WAS ACTUALLY USED WHEN DOMESTIC REMEDIES CLOSED: Swazi participants submitted a report documenting forced evictions to the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights and engaged it at its 63rd Ordinary Session in Banjul in October 2018 — and then invited an ACHPR Commissioner to attend their own community meeting in Manzini in 2019. Bringing a regional Commissioner into the affected village is a move worth copying. The legal standard they invoke is that forced evictions may happen only as a last resort, under a court order, once all feasible alternatives are exhausted and procedural protections are in place. WHO IT SUITS: Swazi households and communities facing eviction from Swazi Nation Land, title-deed farms or plantation land. CAVEATS: NO VERIFIED WEBSITE FOR SJF WAS FOUND, so this entry carries no URL rather than pointing at a third party — approach through Swazi civil society networks or Eswatini's Yonge Nawe entry. For pro bono counsel before the African Commission, the IHRDA entry filed under The Gambia is the counsel; Eswatini is an absolute monarchy and the risks of publicity should be weighed.

trackers.name: Eswatini Legal Aid — opened 2023 at RHUS Office, Mbabane; advice, referrals and mediation now, representation NOT yet
trackers.desc: WHAT EXISTS NOW: Eswatini Legal Aid, the country's FIRST legal aid office, set up following the National Legal Aid Policy adopted by Cabinet in September 2022 and established at the RHUS Office in Mbabane, with technical support from the UN development programme to the justice ministry. THE ONE THING TO KNOW BEFORE YOU GO, STATED BY THE MINISTER HERSELF: services are being rolled out across four thematic areas — legal information and awareness; advice and referrals; mediation; and legal assistance including REPRESENTATION — but because legal aid is at the inception stage, services are provided INCREMENTALLY STARTING WITH THE FIRST THREE, WHICH DO NOT INCLUDE LEGAL REPRESENTATION. So this office will inform you, advise you, refer you and mediate for you; it will not yet stand up in court for you. Ask whether representation has since been added before relying on it for a hearing. THE EVIDENCE BEHIND IT, which is also the argument for using it: a 2022 legal aid needs survey found that 58 per cent of emaSwati cannot afford the services of a lawyer, and 90 per cent said they would use legal support if it were made accessible. The ministry identifies the barriers precisely — lack of money, inadequate awareness of how to access services, insufficient command of legal language, and LONG DISTANCES to service providers. The Legal Aid Bill process began in 2012 and stalled; the policy route was taken instead, and the country has faced a case backlog in the absence of legal aid except where capital punishment was in play. A FREE SOURCE OF THE LAW ITSELF: EswatiniLII, operated by the Judiciary, publishes the country's judgments and legislation free online — which matters where government printers charge per page. WHO IT SUITS: emaSwati who need to understand a land, eviction or inheritance problem, get a referral, or attempt mediation. CAVEATS: NO VERIFIED STANDALONE SITE — this entry points at the UN account of the launch; NO COURT REPRESENTATION at inception; and Eswatini is an absolute monarchy where most land is held by the King in trust, so a state office will not challenge an allocation. For forced evictions and the African Commission route, Eswatini's Swaziland Justice Forum entry; for environmental precedent, Yonge Nawe.

trackers.name: Eswatini Environment Fund — grants up to E300,000, open to COMMUNITY GROUPS AND INDIVIDUALS, with 80% required to go to direct environmental action
trackers.desc: WHERE TO APPLY FOR MONEY: the Eswatini Environment Fund (EEF), established under the ENVIRONMENT MANAGEMENT ACT 2002, administered by the Eswatini Environment Authority and approved by a Board of Trustees on the recommendation of a technical proposal selection committee, through an OPEN NATIONAL CALL FOR PROPOSALS covering all four administrative regions. THE TERMS, WHICH ARE UNUSUALLY OPEN: grants of UP TO E300,000; eligibility runs to community groups, non-governmental organisations, environmental organisations, INDIVIDUALS, and educational or research institutions based in Eswatini; and AT LEAST 80% OF THE FUNDING MUST GO TO DIRECT ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIONS. An 80% floor on direct action is the exact protection missing from the Gabonese and Congolese forest funds recorded in this file, where running costs were charged against the community's share — if your country's fund has no such rule, this is the clause to ask for. Priority areas: climate change adaptation, sustainable water and land management, waste management, and biodiversity conservation, with weight given to community participation and long-term impact. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY FUNDED, AND THE FAILURE THE AUTHORITY PUBLISHES ITSELF: the Luve wetland and donga rehabilitation project, run through a local NGO under a signed contract, with a corporate partner completing the fencing and adding E30,000; a waste project at Lobamba Inkhundla; and the first-ever grant in 2009 to the Langa project, where the earth dam was successfully protected but the spring later dried up. And the Sivule wetland protection project — 12 ha spanning the boundaries of THREE CHIEFDOMS — could not start despite several meetings, because of conflicts between the chiefdoms. Money does not resolve a boundary dispute between traditional authorities; settle who speaks for the land before you apply, or the grant will sit unspent. WHO IT SUITS: Eswatini community groups, individuals and NGOs with a wetland, land-degradation, water or biodiversity project. CAVEATS: A STATE-ADMINISTERED FUND under the environment authority — it funds environmental action, NOT litigation against a development or land purchase; calls are periodic with fixed deadlines, so confirm the current cycle. For litigation that stopped a mine, Eswatini's Yonge Nawe entry; for forced evictions and the African Commission route, the Swaziland Justice Forum; for advice and mediation, Eswatini Legal Aid.

trackers.name: Khonta on Swazi Nation Land and the Lubombo Conservancy — heritable family tenure through the chiefdom, and a community nature reserve sitting inside a 60,000 ha conservancy
trackers.desc: WHAT YOU HOLD ON SWAZI NATION LAND: access runs through KHONTA — individuals seeking Swazi Nation Land must obtain the approval of the structures associated with the LOCAL CHIEFTAINCY, and obtain USE RIGHTS to build on and cultivate; in exchange the household is expected to KUHLEHLA, render services to the chief's house and in his fields. THE TWO FACTS THAT MATTER MOST, AND THE SECOND IS BETTER NEWS THAN MOST OF THIS FILE: the land MAY PASS TO DESCENDANTS under Swazi customary law; and although chiefs retain powers to evict or re-allocate on evidence of crime or witchcraft, customary landholding rights and family tenure are described as STRONG AND SECURE, and IT IS RARE THAT A FAMILY IS EVICTED from a chiefdom. Heritable and rarely disturbed is a real tenure position — the risk in Eswatini is not usually the chief removing your family, it is a project arriving with authority above the chiefdom. WHAT THE CONTEST IS ACTUALLY ABOUT: research records the tension between chiefs and councils as NOT ONLY over allocation powers but over the REVENUE STREAMS attached — chiefs seeking KHONTA FEES, councils seeking plot and rates payments. Know which body is charging you for what; a demand for money is often a claim of jurisdiction in disguise. THE COLLECTIVE INSTRUMENT: the LUBOMBO CONSERVANCY joins FIVE areas totalling about 60,000 HECTARES — and it deliberately mixes tenure, comprising STATUTORILY PROCLAIMED PROTECTED AREAS, PRIVATE PROPERTY AND SWAZI NATION LAND together, including the SHEWULA COMMUNITY NATURE RESERVE alongside a royal national park, a private game reserve, a national trust reserve and a ranch. A conservancy that admits community land, private land and state reserves as equal members is the model to ask for: it lets a chiefdom sit at the same table as a private reserve without surrendering its land. Note also, as the neighbouring benchmark, that Eswatini's private reserves are PROCLAIMED AND GAZETTED IN LAW FOR PERPETUITY, carrying the highest levels of legal protection available, with land use PREDETERMINED BY LAW so it may not be used for anything but nature conservation. That perpetual gazettement is what a community should ask for over its own reserve — the instrument exists in Eswatini law and has been used for privately owned land. WHO IT SUITS: Swazi households on Nation Land, and chiefdoms considering a community reserve or conservancy membership. CAVEATS: USE RIGHTS UNDER A CHIEFDOM, NOT TITLE, in an absolute monarchy where most land is held by the King in trust; conservancy membership does not itself change tenure. For forced evictions and the African Commission route, Eswatini's Swaziland Justice Forum entry; for project grants up to E300,000, the Environment Fund entry; for litigation that stopped a mine, Yonge Nawe.

trackers.name: Eswatini National Trust Commission — the body that PROCLAIMS sites, with further sites already under investigation for proclamation, plus the authority that can halt an unscrutinised development
trackers.desc: THE BODY THAT CAN PROCLAIM YOUR SITE: the ESWATINI NATIONAL TRUST COMMISSION (ENTC, sntc.org.sz) is responsible for conservation of the Kingdom's natural AND CULTURAL heritage under the NATIONAL TRUST COMMISSION ACT NO. 9 OF 1972, amended by the King's Order in Council of 1973, and CARRIES OUT ITS MANDATE THROUGH PROCLAMATION AND MANAGEMENT of national parks and reserves, museums and MONUMENTS. It is an INDEPENDENT STATUTORY BODY and government parastatal under the tourism and environment ministry, with a BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS APPOINTED BY THE MINISTER, a Chief Executive and FOUR DIRECTORS — including one for NATURE CONSERVATION and one for CULTURAL HERITAGE; it is reachable on (+268) 2416 1489 / 1179, info@sntc.org.sz. THE OPENING, STATED IN ITS OWN RECORD: THREE SITES HAVE BEEN PROCLAIMED NATIONAL MONUMENTS AND A NUMBER OF FURTHER SITES ARE BEING INVESTIGATED WITH A VIEW TO FUTURE PROCLAMATION. Proclamation is an open, live process with sites currently under investigation — so a Swazi community with a grave site, a ruin, a sacred place or a rare habitat has a named body to petition, and CULTURAL heritage counts as much as natural. Write to the Director of Cultural Heritage as well as the Director of Nature Conservation; a cultural claim can protect ground that a biodiversity claim cannot. WHAT IT ALREADY HOLDS AND RUNS, which is what a community would be joining: MALOLOTJA NATURE RESERVE with the adjacent HAWANE DAM RESERVE, MLAWULA NATURE RESERVE with Magadzavane Lodge, MANTENGA NATURE RESERVE AND SWAZI CULTURAL VILLAGE, KING SOBHUZA II PARK and the NATIONAL MUSEUM, alongside environmental education and COMMUNITY OUTREACH PROGRAMMES; its funding is AN ANNUAL GOVERNMENT SUBVENTION AUGMENTED BY REVENUE FROM ITS OWN TOURISM AND HOSPITALITY OPERATIONS, and it has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Forestry Department. A conservation body that earns part of its own income is one that can act without waiting for a budget line. THE ENFORCER TO NAME ALONGSIDE IT: the ESWATINI ENVIRONMENT AUTHORITY (EEA), created by the Environment Act 1992 and made a corporate body by the ENVIRONMENT MANAGEMENT ACT 2002 — WHICH GIVES IT THE POWER TO HALT DEVELOPMENTS THAT HAVE NOT BEEN ADEQUATELY SCRUTINISED FOR THEIR ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT. Halting an unscrutinised development is a power somebody must be asked to use. Put the request in writing to the Authority, and copy the Commission if the site has heritage value. WHO IT SUITS: Swazi communities with a heritage, burial, sacred or high-biodiversity site, and anyone facing an unassessed development. CAVEATS: STATE AND PARASTATAL BODIES under a ministry — the independent route is separate. For the group that sued a minister, Eswatini's Yonge Nawe entry; for grants up to E300,000 open to communities, the Environment Fund entry; for heritable khonta tenure and the Lubombo Conservancy, the Swazi Nation Land entry; for advice since 2023, Eswatini Legal Aid.

trackers.name: CANGO and the briefcase-NGO test — Eswatini's NGO umbrella with named officers, the registration confusion it documents, and HUMARAS with a Mbabane address
trackers.desc: THE BRIEFCASE-NGO TEST, WHICH IS THE MOST USEFUL THING ANY COMMUNITY IN THIS FILE CAN CARRY: the COORDINATING ASSEMBLY OF NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS (CANGO) IS ESWATINI'S NGO UMBRELLA, WITH A NAMED DIRECTOR, A NAMED BOARD CHAIRPERSON AND A NAMED PROGRAMME OFFICER on the public record, AND IT HOLDS AN ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING THAT ITS MEMBER NGOs ATTEND. ITS DIRECTOR COINED THE TEST: THE ABSENCE OF A NATIONAL GOVERNING POLICY LEFT THE DOOR OPEN FOR WHAT WE CALL BRIEFCASE NGOs — THESE ARE NGOs IN NAME ONLY, WITH NO FIXED ADDRESSES, NO BOARDS AND NO STAFFS; THEY EXIST ONLY TO SQUEEZE MONEY OUT OF DONORS. Fixed address, a board, staff. Three questions, asked of anyone who offers to help your community or to raise money on its behalf. If the answer to any of them is no, you are dealing with what Eswatini's own NGO umbrella named a briefcase NGO — and that test works in every country in this file. WHAT CANGO WON, AFTER DECADES: THE GOVERNMENT PASSED GUIDELINES ON THE CREATION, REGISTRATION AND RUNNING OF NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS — with CANGO stating that IT VIEWS THIS STEP AS AN INDICATION THAT GOVERNMENT REGARDS NGOs AS EQUAL PARTNERS IN DEVELOPMENT, and its board chairperson saying the policy WILL ENSURE THAT THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN GOVERNMENT AND NGOs IS FORMALISED. CANGO had been working for a national NGO policy SINCE THE 1980s. Forty years of one umbrella body pushing for a registration policy, and it landed. When you are told a national framework is impossible, that is the counter-example — and note the argument that worked was formalising the relationship, not demanding independence. THE REGISTRATION PROBLEM IT DOCUMENTED, WHICH TELLS YOU WHAT TO ASK: TO BE AN NGO IN ESWATINI YOU MUST LEGALLY REGISTER, BUT SOME GROUPS ARE REGISTERING AS ASSOCIATIONS, SOME AS NONPROFIT ORGANISATIONS, AND SOME AS INDIVIDUALS — with CANGO warning that there had to be overall control SO NGOs CANNOT BE CLOSED AT THE WHIM OF THE HOME AFFAIRS MINISTER OF THE DAY. Ask under which form your association is registered, not merely whether it is. An organisation registered as an individual dies with that individual, and one registered without a governing framework can be closed by a minister. Get the form right at the start. CANGO also records the practical obstacle inside parliament: PARLIAMENTARIANS TOLD US PLAINLY THAT THEIR HANDS ARE TIED, AS THEY ARE ONLY MANDATED TO DISCUSS ISSUES THAT HAVE REACHED POLICY LEVEL, and that a new NGO Act developed with UN technical assistance WAS THROWN OUT BY THE ATTORNEY-GENERAL'S OFFICE — WE WERE TOLD IT WAS NOT OUR DUTY TO DEVELOP POLICIES. An MP who cannot act until something reaches policy level is not refusing you — they are telling you where the blockage is. Aim at the stage that unlocks them. ALSO NAMED, WITH CONTACTS: the SWAZILAND ASSOCIATION OF HUMAN RIGHTS (HUMARAS), P.O. Box 1546, MBABANE, telephone (268) 404 5610, with a published email, holding standing before the African human rights commission; and the TRADE UNION CONGRESS OF ESWATINI (TUCOSWA), the national trade union centre formed in 2012 from a federation founded in the 1970s that had around 40,000 members, based at Manzini. A national union congress is a membership body with legal standing and tens of thousands of members. In a small country where this file records civic space as constrained, a union that already has the right to meet is a room your question can be raised in. WHO IT SUITS: Eswatini community groups registering or checking a partner, and anyone needing a rights body or an organised membership. CAVEATS: SOME OF THIS RECORD IS HISTORICAL — confirm the current registration framework before you file. For the body that PROCLAIMS sites and holds three named reserves, Eswatini's ENTC entry, which also carries the authority's power to halt unscrutinised developments.

trackers.name: Team grants of US$15,000 rising to US$50,000 with no minimum education level required — three nationals of the project country, five years' experience or less, plus leadership training and an alumni network
trackers.desc: NO MINIMUM EDUCATION LEVEL REQUIRED — THAT PHRASE IS PUBLISHED IN THEIR OWN ELIGIBILITY, AND IT IS THE FIND. TEAMS FROM UNDERREPRESENTED GROUPS ARE STRONGLY ENCOURAGED TO APPLY. This file has just recorded two conservation funders that in practice require a postgraduate degree or audited accounts. Here neither applies. A ranger, a fisher, a herder or a village committee member with five years of work behind them is eligible on the same terms as a graduate — and almost no other conservation money in this file can be reached without a diploma or an institution. THE TEAM RULE: TEAMS MUST HAVE AT LEAST THREE MEMBERS, AND ALL TEAM MEMBERS MUST BE NATIONALS OF THE COUNTRY IN WHICH THE PROJECT WILL TAKE PLACE — ALTHOUGH ONE TEAM MEMBER CAN BE A NON-NATIONAL IF THIS IS CLEARLY JUSTIFIED. Three people, not one. That suits a community committee better than an individual fellowship does, and the money arrives to a group that already meets — which this file has repeatedly recorded as the difference between a project that survives and one that leaves with its founder. THE CAREER RULE, AND THE DEFINITION IS UNUSUALLY CAREFUL: ALL TEAM MEMBERS MUST BE EARLY IN THEIR CAREERS — NO MORE THAN FIVE YEARS OF PAID CONSERVATION EXPERIENCE EACH, EVIDENCED BY A DETAILED EMPLOYMENT HISTORY ON THE FORM. ACADEMIC PURSUITS SUCH AS A PhD DO NOT COUNT AS PAID EXPERIENCE. PAID experience. Years spent guarding a forest without a salary do not count against you, and study does not either. Read that carefully before assuming your people are too experienced. THE LADDER: UP TO US$15,000 FOR ONE YEAR AT ENTRY; UP TO US$25,000 IN A FOLLOW-UP AWARD FOR EXCEPTIONAL TEAMS ADDRESSING CONTINUING OBJECTIVES; AND UP TO US$50,000 IN A LEADERSHIP AWARD TO CONSOLIDATE THE WORK — GRANTS MADE IN A PROGRESSIVE ORDER SO SUCCESSFUL APPLICANTS AT ENTRY LEVEL CAN APPLY FOR CONTINUED FUNDING AT THE NEXT STAGE. Fifteen thousand to fifty thousand over three stages, for a team that need not hold a single degree between them. The entry step is the one to aim at; the rest follows delivery. WHAT THE PROJECT MUST BE ABOUT: PROTECTING SPECIES CATEGORISED AS GLOBALLY THREATENED OR DATA DEFICIENT, OR WHERE THERE IS INFORMATION INDICATING THE NEED FOR URGENT CONSERVATION ACTION — AND IT MAY ADDRESS THEMES SUCH AS CLIMATE IMPACT AND ADAPTATION, HABITAT RESTORATION AND/OR MANAGEMENT, SOCIAL DEVELOPMENT AND WELLBEING, INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION, AND/OR ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY. DATA DEFICIENT is the opening most communities miss. A species nobody has surveyed qualifies as readily as a famous endangered one — and the animals and plants around a village are very often in that category precisely because no one has looked. INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION and ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY are named themes, so the project need not be a pure wildlife count. THE PROJECT SHAPE: PROJECTS MUST BE NEWLY DEVELOPED AND RUN FOR 3 TO 12 MONTHS. NEWLY DEVELOPED — the opposite of the awards filed under São Tomé and Egypt, which fund proven work only. If your community has an idea rather than a track record, this is the door that fits. THE EXCLUSION TO CHECK BEFORE ASSEMBLING A TEAM: TEAM MEMBERS CANNOT BE EMPLOYEES OR CONTRACTORS OF THE THREE PARTNER ORGANISATIONS THAT RUN THE PROGRAMME. WHAT COMES WITH THE MONEY: LEADERSHIP TRAINING AND ONGOING PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT SUPPORT THROUGH A GLOBAL ALUMNI NETWORK, INCLUDING FUNDING, TRAINING AND MENTORSHIP — COMPREHENSIVE TRAINING IN THE BEST AND MOST EFFECTIVE TOOLS, TECHNIQUES AND STRATEGIES TO LEAD AND IMPLEMENT CONSERVATION ACTION IN THEIR RESPECTIVE SITES. THE ALUMNI NETWORK ITSELF DISBURSES FUNDING, not just contacts. So the first award is entry to a standing source rather than a single payment. THE STATED GOAL FOR THE PEOPLE FUNDED, WHICH IS WORTH QUOTING BACK IN AN APPLICATION: ALL TEAM MEMBERS SHOULD HAVE A DESIRE TO BE IMPACT MULTIPLIERS ACROSS THE CONSERVATION SECTOR, WITH THE ULTIMATE GOAL OF MITIGATING THREATS TO BIOLOGICAL DIVERSITY AND TRANSFERRING CAPACITIES TO LOCAL PEOPLE IN THE FIELD. TRANSFERRING CAPACITIES TO LOCAL PEOPLE is written into what they are funding you to do. A plan that trains twenty villagers scores better here than one that produces a report. WHAT THE WORK ITSELF INVOLVES: TEAMS CONDUCT SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH, ENCOURAGE AND PROMOTE PRO-CONSERVATION ATTITUDES AND DELIVER TANGIBLE RESULTS — COMBINING RESEARCH, ACTION, AND EDUCATION AND AWARENESS OF LOCAL STAKEHOLDERS. THE ADMINISTRATIVE FACTS: GRANTS ARE MADE IN ANNUAL CYCLES, APPLICATIONS ARE SUBMITTED ONLINE IN ENGLISH, AND GRANT GUIDELINES, AN APPLICATION FORM AND THE CALENDAR DEADLINE ARE ALL PUBLISHED. AND WHAT PAST WINNERS SAY IT DID BESIDES PAY: THE AWARDS NOT ONLY GAVE IMPORTANT PROJECT FUNDING, BUT ALSO RATIFIED THE CONSERVATION WORK BEING DONE, INFUSED THE TEAM WITH NEW ENTHUSIASM AND RENEWED SELF-BELIEF. RATIFIED is the word to notice. An outside body naming your work as conservation changes how a district officer, a chief and a ministry treat the same committee — and this file has recorded that recognition functioning as a form of protection. WHO IT SUITS: three or more young Africans from the same country, with or without formal education, wanting to start something on a threatened or unsurveyed species or habitat. CAVEATS: ENGLISH, ONLINE, ANNUAL CYCLE, AND THE PROJECT MUST BE NEW AND SPECIES-FOCUSED — not a fit for a long-running land campaign. For grants an individual can hold alone, Somalia's entry; for the award to a national leading a registered organisation, São Tomé's entry; for the cash award to the village group itself, Egypt's entry.

trackers.name: AgriCord — an alliance whose development agencies are governed by farmers' organisations rather than boards of donors — with published membership rules that a Senegalese farmers' body has already used to join as a full member, and 500+ partner organisations
trackers.desc: THE DEVELOPMENT AGENCIES ARE GOVERNED BY FARMERS — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S MAURITANIA ENTRY COVERS THE WEST AFRICAN PEASANT FEDERATION NAMED BELOW AS A PROGRAMME PARTNER, ITS MALI ENTRY THE EASTERN AND SOUTHERN FARMERS' FORUM, AND ITS SOUTH SUDAN ENTRY THE PRODUCER GRANTS FACILITY THIS ALLIANCE CO-MANAGES. The development agency is owned by farmers, and it exists to strengthen farmers' organisations. That is a different animal from an NGO with a rural programme: the people deciding its priorities hold land themselves, and the counterpart it deals with is your union rather than your ministry. This file has recorded again and again that whoever governs a funder determines what it will pay for. THE MEMBERSHIP OPENING, AND IT IS THE SECOND FIND: SINCE 2011, ORGANISATIONS FROM NON-OECD COUNTRIES HAVE ALSO JOINED THE ALLIANCE — ONE FROM THE ASIAN REGION, AND ONE FROM SENEGAL, THE AGRI-AGENCY FOR A LARGE GROUP OF SENEGALESE FARMERS' ORGANISATIONS. An African farmers' body sits as a full member of the alliance, not as a grantee of it. So the position of member is reachable — and a national federation that wants to stop receiving and start deciding has a precedent and a published route. THE MEMBERSHIP TEST, PUBLISHED: APPLYING ASSOCIATED ORGANISATIONS MUST HAVE THE LEGAL STATUTE OF A NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION, AND MUST HAVE A PROVEN RECORD OF CONCRETE INVOLVEMENT IN DEVELOPMENT COOPERATION ISSUES. Two conditions, both achievable over a few years. Compare the funder entries elsewhere here, where the ceiling for an African organisation is a grant. THE SCALE: SEVEN PROGRAMMES BRINGING TOGETHER 13 AGRI-AGENCY MEMBERS AND OVER 500 PARTNER ORGANISATIONS IN 31 COUNTRIES — OPERATING AS A NETWORK MANAGING A MULTI-DONOR ENVELOPE OF PROGRAMMES IMPLEMENTED BY AGRI-AGENCIES, FARMERS' ORGANISATIONS AND FARMER-LED COOPERATIVES. WHAT THE AGENCIES PROVIDE, WHICH IS THE THING NOBODY ELSE FUNDS: ORGANISATIONAL DEVELOPMENT FOR FARMERS' ORGANISATIONS — TO IMPROVE THEIR SERVICES TO FARMERS, TO RUN THEIR ECONOMIC BUSINESSES IN A MORE RESILIENT, EFFICIENT, SUSTAINABLE AND TRANSPARENT WAY, AND TO REPRESENT FARMERS' VOICES IN VALUE CHAINS AND WITH POLICY MAKERS — THROUGH ADVISORY SERVICES AND PROJECT MANAGEMENT RELATED BACKSTOPPING. BACKSTOPPING is the word to notice: somebody experienced standing behind your project manager when the reporting, the audit or the procurement goes wrong. That is what this file's DR Congo entry identifies as the gap that collapses community organisations between grants. THE EXCHANGE MECHANISM: THE AGRI-AGENCIES FACILITATE SOUTH-SOUTH AND NORTH-SOUTH FARMER TO FARMER AND FARMER ORGANISATION TO FARMER ORGANISATION EXCHANGES AND TWINNING ARRANGEMENTS. TWINNING — a standing relationship between your organisation and a comparable one abroad, rather than a single visit. Ask for that specifically; it survives staff changes on both sides. THE AFRICAN PROGRAMME AND ITS RESULT: A FARMERS' ORGANIZATIONS PROGRAMME RUN 2019 TO 2025 SUPPORTED 28 PROJECTS IN 12 AFRICAN COUNTRIES, REACHING TENS OF THOUSANDS OF PRODUCERS EACH YEAR AND STRENGTHENING FARMERS' ORGANIZATIONS INSTITUTIONALLY AND ECONOMICALLY — WITH A SUB-PROGRAMME OF 23 PROJECTS ACROSS SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA. THE NAMED AFRICAN REGIONAL PARTNERS, WHICH ARE A DIRECTORY IN THEMSELVES: AN EASTERN AFRICA FARMERS FEDERATION IN KENYA, A PAN-AFRICAN FARMERS ORGANISATION IN RWANDA, A CENTRAL AFRICAN PLATFORM IN CAMEROON, A WEST AFRICAN PEASANT NETWORK IN BURKINA FASO, A SOUTHERN AFRICAN CONFEDERATION OF AGRICULTURAL UNIONS IN SOUTH AFRICA, AND A TUNISIAN AGRICULTURAL UNION. Six regional farmer bodies covering the whole continent, each with an address. Whatever region you are in, one of those is the body your national organisation should already belong to — and this file's Mauritania entry describes the West African one from the inside. THE RESEARCH PROGRAMME AND ITS AFRICAN COUNTRIES: A FARMER-LED RESEARCH AND INNOVATION PROGRAMME COVERING BURKINA FASO, MALI, SENEGAL, CAMEROON, BURUNDI, THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, MADAGASCAR AND TANZANIA — 13 PROJECTS IN 17 COUNTRIES, IMPLEMENTED BY 7 MEMBER AGENCIES WITH PARTNER FARMER ORGANISATIONS AT NATIONAL, SUBNATIONAL AND LOCAL LEVEL, WITH A LIST OF ACTION-RESEARCH PROJECTS AND DOWNLOADABLE FACTSHEETS. DOWNLOADABLE FACTSHEETS per project. Before designing your own trial, read what a farmers' organisation two countries away already tested and what it cost. THAT PROGRAMME'S THIRD AIM IS THE ONE TO QUOTE: INCREASE LOCAL FARMER KNOW-HOW TO APPLY AGROECOLOGICAL APPROACHES AND TO INNOVATE FOR SUSTAINABLE AND RESILIENT AGROECOLOGICAL AGRI-FOOD SYSTEMS — ALONGSIDE IMPROVING INFLUENCE OVER OTHER STAKEHOLDERS ON FARMER-LED ACTION RESEARCH. HOW RESULTS TRAVEL, WHICH IS THE DESIGN WORTH COPYING: THE RESULTS OF THESE PROJECTS WILL BE CAPITALISED THROUGH THE ADVOCACY WORK OF THE PARTNER REGIONAL FARMERS ORGANISATIONS. The research is fed to the regional farmer bodies to argue with, rather than to a journal. A finding that ends in a regional federation's policy submission has a route to a ministry; one that ends in a report does not. AND THE PUBLISHED REPOSITORY: A RESOURCE SPACE OF ARTICLES, BOOKS AND VIDEOS, MEANT AS A REPOSITORY FOR KNOW-HOW AND EXPERTISE IN SUPPORT OF FARMERS AND FARMER ORGANISATIONS EVERYWHERE. WHO IT SUITS: African farmers' organisations and cooperatives wanting organisational strengthening, twinning with a peer abroad, or eventually a seat as a member rather than a grantee. CAVEATS: PARTNERSHIPS RUN THROUGH MEMBER AGENCIES AND REGIONAL FARMER BODIES, NOT BY OPEN APPLICATION — join your regional federation first. For the West African peasant federation, Mauritania's entry; for the eastern and southern farmers' forum and its district structure, Mali's entry; for the grants paid straight to producer organisations, South Sudan's entry.

Almost every free legal route in this file ends at an email address with no indication of what happens next or how long to wait; a community can plan around a month, and can tell when something has gone wrong. Firms compete to take the work, and more than one may offer. That means you may be choosing between lawyers rather than accepting whoever is available — ask each what they have done on land, extractives or environmental matters before picking. THE SCHEDULED CALL BEFORE PLACEMENT is worth preparing for: it is where the matter gets defined, and a vague description is what leaves a request unclaimed. THE SIZE OF THE NETWORK: A FREE SERVICE FOR BOTH LAW FIRMS AND NGOs, CONNECTING LAWYERS IN MORE THAN 175 COUNTRIES — MORE THAN 4,000 MEMBERS, INCLUDING OVER 800 LAW FIRMS AND IN-HOUSE LEGAL TEAMS BRINGING THE EXPERTISE OF AROUND 120,000 LAWYERS TO OVER 3,800 NGOs AND SOCIAL ENTERPRISES — WITH ANOTHER SOURCE PUTTING IT AT MORE THAN 900 FIRMS. IN-HOUSE LEGAL TEAMS as well as firms. A company's own lawyers volunteering is a different pool from private practice, and often carries commercial and contract expertise a community negotiating with a developer does not otherwise reach. THE STATED MISSION AND WHY IT MATTERS WHERE PRO BONO IS RARE: TO CONNECT PEOPLE AND SPREAD THE PRACTICE OF PRO BONO AROUND THE WORLD — PARTICULARLY TO COUNTRIES WHERE PRO BONO IS NOT TRADITIONALLY PRACTICED — AIMING TO IMPROVE THE OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY OF NGOs AND GIVE THEM ACCESS TO THE POWER OF THE LAW WHICH CAN BE USED TO TACKLE SOCIAL PROBLEMS AT A FUNDAMENTAL LEVEL. COUNTRIES WHERE PRO BONO IS NOT TRADITIONALLY PRACTICED. In much of Africa there is no expectation that a firm gives free work; this network exists partly to build that habit, so an approach in a country with no pro bono culture is on-mission rather than hopeless. WHO IT SERVES: BOTH INTERNATIONAL AND LOCAL NGOs AND SOCIAL ENTERPRISES WITH THEIR DAY-TO-DAY LEGAL NEEDS. LOCAL is named, and SOCIAL ENTERPRISES too — so a community cooperative or producer company qualifies alongside a non-profit, which this file has recorded as a gap in most legal services. THE MATTERS IT HANDLES: LEGAL ISSUES RELATED TO DAILY OPERATIONS — USE OF IMAGES ON THE INTERNET, TRADEMARK REGISTRATION, EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENTS, COMPLIANCE WITH DATA PROTECTION REGULATIONS, TAX EXEMPTIONS, COLLABORATION AGREEMENTS AND LEGAL STRUCTURES — AND ALSO RESEARCH PROJECTS THAT CAN BE USEFUL TO FULFIL A SOCIAL MISSION AND BE USED AS A TOOL FOR ADVOCACY. RESEARCH USED AS A TOOL FOR ADVOCACY, named by the service itself. That is the opening for a comparative study of how other countries regulate the industry on your land — the sort of document that changes a ministry's position and that no community can pay for. COLLABORATION AGREEMENTS is the other one to use: the memorandum between your committee and an outside NGO is exactly what should be lawyered before it is signed. THE RESEARCH ARM STATED SEPARATELY: IT FACILITATES GROUND-BREAKING PRO BONO LEGAL RESEARCH AND DEVELOPS LEGAL BEST PRACTICE GUIDES FOR THE SOCIAL SECTOR. THE COUNTRY-LEVEL CONNECTION IT OFFERS: IT CAN HELP YOU BETTER UNDERSTAND YOUR SITUATION AND OPTIONS, AND POTENTIALLY CONNECT YOU WITH A SPECIALIZED ATTORNEY OR LEGAL FIRM IN YOUR COUNTRY, FOR FREE. A lawyer in your own country, not only an analysis from abroad. That is what the standing brief keeps asking for, and it is the specific thing to request at the call. THE AFRICAN PRESENCE: HEADQUARTERED IN LONDON WITH REGIONAL HUBS IN NEW YORK AND NAIROBI, KENYA. A Nairobi hub is a nearer contact and an African timezone. Write there first. THE PARTNERSHIP THAT WIDENS THE POOL: A PARTNERSHIP WITH A GLOBAL REFERRAL NETWORK OF 700+ MEMBER FIRMS ACROSS 205 COUNTRIES, EXTENDING REACH TO MORE THAN 1,500 OF THE WORLD'S LEADING LAW FIRMS — INTENDED TO ADDRESS THE GROWING GAP BETWEEN THE NEED FOR PRO BONO LEGAL ADVICE AND THE NUMBER OF FIRMS AVAILABLE TO PROVIDE IT. The gap is acknowledged by the people running the largest network. Demand exceeds supply, so a well-framed request that is easy to say yes to beats a sprawling one. AND THE SEPARATE MEDIA SERVICE: A LEGAL SERVICE FOR INDEPENDENT MEDIA OFFERING TAILORED SUPPORT TO EQUIP JOURNALISTS, NEWSROOMS AND MEDIA FREEDOM FOCUSED NON-PROFITS TO COUNTER LEGAL THREATS AND STRENGTHEN THEIR RESILIENCE. For the local reporter sued for covering a project — which this file has recorded as a standard tactic — there is a separate named service rather than the general queue. WHO IT SUITS: African community organisations, cooperatives and NGOs needing registration, contracts, tax status, agreements with partners, or comparative legal research — free. CAVEATS: OPERATIONAL AND RESEARCH WORK RATHER THAN COURT REPRESENTATION, MEMBERSHIP AND ELIGIBILITY MUST BE CONFIRMED FIRST, AND PLACEMENT DEPENDS ON A FIRM OFFERING — for representation, use the local routes. For the clearinghouse with a published opt-out on sharing your request, São Tomé's entry; for senior lawyers on attorney-client terms, Ethiopia's entry.

trackers.name: The Table Mountain Fund — an endowed African conservation trust fund whose published record includes purchasing conservation land outright — with grant ceilings and durations stated, micro-grants that are often an organisation's first ever funding, and unregistered bodies considered where well motivated

PURCHASING IMPORTANT CONSERVATION LAND, listed first among the things the money has done. The standing question in this file is who pays for the parcel; here is an African fund whose own record says it has, 380 times over and on a published balance. That is the structure to point at when arguing that a national conservation trust fund should exist in your own country — the money outlives the donor. THE MICRO-GRANT AND WHAT IT MEANS, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IT SUPPORTS SMALL AND MICRO GRANT FACILITIES FOR CONSERVATION PROJECTS BEING IMPLEMENTED BY FLEDGLING COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS — AT TIMES THESE MICRO GRANTS REPRESENT THE FIRST FINANCIAL SUPPORT THESE ORGANISATIONS HAVE EVER RECEIVED, AND ALLOW THEM A WELL FACILITATED AND MENTORED INDUCTION EXPERIENCE. A first grant with mentoring attached. This file has recorded the first grant as the hardest one to get and the one that unlocks every subsequent application; a fund that treats being unfunded as the qualifying condition rather than a warning sign is rare. THE REGISTRATION DOOR IT LEAVES OPEN: REGISTERED ORGANISATIONS IN GOOD STANDING WITH A PROVEN TRACK RECORD ARE ENCOURAGED TO APPLY — BUT UNDER EXCEPTIONAL CIRCUMSTANCES AND WHERE WELL MOTIVATED FOR, ORGANISATIONS NOT YET REGISTERED AS NON-PROFITS MAY BE CONSIDERED. Four years is unusually long, and the pool size tells you the real odds: R6.7 million against a R1.2 million ceiling means a handful of projects, not dozens. THE PROGRAMME THE LAND WORK SITS IN: A PROGRAMME ENSURING PRIORITY NATURAL ECOSYSTEMS ARE HEALTHY AND RESILIENT, INCLUDING PROTECTION OF LAND AND THE APPROPRIATE MANAGEMENT THEREOF — WITH APPLICANTS ASKED FOR A TRACK RECORD IN BIODIVERSITY STEWARDSHIP AND/OR PROTECTED AREA EXPANSION. Land held and run by the people on it can be funded under that heading. THE DELEGATED SMALL-GRANT MODEL, WITH ITS NUMBERS: ONE FACILITY WAS DESIGNED TO FINANCE UP TO 21 PROJECTS, EACH OF APPROXIMATELY R30,000, AVAILABLE TO COMMUNITIES AND LANDOWNERS OR LAND MANAGERS INCLUDING FIVE NAMED COMMUNITIES — ADMINISTERED BY A PROVINCIAL CONSERVATION AUTHORITY WITH SUPPORT FROM A CITY OVER THREE YEARS. The fund pays; the provincial authority runs the facility. Worth knowing because the application goes to the authority, not the fund — and a community's own conservation department may already be holding money like this without advertising it widely. HOW THAT FACILITY IS ACCESSED: ADVERTISED VIA A CALL FOR PROPOSALS ANNUALLY, WITH BENEFICIARIES APPLYING BY SUBMITTING A PROJECT PROPOSAL REVIEWED BY A COMMITTEE; ONCE APPROVED, THE AUTHORITY AND THE BENEFICIARY ENTER INTO A CONTRACTUAL AGREEMENT. Annual, so missing it costs a year. Ask the administering authority to put you on the notification list rather than watching for the advertisement. Bursaries plus a two-year placement, which is a route into paid conservation work rather than a training certificate. Read it beside the scholarship recorded in this file's Somalia entry. THE MIXED-TENURE LANDSCAPE IT WORKS IN: ONE PARTNERSHIP AREA COMPRISES PUBLIC, PRIVATE AND COMMUNAL LAND IN HIGHLY THREATENED, POORLY CONSERVED HABITAT — WITH AN AQUIFER SUPPLYING POTABLE WATER TO A MAJOR CITY, AND THE PRESERVATION OF CULTURAL IDENTITY, WATER SECURITY, NATURE-BASED LIVELIHOODS AND ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES NAMED AS PARTICULARLY IMPORTANT. An aquifer supplying a city's drinking water is the argument that moves a municipality. Where the land you are defending feeds a water supply, that connection is worth establishing early and in writing. AND THE THREATS IT NAMES: URBAN AND AGRICULTURAL EXPANSION, COMMERCIAL AFFORESTATION, THE AGGRESSIVE SPREAD OF INVASIVE PLANT SPECIES AND THE CONTINUAL THREAT OF TOO FREQUENT, UNCONTROLLED FIRES. WHO IT SUITS: organisations and communities in its region needing money to buy, protect or manage land — including first-time applicants and, on motivation, unregistered ones. CAVEATS: BOUND TO ONE SOUTH AFRICAN FLORAL REGION, WITH ANNUAL CALLS AND A SMALL POOL; ITS LARGER GRANTS EXPECT A TRACK RECORD, AND SOME FACILITIES ARE APPLIED FOR THROUGH A PROVINCIAL AUTHORITY RATHER THAN THE FUND — it is also a model to cite when arguing for a national conservation trust fund elsewhere. For the trust that registers servitudes on title deeds, São Tomé's entry; for the body that buys farms outright, South Sudan's entry.

trackers.name: A feminist NGO for farm dwellers that identified a statutory grant which can be used to purchase land and housing for people at risk of eviction — then asked the state for the numbers on how often it had been paid, and was told none existed
trackers.desc: THERE IS A GRANT THAT BUYS LAND FOR FARM DWELLERS — ASK FOR THE NUMBERS — method and adjacency declared first: THIS MOVEMENT IS THE THIRD FOUNDER OF THE 170,000-MEMBER ASSEMBLY FILED UNDER SÃO TOMÉ, WHICH NAMES A FARM WOMEN'S PROJECT WITHOUT DESCRIBING IT OR SHIPPING THIS HOST; THIS FILE'S SOUTH AFRICA BUCKET CARRIES THE LAWYERS-FOR-HUMAN-RIGHTS HOST FROM WHICH THIS ORGANISATION ORIGINALLY BEGAN, AND ITS SUDAN ENTRY THE FEMINIST LAW CENTRE NAMING FARM WORKERS. NONE IS RESTATED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THE SHIPPED HOST AND FIVE SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL ABSENT. THE GRANT THAT BUYS LAND, WHICH IS THE FIND: SECTION 4 OF THE EXTENSION OF SECURITY OF TENURE ACT (ESTA) PROVIDES LONG-TERM GRANTS THAT CAN BE USED TO PURCHASE LAND AND DEVELOP HOUSING FOR FARM DWELLERS AT RISK OF EVICTION. A statutory grant, already in law, for buying land for the people about to be thrown off it. This file has spent many entries on foreign funds that might pay for land; here the state has undertaken to do it, and almost nobody knows the section exists. Find the equivalent provision in your own tenure legislation before looking abroad. THE QUESTION THEY ASKED ABOUT IT, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: WE'VE ASKED FOR STATISTICS ON HOW THE TENURE GRANT HAS BEEN APPLIED — THEY DON'T HAVE ANY, SO WE ASSUME IT HAS NOT BEEN IMPLEMENTED; WITH A CALL FOR DATA ON THE NUMBER OF APPLICATIONS RECEIVED AND FINALISED, AND CRITICISM OF DELAYS IN IMPLEMENTING GRANTS PROVIDED FOR UNDER AMENDMENTS SIGNED INTO LAW IN APRIL 2024. The tactic is the whole lesson: ask the department how many times it has used its own power. An answer of none, or no records kept, is a finding a community can campaign on, quote to a parliamentary committee and put in a court paper — and it costs one letter. WHY WOMEN IN PARTICULAR LOSE THE HOUSE: MANY WOMEN LIVE ON FARMS THROUGH MALE RELATIVES, A SITUATION THAT LEAVES WOMEN LEGALLY EXPOSED WHEN EMPLOYMENT RELATIONSHIPS END OR OWNERSHIP CHANGES — FARM WORKERS, ESPECIALLY WOMEN, CONTINUE TO LACK INDEPENDENT TENURE RIGHTS. Tenure held through a husband or father is tenure that ends with him. The same structure this file's Sudan entry records ending in separation, here ending in eviction. THE MECHANISM OF DISPOSSESSION IT DOCUMENTS: FARMS ARE INCREASINGLY BEING SOLD OR SUBDIVIDED, WITH NEW OWNERS OPTING FOR CONTRACT LABOUR RATHER THAN RETAINING RESIDENT WORKERS — WELL-RESOURCED LANDOWNERS ARE OFTEN ABLE TO EXPLOIT LOOPHOLES IN TENURE LAWS, WHILE FARM DWELLERS RELY ON OVERSTRETCHED STATE-FUNDED LEGAL AID; IT ALSO RAISED THE REZONING OF AGRICULTURAL LAND IN HIGH-VALUE AREAS FOR LUXURY ESTATES. SOLD OR SUBDIVIDED, THEN CONTRACT LABOUR. That sequence is the warning sign: when a farm changes hands and the new owner starts hiring by the day, the resident families are next. Watching the deeds registry is cheaper than fighting the eviction. THE PROTECTION IT FOUND IN A LIVE CASE: IT ARGUED THAT A FORMER WORKER'S WIFE HAS LONG-TERM PROTECTED STATUS UNDER THE TENURE ACT BECAUSE SHE BECAME DISABLED WHILST WORKING ON THE FARM — A CLAIM THE FARMER'S LEGAL TEAM DISPUTES, AND WHICH WILL BE ARGUED IN COURT. A specific statutory protection most people never hear of: becoming disabled in the employer's service can convert occupation into long-term protected status. Worth checking against your own facts before accepting that a former worker has no rights. WHAT AN EVICTION LOOKS LIKE WITHOUT PAPERS, IN A RESIDENT'S OWN WORDS: THE OWNER HAS STARTED TRYING TO EVICT PEOPLE BUT IT IS ILLEGAL BECAUSE THERE ARE NO COURT PAPERS — SHE IS OFFERING R38,000 TO SOME BUT THAT IS UNFAIR BECAUSE WE HAVE LIVED THERE ALL OUR LIVES, SAID A WOMAN WHO HAD LIVED ON THE FARM FOR 38 YEARS AND WHOSE PARENTS LIVED THERE TOO; ANOTHER RESIDENT SAID THEY DID NOT TRUST THEY WOULD HAVE A FAIR HEARING IN COURT. NO COURT PAPERS is the single most useful thing a farm dweller can establish. An eviction without an order is unlawful whatever the owner says, and a cash offer made instead of a court process is an admission that the process was never begun. THE CONSTITUTIONAL ARGUMENT IT PUTS TO PARLIAMENT: A PERSON OR COMMUNITY WHOSE TENURE OF LAND IS LEGALLY INSECURE AS A RESULT OF PAST RACIALLY DISCRIMINATORY LAWS OR PRACTICES IS ENTITLED EITHER TO TENURE WHICH IS LEGALLY SECURE OR TO COMPARABLE REDRESS, AND PARLIAMENT MUST ENACT THE LEGISLATION — SO THOSE SUBSECTIONS ALREADY PROVIDE A SUFFICIENT CONSTITUTIONAL BASIS TO REDISTRIBUTE LAND TO FARM DWELLERS. EITHER SECURE TENURE OR COMPARABLE REDRESS. Two alternatives, and the state must supply one of them — which reframes an eviction as a question of what is owed rather than whether anything is. THE FINDING IT MAKES ABOUT THE TENURE ACT ITSELF: THE ACT WAS ENACTED TO GIVE EFFECT TO THAT SUBSECTION, BUT THE REALITY IS THE ACT HAS BEEN USED TO EVICT MILLIONS OF FARM DWELLERS FROM THE LAND WHICH THEY HAVE ALWAYS KNOWN AS HOME ALL THEIR LIVES. A protective statute functioning as the instrument of removal. Recorded because it is the pattern to test for anywhere: read who actually files under a tenure act, and how often they win. THE CONDITIONS DOCUMENTED TO A PARLIAMENTARY DELEGATION: 19 YEARS AFTER A NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS COMMISSION REPORT ON LAND TENURE SECURITY AND LABOUR RELATIONS IN FARMING COMMUNITIES, ILLEGAL EVICTIONS ARE STILL GOING ON DESPITE THE LEGISLATION — WITH FARM WORKERS STILL SUBJECTED TO CONDITIONS INCLUDING THAT THEIR CHILDREN MUST LEAVE THE FARM WHEN THEY REACH 18 YEARS OLD OR PAY R590 TO BE ALLOWED TO LIVE ON THE FARM. Children charged rent to remain in their parents' home at eighteen. That detail, taken to a parliamentary committee, does more work than any general statement about conditions — and a delegation heard it because an organisation brought people to say it. WHAT IT ASKS FOR INSTEAD: ACCELERATED LAND REDISTRIBUTION INCLUDING EXPROPRIATION OF UNUSED FARMLAND, AND EFFECTIVE IMPLEMENTATION OF A NAMED EXPROPRIATION ACT TO FACILITATE REDISTRIBUTION TO FARM WORKERS AND DWELLERS WHO HAVE WORKED THE LAND FOR GENERATIONS — SINCE THE DEPARTMENT SAYS FARMERS ARE UNWILLING TO MAKE LAND AVAILABLE. WHAT THE ORGANISATION IS AND WHERE IT WORKS: A FEMINIST NGO IN A NAMED TOWN, WORKING WITH WOMEN FARM WORKERS AND DWELLERS IN ONE PROVINCE SINCE 1996 AND A SECOND SINCE 2009, ORIGINALLY A PROJECT OF A HUMAN RIGHTS LAWYERS ORGANISATION BEGUN IN 1992 — WITH A PUBLISHED TELEPHONE NUMBER. It began inside a human rights law firm and was spun out as an independent organisation. That is a route worth noting: a law centre can incubate the community organisation it will later represent. AND ITS PORTFOLIOS AND METHOD: LABOUR RIGHTS, ORGANISATION BUILDING AND SOCIAL RIGHTS — THE LAST CONTAINING PROGRAMMES ON MAINTENANCE AND VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN; EQUIPPING FARM WOMEN WITH KNOWLEDGE AND CONFIDENCE ABOUT THEIR LAND AND HOUSING RIGHTS SO THEY CAN SECURE TENURE, DEVELOPING WOMEN'S LEADERSHIP THROUGH TRAINING, AND CREATING AWARENESS OF THE DISADVANTAGES OF FARM WORKERS SO DECISION-MAKERS AND CIVIL SOCIETY CAN ACT. WHO IT SUITS: farm workers and dwellers facing eviction or living on land through a relative — and organisations anywhere wanting the ask-for-the-statistics tactic or a tenure-grant provision to look for at home. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY AND TWO PROVINCES, WITH A WOMEN FARM WORKER FOCUS; IT EDUCATES, ORGANISES AND SUPPORTS CASES RATHER THAN OPERATING AS A LAW CENTRE, AND FARM DWELLERS THERE RELY ON OVERSTRETCHED STATE LEGAL AID BY ITS OWN ACCOUNT. For the assembly it co-founded, São Tomé's entry; for the feminist law centre that litigates tenure loss, Sudan's entry.

trackers.name: National Audit Office
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Kiribati, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Kiribati — Business & Companies Regulatory Division (MCIC)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the Business & Companies Regulatory Division of the Ministry of Commerce, Industry & Cooperatives manages the commercial register (company & business-name registration), Kiribati. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Kiribati — Ministry of Finance & Economic Development (MFED)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; prepares the national budget & financial reports and manages fiscal & economic policy, Kiribati. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Kiribati.

trackers.name: A prohibition without a management duty is not protection
trackers.desc: KIRIBATI'S OWN RECORD SHOWS THREE MODELS THAT FAILED AND ONE THAT WORKED — check which your site sits under. Birnie, Kanton, Enderbury and Orona were ‘prohibited areas’ under the Prohibited Areas Ordinance 1957, which prohibited entry but did not require or contemplate active management measures. Parts of Kanton were protected under the Closed Districts Act 1990 — but the principal objective was to allow orderly development of the atoll, not conservation. Rawaki, Birnie and McKean were wildlife sanctuaries under the Wildlife Conservation Ordinance. And the only previous management plan, from 1983, was never effectively implemented. A prohibition without a management duty is not protection, and a designation made for another purpose will be administered for that purpose. WHAT WORKED: an environment conservation order under the Environment Act 1999 — the PIPA Regulations, 2006, formally extended by the PIPA Regulations 2008 to 408,250 km², or 11.7 percent of Kiribati's EEZ, closing it to extractive activity — and crucially providing for a management plan and clear permitting rules. The instrument is a regulation-level order, so the 1999 Act is the enabling power to cite.

trackers.name: Land sales need next-of-kin and High Court approval — and a needs test
trackers.desc: CUSTOMARY TENURE CONSTRAINS EVERYTHING ON INHABITED ISLANDS, AND ONE RULE PROTECTS FAMILIES DIRECTLY. Under the Gilbert and Phoenix Islands Land Code, which codifies custom, an owner may sell land, a pit or a fish pond only after the owner's next-of-kin AND the High Court approve — and approval turns on the capacity of the owner's remaining land to provide for their needs. A sale that would leave a family without enough land to live on is not approvable. That is a protection in itself, and also why acquisition-based conservation is largely unavailable here. NOTE TWO MORE FEATURES: the Code regulates lands, fish ponds and fish traps together — fish ponds and traps are land interests, which matters for any lagoon or coastal proposal; and joint ownership is provided for, with owners taking access in alternate years. The Native Lands Ordinance 1956 governs ownership and a decision of the Court is indefeasible. Environmental management, as the legislative review puts it, requires the co-operation of landowners. TWO PROCEDURAL HOOKS: the Environment Act 1999 requires any development proposal to be accompanied by an assessment, and General and Detailed Land Use Plans setting out development proposals are presented for public scrutiny. Local Government Councils exist under the Local Government Act 1984 with precise functions.

trackers.name: Pacific Development and Conservation Trust — citizens may apply
trackers.desc: AN INDIVIDUAL CAN APPLY, AND THE FIRST DOCUMENT IS SHORT. The Pacific Development and Conservation Trust, administered through the New Zealand government's Community Matters service with requests assessed by Advisory Trustees, states that ‘citizens or organisations’ from eligible Pacific places may request funding — so an individual can apply, which is rare and matters where no registered body exists. Eligible places include Kiribati, Tonga, Samoa, Cook Islands, Niue, Nauru, Tuvalu, Fiji, Palau, PNG, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, Tokelau, the Marshall Islands, FSM, and the French and US Pacific territories. THE PROCESS IS TWO-STAGE: submit an Expression of Interest, which the Trustees consider; successful applicants are then invited to submit a full project application. Do not prepare a full proposal before the EOI is accepted. Applications must be on the current form with all sections completed, submitted online where connection allows. THE MOST USEFUL THING BEFORE YOU DRAFT: the Trust publishes records of grants by round — 2020/21, 2021/22, 2022/23 (two rounds), 2023/24 and 2024/25. Read the published record of what the Trustees have actually funded, at what size and in which countries — that is better evidence than any guidance note. ONE DISTINCTION THAT AFFECTS HOW YOU REACH UNDP HERE: UNDP's Pacific Office provides country support to ten states — FSM, Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Nauru, Palau, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu and Vanuatu — but only regional support to five, including Samoa, Cook Islands, Niue, PNG and Tokelau. Check which applies to you before expecting an in-country office.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: SPREP EIA and SEA guidelines — intervene at scoping, not after
trackers.desc: SCOPING IS WHERE STAKEHOLDER CONCERNS BECOME TERMS OF REFERENCE — and the guidelines say so themselves. Assessments must be individually customised to the aspects most relevant to stakeholders, and ‘customisation usually occurs during the scoping phase and results in the preparation of terms of reference’. Intervene at scoping and the assessment is required to examine your issue; intervene later and you are commenting on an assessment that was never asked to look. SPREP's Strengthening Environmental Impact Assessment: Guidelines for Pacific Island Countries and Territories (60pp, English and French) is the regional practice standard, SPREP having been mandated on EIA capacity since the 1990s. KNOW WHICH INSTRUMENT YOUR FIGHT NEEDS: EIA assesses a project; the companion Strategic Environmental Assessment guidelines (developed 2018–2020) assess a policy, plan or programme and are addressed to environment agencies, national planning offices, development control agencies, municipal authorities and provincial administrations — so if the problem is a tourism plan or a zoning programme rather than one hotel, SEA is the instrument and the municipal or provincial authority is the addressee. There is also a sector guideline for coastal tourism development, made with the South Pacific Tourism Organisation. THE HONEST PART, FROM A REGULATOR'S OWN ACCOUNT: Vanuatu's Principal EIA Officer publicly described her department's challenges as lack of staff, lack of political support, weaknesses in public consultation, and low capacity in monitoring and enforcement. Expect to supply evidence the agency cannot gather itself, and expect post-consent monitoring to be weak unless someone outside government does it — it is also a citable admission when arguing that a condition needs an independent monitoring mechanism attached. CHECK YOUR OWN ENVIRONMENT ACT FIRST: many Pacific countries have EIA mandated under their Environment Acts and EIA Regulations, and these guidelines support the implementation of current legal requirements rather than replacing them — the practice standard, not the obligation. SPREP runs in-country EIA training workshops, and the Pacific Environment Portal carries regional and national data.

trackers.name: Waigani Convention — radioactive waste, and 200 miles not 12
trackers.desc: IT REACHES WHERE BASEL CANNOT — and for island states that is the whole point. The Waigani Convention is modelled on Basel and is the regional implementation of the hazardous waste regime, but differs in two decisive ways: it also covers radioactive wastes, and its territorial coverage includes each Party's Exclusive Economic Zone — 200 nautical miles — rather than stopping at the 12 nautical mile territorial sea as Basel does. That makes it the instrument for dumping, transhipment and seabed disposal cases Basel cannot touch. It is annex-driven: obligations extend to all wastes in Annex I or those possessing the listed characteristics — check Annex I first; if the substance is listed the obligations attach automatically, and if not, the argument runs through the hazard characteristics instead. It is closely tied to the London Convention on dumping at sea. THE BODY TO CONTACT: the Pacific Regional Centre for the Waigani and Basel Conventions, based at SPREP in Samoa, which has developed a model law implementing all four waste conventions (Basel, Rotterdam, Stockholm, Waigani) with a worked Tonga project — so where a national statute is missing or fragmented, the model already exists and a government can be pointed at it. AND A CONSULTATION WINDOW IS OPEN NOW: Cleaner Pacific 2025, the regional waste and pollution strategy built with 21 member countries around four goals and 15 strategic actions, is being replaced — the successor CP2036 was endorsed at the 31st SPREP Meeting (September 2023) with consultation in Suva, 21–22 July 2025. Priorities for the next decade are being set now. Ask whether your country has a national waste and pollution policy written against the regional strategy — it is the document your government is measured against. Delivery vehicles include PacWaste Plus (EUR 16.5 million, 72 months, EU-funded, across eight waste streams). THE HONEST LIMIT, FROM SPREP'S OWN REVIEW: Australia's reporting capability far exceeds that of most Pacific island countries, relying on weighbridge data requiring infrastructure that is not available — so do not assume an absence of data means an absence of a problem, and community-gathered data may be the best evidence there is. Watch the Clean Pacific Roundtable and CIRCLE EXPO, held alternately for an annual meeting of countries, industry and civil society — named as a participant category, not an observer.

trackers.name: Right to information — what your country actually has
trackers.desc: ASK EVEN WHERE THERE IS NO STATUTE — UNESCO's 2022 report on SDG 16.10.2 records that even Pacific states without access-to-information laws have an environment ‘generally favourable to the public's exercising of their right to information’. The absence of a law is not, on the region's own evidence, a reason to expect refusal. AND THERE IS A COMMITMENT TO CITE WHERE NO LAW EXISTS: the Boe Declaration on Regional Security (2018) Action Plan includes the adoption and implementation of constitutional, statutory and/or policy guarantees for public access to information as a measure for success — a government that signed Boe has already agreed that access to information is a measure of its own success. The Pacific Plan 2005 and the UN Pacific Strategy urge the same. The underlying right sits in article 19 of the ICCPR and of the Universal Declaration. REGIONAL POSITION: only four Pacific island countries have adopted RTI laws — Cook Islands (2008), Palau (2014), Vanuatu (2016) and Fiji (2018) — with several others drafting. A SOURCING WARNING FROM VANUATU'S OWN RTI UNIT, which applies region-wide: its site carries the notice ‘beware of fake websites pretending to be official’ — verify the domain before submitting anything containing your identity and your concern. IN KIRIBATI: an RTI strategy was developed in 2014 and a draft FOI law is reported.

trackers.name: ELAW — free attorneys and scientists who will critique the developer's EIA
trackers.desc: IT WILL READ THE DEVELOPER'S EIA AND TELL YOU WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT — which is the thing a community cannot produce alone and usually cannot afford. ELAW is a global alliance of attorneys, scientists and other advocates, founded 1989 in Eugene, Oregon by public interest lawyers from ten countries, that provides legal and scientific support to grassroots advocates to challenge destructive projects. FOUR CONCRETE FORMS OF HELP: legal support to local public interest lawyers; scientific support, including critiquing environmental assessments; economic insights on projects; and security expertise — ‘ELAW helps environmental lawyers improve their security so they can work without fear. When our partners are targeted, we act quickly to help defend and protect them.’ That last one is a named function, not an aspiration, and ELAW co-founded the Alliance for Land, Indigenous and Environmental Defenders. HOW TO USE IT — THROUGH A LAWYER, NOT AS A CLIENT: ELAW works through more than 300 public interest advocates in its network, and its stated strategy is ‘locating strong lawyers who are committed to protecting the environment in their home countries’. You can approach ELAW directly, but the leverage is greatest when a local advocate is the conduit — that is how the network is built. It has hosted nearly 300 advocates from more than 65 countries as Fellows and provided support on thousands of cases; several partners have won the Goldman Environmental Prize. Focus areas include biodiversity, fossil fuels — expressly assisting advocates in contesting fossil fuel development projects — plastic pollution, and work with coastal communities. It publishes guidebooks, including one to give communities sufficient understanding to challenge oil and gas projects, and clause-level summaries of national EIA law — so its site is also a route to learning exactly what your own EIA law requires. ASK WHETHER ELAW HAS A PARTNER IN YOUR COUNTRY: the network is described as spanning 70 to 80 countries but the member list is not published country by country, so this entry does not assert a presence in yours.

trackers.name: Micronesia Conservation Trust (MCT)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a conservation trust fund based in Kolonia, Pohnpei, running small-grant programmes across the five Micronesia Challenge jurisdictions and accredited as an entity of the Green Climate Fund. Its stated impact areas include coastal fisheries management plans and actions, forest stewardship, expansion and improvement of Protected Areas Networks, watershed and forest management for climate resilience, invasive species control, and livelihoods tied to conservation. WHO IT SUITS: legally recognised not-for-profits in those jurisdictions — NGOs, associations, schools and universities, church groups, women's groups, youth groups, research bodies — and, importantly, communities themselves: a chartered community can apply directly, and an unchartered one can too if its legitimacy is corroborated in writing by a state or municipal government. HOW IT DIFFERS: it gives priority to projects implementing an EXISTING management plan or Local Early Action Plan over projects that would write a new one, so an already-adopted plan is worth more here than a good idea. Money moves by periodic calls for proposals, not on a rolling basis.

trackers.name: Office of the Auditor-General
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Marshall Islands, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Marshall Islands — Ministry of Finance, Banking & Postal Services
trackers.desc: National budget authority; comprehensive public financial management administering revenue, budget & fiscal functions, Republic of the Marshall Islands. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Marshall Islands.

trackers.name: Marshall Islands Corporate Registry (IRI)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); the Republic of the Marshall Islands corporate registry, administered by International Registries Inc. — the official register of RMI companies and legal entities.

trackers.name: SPREP — three conventions, and 26 members is not 12 parties
trackers.desc: THE REGIONAL BODY FOR PACIFIC ENVIRONMENT, AND IT IS SECRETARIAT TO THREE CONVENTIONS. SPREP is an independent intergovernmental organisation, autonomous since the Agreement Establishing SPREP was signed at Apia on 16 June 1993, with the Article 2 purpose of providing assistance to protect and improve the environment and ensure sustainable development for present and future generations. It has 26 members — 14 Pacific island countries, 7 territories and 5 metropolitan states — and is headquartered in Apia, Samoa. ESTABLISH WHICH CONVENTION FITS YOUR ISSUE: the Noumea Convention (1986, in force 1990), described by UNEP as the only comprehensive multilateral umbrella agreement for protection of natural resources and environment in the region; the Waigani Convention on hazardous and radioactive waste imports; and the Apia Convention on nature conservation. THE NOUMEA CONVENTION IS UNDER ACTIVE REVIEW — WHICH IS AN OPENING: a 2021 Review produced recommendations now being implemented through a Noumea Workplan and Budget whose stated aim is to elevate the work of the Convention and enhance awareness and implementation, with a Communications Plan and a Finance Strategy named as critical. BUT CHECK WHETHER YOUR STATE IS A PARTY: SPREP has 26 members while the Noumea Convention has only 12 contracting parties — membership and party status are different things, and this entry does not assert the latter. GOVERNANCE POINT WORTH KNOWING: the SPREP Meeting is the plenary decision-making body; the Executive Board (established 2015) is subordinate to it and has no power to make decisions requiring input of all Members — so a decision affecting all members must go to the Meeting. IF YOUR ISSUE IS SEABED MINING: UNEP records deep sea mining as an emerging contentious issue the region is dealing with — the regional body has already named it. SPREP is also developing a portal for protected areas managers. THERE IS A SPREP PRESENCE IN YOUR COUNTRY: beyond Apia, host country agreements exist with the Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, the Marshall Islands, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu — so you need not approach Samoa first. YOUR STATE IS RECORDED AS A NOUMEA CONVENTION PARTY: it was among those represented at the 18th Conference of the Parties, Apia, 5 September 2025 — so the Convention's obligations and its Workplan apply here.

trackers.name: Micronesia Conservation Trust and your national society — who funds and who acts
trackers.desc: MONEY DESIGNED TO OUTLAST THE GOVERNMENT OF THE DAY. The Micronesia Conservation Trust, established 2002 as a charitable and IRREVOCABLE corporation, exists to support conservation ‘by providing long term sustained funding’ — an endowment, not a project grant cycle. It hosts a regional endowment that has secured US$14.8 million since 2007, with pledges from The Nature Conservancy, Conservation International and the GEF, aiming for a further $41 million. Its goals include strengthening the ability of communities and community organisations — named ahead of government agencies — to conserve biodiversity, and supporting conservation of priority natural biodiversity resource areas. THE REGIONAL PRECEDENT IS LARGE: the Micronesia Challenge has aided in strengthening or establishing over 150 protected areas, so comparable local examples exist. Also active and named in the partnership records: OneReef, Island Conservation, RARE, the Pacific Marine Resources Institute, and PIMPAC, which shares community and government approaches to enforcement of marine managed areas. Micronesians in Island Conservation is a peer network of the national societies with a member-nominated steering committee, offering members peers, mentors and experts, with MCT funding its annual retreats. IN THE MARSHALL ISLANDS: the Marshall Islands Conservation Society is the named national member of these networks, alongside the College of the Marshall Islands.

trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Budget & Economic Management and Treasury divisions manage public finances & the national budget, Federated States of Micronesia. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Micronesia.

trackers.name: Micronesia — Registrar of Corporations (FSM Dept of Justice)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the Registrar of Corporations within the FSM Department of Justice administers the national Corporate Registry Program, Federated States of Micronesia. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: ELAW — free attorneys and scientists who will critique the developer's EIA

trackers.name: Micronesia Conservation Trust and your national society — who funds and who acts
trackers.desc: MONEY DESIGNED TO OUTLAST THE GOVERNMENT OF THE DAY.
