trackers.name: National mangrove initiative naming civil society as a partner, the 190-measure coastal resilience strategy, and the plant atlas and seeds campaign
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE COUNTRY WITH THE THINNEST LOCAL LAYER IN THE PAYLOAD, AND THE MOST USEFUL SENTENCE IN IT IS ABOUT WHO IS INVITED IN: THE NATIONAL MANGROVE INITIATIVE PROCEEDS THROUGH COOPERATION BETWEEN GOVERNMENT BODIES, THE PRIVATE SECTOR AND CIVIL SOCIETY INSTITUTIONS. CIVIL SOCIETY INSTITUTIONS NAMED AS A PARTNER IN A FLAGSHIP NATIONAL PROGRAMME IS THE OPENING A SOCIETY OR A COASTAL COMMUNITY GROUP SHOULD USE. THE ASK IS NARROW AND ANSWERABLE: WHICH CIVIL SOCIETY BODIES ARE ALREADY PARTICIPATING, AND HOW DOES ANOTHER ONE JOIN. THE PROGRAMME IS REAL AND MEASURED: LAUNCHED IN DECEMBER 2024 TO INCREASE MANGROVE COVER FOURFOLD BY 2035 BY PLANTING IN TIDAL AREAS, ON COASTS AND IN RESERVES, IT HAD PLANTED MORE THAN TWO POINT TWO MILLION MANGROVE SEEDLINGS BY THE MIDDLE OF 2026 - REPORTED AS AN ACHIEVEMENT RATE OF A HUNDRED AND THIRTY-EIGHT PER CENT AGAINST TARGET. A PROGRAMME RUNNING AHEAD OF ITS TARGET NEEDS SOMEWHERE TO PUT THE NEXT MILLION SEEDLINGS. A COMMUNITY WITH A TIDAL FLAT, A DEGRADED SHORE OR A SILTED CREEK IS OFFERING A SITE TO A PROGRAMME THAT NEEDS SITES - AND THIS FILE HAS RECORDED THE SAME LOGIC WORKING FOR PROTECTED AREAS IN TWO OTHER COUNTRIES. MANGROVES ARE ALSO THE SPECIFIC DEFENCE FOR THE THING THIS COUNTRY'S COMMUNITIES LOSE MOST OFTEN. THIS PAYLOAD RECORDS RECLAMATION AND DREDGING TAKING SHALLOWS AND FISHING GROUNDS ALONG THIS COAST; A NATIONAL COMMITMENT TO QUADRUPLE MANGROVE COVER IS AN ARGUMENT AGAINST FILLING THE VERY SHALLOWS WHERE MANGROVES WOULD GO. THE SECOND DOCUMENT IS THE MORE POWERFUL ONE FOR ANY SHORE DISPUTE: A COASTAL RESILIENCE STRATEGY RELYING ON ADVANCED DIGITAL TERRAIN MODELS TO ASSESS SEA-LEVEL RISE SCENARIOS, SETTING OUT MORE THAN A HUNDRED AND NINETY MEASURES TO PROTECT THE COUNTRY'S COASTS, WITH A PHASED IMPLEMENTATION PLAN EXTENDING TO 2040. A HUNDRED AND NINETY NAMED MEASURES MEANS SOMEWHERE IN THAT DOCUMENT THERE IS A MEASURE FOR YOUR STRETCH OF COAST. ASKING WHICH MEASURES APPLY HERE, IN WHICH PHASE, AND WHAT THE TERRAIN MODEL SHOWS FOR THIS SHORE IS A SHARPER REQUEST THAN ANY GENERAL OBJECTION - AND THE MODELLING ALREADY EXISTS. TWO SMALLER PROGRAMMES ARE WORTH KNOWING: A PLANT ATLAS PROJECT AND A NATIONAL SEEDS CAMPAIGN LAUNCHED TO STRENGTHEN BIODIVERSITY AND SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE, ALONGSIDE EXPANDED AFFORESTATION IN COOPERATION WITH INTERNATIONAL PARTNERS. A PLANT ATLAS IS AN INVENTORY, AND THIS FILE HAS SAID REPEATEDLY THAT AN INVENTORY IS WHAT TURNS A LOVED PLACE INTO A DEFENSIBLE ONE. A COMMUNITY THAT GETS ITS OWN SPECIES RECORDED IN A NATIONAL ATLAS HAS PUT THEM ON A STATE DOCUMENT. THE ENVIRONMENT COUNCIL HAS ALSO LAUNCHED THIRTY ELECTRONIC SERVICES CONCERNED WITH THE PROTECTION OF MARINE WEALTH - WHICH IS WHERE A FISHERMAN OR A COASTAL RESIDENT SHOULD LOOK FIRST FOR A PERMIT, A REPORT OR A COMPLAINT ROUTE THAT CAN BE FILED WITHOUT ATTENDING AN OFFICE. ONE PIECE OF CONTEXT BELONGS ON THE RECORD, BECAUSE IT SHAPES EVERYTHING ELSE: THE SAME YEAR SAW MISSILE AND DRONE STRIKES ON THIS COUNTRY DAMAGE A DESALINATION PLANT, FUEL STORAGE TANKS AND AN ALUMINIUM SMELTER, ACCORDING TO A PUBLIC ENCYCLOPAEDIA'S CHRONOLOGY. ENVIRONMENTAL PLANNING IN A YEAR LIKE THAT COMPETES WITH EMERGENCY SPENDING, AND A COMMUNITY SHOULD EXPECT DELAY - BUT DAMAGE TO A DESALINATION PLANT AND A SMELTER IS ALSO AN ENVIRONMENTAL EVENT, AND ASKING WHAT WAS RELEASED AND WHAT WAS MONITORED IS A LEGITIMATE QUESTION FOR THE SAME COUNCIL. THE LIMITS: THESE ARE STATE PROGRAMMES ANNOUNCED AND REPORTED BY THE STATE - THE PLANTING FIGURE, THE ACHIEVEMENT PERCENTAGE AND THE STRATEGY'S MEASURE COUNT ALL COME FROM GOVERNMENT PORTALS AND A NEWSPAPER REPORTING OFFICIALS AND SPECIALISTS, WITH NO INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION SEEN, AND SURVIVAL RATES FOR THE SEEDLINGS ARE NOT REPORTED ANYWHERE IN WHAT WAS READ. NOTHING HERE IS A COMMUNITY ORGANISATION: HOW A CIVIL SOCIETY BODY JOINS THE INITIATIVE, WHETHER THE COASTAL STRATEGY OR THE PLANT ATLAS IS PUBLISHED IN FULL, AND WHETHER RESIDENTS MAY PROPOSE PLANTING SITES WERE ALL NOT ESTABLISHED. THIS PAYLOAD RECORDS SEPARATELY THAT INDEPENDENT ASSOCIATION IN THIS COUNTRY IS TIGHTLY CONSTRAINED, WHICH IS THE REAL LIMIT ON THE OPENING DESCRIBED ABOVE. Read it with the professional fishermen's society and the 2026 fisherman law, the environment council's complaints route, the diving and marine reporting services and the endowments directorate recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Jabatan Audit (Audit Department)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Brunei, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Brunei — Ministry of Finance & Economy (MoFE)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; MoFE (and its Treasury Department) prepares & executes the national budget, manages public finances & state stores and publishes the annual budget, Brunei Darussalam. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Brunei.

trackers.name: One Common Portal
trackers.desc: National — Registry of Companies and Business Names (ROCBN), Brunei. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Forest Act Cap. 46 — the inquiry stage is where you intervene
trackers.desc: THE RESERVATION PROCEDURE HAS A HEARING BUILT INTO IT. Chapter 46 runs: power to constitute reserved forests → notification of proposal → proclamation by the Director → inquiry by the Director → order by the Minister → notification declaring the reserved forest, published before it operates. The inquiry stage, between proclamation and the Minister's order, is where claims and objections are heard — that is the point at which an affected person intervenes. ‘Abandonment of proposal to reserve’ is a named outcome, so a proposal can lawfully be dropped. AND THE PROCESS ITSELF FREEZES ACTIVITY: new buildings and cultivation are prohibited after proclamation, before the designation is final — which cuts both ways depending on who wants to build. ONCE RESERVED: forests are classified restricted or non-restricted, entry into restricted forest is prohibited, and rights of entry may be suspended. PRIVILEGES ARE A DEFINED THING that can be granted, regulated, rescinded and modified — establish what privileges attach to your area and whether they have been altered — and they cannot be transferred. Subsidiary legislation provides privileges to natives of Brunei Darussalam, and requires no cutting without permission of the person having control of the land, use permits, licences for removing forest produce, and royalty. THE REVERSE POWER HAS A CATCH: forest may be declared no longer reserved — but the Minister must replace land that ceases to be reserved forest, so de-gazetting is not simply a subtraction.

trackers.name: Two different ‘protected’ Acts — and the six priority sites
trackers.desc: CHECK WHICH ACT SOMEONE MEANS. The Protected Areas and Protected Places Act (Cap. 147) is a security statute, not a conservation one: contravention carries 2 years' imprisonment and a $2,000 fine, and a person who fails to stop after being challenged 3 times by an authorised officer may be arrested by force. The 2004 Protected Places Order lists locations in a Schedule with plans deposited in the office of the Surveyor-General — which is where the plans are held either way. The conservation instrument is the Forest Act, Cap. 46. THE NUMBERS FOR AN ARGUMENT: forest reserves cover 235,519 ha, about 41 percent of land area, but only 17 percent of the country is officially protected — and marine protected areas remained at 0.2 percent in 2022, which is the stark gap. SIX SITES ARE IDENTIFIED AS MERITING PRIORITY ATTENTION AND CONTINUED PROTECTION: the inland forests of Ulu Temburong (Batu Apoi); the peat swamp forests of the Belait system (Ulu Mendaram); the mangroves of Brunei Bay; Tasek Merimbun; Bukit Batu-Sungei Ingei, contiguous with Gunung Mulu National Park in Sarawak; and the coastal kerangas forests. If your site is one of those six, that is a government-sourced argument. Existing protection: Ulu Temburong National Park, the first, since 1991, inside the 50,000 ha Batu Apoi reserve; three protected areas overall; and a proposed Bukit Teraja extension of 2,500 ha valued for connectivity, under the Heart of Borneo initiative.

trackers.name: No community grant window — the route is the national programme
trackers.desc: RECORDED HONESTLY: TWO ROUNDS OF SEARCHING FOUND NO DOMESTIC COMMUNITY GRANT SCHEME IN BRUNEI. Brunei is a high-income state rather than an aid recipient, GEF SGP does not cover it, and the funding architecture runs to governments and programmes, not to community applicants. So do not spend effort looking for an application window — frame a proposal as a contribution to a national programme. WHAT EXISTS: the Heart of Borneo Initiative, a voluntary transboundary cooperation with Indonesia and Malaysia, launched 27 March 2006 and declared in Bali on 12 February 2007 — signed for Brunei by the Minister of Industry and Primary Resources, not an environment ministry, which tells you where the file sits. It covers roughly 220,000 km² and provides ecological services for at least 11 million Borneans. THE ASIAN DEVELOPMENT BANK IS LEAD AGENCY FOR MOBILISING FINANCE, and the HoB project includes ‘pilot schemes for local communities to be paid for ecosystem services’ — the single community-facing element in the whole architecture. If you seek payment for conserving land, ask whether a PES pilot exists under HoB and who administers it; the answer routes through government agencies. DOMESTICALLY, the National Forestry Policy expressly recognises the role of local communities in forest management, and the Forestry Department — which also chairs the National CITES Scientific Authority — delivered 11 forest recreation parks by 1998 under the 6th National Development Plan. WATCH THE SOURCE: Heart of Borneo searches return Sarawak (Malaysian) government pages first, and Brunei's own HoB page has been archived since 2012.

trackers.name: JASTRe — Brunei's EIA authority, and an honest account of how thin participation is
trackers.desc: This is the authority, and the guidelines it publishes are the only public account of how the process runs. The Department of Environment, Parks and Recreation, under the Ministry of Development, publishes the Environmental Impact Assessment Guidelines for Brunei Darussalam, which set out the pathway: screening and then a preliminary assessment during the pre-feasibility phase, a detailed EIA study during feasibility, and environmental monitoring and post-auditing afterwards. The prescribed activities that trigger the process are annexed to the guidelines, and peer-reviewed review of the ASEAN systems counts nineteen project types for which proponents must carry out environmental impact studies. Scoping is where a resident's information is most likely to land. The guidelines state that scoping may require specific studies, data collection and analysis, field studies and consultations to determine what the significant impacts are likely to be — which is the point at which a local observation about flooding, a water source or a species has somewhere to go, before the detailed study is commissioned and its terms are fixed. Set expectations from the published research rather than from the guidelines. Peer-reviewed review of EIA practice across ASEAN records that although Brunei's rules are strict and comprehensive, public participation remains limited in practice: involvement is typically confined to social impact questionnaires and occasional communication with residents near the project, and social impact assessments are usually desktop studies using standard methodologies. Plan on supplying evidence rather than on being consulted. Two practical cautions. The published guidelines carry an October 2012 revision date, so confirm the current version and the current prescribed activities list with the Department before relying on either, and note that the Department's site serves over plain http with no TLS. This research found no independent Bruneian environmental legal or campaigning organisation on its own domain, so a community here is dealing with the Department directly rather than through anybody.

trackers.name: Town and Country Planning (Development Control) Act — permission, zoning and change of use
trackers.desc: The statute that controls what may be built is published in full, and it is the second half of the Brunei picture. The environment department assesses impacts; this Act, administered by the Department of Town and Country Planning under the Ministry of Development, regulates and controls development within designated development control areas in both urban and rural settings. Its subsidiary legislation, published by the ministry, includes regulations on the control of subdivision and consolidation of land and a set of miscellaneous provisions; the subdivision application itself calls for the lot number, the total area, the area of each proposed subdivision, particulars of existing buildings and their uses, and the proposed water supply for each subdivision — which is a description of the scheme in a public form, obtainable before anything is built. Zoning and change of use are where the argument sits. Zoning classifications govern what may be built on a given plot, and land zoned for agriculture cannot be converted to residential development without a formal change of use application. Where a proposal needs a change of use, that application is a decision point distinct from planning permission, and it can be addressed separately. Understand the tenure, because it changes what an objection is about. Ultimate ownership of land in Brunei rests with the Sultan; individuals and entities hold rights through leases or official permissions, and the government allocates and manages land. An objection is therefore rarely about one private owner's rights against a neighbour and much more often about the conditions attached to a permission the state has granted — so the conditions of the lease or permission are the document to seek. Heritage sits with a different ministry. Culturally, historically and religiously significant sites are overseen through planning legislation together with specific statutory provisions, with national heritage falling to the ministry responsible for culture, which maintains registered museums and historical landmarks. A heritage argument is addressed to a different department from a planning one, and both can be made. The Act and its subsidiary regulations are published by the Attorney General's Chambers and the Ministry of Development.

trackers.name: Law Society of Brunei Darussalam — the free legal advice clinic, the firm directory, and the route beyond the clinic
trackers.desc: The clinic publishes only two conditions, and neither is a means test. The society runs free legal advice sessions at court locations on published dates and times, and its stated requirements to apply are that the person must not already be represented by any legal firm and that a current Brunei identity card must be produced. For a country where this file has otherwise recorded only a regulator and a land statute, that is the first door a resident can walk through without money. There is a route beyond the session, and it has a named gatekeeper. Reported accounts of the clinic's revival record around a dozen legal firms volunteering their services free of charge, with senior and junior lawyers covering Syariah, civil and criminal work between them, and record that obtaining pro bono services beyond the clinic is possible but requires the approval of the society's president, assessed so that neither side takes advantage of the scheme. Ask at the session about that referral rather than treating the appointment as the end of the matter. The statutory purposes are worth quoting in a request. The order establishing the society includes protecting and assisting the public in Brunei in all matters touching or ancillary or incidental to the law, and making provision for or assisting a scheme under which impecunious persons on non-capital charges are represented by an advocate and solicitor. The represented-persons scheme is confined to criminal charges, but the public-assistance purpose is not — and a request framed on the wider purpose is asking the society to do what its own constituting instrument says it exists for. Two further things sit on the same site. A published directory of law firms, which lets a community work out who practises what before approaching anyone; and a regulation page carrying the order and the practising certificate and accounts rules, under which a compensation fund, professional indemnity and redress for inadequate professional services exist. A complaint about a lawyer therefore has a defined route as well.

trackers.name: Jabatan Tanah — certified copies of land records, the temporary occupation licence, and a published arrears list
trackers.desc: Get the certified record before arguing about the plot. The land department publishes a form for applying for a certified copy or extract of its official land records, alongside forms for updating a landowner's recorded details, for a landowner's consent to subdivision or amalgamation and to the surrender of part of a plot to the government for public use, and for leasing private land to another party. Registration under the land code rests on the grant as proof of ownership, and the department has administered that system since 1909, so the certified record is the document that settles who holds the ground and on what terms. Where the land is government land, look for the temporary occupation licence. The department publishes application and renewal forms for permission to occupy or use government land temporarily under such a licence. A community objecting to an occupation should establish whether it rests on one of these licences and when that licence falls due for renewal, because a renewal is a decision point and a licence is a shorter thing to contest than a title. The department publishes its own performance and its arrears. It puts out the applications it has received and processed with the time taken to resolve them, departmental statistics, and a list of annual land tax left unpaid from the year 2000 onwards. A published arrears list is an unusual thing to find anywhere in this research — where an occupier or developer appears on it, that is a matter of record rather than an allegation, and processing times let a community judge whether its own application is simply slow or has stalled. Where to go, and one live deadline. District land offices operate in each of the four districts, registration is being digitised through a land registration system, and the department publishes a complaints procedure together with an official channel for enquiries and complaints about its services. An amendment order to the land code also provides a twelve-month window for submitting applications, running from 1 August 2025 to 31 July 2026 — check whether anything you need falls inside it before the window closes.

trackers.name: Talian Darussalam 123 — one number, around the clock, that routes a complaint to the right agency
trackers.desc: A single number, staffed around the clock, for everything that is not an emergency. The government runs a national call centre reached on one short, easy to remember number, operating twenty-four hours a day and seven days a week for non-emergency services. Its stated purpose is to provide and direct the public to information and to the appropriate resources, and to manage requests for services and information addressed to government and to non-government services alike, so that residents, visitors and businesses have accurate, convenient and prompt access at any hour. Routing is the service, and that is the point. Across this research the commonest failure is not that a community has no case but that its complaint arrives at the wrong desk and dies there. Two entries in this file now answer that directly: the municipal application in Singapore, which routes between ten agencies and seventeen town councils, and this line, which does the same work by telephone and at any hour of the night. A community that does not know which department owns its problem is not stopped by not knowing. Where the matter is land, there is a departmental channel as well. The land department publishes its own official channel for enquiries and complaints about its services, so a question about registration, a temporary occupation licence or a survey goes there directly; the national line is for the cases where it is genuinely unclear whose matter it is, or where a first approach has gone nowhere. And one live deadline sits on the same page. The land department repeats on its own front page that the amendment to the land code provides a twelve month window for submitting applications, running from 1 August 2025 to 31 July 2026. Read this with the land records and scientific services entries already recorded for this country: the registry says who holds the ground, the laboratory says what is in the water, and this is the number to call when it is not clear who should be told.

trackers.name: Green Brunei and the Brunei Nature Society — the two civil bodies working on nature, and what each actually does
trackers.desc: A registered social enterprise, working with government rather than against it. Green Brunei is a social enterprise registered under a trading name and established in 2012, working on environmental sustainability through education, conservation and advocacy with a focus on young people, run by a team with more than twenty volunteers. Its own account describes working with government agencies, educational institutions, private sector partners and the general public, running environmental camps, ambassador programmes, field trips and an annual race, and supporting national environmental policy. That posture is the shape civil society takes in this country, and it is worth understanding before an approach: this is a partner to institutions, not an opponent of them. It publishes a running count of what it has done. Its front page carries figures for trees planted, events held, people engaged and waste collected, with a date of last update. An organisation that publishes its own numbers can be asked to stand behind them, and it is the second such published ledger recorded in this file after the Maldivian campaign's dated public record. A second body holds the natural history. The nature society is described as studying and promoting interest in the environment and natural history of the country through monthly lectures, organised nature outings and educational programmes, keeping a natural history library, and running a biodiversity conservation programme supporting threatened species. For a community that needs to establish what actually lives on a site before a project reaches it, a society with a library and a species programme is the nearer expertise — recorded here on third party description and worth confirming directly. Know what neither of them is. Neither body is a litigator or a land-holding trust, and this research has found no organisation in this country that buys land or takes cases. The formal weight sits with the state routes already recorded here — the land records, the accredited laboratories, the assessment route, the legal advice clinic and the national complaints line — and these two are where the knowledge and the volunteers are.

trackers.name: ROCBN — where a Brunei company's record sits, and what is not publicly searchable
trackers.desc: Where the record is kept. The registry of companies and business names sits under the finance and economy ministry and holds company incorporations and business name registrations, with its corporate registry system reached through the government's single business portal, which also carries filing updates, annual declarations and corporate tax returns. The division publishes downloadable registration forms and its own telephone, fax and email contacts, and the government service listing records the portal as the one stop route for starting a business. What this research could not establish is a free public search. Access to the registry system runs through a portal login, published guides record that the fees for registry search outputs are not set out in English-language documentation, and commercial providers sell company search reports sourced from this registry. This entry says so rather than implying a lookup that may not be open to the public: the practical route is to write or telephone the division and ask what a member of the public may obtain about a named company and at what cost, and to record the answer. Two structural cautions before relying on a registration. The registry also holds companies incorporated under the international business companies framework, which carries lighter public disclosure than an ordinary domestic company; and an entity operating in financial services is licensed separately by the monetary authority, so appearing in the registry is not the same as holding the licence its activity requires. Ask which framework a company sits in before drawing conclusions from what the register shows. Carry the registration number. It is stable through name changes and restructuring, which matters in a jurisdiction where a public name search may not be available to test a name against. Read this with the land records, the accredited laboratories, the national call centre and the civil society entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Tender notices in the government newspaper — weekly, with a set content list and a published debarment policy
trackers.desc: The notice board is a weekly newspaper, and its contents are prescribed. The finance and economy ministry's account of the procurement process states that a tender notice is published in English and Malay in the official government newspaper, and that the notice contains the procuring entity, a description of the products, services or works to be procured, the tender opening and closing dates and the venue for collecting the tender documents. Tender notices and quotation notices are published weekly, and some ministries and departments also publish their notices on their own websites. For a community, that means a fixed weekly place to look and a known list of what each notice must say. The rules themselves are published. The designated publications for this country's procurement rules include the state tenders board's general information, the 1983 financial regulation and a series of finance ministry circulars, along with the newspaper's tender advertisement listing. The procedure a project should have followed is therefore readable in advance rather than inferred afterwards. There is a published debarment policy. Among those same designated publications is the debarment policy — the basis on which a contractor can be excluded from government work. That gives a community a precise question to put: whether the contractor on the ground has ever been debarred, and under which provision. No other procurement entry recorded in this file names a published debarment rule. Above a threshold, a board decision exists. Reported accounts describe procurements above a stated value as requiring the approval of the state tenders board, with small and medium purchases handled by direct purchase or by quotation. Where a project sits above that line there is a board decision behind it, which is a different document from the notice and a different addressee from the procuring department. Read this with the land records, the accredited laboratories, the national routing line and the company registry entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Prevention of Corruption Act and the Anti-Corruption Bureau — informer protection written into the statute
trackers.desc: Informer protection is a section of the act, not a policy. The prevention of corruption act, published in full by the attorney general's chambers, contains provisions on the protection of informers, and alongside them an offence of disclosing the identity of a person being investigated. For anybody weighing whether to report what they have seen on a project, the confidentiality question is answered in the statute itself rather than in an assurance from an official, and those sections are worth reading before a decision is made. The mirror provision is an offence of false reporting. The same act makes it an offence to make a false report of the commission of an offence. A complaint should therefore be built on what can be shown — dates, documents, sums, names — rather than on what is suspected, and that discipline also makes the complaint harder to dismiss. The investigative powers are specific enough to matter. The act provides for special powers of investigation, a legal obligation to give information, restriction on the disposal of property, surrender of travel documents, evidence of pecuniary resources or property, a presumption of corruption in certain cases, and makes offences under it seizable. Where money or property connected with a project is moving quickly, the restriction on disposal of property is the provision that matters most, and it is worth naming when reporting. The bureau that enforces it. The anti-corruption bureau is an autonomous body established under the act in 1982 to investigate and prevent corruption across both the public and private sectors, with published contact details and reporting channels including an online route for submitting information. Read this with the tender notices and published debarment policy, the land records and the company registry entries already recorded for this country: the debarment policy answers whether a contractor may still bid, and this answers who investigates how it came to be chosen.

trackers.name: Audit Department — reports laid before the Legislative Council, and not released to the public
trackers.desc: Answering the auditor is legally compulsory. The audit act, published in full by the attorney general's chambers, sets out the auditor general's duties, the nature of the audit and the powers attaching to it, and provides that every person called upon for explanations or information is legally bound to furnish it; the auditor general may also authorise officers in writing to exercise those powers on his behalf. An audit is therefore a process that can compel answers from the people running a project, which is more than most of the routes recorded for this country can do. Reports are laid before the Legislative Council. The act's audit reports provision requires reports relating to the accounts of the country to be laid before the Legislative Council at its next meeting. That is the route by which audit findings become visible: the Council's proceedings, rather than any publication by the department itself. The department does not release its reports to the public. A published profile of the institution records that it audits entities owned or managed by the government and the government's own finances, that it may demand all the financial records of the bodies it audits and may take testimony from experts, that it conducts financial, performance, compliance and information systems audits — and also that it has no power to seal, does not conduct interim audits, and cannot present its audit reports to the public or to the media. That is the opposite of what this file records for Bhutan and Macau, and it decides where a community should look. So look at the Council, not the department. Where an audit of a project or an agency exists, the document a community can reach is the one laid before the Legislative Council, and the questions asked about it there. Read this with the weekly tender notices and the published debarment policy, the prevention of corruption act and bureau, the land records and the company registry entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Health ministry laboratories — accredited environmental testing open to the public, and the laboratory supplies the containers
trackers.desc: The laboratory supplies the containers, and refuses samples sent in anything else. The health ministry's environment laboratory offers chemical analytical services on raw and treated water and other environmental samples, examining their properties, compositions, contaminants and residues — and states plainly that clients should consult the laboratory before sending any samples, that it will provide the sampling containers and the forms once the client agrees to its procedures, and that samples arriving in other containers will not be accepted. The first call is therefore to the laboratory, not to the tap; sending a bottle first is the commonest way a community's evidence is thrown out before anyone looks at the result. It says it serves the public, and it covers environmental samples. The department of scientific services provides laboratory services through scientific analysis and calibration and states that it supplies those services to government agencies and law enforcement agencies as well as to the public. Alongside the water and environmental chemistry laboratory, a branch laboratory offers microbiological analysis of water and environmental samples, together with food, pharmaceuticals and cosmetics, for microbial content and pathogens. For a community that would otherwise have no testing route at all, that is the door. The accreditation is published, and so is its absence. The health science laboratories have been accredited to the international standard for the competence of testing and calibration laboratories, and the published scope marks which parameters fall outside that accreditation — which is the distinction that decides whether a result can be relied on in a formal complaint or only in an argument. Ask for the scope, not merely for confirmation that the laboratory is accredited. The parameter list is published, so a request can be specific. The department publishes what it measures in water, including pH, conductivity, free and total chlorine and further chemical parameters, so a community can name the determinands it wants rather than asking for a general test and accepting whatever comes back. Read this with the environmental assessment authority, the forest reserve categories, the pollution reporting line and the geoportal entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Geoportal Ukur — the cadastre, the land use master plan, and lots subdivided but not yet registered
trackers.desc: The zoning and the cadastre sit on one public map. The survey department's geoportal lets members of the public view and search surveyed cadastral information for lots, temporary occupation licences and gazetted areas at scales from one in a thousand to one in nine thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine, and view the town and country planning department's national land use master plan and district plan. What a plot is zoned for, and where its boundary runs, can therefore be established from one screen rather than from two counters in two ministries. Lots that have been subdivided but not yet registered are visible, and that is an early warning. The portal shows subdivided or consolidated surveyed lots which have not been registered with the lands department. Survey precedes registration and registration precedes any announcement, so a new subdivision appearing on this map is often the earliest public sign that something is planned for a piece of ground — months before a notice, a tender or a clearance application makes it official. Imagery and terrain, with a registration threshold in between. Public users can overlay satellite imagery and orthophotos at fifty centimetre resolution and open street map layers; registered users additionally get orthophotos at nineteen centimetres, contours at two metre and ten metre intervals, the exclusive economic zone and territorial waters, and the lands department's unsurveyed temporary occupation licences. Two-metre contours are what settle an argument about drainage or a cut into a slope, so registering is worth the trouble before a dispute rather than during one. Certified plans can be bought through it. The portal sells survey products including certified plans and survey sheets, and carries control points, roads and the names of districts, mukims and kampungs — so a community can move from looking at a boundary to holding a certified document of it without a separate journey. Read this with the land department entry recording certified copies and temporary occupation licences, the planning and development control act, the environment authority and the weekly tender notice entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Valuers and Estate Agents Order and the acquisition statute — who may value, the numbers that must appear on the report, and the assessors
trackers.desc: Valuation is a registered profession here, with a board and a register. The order of 2009 as amended and revised establishes a board of valuers and estate agents, and provides for the appointment and duties of a registrar, for certificates of registration, for who is eligible to be registered as a valuer and as an estate agent, for practice by a partnership or body corporate, and for cancellation, suspension and reprimand, removal from the register and reinstatement, with penalties for offences including offences by bodies corporate. The land department's own valuation section directs anyone wanting the list of registered valuers and estate agent firms to the board's website. Checking that list before instructing anyone, and again before accepting a report produced by the other side, is the first move. Two numbers must appear on every appraisal report. Officials have stated publicly that every registered practitioner is required to include their registration certificate number and their practising certificate number on all appraisal reports and property marketing advertisements, and that operating unregistered carries a fine of up to five thousand dollars with a further five hundred dollars for each day a continuing offence persists. A valuation report that does not carry those two numbers is therefore a document to question on its face, before any argument about the figure inside it. The acquisition statute sets out how compensation is decided. Its provisions cover the matters to be considered and the matters to be disregarded in determining compensation, the rules as to the amount, the recording of assessors' opinions and what happens where opinions differ, assessors' fees, the requirement that the award be in writing, costs, appeal to the Court of Appeal, and the payment of interest on excess compensation. Knowing that assessors' opinions are recorded, and that the award must be written, tells an owner exactly which documents to ask for. Two provisions to read before anything else. The statute provides for temporary occupation of waste or arable land, with a route for disputes as to the condition of the land, and — importantly — it bars suits to set aside awards. That bar is precisely why the appeal route and the recorded assessor opinions matter: the challenge has to be made through the machinery the statute provides rather than by a separate action afterwards. Read this with the land department's certified copies and temporary occupation licences, the planning and development control act, the law society's free clinic and the survey geoportal entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Majlis Perundingan Mukim dan Kampung — the grassroots council, and the published directory of who leads your mukim
trackers.desc: There is a published directory of who to speak to. District offices publish lists of the names and addresses of the mukim heads and village heads in their district, with a stated update date, and a district office section exists specifically to administer the mukim and village institutions and to coordinate their activities. The country is divided into four districts, each into mukim and each mukim into villages, all falling under the district office of the district concerned, and the mukim and village are described as the principal grassroots institution. The first practical step here is therefore identifying your own mukim head and village head by name — and that list is published rather than something to be asked for. The consultative council is the body they lead. Each mukim or village generally has a consultative council, whose published objectives are to strengthen the effectiveness of the institution of the mukim head and village head as the core of grassroots leadership, to foster good citizenship in support of the national leadership, and to plan and undertake plans for the welfare of the people and residents. That third objective is the one a community with a project on its doorstep should be quoting. The chain of control is stated. A governing board appointed by the Sultan oversees the consultative councils, its membership including four members appointed from among the advisers of the mukim consultative councils, with the power, management and control over the councils exercised by that board through the home affairs ministry as its secretariat and through the district offices. Knowing that the chain runs from the council to the district office and then to the ministry tells a resident where a matter travels next, and who is above the person refusing it. The village headship is filled by nomination and vote. Published rules and reporting record candidates being nominated on a form signed by a proposer and two supporters, endorsed by the mukim head as confirmation of consent, and submitted to the district officer before the closing date, with nominations after that date invalid, and with voting events organised by the district office. A council seat and a village headship are contestable positions rather than fixed ones. Read this with the town and country planning act, the environmental authority, the survey geoportal and the law society's free legal advice entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Antiquities and Treasure Trove Act — the pre-1894 test, declaration by order with limits, and twenty-seven gazetted sites
trackers.desc: The test is a date, and it reaches beyond buildings. The Act provides for the control and preservation of ancient and historical monuments, archaeological sites and remains and antiquities. An ancient monument is defined as any monument in the country which dates, or may reasonably be believed to date, from a period before the first of January 1894, together with any other monument declared under the Act to be one; and an antiquity is defined to include any object movable or immovable, or any part of the soil or of the bed of a river or lake or of the sea, which was constructed, shaped, inscribed, erected, excavated or otherwise produced or modified by human agency before that date or reasonably believed to be before it. A shaped piece of ground, a riverbed feature or a worked stone can therefore qualify — not only a standing building — which widens what a community can point at. Declaration is by order, and the limits are fixed in the same instrument. The Act empowers a declaration by order that any monument is an ancient monument and any site a historical site, and the determination of the limits of that monument or site. Where a project is adjacent rather than on top of a protected place, the limits clause is the one that decides the argument: ask what limits were determined in the order, and get a copy of the order rather than a description of it. Twenty-seven sites are gazetted, on stated criteria. Reported ministerial answers in the legislature record twenty-seven gazetted historic sites — fifteen monuments, sites and buildings and twelve royal mausoleums — recognised on the basis of historical, architectural, cultural and economic value, and record that not all of those buildings are administered by the museums department but that all remain subject to the Act. Being outside the department's day-to-day administration therefore does not put a site outside the statute, which is worth knowing when an owner or occupier claims otherwise. Who administers it, and what the Act does not do. The museums department administers the Act, with a museum board of nine members drawn from various government departments and chaired by the permanent secretary for culture. The Act itself records two limits: nothing in that Part authorises the infringement of any private right or the contravention of any other written law in force, and neither the board nor the government incurs liability for loss or damage arising in the course of a licensed excavation merely because the licence was granted. Read this with the town and country planning act, the environmental authority, the survey geoportal and the mukim and village council entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Forest reserve classification and the wildlife statutes — five categories of reserve, and the penalties for taking anything out of one
trackers.desc: Land inside a forest reserve is classified into five categories, and the category decides what may happen there. The forestry legislation of 1934 allows land within forest reserves to be placed in five categories: protection forest, conservation area, recreational area, production area and national park. For a community, the classification is the lever rather than the reserve boundary itself: land in a production area is being managed for timber output, while protection forest and conservation area carry the strictest purposes, and asking which category a particular compartment falls in is a more precise question than asking whether it is protected. Published accounts record that forest reserves comprise all the designated protected areas in the country, and that proposals have been made to extend protected areas so as to connect an existing protection forest to a neighbouring conservation forest holding one of the island's last intact peat swamp forests. Taking forest products without permission carries heavy penalties. Ministerial answers in the legislature record that harvesting forest products without permission is an offence subject to severe legal action, with a compound fine of one thousand dollars for unauthorised possession and, for harvesting inside a forest reserve, a fine of up to five hundred thousand dollars or five years' imprisonment or both; and that enforcement of the flora and fauna protection laws is carried out in collaboration with the armed forces and the police. Those figures are worth knowing because they are what a report of unlicensed clearing inside a reserve is measured against. Two further statutes cover wildlife and trade. The wild animal protection legislation regulates the hunting, possession and trade of wildlife species, and the wild flora and fauna order of 2007 serves as the national legislation under the international convention on trade in endangered species, to which the country has been a party since 1990, providing for the protection of wild flora and fauna. The agriculture department is named as the national management authority for that convention with the legal mandate to enforce the order, while the forestry department enforces it in the field. Where a project threatens a species rather than a place, that is the second line of argument and it sits with a different department. Where the texts are. The forestry department publishes the forest legislation and its related instruments on its own site, so the statute, the order and the list of related legislation can be read directly rather than through summaries. Read this with the environmental assessment authority, the town and country planning permission route, the two civil conservation bodies and the geoportal entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Land acquisition procedure — six weeks to require a reference to the court, and four things the objection can be about
trackers.desc: Six weeks from the award, and the clock depends on whether you were there. The acquisition statute allows a person interested to apply to the land officer requiring that the matter be referred to the court for determination. The application must state the grounds on which the objection to the award is taken, and it must be made within six weeks from the date of the land officer's award where the person was present or represented before the officer when the award was made; in other cases within six weeks of receiving the copy of the award, or within six months of the date of the award, whichever period expires first. Attending the award therefore shortens nothing and being absent does not lengthen the time indefinitely — but the two clocks run differently, and which one applies is decided by whether anyone was there on the day. The objection can be about four different things. The statute lets the objection go to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the persons to whom it is payable, or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested. A community losing land collectively, or a household whose tenant or heir also has a claim, is often arguing about the third and fourth of those rather than the second, and the grounds stated in the application should say which. The court sits with assessors, and the statute lists what counts. The reference procedure provides for the land officer's statement to the court, service of notice, and the appointment of assessors whose opinions are recorded and whose difference of opinion is provided for; and it sets out, in separate provisions, the matters to be considered in determining compensation and the matters to be disregarded, together with rules as to the amount. Reading those two lists before drafting an objection tells a claimant which arguments the court is permitted to hear. An appeal lies to the court of appeal, and interest is payable on compensation the court finds should have been higher. The rest of the sequence, and the provision that closes it. The Act runs from the power to enter and survey, through the declaration that land is required for a public purpose, the making of a plan and the giving of notices, the power to require statements of names and interests, the land officer's inquiry and award, the power to take possession and the entries made in the register; payment or deposit in court and interest follow, and separate provisions deal with the temporary occupation of waste or arable land and with disputes as to the condition of land returned. The government is not bound to complete an acquisition it has begun, and suits to set aside awards are barred — which is why the six-week reference is the route rather than a fresh action. Read this with the valuers and estate agents register, the land department's certified copies, the survey geoportal and the town and country planning entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Skim Tanah Kurnia Rakyat Jati — a land lot for citizens with none, the village head's certification, and what cancels the application
trackers.desc: A citizen without land can be granted a lot to build on. Alongside the national housing scheme, which allots built houses, the land scheme for citizens allots the land itself: successful applicants are granted a lot by government on which to build their own house. The housing development department publishes the forms, the counters at which they are available and the documents required, so the route is a form and a checklist rather than a negotiation. For a household displaced from land it never held on paper, this is the state's own answer to landlessness. The village head certifies the application. The application form requires the penghulu or village head to certify that the applicant lives in the mukim or village under their charge and that the particulars given are true. That signature is the local gatekeeper of the process, which means the village head is the first person to approach, not the last. The form also asks directly whether the applicant and spouse own titled land or land held on a temporary occupation licence — the distinction between the two is what determines eligibility. What cancels an application, stated on the form itself. The declarations record that if the applicant or the spouse ceases to meet the eligibility conditions the application is automatically cancelled; and that if the applicant or spouse is found to own titled land, to have bought a house or land lot through a financial institution, or to have received a private land lot or house, the application is cancelled and eligibility ends. A family weighing a private purchase while an application is pending should read that clause before signing anything. Getting the grant document afterwards. The department sets out the procedure for issuing the land grant: complete the grant issuance form for the housing and land schemes, available at department counters and branches, and submit it with the required documents to the address for the housing area concerned. The documents listed include copies of the original owner's and spouse's identity cards, a death certificate where an owner has died, the new owner's card where a lot or house has been transferred, a clear housing loan repayment statement, the transfer permission letter where one exists, and a copy of the land grant as registered by the land department. Read this with the land department's certified copies and temporary occupation licence entry, the village consultative council, the survey geoportal and the acquisition procedure entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The Scoop — the country's independent digital newsroom, self-funded, no paywall, founded by four journalists
trackers.desc: An independent newsroom in a place with very few of them. Launched in September 2017, the outlet describes itself as a platform for independent journalism focused on telling thoughtful stories about the people, trends and issues shaping the country. It is published by a company founded by four journalists and describes itself as the country's first and only female-led newsroom and media company. It is financed primarily through advertising revenue and states that it does not receive funding from government or any other political or economic interest group, and it runs without a paywall on the stated view that everyone deserves equal access to accurate news. For a community with a local grievance, that is the one address in the country that is neither a state outlet nor a foreign correspondent passing through. It was founded to fill a gap, and it says so. Reporting on its founding records that the idea came from the founders' frustration that no outlet had emerged to fill the void left when the country's best-known English-language daily closed, and that they chose to self-fund rather than find an investor specifically in order to maintain editorial independence. The same account records that the outlet started with people-driven narratives and moved into harder news as its audience formed, and describes a media environment in which self-censorship is widely practised and outlets typically avoid certain subjects. That last point is the honest limit on this entry: an independent newsroom in a constrained environment can carry a documented, specific story more easily than a confrontational one. What it is set up to do. It describes itself as not a daily, choosing instead to explain the news reflectively, and it publishes across news, commentary and culture with a small permanent staff and a wider group of contributors. Its editor's own reporting has covered environmental and human rights subjects alongside diplomacy and security, and she has filed for international wire services and newspapers — which matters for a community whose story may need to travel beyond the country. How to approach it. Bring the document rather than the grievance: the notice, the plan, the correspondence, the dates. A small self-funded newsroom cannot run a long investigation on an unsupported claim, but it can report what a document says. Read this with the village consultative council, the land department's certified copies, the forest reserve classification and the land scheme entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Where money for community work actually comes from here — the royal foundation, the welfare system and corporate CSR through the mukim
trackers.desc: There is no environmental grant fund here of the kind found elsewhere in the region, and it is better to say so. The funding routes that exist are welfare and charitable rather than conservation-specific, and a community organising against a project should plan its budget around that. Published overviews record that alongside government schemes, non-governmental bodies including the royal foundation, an orphans' fund, the Islamic religious council, voluntary organisations and banking institutions contribute actively to community needs. The royal foundation is the largest single channel, and its remit includes development. Established in October 1992 as the channel for charitable endowments by the Sultan and members of the royal family, the foundation is described as operating on five principles: education, welfare, religion, development and finance, and among other things it awards houses to people who cannot afford a permanent home. Development sits inside that remit, which is the opening for a proposal framed around a village's own capacity rather than around opposition to a project. Individual hardship runs through a single national system. The national welfare system brings the welfare schemes together in one place for the public to apply for assistance, backed by a centralised database; applications are processed by the relevant agencies, which then investigate whether the applicant is eligible. For a household displaced or damaged by a project, that is the route for the individual claim, separate from anything the community does collectively. Corporate money reaches communities through the mukim, not through open calls. Reported corporate responsibility activity in this country runs to named mukim communities and to non-governmental organisations directly — one gas company's contribution of equipment to communities and NGOs in a named mukim being handed over at a local club with the mukim's penghulu present. The practical implication is that the approach for corporate support goes through the village and mukim structures recorded elsewhere in this country's entries, not through an application portal. Read this with the village consultative council, the land scheme for citizens, the two civil environmental bodies and the free legal advice clinic entries already recorded here.

trackers.name: Judiciary judgments — written decisions with subject headnotes, a judgment search, and an email route for decisions not yet listed
trackers.desc: The courts publish written decisions with subject headnotes attached. The judiciary's judgments page lists decisions by date and court — High Court and Court of Appeal — with the outcome noted and a bracketed headnote setting out the legal subjects the decision turned on. The listed civil examples include an appeal against an order for sale in respect of memoranda of charge over two parcels of land and the units built on them, and a costs decision where damages were awarded but the claimant was held partly contributorily negligent. Those headnotes are what let a reader tell in seconds whether a decision is about land, security over land, costs or procedure. The site says the collection is still being built, and invites requests. The judiciary states that the page carries written decisions delivered by the courts, that content building is ongoing, and that readers may email if they wish specific decisions to be listed. That is an unusually direct route: where a judgment a community needs is not on the site, the publisher has invited the request rather than requiring a formal application. There is also a judgment search page on the same site. Two older collections fill part of the gap. Published library guidance records that the judiciary's open-access judgments site carries full-text criminal and civil decisions from 2009 onwards, that an open-access Commonwealth legal information platform holds selected decisions of the High Court since 1987 with search, case name search and alphabetical browsing, and that commercial databases hold the law reports series and unreported decisions. Start with the judiciary site, then the Commonwealth platform, before considering anything paid. Why precedent matters here. The same guidance records that where there is no written law on a matter the courts turn to case law and judicial precedent, that decisions of higher courts bind lower courts, and that decisions of superior courts in comparable jurisdictions are persuasive but not binding. For a community, that means a judgment from a neighbouring common law jurisdiction can be argued, but a local decision is worth more. Read this with the acquisition procedure entry, the land department's certified copies, the law society's free legal advice clinic and the forest reserve classification entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Societies Act — registration before any collective activity, no outside affiliation, and the Registrar's power to call for accounts
trackers.desc: A group that wants to hold money must be a registered society first. The societies legislation, in its revised edition published by the attorney general's chambers, provides for registration by the Registrar, sets out the Registrar's power to make inquiries, the grounds of refusal to register, and — in terms — the consequences of non-registration. It also covers cancellation of registration and its consequences, change of place of business, suspension of activities, the Registrar's power to make orders, the furnishing of information and orders of dissolution, the persons responsible for supplying information, and the establishment of a branch with the society's liability for contracts entered into by that branch. For a community group, registration is not paperwork that follows the campaign; it precedes lawful collective activity. Affiliation outside the country is prohibited. The Act carries an express provision prohibiting affiliation outside the country, which matters directly where an international organisation offers to take a local group under its wing — an arrangement that is ordinary elsewhere in this file and is not available here. Structure the relationship with an outside funder as a grant to a locally registered society, not as membership or affiliation. The Registrar can call for accounts. Provisions in the societies legislation include the Registrar's power to call for accounts and to summon witnesses, powers of entry and search in respect of unlawful societies, prosecutions, forfeiture of seized articles, and penalties for managing or participating in an unlawful society or allowing premises to be used for its meetings. Keep the books in a state where they can be produced. The Minister may declare a society unlawful. The legislation empowers the minister responsible for home affairs, where he considers it essential in the public interest, to declare unlawful by public notification any society which in his opinion is being used or likely to be used for intimidation, extortion or any other unlawful purpose, or for a purpose incompatible with the peace, good order or welfare of the country, or is being used for purposes at variance with its professed objects. That last limb is the one to note: a society whose stated objects are conservation should conduct itself within them. Read this with the village consultative council, the land scheme for citizens, the funding routes through the royal foundation and mukim, and the judgments entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The courts, the published fee scale, and the honest limits of legal aid
trackers.desc: Court fees are published, and the fee scale tells you which court a claim belongs in. The judiciary publishes its court fees, recording that high court suits are administered under the supreme court legislation and hear civil claims above a stated threshold, that intermediate court suits are administered under separate legislation covering claims between stated limits, and that all services are charged at the standard rate prescribed in a named appendix to the supreme court legislation. A community can therefore work out, before instructing anyone, which court its claim falls into and what filing will cost. The judiciary's own pages record that the subordinate court hears civil and criminal cases, road traffic offences, small claims and youth cases, publish annual case figures for each court, and carry written decisions delivered by the courts alongside practice directions and circulars — with an invitation to email if a specific decision is wanted, an unusually direct route to a judgment. Legal aid is narrow, and saying so is the useful part. Reporting records that the legal aid framework administered by the supreme court provides assistance only in cases carrying the death penalty, assigned to members of the law society on a rotational basis. A community in a land or planning dispute should not plan around state legal aid; the law society's free advice service already recorded in this file is the realistic first stop. A society-run fund exists, with its scope stated. The same reporting records the law society launching a pilot legal aid fund for people who cannot afford representation in criminal cases, targeted at five areas — theft, attempted suicide, infanticide, offences involving young persons, and cases where defendants are intellectually challenged or suffering mental illness — created after talks with a supportive judiciary to give structure and accountability. It records that the fund was initially for criminal cases where the defendant wishes to plead guilty and needs counsel for mitigation or plea bargaining, that trial work was excluded on cost grounds, that other criminal or civil cases would be considered case by case, and that syariah cases are not eligible because syariah attorneys belong to a different association. Ask on a case-by-case basis rather than assuming exclusion. Read this with the law society's free advice clinic, the village consultative council, the societies registration and the judgment request entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Environmental Protection and Management Order — a general duty on every person, prescribed activities that must be notified in writing, and the stop-work order
trackers.desc: The Order binds the Government, and that is stated in its second section. The 2016 order, made under the constitution and published in the gazette, applies to the whole territory, is expressed as an order to provide for the protection and management of the environment, and provides that it binds the Government subject to a stated exception. A community objecting to a public works project is therefore not arguing against an instrument that exempts the state. The general duty is on every person, and breaching it is an offence. The order provides that it is the duty of every person to take, so far as is reasonably practicable, such measures to ensure the protection and management of the environment and the prevention, reduction or control of any potential hazard that may cause pollution or damage to the environment, and to comply with the order's requirements; and it makes breach of that duty an offence. That duty is the sentence to quote in a complaint letter about an operator who is doing nothing unlawful in any narrower sense. Prescribed activities require written notification, and the schedules list them. The order requires written notification for undertaking prescribed activities, with two schedules setting out the prescribed activities themselves and the details required in the written notification; published summaries record the listed activities as including agriculture and farming, aviation including airport development and airline operations, and land reclamation, including coastal and river reclamation. Ask whether the notification for a prescribed activity was given, and what it contained. The powers include stopping work, and there is an appeal against that. The order's arrangement of sections records powers of inspection; entry, search and seizure; taking samples; directing; examining and securing attendance; remediation of land; issuing a remedial order or a stop-work order; appeal from such an order; and arrest — alongside parts on investigation of environmental incidents, offences and penalties, and codes of practice. Published descriptions record the authority using inspection, entry, seizure of evidence and sampling for analysis, with routine and targeted inspections in industrial zones and public areas to detect unauthorised discharges or improper hazardous waste handling, and record public reporting mechanisms within the zero-burning policy. The remedial order is the outcome to ask for, because it requires the party to put the damage right rather than merely pay. Read this with the assessment authority entry, the complaint line, the health ministry laboratories and the forest reserve classification entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Water Supply Act — catchment survey, pollution of the waterworks as an offence, and the honest gap in water quality law
trackers.desc: The Act opens with catchment areas, and that part is the one to cite about a project upstream. The water supply legislation, published in the revised edition by the attorney general's chambers, is arranged with a preliminary part, then a part devoted to catchment areas containing the survey of catchment areas, before the parts on administration and the water authority's general and particular powers. Those later parts include custody and administration of waterworks, appointment of officers, supply of water, power to enter on land for the purposes of constructing, repairing or maintaining mains and waterworks, power to lay water mains and to fix standpipes and fire hydrants, and powers to restrict or suspend supply. A community asking what protects the catchment its supply comes from has a named statutory heading to ask about. Polluting the waterworks is a listed offence. The same arrangement of sections lists pollution of the waterworks, water from an unauthorised service, taking water contrary to agreement, penalty for obstructing the water authority in its duty, altering a service and fraudulent conduct, alongside measurement of water supplied, disconnection of an inside service and restriction on the use of hydrants. Where a development is discharging into or interfering with a supply system, the offence exists and can be named in a complaint. The gap is documented, and worth knowing before relying on this Act. Published legal commentary records that none of this country's laws on water quality and pollution is specifically addressed to protecting water quality, the water supply legislation existing only to provide for the control and regulation of the supply of water; and records that sea pollution is covered separately by a 2005 order giving effect to the international convention on pollution from ships and related agreements, with the territorial definition covering the whole sea within the seaward limits of the territorial waters and all other waters including inland waters. For water quality itself, pair this with the environmental protection order already recorded in this bucket, whose general duty and prescribed activities reach discharges. The scale of the resource is small, which sharpens the point. Published research records two dams with a combined storage capacity of forty-five million cubic metres, one reservoir used for supply with a catchment of a few square kilometres and the other regulating a named river with a catchment of some twenty-nine square kilometres, with urban supply derived entirely from surface water and the largest industrial abstraction taken and treated from a named river. Read this with the environmental protection order, the assessment authority, the health ministry laboratories and the forest reserve entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Fisheries Order 2009 — marine reserves and marine parks, licences for appliances and culture systems, and the bans on explosives, poisons and prohibited gear
trackers.desc: The Order provides for establishing marine reserves and marine parks, and the section headings show what else it controls. The 2009 fisheries order, published in the gazette, carries provisions on fisheries plans; applications for and renewal, issue, conditions, validity, cancellation and suspension of licences; fishing appliances; marine culture systems; operation of fishing vessels; refusal to grant or renew; fishing using foreign fishing vessels; innocent passage through the country's waters; establishment of lobster fishing areas, and establishment of marine reserves and marine parks, with restrictions in relation to those areas; the offence of doing certain acts without a licence; promotion and management of inland fisheries; and orders of court with respect to cancellation of a licence. A published summary records that the director must prepare fisheries plans designed to ensure the optimum utilisation of fishery resources, and that licences are required to operate or possess fishing appliances, to operate or establish marine culture systems, to use fishing vessels, and to hold or organise sports fishing events. Ask which licence a coastal operation holds, and whether a fisheries plan covers the area. The destructive-method bans are specific. Published description of the Order records that it is prohibited to use, carry or possess any explosive, poison, pollutant or other noxious substance, apparatus, prohibited gear or any other thing for the purpose of killing, stunning, disabling or catching fish, or in any way rendering fish more easily caught; that fishing for lobsters without a licence or during a declared closed time is prohibited; that possessing or receiving fish of a species prohibited under the international endangered species convention is an offence; and that no person may fish for, disturb, harass, catch, sell or otherwise take any aquatic mammal found in these waters. Those words — disturb and harass — reach conduct short of catching. A protected area network already exists, with numbers attached. Published description of the fisheries department's work records that under this Order it manages fishery resources through marine protected areas, fishing zonation and moratoriums; that in 2015 it established a marine protected area network covering just over twelve hundred square kilometres, designating named coral reef sites as no-take zones where fishing is prohibited; and that complementary measures include mesh size requirements for trawlers, the bans on explosives and poisons, and artificial reef deployment from 2020 to rehabilitate degraded sites. Read this with the forest reserve classification, the environmental protection order, the water supply catchment and the assessment authority entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Wild Life Protection Act — wildlife sanctuaries that can be declared even inside a protected or reserved forest, the game officer's powers, and the penalties recorded for taking forest produce
trackers.desc: A wildlife sanctuary can be declared even inside a protected or reserved forest. The wild life protection legislation, published in the consolidated laws, provides for the protection of wildlife, setting restrictions on hunting seasons, animal age ranges and hunting methods, and establishes wildlife sanctuaries even in a protected or reserved forest, with the Game Officer vested with powers of control and supervision of compliance. Where a forest already carries a reserve classification, a sanctuary declaration on top of it is therefore available rather than excluded — and the Game Officer is a named post to write to. Capture, killing and export are prohibited, against a list. Published legal description records that under this Act capture and killing for flesh, trade and similar purposes is prohibited and export strictly regulated, with a list of protected animals; other published material records that the Act prohibits hunting, capturing or trading protected species without government authorisation, creates penalties of fines and imprisonment, provides for protected areas where biodiversity can be safeguarded, and contains provisions on managing wildlife habitats. Establishing that a species on the site is on that list changes the question from planning to prohibition. Trade in listed species runs through a separate order, enforced by a named department. Reporting of a legislative council session records that the wild animal protection legislation regulates the hunting, possession and trade of wildlife species, that the forestry department enforces the 2007 wild flora and fauna order in line with the international endangered species convention, and that enforcement of flora and fauna protection involves the armed forces and the police. The forest penalties are stated, and they are large. The same reporting records that taking forest products without permission is an offence, with a compound fine for unauthorised possession and fines up to a stated maximum in the hundreds of thousands, or five years' imprisonment, or both, for harvesting in a forest reserve. Published national reporting records six critical sites meriting priority protection — named inland forests, peat swamp forests of a river system, the mangroves of the bay, a freshwater and peat swamp lake, a border area contiguous with a national park across the frontier, and the coastal kerangas forests. Read this with the forest reserve classification, the fisheries order, the environmental protection order and the water catchment entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The national park inside a forest reserve, the forest recreation parks and the fifty-five per cent permanent forest estate — what the forestry department publishes about each site and how access is controlled
trackers.desc: The one national park sits inside a gazetted forest reserve, which means two layers of designation over the same ground. The forestry department publishes the national park among its site pages, alongside the national herbarium, ex-situ conservation, the forestry museum and its tender notices.
