Published material records the park as gazetted in 1991 as the country's first national park, within a named forest reserve, covering some five hundred and fifty square kilometres in the southern part of one district — roughly forty per cent of that district — and ranging from lowland to montane forest at nearly two thousand metres. Where a project is proposed near it, the reserve classification and the park designation are separate things to check. Access is controlled, and most of the park is closed. Published description records that strict conservation permits only scientists and specialists to access much of the park, that independent visitors must apply for a special permit, and that only a small share of the park is open to the public, reached by longboat with a single resort facility inside; and records the park open to the public since 2000, having become a focal point for scientific researchers and a source of employment for the local community. That research access is a route to getting a site's ecology documented by someone other than a proponent. Eleven forest recreation parks are the second tier, and they are named. Published material records that by 1998 eleven forest recreation parks had been established, listing them by name across the districts, and records national planning giving attention to plantation activity, sustainable timber production, the establishment of national parks and recreational areas, wasteland rehabilitation and rattan production, with a stated investment under the forest conservation policy. Asking which tier a patch of forest sits in is therefore a real question with several possible answers. The permanent forest estate target is the number to hold the state to. Published material records the 1989 national forestry policy classifying forests into functional categories and maintaining at least fifty-five per cent of land as permanent forest estate, and records roughly forty-one per cent of the land area protected through national parks, forest reserves and conservation areas. Read this with the forest reserve classification, the wildlife sanctuary entry, the environmental protection order and the assessment authority entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Air quality reporting and the open burning complaint line — PSI published five times a day by district, the bands that define "unhealthy", and the two numbers to call
trackers.desc: Air quality is published district by district, several times a day, with the bands stated. A government press release records the environment department publishing pollutant standards index readings recorded from all the air quality monitoring stations in the four districts, with the highest readings of the day listed by district and hour; and records the classification: below 50 good, 50 to 100 moderate, with reporting recording 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy and above 300 hazardous. Reporting records the department issuing updates five times daily, at 7am, 9am, 11am, 2pm and 4pm, during a hazy period, and records that from 1 September 2026 air quality reporting was enhanced by incorporating fine particulate concentrations into the index, previously based on the coarser fraction. A community measuring its own air now has a published national series to set readings against, and a date on which the method changed. Two numbers are published, and one of them takes open burning complaints. The same release records that the public should call the fire and rescue service immediately for any incidence of bush or forest fire, and that complaints about open burning activities, and requests for health information and advice, go to the national hotline — the same single-number line already recorded in this bucket. It records the public advised to refrain from open burning and other actions that may worsen haze during the dry period. The health advice attached to each band is official too. The release records the health ministry advising that at moderate readings between 50 and 100, minor health effects such as coughs, eye irritations and runny nose may occur; reporting records the advice at that level extending to people with asthma, lung and heart disease, pregnant women, children, the elderly and those with dust allergies reducing outdoor activity, and at unhealthy levels to everyone reducing strenuous or prolonged outdoor activity. It records regional satellite imagery detecting hundreds to over a thousand hotspots on named days in the wider island, and records departmental surveillance finding open burning still occurring domestically. Read this with the reporting hotline, the environmental protection order, the assessment guidelines and the forest reserve entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The statistics department's publications and data library — a yearbook in its forty-eighth edition, a three-yearly key indicators volume, and time-series data published free for the general public
trackers.desc: The statistics department publishes long-running annual volumes, and names the general public among their intended users. Its publications page records the statistical yearbook as an annual publication covering a wide variety of statistics on the general demographic, social and economic characteristics of the country, for the use of planners, policy makers, researchers, academics and the general public, summarising the most recent statistical data available from official sources gathered from government ministries and departments and other relevant bodies, with the 2024 volume its forty-eighth edition; and records a key indicators volume released annually on three years of data, in its forty-second edition, covering a wide range of socio-economic indicators and available as an e-book and in portable document format. Where a project's justification rests on population or economic claims, that is the published series to check them against. A separate data library carries the time series. The same department publishes an electronic data library, recording that its time series statistical data provide up-to-date official statistics on the general demographic, social and economic characteristics of the country, for the same stated users. It also publishes a vital statistics volume, presenting time series over a six-year period on vital events compiled from records provided by relevant government agencies, in its thirty-fourth edition and following internationally recognised methodologies, and the reports of the population and housing census. An open data portal exists, with a stated purpose. A registry of data catalogues records the national open data portal as helping people discover and use open data created and collected by government agencies, to improve public service delivery and enable better-informed decision-making for citizens and businesses; the government portal carries its own open data page. The same registry records a national survey geoportal providing access to geographic datasets and map layers including house numbering and survey products. International compilations cover what the national series does not. Published dataset listings record an environment indicators dataset for this country drawn from an international bank's data portal, covering forests, biodiversity, emissions and pollution, downloadable, with a consolidated country dataset alongside. Read this with the geoportal entry, the air quality reporting, the forest reserve classification and the tender notices entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The nature society and the other specialist bodies — a biodiversity conservation programme, a natural history library, and a university field studies centre in the rainforest
trackers.desc: There is a nature society, and its stated purpose is to get citizens to fight for protection of the natural world. Published description records the nature society as studying and promoting interest in the environment and natural history of the country, and as encouraging citizens, through monthly lectures, organised nature outings and other educational programmes including its library on natural history, to learn more about their surroundings and fight for the protection of the natural world; and records that through its biodiversity conservation programme the society supports the conservation of threatened species in the country. For a community that needs species expertise it cannot buy, that is where the standing interest already sits. Other specialist bodies are named, with what each does. A published directory records a biodiversity and natural history society focused on biodiversity research and conservation supporting local ecosystems and communities, and records a university field studies centre conducting biodiversity research, environmental education and community work; it also lists the youth-led environmental organisation already recorded in this bucket. Published description records another youth body aiming to provide green resources and to be an enabler of youth-initiated environmental projects, running nature camps, tree planting, workshops and talks. The organisations work alongside government and companies, and the pattern is visible in the record. The youth organisation's own listings record clean-ups run with a named technology company, a six-day donation drive with a mukim consultative council, and a school talk with a district office — the local-council and district-office partnerships being the doors a community group can use as well. The transboundary forest agreement is the frame around all of it. Published description records a conservation agreement signed by three governments in 2007 covering a 220,000 square kilometre forested region, providing habitat to ten endemic primate species, more than 350 birds, 150 reptiles and amphibians and 10,000 plants, with 123 new species recorded in the region between 2007 and 2010, and names this country's national park among the protected areas within it — the park already recorded in this bucket. Read this with the youth organisation entry, the national park, the forest reserve classification and the statistics entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: IBER and the permanent forest plots — a university institute that names a contact for collaborative research, a network of measured plots across three districts, and a rainforest field centre
trackers.desc: A university institute publishes a named route for anyone wanting research done in the forest. The institute's research page states that to conduct biodiversity and environmental research at the field studies centre, or for collaborative research with the institute, the research coordinator should be contacted, and for plot details, the director. A community that needs a baseline survey of what lives on a site has, in that sentence, an addressable domestic body. The institute records itself as established in 2013 as a focal agency within the university to coordinate, facilitate, support and execute research, education and outreach in the biodiversity and environmental scope, both terrestrial and marine. The plot network is the baseline data, and its layout is published. The institute records administering and managing a network of one-hectare plots across the country, mainly in lowland mixed dipterocarp forest in three named districts, with two additional one-hectare plots in heath forest; nine quarter-hectare plots set at three altitudes — 200, 500 and 850 metres above sea level; and a 25-hectare permanent plot at the field studies centre, established with a tropical forest science centre. It lists published papers on the floristic composition and structure of the country's mixed dipterocarp and heath forests and on altitudinal zonation. Where a project claims a site is ordinary secondary forest, measured plots are what contradicts it. The field centre is a working facility, not a display. Published material records the centre as a core research focus and premier facility of the institute, drawing international scientists for projects ranging from ecology, taxonomy, medicinal plants research, parasite ecology and soundscape research, and as offering field-based educational opportunities to students from secondary schools, higher education institutions and overseas partner universities. It records the centre operating since the early 1990s, following a fourteen-month scientific expedition, and records a botanical research centre mostly covered in native heath forest with a greenhouse of around 250 plant species, mainly herbaceous species used by herbalists or as ornamentals. The institute's own listings record project collaborations on the country's peatlands and published regional flora checklists. Read this with the nature society and specialist bodies, the forest reserve classification, the national park and the geoportal entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The religious council as sole endowment trustee — the body that takes land given permanently for public benefit, and the development arm that makes it pay for itself
trackers.desc: Land can be endowed here so that it stops being available for sale or development. A published ministerial account records that in the religious council's early years people commonly endowed land for building mosques or roads within villages, though such assets had little income potential; and records that endowed assets that can be developed productively include land. Published description records that all matters relating to endowment are governed and administered by the Islamic religious council under named chapters of the country's legislation, and that the Act makes the council the sole trustee of all types of endowment in the country. For a community wanting a plot held permanently rather than traded, that is the domestic instrument, and it has a single named trustee. Two forms exist, and which one is used decides who controls the purpose. Published description records endowed property divided into a specific form and a general form, distinguished by whether the donor fixed the use in the declaration — in the specific form the donor has determined the use, for example land endowed for building a mosque, while in the general form the use is not fixed and the council is free to determine its management. A donor who wants the land kept as it is must therefore say so in the declaration. It records that endowment may be registered or unregistered: registered donors register the property directly with the council and hold a certificate, while unregistered endowment may be merely oral between donor and manager, with cases where the manager did not know an endowment existed. Registration is the difference between a permanent protection and a story. A development body exists to make endowed land productive. The ministerial account records a development body established in 1994 to develop endowed assets under the council's management, records that in the 1990s one of the simplest income strategies was constructing buildings on endowed land for rental, and records the body now owning several buildings across the country and operating a filling station at a named village. Published material records named endowed lots developed with flats and shophouses producing monthly rent used for community welfare, and records that stated distribution targets include education, health, religious and social purposes. Read this with the land records, the village consultative councils, the forest reserves and the money-for-community-work entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Yayasan Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah — a statutory charitable foundation with published welfare categories, disaster assistance including volunteer labour, and support given jointly with non-government bodies
trackers.desc: The country's main charitable foundation publishes what its welfare arm actually pays for. The foundation records that all its welfare projects and activities focus on improving the welfare and wellbeing of life and advancing socio-cultural and socio-economic development among the people and residents of the country, and lists categories including assistance to lighten the burden of natural disaster victims — flood, strong wind, landslide and fire victims — given as financial contributions, basic food and other appropriate needs, with labour assistance also provided through the foundation's volunteer service. For a village hit by flooding or a landslide after clearance upstream, that is a domestic body with a stated disaster category and volunteers. It works with non-government bodies and funds housing. The same pages record the foundation from time to time giving financial contributions and support and cooperating with other non-governmental bodies to run youth development projects and programmes to increase young people's involvement in community and national development; record assistance to patients who do not qualify under the government medical assistance scheme; and record housing assistance intended to provide comfortable and clean accommodation, housing being named as one of the basic needs in the hierarchy of human needs. Its literary award is recorded as its support for preserving Islamic literary heritage. Its legal basis and its scale are on record. The statute book carries the foundation's own Act as a numbered chapter setting out its objects. Published description records it established on 5 October 1992 as the channel for charitable endowments by the Sultan and members of the royal family, operating on five principles — education, welfare, religion, development and finance. Published reporting records one annual programme handing over contributions of a stated sum in money and food essentials to 150 families across all four districts, and records a national welfare system built by named ministries together with the foundation, with online applications through a government website. Read this with the endowment trustee, the mukim and village consultative councils, the community funding entry and the societies registration entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Beach Bunch and the volunteer wildlife networks — a clean-up organisation with counted volunteers and tonnage, a seat on a national government taskforce, and roadkill and marine-death reporting groups
trackers.desc: Note on sourcing: these groups run mainly on social media and have little formal web presence, so this entry rests on an award citation and published blogs rather than their own sites. A volunteer clean-up organisation exists with counted results. A published award citation records its founder as president and founder of a clean-up organisation which has inspired over 12,000 volunteers to collect 28.2 tonnes of litter from the country's beaches; records that he organised his first clean-up with 20 friends in 2009 before launching the organisation with a named co-founder the following year; and records over 3,000 people taking part in an annual beach event series. For a community that wants a coastline documented and cleaned before a project arrives, that is an existing volunteer base rather than one to build. It holds a place on a government taskforce, which is the part worth copying. The same citation records the founder collaborating with the government on a national beach safety taskforce, promoting lifeguarding courses in schools, installing rescue equipment on beaches and providing information on rip currents. A volunteer organisation that has turned clean-ups into a seat at a national body is a route other community groups can follow. Published material records the organisation described as an environmental non-governmental organisation whose leader presented findings at a forum on coastal environments, and records an inaugural international roundtable on keeping the country's beaches clean. Wildlife reporting runs through named volunteer networks. Published material records a wildlife network and a natural history society circulating reports of roadkill, including a rare otter species identified from photographs by a named specialist, and of a sea turtle carcass found between two named beaches, assessed by a foreign sea turtle expert counterpart as a juvenile of a critically endangered species entangled in fishing net, with the network asking finders to contact them if they find dead sea turtles or turtle eggs being sold, and recording carcasses passed to the museum department. Read this with the nature society and specialist bodies, the biodiversity institute, the youth environmental organisation and the national park entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Tender Board e-Tendering
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Oman, and for how much.

trackers.name: Invest Easy – Commercial Registrations
trackers.desc: National — public search of Oman’s commercial register (Oman Business Platform). — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Oman Data Portal
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Oman.

trackers.name: State Audit Institution
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of Oman. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Oman.

trackers.name: Supreme Judicial Council (Oman)
trackers.desc: Body overseeing Oman's courts and Supreme Court (the apex cassation-level court), with judicial information. · Find here: Oman's Supreme Judicial Council — administration and oversight of the courts.

trackers.name: Kuwait Regional Convention (ROPME) — and its Judicial Commission
trackers.desc: THE ONE BINDING ENVIRONMENTAL INSTRUMENT COVERING ALL EIGHT GULF STATES. The Kuwait Regional Convention for Cooperation on the Protection of the Marine Environment from Pollution was signed 24 April 1978 and entered into force 1 July 1979 — 30 articles, described as the basic legal instrument binding the eight States of the Region. ALL EIGHT ARE FULL PARTIES: ROPME records ‘no signatories without ratification, acceptance, approval or accession’, so unlike some regional instruments there is no signed-but-unratified state to argue about. ARTICLE II fixes the Sea Area by coordinates, from Ras Dharbat Ali (16°39'N, 53°3'30"E) to Ras Al Fasteh (25°04'N, 61°25'E) — a treaty boundary you can check a project location against. Use the term ‘ROPME Sea Area’: it was coined by the Plenipotentiaries to achieve unanimity, cooperating in spite of existing geopolitical boundaries, and it is the name all eight accepted. THE ORGAN MOST PEOPLE DO NOT KNOW EXISTS: alongside the Council and Secretariat, ROPME has a Judicial Commission, established March 1989, of 6 nationals of Member States highly qualified in international law. In a region with almost no environmental litigation route, a standing judicial commission under a ratified convention is the most significant legal fact available — though this entry does not assert that individuals may petition it; establish who may seise it first. AN EVIDENCE SOURCE THAT NEEDS NO SITE ACCESS: ROPME's scientific bodies include a Remote Sensing Unit, alongside RIIS and MEMAC. WHICH PROTOCOL FITS YOUR ISSUE: oil-spill emergency response; land-based sources of pollution — the limb for a coastal development, discharge or reclamation; and transboundary movement of hazardous wastes. Development is named as a stressor in ROPME's own statement of purpose. At stake: over 20 species of dolphin and whale, all five subtropical turtle species, and more than 1,000 fish species, most endemic.

trackers.name: MBZ Species Conservation Fund — frame it as species work, not climate
trackers.desc: DO NOT DRESS A SPECIES PROJECT UP AS A CLIMATE PROJECT HERE — which is the opposite of the advice that fits almost every other fund in this map. The MBZ Fund was established on the basis that direct species conservation has lost out to wider concerns such as climate change, sustainability and poverty alleviation, and is now seen as a by-product of larger issues, leaving underfunded field biologists and wardens. It exists to correct that displacement, so frame the work as direct, field-based species conservation. A philanthropic endowment announced at the World Conservation Congress in Barcelona, October 2008, taking applications since March 2009; managing director Razan Khalifa Al Mubarak, also President of IUCN. By end-2010 it had disbursed just over US$5 million to about 380 projects in almost 100 countries; awards run up to US$25,000. TWO UNUSUAL ELIGIBILITY POINTS: it covers all animal, plant AND FUNGI species — fungi are named, which almost no other fund in this map does — and its focus includes data-deficient species, so you need not prove the species is threatened; where the problem is that nobody knows, that is itself a qualifying category. Individual conservationists may apply, and priority goes to projects supporting young conservationists. Funding is for direct conservation impact rather than administrative costs. HOW IT RUNS: three rounds a year, March, June and October; the Fund forwards recommendations to an independent body, so its staff are not the final decision-makers; and late submissions are automatically moved to the next round — missing a deadline costs a cycle, not the application. Apply online in English; the form requires a budget, references and permits, so have your permissions in order before applying. READ THE PROJECTS DATABASE FIRST — searchable by species, IUCN classification, continent and year, it shows what has been funded for comparable species in comparable places. NOTE: THIS FUND IS GLOBAL, NOT REGIONAL — it is recorded here because this country holds no other funding entry, not because Gulf applicants receive any preference.

trackers.name: Environment Society of Oman — by its own account the only environmental non-profit in the country, and listed in the regulator's own directory
trackers.desc: ESO DESCRIBES ITSELF AS THE ONLY NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION IN OMAN THAT FOCUSES ON CONSERVING THE ENVIRONMENT. For a resident facing a development, that sentence is the whole strategic picture: there is no second organisation to fall back on, and no Omani land trust or public-interest environmental firm was found. WHY IT STILL HAS WEIGHT: ESO appears in the Environment Authority's own online directory of environment-interested groups, and it has been an IUCN member since February 2009 — so a submission carrying ESO's name is not an outsider's letter. MEMBERSHIP IS THE ACCESS ROUTE AND IT IS GENUINELY OPEN: anyone over 18 with an interest may join, and the base has passed 500 individual members alongside corporate members, with an elected board serving two-year terms drawn from Oman's scientific, conservation and business communities and from different regions. Contact admin@eso.org.om, +968 9985 5108, based in Ruwi. Founded March 2004. WHAT YOU CANNOT GET HERE, AND IT IS MOST OF WHAT A LAND DEFENCE NEEDS: ESO does not litigate, does not buy or hold land, and runs no community grant window. Its published strengths are research on threatened and endangered species, education, awareness and advocacy, with a long-running marine emphasis — cetacean and turtle work, and a national strandings database. The realistic use is therefore evidentiary and reputational: commission or obtain species and habitat evidence for the site, and get a recognised conservation body's name attached to it, then take that to the Environment Authority yourself. Treat the absence of any litigating or land-holding body in Oman as a finding to plan around rather than a gap in this file. MEMBERSHIP IS OPEN TO ANYONE AGED EIGHTEEN OR OVER who is keen to protect the environment — the society was founded in March 2004 by Omanis drawn from different regions, wilayats and governorates and from different professional backgrounds, and registered by ministerial decision. ONE OF ITS CHARTERED OBJECTIVES IS WORTH QUOTING TO IT WHEN YOU WRITE: SECURING AN ENVIRONMENT THAT ALLOWS THE EXCHANGE OF OPINION AND INFORMATION IN THE FIELD OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION IN THIS COUNTRY. A body that has registered that as an object has undertaken to be a place where an environmental argument can be had — which, in a country with few such places, is a commitment a community can invoke rather than a hope. Its objects also include ENABLING THE CITIZEN TO PLAY AN ACTIVE ROLE AND VOLUNTEER IN NATURE CONSERVATION PROJECTS, and cooperating with local, regional and international scientific and research organisations. AND ITS RECENT WORK SHOWS WHAT IT CAN ACTUALLY MEASURE, WHICH IS WHAT A COMMUNITY NEEDS FROM IT. IT HAS IDENTIFIED EIGHT CORAL REEF MONITORING SITES, expressly to assess environmental condition and MEASURE CHANGES OVER TIME. A monitoring site with a baseline is the difference between saying a reef has deteriorated and showing it. ITS FIELD TEAM MONITORS GREEN TURTLES FROM MAY TO NOVEMBER, together with hawksbill and olive ridley turtles; in one recent year it rescued six hawksbill turtles, CLEANED TWENTY-FIVE KILOMETRES OF NESTING BEACHES and monitored twenty Egyptian vulture nests. It has also completed an INTERNATIONAL CONSERVATION PLAN for the endangered Arabian humpback whale. MOST INSTRUCTIVE OF ALL: AT A WASTE LANDFILL IN DHOFAR IT MONITORS A RAPTOR FEEDING STATION BUILT WITH THE NATIONAL ENVIRONMENT SERVICES COMPANY AND OPERATED BY AN ENERGY COMPANY, AND IT TRAINS THAT SITE'S OWN WORKERS IN HOW TO MONITOR BIRDS — a pilot running to the middle of 2026, aimed partly at steppe eagles wintering from Central Asia. A civil organisation embedded at an industrial site, teaching the operator's staff to record wildlife, is a shape this file has found nowhere else in twenty-three countries: IT MEANS THE SOCIETY CAN WORK INSIDE A COMPANY'S OPERATION RATHER THAN ONLY OUTSIDE IT, and that monitoring is something it teaches rather than hoards. ASK IT TO TRAIN YOUR PEOPLE.TWO STRUCTURAL FACTS MATTER MORE THAN ANY OF THIS SOCIETY'S PROJECTS, AND NEITHER WAS RECORDED HERE ORIGINALLY. THE ENVIRONMENT AUTHORITY ENSURES THE SOCIETY'S PARTICIPATION AND MEMBERSHIP IN ALL THE NATIONAL COMMITTEES AND TEAMS CONCERNED WITH ENVIRONMENTAL AFFAIRS, AS INTEGRATIVE WORK BETWEEN THE GOVERNMENTAL AND CIVIL SECTORS. AND THE SOCIETY SUPPLIES THE RESULTS OF ITS STUDIES AND ACTIVITIES TO THE AUTHORITY FOR INCLUSION IN THE RULES AND PROCEDURES THE AUTHORITY ADOPTS. SO A CIVIL BODY HOLDS A SEAT ON THE NATIONAL COMMITTEES, AND ITS OWN FIELD DATA FEEDS INTO WHAT THE REGULATOR THEN ADOPTS. THAT IS THE SHORTEST ROUTE FROM A LOCAL OBSERVATION TO A NATIONAL RULE FOUND ANYWHERE IN THIS FILE — AND IT MEANS A COMMUNITY WITH A DOCUMENTED PROBLEM DOES NOT NEED TO REACH THE MINISTRY ITSELF. IT NEEDS TO REACH THE SOCIETY THAT SITS ON THE COMMITTEE. BRING IT DATA, NOT A COMPLAINT. THE SOCIETY'S CURRENCY IS SURVEYS AND MEASUREMENTS: IN A SINGLE YEAR IT RAN FOUR FIELD SURVEYS COVERING SEA TURTLE SPECIES AND RARE TREES, WORKED WITH THIRTY-SIX INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS, CLEANED TWENTY-FIVE KILOMETRES OF NESTING BEACH, MONITORED TWENTY VULTURE NESTS, IDENTIFIED EIGHT CORAL MONITORING SITES, AND REMOVED SIXTY TONNES OF ABANDONED MARINE EQUIPMENT — EIGHT HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIVE TONNES IN TOTAL TO DATE. NOTE THAT RARE TREES SIT ALONGSIDE MARINE SPECIES IN ITS SURVEY WORK, AND THAT IT HAS RUN WORKSHOPS ON TREE CONSERVATION AND ON LIGHT POLLUTION. A COMMUNITY LOSING OLD TREES HAS A BODY HERE THAT ALREADY SURVEYS THEM. ITS PERSISTENCE IS THE OTHER LESSON: SIXTEEN CONSECUTIVE YEARS OF FIELD SURVEYS MONITORING TURTLES ON ONE ISLAND, CARRIED BY FIVE YEARS OF SUPPORT FROM A FOREIGN GOVERNMENT'S MARINE TURTLE CONSERVATION FUND. A SIXTEEN-YEAR DATA SERIES IS WHAT MAKES A CLAIM ABOUT CHANGE UNARGUABLE, and it exists because someone kept counting. AND HERE IS THE WIN WORTH COPYING, BECAUSE IT IS SMALL, PHYSICAL AND AGAINST INSTALLED INFRASTRUCTURE: WORKING ON LIGHTING AT COMMERCIAL AND GOVERNMENT PROPERTIES — A RESORT AND A FISHERMEN'S VILLAGE — THE SOCIETY'S SUSTAINED EFFORTS PRODUCED A DECISION TO SWITCH OFF SOME OF THE VILLAGE STREET LIGHTS, AND EIGHT HOUSES AND A MOSQUE WERE FITTED WITH WILDLIFE-FRIENDLY LIGHTING. STREET LIGHTS ALREADY INSTALLED WERE TURNED OFF FOR THE SAKE OF NESTING WILDLIFE. THAT IS A REVERSAL OF EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE, ACHIEVED WITHOUT LITIGATION, THROUGH SURVEY DATA AND PERSISTENCE — AND LIGHTING IS THE CHEAPEST THING TO ASK ANY DEVELOPER OR MUNICIPALITY TO CHANGE, BECAUSE SWITCHING A LAMP OFF COSTS NOTHING AND SAVES MONEY.

trackers.name: BirdLife Hima Fund — Oman is one of four named grant recipients, and this is the country's only funding route found
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE ONLY GRANT WINDOW THIS FILE HAS FOUND FOR OMAN, AND OMAN IS ONE OF ONLY FOUR COUNTRIES BIRDLIFE NAMES AS HAVING RECEIVED ONE. BirdLife records that the Hima Fund launched in 2011 with four approved grants to Partners in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and Oman, to reinforce or revitalise Himas at four sites. The fund was established in Qatar in 2008 with a one million dollar donation from Sheikha Jawaher Bint Hamad Bin Suhaim Al-Thani, aimed at conserving Important Bird Areas and their threatened species in the Middle East. That matters here because the Oman entry already in this file records a country with no land trust, no public-interest environmental law practice and no community grant window — this is the single documented exception, and it is bird-habitat specific. THE ROUTE: grants go to BirdLife Partners rather than direct to communities, so the application is carried by the national partner organisation; this entry does not name Oman's BirdLife Partner because that was not verified during this round, and the Environment Society of Oman recorded in this file is the obvious body to ask. FRAME THE SITE AS A HIMA: the Hima is a traditional designation under which a defined community controls access and use and may forbid hunting, wood cutting and the destruction of trees and shrubs — which is a far better fit for Omani rangeland than a purchase model. CAVEAT, AND IT IS A SERIOUS ONE: no evidence of grant-making after the early 2010s was found. Treat the fund as documented in its founding and unverified in its current operation. ANTI-FANOUT NOTE: press reporting names twelve countries in the fund's remit; BirdLife's own page names four grant recipients, and this entry exists in those four only.

trackers.name: Oman's electronic waqf system — the auction page tells you which endowment land is going to a developer, and the register tells you if its boundaries just moved
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE BEST EARLY-WARNING SOURCE FOUND ANYWHERE IN THIS REGION, AND IT IS OPEN TO ANYONE: the Ministry of Awqaf and Religious Affairs runs a searchable page of endowment properties put up for auction, and bidding is registered through this same system. Watch it. In June 2026 the ministry offered a set of endowment assets for investment under its Tathmeer project for multi-use plots, land and assets spread across a number of wilayats, with the Wilayat of Sohar alone carrying several separate investment opportunities and independent auctions. The practice is long-standing rather than new — as far back as 2017 the ministry, through its department for the development of endowment funds, advertised open competitive tendering for well-located land plots across the governorates. ENDOWMENT STATUS IS NOT PROTECTION FROM DEVELOPMENT IN OMAN; IT IS A DIFFERENT ROUTE INTO IT. THE SECOND THING TO DO IS READ THE REGISTER ENTRY FOR THE PARCEL. The system holds per-parcel records carrying the property description, its classification as waqf or bayt al-mal, the supervising administrative body, the endower's details, the named agents with civil numbers — and a dated change history recording entries such as the waqf boundaries having been amended, with the name of the person who made the change and the timestamp. A boundary moved shortly before a scheme appears is impossible to prove later and trivial to spot now. Records go down to individual holdings, one covering four commercial shops belonging to a mosque's endowments within a named plan in the Wilayat of Izki. HOW THE DEVELOPMENT ITSELF IS STRUCTURED, WHICH TELLS YOU WHAT TO ARGUE ABOUT: on a summary published by an Omani law firm rather than by the ministry, and so to be checked before it is relied on, investment on vacant endowment land not attached to a mosque may take the form of an investor constructing apartments and shops, assigning the yield of one or more of them to the endowment or paying a monthly ground rent, keeping the use of the rest for the contract term — with ownership of the buildings passing to the endowment when the term ends. The endowment's interest is therefore in the building being built, which is worth knowing before assuming the ministry shares your objection. Investment is stated to follow feasibility studies by a specialised expert body. THE ROUTE THAT RUNS THE OTHER WAY, AND IT IS THE MOST ACCESSIBLE IN THE REGION: the endowment-share scheme accepts in-kind participation expressly including commercial, residential, industrial and agricultural buildings and land, alongside cash, at whatever scale a person can manage, through the same electronic system; the ministry states that what reaches a project's accounts becomes an endowment asset that is not spent but invested, with only its proceeds disbursed. That endowment property sits in the path of infrastructure is visible on the system's own front page, which has carried an appeal for a mosque affected by the Batinah Coastal Line project. A separate mosques system on the same ministry domain publishes a mosques map. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: no enforcement route against misuse of endowment land was found, unlike Türkiye where the civil administration evicts on the directorate's request, and no consent gate on expropriation of the kind Jordan's Awqaf Council provides. Use this as an auction watch, a register and a dedication route, and ask the ministry directly what happens when endowment land is taken or misused.

trackers.name: Rufford Small Grants — Oman is named eligible, and an individual can apply where the country has almost no organisations
trackers.desc: OMAN APPEARS BY NAME ON THE FOUNDATION'S OWN ELIGIBILITY LIST, AND THE APPLICANT CAN BE A PERSON RATHER THAN AN ORGANISATION — which matters here because this file has established that Oman has essentially one independent environmental non-profit, which describes itself as the only one in the country. Where there is no organisation to join, a fund that takes applications from individuals is the difference between doing the work and not. NO DEADLINES: applications are accepted at any time of year. The focus is people early in a conservation career, particularly current or recent MSc and PhD students, with others considered against the published criteria; undergraduates are not funded. THE SPECIES TEST IS EXACT AND CHECKABLE BEFORE YOU WRITE: any species not listed as Least Concern globally on the IUCN Red List qualifies, as do species not yet assessed but thought to be globally threatened. Habitat, human-wildlife conflict and community education projects qualify without a species focus — which suits wadi, coastal and mountain habitat questions. FUNDING IS STAGED: up to £7,000 for a first grant, then a second, a Booster and a Completion Grant, running to roughly £18,000, each conditional on completing and reporting the last, with reports published on the applicant's own page. One application in any twelve months; twelve months' wait after a rejection; the foundation expects to fund between half and all of a project and requires evidence of co-funding where others contribute; it will not support pure research without conservation benefit or expeditions requiring the applicant to fundraise to take part. Pair with the environment society already recorded here, and note that Oman's electronic waqf system lets you check whether the land in question is endowment land before designing any project on it.

trackers.name: Accountability Counsel — Oman is a named dark spot, and it partners with local lawyers rather than replacing them
trackers.desc: OMAN IS NAMED AS AN ACCOUNTABILITY DARK SPOT IN THIS ORGANISATION'S OWN RESEARCH — a country from which no community complaint has ever reached any development bank's accountability office. ITS METHOD SUITS A COUNTRY WITH ALMOST NO INDEPENDENT CIVIL SOCIETY: it partners with local lawyers or organisations to discuss domestic legal strategies alongside its own in-depth work on international complaint procedures, so a single sympathetic local lawyer plus this body is a workable combination where a campaigning organisation does not exist. It assists communities on request in using accountability offices to defend their rights and remedy harm from internationally financed projects, with support ranging from multi-year accompaniment to a limited document review, and it is expert in the mechanisms of the World Bank Group, regional development banks, export credit agencies and OECD National Contact Points. IT PUBLISHES A FREE DATABASE OF EVERY COMPLAINT EVER FILED TO EVERY ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICE. Founded 2009, having worked with communities in fifty countries. ESTABLISH THE FINANCING FIRST — the route exists only where an international institution is lending. Use it with the two Omani resources already in this file: the country's single environmental society, and the electronic endowment register that lets you establish whether the land in question is waqf before a dispute begins.

trackers.name: Inclusive Development International — it identifies the financier, which is what decides whether the complaint route is open
trackers.desc: EVERY INTERNATIONAL ROUTE IN THIS FILE DEPENDS ON KNOWING WHO IS PAYING, AND THIS ORGANISATION ESTABLISHES THAT ON REQUEST. Since 2016 it has researched and mapped the investment and supply chains behind harmful projects for community advocates, identifying banks, investors, insurers, development finance institutions and brands, from financial databases, company reports, import data and shipping manifests. It returns a summary with an analysis of pressure points and advocacy options; in high-potential cases it supports execution, and otherwise refers the case onward to partners. ITS FREE SHAREHOLDER AND DEVELOPMENT BANK INVESTMENT TRACKERS MAKE THE FIRST STAGE SELF-SERVICE, and it has trained more than fifteen hundred advocates in selected methods, teaching around the projects they are actually fighting. IT FITS THE OMANI SET PRECISELY: this file records that Oman has one independent environmental society, an endowment register that reveals whether land is waqf, and an accountability route that has never been used from the country. Establishing the financier is what turns that route from theory into a filing. THE LIMIT: its documented casework is in Southeast Asia, Africa and the Americas, and no work in Oman or this region could be established. Its service is described as open to community requests with no geographic restriction stated — untested here, not closed.

trackers.name: CESAR at Sultan Qaboos University — a published national review of Oman's coastal pollution
trackers.desc: THERE IS A PUBLISHED REVIEW OF THE ENVIRONMENTAL STATUS OF OMAN'S COASTAL AREAS, AND IT IS THE BASELINE A COASTAL OBJECTION NEEDS. It assesses pollution and impacts across the country's coast — SALINITY, HEAVY METALS AND PETROLEUM HYDROCARBONS — covering groundwater, soil, and marine and coastal water, and their effects on biological systems and marine organisms. A community told a scheme will have no significant effect can start from a national review that already documents what is in the water and the soil. AND ITS MONITORING IS MEASURED AGAINST OMANI STANDARDS — its published work compares results for conductivity, nitrite and nitrate, chloride, sulfate and phosphate against the national standards, which means the data arrives already framed in the terms a regulator has to answer, rather than in terms a regulator can dismiss as academic. THE MOST PRACTICAL THING HERE IS THE SEARCHABLE RESEARCH PORTAL: the university publishes its research output in a public expertise database, browsable by organisation and by collaborating country, so you can find WHICH NAMED RESEARCHER WORKS ON YOUR PROBLEM before you write to anyone. Naming the right person is most of the difficulty in getting expert help, and this removes it. ITS SUBJECT RANGE MATCHES OMAN'S ACTUAL LAND PRESSURES: climate change, biodiversity, desertification, wastewater and environmental management, with published work on water quality, groundwater pollution and clean-up, soil and water conservation, salt-affected soils, and the vulnerability and adaptation of FARMERS in a named wilayat — the last of which shows it works at community scale, not only at national scale. Its director combines that technical range with water resources management AND LEGISLATION, which is an unusual pairing and the right one for a permit dispute. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE THE SAME AS FOR ANY UNIVERSITY CENTRE IN THE REGION: this is a state university, its funding sources expressly include EXTERNAL CONTRACTS AND CONSULTANCY, and it has research partnerships with public and private sector organisations. It may have worked for the developer, and it will not campaign. Take the published data first; approach a named researcher second; expect a research collaboration rather than a service. Oman's only independent environmental organisation is recorded separately in this file and describes itself as the country's only one — this is not a second, it is the place the evidence lives.

trackers.name: iNaturalist — free identification, and every confirmed observation enters the scientific record
trackers.desc: IT IDENTIFIES WHAT YOU FOUND AND THEN MAKES IT COUNT. Photograph a plant, animal or fungus with a free app, or record a sound; an automated system offers an identification; a global community reviews it; and once they agree the observation becomes RESEARCH GRADE AND IS AUTOMATICALLY SHARED WITH THE GLOBAL BIODIVERSITY DATABASE. This country has an environmental society and a university research centre, but no route by which a resident's own observation becomes part of the record. This is that route, and it is free. IT SOLVES THE PROBLEM THIS FILE KEEPS FINDING: a community can rarely name what lives on the ground it is defending, and an assessment that lists nothing of interest is hard to contradict without species evidence. Point a phone at it; the community will tell you what it is. Invertebrates and plants — the groups most often absent from assessments — are exactly where crowd identification helps most. OLD PHOTOGRAPHS ARE ACCEPTED provided you know roughly when and where they were taken, so existing pictures of a wadi, a coast or a grove can be turned into dated records now. IT CAPTURES OFFLINE — photographs and coordinates are saved on the phone without a connection and uploaded later — which matters for remote coast and interior. AND LOCATIONS CAN BE OBSCURED: randomised to protect a sensitive species or habitat, with precise coordinates visible only to users you trust. Use that where publishing an exact location could attract collectors or hunters rather than protection. TO MAKE RECORDS USABLE: enable location so coordinates are logged, take SEVERAL PHOTOGRAPHS FROM DIFFERENT ANGLES of one individual, and record sounds where relevant. THE LIMITS: identification depends on volunteers and difficult organisms may go unresolved; uploading requires a connection; the platform is for observations you make yourself, not a place to deposit existing datasets. AND RESEARCH-GRADE RECORDS ARE HARVESTED PERIODICALLY — a contested identification can be changed and the record can drop out of the global database at the next harvest. Once observations reach research grade, download and cite them from that database, where the download carries a permanent identifier.

trackers.name: Hima revival and its fund — community-held protected land, revived at a site in this country
trackers.desc: A HIMA IS A PROTECTED PLACE DECLARED BY A COMMUNITY AND CUSTOMARILY HELD AND MANAGED BY IT, regulating the use of pasture, rangeland and water rather than transferring ownership — and a fund supported the revival of one AT A SITE IN THIS COUNTRY, alongside three others in the region. This map records for this country a conservation society, a university centre and foreign instruments; a community-held protected area is a different kind of thing, and it is native here rather than imported. IT IS ABOUT FIFTEEN HUNDRED YEARS OLD AND IT WORKS: surviving traditional himas are described as THE BEST-MANAGED RANGELANDS IN THE ARABIAN PENINSULA, which is a claim about outcomes rather than intentions. THE GOVERNANCE PRECEDENT IS USABLE IN AN ARGUMENT: tribes held their own himas WITH THE PERMISSION OF THE STATE and acted as SELF-GOVERNMENT where the state was absent. A community asking to manage a stretch of rangeland is asking for something with standing in local history, not a novelty. AND RESEARCHERS ADVISING GOVERNMENTS RECOMMEND REVIVAL FOR THE REASON THAT MATTERS MOST WHEN AN OBJECTION IS DISMISSED AS FOREIGN: it WOULD NOT REQUIRE THE INTRODUCTION OF ALIEN SOCIAL INSTITUTIONS OR VALUES. WHAT TO ASK FOR: the fund that supported the site here was initiated in 2008 on a one-million-dollar donation; a regional CHARTER was adopted by participants from ten countries including this one; and a TRAINING CURRICULUM exists for introducing the system to a community, covering HOW TO SELECT A POTENTIAL HIMA SITE and the environmental, economic and social consequences of the choice. That curriculum is the practical thing — a village deciding which ground to declare, and on what terms, is making the decision the whole system turns on. THE LIMITS: it regulates use rather than conferring title, so it does not by itself stop a state allocating land elsewhere; revival work depends on temporary international funding, which practitioners identify as the main risk to it; and boundary violations by outside livestock owners are documented. The fund is small and site-selected rather than open to applications. Pair it with the environment society and the fisheries route recorded separately for this country, and with the species records tools, which is how a community shows what its hima would protect.

trackers.name: Sultan Qaboos University College of Law — its clinic is the only domestic legal route found here
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY HAS NO OTHER ROUTE TO A LAWYER IN THIS MAP. Its bar association was tested in R197 and showed no legal aid function; its other entries are state portals and foreign accountability bodies. THE NATIONAL UNIVERSITY'S COLLEGE OF LAW OPERATES A LAW CLINIC, AND THAT IS THE ROUTE. THE CLINIC IS NAMED DIRECTLY IN REGIONAL RECORDS: it took part in a 2013 competition on drafting a model law alongside the law clinics of the Qatari national university and a Kuwaiti law school, and it was one of the two counterpart clinics at Gulf meetings on clinical legal education held in 2013 and 2014. Those Gulf clinics share a model, described for the Qatari one recorded separately in this file: legal aid to people who cannot afford a lawyer, delivered by students working under the supervision of practising attorneys, with cases referred on to licensed lawyers. NOW THE WARNING, AND IT IS THE MAIN THING TO CARRY: NO CURRENT PAGE FOR THE CLINIC COULD BE REACHED. The documentary evidence is from 2013 and 2014. WHAT IS DEMONSTRABLY CURRENT IS THE COLLEGE ITSELF — it runs an official account, publishes a university law journal, and supervises postgraduate legal research, including work on subjects such as termination of employment contracts for economic reasons. SO APPROACH THE COLLEGE RATHER THAN THE CLINIC BY NAME: ask whether the legal clinic still operates, what matters it accepts, and whether a member of the faculty will advise on a land, planning or environmental question. A law faculty that has run a clinic once knows how, and academics are often the only people in a country willing to give a written opinion on a contested administrative decision. WHAT THE MODEL DOES NOT COVER, ON THE EVIDENCE FROM ITS SISTER CLINICS: their documented casework is migrant labour, family and criminal matters rather than property or planning. Put a land question to them as a question, not an assumption. AND KNOW WHAT ELSE EXISTS AROUND IT, BECAUSE IT MAY BE EASIER TO REACH: a Middle East and North Africa legal clinics alliance was founded in 2012 by fifteen clinics, an Arab network of legal clinics has convened in the region, and clinical programmes have been established with partners in Egypt, Turkiye, Lebanon, Jordan, Qatar, Kuwait, the Emirates and Iraq. If the clinic here is dormant, the network around it is a way to ask which one is not.

trackers.name: Qanoon — the laws in full and free, including how to become a body that can hold land
trackers.desc: THIS FILE HAS ESTABLISHED ACROSS THE REGION THAT THE BINDING BARRIER BETWEEN A COMMUNITY AND LAND, MONEY OR STANDING IS NOT MERIT BUT THE ABSENCE OF A REGISTERED LEGAL ENTITY. This portal publishes the CIVIL ASSOCIATIONS LAW in full and free, which is the checklist for becoming one. WHAT THE LAW REQUIRES AN ASSOCIATION'S STATUTE TO CONTAIN, AND IT IS WORTH DRAFTING BEFORE YOU APPROACH ANYONE: the NAME, the OBJECTIVES, the field of activity, THE MEANS BY WHICH THOSE OBJECTIVES WILL BE ACHIEVED, THE GEOGRAPHIC SCOPE OF THE WORK, and an administrative centre inside the country; the name, age, nationality, profession and residence OF EVERY FOUNDING MEMBER; the association's RESOURCES and how they are used and disposed of, together with the financial year; and its ORGANS and their competences, how members are chosen and removed, and THE QUORUM for the general assembly and the board and for the validity of their decisions. THE GEOGRAPHIC SCOPE REQUIREMENT IS THE ONE TO NOTICE: an association states the area it works in, which means a body can be constituted FOR A PARTICULAR VALLEY, COAST OR DISTRICT rather than in general terms. That is how a community becomes a legal person able to hold, receive and act for a specific place. TWO NAMING RULES CATCH PEOPLE OUT: a name must not cause confusion with an existing association, and A FOREIGN NAME IS NOT PERMITTED. Check the first before printing anything. THE PORTAL IS USEFUL BEYOND THAT ONE LAW. It carries Omani royal decrees, laws and ministerial regulations in full text, free, including the 2024 advocacy law whose representation thresholds and conflict-of-interest rule are recorded separately in this file for this country, and the commercial companies law. This payload has repeatedly told readers to check what a statute actually says rather than what an official summarises; in this country that is possible without payment or subscription. THE LIMITS. It is a legal information service, not an adviser — nobody there will tell you whether your draft statute is adequate, and registration decisions are made by a ministry. Texts may lag behind amendments, so check the date on the page and look for later decrees. And publication is not endorsement: reading the law tells you what is required, not whether permission will be granted. Use it with the university law college recorded separately for this country, which is where a draft statute can be read by someone qualified.

trackers.name: Municipal councils — elected members for your wilayat, and thirty competences to invoke
trackers.desc: YOUR WILAYAT ELECTS ITS OWN MEMBERS OF THE GOVERNORATE'S MUNICIPAL COUNCIL, AND THE NUMBER RISES WITH POPULATION: two representatives for a wilayat of up to thirty thousand Omanis, FOUR where the population exceeds thirty thousand, and SIX where it exceeds sixty thousand. A populous wilayat therefore has six people elected specifically to carry its concerns, which is more representation than most communities in this map have anywhere. THE LAW GIVES THESE COUNCILS THIRTY COMPETENCES, and the ministry's own framing is that the councils and their elected representatives are close to the reality of society and carry citizens' demands for services into development planning. Ask for the list of thirty and identify which one your problem falls under before you write — this file has found repeatedly across the region that a request naming the specific power being invoked is answered while a general complaint is not. THE COUNCIL IS A MIXED BODY AND YOU SHOULD KNOW THAT BEFORE APPROACHING IT: alongside the elected wilayat representatives sit senior government officials ex officio — none below the rank of director general — and two people of standing chosen by the minister on the governor's nomination, with the governor's office providing the secretariat. The elected members are the part answerable to you. HOW TO USE IT: go to your wilayat's elected members rather than to the council as an institution, give them a short written account with dates and the competence engaged, and ask for it to be tabled. This file has now recorded the same mechanism in three countries — a community does not petition the body, it gives an elected member something they can table. THE LIMITS: the councils advise and propose within government policy rather than deciding; the governor's office runs their administration; and nothing found shows one opposing a development scheme. Use them with the university law college and the free legal texts recorded separately for this country, which supply the rule and the reading of it.

trackers.name: Environment directory — the list of environment-interested groups in this country
trackers.desc: THE ENVIRONMENT AUTHORITY'S KNOWLEDGE CENTRE MAINTAINS A DIRECTORY OF ENVIRONMENT-INTERESTED GROUPS, WHICH IS THE ANSWER TO A QUESTION THIS FILE HAS FAILED TO ANSWER FOR THIS COUNTRY ACROSS SEVERAL ROUNDS: WHO ELSE IS THERE? Searching directly produced one national society and little else; the directory is where the rest are listed, with each group's founding, its registration decision and its stated objectives. USE IT THE WAY THIS FILE LEARNED TO USE THE EQUIVALENT DIRECTORY IN ANOTHER COUNTRY: SEARCH ON WHAT THE GROUPS SAY THEY ARE FOR, NOT ON THEIR NAMES. An organisation whose declared objects include monitoring, conservation of nature, or enabling citizens to take part in protection projects is one that can be approached about a specific place; a name alone tells you nothing. THE ENTRIES CARRY THE REGISTRATION DECISION NUMBER AND DATE, which matters more than it appears: a group's ministerial decision number is what proves it is a constituted legal person, and this payload's most repeated finding is that being a legal person is the barrier to everything else. IF YOU ARE LOOKING FOR A BODY TO APPLY FOR FUNDING WITH, TO HOLD LAND, OR TO PARTNER ON A PLANTING PERMIT, THIS IS WHERE YOU CONFIRM IT EXISTS IN LAW. THE SAME KNOWLEDGE CENTRE SITS ALONGSIDE THE AUTHORITY'S OTHER PUBLISHED MATERIAL, so it is also the place to check what the regulator itself says about a habitat or a species before you argue about it. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE THE SAME ONES THIS FILE ATTACHED TO THE EQUIVALENT DIRECTORY ELSEWHERE. A DIRECTORY IS A FINDING TOOL, NOT A RESOURCE — nobody in it is obliged to help you, and listing does not prove a group is still active. IT IS MAINTAINED BY THE STATE ENVIRONMENT AUTHORITY, so it lists groups the authority recognises and not those it does not. And a group's stated objects are what it registered, not necessarily what it now does — telephone before travelling.THIS DIRECTORY SITS INSIDE A WIDER KNOWLEDGE CENTRE, AND THREE OTHER THINGS IN IT ARE WORTH OPENING ALONGSIDE THE LIST ITSELF: AN ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH PLATFORM, AN ENVIRONMENTAL ATLAS OF THE COUNTRY, AND THE REGULATORY PROCEDURES FOR IMPLEMENTING THE NATIONAL LEGISLATION ON TRADE IN WILD SPECIES LISTED UNDER THE INTERNATIONAL TRADE CONVENTION. THE ENVIRONMENTAL ATLAS IS THE SECOND. AN ATLAS IS A PUBLISHED BASELINE: WHAT WAS RECORDED WHERE, AT A STATED DATE, BY THE AUTHORITY ITSELF. THIS FILE HAS SAID IN A DOZEN COUNTRIES THAT WHOEVER HOLDS THE EARLIER RECORD WINS THE ARGUMENT ABOUT CHANGE — AND HERE THE EARLIER RECORD IS THE REGULATOR'S OWN AND FREE TO CONSULT. THE WILDLIFE TRADE PROCEDURES MATTER FOR A NARROWER BUT SHARPER PURPOSE: WHERE PLANTS OR ANIMALS ARE BEING TAKEN FROM YOUR GROUND AND SOLD, THOSE PUBLISHED PROCEDURES SET OUT WHAT PERMISSION IS REQUIRED. ASK WHETHER THE TAKER HOLDS IT. AND THE RESEARCH PLATFORM IS WHERE TO LOOK BEFORE COMMISSIONING ANYTHING. STUDIES ALREADY DONE ON A HABITAT, A SPECIES OR A COASTLINE ARE FREE; A NEW STUDY IS NOT. ONE FURTHER LEAD, RECORDED HONESTLY AS A LEAD RATHER THAN A SERVICE: A UNIVERSITY CENTRE FOR ENVIRONMENTAL STUDIES AND RESEARCH APPEARS IN THAT DIRECTORY. IT HAS SECURED CLIMATE ADAPTATION AND MITIGATION FUNDING AND HOLDS A NATIONAL RESEARCH GRANT FOR MULTI-SCALE STUDIES TOWARDS THE SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT OF AN INVASIVE MESQUITE PLANT. INVASIVE MESQUITE IS WORTH KNOWING ABOUT WHEREVER IT GROWS: IT TAKES GROUNDWATER, CROWDS OUT NATIVE TREES AND MAKES GRAZING LAND UNUSABLE, AND A FUNDED NATIONAL RESEARCH PROGRAMME ON MANAGING IT MEANS THERE ARE SPECIALISTS TO ASK. WHETHER THE CENTRE ACCEPTS OUTSIDE SAMPLES OR REQUESTS WAS NOT VERIFIED — ASK BEFORE ASSUMING.

trackers.name: University research portal — find the centre and the named researcher who works on your problem
trackers.desc: BEFORE YOU CAN ASK ANYONE TO MEASURE ANYTHING, YOU HAVE TO KNOW WHO IN THE COUNTRY STUDIES IT. The national university publishes a research portal listing its RESEARCH CENTRES, ITS NAMED RESEARCHERS, THEIR PUBLICATIONS AND THEIR PROJECTS — openly, without a login. This file recorded a round earlier that this country has almost no named expertise in its listing at all; THIS IS WHERE THE NAMES ARE. THE CENTRES INCLUDE A WATER RESEARCH CENTRE, and the teaching itself tells you what expertise is held in-house: a course on SOIL AND WATER CONSERVATION covering erosion, sedimentation, wind erosion, salinity and drainage, THE PREDICTION OF SOIL EROSION, and SOIL AND WATER POLLUTION AND REMEDIATION STRATEGIES — with soil degradation and the management of soil and water resources IN THIS COUNTRY specifically discussed. A department that teaches the prediction of soil erosion contains people who can say what a cleared slope or a diverted wadi will do. HOW TO USE IT: search the portal for the subject of your problem — erosion, salinity, groundwater, coastal sediment, waste — read the publications that come back, and note THE AUTHORS AND THEIR DEPARTMENT. Then approach the department by name, citing their own published work on the subject. A request that shows you have read someone's paper is answered far more often than a general appeal for help. NOW THE HONEST LIMIT, AND IT IS THE POINT OF THIS ENTRY. THIS FILE RECORDED IN A NEIGHBOURING COUNTRY A UNIVERSITY LABORATORY THAT ANALYSES SOIL AND WATER SAMPLES FOR CITIZENS AS A STATED COMMUNITY SERVICE. NOTHING FOUND SHOWS THAT THIS UNIVERSITY OFFERS THE SAME, AND THIS ENTRY DOES NOT CLAIM IT DOES. The portal shows what is studied and by whom; it does not show what services are sold, at what price, or to whom. ASK THE DEPARTMENT DIRECTLY WHETHER IT ACCEPTS SAMPLES FROM THE PUBLIC — that single question is worth a telephone call, and the answer would upgrade this entry considerably. THE OTHER LIMITS: it is a state university, so it is not independent of the administration; researchers publish and teach rather than advocate; and a portal records past work, so recent departures and new arrivals may not be reflected. Use it with the environment directory and the national environment society recorded separately for this country — the society can measure and train, the directory lists the constituted bodies, and this names the individual expert.

trackers.name: The advocates' rolls — which courts your lawyer may actually enter, and the trade bar they must satisfy
trackers.desc: INSTRUCTING A LAWYER WHOSE ROLL DOES NOT COVER THE COURT YOUR CASE WILL REACH WASTES MONEY AND TIME YOU CANNOT RECOVER. ADVOCATES HERE ARE ENTERED ON ONE OF FOUR ROLLS: UNDER TRAINING; COURTS OF FIRST INSTANCE AND EQUIVALENT; COURTS OF APPEAL AND EQUIVALENT; AND SUPREME COURTS AND EQUIVALENT. THE ROLL DECIDES WHICH COURTS THE LAWYER MAY ENTER. Ask which roll, and ask it before the first fee is paid — because a land or planning case that begins in a first-instance court will very often go up on appeal, and a lawyer entered only on the lower roll cannot follow it there. THIS IS NOW THE THIRD COUNTRY IN THIS FILE WITH GRADED COURT AUTHORITY FOR ADVOCATES, so the question generalises: in this region, WHICH COURTS MAY THIS LAWYER ENTER is a standard question, not an insult. THE ENTRY CONDITIONS CONTAIN A CONFLICT RULE WORTH KNOWING: an advocate must be of good conduct, MUST NOT BE WORKING IN ANY SECTOR, AND MUST NOT BE ENGAGED IN TRADE. A person acting as your lawyer who also has commercial interests in construction or property is outside the conditions on which the roll admits advocates — the same bar this file recorded in another Gulf state, where an office engineer must declare that he does not trade in construction materials. THE OTHER CONDITIONS ARE PLAIN AND WORTH CHECKING: nationality, a minimum age of twenty-one, and a bachelor's degree in sharia or law. TRAINEES SIT ON THEIR OWN ROLL FOR TWO YEARS, REDUCED TO ONE FOR HOLDERS OF A MASTER'S DEGREE OR HIGHER — so a very junior advocate is identifiable from the roll alone. AND AN ADVOCATE IS ATTACHED TO A PLACE: on re-registration, a new lawyer's card issues ONLY where the applicant applies to open an office or to join a law firm or civil law company. A practising advocate therefore has a registered office, and an advocate who cannot name one is not in good standing. HOW TO USE THIS: ask for the roll, the card, and the office. Three questions, no cost, and they exclude the two failures this file has seen most often — an unqualified person acting as a lawyer, and a qualified one who cannot follow the case to the court that will decide it. THE LIMITS: this is a ministry's registration system, not a service — it will confirm rules and status, it will not find you a lawyer or pay for one. Nothing here provides free representation, and this file records the law college and the free legal texts portal separately for this country. Fees and rules change, so confirm the current position before relying on any figure.

trackers.name: Best environmental initiative award — money and official standing, and an individual or a group can win it
trackers.desc: THE SINGLE MOST COMMON FINDING IN THIS ENTIRE MAP IS THAT MONEY REQUIRES A REGISTERED ORGANISATION. THIS AWARD DOES NOT. Its stated purpose is to recognise the outstanding contributions of INDIVIDUALS, GROUPS, INSTITUTES OR ORGANISATIONS in managing or conserving the environment in this country — and IT CONSISTS OF A CERTIFICATE AND A MONETARY VALUE. A group of neighbours who have planted, cleaned, protected or monitored something is an eligible candidate. AND THE CERTIFICATE MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE MONEY, PERHAPS MORE. A group that the environment authority has publicly honoured is a group that is far harder to dismiss as troublemakers when it later objects to something — official recognition is the cheapest protection a community can hold, and this file has recorded almost no route to it. WHAT TO ENTER: the award is judged against the country's environmental policies, objectives and regulations, so DESCRIBE YOUR WORK IN THE STATE'S OWN TERMS — restored vegetation, reduced waste, protected habitat, monitored species — and cite the policy or regulation your work advances. That framing is what turns a local effort into an award submission. NOW THE SECOND THING THIS ROUND FOUND, AND IT IS TIME-SENSITIVE. THE NATURE RESERVES COMMITTEE HELD ITS FIRST MEETING OF 2026, chaired by the head of the environment authority, discussing files on THE DEVELOPMENT AND DECLARATION OF NATURE RESERVES to strengthen biodiversity protection. DECLARING RESERVES IS LIVE BUSINESS AND THERE IS A NAMED COMMITTEE DOING IT. A community that wants a stretch of coast, wadi or rangeland protected has a body that considers exactly such files — and a documented site, a species record and an award behind it is a stronger file than a letter. TWO FURTHER CURRENT FACTS WORTH KNOWING: the FIFTH PHASE of the plastic bag ban takes effect from 1 JULY 2026, and the country marked the international desertification day under the theme RANGELANDS — RECOGNISE THEIR VALUE, RESPECT THEM, RESTORE THEM. A national theme about rangelands is a hook for anyone defending grazing land this year. THE LIMITS: this is a state authority, the award is discretionary and measured against government policy, and nothing found shows it going to a group that has opposed a development — an application framed as opposition will not succeed. The reserves committee is a government body whose deliberations are not public. Use this with the environment society and the environment directory recorded separately for this country, which is where a group finds partners before it applies.

trackers.name: Native plant propagation — where the seeds, the methods and the map of what grows where actually exist
trackers.desc: THE LAST ROUND OF THIS FILE ESTABLISHED THAT RESTORATION FAILS ON TWO THINGS: WHERE THE PLANTS COME FROM, AND WHETHER ANYONE KNOWS HOW TO GROW THEM. THIS COUNTRY HOLDS AN UNUSUALLY COMPLETE ANSWER — by its own project director's account, THE ONLY BOTANIC GARDEN IN THE WORLD THAT HOLDS AND PROPAGATES NATIVE PLANTS ONLY, NOT IMPORTED ONES: 1,457 NATIVE SPECIES, OF WHICH ABOUT A HUNDRED GROW NOWHERE ELSE, representing the country's seven distinct environments across 430 hectares, and described as the largest plant complex in the region. WHAT IT IS BUILDING IS MORE USEFUL TO A COMMUNITY THAN THE GARDEN ITSELF: A DATABASE OF PLANT NAMES, WHERE EACH SPECIES OCCURS, AND THE METHODS OF PROPAGATING IT — alongside documentation of how those plants are used in daily life. THAT IS THE MISSING MANUAL FOR ANY REPLANTING SCHEME. If you want to restore a wadi, a hillside or a village margin with the species that actually belong there, THE PROPAGATION METHOD IS THE PART NOBODY HAS, and this is where it is being written down. IT ALSO GROWS MOST OF THE TRADITIONAL FIELD CROPS OF THE COUNTRY'S AGRICULTURAL OASES — which matters where a threatened oasis or falaj-fed terrace is being defended, because the crop varieties adapted to it are themselves the argument for what is being lost. THE HISTORY IS THE ENCOURAGEMENT. THESE PLANTS HAD NEVER BEEN PROPAGATED SCIENTIFICALLY OR SYSTEMATICALLY UNTIL 2006. The work began in a modest nursery run by A SINGLE MEMBER OF STAFF; a purpose-built nursery opened in 2008, and within a few years the propagation team had grown FROM ONE PERSON TO THIRTY-TWO. A COUNTRY-WIDE NATIVE PLANT CAPABILITY WAS BUILT IN UNDER TWENTY YEARS FROM ONE PERSON AND A SHADE HOUSE, which is the answer to anyone who says a community nursery is beyond them. WHAT TO ASK FOR, AND ASK PRECISELY: the propagation protocol for the species you want; the recorded distribution of that species, since planting it where it does not belong wastes a season; whether the garden will supply seed or seedlings to a community project, or advise one; and whether its field studies cover your area. Its stated aims include establishing centres for scientific research and FIELD STUDIES on environment and botany, so a request framed as fieldwork fits its purpose better than one framed as a donation. THERE IS A SECOND ADDRESS: A UNIVERSITY BOTANIC GARDEN ESTABLISHED IN 1991, THE FIRST IN THE COUNTRY, covering four and a half hectares within a science faculty — a smaller, academic route to the same expertise, and one this file has found is often more approachable than a flagship institution. THE LIMITS: it is a state institution under a ministry and also a visitor attraction, and NOTHING FOUND CONFIRMS THAT IT SUPPLIES PLANTS TO THE PUBLIC — that is the question to put, not an assumption to act on. Its own site was not reached; this rests on a published interview with its project director and national coverage, so verify before travelling. And a garden will not oppose a development: it grows plants and holds knowledge.

trackers.name: Regional defenders' centre — the outside route, and it names this country among eleven
trackers.desc: EVERY LEGAL AND CIVIC ENTRY THIS FILE HOLDS FOR THIS COUNTRY IS DOMESTIC: THE ADVOCATES' ROLLS, THE MUNICIPAL COUNCILS, THE ENVIRONMENT SOCIETY, THE STATE AWARD. THIS IS THE ONLY EXTERNAL ONE, AND THIS COUNTRY IS NAMED IN ITS REMIT. ITS EMERGENCY ASSISTANCE COVERS MEDICAL SUPPORT, TRAINING, SECURITY, TRIAL OBSERVATION AND EVACUATION, and it provides EMERGENCY GRANTS TO PEOPLE AT RISK alongside capacity grants to civil society partners, working with United Nations and European protection mechanisms including A TEMPORARY RELOCATION PROGRAMME. TRIAL OBSERVATION CONNECTS DIRECTLY TO SOMETHING ELSE IN THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING. This file recorded that advocates here are entered on FOUR GRADED ROLLS and that the roll decides which courts a lawyer may enter — so proceedings can end up before a court your advocate cannot appear in. AN OUTSIDE OBSERVER IN THAT ROOM IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF PROTECTION FROM A LAWYER, and can be requested even where representation is constrained. IT SUPPORTS INDEPENDENT LAWYERS TOO, which matters where the pool of advocates willing to act is small and everyone knows everyone. THE QUIET SERVICES ARE THE ONES TO USE FIRST: TRAINING IN MANAGING YOUR OWN SECURITY, and networking meetings that connect people working separately in different countries. Publication in English and Arabic and advocacy at United Nations bodies are available when needed, but they are the loud end of the range. THE LIMITS: it works on freedom of expression, association and assembly, so an environmental or land dispute reaches it only through detention, prosecution, threats or silencing. It is based abroad and publishes internationally, and approaching it is a deliberate step. ASK FIRST WHAT CAN BE DONE WITHOUT PUBLICITY. Use the domestic routes recorded separately here for anything that can be handled inside the country.

trackers.name: Forming an association or a volunteer team — the governor's no-objection, and a new law that recognises individual initiatives
trackers.desc: ALMOST EVERY ROUTE THIS FILE RECORDS FOR THIS COUNTRY — THE ENVIRONMENTAL AWARD OPEN TO GROUPS, THE RESEARCH PORTAL, THE MUNICIPAL COUNCILS, THE ADVOCATES' ROLLS — WORKS BETTER IF YOU ARE A CONSTITUTED BODY, AND NOTHING SAID HOW TO BECOME ONE. THE PAPERS ARE SHORT: A STATEMENT OF THE FOUNDING MEMBERS AND THE FIRST BOARD, THE MINUTES OF THE FOUNDING ASSEMBLY, THE MINUTES OF THE FIRST BOARD MEETING, AND A BOARD DECISION AUTHORISING WHOEVER FILES THEM. BUT ONE OF THOSE PAPERS IS THE WHOLE TEST, AND IT IS NOT PAPERWORK: THE STATEMENT OF FOUNDERS AND FIRST BOARD MUST BE APPROVED BY THE GOVERNOR, CONFIRMING NO OBJECTION TO THE ASSOCIATION AND TO ITS FOUNDERS. Everything else is form-filling; THIS IS A PERSON WHO MUST AGREE. Approach the governorate early, informally, with a clear and modest statement of purpose — and understand that objection can attach to individuals as well as to the body, which is worth knowing before deciding who signs as a founder. AND THE GROUND HAS JUST MOVED. A CIVIL SOCIETY INSTITUTIONS LAW ANNOUNCED IN JUNE 2026 IS DESCRIBED BY THE MINISTRY AS A LEGISLATIVE SHIFT, AND THREE OF ITS PROVISIONS MATTER TO ANY COMMUNITY. FIRST, IT DEFINES VOLUNTARY WORK as non-governmental, non-profit activity pursuing SOCIAL, HEALTH, CULTURAL, DEVELOPMENTAL, RELIEF OR AWARENESS purposes — and DEVELOPMENTAL is broad enough to cover most of what this map describes. SECOND, IT PERMITS ONE VOLUNTEER TEAM IN EACH DISTRICT, operating within an authorised geographic scope, EACH WITH ITS OWN BOARD OF DIRECTORS. That is a recognised local body with a defined territory — far lighter than an association, and there are already sixty such teams attached to social development committees, so the form is established rather than theoretical. NOTE THE LIMIT: ONE PER DISTRICT, so find out whether yours already has one and join it rather than competing with it. THIRD, AND MOST UNUSUAL, IT PERMITS VOLUNTARY WORK THROUGH INDIVIDUAL INITIATIVES TO IMPLEMENT A SPECIFIC PROJECT, on conditions to be set in the executive regulation. A SINGLE PERSON WITH ONE DEFINED PROJECT IS RECOGNISED — which is the lightest lawful vehicle this file has found anywhere in the Gulf, and the answer for someone who cannot assemble founders or wait for a governor. THE SECTOR YOU WOULD BE JOINING IS SMALL AND KNOWABLE: the ministry's own consultation counted 31 charitable associations, 31 professional associations, 59 women's associations with six branches, and 60 volunteer teams — and IT CONSULTED ALL OF THEM ON THE DRAFT LAW, which tells you these bodies are treated as partners in policy rather than merely licensed. THE LIMITS: registration is discretionary and the governor's no-objection is the point at which a purpose the authorities dislike will stop. The new law was announced in June 2026 and ITS EXECUTIVE REGULATION - which sets the conditions for individual initiatives - WAS NOT PUBLISHED WHEN THIS WAS RECORDED, so confirm before relying on that route. Read it with the environmental award open to individuals and groups, and the environment society, recorded separately here.

trackers.name: Housing and urban planning ministry — title deeds, land requests, and the change-of-use application that turns farmland into building land
trackers.desc: BURIED IN A LIST OF ROUTINE SERVICES IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST TO ANYONE DEFENDING FARMLAND: A REQUEST TO CHANGE THE USE OF AN AGRICULTURAL PLOT TO RESIDENTIAL OR COMMERCIAL — and, separately, A REQUEST TO CHANGE USE TO TOURIST. FARMLAND BECOMES BUILDING LAND BY APPLICATION HERE. THAT IS A FILED, NUMBERED REQUEST, NOT AN INVISIBLE DECISION, and it is the point at which a community can intervene. AND THE FORM ITSELF CARRIES THE OPENING: THE AGRICULTURAL CHANGE-OF-USE APPLICATION IS CONDITIONAL ON OBTAINING THE APPROVALS OF THE CONCERNED AUTHORITIES. Every approval is a body that can be written to, and a body that must answer. Where subdivision follows, the applicant must also produce SUBDIVISION MAPS FROM A CONSULTANCY OFFICE SHOWING THE NUMBER OF PLOTS SOUGHT — a document that reveals the true scale of a scheme long before anything is built. THE SAME MINISTRY HOLDS THE RECORD SIDE: IT REGISTERS ALL ORIGINAL AND SUBSIDIARY REAL RIGHTS OVER PROPERTY UNDER THE REAL ESTATE REGISTER AND ISSUES TITLE DEEDS. So establishing what is registered over a parcel, and what rights attach to it, is one enquiry to one body. IT ALSO PREPARES THE DETAILED LAND-USE PLANS AT REGIONAL AND GOVERNORATE LEVEL. As this file found in another country, THE PLAN DECIDES THE OUTCOME BEFORE ANY PERMIT IS SOUGHT — ask for the detailed plan covering your area first.
