Read this with the village mediation units, the village co-management committees, the district natural resources offices and the village funds entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: MyCO – Myanmar Companies Online
trackers.desc: National — DICA electronic company register, searchable free (Myanmar). — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Office of the Auditor General of the Union
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of Myanmar. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Myanmar.

trackers.name: PERAC Principles — protected zones when domestic machinery has stopped
trackers.desc: AN INSTRUMENT WRITTEN FOR EXACTLY THIS SITUATION, AND IT NAMES NO ONE. The Principles on Protection of the Environment in Relation to Armed Conflicts — 28 principles adopted by the International Law Commission on second reading on 27 May 2022 and welcomed by the UN General Assembly in A/RES/77/104 of 7 December 2022, adopted without vote — cover the whole arc: before, during and after armed conflict, and situations of occupation. BE HONEST ABOUT THEIR STATUS: they are nonbinding — but ILC documents are recorded as increasingly interpreted by tribunals, courts and governments as ‘reflections of customary international law’. Cite them as that, not as treaty obligations. PRINCIPLE 4 IS THE DESIGNATION ROUTE WHEN DOMESTIC MACHINERY HAS STOPPED: States should designate, by agreement or otherwise, areas of environmental importance as protected zones in the event of an armed conflict, including where those areas are of cultural importance — cultural importance is an express qualifying ground. PRINCIPLE 5 requires States, international organisations AND other relevant actors to protect the environment of the lands and territories that indigenous peoples inhabit or traditionally use, and where conflict has harmed it, to consult and cooperate with indigenous peoples on remedial measures — note that the addressees are not only States, which reaches bodies operating where a government cannot or will not act. PRINCIPLE 3 requires effective legislative, administrative, judicial and other measures. AND THE STRUCTURAL POINT: the ILC chose not to differentiate between international and non-international armed conflicts, so the environment-related conduct of non-state armed groups also comes within their purview — which matters where harm is done by armed groups rather than a state army. The distinctions sit in the commentaries, which should be read together with the principles. CITE ALONGSIDE: the 2020 ICRC Guidelines on protection of the natural environment in armed conflict, UNEA resolution 2/15 (27 May 2016), the 2019 Geneva List of Principles on the Protection of Water Infrastructure, and victim-assistance provisions in the Mine Ban Treaty and the Convention on Cluster Munitions.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: ECD — Myanmar's EIA procedure, and the disclosure duty that sits on the regulator
trackers.desc: Two public consultations are required, and the first is at scoping — before the study is designed. Under the Environmental Impact Assessment Procedure, Notification 616/2015, in force from 29 December 2015 under the Environmental Conservation Law 2012, a project is screened into one of three categories: EIA type, IEE type, or neither. For an EIA type project the proponent submits Terms of Reference and a Scoping Report setting out what the study will cover, and must hold a public consultation at that point to collect stakeholders' opinions. A further public consultation must be held at some point during the investigation itself. The Environmental Compliance Certificate is issued by the ministry on successful review. Scoping is where it is decided what will be studied at all, and it is the stage most likely to pass unnoticed. The disclosure duty falls on the department as well as on the proponent. Published research on the Procedure records that the proponent must disclose the report to the public and that the department is likewise required to disclose a submitted IEE or EIA report, so a request for the report goes to the regulator and not only to the company. Screening categories are set out in Annex A of the Procedure, the categorisation of economic activities for assessment purposes. The published account of capacity is not encouraging and should be planned around. The same research records limited resources and technical and institutional capacity producing delay and a backlog of unprocessed reports, poor quality submissions particularly from the mining sector, and limited budget, staff, equipment and facilities for monitoring, inspection and enforcement across the country. It also notes difficulty applying the Procedure to special economic zones, an absence of strategic environmental assessment for large developments, and inadequate public participation and information disclosure on the social impact side. This entry records the legal framework and the department that administers it, and nothing more. Conditions in Myanmar have changed substantially since the Procedure was written, and nothing here is an assessment of whether engaging with the process is currently safe or effective; that judgement belongs to people who can read the situation locally. The constitutional hooks the department itself cites are Section 45, under which the Union shall protect and conserve the natural environment, and Section 390(b), which makes environmental conservation a duty of every citizen.

trackers.name: Community forestry certificates — thirty years, on a residence or distance test
trackers.desc: Eligibility turns on where people live, not on what they own or how they are organised. Published accounts of the community forestry instructions record that local people who have lived around a forest area for at least five years, or within five miles of its periphery, may form a community forest user group and apply to the township or district forest officer for recognition and establishment of a community forest. That is a test most affected villages already satisfy, and it is the first thing to check rather than the last. Thirty years, extendable, and the newest category is the one to claim. A certificate granted to the group runs for thirty years and can be extended. Community forests are permitted in reserved forest, protected public forest, buffer zones within protected areas and land at the disposal of government; the 2019 instructions added forest-covered land managed by government organisations and, notably, natural forests and mangrove forests that local communities have conserved in accordance with their tradition. Where a community has already been protecting a forest or a mangrove, that last category describes what it has been doing. Write the management plan against the objectives the rules name. The department weighs whether the plan is suitable and whether the group is capable of implementing it, and the forest rules direct that a certificate serve stated objectives: supporting local needs for wood and non-wood forest products, reducing rural poverty through employment and income, increasing forest cover and sustainable use, promoting forest management with people's participation, and enhancing environmental services that support climate mitigation and adaptation by protecting against deforestation and degradation. A plan written in those terms is answering the question the department is required to ask. Expect it to take years, and read the caveat. Reported experience includes a mangrove community forest of more than two hundred hectares that took roughly eleven years from application to establishment, with numbers of community forests remaining low and applications delayed by the process itself. This entry records the framework and the department that administers it; conditions in Myanmar have changed substantially since these instructions were issued, and whether the route functions now is a judgement for people who can read the situation locally.

trackers.name: Where defence lawyers actually are — a public defender programme in five places, and why the statutory route cannot be relied on
trackers.desc: An international public defender organisation runs lawyers on the ground in named places. It opened a small office in Yangon in 2017 and describes serving communities in Yangon, Mandalay, Pathein in the Ayeyarwady Region, Lashio in Shan State, and Rakhine State. Its stated aims are expanding access to legal aid for vulnerable people, reducing pre-trial detention, torture and coercion, shortening the time between arrest and first contact with a lawyer, and protecting children and young people; it records that its lawyers have received well over six thousand hours of mentoring from experienced public defenders through its fellowship programme. For a country where this file has otherwise recorded only ministries, that is a list of places where a defence lawyer can be found. The statutory route exists on paper and should not be relied on. Published analysis records that the 2016 legal aid law created a union legal aid board with subsidiary boards at regional and township level, formed by the supreme court in November 2017; that the government-supported legal aid boards collapsed after the military takeover, with the head of the union board arrested; and that amendments in May 2021 removed legal aid at least during pre-trial detention and removed the independence of the legal aid bodies. An entry that recorded the law without recording what happened to it would be worse than useless. Ask for the nearest office rather than the nearest board. Where a statutory scheme has stopped functioning, the practical question is which organisations still have lawyers within reach, and the five locations above are the ones this organisation publishes. Other legal organisations have operated justice centres in Myanmar cities on similar lines, so it is worth asking each what it can still do rather than assuming a single answer. The standing caveat for this country applies with full force. This entry records what an organisation publishes about itself and what published analysis records about the statutory scheme. Conditions in Myanmar have changed substantially and continue to change; whether any office is open, and whether approaching it is safe or wise for a given person, is a judgement only people who can read the situation locally are able to make.

trackers.name: MNHRC complaints — four branch offices, a specified particulars list, and the court-matter bar
trackers.desc: The nearest office is not always Yangon. Complaints are addressed to the commission at its head office in Hlaing Township, Yangon, or to its branch offices in Nay Pyi Taw, Mandalay, Sittway and Pathein, and may be sent by registered post, delivered in person, sent by fax or sent to the commission's email address. For a community far from the commercial capital, the branch list is the practical part of this entry. The particulars are specified, and one of them is the harm. A complaint must give the complainant's full name, permanent address and full contact details; a detailed description of how the complainant's rights were violated and what harm or loss was suffered, with supporting documents or photographic evidence where available; a copy of the complainant's identity card; and the complainant's signature certifying that the particulars are correct. Write down the loss and not only the wrong — the commission asks for both, and a complaint that describes only the conduct leaves the damage unrecorded. The court bar is the limit worth knowing before filing. Matters that have been brought before a court, that are under the proceedings of a court, or that have been finally decided by a court fall outside the commission's complaints announcement. A complaint therefore belongs before litigation starts, or must concern something the litigation does not cover. What happens next, and the caveat this country's entries carry. The commission examines the complaints it receives, interviews the complainant where necessary, coordinates with the relevant departments and organisations, and where it concludes that alleged violations of constitutional fundamental rights are made out, takes steps under its rules of procedure. Against that: the commission's independence and its willingness to examine some categories of matter have been publicly questioned for many years, and conditions in the country have changed substantially. Whether to approach it at all, and under whose name, is a judgement only people who can read the local situation should make. Read this with the other entries recorded for this country.

trackers.name: DALMS — the department that holds the cadastral maps and the farmland records
trackers.desc: This is the office that holds the record. The settlement and land records department was renamed the department of agricultural land management and statistics by ministerial order in 2015, and its published functions include conducting land survey and updating maps and recorded data accurately and on time, collecting, compiling and disseminating land use data and agricultural statistics, and establishing an information system covering agriculture and land utilisation, with a programme to convert existing cadastral paper maps into digital ones. Where a household's farmland record or a village's cadastral sheet exists, this is the department that holds it, working through offices at township level with a staff numbered in the tens of thousands. Two laws are named in its own functions, and the second is the dangerous one. The department lists collaboration with the administrative bodies established under the farmland law and under the vacant, fallow and waste lands management law. A community told that the ground it uses is vacant, fallow or waste is being met with the second of those, and it is the law under which very large areas have historically been granted to agricultural companies. Knowing which of the two statutes a claim is being made under decides which body and which record matter. The honest limit, carried over from an earlier attempt. An earlier round of this research tried to record the farmland certificate procedure — which tier applies, which body decides a dispute over the right to farm — and declined to write it, because every text carrying that procedure sat on an unofficial translation rather than a state publication. That remains the position. This entry records the office and what it holds; it does not state the procedure, and a reader should ask the township office rather than rely on a translation circulating online. And the country caveat applies at full strength. Conditions have changed substantially since these pages were written. Whether the office functions as described in a particular township, who deals with it now, and whether approaching it is wise are judgements only people who can read the local situation should make. Read this with the assessment procedure, community forestry certificate, defence lawyer and complaint entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Tender directives — the township notice board, and the separate rule for leasing state land
trackers.desc: Notices go on the township notice board, and two weeks is the warning. Published translations of the tender procedure directive record that where the floor price of a lease or sale falls below a stated threshold, the tender committee shall prominently announce the lease or sale two weeks before the tender opening date on the notice boards of the relevant ministry, the general administration department, and the district and township administration offices. For a village, that puts the announcement within walking distance, and it means the habit worth forming is reading the township office board rather than waiting to be told. The announcement has prescribed contents. The same text lists what an announcement must contain: the name and address of the purchasing department or organisation, the quality specifications and the content of what is being tendered, the required capacity of the bidder, the fee for the tender documents, the place, procedure and last date to bid, the tender period and the amount of the tender guarantee. A notice missing those is defective against the directive's own list. Leasing state land has its own directive. A later procurement directive refers to the separate directive to be followed when leasing, transferring or entering a joint venture involving state-owned land and buildings, to standard operating procedures for requesting state funds and tenders in construction works, and to a notification on unsolicited proposals submitted voluntarily. Where land beside a village is leased or transferred to a company, there is a named instrument governing it, and asking which one was followed is a narrow question with a documentary answer. The caveat is the entry's most important line. These provisions are recorded from published translations and legal analyses rather than from the state's own publication. This research previously declined to record a farmland procedure for that same reason, and the difference here is what the entry actually claims: not a step-by-step a household must follow, but the existence of local notice board publication, of a required content list, and of a separate instrument for state land — each of which can be checked at the township office rather than against a translation. The standing caution recorded for every entry in this country applies. Read this with the land records department, the assessment procedure, the community forestry certificate and the companies register entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Anti-Corruption Commission — the complaint route, the conflict rule, and the published cases
trackers.desc: Read the caution before the description. Recording an institution in this file is not recommending it, and that applies with particular force here. A complaint of this kind identifies the person making it, conditions in this country have changed substantially since much of this material was published, and whether approaching this body is safe or useful in a given case is a judgement only people who can read the local situation should make. What follows is what the institution is and what its law provides. What the complaint route is. The commission was formed under the anti-corruption law, and the state's own description of it records that members of the public may complain where they have suffered loss because of corruption in their dealings with government departments, private business enterprises and social organisations. Complaint letters are examined by complaint scrutiny and review teams formed for the purpose and are then discussed at the commission's weekly meeting. The law bars a conflicted investigator. The anti-corruption law provides that a person shall not be included in an investigation board if they have an interest in the matter complained of, are prejudiced against the accused, are related to the complainant or the accused, or have a business relationship with either of them. Where an investigation goes nowhere, who sat on the board is a question the statute itself makes relevant. Outcomes are published. The commission publishes case news naming former ministers, mayors, deputy mayors, secretaries, municipal directors and enterprise executives charged or imprisoned under the law, including matters concerning construction projects, mining and electricity enterprises. A published record of who has actually been charged is the only way a community can judge whether a route of this kind has ever led anywhere. Read this with the land records department, the tender directives, the companies register, the assessment procedure and the complaint entries already recorded for this country, each of which carries the same caution.

trackers.name: BANCA — published surveys by place, and the specialists behind them
trackers.desc: The published survey library is the resource. This national conservation association's site carries a substantial set of reports organised by place and subject: coastal wetlands, a Rakhine survey, rapid assessments of the Gulf of Mottama, reports on Tanintharyi, Inle and Moeyungyi, a case study of the ecosystem services a wildlife sanctuary renders to the local communities around it, turtle and dugong material, monitoring of migratory shorebirds, species action plans and annual reports. A community facing a project near any of those places can cite an existing survey rather than commission one, and an existing survey with a date on it is harder to dismiss than a claim made for the first time in an objection. The disciplines are named. The organisation describes its backbone as competent ornithologists together with botanists, foresters, zoologists, social scientists, mammalogists, geologists, environmental scientists, marine biologists and herpetologists. Where the question is what actually lives on a site, or who can say so credibly, that list is the answer, and it is the nearest expertise this file has found in this country. Ecosystem services to local communities is one of its published subjects. Among the reports is a case study of what a wildlife sanctuary provides to the people living around it. That is the argument form a community usually needs: not that a place is valuable in the abstract, but that it supplies something measurable to the households beside it. Standing, and the caveats. The association was officially recognised by the home affairs ministry in 2004 and has been active since 2002, describes itself as non-profit, non-political and non-religious, and is the national partner of an international bird conservation body and a member of a national environmental network. Much of the published library predates 2021, and the standing caution recorded for every entry in this country applies to approaching any organisation — but the reports remain usable as baseline evidence even where present capacity is unknown. Read this with the community forestry certificate, the assessment procedure and the land records entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Office of the Auditor General — an interim report for urgent findings, and the supervisor of the accountants
trackers.desc: Urgent findings produce a document straight away. The published description of how audits are conducted records that findings are thrashed out in discussion with the audited body during the audit and before the final report is issued, and that only those which cannot be resolved that way are written into the report. But where a finding is important — the examples given are fraud or the misappropriation of cash or stores needing immediate legal action — an interim report is issued on it without waiting for the audit programme to be completed. A community that has evidence of something urgent is therefore asking for a document the system already provides for, rather than for an exception. An audit can be assigned, but not by you. Among the categories of audit is the audit of special assignment, carried out where the President, the speaker of one of the legislative chambers, a union level organisation, a union ministry or the council of the capital assigns it; the office's duties include presenting its findings to the relevant organisations after such an audit. The request route therefore runs through those bodies rather than through the office directly, which is worth knowing before a letter is addressed. The accountants who sign a company's accounts are supervised here. The office supervises the accountancy council and the institute of certified public accountants, provides them with guidance, and determines and supervises the duties, ethics and rights of certified public accountants and practising accountants. Where a developer's figures rest on accounts signed by such a professional, the body that supervises the signer has a name and an address. And private accounts can be revisited on tax grounds. The office's duties include auditing, if necessary, the accounts of private businesses which have already been audited by a certified public accountant or practising accountant, in relation to the taxes payable to the Union. The standing caution recorded for every entry in this country applies, and one limit should be stated plainly: the office publishes its legal framework and has a publications section, but this research did not establish a public register of audit reports. Read this with the anti-corruption commission, the land records department, the tender directives and the companies register entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Water testing — the city laboratory's published fees and turnaround, and the accredited national laboratory
trackers.desc: The city health laboratory publishes its fees and its turnaround. The national services portal sets out the water testing offered by the city development committee's public health department: a bacteriological test and a chemical test, each at a stated fee, with the bacteriology result returned in three days and the chemistry result in seven; individual ion determinations — copper, chloride, aluminium, phosphate, zinc, alkalinity, boron, manganese, potassium and iron — are separately priced, with a stated total if the whole set is ordered. A community can therefore budget a water test before it takes a single sample, which is the step that usually stops people. The sampling rules are the part people get wrong. For the bacteriological test a sterile bottle is collected from the laboratory, filled and delivered within two hours, or carried in an icebox where that is not possible; for the chemical test the sample is filled into a two gallon plastic container and sent in. A sample collected outside those rules is a sample the other side can dismiss without arguing about the result, so the collecting should be done exactly as the laboratory specifies. There is an accredited national laboratory for metals in water. The research department's national analytical laboratory holds ISO/IEC 17025:2017 accreditation, issued in 2025 by a foreign accreditation body, for the determination of copper, iron, manganese, nickel and zinc in water by flame atomic absorption spectrometry. Where a result has to survive challenge, accreditation for the exact substance and method is the thing to ask about — the same test this file applies to laboratories in Taiwan and Hong Kong. Other state laboratories exist for narrower purposes, including a fisheries department analytical unit which runs a national monitoring programme for residues of veterinary medicines and environmental contaminants and tests potable water at processing factories. Two cautions: the published fees and turnaround times date from an earlier period and should be confirmed at the office before relying on them, and the standing caution recorded for every entry in this country applies. Read this with the conservation association's surveys, the assessment procedure and the land records entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The sector-wide impact assessments and company disclosure rankings — a closed centre's archive, and who continues it
trackers.desc: The sector assessments are field-based baselines for the industries that take land. Assessments were completed on oil and gas in 2014, tourism and information and communications technology in 2015 and mining in 2017, each built on desk research and on fieldwork in locations across the country that had already experienced investment from the sector in question, with a more limited baseline on private security companies carried out between 2020 and 2022 and further guidance on the link between biodiversity, business and human rights. A community facing a mine, a pipeline or a resort can therefore begin from a published account of what that industry has already done to places like theirs, rather than from an argument about what it might do. The disclosure rankings show what a company does and does not publish. The transparency reports assess information disclosure on the corporate websites of hundreds of large companies — around two hundred and fifty in one edition and two hundred and sixty in another, covering listed and public companies, banks, and in one year dozens of the most important state-owned economic enterprises — and summarise the regulatory requirements on corporate governance and disclosure, including corruption, environmental impact assessment and beneficial ownership. Where a company publishes nothing about who owns it or what it assessed, the ranking turns that silence into a documented finding. The centre has closed; the archive and a successor remain. Published accounts record that the centre operated between 2013 and 2024, and that the transparency reports continue to be produced by a partner consultancy, intended to support the work of a directors' institute. The practical instruction is to cite the archive, which is still online, and to approach the successor for anything current — not to write to a centre that no longer exists. The assessments were built to feed local processes. Each was intended to inform advocacy on the emerging regulatory framework, particularly investment regulation and environmental and social impact assessment, and to supply the agenda for multi-stakeholder dialogue. That is the use to make of them: not as reading, but as the source of the specific questions an assessment of a local project should have answered and did not. The standing caution recorded for every entry in this country applies. Read this with the conservation association's published surveys, the assessment procedure, the companies register and the tender directive entries already recorded here.

trackers.name: Paung Ku — support built for small volunteer groups, in the sectors this file is about
trackers.desc: Read the caution before the description. Recording an organisation in this file is not recommending that anyone approach it. Conditions in this country have changed substantially since much of the published material about civil society support was written, funding routes have narrowed and shifted, and whether contacting any organisation is safe or useful in a given case is a judgement only people who can read the local situation should make. What follows is what the organisation says it does. Its stated sectors include land and natural resource governance. The organisation describes itself as a civil society body working towards a pluralistic society, and lists the work it supports as spanning education, emergency response, investment, labour, land, local governance, media, natural resource governance, peace building, and energy and environment. A dispute about land or about who controls a resource is therefore inside its stated remit rather than an awkward fit — which is not true of most organisations that fund community work. It was designed for groups too small for ordinary grants. Published programme documents record the rationale for its creation: that very few funding and support mechanisms cater for small, volunteer-based community level organisations which do not need large grants and are not seeking to grow into professionalised non-governmental organisations. That is precisely the profile of a village committee formed to oppose a project, and it is the profile most funding structures in this file quietly exclude. Its method is to build on what already exists. The organisation states that its work rests on a belief in the existing strengths and abilities, the networks and relationships, and the resilience of the country's civil society, rather than on installing new structures. Two limits should be stated: this research did not establish current grant windows, sizes or application routes, and they should be confirmed before anything is prepared; and the standing caution recorded for every entry in this country applies with particular force to any approach for money. Read this with the conservation association's published surveys, the community forestry certificate, the companies register and the tender directive entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: MIMU — free boundary data, the place-code system, and eight hundred georeferenced survey sheets from 1899 to 1946
trackers.desc: Free maps and datasets, under a licence that permits reuse. The unit's products are stated to be not for sale and usable free of charge with attribution, and its boundary datasets — township polygons and ward polygons covering more than two hundred towns, digitised mainly at one in two hundred and fifty thousand — download as shapefiles and as GeoJSON, with place names taken from the administration department's township profile maps in Myanmar script with transliteration. One restriction is published and should be respected: the geospatial datasets may not be used on an online platform without prior written agreement. The standing caution recorded for every entry in this country applies to any approach or use. The place-code system is what lets one source be compared with another. The unit maintains a system of codes giving unique references to some sixty-seven thousand locations, carrying place names in Myanmar with English transliteration, commonly used local names where they exist, the location and the administrative structure each place sits in — village tract, ward, township, district — and the status of each place against official listings together with historical changes such as new, deleted or merged villages. When a project document names one village and a government list names another, the code is how a community establishes that the two are the same place, or that one of them has been deleted. Published accounts record that the unit had mapped about four fifths of the country's sixty-six thousand villages by 2023, working with civil society organisations. Historic survey sheets covering three quarters of the country are georeferenced and open. Its resources pages record that about eight hundred and twenty sheets originally produced between 1899 and 1946 at one inch to the mile and at half and quarter inch scales have been scanned, georeferenced and shared publicly under an open licence, covering roughly three quarters of the country. A survey sheet more than a century old showing a village, a stream, a track or a forest edge is evidence about what was there before a project, and it costs nothing. Baseline statistics, township profiles and an assessment library sit alongside the maps. Published descriptions record a baseline dataset compiling hundreds of indicators from hundreds of sources, shared also as interactive township profiles; a tool giving access to thousands of assessment documents from nearly two hundred agencies; activity data contributed voluntarily by hundreds of organisations; and flood monitoring and emergency preparedness dashboards developed with a satellite analysis service. Read this with the cadastral and farmland records department, the community forestry certificate, the assessment procedure and the small-group funding entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Independent media in exile, and where documentation goes when publication is not the aim
trackers.desc: Read the risk before anything else in this entry. Published assessments describe the country as one of the most dangerous in the world for journalists, with more than sixty detained and reports of targeted killings including journalists shot by armed forces; record that the encrypted messaging application most used for secure contact was blocked in July 2024, described at the time as the last remaining secure communication channel; and record that journalists uninstall both that application and their virtual private network before going out in public, because of random checks of passers-by's phones. Reporters describe relying on underground networks, encrypted communication and second-hand verification. Nothing here is a recommendation to make contact: it is a record of who exists and of what the conditions around them are. The independent outlets now work from outside, and there are many of them. Published sector tracking records that most exiled media are based in Thailand, particularly in the northern city and the border towns, with others operating from border areas near India and Bangladesh in semi-exile; that several larger outlets have maintained consistent operations under extreme constraints; that a consortium represents fourteen ethnic outlets; and that fifty-four independent exiled outlets were being tracked as of mid-2025, with a combined following in the tens of millions on one social platform. For a village whose case is regional, the ethnic and region-specific outlets are the ones to identify rather than the national names. Funding models are published, and they tell you something. One newsroom is described as a registered non-profit operating outside the country on subscriptions and donations; another has declined a paywall in favour of a membership programme in order to keep its reporting accessible; the oldest was founded in 1993 by journalists in exile and describes itself as unaffiliated with any political party, organisation or government. Disputes about ownership and past influence have been published between these outlets themselves — read what they have written about each other before choosing where to take anything. Documentation has a destination that is not a newsroom. An independent investigative mechanism established by the United Nations Human Rights Council collects, consolidates, preserves and analyses evidence of the most serious international crimes and violations of international law committed in the country, for use in future trials; separately, a support network exists for media professionals and human rights defenders at risk, and an activist group documenting the military's financial links works with media and whistleblowers on investigative reports. Where the aim is preservation of evidence rather than immediate publication, that mechanism, not a newspaper, is the destination. Read this with the assessment procedure, the community forestry certificate, the cadastral and farmland records department and the small-group support entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Cultural heritage regions — exploration for minerals is prohibited outright inside them, and roads and canals need permission
trackers.desc: The standing caution for this country applies to everything below. The legislation described here is on the statute book and was amended in 2019, but this research did not verify how, or whether, it is administered now, and nothing here is an assurance that an approach to any office is safe or effective. Inside a cultural heritage region, exploring for minerals is prohibited outright. The law provides that no person shall, within a cultural heritage region, destroy an ancient monument, wilfully alter the original ancient form, structure or workmanship of one, excavate to search for antiquities, or explore for petroleum, natural gas, precious stones or minerals. That is a flat prohibition rather than a permit condition, and for a community facing an extraction project it is the strongest sentence in this entry: the question becomes whether the ground falls inside a declared region, not whether the exploration can be made acceptable. Roads, bridges, canals and embankments require prior permission. Within the cultural heritage region, prior permission is required to carry out renovation and maintenance of an ancient monument without altering its original form, to carry out archaeological excavation, and to build a road or construct a bridge, irrigation canal or embankment or extend any of them. Within the ancient monumental zone or the ancient site zone, permission is required to construct or extend a building, or to renovate a monument or extend the boundary of its enclosure. Within the protected and preserved zone, permission covers constructing, extending or renovating a hotel, motel, guest house, lodging house or industrial building, or extending its enclosure. Two further levers exist, and one of them removes buildings. The ministry may cause a building which is not an ancient monument and which obstructs the view of an ancient monument or of the surrounding natural landscape within the region to be dismantled, and may determine region by region the conditions to be observed in constructing buildings; the department may prohibit any person from ploughing or cultivating within the boundary of an ancient monument or site, or from carrying out any activity that may damage the cultural heritage. Where the zones are, and the first thing to check. The cultural heritage region is defined as the ancient monumental zone, the ancient site zone or the protected and preserved zone prescribed under the law, administered by the archaeology department, which has branches in all states and regions; departmental material records forty-six demarcated cultural zones nationally across those three types, at named places. Whether a site sits inside a demarcated zone is therefore the first thing to establish, before any argument about the project itself. Read this with the assessment procedure, the community forestry certificate, the cadastral and farmland records department and the mapping and place code entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Community protected areas — a category in the 2018 law, with co-management, buffer zones and payment for ecosystem services
trackers.desc: The standing caution for this country applies throughout. The law described here was issued in May 2018 and this research did not verify how, or whether, it is administered now; published accounts at the time recorded that the rules under it were still being revised. What follows records what the statute provides, not an assurance that an approach is safe or effective. Community protected areas are a category in the statute. Published analysis of the biodiversity and protected areas law records that its chapter on protected areas recognises community protected areas as a category of protected area in their own right, and that the forest department is required to provide technical coordination and support for the management of them. A community seeking protection for its own forest, wetland or hill is therefore asking to be placed in an existing statutory category and to receive the support the law obliges the department to give, rather than asking for an exception. Co-management and buffer zones apply to every protected area, not only community ones. The same analysis records that the director general may allow co-management in collaboration with the local community in order to maintain a balance between the sustainable socio-economic development of local communities and biodiversity conservation, and may define buffer zones allowing local communities' socio-economic development activities and ecotourism development without adverse impacts on the core zone. Where a community lives beside an existing reserve rather than inside a proposed one, the buffer zone provision is the one to name. Payment for ecosystem services is provided for. The law empowers the director general to determine a system for payment for ecosystem services derived from the ecosystems within a protected area. Published analysis notes that the law gives no further detail on how such a system would work, but that together with the ecotourism provisions it opens the way for communities to earn income from the ecosystem services their protected area provides — which is the answer to the objection that protection costs a village its livelihood. Who else the law creates, and the honest limit. The law creates the position of park warden, an officer of the forest department whose duties include mobilising the public to take part in conservation through public education, and provides for regional or state governments to constitute biodiversity and protected areas management bodies; penalties for infringement are heavier than under the legislation it replaced, and the law also carries the country's obligations under the international convention on trade in endangered species. The limit is that the implementing rules were reported as still under revision, so the procedure for applying for a community protected area may not be settled. Read this with the community forestry certificates, the assessment procedure, the biodiversity association's published surveys and the support organisation for small volunteer groups already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Law reports and judgment lists — where decisions of the highest court are published, with the coup-period caution that applies to all of it
trackers.desc: Caution first: this entry describes institutions operating under military control since the 2021 coup. Everything below is recorded because the documents and collections exist and remain useful for research, not because the courts can be relied on to decide against the authorities. Anyone approaching them should take advice on personal risk before filing anything, and should treat published procedure as a description of the system on paper. The court publishes judgment lists and cause lists. The highest court's site carries a list of cases in which judgment is to be delivered and a list of cases called in advance, alongside its own institutional material. Those two listings answer the question a community can otherwise only answer through a lawyer: whether a case exists and when it will be dealt with. The law reports are the substantive collection, and much of it is open access. Published library guidance records that the law reports published decisions of the central court from 1974 to 1988 and, after 1988, of the reconstituted supreme court; that these reports are available online through an open-access national law library database as replicas of the printed reports; that since 1970 the reports are in the national language only; and that a regional legal information institute carries the English-language reports for 1947 to 1969, linked to a case citator showing which cases were cited and which later cases cite them. Academic work confirms that the English-language volumes of that period are available through the court's own site. The constitutional tribunal publishes separately, and has heard few cases. The same guidance records a submissions and decisions database on the constitutional tribunal's site, some decisions in English and some in the national language, and notes that the tribunal has decided few cases. What the highest court can do. Published accounts of the system record original jurisdiction in disputes between the union and region or state governments and in certain other classes, appellate jurisdiction over judgments of the region and state high courts and other courts, and revisionary power over any judgment or order of a subordinate court. Read this with the farmland registration entry, the environmental conservation complaints and the legal aid entries already recorded for this country, each of which carries the same caution.

trackers.name: Community forestry certificates — a thirty-year certificate to a user group, what land qualifies, and the documented ways it fails
trackers.desc: Caution first, as with every entry for this country: the institutions described operate under military control since 2021, and enforceability is unverified. The certificate is recorded because it is the one instrument by which a community here obtains a documented, time-limited right over forest land. A certificate is issued to a forest user group for thirty years. Published accounts record that the community forestry instructions, issued in 1995 and amended in 2016 and 2019 under the forest legislation, allow a community forestry certificate to be issued to a forest user group for a thirty-year term that can be extended, and that registered users may then form community forestry enterprises and user groups and sell forest products while regenerating degraded forest. The forest rules of 2019 set out the objectives to be considered in granting a certificate: supporting local needs for wood and non-wood products, reducing rural poverty through employment and income, increasing forest cover and sustainable use, promoting management with people's participation, and enhancing environmental services protecting against deforestation and degradation. Write the application to those five objectives in those terms. Where a community forest can be established changed in 2019. The current instructions permit community forests in reserved forest, protected public forest, buffer zones in protected areas and land at the disposal of the government, and — in place of the earlier reference to land under government agencies and land owned by private parties and non-governmental organisations — specify forest-covered lands managed by government organisations and natural and mangrove forests conserved by local communities in accordance with their tradition under a named provision of the forest law. That last category is the one to invoke where a community has conserved a forest customarily. The documented weaknesses, stated plainly. Reporting records that the number of community forests remains low against a master plan target of establishing them on 918,636 hectares by 2030, with about 221,169 hectares achieved as of one count — roughly a quarter of the target; that many community attempts have been frustrated or substantially delayed by the forest department, which authorises them, and by burdensome application bureaucracy; that critics argue the certificates can facilitate land grabs and give rights to a user group rather than the whole community; and that at the end of the thirty years the department can cancel the certificate, while during the term the community forest can be compulsorily acquired with compensation. Read this with the farmland registration, the environmental conservation complaints and the law reports entries already recorded here.

trackers.name: Organisation Registration Law 2022 — registration now compulsory, five citizens to form, and a sixty-day annual report
trackers.desc: Caution first, as with every entry for this country: this law was issued by the authorities that took power in 2021, and registering brings a group into their oversight. The entry is recorded because a community that intends to receive and hold donations needs to know what the current framework demands and what it exposes them to. Take advice on personal risk before registering anything. Registration is no longer voluntary. Published assessments record that the 2022 organisation registration law repealed and replaced the 2014 association registration law, removing the voluntary provision that had made the earlier regime relatively enabling, and mandating registration for all associations regardless of size or location under penalty of criminal sanctions; a United Nations human rights office statement records criminal penalties of up to five years' imprisonment for failure to comply. Practitioner summaries record that a local organisation means a non-governmental body formed with five or more citizens to carry out activities without the purpose of making profits, and that an international organisation must now have at least forty per cent citizens on its executive committee and obtain approval of its intended programmes and objectives. What registration gives, in the law's own terms. Practitioner summaries record that registered organisations are separate legal entities with the right to sue and be sued, to receive aid from local or international organisations or individuals, to collect donations and establish funds, and to own property and trademark rights including their name, seal, mark and uniform design. Those are the powers a community needs to hold money — and they are conditioned on registration. The reporting clock is sixty days. Registered organisations must submit an annual report within sixty days in December each year, with the type of report varying by registration tier; failure attracts administrative action including warning, limitation of activities for a specified period and temporary suspension. Organisations registered under the earlier law and awaiting renewal are recorded as able to begin the re-application process. Read this with the community forestry certificate, the farmland registration, the environmental complaints and the law reports entries already recorded here, each carrying the same caution.

trackers.name: Land Acquisition, Resettlement and Rehabilitation Law 2019 — what it covers, what it excludes, and the committees that run it
trackers.desc: Caution first, as with every entry for this country: enforceability under the present authorities is unverified. The law is recorded because it is the framework a community will be told applies to it, and because knowing what it excludes matters as much as knowing what it covers. A single law now covers acquisition, compensation, resettlement and rehabilitation. Practitioner summaries record that the union parliament enacted the land acquisition, resettlement and rehabilitation law in August 2019 as law number 24 of 2019, replacing the colonial-era acquisition legislation of 1894; that it applies to all matters relating to acquisition of land, payment of compensation and damages, resettlement and socioeconomic rehabilitation for the use, control and management of land for a public purpose; and that it integrates resettlement and rehabilitation into the acquisition framework for the first time in this country. Its stated aims include protecting the interests of people affected by acquisition, promoting a transparent and inclusive approach, and preventing adverse social and environmental impacts. The exclusion is the part to check first. The same summaries record that the law excludes from its scope compensation and damages for the acquisition of farmland and the reclamation of vacant, fallow or virgin land. Since much rural land is held under the farmland regime or classified as vacant, fallow or virgin, a community's first question is which regime the land it stands on is recorded under — because that determines whether this law's compensation provisions apply at all. Who administers it. The union cabinet establishes a union-level central committee to oversee acquisition, resettlement and rehabilitation affairs, and that committee organises working groups in each state or region to implement them. Where a project is proceeding, the working group for the state or region is the body to identify and address. Practitioner summaries also record that the law took effect on a date appointed by notification and that implementing rules were to be issued later, with rules and directions made under the repealed 1894 Act continuing to apply meanwhile so far as they do not contradict the new law. Read it alongside the documented failure mode. Published research opens with the situation this file exists to address: villagers reading a notice at a distant township office about land their families had cultivated for decades, now classified as vacant and partly fenced, with the objection deadline already passed and displaced former cultivators living elsewhere unaware. Watch the township office notice board, and keep a dated photograph of any notice found there. Read this with the cadastral records department, the community forestry certificate, the tender directives and the law reports entries already recorded here, each carrying the same caution.

trackers.name: National Environmental Quality (Emission) Guidelines — published numbers for air, noise, vibration and liquid discharge, and the prior permission chapter
trackers.desc: Caution first, as with every entry for this country: enforcement under the present authorities is unverified. The guidelines are recorded because the numbers are published and can be measured against, whoever is or is not enforcing them. There are national numbers for emissions, noise and discharges. Published resources record that the first set of national environmental quality guidelines regulating emissions across a number of sectors was released on 29 December 2015, providing performance parameters for the regulation and control of air emissions, noise and vibration and liquid discharges from various sources in order to prevent pollution and protect human and ecosystem health, and that they were based primarily on an international lender's general environmental health and safety guidelines. An unofficial English translation is published alongside the Burmese text. A community with a laboratory result or a noise reading can compare it against a stated national parameter rather than an impression. The wider framework, and what the ministry is empowered to prescribe. Practitioner material records that the environmental conservation legislation of 2012 and its rules of 2014 set out the ministry's duties and powers, including prescribing environmental quality standards on emissions, effluents, solid waste, production procedures, processes and products; facilitating the settlement of environmental disputes; specifying categories and classes of hazardous wastes generated from chemicals and other hazardous substances used in industry, agriculture, mineral production and sanitation; prescribing categories of hazardous substances that may significantly affect the environment; and prescribing terms and conditions for effluent treatment in industrial estates, buildings and other sites and for emissions of machines, vehicles and mechanisms. Facilitating dispute settlement is a stated function to invoke. Prior permission is a named chapter. The same material records that the rules devote a chapter to prior permission across named articles, that environmental quality standards and assessment procedures followed in 2015 and 2016, and that new conditions may be attached to existing investments so they comply with evolving requirements — which means an operating project is not beyond the reach of new conditions. It also records the department having reviewed environmental assessments for more than a hundred investment projects, several dozen of which underwent full assessment. The constitutional hook. The same source records the constitutional provision that the union shall protect and conserve the natural environment, and the citizen's duty to assist in environmental conservation and in preservation of cultural heritage and public property. Read this with the assessment procedure, the water testing laboratory, the human rights commission complaints and the community forestry entries already recorded here, each carrying the same caution.

trackers.name: Registered third-party assessment consultants — only approved firms may write the report, and the association that publishes the licensing procedure
trackers.desc: Caution first, as with every entry for this country: the framework described here predates the 2021 coup and current administration of it is unverified. Only registered consultants may write an assessment report, which makes the register a checkable list. Practitioner material records that under a named article of the 2015 assessment procedure only consulting firms approved and registered with the ministry may prepare assessment reports for projects in the country, covering initial environmental examination, environmental and social impact assessment and environmental and social management and monitoring plan reports. Published analysis records that for a full assessment project the proponent must submit detailed information about the organisation undertaking the investigation and reporting to the department for approval before the study starts, and that the study team must be duly registered third-party consultants, individual or organisational — whereas an initial examination may be conducted by the proponent itself or a consultant. Asking who wrote the report and whether they are registered is a first-order question about any assessment. The licensing procedure moved to individual approval first. A national environmental assessment association records that the department launched a licensing procedure for third-party consultants and organisations based mainly on individual consultant approval, that all third-party consultants must apply for new registration under it whether or not they held a previous certificate, and that firms may apply for organisation licences only after their core members have been approved; the association publishes the full procedure for download. That association is also the sector body a community can approach for names of practitioners. The procedure's own steps tell you when to appear. Published analysis records that after departmental approval of the assessing organisation the proponent submits terms of reference and a scoping report, that this scoping stage exists only for full assessment projects, that investigation begins only after those documents are approved, and that public consultation must be held during both scoping and investigation for full assessment projects. Two consultation moments, not one. Other registers exist for the technical trades. The engineering council maintains membership and registration for engineers, including chartered professional recognition at regional level — the place to look for an independent engineer to read a design. Read this with the assessment procedure, the emission guidelines, the water testing laboratory and the biodiversity association entries already recorded here, each carrying the same caution.

trackers.name: National Land Use Policy Part VIII — customary tenure recognised whether or not it is registered, and the village tract committee that maps it
trackers.desc: Caution first, as with every entry for this country: the policy is not legally binding and its implementation has stalled; it is recorded because its words are still the strongest statement a community can quote about customary land. Customary land use tenure is to be recognised, and the mapping is done by local committees through public consultation. The policy, adopted in January 2016 after an extended public consultation and published in full, devotes Part VIII to the land use rights of ethnic nationalities: customary land use tenure systems are to be recognised in the national land law to ensure awareness, compliance and application of traditional land use practices, formal recognition of customary land use rights, protection of those rights and application of readily available impartial dispute resolution mechanisms; and duties are to be assigned for the preparation and revision of land use maps and records through public consultation processes by the ward or village tract land use committees under the supervision of the township land use committee, so as to have accurate understanding of information on land possession, use, availability and allocation where ethnic nationalities live or traditionally use land. The village tract committee, not the capital, is the body that makes the map. The principles are quotable, and they name who is to be protected. Published analysis records the basic principle of legally recognising and protecting legitimate land tenure rights of people as recognised by the local community, with particular attention to smallholder farmers, the poor, ethnic nationalities and women; the objective of recognising and protecting customary land tenure rights and procedures of ethnic nationalities; and the guiding principle of promoting people's participation and collaboration, particularly of ethnic nationalities, women and smallholder farmers, in decision making on land and natural resource management. It also records the policy pledging that environmental and social impact assessments be completed before land is reallocated, and calling for public consultation, negotiation and participatory decision making with preference to local stakeholders where relocation is claimed necessary for an overriding public purpose. One statutory hook survives outside the policy. Published analysis records that the acquisition, resettlement and rehabilitation legislation of 2019 defines a land owner to include a person accepted by the local community and recognised by the relevant regional or state government as owner according to customary practices of ethnic nationalities, though holding no legal document — with the same analysis recording that the law does not clarify how community rights are to be recognised, and that a statement of ethnic nationalities affirms customary rights whether or not existing land use is registered, recorded or mapped. Read this with the acquisition law, the community forestry certificate, the cadastral records and the registered consultants entries already recorded here, each carrying the same caution.

trackers.name: Farmland dispute bodies — the village tract case file, thirty days at each rung, and the level at which the ladder ends
trackers.desc: Caution first, as with every entry for this country: administration of this framework under the present authorities is unverified. A farmland dispute starts at the village tract, and it starts as a case file. The farmland legislation of 2012 provides that the ward or village tract farmland administrative body opens an original case of a dispute in respect of the right to use farmland and shall make examination, hearing and decision; that a person dissatisfied with that decision may appeal to the township body within thirty days of the order or decision; that the township body may approve, amend or cancel the decision below; and that a person dissatisfied with the township decision may appeal to the district body, again within thirty days. Each rung has the same clock, so diarise the date of the order rather than the date you heard about it. The ladder ends at region or state level, and that matters. Published academic analysis records that the dispute system runs from village tract level up through township and district to the region or state level headed by the governor as final, whose decision is recorded as conclusive and incontestable at court; and records that criticism of this government-led system led to a separate standing committee for scrutinising confiscated farmland being established by presidential decree in 2016. Know before you start that this ladder is designed to end outside the courts. The certificate, and who issues it. The law provides that a person with the right to use farmland applies to the township department through the ward or village tract body; that the township department scrutinises and submits the application to the township farmland body; and that the township body, with the approval of the district body, issues the land use certificate after registration and payment of the prescribed fees at the township land records office. The central body's duties include guiding and supervising registration, issuing certificates, permission to use farmland and settling disputes, and revoking the right to use farmland from a person against whom administrative action is taken. Transactions happen in front of the village tract body. The law records that sale, mortgage, lease, exchange and gift of the right to use farmland are executed by bilateral agreement in the presence of the ward or village tract administrative body and registered at the township department, with the central body empowered to ensure the farmland is valued at a proper and reasonable local rate. That presence requirement is a check a community can insist on when a neighbour's land changes hands under pressure. Read this with the cadastral records, the acquisition law, the land use policy and the community forestry entries already recorded here, each carrying the same caution.

trackers.name: Mines Law permits — the regional board that grants small-scale and subsistence permits, the area limits set by commodity and permit type, and the published permit count
trackers.desc: Caution first, as with every entry for this country: administration under the present authorities is unverified, and the figures below date from before 2021. Small-scale and subsistence permits are decided by a board in the region or state, not only in the capital. The 2015 amending law, published in full, provides that a citizen or organisation wishing to carry out prospecting, exploration, small scale or subsistence production, processing, or buying and selling of metallic minerals, industrial minerals or stone with citizen investment shall apply to the work site scrutiny and allocation body of the relevant region or state, formed and assigned with the approval of the union government; and that such a board may, after scrutinising the application and obtaining the ministry's comments, grant the permit for operations that can be carried out in that region or state. Published analysis records that this decentralisation does not extend to foreign investors, who deal with the ministry directly. Ask the regional board for the permit file before writing to the capital. Classification is by stated criteria, and area limits are set by commodity and permit type. The amending law provides that the ministry shall prescribe the terms of operation, the operation area, extent, amount of investment, machinery and use of equipment in classifying large, medium, small and subsistence scale production. A sector-wide impact assessment records that, regardless of the stage of the mine life cycle and the type of licence — prospecting, exploration, feasibility or production — the maximum size of area allowed is set out in a named rule by commodity and permit type. Establish which class a project claims, then check its area against that rule. Permit terms and the published stock of permits. Published analysis records prospecting permits of one year, exploration permits of three years and subsistence production permits of one year with four one-year extensions, with the maximum production permit period for large scale projects raised to fifty years; that exploration permit holders were given a clear right to production permits; and that as at 30 April 2018 the ministry had issued 1,405 valid mining permits, of which 150 were large-scale and 786 small-scale, with no new permits issued for over two and a half years during a moratorium while the 2018 rules were drafted. Those counts are the baseline against which a claimed permit can be questioned. The rules cover closure and inspection too. The same analysis records that the 2018 rules set criteria for permit applications, the duties of permit holders, and rules on mine closure, safety, labour, accidents, inspection and environmental protection, and that subsistence-scale permit holders may sell on the domestic market only. Read this with the cultural heritage regions where exploration is prohibited, the assessment procedure, the farmland dispute bodies and the emission guidelines entries already recorded here, each carrying the same caution.

trackers.name: Freshwater Fisheries Law — the five fishery categories, the reserved fishery where fishing can be prohibited outright, and the exclusive rights a leaseholder can assert over a stretch of water
trackers.desc: Caution first, as with every entry for this country: administration since 2021 is unverified, and the figures below predate it. A reserved fishery is a category in which fishing can be prohibited outright to stop a stock disappearing. The 1991 freshwater fisheries law defines a reserved fishery as fisheries waters in which fishing operations are prohibited from time to time, or in which fishing rights are granted subject to stipulations by the department, in order to prevent the extinction of fish and to propagate them; and defines a leasable fishery as waters in which fishing rights are granted under a lease subject to stipulations on area, species, implement, period and method. Asking for a stretch to be treated as a reserved fishery uses a category the law already provides. The definition of freshwater fisheries waters reaches further than rivers. The law provides that the expression includes leasable and reserved fisheries and licensed waters, reservoirs, waters in an area belonging to any government department, inland tidal places, waters on an island, crocodile nets and turtle banks where crocodiles and turtles lay their eggs, and brackish waters; and that waters inland of the straight line across a river or creek mouth contiguous to the sea are freshwater fisheries waters. Turtle banks being named in the definition is worth knowing where a beach is at issue. Five categories, and who sells or licenses each. Published assessment records the five categories as leasable fisheries, tender licence fisheries, non-licence fisheries, implement licence fisheries and reserved fisheries, non-licence fisheries being open access; the law provides that the township zone officer-in-charge concerned sells a leasable fishery by auction or grants a tender licence in the prescribed manner, that rent, tender and licence fees are paid in full cash down, and that the director general may permit payment by instalment for leasable fisheries in remote areas, and determines fees in foreign currency for foreign-capital operations. A leaseholder's rights are exclusive, and that cuts both ways. Published research records that leaseholders enjoy exclusive rights to fish the lease area, including preventing access by others, and a degree of environmental management; that leases were traditionally auctioned annually with the department extending terms to promote longer-term management; that several thousand leasable fisheries are listed nationally; and that a leaseholder must spend a stated proportion of the lease value on stock from government hatcheries and on maintaining the lease environment. It also records regional fisheries laws made under devolution. Read this with the farmland dispute bodies, the mines permits, the cultural heritage regions and the assessment procedure entries already recorded here, each carrying the same caution.

trackers.name: Conservation of Biodiversity and Protected Areas Law 2018 — the community protected area category, buffer zones managed for local livelihoods, the three wildlife protection classes, and the thirty-day route after a rejection
trackers.desc: Caution first, as with every entry for this country: enforcement since 2021 is unverified, and implementing rules were still being settled when the sources below were written. A community protected area is a category of protected area in its own right. Published analysis of the 2018 law, which replaced the 1994 statute, records that the law recognises community protected areas as a category of protected area; that the forest department is required to provide technical coordination and support for their management; that the director general may allow co-management; and that the law enables buffer zones where communities surrounding protected areas can use natural resources and develop ecotourism, with wardens' duties including managing the buffer zone focused on local community livelihood development, mobilising public participation through education, reporting land use and other conflicts to higher authorities, and providing technical support for co-management with local communities. Where a community is beside a reserve, that category and those warden duties are what to ask about. Three classes of protected wildlife, each declared by notification. The law defines completely protected wildlife declared for rareness and critically endangered status; normally protected wildlife, not critically endangered but needing protection because of a high possibility of becoming threatened; and seasonally protected wildlife, each definition extending to any parts, derivatives or products; and defines hunting as any method used to harm, catch or kill wildlife. Establishing which class a species on a site falls into decides what is prohibited. Regional bodies exist, and a rejection has a stated next step. The law provides that a regional or state government may constitute biodiversity and protected areas management committees, and records a thirty-day window to take a matter to the committee after a rejection is made. Published analysis records that penalties were raised sharply — extracting or destroying any wild plant, punishable by a small fine under the old law, now carrying a fine up to a stated maximum or up to five years' imprisonment — and that permission to breed wild animals or cultivate wild plants must be registered with the forest department. Export or transport of protected species for research requires the director general's allowance with the minister's approval. Read this with the freshwater fisheries law, the cultural heritage regions, the mines permits and the farmland dispute bodies entries already recorded here, each carrying the same caution.

trackers.name: The 2016 Legal Aid Law and the provider landscape — the statutory board and its township structure, the fifty providers mapped before the law, and an honest account of what has happened since 2021
