In 2011 the Association set up Hong Kong's first paddy-rice community supported agriculture membership scheme at Long Valley, selling eco-rice, and it has trained local residents as guides since 2006 — over a thousand people a year take the tours, and part of the revenue is retained for the guides' own development and returned to the village. That turns conservation into a reason for an owner to keep farming rather than sell. Founded 1968, Hong Kong's oldest local environmental group, a tax-exempt charity run by a council elected by its members; cahk@cahk.org.hk. Three cautions on the site: it runs old show_works.php and new /zh-hant/ URL schemes side by side, the older conservancy.org.hk domain is still live, and the postal address has changed — take it from the current site.

trackers.name: Legal Aid Department — funded representation for judicial review, and the waiver that lifts the means cap
trackers.desc: Judicial review is how Hong Kong development decisions are actually challenged, and this is where the money for it comes from. The department provides representation by a solicitor and, where necessary, counsel in civil proceedings in the District Court and above, and judicial review applications are handled by its own legal aid counsel. Eligibility turns on two tests, means and merits. The merits test asks whether there are reasonable grounds for bringing the proceedings, and the department keeps an aided case under review and can discharge the certificate if those grounds fall away. The waiver is the provision worth knowing about. The Director may waive the financial eligibility limit in meritorious cases where a breach of the Bill of Rights Ordinance or an inconsistency with the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights is in issue, subject to a contribution — so a case that can properly be framed as a rights point is not necessarily lost because the applicant owns a flat. Two things that catch people. Aid is open to any applicant irrespective of nationality and residence, which is unusual and matters if the person best placed to bring the case is not a resident. And the Director of Legal Aid holds a first charge over property or damages recovered in an aided case, so a successful outcome can carry a repayment obligation — establish that position before starting, not after. Where aid is refused there are published channels of appeal, and for an appeal to the Court of Final Appeal a review committee comprising the Registrar of the High Court with representatives of the Bar Association and the Law Society; the Bar Association's free legal service scheme is the fallback where aid is refused outright. Check the current financial limits on the day. The department's own pages carry two different figures for the ordinary scheme and two for the supplementary scheme, and the online means calculator is the only version that will be current. Judicial review is a small proportion of civil legal aid work, so expect the merits assessment to be searching.

trackers.name: EIAO register — thirty days to comment, and the monthly monitoring reports stay public
trackers.desc: Two windows, and the second is thirty days. The assessment ordinance provides a two-stage consultation: a project profile is exhibited for fourteen days and the full assessment report for thirty, free of charge, at locations the Director specifies, with the applicant advertising availability in one Chinese and one English newspaper once every ten days of the period. Before deciding whether to approve the report, the Director must consider the comments raised by the public and by the advisory council on the environment during the inspection period. The register publishes how many comments each application drew, which tells you what a serious response looks like. For every application it records the date the applicant was told the report was suitable for inspection, the exact exhibition dates, the number of public comments received and the decision with its date and whether conditions were imposed. Published counts run from a single comment to several dozen. A coordinated set of well-founded submissions is therefore a large share of everything the Director will see, and this is one of the few places in this file where the size of the effort required can actually be read off the record. Monitoring stays public after approval, month by month. Permit conditions require the permit holder to release all finalised submissions for public inspection by depositing them at the register office or on websites the Director specifies, and baseline monitoring reports together with monthly environmental monitoring and audit reports are prepared for public inspection through the register office and the ordinance website in both HTML and PDF. Compliance during construction is therefore checkable every month rather than at the end. Practical points. The register is searchable online and the register office keeps hard copies in Wan Chai; a permit holder may appeal against a permit condition within thirty days of receiving the permit; and non-compliance by any person may contravene the ordinance and be acted on under it. Read this alongside the legal aid entry recorded here, which is what funds a judicial review if the decision itself is to be challenged.

trackers.name: Environment and Conservation Fund — nearly 7,000 projects funded, and a window reserved for first-time applicants
trackers.desc: The eligible list is broad enough to include an ordinary residents' body. Applications are invited from eligible local organisations — local bodies, community organisations, green groups, charitable organisations, school sponsoring bodies, tertiary institutions, schools, nurseries and kindergartens — and the fund reports having supported nearly seven thousand green projects and activities with total funding of over four billion Hong Kong dollars. A committee vets and approves the applications, monitors how funded projects are carried out, and publicises the fund. A group constituted as a local body is inside that list rather than outside it. Write to the stated requirement, not against the development. A proposal put forward for support should help enhance the overall environmental quality of Hong Kong, raise the environmental awareness of the local community and promote public participation. Framing a proposal in those terms is describing what the fund exists to pay for; framing it as opposition to one project is not, however strong the case against that project may be. One window is reserved for organisations that have never been funded. The published application material records a special grant route open only to organisations which have not previously received support under the fund's environmental education and community action scheme. That matters because the assessment takes into account the capability and track record of the applicant organisation and its project team — so a group with no record is otherwise at a structural disadvantage, and this is the door built for it. The application discipline decides admission. Applicants are directed to take account of the funding caps and the allocations available for different project scales and themes when preparing a budget, to complete every section of the form and enter a marker where a question does not apply, and are warned that incomplete applications, or applications not submitted in the prescribed format, are not accepted. Read the guide and the current scheme announcements before drafting. Read this alongside the countryside conservation funding entry recorded here: that scheme pays for work in specified countryside areas, while this one is general and open to far more kinds of applicant.

trackers.name: Reporting pollution — one centre, a three working day pledge, and complaint statistics by district
trackers.desc: One centre, one number, and a response time the department has committed to. The department's customer service centre was set up in 2002 to give the public a single point for reporting pollution and making enquiries. Reports can be made online, by the hotline, which doubles as a fax number and runs on weekday office hours with a voice mail service outside them, or by post to a regional office. The department states that it responds to a request within three working days and publishes a performance pledge alongside that undertaking. Three working days is a commitment a complainant can quote rather than a hope. Progress can be checked, and information can be added later. The department provides routes both for giving further details about a case already lodged and for checking the progress of a previous complaint, with smoky vehicle cases followed up through the same centre. Keep the reference and go back with anything new: an inspection that found nothing on a particular afternoon is not the end of a complaint about something that happens at night or in the rain. The complaint statistics are published by year and by district. The published tables come with notes on how cases are counted — recording, for instance, that from 2015 light nuisance cases handled by the centre with the issue of advisory letters were grouped under their own district rather than under a residual category, and that the noise figures include police cases. A community can therefore see how many complaints its district generates and how they are disposed of before deciding what to expect from its own. Know which door before you dial. The department takes general pollution incidents including air pollution, indiscriminate waste water discharge, illegal waste disposal and noise from industrial or construction sources, and runs a separate hotline for beach water quality, while domestic night-time noise is a matter for the police. Read this alongside the environmental assessment register entry already recorded for this country: the register shows what was permitted and what monitoring was promised, and this is where a departure from it gets reported.

trackers.name: Free Legal Advice Scheme and the Duty Lawyer Scheme — advice in your district, and the courts the Legal Aid Department does not cover
trackers.desc: Free advice from qualified solicitors and barristers, given in the districts. The free legal advice scheme run by the duty lawyer service offers legal advice to members of the public free of charge, delivered by qualified solicitors and barristers at legal advice centres in the districts, with the district office as the point of further information. Where interpretation is needed in a language other than English or Cantonese, the service will assist in arranging it — an access provision almost no other scheme recorded in this file states on the page. Book early, because the wait is longer than most objection windows. Published guidance describes attending a referral agency to make the appointment, staff taking down the background of the case, bringing all the documents relating to it, and attending in person at a designated advice centre, with an appointment card issued; and it records that an applicant should generally be able to meet a volunteer lawyer within six to eight weeks. Set that against the comment periods recorded elsewhere in this file — thirty days on an assessment report here, ten working days in Indonesia, five days for one Indonesian grant round — and the instruction writes itself: book the advice the week the project is announced, not the week the deadline falls. The two schemes divide by court tier. Representation in the magistrates, juvenile and coroner's courts comes through the duty lawyer scheme, which keeps a court liaison office in every magistrates court, while the legal aid department covers proceedings in the district court and above along with committal proceedings. Working out which tier a case sits in before applying saves an application to the wrong body, and the two bodies are separately administered. Two further routes. The same service runs a telephone scheme giving recorded legal information, and the bar has its own pro bono arrangements for cases where a barrister can assist directly. Read this with the legal aid department entry already recorded for this country: that one funds representation including for judicial review, and this is where free advice and the lower courts are handled.

trackers.name: Land Registry searches — the register, the lodged instruments not yet on it, and the alert service
trackers.desc: Searching means inspecting or buying a copy, and it can be done for any property in the territory. To search a land record is to inspect it or obtain a copy of it. Searches can be made through the registry's online system, and at its customer centre and the New Territories search offices by counter search or self-service search, for properties anywhere in Hong Kong; inspection of original government leases and block government leases is available by appointment. Fees are published under the land registration fees regulations, alongside the registry's performance pledges and the list of its offices. Check the unposted memorial list, not only the register. The registry advises customers to check that list, through the online system or the self-service terminals, to find out whether instruments have been lodged for registration but for one reason or another have not yet been entered in the land register. A dealing already lodged and not yet posted is invisible on the register itself — and for a community watching a site quietly change hands, or a lease being dealt with, that gap is precisely where the news sits. No other land record entry in this file names an equivalent list. Search by property, not by person. A member of the public may apply for a search of the properties registered in their own name, but the registry will not accept an application for a search on properties registered in the name of another individual unless the applicant produces that person's authorisation, and a non-refundable fee applies to the owner's check service. The register is open by lot and closed by name, which is the opposite of the position recorded in this file for Punjab. And there is an alert. The registry publishes a property alert service alongside its search and fee schedules. Read this with the environmental assessment register, the pollution reporting centre and the legal aid entries already recorded for this country: the assessment says what was permitted, the register says who holds the ground, and the unposted list says what is about to change.

trackers.name: HOKLAS directory — the scope of accreditation, updated weekly, with past versions kept
trackers.desc: You can look up a laboratory's exact scope, not just whether it is accredited. The accreditation service publishes a directory of the organisations it has accredited as testing laboratories, proficiency testing providers and reference material producers, searchable by the name of the organisation, its registration number or the type of accredited activity, with the detailed scope of accreditation available to view or download for each. The complete directory can also be downloaded as a single file and is updated weekly. The service itself tells you to check per test. Its own note is that because an organisation's accreditation status may change, a user should make sure the organisation is accredited for the particular test, certification or inspection concerned. That is the scope instruction this research repeats for Singapore, Brunei, Taiwan and China, stated here by the accreditation body rather than inferred from a laboratory's marketing. Past versions are published, which lets you check a report against the date it was written. The list of accredited laboratories is also released through the government's open data portal, where historical versions can be downloaded by date range. A community can therefore establish whether a laboratory held accreditation for the relevant test at the time it produced a particular report, rather than only today. Nothing else recorded in this file allows the accreditation record to be checked retrospectively. Government laboratories are in the same directory. The departments' own laboratories appear in the list and are marked as government bodies, among them the government laboratory, public works laboratories and drainage services laboratories. The laboratory a department relies on is therefore listed with a scope of its own, so the figures on both sides of a dispute can be tested with the same instrument. Read this with the pollution reporting centre, the legal advice schemes and the land registry entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Code on Access to Information — an oral request counts, and review by someone senior to the decider
trackers.desc: An oral request counts, and every department has a named officer for this. Requests for information may be made orally or in writing, and an oral request will usually suffice where what is sought can be provided readily and simply. Each department designates an access to information officer who is responsible for promoting and overseeing the application of the code, so a request can be addressed to that officer by title rather than to the department at large. The code covers all government bureaux and departments, together with a list of other bodies including the monetary authority, the anti-corruption commission, the housing authority and the privacy commissioner. The clocks, and the outer limit. Information will be made available within ten days of a written request where possible; where that is not possible the applicant is to be advised by an interim reply within ten days, and the target response time becomes twenty-one days. In exceptional circumstances where processing will exceed twenty-one days an explanation should be given, extensions kept to a minimum, and the total processing time should not normally exceed fifty-one days. A partial refusal must leave the rest, and the wrong department must pass it on. Where disclosure of certain information in a record is refused, access will normally be provided to the remaining part of that record. And where a department receives a written request for information held by another department, it will transfer the request to that department and tell the applicant it has done so. Being sent away to start again is not a permitted outcome. Review goes to someone senior to the person who refused. Anyone who believes a department has failed to apply the code properly may ask the department to review, and the review is to be considered by a directorate officer at least one rank senior to the officer who made the original decision; alternatively a complaint may be made to the ombudsman, whose published compendium of cases records how particular refusals were treated, including a case where the ombudsman held the date of the applicant's original email to be the date of the request and urged release of the information. Published cases give a community arguments that have already worked. One honest limit: this is an administrative code rather than a statute. Read this with the land registry, the accreditation directory and the legal advice scheme entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: ICAC — report in person, and the offence of talking about it afterwards
trackers.desc: Report in person, not by email. The commission states that making a report needs no appointment and no forms: a person contacts the round-the-clock report centre or any regional office and reports to the duty officer, who meets the complainant alone so that the content of the report stays confidential. It also states expressly that, for security reasons, corruption must not be reported and investigation matters must not be discussed by email, by fax or through its website. A community used to writing letters and emails should note that here the recommended channel is a room. Talking about it afterwards is an offence. Under the bribery ordinance any person — the commission's own answer names the complainant among them — who discloses details of the investigation or the identity of the person under investigation, without lawful authority or reasonable excuse, is guilty of an offence. A group that reports a company or an official and then announces it has done so is not merely being unwise; it is committing an offence. This is the sharpest trap recorded anywhere in this file for people whose instinct is to campaign in public. Consent governs some referrals and not others. Reports which are not corruption-related and contain no allegation of a criminal offence may be referred to the appropriate authority with the complainant's consent, while reports alleging criminal offences may be referred to the police or other law enforcement agencies without that consent. A complainant should know before speaking which of those two categories their information falls into. The prevention department studies systems, not only cases. Its corruption prevention department conducts detailed studies of the practices and procedures of government departments and public bodies and assists them in implementing prevention measures, with thousands of assignment reports issued over the years and dozens completed annually, covering fields such as law enforcement; an advisory service also operates for the private sector, including a stream dedicated to building management. Where the problem is how permissions or contracts are handled rather than a single payment, that is the route to raise it. Read this with the land registry, the code on access to information, the accreditation directory and the legal advice entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Director of Audit — whether the data behind a decision was sufficient is itself auditable
trackers.desc: The evidence behind a decision is auditable, even where the decision is not. Under the published guidelines governing value for money audits, the director of audit will not comment on the policy decisions of the executive and the legislature except as to their effect on the public purse — but may investigate and report to the legislature on whether there was a lack of sufficient, relevant and reliable financial and other data available, and whether the critical underlying assumptions were made explicit, when the policy objectives were set or the decisions taken, for further inquiry by the public accounts committee. For a community arguing that a project's justification rests on thin numbers and unstated assumptions, that is the question already framed by the state's own auditor. Any organisation can be brought into scope in the public interest. The audit ordinance allows the chief executive to authorise the director in writing, in the public interest, to audit the accounts and records of any organisation. This is the second provision of that kind recorded in this file, the other being the power over concessionaires in Macau, and it is the route by which a body outside the ordinary audit list can be examined. The publication calendar is fixed. The director issues a report on the government's accounts under the ordinance in October, and two reports on the results of value for money audits, in April and in October. A community following a project can therefore anticipate when findings appear rather than waiting on an unpredictable release. The reports get hearings, and outsiders can be heard. The legislature's public accounts committee considers the director's reports on the accounts and on value for money audits, and may invite government officials and senior staff of public organisations to attend public hearings to give explanation, evidence or information — and any other person to assist it in relation to such explanation, evidence or information if it considers that necessary. A community holding knowledge about a project therefore has a named body with the power to hear it. Read this with the anti-corruption commission, the code on access to information, the land registry and the accreditation directory entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: CSDI Portal and the lands open data — boundary maps, terrain and orthophotos, downloadable free
trackers.desc: Government spatial data downloads free, in machine-readable form. The common spatial data infrastructure portal was launched at the end of 2022 by the development bureau and the lands department as a one-stop platform on which the public can search, view and download the government's spatial data at no charge, with more than five hundred datasets from departments covering planning, lands, buildings, works, population and transport. Datasets are geo-tagged, accompanied by metadata documents and data specifications, and published in open, machine-readable formats with programming interfaces. A residents' group with one laptop can therefore hold the same base data the department holds. The land boundary map and the terrain model are the two that matter in a land fight. A digital land boundary map is published within the department's series of digital maps; the digital terrain model covers the territory in a five-metre raster grid with an accuracy of about five metres, with the honest caveat published alongside it that where land is covered by vegetation the terrain is depicted at the height of the vegetation; and digital orthophoto maps and topographic maps at scales of one in fifty thousand, one in a hundred thousand and one in two hundred thousand are downloadable, georeferenced to the local grid. Arguments about a boundary, a gradient or where water will go start from those files. The three-dimensional data answers the technical questions a project raises. Territory-wide three-dimensional data represents the shape, appearance and position of buildings, infrastructure and terrain, and the government's own description records that it supports urban planning, land management, project development, environmental studies, traffic studies, landscape design and other technical assessments. When the operator's consultant is working from these datasets, the objector can work from the same ones. Two tools worth knowing about. An address lookup service provides lookup on address records in Chinese and English aggregated from across government, and a geo-tagging tool converts textual and non-spatial information — a list of households, for instance — into spatial data that can be displayed on a digital map. A list of affected addresses becomes a map layer, which is a different kind of document to put in front of a board. Read this with the assessment register, the land registry search, the accreditation directory and the countryside conservation funding entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Surveyors Registration Board — a public register searchable by division, and general practice is the resumption one
trackers.desc: The register is public and searchable by division. The board maintains the statutory register of registered professional surveyors, and its site allows the whole register to be listed or searched by surname, by other name, by Chinese name, or by division — building surveying, general practice, land surveying, planning and development, property and facility management, and quantity surveying. Searching by division produces a list of the people qualified for a particular problem rather than a directory of everyone, which is the difference between a register that helps and one that merely exists. General practice is the division for valuation and resumption. The professional institute's own description of that division records services covering the planning, development, use, management and valuation of lands and buildings, the negotiation of sales and lettings, and the financial aspects of property investment, and states that its members' work includes government land disposal, resumption, rating, taxation and public housing, with many employed in the lands department, the rating and valuation department and the housing department as well as in private practice. The same discipline therefore advises the government that resumes land and the household resumed from — so a fair question to any surveyor is which side they usually act for. The board registers, and it disciplines. Under the registration ordinance the board's functions are to establish and maintain the register, to designate the divisions under which a person may be registered, to set and review qualification standards, to examine and verify the qualifications of applicants, to receive and accept or reject applications for registration and renewal, to deal with disciplinary offences in accordance with the ordinance, and to keep proper records of its proceedings and accounts. Local experience is a condition, and the titles are prescribed. No person may be registered without at least one year of relevant professional experience in Hong Kong and competence to practise in the relevant division; the board publishes, division by division, the list of ordinances that require the services of a registered professional surveyor; and it has issued guidance on the correct form of the professional titles, noting that abbreviations written without the prescribed punctuation are incorrect usage under the ordinance. Check the division on the register, then check the title on the report. Read this with the land registry search, the spatial data portal, the assessment register and the free legal guidance entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Town Planning Board — two months to object, three weeks to comment on other people's objections, and a hearing you may attend
trackers.desc: Two months on the plan, then three weeks on everyone else's objections. When a draft plan is exhibited the public is invited to make representations within a two-month period, with notices published weekly in two Chinese and one English daily newspapers and in the gazette setting out where and when the plan may be inspected. The representations received are then published for public inspection, and during the first three weeks of that period any person may comment on them, whether in support or in opposition. A community that missed the first window can therefore still enter the process through the second, by commenting on somebody else's representation — which is the single most useful thing in this entry. You may attend the hearing and be heard. Those who have submitted representations or comments may attend the hearing and address the Board. If the Board proposes amendments to meet the representations, those proposed amendments are published for three weeks for further representations by any person other than the original representer or commenter, who must indicate whether they support or oppose; an adverse further representation triggers a further hearing. Where the representer is not a natural person — a company, an organisation or a group — a representative may be authorised to attend, so a residents' association need not send its chairperson. Forms, counters, and the public inspection rule. Submissions are made on published forms available from the Board's secretariat and from the planning enquiry counters at named government offices with a published hotline, must be made within the statutory time limits, and must comply with the Board's published guidelines. Representations and comments are open to public inspection including the name of the person making them, while identity card or passport numbers, correspondence addresses and telephone, fax and email details are withheld. Decide before filing whether the name on the form should be an individual's or an organisation's. How decisions come out. A gist of the decision is uploaded to the Board's website shortly after the meeting and the confirmed minutes are published there; parties are informed of the decision three to four weeks after the meeting, and no verbal advice or interim replies are given before the decision is released. The ordinance was amended with effect from September 2023 to compress these processes, so check which procedure applies to the particular plan or application. Read this with the assessment register, the spatial data portal, the countryside conservation funding scheme and the surveyors' register entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Historic building grading — anyone may propose a new item, and the proposed monument declaration is the emergency lever
trackers.desc: Members of the public can put a building forward. The advisory board completed the assessment of one thousand four hundred and forty-four historic buildings in 2009 and has since confirmed grades building by building, using the material supplied by the antiquities office together with the views of the public. It also carries out heritage value assessment and grading of new items proposed by members of the public, with those new items handled in phases according to urgency because each requires archival research, verification of information, site inspection and detailed recording. Proposing a building is therefore open to anyone, and the queue is triaged by need — so a submission should say plainly why this one is urgent. The grading is done against six published criteria. Historic buildings are graded on historical value, architectural value, group value, social value and local interest, the degree to which the original state has been retained, and rarity. A submission written against those six headings, in that order, meets the assessors on their own ground; one written as a general plea for preservation does not. The emergency lever is the proposed monument declaration. Published guidance records that where a building needs immediate statutory protection — for example where it faces the threat of demolition, or where alteration or renovation works are proposed that could affect its heritage value — the authority may declare it a proposed monument under the ordinance, after which the ordinance's protection mechanism applies and works are prohibited unless a permit is granted. Buildings in the highest grade are actively considered against the very high threshold for declaration as a monument outright. That is the provision to name when demolition is imminent rather than hypothetical. Proposed gradings are published, and the sources behind them can be inspected. Proposed gradings are made public and views invited before grades are confirmed, and copies of the archival records and publications used in the assessments are kept by the office and may be consulted by appointment at its heritage centre. Published criticism records that the board does not publish its reasons for a particular grading, so the assessment sources are the material to work from when disputing one. Read this with the planning board's comment windows, the environmental assessment register, the spatial data portal and the countryside conservation funding entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Companies Registry search — free basic particulars, paid document images, and the director details withheld since 2021
trackers.desc: Three ways in, and the basic particulars cost nothing. The companies registry's records can be searched through its online search system, through a mobile version of the same service, or in person at the registry's public search centre in the government offices building in the central district, the registry's integrated information system having converted its records into electronic images for online inspection. Published guides record that a search returns, free of charge, the company's Chinese and English names, its registration number, the date of incorporation, the type of company and whether it has entered winding-up, and that searches can be run against the company name, the company particulars, the index of directors and the record of disqualification orders. The documents themselves are paid for, per document. Fuller material — the articles, annual returns, charge registrations, resolutions and the history of changes in directors, shareholders, share capital and address — is obtained by buying image copies, priced per document, with some image records and reports collected at the public search centre or sent by post or courier for a fee. A community should budget for the two or three filings that matter rather than for a full history. Director details have been withheld since August 2021. Published accounts record that the public can no longer obtain a director's usual residential address or full identification number through a search: the register shows a correspondence address in place of the residential address and partial identification numbers in place of full ones, and that protected information is available only to specified persons on application. Anyone planning to identify individuals behind a project should know that before starting, because it changes what the search can and cannot establish. Two practical traps. Unlimited companies — sole proprietorships and partnerships — are not in the companies registry system at all, and their particulars are obtained instead through the business registration office by a different route, so a blank result is not proof that a trading entity does not exist. And the searcher must give their own name and identity document details and select one of the stated purposes of search from a fixed list before proceeding, having read the declaration; the first eight digits of the business registration certificate number now serve as the unique business identifier, and the system matches it against the older company number. Read this with the land registry search, the town planning board objection windows, the code on access to information and the audit entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Land resumption compensation — three months to reversion, ex-gratia rates by zone, and what going to the Lands Tribunal costs you
trackers.desc: Three months from the notice, and the clock is the same whatever the project. Where government resumes private land for a public project — a road scheme, public housing, an urban renewal project, an open space, a drainage improvement, a market or a school — a government notice is published in the gazette, copies are affixed in the area and sent to registered owners where possible, and under normal circumstances ownership reverts to the government three months after the notice, with a shorter period where the acquisition is urgent. On the date of reversion the owners' legal rights end, and former owners can no longer collect rent from tenants or occupants. Resumption may proceed under the resumption ordinance or under the roads or railways ordinances, and the compensatable interest is limited by whichever ordinance is used — so the first thing to establish is which statute the notice cites. Statutory compensation and ex-gratia allowances are two different things. Statutory compensation is the open market value of the resumed property, assessed on a vacant possession or tenancy basis as appropriate, at the date of reversion. On top of that, eligible owner-occupiers of domestic property are offered a home purchase allowance, calculated as the difference between the value of a notional replacement flat — a seven-year-old flat of similar size in the same locality — and the open market value of the resumed flat; supplementary allowances, removal allowances and rehousing or cash in lieu are offered to other eligible occupiers; and occupiers of commercial property may take an ex-gratia allowance in lieu of the right to claim for business loss and disturbance. In the New Territories the department applies two sets of ex-gratia rates, for agricultural land and for building land, under each of two compensation zones. Going to the tribunal has a price, and it is stated in advance. Where a statutory claim cannot be settled by agreement, the owner or tenant may apply to the Lands Tribunal for adjudication, and professional fees reasonably incurred in making a claim may be reimbursed by the government, though without interest. But the department's own guidance records the trade: if the claimant proceeds, the ex-gratia offer is immediately withdrawn and the statutory claim is re-assessed on a market value basis, and once the tribunal makes an award that award is the maximum compensation payable — whether it is higher or lower than the ex-gratia offer that was withdrawn. That is the calculation to make before filing, not after. What to gather first. The gazette notice with its date, the ordinance it is made under, the department's compensation offer with its breakdown between statutory compensation and each allowance, and the valuation date used. Read this with the land registry search, the surveyors' registration board register, the town planning board objection windows and the legal aid entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: New Nature Conservation Policy — twelve priority sites, funded management agreements on private land, and the land exchange that took a valley off the market
trackers.desc: Twelve named sites, and two schemes aimed squarely at privately owned land. The nature conservation policy introduced in 2004 identified twelve priority sites for enhanced conservation and proposed two incentive schemes — public-private partnership, and management agreements — with the stated aim of enhancing the conservation of ecologically important sites that are under private ownership. The department publishes the policy statement, the objectives and the list of priority sites. A community whose valley, marsh or fung shui wood appears on that list is arguing inside an existing policy rather than asking for a new one, and the first thing to check is whether the site is on it. The management agreements are funded, and NGOs sign them with landowners. Funding support for the management agreement scheme is granted through the environment and conservation fund, enabling non-governmental organisations to enter into agreements with landowners to enhance conservation at the priority sites; the department monitors schemes implemented by landowners or by the organisations. In June 2011 the fund's committee supported extending the scheme to country park enclaves and to private land inside country parks. That extension matters: an enclave surrounded by protected land, which is the classic site for a sudden clearance, is now inside the funded scheme. The published project list shows what has actually been agreed. The department lists the schemes it has funded, among them a habitat and biodiversity scheme at one priority valley, a rehabilitation project for a coastal area, a management agreement on private land of high conservation value at a site of special scientific interest, two fishpond conservation schemes including one in the Ramsar site, and a community-based management scheme for a forest village ecosystem. Reading that list tells a group which organisations already hold agreements, in which districts, and on what kind of habitat — which is the shortest route to finding a partner that has done it before. And there is a precedent for taking land off the market entirely. Government announcements record the completion in 2022 of a non-in-situ land exchange under which a development company surrendered its private land at one of the highest-ranked priority sites, which together with adjoining government land exceeds fifty hectares, for long-term conservation — the site concerned having ranked second among the twelve, behind only the Ramsar wetland. Where a landowner wants development value rather than the land itself, the exchange is the mechanism that has been used. Read this with the countryside conservation funding scheme, the conservation association's management agreements, the environment and conservation fund and the town planning board objection entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Hong Kong Free Press — a reader-funded newsroom with published accounts, a code of ethics and a legal defence fund
trackers.desc: A non-profit newsroom that publishes its own accounts. Founded in 2015, the outlet describes itself as an impartial, non-profit, English-language newspaper run by journalists and wholly independent, governed by a public code of ethics, with no shareholders and no tycoon, conglomerate, government or media owner behind it. It is externally audited each year and has published its accounts online since inception, reporting that around ninety-seven per cent of income comes from readers, chiefly about a thousand monthly donors, and that seventy-eight per cent of spending goes on staff pay and pensions. For a community deciding where to take a story, an outlet whose funding is documented is one whose interests can be checked rather than guessed at. It has been externally assessed, which matters when a story is attacked. The outlet records that it holds the Trust Project hallmark, became the city's only newsroom certified under the Journalism Trust Initiative in 2025 after a 130-point evaluation by external auditors, meets all nine of a credibility rating service's criteria, and is a member of regional and international press bodies. Those certifications do not make a story true, but they make it harder to dismiss the outlet itself, which is often the first move against coverage of a contested project. It states the pressures on it, and the reserves it holds. The same reports record a fourth and then a fifth consecutive year of deficit, aggressive cutbacks, a twenty-month tax inspection described as random which strained resources, income falling amid waning interest and population change, and that only a fraction of one per cent of regular visitors donate. They also record that the company retains a legal defence fund of a million dollars alongside an emergency fund of the same size, and that where safety or security is uncertain a staff byline may be used instead of a reporter's name. A community approaching the newsroom should read those two facts together: the outlet is under strain, and it has thought about protecting people who appear in its pages. What to bring. An English-language newsroom of this size runs on documents and specifics: the gazette notice, the planning application number, the correspondence, and people prepared to be named or to explain why they cannot be. Read this with the town planning board objection windows, the countryside conservation funding scheme, the land registry search and the access to information entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Judgments and legal reference — the judiciary's own database including the Lands Tribunal, and the free institute that searches all courts at once
trackers.desc: The judiciary publishes its own judgments database, and the Lands Tribunal is in it. The courts' judgments and legal reference database carries decisions of significance as precedents on points of law, practice and procedure and decisions of public interest, from the Court of Final Appeal since its establishment, the Court of Appeal and Court of First Instance of the High Court, the Competition Tribunal since its establishment, the District Court, the Family Court and the Lands Tribunal, covering a short early period and then from 1966 onwards. Decisions can be browsed by year or searched, and all courts and tribunals can be searched together. For a community whose dispute is about resumption compensation or land, the inclusion of the Lands Tribunal is the point: that is where those cases are decided. Two limits stated on the site itself. The judiciary's page records that newly added judgments are those uploaded in the last six working days; that where a judgment is not available on the site an application must be made to the relevant court registry with justifications; and that judgments may be downloaded for private study and research only, with a written application required for commercial use. University guidance adds that not all judgments appear on the site and that a fee may apply where a registry application is approved. Plan for the possibility that the decision you need is not online. The free legal information institute searches everything at once. A non-governmental institute, developed and operated jointly by a university's computer science department and law faculty with assistance from a regional counterpart, provides free access to primary legal materials including judgments and legislation, and decisions from all courts can be searched there simultaneously. Its stated purpose is free public access to primary legal materials in support of the rule of law, which makes it the practical first stop before the registry route. What to search for. Resumption and compensation decisions of the Lands Tribunal, planning and building matters in the High Court, and judicial review decisions concerning departmental conduct. Note the neutral case citation of anything useful and keep the download for study purposes only. Read this with the land resumption compensation entry, the town planning board objection windows, the legal aid department and the access to information code entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Public Subscription Permits — which permit each way of collecting money needs, and the four departments that issue them
trackers.desc: Collecting money in a public place needs a permit, and the permit depends on the method. The government's own guidance records that the Director of Social Welfare may issue public subscription permits under the summary offences legislation for flag days, general charitable fund-raising activities and solicitation of signed authorisation forms conducted in public places. A permit for general charitable fund-raising is required for setting up donation boxes at stationed counters, moving around soliciting with money-collection boxes or bags, door to door donation, charity sale of badges, tokens or similar articles, and charity rides. The statutory hook is that any person or organisation organising, equipping or taking part in a collection of money, or a sale or exchange for donation of badges or similar articles, in a public place for charitable purposes, must hold a permit from the Director. Different departments issue different permissions. The published listing of approved activities shows temporary hawker licences issued by the food and environmental hygiene department for on-street selling to raise funds; public subscription permits from the social welfare department for flag selling, general fund-raising and signed authorisation forms; and lottery licences from the home affairs department, including approval for selling tickets on public streets. Establish which method you intend to use before applying, because that decides which department you are dealing with. Flag days are allocated, not simply applied for. Guidance records territory-wide and regional flag days, with three organisations selling flags concurrently on each regional day — one on the island, one in Kowloon, one in the New Territories — allocation being an annual exercise conducted on the advice of a lotteries fund advisory committee, and closely related organisations not permitted to apply separately in the same exercise. Lottery proceeds may be used for operating expenses or donations to local registered charities, with organisations generally permitted one lottery licence every twelve months. Accounting is a condition of the permit. Application terms require the permittee to engage an accountant, accounting firm or corporate practice — a practice unit under the accounting regulation legislation — to review the income and expenditure account and prepare an independent practitioner's assurance report under a named professional practice note, to state the balance of donations and bank-in date, and, where funds are passed to another charitable body, to submit that body's receipt within ninety days. Budget for the accountant at the outset. And you can check any collector. A daily published listing names the organisations permitted to collect that day, and permits carry a code linking to the approved activity details. Read this with the countryside conservation funding scheme, the conservancy association, the resumption compensation and the judgments entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Mines Division — who licenses blasting and quarrying, the rehabilitation contract model, and the sand removal permit
trackers.desc: One division licenses blasting and regulates quarrying, and it is named. The engineering department's mines division is responsible for regulatory control of the manufacture, storage, conveyance and use of Schedule 1 dangerous goods under the dangerous goods legislation, for mining operations under the mining legislation, and for the safe operation of quarries under the quarries safety regulations, as well as for the planning and management of quarrying contracts and related quarry studies. The Superintendent of Mines, who is also the chief geotechnical engineer for mines, issues mine blasting certificates permitting shot firers to use explosives, and the division audits blasting assessment reports and method statements for blasting projects, issues blasting permissions and explosives store licences, and inspects blast sites and temporary explosives stores. For a neighbourhood near blasting, that is one office holding the assessment report, the method statement and the permission. Ask for the blasting assessment report by name. The division's published information includes its practice notes and guidance notes, the list of approved explosives, the requirements for use of explosives and blasting in public projects, the buildings department's practice note on control of blasting, and pages on mining and prospecting licences. Those documents set the standard a specific blast is supposed to meet. Rehabilitation is contractual, and the history explains why. A departmental information note records that permit quarries were phased out and replaced by contract quarries, that there was still no contract requirement for operators to rehabilitate quarry sites after quarrying, and that the resulting degraded and dangerous ex-quarry sites were unsuitable for development without extensive remediation — which led the government to introduce quarry rehabilitation contracts, under which the contractor pays for the rights it enjoys, such as processing and selling rock excavated within the quarry and manufacturing and selling concrete, and the rehabilitation works involve major landscaping. Where a quarry is operating under such a contract, the rehabilitation obligation is a contract term, not a hope. Sand has its own permit, and there is no commercial mining. The department publishes pages on removal and importation of sand and a sand removal permit, alongside public filling management and construction and demolition material recycling. Its geology publication records that there are currently no commercial mining or prospecting licences operating, and sets out the production tonnages of the named quarries under rehabilitation contracts. Read this with the legal aid department, the free legal advice scheme, the public subscription permits and the judiciary judgment search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Tree preservation clauses and the Old and Valuable Trees register — the lease condition that bars felling, and the amenity categories that argue for redesign
trackers.desc: The protection on private land lives in the lease, and the guidance says what a proposal must contain. The lands department's guidance notes on tree preservation and removal proposals record that trees of particular value designated to be preserved under lease conditions, and trees in the register of old and valuable trees, are treated with their own status in such a proposal; that diameter at breast height is measured at 1.3 metres above ground; and that a tree's amenity value is to be assessed by its functional values for shade, seasonal interest, screening, reduction of pollution and noise and also its fung shui significance, classified into categories, with high meaning important trees which should be retained by adjusting the design layout accordingly. A neighbour arguing that a tree should stay has, in the government's own guidance, both the categories and the remedy: change the layout. The lease clause is the operative restriction, and it has been in leases for decades. A legislature paper records that tree preservation clauses and landscape clauses have been included in land leases since the 1970s and mid-1980s respectively; published practitioner guides record that where a lot's lease contains such a clause the owner cannot remove or interfere with a tree on the lot except with prior written consent from the lands department, applied for through the district lands office before the work, with routine light pruning excepted. Check whether the lot's lease carries the clause before anything else. The register is a distinct protection. Practitioner guides record that a tree listed in the register of old and valuable trees, mostly on government land, cannot be removed except with very strong justification, and advise seeking expert advice before any action even on private land because the government may have an interest in its preservation. Reporting, and the honest limits. The same material records that a dangerous tree on government land should be reported to the government hotline or the relevant department rather than dealt with privately, that a tree management office operates an adjudication mechanism for disputed responsibility, and that following a fatal tree accident the lands department formed a task group to investigate and review the complaint-handling mechanism. A legislature research note records the ombudsman's finding that there is at present neither a requirement for private owners to maintain trees properly nor power for the government to order pruning or removal of dangerous trees, and that only a small percentage of land leases carry the preservation clause. Read this with the planning board objection window, the countryside conservation fund, the management agreements and the historic building grading entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Country park designation and enclaves — sixty days of public inspection on a draft map, an objection heard by the board, and the enclave route into protection
trackers.desc: Adding land to a country park runs through a statutory map, and the objection window is sixty days. The development bureau's published answers record that designation is carried out under the country parks legislation, which includes a set of statutory consultation procedures; that the authority prepares draft maps in consultation with the country and marine parks board; that the draft maps are made available for public inspection by a gazette notice in both official languages before going to the executive; and that during the sixty-day period of public inspection from gazettal, any person aggrieved by a draft map may send a written statement of objection to the authority and to the board's secretary, the objections then being heard by the board before the maps go forward for approval. That window applies whichever way the map moves — a boundary can be enlarged or reduced by the same procedure. Support counts as well as objection. A press release on one round records nine objections against one draft map and one against another, and records that the authority also received more than three thousand two hundred emails supporting the incorporation of one enclave, plus individual emails supporting the others; that the board heard the objections over two days and rejected them; and that the approved maps were then deposited in the land registry and a designation order gazetted and tabled in the legislature subject to negative vetting, with a subcommittee formed to study it. A community wanting land protected should write in numbers during the inspection period, not afterwards. Enclaves are the specific route for unprotected pockets. The same answers record that where an enclave is assessed as suitable, the authority submits the designation proposal to the board and consults relevant stakeholders — naming rural committees and district councils — before starting the statutory process; and that enclaves once incorporated are regulated by the country parks and special areas regulations, which the government describes as conducive to conserving the natural environment, protecting diverse habitats and preserving the scenic landscape. Other enclaves are recorded as covered instead by development permission area plans. Know what designation does not exclude. A legislature research note records that the director may approve some infrastructure such as overhead power cables proposed by utilities, or recreational facilities by the private sector, after consulting the board; and records that small house development may be considered in country parks under certain conditions subject to final approval by the lands department. Read this with the planning board objection window, the new nature conservation policy, the management agreements and the tree preservation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Water Pollution Control Ordinance — a discharge licence must be advertised in two newspapers, and any person may object within thirty days
trackers.desc: An application to discharge into these waters must be advertised, at the applicant's own expense. The environment department's guide to the water pollution legislation records that for any application for a licence, or renewal or variation of a licence, to make a discharge into the waters of the territory, the applicant should publicly notify the application by a notice published in an English and a Chinese newspaper at his own expense, the only exceptions being applications of the domestic-sewage kind it names. Watch the newspapers for the notice, because it is the applicant who must place it. Thirty days to object, on a stated ground. The guide records that during the period of thirty days after the notice is published, any person may object to the granting of the application on the ground that it would tend to inhibit the attainment or maintenance of the relevant water quality objectives. That ground is narrow and specific: the argument to make is about the zone's water quality objectives, not about nuisance in general. Licences are recorded as generally valid for five years, apart from domestic septic tanks. The zones and their objectives are the framework behind the ground of objection. The department records that the 1980 legislation lets the government declare the territory's waters into ten water control zones, with control of discharges in those zones exercised mainly through licensing to achieve and maintain water quality objectives; that the first zone commenced in 1987 and the last two in 1999; and that amendments in 1990 and 1993 expanded the scope, tightened discharge controls and imposed controls on connection to the public sewerage system and on operation and maintenance of private communal sewage treatment plants. The Ordinance itself sets objectives for each zone, and can set different objectives for different parts of one zone. The remedies after a breach reach restoration and appeal. The guide records that a convicted person may be required to restore the waters damaged by the offending discharge, and that if that person fails to do so the department may undertake the restoration and recover the costs from them; that breach of a licence's terms and conditions is an offence carrying a stated fine, with continuing offences treated separately; and that a full list of requirements and decisions against which an appeal may be lodged is given in a named section, with notice of appeal forms available at the department's offices. Read this with the pollution reporting entry, the assessment register, the country park designation and the tree preservation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Marine parks and marine reserves — the fishing permit reserved to bona fide fishermen and nearby residents, the four parks where commercial fishing is banned, and the territory-wide trawl ban
trackers.desc: In a marine reserve nobody may fish at all; in a marine park only a permit holder may. The conservation department records that no person shall fish by any means in a marine reserve, and that in marine parks only the holder of a valid marine park fishing permit granted under the marine parks and marine reserves regulation may fish; that the director may grant such a permit to a bona fide fisherman or to a person who ordinarily resides near the marine park; and that under the strategy in force since April 2020, commercial fishing by locally registered vessels continues through that permit system in named parks, while commercial fishing is banned outright in four named marine parks — three in the eastern waters and one in the western — to protect coral communities and enhance fisheries resources. Whether a stretch of water sits inside a park or a reserve therefore decides what may happen in it. The legal frame and the advisory board are named. A legislature paper records that the 1995 marine parks legislation provides for the designation, control and management of marine parks and marine reserves for marine conservation and makes the conservation director the country and marine parks authority, with the 1996 regulation providing for the prohibition and control of certain activities in them; the department records that the authority is advised by the Country and Marine Parks Board, the same board already recorded in this bucket for country park designation. A working group advises on permit criteria and on individual cases, including succession and transfer of permits. The trawl ban is territory-wide and dated. The department records that the legislature passed amendments banning trawling — including pair, stern, shrimp and hang trawling — in these waters, in force since 31 December 2012, with a one-off assistance scheme for affected fishermen; and records complementary measures under the 2012 amendment ordinance including a registration system for local fishing vessels, limits on new entrants, restriction of fishing by non-fishing vessels and prohibition of fishing by non-local vessels, and the designation of fisheries protection areas. Registration is recorded as valid for the life of the vessel without renewal. What the rules prohibit is checkable on sight. Published material records that rules applying across protected areas include prohibition of possession of a trawl net, spear gun, explosives, chemicals or devices using an electric charge that may be used for fishing; that zoning such as mooring zones and vessel prohibition zones is applied within them; and that wardens patrol daily. Read this with the country park designation, the water pollution licence advertisement, the assessment register and the pollution reporting entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Wild Animals Protection Ordinance and SSSIs — wilful disturbance of a protected animal is an offence, nests and eggs are protected, restricted areas close a habitat seasonally, and the planning register carries the scientific sites
trackers.desc: Wilful disturbance is an offence, not only hunting. The conservation department records that wild animals specified in the Ordinance's second schedule are protected by law, and that no person shall hunt, wilfully disturb, sell, export or possess any protected wild animal, with a stated maximum fine and up to one year's imprisonment on conviction. Assessment material records that designated wild animals are protected from being hunted while their nests and eggs are protected from injury, destruction and removal, and that all birds and most mammals, including marine cetaceans, are protected under this Ordinance, along with certain reptiles including all sea turtles, amphibians and invertebrates. Where works would disturb a roost, a nest or a cetacean, that wording covers the conduct without requiring a kill. Restricted areas close a habitat, and one closes seasonally. Planning material records that the Ordinance restricts access to designated areas of wildlife habitat, that three restricted areas have been designated — named marshes, an egretry and a bay on an island — and that access controls there are implemented by the conservation department; a published legal review records one of them as a restricted area with a restricted period from 1 June to 31 October, during which patrols are regularly conducted. Asking whether a site sits inside a restricted area, and in which months, is therefore a concrete question. The planning register carries the scientific sites onto the statutory plans. Planning material records that the planning department maintains a register of sites of special scientific interest, that once designated those zones are shown on statutory and non-statutory town plans, and that normally no new development will be permitted within such a zone; that the planning legislation provides for designating coastal protection areas, sites of special scientific interest, conservation areas and green belt; and that the planning board has designated special land use zones and issued planning application guidelines for one bay area to prevent adverse impacts of development projects on the wetland habitats. Published material records that scores of such sites were designated over three decades, identified by the conservation department and documented by the planning department. Country parks and special areas cover a stated share of the land area. Read this with the town planning board window, the country park designation, the assessment register and the conservation policy entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The Ombudsman — direct investigations started without any complainant, jurisdiction over access-to-information refusals, and the twenty-four month limit that decides whether your complaint is heard
trackers.desc: The office can open an investigation with no complainant at all. The office records that it initiates, of its own volition, direct investigation operations into areas of suspected maladministration involving systemic problems or issues of significant public interest; that its considerations for doing so include whether the matter is of significant public interest and concern, and whether a complaint would otherwise not be actionable — for example where it is made anonymously or not by an aggrieved person — but the matter is nevertheless of significant concern because of the magnitude or seriousness of the maladministration involved. Where a community cannot show personal injustice, that is the door: a systemic problem can be put to the office even though an individual complaint would fail. Its powers are investigatory, and its secrecy duty is statutory. The office records that it may conduct inquiries, obtain information and documents, summon witnesses and inspect the premises of organisations under complaint, and reports results to the head of the organisation or, if appropriate, to the chief executive; and that the ombudsman, staff and advisers are bound by the ordinance to maintain secrecy on all matters of any complaint and investigation, liable to a fine and imprisonment for non-compliance, with reports publishable in the public interest without disclosing names. It also polices the access-to-information code already recorded in this bucket. Published material records that the office oversees complaints against the executive branch for non-compliance with the code on access to information, and records its methods as inquiry, full investigation where the complaint involves issues of principle, systemic flaws or serious maladministration, and mediation by trained investigators in minor cases with both parties' consent. Two limits decide whether you get in. The office records that complaints are excluded where the complainant has had knowledge of the subject for more than twenty-four months, or where a statutory right of appeal or remedy by way of legal proceedings is available — except judicial review; that its jurisdiction covers government departments and about thirty public bodies but not the police forces, the corruption commission or a named secretariat; and that a complaint must generally come from the person aggrieved, with identity documents, a postage-free complaint form, an online form and a hotline all published. Read this with the access to information code, the audit director, the pollution reporting entry and the legal aid entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: River and marine water quality data — station series from 1986 downloadable as spreadsheets, monthly dissolved oxygen and bacteria updates, and the ninety-four station marine programme behind them
trackers.desc: Four decades of water quality readings are published as downloadable files, station by station. The government open data portal carries historical river water quality data at different monitoring stations from 1986 to the present year, and historical marine water quality data at different monitoring stations from 1986, both in spreadsheet format, in English and both Chinese scripts, with each year available separately and a facility to specify a date range and download monthly or daily archives, or queue the whole period. The department's open data plan records both sets as updated yearly alongside the annual river and marine water quality reports, usually in the third quarter. A community arguing that a stream has deteriorated has a same-station series going back four decades to set its own sampling against. Recent readings are published at monthly intervals, on the two parameters that matter most for a discharge. The same plan records recent river water quality data — dissolved oxygen and bacteria at downstream monitoring stations of major rivers — in spreadsheet format, updated every mid-month, and recent marine data on the same two parameters. Those are the readings to check after a discharge is reported. The marine programme's scale and method are documented. A spatial data portal record states that the department has run a comprehensive marine monitoring programme since 1986, covering ninety-four sampling stations in the open sea, semi-enclosed bays and typhoon shelters; that temperature, pH, salinity, turbidity and dissolved oxygen are measured in situ; and that samples are taken for laboratory analysis of some twenty parameters including nutrients, organic constituents and microbiological content, retrievable through a hyperlink on each station under its water control zone, with station locations given in an appendix of the latest annual report. The department's own interactive centre displays and downloads the river data. The department runs a river water quality display and download tool, and publishes the annual marine reports for download, noting that the maps in them are indicative only. Read this with the pollution reporting entry, the water pollution control ordinance, the spatial data portal and the assessment register entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Non-in-situ land exchange for conservation — private land at a priority site surrendered in return for land elsewhere, the golf course it stopped, and the reserve run by a non-government body on leased land
trackers.desc: A land exchange took private land at a priority conservation site out of development, and the government announced it. The government's own news service records the completion of non-in-situ land exchange procedures for the long-term conservation of a named site, which ranks second among the twelve priority sites requiring enhanced conservation under the nature conservation policy, after the internationally designated wetland; records that the private land surrendered by the development company and the adjacent government land amount to over fifty hectares; and records the government adopting a strategy of active nature conservation for the site. It describes the habitats at stake — fung shui woods, freshwater marshes and an ecologically important stream, with rare butterflies, fireflies, freshwater fish, amphibians and birds, and one of the territory's important breeding grounds for dragonflies. The trade itself is on record, which is what makes it a usable precedent. Published commentary records an initial land exchange in 2017 with the company holding most of the land putting a massive golf course project on hold, and records that the developer later gave up about twenty hectares of the site in return for fifty hectares elsewhere, with a reduced land premium, to proceed with the golf course; it records the site to be divided into habitat zones accessible only on foot to minimise human impact. Where a community faces a project on ecologically valuable private land, that is the shape of a deal that has actually been done. A non-government body manages the wetland reserve itself. The conservation organisation records managing the reserve as a staging and wintering ground for migratory waterbirds and for threatened indigenous biodiversity, showcasing traditional tidal shrimp pond practice as wise use of wetlands, with five main habitats named; published description records the reserve as part of that organisation since 1983, with the agriculture and conservation department responsible for the wider designated site, and records entry to the reserve requiring a permit, obtainable by joining the organisation's guided activity or by written application. Its works have been funded by a stated multi-hundred-million dollar charitable grant. Read this with the nature conservation policy entry, the conservancy association's management agreements, the countryside funding scheme and the land resumption entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The Ecological Advisory Programme — a standing body that monitors planning applications, zoning proposals and assessments, runs field surveys across named habitat types, and lodges objections
trackers.desc: A non-government programme monitors development proposals and objects to them, as standing work rather than campaign by campaign. The organisation records the programme as actively monitoring ecologically sensitive areas and areas of natural countryside affected by development proposals, playing a direct role in protecting them by carrying out field surveys and site inspections, documenting and sharing ecological information, participating in meetings and forums, submitting letters of concern and lodging objections; and records that it monitors planning applications, land use zoning proposals, environmental impact assessments and development proposals. It records the programme acting upon reports of possible harmful environmental damage caused by activities such as illegal dumping, disturbance to sensitive areas and improper land use — so a resident who sees dumping has somewhere to report it that will follow up in the planning system. The survey coverage is listed by habitat, which tells you whether your site is one they work in.
