The same page records field surveys regularly organised across streams, channels, meanders, marshes, mangroves, rocky shores, boulder shores, sandy shores, mudflats, tidal shrimp ponds, ponds, secondary woodlands, fung shui woodlands, plantations, shrublands, grasslands, farmlands, developed and brownfield sites, and shallows along the coastline, targeting both fauna and flora, some conducted by specialist departments including botanical surveys; and records that submissions on government policies or proposals can be downloaded from its reports and publications page. Published description records the programme, launched in 1998, as advising government, environmental organisations, villagers, ecological consultants, academics and private developers. The organisation behind it holds land and runs the rescue centre. Published material records it established in 1956, its partly reforested, partially terraced land and streams now a sanctuary for native wild animals and plants, with a wild animal rescue centre that has cared for over forty thousand wild animals, around three thousand arriving yearly; and records a wild snake rescue project run with the conservation department and the police since 1999, which had processed over fourteen thousand snakes as of 2019. Read this with the conservancy association, the assessment register, the town planning board and the pollution reporting entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 香港觀鳥會 HKBWS — management agreements with landowners and farmers, an annual bird report published since 1958, and professional comments filed on development plans
trackers.desc: Conservation here is done by agreement with the people who own and farm the land. Published material records the society and a partner organisation running an agricultural wetland conservation management programme since 2005 at a named valley, in cooperation with local farmers and stakeholders, reintroducing wetland crops including paddy rice, water chestnut and Chinese arrowhead to increase habitat heterogeneity; and records that restoration of paddy field was especially successful, with rare migratory species that used to appear in rice fields becoming common and regularly recorded, a globally critically endangered bunting now appearing regularly during migration. A partner records that local stakeholders, particularly landowners, farmers and villagers, are the major partners of the project, conservation management being achieved by cooperating with stakeholders under management agreements. That is a route that pays the owner rather than fighting them. A second site shows what the agreements are for. The society records a village area of highlands, fung shui woodland, village, streams, farmlands, marsh, intertidal zone and bay where river channels and farmlands had been abandoned for decades, with free-roaming water buffalo creating puddles that provide microhabitats for amphibians and dragonflies, and warns that without proper habitat management the low-lying wetlands, rare in the territory, will drain and become drylands, lowering the area's ecological value; it records funding from a named conservation fund since December 2021. Its record is the evidence a case needs. Published description records the society founded in 1957, an approved public charitable institution since 2002, promoting protection of birds and habitats through education, research, habitat management and conservation advocacy; records an annual bird report published since 1958 as a resource for understanding populations and trends; and records that the society presents its views on local development plans and provides professional comments to the government on conservation action, birds and habitat protection. It records citizen science work, a membership in the thousands and the compilation of important bird area listings. Read this with the conservancy association, the nature conservation policy, the assessment register and the ecological advisory programme entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Planning and development surveyors — the professionals a community can hire to draft objections and appear at hearings, their institute's division, and the free guide to the process written for objectors
trackers.desc: There is a named profession whose ordinary work is preparing planning objections, and it can be hired. The surveyors' institute records that planning and development surveyors advise clients on the extent to which the use and value of their land and property would be affected by town planning and environmental policies, and lists their most common professional services as preparation, coordination and submission of planning applications, master layout plans, rezoning requests and planning objections; and acting on behalf of clients in making written representations and attending hearings in planning review and appeal cases under the board's and the appeal board's proceedings. It records them also assisting in site planning, advising on urban design with design experts, and coordinating large-scale planning studies supported by technical impact assessments. A community that has been told its objection must be professionally prepared now knows which profession to ask for. A published guide explains the process from the objector's side. A think tank's user's guide to the town planning process records that the process defines what the community sees as appropriate uses of land and provides ways to ensure it is used in that way; records that an applicant will engage a planning consultant, an estate surveying company, an architect, a solicitor or some other person who understands the system to make the submission and handle the procedures; and works through a real case in which 16 comments in support were received from legislative councillors, business groups and district councillors, 1,034 signatures in support came from the public, and a district council passed a resolution in support — yet the board did not accept the application, appreciating the intentions but not being convinced the proposal was the best solution. That case is a lesson in what weight of support does and does not do. The board's own counters answer questions, and the filing requirements are published. Board guidelines publish the secretariat's address and two telephone numbers and the planning department's enquiry counters with a hotline, email and postal addresses; and record that where supporting information such as colour or large-size plans, planning studies and technical assessments is included in representations, ninety copies must be provided for circulation and public inspection, in either language with a summary in the other. Read this with the participation page, the ecological advisory programme, the bird society and the conservancy association entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Liber Research Community — a registered non-profit that does land searches and site scans, publishes a spatial database and report archive, and trains the public to do the research itself
trackers.desc: A community that needs to know who owns what has an organisation that does that work and publishes it. The group records itself as founded in 2010 and registered as a non-profit company in 2014, one of the few remaining civic research communities in the territory, and states its purposes as raising the public's capacity to research social issues of public interest so that civil society can reveal problems and respond to them with reason; writing and publishing research reports, articles and books through various civic research methods to establish a factual basis; and running research as team collaboration, through volunteer recruitment, exchange activities and division of work. Training the public to do the research is what leaves capacity behind after a campaign ends. Its outputs are the datasets a community would otherwise have to build from scratch. Its spatial database lists items including brownfields in a named development area with development potential; land acquisition by developers within a named redevelopment study area; buildings issued with demolition consent over a decade; public housing estates' non-residential properties divested to a named trust; and a study on avoidance of residential property tax by share transfer. Its report archive records studies including brownfield sites tracing causes and distributions; a case study on short-term lease arrangements at a named site; a study of short-term tenancy sites held by tycoons; and research on abuse of the small house policy by selling rights. Two findings show what such research does to an official case. Published material records its study finding 532 pieces of vacant government land totalling 301 hectares, across all 18 districts, which the government had left vacant or under-utilised; and records a year-long study finding 1,521 hectares of brownfield sites — above the government's own estimate of 1,300 — with almost 90 per cent used for operations that could be relocated into multi-storey buildings and only 12 per cent difficult to relocate, with a researcher quoted that the government has land, policies, power and money. It records a publication written with a citizens' task force to provide counter-arguments to the official land supply debate. Read this with the planning surveyors, the ecological advisory programme, the assessment register and the participation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The Hong Kong Countryside Foundation — a body that leased 40,000 square metres of village farmland from owners to bring a village back, and the four-partner structure that did the work
trackers.desc: A foundation leased farmland from the villagers who owned it, and the area is stated. The foundation records that in 2013, with the help of villagers who sincerely wished to restore the village, it leased about 40,000 square metres of farmland from them — a lease, not a purchase, which is the arrangement available where land cannot or should not change hands. It records working closely with the villagers since 2011, jointly exploring ways to revitalise the village, and describes the starting point plainly: the village mostly deserted, fields fallow for decades and generally overgrown with shrubs, many traditional tiled-roof houses slowly crumbling, with action urgently needed to re-populate the village and bring back meaningful employment for its residents, or it would become yet another abandoned village in the New Territories, forgotten within a decade. The work was split between four named organisations, each with a defined job. Published description records the programme initiated and led by a university institute in collaboration with the foundation, a farming foundation and a conservation association, endorsed by the agriculture, fisheries and conservation department and by the villagers. A university case study records the division: the lead acted as the primary bridge between external associations and the village community; the foundation communicated with villagers and leased fields from them for farming rehabilitation; the farming foundation focused on farming rehabilitation; the conservation association launched environmental education activities; and university scholars conducted ecological and hydrological research. That allocation is the transferable part. The public funding scheme behind later phases lists what it has paid for. The government countryside office's project list records funded projects including an eco-fishpond management agreement scheme, a habitat and biodiversity conservation scheme at a named valley, rehabilitation of village gateway structures, restoration of old houses for village community use, and landscape improvement, and records the office facilitating a non-profit organisation's application for a guesthouse licence for century-old village houses. Read this with the conservancy association, the countryside funding scheme, the bird society's management agreements and the ecological advisory programme entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Rural committees and village representatives — 27 committees covering 642 recognised villages, two representatives per village including one for non-indigenous residents, and district offices as the standing liaison
trackers.desc: Every recognised village has elected representatives, and one of the two seats is for residents who are not indigenous. The home affairs department records that since 2003 village representative elections have been brought under statutory control, and published material records that there have been two elected positions for each village — the indigenous village representative, elected by descendants of families which lived in the village in 1898, and the resident village representative, elected by permanent identity card holders who live in the village, both serving on a rural committee. For a newcomer household in a village facing a project, the resident representative is a seat its own neighbours vote for. The committees are the layer the government reads village opinion through. Published material records that the representatives are elected to serve on a rural committee, of which there are 27; that the committees are influential and are used by the government to assess village sentiment; and that the chair of each committee serves on the rural council and is an ex officio member of the relevant district council. It records the committees as fulfilling a pivotal role in the administration of the small house policy. Knowing that the chair of your rural committee sits on the district council by right is knowing where a village objection travels. The scale is published, and so is the funding. Published research records 642 approved recognised villages, meaning they existed in 1898 with their names on the government leases produced then, organised under the 27 committees; and a legislature reply records over 1,000 village representatives, who serve as the main contact point for the whole village in times of natural disasters and other emergency incidents. That reply records subvention granted to rural committees, adjusted upwards in 2011 and 2018 by 10.8 and 24 per cent, honorarium granted to village representatives, and that the district offices in the New Territories maintain close liaison with village representatives and rural committees. Read this with the countryside foundation, the planning surveyors, the ecological advisory programme and the land research community entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Owners' corporations and the District Building Management Liaison Teams — a body corporate that acts legally for all owners, liaison teams in all 18 district offices, and free lawyers, mediators and a retired judge
trackers.desc: Owners can incorporate into a body that acts legally on their behalf. The department records an owners' corporation as an independent body corporate which acts legally on behalf of all owners in managing the common parts of the building, and exercises and performs the rights, powers, privileges and duties of the owners, and is empowered to appoint property management companies, terminate their appointment and monitor their work. For residents facing a management company or a works decision, a corporation is a legal person with standing that individual owners lack. The district offices help form one, and the threshold is small. The department records that owners of not less than 5 per cent of the shares in aggregate shall appoint an owner as convenor of the meeting of owners; records district offices as issuing an exemption certificate to the convenor for a free copy of the building's land record from the land registry for the purpose of convening that meeting, returnable within 60 days; and records officers attending the meeting of owners for the formation of a corporation and providing information on appointing a management committee. It records district building management liaison teams in all 18 district offices, made up of trained liaison officers, responsible for assisting owners in forming corporations, attending meetings and giving information to help tackle building management issues. When a dispute starts, four free services are named. The department records, for disagreements between corporations and owners: a free legal advice service, under which the law society arranges for its members to give professional advice on the ordinance and related legal matters; a free mediation scheme providing up to 15 hours of professional mediation to save the cost and time of legal action; a panel of advisors comprising lawyers, accountants, surveyors and property managers; and a dispute resolution service in which the department arranges a retired judge or judicial officer to assist the parties. It records a further outreach service launched in September 2019 under which a lawyer experienced in building management attends the pre-meeting and the general meeting and gives legal advice for up to six hours, applied for through the district office at least 28 days ahead. Read this with the rural committees, the planning surveyors, the land research community and the countryside foundation entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: District offices, district minor works and the signature project grant — 18 district offices that fund community projects, a works programme councils prioritise, and a one-off grant of 100 million dollars per district
trackers.desc: Each of the eighteen district offices funds community projects and oversees local works. One district office records that it provides funding to implement or sponsor community involvement projects, and oversees the implementation of works projects under the district minor works programme, and that it serves as the focal point for district administration, ensuring that public policies are effectively implemented at the district level, coordinating the district council, the district services and community care teams, and named district committees. For a neighbourhood with a proposal rather than only a complaint, the district office is the counter that holds money. The minor works programme is district-driven, and the steps are published. Published description records the programme as initiated in 2007 and fully implemented since January 2008, funding minor works projects to improve local facilities, living environment and hygienic conditions through the 18 district councils; records the councils as responsible for collating local views and district aspirations in planning and scheduling minor works, endorsing projects proposed by government departments, determining implementation priority and timetable, and monitoring progress; and records the key steps as council members identifying a project and preparing project statements, then councils prioritising projects, with a proposal that a member or dedicated working group follow up each project's planning, including site inspections. The signature grant shows the scale a district can command. The department records that under a scheme introduced in 2013 a one-off grant of 100 million dollars was reserved for each district to implement one to two projects addressing local needs with a visible and lasting impact, that all such projects are proposed, discussed and agreed by the district councils following consultation with local residents and organisations, and that 27 projects have been implemented across the 18 districts — including improvement of trails and provision of facilities adjoining a named marine park and a global geopark to promote eco-tourism, a pier reconstruction, and a heritage hiking trail with an information centre. Read this with the owners' corporations, the rural committees, the countryside foundation and the land research community entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: District lands offices and the New Territories search offices — twelve district offices handling leases, squatter control and enforcement, four regional search counters, and the cross-reference table that finds a rural lot
trackers.desc: An address alone will not find a rural lot, and the registry says so. The land registry records that for searching the land record of a property in a demarcation district, providing the address of the property alone is not sufficient, and directs enquirers to an index of streets, house numbers and lots for urban properties, or a New Territories lot and address cross reference table for rural properties, both available at its search offices and free online, or to the relevant district survey office of the lands department. For a village community trying to find out who holds the land behind it, that table and that district office are the first stop. Searches are done in person at regional counters, and the identification rules are published. The registry records that land search cannot be conducted by phone, but may be done at the customer centre or any of the New Territories search offices in person, or online; records citizens as able to use the customer service centre in a named district or any of the four centres in the New Territories to search and register property and order photocopies of property documents; and records what identification an individual or an organisation's authorised person must produce. What a land record shows includes court orders. The registry records that the incumbrances section of the land record contains information of court orders, so an enquirer can check for an injunction against sale, and that the user restriction of a lot is in the government lease under which the lot is held, with the unit's restriction in the occupation permit or deed of mutual covenant, obtainable from the buildings department if unregistered. The district lands offices are the enforcement side. Published description records the lands administration office as comprising a headquarters, professional sections and 12 district lands offices, responsible for land grants, valuations, land resumption, property management, lease renewals and amendments, slope maintenance, lease enforcement, land control and management and squatter control, each headed by a district lands officer. Read this with the owners' corporations, the district offices and minor works, the rural committees and the land research community entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The professional advisory scheme for 'three-nil' buildings — free property management advice for buildings with no corporation, 540 corporations formed or revived, and the 30 per cent share threshold when there is no deed provision
trackers.desc: Buildings with no management at all get free professional help to form a corporation. The department records a scheme run to support owners of 'three-nil' buildings, and buildings where the management committee of the owners' corporation was defunct, under which it commissioned property management companies to provide owners of old buildings in need with a range of free professional advisory and follow-up services on building management, including facilitating the formation or re-activation of corporations, assisting corporations in applying for funding under various loan and subsidy schemes for maintenance works, and following up on building and window inspections, maintenance works and tendering. It records a total of 540 corporations formed or re-activated with that assistance across three phases. For residents of an old building with no committee and no manager, that is a named route back to having a legal body. Non-governmental organisations were brought in to knock on doors. The same record describes a pilot inviting local organisations and non-governmental organisations with experience in building management or related fields to reach out to owners of 'three-nil' buildings and encourage and assist them in forming corporations, launched first in two named districts in June 2022 and progressively extended to other districts with a relatively large number of such buildings, seven of which are named. The threshold when the deed is silent is published. A published building management guide records that if there is no deed of mutual covenant, or the deed contains no provision for appointing a management committee, a management committee can be appointed by a resolution of the owners of not less than 30 per cent of the shares in the building; and records that notice of the meeting and the matters to be discussed must be given to all owners at least 14 days before the meeting, displayed in a prominent place in the building and placed in a newspaper from a specified list, that list being obtainable from the district offices and building management resource centres. Read this with the owners' corporations, the district offices and minor works, the rural committees and the district lands offices entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The revitalisation scheme — a charity can take a government-owned historic building at nominal rent, with renovation paid for and start-up losses covered, and size or heritage experience carries no weight
trackers.desc: A charitable organisation can take over a government-owned historic building at nominal rent. The heritage authority records the scheme as identifying government-owned historic buildings considered suitable for adaptive re-use, with non-profit-making organisations invited to submit applications for using these buildings to provide services or run business in the form of social enterprise. It records the support as a one-off grant to cover the cost of major renovation to the buildings, in part or in full; nominal rental for the buildings; and a one-off grant to meet the starting costs and operating deficits of the social enterprises for a maximum of the first two years of operation at a stated ceiling, on the prerequisite that the proposal is projected to become self-sustainable after that period. Renovation paid for, rent at a nominal figure and two years of losses covered is the closest thing in this bucket to being handed a building. The eligibility rule is narrow in one way and wide in another. The authority records that the applicant should be a non-profit-making organisation with charitable status under a named section of the revenue legislation; and other published material records that joint ventures of two or more such organisations are welcome; that applicants need not have obtained charitable status at the time of submission provided they obtain it within nine months after the application deadline; and that participation requirements are broad, with equal weight promised to organisations regardless of size, age or local experience in heritage conservation. A new group with no heritage record is not disadvantaged on paper. The obligations and the risk are recorded too. Published material records that selected organisations are responsible for the renovation and conservation of the buildings as well as the operation of the social enterprises, that any profit generated will be ploughed back into the same project, and that government signs tenancy agreements setting out terms and conditions, examines the operation regularly, and requires regular progress reports and annual reports. It records one building as having been returned to the government by its operator in 2017, then offered again in two later batches. Read this with the countryside conservation funding scheme, the historic building grading, the countryside foundation and the conservancy association entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Macau — Commercial & Movable Property Registry (DSAJ / CRCBM)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the DSAJ’s Commercial & Movable Property Registry runs an online commercial-register information platform (company number, firm, seat, capital, directors), Macau SAR. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Macau — Commission of Audit (Comissariado da Auditoria)
trackers.desc: National public-finance watchdog; the Commission of Audit is Macau’s government auditor, conducting independent financial & performance audits of public operations and publishing audit reports, Macau SAR. — Holds to account: officials handling public money & power — find audit findings and how public money was spent or lost.

trackers.name: Macau — Financial Services Bureau (DSF)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Direcção dos Serviços de Finanças prepares & executes the Macau SAR budget, manages public revenue, expenditure & accounts and publishes budget & financial reports, Macau. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Macau.

trackers.name: The heritage law is the instrument with teeth — and it binds the planners
trackers.desc: IN MACAU THE PROTECTIVE INSTRUMENT OVER LAND IS THE CULTURAL HERITAGE LAW, NOT A NATURE LAW — worth knowing before you search for one. Decree-Law No. 11/2013 of 22 August protects immovable property classified OR in the process of being classified, and property in protection zones or provisional protection zones — the third preliminary-protection instrument in this map, after Bosnia's privremena zaštita and Kosovo's mbrojtja paraprake. THE STATUS GOES ON THE LAND REGISTER: it must be noted (averbada) against the property description, and the noting is made ex officio and free of charge — so protection is discoverable by any buyer or developer from the predial description, and securing it costs the applicant nothing. THE STRONGEST PROVISION IS THE BINDING PRIOR OPINION: issuing plantas de alinhamento oficial or plantas de condições urbanísticas for the Historic Centre, classified property or protection zones requires the parecer vinculativo prévio of the IC — a binding, not advisory, opinion over the planning documents that precede any building permission. Ask whether it was obtained. Urban plans of any nature must contain specific protective measures and are elaborated with the participation of the IC. AND THE TRIGGER THRESHOLD IS LOW: obras de grande impacte are public or private works — expressly including hydraulic works, infrastructure and communication routes — which may imply risk of deterioration, destruction OR DIMINUTION OF THE VALUE of classified property or its protection zones. Risk of diminution suffices; certain harm is not required. The Historic Centre's safeguard plan must also guarantee sustainable use in urban, cultural AND environmental terms.

trackers.name: DSPA — hotline, and the plan vocabulary to write your proposal in
trackers.desc: A REACHABLE BODY AND A FRAME TO USE. The Environmental Protection Bureau (DSPA): Estrada de D. Maria II, 32-36, Edifício CEM, 1.º andar, Macau; main line (853) 2872 5134; Environmental Protection Hotline (853) 2876 2626 — a dedicated hotline is the faster route for a complaint. It produced Macao's first environmental planning (2010–2020), whose stated aim includes establishing an urban ecosystem network composed of green points (greening nodes), lines (linear greening and corridors), areas (parks and leisure zones) and spaces (vertical greening). USE THAT VOCABULARY: points, lines, areas and spaces are the plan's own categories, so a corridor or a single node already has a named place in it — a proposal framed in those terms fits the instrument rather than arguing against it. LANGUAGE CAUTION FROM THE GOVERNMENT'S OWN PORTAL: all information is based on the official language of the Macao SAR, and the English version is a translation from the Chinese originals, provided for reference only. Work from the Chinese or Portuguese text wherever anything turns on wording — and note that this map's heritage-law entry for Macau cites the Portuguese text for that reason.

trackers.name: Instituto Cultural — any Macau resident can ask for a building or site to be classified
trackers.desc: Article 19 of the Cultural Heritage Protection Law puts the trigger in a resident's hands. A classification procedure may be started by the Cultural Affairs Bureau, by another public department or by the owner of the immovable — and residents of the Macau SAR may submit a request for classification to the Bureau. In a territory where almost every fight over land is a fight over a building or a site, that request is the most direct lever a person has. Starting the procedure is itself protective. The law treats property that is pending classification alongside property already classified and property inside a buffer zone, so a site under an open procedure is not in the same position as one nobody has ever asked about — which is why the timing of a request matters as much as its eventual outcome. Buffer zones can be set around a classified property, extending protection past the parcel itself. Four categories, and one of them is not a building. Classified immovables are monuments, buildings of architectural artistic value, ensembles, and sites; the last is the category to reach for where what is threatened is ground rather than a structure. There are currently 165 classified immovables across Macau, Taipa and Coloane, added in batches by administrative regulation, most recently under Regulation 6/2024. The procedure runs research, then public consultation, then assessment of the opinions received, then classification — the first batch of 400 movable items, begun on 4 December 2024, was completed by Regulation 18/2025, so expect roughly a year. There is a carrot for the owner, worth knowing before approaching one. A classified immovable that has been conserved, repaired or restored and is in good condition is exempt from urban property tax, the exemption being confirmed by the Finance Bureau on application and supported by a Bureau certificate of the property's condition. An owner who treats classification as pure cost may not know that. Recommendations on classification, on buffer zones and on acquisition or expropriation of classified, pending and buffer-zone property go to the Cultural Heritage Council, chaired by the Secretary for Social Affairs and Culture with the Bureau's president as vice-chair, and including the Land and Public Works and Municipal Affairs bureaux and up to twelve experts and community figures.

trackers.name: 規劃條件圖 planning condition plans — a minimum fifteen days to comment on a specific plot
trackers.desc: Where a district has no detailed plan, the conditions for an individual plot are fixed by a planning condition plan, and the draft of that document goes out for public comment for not less than fifteen days. The bureau publishes the draft in the newspapers and on its website together with an explanatory note setting out the planning conditions and the basis for them; opinions from interested parties and from the public are collected; and the draft together with the opinions received then goes to the Urban Planning Committee for discussion before the bureau issues it, amends it or studies it further. That is a comment window on a specific parcel, with the reasoning published alongside it. Heritage and ecology have to be asked. Where construction or extension works may affect cultural heritage protection, ecological environment protection or road works, the bureau is required to seek the opinion of the public administration departments competent in those fields — so a submission identifying a heritage or ecological consequence engages a consultation the bureau must run, rather than merely a view it may consider. Know what the document does and does not decide. A planning condition plan records the plot's use, the street alignment and future boundaries, surrounding public infrastructure, construction conditions and any special burdens on the concessionaire, and it is valid for two years. Its development indicators — height, plot ratio, coverage — are upper limits at the planning level only; what is finally approved is further constrained by the site itself, street width and shadow, fire safety and the building regulations, so the maximum shown is not a promise. Two things to read before commenting. The bureau publishes both issued planning condition plans and amended ones, so the documents already issued nearby show what the administration has been prepared to allow. And the Urban Planning Committee, which advises on plans and on these documents, must have fewer than half its members drawn from the public administration, the rest being professionals and persons of recognised standing; its composition is published and its members are subject to the recusal rules of the Administrative Procedure Code.

trackers.name: 法律援助 legal aid — the right to be accompanied by a lawyer before any public authority
trackers.desc: The broadest single right recorded in this file: a lawyer beside you in front of any public authority, with no power of attorney needed in advance. The legal aid statute provides that everyone has the right to legal information and legal consultation, to be represented in court, and to be accompanied by a lawyer when facing any public authority — judicial and criminal investigation authorities in particular — without having to hold or produce a mandate beforehand, and regardless of their standing in relation to that authority. A resident called to a departmental meeting, an inspection or an interview may therefore bring a lawyer as of right rather than by permission. Legal protection comes in two forms, and the test is economic. Protection takes the form of legal consultation and of judicial assistance, and a natural person who shows insufficient economic means to pay the fees of the professional representing them in court and all or part of the general costs of the proceedings is entitled to it. The threshold is inability to pay, not the category of case. The statute's stated purpose is worth putting in the application itself. Access to law and to the courts exists so that no one is hindered or prevented, by reason of their social or cultural condition or of insufficient economic means, from knowing, obtaining or defending their rights. An applicant who frames their request in the statute's own terms is asking for what the law says it is for. Know how a lawyer is actually assigned. Published analysis records that Macau has no dedicated agency delivering judicial assistance services: when a lawyer is selected for a beneficiary the choice is made from the list of practitioners registered with the bar association, and in principle the appointed lawyer then represents the beneficiary through the whole of the proceedings and the procedures deriving from them. The government works through the legal affairs bureau with registered court practitioners to provide consultation services, and a legal aid commission exists alongside them. Read this with the planning condition plan entry recorded here: that is where a Macau objection lands, and this is who can help write it.

trackers.name: 廉政公署 administrative complaints — an ombudsman that reaches concessionaires as well as departments
trackers.desc: The remit reaches concessionaires, which is where many development disputes actually sit. Alongside its anti-corruption work the commission carries out administrative complaint work across public administration departments, public legal persons, public enterprises and companies in which more than half the capital is public, and — the part worth noting — public service concessionaires and concessionaires of public property, in order to protect people's rights, freedoms, safeguards and legitimate interests. Where the protection of rights, freedoms and safeguards is at stake it may also reach relations between private parties standing in a relationship of special dominance. A private operator running a concession over public ground is therefore not outside the door. The powers are investigative rather than advisory. The commission may enter any public entity, with or without notice, to inspect, examine documents, hear the officials concerned and require whatever information it thinks appropriate; may conduct or require special or full investigations and other measures aimed at ascertaining the legality of administrative acts and procedures in the relations between public entities and private persons; and supervises the regularity and administrative correctness of acts involving property interests. Unannounced entry and examination of documents are the operative words. The output is a recommendation to correct, and it is published. It may issue recommendations to any public department to correct illegal or unjust administrative acts, propose improvements to a department's operation, efficiency and transparency, issue guidelines and propose legislation. A recommendation is not an order, and an entry in this file should say so — but it is made in public and against a named department. Read the case summaries before you write. The commission publishes summaries of administrative complaint cases and its investigation reports with recommendations, so a complainant can see how comparable matters were framed and what was found. Complaints may be made online, at the complaint reception centre, or at the community offices, with a dedicated complaints line. Read this with the planning condition plan and legal aid entries recorded here: the comment window is where an objection lands, and this is where unlawful or unfair handling of that objection goes.

trackers.name: 環境保護局 — complaints and objections, station-level annual data, and the assessment platform
trackers.desc: The bureau receives objections as well as complaints, and the distinction matters. Its published service is to receive the public's opinions, complaints and declarations of objection in the environmental field and to follow them up and handle them. A declaration of objection is a more formal act than a complaint, and a resident who is contesting a decision rather than reporting a nuisance should use the word that matches what they are doing. The licence and the inspector sit in the same department. The environmental pollution control department is responsible for the prevention, inspection, supervision and control of pollution and for issuing environmental licences, with an environmental inspection division and a pollution prevention and control division beneath it. A complaint about an operator can therefore ask, in the same letter, what environmental licence that operator holds and on what conditions — which is a shorter route than treating the licence and the nuisance as separate enquiries. The data is published annually and station by station. The bureau publishes environmental data and an environmental geographic information system, an annual state of the environment report, and annual monitoring data reports for its monitoring stations, and takes part in a regional air monitoring network. The air quality network operates around the clock and publishes an index with recommended precautions and next-day forecasts, covering respirable and fine suspended particulates, sulphur dioxide, ozone, carbon monoxide and nitrogen dioxide. Station-level annual data is what allows a resident to compare the year before a project with the year after, using the regulator's own figures rather than commissioned ones. There is an assessment information platform as well. The bureau maintains a platform covering the progress of environmental assessment in Macau, assessment at the planning level, the basic principles of environmental consideration for planning projects, project-level assessment, and the applicable laws, standards and guidelines, and has published a revised list of the projects subject to assessment. Read this with the planning condition plan entry recorded here: the plan is where an objection lands, and this is where the assessment framework and the monitoring data behind it are kept.

trackers.name: 文化發展基金 — money for heritage research, and for work in the streets and heritage buildings themselves
trackers.desc: The intended applicant is a local association. Under its cultural activities and projects scheme the fund requires applicants to be non-profit local associations or foundations legally established on or before a stated cutoff date, and to be the organiser of the activity they are applying for. The funded fields run across visual arts, literature, music, opera, drama and dance, and include tangible and intangible cultural heritage. A residents' association constituted in time is not stretching to fit this scheme; it is the body the scheme is written for. Two of its stated preferences read like a community defence programme. The published criteria favour activities that enter the community, use the community as their stage, draw residents into taking part and improve the community's cultural environment — and activities that make good use of Macau's streets, squares, parks and world heritage buildings as public space, uncovering the history and culture of the community. Work rooted in one particular place, carried out in that place, is what the fund says it is looking for. Heritage knowledge itself is fundable. Among the listed preferences is work on the transmission, education, research and promotion of Macau's cultural heritage and of heritage-protection knowledge. Research establishing what a place is and why it warrants protection can therefore be paid for — and that research is the evidence a classification request needs, which makes this fund the practical companion to the heritage classification entry recorded for this country. Know the ceilings, and promise only what you can deliver. One-year activities are capped by activity type at between thirty thousand and five hundred thousand patacas, and two-year projects at eight hundred thousand, with limits on how many applications each applicant may file and how many may be approved. The fund adjusts the granted amount downward where the quantified indicators actually delivered fall short of those projected in the application, or where a surplus arises. In one recent year it ran eleven schemes, received over two thousand applications and approved more than eleven hundred projects. Applications go through the fund's online system, and it holds briefing sessions before each round.

trackers.name: 物業登記局 — property certificates online, a free authenticity checker, and criminal liability for a false registration
trackers.desc: Get the registration certificate before arguing about the plot. The property registry issues property registration certificates and written reports, and applications can be made online across long daily service hours, with the certificate collected in person or by an authorised representative once notified, or taken as an electronic certificate through the government's single account with payment made online. For anyone contesting what may be built on a particular piece of ground, the certificate is the document that says who is recorded as holding it and on what terms. Anyone can verify a certificate for free, without asking its holder. The justice services operate a public verification platform which checks the authenticity of registration certificates and notarial documents instantly and without charge: entering the document's unique number and its verification code returns the issuing authority, the name of the signatory and the date of issue, and the platform also publishes statistics on the certificates and notarial acts issued. A developer's paperwork can therefore be checked against the state's own record by the people it is being shown to. Nothing else recorded in this file offers that. Validity, renewal and progress are all defined. A certificate used for the signing of a deed is valid for three months, and where the registered data has not changed an electronic certificate can be confirmed online to extend its validity, keeping its original code and gaining a note recording the confirmation. The progress of an application can be checked through an online system by entering the application date and number, or by telephoning the registry. A false registration is a criminal matter. Causing a false act, or an act which does not exist in law, to be registered may attract criminal liability as well as liability for the damage caused; and making or confirming false or inaccurate declarations, whether inside the registry or outside it, carries civil and criminal liability. That is worth knowing before a community is asked to sign anything about land, and worth citing when somebody else's declaration looks wrong. Read this with the heritage classification and planning entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Drinking water results published by district — and the private labs that will test for an individual
trackers.desc: The municipal laboratory publishes the results, not only the standards. Its testing division continuously monitors the treated water leaving the plant, the public supply networks in each district, the reservoirs and the raw water supplied to the territory, in order to keep the public supply safe and stable. The monitoring follows the parameters set by the water supply and drainage regulation and uses international standard analytical methods, covering physico-chemical indicators, organic compounds, ions, heavy metals, microbiology, pesticide residues and radioactive substances — and the laboratory publishes water quality information, results, evaluations and statistics. Before a community commissions any testing of its own, the results for its own district network have already been published. Pesticide residues and radioactivity are on the routine list. Very few of the published monitoring programmes recorded in this file name either, let alone both. A community asking about them here is asking for something the state already measures on a schedule, which is a far shorter conversation than asking for a new test to be devised. A private laboratory will test for an individual. A locally established independent third-party environmental testing company describes its work as water analysis covering industrial wastewater, sewage, seawater and drinking water, together with indoor and outdoor air quality testing, and states that it provides commissioned testing and technical consultancy to government departments, enterprises and individuals. That is recorded from the provider's own material rather than as a state guarantee, and the standing instruction applies: ask what the laboratory is accredited for, confirm your parameters fall inside that scope, and ask for the measurement uncertainty with each figure. And there is a sampling rhythm worth borrowing. Published guidance for public drinking water machines requires sampling and testing by a professional body every three months, the immediate closure of a machine and posting of a notice if a result fails the standard, retesting after repair before it reopens, and proper record keeping of results and shutdowns. A quarterly sampling schedule with a shut-down rule attached is a template a community can propose for any installation it is worried about. Read this with the environmental bureau's station data and complaints entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 商業登記訊息平台 — free instant company data, including who may sign for the company
trackers.desc: A free platform shows the basic registration data instantly, to anyone. The commercial and movable property registry operates a commercial registration information platform which is free, immediate and not restricted by location: entering a registration number or a keyword returns the basic registered particulars of a Macau commercial entrepreneur, whether a natural person or a legal person, and of the enterprise — the registration number, the commercial name, the domicile, the business objects, the capital, and the members of the administrative body together with the manner in which they may sign. That last item is rarely published anywhere in this research, and it decides whether the person sitting across the table from a community can bind the company at all. The certificate is the version with full probative force. A commercial registration certificate is a document of full evidential value in law, usable for judicial purposes and for public acts. It carries no fixed validity of its own — that depends on the body receiving it — except that a certificate used for a notarial act is valid for three months, and where the registered data has not changed the certificate can be confirmed at any time to extend it. Where to apply. Applications are made on a form obtainable at the registry or downloadable from the bureau's site, or through the government's single account service, quoting the commercial name, the establishment or the registration number; electronic certificates carry the same legal effect as paper ones. The registry sits in the public administration building with published office hours and a telephone number, and applications are also taken at the government services centre and the islands services centre. And a business must declare to the tax bureau thirty days before it opens. Anyone intending to carry on an industrial or commercial activity must file a commencement declaration with the finance bureau's business tax centre at least thirty days before the premises open. A project which has not filed that declaration is not yet lawfully open, and the date on the declaration is itself a fact worth asking for. Read this with the property registry, planning condition plan and heritage classification entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Public procurement information — every bidder's price, and the award amount
trackers.desc: The losing bids are published too. For a procurement run as an open tender, the finance bureau's description of what is disclosed covers the tender announcement, the tender programme and the bidding and works rules that make up the tender documents; and then, once the bid opening has been completed, the names of the bidders, their prices, their delivery periods and whether each was accepted or rejected. Nothing else recorded in this procurement sweep publishes the unsuccessful bids, and they are what allow a community to see how far the winning price sat from the rest of the field. After the award: the name, the date, the amount and the period. The information published once an award is made comprises the name of the party awarded the contract, the date of the award, the amount awarded and the delivery period. The value of the contract and the time allowed for it are therefore public without anybody making a request. Direct negotiation is covered as well. Where a procurement is carried out by direct negotiation rather than open tender, the published information includes the result of opening the quotations and the award result. The route most often used to avoid open competition still produces a published outcome, which is the provision worth knowing when a project appears without any tender having been advertised. Where to look, and what it sits beside. Individual agencies publish their own tender pages carrying the announcement, the tender documents, the bid opening results and the award results as downloadable files with dates, alongside the government printing bureau's published tender notices, and the anti-corruption commission publishes guidelines on public procurement procedure. Read this with the planning condition plan, the property registry and the commercial registration platform entries already recorded for this country: the plan says what may be built, the registry says who holds the ground, the commercial platform says who may sign for the company, and the procurement record says who was paid and how much.

trackers.name: 澳門律師公會 — the register every practising lawyer must be on, the duty list, and the mediation and arbitration centres
trackers.desc: Every practising lawyer and trainee must be registered with the association. Under the lawyers' statute the association is responsible for granting professional qualification to lawyers and trainee lawyers, and all who practise in the territory must be registered with it; its site publishes sections for lawyers, for trainee lawyers and for law firms. That makes the register two things at once: the place a community looks to find counsel, and a one-step check that the person already advising it is entitled to. There is a duty list and an appointment route that does not depend on a fee. The association's own sections include a standby list and appointment ex officio, alongside trainee registration, the adaptation course and the assessment examination. Where a case is unpopular or a household cannot pay, appointment ex officio is the named route rather than an informal favour, and the standby list is where the duty comes from. It runs a mediation centre and an arbitration centre. Both sit under the association itself, which means a dispute with a developer, a contractor or a neighbouring owner has an institutional forum short of litigation, with the association's own rules behind it. The association must be heard on legislation, and it publishes what it says. Any proposal or draft concerning the organisation of the courts, the practice of law, civil procedure or criminal procedure must be put to the association for its opinion, and its site carries sections for legislation, for opinions and for typical cases, with a higher council of the legal profession alongside it. A body with a statutory right to be consulted leaves a published trail of what it argued, and those opinions are citable when a procedural change affects the position of objectors. Read this with the legal aid entry, the administrative complaints route, the planning condition plans and the property registry entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 環保與節能基金 and the municipal activity subsidy — money an association can apply for, and the conditions attached
trackers.desc: An association can apply; a building's owners' assembly cannot, directly. The fund's own published answers state that its recipients are associations and commercial enterprises, and that an owners' assembly is different in nature from an association: where some owners form an association, it must be established that the association can represent the owners' assembly and all the owners, and more material may be required to prove that representativeness. Applicants must bear at least twenty per cent of the cost themselves, and once a grant is approved the same applicant may not apply again for a year. Being, or working through, a properly constituted association is therefore the precondition for reaching this money at all. The route and the window are published. An application is made to the chairman of the fund's administrative committee, on the form supplied by the environmental protection bureau and submitted to that bureau with the required documents; the application period for each scheme is fixed by a secretary's dispatch published in the Official Gazette. The documents include identity papers and, for a legal person, the constitutive act and statutes as published in the Gazette or an updated commercial registration certificate. Watching the Gazette for the window is the same discipline this file has already recorded for tender notices in one country and island lease announcements in another. What it pays for, and the condition that follows the money. The schemes run to buying or replacing environmental and energy-saving products and equipment and scrapping polluting vehicles — equipment and vehicles for the recycling trade, replacement of old motorcycles and old diesel vehicles — so this is equipment money, not campaign money. Published accounts record that recipients were later required to keep funded equipment installed and in use at the specified location for five years or more, with written notice required before any major change and repayment of the grant otherwise. Read the conditions before accepting anything. The second door is the municipal activity subsidy. The municipal affairs body runs an annual subsidy scheme providing financial support to civil organisations holding activities that bring the community together and advance social development, expressly including activities that promote environmental hygiene and spread the spirit, awareness and knowledge of environmental protection. Between the two, an association here has one route to equipment money and another to activity money. Read this with the cultural fund, the planning condition plan, the environmental bureau complaints and the bar association entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The gazette's entity database — every registered association listed by field, and every public body with its founding law
trackers.desc: Associations are listed by field, and environmental protection is one of the fields. The official gazette's entity database, maintained by the legal affairs bureau, indexes private entities by category, so the registered associations working on environmental protection can be listed in one place rather than hunted for. For a group looking for who already exists locally — an association to join, a body to co-sign a submission, an organisation that has done this before — that index is the starting point, and it is a government record rather than a search engine result. Public bodies are indexed the same way, with their founding law. The parallel listing for public administration carries, for each body, its organisational structure, the regulation that created and governs it, its organisational history, its service guide, its recruitment and procurement information, its service pledge, a channel for expressing opinions, its contact details, and the date the record was last updated. Knowing which administrative regulation created a body, and in which year, is the first step in establishing what that body is actually obliged to do — and it is the step most objections skip. Advisory committees appear inside those records. The environmental bureau's entry lists the environmental advisory committee alongside the bureau itself, together with the associations registered in the same field and all the related legislation. An advisory committee is a named body with a named membership, and checking who sits on it before making a submission is cheaper than discovering it afterwards. How to use it, and its limit. The database records registration and structure rather than activity: it tells you who exists, not who is currently working, so an entry should be cross-checked against recent gazette notices and the organisation's own publications before anyone is approached. The maintaining bureau publishes its address, telephone, fax and email. Read this with the planning condition plan comment window, the cultural classification request, the environmental bureau complaints and the association funding entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The legislation index — where the expropriation law sits, and the two rules to read before arguing about money
trackers.desc: The legislation index is where the text lives, and the citation is the point. The printing bureau publishes the gazette and an index of legislation in force, in which laws are identified by number and year and by the gazette series, number and date — the expropriation regime is Law 12/92/M of 17 August 1992, published in Series I number 33, with its regulation in Decree-Law 43/97/M of 20 October 1997. Citing a provision by its gazette number and date is what turns an objection into something an authority has to answer. The first rule: buy before taking. The expropriation law provides in its opening articles that expropriation may only take place after the possibility of acquisition by way of private law has been exhausted. That single sentence gives an owner a threshold question that comes before any argument about value: what offer was made, when, on what terms, and how was it recorded. An expropriation begun without a documented attempt to acquire by agreement is vulnerable at the very start of the process, and the documents proving or disproving that attempt are ones the owner is entitled to see. Compensation is to be just, and contemporaneous. The same general principles guarantee the right to private property and to its transmission during life or on death, and provide that immovable property and the rights inherent in it may be expropriated for reasons of public utility against the contemporaneous payment of a just compensation. Contemporaneous is the operative word: payment is not something that follows possession at a convenient later date. The 1992 law sets the bases; a 1997 decree carries the procedure. The law established the general bases of the institution and left its regulation to complementary legislation, which had to be published before the law could enter into force; that regulation states its own guiding aims as altering the procedural sequence to avoid excessive slowness in these cases and establishing a set of guarantees. Its first title deals with the declaration of public utility and with the authorisation of administrative possession, with the request for a declaration to be addressed to the head of the executive accompanied by specified documents. Administrative possession is the provision to read first, because it is the route by which an authority takes the ground before compensation is settled. What to gather, and in what order. The declaration of public utility and the documents that accompanied the request for it; any record of an offer to purchase by agreement; the basis on which the compensation figure was calculated; and the date of any authorisation of administrative possession. Read this with the property registry entry recording certificates online and a free authenticity checker, the planning condition plan comment window, the bar association register and the legal aid entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 論盡媒體 — an independent outlet whose beat includes land grants, and which budgets for legal costs
trackers.desc: Land and planning are on its published beat. Published profiles record that alongside political news the outlet reports on human rights and freedoms, land, conservation and urban planning, and it has run stories such as a private university's application for a land grant where the responsible bureau announced an intention letter for an education site but did not disclose the location, the area, or the progress of the grant procedure. A resident holding a plot reference and an unanswered question therefore has an outlet that has already asked the same question in print, which is a better starting point than explaining why the question matters. It is funded by donations, and it says what the money is for. Operating since October 2012 and made up of veteran media workers and frontline reporters, it is described as one of the territory's few independent outlets, not relying on government or conglomerate funding and sustained by donations and a small amount of advertising, with a printed monthly, news, features and book publishing alongside the website. Its own appeal states that donations will be used for book publishing, legal consultation and, if needed, litigation costs. An outlet that budgets in public for legal advice and litigation is one that expects to be challenged and has decided in advance to defend what it prints. Its audience crosses the border. Reported figures put roughly seven in ten of its readers locally, one in ten in the neighbouring special administrative region and one in ten further afield. In a jurisdiction this small, a story that also lands outside it is considerably harder to smother than one that circulates only among people who all know each other. The pressures on it are documented. Published accounts record problems including illegal interception of telephones, shortages of funding and staff, increasing online competition, and attacks on its own website during particular periods. Approach it as a small newsroom under pressure: bring documents, dates and a clear chronology rather than a request that it investigate from scratch. Read this with the gazette's entity database, the planning condition plan comment window, the legal aid entry and the bar association register already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 《土地法》 — a grant that breaks the planning rules is void, and a provisional grant lapses if the land is not used in time
trackers.desc: A grant or building works that do not comply with urban planning are void. The land law of 2013 replaced the statute that had run since 1980 and governs applications for land, grants, utilisation, supervision and premium. Published summaries of it record an obligation to comply with urban planning, with a grant or construction works that fail to comply being struck with nullity, and a requirement of public tender for land grants of any type except where the law expressly provides otherwise. Where a project rests on a grant that does not match the plan, or on a grant made without the tender the law requires, the objection goes to the validity of the grant rather than to the merits of the building. A provisional grant lapses if the land is not used in time. The law provides that a provisional grant lapses where the utilisation of the land has not been carried out within the fixed period — unless the failure is not attributable to the grantee and the Chief Executive considers the reasons sufficient — and that on lapse all improvements made on the land revert to the territory, with no right to compensation. It also provides for lapse where the grantee fails to apply for renewal within the period the law sets after the first grant period or a renewal expires, or where the application is refused. The date the utilisation period expires is therefore a fact worth establishing early, because it is the government's own ground for taking the land back. Nine stated principles, three of which are about knowing. The law is built on nine principles: sustainable development, effective and actual use of the land, supervision, public knowledge, equal access to land, protection, the binding force of planning, publicity of the legal situation of land, and legal certainty. The principles of public knowledge and of publicity of the legal situation of land are the ones to quote when asking what the status of a particular plot is: they are the statute's own statement that this information is meant to be available. Temporary occupation licences run for one year, with a narrow renewal window. A temporary occupation licence lasts a year and lapses on expiry if renewal is not applied for during the period from sixty to thirty days before it ends, the application going to the lands bureau addressed to the Chief Executive with the identification of the licence holder and of the land. Where a site near a community is held under such a licence, that thirty-day window is when its continuation is decided. Read this with the planning condition plans, the property registry certificates, the audit office's public works reports and the independent outlet entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Keeping a classified building — property tax exemption for owners who maintain it, and the repair subsidy and interest-free loan scheme
trackers.desc: An owner who maintains a classified building stops paying property tax on it. The cultural heritage legislation sets out tax benefits which, by their own terms, cover both classified immovable property and property lying inside its buffer zone. Classified immovable property which has undergone conservation, repair or restoration works and is in a good state of preservation is exempt from urban property tax; only works carried out in accordance with the law count towards it. The exemption is confirmed by the director of the finance bureau on the application of the interested party, accompanied by a document from the cultural affairs bureau certifying the state of preservation of the property together with other supporting evidence — and it must be applied for again each year. Where the argument for demolition is that an old building costs its owner money, this is the counter-offer the law already makes. Buffer zone properties are inside the benefit. The benefits section covers property in the buffer zone as well as the classified property itself, so a neighbour who is not the owner of the monument may still be within the scheme. That is worth checking parcel by parcel before assuming a neighbouring owner has no interest in the classification. There is money for the repairs themselves. A separate scheme provides owners of units in buildings held under the condominium regime with either a financial subsidy or an interest-free repayable loan, apportioned according to the value of each unit, to meet the cost of maintenance, repair or renewal works on the common parts of the building. For a block whose residents are being told that redevelopment is the only way to deal with its condition, the subsidy and the loan are the alternative that has to be priced against it; the scheme's regulation has been amended by chief executive order, so check the current version. What is classified, and how much of it. Official material records 165 classified immovables across the territory following the successive classification batches — 71 monuments, 55 buildings of architectural interest, 14 architectural ensembles and 25 sites — with sites including hills, squares and parks, and buffer zones drawn where necessary to protect the setting. Read this with the classification request route open to any resident, the cultural development fund, the property registry certificates and the land law entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 澳門土木工程實驗室 LECM — an independent laboratory that tests materials, monitors noise and dust, and assesses whether a building is actually unsafe
trackers.desc: An autonomous laboratory, not a government department. The civil engineering laboratory is a non-profit technical and scientific public-interest legal person with autonomy in technical, budgetary and property matters, established in 1988 to provide technical and testing services across the fields of civil engineering, and it states that it provides technical support both to government and to public and private civil engineering companies. That independence is the point for a community: the same body that certifies materials for public works can be commissioned to look at a structure or a nuisance, and its findings are not the developer's. It monitors noise and dust, alongside the materials testing. The materials testing centre provides testing of engineering materials for public and private works — concrete, cement, aggregates, reinforcing and prestressing steel, structural steel, geotextiles, drain and manhole covers, aluminium, coatings and others, for physical and mechanical properties — and, in the same list, outdoor environmental monitoring services such as noise and dust. For a neighbourhood living beside a demolition or a piling site, noise and dust monitoring by a body of this standing is the measurement that an authority cannot easily set aside. It assesses buildings and structures, including whether they are sound. The buildings and structures inspection centre provides structural and durability condition assessment: corrosion determined by visual inspection and verified by ultrasonic thickness measurement, weld inspection using magnetic particle and ultrasonic testing and, more recently, eddy current testing that can find surface fatigue cracks in existing joints without stripping the coating, and evaluation of load-bearing capacity. The laboratory has also carried out monitoring of dangerous buildings, bridges and the airport. Where redevelopment is justified by an assertion that a building is beyond saving, an independent condition assessment is the document that tests the assertion. It also wrote the documents that price the work. At the public works bureau's commission the laboratory prepared three documents on project budgeting and quality — a general technical specification, a guideline on measurement methods and a guideline on preparing bills of quantities — in Chinese, Portuguese and English, with the stated purpose of making tender pricing fairer and avoiding disputes over final costs. Those are useful reading when a public project's costs are the argument. Read this with the environmental protection bureau complaints entry, the planning condition plans, the audit office's value-for-money work and the heritage upkeep and repair funding entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 個人資料保護局 — where to complain when your identity data is collected or disclosed, with published case decisions
trackers.desc: There is a dedicated authority for personal data, and it takes complaints. The personal data protection bureau was established by administrative regulation in 2023 and is the public body performing the functions laid down by the personal data protection legislation of 2005. Its own material records that complaints and enquiries can be submitted through its website. For someone in a land or development dispute, this is the address for a specific and common problem: the collection, retention or passing on of identity information by a private company, a management body or an official process, including the details of people who signed a petition, attended a meeting or filed a complaint. It publishes what it decided, which tells you what it will act on. The bureau publishes case abstracts. One records a complaint that security guards at a property required visitors to enter personal details on a form and retained the original of their resident identity card until they left; the bureau found the retention practice potentially contrary to the identity card legislation and a decree, notified the competent department, and the company stopped the practice. It also analysed the visitor register itself as personal data processing under the Act, identifying the company as the controller with decision-making power over the purpose and means. Reading the abstracts before complaining shows the form an admissible complaint takes. Why this belongs in a land dispute. Development and management companies routinely collect identity data at gates, meetings and site entrances, and complaint procedures generate lists of names. Where those records circulate beyond their purpose, the data legislation is the instrument that addresses it, and it applies to private controllers, not only to government. A complaint here is narrow, documentary and independent of the merits of the development dispute — which is precisely why it can succeed while the larger argument is still running. Keep the evidence in the form the bureau needs. What was collected, by whom, on what form, for what stated purpose, and what happened to it afterwards; a photograph of the form and a note of the date will usually matter more than a description of how it felt. Read this with the administrative complaints ombudsman, the planning condition plans, the legal aid entry and the environmental complaints entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 裁判書搜尋 — judgment search by court including the Administrative Court, with summaries, unified interpretations and annual-report cases
trackers.desc: The courts publish judgments court by court, including the Administrative Court.
