The judiciary's site carries a judgments section split by court — Court of Final Appeal, Court of Second Instance, Court of First Instance and the Administrative Court — together with a judgment search page, a latest judgments listing, judgment summaries, unified judicial interpretations, analyses of typical cases and a page of important judgments carried in the annual reports. For a community challenging a licence, a land grant or an administrative act, the Administrative Court section is the one that matters, and it is published in its own right rather than buried in a general index. Summaries and typical-case analyses do the filtering for you. Beside the full judgments the site publishes judgment summaries and analyses of representative cases, and the important-judgments page lists decisions with a one-line statement of what each decided — among the examples listed, an administrative court decision rejecting compensation claims brought by several hundred pre-sale purchasers of a development against the territory, and a second-instance decision refusing to suspend the effects of an administrative act done to execute a final judicial decision. Reading those one-line statements is the quickest way to find the line of cases that matches a dispute. Unified judicial interpretation is the strongest authority. The site publishes the court's unified judicial interpretations separately; the final appeal court exercises that jurisdiction with the participation of the president and senior judges of the second instance court, which is why those rulings settle a point across later cases. Where one exists on the question in a dispute, it is the first thing to cite. The site also carries the procedural furniture. Case distribution results and scheduling for each court, electronic court notices searchable by date and case number, judicial sales, and annual case statistics by court and year. The site states that its content is for reference and that the court's own notification prevails. Read this with the land law entry, the planning condition plans, the administrative complaints ombudsman and the heritage upkeep entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 澳門基金會資助 — the standing grant route for associations, with one submission window a year and an online account to open first
trackers.desc: The territory's foundation runs a standing sponsorship programme, and the government portal sets out how to apply. The service description records that applications are made during the designated application period for each year's special sponsorship plans, submitted through the foundation's online sponsorship application platform in either official language and then delivered in person to the foundation with all application documents within the same period. Each year's plan accepts a single submission of the application form and related material, including anything that assists assessment — so there is no second attempt in the same cycle if documents are missing. Open the platform account before the window opens. The same description records that an applicant who has not previously opened an account on the online platform, or whose account needs updating, should first submit an account application form with the required documents; the foundation sends an activation link to the registered email of a first-time applicant, or restores access to an existing account, within five working days. That five-day step is the one that causes a missed deadline, and it is avoidable. The rules are published, and they are the criteria. The sponsorship regulation was approved by a numbered chief executive dispatch of 2022 and published in the official gazette; the public finance sponsorship regime is set by a 2022 administrative regulation, and the foundation's own statute was amended by another that year. Read the regulation before writing: a grant refused for a reason stated in it is a refusal that could have been anticipated. Where this fits for a community. This is money for activities and projects run by associations rather than for buying land, so the realistic use is the work around a land dispute — documentation, community surveys, heritage recording, public education — carried out by an association that can hold the grant. Read this with the heritage classification and repair funding, the data protection bureau, the administrative complaints ombudsman and the judgment search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Free legal enquiry from the legal affairs bureau, and the bar association's annual free consultation day
trackers.desc: There is a free legal enquiry service, and it is deliberately remote. The government portal's service description records a legal enquiry service run by the legal affairs bureau's legal promotion and public relations department, reachable by telephone, by leaving a message on its website, by email or by letter. It states expressly that the service is not provided in person: residents make enquiries through those channels and staff reply within office hours, which the description sets out day by day. For someone who cannot take time off to queue, that is the point — but it also means the answer will be general information about the law rather than advice on a file. Use it to establish what the law says before paying anyone. A written enquiry by email or letter produces a written reply, which is worth more than a conversation when a community is trying to establish the rule that governs a plan, a licence condition or a heritage classification. Keep the reply. The bar association runs a free consultation day. The lawyers' association publishes an annual free legal consultation attached to its lawyers' day, with pages for successive years on its own site — the practical opportunity to put a real problem to a practising lawyer at no cost. It also maintains listings of law offices, which is how a community identifies practitioners once it knows what kind of case it has. What the association is, and why that matters. Founded in 1991 and representing over four hundred lawyers, it is both a public law body and a free and autonomous association; it confers professional qualification on lawyers and trainees under the lawyers' statute, all of whom must register with it, and its opinion must be heard on any proposal or draft concerning judicial organisation, the practice of law, or civil and criminal procedure. It also operates arbitration and mediation centres. A community with a systemic complaint about access to justice has a body with standing to raise it. Read this with the legal aid entry, the lawyers' register, the data protection bureau and the judgment search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The environmental assessment information platform and the project-category list — plus the framework law duty to attach an environmental study
trackers.desc: There is a published list of the project categories that require an environmental impact assessment, and it was revised. The environmental protection bureau runs an environmental impact assessment information platform, describing assessment as one of the tools by which environmental considerations are brought into urban planning and project development before they proceed. Government announcements record that the bureau issued a trial list of project categories requiring assessment in 2013, updated it in 2017, and completed a further revision after reviewing practical operation and reference to national and neighbouring practice and to the views of government departments, bodies and the industry, the revised list applying from 1 January 2025 and published on the platform. For a community facing a specific project, the first question is whether it falls inside a listed category — a checkable question against a published document. The framework law states the duty in general terms, which matters where the list is silent. The environmental framework law provides that plans, programmes, works and acts which may affect the environment and citizens' health and quality of life — whether the responsibility of administrative bodies or of public or private entities, and whether required or undertaken on their own initiative — should be accompanied by a study of environmental impact. It also lists, among the state's tasks, prior assessment of the effects of works and infrastructure that may affect the environment and the landscape and of the introduction of new technological activities and products; prior licensing of all potentially or actually polluting activities; reduction or suspension of activities that do not comply with control rules; and territorial planning including the classification and creation of areas, places or protected landscapes under special reservation regimes. Those are the words to quote where a project is not on the list but plainly affects health or quality of life. Assessment is also done at plan level, and those documents are published. Planning material for a major reclamation district publishes a plan-level environmental assessment setting out the assessment scope for each environmental element — for example the whole planning area extended a stated distance beyond its boundary for air, and a shorter stated distance for noise with particular attention to a band along the roads — and aligns the assessment period with the territory's overall urban plan. Where a district plan is the thing being fought, ask for the plan-level assessment and check what distance beyond the boundary it treated as affected. The bureau publishes an annual state of the environment report in Chinese and Portuguese, with an English version following, which is where monitoring figures for air, coastal water quality and waste come from. Read this with the legal aid entry, the free legal enquiry service, the data protection bureau and the judgment search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 規劃條件圖 draft consultations — every draft is posted for comment on a fixed form, with a newsletter that tells you when
trackers.desc: Every planning condition plan draft must be posted for public comment, and batches are published with dates. Government announcements record that under the planning law's implementing regulation each planning condition plan draft, once prepared, must be posted for public display and comment; that batches of drafts — six in one announcement, twelve in another — are uploaded to the urban planning information website for the display period; that comments are made on a numbered form downloadable from that site or the works department's site and submitted by email, fax, post to a stated address, or in person; and that the drafts are also deposited at the urban planning department's floor at that address for inspection. Each announcement gives an opening and closing date roughly a fortnight apart, so this is a short window that recurs. You can be told when a window opens. The same announcements record that the public may subscribe to the works department's electronic newsletter to learn which planning condition plans are currently collecting comments. Subscribing is the cheapest possible early warning system for a neighbourhood. What the document actually fixes. The information website records that for areas without a detailed plan the works department issues the planning condition plan on its own initiative, and that its main object is to set the development indicators for the plot — building height, plot ratio and site coverage among them — which are generally the upper limits permitted at planning level, with the final buildable conditions also shaped by the plot's own conditions, the development use, street width and shadow, fire safety and the urban construction regulations, so the maximum indicators may not be reached. Read the indicators as ceilings, and ask which other constraints bind below them. Plans are made in two tiers, with consultation built into drafting. Published legal commentary records that the master plan sets the overall spatial planning, zoning, infrastructure deployment, general land use conditions and guidelines on protecting the environment, nature and ecological balance, and provides for detailed plans; that a detailed plan sets planning, land use conditions, infrastructure layout, construction conditions and urban design guidelines for each part of the city; that preparation of a draft is decided by an order published in the official gazette stating the purposes the plan is to achieve; and that while preparing a draft the works department must promote and display it and explain its content to the public in order to hear opinions through public consultation. A statutory advisory urban planning committee gives opinions in the preparation, implementation, review and amendment of plans and in the issue of planning condition plans. Read this with the assessment category list, the free legal enquiry service, the legal aid entry and the judgment search entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 《古樹名木保護名錄》 — the protected old-tree list, the four criteria for getting on it, and the one-tree-one-record inspection regime
trackers.desc: There is a published list of protected trees, and it is maintained by the municipal body. The municipal affairs bureau's nature site carries the list of protected old and famous trees alongside its classification of the territory's green areas and the mechanisms that safeguard them. Government reporting records that the list was published in 2016 to conserve trees of historical, cultural and commemorative significance; that the bureau, as the department responsible for tending and conserving trees, monitors and manages them; and that a dedicated old-tree webpage was added in 2020 so residents could learn about the trees, take part in their conservation and inherit their historical, cultural and ecological value. Check whether a tree on a threatened site is already on the list before anything else. The criteria are four, and age is only one of them. Government reporting records that a protected tree here means one over a hundred years old, of precious species, of unusual form, rare, or of special historical or cultural significance, that has been included in the list; and one published account describes a tree not yet thirty years old that is on the list, precisely because age is not the only route. A young tree with a local story is therefore a candidate. The list is updated, and private trees can be added. Reporting records that the list is assessed, drawn up and updated by the public departments with competence to maintain trees, with an updating procedure each year where a listed tree dies and must be removed or a newly found tree meets the definition; that the first update after 2016 brought the total to five hundred and twenty, including the first four privately owned old trees, two of them over four hundred and ninety years old, all four inside a temple; and that the municipal bureau and the cultural bureau planned to add more than sixty further trees located in religious and cultural heritage protection zones. Nominating a private tree is a documented route, not a theoretical one. What listing actually buys. Reporting records that the bureau conducts at least one routine inspection a year and keeps a one-tree-one-record system, and publishes tree data with pamphlets, videos and maintenance guidelines. It also records why forty-two trees were struck off between the two lists — twenty-two felled by named typhoons, fourteen killed by brown root rot, four by root rot, one from continuing decline and one illegally felled. Read this with the cultural classification request, the environmental protection bureau, the planning condition plan consultations and the heritage building entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 《預防和控制環境噪音》 — no piling on Sundays and public holidays, an eighty-five decibel piling limit, the two-hundred-metre rule near homes and hospitals, and the binding opinion before a piling permit
trackers.desc: The environment bureau's opinion on the works method is binding before a piling permit issues. The 2014 noise law, published in the gazette, provides that before issuing a works permit involving piling, the public works bureau shall require the environmental protection bureau to give a binding opinion on the construction plan. Where piling is proposed beside homes, that opinion is a document with real weight, and the bureau that gives it is the one to write to. Two hundred metres from a home or hospital, machinery is barred outside working hours. The law provides that on Sundays and public holidays all day, and on weekdays from eight in the evening to eight the next morning, mobile or fixed mechanical equipment may not be used for civil construction work within two hundred metres of residential buildings or hospitals. Government announcements record further that no piling at all may be carried out during those periods, that piling must not exceed a twenty-minute equivalent continuous sound level of eighty-five decibels, and that highly polluting impact diesel, pneumatic and steam pile hammers are banned outright. Measure the distance and check the hours before anything else. Seven categories of noise are regulated, and alteration works in homes are among them. Announcements record the law covering civil construction works and equipment; alteration, maintenance and repair works in residential buildings — restricted on Sundays and public holidays all day and on weekdays from seven in the evening to nine the next morning; daily activities and pets in residential buildings; activities in public places; performances and entertainment; air conditioning and ventilation equipment; and activities in industrial, commercial or service premises, where the noise level must not exceed the background level by more than ten decibels. Who enforces, and what the exceptions are. The law provides that the environmental protection bureau monitors compliance with the named articles, the public security police monitors two others, and bureau staff exercise public authority powers and may require assistance from other public entities; and that the restrictions do not apply to urgent and unpostponable repairs to public networks, to special techniques permitted by the chief executive's dispatch where geological conditions allow only continuous work, or to exceptional cases of major public interest so permitted. Ask which exception is being relied on. Read this with the environmental protection bureau entry, the planning condition plan consultations, the assessment platform and the old tree register entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 路氹城生態保護區 — the fifty-five hectare wetland reserve, its two management zones, the species counts the agency publishes, and the public visit that anyone can register for
trackers.desc: There is a gazetted wetland reserve here, and its two zones carry different access rules. The environmental protection bureau records that the ecological reserve near the bridge covers about fifty-five hectares and consists of ecological zone one, a limited-access managed area, and ecological zone two, an open managed area. Government material records zone one holding four bird-watching platforms and two bird hides connected by a nature study trail, with rare plants planted beside it, and zone two covering tidal flats on the western dyke with artificial islets and named mangrove species. Where reclamation or works are proposed on that coast, the reserve's boundary and zoning are the first facts. The species counts are published and dated, which makes them citable. Government material records the reserve's recorded biodiversity at stated dates — plankton algae, higher plants, zooplankton, benthic animals, insects, fish, amphibians, reptiles and mammals each counted by species — and records that its food resources attract more than a hundred and seventy bird species to feed and roost, with sixty-odd migratory species wintering there between October and April, including the globally rare black-faced spoonbill and the spoonbill that sometimes accompanies it. Later material records the counts rising to hundreds of plant and animal species and close to two hundred bird species. A community arguing for a wetland has a published inventory to point at. The agency's own works and interventions are on the record. Government news records the bureau completing works to enlarge the tidal flats and water body of the reserve, and clearing unregistered vessel activity that was disturbing it through inter-departmental cooperation, both aimed at improving conditions for birds. That is a precedent for asking that a disturbance be removed rather than merely noted. Access is by registration, and the route is published. The bureau records monthly public viewing days and wetland bird-watching walks during the migratory season, with places limited, registration by hotline or web page, guided entry into both the limited-access zone one and the open zone two, and binoculars provided; the government services portal lists the application for visiting the ecological zone and environmental infrastructure, requiring only a name and local mobile number. Read this with the noise law, the environmental protection bureau entry, the assessment platform and the old tree register entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 《海域管理綱要法》 — the marine functional zoning that sea use must follow, the duty to create marine nature reserves and a monitoring network, and the fifty-day public consultation on all three instruments
trackers.desc: Sea use here has to follow a functional zoning, and the zoning's objectives are written into the framework law. The 2018 marine area management framework legislation, published in the gazette, provides that the marine functional zoning shall scientifically determine the functions of sea areas according to their location, natural resources, environmental conditions and the requirements of development and use; coordinate sea use according to economic and social development needs; ensure coordination with the estuary's management planning so that flood discharge and water supply are safeguarded; and protect and improve the marine ecological environment to ensure sustainable development of the sea area; and that the government may approve use of sea areas by concession, licence or other means, under a dedicated statute. Establishing which functional zone a project sits in comes before arguing about its permit. The law obliges the government to create marine nature reserves and a monitoring network. The same law lists among the government's duties drawing up emergency and prevention plans for major marine pollution incidents; establishing marine nature reserves according to the needs of protecting the sea area's ecology, with effective protection and management measures; building a marine ecological monitoring network and establishing a notification mechanism with neighbouring regions; and promoting regional cooperation on marine environmental protection, disaster prevention and incident response. Those are duties a community can ask whether the government has discharged. All three implementing instruments went out for a fifty-day public consultation. The government portal records that the marine functional zoning, the sea area plan and the sea use law were put out for public consultation from 29 December 2023 to 16 February 2024, with consultation texts published, public sessions held and a named email address for associations and sector bodies to register. Press material records the consultation as fifty days and records the sea area plan as covering liveable city construction, ecological protection and pollution prevention, marine disaster prevention and mitigation, marine tourism, sports, culture and regional cooperation, coordinated with the city master plan. Civil society used that window, and its submission is public. A local association's published submission records that the central government assigned the eighty-five square kilometre sea area in December 2015, that the framework law of 2018 required management to follow the functional zoning and the sea area plan, and that the government delayed until this consultation to bring those instruments forward, urging that public views be seriously collected. Read this with the ecological reserve, the assessment platform, the urban planning consultation and the noise law entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 澳門空氣質量監測統計年度報告 — a yearly statistical report per station going back years, the standard each pollutant is judged against, and the station move recorded to the day
trackers.desc: There is an annual statistical report on air quality, published year after year on the same path. The meteorological bureau publishes the air quality monitoring statistical annual report as a numbered yearly document, with editions available for successive years; each carries the same sections — the year's index overview, the distribution of days by air quality level, the distribution of days by level at each station across the years, and the situation of each main pollutant at the different stations — with appendices describing the automatic monitoring network, a map of station locations and the definition of the index. A community wanting to know whether the air near it has worsened has a per-station, multi-year series to read rather than a snapshot. What each level means is tied to a named standard. The reports record the index as calculated from hourly automatic station data, converting each pollutant to a sub-index and taking the highest as the station's hourly index, with the main pollutant named whenever the index exceeds one hundred; record the level thresholds as referenced to the strictest air quality guideline values of the world health body, with interim target values used for particulates and sulphur dioxide and for ozone, and to the territory's own air quality standard in force since 2021; and record that a level of 'moderate' already means some pollutant concentrations exceed the strictest guideline, while 'unhealthy' or above means concentrations exceed the territory's own reference values. That distinction is what a resident needs when told the air is merely moderate. A station move is recorded to the day, which is what makes the series usable. The report records one station relocated in September 2022, moved about one hundred metres north-west from a building roof to an observation field, with particulate monitoring transferred on one stated date and the gas monitoring on another. Comparisons across that break have to account for it. The daily service is separately listed. The government services portal records the twenty-four hour automatic network monitoring air quality and publishing the index with suggested precautions and a forecast index for the same or next day, over six named pollutants. Read this with the noise law, the ecological reserve, the environmental protection bureau and the assessment platform entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: 政策諮詢列表 — every public policy consultation listed in one place, governed by a 2011 executive order, with the summary report published after each
trackers.desc: Public policy consultation is regulated, and every one is listed on a single government page. The government portal carries a policy consultation list with filters, and records that since 16 August 2011 the consultation of public policies has been governed by a numbered chief executive order. Rather than watching each bureau, a community can watch that list — the numbered consultation pages carry the consultation text, the closing date, the sessions held and the department's later summary report. The individual consultation pages show the mechanics. One consultation's page records the instruction to mark the cover or opening of any submission with a stated wording, invites comments through the opinion form annexed to the consultation text, and records that a respondent wishing their opinion or suggestion kept confidential should clearly indicate that; it carries the dated announcements of the consultation opening, a public session, a reminder before closing, the close, and finally the department publishing the consultation summary report. Another records the government preparing a consultation text and inviting all sectors of society to give opinions and suggestions during the consultation period. The summary reports carry counts, and they can be checked. Reporting of one recent consultation records the summary report giving 1,716 submissions containing 8,230 opinions, with a stated proportion positive, and records fourteen consultation sessions held over a stated period, three of them public sessions, plus submissions by legislators, associations, and members of the public through the government account application, telephone messages, online messages and email. An earlier summary report on procurement legislation sets out question-by-question distributions of responses, including how many answered that they could not judge. Those numbers are what let a community argue that a consultation was thin. A separate route exists for opinions outside a consultation. A 2026 administrative regulation defines an opinion as a question, reflection or demand about public service information, process, effectiveness or the management of related public affairs, including consultations, complaints, suggestions, non-urgent requests for help and reports of suspected administrative illegality, requires bodies to provide diverse and convenient channels and to handle opinions actively, transparently and efficiently, requires an interim reply where handling exceeds the notified period, and requires the result to be replied to the person. Read this with the planning condition plan consultations, the environmental assessment platform, the complaints entry and the association grant entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The neighbourhood associations union — twenty-eight ground-level associations and four district offices, links to more than fifty building owners' committees, and its members on government advisory committees
trackers.desc: There is a federated body of neighbourhood associations, and its structure is published. Published description records the union as formally established in 1983 as a non-profit social service body leading the territory's district neighbourhood associations and their affiliated bodies, with its aims including uniting residents, participating in society, paying attention to people's livelihood, serving the community and building a harmonious community. It records the union as having grown to four district offices, twenty-eight ground-level neighbourhood associations and more than thirty affiliated service bodies, in close contact with more than fifty building owners' committees and community organisations. For a resident whose building or street faces a project, that is an existing structure with a body at street level and a committee in the building. It has seats on government committees, including environmental ones. Published material records the union sending representatives to sit as members of government advisory committees covering environmental protection, medical, education, transport and social work matters, working to maintain and fight for residents' reasonable rights and interests, and records it as conveying residents' demands to the government before each annual policy address. The official entity register records the union appearing in successive executive orders appointing members to named consultative committees, including a statistics advisory committee, a fisheries advisory committee, and social work, education, youth, elderly, and women and children's committees. A seat already held is a route a community can ask to use. Its own structure and its published casework are on record. Published description records eleven working committees under a secretariat, including a grassroots committee, a social affairs committee, a buildings work committee and a community economic affairs committee; and records community centres operated with the social welfare service. It records the union publishing an annual community casework volume since 2009 providing front-line workers a platform to share experience, one edition carrying twenty-six articles across themes including developing diversified services, advancing policies benefiting residents, and community research on livelihood. A directory gives its address and telephone number. Read this with the consultation list, the complaints entry, the association grants and the entity register entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Grants for running an association here — the foundation's operating-cost scheme with its stated eligibility, and the municipal activity scheme that funds community events including environmental ones
trackers.desc: An association's running costs can be funded, not only its projects. A public foundation's published scheme records support for part of the basic operating costs of local non-profit associations that are long-term and properly run, of good social reputation, and with a complete working team, to safeguard those associations' normal operation and service quality. It records the scheme as made under a named foundation charter, a public financial assistance system regulation and a subsidy regulation, all cited by number; records the funding as for locally and lawfully established non-profit associations carrying out services that help the territory's social development; and records the limit as one application per applicant, with rules for affiliated bodies applying through a parent association. Core costs are what usually kill a small association, and this is the scheme aimed at them. The municipal activity scheme funds events, and names environmental protection among its purposes. A municipal body's published scheme records financial assistance to encourage and assist civil organisations to hold distinctive activities, uniting the community, promoting social progress and enriching residents' leisure life, and names among its aims promoting environmental hygiene and spreading the spirit, awareness and knowledge of keeping the environment clean and of environmental protection. That is a public route to pay for a community's own environmental event. The environmental fund's own boundaries are published, and they exclude some obvious applicants. The environmental fund records that its applicants must be associations or commercial enterprises, that ordinary families or individuals are not covered, and that its subsidy is for physical products with environmental benefit — not services, promotion or market activities, and not installation works, maintenance or repair. It records grants of up to eighty per cent of the total cost of the products or equipment purchased or replaced, capped at five hundred thousand patacas, with no further application for one year from the date of approval; and records that a building owners' committee differs in nature from an association, so any association formed by owners must establish that it can represent the committee and all owners, the applicant bearing at least twenty per cent of the cost. Read this with the neighbourhood associations union, the assessment pages, the consultation list and the water testing entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The ecological reserve and its species counts — a 55-hectare protected wetland with published bird, plant and fish totals, public viewing days, and an application route for group visits and study
trackers.desc: The territory's ecological reserve is described with counts, which is what makes it usable as a reference point. The environmental bureau records the reserve near a named bridge as covering 55 hectares in total, made up of a first ecological zone of about 15 hectares open only in a limited way and a second zone of 40 hectares open to the public on the western shore of a reclaimed area. It records the reserve's biodiversity as 162 bird species, 306 higher plants, 35 fish species, 42 molluscs, more than 13 crustaceans and 310 insects. Where a plan claims reclaimed land holds little life, a state-published species count on reclaimed ground is the contradiction. The facilities are listed, which tells a group what can actually be done there. The bureau records four bird-watching platforms built around the first zone, two bird-watching huts on its southern dyke, and a nature study trail along that dyke planted with about 120 characteristic plant species chosen for teaching needs, and records itself as having worked since its establishment to conserve the reserve's animal and plant resources and improve those birdwatching facilities. Access is by application, and the service is published as a numbered procedure. The government portal carries a numbered service for applications to visit the ecological reserve and environmental infrastructure facilities, with registration for reserve activities available to individuals, and records practical instructions including bringing a reusable bag to carry away work and pressed-plant specimens from a parent-child nature workshop, alongside the bureau's own street address and its accessibility facilities. The bureau's public pages record it running public viewing days at the ecological reserve and a fish-knowledge workshop, with guided visits led by interpreters. For a community organising a school or resident visit to a site it wants protected, that is the existing model — a numbered application, a guide, and a published species list to point at. Read this with the assessment pages, the water quality reports, the neighbourhood associations union and the association grant entries already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Greenland — Revisionsudvalget (Inatsisartut Audit Committee)
trackers.desc: National public-finance watchdog; the Inatsisartut Audit Committee (§§18–19) oversees the financial, legal-critical & performance audit of the Landskasse (Treasury) accounts — audit work performed by the appointed Landskasserevisor — and reports to Parliament on their approval, Greenland.

trackers.name: Greenland — Ministry of Finance (Naalakkersuisut)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Government of Greenland’s Ministry of Finance is responsible for the budget, tax policy, the Danish block grant, structural policy & Statistics Greenland, Greenland. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Greenland.

trackers.name: Court of Greenland
trackers.desc: Court of Greenland — tribunal in Greenland (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Two publication regimes — Greenlandic law is on lovgivning.gl
trackers.desc: IDENTIFY WHICH SYSTEM YOUR RULE BELONGS TO BEFORE CITING IT. Under the Act on Greenland Self-Government (Act no. 473 of 12 June 2009), legislative power lies with Inatsisartut, executive power with Naalakkersuisut and judicial power with the courts. The Self-Government authorities' own legal precepts enter into force at the beginning of the day following the day they are made public on www.lovgivning.gl, and each entry must state the day of entry — so that is where you check whether a Greenlandic rule is in force. Realm legislation applying to Greenland is promulgated separately in the Danish Law Gazette, and that promulgation is a precondition for entry into force of administrative orders for Greenland. Two publication regimes run in parallel, and a rule from one will not be found in the other. THE MINERAL POSITION SHAPES MOST LAND DISPUTES HERE: in November 2009 the Self-Government authorities decided to take over the mineral resource area from 1 January 2010, assuming the right to utilise the mineral resources found in the subsoil, with revenues accruing to the Self-Government. So minerals are a Greenlandic competence, not a Danish one — address Naalakkersuisut, and note that the revenue interest sits with the same authority that regulates. The Act records the people of Greenland as a people pursuant to international law with the right of self-determination, Denmark and Greenland being equal partners.

trackers.name: Fredning — read the specific order, because they differ enormously
trackers.desc: TWO ORDERS, TWO COMPLETELY DIFFERENT REGIMES — which is why the general law tells you little. At Lyngmarken, Greenland's oldest natural-history fredning (protected 1954, extended 1979 and 1986) around Arktisk Station, the designation was made for the benefit of scientific investigation and expressly does not restrict the population's right to use the area — the model to cite where a community fears exclusion. At Paradisdalen (Arnangarnuup Qoorua), fredet 1984, all animal and plant life is protected year-round and movement is permitted on foot only. Read the specific bekendtgørelse. Protection rests on Landstingslov nr. 29 af 18. december 2003 om Naturbeskyttelse, with management divided between several departments covering fredning, living resources, råstoffer and genetic resources — establish which holds your issue. A SINGLE COLONY OR HAULING-OUT SITE IS A RECOGNISED UNIT: fredning covers specific localities important for particular species, including bird protection areas, seabird colonies and walrus hauling-out sites — a smaller and more attainable ask than an area designation. SCALE: 12 areas fredet under the Act, 13 bird protection areas regulated in the breeding period, 6 larger area protections, and 11 Ramsar sites; the National Park in North and East Greenland is about 43 percent of Greenland's total area — the world's largest protected area — a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve since 1977. ONE CATEGORY IS NOT PROTECTION: the ‘vigtige områder for dyrelivet’ in the mineral field rules exist to make companies exercise particular regard, and are expressly not protected areas in the proper sense — if a company cites field-rule status, that is not a designation.

trackers.name: Nordic Council of Ministers — Greenland counts toward the three
trackers.desc: YOU COUNT AS A FULL ENTITY, NOT A JUNIOR PARTNER — that is the whole point of this entry. The Nordic Council of Ministers requires that at least three of the following must be involved: Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Iceland, Finland, the Faroe Islands, Greenland, or Åland. The Faroe Islands, Greenland and Åland count toward the three alongside the five states, so a project involving only those three autonomous territories satisfies the requirement without any larger country. The central criterion is that projects provide added value to the Nordic countries, the Faroe Islands, Greenland, and Åland — the three are named again in the added-value test, so the benefit need not accrue to the states. ASK WHICH ROUTE APPLIES BEFORE PREPARING ANYTHING: the Council issues direct calls on particular topics from time to time, but the majority of projects are run by an ‘administrative body’, usually a national agency in the Nordic Region, commissioned by the Council — so most of the money is not distributed by the Council itself. The environment and climate working groups fund Nordic projects as a second layer within the same structure. A GREENLANDIC PRECEDENT WORTH KNOWING FOR ITS OWN SAKE: PISUNA-net, a local observations database built to record, archive and share community observations, won the Nordic Council Environment Prize in 2018 for participatory monitoring protecting marine life. Where a community has observers rather than scientists and needs an evidence base, that is a precedent with a prize attached.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Faroese Parliamentary Ombudsman
trackers.desc: The Faroe Islands’ Parliamentary Ombudsman, investigating complaints against public administration.

trackers.name: Faroe Islands — Landsgrann­ skoðanin (National Audit)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution; Landsgrannskoðanin is the independent audit body under the Løgting (per Audit Act no. 25 of 21 April 1999) that audits the national accounts and publishes annual reports & appropriation-oversight findings, Faroe Islands.

trackers.name: Faroe Islands — Ministry of Finance (Fíggjarmálaráðið)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Ministry of Finance coordinates the Faroese government’s budgetary, financial & economic matters, underpins taxation & fees legislation and oversees public-sector finances, Faroe Islands. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Faroe Islands.

trackers.name: Faroe Islands — Skráseting Føroya (Company Registration Authority)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the Faroese Company Registration Authority registers & maintains records of companies & associations (and the national ship register), Faroe Islands. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Faroe Islands District Court
trackers.desc: Faroe Islands District Court — first instance court in Faroe Islands (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Jurisdiction is Faroese — and the conservation act dates from 1970
trackers.desc: DO NOT ADDRESS A DANISH MINISTRY. Under the Home Rule Act, environment and nature management are Faroese jurisdictions — the islands are responsible for the legislation protecting nature and regulating harmful activities, and the Løgting legislates on environmental matters. THE THREE INSTRUMENTS: the Act on Nature Conservation, 1970, which protects areas of natural beauty, wildlife and habitats and regulates the creation and management of protected areas such as national parks and nature reserves; the Act on Environmental Protection, 1988, on pollution of air, water and soil and vibrations; and the Act on the Protection of the Marine Environment, 2005. NOTE THE 1970 DATE: the conservation act predates the rapid development the islands have seen since the 1960s in infrastructure, energy consumption and tourism — a half-century-old designation statute is worth reading closely for what it does not anticipate. WHAT IS ALREADY PROTECTED: important bird areas as Ramsar sites, including Skúvoy, Nólsoy and Mykines. Over 300 bird species recorded, 50 breeding regularly, with endemic subspecies including the Faroe eider — and the Faroe charr, an endemic fish known only from Lake Leynavatn. A single-lake endemic is the strongest possible site-specific argument. PRESSURES IN THE BAYS: transportation, sand extraction and aquaculture, alongside 70,000 sheep on semi-natural pasture.

trackers.name: The tourism law puts environment first — in those words
trackers.desc: A STATUTORY PRIORITY ORDERING, STATED IN TERMS. The Løgting's law on sustainable tourism is explained by the Ministry's senior adviser as follows: ‘The aim is to achieve environmental, social, and economic sustainability, in that order.’ A government stating the priority sequence explicitly is unusual and directly quotable against any proposal that inverts it. AND COMMUNITIES CAN CAP VISITOR NUMBERS: the law makes it possible for local communities to restrict the number of tourists, to ensure these communities remain good places to live in — a community power exercised on liveability grounds, which is rare. The law is also to protect the natural environment, existing agricultural activities, and local ownership and participation; access may be restricted when collecting sheep, in lambing season, or in poor weather. Fee income is earmarked for hiking paths and tourism planning. WHY IT WAS NEEDED: the previous rule on walking traditional paths was the agriculture law from 1937, long before tourism was contemplated, and as tourism surged farmers and operators met it with various private unauthorised systems. RECORDED HONESTLY: reporting notes the hiking fee has in places been driven by private landowners rather than government, and that it is not yet clear who exactly benefits — treat the fee regime as unsettled rather than as a model.

trackers.name: Granskingarráðið — ‘significant in a Faroese context’ is an alternative limb
trackers.desc: RECORDED HONESTLY: THREE ROUNDS OF SEARCHING, IN ENGLISH AND FAROESE, FOUND NO COMMUNITY ENVIRONMENTAL GRANT SCHEME IN THE FAROE ISLANDS. What exists is research funding plus Horizon Europe access. The Research Council Faroe Islands is a public research funding body which also administers the islands' association agreement on participation in Horizon Europe. Funding opens once a year — the next deadline published as 15 February 2027, 12:00 noon local time — so missing the single date costs a year. ELIGIBILITY HAS THREE ALTERNATIVE LIMBS: research carried out by a Faroese researcher, OR in cooperation with a Faroese research institute, OR considered significant in a Faroese context. That third limb is an alternative, not an additional requirement — so a project need not be led by a Faroese researcher if its significance to the Faroes can be established. That is the limb to argue if you are a community or outside partner rather than an academic body. It funds PhD projects, postdoc or other projects of at least 6 months, and industrial R&D; criteria are scientific excellence, impact and implementation, with advantage to projects producing data and lasting knowledge and skills. THE PRACTICAL ROUTE: pair with a Faroese research institute and frame the work as producing data — baseline surveys, monitoring and inventories fit this funder in a way campaigning does not.

trackers.name: Umhvørvisstovan — conservation, the cadastre and land registration in one agency
trackers.desc: ONE ENQUIRY ESTABLISHES BOTH OWNERSHIP AND STATUS. The Faroese Environment Agency, under the Ministry of Environment and based at Argir, covers environmental protection, environmental research, nature conservation, energy and electricity supply supervision, woodlands and recreational areas, land and sea maps, the cadastre (matrikul), land registration (tinglýsing) and the national population register. Nature conservation, the cadastre and land registration sit in the same agency — so establishing who is registered against a parcel and its conservation status is a single-agency enquiry, which is unusual and makes early fact-finding far cheaper than in most jurisdictions in this map. IT ALSO CO-FUNDS APPLIED RESEARCH: it is recorded as a named financier of Faroese fjord benthic macrofauna classification work alongside the aquaculture association, and the environment and industry ministry has directly financed environmental monitoring in Faroese fjords — by arrangement rather than through an open call. SO THE THREE REALISTIC ROUTES HERE ARE: partnering with a research institute into the Research Council's annual call; a direct arrangement with Umhvørvisstovan; or Horizon Europe via the association agreement. None is an application form a village association can complete alone — plan for a partner.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants Programme (SGP) — Turkmenistan
trackers.desc: TURKMENISTAN WAS ADDED TO SGP PARTICIPATION IN GEF-8, and is named among the 11 new countries on the GEF's own page — so this is a newly available route, and older guidance will not list it. SGP is a GEF corporate programme running since 1992, implemented by UNDP and executed by UNOPS; GEF-8 raised participation from 124 countries to 135, out of 144 eligible. THE MONEY IS NOT COMPETED FOR ACROSS COUNTRIES: GEF-8 secured $135 million for the core programme with equal allocation of nearly $1 million in core financing to each of the 135 countries — a per-country floor, which is unusual. Grants of up to $50,000 go directly to local communities, including community-based organisations and other non-governmental groups. FOCAL AREAS: biodiversity, climate change, land degradation and sustainable forest management, international waters and chemicals. READ YOUR COUNTRY PROGRAMME STRATEGY BEFORE APPLYING: each country writes its own CPS which puts emphasis on certain thematic and geographic areas, so it may exclude your region or theme regardless of global eligibility. WHO DECIDES LOCALLY: a locally recruited National Coordinator and a voluntary National Steering Committee, described as the central element of SGP and the body providing substantive oversight. Note that under SGP 2.0 the implementing agency may be FAO or Conservation International rather than UNDP, and the host may be a national host institution rather than the UNDP country office — confirm which applies before addressing an application. AN UNREGISTERED VILLAGE GROUP CAN BE FUNDED DIRECTLY. The programme states that, with UNOPS, it has developed Memoranda of Agreement allowing grants to community-based groups that are not formally registered, without an intermediary non-governmental organisation. In a country where forming and registering an independent environmental association is itself difficult and potentially exposing, that route matters more than the grant ceiling does — it means a group need not constitute itself publicly in order to be funded. Ask about a Memorandum of Agreement specifically. Note also that National Coordinators are UN-contracted rather than government-employed, to protect neutrality in grant-making, and that the programme now runs with several implementing agencies rather than UNDP alone.

trackers.name: Law on Nature Protection — public associations' rights, and the emergency chapter
trackers.desc: CITE THE RIGHT INSTRUMENT — the statutes are dated and distinct. «Об охране природы» dates from 12 November 1991; «О государственных особо охраняемых природных территориях» from 19 May 1992; «О государственной экологической экспертизе» from 15 June 1995; «Об углеводородных ресурсах» from 1996. WHAT THE NATURE PROTECTION LAW GIVES YOU: it enshrines the rights and obligations of citizens and of public associations (общественных объединений) in nature protection, and establishes financing — a statutory recognition of public associations' rights in the founding law, not a subordinate act. Chapter IX (articles 42–45) covers forests, flora, fauna and specially protected territories, with article 45 on objects subject to special protection. Article 38 sets ecological requirements for activity in the Turkmen sector of the Caspian Sea. AND WHERE DEGRADATION IS ALREADY SEVERE: Chapter XI covers чрезвычайные экологические ситуации and зоны экологического бедствия — emergency ecological situations and ecological disaster zones — with article 49 on the emergency situation. That is a named statutory category with its own chapter, distinct from ordinary protection. Violating the regime of a protected territory carries administrative, civil or criminal responsibility. ASK WHETHER A STATE ECOLOGICAL EXPERTIZA WAS CONDUCTED — it has its own 1995 statute and is a separate act from any permit.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — it takes communications from the public
trackers.desc: A ROUTE THAT DOES NOT DEPEND ON DOMESTIC STANDING. Turkmenistan is a Party to the Aarhus Convention, and UNECE hosts Turkmen environmental legislation within its compliance section under decisions of the Meeting of the Parties, including a country-specific MoP4 decision folder — so the mechanism has been engaged with Turkmenistan before. The Compliance Committee receives communications from members of the public concerning a Party's compliance with obligations on access to information, public participation in decision-making and access to justice. Where domestic routes are closed, this one does not turn on national standing rules — which is why it matters more here than in most jurisdictions in this map. BE REALISTIC ABOUT WHAT IT DELIVERS: the Committee's outputs are findings and recommendations adopted by the Meeting of the Parties, not orders enforceable in a national court. It is a compliance and publicity mechanism, not a remedy — useful for creating a documented international record and for pressure, and it should be planned as that rather than as litigation.

trackers.name: CEPF Mountains of Central Asia — Turkmenistan is a named eligible country, and this is the only resource recorded for it
trackers.desc: TURKMENISTAN IS NAMED AS AN ELIGIBLE COUNTRY IN CEPF'S OWN CALLS FOR PROPOSALS, ALONGSIDE KAZAKHSTAN, KYRGYZSTAN, TAJIKISTAN AND UZBEKISTAN — and the eligible territory is small and specific: a mountainous part of the country's south-east, identified in the ecosystem profile as the Koytendag mountains and Talimerjen. If your site is not in that area it is outside the hotspot, and this route does not apply. WHY THIS IS THE ONLY ENTRY THIS MAP CARRIES FOR TURKMENISTAN, AND WHY IT IS AN EXTERNAL FUND RATHER THAN A LOCAL BODY: Turkmenistan is a closed operating environment, and naming domestic organisations or individuals in a public map can expose the people in them. An international fund names nobody. That is a deliberate limit on what is recorded here, not an omission — and a reader should understand that the absence of Turkmen organisations from this file reflects a decision about safety rather than a finding that none exist. WHAT THE FUND DOES: letters of inquiry are accepted from non-governmental organisations, community groups, Indigenous peoples' organisations, women's groups, private companies and other civil society organisations; large grants in recent calls ran from fifty thousand to a hundred and fifty thousand US dollars and small grants average around fifteen thousand, with a new portfolio beginning in 2026 after nearly a hundred projects in the first phase. Applications must align with the strategic directions, priority species, priority Key Biodiversity Areas or corridors set out in the ecosystem profile, which carries a table of Turkmen priorities of its own. Individuals cannot apply directly and must work through a civil society organisation. CEPF is a joint initiative of the French Development Agency, Conservation International, the European Union, the Global Environment Facility, the Government of Japan and the World Bank. Confirm the current regional implementation team and the open-call status before acting; and consider carefully, in this operating environment, what applying publicly for foreign conservation funding may mean for those named on the application.

trackers.name: Rufford Small Grants — Turkmenistan is named eligible, and no organisation or registration is required
trackers.desc: TURKMENISTAN IS ON THE FOUNDATION'S ELIGIBLE COUNTRY LIST AND NOT ON ITS LIST OF COUNTRIES IT CANNOT CURRENTLY CONSIDER. This is the third international funding route recorded for a country where this map deliberately records no local organisation, and it is the one that asks least of an applicant: individuals and small groups may apply, no registered body is needed, and there are no deadlines at any time of year. The focus is people early in a conservation career, especially current or recent MSc and PhD students, with others considered against the published criteria. THE SPECIES TEST IS PUBLISHED AND CHECKABLE BEFORE YOU START: any species not listed as Least Concern globally on the IUCN Red List, or not yet assessed but thought to be globally threatened. Threatened habitats, human-wildlife conflict and community education projects qualify with no species focus. GRANTS RUN AS A STAIRCASE from up to £7,000 to roughly £18,000 across four stages, each conditional on finishing and reporting the last, with updates and final reports published on the applicant's page. One application per twelve months; a twelve-month wait after rejection; the foundation expects to provide half to all of the cost and requires evidence of co-funding where there is any. THE CAUTION GIVEN FOR THE OTHER TURKMEN ENTRIES APPLIES HERE TOO AND IS REPEATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED TO CARRY: in a closed operating environment, weigh what a public application for foreign conservation funding, and a published project page carrying your name, may mean for you. The reporting that makes this fund attractive elsewhere is a public record, and that cuts both ways.

trackers.name: Copernicus Browser — free imagery, water and vegetation indices, and atmospheric data
trackers.desc: IT NEEDS NOTHING LOCAL. A free service for browsing and downloading FULL-RESOLUTION imagery from the European Copernicus satellite missions, where anyone can select an area and a date range, COMPARE IMAGES SIDE BY SIDE, and BUILD A TIMELAPSE showing how a place has changed — all from a web browser with a free account. Every other entry recorded for this country is a foreign institution or a state portal, because domestic organisations cannot safely be named. A TOOL ONE PERSON OPERATES ALONE IS THEREFORE THE MOST DIRECTLY USABLE RESOURCE IN THIS COUNTRY'S ENTIRE LISTING. IT CARRIES MORE THAN PICTURES: a VEGETATION index for plant health, a WATER index for surface water, radar imagery that sees through cloud, and ATMOSPHERIC AND AIR QUALITY DATA from a dedicated mission. For land drying, canals and irrigation, pasture loss or industrial emissions, those are the layers that turn an impression into a measurement — and this file has recorded across the region that measurement is what an authority or a court will engage with. AN INVESTIGATIVE RESEARCH TOOLKIT LISTS ITS USES AS TRACKING CONSTRUCTION PROJECTS, MINING OPERATIONS AND LAND DEVELOPMENT, and documenting environmental degradation over time. WHAT IT WILL NOT DO: it is imagery and data, not analysis, and nobody interprets it for you. Resolution is moderate, so individual buildings and small clearings may be hard to read; optical images are blocked by cloud; and a free account is currently needed. Pair it with the forest monitoring platform recorded elsewhere in this file, which supplies annual tree cover loss and daily fire alerts for anywhere on earth. AND CHECK THE ADDRESS BEFORE FOLLOWING ANY GUIDE: THE PREDECESSOR VIEWER WAS SHUT DOWN IN FEBRUARY 2025 and its functions were moved here, so older tutorials name a service that no longer exists.

trackers.name: Digital Security Helpline — free, round the clock, answered within two hours, in Russian
trackers.desc: IT COSTS NOTHING, IT RUNS TWENTY-FOUR HOURS A DAY, AND IT ANSWERS EVERY REQUEST WITHIN TWO HOURS — with support available in RUSSIAN among ten languages. Every other entry recorded for this country is a foreign institution, a state portal or a satellite tool used alone, because domestic organisations cannot safely be named here. A HELPLINE IS THE FIRST ENTRY IN THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING THAT PUTS A PERSON ON THE OTHER END OF A MESSAGE. IT DOES TWO DIFFERENT JOBS AND YOU SHOULD KNOW WHICH YOU NEED. Before anything happens, it walks you or your group through ASSESSING THE RISKS YOUR WORK ACTUALLY CREATES and deciding what to secure first. If you are already under attack, it provides RAPID-RESPONSE EMERGENCY ASSISTANCE. AND IT TURNS AN ATTACK INTO EVIDENCE: it helps people ANALYSE, DOCUMENT AND EXPOSE advanced attacks including SPYWARE and targeted phishing. A technically documented intrusion is something an international body can act on; an unverified suspicion is not. IT SECURES WHAT A SMALL GROUP ACTUALLY HAS — devices, accounts, websites and social media — and provides guidance materials, training and onward referrals. REACH IT BY EMAIL AT A PUBLISHED ADDRESS. It is an accredited member of a computer emergency response body for civil society and publishes a data usage policy and helpline terms of service. READ BOTH BEFORE SENDING ANYTHING, AND THINK HARD ABOUT WHICH DEVICE AND CONNECTION YOU USE TO MAKE CONTACT — in this country that decision matters more than the message. THE LIMITS: it handles digital security and nothing else. It will not advise on a land case, fund anything, represent anyone, or change the conditions that make the work dangerous. Use it alongside the satellite imagery browser recorded separately for this country, which is the kind of activity that draws the attention this helpline exists to defend against.

trackers.name: GBIF — free species occurrence records for any location, downloadable and citable
trackers.desc: IT NEEDS NO LOCAL ORGANISATION AND NO PERMISSION. More than three billion species occurrence records — from museums, HERBARIA, government inventories, surveys and citizen science across more than a hundred countries — searchable by place and by species, free to consult, with each record showing the scientific name, coordinates, DATE, source and flags describing its provenance and locational accuracy. Every other entry recorded for this country is a foreign institution, a state portal or a tool used alone, because domestic organisations cannot safely be named here. THIS IS THE FOURTH SUCH TOOL, AND IT ANSWERS THE QUESTION THE OTHERS CANNOT: NOT WHAT CHANGED, BUT WHAT LIVES THERE. AND WHEN YOU DOWNLOAD RECORDS IT ISSUES A PERMANENT IDENTIFIER, so your exact extraction is CITABLE AND REPRODUCIBLE by anyone who wants to check it. That converts a species record from something you assert into something documented, which is the difference this file has repeatedly found between an objection that is dismissed and one that must be answered. THE SPECIMENS AND SURVEYS BEHIND THOSE RECORDS INCLUDE MATERIAL COLLECTED IN THIS REGION OVER MORE THAN A CENTURY AND HELD IN INSTITUTIONS ABROAD — which is precisely the material a person here cannot otherwise reach. DOWNLOADS ARRIVE AS COORDINATES IN A SPREADSHEET AND IMPORT DIRECTLY INTO MAPPING SOFTWARE, including the free satellite imagery browser recorded separately for this country. Species records plus dated imagery is a before-and-after argument built entirely from open sources and made by one person. Access is free under open licences; a free account is required to download, and the programming interface requires no registration at all. THE LIMIT, AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS: IT SHOWS WHAT HAS BEEN OBSERVED AND PUBLISHED, NOT WHAT EXISTS. Sparsely surveyed country looks empty, and an operator can cite that emptiness exactly as a community would cite a record. Treat a blank map as a gap in the record rather than a fact about the ground.

trackers.name: Central Asia Pastoralist Alliance — regional bloc for rangeland rights, covering this country
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY IS NAMED IN A REGIONAL ALLIANCE THAT HAS ALREADY CHANGED PASTURE LAW ELSEWHERE. Its members were HIGHLY INVOLVED IN DRAFTING AND IMPLEMENTING SIX LAND-RELATED POLICIES, INCLUDING AMENDMENTS TO PASTURE LAWS in three countries of the region, prompting RECOGNITION OF PASTORALIST AND HERDER COMMUNITY LAND RIGHTS, SECURING MORE THAN THIRTY-NINE MILLION HECTARES OF PASTURELAND and affecting OVER EIGHTY THOUSAND HOUSEHOLDS. Everything else recorded for this country is a foreign institution, a state portal or a tool used alone. THIS IS THE FIRST ENTRY THAT CONNECTS IT TO A REGIONAL BLOC WITH A RECORD OF WINNING. THE ALLIANCE SPANS Afghanistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Mongolia, Tajikistan, this country and Uzbekistan, and sits within a global land-rights coalition of nearly three hundred organisations across more than eighty countries. EVERY MEMBER OF THAT COALITION SIGNS A PLEDGE TO UPHOLD GENDER JUSTICE AND TO DEFEND LAND AND ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDERS WHO ARE CRIMINALISED, INTIMIDATED AND MARGINALISED FOR ADVOCATING CHANGE. In a country where this file records no domestic organisation that can safely be named, a regional body whose members have signed that commitment is a channel that exists outside the country. THE CONDITION IT ADDRESSES IS DOCUMENTED AND REGIONAL: an estimated SIXTY TO EIGHTY-EIGHT PER CENT OF ALL CENTRAL ASIAN PASTURELANDS HAVE DEGRADED, under pressure from common-resource decline, livestock numbers and the WIDE-SCALE EXPANSION OF INDUSTRIES. THE ROUTE IN IS THROUGH MEMBER ORGANISATIONS IN NEIGHBOURING COUNTRIES, three of which are recorded in this file — a pasture committee association, a rural research fund and a forest and land users association — and through the coalition's Asia office. THE LIMITS, AND THEY MATTER HERE: it is an alliance of organisations rather than a body an individual joins; its work is legislative advocacy rather than casework; and THE ALLIANCE NAMING THIS COUNTRY IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT A MEMBER ORGANISATION IS BASED IN IT. Establish that before relying on it, and consider what contacting a foreign network discloses — the digital security helpline recorded separately here is the place to ask first.

trackers.name: Aarhus Centre — the one body here whose stated job is giving the public environmental information
trackers.desc: ITS STATED PURPOSE IS THE THING THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING HAS NEVER CONTAINED: to facilitate FREE ACCESS TO ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION, PUBLIC PARTICIPATION IN ENVIRONMENTAL DECISION-MAKING, and ACCESS TO JUSTICE ON ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS. Everything else recorded for this country is a foreign institution or a tool used alone, because domestic organisations cannot safely be named. This is a body inside the country whose published mandate is to give people environmental information — and asking a body to do the thing it exists to do is a different proposition from asking a favour. IT HAS OPERATED SINCE 2012 and its published work includes PRODUCING COMPREHENSIVE ENVIRONMENTAL MATERIALS FOR PUBLICATION IN THE NATIONAL MASS MEDIA, developing partnerships with state and civil society representatives and with the network of equivalent centres in other countries, and supporting the projects of international bodies including development, environment and regional development banks. THE NETWORK BEHIND IT MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE CENTRE: sixty such centres operate across fourteen countries, seven of them in this chat's region, and they work as a network. A question that cannot be pressed locally can sometimes be raised through a counterpart centre in a neighbouring country, or through the network's own reporting on how the convention is being implemented. WHAT THE MODEL CAN INCLUDE, THOUGH IT WAS NOT CONFIRMED HERE: centres elsewhere in the network employ LEGAL STAFF — a legal assistant and a legal associate — alongside a standing network of experts and volunteers brought in as needed. Ask what legal capacity this centre has before assuming it has none. THE LIMIT, STATED PLAINLY AND IT IS THE WHOLE CAUTION: the centre is supported by an intergovernmental security organisation and works IN CLOSE CO-OPERATION WITH THE HOST COUNTRY, in particular the ministry responsible for the environment. IT IS NOT INDEPENDENT. Where a dispute is with a state body or a state-owned project, weigh what you disclose and to whom. Use it to obtain information, to find out when and how a decision is open to comment, and to learn what the law requires; take anything adversarial to the international routes and the self-service tools recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: OSME Conservation Fund — it has asked for applications from this country by name
trackers.desc: THE FUND HAS SAID IT IS ESPECIALLY KEEN TO RECEIVE APPLICATIONS FROM THIS COUNTRY. No other funder recorded anywhere in this map names it. The society behind it covers the whole Middle East, Caucasus and Central Asia, and its small grants support conservation and research across that region. THE TERMS ARE BETTER THAN ALMOST ANY OTHER FUND IN THIS FILE: THREE DECISION ROUNDS EACH YEAR with deadlines of 31 January, 31 May and 30 September; typical awards of one to three thousand pounds WITH NO STATED MAXIMUM; and a published funding rate of AROUND FIFTY PER CENT. Most funds in this payload do not say what proportion they fund. One in two is a real chance rather than a lottery. AND THE ELIGIBLE WORK IS THE WORK THAT PROTECTS GROUND, NOT JUST BIRDS: INVESTIGATING POTENTIAL NEW IMPORTANT BIRD AREAS or ornithologically little-known areas; furthering knowledge of EXISTING important bird areas through breeding censuses and systematic counts; investigating the status of threatened species; STUDIES RELATED TO ILLEGAL BIRD KILLING AND UNSUSTAINABLE HUNTING; and educational programmes. Getting a stretch of steppe, wetland or desert recognised as an internationally important bird area is one of the few ways a place in this country can acquire a designation that outsiders recognise — and this fund pays for the survey that does it. ITS CRITERIA ARE WRITTEN IN FAVOUR OF LOCAL PEOPLE: projects should be INITIATED AND CARRIED OUT BY NATIONALS of the region, and/or engage local communities, and/or build long-term sustainability such as TRAINING LOCAL COUNTERPARTS — and applications carrying significant international airfare costs are unlikely to be approved. A fund that discourages flying in foreign experts is a fund that expects the work to be done by people who live there. TWO FURTHER GRANTS EXIST: one focused on threatened species research, a single award of up to five thousand pounds a year with a deadline around 1 December; and a youth fund for bird camps and education projects for people aged sixteen to twenty-five, LED FROM WITHIN THE REGION, typically one to two thousand pounds. The society also publishes a country profile for this country and has made a major international bird reference platform freely accessible across the region. THE LIMITS: it funds birds and their habitats, not land disputes; the sums are small; specimen collection requires justification and local authorisations; and it is a scientific society, not an advocate — it will not object to a project. Use it to fund the survey; use the survey with the species databases and satellite tools recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: The Ombudsman — the only domestic institution in this country's listing that receives complaints
trackers.desc: EVERY OTHER ENTRY RECORDED FOR THIS COUNTRY IS A FOREIGN INSTITUTION OR A TOOL USED ALONE. THIS IS A DOMESTIC OFFICE THAT RECEIVES COMPLAINTS. The post was established to secure state protection of the rights and freedoms of people and citizens and their observance by government authorities, local governments and their officials.
