THEY ARE INCOME AND FOOD, AND THIS FILE HAS RECORDED ACROSS THE REGION THAT GROUND CARRYING A PRODUCTIVE CROP IS HARDER TO RECLASSIFY AS IDLE OR TO REALLOCATE — SO THE ASK AT THE PROVINCIAL ADMINISTRATION IS FOR FRUIT AND VINE STOCK, NOT WHATEVER IS LEFT ON THE LORRY. THE PLANNING BEHIND IT IS PUBLISHED ENOUGH TO ARGUE WITH: A NATIONAL FOREST PROGRAMME ADOPTED AT AN EXPANDED CABINET SESSION SETS THE ANNUAL PLANTING, WITH HALF ONE YEAR'S SAPLINGS GOING TO A SINGLE PROVINCE AND THE REST DIVIDED AMONG THE OTHERS. HALF TO ONE PROVINCE IS AN ALLOCATION DECISION, WHICH MEANS THERE IS SOMETHING TO ASK ABOUT: WHERE THIS SEASON'S STOCK IS GOING, AND WHY NOT HERE. IN A COUNTRY WHERE THIS PAYLOAD HAS FOUND ALMOST NO OPENINGS, AN ALLOCATION QUESTION PUT POLITELY TO A PROVINCIAL ADMINISTRATION IS ONE OF THE FEW. THE TECHNICAL SIDE IS UNUSUALLY SPECIFIC AND WORTH BORROWING: RECOMMENDATIONS FOR GREENING A COASTAL ZONE WERE BUILT ON AGRICULTURAL TECHNIQUE, HYDROGEOLOGICAL INDICATORS, FLUCTUATION IN THE LEVEL OF THE CASPIAN SEA AND HYDROMETEOROLOGICAL FACTORS — WHICH IS THE RIGHT WAY TO CHOOSE WHAT TO PLANT ON SALTY OR SHIFTING GROUND ANYWHERE. THE CAPITAL'S GREENING HAS ALSO BEEN RECOGNISED ABROAD: IT RECEIVED AN INTERNATIONAL CERTIFICATE FROM A UNITED NATIONS ECONOMIC COMMISSION FOR ITS CONTRIBUTION TO A TREES IN CITIES INITIATIVE, WITH A UN HEALTH OFFICIAL NOTING THAT SUCH CERTIFICATES ARE NOT GIVEN LIGHTLY AND THAT THE GREENING MATTERS FOR THE CITY'S ECOLOGY AND FOR PEOPLE'S HEALTH. AN INTERNATIONAL CERTIFICATE IS A COMMITMENT WITH A WITNESS. WHERE TREES ARE FELLED OR A GREEN AREA BUILT OVER, THE EXISTENCE OF THAT RECOGNITION IS THE MILDEST POSSIBLE WAY TO RAISE IT — NOT AS A COMPLAINT, BUT AS A QUESTION ABOUT A STANDARD THE COUNTRY HAS ALREADY BEEN PRAISED FOR MEETING. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE THE USUAL ONES FOR THIS COUNTRY: THIS IS A STATE CAMPAIGN ORDERED FROM THE TOP, ORGANISED THROUGH PROVINCIAL ADMINISTRATIONS AND WORKPLACES, AND PARTICIPATION IN SUCH COLLECTIVE WORK DAYS IS IN PRACTICE EXPECTED RATHER THAN VOLUNTARY - IT IS NOT A SERVICE A RESIDENT REQUESTS BUT AN EVENT A RESIDENT IS CALLED TO. WHETHER SAPLINGS ARE GIVEN TO HOUSEHOLDS FOR THEIR OWN LAND, WHO DECIDES ALLOCATION WITHIN A PROVINCE, AND WHETHER ANYTHING IS AVAILABLE OUTSIDE THE TWO CAMPAIGN DATES WERE ALL NOT ESTABLISHED. INDEPENDENT REPORTING ON ONE YEAR RECORDED A SUBSTANTIAL REDUCTION IN PLANTING MATERIAL AGAINST THE ANNOUNCED FIGURES, AND SURVIVAL RATES FOR MASS PLANTINGS IN ARID CONDITIONS ARE NOT PUBLISHED. THE FIGURES HERE COME FROM STATE NEWS AND GOVERNMENT PORTALS OF SEVERAL YEARS ALONGSIDE ONE EXILE-RUN BROADCASTER AND ONE REGIONAL OUTLET. Read it with the standards service's accredited laboratories, the collegia of advocates and legal consultation offices, the chamber's expert examinations and the Red Crescent's province branches recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Union of industrialists and entrepreneurs — regional branches, a statutory duty to defend members' interests, and its own bank and school
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE MOST CLOSED COUNTRY IN THE PAYLOAD AND THE ONE WHERE THIS FILE HAS FOUND ALMOST NOTHING A PERSON CAN JOIN. HERE IS SOMETHING: A UNION OF INDUSTRIALISTS AND ENTREPRENEURS, A PUBLIC ORGANISATION FOUNDED IN MARCH 2008, UNITING NATURAL AND LEGAL PERSONS WHO CARRY OUT ENTREPRENEURIAL ACTIVITY ON THE BASIS OF PRIVATE OR MIXED OWNERSHIP. ITS STATUTORY PURPOSE IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: IT IS CALLED TO EXPRESS AND DEFEND THE RIGHTS AND LEGITIMATE INTERESTS OF ITS MEMBERS, AND ITS LEGAL, ORGANISATIONAL AND ECONOMIC BASIS IS SET BY A LAW WRITTEN FOR IT ALONE, NOW IN A NEW EDITION. AN ORGANISATION WHOSE OWN LAW SAYS IT EXISTS TO DEFEND ITS MEMBERS' RIGHTS IS A RARE THING IN A STATE WITH ALMOST NO INDEPENDENT ASSOCIATIONS. IT IS NOT A CAMPAIGN GROUP AND WILL NEVER BE ONE - BUT A FARMER OR A WORKSHOP OWNER WITH A GRIEVANCE HAS, IN THIS BODY, A LAWFUL PLACE TO PUT IT. ITS SHAPE IS REGIONAL AND ITS CALENDAR IS FIXED: IT UNITES REGIONAL BRANCHES, ITS HIGHEST GOVERNING BODY IS A CONFERENCE CONVENED NOT LESS THAN ONCE A YEAR, AND BETWEEN CONFERENCES IT IS RUN BY A BOARD HEADED BY A CHAIRMAN, WITH A REVISION COMMISSION. A CONFERENCE THAT MUST BE HELD ANNUALLY IS ONE FIXED OCCASION EACH YEAR WHERE MEMBERS FROM EVERY PROVINCE ARE IN ONE ROOM. IN A COUNTRY WHERE THIS PAYLOAD HAS RECORDED NO PUBLIC MEETINGS AT ALL, THAT IS WORTH KNOWING. ITS MEMBERS ARE NOT ONLY CITY BUSINESSES: THEY WORK IN TRADE, PUBLIC CATERING, AGRICULTURE AND OTHER SECTORS, CARRY OUT LARGE CONSTRUCTION PROJECTS IN THE CAPITAL AND THE REGIONS, AND HAVE OPENED ENTERPRISES INSIDE NAMED FARMERS' ASSOCIATIONS IN NAMED DISTRICTS AND PROVINCES. ENTERPRISES BUILT BY UNION MEMBERS INSIDE VILLAGE FARMING ASSOCIATIONS IS THE DETAIL THAT MAKES THIS SUBNATIONAL RATHER THAN CAPITAL-BOUND. THE UNION REACHES INTO THE DAYHAN ASSOCIATIONS THEMSELVES, WHICH IS WHERE LAND AND WATER DECISIONS BITE. IT ALSO OWNS THINGS THAT MATTER TO ANYONE TRYING TO FINANCE A FARM: THE UNION IS THE FOUNDER OF A JOINT-STOCK COMMERCIAL BANK AND OF A SCHOOL OF ENTREPRENEURSHIP, AND THE ESTABLISHER OF THE COUNTRY'S FIRST PRIVATE NEWSPAPER. A MEMBERS' BANK, A TRAINING SCHOOL AND A NEWSPAPER IN ONE ORGANISATION IS CREDIT, SKILLS AND PUBLICITY UNDER A SINGLE MEMBERSHIP - THE THREE THINGS THIS FILE HAS SPENT HUNDREDS OF ROUNDS SOURCING SEPARATELY ELSEWHERE. IT HAS AN OUTSIDE RELATIONSHIP TOO, WHICH IS UNUSUAL HERE: IN DECEMBER 2023 THE UNITED NATIONS IN THIS COUNTRY AND THE UNION SIGNED AN ACTION PLAN TO IMPLEMENT A MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING, AIMED AT ACCELERATING IMPLEMENTATION OF THE 2030 SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AGENDA. THAT PARTNERSHIP IS THE LANGUAGE TO USE WHEN RAISING ANYTHING ENVIRONMENTAL THROUGH THIS BODY. SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IS A HEADING THE UNION HAS SIGNED UP TO IN WRITING WITH AN INTERNATIONAL COUNTERPART - AND THIS PAYLOAD HAS RECORDED, ACROSS EVERY CLOSED STATE IT COVERS, THAT THE HEADING DECIDES WHETHER A SUBJECT CAN BE DISCUSSED AT ALL. THE STATE PROGRAMMES ITS MEMBERS WORK INSIDE ARE ALSO WORTH KNOWING: PROGRAMMES FOR IMPORT-SUBSTITUTING PRODUCTION AND INCREASED EXPORTS ENVISAGE MORE THAN A HUNDRED AND TEN PROJECTS, INCLUDING IN AGRICULTURE AND THE FOOD INDUSTRY. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE THE HEAVIEST IN THIS PAYLOAD: THIS IS DESCRIBED BY INDEPENDENT SOURCES AS A QUASI-PUBLIC ORGANISATION, CREATED ON THE INITIATIVE OF THE PRESIDENT AND OPERATING UNDER ITS OWN STATE LAW - IT IS THE PRIVATE SECTOR'S OFFICIAL CHANNEL, NOT AN INDEPENDENT ONE, AND NOTHING RECORDED HERE SUGGESTS IT WOULD RAISE A COMPLAINT AGAINST A STATE PROJECT OR AN ALLOCATION OF LAND. MEMBERSHIP TERMS, FEES, WHETHER A SMALL FARMER OR A HOUSEHOLD PLOT HOLDER CAN JOIN, WHERE THE REGIONAL BRANCHES SIT AND HOW TO CONTACT THEM WERE ALL NOT ESTABLISHED. THE DESCRIPTION COMES FROM AN AARHUS CENTRE'S BLOG PAGES, AN ENCYCLOPAEDIA ENTRY, A TURKMEN WIKI, THE TEXT OF THE UNION'S LAW IN AN AGRICULTURAL LEGISLATION DATABASE AND A UNITED NATIONS COUNTRY PAGE OF 2023 - NOT FROM THE UNION'S OWN CURRENT PUBLICATIONS, AND THE 110-PROJECT FIGURE COMES FROM AN EMBASSY PAGE THAT MAY BE A DECADE OLD. Read it with the chamber of commerce's expert examinations, the standards service's accredited laboratories, the collegia of advocates and the Red Crescent's province branches recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Nature protection society of 1968 — province branches on their own annual plans, and membership of the international conservation union
trackers.desc: IN THE MOST CLOSED COUNTRY IN THIS PAYLOAD, THIS IS A PUBLIC ASSOCIATION A PERSON CAN BELONG TO, AND IT HAS EXISTED SINCE 1968 - FOUNDED IN DECEMBER 1967 BY A NAMED INDIVIDUAL AND OFFICIALLY BEGINNING WORK IN JULY 1968 UNDER AN ORDER OF THE THEN COUNCIL OF MINISTERS, MAKING IT ONE OF THE OLDEST PUBLIC ASSOCIATIONS IN THE COUNTRY. ITS STATED PURPOSE CONTAINS A PHRASE WORTH KEEPING: DRAWING CITIZENS INTO THE RESOLUTION OF QUESTIONS OF PROTECTION, RATIONAL USE AND REPRODUCTION OF NATURAL RESOURCES - ALONGSIDE COORDINATING PUBLIC WORK IN NATURE PROTECTION AND ORGANISING A MOVEMENT FOR A HEALTHY AND FAVOURABLE ECOLOGICAL SITUATION. DRAWING CITIZENS INTO DECIDING QUESTIONS OF THE USE OF NATURAL RESOURCES IS, IN THIS COUNTRY, AN EXTRAORDINARY SENTENCE TO HAVE IN A REGISTERED ORGANISATION'S PURPOSE. IT IS THE ONE THIS FILE WOULD QUOTE WHEN ASKING WHY RESIDENTS WERE NOT CONSULTED ABOUT A CANAL, A PIT OR A PLANTATION. ITS STRUCTURE REACHES BEYOND THE CAPITAL: THE PROVINCE BRANCHES CARRY OUT THEIR ACTIVITY ON THE BASIS OF ANNUAL WORK PLANS APPROVED BY THE CENTRAL BOARD, AND STAFF AND MEMBERS HOLD ANNUAL EXHIBITIONS MARKING NATIONAL DAYS AND WORLD ENVIRONMENT DAY. AN ANNUAL WORK PLAN IS A DOCUMENT, AND A DOCUMENT CAN BE ASKED FOR. A COMMUNITY THAT WANTS ITS SPRING, ITS SALTED FIELD OR ITS DYING WINDBREAK ADDRESSED SHOULD BE ASKING WHEN NEXT YEAR'S PROVINCE PLAN IS DRAWN UP AND WHO PROPOSES WHAT GOES IN IT. ITS INTERNATIONAL STANDING IS THE PART THAT GIVES IT WEIGHT: IT IS A MEMBER OF THE INTERNATIONAL UNION FOR CONSERVATION OF NATURE AND A STRATEGIC PARTNER OF A CIVIL SOCIETY DEVELOPMENT ASSOCIATION, AND THAT UNION'S FOURTEENTH GENERAL ASSEMBLY WAS HELD IN THIS COUNTRY IN 1978. THIS PAYLOAD RECORDS THAT SAME UNION SEPARATELY AS A MEMBERSHIP BODY OF GOVERNMENTS AND NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS WITH NATIONAL COMMITTEES AND A REGIONAL OFFICE. A LOCAL SOCIETY THAT IS ALREADY A MEMBER IS THE BRIDGE BETWEEN A VILLAGE HERE AND THAT NETWORK - AND THE QUESTION TO ASK IS WHETHER A NATIONAL COMMITTEE EXISTS AND WHEN IT MEETS. THE LEGAL BACKDROP IS WORTH CARRYING TOO, BECAUSE IT IS STATED BY AN INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATION RATHER THAN BY THE GOVERNMENT: THE COUNTRY'S NEW ENVIRONMENTAL LEGISLATION LARGELY TAKES ACCOUNT OF INTERNATIONAL LEGAL NORMS AND ADDRESSES ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS INCLUDING ACCESS TO ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION AND ACCESS TO JUSTICE FOR THE PROTECTION OF THOSE RIGHTS, WHILE THE CONSTITUTION MAKES THE STATE RESPONSIBLE FOR PRESERVING NATURAL RESOURCES IN ORDER TO PROTECT AND IMPROVE CITIZENS' LIVING CONDITIONS AND TO PROTECT AND RESTORE THE ENVIRONMENT. THE SAME SOURCE RECORDS THAT THE CONSTITUTION ESTABLISHES THE RIGHT OF PRIVATE OWNERSHIP OF LAND - WHICH IN A COUNTRY WHERE THIS FILE HAS RECORDED ALMOST NO PRIVATE HOLDING IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FACT ABOUT WHAT A HOUSEHOLD MIGHT ONE DAY OWN. THE PRACTICAL SEQUENCE IS SHORT AND LOW-RISK: FIND THE PROVINCE BRANCH, ASK ABOUT MEMBERSHIP, ASK WHEN THE ANNUAL PLAN IS PREPARED, AND OFFER A LOCAL SUBJECT FOR THE NEXT EXHIBITION - WHICH IS THE ONE PUBLIC EVENT THE SOCIETY IS RECORDED AS HOLDING EVERY YEAR. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE HEAVY: THIS IS A STATE-SANCTIONED MASS ORGANISATION OF SOVIET ORIGIN OPERATING UNDER THE COUNTRY'S LAWS AND ITS OWN CHARTER, IN A STATE WHERE THIS PAYLOAD HAS RECORDED THAT INDEPENDENT ASSOCIATIONS ARE EFFECTIVELY IMPOSSIBLE - ITS PROVINCE PLANS ARE APPROVED BY A CENTRAL BOARD, AND NOTHING RECORDED HERE SHOWS IT OPPOSING ANY PROJECT OR RAISING ANY GRIEVANCE. WHETHER IT STILL FUNCTIONS AT THE SCALE DESCRIBED, HOW MANY MEMBERS OR BRANCHES IT HAS, WHAT MEMBERSHIP COSTS AND HOW TO CONTACT A PROVINCE BRANCH WERE ALL NOT ESTABLISHED. THE DESCRIPTION COMES FROM AN ENCYCLOPAEDIA ENTRY AND A NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATION CATALOGUE PAGE DATED 2017, WITH THE LEGAL BACKDROP FROM AN INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATION'S STUDY AND A NATIONAL BIODIVERSITY STRATEGY, NONE OF THEM RECENT - SO ITS CURRENT ACTIVITY SHOULD BE TREATED AS UNVERIFIED. Read it with the union of industrialists and entrepreneurs, the Red Crescent's province branches, the chamber of commerce's expert examinations and the nationwide planting action recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: IMF — State of Eritrea
trackers.desc: IMF country page: Article IV assessments and the main public macro-fiscal data for Eritrea, whose national finances are otherwise largely undisclosed. Here you can trace how much Eritrea owes, to whom and on what terms.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: African Convention on Nature — check WHICH version binds your state
trackers.desc: THERE ARE TWO AFRICAN CONVENTIONS OF THIS NAME, AND CITING THE WRONG ONE IS THE AVOIDABLE ERROR HERE. The Algiers Convention was signed 15 September 1968, in force 16 June 1969. The revised Maputo Convention was adopted by the Assembly of the Union in Maputo on 11 July 2003 and entered into force 23 July 2016 — thirteen years later. THE OPERATIVE RULE: the 1968 Convention remains in force for those countries that have not ratified the 2003 revisions, so the two coexist and which binds your state depends on its ratification status. Commentary records only about 30 percent of African states had ratified Maputo. This entry does not assert which binds your state — the African Union publishes a Status List alongside the treaty text at au.int. Check it first. WHY THE DELAY IS AN ARGUMENT FOR IT: commentary attributes the thirteen years to the revised text containing strong provisions that could create accountability and also slow down social and economic development — a treaty resisted for creating accountability is one worth invoking where it applies. PROVISIONS TO KNOW: article XXXIX — no reservation may be made to this Convention, so a ratifying state takes all of it; article XL — withdrawal takes effect only one year after written notification; and no instrument of accession to the 1968 Algiers Convention may be deposited any longer, so the older text is closed to new entrants. THE OBJECTIVES ARE BROADER THAN USUAL: conservation, utilisation and development of soil, water, flora and fauna for present and future welfare, from an economic, nutritional, scientific, educational, cultural and aesthetic point of view — so a claim resting on cultural or aesthetic value has a treaty basis. BUT IF THE 1968 TEXT IS WHAT BINDS YOU, EXPECT LITTLE: parties were encouraged to cooperate but were not required to submit regular reports on implementation, and there were no financial mechanisms — no reporting trail, no funding attached. Article XLI also provides for interim secretariat arrangements, so check current institutional capacity. IUCN publishes a commentary on each provision in English and French.

trackers.name: National Union of Eritrean Women — 200,000+ members, offices in all six zobas, and a group-loan credit programme where the group itself is the collateral
trackers.desc: THE ONE MEMBERSHIP BODY WITH OFFICES EVERYWHERE: the NATIONAL UNION OF ERITREAN WOMEN (NUEW), established 1979 as a mass organisation of the liberation front and describing itself today as AN AUTONOMOUS NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATION, operates from headquarters in ASMARA and REGIONAL OFFICES ACROSS ALL SIX ZONES OF ERITREA, with a MEMBERSHIP EXCEEDING 200,000 WOMEN and funding from membership fees, grants, development projects and member-led fundraising. Published contacts place it at AV Gureito, Asmara, P.O. Box 239, tel +291-1-119304 / +291-1-115172, nuew@nuew.org. In a country where this file could verify no independent civil society, an organisation with 200,000 members and an office in every zoba is the only body a village woman can walk into — and it is where a community group without legal personality can be heard. THE CREDIT TERMS, WHICH ARE THE ACTUAL RESOURCE: NUEW is named among the country's few micro-credit providers alongside the SAVING AND MICROCREDIT PROGRAM (SMCP) and the youth and war-disabled unions. Its published product is A GROUP LOAN — IF ONE MEMBER FAILS TO REPAY, THE OTHER MEMBERS ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE DEBT, AND THIS MECHANISM ACTS AS THE COLLATERAL — with a THREE-CYCLE CEILING of 3,000, then 8,000, then 10,000 NAKFA, repayment within TWO YEARS for agri-business and ONE YEAR for service business, at a 12% FLAT interest rate. A group loan collateralised by the group is how people without land title borrow at all — and in Eritrea, where all land belongs to the state and you can own only the trees you plant, that is the financing route that actually matches the tenure. Start at cycle one; the ceiling rises as the group repays. Access to finance is recorded as limited by the small number of financial institutions and civil society organisations providing credit. WHO IT SUITS: Eritrean women's groups and village associations needing working capital for agri-business, nurseries or restoration work. CAVEATS: NUEW ORIGINATED AS A LIBERATION-FRONT MASS ORGANISATION and this file records no independent Eritrean civil society — read its autonomy claim in that light; contacts should be confirmed. For the seed to plant, Eritrea's NARI and ERCOE entry; for the baito closures and tree tenure, the village closures entry; for community project grants through four phases, the GEF Small Grants entry.

trackers.name: Department of Environment, Ministry of Land, Water and Environment — the EIA guidelines exist, the framework law never did, and there is nobody else to ask
trackers.desc: WHO TO APPROACH, AND WHY THIS IS WRITTEN AS AN ABSENCE: no verified Eritrean civil society organisation providing land defence, environmental litigation or community support could be found. The formal address is the Department of Environment within the Ministry of Land, Water and Environment, responsible for implementing national environmental policy. THE TWO INSTRUMENTS THAT DO EXIST: in March 1999 the department launched National Environmental Impact Assessment Guidelines and Procedures setting out EIA licensing procedures — described as similar in content to World Bank operational policies — later developed into National Environmental Assessment Procedures and Guidelines; and land is governed by the Land Reform Proclamation of 1994, under which the state allots land and grants usufruct rights, including leases for investment and agro-industrial activity. If a project near you is large-scale, the EIA licensing procedure is the only formal hook, and the land you hold is held as usufruct from the state, not as property. THE FINDING THE STATE PUBLISHED ABOUT ITSELF, which is the most useful thing here: an assessment prepared for the ministry recorded that the legal framework for environmental management had yet to be formalised, that this had been identified repeatedly over the years as a serious impediment to the effective functioning of the Department of Environment, and that drafting and redrafting of the environmental proclamation continued without resolution — with the justice ministry indicating the draft would not be acceptable in its current form. An EIA procedure without a framework law behind it is guidance, not enforceable duty; ask which instrument any decision is actually made under. WHO IT SUITS: Eritrean residents facing a large-scale project, as the only formal address available. CAVEATS: THIS IS A GOVERNMENT DEPARTMENT, NOT AN ALLY, in a country with no independent civil society sector recorded here, no complaints route and no free press. NO VERIFIED DEPARTMENTAL SITE EXISTS — this entry points at the state information service's account of the ministry. Published material is old; treat every detail as needing confirmation.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants in Eritrea — a country programme through FOUR operational phases, run with the Ministry of Land, Water and Environment, for community-based organisations
trackers.desc: WHERE TO APPLY FOR MONEY: the GEF SMALL GRANTS PROGRAMME in Eritrea, implemented by the UN development programme on behalf of the facility partnership and executed by the UN office for project services, TAILORED TO SUPPORT COMMUNITIES THROUGH COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS AND LOCAL NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS. THE FACT THAT MATTERS, GIVEN WHAT ELSE THIS FILE RECORDS ABOUT ERITREA: the country office has developed FOUR CONSECUTIVE COUNTRY PROGRAMME STRATEGIES across four operational phases, with the MINISTRY OF LAND, WATER AND ENVIRONMENT (MLWE) and the development programme holding significant roles in establishing and running it. Four completed phases means this is a functioning national window, not a paper one — which is more than can be said for the environmental framework law recorded elsewhere in Eritrea's file as never having been finalised. THE TERMS, PROGRAMME-WIDE: grants of UP TO USD 50,000 per project, averaging around USD 25,000, made DIRECTLY to local communities, community-based organisations and other non-governmental groups, for biodiversity, climate mitigation and adaptation, LAND DEGRADATION AND SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT, international waters and chemicals. Applications must show how the project meets the programme's criteria and how it aligns with the COUNTRY PROGRAMME STRATEGY (CPS) of your own country — read your national CPS before writing anything; it is the document your proposal is scored against. Eritrea's national adaptation programme names its own priorities as rangeland management in the lowlands, and community-based adaptation in pastoralism, forestry, water and agriculture — align to those. WHO IT SUITS: Eritrean community-based organisations and village groups with a land degradation, rangeland, forestry, water or agriculture project. CAVEATS: STATE THIS PLAINLY — Eritrea's civic space is among the most restricted on the continent, independent organising carries serious risk, and the programme runs WITH a government ministry; that shapes what can realistically be proposed. Grants fund environmental action, NOT litigation, land purchase or opposition to a state project. For the environmental framework and what does not exist, Eritrea's Department of Environment entry.

trackers.name: Eritrea — the expropriation DECISION cannot be challenged in court, but COMPENSATION goes to the High Court; community courts hear land disputes, and the only lawyers' association is in exile
trackers.desc: WHAT YOU CAN AND CANNOT TAKE TO COURT, AND KNOWING THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE OF IT HERE: under PROCLAMATION 58/1994, the Land Proclamation, ALL LAND IN ERITREA BELONGS TO THE STATE and a person may hold only USUFRUCTUARY RIGHTS on land allotted by the government. THE LIMIT: analysis of the proclamation records that THE GOVERNMENTAL DECISION TO EXPROPRIATE CANNOT BE CHALLENGED IN COURT. THE OPENING, IN THE SAME TEXT: Article 54 provides that where land is taken for national reconstruction or development projects, DISPUTES INVOLVING COMPENSATION SHALL BE ENTERTAINED BY THE HIGH COURT OF ERITREA — and the previous holder MAY PETITION THE HIGH COURT for compensation for any INSTALLATION OR IMPROVEMENT on the land. So do not spend your money contesting the taking; spend it on the compensation claim and on documenting every installation and improvement you built, because that is the half the law lets a court hear. WHERE A VILLAGE-LEVEL DISPUTE IS HEARD: village courts were established by Proclamation 25/1992 and COMMUNITY COURTS by Proclamation 132/2003, with first-instance jurisdiction over civil disputes including those involving IMMOVEABLE PROPERTY, appealable upward to the high courts and the Court of Final Appeal. WHO REPRESENTS YOU: there is NO BAR ASSOCIATION IN ERITREA — admission to practise is decided by the LEGAL COMMITTEE OF THE MINISTRY OF JUSTICE, CHAIRED BY THE MINISTER, which also handles discipline; practice comes in two layers, attorneys who may appear in Zoba courts only, and those who may also appear in the High Court and Appellate Court. Ask which layer your attorney holds before you plan an appeal. The ERITREAN LAW SOCIETY (erilaw.org) is the only professional association of Eritrean lawyers and states plainly that it was established in exile and operates from exile, because the political situation does not allow free and independent professional associations. WHO IT SUITS: Eritreans facing expropriation or a village land dispute, and anyone needing to know which grievance a court will hear. CAVEATS: STATE THIS PLAINLY — civic space is among the most restricted on the continent; the only lawyers' body is outside the country and there is no independent bar; nothing here is a legal aid service. For community environmental funding through four operational phases, Eritrea's GEF Small Grants entry.

trackers.name: Eritrea's village closures — the BAITOS close wooded hillsides for 5–10 years and reopen them; about 100,000 ha closed, and proclamation 155/2006 gives the trees to whoever plants them
trackers.desc: THE VILLAGE COUNCIL CLOSES THE HILLSIDE: from the late 1980s Eritrea has operated a system of CLOSURES of wooded hillsides and juniper forest, OPERATED BY LOCAL VILLAGE COUNCILS — THE BAITOS — IN PARTNERSHIP WITH GOVERNMENT. Such areas are CLOSED TO ACCESS for tree-cutting, grazing or agriculture for a number of years to allow forest regeneration, including some tree-planting, and to STABILISE SLOPES; after 5-10 YEARS THEY ARE REOPENED AND NEW CLOSURES ESTABLISHED ELSEWHERE. In total ABOUT 100,000 HECTARES have been closed in the Semenawi and Debubawi Bahri regions. The baito is the acquire instrument in a country with no land title — a village council decision, backed by government partnership, that takes ground out of use for a decade. And because the closure ROTATES rather than being permanent, it is negotiable ground rather than an expropriation, which is why it has survived where formal designation has not. THE TENURE RULE THAT GOES WITH IT: the FORESTRY AND WILDLIFE CONSERVATION AND DEVELOPMENT PROCLAMATION NO. 155/2006 states that TREE TENURE RIGHTS BELONG TO THE PERSONS PLANTING THE TREES ON USER-RELATED LANDS, AND OPENS OPPORTUNITIES FOR INDIVIDUALS AND/OR COMMUNITIES TO ESTABLISH SUSTAINABLE-HARVEST WOODLOTS — the same principle recorded for Burundi in this file, and the practical answer where the 1994 Land Reform Proclamation vests ALL LAND IN THE STATE with citizens holding USER RIGHTS. You cannot own the land; you can own the trees you plant on land you have user rights to. Plant, and record who planted. WHAT IS PROPOSED AND WHAT IS NOT YET REAL, STATED HONESTLY: SEMENAWI BAHRI — the GREEN BELT, about 1,300 km2 of tropical montane forest — REMAINS A PROPOSED NATIONAL PARK UNDER DE FACTO MANAGEMENT WITH NO FORMAL GAZETTEMENT; the four priority areas identified for protection are Semenawi and Debubawi Bahri (106,000 ha), Buri-Irori-Hawakil (867,000 ha), the Berasole estuary (13,100 ha) and the Gash-Setit Elephant Sanctuary (44,000 ha), none officially gazetted. A de facto protected area with no gazettement is exactly where a village closure carries the most weight — the baito's decision is the operative protection on the ground. WHO IT SUITS: Eritrean villages on wooded or eroding hillsides, and anyone planting trees under user rights. CAVEATS: A ROTATING ADMINISTRATIVE CLOSURE IN PARTNERSHIP WITH GOVERNMENT, NOT TENURE; civic space is severely restricted. For which grievance a court will hear — the expropriation decision cannot be challenged but COMPENSATION goes to the High Court — Eritrea's Land Proclamation entry; for community project money through four phases, the GEF Small Grants entry.

trackers.name: NARI's seed bank and ERCOE's environmental plan update — 6,300 seed accessions across 160 crop and tree species, and the body commissioned to rewrite the national environment plan
trackers.desc: WHERE THE SEED AND THE PLAN ARE KEPT: two Eritrean institutions are addressable by an ordinary person, and both matter to a village trying to hold ground. (1) THE NATIONAL AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE (NARI), a department of the agriculture ministry whose ORIGINS DATE TO 1910, MAKING IT ONE OF AFRICA'S OLDEST SCIENTIFIC INSTITUTIONS, employing 270 STAFF, ABOUT 80% OF THEM RESEARCHERS AND TECHNICAL PROFESSIONALS, with divisions covering NATURAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT RESEARCH alongside crops, livestock and agricultural engineering, and research conducted at NINE AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH STATIONS since 1997. ITS MOST USEFUL HOLDING: MORE THAN 6,300 SEED ACCESSIONS REPRESENTING ABOUT 160 SPECIES OF CROPS AND TREES. A national seed bank holding tree species is where you go when you must replant what a project or a drought removed — and in Eritrea, where tree tenure belongs to whoever plants, the seed is the first step in the only ownership claim available to you. (2) THE ERITREAN CENTER FOR ORGANIZATIONAL EXCELLENCE (ERCOE), established 10 August 2006, based in Asmara, which provides training, research and consultancy to ministries, REGIONAL ADMINISTRATIONS, parastatals, CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS and colleges — and which WAS COMMISSIONED BY THE MINISTRY OF LAND, WATER AND ENVIRONMENT to run a multi-sectoral project UPDATING THE NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT PLAN FOR ERITREA (NEMP-E), first prepared in 1995. The NEMP-E is the plan that originally identified Semenawi Bahri for national park status — so the body rewriting it is the body deciding what gets named for protection next. If your area has a case, that update is where it belongs. WHAT THE STATE HAS BEEN COUNTING: institutions working over five years have DOCUMENTED MORE THAN 5,000 SPECIES, presented at a national conference on fauna and flora in Asmara under the theme that conserving Eritrea's fauna and flora safeguards its future. WHO IT SUITS: Eritrean villages replanting closures or woodlots, and anyone wanting a protection case recorded in the national plan. CAVEATS: BOTH ARE STATE BODIES — ERCOE operates directly under the Office of the President — and this file records no independent Eritrean civil society; approach accordingly. For the baito closures and tree tenure, Eritrea's village closures entry; for what a court will and will not hear, the Land Proclamation entry; for community project money, the GEF Small Grants entry.

trackers.name: Human Rights Concern-Eritrea and the UN Special Rapporteur route — where a property-seizure record goes when the expropriation decision cannot be challenged at home
trackers.desc: WHERE A COMPLAINT GOES WHEN THE COURTS ARE CLOSED: this file records that in Eritrea the governmental decision to expropriate CANNOT BE CHALLENGED IN COURT — so the route for a record is external. HUMAN RIGHTS CONCERN-ERITREA (HRCE, hrc-eritrea.org) is an Eritrean human rights organisation based in the United Kingdom, founded by an Eritrean director, which MADE A SUBMISSION TO THE UNIVERSAL PERIODIC REVIEW mechanism of the UN Human Rights Council and has been used as a source by a national government's country-information service since 2013 for its documentation of MINERS' WORKING CONDITIONS in Eritrea and of Eritrean refugees abroad. There is also a standing UN SPECIAL RAPPORTEUR ON THE SITUATION OF HUMAN RIGHTS IN ERITREA, and states have publicly urged the government to IMPLEMENT A CONSTITUTIONAL, LEGAL AND INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR LAND AND PROPERTY RIGHTS, INCLUDING THOSE OF FOREIGN COMMUNITIES. Land and property rights are already named in the international dialogue on Eritrea — which means a documented seizure is evidence for a file that is already open, not a new argument you must establish from nothing. WHAT THE SEIZURE PRACTICE ACTUALLY IS, RECORDED IN COUNTRY REPORTING AND WORTH KNOWING BEFORE IT HAPPENS: the government has SEIZED PROPERTIES, BUSINESSES AND LIVESTOCK FROM THE FAMILIES OF DRAFT EVADERS WITHOUT DUE PROCESS or, in some cases, adequate restitution; HOMES AND BUSINESSES WERE RETURNED TO THE FAMILIES AFTER THE EVADERS TURNED THEMSELVES IN — BUT LIVESTOCK GENERALLY WERE NOT RETURNED. The pattern is that fixed property comes back and animals do not. If your family is at risk of this, the livestock is what you will lose permanently — count it, photograph it, and record the brands and numbers now, because that is the only claim that will ever be arguable. HOW A RECORD TRAVELS OUT: satellite radio stations operated by diaspora Eritreans reach listeners inside the country, and printing or disseminating publications without a permit is punishable. Diaspora radio is the one channel documented as reaching people inside Eritrea — for anything you cannot print at home. WHO IT SUITS: Eritrean families facing seizure, and Eritreans abroad documenting what happened to relatives' land and animals. CAVEATS: STATE THIS PLAINLY — these are external reporting routes, not remedies; contacting them carries risk, the government has directed harassment at diaspora members, and this file records no independent civil society inside Eritrea. For what a court WILL hear — compensation for installations and improvements — Eritrea's Land Proclamation entry; for the baito closures and tree tenure, the village closures entry; for group credit, the NUEW entry.

trackers.name: NCEW and NUEYS — Eritrea's workers' confederation with 26,000 members in five federations and the youth union with branches nationwide and abroad, plus a diaspora network that has raised over $100,000
trackers.desc: THE THREE UNIONS AND THE DIASPORA FUND — and this matters because this file has verified NO independent civil society inside Eritrea, which means the mass organisations are the only membership bodies an Eritrean can actually join: the NATIONAL CONFEDERATION OF ERITREAN WORKERS (NCEW), FOUNDED NOVEMBER 1979, HEADQUARTERED IN ASMARA, WITH AROUND 26,000 MEMBERS IN FIVE SUBSIDIARY FEDERATIONS AND A NAMED SECRETARY-GENERAL, AFFILIATED TO THE INTERNATIONAL TRADE UNION CONFEDERATION. Twenty-six thousand members in five federations, with an international affiliation, is the largest organised body in this file's Eritrean record. A trade union confederation with an international parent can raise a workplace or land question through a channel that leaves the country — and it is a body you join rather than petition. THE NATIONAL UNION OF ERITREAN YOUTH AND STUDENTS (NUEYS), FOUNDED 1978, AT KESKESE STREET 173 NO. 27, ASMARA, WITH BRANCHES THROUGHOUT ERITREA AS WELL AS AROUND THE WORLD TO SERVE THE DIASPORA, dedicated to improving the skills and awareness of Eritrean youth at regional, national and international levels, and a member of the ALL-AFRICA STUDENTS UNION. Branches throughout Eritrea is the phrase to act on: NUEYS has a presence outside Asmara, which almost nothing else in this file's Eritrean record does. If your village needs an organised body with young people in it, that is where one already exists. AND THE THREE WORK TOGETHER: NUEYS, NUEW AND NCEW HAVE COLLABORATED ON JOINT INITIATIVES — the youth union, the women's union and the workers' confederation acting as one. Three national unions that already run joint programmes can be approached as a bloc. A request carried by all three is not a complaint from one village; it is the organised population of the country asking. THE DIASPORA ROUTE, WITH NUMBERS RATHER THAN INTENTIONS: the ERITREAN DIASPORA NETWORK (EDN, eritreandiaspora.org), FOUNDED NOVEMBER 2011 BY THREE NAMED FOUNDERS in the Washington DC area, a community organisation DEDICATED TO MOBILISING ERITREAN DIASPORA COMMUNITIES IN A NON-PARTISAN MANNER AROUND ISSUES OF COMMON CONCERN, formed because its founders were ALARMED BY GROWING POLITICAL POLARISATION AND THE DISENGAGEMENT OF DIASPORA YOUTH, and committed to a community THAT RESPECTS DIVERSITY OF THOUGHT AND IS CAPABLE OF WORKING TOGETHER TO SOLVE COMMON PROBLEMS. SINCE LAUNCHING ITS SCHOLARSHIP FUND IN 2019 IT HAS RAISED MORE THAN $100,000 AND AWARDED SCHOLARSHIPS TO 54 STUDENTS. A hundred thousand dollars raised and fifty-four awards made is a diaspora organisation that actually moves money, and its non-partisan rule is what lets Eritreans of every view give to the same fund. For a community that cannot raise money at home, that combination — a stated non-partisan constitution and a track record of disbursing — is the model to copy. Eritrean communities abroad also convene SEMINARS ON DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMMES BASED ON SELF-RELIANCE, with a view to expanding social service provision. WHO IT SUITS: Eritreans seeking an organised body to join, and diaspora Eritreans wanting to fund something at home. CAVEATS: STATE THIS PLAINLY — NCEW, NUEYS AND NUEW ALL ORIGINATE AS LIBERATION-FRONT MASS ORGANISATIONS and this file records no independent civil society inside the country; read their autonomy in that light. For the group-loan credit terms, Eritrea's NUEW entry; for 6,300 seed accessions and the plan being rewritten, the NARI and ERCOE entry; for the baito closures and tree tenure, the village closures entry; for where a record goes when the courts are closed, the HRCE entry.

trackers.name: Eritrea Focus — an association of NGOs open to members inside Eritrea as well as the diaspora, its named member organisations, and the recorded reason domestic associations cannot form
trackers.desc: THE ASSOCIATION THAT TAKES MEMBERS FROM INSIDE THE COUNTRY — which matters because this file already records that in Eritrea the expropriation decision itself cannot be challenged in court: ERITREA FOCUS IS AN ASSOCIATION OF NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS, DESCRIBED AS A THINK TANK AND RESEARCH ORGANISATION WORKING WITH MULTIPLE NGOs — AND IT IS AN OPEN AND INCLUSIVE ORGANISATION THAT WELCOMES MEMBERS FROM ALL SECTIONS OF THE ERITREAN COMMUNITIES BOTH AT HOME AND IN DIASPORA, AS WELL AS NON-ERITREANS. Both at home and in diaspora is the operative phrase. An association of NGOs that will take a member from inside the country is a route to standing that does not require registering anything domestically — which, on this file's own Eritrean record, is the obstacle. Membership of an external association is not the same as a domestic association, but it is a place your account can be lodged and kept. WHO ELSE IS IN IT: its listed member and partner organisations include A GLOBAL CIVIL SOCIETY ALLIANCE, A FREEDOM OF EXPRESSION ORGANISATION, EMDHR, ONE DAY SEYOUM, AFRICA MONITORS, AND NAMED INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS AND ANTI-SLAVERY ORGANISATIONS. Africa Monitors and One Day Seyoum are Eritrean-run; the others are international. A body that puts both in one membership list is the bridge between a case inside the country and an organisation with international standing — ask which member covers land, displacement or forced labour and write to Eritrea Focus for the introduction rather than cold-writing all of them. AND THE DOCUMENTED REASON DOMESTIC ORGANISING IS SO HARD, WHICH BELONGS BESIDE ANY ADVICE TO FORM AN ASSOCIATION: THE FAILURE TO IMPLEMENT THE RATIFIED CONSTITUTION CONSTITUTED A MAJOR OBSTACLE IN THE GROWTH OF CIVIL SOCIETY ASSOCIATIONAL LIFE — THE CONSTITUTIONALLY GUARANTEED RIGHTS OF ASSOCIATION, WHICH COULD HAVE BOOSTED ASSOCIATIONAL LIFE, NEVER MATERIALISED. The right of association exists on paper in a constitution that was never brought into force. That is a precise, citable fact rather than a general complaint — and it is why nothing in this entry advises registering a new body inside the country. WHAT THE SAME ANALYSIS SAYS COMMUNITIES DO INSTEAD: ETHNICITY- AND RELIGION-BASED CIVIL SOCIETY GROUPS ARE TRYING TO PROTECT THE INTEREST OF THEIR COMMUNITIES, AND THERE MIGHT NOT BE AN INHERENT CONTRADICTION BETWEEN STANDING FOR ETHNIC AND RELIGIOUS INTEREST AND DEMOCRACY — INDEED, IN THE AFRICAN REALITY, SOMETIMES THE ONLY OPTION MARGINALISED GROUPS HAVE IS TO MOBILISE AND ORGANISE THEMSELVES. Where formal association is closed, the community bodies that already exist — the religious congregation, the lineage, the village assembly — are what remains. This file records the same pattern in Chad and the Comoros: the form that survives restriction is the one that predates it. THE STRUCTURE THAT ACTUALLY FUNCTIONS, WITH THE CITIES NAMED: the record of Eritrean diaspora organising names BOLOGNA IN ITALY AS THE BEATING HEART, ROME AS A HUB OF COORDINATION AND COMMUNITY MOBILISATION, KASSEL AS A STRONGHOLD OF YOUTH ACTIVISM AND FUNDRAISING, AND ACROSS NORTH AMERICA NEW YORK, WASHINGTON DC, CHICAGO, BOSTON, TORONTO AND OAKLAND AS CENTRES OF DEMONSTRATIONS, MEDIA OUTREACH, LOBBYING, COMMUNITY ORGANIZING AND SOLIDARITY WORK. Those are addresses, not history. If your family or your village has people in any of those cities, the organising capacity your community cannot build at home already exists there — and FUNDRAISING is named among what those centres do. The money and the lobbying are abroad; the account of what is happening has to come from home. WHO IT SUITS: Eritreans inside the country needing somewhere to lodge an account, and diaspora relatives who can act. CAVEATS: THESE ARE ADVOCACY AND RESEARCH BODIES, MOST OF THEM OUTSIDE THE COUNTRY, AND SEVERAL ARE OPENLY OPPOSED TO THE GOVERNMENT — contact carries risk inside Eritrea and this file says so plainly rather than pretending otherwise. For the UN Special Rapporteur route, Eritrea's Human Rights Concern-Eritrea entry; for the compensation route that IS available even though the decision is not challengeable, the expropriation entry; for hillsides closed by the village assemblies for 5–10 years, the baitos entry; for 200,000+ members with offices in all six zobas, the National Union of Eritrean Women entry; for 26,000 members in five federations, NCEW and NUEYS.

trackers.name: The CIVICUS Monitor — the civic space platform built by 20+ civil society research partner organisations — anyone can submit verified information and it is channelled to a researcher, with country ratings, a watch list and an early warning system
trackers.desc: ANYONE CAN SUBMIT, AND IT REACHES A RESEARCHER — that is the find, and it is stated in the platform's own methodology: ANYONE COULD SUBMIT VERIFIED INFORMATION TO THE RESEARCHERS, AND THE TEAM WILL CHANNEL THAT INFORMATION TO THE RESEARCH PARTNERS. No membership, no registration, no partner status required — a person with a verified account of what happened can put it into a global record that governments read. In a country where nothing can be published locally, that route out matters more than almost anything else in this file. WHO BUILDS IT, AND WHO YOUR INFORMATION REACHES: OVER 20 CIVIL SOCIETY RESEARCH PARTNERS ACROSS THE GLOBE, WHO PERIODICALLY PRODUCE CIVIC SPACE COUNTRY UPDATES — OFTEN BASED ON INFORMATION DIRECTLY OBTAINED FROM NATIONAL CIVIL SOCIETY BODIES — THAT UNDERGO RIGOROUS TRIANGULATION AND VERIFICATION PROCESSES BEFORE BEING PUBLISHED. Triangulation means they will look for the same fact from more than one source. So send more than one: a date, a place, a name, and anyone else who can confirm it. A single unverifiable claim goes nowhere; the same claim with two independent witnesses gets published. THE STATED PRINCIPLE, WHICH IS WHY THEY WANT TO HEAR FROM YOU: THE ADVANTAGE OF THE APPROACH IS THAT IT GIVES GREATER VOICE TO NATIONAL LEVEL CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS PRODUCING DATA ON CIVIC SPACE VIOLATIONS — ACTORS CLOSER TO THE SOURCE ARE BEST ABLE TO CONTEXTUALISE INFORMATION, AND POTENTIAL INCENTIVES FOR OVER-STATING RESTRICTIONS ARE OFFSET BY LOCAL ORGANISATIONS' INTEREST IN REMAINING CREDIBLE. They argue that local organisations are more accurate, not less, because their credibility is what they have. That is worth reading twice by anyone who has been told their account is too partisan to count. THE RATINGS: 198 COUNTRIES AND TERRITORIES RATED ANNUALLY IN FIVE CATEGORIES — OPEN, NARROWED, OBSTRUCTED, REPRESSED, OR CLOSED — ASSESSING THE RESPECT, IN LAW AND IN PRACTICE, OF THE FUNDAMENTAL FREEDOMS OF ASSOCIATION, EXPRESSION AND PEACEFUL ASSEMBLY, AND THE STATE'S DUTY TO PROTECT CIVIL SOCIETY — WITH REGULAR UPDATES PUBLISHED FOR A SUBSAMPLE OF AROUND 160 COUNTRIES WHERE RESEARCH PARTNERS PROVIDE CRUCIAL ON-THE-GROUND INFORMATION. IN LAW AND IN PRACTICE, separately. A country can have an association law that looks fine and a practice that is closed, and this measures both — which is the exact gap this file records again and again between a statute and a district office. THE INTERVIEWS, WHICH ARE A DOOR: ON A PERIODIC BASIS AND IN RESPONSE TO DEVELOPMENTS ON THE GROUND, RESEARCHERS CONDUCT STRUCTURED INTERVIEWS WITH COUNTRY-BASED CIVIL SOCIETY REPRESENTATIVES, AND ASSIGN AN ADDITIONAL COUNTRY CONSULTATION SCORE BASED ON THEM. Being interviewed changes a national score. If your organisation has direct experience of registration being refused or a meeting being broken up, ask the regional research partner to include you in the next consultation round. THE WATCH LIST AND THE ALARM: A REGULARLY UPDATED WATCH LIST OF COUNTRIES WHERE, BASED ON RESEARCH AND LOCAL ANALYSIS OF THE SITUATION, THERE IS A SERIOUS, IMMEDIATE OR EMERGING THREAT TO CIVIC SPACE — ALONGSIDE AN EARLY WARNING SYSTEM. EMERGING is the operative word. Getting a country onto the watch list before the crackdown is the point of an early warning system, and it is triggered by exactly the kind of small local incident nobody thinks worth reporting. WHAT THE COUNTRY PAGES CARRY: THE DAILY STORIES OF CIVIC SPACE — THE PHYSICAL ATTACKS ON ACTIVISTS, PROTESTS DISRUPTED, JOURNALISTS KILLED — COUNTRY AFTER COUNTRY, BASED ON UPDATES FROM CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS ALL OVER THE WORLD. THEY ALSO TELL THE GOOD STORIES WHEN THEY CAN FIND THEM — AND AS FAR AS POSSIBLE INCLUDE VIDEO, SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS AND QUOTATIONS FROM LOCAL ORGANISATIONS, TO BRING THEIR VOICES DIRECTLY IN. Video and social media posts are accepted material. A phone recording of a meeting being dispersed is evidence here, which means the footage sitting on somebody's handset has somewhere to go. ITS PURPOSE, IN ITS OWN WORDS: A TIMELY TOOL GROUNDED IN LOCAL REALITIES WHICH, IN THE HANDS OF CIVIL SOCIETY, COULD BE A POWERFUL WEAPON IN THE FIGHT BACK AGAINST CLOSING CIVIC SPACE — LETTING ACTIVISTS, CITIZENS, MEDIA, ACADEMICS AND DECISION-MAKERS TRACK THREATS AND FIND OUT IF FUNDAMENTAL FREEDOMS ARE BEING REALISED OR THREATENED. AND THE HONESTY, WHICH IS RARE ENOUGH TO QUOTE: THEY STATE THAT THE MONITOR ALONE WILL NOT CAUSE GOVERNMENTS AND CORPORATIONS TO STOP VIOLATING CITIZENS' RIGHTS, NOR COMPEL THE INTERNATIONAL COMMUNITY INTO ACTION — WHAT THEY AIM TO DO IS PROVIDE CIVIL SOCIETY, THE MEDIA AND DECISION-MAKERS WITH A RELIABLE, UPDATED PORTRAYAL OF THE REALITY OF CIVIC SPACE. A platform that tells you plainly it will not save you. Use it as evidence for the other routes in this file — a rating and a documented incident strengthen a grant application, a complaint and a submission all at once. AND THE CAVEAT ON READING THE RATINGS: THEY ARE CONCEPTUALISED AS BROAD BANDS, WHERE A VARIETY OF CIVIC EXPERIENCES CAN EXIST WITHIN ANY GIVEN RATING CATEGORY. WHO IT SUITS: African organisations and individuals documenting restrictions on organising, assembly or speech — especially where nothing can be published at home. CAVEATS: A RESEARCH PLATFORM, NOT A FUND OR A PROTECTION SERVICE, and submissions must be verifiable. For the route where a property-seizure record can reach a UN rapporteur, Eritrea's Human Rights Concern entry; for the association of NGOs open to members inside the country and in the diaspora, the Eritrea Focus entry; for the organisation that takes evidence communities gathered themselves, Libya's defender documentation entry.

trackers.name: FIG's Volunteer Community Surveyor Program — the volunteer surveyor programme that deploys young professionals to support land administration in Africa for free — plus the federation of 105 national surveyors' associations, its valuation-of-unregistered-land work, and its route in for countries with no association
trackers.desc: THERE IS A PROGRAMME THAT SENDS SURVEYORS FOR NOTHING — A VOLUNTEER COMMUNITY SURVEYOR PROGRAMME DESIGNED TO ENCOURAGE YOUNG SURVEYORS TO VOLUNTEER THEIR TIME AND SKILLS TO HUMANITARIAN AND ENVIRONMENTAL CAUSES — THE PROGRAM FACILITATES THE DEPLOYMENT OF YOUNG SURVEYORS WHO VOLUNTEER TO SUPPORT LAND ADMINISTRATION IN AFRICA AND ASIA. A surveyor is the professional a community almost never has and almost always needs: to fix a boundary on the ground, to contest a plan drawn by the developer's own consultant, or to check the area figure the compensation was calculated from. Their fees are why communities go without. Here is a programme whose whole purpose is deploying them to Africa for free — ask which countries it is currently active in before assuming it cannot reach you. WHAT THE FEDERATION IS: FOUNDED IN 1878, A UNITED NATIONS AND WORLD BANK RECOGNIZED INTERNATIONAL NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATION OF NATIONAL MEMBER ASSOCIATIONS, CADASTRAL AND MAPPING AGENCIES AND MINISTRIES, UNIVERSITIES AND CORPORATES FROM OVER 120 COUNTRIES — WITH 105 NATIONAL MEMBER ASSOCIATIONS AND OFFICIAL LANGUAGES ENGLISH, FRENCH AND GERMAN. A hundred and five national associations means there is almost certainly one in your country, with a members list. That is where the licensed surveyors are named — and a licensed surveyor's report is what a court will accept where a community's own sketch will not. THE PROFESSIONS IT COVERS, BROADER THAN PEOPLE ASSUME: SURVEYING, CADASTRE, VALUATION, MAPPING, GEODESY, GEOSPATIAL, AND QUANTITY SURVEYORS. VALUATION is the one to notice. When a company offers compensation, somebody valued your land, your trees and your buildings — and that valuation is a professional opinion that another professional can dispute. A valuer, not a lawyer, is who tells you the offer is a third of what it should be. THE CATEGORY FOR PLACES WITH NO ASSOCIATION AT ALL: CORRESPONDENTS — INDIVIDUALS IN COUNTRIES WHERE THERE IS NO ASSOCIATION OR GROUP OF SURVEYORS ELIGIBLE FOR MEMBERSHIP. So even where the profession is barely organised, one named individual may be connected to the federation. In the thinnest countries in this file that single correspondent is the entire professional network, and finding them is a short enquiry. ITS STATED AIMS, WHICH ARE THE ONES TO QUOTE: DEVELOPMENT OF PRO POOR LAND MANAGEMENT AND LAND ADMINISTRATION; PROMOTING THE ROLE OF SURVEYORS IN LAND ADMINISTRATION MATTERS TO THE PUBLIC AND STAKEHOLDERS; AND PROVIDING SOLUTION FUNCTIONALITY, RELIABLY, AFFORDABLY. PRO POOR LAND ADMINISTRATION is a stated aim of the world profession. A surveyor who declines to help a community on the grounds that it is not commercial work is departing from their own federation's purpose. THE FREE GUIDANCE AND ITS METHOD: A JOINT PUBLICATION WITH A DEVELOPMENT BANK PRESENTS AN INNOVATIVE, FLEXIBLE APPROACH ENDORSED BY BOTH, PROVIDING GUIDELINES FOR BUILDING FIT-FOR-PURPOSE LAND ADMINISTRATION SYSTEMS — ESPECIALLY IN LESS DEVELOPED COUNTRIES SEEKING TO ADDRESS INSECURE ACCESS TO LAND, INADEQUATE SHELTER AND SOCIAL INEQUITY — AND IT INCLUDES IDENTIFICATION OF PARCEL BOUNDARIES ON AERIAL IMAGERY. Boundaries identified on aerial imagery rather than by expensive ground survey. That is the same method this file records under Comoros for community land recording, and here it is endorsed by the surveying profession and a development bank together — which is what makes it arguable in front of a lands office that wants a formal survey nobody can pay for. THE CLAIM THAT MATTERS MOST: DRAWING ON IMPLEMENTATION EXPERIENCES IN NAMED AFRICAN COUNTRIES, DOCUMENTING LAND RIGHTS CAN BE ACHIEVED RAPIDLY, AFFORDABLY, AND INCLUSIVELY — WITH A CALL ON GOVERNMENTS AND COMMUNITIES TO DISMANTLE THE SYSTEMIC BARRIERS OF THE PAST. AND AS ONE CONTRIBUTOR PUTS IT: LAND IS FAR MORE THAN A COMMODITY — IT IS A FOUNDATIONAL RESOURCE FOR SURVIVAL, DIGNITY, AND STABILITY. RAPIDLY AND AFFORDABLY, said by surveyors. The usual answer to a community asking to be surveyed is that it would take years and cost more than the land is worth. That answer is contradicted by the profession's own publication, which you can print and bring. THE MAINTENANCE PRINCIPLE, WORTH HOLDING ANY PROJECT TO: LAND ADMINISTRATION PROJECTS ARE NOT ENDS IN THEMSELVES — THEY MUST DELIVER TANGIBLE SOCIAL, ENVIRONMENTAL AND ECONOMIC BENEFITS, AND REMAIN CAPABLE OF BEING UPDATED AND MAINTAINED OVER TIME. A register nobody can update is a snapshot that ages into uselessness. Ask, of any titling or mapping project offered to your community, who updates it in five years and at what cost. THE SCALE OF THE GAP, FROM ONE COUNTRY STUDY: REASONABLE ESTIMATES SUGGEST THERE ARE MORE THAN 5 MILLION LAND OCCUPATIONS THAT EXIST OUTSIDE THE FORMAL LAND TENURE SYSTEM — PEOPLE RESIDING ON COMMUNAL LAND, IN INFORMAL SETTLEMENTS, IN RESETTLED COMMUNITIES, IN OFF-REGISTER HOUSING SCHEMES, AND AS FARM DWELLERS, LABOUR TENANTS AND OTHER OCCUPANTS OF COMMERCIAL FARMS. Five million occupations outside the system in a single country with a good cadastre. Being unregistered is the ordinary condition, not a defect peculiar to your village. AND ITS OTHER WORK: LAND TOOLS FOR TENURE SECURITY INCLUDING A SOCIAL TENURE DOMAIN MODEL AND VALUATION OF UNREGISTERED LAND; A YOUNG SURVEYORS NETWORK TO HELP YOUNG PROFESSIONALS AT THE BEGINNING OF THEIR CAREERS WITH CONTACTS; AND A REGIONAL CAPACITY NETWORK FOR AFRICA. VALUATION OF UNREGISTERED LAND is a tool built for exactly the argument communities lose: that land with no title has no value to compensate. Somebody has written the method for valuing it. WHO IT SUITS: African communities disputing a boundary, a plan or a compensation figure, and anyone seeking a licensed surveyor or valuer they can afford. CAVEATS: THE VOLUNTEER PROGRAMME DEPLOYS THROUGH PROJECTS RATHER THAN ON REQUEST — approach the national association or the regional network. For the free system recording rights neither registered nor registerable, Comoros' entry; for the platform mapping community land against concessions, Mali's LandMark entry; for the national agency's own mandate, Liberia's Land Authority entry.

trackers.name: The free tactics toolbox built in Harare and Kampala by 100+ Global South organisers — with a Pan-Afrika edition, a feature for compiling your own, and the northern Ugandan land eviction it records among its cases
trackers.desc: THE TACTICS WERE WRITTEN DOWN BY PEOPLE WHO USED THEM HERE — WHY IT EXISTS, STATED PLAINLY: LOTS OF RESOURCES ON NONVIOLENT ACTION COME FROM THE GLOBAL NORTH, YET COURAGEOUS ACTIVISTS IN THE GLOBAL SOUTH ARE LIVING A WHOLE OTHER POLITICAL LIFE — THE IDEA WAS TO MERGE AN ANALYTICAL FRAMEWORK OF CREATIVE ACTIVISM TO THE LIVED REALITIES OF ACTIVISTS IN THE GLOBAL SOUTH. Most organising manuals a community is handed assume a functioning court, a free press and a police force that will not shoot. This one was assembled by people organising without any of those, which is why it is worth more than the general article on campaigning. WHO MADE IT AND WHERE: BEGINNING IN 2014, A TOOLKIT DEVELOPED WITH FRONTLINE SOCIAL MOVEMENT ACTIVISTS ACROSS THE GLOBAL SOUTH — OVER A HUNDRED ORGANIZERS FROM FIVE CONTINENTS CONTRIBUTED, MANY THROUGH FACE-TO-FACE JAM SESSIONS HELD IN SIX NAMED CITIES INCLUDING HARARE AND KAMPALA. THE METHOD OF MAKING IT IS ITSELF WORTH COPYING: IN EACH JAM SESSION, LOW-FIDELITY PROTOTYPES OF THE TOOLBOX WERE PRESENTED TO ACTIVISTS TO TAKE APART AND PUT BACK TOGETHER BASED ON THEIR NEEDS AND CHALLENGES. Bring a rough draft to be dismantled rather than a finished product to be approved. Any organisation designing something for a community can borrow that — and any community being consulted should ask for the rough version, because you cannot rebuild something already printed. THE UGANDAN LAND CASE IT RECORDS, WHICH IS EXACTLY THIS FILE'S SUBJECT: FEMALE ELDERS IN NORTHERN UGANDA INVOKED POWERFUL CULTURAL TABOOS BY REMOVING THEIR CLOTHES IN FRONT OF TWO GOVERNMENT MINISTERS WHO WERE ATTEMPTING TO EVICT PEOPLE IN A NAMED VILLAGE BY FORCE, GRAB THEIR LAND AND SELL IT TO A FOREIGN INVESTOR WHO WAS PLANNING TO USE THE TERRITORY FOR ELITE SPORTS GAME HUNTING. TO BLOCK THE MINISTERIAL CONVOY, THE COMMUNITY PUT UP A ROADBLOCK AND LOCAL WOMEN STRIPPED NAKED IN FRONT OF MINISTERS, SOLDIERS AND POLICEMEN — THE MOVE INVOKED A POWERFUL CULTURAL CURSE WHERE IT PROVOKES DEEP SHAME TO SEE A WOMAN THE AGE OF ONE'S MOTHER NAKED. The strongest weapon they had was one the ministers' own culture gave them, and it cost nothing. That is the general lesson under the specific act: before importing a tactic, ask what in your own tradition carries authority over the people you are facing. The elders knew something the security detail could not answer. AND NOTE WHO ACTED. Elder women, not the committee chairman. This file has recorded again and again that the person with standing to stop a convoy is not the person on the letterhead. THE STRUCTURE OF THE TOOLBOX: A SECTION OF STORIES — BRIEF NARRATIVES THAT ANALYSE DECISIVE BEHAVIOURS AND CAMPAIGNS UNDERTAKEN, ALONG WITH A CRITIQUE OF THEIR EFFECTIVENESS AND/OR DEFICIENCY — AND A SECTION OF TACTICS, FORMS OF CREATIVE ACTION TO BE EMPLOYED WISELY GIVEN THE UNIQUENESS OF A GROUP'S CIRCUMSTANCES, INCLUDING DIVESTMENT, CIVIL DISOBEDIENCE, SUBVERSIVE TRAVEL, MUSIC VIDEOS, FLASH MOBS, JAIL SOLIDARITY AND BLOCKADES. A CRITIQUE OF THEIR EFFECTIVENESS AND/OR DEFICIENCY. The cases come with what went wrong, which is the part missing from almost every campaign story a community is shown. And JAIL SOLIDARITY is a tactic with a name and a method — worth reading before anyone is arrested rather than after. ANOTHER RECORDED CASE AND THE PRINCIPLE IT ESTABLISHED: HEARING-IMPAIRED ACTIVISTS IN ZIMBABWE UNIFIED AROUND A COMMON CAUSE DESPITE DISPARATE ECONOMIC AND POLITICAL TRADITIONS, AND THEIR TRIUMPH AFFIRMED THAT THE PROBLEM OF DISABILITY DOES NOT RESIDE IN THE INDIVIDUAL, NOR IN THE IMPAIRMENT, BUT IN THE RESPONSE OF THE SOCIETY TOWARDS A PERSON WITH A DISABILITY. THE AFRICAN EDITION AND THE FEATURE THAT MATTERS MOST PRACTICALLY: IT HAS INSPIRED MANY OTHER COMPILATIONS THROUGHOUT THE GLOBAL SOUTH, FROM A PAN-AFRIKA EDITION TO A COUNTRY-SPECIFIC CRISIS-RESPONSE EDITION COMPILED USING A MY TOOLS FEATURE OF THE SITE. You can assemble your own edition. A committee can select the twenty entries that fit its situation, print them, and hand out something short in the local context rather than a book nobody finishes — and somebody already did exactly that for a national crisis. The Pan-Afrika edition is where to start. THE MERGE: IN WINTER 2020 BOTH TOOLKITS WERE COMBINED INTO A SINGLE ROBUST ONLINE TOOLBOX. AND WHAT IT IS FOR, IN ITS OWN WORDS: IT IS NOT A COFFEE TABLE OBJECT — IT IS A MANUAL, A TOOLKIT FOR CITIZENS WHO DREAM OF GRASSROOTS MOVEMENTS THAT ARE EFFECTIVE, CREATIVE AND COMPELLING; AND AN ACTIVIST AGENDA MUST BE WELL DESIGNED. WELL DESIGNED is the argument. A protest that happens because people are angry is not a plan; the difference between the two is what this toolbox is about, and it is free. WHO IT SUITS: African community committees planning what to actually do, especially where courts and press are closed to them. CAVEATS: A TOOLBOX OF TACTICS AND CASES, NOT FUNDING, LEGAL HELP OR PROTECTION — and several tactics carry real legal risk, so read it alongside the protection entries here. For security plans before acting, Djibouti's protection experts entry; for legal support if members are criminalized, Kenya's Strategic Legal Response Centre entry; for the ranked evidence on which methods actually work, this file's leverage material.

trackers.name: A4ID (Advocates for International Development) — a broker matching 53,000+ lawyers to 930+ organisations including small civil society groups — with a published three-word test for whether your project qualifies, a free legal health check of your own organisation, and an African environment tribunal among its cases
trackers.desc: TENABLE, VALUABLE, AND FINITE — THAT IS THE WHOLE TEST — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE ALREADY CARRIES A PRO BONO LEGAL BROKERAGE UNDER THE CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC AND A PRO BONO LEGAL SERVICE UNDER TOGO. BOTH ARE DIFFERENT ORGANISATIONS, NEITHER HOST IS SHIPPED HERE, AND WHAT DISTINGUISHES THIS ONE IS BELOW. THE THREE-WORD TEST, WHICH IS THE FIND: THE LEGAL PARTNERS CARRY OUT DUE DILIGENCE ON ALL ORGANISATIONS REQUESTING LEGAL ASSISTANCE TO CONFIRM THEIR PROJECTS ARE TENABLE, VALUABLE, AND FINITE. FINITE is the word that decides most refusals. A volunteer lawyer can review a contract, draft a constitution, research a statute or scope a case — they cannot adopt an open-ended land war. So split your need into a discrete piece of work with an end, ask for that, and come back for the next piece. This file has recorded communities asking for a champion and receiving nothing; asking for one finite task is what gets answered. WHO IS ELIGIBLE: DEVELOPMENT PARTNERS INCLUDE OVER 930 ORGANISATIONS — FROM LARGE INTERNATIONAL NGOs AND DEVELOPING COUNTRY GOVERNMENTS TO SMALL CIVIL SOCIETY GROUPS, SOCIAL ENTERPRISES, LAW SOCIETIES AND BAR ASSOCIATIONS. SMALL CIVIL SOCIETY GROUPS listed alongside governments. And LAW SOCIETIES AND BAR ASSOCIATIONS are eligible too — so a national bar that wants training or research can come through the same door, which connects directly to the continental lawyers' union filed under Algeria. THE PUBLISHED JOINING TEST: YOU SHOULD BE A CHARITY, NGO, OR SOCIAL ENTERPRISE WORKING TOWARDS ADVANCING AT LEAST ONE OF THE SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS — AND THE COMMUNITIES YOU WORK WITH SHOULD BE IN A LOW- TO MIDDLE-INCOME COUNTRY, EXCEPT IN CASES OF REFUGEES, CLIMATE AND RENEWABLE ENERGY, OR RACIAL JUSTICE. Every African country in this file clears the income test, and a land or water case advances more than one Goal. The exceptions listed also mean a climate or renewable-energy dispute qualifies wherever it happens — which covers the carbon and solar projects this file records arriving on community land. THE SCALE OF THE LEGAL SIDE: OVER 53,000 LAWYERS IN OVER 100 COUNTRIES, ACROSS MORE THAN 100 JURISDICTIONS — INTERNATIONALLY ACCLAIMED LAW FIRMS, BARRISTERS, LEGAL NETWORKS AND LEGAL ACADEMICS. HOW THE MATCHING ACTUALLY WORKS, AND WHY IT PRODUCES ANSWERS: IT CIRCULATES WEEKLY PRO BONO OPPORTUNITIES BASED ON DETAILED CONSULTATION WITH DEVELOPMENT ORGANISATIONS AS TO THEIR NEEDS — AND THROUGH AN OPT-IN MODEL, LAWYERS TAKE ON WORK AS AND WHEN THEY HAVE CAPACITY. Your request goes out weekly to tens of thousands of lawyers who choose it. Nobody is assigned and nobody is pressured, which is why the lawyer who accepts actually wants the case — and why a clearly scoped, interesting request outperforms a desperate one. THE SCOPING SERVICE, WHICH IS THE STEP BEFORE THAT: IT WORKS WITH DEVELOPMENT ORGANISATIONS TO IDENTIFY AND SCOPE THEIR LEGAL NEEDS ON A PROJECT, IN ORDER TO OBTAIN HIGH-QUALITY AND FREE LEGAL ADVICE. They help you work out what to ask for. If your organisation knows something is wrong but not which legal question that is, that scoping conversation is the service — and it is free. THE LEGAL HEALTH CHECK, WHICH IS THE FIND FOR A SMALL ORGANISATION: IT BROKERS LEGAL HEALTH CHECKS PERFORMED BY PRO BONO LAWYERS — DESIGNED TO IDENTIFY LEGAL WEAKNESSES IN AN ORGANISATION TO ENSURE ITS OPERATIONS ARE SUSTAINABLE, ASSESSING THE STRUCTURE, CAPACITY AND POTENTIAL LEGAL WEAK POINTS OF YOUR ORGANISATION. A free audit of your own constitution, registration and governance, by a commercial lawyer. This file has recorded organisations deregistered, dissolved or captured over exactly those weaknesses — and this is a discrete, finite request that fits their own test perfectly. If you ask for one thing from them, ask for this before the crisis, not during it. THE SUBJECT RANGE, WITH THE LAST ITEM NAMED EXPLICITLY: ADVICE CAN COVER A WIDE RANGE OF PROJECTS, FROM HUMAN RIGHTS DUE DILIGENCE, TO MICROFINANCE WORK, TO DISPUTE RESOLUTION, TO ENVIRONMENTAL LAW. THE AFRICAN CASE STUDIES THEY PUBLISH: RATIFICATION OF A PAN-AFRICAN MEDICAL REGULATORY BODY; THE WORLD'S FIRST FREE-OF-COST INTERNATIONAL SCHOOL FOR REFUGEE CHILDREN IN KENYA; AND ESTABLISHMENT OF THE FIRST ENVIRONMENT TRIBUNAL IN ETHIOPIA. A pro bono network helped build a country's first environment tribunal. That is the scale of thing this route can produce — not only advice to one organisation but the forum every later case will be heard in. THE OTHER WORK ON OFFER, SUITED TO CORPORATE IN-HOUSE TEAMS: LEGAL RESEARCH, POLICY REVIEWS, AND CAPACITY-BUILDING TRAINING FOR NGOs AND COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS. CAPACITY-BUILDING TRAINING FOR COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS is a named category. So a request to train your members on the law that governs their land is a fundable ask, not a favour. THE ORIGIN: FOUNDED IN 2006 AFTER A GROUP OF LAWYERS WERE BROUGHT TOGETHER BY A LARGE AID AGENCY AND SOUGHT TO PROVIDE PRO BONO LEGAL SUPPORT TO MARGINALISED COMMUNITIES IMPACTED BY A DISASTER. AND THE STATED DIAGNOSIS: A LACK OF ACCESS TO LEGAL EXPERTISE CAN REDUCE THEIR IMPACT — AND THE LAW CAN SOMETIMES BE AN IMPEDIMENT TO SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT. A CONTACT EMAIL FOR THE PRO BONO TEAM AND A DOWNLOADABLE INFORMATION PACK ARE PUBLISHED. WHO IT SUITS: African community and civil society organisations with a specific, bounded legal question — and any group that has never had its own constitution and registration checked. CAVEATS: PARTNERSHIP AND DUE DILIGENCE ARE REQUIRED, THE WORK MUST BE FINITE, AND THIS IS ADVICE RATHER THAN COURT REPRESENTATION — an unregistered village group will need a registered partner to apply. For the brokerage where lawyers have two weeks to volunteer, the Central African Republic's entry; for pro bono lawyers already carrying a hundred community cases a year, Togo's entry; for the continental lawyers' union, Algeria's entry.

trackers.name: Send them your photos and observations and they put them in an annual volume that reaches the World Heritage Committee before it drafts its decisions — they advise you on writing it, and they report from sites the UN itself cannot reach
trackers.desc: YOUR REPORT REACHES THE COMMITTEE BEFORE IT WRITES ITS DECISIONS — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S EGYPT ENTRY RECORDS A CAMPAIGN AIMED AT A WORLD HERITAGE BODY OVER EVICTIONS, ITS MOROCCO ENTRY THE INDIGENOUS TERRITORIES CONSORTIUM AND A CONSERVATION UNION HOST, AND ITS DJIBOUTI ENTRY THE COMPLAINT-OFFICE SCORING NETWORK. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE TIMING, WHICH IS THE FIND: SINCE 2015 IT HAS PUBLISHED AN ANNUAL REPORT COMPILING INDEPENDENT INFORMATION FROM CIVIL SOCIETY ON THE SITUATION AT WORLD HERITAGE PROPERTIES — INTENDED TO SUPPLEMENT THE REPORTS SUBMITTED BY THE STATES PARTIES, AND SENT TO THE MEMBER STATES OF THE COMMITTEE, TO THE CENTRE, AND TO THE ADVISORY BODIES IN TIME TO BE CONSIDERED FOR THEIR DECISIONS. TO SUPPLEMENT THE REPORTS SUBMITTED BY THE STATES PARTIES. Your government writes the official account of what is happening at the site on your land; this is the parallel account, delivered to the same desks, before the decisions are drafted. This file has recorded communities discovering an official report that describes their eviction as management — and this is the only route here that puts a competing document in front of the same body at the same moment. THE POINT IN THE CYCLE IT TARGETS: IT SHARES AND DISCUSSES THESE REPORTS WITH THE UN BODY AND ITS TECHNICAL ADVISORY BODIES — ONE FOR NATURAL SITES AND ONE FOR CULTURAL SITES — BEFORE THEY SET THE AGENDA AND DRAFT THE DECISIONS FOR THE NEXT ANNUAL SESSION. Before the agenda is set. Almost every route in this file operates after a decision; this one operates before, which is why an annual deadline is worth diarising even in a quiet year. THE OPEN CALL TO COMMUNITIES, WHICH IS THE WHOLE ENTRY PROCESS: SEND US REPORTS AND PHOTOS ABOUT YOUR OBSERVATIONS AND OF ANY PLANS OR ACTIVITIES WHICH COULD NEGATIVELY AFFECT WORLD HERITAGE SITES; START A LOCAL GROUP IN YOUR COMMUNITY TO MONITOR THE SITE OR SITES IN YOUR COMMUNE, MUNICIPALITY, REGION OR COUNTRY; EDUCATE YOURSELF AND OTHERS ABOUT YOUR SITE AND ITS MANAGEMENT; AND ALERT THE MEDIA AND POST ON SOCIAL MEDIA. Photos and observations. No standing, no registration, no lawyer — and PLANS OR ACTIVITIES WHICH COULD NEGATIVELY AFFECT means a proposed road, dam or concession counts before it is built. THE SUPPORT WITH WRITING: IT SUPPORTS AND ADVISES ITS GLOBAL NETWORK OF ACTIVISTS TO PREPARE REPORTS ABOUT SUCH THREATS. They help you write it. That is the difference between an invitation and a resource — and this file has recorded repeatedly that the barrier is not evidence but the form it must take. THE THREATS THE REPORTS DOCUMENT: UNCONTROLLED TOURISM, LARGE-SCALE INFRASTRUCTURE AND REDEVELOPMENT PROJECTS, EXTRACTIVE INDUSTRIES, CLIMATE CHANGE, WEAK GOVERNANCE, INADEQUATE PUBLIC PARTICIPATION, AND THE POLITICISATION OF HERITAGE — AFFECTING MONUMENTS, HISTORIC CITIES, CULTURAL LANDSCAPES, INDIGENOUS TERRITORIES AND NATURAL PROPERTIES, IN 58 CONTRIBUTIONS IN ONE EDITION. INDIGENOUS TERRITORIES and INADEQUATE PUBLIC PARTICIPATION named as reportable threats in their own right. A consultation that was never held is itself the subject of a report, not merely context for one. THE FINDING THAT REPORT DRAWS, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT TO BORROW: THE LOSS OF WORLD HERITAGE IS OFTEN GRADUAL RATHER THAN SPECTACULAR, RESULTING FROM ACCUMULATED PLANNING DECISIONS, INAPPROPRIATE INTERVENTIONS, INSTITUTIONAL INACTION, AND THE EXCLUSION OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES FROM DECISION-MAKING — WHILE SUCCESSFUL CAMPAIGNS AT TWO NAMED SITES ILLUSTRATE THE CAPACITY OF ORGANISED CIVIL SOCIETY TO INFLUENCE PUBLIC POLICY AND PREVENT IRREVERSIBLE DAMAGE. Gradual, by accumulated decisions. That is why a single permit that looks small is worth reporting: the case is built from the accumulation, and a documented sequence is far stronger than one grievance. THE ACCESS IT PROVIDES WHERE THE UN HAS NONE: SOME OF ITS REPORTS COME FROM SITES TO WHICH THE UN BODY ITSELF HAS NO OR ONLY LIMITED ACCESS — WITH A NORTH AFRICAN COUNTRY NAMED AMONG THE EXAMPLES. Where inspectors cannot go, community reports are the only record that exists. For communities in conflict-affected or closed areas, that is a rare route out. THE REACH AND THE RECORD: REPORTS ON 105 SITES ON ALL CONTINENTS AND ABOUT SITES IN 78 COUNTRIES; NEW CASES ADDED EVERY YEAR THAT WERE PREVIOUSLY UNKNOWN TO THE UN BODY; AND ATTENDANCE AT THE COMMITTEE'S SESSIONS EVERY YEAR SINCE 2015. PREVIOUSLY UNKNOWN. The deciding body did not know these cases existed until a community wrote them up. THE FORUM IT CONVENES TWICE A YEAR: AN INTERNATIONAL CIVIL SOCIETY FORUM, ONE IN FEBRUARY AT THE UN AGENCY'S HEADQUARTERS WHERE REPRESENTATIVES OF CIVIL SOCIETY AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLES PRESENT REPORTS AND DISCUSS THEM WITH THE CENTRE AND THE ADVISORY BODIES, AND A SECOND BEFORE THE COMMITTEE SESSIONS TO DISCUSS STRATEGIC QUESTIONS AND COORDINATE INTERVENTIONS. Community representatives in the room with the technical bodies that write the recommendations. And a second forum purely to coordinate what the movement will say — which is the organised half that this file records missing from most campaigns. THE PLENARY VOICE: IT PARTICIPATES IN THE SESSIONS WHERE IT LOBBIES FOR BETTER PROTECTION AND RAISES ITS VOICE IN THE PLENARY SESSIONS, LIVE-STREAMED GLOBALLY. WHAT PUBLICATION DOES FOR THE COMMUNITY ITSELF: THE REPORT IS READ BY OFFICIALS, EXPERTS, SCHOLARS AND JOURNALISTS WORLDWIDE, CAN BE DOWNLOADED FREE OF CHARGE, AND IS ALSO READ BY PEOPLE AT THE SITES, WHICH HELPS TO GIVE LOCAL COMMUNITIES ENCOURAGEMENT AND STRENGTH. AND THE MEMBERSHIP DISTINCTION, RECORDED HONESTLY: FORMAL MEMBERSHIP EXISTS ONLY FOR THE GERMAN ASSOCIATION AND REQUIRES A RECOMMENDATION FROM AN EXISTING MEMBER, THE ABILITY TO READ OFFICIAL DOCUMENTS IN GERMAN AND TO ATTEND ANNUAL MEETINGS IN BERLIN — SO FORMAL MEMBERSHIP IS KEPT TO A SMALL GROUP, WHILE THE NETWORK IS THE WIDER BODY THE ASSOCIATION MANAGES. You cannot join the association, and you do not need to. Contributing a report puts you in the network, which is the part that matters — and knowing the distinction saves an application that would only be refused. WHO IT SUITS: African communities at or near a World Heritage site facing infrastructure, extraction, tourism or eviction — including where the site designation is being used against them. CAVEATS: WORLD HERITAGE SITES ONLY, ANNUAL PUBLICATION CYCLE, AND IT LOBBIES RATHER THAN LITIGATES OR FUNDS — nothing here compels a state. For the campaign against evictions in the name of conservation, Egypt's entry; for the indigenous territories consortium, Morocco's entry; for the co-complainant route to the continental court, Seychelles' entry.

trackers.name: Community booklets in Swahili, Lingala and Malagasy, and meetings that put communities fighting the same plantation company in a room together — plus a West and Central African alliance spanning 10 countries and a booklet naming the tactics companies use to take land
trackers.desc: BOOKLETS IN SWAHILI, LINGALA AND MALAGASY, AND MEETINGS BETWEEN COMMUNITIES FIGHTING THE SAME COMPANY — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S BURKINA FASO AND MADAGASCAR ENTRIES NAME A FOOD RIGHTS ORGANISATION; ITS EGYPT ENTRY THE INTERNATIONAL PEASANT MOVEMENT; ITS ALGERIA ENTRY THE MOVEMENT FUNDER; AND ITS GABON, CAMEROON AND DR CONGO BUCKETS CARRY PLANTATION AND FOREST HOSTS OF THEIR OWN. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE AFRICAN LANGUAGES, WHICH IS THE FIND: SOME BOOKLETS AND VIDEOS OF PARTICULAR RELEVANCE FOR LOCAL COMMUNITY GROUPS ARE ALSO AVAILABLE IN LANGUAGES SPOKEN IN THESE LOCATIONS, LIKE SWAHILI, LINGALA AND MALAGASY — WITH AN ONLINE LIBRARY MAINTAINED SINCE 1996 IN SPANISH, FRENCH, ENGLISH AND PORTUGUESE. Swahili, Lingala and Malagasy. Not French and English with a promise of more — the actual working languages of Congo Basin, East African and Malagasy villages, in booklets and videos meant to be used at a meeting. This file has recorded language as the barrier that silently excludes more communities than any eligibility rule; this is one of the few resources in it that crossed that line properly. THE CONVENING WORK, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: NETWORKING AND FACILITATING THE GETTING-TOGETHER OF PEOPLE ACTIVE IN RESISTANCE PROCESSES FROM DIFFERENT PLACES WHERE COMMUNITIES FACE SIMILAR THREATS — FOR EXAMPLE, BRINGING TOGETHER COMMUNITY MEMBERS CONFRONTED WITH THE EXPANSION OF INDUSTRIAL OIL PALM OR TIMBER PLANTATIONS OR FOREST-CARBON PROJECTS. IN THESE MEETINGS OR FIELD VISITS, PEOPLE EXCHANGE EXPERIENCES, STRATEGIZE AND SHARE BOTH THE DIFFICULTIES AND INSPIRATIONS. Two villages facing the same company, in the same room. A company negotiates with each community separately and tells each one that the others have already agreed; the single most effective counter is the two communities comparing what they were told. FOREST-CARBON PROJECTS are named alongside plantations as a threat to be organised against. WHY THAT MATTERS, IN ITS OWN WORDS: EXCHANGES WITH COMMUNITY ACTIVISTS INVOLVED IN SIMILAR STRUGGLES HELPS TO BREAK THE ISOLATION AND MAKE VISIBLE THE EXTENT OF VIOLENCE THAT COMMUNITIES OFTEN FACE. THE AFRICAN ALLIANCE IT CARRIES: AN INFORMAL ALLIANCE AGAINST THE EXPANSION OF INDUSTRIAL MONOCULTURES IN WEST AND CENTRAL AFRICA HAS, FOR ALMOST 10 YEARS, CONNECTED GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS AND ACTIVISTS AND STRENGTHENED RESISTANCE AGAINST LAND GRABBING AND OTHER ATTACKS BY OIL PALM AND OTHER PLANTATION COMPANIES — WITH ACTIVISTS FROM 10 COUNTRIES GATHERING AT A GENERAL ASSEMBLY AND ISSUING A NAMED DECLARATION. INFORMAL is the point: no registration, no constitution, no membership fee. Ten years of an alliance that a community organisation can simply be part of, which is the opposite of the registered-body requirement that gates most of this file. THE COUNTRIES IN THAT ALLIANCE: GABON, NIGERIA, CAMEROON, SIERRA LEONE, CÔTE D'IVOIRE, REPUBLIC OF CONGO, DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, LIBERIA, GHANA AND UGANDA. Ten named countries. If yours is on that list, there are already organisations near you inside the alliance — and the fastest route in is through them rather than through the secretariat. THE BOOKLET THAT NAMES THE TACTICS: THE ALLIANCE LAUNCHED A NEW SUMMARY EDITION OF A BOOKLET ON THE TACTICS PALM OIL COMPANIES USE TO GRAB COMMUNITY LANDS — PROMISE, DIVIDE, INTIMIDATE, AND COERCE. Four words that describe the sequence a community is about to experience, written by the people who already have. Read it before the first meeting with the company, not after — and note DIVIDE, because the split it describes runs through the community itself. WHAT THE BULLETIN IS AND WHO WRITES IT: AN E-NEWSLETTER SINCE 1997 EXPOSING STRUGGLES, THREATS AND RESISTANCE IN FORESTS, AS WELL AS FALSE POLICY SOLUTIONS — ARTICLES ARE WRITTEN BY ACTIVISTS AND ORGANIZATIONS FROM ALL OVER THE WORLD, AND IT IS DISTRIBUTED TO MORE THAN 10,000 INDIVIDUALS AND ORGANIZATIONS IN 131 COUNTRIES. WHAT COUNTRY ORGANISATIONS USE IT FOR: THE BULLETIN IS INSTRUMENTAL IN THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PERMANENT LINKS WITH COUNTRY-BASED ORGANISATIONS, WHICH USE IT TO PUBLICISE THEIR STRUGGLES INTERNATIONALLY. You can write in it. Articles come from activists and organisations, and it reaches ten thousand readers in 131 countries — which is a publication route a community organisation can actually use, unlike the press this file records ignoring rural land disputes. WHO IT WAS SET UP AGAINST: IT HAS SUPPORTED FOREST PEOPLES RESISTING THE ENCLOSURE OF THEIR TERRITORIES BY DIFFERENT ECONOMIC INTERESTS AND EXTRACTIVE INDUSTRIES BEYOND TIMBER — PULP, OIL PALM, MINERALS, DAMS, OIL — IN MANY CASES ENDORSED BY BIG CONSERVATION NGOs. ENDORSED BY BIG CONSERVATION NGOs, said plainly. A community whose opponent is a conservation organisation rather than a company has very few places to turn in this file; this is one that names the problem rather than avoiding it. THE BASIS OF ITS ALLIANCES: INFORMAL ALLIANCES WITH COMMUNITY GROUPS AND SOCIAL MOVEMENTS BASED ON TRUST AND SHARED POLITICAL ANALYSIS, AND A COMMITMENT TO PRIORITIZE THE STRENGTHENING OF COMMUNITY STRUGGLES — WITH THE SECRETARIAT BASING ITS WORK ON WHAT IT HAS LEARNED FROM COMMUNITIES WHO LIVE WITH AND FROM THE FOREST IN AFRICA, ASIA AND LATIN AMERICA. THE MATERIALS IT PRODUCES: MATERIALS DESCRIBING COMMUNITY STRUGGLES IN AN ACCESSIBLE FORM AND RELEVANT LANGUAGES, FOCUSING ON INFORMATION PARTICULARLY RELEVANT FOR COMMUNITY ORGANISATIONS — PLUS CRITICAL ANALYSIS OF INTERNATIONAL INITIATIVES AND POLICIES PRESENTED AT GLOBAL CONFERENCES, AND BOOKS AND BRIEFINGS ON THE IMPACTS OF TREE PLANTATIONS. AND THE CARBON WARNING IT CARRIES, PLUS AN AFRICAN RULING IT REPORTS: A BULLETIN HIGHLIGHTING SEVERAL CASES WHERE THE EXPANSION OF CARBON PROJECTS HAS BECOME AN INTEGRAL PART OF THE EXTRACTIVIST MODEL — AND A REPORT THAT THE AFRICAN COMMISSION ON HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS MADE PUBLIC ITS HISTORIC RULING ON AN INDIGENOUS PEOPLE'S RIGHT TO RETURN TO THE ANCESTRAL HOME FROM WHICH THEY WERE VIOLENTLY EVICTED WHEN A NATIONAL PARK WAS CREATED IN EASTERN DR CONGO. A continental commission ruling that people evicted for a national park have a right to return.
