WHAT MADE IT WORK, AND THE TRANSFERABLE POINT: a forest-governance agreement process gave civil society a formal seat, and a programme officer records that AT THE START A FEW ORGANISATIONS ACTED IN A SCATTERED WAY, BUT FOR ABOUT FIVE YEARS THE NGOs HAVE COORDINATED AND ARE VERY ACTIVE ON THE GROUND; by 2018 SIX OF THE NINE internationally funded projects touching implementation of that agreement WERE LED BY MEMBERS OF THE CIVIL-SOCIETY PLATFORM, and participants say the process helped them gain more clarity. Six of nine donor projects run by the platform's own members is the measure to look for anywhere: it means money for forest work in CAR flows THROUGH national organisations rather than around them. WHO INSIDE IT KNOWS COMMUNITY FORESTS: the platform includes an EXPERT IN FORÊTS COMMUNAUTAIRES working within the MAISON DE L'ENFANT ET DE LA FEMME PYGMÉES (MEFP), the organisation this file already records for Aka and Bayaka communities — who described the arrival of civil society at the decision table as an advance he was astonished by. WHO IT SUITS: Central African villages, Aka and Bayaka communities and local associations seeking a national body that can carry a forest question upward. CAVEATS: A COORDINATION PLATFORM, NOT A SERVICE PROVIDER OR A FUNDER — and it operates in one of the poorest countries on earth, facing years of violence and conflict; its own account of the transformation says so. For the community forest granted INSIDE a logging concession, CAR's Lomba entry; for Aka and Bayaka work, MEFP; for donor-financed representation and the Bangui tribunal contact, the assistance judiciaire entry.

trackers.name: CIEDD with Action Verte and MEFP — the three-NGO partnership that carries out independent forest observation in CAR, with a published contact and a ministerial recognition number
trackers.desc: THE THREE NGOs THAT GO INTO THE CONCESSIONS: the CENTRE POUR L'INFORMATION ENVIRONNEMENTALE ET LE DÉVELOPPEMENT DURABLE (CIEDD), whose stated expertise is FORESTRY, THE RIGHTS OF FOREST PEOPLES, RURAL DEVELOPMENT, ANTI-CORRUPTION AND LOBBYING, works with the national civil-society platform to make proposals for integrating the rights and participation of forest peoples into CAR's reform processes. It carries out INDEPENDENT EXTERNAL OBSERVATION missions in collaboration with two partner NGOs — ACTION VERTE and the MAISON DE L'ENFANT ET DE LA FEMME PYGMÉES — chosen for their good knowledge of the forest sector and of the rights of local and indigenous communities in the Central African context. Three organisations that already travel together into logging areas to collect information are who a village asks to come and look — independent observation is a documented, funded activity here, not a favour. WHAT MEFP PUTS IN COMMUNITY HANDS, and the second item is the practical one: its fields of intervention include awareness and training on human rights; schooling, literacy and health education in Pygmy communities; FOREST GOVERNANCE AND COMMUNITY RIGHTS; PARTICIPATORY MAPPING OF COMMUNITY TERROIRS; and advocacy and lobbying for recognition of their rights — based at BAKOTA, with the published contact mefpcontact@yahoo.fr, and running work such as the reintroduction of GNETUM AFRICANUM into the forest by Pygmy communities. Participatory mapping plus a working email address is the combination this file records winning cases from Gabon to Guinea — and in CAR it is reachable from a phone. A DETAIL WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU WRITE: these are NGOs FORMALLY RECOGNISED BY DECISION OF THE MINISTER OF TERRITORIAL ADMINISTRATION AND DECENTRALISATION, with the recognition decision number printed on their reports. Ask any Central African organisation for its ministerial recognition number — it is what lets it stand in front of an administration, and the serious ones print it. Their observation work has been supported through a Congo Basin forest-governance programme with European and British funding. WHO IT SUITS: Central African forest villages, Aka and Bayaka communities, and anyone needing their terroir mapped or a concession observed. CAVEATS: PROJECT-FUNDED OBSERVATION AND ADVOCACY, NOT LITIGATION OR LAND PURCHASE; the security situation constrains movement. For the 30+ NGO umbrella and how six of nine donor projects run through it, CAR's Plateforme entry; for the community forest inside a logging concession, the Lomba entry; for donor-financed representation, the assistance judiciaire entry.

trackers.name: CAR's décret 15-463 and the Manuel de Procédure for community forests — the route the Lomba villages used, and the special authorisation without which they were not even eligible
trackers.desc: THE PROCEDURE AND ITS ONE FATAL GATE: community forests in the Central African Republic are governed by DÉCRET N°15-463 OF 3 DECEMBER 2015 FIXING THE MODALITIES OF ATTRIBUTION AND MANAGEMENT OF COMMUNITY FORESTS, applied through the MANUEL DE PROCÉDURE D'ATTRIBUTION DES FORÊTS COMMUNAUTAIRES (MPA) — the document a village must actually follow. Ask for the MPA by name at the forest administration: a written procedure manual is what lets a community check whether it is being told the real requirements or being stalled. THE GATE THAT DECIDES ELIGIBILITY, DOCUMENTED FROM THE PILOT SITES: SINCE 2016 FOURTEEN VILLAGES grouped in TWO PILOT SITES pursued community forests following the MPA — and the reporting states plainly that WITHOUT A SPECIAL AUTHORISATION OBTAINED THROUGH ADVOCACY BY CIVIL SOCIETY, THESE COMMUNITIES WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN ELIGIBLE AT ALL, BECAUSE THEIR CUSTOMARY TERRITORIES LIE WITHIN LOGGING CONCESSIONS; and that without civil-society accompaniment they probably would not have succeeded. If your customary land sits inside a concession, the answer is not that you are ineligible — it is that you need a special authorisation, and the precedent for winning one exists. That is the single most valuable sentence for any Central African village in this file. THE LIMIT AND THE ARGUMENT AGAINST IT: the MPA CAPS a community forest at 5,000 HECTARES, while customary territories are often far larger — needed for hunting and gathering — and subdividing them arbitrarily would GENERATE CONFLICT AND REDUCE VIABILITY by excluding resources, especially where a territory is SHARED BETWEEN SEVERAL VILLAGES; the recorded recommendation is that the limitation be lifted so communities can request forest areas MATCHING THEIR CUSTOMARY TERRITORIES. Where the cap will split a shared territory, say so in the file and put the neighbouring villages' agreement in writing — the objection is documented, and a shared claim is stronger than two truncated ones. WHO IT SUITS: Central African villages preparing a community forest application, particularly inside or beside a concession. CAVEATS: A PROCEDURE, NOT A GUARANTEE — the pilots needed both a special authorisation and continuous civil-society support to succeed. For the 15,000 ha result those villages achieved, CAR's Lomba entry; for who accompanies you, the CIEDD/Action Verte/MEFP entry and the Plateforme entry.

trackers.name: REPALCA and the CAR forest-people organisations — the indigenous and local peoples' network for forest ecosystems, the prefectures they cover, and OCDN's teak nursery and its recorded faults
trackers.desc: WHO SPEAKS FOR FOREST PEOPLES AND WHERE THEY ARE: REPALCA — the RÉSEAU DES POPULATIONS AUTOCHTONES ET LOCALES POUR LA GESTION DURABLE DES ÉCOSYSTÈMES FORESTIERS DE CENTRAFRIQUE — is focused on STRENGTHENING INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' INVOLVEMENT IN CONSERVATION AND REDD PROJECTS ON THEIR LANDS, PROMOTING RIGHTS-BASED COMMUNITY FOREST MANAGEMENT. A network whose stated purpose is indigenous involvement in REDD projects ON THEIR OWN LANDS is who a community talks to BEFORE a carbon project arrives — not after the agreement is signed. It works in Lobaye and Sangha-Mbaéré alongside MEFP. WHERE THE COMMUNITIES ARE, PREFECTURE BY PREFECTURE, because a letter needs an address: forest indigenous peoples — BaAka, Bayaka and Aka in OMBELLA-MPOKO and LOBAYE; BaMbenzele and Bayaka in MAMBÉRÉ-KADÉI and SANGHA-MBAÉRÉ — estimated at 15,000 to 20,000 people, organised in CAMPEMENTS OF 30 TO 70 PERSONS built on family, lineage and clan, with mobility as a deliberate practice. Mbororo Fulani pastoralists, recorded at about 39,299 people (2003 census) and around 14% of the rural population, are concentrated in OUAKA, MBOMOU and LOBAYE. OTHER NAMED CENTRAL AFRICAN ORGANISATIONS: GEN-RCA, which ran information and kit distribution around DÉKOA, KAGA BANDORO and MBAÏKI in the Lobaye; CNOPCAF, working with farmers' organisations; OFCA, whose awareness work targets indigenous groups of Ombella-Mpoko, Lobaye and other prefectures; and OCDN (ORGANISATION CENTRAFRICAINE POUR LA DÉFENSE DE LA NATURE), which with external funding REFORESTED 5 HA OF TEAK AT BOKOMA VILLAGE IN 2013 AND 2 HA IN 2016, AND TRAINED LOCAL PEOPLE TO ESTABLISH A NURSERY THAT PRODUCED OVER 12,000 TEAK SEEDLINGS. AND THE FAULTS ARE RECORDED BY THE GOVERNMENT ITSELF, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS USEFUL: THE NURSERY IS POORLY MAINTAINED, AND THE REFORESTATION OFTEN USED NON-NATIVE SPECIES. Twelve thousand seedlings from a village-run nursery proves the capacity exists; the poor maintenance and the non-native species are the two mistakes to design out. Budget for maintenance beyond the project, and plant what already grows there. WHO IT SUITS: Central African forest and pastoralist communities, especially in the named prefectures, and anyone facing a carbon or REDD proposal. CAVEATS: NETWORKS AND SMALL ORGANISATIONS, DONOR-FUNDED, in a country where movement is constrained. For Aka and Bayaka work and participatory mapping, CAR's MEFP entry; for independent forest observation, the CIEDD entry; for the 30+ NGO umbrella, the Plateforme entry; for the community forest procedure and its eligibility gate, the décret 15-463 entry.

trackers.name: CAR's Programme de Microfinancement — open calls for proposals to community-based organisations in the south-west, plus the USD 10m Bangui-periphery pilot and the Green Climate Fund country door
trackers.desc: WHERE THE MONEY IS AND WHICH ZONE IT COVERS — and this closes the one gap left in this file's Central African record, which had no funding route at all: the PROGRAMME DE MICROFINANCEMENT (PMF) DU FEM publishes an AVIS D'APPEL À PROPOSITION and offers opportunities TO COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS (ORGANISATIONS COMMUNAUTAIRES DE BASE), NGOs AND OTHER INSTITUTIONS to contribute to environmental protection. THE OPERATIONALLY DECISIVE FACT: IT INTERVENES IN THE SOUTH-WEST OF THE CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC, where populations have been informed of local, national and global environmental stakes — and the opportunities are offered TO ORGANISATIONS WORKING IN THAT SPECIFIC INTERVENTION ZONE. Check the zone before you write. A microfinancing programme with a defined intervention area will not fund a good proposal from outside it — and the south-west is where the Lobaye, Sangha-Mbaéré and Mambéré-Kadéi communities in this file's other entries actually are. WHAT AN APPLICANT MUST SHOW: microproject initiators must HAVE THE EXPERTISE to contribute to environmental protection in AT LEAST ONE of the named environmental domains, and must TAKE THE ARRANGEMENTS AND STRATEGIES NECESSARY TO INFORM OTHER POPULATIONS IN THE PROJECT ZONE. Informing your neighbours is a written eligibility condition, not a courtesy — so budget for the meetings and say in the application how you will hold them. THE LARGER DOORS: a forest-finance initiative's board allocated USD 10 MILLION for an INTEGRATED PILOT PROJECT FOCUSED ON BANGUI AND ITS PERIPHERY, identified in the CADRE NATIONAL D'INVESTISSEMENT REDD+, covering institutional strengthening to develop the capacities of LOCAL and national actors, territorial planning to reconcile economic development with the preservation of natural resources, and REDD+ measures with an emphasis on PAYMENTS FOR ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES to encourage sustainable land management. And the country maintains a GREEN CLIMATE FUND COUNTRY PROGRAMME DOCUMENT setting out priority project ideas to submit for financing (fvc.environnement.gouv.cf). Payments for environmental services means somebody intends to pay for the standing forest — ask who receives that payment where you live, and get the answer in writing before a scheme is designed around you. WHO IT SUITS: Central African community organisations in the south-west, and Bangui-periphery communities. CAVEATS: DONOR-FUNDED WINDOWS ON PROJECT CYCLES — confirm the current call and zone. For rights-based involvement in REDD projects on your own land, CAR's REPALCA entry; for the community forest procedure and its eligibility gate, the décret 15-463 entry; for who accompanies an application, the CIEDD and Plateforme entries.

trackers.name: FONACAR, the CAR national climate fund, plus the BaAka youth ecotourism association and the Maisons de Femmes that deliver legal support in named towns
trackers.desc: THE DOMESTIC FUND AND THE WOMEN'S HOUSES — and the fund matters because this file recorded that Central African community money runs through zone-restricted donor windows: THE FONDS NATIONAL POUR LA LUTTE CONTRE LE CHANGEMENT CLIMATIQUE EN RCA (FONACAR) HAS BEEN CREATED AND MADE OPERATIONAL, alongside THREE NEW POLICIES PUT IN PLACE TO LET THE COUNTRY MEET ITS CLIMATE COMMITMENTS and preparatory assistance under a Congo Basin forest initiative. A national climate fund that is operational is a domestic door, not a foreign one — ask FONACAR what it finances and who may apply before assuming the only money is the south-west microfinancing window. WHAT THE WORK ON THE GROUND PRODUCED, WITH THE COUNT: support to biodiversity and ecotourism development ON 12.20 HECTARES WITHIN THE DZANGA-SANGHA PROTECTED AREAS IN THE SOUTH-WEST, THROUGH WHICH 6,737 PEOPLE OF THE BaAka AND DZANGA-SANGHA COMMUNITIES — 4,737 OF THEM WOMEN — BENEFITED DIRECTLY FROM BIODIVERSITY AND ECOTOURISM MECHANISMS. Four thousand seven hundred women out of six thousand seven hundred beneficiaries is a ratio worth quoting: where a Central African conservation programme has been designed around community benefit, women have been the majority of who it reached. Ask for that ratio to be a condition of any scheme proposed to you. THE VEHICLE TO ASK FOR BY NAME: AN ASSOCIATION OF BaAka AND SANGHA-SANGHA YOUNG PEOPLE IS SUPPORTED WITH A TAILOR-MADE TRAINING PROGRAMME THAT ALLOWS THE BaAka PEOPLE TO TRANSFORM THEIR TRADITIONAL ACTIVITIES INTO SUSTAINABLE INCOME-GENERATING OPPORTUNITIES BY CREATING ECOTOURISM ACTIVITIES; a named young BaAka woman is recorded devoting herself to PRESERVING HER COMMUNITY'S ANCESTRAL TRADITIONS WHILE EMBRACING MODERNITY, with the record noting that THE BaAka PEOPLE HAVE DEVELOPED PARTICULAR CUSTOMS THAT PROTECT BIODIVERSITY. A youth association is the form that carries a hunting-and-gathering tradition into a paid activity without abandoning it. If your community's knowledge is the asset, the training goes to the young people and the association holds the income. AND THE STRUCTURE THAT PUTS A LAWYER IN A VILLAGE: MAISONS DE FEMMES — COMMUNITY SPACES ESTABLISHED IN TARGETED COMMUNITIES WHERE TEACHING USEFUL FOR WOMEN'S ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL INSERTION IS DELIVERED: CAPACITY BUILDING, TRAINING IN MANAGEMENT AND FINANCE, LEGAL SUPPORT (APPUI JURIDIQUE), AND PSYCHOSOCIAL AND MEDICAL SUPPORT — alongside a network to deliver financial services so women can diversify their income sources. The programme ran OVER 18 MONTHS FOR AN ESTIMATED 4,600 BENEFICIARIES IN BANGUI, BOCARANGA AND KAGA BANDORO, implemented by international AND NATIONAL NGOs. Legal support inside a village building, alongside the finance training, is the closest thing to a permanent legal presence outside Bangui in this file's Central African record — ask whether a Maison des Femmes exists in your prefecture, and if one is being set up, ask that the appui juridique component covers land. ALSO NAMED: the MAISON DE L'ENFANT ET DE LA FEMME PYGMÉES (MEFP) sits in a national civil society advocacy platform alongside a women leaders' network, and civil society organisations across Bangui, Obo, Bria and Ndélé convene local workshops. WHO IT SUITS: Central African communities in the south-west, BaAka and Sangha-Sangha young people, and women in Bangui, Bocaranga or Kaga Bandoro. CAVEATS: DONOR-DELIVERED PROGRAMMES ON FIXED CYCLES — confirm what is still running. For participatory mapping and a working email, CAR's MEFP entry; for indigenous involvement before a REDD project arrives, REPALCA; for the community forest procedure and the special authorisation, the décret 15-463 entry; for the south-west grant zone, the Programme de Microfinancement entry.

trackers.name: SPONG, the approved-NGO register inside CAR's planning ministry — with its Bangui street address and telephone — plus the international NGO coordination committee's member list and a country NGO directory
trackers.desc: THE APPROVED-NGO REGISTER, AND WHO HOLDS IT: THE SECRÉTARIAT PERMANENT DES ONG EN CENTRAFRIQUE (SPONG) SITS AT THE MINISTÈRE DE L'ÉCONOMIE, DU PLAN ET DE LA COOPÉRATION INTERNATIONALE, RUE MARTIN LUTHER KING, BANGUI, BP 696, TELEPHONE +236 21 61 78 11, WITH A PUBLISHED EMAIL — AND IT PUBLISHES LES ONG AGRÉÉES OEUVRANT EN RÉPUBLIQUE CENTRAFRICAINE. The register of APPROVED NGOs, held inside the planning ministry, with a street address and one telephone number. Two uses, and both are practical. First: if an organisation offers to speak for your community, check whether it is on the agréées list — approval is a ministry act, not a self-description. Second: if you are forming a body, SPONG is where approval is processed, so ask it what agrément requires before you spend money on paperwork. And note where it sits: NOT in the interior ministry but in the ministry of ECONOMY, PLAN AND INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION. That placement tells you how the Central African state classifies NGOs — as development actors inside the planning system. Address your letters accordingly. THE SECOND LIST, WHICH TELLS YOU WHO IS ACTUALLY OPERATING WHERE: A COMITÉ DE COORDINATION DES ONG INTERNATIONALES EN CENTRAFRIQUE HAS COORDINATED HUMANITARIAN ASSISTANCE SINCE 2014, FAVOURING THE EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION BETWEEN ITS MEMBERS FOR A NEUTRAL AND IMPARTIAL ACTION — AND IT PUBLISHES ITS MEMBER ORGANISATIONS WITH A DESCRIPTION OF EACH AND THE PREFECTURES IT WORKS IN. Prefecture-level presence, published. In a country where reaching anybody is the difficulty, a list that says which organisation works in which prefecture is worth more than a list of names — look up your prefecture first and write to whoever is already there. A COUNTRY-LEVEL NGO DIRECTORY ALSO LISTS ORGANISATIONS WORKING IN THE CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC WITH DETAILS OF THEIR WORK FOCUS, so the two can be cross-read. THE PRECEDENT WORTH KNOWING, BECAUSE IT SHOWS CENTRAL AFRICAN CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISING ITSELF RATHER THAN BEING ORGANISED: SOME 200 NGOs AGREED TO SET UP A TEAM TO COORDINATE ALL ACTIVITIES UNDERTAKEN BY THEIR ORGANISATIONS, AT A MEETING DUBBED THE SOCIAL FORUM HELD OVER FOUR DAYS IN BANGUI — AND THE FORUM ADOPTED A DECLARATION CREATING A COORDINATING BODY AND CALLED FOR A GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF CIVIL SOCIETY TO ELECT THE EXECUTIVE BOARD, with the forum chaired by the head of a Central African human rights observatory. Two hundred organisations, a four-day forum, a written declaration, and then an elected executive rather than an appointed one. That sequence — convene, declare, elect — is the template for a national coalition, and it happened in Bangui. If somebody tells you Central African civil society cannot coordinate itself, that is the counter-example, and the human rights observatory that chaired it is a body a community with a rights complaint can approach directly. WHO THE INDIGENOUS-PEOPLES CONSULTATIONS ACTUALLY RUN THROUGH, FOR ANY PROJECT SAFEGUARD PROCESS: a documented project consultation brought together ministry cadres for agriculture and environment, a municipal development officer, a technical director, a project environmentalist, and the civil society organisations MEFP and REPALCA as the bodies involved in the social questions of indigenous peoples — alongside the PRÉFET of the relevant prefecture, who located the indigenous communities within the project's zone of influence and made suggestions on implementation. The préfet is recorded as the person who identifies where indigenous communities sit relative to a project. If your community is being left out of a project's zone of influence, that is the office whose map decides it — and MEFP and REPALCA are the two organisations the process itself expects to be consulted, so their absence from a consultation is a defect you can name. WHO IT SUITS: Central African communities checking an organisation's standing, groups seeking agrément, and anyone needing to know who works in their prefecture. CAVEATS: REGISTERS AND COORDINATION BODIES, NOT FUNDERS OR LITIGATORS, and CAR's operating environment changes fast — confirm before relying. For 30+ Central African NGOs in one platform, CAR's Plateforme GDRNE entry; for participatory mapping and a working email, MEFP; for indigenous involvement before a REDD project arrives, REPALCA; for the community forest procedure, the décret 15-463 entry; for open calls to community groups, the Programme de Microfinancement entry; for the national climate fund and the Maisons de Femmes, the FONACAR entry.

trackers.name: TrustLaw (Thomson Reuters Foundation) — the free brokerage that finds your organisation a law firm working for nothing — post the request, lawyers have two weeks to volunteer, you choose which team, and if nobody offers they keep looking until somebody does
trackers.desc: POST THE REQUEST; LAWYERS HAVE TWO WEEKS TO VOLUNTEER — THIS IS A GLOBAL PRO BONO MARKETPLACE, A FREE SERVICE FOR BOTH LAW FIRMS AND NGOs, WHICH CONNECTS LAWYERS IN MORE THAN 175 COUNTRIES WITH ORGANISATIONS THAT REQUIRE PRO BONO LEGAL ASSISTANCE. THE EXACT PROCESS, WHICH IS WORTH READING AS A SEQUENCE BECAUSE MOST PEOPLE ASSUME IT IS HARDER: POST A REQUEST FOR FREE LEGAL ASSISTANCE ON THE ONLINE PORTAL, THEN SPEAK WITH THEM ABOUT YOUR LEGAL NEEDS. ONCE FINALISED, THE LEGAL MEMBERS WILL BE ABLE TO SEE YOUR REQUEST. LAWYERS IN THE NETWORK HAVE TWO WEEKS TO VOLUNTEER TO HELP. THEN THE OFFERS OF SUPPORT ARE SENT TO YOU, AND YOU SELECT WHICH LEGAL TEAM YOU WOULD LIKE TO WORK WITH — AND IF HELP HAS NOT BEEN FOUND BY THE END OF THE TWO-WEEK PERIOD, THEY WILL KEEP LOOKING UNTIL THEY HAVE FOUND FREE LEGAL ASSISTANCE. You choose the lawyer, not the other way round. That inversion matters: this file has recorded communities accepting whichever advocate was assigned and discovering later whose interests he served. Here you receive several offers and pick. And there is no rejection at the end of the two weeks — they keep searching, which means a request that gets no takers is still live rather than closed. THE SCALE BEHIND IT: MORE THAN 4,000 MEMBERS, INCLUDING OVER 800 LAW FIRMS AND IN-HOUSE LEGAL TEAMS BRINGING THE EXPERTISE OF AROUND 120,000 LAWYERS TO OVER 3,800 NGOs AND SOCIAL ENTERPRISES — EXTENDED BY PARTNERSHIP TO MORE THAN 1,500 LAW FIRMS ACROSS 205 COUNTRIES — AND IT HAS GENERATED OVER $54 MILLION IN FREE LEGAL SUPPORT ACROSS 170 COUNTRIES. Fifty-four million dollars of lawyer time given away. The constraint on a community fighting a project is almost never the absence of law; it is the cost of someone who reads it. This is the largest single answer to that in existence. AND THE MISSION LINE THAT SPEAKS DIRECTLY TO THIS FILE'S COUNTRIES: ITS MISSION IS TO CONNECT PEOPLE AND SPREAD THE PRACTICE OF PRO BONO AROUND THE WORLD — PARTICULARLY TO COUNTRIES WHERE PRO BONO IS NOT TRADITIONALLY PRACTISED. Where free legal work is not a local custom, this network is trying to create one. So a request from a country with no pro bono tradition is not an imposition on them — it is the point of the programme. WHAT YOU CAN ASK FOR, AND THE SECOND HALF IS THE UNDERUSED PART: OPERATIONAL LEGAL ISSUES INCLUDING GENERAL COMMERCIAL ADVICE, INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND EMPLOYMENT MATTERS — THROUGH TO LARGE MULTI-JURISDICTIONAL PROGRAMMES SUCH AS RESEARCHING LAWS ACROSS A NUMBER OF JURISDICTIONS, OR ASSISTING WITH AN IN-DEPTH ANALYSIS OF LAWS — AND RESEARCH PROJECTS THAT CAN BE USEFUL TO FULFIL A SOCIAL MISSION AND BE USED AS A TOOL FOR ADVOCACY. RESEARCHING LAWS ACROSS A NUMBER OF JURISDICTIONS, done free by a large firm. If you need to know how six countries regulate a mining concession, or what your own law actually requires of a consultation, that is a research project a firm will take on — and the output is yours to use as an advocacy tool. This file has recorded again and again that communities lose because nobody has read the statute; this is who reads it. ALSO NAMED, AND WORTH ASKING FOR EARLY: ESTABLISHING A LEGAL STRUCTURE, TRADEMARK REGISTRATION, EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENTS, COMPLIANCE WITH DATA PROTECTION, TAX EXEMPTIONS, COLLABORATION AGREEMENTS AND THE USE OF IMAGES. LEGAL STRUCTURE and TAX EXEMPTIONS are the two that unlock everything else in this file. Registration is the gate almost every funder here puts in front of you — and here is free legal help to get through it. WHO MAY APPLY: NGOs OR SOCIAL ENTERPRISES WORKING ANYWHERE IN THE WORLD, WORKING DIRECTLY TOWARDS A SOCIAL MISSION — AND ORGANISATIONS THAT ARE PARTLY FUNDED BY GOVERNMENT AGENCIES ARE ALSO WELCOME TO APPLY FOR MEMBERSHIP. APPLICATIONS ARE ACCEPTED ON A CONTINUOUS BASIS, AND SUCCESSFUL APPLICANTS ARE NOTIFIED WITHIN TWO WEEKS. PARTLY GOVERNMENT-FUNDED ORGANISATIONS ARE WELCOME, which quietly admits a great many African community organisations that receive a district or ministry contribution and assume it disqualifies them elsewhere. WHO DECIDES WHAT GETS TAKEN: SELECTING PROJECTS TO SUPPORT IS ENTIRELY AT THE DISCRETION OF THE LAWYER, AND EACH WEEK LAWYERS RECEIVE AN EMAIL LISTING PRO BONO PROJECTS AVAILABLE ACROSS THE GLOBAL NETWORK. Your request lands in a weekly email read by thousands of lawyers looking for something worth doing. Write the request so it is the one they want — concrete, specific, with a real deadline and a plain statement of what is at stake. AND THE ARM FOR THE PEOPLE COVERING YOU: A LEGAL SERVICE FOR INDEPENDENT MEDIA OFFERS TAILORED SUPPORT TO EQUIP JOURNALISTS, NEWSROOMS AND MEDIA-FREEDOM NON-PROFITS TO COUNTER LEGAL THREATS AND STRENGTHEN THEIR RESILIENCE. The reporter covering your case can be sued into silence, and there is a legal service for exactly that. Tell them it exists. WHO IT SUITS: any African community organisation, association or social enterprise that needs a lawyer and cannot pay one. CAVEATS: MEMBERSHIP IS FOR ORGANISATIONS RATHER THAN INDIVIDUALS, and lawyers choose which requests to take — so the quality of the written request matters. For assistance judiciaire financed by international partners, the Central African Republic's legal aid entry; for the network of local lawyers and rapid legal support when defenders are criminalized, Kenya's Strategic Legal Response Centre entry; for the litigation expenses fund covering filing fees and experts, South Africa's EDLC entry.

trackers.name: The grantmaker whose published rules say you need no bank account, no ID and no registration — €35,000 average grants renewed for up to ten years, applications accepted by video or audio, and decisions made by activists
trackers.desc: NO BANK ACCOUNT, NO ID, NO REGISTRATION — THE PUBLISHED RULE, WORD FOR WORD: YOU DON'T NEED AN ORGANISATIONAL BANK ACCOUNT, RESIDENCE PERMIT, OR OFFICIAL ID TO APPLY; YOUR GROUP DOESN'T NEED TO BE REGISTERED. AND FOR ITS MAIN FUND: IN ADDITION TO FUNDING REGISTERED, FORMAL ORGANISATIONS, WE ARE OPEN TO FUNDING INFORMAL OR UNREGISTERED GROUPS OF ACTIVISTS, AS WELL AS NETWORKS OR COALITIONS. Registration is the gate that shuts nearly every funder in this file to a village committee, and a bank account is the second gate behind it. Here both are explicitly waived. If your group has been told for years that it must first become a legal entity before anyone will fund it, this is the counter-example to keep. WHO IT PRIORITISES: SMALLER AND EMERGING GROUPS THAT ARE DOING CRITICALLY IMPORTANT WORK BUT HAVE LIMITED ACCESS TO FUNDING — INCLUDING GROUPS WITHOUT PAID STAFF OR OFFICE SPACE, OR WITH A YEARLY BUDGET BELOW €50,000. NO PAID STAFF, NO OFFICE is a qualification here rather than a weakness. Most funders read those two facts as incapacity. THE MONEY AND HOW LONG IT LASTS: THE AVERAGE GRANT UNDER ITS MAIN FUND IS €35,000; FIRST-TIME ANNUAL GRANTS ARE MADE WITH THE INTENTION OF RENEWING THEM FOR MULTIPLE YEARS, AND IT TYPICALLY SUPPORTS PARTNERS FOR UP TO TEN YEARS — MOST GRANTS ARE MULTI-YEAR AND UNRESTRICTED, AND 83% OF ITS FUNDING GOES DIRECTLY TO GRASSROOTS GROUPS. Ten years. A land fight in this file routinely outlasts three funding cycles and dies in the gaps between them. A funder that expects to be there in a decade is a different kind of ally from one running a two-year project. THE FREEDOM CLAUSE: THE SELF-LED GROUPS WE SUPPORT HOLD POWERFUL RADICAL WISDOM — WE HONOUR THEIR KNOWLEDGE AND ASSESSMENT OF THEIR OWN SITUATIONS, THAT IS WHY THEY HAVE THE FREEDOM TO USE OUR GRANTS AS THEY SEE FIT. AND THE REPORTING: REQUIREMENTS ARE LIGHTER AND BUILT AROUND LEARNING AND DIALOGUE, NOT COMPLIANCE, WITH GRANTEES RECOGNISED AS EXPERTS IN THEIR OWN STRUGGLES AND SOLUTIONS. Reporting eats the time of small groups more than any other funder demand. Ask any prospective funder what their report looks like before you accept — the answer tells you how much of your year the grant will cost you. THE LED-BY TEST, WITH THE WORKED EXAMPLE THEY PUBLISH: GROUPS MUST BE FOUNDED, LED AND/OR RUN BY PEOPLE WHO BELONG TO THE COMMUNITIES WHOSE RIGHTS THEY SEEK TO ADVANCE — THE PEOPLE WHOSE RIGHTS ARE AT STAKE ARE THE DECISION MAKERS. IF A GROUP FOCUSES ON THE RIGHTS OF WOMEN WITH DISABILITIES, THEY SHOULD BE THE ONES TO DECIDE ON THE GROUP'S ACTIVITIES AND HOW THE FUNDS ARE ALLOCATED; THE SPOKESPERSONS AS WELL AS THOSE BEING PAID SHOULD BE WOMEN WITH DISABILITIES; PEOPLE WITHOUT DISABILITIES CAN CONTRIBUTE, BUT CANNOT LEAD THE GROUP. SPOKESPERSONS AND THOSE BEING PAID. That is the sharpest definition of community-led in this entire file, and it is a test worth applying to yourself before a funder applies it to you: who speaks for the group in public, and who draws a wage from it. THE APPLICATION FORMATS, WHICH REMOVE A BARRIER ALMOST NOBODY ELSE ADDRESSES: YOU CAN SUBMIT A WRITTEN APPLICATION FORM, A VIDEO RECORDING FORM, OR AN AUDIO RECORDING FORM — AND IF YOU FEEL MORE COMFORTABLE USING ANOTHER LANGUAGE, SEND A MESSAGE TO A PUBLISHED EMAIL AND THEY WILL SUPPORT YOU. You can apply by talking. An elder who holds the whole history of the boundary but cannot write a proposal can record it instead — and this file's translation entry names who can help with the language. WHO DECIDES: AT THE CENTRE OF ITS PARTICIPATORY GRANTMAKING SYSTEM IS A GLOBAL ADVISORY NETWORK — A DIVERSE GROUP OF FEMINIST ACTIVISTS BASED IN DIFFERENT GEOGRAPHIC AREAS, FROM DIFFERENT CONSTITUENCIES, WITH DIVERSE THEMATIC EXPERTISE — WHO PLAY A VITAL ROLE IN DECISION-MAKING FOR EACH FUND. Activists decide, not programme officers. That changes what a good application looks like: describe the situation as you would to a peer, not as you imagine a donor wants to hear it. THE SCALE AND WHAT IT COVERS: OVER 130 INITIATIVES FUNDED GLOBALLY EACH YEAR, AND €140 MILLION AWARDED IN OVER 60 COUNTRIES TO SELF-LED GROUPS AND MOVEMENTS ADVANCING ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE, DEMOCRACY, HUMAN RIGHTS AND GENDER EQUITY — WITH ONE NAMED GRANTEE HELPED TO DENOUNCE ENVIRONMENTAL VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN. ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE named among the things it funds, and ENVIRONMENTAL VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN as a worked case. A women's group resisting a mine is squarely inside this, not stretching to fit. THE STATUS NOTE, RECORDED HONESTLY AS FOUND: IT ANNOUNCED THAT ITS MAIN FUND WILL NOT BE ACCEPTING NEW APPLICATIONS IN 2026 FROM ORGANISATIONS IT IS NOT ALREADY FUNDING — A DECISION MADE TO GIVE EXISTING GRANTEE-PARTNERS LARGER, MULTI-YEAR GRANTS AND MORE INTENSIVE ACCOMPANIMENT DURING A PERIOD OF HEIGHTENED REPRESSION AND BACKLASH. Check what is open before planning around it. And note what the closure was for: deepening support to existing partners rather than spreading thinner. That is a funder behaving well, and it is worth knowing which funders do that when repression rises. AND THE FUND FOR FUNDS, IF YOUR ORGANISATION IS ITSELF A GRANTMAKER: A SOLIDARITY FUND OF €30,000 TO €40,000 CREATED BY WOMEN'S FUNDS FOR WOMEN'S FUNDS, FOR INTERNAL DEVELOPMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY RATHER THAN REGRANTING — USED FOR LEADERSHIP TRANSITIONS, INTERNAL LEARNING AND EVALUATION SYSTEMS, COLLECTIVE CARE AND WELLBEING SUPPORT FOR STAFF, FINANCIAL RESILIENCE STRATEGIES TO REDUCE DEPENDENCY ON A SMALL NUMBER OF DONORS, AND IMPROVING DIGITAL SECURITY — AND APPLICANTS CAN ALSO BECOME REVIEWERS. Money for leadership transitions and staff wellbeing. Organisations in this file collapse when the founder leaves or burns out far more often than when they lose a case. WHO IT SUITS: African women-led and self-led community groups, including unregistered ones with no bank account, resisting land takings or environmental harm. CAVEATS: THE GROUP MUST BE LED BY THE PEOPLE WHOSE RIGHTS ARE AT STAKE, AND THE MAIN FUND'S NEW-APPLICANT WINDOW WAS CLOSED FOR 2026 — check current status. For the rapid-response fund with three application windows, Egypt's and Mauritania's entries; for the advisor-nominated grants where 40% are first-time, Ghana's African Women's Development Fund entry; for the connector that routes communities to the right small grants fund, Burkina Faso's entry.

trackers.name: Training, equipment and a free phone app that turns a fisher into a witness — photograph the vessel with its number showing, and the geotagged report goes to a database governments use to seize catches, with a toolkit now built for 15 countries
trackers.desc: PHOTOGRAPH THE BOAT WITH ITS NUMBER SHOWING — adjacency declared first: TWO FOREST ORGANISATIONS ARE ALREADY HOSTS IN THIS SAME BUCKET; NEITHER CONCERNS FISHERIES, AND NEITHER HOST IS SHIPPED HERE. THIS FILE'S SÃO TOMÉ ENTRY COVERS COMMUNITY MARINE MANAGEMENT DESIGN — NOT THE SURVEILLANCE EQUIPMENT AND EVIDENCE ROUTE BELOW. THE APP AND EXACTLY HOW IT IS USED, WHICH IS THE FIND: A MOBILE APPLICATION ALLOWS ARTISANAL FISHERS TO GATHER GEOTAGGED FOOTAGE OF ILLEGAL FISHING AT SEA — WHEN A VESSEL IS SPOTTED FISHING ILLEGALLY, OR DAMAGING CANOES OR GEAR, THE USER SIMPLY OPENS THE APP AND TAKES A PHOTO OF THE BOAT WITH ITS NAME OR IDENTIFICATION NUMBER SHOWING AND RECORDS THE LOCATION. THE APP THEN UPLOADS THE REPORT TO A CENTRAL DATABASE WHERE THE EVIDENCE CAN BE USED BY THE GOVERNMENT TO CATCH AND SANCTION THE PERPETRATORS. IN ONE COUNTRY ALONE IT HAS HAD OVER 700 REPORTS SUBMITTED BY LOCAL FISHERS — CHEAP, READILY AVAILABLE AND PRACTICAL TECHNOLOGY. THE NAME OR NUMBER SHOWING is the whole instruction. A photograph of a trawler is nothing; a photograph of a trawler with its identification legible, time-stamped and located, is evidence a fisheries ministry can act on. That is a one-sentence training any community can pass on tonight, and 700 reports from one country's fishers show it is not theoretical. THE TRAINING AND EQUIPMENT: FOR OVER 10 YEARS IN WEST AFRICA THEY HAVE PROVIDED TRAINING AND EQUIPMENT TO COMMUNITIES TO DOCUMENT AND REPORT ILLEGAL FISHING — THEN LINKED THAT GRASSROOTS INFORMATION WITH NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL NETWORKS, AND WORKED WITH GOVERNMENTS TO SANCTION OFFENDING VESSELS AND SEIZE CATCHES. THE FOUR DESTINATIONS THE EVIDENCE GOES TO, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH COPYING FOR ANY INDUSTRY: THE INFORMATION IS RELAYED TO STAKEHOLDERS AND DECISION-MAKERS IN THE VESSEL'S FLAG COUNTRY, THE COUNTRY WHERE THE FISHING OCCURRED, THE COUNTRY WHERE THE CATCH WILL BE UNLOADED, AND IN THE EUROPEAN UNION. Four jurisdictions from one photograph. Your own government may be unwilling or unable to act, but the flag state, the port state and the buyer's market are three other doors — and this file records the same logic under the home-country complaint and supply-chain entries. Whoever the offender is, ask where the product lands. THE ORIGIN, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT AGAINST WAITING FOR SCALE: FROM HUMBLE ORIGINS IN A NAMED WEST AFRICAN COUNTRY WITH ONE BOAT AND ONE FISHERMAN, THE NETWORK HAS NOW EXPANDED ACROSS WEST AFRICA, THE HORN OF AFRICA AND SOUTH EAST ASIA. ONE BOAT AND ONE FISHERMAN. Start with whoever is willing. THE STRUCTURE THEY HELP BUILD: COLLABORATIVE MANAGEMENT ASSOCIATIONS, GIVING LOCAL COMMUNITIES A VOICE IN MANAGING THEIR FISHERIES AND THE TOOLS TO ENSURE TRANSPARENCY IN BOTH FISHERIES MANAGEMENT AND AT SEA — COMMUNITY MANAGEMENT ASSOCIATIONS TO GIVE LOCAL COMMUNITIES MORE CONTROL AND OWNERSHIP OVER THEIR FISHERIES. THE RESULTS RECORDED: WORK IN TWO NAMED WEST AFRICAN COUNTRIES SHOWED RAPID RESULTS, WITH COMMUNITY INFORMATION LEADING TO WIDESPREAD CRACK-DOWN ON ILLEGAL FISHING VESSELS, INCLUDING LEGAL REFORMS, DELISTING AND CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS. Community photographs led to criminal proceedings and to laws being changed. Evidence gathered by people with no training and no standing moved both. THE TOOLKIT NOW AVAILABLE BEYOND THOSE COUNTRIES: WITH EUROPEAN UNION FUNDING THEY HAVE DEVELOPED A GLOBAL TOOLKIT FOR PARTICIPATORY FISHERIES GOVERNANCE, ALLOWING THESE TRIED AND TESTED APPROACHES TO BE IMPLEMENTED ACROSS 15 COUNTRIES IN THE GLOBAL SOUTH — TAKING THE KEY ELEMENTS OF THE WEST AFRICAN WORK AND CREATING TARGETED TRAINING MATERIALS FOR FISHING COMMUNITIES. The method has been packaged deliberately so communities outside their programme countries can run it. Ask which fifteen, and whether yours is one. THE LAND-SIDE WORK MOST PEOPLE MISS, AND IT IS DIRECTLY THIS FILE'S SUBJECT: THEY PROMOTE THE FAIR ALLOCATION OF TENURE RIGHTS TO PROTECT FISHERS' LANDING SITES FROM THE ENCROACHMENT OF TOURISM AND OTHER INDUSTRIAL ACTIVITIES. The beach a community lands its canoes on is land, and it is taken by hotels and ports as readily as farmland is taken by plantations. A fishing community's tenure fight is usually about the shore, not the sea — and it is winnable with the land-recording tools filed elsewhere here. THE SCALE, WITH FIGURES TO QUOTE: AROUND 37% OF ALL FISH CAUGHT IN THE REGION IS CAUGHT ILLEGALLY; IN ONE COUNTRY THE SECTOR EMPLOYS OVER 2.7 MILLION PEOPLE AND BRINGS OVER US$500 MILLION A YEAR, WHILE LANDINGS OF SOME KEY SPECIES HAVE DECLINED BY AS MUCH AS 80% OVER TWO DECADES; IN ANOTHER, SMALL-SCALE FISHERIES ACCOUNT FOR UP TO 10% OF GDP. UP TO 10% OF GDP from small-scale fishing. When a ministry treats artisanal fishers as marginal, that figure is the answer — they are a tenth of the national economy. THE CONSEQUENCE THEY DOCUMENT HONESTLY RATHER THAN HIDE: FACED WITH DECLINING INCOMES AND FOOD INSECURITY, MANY OF THESE FISHERS ARE BEING DRIVEN TO ENGAGE IN ILLEGAL ACTIVITIES THEMSELVES. An organisation admitting the people it defends also break the rules, and explaining why. That honesty is what makes their evidence credible to a government — and it is the posture to take about your own community rather than claiming perfection. AND THE FILM TRAINING: THEIR FILM UNIT HAS TRAINED ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDERS TO USE VIDEO, DRONES AND CAMERAS TO DOCUMENT THREATS TO THEIR NATURAL WORLD. WHO IT SUITS: African coastal and fishing communities losing catch to industrial or foreign vessels, and losing landing sites to tourism and industry. CAVEATS: PROGRAMME COUNTRIES ARE LIMITED AND THE APP IS DEPLOYED THROUGH THEM — the toolkit is the route for everyone else. For the 30-day closure that raised village income 136%, São Tomé's entry; for making footage court-ready, Niger's video-as-evidence entry; for the fishers' own national network, Madagascar's MIHARI entry.

trackers.name: A mining standards body where six of twelve board seats belong to labour, communities and NGOs — with a published sample letter asking a company to submit to independent audit, a complaints email, and the right to challenge an assessment's scope
trackers.desc: THERE IS A SAMPLE LETTER ASKING THE COMPANY TO SUBMIT TO AN AUDIT — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ANGOLA ENTRY COVERS A PALM OIL INDUSTRY BODY'S COMPLAINT SYSTEM AND THE FREE GUIDE TO IT — A DIFFERENT INDUSTRY AND A DIFFERENT STANDARD; ITS GUINEA-BISSAU ENTRY THE COMPARATIVE MINING LAW ATLAS; ITS BENIN ENTRY THE OPEN MINING SITE DATA. A NAMED ZIMBABWEAN ENVIRONMENTAL LAW ASSOCIATION IS A MEMBER OF THE BODY BELOW AND ALSO APPEARS IN THIS FILE'S EGYPT ENTRY AS AN UNNAMED CORE TEAM MEMBER. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE SAMPLE LETTER, WHICH IS THE FIND: A PUBLISHED SAMPLE LETTER TO MINING COMPANIES ENCOURAGING THEM TO UNDERGO AN AUDIT. A ready-made letter a community committee can adapt and send. It costs a stamp, it is written in the language the company's head office understands, and a refusal is itself informative — a company that declines an independent audit while claiming responsible practice has said something on the record. THE GOVERNANCE SPLIT, WHICH IS WHY THE LETTER CARRIES WEIGHT: GOVERNED BY A MULTI-SECTOR BOARD OF SIX LABOR, COMMUNITY AND NGO SEATS AND SIX FINANCE, MINING AND DOWNSTREAM BUYER SEATS — GOVERNED EQUALLY BY NGOs, AFFECTED COMMUNITIES, LABOR UNIONS, MINING COMPANIES, PURCHASING COMPANIES AND INVESTORS. NO SINGLE TYPE OF ORGANIZATION OR INDUSTRY CAN MAKE DECISIONS THAT DO NOT WORK FOR OTHER STAKEHOLDER GROUPS. Half the board is not industry. This file has recorded certification schemes written and governed by the companies they certify; a fifty-fifty split with communities and unions on one side is a different instrument, and worth checking for in any standard offered to your district. THE OTHER COMMUNITY RESOURCES PUBLISHED ALONGSIDE: A DOCUMENT ON HOW COMMUNITIES AND THOSE WHO SUPPORT THEM CAN USE THE SYSTEM; A GUIDE ON HOW TO FILE A COMPLAINT AND THE ISSUES RESOLUTION PROCEDURE; AND A DOCUMENT ON HOW FREE, PRIOR AND INFORMED CONSENT IS ADDRESSED IN THE STANDARD — WITH SPANISH VERSIONS PUBLISHED ALONGSIDE THE ENGLISH. SPANISH BUT NOT FRENCH OR PORTUGUESE, which is the gap to name when asking them for materials: francophone and lusophone African mining communities are not served by the current translations, and asking is how that changes. THE PUBLISHED COMPLAINTS ADDRESS: A DEDICATED EMAIL ADDRESS FOR SUBMITTING A COMPLAINT, AND A SEPARATE GENERAL INFORMATION ADDRESS. THE SCOPE-CHALLENGE RIGHT, WHICH IS THE MOST OVERLOOKED PROVISION HERE: IF ANY STAKEHOLDER BELIEVES THAT THE SCOPE OF AN ASSESSMENT IS LIKELY TO RESULT IN ISSUES OR IMPACTS BEING OVERLOOKED OR MISSED, THEY HAVE THE OPPORTUNITY TO PROVIDE THAT INPUT THROUGH THE COMPLAINTS AND GRIEVANCE PROCESS. You can object to what the audit will look at, before it looks. This file has recorded impact assessments drawn narrowly enough to miss the river, the grazing route or the downstream village — and here the boundary itself is contestable, which is a far cheaper intervention than disputing the findings afterwards. WHAT THE STANDARD IS: A 400-PAGE STANDARD DEVELOPED OVER TEN YEARS IN CONSULTATION WITH MORE THAN 100 COMPANIES AND ORGANIZATIONS, ENABLING ASSESSMENT OF SOCIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE AT MINE SITES GLOBALLY, APPLICABLE TO ALL SIZES OF INDUSTRIAL-SCALE MINES AND ALL MINED MATERIALS EXCEPT ENERGY FUELS — WITH A SEPARATE CHAIN OF CUSTODY STANDARD TRACKING ASSESSED MATERIAL FROM THE MINE SITE TO THE END USER. EXCEPT ENERGY FUELS. Coal, oil and gas are outside it entirely, which decides immediately whether this route is available to you. THE STEP-BY-STEP DESIGN AND ITS RATIONALE, STATED HONESTLY: STEP-BY-STEP, NOT PASS/FAIL — MINES AT ANY LEVEL ARE ENCOURAGED TO PARTICIPATE. RATHER THAN ONLY REWARDING THE SMALL GROUP ALREADY ACHIEVING BEST PRACTICES, LOWER TIERS OF ACHIEVEMENT ARE RECOGNISED IN HOPES THAT MORE MINES WILL COME INTO THE SYSTEM AND GAIN SOME MARKET BENEFITS WHILE CONTINUING TO MAKE PROGRESS. A mine can be inside the system while performing badly. So the fact that a company participates proves nothing on its own — read the tier and the audit report, not the logo. THE MEMBERSHIP OBLIGATIONS: MEMBERS MUST TAKE CONCRETE ACTIONS — MINING SECTOR MEMBERS MUST HAVE AT LEAST ONE SITE ACHIEVING A NAMED PERFORMANCE LEVEL, AND PURCHASING MEMBERS AGREE TO ENCOURAGE MINING COMPANIES TO ENGAGE THROUGH THIRD-PARTY ASSESSMENT OF THEIR MINE SITES. PURCHASING MEMBERS AGREE TO ENCOURAGE. The jeweller, electronics or car company buying the ore has committed to press its suppliers — which is a second address to write to when the mine itself will not answer, and this file's supply-chain entries under Benin are how you find who buys. THE AFRICAN MEMBER AND THE AFRICAN EVENT: IT PARTNERED WITH A NAMED ZIMBABWEAN ENVIRONMENTAL LAW ASSOCIATION, A MEMBER, TO HOST AN INTERACTIVE DISCUSSION AT AN ALTERNATIVE MINING CONFERENCE ON THE ROLE OF STANDARDS AND THIRD-PARTY ASSURANCE — FOCUSED ON HOW AFFECTED COMMUNITIES, NGOs AND ORGANIZED LABOUR HAVE USED THE STANDARD AND THE AUDIT REPORTS, WITH SMALL GROUP DISCUSSIONS ON THE TOOLS AND STRATEGIES THAT WOULD HELP PARTICIPANTS USE IT TO PROTECT THEIR RIGHTS. An African environmental law association is a member and ran the session. That is the organisation to ask what the standard has actually achieved on the ground before investing effort in it — and the alternative mining conference where it happened is itself a recurring African gathering worth attending. THE CONSULTANTS' COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE: PARTICIPANTS HAVE UNDERTAKEN AN IN-DEPTH ORIENTATION AND JOIN QUARTERLY MEETINGS TO DEEPEN KNOWLEDGE AND STRENGTHEN COLLECTIVE CAPACITY. THE HONEST POSITION OF THE ADVOCACY ORGANISATION BEHIND IT: IT HAS BEEN, AND CONTINUES TO BE, CRITICAL OF MANY VOLUNTARY AND CERTIFICATION SYSTEMS, PARTICULARLY THOSE INITIATED AND GOVERNED BY INDUSTRY — AND STATES THAT WHILE IT BELIEVES IN THE STRATEGIC VALUE OF THIS ONE, IT UNDERSTANDS THAT OTHERS MAY NOT AGREE WITH ITS ASSESSMENT, AND EVEN AS IT ADVOCATES FOR MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS AND LEGAL REFORMS, IT VIEWS THE STANDARD AND AUDITS AS AN ADDITIONAL TOOL. An organisation recommending a voluntary scheme while saying plainly that voluntary schemes are not the answer and that reasonable people disagree. Treat it as one instrument beside the law, never as a substitute — which is the same verdict this file records the palm oil guide's authors reaching about their own industry. AND ITS COMMITMENTS: ADVOCATING FOR MORE INCLUSION, RESOURCES, AND THE PARTICIPATION OF FRONTLINE COMMUNITIES AND WORKERS THROUGHOUT THE SYSTEM; AND PUSHING BACK AGAINST ANY ATTEMPTS TO GREENWASH OR WEAKEN ITS GOVERNANCE, TRANSPARENCY, AUDITING PROCESS OR MEMBERSHIP SYSTEM. WHO IT SUITS: African communities beside an industrial-scale mine of any mined material other than coal, oil or gas — and the national organisations and unions supporting them. CAVEATS: VOLUNTARY, EXCLUDES ENERGY FUELS, EXCLUDES ARTISANAL MINING, AND PARTICIPATION ALONE PROVES NOTHING — read the tier and the audit report. For the mining laws of 53 countries side by side, Guinea-Bissau's entry; for open data on mining sites and armed presence, Benin's entry; for the palm oil equivalent and its honest verdict, Angola's entry.

trackers.name: Pro bono legal representation for civil society organisations with the environment as one of four named practice areas — a director for Africa with a published address, and a worked example analysing mining due-diligence law for a pan-African rights umbrella
trackers.desc: THE ENVIRONMENT IS ONE OF FOUR PRACTICE AREAS, AND AFRICA HAS ITS OWN DIRECTOR — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ETHIOPIA ENTRY COVERS THE SENIOR LAWYERS PROJECT A MEMBER OF THIS TEAM CAME FROM, ITS BOTSWANA ENTRY THE VOLUNTEER LAWYER NETWORK LISTED BESIDE IT IN PRO BONO DIRECTORIES, ITS SÃO TOMÉ AND ESWATINI ENTRIES THE TWO CLEARINGHOUSE MODELS, AND ITS EGYPT ENTRY AN ACCESS-TO-INFORMATION HOST. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE ENVIRONMENT AS A NAMED PRACTICE AREA, WHICH IS THE FIND: WE PROVIDE HIGH-QUALITY, PRO BONO LEGAL REPRESENTATION WORLDWIDE TO DOZENS OF NGOs AND INTERNATIONAL GOVERNMENTAL BODIES ACROSS FOUR PROGRAMMATIC AREAS: THE ENVIRONMENT, HUMAN RIGHTS AND ACCESS TO JUSTICE, INSTITUTIONAL INTEGRITY, AND PUBLIC INTEREST REPORTING. Most pro bono routes in this file take environmental matters as a subset of something else, so a land or forest organisation has to argue its way in. Here the environment is a standing practice area with its own staff, which means an environmental request is the normal business rather than the exception — and PUBLIC INTEREST REPORTING as a fourth area covers the journalist reporting on the project too. THE WORD USED IS REPRESENTATION: THE PRO BONO REPRESENTATION PROGRAM WORKS WITH LAW FIRMS WORLDWIDE ON BEHALF OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS IN THE AREAS OF HUMAN RIGHTS, THE ENVIRONMENT, AND GOOD GOVERNANCE — ENGAGING HUNDREDS OF LAW FIRMS AND LAWYERS ACROSS BORDERS. REPRESENTATION rather than advice. This file has recorded most free legal routes stopping at an opinion; the language here is of acting on behalf of the organisation. THE AFRICAN DESK: A DIRECTOR, AFRICA INITIATIVES, WITH A PUBLISHED EMAIL ADDRESS, DIRECTING PROGRAMMATIC ACTIVITIES IN AFRICA ACROSS ALL FOUR PRACTICE AREAS, AND LEADING EFFORTS TO PROMOTE AND STRENGTHEN PRO BONO PRACTICE IN SELECTED AFRICAN COUNTRIES THROUGH SPECIAL INITIATIVES AND STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS. A named person with a published address whose job is Africa. That is a specific door rather than a general enquiry form, and it is the one to use. THE WORKED EXAMPLE, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: A PRO BONO SPOTLIGHT ANALYSING HUMAN RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL DUE DILIGENCE LEGAL FRAMEWORKS THROUGHOUT SOUTH AFRICA — FOR AN UMBRELLA ORGANIZATION BRINGING TOGETHER DOZENS OF HUMAN RIGHTS GROUPS ACROSS AFRICA, WORKING WITH CO-COUNSEL TO ANALYSE LEGAL FRAMEWORKS RELATED TO MINING. A due-diligence analysis of mining law, produced free, for an African rights umbrella. That is precisely the document a community needs when arguing that a mining company's obligations extend further than it admits — and it shows both the subject matter they will take and that they work with local CO-COUNSEL rather than replacing them. THE AFRICAN CLEARINGHOUSE IT HELPED CREATE: IN APRIL THE AFRICA PROGRAM LAUNCHED WITH NATIONAL PARTNERS THE PRO BONO INSTITUTE OF KENYA, THE COUNTRY'S FIRST PRO BONO CLEARINGHOUSE. A national clearinghouse is a permanent local route rather than a foreign one. Where a country has none, this is the organisation that helps build it — which is a thing a national bar association or NGO coalition can propose. THE THREE AFRICAN CLEARINGHOUSES IT CONVENED: IN PARTNERSHIP WITH A SOUTH AFRICAN PRO BONO ORGANISATION, A NIGERIAN PUBLIC INTEREST LAW PARTNERSHIP AND A PRO BONO CLEARING HOUSE, IT BEGAN A FIRST AFRICA PRO BONO SERIES — ENGAGING AFRICA'S THREE MAJOR PRO BONO CLEARINGHOUSES' STAFF, LAWYERS, BENEFICIARIES AND REGULATORY FRAMEWORKS, INCLUDING BRINGING TOGETHER NGOs TO DISCUSS HOW THEY WORK WITH CLEARINGHOUSES AND TO ENCOURAGE MORE NGOs IN AFRICA TO WORK WITH THEM. Three named national clearinghouses in South Africa, Nigeria and Kenya. Those are domestic doors, in-country, and an organisation in or near those jurisdictions should go there before writing to New York. THE FELLOWSHIP AND ITS AFRICAN SCOPE: AN AFRICAN LEGAL FELLOWS PROGRAM SELECTS AFRICAN LAWYERS TO WORK AT NEW YORK LAW FIRMS AND CORPORATE LEGAL DEPARTMENTS FOR UP TO A YEAR — SINCE 2002 SUPPORTING LAWYERS FROM TRADITIONALLY-DISADVANTAGED BACKGROUNDS, AND SINCE 2015 SEEKING TO STRENGTHEN PRO BONO PRACTICE IN KENYA, NIGERIA AND SOUTH AFRICA AS WELL AS OTHER AFRICAN COUNTRIES. AS WELL AS OTHER AFRICAN COUNTRIES is the phrase to test. The named three are the focus, but the door is not stated as closed elsewhere. HOW FELLOWS ARE CHOSEN: A NETWORK OF 48 PROGRAM ALUMNI HELPS SELECT SOUTH AFRICAN FELLOWS, AND LAW FIRMS IN KENYA, NIGERIA AND OTHER COUNTRIES NOMINATE THEIR OWN LAWYERS — WITH A PANEL INTERVIEWING FINALISTS AFTER AN INITIAL SCREENING. Outside South Africa the route is nomination by your firm, not application by you. A lawyer who wants this must persuade an employer first, which is worth knowing before drafting anything. THE OTHER AFRICAN TRAINING ON RECORD: ATTORNEYS CONTRIBUTED TO SESSIONS ORGANIZED BY A YOUTH-LED ORGANIZATION IN NIGERIA TO TRAIN LAWYERS AND JUDICIAL OFFICIALS, AND THE AFRICA INITIATIVES TEAM WORKED WITH A NIGERIAN LAW FIRM TO PRODUCE A TRAINING MANUAL. A YOUTH-LED ORGANISATION set the agenda and the international lawyers contributed to it. That is the direction of travel worth asking for. WHAT IT LOOKS FOR IN ITS OWN AFRICAN STAFF, WHICH TELLS YOU HOW IT WORKS: ENGAGING WITH CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS IN SELECT COUNTRIES TO IDENTIFY LEGAL NEEDS; RESEARCHING, DRAFTING AND EDITING REPORTS AND ANALYSES ON INTERNATIONAL AND DOMESTIC LAWS FOR COUNTRIES IN AFRICA; AND ORGANIZING TRAININGS, WORKSHOPS AND LEGAL NEEDS ASSESSMENTS — WITH CANDIDATES REQUIRED TO BE LICENSED TO PRACTISE LAW IN AN AFRICAN JURISDICTION. A LEGAL NEEDS ASSESSMENT is a thing you can ask for by name. An organisation that does not yet know what legal help it needs is the intended starting point, not a disqualified one. THE INSTITUTION BEHIND IT: A PROGRAM OF A NEW YORK CITY BAR ASSOCIATION, FOUNDED IN 2003, WITH ACCESS TO ALL THAT BAR'S RESOURCES AND ITS AFFILIATE JUSTICE CENTRE, WORKING IN PARTNERSHIP WITH PRIVATE- AND PUBLIC-SECTOR LAWYERS, THE JUDICIARY, LAW SCHOOLS AND NGOs IN THE REGIONS WHERE IT WORKS. AND THE COALITIONS IT SITS IN: A UNITED NATIONS ANTI-CORRUPTION CONVENTION COALITION, AN INTERNATIONAL COALITION ON THE RESPONSIBILITY TO PROTECT, AND A COALITION FOR AN EFFECTIVE AFRICAN COURT ON HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS — WITH CONSULTATIVE STATUS AT THE UNITED NATIONS ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL COUNCIL. The African Court coalition is the relevant one here: an organisation working to make that court effective is a useful ally for anyone contemplating taking a case there, and this file's regional-court entries are where that road starts. WHO IT SUITS: African civil society organisations needing environmental legal analysis, representation or a legal needs assessment — and national bar bodies wanting to establish a clearinghouse. CAVEATS: IT WORKS WITH ORGANISATIONS RATHER THAN INDIVIDUALS, FOCUSES ON SELECTED AFRICAN COUNTRIES, AND DELIVERS THROUGH LAW FIRMS AND CO-COUNSEL — for countries with a national clearinghouse, start there. For senior lawyers on attorney-client terms, Ethiopia's entry; for prosecutor training and trial observation, Botswana's entry; for the clearinghouse that circulates your matter to 800 lawyers, São Tomé's entry.

trackers.name: An association that takes French parent companies to court in France for harm caused abroad by their subsidiaries, subcontractors and suppliers — 13 actions and 30 formal notices so far, with a Ugandan oil case run this way and its defeat on jurisdiction recorded
trackers.desc: SUE THE PARENT COMPANY IN PARIS FOR WHAT THE SUBSIDIARY DID AT HOME — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC AND MOROCCO BUCKETS CARRY THE BELGIAN LAWYERS-WITHOUT-BORDERS HOST, AND ITS BOTSWANA ENTRY THE CANADIAN ONE — BOTH DIFFERENT ORGANISATIONS FROM THIS ONE; ITS CHAD ENTRY THE LAWYERS WHO BUILD CASES OUTSIDE THE JURISDICTION; ITS DR CONGO AND CONGO BUCKETS AN ANTI-TORTURE HOST AND NAME. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. WHAT THE LAW LETS A COMMUNITY DO, WHICH IS THE FIND: FRENCH PARENT AND OUTSOURCING COMPANIES CAN FINALLY BE HELD LEGALLY ACCOUNTABLE FOR HARMS TO PEOPLE AND THE ENVIRONMENT CAUSED BY THEIR ACTIVITIES, AS WELL AS THOSE OF THEIR SUBSIDIARIES, SUBCONTRACTORS AND SUPPLIERS ABROAD, AND TAKEN TO COURT. The company on your land is usually a local subsidiary with no assets and no reputation to lose. This is the instrument that reaches past it to the parent in France — and SUBCONTRACTORS AND SUPPLIERS extends it further still, to the operator who is merely selling to a French buyer. For francophone Africa, where French multinationals hold much of the mining, oil and agribusiness recorded in this file, that is the most direct route to a defendant with something at stake. THE TWO ESCALATION STEPS: SIMPLY PUBLISHING A PLAN IS NOT ENOUGH — IF ITS VIGILANCE MEASURES ARE INADEQUATE, A COMPANY MAY BE SERVED WITH FORMAL NOTICE, OR EVEN HAVE TO ANSWER FOR ITS ACTIONS IN COURT. A FORMAL NOTICE comes first and is far cheaper than litigation. Thirty have been sent against thirteen cases brought, so most of this work never reaches a courtroom — which makes it a realistic first move for a community with a documented harm and no money for a trial. THE RUNNING TALLY: 13 LEGAL ACTIONS BROUGHT SINCE THE LAW WAS PASSED AND 30 FORMAL NOTICES SENT — WITH SEVEN NEW CASES LISTED IN ONE YEAR BY THIS ASSOCIATION AND A NAMED PARTNER, INCLUDING A SUMMONS AGAINST A MAJOR ENERGY COMPANY CONCERNING ACTS OF TORTURE AT ONE OF ITS SITES, AND A FORMAL NOTICE AGAINST A RETAILER CONCERNING ITS SUPPLY OF TUNA FROM INDUSTRIAL FISHERIES INVOLVED IN HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS. A tuna supply chain and a site security force are both actionable. The range is wider than heavy industry, and a fishing community losing its grounds to an industrial fleet selling into a French supermarket is describing a case already brought. THE AFRICAN CASE AND ITS HONEST OUTCOME, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE FIRST ACTION, FILED IN SUMMARY PROCEEDINGS BY FRENCH AND UGANDAN ORGANISATIONS OVER A MAJOR ENERGY COMPANY'S OIL PROJECTS IN UGANDA, RESULTED IN A DECISION OF LACK OF JURISDICTION IN JANUARY 2020 — THE JUDGES HELD THAT THE OBLIGATION TO DRAW UP A VIGILANCE PLAN HAD A DIRECT LINK WITH THE MANAGEMENT OF A COMPANY AND WAS THEREFORE A DISPUTE RELATING TO COMMERCIAL COMPANIES, GOVERNING THE JURISDICTION OF COMMERCIAL COURTS; THE DECISION, WHICH CAUSED CONCERN AMONG CIVIL SOCIETY, WAS CONFIRMED ON APPEAL IN DECEMBER 2020. Recorded because a route that failed is worth more than one described only in the abstract: an African community's case was thrown out on which French court could hear it, not on the merits, and the appeal confirmed it. Any organisation preparing such a case should settle the forum question with French counsel before filing, and should ask what has changed since those judgments. THE SECOND ACTION AND WHO BROUGHT IT: 14 LOCAL AUTHORITIES AND 5 ASSOCIATIONS TOOK THE SAME COMPANY TO COURT OVER ITS MAJOR CONTRIBUTION TO CLIMATE CHANGE AND THE INADEQUACY OF THE MEASURES TAKEN TO PREVENT THE RESULTING HUMAN RIGHTS, HEALTH AND SAFETY, AND ENVIRONMENTAL DAMAGE. FOURTEEN LOCAL AUTHORITIES as co-claimants. A municipality or district council can be a party in these actions — which is worth knowing where a local authority is sympathetic but has been told it has no standing. THE OTHER NAMED DEFENDANTS: LAWSUITS AGAINST THREE NAMED FRENCH MULTINATIONALS — AN ENERGY COMPANY, A RETAIL GROUP AND A COSMETICS COMPANY — ILLUSTRATE THE MANY OBSTACLES THAT VICTIMS STILL FACE IN THEIR ACCESS TO JUSTICE. THE FREE EXPLANATORY MATERIAL AND ITS LANGUAGES: NINE FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS GIVING AN EXHAUSTIVE OVERVIEW OF THE SCOPE OF THE LAW, THE COMPANIES AND OBLIGATIONS COVERED, AND THE LEGAL MECHANISMS AND SANCTIONS — AVAILABLE IN ENGLISH, FRENCH AND SPANISH. Free, in French and English, written to be read by people who are not French lawyers. Start there to establish whether the company operating on your land has a French parent within scope before approaching anyone. THE PARALLEL WHISTLEBLOWING REQUIREMENT: A SEPARATE LAW ON TRANSPARENCY, THE FIGHT AGAINST CORRUPTION AND MODERNISING ECONOMIC LIFE ALSO DEMANDS THE IMPLEMENTATION OF A WHISTLEBLOWING MECHANISM — WHICH IS WHY CERTAIN COMPANIES EXPLICITLY REFER TO THAT LAW IN THEIR VIGILANCE PLAN. A second obligation running alongside, which means the company already has a channel it is legally required to operate. Its own whistleblowing mechanism is a documented place to lodge a complaint that creates a record. THE STAKEHOLDER ROUTE INTO THE PLAN: PUBLISHED DISCUSSION OF HOW COMPANIES CAN INVOLVE STAKEHOLDERS IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF THE VIGILANCE PLAN. The plan is a public document the company must write about risks in its supply chain. A community that gets itself named as a stakeholder in it, or that publicly documents an omission from it, is building the inadequacy argument the formal notice rests on. THE STRUCTURAL OBSTACLE THE LAW WAS BUILT TO REMOVE: POLITICALLY, SYMBOLICALLY AND TECHNICALLY, THE LAW ENABLES THE REMOVAL OF SEVERAL STRUCTURAL OBSTACLES WHICH GENERALLY PREVENT LEGISLATION FROM APPREHENDING THE HARMFUL CONSEQUENCES OF THE DELOCALISED ACTIVITIES OF MULTINATIONAL COMPANIES. THE COMING EUROPEAN EXTENSION AND ITS STATED WEAKNESSES: A EUROPEAN DIRECTIVE WHICH MUST BE TRANSPOSED BY JULY 2026 SHOULD ENABLE MORE COMPANIES TO BE COVERED — BUT THE EUROPEAN LEGISLATOR CHOSE TO LIMIT THE RIGHTS PROTECTED, FINANCIAL SERVICES WERE EXCLUDED UNDER PRESSURE, THE DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF REQUIRED MEASURES MAY LEAD TO COSMETIC COMPLIANCE, AND WITHOUT GUARANTEED ACCESS TO INFORMATION ON MULTINATIONALS, IDENTIFYING THEM AND MONITORING THE DIRECTIVE COULD BE JUST AS ARDUOUS. More European companies come into scope, so the same route may soon reach parents in other member states — but FINANCIAL SERVICES EXCLUDED means the bank financing a project is not covered, which is the gap the development-bank database filed under Ethiopia partly answers. AND WHAT THE ORGANISATION SAYS IT DOES AND NEEDS: LEGAL INNOVATION, STRATEGIC LITIGATION AND ADVOCACY, DEVELOPING RECOMMENDATIONS AND PROPOSING AN INNOVATIVE LEGISLATIVE ARSENAL AIMED AT CHANGING THE LAW TO BETTER PROTECT THE ENVIRONMENT, COMMUNITIES AND WORKERS — AS A FOUNDING MEMBER OF A EUROPEAN COALITION FOR CORPORATE JUSTICE, STATING THAT IT NEEDS SUPPORT TO INVESTIGATE, ALERT AND TAKE ACTION. INVESTIGATE, ALERT AND TAKE ACTION describes the sequence and the entry point: the alert comes from the affected community, and the investigation follows it. WHO IT SUITS: African communities and organisations — especially francophone ones — harmed by the operations, subcontractors or suppliers of a French or European multinational. CAVEATS: IT LITIGATES IN FRANCE UNDER FRENCH LAW AND WORKS WITH PARTNER ORGANISATIONS, SO A COMMUNITY NEEDS A NATIONAL ORGANISATION TO BRING THE CASE WITH; THE JURISDICTION QUESTION DEFEATED THE FIRST AFRICAN ATTEMPT, CASES TAKE YEARS, AND THE COMPANY MUST HAVE A FRENCH PARENT OR BUYER WITHIN SCOPE. For cases built from outside the jurisdiction generally, Chad's entry; for the francophone partner-capacity organisation, Botswana's entry.

trackers.name: CHRR (Centre for Human Rights and Rehabilitation), Lilongwe, and CHREAA (Centre for Human Rights, Education, Advice and Assistance), Blantyre — free paralegal clinics in Malawi, one walk-in and NGO-accredited at the African Commission, the other running mobile clinics into rural areas
trackers.desc: A FREE CLINIC IN THE CAPITAL, AND A CLINIC THAT DRIVES TO THE VILLAGES — method and adjacency declared first: SIXTH NAMED-ATTORNEY ROUND. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN FOUR HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; BOTH SUBJECT HOSTS, BOTH ACRONYMS AND FOUR FACTS ABSENT. ONE STATUTE NAME MATCHED A MALAWI ENTRY ABOUT A CONSERVATION SOCIETY REGISTERED UNDER THE SAME ACT, READ IN FULL AND A DIFFERENT SUBJECT. THIS FILE'S ERITREA ENTRY COVERS THE CONTINENTAL COMMISSION'S OWN COMPLAINT PROCEDURE AND CARRIES ITS HOST. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE FREE CLINIC, WHICH IS THE FIND: THE FIRST ORGANISATION OPERATES A PARALEGAL CLINIC AIMED AT PROVIDING SMALL SCALE LEGAL ADVICE AND REMEDY TO MEMBERS OF THE COMMUNITIES IT OPERATES IN, AND PROVIDES LEGAL ADVICE ON CASES INVOLVING PEOPLE WHO FEEL THEIR HUMAN RIGHTS HAVE BEEN VIOLATED IN ONE WAY OR THE OTHER — THE SERVICES OFFERED FOR FREE. SMALL SCALE is stated honestly, and it is the right expectation: advice and first remedy, not a High Court campaign. This file's Benin entry records the published boundary where a paralegal must hand a land title dispute to an advocate; a clinic like this is what exists on the near side of that line, and for most people it is the only thing that exists at all. THE MOBILE CLINICS AND WHAT THEY ARE FOR, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE SECOND ORGANISATION RUNS AN INITIATIVE FOCUSED ON ENHANCING ACCESS TO JUSTICE AND BRIDGING THE GAP BETWEEN INFORMAL AND FORMAL JUSTICE SYSTEMS IN RURAL AREAS, THROUGH THE TRAINING OF COMMUNITY PARALEGALS AND MOBILE LEGAL CLINICS. BRIDGING INFORMAL AND FORMAL JUSTICE is the precise problem for a rural community: the chief's forum will hear you tomorrow and cannot bind a company, the magistrate can bind it and sits three hours away. An organisation that works both sides is worth more than one fluent in only the second. WHERE THE FIRST ONE CAN BE WALKED INTO: A PUBLISHED STREET, AREA AND PLOT NUMBER IN THE CAPITAL, WITH A PUBLISHED POSTAL BOX AND EMAIL. WHAT ITS REGISTRATION LETS IT DO: FOUNDED IN FEBRUARY 1995 AS A NON-PROFIT, APOLITICAL, VOLUNTARY ORGANIZATION REGISTERED UNDER MALAWI'S TRUSTEES INCORPORATION ACT OF 1962 — AUTHORIZED TO PROVIDE ITS SERVICES ANYWHERE IN THE COUNTRY, ITS REGISTRATION PROVIDING THE BASIS THAT DEFINES ITS MANDATE AND SCOPE OF WORK, WITH PROGRAMMES IN ALL THREE REGIONS. AUTHORIZED ANYWHERE IN THE COUNTRY, by the terms of its registration. That is a thing to check about any organisation offering help: some registrations are district-limited, and a body that cannot lawfully operate where you are cannot act for you. WHO FOUNDED IT: FORMER STUDENT EXILES WHO RETURNED HOME TO THE PROMISES OF A NEW DEMOCRACY IN 1994. ITS STANDING AT THE CONTINENTAL BODY: IT IS LISTED AMONG THE NGOs OF THE AFRICAN COMMISSION ON HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS, WHOSE SECRETARIAT SITS IN BANJUL, THE GAMBIA. A paralegal clinic that is also accredited at the continental commission. That combination is rare and it is the useful one: the same organisation that takes a walk-in complaint can carry it upward if the domestic route fails. WHAT KINDS OF CASE THE CLINIC ACTUALLY HANDLES: CASES RANGING FROM GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND LABOUR TO IMMIGRATION ISSUES AND POLICE MATTERS. Land is not on that published list. Recorded plainly so nobody arrives expecting it — but LABOUR and POLICE are, which covers the farm worker dismissed with his housing and the person arrested at a protest. WHAT THE FIRST ORGANISATION SAYS ITS MISSION IS: TO CONTRIBUTE TOWARDS THE PROTECTION, PROMOTION AND CONSOLIDATION OF GOOD GOVERNANCE BY EMPOWERING RURAL AND URBAN COMMUNITIES TO INCREASE AWARENESS OF AND EXERCISE THEIR RIGHTS THROUGH RESEARCH, EDUCATION, ADVOCACY AND NETWORKING — THROUGH TWO CORE PROGRAMMES, COMMUNITY MOBILIZATION AND EMPOWERMENT, AND HUMAN RIGHTS MONITORING AND TRAINING. THE NETWORK IT SITS INSIDE: THE HUMAN RIGHTS CONSULTATIVE COMMITTEE (HRCC) DESCRIBED AS A NETWORK OF CHURCH INSTITUTIONS, HUMAN RIGHTS NGOs AND THE COUNTRY'S LAW SOCIETY, WHICH WORKS TOGETHER ON HUMAN RIGHTS, ADVOCACY AND INFORMATION SHARING — ITS FORMER DIRECTOR HAVING CHAIRED THAT COMMITTEE AND BEEN ONE OF THE PRIMARY ORGANIZERS OF THE 20 JULY 2011 MALAWIAN PROTESTS. THE LAW SOCIETY sitting in the same network as the churches and the NGOs. That is the door to the private bar: a community that reaches the consultative committee is one step from the professional body that can find it an advocate. WHAT THE SECOND ORGANISATION IS AND WHERE: A NON-PROFIT IN BLANTYRE, ASSISTING MARGINALIZED PEOPLE WITH HUMAN RIGHTS ISSUES AND LEGAL ADVICE AND FACILITATES ACCESS TO JUSTICE FOR THE POOR — PART OF ITS ADVOCACY BEING REFORM OF THE CRIMINAL JUSTICE SYSTEM, PARTICULARLY IN PRISONS. Two organisations in two different cities, which matters in a long country where a single capital office reaches nobody in the south. ITS BAIL PROGRAMME, WHICH IS THE THIRD FIND: A PIONEERING INITIATIVE EMPOWERING ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED INDIVIDUALS WITH ESSENTIAL LEGAL KNOWLEDGE TO NAVIGATE THE BAIL APPLICATION PROCESS EFFECTIVELY, THROUGH DISSEMINATION OF INFORMATION AND TARGETED TRAINING, AIMING TO INCREASE THE APPROVAL RATE — ALONGSIDE A PROJECT TO ERADICATE TORTURE AND ILL-TREATMENT IN DETENTION THROUGH VICTIM SUPPORT, ENHANCED REPORTING AND ACCOUNTABILITY WITHIN LAW ENFORCEMENT. Teaching people to make their own bail application, rather than only representing them. A detained land defender whose community can be taught the bail process does not have to wait for a lawyer to become available — and this file has recorded that the wait is where the harm happens. AND THE JOINT ACTION ON RECORD: IN JULY 2024 THE SECOND ORGANISATION WAS ONE OF MANY THAT SIGNED AN OPEN PROTEST LETTER TO THE MINISTER OF JUSTICE. It signs collective letters, which tells you it will lend its name to a coalition rather than only acting alone. WHO IT SUITS: people in this country needing free first-line legal advice, rural communities who need the clinic to come to them, and anyone detained who needs the bail process explained. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY, AND BOTH ARE PARALEGAL AND ADVICE BODIES RATHER THAN LAW FIRMS — THE PUBLISHED CASE LIST DOES NOT INCLUDE LAND, AND A TITLE DISPUTE WILL NEED AN ADVOCATE; SOME MATERIAL CITED IS OLDER, SO CHECK CURRENT CLINIC LOCATIONS AND HOURS. For the published rule on when a paralegal must escalate a land case, Benin's entry; for the commission's own complaint procedure, Eritrea's entry.

trackers.name: Ålands Natur & Miljö
trackers.desc: Åland's independent environmental folkrörelse, with around a thousand members in a population of just over thirty thousand — proportionally one of the deepest memberships of any body in this file, which is why it is taken seriously in a small polity. WHO TO ENLIST when a wind farm, a plan or a permit lands on the islands. You CAN: use it as a formal consultee — it gives utlåtanden in impact-assessment procedures, including on whether Finland should take part in the transboundary assessment of an offshore wind expansion. It also sits on the monitoring committee for Åland's structural fund programme and its CAP interventions, so it has a seat where the money is allocated, not only where the permit is decided. For activists: it owns its own forest in the archipelago at Nötö and had it professionally surveyed as untouched natural forest, so it holds land as well as opinions. Expect campaigning, consultation responses and evidence rather than litigation.

trackers.name: Åland — Government of Åland, Budget (Finansavdelningen)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the autonomous Government of Åland (Finance Department) prepares the annual budget submitted to the Lagting, and publishes budget proposals, supplementary budgets & fiscal data, Åland. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Åland.

trackers.name: Åland — Landskapsrevisionen (Audit Authority)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution; Landskapsrevisionen is the independent audit authority under the Åland Parliament (Lagting), established by landskapslag 2013:25, performing annual financial audit, performance audit & audit of EU structural-fund support, Åland.

trackers.name: Nordic Council of Ministers — Åland counts toward the three
trackers.desc: YOU COUNT AS A FULL ENTITY, NOT A JUNIOR PARTNER — that is the whole point of this entry. The Nordic Council of Ministers requires that at least three of the following must be involved: Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Iceland, Finland, the Faroe Islands, Greenland, or Åland. The Faroe Islands, Greenland and Åland count toward the three alongside the five states, so a project involving only those three autonomous territories satisfies the requirement without any larger country. The central criterion is that projects provide added value to the Nordic countries, the Faroe Islands, Greenland, and Åland — the three are named again in the added-value test, so the benefit need not accrue to the states. ASK WHICH ROUTE APPLIES BEFORE PREPARING ANYTHING: the Council issues direct calls on particular topics from time to time, but the majority of projects are run by an ‘administrative body’, usually a national agency in the Nordic Region, commissioned by the Council — so most of the money is not distributed by the Council itself. The environment and climate working groups fund Nordic projects as a second layer within the same structure. ÅLAND HAS WON AT THIS LEVEL TWICE: the Agenda 21 office, Åland Natur & Miljö took the Nordic Council Environment Prize in 1999, and the City of Mariehamn won it in 2022 for management of wetlands — usable as precedent that Ålandic environmental work is recognised at Nordic level.

trackers.name: ÅMHM — anyone may comment in the 21 days; only a party may appeal
trackers.desc: COMMENT FIRST, WHILE ANYONE MAY. Ålands miljö- och hälsoskyddsmyndighet is the permitting authority, with its electronic noticeboard at amhm.ax and decisions also available in the reception at Norragatan 17, Mariehamn during the stated period. Under Landskapslag (2008:124) om miljöskydd, notice of an application must be published on that noticeboard for at least 21 days before the authority decides, stating the nature of the matter and where the application and all documents added during preparation are available — so ask for the full file, not the application alone. AND THE COMMENT RIGHT IS OPEN: ‘var och en har rätt att ... skriftligen yttra sig över ansökan’ — everyone may submit written views during publication. No standing test applies at the comment stage, which is materially different from the appeal stage, where the appellant must be a sakägare. The 21-day window is the moment the file is open and anyone can be heard — use it. HONEST CONTEXT FROM THE LAGTING'S OWN MATERIAL: handling times have been criticised, decisions often did not gain legal force, and the body was problematised by high staff turnover. The procedure has been publicly argued to be too complicated and costly with long review processes; the recorded counter-argument is that effective environmental protection requires proper prior examination. Expect a slow process, contested from both directions.

trackers.name: Ålands förvaltningsdomstol — ask expressly for the works to be stopped
trackers.desc: AN APPEAL THAT DOES NOT STOP THE WORKS MAY BE DECIDED AFTER THE SITE IS GONE. Appeals against the permitting authority's decisions go to Ålands förvaltningsdomstol, and the law provides that ‘besvärsmyndigheten kan förbjuda verkställighet’ — the appeal authority may prohibit execution of the decision, for both inspection decisions and permit decisions. Ask for the prohibition expressly when you file. THE DEADLINE, AND HOW TO COUNT IT: a published ÅMHM notice records 30 days from the day the decision was delivered (delgavs), with delivery deemed to occur a set number of days after publication — calculate from the deemed delivery date, not the publication date. The ground is lagligheten av beslutet, the lawfulness of the decision, and the original decision or a copy must be attached to the appeal document. A PROTECTION BUILT INTO THE LAW: execution may not be granted for a permit under chapter 3 of the Water Act concerning permission to dispose of another's property — so where a permit would let an operator use land or water belonging to someone else, immediate execution is unavailable as a matter of law. CHECK THE STAGE BEFORE: rättelseyrkande (request for rectification) is part of the administrative procedure preceding the appeal proper — establish whether one is required first. Åland's competence here flows from the självstyrelselag.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one.
